title: Feature Request: HTTP Server Mode for Remote Control
body:
Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Add an HTTP server mode to cua-driver that exposes the existing CLI functionality via REST API, enabling remote control of Windows machines without requiring direct console access.                                     
     Problem / Use Case                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     When controlling Windows PCs remotely via SSH:                                                                                                                                                                           
     - SSH sessions run in Session 0 (non-interactive), which cannot access the visible desktop                                                                                                                               
     - Current workaround requires creating scheduled tasks with /IT /RU <user> to run in the console session                                                                                                                 
     - This approach is one-directional — commands execute but retrieving output (screenshots, window lists, etc.) is cumbersome                                                                                              
     - No real-time feedback loop for automation workflows                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Current workflow:                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Mac/Linux → SSH → Windows (Session 0) → schtasks /IT → Console Session → cua-driver                                                                                                                                      
                                                         ↑                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                 (output lost here)                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Desired workflow:                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Mac/Linux → HTTP request → cua-driver server (running in Console Session) → response with screenshot/result                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Proposed Solution                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Add a serve or server subcommand that starts an HTTP API server:                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     bash                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
     cua-driver serve --port 8080 [--host 0.0.0.0] [--auth-token <token>]                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Suggested API Endpoints                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     | Method | Endpoint    | Description                       | Maps to CLI  |                                                                                                                                              
     |--------|-------------|-----------------------------------|--------------|                                                                                                                                              
     | GET    | /screenshot | Capture screen, return PNG/base64 | screenshot   |                                                                                                                                              
     | GET    | /windows    | List visible windows              | list-windows |                                                                                                                                              
     | POST   | /click      | Click at coordinates or element   | click        |                                                                                                                                              
     | POST   | /type       | Type text                         | type         |                                                                                                                                              
     | POST   | /key        | Press key combo                   | key          |                                                                                                                                              
     | POST   | /scroll     | Scroll in direction               | scroll       |                                                                                                                                              
     | POST   | /open-url   | Open URL in browser               | open-url     |                                                                                                                                              
     | GET    | /health     | Health check                      | -            |                                                                                                                                              
     Example Usage                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     bash                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
     Start server on Windows (in console session, e.g., via startup script)                                                                                                                                                   
     cua-driver serve --port 8080 --auth-token mysecret                                                                                                                                                                       
     Remote calls from Mac/Linux                                                                                                                                                                                              
     curl -H "Authorization: Bearer mysecret" http://192.168.1.100:8080/screenshot -o screen.png                                                                                                                              
     curl -H "Authorization: Bearer mysecret" -X POST http://192.168.1.100:8080/click -d '{"x": 500, "y": 300}'                                                                                                               
     curl -H "Authorization: Bearer mysecret" http://192.168.1.100:8080/windows                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     Security Considerations                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     - Authentication: Token-based auth (--auth-token) or basic auth                                                                                                                                                          
     - Bind address: Default to 127.0.0.1, require explicit --host 0.0.0.0 for network access                                                                                                                                 
     - Optional TLS: --cert / --key flags for HTTPS                                                                                                                                                                           
     Alternatives Considered                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     1. Install full agent (e.g., Hermes Agent) on each Windows PC — Works but heavier, requires API keys and more setup                                                                                                      
     2. Use RDP/VNC — Adds latency, not scriptable                                                                                                                                                                            
     3. PowerShell remoting with UI Automation — Complex, less reliable than native screen access                                                                                                                             
     Environment                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
     - OS: Windows 10/11                                                                                                                                                                                                      
     - cua-driver version: 0.1.3 (cua-driver-rs)                                                                                                                                                                              
     - Use case: Remote automation from macOS/Linux controlling multiple Windows PCs

## Problem
The Rust driver release workflow can build binaries whose embedded Cargo package version does not match the release tag or manually supplied version. That lets stale `cua-driver --version` output make it into a release asset.

## Change
Add a pre-build release guard to the Linux, Windows, and macOS cua-driver-rs build jobs. The guard reads the `cua-driver` Cargo package version with `cargo pkgid` and fails closed when it differs from the release tag/input version.

title: capture() returns 0x0 empty screenshots (width=0, height=0)
body:
# `capture()` returns 0x0 empty screenshots (width=0, height=0)

## Description

`cua-driver capture` returns PNG data with **width=0, height=0** — the screenshot is effectively empty. The AX accessibility tree and element detection work correctly, but the actual pixel data is missing.

This affects both `som` and `vision` capture modes.

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS 26.5 (25F71) — Apple Silicon (M4)
- **cua-driver version:** 0.2.0 (also reproduced on 0.5.1)
- **Binary:** Universal (x86_64 + arm64)
- **Install method:** GitHub release tarball

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
from tools.computer_use.cua_backend import CuaDriverBackend
import base64

backend = CuaDriverBackend()
backend._session.start()

for mode in ['som', 'vision']:
    result = backend.capture(mode=mode)
    print(f'Mode: {mode}')
    print(f'  Width: {result.width}, Height: {result.height}')
    print(f'  Elements: {len(result.elements) if result.elements else 0}')
    if result.png_b64:
        img = base64.b64decode(result.png_b64)
        print(f'  PNG size: {len(img)} bytes')
```

## Actual Output

```
Mode: som
  Width: 0, Height: 0
  App: BetterDisplay
  Elements: 31
  PNG size: 4127 bytes

Mode: vision
  Width: 0, Height: 0
  App: BetterDisplay
  Elements: 0
  PNG size: 4127 bytes
```

## Expected Output

Width and Height should match the actual screen resolution (e.g., 2560x1440 for a built-in display or external monitor). The PNG data should contain the actual screenshot pixels.

## Additional Context

- **AX tree works fine:** `list_windows` and element detection return valid data (31–119 elements depending on the active app).
- **osascript screencapture works:** Using `screencapture -x` via osascript produces a valid 2560x1440 PNG (~4MB), confirming the screen is accessible.
- **PNG data is small:** The returned PNG is only ~4KB, suggesting it contains a 1x1 or empty image rather than a full screenshot.
- **Multiple apps tested:** Issue persists regardless of which app is in the foreground.
- **cua-driver process is healthy:** Socket connection works, daemon starts without errors.

## Workaround

For screenshot-only use cases, `screencapture -x` via osascript works as a fallback. However, this doesn't integrate with cua-driver's SOM overlay or element indexing.

```bash
osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to do script "screencapture -x /tmp/screenshot.png; exit"'
```

---

**Possibly related:** The `capture()` call returns `CaptureResult` with valid `elements` and `app` fields, but `width=0, height=0`. This suggests the screen capture call itself is failing silently while the AX tree query succeeds.

title: cua-driver MCP daemon proxy returns os error 35 forwarding get_window_state
body:
## Summary

When `get_window_state` is called through the `cua-driver mcp` stdio server and forwarded to the `cua-driver serve` daemon over the Unix socket, the daemon proxy can fail with `os error 35` / `EAGAIN`:

```text
mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError: daemon transport error forwarding `get_window_state`:
Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
```

The same `get_window_state` call succeeds when run in-process with `cua-driver call`, which makes quick CLI testing look healthy while MCP daemon usage fails.

## Environment

- OS: macOS Darwin 25.5.0, Apple Silicon / aarch64
- `cua-driver`: 0.5.1
- App: `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, Developer ID signed
- MCP path: downstream MCP client -> `cua-driver mcp` over stdio -> `cua-driver serve` daemon over `~/Library/Caches/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock`
- macOS permissions: Accessibility and Screen Recording granted for the driver app

## Behavior Observed

Two independent triggers reproduce the proxy failure:

1. Large `get_window_state` response
   - `capture_mode=som` can include a multi-MB base64 screenshot.
   - Smaller calls such as `list_windows`, `click`, and `type_text` forward successfully.

2. Slow accessibility traversal
   - Apple Notes produced a small response of roughly 35 KB, but `capture_mode=som` and `capture_mode=ax` still failed through the MCP -> daemon proxy.
   - `capture_mode=vision` succeeds on the same window, so this does not appear to be purely response-size related.

This looks like the proxy may be treating non-blocking socket `EAGAIN` as a fatal transport error instead of waiting for readiness and retrying. Client-side retry did not help: 5/5 repeated attempts failed. Restarting the daemon also did not help.

## Minimal Repro Shape

This succeeds in-process:

```bash
cua-driver call get_window_state '{"pid":<PID>,"window_id":<WID>,"capture_mode":"som"}'
```

The equivalent call through the MCP stdio server, where `cua-driver mcp` forwards to the daemon socket, fails on large responses or slow accessibility walks:

```text
McpError: daemon transport error forwarding `get_window_state`:
Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
```

Apple Notes reproduces reliably in this environment. `capture_mode=vision` on the same window succeeds.

## Downstream Workarounds Tried

A downstream wrapper was patched locally to reduce impact:

- Use `screenshot_out_file` so screenshots are written to a temp PNG and the MCP response carries the smaller accessibility tree instead of a multi-MB base64 screenshot.
- Fall back to `capture_mode=vision` when `som` / `ax` fails with the daemon transport error.

This avoids hard failures for some workflows, but it does not fix the daemon proxy behavior.

## Related Upstream Questions

- Is `os error 35` / `EAGAIN` in the MCP -> daemon proxy known? Can the proxy wait for socket readiness or retry on `EAGAIN` instead of returning an MCP error?
- Is `screenshot_out_file` the recommended way to keep MCP payloads small? Is there a plan to default screenshots to files or chunk large responses?
- Apple Notes main window can produce an empty or unusable AX tree in this setup. Is that a known limitation, or is there an alternate traversal flag/path?
- For coordinate clicks on scaled HiDPI displays, what coordinate space should `x,y` use when `get_screen_size.scale_factor` reports `1.0` but screenshot scale appears higher? Could the coordinate click path accept `window_id` to disambiguate multi-window apps?
- Idle CPU for the driver process was observed around 52-54% in this setup. Is there a known mitigation or tracking issue?
- Please confirm whether the removed screenshot tool is intentionally replaced by `get_window_state(capture_mode=vision)`.

title: cuabot shell execution still loses exit status on current main
body:
## Summary

Current main still loses structured shell execution status for cuabot bash commands and still marks computer-server run_command() as successful even when the process exits non-zero.

This was previously addressed in stale PR #1404 for issue #1403, but that PR has not been merged for months and current upstream main no longer contains the fix.

## Current behavior on main

- libs/cuabot/src/cuabotd.ts returns only { stdout, stderr, pid? } from execInContainer().
- Failed docker exec calls are compressed into { stdout, stderr }, losing err.code, timeout, and signal metadata.
- libs/cuabot/src/cuabot.tsx exits cuabot --bash with 0 regardless of remote command status.
- libs/python/computer-server/computer_server/handlers/base.py returns success: True for run_command() even when process.returncode != 0.

## Expected behavior

Shell execution should return structured status with stdout, stderr, exit_code, success, timed_out, signal, and pid where applicable.

The local CLI should propagate non-zero remote exits and timeouts.

## Reproduction examples

- cuabot --bash "exit 42" should exit 42 or at least non-zero, but current main exits 0.
- cuabot --bash "sleep 65; echo after" should expose structured timeout metadata and exit non-zero.

## Proposed fix

I opened a fresh PR against current main with the minimal contract fix and regression tests. It supersedes stale PR #1404 while preserving the same intent from #1403.

title: fix: preserve shell execution status across cuabot
body:
## Summary

Refs #1866 and the original shell status contract gap from #1403. Supersedes stale PR #1404.

Adds a structured `BashResult` contract for cuabot command execution, including exit codes, success, timeout metadata, signals, and background process IDs, and updates the client and CLI to consume that result.

- Preserve non-zero Docker exec status and timeout metadata in the execution layer.
- Write raw stdout/stderr from `cuabot --bash` and map structured results to CLI exit codes.
- Avoid advertising stale PIDs when background commands exit immediately.

## Main synchronization

Merged upstream `main` at `c62abf39ba407f385701b0a82a5a4d8b8eacc426` in `711be136783e0a00a376c630bfe80d5bbaa2bada`.

Resolved both modify/delete conflicts by retaining upstream's deletion of the old `computer-server` handler and its test. The current Python SDK already derives `CommandResult.success` from its return code, so this PR no longer changes the removed Python component. The remaining diff is limited to five cuabot source/test files.

## Verification

Executed on the merge commit using Node 22.23.4 and pnpm 10.11.0:

- `python3 bin/ci --quick --no-install --base upstream/main`: 2 checks passed (SPDX headers and image references); docs generators were not routed because docs dependencies were not installed.
- `cd libs/cuabot && pnpm exec node --import tsx --test src/bashResult.test.ts`: 9 tests passed.
- `cd libs/cuabot && pnpm test`: 7 telemetry tests passed.
- `cd libs/cuabot && pnpm run build`: passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.

## Known gaps

This synchronization resolves merge conflicts only. The review finding that the bash HTTP handler drops the new result fields remains unresolved. The `timeout=0` outer timeout boundary also needs a follow-up fix. Existing unit tests and the build do not establish Docker end-to-end correctness.

title: Request: Add License metadata to PyPI distributions and `libs/` directories to support enterprise installation
body:
Hi team! 👋 

First off, thank you for building such an amazing tool. We are really excited about the potential of using `cua` within our enterprise.

We are currently running into a deployment blocker, however. Our internal JFrog Artifactory has strict compliance checks and is blocking the installation of the PyPI distributions because they are missing explicit license metadata. 

We see that the root repository is covered by the MIT License (thank you for making it open source!), but for package managers and enterprise artifactories, PyPI acts as the ultimate source of truth. 

**To help us (and likely other enterprise users) adopt `cua`, could you please:**
1. Add the appropriate license classifiers and metadata to the `pyproject.toml` (or relevant build files) so it reflects accurately on PyPI.
2. Include a copy of the `LICENSE` file within the individual distribution packages inside the `libs/` directory, especially if they are built and published independently.

Let me know if you need any additional context, or if there's a good way I can help contribute this fix. Thanks again for your hard work on this project!

title: Migrate NixOS integration tests from VMs to containers
body:
## Summary
This PR migrates the CUA driver integration tests from NixOS VM-based tests (using QEMU) to container-based tests (using systemd-nspawn). This change improves CI performance and reduces resource requirements while maintaining test coverage.

## Key Changes

- **Test Infrastructure Migration**: Converted all `pkgs.testers.nixosTest` configurations from `nodes.machine` (VM-based) to `containers.machine` (container-based)
  - Updated test files: `linux-background-gui.nix`, `integration.nix`, `screenshot.nix`, `linux-background-terminal-gif.nix`, `linux-cursor-click-gif.nix`, `set-config.nix`

- **Removed VM-Specific Configuration**: Eliminated `virtualisation` blocks that specified:
  - `cores = 2`
  - `memorySize` settings (2048 MB, 4096 MB, 6144 MB variants)
  - `diskSize = 8192`
  - These are no longer needed as containers run at native speed without QEMU emulation overhead

- **Removed Per-App Memory Overrides**: Deleted `memoryMB` parameter from `mkSkeleton` function and individual app configurations (electron-zettlr, electron-joplin, electron-logseq, chromium, tk) since containers don't require memory pre-allocation

- **Updated Documentation**: Changed references from "VM" to "container" throughout comments and docstrings to reflect the new test infrastructure

- **Updated Nixpkgs Pin**: Changed `flake.nix` nixpkgs input from `nixos-unstable` to `nixos-26.05` to ensure compatibility with container-based tests

- **CI Configuration**: Added required Nix experimental features to GitHub Actions workflows:
  - `auto-allocate-uids` and `cgroups` for systemd-nspawn UID/cgroup support
  - `extra-system-features = uid-range` to advertise UID range capability

- **Updated Comments**: Clarified Firefox test status and GTK3 app timeout issues, noting that container tests run at native speed and may resolve previous emulation-related timeouts

- **Migrated `set-config.nix` too**: the `cua-driver-set-config` regression check (#1923/#1928) only needs Xvfb + the driver over MCP stdio — no kernel modules, seat, or DRM — so it moves to a `containers.machine` the same way `integration.nix`/`screenshot.nix` did. It runs in the same `nix-checks` matrix that already advertises the `auto-allocate-uids`/`cgroups`/`uid-range` features, so no extra workflow change was needed.

### Tests intentionally kept on VMs

These cannot run under `systemd-nspawn` and remain `nodes.machine` by design — containers can't load kernel modules (`modprobe uinput` needs `CAP_SYS_MODULE`), expose `/dev/uinput`, allocate a logind seat/VT, or provide DRM:

- `linux-parallel-drag-gif.nix` and `linux-parallel-drag-xserver.nix` — real Xorg + `boot.kernelModules = [ "uinput" ]`; the xserver variant also needs a display-manager seat.
- `nix/cua-driver/tests/wayland/*` — `boot.kernelModules = [ "uinput" ]` + `hardware.graphics`/DRM for the headless compositors.

## Implementation Details

The migration leverages NixOS's native container support via systemd-nspawn, which provides:
- Faster test execution (no QEMU emulation)
- Lower resource consumption (no VM memory overhead)
- Simpler configuration (no virtualization parameters needed)
- Native-speed execution that may resolve previous timeout issues in emulated environments

title: chore(packaging): add license metadata to Python distributions
body:
Fixes #1868

## Missing metadata evidence

Before this change, I built and inspected the wheel/sdist metadata for the Python packages under `libs/`.

- `cua-agent`, `cua-core`, `cua-computer`, `cua-mcp-server`, `cua-bench-ui`, and `cua-sandbox-apps` had no `License` metadata, no license classifier, and no LICENSE entry in the built archives.
- `cua-computer-server` had `License: MIT`, but no license classifier and no LICENSE entry in the built archives.
- `cua-auto`, `cua-cli`, `cua-sandbox`, and `cua-driver` had an MIT classifier but no LICENSE entry in wheel/sdist archives.
- `cua`, `cua-bench`, and `cua-som` already produced license file entries, so this PR leaves their existing license behavior intact.

I also checked for duplicates with:

```bash
gh pr list -R trycua/cua --state open --search "1868" --json number,title,state,headRefName,author,url,updatedAt
gh search prs --repo trycua/cua --state open "license metadata" --json number,title,state,url,author,updatedAt --limit 20
```

Both returned no open PRs.

## Changes

- Add MIT license metadata and MIT license classifiers to the affected Python package `pyproject.toml` files.
- Add package-local `LICENSE` files for the MIT-licensed Python distributions that did not include one.
- Add PDM `source-includes` entries where needed so sdists include the license file.
- Keep the change scoped to packaging metadata and license inclusion; no runtime code changes.

## Verification

I ran a metadata build inspection over these packages:

- `libs/python/agent`
- `libs/python/core`
- `libs/python/computer`
- `libs/python/computer-server`
- `libs/python/som`
- `libs/python/mcp-server`
- `libs/python/bench-ui`
- `libs/python/cua`
- `libs/python/cua-auto`
- `libs/python/cua-cli`
- `libs/python/cua-sandbox`
- `libs/python/cua-sandbox-apps`
- `libs/cua-driver/python`
- `libs/cua-bench`

Command pattern:

```bash
uv build --no-progress --color never --out-dir build/license-green <package-dir>
```

Then I inspected each wheel `METADATA` and each sdist `PKG-INFO` plus archive contents. Result:

```text
All checked distributions include license metadata and a LICENSE file entry.
```

Additional checks:

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import pathlib, tomllib
for path in sorted(pathlib.Path('.').glob('libs/**/pyproject.toml')) + [pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml')]:
    tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
print('parsed pyproject.toml files successfully')
PY

git diff --check
git diff --cached --check
```

Both diff checks exited 0, and all `pyproject.toml` files parsed successfully.

## Not run

I did not run runtime pytest/mypy suites because this PR only changes package metadata and LICENSE files, with no Python runtime source changes. The direct risk is package build metadata, covered by the wheel/sdist inspection above.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): PMv2 DPI manifest from #1821 is never applied - RT_MANIFEST embedded as string-typed resource
body:
## Summary

PR #1821 (v0.5.2) embeds a Per-Monitor V2 DPI manifest to fix pixel-click offsets under
display scaling. The manifest XML is in the binary, but not as a loadable resource:
`cua-driver.rc` declares the type as the identifier `RT_MANIFEST`, which the resource
compiler emits as a *custom string-named type*. The loader only applies manifests under
integer type `24`, ID `1` — so the daemon still starts **DPI-unaware** and the offset
bug #1821 targeted is presumably still present on the raw-injection paths.

## Evidence (installed 0.5.2, Windows 11 build 26200, 3840×2160 @ 125%)

- `GetProcessDpiAwareness` on the running `cua-driver.exe` → `0` (DPI_UNAWARE).
- `get_screen_size` → `3072x1728 points @ 1x` (virtualized; PMv2 would report 3840×2160 @ 1.25x).
- Resource enumeration shows one type: the string `"RT_MANIFEST"`. No integer type 24 / ID 1.
- Pixel clicks on UIA-exposed elements still land correctly (UIA hit-test + Invoke is
  coordinate-space agnostic), which masks the regression in everyday use.

## Root cause and fix

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/cua-driver.rc`:

```rc
1 RT_MANIFEST "cua-driver.manifest"   // RT_MANIFEST is not an .rc keyword
1 24 "cua-driver.manifest"            // fix: 24 = RT_MANIFEST
```

## Must fix together: capture paths double-scale once PMv2 is active

The same PR added `GetDpiForWindow / 96` scaling to capture paths in
`platform-windows/src/capture.rs`, premised on `GetWindowRect` / `GetSystemMetrics`
returning logical pixels under PMv2. Per Microsoft docs it's the opposite: PMv2 processes
get **physical** pixels (virtualization only applies to unaware/system-aware processes).
Today the code accidentally runs in the unaware regime it assumes; once the manifest
loads, three spots multiply physical coordinates by `DPI / 96` again:

1. `screenshot_via_screen_region` (~139–150): BitBlt source rect shifted/oversized by
   25% — wrong screen region for UWP / WinUI3 / DirectComposition targets.
2. `screenshot_window_bytes_with_occlusion_unsafe` (~288–303): buffer 25% too large;
   only masked while the unscaled `DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS` crop (~380–397) passes
   its bounds check.
3. `screenshot_display_bytes` (~478–489): same pattern via `GetDpiForSystem()`.

The click-side transform (`bitmap_to_screen` in `tools/impl_.rs`, no scaling) is correct
under PMv2 — fixing the manifest alone would break captures while clicks keep working.

## Verification (at 125% scaling)

- `get_screen_size` must report physical resolution @ 1.25x; `GetProcessDpiAwareness` → 2.
- With both fixes: capturing a UWP app (e.g. Calculator) positioned away from (0,0)
  must show the window, not a region shifted by ~25% of the window origin.

Side note: `--version` / `get_config` still report `0.5.1` on the 0.5.2 release.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): Windows zoom uses resized-image coordinates as native capture coordinates
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `zoom` documents `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, and `y2` as coordinates in the same pixel space as the screenshot returned by `get_window_state`. If `max_image_dimension` downscales that screenshot, callers therefore pass resized-image coordinates.

The implementation appears to apply those values directly to a fresh native-resolution screenshot. When downscaling is active, `zoom` crops the wrong region. The stored zoom context is then based on that wrong crop, so later `click(..., from_zoom=true)` calls are translated to the wrong window position.

## Reproduction

Tested locally on Windows with `cua-driver` reporting version `0.5.1` (but it is 0.5.2!).

1. Set `max_image_dimension` low enough to force downscaling, for example `400`.
2. Open a large window and call `get_window_state(..., capture_mode: vision)`.
3. Use a region from the returned downscaled screenshot, for example `x1=300, y1=0, x2=395, y2=70` on a 400 px wide screenshot.
4. Call `zoom` with that region.

In my repro, `get_window_state` returned a 400 px wide image while a native capture of the same window was 1981 px wide. The zoom for `x=300..395` should therefore have cropped roughly `x=1486..1956` in native pixels. Instead, the returned zoom image matched a native crop at `x=300..395`.

## Why this seems to happen

`get_window_state` records a resize ratio for the pid, and normal pixel clicks use it before converting screenshot coordinates to screen coordinates.

`ZoomTool::invoke` captures a new native-resolution screenshot and passes the caller's coordinates straight into the crop function:

```rust
let png = crate::capture::screenshot_window_bytes(hwnd)?;
cursor_overlay::capture_utils::crop_png_to_jpeg(&png, x1, y1, x2, y2, 500)
```

That means the documented resized-image coordinate space is skipped for `zoom`.

## Expected behavior

`zoom` should interpret `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, and `y2` in the screenshot coordinate space returned by the last `get_window_state` call, as documented.

A likely fix is to multiply the region coordinates by the stored resize ratio for the pid before cropping the native screenshot. The 500 px max-width validation should still apply to the caller-provided resized-image width.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): a single BuildUpdatedCache failure (0x80004005) returns elements=0 - no retry, no partial tree
body:
## Summary

When the UIA bulk cache build fails for a window, `get_window_state` returns an empty tree (`elements=0`) instead of a partial result. One misbehaving accessibility provider in the target app takes down the entire snapshot, which makes all `element_index`-based tools (click, type_text, ...) unusable for that window — the agent is forced to fall back to pixel clicks.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (build 26200), 125% display scaling
- cua-driver-rs 0.5.2 (also observed on 0.5.1)

## Symptom

```
window_id=2884078 pid=13116 elements=0
BuildUpdatedCache failed: Unbekannter Fehler (0x80004005)
```

The same `get_window_state` call returned 14 elements moments earlier. The failure surfaced while automating an app whose automation peers are replaced at runtime (a rich-text control that rebuilds its document tree on load). Any target with transient/unstable UIA providers can trigger it — the trigger isn't specific to one app. On 0.5.2 the error is rarer but still occurs (e.g. right after Ctrl+A in such a control).

## Where it happens

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs` — the tree walk does a single `BuildUpdatedCache(TreeScope_Subtree)` on the window root and hard-fails on any error:

```rust
let root_elem = match uncached.BuildUpdatedCache(&cache_req) {
    Ok(e) => e,
    Err(e) => return UiaTreeResult {
        tree_markdown: format!("BuildUpdatedCache failed: {e}"),
        nodes: Vec::new(),
    },
};
```

There is no retry and no fallback walk, so a transient `E_FAIL` from one provider yields a total outage for the whole window. (A similar resilience problem was already solved for SAL/VCL windows via the MSAA walker fallback — but that path is class-name-gated and doesn't help here.)

## Why it matters

`element_index` interaction is the most reliable mode the driver offers (works on background windows, exact hits). Losing the whole tree because one subtree is momentarily broken degrades the agent to pixel coordinates, which is precisely the mode with the weakest guarantees.

## Suggested improvements

1. **Retry with a short backoff** — the error is often transient (a second call right after frequently succeeds).
2. **Partial-tree fallback** — if the bulk Subtree cache build fails, fall back to a per-node walk (e.g. `ControlViewWalker` with per-element property reads), skipping nodes that error, and return `elements=N` with a warning instead of `elements=0`.
3. **Better diagnostics** — include which stage failed (root cache build vs. a specific child) so callers can tell a dead provider from a transient hiccup.

## Reproduction

The failure needs a UIA provider that errors mid-walk, which is timing-dependent in real apps. Two practical options:

1. **Real-world shape:** any control that swaps out its automation subtree while the snapshot is taken — e.g. a rich-text editor that rebuilds its document model on load, or a virtualized list re-realizing items. Call `get_window_state` repeatedly while the subtree is being replaced.
2. **Deterministic harness:** a small test app hosting a custom `IRawElementProviderFragment` that returns `E_FAIL` from one child's property fetch reproduces the total outage deterministically — and would double as a regression test for the partial-tree fallback.

title: fix: extend daemon proxy read timeout
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1864.

This PR fixes the MCP -> daemon proxy timeout described in the issue. It does not make `get_window_state` smaller or bypass AX traversal; it makes the daemon transport wait long enough for legitimate tool execution and return a clearer transport timeout if the daemon still does not respond.

## Issue Behavior Addressed

The issue reports that this path can fail:

```text
MCP client -> cua-driver mcp stdio server -> cua-driver serve daemon over Unix socket -> get_window_state
```

The same `get_window_state` operation can look healthy through `cua-driver call`, while the MCP proxy path fails with:

```text
Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
```

The root cause fixed here is the proxy client read timeout: `send_request` used a hardcoded 10-second socket read timeout. Slow but valid daemon calls, especially `get_window_state`, could exceed that transport timeout before the tool returned its own result or timeout. On macOS, that timed-out socket read appears as `WouldBlock` / `EAGAIN` / os error 35.

## What Changed

- Replaced the inline daemon socket timeout with named daemon write/read timeout constants.
- Raised the daemon read timeout from 10 seconds to 60 seconds.
- Kept the write timeout short at 5 seconds.
- Mapped `WouldBlock` / `TimedOut` while reading the daemon response into a clear error:

```text
daemon timed out waiting for response after 60s
```

The 60-second transport budget is intentionally above the macOS `get_window_state` AX walk timeout of 30 seconds, leaving room for screenshot capture, resizing/encoding or `screenshot_out_file`, and JSON response serialization.

This PR intentionally does not blindly retry on `EAGAIN`. In this code path, `EAGAIN` is the socket read timeout firing, not a transient readiness event from a nonblocking socket loop. Retrying would hide the timeout policy instead of fixing the proxy deadline.

## Relation To The Issue's Upstream Questions

Resolved by this PR:

- `os error 35` / `EAGAIN` in the MCP -> daemon proxy no longer leaks as the primary failure for slow-but-valid daemon responses below the transport budget.
- The proxy now waits longer than the old 10-second transport timeout and longer than the macOS `get_window_state` AX timeout.
- If the daemon still does not respond inside the transport budget, the user gets a daemon timeout message instead of raw macOS `EAGAIN`.

Not changed by this PR and still follow-up scope:

- Whether `screenshot_out_file` should be the recommended long-term payload-size strategy.
- Whether large screenshot payloads should default to files or be chunked.
- Whether Apple Notes empty/unusable AX trees are a known platform limitation or need an alternate traversal path.
- Coordinate click semantics on HiDPI displays, including whether coordinate click should accept `window_id` for multi-window disambiguation.
- Idle CPU around 52-54% in the driver process.
- Whether the removed `screenshot` tool is intentionally replaced by `get_window_state(capture_mode=vision)`.

`screenshot_out_file` remains useful as an optional payload-size mitigation, but it is not the primary fix for this bug. The transport timeout/backpressure behavior is the bug addressed here.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cua-driver daemon_response_read_tests`
- `git diff --check`
- local `install-local.sh` rebuild and CuaDriver daemon restart
- forced MCP proxy reproduction with a fake daemon delaying `get_window_state` for 12 seconds; the call succeeds instead of failing at the old ~10-second transport timeout

title: fix(computer-server): serve MCP at both /mcp and /mcp/
body:
## Problem

The MCP app is mounted at `/mcp` with its internal route at `/`, and the outer FastAPI app sets `redirect_slashes=False`. Starlette's `Mount` only matches `/mcp/...`, so a bare `POST /mcp` resolves to inner path `""` → 404, with no 307 rescue. Most MCP clients (claude.ai connectors included) POST to the bare path — for them the MCP server is unreachable even though `/status` advertises the `mcp` feature and the StreamableHTTP session manager is running.

Observed live on a Windows KubeVirt guest running `cua-computer-server`: `POST /mcp` → `404 {"detail":"Not Found"}` while `POST /mcp/` → `200` + `Mcp-Session-Id` from the same process.

## Fix

A small pure-ASGI middleware rewrites bare `/mcp` → `/mcp/` before routing, so both literal forms answer directly:

- **rewrite, not redirect** — POSTed initialize bodies and SSE streams survive; some MCP clients don't follow 307s on POST
- **plain ASGI, not `BaseHTTPMiddleware`** — no response buffering on the MCP event stream
- all other paths pass through untouched

Includes standalone unit tests for the shim (no server deps needed, following the existing skip-on-missing-import style).

body:
### Summary

The cua "computer-server" (the daemon that exposes desktop/computer control to a cua agent: run command, read/write files, take screenshots, drive keyboard/mouse, open PTY shells) listens on `0.0.0.0` by default and performs no authentication when the `CONTAINER_NAME` environment variable is unset. `CONTAINER_NAME` is set only in the hosted/cloud container deployment; when a user runs the server locally or standalone (the documented local path, and the default for the pip-installed server and local VM images), `Server.auth()` returns `True` for every request ("local development mode"). Combined with the default `--host 0.0.0.0` bind, this means any client that can reach TCP port 8000, an attacker on the same LAN, a co-located container, or (because there is no Origin/Host validation) a malicious web page the operator visits, can without credentials execute arbitrary shell commands (`run_command` -> `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell`), read and write arbitrary files (`read_text`/`write_text`/`read_bytes`/`write_bytes`, no path containment), and open an interactive PTY shell. An opt-in fail-closed switch exists (`UNAVAILABLE_WITHOUT_CONTAINER_NAME`) but defaults off for backwards compatibility.

### Details

Bind defaults to all interfaces (`libs/python/computer-server/computer_server/cli.py` and `main.py`):

```python
# cli.py
parser.add_argument("--host", default="0.0.0.0", help="Host to bind the server to (default: 0.0.0.0)")
...
# main.py (module entry)
uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
```

Authentication is skipped entirely when `CONTAINER_NAME` is unset (`main.py`, `Server.auth`):

```python
self.container_name = os.environ.get("CONTAINER_NAME")
...
async def auth(self, container_name: str, api_key: str) -> bool:
    # If no CONTAINER_NAME is set, always allow access (local development)
    if not self.container_name:
        logger.info("No CONTAINER_NAME set in environment. Allowing access (local development mode)")
        return True                              # <-- no token checked
    if container_name != self.container_name:
        return False
    # ... only here is the api_key verified against the TryCUA API
```

Every request path applies the same gate. The HTTP `/cmd` handler (`main.py`):

```python
server_container_name = os.environ.get("CONTAINER_NAME")
if server_container_name:
    # ... require container_name + api_key, authenticate ...
else:
    pass                                         # CONTAINER_NAME unset -> no auth, proceed to execute
```

The WebSocket `/ws` handler and the `/pty*` endpoints behave identically (`_require_auth` returns early when `CONTAINER_NAME` is unset). The dispatched actions are the full computer-control set; the command action runs a shell (`handlers/base.py`):

```python
async def run_command(self, command: str, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    ...
    process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(   # attacker-controlled `command`, shell parsing
        command, stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE)
```

and the file actions have no path containment (`handlers/generic.py`):

```python
async def read_text(self, path: str):
    return {"success": True, "content": resolve_path(path).read_text()}   # any path
async def write_text(self, path: str, content: str):
    ...                                                                    # any path
```

`resolve_path` only does `Path(path).expanduser().resolve()`, so `/etc/shadow`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/root/.aws/credentials`, etc. are readable and `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` is writable. The status/commands endpoints (`GET /status`, `GET /commands`) are also unauthenticated and enumerate the full action set.

The fail-closed middleware that would reject requests when `CONTAINER_NAME` is unset is gated behind `UNAVAILABLE_WITHOUT_CONTAINER_NAME`, which is off by default ("preserves the original local development mode behavior for backwards compatibility").

### PoC
(available upon request)

### Impact

In the default local/standalone configuration the computer-server is an unauthenticated remote-code-execution and arbitrary file read/write service on all network interfaces. Any LAN attacker, co-located container, or malicious web page (no Origin/Host validation) obtains a shell on the machine running the server, with no credentials and no user interaction. When the server runs in "host" mode or in a VM with shared folders, this is code execution on the operator's real environment and disclosure of its secrets. Fix: bind `127.0.0.1` by default with an explicit opt-in to expose; make authentication mandatory (fail closed) rather than allow-all when `CONTAINER_NAME` is unset, e.g. default `UNAVAILABLE_WITHOUT_CONTAINER_NAME` to true or require a locally generated token; add an Origin/Host allowlist on the HTTP and WebSocket endpoints; and pass `run_command` through a non-shell exec where possible.

title: cua-driver 0.5.3 missing com.apple.security.device.screen-capture entitlement on macOS 15
body:
## Problem

cua-driver 0.5.3 vision capture returns 0x0 screenshots on macOS 15 Sequoia despite:
- Binary being properly signed with Developer ID (Cua AI, Inc.)
- TCC Screen Recording permission granted
- ScreenCaptureKit code path existing in the binary

## Root Cause

The binary is signed with a Developer ID but **lacks the `com.apple.security.device.screen-capture` entitlement**. On macOS 15, ScreenCaptureKit requires both:
1. A valid Developer ID signature (✅ present)
2. The `com.apple.security.device.screen-capture` entitlement (❌ missing)

Without the entitlement, `SCStream::start_capture` fails with "Missing entitlements" even though TCC is granted.

## Verification

```
$ codesign -d --entitlements - /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver
# No entitlements output
```

## Fix

Add `com.apple.security.device.screen-capture` to the entitlements in the build/release pipeline.

## Impact

All macOS 15 users cannot use vision capture mode. SOM/AX tree works but screenshots are 0x0.

## References

- Related: #1862 (0x0 screenshots)

title: cua-driver `scroll` tool: prefer AXScrollUpByPage AX action over arrow-key synthesis when element exposes it (Catalyst regression)
body:
## Summary

The `cua-driver` Swift backend's `scroll` tool synthesizes arrow-key `AXPostKeyboardEvent` keystrokes to the focused element. This works on many AppKit apps but **silently no-ops on Catalyst apps that drop their up/down-arrow key handling on the list view while still exposing the AX scroll action** — specifically WhatsApp Desktop for Mac after v26.22.

The fix is to prefer `AXUIElementPerformAction(elem, "AXScrollUpByPage" / "AXScrollDownByPage")` when the target element advertises the action in its `AXUIElementCopyActionNames`, and only fall back to keystroke synthesis when the action is absent.

## Reproduction

- macOS 26.5.1 build 25F80, Apple silicon M4
- WhatsApp Desktop 26.22.77 (Mac App Store distribution)
- cua-driver Swift v0.2.0 (bundle `com.trycua.driver`, build May 17)
- Persistent daemon: `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve`
- Accessibility + Screen Recording granted to CuaDriver.app
- WhatsApp open on a Followed channel; chat scrolled into view
- `get_window_state` tree shows the message list as:
  ```
  [60] AXGroup id=ChatMessagesTableView actions=[AXScrollToVisible, AXCancel, AXScrollUpByPage, AXShowMenu]
  ```

Call:
```
cua-driver call scroll '{"pid":<wa_pid>,"window_id":<wid>,"element_index":60,"direction":"up","amount":3}'
```

Output (looped many times):
```
✅ Scrolled pid <wa_pid> up via 3× up keystroke(s) (target [60] AXGroup).
```

Observed:
- No visual scroll of the message list
- WhatsApp lazy-downloads channel media on view; no new media files appeared after 100+ bursts → empirical proof scroll didn't happen
- The same call pattern worked on WhatsApp 26.18.x earlier

## Root cause

WhatsApp 26.18.x bound the up-arrow key to scroll the channel message list — `AXPostKeyboardEvent` worked. From ~26.19 onward the key binding was dropped, but the `AXScrollUpByPage` AX action remained on the same element. The `scroll` tool keeps sending a keystroke that no longer maps to a list-scroll action in this Catalyst app.

## Validated fix

PyObjC, direct AX action invocation, same daemon and TCC grants:

```python
from ApplicationServices import (
    AXUIElementCreateApplication, AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue,
    AXUIElementCopyActionNames, AXUIElementPerformAction,
    kAXChildrenAttribute, kAXIdentifierAttribute,
)
app = AXUIElementCreateApplication(wa_pid)
# walk children for the AXGroup with id=ChatMessagesTableView
# (any element whose AXUIElementCopyActionNames includes AXScrollUpByPage)
AXUIElementPerformAction(target, "AXScrollUpByPage")
```

Result on the same WhatsApp window: visible scroll, channel media downloads triggered, list advances through history.

## Proposed change

In the Swift `scroll` implementation, after resolving the target element by `element_index`:

1. Query `AXUIElementCopyActionNames(target, &actions)`.
2. Map the requested `direction` to its AX action name:
   - `up` → `AXScrollUpByPage`
   - `down` → `AXScrollDownByPage`
   - (left/right similarly via `AXScrollLeftByPage` / `AXScrollRightByPage` where applicable)
3. If the action is present in `actions`, call `AXUIElementPerformAction(target, actionName)` once per `amount` unit.
4. Otherwise, fall back to the current keystroke synthesis path.

This makes `scroll` durable against Catalyst apps that gate key handling without removing the AX action contract — which is the correct primitive macOS itself uses when an accessibility client (or VoiceOver, or scroll-wheel-via-AX) drives the list.

## Notes

- Same fix applies to the Rust backend (cua-driver-rs).
- The `scroll` tool's success message currently reports `via N× up keystroke(s)` even when nothing scrolls; this is the only signal a caller gets that the synth might have been absorbed. Switching to the AX action path on capable elements would remove the silent-failure mode.
- Happy to send a PR if useful — let me know the preferred shape (drop-in inside `scroll`, or new `scroll_via_action` tool with `scroll` keeping current behavior).

title: fix(computer-server): tolerate any Accept header on /mcp (claude.ai connector)
body:
## Problem

claude.ai's MCP connector fails to connect to the computer-server's `/mcp`
endpoint with `Your account was authorized, but ... returned an error when
connecting`. Hitting `/mcp` returns:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"server-error","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream"}}
```

The MCP Python SDK's StreamableHTTP transport rejects a request unless its
`Accept` header advertises **both** `application/json` and `text/event-stream`
(POST path), or `text/event-stream` (GET SSE path). Some MCP clients (incl.
claude.ai's connector) don't send both, so the handshake POST is rejected
before reaching any tool. supergateway-fronted servers (e.g. cua-driver) are
lenient here and work; the FastMCP-native computer-server does not.

This is distinct from the bare-`/mcp` 404 fixed in #1887 — that fix is intact.

## Fix

Add `McpAcceptHeaderShim`, a pure-ASGI middleware scoped to `/mcp` that
normalizes the inbound `Accept` header to `application/json, text/event-stream`.
It rewrites only the **request** header — it does not set `json_response` or
touch any response semantics, so SSE-vs-JSON negotiation and existing clients
(Claude Code, SDK) are unaffected. Mounted inside the existing
`McpBarePathRewrite` (kept intact); middleware ordering documented in-code.

`json_response=True` was deliberately *not* used: it only relaxes the POST path
(the GET SSE path still hard-requires `text/event-stream`) and would change
response framing for other clients.

## Tests

- `tests/test_server.py::TestMcpAcceptHeaderShim` — normalizes json-only Accept
  on `/mcp`, `/mcp/`, `/mcp/...`; adds a missing Accept; leaves non-mcp paths
  (`/status`, `/`, `/mcpx`, `/ws`) untouched.
- Verified by in-process integration test against the real FastMCP/MCP SDK
  (fastmcp 2.14.x): json-only `Accept` POST `initialize` returns `406 / -32600`
  **without** the shim and `200 + mcp-session-id` **with** it, on both `/mcp`
  and `/mcp/`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added HTTP Accept header normalization for MCP-routed requests to improve compatibility with MCP StreamableHTTP transports and various client implementations.

* **Tests**
  * Added comprehensive test coverage for MCP HTTP Accept header normalization.

title: fix(computer-server): stop exposing an unauthenticated server to the network by default (#1892)
body:
…network by default (#1892)

By default the server bound 0.0.0.0 with auth OFF whenever CONTAINER_NAME wasn't set (local mode). So anyone on your LAN — or any website you happened to visit — could run shell commands, read/write files, and open a PTY shell.

Now,
Local mode now binds 127.0.0.1
If you really want a public --host in local mode, you now have to opt in with CUA_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 Added an Origin check on /ws, /cmd and /pty so a random web page can't drive your local server.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Server now enforces local-only binding by default in local mode, preventing accidental exposure of the unauthenticated service on public interfaces. Override available via environment variable.
  * Added cross-site origin validation for sensitive API endpoints to block malicious cross-site browser requests.

* **Tests**
  * Added comprehensive test coverage for secure binding and origin validation.

title: feat(cua-bench): add cua-bench-kicad dataset + monorepo registry dump
body:
Adds the **cua-bench-kicad** dataset (25 expert-authored KiCad schematic-editing tasks, EDA) and fixes the registry-dump script to target this monorepo instead of the deprecated `cua-bench-registry` repo.

title: Please add an option (or default behavior) for `cua-driver` to **bake the virtual/agent mouse cursor into the PNG pixels returned by `screenshot` / `get_window_state`**, instead of only drawing it as a separate overlay window.
body:
## Why this matters

Most agents built on Computer-Use interfaces follow a fixed observation–action pattern:

1. Take a screenshot.
2. Decide where to click and emit a `click` / `move_cursor`.
3. Take another screenshot.
4. Compare the two frames to verify the cursor landed where intended, or to localize the cursor and re-target a click.

Step 4 only works if the **cursor arrow is visible in the returned PNG**. Right now it is not, in the common case.

## Current behavior

The agent cursor is rendered as a separate top-most overlay window (`platform-{windows,macos,linux}/overlay.rs` / `cursor-overlay` crate). That works for the user's eyes on the full virtual screen, but:

- `get_window_state` / window-specific captures go through **WGC on Windows** or **PrintWindow on macOS**, which only render the target window's own surface. The overlay is a different window, so it never appears in the PNG. (#1882 explicitly calls this out: *"the overlay is useless for the obvious calibration workflow 'move cursor to (x, y), take a window screenshot, check where it landed'"*.)
- The full-screen `BitBlt` fallback *does* include the overlay, so the capability is half-implemented and inconsistent between capture paths.
- The overlay also has its own lifecycle / z-order / render-loop bugs that have nothing to do with what the agent actually sees in the frame (#1819, #1806, #1807, #1800).

Net effect: agents either skip the self-correction step, or they burn an extra full-screen `BitBlt` capture per move to find the cursor, which is slow and defeats the point of window-scoped captures.

## Proposed behavior

After a `screenshot` / `get_window_state` call, the returned PNG should include the virtual/agent cursor at its last known `(x, y)` for the active session — composited into the image pixels themselves, independent of any overlay window.

Sketch of the contract:

- A new tool option (e.g. `embed_agent_cursor: bool`, defaulting to `true` when `set_agent_cursor_*` is enabled) that the driver applies at capture time.
- On the capture side: query the session's cursor state (`get_agent_cursor_state` already returns `(x, y)`, color, enabled) and draw a standard OS-shaped arrow (or a configurable color/shape) into the raw framebuffer *before* any optional downscale, so the cursor is also correct on zoomed-in views.
- Works the same on full-screen and window-specific captures, removing the WGC / PrintWindow gap.
- Does not change the existing overlay window — users who want the on-screen visual cue keep it; agents that need the in-image reference get it from the PNG.

This is purely an additive change to the capture pipeline; it does not require changes to the overlay renderer or the click/move pipeline.

## Acceptance criteria

- Calling `get_window_state` for a window whose center has the agent cursor returns a PNG where the cursor arrow is visible at the expected `(x, y)`, on Windows / macOS / Linux.
- Two consecutive `get_window_state` calls before and after `move_cursor(…)` show the cursor arrow at the new position in the second PNG, so a downstream agent can diff the two frames and recover the move deltas.
- With `embed_agent_cursor: false` (or equivalent), behavior matches today (no in-frame cursor).
- The CPU / latency cost on the capture path is bounded (no per-frame full-screen repaint of the overlay renderer just to bake the cursor in).

## Related issues

- #1882 — cursor not visible in window captures; this FR is the implementation half of the gap that issue documents.
- #1819 — Linux/X11 overlay swallows clicks (orthogonal bug; this FR does not require fixing it, but renders it less critical for headless agent use).
- #1806, #1807, #1800 — overlay render / z-order / lifecycle bugs; again orthogonal, but they reinforce the case for not relying on the overlay window as the only cursor signal.

## Environment

- `cua-driver-rs` 0.5.2 (also relevant on the older Python `cua-driver` 0.5.x line).
- Windows 11 / macOS 15 / X11 Linux — same need on all three platforms.

## Why not just use full-screen `BitBlt`?

It already includes the overlay, but it is much more expensive than a window-scoped capture and it loses per-window context (the very thing that makes `get_window_state` useful for targeting). Compositing into the framebuffer is the cheap, correct fix.

title: feat(cua-driver): add stable health_report MCP tool
body:
## Motivation

Downstream consumers (Hermes Agent and similar) want an end-to-end health check for `cua-driver` but should not have to know `cua-driver` internals: specific MCP tool names, TCC field names, bundle IDs, per-platform check matrix. Today they stitch together `check_permissions`, `doctor`, version probes, bundle-attribution checks, and a screenshot smoke test — which means every diagnostic refactor inside `cua-driver` breaks them.

The right shape is for `cua-driver` to own the health model entirely and expose it as one stable MCP tool. Consumers stay thin. `cua-driver` evolves freely.

This PR adds that tool: `health_report`.

## Schema (stable contract, `schema_version: "1"`)

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "platform": "darwin" | "win32" | "linux",
  "driver_version": "<semver>",
  "overall": "ok" | "degraded" | "failed",
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "binary_version" | "platform_supported" | "tcc_accessibility" | "tcc_screen_recording" | "bundle_identity" | "ax_capability" | "screen_capture_capability" | "session_active",
      "status": "pass" | "fail" | "skip",
      "message": "<one-line summary, always present>",
      "hint": "<remediation step — present when status == fail>",
      "data": { /* check-specific structured data — optional */ }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `overall` rules

- `ok` — every non-skipped check passes
- `degraded` — at least one non-core check fails (binary still usable)
- `failed` — any core check fails (`binary_version`, `platform_supported`, `session_active`)

### Input (all optional)

```json
{
  "include": ["<check_name>", ...],
  "skip":    ["<check_name>", ...]
}
```

Both use canonical check names from the output enum. If both are given, `include` wins. Unknown names in `include` are silently ignored (forward-compat — a consumer may know names from a newer driver).

## Stability commitment

`schema_version: "1"` is the contract. Future breaking changes go to `"2"`.

**Non-breaking under v1**: adding new check names. Consumers must tolerate unknown check names.
**Breaking (would bump to v2)**: removing fields, renaming canonical check names, changing `status` / `overall` enum values, changing JSON-key casing.

## What runs

macOS check matrix (everything in this PR):
- `binary_version` — always pass; surfaces `CuaDriverCore.version`.
- `platform_supported` — pass with `data.os_version`, `data.architecture`.
- `session_active` — pass by construction.
- `bundle_identity` — pass iff `CFBundleIdentifier == com.trycua.driver`; fails with `data.bundle_identifier` populated for downstream attribution-drift detection.
- `tcc_accessibility` — reuses `Permissions.currentStatus()`.
- `tcc_screen_recording` — reuses `Permissions.currentStatus()`.
- `ax_capability` — `AXIsProcessTrusted()` probe.
- `screen_capture_capability` — live `SCShareableContent.excludingDesktopWindows` probe with `data.display_count`. Nothing hits disk. No stream is started.

TCC checks delegate to `Permissions.currentStatus()` — no duplication.

## Test strategy

- **Unit (`HealthReportTests`, 15 tests)** — registry advertisement, schema_version commitment in tool description, `selectChecks`/`computeOverall` truth tables, `parseStringSet` edge cases, end-to-end Codable round-trip asserting documented top-level + per-check keys, `skip` filter honored, and the documented `bundle_identity` fail-mode shape (status=fail + hint + data.bundle_identifier).
- **Integration (`test_health_report_mcp.py`, 6 tests)** — spawns the real `cua-driver mcp` stdio server, performs JSON-RPC handshake, asserts `tools/list` advertises `health_report`, calls it with no args / `skip` filter / `include` filter, validates the schema shape, asserts `isError` is never set, and exercises the documented fail mode end-to-end.
- Full Swift test suite (`swift test`) — 51 tests, all green.

## Scope notes — Rust follow-up

`libs/cua-driver-rs` (and the `libs/cua-driver/rust` workspace) exists with macOS + Windows + Linux ports. Adding `health_report` there means landing it in three `platform-*` crates plus extending the parity suite — too much for one pass. **Filing as a follow-up.** Swift is shipped here; the schema contract above will drive the Rust port verbatim.

## Constraints honored

- No existing MCP tool schemas were modified — new tool only.
- No external dependencies added.
- No code-signing / entitlements / notarization changes.
- All tests pass on the branch.

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): make Cargo.toml the source of truth for release bumps
body:
## What

Stop the cua-driver-rs release version from drifting, so a bump can never cut a
release at the wrong version again.

## Why (root cause behind #1870, and the reason the 0.5.x re-release needed care)

`release-bump-version` runs `bump2version` off
`libs/cua-driver/rust/.bumpversion.cfg`, which keeps a **duplicate**
`current_version`. That copy had drifted badly:

```
.bumpversion.cfg current_version = 0.4.3
Cargo.toml       version          = 0.5.3
```

`bump2version` bumps from `current_version` and search-replaces
`version = "{current_version}"` in `Cargo.toml`. With the cfg at 0.4.3, a patch
bump would compute `0.4.4` (a downgrade tag) and the `version = "0.4.3"` search
would miss `0.5.3` entirely — so `Cargo.toml` stays put and the built binary
reports a stale version. That is the 0.5.2 stale-binary failure mode (#1870).
PR #1854 tried to fix this by setting the cfg to `0.5.1`, but that value was
already stale too — it just moves the drift.

## Fix (make it impossible to recur)

1. Sync `.bumpversion.cfg` `current_version` to `0.5.3` (matches `Cargo.toml`).
2. Add a **reconcile step** to `release-bump-version.yml` (gated on
   `service == cua-driver-rs`) that rewrites `current_version` from `Cargo.toml`
   **before** bump2version reads it — for both the dry-run tag-clean and the
   real bump. `Cargo.toml` is now the single source of truth, so the cfg can
   never start a bump from a stale base again no matter how it drifts. It emits
   a `::warning::` when it has to correct, so silent drift stays visible.

## Verification

- `bump2version --dry-run` from base `0.5.3` -> `new_version=0.5.4`, tag
  `cua-driver-rs-v0.5.4`.
- Reconcile logic self-heals a simulated `0.4.3` drift back to `0.5.3` against
  the real `Cargo.toml`.

## Notes

- Release-infra only; no driver code or user-facing behavior change, so no
  changelog entry.
- **Supersedes #1854** — recommend closing it.
- Pairs with #1906 (macOS screen-capture entitlement); both need to be on
  `main` before the next `release-bump-version` cuts 0.5.4 cleanly.

title: feat(cua-driver): add stable health_report MCP tool for end-to-end driver diagnostics
body:
## Summary

Adds a single-call `health_report` MCP tool to cua-driver so downstream consumers (Hermes Agent's `hermes computer-use doctor`, tracked at NousResearch/hermes-agent#47065) can ship one stable diagnostic call without knowing cua-driver internals — specific MCP tool names, TCC field names, bundle IDs, per-platform check matrix. cua-driver owns the health model entirely; consumers stay thin and the driver evolves freely.

This is the **canonical Rust port** of the now-closed Swift PR #1905. A previous agent landed that work in the **deprecated** `swift/` tree by mistake; this lands the same schema + test contract in the canonical Rust workspace at `libs/cua-driver/rust/`. The schema is byte-for-byte identical to the Swift PR's contract; the implementation is fresh against the Rust crates.

## Schema (stable contract — schema_version="1")

Input — all optional. `include` wins over `skip`:

```json
{
  "include": ["<check_name>", ...],
  "skip":    ["<check_name>", ...]
}
```

Output:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "platform": "darwin" | "win32" | "linux",
  "driver_version": "<semver>",
  "overall": "ok" | "degraded" | "failed",
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "binary_version" | "platform_supported" | "tcc_accessibility" |
              "tcc_screen_recording" | "bundle_identity" | "ax_capability" |
              "screen_capture_capability" | "session_active",
      "status": "pass" | "fail" | "skip",
      "message": "<one-line summary, always present>",
      "hint": "<remediation step — present when status == fail>",
      "data": { /* check-specific structured data — optional */ }
    }
  ]
}
```

`overall` rollup:
- `ok` — every check passes or is intentionally skipped
- `degraded` — at least one non-core check fails (binary still usable)
- `failed` — any core check fails (`binary_version`, `platform_supported`, `session_active`)

**Stability**: `schema_version="1"` is the commitment. Future breaking changes go to `"2"`. Adding new check names under the same `schema_version` is non-breaking; consumers must tolerate unknown check names. `health_report` NEVER itself sets `isError` — consumers must be able to tell "tool broken" from "driver degraded".

## Architecture

| Layer | Location | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-platform skeleton | `cua-driver-core/src/health_report.rs` | `Report` / `CheckEntry` / `CheckStatus` / `CheckData` types; `HealthCheckProvider` trait; `select_checks` / `compute_overall` / `parse_string_set` filter+rollup logic; `HealthReportTool` MCP wrapper + schema text |
| macOS provider | `platform-macos/src/tools/health_report.rs` | TCC reuse via existing `permissions::status` plumbing (NO duplication); live `SCShareableContent` probe for `screen_capture_capability`; `CFBundleGetMainBundle` for runtime `CFBundleIdentifier` |
| Windows provider | `platform-windows/src/health_report.rs` | `ax_capability` via existing `diagnostics::ui_automation_available`; `screen_capture_capability` via `D3D11CreateDevice` probe; TCC + bundle entries surface as `skip("not applicable on Windows")` |
| Linux provider | `platform-linux/src/health_report.rs` | `ax_capability` + `screen_capture_capability` share an X11 connect probe; TCC + bundle entries surface as `skip("not applicable on Linux")` |

Per-platform check matrix:
- **macOS**: `binary_version`, `platform_supported`, `session_active`, `bundle_identity`, `tcc_accessibility`, `tcc_screen_recording`, `ax_capability`, `screen_capture_capability` — all 8 active
- **Windows**: same 8 names emitted; `tcc_*` and `bundle_identity` emit `status: "skip"` with `message: "not applicable on Windows"` (the documented contract for cross-platform consumers)
- **Linux**: same 8 names emitted; `tcc_*` and `bundle_identity` emit `status: "skip"` with `message: "not applicable on Linux"`

The full set of canonical check names always appears on every platform so cross-platform consumers see a complete map.

## Test strategy

Mirrors the Swift PR's test contracts. PARITY.md expectations: same wire format and `tools/list` advertisement across darwin / win32 / linux.

| Crate | Tests | What they cover |
|---|---:|---|
| `cua-driver-core` | 16 | `select_checks` (include-wins, skip filter, empty, unknown-name forward compat); `compute_overall` (all-pass, all-skip, non-core fail → degraded, core fail → failed); `parse_string_set` (non-string items, scalars, nil); dispatcher round-trip (no-args schema shape, skip filter end-to-end, include filter end-to-end, all-fail never sets isError); `schema_version="1"` description commitment |
| `platform-macos` | 5 | `binary_version` always passes; `platform_supported` carries os+arch data; `session_active` passes; `bundle_identity` documented fail-mode fixture (the Rust test binary's bundle is not `com.trycua.driver`, so the canonical attribution-drift fail mode reproduces without mocking); full-run dispatcher emits the macOS check set in declared order |
| `platform-windows` | 4 | `binary_version` passes; `session_active` passes; `tcc_*` + `bundle_identity` skip with canonical message; full-run dispatcher emits the Windows check set in order with TCC/bundle skipped |
| `platform-linux` | 4 | Same coverage as Windows for the Linux platform |
| `tests/integration/test_health_report_mcp.py` | 6 | Real stdio MCP server: `tools/list` advertises `health_report` + `schema_version` in description; no-args call returns documented top-level keys + per-check keys; skip filter honored; include filter narrows to single check; documented fail-mode shape under stdio (macOS) tolerates skip (Win/Linux); `isError` never set |

**169 library tests pass workspace-wide** (`cargo test --lib --workspace`). All 6 integration tests pass against the rebuilt binary.

## Implementation notes

- Reuses the existing macOS TCC plumbing in `crate::permissions::status` (`current_status`, `accessibility_granted`, `screen_recording_granted`) — does NOT duplicate `AXIsProcessTrusted` / `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`.
- Reuses the existing Windows `diagnostics::ui_automation_available` for AX capability.
- Live ScreenCaptureKit probe writes nothing to disk; never starts a stream.
- TCC entries surface the runtime `CFBundleIdentifier` in `data.bundle_identifier` so consumers can detect TCC attribution drift without parsing message text — matches the Swift PR's wire format.
- Tool annotations: `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructive: false`, `idempotent: true`, `openWorldHint: false` — `health_report` is a pure diagnostic probe.

## Out of scope

- No changes to the deprecated Swift implementation under `libs/cua-driver/swift/`.
- No changes to existing MCP tool schemas.
- No code-signing / notarization / installer / CD changes.

## Refs

- Closed Swift PR (deprecated swift/ tree, schema reference): #1905
- Downstream consumer: NousResearch/hermes-agent#47065

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p cua-driver-core health_report` — 16/16 pass
- [x] `cargo test -p platform-macos health_report` — 5/5 pass
- [x] `cargo test -p platform-windows health_report` — 4/4 pass
- [x] `cargo test -p platform-linux health_report` — 4/4 pass
- [x] `cargo test --lib --workspace` — 169/169 pass (no new failures)
- [x] `python3 -m unittest test_health_report_mcp -v` — 6/6 pass
- [x] CLI sanity: `cua-driver call health_report` produces the documented JSON shape
