title: fix(cua-driver): don't treat socket read-timeout (EAGAIN) as fatal in daemon proxy (#1864)
body:
## Problem

`get_window_state` through the `cua-driver mcp` stdio server (which forwards to the `cua-driver serve` daemon over the Unix socket) fails with:

```
daemon transport error forwarding `get_window_state`: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
```

The same call succeeds in-process via `cua-driver call`. Two triggers reproduce it: a large response (`capture_mode=som` with a multi-MB base64 screenshot) and a slow accessibility walk (Apple Notes `som`/`ax`). Small/fast calls (`list_windows`, `click`, `type_text`) forward fine. Fixes #1864.

## Root cause

The unix `send_request` (`serve.rs`) set a 10 s `SO_RCVTIMEO` and read the response with `BufRead::lines().next()`. On a blocking `UnixStream`, when that timeout elapses with no bytes ready the read returns `WouldBlock`/`TimedOut` — which on macOS is **EAGAIN, os error 35**. `lines()` surfaces that as a hard `Err`, so any response that takes longer than one 10 s window to start/stream is reported as a fatal transport failure even though the daemon is still working.

## Fix

Replace the single timed `lines()` read with a manual newline-framed read loop that treats the per-read timeout as a **liveness poll, not a hard cap**:

- keep reading into a buffer until a `\n` is found;
- on `WouldBlock` / `TimedOut` / `Interrupted`, keep waiting (re-arming the poll) rather than failing;
- bound the total wait by a generous **120 s overall deadline** (covers the slowest AX walk / largest response) and still surface a clear error if the daemon truly hangs or closes early.

EAGAIN is no longer fatal; the existing connect + 5 s write timeouts are unchanged.

## Verification

- **Build-verified** (`#[cfg(unix)]` path, same code on macOS and Linux): `cargo build -p cua-driver` recompiled green at commit `7e6527d`.
- Runtime repro is environment-specific (macOS + Apple Notes `som`); not reproduced on the Linux build host. The change is confined to the response-read loop and preserves all existing success/error envelopes.

title: Add Cyclops CS Backend API reference documentation
body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive HTTP API reference documentation for the Cyclops CS Backend by introducing a vendored OpenAPI/Swagger 2.0 spec and an automated documentation generator. This enables the docs site to maintain up-to-date API reference material that stays in sync with the backend's actual interface.

## Key Changes

- **Vendored OpenAPI spec** (`scripts/docs-generators/specs/cyclops-cs.swagger.json`): Committed copy of the Cyclops CS backend's Swagger 2.0 specification, sourced from the private `trycua/cloud` repository. Documents 29 endpoints across 9 groups (batch, config, gateway, keys, namespaces, passthrough, pool templates, user keys, and health).

- **Documentation generator** (`scripts/docs-generators/cyclops-cs.ts`): New TypeScript generator that transforms the vendored Swagger spec into MDX documentation. Produces a comprehensive reference page with endpoint tables, parameter documentation, response schemas, and deprecation notices. Includes MDX-safe escaping for special characters and template syntax.

- **Spec sync automation** (`scripts/docs-generators/sync-cyclops-cs-spec.ts`): Utility script that refreshes the vendored spec from its source of truth in `trycua/cloud`. Supports fetching from local checkouts, filesystem paths, or GitHub API URLs (with optional token authentication for private repos).

- **CI workflow** (`.github/workflows/sync-cyclops-cs-spec.yml`): New GitHub Actions workflow that automatically syncs the vendored spec and regenerates docs when triggered by:

- **Documentation configuration**: Updated `scripts/docs-generators/config.json` and `docs/content/docs/reference/meta.json` to register the new Cyclops CS Backend reference section in the docs site navigation.

title: Linux distribution strategy: one portable binary vs. desktop + feature coverage (umbrella)
body:
## Problem

cua-driver's Linux release aims to be a single curl-pipe-bash binary that works across X11/Wayland and XFCE/GNOME/KDE. Two compatibility axes pull against each other:

**1. Runtime desktop adaptation** — *solvable in one binary.* Detect the session and pick the path (x11rb/libxcb on X11, `zwlr_virtual_pointer` on wlroots Wayland, libei via xdg-desktop-portal on KWin/Mutter). The per-desktop CI runners (gnome/kde/xfce/sway) exist to *verify* this, not to build variants.

**2. Build/ABI compatibility** — *the hard part.* What the binary links against:
- **glibc floor** — build on the oldest supported distro so it runs everywhere newer (resolved: #1919, was #1925).
- **libxcb** — hard-linking it makes it a runtime requirement; this is what #1978 / #1991 touched and likely why #1991's CI went red. Decide: hard-link vs `dlopen`.
- **libpipewire + libei (`portal-libei`)** — need *newer* versions than the debian:11 CD container has; can't bump the container's glibc without breaking axis-1 broad-distro support (#1967 gated this OFF).

### The core conflict

You cannot build one binary with **both** a low glibc floor **and** libei/PipeWire input. So today the published binary ships **without `portal-libei`** → KDE/GNOME Wayland input silently fails (**#1982**).

## Work required (checklist)

- [ ] Decide the strategy: **two build variants** (`…-portable` low-glibc/no-portal + `…-portal` newer-glibc/full) with `install.sh` glibc-sniff, vs. an alternative (static musl? vendored libs? dlopen-everything?)
- [ ] CD: produce the second (portal-libei) variant; `install.sh` selects by host glibc
- [ ] libxcb: hard-link vs `dlopen` decision (unblocks #1991 / #1978 without making libxcb a hard runtime dep)
- [ ] Make KDE/GNOME Wayland input actually work in a shipped artifact (closes #1982)
- [ ] Guard the CD/publish path against silent failures (#1969)
- [ ] Document the support matrix (distro × desktop × feature)

## Related

#1982 (KDE/GNOME input — blocked on this), #1978 / #1991 (libxcb), #1967 (portal-libei gate), #1919 / #1925 (glibc floor), #1922 (native-Wayland deps), #1969 (CD race).

title: cua-driver (Linux/WSL): capture/get_screen_size returns zero/null dimensions → downstream int(None) on WSL
body:
## Report

A user on X reported, using cua computer-use via Hermes on **WSL (Linux under Windows), cua-driver 0.6.5**:

> trying to use computer use, got this error: `capture failed: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'NoneType'`

Hermes surfaced it and told them to wait for a fix.

## Root cause — cua-driver (Rust), Linux/WSL capture + get_screen_size path

This is a **cua-driver bug**, not primarily a Python `cua-computer` bug. On WSL there are two sub-cases, and the driver mishandled both by emitting **zero/garbage dimensions** instead of a clear typed error:

1. **No display at all** (WSL with no X server / WSLg not provisioning `$DISPLAY`): `RustConnection::connect(None)` fails and the driver already returned a clean error — but the message gave no hint that the real problem was "no usable display on WSL".

2. **WSLg / headless XWayland present but 0×0** (the more insidious case): the X server *connects*, but the root screen advertises a **0-px geometry** until a real output is attached. In this state:
   - `GetScreenSizeTool::invoke` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`, the `get_screen_size` tool) read `screen.width_in_pixels` / `height_in_pixels` (both `0`) and returned a structured **success**: `{"width": 0, "height": 0, "scale_factor": 1.0}`.
   - The X11 display-capture path `screenshot_display_bytes_x11` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/capture.rs`) read the root geometry as `0×0` and called `get_image(... w=0, h=0 ...)`, producing an empty/0-px buffer.

So the driver handed the client a `0` width/height (or a 0-px image whose decoded dimensions are 0). Downstream in `cua-computer` that becomes either a **divide-by-zero** when scaling (`generic.py:368` `screenshot_width / screen_size["width"]`) or, once a zeroed/missing dimension collapses to `None`, an `int(None)` — which is the `int() argument ... not 'NoneType'` TypeError the user saw. The `capture failed:` prefix is added by the Hermes/computer-use wrapper around that TypeError.

**Bottom line:** the null/zero originates in the **Rust driver** (`platform-linux`), in the `get_screen_size` tool and the X11 display-capture path, when no usable display geometry is resolvable on WSL/WSLg. The Python `int(None)` is only the downstream symptom.

## Fix (PR open)

In the Rust driver, where the zero/null originates:
- **`GetScreenSizeTool`** (`platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`): when X11 connects but reports a `0×0` root screen, **bail with an actionable typed error** instead of returning `{width:0,height:0}`.
- **`screenshot_display_bytes_x11`** (`platform-linux/src/capture.rs`): bail on `0×0` root geometry instead of capturing a 0-px image.
- New crate helpers `is_wsl()` (env + `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease` probe) and `no_display_hint()` so both the connect-failure and the `0×0` errors carry a WSL-aware message: *"no usable display detected (WSL) … WSLg provides $DISPLAY/$WAYLAND_DISPLAY under recent Windows 11 + `wsl --update`; otherwise install an X server and export DISPLAY."*

Net effect: the driver **never emits a 0/null where the client expects a usable int** — it fails loudly with a message that tells the user exactly what's wrong on WSL.

PR: see linked PR below.

## Downstream symptom (secondary, optional hardening in cua-computer)

Not the root cause, but worth hardening so a future bad value degrades gracefully rather than as a cryptic `int(None)`:
- `libs/python/computer/computer/interface/generic.py:636` — `int(result.get("width", 0))`: `.get("width", 0)` only defaults when the key is **absent**; an explicit `"width": null` returns `None` → `int(None)`. Consider `int(result.get("width") or 0)`.
- `generic.py:368-369` / `:384-387` — validate `screen_size["width"]/["height"]` are non-null/non-zero before scaling, raising a clear "screen size unavailable" rather than dividing by zero or `int(None)`.

## Repro (to confirm on a real WSL box)

1. WSL (no X server, or WSLg in a 0×0 state), `cua-driver` 0.6.5+.
2. Run a computer-use agent (Hermes) → `get_screen_size` / capture.
3. Before fix: `capture failed: int() argument ... not 'NoneType'`.
4. After fix: driver returns a clear error — *"no usable display detected (WSL …)"* — instead of null/zero dimensions.

A live WSL repro (exact distro, WSLg on/off, `cua-driver doctor` output) would confirm whether the user hit sub-case 1 (no display) or 2 (WSLg 0×0); the fix covers both. A normal (non-WSL) Linux VM does not reproduce the no-display case, so the fix is reasoned from the Rust code path and compile-verified on Linux.

title: ci(cua-driver-rs): gate Linux release bumps on the harness suite (Phase 0)
body:
Phase 0 of the cua-driver-rs release test-gate (see `RELEASE_TEST_GATE_PLAN.md`). **Linux only.** Draft until validated by a CI dry-run (reusable-workflow + OIDC perms + conditional `needs` can only be confirmed live).

## What

Two gates, distinct jobs:
1. **PR required checks** (branch protection, configured separately) — the merge gate.
2. **A harness preamble inside the bump action** (this PR) — the release gate: `release-bump-version.yml` now **runs the Linux harness suite against the exact release commit** before `bump-version`. Red suite ⇒ no bump ⇒ no tag ⇒ no publish.

## How

- **`nix-build.yml`**: add `workflow_call` so the bump action can invoke the *same* suite the PR gate runs (no divergence between merge-gate and release-gate). Quarantine the known-flaky `cursor-click-gif` (`allow_failure: true` + job-level `continue-on-error`) so a flake can't block a PR merge or a release. *De-flake and remove the flag as a follow-up.*
- **`release-bump-version.yml`**:
  - `harness-preamble` job → `uses: ./.github/workflows/nix-build.yml`, gated `if: service == 'cua-driver-rs' && !force_release` (skipped for all other services).
  - `bump-version` `needs: [harness-preamble]`, proceeds on `success || skipped || force_release`.
  - `force_release` boolean input — audited emergency bypass for when the gate is blocked by *infra*, not failing tests.
  - `+id-token: write` / `+pull-requests: write` perms (the reusable gate's AWS-OIDC Nix cache needs them).

## Why re-run, not query

The PR's checks ran against the PR head, not the post-squash `main` commit that gets tagged. Querying the Checks API can pass on stale evidence (main moved, or the merge commit's CI hasn't finished). Re-running against the release commit tests the precise artifact. Cost: extra latency + duplicate compute at release time — acceptable for an infrequent patch release.

## Validate before un-drafting

1. Dispatch `release-bump-version` with a **non-cua-driver-rs** service → `harness-preamble` is **skipped**, `bump-version` proceeds (no regression for other packages).
2. Dispatch with `service=cua-driver-rs` on a branch with a **deliberately broken** harness → `bump-version` is **blocked** (no tag).
3. Same, healthy branch → suite passes, bump proceeds.
4. `force_release=true` → preamble skipped, bump proceeds (confirm it's audited in the run log).

## Limitations / follow-ups

- The preamble tests the **ref the bump runs on** (normally `main`); if `target_branch` differs from the dispatch ref, it'd test the wrong commit — fine for the common case, worth hardening later.
- **Windows/macOS** gates need self-hosted interactive runners → later phases.
- **#1969** (post-publish distro-compat smoke) is still separate — the preamble gates the *source*, not the *published binary*.
- De-flake `cursor-click-gif` and drop the quarantine flag.

title: GNOME: cua-driver setting ScreenReaderEnabled=true on org.a11y.Status triggers Orca screen reader on every session
body:
## Description

On GNOME, every time `cua-driver serve` starts, the Orca screen reader is automatically launched and starts reading UI elements aloud. This is disruptive for users on voice channels, in quiet environments, or with hearing impairments.

## Root Cause

When `cua-driver serve` initializes on Linux, it calls `ensure_chromium_accessibility_enabled()` (at `main.rs:808-810`), which sets the `ScreenReaderEnabled=true` property on the `org.a11y.Status` D-Bus interface (at `a11y.rs:103-107`).

The intended purpose is to force Chromium/Electron apps to build their AT-SPI accessibility trees — they keep them disabled by default and only expose them when they detect an assistive technology listening. As the code comments in `a11y.rs:1-28` explain:

> *"A real screen reader (Orca) turns the tree on simply by writing that status property when it starts. We do the same once, at daemon startup."*

However, on GNOME, this has a side effect: `gsd-a11y-settings` (part of `gnome-settings-daemon`) monitors `ScreenReaderEnabled` and, when it becomes `true`:
1. Mirrors the change to gsettings: `org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications.screen-reader-enabled` → `true`
2. Activates `orca.service` via systemd (user unit, `Restart=always`)
3. Orca starts reading all UI elements aloud via speech synthesis

This does **not** happen on KDE Plasma or other non-GNOME desktops, as `gsd-a11y-settings` is GNOME-specific.

## Reproduction

**Tested on:** Fedora 44, GNOME 48 (Wayland)
**cua-driver version:** 0.6.5

1. Ensure `ScreenReaderEnabled` is `false`:
   ```
   gdbus call --session --dest org.a11y.Bus --object-path /org/a11y/bus \
     --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get \
     org.a11y.Status ScreenReaderEnabled
   ```
2. Start `cua-driver serve`
3. Observe:
   - `ScreenReaderEnabled` immediately changes to `true`
   - `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled` → `true`
   - `systemctl --user status orca.service` shows the service was activated
   - Orca process appears: `ps aux | grep orca`
   - Audible screen reader output

## Evidence

Journal output after starting `cua-driver serve` with flags initially `false`:
```
jun 24 11:10:44 fedora systemd[1601]: Starting orca.service - Orca Screen Reader...
jun 24 11:10:45 fedora systemd[1601]: Started orca.service - Orca Screen Reader.
jun 24 11:10:49 fedora orca[34490]: /usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/orca/orca.py:306: ...
```

## Relevant Code

- **`main.rs:808-810`** — calls `ensure_chromium_accessibility_enabled()` during Linux serve initialization
  https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs#L808-L810

- **`a11y.rs:103-107`** — sets `ScreenReaderEnabled=true` and `IsEnabled=true` on `org.a11y.Status`
  https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/a11y.rs#L103-L107

- **`a11y.rs:1-28`** — module documentation explaining the rationale
  https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/a11y.rs#L1-L28

## Existing Workaround (destructive, system-level)

Users on GNOME can suppress Orca via:
1. Create a no-op stub at `~/.local/bin/orca` that sleeps forever
2. Rename the real binary: `mv /usr/bin/orca /usr/bin/orca.orig`
3. Mask the systemd service: `systemctl --user mask orca.service`
4. Disable autostart: `mv /etc/xdg/autostart/orca-autostart.desktop ...disabled`

This workaround is fragile, host-specific, requires manual root-level changes, and prevents Orca from working even when a user genuinely needs it.

## Existing Escape Hatch

`CUA_DRIVER_RS_DISABLE_A11Y_ADVERTISE=1` disables the entire accessibility advertisement — but this is all-or-nothing, so Chromium/Electron/GTK/Qt trees all stay invisible and `get_window_state` returns empty trees for those apps.

## Suggested Approaches

### 1. Test if `IsEnabled=true` alone suffices
The code currently sets both `ScreenReaderEnabled` and `IsEnabled`. On modern Chromium/Electron/AT-SPI2, `IsEnabled` (the GTK/Qt bridge gate) may be sufficient for accessibility tree visibility without the GNOME screen-reader side effect. If so, setting only `IsEnabled=true` would be a clean fix.

### 2. Granular env var
Add `CUA_DRIVER_RS_A11Y_ADVERTISE_MODE` with values:
- `all` (current behavior, default)
- `is_enabled_only` (sets only `IsEnabled=true`, skips `ScreenReaderEnabled`)
- `none` (same as current `CUA_DRIVER_RS_DISABLE_A11Y_ADVERTISE`)

### 3. Desktop environment detection
Detect GNOME at runtime (`$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`) and apply different behavior — e.g., use Chromium-specific activation instead of the session-global flag.

### 4. Chromium-specific activation
Instead of the session-global `ScreenReaderEnabled`, explore Chromium-specific activation methods (e.g., `--force-renderer-accessibility` via launcher flags or a targeted D-Bus message). However, this is less portable across Electron apps and may not work with already-running browser windows.

title: Windows: Graphics Capture returns only Explorer desktop/icons layer, excludes visible app windows on single monitor
body:
## Environment

* OS: Windows 10.0.26200.8655
* Display setup: single physical monitor
* cua-driver: 0.6.7, upgraded from 0.6.5
* Client setup: Hermes Agent running in WSL2, connected to Windows cua-driver through the named pipe `\\.\pipe\cua-driver`

Bridge command:

```bash
/mnt/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/Cua/cua-driver/bin/cua-driver.exe mcp --no-daemon-relaunch --socket '\\.\pipe\cua-driver'
```

Windows driver install path:

```text
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin\cua-driver.exe
```

## Expected behavior

A full desktop capture should return the visible, fully composited Windows desktop, including top-level application windows such as Chrome, Hermes Desktop, PowerShell, etc.

SOM / vision / AX capture should expose visible top-level windows, or provide a way to target them.

## Actual behavior

Every full desktop capture returns only the Explorer desktop/background layer:

* Captured resolution: `1568×656`
* Surface/app reported: `explorer.exe`
* Visible content: wallpaper + real desktop icons only
* No top-level application windows appear
* Chrome, Hermes Desktop, PowerShell, etc. are visibly open on the same physical monitor, but absent from the capture
* `focus_app` cannot find the visible Chrome window even though the process exists
* Hotkeys would target Explorer rather than the intended app, so UI control is unsafe

## Reproduction steps

1. Start the Windows cua-driver daemon in the interactive Windows session.

2. Connect from WSL through the named-pipe bridge.

3. Run:

   ```bash
   HERMES_CUA_DRIVER_CMD=/home/<user>/.local/bin/cua-windows-bridge hermes computer-use doctor --json
   ```

4. Confirm doctor reports:

   * `platform: win32`
   * `driver_version: 0.6.7`
   * UIAutomation pass
   * Windows Graphics Capture pass
   * overall ok

5. Open normal Windows application windows on the single monitor, e.g. Chrome, Hermes Desktop, PowerShell.

6. Run a full desktop capture in SOM / vision / AX mode.

7. Observe that the result contains only the Explorer desktop/icons layer and excludes visible application windows.

## Diagnostics already performed

* Verified the WSL bridge connects to the Windows cua-driver daemon via named pipe.
* Verified `hermes computer-use doctor --json` through the Windows bridge reports:

  * `platform: win32`
  * `driver_version: 0.6.7`
  * UIAutomation: pass
  * Windows Graphics Capture / D3D11: pass
  * overall: ok
* Confirmed only one physical monitor is connected.
* Confirmed the driver processes are running in the correct interactive Windows session.
* Restarted the Windows cua-driver daemon from the interactive Windows session.
* Upgraded Windows cua-driver from 0.6.5 to 0.6.7.
* Re-ran doctor after upgrade and confirmed `driver_version: 0.6.7`.
* Re-tested capture after restart and upgrade.
* Result remained unchanged: `1568×656 explorer.exe` desktop/icons layer only, with no top-level app windows.

## Why this appears to be cua-driver / Windows Graphics Capture rather than Hermes routing

Hermes routing was separately verified:

* Hermes reaches the real `computer_use` callable.
* The WSL bridge reaches the Windows cua-driver named pipe.
* Doctor reports `platform: win32`.
* The issue persists after Hermes successfully invokes the real Windows driver.

Hermes can only act on the surface/elements returned by cua-driver, and the returned surface contains only Explorer desktop icons.

This suggests the Windows capture source may be locked to the Explorer desktop/background layer or an overlay/source that excludes composited top-level application windows.

## Question for maintainers

Is this a known Windows Graphics Capture / overlay / window-station issue in cua-driver 0.6.7?

Is there a configuration option or lower-level MCP call to force full composited desktop capture, enumerate top-level windows, or select the correct capture source/window?

If additional logs or a specific lower-level cua-driver command would help isolate the capture source, I can run them.

title: Cloud sandbox: VM reaches running and noVNC works, but computer-server control API (*-api.cua.sh /cmd, /ws) returns persistent HTTP 502; cua-sandbox stuck in _wait_for_server_ready
body:
## Summary

On freshly created **cloud Linux sandboxes** (`"source": "incus"`), the VM reaches `status: running` and the noVNC web desktop works, but the **computer-server control API endpoint returns HTTP `502 Bad Gateway` on every request**. As a result the official `cua-sandbox` Python SDK can never connect; it loops in `_wait_for_server_ready` for 6+ minutes and times out.

It looks like the public gateway/proxy for `*-api.cua.sh` is up (it answers, with 502), but the computer-server upstream inside the incus VM is not listening / not routed. The noVNC path (`*-vnc.cua.sh`) on the same VM works fine, so this seems isolated to the control-API route, not the VM itself.

## Environment

- `cua-sandbox` Python SDK **v0.1.16**
- Cloud sandbox, **OS: linux**, `"source": "incus"`
- Created via `POST https://api.cua.ai/v1/vms` (also reproduces through the SDK)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a cloud Linux VM:
   ```
   POST https://api.cua.ai/v1/vms
   Authorization: Bearer <CUA_API_KEY>
   {"os": "linux", "region": "us-east-1", "configuration": "small"}
   ```
   succeeds; VM transitions to `status: running` (`"source": "incus"`).
2. Open the noVNC desktop: `https://<name>-vnc.cua.sh/vnc.html` returns **HTTP 200**, desktop renders. OK
3. Hit the computer-server control API on the same VM:
   ```
   GET/POST https://<name>-api.cua.sh/cmd      -> HTTP 502 Bad Gateway
   WS       wss://<name>-api.cua.sh/ws          -> fails (502 / cannot upgrade)
   ```
   Returns `502` on **every** request, on every fresh VM, sustained over several minutes (not a boot delay).
4. The SDK resolves the endpoint to `https://<name>-api.cua.sh/cmd` and loops in `_wait_for_server_ready`, receiving 404/502, never becoming ready (times out after 6+ min).

## Expected

The computer-server control API (`/cmd`, `/ws`) on `<name>-api.cua.sh` should become reachable once the VM is `running`, so the SDK's `_wait_for_server_ready` succeeds and screenshot/click/type work, matching what the noVNC endpoint already does.

## Actual

`<name>-vnc.cua.sh` returns 200 (works), but `<name>-api.cua.sh/cmd` + `/ws` return persistent `502 Bad Gateway`; the SDK never connects.

## Questions

1. Is the computer-server expected to be **auto-started and routed** on cloud `incus` Linux VMs, or does it require a manual start / specific image / plan / region?
2. Is the `502` on `*-api.cua.sh` (while `*-vnc.cua.sh` is healthy) a known gateway/routing issue on the cloud incus image?
3. If there is a flag, region, or plan tier required for the control API to be exposed, could that be documented? I did not find it in the cloud docs.

Happy to provide the exact VM name, `job_id`, and timestamps privately if useful. Thanks!

title: cua-driver(windows): UIA element bounds return -32000 sentinel on secondary monitor, PostMessage clicks no-op
body:
## Symptom

On Windows multi-monitor setups with a secondary screen positioned at a **non-zero offset** (negative-X or negative-Y), `computer_use` clicks / type / set_value on elements that live in the secondary screen's window silently no-op. Capture and UIA tree reading work perfectly — only input dispatch is affected.

Two independent reports against cua-driver-rs 0.6.5, both on real hardware:

- **@1mestre** (original #1979): negative-X layout; secondary at `X = -1920`. SendInput VIRTUALDESK normalization fence-post fixed in #1980, PostMessage LPARAM packing hardened in #1983. Both ship in v0.6.5.
- **@Cdddo** validated v0.6.5 on a `(-1920, 0, 3840×1080)` rig in [#1981 comment](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/1981#issuecomment-4775038611) — negative-X clicks now round-trip correctly (Spotify clicks landed; Web API confirmed state changes).
- **@phixz668-hub** ([#1981 comment](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/1981#issuecomment-4781020849)) on **negative-Y** (primary `1568×832`, secondary `1920×1080` above primary): Chrome elements on secondary report bounds with **`~ -32000 Y`**, clicks "succeed" but land nowhere. Drag Chrome to primary → works. Capture/UIA tree both fine.

## Likely root cause: iconic-sentinel leak in the bounds path

`-32000, -32000` is the canonical Win32 sentinel for **minimized/iconic windows** — `GetWindowRect` returns it whenever `WS_MINIMIZE` is set, regardless of where the window was last positioned. (This is also why the iconic-bail in PR #1974 specifically catches it for capture.)

That the bound `Y` matches this sentinel exactly is a strong signal that the UIA element-bounds resolver for elements on a secondary monitor is going through a code path that:

1. Calls `GetWindowRect` (or a screen-coord transform built on top of it) against an HWND that *looks* iconic to Win32 even when it's actually visible on the secondary, **or**
2. Calls the iconic-check too eagerly and short-circuits to the sentinel rect.

The candidates are #1984's candidate A (stale `ElementCache::get_element_center`) and B (`DoubleClickTool` missing Chromium short-circuit) but neither matches this symptom shape — capture/UIA reading work, and the sentinel value is too specific to be cache staleness. This is a third, distinct candidate.

## What to audit

- `crates/platform-windows/src/uia/cache.rs::ElementCache::get_element_center` and any caller — does the resolver short-circuit on `IsIconic(hwnd)` and substitute a sentinel rect, or call `GetWindowRect` without normalizing against the screen the window actually lives on?
- The bounds path used by `get_window_state` to populate `structuredContent.elements[].frame` — does it pass through the same code path that downstream click dispatch consumes? @phixz668-hub's `(4)` log (AX tree dump from the secondary) will pin this down: if the dump shows real positive bounds, the bug is *downstream* (between AX read and click dispatch); if it already shows `-32000`, the bug is in the AX bounds resolver itself.
- `crates/platform-windows/src/tools/click.rs` (or wherever screen-to-client transform lives for PostMessage): does it normalize a sentinel-bounded HWND against the actual screen rect before packing into LPARAM, or just pack the raw `(-32000, ...)` as-is? (PR #1983's LPARAM packer would happily round-trip `-32000` since it's within `i16` range — math is fine, but the input is poisoned.)

## Logs requested (waiting on @phixz668-hub)

Asked in [#1981 follow-up](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/1981) for:

1. `cua-driver --version`.
2. `RUST_LOG=cua_driver=debug,platform_windows=debug cua-driver mcp` stderr during one failed click on the secondary + one successful click on the primary. Specifically lines mentioning `IsIconic`, `GetWindowRect`, `screen_to_client`, `get_window_state`, `click`, `list_windows`.
3. `cua-driver doctor` output.
4. SOM-mode AX dump for Chrome on the secondary monitor — confirms whether `-32000` shows up at AX-resolution time or downstream.

## Why this can't wait for #1984

#1984 candidate A is a cache-invalidation question, candidate B is a Chromium-dispatch short-circuit. Neither addresses the iconic-sentinel leak. With v0.6.5 already shipped and two of three reports still seeing wrong-screen clicks, this is the highest-confidence path to the actual user-visible bug.

## References

- Original reporter ticket: #1979
- SendInput half: #1980
- PostMessage half: #1983
- Cache-stale + Chromium short-circuit candidates: #1984
- Multi-monitor rig coverage: #1981

cua-driver: Linux `list_windows` emits flat x/y/width/height instead of `bounds: {...}` — breaks cross-platform parity
body:
cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

`list_windows` returns window geometry under a nested **`bounds: {x, y, width, height}`** object on macOS and Windows, but as **flat top-level `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`** on Linux. A cross-platform consumer that reads `window.bounds.width` works on macOS/Windows and silently breaks on Linux.

Linux is also missing `app_name` and `is_on_screen`, which macOS and Windows both emit.

## Current behavior

```jsonc
// macOS  (crates/platform-macos/src/tools/list_windows.rs)
// Windows (crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs)
{ "window_id": 1234, "pid": 99, "app_name": "...", "title": "...",
  "bounds": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
  "is_on_screen": true, ... }

// Linux  (crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs, ListWindowsTool::invoke)
{ "window_id": 1234, "pid": 99, "title": "...",
  "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1280, "height": 800 }
```

## Why this is a bug, not a design choice

- macOS and Windows already agree on the nested `bounds` shape. Linux is the lone outlier.
- There is no platform reason — X11/Wayland geometry is `(x, y, w, h)` like everywhere else and nests into `bounds` identically.
- cua-driver markets a cross-platform tool surface with parity (see `platform-windows/examples/list_tools_parity.rs` and the `schema_version` machinery in `cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs`). This divergence forces every consumer to special-case Linux. It surfaced while wiring a Gemini `computers/desktop` backend, which had to add a `_window_dims()` shim purely to tolerate the two shapes.

## Proposed fix (additive-safe)

In `crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`, change the `ListWindowsTool` structured output so each record emits `bounds: { x, y, width, height }` (and `app_name` + `is_on_screen` where derivable), matching macOS/Windows.

Mirror what **Windows already does**: keep the flat `x/y/width/height` fields too (Windows exposes them under `_legacy_windows`) so any existing Linux Rust/CLI caller does not break. Net effect: `bounds` becomes the canonical cross-platform field; flat fields remain as a legacy alias.

This is additive (no field removed) so `schema_version` does not need a bump.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Linux `list_windows` structured records contain `bounds: { x, y, width, height }`.
- [ ] Linux records include `app_name` and `is_on_screen` (best-effort; empty string / derived boolean acceptable where the data is unavailable).
- [ ] Flat `x/y/width/height` retained as a legacy alias so existing Linux consumers keep working.
- [ ] A test asserts the Linux record shape matches the macOS/Windows `bounds` contract.

## References

- `crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs` — `ListWindowsTool::invoke` (the flat-field json! block)
- `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/list_windows.rs` — canonical `bounds` shape
- `crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs` — `bounds` + `_legacy_windows` pattern to mirror
EOF

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): list_windows / get_window_state drop empty-/null-title top-level windows (WPF, borderless, custom-chrome) — debug_window_info sees them but the agent can't target them
body:
## Symptom

On Windows, `list_windows` (and therefore `get_window_state` and every input tool that resolves a pid → windows) silently **drops any top-level window whose title is empty/null**. The window is real, visible, non-iconic, and has no owner — it's just untitled. Apps that legitimately ship empty-caption top-level windows (WPF, custom-chrome / borderless / self-drawn apps, some splash and tool windows) become impossible for the agent to target.

Concrete repro that surfaced this — **`Ruler.Wpf.exe`**, a WPF on-screen ruler:

- Class name is the canonical WPF shape `HwndWrapper[App.exe;;<guid>]`, window `title` is **null/empty**.
- `debug_window_info {"pid": <pid>}` lists the window fine — e.g. **hwnd `393542`**, visible, no owner.
- `list_windows {"pid": <pid>}` returns an **empty `windows` array** — the hwnd is gone.
- `get_window_state {"window_id": 393542}` → `"No window with window_id 393542 exists"`.
- Every subsequent `click` / `scroll` is then rejected with `"No windows found for pid <pid>"`.

So the driver can *see* the window in its own debug tool but cannot expose it to the agent — a hard wall for the whole interaction.

Observed on cua-driver-rs 0.6.7; the filter is unchanged on current `main` (0.6.8).

## Root cause: both `list_windows` enumeration sources hard-filter on non-empty title

`list_windows` walks two sources and unions them by HWND (introduced in #1542). The module doc-comment states the contract outright:

> `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/win32/windows.rs:17`
> *"Both sources apply the same filters (visible, non-iconic, **non-empty title**)."*

Both paths discard an empty title **before** the window can ever reach the merged list:

**1. `EnumWindows` path** — `enum_windows_cb` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/win32/windows.rs:110-118`:
```rust
let title_len = GetWindowTextLengthW(hwnd);
if title_len == 0 { return TRUE; }          // ← empty-title window dropped here
...
if title.trim().is_empty() { return TRUE; } // ← whitespace-only title dropped here
```

**2. UI Automation path** — `window_info_from_uia_element` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/windows_enum.rs:652-662`:
```rust
let title_len = GetWindowTextLengthW(hwnd);
if title_len == 0 { return None; }          // ← empty-title window dropped here
...
if title.trim().is_empty() { return None; } // ← whitespace-only title dropped here
```

This filter was **added deliberately as "filter parity"** in #1542, whose goal was the opposite problem (UWP/WebView2 frames returning an *empty* array). That PR never considered that an honest, visible, owner-less top-level window can legitimately have no caption — so the non-empty-title guard now produces false negatives for WPF / borderless / custom-chrome apps.

## Why `debug_window_info` disagrees

`debug_window_info` (added in #1597) uses a **looser** enumeration that does not look at the title at all — `enum_cb` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs:5681-5695`:
```rust
if p == ctx.target_pid && IsWindowVisible(hwnd).as_bool() {
    let owner = GetWindow(hwnd, GW_OWNER);
    if owner.unwrap_or_default().is_invalid() {   // visible + no owner — title is irrelevant
        ctx.hwnds.push(hwnd.0 as isize);
    }
}
```

So `debug_window_info` lists the window (visible + no owner) while `list_windows` hides it (visible + no owner + **empty title → rejected**). The two tools apply inconsistent visibility criteria for the same HWND, which is exactly why the window looks "present in debug, absent everywhere else."

## Suggested fix

Stop using "has a non-empty caption" as a proxy for "is a real, targetable window." A visible, non-iconic, owner-less top-level HWND should be listed even with an empty title. Concretely, in **both** `enum_windows_cb` and `window_info_from_uia_element`:

- Drop the `title_len == 0` / `title.trim().is_empty()` early-returns (or gate them behind a far narrower condition).
- Emit the record with an empty `title` (callers already treat `title` as a plain string; an empty string is fine), or synthesize a stable placeholder from the window class (e.g. `HwndWrapper[...]`) so the agent still has something human-readable.
- Update the `win32/windows.rs:17` doc-comment and PARITY.md once the contract changes.

If the original #1542 motivation (suppressing noisy UWP `ApplicationFrameHost` shells / zero-area phantoms) still needs guarding, replace the title check with criteria that actually express "not a real window" rather than "untitled" — e.g. require a non-zero/visible client rect and/or keep the existing `GW_OWNER`-is-invalid check, both of which `Ruler.Wpf.exe` satisfies. That preserves #1542's intent without the empty-title false negatives.

Happy to send a PR if the maintainers agree on the direction (drop the title filter vs. replace it with a geometry/owner check).

## References

- Filter introduced as "filter parity": #1542 (UIA-first top-level window enumeration on Windows)
- Looser debug enumerator: #1597 (`debug_window_info` tool)
- Affected code (current `main`, 0.6.8):
  - `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/win32/windows.rs:17,110-118`
  - `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/windows_enum.rs:652-662`
  - `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs:5681-5695`

title: fix(cua-driver)(windows): list empty-/null-title top-level windows (WPF, borderless, custom-chrome) (#2020)
body:
Closes #2020.

> **Draft / direction check.** This changes the Windows `list_windows`
> enumeration contract, and I can't run the Windows test suite locally
> (`platform-windows` needs an MSVC toolchain + a real interactive desktop;
> see Verification below). Opening as a draft to confirm the direction —
> replace the non-empty-title proxy with an explicit "is this a real window?"
> predicate — before asking for a real-hardware regression run.

## Problem

On Windows, `list_windows` silently dropped any visible top-level window whose
**title is empty/null**. Because `get_window_state`, `click`, `scroll`, etc. all
resolve a pid → windows through `crate::win32::list_windows`, such a window was
completely untargetable by the agent:

- `debug_window_info {"pid": <pid>}` listed the window (e.g. a WPF
  `Ruler.Wpf.exe`, class `HwndWrapper[App.exe;;<guid>]`, hwnd `393542`, title
  null).
- `list_windows {"pid": <pid>}` returned an **empty array**.
- `get_window_state {"window_id": 393542}` → `"No window with window_id … exists"`.
- Every following `click` / `scroll` → `"No windows found for pid <pid>"`.

WPF, borderless, and custom-chrome apps legitimately ship empty-caption
top-level windows, so this is a hard wall for a whole class of apps.

## Root cause

Both enumeration sources hard-filtered on a non-empty title before the window
could reach the merged list:

- `EnumWindows` path — `enum_windows_cb`, `win32/windows.rs` (`title_len == 0 → skip`).
- UI Automation path — `window_info_from_uia_element`, `uia/windows_enum.rs`
  (`title_len == 0 → None`).

The module doc-comment even stated it as the contract: *"Both sources apply the
same filters (visible, non-iconic, non-empty title)."* This non-empty-title gate
was introduced as "filter parity" in #1542 (whose actual goal was the opposite —
UWP/WebView2 frames returning an *empty* array), and was never reconsidered for
honest untitled windows. Meanwhile `debug_window_info` (#1597) enumerated with a
looser filter (visible + no owner, title ignored), which is why the window showed
up there but nowhere else.

## Fix

Replace the title proxy with an explicit predicate for "real, targetable
top-level window", shared by **both** enumeration sources so they can't drift
again (the drift was the root cause):

```rust
pub(crate) fn is_listable_top_level(hwnd: HWND) -> bool {
    // visible && !iconic && owner-less (GW_OWNER null) && !DWM-cloaked
}
```

- `GW_OWNER` null → excludes tool-tips / owned pop-ups / transient children
  (the EnumWindows path previously had **no** owner check — this is what lets us
  safely drop the title gate without admitting noise). Mirrors the top-level
  test `debug_window_info` already uses, so the two tools now agree.
- `DWMWA_CLOAKED == 0` → excludes suspended-UWP / `ApplicationFrameHost`
  background frames that keep `WS_VISIBLE` but aren't on screen (the noise class
  #1542 cared about).
- Title is now read for display only via a shared `window_title` helper; empty
  caption → empty string. The tool layer already renders `(no title)` for these
  records, so nothing downstream needed to change.

Touches: `win32/windows.rs` (predicate + helpers + `enum_windows_cb`),
`uia/windows_enum.rs` (reuse the predicate, drop the title gate),
`PARITY.md` (enumeration-source contract).

## Tests

Added `empty_title_top_level_window_is_listed` in `win32/windows.rs` — creates a
real visible, owner-less, **empty-caption** top-level window via `CreateWindowExW`
and asserts it appears in `list_windows(Some(own_pid))` with an empty title. It's
`#[ignore]` (needs an interactive window station), matching the existing Windows
GUI tests; run via the sandbox harness runner or
`cargo test -p platform-windows -- --ignored empty_title`.

## Verification status

- ✅ `cargo check -p platform-windows --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` — clean (lib).
- ✅ `cargo check … --tests` — clean, **including the new `CreateWindowExW`-based
  test module** (the part I was least sure about, since it exercises Win32 API
  signatures directly). The only warning is a pre-existing unused import in
  `impl_.rs`, unrelated to this change.
- ✅ Static review against existing call sites (`overlay.rs` for
  `CreateWindowExW`/`RegisterClassExW`, `impl_.rs` for
  `GetWindow(GW_OWNER).unwrap_or_default().is_invalid()`, `get_window_bounds`
  for the `DwmGetWindowAttribute` shape).
- ⚠️ **Not run on real Windows.** Cross-`check` proves it compiles for the
  Windows target, but I have no rig / interactive desktop to execute the new
  `#[ignore]` test or run a real-desktop regression. The owner/cloaked gates'
  effect on real noise windows still needs a hardware run — ideally the same
  folks helping with #1981.

Happy to adjust the predicate (e.g. add a non-zero-area check, or keep/drop the
cloaked gate) based on what a real run shows.

title: feat(computer): add useHostComputerServer to the TypeScript SDK (#916)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #916.

The TypeScript [get-started guide](https://cua.ai/docs/cua/guide/get-started/using-computer-sdk) shows:

```ts
import { Computer } from '@trycua/computer';

const computer = new Computer({ useHostComputerServer: true });
await computer.run(); // Connect to the host desktop
```

…but `@trycua/computer` only exported `CloudComputer` (aliased as `Computer`), which requires an `apiKey` and connects to a cua.ai VM — so the documented call threw and there was no way to drive the local host desktop from TS. This PR brings the TS SDK to parity with the Python SDK's `use_host_computer_server=True`.

## What changed

- **Unified `Computer`** with two connection modes:
  - **Host** (`useHostComputerServer: true`) — connects to a local [Computer Server](https://cua.ai/docs/libraries/computer-server) over plain `ws://localhost:8000/ws` with **no API key**. `osType` defaults to the current platform; optional `host` / `port` overrides for a server reachable over the network.
  - **Cloud** (`apiKey` + `name`) — unchanged behavior and telemetry.
- `CloudComputer` and a new `HostComputer` are thin, explicitly-typed subclasses of `Computer`. `new Computer(cloudConfig)` is unchanged and `instanceof Computer` still holds.
- The interface layer already supported the no-auth local connection (`base.ts` uses `ws://` and skips the auth handshake when no apiKey is set), so this is a **provider-level change only** — no protocol or interface changes.
- Package README now documents both modes.

## API

```ts
import { Computer, HostComputer } from '@trycua/computer';

// Drive the local desktop (no VM, no API key)
const computer = new Computer({ useHostComputerServer: true });
```

title: fix(cua-driver): persist set_config to disk on Windows + Linux (config parity)
body:
Persist `set_config` to disk on **Windows and Linux** so config survives across stateless `cua-driver call` invocations — bringing them to parity with macOS, which already does this. Addresses #2011 (Windows config disagreement) and fixes the footgun where the desktop-scope flow (#2019) couldn't hold `capture_scope` across CLI calls.

## The bug

Each `cua-driver call` is a fresh process. On macOS, `ToolState::default()` loads `~/.cua-driver/config.json` at startup and `set_config` writes keys back, so config persists across calls. On **Windows/Linux**, `ToolState::new()` built `DriverConfig::default()` with **no disk load**, and `set_config` mutated only the in-memory config for `capture_mode` / `max_image_dimension` (only `experimental_pip*` ever touched disk). So a separate `cua-driver call get_config` reverted to defaults (`som`). This is exactly why `set_config capture_scope=desktop` then a separate `click` didn't take effect.

## Changes (3 files)

- **`crates/pip-preview/src/lib.rs`** (the already-shared config helper):
  - `default_config_path()` now falls back to `%USERPROFILE%` when `HOME` is unset. **Windows runs with `HOME` empty**, so without this the config file can't even be resolved there — meaning the existing pip persistence was *latently broken on Windows too*.
  - Added `read_config_value(key)` so per-platform loaders can read arbitrary keys.
- **`crates/platform-windows/.../tools/impl_.rs`** & **`crates/platform-linux/.../tools/impl_.rs`**:
  - Added `load_driver_config()` (mirrors macOS), wired into `ToolState::new()` to load `capture_mode` + `max_image_dimension` from disk at startup.
  - `set_config` now persists both fields via `pip_preview::write_config_key`, in **both** input shapes (`{key,value}` and legacy per-field). Persist failures `warn!` and continue, matching macOS.

`platform-macos` is untouched (already correct).

## Verified live (two separate `call` processes)

- **Linux** (`cua-gnome-test`): fresh `get_config` → `som`; `set_config capture_mode=vision` in one process; **separate** `get_config` → `vision`. On-disk `/root/.cua-driver/config.json` = `{"capture_mode":"ax","max_image_dimension":800}`.
- **Windows** (`fbonacci-windows-vm`, with `HOME` empty): same round-trip persists; on-disk `C:\Windows\system32\config\systemprofile\.cua-driver\config.json` confirms the `%USERPROFILE%` fallback works.

(Tested with `capture_mode` because `capture_scope` only exists on the #2019 branch — it exercises the identical persistence path.)

## Relationship to other PRs

- **#2011** — addresses the Windows config inconsistency for both Windows and Linux.
- **#2033** — supersedes its Windows-only approach: that PR's `config_file_path()` keys only on `HOME` (errors `"$HOME is not set"` when unset), so it silently no-ops on stock Windows; its own test forces `HOME=…`, masking the gap. This PR adds the `%USERPROFILE%` fallback and is runtime-verified on Windows with `HOME` empty.
- **#2019** — should rebase on top and add `capture_scope` to each platform's `load_driver_config()` + the `set_config` persist calls (~2 lines/platform, same pattern) so desktop-scope survives across processes.

title: fix(cua-driver): let start_session revive an idle-reaped session (recover from "session ended")
body:
## Problem

A caller-declared `session` reclaimed by the idle-TTL sweep is **permanently dead**, and `start_session` cannot bring it back — so a run that goes quiet for >5 min (the agent reasoning / writing code without calling an MCP tool) loses the driver entirely.

Seen in agent trajectories: a run does `start_session{session:"X"}`, works fine for ~80 tool calls (all carrying `session:"X"`), then idles past the TTL. After that **every** MCP tool — including `start_session{session:"X"}` itself — returns `session ended; tool call ignored`, with no way to recover.

## Root cause

Three things compound (`cua-driver-core/src/session.rs`, `cua-driver/src/serve.rs`):

1. `evict_idle` marks an idle session ended by inserting it into `ENDED_SESSIONS`, which is **never cleared**.
2. `touch_session` **no-ops on an ended id**, so it can't re-arm one.
3. The daemon's resurrection guard (serve.rs "call" arm) rejects any call whose session `is_session_ended` — **including `start_session`**, which is itself a normal tool call routed through that same arm. So the one tool meant to (re)start a session is blocked before its `invoke` ever runs.

Net: once `X` is reaped, `is_session_ended("X")` is true forever and nothing flips it back.

## Fix

- **`session::revive_session`** — clears the ended tombstone + re-arms the idle-TTL clock. A superset of `touch_session`: equivalent for a live/new id; resumes an ended one.
- **`start_session` tool** — calls `revive_session` instead of `touch_session`, so it can resume a reaped run.
- **serve.rs** — exempts `start_session` from the resurrection guard in both dispatch arms so it actually runs (it is the recovery path); every other tool stays guarded so a stale in-flight call can't rebuild reaped state.
- The guard message now tells the agent how to recover.

`revive` semantics: a later `end_session` re-fires the cleanup hooks (they key on `ENDED_SESSIONS`), which is correct — a fresh lifecycle for the id.

This is the core correctness fix and is independent of the TTL value: a short TTL just triggers reaping more often — with revival that's recoverable instead of fatal. Whether to also raise the 300 s default (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_SESSION_IDLE_TTL_SECS`) is a separate tuning call, intentionally left out.

## Tests

New `revive_resumes_an_ended_session` proves an ended id is usable again after `revive`; the sweep-using session tests are serialized so a cross-test zero-TTL reap can't flake them.

## Verification status

- ✅ `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` green (101 passed, incl. the new revive test).
- ✅ `cargo check -p cua-driver` green.
- ⚠️ No end-to-end daemon test: the `cua-driver` binary doesn't link on my machine (unrelated platform-macos Swift/Metal interop vs the local SDK), and I can't re-run the eval that surfaced this. The core logic is unit-tested and the serve.rs guard exemption is a one-line condition. A daemon-level smoke (reap a session → `start_session` → confirm subsequent calls work) would be a good addition on infra that can build the binary.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **New Features**
  * You can now resume a previously ended or idle-reclaimed session by calling `start_session` again with the same session ID.
  * Session recovery now works even after a session has been marked ended, instead of being permanently unavailable.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of ended sessions so non-resume tool calls return clearer guidance on how to continue.
  * Fixed session lifecycle behavior so revived sessions can be used normally again and ended afterward.

title: fix(cua-driver): retry daemon socket writes on EAGAIN instead of failing fatally (write-side mirror of #1997)
body:
## Problem

`list_apps` (and other tools) intermittently fail with:

```
MCP error -32603: daemon transport error forwarding `list_apps`: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
```

even though the request is tiny. Seen across a large fraction of trajectories; the heavy hitters are slow system queries (`list_apps`, `get_accessibility_tree`, `launch_app`).

## Root cause

`serve.rs::send_request` handles EAGAIN asymmetrically:

- **read side** (the response loop) already treats `WouldBlock`/`TimedOut` as "daemon still working, keep waiting" up to a 120 s deadline — the #1997 fix for #1864.
- **write side** had a 5 s `SO_SNDTIMEO` (`set_write_timeout`) but **no retry**: `w.write_all(...)?` propagates the timeout as a bare `os error 35`.

When the daemon (a machine-wide singleton serving every proxy) is momentarily too busy to read — backpressure from concurrent slow system tools — the proxy's write times out and the bare EAGAIN becomes a fatal transport error, wrapped by `proxy.rs` into the message above.

That `os error 35` has no `connect to …:` prefix (so not the connect path) and isn't the `timed out after 120s` read message — by elimination it's `write_all`, the only bare-EAGAIN site left after #1997 fixed the read side. A daemon momentarily not reading is the exact write-side mirror of a daemon still computing a response: not a transport failure.

## Fix

`cua-driver-core::socket_io::write_all_with_retry`: write with offset bookkeeping, treat `WouldBlock`/`TimedOut` as "keep waiting" until an overall deadline (the same 120 s budget as the read loop). `send_request` uses it instead of `write_all`. Extracted to `core` so the retry logic is unit-testable without linking the platform crates (and their Swift/Metal interop) the `cua-driver` binary pulls in.

## Tests

New `socket_io` tests:
- `retries_through_transient_eagain` — N transient `WouldBlock`s then success.
- `times_out_when_daemon_never_drains` — a never-draining writer surfaces `TimedOut` (not a bare EAGAIN) after the deadline.
- `accumulates_partial_writes` — offset bookkeeping for short writes.

## Verification status

- ✅ `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` green (3 socket_io tests + all core).
- ✅ `cargo check -p cua-driver` green.
- ⚠️ Not reproduced against a live backpressured daemon: the `cua-driver` binary doesn't link on my machine (unrelated platform-macos Swift/Metal interop vs the local SDK) and I can't re-run the eval that surfaced this. The retry logic is unit-tested and the `send_request` change is a drop-in for the existing `write_all`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved socket writes to better handle temporary backpressure and partial writes.
  * Reduced failures caused by transient “resource temporarily unavailable” errors when communicating with the daemon.
  * Added a longer overall timeout so requests can keep retrying before failing.
  * Included validation to ensure writes complete reliably across retries and short writes.

## Why
`tests/` had no shared module — every file re-implemented the same code:

| Duplicated | Copies |
|---|---|
| `workspace_root()` / `driver_binary()` | ×9 (4 divergent path spellings) |
| JSON-RPC-over-stdio client (`send`/`call`/`init`) | ×10 |

New **`crates/cua-driver-testkit`** (dev-dependency only, never shipped):
- **`Driver` trait + two transports** — `McpDriver` (long-lived server, session-scoped state) and `CliDriver` (stateless `cua-driver call`). - **`ChildReaper`** — cross-platform child kill-on-drop; on Windows assigns to a `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` job (no orphaned windows / held ports on panic or SIGKILL).
- **`paths`** — one `driver_binary()` (`.exe` via `cfg!`), `workspace_root()`, `harness_app()`.

title: feat(driver): add experimental MCP OAuth bridge
body:
﻿## Goal

We want Cua's local desktop MCP server to be usable from OAuth-only MCP clients such as ChatGPT custom connectors.

Today `cua-driver` works well for local stdio/no-auth MCP clients, but OAuth-only remote connector flows will not even start unless the MCP endpoint also exposes OAuth discovery, Dynamic Client Registration, authorization-code + PKCE, Bearer-protected HTTP access, and the Streamable HTTP session shape expected by modern MCP clients. The target user flow is:

1. The user starts `cua-driver mcp-oauth --public-url https://...`.
2. The user points their own trusted HTTPS tunnel at the loopback listener.
3. The MCP client discovers OAuth metadata, registers dynamically, asks the user to authorize, exchanges the code for a token, then calls `/mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer ...`.
4. The existing `cua-driver` tool registry handles the actual desktop automation.

This PR folds the bridge into the driver binary instead of requiring a separate sidecar package.

## Why this shape

The goal is not to replace the existing stdio MCP path or make local users deal with OAuth. The existing `cua-driver mcp` command remains unchanged.

The new command is explicitly opt-in and loopback-first:

- It binds to `127.0.0.1:7676` by default.
- It requires an HTTPS `--public-url`, so users can put their own trusted tunnel in front.
- It stores OAuth clients, authorization codes, consent transactions, and access tokens locally under `~/.cua-driver/oauth` unless `--storage-dir` is provided.
- It reuses the existing Rust tool registry instead of adding a separate proxy process or duplicating tool logic.

## What changed

Adds an experimental `cua-driver mcp-oauth` command with:

- OAuth Authorization Server Metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.
- OAuth Protected Resource Metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`.
- Dynamic Client Registration: `POST /register`.
- Authorization Code + PKCE S256: `GET/POST /authorize` and `POST /token`.
- Bearer-protected MCP dispatch under `/mcp`.
- Streamable HTTP session basics: `initialize` returns `MCP-Session-Id`, later `/mcp` requests require it, `GET /mcp` returns an SSE stream, and `DELETE /mcp` ends the session.
- `MCP-Protocol-Version` validation for the supported 2025-06-18 path, with compatibility for missing / 2025-03-26 headers.
- CORS headers needed by browser-based MCP clients, including `MCP-Session-Id` and `MCP-Protocol-Version`.
- JSON-backed local storage for clients, authorization codes, consent transactions, and tokens.
- CLI help, manifest entry, telemetry entry, and README safety notes for the new command.

Follow-up hardening based on review feedback:

- Reject malformed TTL CLI values instead of silently falling back to defaults.
- Validate registered redirect URIs before storage: HTTPS is allowed, HTTP is limited to loopback, fragments/control characters/user-info style authorities are rejected.
- Bind consent POSTs to a server-generated nonce and consume it once to prevent trusting posted hidden fields alone.
- Redeem authorization codes and mint access tokens under a store-level critical section to avoid replay races.
- Preserve malformed OAuth JSON state as `InvalidData` instead of treating corrupted files as empty state.
- Create local OAuth state directories/files with private permissions on Unix where supported.
- Add bounded HTTP header/body read deadlines to avoid slow clients holding spawned tasks indefinitely.
- On macOS, relaunch `mcp-oauth` through `CuaDriver.app` when the existing TCC attribution proxy heuristic says the shell-spawned binary should not run in-process.

## Current PR scope

This now covers the OAuth/DCR flow plus the minimal Streamable HTTP session lifecycle needed by connector-style clients.

Still intentionally out of scope:

- Built-in tunnel management.
- Refresh tokens, revocation, introspection, or fine-grained scopes.
- Server-initiated message queues beyond the basic `GET /mcp` SSE stream response.
- A polished account/admin UI for active clients or tokens.

## Testing

Passed:

- `cargo test --offline --manifest-path libs\\cua-driver\\rust\\Cargo.toml -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver mcp_oauth -- --nocapture` (12 MCP OAuth tests)
- `cargo test --offline --manifest-path libs\\cua-driver\\rust\\Cargo.toml -p cua-driver --bins -- --nocapture --test-threads=1` (77 tests)
- `cargo build --offline --manifest-path libs\\cua-driver\\rust\\Cargo.toml -p cua-driver`
- Local first-stage smoke: started `target/debug/cua-driver.exe mcp-oauth --public-url https://example.test --listen 127.0.0.1:<port> --storage-dir <temp> --no-consent-page`, then verified `/health` and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.
- Local Streamable HTTP smoke: `POST /register` -> `GET /authorize` redirect -> `POST /token` -> `POST /mcp initialize` returning `MCP-Session-Id` -> `POST /mcp tools/list` with the session header -> `GET /mcp` returning `text/event-stream` -> `DELETE /mcp` returning 202.
- Public HTTPS tunnel smoke: exposed `cua-driver mcp-oauth` through a temporary `localhost.run` HTTPS tunnel and completed the full connector-style flow using the real consent page: `/health` -> OAuth metadata -> `POST /register` -> `GET /authorize` consent page with nonce -> `POST /authorize` redirect -> `POST /token` -> `POST /mcp initialize` returning `MCP-Session-Id` -> `POST /mcp tools/list` (39 tools) -> `GET /mcp` SSE -> `DELETE /mcp` 202. The tunnel and local OAuth storage were removed after the run.

The MCP OAuth unit tests now also cover unsafe redirect URI rejection, consent nonce replay prevention, malformed JSON state handling, supported scope validation, and Streamable HTTP session lifecycle behavior.

Note: the default parallel `cargo test --offline --manifest-path libs\\cua-driver\\rust\\Cargo.toml -p cua-driver --bins -- --nocapture` previously hit existing `version_check` test shared-state failures locally. The OAuth tests passed, and the full bin test set passed with `--test-threads=1`.

title: feat(test-harness): Linux GTK3 harness app + test (parity with macOS/Windows)
body:
Closes the **controlled-harness parity gap**: Linux had no native-toolkit harness app — only the real-app Nix GUI scenarios — whereas Windows has WPF/WinUI3 and macOS has AppKit/SwiftUI. This adds the Linux peer.

## What
- **`apps/linux/gtk3/main.py`** — PyGObject GTK3 app mirroring the SwiftUI scenario set (counter, text_body, text_input, popover, exit). Real GTK3 widgets = real AT-SPI tree.
- **`shared/scenarios.json`** — new `gtk3` entry. Documents the **Linux id contract**: AT-SPI exposes element NAME (rendered `[idx] role "name"`), not an AutomationId/AX-id, so each control's accessible NAME is its `aid`.
- **`build/linux.sh`** — stages the app + an X11-forcing launcher into `test-apps/harness-gtk3/` (peer of `macos.sh` / `windows.ps1`).
- **`harness_gtk3_test.rs`** — `cfg(target_os="linux")`, on `cua-driver-testkit`, mirrors `harness_swiftui_test`; matches on name via `ax::element_index_containing` (not `ax::has_id`, since Linux has no `id=`).

## Verified on the GNOME test VM
- ✅ `build/linux.sh` stages the app; PyGObject/GTK3 present.
- ✅ App launches and is enumerable via `list_windows` (Xwayland).
- ✅ `get_window_state` AT-SPI tree exposes **every** control by name: `btn-increment`, `btn-reset`, `txt-input`, `btn-open-popover`, `btn-exit`, `HARNESS_TEXT_MARKER_v1`, `counter=0`.
- ✅ `harness_gtk3_test` compiles on Linux (`cargo test --no-run`).
- ⏳ The full `--ignored` click/type/popover run is reserved for an interactive Linux session (needs the session's `DISPLAY`+`XAUTHORITY`+AT-SPI env, which a `cargo test` in-session inherits). `#[ignore]` so it never runs in CI.

## Note
Linux trades the precise `id=`-keyed assertions of Windows/macOS for **name-keyed** ones — an inherent AT-SPI vs UIA/AX difference (documented in the test + `scenarios.json`). A future driver enhancement could emit AT-SPI `accessible-id` as `id=` for exact parity.

title: test(cua-driver): cross-platform capture_mode matrix coverage + modality docs
body:
## What

Two halves of one ask: **document the modality test matrix** and **cover it across platforms**.

### Docs (fumadocs)
New explanation page **Capture and Dispatch Modalities** (`docs/content/docs/explanation/capture-and-dispatch-modalities.mdx`), wired into the Explanation nav + index. It documents the three independent axes of every action and the validity matrix:

- **capture_mode** — `ax` / `vision` / `som` (what the agent observes)
- **dispatch** — `background` (default) / `foreground` (how input lands)
- **capture_scope** — `window` (default) / `desktop` (the coordinate space)

Validity: **window scope supports any combination**; **desktop scope is vision + foreground only** (no window handle → no AX tree → vision; screen-absolute input → must own the desktop → foreground). The two rejected combinations (`desktop`+`ax`/`background`, and window-less click under `window` scope → `desktop_scope_disabled`) are called out, with an honest per-platform support table.

### Tests
New **`modality_capture_mode_test`** — the cross-platform spine of the `capture_mode` axis. It drives each platform's native controlled harness (WPF / AppKit / GTK3) and asserts:

| capture_mode | oracle |
|---|---|
| `ax` | accessibility tree present (`btn-increment`), **no** image |
| `vision` | screenshot present, **no** tree |
| `som` | both (the default) |

The oracle reads the canonical structured fields (`tree_markdown`, `screenshot_png_b64`) so it is transport-agnostic. A bounded settle-retry handles cold-start AX registration, and a pid-diff new-instance window resolver keeps the three tests deterministic under `--test-threads=1`. Missing OS grants (Screen Recording / Accessibility) skip-with-note rather than false-fail.

This closes the audited **"`capture_mode` only on Windows"** gap — the macOS/Linux native vision path was previously untested.

`TEST_SUITE.md` gains a per-platform modality-matrix coverage table with an honest remaining-gaps note.

## Verification — runtime-green with real assertions on all three platforms

| Platform | Harness | Result |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | AppKit | ✅ `ax` tree-only · `vision` image-only · `som` both; 3× deterministic |
| Linux (Ubuntu 24.04) | GTK3 + live AT-SPI | ✅ all 3 assertions exercised; `pyatspi`-confirmed |
| Windows | WPF + UIA (Session 2) | ✅ all 3 assertions; `test result: ok. 3 passed; finished in 6.01s` |

See thread comments for the full per-platform run logs.

## Honest remaining gaps (documented, not closed here)
- `window`/`vision`/`foreground` has no explicit test on any platform.
- The desktop-scope window-less actuator is Windows-only (macOS `click` still requires `pid`), so the desktop cell and its negative gate stay Windows-only until that loop lands on macOS/Linux.

title: feat(cua-driver): window-less desktop-scope click — macOS + Linux (unified interface)
body:
> **Draft** — implementation complete + compiling; end-to-end click-landing verification is pending a dedicated sandbox (dev host was in use). The window-scope rejection gate ran green on macOS.

## What
Implements the macOS half of the **vision/foreground** desktop-scope modality through the **same cua-driver interface** the agent uses on Windows — no parallel actuator binary, no Python. Under `capture_scope=desktop`, `click {x, y}` with **no `pid`/`window_id`** (and no `list_windows`) treats x,y as true screen pixels and lands on whatever is visually frontmost there.

This is the design direction from review: rather than a standalone shim, exercise/extend cua-driver's own desktop-capture interface (skip `window_id`/`list_windows` in desktop mode). The desktop-capture surface (`get_desktop_state`) already existed on macOS; this adds only the missing **window-less input** half.

## Changes
- `input/mouse.rs::click_at_xy_desktop` — posts to the GLOBAL HID tap (`CGEventTapLocation::HID`), not pid-routed, so delivery follows real Z-order. The macOS peer of Windows' `WindowFromPoint` + `SendInput`. Deliberate foreground complement to the background no-foreground contract (still the default).
- `tools/click.rs` — window-less branch before the `pid` requirement, gated on effective `capture_scope`: `desktop` → screen-absolute click; `window` → the same structured `desktop_scope_disabled` error Windows returns.

## Test
`modality_desktop_scope_macos_test` drives it through the cua-driver interface (grounds the click on the AppKit harness increment button's screen-absolute `frame`, asserts the counter advances; plus the window-scope rejection gate). `set_config` is session-scoped (`session` arg) so it never writes the dev's on-disk config.

- ✅ Window-scope rejection gate ran green on macOS.

title: feat(lume): add additional virtio-blk data disks
body:
lume has no way to attach an additional read-write disk to a macOS guest: `--mount` is blocked for macOS guests, and `--usb-storage` builds a VZUSBMassStorageDeviceConfiguration, which Virtualization.framework rejects for macOS guests ("Operation not supported"). The boot disk, however, is attached as virtio-blk (VZVirtioBlockDeviceConfiguration), which works for macOS guests.

This adds a repeatable `--disk <path>` option that attaches additional read-write disks as virtio-blk devices for both macOS and Linux guests. 

Validated on macOS 26 (Tahoe): a macOS guest sees the extra disk, formats it APFS, and runs at boot-disk parity.

title: fix(cua-driver/macos): set_config accepts {key,value} shape (parity with Win/Linux)
body:
## What
macOS `set_config` read only the **direct fields** (`{"capture_scope":"desktop"}`) and silently ignored the **`{key, value}`** shape that Windows, Linux, and the CLI `config set` all accept. So an MCP client sending `{"key":"capture_scope","value":"desktop"}` was a **no-op on macOS** — the agent then saw `capture_scope` still `"window"`. This is the cross-platform inconsistency flagged during the desktop-scope work (and it bit the macOS desktop-scope test until worked around).

## Fix (additive, fully back-compat)
macOS now accepts **both** shapes: a direct field wins if both are present, otherwise it falls back to the `{key, value}` pair — mirroring the Linux normalization. Also adds `key`/`value` to the tool schema (they were rejected under `additionalProperties: false`).

The contract is now identical on all three platforms. Documented in the `set_config` reference.

## Verification
Compiles clean (release). The canonical `{key, value}` shape is what `transport_config_persistence_test` already uses; no behavior change for direct-field callers.

title: ci(cua-driver): automated lane for the interactive modality #[ignore] suite
body:
## Why
The harness/modality integration tests are `#[ignore]` — they need a display, the AT-SPI bus, and the GTK3 harness. So **the rest of CI only compiles them**; their behavioral signal has come from manual VM/host runs at a point in time, not continuous protection. This was called out as the single biggest gap in the desktop-scope confidence review.

## What
A Linux job that actually **runs** them on every cua-driver change:
- `modality_capture_mode_test` (ax→tree-only / vision→image-only / som→both)
- `modality_desktop_scope_linux_test` (window-less screen-absolute click via XTest + the `desktop_scope_disabled` gate)

The GUI session is provided headlessly: **Xvfb** (display) + a per-job **D-Bus session bus** (so AT-SPI `org.a11y.Bus` auto-activates) + **at-spi2-core** (bridge) + GTK3/PyGObject (harness runtime). An AT-SPI reachability probe prints up front for visibility.

## Honest framing
The tests **skip-with-note** when the a11y bus is unavailable rather than false-failing, so a vacuous run is *visible* (no green-for-nothing). **This PR's own run is the experiment**: it tells us whether headless AT-SPI is viable on GitHub runners, or whether this coverage must live in the Nix desktop sessions (`nix-wayland.yml`) instead. If the AT-SPI probe + the `ax`/`som` assertions come back real (not skipped), we have the lane; if not, the follow-up is a Nix-session check.

Runs on free runners, path-filtered to the Rust driver + harness, plus push-to-main and manual dispatch. Companion to — not a replacement for — `nix-build.yml` / `nix-wayland.yml`.

title: feat(cua-driver): add experimental MCP OAuth front door
body:
## What changed

Adds an experimental `cua-driver mcp-oauth` subcommand that serves as an OAuth/DCR front door for an existing local MCP HTTP endpoint.

The new entry point:
- exposes OAuth protected-resource and authorization-server discovery metadata
- supports Dynamic Client Registration, authorization code + PKCE, and token exchange
- stores OAuth clients/codes/tokens in a local JSON store with atomic writes
- validates Bearer tokens and binds token audience/resource to `<public-url>/mcp`
- forwards authenticated `/mcp` requests to a loopback-only upstream such as `http://127.0.0.1:7677/mcp`
- preserves streaming proxy behavior for non-`tools/list` responses
- returns a connector-friendly `tools/list` descriptor view while leaving `tools/call` and other MCP JSON-RPC methods untouched

This does not change the existing `cua-driver mcp`, `serve`, or `mcp_http` behavior.

## Why

Some OAuth-only MCP clients require OAuth discovery and Dynamic Client Registration before they will call an MCP endpoint. This keeps that compatibility layer opt-in and isolated from the existing local stdio/HTTP MCP transports.

## Safety notes

- `--public-url` must be HTTPS.
- `--mcp-upstream` is restricted to loopback HTTP hosts.
- The proxy forwards only selected MCP request headers to the upstream and strips the front-door Bearer token.
- Clients should be configured with the full MCP endpoint, e.g. `https://your-tunnel.example/mcp`.

## Testing

- `cargo check --offline -p cua-driver`
- `cargo test --offline -p cua-driver mcp_oauth -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --offline -p cua-driver parse_positive_u64_accepts_positive_and_rejects_zero_or_invalid -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --offline -p cua-driver manifest_has_documented_top_level_shape -- --nocapture`
- `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check crates/cua-driver/src/mcp_oauth.rs`
- `git diff --check`

Manual acceptance:
- Started local MCP upstream on `127.0.0.1:7677`.
- Exposed `mcp-oauth` through a Tailscale HTTPS URL.
- Connected ChatGPT web to the `/mcp` URL.
- Refreshed actions successfully and confirmed the connector can inspect the desktop via MCP tools.

* **New Features**

title: feat(examples): add Router Learning System — self-improving task routing with multi-tier fallback for Cua agents
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a Router Learning System as a reference example for building production-grade computer-use agents with Cua Driver.

## Problem

Current Cua examples show single-tool usage, but real agents need to gracefully handle failures. When CDP is unavailable, an agent should fall back to Cua pixel automation. When that fails, it should try Vision AI. Current examples don't address this escalation pattern.

## Solution

A compact (~700 lines), self-contained task routing engine with:

- Dynamic path sorting — reorders tiers by historical success_rate / execution_time
- Self-learning — SQLite-backed history that improves after 5+ samples
- Consecutive failure skip — skips paths with 3+ failures
- 10 pre-configured tasks — git_commit, git_push, browser_navigate, browser_fill_input, browser_click_button, app_hotkey, app_type, app_click, app_screenshot, create_github_token

## Why This Matters for Cua

Computer-use agents are entering production. The key challenge is orchestration — which tool to use, what to do when it fails, how to get smarter over time. This router demonstrates the architectural pattern we use at scale, battle-tested across 100+ real desktop automation sessions.

## Files Changed

- examples/router-learning-system/router.py — Main routing engine
- examples/router-learning-system/README.md — Usage documentation

## Testing
