title: fix(cua-driver): avoid false foreground-click failure after Edge chrome action succeeds
body:
## Summary

A desktop-scope foreground click on Microsoft Edge's browser-owned notification indicator can successfully open the permission panel and still return an error:

> The foreground click did not activate its target window.

This makes the action result contradict the externally visible effect.

## Reproduction

1. Launch Edge with a fresh profile on the `windows-latest` hosted runner.
2. Trigger `Notification.requestPermission()` from the page.
3. Escalate the window session to desktop observation.
4. Click the changed browser-chrome indicator with `scope: "desktop"`.
5. Observe the permission panel open, while the `click` result has `isError: true`.

The exact-tag standalone-browser workflow reproduced this on two independent attempts at `3cf5cc1bd701d7c41d823cf995740dc7678200a0`:

- https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/30465760684
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/30465760684/attempts/2

Both reports had 31 delivered cases, 2 expected refusals, and this single failed Edge case. Chrome's equivalent permission-control case passed, and every other Edge case passed.

## Evidence

The recorded behavior shows the Edge “Notifications blocked” panel open after the click. The failure is emitted afterward by the foreground root-window equality check in `platform-windows/src/input/mouse.rs`, so delivery succeeded but verification reported an error.

## Expected

A foreground click that visibly opens the targeted transient browser-chrome surface should not be returned as a failed action. The post-click activation check should account for browser-owned transient surfaces or otherwise verify delivery without producing a false-negative result.

title: fix(cua-driver): accept owned foreground windows after clicks
body:
## What changed

- compare the foreground window and click target by Win32 root-owner activation family after a foreground click
- accept browser-owned transient windows, such as Edge's permission panel, when they belong to the clicked browser
- retain the failure for missing or unrelated foreground windows
- add focused Windows regression coverage for same-root, owned-transient, unrelated, and missing-foreground cases

## Root cause

The click was delivered and Edge opened its browser-owned permission panel, but the postcondition compared `GA_ROOT` handles. Owned transient browser chrome can have a different root handle from the browser window even though both are in the same activation family, producing a false delivery error.

## Impact

Successful foreground clicks that open browser-owned transient chrome no longer report a false activation failure. Clicks that leave an unrelated window foreground still fail closed.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

title: fix(cua-driver): fall back to the releases API when the baked version has no assets
body:
﻿## Problem

Every release opens a window where the public one-liner install fails outright on all three platforms.

Merging the Release Please pull request bumps the baked version constant on `main` and creates the tag, but the release it creates is a **draft** — `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml` publishes it only after the build verifies (`Publish the verified Release Please draft`). Its assets are not downloadable until then. Meanwhile `cua.ai/driver/install.ps1` and `_install-rust.sh` are served **byte-identically from `main`**, so the advertised version cannot be fetched for the length of the release build:

```
==> using baked release: cua-driver-rs-v0.13.0
==> downloading .../cua-driver-rs-0.13.0-windows-x86_64.zip
error: download failed: The remote server returned an error: (404) Not Found.
error:   Try pinning a known-good version via $env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION = '<x.y.z>'.
```

Observed windows (release object `created_at` → `published_at`):

| version | window |
| ------- | ------ |
| 0.13.0  | 3h 24m |
| 0.12.2  | 1h 38m |
| 0.14.0  | 1h 21m |
| 0.12.3  | 44m    |
| 0.12.6  | 39m    |
| 0.12.5  | 30m    |
| 0.12.4  | 23m    |
| 0.11.0  | 12m    |

It recurred while this pull request was open: 0.14.0 was created 2026-07-29T15:23:31Z and published 2026-07-29T16:44:14Z.

A first-time user inside that window has no way through but an explicit version pin — which they have no reason to know exists.

## Fix

Track where the version came from. When a **baked** version has no downloadable asset, resolve the newest published release and retry once.

- An explicit pin (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION`, `-Release`) stays fatal. The user named that version; quietly installing a different one would defy an instruction.
- When the API returns the same version, the tag exists but its assets do not, so the retry is skipped rather than re-issuing an identical 404.
- On Windows the download helper is split out of `Get-ReleaseAsset` so failure *returns* instead of exiting — an `exit 1` inside it is what made the original failure unrecoverable. `Get-ReleaseAsset` now reports the version that actually downloaded and the caller re-derives `$versionedDir` from it, since both the install path and the cursor-theme capability check key off the version.

This is runtime resilience, **not a cure**. The window itself closes only by serving the public installers from the last published release instead of `main`, or by deferring the constant bump until after publish. Both touch release/hosting infrastructure outside this repository, so they are left alone here.

## Also in the code being touched

- The Unix API query used `per_page=40`, which can contain no `cua-driver-rs-v*` tag at all now that lume, Python, and Swift releases interleave with them (573 releases total) — that would make the new fallback a dead end. Raised to the API maximum of 100. The PowerShell resolver already paginates.
- The PowerShell resolver held its matches in `$matches`, the automatic variable every `-match` clobbers. Renamed to `$releaseMatches`.

## Verification

Reproduced against the real broken state (baked 0.13.0 while its assets were still unpublished), installing into an isolated `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME` / `CUA_DRIVER_RS_INSTALL_DIR`:

```
==> using baked release: cua-driver-rs-v0.13.0
WARNING: download failed: (404) Not Found.
WARNING: baked release cua-driver-rs-v0.13.0 has no downloadable windows-x86_64 asset; falling back to the GitHub Releases API
==> resolving latest cua-driver-rs-v* release via GitHub API
==> latest release: cua-driver-rs-v0.12.6
WARNING: falling back to cua-driver-rs-v0.12.6
==> installed ...\0.12.6-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\cua-driver.exe (version 0.12.6)
cua-driver-rs 0.12.6 installed.
```

Then `cua-driver doctor` clean, daemon up, and a full background drive of Calculator through the accessibility path (`launch_app` with `active: false` → `click` 6 × 7 = → `get_window_state` reads 42).

The explicit-pin invariant holds — `CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION=9.9.9` fails without consulting the API:

```
==> using version from $env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION: 9.9.9
WARNING: download failed: (404) Not Found.
error: could not download a windows-x86_64 release asset for cua-driver-rs-v9.9.9.
```

## Tests

New `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_install_version_fallback.py` — 11 tests pinning the invariants that were absent: the baked route falls back, both pin routes do not, the download helper is non-fatal, and the resolved version is adopted before any path or capability check derives from it. Two behavioral tests execute the real Unix resolver with `curl` shadowed by a shell function, asserting `0.9.1` does not outrank `0.12.6` and that a no-match returns non-zero.

Those two are gated on a posix host: on Windows `CreateProcess` searches `System32` before `PATH`, so `subprocess.run(["bash", ...])` always resolves to the WSL launcher rather than any bash on `PATH`. They were verified against a real bash before gating.

`9 passed, 2 skipped` on Windows. No regression in the sibling suites — the 11 pre-existing failures in `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/` reproduce identically on a clean tree on this host (clean: `11 failed, 3 passed`; with this change: `11 failed, 12 passed, 2 skipped`).

Version *agreement* across checked-in sources is deliberately not retested — `.github/scripts/validate_release_versions.py` owns that, and it cannot cover these invariants because at merge time the release genuinely is unpublished.

title: fix(cua-driver): advance installers only after release publication
body:
## Problem

Release Please currently bumps the baked versions in the public `main` installers when it creates the release tag. The GitHub release is still a draft at that point, so the public one-liners advertise assets that do not exist yet. #2683 makes that window survivable; this removes the routine window.

## Fix

- Remove both installer constants from Release Please version updates.
- Track the last fully published installer version independently and validate both installers against it.
- Stamp tag-pinned installer assets with the version they ship.
- After publication, verify the release and every staged asset are public.
- Only then use the release app to atomically advance `main`, with bounded conflict retries and downgrade protection.
- Keep the #2683 fallback as defense in depth for manual drift, removed assets, and interrupted legacy releases.

## Verification

- `143 passed` in `.github/scripts/tests`
- `113 passed, 5 skipped` in `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests` on this host

title: cua-driver (macOS): launch_app completion times out for installed apps in a logged-in VM
body:
## Summary

On macOS 26.5.2 arm64 in a logged-in Apple Virtualization Framework VM, `launch_app` consistently returns:

    Launch failed: Failed to launch <bundle>: NSWorkspace launch did not complete within 30s

This reproduces with installed third-party, system, and built-in apps (`com.google.Chrome`, `com.apple.Safari`, and `com.apple.TextEdit`). The driver has Accessibility and Screen Recording permission, the console is unlocked, and the same logged-in GUI session can launch apps through ordinary LaunchServices-based setup.

## Reproduction

Tested from a source-built signed app/daemon at `1bb489089160f736148840ecd165d7d2a19552b2` (reported version `0.14.1`):

1. Start the daemon in unrestricted mode.
2. Start an MCP session with `capture_scope: auto`.
3. Confirm `check_permissions(prompt: false)` reports `accessibility: true` and `screen_recording: true`.
4. Call `launch_app({bundle_id: "com.apple.TextEdit"})`.

The call blocks for 30 seconds and returns the timeout above. Repeating with Safari and Chrome produces the same result. `list_apps` after the timeout does not show the requested app as running.

## Expected

`launch_app` should return the launched/running PID and window metadata, or a structured launch error from LaunchServices. A missing completion callback should not make every installed app unusable through the tool.

## Suspected area

`platform-macos/src/apps/nsworkspace.rs` waits synchronously for the `NSWorkspace` completion handler on a blocking worker. In this environment, the completion handler appears not to run before `COMPLETION_TIMEOUT`. It may need explicit run-loop scheduling or a fallback that reconciles `NSRunningApplication` state before returning a timeout.

## Acceptance criteria

- A regression test covers a cold launch of TextEdit from the signed daemon in a logged-in macOS VM.
- The call returns a PID/window result without stealing focus.
- If the completion callback is missing but the process starts, the result reconciles actual running-app state instead of returning a false timeout.
- A true launch failure remains structured and bounded.

title: fix(cua-driver): type_text into Screen Sharing repeats a single key
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `type_text` targeting a Screen Sharing window can report that it sent the requested character count while the remote Terminal receives only repeated `a` characters.

## Environment

- Cua Driver: `0.12.3`
- Host: macOS `26.5.2` arm64
- Bundle: `com.trycua.driver`
- Accessibility: granted
- Screen Recording: granted
- Target: Apple Screen Sharing controlling a disposable macOS VM

## Reproduction

1. Connect Apple Screen Sharing to a disposable macOS VM.
2. Open Terminal in the VM and place the insertion point at an empty shell prompt.
3. Snapshot the Screen Sharing window.
4. Call `type_text` against the Screen Sharing PID/window using the pixel form and `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, with a mixed-character shell command as `text`.
5. Snapshot the Screen Sharing window again.

Observed tool result for a 250-character input:

```json
{
  "characters": 250,
  "effect": "unverifiable",
  "path": "key_events_fg",
  "verified": false
}
```

## Actual behavior

The remote Terminal receives a long run of `a` characters instead of the requested mixed-character text. Pressing Return then produces `zsh: command not found` for that repeated-`a` string.

A separate `hotkey(["cmd", "v"])` call also arrived remotely as the literal character `v`, suggesting modifier/key-state forwarding through Screen Sharing is affected by the same delivery path.

## Expected behavior

The remote application should receive the requested characters and modifier state, or Cua Driver should reject/escalate this target instead of reporting only the requested character count.

## Notes

- A before/after screenshot confirmed the prompt was active and the repeated characters appeared only after `type_text`.
- Screen Sharing's “Control Screen” mode was enabled.
- This occurred during disposable VM setup; Screen Sharing/VNC was only the setup and observation channel, not benchmark proof.

title: `check_permissions` / `health_report`'s `screen_capture_capability` can hang the MCP stdio session (macOS, 0.12.x)
body:
**Version**: cua-driver-rs 0.12.3 (macOS 15/Tahoe, Apple silicon), TCC Accessibility + Screen Recording both granted to `com.trycua.driver`.

**Symptom**: serving `check_permissions`, or `health_report` with the `screen_capture_capability`
probe included, can leave a Swift continuation unresumed inside `capture(with:)`. The MCP stdio
session then never answers — it does not error, it stops responding. Any agent host that keeps a
long-lived stdio bridge to the driver stalls with it, and a host that supervises the bridge in-process
can be taken down by the stall rather than by a failure it can catch.

**Impact**: because the failure mode is a hang rather than an error, callers cannot distinguish it
from a slow machine. A diagnostics probe is the last place you want an unbounded wait — it is usually
the call made *because* something already looks wrong.

**Workaround we currently ship** (would like to delete):
- never send `screen_capture_capability` unless explicitly requested; default it into `skip`
- substitute `check_permissions` with `health_report` limited to
  `tcc_accessibility` + `tcc_screen_recording` + `bundle_identity`
- wrap the diagnostics stdio read in a deadline so a hang surfaces as a timeout

**What would let us drop it**: a bounded internal timeout on the capture probe so it returns a
structured failure instead of hanging — ideally with a distinct code so callers can tell
"capture unavailable" from "capture slow".

**Note for anyone hitting this**: `cua-driver check-update` reports the newest tag without saying
whether it is a prerelease. On 2026-07-30 the reported latest (`0.14.1`) and `0.14.0` / `0.13.1` were
all `prerelease: true`, so `update_available: true` was not an actionable upgrade signal. A
`prerelease` field in the `check_for_update` payload would help.

title: lume stop can SIGINT itself after macOS pid wraparound (lsof picks the stopper's own pid)
body:
## Summary

`lume stop <name>` can kill itself instead of the VM process. On machines where macOS pids have wrapped past 99999, the stop command reliably exits immediately with code 130 (killed by SIGINT) and the VM keeps running.

## Root cause

In `VM.stop()` (libs/lume/src/VM/VM.swift):

1. The config file is opened read-only (`FileHandle(forReadingFrom:)`).
2. `lsof -F p <config>` is used to find the process holding the lock, and the **first** `p<pid>` line is taken as the lock holder.
3. Because the stop process itself has the file open, it appears in the lsof output too. lsof output is pid-sorted; after a pid wraparound the stop process's own pid is often *smaller* than the VM process's pid, so the stop process sorts first.
4. `kill(pid, SIGINT)` is then sent to the stop process itself → it dies instantly (exit 130), buffered logs are lost, and the VM is never stopped.

## Reproduction

On a Mac where current pids have wrapped (easy to check: spawn a shell, `echo $$` shows a value much lower than an older long-running process):

```bash
lume run my-vm --display none &   # note its pid, e.g. 98700
# from another process whose pid is lower (post-wrap):
lume stop my-vm
echo $?   # → 130, instantly; VM still running
```

Minimal demonstration of the mechanism:

```bash
exec 9< ~/.lume/my-vm/config.json   # hold the file open like stop() does
lsof -F p ~/.lume/my-vm/config.json # own pid appears, sorted first if smaller
```

```
self_pid=91633
p91633   ← lsof lists the caller itself, first
p91634   ← actual VM process comes second
```

## Suggested fix

Exclude the caller's own pid when parsing lsof output (and skip non-`p` lines), then take the first remaining pid:

```swift
let selfPid = getpid()
let lockPids = String(decoding: outputData, as: UTF8.self)
    .split(separator: "\n")
    .filter { $0.hasPrefix("p") }
    .compactMap { pid_t($0.dropFirst()) }
    .filter { $0 != selfPid }
guard let pid = lockPids.first else { ... }
```

We have been running with this patch locally; `lume stop` from a separate process then works correctly (graceful SIGINT, SIGKILL fallback after timeout).

## Environment

- lume 0.5.0 (main @ 1bb4890)
- macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon)

title: lume create --ipsw crashes with SIGTRAP: VZMacOSInstaller created off the VM's dispatch queue
body:
## Summary

`lume create <name> --ipsw <restore image>` crashes immediately with SIGTRAP (`EXC_BREAKPOINT`, exit 133) on macOS 26 / Swift 6.2, leaving the VM stuck in `provisioning` state.

## Root cause

`DarwinVirtualizationService.installMacOS(imagePath:progressHandler:)` (libs/lume/src/Virtualization/VMVirtualizationService.swift) creates `VZMacOSInstaller` inside an unstructured `Task { }`:

```swift
try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
    Task {
        let installer = VZMacOSInstaller(
            virtualMachine: virtualMachine, restoringFromImageAt: imagePath.url)
        ...
```

`VZMacOSInstaller.init(virtualMachine:restoringFromImageAt:)` asserts it is called on the virtual machine's dispatch queue (`_dispatch_assert_queue_fail`). The unstructured task runs on the cooperative thread pool, not on the VM's serial queue (`ai.cua.lume.virtual-machine.darwin`), so the assertion fails and the process traps.

Crash report (faulting thread):

```
_dispatch_assert_queue_fail
dispatch_assert_queue
-[VZMacOSInstaller initWithVirtualMachine:restoreImageURL:]
@nonobjc VZMacOSInstaller.init(virtualMachine:restoringFromImageAt:)
closure #1 in closure #1 in DarwinVirtualizationService.installMacOS(imagePath:progressHandler:)
```

## Reproduction

```bash
lume create test-vm --os macOS --ipsw <any supported restore.ipsw> --unattended tahoe
echo $?   # → 133 (SIGTRAP)
lume ls   # test-vm stuck in provisioning / ipsw_install
```

Whether the trap fires appears timing-dependent (it succeeded once for us, then failed 3/3 runs), but the queue contract is unambiguous: the installer is created on an arbitrary task context instead of the VM's queue.

## Suggested fix

Create and start the installer on the VM's dispatch queue, and retain it for the duration of the install:

```swift
let handle = virtualMachineHandle
try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { (continuation: CheckedContinuation<Void, Error>) in
    handle.queue.async {
        let installer = VZMacOSInstaller(
            virtualMachine: handle.machine, restoringFromImageAt: imagePath.url)
        // retain installer + KVO observer until the completion handler runs
        installer.install { result in ... }
    }
}
```

We run with this patch locally; `lume create --ipsw ... --unattended tahoe` then completes end-to-end (install + offline unattended setup + marker cleared) in a few minutes.

## Environment

- lume 0.5.0 (main @ 1bb4890)
- macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon), Swift 6.2.3

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve Screen Sharing keyboard input
body:
## Summary

- send printable US-layout ASCII through Apple Screen Sharing as physical foreground key events instead of Unicode events with a zero keycode
- use Apple's bare `CGEventCreateKeyboardEvent(NULL, ...)` sequence so Shift and modifier chords survive forwarding
- fail closed with structured foreground escalation for Screen Sharing background text and modifier chords
- validate the complete text payload before dispatch so unsupported Unicode cannot be partially typed

## Root cause

Apple Screen Sharing forwards the physical keyboard identity of synthesized events. The generic Unicode path assigned every character keycode 0, which the guest interpreted as repeated `a` characters. PID-routed base-key events also lost modifier state, turning Cmd+V into literal `v`.

## User impact

Foreground Screen Sharing text and common modifier chords now arrive correctly. Unsafe background delivery is explicitly refused instead of reporting an unverifiable success that may corrupt guest input. Other applications retain their existing PID-routed Unicode behavior.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` — 249 passed
- `cargo check -p platform-macos --lib`
- `git diff --check`
- exact-source nested Lume macOS VMs: mixed-case letters, digits, underscore, and punctuation arrived byte-for-byte
- foreground Cmd+V preserved Command and produced the exact expected target bytes
- background text and modifier attempts returned `SCREEN_SHARING_REQUIRES_FOREGROUND_HID`; a post-Return leak oracle remained zero bytes

Closes #2690

title: Linux/X11: existing_profile attaches but get_browser_state fails on Chrome 151 — Browser.getWindowForTarget "Browser window not found"
body:
## Bug description

On Linux/X11 with Google Chrome 151, `browser_prepare` with
`strategy.kind=existing_profile` succeeds, but every following browser call fails because the driver
cannot correlate the native X11 window with a CDP target:

```json
{
  "refusal": {
    "code": "browser_route_unavailable",
    "message": "Browser.getWindowForTarget failed while proving the native window: CDP Browser.getWindowForTarget failed (-32000): Browser window not found"
  },
  "status": "refused"
}
```

The attachment itself is clean:

```json
{
  "action": "attached_existing_profile",
  "prepared": true,
  "endpoint_ownership": { "method": "listening_socket_pid", "detail": "/proc owner plus /json/version" }
}
```

This machine upgraded Chrome from `150.0.7871.186` to `151.0.7922.71` on 2026-07-30, and the
failure appeared the same day, so this looks like a Chrome 151 regression or behavior change rather
than a config problem.

## Environment

- OS: Linux Mint (Cinnamon), X11 (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11`)
- cua-driver: `0.14.1` (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`)
- Google Chrome: `151.0.7922.71` (was `150.0.7871.186` until 2026-07-30)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Chrome with CDP on a non-default profile directory (see note below):

   ```bash
   google-chrome --user-data-dir="$HOME/.config/google-chrome-cua" --remote-debugging-port=9222
   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version     # responds, webSocketDebuggerUrl present
   ```

2. Start the daemon with the port exported:

   ```bash
   CUA_DRIVER_CDP_PORT=9222 cua-driver serve \
     --permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals
   ```

3. Attach:

   ```bash
   cua-driver call start_session --json '{"session":"t","capture_scope":"window"}'
   cua-driver call list_windows                       # take the Chrome pid + window_id
   cua-driver call browser_prepare --json '{"session":"t","pid":PID,"window_id":WID,"strategy":{"kind":"existing_profile"}}'
   # -> attached_existing_profile, prepared: true, ~0.05s
   ```

4. Use it:

   ```bash
   cua-driver call get_browser_state --json '{"session":"t","pid":PID,"window_id":WID}'
   # -> browser_route_unavailable / Browser.getWindowForTarget (-32000)
   ```

## What I ruled out

- **Not the onboarding window.** The fresh profile opens `chrome://profile-customization`; I closed
  that target and retried — same refusal.
- **Not a missing page target.** Created a normal `about:blank` tab via `PUT /json/new`; `/json/list`
  then showed `about:blank`, `chrome://newtab/` as `page` targets. Same refusal.
- **Not the wrong window.** Two Chrome X11 windows existed; I re-ran `browser_prepare` and
  `get_browser_state` against each in turn. Identical refusal for both.
- **Not a stale binding.** Re-ran `browser_prepare` immediately before each `get_browser_state`, as
  the prepare response instructs ("Bind the native window again before using browser capabilities").

## Side note that affects the documented existing_profile flow on Linux

Chrome >= 136 refuses remote debugging on the default profile directory:

```
DevTools remote debugging requires a non-default data directory. Specify this using --user-data-dir.
```

Passing `--user-data-dir` explicitly still fails if it points at the default path — the directory
itself must be non-default. So on current Chrome, "attach to the browser the user already has open"
is only reachable if that browser was already started with a separate `--user-data-dir` plus
`--remote-debugging-port`. It may be worth documenting, since the natural reading of
`existing_profile` is the user's everyday browser.

title: Linux/AT-SPI: get_window_state returns only the bare window root when an app registers twice on the a11y bus (first pid match is an empty application accessible, Qt/FeatherPad)
body:
## Environment

* cua-driver **0.13.1**, native Wayland backend
* Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, GNOME Shell 50.1 (Wayland), at-spi2-core 2.60.4
* Qt 6.10.2 (libqt6gui6 6.10.2+dfsg-7), FeatherPad 1.6.3 as the Qt specimen
* Screen reader active (driver sets `ScreenReaderEnabled=true`, #2010), so
  Qt's a11y bridge is up without extra env vars

## Symptom

Against a running, fully accessible FeatherPad window:

```
$ cua-driver call get_window_state --json '{"pid":437805,"window_id":337}'
element_count: 1
  {'role': 'window', 'label': None}
```

One element, the bare window root, no label — while `pyatspi` reads **86
elements** (menu bar, 70 named menu items, text area with caret) from the very
same process at the same moment. All element-addressed tools are dead on this
app; checkpoints that read texts/roles see an "empty" window.

## Root cause (measured, not guessed)

The process is registered **twice** on the accessibility bus. Querying the
registry root's children and asking each one directly:

```
GetChildren on org.a11y.atspi.Registry → two entries with the same pid:
  :1.665  Name='featherpad'  ChildCount=0   ← registered first
  :1.666  Name='FeatherPad'  ChildCount=1   ← the real tree
```

`app_for_pid` in
`crates/platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs` walks the registry children and
**returns the first entry whose pid matches**:

```rust
if cpid == Some(pid) {
    ...
    return match call(accessible_for(conn, &child)).await { ... };
}
```

The first match is the empty hull (`ChildCount=0`), so the walk yields just
the synthesized window root. The registry consistently lists the empty
registration first on this system (observed across several app restarts).

Why Qt ends up with two connections (an early one named after `argv[0]`, a
later one with the display name once the bridge is live) we have not
diagnosed — but the driver's failure mode exists regardless of who causes the
duplicate: first-match-by-pid silently loses whenever any extra, empty
application accessible shares the pid.

## Repro

1. GNOME Wayland session with a11y enabled (the driver's own
   `ScreenReaderEnabled=true` suffices).
2. Start FeatherPad (`featherpad` from the Ubuntu archive).
3. List the registry root's children with pid + `ChildCount` (script below) —
   two entries for the pid, the childless one first.
4. `cua-driver call get_window_state` for that pid → `element_count: 1`.

```python
import gi
gi.require_version("Gio", "2.0")
from gi.repository import Gio, GLib
session = Gio.bus_get_sync(Gio.BusType.SESSION, None)
addr = session.call_sync("org.a11y.Bus", "/org/a11y/bus", "org.a11y.Bus",
    "GetAddress", None, None, Gio.DBusCallFlags.NONE, 3000, None).unpack()[0]
bus = Gio.DBusConnection.new_for_address_sync(addr,
    Gio.DBusConnectionFlags.AUTHENTICATION_CLIENT |
    Gio.DBusConnectionFlags.MESSAGE_BUS_CONNECTION, None, None)
kids = bus.call_sync("org.a11y.atspi.Registry",
    "/org/a11y/atspi/accessible/root", "org.a11y.atspi.Accessible",
    "GetChildren", None, None, Gio.DBusCallFlags.NONE, 3000, None).unpack()[0]
for busname, _path in kids:
    pid = bus.call_sync("org.freedesktop.DBus", "/org/freedesktop/DBus",
        "org.freedesktop.DBus", "GetConnectionUnixProcessID",
        GLib.Variant("(s)", (busname,)), None,
        Gio.DBusCallFlags.NONE, 3000, None).unpack()[0]
    cc = bus.call_sync(busname, "/org/a11y/atspi/accessible/root",
        "org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties", "Get",
        GLib.Variant("(ss)", ("org.a11y.atspi.Accessible", "ChildCount")),
        None, Gio.DBusCallFlags.NONE, 3000, None).unpack()[0]
    print(busname, pid, cc)
```

## Suggested fix

In `app_for_pid`, don't return the first pid match unconditionally: keep
scanning, **prefer a matching application accessible with `ChildCount > 0`**,
and fall back to a childless match only if no populated one exists. We ship
exactly that rule in our own AT-SPI client since running into this, and it
resolves the symptom (86 elements instead of 1); the childless-fallback
preserves today's behaviour for apps that genuinely expose nothing.

Related but distinct from #2349 (dead persistent connection → whole desktop
looks empty): here the connection is healthy and the emptiness is per-app,
caused by duplicate registration.

title: feat(cua-driver)!: standardize action results
body:
## Summary

- replace legacy action-specific structured outputs with one closed `ActionResult` across all 18 pointer, keyboard, value, and browser-input tools
- keep task postconditions separate in `verify_state`, while preserving diagnostic MCP text/images and an internal rich execution record
- expose typed `action` and `verification` views in Rust, Python, and TypeScript; intentionally reject legacy or missing action payloads
- advertise and validate the same action output schema at the live MCP boundary, and retain a deliberately lossy `verified` adapter only in `computer-server` compatibility output
- document the 0.14 → 0.15 migration and update the canonical agent skill for stop/retry/escalation ownership

## Why

The old `verified` boolean and platform-specific request echoes mixed dispatch acknowledgement with evidence of effect. That made no-op or under-verified actions easy for harnesses to mistake for success. This cutover narrows the public contract to stable outcome facts (`effect`, `route`, optional delivery/evidence/escalation) and leaves visual interpretation and task completion to the multimodal agent harness.

## Breaking impact

The outer MCP `ToolResult` envelope is unchanged. For the 18 action tools, `structuredContent` is intentionally breaking: legacy fields and action-specific output types are removed. SDK callers migrate from `result.verified` to `result.action.effect`; postcondition callers use `result.verification.status`. Daemon and SDK must be upgraded together because 0.15 clients fail closed on 0.14 action payloads.

This PR now targets `main` directly and includes the internal action-truth layer that previously lived in #2711. Its prerequisite verification work landed through #2705 before this branch was rebased.

## Review

Claude Code Fable reviewed the complete design and implementation and returned **safe after fixes**. Its two release blockers are covered here:

- Windows `PostMessage` text is confirmed only when read-back changed and contains the complete requested text.
- browser refusal telemetry recognizes `ActionResult.effect == refused` and recovers only the closed refusal code from preserved diagnostic text, without retaining prose or widening the result schema.

title: cua-driver (Linux/X11): pixel click panics the worker in evdev — assertion failed: name_bytes.len() + 1 < UINPUT_MAX_NAME_SIZE
body:
## Summary

On Linux/X11, escalating an accessibility click to a **pixel** click kills a `tokio-rt-worker` with a panic inside `evdev`, in the code path that creates the ephemeral uinput pointer:

```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at
/github/home/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/evdev-0.12.2/src/uinput.rs:209:9:
assertion failed: name_bytes.len() + 1 < UINPUT_MAX_NAME_SIZE
```

After the panic the daemon keeps listening but is effectively dead for input: every subsequent call fails with

```
A connection to the bus can't be made
```

Reproduced twice, deterministically, on the same setup.

## Why this is worth fixing regardless of the name

Two separate problems, and the second one is the expensive one:

1. The uinput device name exceeds the kernel's `UINPUT_MAX_NAME_SIZE` (80 bytes). Whatever the name is built from should be clamped or truncated.
2. **An `assert!` inside a dependency takes down a worker thread instead of the call returning an error.** From the caller's side this does not look like "the click failed" — it looks like the *application under test* stopped responding, because the driver goes quiet and every later call reports a bus error. It cost a full debugging session to attribute the symptom correctly: a GUI app was suspected of a main-loop freeze, when in fact the harness's own cleanup had killed it after the driver died.

Returning a structured error here (`{"code": "uinput_unavailable", ...}`) would make the failure self-describing even if the name issue is not addressed.

## What triggers it

The accessibility action is tried first and the driver reports:

```json
{"effect":"suspected_noop","path":"ax",
 "escalation":{"reason":"non-AX surface — act by pixel (x,y) off the screenshot in this response (an element px action).",
               "recommended":"px"}}
```

The caller then follows that recommendation and issues a pixel `click` with `{pid, window_id, x, y, session}`. That is the call that panics. Elements which *do* expose a real AT-SPI action never reach the uinput path and work fine — so this only bites on surfaces where the driver itself asks for pixel escalation.

## Not the cause

The daemon socket path length. First observed with a 57-character socket path under `~/.cache/...`; moving it to `/tmp/rv-cua.sock` (12 characters) and shortening the session id to two characters reproduced the identical panic. So the over-long string comes from somewhere else in the name construction.

`strings` on the binary shows the pointers are pooled in a `HashMap<String, Arc<Mutex<evdev::uinput::VirtualDevice>>>` behind `platform_linux::input::uinput_pointers` (`OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<..>>>`), alongside literals `" uinput pointer"` and `"missing uinput pointer for '"`. If the map key doubles as the device name, that key is the thing to clamp.

I could not build a minimal reproducer without a real toolkit window: `click` with `scope=desktop` is refused with `desktop_escalation_required`, and a window-scoped click needs a live window plus an element index, so the uinput path is not reachable from a bare daemon.

## Environment

| | |
| --- | --- |
| cua-driver | 0.14.1 |
| OS | Manjaro Linux, kernel 6.18.39-1-MANJARO, x86_64 |
| Display | Xvfb 800x600/1600x900 + openbox, private session bus, private `at-spi-bus-launcher` + `at-spi2-registryd` |
| `/dev/uinput` | `crw-rw----+ root:input`, user **is** in `input` |
| Session | X11 (not the Wayland backend) |

`health_report` reports `overall: ok` — AT-SPI and screen capture both pass — right up until the first pixel click.

## Suggested fix

- Clamp the uinput device name to `UINPUT_MAX_NAME_SIZE - 1` bytes (truncate on a char boundary) before handing it to `evdev`.
- Wrap the `VirtualDevice` construction so a failure returns an error to the caller rather than unwinding a runtime worker; a panicking worker leaves the daemon in a state that reports a misleading bus error for the rest of its life.

Possibly related but distinct: #2304 (ephemeral uinput pointer, Qt/Plasma SIGSEGV).

title: fix(cua-driver): extend long Linux typing deadlines
body:
## Summary

- make Unix daemon response deadlines action-aware
- allow long Linux `type_text` calls to include the platform's 10 ms/character pacing plus bounded overhead
- preserve the 120-second default for ordinary calls and allow callers to override it with `CUA_DRIVER_DAEMON_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS`
- cover a 16,000-character request in the deadline policy and through the Python SDK Unix-socket path

## Root cause

The shared Unix daemon client used one hard-coded 120-second read deadline for every action. Linux X11 keyboard delivery intentionally paces characters, so a healthy 16k-character mutation can exceed that transport deadline even when the daemon is still making progress.

## User impact

Long Linux typing no longer fails at the transport boundary solely because its predictable pacing exceeds 120 seconds. Other calls keep the existing fail-fast behavior, while unusually slow targets can opt into a larger explicit deadline.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check`
- `python3 -m py_compile libs/cua-driver/python/tests/test_uniffi_loader.py`

title: fix(cua-driver): verify Linux process control results

## Summary

- execute Linux `launch_path` values through the documented shell contract with detached stdio
- observe bounded startup before reporting a live PID and retain an async child reaper

Linux `launch_app` treated a shell command line as whitespace-delimited argv, inherited the MCP daemon's stdio, dropped the child handle, and reported `running: true` without checking whether the child had already exited. title: fix(cua-driver): open Finder folder URLs reliably
body:
## Summary

- normalize local `launch_app.urls` before handing them to macOS, including `~/...` paths
- dispatch Finder folder opens to Finder's synchronous native selector on the AppKit main queue, with a bounded wait
- avoid blocking that selector with the wildcard activation observer, while retaining targeted post-launch focus restoration

## Root cause

The existing macOS preflight expanded a leading `~`, but the original string was still handed to `NSURL.fileURLWithPath`. Finder therefore received a literal home-relative target and `NSWorkspace` reported that Finder could not be launched.

Using `NSWorkspace.openURLs(...withApplicationAt:)` for an already-running Finder also fails to complete reliably. The fallback process reconciliation cannot prove that a folder-open action occurred because Finder was already running. Finder's synchronous `selectFile(nil, inFileViewerRootedAtPath:)` selector returns an actionable success boolean for this Finder-specific folder operation, but AppKit requires it on the main thread. The driver therefore dispatches the narrow Finder handoff to its existing AppKit main queue, bounds the wait, and restores the prior foreground app after Finder performs it.

This is a follow-up to #1719 (local URL preflight) and #2697 (launch callback reconciliation). Repository issue/PR searches found no duplicate for Finder folder URL handoff.

## User impact

`launch_app` can open an existing local folder in Finder when the caller supplies either an absolute path or a home-relative path, without timing out on Finder's missing NSWorkspace callback and while restoring foreground focus.

## Benchmark relevance and scope

This is the first driver-owned failure in the valid task-15 full-system trace (`20260731-211044-full-system-cua-skill-15-move-conflict-t1`):

1. Immediately after session setup, the agent called `launch_app` with bundle ID `com.apple.finder` and `urls: ["~/Desktop/BenchInbox"]`.
2. That exact request failed twice with `The application “Finder” could not be launched because it was not found.`
3. The agent then spent the run navigating overlapping Finder windows manually; the run timed out after 500 seconds and never moved the renamed PNG.

The focused normalization regression below uses the benchmark's exact `~/Desktop/BenchInbox` input, while the Finder handoff regression proves that an existing local directory is selected only for `com.apple.finder`. The source-built live proof confirms the combined public-tool path opens the requested folder.

This PR deliberately does not claim to fix task 15 end to end. In the GUI-common trace, benchmark setup had already opened both `BenchInbox` and `BenchImages`, so no Finder URL launch was attempted. That run successfully renamed `a.png` to `a-new.png`, then repeatedly received `effect: unverifiable` for cross-window copy/move hotkeys and timed out without moving it. Stable Finder item selection and verified cross-window move are a separate driver-owned issue and should be handled independently.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p platform-macos apps::tests::finder_folder_handoff_is_narrowly_selected`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos tools::launch_app::tests::launch_url_normalization_expands_home_relative_paths`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos apps::nsworkspace::tests`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` — 268 passed on merged head `c50bf5fc2c1ad8a40f0c96dc7a1eecbc13a582a4`
- `cargo check -p platform-macos --lib`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

Fresh Lume macOS 26.5.2 verification used a signed source build from the exact pushed head `c50bf5fc2c1ad8a40f0c96dc7a1eecbc13a582a4` (`get_config.source_sha` matched; SHA-256 `791b1cd7d41b288bced1dd4232518a8f6f108248d34bd5bb0a36ca1718fb27dc`). Before the action no window had the target title. The exact home-relative request `~/Desktop/CuaFinderExactProof.2754.provenance` returned Finder PID 433 with `requested`, `process_running`, and `window_ready` all true; a follow-up `list_windows` observed window 423 titled `CuaFinderExactProof.2754.provenance`, and `get_window_state` resolved 57 accessibility elements with a valid screenshot frame.

title: fix(cua-driver): reuse existing app windows before launching
body:
## Summary

This draft expands the existing isolated-launch refusal fix into one cross-platform app-acquisition and lifecycle correction:

- preserve typed **NEW_APPLICATION_INSTANCE_UNAVAILABLE** reporting for macOS isolated-launch failures
- let **launch_app** carry the public session label so the first ordinary call lazily creates the named session
- make default acquisition atomically reuse one exact existing process/window before requesting a launch
- add **instance_policy: reuse_or_launch | reuse_only | new** and canonical reuse-versus-launch disposition
- replace silent unsupported/no-op instance behavior with truthful structured results
- align MCP initialization instructions, generated contracts, reference docs, and bundled Cua Driver skills

## Behavior

**reuse_or_launch** is the default on macOS, Windows, and Linux. **reuse_only** never sends a launch request. **new** requires a distinct process: macOS verifies that the returned PID is new, while Windows and Linux fail closed because their shell/desktop activation paths cannot guarantee a distinct live app instance.

Successful results retain **requested**, **process_running**, and **window_ready**, and add:

- **request_sent**
- **process_disposition: reused | created | none**
- **window_disposition: reused | materialized | none**

The deprecated **creates_new_application_instance: true** spelling maps to **instance_policy: new**.

## Root causes fixed

The lifecycle runtime already created sessions on first ordinary dispatch, but the MCP and skill prose still presented **start_session** as a normal step zero. **launch_app** was session-managed internally while all three public schemas rejected **session**.

App launch semantics also drifted by platform: macOS always sent an open request, Windows accepted the new-instance field as a no-op, Linux advertised non-idempotent launch behavior, and responses did not identify reuse versus creation.

## Scope and progress

- [x] retain the original macOS unavailable-isolated-instance refusal
- [x] add shared lazy-session launch schema and guidance
- [x] add shared instance policy, strict compatibility parsing, and typed launch-state disposition
- [x] implement atomic reuse-first acquisition on macOS
- [x] implement exact executable/process reuse on Windows and Linux when identity is provable
- [x] fail closed for reuse-only misses, ambiguity, and unsupported distinct-instance guarantees
- [x] update MCP initialization instructions, generated contract, reference docs, and bundled skills
- [x] add focused core, schema, platform, and skill tests

## Validation

- **cargo fmt --all -- --check**
- **cargo test -q -p cua-driver-contract** — 32 unit + 1 generator test passed
- **cargo run -q -p cua-driver-contract --bin cua-contract-gen -- all --check**
- **cargo test -q -p cua-driver-core** — 542 unit + 5 integration passed; 1 unrelated test ignored
- **cargo test -q -p platform-macos --lib** — 345 passed
- **cargo test -q -p cua-driver --test schema_consistency_test** — 4 passed
- **cargo check -p platform-linux -p platform-windows** — host adapter checks passed
- **ZSTD_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG=1 PKG_CONFIG_ALLOW_CROSS=1 cargo +stable check -p platform-windows --tests --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc** — real Windows implementation and tests compiled
- **git diff --check**
- **documentation generator --check** — generated reference docs are current
- **UniFFI bindings generator --check** — Python and TypeScript bindings are current

The native Linux cross-target check is blocked on this Mac before platform compilation because the host lacks **xtst.pc**; canonical Linux CI remains required. Windows packaged-app identity cannot be correlated to a running PID without activation, and Linux reuse depends on compositor/window PID metadata, so those cases fail closed under **reuse_only**.

The exact candidate SHA is **628cc196210278c028b3795afdbe59cc78afcb7c**. Canonical Linux run [31889546023](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/31889546023) and Windows run [31889545981](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/31889545981) are in progress. title: fix(cua-driver): index writable native value controls
body:
## Summary

- index native macOS controls whose `AXValue` is writable even when they expose no AX action names
- limit the additional settable probe to the small family of value-control roles
- document `set_value` for whole-value replacement and `type_text` for insertion at the cursor

## Motivation

A transient native text editor can be visible in the accessibility outline but have no `element_index` when it exposes no action names. The agent can read the value yet cannot address the control with `set_value`. Finder inline rename is a minimal reproduction: select an item, press Return, inspect the window, and observe the writable `AXTextField`.

## Verification

- direct `rustfmt --check` on the changed Rust sources
- `git diff --check`
- pure addressability tests cover the allowed writable-control roles and excluded display/container roles
- fresh Lume macOS 26.5.2 source build and live Finder verification at exact pushed head `6f8f7aba5a9d33adef763e8c23e0898338e30d2c` (`get_config.source_sha` matched; signed binary SHA-256 `b21316fc77fe2fe0f45f53fdf1581ba41f7122ee40c58274cb295ca1215be95c`): Finder inline rename exposed an actionless writable `AXTextField` with `element_index: 0`; `set_value` returned confirmed value-readback evidence, the next Cua snapshot showed `renamed-by-2766-6f8f7ab.txt`, and the guest filesystem confirmed the committed rename

title: fix(lume): refuse writable VM starts when host free space is unsafe
body:
## Summary

Lume can start and run a writable sparse-disk macOS VM when the host volume has almost no allocatable space. The guest still reports the virtual disk logical free capacity, then ordinary guest writes fail and its APFS Data volume becomes unusable.

## Reproduction

Environment:

- Lume 0.5.0
- arm64 macOS host and guest
- host Data volume: approximately 115 MiB available
- stopped source VM: 50 GiB virtual disk, approximately 26 GiB allocated
- cloned guest initially reported approximately 21 GiB available

Steps:

1. Clone the stopped VM.
2. Start the clone.
3. Verify /System/Volumes/Data read-only with diskutil verifyVolume; it initially reports the volume appears OK.
4. Write a large development toolchain into the guest.
5. Attempt ordinary writes such as touch ~/ascii-test or mkdir ~/ascii-dir.
6. Re-run the read-only Data-volume verification.

Observed after the host-backed disk needs more blocks:

    touch: ...: Illegal byte sequence
    mkdir: ...: Illegal byte sequence
    error: could not freeze volume: Illegal byte sequence
    File system check exit code is 71

The VM logical free-space report did not reflect that its sparse backing store could not grow. The affected clone was stopped and quarantined.

## Expected behavior

Before clone or start, Lume should compare host allocatable capacity with a conservative writable-disk reserve. If it cannot safely guarantee growth, it should refuse the operation with a clear error. At minimum, get or run should expose host-capacity risk rather than allowing guest logical free space to imply that writes are safe.

## Suggested regression

Use a bounded test backing volume with insufficient physical capacity, start a sparse-disk guest, and require Lume to fail before the guest can accept writes. Verify that the refusal names required versus available host space and leaves the source VM untouched.

title: macOS menu traversal can lose safe handles after queried snapshots
body:
## Summary

Native macOS menu traversal can lose the current safe element handles when a queried `get_window_state` response is persisted for size. A caller without filesystem access may then reuse remembered bare numeric indices after a re-snapshot, silently targeting different controls.

This is an agent-operability issue, not an AX delivery failure: the Driver correctly refuses a disabled target, but another shifted index can remain enabled and perform the wrong action.

## Version and environment

- Cua Driver 0.16.0
- macOS 26.5
- Native TextEdit window

## Minimal synthetic reproduction

1. Snapshot a frontmost TextEdit window.
2. Find the `AXMenuBarItem "Window"` and invoke `pick`.
3. Re-snapshot with `include_screenshot:false, query:"Left"`.
4. Traverse `Window > Move & Resize > Left`.

Observed index movement across two snapshots:

| Index | Earlier snapshot | Later snapshot |
|---:|---|---|
| 279 | `Move & Resize` | `Zoom All` |
| 282 | `Left` | disabled separator |
| 283 | `Right` | `Move & Resize` |
| 286 | another menu row | `Left` |

The queried later response was approximately 52 KB because `query` filters `tree_markdown` but retains the complete structured `elements` payload. The MCP host persisted the response rather than returning the matching rows inline. In a tool-only environment without file access, the caller could not recover the new token/index from the persisted result.

The installed macOS guidance also says closed menu subtrees are skipped until opened, but the initial snapshot included closed `Move & Resize` descendants as disabled actionable rows. That makes pre-open indices look reusable even though every re-snapshot replaces the index cache.

## Expected

A tool-only caller should be able to complete the documented two-snapshot menu flow without reading a persisted file and without relying on bare numeric indices from an earlier snapshot.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- Provide an opt-in query mode that returns matching structured elements plus their ancestor chain while preserving original indices and tokens.
- Ensure menu-flow examples use `element_token`, so a stale handle fails explicitly after any re-snapshot.
- Align the closed-menu-subtree behavior with the installed guidance, or update the guidance to describe the actual platform behavior.
- Add a macOS test covering `Window > Move & Resize > Left` across successive snapshots and proving that an old handle cannot activate a different menu item.

## Impact

The caller can perform an unintended but non-destructive menu action and exhaust its task deadline even though the desired menu item is present and actionable.

title: [RFC]: Expose platform control IDs in structured snapshots
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Add an optional platform-neutral `id` field to structured accessibility elements. On Windows, populate it from UIA `AutomationId` for native host controls.

### Motivation and current state

A Windows control can have a stable `AutomationId` without exposing Invoke, Value, Toggle, or Selection patterns. The current snapshot omits such controls from its indexed elements, so callers cannot address them by their developer-assigned ID.

Closed PR #1993 proposed a broader `stable_id` and `find_element` model. This RFC asks for the smallest additive subset needed by current structured snapshots. It does not reopen that broader query surface.

### Goals

- Expose developer-assigned host control IDs through one platform-neutral field.
- Keep a host control addressable when its stable ID is its only useful property.
- Keep existing Markdown row syntax compatible; newly indexed ID-only controls may add rows.
- Exclude unstable IDs from web content.

### Non-goals

- Define IDs for controls whose platform provider does not supply one.
- Treat DOM IDs as native control IDs.
- Change action discovery or delivery.
- Add element lookup in this RFC.

### Proposal

Add optional `id` to each structured element. On Windows, read it from a non-empty UIA `AutomationId`. A native host control with such an ID remains indexed even without an action pattern. Document nodes and their descendants count as web content and do not contribute IDs. Disabled host controls remain observable by ID.

### Alternatives considered

- Require an action pattern: stable host controls remain invisible.
- Expose `automation_id`: this leaks a Windows-specific name into the shared output.
- Parse IDs from Markdown: this preserves an untyped compatibility format instead of the structured contract.
- Revive the full `stable_id` and `find_element` design from #1993: it may be the long-term direction, but it is broader than this snapshot omission.

### Compatibility and migration

The field is optional and additive. Existing Markdown row syntax does not change. Snapshots may gain rows for controls that become indexable by ID. Clients may use `id` when present and must continue to handle its absence.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

The field exposes only the identifier already published by the platform accessibility provider. Web-content IDs are excluded to avoid noisy or unstable page data. No new telemetry is added.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

- A host control with only a stable ID appears in structured output.
- Blank IDs do not make a node indexable.
- Document nodes and descendants do not make web content indexable by ID.
- Disabled host controls remain observable by ID.
- Existing action-pattern indexing still works.
- A native harness proves both an actionable ID and an ID-only control in structured output.

### Cross-platform shape

The field name is platform-neutral. Windows can populate it from UIA `AutomationId`. macOS has `AXIdentifier`; Linux AT-SPI has `AccessibleId` on stacks whose deployed adapter exposes it. This RFC does not claim untested macOS or Linux implementations.

### Platform decision

The first implementation is Windows-only. The field remains optional so macOS and Linux can add their native mappings after platform-specific behavior and stability are tested.

### Implementation pull request

#3005

### RFC document pull request

None.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs immediately before filing.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required.

title: [RFC]: Add an authenticated adapter for cooperating embedded webviews
body:
### Primary area

Security, privacy, or permissions

### Summary

Define an opt-in local protocol through which a native host can expose bounded metadata and navigation for the exact embedded webview owned by one accessible host control. CUA verifies the native owner, transport peer, process-start identity, pane identity, and generations before using the route.

### Motivation and current state

Native accessibility identifies a host control. Browser debugging protocols identify a renderer target. In a process containing several embedded webviews, URL, title, geometry, creation order, process order, and target order do not prove which control owns which renderer.

The host owns the direct join because it holds both the native control and the engine-specific webview object. CUA needs an explicit cooperating-host route or it must refuse exact embedded-webview actions. Existing top-level browser binding does not solve same-URL sibling panes.

Closed PR #1993 proposed stable native control IDs and element lookup. RFC #2798 now proposes the smaller structured-ID field this adapter would consume. This RFC uses that stable host-control ID as one input to attestation; it does not add the broader query API.

### Goals

- Address one embedded webview through the stable ID of its native host control.
- Support late attachment, dynamic panes, same-URL siblings, navigation, webview recreation, and host restart.
- Authenticate the local peer and reject PID reuse or stale process identity.
- Start with bounded metadata reads and navigation, with explicit version and capability checks.
- Reject stale reads and mutations through pane and document generations.
- Leave room for a platform-neutral contract without claiming unimplemented engines.

### Non-goals

- Infer ownership from URL, title, geometry, enumeration order, or process ancestry.
- Accept caller-provided JavaScript.
- Expose cookies, storage, network interception, arbitrary targets, or profile-wide debugger access.
- Put a filesystem path, socket path, browser target ID, or secret in accessibility metadata.
- Claim that CUA can independently prove how an authenticated host routes inside its own process.
- Add semantic-tree, click, type, or scroll operations in the first slice.

### Proposed first slice

A pane is one embedded webview together with the native control that hosts it. The host opts into a versioned local adapter. Its accessibility node publishes a stable pane identity and an opaque adapter identity. It does not publish a path, endpoint, renderer target, or bearer secret.

The initial protocol contains four methods:

- `hello`: protocol version, adapter identity, host PID, and process-start identity;
- `list_panes`: bounded metadata for live panes, supporting late attachment and restart recovery;
- `snapshot`: committed metadata for one pane—pane instance, pane generation, document generation, URL, and optional title;
- `navigate`: a bounded URL plus the expected pane and document generations.

The first slice does not return a semantic tree. Unsupported operations fail explicitly. Each navigation runs through the exact webview object held by the host. A successful request means the host accepted it; callers observe the later committed document generation before treating navigation as complete.

On Windows, the prototype uses an owner-local named pipe. CUA resolves exactly one native accessibility node outside web content, proves its owning PID/window, proves that the pipe server PID is the same process, then checks protocol, opaque adapter identity, PID, and process start time in `hello`. Requests and responses are newline-framed JSON capped below 64 KiB with five-second I/O timeouts. The host caps pane inventory at 256 and URLs at 4096 bytes.

A later cross-platform design could use XPC or a user-only Unix-domain socket on macOS and a user-only runtime-directory socket on Linux. Those transports need equivalent peer and process-start checks before CUA should claim support.

### Trust boundary

CUA can prove that it is speaking to the live process that owns the selected native control. It cannot independently prove that an authenticated host routed an operation to the correct internal webview. That trust is equivalent to trusting the host's accessibility provider. Pane and document generations detect stale routing but do not remove this boundary.

### Alternatives considered

- Host-written JSON manifests: weak lifecycle, late-attach, stale-file, and path-disclosure behavior.
- Raw CDP endpoints: broad authority, Chromium-only behavior, and the same unresolved native-control join.
- WebView2 debugger discovery: useful for target discovery, but it does not provide the host control's stable accessibility identity.
- URL, title, geometry, or enumeration matching: mutable and ambiguous, especially for same-URL siblings.
- Caller script injection: broader authority than the first slice requires and engine-specific.

### Compatibility and migration

The adapter is optional and disabled by default. Existing native and browser automation paths remain unchanged. Hosts that do not opt in retain the current exact-ownership refusal. Capabilities are negotiated; unsupported methods fail without approximation.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

The transport is local and owner-scoped. The route binds the native accessibility node, window owner, pipe server PID, process start time, opaque adapter identity, pane identity, and generations. Wrong peers, PID reuse, duplicate native IDs, stale generations, invalid schemes, malformed frames, and oversized frames fail closed. No adapter traffic or page metadata is added to telemetry.

### Prototype evidence

A local Windows prototype proves the first slice without CDP, a JSON manifest, or path-bearing accessibility IDs:

- late driver attachment and dynamic pane discovery;
- distinct binding for same-URL sibling panes;
- exact-pane navigation and sibling isolation;
- pane/document generation refusal after close, replacement, and navigation;
- wrong peer identity, malformed input, oversized input, unsupported method, invalid scheme, and deleted-pane refusal;
- broker survival after refused requests and exact owned-process cleanup.

Exact local tests:

- Windows adapter suite: 145 passed, 2 ignored;
- core cooperative-route additions: 10 passed; full core: 486 passed with the same two Windows fixture failures as current main;
- contract: 29 passed, 1 ignored;
- schema: 4 passed;
- tool routing: 12 passed;
- protocol schema: 2 passed;
- handshake: 4 passed;
- retained application UAT: 8/8, including the browser-correlation scenario.

The prototype's session and compatibility-fixture failures reproduce on current main or are absent from both trees. The warnings-denied Clippy comparison has the same 36 baseline errors on candidate and base and no candidate-only finding.

### Unresolved questions

- Should CUA own this cooperating-host contract, or consume a small protocol crate maintained with host adapters?
- Is metadata plus navigation the right first slice?
- Should the first implementation remain Windows-only until equivalent macOS and Linux peer attestation exists?
- Does the opaque adapter identity belong in accessibility metadata, or should CUA derive the local route from an independently registered host capability?

### RFC document pull request

None.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs immediately before filing.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the trust boundary, alternatives, compatibility, and acceptance evidence.

title: cua-driver-rs (Windows): update --apply always aborts — the current version's own ~/.cua-driver-rs cache is misdetected as a v0.2.13 legacy layout, and the migration taskkills the updater itself
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver update --apply` never completes on Windows. It stops at the legacy-migration step and exits
with code 1; the installed version is unchanged. Two independent defects combine:

1. `install.ps1` treats the existence of `~/.cua-driver-rs` as "legacy layout v0.2.13 or earlier" —
   but **the current version creates that directory itself** (update-check cache + telemetry).
2. The migration branch runs `taskkill /F /IM "cua-driver.exe" /T`, which kills the very
   `cua-driver update --apply` process that launched the installer.

So every `update --apply` walks into the migration path and then terminates itself.

## Environment

- `cua-driver-rs` 0.14.1 → attempted upgrade to 0.16.0, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
- Windows 11 26100, non-elevated user shell, per-user install (no admin)

## Clean-room reproduction (host that never had cua-driver installed)

```
STATE BEFORE: modern=False legacy=False bin=False
install.ps1 -Release 0.16.0 -NoAutoStart        → cua-driver 0.16.0, ~/.cua-driver-rs absent
cua-driver check-update                          → ~/.cua-driver-rs created (version_check.json)
cua-driver update --apply                        → exit 1, version still 0.16.0
```

So a brand-new install is one ordinary command away from a permanently broken `update --apply`.

Confirming the causal chain: setting `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME` / `CUA_DRIVER_RS_INSTALL_DIR` to the paths
already in use makes the migration branch return early (see the guard below) and `update --apply`
then succeeds — 0.16.0 → 0.17.0 in one run.

## Reproduction (existing install)

```
> cua-driver update --apply
Current version: 0.14.1
Checking for updates…
New version available: 0.16.0
Downloading and installing cua-driver 0.16.0…
==> cua-driver-rs installer (Windows)
==>   install dir : C:\Users\<u>\AppData\Local\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin
==>   package home: C:\Users\<u>\.cua-driver
==> detected legacy install layout (v0.2.13 or earlier); migrating to Cua\cua-driver
   ← output ends here, exit code 1

> cua-driver --version
cua-driver 0.14.1        # unchanged
```

Repeats identically every time.

## Root cause 1 — the "legacy" marker is written by the current version

`install.ps1`:

```powershell
$LegacyHomeDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".cua-driver-rs"
...
$hasLegacy = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $LegacyVisibleBinDir) -or (Test-Path -LiteralPath $LegacyHomeDir)
if (-not $hasLegacy) { return }
Write-Step "detected legacy install layout (v0.2.13 or earlier); migrating to Cua\cua-driver"
```

`crates/cua-driver/src/version_check.rs`:

```rust
/// `~/.cua-driver-rs/` — same subdirectory the telemetry client uses,
/// kept separate from the `~/.cua-driver/` config tree that the Swift
/// reference owns.
const HOME_SUBDIRECTORY: &str = ".cua-driver-rs";
```

On this machine `~/.cua-driver-rs` contains exactly one file — `version_check.json`, timestamped
minutes ago by `cua-driver check-update`. There is no legacy install: the modern layout
(`~/.cua-driver/packages/...` + `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin`) is the only one present,
and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\...` does not exist.

Because `update --apply` runs a version check first, the directory is guaranteed to exist by the time
the installer inspects it — the false positive is self-inflicted and permanent.

## Root cause 2 — the migration kills the updater

Inside the same branch:

```powershell
& schtasks.exe /End /TN "cua-driver-serve" 2>$null | Out-Null
& taskkill.exe /F /IM "cua-driver.exe" /T 2>$null | Out-Null
```

`cua-driver update --apply` is itself `cua-driver.exe`, so `/IM cua-driver.exe /T` terminates the
parent of the running installer. That explains the truncated output and exit 1 immediately after the
`Write-Step` line.

## Suggested fix

1. Detect legacy by an actual legacy artifact rather than the directory alone — e.g. require
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\trycua\cua-driver-rs\bin\cua-driver.exe` or a `packages/` tree inside
   `~/.cua-driver-rs`; a lone `version_check.json` must not trigger migration. Alternatively move the
   update-check/telemetry cache into `~/.cua-driver/` so the two namespaces stop overlapping.
2. Exclude the current process from the kill in the migration path (e.g. `taskkill /FI "PID ne <self>"`,
   or enumerate and skip `$PID`), so a self-invoked `update --apply` can survive it.

## Why this may have gone unnoticed

The documented upgrade path (`irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex`) is unaffected: there the
installer runs inside `powershell.exe`, so `taskkill /IM cua-driver.exe` does not kill it. The failure
is specific to the installer being a child of `cua-driver.exe`, i.e. exactly `update --apply`.

## Workaround

Set both env vars to the paths already in use before updating — the migration branch returns early:

```powershell
$env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME = "$env:USERPROFILE\.cua-driver"
$env:CUA_DRIVER_RS_INSTALL_DIR = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin"
cua-driver update --apply     # 0.16.0 → 0.17.0, no migration attempted
```

## Alternative workaround

Manual layout swap: download the release zip, unpack into
`~/.cua-driver/packages/releases/<ver>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, repoint the `current` and `bin`
junctions, restart the daemon. Works reliably.

title: cua-overlay-wl burns ~17-28% of one core indefinitely on KDE Wayland; --no-overlay doesn't gate it
body:
### Summary
On KDE Plasma (KWin) under Wayland, the `cua-overlay-wl` thread — the Wayland agent-cursor overlay — enters an **unbounded redraw loop** after certain capture/cursor activity, burning ~17-28% of one core forever, even with zero calls in flight. `--no-overlay` suppresses only the X11 overlay variant; the wl thread is unaffected. Reproduced on **cua-driver 0.17.0** (latest release as of 2026-08-03).

### Environment
- cua-driver 0.17.0 (`check-update` confirms latest)
- KDE Plasma 6.7.3 / KWin 6.7.3, Wayland session
- CachyOS (Arch-based), NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti (proprietary), fractional scale 1.6
- Daemon spawned as stdio child of an MCP host (`cua-driver mcp --no-overlay` / embedded `serve`)

### Evidence
- **Thread census** after ~23 min of burn: `cua-overlay-wl` at **14,917 CPU ticks**; every other thread ≤26 ticks → the overlay thread is 100% of the burn.
- **Sustained burn measured at reap:** daemon spawned 02:10:40, last tool call 02:11:46, still burning at 02:30:57 → `age=1217s, cpu=33,433 ticks` ≈ **27.5% of one core for 20+ minutes with zero activity**.
- `set_agent_cursor_enabled(False)` does **not** stop it.
- **NOT version-deterministic:** same 0.17.0 binary, same host, same day — a second daemon sat at **0 ticks** the entire time. The trigger is situational (some capture/cursor patterns kick the loop; most don't).
- Note: KWin 6.7.3 **does** expose `zwlr_layer_shell_v1` (v5) — the overlay can attach; this is a pacing/redraw defect, not a display failure.

### Relationship to PR #2331
PR #2331 ("bound X11 overlay render work", merged Jul 18) fixed this bug class for `cua-overlay-x11` (idle 99.5% → 0%). The Wayland overlay is a **separate code path** and still reproduces on 0.17.0.

### Suggested fixes (any would help)
1. **Idle-bounding** for the wl render loop — mirror #2331: skip redraws when the cursor hasn't moved; pace on `wl_surface.frame` callbacks instead of busy redraw.
2. Make `--no-overlay` **authoritative for both variants** (it currently only kills the x11 thread).
3. Don't start the overlay thread when agent-cursor visuals are disabled.

### Repro
1. KDE Plasma 6.7 Wayland.
2. `cua-driver serve` (0.17.0).
3. Start a session; run a few captures/cursor moves with the agent cursor enabled.
4. Stop all calls → within minutes `cua-overlay-wl` burns a core indefinitely.
5. Confirm: `for t in /proc/<pid>/task/*; do cat "$t/comm"; done` → `cua-overlay-wl` present; `/proc/<pid>/stat` fields 14+15 delta ≈ 17 ticks/s.

### Mitigation (until fixed)
Daemon lifecycle management is required on KDE Wayland — kill the daemon when idle (a watchdog that kills daemons aged >5 min with >120s CPU works; it respawns on next use). Happy to test a patch.

title: cua-driver: press_key can report delivery_failed after the key is delivered
body:
## Summary

On macOS, a background pixel-addressed `press_key` can deliver Return successfully while returning `effect: "unverifiable"` with `escalation.reason: "delivery_failed"` and recommending foreground delivery.

## Environment

- Cua Driver 0.17.0 (signed release artifact)
- macOS 26.5.2, arm64
- Declared window-scoped session
- Terminal.app target

## Reproduction

1. Start a window-scoped session.
2. Launch or select a Terminal window and take a fresh `get_window_state` snapshot.
3. Use pixel-addressed `type_text` to enter a harmless long-running shell command; verify the text delivery.
4. Take another fresh window snapshot.
5. Call pixel-addressed `press_key` with `key: "return"` and background delivery.
6. Verify execution through an external oracle such as the Terminal title and the spawned child process.

## Actual result

The key was delivered and the command executed, but `press_key` returned:

```json
{
  "delivery": {"mode": "background"},
  "effect": "unverifiable",
  "escalation": {
    "reason": "delivery_failed",
    "target": "foreground"
  },
  "route": "synthetic_events"
}
```

## Expected result

When delivery cannot be positively confirmed, the result should remain explicitly unverifiable without asserting `delivery_failed`. If a delivery oracle exists, the action should report the confirmed outcome. A successful background key should not trigger unnecessary foreground escalation.

title: bug(cua-driver): macOS bring_to_front reports exact-window success without raising it
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `bring_to_front` can return `activated: true` with `path: "skylight"` even though the requested window remains behind other ordinary layer-0 windows.

The target process becomes the frontmost application, but the exact requested window is not raised. This contradicts the tool contract, which says the app genuinely holds foreground and that `window_id` fronts the exact macOS window.

## Reproduction

Reproduced with `cua-driver 0.12.3` using two ordinary applications, where application B had two visible windows:

1. Put application A in the foreground.
2. Record the WindowServer order with `list_windows`.
3. Call `bring_to_front` for application B's lower window, passing both `pid` and `window_id`.
4. Read the frontmost process and call `list_windows` again.

The tool returned:

```json
{
  "activated": true,
  "path": "skylight",
  "window_id": "B2"
}
```

macOS reported application B as the frontmost process, but the relevant WindowServer order was unchanged:

```text
B1  z_index 31
A   z_index 30
B2  z_index 26  <- requested exact window
```

The requested B2 window remained behind both B1 and application A.

## Current source behavior

The same result contract remains on current `main` at `e7b42ca04f306084b8bd5dc60c47b18bbdf9aed1`:

- `platform-macos/src/tools/bring_to_front.rs` maps `set_front_process_persistently(...) == true` directly to `activated: true`.
- `platform-macos/src/input/skylight.rs` returns `true` when `SLPSSetFrontProcessWithOptions` returns zero.
- There is no bounded post-action check that the requested window became key/frontmost or moved to the expected z-order.

In other words, `activated` currently proves that WindowServer accepted the request, not that the documented exact-window postcondition occurred.

## Expected behavior

When `window_id` is supplied, `activated: true` should mean that the requested window was verified as the frontmost window for the target application and is no longer behind another ordinary layer-0 application window.

If macOS activates the process but does not raise the exact window, the tool should either complete a bounded exact-window activation sequence or return an honest partial/failure result rather than `activated: true`.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verify both target-process activation and exact requested-window identity after a bounded settle.
- [ ] Distinguish request acceptance from verified effect in the structured result.
- [ ] Return a structured partial/failure result when the process activates but the exact window remains behind another layer-0 application window.
- [ ] Add a macOS E2E test with two applications and two target-process windows, using the frontmost process and WindowServer z-order as independent oracles.
- [ ] Cover a modal sheet or floating-window case in addition to ordinary windows.

## Related

- #2206 covers action-scoped foreground delivery and restoration. This issue covers the separate persistent `bring_to_front` exact-window contract.

title: docs(cua-driver): document elements[].frame coordinate space
body:
## Problem

`get_window_state` returns per-element geometry in `structuredContent.elements[].frame`, but the reference docs did not state which coordinate space it uses.

The frames are screen-absolute. Pixel actions addressed with `pid` and `window_id` instead take window-local screenshot pixels. Passing a frame center directly into `click({pid, window_id, x, y})` can therefore land off-target by the window origin and capture scale without producing a structural error.

This is the remaining documentation gap related to #1564: the geometry shipped, but its coordinate space was not written down.

## What this changes

Documentation only — one new section in `docs/content/docs/reference/cua-driver/limits.mdx`:

- a table of coordinate spaces and units for `elements[].frame`, window-scoped pixel arguments, and desktop-scoped pixel arguments
- `element_token` as the preferred route, or `element_index` with its matching `snapshot_id`
- the correct window-scoped conversion: rebase against `list_windows` bounds, then rescale to the `get_window_state` PNG
- the correct desktop-scoped conversion: rescale the frame center into the `get_desktop_state` PNG; this matters on macOS Retina displays because frames are logical points while the desktop capture is native pixels
- clarification that `double_click` uses the same window-local pixel conversion even though its generated argument description currently says “Screen”
- a note that `window_bounds` is emitted by `get_window_state` on macOS only

No production files are touched.

## Validation

The coordinate-space claims were checked against the current implementations and canonical harnesses on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Local checks:

- `git diff --check`
- Cua Driver generated-reference drift check
- docs internal-link check
- public docs hygiene check
- production docs build compiled and type-checked successfully; static generation then encountered the pre-existing unrelated `/reference/lume/cli-reference` error, `ReferenceError: vm is not defined`

Refs #1564
