title: cua-driver 0.17.0 Linux/X11: serve hangs forever in AT-SPI listener activation (works when AT-SPI connect fails)
body:
# cua-driver 0.17.0 Linux/X11: `serve` hangs forever in AT-SPI listener activation (works when AT-SPI connect fails)

## Environment
- OS: Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena), kernel 7.0.0-28-generic
- Desktop: XFCE 4 (xfce4-session), X11 (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11`, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=XFCE`)
- cua-driver: 0.17.0 (also reproduced on 0.16.0 and 0.14.1)
- at-spi2-core: 2.52.0-1build1
- D-Bus: 1.14.10
- GTK3: 3.24.41-4ubuntu1.3
- Access path: SSH session with `DISPLAY=:0`, `XAUTHORITY` set, session bus reachable (`unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus`)

## Symptom
`cua-driver serve` never reaches "listening". Process stays alive, zero stdout/stderr, socket file never appears. `health_report` reports daemon not running. `hermes computer-use doctor` also times out. Same result for `cua-driver mcp` (MCP stdio mode).

## Root cause isolation
`cua-driver doctor` passes everything: X11 connected (3 visible top-level windows), `org.a11y.Bus` reachable via session bus. `pyatspi` works fine (26 desktop children).

The hang is in cua-driver's own AT-SPI listener activation. Evidence:

**Experiment 1 — normal session bus (hangs):**
```bash
DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus" timeout 8 cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/repro-ok.sock --permission-mode standard --no-overlay
# → no output, killed by timeout (hang)
```

**Experiment 2 — broken session bus (works):**
```bash
DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=/run/user/1000/nonexistent-bus" timeout 8 cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/repro-bad.sock --permission-mode standard --no-overlay
# → WARN: could not activate the persistent AT-SPI listener: AT-SPI connect failed
# → Cua Driver daemon listening on /tmp/repro-bad.sock
```

**Experiment 3 — pyatspi control (works):**
```bash
DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus" python3 -c "import pyatspi; print(pyatspi.Registry.getDesktop(0).childCount)"
# → 26
```

So: when AT-SPI connect *fails*, serve starts fine (listener activation is best-effort and skipped). When AT-SPI *succeeds*, serve hangs forever waiting on something in the AT-SPI interaction.

## strace evidence (normal session bus)
strace shows: connects to session bus → `GetAddress` on `org.a11y.Bus` returns `unix:path=/run/user/1000/at-spi/bus_0` → connects to the AT-SPI bus → AUTH EXTERNAL / NEGOTIATE_UNIX_FD handshake succeeds → sends a D-Bus method call targeting an `/org/a11y/...` object → then blocks in `recvmsg` + `futex`/`epoll_wait` forever. No reply ever arrives from the AT-SPI side. The session's AT-SPI bus (`org.a11y.atspi.Registry` on bus_0) is up and responds to other clients.

## Version testing
Reproduced identically on 0.17.0, 0.16.0, and 0.14.1 — not a recent regression.

## Workarounds tried
- `CUA_DRIVER_RS_DISABLE_A11Y_ADVERTISE=1` → no effect (the hang is not the advertise step; advertise runs on a separate thread and the binary logs `unknown CUA_DRIVER_RS_A11Y_ADVERTISE_MODE; using desktop default` for other values)
- `--no-overlay` → no effect
- Broken `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` → works, but loses the AT-SPI element tree entirely (ax_capability fails; screenshot still works, element-index/SOM interaction does not)

## Request
Please investigate the AT-SPI listener activation path on Linux/X11 — it appears to block forever when the AT-SPI bus is reachable but something in the initial interaction (register listener / enumerate registry?) never completes. Happy to provide full strace logs or run any diagnostic you suggest.

title: chore(deps): bump undici from 7.28.0 to 7.29.0 in /libs/cua-driver/typescript
body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) from 7.28.0 to 7.29.0.
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.29.0

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272: malformed qualified private Cache-Control directives could cause cross-user information disclosure in shared caches or a parse-time crash. The cache parser now treats empty qualified directives conservatively and safely handles mixed qualified and unqualified directives. Fixed by 9f10f1e9, with regression coverage in 466e99d1.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5: a malicious type property on a duck-typed blob-like HTTP/1.1 request body could inject CRLF sequences into the generated content-type header. Undici now coerces and validates the value before adding it to the request. Fixed by 33928bc2.
  • GHSA-jr45-8vmc-qm54: optional whitespace around = in qualified no-cache and private directives could bypass shared-cache restrictions and disclose authenticated data across users. Cache-Control parsing now normalizes these forms and applies conservative cache decisions. Fixed by 98011a86.
  • GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524: the retry interceptor could expose a stale Content-Length after resuming a partial response, potentially causing downstream response desynchronization, hangs, or corruption. Undici now rejects partial responses whose Content-Length is inconsistent with Content-Range. Fixed by 1b5a5312, with corrected fixtures in 4a9dafb1.
  • GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm: unsanitized domain and unparsed values passed to setCookie() could inject cookie attributes. Undici now validates cookie domains, paths, and unparsed attributes more strictly. Fixed by 3bf91ddb.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.28.0...v7.29.0

title: Add a reusable Cua Driver release-certification skill for Lume macOS Tahoe
body:
## Problem

Cua Driver has strong low-level guidance for macOS, recording, browser mode, and the repository-owned Lume runner, plus a public how-to guide. The internal `trycua/skills` catalog currently has no reusable scenario skill for certifying Cua Driver from source in a clean Lume macOS Tahoe Cua VM.

As a result, agents must reconstruct the release-certification workflow each time and commonly lose time on VM selection, host capacity, signing/TCC setup, provenance checks, recording finalization, and evidence packaging.

## Proposed skill

Add a focused skill such as `cua-driver-lume-release-qa` to `trycua/skills`. Keep it above the core Cua Driver contract and reference the canonical repository docs rather than duplicating them.

The workflow should:

1. Resolve and freeze the requested Cua source SHA/version, with a clean named worktree and an exact source marker.
2. Preflight host disk headroom and the Apple two-active-VM limit before starting or pulling a VM.
3. Pull a pinned `macos-tahoe-cua` image tag, verify its OCI manifest/config, and use a task-specific VM name.
4. Sync the exact source and run `install-local.sh --release --autostart --require-stable-signing`.
5. Establish a certificate-backed stable local identity and verify installed binary/app provenance.
6. Grant Accessibility and Screen Recording through VNC in the disposable guest, then verify both grants.
7. Restart the installed daemon in unrestricted mode with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals` for QA.
8. Run representative Calculator and typed-browser Chrome workflows using snapshot/action/snapshot, independent postcondition oracles, and explicit sessions.
9. Start recording before the first action, stop/finalize it, validate `recording.mp4` with ffprobe, and retain trajectory/screenshot evidence.
10. Produce a sanitized evidence bundle containing source SHA, installed version/provenance, signing/TCC state, action/oracle summaries, and playable videos.
11. Define safe cleanup behavior without deleting VM disks or unrelated evidence by default.

## Guardrails

- Never infer installation success from an installer exit code alone.
- Never accept a result from a VM whose guest filesystem reported write/I/O corruption.
- Never overlap another task's active VM or stop its process without authorization.
- Never include credentials, IPs, VM names from private environments, raw session traces, or machine-specific paths in reusable artifacts.
- Use VNC only for disposable guest setup and observation. Cua Driver actions plus independent oracles remain the certification proof.
- Keep browser QA on a disposable driver-owned profile unless an authenticated-profile test is explicitly required.

## Acceptance criteria

- New skill lands in `trycua/skills` with `agents/openai.yaml`.
- It references the canonical Cua Driver skill, Lume runner, and public Tahoe QA guide.
- Repository and skill-creator validators pass.
- The skill is dogfooded from a clean pulled Tahoe Cua image against an exact source SHA.
- One successful run produces independently validated Calculator and Chrome MP4s plus a sanitized provenance/evidence summary.

title: Windows 10: list_apps UWP scan logs 0x80070005 and blocks for ~30 seconds
body:
### Environment

- OS: Windows 10 Pro, 22H2, build 19045
- cua-driver: 0.14.2 (reproduced) and 0.17.0 (reproduced; latest release at time of testing)
- Install form: per-user installation at `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin\cua-driver.exe`
- Daemon: started natively on Windows via the logon scheduled task, standard permission mode. The same delay was also observed from a daemon launched through a WSL-initiated process path.
- Client: `cua-driver call` CLI, and an MCP client whose tool-call deadline is 30 seconds.

### Summary

- `--version`, `list-tools`, and `status` complete quickly (0.04 s to ~1.3 s).
- `call list_apps` consistently takes about 30 seconds and logs the WinRT access-denied warning. `call list_windows` independently shows similar 31–32 second latency, but current source does not route it through the installed-app scan, so it may be a separate symptom.
- During `list_apps`, the daemon logs `WARN installed_apps: scan_uwp_packages: WinRT error: Access is denied. (0x80070005)`.
- A client with a 30-second tool-call deadline times out on these calls.

### Minimal reproduction

Terminal A — daemon (if not already running):

```
cua-driver serve
```

Terminal B — client:

```
cua-driver call list_apps
cua-driver call list_windows
cua-driver status
```

All commands above were executed against both 0.14.2 and 0.17.0 during testing. Both `call list_apps` and `call list_windows` exhibited the delay in this minimal reproduction. The UWP scan warning was observed for `list_apps`; the similar `list_windows` latency is reported as a separate observation.

### Expected behavior

`list_apps` should return promptly, or fail promptly with an actionable error when the optional UWP enumeration is unavailable. `list_windows` should also return promptly; its similar latency is not attributed here to the UWP scan.

### Actual behavior

| Command | Observed duration |
|---|---|
| `cua-driver --version` | 0.036 s |
| `cua-driver list-tools` | 0.043 s |
| `cua-driver status` | 1.3 s |
| `cua-driver call list_apps` (0.14.2) | 30.5 s (two runs: 30.46, 30.62) |
| `cua-driver call list_windows` (0.14.2) | 31.8 s |
| `cua-driver call list_apps` (0.17.0) | 30.3 s (two runs: 30.30, 30.28) |
| `cua-driver call list_windows` (0.17.0) | 31.7 s |
| PowerShell `Get-AppxPackage` (same user session, comparison) | 0.37 s |

### Relevant daemon log

```
WARN installed_apps: scan_uwp_packages: WinRT error: Access is denied. (0x80070005)
```

### Additional configurations tested

- Unrestricted permission mode (daemon started with `--permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals`): same ~30 s delay.
- cua-driver 0.14.2 vs 0.17.0: identical behavior.
- Native Windows daemon startup (logon scheduled task) vs WSL-initiated process path: identical behavior.
- AppX-related services (AppXSvc, StateRepository) were running at test time; `Get-AppxPackage` from PowerShell in the same user session enumerated 202 packages in ~0.37 s, indicating general AppX package enumeration is available.
- Note: these observations do not fully exclude permission/token-level causes; an elevated-process comparison has not been performed.

### Suspected source area

Verified against current `main` (commit `53e6736f0bc549d5be01fcc550a180b7cac4f10f`):

- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/win32/installed_apps.rs`: `list_installed_apps()` unconditionally calls `scan_start_menu()` then `scan_uwp_packages()`; `scan_uwp_packages()` calls WinRT `PackageManager::FindPackagesWithPackageTypes(PackageTypes::Main)` and swallows errors (best-effort enumeration). No option to skip or disable the UWP scan was found in the current source or driver config schema.
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`: `ListAppsTool::invoke` calls `crate::win32::list_installed_apps()` as part of its merge step.
- The warning line above was introduced by #1643 (observability for #1636), so it is expected to appear whenever the WinRT call fails.

This is localization evidence, not a final root-cause proof. The exact underlying cause remains unresolved and could involve the specific WinRT API path, initialization/threading behavior, or token interaction.

Note: `list_windows` does not call the installed-app enumeration path in current source (`win32/windows.rs` uses EnumWindows + UI Automation; the `ListWindowsTool` implementation uses `list_windows` plus the process table only). Its similar ~31 s delay has not been independently isolated; it may share an underlying environment factor or be a separate issue.

### Workaround

- Using a non-semantic coordinate backend (from the MCP client side) avoids this code path.
- Raising the client timeout beyond 30 s allows the calls to complete, but leaves poor latency; not considered a satisfactory fix.

### Unresolved questions

1. Is Windows 10 22H2 expected to support the WinRT `PackageManager` enumeration path used here?
2. Is there a supported way to disable or skip the UWP package scan?
3. Could the best-effort UWP scan use a shorter timeout, or return immediately after an access-denied error?
4. Could the UWP scan be isolated from `list_apps` (and any callers that do not strictly need it) when its result is optional?
5. Would maintainers prefer: a minimal C#/PowerShell reproduction, additional debug logs (e.g. `RUST_LOG=cua_driver=debug`), an elevated-process comparison, Windows event-log evidence, or a diagnostic build?

### Related

- #1636 (closed): `list_apps` misses UWP apps for non-RID-500 admin users — same enumeration path and the same observability log line, but the symptom differs (empty UWP section vs ~30 s blocking delay). Related, not a duplicate.

title: feat(cua-sandbox): migrate to the native fleet CRDs (fleet_sdk post cloud#6316)
body:
`fleet_sdk` (shipped in the `cua-fleet` wheel) now speaks the `osgym.cua.ai` CRDs directly — see trycua/cloud#6316. `PoolSpec` and `PoolTemplate` no longer exist, so `cua_sandbox` does not import today against the new binding. This migrates the package.

## What changed in the underlying API

A warm pool no longer carries a VM shape. It holds `replicas` plus a `sandboxTemplateRef`, and the VM shape moved into an `OSGymSandboxTemplate` at `spec.vmTemplate` — with the service list now living *inside* the VM template rather than beside it. Pool status reports `replicas`/`readyReplicas` instead of `availableCount`.

## Consumer-facing API change

`PoolSpec` and `PoolTemplate` are removed from `cua_sandbox`. Replace them with a template reconcile followed by a pool reconcile:

```python
# before
await Pool.reconcile(CreatePoolRequest(
    namespace="foo",
    spec=PoolSpec(
        replicas=1,
        services=[SandboxService(name="server", target_port=8000, protocol=ServiceProtocol.TCP)],
        template=PoolTemplate(container_disk_image="registry.example/workspace:latest", ...),
        autoscaling=None,
    ),
))

# after
await Template.reconcile(CreateTemplateRequest(
    namespace="foo",
    name="workspace",
    spec=OsGymSandboxTemplateSpec(
        vm_template=VmTemplate(
            container_disk_image="registry.example/workspace:latest",
            services=[SandboxService(name="server", target_port=8000, protocol=ServiceProtocol.TCP)],
            ...,
        ),
    ),
))

pool = await Pool.reconcile(CreatePoolRequest(
    namespace="foo",
    spec=OsGymSandboxWarmPoolSpec(
        replicas=1,
        sandbox_template_ref=SandboxTemplateRef(name="workspace"),
        autoscaling=None,
    ),
))
```

`pool.claim()` is unchanged. Claiming without an explicit spec still does the right thing: `create_claim` now defaults `sandboxTemplateRef` from the pool's own spec, so the default is correct by construction rather than by convention.

## Per-file

- **`cua_sandbox/__init__.py`** — dropped the `PoolSpec`/`PoolTemplate` re-exports; added `CreateTemplateRequest`, `OsGymSandboxTemplateSpec`, `OsGymSandboxWarmPoolSpec`, `VmTemplate`. `Template` is the new wrapper class; the SDK record is re-exported as `TemplateResource`, mirroring how `Pool` wraps the pool resource.
- **`cua_sandbox/pool.py`** — added a `Template` wrapper mirroring `Pool`, with a type-checked `Template.reconcile(CreateTemplateRequest)`. `Pool` is otherwise unchanged.
- **`cua_sandbox/transport/fleet_cloud.py`** — `_FleetClient` gained `create_template`, `reconcile_template`, `get_template`, and `delete_template` passthroughs. `wait_pool` reads `ready_replicas`. `_pool_request()` now emits only replicas plus the template ref; the VM shape moved to a new `_template_request()`. `connect()` creates the template before the pool, `_cleanup_resources()` deletes it after the pool, and `delete_sandbox` resolves the template through the pool's `sandboxTemplateRef`.
- **`cua_sandbox/sandbox.py`** — the Fleet listing state machine reads `readyReplicas` instead of `availableCount`.
- **`cua_sandbox/sync/__init__.py`** — added a blocking `Template` facade alongside `Pool`.
- **`README.md`** — the pool section now documents the template-then-pool flow with native request objects (it previously showed a dict form that the typed API had already outgrown).
- **tests** — `test_pool.py`, `test_fleet_cloud_transport.py`, and `test_fleet_cloud_client.py` migrated to the new shapes, with coverage added for template reconcile, template-before-pool ordering, cleanup ordering, and `readyReplicas` polling.

## Versions

Bumped to `0.1.25` and pinned `cua-fleet==0.0.9`.

**`uv.lock` is deliberately untouched**: `cua-fleet` 0.0.9 is being released in parallel and is not on PyPI yet, so `uv lock` cannot resolve it (`no version of cua-fleet==0.0.9`). Someone needs to re-run `uv lock` in `libs/python/cua-sandbox` once the wheel publishes, and move the `0.0.8` assertion in `tests/test_fleet_sdk_packaging.py::test_lock_uses_the_published_fleet_bundle` to `0.0.9` at the same time. The lock was already stale relative to `pyproject.toml` before this PR (it pins `cua-sandbox` 0.1.21 against a declared 0.1.24), and it is not consumed by CI.

## Also in this PR

`tests/test_fleet_cloud_client.py::test_pool_lookup_matches_sdk_resources` was deleted. It asserted that `get_pool` falls back to listing pools, which stopped being true when the SDK gained named-pool lookup; it has been failing with `AttributeError: no attribute '_client'` independently of this migration, and `test_pool.py::test_fleet_client_get_pool_uses_name_lookup_without_listing` asserts the current behaviour.

## Validation

Run against a local build of the post-#6316 `fleet_sdk` binding (`libcyclops_sdk.dylib` built from `cyclops-cs` at the migration commit), since the `cua-fleet` 0.0.9 wheel is not published yet:

- `python3 -m py_compile` over all changed Python files — clean.
- `pytest tests/test_pool.py tests/test_fleet_cloud_client.py tests/test_fleet_cloud_transport.py tests/test_fleet_sdk_packaging.py` — **45 passed**.
- Wider unit run (excluding integration/runtime suites needing Docker, QEMU, adb, or cloud credentials) — **125 passed, 12 skipped**. The one failure, `test_fleet_sdk_distribution`, is an artifact of the harness: it asserts `fleet_sdk` is provided by an installed `cua-fleet` distribution, and the binding was injected on `PYTHONPATH` rather than pip-installed.
- Not run: `test_vm_cleanup` (8 pre-existing failures in the legacy API-key `CloudTransport` path, unrelated to Fleet), `test_runtime`, `test_android_multitouch`, and the integration suites — all need local hypervisors, devices, or credentials.
- `grep -rE "\bPoolSpec\b|\bPoolTemplate\b" libs/python/cua-sandbox/` — 0 matches. Same for `availableCount`/`spec.template`.
- `ruff`, `black`, and `isort --check-only` clean on every changed file.

title: feat(cua-driver): drop the session orb from the cursor badge
body:
## What

Removes the session orb — the 10pt session-colored dot at the leading edge of the cursor badge — on every platform, and moves the identity signal it carried into the pill itself.

## Why

The orb duplicated a signal the badge already carried:

- Any state with an active **delivery chip** already renders the pure session color, since that chip is filled with it at 220 alpha (`badge_glyphs.rs`).
- `session_badge_layout` returns `None` when there is no label *and* no chips, so the contracted state documented in the badge restructuring plan always contains that filled chip. The orb contributed nothing there.

That left exactly one state where the orb was load-bearing: **label-only display** (session reveal, hover restore). Rather than keep 17pt of permanent width for one state, that state's identity moves into the pill:

- Gradient accent weights raised `0.52/0.40/0.18` → `0.66/0.52/0.26`.
- The 1px rim is now tinted 55% toward the session color instead of plain white. The rim costs no width and does not sit under the label, so text contrast is unaffected regardless of how bright a session color hashes to.

Net effect: identity is present in *every* state the badge renders, and the label gets back 17pt of a 188pt budget (~9%) before it ellipsizes.

## Before / after

Same state — `background` delivery, `ax` target, label `Research`:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Orb + white rim, label pushed right | No orb, label at the leading padding, session-tinted rim |

Rendered from `cargo run -p cursor-overlay --example export_gallery_frames --features theme-authoring`.

## Every OS

The orb existed in two places, both updated:

- `rust/crates/cursor-overlay/src/session_badge.rs` — the shared renderer consumed by **macOS**, **Windows**, **Linux X11**, and **Linux Wayland** overlays. Verified: no platform crate duplicates the badge geometry; they all call `session_badge_layout` / `paint_session_badge`.
- `wayland-helper/winrects@cua/extension.js` — the GNOME Shell actor that hand-mirrors the Rust design (`_badgeDot` removed, `badgeStyle` gradient + rim brought in line).

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cursor-overlay` — 42 passed, 0 failed.
- New guard `label_starts_at_the_leading_padding_with_no_reserved_marker` pins the invariant that nothing reserves space ahead of the label.
- The existing `badge_gradient_tracks_session_color_and_zero_alpha_paints_nothing` covers the label-only state and still distinguishes two session colors — now via gradient + rim rather than the orb.
- Installed locally via `scripts/install-local.sh` (exit 0).

Two `cua-driver` integration tests (`set_value_via_element_index`, `type_text_chars_tool`) fail in this environment, and `platform-linux` examples don't compile on macOS (`x11rb`). Both confirmed pre-existing on a stashed clean baseline — unrelated to this change.

## Follow-up not in this PR

The two badge screenshots in `docs/content/docs/how-to-guides/driver/personalize-cursor.mdx` are externally hosted GitHub assets that still show the orb. The prose needs no change (it never described the orb), but those images want regenerating. Flagging rather than silently leaving them stale.

title: docs(cua-driver): fix bounded manifest examples that cannot load
body:
## Problem

Three published bounded-manifest examples are refused by the runtime at startup, so anyone following them gets a daemon that will not start.

| Page | Failure |
| --- | --- |
| `how-to-guides/driver/write-a-bounded-manifest.mdx` | `origin-scoped bounded manifests cannot allow 'click' because it bypasses the typed browser origin adapter` |
| `reference/cua-driver/permission-modes.mdx` | same refusal |
| `how-to-guides/driver/drive-a-web-page.mdx` | `unsupported application terminate scope 'never'; expected deny, driver_launched, or any` |

The first two paired `resources.browser.origins` with `click`, `type_text`, `press_key`, and `get_window_state`. `session_manifest.rs:813-841` rejects that combination at load time.

## Why the examples had to be restructured rather than trimmed

Every navigation is checked against the origin set (`session_manifest.rs:141`), so a manifest allowing `browser_navigate` with no origins refuses every navigation — verified live:

```
call browser_navigate {url: https://example.com}  # manifest declares no origins
→ Permission denied: the live browser origin is outside the bounded session policy
```

A browser manifest therefore always needs origins, and declaring origins always excludes generic input. Browser work and desktop work cannot share one manifest. The how-to now presents an application manifest in step 1 and a complete typed-browser-only manifest in step 2.

## Also documented

- The full excluded tool set.
- Why observation (`get_window_state`, `verify_state`, `get_desktop_state`) is excluded alongside input: a browser-window screenshot or AX tree exposes whichever tab is open, regardless of the allow-list.
- That the check reads `allow.tools` alone and does not analyze whether a browser is reachable, so a manifest naming only a non-browser application is refused on the same terms. Verified: a TextEdit-only manifest with `desktop.display: false` still cannot list `click` beside origins, even though `click` against an out-of-scope pid is independently refused with `bounded_resource_outside_manifest`. Noted as deliberate fail-closed behavior rather than presented as a tight invariant.
- `list_windows` as the substitute for `get_window_state` when a browser call needs a `window_id`.

## Verification

Every complete manifest example on all three pages was extracted from the MDX and loaded against cua-driver 0.17.0 in bounded mode. All four now start; before this change, three of four failed.

```
howto-0.yaml Cua Driver daemon listening on ...
howto-1.yaml Cua Driver daemon listening on ...
ref-0.yaml   Cua Driver daemon listening on ...
web-0.yaml   Cua Driver daemon listening on ...
```

Docs-only; no runtime behavior changes.

title: computer_server --backend vnc silently falls back to native handler (wrong/blank screenshots); twisted/vncdotool undeclared deps
body:
## Summary

`python -m computer_server --backend vnc ...` silently falls back to the **native** (local-OS) automation handler instead of the VNC handler, with no error. Every `screenshot` (and therefore every action the Agent SDK takes based on a screenshot) then operates on whatever local `DISPLAY` the process happens to have — not the remote VNC target — and returns `"success": true` with a plausible-looking but wrong image.

Two separate root causes compound to produce this:

### 1. `--backend vnc` (CLI flag) doesn't actually select the VNC handler

`computer_server/handlers/factory.py`'s `HandlerFactory.create_handlers()` reads the backend from `os.environ.get("CUA_BACKEND", "native")`. `computer_server/cli.py` does set `os.environ["CUA_BACKEND"] = "vnc"` when `--backend vnc` is passed — but `computer_server/__init__.py` unconditionally does `from .server import Server`, and that import chain reaches `main.py`'s module-level `(...) = HandlerFactory.create_handlers()` **before** `cli.py`'s `main()` function body (which sets the env var) ever executes. Import order:

```
python -m computer_server
  → __main__.py: from .cli import main
    → triggers import of the `computer_server` package
      → __init__.py: from .server import Server
        → server.py: from .main import app
          → main.py (module scope): automation_handler = HandlerFactory.create_handlers()[1]
            → reads os.environ.get("CUA_BACKEND", "native")  # not set yet!
  ← only now does cli.py's main() run and set CUA_BACKEND=vnc (too late)
```

The handler is already permanently bound to the native handler by the time the env var is set. No error is raised — `factory.py`'s own `logger.info(f"Using VNC backend → ...")` line never fires (confirmed via `journalctl`), while `cli.py`'s separate "VNC backend enabled → ..." log line *does* fire, which is misleading — it only describes intent, not what actually happened.

**Workaround:** set `CUA_BACKEND`, `CUA_VNC_HOST`, `CUA_VNC_PORT`, `CUA_VNC_PASSWORD` as real process **environment variables** *before* the Python process starts (e.g. in a wrapper shell script or `docker-compose.yml` `environment:`), not just as CLI flags.

### 2. `twisted` / `vncdotool` are required but not declared as dependencies

Once the VNC backend *is* correctly selected (via the workaround above), `computer_server/handlers/vnc.py` does a lazy `from twisted.internet import defer, reactor` and `from vncdotool.client import VNCDoToolFactory` inside the methods that need them. Neither package is listed in `cua-computer-server`'s declared dependencies:

```
$ pip show cua-computer-server
...
Requires: aiohttp, cua-auto, cua-core, fastapi, fastmcp, grpcio, pillow, playwright, protobuf, pydantic, pynput, pyperclip, python-xlib, pywinctl, uvicorn, websockets
```

Without them installed, `screenshot()` returns `{"success": false, "error": "... No module named 'twisted'"}` — but because of bug (1) above, most users never even see this, since they're silently on the native handler already.

### Also worth knowing

`handlers/factory.py` unconditionally imports the native handler at **module import time** regardless of the chosen backend:

```python
elif OS_TYPE == "linux":
    from .linux import LinuxAccessibilityHandler, LinuxAutomationHandler
```

`handlers/linux.py` imports `pynput`, which raises `ImportError: this platform is not supported: ('failed to acquire X connection: Bad display name ""', ...)` at import time if `DISPLAY` is unset. So a pure VNC-backend deployment (e.g. a headless Docker container with no local X server at all) needs a throwaway `Xvfb` running just to satisfy this import, even though it's never actually used for anything.

## Environment

- `cua-computer-server` 0.3.42
- Python 3.12, both a plain venv on Debian/Ubuntu and a `python:3.12-slim` Docker image (reproduces in both)
- Target: `trycua/xfce-cua:latest` container as the VNC server

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1) No env vars pre-set, twisted/vncdotool NOT installed:
python -m computer_server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --backend vnc --vnc-host 127.0.0.1 --vnc-port 5901 --vnc-password secret

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/cmd -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"command":"screenshot","params":{}}'
# → "success": true, but with a small (~2-3 KB), WRONG image (native handler capturing
#    the process's own DISPLAY, not the VNC target)

# 2) Install twisted+vncdotool, retry same command (still no env vars pre-set):
pip install twisted vncdotool
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/cmd ...
# → still "success": true, still wrong — handler was already bound at import time

# 3) Restart the server with CUA_BACKEND/CUA_VNC_HOST/CUA_VNC_PORT/CUA_VNC_PASSWORD
#    exported as real env vars BEFORE launching python, WITHOUT twisted/vncdotool:
export CUA_BACKEND=vnc CUA_VNC_HOST=127.0.0.1 CUA_VNC_PORT=5901 CUA_VNC_PASSWORD=secret
python -m computer_server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --backend vnc --vnc-host 127.0.0.1 --vnc-port 5901 --vnc-password secret
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/cmd ...
# → "success": false, "error": "VNC screenshot error: No module named 'twisted'"
# (backend correctly selected this time — the real underlying bug (2) surfaces)

# 4) With env vars set AND twisted+vncdotool installed:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/cmd ...
# → "success": true, correct full screenshot of the actual VNC target
```

## Expected behavior

- `--backend vnc` on the CLI should reliably select the VNC handler regardless of package import order (e.g. by moving handler creation to first-request time, or having `cli.py` set the env vars via `os.environ` at the very top of `__main__`/before any package-internal import touches `HandlerFactory`).
- If VNC backend selection fails for any reason, it should raise/log loudly rather than silently falling back to a handler that captures the wrong target.
- `twisted` and `vncdotool` should be declared as install dependencies (perhaps under a `[vnc]` extra) so `pip install cua-computer-server` (or `[vnc]`) is sufficient.

## Context

Found while building [deskswarm](https://github.com/ahmedvnabil/deskswarm), a self-hosted fleet-of-desktops dashboard on top of the cua Agent/Computer SDKs. Full writeup with more detail (including confirmation via `docker exec ... ps aux` that the real desktop was fully functional the whole time — only the screenshot capture was wrong) is at [`docs/UPSTREAM_CUA_BUG.md`](https://github.com/ahmedvnabil/deskswarm/blob/main/docs/UPSTREAM_CUA_BUG.md) in that repo. Happy to help test a fix or open a PR if a maintainer can point me at the intended approach.

title: lume: standardize CLI logging and progress rendering (pull output is unreadable)
body:
## Summary `lume`'s terminal output is noisy and visually broken. Log lines and in-place progress bars are written by different code paths that both own the terminal, so they overwrite each other, leave stray padding, and re-print stale frames. On top of that, a lot of internal debug detail (raw config JSON, the full manifest layer list) is emitted at `INFO`. We should standardize on a single logging/reporting layer for lume that owns the terminal, with proper levels and a progress renderer that coexists with log lines. ## Repro ``` lume pull macos-tahoe-cua:latest ``` ## What it looks like today
Actual output from lume pull macos-tahoe-cua:latest (trimmed) ``` [2026-08-05T10:11:32Z] INFO: Downloading OCI-compliant layers [2026-08-05T10:11:32Z] INFO: Downloading config layer (sha256:56fd425ee0ab…) [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0% | Current: 1.6 KB/s | Avg: 1.6 KB/s | Peak: 1.6 KB/s | ETA: 3915:56:40 [2026-08-05T10:11:32Z] INFO: Downloading nvram layer (sha256:67825595efad…) [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0% | Current: 20.1 MB/s | Avg: 13.4 MB/s | Peak: 20.1 MB/s | ETA: 34:09 [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Config layer raw JSON: { "hardwareModel" : "YnBsaXN0MDDTAQIDBAQFXxAZRGF0YVJlcHJlc2VudGF0aW9uVmVyc2lvbl8QD1BsYXRmb3JtVmVyc2lvbl8QEk1pbmltdW1TdXBwb3J0ZWRPUxACowYHBxANEAAIDys9UlRYWgAAAAAAAAEBAAAAAAAAAAgAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAABc", ... } [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Manifest layers: application/vnd.trycua.lume.nvram.v1 size=33579164, application/vnd.trycua.lume.disk.v1 size=868083, ... (≈300 more entries on one line) [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Manifest config mediaType: application/vnd.trycua.lume.config.v1+json [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Decoded LumeOCIConfig: os=macOS hardwareModel=YnBsaXN0MDDTAQIDBAQF... [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Wrote config.json [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Saved nvram.bin [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: Chunked disk: 300 parts, total uncompressed size: 161061273600 disk layer disk layer 1: Pull complete disk layer 3: Pull complete disk layedisk layer 1: Pull complete disk layer 2: Pull complete disk layer 1 disk layer 1 disk layer disk layer 1: Pull complete disk layer 2: Pull complete disk layer 3: Pull complete disk layer 4: Pull complete disk layer 5: Pull complete disk layer 6: Pull complete disk layer 7: Pull complete disk layer 8: Pull complete disk layer 9: Pull complete disk layer 1: Downloading [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0.0 B/248.0 MB disk layer 1: Downloading [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0.0 B/448.1 MB disk layer 1: Downloading [░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░] 0.0 B/464.8 MB 9/300 done | 238.4 MB/21.5 GB | 19s ```
## Concrete problems 1. **Log lines and progress bars fight over the terminal.** An `INFO:` line is appended directly onto the end of a progress-bar line (`... ETA: 34:09 [2026-08-05T10:11:34Z] INFO: ...`). Nothing coordinates the two writers. 2. **Stray padding and torn frames.** Long runs of spaces and truncated text (`disk layedisk layer 1: Pull complete`, `disk layer 1` with no suffix) — the result of `\r` overwrites with a shorter string and no clear-to-end-of-line. 3. **Completed-layer list is re-rendered repeatedly**, so `disk layer 1: Pull complete` shows up many times in scrollback instead of once. 4. **Layer identity is wrong/confusing.** Three concurrent downloads are all labelled `disk layer 1` with three different sizes (248.0 MB / 448.1 MB / 464.8 MB). Layer numbering appears to be per-worker rather than a stable identifier. 5. **Debug internals at INFO level.** The raw config JSON blob, the ~300-entry manifest layer list, `Decoded LumeOCIConfig`, `Wrote config.json`, `Saved nvram.bin` are implementation detail. Nobody running `lume pull` needs them; they bury the two lines that actually matter. 6. **Nonsense ETA from a single sample.** `ETA: 3915:56:40` on the config layer, computed off a 1.6 KB/s first reading. 7. **Timestamps on every line in an interactive session.** `[2026-08-05T10:11:32Z] INFO:` per line is server-log formatting on a foreground CLI. Useful when piped to a file, noise on a TTY. 8. **Two different progress-bar styles in the same run** — the top-level `[░░░] 0% | Current: … | Avg: … | Peak: … | ETA: …` bar vs. the per-layer `[░░░] 0.0 B/248.0 MB` bar vs. the `9/300 done | 238.4 MB/21.5 GB | 19s` summary line. No shared renderer. ## Proposal **One reporting layer that owns stdout.** All user-facing output — log lines and progress — goes through a single component. Progress lives in a pinned region at the bottom of the screen; log lines scroll above it; the region is cleared (`\r` + erase-to-EOL, or a proper ANSI region) and redrawn on every update. This removes problems 1–3 by construction. **Levels, applied honestly.** - `INFO` (default): what the user asked for and its outcome — image being pulled, total size, progress, done/failed. - `DEBUG`: manifest contents, config JSON, per-file writes, decoded structs. Everything in problem 5 moves here. - `WARN`/`ERROR`: unchanged, to stderr. **Stable layer identity.** Label layers by short digest (`a3f1c9d2`) or a stable index assigned from the manifest, not a per-worker counter. Rendering should look closer to `docker pull`: one line per in-flight layer with a fixed identity, plus an aggregate line. **TTY vs. non-TTY.** On a TTY: no timestamps, no level prefix for `INFO`, colors, live progress. When not a TTY (piped, CI, `lume serve` logs): no ANSI, timestamps + level on every line, periodic progress lines instead of in-place redraws. **Suppress ETA until it's meaningful** — needs a minimum number of samples / elapsed time, and should use a smoothed rate rather than the instantaneous one. ### Sketch of the target output ``` Pulling macos-tahoe-cua:latest Manifest: 300 layers, 21.5 GB compressed / 150 GB on disk a3f1c9d2 ██████████████████░░░░░░░ 412 MB / 464 MB 58 MB/s 7b20e4f1 ████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 180 MB / 448 MB 61 MB/s ee91c507 ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 28 MB / 248 MB 44 MB/s 9/300 layers · 238 MB / 21.5 GB · 163 MB/s · ETA 2m 10s ``` ## Scope Applies to every lume command that prints progress or logs, not just `pull` — `push`, `run`, `create`, `clone`, `serve`. The point is to fix this once in a shared reporting layer rather than per-command.

title: e2e(cua-driver): require visible pointer and badge on Linux, Windows, and macOS
body:
## Problem

The shared `agent_cursor_showcase_test` currently proves only that *some* pixels change in one large region after an explicit `move_cursor`. It does not independently prove that both the agent pointer and session badge are composited, that they appear for the first recorded action, or that non-coordinate actions keep the overlay visible.

In a Linux X11 dogfood run with Cua Driver 0.17.0 at `fb2a6f60522ebf132270a3377c9a0496d2c0ba98`, the beginning of an MP4 contained keyboard and semantic accessibility actions without the pointer/badge; both appeared only after a later coordinate action. This issue is about the native overlay and recording contract, distinct from baking a virtual cursor into screenshot pixels (#1902).

## Acceptance criteria

- Use one shared behavior contract and pixel oracle across Linux, Windows, and macOS.
- Start recording before the first declared-session action, then exercise a keyboard action, a semantic accessibility action, and a coordinate action.
- Assert the pointer and session badge separately in captured pixels within a bounded startup deadline; a pointer without its badge (or vice versa) must fail.
- Inspect the produced MP4, not only tool state or a still screenshot, and verify the overlay is present from the first action.
- Run the contract in the existing interactive E2E lanes:
  - Linux X11 and Wayland
  - Windows interactive desktop
  - macOS Lume
- Retain the MP4, trajectory, and cursor-oracle screenshots as CI artifacts, with no silent platform skip.

## Existing seam

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/tests/agent_cursor_showcase_test.rs` already runs from the Linux, Windows, and macOS native E2E entry points. It is the natural place to strengthen the cross-platform oracle and add first-action coverage.

title: fix(cua-driver): direct capture grant is unobservable — `permissions status` always reports "not checked"
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver permissions grant` claims it requested **and verified** direct capture ("✅ … Accessibility, Screen Recording, and direct capture access"), but no direct-capture consent dialog was observed, and `cua-driver permissions status` run immediately afterwards still reports:

```
Direct Capture:     ❓ not checked (status is read-only; run `cua-driver-local permissions grant`)
```

So there is no way to observe that direct capture was ever actually granted. `grant` says yes; `status` can never say anything but "not checked". Running `grant` again produces the same claim, so re-running is not a way to confirm either.

## Reproduction

```console
$ /Users/francesco/.local/bin/cua-driver-local permissions grant
Launching CuaDriverLocal to request permissions.
A dialog for CuaDriverLocal will appear — approve Accessibility and Screen Recording in System Settings, then this command continues.

Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted.
macOS may now ask CuaDriverLocal to bypass the system private window picker and directly access your screen and audio. …
Choose Allow to request and verify direct capture now…

✅ CuaDriverLocal has Accessibility, Screen Recording, and direct capture access. You're set.

$ /Users/francesco/.local/bin/cua-driver-local permissions status
Accessibility:    ✅ granted
Screen Recording: ✅ granted
Direct Capture:     ❓ not checked (status is read-only; run `cua-driver-local permissions grant`)
Source: driver-daemon
```

Host: macOS, local install (`com.trycua.driver.local` identity), daemon running under the driver's own identity (`Source: driver-daemon`).

## Why this happens (code)

- `permission_status_request()` sends `check_permissions` with `prompt:false, probe_direct_capture:false` — `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2594`.
- `check_permissions` short-circuits to `(None, "not_checked", None)` whenever `!should_prompt` — `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/check_permissions.rs:322-337`.
- The CLI then prints the `None` branch — `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs:2560-2565`.

That read-only behaviour is deliberate (`SCShareableContent::get()` can itself raise Tahoe's picker-bypass consent, so a status call must not run it). The gap is that **the successful probe result from `grant` is never persisted**, so nothing can report it later. `screen_recording_capturable` is computed and thrown away on every call; there is no cache, no marker file, no daemon-held last-verified state.

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. `permissions grant` records the verified direct-capture outcome (timestamp + identity) and `permissions status` reports it as e.g. `✅ verified (2026-08-05, by permissions grant)` — still without running a probe itself; or
2. `permissions grant` stops claiming "direct capture access" as verified when the result cannot subsequently be observed, and says exactly what it did.

Option 1 is preferable — otherwise the only user-visible signal is a claim that no later command can corroborate.

## Secondary question: was the consent actually triggered?

No dialog appeared during `grant` on this machine, yet `grant` reported direct capture verified. Two indistinguishable explanations, and the current output does not disambiguate:

- the consent was already granted earlier (probe returned `ready` without a prompt) — fine; or
- the probe never raised the consent, and consent will instead be deferred to the first real recording — which is exactly the failure mode tracked in #2443.

`grant` should distinguish "consent already present" from "consent newly requested and approved" in its output, so this is not guesswork.

## Related

- #2443 — probe reports `ready` while Tahoe consent is still deferred to the first recording (adjacent, but that one is about the probe's truthfulness; this one is about the status surface never being able to report a result at all).
- #2296 / #2407 — made the direct ScreenCaptureKit consent explicit and observable.

title: cua-driver: re-validate trusted vs dom_event browser input routes across platforms
body:
## Summary Ad-hoc validation on macOS shows that the platform limitation which makes `browser_click` / `browser_pointer` refuse the **trusted** CDP Input route against a standalone browser **no longer reproduces** on current Chrome. In the same session, two *new* limitations of the trusted route surfaced that were not previously documented. We are **not** proposing a behavior change yet. `dom_event` remains fine for current use. This issue tracks the focused session needed to decide the routing story across all three platforms. ## Where the behavior lives - Declaration hook: `cua-driver-core/src/browser/platform.rs:226` (`standalone_trusted_input_background_limitation`) - Enforcement: `cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:1006` (`browser_click`), `cua-driver-core/src/browser/pointer.rs:371` (`browser_pointer`) - Platform declarations: - `platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs:399` — declares activation - `platform-linux/src/browser_platform.rs:391` — declares activation - `platform-windows` — no override (trusted allowed today) - Prior validation record: `docs/browser-tool-implementation-journal.md` (~369-372, ~666-671) ## Environment - macOS 26.5.2 - Google Chrome 150.0.7871.188 (standalone, user profile, attached via `browser_prepare` `existing_profile`) - cua-driver 0.17.0, local build with the macOS override removed so the default route could run - Target: a logged-in webmail SPA (list/detail layout). Mailbox contents intentionally omitted. ## Finding 1 — trusted route did not activate the window (macOS) Method: immediately before each dispatch, Chrome was verified **not** frontmost via `osascript … get frontmost of process "Google Chrome"`; foreground was re-sampled at t+0s/1s/2s after. Delivery was proven independently with a page-side capture-phase `click` listener recording `event.isTrusted` and coordinates. Five trusted dispatches: two onto an inert `

` (delivery proof), three onto real list rows (functional postconditions verified via `aria-selected` row change and SPA URL change). Result: `chromeIsFrontmost=false` at baseline and at **every** post-dispatch sample. A human observer watching the screen independently confirmed no visible raise. This also held when the bound tab was **not** the active tab: `document.visibilityState === "hidden"` *after* delivery, with no window raise and no tab switch. Hypothesis worth checking during re-validation: the original macOS/Linux measurement may have attributed Chrome's **connect-time** `"Allow remote debugging?"` consent surface (see `platform-macos/src/browser/consent_ui.rs`) to the input route. During this session, Chrome was repeatedly observed becoming frontmost right after a *fresh CDP connection*, seconds before any input was dispatched. Note the Windows/macOS/Linux split is equally consistent with either explanation, so this is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. ## Finding 2 — trusted ref-clicks silently miss partially-off-viewport elements The trusted route dispatches at the ref's box-model center without ensuring the node is in the viewport. ``` target row rect: top=645 bottom=726 height=81 viewport height: 725 dispatched at: (442, 685) page received: { isTrusted: true, x: 442, y: 685, tag: "DIV" } <-- not the target row result: row did not activate; reported effect: "unverifiable" ``` `dom_event` on the **same ref** activated the row immediately, since `el.click()` does not depend on viewport position. ## Finding 3 — wheel scroll is a no-op in a hidden tab The natural fix for Finding 2 is scroll-into-view, but `browser_pointer` `scroll` (`delta_y: 160`, coordinates over the scrollable list) left the rect byte-identical at `645/726`. Likely because scrolling is compositor-driven and a hidden tab has no active compositor, whereas discrete input still reaches the main thread. So in a hidden tab the trusted route currently cannot self-correct. ## Finding 4 — `effect: "unverifiable"` does not discriminate success from silent miss The successful clicks, the missed click, and the no-op scroll all returned `effect: "unverifiable"`. Accurate in each case, but it carries no signal; every outcome above was only distinguishable by checking page state out-of-band. ## Open questions to resolve 1. **Windows + Linux re-validation.** Does the trusted route actually steal foreground there? Linux declares the same limitation and has never been measured with a verified background baseline. Windows currently permits trusted input — confirm it still holds and that the consent surface is not a factor. 2. **Is `dom_event`-only sufficient?** Enumerate what it cannot do: trust-gated controls that check `isTrusted`, drag and drop, paste/clipboard-gated flows, file pickers, media/autoplay gestures, and anything requiring a real user-activation token. If that set is empty in practice, dom-only is a legitimate simplification. 3. **If trusted is worth keeping, make it reliable.** Scroll-into-view or hit-test the computed point (e.g. verify it resolves to the target backend node) and refuse rather than silently missing; add a real postcondition check so Finding 4 stops being ambiguous. 4. **Can trusted work dependably from a non-active tab?** Finding 3 suggests scroll-dependent corrections are unavailable there. Determine whether trusted-from-background-tab can be made sound, or whether it should be explicitly refused in that state. 5. **Correct the record** in `docs/browser-tool-implementation-journal.md`, `Skills/cua-driver/MACOS.md:460`, and `Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md:283-285` (+ the platform matrix ~412) once the cross-platform answer is known. ## Tasks - [ ] Re-validate trusted-route foreground behavior on Windows with a verified background baseline - [ ] Re-validate trusted-route foreground behavior on Linux (X11 + Wayland) - [ ] Confirm or rule out the consent-surface confound in the original measurement - [ ] Enumerate concrete `dom_event`-only limitations - [ ] Decide: dom-only, trusted-with-guardrails, or per-platform - [ ] If trusted is kept: viewport/hit-test guarantee + postcondition verification - [ ] Update journal, skills docs, and platform matrix to match the outcome ## Not covered by this evidence Minimized windows, windows on another Space, multi-display setups, other Chromium products (Edge, Brave), and non-Chromium engines. Embedded/Electron routes are separately proven and unaffected. The macOS change used to run this experiment is a local, uncommitted spike and is not proposed for merge.

title: cua-driver: adopt ActionEffect/effect_from_value_readback — browser hardcodes effect: "unverifiable"
body:
## Summary

`ActionEffect` already models the distinction the driver needs, and a classifier for it already exists — but adoption is near zero, and the browser stack bypasses both with a hardcoded string literal. The result is that successful actions, silent misses, and complete no-ops are all reported identically as `effect: "unverifiable"`.

## What already exists

`cua-driver-core/src/action_record.rs:9`

```rust
pub enum ActionEffect { Confirmed, Partial, Unverifiable, SuspectedNoop, Refused }
```

`cua-driver-core/src/action_record.rs:20` — `effect_from_value_readback(confirmed, changed, readback_available)`, whose doc comment already states the correct rule:

> "A missing readback never confirms success, while a readable unchanged value is stronger evidence of a no-op than of an unknown outcome."

`SuspectedNoop` is exactly the value that distinguishes *"I looked and nothing moved"* from *"I didn't look."*

## Current adoption

| Location | `effect_from_value_readback` | `ActionEffect::` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `platform-macos` | 1 file (`tools/set_window_frame.rs`) | 6 |
| `platform-windows` | 1 file (`tools/impl_.rs`) | 1 |
| `platform-linux` | 1 file (`tools/impl_.rs`) | 1 |
| `cua-driver-core/src/browser/` | **0** | **0** |

The browser path emits a literal instead — `cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs:1157`:

```rust
"effect": "unverifiable",
```

Reproduce:
```
grep -rn "ActionEffect\|effect_from_value_readback" --include="*.rs" cua-driver-core/src/browser/   # empty
```

## Measured consequence

In one session on macOS, five `browser_click` calls all returned `effect: "unverifiable"`:

- 3 changed page state (verified out-of-band via `aria-pressed` / `aria-selected` / URL change)
- 1 delivered a genuinely trusted click that missed its target entirely and changed nothing
- 1 `browser_pointer` scroll was a complete no-op (hidden tab, no compositor)

The field did not discriminate success from total failure in any case. Every outcome was only distinguishable by inspecting page state out of band.

## Proposed change

Route browser actions through the existing classifier rather than a literal, and widen adoption on the desktop side.

For a ref-targeted click the driver already resolves a `backendNodeId`, so a bounded before/after vector on the target node is cheap:

- ARIA state: `aria-pressed`, `aria-selected`, `aria-checked`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-current`, `disabled`
- Form state: `checked`, `value`
- The node's own `innerText` (bounded length)
- Document level: `location.href`, `document.activeElement` identity

Poll to a bounded deadline (~400ms, early-exit on first delta) and report the delta plus `observed_after_ms`:

```json
{"effect": "confirmed",
 "observed": {"aria-pressed": ["false", "true"], "innerText": ["378", "379"]},
 "observed_after_ms": 180}
```

## Design constraints (learned the hard way)

**Do not diff the whole document.** A media page mutates continuously; a generic `MutationObserver` returns "changed" for a click that did nothing. A confident false positive is worse than today's honest shrug.

**Do not use accessible names as postconditions.** On YouTube a like button's `aria-label` still read `"...come hanno fatto 378 altre persone"` *after* the like registered; the truth was only in `aria-pressed="true"` and the rendered count `378`→`379`. Comparing accessible names would report failure on a successful action — the false-negative mirror of the current problem.

**Do not add a flag to enable verification.** Make it the default behavior.

**Do not add a caller-supplied `expect` API yet.** Desktop callers have `verify_state` / `ObservationProvider` (`cua-driver-core/src/expectation.rs:48`); the browser stack has no equivalent (`grep -rn "verify_state\|ObservationProvider" cua-driver-core/src/browser/` is empty). Tempting to mirror it, but the automatic vector would have caught every observed case — add the explicit API only if something real escapes it.

## Risk to document

`SuspectedNoop` is **not** "failed". An action can legitimately do something the vector cannot observe (a fetch with no immediate DOM effect, a change inside a child frame). If the docs do not say this plainly, agents will treat it as hard failure and retry destructively.

This changes the action-result contract (`docs/action-result-contract.md`), so it needs the values documented, a CHANGELOG entry, and tests pinning each value — callers may already branch on `effect`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the hardcoded literal in `browser/tools.rs:1157` with the classifier
- [ ] Implement the bounded before/after vector for ref-targeted browser clicks
- [ ] Widen `effect_from_value_readback` adoption across desktop tools on all three OSs
- [ ] Document that `SuspectedNoop` is not failure
- [ ] Tests pinning each `ActionEffect` value; CHANGELOG + contract doc update

title: cua-driver: Linux browser actions render no agent cursor (visualize_browser_action unimplemented)
body:
## Summary

`visualize_browser_action` is not implemented in `platform-linux`, so it falls through to the empty default in the `BrowserPlatform` trait. Browser tool calls on Linux therefore place no agent cursor over the browser and render no badge — the agent is invisible during browser automation, with no refusal, warning, or log.

## Evidence

Trait default (a no-op body) — `cua-driver-core/src/browser/platform.rs:234`:

```rust
async fn visualize_browser_action(&self, _action: BrowserVisualAction) {}
```

Implementations:

- macOS: `platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs:403` ✅
- Windows: `platform-windows/src/browser_platform.rs:814` ✅
- Linux: **none** — `grep -c "visualize_browser_action" platform-linux/src/browser_platform.rs` → `0`

The badge rendering itself is fine and platform-independent: an audit of all 180 combinations (12 actions x 3 deliveries x 5 targets) in the shared `cursor-overlay` crate shows every glyph drawing correctly, including the browser globe, on both light and dark backgrounds. The gap is purely that Linux never places the cursor.

## The broader problem

`BrowserPlatform` mixes required and defaulted methods. A platform that does not override a defaulted method silently gets no-op behavior, and nothing distinguishes "deliberately accepts the default" from "nobody implemented this yet."

Full audit of all 15 methods:

| Method | Default? | macOS | Windows | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `standalone_trusted_input_background_limitation` | yes | yes | **default** | yes |
| `visualize_browser_action` | yes | yes | yes | **default (no-op)** |
| `discover_spawned_endpoint` | yes | **default** | yes | **default** |
| all 12 others | — | yes | yes | yes |

The other two rows are likely intentional (Windows genuinely has no trusted-input limitation; the `discover_spawned_endpoint` default preserves ordinary exact-pid ownership) — but that is inference, not something the code states.

## Proposed change

1. Implement `visualize_browser_action` for Linux, or have it refuse visibly rather than silently no-op.
2. Make deliberate non-implementation explicit so this class of gap cannot recur silently — e.g. require each platform to declare the set of defaults it accepts, and assert that set in a test. A gap that must be declared is a gap someone reviews.

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement Linux `visualize_browser_action` (X11 + Wayland), or refuse visibly
- [ ] Verify the agent cursor + badge appear over the browser on Linux
- [ ] Add an explicit per-platform declaration of accepted trait defaults, asserted in a test
- [ ] Confirm whether the `discover_spawned_endpoint` defaults on macOS/Linux are intentional

title: cua-driver: close out and generalize the macOS modality-ladder audit to Windows and Linux
body:
## Summary

`CUA_DRIVER_MODALITY_LADDER_AUDIT.md` (2026-06-28) identified a systemic false-success pattern across macOS desktop tools and prescribed a fix. It has no status tracking, so it is not possible to tell from the document which items shipped — and the same question was never asked for Windows or Linux at all.

## Background

That audit's root finding:

> A primary path returns a "success" status code, the tool reports success **without confirming the effect**, and there is no automatic escalation to the next rung.

Its prescribed fix: *"read back a post-condition, and treat *unverifiable* as *not-success* → escalate, surfacing the delivering path."*

P0 items listed: `type_text`, `click` (pixel), `drag`, `scroll`, `get_window_state`. P1 items include `set_value`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `click` (AX), `type_text_chars`, `press_key`, `hotkey`, `get_desktop_state`, `zoom`, `page`, `launch_app`.

## Why this needs closing out

Adoption numbers for the shared classifier suggest the prescribed pattern was not broadly applied — `effect_from_value_readback` appears in exactly one file per platform (see #2883). But the audit has no outcome column, so "is the false-success pattern fixed?" cannot be answered without re-reading every tool.

Note this is an open question, not an assertion of regression: the P0/P1 items were **not** individually re-verified against current code during the 2026-08-05 audit.

Separately, the ladder question has never been asked for Windows or Linux. Their tool code lives in single files (`platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`, 10,096 lines; `platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`, 7,809 lines), so a per-tool pass there is a materially different amount of work than on macOS — worth scoping before committing.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add an outcome column to the June audit (shipped / not shipped / no longer applicable) per P0 and P1 item
- [ ] Re-verify the five P0 items against current macOS code
- [ ] Run the equivalent per-tool ladder pass for Windows
- [ ] Run the equivalent per-tool ladder pass for Linux
- [ ] Supersede or archive the June document once cross-platform coverage exists

Context: `libs/cua-driver/docs/cross-platform-verification-audit.md` (F9).

title: ci(cua-driver): run distro checks after publication
body:
## Summary

- stop starting released-binary distro compatibility from the private candidate tag
- dispatch the standalone distro matrix from the Cua Driver finalizer only after it verifies the release and every staged asset are public
- scope `actions: write` to the finalizer job and pass the exact published version to the dispatch
- retain a one-minute retry window only for public CDN propagation
- add release-wiring regressions for the trigger and dispatch ordering

## Root cause

Tag candidate creation and distro compatibility started concurrently, but the release process intentionally keeps tag artifacts in a private draft until post-certification publication. The distro workflow therefore polled a public URL that could not exist during its 15-minute window.

GitHub also suppresses ordinary workflow-triggering events created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so this uses an explicit `workflow_dispatch` after publication instead of relying on `release.published`.

Fixes #2896.

## Validation

- `python3 .github/scripts/tests/test_cua_driver_release_wiring.py` (36 passed)
- full `.github/scripts/tests` suite with Python 3.13 and test dependencies (75 passed)
- `actionlint` on the distro workflow
- `actionlint` on the release workflow with its two pre-existing diagnostics excluded (`macos-26` runner catalog and SC2129)
- Prettier check on the distro workflow
- YAML parse checks for both workflows
- `git diff --check`

The active release tag and draft were not changed.

title: Linux: get_desktop_state capture fails with X11 GetImage BadMatch on WSLg (Xwayland, dual RANDR outputs)
body:
## Summary
On WSL2 with WSLg, `get_desktop_state` (and any full-root capture) fails with an X11 protocol error. Reproduced on cua-driver 0.17.0 AND 0.18.0 (linux x86_64).

## Environment
- WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04, WSLg (Weston compositor + Xwayland)
- DISPLAY=:0, WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0
- X screen: 3840x1080, two RANDR outputs side by side:
  - rdp-0 connected 1920x1080+0+0
  - rdp-2 connected 1920x1080+1920+0

## Repro
```
echo '{"screenshot_out_file":"/tmp/shot.png"}' | cua-driver call get_desktop_state
```

## Actual result
```
Capture error: X11 error X11Error { error_kind: Match, error_code: 8, sequence: 2, bad_value: 1080, minor_opcode: 0, major_opcode: 73, extension_name: None, request_name: Some("GetImage") }
```
No PNG is written. Identical error on both 0.17.0 and 0.18.0.

## Analysis
`bad_value: 1080` on a core `GetImage` (opcode 73) request suggests the capture path computes an out-of-bounds region for the second RANDR output — consistent with the second output's offset being computed as y=1080 (vertical stacking) instead of x=+1920 (the actual horizontal layout reported by RANDR). Root window is 3840x1080 per xdpyinfo/xrandr, so a correct full-root GetImage(0,0,3840,1080) would be in bounds.

Also note: `cua-driver doctor` reports `screen_capture_capability: X11 reachable; screen capture path is functional` — a false green in this environment.

Wayland backend (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`) does not help: WSLg's Weston does not expose wlr-screencopy, so capture falls back to the same X11 path and fails identically.

## Expected
Full-desktop capture works on WSLg Xwayland multi-output layouts (or doctor flags the unsupported layout honestly).

title: fix(cua-driver): activate exact macOS window for foreground drag
body:
## Summary

- activate the exact macOS window for foreground HID drag using the shared WindowServer activation guard
- add complete Electron pointer and HTML5 drag event evidence to the shared fixture
- require macOS foreground Electron drag coverage to prove the full receiver event sequence

## Root cause

The first missing receiver event was `pointerdown`. The foreground drag path used app-level activation plus a fixed delay, so Electron could receive the HID gesture before the requested native window owned focus. The click path already used exact-window activation; drag now uses the same fail-closed guard for the whole gesture.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (331 passed)
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --test cross_platform_behavior_test drag_event_evidence_matches_complete_event_names_only`

Closes #2906

title: docs(cua-driver): define target-bound credential delivery
body:
## Summary

- define target-first `find_credentials(target)` discovery that matches only trusted host-registered bindings and returns safe descriptors with fresh target-bound handles
- define `type_secret(handle, field, target)` delivery without plaintext, provider locators, or vault search in agent-visible traffic
- add a diagram-first architecture companion covering the permission-model fit, Computer History separation, OpenShell integration, and standards reuse
- treat OpenShell as the standard outer runtime and policy boundary for unattended agents while keeping Cua authorization and live GUI target proof mandatory
- use a dedicated automation service account and least-privilege vault with host-only bootstrap enrollment, rotation, revocation, and health
- keep the implementation internal until the public manifest, ABI, UniFFI, generated Python and TypeScript SDKs, and MCP can flip together

## Why

Generic text input requires the caller to possess plaintext before Cua Driver can act. This proposal adds a release capability: trusted host code selects and scopes credentials, while the agent can only discover matches for a verified target and request delivery with a fresh handle bound to that exact browser, document, and field context.

The design reuses OpenShell for sandbox, network, MCP admission, workload identity seams, credential-driver storage, and outer security events. It reuses OAuth, SPIFFE, sender-constrained tokens, WebAuthn, OCSF, and non-exportable-operation patterns where they apply. Cua-specific work is limited to binding one secret release to a freshly verified live GUI password field and delivering it without exposing the value to the agent.

## Implementation sequence

1. Make recording and visible action labels fail closed.
2. Add semantic-v2 secure browser-field eligibility.
3. Add the internal broker, provider, binding, handle, lease, release-plan, and fake-provider foundation.
4. Add R3 `secret_release` authorization.
5. Add target-first discovery and guarded browser delivery.
6. Add dedicated bootstrap secret stores and service-account lifecycle.
7. Implement the selected dedicated-vault provider adapter.
8. Certify an authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP bridge through OpenShell; retain stdio only as a directly supervised compatibility path.
9. Flip contract, manifest, ABI, UniFFI, generated SDKs, and MCP together.
10. Certify exact-candidate-SHA Windows and Linux Fleet browser rows before advertising them.

## Validation

- all nine Mermaid blocks render successfully with Mermaid CLI and Chrome
- Prettier formatting check passes for both changed Markdown files
- Markdown diff whitespace check passes
- all local relative links resolve
- all external references in the architecture companion return HTTP 200
- public-text scan finds no prohibited unrelated project references, private paths, credentials, or drafting placeholders
- staged diff reviewed before commit
