title: fix(cua-driver): keep named CLI sessions and include X11 overlay in screenshots
body: ## Summary - One-shot `cua-driver call` (and `cua-driver-local call`) always minted a disposable transport `cli-{uuid}` and sent `session_end` after the response. That reaped every public session owned by that transport, so the agent cursor overlay disappeared immediately. A following `get_agent_cursor_state` with the same public `session` returned "session has ended". A held MCP connection kept the overlay because its transport stayed alive. - X11 `get_desktop_state` captured the root via ImageMagick `import -window root` or `XGetImage` on root. The overlay is a shaped override-redirect window (`Cua.AgentCursorOverlay.*`). Root reads cannot see those pixels (daemon log: "root reads cannot see this window's own pixels"), so PNG screenshots omitted the cursor even while picom composited it into x11vnc/noVNC. ## What changed - **Named CLI sessions keep the overlay.** If JSON args include a non-empty `session` string, that public name is the daemon transport id and the CLI does **not** send `session_end`. Later `call` invocations with the same `session` continue that overlay. `end_session` still tears it down. Calls without `session` still mint `cli-{uuid}` and `session_end` it (security / one-shot cleanup unchanged). - **X11 desktop screenshots include the mapped overlay.** After the root capture, the screenshot path finds mapped `Cua.AgentCursorOverlay.*` windows, reads their shaped pixmap, and blends those premultiplied pixels onto the root buffer. Disabled or unmapped overlays leave the root capture unchanged. Root-only `XGetImage` is no longer the final capture when the overlay is shown. ## Grok Bot / Xvfb reproduction Observed on a Grok Bot Linux VM (Debian 13, Xvfb `:2`, picom, no root): 1. `cua-driver call move_cursor '{"session":"demo","x":...,"y":...}'` painted the overlay, then tore it down on the synchronous `session_end` of `cli-{uuid}`. `get_agent_cursor_state` with `{"session":"demo"}` then failed with "session has ended". The same sequence over a held MCP connection kept the overlay. 2. `get_desktop_state` / root `XGetImage` omitted the cursor while the x11vnc/noVNC view (picom-composited) showed it. ## Related work No linked GitHub issue. Aligns CLI with the already-documented public session label ("repeat a short public session on every call"). Not a new SDK/MCP contract; no RFC. ## Compatibility and risk - User-visible: named `cua-driver call` sessions now persist until `end_session` or idle TTL, matching MCP/SDK. Unnamed one-shot calls are unchanged. - X11 screenshots may now include overlay pixels when the overlay is mapped. macOS/Windows capture is unchanged. - Rollback: revert this commit. ## Validation - `cargo test -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver named_cli_session unnamed_cli_call blank_or_non_string_session` - `cargo test -p platform-linux capture::` (19 passed, 1 ignored live XShm test) - Known gap: no live Xvfb overlay-in-screenshot run in this environment. Compositing is covered by focused unit tests (empty/unmapped tiles, opaque and translucent blend, ARGB zpixmap alpha). Linux CI X11 overlay click-through remains the live overlay gate. ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] This change does not require an RFC (documented session-label contract; CLI now honors it). - [x] Tests and the Xvfb/Grok Bot reproduction are in this description; live screenshot-with-overlay on Xvfb is the remaining CI/maintainer gap. - [x] Title is a Conventional Commit for the production fix (`fix(cua-driver): ...`). - [x] No external contribution to attribute. - [x] Release-tracked: user-visible CLI session + X11 screenshot behavior, so this should release.

title: fix(cua-driver): diagnose Linux hosts and refuse dishonest background PX
body: ## Summary - Problem this solves: `cua-driver diagnose` on Linux printed a broken macOS TCC dump, and `doctor` did not warn that Xvfb / missing `/dev/uinput` cannot host background MPX. Background pixel clicks on those hosts fell through to XSendEvent and returned `effect: unverifiable`, which looks like a landed click. - What changed: Linux `diagnose` prints a host section (display server, compositor, uinput, session bus, AT-SPI, background MPX) and explicitly skips macOS TCC/codesign. Linux `doctor` warns on Xvfb/Xtigervnc and missing/inaccessible `/dev/uinput`. When AT-SPI-at-point misses and MPX cannot run, background PX/scroll/drag returns structured `background_unavailable` so the caller retries with `delivery_mode: foreground`. ## Reproduction (Grok Bot Linux VM) Debian 13, user `box`, no root: - Display: `Xvfb :2 -screen 0 1280x800x24` plus `x11vnc`. `xfwm4 --compositor=off` and `picom --backend xrender`. - `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` unset, `/run/user/1000` does not exist, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` unset in the agent shell, no systemd user (`systemctl` missing), no `xfce4-session`. - `/dev/uinput` does not exist. - `at-spi2-core` not installed; `at-spi-bus-launcher` absent; `org.a11y.Bus` ServiceUnknown. `get_window_state` returns `degraded: true` with that reason. - Before this change, `doctor` warned AT-SPI only. It did not warn about Xvfb or missing uinput. - `diagnose` was macOS-shaped (TCC, `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, `~/Library/.../TCC.db`, LaunchAgents) and needed `sqlite3`. - Background PX on Chromium cannot use MPX; AT-SPI-at-point is dead; remaining rungs were XSendEvent (unreliable on Chrome) or `delivery_mode: foreground`. Clicks often returned `effect: unverifiable`. ## Related work No linked intake issue. Small, self-contained fix from maintainer-selected Cloud Agent work. RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change): not required. The `background_unavailable` / `delivery_mode: foreground` contract is unchanged; the driver now emits it when the host cannot land background PX. ## Compatibility and risk - User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux `doctor`/`diagnose` output changes. Background PX/scroll/drag on Xvfb or no-uinput hosts now refuse with `code: background_unavailable` instead of a quiet unverifiable success. Foreground delivery and AT-SPI-at-point are unchanged. macOS diagnose is unchanged. - Risk and rollback: revert this commit. GTK3 harness already expected this refusal when MPX is unavailable (except left-click AT-SPI). ## Validation - Focused tests and checks: - `cargo test -p platform-linux --locked --lib` filters: `diagnostics::`, `background_pixel_refuses`, `no_mpx_pointer`, `real_pointer_capabilities` - `cargo test -p cua-driver --locked --bin cua-driver` filters: `doctor::`, `diagnose_linux` - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - Manual or platform evidence: unit tests inject the Grok Bot facts (Xvfb `:2`, missing uinput, unset `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, no `/run/user/1000/bus`, AT-SPI down). Full desktop E2E matrix not rerun; this is probe/honesty logic, not a harness-app behavior change on real Xorg. - Known gaps or CI still required: ordinary PR CI (`CI: Release metadata`, Linux Rust unit/compile). Doctor does not apt-install `at-spi2-core`. ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above. - [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained. - [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change. - [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included. - [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

title: sandbox: QEMURuntime defaults to docker, where extra_args is rejected
body:
`QEMURuntime(mode: str = "docker", **kwargs)` routes to `QEMUDockerRuntime` unless the caller passes `mode="bare-metal"`. `QEMUDockerRuntime` does not accept `extra_args`, so:

```python
QEMURuntime(extra_args=["-cpu", "host"])
```

fails with `TypeError: QEMUDockerRuntime.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'extra_args'` — naming a class the caller never mentioned.

`extra_args` is how you pass `-cpu host`, which is the documented fix for the most common local failure in the Minecraft guide (the game exiting during resource loading under the default `qemu64` model). So the default silently selects a backend that cannot accept the flag most needed on the other one.

Same shape as the `os_type` default fixed in #3154: a default that quietly picks the wrong thing and reports it as a low-level type error. Options: reject unknown kwargs with a message naming `mode`, accept and ignore, or make the factory dispatch on what was actually requested.

title: sandbox: tunnel.forward() unavailable on pool-claim sandboxes
body:
Whether `sb.tunnel.forward(port)` works depends on how the sandbox was obtained, through the same public API:

- `Sandbox.create(...)` → `FleetCloudTransport`, which implements `forward_tunnel` ✅
- a pool claim (`pool.py:161`) → base `FleetTransport`, which does not ❌

The failure message compounds it:

```
FleetTransport does not support port forwarding.
Supported transports: ADBTransport, FleetCloudTransport, GRPCEmulatorTransport, SSHTransport.
```

which reads as "Fleet cannot tunnel" when the truth is "this Fleet path cannot". Hit while booting a custom containerDisk on Fleet; the Minecraft guide now carries a caveat pointing readers at `/api/svc/<namespace>/<sandbox>-port-3000/` instead.

Either `FleetTransport` should implement `forward_tunnel`, or the pool path should hand back the transport that does.

title: docs: the Minecraft containerDisk image is unverified as actually launching the game
body:
The published image `ghcr.io/trycua/minecraft-agent:1.20.1`, and the how-to section that builds it, are verified only as far as **files being present**, not the game running.

Verified: the image pulls anonymously, boots locally (READY 248s) and on Fleet (READY 187s), and contains `instances/1.20.1`, `java-runtime-gamma`, Mesa `opengl32.dll` beside `javaw.exe`, and the client jar — with no `accounts.json`.

**Not verified: that Minecraft actually launches from it.** Prism will not add an offline account without a Microsoft account signed in first, so there is no credential-free smoke test, and the published image is deliberately never-signed-in.

One concrete residual risk: this image's Java came from *Settings → Java → Installations → Download* rather than from a Launch, so Prism auto-detecting `java-runtime-gamma` at launch is untested. If it does not, the first thing a reader does with this image fails.

Needs a throwaway sign-in on a scratch overlay of the published disk (never on the published disk itself) to confirm the game reaches a world.

title: fix(cua-driver): print skill path from singular command
body:
## What changed

- route the exact singular command `cua-driver skill` to the existing read-only `skills path` implementation
- classify the alias as the reviewed finite `skills/path` operation instead of an implicit MCP tool call
- advertise the alias in `--help`, the CLI manifest, generated CLI docs, and the checked-in CLI reference
- add focused binary-level coverage while preserving bare plural `cua-driver skills` status behavior

## Why

Unknown top-level verbs currently fall through to the implicit MCP tool-call route. As a result, `skill` reaches authorization as an unclassified tool and fails with `Permission denied: tool 'skill' has no reviewed risk classification` instead of serving the natural read-only discovery request.

## User impact

Agents and users can run `cua-driver skill` to print the installed skill-pack directory. Existing plural skill management commands are unchanged.

## Validation

Candidate `4b2ea303e48b37a00b9b2772076e3cc6592193d3`:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver`
- `npx tsx scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.ts --check`
- ordinary pull request CI, including `CI: Release metadata`
- Linux exact-SHA canonical matrix: passed (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/31882701192)
- Windows exact-SHA canonical matrix: passed (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/31882701387)

## Known gaps / blockers

The canonical macOS Lume runner cannot start on this host because strict preflight requires the private signing keychain at `~/Library/Keychains/cua-driver-signing.keychain-db`, which is not present. No partial macOS result is being treated as certification.

Fixes #3181

title: docs(cua-driver): permission-modes/browser docs disagree with shipped 0.19.3/0.20.0 (bounded serve flags, manifest format, retired approval token)
body:
## What this is

While wiring cua-driver's browser authorization into Hermes Agent (NousResearch/hermes-agent#86342), we live-verified the documented flags and flows against release binaries (0.19.3, then re-audited on 0.20.0 via `cua-driver manifest`). Three places where the docs disagree with the shipped driver cost us a debugging round trip each; filing them together since they share a root (docs lagging the binary).

**Environment:** cua-driver-rs 0.19.3 and 0.20.0 release binaries, Linux x86_64. Every claim reproduced against the binary; nothing inferred from source alone.

## 1. Bounded-mode serve flags: docs say `--capability-manifest`, binary requires `--session-policy`

The [permission modes reference](https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/permission-modes) and the [Drive a Web Page guide](https://cua.ai/docs/how-to-guides/driver/drive-a-web-page) both show:

```bash
cua-driver serve --permission-mode bounded \
  --capability-manifest ./browser-session.yaml \
  --approve-capability-manifest
```

The 0.19.3/0.20.0 binary rejects that spelling:

```
Error: permission mode bounded requires --session-policy <path> at trusted daemon startup
```

`--session-policy` + `--approve-session-policy` work (0.20.0 `manifest` output lists both spellings in the args table, but only the session-policy pair is accepted for bounded startup on the builds we tested).

## 2. Manifest example format: `version: 3` rejected; required fields undocumented

The docs' example manifest (`version: 3`, no `mode`) fails to load, with the binary demanding in sequence:

```
missing field `mode`
missing field `idle_timeout`
unsupported session policy version 3; expected 1 or 2
session policy mode must be bounded
```

A minimal loading policy on 0.19.3/0.20.0 is:

```yaml
mode: bounded
version: 2
expires_after: 2h
idle_timeout: 20m
allow:
  tools: [start_session, end_session, get_browser_state, browser_prepare, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type]
```

(Related: #2847 fixed example-loading issues before; the live pages still show the failing shape as of 2026-08-16.)

## 3. `browser-approve` token flow still documented as the primary CLI route after #3185 removed it

The Drive a Web Page guide still leads the "direct CLI or raw-socket use" path with `cua-driver browser-approve` minting an `approval_token` for `browser_prepare`. On 0.19.3 the `browser_prepare` schema already called the token "legacy … disabled unless a trusted launcher explicitly enables the same-user-writable compatibility path"; on 0.20.0 the `approval_token` property is gone from the schema entirely (consistent with #3185). The working route we landed on is the trusted-launcher grant (`mcp --grant existing-profile` / `serve --grant existing-profile`), which the docs mention only in passing.

Happy to PR the doc edits if that's welcome — we have the exact tested command lines and a loading manifest example from the integration work.

title: docs(rfcs): define OAuth and MCP gateway boundary
body:
## Summary

- define Cua Driver's standard, transport-neutral MCP boundary
- place OAuth, DCR, TLS, tunnels, and provider adapters in a separate optional gateway
- keep one canonical Driver tool inventory and require trusted local approval for remote desktop access

## Why

PR #2063 demonstrates demand from remote MCP clients that require OAuth and HTTPS. Keeping the public OAuth edge inside `cua-driver` would couple the desktop runtime to token storage, tunnel operations, and client-specific compatibility rules.

This RFC moves those responsibilities to a separately owned gateway while keeping Driver as the final authorization point.

Refs #3197.

Salvaged from #2063. The RFC and commit preserve `outdog-hwh`'s design credit; later implementations must preserve authorship for any material code they adapt.

## Validation

- `prettier --check rfcs/3197-oauth-mcp-gateway-boundary.md`
- RFC template-section and placeholder scan
- `git diff --check`
- repository-relative target check for every linked source and RFC file

## Review focus

- ownership and packaging of the gateway
- the minimum authenticated Driver connection-lease contract
- trusted local approval ownership on each platform
- first supported OAuth and MCP transport profiles
- DCR, token lifetime, revocation, storage, and tunnel policy

This is a draft decision document. It does not authorize implementation until the RFC is accepted.

title: fix(cua-driver): route foreground typing into Screen Sharing canvases
body:
## Problem

`type_text` cannot deliver foreground keyboard input to an exact Apple Screen Sharing window whose content is exposed as `AXSharedScreen`.

## Reproduction

Environment:

- macOS host
- Cua Driver `0.19.4-nightly.20260812.31613035038`
- Apple Screen Sharing connected to a local disposable VNC target
- multiple Screen Sharing windows present

Steps:

1. Resolve the Screen Sharing PID and exact connected window with `launch_app` / `list_windows`.
2. Snapshot that exact window. Its content is an `AXSharedScreen`; the response reports `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` for the PID keyboard route.
3. A foreground pixel click against the exact PID/window returns:

   `effect: unverifiable`, `route: global_input`

4. Attempt foreground pixel-addressed typing against the same exact PID/window:

   `type_text({pid, window_id, x, y, text, delivery_mode: "foreground"})`

Actual result:

`type_text failed: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery`

The text is not delivered to the remote canvas.

## Expected

Foreground delivery should temporarily focus the exact Screen Sharing connection window, route text into its shared-screen canvas, and restore the prior foreground app. If this surface cannot be supported safely, the driver should return a specific pre-dispatch capability error that identifies Screen Sharing / `AXSharedScreen`, instead of the generic exact-window focus failure.

## Notes

The exact-window binding matters because several Screen Sharing windows may share one PID. No remote address, credentials, screenshots, or private task data are required to reproduce.

title: Windows: VMware Workstation console drops foreground SendInput; needs focus-proxy/scancode route
body:
## Summary

On Windows 11 with VMware Workstation 26.0.0, cua-driver 0.20.0 can capture the `VMUIFrame` and reports successful foreground input, but the guest console receives nothing.

## Reproduction

1. Run a VM in VMware Workstation and stop at a text prompt in the guest console.
2. Capture the exact VMware window.
3. Call `type_text` with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`.
4. Call `press_key` for a digit and Return with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`.
5. Optionally call standalone `bring_to_front` before each action.
6. Re-capture the window.

Observed driver results include:

```text
Typed 1 char(s) via SendInput (delivery_mode:foreground)
Sent 9 via SendInput (delivery_mode:foreground)
Sent return via SendInput (delivery_mode:foreground)
foreground_focus: bring_to_front invoked
```

The guest remains at the same prompt. VMware's status bar still says `To direct input to this VM, click inside or press Ctrl+G.`

## Root-cause evidence

The visible console is a nested raw-input surface, not the top-level `VMUIFrame`. Live child-window enumeration shows:

```text
VMUIView
VMware.GuestWindow
MKSEmbedded  MKSWindow#1
MKSEmbedded  MKSWindow#0
```

Additional live probes tried all of the following against the nested `MKSEmbedded` child and still did not reach the guest:

- foreground activation of the root window;
- real system-queue mouse click at the child center;
- `SendInput` keyboard events with `KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE`;
- direct `WM_KEYDOWN` / `WM_KEYUP` with scan-code bits;
- per-key delay and Return;
- `Ctrl+G` through cua-driver foreground hotkey.

This indicates VMware's MKS console requires a dedicated focus-proxy/raw-input path. Top-level `SetForegroundWindow` plus ordinary `SendInput` is insufficient. `SendInput` acceptance is not proof of guest delivery, so the current success message is a false positive for this surface.

## Proposed minimal fix

1. Detect VMware `VMUIFrame` with a live descendant `MKSEmbedded` / `MKSWindow#*`.
2. Treat it as a focus-proxy surface, similar in spirit to the RDP limitation in #2083.
3. Keep the root foreground across the whole sequence, establish focus/capture on the MKS child using VMware-compatible activation, then send physical-key scancodes.
4. Return `effect:unverifiable` or `suspected_noop` unless a post-action visual predicate proves change; do not report success solely from `SendInput`'s inserted-event count.
5. Add a Windows integration fixture or a documented live acceptance test for VMware console input.

## Environment

```text
Windows 11 Pro for Workstations 10.0.26200.9168
VMware Workstation 26.0.0 build-25388281
cua-driver 0.20.0
Hermes computer_use
```

title: Linux X11: pixel action frame excludes title bar while get_window_state screenshot includes it (~47px systematic miss)
body:
## Environment
- cua-driver 0.20.0 (linux-x86_64), Ubuntu 22.04.5, GNOME Shell 42.9, X11 dual-head 5120x1600, scale 1.0

## Summary
On Linux X11, pixel coordinates for window-scoped input actions (`click` with `pid`+`window_id`+`x`+`y`) use a coordinate frame that **excludes** the window's title bar, while the screenshot returned by `get_window_state` for the same window **includes** the title bar. Grounding coordinates on that screenshot therefore lands systematically low by the header height.

## Reproduction (2026-08-18)
1. Launched gnome-calculator (GTK4 window, 732x594, stock GNOME header bar ≈47px).
2. `get_window_state` → screenshot (732x594, includes header bar). Grounded the "5" keypad button at screenshot coords (140, 465) via a vision model.
3. `click {pid, window_id, x:140, y:465}` → landed on the button one row **below** ("2" appeared in the readout).
4. `click {x:140, y:418}` (= 465 − 47) → landed on "5" exactly ("25" in the readout).

## Expected
Either the click frame should match the screenshot frame (both include the header), or the tool description should document the offset. Right now the docs for `drag` say "window-local screenshot pixels", which implies the frames agree.

## Note
Possibly the Linux cousin of #1979 (Windows multi-monitor click offset). Happy to test a fix — easy to reproduce with any GTK4 app + the calculator method above.

title: launch_app steals focus on GNOME/X11 despite active:false reply
body:
## Environment
- cua-driver 0.20.0 (linux-x86_64), Ubuntu 22.04.5, GNOME Shell 42.9, X11

## Summary
`launch_app` on GNOME/X11 gives the newly launched window keyboard focus, even though the response reports `"active": false`. For co-work ("no-foreground") workflows this is disruptive: launching an app while the user is typing steals their focus.

## Reproduction (2026-08-18)
- Active window: user's terminal (verified via `xdotool getactivewindow`).
- `launch_app {"name": "gnome-calculator"}` → response `"active": false`, but the calculator window received keyboard focus (user observed focus switch; verified active window changed).
- Input-delivery tools correctly avoid focus changes (background `click` verified: digits landed in an unfocused calculator while focus and cursor stayed in the user's window) — only `launch_app` has the problem.

## Suspicion
The daemon spawns the process without a startup-notification (SN) timestamp, so the WM applies its default new-window focus policy. Passing a SN sequence with a stale/zero timestamp (or setting `_NET_WM_USER_TIME` to 0 on the launched window) would make GNOME keep focus with the user's window.

## Suggestion
A `--no-focus`/`background: true` option on `launch_app`, or SN timestamp handling. Thanks — the rest of the input model is exemplary for co-work use.

title: macOS: no way to exclude a window from get_desktop_state capture
body:
Hello — we are embedding `@trycua/cua-driver@0.20.0` (darwin-arm64) as the capability layer for a macOS desktop agent, and have hit a gap we would like to check we have read correctly before working around it permanently.

## What we need

Our own UI is a floating panel that stays on screen while the agent drives. Its pixels must not reach the model: if they do, the model can see — and try to click — our own Stop control, which is the one thing that must remain the human's.

## What we found

There appears to be no capture-exclusion capability. Probing the runtime surface of 0.20.0:

- `listToolsJson()` returns 55 tools; none matches `exclude`, `filter`, `occlusion` or `content_protect`. The nearest are `list_windows`, `get_window_state` and `set_window_frame`, which are window *management* rather than capture filtering.
- The typed surface has no equivalent. `GetDesktopStateInput` takes only `session` and `screenshot_out_file`.
- `SCContentFilter`'s exclusion semantics do not appear to be reachable through the SDK.

For completeness: `setContentProtection(true)` on the Electron side is *not* a substitute — it is verified not to exclude a window from ScreenCaptureKit on macOS 15 (filed against both Tauri and Electron, acknowledged by Apple DTS).

## Questions

1. Is exclusion reachable in 0.20.0 by some route we have missed?
2. Is `SCContentFilter`-style exclusion (by window id, or by excluding the calling application) on the roadmap for the desktop capture path?
3. If we contributed it, what shape would you want — an optional `exclude_window_ids` on `get_desktop_state`, or configuration at session start?

## What we are doing meanwhile

Cropping. While driving, our panel docks to a full screen edge, so we remove that band from the capture before the image reaches the model, and publish the crop rectangle so coordinates can be mapped back. It works, and it costs us a strip of the screen the agent can then no longer see — which is why we would rather have exclusion.

## Reproduction

Node 20, macOS 15.7.4, arm64, Screen Recording granted:

```js
import { CuaDriver } from "@trycua/cua-driver";
const d = CuaDriver.create(undefined);
const tools = JSON.parse(await d.listToolsJson()).tools.map(t => t.name);
console.log(tools.length);                                              // 55
console.log(tools.filter(n => /exclud|filter|occlu|protect/i.test(n))); // []
await d.shutdown(); d.uniffiDestroy();
```

---

## Two smaller documentation points, found while integrating

Happy to split these into their own issues if you would prefer.

**1. `get_screen_size` contradicts `click` / `move_cursor` about the desktop coordinate space.**

- `get_screen_size`: *"Agents click in points; Retina displays have `scale_factor` 2.0"*
- `click.x`: *"X in screenshot pixels … a desktop target uses the native `get_desktop_state` PNG"*
- `move_cursor`: *"With `scope=desktop`, moves the real OS pointer in native `get_desktop_state` screenshot coordinates"*

We measured it rather than picking one. On a 1470×956-point display, `move_cursor` with `scope: "desktop"` at `(1470, 956)` — the raw capture's centre — put the pointer at `(735, 478)` points, i.e. the centre of the screen. So desktop input is in **capture pixels** and the `click` / `move_cursor` text is right; the `get_screen_size` line reads as a contradiction. On a 2× display, following the wrong one is a doubled click offset that presents as the model aiming badly rather than as a coordinate bug.

This may be the same class as #3237 (Linux X11: pixel action frame vs `get_window_state` screenshot, ~47px systematic miss) — a coordinate-space mismatch that surfaces as apparent aim drift.

**2. `scale_factor` reports 1.0 for a 2× capture.**

On the same display, `structuredJson` reports `scale_factor: 1.0` on both `get_screen_size` and `get_desktop_state`, while `get_desktop_state` returns a 2940×1912 PNG for a 1470×956-point screen:

```
get_screen_size    {"height":956,"scale_factor":1.0,"width":1470}
get_desktop_state  screenshot_width 2940, screenshot_height 1912, scale_factor 1.0
```

`screenshot_width` / `screenshot_height` are correct and agree with the PNG's IHDR — it is only `scale_factor` that looks wrong. If it is meant to describe the backing-store ratio it appears to be reporting the wrong value; if it means something else, a note in the description would save the next integrator the measurement. We now derive the ratio as PNG dimensions ÷ reported point size and never read the field.

Thanks for the driver — the embedded/same-process path has been straightforward to build on, and `invoke_menu` in particular solved a problem we expected to have to hack around.

title: [Bug]: Docs AI assistant fails because /docs/api/copilotkit returns HTTP 500
body: ### Primary area Documentation ### Summary The AI assistant on `cua.ai/docs` is currently unusable because the production CopilotKit runtime endpoint returns HTTP 500 during runtime discovery. I originally thought Pi-hole might be blocking it, but DNS resolves normally and the failure reproduces directly against the site outside the browser. ### Reproduction 1. Open `https://cua.ai/docs/tutorials/drive-your-first-app`. 2. Let the docs assistant initialize. 3. Observe the frontend send: ```json {"method":"info"} ``` 4. The request to `POST https://cua.ai/docs/api/copilotkit` returns: ```text HTTP 500 Unexpected Server Error ``` 5. The frontend then reports: ```text useAgent: Agent 'default' not found after runtime sync (runtimeUrl=/docs/api/copilotkit). No agents registered. ``` 6. I also reproduced it directly from PowerShell, without depending on the browser: ```powershell Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://cua.ai/docs/api/copilotkit' ` -Method Post ` -ContentType 'application/json' ` -Body '{"method":"info"}' ` -SkipHttpErrorCheck ``` This consistently returns HTTP 500. ### Expected behavior `POST /docs/api/copilotkit` with `{"method":"info"}` should return HTTP 200 with the runtime/agent metadata needed for the docs assistant to initialize, and the `default` agent should become available. ### Actual behavior The production endpoint returns HTTP 500 with a plain-text `Unexpected Server Error`. The assistant then fails runtime sync and cannot find the `default` agent. A fresh reproduction on August 18, 2026 returned: ```text Status: 500 Body: Unexpected Server Error Server: Vercel Vercel cache: MISS x-vercel-id: sfo1:sfo1:sfo1::sfo1::z8hzs-1787085847970-afc6dcb23349 Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 20:44:08 GMT ``` I also tested the route with GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, malformed POST bodies, and `agent/connect`. They all return the same 500 response with separate Vercel request IDs, so this does not look like a cached error. ### Environment - Cua component/version: production `cua.ai` docs website - CopilotKit frontend bundle observed on production: `1.50.1` - Operating system: Windows 11 x64 - Browser where I first saw it: Firefox 156 - Also reproduced in Chromium 151 and directly through PowerShell ### Evidence - `cua.ai`, `/docs/`, and the frontend assets load normally with HTTP 200. - `cua.ai` DNS resolution matched Cloudflare `1.1.1.1` during testing. - The failure is isolated to the CopilotKit backend route returning HTTP 500 from Vercel. - Subsequent `agent/connect` requests for `agentId: "default"` also return 500. ### Workaround and additional context I do not know the exact server-side exception because that would require access to the Vercel function logs. The failure appears to happen server-side in the production CopilotKit route. I would start by looking up the `x-vercel-id` above and checking the `/docs/api/copilotkit` runtime initialization, production environment variables/provider configuration, `default` agent registration, and frontend/backend CopilotKit version compatibility. I searched the existing issues for `copilotkit` and `/docs/api/copilotkit` and did not find a duplicate. ### Screenshot

title: feat(cua-driver): support Helium profile attachment on Linux and macOS
body:
Fixes #3252

Helium was classified as an unknown browser, so authorized existing-profile attachment failed before endpoint discovery. This change recognizes Helium as a Chromium-family standalone browser on Linux and macOS and resolves its default profile directory.

## Behavior

- Linux: recognize the exact Helium executable basename and resolve `~/.config/net.imput.helium`.
- macOS: recognize `net.imput.helium`, classify the main process as a standalone consumer, and resolve `~/Library/Application Support/net.imput.helium`.
- Preserve existing-profile grants, exact PID/window binding, loopback ownership, and fresh endpoint reproof. Helium requires its own PID-owned `DevToolsActivePort`; its generic `/json/version` fallback remains disabled.
- Linux packed command lines retain normal NUL-delimited parsing whenever available. A recovered profile candidate must be corroborated by a live SingletonSocket held by the exact process tree; ordinary path/URL text and ambient working directories cannot prove a profile.
- Automatic setup without an existing endpoint remains an explicit refusal. Windows Helium recognition is outside this change and is documented as unsupported.

## Regression and E2E coverage

The existing reviewer-requested Linux parser, role, and kernel socket ownership regressions are retained. macOS adds product identity and default-profile coverage.

The standalone Rust harness accepts `CUA_E2E_BROWSER_PRODUCTS=helium`, discovers Linux/macOS installations, launches disposable profiles with spaces in their paths, and obtains the browser-written endpoint using port zero. It tests actual attachment, missing-endpoint refusal while the real listener remains alive, no-endpoint setup refusal, and isolated launch selected by the exact Helium PID. Existing application, focus, z-order, cursor, and leaked-input oracles remain enforced.

The Linux standalone CI lane includes Chrome and a pinned Helium 0.18.1.1 package verified against its SHA-256 digest. The macOS hosted browser lane opts into Helium alongside Chrome/Edge, installs a pinned architecture-specific 0.18.1.1 image with a verified SHA-256 digest, and attests the Helium code-signing identifier/team.

## Validation

Final candidate: `7e4d924bdcaef2e770eb02b378e239757aa447fc` (based on upstream `0f29c142d`).

Linux/Windows product and browser-harness certification uses `05285d04809da09dbb3ac73386817d814c9e604c`. The final diff adds only a pinned macOS Helium installation and opt-in hosted browser selection in `.github/workflows/e2e-rust-macos.yml` and `scripts/ci/macos/run-hosted-rust-e2e.sh`; Linux/Windows code and environments are unchanged. The affected macOS matrix is dispatched anew on the final candidate.

Local focused evidence:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Linux platform tests with Wayland variables unset: 587 unit tests and 8 integration tests pass; desktop-only rows remain ignored in this unit invocation.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked`: 771 unit tests and all invoked integration tests pass.
- Strict browser-product selection: pass.
- Live Helium in a disposable Xvfb/Openbox X11 desktop: authorized existing-profile attachment, missing-active-port refusal, unavailable-setup refusal, and exact-product isolated launch pass.
- Docs hygiene, internal links, production build, and Cua Driver generated-reference drift checks pass.
- Complete local standalone Helium suite at `05285d048`: **23 cells pass: 16 delivered, 7 expected refusals, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. The canonical report validator accepts all required video and trajectory evidence. Environment: disposable Xvfb/Openbox X11; CDP reports Chromium `152.0.7977.64`.
- [Linux unit CI](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723419678), [Windows unit CI](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723424688), and [macOS unit CI](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36724747367): pass. The macOS run includes the final isolated-launch test adjustment.

Cross-platform complete certification (pending; the local standalone result above does not replace the complete desktop matrices):

- [Linux complete desktop matrix](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723696716)
- [Windows complete desktop matrix](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723701276)
- [macOS supplemental hosted matrix](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36725009450)
- [Standalone browser matrix, including Linux Helium](https://github.com/saatvik333/cua/actions/runs/36723691551)

## Remaining gates and environment limits

- Native macOS Helium attachment has not been verified on this Linux host. Hosted macOS validation is supplemental; the canonical Lume environment is not available here.
- On this Niri/Wayland host, the upstream overlay test `unreported_arrival_releases_the_waiter_after_the_cap` fails; unsetting Wayland variables makes the entire platform suite pass. The overlay file is unchanged from upstream.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` on Linux hits the existing macOS-only `cursor_hook_registry` import failure; the driver builds successfully with `portal-input`.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets --locked` hits the unchanged upstream input-test `approx_constant` error for `6.28` at `input/mod.rs:4627`. That file has no diff against upstream.
- Linux unit CI initially hit `ETXTBSY` in the unchanged upstream perception-worker fixture after 770 core tests passed; its one failed-job retry passes. The complete core suite also passes locally.
- Upstream CI, including `CI: Release metadata`, is `action_required`: a maintainer must approve the fork workflows. This account has no canonical-repository write access and cannot approve them.
- Upstream currently reports `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Maintainer re-review and the required `CI: Release metadata` pass remain necessary before readiness or merge.

Contributor authorship is preserved in the existing pull request and commit history. This PR is not its own salvage source.

title: [RFC]: Complete embedded host parity for managed integrations
body:
## Primary area

SDK or bindings

## Summary

Cua should complete the released `EmbeddedCuaDriverHost` service adapter so downstream hosts can delegate private-daemon lifecycle without losing host policy, diagnostics, or control over binary distribution. The public contract should add typed daemon-presentation and bounded-diagnostics surfaces, retain exact protocol compatibility, and offer host-only SDK artifacts that do not bundle a second executable.

## Motivation and current state

`EmbeddedCuaDriverHost` already owns endpoint safety, readiness validation, MCP configuration, parent-liveness shutdown, and cleanup. Downstream hosts still keep parallel process managers because the adapter cannot express serve-side overlay policy, cannot return captured startup diagnostics, and is distributed only with a bundled driver executable. Passing a separately installed executable avoids using the duplicate but couples independently updated SDK and driver versions without a stated distribution contract.

This is the remaining compatibility-adapter slice of RFC #2549. It does not replace the direct SDK runtime or change which application owns desktop permissions.

## Goals

- Add an additive typed `no_overlay` embedded-host option with unchanged defaults.
- Let a host retrieve bounded structured diagnostics after startup failure without exposing unbounded child output.
- Publish host-only Python and Node artifacts without a bundled driver executable.
- Retain exact generated-contract validation and state how host-only artifacts select a matching executable.
- Keep existing packages, constructors, defaults, and bundled-binary behavior compatible.
- Give downstream integrations enough parity to remove duplicate process lifecycle code.

## Non-goals

- Relax exact contract validation across incompatible Cua Driver releases.
- Search `PATH` for or silently download an executable.
- Change direct-runtime behavior or make the daemon the default SDK topology.
- Transfer macOS TCC ownership to `CuaDriver.app`; the signed embedding host remains responsible.
- Add arbitrary serve-argument or environment passthrough.
- Define downstream product permission policy.

## Proposal

Extend `EmbeddedDriverHostOptions` with an additive, default-false `no_overlay` field and have the host place `--no-overlay` on the owned `serve` process.

Add a bounded diagnostics record retrievable from the host after a failed start. It records lifecycle phase, exit status when known, truncation state, and a size-bounded stderr tail. Existing stderr inheritance remains the default; capture can be enabled explicitly and may tee to inherited stderr.

Publish host-only Python and Node distributions containing generated bindings and the native SDK library but no `cua-driver` executable. Existing `cua-driver` and `@trycua/cua-driver` packages remain unchanged. Host-only callers continue supplying an absolute executable path.

Retain exact contract, tools-schema, capability, and MCP protocol validation. Host-only distributions and external executables must use matching Cua Driver component releases. Mismatch remains a structured startup refusal with expected and observed versions. The SDK does not trust `PATH`, auto-update the executable, or weaken metadata validation.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep downstream lifecycle managers. This preserves parity but duplicates Cua endpoint, readiness, shutdown, and protocol rules.
- Add arbitrary serve arguments. This is flexible but bypasses the typed, reviewed embedding contract.
- Bundle the executable in every SDK package. This guarantees matching versions but duplicates an existing managed installation for hosts that already distribute Cua Driver.
- Accept protocol ranges. This reduces release coupling but can silently combine schemas and authorization behavior that were not certified together.
- Launch through `CuaDriver.app`. That changes permission ownership and conflicts with host-owned embedded topology.

## Compatibility and migration

All option fields and diagnostics methods are additive and default to current behavior. Existing packages continue bundling their exact executable. Host-only packages are additional distribution names and require an explicitly supplied matching binary. Downstream hosts migrate one lifecycle implementation at a time and can roll back to their current process manager without changing Cua Driver.

The proposed implementation order is overlay policy, diagnostics, exact external-binary diagnostics, then host-only packaging. Packaging does not ship before matching-version failure behavior is deterministic.

## Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

The SDK keeps its fixed child-environment allowlist and typed serve options. It does not expose arbitrary argument injection. Exact metadata validation, endpoint identity checks, and parent-liveness ownership remain mandatory.

Captured stderr stays local, is opt-in, and is strictly size-bounded. Public telemetry must not include captured stderr, local paths, manifests, screenshots, accessibility content, typed text, or environment values.

The embedding application remains responsible for macOS TCC identity, Windows interactive-session placement, and Linux display ownership. A gateway or unrelated helper must not claim the host identity.

## Validation and acceptance evidence

- Rust tests prove default and `no_overlay` serve arguments.
- Generated Rust, Python, and TypeScript bindings remain synchronized and additive.
- Startup tests prove bounded capture, truncation, inheritance behavior, and no telemetry inclusion.
- Contract mismatch tests report expected and observed versions before returning a connection.
- Package tests prove host-only artifacts contain the native SDK library, omit the executable, and can launch an explicitly supplied matching fixture.
- macOS, Windows, and Linux compile and contract lanes pass.
- Existing embedded-host lifecycle and package smoke tests remain green.

## Unresolved questions

- Should diagnostics use a host `last_diagnostics()` accessor or enrich lifecycle errors directly?
- What byte limit and redaction rules should the stderr tail use?
- Should host-only packages have new names or be published as explicit package variants where the ecosystem supports them?
- Must external executable preflight inspect semantic version before spawn, or is the authenticated daemon metadata handshake sufficient?

## RFC document pull request

To be opened as a linked draft.

## Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: feat(cua-driver): capture embedded startup diagnostics
body:
## Summary

- Add opt-in stderr capture to `EmbeddedCuaDriverHost` and expose bounded startup diagnostics through generated Python and TypeScript bindings.
- Retain the final 65,536 stderr bytes, report truncation only when bytes were discarded, and preserve the child exit code when known.
- Give each startup its own diagnostics capture so stale stderr tasks cannot modify a later generation.
- Make one managed child own the process, liveness pipe, stderr pump, and shutdown timeout.
- Preserve existing stderr inheritance and constructor defaults, export `EmbeddedDriverDiagnostics` from Python, and document the sensitivity of raw stderr.

Refs #3278.

## Design

Each startup creates one shared diagnostics capture. The host retains it as the latest result, while the stderr pump writes directly to that same capture. A successful startup clears it by reference identity. An old pump only retains its detached capture and therefore cannot reach diagnostics from a newer startup.

The managed child provides one cleanup path for graceful shutdown, forced termination, stderr draining, and exit-status recording. This removes generation fields and comparisons from diagnostics, the fixed 250 ms startup shutdown path, and the former standalone append, clear, finish, and terminate helpers.

## Diff scope

The committed generated bindings account for 203 added lines. Focused tests account for 139 added lines. The handwritten Rust runtime change is 293 additions and 57 removals, or 236 net lines. The ownership refactor removed 43 net handwritten lines from the earlier candidate. No unrelated product files are included.

## Validation

Local validation:

- `cargo check -p cua-driver-sdk --lib --locked`: passed
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-sdk --lib --locked`: 53 passed
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --test embedded_host_sdk_mcp_test --locked`: 6 passed
- `node libs/cua-driver/scripts/generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check`: passed
- Python generated-options and public diagnostics import tests: 2 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

All required pull request checks pass across macOS, Linux, and Windows. The first Nix YAML policy run failed while downloading from `cache.nixos.org`; its rerun passed without a code change.

No desktop E2E certification is claimed because this change affects SDK-owned startup lifecycle rather than desktop interaction behavior.

## Current-main refresh, 3 Nov

- Merged current `main` without rewriting earlier commits. Conflicts were limited to test fixtures and generated TypeScript: main's new `isolated_driver_host` helper and the private-worker fixture now pass `capture_stderr: false`, and the UniFFI bindings were regenerated (`--check` passes).
- Replaced the stderr pump's `loop`/`let else` with `while let` to satisfy clippy on the pinned toolchain. Behavior is unchanged: stop on read error or EOF.
- The scoped repository checks pass on macOS: `cargo fmt` and `cargo test --locked` for `cua-driver` and `cua-driver-sdk`, which includes the six embedded-host tests and 110 SDK tests. The UniFFI generated bindings check passes. The Python UniFFI loader tests and the TypeScript typecheck and tests pass with `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1`. Without that variable, the two "own the runtime in process" tests take the CuaDriver.app daemon path from #5090 on a Mac that has the app installed. The PR does not touch that path.
- Linux and Windows CI cover the remaining platforms.

Size limit: the managed-child ownership refactor and bounded capture form one lifecycle change; splitting them would leave the stderr pump without a single owner.

CUA-3225

title: [RFC]: Host-rate Linux GPU acceleration in Lume
body:
### Primary area

Cross-component architecture

### Summary

Lume should support an explicit Linux `graphics: host` mode on certified arm64 macOS 27 hosts. The VM keeps stock VZ graphics for the existing input/VNC bridge, adds an SDK-27 custom virtio-gpu Venus device for guest rendering and KMS, presents that scanout in the existing native Lume window through Metal at the current host display rate, and never silently falls back when the pinned host runtime or matched guest image is unavailable.

### Motivation and current state

Lume's Linux VMs currently expose stock Virtualization.framework graphics at approximately 60 Hz and do not provide the Venus/MoltenVK path required for a fully accelerated Omarchy desktop on Apple Silicon. Local feasibility work on an M4 Max proved Venus to virglrenderer to MoltenVK to Metal rendering, custom KMS scanout, host-derived EDID and refresh, native keyboard/pointer input, clean fence/blob teardown, validated external images, and the required shader techniques for custom border color and transform feedback. The production decision is cross-component because it changes persisted VM configuration, bundled native process boundaries, guest package/image compatibility, lifecycle cleanup, and release certification.

### Goals

- Add persisted `graphics: virtual|host`, with `virtual` preserving every existing VM and image.
- Make `host` explicit, Linux-only, arm64-only, macOS-27-only, and native-display-only with clear errors and no fallback.
- Isolate SDK-27 custom-device code in a versioned native plugin so the main Lume target keeps macOS 14/Xcode 16 compatibility.
- Ship pinned virglrenderer, MoltenVK, SPIRV-Cross, and render-server artifacts inside the signed Lume app with no Homebrew/runtime downloads/developer paths.
- Implement standards-correct null descriptors, external images, custom border colors, transform feedback, depth transport, and Darwin fence retirement before advertising those capabilities.
- Reuse the existing Lume window/input/clipboard/drop lifecycle, render custom scanout at host rate, and scale or letterbox across resize/screen changes without black frames.
- Build a matched aarch64 Omarchy image with deterministic custom GPU selection, no GLES override, no software fallback, stock visual effects, automated installation/acceptance, and direct desktop startup.
- Certify a new local `omarchy-gpu` VM while preserving the existing `omarchy` VM as rollback.

### Non-goals

- Changing existing `graphics: virtual` behavior or removing stock VZ graphics.
- Supporting non-arm64 hosts, macOS before 27, arbitrary Linux images, or public image rollout in the first certified matrix.
- Exposing virgl/Venus/blob/fence tuning through CLI, HTTP, MCP, or VM config.
- Using VNC as the final visible display, disabling Omarchy effects, hardcoding refresh, suppressing warnings, or permanently forcing a GLES version.
- Connecting public pull requests to a privileged self-hosted runner.

### Proposal

Persist `VMGraphicsMode.virtual|host` in `VMConfig`, VM details, create/set HTTP and CLI surfaces, and OCI image metadata. `host` validates before VM construction and never falls back. Keep `VM.run` as lifecycle owner and `LinuxVirtualizationService` as the owner of one opaque host-GPU session. A separately built SDK-27 plugin attaches the custom device to the existing `VZVirtualMachineConfiguration`, owns virglrenderer/MoltenVK/shared mappings/fences/child cleanup, and exposes a small versioned C ABI with retained Metal surface leases. The main native presenter keeps the existing AppKit window and transparent `VZVirtualMachineView` input layer, adds a Metal surface underneath, polls zero-copy frame metadata, retains textures through command completion, follows the current NSScreen refresh, and scales or letterboxes the last valid frame. A matched aarch64 Omarchy profile installs pinned Mesa Venus/Zink packages, stable DRM names, UWSM device selection, and functional GPU tests. Host and guest revisions are locked and released as one compatibility set.

### Alternatives considered

- Directly compile SDK-27 APIs into the main Swift target: rejected because current Lume CI/release builds with Xcode 16.3 and supports macOS 14.
- Let a plugin own a second VZVirtualMachine and duplicate VM configuration: rejected because storage/network/audio/share/VNC lifecycle would drift from `LinuxVirtualizationService`.
- Use stock VZ scanout or VNC for final presentation: rejected because neither provides the required host-rate native display.
- Suppress Zink warnings or bake in `MESA_GLES_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.2`: rejected because that advertises behavior without implementing custom border color or transform feedback.
- Reuse the experimental guest disk: rejected because the deployed image must be reproducible from pinned aarch64 packages and installer inputs.

### Compatibility and migration

Existing VM configs and OCI images decode a missing `graphics` key as `virtual`; existing commands and virtual-mode code paths remain unchanged. Host mode is additive and fails before VM start when architecture, OS, display mode, artifacts, ABI, feature manifest, or guest compatibility is wrong. The first rollout is a local M4 Max/macOS 27 plus matched Omarchy aarch64 image. The Cua PR remains draft and no Lume release is cut until a GitHub-hosted Xcode-27 job can build/sign/test the native runtime. The existing `omarchy` VM remains stopped and untouched during local deployment. Downstream dependency patches are removed in the same change that updates to an upstream release containing them.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

The runtime loads only same-bundle, same-signature native artifacts and validates canonical paths, hashes, ABI, and required feature bits. It performs no runtime downloads and accepts no arbitrary library/helper path from user input. The render server runs unprivileged as a child of Lume; every mapping, callback, thread, surface lease, and child process has bounded ownership and idempotent cleanup. Logs may report typed failure stage and feature name but never guest memory, clipboard contents, credentials, local source paths, or private screenshots. Local Omarchy autologin stores no password and is confined to the Lume-specific image profile.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

- Main Xcode-16 Lume tests prove legacy config/API/OCI behavior and VM cleanup remain unchanged.
- SDK-27 native tests under Metal API Validation prove null reads/writes, custom border float/int/compare/filtering, complete transform feedback semantics, external image export, depth memory transport, EDID timing, fences, maps, and shutdown.
- Package verification proves arm64 artifacts, install names/rpaths, same-team signatures, licenses, hashes, and absence of Homebrew, proof paths, tracing, and GLES override strings.
- Fresh aarch64 ISO and image tests prove package ownership, autologin configuration, and stock Omarchy behavior; a separate Lume runtime test proves Zink/Venus/MoltenVK/M4 rendering, natural GLES 3.2, no software fallback/warnings, Spice clipboard, input/cursor, Chromium, repeated contexts, and clean teardown.
- Exact build manifests bind QEMU, Lume install, certification, and deployment to one ISO path and SHA.
- At 2560x1600, host presentation must sustain at least 99% of active refresh after warmup, avoid recurring 33 ms intervals, update when moving from 165 Hz to 75 Hz, and remain visible through resize/fullscreen transitions.
- The exact candidate SHA must pass Lume CI, release metadata, hosted SDK-27 packaging/notarization when available, and final local VM certification before merge/release.

### Unresolved questions

No design question remains for the local-first matrix. Reviewers should focus on the public `graphics` contract, SDK-isolated plugin boundary, exact ownership/cleanup semantics, dependency patch acceptability, and the merge gate requiring a GitHub-hosted Xcode-27 environment.

### RFC document pull request

_No response_

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: CUA driver fails to manipulate desktop, causing agent to fall back to shell scripting
body:
## Bug description

The CUA driver failed to manipulate the desktop during an agent run. The agent then fell back to shell scripting instead of completing the interaction through the desktop driver.

## Expected behavior

The CUA driver should successfully perform the requested desktop interaction, or surface a clear actionable driver error without requiring an unintended shell-script fallback.

Desktop manipulation failed and the agent fell back to shell scripting.

Slack thread: https://trycua.slack.com/archives/C0BBU2W6U8M/p1787242809666629?thread_ts=1787239160.068069&cid=C0BBU2W6U8M

title: feat(cua-driver): support relative mouse movement for pointer-locked apps
body:
## Feature request

Add a relative mouse movement primitive to cua-driver for applications that capture or lock the pointer, including first-person games such as Minecraft.

The current absolute-coordinate pointer controls are not sufficient for continuous camera rotation. The driver should inject genuine relative mouse deltas rather than compute a new absolute cursor position.

## Proposed API

A primitive along these lines:

```json
{
  "type": "mouse_move_relative",
  "dx": 240,
  "dy": -30,
  "duration_ms": 300
}
```

It should compose with explicit stateful input operations such as `key_down` / `key_up` and `mouse_down` / `mouse_up`, so an agent can hold `W` while sending multiple camera-movement deltas.

## Existing library models

- PyAutoGUI: `moveRel(dx, dy)`, `dragRel(...)`, `mouseDown()`, and `mouseUp()`
- pynput: `Controller.move(dx, dy)` plus explicit button press/release
- Native APIs: Windows `SendInput` relative deltas; Linux evdev/uinput `REL_X` and `REL_Y`
- Browser Pointer Lock: unbounded relative `movementX` / `movementY`

## Acceptance criteria

- Move the pointer by relative `dx` / `dy`, independent of absolute screen coordinates.
- Inject events that work while an application captures or locks the cursor.
- Support held keys/buttons concurrently with repeated relative movement.
- Define consistent behavior across supported platforms and return a clear unsupported error where unavailable.
- Add a reproducible integration test or demonstration that pans/rotates the camera in Minecraft.

title: [RFC]: Coordinate-free macOS menu-extra discovery and invocation
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Add an explicit, capability-gated macOS menu-extra accessibility scope so callers can discover and invoke `AXExtrasMenuBar` items without pixel coordinates. Keep the existing exact-window `invoke_menu(pid, window_id, path)` contract unchanged. The first adapter would expose bounded read-only discovery plus a separately authorized exact-path action for a named running application; Windows and Linux would advertise the capability as unavailable until they have an equivalent status-item adapter.

### Motivation and current state

`invoke_menu` currently resolves an application's `AXMenuBar` and intentionally requires an exact `(pid, window_id)` target because application menu availability is tied to the active/key window. macOS menu extras are a different system surface: accessory processes expose them through `AXExtrasMenuBar`, they may own no layer-0 application window, and invoking one must not activate an unrelated application window.

As a result, agents currently fall back to a desktop screenshot and fixed coordinates for system menu extras such as accessibility, network, audio, or user-session controls. That route is layout-dependent and can type or click into an unintended surface after a display, locale, menu-bar, or popover change. Cua's existing exact-path menu resolver already has the desirable safety properties—live re-resolution, exact case-sensitive labels, ambiguity refusal, disabled-state checks, and no pixel fallback—but it cannot target this accessibility root.

The adjacent application-composite AX proposal in #2807 and implementation PR #2894 deliberately concern unattributed `AXWindow` roots and exclude menu bars and actions. Menu extras therefore need a separate identity and authorization contract rather than an application-root fallback.

### Goals

- Discover one named running application's `AXExtrasMenuBar` hierarchy through a bounded, read-only tool.
- Invoke a menu extra or one of its descendants through an exact, immediate-child accessibility path with no coordinate fallback.
- Preserve the current application-menu contract and exact `(pid, window_id)` validation unchanged.
- Preserve the user's current frontmost application/window; menu-extra invocation must not activate or raise a target application window.
- Refuse missing, duplicate, disabled, stale, permission-denied, and unsupported targets with typed machine-readable outcomes.
- Give bounded permission mode a distinct capability for system menu-extra mutation.

### Non-goals

- A desktop-wide accessibility tree or generic application-root action API.
- Fast User Switching-specific selectors, account logic, password entry, or customer data handling.
- Pixel-coordinate fallback, OCR label matching, fuzzy matching, or first-match selection.
- Replacing the current exact-window `invoke_menu` behavior.
- Claiming immediate Windows notification-area or Linux panel/status-notifier parity.
- Persisting accessibility objects or menu content across calls.

### Proposal

Add two additive tools with a typed application target that accepts either an exact positive PID or an exact bundle identifier. Bundle-identifier resolution must produce exactly one running process; zero or multiple matches fail closed.

1. `get_menu_extra_state(target, max_depth?, max_elements?)` is read-only. It reads only the target application's `AXExtrasMenuBar`, returns a bounded semantic hierarchy with role, title/description, enabled state, and supported actions, and never writes the action cache. It returns no screenshot and retains no native accessibility objects after the call.
2. `invoke_menu_extra(target, path)` is mutating. `path` contains 1–16 exact, trimmed, case-sensitive immediate-child labels. At every hop it re-reads `AXExtrasMenuBar` from the live application root, treats an untitled `AXMenu` container as transparent, requires exactly one matching child, checks enabled state, and selects only a declared native accessibility action. It never falls back to coordinates and never activates or raises an application window.

The tools get separate capability advertisement and authorization entries rather than overloading `invoke_menu`. This preserves wire compatibility and lets bounded manifests allow read-only discovery without authorizing system-menu mutation. macOS implements the first adapter. Windows and Linux register the same tool contract but return a typed `unsupported_platform` result until equivalent system status-item semantics and evidence exist.

If opening a menu extra replaces its accessibility subtree, each action hop re-resolves from the application root, matching the existing `invoke_menu` approach. The action result remains explicitly unverifiable until the caller observes a semantic postcondition from fresh state.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Add `menu_bar: application | extras` and make `window_id` optional on `invoke_menu`.** Smaller implementation, but it weakens an established cross-platform input schema and makes authorization unable to distinguish application commands from system-menu mutation cleanly.
2. **Expose all accessory applications through `list_apps`.** Useful process discovery, but it does not supply semantic menu state or a safe action identity and broadens a separate public contract.
3. **Walk the application root or reuse application-composite AX scope.** Rejected because it mixes windows, application menus, extras, and unrelated controls under ambiguous PID scope.
4. **Use screenshots plus coordinates.** Works as a prototype but is not safe under layout, localization, display, or popover changes and cannot prove semantic identity.
5. **Model a cross-platform `status_item` abstraction immediately.** Potentially desirable, but Windows notification-area and Linux status-notifier semantics need separate research; requiring them now would either overgeneralize from macOS or delay an explicitly capability-gated adapter.

### Compatibility and migration

The change is additive. Existing tool names, schemas, action tokens, and `invoke_menu` behavior do not change. Older drivers simply do not advertise the two new tools. Rollback removes their capability advertisement; no persisted state or data migration exists.

The implementation should land behind normal capability discovery and documentation. A later accepted RFC can map Windows notification-area or Linux status-notifier behavior to the same contract or supersede the macOS-specific names with a proven common abstraction.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Both tools require the driver's existing macOS Accessibility grant. The mutating tool is a distinct bounded-mode capability because menu extras can trigger system-level effects such as session, network, audio, or accessibility changes. Authorization is checked before any accessibility traversal or action.

Discovery is restricted to one exact running application target, bounded by native query, depth, and serialized-element limits, and never crosses into another PID without an explicit typed relationship accepted by this RFC. No application content, menu labels, account names, element descriptions, bundle identifiers, accessibility objects, paths, screenshots, or action arguments are emitted in telemetry. Allowed telemetry is limited to capability availability, counts, latency, platform, and typed failure/refusal codes.

Calls retain no native objects after completion. Missing permission, dead/ambiguous target, duplicate path labels, changed hierarchy, unsupported native action, and messaging timeout all fail closed. The action preserves frontmost app/window state and must not deliver keyboard input.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

- Contract/schema tests prove both tools are additive, strictly typed, bounded, separately authorized, and advertised or unavailable per platform.
- macOS unit tests prove exact label matching, transparent untitled-menu handling, duplicate/missing/disabled refusal, action selection, query bounds, and native-reference cleanup.
- A repository-owned macOS fixture publishes an `AXExtrasMenuBar` item whose action changes independently observable fixture state.
- Canonical macOS Lume E2E proves bounded discovery and exact-path invocation while preserving the prior frontmost PID/window, z-order, cursor, and keyboard-input sentinel.
- Negative E2E rows cover stale/dead targets, duplicate labels, permission denial, locked/no-GUI session, and a hierarchy replaced between hops.
- Windows and Linux protocol tests return the declared typed unsupported result and do not silently substitute window menus or pixel input.
- A supporting live macOS smoke may exercise a built-in menu extra, but its screenshot, labels, or user-specific content are not required acceptance evidence.

### Unresolved questions

- Should the accepted names remain macOS-specific (`menu_extra`) or use a future-facing `status_item` term before Windows/Linux adapters exist?
- Is exact bundle identifier an acceptable stable target alongside PID, or should the first increment require PID and add accessory-process discovery separately?
- May a popover opened by one process expose descendants owned by a different process, and if so, should v1 refuse that boundary or bind an explicit owner transition?
- Should discovery return only semantic labels/actions, or opaque short-lived tokens that the action tool must consume?
- Which native query limit is required so one unresponsive accessory process cannot exhaust the driver call budget?

### RFC document pull request

https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3302

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: refactor(cua-driver): share cursor movement spec with playground
body:
## Summary

Promotes the playground's movement parameters into a shared, repository-owned movement spec, so the gallery and the production platform overlays consume one source of truth for cursor motion.

- **Shared spec** (`assets/motion.default.json`, schema `cua.cursor-motion/1`): embedded at compile time via `include_str!` and parsed once. `MotionConfig::default()`, the Windows/Linux spring derivation, the macOS reference settle constants, and the thrice-duplicated `CLICK_OFFSET` all now derive from this single file. The per-platform `spring_settle` sections are explicit (macOS `k=400, c=17, overshoot=0.8`; Windows/Linux derived `spring*400 / spring*20`, overshoot 0.5) — behavior-preserving, not unified.
- **Strict checked-in contract**: parsing validates the exact schema, typed `fixed`/`derived` platform modes, finite production bounds, and speed-floor cross-fields. An invalid embedded asset fails fast with no shadow defaults.
- **Parity gates**: a double-entry test pins the embedded spec against an independent Rust literal (`reference_defaults()`), and a thrown-away harness proved trajectories bit-identical to the pre-change build on both platform tick paths before being discarded.
- **Gallery manifest v2**: the exporter records the exact movement contract it rendered (effective values, spring mode, overridden fields), so an overridden recording can never be mistaken for production defaults.
- **Movement lab UI** (dev-only): six sliders bounded to production ranges rebuild the preview through the production renderer; state echoes from the server so UI and file never drift.
- **Dev server**: one whitelisted loopback POST endpoint writes the override to a fixed ignored path; payload size-capped, origin-checked, and sanitized (unknown fields/non-finite/out-of-range rejected).
- **Promotion workflow**: `cursor-gallery.sh promote-motion` merges a tuned override into the shared spec with a value-only canonical diff, re-validating hand-edited files through the same sanitizer and the exporter's cross-field rule (floors ≤ effective peak). Parity tests gate the promotion.

## Decision record

An advisory architecture review (Claude Code Fable, read-only plan mode) recommended the JSON-spec + `include_str!` + parse-once-static approach, per-platform spring-settle sections instead of unification, a single whitelisted dev endpoint, and promotion with contract tests. The implemented design follows it. Full advisory archived in the linked card.

## Validation

Local, at candidate SHA `a5690ed2f`:

- `cargo test -p cursor-overlay --lib` — 49 passed (incl. spec parity and rejection tests)
- `cargo test -p cursor-overlay --example export_gallery_frames --features theme-authoring` — 11 passed
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s libs/cua-driver/tools/cursor-gallery -p "test_*.py"` — 16 passed
- `cargo fmt --check`, `bash -n`, `node --check` clean; `platform-macos/windows/linux` `cargo check` clean
- Loopback e2e: POST override → rebuild → manifest echoes `overridden_fields` + effective values
- Trajectory parity: bit-identical pre/post refactor on both tick paths (throwaway harness, not committed)

Platform evidence at exact candidate SHA `a5690ed2f` (workflow_dispatch with requested SHA; the resolve job pinned `CUA_E2E_SOURCE_SHA` and every downstream job fetched this commit):

- **Linux X11 — exact-candidate recert** ([run 32519842962](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32519842962)): success — all 6 jobs (install-local.sh smoke, shared Electron + Tauri, capture and desktop scope, GTK3 + GTK4 native harnesses, matrix summary); this run's head SHA is `a5690ed2f` directly, pinning the interactive X11 gate to the exact candidate.
- **Linux X11 — companion recert** ([run 32517328710](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32517328710)): success — all 6 jobs, confirming the same gate.
- **Standalone browsers at `a5690ed2f`** ([run 32519839892](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32519839892) + companion [run 32517331028](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32517331028)): both runs conclusive. Linux X11/chrome succeeded in both. Windows chrome+edge failed with the pre-existing attestation defect — decisive: the test `standalone_browser_prepare_isolated` panicked at `standalone_browser_behavior_test.rs:2229` (`left: String("refused")` / `right: "ok"`), structured `code: browser_route_unavailable`, message `no vendor-signed protected Chromium executable is available for isolated launch`, identical on Chrome and Edge — a runner-environment attestation gap, not a movement-spec regression; tracked separately on the Windows triage card.

Pre-hardening platform diagnostics at SHA `5ebe5f012`:

- **Windows** ([run 32509120689](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32509120689)): success — native WPF + WinUI3 + WebView2, capture + desktop scope, shared Electron + Tauri, installer + update smoke, matrix summary
- **Linux X11** ([run 32509122525](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32509122525)): success
- **Standalone browsers** ([run 32512934295](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/32512934295)): Linux X11/chrome success. Windows chrome+edge failed with `browser_route_unavailable: no vendor-signed protected Chromium executable is available for isolated launch` — a runner-environment issue pre-existing on `main` (the last 7 main runs of this workflow failed identically), not caused by this change.

## Interactive playground evidence

Real Movement Lab interaction was verified at exact candidate `a5690ed2f` through an exactly bound, driver-owned Chrome window using Cua Driver's snapshot-before/action/fresh-snapshot-after loop:

- A real pointer drag changed `peak_speed` from `900` to `2000`. macOS correctly refused the background gesture; the explicit foreground fallback delivered it with input route `global_input`.
- The page moved from `ready` to `building`, then returned to `ready` after rebuilding through the production Rust renderer.
- Gallery manifest v2 echoed effective `peak_speed: 2000` with `overridden_fields: ["peak_speed"]`; all other effective fields remained at production defaults.
- All 3,000 generated movement frames retained transparent canvas margin: zero frames touched an image edge and the minimum margin was 56 pixels.
- The rendered Reset control rebuilt the preview to production defaults (`peak_speed: 900`, no overridden fields) and removed the fixed override file.
- Browser binding quality was `exact`, endpoint access was `driver_owned`, mutation was allowed, and the slider gesture's successful input trust class was native foreground `global_input` after the platform-declared background refusal.

## Pending requested platform evidence

This pull request remains draft and the following user-requested exact-candidate rows remain gates for the active validation goal:

- Exact-candidate Azure Windows replay after independently observing a live interactive non-Session-0 desktop through FreeRDP/RDP. GitHub-hosted Windows evidence is supplemental and does not replace this named environment-parity replay.
- Exact-candidate macOS Lume canonical harness (`libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh --standalone-browser`) in the logged-in, TCC-authorized guest.

The Windows standalone-browser leg at `a5690ed2f` remains a separate pre-existing `browser_route_unavailable` runner-environment attestation gap; Linux X11/chrome succeeded and the Windows defect is tracked independently rather than attributed to this movement-spec change.

## Release

`no-release` label kept: repository playground + internal refactor with no user-visible behavior change (proven bit-identical trajectories). Will revisit if release-metadata review disagrees.

title: test(cua-driver): normalize Windows browser trust posture
body:
## What this fixes

The canonical standalone-browser workflow failed the isolated-launch cells on GitHub-hosted Windows even though Chrome and Edge were vendor-signed. The runner token is elevated and can write beneath `Program Files`, while production Cua Driver intentionally refuses pid-free isolated launch from any browser tree writable by its current token.

## Root cause

This was an environment-parity defect in the E2E harness, not a product trust defect. Weakening the production check would have broadened the isolated-launch trust boundary.

## Change

Before the Windows browser matrix runs, the disposable hosted runner now adds non-inherited deny rules for the exact write/modify rights that Cua Driver probes on the installed Chrome/Edge executable and every ancestor through the relevant `Program Files` root.

This preserves the real product contract during certification:

- the candidate browser remains readable and executable;
- the current test token cannot modify the browser installation chain;
- vendor Authenticode verification remains mandatory and unchanged;
- no production Cua Driver code changes;
- Linux behavior is unchanged.

The ACL changes are confined to the ephemeral GitHub-hosted runner, which is discarded after the job.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check`: PASS
- `cargo test --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-windows --lib`: 42 passed
- workflow YAML parse: PASS
- `git diff --check`: PASS

## Release impact

Harness-only correction. The `no-release` label is intentional; production behavior is unchanged.
