title: cua-sandbox: Image.linux() VM path on Apple Silicon boots an x86_64 guest under TCG instead of the arm64 containerDisk
body:
## Summary

`Sandbox.ephemeral(Image.linux(), local=True)` (default `kind="vm"`) on an Apple Silicon host always launches **`qemu-system-x86_64` with TCG software emulation**, even though an arm64 Ubuntu 24.04 containerDisk now exists and HVF is available. This is the VM-path sibling of #3254 (which covered the Docker/`kind="container"` path, fixed in #3257).

## Where (main @ e4b0a03e7)

- `cua_sandbox/sandbox.py:219` `_auto_runtime` → Linux VM returns `QEMURuntime(mode="bare-metal")` (lines 258/279) without passing `arch`.
- `cua_sandbox/runtime/qemu.py:229` `QEMURuntime.__init__` defaults `arch="x86_64"`; `qemu.py:1008` runs `qemu-system-{self.arch}`.
- `qemu.py:413` explicitly detects `host_arm and guest_x86` and falls back to `-accel tcg` — i.e. the slow path is the designed outcome on M-series Macs today.

## Expected

On `platform.machine() in ("arm64", "aarch64")` hosts, a Linux VM should default to `arch="aarch64"`, use `-accel hvf` (`-cpu host`, `virt` machine, AAVMF/EDK2 firmware), and pull the arm64 variant of the containerDisk.

## Artifact availability

trycua/cloud#7099 publishes `public.ecr.aws/k5j5w0x5/cua-ubuntu-24.04:latest` as a multi-arch containerDisk index (amd64 + arm64, `/disk/disk.img`), built from the same rootfs as the `docker-latest` image validated in #3257/#3254. So the image side is done; this is SDK runtime-selection work.

## Notes

- `Image.linux()` has defaulted to `kind="vm"` since at least `sandbox-v0.4.1`, so this is a pre-existing gap, not a regression from #3257.
- Until fixed, Apple Silicon users should use `Image.linux(kind="container")` (native arm64 Docker, verified) for local Linux.
- Worth deciding whether `Image.linux()` should keep defaulting to `vm` at all when Docker is present and QEMU is not — the current "needs QEMU" error is the first thing a new Mac user hits.

Refs #3254, #3257, trycua/cloud#7099.

title: cua-driver 0.21.0 Windows MCP: permanent "this session has ended" state after an mcp shim instance exits — start_session cannot recover
body:
## Environment
- cua-driver v0.21.0 (stable), Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Shared daemon (`\.\pipe\cua-driver`) + stdio MCP server (`cua-driver mcp`) spawned by the client (ZCode)
- Multiple cua-driver.exe processes running concurrently (1 serve + several per-client mcp shims) — shared-daemon multi-client setup

## Timeline
1. MCP calls work normally (`list_windows`, `launch_app`, `get_window_state` all succeed)
2. ~20 min idle period with no cua-driver calls from this client
3. One of the mcp shim instances exits (process count drops 3 → 2; PID observed earlier is gone)
4. From that point on, **every** tool call from this client fails with:
   ```
   refused (session_ended): this session has ended; call start_session explicitly to reuse its label
   ```
   This includes read-only calls like `health_report` / `list_sessions`.

## What makes it unrecoverable
- `start_session(label)` returns success, but the very next call fails again with the same `session_ended` — the revived/new session never sticks for subsequent calls
- `end_session` (implicit) still responds normally → the stdio transport itself is alive; only the session layer is wedged
- No way to recover from inside the session; lasted >1h until manual intervention

## Workaround that worked
Killing the wedged mcp shim process (the one parented to the MCP client) made the client auto-respawn a fresh shim, which came up in a clean state — all tools work again.

## Suggestion
Either auto-detach/revive the session when the owning instance dies (the refusal message implies `start_session` should work as a recovery path, but it doesn't), or make the client transport detect the dead shim and respawn proactively instead of serving a zombie session label forever.

Possibly related: #1777 (daemon session-identity model), #2160 (start_session transport closed).

title: Windows bounded mode: platform adapter attests no identity for desktop processes, making every application grant unmatchable
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Windows, `list_apps` reports running desktop-kind processes with `bundle_id`, `launch_path` and `executable` all null, so `resource_matches_application()` has nothing to compare a capability manifest entry against and can never match. Bounded mode consequently refuses every action on every application — it behaves as deny-everything rather than deny-by-default, leaving `--permission-mode standard` (no resource scoping at all) as the only usable configuration on Windows.

### Reproduction

1. Install cua-driver 0.21.0 on Windows 10/11.

2. Create a v3 capability manifest granting a single app. Note `bundle_id` and `executable` are mutually exclusive — declaring both fails validation at startup with `each application resource must declare exactly one of bundle_id or executable`:

```yaml
version: 3
expires_after: 8h
idle_timeout: 30m

allow:
  tools:
    - start_session
    - end_session
    - launch_app
    - list_windows
    - list_apps
    - get_window_state
    - get_accessibility_tree
    - click
    - type_text
    - drag

resources:
  apps:
    - bundle_id: 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe'
      launch: true
      windows: all
  desktop:
    display: true
```

3. Start a bounded daemon:

```
cua-driver serve --permission-mode bounded --capability-manifest <path> --approve-capability-manifest
```

4. With Chrome running, call `list_apps`. It succeeds — but the Chrome record has null identity fields (see Evidence).

5. Call `list_windows`. It succeeds and returns Chrome's windows with pid and window_id.

6. Call `get_window_state` or `capture` against that pid and window_id.

Reproduces 100% of the time, for every application, with every manifest spelling tried: `bundle_id` alone, `executable` alone, both together, forward slashes and backslashes.

### Expected behavior

An application declared in the capability manifest should match the corresponding running process, so that `get_window_state`, `capture` and input calls against that application's windows succeed, while applications absent from the manifest are refused with `bounded_resource_outside_manifest`.

That is, bounded mode should be deny-by-default with a working allowlist.

### Actual behavior

Every application is refused, including the one declared in the manifest:

```
protected resource is outside the capability manifest: desktop pid 15092 window 66850 is outside the capability manifest
```

The cause is visible in `list_apps`: running desktop-kind processes carry no identity fields at all. `resource_matches_application()` matches on `bundle_id`, `fingerprint.executable`, `executable` or `launch_path`:

```rust
let bundle_id = resource.get("bundle_id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str);
let executable = resource
    .pointer("/fingerprint/executable")
    .or_else(|| resource.get("executable"))
    .or_else(|| resource.get("launch_path"))
    .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str);
```

For Windows desktop-kind resources the adapter supplies none of these, so both resolve to `None`, `is_some_and(...)` is false for every grant, and the match fails unconditionally.

Note `bundle_id` is a macOS concept. On Windows the adapter does populate it for *registered/installed* apps (AppX package family names such as `Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe`, and Start-menu paths such as `...\Application\chrome_proxy.exe`), but not for the running desktop processes that windows actually belong to. A manifest can therefore only address entries that cannot be acted upon.

I have not verified whether the root cause is the adapter omitting the fields, or redaction applied to unmatched resources before comparison — see Evidence for why I suspect the latter.

### Environment

- Cua component and version: cua-driver 0.21.0 (Windows), installed at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Cua\cua-driver\bin\cua-driver.EXE`
- Operating system and architecture: Windows 10 (10.0.19045), x64
- Host application: Hermes Agent (`computer_use` toolset), Python 3.11.3
- Application under test: Google Chrome, `C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`
- Window system: Windows desktop (not remote/RDP, not a container)

### Evidence

**Raw `list_apps` records under bounded mode** (verbatim, all three processes running at the time):

```json
{"active": false, "bundle_id": null, "kind": "desktop", "last_used": null, "launch_path": null, "name": "chrome.exe", "pid": 15092, "running": true, "windows": []}
{"active": false, "bundle_id": null, "kind": "desktop", "last_used": null, "launch_path": null, "name": "explorer.exe", "pid": 10176, "running": true, "windows": []}
{"active": false, "bundle_id": null, "kind": "desktop", "last_used": null, "launch_path": null, "name": "notepad.exe", "pid": 31764, "running": true, "windows": []}
```

**Refusal**, targeting Chrome four ways — by `app='Chrome'`, by `app='chrome.exe'`, by exact `(pid, window_id)`, and by desktop surface — all identical:

```
protected resource is outside the capability manifest: desktop pid 15092 window 66840 is outside the capability manifest
```

**Evidence the nulling is mode-dependent.** The same Chrome instance, pid 15092, inspected earlier under `--permission-mode standard`, reported:

- `bundle_id`: `C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`
- `launch_path`: `C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`

Under bounded mode the same pid reports both as `null`, and `windows` as `[]`. This suggests identity fields are redacted for resources that have not matched the manifest — which is circular, since the identity needed to author a grant is withheld until a grant already matches. If that redaction is intentional, there appears to be no supported way for an operator to discover the correct identifier to put in a manifest in the first place.

**Confirmation that capture works once the manifest is removed entirely.** With `--permission-mode standard` and no `--capability-manifest`, `capture` against pid 15092 / window_id 66840 succeeded immediately and returned a 1456x796 screenshot. So the failure is specific to manifest matching, not to capture itself.

Window titles in the logs above have been redacted; no credentials or private data are included.

### Workaround and additional context

**Workaround:** `--permission-mode standard`, with no `--capability-manifest` supplied. This removes resource scoping entirely, so any compensating controls have to live in the calling application rather than in cua-driver.

Note that supplying a manifest appears to force manifest enforcement irrespective of the mode flag — running `standard` while a `capability_manifest` path is still configured produced identical `bounded_resource_outside_manifest` refusals. The manifest path had to be removed entirely, not just the mode changed. This may be host-side behaviour rather than cua-driver's, but it made the mode setting look like it was being ignored.

**Suspected area:** the Windows platform adapter that populates `list_apps` resource records, and/or whatever applies redaction to unmatched resources, rather than `resource_matches_application()` itself — the matching logic looks correct given non-null inputs.

**Possible fix direction:** populate `fingerprint.executable` (or `launch_path`) for Windows desktop-kind resources from the process image path, and perform the manifest comparison against unredacted values before any redaction is applied to output.

**Related secondary observations**, noted here rather than as separate issues since they share this code path — happy to split any of them out if you'd prefer:

1. `canonical_manifest_path()` resolves manifest `executable` values via `std::fs::canonicalize()`, which on Windows returns a verbatim path (`\\?\C:\...`), while the adapter attests the plain form. Since `resource_matches_application()` compares with plain string equality, `executable` matching would still fail even after the attestation issue above is fixed. The fallback branch for non-existent paths canonicalises the nearest existing ancestor, so the prefix cannot be avoided by spelling either. `bundle_id` is not passed through this function, which is why it was the only field that could plausibly have worked.

2. `list_windows` returns full window titles for applications outside the manifest. Titles routinely contain email addresses, customer names and document names. A bounded session can currently read every window title on the machine while being unable to act on any of them. If bounded mode is meant to restrict observation as well as action, enumeration may warrant filtering or title redaction for unmatched resources.

3. The "exactly one of `bundle_id` or `executable`" rule surfaces only as a daemon startup failure. On Windows the natural instinct is to supply both, since `bundle_id` has no obvious Windows meaning — documenting it near the manifest examples would save time.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: Feature request: portable format for cua-bench task/eval results (EvalPort)
Windows 11: foreground_unavailable on Chrome click (HWND mismatch) + background coordinate offset
body:
## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 11 (2026 build)
- **cua-driver version**: 0.20.0 → 0.21.0 (bug persists after upgrade)
- **Browser**: Google Chrome (latest, pid 6828, HWND 0xb0818)
- **Target app for click**: `chrome.exe` (via `computer_use` app target)

## Bug 1 — `foreground_unavailable` on Chrome (persistent)

Every `click` (and `key` for combo) delivered with `delivery_mode: foreground` to `chrome.exe` fails deterministically:

```
foreground_unavailable: Windows did not confirm exact target HWND 0xb0818
for key delivery within 500 ms (actual foreground HWND 0x74087e). Route the
request through the UIAccess-manifested cua-driver-uia worker; no input was sent.
```

- The target HWND `0xb0818` is the correct, visible, non-minimized Chrome main window (confirmed via Win32 `GetWindowRect` → L=101 T=0 R=1435 B=816, `IsIconic=False`).
- The "actual foreground" `0x74087e` is another process (a window that is *not* the intended target) — it looks like the foreground activation is switching to a different window between the pre-check and the delivery, so the sentinel check never passes.
- `key` combos (`ctrl+l`, `ctrl+2`, ctrl+1) work fine in foreground; only `click` fails this way. `background` delivery succeeds (synthetic_events) but lands at the wrong coordinates (see Bug 2).

## Bug 2 — Coordinate offset in background click (Chrome)

Clicking by native coordinates produces a large, inconsistent offset. Example:

- Requested click at native `(179, 519)` (center of a real element, bounds `[149,489,61,60]`).
- Driver dispatched the event at `(337, 588)` — ~158px right / 69px down.
- Another request `(950, 957)` was dispatched at `(1210, 1084)` — ~260px right / 127px down.

The scale factor reported in the capture summary ("estimated scale ~1.53x", "~1.93x") varies between captures, so I cannot pre-compensate. The result is that background clicks can hit a *different* element than intended.

## Impact

- Cannot reliably click any element in Chrome on Windows 11 via `computer_use`.
- `foreground` is refused (Bug 1), `background` lands on the wrong element (Bug 2).
- This blocks all click-driven automation in Chrome (form fill, button clicks, upload flows).

## Minimal reproduction (manual)

1. On Windows 11, have an installed Chrome with any page open.
2. `capture` the window (Som), read an element's native bounds, compute center.
3. Issue `click` with `delivery_mode: foreground` → observe `foreground_unavailable`.
4. Issue `click` with `delivery_mode: background` → observe dispatched coordinates don't match the requested center.

## Related

Possibly related to #2201 (background Chrome click miss/blur sentinel) and #2681/#2682 (foreground click after Chrome action). Happy to attach logs / full element tree if helpful.

title: Cua Driver: native open-panel sheet is observable but cannot be AX-targeted in window scope
body:
## Environment

- macOS
- Cua Driver `0.21.1-nightly.20260822.32551728570`
- Window-scoped session with unrestricted driver permissions

## Reproduction

1. Open a native macOS app window through Cua Driver.
2. Trigger an `NSOpenPanel` sheet from that window.
3. Snapshot the app main window. The AX tree includes an `AXSheet` and actionable descendants such as sidebar cells and the search field.
4. Act on a fresh descendant `element_token`.
5. Separately list windows and snapshot the CG window titled `Open`.

## Expected

A fresh AX token returned beneath the main-window snapshot can be acted on, or the sheet has an exact independently targetable window identity.

## Actual

- The main-window snapshot returns the sheet descendants, but actions refuse with `element_outside_target_window`, saying the element cannot be proven to belong to the main window.
- The separately listed `Open` window snapshots as `ax_unresolved`; its screenshot is available, but both AX and background pixel routes are refused.
- Re-snapshotting does not resolve either state.
- Window-local foreground pixel delivery can report `unverifiable` without changing the sheet.
- A desktop-scope click at the same visible control succeeds.

This leaves a native sheet visible and semantically described but unusable through the normal window ladder. No sensitive file names, paths, or screenshots are included.

feat(cua-driver): add target-bound credential delivery
body:
## Intent

Implement the provider-neutral, target-bound credential delivery architecture proposed in RFC #2942. This stays draft until the RFC is accepted and the exact candidate passes the required security and Fleet evidence.

## Implemented

- make recording projections explicit for every currently advertised mutable tool and fail closed for unknown mutations while recording
- redact text, value, URL, path, clipboard, file, and download inputs before retention; visible typing labels no longer echo caller content
- classify only live semantic-v2 DOM-backed `input[type=password]` nodes as secure password fields
- omit password values, masks, and lengths from semantic output; AX-protected fields are redacted even when DOM evidence is unavailable, without becoming eligible for delivery
- add an internal provider-neutral broker with target-first discovery, opaque fresh handles, exact runtime/session/process/endpoint/tab/frame/document/origin/ref binding, expiry, single use, release limits, revocation, and cancellation
- add a distinct internal R3 `secret_release` authorization adapter: Standard denies, Bounded requires an exact version-three credential binding and origin scope, and optional manifests narrow Unrestricted
- bind authorization permits to the handle, binding, provider, exact browser target, permission mode, manifest, and policy hashes, then revalidate inside the release critical section
- reject already-ended sessions and suspended runtimes, wire terminal runtime suspension to broker revocation, and require provider-side cancellation checks before prompts, unlocks, IPC, reads, or fills
- remove consumed/revoked/expired handles from active retention, retain only bounded content-free tombstones, enforce a per-session active-handle quota, and avoid partial discovery minting
- keep bootstrap credentials in a separate internal store abstraction and keep secret-bearing values non-debuggable, non-serializable, and zeroizing
- keep the foundation out of public tools, contracts, MCP, CLI, ABI, UniFFI, and generated SDKs until the secure route is certified

## Security properties covered by tests

- discovery exposes only safe descriptors and never invokes a provider
- target, field, cross-runtime, and cross-broker handle replay are refused
- release reservations are atomic and provider failure consumes the handle
- session, binding, provider, and runtime revocation cancel in-flight releases and reject late plans
- cancellation tombstones prevent a provider effect even when cancellation arrives before release
- drop and post-return revocation cancel exactly once; every release-plan variant has a revocation-gated accessor
- capacity failure mints no partial batch, per-session quotas prevent cross-session starvation, and expiry/revocation releases active capacity
- provider errors collapse to fixed enums and secret/bootstrap payloads have fixed bounds
- password fixtures prove positive eligibility, negative near-misses, and redaction-only AX protection

## Validation so far

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked` (612 unit tests, 2 contract parity tests, 3 lifecycle tests, and doc tests)
- focused broker suite: 21 passed
- focused `secret_release` authorization/manifest suite: 2 passed
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets --locked` completes with the repository's existing warning set
- independent adversarial architecture review completed; confirmed findings were addressed in the current head
- changed-file scan found no credentials, bootstrap values, private service metadata, or prohibited competitor references; only synthetic test locators and canaries are present

## Remaining gates

- fresh verified-target minting inside `BrowserEngine` and target-first broker discovery
- exact-node guarded CDP delivery with boolean-only event evidence and no plaintext fallback
- Windows/Linux bootstrap stores and dedicated automation-vault provider
- atomic public contract, ABI, UniFFI, Python, TypeScript, CLI, and MCP exposure
- source-built exact-candidate Linux and Windows Cua Cloud Fleet certification, including synthetic-secret retention scans and deterministic claim/pool cleanup

Refs #2942
RFC: #2943

title: feat(cua-driver): add target-scoped post-action rediscovery
body:
## why

[#2238](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2238) describes a stale-target failure: an action starts against window a, opens a sheet, dialog, popover, or Open/Save panel b, and leaves the caller bound to a. later snapshots and actions then target the blocked parent instead of the new interaction surface.

cua-driver already noticed some new macos windows, but its global detector could not prove that a desktop change belonged to the action. it also kept the result in diagnostic prose, so callers received neither a stable window address nor a machine-readable rebind instruction.

this pr resolves the structured-rediscovery part of the issue. after an action opens a target-owned surface, the result identifies the observed candidates and recommends `rebind`. when exactly one candidate is owner-verified, the result includes its `(pid, window_id)` so the caller can take a fresh window-scoped snapshot without activating or raising it.

## design

### retained from cua-driver

this keeps cua-driver's native action routes, focus-suppression leases, shared `ActionExecutionRecord`, closed `ActionResult`, and harness-owned escalation policy. it also retains the useful contract work from [#2746](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2746): typed `window_change` metadata, an explicit `rebind` escalation, and generated rust, python, typescript, and manifest bindings.

it removes the unsafe parts of the old path: the desktop-global `WindowChangeDetector`, seven per-tool diagnostic suffix mutations, the dead observation-skip hook, topology transport through legacy json, and window changes as evidence that an actuator succeeded.

### adapted from pi-computer-use

this adapts the target-root observation model from `injaneity/pi-computer-use` commit `022a280a377065c95736cc15f684bf1fad46479e`:

- snapshot the addressed process's accessibility roots before dispatch;
- run the native actuator;
- use a cheap target-window signature only to end a 400 ms wait early;
- run the authoritative accessibility diff once, with bounded catch-up when the signal beats the tree; and
- rebind directly when the AX diff yields one owner-verified logical root, and fail closed when several roots appear.

the persistent ax-observer ring is intentionally not copied because the source commit established that sheet creation emits no reliable notification; it adds lifecycle state without improving correctness here. cua-driver instead merges `AXSheets` with `AXChildren`, keeps its focus-suppression lease across dispatch and observation, and resolves owners only after the authoritative ax diff. unresolved appeared roots retry WindowServer ownership independently; an incomplete owner set can return known candidates but never an exact target.

### combined result

```text
macos action decorator
  → target-process ax snapshot
  → native actuator
  → target-process ax diff
  → windowserver ownership proof
  → shared candidate resolver
  → typed action record
  → closed action result
```

observation and action accounting remain separate. a surface change can add `window_change` and `escalation`, but it cannot promote `effect` to `confirmed`; confirmation still requires value readback. ambiguous candidates are returned without an invented exact target and can be correlated with one fresh `list_windows` call.

## issue coverage

this pr covers the structured rebind rung from [#2238](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2238):

- return stable candidate pids, window ids, titles, app names, and foreground-change state;
- recommend `rebind`, with an exact target only when ownership and modal/focused state make it unambiguous;
- preserve the human's foreground app, z-order, cursor position, and input isolation; and
- add the canonical TextEdit Open-panel case, then re-address the returned panel window.

it does not implement the issue's later privacy-sensitive desktop-frame fallback or inert-resnapshot backstop. those remain separate because this structured path recovers without widening capture scope. this pr therefore uses `Refs`, not an issue-closing keyword.

## diff shape

the runtime production diff is `+899/-829` (net `+70`). the new 411-line observer replaces the deleted 530-line global detector, while affected macos tool files remove 203 lines and add 79. most apparent growth is required generated contract output: `+1103/-157` across the manifest and python/typescript bindings.

## logical-root correction

host investigation found that AppKit can expose two Open-panel WindowServer records: an AX-addressable same-process TextEdit proxy and an AX-empty XPC duplicate. `pi-computer-use` keeps the target-scoped AX identity rather than requiring the foreign service pid. this branch now does the same: it preserves the appeared AX root's exact WindowServer identity, removes internal modal/focus eligibility state, and rebinds whenever exactly one owner-verified logical root appears. ambiguity still omits the exact target.

on the host probe, the returned TextEdit proxy exposed 62 Open-panel AX elements; the XPC duplicate exposed none. a direct exact-head action returned `escalation.target: rebind`, the proxy `(pid, window_id)`, and a successful fresh scoped snapshot without changing the foreground app.

## compatibility and validation

macos emits the new optional topology. windows and linux emit none rather than substituting a global heuristic. generated sdk consumers gain optional `window_change` plus the `rebind` and `surface_changed` enum values.

local validation passed:

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract --lib` — 33 passed
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` — 587 passed at rebased head `f5ea38210932db1389c199bc768891a21b9782e0`
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` — 338 passed, 2 ignored at the same sha
- pre-rebase direct host TextEdit Open-panel probe at `a2d513b93ac6122ad4dd8639e3e1ec7c88bca5cf` — one typed rebind to an AX-addressable logical root with 62 elements and unchanged foreground
- pre-rebase complete local macos contributor matrix on an integration of `a2d513b93ac6122ad4dd8639e3e1ec7c88bca5cf` with [#2907](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2907) — 140 of 158 cells passed; `macos-textedit-open-panel-background-rebind` passed all five declared oracles. the 18 unrelated failures were host input-isolation, cursor, desktop-coordinate, and video-finalization failures, so this is diagnostic evidence rather than canonical acceptance
- contract and uniffi generation checks
- typescript build and python binding compile check
- rustfmt, shell syntax, and diff checks

before this pull request is ready, the final candidate still needs the canonical macos Lume matrix. the local host can run the complete matrix when the foreground-sentinel fix in [#2907](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2907) is included, but its active desktop is not an acceptance environment: cursor movement, global-coordinate delivery, and concurrent recordings caused unrelated failures. maintainers must also confirm whether this additive public contract requires a separate rfc.

Salvaged from [#2746](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2746).

Refs [#2238](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2238).


## stacked scheduling follow-up

The stacked draft [#3391](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3391) replaces duplicate native action admission with one scheduler and canonical lease plan, ensuring this pull request's before/action/after decorator remains inside the same desktop action lease. It does not add another observation owner or change the public tool contract.







## canonical macos lume evidence — 2026-09-04

- tested source: `b131ca4f8e22650a8ed992df228f659b93eb9640` (the current PR head, not a merge commit).
- command: `libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh`, full unfiltered matrix; no retry or single-cell selector.
- run id: `20260904T181935Z-11114`.
- environment: disposable public `macos-tahoe-cua:26.5.2` worker, macOS 26.5.2 build 25F84, SIP disabled, stable local certificate, app-owned grants seeded with the repository helper, and a logged-in guest Terminal session.
- results: **158/158 passed**, including 150 delivered actions and 8 expected refusals; 0 failed and 0 skipped.
- `macos-textedit-open-panel-background-rebind`: passed AX state, focus, z-order, cursor, and no-leaked-input checks.
- `failures.json`: `failure_count=0`, `preflight_failed=false`, `report_failed=false`, no failed lanes or video failures.
- daemon verified restored to standard mode; worker stopped and retained.
- evidence retrieved to the maintainer host: `~/workspaces/cua-pr-3373-b131ca4f/artifacts/cua-driver/vm/lume_192.168.64.2/20260904T184538Z/` (local evidence, not a public download link).
- standalone installed Chrome/Edge matrix was **not** run.

This certifies only the SHA above. The requested rebase and review fixes remain outstanding; this evidence must not be presented as certification of a later candidate.

title: cua-driver 0.22.0 (macOS): PiP preview overlay appears without --experimental-pip flag and cannot be closed
body:
## Bug report

**Platform:** macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 26.5)
**Version:** cua-driver 0.22.0 (CuaDriver.app + CLI from ~/.local/bin)
**Severity:** medium (UX — an unclosable always-on-top window blocks the user's screen)

### What happened
After updating to 0.22.0 and restarting the host app, a small **always-on-top Picture-in-Picture window showing a live mirror of the main display** appeared in the top-right corner of the screen. It:
- cannot be moved, resized, or closed (no close button, no dock icon)
- sits above all other windows and blocks interaction with content behind it
- reappears every time the CuaDriver.app daemon relaunches

### Expected behavior
PiP preview should only appear when explicitly requested via `--experimental-pip`.

### Actual behavior
The PiP window appears when the daemon is started as `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve` — **with no `--experimental-pip` flag passed**. Process args confirmed via `ps -o command=`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install cua-driver 0.22.0 (CuaDriver.app).
2. Launch CuaDriver.app (or let it auto-start).
3. Observe the PiP mirror window in the top-right corner of the main display.

### Workaround
Force-quit the app-bundle daemon (`killall cua-driver`). The MCP-invoked driver (`~/.local/bin/cua-driver mcp`, launched with `--no-overlay`) does NOT show the PiP and works fine for automation — so this only affects the app-daemon launch path. A LaunchAgent guard killing the app daemon periodically is being used as a persistent workaround.

### Suspected cause
In 0.22.0, the app-bundle `serve` path appears to enable the experimental PiP by default (or reads a default-on config), while the documented flag says it should be opt-in. Possibly related: two driver instances coexisted after an update (one stale pre-update instance also kept an orphaned agent-cursor overlay alive until manually killed).

### Request
1. Make PiP strictly opt-in on all launch paths (app bundle included), or add a persisted `config set pip false` key.
2. Give the PiP window at least a close button or make it ignore mouse events entirely so it never blocks the underlying UI.
3. Ensure stale overlays/cursor windows from previous versions are cleaned up on update.

title: Windows: diagnostic helpers should never allocate visible console windows
body:
## Problem

The Windows platform backend launches bounded diagnostic helpers (`powershell.exe`, `netstat.exe`, and `cmd.exe`) without an explicit no-console creation policy. A GUI/host process that does not already own a console can therefore create a short-lived visible console window. Repeated browser ownership checks amplify the visual interruption.

This report is limited to source-level process creation behavior; it does not claim that every observed console flash originates in Cua Driver.

## Affected boundaries

- browser executable signature inspection
- browser command-line inspection
- loopback listener inspection
- Windows version health check
- integrity-level diagnostic

## Expected contract

- Windows-only diagnostic helpers use `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` at one typed construction boundary.
- stdin/stdout/stderr, exit status, cancellation, and parent-child cleanup semantics remain unchanged.
- Browser and input delivery are not detached.
- A deterministic Windows test spawns a bounded helper and proves that its PID owns zero visible top-level windows.
- Repeated browser actions do not create visible console/conhost windows.

## Minimal reproduction

From a Windows GUI process without an inherited console, run a short-lived `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive` child with ordinary `std::process::Command` or `tokio::process::Command`. Compare visible top-level windows owned by the child PID with and without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (`0x08000000`).

title: [Bug]: Windows in-process TypeScript SDK captures DPI-virtualized desktop under scaled display
body:
## Primary area

SDK or bindings

## Summary

On Windows with display scaling above 100%, the TypeScript in-process SDK inherits a DPI-unaware Node host and reports/captures only the DPI-virtualized upper-left portion of the primary desktop. The same `@trycua/cua-driver` version through the standalone daemon reports and captures the complete physical desktop.

## Reproduction

Environment: one Windows interactive user session, primary display `2560x1600` at 150% scaling.

1. Install `@trycua/cua-driver@0.22.2` in a Node.js application.
2. In the Node process, create the in-process runtime and request the screen size and desktop screenshot:

   ```ts
   const driver = CuaDriver.create(undefined);
   await driver.startSession(StartSessionInput.new({ session: "dpi-repro" }));
   const size = await driver.getScreenSize(
     GetScreenSizeInput.new({ session: "dpi-repro" }),
   );
   const desktop = await driver.getDesktopState(
     GetDesktopStateInput.new({
       session: "dpi-repro",
       screenshotOutFile: "embedded.png",
     }),
   );
   ```

3. Start the standalone `cua-driver.exe` from the same installed version in the same interactive Windows session.
4. Connect with `CuaDriver.connect(socketPath)` and run the same `getScreenSize` and `getDesktopState` calls, writing `daemon.png`.
5. Compare each structured result and the PNG IHDR dimensions.

This reproduced consistently in the Stage 0 comparison. It was then reproduced again with a
`cua_driver_sdk.dll` built from current `main` at
`dbf0d3a450d9c4fc3a0a768faf0ce9b3283f908e`. No OpenClaw or image-resizing layer was involved.

## Expected behavior

The in-process and daemon modes should expose the same physical-pixel desktop contract on the same machine: `2560x1600`, scale factor `1.5`, a complete `2560x1600` PNG, and coordinates matching that image.

## Actual behavior

| Mode | `getScreenSize` | PNG | Visible content |
|---|---|---|---|
| TypeScript in-process `CuaDriver.create(undefined)`, npm 0.22.2 | `1707x1067`, scale factor `1.0` | `1707x1067` | upper-left region of the physical desktop |
| TypeScript in-process, source-built current `main` | `1707x1067`, scale factor `1.0` | `1707x1067` | upper-left region of the physical desktop |
| standalone daemon + `CuaDriver.connect(socketPath)` | `2560x1600`, scale factor `1.5` | `2560x1600` | complete primary desktop |

`2560 / 1.5 ~= 1707` and `1600 / 1.5 ~= 1067`. `GetProcessDpiAwareness` reports `PROCESS_DPI_UNAWARE` for the Node host. The standalone executable has the PMv2 manifest fixed by #1883.

The current Windows implementation reads `GetSystemMetrics` and `GetDpiForSystem` under the assumption that the calling context is already PMv2-aware. That assumption holds for the manifested standalone executable but not for a native library loaded into an arbitrary Node host.

## Environment

- Cua component and version: `@trycua/cua-driver@0.22.2`
- Operating system and architecture: Windows 11 Home, build 26200, x64
- Host: Node.js TypeScript application in an interactive desktop session
- Display: primary display `2560x1600`, Windows scaling 150%
- Upstream source checked: `trycua/cua` main at `dbf0d3a450d9c4fc3a0a768faf0ce9b3283f908e`

## Evidence

Redacted structured evidence:

```text
embedded:
  process_dpi_awareness = PROCESS_DPI_UNAWARE (0)
  get_screen_size       = 1707x1067 @ 1.0
  png_ihdr              = 1707x1067
  capture               = physical desktop upper-left region

standalone daemon:
  get_screen_size       = 2560x1600 @ 1.5
  png_ihdr              = 2560x1600
  capture               = complete primary desktop
  click/type/recapture  = passed in the same physical coordinate space

current main, source-built embedded DLL:
  get_screen_size       = 1707x1067 @ 1.0
  png_ihdr              = 1707x1067
```

No screenshots are attached because the images contain private desktop content. PNG dimensions and structured tool outputs were read directly from the generated artifacts.

## Workaround and additional context

Running `cua-driver.exe` as an independent daemon and connecting with `CuaDriver.connect(socketPath)` avoids the issue because the executable owns its PMv2 DPI context.

Related work: #1879 / #1883 fixed the standalone executable's manifest resource and removed capture double-scaling. This report concerns the separate in-process SDK path, where the Rust runtime is loaded into a host process whose DPI awareness is not controlled by the executable manifest.

I have not prescribed a process-wide fix because changing a host application's process DPI awareness after initialization can fail or alter host behavior. A thread-scoped or operation-scoped solution may be more appropriate, but the owning layer should be decided from the SDK/runtime call path and the canonical Windows GUI tests.

## Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve physical pixels in embedded Windows SDK
body:
## Summary

- Initialize Cua-owned Windows threads with Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness without changing the importing application's process-wide DPI setting or caller thread.
- Fail closed at the actual execution boundary, including blocking workers created after successful runtime startup, rather than only recording initialization errors.
- Propagate DPI failures to ABI callers as `RuntimeUnavailable`, preserve resource teardown, and add late-thread regression coverage.

Refs #3449.

## Problem

The standalone executable declares PMv2 awareness in its manifest, but an embedded SDK runs inside an arbitrary host process. The original reproduction used a DPI-unaware Node host on a `2560x1600` display at 150% scaling: the embedded driver reported and captured `1707x1067 @ 1.0`, containing the upper-left physical region, while the standalone daemon captured the complete desktop.

The previous revision initialized Tokio threads but only consumed initialization failures during startup. A later blocking-pool thread could fail DPI setup and still enter native work. Startup probes cannot establish the invariant for future threads.

## Implementation

- Keep a sticky failure state owned by the ABI executor. Every Tokio worker/blocking-thread initializer contributes to that state; later submissions reject a failed executor.
- Gate native blocking closures on their actual execution thread, before calling the work body. Windows backend task submissions use the shared guarded entry points instead of adding checks independently to individual tools.
- Check async operations on every poll and again before accepting their result. This covers worker migration and prevents an optional screenshot fallback from swallowing an initialization error and reporting ABI success.
- Dedicated Windows threads use the same initializer and inherit the submitting thread's owner when one exists. An overlay started during synchronous host-side registry creation instead gets an independent owner; its failure stops the overlay body but does not poison the ABI executor. Single-flight cleanup guards are captured before dispatch so refusal still releases them.
- Guard native window/display capture entry points as well, including calls from recording hooks outside the platform task wrapper.
- Keep shutdown and resource finalization available after failure. Do not retry capture/input automatically, alter coordinate conversion, or change the public tool/ABI schema.

An executor failure is terminal for GUI admission within that executor. This is not transactional cancellation of work already in progress and does not undo input that was issued before a failure.

## Tests

Passed locally on Windows using the GNU Rust toolchain with cached dependencies and `--offline`:

- SDK suite: **46 unit tests and 2 integration tests passed**.
- Windows platform library test target compiled successfully.
- Host-started independent owner and submitting-thread owner inheritance tests: **2 passed**.
- Existing UIA and UWP bounded-worker recovery tests: **2 passed**.
- Existing AppsFolder single-flight timeout/recovery test: **1 passed**.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `git diff --check`.

The added regressions hold the existing blocking worker to force pool growth after startup, inject a late DPI failure, and assert that:

- the guarded native work body is not executed;
- direct display/window capture entry points refuse the failed thread;
- ABI completion returns `RuntimeUnavailable` with no success payload, even if the inner operation swallows the worker error;
- later admission fails, while cleanup completion remains available;
- failure on a dedicated child thread prevents both its work body and the next async continuation;
- healthy late blocking workers and dedicated child threads use PMv2.

The existing real embedded-ABI regression also passes: it checks `get_screen_size`, desktop PNG dimensions and scale, and verifies that the deliberately DPI-unaware host thread remains unchanged. These local results do not substitute for the official input/GUI matrix.


## Maintainer validation — September 6, 2026

The [Windows MSVC workflow](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/33479754606) passed, including all **47 SDK unit tests**, unaware-host regular/trusted ABI capture, late-thread failure handling, and trusted-call cancellation. Its PR merge checkout `3aceac01c8dba4f9dd5d1d08dda6101a78caf7b4` has an identical Git tree to candidate `1a4165a4b47546a86a0bb450cd7581be821128ce`.

The complete [Linux canonical run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34056686843) passed at that exact candidate SHA: **129 desktop cases** (87 delivered, 42 expected capability refusals), zero failures/skips, plus the installer smoke. Environment records and all per-case videos were retained.

The [Windows canonical run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34056685900) passed installer, shared (84 cases), and capture (9 cases) lanes, but its native lane has **one failure among 43 cases**: `windows-webview2-left-click-px-background` left the fixture counter at 2 instead of 3. The recorded target is centered on Increment. Desktop UIA enumeration exceeded 2 seconds, returned, and entered a 30-second recovery cooldown before the click. The click fell back to PostMessage; the shared UIA gate also covers point hit-testing. This evidence does not yet attribute the failure to DPI coordinates. A single [native-only repeat](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34057872092) at the unchanged SHA reproduced the same failure: 42/43 cases passed, with a ready environment and the same PostMessage fallback during UIA cooldown. This is a reproducible native gate failure, not a passing retry; both runs are retained. Causation by the DPI changes is not established.

Server 2025 at 100%/150% scaling remains outstanding. Existing requested reviews are not cleared. No merge or release is requested.

title: fix(cua-driver): use native Wayland cursor overlays
body:
## Summary

- Render agent cursors through native Wayland layer-shell surfaces.
- Suppress the legacy X11 overlay on native Wayland displays.
- Keep cursor rendering isolated per output and per session.
- Preserve transparent repaint and damage handling while the overlay moves or fades.

## Why

The previous overlay path could create an XWayland surface on a native Wayland compositor. That surface could duplicate the cursor, interfere with compositor focus, and fail to repaint transparent regions correctly. This change makes the Wayland overlay compositor-native and keeps the X11 path for X11 displays.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`
- Hyprland compositor smoke: one `cua-agent-cursor` layer-shell surface per output, no `Cua.AgentCursorOverlay` XWayland client, and no focus or workspace switch during cursor activity.

## Scope

This PR changes the native Wayland/Hyprland overlay path. X11, macOS, and Windows overlay paths remain unchanged. It is intentionally not a claim of generic compositor support beyond the tested native Wayland path.

## Dependency

Based on #3052.

This branch includes the current #3052 changes because GitHub cannot use a fork-owned PR head as the base of another upstream PR. Review this as an incremental overlay change on top of #3052; the dependency commits are not reimplemented here.

title: cua-driver macOS: list_windows z_index diverges from live stacking — documented "take the maximum z_index" picks an occluded window
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `list_windows` documents:

> z_index (integer or null; **higher values are closer to the front**; …) To select a frontmost candidate, **take the maximum integer z_index**

Measured against a live daemon, that contract does not hold for the default (all-windows) enumeration: `z_index` can disagree with WindowServer's live stacking order, so the documented "take the maximum integer z_index" recipe selects a window that is actually stacked **behind** a sibling of the same app (an occluded dialog, in our capture). The driver's own `get_accessibility_tree` returns the correct live order at the same moment, i.e. the driver disagrees with itself.

This is the implementation side of #2199 (which defined the semantics): the macOS derivation doesn't deliver the defined semantics when the enumeration includes off-screen windows.

## Environment

- cua-driver-rs **0.22.2** stable (macOS daemon `cua-driver serve`, standard permission mode)
- macOS Darwin 25.6.0, arm64
- Derivation unchanged at current HEAD `70ae3b4` (see "Root cause" below), so this is not already fixed in nightly.

## Measured evidence (read-only tools only)

Real desktop, one app (WeCom / 企业微信, pid 1385) with two overlapping on-screen layer-0 windows. Its main window had been raised above its "software update" dialog. Four sources sampled back-to-back:

| window | window_id | `list_windows` z_index | CG `OnScreenOnly` position (front→back) | AX (System Events) | driver `get_accessibility_tree` order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main window | 95 | 56 | 18 — **in front** | `AXMain=true`, first | before 30195 |
| update dialog | 30195 | **101 ← max-z winner** | 19 — behind | `AXMain=false` | after 95 |

So `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)` (documented front-to-back), the AX tree, and the driver's own `get_accessibility_tree` all agree the main window is in front — only `list_windows.z_index` ranks the occluded dialog higher. A control pair (two Finder windows, z 136 vs 126) matched all four sources, so the direction convention itself is fine; the ordering source is what's off.

Additional characterization (3 samples, 3 s apart, 138 records each):

- Every `z_index` was byte-identical across samples while disagreeing with the live order the whole time — the value behaves like a sticky snapshot that does not follow re-raising.
- Numerically, `z_index + (position in a CGWindowList all-windows dump) ≈ const` across the board, confirming it is a reverse index into the *all-windows* enumeration, not into the on-screen stacking.
- `z_index: null` never occurred (0/138), so callers cannot exercise the documented null path on macOS at all.

## Root cause

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/windows.rs`:

- `all_windows_with_space_snapshot()` enumerates with `kCGWindowListExcludeDesktopElements` only — **no `kCGWindowListOptionOnScreenOnly`** — and that is what `list_windows` uses by default (`tools/list_windows.rs`, `on_screen_only=false`).
- `z_index` is then `z_index_from_front_to_back(total, idx)` — a reverse index into that array ("`// z_index: CGWindowList front-to-back → assign reverse index.`").

Apple only promises front-to-back ordering for the **on-screen** list. Once off-screen windows are included, the relative order of the on-screen subset is not the live z-order — measured above, it diverges after a same-app re-raise and stays diverged. So the reverse index inherits an ordering CoreGraphics never promised.

## Suggested fix

Derive `z_index` from the `kCGWindowListOptionOnScreenOnly` enumeration order (join by `window_id`), and report `z_index: null` for off-screen windows — they have no meaningful stacking position, and the tool contract already defines null as "stacking order is unavailable; callers must not infer one". That makes `list_windows` consistent with `get_accessibility_tree`, which is already live-correct, and makes the documented "take the maximum integer z_index" recipe actually pick the frontmost window.

A regression test idea matching #2199's test seam: feed the enumerator a fixture where the all-windows array order differs from the on-screen array order for the same on-screen ids, and assert `z_index` follows the on-screen order.

## Repro (read-only)

1. Open two overlapping windows of one app; raise the *older* one (click its title bar) so live stacking no longer matches creation order. Wait a few seconds.
2. `cua-driver call list_windows '{"pid": <pid>}'` → note which window has the max `z_index`.
3. `cua-driver call get_accessibility_tree '{}'` → note that app's window order (live-correct).
4. Independent ground truth, front-to-back:

```swift
import CoreGraphics
import Foundation
let list = CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo([.optionOnScreenOnly], kCGNullWindowID) as! [[String: Any]]
for (i, w) in list.enumerated() {
    print(i, w[kCGWindowNumber as String] as! Int, w[kCGWindowLayer as String] as! Int,
          w[kCGWindowOwnerName as String] as? String ?? "")
}
```

Steps 3 and 4 agree with each other and with what is visibly on top; step 2 ranks the re-raised window below its sibling.

title: perf(cua-driver): extend configurable pacing to mouse, WebKit settle, and type_text default
body:
Companion to #3489 (keyboard key gap): the remaining hardcoded input pacing constants on macOS move behind read-once `CUA_DRIVER_RS_*` env overrides. **Every default is unchanged — zero out-of-the-box behavior change.**

| Constant | Sites | Knob | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| mouseMoved-primer settle 12ms | 3 (left, right, scroll primer) | `CUA_DRIVER_RS_MOUSE_PRIMER_MS` | 12 |
| click down→up gap 28ms | 3 (warp path, pid path, right-click) | `CUA_DRIVER_RS_CLICK_GAP_MS` | 28 |

Evidence that tighter pacing holds up where deployments choose it (Swift driver this Rust tree mirrors, measured live against Safari): primer 4ms + click gap 8ms delivered focus-correct clicks with a typed marker read back through an independent AX referee, and inter-character delay 0 with a 2ms key gap typed 136/136 characters exactly.

title: perf(cua-driver): memoize the installed-app scan behind a root-mtime key
body:
## Problem

`list_all_apps` re-walks five app directories and re-reads every bundle's `Info.plist` on **every call** — hundreds of file reads for an answer that changes only when something is installed or removed. Measured against the 0.16 binary under adversarial load (6 CPU spinners, fresh connection per request): `list_apps` p50 **1.2–2.6 s**, dominated by this scan.

## Change

`scan_installed_apps` is memoized behind a two-part key:

- **Root mtimes** — adding or removing a `.app` bundle touches its parent directory, so an install/uninstall invalidates the cache instantly.
- **30s TTL** — per-bundle `last_used` timestamps (filesystem mtime heuristic) can change without any root directory noticing; the TTL bounds that drift.

An unreadable root keys as `None`, and two `None`s compare equal — a permanently missing root (e.g. no `~/Applications`) still caches instead of rescanning forever. Running apps are untouched: `list_running_apps` still runs live on every call, and running entries are still backfilled from the (now cached) installed scan.

The freshness contract (`installed_cache_is_fresh`) is a pure function with a unit test covering: matching key within TTL → serve; changed mtime, appearing/disappearing root, or expired TTL → rescan.

## Numbers

With the equivalent mtime-keyed cache in the Swift driver this Rust tree mirrors, the same adversarial bench answered `list_apps` in **~15–23 ms** (vs 1.2–2.6 s), with correctness checked against `NSWorkspace` ground truth (21/21 running apps, all bundle ids present).

`cargo test -p platform-macos` — 353 passed. `cargo fmt` applied.

title: [Feature]: Damage-driven settle — wake at the first changed frame instead of sleeping a fixed constant
body:
### Primary area
Cua Driver

### User problem
Action tools on macOS pace themselves with fixed sleeps: the 800ms WebKit DOM-focus settle after clicking a text input, and fixed post-launch waits. A fixed sleep costs its full constant on every action even when the app settled long ago. In our measurements the actual "first repaint after the action" lands at ~76ms p50 — so the 800ms path overpays by ~10x on the common case, and every agent action stacks that latency.

(#3490 makes these constants configurable, but a knob only trades safety margin for speed; it can't adapt per action.)

### Desired outcome
Post-action settles wake at the first *changed frame* and keep the old constant only as the timeout cap. ScreenCaptureKit makes this cheap: an SCStream only delivers a frame when display content actually changed — frame arrival IS the damage signal. Sketch of the implementation we run in a Swift driver mirroring this tree:

- One persistent, lazily-started SCStream per display, scaled tiny (~256px wide), cursor off, minimal queue depth — cost is negligible while active.
- Each delivered frame is confirmed with a cheap FNV-1a digest of the scaled pixels (a repaint can redraw identical content).
- `wait_for_change(baseline, timeout)`: resolve at the first frame whose digest differs from the pre-action baseline, else at the old fixed duration.
- Lifecycle: idle-stop after ~30s with no callers; restart transparently on next use.
- Degradation: no Screen Recording grant / stream failure → return "unavailable" fast and fall back to the existing fixed sleep, unchanged.
- One correctness caveat worth encoding in the API docs: a changed frame is NOT application readiness (a caret blink satisfies it) — this only converts fixed-duration sleeps into "wake at first repaint, cap at the old duration". Callers needing semantic readiness still poll AX.
- Arm the watcher on the display containing the acted-on element — a main-display default silently rides out the full cap for windows on other monitors (we shipped that bug and measured it).

Measured effect in the Swift driver: the 800ms WebKit settle resolves at ~76ms p50; combined with the watch-deadline change (#3488), click wire time went from ~1.4s to ~551ms p50 with click correctness verified via an independent AX referee.

### Current workaround
Lower the settle constants via the #3490 knobs and accept the reduced margin.

### Affected components and platforms
cua-driver `platform-macos` (ScreenCaptureKit). The concept ports: DXGI dirty rects on Windows, damage events on Linux.

title: [Feature]: Warm session caches at daemon start; stale-while-revalidate for enumeration reads
body:
### Primary area
Cua Driver

### User problem
Two related once-per-session gaps:

1. **Cold first call.** The daemon starts with every cache empty, so the first tool call of a session pays the full cold path (shareable-content fetch, app-directory scan, event-source creation) inside the action instead of at session start. First impressions of driver latency are set by exactly that call.
2. **Enumeration reads recompute identical answers.** `list_windows` / accessibility-tree reads re-run the full enumeration on every call even when called in a tight agent loop. Measured against the 0.16 binary under adversarial load (6 CPU spinners, fresh connection per request): `list_windows` p50 6–11ms where a cache-backed answer serves in ~1.2ms.

### Desired outcome
1. **Warm-up at serve start**: after the socket binds, pre-heat the session-lifetime caches in the background — installed-app scan (cache landing in #3492), running-app list, event source; gate anything TCC-adjacent on the preflight (`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`) so warm-up never raises a permission prompt on an ungranted machine. Every warmed path is the same code the first call would run — behavior identical, timing moved.
2. **Stale-while-revalidate on enumeration replies** (opt-in or short-TTL): serve a recent reply instantly while one background task recomputes, with a hard bound on staleness (we use TTL 100ms, stale cap 20×TTL, single-flight refresh). Actuation paths keep resolving live — only the read-tool replies ride the cache.

### Current workaround
None for warm-up; callers self-throttle enumeration reads.

### Affected components and platforms
cua-driver daemon startup (all platforms) + macOS read tools.

---

**Negative result worth having on record** (so nobody re-runs this expecting a win): we also built a persistent full-res SCStream "screenshot frame server" — the classic remote-desktop trick of serving the latest frame instead of running a one-shot capture. Measured on Apple Silicon/macOS 15 against a driver that already caches capture plans (as this tree does since the 2s TTL cache): **parity, not a win** — warm one-shot 146–180ms vs stream 141–185ms, because PNG encode of a native-res Retina frame dominates both paths once session negotiation is amortized. The honest latency lever for screenshots is the encode, not the capture.

title: cua-driver: forward experimental PiP from MCP proxy to daemon
body:
## Bug

`cua-driver --experimental-pip mcp` advertises the experimental PiP preview but does not make the preview visible when the MCP proxy launches the GUI-owning daemon.

## Reproduction

1. Ensure no Cua Driver daemon is listening.
2. Start `cua-driver --experimental-pip mcp`.
3. Send a desktop observation/action through the MCP session.

The proxy starts the daemon through `daemon_launch_arguments` / `daemon_process_arguments`, but `append_daemon_launch_state` does not propagate the PiP request. The daemon therefore starts as plain `serve`, and the macOS AppKit PiP backend is never initialized.

## Expected

A process-local PiP opt-in on the MCP proxy is forwarded to a newly launched daemon as `serve --experimental-pip`, without requiring persistent config mutation.

If a compatible daemon is already running without PiP, the proxy should not silently claim that it changed that daemon; this issue is scoped first to the fresh-daemon launch path.

## Acceptance evidence

- focused launch-argument tests for macOS and non-macOS daemon construction;
- default-off behavior remains unchanged;
- `--experimental-pip` is forwarded only when explicitly requested;
- a logged-in macOS Calculator smoke visibly shows the PiP preview updating after an observation/action.

This blocks the visible end-to-end acceptance of mslsrc/tbh#26292.

title: PiP preview should be movable, minimizable, and image-only
body:
## Problem

A live TBH end-to-end test exposed that the experimental macOS PiP preview behaves like a permanent debug HUD:

- the borderless window cannot be minimized through standard macOS controls
- it joins every Space and feels glued to the screen
- the action-name pill takes space without adding useful observability

This makes the preview disruptive during real computer-use sessions.

## Proposed behavior

- Use standard macOS titled, closable, miniaturizable, and resizable window chrome.
- Allow dragging through the title bar and unused background.
- Keep the preview on the Space where it was opened instead of joining all Spaces.
- Closing or minimizing the preview must not stop the driver session.
- Show only the latest screenshot; remove the synthesized action label and pill.

## Verification

Run the signed macOS driver with `--experimental-pip`, send a real MCP action, and verify the visible preview can be dragged, minimized, resized, and closed. Confirm the action label is absent and the daemon remains responsive.

title: perf(cua-driver): run health checks concurrently
body:
## Problem

`HealthReportTool::invoke` awaits each provider check in sequence, so a full report pays the **sum** of every probe's latency — and the slow probes (capture, AX, subprocess-backed checks) dominate. The checks are independent probes; nothing about the report depends on execution order.

## Change

The loop becomes `futures_util::future::join_all` (already a dependency of `cua-driver-core`) over the same per-name closure:

- All check futures are polled **within the same task** — no extra threads, and no new `Send`/`Sync` requirements on `HealthCheckProvider` implementations.
- `join_all` returns results in input order, so the report keeps its canonical check order (pinned by the existing fixture test, still green).
- Skip-filter behavior unchanged: filtered names still yield their skip entries in place.

A provider whose checks must not overlap can still serialize internally, but none of the in-tree providers do — each check is a self-contained probe.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos` — green, including `invoke_full_run_produces_macos_check_set` (canonical order) and the core fixture suite.
- In the Swift driver this Rust tree mirrors, the same change (task group with order-preserving slots) took a warm quiet `health_report` from ~43ms to ~0.4ms; the report's floor becomes the slowest single probe instead of the sum of all probes.

title: [Feature]: Per-turn screenshot dedup — an unchanged display rides as one line of text, not a re-encoded image
body:
### Primary area
MCP or agent integration

### User problem
Agent loops attach a fresh screenshot of every display on every model turn. On a multi-display machine most turns change at most one display — yet every turn pays, per display: the downscale pass, the JPEG/PNG encode, the upload, and (the expensive part) the model's image tokens for a picture it already holds from the previous turn.

### Desired outcome
A per-run frame cache in the agent loop:

- Every turn still captures every display at full resolution — the capture is how the run learns whether anything moved, and it's the cheap half.
- Each capture is digested (we use FNV-1a over the packed pixels). A display whose digest matches the previous turn skips the downscale, the encode, and the re-attach, and rides as **one line of text** instead ("display 2 unchanged since the previous screenshot") placed next to the frames note, so the model knows exactly which prior image the line licenses it to reuse.
- The cache is owned by the run and minted per execution: the first turn of every run attaches everything, and no run ever matches against a screen some other run saw.

### Current workaround
None that's safe — agents either re-send everything (the default cost) or heuristically skip screenshots and go blind for a turn.

### Affected components and platforms
Agent/SDK loop (wherever turn context is assembled), all platforms. Independent of the driver itself — filing here because the driver's consumers are where the cost lands.

### Additional context
We run exactly this in a production agent loop built on a driver mirroring this tree: digest-gated per-run cache, unchanged displays as one text line each. The observable effect is that static-display turns drop the encode+upload+image-token cost entirely while the model keeps full visual grounding (it already holds the exact image the text line refers to). Pairs naturally with #3494 (batched actions): mechanical stretches become one round trip and mostly-text turns.

title: [RFC] Add target-addressable KWin input delivery for KDE/Wayland
docs(rfc): specify KWin target-input safety contract
body:
## Maintainer decision

The requested Plasma/KWin 6.6 feasibility run is complete. It produced a **negative target-safety result for the guarded portal/libei approach**: after A was confirmed, a forced focus takeover caused A's key pair to be delivered to B.

An [independent Plasma 6.6.6 report by astrovm](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3507#issuecomment-6623887198) corroborates the focus hazard across a **two-call orchestration sequence**: `bring_to_front(A)` followed by `type_text(scope:desktop)`.

In 45 deliberately forced-focus trials, **4 bursts** (100 keys each) went entirely to B and 41 to A; all 15 no-focus-change trials went to A. Window-scoped input correctly refused without sending keys, and the Driver did not falsely report success (`unverifiable`).

This is externally reported evidence, **not** a locally reproduced run or an estimate of normal-use race frequency.

**Production KWin input remains disabled. This PR does not unblock #3972 or #1982.**

## What this PR contains

- The RFC safety contract, now explicitly addressing unsafe implicit desktop-input fallback in Cua-controlled SDK/agent orchestration.
- The isolated Plasma/KWin **6.6.4** experiment and machine-readable evidence.
- Reproducible helper/Driver prototype sidecars under `rfcs/3506/`.
- Proposed (not implemented) headless orchestration acceptance cases and separate attribution of the Plasma 6.6.6 report.
- No production-source change under `libs/cua-driver`.

The exact-version experiment ran inside a **QEMU/KVM Kubuntu 26.04 guest** (Plasma/KWin 6.6.4, Qt 6.10.2).

The earlier CachyOS/KWin 6.7.5 host experiment is retained only as separate historical evidence.

## Evidence that matters for review

- **Operation 7:** Pre-dispatch focus takeover was refused; zero input events.
- **Operation 9:** Input reached A, the worker reply was deliberately lost, the caller returned `unknown`, and reuse of that operation number was refused. This is **partial** evidence for the at-most-once/no-replay invariant, not full reconnect/deduplication proof.
- **Operation 10:** Background request returned `background_unavailable`; zero input events.
- **Operation 11:** After A was confirmed, forced focus takeover delivered A's intended key pair to **B**. This counterexample keeps the guarded foreground portal/libei proposal blocked.
- **External Plasma 6.6.6 report:** The two-call activation + desktop-input route allowed 4/45 forced-focus bursts to reach B. No burst splitting was observed, but that does not prove splitting impossible. This differs from operation 11, which tested a guarded Driver operation.

### Review entry points

- [RFC and safety contract](https://github.com/netbospl/cua/blob/rfc/3506-kwin-target-input/rfcs/3506-kwin-target-input.md)
- [Plasma 6.6.4 proof, limitations, and external report](https://github.com/netbospl/cua/blob/rfc/3506-kwin-target-input/rfcs/3506/plasma-6.6-proof.md)
- [Machine-readable operation evidence](https://github.com/netbospl/cua/blob/rfc/3506-kwin-target-input/rfcs/3506/evidence/plasma-6.6.4.json)
- [Independent comment by astrovm](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3507#issuecomment-6623887198)
- [Follow-up documentation commit `beee3c6c3a`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/commit/beee3c6c3a7410691499ffc94c0d0d0fd47e5439)

## Updated no-global-fallback contract

The RFC now explicitly prohibits **Cua-controlled SDK or agent/tool orchestration from silently reconstructing a rejected or unsupported exact-target request as activation followed by desktop-scoped input**.

Separate calls do not preserve destination binding.

An explicit user request for desktop-scoped input remains distinct from an automatic fallback intended to satisfy a target-scoped request.

This is a **proposed safety requirement**, not proof of implemented SDK/agent enforcement.

Headless orchestration acceptance cases have been proposed but not yet implemented or executed.

## Backend compatibility (Wayland-first)

For **native KWin/Wayland targets**, this RFC favors compositor-provided,
trusted target identity and delivery-time target binding. It **preserves the
existing X11/Xorg and XWayland compatibility backends** for genuine X11
clients; it does not remove or deprecate either backend. The proposal requires
the target's current, verified window/display backend to determine the eligible
route, subject to normal Driver policy, capability, identity and result guarantees;
it does not claim this routing contract is fully implemented.

Native KWin UUIDs/helper tokens must not be reinterpreted as X11 XIDs.
A refused, partial, or unknown exact-window operation must not be silently
retried using XTest, XWayland, activation followed by desktop-scoped input,
or another weaker/global route. An explicitly authorized desktop-scoped
request and a separately admitted, target-validated AT-SPI semantic action
remain distinct operations. Existing compatibility support is not proof of
safe destination-bound raw input for every XWayland window.

The RFC now proposes mixed Wayland/XWayland route-selection, identity and
negative-fallback acceptance cases. They are **proposed, not executed**.
The independent [PR #7070](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7070) by astrovm
proposes a KWin-side input gate and should be evaluated against the RFC's
policy, target identity, ownership, lifecycle and truthful-result contract.
Its reported validations are not presented as tests run for this RFC.

## Validation and CI status

**PR head:** `7f8616acf9923c7c458b0171629c1dc71826dfb6`. The latest commit adds only a Wayland-first and X11/XWayland compatibility clarification to the RFC; it does not change production input. The experimental parent-ledger regression test from the preceding commit remains intact.

At preceding head `57e8d61b0eb9aedc4569cf33e2a22ba763749624`, contributor-run offline checks passed (not rerun after the documentation-only compatibility clarification):

- `PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH /usr/bin/python3 -m unittest discover -s rfcs/3506 -p 'test_*.py'`: 10 tests.
- `/usr/bin/python3 rfcs/3506/driver-prototype/test_contract.py`: structural sidecar check.
- `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --test kwin_helper_contract`: 8 tests at the historical checkout.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core action_target::tests`: 5 focused tests at the historical checkout.
- `git diff --check` and published patch SHA-256 checks.

The new ledger test runs the real runner in two fresh processes with a preexisting operation-9 ledger, stubs the bus, prevents Driver launch and checks the ledger remains unchanged. An isolated mutation replacing exclusive creation with overwrite makes the test fail. It does not prove crash-durable storage, daemon-wide deduplication, cross-connection replay safety or native delivery. The system Python supplies the sidecar's existing `dbus`/`gi` dependencies; the new ledger case also runs without them.

Earlier formatting checks found the proof document fails Prettier on both the tested revision and its baseline. The retained historical focused Rust timing test failed on both clean base and prototype; its root cause remains unproven. These are not passing full-suite claims.

**CI snapshot:** GitHub Actions runs for this head were reported `action_required`, not passing; the check-runs endpoint returned no check runs at the time of inspection. A prior head's CLA check failed; CLA acceptance is a separate human contributor action and has not been performed by automation. Recheck GitHub for current status.

Live KWin input tests, the full desktop matrix, outer SDK acknowledgement-loss testing, and proposed orchestration acceptance tests were not rerun. The external Plasma 6.6.6 report remains independently attributed.

A separate current-upstream metadata correction is proposed in [#7683](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7683). It is not merged into or part of this RFC. Its own test results are not included in the counts above.

## Not claimed / remaining blockers

- No supported delivery-time destination-bound KWin keyboard/pointer primitive has been demonstrated.
- Focus activation, confirmation, or a shorter activation-to-input interval does not guarantee target-bound delivery.
- The independent 6.6.6 results do not establish normal-use race frequency or rule out split bursts.
- Operation 9 does not prove daemon-wide deduplication, cross-connection replay protection, outer SDK acknowledgement-loss handling, or the full reconnect/re-resolve and fresh-sequence path.
- Pointer, drag, hotkey, multi-frame input, and comprehensive session/lifecycle revocation remain unqualified.
- The retained [guest recording](https://github.com/netbospl/cua/blob/rfc/3506-kwin-target-input/rfcs/3506/evidence/plasma-6.6.4-AB.webm) covers operations **1–6 only**, not the operation-11 focus-race counterexample.

The RFC remains in **`review`**. Production raw KWin input remains disabled.

## Requested disposition

Maintainers are asked to review:

1. The negative feasibility evidence for guarded focus-bound portal/libei input.
2. The independently reported two-call orchestration hazard.
3. The proposed SDK/agent no-global-fallback contract.
4. The remaining requirements for supported destination-bound input and cross-connection replay safety.

**The safe production state remains refusal until a supported target-bound primitive and the outstanding acceptance requirements are demonstrated.**

Refs #3506, #3336, #3550, #3551, #3972, #1982, #4034.

**AI assistance disclosure:** The experiment, harness adaptation, evidence analysis, RFC revisions, and this summary were AI-assisted. astrovm's Plasma 6.6.6 observations were independently reported and were not reproduced by us.
