title: uninstall-local.sh reports success while app-bundle daemon and release markers remain
body:
## Summary

`uninstall-local.sh` can print a successful uninstall while a daemon launched from `/Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app` is still running and local release-marker files remain.

The script stops processes launched through the CLI symlink or the package-current executable, but it does not stop the app-bundle executable before deleting the bundle. Its local-home cleanup list also omits `.release_installed` marker files.

## Reproduction

1. Install the local macOS build using the repository's local installer.
2. Start the daemon through the app bundle:

   ```bash
   /Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver-local serve --dangerously-bypass-approvals
   ```

3. Run the repository's `uninstall-local.sh`.
4. Inspect the local daemon processes and the local product home.

## Expected behavior

The uninstaller should stop every process owned by the local installation before removing its executable, remove all installer-owned marker files, and report success only after the local installation is inactive and its owned state is gone.

## Actual behavior

- The app bundle is removed, but the daemon launched from the app-bundle executable remains running.
- `.release_installed` remains under the local product home, so the directory is preserved.
- The script still prints `cua-driver-local uninstalled`.

## Root cause in the current script

- The process-stop loop checks only the CLI symlink and `$HOME/.cua-driver-local/packages/current/cua-driver-local`; it omits `/Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver-local`.
- The known-file cleanup list omits `.release_installed`.
- No final verification checks for a remaining local daemon before reporting success.

## Suggested fix

- Stop the exact app-bundle executable path before removing the app.
- Include all installer-owned release markers in the bounded cleanup list.
- Add a final local-identity process check and fail or warn if a daemon remains.

This is distinct from #3191, which addressed the release Unix uninstaller rather than the local macOS app-bundle path.

Confirmed with local package version `0.23.1`; the same omissions remain on current `origin/main` at `72fe7fff6e2d84863585f7164d9663367e8fa465`.

title: cua-driver status reports unrelated PID after custom-socket daemon overwrites default PID file
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver status` can report the PID of an unrelated daemon when another daemon is started with a custom socket. Every `serve` process writes the same default PID file, while `status --socket ...` reads that shared file instead of identifying the process serving the selected socket.

This makes daemon identity diagnostics contradictory: the socket is live and commands reach one process, but `status` can display another process's PID.

## Reproduction

1. Start the normal daemon on its default socket (synthetic PID `1111`).
2. Start a second daemon on a custom socket (synthetic PID `2222`):

   ```bash
   cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/cua-driver-secondary.sock --dangerously-bypass-approvals
   ```

3. Query the default daemon:

   ```bash
   cua-driver status
   cua-driver permissions status
   ```

4. Observe that `status` reports PID `2222`, while the permission probe and process inspection identify PID `1111` as the daemon serving the default socket.

The same problem applies in the other direction: `status --socket /tmp/cua-driver-secondary.sock` still reads the shared default PID file rather than socket-specific identity.

## Expected behavior

`status` should report the process that serves the selected socket. A custom-socket daemon should not overwrite identity state for the default daemon.

Possible approaches include using a socket-specific PID file, returning the daemon PID over the selected socket, or omitting the PID when it cannot be bound reliably to that socket.

## Actual behavior

- `serve` always passes the default PID-file path, even when `--socket` selects another socket.
- Each daemon overwrites the shared PID file after binding.
- `status` reads that shared PID file and presents it as the PID for the selected live socket.

## Related diagnostic gap

The local-build `diagnose` path also reports release-app install paths and the release bundle identity instead of deriving the active executable's local identity. Keeping status and diagnostic identity tied to the selected executable/socket would make permission audits substantially less ambiguous.

## Source pointers

- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/main.rs`: `serve` and `status` both use `default_pid_file_path()` independently of the selected socket.
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/serve.rs`: `run_serve` writes the supplied PID file; `run_status_cmd` reads it after checking the selected socket.
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs`: `diagnose` contains release-specific install and TCC identity assumptions.

Confirmed against current `origin/main` at `72fe7fff6e2d84863585f7164d9663367e8fa465`.

title: cua-driver: process churn (~241 procs/3min) prevents TCC permission state from settling; daemon also hangs at MCP-initialize
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver` intermittently fails to hand off after startup — either hanging in an MCP-initialize phase for 180s+, or (once macOS TCC permissions were confirmed granted via System Settings) returning empty/`permissions_pending` results from `list_apps`/`capture` even though the grant is genuinely present. Diagnosed via `log show` that a large number of short-lived `cua-driver` processes were spawning in quick succession rather than one stable daemon persisting, each issuing its own `TCCAccessRequest()` IPC call — which likely prevents TCC's permission cache from ever settling against a stable process identity.

**Caveat / possible contributing factor on my end:** during diagnosis I ran `cua-driver serve`/`cua-driver mcp` manually from a terminal several times outside Hermes's normal embedded-daemon lifecycle (to isolate whether the bug was in Hermes's Python or the driver itself). I later found this note in your README: *"A gateway, terminal, or unrelated helper must not spawn the daemon on the app's behalf."* It's possible my manual invocations directly caused or worsened the process churn I measured, rather than it being a pure upstream defect independent of any caller behavior. I'm filing this with that caveat explicit rather than asserting it's 100% driver-side, since I can't rule out that contribution — but the same intermittent failure (hang / empty result / `permissions_pending` after a confirmed grant) also happened during normal Hermes-driven calls before I started manual testing, so there does appear to be an underlying issue independent of that.

## Environment

- `cua-driver 0.23.2` (darwin)
- macOS, Intel iMac (spinning HDD, not SSD — relevant to timing)
- Installed via `hermes computer-use install`, launched through `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` (correct TCC-attributed launch path per your embedded-daemon docs)
- Both Accessibility and Screen Recording confirmed granted in System Settings → Privacy & Security (visually verified, toggle ON) for "Cua Driver"

## Evidence

`log show --predicate 'process == "cua-driver"' --last 5m` over roughly 3 minutes of light interactive use (a handful of `capture`/`list_apps` calls, not a stress test) showed:

- **596 `TCCAccessRequest()` IPC log lines**
- **241 distinct PIDs** for `cua-driver` in that window (PID range ~85693–87527)
- i.e. roughly **1.3 new `cua-driver` processes per second**, sustained

Sample log lines:
```
2026-09-02 12:05:31.699208-0400 ... 85693  0  cua-driver: (TCC) TCCAccessRequest() IPC
2026-09-02 12:05:31.758206-0400 ... 85693  0  cua-driver: (TCC) TCCAccessRequest() IPC
2026-09-02 12:05:32.815392-0400 ... 85705  0  cua-driver: (TCC) TCCAccessRequest() IPC
2026-09-02 12:05:32.876989-0400 ... 85705  0  cua-driver: (TCC) TCCAccessRequest() IPC
[... continues at ~1/sec with a new PID nearly every time ...]
```

Separately, before the permission dance, a direct standalone repro (`cua-driver serve --embedded ...` in one terminal, `cua-driver status --socket ...` in another) showed the daemon printing "Cua Driver daemon listening on ..." successfully, but its own `status` subcommand against that exact socket hanging indefinitely (8s+ timeout, no response) — suggesting the control-socket handshake itself can wedge independent of the process-churn issue above.

## Expected behavior

A single `cua-driver` daemon process should stay alive across a session and answer its MCP/control socket promptly, with TCC permission state settling once granted and staying settled.

## Actual behavior

- Either the daemon start sequence hangs for 180s+ never completing MCP `initialize`, or
- Many short-lived processes spawn in rapid succession, each re-triggering TCC, and permission state never reads as "granted" to the caller even when System Settings shows it on.

Happy to provide the full `log show` output, `hermes computer-use doctor` output (`health_report failed: cua-driver mcp produced no response for 'initialize'. stderr tail: ['cua-driver-rs: daemon did not acknowledge the MCP control session']`), or reproduce with more instrumentation if useful.

title: Windows QEMU container can never report ready: computer-server binds 127.0.0.1 but entry.sh polls the VM IP
body:
## Summary

`libs/qemu-docker/windows` starts `cua-computer-server` without a `--host` argument, so it listens on `127.0.0.1:5000` inside the guest only. `src/entry.sh` waits on `http://$VM_IP:5000/status`, which can never succeed. The container therefore prints `Waiting for Cua computer-server to be ready. This might take a while...` forever, and the published `-p 5000:5000` port is dead from both the container and the Docker host.

The server itself is healthy — this is purely a bind-address / readiness-probe mismatch.

## Environment

- image `trycua/cua-qemu-windows:latest` (VERSION 0.1.3)
- guest: Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 2024, build 26100.1742, supplied as `/storage/custom.iso`
- host: Docker 29.7.2 on Windows/WSL2, `--device /dev/kvm --device /dev/net/tun --cap-add NET_ADMIN`

## Evidence

Inside the guest, the server is up and answering on loopback:

```
=== LISTEN 5000 ===
LocalAddress LocalPort OwningProcess
127.0.0.1         5000          6364

=== LOCAL PROBE ===
{"status":"ok","os_type":"windows","features":["agent","mcp"]}
```

From the container, the guest is reachable but port 5000 is not:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://172.30.0.2:5000/status
000
$ for p in 5000 3389 445 135; do (echo > /dev/tcp/172.30.0.2/$p) && echo "$p OPEN" || echo "$p closed"; done
5000 closed
3389 OPEN
445 OPEN
135 OPEN
```

Guest networking is fine (RDP, SMB and RPC all answer) — only 5000 is unreachable, matching a loopback-only bind.

The scheduled task itself works: `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo` shows `LastTaskResult: 0`, and the server log records a clean start at logon. The `AtLogOn` trigger is not the problem.

## Cause

`src/vm/setup/setup-cua-server.ps1` builds the start script with:

```powershell
& uv run --directory $ProjectDir python -m computer_server --port 5000
```

No `--host`, so the server takes its loopback default. Meanwhile `src/entry.sh` polls:

```bash
response=$(curl --write-out '%{http_code}' --silent --output /dev/null $VM_IP:5000/status)
```

`$VM_IP` is the guest's DHCP address (`172.30.0.2`), never `127.0.0.1` from the server's point of view.

The firewall is not involved: the same script already adds an inbound rule for 5000, and that rule is created successfully.

## Suggested fix

Pass an explicit bind address in the generated start script, e.g.

```powershell
& uv run --directory $ProjectDir python -m computer_server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5000
```

## Secondary observation

The readiness loop in `entry.sh` has no failure path — it prints the same "waiting" line indefinitely with no timeout and no diagnostic, which is what made this take a while to pin down. A bounded wait that eventually prints what it probed would surface this class of problem immediately.

title: Windows QEMU container exits 61 with no message when no ISO is supplied; the only working path is /storage/custom.iso
body:
## Summary

`trycua/cua-qemu-windows` inherits `trycua/windows-local`, whose `/run/install.sh` has **no ISO download logic** — no `downloadImage`, no mido, no curl. `define.sh` hardcodes `parseVersion()` to `win11x64-enterprise-eval` regardless of the `VERSION` env var, and the non-custom path then requires `/storage/tmp/win11x64-enterprise-eval.iso` to already exist. It never can, so the VM process exits 61.

Nothing is printed. The outer `src/entry.sh` keeps looping on `Waiting for VM to start...` after its child has already died, so the container looks alive while doing nothing.

## Reproduction

```bash
docker run -d --name cua-win --device /dev/kvm --device /dev/net/tun --cap-add NET_ADMIN \
  -p 8006:8006 -p 5000:5000 -v cua-win-storage:/storage trycua/cua-qemu-windows:latest
docker logs cua-win
```

Output stops after the `CPU: ... KERNEL: ...` banner. `ps` inside the container shows the `tini -s /run/entry.sh` child is gone while PID 1 keeps printing.

Tracing it (`bash -x /run/entry.sh`) ends at:

```
++ '[' '!' -s /storage/tmp/win11x64-enterprise-eval.iso ']'
++ exit 61
```

## What actually works

Placing a Windows ISO where `detectCustom()` -> `findFile()` looks — `/storage/custom.iso` (or `/boot.iso`, `/custom.iso`, `/storage/boot.iso`) — takes the `CUSTOM` branch and installs normally. A read-only bind mount is enough:

```bash
-v /path/to/windows.iso:/storage/custom.iso:ro
```

`src/vm/image/README.md` does tell users to supply their own ISO, but it describes dropping `setup.iso` into a build-context folder that the Dockerfile never copies, and it does not mention `/storage/custom.iso` or the runtime bind mount.

## Two suggestions

1. Fail loudly. Exit 61 with a message naming the paths that were searched would make this self-service. Better still, have the outer `entry.sh` stop looping when its child dies rather than printing `Waiting for VM to start...` forever.
2. Document the working invocation — the `/storage/custom.iso` bind mount — in the container README.

## Note for multi-edition ISOs

The bundled answer file `/run/assets/win11x64-enterprise-eval.xml` has an `<ImageInstall><OSImage>` with `<InstallTo>` but no `<InstallFrom><MetaData>`, so a multi-edition ISO stalls at Setup's edition picker. Volume-license media generally carries two images (e.g. Enterprise LTSC 2024 + Enterprise N LTSC 2024). Supplying `/storage/custom.xml` with an explicit `<InstallFrom>` works around it, since `setXML()` prefers that path over the bundled asset — also worth a line in the README.

## Summary

Add Hyprland hardware-cursor sampling for recording telemetry through the compositor instance socket. Other Wayland compositors remain unsupported by this sampler.

This PR covers **only** the recording-telemetry path:

- Sample cursor position with a non-blocking JSON `j/cursorpos` request on `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket.sock`.
- Bound connect/read/write, shut down the write half after the request, and honor the sampler stop flag during reads so an unresponsive query cannot indefinitely block recording shutdown.
- Reject inherited Hyprland signatures when session metadata selects X11 or another desktop. Nonempty `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` takes precedence over `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP`, including nested Sway/GNOME sessions with an inherited Hyprland login-session value.
- Reject non-object replies and non-finite coordinates so `cursor.jsonl` stays valid JSON.

LinuxObserver, native-case `Cursor` oracle attachment, identity, occlusion, and runtime preflight **are not in this PR**. Those remain in the #3052 / #3466 / #2194 workstream; this does not land a second observer.

## Validation

The local source subsequently committed as `1a4d074847fa63f50ecd13bd9419c45984a6ee3e` was tested using the repository-pinned Rust 1.97.1 toolchain:

- Linux ARM64 container under Colima: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib --locked` - 598 passed, including bounded socket queries, desktop precedence, malformed/non-finite JSON, and sampler shutdown.
- Linux ARM64 container: `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11 cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit --lib --locked` - 68 passed. This is a unit-test run, not a live X11 desktop certification.
- macOS ARM64: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib --locked` - 587 passed. Linux-only tests are excluded on macOS.
- `cargo fmt -p cua-driver-core -- --check` and `git diff --check` - passed.
- The replacement shutdown regression receives the full request on a real Unix socket, withholds the response, and verifies both `stop()` and `Drop` finish before half of the 100ms query deadline. It passed 20 repeated runs.
- Regression sensitivity: temporarily restoring the old desktop-selection logic failed the nested-Sway case; temporarily disabling read cancellation failed the shutdown test at about 101ms. Both mutations were removed and the complete Linux core suite passed again.

Native Omarchy / Hyprland rerun of the same head (`1a4d074847fa63f50ecd13bd9419c45984a6ee3e`), not a container and not macOS cargo-only:

- Host: Omarchy 4.0.2-2 on Apple Silicon (`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`), Hyprland 0.56.2 (`efb50993780079460b0cbed1363e2166a2de1d9f`), `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Hyprland`.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib --locked` - 598 passed, including 10 `cursor_sampler::linux_cursor_tests`.
- `cargo fmt -p cua-driver-core -- --check` and `git diff --check` - passed.
- `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11 cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit --lib --locked` - 68 passed. Same override as above; still not an X11 desktop certification.
- Read-only live `j/cursorpos` on the instance socket with `SHUT_WR` and a 100ms timeout: structured `{"x","y"}` object, finite coordinates, 32-byte replies, 0.11ms and 2.73ms. Coordinates redacted. No pointer injection and no `hyprctl dispatch`.

`cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit --lib --locked` without the x11 override, on that live Hyprland session, is 67 passed / 1 failed: `e2e::tests::native_case_builders_encode_delivery_and_oracle_contracts`. `native_background_case` omits `OracleKind::Cursor` when `DisplayServer::current()` is Wayland, so the assertion that background cases always contain Cursor fails there. That matches this PR's recording-only scope. The x11 override hides that path.

Earlier supporting evidence, reported for `936378db8`: a read-only protocol probe on Omarchy / Hyprland 0.56 returned finite `x`/`y` JSON in 0.12ms. Coordinates were redacted and no input was injected. That probe has now been rerun for `1a4d074` as above.

## Known Gaps

- Does not claim generic Wayland cursor support.
- Does not implement isolated background pointer injection (see #3550 / #3551 / #3552).
- Does not certify the Cursor oracle or close #2194.
- The full cross-platform desktop E2E matrix has not been run for this revision.
- Upstream pull-request workflows require maintainer approval; local results above are not hosted-CI results.

Refs #2194

title: [Bug]: macOS foreground type_text targets a sibling window in the same process (0.23.2)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `type_text` with an explicit `pid`, `window_id`, and `delivery_mode: "foreground"` typed into a different window belonging to the same process. Reproduced with two ordinary AppKit text fields on `@trycua/cua-driver` 0.23.2; the requested window remained unchanged while the decoy received the entire marker.

### Reproduction

1. Compile and launch the minimal Swift/AppKit fixture below. It creates Target and Decoy windows in one process, gives each an editable field, and makes Decoy key last. Both fields initially contain selected baseline text.
2. Use `list_windows` to identify the fixture PID and the Target window ID. Observe that exact window with `get_window_state`; confirm its title and `target-baseline` field value. Do not click or manually activate Target first.
3. Call `type_text` through the Node SDK's `driver.callTool('type_text', JSON.stringify(args))`, with the following arguments (substitute the discovered PID/window ID):

```json
{
  "pid": 15653,
  "window_id": 235,
  "delivery_mode": "foreground",
  "text": "TARGET-0232",
  "session": "isolated-target-test"
}
```

No element index/token or coordinates were supplied. In this run the sibling Decoy window ID was 237.

4. Read `/tmp/pi-window-target-test/state.json`. The fixture writes both field values on `controlTextDidChange`, independently of the driver's success/status report.

Observed on the single isolated attempt performed so far (1/1). No repeatability rate beyond that is claimed. The action completed normally; it was not interrupted.

### Expected behavior

Only the requested Target window receives input; Decoy stays `decoy-baseline`. If exact-window foreground delivery cannot be established, refuse without typing into a sibling window.

### Actual behavior

```json
{
  "decoy": "TARGET-0232",
  "target": "target-baseline"
}
```

The driver returned `isError: false`, `degraded: false`, and:

```json
{
  "delivery": { "mode": "foreground" },
  "effect": "unverifiable",
  "route": "global_input"
}
```

Response text:

```text
Sent (unverified) 11 char(s) via foreground keystrokes (30ms delay). — driver could not confirm; verify via screenshot.
```

The literal marker has 11 characters. The observation was not merely an unconfirmed successful delivery: the independent fixture state shows delivery to the wrong sibling.

### Environment

- Package: `@trycua/cua-driver` 0.23.2, installed from npm, with its Darwin ARM64 native package.
- Host process restarted after upgrading from 0.22.2 before this test.
- macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64.
- Target application: standalone Swift/AppKit fixture with two `NSWindow`s and one `NSTextField` in each.
- Integration: Pi extension using `CuaDriver.create(undefined)` and `callTool`; the extension resolves an observed window handle to the numeric PID/window ID above. It forwards explicit foreground mode rather than retrying background input automatically.
- This is a manual isolated reproduction, not a run of the canonical Rust certification harness.

### Evidence

The pre-action Target observation identified `window_id=235`, `pid=15653`, title `Pi Input Fixture — Target`, and field value `target-baseline`. The Decoy field received the marker, as recorded above.

<details>
<summary>Complete fixture source and build instructions</summary>

Save the following as `/tmp/pi-window-target-test/main.swift` after creating that directory:

```swift
import AppKit

final class Delegate: NSObject, NSApplicationDelegate, NSTextFieldDelegate {
    var windows: [NSWindow] = []
    var fields: [NSTextField] = []
    func save() {
        let state = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: zip(["target", "decoy"], fields.map { $0.stringValue }))
        if let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: state, options: [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]) {
            try? data.write(to: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/pi-window-target-test/state.json"), options: .atomic)
        }
    }
    func controlTextDidChange(_ notification: Notification) { save() }
    func applicationDidFinishLaunching(_ notification: Notification) {
        for (index, name) in ["Target", "Decoy"].enumerated() {
            let window = NSWindow(contentRect: NSRect(x: 150 + index * 500, y: 250, width: 460, height: 180), styleMask: [.titled, .closable], backing: .buffered, defer: false)
            window.title = "Pi Input Fixture — \(name)"
            window.isReleasedWhenClosed = false
            let label = NSTextField(labelWithString: "\(name) field — isolated input test")
            label.frame = NSRect(x: 20, y: 115, width: 420, height: 25)
            let field = NSTextField(frame: NSRect(x: 20, y: 65, width: 420, height: 30))
            field.stringValue = "\(name.lowercased())-baseline"
            field.setAccessibilityLabel("\(name) input")
            field.delegate = self
            window.contentView?.addSubview(label)
            window.contentView?.addSubview(field)
            windows.append(window)
            fields.append(field)
            window.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
            window.makeFirstResponder(field)
        }
        NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true)
        save()
    }
}
let app = NSApplication.shared
let delegate = Delegate()
app.setActivationPolicy(.regular)
app.delegate = delegate
app.run()
```

Compile and launch from a separate terminal:

```sh
swiftc /tmp/pi-window-target-test/main.swift \
  -o /tmp/pi-window-target-test/fixture -framework AppKit
/tmp/pi-window-target-test/fixture
```

The fixture intentionally creates the two windows in one process and leaves Decoy key last. Use only these disposable windows for the input test.

</details>

### Workaround and additional context

No verified workaround. Element-addressed typing was not tested in this reproduction.

Related: #2206 and merged PR #3068. I did not find an exact existing report of this two-window foreground typing case.

A possible area to investigate is `with_foreground_assist` in `platform-macos/src/input/skylight.rs`: current main calls `await_window_focused` without checking its boolean result and can run the body when foreground activation is unavailable. However, there are downstream focus checks too; this is a lead, **not a proven root cause**. I have not established the exact source SHA bundled in the npm artifact.

This report concerns observed same-process window-routing correctness; no cross-process exploit or permission-boundary bypass was tested or is claimed.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: Diorama demo blocks the event loop in its mouse-tracking loop
body:
**Description**

The async Diorama demonstration `main` function throttles its mouse-tracking loop with `time.sleep(0.05)`. This synchronous sleep runs after each iteration on the event-loop thread, preventing the other async desktop operations or any unrelated scheduled coroutine from progressing during every 50 ms pause. Using `await asyncio.sleep(0.05)` would preserve the intended throttle without stopping the loop.

**Observed Behavior**

A local call-site reproduction executed the extracted `time.sleep` expression with a controlled 0.03-second operand. The wrapper took 0.0302 seconds; 6 heartbeat opportunities were expected while it ran, but 0 heartbeats were observed. No external GUI, device, or service was contacted.

**Affected Version**

- Package: `cua-computer-server` 0.3.42
- Python: CPython 3.12.13
- File: `computer_server/diorama/diorama.py`
- Function: `main`
- Call site: line 540, `time.sleep(0.05)`
- The same call remains in the current repository source.

**Reproduction**

Run the PoC below from its material directory. The shared `_site_harness` extracts the exact reported call expression from the 0.3.42 source, substitutes a finite local operand, and measures event-loop progress with a heartbeat coroutine.

**PoC Source Code**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
from pathlib import Path
import sys

POC_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(POC_ROOT))
from _site_harness import run

REPO_ROOT = next(
    parent
    for parent in Path(__file__).resolve().parents
    if (parent / "artifacts").is_dir()
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(run(Path(__file__).with_name("inputs") / "sites.json", Path(__file__).with_name("result.json"), REPO_ROOT))
```

title: macOS drag_to blocks the event loop for the full drag duration
body:
**Description**

`MacOSAutomationHandler.drag_to` is async, but it implements the drag delay with synchronous `time.sleep` calls inside a 20-step loop. The sleeps add up to the caller-provided `duration` (0.5 seconds by default), keeping the server's event-loop thread blocked for essentially the entire drag and delaying unrelated requests and coroutines.

**Observed Behavior**

A local call-site reproduction executed the extracted `time.sleep` expression with a controlled 0.03-second operand. The wrapper took 0.0305 seconds; 6 heartbeat opportunities were expected during the call, but 0 heartbeats ran. The reproduction contacted no GUI, device, or external service.

- Package: `cua-computer-server` 0.3.42

- File: `computer_server/handlers/macos.py`
- Method: `MacOSAutomationHandler.drag_to`
- Confirmed call site: line 1188 in the 0.3.42 source

title: fix(cua-cli): preflight credential storage before device login
body:
## Summary

Detect unavailable or explicitly disabled credential storage before starting device authorization. This is a narrow login correction: it does not change identity providers, token scopes, credential precedence, or CLI-to-SDK handoff.

- Perform a read-only check of the configured store before discovery or browser launch. Do not write a probe credential, parse stale data, or select a fallback backend.
- Reject the null backend, whose writes silently discard tokens.
- Keep later save failures actionable and sanitize keyring/OS errors.
- Isolate command tests from the host keychain and add CLI unit CI for Python 3.12/3.13.

## Validation

- CLI suite: 201 passed on Python 3.13.15; five coroutine warnings from unrelated image-command tests.
- Focused Ruff, Black, isort, and whitespace checks.
- Synthetic tests cover unavailable/disabled storage, empty/corrupt old contents, pre-network refusal, later write failure, and credential redaction.

A read check does not prove later writability. No real login is required for these tests. Native platform keyring integration remains a separate manual smoke.

## Review and rollback

Requested implementation scope is the pre-login storage diagnostic. Draft for maintainer review; do not merge automatically. Revert this commit to restore the previous login sequence. No migration, plaintext fallback, package upgrade, or deployment is included.

title: fix(cua-sandbox): explain supported Fleet credential routes
body:
## Summary

Explain the actual credential routes when the Fleet SDK has no usable token or complete client-credential pair. This changes the early error only; it does not implement a new CLI-to-SDK handoff.

- Name `FLEETS_TOKEN` and `cua.configure(fleet_token=...)` alongside client credentials.
- Identify missing client-credential field names without printing values.
- Explain that this SDK path does not read the separate session stored by `cua auth login`, and that `CUA_API_KEY` is not a Fleet credential.
- Continue failing before HTTP client construction.

## Validation

- Three missing/partial-credential regressions failed against the original diagnostic and pass with the correction.
- 82 Fleet client, transport and configuration tests passed on Python 3.13.15, including token precedence, configured endpoints and generated-SDK refresh behavior.
- Ruff, Black, isort and whitespace checks passed.
- Only synthetic credentials used; no network or credential-store access in the new tests.

## Boundaries

No token audience, refresh policy, environment precedence, legacy/custom endpoint routing or permissions change. A static token still has its existing lifetime; this does not resolve #3127. Existing credential-acquisition documentation remains in #3556 rather than being duplicated here. A unified session handoff would require a separate accepted auth contract.

## Review and rollback

Draft for review, no merge or release authorized. Revert the diagnostic/tests to roll back; no migration or persistent state change.

title: fix(cua-sandbox): reject unauthorized readiness responses
body:
## Summary

Reject HTTP 401/403 during the Fleet guest-service readiness probe instead of reporting the service ready. Previously the `200 <= status < 500` condition accepted those authorization failures.

- Raise an actionable `PermissionError` after an unauthorized/forbidden readiness response.
- Do not print guest/proxy response bodies or retry a terminal access denial in this layer.
- Preserve existing reachable-service behavior for other statuses, including 404 compatibility, and the existing 5xx readiness retry.

## Validation

- Both 401/403 regressions failed against unchanged production code (`DID NOT RAISE`) and pass with this correction.
- 85 Fleet client, transport and configuration tests passed on Python 3.13.15, including resource cleanup on provisioning failure.
- New tests cover 200/204/404 compatibility, 503-to-200 retry, terminal-denial call count and response-body redaction.
- Ruff, Black, isort and whitespace checks passed.

## Limits and related work

This is a reproduced unit-level readiness defect, not a diagnosis or fix for historical 502s, tenant permissions or billing. No live workload or pool was created. Existing cleanup-convergence work remains in #3367 and is not duplicated. This PR and #3582 touch the same client/test files in separate scopes; rebase and rerun the targeted suites after either lands.

## Review and rollback

Draft for SDK maintainer review; no merge or release authorized. Verify the selected hosted path with an authorized test account before release. Revert this commit to restore prior status handling; no migration or production state change.

title: cua-cli: `cua do` cloud targets and `serve-mcp` sandbox/computer tools use the legacy /v1/vms API against run.cua.ai (JSONDecodeError) instead of Fleet
body:
## Summary

With Fleet credentials configured (`CUA_CLIENT_ID`/`CUA_CLIENT_SECRET`, or `FLEETS_TOKEN`), `cua serve-mcp`'s `sandbox_*`/`computer_*` tools and every `cua do` verb targeting `cloud`/`cloudv2` fail with:

```
JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

Root cause: those entry points resolve the sandbox through the legacy API-key VM client (`cloud_get_vm` → `GET {CUA_BASE_URL}/v1/vms`), while `cua_cli/main.py` forces `CUA_BASE_URL=https://run.cua.ai`. `run.cua.ai` serves Fleet (and the web app's SPA for unknown paths), not `/v1/vms`, so the client receives HTML. The legacy hosts are not usable either (`api.cua.ai/v1/vms` → 503, `api.cua.sh` → Cloudflare 1010). `cua sb` is only partly affected: it switches to Fleet mode, but only when `FLEETS_TOKEN` is set (`_cloud_auth_kwargs`), not for client credentials, and `sb shell`/`sb exec`/`sb vnc` go through the same legacy resolver.

Docs still advertise `cua do switch cloud <name>` and the MCP server for cloud sandboxes.

## Environment

- `cua-cli` 0.1.15 (PyPI, 2026-08-22) — identical to `main` (`libs/python/cua-cli` has no diffs since the release commit); `@trycua/cli` 0.2.0 on `main` hardcodes the same `/v1/vms` paths
- `cua-sandbox` 0.1.28 (pinned by cua-cli's `cua-sandbox<0.2.0`)
- macOS 15, Python 3.13, `cua auth login` completed (OIDC session valid), Fleet client credentials valid (client-credentials grant against `auth.cua.ai` succeeds; `Pool.get` reaches the Fleet API)

## Reproduction

```console
$ export CUA_CLIENT_ID=... CUA_CLIENT_SECRET=...
$ cua auth login            # succeeds
$ cua sb ls --json
{"sandboxes": [], "errors": [{"source": "cloud", "error": "JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"}]}
$ cua do switch cloud my-pool && cua do screenshot
❌ Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

MCP (`claude mcp add cua -- cua serve-mcp`), any `sandbox_*` or `computer_*` call:

```
Error executing tool sandbox_list: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

HTTP trace of `cua sb ls` (httpx patched to log):

```
GET https://run.cua.ai/v1/vms -> 200 text/html  <!doctype html><html lang="en"> ...
```

Code paths on `main`:

- `libs/python/cua-cli/cua_cli/main.py:80` — `os.environ["CUA_BASE_URL"] = DEFAULT_RUN_API_BASE` (`https://run.cua.ai`)
- `libs/python/cua-cli/cua_cli/commands/do.py:107-115` — `cloud_get_vm` + `CloudTransport._resolve_endpoint`
- `libs/python/cua-cli/cua_cli/commands/mcp.py:404-409` — same, plus every `sandbox_*` tool passing `api_key=await get_access_token()`, which forces `Sandbox._uses_fleet()` to `False`
- `libs/python/cua-cli/cua_cli/commands/sandbox.py:152-162,165-169` — legacy resolver; Fleet gate only on `FLEETS_TOKEN`
- `libs/python/cua-sandbox/README.md` — "The legacy API-key VM API continues to use `https://api.cua.ai`", which the CLI override contradicts

## Expected

When Fleet credentials are present, `cua do`, `cua sb shell|exec`, and `cua serve-mcp` should resolve the sandbox through Fleet: pool → claim → bound sandbox → `service_url(sandbox, "server")` (`{fleet_base}/api/svc/{namespace}/{sandbox}-server/`) with a Fleet bearer token.

## Local fix (verified, not submitted as a PR)

I patched this locally and confirmed it end to end against a Fleet Ubuntu sandbox (`cua do screenshot/click/type/shell`, `cua sb exec`, MCP `computer_screenshot`/`computer_shell`/`sandbox_get`). Approach:

- new `cua_cli/auth/fleet.py`: `fleet_mode()` (delegates to `cua_sandbox._config.has_fleet_auth`), `fleet_access_token()` (workload token, else a cached client-credentials token refreshed 60 s before expiry), `cloud_bearer_token()`, `resolve_fleet_server(name)` (via `_FleetClient.get_pool/get_claim/wait_claim/service_url`)
- `do.py` `_get_api_url` + both `Authorization` header sites → Fleet first, legacy fallback
- `mcp.py`: module-level `_resolve_server_url` / `_sandbox_auth_kwargs`; `sandbox_*` tools stop passing `api_key=` in Fleet mode; `sandbox_create` takes `name` (pool name) in Fleet mode; `sandbox_list` returns an explanatory error (Fleet has no listing)
- `sandbox.py`: `_cloud_auth_kwargs` and `_get_sandbox_api_url` gate on `fleet_mode()`
- 13 unit tests (`tests/auth/test_fleet.py`, `tests/commands/test_fleet_routing.py`); existing suite still green

Two related things I hit while verifying, in case they help:

- `cua-sandbox` 0.1.28's Fleet transport has no firmware selection, so a Windows pool created through this CLI defaults to BIOS and never boots (fixed in 0.4.3 which selects EFI). Bumping the CLI's `cua-sandbox` pin would fix that as well.
- `cua sb delete` / `Sandbox.delete` in Fleet mode deletes only the claim; the pool keeps its warm replica.

Happy to share the patch if useful.

title: Windows: UI-tree revision id + conditional get_window_state (no_change response) to avoid full re-walks
body:
## Context

Consumer: dsh-computer-use (a dsh plugin wrapping cua-driver 0.23.2 on Windows 11 x64, DPI 150%, daemon over named pipe).

Today every `screen_observe` → `get_window_state` performs a full UIA walk + optional screenshot. In our pipeline one full observe costs ~9–12s (walk + password sidecar + optional screenshot). Agent loops re-observe before acting, and the majority of those re-observations return a tree identical to the previous one — while our freshness check is a blunt time-to-live instead of a fact.

## Request

Two related capabilities (either alone already helps):

1. **UI-tree revision id**: expose a monotonic `ui_tree_revision` (or content hash) per (pid, window_id), bumped whenever the captured tree actually changes. Consumers treat it as a consistency token: an action carries the revision it was computed from, and the driver can reject with a structured `stale_revision` when the tree moved on.

2. **Conditional get_window_state**: accept an `if_unchanged_since=<revision>` parameter; when the tree is unchanged, return a lightweight `no_change` response (no element array, no screenshot). This turns the common re-observe into an O(1) check instead of a full walk.

Prior art (measured in competing products, for shape only): Trae's Windows SDK answers `get_app_state` with `mode: full|diff|no_change` plus `ui_revision_id`; the client keeps a per-window baseline, applies `changes[]`/`removed_element_ids` diffs, and "no_change" reuses the baseline — making the observe→act→observe loop cheap. A `no_change` mode alone would unblock us; diff is a bonus.

## Why it matters

- **Cost**: with a conditional request, act→confirm loops (the majority of re-observations in multi-step tasks) stop paying the full walk. We estimate roughly half the wall time of multi-step tasks disappears.
- **Safety**: a revision token lets consumers replace TTL-based snapshot expiry (time approximation, double failure: "expired but unchanged" wastes a re-observe; "unexpired but changed" acts on a stale world) with exact change detection.

Happy to provide UIA walk logs and repro probe windows (WinForms + UWP) if useful.

title: Windows: structured user-intervention signal (cursor displacement / input hook event)
body:
## Context

Same consumer/environment as the tree-revision request: dsh-computer-use over cua-driver 0.23.2, Windows 11 x64.

When a human grabs the mouse mid-task, an agent's cached observation becomes untrustworthy — the agent keeps acting on a world that was just changed externally, with no attribution. Competing products (Trae's computer-use) solve this with a low-level input hook that flags the target pid as "dirty" and lets the agent-side pause; prior art cited for shape only.

## Request

A **read-only, structured intervention signal**. Any of the following (in increasing fidelity) would help:

1. **Cursor displacement probe**: the driver already owns `move_cursor` and knows its own synthetic moves; expose a cheap `get_cursor_pos` / "did the physical cursor move between t0 and t1 without an agent-issued move" answer (boolean or displacement). Enough for consumers to annotate "suspected external intervention".
2. **Low-level input hook event** (WH_MOUSE_LL) surfaced as a structured event: `{type: "user_input", pid, kind: "mouse_down"}` — pid attribution lets consumers decide per-window.

Both are read-only; policy stays with the consumer. We would annotate the affected snapshot as suspect and require re-observation — no blocking in the driver.

## Why it matters

Agent-vs-human races are a real attribution/safety gap today: after an intervention every cached observation is stale by definition, and we can only guess from unverifiable action receipts. A structured signal lets consumers invalidate exactly the right snapshot and record the cause.

title: bug(windows): foreground click on secondary monitor mis-routes to Progman (Desktop); element_token capability undeclared in tools/list
body:
## Summary
When running `cua-driver` (v0.23.2) on a Windows 11 multi-monitor workstation, two distinct issues occur during GUI automation:
1. **Secondary-monitor foreground click mis-routing**: Sending `click(delivery_mode="foreground", coordinate=[X, Y])` to a target application maximized on a secondary monitor (Monitor 1, X > 1920) causes the synthetic click to land on the Primary Monitor's desktop (`Progman`, HWND `0x1022e`). This steals focus and immediately fails the post-action foreground check with `foreground_unavailable`. Moving the same application to the Primary Monitor completely resolves this error.
2. **`element_token` capability omitted in capability map**: While `cua-driver 0.23.2` strictly requires `element_token` or `snapshot_id` alongside `element_index` (rejecting bare indices with `snapshot_id_required`), the MCP `tools/list` capability manifest omits `accessibility.element_tokens` in its capability discovery map despite exposing it in `inputSchema.properties`. Client harnesses relying on capability checks rather than raw schema properties silently drop the token.

---

## Environment & Test Rig Topology
- **OS**: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro [Version 10.0.26200.9278] (x86_64)
- **Display Topology**:
  - **Monitor 0 (Primary, Flags=1)**: `MonitorRect=(0, 0, 1536, 960)`, `WorkRect=(0, 0, 1536, 912)`, DPI scale 125% (1920×1200 physical panel scaled to 1536×960 logical).
  - **Monitor 1 (Secondary, Flags=0)**: `MonitorRect=(1920, 0, 3840, 1080)`, `WorkRect=(1920, 0, 3840, 1032)`, DPI scale 100%.
  - **Virtual Desktop Metrics**: `SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN=0`, `SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN=0`, `SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN=3840`, `SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN=1080`.
- **Target Application**: Bluebeam Revu 21 (x64) (WPF / Direct2D workstation application).
- **Harness**: Hermes Agent Desktop running on Windows 11 via MCP client.
- **Model**: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash (consuming native SOM screenshots).
- **cua-driver Version**: `cua-driver 0.23.2` (release date 2026-08-31).

---

## Workload / Test Scenario
Automating a PDF markup workflow in Bluebeam Revu:
1. Launch Bluebeam Revu with a multi-page document (`sample-handbook.pdf`).
2. Navigate across pages (`ctrl+right` / `ctrl+left`).
3. Activate the Rectangle markup tool (`r`), select blue line color (`#FF0000FF`), and draw a bounding box around the bottom-right page number on pages 3 and 5.

---

## Observed Behavior & Failure Logs

### Issue 1: Multi-Monitor Click Mis-Routing
When Revu is positioned on Monitor 1 (window rect: `(1913, -7, 3847, 1039)`):
```json
{
  "action": "click",
  "app": "Revu.exe",
  "coordinate": [3228, 770],
  "delivery_mode": "foreground",
  "bring_to_front": true
}
```
**Driver Result**:
```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "action": "click",
  "delivery_mode": "foreground",
  "message": "foreground_unavailable: exact target HWND 0x130cb4 or a verified same-process post-action window was not foreground after the click (actual foreground HWND 0x1022e)"
}
```
Querying HWND `0x1022e` via Win32 confirms:
- **Title**: `Program Manager`
- **Class**: `Progman`
- **Process**: `explorer.exe` (Primary desktop surface on Monitor 0)

The target window (Revu) was foreground before the click, but the click physically struck Monitor 0's desktop, shifting system focus to `Progman`.

### Issue 2: `element_token` Contract Desync
When calling element-index clicks:
```json
{
  "action": "click",
  "element": 16
}
```
**Driver Refusal**:
```text
click: bare element_index is not accepted; pass element_token, or snapshot_id together with element_index
code: snapshot_id_required
```
Checking `_session.supports_capability("accessibility.element_tokens", tool="click")` returns `False`, because the capability string is not advertised in driver capability metadata, even though `element_token` is present in `click`'s `inputSchema.properties`.

---

## Root Cause Analysis
1. **SendInput Multi-Monitor Normalization**:
   In Win32 `SendInput` with `MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE`:
   - Without `MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK`, coordinates normalized to `0..65535` map strictly to the Primary Monitor (Monitor 0).
   - Coordinates referencing Monitor 1 (X: 1920~3840) either wrap around, clamp, or project onto Monitor 0 space.
   - When the synthetic click lands on Monitor 0's desktop, `Progman` gains focus, causing cua-driver's post-click foreground verification heuristic to detect a focus change and report `foreground_unavailable`.
2. **Capability Advertising**:
   `cua-driver` v0.23.2 tightened the element index validation to prevent stale snapshot clicks, but did not update the capability advertisement map to match the schema properties.

---

## Proposed Fix Directions
1. **Multi-Monitor Mouse Events**:
   Ensure all `SendInput` mouse inputs on Windows:
   - Include `MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK` when multi-monitor metrics indicate `SM_CMONITORS > 1`.
   - Normalize X/Y coordinates against the entire virtual desktop span:
   ```text
   norm_x = ((x - SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN) * 65536) / SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN
   norm_y = ((y - SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN) * 65536) / SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN
   ```
2. **Capability Map Parity**:
   Register `accessibility.element_tokens` in the tool capabilities set whenever `element_token` is exposed in `inputSchema`.

---

## 中文说明

### 概述
在 Windows 11 双显示器物理工作站环境下运行 `cua-driver` (v0.23.2) 进行桌面自动化测试时，发现了两个底层实现问题：
1. **副屏前台点击焦点穿透**：当目标应用窗口在副显示器（Monitor 1，X 轴范围 1920~3840）最大化运行时，调用 `click(delivery_mode="foreground")` 会导致物理点击偏移并击中主屏（Monitor 0）的桌面背景（`Progman`，HWND `0x1022e`），导致目标窗口失焦，驱动报错 `foreground_unavailable`。将应用移至主屏后该问题立即消失。
2. **`element_token` 协议能力广播遗漏**：`cua-driver 0.23.2` 严格要求传递 `element_token` 或 `snapshot_id`，禁止裸 `element_index`；但在 MCP `tools/list` 的能力字典中未广播 `accessibility.element_tokens`，导致依据能力表判定的客户端（如 Hermes Agent）静默过滤了该参数。

### 硬件与软件环境
- **操作系统**：Microsoft Windows 11 Pro [Version 10.0.26200.9278] (x86_64)
- **显示器物理拓扑**：
  - **Monitor 0（主屏）**：`MonitorRect=(0, 0, 1536, 960)`，125% DPI 缩放（物理面板 1920×1200 逻辑映射为 1536×960）。
  - **Monitor 1（副屏）**：`MonitorRect=(1920, 0, 3840, 1080)`，100% DPI 缩放。
  - **虚拟屏幕跨度**：`SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN=0`, `SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN=3840`。
- **被测目标应用**：Bluebeam Revu 21 (x64)（基于 WPF / Direct2D 渲染管线）。
- **Agent 框架与底模**：Hermes Agent Desktop (Windows) + Google Gemini 3.8 Flash（原生视觉多模态输入）。
- **驱动版本**：`cua-driver 0.23.2`（2026-08-31 官方最新版本）。

### 修复思路建议
1. **多显示器 `SendInput` 坐标归一化**：
   - 检查并显式加入 `MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK` 标志位。
   - 采用全虚拟桌面宽度（`GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN)`）而非主屏宽度作为 0~65535 归一化分母：
   ```text
   norm_x = ((x - SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN) * 65536) / SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN
   norm_y = ((y - SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN) * 65536) / SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN
   ```
2. **能力清单同步**：
   - 确保 `tools/list` 中的 `capabilities` 字典完整声明 `accessibility.element_tokens`。

title: build(cua-driver): eliminate duplicate macOS Swift bridge symbols
body:
## Problem

Successful macOS Cua Driver builds and focused tests emit repeated duplicate Swift bridge symbol warnings, obscuring actual failures and test summaries. Recorded independently during build/test work on July 20 and August 21, with an additional incidental report on September 7, 2026.

## Investigation

Current main still locks `screencapturekit 6.0.1` and `apple-cf 0.9.3`. Both published Swift packages declare a target named `CoreMediaBridge`. Upstream confirmed that their `AudioBufferBridge` and `AudioBufferListRaw` Swift metadata symbols collide when both object files are linked.

The exact upstream fix already exists: https://github.com/doom-fish/screencapturekit-rs/pull/159 (merged July 18). It renames screencapturekit's private Swift module while preserving its C exports. Preserve that contribution rather than independently reimplementing it.

The fix postdates the published 6.x releases. A dependency update must therefore assess API migration and runtime implications rather than assume a patch-level lockfile refresh is sufficient.

Related Cua evidence: https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2356 records the same warning, but is not a linker-fix workstream. No dedicated active Cua fix was found in searches for duplicate Swift symbols, CoreMediaBridge, apple_cf, and linker warnings.

## Acceptance evidence

- Retain baseline native link output identifying the duplicate Swift symbols.
- Show the same link succeeds without those warnings after the change, while unrelated warnings remain visible.
- Add a focused regression check for the duplicate module/symbol boundary.
- If updating capture dependencies changes production code or behavior, run affected native capture/recording coverage and the required exact-candidate desktop certification before readiness.
- Document Windows/Linux impact explicitly; the colliding Swift bridges are macOS dependencies.

Fresh native reproduction and candidate validation are still pending. Source inspection and upstream evidence are not being presented as a completed local build.

title: fix(agent): execute computer tool calls that arrive as function calls
body:
Fixes #3614.

## Problem

When the configured model does not match `computer-use-preview`, the OpenAI loop hands it the computer tool as a **plain function** (`_map_computer_tool_to_openai(use_native_tool=False)`). The model then answers with a `function_call` named `computer` instead of a `computer_call`.

The dispatch loop had no execution path for that item. `function_call` went straight to `_get_tool()`, which only searches caller-registered tools, so `"computer"` was never found:

```python
if item_type == "function_call":
    await self._on_function_call_start(item)
    function = self._get_tool(item.get("name"))
    if not function:
        raise ToolError(f"Function {item.get('name')} not found")
```

The `ToolError` is caught and fed back to the model, which concludes the tool is unavailable and stops — an accurate report of what happened. As the issue notes, this means the function-calling harness has never actually been able to execute a computer action; only literal `computer-use-preview` models worked, and for models where `computer_use_preview` is rejected by the API this is a hard blocker rather than a degraded path.

## Change

A `computer` function call now runs the same action semantics as a native `computer_call`.

- The shared execution — method lookup, argument validation, telemetry, terminate detection, post-action screenshot — moved into `_execute_computer_action`, which both item types call, so the two paths cannot drift.
- **Both argument spellings are accepted**: the flat schema the function tool advertises (`{"action": "click", "x": 12, "y": 34}`) and the native action dict (`{"type": "click", ...}`), which `replace_failed_computer_calls_with_function_calls` re-emits when a computer_call is retried as a function_call.
- **Flat drag coordinates** (`start_x`/`start_y`/`end_x`/`end_y`) map onto the handler protocol's `path`.
- **Null and non-applicable fields are dropped.** The function tool advertises one flat parameter object shared by every action, so fields belonging to other actions are noise by construction — the trace in the issue shows a `keypress` carrying `status: "success"`. Native `computer_call` items are untouched by this: their action dict is already per-action.
- The reply is a **`function_call_output`**, because the model holds the function tool and not `computer_use_preview`; a `computer_call_output` would not be a valid input item for it. That output carries text only, so the post-action screenshot rides in its own user message.
- `ImageRetentionCallback` now recognizes those captures, so `only_n_most_recent_images` keeps working on this path. It trims only the image message: the `function_call` / `function_call_output` pair is text and has to stay paired.
- A caller-registered tool named `computer` still wins. The built-in semantics are the fallback, not an override.

Malformed arguments, a missing `action`, and an unknown action are reported to the model as tool errors rather than raising.

## Validation

```
CUA_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false uv run pytest libs/python/agent/tests -q   # 62 passed
uv run ruff check libs/python/agent                                    # All checks passed
uv run ruff format ...                                                 # clean
```

`libs/python/agent/tests/test_computer_function_call.py` is new: 13 tests over flat and native argument shapes, field filtering, drag mapping, terminate, screenshot delivery, custom-tool precedence, the three error paths, and retention. Verified against unmodified `main` (stashing only the two source files): **11 fail, 2 pass** — the two that pass are the deliberate no-change guards, `test_native_computer_call_path_is_unchanged` and `test_a_registered_tool_named_computer_still_wins`.

## Known gaps

- No live API call was made from here; the tests drive `_handle_item` against a fake computer handler. The issue already carries the live evidence that the model emits well-formed `function_call` items against this exact schema.
- Only the dispatch gap is addressed. `OperatorNormalizerCallback` still normalizes hallucinated action spellings for `computer_call` items only; extending it to function-call items is a separate change.

title: [Field Report]: Practical computer use findings across Linux (GNOME/KDE Wayland) and macOS
body:
### Environment tested
- **Linux:** CachyOS / Arch Linux (x86_64), GNOME Shell 50.3 on Wayland (Mutter), Plasma 6.x (KWin), running `cua-driver` 0.19.3 through 0.23.2.
- **macOS:** macOS Sequoia (15.x) on Apple Silicon (M-series), running `cua-driver` 0.22.x through 0.24.0.

---

### 1. Linux Wayland (GNOME / KDE)

#### A. D-Bus portal race and silent `portals.conf` permission ignore
- **Symptom:** `cua-driver doctor` reports green, but clicking or typing hangs for 20s and fails:
  ```
  A backend call failed: No such interface 'org.freedesktop.impl.portal.RemoteDesktop'
  libei input backend did not become ready within 20s
  ```
- **Root cause:** If `xdg-desktop-portal-kde` is active (left over from a Plasma login or D-Bus activated by a Qt app), it wins the `impl.portal` registration race against `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome`. The KDE backend doesn't serve `RemoteDesktop` in a Mutter session.
- **Permission trap:** Pinning the backend in `~/.config/xdg-desktop-portal/portals.conf` fixes this:
  ```ini
  [preferred]
  default=gnome
  org.freedesktop.impl.portal.Secret=gnome-keyring
  ```
  However, `xdg-desktop-portal` **silently ignores `portals.conf` if its file permissions are `0600`** (often produced by automation scripts or default umasks). The file must be mode `0644`.
- **Doctor check suggestion:** It would be helpful if `cua-driver doctor` verified:
  1. The active D-Bus owner of `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.RemoteDesktop`.
  2. The permissions of `~/.config/xdg-desktop-portal/portals.conf` if present (flagging `0600`).

#### B. Remote Desktop consent dialog defaults to read-only
- On GNOME Wayland, the `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome` Remote Desktop prompt defaults `Allow Remote Interaction` to unchecked.
- Capture works immediately, but input calls fail with 20s timeouts. Since this is an OS consent barrier, an agent cannot self-grant it.
- Checking *Remember This Selection* writes the persistence token to `~/.config/cua-driver/libei-persistent.token`.
- Worth noting in docs that capture succeeding does not imply input is enabled, and documenting the token path for pre-seeding setups.

#### C. Overlay actor blocking Mutter screenshot portal
- On `cua-driver` 0.19.x, passing `--no-overlay` still created the full-screen `Cua.AgentCursorOverlay` Clutter actor.
- Because Mutter / GNOME Shell implements the screenshot portal directly in the compositor process, having the top-level overlay active occluded the shell, causing subsequent screenshot portal requests to fail or return black captures and hiding the top panel.
- The workaround was explicitly calling `set_agent_cursor_enabled(false)`. (Ties closely into #3062 where daemon restarts leave orphaned actors in `gnome-shell`).

#### D. Decoupling AT-SPI inspection from the Orca screen reader
- `cua-driver` relies on AT-SPI (`toolkit-accessibility`) over D-Bus (`zbus`) for accessibility tree inspection.
- On GNOME, disabling the Orca screen reader through UI settings causes `gsd-a11y-settings` to disable `toolkit-accessibility`, killing AT-SPI tree inspection.
- Turning on `screen-reader-enabled` restores AT-SPI, but spawns `/usr/bin/orca`, which vocalizes every single click, keypress, and focus event across the system.
- To keep AT-SPI active without running an audible screen reader, we had to decouple them:
  ```bash
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled false
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface toolkit-accessibility true
  ```
  along with setting `GTK_A11Y=atspi` and `QT_ACCESSIBILITY=1` in the environment.

#### E. Element actions vs X11 `TranslateCoordinates` on native Wayland
- When an AT-SPI element action falls back to coordinate translation via X11 `TranslateCoordinates`, it fails with an X11 `BadWindow` error on Wayland-native windows (since Wayland surface IDs are not valid X11 XIDs).
- Workaround: Fall back directly to coordinate clicks (`coordinate=[x, y]`) instead of element index translation.

---

### 2. macOS

#### A. Headless daemon and SSH permission gate hang
- TCC grants (Accessibility and Screen Recording) belong to `com.trycua.driver` (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app`).
- When running `cua-driver serve` headlessly, in a background daemon, or over SSH, the preflight permissions gate attempts to open GUI System Settings and enters an infinite polling loop:
  ```
  [cua-driver] still waiting on: Screen Recording (open System Settings → Privacy & Security to grant)
  ```
- In headless/remote agent setups, setting `CUA_DRIVER_RS_PERMISSIONS_GATE=0` or passing `--no-permissions-gate` is essential to prevent hangs when TCC grants are managed out-of-band.

#### B. Mac Catalyst `AXValue` reporting
- Mac Catalyst applications consistently report `null` or placeholder values for `AXValue` attributes across text and control nodes.
- Strict tree-based verification fails on these surfaces. Verification on Catalyst requires multimodal/screenshot diffing rather than accessibility tree readbacks.

#### C. Cross-Space background input via SkyLight
- SkyLight private SPIs (`SLEventPostToPid`, `SLPSPostEventRecordTo`) dispatch background clicks and keystrokes cleanly across macOS Spaces without forcing a Space switch.
- The main caveat is that window bounds queried via CoreGraphics (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo`) for windows on inactive Spaces can return unnormalized coordinates before dispatch.

title: Anthropic computer-use loop: no tool-version mapping for Claude Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 (falls back to retired computer_20241022)
body:
## Summary
`cua_agent/loops/anthropic.py`'s `MODEL_TOOL_MAPPING` table (used by `_get_tool_config_for_model`) has regex patterns for Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.6, Claude 4, Claude 3.7, and Claude 3.5, but none for the new Claude 5 family (e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`). Since none of the patterns match, model lookups for Sonnet 5 silently fall through to the final default:

```python
# Default to Claude 3.5 configuration
return {"tool_version": "computer_20241022", "beta_flag": "computer-use-2024-10-22"}
```

`computer_20241022` has since been fully retired by the Anthropic API — it is not in the list of tool tags the API currently accepts. Every request built with this fallback fails outright:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: AnthropicException - {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"tools.0: Input tag 'computer_20241022' found using 'type' does not match any of the expected tags: 'bash_20250124', 'browser_toolset_20260801', 'code_execution_20250522', 'code_execution_20250825', 'code_execution_20260120', 'code_execution_20260521', 'computer_toolset_20260801', 'custom', 'memory_20250818', 'text_editor_20250124', 'text_editor_20250429', 'text_editor_20250728', 'tool_search_tool_bm25', 'tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119', 'tool_search_tool_regex', 'tool_search_tool_regex_20251119', 'web_fetch_20250910', 'web_fetch_20260209', 'web_fetch_20260309', 'web_fetch_20260318', 'web_search_20250305', 'web_search_20260209', 'web_search_20260318'"}}
```

## Repro
```python
from cua_agent.loops.anthropic import _get_tool_config_for_model
_get_tool_config_for_model("claude-sonnet-5")
# {'tool_version': 'computer_20241022', 'beta_flag': 'computer-use-2024-10-22'}  <- wrong, and now rejected server-side
```
Confirmed live: running the ComputerAgent loop end-to-end against `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5" (via litellm) with a real E2B sandbox fails on every retry with the 400 above. Reproduced on `cua-agent` 0.8.3 (currently installed) and confirmed the same fallback logic is still present in the latest published 0.8.4.

## Suggested fix
Add a `MODEL_TOOL_MAPPING` entry for the Claude 5 family (`claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-5`, etc.) pointing at whatever tool version/beta flag Anthropic expects for that generation (from the accepted-tags list above, looks like `computer_toolset_20260801` is the current computer-use tag, though I don't have Anthropic's docs confirmation of the exact beta flag name to pair with it).

## Environment
- cua-agent: 0.8.3 (also checked 0.8.4 source on PyPI — same gap)
- Called via gl-computer-use (GDP-ADMIN/gl-sdk), which wraps cua-agent's ComputerAgent as its default automation backend.

title: 0.23.2 (Windows): serve daemon crashes 0xC0000005 in uiautomationcore.dll when walking a HIGH-IL (elevated) target tree
body:
### Environment
- **cua-driver version**: 0.23.2 (Windows x86_64 binary from GitHub Releases)
- **OS**: Windows 10 Pro 22H2 build 19045.5247 (x86_64)
- **Binary signed**: Valid (Authenticode)
- **Launch context**: elevated daemon (`cua-driver serve --socket \\.\pipe\cua-driver` via UAC RunAs, High IL) + manually spawned UIAccess worker (`cua-driver-uia.exe --authorized-parent-pid <daemon_pid>`, also via UAC)
- **Hermes MCP child** (`cua-driver mcp --grant existing-profile`) running separately on stdio (medium IL)

### Summary
The serve daemon deterministically crashes with an access violation **inside `uiautomationcore.dll`** when walking the UIA tree of a **high-integrity (elevated) target process** (Task Manager launched via UAC). The MCP child / client sees `daemon closed connection without response` and the pipe disappears. Reproduced on 4 consecutive attempts; Windows Error Reporting records 4 identical crash buckets within 10 minutes.

### Crash signature (Windows Event Log, EventID 1000)
```
Faulting application: cua-driver.exe (0.23.2)
Faulting module:      uiautomationcore.dll 7.2.19041.4355
Exception code:       0xC0000005
Fault offset:         0x00030eb1   (identical on all 4 crashes)
```
Note: unlike #2298 (0.8.3, faulting module = cua-driver.exe itself), the fault here is in the Windows UIA system DLL, consistent with the known UIPI/UIA cross-integrity-level fragility.

### Reproduction steps
1. Start an elevated daemon: `cua-driver serve --socket \\.\pipe\cua-driver` (UAC → High IL). `health_report` OK.
2. Launch an elevated target: `taskmgr.exe` (UAC → High IL, pid visible in tasklist).
3. `cua-driver call list_windows "{}"` → works fine, Task Manager window enumerated OK (14 windows returned, daemon alive).
4. `cua-driver call get_window_state {"pid": <taskmgr_pid>, "window_id": <wid>}` → daemon **silently dies mid-request** (no panic message on stderr/log; pipe gone; client gets `daemon closed connection without response`).
5. Event Log shows the 0xC0000005 in `uiautomationcore.dll` (offset 0x30eb1).
6. `cua-driver call list_windows {"pid": <taskmgr_pid>}` (pid-filtered enumeration) also crashed the daemon on an earlier attempt.

Step 3→4 shows the crash is specifically in the **tree walk of the elevated target**, not window enumeration.

### What was being tested
Full UIAccess activation path on Windows: elevated daemon + `cua-driver-uia.exe` worker (uiAccess=true manifest, valid signature) with `--authorized-parent-pid`. The worker starts and registers `\\.\pipe\cua-driver-uia` correctly, and rejects direct client connections as designed. The chain dead-ends at step 4 above: the high-IL target tree walk crashes before any worker routing can matter.

### Expected behavior
- Walking a high-IL target should either work (via the UIAccess worker path) or fail gracefully with a structured error (e.g. `access_denied` / `uipi_blocked`), never take down the whole daemon.

### Observed impact
- Every elevated-target tree walk kills the daemon; any session loses all in-flight state.
- The UIAccess worker architecture (documented as the supported path for elevated/AppContainer input, see #1602) is unreachable in practice on this build because the daemon dies before forwarding.

### Notes
- Medium-IL targets work fine on the same daemon (Chromium page content, notepad UIA walks verified).
- Happy to capture WER dump (`C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportArchive\AppCrash_cua-driver.exe_*`) or test a fix build.

title: feat(cua-driver): add driver-selected DevTools port
body:
## What this changes

This PR adds an optional browser startup mode and fixes slow or incorrect page reads.

Normally, the browser chooses the local connection number that Driver uses to control it. In the new mode, Driver chooses that number before it starts the browser. Normal startup remains the default. Callers can select the new mode with `launch_posture: "driver_selected_port"` in `browser_prepare`.

The new mode works only with browser profiles managed by Driver. A profile holds browser settings and session data. Driver refuses personal profiles and browsers started outside Driver. It also checks that the control connection belongs to the browser it started.

## Main changes

- Clean up the browser and its temporary data if startup fails or the request is cancelled. On Windows, finish cleanup before retrying a connection-number conflict.
- Stop reporting some complex page replies as timeouts. Incomplete page reads still report that they are incomplete.
- Reduce unnecessary work when checking whether page controls are visible.
- Return the title of the page that was read, instead of an old title saved for the tab.

This does not change cookies, network routing, or how input reaches the browser. It does not establish that the browser can reliably avoid website verification challenges.

## Status and remaining work

This remains a draft. Windows Chrome/Edge and Linux Chrome tests passed for the browser code in this branch. The latest script checks also pass. The full macOS run had one pointer-movement failure; that test passed on retry, but the full run still needs to pass. The latest macOS attempt stopped because the test machine's SSH identity was not verified.

- [ ] Complete the full macOS desktop tests.
- [ ] Get maintainer approval for the startup option and page-reader changes.
