title: fix(cua-driver): keep strict local signing noninteractive
body:
## Summary

Strict macOS source installs could find an older signing identity in the user's
login Keychain and unexpectedly open a password dialog during unattended tests.
The test then appeared stuck, and the dialog did not make it clear that local
code signing—not the website—caused the prompt.

This PR makes strict local signing noninteractive by default and gives clearer
instructions when a user deliberately chooses a keychain that may prompt.

## What changes

- Do not select the login Keychain automatically during strict source signing.
- Prefer the dedicated Cua Driver development keychain when it is available.
- Continue to support an explicitly selected signing identity and keychain.
- When the login Keychain was selected explicitly, explain that any prompt is
  for local-build signing and should not be approved for an unrelated key.
- Stop waiting for keychain-backed signing after 20 seconds.
- In normal non-strict installs, preserve the existing ad-hoc signing fallback.
  In strict installs, report an error before replacing the working app.
- Limit setup guidance to the dedicated development identity rather than
  changing permissions for every key in a keychain.

This does not teach the agent to enter passwords or approve system dialogs.

## Validation

Nineteen focused policy tests cover automatic keychain selection, explicit
login-keychain guidance, timeouts, strict and non-strict results, ad-hoc
fallback, signing requirements, and preservation of the installed signed app.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Keep unattended strict signing noninteractive by default.
- [x] Prefer a dedicated, reusable local-development keychain.
- [x] Preserve explicitly configured signing identities and keychains.
- [x] Bound unexpected authorization waits to 20 seconds.
- [x] Leave the installed app unchanged when strict signing cannot finish.
- [x] Scope keychain authorization guidance to the intended identity.
- [ ] Exercise the real macOS first-use and stale-key dialogs.
- [ ] Receive maintainer review for the installer behavior.

title: feat(cua-driver): add explicit window-only recording
body:
## Scope

Refs #3644. Implements the accepted window-video increment in `rfcs/3644-window-recording.md`; it does not close the broader recorder ownership/concurrency issue or duplicate #3632's trajectory attribution work.

The implementation and focused native macOS diagnostics pass at `98485717048e0b52ad1ea7e96cd551faf0909c3c`. This PR remains a draft for review and complete affected-platform certification. No merge or release is requested.

## Implementation

- Add `target: {kind: "window", pid, window_id}` to `start_recording`, requiring `record_video: true`, and equivalent `recording start DIR --video --pid PID --window-id WINDOW_ID` CLI flags.
- Validate before authorization and recorder mutation; attest the exact window for observation grants. Reject invalid/ambiguous targets and refuse unsupported backends without display or trajectory fallback.
- Write only `recording.mp4` and bounded `session.json` metadata in window mode. Suppress trajectory turns, global cursor logs, system cursor, separate agent overlay windows, audio, and microphone capture. The live input-safety overlay remains enabled.
- Use macOS 15+ ScreenCaptureKit's desktop-independent window filter, dual PID checks, fixed encoder geometry, callback-backed live state and finalization, and explicit termination on resize, scale change, close/minimize, or lost shareability. Track each native API's dimensions separately because WindowServer and ScreenCaptureKit can report different bounds.
- Keep singleton busy protection and existing daemon-wide manual stop. After automatic termination, `stop_recording` or owner teardown joins/releases the retained recorder. No-target legacy replacement behavior stays unchanged.
- Update skills and generated CLI/MCP references. Add a synthetic native test and fixture covering exact-window isolation, lifecycle, finalized MP4s, and repeated descriptor counts.

## Validation at the candidate SHA

Source and installed Local version: **0.24.0**. The source-built Local app passed strict certificate-backed signature verification and runtime source-SHA readback. Accessibility, Screen Recording, and native capture were verified on the explicitly authorized macOS host. The separate released 0.23.2 executable and its existing daemon were preserved.

- Native `exact_window_recording_isolation_and_lifecycle`: **passed all seven cases**: manual stop, two repeat recordings, minimize, close, resize, and owner disconnect. Each produced a finalized, fully decoded H.264 MP4 with no audio and exactly two recording artifacts.
- All seven recordings excluded the adjacent and occluding red sibling window while retaining the animated target. Every decoded frame passed the color-isolation oracle; frame counts matched `ffprobe`, timestamps increased, and full-brightness changing content spanned at least 1.5 seconds. Representative final-candidate frames were visually inspected.
- Movement preserved recording. Start and explicit stop/disconnect preserved the foreground PID, fixture window order, key window, and physical cursor. Wrong-PID and busy requests were rejected. Descriptor counts were 11 before native warm-up and 12 after each of the seven recordings, with no repeated growth.
- Native environment: macOS 26.6.1 build 25G76, backing scale 1, Rust 1.97.1, Swift 6.3.3, FFmpeg/FFprobe 8.1.2. A 321-by-241-point fixture produced 322-by-242-pixel video, rounding up to even encoder dimensions.
- Separate installed-CLI smoke: `recording start ... --video --pid ... --window-id ...` survived the start command's exit; `recording stop` finalized a 21.47-second H.264 MP4. All 72 decoded frame timestamps strictly increased. Before/after Driver snapshots matched the synthetic target, with no trajectory or cursor-log artifacts.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: **617 passed**.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos window_video_tests --lib`: **7 passed**.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver cli::tests::recording_`: **7 passed**.
- Non-GUI `window_recording_macos_test` checks: **2 passed**; the native case was separately executed with explicit host opt-in, as reported above.
- Release build, signed installation through `install-local.sh --release --require-stable-signing`, Swift fixture compilation, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npx tsx scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.ts --check`: passed.
- Independent integrated and focused native-geometry/test reviews completed; findings were corrected with regression coverage. Build output contains duplicate CoreMedia Swift-symbol dependency and existing dead-code warnings; successful exit is not a warning-free claim.

The fixture README contains reproducible setup, host opt-in and isolation requirements, and artifact expectations. These focused host diagnostics do not replace canonical desktop certification. Use the live PR checks for CI status at this SHA.

## Remaining proof and limitations

- Before a later ready/merge action, the maintainer must review the native evidence and run the canonical complete affected-platform matrix at the exact candidate SHA. This draft does not claim that certification.
- Native capture was exercised at scale 1 only. Retina, live scale changes, display reconfiguration, cross-process occlusion, session ownership races, permission revocation, and encoder failure recovery remain unverified by this focused lane. Shared tests cover scale arithmetic and scale-change policy.
- Windows, X11, and Wayland explicitly return `window_recording_unsupported`; this increment adds no native window-video implementation for them.
- Closing and minimizing can change native bounds before disappearance. The tested macOS animations reported `window_resized` as the first observed stop reason; the test separately confirmed close/minimize and successful finalization. A bounded terminal source fade is accepted only for those cases, without weakening foreign-color rejection.
- Shareable-content queries have a two-second deadline and recording callbacks have ten-second deadlines. The pinned `screencapturekit` 6.0.1 synchronous attach/start/stop/detach calls have no cancellation API and can still hang. This is not a hard end-to-end timeout guarantee.
- Browser chrome inside the selected window is included. Cursor compositing, tab-only capture, dynamic resizing, and independent concurrent recorders are out of scope.

title: fix(cua-driver): bind semantic snapshots to one document
body:
## Summary

Cua Driver can turn the current web page into a structured snapshot that an
agent can read and act on. Before this change, the page could navigate while a
snapshot was being assembled, leaving the text, action references, or optional
screenshot tied to different page versions.

This PR keeps the complete `semantic_v2` snapshot operation tied to one browser
tab and one set of page documents. If the main page or a collected embedded
frame changes during the operation, the Driver refuses the result instead of
publishing stale references.

## What changes

- Collect semantic content and an optional screenshot through the same browser
  connection while holding the existing per-tab operation lock.
- Check the main document and every collected embedded-frame document before
  and after collection.
- Publish only while the original session, browser target, tab, and connection
  are still current.
- Consume a continuation token only when the replacement page is successfully
  published. Two concurrent users of one token have exactly one winner.
- Include the frame and document identity in scoped references, preventing a
  matching node number from another frame from being accepted by mistake.
- Remove cancelled browser requests from the pending-response table.
- Limit embedded-frame collection to 16 frames and eight seconds, with a
  separate bounded cleanup step.

The older `dom_refs_v1` response format is unchanged.

## Validation

Deterministic tests cover navigation during first-page and continuation
collection, screenshot failure, cancellation, concurrent continuation use,
replaced targets, frame-number collisions, stale embedded frames, and bounded
cleanup. The full 625-test core suite passed after the shared frame-lifetime
change; the final cleanup-bound adjustment also passed its focused test.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Refuse a snapshot when a collected document is replaced.
- [x] Keep the screenshot and semantic data in one tab operation.
- [x] Preserve continuation tokens after cancellation or capture failure.
- [x] Allow only one successful use of a continuation token.
- [x] Bind scoped references to the exact frame and document.
- [x] Bound embedded-frame collection and cleanup.
- [ ] Run the supported installed-browser matrix at this exact commit.
- [ ] Receive maintainer review for the snapshot-lifetime contract.

title: feat(cua-driver): prototype Android background runtime and device-owned agent
body:
Android has no local Cua Driver backend. This draft adds an experimental Android 17 runtime, host/phone CLI, typed Kotlin SDK, and an Android-owned visual agent that operates selected real apps in a background virtual workspace while the main display remains usable.

Host commands use `cua-driver --device SERIAL`; authorized on-device shell commands use `cua-driver --local`. There is no `android` verb. Without an Android selector, existing desktop dispatch is unchanged. The experimental contract is separate from the stable desktop platform enum and ToolRegistry.

### Runtime and SDK

- One virtual display per leased session; allowlisted apps get owned tasks on that display. Repeated app switches preserve task identity and issue fresh target generations. A task already running outside the session is refused, including `singleTask` activities; it is never adopted from display 0.
- PNG snapshots, downscaled previews, and snapshot-bound taps/swipes. Static capture requests a genuine new producer frame by replacing the capture surface; five-second producer-frame and input-token limits remain enforced.
- Signing-identity-checked app provider/Binder transport and peer-checked shell sockets, caller/session ownership, bounded gestures, mutation deduplication, lease renewal, and cleanup of every owned task plus the virtual display. Input API acceptance remains `effect: unverifiable` and `actual_delivery: unknown` until application evidence is inspected.
- Coroutine SDK preserves request/runtime identities and distinguishes refusal, uncertainty, and cancellation. The foreground service owns renewal and preview across Activity recreation/backgrounding, exposes Stop, and handles cleanup/restart ordering. Process death falls back to lease expiry.

### Device-owned visual agent

The debug controller runs the snapshot → model decision → fresh-frame verification → SDK action loop on Android. It owns session renewal, app switching, preview, Stop and cleanup. Decisions are bounded to 40 steps/10 minutes; uncertain input stops the run. After slow inference, only exact decoded-pixel and target/display/runtime/geometry matches may bind a decision to a new input handle. Bounded extra captures accommodate blinking caret phases without masking pixels or weakening freshness.

Inference uses a loopback-only, authenticated host relay and the host's existing Claude Code authentication. The model has no shell, file, browser, Driver or MCP tools; its sole permitted formatter produces a strict action. Disconnect cancels and reaps the request's subprocess. The formatter can revise its proposal at most twice within one inference request. Earlier proposals have no side effects; only the final response is validated against the strict schema, allowlist and coordinate bounds and must equal the last formatter input. Other tools, excess proposals, invalid final responses and policy errors are refused. There is no automatic inference retry or retry of uncertain driver input.

This is a device-owned agent loop with host-relayed inference, not offline on-device inference or a system-UID app. The runtime is an explicitly authorized shell-UID helper. Raw screenshots and model evidence remain local and outside Git.

### Validation

- 42 JVM tests across runtime, SDK and demo; all four Android lint tasks pass. All APKs build, and installed APK versions/digests match the verified source builds.
- 35 relay tests cover strict final-action/tool admission, bounded formatter revisions, invalid final responses, the deadline, socket cancellation, subprocess cleanup and admission of the next request.
- Android 17/API 37 Google APIs ARM64 emulator: repeated switching between unmodified OpenCalc 3.2.1 and Tasks.org 15.10 preserves task IDs, uses one nonzero display, rejects stale handles, refreshes static frames, preserves main-display focus and destroys both tasks on Stop.
- Existing fixture smoke passes, including simultaneous synthetic display-0 text and virtual-display input, phone-local CLI, geometry/swipe/PNG, SDK preview, refusals, deduplication and lease cleanup. These checks do not establish physical-phone or human IME isolation.
- Native Stop during model inference cancels the relay request and cleans the workspace; a subsequent run is admitted. Earlier lifecycle verification covers Activity recreation, 65 seconds of service-owned background preview/renewal, notification Stop and process-death cleanup.
- Actual model-driven two-app run on candidate `0d8de736829970dc5bb6d016944a8be021ef72b2`: a 129-second continuous capture records 15 model decisions and 14 renewals. Independent image inspection confirms OpenCalc result 42, the matching snack-pack task checked/struck through in Tasks.org, and the venue task left unchecked. Synthetic main-display text/focus survives; both tasks and the virtual display are removed. The real CLI exercises formatter revisions successfully. A prior single-app run also computed 42. Recordings and model evidence remain local; model-declared `done` alone is not treated as task proof.

### Scope and remaining gates

Phase 1 local experiment; keep draft. Accessibility/semantic text, raw keys and human IME isolation, ordinary app/Termux UIDs, physical-phone/vendor-image qualification, general application coverage, streaming, stable API/authorization integration and Fleet work remain open. No Fleet changes or deployment are included. Full desktop certification remains a readiness/merge gate; Android fixtures and recordings do not replace it.

Setup, SDK examples, real-app provenance links, and reproducible harness commands: [Android README](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/feat/cua-driver-android-local/libs/cua-driver/android/README.md).

Refs #3673

title: feat(cua-driver-bench): import public benchmark runtime and tooling
body:
## Summary

- import an allowlisted Cua Driver Bench snapshot into the public monorepo without its private Git history
- add the `cua-bench-runtime` package and collision-free `cua_bench_runtime` / `cdb` names
- add schemas, synthetic conformance material, profiles, calibration, and Jainish Patel's automated driver-comparison runner
- add Diátaxis documentation, CODEOWNERS, documentation-link coverage, and Python 3.11–3.13 CI

## Public boundary

This PR excludes executable benchmark tasks, private manifests, task fixtures, hidden evaluators, expected-state definitions, oracles, datasets, releases, results, traces, screenshots, and evidence.

The public runtime contains generic protected-execution apparatus, but no task-specific protected mediator. An authorized task pack or prepared seed must provide the task application, launch contract, and mediator. CDB task IDs appear only as opaque selectors in the comparison runner; the public runtime and tests contain no held-out target or end-state values.

The comparison runner requires an explicit `--tasks-root`; it does not search private or machine-specific locations.

## Source and attribution

Source snapshot: `trycua/cua-driver-bench@a820570ae02844d3615e784dfc366df16183701c`

The automated driver-comparison runner is adapted from `trycua/cua-driver-bench#58`, authored by Jainish Patel. The import commit preserves his credit with both `Salvaged from trycua/cua-driver-bench#58` and a GitHub-linked `Co-authored-by` trailer.

See `benchmarks/cua-driver-bench/PROVENANCE.md` and the public-boundary ADR for the complete import policy.

## Validation

Validated on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13:

- repository schema suite: valid
- runtime: 388 tests and 307 subtests passed per Python version
- synthetic runtime conformance: passed per Python version
- documentation links: passed per Python version
- automated-eval runner: 37 tests and two subtests passed per Python version
- Ruff lint and format checks: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

Packaging validation on Python 3.13:

- built both wheel and source distribution
- confirmed all 87 schema-data files are present in the wheel
- installed the wheel into a clean virtual environment
- imported `cua_bench_runtime` from `site-packages`
- passed installed `cdb validate --json`

The proposed tree was also scanned for protected task vocabulary, private machine paths, credential patterns, binaries, symlinks, and generated build artifacts.

title: Windows recorder intermittently reports failed FFmpeg finalization during native E2E preflight
body:
## Verified failure

The production stop_recording operation reports failed FFmpeg finalization during Windows native preflight. The harness correctly stops before native behavior rows. This predates #3706/#3704:

- Main bd4c10020cd7cac07c0d19b0f53ba4b007fbcb15 failed: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34306620850/job/102324572423
- The identical main SHA later passed the native lane: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34307741070/job/102327857162
- Stack candidate 603d50e6bc76d5cb0538f827b536c4d21f47c6ae failed with the same signature: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34499846099/job/102947618595

The recorder backend, recording manager, preflight test, and FFmpeg setup script are byte-identical across baseline and failing candidate. Both failures used FFmpeg 9.0.1 through the Chocolatey shim. Retained MP4s are nonempty and have moov boxes, but that does not override the failed finalization contract or prove valid recordings.

## Unknown cause

FfmpegVideoBackend::stop ignores stdin write/flush errors and collapses a nonzero child exit or its three-second shutdown timeout into finalized=false. The retained stderr tail is empty. We cannot distinguish a recorder bug, shim/process behavior, or environmental timing from these logs alone. Do not attribute this to Session 0 or weaken the video gate.

## Selected investigation

Maintainer requested attribution and root-cause diagnosis. Run a bounded diagnostic on a GitHub-hosted interactive Windows runner, preserving every result. Compare identical FFmpeg arguments and production shutdown timing via the Chocolatey shim versus the underlying executable, recording stdin errors, exit status, shutdown elapsed time, and forced termination. If needed, follow with product-boundary instrumentation. This is diagnostic evidence, not certification or retry-to-green.

Acceptance: identify the failing shutdown path with observable evidence, then scope a focused regression/fix without mixing it into the macOS consent or overlay changes. Track readiness impact on #3704 and #3706.

title: fix(cua-driver): reject mismatched native window pixel geometry
body:
CUA-3283. Refs #3631.

## Why

On macOS, a window's native logical frame and its compositor frame can disagree, for example during Stage Manager transitions. Pixel coordinates taken from a screenshot then land in the wrong place. With this change the driver samples native window geometry around capture and refuses pixel targeting when the two frames really disagree. Semantic (AX) actions keep working.

## What changed

- `cua-driver-core::native_window_geometry`: a shared model that sorts a window into aligned, mismatched, unstable or unavailable from bounded samples under a shared metadata budget. Only a confirmed mismatch vetoes pointer input.
- `platform-macos`: an exact-window native probe, wired into `get_window_state` and the `px_frame` resolver. Every pixel tool (`click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `move_cursor`, and the pixel focus path of `press_key` and `hotkey`) checks geometry before any reveal, activation or cursor move. A mismatch returns `code=native_window_geometry_mismatch`, `effect=refused`.
- Contract, bindings and tests: optional geometry metadata on window state, plus AppKit fixture cells for background and foreground mismatch, pixel key focus, pixel focus latency and snapshot publication. The cells are registered in `scripts/ci/macos/appkit-cells.tsv`.

## Scope

Only macOS supplies native evidence. Linux and Windows adapters report geometry as unassessed and behave as before. There is no minimum-size heuristic, no automatic activation, no geometry cache and no blanket veto on semantic actions.

This update merges main again. Main now has `scripts/ci/macos/appkit-cells.tsv` and its runner from #7229, which this PR had introduced too, so the PR keeps main's runner and adds its six AppKit rows to the table. Main's check that every ignored AppKit test has a row now also reads the `native_geometry` and `pixel_focus_latency` test modules. The focus-click and AX-click error paths keep main's security-prompt refusal and settle polling as well as this PR's geometry refusal.

The latest main merge brings in #8081, which runs a pixel-targeted `hotkey` through a background menu key equivalent. The geometry check for a pixel `hotkey` now runs before that route, and the shared web-content focus lookup (`web_ax_focus_point`) refuses on a mismatch instead of silently dropping the focus point. The menu route makes the window key only after that lookup.

Review fixes on top of that merge: `resolve_window_px_frame` now reports a confirmed mismatch ahead of a capture failure; `get_window_state` samples geometry around main's prefetched screenshot and reports that assessment when the prefetched image is the one delivered; and a native scroll button whose first press fails falls back to the wheel again, as on main. A focus click that refuses after `hotkey` made the window key leaves no change behind: `WindowKeyScope` hands key back on drop. The key window still has to be taken before the focus click, as on main.

Size-limit reason: the shared geometry model and the macOS probe have to cover every pointer route for the refusal to hold.

## Blast radius

This affects macOS pixel-targeted tools. When a window's frames disagree, the caller now gets a refusal instead of a mis-aimed event. Windows whose geometry is aligned, unstable or unavailable go through the existing route checks unchanged.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks passed at the head before the latest main merge:

- fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, and tests for cua-driver, cua-driver-contract, cua-driver-core, cua-driver-e2e, cua-driver-sdk, cua-driver-testkit and platform-macos
- the contract and UniFFI binding checks, SPDX headers, the `.github/scripts` tests and the TypeScript typecheck

In the macOS Lume lane, at the head before this main merge, three focused cells passed: `macos-appkit-native-geometry-mismatch-px-background`, `macos-appkit-native-geometry-mismatch-px-foreground` and `macos-appkit-pixel-key-focus-px-foreground`. The two mismatch cells passed as the expected refusals. They were not rerun after the merge; the merge touched only the error paths around them, and macOS CI covers the build.

After the latest main merge: rustfmt, the quick repository checks, the contract regeneration and the UniFFI binding regeneration ran on Linux. The macOS crate cannot be compiled on that host, so macOS CI covers its build.

At head `8dc22748f584f9aacc15da9410ef96760917806b`, GitHub CI is green, including macOS clippy and unit tests, the hosted macOS E2E lane and `ci-gate`.

- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`): not ticked. The host that ran this update ran only `bin/ci --quick` (7 passed, 6 skipped as heavy). It cannot build platform-macos, so it cannot produce a sign-off run with no skipped checks.

Not run: the full macOS matrix, standalone browsers, and the Linux desktop and Windows lanes.

title: RFC: Bounded native held input for state-polled desktop apps
body:
## User problem

State-polled desktop applications need sustained input. CUA Driver currently exposes key taps but no bounded held-key operation in its native SDK/MCP contract. In a real Chocolate Doom/Freedoom session, menu navigation worked while short keyboard taps produced little movement and no confirmed firing. Successful input delivery alone does not establish that the application's command sampling observed the held state.

This is distinct from the X11 event delivery/timing defect in #3708 / #3709. It also differs from the process-level macOS pacing knob in #3489. RFC #2794 covers sequential desktop action composition and explicitly excludes raw held-button operations.

## Proposed contract for discussion

Add one bounded native held-input operation for a supported desktop target (window, element, and background targets are explicitly outside the initial scope). It would hold a small validated set of keys/buttons simultaneously for a strictly bounded duration, then release them. Existing tap defaults remain unchanged. Unsupported backends or target scopes must refuse explicitly and must not advertise support.

The native operation must own release on success, partial acquisition failure, cancellation, and session teardown. Client-side down/sleep/up calls are insufficient because asynchronous cancellation can leave blocking platform work running. Shared native ownership should serialize conflicting seat input; backend adapters provide the transitions.

A linked RFC document PR will specify the proposed bounds, cancellation semantics, capability discovery, platform limitations, and validation. This issue requests the repository's recorded RFC decision before public SDK/MCP implementation.

## Acceptance evidence proposed

- Native tests observe held state for the requested interval and released state after cancellation/error.
- SDL-style state-polling fixtures prove taps and holds behave differently without relying only on event counts.
- A real game smoke confirms visible movement, ammunition reduction on firing, and opening a reachable door through CUA controls.
- Generated SDK/MCP contracts and runtime capability reporting agree for every supported platform.

No indefinite raw down/up API, game autoplay, application-specific cheats, or package release is proposed here.

Proposal document: #3759 (pending review and decision).

title: Preserve the configured HTTP timeout for commands without a server timeout
body:
Local and cloud Sandbox users of HTTPTransport can wait indefinitely on a stalled computer-server command despite configuring a finite timeout. All /cmd operations without a server-side timeout are affected. PTY routes and the separate FleetTransport implementation are outside this fix.

At `libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/transport/http.py:97`:

The constructor saves timeout in self._timeout and connect passes it to httpx.AsyncClient at lines 55 and 68. In _cmd, requests without params['timeout'] take `req_timeout = None  # use client default`, then line 101 explicitly passes `timeout=req_timeout`. HTTPX defines an explicit timeout=None as disabling all timeout phases, not inheriting the client default. Thus get_screen_size, screenshot, and ordinary send calls discard the configured timeout. Root cause: confusing HTTPX's omitted request option with its explicit timeout-disabling value. Existing test_transport_http_retry.py:117 manually raises ReadTimeout and never inspects the request timeout configuration, so it cannot catch this defect. The upstream diff for merged PR 1355 introduces this exact branch rather than fixing it.

## Proposed fix

In transport/http.py, omit the per-request timeout keyword when no server timeout is present, or supply the configured finite timeout rather than None. Preserve the existing read-timeout override when a server timeout is supplied. Add focused request-extension assertions in tests/test_transport_http_retry.py for ordinary commands and the server-timeout branch, closing clients in the new tests. No retry policy or public signature change is needed.

## How to see it

Unexecuted deterministic regression plan: extend tests/test_transport_http_retry.py using its _make_transport helper, which configures an actual httpx.AsyncClient with timeout=5.0 and MockTransport. Capture request.extensions['timeout'] in the mock handler while awaiting t._cmd('get_screen_size'), and close t in finally. Expect connect/read/write/pool values all equal 5.0. The current code deterministically produces None for all four phases because it passes timeout=None. Parameterize no params and ordinary params without timeout. Add a server-timeout case with params={'timeout': 60}, expecting read=70 and the other phases=5, to preserve the existing extension behavior. No network or timing-dependent sleep is needed. This is a source-and-library-contract trace, not a claim that tests were run.

If this looks right I can push `fix/sandbox-http-default-timeout` on `anxkhn/cua` instead of opening a pull request first.

title: Roll back opened tunnels when a multi-port acquisition fails
body:
Users forwarding multiple ports through one await or async context retain earlier successful port forwards when a later acquisition fails. Callers receive no TunnelInfo result with which to close those resources. SSH listeners remain until broader transport teardown, while ADB forwarding rules require explicit removal. The shared interface affects every resource-owning tunnel transport.

At `libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/interfaces/tunnel.py:69`:

_TunnelContext._open opens each port sequentially and appends each successful TunnelInfo to self._infos at lines 68-71, without an exception cleanup path. __aenter__ directly awaits _open at line 82. If the second forward_tunnel raises, context entry never completes and __aexit__ is not called, so the first tunnel is never closed. The plain-await path at line 65 has the same failure. Actual resource owners exist: transport/adb.py:222 allocates an ADB forward and line 230 removes it only through close_tunnel; transport/ssh.py:119 starts a listener and line 132 stops it through close_tunnel. Root cause: partial acquisition cleanup is deferred to an exit method that cannot run after failed entry.

## Proposed fix

Add rollback around the acquisition loop in interfaces/tunnel.py. On failure or cancellation, attempt to close every handle acquired by that attempt, clear successfully released handles and their closers, and re-raise the original acquisition exception. Do not let one cleanup failure prevent attempts to release the remaining handles. Add tests/test_tunnel.py with fake-transport regression cases for async-with, plain await, cancellation after one successful acquisition, and successful acquisition/exit. Keep existing backend allocation behavior unchanged.

## How to see it

Unexecuted deterministic test plan: use a fake transport whose first forward_tunnel returns TunnelInfo('localhost', 45001, 9222) and whose second call raises RuntimeError('second forward failed'). Record close_tunnel calls. Execute async with Tunnel(fake).forward(9222, 8080) under pytest.raises and assert the body never runs and the first TunnelInfo is closed exactly once. Current trace leaves the close-call list empty; after rollback it contains the first handle. Parameterize the same test for plain await. Add a cancellation case that cancels while the second acquisition awaits an event, after the first handle has been recorded; require cleanup and propagation of CancelledError. No sockets, commands, ADB process, or remote sandbox are necessary.

If this looks right I can push `fix/sandbox-tunnel-acquisition-cleanup` on `anxkhn/cua` instead of opening a pull request first.

title: Match the computer-server WebSocket command and response envelopes
body:
Sandbox users connecting to computer-server over WebSocket cannot use ordinary parameterized commands correctly and can receive None or empty screenshot bytes from successful responses. HTTP uses the correct nested command parameters and shared screenshot decoder, so changing transport breaks the same SDK interfaces.

At `libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/transport/websocket.py:49`:

WebSocketTransport.send sends `{'command': action, **params}` and returns only resp.get('result'). The actual server reads `params = data.get('params', {})` in computer_server/main.py:707 and sends `{'success': True, **result}` at line 732, without wrapping handler results in a result field. For read_text, GenericFileHandler.read_text requires path at handlers/generic.py:325, so the flattened path is discarded and the handler raises a missing-argument error. Even a parameterless successful response such as {'success': True, 'exists': True} loses its fields in send. screenshot has the same envelope mismatch at websocket.py:56: it reads result/screenshot and ignores the image_data field returned by the current handlers. Root cause: the SDK WebSocket adapter implements a different wire shape from the computer-server endpoint it targets. Public Sandbox.connect accepts ws_url at sandbox.py:720, and the transport selector returns WebSocketTransport at line 1913.

## Proposed fix

Correct command serialization and response extraction in transport/websocket.py to match the existing computer-server protocol. Preserve unwrapped handler fields, consistently raise explicit remote errors, and reuse transport/computer_server.py's screenshot and screen-size normalization helpers where appropriate. Add tests/test_transport_websocket.py with in-memory socket contract tests for nested params, successful response fields, screenshot bytes, screen size, and remote errors. Do not change the server protocol or expand this fix into authentication or reconnect behavior.

## How to see it

Unexecuted wire-contract test plan: inject an in-memory socket into WebSocketTransport._ws. Its send method records decoded JSON and its recv method supplies current server-shaped responses. Call send('read_text', path='/tmp/example.txt'); assert the outgoing message is {'command': 'read_text', 'params': {'path': '/tmp/example.txt'}} and that {'success': True, 'content': 'hello'} yields a result containing content='hello'. Current code flattens path and returns None. Supply screenshot response {'success': True, 'image_data': base64.b64encode(b'example-image').decode()} and assert screenshot() returns b'example-image'; current code returns b''. Include a server error response and assert it is raised rather than decoded as an empty screenshot. The server's read/dispatch/write lines independently establish these fixture shapes. No live connection or desktop interaction is required.

If this looks right I can push `fix/sandbox-websocket-command-envelopes` on `anxkhn/cua` instead of opening a pull request first.

title: Report directory entries accurately when list_dir returns names
body:
Remote Sandbox directory traversal and file browsers using FileEntry.is_dir misclassify every directory returned by GenericFileHandler. Code that recurses only into directories skips subtrees, while code that downloads entries classified as files tries to read directories. Entries returned with explicit metadata are not affected.

At `libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/interfaces/files.py:66`:

Files.list converts every string item to `FileEntry(name=item, path=f"{path.rstrip('/')}/{item}", is_dir=False)`. This is the normal server response, not a hypothetical legacy shape: computer_server/handlers/generic.py:318 returns a files array of p.name for both p.is_file() and p.is_dir(). Thus a real subdirectory is always exposed as is_dir=False by the Sandbox SDK. Files.is_dir already implements the directory_exists operation at files.py:51, and the server implements it at generic.py:290. Root cause: treating absent metadata in a name-only listing as a definitive file classification.

## Proposed fix

In Files.list, resolve is_dir for name-only entries through the existing remote Files.is_dir operation instead of hardcoding False. Keep the dictionary-entry fast path and the current wire protocol unchanged. Add tests/test_files.py with mixed file/directory listings, empty listings, trailing separators, and metadata-bearing entries. Do not add a new server response format or infer remote file types from the local host filesystem.

## How to see it

Unexecuted focused regression plan: use a fake transport returning {'success': True, 'files': ['subdir', 'note.txt']} for list_dir('/work'), and returning exists=True only for directory_exists('/work/subdir'). Await Files(fake).list('/work'). Expect subdir.is_dir=True and note.txt.is_dir=False. Current code never requests directory metadata and returns False for both. Add a trailing-slash case and retain coverage for an empty listing and dictionary entries that already include is_dir, verifying the latter do not incur metadata lookups. These fixtures follow the actual GenericFileHandler listing and directory_exists response contracts.

If this looks right I can push `fix/sandbox-directory-entry-types` on `anxkhn/cua` instead of opening a pull request first.

title: [Bug]: macOS window-scoped snapshots list the application's menu bar rows, but every action on them is refused with `element_outside_target_window`
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`get_window_state` on macOS deliberately keeps the application's `AXMenuBar` in a window snapshot (it is the first step of the documented two-snapshot menu flow), but the background-input gate requires an addressed element to prove ancestry to the requested window. A menu bar cannot: it is process-scoped, carries no CGWindowID, and its `AXParent` chain reaches `AXApplication` without passing an `AXWindow`. Every menu row the snapshot surfaces is therefore refused, and the refusal's advice ("take a fresh snapshot and re-address it") can never be satisfied.

### Reproduction

1. Open TextEdit with one document window; note `pid` and `window_id`.
2. `get_window_state` with `include_accessibility_tree: true`; find the `AXMenuBarItem` row titled "Format" (it is listed with `actions: ["AXPress"]` and an `element_token`).
3. `click` that `element_token` against the same `pid`/`window_id` with `delivery_mode: "background"`.
4. Take a fresh snapshot as the refusal suggests and repeat step 3 with the new token.

### Expected behavior

The semantic AX action (`AXPress`) on a menu bar item that belongs to the requested window's own process is admitted; the menu opens. Window-aimed routes (routed pointer, process keyboard) may still refuse, since a stamped pointer event cannot be aimed at a row that lives outside every window. When an element does belong to a different window, the refusal should name that window so the caller can re-target it.

### Actual behavior

Both attempts return `code: "element_outside_target_window"` with the re-snapshot advice, for every `AXMenuBarItem` the snapshot advertises as actionable. `invoke_menu` works because it resolves the path itself. The refusal also never says which window the element does belong to.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.0 (`cua-driver-rs-v0.28.0`, e7e141ae)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: TextEdit (any AppKit app)

### Evidence

`platform-macos/src/ax/window_scope.rs` keeps `AXMenuBar` in the top-level candidate set for window snapshots ("dropping AXMenuBar here would remove" the two-snapshot menu flow) while `cua-driver-core/src/background_input.rs::decide_background_input` admits only `ElementAncestry::ProvenDescendant` of the requested window. `platform-macos/src/ax/exact_target.rs::element_window_id` resolves ancestry through `AXWindow` / `_AXUIElementGetWindow`, which a menu bar never satisfies, so `gather_background_facts` classifies every menu row as `Unproven` and the gate refuses it.

### Workaround and additional context

Use `invoke_menu` with the full path. Related: #2645 (bound state and actions to the requested window; the gate this hits), #2788 (`invoke_menu` exact focus), #3301 (RFC on coordinate-free menu-extra invocation, a different surface), #3351 / #3353 (the same class of refusal for sheets, handled separately).

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): let semantic actions reach an app's own menu bar
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: every menu-bar row a macOS window snapshot surfaced was refused as outside the target window, with advice to re-snapshot that could never be satisfied (#3792).
- What changed: a semantic action on the application's own menu bar is admitted when the addressed window is where the process directs its input, refused with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` naming the focused window otherwise, and reported `unverifiable` after dispatch.

<details><summary>Mechanism and measurements</summary>

- `ElementAncestry::ProvenAppMenu` in `cua-driver-core/src/background_input.rs` proves the fact that does exist: the element ascends to the requested process's own `AXMenuBar`. `decide_background_input` admits it for `AxSemantic` only.
- Review round 1 (f-trycua, 2026-09-13): admission needed the focused-window guard the process-scoped keyboard route already implied. `process_directs_input_at_target` is now one predicate shared by both routes; the keyboard route gains the same focused-window escape, so a two-window process no longer refuses when the requested window is the proven focused one. Facts carry the focused window id from `ax::bindings::focused_window_id_of_pid`, the reader `bring_to_front` and `invoke_menu` already trust; unreadable focus fails closed.
- Sheet remediation: `ax::exact_target::foreign_window_ancestry` verifies acquirability against the layer-0 listing; a sheet resolves to an id that listing cannot return, so `ElementAncestry::OutsideUnacquirableSurface` names the condition and points at the presenting window, with no id.
- The `ProvenAppMenu` refusal arm has its own advice instead of sharing `Unproven`'s "re-observe" text; no gate change.
- Gate matrix: two same-app windows with the addressed one not focused (refused, reason names the focused window), focused (admitted), single-window process (admitted), the keyboard route on a proven focused window, the listing lookup behind the sheet refusal.
- Native producer: `harness_appkit_app_menu_row_is_admitted_and_reported_unverifiable` snapshots the AppKit harness window, fronts it (the fixture gates its Window-menu command on `NSApp.isActive && window.isKeyWindow`), presses the `menu-window-arrange-left` row through `click` and asserts `{"delivery":{"mode":"background"},"effect":"unverifiable","route":"accessibility"}` with the fixture recording `menu_action=window_arrange_left`, so `element_is_app_menu_descendant` and `classify_foreign_ancestry` run against a real AX tree. It sits in the AppKit allowlist of `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh` next to `harness_appkit_invoke_menu_live_path` and goes through `run_case` and the installed candidate daemon. The released driver refuses the same press with `element_outside_target_window`.
- Non-goal: window-aimed routes still require window ancestry; a menu action is never reported confirmed. Foreign-window refusals name a CGWindowID only when `list_windows` can serve it; a sheet names the condition and the presenting window instead.

**Rebased onto main `c5ee191c0`.** #4144 moved the harness case into `crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/`; it is selected by `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh` in the same commit. #4116 deleted `scroll::tests::exact_target_refusal_prevents_ax_reveal`, which this PR had only adapted to the new `OutsideTargetWindow` fields, so that edit is gone. The sibling-window and sheet refusal tests now assert `element_outside_target_window` before the wording.

**Mutation checks** at this head, each reverted afterwards: the `ProvenAppMenu` admission arm disabled fails `proven_app_menu_ancestry_admits_only_semantic_ax` and `app_menu_action_requires_the_process_to_direct_input_at_the_addressed_window`; dropping the focused-window escape from `process_directs_input_at_target` fails `process_scoped_keyboard_admits_the_proven_focused_window`; making it always true fails the app-menu guard test; the sibling-window refusal code swapped fails `sibling_window_refusal_names_the_window_the_element_belongs_to`; `foreign_window_ancestry` naming an unlisted surface by id fails `a_surface_missing_from_the_listing_is_never_named_by_id`, and matching any listed window fails `a_listed_sibling_window_is_named_with_its_owner`. The harness case is not hermetic; its before-proof is #3792's refusal on main.

**Supporting evidence (local `harness.sh`, pre-rebase head `5230ec1d2`, not re-run at this head).** AppKit harness (`mcp --direct`) through the installed daemon `com.ohmypi.cua-driver/OMP Computer Use` on macOS 26.1, driver built from this head (binary sha256 prefix `30bff9e346be`): 21/24 cells. title: [Feature]: expose the document path and unsaved-changes state of a macOS document window on `get_window_state`
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

An agent editing a document window cannot tell from a snapshot which file the window represents or whether the application is holding unsaved changes. Both facts are one AX attribute read away on the window element `get_window_state` has already resolved (`AXDocument` on the window, `AXEdited` on its close button), but neither is surfaced, so the agent infers "is this the right file" and "did that edit register" from the title string, which is app-specific, or from the close button's dot in a screenshot.

This matters for `set_value`. On TextEdit (macOS 26.1 arm64, driver built from `main`), an AX `set_value` on the text area puts the new text into the AX tree, the file on disk stays byte-identical, and the dirty flag stays `false`; nothing in the response tells the agent that its edit will not survive a close.

### Desired outcome

`get_window_state` on macOS reports, when the application provides them:

- `document_path`: the file URL from `AXDocument` on the window.
- `document_edited`: the boolean `AXEdited` state. AppKit mirrors `NSWindow.isDocumentEdited` on the window's close button; the window element itself answers `kAXErrorAttributeUnsupported`.

Each key is omitted when the app reports nothing, so an absent key means "unknown", never "clean". The two reads are per window (not per element) and bounded by the same per-request AX messaging timeout as the rest of the walk.

### Current workaround

Parse the window title for "Edited" (TextEdit) or a leading dot/asterisk (editors); or open the File menu and read whether Save is enabled. Neither is reliable across apps.

### Affected components and platforms

`cua-driver` macOS backend (`platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs`, `tools/get_window_state.rs`), the shared window-snapshot helpers in `cua-driver-core`, and the `WindowStateOutput` contract (two additive optional fields, manifest and generated SDK records regenerated). Windows exposes no equivalent through UIA and Linux exposes none through AT-SPI, so the keys are simply absent there.

### Alternatives and prior art

- Title parsing (above).
- `verify_state` cannot express "document is clean" today because nothing in the snapshot carries the bit.
- Apple documents `AXDocument` for document windows and `AXEdited` on the close button.

### Implementation ideas

Two attribute reads on the resolved target window during the existing AX walk, emitted as optional fields; document on `set_value` and on `get_window_state` that an AX value write never reaches disk and is not guaranteed to register as an edit, and that `document_edited` plus the app's own save action is what makes an edit durable. A pull request follows.

title: [Feature]: identify the captured display on `get_screen_size` and `get_desktop_state`
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

A caller that maps desktop-scope coordinates onto a desktop screenshot has to trust that two consecutive `get_screen_size`/`get_desktop_state` results describe the same physical display. Today the only identity is `width x height x scale_factor`. Two same-sized displays, a display swap (mirroring toggled, the primary reassigned, a monitor hot-plugged) or a session whose primary moved to a non-zero global origin all produce results that look identical, so a cached transform is silently applied to the wrong pixels. #3630 shows the same failure from the multi-client side: a transform replaced underneath an earlier screenshot causes a wrong-position click.

On multi-monitor Windows and Linux hosts the primary display is not necessarily at global `(0, 0)` (#1981, #2992 show negative-X layouts), and nothing in the result says where the captured display sits.

### Desired outcome

Both results carry, when the platform can supply them:

- `display_identity: { uuid, native_id }`: the operating system's stable display identifier (`CGDisplayCreateUUIDFromDisplayID` on macOS) and the current native handle (`CGDirectDisplayID`), so a caller can detect "same size, different source" and "same display, re-plugged".
- `screen_origin: { x, y }`: the display's origin in global logical coordinates (top-left on macOS).

Absent fields mean the backend cannot prove identity; a caller then treats desktop coordinates as unverified rather than assuming `(0, 0)`.

### Current workaround

Compare `width/height/scale_factor` and hope. Some clients re-capture before every desktop action to avoid the stale transform.

### Affected components and platforms

`cua-driver-contract` (`ScreenSizeOutput`, `DesktopStateOutput`: two additive optional records), `cua-driver-core` (forward the fields when the platform emits them), `platform-macos` (main display). Windows and Linux would omit the fields until they can prove identity (RANDR/XRandR output id and origin on X11; per-output identity on Wayland is already part of the Hyprland work).

### Alternatives and prior art

- Per-call `display` selectors exist in the request shape but do not identify what was captured.
- #3630 (screenshot transform replaced by another client; the tracked fix owns the transform alongside snapshot identity, which still needs a display identity to key on).
- #3326/#3328 added `scale_factor` correctness for Retina; this is the same class of "what did I capture" metadata.

### Implementation ideas

macOS: read `CGMainDisplayID`, its UUID and `CGDisplayBounds` once per call and refuse to emit identity if the display changed between the size read and the bounds read (same-size source replacement during a read). Core: forward `display_identity` and `screen_origin` only when the platform supplies both. This adds two optional records to a public contract; if maintainers consider that an RFC-level decision rather than an additive field change (as #3328 was), I will move it to the RFC form before opening a pull request.

title: install-local.sh --require-stable-signing rejects a trusted local certificate and fails on a freshly generated key
body:
`install-local.sh --require-stable-signing` refuses to install on a macOS host for two independent reasons, and both surface as the same message, so neither is diagnosable from the output:

```
warning: the requested stable identity produced a non-certificate designated requirement
Error: stable macOS signing is required, but no usable certificate-backed identity was available.
The live installation was not changed.
```

## 1. A trust-anchored local certificate is classified as non-certificate-backed

`classify_designated_requirement` in `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_local-signing.sh` treats a designated requirement as certificate-backed only when it contains `certificate leaf`. But codesign spells a certificate pin two ways, and which one you get depends on keychain trust, not on chain length:

```
# a self-signed certificate that is imported but not marked trusted
$ codesign --force --keychain <scratch> --sign <sha1> probe && codesign -d -r- probe
designated => identifier probe and certificate leaf = H"<sha1>"

# the same shape of certificate, marked trusted, so it evaluates as its own anchor
$ codesign --force --sign <sha1> probe2 && codesign -d -r- probe2
designated => identifier probe2 and certificate root = H"<sha1>"
```

A developer whose local signing identity is trusted therefore gets no install at all, even though the `certificate root` pin is exactly as stable across rebuilds as the leaf pin, which is the property `--require-stable-signing` exists to guarantee for TCC. Only a cdhash pin is rebuild-fragile.

`validate_history_app_signature` in `crates/cua-driver/src/history_runtime.rs` makes the same leaf-only assumption, so even with the installer fixed, `--experimental-history` would reject a trust-anchored local app as not certificate-backed.

There is a third site with the same assumption: `libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh` greps `codesign -d -r-` output for `certificate leaf` and exits 1 otherwise. That runner targets the Lume golden image, whose identity is untrusted, so it is not currently affected.

## 2. The generated signing key is never authorized for codesign

`ensure_local_signing_identity` imports its generated p12 with `security import -A -T /usr/bin/codesign`, but never runs `security set-key-partition-list`. Since macOS 10.12 the ACL from `-T` is not sufficient on its own: the private key's partition list stays closed, so the first `codesign` against the certificate the script just created either raises a GUI keychain-password prompt or, in a non-interactive shell, fails with `errSecInternalComponent`. The installer then reports "no usable certificate-backed identity was available" for a certificate that exists and is perfectly good.

Reproduced by running the identity bootstrap into a scratch keychain and signing with the resulting identity in a non-interactive shell.

Opening the partition list requires the keychain password, which only the developer has, so the script cannot do it unconditionally. A reasonable fix is to honour an explicitly exported keychain password when present and otherwise print the exact `security set-key-partition-list` command, rather than letting codesign fail opaquely.

### Environment

macOS 26.1 on Apple silicon, installer script from current `main`, `install-local.sh --release --require-stable-signing`.

title: [Bug]: macOS fullscreen app exposes agent cursor during background computer use
body:
## Bug description

When a user is focused on a fullscreen macOS app, Cua Driver background computer-use actions against another app are not visually isolated. A floating agent cursor appears over the foreground fullscreen app, and it is unclear whether the action is actually being delivered to the intended background target.

In the observed use case, the background target is the Notch app.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS, open an app in fullscreen mode and keep it focused.
2. Use Cua Driver to perform a computer-use action against another app in the background (for example, click a control in the Notch app).
3. Observe the fullscreen app and the target app's resulting state.

## Expected behavior

- Computer-use actions are delivered to the intended background app without changing the user's current fullscreen app or Space.
- The agent cursor does not float over or interfere visually with the foreground fullscreen app.
- The driver provides a reliable indication that the background action succeeded or failed.

## Actual behavior

- A floating agent cursor appears on top of the foreground fullscreen app.
- It is ambiguous whether the click is delivered successfully to the intended background target.

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- Foreground state: another app focused in fullscreen mode
- Background target in the observed case: Notch app

## Acceptance criteria

- Background actions remain correctly routed while an unrelated fullscreen app is focused.
- The agent cursor overlay does not appear over the unrelated fullscreen app.
- Action results can be verified without switching focus or Spaces.

title: [Bug]: generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs resolves the SDK library under `rust/target/release`, ignoring CARGO_TARGET_DIR
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs` builds `cua-driver-sdk` with cargo and then passes a hand-built path under `rust/target/release` as `--library` to both generators. Cargo honours `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, the script does not, so whenever a contributor or CI builds with a target directory outside the tree the script either fails with `missing built SDK library` or, worse, silently generates bindings from whatever stale library still sits in `rust/target/release`.

The second case is the dangerous one: it produces bindings that do not correspond to the branch being built, and `--check` then reports them as up to date.

### Reproduction

1. `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/some-target`
2. `node libs/cua-driver/scripts/generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check`
3. Repeat with a `rust/target/release/libcua_driver_sdk.dylib` left behind by an earlier build of a different branch.

### Expected behavior

The script resolves the library from the same target directory cargo just used (`cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq -r .target_directory`, or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`), and fails loudly if the file it finds was not produced by the build it just ran.

### Actual behavior

Step 2 aborts with `missing built SDK library …/rust/target/release/…` although the build succeeded. Step 3 completes and reports the bindings as current, having generated them from the other branch's library. We hit exactly this while preparing per-PR branches in separate worktrees with private target directories: the script consumed a sibling worktree's binary.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs` at `31c2184f8`
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: n/a

### Evidence

`generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs::nativeLibraryPath` composes the path from `rustRoot` plus `target/release`, and the `existsSync` guard after the cargo build only proves that *some* library exists there.

### Workaround and additional context

Unset `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for this script and delete `rust/target` afterwards, which is what we do per PR branch today.

title: [Feature]: report AXHelp and AXDescription on macOS `get_window_state` elements
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

A caller reading `structuredContent.elements`, the side `get_window_state` tells it to prefer, cannot see an element's `AXHelp` or `AXDescription`. The walk reads both (`platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs::walk_element`) and renders them into the markdown (`platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs::format_node_line`), but each structured row carries only a derived `label` that collapses title, description, value and identifier into one string (`platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs::build_elements_array_with_token`). Two things are lost:

- An icon-only or toolbar button whose only human-readable identity is its tooltip arrives as a row with a role, a frame and no name.
- A control that has both a title and a description keeps the title and drops the description entirely.

Concretely, Calendar puts an event's calendar membership in `AXHelp` and Reminders puts "mark completed" on the completion toggle. An agent deciding between a completion toggle and an open action on the structured side has nothing to decide on, so it falls back to grepping `tree_markdown` or guessing which row it wants.

### Desired outcome

Each element row reports, when the application provides it:

- `help`: the `AXHelp` string.
- `description`: the `AXDescription` string, omitted when it is already the row's `label` so the payload does not repeat itself.

Both keys are omitted when the app reports nothing, so an absent key means "the app said nothing". No new accessibility traffic is needed: the walk already has both values on the node, they are simply dropped on the way into the structured array.

### Current workaround

Parse `tree_markdown`, where the description renders as `(description)` and the tooltip as `help="..."` inside the bracketed metadata block. That is exactly the text parsing the structured array exists to remove, and it re-couples callers to the markdown's formatting.

### Affected components and platforms

The macOS `get_window_state` row builder (`platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs::build_elements_array_with_token`) and the shared contract record (`cua-driver-contract/src/windows.rs::WindowElement`), which gains two additive optional fields, with the manifest and the generated SDK records regenerated. Windows `HelpText` through UIA and AT-SPI descriptions on Linux are separate work; the keys are simply absent on those backends.

### Alternatives and prior art

- Folding help into `label` when the label would otherwise be empty: changes the meaning of an existing field and loses which attribute the text came from.
- Markdown parsing, as above.
- The row shape already carries this class of attribute: `value_description` (`AXValueDescription`) is surfaced structurally today, so `help` and `description` are the consistent completion of that, not a new concept.

### Implementation ideas

Emit both in `build_elements_array_with_token`, skipping an empty description and one that already equals the label, and add the two optional fields to `WindowElement`. One thing to know before regenerating: the generated manifest will advertise `help` but not `description`, because contract schema generation deletes every object property named `description` (#3802). The Rust field and the JSON response still carry the value and typed clients still deserialize it. A pull request follows.

title: [Bug]: macOS `set_value` reports a verified write that the application's own editing pipeline never sees
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS `set_value` writes `AXValue`, reads `AXValue` back to confirm it, and reports a verified write. On an AppKit text control the string stays in the window's field editor: the app's `controlTextDidEndEditing` never fires, so the application's own model keeps its pre-edit value while the AX read-back echoes the new string. Nothing in the result distinguishes a write the app accepted from one it never saw, and a later save writes the old value.

### Reproduction

1. Build the AppKit harness fixture (`libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures/build/macos.sh`). Its `txt-input` field has a sibling label that publishes the app's own committed value as `committed=<value>`, set from `controlTextDidEndEditing`; it starts at `committed=none`.
2. `get_window_state` on the fixture window, then `set_value` on the `txt-input` element with `"value": "commit-cua"`.
3. `get_window_state` again and read both the `txt-input` value and the `committed=` label.

### Expected behavior

Either the write reaches the application's editing pipeline, so the label reads `committed=commit-cua`, or the result says the value was written to AX but not committed, so the caller knows it must still end the edit.

### Actual behavior

cua-driver 0.28.1 at 31c2184f8: `set_value` returns `✅ Set AXValue on [N] AXTextField.` with `verified: true`, the element reads back `commit-cua`, and the label stays `committed=none`. The result has no field that could report the difference.

The repo's own harness encodes this behavior: `harness_appkit_element_foreground_press_key_commits_edit` seeds the edit with `set_value`, asserts `committed=none` with the message "fixture reported a commit before Return", and only a foreground `press_key` Return makes the app register the edit.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.1 (origin/main 31c2184f8)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: AppKit harness fixture (`NSTextField` inside an `NSWindow` field editor); any AppKit app that acts on `controlTextDidEndEditing`, including save panels and inspector fields

### Evidence

`platform-macos/src/tools/set_value.rs::set_value_blocking` writes `AXValue` and then only classifies the read-back through `classify_write`; the file contains no confirm or end-of-edit gesture, so the field editor is never ended. `platform-macos/src/browser/setup_ui.rs` has to run `perform_action(omnibox, "AXConfirm")` by hand after writing the omnibox value, which shows the confirm step is required but is implemented for that one call site rather than for the tool. `cua-driver-contract::outputs::ActionResult` has no field for commit state, so even a tool that knew the write was uncommitted could not say so. The fixture hook is `tests/fixtures/apps/macos/appkit/main.swift::controlTextDidEndEditing`.

### Workaround and additional context

After `set_value`, end the edit yourself with a `press_key` Return or Tab. That only works in `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, so it activates the target app and steals focus, which defeats the point of the background AX write.

title: [Bug]: macOS right-click reports a context menu as opened when AXShowMenu succeeds without opening one
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS both `right_click` with an `element_index` and `click` with `button: "right"` dispatch `AXShowMenu` and report success the moment `AXUIElementPerformAction` returns `kAXErrorSuccess`. Many AppKit views advertise `AXShowMenu` and implement it as a no-op, so the action succeeds while no context menu ever appears. The agent is told a menu is open, its next step targets menu items that do not exist, and the pixel right-click fallback that already exists for this exact situation is never reached because it only runs when the action is unadvertised or returns an error.

### Reproduction

1. `get_window_state` on any macOS window and pick an element whose advertised actions include `AXShowMenu` but whose view has no menu to show (custom `NSView` click targets and table/collection cells commonly inherit the action from `NSView` without implementing `menu(for:)`).
2. `right_click` with that `element_index`, or `click` with that `element_index` and `button: "right"`.
3. Screenshot the display: no context menu is open anywhere.

### Expected behavior

The reply distinguishes "the menu opened" from "the action returned success and nothing happened". When no menu appeared, the driver either delivers the actuation a user performs (a pointer right-click at the element centre, the same fallback it already uses for elements that do not advertise `AXShowMenu`) or says plainly that no menu opened, so the agent does not plan against a menu that is not there.

### Actual behavior

cua-driver 0.28.1 (`main`, 31c2184f8):

| `AXShowMenu` result | Driver reply | Menu on screen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| advertised, succeeds, opens a menu | `Shown menu for [{idx}] {role} "{title}" (AXShowMenu).` | yes |
| advertised, succeeds, opens nothing | same reply, byte for byte | no |
| not advertised, or returns an error | `Right-clicked [{idx}] {role} "{title}" at element center ({cx}, {cy})` after a real pointer right-click | yes, when the view has a menu |

Rows one and two are the same tool result, so the agent cannot tell them apart, and `click` with `button: "right"` reports `✅ Performed AXShowMenu on [{idx}] ...` under the same conditions. Row three is the path that works; it is unreachable for an element that advertises the action.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.1 (`main`, 31c2184f8)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1 (25B78), arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: AppKit, any view that advertises `AXShowMenu` without implementing a menu

### Evidence

`platform-macos/src/tools/right_click.rs::ax_show_menu` returns `Ok(format!("Shown menu for [{idx}] ..."))` as soon as `perform_action(element, "AXShowMenu")` equals `kAXErrorSuccess`; the pixel right-click below it is reachable only when the action is unadvertised or returns a non-success error. `platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs::map_action` maps the `show_menu` action that `button: "right"` rewrites to (see `ClickTool::invoke`, `effective_action`) onto `AXShowMenu`, and `perform_ax_click` formats `✅ Performed {ax_action} ...` on any success. Nothing in either path observes whether a menu window exists. Apple's `accessibilityPerformShowMenu` contract is a request, not a guarantee that a menu became visible.

### Workaround and additional context

Take a screenshot after every element right-click and fall back to pixel coordinates when no menu is visible, which costs an extra observation on every call and needs the element centre the driver already resolved. Related but distinct: #3802, #3803.

title: [Bug]: macOS `type_text` reports complete delivery as incomplete when the app replaces the edited element
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

After the keystrokes are posted, `type_text` reads the text back only through the element pointer it resolved before typing. AppKit installs a field editor over an `NSTextField` while it is edited, and some apps replace or re-create the row outright (search fields, SwiftUI re-renders), so that pinned pointer keeps reporting the pre-edit string. Delivery that fully landed is then classified as `Partial` or `Unchanged` and returned as `type_text_incomplete`, advising a retry of a suffix that is already in the field.

### Reproduction

1. `get_window_state` on a Contacts window with a contact open for editing, and note the `element_index` of a phone or name field.
2. `type_text` into that element with a short payload such as `555-1234`.
3. Read the result, then screenshot the window.

### Expected behavior

The field visibly holds the full text and the result reports delivery. A read-back that cannot see the addressed element should not contradict text that provably landed in the window that was addressed.

### Actual behavior

cua-driver 0.28.0, `mcp --direct`, macOS 26.1: the text is in the field, and every complete insertion came back as `type_text incomplete: delivered k of n character(s); retry only the remaining suffix` with `"code": "type_text_incomplete"`. Each false partial costs the caller a re-observe to find out whether anything actually landed, and following the advice appends a suffix that is already there.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.0 (`mcp --direct`); the same read-back is on `main` at 31c2184f8
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: Contacts (AppKit); any app that swaps the edited element while typing

### Evidence

`platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs::cgevent_type_verified` passes `await_typed_delivery` a closure that is exactly `read_axvalue_bound(pid, element_ptr_and_idx, window_id)`, and with an explicit element `platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs::read_axvalue` reads `AXValue` straight off that stored pointer with no re-resolution. When the pointer no longer holds the text, `platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs::typed_progress` sees no growth and returns `Unchanged` or a prefix-sized `Partial`, which is what the `type_text_incomplete` branch of `platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs::TypeTextTool` reports. The same file already knows how to read the window's focused element safely: `read_axvalue_bound` with no addressed element uses `focused_element_in_window`, which refuses focus that does not provably resolve inside the requested window.

### Workaround and additional context

Ignore the incomplete verdict and re-observe the window instead; do not follow the suffix-retry advice, since the text may already be complete. Related but distinct: #3574 (foreground `type_text` targeting a sibling window in the same process) and #3389 (Electron background delivery reported unverifiable while the text lands).
