title: [Bug]: Linux `get_window_state` spends `max_elements` on the application's other windows, so a capped snapshot of a second window returns no controls
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux `max_elements` is charged to every AT-SPI node the walk visits, including nodes belonging to the application's other windows, which the renderer then drops because they are out of the requested frame. A capped snapshot of an application's second window therefore comes back with the window row and no controls at all, and because `elements_complete` is hard-coded `false`, the caller cannot tell a starved snapshot from a window that genuinely has nothing.

### Reproduction

1. Run a GTK 3 application that publishes two top-levels from one process, 60 buttons in each (labels `one-00`..`one-59` and `two-00`..`two-59`).
2. `get_window_state` on the first window with `"max_elements": 10`.
3. `get_window_state` on the second window with `"max_elements": 10`, then again with no cap.

### Expected behavior

`max_elements` bounds the window named by `window_id`, so a capped snapshot of the second window returns about as many of its controls as a capped snapshot of the first. `elements_complete` is true when the walk enumerated that window exhaustively, so a caller can prove a control is absent.

### Actual behavior

cua-driver 0.28.1 (`main`, 31c2184f8), `mcp --direct`, same fixture:

| snapshot | `element_count` | `elements_complete` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| window one, `max_elements: 10` | 8 controls | `false` |
| window two, `max_elements: 10` | 1 (the window row, zero controls) | `false` |
| window two, uncapped | 60 controls | `false` |

The capped second-window snapshot contains no addressable control, so a follow-up `click` by `element_index` or `element_token` has nothing to target. The uncapped snapshot did enumerate the whole window, yet still reports `elements_complete: false`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.1 (`main`, 31c2184f8)
Operating system and architecture: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, x86_64, Linux 6.8.0
Application/browser/window system/image: X11 with a private session bus and an at-spi registry; GTK 3.24.41 two-top-level fixture

### Evidence

`platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs::collect_visited_bounded` resolves `scoped_frame` from the caller's `xid`, then spends one unit of a single `budget` (`max_elements.unwrap_or(5000)`) on every popped node regardless of its `frame_ordinal`. `platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs::render` emits only nodes whose frame matches (`let emit = only_frame.is_none_or(|frame| frame == v.frame_ordinal);`), so the cap is spent on rows the caller never receives, and whichever window the walk reaches last is the one that starves.

Those nodes cannot simply be skipped instead: element indices are application-wide, and actuators such as `platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs::perform_action_at_screen_point` and `platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs::get_element_bounds_for_window` resolve an index against an unbounded walk of the whole application, so dropping a sibling window's subtree would renumber every element emitted after it.

Separately, `platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs::GetWindowStateTool` sets `structured["elements_complete"] = json!(false)` unconditionally, so negative existence is permanently unknowable on Linux even for an exhaustive walk.

### Workaround and additional context

Omit `max_elements` and pay for the entire application tree; no value of the cap yields the second window's controls. Related but distinct: #2242 (macOS Chromium snapshots apply element limits before scoping) and #2958.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: macOS `get_window_state` always reports `elements_complete: false`, so element absence can never be proven
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS `get_window_state` hard-codes `elements_complete: false`, so the one field that tells a caller whether `elements` is the whole addressable-element set of the window never carries information. Absence can never be proven: a predicate that matches nothing resolves to Unknown for every window, however small and however completely the AX walk enumerated it. The walker already computes the answer and the contract already declares the field.

### Reproduction

1. `get_window_state` on a window whose AX tree is far below the default caps (2000 elements, depth 25), for example macOS Calculator, and read `structuredContent.elements_complete`.
2. `verify_state` (or any `cua-driver-core::expectation` predicate) with `exists: true` on a selector that matches nothing in that window.
3. Repeat step 1 with `max_elements: 1` to force a walk that really did stop early.

### Expected behavior

Step 1 reports `elements_complete: true` (a resolved window, a walk that gave nothing up) and step 3 reports `false`, with the contract's `truncated` field naming why the observation is partial. Step 2 is then Unsatisfied rather than Unknown.

### Actual behavior

`elements_complete` is `false` in every case, step 1 included, and `truncated` is never emitted at all. Step 2 returns Unknown with `ObservationUnavailable` and evidence `{"matches": 0, "elements_complete": false}` forever, which is the branch `cua-driver-core::expectation` takes when the observation is admittedly partial.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.1 (trycua/cua main, 31c2184f8)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1 (25B78), arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: any AX-exposing macOS app (Calculator, TextEdit)

### Evidence

`platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs::GetWindowStateTool` assigns `let elements_complete = false;` and publishes that constant; the comment above it names the blocker as AX child reads failing independently of the element and depth caps. That is `platform-macos/src/ax/bindings.rs::copy_children`, which drops the `AXError` and returns an empty vector, making a failed read indistinguishable from an element that genuinely has no children. `platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs::walk_element` also returns silently at the depth cap without setting `truncated`, so `TreeWalkResult::truncated` currently answers for the element cap alone. On the consumer side, `cua-driver-core::expectation` gates the Unsatisfied verdict on `snapshot.elements_complete`. `cua-driver-contract::WindowStateOutput` already declares both `elements_complete` and `truncated`, so nothing in the schema blocks a real verdict.

### Workaround and additional context

None that recovers the promise: a caller can only walk with generous caps and keep treating absence as unknown, which is exactly what the field exists to remove. The Linux path (`platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs`) hard-codes the same constant and is a separate fix. Related but distinct: #2958 (display-only `AXStaticText` sits outside the addressable set `elements` publishes) and #2242 (element limits applied before window scoping).

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: cua-bench: linux-docker broken out of the box (private default env image, localhost-bound computer-server) + oracle flakiness on cua-bench-basic
body:
## Environment
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64, Docker 29.1.3, KVM available
- Tool: `cua-bench` v0.2.11 from PyPI (`uv tool install 'cua-bench[browser]'`), Chromium present
- Registry: main @ `c0a655c` (also repros on 0.2.x-era tasks)
- Env image: `trycua/cua-xfce:latest` (pulled by `cb image create linux-docker`)

## Bug 1: default linux-docker env image is private (`nikri/kicad-snorkel:20260316b`)
`ENV_CONFIGS["linux-docker"]["image"]` in `cua_bench/runner/task_runner.py` (and the fallback default) points at `nikri/kicad-snorkel:20260316b`, which is not pullable:

```
Failed to start container cua-env-...: Unable to find image 'nikri/kicad-snorkel:20260316b' locally
docker: Error response from daemon: pull access denied for nikri/kicad-snorkel, repository does not exist or may require 'docker login'
```

Every `cb run dataset cua-bench-basic --oracle` task fails 0.0 with empty logs because of this. `--image` does not help: `_start_env_container` uses `config["image"]` directly and ignores `golden_name`. Meanwhile `cb image create linux-docker` pulls `trycua/cua-xfce:latest`, which the runner never uses.

## Bug 2: cua-xfce computer-server binds 127.0.0.1, unreachable from agent container
`/usr/local/bin/start-computer-server.sh` in `trycua/cua-xfce:latest` runs `python3 -m computer_server --port ...` with no `--host`, and the default bind is `127.0.0.1:8000`. The agent container connects to `cua-env:8000` (external interface) and times out after 100s:

```
ClientConnectorError: Cannot connect to host cua-env:8000 ... Connect call failed ('172.18.0.2', 8000)
```

Local workaround: append `--host 0.0.0.0` in the start script and commit.

## Bug 3 (flakiness, undiagnosed): oracle clicks intermittently don't flip state
With bugs 1+2 worked around locally, `cb run dataset cua-bench-basic --oracle` executes 13/13 and exports traces, but scores fluctuate run to run (observed 3/13 x1.0 once, usually 0-2/13). Evidence from direct probes against the same image:
- `get_element_rect` is stable across 15s and cursor delivery is verified (`get_cursor_position` tracks moves exactly).
- A page-side event spy once recorded the full `mousedown/focus/mouseup/click` sequence with `hasFocus=true` and `__submitted=true`; most runs record nothing and score 0.0.
- Screenshots show the window mapped, focused (`Btn` active in taskbar), button visible; clicks still don't land.
- Separating move and click across calls (move, sleep 2s, click-at-current) succeeded where atomic position+click usually fails — smells like a motion/press delivery race in the pynput path or a focus race at click time, but I could not isolate it deterministically.

Happy to provide run logs/traces. The silent failure mode (CLI prints `reward=?`/`0.0` with no error although `TaskResult.error` is populated) made all of the above much harder to find — consider surfacing `result.error` in dataset output.

title: cua-driver: expose link target URL (AXURL) in get_window_state elements
body:
### Problem

`get_window_state` structured `elements` on macOS carry `label`, `value`, `actions`, `frame` and `in_web_content`, but not where a link leads. For web content (Chrome, Safari, Electron apps) a caller can read a link's text and press it, yet cannot know its target without navigating. Reading search results, deciding which link to follow, or citing a source all need the target.

Chromium and WebKit already expose it: `AXLink` elements answer `AXURL` (a `CFURL`). The macOS walker in `platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs` reads `AXRole`, `AXTitle`, `AXValue`, `AXDescription`, `AXIdentifier`, `AXHelp`, `AXEnabled`, `AXSelected` and friends, but never `AXURL`. `copy_string_attr` also returns `None` for `CFURL` values.

Measured with a small native probe against Google Chrome 152 on macOS (not through cua-driver): on a Google results page 64 of 66 `AXLink` elements answer `AXURL`, on a Baidu results page 105 of 105; a whole-tree walk including the attribute took 250–420 ms.

### Proposal

- Add an optional `url` field to the structured element (`WindowElement` in `cua-driver-contract`), populated on macOS from `AXURL`.
- Read it only for actionable `AXLink` nodes, behind the existing `read_control_state_if_actionable` gate, so display-only rows and other roles pay no extra AX round trip.
- Leave `tree_markdown` unchanged, per the tool description ("new fields will only be added to the structured side").
- macOS only in this change, following the precedent of `value_description` / `min` / `max`. Windows UIA already reports a link's URL through the Value pattern (`value`), and AT-SPI exposes it through the Hyperlink interface; those can follow separately.

This is an additive optional field, so existing consumers are unaffected.

title: test(cua-driver): guard Hyprland element-reveal output coordinates
body:
Refs #3554.

The issue reported that a Hyprland AT-SPI action could place the agent cursor outside the target window, with window-local accessibility bounds behaving as output-space coordinates. Checked against current `main` with the issue's scenario: the reveal path already resolves proven output coordinates, but nothing guarded that contract. This adds the live regression.

## What changed

- `hyprland_element_reveal_test.rs` (live, `#[ignore]`, Hyprland-only): moves the agent cursor to a neutral point, locates the overlay's debug square (`CUA_OVERLAY_DEBUG=1`) in a driver desktop capture, performs a background element click by token, and asserts the revealed cursor lands on the element's absolute frame center (within the cursor-artwork anchor tolerance, 32 points) and inside the target window. It requires the fixture window to sit away from the output origin, so a window-local leak cannot pass.
- `McpDriver::spawn_named_with_overlay_and_env` (testkit, additive): overlay-enabled spawn with child-scoped environment, mirroring the existing `RawDriver::spawn_with_overlay_and_env`.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` — 440 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit --lib` — 106 passed, 0 failed when the test process is in the CI-shaped X11 session (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE` unset/x11). Note: on a live Wayland session one pre-existing assertion on `main` fails (`native_case_builders_encode_delivery_and_oracle_contracts` hard-codes the `Cursor` oracle for every display server) — #3466 carries that fix and is not part of this branch.
- Live on Hyprland 0.56 with a single output at a non-zero global origin and scale 1.8 (so raw-pixel mapping is genuinely exercised): `cargo test -p cua-driver --test hyprland_element_reveal_test -- --ignored` — 1 passed, 0 failed.
- Measured on the same run: the click resolved the element's frame center `(3830.5, 1581.0)` exactly as reported by the snapshot, and the overlay's debug square landed within ~15 points of it (the artwork anchor offset) — not near the output origin, and inside the target window.

title: fix(cua-driver): correct keyboard delivery and outcome reporting
body:
Refs #3473 and #3657. Salvaged from #3658.

## Scope

Preserve Ben Kamholtz’s Enter/Return terminal-gate fix and reference update via `cherry-pick -x` of 78875a32 and c2ca6f1c; Francesco Bonacci’s coauthor credit remains intact. Keep the earlier XTest hotkey reporting correction. Source #3658 stays open pending landing disposition.

The maintainer clarified that completing the red-case phase does not require native certification and explicitly selected the tech-spec handoff. **Red-case characterization is complete for this slice; the design proposal is ready for review. No typed-producer implementation or further production fix has started.** Native execution gaps and intentional reds remain explicit; this is not merge-ready.

### Revised vertical-slice proposal awaiting review

At the maintainer's request, the additive accounting-layer proposal is superseded by a deletion-led design: separate compatibility-preserving entry parsers feed one keyboard executor per platform; native backend transactions own retained targets, focus and input lifetimes and return immutable typed outcomes. No shared mutable progress tracker, universal keyboard planner, phantom search transport or duplicate recorded/unrecorded actuator implementations.

Separate preparation failure from attempted dispatch failure. Source review shows that Wayland may try another backend after a post-input error, and the XAML scan may continue to another matching control after Invoke/Toggle failure. These are source-verified risks, not new native fault reproductions. No-replay, owned cleanup and Wayland focus restoration are proposed as explicit behavior-changing red-to-green slices, not hidden refactors. XAML no-transient-focus-steal still needs a verified mechanism or an explicit capability decision; an after-the-fact restore is not sufficient.

Keep ActionExecutionRecord as the canonical outcome, but distinguish refused routes, execution facts and genuinely unknown worker outcomes rather than inventing an actuator for refusals. The core crate is unpublished; this internal representation change requires workspace caller migration and cross-action projection regression coverage. Successful SDK/MCP schemas and existing error envelopes remain unchanged. Recording/debug readers must explicitly support transport-less refusals and unknown outcomes without reinterpreting historical artifacts as proof of delivery.

Remove keyboard-only legacy payloads/inference after producer migration; preserve unrelated compatibility. The proposal includes a scoped inventory of structural deletions, FFI ownership improvements, schema/parser opportunities, test/CI cleanup and deferred optimizations. Preserve Enter/Return provenance, native route exceptions, admission timing, existing protocol count units and independent test oracles. No implementation or additional native test runs have started.

## Implemented coverage

- Real producer invocation before dispatch reconstruction on Linux, Windows and macOS. Implemented cases cover foreground/background routes, unchanged-value versus genuine AX readback, target closure, duplicate modifiers, and focus preservation/restoration using a separate native sentinel and global key probes. Implemented is not synonymous with natively observed: macOS positive producer cases remain permission-blocked below.
- Public dispatch: malformed/unknown input and token refusals, authorization targets, real multi-window ambiguity, admitted-action serialization, queued cancellation, and deterministic cancellation after native key/modifier down. The latter observes the existing in-flight sequence finish and release; it does **not** certify cancelled-worker drain/readiness before completion or redesign it.
- Real X11 connection-loss injection after independently received key/modifier down, retaining missing-record failures and checking that input is not replayed.
- Real xterm PTYs: aliases/case, modified-key and hotkey bypass, no-PTY fallback, actual transport and delivery. An XI2 observer and managed focus sentinel distinguish consumed PTY input from XTest and transient foreground activation. Positive XTest controls validate the observer.
- Native GTK terminal with a real owned PTY and real snapshot-bound accessible entry: bare Return takes the PTY shortcut; valid element-targeted press_key/hotkey reach the exact GTK entry, preserve modifiers and do not duplicate delivery.
- Shared SDK/native harness: stale/conflicting targets, runtime isolation and retirement; shared/desktop outcome schemas, truthful route/mode/effect, absent invented evidence/counts, and recording/public parity. An accepted independently observed action must not be described as `delivery_failed` merely because its effect is `unverifiable`.

## Exact 58a1b2531d0eaad1ba490cf6780eb143672340df evidence

Linux focused native keyboard suite: **48 cases, 35 pass / 13 intentional reporting reds**, no fixture failure:

- 8 real producer results omit execution records after observed input.
- 2 public post-input native errors omit execution records after observed key/modifier down.
- F5 uses XTest but reports `synthetic_events`; a PTY write is recorded as `LinuxXSendEvent`; a focus-free PTY write requested as foreground reports foreground.

Additional Linux validation: platform unit tests **448 pass / 15 ignored** (ignored native cases were run explicitly above); core **628 pass**; SDK **93 pass serially**; testkit **106 pass**; session/snapshot/dispatch integrations **13 pass**; shared native harness compiles. Formatting and diff checks pass.

Retained diagnostics are not replaced with favorable results:

- Default parallel SDK execution failed a process-global hook-count assertion (4 versus baseline 0) and eight poisoned-lock cascades. The documented serial native-harness setting passed 93/93; the parallel isolation issue remains unfixed and separately logged.
- An unmanaged root-focus canary was invalid: a no-driver control reproduced focus reclamation. Its replacement is a real managed sentinel with stricter transient-focus and raw-key observation; the original failures remain retained.
- Native terminal host construction initially used mismatched runtime/cache scopes. The fixture now follows the SDK’s immutable context and `with_runtime_scope` construction contract; no token validation changed.

Local evidence is retained under `artifacts/keyboard-completion/` in the isolated Linux checkout and transferred verbatim to the maintainer host. SHA-256 of the transferred evidence archive: `aa01565add94f57712ec1d167fca5ea941210372660089adc2ad7cef6e28f370`.

## Completed canonical runs at 58a1b2531d0eaad1ba490cf6780eb143672340df

| Environment | Desktop rows passing, including expected refusals | Failed rows | Classification |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [Linux X11](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34893920047) | 126 | 5 | Foreground press_key reports synthetic instead of global input |
| [Windows](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34893922524) | 134 | 4 | Observed press_key actions incorrectly advertise delivery_failed |
| [Sway](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34893925305) | 122 | 8 | Foreground press_key/hotkey report synthetic instead of global input |
| macOS Lume `20260914T204105Z-0cf607e5` | 155 | 9 | Six background hotkey failure-advice errors; three pixel press_key route/mode errors |

Failed rows are not complete evidence passes: reporting assertions stop later checks. Raw logs and recordings remain retained. Windows strict GUI preflight, capture/native framework lanes, and installer smoke passed. macOS producer diagnostics separately report **2 pass / 7 permission-blocked**; daemon authorization does not authorize the Cargo test executable, and no grants were changed.

[Cua compositor](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34893927797) does not qualify keyboard behavior: native/capture fail ready-window/AX/screenshot preflight; shared stops earlier because the Nix environment lacks `gnome-keyring-daemon`. These are not keyboard reporting reds. Real Hyprland execution is also unqualified; its unit/mock workflow is not native evidence.

## Focused continuation and exact-diff accounting

Current published head: `b4e5f6f54b34534378fc0a343cffd948e535d7f8`.

**Latest runnable batches are fully classified, with no fixture failures at 9acad90:** [Windows](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34936998965) **5 pass / 10 missing-record reds**; [native Sway](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34937001391) **5 missing-record reds**, including independently confirmed hotkey focus loss. These are intentional product-red tests, not passing acceptance. macOS positive producer execution and the previously documented compositor environments remain blocked/unqualified. These are native-validation gaps, not blockers to completing the red-case phase or reviewing the tech spec.

The final b4e5f6f delta only wires the existing Sway producer group into the normal native/all session tail, preserving earlier failures and not rerunning diagnostics recursively. Six shell control-flow cases passed against the actual dispatch block with external command stubs; shell syntax/diff checks passed. Native product/test bodies remain those tested at 9acad90. No unrelated matrix rerun.

### Latest canonical macOS run

Maintainer-authorized Lume run `20260915T064932Z-46ba3173` tested the exact current b4e5f6f head after waiting for another workstream's lock to clear. **146 delivered / 9 expected refusals / 9 failed** (155 passing desktop rows). The failures remain six background hotkey `delivery_failed` advice errors and three pixel press_key foreground-request route/mode errors. Failed rows do not establish their later oracle assertions. Strict preflight and report validation passed; no video failures.

Direct producer suite: **2 pass / 10 Accessibility-blocked**. The installed app's daemon reports Accessibility and Screen Recording granted, while the distinct Cargo test executable reports no Accessibility permission. The VM therefore does not qualify the positive producer, AX-retention or closure cases. No grants were changed and no failed tests were retried.

Evidence collected and worker stop confirmed. The standard-daemon restoration trap reported no error or deferred restoration; this failed run has no separate post-run daemon-status attestation. Clone source `cua-driver-browser-baseline-20260908-chrome152` is worker-derived from #2907/#3373, not an immutable certified seed. Standalone-browser was outside scope and not run. Local evidence is retained at `/Users/administrator/.local/share/cua-lume-e2e/runs/20260915T064932Z-46ba3173/`; that path is not a public download link. PR head remained unchanged after execution.

### Latest focused batches

- [Windows fbb0c79 keyboard](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34931831446): **5 pass / 8 missing-record reds**, no fixture failures; strengthened retained UIA PID/name checks and native input observations passed before reporting assertions.
- [Windows fbb0c79 native lane](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34931833408): **39 delivered / 4 expected refusals / 0 failed**, including eight WinUI3 rows after fixture changes. The attempted harness filter did not limit the native script. This is not a full shared/capture/desktop certification; subsequent keyboard-xaml diagnostics build only their fixture and skip the native matrix.
- The initial XAML diagnostic had **1 physical-control pass / 3 fixture failures** from an incorrectly scoped focus probe. Those failures are retained; the established desktop probe is now shared instead of duplicated.
- [XAML d5abd2b](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34935387410): **1 pass / 3 product-red cases**. Invoke/Toggle callbacks occurred once with no native key replay, but native foreground PID/HWND observation shows the target app has taken foreground from the sentinel, and producer records are absent. This is verified focus loss, not merely a probe error. A no-matching-accelerator refusal also lacks a producer record. The focus behavior has not been fixed or silently excluded.
- Five native-Wayland GTK producer cases compiled at ffdc9dc; their first run stopped on a GTK/GDK namespace mismatch before input. Both namespaces were pinned to version 3 at 9afeb22. Original fixture failures and the later misplaced post-hotkey probe are retained. At 9acad90 all five reach intended reporting reds after independent receipt or observed refusal. Both press_key variants restore the sentinel; hotkey leaves the target foreground (Sway IPC PID10911, expected sentinel PID10946). Source review confirms hotkey calls an activating helper without the restoring wrapper used by press_key. No production focus fix.
- Two Windows tests simulate partial acceptance at the external SendInput boundary. At 632303a the API accepted one event and returned the expected short-count error, but app receipt timed out; those failures are retained and not counted as delivered input. At 9acad90 the test-only syscall boundary waits for independent receipt before returning the real short count to the unchanged producer error path. Both cases now observe key/modifier down, owned key-up cleanup, global release, no replay and restored-focus recovery, then fail solely on missing execution records. This is controlled syscall-boundary partial acceptance, not spontaneous OS failure or product-owned cleanup.
- macOS producer compilation and **94 testkit unit tests** passed at fbb0c79. Positive macOS producers remain blocked as documented below; no grant changed.

### Earlier focused evidence

Linux at a721db4: queued lifecycle/terminal-element group **9/9 pass**; full focused native group **50 cases, 37 pass / 13 reporting reds**, no fixture failures. Adding hotkey target loss at 118f338 produced **11 producer cases, 2 pass / 9 missing-record reds**. e10f9ad retained complete ToolResult diagnostics and its native-producer-only filter produced **1 pass / 9 reds** (registry ambiguity remained covered at 118f338). Combined with unchanged integrations this is **51 cases, 37 pass / 14 reporting reds by explicit delta accounting**, not a single exact-head run. The remote launcher returned transport status 255 after one completed run; original logs and exited processes were recovered without rerunning or replacing the evidence.

[Windows e10f9ad](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34927957630): **5 pass / 6 missing-record reds**, no fixture failures. Hotkey target loss observed real Ctrl down and window closure; the producer still returned legacy success without a record. Closure need not force an OS error; the Linux connection-loss cases remain separate actual post-input error coverage.

[Windows 46ac840](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34929689654): **5 pass / 8 missing-record reds**, no fixture failures. Two new tests pause immediately before the real UIA SetFocus boundary, clear the owning snapshot cache, successfully query the retained native handle's PID, require a reused token to be refused, then release and independently observe a single completed key/chord in the original field. These ownership/input assertions passed before the final missing-record assertion failed. The hooks are test-only and do not mock native results. The bounded barrier's release/abandonment unit test passed.

macOS 46ac840 producer suite: **2 pass / 10 permission-blocked**. This includes the new hotkey closure and two AX retained-target cases; none of those positive cases reached native input. The changed Swift fixture compiled and its real invalid-input and ambiguity cases passed. No grants were changed.

[Windows keyboard-only diagnostics](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34900062224) at `75f473d2b2f6de443784df62b8d97f819134a286`: **5 pass / 5 missing-record reds**, no fixture failures. The corrected oracle observes both root-window and text-field messages. Background receipts were root-window PostMessage sequences, with modifier flags zero; they establish message receipt, not a confirmed application shortcut. Foreground receipts and sentinel F6 probes establish sequence completion and focus restoration. Modifier-only hotkeys are explicitly rejected before input; the earlier compatibility assumption was wrong.

That commit was amended only to correct the agent commit identity as `4bd6cbcc799e76be303fba27f50e118b19ad97af`; Git tree hashes are identical. Subsequent heads add the observed queued-token cases, hotkey target-loss cases and native-retention tests above. The keyboard-only workflow no longer publishes a desktop matrix summary. This continuation changes tests, fixtures and cfg(test)-only native-boundary pauses, not production behavior; the prior full desktop runs are not presented as exact-head certification.

The original Windows 58a1b25 observer timeouts and incorrect modifier-only assertion remain retained, alongside the corrected diagnostic run.

## Historical evidence and remaining limits

The pre-salvage 059b36521 terminal fixture delivered Enter but timed out on Return; salvaged code delivered both and case variants. The mixed-source Cargo-cache run is invalid and retained. No permissions or credentials were repaired.

At c47e75ed, [Windows native diagnostics](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34880967983) passed native framework tests, then five producer record cases failed after receipt. The sixth revealed a test assumption: Windows retains first-character key-name compatibility; new tests observe that behavior rather than silently changing parsing. [Linux SDK diagnostics](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34880965059) passed live foreign-runtime rejection, then hit an incorrect retired-token expectation; retirement correctly reports `stale_element_token`.

Remaining work includes maintainer disposition of the newly observed XAML and Wayland hotkey focus loss and resolving or explicitly bounding unavailable native environments. The new runnable Wayland and Windows partial-acceptance batches are now classified; original fixture failures remain retained separately. Queue-time token retirement is not proof of retained native handles after admission; the Windows ownership assertions above now independently cover post-admission cache clearing, while corresponding macOS execution remains blocked. Permission-blocked macOS cases and compositor setup failures remain outstanding for native qualification. Historical green runs do not certify this head. **The red-case phase is complete and the typed-producer tech-spec proposal is ready for review; implementation, green acceptance and native qualification are not complete. This draft remains unmerged.**

title: macOS: type_text reports a false type_text_incomplete when the field publishes AXValue after the write
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `type_text`'s AX rung writes `AXSelectedText` and then reads `AXValue` back exactly once, immediately. When the application applies the insertion asynchronously — an AppKit field rebuilding its editor around the write — that read returns a prefix, and the call fails with `type_text_incomplete` naming a delivered count that is wrong. The caller is told to retype a suffix that is already in the field.

### Environment

macOS 26.1 (arm64), `cua-driver` built from `main`. Target: Contacts (system app), a new contact card in edit mode, `type_text` addressed at the window with the editor field focused (`delivery_mode` default, background).

### Reproduction

1. Open Contacts, create a card, put it in edit mode, and focus an empty Phone field.
2. `type_text` with `pid` + `window_id` and `text: "(408) 961-1560"`.
3. Read the field back a moment later.

### Actual

```
type_text incomplete: delivered 6 of 14 character(s) via partial AX write into AXTextField ""; retry only the remaining suffix
{"code":"type_text_incomplete","delivered_chars":6,"effect":"partial","path":"ax","requested_chars":14,"retry_from_character":6,"retryable":true}
```

The field holds the complete `(408) 961-1560`. The same call on an empty Street field reports `delivered 4 of 25` for `10600 North Tantau Avenue`, again complete in the field. Polling the field's `AXValue` through System Events puts the complete value in place within ~22 ms of the write (the finest resolution that instrument allows), so the window in which the prefix is visible is short — but the driver reads inside it.

It reproduces only on the *first* insertion into a fresh field, i.e. when the app is also laying the row out. Repeating the same call on a field that already took text once returns `effect: "confirmed"`, `delivered_count: 25`.

### Expected

`type_text` should only claim incompleteness it has verified against a field that settled. The character count it publishes drives a retry, so it must not be read from a value the app is still applying.

### Where it is

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs`:

- the AX rung writes and reads back with nothing in between (`set_string_attr(element, "AXSelectedText", text)` then `copy_string_attr(element, "AXValue")`), and classifies that single sample;
- the keystroke rung on the same file already treats this as a settling problem: `cgevent_type_verified` polls through `await_typed_delivery` until the read-back proves complete or `DELIVERY_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (2 s) passes, precisely because "CGEvent posting is asynchronous with respect to the renderer".

The AX rung has the same asynchrony for a different reason and none of the drain.

### Suggested fix

Run the AX rung's read-back through the same drain. An unchanged window still has to summarise as unchanged so an AX write the app ignored keeps falling through to keystrokes rather than reporting "delivered 0 of n", and a write the driver rejected should not wait at all.

title: [Bug]: macOS `click` on a text role dispatches an unadvertised `AXPress` instead of focusing it
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `click` on a text-entry element dispatches `AXPress` at it even though no text role advertises that action. The app answers `-25206`, the driver appends "Element does not advertise AXPress ... Action may have been a no-op", reports `effect: "suspected_noop"` and escalates to a pixel click - while the one thing a click on a text field means, "put the caret here", was never attempted. Agents read the reply as a failure and either retry or fall back to pixels.

### Reproduction

1. Open Automator, `cmd+shift+s` to raise the Save As sheet.
2. `get_window_state` for the sheet's window; its name field is `AXTextField` with `actions: [AXShowMenu, AXConfirm]`.
3. `cua-driver call click '{"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<wid>,"element_token":"<token>"}'`.

Reproduces on every attempt, on any `AXTextField`/`AXTextArea`/`AXSecureTextField`/`AXSearchField`/`AXComboBox` with no selectable ancestor.

### Expected behavior

A click on a text-entry role sets keyboard focus and says so, proving it through the application's own `AXFocusedUIElement` rather than through the driver's own write returning success. If the focus write does not stick, escalate to a pointer click at the control's centre and re-prove; report honestly when neither works. The existing collection-selection fallback must keep precedence so clicking a Finder filename label still selects its row rather than entering rename mode.

### Actual behavior

cua-driver 0.28.0, Automator's Save As sheet name field:

```json
{"delivery":{"mode":"unknown"},"effect":"suspected_noop",
 "escalation":{"reason":"suspected_noop","target":"pixel"},"route":"accessibility"}
```

with the text

```
❔ Dispatched AXPress to [296] AXTextField ""; the app replied -25206 (kAXErrorActionUnsupported) ...
⚠️ Element does not advertise AXPress (actions: AXShowMenu, AXConfirm). Action may have been a no-op.
⚠️ Unverified: the target was watched for 2120 ms after the dispatch and nothing changed ...
```

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.0 (`click.rs::perform_ax_click` and its `suspected_noop` path are identical on `main`)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: AppKit; Automator save panel, also reproducible on any action-parameter text field

### Evidence

`platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs::perform_ax_click` handles an unadvertised `AXPress` by trying `select_nearest_container` and then a pixel click verified by an `AXSelected` read-back. A text field in a save panel or an action parameter has no selectable ancestor, so both return `None` and control falls through to the plain `perform_action(element, "AXPress")`, which returns `-25206`; `suspected_noop` then appends the "does not advertise" warning. No branch ever writes `AXFocused`, which is the action the role actually supports.

### Workaround and additional context

Call `set_value` (which focuses the control itself) or click by pixel coordinates. Both cost a step and the pixel route needs a fresh snapshot. Related: #3835 (the same `-25206` reply being turned into a tool error).

title: [Bug]: macOS `set_value` cannot report its commit as a boolean: a bound control echoes the read-back
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

A `set_value` commit signal cannot be a boolean. The evidence a driver has for "the application took this value" is an accessibility read-back, and a control whose value is a binding target echoes that read-back whether or not the application took it - so the read-back can refute a commit and never establish one. #3816 (for #3807) introduces `ActionResult.committed: Option<bool>` and sets it to `true` when the written value survives the commit gesture. Measured against an application's own persisted model, that `true` is wrong on exactly the controls the field exists for.

### Reproduction

Automator's "New Text File" action has a `Save as:` parameter field whose value the workflow persists into `<doc>.workflow/Contents/document.wflow` as `newFileName`, which makes the application's own model readable.

1. `set_value` a new name on that field through the `AXValue` + `AXConfirm` route.
2. Read the reply: the value survived the gesture.
3. `cmd+s` and read `newFileName`: the application kept its own value.

### Expected behavior

Report a three-valued verdict instead of a boolean:

- `not_committed` - the gesture could not be dispatched, or the value did not survive it.
- `committed` - an editing session that carried this value through the application's own field editor was observed to end with the value in place.
- `unproven` - the value survived, and the only evidence is a read-back.

`unproven` has to be a distinct value rather than an absent field, because an absent field already means "this action has no commit step" (a popup, a slider). An `AXValue`-delivered value can only ever reach `unproven`, which is the honest answer and is why the boolean was reachable at all.

### Actual behavior

cua-driver 0.28.0 with #3816 applied, on that parameter field and on Automator's save-panel name field:

```json
{"committed":true,"delivery":{"mode":"background"},"effect":"confirmed",
 "evidence":[{"kind":"value_readback"}],"route":"accessibility"}
```

"Committed via AXConfirm: the app's editing pipeline holds the value." The application's `document.wflow` still held its own value.

A second measurement rules out the obvious repair. Writing `AXValue`, proving focus, then pressing Tab really does end the edit session (the app stops reporting the element as its focused element) and the value still survives the read-back - and the application discarded it. So "the edit session ended" is not a positive signal either unless the value reached the field editor, which only keystrokes do.

`type_text` has the same gap from the other side: it delivers no end-of-edit at all, so its successful read-back on a native single-line text role says the characters are in the editor and nothing about what the application will keep.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.0; the `committed` field itself arrives with #3816 (`pr/set-value-commit`), so this report is against that shape rather than `main`
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: AppKit; Automator (action parameter field, save panel name field)

### Evidence

`platform-macos/src/tools/set_value.rs::judge_commit` (as proposed in #3816) returns `Some(true)` whenever the written value survives the commit gesture, and the survival check is `copy_string_attr(element, "AXValue")`. That is the same attribute the write set, on a control that answers from its own string rather than from the model behind the binding. The driver's AppKit harness fixture already encodes the distinction: it mirrors `controlTextDidChange` into a label, and AppKit raises that notification for keystrokes but not for a programmatic `setStringValue:`.

### Workaround and additional context

Treat `committed: true` as "not refuted" and verify against the application's own output. Refs #3807, #3816.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): make set_value on a native text field reach the app
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: a native single-line text field on macOS reported a successful value write the app never saw (#3807), and could not say whether the app took it (#3851).
- What changed: such a field is now typed; `ActionResult.committed` (`committed` / `not_committed` / `unproven`, RFC #4009) is `committed` only after a typed edit ended with the value in place. Contract 0.9.0. Non-goals: `AXTextArea`, secure fields.

<details><summary>Mechanism and measurements</summary>

| control | route | `committed` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AXTextField` (not search, not secure), typeable value | select the old value in UTF-16 units, type, Tab | `committed` if the value survived the ended edit |
| search field, combo box, date/time field | `AXValue`, then `AXConfirm` or Return/Tab | `unproven` at best |
| secure field | `AXValue` only, as on main | absent |
| `AXTextArea`, web content | `AXValue` (main's net-zero document edit kept) | `not_committed` with the reason |
| popups, sliders, steppers | unchanged | absent |

**Since the last round.** Re-expressed on main `09b38ab66` (cua-driver-rs 0.47.4) instead of replaying the October branch, keeping main's later `set_value` work, including #4989's net-zero document edit after a direct `AXValue` write. Two decisions changed. Secure fields stay `AXValue`-only: a masked or unreadable value gives no safe length for the whole-value selection, so typing could leave part of the old value in place. Typed writes skip the net-zero document edit, because they already go through the app's own edit model.

**Why the typed route.** Measured on an Automator action parameter, one probe per route, with the app's persisted model (`document.wflow` `newFileName`) as the oracle:

| route | accessibility read-back | app's own model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| focus + select-all + typed keystrokes + Tab (shipped) | `M1_retype.txt` | `M1_retype.txt`; the app took it |
| `AXValue` + proven `AXFocused` + Tab | `R2_valtab.txt` | pre-edit value; discarded |
| `AXValue` + the element's advertised `AXConfirm` | `R1_confirm.txt` | pre-edit value; discarded |

Ending the edit session is not what commits; going through the field editor is.

**Why a confirm alone is never `committed`.** Font Book's search field advertises `AXConfirm`, answers it with success, and searches only on typed input, so an `AXValue` write plus that confirm reads back the query while the list stays on all typefaces. `judge_commit` has one positive signal, a typed edit that ended with the value in place (the control lost the app's keyboard focus after the typed gesture); every `AXValue` route reaches `unproven` at best, with the sentence naming why.

**Verdict plumbing.** `ActionCommit` in `cua-driver-contract::outputs` has one wire spelling per value (`as_wire` / `from_wire`); `ActionExecutionRecord::committed` parses it back and an unknown spelling yields `None`. `type_text` reports `unproven` on a binding target, since it delivers no end-of-edit. `committed` never promotes `effect`.

**Save panel fallback.** The background keystroke gate refuses process-scoped keys while the app owns another eligible top-level window, which an open save panel always is. A refused `Retype` falls back to the control's advertised `AXConfirm` (`refused_keystroke_plan`), whose verdict stays `unproven`; the keystroke rung is re-gated as `GenericKey` in `resolve_write_plan` before it is promised.

**Retype mechanics.** Reuses `type_text::type_and_drain` without its focus and settle logic, because `set_value` sets focus and the replaced selection itself. The old value is selected with an `AXSelectedTextRange` write measured in UTF-16 units, as `NSString` counts: a `chars()` count left the tail of `😀AB` unselected, so retyping `zed` committed `zedB`. A control that refuses the range gets an `AXValue` clear; if neither works the write refuses rather than appending.

**Compatibility.** `ActionResult.committed` is additive: a 0.9.0 SDK against a 0.8.0 daemon sees it absent, and a typed 0.8.0 SDK rejects it, so SDK and daemon upgrade together (RFC #4009's recorded risk). The manifest and both UniFFI binding sets are regenerated, not hand-merged.

**Mutation.** Routing a binding-target field back to `ValueThenKey("tab")` in `write_plan` fails `a_binding_target_field_is_written_by_typing` and `a_value_keystrokes_cannot_carry_keeps_the_ax_value_route` (platform-macos lib: 734 passed, 2 failed). The same mutant at `a91c7d322` also fails `harness_appkit_set_value_commits_the_edit` in the bench VM (0/1 pass).

**Supporting AppKit harness.** Full `harness_appkit_test` at `e43ce5118` in the bench VM (`bench-seed-v11`, `mcp --direct` shim, cua-driver 0.47.4 unsigned build sha256 `91e8e926…`): 33/36 pass, including `harness_appkit_set_value_commits_the_edit`, `harness_appkit_set_value_replaces_a_non_bmp_value_whole` and `harness_appkit_popup_set_value_keeps_front_key_focus_background`. The three failures are the documented direct-mode limits that fail the same way on main in this seed: `counter_px_background`, `exact_activation_with_agent_cursor`, `pending_snapshot_cannot_retarget_token`. The mutation at `a91c7d322` fails its owner case (0/1 pass).

**Known gaps.** No live case covers the `AXConfirm` route (the AppKit fixture has no control that advertises it), so "a confirm alone is at most `unproven`" rests on `judge_commit`'s unit test. `AXComboBox`, `AXDateField` and `AXTimeField` are covered by the unit route table only, and the web path by the existing `target_in_web_area` check.

</details>

## Related work

Fixes #3807, #3851. Supersedes #3816, #3857.

RFC: accepted #4009 (items 2, 4); its document #4367 lands with or before this.

## Compatibility and risk

Review first: `platform-macos/src/tools/set_value.rs::write_plan`.

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS; typed writes are gated like keystrokes; other single-line text roles get a confirm or end-of-edit key.
- Risk and rollback: other roles keep `AXValue`; the verdict is advisory; revert.

## Validation

- Checks at `e43ce5118`: contract 72, core 1238+1, platform-macos 736, e2e 38, sdk 113, Python 23, TS 16, 0 failed; generators clean; mutation in details. Production +511/-68, tests +359/-9.
- Manual or platform evidence: supporting bench-VM AppKit run at `e43ce5118`, 33/36; three setup limits also fail on main (details).
- Known gaps or CI still required: the canonical macOS Lume run.

- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

title: [RFC]: Independent session-label visibility for native cursors
body:
## Primary area
Cua Driver

## Summary
Add an opt-in, per-session way to suppress the native cursor's session-label text while retaining the cursor and existing delivery/target context indicators. Keep current rendering as the default. The session identifier and transport ownership must remain unchanged.

## Motivation and current state
An embedding application may already show the active task in its own UI. Repeating an opaque session identifier next to the native cursor adds visual noise. Renaming or rotating the session to change its appearance is not an appropriate presentation API.

Source inspection at `5fcd67326dd0406bca823e5488cf39f47491c869` confirms:
- [`StartSessionInput` and cursor setters](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/5fcd67326dd0406bca823e5488cf39f47491c869/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-contract/src/inputs.rs#L302-L440) have no independent label-visibility option.
- [Shared render state](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/5fcd67326dd0406bca823e5488cf39f47491c869/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cursor-overlay/src/render_state.rs#L153-L206) reveals labels initially and on hover, with no public suppression setting.
- [Theme documentation](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/5fcd67326dd0406bca823e5488cf39f47491c869/libs/cua-driver/docs/cursor-themes.md#L18-L43) explicitly separates native badges from dotLottie artwork. Custom cursor themes cannot hide this text.

The same missing public option was observed when inspecting the `cua-driver-rs-v0.28.1` source. This is a source-level capability assessment, not a claim of fresh native runtime tests.

## Goals
- Hide label text, including initial and hover reveals, without disabling the native cursor.
- Preserve distinct named sessions and lease isolation.
- Apply the initial preference before the first cursor frame; expose the effective preference for inspection.
- Use shared policy across macOS, Windows, and Linux, preserving existing behavior when omitted.

## Non-goals
Custom label text, action-status text, font/color/CSS customization, hiding delivery/target chips, changing input delivery, hiding consent or stop controls, or changing the theme artifact format.

## Proposal
Introduce an optional `cursor_badge: { show_session_label: boolean }` on `start_session`, with `true` as the creation default. A separate `set_agent_cursor_badge` operation changes the preference for an existing owned session; `get_agent_cursor_state` reports it. Exact public API placement is a maintainer decision in this RFC.

Store visibility separately from the label and runtime key. Route it through shared cursor render state. When false, suppress text and label-only hover polling/timers; continue drawing existing context chips according to their lifecycle. Do not leave an empty label pill when no other badge content is visible. Preserve the normal chip background when chips remain visible.

Repeated `start_session` without the new field must preserve an existing session's preference. Explicit settings update it atomically before any first reveal. Ordinary actions, theme changes, idle wakeups, and metadata refreshes must not reset it. Ending a session drops the preference with the session.

## Alternatives considered
- Omit, blank, or reuse one session label: changes naming/lookup semantics and is unsuitable for independent concurrent named sessions.
- Change dotLottie artwork: the host renders labels outside the theme.
- Disable the entire cursor: removes useful action feedback.
- Add only an initial setting: smaller API, but requires session recreation to change presentation.

## Compatibility and migration
Additive, default-preserving API. Clients must feature-detect support and retain current visuals on older runtimes; do not send unknown fields to old strict schemas. Do not reinterpret the removed legacy `set_agent_cursor_style` API. No runtime implementation is included before the RFC decision.

## Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry
Existing ownership checks, permission prompts, delivery/target indicators, and stop controls remain intact. Suppression is presentation only and does not make identifiers secret in logs or protocol responses. No new telemetry or session-content logging. The public proposal includes no private screenshots or transcripts.

## Validation and acceptance evidence
Required after acceptance: default/round-trip/schema tests; hidden-label initial, hover, idle, and theme-change tests; preserved chip layout and no empty pill; two-session isolation; end/recreate lifecycle; and native overlay evidence on macOS, Windows, X11 and supported Wayland environments. Verify that label-only hover polling stops without stopping chip/action animation. Do not mark implementation complete without the repository's platform evidence.

## Unresolved questions
- Is this best exposed as a dedicated badge operation plus initial selection, or another existing host configuration surface?
- Should changing false to true replay the normal initial reveal? Proposed: yes.

## Submission checks
- [x] Searched issues and PRs for session-label and hide-label/cursor proposals; no matching open implementation was identified.
- [x] Contains no credentials, private user/partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] Describes alternatives, compatibility, and required acceptance evidence.

## RFC document pull request

https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3875

title: [RFC]: Add an explicit bind address to Lume VNC listeners
body:
**Primary area**

Lume

**Summary**

Lume should expose an explicit VNC listener bind address across every VM-run surface. A caller should be able to keep VNC enabled while binding it to IPv4 loopback, and should be able to request wildcard/LAN binding explicitly when remote access is intended. Omission should initially preserve the current all-interface behavior for compatibility; changing the default can be evaluated separately after the explicit contract exists.

**Motivation and current state**

In the tested Lume 0.5.3 daemon setup, the management HTTP listener is loopback-only, but each enabled VNC service is observed listening on `*:<ephemeral-port>`. This creates a separate network reachability boundary even when operators deliberately expose the management API only through local access or an SSH local forward.

The desired deployment still needs VNC for local automation, so disabling the VNC listener is not equivalent. Lume’s current VNC service contract accepts only port, password, and virtual-machine inputs; it has no bind/listen-address input ([VNCService.swift lines 7–12](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/754eec754991e1760100621e9bfe7ec1395cc7db/libs/lume/src/VNC/VNCService.swift#L7-L12)). Its `_VZVNCServer` construction likewise supplies a port, queue, and security configuration, but no address ([VNCService.swift lines 72–82](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/754eec754991e1760100621e9bfe7ec1395cc7db/libs/lume/src/VNC/VNCService.swift#L72-L82)). The direct-run CLI exposes VNC port and password but no bind address ([Run.swift lines 69–77](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/754eec754991e1760100621e9bfe7ec1395cc7db/libs/lume/src/Commands/Run.swift#L69-L77)). By contrast, the management HTTP server explicitly binds `127.0.0.1` ([Server.swift lines 424–443](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/754eec754991e1760100621e9bfe7ec1395cc7db/libs/lume/src/Server/Server.swift#L424-L443)).

**Goals**

- Keep VNC enabled while binding its listener to `127.0.0.1`.
- Retain an explicit wildcard/LAN mode for users who intentionally connect from another host.
- Apply one bind-address contract consistently to direct CLI, detached, HTTP, and MCP VM starts.
- Reject invalid or unavailable bind addresses observably rather than accepting a run whose requested listener policy was not applied.
- Preserve ephemeral-port and fixed-port behavior.
- Report session/connect information consistent with the address actually bound.

**Non-goals**

- Removing VNC or changing the separate enabled/disabled policy delivered by [PR #3209](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3209).
- Changing VNC authentication or password generation.
- Exposing the Lume management API beyond loopback.
- Weakening SSH server restrictions, enabling remote SSH forwarding, or changing guest networking.
- Treating this public design request as a vulnerability disclosure.

**Proposal**

1. Extend the common VNC run policy with an optional `bindAddress` value owned by the VNC service.
2. Expose it as `lume run <vm> --vnc-bind-address <address>` and as the corresponding `vncBindAddress` field on HTTP and MCP run requests. Detached starts must forward the same value unchanged.
3. Support at minimum explicit IPv4 loopback (`127.0.0.1`) and wildcard (`0.0.0.0`). IPv6 loopback/wildcard should be added only if the underlying VNC service can implement it with the same semantics.
4. Validate that a specific non-wildcard address belongs to the host and can be bound. Reject invalid or unavailable addresses before returning an accepted asynchronous start, or expose a terminal start failure through the run-operation result.
5. Record the selected bind mode in VM session/status information. Do not advertise an external/LAN VNC URL when the listener is loopback-only; preserve the local VNC client path, which already connects to `127.0.0.1` ([VNCService.swift lines 203–212](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/754eec754991e1760100621e9bfe7ec1395cc7db/libs/lume/src/VNC/VNCService.swift#L203-L212)).
6. In the first compatible release, omission retains the existing all-interface behavior established in [#30](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/30). Operators who require the narrower boundary opt in explicitly. A later default change, if desired, should have its own deprecation and migration decision.

**Alternatives considered**

- **Disable VNC:** Supported on current `main` by [PR #3209](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3209), but it removes the local VNC service needed by this use case.
- **Rely on the host firewall:** Can narrow reachability, but does not make the Lume process’s requested listener boundary explicit or portable.
- **Keep wildcard binding and use an SSH tunnel anyway:** The tunnel works, but the original wildcard listener remains independently reachable on interfaces allowed by host networking.
- **Change the default to loopback immediately:** Safer for new deployments, but breaks the intentional LAN-access behavior requested in [#30](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/30). The additive option should land first.

**Compatibility and migration**

This proposal is additive when the field is omitted: existing commands and API clients keep the current listener behavior. Loopback-only deployments add the new value; LAN deployments may continue omitting it initially or set `0.0.0.0` explicitly. Rollback is omission of the new field. If maintainers later choose loopback as the default, first document and warn about the future change, then require explicit wildcard binding for LAN users in the designated breaking/default-change release.

**Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry**

The bind address is a network permission boundary, not a replacement for VNC authentication. Loopback mode should create no wildcard listener; wildcard mode must be explicit when selected. Logs and telemetry may record only a normalized bind mode such as `loopback`, `specific`, or `wildcard`; they must not record VNC passwords, private host identities, or session contents. This proposal does not change the dedicated-account or SSH-forwarding restrictions of the deployment that motivated it.

**Validation and acceptance evidence**

- In loopback mode, the owning Lume process listens only on `127.0.0.1:<assigned-port>`; a local VNC connection succeeds and a connection to the host’s non-loopback address is refused.
- In explicit wildcard mode, the listener binds the documented wildcard address and a controlled LAN connection succeeds.
- Both modes work with ephemeral and fixed ports.
- Direct CLI, detached CLI, HTTP, and MCP starts produce the same bind result.
- Invalid, non-local, or unavailable specific addresses produce a structured failure and never silently fall back to wildcard.
- Returned VNC/session information matches the selected boundary.
- The `vnc disabled` policy still creates no listener.
- Tests and evidence use synthetic VM names and contain no VNC password or private network identifier.

**Unresolved questions**

- Does the private `_VZVNCServer` runtime used by Lume expose a bind-address selector or property that Lume can call safely? No such selector exists in Lume’s current `VNCService` protocol, implementation, or constructor call ([VNCService.swift lines 7–12 and 72–82](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/754eec754991e1760100621e9bfe7ec1395cc7db/libs/lume/src/VNC/VNCService.swift#L7-L82)), but source inspection does not establish whether the private runtime has an undocumented capability.
- Should the public contract accept only IP literals, or also interface names/hostnames with clearly defined resolution semantics?
- Should IPv6 be included in the first implementation or deferred until the underlying service behavior is proven?
- Should a later release change the omitted default from wildcard to loopback, given the compatibility expectation established by [#30](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/30)?

**RFC document pull request**

None; the issue body is sufficient for initial discussion.

**Submission checks**

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: fix(cua-driver): hide agent cursor for background actions on another Space
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a Cua Driver background computer-use action against an app on another Space paints the floating agent cursor over the user's current (e.g. fullscreen) app, and it is unclear the action is isolated. Fixes #3801.
- What changed: window-targeted actions (click, double-click, right-click, drag, scroll, type_text, set_value) now route cursor display through one helper that hides the agent cursor when a background delivery targets a window not painted on the current Space. The show/hide decision lives in portable `cua-driver-core`; Space resolution and a sticky per-cursor paint flag live in the macOS overlay. Delivery, focus suppression, pacing, and result reporting are unchanged — the cursor is display-only telemetry.

## Related work

Fixes #3801

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required — no tool schema, MCP, protocol, or CLI change; behavior delta is confined to an off-Space background paint path.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: user-visible only when a background action targets an off-Space window (cursor stays hidden instead of floating over the foreground app). Same-Space background, foreground, desktop-scope, and explicit move_cursor behavior unchanged. No API/CLI/MCP change; Windows/Linux overlays untouched.
- Risk and rollback: low — suppression requires positive off-Space evidence and fails visible on unknown state; any later positioning command unhides. Rollback: revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` 632 passed (4 new decision-table tests); `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract` 45 passed; 6 new headless overlay-model tests cover the hide/unhide state machine; `rustfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: none on macOS hardware from this environment — needs the macOS harness (`libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh`) in CI.
- Known gaps or CI still required: macOS build + overlay model tests + desktop E2E on the candidate SHA; upstream CI must cover the Apple-only crate.

title: fix(cua-driver): unify Wayland screenshot and input frames under fractional scaling
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves:
  On a Wayland session with fractional display scaling (e.g. GNOME at 150%), the coordinate frame of the screenshots returned by `get_desktop_state` and `get_window_state` did not match the frame the input tools consume. Any `px` action grounded on a driver screenshot missed its target by exactly the scale factor, and `get_window_state` returned an image of the wrong region entirely. `get_screen_size` additionally reported the XWayland root geometry with `scale_factor: 1.0`, matching neither frame.
- What changed:
  The driver now resolves the compositor-logical frame from `zxdg_output_manager_v1` (the same protocol the overlay already consumes) on single-output layouts and unifies all three tools around it: `get_desktop_state` feeds the logical frame to the existing capture normalizer so the PNG is downscaled into the input frame with a truthful scale factor; `get_window_state` maps the logical crop rect through the capture buffer's own backing scale and resizes back to logical dims; `get_screen_size` reports the logical size with the real backing scale. When no single logical output is advertised (older compositors, multi-output fractional layouts), each tool keeps its previous frame and logs the fallback at debug level.

## Related work

Refs #3061 (the crop-and-resize direction follows the approach demonstrated in the issue report).

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): N/A — bug fix restoring the documented screenshot-to-action contract; no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  Screenshot pixel dimensions and `scale_factor` values change on single-output fractional-scale Wayland desktops (they now match the input frame, as documented). Scale-1.0 desktops, X11 sessions, and Hyprland sessions are byte-for-byte unchanged: at scale 1.0 the new crop path delegates to the legacy 1:1 crop, and the X11/Hyprland branches are untouched.
- Risk and rollback:
  Low. Every new lookup fails closed to the exact legacy frame (multi-output and missing-protocol cases keep prior behavior), guarded by a 5s probe cache shared across the three call sites. Roll back by reverting these two files.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` — 454 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (11 new: 1.5x frame fixtures for the desktop normalizer, logical-output/scale unit guards, scale-aware crop discrimination showing the legacy 1:1 crop returns the wrong region, unit-scale equivalence, degenerate-input and negative-origin guards, fail-closed query without a compositor). `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Manual or platform evidence:
  Headless unit coverage only. No live GNOME fractional-scale session was available in this environment, and the canonical Linux desktop harness (`scripts/ci/linux/run-rust-e2e.sh`) requires a GUI session, so it was not run here.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  Live GNOME 150% confirmation on the exact candidate SHA (`get_screen_size` logical + scale, desktop PNG dims, window-crop region) plus the Linux Rust unit/compile lane and the canonical desktop E2E matrix before merge. Multi-output fractional layouts remain on the legacy frame (documented limitation).

- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
