title: fix(cua-driver): preserve uncertainty in macOS text outcomes
body:
## Scope

Refs #3389

Makes macOS `type_text` results report only what the driver observed. An uncertain AX write can become confirmed when fresh evidence shows up. It never turns into "zero delivered" or "safe to replay".

```diff
 native text attempt
-  ↳ boolean/count → legacy JSON → inferred action result
-  ↳ unknown AX effect → keystroke replay / retry advice
+  ↳ retained target + trusted native readback, drained → TypedProgress
+      ↳ actual transport/delivery → existing ActionExecutionRecord
+  ↳ still unknown after the drain → unverifiable; reobserve, never replay
```

- Missing, unchanged, unrelated, reverted, web, or unproven-ancestry observations can't invent delivery counts, `delivery_failed`, or safe suffix retries.
- The ladder stops after an accepted or uncertain AX write. Three cases skip the AX write and go to bounded synthesis: a known unsupported attribute, an element that reports `AXSelectedText` as not settable, and web content. Nothing was written in those cases, so the keystrokes are the first delivery, not a replay.
- The exact-target, snapshot, permission, session, foreground-restoration and synthesis-budget gates are unchanged.
- No public schema, new module or dependency, or other-platform migration. The work is in `platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs`, plus small ancestry-result comparisons in `hotkey`, `press_key` and `set_value`, and the shared `type_text` recovery hint.

### Recovery invariant

A fresh read can resolve an uncertain write to "confirmed", but absence after a read/drain must not by itself resolve it to "zero delivered / safe to replay".

An accepted `AXSelectedText` write is read back through the same bounded drain the keystroke rung uses (the #3842 mechanism). The drain watches the same target's value and keeps the strongest `TypedProgress` it observes:

- If the expected full value appears, the write is `confirmed` and the drain stops.
- If a trusted prefix appears, the write is `partial` with the known delivered count. It is never replayed automatically.
- If the value stays unchanged, missing or untrusted through the drain, the write is still `unverifiable`. It gets no "0 delivered" count and is not retryable.

User-facing guidance, in the result text, the tool description, the `type_text` recovery hint and the action-result contract:

> Reobserve/verify the intended postcondition. Seeing the expected text confirms the earlier write. If the effect is still absent or ambiguous, keep the prior action outcome unknown; do not replay automatically.

### Native findings from review

- **The `unsupported` fixture cell returned `unverifiable`, not `confirmed`.** `isAccessibilitySelectorAllowed` alone doesn't make AppKit reject the attribute. AppKit reports it settable, accepts the write and drops it, so the synthesis fallback was unreachable. The fixture now removes `AXSelectedText` from the attribute list and the legacy setter. A probe confirms the write returns `kAXErrorAttributeUnsupported` (-25205).
- **Production consequence.** A stock `NSTextField` that isn't being edited reports `AXSelectedText` as not settable, yet `AXUIElementSetAttributeValue` returns success and drops the text. Before this change the rung would have stopped there with zero characters and `unverifiable`. The rung now checks `AXIsAttributeSettable` first and types into such an element. A new `unsettable` fixture cell (a stock `NSTextField`) covers it.
- **The background web rows (Electron px, Tauri AX, WKWebView AX/px, Tauri editor) failed on the hosted lane.** In web content an AX write is a shim echo that the page never sees, so it could only ever end `unverifiable`. When keystrokes are allowed, web content now goes straight to keystrokes without an AX write. Semantic-only routes still use the AX write and stay `unverifiable`.
- **The single synchronous read produced a false partial on a field that publishes late** (the #3841 shape). The drain above fixes it. A new `lagging` fixture cell publishes its value 400 ms after the write and must confirm with one write and zero keystrokes.

### Regressions

- `accepted_write_published_after_several_polls_is_confirmed_once`: the write is accepted at t=0 and the value is unchanged at the immediate sample, then published after several polls. Result: one action, eventual confirmation with 6 delivered, accessibility route, no CGEvent fallback.
- `accepted_write_that_never_publishes_stays_unverifiable_after_the_drain`: the value never publishes. After the drain the result is `unverifiable`, with no delivered count, no structured retry, no `retry_from_character`, and the do-not-replay guidance.
- The AppKit text-outcome harness now has five cells: `native`, `stale`, `unsupported`, `unsettable` and `lagging`. Each is checked against independent fixture state (writes, keystrokes, value, unrelated field).

### Main merge (single-line submit)

Main's single-line submit path (#7352) now runs on this branch's outcome model. When a single-line field is asked for one line plus Return, the line is written alone and drained until the field reads back the pre-write value with its selection replaced by the line. Only that match confirms the write and lets Return go out, and only after the field is confirmed focused. Anything else is `unverifiable`, never a partial count, so a replaced selection can't invite a duplicating retry. A confirmed line whose field lost focus reports partial delivery without the Return. Main's `write_left_field_untouched` keystroke fallback is gone, because this branch never replays after an accepted AX write.

### Main merge (AppKit cell manifest)

Main now lists AppKit E2E cells in `scripts/ci/macos/appkit-cells.tsv` (#7229). Each row maps one cell id to one exact test, so a single cell can run alone. The text-outcome test used to record five cells from one test. It is now five tests, one per field (`native`, `stale`, `unsupported`, `unsettable`, `lagging`), each with its own row. The assertions are unchanged. The runner test that checks the manifest now also scans `appkit_text_outcomes.rs`. The scoped repository checks for this merge ran on Linux: the macOS runner and E2E inventory tests, rustfmt, and `cargo check -p cua-driver-e2e --tests`. The AppKit harness is macOS-only, so it was not compiled or run.

### Main merge (WebKit set_value retry)

Main's #7950 added a focused retry to `set_value` for WebKit fields that ignore a write. On this branch `target_in_web_area` returns `Option<bool>`, so the merge keeps unknown ancestry untrusted for read-back but runs the focused retry only on confirmed web content, as main did. Verified on Linux by code review and rustfmt; the macOS crate was not built here.

### Replaced selections

Typing replaces the selection, so a growing value can't tell a partial insert from a complete replacement. With `bc` selected in `abc`, typing `Xbc` leaves `aXbc`. Counting growth reports only `X`, and the batched keystroke path would then resend `bc`. The AX write and the keystroke rung now read the selection just before writing, after the element is focused. A shortfall is counted only from what took the selection's place. The value is read together with the selection, so a focus handler that rewrites the field can't leave a stale baseline. When the selection can't be read, or its range doesn't fit the value, the drain still waits through a growing prefix, but a final shortfall is `unverifiable` and is never resent. When a batched send is partly taken, the rest goes out only if a fresh read shows exactly the delivered prefix with a collapsed caret right after it. Otherwise the partial result is reported as is.

The shared `type_text_incomplete` recovery hint said to "type only the missing rest" even when the result set `retryable: false`. It now says to read the field and not type the rest automatically in that case.

### Main merge (web focus helper)

Main moved the hotkey web-area focus point into `web_ax_focus_point` (#8081). The merge keeps main's helper and compares `target_in_web_area(...) == Some(true)`, because this branch returns `Option<bool>` there.

### Compatibility

Trusted partial insertion keeps `type_text_incomplete`, but it now has `retryable: false` and no `retry_from_character`. Uncertain accepted AX writes, including large atomic writes, report uncertainty instead of going through synthesis-budget or replay handling. An accepted write can take up to the drain bound before it reports `unverifiable`.

## Contributor coordination

#3811 by @will-bogusz targets #3809's replacement-editor readback, and #3842 is his bounded drain. Will's native findings (the fixture's dropped write, its production consequence, the late-publishing false partial) and @kvnloo's recovery invariant are what this revision addresses. The drain composes #3842's mechanism onto this branch's `TypedProgress` shape. This PR does not supersede #3811.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks:

- `platform-macos`: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos`, 659 passed and 7 ignored, including the `type_text` tests.
- `cua-driver-core`: clippy `-D warnings` and lib tests, 1173 passed.
- `cua-driver-e2e`: clippy `-D warnings`, and `harness_appkit_test` compiles.
- The AppKit fixture builds with `tests/fixtures/build/macos.sh --only appkit`.
- The generated macOS MCP reference is regenerated and `runner.ts --library cua-driver --check` passes.

The verify-cua-driver macOS Lume lane ran `full` at 058927670b, before the main merge, on seed `cua-driver-browser-baseline-20261104-tk86-ax`: 188 cells passed (183 delivered, 5 expected refusals), 0 failed. That includes all five `harness_appkit_text_outcomes_match_independent_state` cells and every Electron, Tauri and WKWebView `type_text`, `type_submit` and `editor_save` row in both delivery modes. The worker stopped and the standard daemon was restored.

After an earlier main merge, head 8de013c167 merged with main c49e729df6 was checked on macOS:

- `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-core`: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` (with `cua-driver-e2e`, all targets) and `cargo test --locked`, all passing. `harness_appkit_test` compiles.
- The verify-cua-driver macOS Lume lane ran `full` on the same merge and passed: 190 cells delivered, 5 expected refusals, 0 failed. That includes all five `harness_appkit_text_outcomes_match_independent_state` cells (`native`, `stale`, `unsupported`, `unsettable`, `lagging`) and every Electron, Tauri and WKWebView `type_text`, `type_submit` and `editor_save` row. The worker stopped.

Not run here: the standalone-browser lane, the SIP-on permission flow, the Linux and Windows platform crates and reference snapshots, and Linux desktop E2E.

The CI quick stage's `SPDX headers (Cua Driver, MIT)` check is not caused by this PR. It reports 659 files across `libs/cua-driver` that lack the header, and main has the same count. This PR's only new source file carries the header. Clippy on `cursor-overlay` also fails in code this PR doesn't touch.

Size: production code is over the add limit because the outcome model rewrites `type_text` result handling, but the net change is negative.

title: [RFC]: expose passive native observations without action handles
body:
## Primary area

Cua Driver

## Summary

Add typed passive `observations` to `get_window_state`, alongside the unchanged actionable `elements` array, and let shared `verify_state` evaluate both. Observable state must not require an action handle. This is the compatibility-preserving proposal for #2958; it is not yet an accepted public-contract decision.

## Motivation and current state

In #2958, Calculator display text appears in `tree_markdown` but not `structuredContent.elements`. The macOS projector drops every node without an action index. `verify_state` reads only that array and therefore returns `unknown / observation_unavailable` for the display.

The mechanism remains in main `625118a9076e51da2f57b6a5d475972030197443`:

- `platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs:823` requires `node.element_index` before projecting a row.
- `cua-driver-core/src/expectation.rs:154` consumes only structured `elements`.
- `cua-driver-contract/src/windows.rs:203` requires a non-null `WindowElement.element_index: u64`; inserting nullable indices is not a transparent additive change.

Paths are under `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/`. Linux and Windows builders contain the same non-indexed-row filter, although native providers differ in which rows they index.

Eight out-of-tree cases against the real shared evaluator, two public-type deserialization assertions, and 16 existing expectation tests passed during investigation. These are source/shared-contract characterization, not a fresh current-main native Calculator reproduction or a fix certification.

## Goals

- Publish readable passive native state structurally without granting an action handle.
- Verify a uniquely selected passive value through the existing shared predicate engine.
- Preserve actionable rows, tokens, counts, authorization, and action-cache isolation.
- Keep scope, query, traversal bounds, provenance, and completeness explicit across platforms.

## Non-goals

- Treating action acknowledgement as task success or retrying delivered actions.
- Normalizing bidi characters, locale-specific numbers, whitespace, or Calculator presentation implicitly.
- Adding ordinal selectors, first-match behavior, cached observation stores, new tools, or a new authorization path.
- Claiming role-only `value_equals: "6"` is unambiguous when Calculator exposes both expression and result.
- Replacing or absorbing contributor work in #3817 or #3814.

## Proposal

Keep `WindowElement` and the actionable `elements` contract unchanged. Add optional `observations: Vec<WindowObservation>` and `observations_complete: bool` fields to `WindowStateOutput`.

A passive observation has `role`, `depth`, and optional `label`, `value`, `frame`, `parent_index`, and `in_web_content`. It has no action index or token. `parent_index`, when available, refers to the nearest published actionable ancestor, not a new passive-node identity. Raw values remain unchanged.

Both projections come from the same bounded native traversal. Passive rows must honor the requested exact window and query, and retain web-content provenance through collapsed containers. A query excludes unrelated passive rows; this change must not invent action indices to reuse the current index-only query projector. Missing native metadata stays absent, not false or fabricated.

The shared observation provider combines indexed rows with passive rows for the existing predicate evaluator. This is a private evaluation projection, not a new public actionable array. It does not parse `tree_markdown`, refresh the action cache, or perform an extra native walk.

`elements_complete` retains its existing addressable-domain meaning. `observations_complete` describes the passive domain; missing means unknown. The combined verifier can claim complete coverage only when both domains are proven complete and unfiltered. Absent new fields from older producers must not become proof of absence. Publishing useful positive observations does not require claiming completeness; adapters may report false until the native walk can prove exhaustion.

macOS AX, Windows UIA, and Linux AT-SPI adapters implement the same contract. X11/Wayland transport choice does not excuse silently omitting available passive AT-SPI state; inaccessible providers/compositors retain explicit degraded or incomplete outcomes.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Unified `elements` with optional index:** structurally simplest, with one model and no provider union, but changes a required SDK field and the addressable-only/count/query contract. It requires explicit migration and consumer audits. This remains the strongest alternative for review.
2. **Assign action indices to passive rows:** conflates observation with actionability and changes dispatch/cache behavior; rejected.
3. **Parse markdown inside verification:** makes presentation formatting authoritative and bypasses typed provenance; rejected.
4. **Change only completeness:** #3817 addresses the addressable domain. It cannot restore missing display values.
5. **Normalize every value or select the first match:** silently changes exact-equality/ambiguity semantics and can produce misleading success; excluded.

## Compatibility and migration

The proposed fields and record are additive. Existing `WindowElement`, action indices/tokens, and actionable counts stay unchanged. Generated MCP schemas, SDK bindings, and documentation must evolve together. New clients must tolerate missing passive observations on older drivers.

The verifier can newly satisfy or reject passive predicates when native evidence exists; it retains conservative unknown results when evidence is missing, ambiguous, or untrusted. `value_equals` remains exact. No disk migration, new dependency, retained observation store, or new lifecycle is proposed.

A feature release is appropriate for the new typed public capability. Rollback removes adapter publication/provider consumption while retaining optional contract fields for compatibility; it must not reinterpret a missing field as empty, complete state.

## Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Use the existing read-only tool admission, exact-window authorization, and native accessibility permissions. No new grant, foreground activation, or wider desktop inspection. Passive data never gains action authority. Preserve untrusted web-region provenance. No new telemetry, persistence, or raw-value logging; implementation evidence should use controlled fixtures, not user content.

## Validation and acceptance evidence

- Public native fixture baseline fails to expose a readable passive label, then passes after implementation.
- Snapshot publishes its raw value without a token; a unique exact-value predicate satisfies and an incorrect value is unsatisfied.
- Verification preserves the session's existing action token. Passive rows cannot be addressed as actions.
- Duplicate targets remain `multi_match`; untrusted regions remain unknown; bidi-bearing raw values compare exactly.
- Query, cap/depth, unreadable children, unresolved window, and old-producer cases cannot claim false completeness or widen scope.
- Equivalent focused fixture coverage on macOS, Windows, and Linux X11, with concrete Wayland/provider limitations recorded.
- Real Calculator supporting evidence uses an actually unique selector and raw value, not role-only selection or implicit normalization.
- Generated contracts/bindings/docs and ordinary CI pass. Run the complete canonical desktop matrix once on the stable implementation candidate, not the RFC-only change.

## Unresolved questions

- Confirm the additive passive-array design versus the simpler but breaking unified array.
- Confirm separate passive completeness with conservative legacy fallback.
- Review query-projection and native retention details before tightening the preliminary 150–300 handwritten-line estimate; generated bindings are additional.

## RFC document pull request

Draft #3904 contains `rfcs/3903-passive-native-observations.md` with `status: review`. Product implementation waits for the recorded maintainer decision required by `rfcs/README.md`.

## Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues, RFCs, and active pull requests. #2958 remains the bug record; withdrawn #3390 concerned a different state-store design and does not authorize this contract change.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] The proposal includes alternatives, compatibility, platform boundaries, and observable acceptance evidence.

title: cua-driver (Windows): hotkey always fails on WinUI3/XAML targets — "UIA accelerator scan exceeded 4000ms" (Ctrl+S unusable in Notepad), while the same window's UIA tree is readable
body:
## Summary

On Windows 11, `hotkey` against a **WinUI3 / modern XAML target** (Notepad) fails on *every* attempt with:

```
hotkey (UIA path): UIA accelerator scan exceeded 4000ms; a UIA provider in the target app is likely unresponsive
```

The same code path works on a **classic Win32** target (regedit), and the *same Notepad window's UIA tree is fully readable* (`get_window_state` → 30–34 elements). So this looks specific to the accelerator-scan path, not a system-wide UIA/input outage.

Net effect: `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+O` / `Ctrl+F` / `Ctrl+W` are unusable on modern XAML/UWP apps (Notepad, Calculator, Settings, Photos …), so agents must fall back to clicking toolbar/menu controls.

## Environment

- `cua-driver 0.23.2` (`cua-driver --version`)
- Windows 11, build `10.0.26200`, single 2560×1600 display at **150% scaling**
- Reproduced both ways: direct CLI (`cua-driver call hotkey ...`) and through a client harness that spawns `cua-driver call ...` (dsh-computer-use 0.5.3)
- Target: Windows 11 **Notepad (Store/WinUI3 app)** — both an *untitled* document and one *opened from a file*

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
start notepad
cua-driver call list_windows '{"on_screen_only":true}'        # take pid / window_id
cua-driver call hotkey '{"keys":["ctrl","s"],"pid":PID,"window_id":WID}'
```

Expected on an untitled Notepad: the Save-As dialog appears.
Observed: non-JSON error (text above), no dialog, no key delivered.

## Evidence

Repeated attempts on the same window (fresh state before each attempt):

| Target | Attempts | UIA accelerator timeout | Delivered |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notepad (opened from file), `ctrl+s` | 5 | **5** | 0 |
| Notepad (untitled), `ctrl+s` | 5 | **4** (+1 `hotkey on a modern XAML / UWP target (pid …)`) | 0 |
| regedit (classic Win32), `ctrl+f` → Find dialog | 5 | **0** | 3/3 when routed through the client's foreground-escalation path |

Controls that rule out a broken local environment:

- The same Notepad window is observable: `get_window_state {include_screenshot:false, max_elements:200}` returns **30–34 elements** (UIA tree works; only the accelerator scan times out)
- Session is not locked (input desktop opens), no topmost/overlay windows present, no other input-injection software involved
- The classic-Win32 target delivers normally through the identical client path — so the input stack and the driver's legacy route are fine

## Related observation on the same target

The usual workaround (drive the menu instead of the shortcut) is also unavailable:

```
cua-driver call invoke_menu '{"pid":PID,"window_id":WID,"path":["File","Save"]}'
→ {"refusal":{"code":"menu_path_unavailable","message":"menu path segment 1 was not found"}}
```

## Notes

- **Silent-failure sibling**: on the same Notepad window, `press_key` (PostMessage route) returns **no error** but reports `effect: "unverifiable"` and delivers nothing. A key that is silently dropped is more dangerous than one that fails loudly — this looks like the same family as #2022 (Linux `click` reporting success while no input lands).
- The client now translates the accelerator timeout into actionable guidance ("click the toolbar/menu control instead"), but that is a workaround, not a fix.

## Suggested fixes (any of these would unblock users)

1. **Best-effort accelerator scan**: on scan timeout, fall back to dispatching the chord through the SendInput/foreground path (the one already used for classic targets) before failing.
2. **Make the scan budget configurable** — 4000 ms seems below what this provider needs here.
3. **Typed error code** (e.g. `uia_accelerator_unavailable`) so clients can branch without parsing message text.
4. For `invoke_menu` on XAML menu bars, consider the UIA expand/collapse route, or include the discovered menu item names in the refusal to help clients adapt.

Happy to run further probes (UIA tree dump of the Notepad menu bar, scan timing measurements, additional WinUI apps) if that helps.

title: [Bug]: macOS `list_windows` reports the system window-sharing indicator as an ordinary application window
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

While something holds a capture lease on an app, macOS adds a small window-sharing indicator window to that app, and `list_windows` reports it with exactly the shape of a real application window. Nothing in the record says what it is, so a consumer picking "the app's window" can pick the indicator.

### Reproduction

1. Capture a window of some app (any path that holds a ScreenCaptureKit window-sharing session on it).
2. Call `list_windows` with that app's `pid` while the lease is held.
3. Try to tell the indicator row from the app's real windows using only the fields `list_windows` returns.

### Expected behavior

The row stays listed - it is the only signal a consumer has that something is capturing that app - but carries a classification, in the vocabulary the contract already uses for `AppInfo.kind`, so callers can filter it by default and resolve a real window without guessing.

### Actual behavior

The record is `window_id`, `pid`, `app_name`, `title`, `bounds`, `layer`, `z_index`, `is_on_screen`, space fields - and nothing else. Measured on this machine: `window_id 10871`, `app_name "TextEdit"`, `pid 758`, `title "Window"`, `layer 0`, bounds 66x20. A caller cannot distinguish it, and `get_window_state` walks it happily: its AX surface is an `AXWindow` with subrole `AXDialog` whose only child is an `AXButton` titled `WindowSharingSessionButton`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.2 (trycua/cua main, 625118a90)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1 (25B78), arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: any app under a window-sharing capture session (observed on TextEdit and Google Chrome)

### Evidence

Its CGWindow dictionary is indistinguishable from an ordinary window: `kCGWindowLayer 0`, `kCGWindowAlpha 1.0`, `kCGWindowSharingState 1`, `kCGWindowStoreType 1`, owner name the app itself. The one piece of provenance available is geometric: the indicator contains a 14x14 window owned by a different process whose `proc_pidpath` is exactly `/System/Library/Frameworks/AppKit.framework/Versions/C/XPCServices/ThemeWidgetControlViewService.xpc/Contents/MacOS/ThemeWidgetControlViewService`, AppKit's theme-widget XPC service, which hosts the indicator's only control. Across a 192-row roster on this desktop, that is true of exactly one row.

### Workaround and additional context

None from the returned fields; a caller can only hard-code a title and a size, which is what the driver should be doing once, centrally, instead. The same recognition would also keep the indicator from making an app look like it has two windows in the background-input ambiguity judgement (`platform-macos/src/ax/exact_target.rs`), which is a separate fix. Happy to open the PR for the classification.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(lume): keep the login keychain usable after automatic setup
body:
Lume's automatic macOS setup must encode a NUL-terminated password before writing the automatic-login password file. Padding after encoding can prevent the normal account password from unlocking the login keychain. This change pads the UTF-8 plaintext before XOR encoding and always includes a terminator, including at exact 12-byte boundaries.

Both setup paths now use byte counts. The shell path previously counted Unicode characters: a 12-byte fixture password produced an 18-byte buffer, while the Swift path produced the expected 24 bytes. The follow-up aligns those paths and adds boundary coverage to CI. Commands and public APIs are unchanged.

Validation of candidate `b0408db3e969345a2ca3394599e3ea41a8e0b638`:

- All 143 Swift tests passed.
- The setup-script regression tests passed across eight ASCII lengths and five UTF-8 boundary fixtures; four non-ASCII cases failed before the follow-up.
- Shell syntax, CI workflow syntax/wiring, and diff checks passed.
- In a disposable macOS Tahoe 26.5.2 VM, the Swift helper compiled from the candidate source and the shell encoder produced identical bytes for a Unicode fixture password. A fresh test account logged in automatically, its normal password unlocked the login keychain, and no renamed replacement keychain appeared across two boots. The second boot's keychain was already unlocked before the manual unlock check.

The VM check exercises generated password bytes with a fresh account. It does not replace a complete fresh `lume create` or unattended-install run. The prior PR head's six-boot report remains historical evidence; those six boots were not repeated for this follow-up. Existing images whose login keychains were already replaced still need a clean rebuild.

Visual follow-up: the fixture reached first-login Setup Assistant on a subsequent boot; optional screens were completed manually. At the user's request, the synthetic account and existing login-keychain password were then changed to a normal ASCII fixture. Keychain Access accepted that password in the actual GUI and displayed an unlocked login keychain. This confirms GUI authentication after the explicit password change. It does not establish original Unicode GUI authentication, a fresh unattended installation, or unattended desktop readiness.

title: macOS type_text reports a value the app discarded as a partial insertion, and that ends the delivery ladder
body:
## What happens

`type_text` classifies delivery from the strongest read-back seen anywhere in its drain window instead of the value the field settled on, so a value an application publishes transiently and then discards is reported as a partial insertion — with a character count and retry advice that corrupt the field if followed.

Measured on Contacts (macOS 26.1, driver 0.28.0), typing a street address into a contact card's address group:

```
type_text_incomplete: type_text incomplete: delivered 14 of 25 character(s)
  via partial AX write into [57] AXTextField ""; retry only the remaining suffix
{"code":"type_text_incomplete","delivered_chars":14,"effect":"partial","path":"ax",
 "requested_chars":25,"retry_from_character":14,"retryable":true}
```

The field held `""` immediately afterwards (`get_window_state` on the same window: `AXTextField "Street" value=""`). Contacts rebuilds the address group's field editor around an `AXSelectedText` insert, so the value is briefly a prefix and then empty. A caller obeying "retry only the remaining suffix" writes `ntau Avenue` into an empty field.

## Where

`crates/platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs` at `f6be60087`:

- `await_typed_delivery` (:1053-1080) keeps `best_partial = max(delivered)` across the whole 2 s window and returns that at the deadline (`return (false, best_partial)`), so a transient reading outlives the settled one.
- The background AX rung samples `AXValue` exactly once, microseconds after the write (`let after = unsafe { copy_string_attr(element, "AXValue") };`, :1270), which is the same defect in its sharpest form — the code's own comment elsewhere records Contacts publishing `"(408) "` of `"(408) 961-1560"` and completing ~20 ms later.
- A `Partial` verdict returns from the rung (:1295-1303), and that is the one classification that does **not** fall through to the CGEvent keystroke rung, so a transient partial also ends the ladder that would have delivered the text.

## Expected

The verdict comes from the settled read at the end of the drain window (falling back to the strongest partial only when the final read is unreadable), and a partial the settled read contradicts classifies as unchanged, which is already the fall-through to keystrokes.

I have this fixed and unit-tested on a branch and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: macOS element actions carry macOS's three-line envelope, which breaks tree_markdown's one-row-per-line contract
body:
## What happens

An application's own secondary actions reach `AXUIElementCopyActionNames` as ordinary strings wrapped in a three-line envelope. The driver passes them through verbatim, so a single Reminders row publishes:

```json
{"role": "AXCell", "element_index": 15,
 "actions": ["Name:Customize info and appearance\nTarget:0x0\nSelector:(null)",
             "Name:Pin List\nTarget:0x0\nSelector:(null)",
             "Name:Customize info and appearance\nTarget:0x0\nSelector:(null)",
             "Name:Pin List\nTarget:0x0\nSelector:(null)"]}
```

and `format_node_line` lowercases the same strings into its `actions=[...]` block, so that one row renders as eight lines of `name:pin list` / `target:0x0` / `selector:(null)` inside `tree_markdown`. Every consumer that parses the tree as one row per element is wrong on any row carrying these.

Note for anyone reaching for `AXCustomActions`: on macOS 26.1 that attribute is absent on every node of Reminders' tree. The envelope strings in `AXUIElementCopyActionNames` are the only surface, and they are invocable — `AXUIElementPerformAction(cell, "Name:Pin List\nTarget:0x0\nSelector:(null)")` returned `kAXErrorSuccess` in 3 ms and the element then advertised `Name:Unpin List`.

## Where (`f6be60087`)

- `crates/platform-macos/src/ax/bindings.rs`: `copy_action_names` returns the raw array.
- `crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs`: the walk stores it as `AXNode.actions`, and `format_node_line` maps each entry through `strip_prefix("AX").unwrap_or(a).to_lowercase()` into `actions=[...]`.
- `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs`: `entry["actions"] = json!(node.actions)`.

Also note AppKit lists each of these twice on the `AXCell` (the inner group carries one copy), so a fix wants dedupe.

## Expected

`actions` carries the standard AX names; the application's own actions are published separately with the label a person reads and the exact string that performs them, and the markdown carries only single-line names.

I have this implemented and unit-tested on a branch and can open a PR referencing this issue.

title: macOS click dispatches an unrecognised action name as AXPress
body:
## What happens

`crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs` at `f6be60087`:

```rust
fn map_action(action: &str) -> &'static str {
    match action.to_lowercase().as_str() {
        "press" | "click" => "AXPress",
        ...
        _ => "AXPress",
    }
}
```

So `click(action: "AXScrollToVisible")`, `click(action: "Flag")` or any typo presses the element and reports a press. The reply's advertised-action warning fires ("Element does not advertise AXPress") but the press already happened, and `effect` is the ordinary press effect, so a caller cannot tell a refused action from a performed one.

This matters more as soon as element payloads carry real action names (the AX names an element advertises, and an application's own secondary actions - see #3919): a caller can read a genuine name off the tree, pass it back, and get a press instead.

## Expected

A documented alias (press, show_menu, pick, confirm, cancel, open) maps as today. Any other value is accepted only when the element itself advertises it verbatim, in which case it is dispatched as given; otherwise the call is refused before anything is dispatched, naming the actions the element does advertise.

I have this implemented and unit-tested on a branch and can open a PR referencing this issue.

title: fix(cua-driver): name the state behind a macOS press or click refusal
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: A macOS refusal did not say which window held focus or why a control was disabled, so agents retried the wrong route.
- What changed: a disabled control is refused with `code: element_disabled` and one cause; only a window that is not key adds `escalation: {target: foreground, reason: route_unavailable}`. Before: one uncoded text in every state. `press_key` names the window holding focus. Detail fields are documented macOS-only (`MACOS.md`), not typed contract.

<details><summary>Mechanism and measurements</summary>

Sheet refusal. `with_foreground_hid_activation` reached its bail only when `focused_window_id_of_pid` reported a window other than the target, so the id was in hand and thrown away. `ax::bindings::focused_window_of_pid` returns the focused window's id and role in the one native round-trip the id already cost. The bail is a typed `ForegroundActivationRefused`; its `Display` names both windows (`window 11151, a sheet attached to 11139, holds keyboard focus - snapshot that window_id and press its own buttons`, measured on Calendar), and `press_key`'s refusal publishes `target_window_id`, `focused_window_id` and `focused_window_relation`. An unknown focus holder leaves the old payload plus `target_window_id`.

Disabled control. `ensure_ax_action_enabled` answered every disabled element with one literal naming `delivery_mode:"foreground"` and `bring_to_front`. Measured in Chrome and Notes across four states, the text was byte-identical, and in the plain state both routes were already taken; on the foreground rung the check runs inside `with_foreground_assist`, so the window was already in front. It was right only for a control disabled until its window is key (Notes' toolbar search field), and even there it carried no code. `perform_ax_click` now builds `ElementDisabled` from the element's role and label, the process's front window on the target's display (`bring_to_front::process_front_window_on_display`, the resolution #3785 uses) and the process's key-window state, and `cause()` picks one arm:

1. a menu item tracks the application's applicability: no route;
2. the process's own window drawn in front: `obscured_by: {window_id, title}`, dismiss or address it;
3. background delivery and the window not key (`key_window: {is_key, app_frontmost, focused_window_id}`): the foreground escalation;
4. otherwise the application disabled it: no route.

Prose and payload branch on the same `cause()`, so a reply cannot name a route its escalation withholds. The escalation uses existing contract values only, as #4009 accepted. `ax_actions` keeps only `ax_element_enabled`; the unused `perform_ax_action` and its re-export go with the literal.

Tests. `harness_appkit_key_window_control_refusal_names_the_foreground_rung` (new; selected by `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh`): the AppKit fixture gains a button enabled only while its window is key; the cell snapshots it, presses it in the background behind the foreground sentinel and asserts `code`, `escalation` and `key_window`, then presses it with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` and reads `key_only_pressed=1` back. Unit tests pin the arms the fixture does not reach: key window (no route, prose names neither taken route), another window holding focus (escalation), own window in front outranks the key-window fact, menu item, foreground rung in force. Press_key: the sheet and unidentified-holder payloads.

Before-proof and mutations. The new cell run with a driver built from `origin/main` `0f29c142d` fails at the code assertion (`tool_invocation_failed` with main's literal, not `element_disabled`). Moving the key-window arm above the owned-window arm, dropping the foreground-rung filter and dropping the menu arm fail `the_apps_own_window_in_front_outranks_the_key_window_fact`, `the_foreground_rung_is_not_offered_once_it_is_in_force` and `a_disabled_menu_item_names_no_route`.

Supporting evidence: AppKit harness (`mcp --direct` shim) in a throwaway macOS 26.5.2 bench VM (seed `bench-seed-v5`), driver built and signed from this head, 2026-10-03: 25/28. `origin/main` `542046496` in the same seed the same day: 24/27, failing the same three cells. Those are direct-mode limits: the agent-cursor cell needs a certified overlay host, and the snapshot-publication and px-background peer checks need two clients on one shared daemon. The extra case here is this PR's new cell.

The new cell passed in this run. The 11/11 repeat count (this run plus ten filtered runs) was taken at the previous head `5c2858363`, before this rebase.

Foreground rung race (new commit `5c2858363`). Repeating the new cell after rebasing onto main showed the foreground press itself refused as `element_disabled` in 4 of 7 filtered runs at `49f5e3718` (the rebase without this commit), and in 1 of 4 with the `7b5441718` driver under main's test binary, so the race predates the rebase; earlier runs passed because the fixture happened to be frontmost already. A diagnostic build showed the mechanism: `with_foreground_assist` waits for `AXFocusedWindow`, which is the application's own focused window and already names the target, so the wait ended in 0-3 ms and the enablement re-read ran before AppKit had processed the activation and its key-window update. On the foreground rung a disabled read now waits, bounded at 400 ms, for the application to report itself frontmost (`AXFrontmost`) with the target window focused, then reads the control again (`await_application_key_window`). The background rung and enabled controls are unchanged; a control that stays disabled costs at most the bound.

Rebased onto main `542046496` (cua-driver-rs 0.33.0, 2026-10-03). Two conflicts, both where #4485 (an erroring toggle press counts when its value moved) added code beside this PR's additions: its AppKit cell next to the new key-window cell in `harness_appkit_test.rs`, and its unit tests next to the `ElementDisabled` tests in `click.rs`. Both sides are kept; #4485 changes the press outcome after dispatch, and this PR's enablement check runs before dispatch, so neither path changes the other. One wording change follows #4507 (sheet elements resolve to their parent window): a sheet's controls are now addressed through the window it is attached to, so the `press_key` sheet refusal and its `MACOS.md` entry now point at the target window's snapshot instead of the sheet's own `window_id`. The previous rebase onto `ab628e0d1` (0.32.0, 2026-10-02) resolved one conflict in `input/ax_actions.rs`, keeping main's test-module layout without the two tests of the removed `ensure_ax_enabled` helper.

</details>

## Related work

Fixes #3918
Refs #4009 (accepted; document #4367). No longer stacked on #3910 (overlay rows wait for it).

## Compatibility and risk

Review first: `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs::ElementDisabled::cause` - arm order decides the route named.
- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only; refusal fields only.
- Risk and rollback: revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `platform-macos` lib 442, contract 59 + 4 passed at `98d134d13`; before-proof in details. Production +357/-51, tests +249/-15, docs +28.
- Manual or platform evidence: supporting only, bench-VM AppKit harness at `98d134d13`: 25/28; main `542046496` 24/27, same 3 failures; new cell 11/11 at `5c2858363` (details).
- Known gaps or CI still required: canonical macOS Lume run (`libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh`) at this head; no sheet fixture for the focus holder.

title: test(cua-driver): follow canonical release title guidance
body:
Fixes #3935

title: macOS invoke_menu presses a submenu-bearing final segment and discards the labels it just enumerated
body:
## What happens

`invoke_menu` presses whatever its final path segment resolves to, and a menu item that bears a submenu advertises `AXPress` like any other:

```rust
fn choose_action(actions: &[String], final_segment: bool) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let supports = |name: &str| actions.iter().any(|action| action == name);
    let order: &[&str] = if final_segment {
        &["AXPress", "AXPick", "AXConfirm"]
    } else {
        &["AXPress", "AXPick", "AXShowMenu", "AXOpen"]
    };
    order.iter().copied().find(|action| supports(action))
}
```

So `invoke_menu(["Format", "Font"])` presses `Font`. That press cannot invoke a command — there is none — it opens the submenu and leaves the application tracking an open menu. The reply nevertheless says:

> Resolved the live native menu path and dispatched its final accessibility action; verify the command's semantic effect from fresh state.

A caller cannot tell that from a real dispatch, and there is no way to ask what is inside a submenu, so the caller has to guess the next segment. Two consequences we hit in practice:

**A wrong guess returns nothing to correct it.** The refusal names the index and stops:

```
await win.menu(["File", "New Contact"], …)
→ CuaError: invoke_menu: path segment 1 was not found
```

The labels that *are* at that level are known to the driver at the moment it refuses — `resolve_exact_prefix` just enumerated them to decide there was no exact match — and they are discarded. In the bench run above both harness runs then fell back to blind pixel clicks at the toolbar, typed into whatever had focus, and did not complete the task.

**Callers read menus out of `get_window_state` instead, which is expensive.** Because the menu tree is reachable through the ordinary AX walk, a consumer that needs menu labels asks for the window tree and parses the rendered menu bar out of it. On Contacts that observation is 68.7 kB / 530 lines, of which lines 413-530 are the entire menu bar with every submenu expanded (`Apple ▸ Recent Items`, `Card ▸ Add Field ▸ …`); the consumer's 50 kB cap then elided lines 264-454 — the contact rows, the card pane and the whole `AXToolbar`. The menu listing displaced the window content the caller actually asked about.

For the "the press did not invoke the command" half, a related live case: Chrome's `View ▸ Developer ▸ Allow JavaScript from Apple Events`. `AXPress` on `Developer` (tried three times) left the toggle unchanged; opening `View ▸ Developer` and then walking the open submenu with real key events (`key code 125` ×5, `key code 36`) did flip it.

## Where (`8cb8f6d2b`)

- `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/invoke_menu.rs`, `choose_action` — `final_segment: true` offers `AXPress` first, with nothing asking whether the target bears a submenu.
- same file, `invoke_path` — presses at every depth including the last, then reports the success text above.
- same file, `resolve_exact_prefix` — has the sibling titles in hand when it returns `path segment {depth} is ambiguous` / `was not found`, and drops them.

## Expected

- A final segment that bears a submenu is listed, not pressed: the items macOS actually has under it, in order, each with the title a path segment can address and whether it opens a further submenu.
- A segment resolution failure names which segment failed and the items at that level, so a caller that guessed a label wrong can correct it from the refusal.
- A leaf segment keeps pressing exactly as it does today.

That makes the menu reachable without the window-tree detour, and it removes the class of reply that claims a command was dispatched when a submenu was opened.

I have this implemented and unit-tested on a branch and can open a PR referencing this issue. Shape there: `{status: "listed", resolved_path, items: [{title, enabled?, has_submenu, shortcut?}]}` on the listing path and `refusal.failed_segment` / `refusal.items` under the existing `menu_path_unavailable` code — no contract types change, since this tool's structured payloads are already free-form. The listing resolves against the closed menu tree first and only falls back to the press walk for lazily populated menus, so listing opens nothing on screen.

title: [RFC]: annotate tool — persistent highlight shapes on the per-session overlay layer
body:
## Summary

The cursor-overlay crate renders a per-session agent cursor, which covers "show where the agent is acting". Agents also need the inverse: **point something out to the user** — highlight a widget, box a region the user asked about, annotate a finding on screen. Today the only on-screen primitive is the cursor itself, so "highlight X for me" gets approximated by tracing the cursor around the target's bounds. That works for a glance, but the trace is ephemeral (idle-hide) and costs a stream of `move_cursor` calls to draw one rectangle.

## Proposal

An `annotate` tool rendered by the same per-session overlay machinery as the agent cursor:

```
annotate({
  shapes: [{ kind: "rect" | "ellipse" | "path", points: [{x, y}, ...], color?, stroke_width? }],
  ttl_ms?: number,        // default a few seconds; 0 = until cleared
  anchor?: "screen" | { pid, window_id }
})
clear_annotations()
```

- Per-session, keyed like the agent cursor; torn down at session end.
- Screen-space coordinates, or window-anchored so the highlight follows the window on move/resize where the platform allows it.
- Visual-only: never intercepts or delivers input, same non-interactive posture as the cursor overlay.

## Prior art / related

- #1800 — per-session overlay windows; likely the same layering machinery.
- Host-side implementations of exactly this exist downstream (an AppKit overlay-window + annotation view layer), so there is proven demand; driver-side would give every host the capability cross-platform instead of each app re-implementing it.

Would a PR in this direction be welcome? If the shape looks right I can start on the cursor-overlay crate side.

title: macOS AX walk withholds two facts about a control: a disabled control gets no element_index, and AXSubrole is never read
body:
## What happens

The macOS AX walk withholds two facts about a control that a caller needs, and both are decided in `is_addressable` / the node read.

### 1. A disabled control gets no `element_index`, so it is not published at all

```rust
fn is_addressable(actions_present: bool, value_settable: bool, enabled: Option<bool>) -> bool {
    (actions_present || value_settable) && enabled != Some(false)
}
```

The walker's own test pins the consequence — `assert!(!is_addressable(true, false, Some(false)))`: a control that advertises actions is refused an index purely because it reports `AXEnabled=false`. `get_window_state` then publishes only indexed nodes (`let idx = node.element_index?;`), so such a control appears in `tree_markdown` as a display-only row with no index and no actions, and is absent from the `elements` array entirely — including from its own `enabled` field, which the payload already has.

That erases a recoverable state. macOS reports controls disabled for reasons the caller can undo: a toolbar control in a window that has never been key reads `AXEnabled=false` until the window becomes key, and the dispatch path already knows this and says so —

```rust
// input/ax_actions.rs:200-218
"refusing {action}: the target reports AXEnabled=false. \
 Retry this action with delivery_mode:\"foreground\" or call bring_to_front first"
```

— but that advice can never reach a caller, because the control it is about has no index to dispatch against. The caller sees an inert row indistinguishable from decoration, with no way to learn why.

Live: Notes' collapsed toolbar search control. AX reports it as

```
/1/10/0 AXRole='AXButton' AXSubrole='AXSearchField' AXTitle='' AXDescription='Search' AXEnabled='False'
```

and the driver's own tree for that window renders it as

```
    - AXButton (Search)
```

— no index, and none of that snapshot's 231 `elements` rows is it. (Captured from a build carrying these exact two lines; the walker is unchanged here at `9e60d90b8`.)

### 2. `AXSubrole` is never read, so the role is the only class token on a node

`AXSubrole` is read for windows (`list_windows`, `window_scope`) and for the text-field write plan (`set_value`), but never for a tree node. macOS puts the control class there rather than in the role, and the role alone is frequently not enough to identify a control.

Same Notes window, search expanded. AX reports `AXRole='AXTextField' AXSubrole='AXSearchField' AXValue='' AXEnabled='True'` — and no title, description, placeholder or identifier at all. So the only thing the driver can render is:

```
    - [85] AXTextField = "" [actions=[showmenu,confirm]]
```

The structured element is `{element_index: 85, role: "AXTextField", depth: …}` with no `label`. A consumer looking for the search field has nothing to match on; measured against that snapshot: `find({role:"AXSearchField"}) -> 0`, `find({label:"Search"}) -> 0`, `find({role:"AXButton", label:"Search"}) -> 0`.

It is not only search fields. On that one window, 173 of 1558 walked nodes publish a subrole, and the ones whose subrole is the only class token include the window's close / minimize / full-screen buttons and the scroll bar's increment/decrement arrows — all `AXButton` with an empty title.

## Where (`9e60d90b8`)

- `crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs:131-132` — `is_addressable`, the `enabled != Some(false)` conjunct.
- same file, `:434-443` — the `AXEnabled` pre-read feeding it, with a comment explaining the exclusion as protection against closed-submenu descendants.
- same file, `:744` — the test that pins "actions present, disabled ⇒ not addressable".
- `crates/platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs:820` — `let idx = node.element_index?;`, the publish gate.
- `crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs:47-95` — `AXNode`: `AXRole` is read, `AXSubrole` is not a field.
- `crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs:612-659` — `format_node_line`, the rendered row and its bracketed metadata block.
- `crates/cua-driver-contract/src/windows.rs:202-230` — `WindowElement`, which already carries `enabled`.
- `crates/platform-macos/src/input/ax_actions.rs:215-218` — `ensure_ax_action_enabled`, which re-reads `AXEnabled` immediately before every dispatch.

## Expected

- **Enablement is state, not existence.** A control that advertises an action or exposes a writable value gets an `element_index` regardless of its enablement, and publishes `enabled: false`. Nothing can be dispatched by mistake: `ensure_ax_action_enabled` re-reads the attribute immediately before performing and refuses with the recovery advice above, so the only change is that the caller can now reach the refusal instead of the control being invisible. The closed-submenu case the current comment protects against is answered by the same publication — the row says it is disabled rather than vanishing.
- **`AXSubrole` is published.** One read per addressable node, carried as `subrole` on the element payload (`Option<String>`, omitted when the app reports none) and rendered on the tree row.

### Cost, measured

On a captured 1558-node Notes window:

- **AX requests:** one `AXSubrole` read per addressable node — 314 of that window's 500 rendered rows are indexed — against the ~10 reads every visited node already pays and the 5 more an indexed node pays. That is +1.8% requests for the window, and zero for display-only rows, because the read sits inside the existing actionable gate (`read_control_state_if_actionable`'s precondition).
- **Rendered bytes:** 173 of the 1558 nodes publish a subrole, but 164 of them are `AXRow`+`AXTableRow` (153), `AXRow`+`AXOutlineRow` (11) and `AXWindow`+`AXStandardWindow` (1) — tokens that restate the role the row already prints. Rendering all of them costs ~3.1 kB on a 33.2 kB tree (+9.4%) for no information. So the row omits a subrole that ends in its own role's stem (`AXRow`/`AXTableRow` is suppressed, `AXTextField`/`AXSearchField` is not) and the payload always carries the raw value; the 9 that survive on that window cost ~0.2 kB and are exactly the ones that name a different control class.

Rendered shape, for the two cases above:

```
    - [3] AXButton (Search) [subrole=AXSearchField actions=[press] enabled=false]
    - [85] AXTextField = "" [subrole=AXSearchField actions=[showmenu,confirm]]
```

`enabled=false` is rendered only when the app reports the control disabled; an enabled control adds nothing to the line.

I have this implemented and unit-tested on a branch and can open a PR referencing this issue.

title: fix(cua-driver): let callers perform an app's own macOS element actions
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: an app's own row actions (Reminders' "Pin List") showed up in a macOS snapshot as raw multi-line text that click refused, so a caller could never perform them; a group carrying the app's help vanished.
- What changed: app actions move to `custom_actions` (`{name, raw}`) and `click.action` performs either spelling; unknown names still refuse before dispatch. A group with a label or help is kept.

<details><summary>Mechanism and measurements</summary>

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| app action | in `actions` as `"Name:Pin List\nTarget:0x0\n..."`; `click` refuses | `custom_actions[].name` / `.raw`; `click` performs it |
| group with help | collapsed | kept; indexed when actionable |

**Since the last round.** Re-expressed on main `09b38ab66` (cua-driver-rs 0.47.4). Disabled-control indexing (#5635) and `subrole` (#6893) landed upstream in their own form, so this branch keeps only custom actions and content-bearing groups. Main has since started refusing unknown `click.action` names before any dispatch (`validate_click_action`); an element click now also passes that check when the element advertises the name as a custom action, read once from the element, so a typo still refuses before the background gate, cursor or activation run.

**Envelope.** `AXUIElementCopyActionNames` returns an app's own actions as `"Name:Pin List\nTarget:0x0\nSelector:(null)"`. `ax/actions.rs::split` keeps `AX*` names in `actions` and publishes the rest once each as `{name, raw}`; a nameless envelope is dropped. `custom_wire_name` maps a caller's name or raw string back to the advertised envelope, which is what `AXPerformAction` needs; `click` and `perform_ax_action` use it before falling back to `map_action`. The tree line prints names JSON-quoted (`custom_actions=["Pin List"]`), so a name cannot add tree rows.

**Groups.** `AXGroup` and `AXScrollArea` used to collapse unconditionally. They now collapse only when title, description, value and help are all empty, which is checked before the action query, so pure layout nodes cost no extra AX request. A kept group is indexed only when it is actionable.

**Tests.** Owner tests are the two AppKit cases, `harness_appkit_custom_actions_are_published_and_dispatch_by_name_or_envelope` (performs a fixture action by name and by raw envelope and checks it did not press instead) and `harness_appkit_a_content_bearing_group_stays_addressable`, both selected by `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh`. Unit tests in `ax/actions.rs` and `ax/tree.rs` own the parsing edge cases (duplicates, nameless and unenveloped names, one tree row) and `validate_click_action` owns refusal before dispatch.

**Mutation.** Dispatching through `map_action` only (no `custom_wire_name` in `click` or `perform_ax_action`) at `9e3bebddf` fails `harness_appkit_custom_actions_are_published_and_dispatch_by_name_or_envelope` in the bench VM (0/1 pass). The Python and TypeScript loader suites caught a stale binding set on the first rebased head (the new record was missing, `read past end of rust buffer`); the bindings at this head are regenerated.

**Supporting AppKit harness.** Full `harness_appkit_test` at `5ce154de0` in the bench VM (`bench-seed-v11`, `mcp --direct` shim, cua-driver 0.47.4 unsigned build sha256 `eaa7a2e5…`): 33/36 pass, including both new cases, `harness_appkit_custom_actions_are_published_and_dispatch_by_name_or_envelope` and `harness_appkit_a_content_bearing_group_stays_addressable`. The three failures are the documented direct-mode limits that fail the same way on main in this seed: `counter_px_background`, `exact_activation_with_agent_cursor`, `pending_snapshot_cannot_retarget_token`. The mutation at `9e3bebddf` fails its owner case (0/1 pass).

</details>

## Related work

Refs #3949 (its index and subrole facts landed in #5635 and #6893); folds #3947.

RFC: not required; one additive macOS-only element field.

## Compatibility and risk

Review first: `platform-macos/src/ax/actions.rs::split`, `tools/click.rs::validate_click_action`.

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only; envelopes leave `actions`, where nothing could invoke them.
- Risk and rollback: empty groups still collapse before any action query; revert.

## Validation

- Checks at `5ce154de0`: contract 71, core 1237+1, platform-macos 735, e2e 38, sdk 113, Python 23, TS 16, 0 failed; generators clean. Production +134/-50, tests +324, generated +172/-2.
- Manual or platform evidence: supporting VM AppKit run at `5ce154de0`, 33/36; three setup limits also fail on main (details).
- Known gaps or CI still required: canonical macOS Lume run.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). Heavy checks ran individually.

title: feat(cua-driver): add OpenJev decision model adapter
body:
## TL;DR

Re-cut per maintainer review: this PR is now **OpenJev backend only** on current `main`'s accepted decision architecture. The old parallel `jev_backends` layer, browser-runner routing changes, TypeSafe configuration changes, and backend telemetry are gone.

Candidate: `48c9fc770674f57ca40466b9f7e006150456a183` on base `9545a3d17b44b587b593d59090dc140740876a6e`.

## Change

Adds Python + TypeScript OpenJev System One adapters for `jev-use`.

- Python implements the existing `DecisionModel` / `DecisionRequest` seam and returns `ModelScores`.
- Both languages consume the existing validated `cua.jev_choice_request_v1|v2` shape; a v2 request is sent directly as the System One `state`.
- The provider can only score caller-supplied IDs. It does not construct Driver actions or own retry/routing policy.
- The remote contract is `POST /v1/systemone` with one `choice` question over the immutable candidate criteria.

### Transport boundary

Configuration is intentionally explicit:

- `OPENJEV_BASE_URL` — required remote base or full `/v1/systemone` endpoint;
- `OPENJEV_API_KEY` — optional;
- `OPENJEV_MODEL` — defaults to `openjev`;
- `OPENJEV_TIMEOUT_MS` — bounded to 100–60000 ms.

Safety properties retained from the earlier #3961 investigation:

- API keys are sent only over HTTPS;
- URL-embedded credentials are rejected;
- query/fragment-bearing base URLs are rejected;
- redirects are not followed;
- response reads are capped at 256 KiB;
- timeout / transport / malformed-response failures are bounded errors;
- no provider error causes action replay in this adapter.

The existing Python `choose()` validator remains the final authority for exact candidate-set equality, finite probability mass, unique argmax and selected ID. The TypeScript mirror enforces the same score invariants before returning.

## Scope deliberately removed

Per the review on this PR:

- no replacement `jev_backends` abstraction;
- no Driver changes;
- no visual-routing changes;
- no browser runner provider selection in this slice;
- no content-free `backend` event field in this slice;
- no S1 duplication;
- no TypeSafe base/model/timeout change yet.

Browser provider parity + backend receipts are tracked separately in https://github.com/kvnloo/cua/issues/78.

## Invocation surface

The backend is now selectable through the existing Python decision CLI:

`python/choose_decision.py --model openjev`

and through `verify_decision_cli.py --model openjev`. This is still only the bounded decision interface; browser/native runner provider routing remains the separate follow-up.

## Validation status

Exact head `48c9fc770674f57ca40466b9f7e006150456a183`, from `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use`:

- `uv run --frozen python -m unittest python/tests/test_openjev_model.py` — 15 tests OK
- `uv run --frozen python -m unittest discover -s python/tests` — 226 tests OK, 1 skipped
- `npm test` — 113 pass
- `npm run typecheck` — pass

The added loopback rows use the real HTTP transport. Valid selection, unknown candidate ID, HTTP 503, malformed body, redirect, and oversized response each made exactly one request to `/v1/systemone`. The redirect target was not fetched. 503 and malformed responses are bounded transport errors; an unknown ID becomes `kind: "error"` / `reason: "model_error"` and dispatches no action.

The PR is ready for re-review after the maintainer-requested re-cut. Browser provider parity and backend receipts remain https://github.com/kvnloo/cua/issues/78.

## Related work

Refs #3915.

- Maintainer re-cut request: https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3961#pullrequestreview-5345901372
- downstream execution packet: https://github.com/kvnloo/cua/issues/77
- browser provider follow-up: https://github.com/kvnloo/cua/issues/78



## 2026-10-01 current-main refresh

Rebuilt the backend-only slice directly on current upstream `9545a3d17b44b587b593d59090dc140740876a6e` as exact head `48c9fc770674f57ca40466b9f7e006150456a183`. The PR is one commit / seven files with the same intended OpenJev-only delta. Exact-head fork validation is `kvnloo/cua#88`; its checks are queued, so the earlier green evidence remains historical rather than a claim about this head.

## Credit / provenance

- @f-trycua opened #3915 proposing a mockable TypeSafe Jev decision-loop example for Cua Driver. This PR implements that requested integration surface and extends it with the adapter/evidence work described above.


## 2026-10-16 supported CLI acceptance update (supersedes earlier head pins)

Current exact head: `6ece26927ab4c532af8fb459c2de6434a8339aa0`, fast-forward test/docs-only extension of `97cd02c2`. The adapter implementation and existing contributor history are unchanged.

Fresh Python 3.14.8 focused suite: `python -m unittest discover -s python/tests -p test_openjev_model.py -v` — **19 tests PASS**, including eight real subprocess/loopback-HTTP CLI scenarios (exact v2 state/criteria, valid choice, five response failures without retry, and two pre-transport refusals). [Exact evidence, scope and CI handoff](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3961#issuecomment-6217323201).

This is decision-boundary proof only: no Driver, external service, browser/native effect, speedup, TypeScript rerun or full-suite claim. Current-head [jev-use CI](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/38913473901) is `action_required`, not executed green; maintainer re-review remains required. The older tests/timing in this body remain historical at their named SHAs.

title: KDE Plasma 6.6 (Kubuntu 26.04): doctor wayland_backend FAIL — KWin exposes none of the probed target-activation protocols; native Wayland input unavailable (request KWin adapter parity with GNOME WinRects helper)
body:
## Environment

- OS: Kubuntu 26.04 (Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS base), x86_64
- Desktop: KDE Plasma 6.6 / KWin (kwin_wayland) 6.6.6, Wayland session with XWayland (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`, `DISPLAY=:0`)
- cua-driver: 0.28.1 (installed via Hermes installer path, `/home/pokho/.local/bin/cua-driver`)
- Experimental Wayland backend opted in: `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`
- AT-SPI on (org.a11y.Bus reachable); xdg-desktop-portal present; RemoteDesktop portal reachable

## What happens

`cua-driver doctor` (with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`) reports all other checks green but:

```text
❌ wayland_backend: The RemoteDesktop portal is reachable, but this compositor has no verified
   target-activation adapter (foreign-toplevel=false, screencopy=false, ext-image-copy=false,
   ext-output-source=false, virtual-pointer=false, wl_shm=true). Portal/libei input is global
   and would otherwise affect whichever window is focused, potentially the wrong application,
   so cua-driver refuses foreground dispatch.
   → On GNOME, install and enable the bundled WinRects Shell helper, then log out and back in.
     KDE foreground input remains unavailable until a target-addressable KWin activation
     adapter is installed; AX actions and exact background refusals remain usable.
```

So on this stock Kubuntu 26.04 Plasma Wayland session: AT-SPI inspection and portal-based capture work, but synthesized input (clicks/typing) to Wayland-native windows is refused.

## Verification that this is compositor-protocol reality, not a probing bug

`wayland-info` on this KWin 6.6.6 session advertises 65 globals — none of them are the protocols `doctor` probes for:

- `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` — **absent** (consistent with the public compositor support table: KWin is listed "x" for this protocol at 6.6)
- `zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1` — absent (expected; wlroots-only)
- `ext-image-copy-capture-v1` / `ext-output-image-capture-source-v1` — absent
- `zwlr_virtual_pointer_v1` — absent (expected; KWin doesn't implement it)

Full sorted global list for reference:

```text
ext_data_control_manager_v1 ext_idle_notifier_v1 frog_color_management_factory_v1
kde_external_brightness_v1 kde_output_device_v2 kde_output_management_v2 kde_output_order_v1
kde_screen_edge_manager_v1 org_kde_kwin_appmenu_manager org_kde_kwin_blur_manager
org_kde_kwin_contrast_manager org_kde_kwin_dpms_manager org_kde_kwin_idle org_kde_kwin_keystate
org_kde_kwin_server_decoration_manager org_kde_kwin_server_decoration_palette_manager
org_kde_kwin_shadow_manager org_kde_kwin_slide_manager org_kde_plasma_shell
org_kde_plasma_virtual_desktop_management wl_compositor wl_data_device_manager wl_fixes
wl_output wl_seat wl_shm wl_subcompositor wp_alpha_modifier_v1 wp_color_manager_v1
wp_color_representation_manager_v1 wp_content_type_manager_v1 wp_cursor_shape_manager_v1
wp_drm_lease_device_v1 wp_fifo_manager_v1 wp_fractional_scale_manager_v1
wp_linux_drm_syncobj_manager_v1 wp_pointer_warp_v1 wp_presentation
wp_security_context_manager_v1 wp_single_pixel_buffer_manager_v1 wp_tearing_control_manager_v1
wp_viewporter xdg_activation_v1 xdg_system_bell_v1 xdg_toplevel_drag_manager_v1
xdg_toplevel_icon_manager_v1 xdg_toplevel_tag_manager_v1 xdg_wm_base xdg_wm_dialog_v1
zwlr_layer_shell_v1 zwp_idle_inhibit_manager_v1 zwp_keyboard_shortcuts_inhibit_manager_v1
zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 zwp_pointer_constraints_v1 zwp_pointer_gestures_v1
zwp_primary_selection_device_manager_v1 zwp_relative_pointer_manager_v1 zwp_tablet_manager_v2
zwp_text_input_manager_v1 zwp_text_input_manager_v2 zwp_text_input_manager_v3
zxdg_exporter_v2 zxdg_importer_v2 xdg_output_manager_v1
```

Notably KWin 6.6 DOES expose `org_kde_plasma_shell` and `org_kde_plasma_virtual_desktop_management`, and the doctor's own message already has a GNOME-parity escape hatch (the WinRects Shell helper, #2565). I could not find an equivalent KWin-side adapter shipped or documented.

## Ask

1. Is a KWin target-activation adapter (KWin script / KDE-side helper equivalent to the GNOME WinRects extension) planned or in progress (I believe #2793 relates)? If so, is there a tracking issue Plasma users can subscribe to?
2. If not: please consider this a request for one — the diagnosis message itself says "KDE foreground input remains unavailable until a target-addressable KWin activation adapter is installed", but there is currently no way for a Plasma user to obtain/install such an adapter.
3. Minor: consider documenting the Plasma status in the Linux support matrix (distro × desktop × feature, per umbrella #2004) — on stock Kubuntu 26.04 the practical state is: AT-SPI read + portal capture yes, Wayland-native input no, XWayland windows fully functional.

Happy to test any experimental adapter build on this machine.

Related: #1982 (KDE input generally), #2004 (Linux distribution umbrella), #2565 (GNOME WinRects helper), #2793 (trusted KWin target activation, appears in flight).
