title: [Feature]: Omarchy profile kit for the Hyprland plugin on current Driver source
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### User problem

Omarchy ships Cua Driver as `cua-driver-bin` (0.28.2 in its edge, rc and stable channels) and ships `cua-hyprland-plugin` as an optional package, currently in edge only. The plugin is built from [`cua-hyprland-kit-v1.1.0-omarchy-stable-20260910`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-hyprland-kit-v1.1.0-omarchy-stable-20260910), whose source is `cc54254` (Driver 0.26.1). Omarchy users of the plugin therefore don't get #3901 or any later plugin fixes.

Every Driver release also ships a plugin build kit (for example in [`cua-driver-rs-v0.29.1`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.29.1)). Those kits pin Hyprland `0.56.2-1` and GCC `16.1.1 20260728`, and no Omarchy channel ships either:

| Package | edge | rc | stable |
|---|---|---|---|
| hyprland | 0.56.2-3 | 0.56.2-2 | 0.56.2-2 |
| aquamarine | 0.15.1-1 | 0.15.0-2 | 0.15.0-2 |
| gcc / libgcc / libstdc++ | 16.2.1+r23+gd564253eb6c8-1 (GCC 16.2.1 20260810) | same | same |

Under the ownership split agreed in omacom/omarchy-pkgs#346, profiles and build kits belong to Cua, so Omarchy can't move the plugin to current source on its own.

### Desired outcome

- A kit like v1.1.0, built from a revision that includes #3901 (0.28.3 or later), with a profile matching Omarchy edge: Hyprland 0.56.2-3, Aquamarine 0.15.1-1, GCC 16.2.1 20260810 and shared `libstdc++.so.6.0.36`. rc and stable will match it at their next snapshot, so one edge profile is enough.
- The kit names the Driver releases it is qualified with. Omarchy updates Driver on its own cadence, so we need to know when a Driver bump changes the pairing.
- Guidance on which Arch rebuilds of a pinned package can reuse a kit after re-measuring (for example Hyprland `-3`, whose executable and headers are byte-identical to `-2`), and which need a new kit and native qualification (for example an Aquamarine version change).

### Current workaround

Omarchy stays on the v1.1.0 kit. When Arch rebuilt pinned packages, Omarchy derived a profile locally from the verified kit. The derived profile changes only the profile id, the package release and the Hyprland/Aquamarine package versions, and keeps every source, compiler, header and runtime hash (omacom/omarchy-pkgs#507, [derivation in the PKGBUILD](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-pkgs/blob/f7577b59a6d8e6285e0753f64638928a5779b56d/pkgbuilds/cua-hyprland-plugin/PKGBUILD#L80)).

Omarchy also applies a downstream keymap patch on top of the kit source: [`independent-keymaps.patch`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-pkgs/blob/b2176d5cab67cb4bd7b400251ab5d00396bc07de/pkgbuilds/cua-hyprland-plugin/independent-keymaps.patch), from omacom/omarchy-pkgs#473. Its foreground Num Lock part is the same problem as #3968 and #3970.

### Affected components and platforms

- `libs/cua-driver/hyprland-plugin` kits and profiles.
- Arch Linux x86_64, Hyprland 0.56.2, Omarchy edge, rc and stable.
- The other pinned packages are identical in all three channels: glibc 2.44+r24+g16be1518495f-1, hyprcursor 0.1.13-7, hyprgraphics 0.5.1-4, hyprlang 0.6.8-5, hyprutils 0.14.2-1, libxkbcommon 1.13.2-1 and wayland 1.26.0-1.
- Hyprland `0.56.2-3` only splits out `hyprpm`. Its executable (SHA-256 `da8fcacf347bcbed83edc40108c6e2298da095e22246bd764e9bb382786cebb2`) and all 498 header/pkg-config files are byte-identical to `-2`.

### Alternatives and prior art

- RFC #3550 covers the design of Hyprland background input. This request is only about packaging current source for Omarchy's environments.
- The per-release build kits are the closest fit, but they target a Hyprland and GCC that Omarchy doesn't ship.
- Omarchy could re-profile a per-release kit itself, but under the omacom/omarchy-pkgs#346 split, profiles and native qualification belong to Cua.

### Implementation ideas

Kit tooling could support re-measuring an existing profile: take a verified kit, measure the installed environment, and produce a derived profile only if every compiler, header, executable and runtime hash still matches. Omarchy could then stop carrying its own derivation code in the PKGBUILD.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: feat(cua-driver): four Hyprland input lanes with concurrent parallel_mouse_drag
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on native Hyprland the input plugin exposes only two agent lanes, and `parallel_mouse_drag` hard-errors unless the nested cua-compositor socket is set. So two is the ceiling for agents with their own pointer on one desktop, and even those cannot run a batch of drags at the same time.
- What changed:
  - The v3 input plugin now has four independent lanes (`kInputLanes` in the plugin, `MAX_LANES` in the driver). Lanes 0/1 keep their socket and seat names byte-identical; lanes 2/3 add `cua-input-v3-3.sock` / `cua-input-v3-4.sock` and the `Cua-Agent-3` / `Cua-Agent-4` seats. Status JSON aggregates over every lane.
  - The driver treats a missing higher-lane socket (an older two-lane plugin) as a busy lane rather than a connect error, keeps the new seats out of primary-seat selection, and exposes `background_admission()` so batch callers can apply the per-app gate before dispatching anything.
  - `parallel_mouse_drag` on native Hyprland (no `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET`) runs every item at the same time on its own lane, keyed by the item's `session`, and moves each item's overlay cursor. Everything is validated before any lane is claimed: 2 to 4 items, distinct non-default sessions, one item per application process (the plugin refuses a second lane on the same client), left button, straight `from`/`to` segments or a two-point `path` only (the plugin `DRAG` cannot hold a press across segments, so `fn` and longer paths refuse), duration clamped to the plugin's 50 to 2000 ms. Partial outcomes report per-item results.
  - `CUA_HYPRLAND_QUALIFY_ANY_APP=1` (default off, exact value `1`) admits every app to the background plugin route instead of only the exact Calc/Inkscape builds that were proven. The code comment records why the gate exists: an unqualified app can drop second-seat input or act on the wrong widget while the call still reports `unverifiable`.

## Related work

Independent of #3969 and #3970 (other Hyprland plugin fixes); the branches do not depend on each other.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change): this changes the lane count documented in `protocol/cua-input-v3.md` and adds an opt-in escape hatch for the per-app background gate, so I am opening it as a draft for a maintainer decision. Happy to split the gate into its own PR, drop it, or move the discussion to an RFC.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - Plugin: two more agent seats exist while the module is loaded. Lanes 0/1 are unchanged, so an older driver keeps working against the new plugin, and the new driver works against an older two-lane plugin (lanes 2/3 read as busy).
  - `parallel_mouse_drag` now succeeds on native Hyprland where it used to return an error. No schema change: it reuses the existing per-item `session`.
  - The any-app gate is opt-in and off by default; default admission is unchanged.
- Risk and rollback:
  - Four agent seats means up to four virtual pointers/keyboards registered with the compositor while agents hold lanes (lanes still expire on the plugin's idle timeout).
  - The primary-target guard still applies: a lane is refused (`primary_target_busy`) for the surface under the user's pointer or keyboard focus, so a batch can partially succeed. Callers get per-item results.
  - Rollback: revert the two commits; the plugin rebuild returns to two lanes.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - Plugin: `ctest` 16/16 with the input build (`-DCUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT=ON`) on this branch.
  - Driver on this branch: `cargo test --release -p platform-linux --lib` 559 passed, 0 failed (6 ignored); `-p cua-driver-core --lib` 751 passed, 0 failed. New tests cover the four-lane pool, socket naming, the batch planner (item count, duplicate sessions, same-process items, path shapes, duration clamp) and the opt-in gate.
  - `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: Omarchy, Hyprland 0.56.2, plugin loaded at login in a fresh session, `hyprctl -j cua:status` reporting four lanes and all four sockets present.
  - Four separate `foot` terminal processes on one workspace, the user's focus and pointer on a fifth window. One `parallel_mouse_drag` call with four items (one per terminal, 1800 ms each) returned `ok` on lanes 0 to 3 and took 1.81 s end to end, so the drags ran concurrently. Each terminal showed its own text selection afterwards.
  - With the pointer left over one of the four terminals, that item refused `primary_target_busy` and the other three still ran, as intended.
  - Foreground `type_text` on the same session was unaffected.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The canonical native harness and the qualified-app proofs were not run. The Python live-certification harnesses under `hyprland-plugin/tests` still assume two lanes.
  - Live testing used `foot` with the opt-in gate; the Calc/Inkscape qualified builds were not available on the test machine.
  - Built and tested on this branch (current `main`); the live run used the same two commits on top of v0.29.1.

title: feat(cua-driver): opt-in parallel background input lanes on macOS
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: every physical action takes the process-wide desktop-action coordinator, and on macOS all MCP clients share one daemon. Several agents working in different apps therefore run strictly one action at a time, even when every action is a background AX or PID-routed event that never touches the real pointer, the global HID queue or the frontmost app. Overlay cursors also queue behind that lock, so two sessions' cursors cannot glide at once.
- What changed:
  - New opt-in switch `CUA_DRIVER_PARALLEL_BACKGROUND=1` (read once at startup, default off). When set, macOS `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `scroll`, `type_text`, `press_key` and `set_value` report an independent input lane for exact pid + window background calls. Left-button pixel clicks are excluded, because that route briefly makes the target app active.
  - The coordinator becomes a fair read/write lock. Coordinated actions (foreground, desktop scope, global keyboard) stay exclusive. Independent lanes are admitted shared, so they overlap each other but never a coordinated action. Same-app actions still serialize on the existing per-pid mutation lease and the per-pid text-input guard.
  - `move_cursor` outside desktop scope only moves the overlay, so it no longer takes the lock at all (switch or not). Desktop-scope moves stay exclusive.
  - Small fix found along the way: if the background pixel-focus hit test panics, `click` now returns an error instead of falling through to the activating pixel rung.

## Related work

Refs the Linux precedent: `DragTool` already overrides `has_independent_input_lane`; this extends the same mechanism to the macOS background routes.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change): this changes the driver's concurrency contract for physical actions, so I am opening it as a draft for a maintainer decision. Happy to move it to an RFC, narrow the tool list, or drop the env switch in favour of a config or manifest setting.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - Default behaviour is unchanged apart from `move_cursor` (overlay-only moves no longer queue behind other actions).
  - With the switch on, background actions against different apps overlap. No schema, CLI or MCP change.
- Risk and rollback:
  - A foreground action now waits for background actions already in flight instead of interleaving with them.
  - While several agents work at once, background focus-steal suppression is active for more of the time, so a user switching apps during that window may be pulled back more often.
  - Recordings of parallel runs contain interleaved steps.
  - Calls with an `element_token` but no `window_id` stay serialized; agents should pass pid and window_id.
  - Rollback: unset the switch, or revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - On this branch (macOS): `cargo test --release -p platform-macos --lib` 343 passed, 0 failed (3 ignored); `-p cua-driver-core --lib` 747 passed, 12 failed. The same 12 tests (the `perception_client` / `perception_tools` worker tests) fail identically on unmodified `main` in this environment. New tests cover the coordination predicate: switch off keeps every tool coordinated; switch on + exact background window is independent; foreground or desktop calls stay coordinated; window-scope `move_cursor` is independent and desktop-scope is coordinated; shared admissions overlap while an exclusive admission waits for them.
  - Breaking the left-button pixel-click exclusion on purpose made two tests fail.
  - `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS, driver running as the LaunchAgent daemon with the switch set in its environment. Four sessions, each with its own overlay cursor, worked in four apps at once (TextEdit `type_text`, Calculator button presses, Dictionary search `set_value`, Font Book search `set_value`). Their first actions landed within about 30 ms of each other, the frontmost app never changed, and Calculator's result was correct for the pressed sequence.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The canonical macOS E2E suites were not run.
  - The live run used this commit on v0.29.1 with two unrelated local patches (the #3353 sheet fix and a larger AX walk cap); this branch is the commit alone on current `main`.
  - Not measured: throughput under heavy contention, and interaction with recording and the perception extension. Simultaneous overlay glides were not checked visually on this build.

title: test(cua-driver): add a Wayland presentation-timestamp fixture
body:
## Summary

Adds the first fixture-only Wayland presentation evidence slice for #4012: one fixture-owned counter and `wl_surface` in the existing native Sway lane. The fixture assigns an update ID before changing the counter, writes it to independent state and the window title, requests `wp_presentation.feedback` before that update's commit, and accepts feedback only for the matching ID. Unknown or late callbacks are recorded and cannot claim another row.

The fixture records the compositor's presentation clock and callback receipt separately from presentation time. The runner reports an incomparable clock or unavailable feedback as a typed lane limitation; it never subtracts timestamps across clock domains. The joined `return_minus_present_ns` remains signed. The cell covers a matched presented mutation, no-op, superseded/discarded update, and a refused Driver action that produces no fixture input or sample. This PR changes no scheduler or public Driver action API.

Refs #4012. Protocol review and acceptance clarifications were provided by @kvnloo in that issue; no external code was incorporated.

## Compatibility and risk

- Test fixture, E2E runner, and documentation only. No production behavior or public contract changes.
- Presentation-relative deltas require the advertised `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` clock in this lane. A foreign clock is retained as `clock_mismatch` without a latency claim.
- The native test is limited to one Sway lane; it makes no cross-compositor performance claim.

## Validation

- Fixture unit tests: 25 passed, including wrong and late feedback correlation.
- `cua-driver-e2e` row tests: 7 passed; native cell is ignored in ordinary unit runs.
- Probe classification shell test: passed for ready, foreign-clock, unsupported protocol, unavailable feedback, and invalid-evidence paths.
- Focused native cell against local headless Sway 1.9 / wlroots 0.17: 1 passed at commit `409af68`. Four retained rows: 2 verified presentations, 1 no-op, 1 discarded superseded update; no clock mismatches or deadline misses. The probe observed feedback for its own update ID in `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`.
- Rust formatting checks, shell syntax checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

The GitHub-hosted native Wayland lane and final candidate desktop matrix have not run yet. This PR is ready for review; promotion remains pending that evidence and maintainer scope review. This is intentionally non-releasing; the `no-release` label is required by the repository's release rules. RyanL2 lacks permission to apply labels in `trycua/cua`, so a maintainer needs to add it.

title: [Bug]: Linux/Hyprland: Brave PWA fails exact AT-SPI binding (root class + app-name prefix)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Cua Driver 0.29.1 discovers a Brave installed web-app window on native Hyprland, but its AT-SPI tree cannot be bound to the exact native window. BraveBrowserRootView and the installed app-name prefix differ from the Chromium root/title cases recognized by the release.

### Reproduction

1. Open an installed Brave web app on native Wayland/Hyprland. The observed example was X, with its existing desktop starter and --app-id/StartupWMClass.
2. Use list_windows and select that exact (pid, window_id).
3. Call get_window_state for that exact pair.
4. Compare the compositor title with the AT-SPI top-level attributes and geometry.

Observed identity data, page content omitted:
```text
Native title: X - <page title>
AT-SPI frame title: <page title>
AT-SPI class: BraveBrowserRootView
AT-SPI extents: 1920 x 1080 (matching selected native window)
Executable: /opt/brave-bin/brave
Result: accessibility_window_identity_unproven
```
The identity refusal was repeatedly observed before the local candidate described below. This is physical-host evidence, not a disposable-VM canonical replay.

### Expected behavior

A uniquely proven Brave PWA/native-root relationship yields exact-window tokens and bounds. Ambiguous sibling windows, unrelated prefix matches and mismatched geometry must still be refused. No request to weaken identity, permission or input protections.

### Actual behavior

The unmodified release returns an application-scoped AT-SPI tree without an exact binding for the observed window: accessibility_window_identity_unproven. The editor is visible, but exact-window element tokens and bounds are unavailable.

### Environment

- Arch Linux / Omarchy 4.0.4-1, x86_64, native Wayland.
- Hyprland 0.56.2-2, commit efb50993780079460b0cbed1363e2166a2de1d9f.
- brave-bin 1:1.96.59-1; executable /opt/brave-bin/brave.
- Cua Driver 0.29.1, release source 7a8f66ad04e62fccb18cca9965f2964fcaee124e.
- MCP direct mode, CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1.
- Three monitors; physical keyboard layout German.
- Optional Hyprland input-v3 plugin built against the host ABI/toolchain. After desktop restart its status reported ABI match and both transports ready; no Hyprland configuration errors.

### Evidence

A local candidate based on the exact release recognized BraveBrowserRootView and the installed-app title prefix only when backed by the matching installed starter (name, app ID, StartupWMClass, Exec), Chromium executable identity, matching dimensions and bidirectional uniqueness. The same real window then returned snapshot_id and element_token without the identity refusal. Seven focused binding tests passed, including negative identity/geometry/ambiguity cases.

This candidate is NOT installed as the production driver and has not passed the complete canonical desktop matrix. It also contains separate input experiments; those are not evidence of a fully working Brave input route. No raw traces, private profile data, account content or screenshots are attached. A synthetic-page reproduction or focused patch can be provided if useful.

### Workaround and additional context

Related: #4029 describes a Chromium profile-suffix mismatch. This case concerns BraveBrowserRootView and an installed web app's app-name PREFIX, not a profile suffix. Please link/merge if an existing issue already covers both cases.

Separate known/unproven capability limits observed after the local binding fix (context, NOT additional bug claims): background text was refused; the editor exposed no usable EditableText/Value route; German-layout foreground keyboard input is outside the documented canonical-US contract. Some native attempts returned transport errors with unknown delivery; a keymap-related cause is NOT confirmed. A semantic showContextMenu experiment opened the visible menu, but native menu selection did not reach Paste. Desktop observation also refused the tested multi-output layout.

A separate Codex browser-extension connector successfully entered and submitted German text in the same Brave profile. That is a workaround through a DIFFERENT integration, not proof that Cua Driver's native route works.

Please assess safe exact binding for Brave installed web apps and clarify the supported foreground text/paste route for Brave on Hyprland with a non-US keyboard.

### Submission checks

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.

title: macOS: background keyboard refused (same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity) when Chrome has a single visible window
body:
## Summary
Background keyboard input (`type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey`) to a Chrome window is refused with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` even though Chrome has only **one** visible, on-screen top-level window. The "other eligible top-level windows" appear to be Chrome's own transient helper surfaces (the omnibox suggestion dropdown, small popups/bubbles), not real sibling windows.

This looks like the same class of problem as #2905 (compositor surfaces counted as siblings), but for Chrome's helper windows.

## Environment
- cua-driver 0.28.2
- macOS 26.6.1
- Google Chrome (stable), single profile window, many tabs

## Steps
1. Have Chrome open with exactly one normal browser window.
2. `list_windows({pid})` — only one window has `is_on_screen: true`. The rest are off-screen, 1×1, 30px-high strips, or omnibox-popup-sized (~1385×218) windows.
3. `type_text({pid, element_token: <text field in the page>, text: "..."})`, or `press_key({pid, window_id, key: "escape"})`.

## Expected
The keyboard goes to the target window, or the gate ignores Chrome's own non-activatable helper surfaces.

## Actual
```json
{"code":"same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity","effect":"refused",
 "reason":"pid N owns 2 other eligible top-level window(s); process-scoped key events cannot be proven to reach window W ..."}
```
The refusal went away later in the session once the transient popup had closed. Enter in the omnibox was still refused (`press_key` returned `refused`) while its suggestion dropdown was open.

## Impact
Any form entry in a web app has to escalate to `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, or fall back to pixel-focus typing.

## Possible fix
Exclude windows that are not on screen, have a zero or near-zero area, or have a helper window role (popup, menu, tooltip) from the sibling count. Alternatively, treat a Chrome popup that is a child of the target window as part of the target.

title: macOS: Chrome popups/menus drawn in screenshot but missing from AX tree and list_windows; pixel clicks fall through to window underneath
body:
## Summary
Chrome's native popups — the omnibox suggestion dropdown and the context menu of a saved tab group on the bookmarks bar — are **painted in the `get_window_state` screenshot of the main window**, but:
- they are absent from that window's AX tree (and not in `elements`),
- they are not listed by `list_windows` as on-screen,
- a window-local pixel click aimed at them lands on the **main window underneath**.

## Environment
- cua-driver 0.28.2, macOS 26.6.1, Google Chrome stable

## Repro A — omnibox suggestion click goes to the bookmarks bar
1. `set_value` the address bar to a URL. The suggestion dropdown opens, visible in the screenshot.
2. `press_key` Enter → `refused` (see the keyboard-gate issue).
3. `click({pid, window_id: <main>, x, y})` at a suggestion row taken from the screenshot, just below the omnibox.
4. **Actual:** the click hits the bookmarks bar under the dropdown and opens a *saved tab group* (a new tab is restored). The suggestion is not chosen.

## Repro B — a context menu that can't be dismissed or seen in AX
1. `click({element_token: <saved tab group button on the bookmarks bar>, action: "show_menu"})` — the menu (Open Group / Move Group to New Window / Unpin / **Delete Group** / tabs) appears in the screenshot.
2. No `AXMenu` is present in `get_window_state` (even with max_elements=1500), and none of the listed windows are on screen.
3. A background pixel click on blank page content leaves the menu open.
4. Only `press_key({key:"escape", delivery_mode:"foreground"})` closed it.

## Why it matters
- **Safety:** a destructive menu item (Delete Group) sits on screen and the agent can't observe it semantically. Clicks meant for an overlay silently land on something else.
- The screenshot and the AX tree disagree, with nothing like `degraded` or a blocker to signal it.

## Expected
One of these:
- expose Chrome's popup/menu windows (`list_windows` + AX), or
- report them as blockers on the target window (see #2589), and refuse or redirect pixel clicks whose point is covered by a different same-pid surface.

title: macOS: background clicks silently no-op on some React controls in Chrome; foreground works, result gives no escalation
body:
## Summary
In a React single-page app in Chrome, several controls ignore **background** clicks — both the accessibility `press` and window-pixel clicks — while the same click with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` works first time. The driver returns `effect:"unverifiable"` and no escalation hint, so the agent can't tell that the action silently did nothing.

## Environment
- cua-driver 0.28.2, macOS 26.6.1, Google Chrome stable, no CDP/browser binding (consumer profile)

## Cases observed
1. **Icon toggle (show/hide a masked value):**
   - `click({element_token})` on the AX element labelled "Show" → `unverifiable`, nothing changes.
   - Background pixel click on the eye icon → `unverifiable`, nothing changes.
   - The same pixel with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` → the value is revealed immediately.
2. **Global search result rows (a React combobox dropdown):** a background pixel click on a result row closes the dropdown without navigating. The `AXLink` `press` for the same result works.
3. **Calendar day cell in a date picker:** a background pixel click closes the picker without selecting the date. Typing the digits into the date field works.

## Expected
- Background delivery reaches these controls, as it does for most other buttons on the same page, or
- the result carries `escalation: {target: "foreground"}` / `suspected_noop` when post-click state (the AX tree and pixels) is unchanged, instead of a bare `unverifiable`.

## Notes
Other buttons, radios, tabs and links on the same page worked fine in the background. The failures seem to be controls that act on `pointerdown`/`mousedown` or check `isTrusted`/focus. This may overlap with the #4009 ActionResult vocabulary work.

title: feat(cua-driver): select an exported Android Activity in app launch
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `app launch` can only start a package's default launcher Activity. Apps with secondary exported screens (debug galleries, previews, test entry points) need a manifest overlay that rewrites the launcher before Cua can reach them.
- What changed: `app launch` accepts an optional `activity`, a fully qualified class name inside the allowlisted package. Package-only launch is unchanged.
  - The runtime resolves the component before any session state changes. It refuses `activity_not_found` (including a class that belongs to another package), `activity_not_exported`, `activity_disabled`, and `activity_alias_unsupported`. `app_not_allowed` still applies first.
  - After dispatch, the runtime reads back the new task's base Activity before returning a target. A mismatch is `uncertain`, so Stop is required, as with other post-dispatch failures.
  - The Activity that starts a package's owned task stays bound for the session. A package-only launch keeps switching to that task. An explicit different Activity is refused with `launch_target_conflict`, and the current target stays usable.
  - The launch response adds `activity`, which is the bound component.
  - The fixture gains a non-launcher `DetailActivity` that reports its own class, task, and display, plus non-exported and disabled variants for the refusal cases.
  - The field is carried through the Rust contract and schema, host CLI (`--activity`), phone-local CLI, SDK (`launchApp(..., activity)`), shared invalid-request cases, `smoke.py`, and the README.

## Related work

Refs #3673. Scope follows the maintainer reply on #3673. Based on `feat/cua-driver-android-local` (#3674 at `271d2e46`); I'll retarget to `main` when #3674 lands.

RFC: #3673

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - This adds one optional `app.launch` field to the experimental `cua.android.v0` contract.
  - Callers that omit it see the same behaviour, apart from the extra `activity` field in the response.
  - An older runtime refuses the new field with `unknown_field` (exit 2), so it fails closed.
  - No new Android permission is used. Selection is limited to exported, enabled components of the allowlisted package, and task ownership, stale-handle, and Stop rules are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: this is a self-contained change to the experimental Android path; revert the commit to roll back. Desktop dispatch is untouched.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `./gradlew :runtime:assembleDebug :sdk:assembleDebug :demo:assembleDebug :fixture-target:assembleDebug :runtime:testDebugUnitTest :sdk:testDebugUnitTest :demo:testDebugUnitTest :runtime:lintDebug :sdk:lintDebug :demo:lintDebug :fixture-target:lintDebug`: pass. Unit tests: runtime 5, sdk 11, demo 28.
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract` (59 pass), the `android_bridge` tests in `cua-driver` (10 pass), and `cargo fmt --check`: pass.
  - Mutation check: deleting the `launch_target_conflict` refusal makes `SessionTasksTest` fail.
- Manual or platform evidence: `scripts/smoke.py --runs 2` passes every block, including the new selection block, on two targets:
  - API 37 `google_apis` arm64 emulator.
  - Physical Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Android 17 / API 37, unfolded.

  The new block checks each refusal code. It then checks the fixture's own report of the selected class, task, and display, and a Cua tap on the selected screen. After that it checks the stale-handle refusal after a relaunch, the package-only switch, the conflict refusal leaving the target usable, and task removal on Stop.

  As downstream evidence, the RepoGlance debug widget gallery opened directly with `--activity` on the Fold, with no manifest overlay. Sanitized captures and per-call results: [proof assets](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/tree/main/cua-android/3673/2026-09-26) (`pr1-*`).
- Independent review: an exact-head OpenClaw code review of `9216d6afe` against base `271d2e46` ran on our review host (request `req-20260926T230931Z-12706745289`). It was comprehensive scope, with priorities up to P3 and an exact repository/PR/base/head match. It completed clean, with 0 findings.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - Repository CI hasn't run yet. As a first-time contributor from a fork, my `pull_request` workflows (including `CI: Release metadata`) are waiting for maintainer workflow approval.
  - No shared desktop behavior changed, so I didn't run the desktop E2E matrix.
  - `cargo clippy` was not run locally.
  - Intent extras, data URIs, and deep links are out of scope.
  - An exported Activity protected by a permission the shell lacks fails at dispatch and reports `uncertain`, not a pre-dispatch refusal.
  - No `capabilities` entry was added. I'm happy to add `app.launch.activity` if you want it discoverable.
  - Pre-existing harness gap, not changed here: on a fresh physical install `smoke.py` fails its display-0 typing check. The demo's first-launch notification-permission dialog takes focus, and `lifecycle-smoke.py` pre-grants that permission while `smoke.py` does not. Both runs above pre-granted it. It is fixed in the emulator→Pixel harness PR, #4249 ([capture](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/blob/main/cua-android/3673/2026-09-26/fold-display0-fresh-install-permission-dialog.png)).

title: test(cua-driver): qualify one Android candidate on an emulator, then a physical phone
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: the Android harnesses are run by hand, one device at a time. Nothing ties an emulator pass to the physical-phone pass of the same build, confirms the phone is really a phone, or records what a physical run leaves out. On a fresh physical install, `smoke.py` also failed for reasons unrelated to the driver.
- What changed:
  - **`scripts/qualify.py`:** qualifies one built candidate on an explicitly selected emulator, then on an explicitly selected physical phone. `--physical` is required unless `--emulator-only` is passed. The receipt's top-level `qualification` is `full` only when both phases pass, `emulator_only` for an explicit emulator-only pass, and `incomplete` (exit 1) otherwise.
    - **Admission before any install:** it refuses, with exit 2, a device of the wrong class for its role (checked via `ro.kernel.qemu`/`ro.boot.qemu`), an offline or unauthorized device, the same serial in both roles, `--runs` below 1, and an evidence directory that Git would track.
    - **Same candidate on both devices:** the same APKs and host Driver go through the existing `deploy.py` and `smoke.py` on the emulator, and optionally `lifecycle-smoke.py` with `--lifecycle`. The phone runs only after the emulator passes; otherwise it is recorded as `blocked`. Before each phase the harness re-hashes the artifacts and compares the bytes of every installed package with them.
    - **Unsupported cases are recorded, not skipped:** a device on an API level the runtime cannot install on is recorded as `unsupported`. On the phone, `receipt.json` lists the checks deliberately not run: `lifecycle-smoke.py` (it reads the notification shade), human IME concurrency, and fold or rotation changes during a session. It also records the Driver's own unsupported and unverified capabilities.
    - **Cleanup:** it force-stops only the synthetic apps and waits out the runtime lease if a controller died. It then records any leftover Cua display or synthetic task, separately from the original failure.
    - **No device identifiers in the receipt:** devices are named by role only, and failure tails are redacted. Screenshots and full logs stay in the evidence directory.
  - **Two existing harness assumptions that broke on real devices:**
    - `smoke.py` typed into the demo while its first-launch notification-permission dialog held display-0 focus on a fresh install. It now grants the permission, as `lifecycle-smoke.py` already did, and requires the demo editor to have focus before synthetic typing. Any other window on top now fails with the focused package named, instead of a text mismatch ([capture of the original failure](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/blob/main/cua-android/3673/2026-09-26/fold-display0-fresh-install-permission-dialog.png)).
    - `lifecycle-smoke.py` expected the Cua notification to be expanded. The shade expands only its top notification, and on this API 37 image "Set a screen lock" and "Serial console enabled" sit above Cua, so the Stop action was hidden. It now expands the Cua row when needed.
  - The README documents the flow, and the unittest command now covers every `scripts/test_*.py`.

## Related work

Refs #3673. This is the second of the two PRs agreed on #3673; the first is #4247. Both are based on `feat/cua-driver-android-local` (#3674 at `271d2e46`), and a trial merge of the two branches is clean.

RFC: #3673

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: test harness only; no runtime, SDK, contract, or CLI change. `smoke.py` now grants `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` to the synthetic demo on the selected device, the same grant `lifecycle-smoke.py` already made.
- Risk and rollback: revert the commit. The harness mutates only the synthetic packages the existing scripts already install.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 42 pass (35 existing relay tests plus 7 new `test_qualify.py` tests covering admission, gating, the overall verdict, unsupported API levels, redaction, and residue parsing).
- Pre-mutation refusals (each exits 2 and creates no evidence directory):
  - a phone passed as `--emulator`
  - the same serial for both roles
  - an absent serial
  - an evidence directory inside the repository
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - `qualify.py --emulator <API 37 google_apis arm64 emulator> --physical <Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Android 17 / API 37, unfolded> --lifecycle` at `924591f28`, with the synthetic demo uninstalled first on both devices so each started as a fresh install:
    - Emulator: `deploy`, `smoke`, and `lifecycle` all pass.
    - Phone: `deploy` and `smoke` pass.
    - Installed bytes match on both devices, and cleanup is clean on both.
    - The receipt's verdict is `qualification: full`: [pr2-receipt-final-924591f28.json](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/blob/main/cua-android/3673/2026-09-26/pr2-receipt-final-924591f28.json).
  - The first real run ([receipt](https://github.com/saari-co/public-oss-proof-assets/blob/main/cua-android/3673/2026-09-26/pr2-receipt-first-run.json)) caught both harness problems above: `smoke.py` passed on a fresh emulator install with the permission fix, `lifecycle-smoke.py` failed on the collapsed notification, and the phone phase was correctly `blocked`.
  - Also observed on that failed run: after the harness force-stopped the demo, lease expiry destroyed the owned task, but one Cua display stayed in `dumpsys display` until the next session was created and stopped. A shell-owned session left to expire removed both the task and the display within 75 s, so I'm reporting this as an observation, not a reproduced defect.
- Independent review: exact-head OpenClaw code reviews against base `271d2e46` ran on our review host, at comprehensive scope, with priorities up to P3 and an exact repository/PR/base/head match.
  - `cf41cfbd3`, epoch 1 (`req-20260926T230932Z-127108128095`): 2 findings at P2.
    1. Omitting `--physical` exited 0 and looked like a full qualification. Accepted and fixed: the phone is now required unless `--emulator-only` is passed, and the verdict is recorded explicitly.
    2. `--runs 0` would pass without any smoke runs. The claimed consequence doesn't hold, because `smoke.py` already asserts `runs > 0` and would fail the phase. But that check only fired after deploy, so `qualify.py` now refuses it before touching any device. Fixed in `924591f28`.
  - `924591f28`, epoch 2 (`req-20260926T231510Z-1291324608`): completed clean, 0 findings.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - Repository CI hasn't run yet. As a first-time contributor from a fork, my `pull_request` workflows (including `CI: Release metadata`) are waiting for maintainer workflow approval.
  - No shared desktop behavior changed, so I didn't run the desktop E2E matrix.
  - There is no Android CI workflow, so these checks were run locally.
  - The focus precondition was exercised by the fresh-install run, not by a synthetic overlay test.
  - Release-tracked Cua Driver files changed with no release entry intended. Could a maintainer apply `no-release`? I don't have label permissions.

title: [Bug]: X11 cursor badges repeat across render tiles
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On X11, multiple session cursors can display copies of another session's label or delivery/target chips. Observed in [Maka's native cursor helper](https://github.com/apache/maka/blob/3e916d8640f233b7a7063d298944e34022c486b0/crates/computer-use/src/cursor/helper.rs).

### Reproduction

1. Initialize `platform_linux::overlay` and start its render thread in an X11 session.
2. Using `send_command_for` with two distinct session keys, send `SetEnabled(true)`, distinct `SetSessionLabel` values, and `SnapTo` positions `(160,160)` and `(320,240)`.
3. Inspect the overlay while both labels are visible. `BeginAction` with delivery/target modifiers reproduces the same problem with chips.

### Expected behavior

Each session's badge appears once at its screen-relative position, including where tiles overlap or touch screen edges.

### Actual behavior

Other sessions' badges are clamped into each cursor's render tile, producing duplicate labels/chips.

### Environment

Cua Driver Rust 0.29.1 (`5b3d48df`); Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64; X11 via Xvfb at 1024×768, with picom 12.5.

### Evidence

[PR #4260](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4260) includes a regression comparing tiled rendering with a full-frame reference. It fails with the original badge layout and passes with the fix. Run from `libs/cua-driver/rust` on that branch:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib cursor_tiles_match_full_frame
```

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): lay out X11 cursor badges in screen coordinates
body:
## Summary

X11 cursor tiles lay out badges against their own bounds, pulling other sessions' labels/chips into each tile. Use the screen viewport for layout and tile bounds for clipping, so each badge appears once at its screen-relative position.

Keep bounded tiles and correct glyph placement where tiles clip labels, including at screen edges.

## Related work

Fixes #4259. No RFC required; this corrects internal rendering.

## Compatibility and risk

Public APIs and bounded tile allocation are unchanged. Glyph rasterization is shared across platforms; validation is listed below.

## Validation

- Formatting, release-title/version checks, and focused `cursor-overlay` / `platform-linux` unit tests passed.
- Regression covers distant and overlapping tiles, screen corners, and clipped glyphs; restoring either badge clamping or incorrect glyph rounding makes it fail.
- Native X11 smoke with and without picom confirmed two distinct labels and independent cursor cleanup.

title: fix(cua-driver): hide agent seats from unrelated Wayland clients
body:
## Problem

The Hyprland plugin advertises its synthetic `wl_seat` globals to every Wayland client. A single-seat client can bind an agent seat instead of the physical user seat.

## Changes

Compose agent-seat visibility with Hyprland's sandbox and privileged-global policy so only `cua-driver` clients receive the synthetic seats. Add focused policy coverage. This changes registry visibility; it does not expand the input lanes in [#4230](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4230).

- The agent-seat policy test compiled with `g++ -std=c++2c -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror` and passed.

Fixes #4257

title: [Bug]: existing-profile attach through the macOS daemon cannot read DevToolsActivePort
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile` against Chrome's default profile is refused with `could not read the browser's DevToolsActivePort file: Operation not permitted (os error 1)` when it runs in the LaunchAgent daemon. The same file reads fine from the calling terminal, and the same prepare succeeds in a runtime started with `cua-driver mcp --direct`.

### Reproduction

1. In Chrome, turn on "Allow remote debugging for this browser instance" at `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging`. `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/DevToolsActivePort` then names the port Chrome listens on.
2. Run the daemon from its LaunchAgent: `cua-driver serve --permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals`.
3. `cua-driver call get_browser_state '{"pid": <chrome pid>, "window_id": <window id>, "session": "s"}'` returns `browser_consent_required` with `next_action: browser_prepare`, as expected.
4. `cua-driver call browser_prepare '{"pid": <chrome pid>, "window_id": <window id>, "session": "s", "strategy": {"kind": "existing_profile"}}'`

Seen on my one attempt through the daemon. The same browser attached from a direct runtime a few minutes later.

### Expected behavior

The prepare attaches to the existing profile, as it does from a direct runtime.

### Actual behavior

```
$ cua-driver call browser_prepare '{"pid": 1622, "window_id": 333, "session": "s", "strategy": {"kind": "existing_profile"}}'
{
  "refusal": {
    "code": "browser_route_unavailable",
    "message": "could not read the browser's DevToolsActivePort file: Operation not permitted (os error 1)"
  },
  "status": "refused"
}
```

From the same terminal, `head -1 ~/Library/Application\ Support/Google/Chrome/DevToolsActivePort` prints the port. In a runtime started with `cua-driver mcp --direct --grant existing-profile`, the same call returns `attached_existing_profile` with `endpoint_ownership.method: devtools_active_ports_file` and every `side_effects` entry false. I don't know which macOS protection refuses the daemon's read.

### Environment

Cua Driver 0.30.1, daemon started by its LaunchAgent in unrestricted mode; CuaDriver.app holds Accessibility and Screen Recording. macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon. Google Chrome 154.0.8037.57, default profile, remote debugging turned on through `chrome://inspect`. `main` at 1fadc40 reads the file the same way.

### Evidence

`active_port_endpoint` reads the file with `tokio::fs::read_to_string` and turns any error other than `NotFound` into this refusal:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/1fadc40b3e40e042590c9f63cf8ef837a6263258/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs#L567-L587

### Workaround and additional context

`cua-driver mcp --direct --grant existing-profile` works, since that runtime runs under the calling host. A Chrome started with `--remote-debugging-port` and its own `--user-data-dir` attaches through the daemon without trouble, because its endpoint is found from the listening socket rather than this file.

Related but different: #3241 (an attach wedging a long-lived daemon) and #3287 (a consent race on Windows).

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: element clicks on a second display take about 9 s each, even with the agent cursor disabled
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Every element `click` on a Calculator window on a second display takes about 9 seconds, including consecutive clicks on neighbouring buttons, and turning the agent cursor off with `set_agent_cursor_enabled` does not change that. Setting `glide_duration_ms` to 150 brings each click down to about 1.4 s.

### Reproduction

1. Put Calculator's window on a second display. Here it is a `CGVirtualDisplay` placed left of and below the main display.
2. Start `cua-driver mcp`, call `get_window_state` for Calculator, then `click` the element tokens for Add, Equals and Add again, timing each call.
3. In a new connection, call `set_agent_cursor_enabled {"enabled": false}`, confirm it with `get_agent_cursor_state`, and repeat step 2.

It happens on every click.

### Expected behavior

With the cursor disabled, a click does not wait for a cursor animation (`animate_cursor_to` says a disabled cursor never animates), and an element click on this window finishes in well under a second.

### Actual behavior

| Connection | Add | Equals | Add |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default cursor | 9.18 s | 9.45 s | 9.02 s |
| `set_agent_cursor_enabled {"enabled": false}` first | 9.25 s | 9.13 s | 9.09 s |

`get_agent_cursor_state` in the second connection reports `"enabled": false` and `"glide_duration_ms": 0.0`. With `set_agent_cursor_motion {"glide_duration_ms": 150}` instead, the same clicks take about 1.4 s. The buttons are pressed every time, and an AXPress sent to the same button directly takes about 0.01 s. I don't know where the wait comes from while the cursor is disabled.

### Environment

`animate_cursor_to` returns early for a disabled cursor:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/1fadc40b3e40e042590c9f63cf8ef837a6263258/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L346-L387

https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/1fadc40b3e40e042590c9f63cf8ef837a6263258/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L598-L604

title: [Bug]: macOS background click briefly deactivates the user's active app (~250 ms) despite delivery: BACKGROUND
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, a window-targeted `click` with `delivery_mode=BACKGROUND` returns `delivery: BACKGROUND` and says the hardware pointer was not moved, but the app the user is working in (Chrome) briefly stops being the active application for roughly 220–250 ms. Keystrokes the user types during that window do not reach their app.

### Reproduction

1. Open TextEdit with exactly one document window, and a Chrome window.
2. Click into Chrome so it is the active app; then do not touch the mouse or keyboard.
3. Run the following (Python SDK, embedded runtime):

```python
import asyncio, cua_driver as c

async def main():
    d = c.CuaDriver.create(None)
    await d.start_session(c.StartSessionInput(session=None, capture_scope=None, cursor_theme=None))
    wins = (await d.list_windows(c.ListWindowsInput(pid=None, on_screen_only=False))).windows
    w = next(w for w in wins if w.app_name == "TextEdit" and w.bounds.height > 100)
    res = await d.click(c.ClickInput(
        target=c.ActionTarget.WINDOW(pid=w.pid, window_id=w.window_id),
        position=c.ClickPosition.COORDINATES(x=w.bounds.width * 0.5, y=w.bounds.height * 0.6),
        delivery_mode=c.InputDeliveryMode.BACKGROUND,
        session=None, button=None, count=None))
    print(res)
    await d.shutdown()

asyncio.run(main())
```

4. While it runs, poll Chrome's `AXFrontmost` attribute (e.g. `AXUIElementCreateApplication(chrome_pid)`) every ~20 ms.

Observed on 2 of 2 background clicks in a fully hands-off, instrumented run.

### Expected behavior

A background click to a TextEdit window leaves the user's active application (Chrome) active throughout, consistent with the result's `delivery: BACKGROUND` and "the hardware pointer was not moved".

### Actual behavior

The click result:

```
effect=UNVERIFIABLE, route=SYNTHETIC_EVENTS, delivery=BACKGROUND, escalation=None, error=None
summary: "✅ Posted click to pid <textedit> (background CGEvent routed to the pid; the hardware pointer was not moved, ...)"
```

During each click, Chrome's `AXFrontmost` went `True → False → True`:

| Click | Chrome inactive at | Chrome active again at | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | 9.661 s | 9.885 s | 224 ms |
| 2nd | 18.472 s | 18.724 s | 252 ms |

Across the same run:

- The top-most layer-0 window in `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` stayed Chrome's the whole time, so no window was visibly raised.
- The hardware pointer did not move during either click.
- No on-screen window owned by the calling process appeared.
- `type_text` (route `ACCESSIBILITY`), `press_key`, `hotkey`, and window-targeted `scroll` in the same run caused no change in Chrome's active state.

I do not know which process became active during the gap. In an earlier, less precise run (the user was also using the machine), `lsappinfo front` once reported TextEdit, the click target, as frontmost during a background click.

The user also observed it directly in earlier runs: Chrome visibly lost focus, and text they were typing into Chrome was lost.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver` 0.30.2 from PyPI, Python SDK, `CuaDriver.create(None)` (execution mode `EMBEDDED`), Python 3.12.9
Operating system and architecture: macOS 15.6 (24G84), Apple M3, built-in Retina display (1512×982 pt @ 2×)
Application/browser/window system/image: target TextEdit 1.20 (single document window); user's active app Google Chrome 153.0.8010.53. Accessibility and Screen Recording granted to the calling process's host app.

### Evidence

Timeline from a monitor thread sampling every ~20 ms for the whole run (times relative to monitor start; steps separated by 1 s pauses):

```
 8.320s >> click
   9.661s [click] chrome_app_frontmost: True -> False
   9.885s [click] chrome_app_frontmost: False -> True
11.900s >> type_text
14.011s >> press_key return
16.162s >> hotkey cmd+a
18.291s >> click again
  18.472s [click again] chrome_app_frontmost: True -> False
  18.724s [click again] chrome_app_frontmost: False -> True
20.744s >> scroll WINDOW
```

### Workaround and additional context

No workaround found. `type_text` into the same window, which routes through `ACCESSIBILITY`, did not cause the flicker. Related but different: #3331 is about the *foreground* route stealing focus. Here the action is reported as background delivery.

Found while evaluating cua-driver as a non-interfering local desktop backend for an agent SDK. An agent clicks every few seconds, so a ~250 ms activation change per click repeatedly interrupts the user.

title: [Bug]: macOS desktop-targeted scroll moves the hardware pointer and reports delivery: NOT_APPLICABLE
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, a desktop-targeted `scroll` moves the user's real hardware pointer to the scroll location and leaves it there. The result reports `route: GLOBAL_INPUT` and `delivery: NOT_APPLICABLE`. `ScrollInput` has no `delivery_mode`, so a caller cannot ask for background-only delivery or a refusal. A desktop-targeted `click` with `delivery_mode=BACKGROUND`, by contrast, is refused explicitly.

### Reproduction

1. Note the current pointer position; do not touch the mouse.
2. Run:

```python
import asyncio, cua_driver as c

async def main():
    d = c.CuaDriver.create(None)
    await d.start_session(c.StartSessionInput(session=None, capture_scope=None, cursor_theme=None))
    res = await d.scroll(c.ScrollInput(
        x=474.0, y=394.6, direction=c.ScrollDirection.DOWN,
        target=c.ActionTarget.DESKTOP(display_id="primary"),
        scope=None, session=None, by=None, amount=3))
    print(res.text, res.action)
    await d.shutdown()

asyncio.run(main())
```

3. Read the hardware pointer position (e.g. `CGEventGetLocation(CGEventCreate(NULL))`).

Observed in 4 of 4 runs.

### Expected behavior

One of the following:

- A desktop scroll does not move the user's hardware pointer.
- If it has to, the result reports it as foreground delivery.
- The caller can request background-only delivery and get an explicit refusal, as a desktop `click` does: `desktop clicks require delivery_mode:"foreground"; background delivery is unavailable for desktop targets`.

### Actual behavior

```
text: "Scrolled desktop down by line × 3 at (237.0, 197.3)."
effect=UNVERIFIABLE, route=GLOBAL_INPUT, delivery=NOT_APPLICABLE, escalation=None, error=None
```

- The hardware pointer jumped to the reported scroll location and stayed there after the call returned.
- A pointer monitor recorded the jump in three runs: `(1139, 973) → (222, 182)` and `(1394, 366) → (222, 182)` in two hands-off runs sampled every 5–20 ms, and `(1273, 559) → (222, 182)` in a third. The reported location in those runs was `(222.5, 182.8)`.
- In a fourth, uninstrumented run, the user saw the pointer move by itself when the desktop scroll ran.

The reported location is half of the coordinates passed: `(474.0, 394.6)` → `(237.0, 197.3)` on a 2× display. That may be intended, if desktop-target scroll coordinates are screenshot pixels, but it differs from the screen-point coordinates `list_windows` bounds use.

In the hands-off runs, a window-targeted `scroll` reported `delivery: BACKGROUND` and did not move the pointer.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver` 0.30.2 from PyPI, Python SDK, `CuaDriver.create(None)` (execution mode `EMBEDDED`), Python 3.12.9
Operating system and architecture: macOS 15.6 (24G84), Apple M3, built-in Retina display (1512×982 pt @ 2×)
Application/browser/window system/image: scroll point over a TextEdit 1.20 window. Accessibility and Screen Recording granted to the calling process's host app.

### Evidence

Pointer-monitor excerpt (hands-off run; times relative to monitor start):

```
23.126s >> scroll DESKTOP
  23.357s [scroll DESKTOP] pointer: (1139,973) -> (222,182)
24.493s >> drag WINDOW
```

No other pointer movement was recorded in that run.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: target the window (`ActionTarget.WINDOW`) instead of the desktop. That route reported background delivery and did not move the pointer.

Found while evaluating cua-driver as a non-interfering local desktop backend for an agent SDK.

title: fix(cua-driver): prevent second-display cursor re-seeding and honor runtime disable (#4276)
body:
## Summary
- Problem this solves:
  - Clicking or interacting with elements on a secondary display—especially monitors arranged at negative virtual-desktop coordinates (`x < 0` or `y < 0`)—took ~9 seconds per action because coordinate-threshold sentinel checks (`pos.0 < -50.0`, `pos.0 < -100.0`, `pos.0 < 0.0 && pos.1 < 0.0`) treated valid negative monitor coordinates as an unplaced cursor on every click, and `seed_position` clamped secondary-display targets back onto the primary display frame.
  - Disabling the agent cursor via `cua cursor --enabled false` (or `CUA_CURSOR_ENABLED=false`) did not take effect synchronously before `animate_cursor_to` / `overlay_glide_to`, did not cancel in-flight glide waiters or active path/spring/click animations, and still allowed full-screen off-window pixmap allocations on macOS while the cursor was outside the primary overlay window.
- What changed:
  - Replaced coordinate-threshold sentinel heuristics with an explicit `placed: bool` state (`is_placed()`) and `is_enabled()` helper on `RenderStateCore`, and updated `seed_position` so targets on secondary displays outside the primary screen frame seed locally on that display without clamping back onto the primary monitor.
  - Applied `SetEnabled`, `SetMotion`, and `SetTheme` synchronously inside `send_command` / `try_send_command_for` across macOS, Windows, and Linux, quiesced active path/spring/click animations, and cancelled pending arrival waiters when `SetEnabled(false)` is received.
  - Skipped full-screen Retina pixmap allocation in the macOS overlay loop when the cursor and focus rectangles do not intersect the main-screen overlay window, and short-circuited empty dirty unions before surface creation on Windows.
<!-- Describe observable behavior. Do not narrate the diff file by file. -->
## Related work
<!-- Use Fixes only when this PR fully resolves the issue. Otherwise use Refs. -->
Fixes #4276
RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): None — bug fix preserving existing CLI, HTTP, and MCP contracts.
## Compatibility and risk
- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - Restores expected click latency on secondary displays (including negative-coordinate display layouts) and ensures `cua cursor --enabled false` / `CUA_CURSOR_ENABLED=false` immediately suppresses cursor glide delays and overlay rendering across macOS, Windows, and Linux (X11/Wayland). No API, CLI, MCP, or permission changes.
- Risk and rollback:
  - Low risk; changes are contained within `cursor-overlay` state management and the platform overlay adapters. Cleanly revertible via a single commit revert if needed.
## Validation
- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p cursor-overlay` (70 passed, including `negative_coordinate_display_cursor_paints_and_runtime_disable_quiesces`)
  - `cargo test --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-windows --lib` (231 passed)
  - `cargo fmt --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check`
  - `python .github/scripts/tests/test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py`
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Verified live on a dual-monitor Windows 11 setup with a secondary display positioned to the left of the primary display at negative coordinates (`X = -1920..0, Y = 0..1080`):
    - With `CUA_CURSOR_ENABLED=false`, consecutive clicks on the secondary display (`(-1300, 420)` and `(-620, 420)`) completed in `37 ms` and `10 ms` (0 ms glide wait) without moving the physical OS cursor on the primary monitor.
    - With `CUA_CURSOR_ENABLED=true`, initial cursor placement on the secondary display completed in `10 ms`, subsequent local glide (`680 px` on the secondary display) completed in `1528 ms` without re-seeding from the primary display, and `glide_duration_ms=150` completed in `169 ms`.

title: perf(cua-driver): add guarded completion to jev-use
body:
## TL;DR

Adds an **opt-in, recipe-local guarded completion** to the browser `jev-use` example.

After the provider chooses the first `type` mutation, `--guarded-completion` can skip exactly one later provider decision **only** when a fresh `semantic_v2` snapshot re-proves the required completion and supplies one unique fresh Submit ref.

Default behavior is unchanged.

Refs #3963.

## Why

The current loop normally pays one provider decision per action:

`observe → decide → type → observe → decide → submit`

Downstream real Driver/MCP/Chromium evidence in `kvnloo/cua#5`, generalized in `kvnloo/cua#24`, showed that the second decision can be deleted for narrow two-step obligations when the completion is independently bound and freshly resolved. `kvnloo/cua#33` then failure-injected may-have-landed mutations and kept the guarded caller from blind replay.

This PR ports only that narrow surviving rule onto current main. It does **not** add a Driver batch API, a generic authorization service, or a Driver-side decision router.

## Safety boundary

The plan stores:

- the named Cua session;
- first/completion candidate IDs;
- logical target role/name;
- the prior ref only as evidence that it is **not** reused.

Before skipping the provider, the next step must:

1. take a fresh semantic snapshot;
2. remain in the same Cua session;
3. observe the field containing the required token;
4. find exactly one `button / Submit` page target;
5. build exactly one page `browser_click` completion candidate; and
6. prove that candidate uses the fresh ref; and
7. refuse if the post-mutation snapshot presents the exact same ref string as the pre-mutation plan.

Any mismatch, ambiguity, missing target, wrong session, changed field, or tampered/old ref falls back to the ordinary provider path.

Driver remains the authority for session-scoped targets/refs and stale-ref refusal.

## Scope

- Python + TypeScript parity.
- New `--guarded-completion` flag.
- Default stays conservative/off.
- JSONL step records add `decision_route = provider | guarded-completion`.
- Browser fixture only; native tasks are unchanged.

## Tests

New Python and TypeScript tests cover:

- fresh-ref success;
- foreign-session refusal;
- ambiguous/missing completion target;
- unverified first postcondition;
- old/tampered ref reuse, including a same-ref post-mutation snapshot;
- unique initial logical-target requirement.

Reconciled base SHA: `4c2403fc557492cbd1e8018a0f2104cdcd6fd838`; exact head: `9ab4878e4933897b33c34ef00e776400a947ee30`.

## Timing integration

The rebase preserves merged #4052 phase telemetry. Guarded steps report `provider_decision_ms = 0` while retaining semantic/visual/candidate-build timing and `total_step_ms`, so the skipped provider call is visible rather than hidden inside aggregate decision time.

## Evidence / claim boundary

Historical downstream A/B showed the provider-decision reduction on a real isolated Driver/MCP/Chromium fixture. That evidence motivates this port but does not substitute for CI/current-head recertification of this exact implementation.

The claim here is intentionally narrow: **one provider decision may be removed from the built-in two-step browser fixture without reusing stale authority.**

## Local exact-head evidence

Independent local execution on runtime head `66c72b1977197dc453260007b77f01f5b0623c4f` produced:

- mock interleaved A/B: 78/78 independently verified fixture outcomes;
- baseline/default: 2 provider decisions;
- guarded: exactly 1 provider decision with `decision_routes = ["provider", "guarded-completion"]`;
- guarded step 2: `provider_decision_ms = 0`;
- 18 traced cells: fresh post-mutation ref used, zero stale-ref reuse;
- mock wall clock: no supported speedup claim (paired median +16.8 ms, CI crosses zero);
- small live TypeSafe A/B: 6/6 pairs faster, paired median about -175 ms; n=6, so this is suggestive rather than a merge gate.

That runtime evidence is historical and remains scoped to its recorded SHA; current-head execution is reported separately below.

The prior CI-unit defect was in `test_verify_setup.py`: `acted_path()` gained `decision_routes`, but one exact-dict expectation had not. Current head updates that assertion and adds exact guarded-route regression coverage.

## 2026-10-08 current-main refresh

The branch was rebuilt directly on upstream `4c2403fc557492cbd1e8018a0f2104cdcd6fd838`; current exact head is `9ab4878e4933897b33c34ef00e776400a947ee30`.

GitHub compare reports 1 commit ahead / 0 behind, with the same 12 guarded-completion files and no scope expansion. Every pre-existing touched file is blob-identical between the previous base and current main, so the refresh required no conflict resolution.

Fresh CI for this exact head is required; the earlier green run remains historical evidence for the previous SHA and is not relabeled as certification of this one.

title: [Bug] App-name window resolution can target the wrong window for input actions (focus_app / capture(app=...))
body:
### Environment
- cua-driver `0.30.4` (x86_64-windows), invoked via Hermes Agent `<redacted version>` (computer_use wrapper) on Windows 11 (build 26200.9457), interactive session 1.

### Bug Description
App-name based window resolution can send input to a **different window than the caller intended**, including a window that holds a user's unsaved document. Since input actions are scoped only by app name (there is no `pid`/`window_id` parameter for input — only `capture` accepts them), a caller that trusts `app=` can type into the wrong document. This is a safety-relevant behaviour gap, not just a naming annoyance.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Two Notepad windows are open. One is a tabbed document set that includes a user's **unsaved** file; the other is a scratch instance the agent created (`Start-Process notepad.exe <scratch file>`).
2. `focus_app(app="Notepad")` returns:
   ```
   Targeted Notepad.exe (pid 54376, window 39587252) without raising window.
   verdict: {"decision":"verify_fresh_state","hint":"Transport succeeded but the effect is unproven..."}
   ```
   pid 54376 is **the user's window**, not the scratch instance. Windows 11 Notepad is tabbed, so a newly opened scratch file can also appear as a tab inside the same window as the user's dirty documents — leaving the caller no safe way to tell them apart by name.
3. Separately: after a failed `set_value` (`code:"timeout_outcome_unknown"`, session marked suspect and recreated), the very next `capture(app="explorer")` resolved to an unrelated **350×154 window with 0 elements** while the intended folder window (`<folder> - 文件资源管理器`) was still present and had captured correctly minutes earlier.

### Expected Behavior
Target resolution should be deterministic, self-evidencing and fail closed:
- every input action's response should echo the resolved `pid`, `window_id` and window title;
- when more than one candidate window matches the `app` value, refuse with a structured code (e.g. `ambiguous_target`) instead of picking one silently;
- document that input actions are only safely scoped by `pid`+`window_id` — and accept those parameters for input actions, not just for `capture`.

### Actual Behavior
A name-based call silently binds to whichever window the resolver picks; the caller only learns the target from `focus_app`'s echo (and, for `capture`, the returned AX tree). In the Notepad case the resolver picked the user's window; in the explorer case it picked an unrelated 350×154 window. An agent that proceeds on `app=` alone would type into the user's unsaved document.

### Impact
Agent input can land in a human's document. That risk scales with the number of same-app windows (tabbed editors, multiple browser windows, Explorer + desktop shell), i.e. it is the common case on a real desktop, not an edge case.

### Suggested Fix
Return the resolved target identity with every input result; refuse ambiguous name resolution with a structured non-retryable code unless a `pid`/`window_id` is supplied; add `pid`/`window_id` to the input-action schema so a caller can pin the exact window it captured.
