title: fix(sandbox): replace a terminal named claim instead of reattaching to it
body:
Closes #4054.

## Problem

`Pool.claim(name=...)` adopts an existing claim with a matching name so an interrupted run can resume. That reattach is correct for a claim still in progress, but a claim that reached a **terminal** Fleet phase can never bind — and it is reattached on every subsequent run, so the failure replays forever and the run never self-heals.

The scheduled `Periodic: Cua Sandbox Live Fleet E2E` monitor hits this on both persistent-pool lanes: it passes a stable pool namespace as the claim name, and the month-old `lastTransitionTime` values in [the linked runs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/35910937174) show the same terminal claim being re-adopted across runs and source SHAs.

## Change

Treat the phases the control plane already considers terminal as non-adoptable. The set mirrors `is_terminal_claim_phase` in [`libs/fleet/sdk/src/claims.rs`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/fleet/sdk/src/claims.rs), so the SDK and the client agree on what "terminal" means instead of the list drifting:

```python
_TERMINAL_CLAIM_PHASES = frozenset({"Failed", "Error", "Expired"})
```

In `Pool.claim()`, a matching existing claim in one of those phases is deleted and a fresh one is created in its place.

## Scope, per the issue's guardrails

- **Only the claim is removed.** The pool, template and namespace are never touched — covered by `assert client.deleted_pools == []` / `deleted_templates == []`.
- **Resumable claims keep the existing reattach contract.** `None`, `Pending`, `Binding`, `Bound` and `Ready` are still adopted, and the pre-existing `test_named_claim_retry_reattaches_without_creating` and `test_named_claim_reattach_failure_does_not_release_existing_claim` continue to pass unchanged.
- **Reattachment is not turned into unconditional deletion.** The replacement is gated on the phase, not on age or on having seen a failure.
- **A cleanup failure still re-claims.** If the delete is rejected the error is logged and the fresh claim is attempted, rather than aborting the call and leaving the caller with no claim at all.

`_claim_phase` reads `claim.status.phase` defensively via `getattr`, returning `None` for claims that carry no status. An unknown phase is therefore treated as resumable, which is the conservative choice.

## Tests

Three new cases in `libs/python/cua-sandbox/tests/test_pool.py`:

- `test_named_claim_replaces_terminal_existing_claim` — parametrized over all three terminal phases; asserts the stale claim is released, a fresh one created, and no pool/template deleted.
- `test_named_claim_still_reattaches_resumable_existing_claim` — parametrized over `None` and four non-terminal phases; asserts nothing is released and nothing is created.
- `test_named_claim_replace_survives_delete_failure` — the first delete raises; the call still re-claims.

Both directions were mutation-checked, per the #4094 test-ownership rules:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `_is_terminal_claim` always `False` (the reported bug) | 4 failed — the 3 terminal-phase params and the delete-failure case |
| `_is_terminal_claim` always `True` (over-broad) | 7 failed — both pre-existing reattach tests plus all 5 resumable params |

## Validation

```
$ python -m pytest tests/test_pool.py -q
73 passed
```

Full package suite, compared against the base commit to separate pre-existing failures (missing optional `oras` / integration-fixture deps) from anything this change introduced:

| | failed | passed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base `c394149` | 56 | 509 |
| this branch | 56 | 518 |

No new failures; the 9 added passes are the new tests. `black`, `isort --profile black` and `ruff` are clean on both files.

I have not run the live scheduled pool lanes locally — they need Fleet credentials and a real warm pool, so the monitor recovery itself remains to be confirmed on the next scheduled run.

title: Embedded Node SDK waitForExit retains native callbacks during long-running sessions
body:
## Observation

I measured growing retained JavaScript heap with `@trycua/cua-driver@0.30.4` when `EmbeddedCuaDriverHost.waitForExit(generation)` stays pending for a long-running embedded session.

Environment: macOS arm64, Node.js 24.21.0, `@ubjs/core@0.31.0-3`, Cua Driver 0.30.4. The workload keeps one isolated Chrome tab open and performs a semantic MCP observation every 500 ms. The application uses the SDK for embedded host startup and shutdown.

## Measurements

The original 7,200-observation run lasted 3,683,665 ms. Host JavaScript heap samples were 59,411,200 bytes at observation 601 and 100,227,704 bytes at observation 7,200.

A heap snapshot around minute 46 contained **50,535 `cb_tsfn_dispatch` closures**. Their shortest strong retaining paths were `(GC roots) → (Global handles) → cb_tsfn_dispatch`.

I ran the same observation workload with process-loss reporting connected to the existing MCP transport close event. Host startup and shutdown use the same SDK. This run has **44 `cb_tsfn_dispatch` closures** at approximately minute 46. JavaScript heap samples during minutes 5–46 range from 53,745,360 to 59,947,896 bytes.

Explicit full-GC measurements:

| Measurement | Pending SDK exit waiter | MCP close-event consumer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained JavaScript heap | 86,688,432 bytes | 52,759,680 bytes |
| Host RSS immediately after GC | 254,033,920 bytes | 140,738,560 bytes |
| Native callback closures in heap snapshot | 50,535 | 44 |

These are local measurements for this workload. The heap snapshots remain local because a process heap may contain environment data.

## Source path

[`EmbeddedCuaDriverHost::wait_for_exit`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/bf6c76786d938070f4ecf1e44004752f69f518b8/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-sdk/src/embedded.rs#L378-L409) sleeps for 50 ms on each pending iteration. The generated JavaScript `uniffiRustCallAsync` re-polls the Rust future on every wakeup.

The native callback count is consistent with the waiter wakeup cadence. I have isolated the application-side trigger and retaining path. The N-API callback release implementation needs upstream investigation.

## Expected behavior

A pending exit subscription should retain a bounded set of native callback resources for the lifetime of the process. A one-shot process-exit notification would also remove the periodic wakeup work.

The event-driven run completed all 7,200 semantic observations in 3,693,993 ms, then completed driver-crash recovery, canceled native typing, pause, resume, lock, and repeated host restart scenarios. Its final sampled JavaScript heap was 55,732,984 bytes. The complete run executed 7,417 tool calls, including deliberate refusal and cancellation cases. Seventeen consecutive shorter native lifecycle runs also passed.

title: macOS embedded Electron: inherited DevTools listener selects the host endpoint during isolated browser preparation
body:
## Reproduction

I reproduced `browser_endpoint_owner_mismatch` with Cua Driver 0.30.4 embedded in Electron 44.4.5 on macOS arm64. Playwright 1.63.0 starts the Electron host with `--remote-debugging-port=0`. The host starts the embedded driver, then calls `browser_prepare` with `profile.mode=isolated_new` and `allow_launch=true`.

The launched Chrome process inherits the host's listening descriptor. `lsof -a -p <chrome-pid> -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -Fn -P` reports two loopback listeners for that process. In one reproduction:

- Port 60638 returned `Browser: Chrome/152.0.7977.130`, the Electron host's Chromium version.
- Port 60703 returned `Browser: Chrome/154.0.8037.58`, the launched Chrome version.
- The isolated profile's `DevToolsActivePort` contained port 60703 and its exact browser WebSocket path.

Both endpoints answered `/json/version`. A standalone Node host completed the same preparation successfully.

## Source path

In `platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs`, `loopback_ports_for_pid` sorts the ports. `discover_owned_endpoint` returns the first endpoint answering `/json/version`. The default `BrowserPlatform::discover_spawned_endpoint` filters that single result against the expected WebSocket URL. Preparation retries that discovery for five seconds and returns the ownership mismatch.

The same discovery code is present at `c3941497a5545b6b977c55962c29391da10bdc03`.

## Local fix and behavior verification

I reused the existing `active_port_endpoint` path at the start of macOS `discover_owned_endpoint`:

```rust
let classification = self.classify_browser(pid).await?;
if let Some(endpoint) = active_port_endpoint(pid, classification.product_kind).await? {
    return Ok(Some(endpoint));
}
```

This path reads the exact profile from process arguments and proves the recorded port through the process's loopback listeners. The existing listener discovery remains the fallback. I also used `-nP` for numeric listener addresses.

The rebuilt universal driver completed an Electron end-to-end journey through streamed model tool calls, deferred MCP discovery, isolated Chrome preparation, native window discovery, browser binding, user pause, owned-process cleanup, user resume, a fresh browser process, and normal run completion. The native browser preparation and binding kept the exact endpoint ownership checks.

A useful upstream regression scenario is an embedded host with its own inherited DevTools listener followed by preparation and observation of a driver-owned isolated browser.

title: [Bug]: Text-only MCP clients cannot address elements: snapshot_id and element_token exist only in structuredContent
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

`get_window_state` returns `snapshot_id` and every `element_token` only in `structuredContent`. Its text content (the header plus the Markdown tree) has neither, and `click` refuses a bare `element_index` with `snapshot_id_required`. An MCP client that only shows the model text content therefore can't do any element-addressed action; only pixel clicks work.

### Reproduction

1. Install cua-driver 0.30.4, grant Accessibility and Screen Recording, and start the daemon (`open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve`).
2. Over `cua-driver mcp` stdio, call `get_window_state` with `{pid, window_id, include_screenshot: false}` for Calculator.
3. Inspect the result: `content[0]` is text (14,400 chars) and contains neither `snapshot_id` nor any `element_token`. `structuredContent.snapshot_id` is `s00000009`, and the Clear button's element is `{"element_index": 2, "element_token": "s00000009:2", ...}`.
4. Call `click` with `{pid, window_id, element_index: 2}`.

I hit this through Google Antigravity CLI 1.2.9 (`agy -p`, Gemini 3.8 Flash), which forwards only text content to the model. The agent found Clear at index 2 in the text tree, and every element click was refused. Reproducible every time.

### Expected behavior

A client that only surfaces text content can still address an element it can see in the tree, for example because the text header carries `snapshot_id` (so `snapshot_id` + `element_index` works) or each element line carries its token. MCP 2025-06-18 also says a tool returning structured content SHOULD return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block for backwards compatibility.

### Actual behavior

- `click` with bare `element_index` + `window_id`: `click: bare element_index is not accepted; pass element_token, or snapshot_id together with element_index` (`snapshot_id_required`).
- The agent then guessed `snapshot_id: "1"` → `click: snapshot_id has invalid format`, and `element_token: "Clear"` → `element_token has invalid format`.
- With no addressing args, `click` says `Provide either (element_index + window_id) or (x + y). pid is always required.` (`platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs:1304` on main), which points clients at the shape that is then refused.
- Pixel clicks after a screenshot snapshot do work: `PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX.` The agent completed 17 × 23 = 391 that way, and a fresh MCP connection read back `17×23` / `391`.

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.30.4 (CuaDriver.app from the canonical installer at main `c3941497a`), macOS 26.5.2 arm64, Calculator.
- Client: Antigravity CLI 1.2.9, model `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, cua-driver registered as a stdio MCP server.
- On main `c3941497a` the text header is `window_id=… pid=… elements=…` in `platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs:497/507`, `platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs:1411` and `platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs:1426`, so this is likely cross-platform. I've only verified it on macOS.

### Evidence

Raw MCP probe (`initialize` → `tools/call get_window_state`) against Calculator:

```text
protocolVersion: 2025-06-18
content[0] type=text len=14400 has_snapshot_id=False has_element_token=False
structuredContent keys: ['_note', 'app_name', 'background_input', 'element_count', 'elements', 'elements_complete', 'nodes_pending', 'nodes_visited', 'pid', 'returned_element_count', 'snapshot_id', 'timeout_ms', 'total_element_count', 'tree_markdown', 'truncated', 'walk_elapsed_ms', 'window_id', 'window_title']
snapshot_id: s00000009
Clear element: {"actions": ["AXPress"], "depth": 2, "element_index": 2, "element_token": "s00000009:2", "enabled": true, "label": "Clear", "role": "AXButton", ...}
```

Text tree the model sees (excerpt):

```text
window_id=<id> pid=<pid> elements=148

- [0] AXWindow "Calculator" [id=main actions=[raise]]
    - [1] AXButton (Delete) [id=Delete ... actions=[press]]
    - [2] AXButton (Clear) [id=Clear actions=[press]]
```

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: click by window-local pixels after `get_window_state` with a screenshot. That loses token addressing for backgrounded, minimized or off-Space windows.

Simplest fix I can see: add `snapshot_id=<id>` to the shared text header on every platform. Happy to send a PR if that direction works for you.

Related: #4220 (Gemini schema compatibility, closed), #3613 (element_token capability undeclared in `tools/list`).

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): expose snapshot identity in full window-state text
body:
Refs #4346

## Current scope

title: perf(cua-driver): acknowledge witnessed intermediate effects in native jev-use
body:
## Problem and behavior

Native jev-use runners used the whole-task oracle after every action. A valid intermediate counter increment or Large radio selection therefore consumed the entire wait even when independent harness state already showed the action's effect.

The Python and TypeScript examples bind optional intermediate-effect predicates to the built-in counter and choose-size task factories. Counter must advance an integer by exactly +1 from pre-dispatch state; Large must read `size: large`. Whole-task `verified` or `refuted` wins. A supported effect that never arrives returns `intermediate_timeout`, stopping before a dependent mutation. Save-note, custom tasks, terminal actions, empty step lists, and exhausted budgets retain conservative polling.

No Driver tool schema, snapshot resolver, daemon, fixture schema, or permission change. Jev and task policy stay above Driver. Refs #4336; no issue-closing claim.

## 2026-10-18 refresh

Exact head: `f998e1aa993a32011379f72b83ef3ee248748e3d`. Additively merged upstream `b286bea824eef1a3a1c154ab140223a7b97e0048`, preserving the current full-output snapshot compatibility reads in both runners. No rewritten published history. The only change after the executed checks was a dated proof-note update; executable sources were unchanged.

Locked dependencies, offline/mock only:

- Python 3.12 unittest discovery: 255 ran, 1 skipped, passed.
- TypeScript: 123 passed; `npm run typecheck` passed.

- `verify_decision_cli.py --model mock`: default and `--fixture native` passed.
- `verify_native_waits.py --baseline-sha b286bea824eef1a3a1c154ab140223a7b97e0048`: 9 cells, 18 verified terminal outcomes; virtual policy waits 25.5s baseline versus 9.3s candidate. The unchanged main poller and original immutable baseline have identical AST hashes.
- Negative cases exercise missing/delayed effects, boolean/fractional/non-finite counters, terminal precedence, foreign-PID/schema failures, cancellation, and no second mutation after timeout.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The virtual timings are simulated wait-policy timings, not a new live or model benchmark. No provider calls, GUI fixtures, or changes to the shared Mac runtime were made for this refresh.

title: feat(jev-use): detect bounded no-progress loops in native decision runs
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

### Primary area

MCP or agent integration (`jev-use` recipe only)

### User problem

The native `jev-use` decision loop already keeps bounded action history, exposes task `progress`, supports `reobserve` / `abstain`, and recovers from stale element tokens.

However, the runner currently has no explicit way to detect when a trajectory has stopped making progress.

A task can therefore spend most or all of its step budget repeatedly:

- selecting `reobserve` without any subsequent task progress;
- retrying an action after stale/refused executions without eventually advancing the declared task steps;
- selecting the same non-performing action across multiple observations.

In these cases the loop usually stops only when `max_steps` is exhausted, even though the recent history already contains enough information to identify a bounded no-progress pattern.

### Current behavior

The native runner is bounded by `task.max_steps` and records compact history entries for previous decisions.

For example, a trajectory may look like:

```text
step 1: reobserve
step 2: reobserve
step 3: reobserve
step 4: reobserve
...
max_steps reached
```

or:

```text
action
-> stale_element_token
-> reobserve
-> action
-> stale_element_token
-> reobserve
...
```

A single stale action followed by a successful retry is normal recovery and should not be treated as failure. The missing case is repeated recovery or observation steps with no measurable task progress.

### Proposed behavior

Add a small, recipe-local no-progress guard for native `jev-use` runs.

The guard would inspect only information the runner already owns, such as:

- bounded decision/action history;
- whether an action was actually performed;
- `reobserve` selections;
- stale/refused action outcomes;
- declared task progress from `NativeTask.progress(...)`.

When a bounded repeated pattern shows that the run is no longer advancing, the runner should stop safely using the existing non-success outcome rather than consume the rest of the task budget.

Possible initial patterns:

1. repeated `reobserve` decisions without task progress;
2. repeated non-performing/recovery actions without task progress;
3. several consecutive steps where declared task progress remains unchanged.

The threshold should remain small and deterministic. A successful action or an increase in declared task progress should reset the no-progress counter.

### Scope

This proposal is intentionally limited to the `jev-use` example layer.

In scope:

- `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use/python/...`
- `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use/typescript/...`
- deterministic Python/TypeScript parity tests
- structured logging of the no-progress stop reason

Out of scope:

- no Cua Driver behavior change;
- no new MCP/SDK/CLI contract;
- no provider or model change;
- no planner implementation;
- no automatic model routing;
- no change to permission or authorization behavior.

This should remain compatible with the existing `reobserve`, `abstain`, stale-token recovery, and task-progress behavior.

It could also compose with the separate structured abstain/handoff work in #4014 without depending on it.

### Validation

I would propose deterministic coverage for at least:

1. repeated `reobserve` with unchanged progress stops as no-progress;
2. `stale -> reobserve -> successful action` does **not** stop early;
3. repeated stale/non-performing recovery eventually stops;
4. any increase in declared task progress resets the no-progress state;
5. existing successful native tasks preserve their current behavior.

Python and TypeScript implementations should produce equivalent decisions for the same synthetic history.

If this scope fits the intended `jev-use` boundary, I can prepare a focused implementation and parity tests.

### Desired outcome

The native `jev-use` runner should detect bounded no-progress patterns before the full `max_steps` budget is exhausted.

For example, the runner should stop safely when it repeatedly selects `reobserve`, repeatedly encounters non-performing recovery actions, or completes several consecutive steps without any change in the task's declared progress.

A successful action or an increase in declared task progress should reset the no-progress state, so normal recovery patterns such as `stale_element_token -> reobserve -> successful action` continue to work unchanged.

The behavior should remain local to the `jev-use` recipe, preserve the existing `abstain` / `reobserve` semantics, and expose a structured stop reason in the run log so callers can distinguish no-progress termination from ordinary budget exhaustion.

### Current workaround

Today the runner relies on the existing `max_steps` budget to bound these cases.

Repeated `reobserve`, stale-token recovery, or other non-progressing decisions continue until the task eventually succeeds, explicitly abstains, or exhausts the step budget. Callers can inspect the trajectory logs afterward, but there is no built-in mechanism that identifies a stuck trajectory and terminates it early.

### Affected components and platforms

Primary scope:

libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use/python/

libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use/typescript/

native jev-use decision runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux

Relevant integrations:

TypeSafe Jev decision model

Cua-S1 decision service

native accessibility candidate path introduced by #4268

The proposed behavior should remain recipe-local. It should not require changes to the Cua Driver public API, MCP/SDK/CLI contracts, permissions, or provider protocols.

The existing browser jev-use path should remain unchanged unless the same internal helper can be reused without changing its current behavior.

### Alternatives and prior art

Related work already addresses several adjacent failure modes, but not bounded no-progress detection itself:

#4268 introduced native accessibility candidates, bounded task steps, reobserve / abstain, and the native jev-use decision loop.

#4255 fixed a browser-path failure where Jev repeatedly selected reobserve because it lacked a compact representation of the filled form state. It improved the observation and history presented to the model, but does not provide a general mechanism for detecting repeated no-progress trajectories.

#4324 added value-free task progress to native requests so Jev and Cua-S1 do not need to infer ordered task progress from history. This gives the runner a useful progress signal, but the runner does not currently use that signal to terminate a trajectory that repeatedly fails to advance.

#4014 proposes a structured handoff payload when jev-use abstains, allowing a caller-owned planner to resume with bounded context. That work begins after an abstain decision; it does not determine when a repeatedly non-progressing trajectory should stop and abstain.

Relying only on max_steps remains a valid safety bound, but it cannot distinguish a healthy long task from a trajectory that has already repeated the same recovery or observation pattern without progress.

### Implementation ideas

One possible implementation is a small recipe-local no-progress guard that evaluates the bounded history already maintained by the native runner.

It could conservatively detect patterns such as:

consecutive reobserve decisions with unchanged declared task progress;

repeated stale/refused/non-performing recovery attempts with no later successful progress;

several consecutive steps where NativeTask.progress(...) remains unchanged.

Any successful task-progress change should reset the no-progress state. A normal recovery sequence such as:

stale_element_token -> reobserve -> successful action

must therefore continue normally.

If a configured bounded threshold is reached, the runner could terminate through its existing non-success/abstain path and add a structured log reason such as no_progress plus a more specific pattern identifier.

I would keep this implementation entirely inside the jev-use recipe and maintain Python/TypeScript parity with deterministic tests. No new Driver, MCP, provider, or planner contract should be necessary.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: [Bug]: KWin Wayland window screenshots fail with surface_identity_unproven
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On KDE/KWin Wayland, Cua Driver can read an application's accessibility tree and capture the desktop, but individual window screenshots fail with `surface_identity_unproven`. KWin has a native window capture interface, but the existing capture dispatch does not use it.

### Reproduction

1. Run Cua Driver 0.30.4 in a KDE/KWin Wayland session with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`, without the optional Cua KWin target helper.
2. Open a normal application window and call `list_windows`.
3. In the same driver connection, call `get_window_state` with the returned `pid` and `window_id` and request a screenshot.
4. Compare with desktop capture in that session.

### Expected behavior

When the compositor provides permitted, exact-window capture, return pixels from the requested window. If exact identity or capture permission cannot be established, report an explicit refusal rather than an unrelated desktop crop.

### Actual behavior

Individual captures fail before the actual capture request:

```text
surface_identity_unproven: Wayland capture cannot prove pixels belong to window <window_id>: no compositor-attested window geometry is available
```

No authorization prompt appeared on those attempts. Accessibility inspection and desktop capture succeeded.

### Environment

- Cua Driver: 0.30.4
- OS: NixOS, x86_64 Linux
- Desktop/window system: KDE Plasma, KWin 6.7.4, Wayland
- Qt: 6.11.2
- Display scale: 2
- Applications: multiple ordinary desktop windows; titles and private content omitted
- Optional Cua KWin target helper: not loaded

### Evidence

- All seven enumerated window entries returned the same single-window capture refusal. Some entries had zero-sized accessibility bounds; ordinary nonzero-sized windows failed as well.
- Desktop capture succeeded at 3200 × 2000.
- D-Bus introspection of `org.kde.KWin.ScreenShot2` reported version 5 and `CaptureWindow` (`sa{sv}h → a{sv}`).
- Existing Wayland capture requires compositor-attested identity/geometry; accessibility bounds alone do not supply that proof.

### Workaround and additional context

Spectacle can capture an active window. Desktop capture is also available, but does not provide the requested exact-window contract.

Related: #3336 provides optional trusted KWin identity metadata; #4034 addresses desktop recording rather than exact-window screenshots. Implementation: #4378, including installation requirements, exact-identity tests, and outstanding platform evidence. This is an unselected contribution pending maintainer review.

### Native-ID input follow-up

After enabling UUID-based capture, a control without a usable AT-SPI click action could fall through to X11 injection using a native driver-local window ID, producing `GetWindowAttributes` errors. Foreground input also did not recognize these IDs in its helper-only path.

The linked PR's follow-up corrects the pointer fallback routing and validates the live native PID/window pair. Acceptance evidence is an extended isolated KWin fixture covering native capture, foreground typing/keys/pixel-click refusals and both delivery modes of semantic-click pointer fallback. It does not enable KWin raw input: the existing helper is read-only, and activation followed by focus-bound portal/libei events is not a target-bound transaction. A new compositor-side input API requires a separate scope and permission decision.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): capture KWin windows and keep native input off X11
body:
## Summary

- **Problem this solves:** KDE/KWin Wayland window screenshots fail with `surface_identity_unproven` despite working desktop capture and accessibility inspection. The generic crop path has no compositor-attested geometry for these windows.
- **What changed:** use Plasma window-management UUIDs and KWin's `getWindowInfo` to enumerate exact window identities, then call `ScreenShot2.CaptureWindow` and validate its returned `windowId`. Screenshots include decorations, exclude shadows/cursors, and use logical resolution. Raw Qt image data is decoded with bounded dimensions, row-stride handling, and premultiplied-alpha conversion.
- Native capture does not require the optional Cua KWin effect. When native enumeration is unavailable, existing discovery fallbacks remain; native capture errors do not fall back to an unrelated desktop crop.
- The Nix package installs a desktop entry declaring the existing KWin window-management and screenshot interfaces. KWin's normal permission checks remain enabled.
- A follow-up fixes native Wayland element-click fallback routing, validates native KWin IDs on foreground requests, and reports the existing target-bound-input limitation. Raw KWin input remains unsupported; details and new regression evidence are below.

**Validation status:** the complete canonical desktop matrix is outstanding, and this contribution awaits maintainer selection/scope confirmation. Focused test evidence does not certify readiness.

## Related work

Refs #4377 (reproduction and proposed acceptance scope).

Related: #3336 (optional trusted KWin identity helper), #4034 (KDE desktop recording), and #3200 (fail-closed Wayland window capture). This PR addresses exact-window screenshots rather than recording or target-bound raw input.

**RFC:** CLI/MCP request fields and the existing exact-window capture contract are preserved. This is intended as a platform implementation of that contract, using KWin's existing installation-based permission mechanism. Please confirm whether the native capability/desktop-entry declarations require a separate RFC; this draft does not claim an accepted permission-design decision.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: permitted KWin native windows receive stable driver-lifetime IDs, compositor geometry/visibility, and exact-window PNGs. IDs are not persisted across daemon lifetimes. Window titles alone are never used to select a capture target.
- Installation: source binaries alone do not acquire KWin's restricted capabilities. The Nix package contains the executable-matching desktop entry; other installation paths must provide equivalent host-approved metadata. No permission checks are disabled.
- The screenshot interface must return `windowId` identity metadata. Implementations without that evidence are refused. Native verification used KWin 6.7.4, not an asserted all-KWin-version compatibility range.
- Shared screenshot schemas and macOS/Windows adapters are not changed. The existing bounded Wayland dispatch loop is reused through a generic state parameter; the KWin helper's process checks also recognize Nix-wrapped KWin executables.
- KWin raw keyboard/pointer targeting is not enabled by this change. Unsupported native capture, stale windows, wrong owners/UUIDs, malformed image layouts and timeouts remain errors.
- Rollback: revert this change and rebuild; no installed/shared driver service was replaced during validation.

## Validation

Candidate: **`0ec6bae105a0971b6551f8a8763855b3c4e63b94`**. The validation source tree became this candidate; the later author/committer-email amendment changed commit metadata only (`git diff 696714fd0 0ec6bae10` is empty). The evidence below is focused validation, not full desktop certification.

### Focused tests and checks

Run from `libs/cua-driver/rust` with the Linux development dependencies:

```sh
env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY \
  cargo test -p platform-linux --features portal-input,portal-capture --locked -- --test-threads=1
env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY \
  cargo test -p cua-driver --features portal-input,portal-capture --locked
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

- `platform-linux`: **582 unit tests and 8 KWin helper contract tests passed**; desktop-bound ignored tests were not run by this hermetic command.
- `cua-driver`: the complete non-ignored test run passed, including **285 main-binary unit tests** and the integration test binaries; ignored desktop tests remain outstanding.
- The new pure tests cover stable ID mapping, Qt property type validation, supported pixel formats, padding/alpha conversion, and exact errors for invalid layouts.
- `python3 -m pytest .github/scripts/tests/test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py -q`: **10 passed**. The focused native test is explicitly listed in the manual E2E allowlist.
- `git diff --check`, workspace formatting, and `nix-instantiate --parse nix/cua-driver/package.nix`: passed. The full canonical Nix package/check build has not been run.

### Manual or platform evidence

The checked-in `kwin_native_capture_test` drove a separately packaged candidate via MCP in **isolated KWin 6.7.4 Wayland sessions at scales 1 and 2**, with an independent D-Bus, virtual output, software OpenGL, normal restricted-interface checks, and no Cua KWin helper. Both runs passed.

The fixture creates red/blue fullscreen siblings with the **same PID and title**. Screenshot center-pixel oracles proved that each UUID returned its own color, including the covered sibling. The test also checks repeat capture, logical image dimensions, wrong PID refusal, closed-window refusal, stable identity after resize, resized dimensions, and minimized visibility.

Reproduce with an installed candidate whose desktop entry matches its executable, in a disposable native KWin session with Python GTK3/PyGObject:

```sh
CUA_TEST_DRIVER_BIN=/path/to/installed/cua-driver \
CUA_TEST_REQUIRE_DRIVER_BIN=1 \
CUA_E2E_UNRESTRICTED_GUI=1 \
cargo test -p cua-driver-e2e --test kwin_native_capture_test --locked -- \
  --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

See `libs/cua-driver/docs/kwin-window-capture.md` for installation and test prerequisites. The fixture opens two fullscreen windows; use a disposable desktop. Repeat at both output scales.

### Known gaps or CI still required

- Complete canonical Linux X11/compositor-specific Wayland, Windows, and macOS desktop matrix on the exact ready candidate, per the test harness/CI guides.
- GitHub's contributor-attribution check and release reminder passed. Ordinary `pull_request` workflows—including `CI: Release metadata`, Linux/macOS/Windows units, formatting and Nix source checks—currently report `action_required`, awaiting maintainer approval for this fork contribution. They have not certified this candidate.
- Native GNOME/Sway/Hyprland regression evidence for the shared dispatch-loop reuse; source preservation is not native certification.
- Native KWin versions other than 6.7.4, other packaging/installers, fractional scale, mixed-scale/multiple outputs, off-workspace capture, permission revocation, compositor restart, and resize/close racing an in-flight capture.
- Existing real-user applications on the active desktop were used to reproduce the failure; candidate acceptance used isolated fixture windows, not screenshots of private applications.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [ ] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above. **Maintainer confirmation requested as described above.**
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change (`fix(cua-driver)`, patch release).
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included. No other submitted contribution was transplanted; commit author/committer are ShellWen (`me@shellwen.com`), resolved by GitHub to `ShellWen`, with a verified GPG signature. Implementation was agent-assisted.
- [x] Release impact is declared: this is a user-visible fix; the non-releasing `no-release` condition does not apply.
## Follow-up: native input routing and the foreground refusal

This follow-up fixes the native-ID/X11 fallback regression exposed while using
the capture adapter. It **does not enable KWin raw input**.

- AT-SPI element clicks retain genuine semantic actions. When those actions are
  unavailable, a native Wayland target now uses the Wayland input adapter rather
  than passing its driver-local window ID to `XGetWindowAttributes`/XSendEvent.
- Background raw pointer fallback returns `background_unavailable`. Foreground
  fallback uses the existing compositor-bound transaction and screen coordinates
  from the observed element, without an X11 coordinate translation.
- Native KWin foreground requests revalidate the current PID/window identity and
  return the existing, specific refusal for missing **target-bound KWin input**.
  Previously these IDs were unknown to the helper-only foreground route.
- The native fixture exposes a GTK slider without an actionable click, so the
  public MCP regression exercises both background and foreground element pointer
  fallback, plus foreground typing, keys and pixel clicks. Capture checks remain
  in the same owner test.
- The installation guide explains why UUID activation plus focus readback is not
  sufficient: portal/libei delivers to the focused surface at event processing
  time. The existing KWin helper is deliberately read-only. A compositor-side
  target-bound input API requires a separate design/permission decision; no new
  helper methods, permissions or global-input bypass are introduced here.

### Follow-up validation

Candidate: **da3b558cd7ef5de7c85585700d0a99e3018393a3**. Validation used the candidate source tree; the commit
adds no later executable changes.

- Linux platform: 582 unit tests and 8 KWin helper contract tests passed.
- Driver: 285 main-binary unit tests and the remaining non-ignored integration
  suites passed with the one baseline failing startup test explicitly filtered.
- E2E inventory: 10 passed. Workspace formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- The extended native KWin 6.7.4 fixture passed at output scales 1 and 2 with an
  installed candidate, independent session bus, explicit private AT-SPI launcher
  and registry, and no Cua KWin helper. Its accessibility address was checked to
  be inside the disposable runtime directory before the apps started.
- `serve_binds_while_reachable_atspi_initialization_is_stalled` failed in the
  unfiltered driver run because the driver never connected to the fake session
  bus. A same-environment process probe against both the original installed
  `0ec6bae` package and the follow-up binary reproduced `accepted=false` with the
  daemon socket ready in both cases. This is an outstanding baseline/environment
  discrepancy, not a passing full driver suite claim.

The complete canonical desktop matrix and other compositor-native regression
evidence remain outstanding. The shared fallback branch also affects native
Wayland compositors other than KWin; X11, macOS and Windows dispatch are not
changed by this follow-up. KWin raw input remains unsupported after this commit.


## Copilot review follow-up

Candidate: **50cbe60b422c7f024f2e7e5c7d432884e6d3a22f**. The tested source tree
became this commit with no subsequent executable changes.

- UUID enumeration accepts advertised Plasma window-management v13+, binding
  `min(advertised, 17)`. Hermetic Unix-socket protocol fixtures exercise v12
  rejection, every v13–v16 legacy path, v17 and a v20 advertisement capped at v17.
  This does not assert older KWin screenshot compatibility: identity metadata
  from `ScreenShot2` is still required independently.
- Stacking is obtained from `stacking_order_uuid_changed` below v17 and an
  explicit `get_stacking_order` object on v17+. The snapshot waits for complete
  stacking evidence and maps UUID order to `z_index`; UUID sorting is not used
  as a front-to-back heuristic.
- On-screen metadata now includes Activity membership. Empty/absent membership
  means unrestricted; current membership is visible and inactive membership is
  hidden. Restricted windows with unknown current Activity are not advertised
  as on-screen. `NameHasOwner` avoids starting an absent Activity Manager.
- The native E2E exposed a related consumer bug: PID-only `get_window_state`
  still enumerated X11 windows. It now reuses the existing Wayland PID fallback
  resolver, so the compositor stacking result governs native window selection.

### Validation

- Platform Linux: **584 unit tests and 8 helper contract tests passed**. The two
  new owner tests cover actual Wayland wire negotiation/stacking and Activity
  metadata including disabled/all/current/inactive/unknown/malformed cases.
- The extended installed-candidate KWin 6.7.4 regression passed at **1× and 2×**.
  It verifies two same-PID/same-title windows, numeric stacking order, a stacking
  change after presenting the covered sibling, stable IDs, and PID-only capture
  choosing the new topmost window. Existing capture and raw-input-refusal checks
  remain in the same test. Both runs used private session and AT-SPI buses.
- Driver tests passed serially with the previously documented failing
  `serve_binds_while_reachable_atspi_initialization_is_stalled` test explicitly
  filtered. An initial concurrent run failed
  `updater::tests::ownership_requires_successful_query_with_literal_path`; the
  serial rerun retained that test and passed.
- E2E inventory: **10 passed**; formatting and diff checks passed.

Live multi-Activity desktop validation, native older-KWin capture certification,
and the complete canonical desktop matrix remain outstanding. KWin raw input
remains unsupported. These changes address all three Copilot review comments;
they do not declare full desktop certification.

title: [Feature]: Let text-only models use Cua Driver without receiving screenshots
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### User problem

Text-only models can't keep a Cua Driver session alive, because `get_window_state` returns a screenshot by default.

I hit this with iFlytek's Spark-X2.5 (served through the Astron Token Plan's Anthropic-compatible endpoint) in Claude Code 2.1.284 against Cua Driver 0.30.4 on Windows 11. The endpoint rejects any request that carries an image. That includes a screenshot inside a `tool_result`:

| Request to `/anthropic/v1/messages`, model `spark-x2.5` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| text only | 200 |
| `tool_result` with a text block | 200 |
| `tool_result` with a text block and an 8×8 PNG | 400 `invalid request` (code 10005) |
| user message with the same PNG | 400 `invalid request` |

In a Calculator task the model found the window, cleared it, and entered 12 + 30 through `element_token` clicks. Its verification `get_window_state` call came back with a screenshot, and the next request failed with `API Error: 400 invalid request`. The image stays in the conversation history, so the session can't recover. The model can do the whole task from the accessibility tree; the one screenshot is what breaks it.

A model can pass `include_screenshot: false` on every call, but it only takes one call without it to end the session.

### Desired outcome

A client driving a text-only model can use Cua Driver without an image block ever reaching the model.

### Current workaround

None in the product today. `set_config` only exposes `max_image_dimension`, `experimental_pip`, and `experimental_pip_geometry`, so screenshots can't be turned off for a whole session.

### Affected components and platforms

Cua Driver MCP, all platforms. Any harness whose model has no image input: Spark-X2.5, and other text-only models that sit behind Anthropic- or OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

### Alternatives and prior art

- RFC #2969 Tier 2 proposes negotiating image support at MCP `initialize`. The maintainer decision on 2026-09-29 deferred it to its own amendment. This report is a concrete case for that amendment: a production endpoint that refuses images outright.
- RFC #2969 Tier 1 item 6 (flipping the `include_screenshot` default to `false`) would also cover `get_window_state`, but not `screenshot` or `zoom`.
- #4346 / #4347 put `snapshot_id` into the text content. In my runs Claude Code serialized `structuredContent` as text, so the model already had `element_token`. Harnesses that forward only `content` still need #4347.

### Implementation ideas

A contract-free stopgap is in the MCP schema filter that the local-model guide already ships (`docs/public/examples/local-models/cua-mcp-filter.py`). Docs PR #4380 adds `--text-only` to it. With that flag the filter:

- requests `get_window_state` with `include_screenshot: false`;
- replaces remaining image content with a one-line note;
- copies `snapshot_id` into the text when the text lacks it.

With the filter, the same Claude Code + Spark-X2.5 setup completed 12 + 30 and 17 × 23 in Calculator and confirmed the results from fresh window state, with 0 image blocks sent. The longer-term fix is still the RFC #2969 Tier 2 negotiation.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve KWin activity visibility and stacking metadata
body:
Native KWin discovery reported windows from inactive Plasma Activities as on-screen and omitted compositor stacking ranks. That could let a covered same-PID window win topmost selection.

Retain ShellWen's native UUID-based capture implementation, filter visibility by current Activity membership, and obtain compositor stacking order. Add metadata regression tests and a native fixture stacking assertion. Document the existing Plasma window-management protocol >=17 requirement; versions 13–16 remain unsupported by this native adapter. Capture permission checks and decoding are unchanged.

title: fix(cua-driver): qualify desktop snapshots and signed cursor placement
body:
Desktop coordinates on monitors left of or above the origin were treated as an unplaced cursor, and Hyprland desktop calls could mix monitor snapshots. This draft preserves the contributed multi-monitor capture implementation, uses explicit cursor placement, shares a qualified monitor snapshot within input operations, rebases window metadata, and refuses unqualified layouts.

Salvaged from #4305. Based on #4217 (CARLOSDAVID33's original source PR). Both original commits remain intact: CARLOSDAVID33's 1a777f893a5b32ca7437cb20808a00653b61e8e3 (from #4217) and Iann29's 3c04d301ed7f4173c17b83df3814426c6f011e87. The separate repair adapts [CARLOSDAVID33's public follow-up design](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4305#issuecomment-5898459156) with a verified Co-authored-by trailer. Offered follow-up commit SHAs were unavailable; those commits were not inspected or cherry-picked.

Validation of tree a71a59cdcaf9f1636764d3ee3fa6fdf4dc55f8b8:

- Linux worker, isolated target: `cargo test -j 2 -p cursor-overlay -p platform-linux --locked --lib`: 71 overlay and 589 Linux tests passed, 9 ignored. Both negative-coordinate and dimensions-only snapshot mutations were caught. Formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- Mac Studio, isolated target: `cargo test -p cursor-overlay -p platform-macos --locked`: 71 overlay, 370 macOS unit and 2 integration tests passed; 4 unit tests and 1 doctest ignored, GUI binary skipped. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p cursor-overlay -p platform-macos --all-targets --locked` passed (warnings remain).

Still blocked from readiness:

- P1: an old capture_id remains admissible after same-sized DPMS/output-origin changes because capture publication/admission bind dimensions and PrimaryDesktop, not complete geometry identity. Per-action snapshots do not solve this earlier-capture gap.
- No native Hyprland input/capture, DPMS, scale, mirror or overlay run; canonical exact-head native and foreground/identity suites remain required.
- Windows compilation and GUI validation are unavailable. macOS GUI validation was not run; this Mac lacks the required existing OS permissions.
- Published references for the contributor's offered follow-up commits remain needed for byte-level reconciliation. Observation before/after capture is not an atomic compositor snapshot.

Draft only; no merge or CI approval requested.

title: feat(cua-driver): attach to a logged-in Brave profile
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Existing-profile attachment refused Brave with "approved existing-profile setup is not implemented for Brave", even though Brave is Chromium and shows the same per-instance remote debugging toggle as Chrome on its inspect page. Isolated launch (`browser_prepare` without a `pid`) could not start Brave either.
- Scope: this PR now has two parts. (1) Existing-profile attachment for Brave. (2) Isolated launch for Brave, which adds Brave to the binaries the driver will start with DevTools enabled, after Chrome and Edge. Part 2 widens the trust boundary, so I'm happy to split it into its own PR if maintainers prefer.
- What changed:
  - **Brave's default user-data directory** is now known on macOS (`~/Library/Application Support/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser`) and Linux (`~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser`). Without it the driver never found Brave's `DevToolsActivePort`, so it could not prove the PID-owned endpoint. Windows already had Brave's directory.
  - **A Brave setup descriptor** for `brave://inspect/#remote-debugging`. The page title ("Inspect with Chrome Developer Tools"; "Inspect with Brave Developer Tools" is also accepted), heading ("Remote debugging") and checkbox label ("Allow remote debugging for this browser instance") are Chrome's. Tab close labels "Close" and "Close tab" are both accepted.
  - **Brave uses Edge's trusted-click fallback** on macOS for the checkbox when AXPress does not toggle it (previously Edge-only; now a small `uses_trusted_checkbox_fallback` predicate).
  - **Isolated launch for Brave** (87f77ba), only from a vendor-attested install a standard user cannot modify:
    - macOS: `/Applications/Brave Browser.app`, identifier `com.brave.Browser`, Team ID `KL8N8XSYF4`.
    - Windows: `%ProgramFiles%\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\Application\brave.exe`, Authenticode subject `CN="Brave Software, Inc.", O="Brave Software, Inc."`. Brave's default installer installs per user, which is refused.
    - Linux: `/opt/brave.com/brave/brave` (the binary, not the `brave-browser` wrapper script, which forks), root-owned, from Brave's own package. Snap and Flatpak are not covered.
  - **Setup UI waits on macOS go from 2 s to 8 s** (`SETUP_UI_UPDATE_TIMEOUT`) for the new tab, the omnibox suggestion and the checkbox rollback. Brave with ~42 tabs open took ~2.8 s to expose its new tab in the AX tree, so the first live attempt failed with "Brave did not expose exactly one newly created tab". Each wait polls and returns as soon as the change appears, so only slow browsers wait longer. The new bound stays within the overall 12 s `EXISTING_PROFILE_SETUP_READY_TIMEOUT`.

## Related work

Refs #3252 (same shape of change for Helium: teach existing-profile attachment a new Chromium product).

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Not required. This adds a recognized product to the existing, already-gated existing-profile flow. No API, permission or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: `browser_prepare` existing-profile attachment now works for Brave on macOS, Windows and Linux X11. `browser_prepare` isolated launch can now start Brave from the installs listed above; this widens the set of binaries the driver launches with DevTools enabled. The permission model is unchanged: standard mode still needs `--grant existing-profile` or an embedding authorization host. The longer setup waits on macOS only matter when a browser is slow to update its accessibility tree.
- Risk and rollback: Low. Other products' behavior is unchanged apart from the longer setup waits on macOS. Revert the Brave commits to roll back; isolated launch (87f77ba) can be reverted on its own.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (on this branch, based on `main` at 9545a3d1):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos`: core 769 passed; platform-macos 385 passed, 4 ignored; integration tests all pass.
  - New and updated tests: `setup_is_limited_to_products_with_exact_descriptors` (now expects Brave), `default_user_data_dir_covers_existing_profile_products`, `trusted_checkbox_fallback_is_limited_to_edge_and_brave`, `setup_ui_steps_allow_slow_browsers_within_the_overall_setup_budget`.
  - `cargo build --locked -p cua-driver --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin`
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Brave 149.1.91.168 (`com.brave.Browser`): its inspect page in `resources.pak` has `<title>Inspect with Chrome Developer Tools</title>`, the heading "Remote debugging" and the checkbox "Allow remote debugging for this browser instance", the same as Chrome. Brave's `locale.pak` contains "Address and search bar", the omnibox name the macOS setup UI matches.
  - Live test on macOS 26.3 with the same two changes applied to 0.28.2 (Brave 149, ~42 tabs, logged-in default profile, daemon in standard mode with `--grant existing-profile`): `browser_prepare` returned `attached_existing_profile` through `DevToolsActivePort`, with the endpoint owned by Brave's pid. It enabled remote debugging and closed the temporary setup tab. `get_browser_state` listed the tabs, and `browser_navigate` to https://example.com loaded "Example Domain". An earlier attempt with the 2 s waits failed with "Brave did not expose exactly one newly created tab".
- Windows and Linux X11, live in CI: fork run [37025900333](https://github.com/DragonQLF/cua/actions/runs/37025900333). It ran this PR's head plus test-only printing, with Brave 154.1.96.60 installed from Brave's own channels. `standalone_browser_existing_profile`, `standalone_browser_existing_profile_setup` (`browser_prepare` → `attached_existing_profile`, side effects posted in the review thread), `standalone_browser_existing_profile_standard_refusal` and `standalone_browser_prepare_isolated` all passed on both. On Windows, the isolated-launch run used Brave's signed `Application` folder placed under Program Files, because Brave's installer only installs per user.
- Known gaps: no lane in this repo's CI exercises Brave. The evidence above comes from a fork-only workflow. The macOS live test ran on the 0.28.2-based build.

This change was prepared with Claude Code (agent-assisted); the diff, tests and live check above are what was run.

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve controls during screenshot-only previews
body:
Screenshot-only `get_window_state` currently replaces the window's accessibility payload with an empty snapshot. A continuously refreshing viewer can therefore invalidate the element tokens between an agent's observation and action, even when the application has not changed. This proposes preserving the current same-session semantic snapshot during capture-only publication.

The existing `SnapshotStore` owns the change: preview publication refreshes screenshot scale, clears obsolete zoom coordinates and refreshes its LRU entry without replacing the payload or tokens. A real accessibility read, including an empty result, still replaces the snapshot. Cold reads, different owners/windows and ended sessions retain their existing refusal and replacement behavior. macOS, Linux and Windows call sites share the same policy; no additional cache, mutex, public request option or action retry is introduced.

Refs #4376. This is an unselected draft contribution for review of the preview contract; it is not ready for merge or release.

Validation on exact commit `544dbac2f30cc02cbd755a03774c4420fd5c9259`, based on `9545a3d17b44b587b593d59090dc140740876a6e`:

- From `libs/cua-driver/rust`: `cargo +1.97.1 test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos` passes 1,184 tests. Four host-dependent Mac tests and two illustrative doctests remain ignored; the GUI-only integration binary reports skipped.
- Four new common-store regressions cover repeated previews and coordinates/zoom, different owners/windows and cold reads, ended sessions, and native payload disposal outside the store lock. Disabling preservation makes the keeper regression fail; the exact candidate was then restored and the full batch passed.
- `cargo +1.97.1 fmt --all --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Linux ARM64, same exact source and Rust 1.97.1 in an isolated Debian container: 773 core and 575 platform unit tests pass; nine host-dependent tests remain ignored. All seven real Xvfb click/key integration tests pass. The real X11 screenshot exclusion test passes: the resting overlay is visible before/after capture and absent from the captured pixels. No host desktop, credentials or private data were mounted.
- Further Linux ARM64/X11 acceptance on the same frozen source: nine focused real GTK tests pass (seven GTK3 cases, GTK4 target selection after a foreign application, and a live-preview keeper). Five decoded screenshot-only PNGs preserve the original semantic handle; its click produces exactly one increment, and a new accessibility read then rejects that old handle with `stale_element_token` while the counter remains one. The keeper also replaces an already-filled field exactly, including Unicode. All nine initial clips and the amended keeper clip decode with nonzero frames. All 1,244 archived tracked files match the source Git blobs; the preview/replacement experiment is a separate test-only target. Disposable Xvfb desktops have no host display, home or credential mounts. This does not certify the full GTK/Wayland matrix or OpenGeni Linux integration.
- Windows x64, same exact source and Rust 1.97.1 on an interactive GitHub Windows runner (session 2): all driver/core/SDK/testkit/cursor/UIA targets compile. 761 core, two recording-shutdown, 231 platform and 82 full SDK unit tests pass; one platform test remains ignored. ABI and remote-authorization subsets also pass and are already included in the SDK count. [Fork validation run](https://github.com/jorgensandhaug/cua/actions/runs/36780568912) uses a separate workflow-only validation branch and checks out the frozen source; this contribution's head is unchanged.
- Five real WPF GUI cases also pass on exact 544dbac in Windows session 2: UIA tree, structured lookup, exact stale-token rejection, layered-popup PNG decoding/non-black pixels (378×178), and foreground typing into the intended field with the pre-focused decoy still empty. [WPF experiment](https://github.com/jorgensandhaug/cua/actions/runs/36785828429) retains result rows, trajectories and fixture screenshots. This is narrow native GUI evidence, not the full canonical matrix or OpenGeni adapter acceptance.
- A separate Windows WPF experiment now verifies the proposed preview behavior using the exact candidate and unchanged upstream. After five decoded screenshot-only PNG captures, the original semantic handle delivers a background click on the candidate; the fixture's independent counter reaches exactly one. A subsequent accessibility read rejects that old handle with `stale_element_token`, leaving the counter at one. The [candidate job](https://github.com/jorgensandhaug/cua/actions/runs/36787879690/job/110133539412) passes. Unchanged upstream fails precisely at that original-handle click and the counter remains zero; the [baseline reproduction](https://github.com/jorgensandhaug/cua/actions/runs/36789433253) confirms the expected refusal. Both use the same test-only overlay hash `1023BCC92D6D1F061790A160397FEFE8ED21ADF8B20CF04F0CA17F01B0E4D4FC`; tracked driver/library source remains frozen. The first baseline wrapper incorrectly propagated its expected native failure as a workflow failure; the corrected baseline-only reporter validates that exact refusal before exiting successfully. This does not certify global focus/cursor noninterference or the full desktop matrix.
- OpenGeni controller experiment on exact downstream e789c63712ec3f5554c5fa865cf98143e26f2cef now verifies this repaired native candidate through its real ComputerDriver, ComputerSupervisor and SQLite operation receipts. In native Linux ARM64 (no CPU emulation), exact Unicode replacement succeeds, a replayed semantic click leaves the independent native counter one, and a field edit succeeds while PNG preview streaming continues. The final 480×617 PNG was visually inspected and agrees with native readback. A genuine accessibility refresh still refuses the old handle and retains text/counter. Generated0.31bindings pair with the rebuilt candidate library and released generic Node FFI wrapper; one explicit library resolver and test-only downstream permission/role projection are recorded. No click-request translation or action retry. All677native Rust and6866effective downstream tracked files match their frozen revisions; all ten SDK source files match except that resolver. A bounded public GTK fixture only; no host desktop, credentials or private data mounted; owned container removed. This is focused controller-boundary proof, not production Linux enabling, packaged Mac GUI acceptance or released SDK adoption.
- Strict Clippy remains blocked: candidate and unchanged upstream both produce the same 59 diagnostic headings. No unrelated suppressions were added.

The exact-candidate canonical desktop E2E matrix remains required before readiness. Linux now has focused X11/GTK input, capture and live-preview acceptance; the full GTK matrix, Wayland and production OpenGeni Linux integration remain unverified; the focused controller experiment above is accepted. Windows has five accepted WPF cases and a direct preview-contract comparison, while the full WPF/WinUI/WebView2/capture matrix, signed release and OpenGeni's Windows adapter remain unverified. An earlier release-based Mac experiment reproduced the original viewer failure, but that is not certification of this current-main implementation.

title: feat(jev-use): add browser provider parity and backend receipts
body:
## TL;DR

Bring the browser `jev-use` runners onto the same bounded provider choices already available around the native path, without waiting on the separate OpenJev backend PR.

Browser runners now accept:
- `mock`
- `live` / `typesafe`
- `s1`

Decision-bearing JSONL records also include a content-free `backend` field naming the backend that actually handled the request.

## Boundary

This stays caller-side. Driver still owns fresh state, refs, action validity, execution, and verification. The browser runner still owns candidate construction and action arguments; providers receive only the existing validated closed-choice request.

Browser tasks intentionally keep `cua.jev_choice_request_v1`, matching the current jev-use README / skill / RFC 4268 contract. Native tasks remain the v2 path.

No OpenJev dependency is included here. If #3961 lands, OpenJev can be added as a tiny follow-up provider option.

## Failure behavior

Provider failures produce a bounded `unknown` decision outcome before action dispatch. Backend receipts contain only the backend name and error class; action arguments, secrets, refs, and screenshot bytes are not added to the provider request.

## Tests

Python and TypeScript coverage verifies:
- bounded request shape and no action arguments / secret token;
- existing mock behavior remains unchanged;
- S1 receives the validated browser request and reports `backend=s1`;
- `live` and `typesafe` both report the actual backend as `typesafe`.

Exact head: `7a1f90fbc212ccf1976fa74095f7b6456116b2a0` on current main `9545a3d17b44b587b593d59090dc140740876a6e`.

Refs #3961, RFC #4268.

title: build(deps): bump transformers from 5.5.4 to 5.10.1 in /libs/cua-bench-rl
body:
Bumps [transformers](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers) from 5.5.4 to 5.10.1.
Release notes

Sourced from transformers's releases.

Release v5.10.1

v5.10.0 was yanked as we publish on a corrupted branch. Sorry everyone, this happens when we rush a release!!!

New Model additions

Gemma4 unified+ Gemma4 MTP

Gemma 4 12B Unified is an encoder-free multimodal model with pretrained and instruction-tuned variants. Unlike standard Gemma 4, which uses dedicated encoder towers, Gemma 4 12B Unified projects raw inputs directly into the language model's embedding space through lightweight linear pipelines. This results in a simpler architecture while maintaining strong multimodal performance.

Key differences from standard Gemma 4:

  • No Vision Tower: Raw pixel patches are projected directly into LM space via a Dense + LayerNorm pipeline with factorized 2D positional embeddings, replacing the vision encoder.
  • No Audio Tower: Raw 16 kHz waveform samples are chunked into fixed-length frames and projected through a simple RMSNorm → Linear pipeline, replacing the mel spectrogram + Conformer encoder.
  • Shared Multimodal Pipeline: Both vision and audio use the same Gemma4UnifiedMultimodalEmbedder (RMSNorm → Linear) for the final projection to text hidden space.

You can find the original Gemma 4 12B Unified checkpoints under the Gemma 4 release.

  • who needs encoders? (#46385) by @​douglas-reid @​sgerrard @​vasqu @​molbap

Sapiens2

Sapiens2 is a family of high-resolution vision transformers pretrained on ~1 billion curated human images, designed for human-centric computer vision tasks including pose estimation, body-part segmentation, surface normal estimation, and pointmap estimation. The models scale from 0.4B to 5B parameters and train at native 1K resolution, with hierarchical 4K variants for extended spatial reasoning. Sapiens2 achieves substantial improvements over its predecessor with +4 mAP in pose estimation, +24.3 mIoU in body-part segmentation, and 45.6% error reduction in normal estimation.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Add Sapiens2 Model (#45919) by @​guarin in #45919

DeepSeek-OCR-2

DeepSeek-OCR-2 is an OCR-specialized vision-language model built on a distinctive architecture that combines a SAM ViT-B vision encoder with a Qwen2 hybrid attention encoder, connected through an MLP projector to a DeepSeek-V2 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model. The model features a hybrid attention mechanism that applies bidirectional attention over image tokens and causal attention over query tokens, enabling efficient and accurate document understanding. It supports both plain OCR tasks and grounding capabilities with coordinate-aware output for document conversion to markdown format.

Links: Documentation

  • Add Deepseek-OCR-2 model (#45075) by @​thisisiron in #45075

Mellum

Mellum is a code-focused Mixture-of-Experts language model developed by JetBrains. It is derived from the Qwen3-MoE architecture with per-layer-type RoPE and interleaved sliding window attention. The model has 12B total parameters with 2.5B active parameters per token, using 64 routed experts with 8 activated per token across 28 layers.

Links: Documentation

  • feat: Add support for JetBrains' Mellum v2 code generation model (#46112) by @​shadeMe in #46112

Breaking changes

The Gemma4 vision pooler now casts inputs to float32 before scaling to prevent float16 overflow (inf saturation) with large checkpoints, which may cause minor numerical differences in outputs for users running Gemma-4 vision models in float16.

  • 🚨 Fix float16 overflow in Gemma4 vision pooler (#46277) by @​Bluear7878

Audio Language Models (ALMs) now have a dedicated base model class without a language modeling head, aligning them with the design of Vision Language Models (VLMs); users relying on the previous model class structure should update their code to use the new base model class where appropriate.

  • 🚨 [ALM] Add base model without head (#45534) by @​eustlb

title: macOS: existing_profile setup always refuses on Chrome 154 — duplicated "New Tab" AXButtons
body:
## Summary

On macOS with Chrome 154, `browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile` always refuses when the remote-debugging setting is off:

```
browser_wrong_target_refused: multiple exact AXButton controls matched "New Tab"
```

`unique_actionable(nodes, "AXButton", "New Tab", "AXPress")` in `platform-macos/src/browser/setup_ui.rs` requires a single match. Chrome 154 exposes the tab strip several times in one window's AX tree. In a normal window, `get_window_state(query: "tab")` returned four distinct `AXButton "New tab"` elements (indices 615, 660, 719, 764), all with the identical frame `{x:1628, y:35, w:28, h:41}`. Each tab-strip `AXRadioButton` and the "Tab search" `AXPopUpButton` are repeated the same way.

## Environment

- cua-driver 0.31.0, macOS (MacBook Air), Google Chrome 154.0.8037.59
- `serve --grant existing-profile`
- It reproduced on two different windows.

## Workaround

Manually open `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` in a new window and tick "Allow remote debugging for this browser instance". After that, `browser_prepare` reports no side effects and binding is `exact` with `mutation_allowed: true`.

## Suggestion

Elements with identical role, label and frame inside one window most likely all represent one control. Collapsing those duplicates before the uniqueness check would keep genuine ambiguity refused while allowing this case.

title: fix(cua-driver): run own-process window operations on the AppKit thread
body:
## Why

`set_window_frame` still refuses windows in the driver's own process (#4348), because AppKit window writes have to run on the main thread. This PR runs those writes on AppKit's main queue instead of refusing them. It also stops SDK cancellation from returning while started native window work can still write.

Follow-on to #4348, inspired by Irfanwani's original containment fix. Salvaged from #4348; Irfanwani is credited in commit history.

## What changed

- `set_window_frame` resolves the exact AX window, checks WindowServer ownership, and runs every AX write through `ax::main_thread::run_ax_mutation` (`platform-macos/src/tools/ax_window.rs`). The own-process refusal is gone.
- `run_ax_mutation` (main's helper from #6559) now waits for work that has already started instead of reporting a timeout while that work can still write. It also catches a panic before it reaches libdispatch.
- `cua_driver_core::native_operation::NativeOperation` replaces the ABI's private cancellation flag. Native work claims its start with `begin()`, so a cancel that wins stops every later native write and reports `Cancelled`, even when the worker's result is ready at the same moment. A cancel that loses waits for the real outcome. `bring_to_front`, foreground `invoke_menu` and `set_window_frame` claim their start on their blocking workers.

## Scope

Covers own-process `set_window_frame`, the main-queue start race, and ABI cancellation ownership for those three tools. Other tools never call `begin()`, so their cancellation behaves as before. Background `invoke_menu` paths keep main's `PressAdmission`. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

Merged current main (1257 commits). Main had meanwhile landed its own main-queue raise (#6559), so this PR now uses main's `bring_to_front` and `invoke_menu` and drops its duplicate dispatch helper. It keeps only the cancellation gates on their blocking workers.

## Blast Radius

macOS only: embedded-SDK hosts that move or raise their own windows, and every caller of `run_ax_mutation` (own-window raises in `ax::bindings` and `invoke_menu`). Calls to other processes still run inline, as before.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks on this head (macOS arm64):
- `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, SPDX headers, lockfiles, image refs).
- `cargo check --all-targets` on `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver-sdk` and `platform-macos` was clean.
- Focused `cargo test` passed: `platform-macos` main_thread, ax_window, set_window_frame, bring_to_front and invoke_menu, `cua-driver-core` native_operation, and all of `cua-driver-sdk`. The new `accepted_cancellation_wins_over_a_result_ready_at_the_same_time` passes and fails when the post-join cancellation check is removed.

Not run on this head: the native product-window harness in `libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/README.md` (it needs a disposable signed worker), the embedded-SDK native run, the representative desktop matrix, Windows and Linux.

Fixes #4323
CUA-3279
risk: deep

title: ci: easy-win speedups
body:
Cheap CI speedups that keep behaviour the same. Every test still runs somewhere that guards the code it covers. "Before" is the median over the last 48 h of `pull_request` runs (about 5,400 runs, from the Actions API). "After" is this PR's own runs. Both sides compiled cold: the Rust caches almost never survive (see the cache note).

| Workflow / job | Before | After (this PR) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CI: Image API** (72 runs / 48 h) | 16.9 min (≈15 min of it a cold `cargo build --release -p cua-sdk`) | **2.0 min** | No Rust build. Narrower paths would have skipped 28 of the 72 runs. Branch pushes no longer run it twice (push and pull_request). |
| **CI: Test Python**, cua-sandbox job (110 runs / 48 h) | 25.5 min (build step 20.8) | **15.3 / 17.9 min** (build step 10.6 cold). 840 passed, the same suite | Debug `cua-sdk`, one profile with the fixture |
| CI: cua SDK, python smoke (ubuntu) | 32.2 min | **19.1 / 24.8 min** | Debug, one profile |
| CI: cua SDK, python smoke (macos-26) | 55.1 min | **46.4 / 50.5 min** | Debug, one profile |
| CI: cua SDK, node smoke (ubuntu) | 29.1 min | **14.5 / 17.9 min** | Debug, one profile |
| CI: cua SDK, node smoke (macos-26) | 45.4 min (hits its 45 min timeout) | **24.8 / 38.0 min** |
| CI: cua SDK, python smoke (windows-latest) | 48.6 min | **20.3 min** (green; before this, main failed it on the `geteuid` build break fixed in #4462) | Debug, one profile |
| CI: Cua Spaces (Tauri bundles: Windows ~90 min, macOS ~70 min), openkoalabot Tauri and samples, infinite-canvas | ran on any `libs/cua/**` change | skip binding-only changes | 10 runs of each in 48 h would not have triggered |
| 34 PR workflows without `concurrency` (Test Python, docs links, containers, ...) | superseded runs kept running | cancelled on a new push | About 1,585 runner-minutes in 48 h were spent after supersession (Test Python alone: 823) |
| CI: Check Docs Links, Check External Links (lychee) | flaky: 503s from github.com on this repo's own blob links | 24 s, green | Links to this repo are checked with git; a missing path still fails |

### Commits
1. **Required-check collision fix.** CI: Image API's job was named `validate`, the same name as the required `validate` check (the release-metadata gate). On every PR it triggered on, the slow job became required. It is renamed to `image-api`, and `cd-py-fleet`'s `validate` is renamed to `validate-wheels`. The intended required jobs (`validate` in ci-release-metadata, `contributor-attribution`, `fleet-mirror-guard`) keep their exact names.
2. **Image API.**
   - No Rust build. Only `test_image.py` needed the native library. It checks the native resolver, which embeds `libs/images/sandbox-images.json`, so a published PyPI wheel would drift from main between releases. The 0.2.0 wheel is already 88 files behind.
   - CI: Test Python already runs `test_image.py` against a source build, on a superset of these paths. The workflow contract test now asserts that.
   - `libs/cua/python/**` is dropped from the paths, since no Image API input lives there.
   - The push trigger now runs on main only.
3. **Path filters.** The Tauri and Swift sample lanes and Cua Spaces exclude `libs/cua/{python,kotlin}` (and `swift` for the Tauri builds). None of their builds read those directories. I checked `include_str!`/`build.rs`, `tsconfig`, `vite.config` and the scripts.
4. **Concurrency.** PR runs are grouped by PR number with `cancel-in-progress`. Every other event gets its own group (the run id), so push, schedule and dispatch runs are never queued or cancelled. The required-check workflows are untouched.
5. **Debug builds.** The debug library is staged or copied straight after `cargo build -p cua-sdk`. The CLIs and the fixture depend on cua-sdk with other features, and cargo rewrites `target/debug`'s cua-sdk cdylib for each feature set; Windows caught this as a missing `clone_devices` symbol. The hermetic suites build `cua-sdk` in debug next to the debug fixtures and CLIs, so dependencies compile once. `stage-uniffi-library.mjs` gains `--profile` (default `release`, so other callers are unchanged). Swift smoke keeps release because its XCFramework step builds release libraries anyway.
6. **Rust cache: only main writes.** This applies to workflows that also run on main or on a schedule (cua SDK, cua-spacesd, cua proto, the image CLI builds), matching what the Rust unit and contract-client workflows already do. The repository cache holds about 13 GB against a 10 GB cap, and its oldest entry was minutes old. Per-PR copies, which only that PR can read, were evicting the main caches every PR restores. Workflows that run only on PRs keep saving.
7. **Docs links.** `github.com/trycua/cua/{blob,tree}/<ref>/<path>` links are checked with git: the checkout for `main`, and a blob-less depth-1 fetch plus `ls-tree` for pinned commits. lychee skips those links and retries the rest with backoff. A real missing path still fails.

### Notes
- The cache gain (6) and the PR-#4455 main-run fix show up only after merge, once main runs save warm caches. The cheapest large win left is raising the repository's Actions cache limit above 10 GB (Settings, Actions, Caches; billable). Today almost every heavy Rust job compiles cold.
- YAML is validated with `actionlint -shellcheck= -pyflakes=`, as CI runs it. The `.github/scripts/tests` suite passes (619 passed).
- `no-release` label: the only product-file edits are a CI helper script option and a workflow contract test.
