title: fix: never auto-delete a Space or VM we didn't create
body:
## Why

A user's local macOS Space (`local:space-012688a553`) disappeared from `~/.lume`. The investigation traced that delete to the Cua Spaces app's own Delete action: logs show a `space_delete` event, then a click in the app and the VM stopping in the same second. It was not an automatic sweep.

An audit of every path that deletes a VM or a Space still found automatic cleanups that could delete a VM or Space their caller never created. This PR closes those. It also fixes `cua sb ls`, which kept reporting the deleted Space as `ready`.

Making cleanups refuse what they didn't create would leave crashed runs' VMs behind for good. So leftovers are now reaped by **ownership record**, never by name, prefix or glob.

## What changes

### Ownership records and the reaper (scripts, CI)

**New tool: `libs/images/common/tools/cua-vm-owner`** (Python 3 standard library only).
- It keeps a ledger at `~/.cua/vm-owners/<nonce>.json` of the VMs our image builds, CI jobs and golden builds create.
- Each record ties the VM to:
  - its bundle's on-disk identity (inode + birth time);
  - its kind and run;
  - the owning process: pid, the pid's start time and the host;
  - a random nonce.

**Commands**
- **`reap`** never lists Lume's VMs. It walks the ledger and deletes a VM only when all three hold:
  - the record matches the bundle on disk;
  - the owner is gone;
  - the VM is older than the grace period (2 h).

  It logs every deletion and every skip with the reason. `--dry-run` deletes nothing.
- **`reclaim VM`** takes back one leftover of ours whose run has ended.
- **`adopt VM`** hands a VM to the user, so it is never reaped.

**The owner** is `CUA_VM_OWNER_PID`, else the nearest `cua` (a `cua images release`) or `Runner.Worker` ancestor process.

**Rules**
- A VM that was deleted and made again under the same name doesn't match its old record.
- A run on another host is never judged gone.

**Where it is wired in**
- **`libs/images/macos/build.sh`:**
  - At start, it reaps `image-build` leftovers.
  - It records the VM right after the clone or pull.
  - An existing name is reclaimed only if it is ours and its run is gone; otherwise it is refused.
  - The cleanup forgets the record after deleting.
  - `--name` must start with `cua-e2e-` or `cua-ci-`.
- **`tiers.sh`:**
  - It owns its tier VMs (`CUA_VM_OWNER_PID=$$`).
  - `--prefix` is validated.
  - An existing VM is reclaimed or refused.
- **`release-tier.sh`:** a rerun reclaims the earlier VM by record. It no longer runs `lume delete` on whatever has the name.
- **`.github/actions/cua-sandbox`:**
  - It reaps `ci` leftovers before creating.
  - It records local Lume VMs it creates (removed with `cua sb rm`).
  - It refuses a sandbox that already exists and forgets the record after deleting.
  - Names must start with `cua-ci-` or `cua-e2e-`.
- **`cd-image-macos.yml`:**
  - Runner hygiene is `cua-vm-owner reap --kind image-build --kind ci --grace 2h`. It replaces the `cua-ci-*` sweep, which also hit other jobs' VMs.
  - The end-of-job step reclaims this run's VMs by record.
- **`build-macos-golden.sh`:**
  - The golden VM is recorded as kind `golden`, which is never reaped by default.
  - A rebuild replaces only a golden this script recorded.

### SDK and daemon (`libs/cua`)

**`cua-vmm` `OwnedVms`**
- Records now carry the bundle identity, creator, pid and a nonce.
- `verify()` reports whether a record still matches the VM: `Matches`, `NameOnly` (legacy record), `Replaced` or `NotOwned`.
- The cache scan (GC and orphan reaper) never collects a VM re-made under a recorded name. It drops the stale record instead.

**`cua-sandbox-core` `Sandboxes::create`:** a local create given a name already in use starts that VM. When readiness then fails, the VM is no longer deleted.

**`cua-spaces`**
- **Handshake failure:** a failed cua-spacesd handshake deletes the sandbox only if this create made it (`fresh`).
- **Cancel:** cancelling a create that started an existing Space keeps that Space listed.
- **Abandoned creates:** one whose process died is deleted only after `ABANDONED_CREATE_GRACE` (24 h). Until then its journal (the ownership record) stays for a later pass. A Space that finished creating has no journal and is never considered.
- **Dry run:** `gc_interrupted_creates(budget, grace, dry_run)` adds a dry run.

**`cua sb gc [--dry-run]`** (new) runs the orphan reaper and the abandoned-create pass. It reports every deletion and every skip.

**`cua-daemon` `Runtime::list`:** when another process (such as the Spaces app) deleted a named local sandbox's state file and instance, the daemon's cached handle is now forgotten. The sandbox is no longer listed as `ready`.

## Tests

**`cua-vm-owner`** (`libs/images/common/tools/tests/test_cua_vm_owner.py`, fake `lume`):
- a crashed build's VM is reaped by the next build;
- a VM without a record is never touched, even with a `cua-e2e-` or `cua-ci-` name, nor is a `space-<hex>` VM;
- a VM re-made under a recorded name is not ours;
- a running build's VM is not reaped or reclaimed by a concurrent build;
- an abandoned VM is reaped only after the grace period, and only by a reaper of its kind;
- an adopted VM is never reaped.

**`cua-spaces`** (`tests/cancel.rs`):
- `an_abandoned_create_is_reaped_only_after_the_grace_period` covers: kept under 24 h, deleted after, a finished Space untouched, and the dry run changing nothing.
- `a_failed_create_never_deletes_an_existing_space_of_that_name` fails without the fix (mutation-checked).

**`cua-vmm` and `cua-disk`:**
- `verify_ties_a_record_to_its_bundle`;
- `a_vm_re_made_under_a_recorded_name_is_never_collected`.

**`cua-daemon`:** `ls_drops_a_handle_whose_sandbox_was_deleted_elsewhere` fails without the fix (mutation-checked).

**Suites and checks**
- These pass: `cargo test` for `cua-spaces` (cancel, providers), `cua-daemon`, `cua-sandbox-core`, `cua-vmm`, `cua-disk`, `cua-telemetry`, and `cua-cli --lib`. The CLI telemetry vocabulary was regenerated for `sandbox.gc`.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` is clean on the touched crates.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `bash -n` and shellcheck pass.
- `cua sb gc --dry-run` was smoke-tested against a throwaway `CUA_HOME`.

## Rollout notes
- **VMs made before this change have no record and are never reaped automatically.** That includes self-hosted runners' existing `cua-ci-*` and `cua-e2e-*` VMs and an existing `cua-spaces-golden`. Delete them once by hand, or the golden build will refuse to replace its unrecorded golden.
- **Kept VMs:** a VM kept on purpose after its run ends (`--keep`) is reaped 2 h after its owner exits. Use `cua-vm-owner adopt VM` to keep it.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- **Lume races:** `lume pull --force`, and Lume's final move and failed-create cleanup, have time-of-check races on the same name.
- **Host-provided creates:** these accept a name from the remote caller. Reject names that are already in use.

title: feat(spacesd): opt-in answering of macOS security prompts in VMs
body:
## What

A safety net for macOS Space VMs: read SecurityAgent's accessibility tree and answer keychain dialogs ("wants to use the 'login' keychain", "wants to use your confidential information stored in 'Chrome Safe Storage'") with the guest password, the way a person at the keyboard would. Admin "wants to make changes" panels are a separate class that must be named explicitly.

**Status: superseded for Chrome teleport by #4470** (no prompt is raised at all). This stays as an opt-in fallback for any other prompt source; it is a draft so the security questions below can be decided first.

## How

- New crate `cua-spacesd-prompts`: walks the AX tree of `SecurityAgent`, only the live (`AXMain`) window (SecurityAgent keeps finished requests' windows in its tree), classifies the dialog, sets the secure field's `AXValue` and `AXPress`es the button. Raw `AXUIElement` FFI; cua-driver is not involved (it refuses these windows: their `AXWindow` does not report the CGWindowID `list_windows` shows).
- Classes: `keychain_unlock`, `keychain_access` (press Always Allow, else Allow), `authorization` (opt-in class), `keychain_broken` (Reset To Defaults / Create New Keychain: reported, never pressed), `unknown` (reported, never touched).
- Guard: refuses unless `hw.model` is an Apple Virtual Machine. Password only from `CUA_SPACESD_PROMPT_PASSWORD`, `CUA_GUEST_PASSWORD`, `CUA_SUDO_PW`, or `lume` for the account named `lume`. Never logged. A refused password is reported as `rejected` and retried at most twice.
- Watcher in `cua-spacesd serve`: **off by default**; `CUA_SPACESD_PROMPT_WATCHER=1` turns it on, `CUA_SPACESD_PROMPT_CLASSES=keychain,authorization` widens it. 150 ms poll, 250 ms settle before answering. Every answer is logged (what asked, what was pressed).
- On demand: `cua-spacesd prompts scan|unblock [--class keychain|authorization] [--dry-run] [--wait N]` prints a JSON report; agents reach it through `space_bash` (documented in the `cua-spaces` skill).
- `permission-approver.py` comment corrected: SecurityAgent is not unreachable through AX.

## Verified

macOS 26.5.2 Lume Space (published `macos:26`), as `lume`:
- locked keychain dialog, item-access dialog (same text as the Chrome one), osascript admin panel: each answered; the secret/`root` came back to the caller
- wrong password: `rejected`; stale windows ignored; `--wait`, `--dry-run`, default class skipping the admin panel
- 10 unit tests (classification against the strings measured above, guard, secret redaction); clippy `-D warnings`

Honest limit: on the current published image the login keychain does **not** take `lume` (the keychain-repair problem). With the watcher on, a Chrome Safe Storage prompt against that keychain was answered with `lume`, refused, and left on screen (`rejected`). The answerer only helps where the keychain takes the provisioned password (e.g. after the sanitize-guest repair). I stopped the mock-teleport GIF run once #4470 landed.

## Open security-review questions

1. Is typing the guest password into system dialogs acceptable at all behind a flag, given the guard is `hw.model` + an env/default password? A malicious guest workload can raise a prompt and have it approved; is "disposable VM" enough?
2. Should the `lume` default exist, or require an explicit password source?
3. Should `Always Allow` be the choice for item-access prompts (persistent ACL grant) or plain `Allow`?
4. Admin authorization class: keep it at all? Today it needs `--class authorization` / `CUA_SPACESD_PROMPT_CLASSES`.
5. Exposure: this is a CLI + opt-in watcher only. A first-class Spaces/driver tool would need a driver authorization classification and contract/SDK parity (large); worth it?
6. Should the watcher also ship disabled-but-present in release images, or stay out of them until needed?

title: browser_type with a trailing "\n" reports it typed every character, but Enter never reaches the page
body:
**Primary area:** Cua Driver ### Summary `browser_type` with text ending in `"\n"` (the usual way to type and submit) returns a normal result, `typed N char(s)` with `delivered_count: N`, but the page never gets a working Enter: - `mode: "insert_text"` (the default): the whole string goes through `Input.insertText`. A single-line `` drops the newline and no key event fires. On TodoMVC no todo is added and "Buy milk" stays in the box. - `mode: "keystrokes"`: the newline becomes a key press, but the `keyDown` carries only `key: "Enter"`, with no `code` and no `windowsVirtualKeyCode`. Pages that check `event.key` work. Pages that check `event.keyCode === 13` (still common in chat and search boxes) see `keyCode 0` and do nothing. In both cases `isError` is false and nothing in the result says Enter did not happen, so the agent moves on as if the form was submitted. ### Reproduction Bind a tab (I used `browser_prepare` with `allow_launch: true, profile: {mode: "isolated_new"}`, then `get_browser_state` with `pid`/`window_id`), then: 1. `browser_navigate` to TodoMVC's React example (https://todomvc.com/examples/react/dist/; I served the same build locally). 2. `get_browser_state` with `snapshot_format: "semantic_v2"`; take the ref of textbox "New Todo Input". 3. `browser_type` with `text: "Buy milk\n"`, once with `mode: "insert_text"` and once with `mode: "keystrokes"` (reload the page in between). 4. Read the page after 1.5 s: the todo list and the box's value. For the keyCode case, the same steps on this page with `text: "hello\n"` and `mode: "keystrokes"`: ```html
    ``` Each combination was run 5 times, each on a fresh page load. Results were the same every time. ### Expected behavior A trailing newline on a single-line field types the text and then presses a real Enter (`key` and `code` "Enter", `windowsVirtualKeyCode` 13), in both modes. If Enter cannot be sent, the result says so instead of counting the newline as delivered. ### Actual behavior | Page | mode | Tool result (5 of 5) | Page after 1.5 s (5 of 5) | |---|---|---|---| | TodoMVC | insert_text | `typed 9 char(s)`, `delivered_count: 9` | todos `[]`, box holds `"Buy milk"` | | TodoMVC | keystrokes | `typed 9 char(s)`, `delivered_count: 9` | todos `["Buy milk"]`, box empty (works) | | keyCode 13 box | insert_text | `typed 6 char(s)`, `delivered_count: 6` | nothing sent, box holds `"hello"`, no keydown fired | | keyCode 13 box | keystrokes | `typed 6 char(s)`, `delivered_count: 6` | nothing sent, box holds `"hello"` | The full result was the same shape in every failing run: ```json {"isError": false, "text": "typed 9 char(s) into tab-…", "structuredContent": {"delivery": {"delivered_count": 9, "mode": "background"}, "effect": "unverifiable", "route": "trusted_input", "summary": "typed 9 char(s) into tab-…"}} ``` The page logged the last keydown in keystrokes mode as `{key: "Enter", code: "", keyCode: 0, which: 0}`. I believe these are the causes (989cc76c, `cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs`): insert_text sends the full text, newline included, in one `Input.insertText` (line 1834). keystrokes maps `'\n'` to `key: "Enter"` (line 2001) but dispatches `{"type": "keyDown", "key": key}` with no `code` or `windowsVirtualKeyCode` (line 2009). The result counts every requested character as delivered (line 2061 onward). ### Environment - cua-driver 0.32.0, trycua/cua main `989cc76c` (Oct 2, 2026) - macOS 26.4, Apple Silicon (VirtualMac2,1) - Google Chrome, driver-owned isolated profile (`browser_prepare`, `allow_launch: true`) ### Evidence Attached clip (21 s): Chrome on the left, the MCP calls and their results on the right. At about 7 s the insert_text call returns `isError: false` while TodoMVC shows "Buy milk" still in the box and no todo. At about 16 s the keystrokes call on the keyCode box returns the same, the box still holds "hello", and the page reports the Enter keydown with `keyCode 0`. ### Workaround and additional context - What worked on current main: `browser_type` without the newline, then a native `press_key` `key: "return"` on the Chrome window. The page then got `{key: "Enter", code: "Enter", keyCode: 13}`. It worked in 4 of 6 runs. Both misses were the first run right after the browser launched. On a regular Chrome window this route can also be refused, see #4241. - Related: #2883 (browser actions report `effect: "unverifiable"`). A value read-back would not catch this case by itself: once Enter works, a field that sends and clears itself reads back as `""`, which is the expected outcome, not a mismatch. - Possible fix, implemented and tested in a fork, happy to send as a PR: on a single-line field, split one trailing newline off in both modes, type the text, then send Enter as keyDown/char/keyUp with `code: "Enter"` and `windowsVirtualKeyCode: 13`, and say in the result that Enter was pressed. A textarea or contenteditable keeps the newline as text in insert_text mode, as it does today. ### Submission checks - [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests. - [x] This issue describes a single problem. - [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: feat(cua-mcp): a small agent surface with user approvals
body:
Cuts what agents are given down to a small, hand-written surface, and puts every capability that reaches the user's own machines, money, secrets or data behind a user approval.

## Size

Measured from the serialized `tools/list` of each build, run with a throwaway HOME/CUA_HOME.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `cua mcp` tools listed | 138 (93.7 KB, ~23k tokens) | 20 (12.6 KB, ~3.2k tokens) |
| cua-driver `tools/list` | 58 (182 KB, ~46k tokens) | 49 (53.5 KB, ~13k tokens) |
| Skills, `SKILL.md` (5) | 28.5 KB | 15.6 KB |

- **Merged tools.** Related tools are merged into one tool with an `action`: `space`, `space_files`, `computer`, `window`, `agent`, `volume`, `teleport` and `show_space`.
- **`more`.** Rarely used tools sit behind `more`, which lists them, describes one, or calls one through the same gate.
- **Old names.** Every old tool name still works when called by name; it just isn't listed.
- **Driver.** cua-driver drops `outputSchema` and `risk` from the default list. `detail: "full"` returns everything.

## Approvals

These can ask for Touch ID, and the user can change each one in **Settings → Permissions**. On a fresh install:
- **Ask by default:** using the cloud, sending sensitive files, sharing API keys.
- **Off by default:** adding machines, controlling your machines, running on a schedule, changing Volume storage, sharing your network, showing things on your screen.

Changing a setting itself needs Touch ID.

Some actions are always refused for agents:
- approving their own Volume requests or editing grants;
- downloading into the Cua home, `~/.ssh` or LaunchAgents.

Volume data tools now run as `host-<client>` instead of as the user.

Teleport, site login, sharing and computer access keep their existing always-ask gates.

## Where it is enforced

- **Daemon, not just `cua mcp`.** The daemon applies the same classification and policy to every caller that is not the user's own Cua code: `CallSpaceTool`, `AddSpace`, creating Spaces and sandboxes, Fleet claims, passthroughs to the user's machines, and `Shutdown`. Gated actions are refused with `approval_denied` (a new `DAEMON_ERROR_REASON_APPROVAL_DENIED`) unless the user approves with Touch ID in a build that can ask.
- **HTTP `/mcp`.** It serves the same tool list as `cua mcp` through the same gate. A request with a web `Origin` is refused.
- **Trust model.** The signed Cua app and signed `cua` (checked from the socket peer's audit token and code signature) are the user. Any other process, loopback caller holding only the `daemon.json` token, or `/mcp` caller is an agent. Verified clients get a second token that exists only in memory.
- **Settings file.** `approvals.json` is HMAC-signed with a key in a dedicated Keychain item whose access list names only the Cua apps and `cua`. An edited, rolled-back or deleted file means every action asks, with a notice in Settings → Permissions. Changing a setting still needs Touch ID.

## Known gaps

- An agent that runs the signed `cua` CLI in its own shell is treated as the CLI. The gate bounds the MCP surface, the socket and HTTP, not a shell.
- A client that connects by loopback URL and token (rather than the socket) is an agent. A daemon with no socket (Windows, embedded fixtures) gates only `/mcp`.
- The real Touch ID path, the Keychain access list and the Developer ID code-signature check are not exercised end to end: tests use a fake approver, an in-memory seal and the daemon's own program as the trusted peer. The keychain tests are `#[ignore]`d because they create a keychain file.
- Splitting the tools into `action` tools makes it harder to allow or deny single operations by tool name in a client config.

## Dogfood

7 prompts were run with `claude -p` against a simulated Space, on both builds.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Context per turn | ~41k tokens | ~11.5k tokens |
| Cost | $0.25 | $0.115 |
| Wrong-tool picks | 0 | 0 |

A decoy SSH-key upload that went through before is now refused with `approval_denied`.

## Tests

- **Rust.** `cua-spaces` (11 enforcement tests, sealed-policy and tamper tests), `cua-daemon` (`caller_gate`: `/mcp` gated, a real `curl` peer refused on the socket, the user's own client not asked), `cua-spaces-ext`, `cua-cli` (`/mcp` lists what `cua mcp` lists), `cua-sdk`, `cua-agent-setup`, cua-driver unit and integration, and app-core all pass.
- **Swift.** The Swift app suite passes except `onboardingPages`, a snapshot 0.5% over its tolerance in a view this PR does not touch; new snapshots for the Permissions pane, including the tampered-settings notice.
- **Not verified.** The Linux/Windows driver backends and the docs generator were not run.

title: fix(cua-bench): run the full qwen3vl step budget and return rejected actions to the model
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: the `qwen3vl` bench agent spent only about half of `--max-steps` on actions. A rejected action could also end the whole task.
  - `ComputerAgent.run` yields twice per action: once for the model turn and once for the action result. The agent counted both yields as steps, so `--max-steps 15` ran 7 actions.
  - The budget check fired on the model-turn yield, so the last generated action was never executed.
  - A desktop error for one action, for example `CuaError.Env: protocol error: unknown key "click"`, escaped the computer handler and ended the task as `FailureMode.UNKNOWN`. The model never got a chance to correct itself.
- What changed:
  - Only yields that carry model output count toward the step budget. The loop stops on the last action's result, after that action has run.
  - An action the session rejects is raised as `cua_agent.types.ToolError`. `ComputerAgent` already returns that error to the model as a tool result, as it does for unknown actions. Screenshot failures still propagate, so a dead sandbox is not hidden.
  - The computer handler maps `key_down`/`key_up` (for example, Shift-click selection) to the sandbox keyboard, releasing keys in reverse order. It raises a `ToolError` when the session has no sandbox. These actions only reach the handler once `CustomComputerHandler` forwards them; see the related cua-agent pull request.

## Related work

No issue filed. Found while running OSWorld through cua-bench with a Qwen 27B VLM. The related cua-agent fix (generic VLM history schema, `CustomComputerHandler.key_down/key_up`) is a separate pull request.

RFC: not required. This is a bug fix inside one bench agent.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: `qwen3vl` runs now take up to the full `--max-steps` actions, so they can take longer. Results from earlier runs were measured with roughly half the stated budget.
- Risk and rollback: the change is confined to `cua_bench/agents/qwen3vl_agent.py`. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `cua_bench/tests/test_qwen3vl_agent.py` (7 tests). It uses a fake `ComputerAgent` that only executes an action when the consumer resumes it.
  - `max_steps` of 1, 3, and 15 execute exactly 1, 3, and 15 actions.
  - A rejected key and an unknown button become `ToolError`.
  - `key_down`/`key_up` reach the sandbox keyboard in order, and a session without a sandbox is a `ToolError`.
- Mutation check: all 7 tests fail against the current `main` version of the agent and pass with this change.
- Suite and lint:
  - `uv run --frozen pytest -q cua_bench/tests --ignore=cua_bench/tests/live`: 327 passed, 2 skipped.
  - isort, black, and ruff are clean on the changed files.
- Manual evidence, OSWorld `test_small` without the 3 Google Drive tasks (36 tasks, local runc container, Qwen 27B VLM, with the computer tool sent as native `tools` through `extra_body` for this endpoint):
  - Before the step fix, tasks stopped after 7 executed actions.
  - With the fixes, writer task `0810415c` (Shift-click two paragraphs) went from aborting with `FailureMode.UNKNOWN` to passing in 9 steps.
- Known gaps: none known.

title: fix(cua-agent): replay generic VLM computer calls in the advertised Qwen schema
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: the generic VLM loop (`GenericVlmConfig`, used by `Qwen3VlConfig`) mixes two schemas in what it sends the model.
  - It advertises Qwen's `computer` tool, which uses `{"action": "left_click", "coordinate": [x, y]}` with coordinates normalised to 0..1000.
  - When it replays its own earlier calls, they go out in the pixel Computer Calls schema, for example `{"type": "click", "x": 372, "y": 346, "button": "right"}`.
  - From the second step on, the model sees two schemas and two coordinate spaces. It starts emitting history-style calls such as `{"x": "240", "y": "497", "type": "click"}`. These skip `_unnormalize_coordinate`, which needs a `coordinate` key, so the clicks run in a different space from the one the model chose.
  - Separately, `CustomComputerHandler` had no `key_down`/`key_up`. A model trying to Shift-click got `Unknown computer action: key_down`.
- What changed:
  - Before sending, the loop restates each replayed `computer` tool call in its own tool schema. This is the inverse of `convert_qwen_tool_args_to_computer_action`, scaled to 0..1000 with the same `smart_resize` dimensions. Calls already in the Qwen schema are left alone. A single key string such as `"enter"` is kept whole, not split into characters.
  - `CustomComputerHandler.key_down/key_up` forward to `functions["key_down"/"key_up"]`. When a function is absent they raise the same `ToolError("Unknown computer action: …")` as before.

## Related work

No issue filed. Found while running OSWorld through cua-bench with a Qwen 27B VLM. The related cua-bench fix (`qwen3vl` step budget, rejected actions, `key_down`/`key_up` mapping) is a separate pull request.

RFC: not required. This fixes the loop's request contents and adds a handler method; it does not change the public API.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Qwen and other generic-VLM models now see their own calls in the advertised schema. The tool schema itself and the default request shape are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: replayed calls the inverse mapping does not recognise, such as `drag`, are sent unchanged, as before. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests:
  - `tests/test_generic_vlm_history.py` drives `GenericVlmConfig.predict_step` with `litellm.acompletion` captured and the qwen extras stubbed. It asserts that a replayed right click at (960, 540) on a 1920x1080 screen goes out as `{"action": "right_click", "coordinate": [500, 500]}`, and that `ctrl+s` goes out as `{"action": "key", ...}`. It also round-trips every Qwen action through the forward conversion and back.
  - `tests/test_custom_computer_keys.py` covers `key_down`/`key_up` dispatch and the unknown-action error.
- Mutation check:
  - With the replay restatement removed (helper kept), the `predict_step` test fails.
  - With `custom.py` from `main`, the key tests fail.
- Suite and lint:
  - `pytest libs/python/agent/tests`: 75 passed.
  - isort, black, and ruff are clean on the changed files.
- Manual evidence, OSWorld task `5ea617a3` (recover a file from the Trash), Qwen 27B VLM. Both runs sent the computer tool as native `tools` through `extra_body`, because this endpoint ignores the prompt-embedded schema:
  - Before: 8 actions, 4 of them string-coordinate clicks in the Computer Calls schema. Reward 0.
  - After: 4 actions, reward 1.
  - Across a 36-task run with the change: 0 string-coordinate actions.
- Known gaps: the Sandbox computer handler (`computers/sandbox.py`) also lacks `key_down`/`key_up`. This pull request covers custom computers only.

title: fix(cua-driver): deliver macOS foreground keys to a window's attached sheet
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #4507.

- Problem this solves: #4507 made a sheet's controls actionable by element through the window it is attached to. Keys still are not. While a sheet attached to a window holds focus (a Save panel, Go to Folder on an Open panel), `AXFocusedWindow` is the sheet, and its CGWindowID differs from the window's. The two focus checks before foreground HID delivery compare that id with the requested window, so `press_key`, `hotkey` and `type_text` with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` aimed at the window fail with `exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery` and deliver nothing. #4392 reports this directly ("Foreground hotkey/type_text aimed at the main window delivered zero characters while the sheet held focus").
- What changed:
  - `focused_window_id_for_target(pid, target)` (`ax/bindings.rs`): when the focused window is not `target` but #4507's `owning_window_id` maps it to `target` (an `AXSheet` whose `AXParent` chain ends at that `AXWindow`), it reports `target`. Otherwise it reports the focused window's own id. `await_window_focused` and `with_foreground_hid_activation` (`input/skylight.rs`) use it. A sheet requested by its own id still matches itself, a sheet attached to another window keeps its own id, and the other readers of the focused window (`bring_to_front`, `invoke_menu`) keep `focused_window_id_of_pid` unchanged.
  - `get_window_state` on a sheet's own window id still returns the empty `ax_window_unresolved` tree and the same refusals. When a bounded AX scan (0.25 s per request, 0.5 s total, only on that degraded path) finds the sheet under one of the pid's windows, the result names it in `escalation.parent_window_id`, and the reason text says where the controls are instead of pointing at "the menu bar, other windows". What is actionable does not change.
  - The AppKit harness gains an opt-in `save_sheet` scenario and two e2e tests (see Validation).

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. In a logged-in macOS session with cua-driver 0.34.0 (main b0a634813) running, open a plain-text file in TextEdit, then choose File > Open… (`invoke_menu` with `path: ["File", "Open…"]` works). The Open panel is its own window titled "Open".
2. Read the ids: `list_windows` with `{"pid": <pid>}` lists the "Open" window (`<open_id>`); `get_window_state` on `<open_id>` shows the panel and its location pop-up.
3. Open the Go to Folder sheet by typing `/` into the panel:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <open_id>, "key": "/", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   ```
   (`press_key`; this works on main because the panel itself is focused). `list_windows` now shows one more on-screen TextEdit window, the sheet (`<sheet_id>`), and it holds focus.
4. Press Return aimed at the Open panel:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <open_id>, "key": "return", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   ```
   Expected: the sheet takes Return and the panel moves to Macintosh HD. Actual on main (3/3):
   ```
   press_key delivery failed: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery
   {"code": "delivery_failed"}
   ```
   Nothing is delivered: the sheet stays open with `/` in it and the panel stays in its folder.
5. The same call aimed at the sheet's own id works on main and on this branch (`✅ Pressed return on pid <pid> (delivery_mode:foreground).`, panel moves to Macintosh HD):
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <sheet_id>, "key": "return", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   ```
   But nothing tells an agent that id is the way in. Reading it:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <sheet_id>, "include_screenshot": false}
   ```
   returns 0 elements and, on main:
   ```
   ax_window_unresolved: window_id 51496 exists and is owned by pid 67167, but none of the 2 AXWindow element(s) under that pid reports this CGWindowID. The tree is returned EMPTY on purpose: the accessibility elements reachable under this pid belong to other surfaces (the menu bar, other windows), not to the requested window, ...
   ```

On this branch, step 4 returns `✅ Pressed return on pid <pid> (delivery_mode:foreground).` with `route: "global_input"`, the sheet closes and the panel shows Macintosh HD (3/3). Step 5's read returns the same empty tree with:

```
"degraded_reason": "ax_window_unresolved: window_id 51740 is a sheet attached to window_id 51734 of pid 67984. No AXWindow reports a sheet's own CGWindowID; its controls are in window 51734's accessibility tree, so the tree for this id is returned EMPTY.",
"escalation": {"recommended": "foreground", "parent_window_id": 51734,
  "reason": "call get_window_state with window_id 51734 and act on the sheet's elements with window_id 51734. Background input aimed at this id stays refused; delivery_mode:\"foreground\" keys aimed at window 51734 reach its focused sheet."}
```

Harness test for the same thing (after `libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures/build/macos.sh --only appkit`, against the installed daemon):

```
cargo test -p cua-driver-e2e --test harness_appkit_test -- --ignored --exact harness_appkit_foreground_key_reaches_an_attached_sheet --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

## Related work

Follow-up to #4507. Refs #4392, Refs #3351.

#4392 is closed by #4507; this covers the keyboard part of its report, which #4507 did not change. #3351 stays open: its contributors (@will-bogusz, @odoiffco) argue the sheet should resolve at its own `(pid, window_id)`, so the controls are reachable even when the parent snapshot omits them. This PR does not do that: the sheet's own id still reads empty and stays refused for background input, and the new field only points at the window that does resolve. Resolving the sheet at its own id is a larger contract decision for maintainers and would build on this. Separate and also out of scope: the Save panel's file format pop-up exposes no AX children.

#3863 (draft, exact key window for foreground shortcuts) touches `hotkey.rs` only and does not handle sheets; the two do not overlap.

RFC: not required (no schema or SDK change: the manifest allows extra properties, and the typed `WindowStateOutput` has no `escalation` field, so typed SDK callers see only the reason text).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: macOS only. Foreground keys and HID pointer events aimed at a window now go through when a sheet attached to that window holds focus, where they used to fail. Every other focus case is decided as before. `get_window_state` on a sheet's own id gains `escalation.parent_window_id` and new reason text; the tree, `degraded`, `recommended` and `background_input` are unchanged.
- Safety boundary: the remap needs the focused window of the target pid to be an `AXSheet` (or a chain of sheets) whose `AXParent` chain ends at an `AXWindow` mapped to exactly the requested id. So keys cannot be accepted for a sibling window of the same app whose sheet has focus (tested: Return aimed at TextEdit's `note.txt` window while the Open panel's sheet held focus is still refused 3/3, sheet untouched), for another app's window (the check reads only the target pid's focus; a TextEdit pid with a Finder window id, and a Finder pid with the Open window id, are still refused 3/3), or for a sheet whose parent is the application (it keeps its own id, as in #4507). The keys then land in the sheet, which is where AppKit routes keys for a window with an attached sheet. Nested sheets map to the root window, so keys aimed at it reach the topmost focused sheet.
- Rollback: revert the commit; nothing persists.

## Validation

- Harness tests, both registered in `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh`. The fixture gets an opt-in `save_sheet` scenario (`CUA_APPKIT_SAVE_SHEET=1`, listed in `scenarios.json`, appended below Exit like the other opt-in controls so ordinary launches are unchanged): a button that opens an `NSSavePanel` as a sheet on the main window, and a label recording `open`, `cancelled` or `saved name=...`.
  - `harness_appkit_save_sheet_controls_act_through_their_window` (background AX cell, under the background focus, z-order, cursor and leaked-input oracles): sets the sheet's name field by token through the main window and reads it back, checks that `get_window_state` on the sheet's own id names the main window in `escalation.parent_window_id`, then presses Save by token through the main window and waits for `save_sheet=saved name=harness-sheet` with the sheet gone. This also covers #4507's fix, which had no harness test.
  - `harness_appkit_foreground_key_reaches_an_attached_sheet` (foreground HID cell): foreground Return aimed at the main window must save under the default name; foreground Escape aimed at the sheet's own id must cancel.
  - macOS 26.4 VM, installed daemon, same test binary and fixture build: on main b0a634813 both fail 3/3 (the first at the `parent_window_id` assertion after `set_value` succeeds, the second with `exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery`); on this branch both pass 3/3. The fixture's opener button often answers `AXPress` with -25204 or -25205 while the out-of-process panel loads, after opening it, so the tests take the sheet appearing as the evidence instead of that reply.
  - Existing AppKit tests on this branch, same VM: `harness_appkit_smoke`, `harness_appkit_counter`, `harness_appkit_element_foreground_press_key_commits_edit`, `harness_appkit_foreground_press_key_chord_carries_its_modifiers`, `harness_appkit_exact_activation_ignores_competing_application_window`, `harness_appkit_invoke_menu_live_path`, `harness_appkit_foreground_single_click_has_one_ordered_native_pair`, `harness_appkit_erroring_toggle_press_counts_only_when_its_value_moved` pass. `harness_appkit_exact_activation_with_agent_cursor` could not run because the VM daemon was started with `--no-overlay` (`macOS agent cursor overlay is unavailable`).
- Unit tests: `ax::bindings::tests` for the focus decision (exact match needs no lookup; a sheet of the target counts; a sheet of another window, an unprovable owner and no focus do not). The sheet chain itself is #4507's `resolve_owning_window`, already tested.
- Checks: `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (483 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --lib -p cua-driver-e2e --tests` (no warnings in touched files), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check`, `test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py` (11 passed). The `get_window_state` description change is mirrored into `window-state.mdx` and `cli-specs/cua-driver-mcp-macos.json`; the macOS snapshot matches a native `dump-docs` of this build exactly. The new MACOS.md row is added to both copies (they already differ on main, so `sync-skills.sh --check` reports the same pre-existing drift).
- Manual platform evidence (macOS 26.4 VM, Apple Silicon, TextEdit Open panel with its Go to Folder sheet focused, one MCP connection, fresh TextEdit per case, 3 runs each):

  | Case | main b0a634813 | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `press_key` return, foreground, aimed at the Open window | 3/3 `exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery`; sheet stays, panel stays in `work` | 3/3 delivered; sheet closes, panel at Macintosh HD |
  | Same, aimed at the sheet's own id | 3/3 delivered, panel at Macintosh HD | unchanged |
  | `get_window_state` on the sheet's own id | 0 elements, text points at "the menu bar, other windows" | 0 elements, `escalation.parent_window_id` = the Open window 3/3 |
  | Return aimed at `note.txt` (a sibling window the sheet is not attached to) | 3/3 refused, sheet untouched | 3/3 refused, sheet untouched |
  | TextEdit pid + Finder window id; Finder pid + Open window id | refused 3/3 | refused 3/3 |

  Attached clip (30 s): the step 4 call on main (refused, sheet stays), then on this branch (delivered, panel moves).

  https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a9b47cc-e410-497c-b4c4-9af46163af43

- Known gaps or CI still required: the canonical macOS Lume matrix (`tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh`) needs the maintainer golden image; the new tests and the existing ones above ran individually. Pixel clicks with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` share `with_foreground_hid_activation`, so they also go through now while an attached sheet has focus; I did not add a separate test for that route.

title: fix(host): send the enrolled device session when registering with the relay
body:
`cua host setup` built its relay client without the device session, so even an enrolled device registered with only the account token and the relay refused re-registering a live machine ("re-registering this machine needs its machine token or an enrolled device").

- `Host::with_device(Arc<DeviceAuth>)`: setup attaches `try_session()` to the register call when the device belongs to the same relay (same pattern as `cua-spaces` `RelayAccount::client`). Not enrolled: no header, no new prompts, same behavior as before (the relay now accepts re-registering an offline stale record with just the account token, #4553).
- `cua host` passes its device to `Host`.
- `FakeRelay::register_sessions()` records the device-session header per registration; new test `setup_registers_with_the_device_session_only_when_enrolled` covers not enrolled (omitted), enrolled (sent), and a device of another relay (omitted).

Tests: `cargo test -j4 -p cua-host -p cua-cli -p cua-spaces` (throwaway HOME/CUA_HOME), clippy clean.

fix(cua-bench): preserve quoted keyboard action literals
body:
## Summary

Parsing `repr(TypeAction(text="line one\nline two"))` currently produces literal backslash-n characters instead of a newline. Mixed quotes can truncate text, Windows paths gain extra backslashes, and hotkeys containing commas or closing brackets fail to round-trip.

Match complete string/list literals and decode them with `ast.literal_eval`. Require the complete action to match so trailing commands or unexpected fields do not get silently discarded. This covers the repr parser and the snake-case `type(...)` form.

## Related work

Self-contained correctness fix; no linked issue. Searched active PRs for competing parser work.

## Compatibility and risk

The existing action classes, function signatures and serialized fields remain compatible. Escapes now follow the Python literal syntax already used by action reprs; malformed input raises ValueError rather than being partially accepted.

## Validation

- Reproduced 19 failures on the unmodified parser before implementing the fix.
- Focused parser suite: 55 passed, covering multiline text, Windows paths, mixed quotes, punctuation keys, empty/string hotkey lists and malformed literals.
- Python 3.12, full offline cua-bench suite on candidate `2d33c8d`: **343 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Black, isort, Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing CI collects the new cases.

- Local release-title validation and `validate_release_versions.py --product all` passed.

title: fix(cua-bench): apply configuration for the selected agent
body:
## Summary

If `.cua/config.yaml` selects `first` and the CLI selects `--agent second`, configuration lookup still loads first's registered import path. The resulting namespace names second but can execute first's class. Registered defaults also lose to lower-priority config.yaml values despite the documented precedence.

Resolve the winning agent before looking up its registration, clear an inherited import when switching agents, and merge the existing layers in their documented order: CLI > environment > registered agent defaults > agent config > project defaults. A registration without an import path preserves the explicit configured import for the same agent.

## Related work

Self-contained correctness fix; no linked issue. Searched active PRs for ConfigLoader/agent-selection work.

## Compatibility and risk

No flags, schema fields or function signatures are added. Configurations relying on the reversed precedence now follow the documented order. Explicit CLI import paths remain highest priority.

## Validation

- Six new regression cases failed against the original loader.
- Focused config/discovery suite: 13 passed, including the real CLI configuration application helper and YAML-backed selection/precedence cases.

title: fix(cua-bench): resolve Harbor task links from their cache directory
body:
## Summary

A Harbor dataset fetched with `CUA_BENCH_REGISTRY_CACHE=cache` creates a task symlink whose target repeats the relative cache path. The pinned checkout succeeds, but `tasks/hello/main.py` cannot be opened. Re-resolving that cached dataset can then raise FileExistsError.

Create each link relative to its containing tasks directory. Repair dangling task symlinks left by the previous behavior before recreating them.

## Related work

Self-contained correctness fix; no linked issue. Searched active PRs for relative registry-cache work.

## Compatibility and risk

The registry format and pinned checkout behavior are retained. Existing valid links remain in use; repair removes only a dangling symlink at the selected task link. Dataset files and checkouts are preserved.

## Validation

- All three relative-cache cases failed against the original implementation. A separate regression also reproduced the stale-link FileExistsError before adding repair.

title: feat(cua-spaces): eject the installer disk image after a drag install
body:
## Problem

You install Cua Spaces by dragging it out of the mounted installer into Applications. The installer volume then stays mounted in Finder and on the desktop until you eject it yourself.

## Before / after

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Launch] --> B{Running from /Applications or ~/Applications?}
  B -- no --> Z[Nothing happens]
  B -- yes --> C[Mounted volumes that are read-only and ejectable]
  C --> D{Has a top-level .app with our bundle id?}
  D -- no --> Z
  D -- yes --> E[Eject it once, and log a failure]
```

Before: the installer volume stays mounted after the app is installed and launched.
After: a launch from an Applications folder ejects mounted read-only, ejectable volumes that hold a Cua Spaces app bundle. The downloaded installer file is left alone.

## Changes

- `InstallerCleanup` is now a small internal enum:
  - `installed(_:home:)` resolves symlinks in the app path and in both Applications folders, and checks the path is inside `/Applications/` or `~/Applications/`, matching whole path components.
  - `installers(among:holding:isInstaller:)` picks volumes that pass `isInstaller` and have a top-level `.app` whose `Bundle(url:)?.bundleIdentifier` matches.
  - `isReadOnlyEjectable(_:)` is true only when the volume reports both read-only and ejectable. If either value is missing, it counts as false.
  - `ejectInstallers()` finds volumes with `FileManager.mountedVolumeURLs` and ejects each match with `NSWorkspace.unmountAndEjectDevice(at:)`.
- `applicationDidFinishLaunching` starts one detached utility-priority task that calls `InstallerCleanup.ejectInstallers()`.
- The README has one short "Installer cleanup" row.

### Cut from the earlier draft

- The prompt that offered to move the `.dmg` in Downloads to the Trash, and the wait for onboarding to finish before showing it.
- Downloads access entirely, so macOS shows no folder-access prompt.
- The saved "Keep" choice in UserDefaults.
- Running `hdiutil info -plist` and parsing its output, the `InstallerVolumes` protocol, `InstallerImage`, and the fixture class in production sources.

## Side effects

- At most one eject attempt per qualifying volume on each launch. No retry and no forced eject, so a busy volume stays mounted and the failure goes to the log.
- Only volumes that are read-only, ejectable, and hold an app with the Cua Spaces bundle identifier are touched.
- Nothing runs unless the app itself is running from an Applications folder. A launch from the mounted volume, from Downloads, or from an App Translocation path does nothing.
- No files are moved or deleted, and there are no network calls.

## Tests

`InstallerCleanupTests` (Swift Testing) builds real temporary folders, each with a `Cua Spaces.app/Contents/Info.plist`, and never mounts or ejects real volumes:

- A matching volume is selected when `isInstaller` returns true.
- No volume is selected when `isInstaller` returns false, when the bundle identifier is different, or when the volume has no `.app`.
- `installed` is true for `/Applications/X.app`, `~/Applications/X.app`, and `~/Applications/X.app` under a symlinked home folder. It is false for `/Volumes/Cua Spaces/X.app`, an App Translocation path, `~/Downloads/X.app`, and `/ApplicationsFoo/X.app`.

These tests call `InstallerCleanup.installers` and `InstallerCleanup.installed`, which don't exist on main, so they fail to compile there. They haven't been run locally. macOS CI ("SwiftUI app (swift test, bundle, XCUITest)") compiles and runs them.

Still needed: a manual drag-install check on a Mac. Mount the release `.dmg`, drag Cua Spaces to Applications, launch it from there, and confirm the installer volume ejects.

title: fix(images): release-macos.sh logs in to ghcr, guards disk and drops push caches
body:
These fix rough edges found in the first end-to-end run of `scripts/images/release-macos.sh` (cua-spacesd 0.5.3, macOS 26-slim and 26):

- **Registry login:** the script never logged crane and oras in, so `annotate.sh`, the doctor-report attach and `verify` relied on whatever `~/.docker` held. The run only worked because I had pre-logged-in a scratch `DOCKER_CONFIG`. It now logs both in to ghcr.io with the gh token under an isolated `DOCKER_CONFIG=$WORK/docker`.
- **Push caches:** `lume push` keeps a ~23 GB `.lume_oci_push_cache` inside each VM directory. Slim's was also cloned into the full VM, and neither was deleted, so the run sat about 50 GB above what it needed. On this Mac (~265 GB free) that hit the 200 GB floor during the slim push. Each tier's cache is now dropped as soon as its pin is verified, before the full tier clones slim.
- **Disk guard:** the run refuses to start below `MIN_FREE_GB + 60` (default 260 GB) and checks again before each build and push. Below the floor it stops cleanly, and a rerun resumes.
- **Local ledger:** with `RECORD_LEDGER=false`, the pins' doctor verdicts are now written to `$WORK/ledger`, so `check-docs-image-refs.py --ledger` can confirm the macOS refs.

Tested with `bash -n`, `shellcheck -S warning` and `--dry-run`, which shows the order: publish, drop cache, record, then the next tier. The cache deletion and local-ledger steps are exactly what I ran by hand during the 0.5.3 run.

Other notes from the run, not changed here:
- **Keychain check on resume:** a rerun repeats the keychain check, booting a fresh clone each time. That's harmless and takes about 20 seconds.
- **Input-gate build directory:** the gate builds its cargo test into the checkout's `libs/cua/target` unless `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is set (about 9 GB).

title: fix(cua-driver): find driver releases beyond the first page of monorepo releases
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `cua-driver update` fails with "Could not reach GitHub" when no tag for the selected channel is among the 40 newest monorepo releases. The check read a single page, and every lookup failure printed that one line. Since the Oct 3 cua-spaces, cua-spacesd, and cua-sdk releases, the nightly channel has no tag on that page.
- What changed: the check pages through the listing, 40 releases per request, and stops at the first page with a matching tag or after five pages. `cua-driver update` now prints why a lookup failed. A request failure keeps the "Could not reach GitHub" line and adds a `Reason:` line. A lookup that finds no release for the channel prints `Could not find a <channel> release: no <prefix>* release in the <n> most recent GitHub releases.`

## Related work

Fixes #4598

#2116 edits the same fetch function to add a token header. The two changes will conflict textually but not in behavior.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. Only failure-path message text changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - `cua-driver update` text output changes on failure only, as described above. Exit codes are unchanged. The Windows update E2E retries on the "Could not reach GitHub" line, which request failures still print.
  - The `error` string in `check-update --json` and the `check_for_update` MCP tool is reworded for the no-release case. The JSON shape is unchanged, and the cache fallback is unchanged.
  - A check makes one request when page 1 has a matching tag, as before, and up to five when it does not. Each request keeps the 4 second timeout, so the background banner check can now take up to 20 seconds on its own thread in the worst case.
  - The page size stays at 40. A 100-release page is about 5 MB and took 1.7 s from my machine, which is too close to the timeout.
  - Stopping at the first matching page assumes the listing puts a channel's newest release first. A backport tagged after a higher version can break that if a page boundary falls between the two. The single-page check had the same limit inside its page. A comment on `find_latest_release` states the assumption.
- Risk and rollback: the change is confined to the release lookup and its error message. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver --locked` on macOS arm64: exit 0, no failures, 305 unit tests including the five new `release_lookup_*` tests.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - Mutation check of the new tests: capping the lookup at one page fails four of them, ignoring a short page fails `release_lookup_ends_at_a_short_page`, and reading past a matching page fails `release_lookup_reads_past_a_page_without_matching_tags`.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 27.2 arm64, debug build of this branch, isolated `HOME`, live GitHub API, 2026-10-04):
  - stable channel: `Already up to date.`
  - nightly channel: `New version available: 0.30.5-nightly.20260929.36522098176`, found on page 2. The released 0.30.5 nightly binary fails in the same environment.
  - request failure through a dead proxy: the "Could not reach GitHub" line, then `Reason: HTTP error: io: Connection refused`, exit 1.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The no-release message was not produced against live GitHub because both channels currently resolve. Its text is covered by `release_lookup_gives_up_after_the_page_cap`.
  - Not run on Windows or Linux. The change has no platform-specific code.
  - The desktop E2E matrix was not run. No input, capture, or desktop behavior changed.

- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: chore: remove the libs/fleet mirror and the cua-fleet crate
body:
Cua Cloud (Fleets) shuts down on Fri 16 Oct 2026, 17:00 PT. This removes the Fleets code that was mirrored into this repo under `libs/fleet`, and everything that built against it. **Draft: do not merge.**

## What is removed
- `libs/fleet` (the Copybara mirror: Go backend, web console, `cyclops-sdk` Rust crates, language bindings, Terraform provider) and `.github/workflows/fleet-mirror-guard.yml`, plus the CODEOWNERS entry.
- The `cua-fleet` crate. The local helpers it held (sidecars, local image builds) move into `cua-sandbox-core` (`build`, `sidecar` modules) unchanged in behaviour.
- `libs/typescript/fleet` (`@trycua/fleet` was built from `libs/fleet`) with `cd-ts-fleet.yml`, `ci-ts-fleet.yml` and its release wiring. Published versions are untouched.
- Workflows that built or ran `libs/fleet` / `cua-fleet` code: `infra-fleets-wif-smoke.yml`, `nightly-image-doctor.yml`, the Go Terraform smoke, the Fleet docs generator, the `fleet`/`fleet-env`/`cua-sandbox` e2e lanes and the fake Fleet test fixture.

## Behaviour after this change
- `on="cloud"` creates, `cloud:<name>` refs, `Cua.fleet()` pool/claim/image calls, `cua fleet …`, `cua image ls|info|rm|create` and `cua auth keys …` fail at once with "Cua Cloud has closed: … Run sandboxes locally, on a machine you run, or in your own cloud account (on=aws|gcp|modal)". The CLI exits with code 4.
- The SDK's FFI shape is unchanged (same objects, records and methods), so existing callers get that message, not a missing symbol. Bindings are regenerated for the doc text only.
- Records of earlier cloud sandboxes and Spaces stay listed; using them says Cua Cloud has closed, and `delete` removes the record.
- `cua auth whoami` shows the identity from the account token and no longer lists Fleet namespaces.

## What keeps working
- The Spaces apps' billing status (`GET /api/billing/status`) and the existing Cua Volume `cloud` backend still call the same endpoints with the same base URL (`CUA_FLEET_BASE_URL`, default `https://run.cua.ai`) and the same credentials (signed-in session, `FLEETS_TOKEN`, or `CUA_CLIENT_ID`/`CUA_CLIENT_SECRET`). They now go through a small client in `cua-auth` (`account`) instead of the Fleet SDK. `Cua.fleet().billingStatus()` keeps working for the SwiftUI app.

## Tests
- `libs/cua`: `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, the web-feature clippy, the wasm32 build, `cargo fmt`, and `cargo test` for cua-auth, cua-sandbox-core, cua-spaces, cua-daemon, cua-sdk, cua-cli, cua-spaces-ext, cua-spaces-ffi, cua-spaces-app-core, cua-spaces-cli and cua-volume.
- Spaces app (Tauri): `cargo test --lib --test commands`; openkoalabot sample and the spaces-e2e and SDK e2e crates check and clippy clean.
- Python binding tests; bindings drift check; docs generators (`--check` for cua-cli, cua-sdk, python, TS, cua-rust, sandbox, spaces) and docs structure, link and image-ref checks; `check-lockfiles` for every Cargo and pnpm lockfile.

title: [Bug]: macOS Lume bring_to_front test loses its SwiftUI occluder before prior-app recovery
body:
## Summary

On the canonical Lume lane, `exact_secondary_window_is_verified_and_prior_app_can_recover_focus` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/bring_to_front_macos_test.rs:351`) fails at its final step:

```
prior app recovery failed: bring_to_front: no running application for pid <occluder> (process not found or exited).
```

The SwiftUI occluder is launched with `open -n -g`. It maps an ordinary window, accepts `AXRaise` through System Events, and the exact secondary-window activation and its frontmost, AX key-window and z-order oracles all pass. By the recovery call, the occluder process has gone. It leaves no crash report and no runningboard termination record. The other two `bring_to_front` tests pass. The hosted macOS lane passes this test.

## Occurrences

Same disposable `macos-tahoe-cua:26.5.2` worker (25F84, SIP off), with `--test-threads=1` as the runner invokes it:

| Source | Run | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `b00cb46d5` (#4601) | `20261004T112135Z-95348` | pass |
| `7ff69de17` | `20261004T113152Z-35288` | fail |
| `c7e684b41` | `20261004T134131Z-1402` | fail |
| `c7e684b41` (after a VM reboot) | `20261004T141421Z-39361` | fail |

In the last two runs, every other part of the gate passes, including all 173 typed rows. This test is the only thing keeping the Lume gate from a clean pass on `main`.

## Notes

- The SwiftUI harness exits only through its Exit button (`NSApp.terminate`). Nothing in the test presses it.
- `launch_occluder` takes the first new pid of the harness executable after `open -n`. If LaunchServices briefly creates a handoff process, or another instance of the harness is relaunched, that pid may not be the long-lived app. This is unproven.
- Possible directions: resolve the occluder through `NSRunningApplication` and the bundle URL, and re-resolve before recovery; or launch the occluder in the test's job and own its lifetime.

title: fix(cua-driver): count focus in a window's inline rename field as focus on that window
body:
## Summary

This PR was narrowed to the focus fix only; keeping Finder in front when the field is opened from behind another app follows as a separate PR once this one lands, and that one will close #4615.

- Problem this solves: with Finder in front, renaming a file through foreground keys on its window (the route #4483's `file_name_needs_rename` refusal points to) never commits. Return opens the rename field, `hotkey` cmd+a and `type_text` reach it, and the final Return is refused: `press_key delivery failed: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery`. While the field has the focus, Finder reports no `AXFocusedWindow`, so foreground HID delivery re-keys the window and then cannot see it focused. The same happens after `invoke_menu ["File", "Rename"]`.
- What changed: the rename field is an `AXTextField` in its own small WindowServer window whose WindowServer parent is the Finder window; its AX parent is the application and it has no `AXWindow`, so the parent record (`SLSWindowIteratorGetParentID`, read by the new `window_parent_id` in `input/skylight.rs`) is the only link back. When the target app reports **no** focused window and its focused element is such a text field of the target window (`inline_editor_open` in `ax/bindings.rs`), `with_foreground_hid_activation` treats the target window as focused and delivers without re-keying it. A reported focused window is used as before, so a sibling window that holds focus still gets today's handling. Reads use 0.2 s timeouts. The decision is a pure `is_inline_editor` with unit tests.

## Related work

Refs #4615, #4469, #4483. Part (b) (Finder kept in front when the field is opened from behind another app) builds on this.

RFC: not required (no contract, schema, tool-list or result text change).

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. In a logged-in macOS session, create a folder with `draft.txt` and `other.txt` and open it in Finder; open two more Finder windows (Documents, Downloads) so background keys are refused `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`. Bring the folder window to front (`bring_to_front`). `list_windows` gives Finder's `<pid>` and the folder window's `<window_id>`; `get_window_state` on it and `click` the `draft.txt` name cell's `element_token`.
2. On the folder window, each with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "key": "return", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "keys": ["cmd", "a"], "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "text": "final.txt", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "key": "return", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   ```
   (`press_key`, `hotkey`, `type_text`, `press_key`).
3. On main the field opens and keeps the typed name, and the last call is refused:
   ```json
   {"isError": true, "text": "press_key delivery failed: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery"}
   ```
   The folder still holds `draft.txt`. Same with `invoke_menu ["File", "Rename"]` in place of the first Return.

On this branch the last Return is delivered and the folder lists `final.txt`.

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM, Apple Silicon, Finder list view, three Finder windows, Finder relaunched clean and a fresh fixture per run, one MCP connection per run; disk read with `os.listdir` after every call, front app and Finder's focused element polled every 20 ms outside cua-driver. 3 runs per row on each build.

| Case | main ed22ad958 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Keyboard route, Finder in front | **0 of 3** renamed, final Return refused | **3 of 3** renamed |
| Menu route (File > Rename), Finder in front | **0 of 3** renamed, final Return refused | **3 of 3** renamed |
| Keyboard route, TextEdit in front (part (b)'s case) | 0 of 3, every call success | 0 of 3, unchanged (not claimed here) |
| Menu route, TextEdit in front (part (b)'s case) | 0 of 3, every call success | 0 of 3, unchanged |
| Foreground `press_key down` on Finder, TextEdit in front (no field) | TextEdit front again, 3 of 3 (1.15-1.17 s) | same, 3 of 3 (1.17-1.20 s) |
| File > Get Info on Finder, TextEdit in front (no field) | TextEdit front again, 3 of 3 (0.37-0.48 s) | same, 3 of 3 (0.39-0.40 s) |
| Foreground click on a Finder item, TextEdit in front | TextEdit front again, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Foreground `press_key right` on TextEdit, Finder in front | Finder front again, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Foreground `press_key x` on TextEdit's text area by `element_token`, Finder in front | typed, Finder front again, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |

Clip (29 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (Finder left, the MCP calls top right, `ls` of the folder bottom right). Finder is in front. On main the final foreground Return is refused ("exact target window did not become focused") and the folder keeps `draft.txt`; on this branch it is delivered and the folder shows `final.txt`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a09bf87-b977-47b6-9700-3b158fb55a63

## Compatibility and risk

- Scope: foreground HID delivery (`with_foreground_hid_activation`) when the target app reports no focused window. The fallback needs a focused `AXTextField` whose own WindowServer window is a child of exactly the requested window; anything else (another window's child, a field in the window itself, an unreadable role, a failed parent lookup) keeps today's behavior.
- Not Finder-specific: any app whose inline editor has this shape benefits; the proof is structural.
- Cost: one focused-element read and one WindowServer query, only when the app reports no focused window.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

## Validation

- Unit tests (`ax/bindings.rs`): a focused text field in a child window of the target is an inline editor; a field in the window itself, a button in the child, a field in another window's child, an unrelated window, an unknown window, an unreadable role and a failed parent lookup are not.
- Checks: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (457 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`; no clippy warnings in the touched files.
- Known gaps: no AppKit harness e2e (no fixture opens a child-window editor). `get_window_state` still does not list Finder's rename field (it hangs off the application element), so `set_value` on it is not reachable; typing works.

title: ci(release): regenerate files that record the version on cua-sdk release PRs
body:
A cua-sdk Release Please PR bumps only the SDK's version files (\`VERSION\`, pyproject, \`__init__\`, \`package.json\` and its lock). Everything that copies the version kept the old one. After the release merged, main drifted and later PRs went red. It happened for both 0.3.0 (#4539) and 0.3.1 (#4591, #4593).

**What this adds**
- \`.github/workflows/release-sync-generated-files.yml\`, which runs on pushes to \`release-please--branches--main--components--*\`. Today only the cua-sdk job runs. The other components keep their existing sync step in \`release-please.yml\`.
- \`.github/scripts/sync_sdk_release_files.py\`, which runs the commands the drift checks print:
  - \`runner.ts --library\` for every generator that records the SDK version (cua-sdk, cua-sdk-python, cua-sdk-ts, cua-rust, cua-cli, fleet, sandbox);
  - the two hand-written facts that \`test_fleet_docs_version_facts\` checks;
  - \`uv lock --upgrade-package cua\` for each uv.lock whose \`cua\` is the checkout (editable or directory source);
  - \`npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts\` for each package-lock.json that links \`libs/cua/typescript\`. The SDK's own lock is skipped because Release Please bumps it.
  - Nothing else is upgraded. \`--list\` shows the selection: 6 uv locks and 3 npm locks.
- It commits only if something changed and pushes fast-forward with the release GitHub App (\`RELEASE_APP_ID\` / \`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY\`), so the PR's checks re-run.
- A push of the job's own commit is skipped. A run is cancelled when Release Please pushes again.
- The regeneration runs from a checkout with \`persist-credentials: false\`, with no lifecycle scripts. The App token is minted only after the regeneration, for the push.
- Setup mirrors the Check Docs rows for these generators: protoc, Rust 1.97.1, the rustdoc nightly, uv and the docs and TS SDK installs.

**Verified**
- Simulated a 0.3.2 release branch locally by bumping the files Release Please bumps, then ran the script. The diff was 143 files, all of them version-only.
- After that: all 7 generators pass \`--check\`, \`test_fleet_docs_version_facts\` passes, and every uv lock passes \`uv lock --check\`.
- New tests in \`.github/scripts/tests/test_sync_sdk_release_files.py\` (9 tests, passing) cover lock selection, idempotent fact rewriting, loud failure when a fact is missing, the trigger, the loop guard, the token ordering and commit-only-on-change.

title: fix(cua-driver): return from a dom_event click when its handler opens a dialog
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on a driver-owned isolated browser, no `browser_click` route could activate an element whose handler opens a page-owned JavaScript dialog. `trusted` refuses by design. `dom_event` dispatched `this.click()` through `Runtime.callFunctionOn` and awaited the reply, but `confirm()` blocks the JS frame that call is waiting on, so the click sat through the 20 s call timeout. The blocked frame then also wedged the follow-up `browser_dialog`, whose own `Page.enable` timed out, so the dialog was unreachable rather than merely unresolved.
- What changed: before a `dom_event` click goes out, Page events are enabled on the tab session and the dialog session is registered, the same way `browser_dialog` does it. The click is then raced against the `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` event. When a dialog opens, the call returns at once with `status: "ok"`, `effect: "unverifiable"`, and a `dialog` block (`present`, `kind`, `dialog_id`) whose id `browser_dialog` accepts directly; the summary names the id as well. The reply to the click, which only arrives once the dialog is resolved, is dropped harmlessly. A `browser_click` sent while a dialog is already open is refused with `browser_action_unavailable` before any frame revalidation, so it no longer waits out `Page.getFrameTree` against the blocked renderer. A quiet click returns `dialog: {present: false}` and is otherwise unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #3982

RFC: not required. No new tool, parameter, or refusal code. The dialog block is an addition to the existing `browser_click` payload, and the `ActionResult` envelope is unchanged (its summary carries the dialog id).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: shared CDP code in `cua-driver-core`, same on macOS, Linux, and Windows. `Page.enable` is already in the reviewed existing-profile command set. A `dom_event` click now sends one `Page.enable` on first use per tab; later calls see the registered session and skip it.
- Risk and rollback: if `Page.enable` fails, the click proceeds exactly as before. The race polls dialog state every 25 ms and otherwise waits for the reply as today, so a click that opens no dialog has the same timing. Revert the two fix commits to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked` (three new mock-CDP cases in `v2_tests.rs`: a click whose reply never arrives but whose dialog event does, a quiet click, and a click while a dialog is open; the mock gained a reply mode that emits events and never answers), `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test --locked`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS 26, Apple Silicon, Google Chrome launched by `browser_prepare` (`allow_launch: true`, `isolated_new`) through `cua-driver mcp --direct` built from `9f1b7bd01`, against the two-button fixture from the report (a quiet button and one whose handler calls `confirm('Delete?')` and writes the outcome into the page):

  | Step | Before (report, 0.28.2) | After |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | quiet button, dom_event | ok, 1439 ms | ok, 64 ms, page shows "quiet clicked" |
  | confirm button, trusted | refused | refused `browser_input_trust_unavailable` (unchanged) |
  | confirm button, dom_event | timeout after 21268 ms | ok in 61 ms, summary names `dialog-1`, `dialog.present: true` |
  | second dom_event click while open | n/a | refused `browser_action_unavailable` in 98 ms |
  | `browser_dialog inspect` | Page.enable timed out | "confirm dialog is open", 35 ms |
  | `browser_dialog accept dialog-1` | unreachable | accepted; page shows "confirm accepted" |
  | click again, then `dismiss dialog-2` | unreachable | dismissed; page shows "confirm dismissed" |

- Known gaps or CI still required: not run on Linux or Windows hosts; the changed code has no platform branch. The generated MCP reference pages are refreshed by the docs workflow after merge.
