title: [Bug]: macOS background click on a Mac Catalyst pop-up menu item is refused `element_outside_target_window`, and the menu left open swallows the next click
body:
**Primary area:** Cua Driver

### Summary
In a Mac Catalyst app, a `UIButton` pop-up (`showsMenuAsPrimaryAction`) opens its menu in its own WindowServer window. A background `click` on the pop-up opens the menu, and `get_window_state` of the app's window lists the menu items with element tokens. A background `click` on any of those items is refused `element_outside_target_window`, with the advice to take a fresh snapshot and re-address it; a fresh snapshot gives the same refusal. The app keeps its old value and the menu stays open. The next background click on the window (here Save) then reports "Performed AXPress", but it only closes the menu: the button never acts.

### Reproduction
1. A Catalyst app with a pop-up button: here a form with a "Digest" pop-up (Never, Daily, Weekly, Monthly; Daily chosen) and a Save button. Launch it in the background.
2. `list_windows` gives `<pid>` and `<window_id>`; `get_window_state` on that window.
3. `click` the pop-up (the `AXButton` labelled "Daily"):
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "element_token": "<Daily button token>"}
   ```
4. `get_window_state` again; it lists an `AXMenuItem` "Weekly" with a token. `click` it:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "element_token": "<Weekly item token>"}
   ```
5. `click` the Save button's token the same way.
6. Read the app's own state and WindowServer's on-screen windows of the app (layer 101 is a menu).

Reproduced 5 of 5 on main `f83bd7a5c`, the app relaunched clean each run.

### Expected behavior
The item is picked (the pop-up shows Weekly, the menu closes) and Save then saves. Or, if the click cannot be proven to belong to the window, the refusal says the menu is still open.

### Actual behavior
Step 3: `✅ Performed AXPress on [16] AXButton "".`, the menu opens. Step 4, every run:

```json
{"code": "element_outside_target_window", "effect": "refused",
 "reason": "the addressed element could not be proven to belong to window <window_id>; take a fresh get_window_state snapshot and re-address it"}
```

The app still holds Daily and one layer-101 window of the app stays on screen. A fresh snapshot and the same click: refused again (5/5). Step 5 returns `✅ Performed AXPress on [17] AXButton "".` and the menu closes, but the app saved nothing (5/5).

Cause: `ax/exact_target.rs` `element_window_id` ties an element to a window through `AXWindow` or an `AXParent` walk up to an `AXWindow`/`AXSheet`. Read with a separate AX probe: the item's parent is the `AXMenu`, the `AXMenu` has no readable `AXParent`, neither has `AXWindow`, and `_AXUIElementGetWindow` fails on both. So `gather_background_facts` returns `Unproven`. AX does link the menu downward: the window's root `AXGroup` lists the `AXMenu` among its children, which is how `get_window_state` finds the items. AppKit pop-ups are not affected (their menu's parent is the button). #4507 handles sheets and does not cover this.

Other routes on main (3 runs each): `click` with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` on the item token works (the foreground element path is not exact-target gated). `set_value "Weekly"` on the pop-up reports "Sent (unverified)" and changes nothing. Background `press_key` down, return picks "Never", not the item after Daily. Foreground keys close the menu when the window is fronted. A pixel click on the item's centre, background or foreground, closes the menu without picking.

### Environment
- cua-driver 0.33.2, trycua/cua main `f83bd7a5c` (Oct 4, 2026); first seen on `2400bbefd`
- macOS 26.4, Apple Silicon (VirtualMac2,1)

### Evidence
Attached clip (40 s). Same steps and layout in both runs: the app on the left, the MCP calls and their results on the right, the app's own state (its digest, whether a menu window is on screen, what Save wrote) read ten times a second outside cua-driver at the bottom left. On main it zooms in on the item click, highlights the refusal, shows the menu still open and the Save click reporting success with nothing saved. The second run is the same steps on the branch from the PR below. It ends on a side-by-side card.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6e30900-4cd1-4ca3-b6a1-7a3ee18a49c6

### Workaround and additional context
- Workaround on main: click the item with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.
- A PR is ready: when an item's parent chain ends at an `AXMenu` with no parent, the target window's own AX subtree is searched (bounded) for that menu, and a semantic AX action on the item is admitted when it is there. A refusal of such an item while a menu of the app is on screen says so and recommends the foreground click. Before/after: 0/5 to 5/5, and Save lands 5/5.
- Related: #3792 / #3793 (menu bar rows refused the same way; a different surface), #4507 (sheets), #4484 (closing a menu a failed `invoke_menu` opened).

### Submission checks
- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): say when a refused Catalyst menu item leaves its menu open
body:
## Summary

This PR was narrowed to the refusal note only; the structural proof that admits these items in the background follows as a separate PR once this one lands, and that one will close #4619.

- Problem this solves: in a Mac Catalyst app, a background `click` on a pop-up menu item is refused `element_outside_target_window` with the advice to take a fresh `get_window_state` snapshot, while the menu stays open. Following that advice is refused again, and the next background click on the window then only closes the menu while reporting success. The refusal does not say that the menu is still open, or that the foreground route (which picks the item) exists.
- What changed: when the refused element is an `AXMenuItem` whose `AXMenu` has no readable `AXParent` (the shape of a Catalyst pop-up's menu, which is its own WindowServer window and names no window) and a menu window of the app (WindowServer layer 101, the helper from #4484) is on screen, the refusal now says so and recommends `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, in the reason text and in `escalation.recommended`:

  ```
  click: Background input refused (element_outside_target_window): the addressed element could not be proven to belong to window <id>; take a fresh get_window_state snapshot and re-address it. It is an item of a menu that names no window, and a menu of this app is still on screen; click this item with delivery_mode "foreground" to pick it
  ```

  Admission is unchanged: every action that was refused is still refused.

## Related work

Refs #4619. Part (b), the structural proof that admits these items for semantic AX actions, builds on this. Related: #3792 / #3793 (menu bar rows), #4507 (sheets), #4484.

RFC: not required (one sentence appended to an existing refusal and an existing `escalation.recommended` value).

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Launch a Catalyst app with a `UIButton` pop-up (`showsMenuAsPrimaryAction`; items Never, Daily, Weekly, Monthly; Daily chosen) and a Save button, in the background. `list_windows` gives `<pid>` and `<window_id>`.
2. `get_window_state` on that window, then `click` the pop-up by its token. A layer-101 window of the app appears.
3. `get_window_state` again, then `click` the "Weekly" `AXMenuItem` by its token.
4. On main: refused `element_outside_target_window`, `escalation.recommended: "get_window_state"`, nothing about the open menu; a fresh snapshot and retry is refused the same way. On this branch: the same refusal with the sentence above and `escalation.recommended: "foreground"`. `click` on the same token with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` picks Weekly (unchanged, works on main too).

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM, Apple Silicon, the lab's CatalystProfile app relaunched clean each run, one MCP connection per run. App state read outside cua-driver (the app's own state file, WindowServer's window list). 3 runs per row on each build.

| Case | main b0a634813 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Background click pop-up, then background click "Weekly" | refused, recommends `get_window_state`, menu left open, 3 of 3; retry refused the same way | refused, **says the menu is open and recommends `foreground`**, 3 of 3 (retry likewise); app state unchanged (Daily) |
| Then background click Save | "Performed AXPress", nothing saved (it only closed the menu), 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 (admission unchanged) |
| Menu opened outside cua, background click "Weekly" | refused, no note, 3 of 3 | refused with the note, 3 of 3 |
| `scroll` by the item's token (a pointer route) while its menu is open | refused, no note, 3 of 3 | refused with the note, 3 of 3 |
| Following the note: `click` "Weekly" with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` | picks Weekly (Oct 4 main f83bd7a5c, 3 of 3; unchanged code path) | picks Weekly, menu closed, 3 of 3 |
| Control: AppKit pop-up in TextEdit's Save sheet, click it, click "Unicode (UTF-16)" | picked, 3 of 3 | picked, 3 of 3 |
| Control: TextEdit menu bar row by token (#3792) | refused, no note, no menu left, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Control: element token of one TextEdit window clicked with the other window's id | refused `conflicting_element_target`, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Control: `invoke_menu ["File","Nope"]` (#4484) | refused, no menu left, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |

Clip (30 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (CatalystProfile left, the MCP calls right). On main the background click on "Weekly" is refused with only the fresh-snapshot advice, a retry is refused the same way, and the menu stays open. On this branch the refusal says the menu is still open and recommends foreground; following it picks Weekly.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93acb948-3dad-4c38-bd06-88a141299233

## Compatibility and risk

- Scope: only refusals with code `element_outside_target_window` for an `AXMenuItem` whose `AXMenu` has no readable parent, while a layer-101 window of the same pid is on screen. Other refusals are unchanged.
- The recommended route is the existing foreground element path, which is not exact-target gated; the note does not prove the item belongs to the window, it states what is on screen.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

## Validation

- Unit test `only_items_of_a_menu_with_no_parent_qualify` (`ax/exact_target.rs`): the measured Catalyst shape qualifies; an AppKit pop-up's menu (parent is the button), a menu under the application, the menu itself, a non-item and an unreadable role do not.
- Checks: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (481 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`; no clippy warnings in the touched files.
- Known gaps: no harness e2e (the fixture's menus have AX parents, so they never reach this path). Submenus of such a menu are not covered (no measured case).

title: Daemon spawns agent harness on host instead of in sandbox (ENOENT on /home/cua/.cua/tools)
body:
## Bug

`cua agent tell` (daemon mode) fails to start any harness with:

```
[error] could not start the agent: spawn /home/cua/.cua/tools/pi/0.87.1/node_modules/pi-acp/dist/index.js ENOENT
```

## Root cause

The daemon installs harness tools correctly **inside the sandbox** at `/home/cua/.cua/tools/` (verified: files exist, are executable, and run manually via `cua do shell`).

But when spawning the agent, the daemon uses Node `child_process.spawn()` with the **sandbox-internal path** on the **host**. The Mac host has no `/home/cua/` (`/home` is a symlink to the read-only system volume), so spawn fails with ENOENT.

The daemon process runs as the Mac user with `HOME=/Users/rook`, yet constructs the hardcoded sandbox path `/home/cua/.cua/tools` instead of either:
1. Spawning via the sandbox exec API (like `--embedded` mode does), or
2. Using a host-accessible tools path

## Workaround

`cua agent run --embedded` works correctly — the harness spawns, connects to the model, and uses sandbox MCP tools. Only daemon-mode (`tell` / persistent agents) is broken.

## Repro

1. `cua agent create combo --harness pi --in local:chrome-space --model <model> --base-url <url>`
2. `cua agent tell combo "test"`
3. Observe ENOENT in `cua agent logs`

## Environment

- cua 0.3.1 (CLI), cua-spacesd 0.5.0 (daemon)
- Mac host (arm64), Linux sandbox (gVisor, ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04)
- Happens with pi and opencode harnesses

title: fix(cua-driver): report macOS 27 browser profile denials
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS 27, attaching to an existing Chrome profile through the daemon (`browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile`) refuses with `could not read the browser's DevToolsActivePort file: Operation not permitted (os error 1)` and doesn't say why (#4275). macOS 27 blocks reads of the Chrome and Edge profile folders for apps without Full Disk Access or a per-app grant, root and LaunchAgents included ([write-up](https://wojciechregula.blog/post/golden-gate-appdata-protection/)). On the tested machine a LaunchAgent got `EPERM` there while the direct runtime could read the folder. `EPERM`, unlike a mode-bit `EACCES`, points at this protection without proving it, so the new hint names the likely cause. The same denial hits `page` `enable_javascript_apple_events`, which quits the browser, patches nothing, relaunches it and reports success.
- What changed:
  - An `EPERM` read of `DevToolsActivePort` still refuses with `browser_route_unavailable` and the old message, followed by the likely cause and the two fixes: Full Disk Access for CuaDriver.app, or `cua-driver mcp --direct` from an app that has it. `detail` carries `resource`, `os_error` and `hint`, like the descriptor-exhaustion refusal. Every other read error is unchanged.
  - `enable_javascript_apple_events` now lists the `Preferences` files before it quits the browser. If the folder can't be read, has no profiles or doesn't exist for the bundle (Safari), it errors and the browser keeps running. Before, Safari was quit and never relaunched. If no file gets patched after the quit, it errors after relaunching.
  - The browsers guide gets a short macOS 27 note.

## Related work

Refs #4275

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. Same refusal code; `detail` is additive, as on the descriptor-exhaustion refusal.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Callers that branch on `browser_route_unavailable` see no change; only `EPERM` gets the longer message and `detail`. `enable_javascript_apple_events` is a legacy mutation behind `CUA_DRIVER_ENABLE_LEGACY_PAGE_MUTATIONS=1`; where it used to report success without changing anything, it now errors. Windows and Linux read `DevToolsActivePort` in their own adapters and have no such protection, so they're untouched.
- Risk and rollback: the refusal code stays the same, but `EPERM` adds guidance and detail. The legacy page command now fails before quitting when it cannot find profile files, and fails after relaunch when no file was patched. Those command paths have not been driven live. Revert the commit to restore the prior behavior.

## Validation

Candidate: `28e3b811e`, which merges current main (`56725dd7e`) into the branch. The only conflict was the `DevToolsActivePort` read error, which main now builds inline with `BrowserRefusal::new` (#5963); the refusal helper here now uses `BrowserRefusal::new` as well. The hint and the guide say Full Disk Access or a per-app grant, as #4275 found.

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib -- devtools_active_port_read_refusal apple_events_targets patching_counts`: 4 passed. Against the unfixed code, 2 of them fail: no Full Disk Access text on the `EPERM` refusal, and an empty profiles folder returns `Ok(("Google Chrome", []))`. Mutation check: swallowing the `read_dir` error again, or counting failed patches, fails the matching test.
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib`: 642 passed, 7 ignored.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon. A one-shot LaunchAgent without Full Disk Access:

  ```text
  DENY list ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome: Operation not permitted
  DENY read ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/DevToolsActivePort: Operation not permitted
  OK   list ~/Library/Application Support/Google
  ```

  The daemon refusal before the change is in #4275. The refusal builder now turns that `EPERM` into:

  ```text
  could not read the browser's DevToolsActivePort file: Operation not permitted (os error 1); on macOS 27 and later, reading this browser's profile folder needs Full Disk Access or a per-app grant; grant Full Disk Access to CuaDriver.app and restart the daemon, or attach from `cua-driver mcp --direct` in an app that has it
  ```

- Known gaps or CI still required: canonical desktop E2E was not run. The daemon now has Full Disk Access, so the refusal text shown here comes from the refusal builder, not a denied live `browser_prepare` call. The tests cover profile discovery, refusal construction and patch counts; they do not exercise the page command's quit and relaunch sequence. Current-head macOS and docs workflows await maintainer approval. The wording choice between Full Disk Access and `--direct`, raised on #4275, is still open.

title: [Bug]: macOS background pixel clicks reach the app but never the custom-drawn view under them
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, a background pixel `click` on a view with no accessibility element (a custom-drawn `NSView`) reaches the app but never the view. The posted events carry the right screen location, but AppKit sets their `locationInWindow` from the stamped window location, and the background route stamps the screen point there. The press then sits outside the window and hit testing finds no view. Every call reports `route: "synthetic_events"` with `effect: "unverifiable"`.

### Reproduction

1. Run a window whose content is one custom view that logs presses:

   ```swift
   import AppKit

   final class Receiver: NSView {
       override func acceptsFirstMouse(for event: NSEvent?) -> Bool { true }
       override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
           NSColor.systemTeal.setFill()
           bounds.fill()
       }
       override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
           NSLog("mouseDown locationInWindow=%@", NSStringFromPoint(event.locationInWindow))
       }
   }

   let app = NSApplication.shared
   app.setActivationPolicy(.regular)
   let window = NSWindow(contentRect: NSRect(x: 200, y: 200, width: 760, height: 380),
                         styleMask: [.titled], backing: .buffered, defer: false)
   window.contentView = Receiver()
   window.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
   app.run()
   ```

   `swiftc receiver.swift -o receiver && ./receiver`, then bring another app to the front.
2. `list_windows` for its pid, then `get_window_state` on the window.
3. `click` the middle of the teal area in screenshot pixels, for example at a screenshot scale of 1:

   ```json
   {"target": {"kind": "window", "pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>}, "x": 380, "y": 222, "session": "s"}
   ```

3 of 3 clicks reproduce it.

### Expected behavior

The receiver logs a `mouseDown` for each click, at `locationInWindow` (380, 190).

### Actual behavior

Nothing is logged. A second probe app that also records every event reaching the app (an `NSEvent` local monitor) shows the clicks do arrive, with the right screen location but the screen point read as a window point:

```text
window frame, top-left origin      x -3300, y 1177, 760 by 412
press requested at window point    (130, 222)
CGEvent location of the press      (-3170, 1399)
NSEvent.locationInWindow           (-3170, -987)   (screen x, 412 minus screen y)
expected locationInWindow          (130, 190)
```

So only a window whose top-left corner sits at the screen origin would get these clicks.

### Environment

Cua Driver 0.33.3 release app, daemon from its LaunchAgent. Also a debug build of main `2b3e4e548` run in-process with `cua-driver mcp --direct`. macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon. The target window was on a second display to the left of the built-in one, with another app in front.

### Evidence

`chromium_click_route_plan` receives the window-local point, discards it (`let _ = (win_local_x, win_local_y);`) and stamps the screen point on the move, press and release:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/input/mouse.rs#L482-L555

Before 681bc44807d1be81a4357f8e158f1c74a81d5a5b (2026-09-22, first released in 0.28.3) the same function stamped the window-local point, and the foreground route still does:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/input/mouse.rs#L290-L313

Presses that reached a custom view under the point, background `click`, same window:

| Build | Reached the view |
| --- | --- |
| 0.33.3 release | 0 of 6 |
| main `2b3e4e548`, debug, `mcp --direct` | 0 of 20 |
| main with the window-local stamp restored | 23 of 23 |

Chrome is not affected: a full-window canvas page got 10 of 10 at the right point with either stamp.

### Workaround and additional context

- No background workaround. `delivery_mode: "foreground"` stamps the window-local point but fronts the window and moves the pointer (not tried here).
- A fix that restores the window-local stamp is ready; PR to follow.

title: fix(cua-driver): let background pixel clicks reach custom-drawn macOS views
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, background pixel clicks on a view with no accessibility element never reach the view (#4631). `chromium_click_route_plan` stamps the screen point through `CGEventSetWindowLocation`, and AppKit takes that stamp as the window-local point, so the press lands outside any window whose top-left corner is not at the screen origin.
- What changed: the move, press and release now stamp the window-local point the plan already receives, as this route did before 681bc4480 and as the foreground route does. The off-screen primer keeps (-1, -1). The doc comments said macOS reads the stamp in screen space; they now say what AppKit does with it. `capture_bound_background_route_preserves_nonzero_origin_hit` modeled the receiver as subtracting the window origin from the stamp; it now asserts the window-local stamp for the same nonzero-origin window.

## Related work

Fixes #4631

Refs #5389, #5425. Both change the same background window-location stamp. This PR keeps the existing transport choice and uses the window-local point on both routes, which matches the smaller approach the review of #5389 asked for. #5425 limits the change to macOS 27; this PR changes earlier versions too, but has no macOS 26 run, so that compatibility question remains open.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change):
Not required. No schema, CLI or MCP change; background pixel clicks land where the existing `click` contract says.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Background pixel clicks that reach the app as posted events, such as clicks on custom-drawn views, now land at the requested point. Chrome got the same result with either stamp in the run below. Windows and Linux are untouched.
- Risk and rollback: an OS version that reads this stamp as a screen point would miss with this change. The route stamped the window-local point through 0.28.2, and the foreground route does today. Revert to roll back.

## Validation

Candidate: `906176f7f`.

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p platform-macos --locked --lib`: 442 passed, 6 ignored. The rewritten `capture_bound_background_route_preserves_nonzero_origin_hit` fails on main (the plan stamps (564, 504) where the test expects (394, 310)) and passes here.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check` and `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`: clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon. Background `click` on the same window, on a second display (window origin -3300, 1177), with another app in front: the 0.33.3 release through its daemon, and debug builds of main `2b3e4e548` and this branch through `cua-driver mcp --direct`. The views logged what they received.

  | Target | 0.33.3 release | main | this branch |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Custom view, `acceptsFirstMouse` false | 0 of 2 | 0 of 10 | 10 of 10 |
  | Custom view, `acceptsFirstMouse` true | 0 of 1 | 0 of 10 | 10 of 10 |
  | Receiver from #4631 | 0 of 3 | not run | 3 of 3 |
  | `locationInWindow` of a press at window point (130, 222) | (-3170, -987) | (-3170, -987) | (130, 190) |
  | Chrome, full-window canvas, at its center | not run | 10 of 10 | 10 of 10 |

- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - macOS 26 was not run. The change affects that version too; #5425 takes the narrower macOS 27 only approach.
  - The canonical AppKit harness was not run. `harness_appkit_double_click_px_background` posts through this route.
  - The native comparison used main `2b3e4e548` and candidate `906176f7f`; it has not been repeated against current main.
  - Off-center points on the Chrome canvas land on its center with both builds (#4350), so Chrome delivery away from an element's center is not covered.
  - Earlier macOS unit and release-metadata checks passed on this head. Later workflows need maintainer approval, and this head has no result from the newly required `ci-gate`.

title: [Bug]: macOS cua-driver mcp starts a standard-mode daemon while the LaunchAgent reloads
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `cua-driver mcp` starts its own daemon with `open -n -g -a CuaDriver --args serve` whenever the socket is down, even when the LaunchAgent from the operate guide manages the daemon. An MCP client that starts during the guide's unload and load step gets a daemon in `standard` mode, and the agent's own daemon then exits with "already running" on every respawn. On Linux and Windows the same path tries the managed service first.

### Reproduction

1. Install the LaunchAgent from the operate guide with mode flags after `serve` (here `--permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals`).
2. `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.trycua.cua-driver` (the guide's unload).
3. Start any MCP client of the stock binary; here, one `initialize` request to `cua-driver mcp`.
4. `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.trycua.cua-driver.plist` (the guide's load).
5. `cua-driver status`.

1 of 1 deliberate runs. I first hit it by accident on 0.28.2 while reloading the agent.

### Expected behavior

The pinned mode survives: the client restarts the managed agent, as the systemd and scheduled task paths try to, or refuses and says to start it. The operate guide says "A bad configuration fails startup instead of falling back to `standard`."

### Actual behavior

```text
 0.0 s  status: pid 30110, permission mode: unrestricted (trusted_startup_configuration)
 2.1 s  after bootout: Cua Driver daemon is not running
 2.6 s  cua-driver mcp answers initialize
        status: pid 28513, permission mode: standard (built_in_default)
        ps: 28513, ppid 1, /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve
 7.7 s  after bootstrap: still pid 28513, standard (built_in_default)
        launchctl print: state = spawn scheduled, last exit code = 1
        agent stderr: Cua Driver daemon is already running on .../cua-driver.sock (pid 28513)
```

The agent keeps respawning and exiting until the other daemon is stopped.

### Environment

Cua Driver 0.33.3 release app. LaunchAgent `com.trycua.cua-driver` as in the operate guide, plus mode flags. macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon.

### Evidence

The macOS `launch_daemon_with_state_and_wait` ignores `_allow_managed_restart` and always opens the app with a bare `serve`:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs#L1313-L1319

The Linux and Windows version tries `restart_managed_daemon_if_present` first:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs#L1421-L1437

### Workaround and additional context

`cua-driver stop`, then `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.trycua.cua-driver`.

One open question for a fix is the label: the operate guide's agent is `com.trycua.cua-driver`, while #2196 and #2990 use `com.trycua.driver`.

title: [Bug]: set_window_frame and invoke_menu can't find an off-Space window that get_window_state resolves
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `get_window_state` resolves an AppKit window on another Space through the off-Space probe from #4068 and #4085, but `set_window_frame` and `invoke_menu` can't find that same window. They look it up with `copy_ax_windows`, which has nothing for an app whose windows are all off the current Space.

### Reproduction

1. Open a TextEdit document on a desktop Space, then switch to another Space (here a fullscreen app), so TextEdit has no window on the current Space.
2. `get_window_state` on the TextEdit window.
3. `set_window_frame` on it, same size, moved 40 pt.
4. `invoke_menu` on it with `["Edit", "Select All"]`.

### Expected behavior

`set_window_frame` and `invoke_menu` act on the window `get_window_state` just resolved, or refuse with an off-Space reason.

### Actual behavior

```text
list_windows:     window 34189, space_ids [6], on_current_space false (current Space 1239)
get_window_state: exact_window matched, 169 elements, AXWindow frame 656x422 at 218,84
set_window_frame: exit 1, "set_window_frame: window_id 34189 belongs to pid 34255 in WindowServer but has no matching AXWindow"
invoke_menu:      refused, menu_path_unavailable, "invoke_menu: target accessibility window is unavailable"
```

With the window on the current Space, both tools find it. (Stage Manager is on here, so `set_window_frame` then reported `suspected_noop` for a window in the strip; that part is separate.)

### Environment

Cua Driver 0.33.3 release app, called through `cua-driver call`. macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon, Stage Manager on. TextEdit.

### Evidence

`get_window_state` gets the window through `copy_ax_windows_including`, which adds the probe:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs#L346

`set_window_frame` and `invoke_menu` use `copy_ax_windows`:
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/set_window_frame.rs#L208
https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/2b3e4e548c6d27f918f5367f84c094151aa10c8f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/invoke_menu.rs#L319

### Workaround and additional context

Bring the window onto the current Space first. Refs #3458.

Not the helper-window case from #4525: #4534 drops AX-less helper windows from `list_windows` and keeps windows on another Space. This one is titled, sits on Space 6 and `get_window_state` resolves it with 169 elements.

title: fix(cua-driver): send AXEnhancedUserInterface only to Chromium and Electron apps
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, one read-only `get_window_state` of a native app (TextEdit, Calculator, Stocks) turns on that app's `AXEnhancedUserInterface`, the legacy flag that tells an app a screen reader is attached. It stays on for the rest of the app's life. The walker's Chromium opt-in (`ensure_chromium_ax_enabled`, which runs for every app) writes `AXManualAccessibility` first and falls back to `AXEnhancedUserInterface` whenever the modern attribute is unsupported. Native AppKit and Catalyst apps reject the modern attribute but accept the legacy one, so they get it. The same opt-in also runs before background input (`gather_background_facts`).
- What changed: the legacy fallback is written only when the app is Chromium-family by name or bundle id (the existing `browser::platform::is_chromium` list) or its bundle carries `Contents/Frameworks/Electron Framework.framework`. The check runs only when `AXManualAccessibility` was refused as unsupported, so apps that accept the modern attribute pay nothing. A native app now gets a new `AccessibilityOptIn::NotNeeded` outcome, which is cached for its process lifetime like a completed opt-in, so later walks skip it. Chromium and Electron keep today's behavior exactly, including Chrome, which answers `AXManualAccessibility` as unsupported and relies on the legacy fallback.

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Save this probe as `eui.swift` (it reads the app-level attribute outside cua-driver; the terminal needs Accessibility permission):
   ```swift
   import ApplicationServices
   let app = AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid_t(CommandLine.arguments[1])!)
   var value: AnyObject?
   let err = AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue(app, "AXEnhancedUserInterface" as CFString, &value)
   print("AXEnhancedUserInterface:", err == .success ? "\(value as! Bool)" : "error \(err.rawValue)")
   ```
2. Launch TextEdit fresh with a document open. `list_windows` gives its `<pid>` and `<window_id>`. `swift eui.swift <pid>` prints `false`.
3. Read the window once:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "include_screenshot": false}
   ```
4. `swift eui.swift <pid>` again.

On main, step 4 prints `true`; Calculator and Stocks behave the same. On this branch it prints `false`, and the snapshot in step 3 is the same.

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM (Apple Silicon). Each app freshly launched per run; the attribute read by a separate AX probe running in the GUI session (not through cua-driver).

| Case | main 2b3e4e548 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| TextEdit, `AXEnhancedUserInterface` before -> after one `get_window_state` | **0 -> 1**, 3 of 3 | **0 -> 0**, 3 of 3 |
| Calculator | **0 -> 1**, 3 of 3 | **0 -> 0**, 3 of 3 |
| Stocks | **0 -> 1**, 3 of 3 | **0 -> 0**, 3 of 3 |
| Snapshot size (elements: TextEdit / Calculator / Stocks) | 269 / 163 / 190 | 269 / 163 / 192 (Stocks' news list varies) |
| Chrome (driver-owned isolated profile, local test page): `AXManualAccessibility` unsupported, so legacy opt-in | 0 -> 1; page heading and button in the tree on the second snapshot, 2 of 2 | 0 -> 1; same page elements on the second snapshot, 2 of 2 (unchanged) |
| Electron fixture (`CuaTestHarness.Electron`) | 250 elements, `AXWebArea` present, legacy flag stays 0, 2 of 2 | same, 2 of 2 |

Clip (22 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (the three apps left, the MCP calls top right, the outside probe's live reading bottom right), with a punch-in on the calls and the values, ending on a side-by-side frame.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99047e6a-2e1b-456e-b7de-7bb8e99a4890

## Related work

No existing issue for macOS. Same class of side effect as #2010 on Linux (an accessibility opt-in meant for Chromium switched on screen-reader behavior for everything).

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. Internal macOS behavior only; `AccessibilityOptIn` is a crate-internal enum; no schema, contract or binding change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Native apps are no longer switched into screen-reader mode by reads or background actions. Chromium and Electron are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: an app that needs the legacy flag to build its tree but is neither on the Chromium name list nor bundles Electron Framework (for example a CEF app that also rejects `AXManualAccessibility`) would no longer get it. Rollback is reverting the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `enhanced_user_interface_is_written_only_for_chromium_family_apps` (`bindings.rs`): with an injected attribute setter, a native app (modern attribute unsupported, not Chromium) gets only the `AXManualAccessibility` write and `NotNeeded`; a Chromium/Electron app still gets the legacy write; success and transient errors are unchanged.
  - `electron_is_recognised_by_the_framework_in_its_bundle` (`apps/mod.rs`): a bundle-shaped temp dir with and without `Electron Framework.framework`; the test runner itself is not Electron.
  - `only_the_manual_accessibility_path_polls_for_web_content` (`enablement.rs`) now also checks that `NotNeeded` completes without polling.
  - `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (444 passed, 6 ignored), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`.
- Manual or platform evidence: the table and clip above.
- Known gaps or CI still required: no Electron build that rejects `AXManualAccessibility` was available, so the legacy path for Electron is covered by the unit test, and in the VM by Chrome (which takes that path).

title: fix(cua-driver): count a macOS AXOpen that replaced its own element
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: opening a Finder folder by element reports an error after it worked. `double_click` on a folder icon's `element_token` returns `isError: true`, `double_click failed: AXOpen returned -25205 for element [3]; background delivery will not improvise a pointer fallback after choosing the semantic route`, and `click` with `action: "open"` returns `AX action failed: AXUIElementPerformAction(AXOpen) returned -25205`, while the window has already navigated into the folder. Finder's AXOpen replaces the window's contents, destroying the icon it was performed on, and the action call then returns -25205. The agent is told the open failed, so it retries or falls back to pixels. With `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, `double_click` goes on to its pixel fallback for an icon that no longer exists (`Cannot resolve screen center for element [3]`, or, when a new item sits where the icon was, a second double-click that opens it).
- What changed: for an AXOpen the element advertises (`click` with `action: "open"`, and `double_click`'s AXOpen route), the driver reads the element's window title right before the action. If the action returns -25205 (`kAXErrorAttributeUnsupported`, the error measured here), it polls for up to 800 ms with 100 ms reads. When the element no longer exists (`kAXErrorInvalidUIElement` on a read) and the window's title has moved away from the one read before, the open is reported as performed with `effect: "unverifiable"`, naming the AX error and both titles:

  ```
  ✅ Performed AXOpen on [3] AXImage "old"; the element no longer exists and the window title is now "old" (was "findme"), although the app returned AX error -25205. Take a fresh snapshot before acting again.
  ```

  Every other case keeps today's error: another error code (a stale handle's -25202 included), an element that does not advertise AXOpen, the element still existing, an unchanged title, or no readable title before the action. The check runs before `double_click`'s foreground pixel fallback, so a replaced element no longer gets an improvised double-click.

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Make a folder with a subfolder and open it in Finder, icon view:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p ~/findme/old/2023 ~/findme/old/2024 ~/findme/Important && echo r > ~/findme/readme.txt && open ~/findme
   ```
2. `list_windows` gives Finder's `<pid>` and the `findme` window's `<window_id>`. `get_window_state` on it; the folder is `[3] AXImage "old"`.
3. Open it by element, background:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "element_token": "<token of [3]>"}
   ```
   with `double_click`. Then `list_windows`: the same window is now titled `old`.
4. Repeat steps 1-3 with `click` and `{"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "element_token": "<token>", "action": "open"}`.

On main both calls return `isError: true` (-25205) while the window shows `old`. On this branch both return the performed text above with `effect: "unverifiable"`.

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM (Apple Silicon). Finder relaunched with a fresh `findme` folder for every call; window titles read from `list_windows` (WindowServer). 3 runs per row on each build.

| Case | main ed22ad958 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `double_click` folder "old" by token (background) | **`isError: true`** (-25205), 3 of 3; window `old` | **performed**, `effect: "unverifiable"`, 3 of 3; window `old`; returns in 0.03-0.06 s |
| `click` `action: "open"` on the same folder | **`isError: true`** (-25205), 3 of 3; window `old` | **performed**, `effect: "unverifiable"`, 3 of 3; window `old` |
| `double_click` with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` | **`isError: true`**, 3 of 3: the pixel fallback ran after the error and failed with `Cannot resolve screen center for element [3]`; window `old` | performed, 3 of 3; window `old`; no pixel fallback |
| Control: `click` `action: "open"` on TextEdit's text area (AXOpen not advertised; fails, element stays) | `isError: true` (-25205), 3 of 3, 1.06-1.12 s | `isError: true` (-25205), 3 of 3, 1.06-1.09 s (no poll: the action is not advertised) |
| Control (#4485): Finder toolbar "list view" radio pressed by token | `effect: "confirmed"`, radio 0 -> 1, list outline appears, 3 of 3 | unchanged, 3 of 3 |

Clip (21 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (Finder window left, the MCP calls right), with the focus moving to the result and on the window that opened `old`, ending on a side-by-side frame.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69b0799a-e513-4e9a-a906-ee612e90be58

## Related work

Refs #3835 (closed). Same shape as #4485, which counts an erroring toggle press only when the control's own value shows it; here the evidence is that the element is gone and its window changed. #3836 (open) proposes reporting -25200/-25205/-25206 from presses as dispatched in general; it keeps non-press actions such as AXOpen failing and does not touch `double_click`, so it does not cover this case, and this change does not depend on it.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. The result uses existing `effect` values; no schema, contract or binding change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS `click` (`action: "open"`) and `double_click` by element. A call that used to error now succeeds, only when an advertised AXOpen returned -25205, the element disappeared and its window's title changed, all within 800 ms.
- Risk and rollback: a false success needs the element to vanish and the window title to change in that window for another reason during those 800 ms. Cost: an advertised AXOpen that returns -25205 and leaves its element in place now waits up to 800 ms more before the error. Every advertised AXOpen does one extra `AXWindow` and `AXTitle` read (100 ms timeout) before the action. Rollback is reverting the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - Unit test `an_erroring_open_counts_only_when_its_element_is_gone_and_the_window_changed` (`click.rs`): the Finder case (-25205, element gone after a few polls, title changed) counts; element still there and title unchanged do not; -25202, -25200 and success are never probed.
  - `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (456 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`.
- Manual or platform evidence: the table and clip above.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - Only AXOpen and only -25205 are covered. An AXPress that navigates and destroys its own button (a "Back" button, say) still errors; #3835's broader question stays with #3836.
  - Finder list and column views were not measured. In column view the folder row survives navigation, so it would keep the error.
  - No harness e2e row; Finder is the oracle.

title: fix(cua-driver): release a background Command chord's base key without Command
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, one background `hotkey` with Command to a Mac Catalyst app fires the app's key command over and over. A `UIKeyCommand` for cmd+shift+[ (the kind Messages uses to switch conversations) fired about 125 times in 3 s from one call, and keeps firing until some other key event reaches the app. An event tap on the app sees exactly one key-down and one key-up, so the driver sends the chord once; the problem is the key-up. It carries the Command flag, the app drops it, and UIKit treats the key as still held.
- What changed: the background PID-routed key press (`keyboard::press_key`, used by background `hotkey` and `press_key`) now sends its key-up without Command. The key-down is unchanged and keeps every modifier, so menus and key commands still match it. Other modifiers (Shift, Option, Control, fn) stay on both halves. The foreground menu-shortcut helpers (`hotkey_no_auth`, `press_key_no_auth`) and the global HID paths are not touched. The pair of events is built by a small `pid_key_press` function so the sequence is unit-tested.

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Build a tiny Catalyst probe whose window shows how often its cmd+shift+[ key command fired (source and build command below), and open it.
2. Bring another app to the front (Finder), so the probe is in the background.
3. `list_windows` gives the probe's `<pid>` and `<window_id>`. Send one background chord:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "keys": ["cmd", "shift", "["]}
   ```
4. Wait 3 s and read the probe's label (on screen, or the `counts` element's value in `get_window_state`).

On main, the call returns success and the label reads `fired=125 began=1 ended=0`, still climbing. On this branch it reads `fired=1 began=1 ended=1`.

<details><summary>Probe source (main.swift) and build</summary>

```swift
import UIKit

final class ProbeController: UIViewController {
    var fired = 0, began = 0, ended = 0
    let label = UILabel()
    override func viewDidLoad() {
        super.viewDidLoad()
        view.backgroundColor = .systemBackground
        label.accessibilityIdentifier = "counts"
        label.frame = CGRect(x: 20, y: 40, width: 600, height: 80)
        view.addSubview(label)
        render()
    }
    override var canBecomeFirstResponder: Bool { true }
    override func viewDidAppear(_ animated: Bool) { super.viewDidAppear(animated); becomeFirstResponder() }
    override var keyCommands: [UIKeyCommand]? {
        let command = UIKeyCommand(input: "[", modifierFlags: [.command, .shift], action: #selector(onCommand))
        command.wantsPriorityOverSystemBehavior = true
        return [command]
    }
    @objc func onCommand() { fired += 1; render() }
    override func pressesBegan(_ presses: Set<UIPress>, with event: UIPressesEvent?) {
        if presses.contains(where: { $0.key?.keyCode == .keyboardOpenBracket }) { began += 1; render() }
        super.pressesBegan(presses, with: event)
    }
    override func pressesEnded(_ presses: Set<UIPress>, with event: UIPressesEvent?) {
        if presses.contains(where: { $0.key?.keyCode == .keyboardOpenBracket }) { ended += 1; render() }
        super.pressesEnded(presses, with: event)
    }
    func render() { label.text = "fired=\(fired) began=\(began) ended=\(ended)"; label.accessibilityValue = label.text }
}

final class AppDelegate: UIResponder, UIApplicationDelegate {
    var window: UIWindow?
    func application(_ application: UIApplication,
                     didFinishLaunchingWithOptions options: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]?) -> Bool {
        window = UIWindow(frame: CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 640, height: 240))
        window?.rootViewController = ProbeController()
        window?.makeKeyAndVisible()
        return true
    }
}

UIApplicationMain(CommandLine.argc, CommandLine.unsafeArgv, nil, NSStringFromClass(AppDelegate.self))
```

title: fix(cua-driver): keep named macOS accessibility groups in the tree
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `get_window_state` drops the names of accessibility sections. The tree walk collapses every AXGroup and AXScrollArea before reading its name, so a named section disappears along with anonymous layout wrappers. Two Save buttons in groups described "Profile" and "Billing" come out as two identical rows side by side, with nothing in the tree saying which section each belongs to. Stock apps have the same shape: in Stocks the watchlist rows run on straight after the news list with the "Stock list" section name gone, and Clock and Weather lose "World clocks", "Conditions" and "Location List".
- What changed: an AXGroup or AXScrollArea with a non-empty AXTitle or AXDescription keeps a row (`AXGroup (Billing)`), and its children are indented under it. Unnamed ones still collapse exactly as before. A kept group is a display row only: its actions are not read (in SwiftUI and Catalyst apps these are generic scroll and menu actions), so it gets no `element_index`, the element list is unchanged, and the indexes of the elements after it do not shift. The title and description reads move ahead of the collapse check and are reused for kept nodes, so a kept group adds no extra AX round trip; an unnamed group now costs two attribute reads it did not before.

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Build a small AppKit window with two `NSView`s whose accessibility role is group, labelled "Profile" and "Billing", each holding a "Save" button (source in the Notes below), and open it. Or open Stocks.
2. `list_windows`, then `get_window_state` on the window:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "include_screenshot": false}
   ```

On main the fixture's tree is:
```
- [0] AXWindow "Groups" [actions=[raise]]
  - AXStaticText = "Profile section"
  - [1] AXButton "Save" [actions=[press]]
  - AXStaticText = "Billing section"
  - [2] AXButton "Save" [actions=[press]]
```
On this branch:
```
- [0] AXWindow "Groups" [actions=[raise]]
  - AXGroup (Profile)
    - AXStaticText = "Profile section"
    - [1] AXButton "Save" [actions=[press]]
  - AXGroup (Billing)
    - AXStaticText = "Billing section"
    - [2] AXButton "Save" [actions=[press]]
```
Stocks on main (excerpt, long labels shortened):
```
  - [3] AXHeading (Top Stories)
  - [4] AXGenericElement (CNBC, Stock futures are flat ...)
  ...
  - [10] AXTextField = "Stocks" (Stocks)
  - [11] AXStaticText (Business News From News)
  - [12] AXGenericElement = "51,176.96, ..." (Dow Jones Industrial Average, Dow Jones)
```
On this branch:
```
  - AXGroup (Business News)
    - [3] AXHeading (Top Stories)
    - [4] AXGenericElement (CNBC, Stock futures are flat ...)
    ...
  - [10] AXTextField = "Stocks" (Stocks)
  - AXGroup (Stock list)
    - [11] AXStaticText (Business News From News)
    - [12] AXGenericElement = "51,176.96, ..." (Dow Jones Industrial Average, Dow Jones)
```
The element indexes are the same on both.

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM (Apple Silicon). Named groups listed by a separate AX probe (every AXGroup with a title or description); counts from the same `get_window_state` call.

| Window | named groups the app exposes | names in the tree: main a3d55cef2 | this branch | elements main / branch | tree lines main / branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixture (Profile, Billing) | 2 | 0 of 2, 3 of 3 runs | **2 of 2**, 3 of 3 runs | 67 / 67 | 7 / 9 |
| Stocks | 3 | 2 ("Stock list" missing) | **3** | 192 / 192 | 149 / 152 |
| Clock | 3 | 2 ("World clocks" missing) | **3** | 160 / 160 | 22 / 25 |
| Weather | 5 | 3 ("Conditions", "Location List" missing) | **5** | live content changed between runs | |
| Font Book | 48 ("Show <font>" rows) | 0 | 48 | 325 / 325 | 189 / 237 |
| Finder window, 30 files | not probed | n/a | 3 rows (Back/Forward, desktop) | 267 / 267 | 78 / 81 |
| System Settings | 0 | n/a | n/a | 256 / 256 | 98 / 98 |
| TextEdit Settings | 0 | n/a | n/a | 243 / 243 | 48 / 48 |

Size: element counts are unchanged in every window measured. The tree text grows by one line per named section; Font Book is the largest case seen, +48 lines and +14% characters (14,797 to 16,830). Walk time was within noise (Font Book 0.24 s and 0.26 s, Stocks 0.32 s and 0.35 s).

Clip (23 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (the fixture window top left, the AX probe's view of its groups bottom left, the `get_window_state` tree right), with the focus moving to the tree, ending on a side-by-side frame.

No existing issue or PR covers this. #3950 and #3787 (open, will-bogusz) change which macOS rows are addressable and how rows are rendered, and #4061 adds enumeration diagnostics; none keeps named groups. This PR does not touch addressability rules for any other role.

## Compatibility and risk

Named groups and scroll areas appear as unindexed rows, and their children are indented one level deeper. AXNode depth changes accordingly for those children.
- Risk and rollback: a client that parses `tree_markdown` by indentation sees one more level under named sections; a very large tree gains one line per named section, and the depth budget (`max_depth`) is reached one level sooner inside them. Rollback is reverting the commit.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep a macOS menu command's window key within its app
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `invoke_menu` File > Save on a document that is not the key window saves nothing. With note.txt and other.txt open in TextEdit and other.txt key, `invoke_menu` `["File", "Save"]` on note.txt's window returns success, but note.txt on disk is unchanged and the save goes to other.txt (its modification time moves). invoke_menu makes the requested window key, presses the item, and then puts the previously key window back, also when that window belongs to the same app. AppKit runs some menu actions after the press returns, against whichever window is key at that moment, so the restore retargets them.
- What changed: once the command was dispatched, the requested window stays key within its own app. Everything else keeps today's behavior: when another application was in front before the call, its window is still brought back, and when the path is refused (nothing was dispatched) the sibling window is still put back. The decision is a small `restores_prior_window` function with a unit test.

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Open two plain-text files in TextEdit, note.txt and then other.txt, so other.txt is the key window and TextEdit is in front:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p ~/w && : > ~/w/note.txt && echo "leave me alone" > ~/w/other.txt
   open -a TextEdit ~/w/note.txt && sleep 1 && open -a TextEdit ~/w/other.txt
   ```
2. `list_windows` gives TextEdit's `<pid>` and note.txt's `<note_id>`. `get_window_state` on `<note_id>`, then `type_text` into its text area by token:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <note_id>, "element_token": "<token of the AXTextArea>", "text": "only in note"}
   ```
3. Save note.txt by menu:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <note_id>, "path": ["File", "Save"]}
   ```
4. Two seconds later, `cat ~/w/note.txt`.

On main step 3 returns `Resolved the live native menu path and dispatched its final accessibility action; ...` with `effect: "unverifiable"`, note.txt on disk is still empty, its title still says Edited, other.txt stays the key window, and in the recorded run other.txt's modification time moved (it was the document saved). On this branch the same call returns the same text, note.txt on disk holds `only in note`, and note.txt is the key window.

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM (Apple Silicon). Disk is the oracle; the key window is read by a separate AX probe (`AXFocusedWindow`), and leftover menu windows from the WindowServer list (layer 101).

| Case | main a3d55cef2 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Two windows, other.txt key: File > Save on note.txt | **note.txt on disk `""`**, 3 of 3; key window stays other.txt | **note.txt on disk `"only in note"`**, 3 of 3; key window note.txt; other.txt unchanged |
| Control: note.txt alone, File > Save | saved, 3 of 3 | saved, 3 of 3 |
| Control (#4484): two windows, path `["File", "No Such Item"]` on note.txt | refused `menu_path_unavailable`, "No menu window this call opened is still on screen.", 0 menus left, key back to other.txt, 3 of 3 | identical, 3 of 3 |
| Control (#4578): note.txt, path `["File", "Save As..."]` | Save sheet opens, 3 of 3 | Save sheet opens, 3 of 3 |

Clip (29 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (TextEdit windows left, the MCP calls top right, files on disk and the key window bottom right), with the focus moving to the Save result and on the disk listing, ending on a side-by-side frame.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc9a321e-32ba-42a6-bcaf-7f600fda7bb8

## Related work

No existing issue or PR covers this. #3781 and #2788 introduced the exact prior-window restore; this keeps it for other applications and for refused paths.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. No schema, contract, or result text change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS `invoke_menu` only. After a dispatched command in an app that was already in front, the requested window now stays key instead of the window that was key before the call. Calls made while another app is in front are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: a caller that relied on the sibling window becoming key again after a menu command now finds the requested window key; for deferred commands that restore was what broke them. Rollback is reverting the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - Unit test `a_dispatched_command_keeps_its_window_key_within_the_app` (`invoke_menu.rs`): another app comes back whether or not the command was dispatched; a same-app sibling stays behind after a dispatch and comes back after a refusal; nothing is restored when the requested window was already key.

title: fix(cua-driver): focus the exact sibling window for macOS foreground input
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS a foreground click into a Finder window is refused whenever another Finder window is key and Finder is in front. `click` with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` and the target's `window_id` returns `isError: true`, `click failed: foreground HID delivery to window <id> was not possible: exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery`, and nothing happens. Foreground HID delivery asks SkyLight to make the exact window key (`make_exact_window_key`) and then requires AX to report it focused; in that state Finder ignores those key-window records and keeps its current key window, so the check fails every time. The same refusal applies to every foreground input that goes through this helper (double and right clicks, drags, focused-field keys).
- What changed: when the records alone did not focus the window, `with_foreground_hid_activation` now runs the exact AX window raise that `bring_to_front` already uses (`raise_exact_ax_window`: AXRaise, AXMain and AXFocused on that one window, never the app's other windows) and waits for focus once more before refusing. The focus proof is unchanged: input is still only posted after AX reports the exact window focused. The driver's own windows keep today's refusal (AppKit orders windows on the main thread only). The helper stays where it is; it becomes `pub(crate)`, and so does the `bring_to_front` module. Only the would-refuse path changes; when the records work, nothing extra runs.

## How to reproduce (on main)

1. Open two Finder windows side by side, the second one key, and keep Finder in front:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p ~/r2click ~/r2clickfront && touch ~/r2click/a.txt ~/r2click/b.txt ~/r2clickfront/c.txt
   open ~/r2click && sleep 1 && open ~/r2clickfront
   ```
   (Move r2clickfront so it does not cover r2click; `set_window_frame` works.)
2. `list_windows` gives Finder's `<pid>` and r2click's `<window_id>`. `get_window_state` on r2click (with its screenshot) gives a.txt's frame; take its centre `x,y` in screenshot pixels.
3. Click it in the foreground:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "x": <x>, "y": <y>, "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
   ```

On main step 3 returns the refusal above, r2clickfront stays key and nothing is selected in r2click. On this branch it returns `<check mark> Posted click at screen-point ... (foreground: exact window activated, ...)`, r2click becomes key and a.txt is selected.

## Before and after

macOS 26.4 VM (Apple Silicon). Key window and selection read by a separate AX probe (`AXFocusedWindow`, `AXSelected`); 3 runs per row on each build.

| Case | main b0a634813 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Finder in front, r2clickfront key, foreground click a.txt in r2click (windows apart) | **refused**, 3 of 3 (1.88-1.91 s); key stays r2clickfront; nothing selected | **posted**, 3 of 3 (2.06-2.09 s); key r2click; a.txt selected |
| Same, r2clickfront overlapping r2click | **refused**, 3 of 3 | **posted**, 3 of 3; a.txt selected |
| Control: TextEdit in front, two Finder windows | posted, a.txt selected, 3 of 3 (1.20-1.26 s) | same, 3 of 3 (1.22-1.26 s) |
| Control: one Finder window behind TextEdit | posted, a.txt selected, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Control: background click, two Finder windows | AX press via hit-test, key unchanged, 3 of 3 | same, 3 of 3 |
| Control (#4551 case): TextEdit Open panel with its Go to Folder sheet focused, foreground Return aimed at the Open window | refused, sheet stays, 3 of 3 | refused, sheet stays, 3 of 3 |
| Same panel and sheet, foreground key "z" aimed at the note.txt window | refused, 3 of 3 | delivered to note.txt (`zx`), sheet stays open, 3 of 3 |

The last row is the one behavior change outside Finder: a foreground key aimed at a sibling document while another window of the app holds focus now reaches the requested window, as it does when the key-window records work.

Clip (26 s): main first, then this branch, same layout (both Finder windows left, the MCP calls right), with the focus moving to the result and on the key window and selection, ending on a side-by-side frame.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e0e1998-67f3-4b96-9564-0803377c4e3c

## Related work

No existing issue or PR covers the refusal. Related: #3574 (open issue, foreground `type_text` reaching a sibling window, a different helper that this does not touch), #3923 (open, adds the focused window's id to this refusal's text; partly superseded by #4821, which now names the window holding focus in the refusal), #4821 (merged: retries the activation once before this fallback; on its own that retry does not focus the Finder window in the rows above, so main still refuses), #3863 (draft, exact key window for foreground shortcuts on the menu path).

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. No schema, contract, or result text change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS foreground input through `with_foreground_hid_activation` (window-scoped foreground `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `drag`, and focused-field `press_key`, `hotkey`, `type_text`). Calls that were refused because the window never became focused can now succeed when an AX raise focuses it.
- Risk and rollback: on that path the target window is also raised in z-order (AXRaise), as `bring_to_front` does. A call that still cannot focus the window is refused as before, about 0.4 s later (one more focus wait). Rollback is reverting the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: no new unit test (the change is one boolean condition calling an existing helper; the behavior is covered by the VM rows above). `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (480 passed, 6 ignored, run in the VM), `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test contract_parity`, `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` (up to date), `scripts/check-no-em-dash.sh`, `git diff --check`.

- Known gaps or CI still required: Finder and TextEdit only; `with_foreground_assist` (the foreground rung for scroll and some `type_text` paths, which proceeds without the focus proof) is unchanged; no harness e2e row.

title: fix(spaces-macos): run the app's daemon as its launchd agent so it keeps Local Network access
body:
A user reported that after quitting Cua Spaces while the daemon kept running, creating a Space failed with "No route to host": the daemon had lost Local Network access to the macOS VMs on vmnet (192.168.64.x).

## Cause

The app started its daemon as a child process: `DaemonSupervisor.start` runs `cua daemon start` with `Process`, which spawns the daemon with `Command::spawn` (`libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/lib.rs`, `daemon_start`). macOS attributes a child's Local Network access to its responsible process, which for the daemon was the app process. On this Mac, `responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid` on the installed daemon returns the app's pid. Once the app quits, the daemon's access no longer comes from a running app.

## Fix

The daemon now runs as the app's launchd agent, which Apple documents as the way to tie a helper to the app's Local Network permission whether or not the app runs ([TN3179](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3179-understanding-local-network-privacy)).

- `Support/com.trycua.spaces.daemon.plist` is copied to `Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/`. It runs `Contents/MacOS/cua daemon start --foreground --loopback 127.0.0.1:0` and is set to `RunAtLoad false` and `KeepAlive false`, so it starts only when asked and `cua daemon stop` keeps it stopped.
- `DaemonSupervisor` registers the agent with `SMAppService.agent(plistName:)` and passes its label to `cua daemon start` in `CUA_DAEMON_LAUNCHD_LABEL`.
- With that label set, `cua daemon start` uses `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/<label>` and waits for the job's pid in the discovery file. It no longer spawns the daemon itself (`cua-cli/src/daemon_launchd.rs`).
- `cua daemon start` started by something other than the app also uses the agent when it is loaded. That covers a terminal, an MCP server, and the relay host's `cua-spacesd` LaunchAgent. The start must use default arguments and this user's own home (no `CUA_HOME`, and `HOME` is the account's), and the `cua` must not be inside another app's bundle. Before, such a daemon got its access from whoever started it. A LaunchAgent is responsible for itself and has no grant, so its daemon got "No route to host".
- In these cases the daemon is still spawned as a child, as before:
  - the agent is missing, or the user turned it off in Login Items (`requiresApproval`);
  - registering it fails, or `launchctl` fails;
  - the start uses `--socket`, `--state-dir` or a different `--loopback`;
  - another executable runs the daemon;
  - the app runs with its own `HOME` or `CUA_*` settings (tests, development runs).

  The spawned daemon does not inherit the label, so a `cua daemon start` inside it cannot restart the agent's job.

The first registration shows macOS's "Background item added" notice for Cua Spaces.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p cua-cli --lib daemon_launchd`: tests for when the label is used, parsing the `launchctl print` pid, and the launchd target. `cargo clippy -p cua-cli --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- `apps/cua-spaces-macos/scripts/test.sh --filter DaemonSupervisorTests`: 9 tests pass. The new ones cover registering the agent, the fallbacks (not registered, approval needed, missing, register fails, own `HOME`/`CUA_HOME`), the label reaching `cua daemon start`, and the bundled plist matching what the CLI would spawn.
- On a Mac, using a debug `cua-spaces-cli` with a throwaway `HOME`/`CUA_HOME` and a test launchd job:
  - With the label, `cua daemon start` started the daemon through launchd. Its parent pid was 1, it was its own responsible process, and the job showed `state = running` with the same pid.
  - A second start was a no-op, and `cua daemon stop` left the job not running.
  - An unknown label logged the reason and fell back to the spawn. With no label, the spawn ran as before.
- The installed app's `cua` (Developer ID, `com.trycua.cua`), spawned with responsibility disclaimed, could not reach a vmnet VM: its TCP connect failed. Spawned plainly from a shell, the same connect went through. So the binary has no Local Network grant of its own, and any daemon that answers for itself fails.
- A harness of small C programs measured how responsibility works on macOS 26.6 (Darwin 25.6):
  - A self-responsible ad hoc binary with no grant got exactly `connect: No route to host` to a vmnet VM. This is the user's error.
  - Children spawned by a granted parent kept access after the parent exited, so I could not reproduce the loss itself on this Mac.

Not verified here: that macOS applies the app's grant to the SMAppService agent. That needs a Developer ID-signed build. Ad hoc test jobs with `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` were not given another app's grant.

title: cua-driver (macOS): every window screenshot leaks its full-resolution pixel buffer in the serve process
body:
### Summary

On macOS, every window screenshot taken by `cua-driver serve --embedded` leaves one full-resolution pixel buffer allocated in the driver process. The buffers are never released: not after the call returns, not after `end_session`, and not after the MCP client disconnects. Memory grows by `width × height × 4` bytes per capture until the driver is restarted.

### Environment

- cua-driver-rs 0.28.3 (universal macOS binary from the GitHub release), embedded via `@trycua/cua-driver` 0.28.3 (`EmbeddedCuaDriverHost`, `permissionMode: Unrestricted`)
- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple silicon, built-in 3024×1964 Retina display
- Client: `cua-driver mcp --embedded --socket …` over stdio

I have not run a newer release, but the macOS capture path (`crates/platform-macos/src/capture.rs`, `capture_window_from_plan` → `SCScreenshotManager::capture_image` → `rgba_data`) and the `screencapturekit = 8.0.1` pin look unchanged between `cua-driver-rs-v0.28.3` and `main`.

### Reproduction

1. Start an embedded host and connect an MCP client.
2. `start_session`, then call `get_window_state` with a screenshot (the default) on any window, N times.
3. Inspect the `serve` process: `vmmap <pid> | grep '^MALLOC_LARGE '`.
4. `end_session`, close the client, wait, and inspect again.

### Observed

Each capture adds one `MALLOC_LARGE` region the size of the window's backing pixels, in `DefaultPurgeableMallocZone`:

- A 1800×1130 pt window at 2× adds 32.1 MB per capture.
- A 920×436 pt Finder window at 2× adds about 6.8 MB per capture. Four captures: `MALLOC_LARGE` went from 875.2 MB to 903.8 MB (27 → 33 regions; a 22 MB region also came and went with unrelated calls).
- `get_window_state` with `include_screenshot: false` adds nothing.
- After `end_session` and after closing the client, the capture regions are all still there.

A driver that had served agent sessions for about an hour held 22 such regions (19 × 32.1 MB, 3 × 54.1 MB) and had a 1.1 GB physical footprint:

```
MALLOC ZONE                              VIRTUAL  RESIDENT  ALLOCATION COUNT  BYTES ALLOCATED
DefaultPurgeableMallocZone_0x10f270000    772.6M    772.6M                22           772.3M
DefaultMallocZone_0x106e54000             124.6M     84.6M             85647            54.2M
```

The returned image is downscaled (1567×984 here), but the retained buffers are native resolution.

### Expected

The native-resolution pixels are released once the PNG/JPEG for the response has been encoded, or at the latest when the session that captured them ends.

### Notes

The buffers sit in the purgeable malloc zone rather than the default zone, which suggests CoreGraphics-owned image data (the `CGImage` returned by `SCScreenshotManager`, or data copied from its provider) that is never released, rather than a Rust-side `Vec`. I have not traced it further than that, so the leak may be in the `screencapturekit` crate's bridge rather than in the driver itself.

title: fix(cua-driver): say how to recover from an unapproved browser profile
body:
## What

`browser_consent_required` refusals now say how to get past them.

- **`get_browser_state` on a person's own Chrome or Edge window.** The message used to say the profile "requires explicit existing-profile approval". It now names both routes:
  - `browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile`, which needs the runtime grant;
  - `browser_prepare` with `allow_launch` and `profile: {mode: "isolated_new"}`, which needs no grant.
- **`browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile` on a standard runtime without the grant.** The message now says that a running daemon cannot gain the grant and must be restarted.
- **Machine-readable recovery.** Both refusals now carry `detail.recovery`:
  - `grant_restart_command` is the platform's restart command with `--grant existing-profile`. It is `null` on embedded runtimes, because the host owns the launch there.
  - `isolated_alternative` holds the exact `browser_prepare` arguments for the isolated route.
- **Docs.** The browsers guide now shows the restart command. It also says what a person sees during existing-profile setup on each new session: the browser comes to the front, a setup tab opens, and Chrome asks "Allow remote debugging?". It names the two refusals to retry once when setup is interrupted.

The existing fields `reason`, `supported_strategies` and `next_action` are unchanged, so this is additive.

## Why

I reproduced this on macOS 26 with Chrome 154, using a throwaway `--user-data-dir` and the quickstart's default daemon. The first refusal an agent got didn't say that a restart was needed, or that an isolated profile needed no grant. With the grant, 2 of 5 attaches on 0.28.2 failed on a busy desktop:
- once with `browser_wrong_target_refused`, because the window lost focus before the setup URL was committed;
- once with `browser_reconnect_exhausted`.

On 0.33.4, 4 of 4 succeeded, taking about 6-7 s each. Each new session repeated the visible setup.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::`: 188 passed, including the new `existing_profile_recovery_names_the_grant_restart_and_the_isolated_route` and extended assertions in `existing_profile_requires_runtime_authorization` and `standalone_consumer_refuses_existing_profile_approval_without_preparing`.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Live: I ran a debug `cua-driver serve` against the throwaway Chrome, and both refusals returned the new `detail.recovery`.

title: ci: sign Windows binaries without the signing action's dependency cache
body:
`azure/artifact-signing-action` v2.0.0 fails whenever it restores its own cached `ArtifactSigning` PowerShell module:

```
Cache hit for: ArtifactSigning-0.1.8
Invoke-ArtifactSigning: The term 'Invoke-ArtifactSigning' is not recognized as a name of a cmdlet
```

A first run (cache miss) installs the module, signs and saves the cache; any later run that restores it fails. cua-sdk 0.3.1, 0.4.0 and 0.4.1 each failed this way and only passed after the cache entry was deleted.

This sets `cache-dependencies: false` (an input the action already has) on all five uses: `cd-cua-sdk.yml`, `cd-cua-spaces.yml` (2), `cd-cua-spacesd.yml` and `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml`. Costs a module download per signing job, about a minute.

actionlint is clean apart from an existing SC2129 note in cd-rust-cua-driver.yml, and the 51 release-wiring tests pass.

title: fix(cua-driver): sweep orphaned isolated_new browser profiles
body:
## Problem

`browser_prepare` with `profile.mode=isolated_new` creates `~/Library/Application Support/CuaDriver/BrowserProfiles/isolated-<uuid>` (Linux: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cua-driver/browser-profiles`) and is meant to delete it when the session ends. The deletion only happens in `ManagedBrowser::drop`, i.e. in daemon memory. If the daemon is killed, crashes, is restarted or exits without dropping the engine before the session ends, nothing ever removes the directory. Anything the agent signed into stays on disk, unencrypted from the driver's point of view.

Found on a dogfooding Mac: three `isolated-*` profiles dated 16 Aug, 17 Aug and 8 Sep had survived (two with a stale Chrome `SingletonLock` pointing at a dead pid, which matches a daemon killed mid-session). They held cookies for sites the agents had visited.

## Fix

Before creating a new profile, `prepare_profile` now sweeps orphans (`sweep_orphaned_isolated_profiles`). A directory is removed only if all of these hold:

- the name starts with `isolated-`;
- it carries this driver's marker with `mode=isolated_new` (named profiles and unmarked directories are never touched);
- the marker is at least 1 hour old, so a profile another daemon just created is safe;
- Chrome's `SingletonLock` does not point at a live process.

Unix only (macOS and Linux). Windows has no `SingletonLock`, so it is left as before.

## Tests

- New unit test `sweep_removes_only_stale_unowned_isolated_new_profiles`: covers an orphan, a live-lock profile, a dead-lock profile, an `isolated_named` profile with an `isolated-` name, a normal named profile, an unmarked directory, and the age gate.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::prepare`: 21 passed. `cargo clippy` is clean for the changed file.

Not merging; for review.
