title: [Bug]: one sandbox call that never returns stalls `cb run` and the Tinker trainer indefinitely
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

If one call into a variant's sandbox never returns (for example a shell command that hangs in a healthy sandbox), `cb run` never finishes: BatchRunner has no bound on a variant's task setup, agent and evaluation, so the batch's `gather` never returns and `summary.json` is never written. The Tinker GRPO loop (`cua_bench_rl/trainer/off_policy/tinker/rollout.py`) waits on `cb run` with no timeout, so training stops with no error, and the variants of that run that did finish never reach the trainer. Separately, if `cb run` is killed, rollout.py polls the session store for up to `timeout` (3600 s by default) for sessions that can no longer finish.

### Reproduction

Local sandbox, no model calls (a scripted agent):

1. A dataset with two variants of a task like `example_tasks/hello_file_env`, whose agent calls `await session.run_command("sleep 100000")` in one variant (a command that never returns; the sandbox stays healthy).
2. Collect rollouts the way the Tinker loop does: `rollout.run_rollouts(tasks_path, agent, model, max_steps, num_rollouts=2)` (it runs `cb run dataset ...`).
3. The other variant finishes and writes its `result.json`; `cb run` never exits; `run_rollouts` never returns.

Also: `cb run` killed mid-run (SIGKILL): `run_rollouts` keeps polling for up to `timeout` (3600 s), then raises `TimeoutError`.

Observed in 3/3 runs on a real local container (`ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`, runc on Colima) and 3/3 with cua-bench's in-memory test sandbox; the `cb run` kill case 2/2 on the real container and 3/3 in-memory (numbers below).

### Expected behavior

A stuck variant fails after a bound and releases its sandbox; the batch finishes; the trainer gets the variants that finished. A `cb run` that died is not waited on.

### Actual behavior

- Hung command in one variant: the trainer made no further progress, with no error, in every run (3/3, real container, 5-minute windows); 1 evaluated episode of that run never reached the trainer; the hung variant's sandbox stays up for as long as `cb` waits.
- `cb run` SIGKILLed mid-run: no progress for the rest of the window (128 s+ of 180 s; by the code, up to 3600 s, then `TimeoutError`); 2 local sandboxes left running.
- For comparison, a sandbox frozen with `docker pause` mid-episode is handled: the native transport fails the call (`CuaError.Transport: ... http2 error (operation timed out)`) and the run continues (recovered in 43.5 s, 1 episode lost). The stall needs a call that never errors.

### Environment

- cua-bench / cua-bench-rl at main 8be7052a; cua 0.4.1, cua-sandbox 0.9.0 (PyPI wheels)
- macOS 26 (Apple silicon), Python 3.12.15, Colima (runc), image `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04` (arm64)
- Local only; outbound network denied for the run (sandbox-exec), no model calls

### Evidence

Fault-injection study (deterministic, local; harness drives the real `cb` CLI, BatchRunner, run_episode, RemoteDesktopSession and the Tinker loop's `run_rollouts` + `traces.load_runs`):

Real container (`ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`), each epoch = 2 rollouts of a 2-variant dataset, 3 seeds × 5 min. "Fixed" passes `variant_timeout=90` (scaled to these ~20–50 s episodes):

| Fault | Code | Episodes reaching the trainer per hour | Evaluated but never delivered | Trainer recovers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shell command never returns in one variant | main | 48 | 1 per run | never (3/3; no progress for ~275 s of 300 s) |
| same | fixed | 420 | 0 (only the stuck episode is lost) | after 95 s (94.9–95.0) |

cua-bench's in-memory test sandbox (8 variants × 2 rollouts per epoch; "fixed" passes `variant_timeout=30`), 3 seeds × 5 min:

| Fault | Code | Episodes/h | Evaluated but never delivered | Trainer recovers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| one sandbox call never returns | main | 192 | 7 per run | never (3/3) |
| same | fixed | 2,164 (2,100–2,292) | 0 | after 37 s (37.3–37.6) |
| `cb run` SIGKILLed mid-run | main | 192 | — | never (3/3; the code waits up to 3600 s) |
| same | fixed | 2,272 (2,208–2,400) | — | after 12 s (11.5–12.1) |
| no fault | main / fixed | 2,304 / 2,304 | 0 | — |

The deadlines above are scaled to the short test episodes; with the proposed 3600 s default the same recovery comes an hour after the hang instead of never. The fixed runs also included a separate `file_exists` fix that does not touch these paths.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: run `cb run` under an external watchdog and kill it; finished variants are then on disk but `rollout.py` still waits on their sessions.

Proposed fix (I have it on a branch with tests and can open a PR once the option and default are agreed):

- `cb run --variant-timeout SECONDS` (and `BatchRunner(variant_timeout_s=...)`): a variant whose task setup, agent and evaluation (not sandbox start) run longer is cancelled the same way Ctrl-C cancels it (its sandbox is released by the existing `async with`), recorded as failed ("variant timed out after N s"), and not retried.
- Default: **3600 s** proposed (above the 1800 s `CUA_BENCH_HARNESS_TIMEOUT` a harness agent gets, which the deadline must not cut off), `0` = no limit. Decision for you: this changes behaviour for anyone with a variant that legitimately runs longer than the default; alternatives are a larger default or opt-in (`0` by default). Migration note: such users pass `--variant-timeout 0` (or a larger value).
- `rollout.py`: pass an optional `variant_timeout` through to `cb`; an optional `run_timeout` for the whole `cb run` (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 60 s; the run directory is returned so finished variants are kept); do not wait on the sessions of a `cb` that exited non-zero.

Related: #4929 (draft) also edits `cli/main.py` and `cli/commands/run.py`. Not a duplicate: I searched issues and PRs for cb run hangs, variant/rollout timeouts and the Tinker rollout.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: feat(spaces): right-click menus in the New UI (CUA-1639)
body:
**Held for feature freeze. Don't merge until the freeze lifts.**

Right-clicking a Space tile in the New UI showed the web view's own menu ("Copy Image"). Now Spaces and machines have menus of their own. The Mac app and Electron draw them natively, and they work from the keyboard.

Linear: CUA-1639 (part A: the shared plumbing, Space tiles and rows, machines. Part B, which covers Agents, Keyvault items and Notifications, stacks on this branch).

## What changes for users
- **Space tile or row:** Open, Turn on / Turn off… / Restart…, Teleport an app…, Send file…, Share…, Copy Name, Copy ID, Delete Space… (or Remove… / Remove from List). An item appears only when the Space's page would offer it, by the same rules: the core's detail actions and power button. Turn off, Restart and Delete ask first.
- **Machine row:** Open, New Space on This Machine…, Copy Name, and Remove… where the machine's detail has Remove.
- **Everywhere else:** the web view's own menu is gone. Text fields and selected text keep the system menu (Cut/Copy/Paste). Links that leave the app get Open Link / Copy Link. Electron now also gets Cut/Copy/Paste in text fields, which it never had.
- **Keyboard:** Shift+F10 or the context-menu key on a focused tile or row opens the menu.

## How
- `useContextMenu(items)` and `<ContextMenuHost />` in `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/components/context-menu.tsx`. Each item has a stable action id (`space.stop`, `machine.copyName`, …), and choosing one runs the existing action. Destructive items carry a `confirm`.
- New bridge method `window.showContextMenu {items, x, y}` answers `{id | null}`. It's in the web contract (shapes, coverage), Swift (`WebUIBridge+ContextMenu.swift`, NSMenu) and Electron (`src/context-menu.ts`, `Menu.popup`). When an item has `copy`, the host writes that text to the clipboard itself.
- The demo, Tauri, and an older app that answers `unimplemented` all fall back to a menu drawn in the page.
- Not included: **Rename** for a Space, because neither the core nor the hosts have a rename for Spaces. **Revoke** stays in Settings > Devices, since the Machines page doesn't offer it today.

## Tests
- web (vitest): `components/__tests__/context-menu.test.tsx` covers the native path, the confirmation, keyboard, the in-page fallback, default-menu suppression, and the menus on the real Spaces and Machines pages with the wasm core.
- Electron: `test/context-menu.test.ts` (request checks, the template, zoom, Cut/Copy/Paste) and a `bridge-native` case.
- Swift: `WebUIHostTests.thePagesContextMenusAreNative` and a `BridgeContractTests` case.

## Verified on a signed build
I tested signed, notarized CI builds of this branch (CD run 38642709685, version 0.9.0-ctxmenu.1, nothing published) on a spare test Mac.
- **Mac app, New UI:** right-clicking a Space tile opens the native NSMenu with Open, Turn off…, Restart…, Teleport an app…, Send file…, Copy Name, Copy ID and Delete Space…. Choosing Copy ID put the Space's id on the clipboard. Right-clicking a machine row shows Open, New Space on This Machine… and Copy Name, and Copy Name copied "This Mac". A Space row in a machine's detail, here a suspended one, shows Teleport greyed out, the same rule as its page. Right-clicking a blank area, a sidebar link or the Space page shows no menu. The Filter field keeps the system menu (Cut/Copy/Paste…). "Copy Image" never appeared.
- **Electron:** the same native menus on the Space tile and the machine row, and Copy ID copied the id. The Filter field gets Undo/Redo/Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All. A blank area shows no menu.
- One test-harness quirk: a *synthetic background* right-click (posted straight to the process) opened the Mac menu twice. A real HID right-click opens exactly one menu, and choosing an item or pressing Escape closes it.

title: feat(spaces): right-click menus for Agents and Keyvault items (CUA-1639)
body:
Part B of CUA-1639. It is stacked on #5197 (part A: the context-menu plumbing plus Space and Machine menus) and targets that branch.

**For users:** right-clicking an agent, a run or a Keyvault item in the New UI (Mac app and Electron) now shows a menu of that item's actions instead of the web view's default menu.

### Menus
- **Agents** (list rows and the detail header): Open, Pause/Resume (the core's label, as on the detail's button), Stop (only while a run is running), Copy Name, and Remove… with a confirmation. The agent's home stays in Cua Volume.
- **Runs** (Recent runs): Open, and Stop while the run is running.
- **Keyvault items:** Copy Name (the item's name, never a value, and hidden while names are hidden), Unlock… or Lock (as the row's lock button does), and Delete…. Delete asks first the same way the batch bar's Delete does: the page's dialog in the demo, the host's own alert in the Mac app and Electron. Labels are fixed words and never contain item names or values.
- **Everything else** (Settings images and icons, the checklist, the palette): part A's host already cancels the web view's default menu outside text fields and selected text, so these show no menu. Text fields keep Cut/Copy/Paste.

### Bridge
Adds `agents.remove` (`persistent_agent_remove`) and `agents.stop` (`agent_stop`, `{spaceId, runId}`). The daemon already had both tools. This change wires them into the web contract (protocol, shapes, `bridge-shapes.json`, coverage), the Mac app host (`WebUIBridge.agents`), Electron (`PersistentAgents.remove/stopRun`) and the demo host. Tauri reports them as unsupported, because its tool allow-list creates and deletes nothing. No change to part A's plumbing.

### Decisions
- No **Edit** for Keyvault items, because no edit action for an item exists in the core or the bridge.
- No **copy of a secret's value**, because the UI only ever has the redacted list.
- **Notifications** (Open, Mark as Read, Open Space) wait for #5196 (CUA-1636), which adds expandable rows and `notifications.markRead`. #5196 has merged. The commit is ready and goes in after the retarget. Mark as Unread and Dismiss are left out because the daemon can only mark entries read.

### Tests
- Web vitest: `src/__tests__/context-menus-pages.test.tsx` covers the menus on the real Agents page and Keyvault list (wasm core, demo host): items by state, Open selects, Stop calls `agents.stop`, Remove and Delete run only after confirming, Copy Name copies the name, and labels never name the item. The full suite passes locally (567 tests).
- Electron: `test/agents.test.ts` covers `agents.remove` and `agents.stop` through the host (the tools' args, the list read again, failed, bad_args, unsupported). The full suite passes locally (548 tests).
- Swift: `WebUIHostTests.agentsRemoveAndStopRunTheDaemonsTools` and the unsupported/bad_args cases. `WebUIHostTests`, `BridgeContractTests` and `AgentsPagesTests` pass locally.

### Verified on a signed build
CI build `0.9.1-ctxmenus.b1` (Developer ID signed and notarized; this branch plus #5196 plus the notifications commit), on a spare test Mac, in both the Mac app's New UI and Electron:
- Agents: the row's native menu shows Open, Pause, Copy Name and Remove…. The detail header shows the same menu without Open. Remove… asks first, then removes the agent (it's gone from the page and from `cua agent persistent`).
- Notifications: Open, Mark as Read (unread only) and Copy Text. Mark as Read and Open both work.
- Right-clicking an icon on the Keyvault page shows no menu. The test Mac has no Keyvault, so the item menu is covered by the web tests only.

### Before merge
Once #5197 merges: retarget to main, add the notifications commit, rerun CI, then squash-merge.

title: fix(spaces): list the Spaces on your other machines with their live state (CUA-1638, CUA-1637)
body:
Fixes CUA-1638 and CUA-1637.

**For users:**
- The Spaces on a Mac that has "Provide Spaces" on now show on every other device signed in to the same account, labelled "on <machine>". This covers its own Linux and macOS Spaces, not only the ones other devices created there.
- Each Space shows what it is actually doing:
  - Starting while it boots or joins the relay. Before, it showed Stopped (CUA-1637).
  - Running or Stopped.
  - Failed, with the reason.
  - When its machine is offline, it says so.
- You can open, start and stop these Spaces from the other device.
- The same list is used everywhere: the Mac app (classic and New UI), Electron, the menu bar and notch counts, and `cua sandbox ls`.

- **Machines page:** each computer is listed once, under its computer name. Reinstalls, sign-ins and host setups used to leave the same Mac behind as several rows: "This Mac", "Dillons-MacBook-Pro-2.local" and "Dillon's MacBook Pro (2)" for one laptop.

### Causes
- **Spaces missing (CUA-1638):** a Space got a relay entry only when another device created it through the relay. Spaces made on the providing machine itself were never put on the relay, and nothing else listed them.
- **"Stopped" while starting (CUA-1637):** the relay only says whether a Space's connection is up right now. Every app turned "not connected" into Stopped, so a Space that was being created, booting or joining the relay read Stopped. The machine running it knew the real state, but nothing asked it.

### What changes
- **The providing machine publishes its own Spaces** (`HostSpacesServer::publish_own`, run by `cua daemon` every 20 s):
  - It runs while "Provide Spaces" is on and the machine is signed in.
  - Each Space made on the machine gets a relay entry under the machine. The entry id comes from the machine id and the Space id, so a Space is published once. Only the owner can see it.
  - A running Space's driver is attached to its entry. A stopped Space is attached when it is started, from any device.
  - These Spaces count as provided Spaces, so the existing remote start, stop and delete work for them. They do not count toward the machine's `max_spaces` limit.
  - Turning "Provide Spaces" off takes them off the relay again. A refused registration, such as the account's relay machine limit, is retried every 2 minutes instead of on every pass.
- **The host reports state:** each Space in `GetHostSpaces` now carries `state` (running, starting, suspended, stopped or failed) and `state_reason`, read from its runtime.
- **One roster in the core** (`cua-spaces/src/pool_roster.rs`):
  - `Spaces::list_all` asks each of the account's machines that provides Spaces for its listing. It does this through the relay, at most every 5 s per machine, with a 4 s budget each. A machine that doesn't answer is left alone for 30 s.
  - `Spaces::list` gives each Space on another machine that machine's state, in `power_state` plus `state_reason`. The daemon's `ListSpaces`, the SDK's `SpaceInfo` and the apps' rows carry it.
- **Apps:**
  - The app core maps `starting` to Starting (Provisioning), and `failed` to "Failed · <reason>" with Start offered. A row whose machine is offline says why.
  - The Swift and Electron shells pass the reason through, and skip their 4 s probe for Spaces their machine says are starting, failed or off.
  - The New UI bridge keeps these states.
- **CLI:** `cua sandbox ls` also lists the Spaces on your other machines, as "on <machine>" with their state (JSON: `location: relay`, `machine`, `state`, `reason`).

- **One computer per row** (app core `machines::merge`):
  - A machine and a device are paired by their computer name, however it is spelled ("Dillon's MacBook Pro (2)" and "Dillons-MacBook-Pro-2.local").
  - A stale identity folds into the one live row of that computer. Stale means offline and, for a device, not seen for a day.
  - A machine named after its hostname takes its device's computer name.
  - A host whose relay entry still has the hostname an older setup gave it renames it once to its computer name (`label_own_machine`, an owner `PATCH`). A name the owner chose is kept.
  - Two computers that share a name, or that are both in use, stay apart.
- **Steadier states:**
  - While its runtimes are slow to list (cloning or booting a VM), a host answers with its last listing, and lists a Space it is turning on as starting.
  - A client keeps a machine's last answer when one read fails.
  - Spaces whose driver can't join the relay are not published.
  - Every Space the host provides on the relay is attached again after its driver loses the relay, for example after a daemon restart.

### Compatibility
- **No relay change.** This uses `POST /v1/machines` with `host` and `GET /v1/machines`, which the current prod relay already serves.
- **Old clients** keep working. They already list relay Spaces that have a `host`, so they also see the published Spaces, with their old connected-or-Stopped status.
- **Old hosts** list no states. Their Spaces read as they did before.
- **Live states need the new cua-spacesd on the providing machine.** cua-spacesd forwards the host's listing typed, and an older one drops the new fields. This PR changes a cua-spacesd test so its next release carries them. Publishing needs only the new `cua` daemon.
- **CUA-1527:** Spaces are still never machines, since they have a `host` and a `space-` id. On the providing machine each published Space is listed once, as its local Space.
- Fields added to protos: `HostSpace.state` = 12, `HostSpace.state_reason` = 13, `cua.daemon.v1.Space.state_reason` = 21. Field 8 of `GetHostSpacesResponse` and field 10 of `CreateHostSpaceRequest` stay free for CUA-1635.

### With CUA-1635
A create still running on another machine reads Starting with the step it is on, such as "Downloading the image, 41%…". This comes from the machine's `creating` listing (#5198), keyed by the Space's relay entry. This PR reuses those fields and adds none of its own.

### Tests
- **`cua-spaces` `tests/host_spaces.rs`**, `spaces_made_on_a_providing_machine_list_on_other_devices_with_their_state`. It runs against the fake relay, a fake runtime and a second device's `Spaces`, and checks:
  - publishing happens once, and only when signed in;
  - the host lists each Space once and its limit is untouched;
  - the other device lists the Spaces "on Mac mini (spare)", Running and Suspended;
  - a Space started from the other device reads Starting, then Running;
  - a Space stopped from the other device reads Stopped;
  - with the host offline, the Spaces say why;
  - with "Provide Spaces" off, they leave the relay.
- **`cua-spaces` `pool_roster` unit tests:** state mapping, including a create still running there, and which machines are asked.
- **App core:** `a_space_on_another_machine_reads_its_machines_state`.
- **cua-spacesd-server:** the host's states reach the caller through the driver.

title: ci: PR runs restore Rust caches but never save them
body:
Part of CUA-1653 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-1653).

**Problem.** The repo's Actions cache is capped at 10 GB but holds about 18.9 GB. GitHub evicts the least recently used entries, so entries live about 10 minutes. 24 of the 30 live entries were Rust caches saved by PR runs, and other PRs can't restore those. In the last runs I sampled, only 7 of about 41 rust-cache restores in PR jobs found anything. Examples of cold builds:
- SwiftUI app job: "Cache not found", then a 34 min cold `cargo build --release -p cua-spaces-ffi` (run 38638558590).
- In #5186's dry run, a native cache saved at 20:06 was gone by 20:35 for the same key.

**Change.**
- Every `Swatinem/rust-cache` step in PR-triggered and reusable workflows: `save-if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}` (38 steps, 24 files). Steps that already had a `save-if` are unchanged. Main, schedule and dispatch runs still save, and PRs restore main's cache.
- `ci-cua-spaces.yml` and `ci-openkoalabot-example-tauri.yml` (2.4 GB entries): `actions/cache` is split into restore, plus a save step that runs only outside PRs.

No tests, jobs or required checks are removed. CD workflows are not touched (`cd-cua-spaces.yml` belongs to #5186).

title: fix(cua-driver): send key identity with browser_type keystrokes
body:
Fixes #5212

## What changes for users

Agents can now press Enter in a search or combobox field in a background browser tab (`browser_type` with `mode: "keystrokes"` and `"\n"`), and pages that check `keyCode`/`code` see real key identities.

`browser_type` keystrokes sent `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` with only `key`, so Chromium delivered `code: ""` and `keyCode: 0`. Other characters keep the previous key-only shape.

## Testing

- `keystrokes_use_char_events_for_text_delivery` now asserts `KeyA`/65 and `Enter`/13 on every phase.
- New `keystroke_identity_covers_enter_space_letters_and_digits` unit test.

- Manual: against a hidden tab in Chrome 155 on macOS 26.6.1, the old event shape logged `kd:Enter//0` and didn't submit; the new shape logged `kd:Enter/Enter/13` and submitted.

title: fix(spaces): Back after a refused window drop shows the whole app picker (CUA-1671)
body:
Fixes CUA-1671.

**What changes for users:** drag a window onto a Space, and if its app can't be teleported (for example TextEdit), Back now shows the full app picker, the same as the Space's "Teleport an app" button. Before, it showed an empty "No apps match." list. This works in the New UI (Mac app and Electron) and in the classic Mac UI.

**Why:** a drop opens the sheet straight at the dropped app and never reads the app list (catalog). Back then landed on a picker with no catalog loaded.

- Core (`teleport/flow.rs`): Back from an app's options or error always leads to the full picker. If the catalog hasn't been read yet, it goes to the loading step, and the picker appears once the list arrives, with the same selection as a fresh picker. A drop clears the search.
- React store (`bridge/teleport.ts`): Back onto the loading step reads the catalog. A failed read is retried; before, it could hang on "Loading apps…".
- SwiftUI (`TeleportModel.swift`): the same read on Back.
- Tests:
  - core: `back_from_a_dropped_app_shows_the_whole_grid`;
  - web: two tests with the wasm core (a refused drop then Back; a catalog read that fails then succeeds on retry);
  - Swift: `backFromADroppedAppShowsTheWholeGrid`.

title: fix(spaces): window-drag detection survives a slow first drag (CUA-1670)
body:
Fixes CUA-1670.

**What changes for users:** dragging a window onto a Space tile, or onto the notch, keeps working after the first drag, in both the Mac app and Electron. Before, the first drag (often the one that raises macOS's screen-capture consent) could switch off drag detection for the rest of the session.

**Why:** the macOS event tap called the app's listener on the tap's own thread. In Electron that call waits for the JS thread, which was busy capturing the ghost image while the consent prompt was up. In the Mac app, the dragged window's app was matched against the catalog on that same thread. macOS switches off a tap whose callback is slow. We ignored the "tap disabled" event, and the "never start a second tracker" guard kept the dead tap in place.

- `cua-teleport` (`ux/window_macos.rs`, `ux/window.rs`):
  - The tap thread only works out the drag and queues events. A separate thread runs the listener and the app lookup, coalescing stale moves.
  - A disabled tap is re-enabled. If it keeps dying, or stops on its own, the tracker ends with a `stopped` event and `is_running()` turns false.
  - Mouse-down remembers up to 4 windows under the cursor, skipping fully transparent ones.
- Electron (`notch/model.ts`) and the Mac app (`NotchController.swift`) drop a stopped tracker and start a fresh one on the next readiness check, activation or toggle, or within 2 s.
- Logging: `[cua] window drag:` lines on stderr (tap up, failed, disabled and re-enabled, stopped). With `CUA_SPACES_NOTCH_DEBUG=1`, the windows under the cursor at mouse-down are logged too.
- Tests: Rust (6 new: re-enable, give up, coalescing, slow listener never blocks the tap, invisible window on top), Electron (stopped tracker restarts, late stop from an old tracker ignored), Swift (stopped tracker restarts).

title: [Bug]: cua-spacesd streams a black desktop on GNOME 50 Wayland (captures rootless Xwayland :0)
body:
### Primary area

Other (Cua Spaces / cua-spacesd direct host)

### Summary

On an Ubuntu 26.04 host running GNOME 50 on Wayland, a machine added to Cua Spaces by address (`cua-spacesd` direct host) streams an all-black desktop. The stream itself is healthy (frames are encoded), but `cua-spacesd` appears to capture the rootless Xwayland display `:0`, which has no visible content under a GNOME Wayland session.

### Reproduction

1. On Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland session — Ubuntu 26.04 ships no Xorg session), install `cua-spacesd` 0.5.3 as the unattended-access user service (`cua-spacesd-host.service`), with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1` set via a drop-in.
2. Log in to the GNOME desktop on the physical seat (`gdm-wayland-session`).
3. From Cua Spaces on macOS, add the machine by address (`direct:<host>:3211`) and open the Space.
4. The Space shows `Running` and the `Desktop (1920x1080)` stream target, but the desktop preview is black (reproduces every time).

### Expected behavior

The Space stream shows the user's GNOME desktop (or reports that Wayland capture is unsupported instead of streaming black frames).

### Actual behavior

- The desktop preview in the Space is fully black.
- `driver.log` shows the encoder running normally, with no capture errors, e.g.
  `INFO cua_spacesd_client::encoder: encoder stopped seconds="41.2" frames=15 fps="0.4" avg_ms="12.6" max_ms="15.7"`
- The `cua-spacesd` process environment has `DISPLAY=:0`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`.
- `driver.log` contains no `wayland` / `portal` / `pipewire` entries, so the Wayland opt-in does not seem to affect the stream path.

I don't know the exact capture backend the encoder uses; the X11 grab below reproduces the same black frame, which is why I suspect it is X11 capture of Xwayland `:0`.

### Environment

- Cua component and version: `cua-spacesd` 0.5.3 (latest `cua-spacesd` release), `cua` CLI 0.4.1, `cua-driver` 0.22.1; client: Cua Spaces app on macOS
- OS and architecture: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic, x86_64
- Window system: GNOME Shell 50.1 on Wayland, Xwayland 24.1.10 (rootless, `:0`); no X11 session available (`/usr/share/xsessions` absent)
- GPU: NVIDIA GA107 (RTX 3050) + AMD Granite Ridge iGPU; VA-API opens `radeonsi`
- Screen lock: inactive (`org.gnome.ScreenSaver.GetActive` → `false`)

### Evidence

Capturing both X displays on the host with ffmpeg:

```
ffmpeg -f x11grab -video_size 1920x1080 -i :0  -frames:v 1 cap_0.png   # all black, cursor only
ffmpeg -f x11grab -video_size 1920x1080 -i :99 -frames:v 1 cap_99.png  # separate Xvfb with a Chrome window, renders normally
```

So X11 capture works in general; it is black only for the Xwayland display of the GNOME Wayland session, which matches what the Space shows.

### Workaround and additional context

- Workaround: point `cua-spacesd` at a separate Xvfb display (`Environment=DISPLAY=:<n>` in the service drop-in). This shows that display, not the user's GNOME desktop.
- Related: #2675 (cua-driver captures 0x0 on Fedora 44 GNOME 50 Wayland), #1922 (Linux screen capture is X11-only). Neither covers the Spaces stream path.
- Possible direction: capture via the xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast / PipeWire path (or Mutter's ScreenCast D-Bus API) on GNOME Wayland, or fail visibly when only a rootless Xwayland display is available.

title: fix(cua): split the rest of create runtime errors and explain the macOS VM limit (CUA-1356)
body:
Refs CUA-1356.

## Why
`runtime` is still the top failed-create kind: 67 `cua_sandbox_created` errors in the last 7 days (non-CI). Every one comes from a CLI build that predates the fixes already on main: 0.4.1 (5 Oct), or 0.2.0 (one Windows install, 14 errors). Rough split:
- Windows, about half (34): mostly no Docker engine, or `--runtime qemu|gvisor|runc` without that runtime installed. #5000 and #5111 already fix the messages and pipe discovery on main.
- macOS, 20: Linux containers failing in under 1 s (11), and macOS VMs on Lume (9). The Lume ones are the 2-VM cap, Local Network access and failed image pulls; the same installs succeed before and after.
- Linux, 12: no engine, or an engine that is stopped or denies access. #5000 already covers these.

The fixes on main reach users only when the next `cua-sdk` release ships (release PR #4672).

## What changes
- **Telemetry:** the error causes that still landed in `runtime` now get bounded kinds: `local_network`, `vm_limit`, `vm_runtime_missing` (QEMU, Lume or UEFI firmware), `container_exited`, `vm_error` (QEMU or Lume failed) and `engine_error`. They are fixed words, never message text. The daily report groups by `error_kind`, so it splits the old bucket with no report change.
- **CLI message:** when Lume refuses a start with HTTP 409 at Apple's limit of two macOS VMs, the error now tells the user how to free a slot: stop one in Cua Spaces, or run `cua sb ls` then `cua sb suspend <name>`.
- **Spaces app:** the VM-limit check now also matches Lume's own 409 wording. Before, it matched only Virtualization.framework's text, so this case showed the raw error.

## For users
A failed Space create on Apple's two-VM limit now says what to do. The next report shows what `runtime` failures remain, by cause.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p cua-vmm` (classifier cases; a scripted Lume 409)
- `cargo test -p cua-sdk` (create_error_kind maps each new kind to a schema word)
- `cargo test -p cua-spaces-app-core` (spaces::creating)
- `cargo test -p cua-telemetry`

title: cua-driver: browser_click trusted route refuses in standalone Chrome; dom_event fallback can't be verified
body:
## What happened

In the same existing-profile Chrome session, `browser_type` with `mode: keystrokes` worked in the background, through the trusted Input route. But `browser_click` on a button in the same tab was refused:

`browser_input_trust_unavailable: Chromium's trusted CDP Input route activates its standalone browser window on macOS`

The suggested fallback, `input_route: dom_event`, dispatched a synthetic click with `effect: unverifiable`. In this case the click did work: an "Enter address manually" button expanded the address fields. But the agent has to take a new snapshot every time to find out whether it worked. On trust-gated controls, such as payment submit buttons, a synthetic click is likely to be ignored.

## Expected

- Typing and clicking should behave the same way in the background. If keystrokes can be delivered without activating the window, mouse events should be possible too (for example `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` to a background target with focus emulation), or the tool should explain why they can't.
- When `dom_event` is used, the tool should check a cheap postcondition itself, such as DOM mutation or an aria-expanded change, so the effect isn't left as `unverifiable`.
- The refusal should name the exact option to pass for foreground delivery. The hint mentions `delivery_mode="foreground"`, but that parameter isn't in the `browser_click` schema.

## Environment

macOS 26, Chrome stable, existing profile, cua-driver typed browser tools.

title: [Bug]: element-token scroll aims outside the window when the element is taller than it
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `scroll` with an element token aims the wheel at the centre of the element's full AX frame. When the element is taller (or wider) than the window, as a long text view or web area usually is, that centre lies outside the window, so background delivery is refused even though most of the window is that element.

### Reproduction

1. Open a window whose scrollable content element is taller than the window, for example a long document in a text view or web area.
2. `get_window_state` for that window and take the content element's `element_index`.
3. Call `scroll` with that `element_index`, `delivery_mode: background`, and a direction that takes the wheel path (left/right for an AppKit text area; up/down there goes through the AX scroll bar instead).

Seen every time on an element taller than the window. Pixel-targeted scroll at a window-local point inside the same element works.

### Expected behavior

The wheel is posted at a point that is on the element and inside the window, and the element scrolls.

### Actual behavior

The tool returns the outside-window refusal from `tools/scroll.rs`:

```
scroll: window-local point (…) pt lies outside window <id>'s W×H pt frame; background delivery refused
```

The window-local point is the centre of the whole element frame, which sits below (or past) the window edge.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.34.0 (seen); code path unchanged on `main` at 9c97c20ad
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.7.1, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: native macOS apps; AppKit text area and long scroll views

### Evidence

No reproduction recording available. I saw the refusal while driving a real window with 0.34.0 but did not keep the exact output, and a later attempt with the AppKit fixture did not reach the wheel path because the fixture window opened on another Space (`off_space_or_ax_unresolved`).

Code path: after `AXScrollToVisible`, the element branch of `ScrollTool` takes `element_screen_center(element)` as the wheel point. For an element larger than the window, `AXScrollToVisible` cannot bring that centre on screen, and the background guard then refuses the out-of-frame point.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: scroll by window-local screenshot pixels instead of the element token.

Suspected fix: aim at the centre of the element frame intersected with the window bounds, and keep the old centre (and the existing refusal) when they do not overlap. `ax/reveal_scroll.rs` already has an `intersect` helper for this. I have a small PR with unit tests ready.

title: [Bug]: Wayland window capture fails on Umbriel (wlroots) although ext-foreign-toplevel-image-capture-source is available
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On a native-Wayland wlroots compositor with no compositor-specific adapter (Umbriel), `get_window_state(include_screenshot: true)` always fails with `surface_identity_unproven`, and `list_windows` reports no pid and zero geometry. The compositor exposes `ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1` + `ext_image_copy_capture_manager_v1`, so per-window capture should be reachable without a compositor-specific geometry provider.

### Reproduction

1. Run cua-driver 0.35.4 in an Umbriel session with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`.
2. Call `list_windows` — the single window is reported with `pid=?` and geometry `0x0+0+0`.
3. Call `get_window_state` with that `window_id` and `include_screenshot: true`.

Reproduces every time.

### Expected behavior

Either the requested window's own pixels, or a refusal that names the missing capability. Since the compositor implements the `ext-image-copy-capture` stack, a per-toplevel capture source is available to build on.

### Actual behavior

`list_windows`:

```
Found 1 windows:
  window_id=4278190080 pid=? "<title> [kitty]" 0x0+0+0 app=kitty
```

`get_window_state`:

```
surface_identity_unproven: Wayland capture cannot prove pixels belong to window 4278190080:
no compositor-attested window geometry is available
```

Display capture succeeds in the same session (`get_desktop_state` returns the full output).

### Environment

- Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.35.4 (`cua-driver-rs-v0.35.4`, commit `d74a9ca`)
- Operating system and architecture: CachyOS (Arch), x86_64, glibc
- Application/browser/window system: Umbriel 0.1.0 (wlroots 0.20.3), native Wayland, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`, single output at scale 1.0

### Evidence

**Where it refuses.** `platform-linux/src/wayland/mod.rs` `wayland_window_crop()` consults only `sway_ipc::window_for_id` (Sway IPC) and `shell_helper::list_windows` (GNOME helper) before returning the error above. Correspondingly, `list_windows()` correlates wlr-foreign-toplevel handles against `sway_ipc` records and otherwise falls back to the connection-local protocol id with no pid and zero geometry.

**The compositor has what is needed.** Umbriel's in-tree protocol harness asserts these globals are present:

```
zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1
ext_output_image_capture_source_manager_v1
ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1
ext_image_copy_capture_manager_v1
ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1
```

and it accepts toplevel capture requests (`wlr_ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1_request_accept` in `server_events.cpp`). So a generic path built on the ext capture source would work here without any Umbriel-specific code.

**Upstream already tracks this.** `platform-linux/src/wayland/ext_screencopy.rs` module docs say:

> Per-window capture (ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1) is a follow-up — needs the existing `list_windows` to migrate from `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` to `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` so the window_id handles match up.

**Related.** #4377 (KWin — same symptom, optional helper not installed), #3399 (Hyprland — resolved by adding a compositor-specific adapter in 0.24.0).

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: desktop scope works today — `get_desktop_state` plus `target: {kind: "desktop", display_id: "primary"}` on input, verifying with a second desktop snapshot.

title: [Feature]: macOS agent cursor should draw on the display that contains the target, not only the main display
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On macOS with more than one display, the agent cursor overlay is drawn only on the **main display** (the one with the menu bar). When an agent clicks an element in a window that sits on a secondary display, the overlay cursor is not drawn over that window. Depending on the layout it is either not visible at all, or it appears pinned along the edge of the main display nearest the target. In my layout the secondary display sits directly below the main display, so the cursor slides along the bottom edge of the main display while the click actually lands on the other screen.

That defeats the purpose of the agent cursor: a person watching can't see what is being clicked, and the cursor appearing in the wrong place is actively misleading ("why is it clicking on my TV?").

Setup where observed: macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon, three displays (main external 3008×1692 pt at origin; built-in 1800×1169 pt directly below it at y = 1692; portrait external to the left at negative X). cua-driver 0.22.2; behaviour confirmed by reading current `main`.

### Desired outcome

The agent cursor is drawn on whichever display contains the target point / target window, so it appears exactly over the element being acted on, on every connected display. Cursors keep animating smoothly when a motion crosses from one display to another.

### Current workaround

Disable the agent cursor (`set_agent_cursor_enabled false`) whenever the target window is not on the main display. Clicks still work (AX path), but you lose the visual feedback, which is the whole point of the cursor.

Alternatively, make the target's display the main display in System Settings, which moves the menu bar and Dock and only helps for that one display.

### Affected components and platforms

macOS agent cursor overlay: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs`.

From reading `main`:
- `run_appkit()` creates one borderless NSWindow sized to `NSScreen.mainScreen.frame` (around line 648).
- `on_main_screen()` only rejects points more than 50 pt left of/above the origin, but anything past the right/bottom edge of the main screen is still "painted" into a pixmap that is only main-screen-sized, so it is clipped or never visible.
- `backing_scale` is taken from the main screen only.
- The module doc comment says the window "covers `NSScreen.mainScreen.frame`".

Windows already spans the virtual screen (per your blog post on synthetic cursors), and Hyprland multi-monitor was handled in #4305, so macOS seems to be the remaining gap.

### Alternatives and prior art

- #4276 (element clicks on a second display are slow even with the agent cursor disabled): same multi-display area, different symptom.
- #4305: multi-monitor Hyprland support.
- #1981: Windows negative-X multi-monitor validation.

### Implementation ideas

One overlay NSWindow per `NSScreen` (recreated on `NSApplicationDidChangeScreenParametersNotification`), each with its own pixmap and that screen's `backingScaleFactor`. Paint each cursor into the overlay whose screen frame contains its position, translating global top-left points into that screen's local coordinates (AppKit's bottom-left global space needs the usual flip against the primary screen height, and negative-X/negative-Y screens must be handled). Replace the `on_main_screen` gate with "find the screen containing pos". During a cross-screen glide, painting into both overlays for the frames where the cursor straddles the boundary avoids a visible jump.

Happy to test a build on a three-display setup (including a display below and one at negative X).

title: fix(spaces): Set up installs and checks cua-driver before saying done (CUA-1797)
body:
## What was wrong

In Cua Spaces (macOS, 0.9.x), Settings → **Background computer use** → **Set up** (and the same card in the first-run "AI agents" step) reported "Claude Code: done … cua-driver configured" while cua-driver wasn't on the machine. Agents then failed to start the server: `/mcp` → `ENOENT: Executable not found in $PATH: cua-driver`.

## Root cause

- **Nothing installed cua-driver.** cua-driver isn't bundled with Cua Spaces. On macOS it is its own signed app (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, the identity that gets Accessibility and Screen Recording), installed by `cua.ai/driver/install.sh`. The `cua.ai/install.sh` "cua-driver" item runs that installer and then `cua agents setup --cua-driver`. The app's Set up ran only the second half.
- **A bare `cua-driver` command was written.** `McpServer::driver_for` looks for cua-driver on the PATH and in `~/.local/bin`. When it found nothing, it fell back to the bare name `cua-driver`, and `setup_cua_driver` wrote that into every agent's MCP config. GUI agents like VS Code and Claude Desktop don't get the shell PATH, so a bare name fails even when the binary exists somewhere.
- **"Done" was never checked.** A row was "done" as soon as the config file was written. Nothing checked that the command exists or that `cua-driver mcp` answers.
- **Not a code regression.** This behaviour dates from the SDK merge (#4397); the Settings card (#4893) put it in front of more people. On machines that still had the legacy `/usr/local/bin/cua-driver` link from older cua-driver installers, the PATH lookup found it and wrote an absolute path, so Set up appeared to work there. Without that link it wrote the bare name.

## Fix

- **`cua-agent-setup`: new `driver` module.**
  - `locate` finds cua-driver: on the PATH, in `~/.local/bin`, then inside `CuaDriver.app`.
  - `check` runs `cua-driver mcp` and sends an MCP `initialize`; it passes only on a valid answer.
  - `install` downloads cua-driver's release installer (`cua.ai/driver/install.sh`, or `install.ps1` on Windows) and runs it. That installer verifies the archive against `SHA256SUMS` and checks the `CuaDriver.app` signature. Its output goes to `~/.cua/logs/cua-driver-install.log`.
  - `ensure` uses an existing cua-driver that passes `check`, and otherwise installs one and checks it again.
- **`AgentSetup::setup_cua_driver`.** The MCP server is written only by absolute path, and only after `check` passes. Otherwise each agent's `cua-driver` row fails with the reason, and its config is left unchanged. Re-running Set up repairs entries that point at a missing binary: the entry is updated to the checked absolute path.
- **SDK `AgentSetup.setup_cua_driver`** (the Set up button in the SwiftUI and Electron apps) calls `ensure` first, so it installs cua-driver when it's missing or broken. A failed row says how to fix it: "Set up again to retry, or install it with: …".
- **UI.** The SwiftUI first-run view now shows each failure reason under the agent's row; before, it was only in a tooltip. The shared web card (used by both the Mac app and Electron) wraps the reason instead of truncating it.
- **`cua agents setup --cua-driver`** no longer writes a bare entry. When cua-driver is missing it fails with the reason and prints the install one-liner, as before.

## Verification

All runs used a real `Cua Spaces.app` (release build of this repo) on a spare macOS 26 Mac. Each run had a throwaway `HOME` containing Claude Code 2.1.301, a Copilot CLI dir and a VS Code user dir. `CUA_AGENT_APP_DIRS` pointed into that home, so the Mac's own `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` didn't count as installed. I drove the app with cua-driver.

1. **main (9737d6f), reproduced.** First-run AI agents → **Set up** showed "Claude Code: done / … / VS Code (Copilot agent mode): done". `~/.claude.json` and VS Code `mcp.json` got `"command": "cua-driver"`. `cua-driver mcp` in a shell → `command not found`. `claude mcp list` → `cua-driver: cua-driver mcp - ✘ Failed to connect — ENOENT: Executable not found in $PATH: "cua-driver"`.
2. **This branch, identical steps.** Set up ran cua-driver's installer (cua-driver-rs 0.35.4: SHA256SUMS verified; the existing Accessibility and Screen Recording grants were kept). The rows said "done", and both configs got `"command": "<home>/.local/bin/cua-driver"`. `cua-driver mcp` answered `initialize` from a fresh shell. `claude mcp list` → `cua-driver: … - ✔ Connected`.
3. **Repair.** I ran this branch against the home that main had broken, using Settings → Background computer use → **Set up** in the web UI. The Claude Code and VS Code entries changed from `cua-driver` to the absolute path, and `claude mcp list` → `✔ Connected`.
4. **Failure path.** I made the install impossible: a directory sits where the `cua-driver` link goes. The rows read "Claude Code: failed", followed by "the cua-driver installer finished, but no cua-driver was found. Set up again to retry, or install it with: …". No `cua-driver` MCP entry was written.
5. **Neighbouring flows didn't change.** The cua MCP server and cua skills were written the same on main and on this branch, and `cua: … mcp - ✔ Connected` both times. The `cua agents` CLI tests pass.

Tests: `cargo test -p cua-agent-setup` covers these cases:
- a missing driver fails and leaves the config untouched;
- a driver that never answers MCP fails;
- a bare entry is repaired to an absolute path;
- the binary inside `CuaDriver.app` is found.

`cargo test -p cua-cli --test agents_login` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` pass on the changed crates.

## Not verified / known limits

- **Not run:** the Windows install path (`install.ps1` via PowerShell), Linux, and the Electron app. Electron uses the same SDK call and web card.
- **Running sessions are interrupted.** cua-driver's installer stops a running cua-driver daemon while it swaps the app, so agent sessions using cua-driver drop during Set up.
- **Fresh machines still need permissions.** Set up doesn't ask for Accessibility or Screen Recording; cua-driver asks the first time it's used. On an upgrade, the installer keeps the existing grants.
- **First-run heading is unchanged.** The heading still reads "Your AI agents are set up" when a row failed. That copy wasn't changed.

title: [Bug]: Super shortcuts from the Spaces viewer never reach the guest compositor (Omarchy/Hyprland)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (Spaces interactive input on Hyprland guests: cua-spacesd → cua-driver tools)

### Summary

When a person drives an Omarchy (Hyprland) Space from the Spaces viewer, Super chords never reach the guest compositor. Super+W arrives in the focused window as a plain `w`, so none of Omarchy's Super-based Hyprland bindings can be used from the viewer. Ctrl, Alt and Shift chords arrive correctly.

### Reproduction

1. Run Cua Spaces 0.9.3 (Linux AppImage) and open an Omarchy Space (`ghcr.io/trycua/omarchy`, local QEMU VM), streaming the desktop.
2. In the Space, open a terminal and run `showkey -a`.
3. Focus the Space window and press, one at a time: Alt+W, Super+Shift+W, Shift+W, Super+W, Ctrl+W, then Ctrl+D.
4. Compare what `showkey` prints with what was pressed, and note that Super+W does not close the window (Omarchy binds SUPER+W to close).

Reproduced with the physical keyboard and with `wtype` injecting the same chords into the focused Space window.

### Expected behavior

Keyboard input on a desktop stream behaves like a physical keyboard: Super+W reaches Hyprland as SUPER+W and triggers the binding (closes the window), the same way the chord would on the machine itself.

### Actual behavior

| Pressed in the Space window | Received by the focused window (`showkey -a`) |
|---|---|
| Super+W | `w` (119); the Hyprland binding does not fire |
| Super+Shift+W | `W`; Super has no effect |
| Ctrl+W | `^W` (23) ✅ |
| Alt+W | `ESC w` (27, 119) ✅ |

In the same Space, `cua do hotkey super+return` does trigger the Omarchy binding (a terminal opens), so Hyprland accepts injected Super chords that arrive through that route.

### Environment

- Viewer host: CachyOS (Arch), niri 26.04 Wayland session, Cua Spaces 0.9.3 AppImage (bundled `cua` 0.4.1)
- Guest: Omarchy image (`ghcr.io/trycua/omarchy`), local QEMU VM, cua-spacesd 0.5.3, cua-driver-bin 0.33.4, cua-hyprland-plugin 0.33.2, Hyprland 0.56.2
- Same result before upgrading the guest's cua-driver from 0.28.2.

### Evidence

- `showkey -a` capture summarized above.
- The modifier name survives the pipeline: the viewer encodes `metaKey` as `command`, cua-spacesd maps `InputModifier::Command` to the driver's `Modifier::Command` ([driver_input.rs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85d001220940b7fb171634ba5de9262082fbbdd3/libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/driver_input.rs#L111)), and the tool adapter names it `super` ([tool_input.rs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85d001220940b7fb171634ba5de9262082fbbdd3/libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/tool_input.rs#L186)).
- On Hyprland there is no stateful input session; each batch is folded into cua-driver tool calls ([lib.rs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85d001220940b7fb171634ba5de9262082fbbdd3/libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/lib.rs#L1079-L1083)). For a desktop target, every key becomes a `press_key` call addressed to the focused window (`pid`/`window_id`, foreground) with `modifiers: ["super"]` ([tool_input.rs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85d001220940b7fb171634ba5de9262082fbbdd3/libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/tool_input.rs#L275-L290), [L371-L378](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85d001220940b7fb171634ba5de9262082fbbdd3/libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/tool_input.rs#L371-L378)).
- Given the observed result, that window-addressed `press_key` route appears not to produce a compositor-visible Super chord, while `cua do hotkey` does. I have not traced which delivery the driver uses for that `press_key` call, so this is the likely location rather than a confirmed root cause.

### Workaround and additional context

- No in-viewer workaround; Super shortcuts cannot be used from the viewer.
- Related but separate: on Wayland hosts such as niri, the Space window does not request `zwp_keyboard_shortcuts_inhibit_v1`, so Super chords bound by the host compositor (e.g. Mod+Return, Mod+1..9) never reach the window at all. Remote-desktop style clients usually request the inhibitor while focused.

### Submission checks

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Feature]: Allow sending Super from Cua Spaces for macOS to Linux guests
body:
### Primary area

Other (Cua Spaces app — macOS, interactive Space viewer)

### User problem

When a Mac user operates a Linux Space from Cua Spaces for macOS, the Command key is always sent as Control and the Control key is also sent as Control. No key on the Mac keyboard produces Super (Meta/Win) in the guest.

That makes Super-centric Linux desktops unusable from the keyboard. The clearest case is Cua's own Omarchy image: Hyprland has about 180 Super-based bindings there (launching the terminal and launcher, closing windows, switching workspaces, tiling), and none of them can be triggered from the Mac viewer.

### Desired outcome

A way to send Super from macOS to non-macOS guests, for example one of:

- a per-Space or global setting "Send ⌘ as Super" (alongside the current "⌘ as Control" behavior);
- treating left and right Command differently (e.g. left ⌘ → Control, right ⌘ → Super);
- picking the mapping by guest desktop (e.g. Super for Hyprland/Omarchy images).

Keeping ⌘→Control as the default makes sense for copy/paste muscle memory; the problem is that the mapping is lossy (two Mac keys map to Control, none to Super) and cannot be changed.

### Current workaround

None inside Cua Spaces. Users have to leave the viewer: connect over VNC with a client that sends ⌘ as Super, or trigger individual shortcuts with `cua do hotkey super+…` from a terminal.

### Affected components and platforms

- Cua Spaces for macOS 0.9.3 (macOS 26.5.2): the native input path has `InputEncoder.commandAsControl`, and the bundled WebUI viewer enables `metaAsControl` when the host is macOS and the guest OS is not macOS.
- Any Linux or Windows guest whose shortcuts rely on Super/Win; most visibly the Omarchy image (Hyprland).
- Related: Super shortcuts sent from the viewer also do not reach the guest compositor on Hyprland (#5344), so currently no Spaces client can use Super-based shortcuts in a Linux guest.

title: [Feature]: Use the advertised QUIC media endpoint for direct Spaces
body:
### Primary area

Other (Cua Spaces app — macOS, desktop streaming transport)

### User problem

A Space registered by address (`cua spaces add <host>:<port>`, provider `direct`) is always streamed over the `/media` WebSocket on the spacesd TCP port, even when cua-spacesd advertises `sideChannels.mediaQuicPort = 3212`, lists the `quic_media` feature, and the UDP port is reachable from the client. Streaming over TCP is more exposed to latency spikes and head-of-line blocking than the direct QUIC media path the daemon already provides.

### Desired outcome

For direct Spaces, the client tries the advertised QUIC media endpoint (`<spacesd host>:mediaQuicPort`) and falls back to the WebSocket only when QUIC is unreachable — or the documentation states that direct Spaces never use QUIC, so users do not open UDP paths for nothing.

### Current workaround

None; the WebSocket is used.

### Affected components and platforms

Observed with:

- Client: Cua Spaces for macOS 0.9.3 (macOS 26.5.2), bundled `cua` daemon 0.4.1; Space registered as `direct:<tailnet-ip>:<port>`
- Server: Omarchy image, cua-spacesd 0.5.3; `caps` reports `mediaWsPath=/media`, `mediaQuicPort=3212`, features include `quic_media`

What was checked:

1. UDP from the Mac to `<spacesd host>:3212` reaches the guest's QUIC listener (verified with test datagrams through the path).
2. Restarted the Cua Spaces app and its daemon, then opened the Space window.
3. The Mac opens no UDP flow to port 3212, and cua-spacesd logs no QUIC session. Video arrives over a long-lived TCP connection to the spacesd port (several MB, continuously sending).

title: [Bug]: macOS background hotkey cmd+v reports success but an inactive WKWebView app never pastes; invoke_menu Edit > Paste works
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

With the target app in the background, `hotkey` with `["cmd","v"]` to a WKWebView page returns success ("Pressed cmd+v on pid N.") but the page receives no `paste` event. This happens both with `element_token` and with the `x`,`y` form that pixel-focuses first. Invoking the app's own Edit > Paste menu item with `invoke_menu` pastes into the same focused field. Probably AppKit routes Cmd+V through the main menu's key equivalents, which an app that is not active does not process, and WKWebView pastes only from the `paste:` action. The delivery matrix in #2239 covers native, Chromium and Electron surfaces, but not WKWebView (Tauri and other WebKit-based apps).

### Reproduction

1. An AppKit app with a standard Edit menu (Paste uses `paste:` with key equivalent `v`) and a WKWebView whose focused textarea logs `paste` events (`event.clipboardData.getData('text/plain')`). Launch it in the background (`open -g`).
2. Put a sentinel string on the general pasteboard.
3. `hotkey {pid, window_id, keys: ["cmd","v"], element_token}` (background delivery): "Pressed cmd+v on pid N."; the page logs nothing.
4. `hotkey {pid, window_id, keys: ["cmd","v"], x, y}`: same result.
5. `invoke_menu {pid, window_id, path: ["Edit","Paste"]}`: the page logs the sentinel (about 0.9 s).

### Expected behavior

Either the paste reaches the page, for example by performing the matching menu item's action for a key equivalent when the app is inactive, or the result says that background Cmd+V cannot reach this surface and recommends `invoke_menu` or foreground delivery, as #2239 asks for unsupported cells.

### Actual behavior

Steps 3 and 4 report success and nothing is pasted; step 5 works.

A related detail for callers who want to fall back to `invoke_menu`: in this inactive app's accessibility tree, `get_window_state` listed only the system-added items of the Edit menu (AutoFill, Emoji & Symbols); Cut, Copy and Paste were absent. `invoke_menu` still resolved `["Edit","Paste"]` live, and a wrong name failed with `menu_path_unavailable` before anything was pressed.

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.28.2, embedded daemon driven through the socket SDK; not re-tested on 0.36.0.
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple silicon.
- Target: minimal AppKit app hosting a WKWebView, launched in the background.

title: fix(cua-driver): aim element scroll at the part inside the window
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `scroll` with an element token posts the wheel at the centre of the element's whole AX frame. When the element is taller or wider than the window (a long text view or web area), that centre is outside the window, so background delivery is refused.
- What changed: the element path now aims at the centre of the element frame intersected with the window bounds. If they don't overlap, or either rect is unknown, it falls back to the old centre, so the existing outside-window refusal still applies.

## Related work

Fixes #5281

RFC: not needed, no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. An element that fits inside the window gets the same point as before. No schema or API change.
- Risk and rollback: low. One call site in `tools/scroll.rs`; `intersect()` in `ax/reveal_scroll.rs` is now `pub(crate)`. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: 4 new unit tests for the wheel point (element inside the window, taller than the window, partly above it, outside it). `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 606 passed. `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy` adds no new warnings.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. The AppKit fixture window opened on another Space on my machine, so I couldn't drive the wheel path live (details in the issue).

title: [Bug]: No way to require authentication on /ws for a self-hosted computer-server instance
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

reported on 9 sep 2026 via https://github.com/trycua/cua/security/advisories/GHSA-24j3-j457-p2mc:

`computer_server`'s WebSocket endpoint at `/ws` is the control channel for the full "computer use" surface: arbitrary shell command execution (`run_command`), file read/write anywhere on the host, and mouse/keyboard/window control. Authentication only exists for the cloud deployment mode (`CONTAINER_NAME` set, validated against TryCUA's own API). In the self-hosted mode, every command is accepted with no authentication at all, and there is no configuration option to change that short of taking the server fully offline via `UNAVAILABLE_WITHOUT_CONTAINER_NAME`. The project's own README documents running with `--host 0.0.0.0` specifically "for external access" and "other hosts should pass `--host 0.0.0.0`", without pairing that guidance with any way to secure the resulting reachable endpoint.

## Details

`libs/python/computer-server/computer_server/main.py`, `websocket_endpoint` (pre-fix):

```python
@app.websocket("/ws", name="websocket_endpoint")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    global handlers
    await manager.connect(websocket)
    server_container_name = os.environ.get("CONTAINER_NAME")
    if server_container_name:
        # ... authentication handshake against TryCUA's cloud API ...
    try:
        # every command, including run_command, is now dispatched with no
        # authentication check at all when server_container_name is unset
```

`AuthenticationManager.auth` documents this explicitly:

```python
# If no CONTAINER_NAME is set, always allow access (local development)
if not self.container_name:
    logger.info(
        "No CONTAINER_NAME set in environment. Allowing access (local development mode)"
    )
    return True
```

The one existing mitigation for this mode, `UNAVAILABLE_WITHOUT_CONTAINER_NAME`, is checked by `_unavailable_status_code()` and gates the `/cmd`, `/pty`, `/status`, and Playwright-exec HTTP endpoints, returning 503 when set. It does not authenticate the server, it disables it, and it is opt-in with no default. An operator following the README's `--host 0.0.0.0` guidance for reaching the server from another machine, without also knowing about and setting this flag, exposes full unauthenticated remote code execution; setting the flag instead makes the server unusable for its documented multi-host purpose.

### Reproduction

(poc included in ghsa)

### Expected behavior


## Fix

Add an opt-in `CUA_LOCAL_API_KEY` environment variable. When set, the WebSocket handshake requires a matching `api_key` (checked via `hmac.compare_digest`) in an `authenticate` command before any other command is dispatched. When unset, behavior is unchanged, preserving the project's own tested backwards-compatibility contract for zero-config local development (`tests/test_auth_availability.py`).

```diff
+LOCAL_API_KEY = os.environ.get("CUA_LOCAL_API_KEY")
+
 @app.websocket("/ws", name="websocket_endpoint")
 async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
     ...
     if server_container_name:
         # existing cloud auth handshake, unchanged
+    elif LOCAL_API_KEY:
+        auth_data = await websocket.receive_json()
+        if auth_data.get("command") != "authenticate":
+            await websocket.send_json({"success": False, "error": "First message must be authentication"})
+            await websocket.close(); return
+        client_api_key = auth_data.get("params", {}).get("api_key", "")
+        if not hmac.compare_digest(client_api_key, LOCAL_API_KEY):
+            await websocket.send_json({"success": False, "error": "Authentication failed"})
+            await websocket.close(); return
+        await websocket.send_json({"success": True, "message": "Authentication successful"})
```

New PoC/regression tests in `tests/test_ws_local_auth_poc.py`: key required when set, wrong key rejected, correct key accepted, and a backwards-compat guard confirming the zero-config case is untouched. Full existing suite, including `test_auth_availability.py`, passes after the change.


### Actual behavior

-

### Environment

Affected: `trycua/computer`, `computer-server` package, confirmed on commit `6c0348b` (current `main`), package version `0.3.45`.

### Evidence

-

### Workaround and additional context

_No response_

title: fix(cua-driver): keep trusting GNOME Shell and KWin after an update replaces their binary
body:
Salvaged from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5329

## Why
A distro update replaces `/usr/bin/gnome-shell` or `/usr/bin/kwin_wayland` while the compositor keeps running. `/proc/<pid>/exe` then reads `<path> (deleted)`, the old check called `fs::metadata` on that string and failed, and the driver stopped trusting the session's own Shell or KWin until the user logged out.

## What changed
- `proc_fs::running_executable` judges the running image. It opens `/proc/<pid>/exe` with `O_PATH`, rechecks the process instance, and drops the ` (deleted)` suffix only when the image has no links left. It accepts a replaced image only from the driver's mount namespace and from a mount the driver can see.
- `is_trusted_gnome_shell` and `is_trusted_kwin` both use `RunningExecutable::is_system_program`, which keeps the existing rule (matching `comm` and file name, root-owned, not group- or world-writable).
- The test fixtures now copy `sh` instead of `sleep`. Nix's multi-call coreutils `sleep` renames its `comm` to `sleep`, and that broke `Nix / Rust unit tests`.

## Scope
Linux helper trust only: `platform-linux/src/proc_fs.rs`, `wayland/shell_helper.rs` and `wayland/kwin_helper.rs`. Discovery, transport and the other `/proc/<pid>/exe` readers are unchanged.

## Blast Radius
GNOME and KDE Wayland sessions. A compositor whose binary was not replaced takes the same path as before, with an added dev/inode match between the path and the running image. A replaced image from another mount namespace, or one reached through a mount the driver can't see, is still refused (covered by the namespace and private-mount tests).

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, plus `cargo test -p platform-linux --all-targets` (918 lib tests passed). I ran the test suite once with a `sleep` that renames its `comm`, like Nix's, ahead on PATH, and once with `sh` as a bash symlink. I ran the replaced-program and namespace tests both unprivileged and as root, so the namespace cases ran instead of skipping.
- `verify-cua-driver` X11 lane (`verify-linux.sh x11`): 2 delivered, 0 failed, evidence check passed after cleanup.
- `runner.ts --library cua-driver --check`: the Linux reference is up to date. The earlier `Reference / cua-driver / linux` failure was a runner "The server is busy" error, not drift.

title: cua-spacesd stops answering :3211 after viewer teardown (deadlock in MacosCaptureLease::stop)
body:
Environment: cua 0.2.0, cua-spacesd 0.2.0 (launchd `com.trycua.spacesd.host`), macOS 27.0.1, Apple silicon, SIP on.

What happens
- After a few view-only `cua sb view direct:127.0.0.1:3211` sessions are opened and closed, the host stops answering HTTP on 127.0.0.1:3211. Connections are accepted, but no response comes back.
- `cua sb view` then blocks until its caller times out. Clients see "Could not create the Cua invitation".
- The process stays alive, so launchd KeepAlive never restarts it.

Likely cause
- Sampling the hung process shows the viewer teardown path waiting on the capture lease mutex inside `MacosCaptureLease::stop`.
- At the same time, a ScreenCaptureKit sample callback holds that mutex while it waits on the teardown.

Workaround
- `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.trycua.spacesd.host`. Afterwards the host answers in under 1 ms (HTTP 400 on `/`).
- We now run a 60 s watchdog that kickstarts the host after two failed probes.

Expected
- Teardown should not wait on the capture callback while holding the lease lock. For example, stop the SCStream outside the lock, or drop frames once the lease is marked stopping.
- A health endpoint would let supervisors detect the hang.

title: chore(deps): bump claude-agent-sdk from 0.1.58 to 0.2.121 in /libs/python/cua-sandbox-apps
body:
Bumps [claude-agent-sdk](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python) from 0.1.58 to 0.2.121.
Release notes

Sourced from claude-agent-sdk's releases.

v0.2.121

Bug Fixes

title: fix(cua-driver): invoke a menu for a window behind the user's window without raising it on macOS
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `invoke_menu` for a window of the **frontmost** app that is **not its key window** raised and focused that window. `invoke()` sends every frontmost-app call through `focus_exact_window` (SkyLight make-key, `AXRaise`/`AXMain`/`AXFocused`), opens the menu on screen through `invoke_path`, then restores the prior key window. The user is working in that app, so their window loses key for the call, the raised window covers it for a moment, and their typing can land in the open menu. A background agent hits this whenever it runs a menu command in another window of the app the user is in (a second document, terminal or browser window), directly or through `run_steps`' menu-bar click route (`menu_bar_route`), which calls `invoke_menu`.
- What changed: that one case now uses the same mechanism keys already use for a window behind the user's window (`key_scope` → `enter_exact_window_key`): the target becomes the app's key window through the in-app key-window record (no raise, no activation, no pointer), the item is pressed through the existing background route without opening its menu (`run_in_background`), and the scope hands key back to the user's window. If the window cannot be confirmed key that way, the call is refused with the existing `window_not_key` code, escalation `bring_to_front`, and nothing is invoked (pressing it with the user's window still key would run the command there). A background app and the frontmost app's key window keep their current routes. When the app's key window (`AXFocusedWindow`) cannot be read, the route falls back to its on-screen window order: the app's frontmost window on screen is the user's own window and keeps the old path (raising it changes nothing); any other window, and every window when no frontmost window can be found, is refused with `window_not_key` before any key-window record is posted. One per-process mutation lease covers the route decision, the key change, the press and the hand-back. Results and refusals on this route say where the window was, not that the app is in the background (`MenuRequest` words them per route, as `placement()` does); the core recovery hint for a disabled `invoke_menu` item now says its window is behind the user's window, which holds on both routes.

## Related work

Refs #3780 (the exact-window readiness wait this path uses), Refs #4955 (the background menu route and key-focus guard this reuses).

I found no issue or pull request for this case (searched `invoke_menu`, focus, raise, frontmost, `focus_exact_window`). Found while building a background voice agent that runs tasks in the user's apps.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required, I believe: no schema, parameter or new refusal code; one macOS route changes for one placement.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. A call that used to raise another window of the frontmost app now presses the item without raising it, or is refused with `window_not_key` when the key-window record cannot be confirmed (e.g. where focus without raise is unavailable) or when the app's key window cannot be read and the target is not its frontmost window on screen. Callers that want the old raise can call `bring_to_front` first, as the existing `background_unavailable` guidance already says. `MACOS.md` (the driver's skill) now describes the three placements.
- Risk and rollback: an app whose menu command runs after the AX press returns (a deferred perform) could run it after key went back to the user's window; I did not see this for menu items, which AppKit performs within the press, but I could not test it live (below). Since d52ec6ebe (#5520, salvaged from #5514), the press on this route also requires `AXFocusedWindow` and `AXMainWindow` to be the target; if the key-window record does not move `AXMainWindow`, this route refuses with `window_not_key` instead of pressing (not checked on a desktop). `invoke_menu` now holds the pid's mutation lease through the old path too, so same-pid background actions wait for it. Rollback is reverting the PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (rustc 1.97.1, the pin; branch updated by merging main at 87ffb67bf): `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core` → all pass: `platform-macos` unit 643 passed, 7 ignored (636 on that main), `cursor_hook_registry` 2 passed, `embedded_menu_restore` skipped itself (it needs `--run-gui`); `cua-driver-core` unit 1080 passed, 1 ignored, and 45 tests passed across its 16 integration test binaries; each crate's doc-tests 0 passed, 1 ignored; `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test` → 2 passed, 1 ignored; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core --lib --tests` reports nothing in the touched files (5 warnings elsewhere). Tests in `tools::invoke_menu::tests` cover the route decision (`menu_route`: background, behind the user's window, the key window, and an unreadable key window with the target in front, another window in front, or no front window), each refusal's code and escalation, the texts on each route, and the reuse of a held mutation lease. Breaking each rule (old path for any unknown key window, no front-window rule, background wording on the behind route, no held-lease check) fails a test.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. Reproducing it means making an app frontmost on a machine someone is using; I did not run the Lume harness.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the fork's `pull_request` workflows are waiting for maintainer approval, so no CI beyond CLA, contributor attribution and release reminder has run on this branch. Not run here (deterministic but outside these two crates, or desktop-bound): `cua-driver` `status_pid_file_cli_test`, the hermetic `cua-driver-e2e` tests, `embedded_menu_restore --run-gui`, and the desktop E2E matrix that `AGENTS.md` asks for on the candidate SHA before the PR is ready. The one that matters most is a desktop run (Lume) of `invoke_menu` on a second window of a frontmost TextEdit or Terminal, checking that the user's window keeps key and order, that `AXMainWindow` follows the key-window record so the press is not refused, and that the command lands in the target window.

- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

body:
Bumps [mcp](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk) from 1.28.1 to 1.30.0.
Release notes

Sourced from mcp's releases.

v1.30.0

Maintenance release of the 1.x line. 2.x is the current line; 1.x docs are at https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v1/.

A few defaults changed in this release. If you run a server or client on 1.x, skim these first:

Behaviour changes

HTTP client redirects are only followed within the endpoint's origin (#3448)

  • streamable_http_client and sse_client follow a redirect only if it stays on the same scheme, host and port (or upgrades http to https on the same host).
  • A redirect anywhere else now fails the request with httpx.HTTPStatusError. If that other URL is the server you meant, use it as the endpoint URL.
  • The follow_redirects setting on an httpx.AsyncClient you pass in is no longer used for MCP requests, so you don't need it for the trailing-slash redirect any more.
  • OAuthClientProvider applies the same rule to its own requests.

Idle Streamable HTTP sessions now expire (#3426)

  • A stateful session with nothing in flight for 30 minutes is closed. The client's next request gets a 404 and it has to initialize again.
  • Clients that keep the GET stream open (the SDK's client does) are not affected.
  • A server also holds at most 10 000 sessions at once; beyond that, new sessions get a 503.
  • To turn either off: FastMCP(..., session_idle_timeout=None, max_sessions=None).

The OAuth client checks the authorization server's issuer (#3431)

  • Authorization server metadata whose issuer doesn't match the server it was fetched for is now rejected with OAuthFlowError: Authorization server metadata issuer mismatch.
  • Client registrations are now remembered per issuer; if the server later points at a different authorization server, the client registers again.
  • If protected resource metadata can't be fetched because of a 5xx/429, the flow now stops instead of falling back to the legacy endpoints.

Two new DeprecationWarnings (#3431, #3451)

  • ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider / PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider without issuer=. Pass your authorization server's issuer URL.
  • AuthSettings with resource_server_url set but validate_token_resource unset. Set it to True or False.
  • Both keep working as before in 1.x; this mostly matters if your tests turn warnings into errors.

New

  • AuthSettings.validate_token_resource: only accept tokens your TokenVerifier reports as issued for this server (#3451).
  • issuer= on ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider (#3431).
  • session_idle_timeout= and max_sessions= on FastMCP (#3426).
