title: [RFC]: Refuse GNOME window screenshots from helpers below API 9
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On GNOME Wayland, Cua Driver should return a window screenshot only when the WinRects helper can capture that window's own actor (`CaptureWindow`, helper API 9 or newer). With an older helper loaded, `get_window_state` should keep the accessibility tree and return the existing `surface_identity_unproven` refusal instead of a crop of the Shell stage. This reverses the backward-compatibility choice #4882 made for helpers below API 9.

### Motivation and current state

#4882 added per-window capture because a stage crop proves the window's geometry, not that nothing covers it, so a covered window's screenshot can show another app. It kept the crop for helpers below API 9 so users who had not reinstalled the helper would keep window screenshots, and the helper README documents that caveat.

That crop is still reached by anyone whose loaded helper is older than the one Cua Driver 0.35.0 bundles: helpers from Cua Driver 0.34 or earlier, helpers an older installer downgraded, and newer helpers on disk that GNOME Shell has not loaded yet because it loads extensions at login. In each case the driver labels an image that may contain another app's pixels as the target window and issues a `capture_id` that pixel actions are grounded on. The decision needed is whether the exact-window guarantee outranks keeping screenshots for those users.

### Goals

- Every GNOME window image comes from the helper's per-window capture; no GNOME window image comes from a stage crop.
- A user on an older helper gets a refusal naming the loaded API, the required API and the fix (re-run the installer, then log in again).
- The accessibility tree, `get_desktop_state` and desktop-target input keep working with an older helper.
- Helper API 9 or newer, and every other platform and compositor, behave as before.

### Non-goals

- Changing the helper D-Bus API or its version.
- Proving a stage crop clean with stacking or overlap checks.
- Changing installer upgrade behavior or forcing a helper reload.
- Changing capture on X11, wlroots compositors, Hyprland, KDE, macOS or Windows.

### Proposal

The helper boundary reports three outcomes: no verified helper, a verified helper that cannot capture one window (with its API), and a per-window capture result. On GNOME the second outcome and a helper refusal both return `surface_identity_unproven`; only "no verified helper" may take another route. The GNOME stage-crop branch is removed, so a failed `GetVersion` also refuses. The refusal reuses the existing `get_window_state` shape (`screenshot_frame_valid: false`, typed `screenshot_error`), adds no error code or field, and its reason names the API and the fix. The helper README and the skill's Linux notes describe it. The implementation is written and tested on a branch and is available on request; its pull request will be opened after acceptance.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep the crop for older helpers (the #4882 choice): screenshots stay, and so does the chance of another app's pixels in them.
- Refuse only when `GetRects` shows an overlapping higher window: `GetRects` lists application windows only, not Shell's own surfaces such as notifications, menus and Shell dialogs, so it cannot prove a crop clean.
- Keep the crop but withhold `capture_id` or mark the frame unverified: the image still reaches the caller, and existing fields change meaning.
- An opt-in configuration flag: preserves the default but adds a public setting and leaves the default as is.
- A new refusal code or `helper_api_version` field: widens the MCP contract when `surface_identity_unproven` already covers the case.

### Compatibility and migration

GNOME Wayland users with a helper below API 9 loaded lose window screenshots until they update the helper and log in again: no image or `capture_id` from `get_window_state`, an error from a screenshot-only read, and no window image for `zoom`. Accessibility actions, `get_desktop_state`, desktop-target input and Wayland action recordings are unchanged. An installer from 0.35.0 onward replaces an older helper in the user's GNOME Shell extensions directory. Users who have already run one, and whose loaded helper is older only because GNOME Shell has not reloaded it, need only a new login; users whose installed helper is still older re-run a current installer and then log in again. The refusal names both steps. Rollback is reverting the implementation commit.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Boundary: a window screenshot contains only pixels the compositor attributes to that window; otherwise the driver returns a typed refusal and no image. The change removes a path and adds no permission, process or data collection. The refusal reason carries the helper API number and fixed text only. Telemetry is unchanged.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

Unit tests for the version gate, the GNOME refusal text and the no-fallback rule, with negative controls that fail under the current rule; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test -p platform-linux --all-targets --locked`, `cargo check -p cua-driver --features portal-input --locked`; existing X11, Sway and Wayland fail-closed capture tests unchanged; before completion, a GNOME desktop run with an API 8 helper loaded showing the tree kept and the refusal naming API 8.

### Unresolved questions

- Is losing window screenshots on older helpers acceptable, given that users who already ran a 0.35.0 or newer installer need only a new login?
- Should the GNOME desktop E2E runner require helper API 9 or newer?
- Should `doctor` report when the loaded helper is older than the installed one?

### RFC document pull request

_No response_

### Submission checks

- [X] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [X] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [X] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: [Bug]: browser_prepare reports existing-profile success before CDP responds
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`browser_prepare(strategy=existing_profile)` can report `attached_existing_profile` after the WebSocket handshake succeeds even when that connection cannot complete a CDP command. The prepare path currently claims the socket without a read-only CDP readiness probe.

### Reproduction

A deterministic loopback fixture reproduces this on current main:

1. Supply the existing protected-consent fixture with an attested loopback browser endpoint.
2. Complete the WebSocket handshake.
3. Have the endpoint either return `-32601` for `Target.getTargets`, or keep the socket open without answering CDP.
4. Invoke `BrowserPrepareTool` with an approved `existing_profile` request.

The fixture is synthetic; this report does not claim a new native Chrome/Edge reproduction.

### Expected behavior

Preparation should succeed only after a read-only CDP command succeeds on the claimed socket. Failure or cancellation during the probe should release only the preparing generation's hold. An existing peer session must retain its shared connection.

### Actual behavior

Both fixture cases return `status: "ok"`, `prepared: true`, and `action: "attached_existing_profile"` immediately after the handshake, without waiting for a CDP response.

### Environment

- Cua Driver core, current main `5df19ea9ba78a4aa0a396c682685c69ae1eca51a` (workspace version 0.36.0)
- Linux x86_64, Rust 1.97.1
- Real loopback TCP/WebSocket transport with scripted CDP responses; no real browser or desktop session

### Evidence

New tests through `BrowserPrepareTool`, run against unchanged production code:

- `failed_prepare_probe_releases_only_the_preparing_session`: fails because actual status is `ok`, expected `refused`.
- `silent_prepare_socket_is_refused_and_released`: same false-success failure while the socket stays open and never answers CDP.
- `cancelled_prepare_probe_releases_only_its_socket_hold`: fails because preparation finishes before any probe response.

Commands from `libs/cua-driver/rust`:

`cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core prepare_probe -- --nocapture`

`cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core silent_prepare_socket -- --nocapture`

### Workaround and additional context

I intend to contribute a small fix that probes with the already-allowed `Target.getTargets` command, discards its result, and retains the existing attestation, consent, refusal, and bounded-retry decisions. Cleanup must respect the shared-generation ownership introduced in #5115, including cancellation while the probe is pending.

Related: #3288 already handles consent for the one permitted retry; this report concerns the missing readiness proof rather than that retry wiring.

The fix will be adapted from the existing public [fork commit](https://github.com/loonghao/cua/commit/c8be5551dd262d886fca08528792aa6995460dcb), with source authorship preserved and public-seam regressions added. Native-browser acceptance remains a separate validation gap.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

Implementation draft: #5448. Scope, validation, and remaining gaps are tracked in that PR.

title: fix(cua-driver): verify existing-profile CDP readiness
body:
## Summary

- `browser_prepare(existing_profile)` currently treats a completed WebSocket handshake as readiness, even when the socket cannot complete a CDP command.
- Probe with the already-allowed, read-only `Target.getTargets` before either the initial claim or the one permitted retry can report success. Discard the response.
- Release only the preparing generation on probe error or cancellation. Preserve peer-held shared connections; a later claim redials when the failed probe was the last holder.
- Add four regressions through `BrowserPrepareTool`, using loopback TCP/WebSockets and scripted CDP responses.

## Related work

Fixes #5446.

Retains the consent/retry behavior from #3288 and shared-socket ownership from #5115. This is a small, currently unselected bug-fix contribution submitted for maintainer review.

Adapted from [loonghao's original liveness commit](https://github.com/loonghao/cua/commit/c8be5551dd262d886fca08528792aa6995460dcb) and the shared-generation correction in [loonghao/cua#7](https://github.com/loonghao/cua/pull/7). The landing commit is a new adaptation: it preserves source links, original author/date metadata in its message, and the original author's coauthor credit. It adds cancellation cleanup and stronger public-seam tests.

## Compatibility and risk

- No new public request parameters, response shapes, refusal codes, consent authority, endpoint scope, or CDP methods.
- Healthy preparation adds one read-only CDP round trip. The current consent observation and CDP timeout policies remain unchanged.
- A silent socket can be refused by the existing consent path before the CDP timeout. A peer-held socket is intentionally retained, so a retry does not always imply a new physical connection.
- Cleanup here covers the pending probe's socket hold. General whole-prepare grant cancellation and cancellation cleanup of the CDP pending-response map are outside this change.
- Rollback is a revert of this focused patch.

## Validation

Base: `trycua/cua@5df19ea9`. Published head: `8194ada2`. The published tree exactly matches the locally tested candidate tree `3e067822f87a26c9a58fe9c6c578ba0e5fcbc3c0`.

From `libs/cua-driver/rust`:

- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib prepare_ -- --nocapture`: 10 passed, including four new tests.
- Negative controls on unchanged official production code reproduce false success for failed/silent CDP and no opportunity to cancel a pending probe.
- Removing the pending-probe cleanup makes the cancellation regression fail.
- Reverting only the retry callsite to plain `claim_existing` makes the accepted-consent retry regression fail with false success.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::`: 229 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --test '*'`: 28 passed across 13 integration binaries.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on Rust 1.97.1.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 989 passed, 13 failed, 1 ignored. The same 13 perception-worker tests fail on untouched official `5df19ea9` (985 passed, 13 failed, 1 ignored), because this cloud kernel does not provide the required Landlock containment. The failing-test sets are identical; this is not a clean full-suite pass.
- Exact-head hosted CLA, contributor-attribution, and release-reminder checks pass. The 19 code/test workflows are `action_required`, awaiting maintainer approval for this fork; for example [quick feedback](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/39181568653) and [Windows unit tests](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/39181568673).

These tests use real loopback transport but simulated platform/CDP behavior. No real Chrome/Edge, Windows UIA, or desktop acceptance is claimed. Hosted code/test CI and maintainer/native review remain pending; this PR stays draft.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This small internal bug fix does not require an RFC.
- [x] Tests and platform-evidence limits are explained.
- [x] The title describes the production fix using a Conventional Commit.
- [x] Source authorship and provenance are credited.
- [ ] Hosted checks and native acceptance reviewed before marking ready.

title: [RFC]: Ancestor-scoped semantic browser snapshots
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Add an opt-in ancestor lookup to `get_browser_state` with `snapshot_format: "semantic_v2"`: resolve an existing `scope_ref` to its nearest strict ancestor with a requested accessibility role, then apply the existing `query` within that ancestor's subtree. The proposed input is `scope_ancestor_role`; the response identifies the resolved scope, and an unprovable scope returns a structured refusal. This issue requests a decision on that public contract before upstream implementation.

### Motivation and current state

A repeated list or table can expose a distinctive item label beside an identically named action in every row. A caller may already have the current semantic ref for the intended item's label, but a page-wide query for `"Options"` finds several controls. Direct `scope_ref` observes descendants of the supplied ref, so scoping to the label does not reach its sibling action. The missing operation is to identify the containing row from the known item, then query inside that row.

At [`main@6bb30296`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/6bb30296951f4424503d1466f25ed34bd3c5dd53/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs), `get_browser_state` already offers `scope_ref`, `query`, and opaque continuation for `semantic_v2`. It does not offer ancestor-role lookup. This proposal adds that targeting relationship; it makes no latency or payload-reduction claim.

Related work checked on 2026-10-19:

- [#2299](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2299) established semantic snapshots and is complete.
- [#2969](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2969) and [#2970](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2970) own compact payloads. Their existing scope/query discussion and preference for no additional parameters are relevant tradeoffs. Ancestor lookup needs its own explicit decision; that RFC's acceptance does not approve this input.
- [#4055 was withdrawn](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/4055#issuecomment-5896356612), with response-size options directed to #2969.
- [#5387](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5387) is active work on renderer-target AX identity and cycle handling for [#5381](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/5381). It preserves same-process iframe traversal without adding a public ancestor API. This proposal must compose with that work rather than duplicate or replace it.

The design originates in [loonghao's public fork commit `9de510aa`](https://github.com/loonghao/cua/commit/9de510aa6c407c5b36a5f62b288702127192f40c). That prototype supplies concrete contract and test examples, not upstream approval or a ready-to-merge implementation. Any material adaptation should preserve the original contributor's authorship and source provenance under CONTRIBUTING.md.

### Goals

- From a current item ref, return matching controls from exactly its nearest qualifying container, excluding otherwise identical controls in sibling containers.
- Explain the selected scope through structured metadata without exposing internal AX or DOM identities.
- Refuse stale, ambiguous, malformed, or cross-frame ancestor resolution without silently broadening the query.
- Keep the same scope across continuation pages and preserve existing ref lifetime, visibility, permissions, and background-read guarantees.
- Leave requests that omit the new input unchanged, including direct scopes containing same-process iframe content.

### Non-goals

- New browser actions, navigation or activation behavior, file-upload associations, or changes to browser setup and consent.
- CSS/XPath selectors, arbitrary JavaScript, positional row selection, or automatic choice among several query matches.
- Crossing a frame/document boundary to find a containing ancestor.
- Native desktop accessibility ancestor lookup, payload compaction, ref collapsing, or new node-budget controls.
- Reimplementing #5387, changing the default snapshot format, or treating this issue as permission to start implementation.

### Proposal

#### Request and ownership

The shared Cua Driver browser core owns the behavior. Add one optional string to the existing tool, with identical behavior through CLI, MCP, SDK tool invocation, and the raw protocol:

```json
{
  "session": "example-session",
  "target_id": "<bound target>",
  "tab_id": "<bound tab>",
  "snapshot_format": "semantic_v2",
  "scope_ref": "<current item ref>",
  "scope_ancestor_role": "row",
  "query": "Options"
}
```

- Require explicit session, target, tab, `semantic_v2`, `scope_ref`, and `query` when `scope_ancestor_role` is present. Reject the new input in native-window bind mode or `dom_refs_v1`.
- Accept a 1–128-byte ASCII role matching `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`; compare the normalized lowercase role exactly. Do not trim invalid whitespace or interpret the value as a selector. A well-formed role with no matching ancestor is a scope refusal.
- Reuse the existing query matching and ranking semantics. The initial proposal requires the query field but keeps its existing empty-string behavior, which requests all eligible nodes within the resolved scope.
- Continuation requests supply the existing continuation token without a new `scope_ref`, role, or query. Schema and runtime validation must agree for the new combinations, without tightening unrelated legacy requests.

#### Resolution and frame policy

1. Resolve the source as a current semantic action ref or content ref in the same session, target, tab, and snapshot namespace. A content ref remains read-only.
2. Collect fresh semantics and prove that the source still identifies the same backend node in the same frame/document. A changed source role or accessible name is stale; never relocate it by text similarity.
3. Starting at the source's parent, walk the raw AX ancestry. Select the first retained semantic ancestor with the requested role. The source itself never qualifies, even if its role matches. Ignored wrappers may connect the path; distance counts every AX parent edge, including those wrappers.
4. Prove the selected subtree before querying it. Cycles, duplicate/ambiguous identities, missing links, and inconsistent parent/child edges refuse. A successful empty query result is allowed when the scope is proven but no eligible node matches.
5. Keep this new scope within the source's exact frame/document. The initial proposal refuses a discovered cross-document edge in the ancestor path or selected subtree. The rule applies equally to same-process frames and out-of-process iframes (OOPIFs). A proven lookup wholly inside an OOPIF is allowed; jumping to its embedding page is not. Shadow DOM may participate through the existing composed AX tree in the same document.

Keep renderer identity and document proof separate. Generic AX traversal must retain the renderer-target namespace used by #5387, including legitimate same-process iframe links. The ancestor operation adds its stricter document checks locally; it must not make ordinary direct scopes or page outlines frame-isolated.

#### Response, pagination, and lifecycle

The first successful page reports `snapshot.scope: "ancestor_subtree"` and:

```json
{
  "scope_anchor": {
    "requested_ref": "<input scope_ref>",
    "role": "row",
    "name": "Example item",
    "frame": "main",
    "distance": 2
  }
}
```

`name` is nullable, `frame` uses the existing `main` / `iframe` / `oopif` vocabulary, and `distance` is a positive integer. This metadata describes the anchor; it is not an action ref. Raw AX IDs, backend IDs, loader IDs, and CDP target IDs stay internal. No `scope_anchor` field is needed on legacy requests.

Apply the existing visibility/ranking rules and 300-node page budget after scope and query selection. Outline context stops at the scope anchor. Preserve existing completeness and omission accounting, including the distinction between collected-document omissions and scoped candidate counts; do not claim a complete page when collection is incomplete.

Store the resolved anchor and query with the existing snapshot continuation. Later pages retain `snapshot.scope: "continuation"` and the identical `scope_anchor`; they page the cached snapshot rather than selecting a new ancestor. Re-prove both the top-level document and the anchor's frame/document before serving them. Navigation, frame removal/reload, session teardown, or a superseding snapshot invalidates the relevant refs and tokens. Continuation consumes/replaces tokens under the current lifecycle. A concurrent refresh must produce either a coherent response for the valid namespace or a stale refusal, never a mixture.

Collection, cancellation, CDP attachment cleanup, and bounded traversal stay with the existing browser lifecycle. No new process, transport, background worker, permission prompt, focus change, or tab activation is introduced.

#### Failure vocabulary

- Invalid argument types, role syntax, or missing required inputs use tool argument errors.
- Existing stale/foreign-ref and target/session checks keep their existing refusal codes. A changed source returns `browser_ref_stale` with `reason: "source_changed"`; a reloaded or removed continuation frame returns `browser_ref_stale` with `reason: "scope_frame_changed"`.
- An otherwise valid request whose scope cannot be proven returns the proposed `browser_scope_unavailable`, with `detail.reason` from `source_missing`, `source_not_semantic`, `ancestor_missing`, `unproven_frame`, `broken_parent`, `cycle`, `ambiguous`, or `cross_frame`. Detail may echo the supplied `scope_ref` and role, but no page content.
- Combining continuation with a new scope/query keeps the existing `browser_ref_stale` behavior at invocation time. Transport and permission failures retain their existing classifications.

Recovery is to refresh page state and obtain a new source ref. A refusal must never trigger an automatic page-wide retry.

### Alternatives considered

- **Use existing direct `scope_ref`.** This works when the caller already has the container ref. It cannot move from a known label to its containing row, and containers need not have mintable refs. It remains the preferred path when sufficient.
- **Have callers infer a parent from the outline.** This avoids an input, but the outline is presentation rather than a stable parent-reference graph, and a guessed container cannot supply the same exact-scope proof.
- **Return ancestor refs on every snapshot or add a separate lookup tool.** Either can support richer traversal. They add response/schema surface or another tool and lifecycle decision; they are larger than this one lookup.
- **Solve duplicate names through #2969 ref collapsing.** Useful for several representations of the same control. Separate rows can legitimately contain distinct identically named controls, so collapsing them would lose information.
- **Allow self-or-ancestor matching or cross-frame lookup.** More permissive, but less predictable and broader than the requested containing-context relationship. The proposal uses strict ancestry and exact-document boundaries.
- **Use a CSS/XPath or script escape hatch.** This changes the addressing and trust contract. It is outside this proposal.

### Compatibility and migration

The wire change is opt-in. Requests without `scope_ancestor_role` retain their input combinations, response shape, direct-scope behavior, visibility policy, and ref semantics. In particular, preserve empty-success behavior for a legacy direct scope whose source is absent from the fresh semantic composition.

Clients should check the advertised schema before using the input and require the returned `ancestor_subtree` scope and anchor metadata. Older servers may ignore unknown properties; sending the input alone is not evidence that ancestor lookup ran. Do not fall back to an unscoped query when support is absent.

Wire compatibility does not imply Rust source compatibility. The public `SemanticContinuation` currently exposes `scope_backend_node_id`; the fork replaces that field with private scope state. Copying that change would break downstream construction/access. Adding variants to public refusal enums also affects exhaustive matches. Keep new bookkeeping private without changing existing public struct fields where feasible, and have review explicitly decide any unavoidable Rust compatibility/release impact. The snapshot engine method is already crate-private at the cited baseline.

Record the maintainer decision first, coordinate with #5387's owner, then use a focused implementation PR with generated contracts, documentation, and release notes. No navigation, upload, or unrelated fork code belongs in that PR. Rollback disables use of the new optional capability; there is no persisted-data migration. Clients must continue to reject missing scope proof after rollback.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Use the existing session, target, tab, origin, and observation authorization. Ancestor scope does not grant access to another document or authorize any action. Returned refs keep their existing typed capabilities and action-time liveness checks. The feature narrows returned semantic content, but the current collector may still read the whole authorized document; this is not a claim of reduced collection.

Do not add telemetry containing query text, accessible names, page text, URLs, raw protocol identifiers, or screenshots. Scope reasons, counts, and timing are sufficient for diagnostics. Anchor names appear only in the authorized observation response under the existing handling of page content. Test artifacts use synthetic fixture data.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

The public fork contains prototype unit and mock-CDP tests. This RFC does not claim current-main implementation, newly executed test results, or native browser acceptance.

Acceptance should include:

- Repeated-row fixtures: a known item ref resolves only its row's identically named controls; nested same-role containers select the nearest strict ancestor; source-as-match is excluded; ignored wrappers preserve correct distance.
- Exact refusal tests for stale/foreign refs, changed source semantics, no ancestor, unproven frames, duplicate IDs, cycles, dangling/conflicting edges, and cross-frame traversal. Prove that no wider fallback occurs. Proven scope plus no query match returns empty success.
- Main-frame, same-process iframe, OOPIF, and shadow-DOM cases; renderer-local ID collisions cannot mix scopes. Preserve #5387's ordinary direct-scope same-process iframe regression and current unscoped behavior.
- More than 300 scoped matches: stable anchor, counts, ordering, and ref namespace across pages; no sibling leakage. Cover token reuse, incompatible arguments, top-level/frame navigation, frame removal, superseding snapshots, and concurrent refreshes.
- Current-main visibility and native-select behavior remain intact. Exact schema/runtime and refusal parity through CLI, MCP, SDK tool invocation, and raw protocol; generated-contract drift checks and compile coverage for public Rust consumers.
- Canonical real-browser fixtures on macOS, Windows, Linux X11, and the supported compositor-specific Wayland lanes, with exact candidate SHA recorded. Verify intended-row membership and background focus/tab/cursor sentinels; where actions consume returned refs, observe the fixture's actual effect. Record concrete unsupported platform/browser limitations rather than treating mock CDP as native evidence.
- Measure bounded completion/cancellation and confirm CDP child sessions are cleaned up. Run the component's normal format, lint, unit, integration, and canonical acceptance gates without replacing them with a hand-maintained module list.

### Unresolved questions

1. Is this distinct containing-context capability worth one additional input, or should review place it in an amendment to #2969? This issue does not assume that decision.
2. Should `query` remain required, including its existing empty-string semantics, or should omission explicitly request the full ancestor subtree?
3. Should a child-frame edge inside an otherwise valid ancestor subtree refuse the whole new request, as proposed, or terminate that branch with explicit omission accounting? Neither choice should change legacy direct scopes.
4. Are the proposed anchor fields and exact failure reasons the right stable public surface? Should absent frame-tree support use `browser_scope_unavailable` or the existing route-unavailable classification?
5. What Rust compatibility and release policy should govern the new refusal variants and continuation bookkeeping?

### RFC document pull request

None yet. The issue body is the proposed decision record. A repository-local RFC can be linked after an issue number exists if maintainers want a longer specification.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop re-sending input that may already have landed
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On Linux, an AT-SPI `EditableText` write or `doAction` can be sent and then fail with an error reply, or not answer within its budget, after the application has already acted on it. The driver often treated that as "nothing delivered". Within the same call it moved on to the next route: `SetTextContents` after a failed `InsertText`, a second write after `GrabFocus`, the same index re-resolved in a fresh walk, another hit-test tier, key events, or a pointer click. Or it returned a result that invites sending again: `background_unavailable` with `escalation.recommended: "foreground"` and `Retry this action with delivery_mode:"foreground"` (element-token `type_text` on Wayland, the background pixel click on Wayland and X11), `element_bounds_unavailable` with "no input was sent" (an X11 foreground element click on an element without usable bounds), or a `menu_path_unavailable` refusal from `invoke_menu`. That last one also happened when nothing failed: `invoke_menu` waited on the last menu item's action with no bound of its own, and a GTK item whose command opens a dialog answers only once the dialog closes, so the call ran into the 25 s operation timeout. A cleanup step sent after the input could also replace its outcome: a failed synthetic FocusOut in the Qt5 workaround turned a delivered write into an X11 error, after which the next route wrote the text again, and a failed Escape after a `set_value` combo-box pick turned the pick into an error. The browser consent and remote-debugging setup flows turned an action that may have acted into a refusal before reading the UI back, so a checkbox toggle that may have landed was never recorded for rollback. `run_steps` with `foreground_fallback: true` replays results that carry the foreground hint; it also replayed a token click's `ax_timeout` on Wayland and the Windows UIA pixel click whose provider failed or timed out (`effect: "unverifiable"`; its own text asks the caller to inspect state first). Either way, text could be typed twice or a control clicked twice. Separately, Hyprland isolated background input that stopped after two or more acknowledged keys or wheel packets was reported as `refused` with its delivered count removed, which reads as "nothing was sent".
- What changed:
  - Linux: an `EditableText` write that fails or times out after it was sent, and a `doAction` that gets an error reply, are marked as possibly landed where the request is sent. Every caller checks that mark before any fallback or refusal of its own, the X11 foreground click on an element without usable bounds included.
  - Such a call ends in an error with `effect: "unverifiable"` and `delivery: {"mode": "unknown"}`, the action-result shape the Hyprland foreground click already returns when its AT-SPI outcome is unknown. It has no `background_unavailable` code, no `suggestion`, no `refusal` and no `escalation`, and its text asks the caller to read the target back before sending again. Refusals raised before anything is sent keep their codes and the foreground hint.
  - A `doAction` that does not answer counts as dispatched in every at-point hit-test tier, the passive fallback (a label) included, so the full-walk tier never runs after it. Only a declined action falls through.
  - `invoke_menu` bounds the last menu item's action like every other action. If it does not answer, the call succeeds with `effect: "unverifiable"` and says so; an error reply ends in the unknown-outcome error; only a declined action is still refused.
  - The browser consent and remote-debugging setup flows count an action that may have acted as sent and read the UI back, as they already do after an accepted one.
  - A cleanup step that fails after the input was sent no longer replaces the input's outcome. A failed FocusOut in the Qt5 workaround, or a failed Escape after a `set_value` combo pick, becomes a warning sentence at the end of the result text. A successful write or pick stays a success, and the dispatcher's action-result projection carries that text as `summary`, so the warning reaches `structuredContent` only there, with no `warning` key. The one error result that can carry the warning is a Qt5 workaround write that may have landed: it stays the unknown-outcome error above, and its `structuredContent` also has a `warning` key. A combo pick that fails is reported as before, without the warning.
  - A token click's `ax_timeout` keeps its code and `effect: "unknown"` and drops its escalation. Its text asks for a screenshot before any retry.
  - `run_steps` replays a step with `foreground_fallback` only when the failed result shows nothing was delivered: no `effect` or one of `refused`, `none` and macOS `no_drop`, and no `delivery`. Any other effect, `suspected_noop` and values the rule does not know included, is not replayed.
  - Hyprland isolated background input interrupted after N ≥ 2 acknowledged keys or packets reports `effect: "partial"` with `delivery.delivered_count: N`, as a single key and every foreground count already did.
  - Unchanged: a `doAction` that never answers is still reported as dispatched with `effect: "unverifiable"`.

## Related work

No issue is filed for this. Refs #5431: its description lists these results as a known gap in the driver, and its `WORKFLOW.md` rule says that on Linux/Wayland `background_unavailable` can follow an AT-SPI write or action that already ran, and that Hyprland isolated input can report `refused` after delivering part of a text. With this change both clauses describe the old behavior; whichever of the two merges second should update them. The rule itself (fresh state before re-sending) still holds.

Interaction with the other open pull requests:

- #5430 (keep GNOME element actions inside the requested window): eight textual conflicts. Three are in `tools/impl_.rs`: the Hyprland foreground token write, and two in the `set_value` keyboard fallback, which #5430 moves to its token element. Two are in `atspi/mod.rs`, where #5430 replaces `perform_action_in` and `type_into_editable_at`; three are in the browser consent and setup flows, where #5430 switches to `perform_action_walked`. Two rules must carry over, and whichever pull request lands second adds them. #5430's `TokenElement::act` re-resolves the index after the observed object fails when `may_reresolve` is set; it must instead return the error when that error reports input that may have landed. Its browser consent and setup calls (`perform_action_walked`) need the same read-back wrapper as the calls they replace.
- #5431 is stacked on #5430 and conflicts the same way, in addition to the docs clauses above.
- #5429 and #5370 change other files and merge cleanly with this branch.

RFC: not needed in my reading. `rfcs/README.md` does not require an RFC for small bug fixes, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` lets a small, self-contained fix go straight to a focused pull request. These are bug fixes on error paths: tool schemas, descriptions and refusal codes are unchanged, and the new results use existing action-result values. Success results gain no field: when a cleanup step fails after a successful write or pick, the warning is a sentence in the result text, which success results already carry as `summary`. The one added key is `warning` on the error result of a Qt5 workaround write that may have landed when its FocusOut also failed; the dispatcher neither projects nor validates error results against the action-result contract. Clients do get different results on these paths:

- A Linux AT-SPI write or action that failed after it was sent: an error with `effect: "unverifiable"` and `delivery: {"mode": "unknown"}`, instead of `background_unavailable` with the foreground hint, `element_bounds_unavailable` with `effect: "none"`, or a `menu_path_unavailable` refusal. The call no longer tries a second route.
- `invoke_menu` whose last action does not answer in time: a success with `effect: "unverifiable"` after a few seconds, instead of a `menu_path_unavailable` refusal after 25 s.
- A token click's `ax_timeout`: no `escalation`.
- Hyprland isolated input interrupted after two or more keys or packets: `effect: "partial"` with `delivered_count`, instead of `refused`.
- `type_text` through the Qt5 workaround and `set_value` on a combo box, when the cleanup step fails after the write or pick: the write's or pick's own result instead of an error. On success the warning is the last sentence of `summary`. A Qt5 write that may have landed returns the unknown-outcome error above, with a `warning` key in its `structuredContent`.
- The browser remote-debugging consent and setup flows: the UI readback decides, instead of an immediate refusal.
- `run_steps` with `foreground_fallback`: no replay of a failed step whose result does not show that nothing was delivered.

If maintainers read any of this as a contract change, I will open an RFC before this goes further.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux changes, plus one shared `run_steps` rule; the result changes are listed under RFC above. On X11 the pointer or key-event fallback no longer runs after such a failure. `run_steps` on Windows no longer replays the UIA pixel click whose provider failed or timed out. Every other foreground-hinted error result on macOS and Windows has `effect` `refused` or `no_drop`, or no `effect` at all, so their replay is unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: The marking is conservative. An error reply after which the toolkit in fact did nothing now reports an unknown outcome instead of trying another route, so the caller re-reads state before deciding. In the browser setup flows the readback that follows an accepted action now also follows such a failure, with the same deadline and fallbacks. Reverting the commits restores the previous behavior.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `atspi::native::input_dispatch_tests` serves a fake `org.a11y.atspi.EditableText`, `org.a11y.atspi.Action` and passive `label` accessibles on a private `dbus-daemon`, skipping when it is absent, like the shell helper transport test. An `InsertText` that raises, or that does not answer within the budget, reaches the field once and is reported as possibly landed; a declined insert still falls back to `SetTextContents`; a `doAction` error reply is reported as possibly landed. A passive label whose action does not answer, is accepted, or raises is a hit (or the possibly-landed error), and the full-walk tier never runs; a declined one falls through to it. The last menu action is never refused unless declined.
  - `atspi_input_that_may_have_landed_is_reported_without_a_retry_hint`: the text, click, menu and `ax_timeout` results carry no `background_unavailable` code, refusal, suggestion or escalation, and the text, click and menu results equal their public action result.
  - `a_boundless_foreground_click_whose_action_may_have_landed_is_not_refused`, `a_failed_focus_out_never_hides_a_write_that_was_sent` (delivered and possibly-landed writes with a failing FocusOut), `a_failed_popup_close_never_turns_a_pick_into_an_error` and `an_action_that_may_have_acted_is_read_back_not_refused`.
  - `isolated_hyprland_refused_partial_and_unknown_outcomes_stay_distinct` gains a background text interrupted after three keys: `partial` with `delivered_count: 3`.
  - `a_step_whose_input_may_have_landed_is_never_replayed`: `run_steps` with `foreground_fallback` sends each step once whose result reports `unverifiable`, `unknown`, `partial`, `suspected_noop`, an unknown effect, or a refusal with a `delivery` record, and still replays a step refused before sending, including macOS `no_drop`.
  - Negative controls: putting the previous rule back into each owning function, or breaking each new guard, makes its test fail (14 controls; each test run exits 101).
  - CI parity at `8c31dc9b1`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-linux --all-targets --locked` passes (1702 passed, 31 ignored). The full Linux CI line `cargo test -p cua-driver -p cua-driver-e2e -p cua-driver-contract -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver-testkit -p cursor-overlay -p cursor-theme-cli -p platform-linux --all-targets --locked --no-fail-fast` gives 2482 passed and 126 ignored, with `platform-linux` 667 and `cua-driver-core` 999 library tests passing. Three tests fail locally in the two perception binaries (`perception_cli_test`, `perception_capture_loop_test`): their fixture worker links as a static PIE and this machine has no static glibc (`unable to find library -lc`). The CLI one fails the same way at the base commit.
  - `cargo check -p cua-driver --features portal-input --locked` passes.
- Manual or platform evidence: a release build with `portal-input` ran read-only on GNOME Shell 50 under Wayland (Fedora 44): `--version`, `doctor`, `serve`, `list_windows` and `stop`. No input was sent, so the changed paths were not exercised on a live desktop; the fake-bus tests exercise the AT-SPI calls.
- Known gaps or CI still required: The marker checks at the tool call sites, in `atspi/mod.rs` and in the browser flows are one-line guards on tested helpers. They have no hermetic test of their own, because reaching them needs a live AT-SPI tree. The desktop E2E matrix was not run. The 12 s deadline around a foreground X11 action still reports `foreground_timeout` with `effect: "none"`; every bounded phase inside it ends sooner, so it fires only when the X server or the blocking pool stalls, and its text asks for a screenshot first. Out of scope and unchanged: the `set_value` value writes and keyboard fallback (they replace the whole value, so a repeat does not duplicate text), combo-box option picks that fail, AT-SPI scroll, and Hyprland's unknown-dispatch result, which keeps the `background_unavailable` code with `effect` and `delivery` stating the outcome and no hint.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (Not applicable: releasing fix.)

title: cua-driver (macOS): drag-and-drop in native apps without taking the user's pointer
body:
**Problem:** native AppKit drag-and-drop is tracked by macOS with the real pointer, so a background drag currently refuses ("drop did not land"). Tasks that need a native drag can't be completed in the background.

**Proposal:** investigate background options (accessibility-driven moves where the app supports them, synthesized dragging sessions, app-specific APIs). Where no background route exists, see the companion issue for a permitted, brief foreground fallback.

**Done when:** there is either a working background route for common native drag cases with tests, or a documented, tested decision to use the foreground fallback.

title: [Bug]: Background pixel click on Electron/Chromium web content is silently degraded to AXPress
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, a window-scoped left click with x,y and the default delivery_mode is delivered as an AX hit-test + AXPress. The call returns success ("PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX", path "ax") but the requested coordinates are dropped, so Chromium/Electron web content usually does nothing. Reproduced with VS Code 1.136.1 (Electron 42.10.0) and Chrome.

### Reproduction

1. Open an Electron app with a text editor (VS Code 1.136.1, Electron Framework 42.10.0) and place the caret at Ln 1, Col 1.
2. Call click with pid, window_id, x=300, y=336, left button, single click, no modifiers, and omit delivery_mode (background default).
3. Observe the success text and the editor caret/status bar.
4. Repeat the same click with delivery_mode:"foreground".

### Expected behavior

A left click at x,y should deliver a real pointer event at that coordinate (or refuse when it cannot), not a semantic AXPress on whatever element the hit-test finds.

### Actual behavior

The call reports success while dropping the coordinates. The renderer receives no real pointerdown/mousedown sequence; canvas/WebGL/React pointer handlers and caret placement do nothing, and agents treat the success as completion.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.28.0 (bundled @trycua/cua-driver 0.28.0); also reproducible with the 0.28.2 CLI build.
Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.1 (Darwin 25.0.0), arm64.
Application/browser/window system/image: Visual Studio Code 1.136.1 (Electron 42.10.0), Chrome; no image.

### Evidence

- Result text: "✅ PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX." with structured path:"ax", verified:false, effect:"unverifiable".
- Status bar before/after the background click: Ln 1, Col 1 -> Ln 1, Col 1 (no change).
- Same click with delivery_mode:"foreground": "✅ Posted click ... (foreground CGEvent)"; status bar Ln 3, Col 13.
- Source: crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs, 0.28.x lines ~879-936 (main ~1156-1224). The background PX backend resolves the point with AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition and returns immediately after a successful AXPress.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: use delivery_mode:"foreground" for coordinate clicks, or element_token for semantic controls.
Suggested fix: skip the AX backend when the hit-test element is inside an AXWebArea, or require an advertised AXPress and a non-web role; alternatively add an explicit px_only delivery flag.
The existing silent-no-op guard only covers the LibreOffice VCL toolkit; Electron/Chromium has no equivalent.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): stamp the window-local point on macOS 27 background clicks
body:
Salvaged from #5425 (rebuilt on current main so it can land; original authorship kept).

On macOS 27, WindowServer reads the `CGEventSetWindowLocation` stamp of a pid-routed background click as the window-local point, so a screen-point stamp lands shifted by the window origin. Background clicks now stamp the window-local point on macOS 27+ and keep the screen point on earlier releases, for both the SkyLight route and the public pid fallback.

Proof: `macos_27_route_stamps_the_window_local_point` asserts the macOS 27 route plan stamps (394, 310) for a window at (170, 194) while every event keeps the screen location (564, 504), and the existing route test keeps the pre-27 screen-point stamp.

title: ci: pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, enforce it, add lefthook pre-push guard
body:
## What changed

- Every external GitHub Action in `.github/workflows` and `.github/actions` is now pinned to a full commit SHA, with the old tag kept as a trailing comment (`uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`). That is 347 references in 86 files. The SHAs are the ones the repo already used for `checkout`, `setup-node`, `setup-python`, `rust-toolchain` and the rest; the only new lookup was `actions/github-script@v7`.
- `.github/scripts/check_actions_pinned.sh` fails when an external action is not SHA-pinned. `ci-lint-workflows` runs it on every workflow change, so new unpinned refs can't land.
- `.github/dependabot.yml` opens one grouped PR a month to bump the pinned SHAs and their comments.

- Optional lefthook pre-push hook (`lefthook.yml`, `scripts/hooks/pre-push-guard.sh`). Before a push leaves the machine it refuses: a push to `main` on trycua/cua; history whose root commit is not cua's (another repo's history); a push of more than 300 new commits (`CUA_ALLOW_LARGE_PUSH=1` overrides); likely secrets in the new commits (gitleaks, high-confidence provider rules only); tailnet hostnames in added lines; and any unpinned Action. Install with `brew install lefthook gitleaks && scripts/hooks/install.sh`, not `lefthook install`: the script never writes into a global `core.hooksPath` (where `lefthook install --force` would overwrite the shared push guards). With a hooksPath set it adds a pre-push hook to the repo's own hooks directory, which the shared dispatcher chains to, and runs lefthook with `--no-auto-install`. Documented in CONTRIBUTING.

## Why

A tag can be moved by whoever controls the action's repo, and the workflows here run with release and signing secrets. Pinning removes that supply-chain path. This is part of the GitHub org hardening after the 13 Oct leak (CUA-1886). `trycua/cloud` was already fully pinned.

## User impact

None. Workflows run the same code as before.

## Test plan

- [x] `actionlint` reports the same findings on changed files before and after (all existing shellcheck notes).
- [x] All workflow and action YAML parses.
- [x] `check_actions_pinned.sh` passes on this branch and fails on `origin/main`.
- [x] Hook tested with synthetic pushes: main push, foreign root commit, size limit, a fake AWS key, a fake Slack token, a tailnet hostname and an unpinned Action are all blocked; a clean branch and a ref delete pass. Also run through real `git push` with lefthook 2.2.2 in a scratch clone.
- [x] Installer tested in a throwaway clone with a global `core.hooksPath` set: the shared guard still blocks foreign history and pushes to `main`, lefthook still runs on push, no `--force` hint is printed, and the shared hooks are byte-identical afterwards.
- [ ] `CI: Lint workflows` is green.

title: [Feature]: Keep policy-forced extensions in isolated browser launches
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

We want the browser `browser_prepare` launches (`isolated_named`) to keep extensions the machine admin forces through Chrome managed policy (`ExtensionInstallForcelist`), such as an ad or cookie-banner blocker. Isolated launches pass `--disable-extensions` and `--disable-background-networking`, so Chrome never installs them, and relaunching a profile that has one removes it. Other managed policies, such as `ForcedLanguages`, still apply.

**Repro**

1. As root, create `/etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed/test.json`:
   ```json
   {"ExtensionInstallForcelist": ["ddkjiahejlhfcafbddmgiahcphecmpfh;https://clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx"]}
   ```
2. As the desktop user, run `cua-driver serve` (standard mode) and call `browser_prepare` with `{"allow_launch": true, "profile": {"mode": "isolated_named", "name": "charlie"}}`.
3. After 60 s, `~/.local/state/cua-driver/browser-profiles/charlie/Default/Extensions` doesn't exist. Chrome's command line includes `--disable-extensions --disable-background-networking --disable-component-update`.

Launching the same Chrome directly without those three flags installs the extension.

### Desired outcome

Isolated launches keep extensions forced by root-owned managed policy, either automatically when such a policy exists or behind a trusted driver setting (not model input). `--load-extension` can stay unsupported.

### Current workaround

None that keeps Cua's launch path. Replacing Chrome's launcher to strip the flags works but bypasses Cua's launch posture.

### Affected components and platforms

Cua Driver 0.34.0 and 0.36.0 (linux-arm64), Debian bookworm, `google-chrome-stable` 155.0.8059.84, Xvfb + Openbox, unprivileged desktop user.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep browser attestation off the renderer while a dialog is open
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `browser_dialog` cannot reach a tab that has a JavaScript dialog open. Every browser tool proves the tab's live top-level origin before it runs, and that proof asked the renderer for `Page.getFrameTree`. A page-owned `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt` blocks the renderer, so the one tool meant to resolve the dialog waited out the 20 s CDP deadline and refused:

  ```
  $ echo '{"target_id":"bt-…","tab_id":"tab-…","action":"inspect"}' | cua-driver call browser_dialog
  { "refusal": { "code": "authorization_host_failed",
      "message": "confirmation provider failed: could not prove the live top-level browser document: CDP Page.getFrameTree timed out after 20s" } }
    took 20.4s
  ```

  A second problem sits behind it. Chromium reports a dialog only to CDP sessions that enabled the Page domain *before* the dialog opened. Only `browser_dialog` itself enabled it, so a dialog raised by a trusted click, a timer or the person was invisible to the driver even once the proof got out of the way.

- What changed:

  1. While a dialog is known to be open on the tab, the origin proof reads the browser process's own record of the target instead of asking the blocked renderer. `Target.getTargetInfo` answers while a dialog is up, and the document cannot navigate until the dialog is handled, so the record is current. The method joins the existing-profile allowlist (read-only, same data as `Target.getTargets`).

     ```rust
     let (method, params, session, pointer) = if conn.dialog_state(cdp_target_id).is_some() {
         ("Target.getTargetInfo", json!({ "targetId": cdp_target_id }), None, "/targetInfo/url")
     } else {
         ("Page.getFrameTree", json!({}), Some(cdp_session), "/frameTree/frame/url")
     };
     ```

  2. The first session attached to a tab enables Page events on behalf of every later caller (tab sessions stay attached for the life of the connection). The enable has a 2 s deadline so a renderer already blocked by an unseen dialog cannot stall the attach; `browser_dialog` keeps its own enable as the retry for that case.

     ```
     browser_click / browser_type / get_browser_state snapshot / browser_dialog
       └─ revalidate_for_mutation
            └─ attach(tab)  ──►  Target.attachToTarget
                                 Page.enable (once per tab, 2 s cap)   <- new
     page opens confirm()  ──►  Page.javascriptDialogOpening  journaled for the tab
     browser_dialog        ──►  attestation via Target.getTargetInfo  <- new
                                Page.handleJavaScriptDialog
     ```

  Observable behavior: after any tool has touched the tab, a dialog opened by the page is inspected and resolved in under a second instead of refusing after 20 s.

## Related work

Refs #3982, which asked for Page events to be enabled before the click rather than on the first `browser_dialog` call. #4618 handles the other half of that issue (returning from a `dom_event` click whose handler opens a dialog); the two are independent and compose, since the dialog tool's own enable is skipped when a session already subscribed.

RFC: not required, no contract change. One read-only method added to the existing-profile allowlist.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none in the API. Every tab attach now sends one extra `Page.enable` the first time a tab is touched on a connection. Embedded hosts without the Page domain answer it with an error, which is ignored.
- Risk and rollback: the attestation source changes only while a dialog is journaled for the tab. Revert the commit to restore the previous path.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`: 1075 passed (224 in `browser::`)
  - `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --tests`, `cargo fmt --check`: clean (pre-existing warnings only)
  - New test `an_open_dialog_moves_the_origin_proof_off_the_blocked_renderer` (`v2_tests.rs`): with a dialog journaled, the protected-scope attestation for `browser_click` proves the origin through `Target.getTargetInfo`, never asks `Page.getFrameTree`, and two tool calls produce exactly one `Page.enable`. Fails on main with `could not prove the live top-level browser document: CDP Page.getFrameTree failed`.

- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 15.8, Chrome with a throwaway profile, embedded daemon with `--grant existing-profile`, page with `setTimeout(() => alert("hello from the page"), 9000)`; `browser_prepare` + `get_browser_state`, one `browser_dialog inspect` before the alert so a tab session exists, then `inspect` and `accept` after it opens):

  | step | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `browser_dialog inspect`, alert open | `Page.getFrameTree timed out after 20s`, 20.4 s | `{"present": true, "kind": "alert", "dialog_id": "dialog-1"}`, 0.7 s |
  | `browser_dialog accept` | `Page.getFrameTree timed out after 20s`, 20.4 s | `{"action": "accept", "status": "ok"}`, 0.8 s |

  <details><summary>Receipt on this branch</summary>

  ```
  --- before the alert: browser_dialog inspect (first attach)
  { "present": false, "status": "ok", ... }   took 0.8s
  --- alert open: browser_dialog inspect
  { "dialog_id": "dialog-1", "kind": "alert", "present": true, "status": "ok", ... }   took 0.7s
  --- alert open: browser_dialog accept
  { "action": "accept", "dialog_id": "dialog-1", "kind": "alert", "status": "ok", ... }   took 0.8s
  ```
  </details>

- Known gaps or CI still required: a dialog that opens before *any* tool has attached to the tab (bind alone does not attach) is still unreachable: Chromium will not report it to a session that enables Page afterwards, so the enable times out (2 s) and the proof still waits on `Page.getFrameTree` (20 s), measured at 22.4 s on this branch versus 20.4 s on main. Closing that requires subscribing at bind time, which means attaching a session to the tab from `get_browser_state`; I left that out of this change since it touches the observation-only posture of the bind and is better decided by the maintainers. title: fix(cua-driver): list bound tabs in the order the browser reports them
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `get_browser_state` in bind mode lists the tabs of the bound window in `HashMap` iteration order. Six binds of the same untouched four-tab window on main:

  ```
  $ echo '{"pid":25494,"window_id":6964,"session":"s"}' | cua-driver call get_browser_state   # x6
  tabs: [four, one*, two, three]
  tabs: [three, one*, two, four]
  tabs: [three, four, two, one*]
  tabs: [one*, two, three, four]
  tabs: [one*, three, two, four]
  tabs: [two, three, one*, four]
  ```

  A caller that picks "the second tab" or diffs two binds gets a different answer each time, and nothing in the output says which order is the tab strip.

- What changed: the bound target keeps its tabs in an `IndexMap`, so the record preserves the order `Target.getTargets` returned them and the bind output lists them that way every time. Same six binds on this branch:

  ```
  tabs: [one*, two, three, four]   (x6, matches the tab strip)
  ```

  ```diff
  -    pub tabs: HashMap<String, TabRecord>,
  +    pub tabs: IndexMap<String, TabRecord>,
  ```

  Tab ids are still minted per bind, which is deliberate (they are session capabilities), so this only fixes the order, not identity across binds.

## Related work

No open issue or PR covers this. `indexmap` is already in the lockfile through `cursor-overlay`; this adds it as a direct dependency of `cua-driver-core`.

RFC: not required, no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: the `tabs` array of a bind keeps the same shape; only its order becomes deterministic. No new field, no id change.
- Risk and rollback: type swap with identical lookup API; every `tabs.get`/`get_mut` site compiles unchanged. Revert the commit to go back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`: 1075 passed (224 in `browser::`)
  - `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --tests`, `cargo fmt --check`: clean on the touched files
  - New test `bound_tabs_keep_the_browser_order_across_binds` (`v2_tests.rs`): a window with five page targets binds twice and lists them in `Target.getTargets` order both times, the selected one first. On main it fails with
    ```
    left:  ["https://fixture.test/", "https://tab4.test/", "https://tab5.test/", "https://tab2.test/", "https://tab3.test/"]
    right: ["https://fixture.test/", "https://tab2.test/", "https://tab3.test/", "https://tab4.test/", "https://tab5.test/"]
    ```

- Manual or platform evidence: macOS 15.8, Chrome on a throwaway profile opened with four `data:` tabs, embedded daemon with `--grant existing-profile`, `browser_prepare` then six `get_browser_state` binds. Receipts above (main shuffles, branch stable). Browser e2e lanes still need to run on the maintainers' runners.

title: feat(cua-driver): add a niri compositor adapter for Linux Wayland
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on niri, cua-driver could take screenshots and list windows, but every pointer, keyboard and focus action refused with `foreground_unavailable`. Window capture came back 0x0, and a 1.5 scale read as 1.0.
- What changed: a niri adapter in `platform-linux/src/wayland/niri/`, held to the Sway row's contract in `action-support.md`, and a nested niri lane in the Linux Wayland E2E matrix.

On niri 25.08 and later:

- Windows are found, activated and focused through niri IPC, after checking that the IPC socket belongs to the compositor serving `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`.
- Floating windows get window capture and window-coordinate input once the layout has been quiet for 1 s.
- Tiled windows (niri's default) have no position in IPC (niri-wm/niri#4369), so window-coordinate input on them refuses and points to `get_desktop_state`. Desktop-scope input uses the latest desktop screenshot and refuses after niri reports a layout or focus change.
- Typing uses niri's own keymap. Characters the layout lacks go on spare keys of a temporary keymap, restored afterwards. No wtype.
- Input and capture refuse while logind reports the session locked.

The adapter talks to `$NIRI_SOCKET` directly, with deadlines, instead of using the `niri-ipc` crate, which pins one niri version. There is no shared compositor trait yet.

The diff is +15k/-1k across 50 files; about 4,200 added lines are the E2E lane, harness and CI.

## Related work

Refs #3735

RFC: none; @f-trycua asked for a draft PR in #3735, with @injaneity reviewing. The only schema change is click `count` gaining `maximum: 3`, which the routes already enforced.

## Compatibility and risk

Changes outside niri:

- `cua-driver-core` `tool.rs`: the desktop lock becomes an owned `DesktopLease`. A Linux input worker that outlives its call keeps it until it stops, so the next action can't overlap leftover input. A waiter gives up after 12 s with `input_busy`. A worker that never returns, because the compositor or X server stopped answering, keeps later actions refusing until the driver restarts. macOS and Windows take and drop the lease where they took and dropped the lock.
- Every Linux worker that sends Wayland or X11 input runs under `spawn_blocking_bounded` with its call's budget. Most had no time limit before; a structural test fails on a new unbounded one.
- A held mouse button is released or tracked through cancellation, panics and failed releases.
- Click `count` is clamped to 1 to 3 and drag steps to 1 to 200, on X11 too. The Wayland drag path uses i64, so extreme coordinates no longer overflow on Sway or Hyprland.
- Compositor peer attestation moved from `hyprland.rs` to `compositor_peer.rs` without behaviour changes.
- zbus gains `blocking-api`, and `xkbcommon` 0.9 is no longer optional.
- The Wayland E2E runner gives each session its own session bus and keyring, unsets inherited compositor sockets, and bounds startup and cleanup.

Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

Fork CI passed on every Linux, macOS and Windows workflow before the rebase onto current `main`; this PR's CI covers the head. On the niri and Sway lanes, all 132 declared outcomes held (84 deliveries and 48 exact refusals on niri). Locally, `platform-linux` unit tests pass except upstream's Xvfb test, which needs Xvfb.

The niri lane runs niri's winit backend in a headless `cage` (`nix develop .#cua-driver-niri-e2e`) with one 1920x1080 output, floating windows, a US keymap and animations off. Tiled windows, the `us,de` keymap, the lock check and the drag rules are covered by unit tests and nested smokes.

I also ran it on my own niri 26.04 desktop (2560x1440, `focus-follows-mouse` on) against GTK 3, kitty and Chromium, twice, the second time at this head. Text arrived exactly, no click hit the wrong window, and the refusals matched. The first run found three bugs and the second found the `€` one; all are fixed here.

### Limits

- No background input: niri has no per-window capture protocol and no RemoteDesktop/libei.
- IPC reports where a window will be, not where an animation draws it. Animations longer than 1 s can misplace a click; niri's defaults are shorter.
- Overlapping floating windows refuse the affected point, since IPC has no stacking order. Bars and notifications aren't in IPC and can take a click drawn over a window.
- niri scrolls its view without an event for `center-column` and similar actions. The 60 s screenshot age limit bounds that.
- At desktop scope, a double click or drag that starts on an unfocused tiled window stops after the first press, which moves focus.
- With `focus-follows-mouse`, a desktop-scope click on an unfocused window refuses before its press; a new `get_desktop_state` and a second click work.
- With several outputs, window capture and pointer input refuse.
- With client-side decorations, GTK 3 and Chromium windows publish no element frames. Element actions still work.
- Browser identity routes are refused on niri until a browser threat matrix runs there.
- The generated `click.mdx` and Linux MCP spec still lack the click `count` maximum; `cd-cua-driver-docs.yml` regenerates them.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep browser attestation off the renderer while a dialog is open
body:
Salvaged from #5511 (rebuilt on current main so it can land; original authorship kept).

CUA-3261

## What changed

Every browser tool proves the tab's live top-level origin before it runs. That proof asked the renderer for `Page.getFrameTree`, and a page-owned alert, confirm or prompt blocks the renderer, so `browser_dialog` (the tool meant to resolve the dialog) waited out the CDP deadline and refused.

- While a dialog is known to be open on the tab, the origin proof reads the browser process's record of the target (`Target.getTargetInfo`), which answers while the renderer is blocked. The document cannot navigate until the dialog is handled, so that record is current. The existing-profile method policy now allows `Target.getTargetInfo`.
- The first session attached to a tab enables Page events for every later caller, with a 2 s best-effort deadline so a renderer already blocked by an unseen dialog cannot stall the attach. `browser_dialog` keeps its own `Page.enable` as the retry.

Refs #3982.

## Proof

- `an_open_dialog_moves_the_origin_proof_off_the_blocked_renderer`: with a dialog open in the fixture, protected-scope attestation returns the live origin without asking the renderer for its frame tree, and only one `Page.enable` is sent across two calls. With `engine.rs` reverted to main, this test fails.
- Merged origin/main. The only conflict was in `v2_tests.rs`, where both sides added fixture fields and a test. Kept both.

The scoped repository checks, on macOS arm64: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` (1170 passed).
Skipped: the verify-cua-driver desktop lane (Linux X11/Wayland only), and the Linux and Windows builds. Clippy reports one `manual_checked_ops` finding in `fast_path/pixel_guard.rs`, a file this PR does not touch, so main has the same finding. With that lint allowed, the rest is clean.

title: feat(cua-driver): experimental held-pointer route for background native drag-and-drop on macOS
body:
Refs #5477 (MB-09). Draft, experimental, off by default. Do not merge before the decision in "Open question".

## What changes for users
With `CUA_DRIVER_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_DND=1` in the daemon environment, a background `drag` can finish native macOS drag-and-drop (list reordering, moving a file between windows, dragging an object onto a drop zone) without moving the pointer or raising the window. Without the flag nothing changes: same `background_unavailable` refusal, or the brief foreground step from #5481.

## Why the current route fails
A drag-and-drop session ends as soon as the window server reports the hardware button as up. Window-routed events don't change that state (inside the target `NSEvent.pressedMouseButtons` is 0 during a posted drag), so the session cancels about 0.6 s after it starts.

## The route
1. Detect the session as today (drag image window appears).
2. Put a transparent, non-activating shield window under the pointer, then post one hardware `leftMouseDown` at the stationary pointer. The shield takes the press, so the app under the pointer never sees a click.
3. Keep posting the pid-routed drags to the drop point, plus a short settle there.
4. Post the hardware `leftMouseUp` first, then the window-routed up at the drop point (the other order never ends the session).
5. If the pointer moved during the gesture, return an error instead of reporting a drop. If the hold can't be made (no AppKit main loop, button already down), fall back to the existing refusal or foreground step.

## Evidence (macOS 26.5.2 VM, DragLab test app)
- NSTableView reorder, in-app object to drop zone, and Finder file to another app's drop zone all dropped at the requested point; pointer and frontmost app unchanged. Plain canvas drags are untouched.
- Flag off: same refusal as before. User moves the pointer mid-gesture: error, no drop.
- Findings, candidates ruled out (AX drag attributes, global events, pasteboard routes) and limits: the internal findings doc (shared separately).
- Unit tests added for the held gesture order (engage once, settle, hardware release before the window up), no-session and failed-engage cases, and the result shapes.

## Open question
The route posts two hardware events (a down and an up, absorbed by the shield). The bench harness counts `hid_events`, so a scored background run may flag them. Needs a decision before it is used in scoring. Also untested on macOS versions other than 26.5.2, and only AppKit sources and destinations.

title: chore(deps-dev): bump undici from 7.29.0 to 7.30.1 in /libs/cua-driver-bench/taskpack/tasks/shared/cdb-s04/apps/rillwatch-cases
body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) from 7.29.0 to 7.30.1.
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

An exception thrown by a downstream response handler from an asynchronous decompression callback could escape as an uncaught exception. A server could trigger this when decompress was composed with a handler such as dump with a size limit. This release converts downstream handler exceptions into per-request errors.

Subresource Integrity bypass with non-lowercase algorithm tokens

CVE-2026-109841 · GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472

fetch() treated valid mixed-case or uppercase SRI algorithm tokens, such as SHA256, as unknown and could accept a response whose body did not match the configured digest. This release normalizes algorithm tokens before validation and digest selection.

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

... (truncated)

  • 7d60c7b [v7.x] fix(cookies): backport #5663, #5808 and #5832 (#6019)
  • 0227d5d fix: avoid unbounded recursion in Set-Cookie attribute parser (#5757) (#5997)
  • 5394462 fix(websocket): bound automatic PONG writes under backpressure
