title: [Bug]: `protocol_proxy_recovery_test leaves its serve daemons running on macOS after every passing run`
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, every passing run of `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_proxy_recovery_test` leaves two
`cua-driver serve` processes running with PPID 1. They outlive their deleted `/tmp/cua-{idle,recovery}-*` socket
directories, so nothing can reach or stop them, and they keep the test's stderr pipe open, so a caller that pipes
the test's output never finishes.


### Reproduction

1. On macOS, from `libs/cua-driver/rust` at `9bd1d8b76`: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_proxy_recovery_test`
2. After `test result: ok. 2 passed`, run: `ps -axo pid,ppid,pgid,etime,command | grep '[c]ua-driver serve --socket /tmp/cua-'`
3. Two lines remain. Every run adds two more (observed on 3 of 3 runs).
4. Variation, output captured: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_proxy_recovery_test 2>&1 | grep -c ok` never
   returns, although the test binary has exited.
5. Variation, Ctrl-C during the run: four processes remain (two outer, two inner, below).

### Expected behavior

When the test ends, no `cua-driver serve` process it started is still running, and its output pipe closes.

### Actual behavior

```text
 4331     1  4330   00:32 .../target/debug/cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/cua-recovery-dDc0OK/d.sock --no-overlay --no-permissions-gate --dangerously-bypass-approvals
 4332     1  4329   00:32 .../target/debug/cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/cua-idle-ox08vR/d.sock --no-overlay --no-permissions-gate --dangerously-bypass-approvals
```
The PGID (4330) is not the process's own PID: these are the re-exec'd children of the `serve` processes the test
started, and those parents are gone. Two such processes from an earlier run on this machine were still running 7
days later. While a pipe was open, `lsof` showed the leaked daemons' fd 2 connected to the reading end that `grep`
was waiting on.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.37.0 from source, `origin/main` `9bd1d8b76`, debug build. macOS on Apple Silicon (MacBook Air).
Unbundled binary (`target/debug/cua-driver`), as `cargo test` runs it.

### Evidence

Cause, as far as I can trace it:
- The test starts each daemon through `cua_driver_testkit::spawn_in_job`, which puts it in its own process group
  (`process_group(0)`).
- On macOS an unbundled `serve` re-execs itself with responsibility disclaimed
  (`crates/cua-driver/src/responsibility.rs`, `reexec_disclaimed_if_needed`). The outer process only waits; the inner
  one is the daemon. The inner stays in the outer's process group (no `POSIX_SPAWN_SETPGROUP`).
- The test's own `impl Drop for Process` (`tests/protocol_proxy_recovery_test.rs:181`) calls `Child::kill()`, which
  sends SIGKILL to the outer PID only. The inner is reparented to launchd and keeps running.
- The testkit's `ChildReaper` already kills the whole process group on Unix (`reaper.rs`, `process_group_kill`);
  this test uses its own `Drop` instead.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: `pkill -f 'cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/cua-'` after running the test.
I have a test-only fix ready: kill the child's process group in this test's `Drop`. Draft PR to follow and link
here. Alternatives if you'd prefer: hand the daemon to `ChildReaper`, or expose a group kill from the testkit.
The Ctrl-C case is not covered by that fix: the test binary dies before any `Drop` runs.
Unrelated, seen with and without the fix: one or two `service connection rejected before request parsing: read Unix
peer credentials: Socket is not connected (os error 57)` warnings at startup (3 of 3 runs each way).

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: test(cua-driver): stop the proxy recovery test leaking its macOS serve daemons
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS every passing run of `protocol_proxy_recovery_test` leaves two `cua-driver serve`
  daemons running forever, and a caller that pipes the test's output never finishes. Fixes #5588.
- What changed: the test's `Drop` for its spawned processes now kills the child's whole process group on Unix,
  so the re-exec'd daemon goes down with its parent.

## Problem

The test starts `serve` in its own process group (`spawn_in_job`). On macOS an unbundled `serve` re-execs itself
(`responsibility.rs`), and the re-exec'd child is the real daemon. The test's `Drop` sent SIGKILL to the outer PID
only, so the inner daemon was reparented to launchd (PPID 1). It kept running after its socket directory was
deleted, and it held the test's inherited stderr, so `cargo test ... | grep ...` never got EOF.

## Root cause

`impl Drop for Process` used `Child::kill()`, which signals one PID. The inner daemon shares the outer's process
group, and a child does not die with its parent. The testkit's `ChildReaper` already kills the group on Unix; this
test has its own `Drop` and skipped that step.

## Fix

Before `Child::kill()`, send SIGKILL to the child's process group (`libc::kill(-pid, SIGKILL)`, `#[cfg(unix)]`).
The child is a group leader, so its PID is the group ID. Test file only; no shipped code changes. Windows is
unchanged (its kill-on-close Job Object already covers the tree).

## Tests

### Before/after

| Build | `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_proxy_recovery_test` | Test `serve` daemons left after the run | `... 2>&1 \| grep -c ...` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` `9bd1d8b76` | 2 passed | 2 | never returns (2 of 2 attempts) |
| this branch | 2 passed | 0 | returns (6 of 6 runs) |

Check: `ps -axo pid,ppid,pgid,etime,command | grep '[c]ua-driver serve --socket /tmp/cua-'` after the run.

### Checks run

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (passes)
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_proxy_recovery_test` on macOS (2 passed)

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none; test code only.
- Risk and rollback: the group kill only reaches processes in the test child's own group. Revert is one hunk.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: above.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS before/after above. Not run on Linux (no re-exec there; the group kill is
  harmless) or Windows (unchanged).
- Known gaps or CI still required: Ctrl-C during the run still leaks, because the test binary dies before `Drop`;
  out of scope. Alternatives if preferred: route the daemon through `ChildReaper`, or expose a testkit group kill.
  Unrelated, seen with and without this change: one or two startup warnings `read Unix peer credentials: Socket is
  not connected (os error 57)`.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

title: feat(cua-driver): observe ax-only macos window surfaces
body:
Salvaged from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2894.

## Why
Same-process AXWindow surfaces with no CGWindowID are invisible to exact-window snapshots and `list_windows`, so agents cannot read them. This adds the read-only `get_accessibility_surfaces` MCP tool on macOS to report them.

## What changed
- New `get_accessibility_surfaces` tool: a stateless AX walker in `platform-macos`, with its contract types in `cua-driver-core`. The response holds no window id, surface token, element index or action handle.

- Regenerated MCP reference docs and the compat tool list.

## Scope
Observation only. Actions and screenshots stay unsupported for these surfaces. The tool is darwin-only: Linux and Windows do not register it, as with `agent_display`, and its description and the reference say so.

The five source implementation commits are cherry-picked with their original authorship. The branch is updated by merging main. The merges move the new test into the `appkit-cells.tsv` table that main now uses, add SPDX headers to the three new source files, list `get_accessibility_surfaces` next to main's `agent_display` in the darwin compat tool list, and count both in the Reference index.

Size: about 700 production lines added. The new tool needs its own AX walker, tool and contract types, and none can be split out without leaving an unused API.

title: fix(cua-driver): never borrow keycode 8 for a Linux text character
body:
On Linux, a text that needs every free keycode no longer drops a character while reporting it typed. Keycode 8 is no longer borrowed as a spare keycode.

**Why.** X keycodes are evdev codes plus 8, so X keycode 8 is evdev code 0, `KEY_RESERVED`, which the uinput keyboard cannot send. When keycode 8 has no keysyms, `reserve_spare_keycode` scans from the top and reaches keycode 8 last, so the character bound there is lost while the result still counts it as typed. `type_text_in_spare_batches` also counted keycode 8 as a spare, so a batch sized to the free keycodes could lose a character the same way. Both now use `is_spare_keycode`, which skips keycode 8. A text that would have needed keycode 8 now gets the existing "the text needs N spare keycodes" error instead of a silent loss.

**Testing.** On an Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE X11 desktop whose keymap has 19 free keycodes, keycode 8 among them. Distinct CJK characters typed into Mousepad with `type_text` by pid (virtual-keyboard route), current main (a4b5fec) against this branch, alternating builds (ABBA, 10 runs per block, 20 per build):
- 19 characters: main replies "Typed 19 character(s)" but the file holds 18 (the last character, bound to keycode 8, is missing), 20/20 runs; this branch refuses with "typed 0 of 19 characters: the text needs 19 spare keycodes", 20/20.
- 18 characters: both type all 18, 5/5 each.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. In a Debian bookworm container with Rust 1.97.1, `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` passes (671 passed, 0 failed; main has 669, the 2 new tests are `spare_keycodes_skip_keycode_8` and `text_batches_do_not_count_keycode_8_as_spare`), and `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets` reports the same findings as main, none new.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop the Linux focus restore when the saved window is gone
body:
On Linux, a background click that closes the active window (OK in a message box, File > Quit) now returns in about 0.57 s instead of 5.2 s.

**Why.** After a background pointer click, `restore_focus_state` re-activates the window that was active before the click and waits until it stays active. When the click closed that window, the restore kept re-activating a window that no longer existed until its budget ran out. It now returns as soon as the saved window is gone (`XGetWindowAttributes` fails; the X error is ignored for that check).

**Testing.** On an Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE (xfwm4) X11 desktop, a background `click` at the OK button of an active `xmessage` window (path `mpx_pointer`, "focus restored"), current main (a4b5fec) against this branch, alternating builds (ABBA, 10 runs per block, 20 per build):
- click call time p50 5179 ms (5177-5184) on main, 570 ms (569-574) on this branch;
- the window closed in 20/20 runs on both, and a window mapped right after the click got the focus in 20/20 on both.

A click on an accessible target goes through AT-SPI and never reaches this restore, so the delay only shows on windows without AT-SPI, such as `xmessage` or other plain X11 dialogs.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. In a Debian bookworm container with Rust 1.97.1, `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` passes (669 passed, 0 failed, including the Xvfb test `focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened`), and `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets` reports the same findings as main, none new.

title: fix(cua-driver): keys for a popup an MPX click opened go through the master keyboard of the session that clicked
body:
On Linux, keys for a popup that a session's MPX click opened now reach the popup. Escape closes a Chrome context menu opened by a background right-click, and the text typed after it lands in the page.

**Why.** A popup opened by a click from a session's MPX master pointer (a context menu) grabs that master's paired keyboard, not the core keyboard. The popup route sent its keys on the core keyboard with XTest, so Escape never reached the menu, the menu stayed open with its grab, and the next text was lost. This is the key-routing half of #4966 (20342d49b); #5254 carried the master-pointer lifetime but not this part.

Now a click records the popups of the clicked pid (read off the window or a direct child, as popup discovery does) that appeared during its post-check, in the session's click popups from #5254. Keys for such a popup go through that live session's master keyboard, focused on the popup, even when they come from another session (a host that sends each pid-addressed key on a one-call session). These keys do not stamp the session's last use and do not create a pair: the owner check runs under the MPX operation lock, and once the pair is gone the keys take the core route. Keys for any other popup of the pid, such as one that maps after the post-check, keep the core route.

**Testing.** On an Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE X11 desktop with Chrome, current main (de1ba41) against this branch, alternating builds (ABBA, 2 blocks per build):
- right-click a text field (the context menu opens through the session's MPX pointer), 20 arrow keys, Escape, then type: main 0/10, with Escape sent as `xtest_core_grab`, the menu still open afterwards, the text lost and one MPX master left after each block; this branch 10/10, with Escape sent as `mpx_uinput`, the menu closed, the text in the field and no master left;
- a page flow that types after a select popup, after a context menu closed with Escape, and after a cancelled GTK file dialog: the field typed after the context menu is right in 0/10 rounds on main and 10/10 on this branch; the other fields are right on both. The first round after each driver restart read an empty page on both builds and is not counted.

Checks: on this branch, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo build --locked -p cua-driver`, `xvfb-run cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib`, and the `key_input_x11` and `click_input_x11` X11 tests under `xvfb-run` all pass (ubuntu-24.04 runner).

title: fix(cua-driver): await Wayland cursor arrival before desktop clicks
body:
Salvaged from #4735

## Why
A desktop-scope click on native Wayland warped the real pointer and clicked while the agent-cursor overlay was still gliding, so the click could land before the cursor visibly arrived. With the layer-shell overlay backend, the click now waits for the compositor to confirm the cursor reached the target, and refuses if it cannot confirm.

## What changed
- `ClickTool` desktop scope (`tools/click.rs`): on native Wayland with the layer-shell backend, waits for `wayland::overlay::animate_and_wait` before the native click and returns an error when arrival fails. X11 and non-layer-shell sessions keep the best-effort reveal. After a delivered click the pressed cursor hook and the click pulse fire once.
- `wayland/overlay.rs`: arrival is acknowledged by a frame callback at the target, and stale arrival callbacks are cancelled when a newer move supersedes them.
- `prepare_desktop_click_cursor` in `tools/impl_.rs` holds the routing choice, with tests for the unavailable overlay, arrival before one delivery, arrival failure with no fallback, and the X11 reveal.

## Scope
Linux desktop-scope pointer clicks only. Window-scope and element clicks, drag, scroll and keyboard paths are unchanged. Main moved `ClickTool` into `tools/click.rs`, so the original hunk was ported there when merging main.

## Blast Radius
Native Wayland desktop clicks on layer-shell compositors (sway, Hyprland, other wlroots) now wait for cursor arrival and can refuse a click they used to send blind. X11, XWayland and KWin/GNOME without layer-shell keep the previous behavior.

## Verification
At head 2d7483301a85f5379fe6291de26c9c0209cb2e27: the scoped repository checks (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p platform-linux`) passed. The cua-driver verify skill's Linux X11 and Linux Wayland (nested Sway) lanes passed with evidence checks. The nested-Sway capture lane ran twice: `linux-gtk3-desktop-left-click-px-foreground`, the desktop-scope click this changes, was delivered and passed both times. Its one failure, `linux-gtk3-desktop-drag-modifier-px-foreground` (the refusal text now carries a `Next:` hint the test does not expect), fails the same way on main and is outside this diff. Not run: GNOME, KDE and niri lanes. macOS and Windows checks do not apply to this Linux-only change.

title: fix(cua-driver): index disabled macOS controls and report enabled: false
body:
Since 0.17 (#2783), a disabled control on macOS gets no element index, so it's missing from `get_window_state`'s `elements` and its `enabled: false` can never be read. We use cua-driver for UI tests that check things like "Save stays disabled until the form is valid", and that broke when we tried to upgrade.

This indexes disabled controls like any other control. They show up in `elements` with `enabled: false`, and their tree row is tagged `enabled=false`. Actions on them are still refused by `ensure_ax_action_enabled`, so nothing new becomes clickable.

This is the disabled-control part of #3950 on its own. That PR also adds subroles and custom actions and has been waiting on review, so this is meant to be a smaller piece that can land more surgically.

Testing:
- New AppKit harness case `harness_appkit_disabled_control_is_published_and_its_press_refused`, with an opt-in disabled checkbox in the fixture (`CUA_APPKIT_DISABLED_CONTROL=1`), added to the macOS e2e lane. It passes against a local build and fails with the fix reverted ("the disabled checkbox has no element_index"). `smoke`, `query_projects_structured_elements`, `stale_element_token_fails_closed` and `counter` still pass.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (638 pass, two new) and `cargo fmt --check`.
- On a real WebView app (our fitting app's create-client form), the disabled Save button now reads `[25] AXButton "Save" [enabled=false actions=[press]]`, and clicking it is refused with the `AXEnabled=false` message.

Refs #3949, #3950

title: fix(cua-driver): return from a dom_event click when its handler opens a dialog
body:
Salvaged from #4618. Keeps the original authorship and cherry-pick provenance.

A `browser_click` with `input_route="dom_event"` waited out the 20 s CDP call timeout when the element's handler opened a page-owned alert, confirm or prompt, because the dialog blocks the renderer and with it the reply to `Runtime.callFunctionOn`. The click now polls the tab's dialog state while the call is in flight and returns as soon as a dialog opens, with a `dialog` block (`present`, `kind`, `dialog_id`) that `browser_dialog` accepts directly. A click on a tab that already has a dialog open is refused before frame revalidation, which the blocked renderer could not answer either.

- Dialog events come from the attach-time Page subscription that main added in #5524; the click needs no subscription of its own.
- The mock CDP server sends a call's events before suppressing its reply, so a test can model a call that opens a dialog and never returns. The fixture reports a dialog to every session that enabled Page, as Chromium does.
- The `browser_click` description is regenerated into the cua-driver reference page and the macOS, Linux and Windows MCP specs.

Tests: `dom_event_click_returns_when_its_handler_opens_a_dialog` fails with the in-flight dialog check removed (the click takes the full 20 s) and passes with it. `dom_event_click_refuses_while_a_dialog_is_already_open` fails with the early refusal removed and covers both the `dom_event` and trusted coordinate routes.

Checks: the scoped repository checks ran on macOS for `cua-driver-core`, namely `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, the full library test suite, the `cua-driver` protocol and schema consistency tests, a `cua-driver` build, and the cua-driver docs generator in `--check` mode. Clippy allows `manual_checked_ops`, because that lint fires in `fast_path/pixel_guard.rs` on main and is not touched here. Skipped: the verify-cua-driver Linux desktop lanes (X11 and Wayland) and the Windows build, which this host cannot run. The Linux and Windows MCP specs were edited to match, not regenerated on those hosts.

body:
Bumps [@modelcontextprotocol/client](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) from 2.1.0 to 2.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​modelcontextprotocol/client's releases.

@​modelcontextprotocol/client@​2.3.0

Minor Changes

  • #2901 433eb41 Thanks @​claude! - The HTTP client transports and the OAuth client helpers now follow a redirect only when it stays within the origin of the request (same scheme, host and port, or http to https on the same host with default ports) and keeps the method (a 307 or 308, or any redirect of a GET). Any other redirect is not followed. A transport then fails the request with an error that names the target; the session is kept and later messages still send. OAuth metadata discovery moves on to the next well-known URL, and any other OAuth request fails with an error that gives the status. Same-origin redirects that keep the method keep working on Node, up to five in a row, and no code changes are needed there. If your endpoint redirects to another origin, configure the transport with the URL it redirects to. A requestInit.redirect of 'error' or 'manual' is passed to fetch as it is for the requests a transport sends to the server (POST, GET and DELETE of the Streamable HTTP transport, POST of the SSE transport); for its OAuth requests, and for any other value, requestInit.redirect is not consulted by default. Browsers do not expose the target of a redirect to a page, so there a redirected request fails instead of being followed. Setting redirectPolicy: 'follow' on a transport leaves its redirects to the fetch implementation, as before this change.

Patch Changes

  • #2599 5238fba Thanks @​freya0926! - A server can now serve, and a client can now call, tasks/get and tasks/cancel of the Tasks extension (SEP-2663) on a 2026-07-28 connection, when the handler is registered and the request is sent with an explicit schema. Every other method that a protocol revision removed is still refused. If one server factory serves both eras and such a handler is meant for 2025-era clients only, register it only when ctx.era === 'legacy'.

  • #2846 63c0fca Thanks @​Sthreal! - Receiving a large message as a single SSE event over Streamable HTTP, such as a tool result of tens of megabytes, is now fast: a 50 MB result that took about 13 seconds arrives in under a second. The client now requires eventsource-parser 3.0.8 or later. SSEClientTransport reads through the eventsource package and gets the same speed-up once that also resolves eventsource-parser 3.0.8 or later.

  • #2908 633dd3e Thanks @​claude! - The license field of the package manifests is now Apache-2.0; the LICENSE file shipped in each package carries the full terms, including the MIT text for earlier contributions. No code change.

  • #2903 e765b3b Thanks @​claude! - With versionNegotiation in 'auto' or pin mode, a server/discover probe answered with a 2xx that carries no usable reply (a body that is not JSON under application/json, a bare 204, a missing or unaccepted content type) still rejects connect() with EraNegotiationFailed; an empty SSE stream or a 202 surfaces as the probe timeout instead. The message now says the server answered with an unusable reply (...) instead of reading like a network failure. To connect to a 2025 server behind a front that answers the probe this way, pass connect(transport, { prior: { kind: 'legacy' } }) or use mode: 'legacy'.

  • #2905 c0cd01a Thanks @​claude! - SSEClientTransport now retries the SSE connection once after onUnauthorized() resolves, as documented. If the retry is also answered with 401, start() rejects with SdkHttpError (ClientHttpAuthentication) instead of calling onUnauthorized() again. A 401 on a later reconnect of a stream that had opened still gets one refresh.

  • Updated dependencies [633dd3e]:

    • @​modelcontextprotocol/core@​2.3.0

@​modelcontextprotocol/client@​2.2.0

Minor Changes

  • #2887 edd12e2 Thanks @​maxisbey! - Constructing ClientCredentialsProvider, PrivateKeyJwtProvider, StaticPrivateKeyJwtProvider or CrossAppAccessProvider without expectedIssuer is deprecated: the constructor logs one console.warn and that call signature is marked @deprecated. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged. Pass the issuer of the authorization server the credentials were registered with.

    fetchToken() throws AuthorizationServerMismatchError, before sending anything, when the provider's client information is bound to a different authorization server than the one it is called with. The AuthorizationServerMismatchError message no longer assumes the authorization-code callback; its fields are unchanged.

    OAuthTokensSchema and OAuthClientInformationSchema accept the optional issuer stamp, so a provider that reads storage back through them keeps it. auth() overwrites it on every save.

Patch Changes

  • #2885 9dd722f Thanks @​claude! - Sending a notification on a closed connection no longer produces a briefly unhandled promise rejection (seen as unhandledrejection on Cloudflare Workers) in addition to the returned rejection.

  • #2883 c0f7aec Thanks @​claude! - Fix a type-check failure for CommonJS TypeScript projects introduced in 2.1.0: dist/index.d.cts imported types from jose, which is ESM-only, so tsc with module: node16/node18 and skipLibCheck: false failed with TS1479. The two jose types used by the DPoP API (CryptoKey, JWK) are now inlined into the declaration files. No runtime change.

  • #2768 efebf5b Thanks @​web-abin! - Correct the JSDoc for insecure OAuth token endpoints. The TLS requirement comes from the MCP authorization specification's OAuth 2.1 communication-security rules, not SEP-2207, which covers OIDC-flavored refresh-token guidance. Documentation only; no runtime behavior change.

  • #2729 a4ae2f9 Thanks @​claude! - Correct the registerClient @deprecated notice: Dynamic Client Registration was deprecated by spec PR modelcontextprotocol#2858 (Client ID Metadata Documents), not SEP-2577 (which deprecates roots, sampling, and logging). The notice now also names the earliest possible removal date under the feature lifecycle policy (2027-07-28) and clarifies that the client_id_metadata_document_supported gating lives in the built-in auth() flow — registerClient called directly always sends the registration request. Documentation only; no runtime behavior change.

  • #2862 e780e13 Thanks @​SyedTashfin! - Preserve _meta on input_required results. The 2026-07-28 decode seam rebuilt the payload from inputRequests and requestState only, so result-level metadata a server sent on an input_required result (including io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo) was dropped before an allowInputRequired: true caller could see it. Result._meta is a result-level field, so input_required carries it exactly like any other result.

  • #2886 ef39308 Thanks @​claude! - listTools(), listPrompts(), listResources() and listResourceTemplates() called without a cursor now follow nextCursor until the server stops sending one, instead of stopping silently with a short list when a cursor repeats; a page that has the same items and the same nextCursor as the page before it ends the walk and is not added twice, and listMaxPages still caps the walk.

  • #2642 cfa09db Thanks @​claude! - Fix Client.listen() rejections escaping as process-level unhandled rejections. The internal opening promise could reject (ack timeout, transport close, server cancel, caller abort) while listen() was still serially awaiting transport.send(...), so no rejection handler was attached yet — the rejection surfaced as an unhandledRejection that caller-side handling cannot prevent, and a send that never settles (e.g. a stdio write parked on 'drain') left listen() suspended forever even though the ack timer had already fired. listen() now suspends on the opening state machine directly and routes send failures into it, so every termination path rejects the returned promise and nothing escapes.

  • #2597 7f7a94c Thanks @​arimu1! - Treat hostnames ending in .localhost as loopback for the SEP-2207 token-endpoint https guard (RFC 6761 §6.3), so host-based multi-tenant local OAuth works. The SDK does not resolve the name itself: *.localhost reaches the local machine only if the system resolver follows RFC 6761.

title: fix(cua-driver): count only the returned elements in an elements diff read
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `get_window_state` with `since` and `tree_format` `"elements"` or `"both"` fails its own
  output check whenever the read is a diff or "no change". `window_state_view::apply` keeps only the added and changed
  rows in `elements` (`retain_elements`), but `returned_element_count` still holds the full read's count, set by the
  backend before `apply` runs. `WindowStateOutput::validate` then refuses the result: "returned_element_count does
  not match elements". On Cua Driver 0.35.4 this came back from a `run_steps` observation with
  `{"since": "latest", "tree_format": "elements"}` after a press; with the default Markdown format the same read
  works, because `elements` is dropped.
- What changed: after the filter, `retain_elements` sets `returned_element_count` (when the backend set it) to the
  number of elements kept. `total_element_count` still describes the whole read, and `filtered_element_count` (the
  query projection) is unchanged.

## Related work

Refs #4743 (added `since` diffs). I found no issue or pull request for this (searched `returned_element_count`, its
error text, `since`, `tree_format elements diff`). Found while building a voice agent that checks a press's effect
with a diff read.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change):
not required: no schema, parameter or field change; a count in diff reads now matches the contract it already had.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: all three backends share
  `window_state_view::apply`, so diff reads in `"elements"` or `"both"` format return a result instead of failing
  the output check on macOS, Linux and Windows. Markdown reads and full reads (no `since`, or a fallback) are
  unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: five lines in one function. A caller that read `returned_element_count` on a diff as the full
  read's count gets the kept count; such a read failed the output check before this change, so no working caller
  depended on it. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (rustc 1.97.1, the pin): new test
  `window_state_view::tests::an_elements_diff_counts_only_the_elements_it_returns` runs a read, an edited read and an
  unchanged read with `since: "latest"` in `"elements"` and `"both"`, and checks each result against
  `WindowStateOutput::validate`, the kept elements and both counts. On `main` it fails with
  `Err("returned_element_count does not match elements")`. With the change:
  `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib` 1081 passed, 1 ignored (three runs);
  `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test` 2 passed, 1 ignored; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
  clean; `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib --tests` no warnings.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. This is in shared response shaping, below every backend; I did not run a
  desktop harness.
- Known gaps or CI still required: a desktop run of `get_window_state` / `run_steps` observation with
  `tree_format: "elements"` and `since: "latest"` on any backend.

Review: one round by a second model (Codex), read-only: no P1, P2 or P3 findings. It checked that
`filtered_element_count` should stay the query count and that no other path filters `elements` after the backend
counts them.

- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

title: fix(cua-driver): index disabled macOS controls and report enabled: false
body:
Salvaged from #5619. Both contributor commits are cherry-picked unchanged (-x), with the original author and author dates kept. The branch has since merged origin/main, plus one follow-up commit that corrects a code comment.

Fixes #3949 for its first half on macOS. Disabled actionable and writable-value controls stay indexed. They are published with `enabled: false` in `elements` and show `enabled=false` in tree rows. `AXEnabled` reads stay gated to actionable or value-settable nodes. title: cua-driver bounded mode: launch_app is not scoped to resources.apps (per-app launch flag is never enforced)
body:
## Summary

In `bounded` mode, `launch_app` is authorized by the tool allowlist only. It is not scoped to the manifest's `resources.apps` allowlist, and the per-application `launch` flag is parsed but never enforced. An agent can therefore launch any installed application, including apps that are not in the manifest.

## Environment

- cua-driver 0.23.2 (macOS 26.2, arm64), daemon started with `serve --permission-mode bounded --capability-manifest <path> --approve-capability-manifest`
- Same code path appears unchanged in 0.37.0 (see below)

## Manifest (minimal)

```yaml
version: 3
allow:
  tools: [start_session, end_session, list_windows, launch_app, get_window_state]
resources:
  apps:
    - bundle_id: com.apple.TextEdit
      launch: true
      windows: all
  desktop:
    display: false
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Make sure Calculator is not running.
2. Call `launch_app` with `{"name": "Calculator"}` (or `{"bundle_id": "com.apple.calculator"}`).

## Expected

The call is refused as outside the capability manifest, because Calculator is not in `resources.apps` (and, for listed apps, only allowed when `launch: true`).

## Actual

Calculator is launched. A follow-up `list_windows {"pid": <calculator pid>}` is then refused with `desktop application pid <pid> is outside the capability manifest`, so the manifest is enforced for observation but not for the launch itself.

## Code pointers (tag `cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0`)

- `cua-driver-core/src/session_manifest.rs`: `ApplicationGrant.launch` is assigned when the manifest is parsed (`launch: raw.launch`) but is not read anywhere else in the crates.
- `cua-driver-core/src/authorization.rs`: `launch_app` is classified as an R1 action; the protected-resource authorization (`private_observation`, `desktop_input`, `process_control`, ...) has no application-launch resource kind, so no app-level check runs for it.

The same holds at `cua-driver-rs-v0.23.2`.

## Suggested fix

Treat `launch_app` as an application resource: resolve the requested `bundle_id`/`name` (or `launch_path`) to an identity and allow it only when a `resources.apps` entry matches that identity with `launch: true`. Refuse with `bounded_resource_outside_manifest` otherwise.

## Impact

In `bounded` mode the manifest is meant to be the ceiling. Today a client that may call `launch_app` for one app can start any app, which can have side effects (login items, network activity, document recovery) without the reviewer having allowed that app.

title: cua-driver bounded mode: allowlist-filtered app/window discovery when desktop.display is not granted
body:
## Summary

Feature request: in `bounded` mode without `resources.desktop.display`, provide app/window discovery filtered to the manifest's `resources.apps` allowlist instead of refusing it.

## Problem

With an apps-only manifest (`desktop.display: false`), `list_apps`, unfiltered `list_windows` and `get_accessibility_tree` are refused as desktop observation. Pid-scoped calls (`list_windows {"pid": ...}`, `get_window_state`) work for allowlisted apps, but there is no read-only way to find the pid of an allowlisted app that is already running. The only remaining route is `launch_app` (idempotent for a running app), which has side effects when the app is not running and is currently not scoped to the allowlist (see the related issue on `launch_app` scoping).

As a result, clients such as agent frameworks cannot do the most common bounded workflow ("capture or act on the TextEdit window") without either granting `desktop.display: true` (which exposes the names and titles of every window and enables full-screen capture where the tool is allowed) or launching apps.

## Proposal

When the manifest has no `desktop.display` grant:

- `list_windows` without `pid` returns only windows whose owning process matches a `resources.apps` entry (the same identity check `authorize_desktop_window` already performs), instead of refusing.
- `list_apps` returns only running/installed apps that match a `resources.apps` entry.
- Optionally the same for `get_accessibility_tree`.
- `get_desktop_state` (full-screen pixels) stays gated by `desktop.display`.

A response field such as `"filtered_by_manifest": true` would let clients tell a filtered listing from a complete one.

## Why this is safe

The filtered results reveal nothing beyond what the manifest already authorizes: any listed window can already be observed with `list_windows {"pid": ...}` once its pid is known. Non-allowlisted apps stay invisible, so the bounded profile keeps its meaning while becoming usable for discovery.

## Environment

cua-driver 0.23.2 on macOS 26.2 (arm64); the relevant authorization code appears unchanged in 0.37.0.

title: fix(cua-driver): paint the macOS cursor overlay as a region, not a full-screen frame
body:
On macOS, while the agent cursor animates (glide, click, resting float, idle fade; several seconds after each action), background actions are now 3–4x faster and WindowServer stays nearly idle.

**Why.** Every animation frame allocated a pixmap the size of the main display, converted it to a `CGImage` and set it as the contents of the full-screen overlay layer. At 60 fps that kept WindowServer compositing a full-screen layer (163–184% CPU on a VM without GPU) and the driver busy converting images, and every window-list query and background action in that time waited behind it. Frames now paint only the region the cursors cover, grown by their motion effects (`effect_bounds`), focus rect and laid-out session badge (the screen edge clamps the badge, which can shift it away from the cursor), into a sublayer placed at that region with implicit animations off, as the Linux overlay paints a tile. The full-screen window and its z-order handling are unchanged. A cursor drawn with a custom theme takes the whole screen, since theme validation does not bound geometry to the cursor's region. The focus rect now honours the paint origin (`paint_cursor` subtracted the origin from everything but the focus rect; only macOS passes one).

**Testing.** macOS 26.5 VMs without GPU, background `press_key` / `type_text` / `scroll` to a TextEdit window behind Calculator, overlay on, current main against this branch (and against this branch plus #5641), alternating builds in the order main, branch, branch+PR2, branch+PR2, branch, main, 10 calls per block, so 20 per build and tool, 1 s apart, 0 errors, p50:

| tool | 1x (1280x800) main → this branch | 2x (2560x1600) main → this branch |
|---|---|---|
| press_key | 1386 → 482 ms | 1946 → 472 ms |
| type_text | 1610 → 584 ms | 2394 → 572 ms |
| scroll | 1817 → 598 ms | 1912 → 582 ms |

- Every block of this branch was faster than every block of main (1x press_key block medians: main 1584 and 1386, branch 482 and 476).
- CPU during ten background key presses, alternating builds twice: WindowServer 166–167% → 14–16% at 1x and 183–186% → 7.5–7.7% at 2x; the driver 53–62% → 7–11%. A Mac with a GPU composites the old frames more cheaply, so its gain is smaller.
- With the overlay disabled at runtime (`set_agent_cursor_enabled false`), the old code's background `press_key` was already 0.87–1.1 s, which isolates the cost to the overlay.
- Pixels: the new test `the_tile_holds_every_pixel_of_the_full_screen_paint` paints glide and click frames both ways at 1x and 2x, from four start points (including the screen edges, where the badge clamps), with and without the verbose badge and with three focus rects: no pixel is drawn outside the region, and inside it pixels differ by at most one antialiasing coverage sample (≤17/255, sub-pixel rounding at a different origin). `a_custom_theme_paints_the_whole_screen` covers the custom-theme path.
- On screen (reduced motion, after a background action): position, shape and stacking above the target window match the old build at 1x and 2x; at 2x the cursor is drawn at backing resolution.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes; `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib cursor::overlay` (13 passed) and `cargo test -p cursor-overlay --lib` (111 passed) on macOS 15; clippy reports nothing in the touched files.

title: fix(cua-driver): skip the Space snapshot in the macOS background gate and window-change detector
body:
**Why.** The background gate's keyboard-destination count (`gather_background_facts`) and the window-change detector's snapshot and polls enumerated windows through `all_windows()` / `visible_windows()`, which also ask SkyLight for every window's Spaces. Neither reads the Space fields: the gate uses pid, window id, on-screen state and bounds; the detector uses id, pid, app name and title. They now use Space-free enumerations of the same lists (`all_windows_without_spaces`, `visible_windows_without_spaces`).

**Testing.** macOS 26.5 VM: with a temporary assert mode that computed both lists on every call, the gate's rows and its competing-destination count were equal in 10/10 calls and the detector's lists in 148/148 observations, across a normal background window, another app's window above the target, a print sheet on the target, a minimized target, a full-screen target, and two windows on another Space. The refusals for the sheet (`window_not_key`) and the minimized window (`minimized_or_hidden_window`) were unchanged, and a background cmd+n and cmd+o to TextEdit still report `TextEdit ("Untitled")` (336 ms) and `TextEdit ("Open")` (533 ms) on upstream main plus this change and the overlay change.

On upstream main plus the overlay change (#5640), adding this change moves the background p50 by a few milliseconds (1x: press_key 482 → 474, type_text 584 → 576, scroll 598 → 594 ms; 2x: 472 → 466, 572 → 571, 582 → 578 ms, 20 calls per build, alternating). The Space snapshot costs little while WindowServer is idle, about 3 ms per enumeration against under 1 ms without it in the driver's phase timings, and much more while it is busy: with the full-screen overlay running, these enumerations took 200–260 ms.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes; builds on macOS 15.

title: fix(cua-driver): restore the X11 active window by bouncing the core focus when only the WM's record moved
body:
On Linux under xfwm4, a background `type_text` into a window behind another no longer leaves the front window looking inactive.

**Why.** xfwm4 takes a FocusIn from any master keyboard as the desktop focus, so focusing the session's MPX keyboard on a background window moves `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` there while the core focus stays on the user's window. The focus guard's EWMH re-activation then hands xfwm4 its stale record back: the core focus already sits there, no FocusIn follows, and the active window stays wrong (`focus_outcome=not_restored` after the full 600 ms restore budget), or the same-app rule leaves it in place. When the core focus and the stacking top are unchanged and only the active window moved, the restore now sets the core focus to None and back, which gives the WM a real FocusIn. Both requests are sent before either is checked, so the focus is None only while the server processes them, and the restore is reported only when the core focus reads back as the saved window (a failed second request, e.g. the window unmapped meanwhile, ends the restore).

**Testing.** Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE (xfwm4 4.18) X11 desktop, background `type_text` into the back window of two, current main (fe6498d) against this branch, alternating builds (ABBA, 10 rounds per block, 20 per build and pair), 0 errors:

| back:front | active window kept main → branch | outcome main → branch | `type_text` p50 main → branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| mousepad:mousepad | 0/20 → 20/20 | same_app_dialog 20 → restored 20 | 485 → 635 ms |
| gedit:mousepad | 1/20 → 20/20 | not_restored 19, restored 1 → restored 20 | 1103 → 636 ms |
| gnome-text-editor:mousepad | 1/20 → 20/20 | not_restored 19, restored 1 → restored 20 | 1103 → 636 ms |
| xfce4-terminal:mousepad | 1/20 → 20/20 | not_restored 19, restored 1 → restored 20 | 1105 → 639 ms |

On main the active window points away from the front window for about 1.8–2.4 s per call; with this branch for about 0.23 s (the typing itself). On the same-app pair main skips the restore and leaves the front window inactive; the branch restores it, which costs the restore's three stable polls (+150 ms).

- Text landed in the back window 20/20 and the core focus stayed on the front window in every call of both builds.
- A uinput keyboard typing into the front window every 25 ms around each call (measured on the same code before this rebase): 2000/2000 keys in front, none in back, none lost, with and without the change.
- New tests with a fake connection: `the_bounce_sends_both_focus_requests_before_checking_either`, `a_bounce_whose_saved_window_is_gone_does_not_restore`.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes; `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` (713 passed) and the X11 key and click regressions under Xvfb pass.

title: fix(cua-driver): paint the macOS cursor overlay as a region, not a full-screen frame
body:
Salvaged from #5640.

## Why

On macOS, every animation frame of the agent cursor allocated a pixmap the size of the main display, converted it to a `CGImage`, and set it as the contents of the full-screen overlay layer. At 60 fps this kept WindowServer compositing a full-screen layer, and background actions queued behind it. CMGS measured `press_key` going from 1386 to 482 ms (p50, 1x) and WindowServer CPU from 166% to 15% on GPU-less macOS 26.5 VMs (#5640). Current main (0cdcec94b) still paints the full frame.

## What changed

- `paint_tile` paints only the region the cursors cover (`paint_bounds`), into a `CALayer` sublayer placed at that region with implicit animations off. The region is the 64 pt cursor tile plus `effect_bounds()`, the focus rect, and the laid-out, edge-clamped session badge. Linux already paints its overlay this way. A cursor with a custom theme still gets the whole screen. CMGS's commit (f25b76af8) is unchanged.
- `paint_cursor` now subtracts the paint origin from the focus rect as well. Before, only macOS passed a non-zero origin.
- New on merge: since #6142 made marks (including the focus rect) and motion effects opt-in, the pixel test `the_tile_holds_every_pixel_of_the_full_screen_paint` turns on `CursorOptions::ALL_ON` and every `MotionEffects` flag, and asserts that at least one frame played an effect. Without this, the test would only compare a plain arrow.

## Scope

The macOS overlay render path only. Window placement, z-order handling, and the Linux and Windows overlays are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS user with the agent cursor on. If an effect is drawn outside `paint_bounds`, it gets clipped on screen. The pixel test is the guard against that, and it runs only on macOS.

## Verification

Merged current main (0cdcec94b) into the branch. There were no conflicts, including with #6142, #6117 and #5780, which touched the overlay since.

- `cargo test --locked -p cursor-overlay` on Linux: 127 passed, 0 failed. This covers the shared `paint_cursor` origin change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes.
- `CI: Rust macOS unit` at this head: `the_tile_holds_every_pixel_of_the_full_screen_paint` and `a_custom_theme_paints_the_whole_screen` pass, with the full `platform-macos` lib suite ([run](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/41330404457/job/124919098070)).

Not verified locally: `platform-macos` does not build on this Linux host (no macOS SDK; cross `cargo check` fails in `rquickjs-sys`). Clippy for `platform-macos` was not run. On-screen rendering and the performance numbers come from #5640 and were measured before #6142.

title: fix(cua-driver): restore the X11 active window by bouncing the core focus when only the WM's record moved
body:
Salvaged from #5642.

Cherry-picked aa52d43249a36c032955c88accb1f80ebc55de53 onto origin/main d0031e5461f546b42881b1a3ab04030e7b85bed1, preserving CMGS's authorship. Commit message checked for coauthor trailers (none present).

Restores WM-only focus changes by bouncing core focus through None, queues both requests before checking, and verifies saved focus before reporting success. Includes regression tests for request ordering and failed restoration.

Merged main in to clear the conflict. Main had moved the closed / same-app / grab decision into `interaction::policy::guard_restore` and the restore deadline to `CLEANUP_CAP`. The resolution keeps both: the WM-only case now passes `new_owner.filter(|_| !wm_only)` to `guard_restore`, which suppresses only the same-app arm (it needs all three owners equal), while the closed-window and grab-held arms work as before. `classify_focus_move` / `FocusMove` stay removed as on main.

Proof, live X11 (Xvfb, no compositor), run once under xfwm4 4.20 and once under openbox. Window A is focused. A second XI2 master keyboard then sets its focus to window B, so `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` moves to B while the core focus and stacking stay on A. `FocusSnapshot::capture` / `restore_if_changed` run around it:

- main: `focus_outcome=not_restored`, active window left on B (both WMs)
- this branch: `focus_outcome=restored`, core focus and active window back on A (both WMs)

The scoped repository checks pass for `platform-linux` (fmt, test). `cargo clippy -D warnings` fails only on existing lints in files this PR does not touch; `focus_guard.rs` has none. No Windows or macOS crates are touched.

Review notes: if the saved window unmaps between the two focus requests, the second one fails and the restore stops, leaving the core focus on None rather than at the window's revert target. That window is two back-to-back requests wide. The `wm_only` gate itself is covered by the live proof, not by a unit test.

title: fix(cua-driver): scope bounded launch_app to resources.apps launch grants
body:
## Problem

In `bounded` mode, `launch_app` was authorized by the tool allow-list only.
`ApplicationGrant.launch` was parsed from the manifest (`launch: raw.launch`)
but never read (it carried `#[allow(dead_code)]`), and
`SessionManifest::authorize_call` had no `launch_app` arm. A manifest that
allowed `launch_app` for one app therefore let the agent start any installed
app (for example Calculator with only TextEdit listed). Observation of the
launched app was still refused afterwards, but the launch had already happened.

## Fix

`SessionManifest::authorize_call` now handles `launch_app`. The call is allowed
only when **every** identity field the request names matches a
`resources.apps` entry with `launch: true`:

| Request field | Must match |
| --- | --- |
| `bundle_id`, `aumid` | a granted `bundle_id`, exactly (not a Windows path identity) |
| `name`, `path`, `launch_path` | a granted absolute `executable`, exactly; Windows paths (and Windows path `bundle_id` grants) compare normalized with the existing `normalize_windows_executable_path` |

Why every field: the platforms prefer different fields (Linux ignores
`bundle_id`; Windows prefers `launch_path`, then `path`). Without this, a
granted `bundle_id` could stand in front of a `name` that the platform
actually launches.

It fails closed:

- A display name or bare command (`{"name": "Calculator"}`) is refused,
  because the core cannot tie it to an identity before the platform resolves
  it. Callers pass the `bundle_id` or the absolute executable path instead.
- A request that names no identity, or an empty or non-string identity field,
  is refused.
- Entries listed with `launch: false` (the default) do not admit a launch.

Refusals use the existing manifest wording, for example
`launch_app bundle_id 'com.apple.calculator' is outside the capability manifest`.

`run_script`'s `cua.launch()` calls `launch_app` through `ToolRegistry::invoke`,
which runs the same `authorize_tool_call_with_context` → `authorize_call`
path, so scripts are covered without a separate change.

## Tests

- `session_manifest::tests::launch_app_is_scoped_to_application_grants_with_launch`:
  allowed `bundle_id`, executable and Windows path grants; an app listed with
  `launch: false`; unlisted bundle id, display name and AUMID; a `launch_path`
  with extra arguments; a granted `bundle_id` paired with an unlisted `name`;
  missing, empty and non-string identities. Each refusal asserts the exact
  message.
- `tool::runtime_isolation_tests::manifest_launch_reaches_the_platform_only_for_launchable_apps`:
  goes through `ToolRegistry::invoke_with_context` with a manifest loaded in
  `bounded`, `standard` and `unrestricted` contexts (a manifest narrows every
  mode) and asserts the platform tool runs only for the `launch: true` app,
  plus the exact refusal code and message for the others.

Both tests fail when the `launch_app` arm is removed (mutation-checked). The
first one also fails when the `launch` flag check is dropped.

Run locally (macOS 26, arm64, toolchain 1.97.1 from `rust-toolchain.toml`):

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check                          # clean
cargo test -p cua-driver-core                       # 1082 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (lib) + all other targets ok
cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test  # ok
cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets       # no warnings
```

No desktop E2E was run. The change is in the platform-independent
authorization layer, and the platform `launch_app` implementations are
unchanged.

## Known gaps and questions for reviewers

- **Refusal code.** Like the existing `browser_prepare` and `browser_navigate`
  checks in `authorize_call`, the refusal comes back as `permission_denied`.
  The issue and `guides/permissions.mdx` suggest `bounded_resource_outside_manifest`.
  Changing that would also affect the existing `authorize_call` arms, so I left
  it for a maintainer decision.
- **Display names are refused under a manifest.** `{"name": "TextEdit"}` no
  longer works with a TextEdit grant; callers pass `bundle_id` or the absolute
  executable. The reporter confirmed this is fine for their use.
- **Windows `urls`.** On Windows, `launch_app` opens `urls` in the default
  browser. With this change the request must still name a granted app, but the
  URLs themselves are not checked against the manifest. This is unchanged
  from before.

Fixes #5638

title: [Feature]: Publish a public Nix binary cache for cua-driver
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### User problem

I use cua-driver on NixOS with Hyprland through this repository's flake package and `nixosModules.cua-driver`. Installing or upgrading it requires compiling the Rust driver and its dependencies locally, which makes NixOS updates noticeably slower.

### Desired outcome

Provide a documented public Nix binary cache for the existing cua-driver package, starting with `x86_64-linux`, so users with matching build inputs can download the built package. The cached package should retain the current Nix build's `portal-input` and `portal-capture` features.

### Current workaround

Build the flake package locally. The published Linux release binaries are another distribution option, but the current release workflow enables `portal-input`, while the Nix package also enables `portal-capture`. I would like to preserve the Nix package's Wayland capabilities.

### Affected components and platforms

- `packages.x86_64-linux.cua-driver`
- `nixosModules.cua-driver`
- NixOS users, including Hyprland/Wayland setups

### Alternatives and prior art

- #4098 added Magic Nix Cache for GitHub Actions. The current workflow sets `use-flakehub: disabled`; the action's [documentation](https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/magic-nix-cache-action/tree/84c0677f58dcedf3b91f8223ce36a9ea5b3c84b7#why-use-the-magic-nix-cache) explains that its GitHub Actions cache is only usable in CI.
- #4155 discusses Nix CI costs and the status of the NixOS module. This is a concrete end-user use case for the exported package and module.

### Implementation ideas

Publish successful existing Nix builds from trusted `main` or release-tag workflows to a maintainer-controlled public cache, such as Cachix, Attic, or FlakeHub Cache.

Document the substituter URL, public signing key, supported platform, and an example configuration that actually gets cache hits. In particular, explain that consumers need matching build inputs: overriding `cua.inputs.nixpkgs` with `follows = "nixpkgs"` can change the derivation and miss a cache built with the repository's own lockfile.

### Contribution question

If I prepare a focused PR for publishing the existing Nix build outputs and adding the consumer setup documentation, would you be willing to review it? Or would you prefer this work to be implemented by the official maintainers, in which case I should wait for a maintainer-led PR?

If a community PR is welcome, please let me know the preferred cache backend and which infrastructure setup would need to be handled by maintainers.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop the Node runtime leaking a libuv handle per future poll
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: every `await` of an async SDK call leaks a ThreadsafeFunction, and with it a libuv async handle, in the host process. libuv walks every async handle on each event loop wakeup, so the host slows down for as long as it runs. A pending `EmbeddedCuaDriverHost.waitForExit(generation)` polls about 19 times a second (582 polls in 30 s on an idle host). In our Electron app, after about a day the main thread sat at 100% CPU: 3,643 of 3,658 `sample` stacks were inside libuv's `uv__async_io` loop, checking handles that weren't pending, and every window stuttered because input routing runs on that thread.
- What changed: both Node runtime builds (`libs/cua-driver` and `libs/cua`) now cache one callback trampoline per callback name and JS function, so a given continuation builds its ThreadsafeFunction once instead of on every poll. This is UBRN's own fix (jhugman/uniffi-bindgen-react-native#440, released in 0.31.0-4), backported onto the pinned 0.31.0-3 source.

Why a backport instead of bumping UBRN: 0.31.0-4 also rewrote the RustBuffer boundary that `patchRegister` and `patchCall` patch for Electron. Neither applies to 0.31.0-4 or 0.31.0-6. Bumping means porting the copy-mode patch to the new buffer ownership model and regenerating bindings against the newer `@ubjs/core`, which is a larger change than this fix needs.

How: `node-runtime-trampoline-cache.rs` is UBRN's `callback/cache.rs` from #440, unmodified (MPL-2.0, like the rest of the runtime). Three new transformations declare the module, create one `TrampolineCache` per registration, and check it in call dispatch before building a trampoline, the way #440 does. Every replacement goes through `replaceOnce`, so a later UBRN bump fails the build loudly instead of shipping a silently unpatched runtime. The Electron buffer patches are unchanged. Both `node-runtime-NOTICE.md` files now credit the backported file.

## Third-party work

Submitted on behalf of a third party: jhugman and the uniffi-bindgen-react-native contributors.

- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/node-runtime-trampoline-cache.rs` and `libs/cua/scripts/node-runtime-trampoline-cache.rs` are `runtimes/napi/src/callback/cache.rs` from jhugman/uniffi-bindgen-react-native commit [5d24b38](https://github.com/jhugman/uniffi-bindgen-react-native/commit/5d24b38f2e838f5f37ae44bc1a94c8be500de673) (#440), unmodified.
- The call-dispatch and registration code that `patchCallTrampolines` and `patchRegisterTrampolines` insert is adapted from the same commit.
- License: Mozilla Public License 2.0, the same license as the rest of the runtime this build already derives from. The MPL header is kept in the file, and both `node-runtime-NOTICE.md` files now name the file, its source commit and its license.
- I'm not aware of any related patents, trademarks or other restrictions.

My own contribution is the integration into `build-node-runtime.mjs`, the regression test, the notice updates and the measurements.

## Related work

Refs #4339

#4339 reports this leak. A comment there identifies the runtime cause and #440, and notes that an npm override to a newer runtime breaks the generated bindings. #4488 makes `wait_for_exit` wake its caller once instead of every 50 ms. That removes the biggest trigger, but as its description says, every other repeatedly woken future (such as the readiness loop in `start()`) still leaks one handle per wake until the runtime is fixed. The two changes are independent and touch different files.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. No API, generated binding, or checksum changes. Only the internals of the shipped `.node` runtime change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: no API change. Hosts that await SDK calls stop accumulating native callbacks. The cached trampoline is stored on the JS function under a per-registration Symbol, as in UBRN 0.31.0-4 and later. Trampolines are still never freed; there is now one per distinct function instead of one per call.
- Risk and rollback: the cache code is the upstream implementation that UBRN 0.31.0-4 onward ship. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (macOS 27 arm64, Rust 1.97.1, `uniffi-bindgen-react-native@0.31.0-3` as pinned):
  - Built the runtime with `build-node-runtime.mjs` from `8cb196a` (the follow-up commit changes only the notices). Unpatched and patched builds emit the same compiler warnings.
  - New `libs/cua-driver/typescript/test/native-runtime-callbacks.test.mjs` records the continuation passed to `rust_future_poll` over 50 awaits and asserts it carries exactly one cached trampoline marker, unchanged across polls. It fails on the current runtime (`actual: 0, expected: 1`) and passes with this change. RSS is too noisy to assert on, so the test asserts the invariant directly, as #440's own test does.
  - Event-loop cost, measured as a worker-thread `postMessage` round trip after N async SDK calls, with each runtime swapped into `@trycua/cua-driver@0.36.0`:

    | | 5,000 calls | 20,000 calls | 60,000 calls |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | current runtime | 52 µs | 244 µs | 4.1 ms |
    | this change | 8.8 µs | 8.7 µs | 8.7 µs |

    JS heap after a forced GC, from 20,000 to 200,000 calls: 22 MB to 148 MB before, 8 MB to 8 MB after.
  - Under Electron 42's Node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`), the 60,000-call round trip is 2.7 ms on the current runtime and 10.3 µs with this change.
- Manual or platform evidence: with this runtime swapped into `@trycua/cua-driver-darwin-arm64@0.36.0`, our Electron app's native tests pass against a 0.36.0 driver in a real Electron main process: SDK load, embedded MCP connect and stop, then isolated-browser open, navigate, semantic snapshot, type, click, dropdown, date, save, edit and reload.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - Built and tested on macOS arm64 only. The cache uses only `napi::sys` calls, and UBRN ships it on every platform, but the Windows and Linux runtime builds still need CI.
  - The `libs/cua` runtime builds with this change, but I didn't exercise it through the `@trycua/cua` API.
  - I didn't run the full SDK `npm test` suite; I ran the new test against the built runtime.
  - A separate, smaller leak remains: each async call still leaks 288 bytes of native memory. macOS `leaks` attributes it to one 128-byte object allocated in `uniffi_core::ffi::rustfuture::rust_future_new` in `cua_driver_sdk`, plus the two 80-byte mutexes it owns, on every call, including successful ones such as `host.stop()` on a stopped host. Something appears to keep the `RustFuture` alive after `rust_future_free`. It doesn't involve the event loop, so I've left it out of this PR rather than guess at a fix.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included. (`node-runtime-trampoline-cache.rs` is jhugman's upstream code; the commit carries a `Co-authored-by: jhugman` trailer.)
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (Not applicable: this is a releasing `fix`.)

title: [Bug]: Daemon-backed direct Spaces wait ~10s for presence QUIC on loopback before starting video
body:
## Summary

In the macOS Cua Spaces app, opening a daemon-backed **direct** Space spends approximately ten seconds at “Connecting…” before showing video. The optional presence QUIC connection appears to use the daemon's loopback HTTP passthrough hostname together with the remote host's advertised UDP port. Video startup awaits that connection before falling back to TCP presence.

## Environment

- Mac client: Cua Spaces 0.12.1 (0.12.1.94), bundled cua daemon 0.6.0, macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon.
- Remote Mac: macOS 27.0.1, cua-spacesd 0.5.3.
- Space registered by its Tailscale address, with local token authentication; no Cua relay.
- Remote desktop: 3840×2160. Display held awake during the controlled timing comparisons.

## Reproduction

1. Run a direct host with its default QUIC listener enabled.
2. Register it in the Mac app and use the app's normal daemon-backed connection.
3. Navigate from the Spaces list to that Space's embedded desktop viewer.
4. Measure until the viewer receives/displays its first frame.

Expected: optional cursor transport negotiation should not add a ten-second delay before video.

Observed: the app remains at “Connecting…” for roughly eleven seconds in total, despite fast direct media startup.

## Evidence

| Test | Observation |
|---|---|
| Direct Tailscale reachability | Approximately 23 ms round trip |
| Standalone OpenMedia + WebSocket probe, native 4K and 1080p cap | First binary video packet in 277–351 ms; this measures packet arrival, not GUI decoding |
| App UDP traffic during Connecting | nettop shows outgoing UDP over lo0, without replies |
| Temporary loopback UDP forward from 127.0.0.1:3212 to the remote host's Tailscale UDP port | Bidirectional QUIC packets; the same embedded viewer became live in **1.313 s** |
| Remove that forward and repeat with the display still awake | Embedded viewer became live in **11.254 s** |
| Restart host with CUA_ENV_QUIC_PORT=0; no forward present | Embedded viewer became live in **1.250 s** |

These are local single-run GUI comparisons, not a broad benchmark. The temporary forward was removed after diagnosis. No token, packet payload, or private screenshot is included here.

Display sleep was separately observed to cause empty display discovery; it was excluded from these controlled comparisons.

## Relevant code path

The relevant code was inspected in both the 0.12.1 tag and current main:

- [native/spaces.rs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.12.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-sdk/src/native/spaces.rs): daemon-backed native handles use a loopback HTTP passthrough while retaining the direct Space identity.
- [presence_datagrams.rs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.12.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces-ext/src/presence_datagrams.rs): derives the QUIC hostname from the Space websocket URL and uses the advertised remote port.
- [presence.rs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.12.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/presence.rs): join_presence_with awaits the optional datagram connection with the caller's timeout, then silently falls back on failure.
- [SpaceStreamProvider.swift](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.12.1/libs/spaces-app-swift/Sources/CuaSpacesStreaming/SpaceStreamProvider.swift) supplies a 10,000 ms presence timeout; [LiveStreamSession.swift](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.12.1/libs/spaces-app-swift/Sources/CuaSpacesStreaming/LiveStreamSession.swift) awaits presence before opening media.

## Possible narrow fix

In the SDK's native Space::join_presence, use the existing join_presence_with(..., datagrams) API with datagrams=false for Host::Daemon handles until a reachable UDP endpoint is represented correctly. Embedded direct connections could retain QUIC. Cursor updates would continue through the Join stream and UpdateCursor RPC, without disabling QUIC globally on the host.

This is a proposed fix, not a tested patch. Regression coverage should verify prompt daemon-backed direct startup, working TCP cursor updates, unchanged embedded/direct QUIC, and relay/cloud/older-server behavior.

A complete solution could carry a separately validated reachable UDP endpoint. Deriving reachability from the original Space ID alone would not cover remote daemons and forwarded guests safely.

## Workaround and related issue

CUA_ENV_QUIC_PORT=0 (or serve --quic-port 0) on the host avoids the timeout; TCP/WebSocket media and input continue to work.

Related: #5346 requests QUIC **media** support. This report concerns the existing QUIC **presence** path blocking startup and selecting the wrong host. Searches for QUIC, presence, datagrams, cursor_datagrams, join_presence and loopback did not reveal an existing report of this specific failure.

feat(cua-host): add `cua host update` to refresh cua-spacesd in place
body:
## Problem

There is no supported way to update `cua-spacesd` on a computer that is already set up as a host.

- `cua host setup` is the only command that downloads a release, and it also re-registers with the relay and rewrites config and policy. With both sharing options off it stops at its first check (`with neither the desktop nor Spaces there is nothing to share`), so nothing is downloaded.
- `cua host start` is refused in that state too, and `cua host config --desktop on` would change what the computer shares just to get an update.
- The Cua Spaces app does not bundle `cua-spacesd`, so app updates never refresh it.

The binary stays on whatever version was installed first. Refreshing it by hand (download, swap, restart) cannot be scripted safely, and package or update managers want one command to call.

## What this does

`cua host update [--check] [--driver-bin <path>]`:

1. Reads the existing host config; errors (exit 3, "run `cua host setup`") if the computer was never set up.
2. Resolves the binary the same way setup does (`driver::locate` + `driver::install_to`), or uses `--driver-bin`.
3. Compares the installed version (`cua-spacesd --version`) with the one to install. If equal, prints "up to date", exits 0 and does not touch the service.
4. Otherwise stages the new binary next to the old one, stops the service, renames it into place and starts the service again through the existing `ServiceManager`. Renames and deletes are retried for a few seconds (as `remove_dir_retrying` does) because Windows releases a stopped exe a moment late. If the new service does not start or is not running afterwards, the previous binary is put back and the service restarted. Every rollback step is checked: if the old binary cannot be put back, the error says where it is (`cua-spacesd-previous`) and that the service is stopped, and nothing claims it was restored.
5. Does not read or write the relay registration, machine token, policy, sharing flag or desktop/Spaces settings, and does not go through setup's preflight, so it works with both sharing options off.

Choices:

- A service that was not running before (stopped, paused, not installed) is left stopped: the binary is replaced but nothing is started.
- "Latest" is the cua-spacesd release this `cua` build pins, the same one `cua host setup` installs. If that release is not published and the download falls back to an older one, the staged binary's version is compared before anything is replaced.
- `--check` changes nothing: it downloads, stages and runs nothing except the installed binary (and a local `--driver-bin`). It exits 0 when current, 10 when an update is available (added to the documented exit codes). If a version cannot be determined (the installed binary does not report one, or the version to install is unknown without downloading), it fails with exit 1 and a message instead of guessing; a plain `cua host update` still installs in that case.
- Versions are read from `--version` tolerantly (`0.2.0+abc`, `0.2.0 (build 12)` both read as `0.2.0`).
- No auto-restart race: `systemctl stop` is an explicit stop, which `Restart=always` does not undo; launchd's stop is `bootout` (unloads the job, so `KeepAlive` no longer applies); the Windows and process runners kill the process and have no supervisor.
- `--json` prints `{"status": "current|available|updated", "installed", "latest", "restarted"}`.

## Tests

New unit tests in `cua-host` (`update_tests.rs`) use shell-script fake drivers and `FakeServiceManager`: not set up, already current, `--check` leaves binary/config/service untouched, running service stopped/swapped/started, stopped service stays stopped, both sharing options off works and settings are unchanged, failed start restores the old binary, service down after start rolls back, `stop()` failure changes nothing, a blocked move-aside restarts the old binary, a failed restore reports where the old binary is, stale leftovers from a crashed run, build-metadata versions, an unreadable installed version, missing `--driver-bin`; plus a version-parse test. In `cua-cli`: exit codes (3, 10, 0) with JSON output, and the plain-text messages. The Unix-only tests are gated with `cfg(unix)`; I could not run Windows or macOS.

Also updated: telemetry command vocabulary (`host.update`), the CLI reference pages and the exit-code table.

`scripts/docs-generators/cli-specs/cua.json` was not regenerated here (no npm in my environment), please regenerate or I'll push it.

Checked locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-host -p cua-cli -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-host -p cua-cli --lib`.

Refs: similar ask for the driver in #2270 (`cua-driver self-update`).
