title: [Bug]: `cua sb create --view` on a local Lume sandbox opens a viewer link that is not a secure context
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

`cua sb create --view` on a local Lume macOS sandbox opens the cua-spacesd viewer at the VM's NAT address over plain HTTP, the same link that made `cua sb view` fail in #5734. That page is not a secure context, so it has no WebCodecs and should fail with "no acceptable codec".

### Reproduction

1. On a macOS host with Lume, create a macOS sandbox with the viewer: `cua sb create macos --name view-test --view`.
2. When the sandbox is ready, `cua` prints `Viewer: http://192.168.64.N:3211/viewer/#ticket=…` and opens it in the browser.
3. Look at the viewer page.

### Expected behavior

The viewer streams the desktop, as `cua sb view` does after the #5734 fix: a `127.0.0.1` link, which is a secure context.

### Actual behavior

Not reproduced end to end; found by reading the code while fixing #5734. `create` (`libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/sandbox.rs`, the `if a.view` block at the end of `create`) prints and opens `viewer_link(…).url` as minted, and then returns. For a Lume VM that is the NAT address over HTTP. `cua sb view` opened exactly this kind of link before the #5734 fix, and there the page had `isSecureContext === false` and `typeof VideoDecoder === "undefined"`, and showed `no acceptable codec: the target offers none of the requested codecs`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua` CLI 0.7.0, and `fix/cua-cli-sb-view-loopback` at the time of filing
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27 on Apple silicon
Application/browser/window system/image: Lume, `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26` with cua-spacesd 0.7.0

### Evidence

The before/after evidence for `cua sb view` is in #5734 and its pull request. This path uses the same `viewer_link` call.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: run `cua sb view NAME` after `create` finishes. With the #5734 fix it serves the link through a loopback proxy.

Why this was left out of the #5734 fix: `cua sb view`, the MCP `sandbox_view` tool and `cua skills record --sandbox` each keep running while the link is in use, so each holds the proxy. `create --view` returns as soon as the browser opens, so nothing keeps the proxy alive. It needs a decision on one of:
- wait until Ctrl-C after opening, as `cua sb view` now does (a behaviour change for `create`);
- hand the forward to the daemon so it outlives the command; or
- print a hint to run `cua sb view` instead of opening the NAT link.

The SDK's `Sandbox::viewer_url()` also returns the raw NAT link for a Lume VM; callers of the SDK have to proxy it themselves.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(platform-windows): route overlay-style windows through MSAA and honor desktop-scope foreground drag
body:
Fixes #5783 (partial)

## What this does

### 1. Stop daemon crashes on overlay-style windows
`get_window_state` on a Win32 window with `WS_EX_LAYERED | WS_EX_NOACTIVATE | WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW` (typical Wails / Tauri floating ball) currently calls `ElementFromHandle` + `BuildUpdatedCache(TreeScope_Subtree)` through the regular UIA path. On Windows 10 19041 against a Go/Wails app using a native HTCAPTION-only layered window, that deterministically crashes `uiautomationcore.dll` (`0xC0000005`), which takes the whole `cua-driver serve` daemon down — the CLI then sees `daemon closed connection without response`.

The fix: detect this exact style combination (layered + noactivate + toolwindow) in `walk_tree_unsafe` and route those windows through the existing MSAA walker (`walk_msaa_tree_budgeted`), the same escape hatch already used for SAL/VCL windows. MSAA does not enter the crashing `BuildUpdatedCache` path. A tree with zero actionable rows is expected here — the caller should treat the surface as pixel-only, which is exactly what an overlay widget is.

### 2. Make `scope=desktop` + `delivery_mode=foreground` actually use SendInput with activation
The desktop-scope drag path (used for screen-absolute coordinate drags from `get_desktop_state`) currently calls `send_drag_synthesized` unconditionally — the *non-activating* variant, even when the caller explicitly asks for `delivery_mode:"foreground"`. For HTCAPTION-style moves, the non-activating z-order-only raise + SendInput cannot drive the OS interactive move loop on every target (we observed the ball window staying put while `drag` returned `effect:unverifiable` with exit 0).

The fix: when `input.delivery_mode == Some(DeliveryMode::Foreground)`, route through `send_drag_synthesized_active` instead. That path already does `force_foreground_assisted(target)` + hit-tests the start point + refuses with `foreground_unavailable` if activation fails, which is the honest escalation contract callers expect. `delivery_mode:"background"` on desktop scope keeps the previous `send_drag_synthesized` behavior unchanged.

## Testing
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib` — 93/93 pass locally (macOS dev host, Windows-target crate compiled with `--target` via the workspace's existing config; the same tests that upstream CI runs on `windows-latest`).

## Not covered here (follow-up)
- Issue #5783 part (3): desktop-scope `drag` still reports `effect: unverifiable` because there is no readback to prove the window moved. A complete fix would add a frame-readback after the drag (comparing `GetWindowRect` before/after when the drag started on an `HTCAPTION`-classified region) so the tool can emit `confirmed` instead of `unverifiable`. That requires plumbing a pre/post window rect through `send_drag_synthesized_active` and is deliberately left for a follow-up so this PR stays narrow and reviewable.
- The app-side root cause we saw (native `SetWindowPos` also no-op'ing on the same ball from an Administrator Session 1 process) may be a secondary bug in our app's window setup, not in Cua Driver — we're investigating separately and will file against `wails-demo1` if confirmed.

title: chore(deps): bump filelock from 3.29.4 to 4.2.1
body:
Bumps [filelock](https://github.com/tox-dev/py-filelock) from 3.29.4 to 4.2.1.
Release notes

Sourced from filelock's releases.

4.2.1

  • On a singleton wrapper, close> and close> end only the holds that tasks acquired through that wrapper. A reader that arrives during close() gets the closed error instead of joining the ending hold. After synchronous code closes or force-releases the shared lock, the wrappers refuse to admit readers into the ended hold, and close() on such a wrapper returns. Closing one wrapper no longer ends a task's nested hold taken through another wrapper on the same path. #832
  • ReadWriteLock locks again after a release() that an exception from a signal handler interrupted. The async read-write wrappers stop admitting readers into such a level. The async read-write locks forget a hold whose backend release failed after the backend let go, and they free the memory of each acquire that times out or is canceled. AsyncFileLock returns from release() after a few hundred acquires gave up behind a waiting one. An exception from a signal handler delivered while an AsyncFileLock call joins its queue no longer blocks every later call on that lock. #833
  • Fix ReadWriteLock acting on -journal, -wal or -shm files another process puts beside its database: a write could land in another file, a reader could get in beside a writer, and an acquire could fail. SQLite now opens the database by name only in a directory no other account can write, and through a private hard link elsewhere. On Windows the directory's access control list decides. Where hard links are unavailable, keep the database in a directory other accounts cannot write, such as one under %LOCALAPPDATA%. The lock removes link directories through a checked descriptor rather than by name, reads a link directory's name only when the locking account owns it, and leaves alone a directory with other content renamed onto a link directory's name. A database whose schema takes more than a few kilobytes to load raises ValueError instead of running past the acquire timeout. #834
  • Fix five bugs in opening the lock file. UnixFileLock no longer truncates a file it did not create, such as one renamed to the lock path, and no longer applies mode to it. An on_acquired hook that writes holder metadata now truncates the file itself. A lease (Linux) or an oplock (Windows) on the lock file or a soft lock's marker no longer holds acquire() past its timeout or blocking=False, and an oplock no longer holds release(); ReadWriteLock on Windows waits for its timeout and raises Timeout. On Windows, a mode without group and other bits, such as 0o600, now creates the lock file with an owner-only permission list; the ReadWriteLock database gets the same. The soft locks' writability check no longer follows a symlink swapped in at the lock path. On a filesystem without flock, a contender from another account now waits on a marker it cannot write instead of raising PermissionError. #835
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing a live holder's marker in three cases: the holder and the contender run in Linux time namespaces with different boottime offsets; only one of them can read the boot id; a process other than the owner rewrote the marker. Soft markers no longer carry group or other write bits. A process name containing a carriage return or another line separator no longer makes the stale check raise ValueError. When /proc/self/ns/time exists but cannot be read, the stale check no longer compares start times and keeps the marker. #836
  • The async read-write locks record their hold under a task owner, so synchronous code on the executor thread that took the hold can no longer re-enter or release it. AsyncSoftReadWriteLock gives back one level on release, so synchronous readers of a shared singleton keep theirs. SoftReadWriteLock tracks read levels per thread: release() from a thread that holds none raises RuntimeError. After its heartbeat recorded a lost hold, it refuses new acquires until that hold is released. #838
  • StrictSoftFileLock creates <path>.filelock and its claims directory with the lock's mode and sets the sticky bit (a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it) on both. On the next acquisition it narrows a directory it owns that an earlier release created wider; it leaves a directory of another account as it is, so remove such leftovers by hand. It reaches claims through a descriptor opened without following symlinks; on Windows it holds both directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). Under a sticky parent such as /tmp it refuses a coordination directory of another account, as SoftReadWriteLock does for <path>.rw. One read grace now covers a whole claim scan, a failed claim cleanup no longer leaves the sentinel descriptor open, and a non-regular node at a sentinel private-record name raises SoftFileLockProtocolError. On Windows, contenders read claims without blocking their owner's unlink. #839

... (truncated)

title: [Bug]: Linux Space freezes and drops off the relay when its Cua Volume host daemon goes away (FUSE /volume blocks forever)
body:
### Primary area

Containers or images

### Summary

When the host `cua daemon` that serves a Linux Space's Cua Volume goes away, the guest's FUSE mount at `/volume` blocks forever instead of failing. Anything that touches it hangs, including the guest `cua-spacesd`. The Space then stops answering on 3211 and drops off the relay, while `cua sb ls` on the host still reports it `ready`.

### Reproduction

Seen on two host-provided gVisor Spaces, both at once. It happened after two `cua daemon` processes had been running on the host (see #5796); I don't have a deterministic trigger.

1. Create two Linux Spaces on a macOS host that provides Spaces (`ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`, container/gVisor).
2. Let the daemon that mounted their Cua Volume end while the guests still hold the mount. Here two daemons alternated on the mounts: "Cua Volume mounted again" from both, then "the guest detached the volume".
3. In the guest, `stat /volume`, or read `/proc/self/mountinfo`.

### Expected behavior

FUSE operations on `/volume` fail quickly (for example `ENOTCONN`/`EIO`) while the backend is unavailable, and `cua-spacesd` stays responsive, so the Space stays on the relay and the daemon can re-attach the volume.

### Actual behavior

- The guest `cua-spacesd volume-helper` log: `volume-helper: /volume: backend: the volume's host is not connected`.
- `stat /volume` inside the guest never returns, and `timeout 3 stat /volume` can't kill it; `docker exec` itself timed out.
- `/opt/cua/bin/start-token-sync.sh`'s `awk ... /proc/self/mountinfo` spun at 85–90% CPU for 29+ minutes in both guests.
- `cua-spacesd` stopped answering HTTP/2 on 3211 even from inside the container (`curl --http2-prior-knowledge http://127.0.0.1:3211/` timed out).
- The guest's relay websocket stayed ESTABLISHED but carried 0 bytes in either direction for 60 s+. The relay showed the Space `phase: offline`, and `space_bash` returned `machine "space-…" is not connected`.
- The host daemon logged `re-attach failed error=Cua Volume not mounted: transport error: http2 error (operation timed out)`, repeated.
- `start_space` through the relay failed with `does not support relay_attach: this Space's image runs no cua-spacesd`, apparently because the handshake timed out. The sandbox state still says `spacesd: true`.

### Environment

- Cua Spaces app 0.13.1 (0.13.1.96), `cua` CLI/daemon 0.7.0, host `cua-spacesd` 0.7.0 (app-helper runner)
- Guest image `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04` (`sha256:600f590eef65…`), guest `cua-spacesd` 0.5.3
- macOS 26.6.2 arm64 (Mac mini); built-in Linux runtime: colima 0.10.3 / lima 2.2.0 (vz), Docker 29.5.2, default runtime runsc

### Evidence

Killing only the guest volume-helper unblocked everything:

```
# inside the guest; supervisord restarts the helper
kill -9 <pid of /usr/local/bin/cua-spacesd volume-helper>
```

Right after that, the stuck `awk` exited and `cua-spacesd` answered on 3211 in 6 ms (it had been timing out). The Space came back `phase: ready` on the relay by itself, with no re-attach. In the second Space, the killed helper stayed a zombie that supervisord didn't reap, and the mountinfo `awk` kept spinning. Only a relay `stop_space` + `start_space` recovered that one.

### Workaround and additional context

- Workaround: a host-side watchdog probes each guest's 3211; if it hangs, it kills the guest volume-helper, and then falls back to relay `stop_space`/`start_space`.
- The Cua Spaces app's settings have `experiments.cuaVolume: false`, yet the daemon still mounts the Cua Volume into every Space (`/volume` or `/home/cua/Cua Volume`). Turning that off would remove this coupling for users who don't use the volume.
- Related: #4950 (an orphan daemon surviving a replacement).

title: [Bug]: Concurrent cua daemons still happen on 0.7.0; an orphan keeps managing Spaces after another daemon takes over (follow-up to #4950)
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

On 0.7.0 / app 0.13.1, several `cua daemon` processes still end up running at once, and one stays alive untracked after another daemon has taken over `~/.cua/cua.sock` and `daemon.json`. This looks like #4950 is not fully fixed. The orphan kept running its own Cua Volume and re-attach loops for the same local Spaces.

### Reproduction

Intermittent. Seen on one host over about 5 hours on 2026-10-23, after the app updated itself to 0.13.1. A partial trigger:

1. Run the Cua Spaces app with its daemon.
2. Stall the daemon: `kill -STOP <daemon pid>`.
3. The app launches `cua daemon start` processes (parent `CuaSpacesMac`) about 17 s and 60 s later.
4. `kill -CONT <daemon pid>`.

In my 60-second test, the extra launchers exited after the daemon resumed ("already running"), so this doesn't reliably leave an orphan. In the incident, the stalls were presumably longer: the daemon was blocked on hung guests, see #5795.

### Expected behavior

At most one `cua daemon` runs. A daemon that is replaced exits for certain (the replacing side checks the process actually exited), and the app doesn't launch new daemons while an existing one is merely slow.

### Actual behavior

- `ps` showed two `cua daemon start --foreground --loopback 127.0.0.1:0` processes with parent 1 (started 21:07 and 22:57 UTC). `daemon.json` and `cua.sock` belonged to the newer one; the older one had no clients but still held its own relay/mesh connection, NFS listeners and a connection to a guest's forwarded 3211.
- `daemon.log` showed daemons ending each other:

```
20:13:29 WARN keyvault: ended an old cua daemon that still held the socket pid=78461
23:06:54 WARN keyvault: ended an old cua daemon that still held the socket pid=2326
23:06:54 WARN keyvault: socket not served error=invalid: another Keyvault is already listening at ~/.cua/keyvault.sock
23:07:04 WARN keyvault: ended an old cua daemon that still held the socket pid=31249
23:07:04 WARN keyvault: ended an old cua daemon that still held the socket pid=42222
```

- In the same seconds, the Spaces' volumes flapped: `Cua Volume mounted again`, `re-attach failed ... the guest detached the volume`, `... http2 error (operation timed out)`. Both Spaces then went relay-offline.
- `kill -TERM` and `kill -KILL` of a single, sole daemon both recovered cleanly: the app started a new one within about 3 s, and it remounted the volumes. The failure needs two concurrent daemons.

### Environment

- Cua Spaces app 0.13.1 (0.13.1.96, Sparkle stable), `cua` 0.7.0, host `cua-spacesd` 0.7.0 as the app's service helper
- macOS 26.6.2 arm64
- Other `cua mcp` clients on the host: two Codex sessions. One ran a pre-update `cua` binary from the Sparkle cache, still running since before the update.

### Evidence

Process tree and log lines above. With a 1-second process watcher, the launchers during the stall test were:

```
23:59:12Z kill -STOP <daemon>
23:59:29Z cua daemon start  (parent CuaSpacesMac)   # +17 s
00:00:12Z cua daemon start  (parent CuaSpacesMac)   # +60 s
```

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: a host watchdog that `TERM`s any `cua daemon start --foreground` process that isn't the one named in `~/.cua/daemon.json` (seen on two runs a minute apart). Related: #4950.

title: [Bug]: `cua sb restart` on a gVisor container Space leaves the daemon on the old host port
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

`cua sb restart local:<space>` on a gVisor container Space restarts the container on a new Docker-assigned host port. The daemon keeps using the old port, so it can't reach the guest's `cua-spacesd` afterwards: re-attach fails with "Connection refused", and the volume and relay never re-attach.

### Reproduction

1. Have a local Linux container Space (`ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`, runtime gvisor). Its sandbox state has `"api_port": 32768, "exposed_ports": {"3211": 32768}`.
2. `cua sb restart local:<space>` prints "Sandbox 'local:<space>' is restarting."
3. `docker port <space>` in the runtime VM now shows `3211/tcp -> 127.0.0.1:32770`.

### Expected behavior

After a restart, the daemon reaches the guest at its current port (or the restart keeps the same host port), and it re-attaches the volume and relay as it does after `start`.

### Actual behavior

- `~/.cua/sandboxes/<space>.json` still says `api_port: 32768`; the container listens on 32770.
- `daemon.log`: `re-attach failed error=Cua Volume not mounted: transport error: tcp connect error (Connection refused (os error 61)) retry_in=60s`, repeated every 60 s.
- The Space stayed relay-offline.

### Environment

- `cua` 0.7.0, Cua Spaces app 0.13.1, macOS 26.6.2 arm64
- Built-in Linux runtime (colima 0.10.3 / lima 2.2.0, Docker 29.5.2, runsc); guest `cua-spacesd` 0.5.3

### Evidence

Commands and log lines above. After that, a relay `stop_space` + `start_space` of the same Space (container now on 32771) worked: the volume mounted and `space_bash` succeeded. So the start path does pick up the new port, while restart doesn't.

### Workaround and additional context

Use `stop_space` + `start_space` (or `cua spaces stop`/`start`) instead of `cua sb restart` for container Spaces.

title: cua sandbox launch --local fails on ARM64 hosts: runtime resolves ubuntu:24.04 to trycua/cua-xfce:latest, which publishes no arm64 build
body:
**What happened**

On an ARM64 host, `cua sandbox launch --local ubuntu:24.04` fails before any container is created. The cua-sandbox local Docker runtime resolves `ubuntu:24.04` to `trycua/cua-xfce:latest`, and Docker refuses the image because `trycua/cua-xfce:latest` publishes no linux/arm64 build.

**Environment**

- Host: Lenovo Yoga, Windows 11 on ARM64 (NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X)
- WSL2: Ubuntu 24.04, aarch64
- Docker Engine 29.9.1 (linux/arm64, native in WSL2)
- Python 3.12.3 venv
- cua 0.7.0, cua-cli 0.1.15, cua-sandbox 0.1.28, cua-computer 0.5.19

**Reproduction**

```
cua sandbox launch --local ubuntu:24.04 --name gen2-settle
```

Result (exit code 1):

```
RuntimeError("docker run failed: Unable to find image 'trycua/cua-xfce:latest' locally
docker: Error response from daemon: no matching manifest for linux/arm64/v8 in the manifest list entries: no match for platform in manifest: not found
...")
```

(raised from cua_sandbox/runtime/docker.py)

**Registry evidence**

`trycua/cua-xfce:latest` publishes no arm64 build: its manifest index contains linux/amd64 (sha256:0ac954ee…) plus an unknown/unknown attestation entry only. By contrast, `trycua/cua-ubuntu:latest` and `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04` both publish linux/arm64, and arm64 containers run fine on this host (the ghcr.io image was pulled and verified: linux/arm64, 4,395,581,727 bytes, digest sha256:d0f845852b717aca5f3692fbe244e724500847f22400f2f672c505623ed542bf).

**Related**

- #3254 (closed) covers an Apple Silicon failure with a different image in the path.
- #353 concerns cua-ubuntu arm64; that image has since gained an arm64 build.

title: fix(cua-driver-testkit): collapse daemon-proxy spawn and test the macOS proxy path
body:
Problem: the macOS daemon proxy duplicated the socket probe and diagnostic of the generic daemon-proxy spawn.

Before: two spawn paths each probed the socket and printed their own message.
After: spawn_macos_daemon_proxy_named delegates to spawn_daemon_proxy_named, which probes once and prints the platform-specific hint inline.

Tests: macOS-only tests run the real spawn_macos_daemon_proxy_named in a child process against a missing socket (asserts the install/permissions hint) and a listening socket (asserts exactly one probe). The scoped repository checks pass on macOS, including the macOS proxy tests.

## Fix rounds

- Qualified the macOS proxy child test filter and assert exactly one child test runs.
- Merged main; retitled to fix(...) because the testkit crate is release-tracked.

title: fix(cua-driver): match flatpak apps on the a11y bus and click elements in native Wayland windows
body:
Two Linux fixes found while driving a GNOME 50 Wayland desktop (Ubuntu 26.04) with cua-driver 0.38.0.

**1. Flatpak apps resolve to an empty, degraded window**

Sandboxed flatpak apps reach the AT-SPI bus through their instance's `xdg-dbus-proxy`, so `GetConnectionUnixProcessID` returns the proxy's pid, not the app's. `pid_of` then never matches the window's pid and `get_window_state` falls back to window metadata only ("AT-SPI was unavailable…").

`pid_of` now maps an `xdg-dbus-proxy` pid to the sandboxed app: read `instance-id` from `/proc/<proxy>/root/.flatpak-info`, the inner bwrap pid from `/run/user/<uid>/.flatpak/<instance>/bwrapinfo.json` (`child-pid`), and take that process's first child. Non-proxy pids are unchanged.

Result with flatpak Telegram (`org.telegram.desktop`): 1 degraded element → 350–424 elements.

**2. Element clicks fail on native Wayland toplevels**

With Wayland input enabled, an element click on a native Wayland window (no X11 xid) went down the X11 routes and failed. It now uses the same portal pointer path as coordinate clicks (`with_target_foreground` + `click_focused`) at the element's screen centre. Background delivery isn't possible there, so it returns an explicit error asking for `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.

Verified: click on Telegram's Search field by element, typed text appeared, Escape cleared it.

`cargo check -p platform-linux` passes on current main.

title: fix(cua-driver): skip PATH append when the shell rc already covers the bin dir
body:
Fixes #5694

The installer appends its PATH block on every run. `curl ... | bash` never sources `.zshrc`, so the process `$PATH` never shows `~/.local/bin` even though the user's shell exports it, and each install or upgrade added another copy (the reporter counted 20). Each block also prepends the dir, so the newest copy wins over anything appended after the first one.

Before appending, the installer now greps the resolved rc file (comment lines excluded) for the bin dir. To catch hand-written spellings it matches on the `$HOME`-stripped suffix, so `$HOME/.local/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, and the absolute path all count as coverage. When coverage is found the append is skipped and the follow-on `print_path_hint` warning is suppressed. `--no-modify-path` and the fish/nu hint path are unchanged.

## Tests

- `pytest libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_install_path_update.py -v` (new): 8 pass. The PATH-append block is extracted verbatim from `_install-rust.sh` and run under `/bin/bash` with `set -euo pipefail` against a stub HOME. Cases: reruns append once, existing exports (absolute, `$HOME`-relative, tilde) prevent append, a commented-out export does not, `--no-modify-path` still disables, `.bashrc` selection, and a rerun with a different `--bin-dir` still appends.
- `pytest libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests`: 346 passed, 24 skipped (PowerShell-gated; this host is macOS).
- Manual: ran the extracted block twice against a stub `.zshrc` → 1 marker line (was 2).

Not run: Windows PS1 regression lanes (no PowerShell on this host) and the installer-compat download matrix (its `--no-modify-path` runs do not exercise this block).

title: Windows: run_steps refused with "no reviewed risk classification" - blocks batching for out-of-process integrators (0.28.2)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, the `run_steps` tool is refused with **"Permission denied: tool 'run_steps' has no reviewed risk classification"**, which blocks the one structural fix available to CLI integrators for per-call process overhead.

## Environment

- `cua-driver 0.28.2 (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)`, Windows 11 (10.0.26300)
- Daemon running (`\.\pipe\cua-driver`), permission mode `standard (built_in_default)`
- Calling through the one-shot CLI (`cua-driver call <tool>` with JSON on stdin), from a Node.js integrator

## Reproduction

```console
$ echo '{"steps":[]}' | cua-driver call run_steps
Permission denied: tool 'run_steps' has no reviewed risk classification
```

## Why it matters (measured)

Every tool call from an out-of-process integrator pays the CLI process start even with the daemon up:

- `cua-driver call get_screen_size` with the daemon running: **~270 ms** per call (median of 3: 266/276/287 ms)
- ~790 ms per call measured earlier without the daemon

One agent step for us is roughly 5 driver calls (integrity check, two accessibility walks for two-frame stability, `verify_state`, the action itself, plus cursor moves) — so **1.4–1.7 s of every step is process startup, not work**. `run_steps` is exactly the batching escape hatch for this pattern.

## Ask

Either:

1. give `run_steps` a reviewed risk classification, or
2. document how a local integrator can pre-approve the tool for its own machine (a permissions/config stanza we set once, similar to the existing user-policy surface), or
3. if batching is intentionally gated, point us at the supported alternative for multi-call steps from an out-of-process client (we looked at `cua-driver mcp` as a persistent stdio transport, which helps, but batching would still cut per-call dispatch further).

Not asking to weaken review for anything mutating-by-default — an explicit local opt-in we configure ourselves would be perfectly fine.

(Context: integrator is [jevdesk](https://github.com/malgaroshy-maker/jevdesk) (private), a Windows computer-use loop that drives the machine entirely through `call`.)

title: Windows: check_permissions reports High via `call` but Medium via `mcp` (same elevated shell, 0.28.2)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `check_permissions` reports a different integrity level depending on which surface answers it: the one-shot CLI (`cua-driver call`) reports **High (elevated)**, while the `cua-driver mcp` stdio server reports **Medium (non-elevated)** — probed back-to-back from the same (elevated) shell.

## Environment

- `cua-driver 0.28.2 (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)`, Windows 11 (10.0.26300)
- Shell: an elevated terminal (the `call` child inherits High integrity, rid 12288)
- Daemon running (`\.\pipe\cua-driver`)

## Reproduction

One-shot:

```console
$ echo '{}' | cua-driver call check_permissions
{
  "elevated": true,
  "integrity_level": "High",
  "integrity_level_rid": 12288,
  ...
}
```

MCP (spawn `cua-driver mcp`, complete the `initialize` handshake, then `tools/call check_permissions`):

```json
{"content":[{"text":"Process integrity level: Medium (RID 0x2000, non-elevated)...","type":"text"}],
 "structuredContent":{"elevated":false,"integrity_level":"Medium","integrity_level_rid":8192,...}}
```

## Impact

An integrator that gates actions on "am I elevated enough for UIPI?" (a reasonable policy on Windows, since target-window integrity is not readable) gets two different answers from the same installed driver in the same session. For us the practical effect: tool calls routed through the MCP server run (or at least report) non-elevated, so every action is conservatively refused over that transport even though the equivalent one-shot calls are elevated and succeed.

## Ask

Either make the MCP server context inherit the caller's elevation consistently with `call`, or document the difference and the intended way to run an elevated MCP session. (If the server deliberately drops privileges for safety, a note in the docs would let integrators decide knowingly.)

(Context: integrator is jevdesk, a Windows computer-use loop driving the machine through `call`/`mcp`; related batching question in #5897.)

title: fix(lume): keep a Linux VM's machine identifier so suspend can resume it
body:
## What

`lume suspend` never resumes a Linux VM. A saved state restores only into a VM with the machine identifier it was saved with, and Linux VMs get a new `VZGenericPlatformConfiguration` identifier on every run. So the next run's `restoreMachineState` fails with "invalid argument", `restoreOrBoot` boots the VM instead, and its memory is lost.

Each Linux VM now keeps one `VZGenericMachineIdentifier` in `machine-identifier` beside its disk. It's created on first use and reused on every run. A clone gets its own identifier, unless it keeps the source's saved state (`includeSavedState`), which is bound to the source's identifier.

## Reproduced and fixed

On an Apple M5 running macOS 27, with an Ubuntu 26.04 arm64 guest under `lume serve`, I ran run → `POST /lume/vms/<vm>/suspend` → run:
- **Before:** `ERROR: Could not restore the saved state; booting the VM instead … VZErrorDomain Code=12 "…failed to restore with error “invalid argument”"`, and the guest's `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` changed.
- **After:** `INFO: VM resumed from its saved state … ms=1278`, and the same `boot_id`.

## Tests

`tests/LinuxMachineIdentifierTests.swift` checks that the identifier is stable and valid, that an unreadable one is replaced, and that a clone gets its own unless it keeps the saved state. `swift test --no-parallel`: 246 tests pass.

## Two further ideas

We run a fork of Lume 0.5.3 that saves and restores VMs held by `lume run` processes (no `lume serve`). Two pieces of it might interest you; happy to send PRs if they fit:
- **Bind the saved state to the disk it was saved against.** Record the disk's size and mtime, plus a generation counter bumped at every start. A run then never restores memory onto a disk something else booted in the meantime (say an older Lume, or a manual `lume run` after a downgrade).
- **A signal that suspends a VM held by its own `lume run` process.** This works for VMs not started through `lume serve`.

title: Windows 0.38.0: element_tokens no longer valid across one-shot call processes - no supported walk-then-act path for out-of-process integrators
body:
## Summary

On Windows, cua-driver 0.38.0 changed the scope of element-token validity: a token returned by `get_window_state` in one `cua-driver call` process is stale to the next process, even with no other snapshot taken in between (`current_snapshots: []` in the refusal). On 0.28.2 the same walk-then-act sequence across two one-shot `call` processes works.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (10.0.26300), daemon running
- Reproduced on 0.38.0; the identical sequence works on 0.28.2 (both release dirs cached, symlink switched to compare)

## Reproduction

```console
$ echo '{"pid":X,"window_id":Y,"include_screenshot":false,"tree_format":"elements","max_elements":60,"max_depth":12}' | cua-driver call get_window_state
# -> snapshot_id s0000000d, element_token s0000000d:2

$ echo '{"pid":X,"window_id":Y,"element_token":"s0000000d:2","text":"X"}' | cua-driver call type_text
# isError: "That element_token comes from an older read. Read the window again for fresh tokens..."
# structuredContent.current_snapshots: []   <- nothing has superseded it; the cache is just gone
```

The only calls between the two were from separate OS processes. Inside one `cua-driver mcp` session the snapshot persists (a subsequent call's error can see `snapshot s00000001 has rows [0] to [39]`), so the cache is session/process-scoped now.

## Impact for out-of-process integrators

An integrator that drives the driver through the `call` CLI (one process per tool call) can no longer walk-then-act at all: every action token is stale on arrival. The alternatives each have a blocker today:

- `run_steps` batching — permission-blocked ("no reviewed risk classification", #5897)
- `cua-driver mcp` persistent session — reports Medium integrity where `call` reports High from the same elevated shell (#5899), so an elevation-gated integrator must refuse to act through it

Net: on 0.38.0 (Windows) there is currently no supported path for an out-of-process, elevation-gated integrator to perform a walk followed by an action. (Reads are fine — we adapted to `tree_format:"elements"` for the structured array and walks work well, including the new `since:` diff reads being very attractive.)

## Ask

One of:
1. restore cross-process token validity (or an opt-in daemon-scoped cache), or
2. document `run_steps` classification / a local pre-approval so batching becomes usable, or
3. fix the mcp context's integrity so a persistent session is a viable acting path.

(Context: integrator is jevdesk, pinned to 0.28.2 for now; related: #5897, #5899.)

title: feat(spaces): cua sync — make a folder in a Space match a folder here, sending only what changed
body:
CUA-2190

**What changes for users:** `cua sync ./my-repo builder:/src/my-repo` makes a folder in a Space hold what a folder on this computer holds now, and a second sync sends only what changed. It is also available as `cua spaces sync`, MCP `space_sync` and `Spaces.sync`. This is the step an agent needs before it builds or tests its worktree on another machine; today that means hand-rolled rsync or tarballs.

**How it works:**
- **Like git:** files `.gitignore` (and `.git/info/exclude`) leave out stay behind, and so does `.git`. `--no-gitignore`, `--include-git` and `--exclude PATTERN` change that.
- **The host side** hashes the folder (SHA-256), with a size/mtime cache under the cua home, so an unchanged file is not read again.
- **The Space side** keeps a manifest of what the last sync put there (`<dest>/.cua-sync.json`). New and changed files travel as one gzipped tar through the file service, are unpacked with the time of the sync, and are then deleted from `/tmp`.
- **Builds stay correct:** a changed file gets the time of the sync, so cargo, make and tsc rebuild exactly the changed files. An unchanged file keeps its time.
- **Deletes:** files the last sync put there and that are gone here are deleted (`--no-delete` keeps them). Nothing else in the destination is touched, such as a `target/` or `node_modules/`.
- Linux and macOS Spaces. A Windows Space is refused with a message for now.

**Verified:**
- Unit tests in `cua-spaces/src/sync.rs`:
  - the walk honours .gitignore (nested ones too), .git, `--include-git` and excludes;
  - the plan sends only changed and new files and deletes only synced files;
  - the hash cache, and the tar's contents.
- End to end, on a real build: `cua` was built from this branch and run in a Linux VM Space against a real cua-spacesd, on a 10,364-file checkout of this repository:
  1. First sync: all 10,364 files, 226 MiB over the wire, in 28.6 s.
  2. Sync again with nothing changed: 0 sent, in 0.4 s.
  3. One file edited and one deleted: 1 sent (7.4 KB over the wire) and 1 deleted, in 0.4 s. The edited file matches. The deleted file is gone. The destination's own `target/` is untouched, and the gitignored `target/` was not sent. The unchanged file kept its time, and the edited file has the time of the sync.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-spaces -p cua-spaces-contract -p cua-sdk -p cua-cli --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings` is clean. Regenerated: the contract manifest, bindings (including the Electron binding) and the CLI/SDK reference (a new "Sync a folder" page).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: perf(cua-driver): read each AX node in one batched round trip
body:
## Summary

The macOS tree walker reads every node attribute by attribute: AXRole, AXTitle, AXValue, AXPlaceholderValue, AXDescription, AXIdentifier, AXHelp, AXEnabled, AXPosition, AXSize, AXValueDescription, AXMinValue, AXMaxValue, AXSelected and AXChildren are each one Mach round trip that the target app answers on its main thread.

This reads them with one `AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues` call per node (new `ax/batch.rs`) and converts the reply with the same rules as the single-read helpers (`copy_string_attr`, `copy_stringish_attr`, `copy_bool_attr`, `copy_number_attr`, `element_screen_rect`, `copy_children`), so `tree_markdown` and `elements` are unchanged. Action names and `AXValue` settability stay separate reads.

- If an app refuses the batch, the node falls back to the single reads.
- If the app does not answer in time (`kAXErrorCannotComplete`), the node is treated as unreadable instead of waiting out the 2 s messaging timeout once per attribute.

Refs #1757. That draft batches the same attributes on a much older walker. This version is rebased onto the current walker (menu collapsing, control state, web-content marker, value-settable rows). If maintainers would rather land it through #1757, I'm happy to close this one.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1, about 1,400 WindowServer windows open. Daemon run as `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1 cua-driver serve --socket …`, driven by a stdio MCP client through `cua-driver mcp --socket …`. Walk phase from timing marks around `walk_tree_budgeted` in `get_window_state`, median of 15:

| window | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Calculator (36 indexed rows) | 117–145 ms | 56–61 ms |
| TextEdit document | 128–144 ms | 69–85 ms |

Those runs were under machine load (load average about 10). On an idle machine the walk went from 47–51 ms to 16–19 ms, combined with the window-lookup change in the companion PR.

## Validation

- Live A/B on the same windows: `tree_markdown`, `elements` (minus tokens) and the structured key set are byte-identical to main for Calculator and a TextEdit document.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 639 passed. One unrelated port-discovery test (`owned_discovery_prefers_profile_endpoint_over_inherited_listener`) failed once and passed on three reruns.
- `cargo fmt` passes. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets` adds no new warnings.

title: perf(cua-driver): look up one window by id instead of enumerating all
body:
## Summary

`get_window_state` and every background action resolve the target window several times per call: owner pre-flight, bounds, title, Space membership, capture identity and the keyboard-sibling count in `gather_background_facts`. Each lookup called `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` for every window in the session. On a busy Mac that is about 1,400 windows and 10–15 ms per enumeration. `window_on_current_space_by_id` also queried SkyLight for the Spaces of each of those windows, about 30 ms.

This PR:

- Adds `windows::describe_window(id)`, which describes one window with `CGWindowListCreateDescriptionFromArray`. A window below the normal level is checked against the `kCGWindowListExcludeDesktopElements` enumeration, so a lookup lists exactly what that enumeration lists. The desktop-element set (wallpaper, backstop, desktop icons, underbelly) does not follow one level rule, so it is not guessed.
- Switches `resolve_window_owner`, `window_bounds_by_id`, `window_space_view_by_id` / `window_on_current_space_by_id` (Spaces read for that one window), the capture identity check, the `window_title` / `app_name` lookup in `get_window_state`, and the focus-failure hint to it.
- Makes `gather_background_facts` describe only the AX-mapped sibling windows its keyboard-ambiguity count can match, lazily, instead of enumerating all windows.
- Makes `list_running_apps`, which only reads owner pids, enumerate without the per-window Space queries.

Refs #4534 and #4940. #4940 scopes the Space queries for pid listings; this PR covers lookups by window id.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1, about 1,400 windows. Embedded daemon plus a stdio MCP client, p50/p90 of 12 calls, two rounds:

| call | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| get_window_state, tree only (Calculator) | 129–134 / 141 ms | 67 / 72–76 ms |
| get_window_state, tree + screenshot (Calculator) | 183–188 ms | 79–83 ms |
| get_window_state, tree only (TextEdit) | 139–141 ms | 75–76 ms |
| get_window_state, tree + screenshot (TextEdit) | 242–244 ms | 130–133 ms |

Per-phase marks on Calculator: owner pre-flight 13.4 → 0.4 ms, title lookup 12.6 → 0.3 ms, Space lookup 16.4 → 0.2 ms, tree-only snapshot bounds 13.0 → 0.4 ms, background facts 26.9 → 13.9 ms. The table and these marks were measured before the sibling-row and app-list commits, so the branch head is faster still.

## Validation

- New ignored live test `windows::tests::single_window_lookups_match_the_enumerations`. For every window in the session (1,397 here, including 22 desktop elements), it checks that `describe_window`, `window_space_view_by_id` and `resolve_window_owner` match the enumerations they replace. Run with `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib single_window_lookups -- --ignored`. It passes.
- `get_window_state` output (tree, elements, key set) is identical to main for Calculator and TextEdit.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` passes (`exact_target` included). `cargo fmt` passes. `cargo clippy` adds no new warnings.

title: perf(cua-driver): identify apps without spawning ps or listing every process
body:
## Summary

- `apps::get_app_name_for_pid` spawned `ps -p <pid> -o comm=` on every call, and `get_window_state` called it twice per read through `chromium_browser_window`.
- `ElectronJs::is_electron` runs before every background click, `type_text`, scroll, hotkey and `set_value`. It listed every running app (about 35 ms with roughly 950 processes) to find the pid's name, then spawned `ps` for the executable path.

This PR:

- The `comm` column is the process's argv[0]. `process_command` reads it with `sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2)`, which the kernel answers for the user's own processes (every app the driver targets). It falls back to the setuid `ps` only when the kernel withholds the arguments.
- `get_window_state` asks once per read.
- `is_electron` checks the executable first. It lists the running apps only when the pid's own bundle name could lead to an Electron bundle. Both checks still run whenever either could be true, so the answer is unchanged.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1:

- `is_electron` over all 948 running pids: old and new agree on every pid (4 Electron). Total time drops from 33.8 s to 1.06 s, about 35 ms to 1.1 ms per call.
- `get_window_state` tree-only: the two `ps` spawns cost 7.7–10.5 ms per read, now 0.2 ms.
- AX click on Calculator: the key-window prime step falls by the `is_electron` cost.

## Validation

- New unit tests: `procargs2_argv0_skips_the_executable_path_and_padding` (parser) and `app_name_matches_ps_for_this_process` (`ps` and the new path agree for the test process).
- A one-off equivalence test (not committed) compared old and new `is_electron` on every running pid.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` passes. `cargo fmt` passes. `cargo clippy` adds no new warnings.

title: fix(cua-driver): start the macOS LaunchAgent instead of a second daemon
body: ## Summary - Problem this solves: on macOS, `cua-driver mcp` opens the app with a bare `serve` whenever the socket is down, even when the LaunchAgent from the operate guide manages the daemon (#4634). An MCP client that starts while the agent is unloaded or restarting gets a daemon in `standard` mode, and the agent then exits "already running" on every `KeepAlive` respawn. A second report on the issue counted 5,966 of those respawns in 21 hours. Linux and Windows already start their managed service first. - What changed: - When the caller allows a managed restart and the socket is the default one, macOS now starts the installed LaunchAgent instead of opening the app. The label is `com.trycua.cua-driver`, or `com.trycua.cua-driver-local` for a local build: the labels the operate guide and `install-local.sh --autostart` use. - A loaded agent gets `launchctl kickstart`, without `-k`, so a daemon that is still starting is left alone. An agent whose plist is in `~/Library/LaunchAgents` but isn't loaded is left alone: the client fails with an error that names the `launchctl load ` command, so an agent the user unloaded stays off. - If the agent doesn't bring the socket up in time, the client reports a timeout that names the agent instead of opening a second daemon. - No plist, a failed `kickstart`, a non-default socket and `history enable` (which passes `allow_managed_restart: false`) keep the current `open` launch. A failed `kickstart` is not distinguished from a missing agent when choosing that fallback. What `cua-driver mcp` does on macOS when the socket is down. Before this PR every path went straight to "Open the app". ## Related work Fixes #4634 RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change): not required. No new command, flag or setting; macOS now takes the managed-service path Linux and Windows already take. ## Compatibility and risk - User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Machines without the LaunchAgent see no change. With it, the daemon an MCP client brings up is the agent's, with the agent's flags, instead of a `standard` one. While the agent is unloaded, a client fails with the `launchctl load` command instead of starting a daemon, so in the #4634 sequence (unload, client, load) the client fails during the reload window and the user's load brings the daemon up in the agent's mode. #2990 (open) registers its agent as `com.trycua.driver`; if it lands with that label, this lookup should follow it. - Risk and rollback: a client that used to get a `standard` daemon while the agent was unloaded now gets an error until the agent is loaded. If `kickstart` fails, it falls back to the existing bundle launch, which can still start a daemon without the agent's flags. After a successful kickstart, a missing socket returns a timeout instead. Revert the two commits to restore the previous launch path. ## Validation Candidate: `e2985564b`. The second commit takes the review's suggestion: an installed but unloaded agent is refused instead of bootstrapped. - Focused tests and checks (macOS 27.0, Apple silicon, Rust 1.97.1): - No new test. The behavior only shows when `cua-driver mcp` runs against a real LaunchAgent, which is a desktop run rather than plain `cargo test`, and faking launchctl would need a test-only injector in shipped code. The Linux and Windows managed-restart paths have no unit tests either. - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver`: 354 passed. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: clean. `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver` reports nothing in `cli.rs`; its warnings are in `platform-macos`. - On `a0a790dcf`, before the second commit: `cargo build --locked -p cua-driver`, then `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test --test status_pid_file_cli_test`: 2 passed with 1 ignored, and 1 passed. Not rerun. - Manual or platform evidence: macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon, the 0.33.3 release app installed as the operate guide's LaunchAgent with `--permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals`. The #4634 sequence, with this change's `cua-driver mcp` (built on current main) as the client: ```text 0.0 s status: running, pid 83652, permission mode: unrestricted (trusted_startup_configuration) 0.2 s launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.trycua.cua-driver 0.3 s status: not running 0.5 s one initialize request to this build's cua-driver mcp: exit 1, no reply cua-driver-rs: the com.trycua.cua-driver LaunchAgent is installed but not loaded; run `launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.trycua.cua-driver.plist` to start the daemon, then re-run `cua-driver mcp` 2.5 s status: not running; launchctl print: not loaded 2.7 s launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.trycua.cua-driver.plist: exit 0, no output 4.0 s status: running, pid 88575, permission mode: unrestricted (trusted_startup_configuration) ps: 88575, ppid 1, /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve --permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals ``` On main the same sequence ends with a `standard` daemon started by `open` and the agent exiting "already running" on every respawn, as in #4634. - Known gaps or CI still required: the loaded-agent `kickstart` path was not run live; with `KeepAlive`, launchd is usually already restarting a loaded agent's daemon. The new path has no unit test, for the reason above. Current fork workflows await maintainer approval. ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above. - [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained. - [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change. - [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included. - [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (Not applicable: this is a releasing `fix`.)

title: fix: implement persistent connection pooling for VzApi
body:
### Description

This PR implements a persistent connection pooling mechanism for . 

Previously, every call to the  control socket opened a new Unix domain socket, which caused significant overhead and risked socket exhaustion (EMFILE) when managing multiple VMs or high-frequency agent requests.

### Changes

- **Connection Pooling**: Introduced  to  to maintain a single, long-lived connection to the daemon.
- **Reduced Latency**: Eliminated the repeated socket handshake for every operation (, , , etc.).
- **Resource Efficiency**: Drastically reduced the number of open file descriptors required per agent session.

### Technical Impact

This change transforms the control plane from a naive request-response model to a persistent stream model, ensuring stability and performance for high-density agent runtimes.

title: [Bug]: Windows element tree drops mixed and expand/collapse state, and reports checked as selected
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Windows, `get_window_state` element entries cannot express three control states that UI Automation provides: an indeterminate (mixed) checkbox has no state at all, expand/collapse state is never reported, and a checkbox's checked state and a list item's selected state share one `selected` field, so a client cannot tell them apart.

### Reproduction

1. On Windows, open a WinForms window with a three-state `CheckBox` set to `Indeterminate`, a `TreeView` with one collapsed and one expanded node, and a `ListBox` with one selected item.
2. Call `get_window_state` for that window.
3. Compare the element entries for the checkbox, the two tree nodes and the list item.

### Expected behavior

- The indeterminate checkbox carries a value that says it is mixed.
- The collapsed and expanded tree nodes carry their expand/collapse state.
- A checkbox's checked state and a list item's selected state are distinguishable, for example separate `checked` (true/false/mixed) and `selected` fields.

### Actual behavior

From the source on `main` (`685f81c8753e`):

- `read_cached_selected` maps `ToggleState_On` → `Some(true)`, `ToggleState_Off` → `Some(false)`, and anything else, including `ToggleState_Indeterminate`, → `None`, so the mixed checkbox gets no `selected` field ([uia/mod.rs#L1029-L1050](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/685f81c8753e10617b231255e4ceb72df8181273/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs#L1029-L1050)).
- The same function falls back to `SelectionItemPattern.IsSelected`, so toggles and selection items both land in `UiaNode.selected` ([uia/mod.rs#L50-L62](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/685f81c8753e10617b231255e4ceb72df8181273/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs#L50-L62)), which is emitted as `selected` ([tools/impl_.rs#L1149-L1154](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/685f81c8753e10617b231255e4ceb72df8181273/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs#L1149-L1154)).
- `ExpandCollapsePattern` is cached and used to derive actions and to expand ([uia/mod.rs#L199-L203](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/685f81c8753e10617b231255e4ceb72df8181273/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs#L199-L203), [#L997](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/685f81c8753e10617b231255e4ceb72df8181273/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs#L997)), but `ExpandCollapseState` is never read or emitted.

I have not checked how macOS or Linux report these states.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: Cua Driver, `main` at `685f81c8753e`; the same code is in `cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0` (`uia/mod.rs` L1024-L1045).
Operating system and architecture: Windows 11 x64.
Application/browser/window system/image: any UIA provider with Toggle, SelectionItem and ExpandCollapse patterns (WinForms CheckBox / TreeView / ListBox shown above).

### Evidence

Source references above. A downstream project currently reads `TogglePattern.ToggleState` and `ExpandCollapsePattern.ExpandCollapseState` itself and joins them to the driver's elements to fill this gap.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: a client re-reads the UIA patterns for the same window and matches elements by role, label and bounds. That duplicates a tree walk and can only match uniquely identified elements.

A possible shape: keep `selected` for `SelectionItem.IsSelected`, add `checked` (`true` / `false` / `"mixed"`) from `TogglePattern`, and add `expanded` from `ExpandCollapseState` (`PartiallyExpanded` as expanded; omit for `LeafNode`). Glad to open a PR along those lines if that direction fits.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Cua Driver THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES omits Inter (OFL), two Wayland protocols and MPL-2.0 source pointers
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### Summary

`libs/cua-driver/rust/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists six MIT projects. Release binaries also contain material whose licenses require a notice in binary distributions, and that material is not listed.

### Reproduction

1. At `main` (`685f81c8`) or tag `cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0`, open `libs/cua-driver/rust/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
2. Compare it with what the release builds compile in:
   - `rust/crates/cursor-overlay/src/session_badge.rs:29` embeds the Inter font (OFL-1.1, text at `rust/crates/cursor-overlay/assets/Inter-OFL.txt`).
   - `rust/crates/platform-linux/protocol/virtual-keyboard-unstable-v1.xml:3` (MIT; Høgsberg, Intel, Collabora, Purism) generates bindings used by `src/wayland/virtual_keyboard.rs`.
   - `rust/crates/platform-linux/protocols/hyprland-toplevel-export-v1.xml` (BSD-3; line 13 requires the notice in binary distributions) generates bindings used by `src/wayland/hyprland_capture.rs`.
   - `uniffi`, `uniffi_core` and `uniffi_pipeline` 0.31.0 (all platforms) and `option-ext` 0.2.0 (Linux) are MPL-2.0. MPL §3.2 asks binary distributions to say where the covered source is.

### Expected behavior

The notice shipped in the release archives (copied as `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`) covers everything the binaries contain that requires attribution, including where the MPL-covered source can be obtained.

### Actual behavior

None of the items above appear in the notice. Separately, `Inter-OFL.txt` says "Copyright (c) 2020", while the embedded font's name table and rsms/inter's license say 2016.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: Cua Driver `cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0` (`2d2f99228d`); still present at `main` `685f81c8`
Operating system and architecture: all release targets
Application/browser/window system/image: n/a

### Evidence

Found by a license audit of the 0.37.0 workspace (`cargo metadata` and target-specific `cargo tree` over the release package/feature selection in `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml`, plus a source search for copied code and assets). `cargo deny check licenses` passes with version-specific MPL-2.0 exceptions, so this is a notice gap, not an incompatible license.

### Workaround and additional context

The Hyprland plugin, which is not in the core archives, also carries an Omarchy (MIT) credit in `hyprland-plugin/src/keymap_equivalence.hpp:3` and a prototype credit in `src/input_experiment.cpp:1` that names no license. We maintain a downstream fork (goat-si/cua-driver#3) and are happy to send a PR that extends the notice.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Cua Driver Node runtime is built without a lockfile
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### Summary

`libs/cua-driver/scripts/build-node-runtime.mjs` builds `cua_driver_node_runtime.node` from a temporary Cargo project that has no lockfile, and it runs `cargo build` without `--locked`. The released addon's Rust dependencies are therefore resolved from crates.io at build time and are not pinned by `rust/Cargo.lock`.

### Reproduction

1. At `main` (`685f81c8`), read `libs/cua-driver/scripts/build-node-runtime.mjs`. It copies uniffi-bindgen-react-native's runtime `core` and `napi` crates into a temporary project (around line 149) and runs `cargo` there (line 163).
2. Run `cargo metadata --locked` in that generated project. It fails because no `Cargo.lock` exists.

### Expected behavior

Release builds of the addon are reproducible and use reviewed dependency versions, like the rest of the workspace (`cargo build --locked`).

### Actual behavior

Two release builds from the same commit can link different crate versions if anything upstream publishes in between. License and source checks on `rust/Cargo.lock` do not cover the addon. One resolved crate, `uniffi-runtime-napi`, also has no `license` field in its Cargo metadata, although its source header says MPL-2.0.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: Cua Driver `cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0`; still present at `main` `685f81c8`
Operating system and architecture: all release targets
Application/browser/window system/image: n/a

### Evidence

Found during a license audit of the 0.37.0 release build. The `cargo metadata --locked` attempt in the generated project reported a missing lockfile.

### Workaround and additional context

Suggested fix: commit a lockfile for the runtime project (or vendor it into the workspace), then build with `--locked`. Tracked downstream as goat-si/cua-driver#4; we can send a PR.

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.

title: fix(cua-driver): run screencapture by absolute path and let hosts turn it off
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: when ScreenCaptureKit cannot capture a window, the macOS driver falls back to `screencapture -l <id> -x -o`, started by name through the inherited `PATH`. `/usr/sbin/screencapture` is entitled to record audio and macOS checks its privacy access against the host app, so in an embedded host it can raise a Microphone prompt attributed to the host and take focus during background control (#5938).
- What changed: `screencapture` now runs only from `/usr/sbin/screencapture`, for both the window fallback and the display capture. A host can set `CUA_DRIVER_DISABLE_SCREENCAPTURE=1` so the driver never starts the tool: a failed native window capture then returns the native error, and every whole-display capture (the agent desktop capture without a cursor overlay, recording before/after snapshots, picture-in-picture frames) goes through ScreenCaptureKit with nothing excluded, the same image `screencapture -x` takes. The embedded SDK passes the variable through its environment allowlist. An embedded driver (`--embedded`), and the SDK's private worker runtime (`__private-worker`, host-owned but launched without `--embedded`), keep `screencapture` off by default, since a host on an SDK whose allowlist predates the variable cannot pass it, and the tool's prompts and its temporary capture file (`${TMPDIR}/cua-driver-rs-capture-<pid>-<uuid>/window.png`, readable by the host's user) land under the host's identity; a host that wants the tool sets `CUA_DRIVER_DISABLE_SCREENCAPTURE=0`, which requires an SDK that allowlists the variable (this PR's; npm `@trycua/cua-driver` 0.37.0 rejects the name whatever its value). Standalone drivers keep it on by default. The in-process runtime (`RuntimeOptions`, the C ABI, the Node addon) is left as is: it runs inside the host app's own process, which can set the variable in its own environment with no allowlist in the way.

## Related work

Refs #5938

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): MCP schemas and the protocol are unchanged, but this does change a default: embedded and SDK-worker runtimes no longer start `screencapture` unless the host allows it. I treated that as part of the #5938 bug fix, since the tool raises unrelated privacy prompts and writes a temporary capture file under the host's identity. I'm happy to open an RFC first if maintainers want the default change reviewed that way.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Embedded hosts change default: when ScreenCaptureKit cannot capture a window, the `screencapture` shell fallback is refused (the in-memory SkyLight route may still succeed) unless the host sets `CUA_DRIVER_DISABLE_SCREENCAPTURE=0`. Standalone drivers that do not set the variable keep the same fallbacks, except that a different `screencapture` earlier on `PATH` is no longer used. With the variable set, a window ScreenCaptureKit cannot capture returns an error instead of a `screencapture` image; the off-Space SkyLight route is unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: small and local to `platform-macos/src/capture.rs` and the SDK allowlist; revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (macOS 27.2 arm64, from `libs/cua-driver/rust`):
  - `cargo fmt -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-sdk --check`: pass.
  - `cargo test -q -p platform-macos --lib`: 639 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored.
  - `TMPDIR=/tmp cargo test -q -p cua-driver-sdk --lib`: 109 passed, 0 failed.
  - `capture::tests::an_embedded_driver_keeps_screencapture_off_unless_the_host_allows_it` failed with the embedded default ignored and passes with it; `cargo test -q -p platform-macos --lib` at the new head: 640 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored.
  - `capture::tests::a_host_owned_runtime_gets_the_embedded_default` failed against a no-op marker and passes once the private worker's marker is set; at head `60f13a9642`: `cargo test -q -p platform-macos --lib` 641 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored; `cargo check -q -p cua-driver` passes.
  - New tests `capture::tests::screencapture_runs_only_from_its_absolute_path`, `capture::tests::a_host_can_turn_screencapture_off` and `embedded::tests::disable_screencapture_env_propagates`. With the previous behavior restored (relative `screencapture`, no allowlist entry) the absolute-path and allowlist tests fail.
- Manual or platform evidence: none yet for the TCC prompt itself; it is being verified live with a host app built from this change.
- Known gaps or CI still required: `cargo clippy -D warnings` on this toolchain reports 5 errors in files this change does not touch (`ax/reveal_scroll.rs`, `tools/click.rs`, `document_edit.rs`), reported in #5943. Repository CI still required.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

title: [Bug]: cargo clippy -D warnings fails on platform-macos (5 existing errors)
body:
### Primary area

cua-driver (Rust), macOS crate `platform-macos`

### Summary

`cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on `main` with five errors in existing code. CONTRIBUTING asks for `cargo clippy -D warnings` on the crates a change touches, so any contributor changing `platform-macos` hits these before their own change is checked. No CI workflow runs clippy for this crate, which is likely why they went unnoticed.

### Reproduction

1. Check out `main` (seen at 685f81c87) on macOS.
2. `cd libs/cua-driver/rust && rustup component add clippy` (toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml`, 1.97.1).
3. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

### Expected behavior

The command passes, or the crate's lint policy allows these patterns explicitly.

### Actual behavior

```
error: you seem to be trying to use `match` for destructuring a single pattern. Consider using `if let`
   --> crates/platform-macos/src/ax/reveal_scroll.rs:185:9
error: constant in pattern `kAXErrorFailure` should have an upper case name
   --> crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs:153:9
error: constant in pattern `kAXErrorAttributeUnsupported` should have an upper case name
   --> crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs:153:27
error: constant in pattern `kAXErrorActionUnsupported` should have an upper case name
   --> crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs:153:58
error: `AXValueCreate` redeclared with a different signature
   --> crates/platform-macos/src/document_edit.rs:65:5
```

The last one is `clashing_extern_declarations`: `document_edit.rs` declares `AXValueCreate(u32, *const c_void) -> *const c_void` while `ax/bindings.rs:127` declares `AXValueCreate(AXValueType, *const c_void) -> AXValueRef`. That one is worth a real fix (one declaration), not only a lint allow.

### Environment

macOS 27.2, Apple silicon, Rust 1.97.1 with clippy. The same five errors appear at `cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0`.

### Evidence

Command output above. Found while validating #5942.

### Workaround and additional context

Run clippy on the other crates only. Suggested fix: use `if let` in `reveal_scroll.rs`, compare the AX error constants by value or allow `non_upper_case_globals` for the Apple names, and have `document_edit.rs` use the binding from `ax/bindings.rs`.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11 window captures from get_window_state include the agent cursor overlay
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, the screenshot that `get_window_state` returns for a window can contain the Driver's own agent-cursor overlay (cursor and session pill) drawn over the controls the agent just acted on. The overlay is hidden only around desktop captures (#4194 / #4199), not around window captures.

### Reproduction

1. Linux X11 without a compositing manager (Xvfb 21.1, no WM compositor), cua-driver 0.37.0, agent cursor enabled (default).
2. Start an app with a button, then `click` that button by element token through `cua-driver mcp`.
3. Call `get_window_state` on the same window with a screenshot and look at the image around the clicked control.

### Expected behavior

An agent-facing window capture contains no Driver-owned overlay pixels, as #4194 established for desktop captures. When the platform cannot exclude them, the result says so (as `get_desktop_state` does with `agent_overlay_capture`) instead of silently including them.

### Actual behavior

The overlay is in the window image: on Xvfb it renders as a solid black cursor shape over the control that was just clicked, hiding it from the model. No field in the result reports that the overlay was included.

Source reading on `main` (685f81c875): the hide-and-restore excluder (`platform-linux/src/overlay_capture.rs`) is used only by desktop capture (`tools/impl_.rs:12797`) and `overlay.rs:3795`. The `get_window_state` capture path (`tools/impl_.rs:1387-1411`) calls `wayland::screenshot_dispatch_with_pid` (window drawable) or, when a popup overlaps, `capture::screenshot_root_region_png` (a root grab), neither wrapped in the excluder. Without compositing, a window-drawable `GetImage` returns what is on screen in that rectangle, overlay included; the root-region path includes it by construction.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver-rs 0.37.0 Linux x86_64 release binary; source checked against `main` at 685f81c875
Operating system and architecture: Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64
Application/browser/window system/image: Xvfb 21.1.12, no compositing manager; a small Tk fixture app

### Evidence

Window captures returned by `get_window_state` after a click (fixture app, no private data):
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goat-si/goat/d5d7849330085a5db6edb47077515a967de64acf/1220/linux-2-after-click.png
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goat-si/goat/d5d7849330085a5db6edb47077515a967de64acf/1220/linux-3-after-set-value.png

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: `set_agent_cursor_enabled false` for sessions whose window captures go to a model. Related: #4194 (desktop captures, closed by #4199), #1902 (a request to bake the cursor in on purpose, the opposite default). A fix could wrap the window-capture branches in the same `capture_excluding_overlays` and publish the same outcome field. We can send a PR. Downstream report: goat-si/goat#1221.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Linux get_window_state does not export checked/mixed or expanded element states
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux, `get_window_state` element rows do not say whether a checkbox is checked, mixed (indeterminate) or whether an expandable control is expanded. A checked checkbox is reported as `selected`, and `expanded` is read internally but never exported.

### Reproduction

1. Linux with AT-SPI (any GTK or Qt app with a checkbox, a tri-state checkbox and an expander or tree row).
2. Call `get_window_state` on its window.
3. Look at the element rows for those controls.

### Expected behavior

Rows carry the states AT-SPI exposes, as separate fields: `checked` (`true` / `false` / `"mixed"` from CHECKED and INDETERMINATE, on CHECKABLE controls) and `expanded` (from EXPANDED, only when EXPANDABLE). An absent field means the platform did not say, never false.

### Actual behavior

Rows have only `enabled` and `selected` (`platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs:733-737` on `main` at 685f81c875). For roles containing "check", `selected` is the CHECKED state (`atspi/native.rs:1637-1638`), so a checked box and a selected list item look the same, and INDETERMINATE is lost. `expanded` is computed (`atspi/native.rs:1632-1635`) and used only to decide menu descent. `AtspiNode.checked` exists but is not serialized.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver-rs 0.37.0 Linux x86_64 release binary; source checked against `main` at 685f81c875
Operating system and architecture: Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64
Application/browser/window system/image: GTK 3 and Tk apps over AT-SPI 2.52 (X11)

### Evidence

None available beyond the source references above. The rows simply lack the fields.

### Workaround and additional context

A client can read AT-SPI state sets itself, but it cannot map the Driver's element rows to AT-SPI object paths reliably (duplicate siblings), so it cannot fill these fields without guessing. A small change in `get_window_state` (export `checked` with mixed, and `expanded` when expandable) would cover it; we can send a PR. Downstream report: goat-si/goat#1261.

title: fix(cua-driver): report Windows toggle and expand/collapse state on elements
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, `get_window_state` elements cannot express three UI Automation states. An indeterminate checkbox has no state (`read_cached_selected` maps only On/Off), expand/collapse state is never read, and toggle state shares `selected` with `SelectionItem.IsSelected` (#5939).
- What changed: Windows elements now carry `toggle_state` (`"on"` / `"off"` / `"mixed"`) and `expanded` (bool) when UIA reports them, read from the already-cached TogglePattern and ExpandCollapsePattern (`ExpandCollapseExpandCollapseStateProperty` is added to the cache request; PartiallyExpanded counts as expanded, LeafNode reports nothing). Tree rows show the same states as `toggle=…` and `expanded=…` attributes, so an incremental read (`since`) reports a state-only change, such as ticking a checkbox, as a change. `selected` keeps its current meaning.

## Related work

Refs #5939

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change): none. This adds optional output fields to Windows `get_window_state` and two row attributes; nothing existing changes meaning. If you consider additive MCP output fields RFC-worthy, say so and I'll open one, or keep this as a draft until then.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. New optional structured fields and row attributes; existing fields, `selected` included, are unchanged. The typed contract (`WindowElement` in `cua-driver-contract`) does not list the new fields yet, so typed SDK results ignore them while raw/MCP output carries them; adding them to the contract plus regenerating the bindings is a natural follow-up I kept out to keep this PR to the Windows walk. `toggle_state` is a string so the contract can carry it as a `snake_case` enum.
- Risk and rollback: reads stay inside the existing cached walk (no new live COM calls). Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `get_window_state_actions_tests.rs` covers `toggle_state` for on/off/mixed, `expanded` for both values, both omitted when unknown, and a tree row that changes when only the toggle or expanded state changes.
- Manual or platform evidence: the same change, on top of `cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0`, passed `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib` on Windows 11 x64 (287 passed, 1 ignored) and the Windows/macOS/Linux release builds plus a 0.37.0 protocol-compatibility check in GOAT's fork of the driver (goat-si/cua-driver#6). On this `main` I applied it by hand (the import list differs) and ran `rustfmt`; I have not built this exact branch.
- Known gaps or CI still required: a build and test run of this branch on Windows (CI here); a live run against a three-state CheckBox and a TreeView.
