title: fix(cua-driver): get_screen_size reads the GNOME Wayland monitor layout from Mutter
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on a GNOME Wayland session without an X11 `DISPLAY`, `get_screen_size` fails ("`$DISPLAY` variable not set"). Consent scopes whole-desktop and unfiltered listing calls to that geometry (`cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs`), so `list_windows {app}` and similar calls are refused with "confirmation provider failed: display identity could not be read". An embedded host on native GNOME Wayland cannot list or act on any window.
- What changed: `get_screen_size` reads GNOME's monitor layout from `org.gnome.Mutter.DisplayConfig.GetCurrentState` when the driver runs on Wayland without `DISPLAY`. The answer is content-free (logical-monitor positions, scale, transform, current mode) and has the Hyprland path's shape: frame size, largest scale, and per-monitor `frame_x`/`frame_y`. Like Hyprland's IPC check, the unique D-Bus connection that owns the name must be the `SO_PEERCRED` peer of the `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` socket, and the layout is read from that unique connection, so a handover of the well-known name cannot substitute another process. An inherited `WAYLAND_SOCKET` is refused, and the socket connect is non-blocking and bounded on the calling thread. Any refusal keeps today's error.

## Related work

Refs #1922 (scope comment: https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/1922#issuecomment-6395031516)

RFC: not required in our reading. No public API, schema or permission changes; the tool returns data it could not return before on this platform.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: only GNOME Wayland without `DISPLAY`. There, `get_screen_size` now succeeds, and consent-scoped listing calls work. X11, Hyprland, and other compositors (KDE, other wlroots) are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: any failure (no Mutter, attestation mismatch, timeout, odd layout) falls through to the previous X11 read and its error. Reverting restores today's behavior.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib mutter_display` on this branch (`main` at 9f910eae0): 10 passed. They cover the frame math (layout mode, scale, rotation, offsets, unusable layouts), reading from the attested owner when the name moves, refusal of an inherited `WAYLAND_SOCKET`, a non-blocking connect that leaves nothing behind on a full backlog, a `WAYLAND_SOCKET` found in the start environment, and NUL paths refused.
- Manual or platform evidence: in an isolated headless GNOME 46 Wayland session without XWayland, `cua-driver mcp` → `get_screen_size` returned "Desktop frame: 1600x1000 points @ 1x … Meta-0 1600x1000 on, at (0,0)", matching `GetCurrentState`. 0.37.0 in the same session returned "`$DISPLAY` variable not set and no value was provided explicitly". (Measured on our fork build, which carries the identical commit.)
- Known gaps or CI still required: real seat GNOME and multi-monitor hardware not tested. Forged-owner attestation is covered by unit tests, not live (needs a second compositor). KDE is not covered.

**Known limits.** The check refuses a `WAYLAND_SOCKET` the process started with, read from `/proc/self/environ` because `wayland-client` unsets it on use. Once a connection has consumed the socket, every connection the driver opens later with `connect_to_env` (listing, capture, pointer sessions, virtual keyboard) goes to `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, the compositor this attests; connections it keeps open (the overlay, a held drag) stay where they were opened, which is why a socket the process started with is refused outright. Code running inside the process that sets `WAYLAND_SOCKET` after start, or rewrites the start environment (`PR_SET_MM_MAP`), is outside this check: such code could ask Mutter itself.

## Contributor and release checks

title: 0.28.2 Windows: no one-shot CLI path to the existing-profile browser grant - out-of-process integrators cannot attach a browser with per-user installs
body:
## Summary

On 0.28.2 (Windows), there appears to be no way for an out-of-process integrator using the one-shot `cua-driver call` surface to attach to a browser, even with the operator's explicit consent:

- `browser_prepare` with `strategy: {kind: "existing_profile"}` + `pid` + `window_id` refuses with `browser_consent_required`: "standard mode requires `--grant existing-profile` or an embedding authorization host".
- The `--grant existing-profile` flag does not exist on the `call` subcommand (tried before the tool name, after it, and globally — same refusal each time), and the tool's own description states "Ordinary MCP transport approval never proves profile authorization."
- Launching a fresh separate Edge with `--remote-debugging-port` and a throwaway `--user-data-dir` is recognized by `browser_prepare` as an owned endpoint (`already_prepared`, listener-pid ownership proven, zero side effects) — but `get_browser_state` (bind mode) still refuses it: `consumer_profile_endpoint_requires_grant`, "this standalone browser profile requires explicit existing-profile approval".
- `allow_launch: true` + `profile: {mode: "isolated_new"}` refuses with `browser_route_unavailable`: "no vendor-signed protected Chromium executable is available for isolated launch" (this machine has per-user Edge only).

Net: with a per-user browser install, an out-of-process integrator cannot reach the browser surface at all on 0.28.2, with or without operator consent.

## Ask

One of:
1. a documented CLI path for the operator to give the `existing_profile` grant to a one-shot integrator (e.g. a `cua-driver` subcommand that records the approval), or
2. let an externally-launched browser with an owned loopback endpoint (proven listener pid + fresh temp profile) count as attachable without the consumer-profile grant, or
3. document that browser attachment is embedding-host-only on 0.28.2, so integrators know to install a system-level Chromium (which then passes isolated launch attestation).

(Context: integrator is jevdesk; related: #5897, #5899, #5910. Happy to test any of the above on this machine — the repro is two shell commands.)

title: cua-driver-rs (Linux/X11): window screenshots return a stale frame while the screen is locked
body:
### Primary area

cua-driver-rs, platform-linux (X11 window capture)

### Summary

On X11, `get_window_state` (and other window captures) can return a stale picture of a window while the screen is locked or blanked. The driver reads the window's drawable as it is (`capture.rs` `capture_raw`: `GetGeometry` then `GetImage`, or the SHM equivalent). Under a compositing window manager the screensaver/lock stops painting, apps' frame clocks stop, and the drawable keeps its last frame. The driver returns that frame with no sign it is old.

### Reproduction

1. GNOME 46 X11 session (Mutter compositing), any GTK window whose content changes on a timer (e.g. a label counting up every 5 s).
2. Activate the screensaver: `gdbus call --session -d org.gnome.ScreenSaver -o /org/gnome/ScreenSaver -m org.gnome.ScreenSaver.SetActive true`.
3. Call `get_window_state` with `include_screenshot: true` on that window a few times, 10 s apart.
4. Compare the screenshot with the window's real state (e.g. its label over AT-SPI).

### Expected

A screenshot shows the window's current content, or the call says it cannot (for example an error such as "window is not being painted"). The tree part of the result is unaffected.

### Actual

Every screenshot shows the same old frame. In our run the label read "Count: 487" in all three screenshots while AT-SPI read 505, 507, 509 at the same moments. After unlocking, screenshots track the label again.

### Environment

- cua-driver-rs 0.37.0 (also main at 9f910eae0, same capture code).
- Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME Shell 46 on X11 (xrdp Xvnc session with one virtual monitor).
- Embedded host over MCP.

### Evidence

Readings from our run; no screenshots attached because they would show a real session.

### Workaround

The embedding host can capture the window itself from its Composite pixmap after asking for a redraw and checking Damage, and refuse when the app does not redraw. GOAT does that for its own captures (goat-si/goat#1677, goat-si/goat#1683).

A driver-side option would be to check freshness before returning an image: request a redraw (Expose) and wait for Damage covering the window, or detect an active screensaver/blanked output and refuse.

- [x] No personal data or sensitive screenshots are included.

title: cua-sandbox: Mouse.drag raises TypeError on QMPTransport (path= vs start_x/start_y/end_x/end_y)
body:
### Primary area

SDK or bindings

### Summary

`Mouse.drag()` always fails with a `TypeError` when the sandbox uses `QMPTransport`, so no drag is performed.

### Reproduction

1. Use a sandbox that runs on `QMPTransport` (QMP-driven VMs, or the fallback transport when spacesd isn't available).
2. Call `await sandbox.mouse.drag(10, 10, 200, 200)` (or let an agent issue a drag).
3. Minimal repro with a mocked QMP socket:

```python
import asyncio
from cua_sandbox.transport.qmp import QMPTransport
from cua_sandbox.interfaces.mouse import Mouse

class FakeQMP(QMPTransport):
    async def _execute(self, command, arguments=None):
        return {"return": {}}

asyncio.run(Mouse(FakeQMP()).drag(10, 10, 200, 200))
```

### Expected behavior

A press at (10, 10), interpolated moves, and a release at (200, 200).

### Actual behavior

```
TypeError: QMPTransport._drag() missing 4 required positional arguments: 'start_x', 'start_y', 'end_x', and 'end_y'
```

`Mouse.drag` (`cua_sandbox/interfaces/mouse.py`) sends `send("drag", path=[[start_x, start_y], [end_x, end_y]], button=...)`, but `QMPTransport._drag` (`transport/qmp.py`) takes `start_x, start_y, end_x, end_y`, and `send()` passes the params straight through as keyword arguments. `EnvTransport` handles the same `path=` form, so it looks like QMP wasn't updated when the interface switched to `path`.

### Environment

cua-sandbox 0.9.1 (main @ 03eda7b), Python 3.12, Linux. Reproduced with the QMP socket mocked.

### Evidence

The TypeError above, from the snippet in Reproduction. "drag" is listed in QMP's `_ACTION_DISPATCH`, so it's meant to be supported.

### Workaround and additional context

A possible fix is for `_drag` to accept `path` (start = `path[0]`, end = `path[-1]`), optionally still accepting the old keyword form.

title: [Bug]: Windows host status reports a running scheduled task as stopped on non-English Windows
body:
## Primary area

CLI (cua-host; also consumed by Cua Spaces)

## Summary

On a Simplified Chinese Windows installation, the configured `\Cua\SpacesdHost` scheduled task is enabled and running, and the host is online, but `cua host status` reports `service.running=false`. `WindowsTask::state` parses localized `schtasks /FO CSV` output using the English substring `Running`.

This is a reproduced native status false negative, not a report that the service failed to start. The app-core maps that same false status to `Host service stopped`; that UI consequence is source-confirmed, but the original application window was hidden during this investigation, so no GUI screenshot is claimed as reproduction evidence.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26300, x86_64, Simplified Chinese Windows UI.
- Installed Cua Spaces 0.13.1, bundled `cua` CLI 0.7.0.
- Host `cua-spacesd` 0.5.3, running via the scheduled-task path.
- The existing task action is a hidden `wscript.exe` -> PowerShell wrapper waiting for `cua-spacesd.exe`. The task itself, not merely a detached child, is reported as Running by Windows Task Scheduler. No task was re-registered or restarted for this investigation.
- Static cross-check: official `cua-spaces-v0.15.0` retains the same parser. That release was not installed or runtime-tested here.

## Reproduction

On non-English Windows with an already configured, enabled and running host task:

1. Query the authoritative task state without changing the task:

```powershell
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskPath '\Cua\' -TaskName 'SpacesdHost' |
    Select-Object State, @{n='Enabled'; e={$_.Settings.Enabled}}

$service = New-Object -ComObject Schedule.Service
$service.Connect()
$task = $service.GetFolder('\Cua').GetTask('SpacesdHost')
[pscustomobject]@{ State = [int]$task.State; Enabled = $task.Enabled }
```

2. Query the same task using the command used by cua-host:

```powershell
schtasks.exe /Query /TN 'Cua\SpacesdHost' /FO CSV /NH
```

Its running-status field is localized rather than the English literal `Running`.

3. Query the bundled CLI on the actual Windows host, not from an environment that blocks its loopback daemon:

```powershell
$status = cua --json host status | ConvertFrom-Json
[pscustomobject]@{
    Installed = $status.service.installed
    Running = $status.service.running
    Kind = $status.service.kind
    Sharing = $status.sharing
    Online = $status.online
}
```

## Actual behavior

| Observation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Windows Task Scheduler state | Running, enabled |
| Task result at live check | 0x41301 (task is currently running) |
| Scheduled-task process chain | Present, ending in the configured cua-spacesd executable |
| `cua host status`: service | installed=true, running=false, kind=windows-task |
| `cua host status`: sharing / online | true / true |
| Bundled daemon actual GetInfo RPC | Four successful responses, same PID, 0-45 ms |

The Task Scheduler COM query above is also provided as a numeric, locale-independent reproduction/check direction; the live authoritative state reported here was obtained with `Get-ScheduledTask` and `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`.

An in-sandbox CLI initially reported no daemon because loopback access was restricted. Running on the original host removed that unrelated failure; the localized task-state false negative remained.

## Expected behavior

An installed, enabled task with numeric `TASK_STATE_RUNNING` (4) is reported as running regardless of Windows UI language. Missing tasks, real stopped/disabled states, and query/access failures must remain distinct and must not be converted into false success.

## Evidence

- [Installed-release WindowsTask::state](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.13.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-host/src/service.rs#L981) and [0.15.0 still using the same check](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.15.0/libs/cua/crates/cua-host/src/service.rs#L1064): `schtasks /Query /FO CSV /NH`, UTF-8 lossy decoding, then `text.contains("Running")`. Both the localized status string and lossy decoding of localized stdout are fragile; decoding alone does not fix the English-only comparison.
- [App-core status label](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.13.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces-app-core/src/host.rs#L44): `!service_running` produces `Host service stopped`.
- [Host::start_sharing](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.13.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-host/src/host.rs#L1603) also uses this status to decide whether to install/start the service. This makes the faulty status more than cosmetic. That reinstall/start consequence is a source-level risk; it was deliberately not exercised against the working host.
- Scope: the scheduled-task Windows branch. The per-user Run-entry fallback detects the process by executable path instead. The macOS launchd branch parses `launchctl print` for `state = running`, not Windows localized CSV; the Windows evidence does not establish a macOS regression.

## Suggested direction

Query the exact task through the Task Scheduler API and numeric state (for example COM), rather than parsing human-localized display text. Preserve other host errors, relay state, and audit integrity warnings. Regression coverage should include running/stopped/disabled/missing, non-English output, and permission/query failure.

No installed package, task action, PATH, audit logs, or service processes were changed. No local patch was activated. A separately observed historical audit-log integrity warning is outside this issue and is not being attributed to this parser.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues/PRs for `schtasks`, `SpacesdHost`, `Host service stopped`, and combinations of Windows/localized/locale/Chinese; no exact matching public report was found.

- #2345 handles cua-driver autostart query HRESULT failures, not cua-host's localized running-status comparison.
- #5262 handles Windows unattended-access registration/launch failures, not this state check.
- #5315 handles transient relay outages; its mention of `Host service stopped` does not fix this Windows parser.

## Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes one reproduced native status problem.
- [x] Credentials, account IDs, private paths, raw audit data, and unrelated window content are excluded.
- [x] Runtime observations, source-confirmed consequences, and untested directions are distinguished.

title: fix(cua-driver): let another connection restart a session label once its owner has exited
body:
## Summary

In daemon mode a named session's label is tied to the MCP connection (transport) that started it. Once that session ends, only the same connection may call `start_session` to start it again. When that connection then closes, nothing can ever restart the label: every later connection gets

- `session has ended; … Call start_session with session 'X' to start it again` on an ordinary call, and
- `session is not available to this transport` when it follows that advice.

So clients that reconnect (a new `cua-driver mcp` proxy per agent run, for example) have to keep minting unique labels.

This change keeps the existing rules while the owning connection is open, and frees the label when it closes:

- When a transport exits (`SessionEndReason::ProcessExit` from the control-connection EOF reaper or the legacy `session_end`), its ended sessions, including ones it ended earlier, are marked orphaned (a new set held under the `ENDED_SESSIONS` lock, reset whenever a tombstone is written).
- `activate_or_revive_session_for_owner` (what `start_session` uses) lets another transport start an orphaned id. It still completes the old episode's cleanup first and fails closed if cleanup is incomplete, then binds the new episode to the new transport and fires the revive hooks, exactly like a same-owner revival, so capture scopes, grants, snapshots and cursor state from the old episode do not carry over.
- Unchanged: a live session, or an ended one whose owner is still connected, is never handed to another transport (`atomic_start_cannot_transfer_an_ended_label_to_another_transport` still holds), and ordinary actions still never revive an ended name: only an explicit `start_session` does, as the `start_session` description says.

The change is in `cua-driver-core`, so it applies to every platform. The private lifecycle id stays derived from the label (as for same-owner revival today); what keeps the old episode dead is the completed cleanup and the revive hooks, not a new id.

## Numbers

Reproduction: a raw stdio MCP script against an embedded daemon (`CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1 cua-driver serve --socket …`), three `cua-driver mcp --socket …` connections, on macOS 26.3.1.

main:

```
A  end_session          ok
A  get_cursor_position  ERR session has ended; … Call start_session with session 'repro-21765' to start it again …
A  start_session        ok revived=true          (same connection: works)
A  end_session          ok; connection A closes
B  get_cursor_position  ERR session has ended; … Call start_session …
B  start_session        ERR session is not available to this transport
B  get_cursor_position  ERR session has ended …   (label unusable for the daemon's lifetime)
```

this PR:

```
A  … same as main up to A closing …
B  get_cursor_position  ERR session has ended; … Call start_session …   (ordinary calls still never revive)
B  start_session        ok revived=true
B  get_cursor_position  ok
C  get_cursor_position  ERR session is not available to this transport   (B's live label is not hijacked)
C  start_session        ERR session is not available to this transport
```

## Validation

- New unit tests in `session.rs`: `exited_transports_ended_label_can_be_started_by_another_transport` (owner still connected: refused; owner exits: an explicit start from another transport succeeds for both an explicitly ended and a live-at-exit session, cleanup ran once, ordinary dispatch is still refused, the old owner can't take it back, a re-ended label is again owner-only) and `exited_transport_with_incomplete_cleanup_is_not_claimable`.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 1082 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. An earlier run under a parallel build had one timing failure in `batch_tools::tests::pauses_between_steps_but_not_after_the_last`; it passed 3/3 alone and in this run.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes; `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets` adds no warnings in `session.rs`.
- Live repro above with release builds of main and this branch.
- Tests, release binaries and the repro were re-run from a target directory private to this branch.
- Not run: the desktop E2E matrix.

title: fix(cua-driver): show a labelled live TCC check when permissions status can't read the driver's grants
body:
## Summary

`cua-driver permissions status` prints `❓ unknown` for both grants whenever no daemon answers as the driver's own identity: before the first `permissions grant` (or after the daemon stops), and whenever the listening daemon is embedded or was started from a terminal. That rule is deliberate (an in-process check reports the terminal's grants, which are not `com.trycua.driver`'s), but it leaves no way to see the grants that `cua-driver mcp --direct` and embedded daemons actually run with.

This keeps the driver's status `unknown` in those cases, with no top-level booleans, and adds a labelled live check:

- No daemon: the CLI runs a non-prompting probe of itself (`AXIsProcessTrusted` and `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`, never the prompting variants or the ScreenCaptureKit probe) through a new `platform_macos::tools::live_permission_probe()`. Its `source` uses the same attribution rules as `check_permissions`, plus `responsible_process` (`{pid, executable}` from `responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid`), which is the identity TCC charges the grants to.
- A listening daemon that is not `driver-daemon`: its own `check_permissions` answer, previously discarded, is shown the same way.
- If the CLI process itself is the driver's responsible process (attribution `driver-daemon`), its probe is reported as the driver's status.

The probe goes under a new `live_probe` key in `--json` (`probed`: `this_process` or `daemon`; `accessibility`, `screen_recording`, `source`). Existing keys and the first lines of the text output are unchanged, and output with a `driver-daemon` daemon is unchanged. macOS only; other platforms keep the current output. Docs (CLI reference header and generated page, troubleshooting row) describe `live_probe`.

Not done: reading `com.trycua.driver`'s own grants without a daemon. That needs a process whose responsible process is the app (the LaunchServices child `permissions grant` uses); launching the app bundle for a read-only status seemed too heavy, but it could be added behind a flag.

## Numbers

Before (main), no daemon (`HOME` pointed at an empty directory so the default socket is free):

```
Accessibility:    ❓ unknown
Screen Recording: ❓ unknown
No CuaDriver daemon is running under the driver's own identity (com.trycua.driver), so its real TCC status can't be read from this process. Run `cua-driver permissions grant` …
```

After:

```
Accessibility:    ❓ unknown
Screen Recording: ❓ unknown
No CuaDriver daemon is running under the driver's own identity (com.trycua.driver), …

Live check of this process (no prompt), attribution caller; macOS attributes it to /Applications/Pyramid.app/Contents/MacOS/Pyramid (pid 44016):
  Accessibility:    ✅ granted
  Screen Recording: ✅ granted
  These are not CuaDriver's (com.trycua.driver) grants. They are what `cua-driver mcp --direct` or an embedded daemon started from the same app uses.
```

With an embedded daemon (`CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1 cua-driver serve`) on the default socket, main prints the three `unknown` lines; this PR adds `Live check of the listening daemon, attribution host; …` with its booleans, and `--json` gains `"live_probe": {"probed": "daemon", "accessibility": true, "screen_recording": true, "source": {"attribution": "host", "embedded": true, …}}`. With the installed app's daemon running, output is identical to main (`Source: driver-daemon`).

## Validation

- New tests in `cli.rs` for the status mapping: `unattributed_status_without_probe_keeps_unknown_shape`, `unattributed_status_reports_caller_probe_separately`, `unattributed_status_reports_host_daemon_probe`, `only_driver_daemon_or_unattributed_answers_count_as_the_drivers`. `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --bins -- unattributed only_driver permission_grant`: 8 passed.
- `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib check_permissions`: 15 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes; `cargo clippy -p cua-driver -p platform-macos --all-targets` adds no warnings in the changed code.
- Manual before/after above with release builds on macOS 26.3.1 (no daemon, embedded daemon, installed app daemon). No prompt appeared in any run.
- Tests and the before/after binaries were re-run from target directories private to each branch.
- Not run: the desktop E2E matrix, and the `scripts/docs-generators` drift check (the header and the generated page were edited identically).

title: perf(cua-driver): let actions skip the post-action window-change wait
body:
## Summary

After an input action the macOS adapter watches the window list so the result can name a menu, dialog, new window or foreground change the action caused. A direct call waits up to 300 ms for that report before returning, and the rest of the 1 s watch runs detached. For an agent that reads the window state after every action anyway, that wait is most of a background click's latency.

This adds an optional per-call argument, `post_action_wait` (`"default"` | `"none"`), to the actions that wait for the report: `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `set_value`.

- Omitted or `"default"`: unchanged.
- `"none"`: the result returns as soon as the input is delivered and ends with `Window changes not observed: post_action_wait "none" returned without waiting. A new window or foreground change seen afterwards is reported on the next action's result.` It does not claim "no change". The watch still runs detached for its whole deadline and keeps the focus-steal lease, exactly like the remainder of a quiet watch today, so focus protection is the same as for a step inside `run_steps` and a late window is still reported on the next result.

How it is wired:

- Shared semantics live in `cua-driver-core` (new `post_action_wait` module). The registry's dispatch boundary validates the argument and runs the tool inside a task-local scope, the same pattern `step_pacing` uses for batch steps. The property is injected into the advertised schema of those nine tools centrally, like `session`, so no adapter schema changes.
- The macOS adapter reads the scope in `Snapshot::detect_async`, the one funnel every action uses: a zero report window hands the whole deadline to the existing detached watch and returns a `Changes` marked `deferred` (and `polled: false`).
- Linux and Windows refuse `"none"` with `unsupported_platform` instead of ignoring it: the Linux X11 foreground transaction uses its window watch as delivery evidence (`effect: "confirmed"`), and the Windows adapter does not wait for window changes after an action. Invalid values are refused with `invalid_arguments`.
- Not part of the typed portable SDK subset, so `libs/cua-driver/contract/manifest.json` and the bindings are unchanged (`cua-contract-gen all --check` passes).

The ~80 ms key-window settle in `prime_key_window_for_background_press` is left alone: it is what makes a background AXPress on a key-window-routed control (TextEdit's format bar) land, and it only runs for native apps that are not frontmost.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1. Calculator in the background, another app frontmost. Daemon run as `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1 cua-driver serve --socket …`, driven through `cua-driver mcp --socket …` by a stdio MCP client. `main` is upstream main at 96b1faef. Median (p90) of 20 calls; the machine was shared with other builds (load average around 35), so treat single numbers as noisy:

| click | main | this PR, argument omitted | this PR, `"none"` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `element_token` (AXPress on All Clear) | 753 (2249) ms | 568 (606) ms | 249 (270) ms |
| coordinate, routed pixel path (display area) | 870 (1670) ms | 921 (1515) ms | 511 (1045) ms |

Two earlier rounds gave the same picture: AXPress 593–626 ms on main, 602–732 ms with the argument omitted or `"default"`, 301–352 ms with `"none"`; pixel path 990–1012 ms, 934–1160 ms and 644–693 ms. A coordinate click that the hit-test resolves to an AX press (All Clear) never watched the window list and stayed at 234–387 ms in every configuration.

Delivery check with `"none"` on every call: AXPress on 5 twice showed `55`, All Clear showed `0`, a background coordinate click on 5 showed `5`.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 1085 passed, 1 ignored. New `post_action_wait` tests cover omitted/null/default, `"none"`, the `unsupported_platform` refusal, invalid values and the task-local scope.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 637 passed, 7 ignored. New `a_skipped_wait_returns_at_once_and_watches_detached` checks that a zero report window returns in under 100 ms without observing, says so in the suffix, leaves the detached watch armed, and that the watch still records a late window.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets`: no findings in the changed files. It reports 5 findings in files this PR does not touch (`ax/reveal_scroll.rs:185`, `tools/click.rs:153` ×3, `document_edit.rs:65`), which fail `-D warnings` on main with the pinned 1.97.1 toolchain too.
- `cargo run -p cua-driver-contract --bin cua-contract-gen -- all --check` passes.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test --test protocol_tools_call_test`: pass (2 passed and 1 passed; the rest are ignored desktop tests).
- Docs: regenerated `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/mcp-tools` with `scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.ts` from a native macOS dump (`--check` passes). The Linux and Windows snapshots in `scripts/docs-generators/cli-specs` were edited to add the same injected property (it comes from the shared registry), not dumped natively. `Skills/cua-driver/EMBEDDING.md` documents the argument next to the existing window-observation bounds.
- Not run: Linux and Windows builds and the desktop E2E matrix. The non-macOS change is the core refusal path, covered by the unit test with the platform flag passed in.
- All Rust checks above ran from a private target directory for this worktree.

title: feat(cua-driver): add select_text to select text or place the caret by element_token
body:
## Summary

Adds a `select_text` tool: select a string inside a text element, or put the caret right before or after it, without typing or bringing the app forward. It targets the element the way `set_value` does (`element_token` from `get_window_state`, optional `pid`/`window_id`) and takes:

- `text` (required): exact, case-sensitive text to find in the element's value.
- `prefix` / `suffix` (optional): text that must come immediately before/after the match, to pick one of several occurrences.
- `selection_type` (optional): `"text"` (default) selects the match; `"cursor_before"` / `"cursor_after"` set a zero-length range at its start/end.

Matching is shared. `cua-driver-core/src/text_selection.rs` finds the occurrence (every start position counts, so overlapping repeats are reported as ambiguous instead of silently picking one) and converts the byte offset to UTF-16 code units, which is what AX text ranges count. The macOS adapter (`platform-macos/src/tools/select_text.rs`) resolves the token, takes the same background-window gate as `set_value`, writes `AXSelectedTextRange` as a `CFRange` `AXValue`, reads it back and only reports success when the read-back equals the requested range. `structuredContent` carries `range`, `match_range`, `selected_text`, `previous_range`, `role` and `verified`.

Refusals are structured errors (`effect: "refused"`, `code`):

- `text_not_found` (with `occurrences`: 0, or how many there were when prefix/suffix ruled them all out)
- `ambiguous_text_match` (with `matches`, and a message asking for prefix/suffix)
- `selection_not_settable`: the element has no settable `AXSelectedTextRange` or no text value
- `selection_not_applied`: the write failed or the read-back differs
- `unsupported_platform`: Linux and Windows register `UnsupportedSelectTextTool` from core with the same schema, so the tool exists everywhere and refuses explicitly there. AT-SPI `Text.setSelection` and UIA `TextPattern` could implement it later.

Registration follows `set_value`: capabilities (`accessibility.text_selection`, new in the vocabulary, plus `accessibility.element_tokens`), risk class R1 and desktop-input operation, desktop coordination, capture scope, the shared required-set gate, the MCP compat roster, the docs generator category (Typing tools) and the regenerated reference pages and specs. Like `set_value`, it is not part of the portable contract manifest (`libs/cua-driver/contract/manifest.json`), and it does not return the shared `ActionResult`. Nothing existing changes behavior.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1, `cua-driver mcp --direct` from a stdio MCP client, on a TextEdit document opened for the test with `Hello 😀 world.\nThe cat sat. The cat ran. café ☕ end\n` (53 UTF-16 units):

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `text:"world"` | range {9, 5}, selected "world" (the emoji before it counts as 2 units), previous {0, 0} |
| `text:"cat"` | `ambiguous_text_match`, matches 2 |
| `text:"cat", prefix:"The "` | `ambiguous_text_match`, matches 2 |
| `text:"cat", suffix:" ran"` | range {33, 3}, selected "cat" |
| `text:"café"` | range {42, 4} |
| `text:"☕", selection_type:"cursor_after"` | range {48, 0} |
| `text:"😀", selection_type:"cursor_before"` | range {6, 0} |
| `text:"zzz"` | `text_not_found`, occurrences 0 |
| `text:"cat", prefix:"dog "` | `text_not_found`, occurrences 2 |
| an `AXButton` token | `selection_not_settable` |

Every success was read back from `AXSelectedTextRange` by the tool and matched. The caret was put back at {0, 0} afterwards and the document was never edited. Latency of a successful call, 40 calls: p50 45 ms, p90 136 ms. The machine was under load from parallel builds; an earlier run gave p50 49 ms, p90 79 ms.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 1094 passed, including 14 new `text_selection` tests (UTF-16 offsets across emoji and accents, overlapping matches, prefix/suffix narrowing, not-found counts, selection_type parsing, the unsupported-platform refusal).
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 636 passed.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --tests`: 457 passed, 2 failed in `embedded_host_sdk_mcp_test` (`test fixture writer failed: exit status: 2` from its shell fixture helper on this machine). They don't touch this change, but I didn't confirm they fail on main here.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` passes. `cargo clippy` on cua-driver-core, platform-macos, platform-linux, platform-windows and cua-driver reports no warnings in the changed files. `-D warnings` fails on warnings that are already there (`click.rs`, `document_edit.rs`, `reveal_scroll.rs`, `version_check.rs`).
- `docs:generate:cua-driver` regenerated the macOS spec and reference pages. `runner.ts --library cua-driver --check` passes. I added the Linux and Windows `cli-specs` entries by hand, from the macOS dump with the unsupported description, because only a run on those hosts regenerates them.
- Not run: Linux/Windows builds (the cross targets aren't installed for this toolchain), so the `platform-linux`/`platform-windows` `impl_.rs` registration lines are compiled only by CI. Their `stubs.rs` registrations do build on macOS. The desktop E2E matrix was not run either.

title: feat(cua-driver): add JPEG screenshots to get_window_state and encode from raw pixels
body:
## Summary

`get_window_state` on macOS encoded every capture as PNG, and when the window was larger than the `max_image_dimension` ceiling (1366 by default) it decoded that PNG again, resized it with Lanczos3 and re-encoded it.

This keeps the raw RGBA pixels from ScreenCaptureKit and the SkyLight off-Space capture (new `CapturedImage` / `RgbaFrame` in `cua_driver_core::image_utils`), so the screenshot is resized and encoded once. The `screencapture` shell fallback still hands back a PNG and goes through the old path. `screenshot_window_bytes` keeps its signature and output for every other caller.

It also adds two optional `get_window_state` arguments on macOS:

- `screenshot_format`: `"png"` (default) or `"jpeg"`.
- `screenshot_quality`: JPEG quality 1–95, default 85; refused unless `screenshot_format` is `"jpeg"`.

The values and range mirror the existing `screenshot` tool's `format`/`quality`; the `screenshot_` prefix matches `include_screenshot` and `screenshot_out_file` and keeps them apart from `tree_format`. A JPEG read sets `screenshot_mime_type: "image/jpeg"`, sends an `image/jpeg` image part (or writes JPEG to `screenshot_out_file`), drops alpha, keeps the same dimensions and pixel-to-window mapping, and mints no `capture_id`, because the capture registry stores and validates PNG captures only.

Scope and limits:

- Default output is byte-identical: PNG is lossless, so resizing the raw pixels gives the same image as resizing the decoded PNG, and both go through the same encoder. A unit test checks this for several caps, and live reads of Calculator (230×408, not resized) and a TextEdit document (768×1569, resized to 669×1366) returned the same SHA-256 as main.
- `get_desktop_state` and `zoom` are unchanged: `zoom` already returns JPEG, and the desktop PNG is the coordinate source behind its mandatory `capture_id`.
- Linux and Windows do not advertise the new arguments, so the registry refuses them there as unknown arguments. The portable contract manifest is a subset and does not list them; `cua-contract-gen all --check` is unaffected.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1, on the external 1× display. In-process timings of the encode step on real captures (median of 30, release build):

| window (raw capture) | main path | this PR, PNG | this PR, JPEG q85 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calculator 230×408 (no resize) | 0.5 ms | 0.4 ms | 1.0 ms |
| TextEdit 768×1569 → 669×1366 | 25.3 ms | 23.4 ms | 29.0 ms |

Breakdown for the TextEdit capture: the Lanczos3 resize is 23 ms of it at 1× and 72 ms when the same content is doubled to a Retina-sized 1536×3138 frame, while the PNG round trip this PR removes is about 2 ms at 1× and about 7 ms at 2× (full-size encode plus decode). So the default-path saving is small for flat UI content and grows with capture size and entropy; the resize dominates and is untouched here.

Image size, same reads:

| window | PNG | JPEG q85 |
|---|---|---|
| Calculator | 46,524 B | 22,127 B (−52%) |
| TextEdit document | 44,380 B | 36,536 B (−18%) |

For flat UI captures like these, the `image` crate's JPEG encoder is slower than its PNG encoder (6.5 ms vs 0.8 ms on the resized TextEdit frame), so `"jpeg"` trades a few milliseconds for a smaller payload; it does not make the read faster. End to end through the daemon (`cua-driver serve` plus `cua-driver mcp --socket`, 15 reads, two rounds), `get_window_state` tree+shot medians were 211–384 ms on main, 249–421 ms for this PR's PNG and 233–297 ms for JPEG on the two windows, with p90 up to 700 ms: the machine was shared with other builds (load average 35–50), so those numbers do not resolve differences of a few milliseconds either way.

## Validation

title: fix(cua-sdk): let runtime setup provision the managed backend
body:
## Problem

On a Mac with no Docker-API container engine, `cua runtime doctor` reports the
`managed` backend as provisionable, so `cua runtime setup` with no components
picks it, then rejects the name with `unknown component "managed"` and exits 2.
`setup_with` had no arm for `BackendKind::Managed`.

## Fix

`managed` gets its own setup step: `managed::ensure()` downloads the built-in
Linux runtime and boots its VM. Component names now all resolve before any
installer runs, so a bad name fails fast instead of leaving earlier installs
unreported.

Fixes #5718

## Testing

- `cargo test -p cua-daemon --lib`: new cases cover `managed` in the default
  set and the fail-fast on an unknown component.
- `cua --embedded runtime setup --dry-run` with no reachable container engine
  now lists `managed` as Installable and exits 0 (was exit 2).
- The real `setup managed` path (`managed::ensure`, about 455 MB download and
  a VM boot) was not run here; it is the same entry point the runtime uses on
  first use.

title: cua-driver (macOS) docs: launch_app with urls opens a tab in Chrome's front window, not a separate window
body:
## Summary

`skills/cua-driver/MACOS.md` says that for a browser page you can't bind exactly, `launch_app({bundle_id, urls})` creates "a separately addressable window". With Google Chrome already running, it doesn't: Chrome opens each URL as a new tab in its frontmost existing window.

## Where the docs say it

In the "Keyboard shortcuts that semantically mean 'focus here'" bullet:

> For an exactly bound Chromium page, use `browser_navigate`; otherwise use `launch_app({bundle_id, urls})` to create a separately addressable window.

The next bullet, on tab-switching shortcuts, also recommends "separately addressable windows over visible tab switching".

## What happens

- cua-driver 0.37.0 on macOS, Google Chrome stable, already running with the user's own windows open.
- `cua-driver launch_app '{"bundle_id":"com.google.Chrome","urls":["https://example.com/"]}'` loads the URL in a new tab of Chrome's frontmost window. `list_windows` shows no new window.
- Each further call adds another tab to the same window. Later `get_window_state` reads of that window return whatever tab is active, so an agent following the docs ends up reading, or acting in, the user's own window, and can capture their other tabs (the tab strip is part of the window's tree).

That's how Chrome treats an open-URL request when it's already running, so `launch_app` is behaving correctly; the doc's promise is what's wrong.

## What does give a separate window

This opens a new window in the running Chrome, which you can find by comparing `list_windows` before and after:

```json
{
  "bundle_id": "com.google.Chrome",
  "creates_new_application_instance": true,
  "additional_arguments": ["--profile-directory=Default", "--new-window", "https://example.com/"]
}
```

## Suggested fix

Replace the sentence with something like: "otherwise open a window of your own: `launch_app` with `creates_new_application_instance: true` and `additional_arguments: ["--new-window", url]` (plus `--profile-directory=<profile>` for a specific profile), then diff `list_windows` to find its window ID. For Chrome, `launch_app` with `urls` opens a tab in the user's frontmost window."

title: feat(spaces): Stable / Beta / Nightly picker with switch, download and restart (CUA-2354)
body:
Part of CUA-1991. Linear: https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-2354. The builds and the feed are in the companion PR (CUA-2353).

**For users:** in Settings, Advanced, Updates, pick Stable, Beta or Nightly. Nightly downloads right away and offers "Restart to update". Going back to Stable is one click, and the app explains what happens next.

**Behavior (modelled on T3 Code's channel switch)**
- "Get updates from: Stable | Beta | Nightly" replaces the "Get early releases (Beta)" toggle. Nightly appears only where the host can follow the nightly feed (the Mac app); Electron keeps Stable and Beta.
- Choosing a channel saves it and checks that channel at once. An update found downloads by itself and shows inline as "Cua Spaces 0.17.0-nightly.… is ready", with **Restart to update**. The sidebar button (#5404) picks it up too. This PR doesn't touch #5404's files.
- Plain-words copy: Nightly is "A new build most nights with the very latest changes. Nightly builds are not tested, so something may break." A short note explains how to switch back.
- Back on Stable from a nightly build: Sparkle refuses to install an older version (`SUPlainInstaller` downgrade guard), so the build stays until the next Stable release replaces it. The page says exactly that and offers **Download Stable** to go back right now. The nightly bundle version is chosen so that the next stable release always counts as an upgrade.
- No native views: everything is the React UI. Swift only points Sparkle at the feed through `feedURLString(for:)` and allowed channels `["nightly"]`.

**Changes by layer**
- Core: `UpdateChannel::Nightly`, `feed_url` / `nightly_feed_url` (next to `SUFeedURL`), help and note per channel, nightly first launch. Nightly is stored as `beta` + `nightlyUpdates: true`, so a pre-Nightly release reads Beta instead of dropping the whole settings file. FFI and Swift/TS bindings are regenerated, and the parity golden is updated.
- macOS: `UpdatesModel` follows the channel (Sparkle channels plus the feed URL) and checks on a switch. Telemetry uses the channel id. A nightly's release-notes link points to the nightly release.
- Web: `UpdateChannelGroup` (picker, inline status, restart, note, download), contracts and shapes. The demo host runs the whole switch.

**Tests:** cargo test, clippy and fmt (app-core, ffi); Swift full suite (624 tests); web vitest (829) and tsc; Electron vitest and tsc.

title: perf(cua-driver): capture the macOS desktop with captureImage(in:) when there is no overlay to leave out
body:
On macOS, `get_desktop_state` captures the main display in about half the time when the agent cursor overlay is not on screen.

**Problem.** With no overlay window to leave out, `screenshot_display_bytes_excluding_overlay` runs `/usr/sbin/screencapture -x`: a process, a temporary file and a PNG decode, about 300 ms per call on a 1280x800 display.

**Fix.** That path now captures with `SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(in:)` over the main display bounds, which skips the shareable-content query and the content filter: about 115 ms for the same pixels, against 180–240 ms for the content-filter capture the overlay path uses. `screencapture` stays the fallback when ScreenCaptureKit fails. The `screencapturekit` feature moves from `macos_15_0` to `macos_15_2`; the crate's bridge checks `#available(macOS 15.2, *)` at run time and returns an error before 15.2, so older systems keep the `screencapture` path.

**Testing.** macOS 26.5 VM without GPU, `get_desktop_state` at 1024 px, builds alternated A/B/B/A: p50 325 → 170 ms. At 2x (2560x1600) the image size is unchanged and the 1024 px image is identical; at full size the only difference is the menu bar's screen-recording indicator. No unit test: the capture needs a display and Screen Recording, which plain `cargo test` does not use.

Platforms: macOS only.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` (636 passed) on a macos-15 runner. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` reports nothing in the touched files; it stops on `ax/reveal_scroll.rs:185` (`single_match`), which is on `main` too.

title: fix(cua-driver): type background text into kitty through AXValue, and stop reading a blank terminal as zero delivered
body:
On macOS, background `type_text` to kitty goes in through its text view's `AXValue`, which kitty commits to the shell, and a blank kitty read-back is reported as unverified instead of zero characters delivered.

**Problem.** kitty forwards a key event only to its key window. With another app frontmost, `type_text {pid: <kitty>, text}` posts pid-routed keys that kitty drops: 0 of 10 background calls reached the shell on a real Mac (macOS 26, kitty on a second display). kitty's `AXValue` is the text around the cursor and only while kitty is focused, so an unfocused kitty reads blank before and after any write. `type_text` then reported zero characters delivered, and `set_value` reported `write_not_applied` while the text was in fact at kitty's prompt (`kitty @ get-text` showed it).

**Fix.**
- Background `type_text` to kitty (matched by bundle id) writes plain text as `AXValue` on its text view, which kitty commits to the pty as typed text. Text with control characters keeps the key route, since the pty would take them as Enter or completion.
- It falls back to keys only when AX refused the write before kitty saw it (unsupported attribute, illegal argument, invalid element, AX disabled). After a messaging timeout or another indeterminate error the write may have landed, and keys could type the text twice.
- For kitty, a blank read-back is unverifiable, not zero delivered (`type_text`) or `write_not_applied` (`set_value`). Terminal.app and iTerm2 drop `AXValue` writes, so their blank read-back stays `write_not_applied`.

**Testing.** New unit tests cover the route choice (`only_kitty_takes_plain_text_as_an_ax_value`), the fallback only after a refusal (`kitty_text_falls_back_to_keys_only_after_a_refused_ax_write`), when an insert counts as landed (`a_kitty_insert_lands_only_when_its_line_changed_to_hold_the_text`) and the blank read-back verdicts for `type_text` and `set_value`. The AX write landing at a background kitty's prompt was seen on a real kitty, as above. A recorded end-to-end background `type_text` run on kitty with this branch is still missing: kitty needs OpenGL 3.3, which our GPU-less macOS VMs lack.

Platforms: macOS only.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` (643 passed) on a macos-15 runner. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` reports nothing in the touched files; it stops on `ax/reveal_scroll.rs:185` (`single_match`), which is on `main` too.

title: fix(cua-driver): find a macOS window on another Space through the app's focused and main window, and say when its pixels are stale
body:
On macOS, `get_window_state` finds a window on another Space through the app's focused and main window before the remote-token probe, and says when that window's pixels can be stale.

**Problem.**
- A window on another Space is missing from `AXWindows`. The remote-token probe (#4068, #4085) recovers it by walking element ids 0..2000 within 300 ms, which a large app can exceed. WeChat 4.x on macOS 26, main window on another Space: `get_window_state` returned 13 elements (the menu bar and the window's three title-bar buttons) and none of the chat.
- Apps that draw with their own renderer stop painting while hidden, so an off-Space capture is their last frame. A background `type_text` into that WeChat window landed, while captures 2–3 s later still showed the empty input box; it caught up minutes later.

**Fix.**
- Before the probe, `copy_ax_windows_including` asks the app's `AXFocusedWindow`, `AXMainWindow` and the focused element's `AXWindow`. AX keeps these for a window on another Space, and they name the usual target. A candidate counts only as an `AXWindow` with the requested CGWindowID; the first match is kept and the others are released. The probe stays the fallback.
- For a window off the current Space whose app bundles ANGLE, Electron, CEF or Qt frameworks, `get_window_state` adds a note: the screenshot may be the last frame, and the accessibility tree is the better signal (Electron also throttles accessibility updates while hidden, so confirm with a later read).

**Testing.** New unit tests: `the_first_matching_window_wins_and_the_rest_are_released`, `bundled_angle_electron_cef_or_qt_marks_an_own_renderer`, `an_off_space_own_renderer_window_gets_a_pixels_only_note`. On a macOS 26.5 VM an off-Space TextEdit window reads the same 14 elements with and without this branch (the probe already finds a small app's window). A recorded re-read of the WeChat window with this branch is still missing.

Platforms: macOS only.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` (639 passed) on a macos-15 runner. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` reports nothing in the touched files; it stops on `ax/reveal_scroll.rs:185` (`single_match`), which is on `main` too.

title: fix(cua-driver): corroborate ambiguous XAML-host exe basenames with window evidence
body:
### Summary

- **Problem this solves**: `cua-driver`'s XAML/UWP host detection (`is_xaml_host_hwnd` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/input/keyboard.rs`) treats a hardcoded **exe-basename list as a verdict on its own**. `notepad.exe` is in that list, so on Windows 10 — where `C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe` is the classic Win32 Notepad (top-level class `Notepad`, `Edit` child control, menu bar, no XAML anywhere) — the window is misrouted into the XAML/UWP path. Observable effects: decorated hotkeys (`ctrl+s`, `alt+f`) are refused after a failed UIA AcceleratorKey scan with PostMessage fallback suppressed, and background pixel clicks lose their PostMessage fallback. The upstream `DebugWindowInfoTool` payload is self-contradictory on the very same window: `exe_xaml_match: true` while `xaml_class_match: false`.
  Windows 11 ships a WinUI3 Notepad under the **same basename** from `...\WindowsApps\`, which is why the basename was added — but the basename alone can never decide for that name.
- **What changed**: exe basename is kept as a signal, but ambiguous basenames now require independent corroboration:
  1. `XAML_HOST_EXES` keeps only unambiguous UWP/packaged host basenames (`calculatorapp.exe`, `calc.exe`, `applicationframehost.exe`, `photos.exe`, `systemsettings.exe`); `notepad.exe` moves to a new `AMBIGUOUS_XAML_HOST_EXES`.
  2. An ambiguous basename routes as XAML only with corroboration (`xaml_host_evidence`): the image path is packaged (`\WindowsApps\`) **or** a descendant window carries a XAML host class (`Microsoft.UI.Content.DesktopChildSiteBridge` is embedded as a *child* HWND by WinUI3 desktop hosts, invisible to the top-level class check).
  3. `DebugWindowInfoTool` drops its duplicated hand-maintained lists and calls the same `crate::input` helpers the router calls; `xaml_routing_recommended` is now derived from `is_xaml_host_hwnd()` itself, so the diagnostic can never disagree with the routing it explains. New diagnostic fields: `xaml_descendant_match`, `exe_xaml_evidence{packaged_path, xaml_descendant_class}`.
  4. Six unit tests (`xaml_host_detection_tests`) cover the ambiguous/unambiguous split, packaged-path case-insensitivity, basename extraction, class-set positive/negative samples, and null HWND.

### Related work

- Refs CUA-543 (the diagnostic comparison cited by the existing comment; note it only ever covered the Windows 11 build).
- No open upstream issue/PR found for the Windows 10 classic-Notepad misroute at submission time (will link if one surfaces).
- Not an RFC-scoped change: no public SDK/CLI/MCP/protocol contract changes — internal routing predicate + diagnostic tool only.

### Compatibility and risk

- **User-visible impact**: on Windows 10, classic Win32 Notepad (and any other app whose exe basename is later found ambiguous) is correctly routed back to the Win32 PostMessage/SendInput path — hotkeys like `alt+f`/`ctrl+s` work again and background pixel clicks regain their PostMessage fallback. On Windows 11, modern Notepad/Calculator/Photos/Settings are unchanged (packaged path or unambiguous basename still routes to XAML).
- **API/CLI/MCP impact**: `debug_window_info` gains two additive diagnostic fields; existing fields keep their meaning (`exe_xaml_match` semantics change only for the ambiguous-basename case, which is the bug being fixed).
- **Risk and rollback**: the only behavior change is gated on the ambiguous-basename list (initially just `notepad.exe`); all other targets behave identically. Rollback = revert the single commit.
- No version bump included; if this lands in a patch release the maintainers may want the `no-release` label or to fold it into the next driver release.

### Validation

- **Focused tests**: new `xaml_host_detection_tests` (6 tests) pass on the patched build; existing keyboard/input tests unaffected.
- **Manual / platform evidence** (Windows 10.0.19042.1706, console session; classic Notepad from `C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe`, 201728 bytes, 2022-03-11; same window, same session, A/B: pinned 0.37.0 driver vs locally built patched driver from upstream commit `2d2f992`):

  | Check | 0.37.0 (pinned) | Patched build |
  |---|---|---|
  | `debug_window_info.exe_xaml_match` (classic Notepad) | `true` | **`false`** |
  | `debug_window_info.xaml_class_match` (same payload) | `false` (self-contradiction) | `false` (now consistent) |
  | `debug_window_info.xaml_routing_recommended` | `true` | **`false`** |
  | `hotkey ["alt","f"]` | exit=1, refused as "modern XAML / UWP target", no UIA AcceleratorKey found | exit=0, delivered via PostMessage (Win32 target) |
  | Unit tests `xaml_host_detection` | — | 6 passed / 0 failed |

- **Real-UWP no-regression** (Windows 10 Settings, patched build, two host processes):

  | Target | exe_basename | exe_xaml_evidence | exe_xaml_match after patch |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Settings (SystemSettings.exe) | `systemsettings.exe` | n/a (unambiguous basename decides) | **still `true`** |
  | Settings (ApplicationFrameHost.exe) | `applicationframehost.exe` | `xaml_descendant_class: true` | **still `true`** |

- **Repro steps for reviewers** (on a Windows 10 machine with classic Notepad):
  1. Launch classic Notepad (`C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe`).
  2. `cua-driver call debug_window_info '{"pid":<notepad pid>}'` → note `exe_xaml_match: true` while `windows[].xaml_class_match` is `false`.
  3. `cua-driver call hotkey '{"keys":["alt","f"],"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<hwnd>}'` → refused as a XAML/UWP target.
  4. Apply this branch, rebuild, repeat steps 2–3 → judgment flips, hotkey delivers via PostMessage.
- **Known gaps**: a separate inconsistency ("reports ✅ but classic Notepad ignores PostMessage modified keys" in some menus) is **not** addressed here — it originates in `finish_pixel_uia_attempt()` refusing on UIA hit-test `Unavailable`, independent of XAML detection. Left out to keep this PR focused.

### Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff (3 files, +230/−46 incl. comments and tests).
- [x] No RFC required (internal routing predicate + diagnostic; no public contract change).
- [x] Tests + platform evidence included.
- [x] Title is a Conventional Commit.
- [x] External contributor authorship preserved (single author commit).
- [ ] `no-release` label — N/A unless maintainers prefer it (no version bump in diff).

title: fix(cua): read Windows host task state independently of locale
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on a non-English Windows host, `schtasks /FO CSV`
  localizes its status field, while `WindowsTask::state` matches the English
  substring `Running`. A running host is therefore reported as stopped.
- Read the exact host task through the local Task Scheduler COM API and compare
  its numeric state with `TASK_STATE_RUNNING` instead. Retain the existing
  per-user Run-entry fallback, service controls and platform implementations.
- Balance COM initialization on fresh or MTA threads and preserve an existing
  STA apartment. Keep COM interfaces on the calling thread and do not change
  process-wide COM security.
- Preserve operation/HRESULT diagnostics on query failure and distinguish a
  confirmed missing task from an unavailable query in the detail string.

## Related work

Fixes #5969

No RFC: this corrects an internal platform status observation without changing
the public API, protocol, configuration, permissions or compatibility policy.

## Compatibility and risk

- Only the Windows scheduled-task status path changes. No task is registered,
  stopped, started or modified by the query. No UI workaround or language change
  is involved.
- A task with a running instance is running even if future launches are
  disabled. `Enabled` is deliberately not used as a second running condition.
- Query-unavailable is still constrained by the existing boolean
  `ServiceState` API. It remains `running=false`, with explicit failure detail;
  this PR does not redesign callers' recovery decisions or claim to eliminate
  the pre-existing install/start behavior on arbitrary query errors.
- The COM calls are synchronous, like the prior task query. No new hard timeout
  or cancellation guarantee is claimed.
- Reverting the commit restores the prior status query. Installed user Cua
  packages and services were not replaced or restarted for validation.

## Validation

Native Windows 11 x86_64, Simplified Chinese; Rust 1.97.1, MSVC:

- Tested candidate commit: `6378976` (base `4b84caa4053bd86be7746c5527cee3d1626612ed`).
- Baseline: `cargo test --locked -p cua-host --lib`: 183 passed.
- RED on the original production code: the opt-in read-only test compares the
  existing host task's numeric COM state with public `WindowsTask::state`.
  Windows reported State=4; original code returned `running=false`.
- GREEN: the same opt-in test passed after the change, without restarting or
  changing the task or host process.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-host`: 188 passed; the one real-task probe is
  ignored in the default run.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-host --test windows_task_state -- --ignored --nocapture`:
  1 passed. This requires an existing host task and performs reads only.
- `cargo fmt -p cua-host -- --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-host --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on
  native Windows.
- `cargo metadata --locked --offline --no-deps --format-version 1`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Clean merge dry-run against current `origin/main`: passed.

The default owner tests cover numeric states 0-4, missing-task HRESULTs,
non-missing failures and diagnostics, balanced fresh/nested COM initialization,
and preservation of an existing STA apartment. They do not contact Task
Scheduler, register fixtures or access a user's real task.

Known gaps / other checks:

- Real stopped/disabled task fixtures were not created or exercised; their
  numeric-state mapping is covered by hermetic tests. The real probe only
  observed the existing running task.
- Linux/macOS execution and the repository's remote CI have not been run here.
- `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast` did not pass: its global FSL header check
  reports two untouched existing HTML5 assets, and its all-repository lockfile
  checker cannot validate workspaces omitted from this sparse checkout. The
  changed crate's format check passed and its locked metadata was checked
  separately. No unrelated files or CI rules were changed to suppress this.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

This is a user-visible fix; it is not intentionally non-releasing.
Prepared with AI assistance; all checks claimed above were executed against
the native Rust implementation, not a generated UI mock or installed-app patch.

title: docs(rfc): propose 1Password fill-and-submit login for Cua Driver
body:
Adds a modified copy of @f-trycua's target-bound credential delivery RFC from [#2943](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2943), discussed in [#2942](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2942), and links the earlier credential-broker draft in [#3364](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/3364). Most of Francesco's text is retained, with his authorship and source commits preserved. The original PR remains open; this proposal records no maintainer decision.

The revision proposes three changes:
- 1Password desktop-app logins use one combined `fill_and_submit_login` action with a fixed, secret-free outcome. There is no fill-only desktop login operation: leaving a populated password field between calls could expose the password through later observation or verification read-back.
- Cua owns one 1Password integration shared by every agent running on cua. The runtime owns the SDK client, and the desktop-app authorization prompt names a cua executable.
- `type_secret` remains only on the service-account path, gated on fail-closed recording and password-field masking. Submission on that path remains separately authorized.

The desktop-app route resolves values inside cua through the published SDK, then cua fills and submits. Provider-owned fill and submit remains conditional on a future documented API; the proposal does not claim that such an API is available today.

Only one RFC document is added under `docs/rfcs/`. No implementation changes are included.

verify: PASS at 5371cae3bffea8cc7885134cc8c7657915067e7f
risk: light

## Verification
- Confirmed the diff contains only the new RFC; `git diff --check`, relative-link checks, ASCII and vocabulary checks passed.
- Ran the scoped repository checks: the em-dash check passed; the script reported an unbound `rootpaths` variable in its crate/project stage. No code or project configuration changed.
- Checked the referenced GitHub records and compared provider claims with published 1Password SDK documentation. No incorrect provider claims were found in the inspected sources.
- Reviewed operation boundaries, masking and recording gates, submission semantics, and the future-only provider-owned route. No runtime or native-platform tests were run for this documentation-only change.

title: ci: switch macOS xlarge jobs to self-hosted Macs with one repo variable (MAC_RUNNER_LABELS)
body:
Linear: CUA-2444. Related: #5846 (larger runners).

## What changes for users and customers

Nothing, until a repo variable is set. When it is set, Mac CI jobs run on our own Macs instead of GitHub's paid `macos-26-xlarge` runners (estimated about $980 a day against $140 planned).

## What this does

Every job on `macos-26-xlarge` now uses:

```yaml
runs-on: ${{ (<gate> && fromJSON(vars.MAC_RUNNER_LABELS || '"macos-26-xlarge"') || 'macos-26-xlarge') }}
```

- `MAC_RUNNER_LABELS` unset: `macos-26-xlarge`, exactly as today.
- `MAC_RUNNER_LABELS` set: the self-hosted labels, but only when the event is `push`, `merge_group`, `workflow_dispatch`, or a `pull_request` with `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`.
- Fork PRs and `schedule` stay on `macos-26-xlarge` even when the variable is set.
- No `pull_request_target` is added or used.

## Jobs switched (7 jobs in 6 workflows)

- `ci-openkoalabot-example-samples.yml`: `swift`
- `ci-infinite-canvas-swift.yml`: `swift`
- `e2b-bindings.yml`: `swift`
- `ci-cua-spaces-macos.yml`: `ffi`, `swift-tests`, `app-bundle`
- `ci-cua-sdk.yml`: `rust` (macOS matrix entry only)
- `ci-cua-spaces.yml`: `bundle` (`macos-dmg` matrix entry only)

Not touched: standard `macos-26`, `macos-15` and `macos-latest` jobs (free on a public repo), Linux 16-core and Windows 8-core larger runners, and the existing Lume self-hosted lanes.

Also: `.github/actionlint.yaml` knows the `cua-ci` label, `test_ci_swift_samples_scope.py` checks the new expression, and `docs/ci/self-hosted-mac-runners.md` covers runner registration, labels, the non-admin user, Xcode pinning, disk cleanup and the fork-PR rule.

## What Francesco must set

After the Macs are registered as ephemeral/JIT runners in a runner group restricted to `trycua/cua` (see the doc), set the repository variable:

- Name: `MAC_RUNNER_LABELS`
- Value: `["self-hosted","macOS","ARM64","cua-ci"]`

To roll back, delete the variable.

## Testing

- All workflow YAML parses; `actionlint` is clean on the changed workflows; `test_ci_swift_samples_scope.py` passes (22 tests).
- Not run on real self-hosted runners yet. After merge, check one same-repo PR with the variable unset (hosted), then set it and re-check (self-hosted), then a fork PR (hosted).

title: ci: build only the amd64 slim image on PRs (CUA-2445)
body:
Linear: CUA-2445 (item 9 of the CI speed plan, #5846 / CUA-2335)

**What changes for users:** PRs wait less on the Linux image build. A PR that does not change the image definitions or build scripts builds only the amd64 slim image instead of arm64 plus every tier (31 to 40 min each).

## Change (`cd-image-linux.yml` only)

- `meta` decides the scope. On `pull_request` it reads the PR file list. It builds the full matrix when a file is under `libs/images/` or `scripts/images/`, is one of the image build sources already in this workflow's path filter (`image_build.rs`, `image_release.rs`, `sandbox/bake.rs`, `cua-image` `canonical.rs`/`publish.rs`, `cua-vmm` `density.rs`/`qemu/`), or is `cd-image-linux.yml` / `image-doctor.yml`. If the file list cannot be read, it builds the full matrix.
- Otherwise (for example a `libs/cua-spacesd/**` only PR): `spacesd` and `cli` build amd64 only, `release` runs amd64 slim only, and `plain` and `docker-bake` are skipped.
- Push (tags), `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call` (releases) keep the full matrix. The workflow has no `merge_group` trigger, and `ci-gate` only waits on `pull_request` runs, so the queue is unchanged.
- Job names, path filters and `ci-gate` are untouched. Skipped jobs count as skipped, as before.

## Larger runners

This workflow runs on standard `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners, not `cua-linux-16core`, so this change saves wall time but little or no larger-runner spend. The remaining `cua-linux-16core` jobs (Nix lanes in `ci-nix-linux.yml`, `rust (ubuntu)` in `ci-cua-sdk.yml`, the five build jobs in `e2e-cua-sdk.yml`) are all cargo or Nix compiles and test runs, not light lint jobs, so none were moved. Mac jobs (#6046) are untouched.

Checked with `actionlint`.

body:

Head `db2d8f5ab08a20399a11428fd97cdacd4b1dd894` fixes only rustfmt layout in `scroll.rs`: the long Unknown string arm is wrapped in a plain block, and one alignment gap is removed. No dispatch, observation, label, or test behavior changes.

## Summary
Correct the reported transport and activation evidence for **macOS targeted pixel-wheel scroll only**. The wheel actuator posts PID-routed CGEvents, but legacy result inference can turn a requested foreground mode into reported foreground/global-HID delivery even when activation was not observed.

- Keep the legacy foreground helper's boolean as `activation attempted`, preserving existing caller abort/rollback behavior.
- Add an internal observation result for this wheel path. AX focus alone is insufficient; foreground is reported only when the app-local focused window and the dispatch-time WindowServer front-process sample both match. Otherwise use the already-supported `Unknown` delivery state.

This does not implement the broad lifecycle/guaranteed restoration proposal in #2206 and does not close it. #2446 addresses interactive scroll routing; #4652 changes the separate foreground-HID activation helper for exact sibling-window focus. Neither is superseded or reimplemented here. No public schema, new capability, permission change, additional fallback or persistent activation is introduced. This is an unselected, focused bug-fix contribution pending maintainer review.

Other eight direct legacy-helper callers (AX click, two typing branches, AX scroll and four browser setup paths), keyboard-scroll, and the HID helper are not migrated. The dispatch-time sample is not proof of focus throughout the whole action or successful restoration.

title: test(cli): isolate the Windows low-disk guard test from QEMU availability
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Since #5755, a VM create on Windows is refused when QEMU is not installed, and that check comes before the disk guard. So on GitHub's Windows runner, which has no QEMU, `low_disk_guard_fails_typed_with_a_prune_hint` got exit 1 instead of the expected exit 7. While this PR was open, main (#6151) worked around that by skipping the test on Windows with `#[cfg(not(windows))]`. Merged as-is, that skip would remove the whole test on Windows, and the placeholder setup in this PR would never run.
- What changed: The branch is brought up to date with main through a `Merge main` merge commit. On Windows the test now writes discovery-only `qemu-system-<arch>.exe` and `qemu-img.exe` placeholders into its isolated `CUA_HOME/bin`, where `cua_vmm::host::which` looks. The QEMU check then passes, and the disk guard refuses with exit 7, "insufficient disk" and the `cua cache prune` hint. The test is no longer skipped on Windows. These placeholders are now the only Windows handling for this test. On a host whose own preflight refuses a VM, the test returns early, because the create is refused there before the disk guard and nothing it checks is reachable. That covers a Mac that cannot run virtual machines (#6323; GitHub's macOS runners are VMs) and a PC with the Windows Hypervisor Platform off. The test asks the same preflight checks the create asks, with the disk left to the guard, and adds `cua-create-failure` as a dev-dependency of `cua-cli` for them. The assertions are unchanged: exit 7, the error text, the prune hint, and no instance directory.

## Related work

Refs #5755, #6151, #6323. CUA-3170.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none. Test-only change (plus a `cua-cli` dev-dependency); no production code, preflight order or release entry changes. Linux and Macs that can run VMs run this test exactly as before.
- Risk and rollback: low. The placeholders stay inside the test's temporary home. Rollback is reverting the test commit.
- CI failures seen before the merge were not caused by this PR, which changes only the `cua-cli` test, its dev-dependencies and the lockfile:
  - The `CuaBackedTests.swift:223` failure and `dump_docs::tests::help_snapshots` are fixed on main (#6151, #6078), and the merge brings those fixes in.

That step stays red on main until #7508 (tracked in #7638) lands.
- Fifth update: merged current main (262 commits, no conflicts); `git diff origin/main...HEAD` still shows only the `cua-cli` test, its dev-dependency and the lockfile. At this head the quick scoped repository checks passed locally (rustfmt for `cua-cli`, cargo lockfiles, SPDX headers, image refs). The red jobs at the previous head ran on 16 Nov against a base 262 commits old; this PR's CI at the new head confirms Rust on Linux, Windows and macOS.

title: macOS native click/press on SwiftUI menu button returns before the menu is observable in the AX tree
body:
## Summary
macOS native `click` (AX `press`, background delivery) on a SwiftUI `Menu` button (`AXMenuButton`) returns success before the opened menu is observable in the AX tree. A snapshot taken immediately after the call has no menu items; a snapshot a moment later has them, and a screenshot shows the menu open. Please add a bounded, menu-specific completion/postcondition (or an explicit completion signal) for menu-opening presses.

## Environment
cua-driver-rs 0.38.0 (local build `0.38.0-local01` on the 0.38.0 base), macOS arm64. Driven via the native SDK by an external runner (eejd/swift-uirunner-broker 0.2.15), which maps its `press` to the element-token `click` tool with background delivery. Target app: SwiftUI, toolbar `Menu` exposed as `AXMenuButton` (identifier `library-create`).

## Observed (4/4 runs)
1. `click` (press) on the `AXMenuButton` → success, structured result `verified:false`, `effect:"unverifiable"` (`platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs`, ~lines 523-554).
2. Immediate snapshot, looking for `AXMenuItem` id `library-create-item`: 0 matches.
3. Next snapshot: window tree grows 27 → 35 elements, now including
   `AXMenu > AXMenuItem{id: library-create-item, label: "New Item"}`, `New Note`, `New Collection`. SwiftUI publishes two `AXMenu` nodes (one under the button, one sibling), so the menu count rises by 2.
4. Screenshot shows the menu open.

## Cause (from reading the source, not verified by tracing)
The background AX path returns right after `perform_ax_click`; the only post-action settle is the 800 ms WebKit delay for text inputs, and the foreground path sleeps a fixed 150 ms. Nothing waits for a menu opened by `AXMenuButton`/`AXPopUpButton`/`AXMenuBarItem`/`AXShowMenu`.

## Ask
For menu-opening targets, wait (bounded, ~1 s, non-failing) until the AX menu count exceeds the pre-action baseline or the target becomes `AXSelected`, and report the observation (e.g. in `effect`/structured output), or otherwise expose a completion signal. This is not a claim that a successful `click` promises a visible effect generally; it is about menu-opening presses where a follow-up snapshot is the natural next call.

Related downstream tracking: eejd/swift-uirunner-broker#171 (full diagnostics), fork issue eejd/rs-cua#10.
