title: [Bug]: a local create whose readiness check fails leaves its container running, though a failed create should delete it
body:
### Primary area

Containers or images

### Summary

On macOS with Docker Desktop, when `cua sb create` fails its readiness check (here a `--wait` port nobody listens on), it
exits 1 but leaves the container running. `--keep-on-failure` is documented as "Default: a failed create deletes it."
`cua sb list` then shows the sandbox as `ready`, and `cua sb exec` / `get` say `not found`. Ctrl-C during the same wait
does delete it (`cancelled: removed t4`). This happens with or without `--name`.

### Reproduction

```bash
pip install -U cua-sandbox   # cua 0.9.0, cua-sandbox 0.9.1; Python 3.13
cua sb create linux --tier slim --name t2 --port web=9999 --wait tcp:web --ready-timeout 20; echo "rc=$?"
cua sb list
docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}  {{.Status}}'
cua sb exec t2 true; echo "exec rc=$?"
```

### Expected behavior

The create fails and deletes the container it made (no `--keep-on-failure` given), as it does on Ctrl-C.

### Actual behavior

```
cua: local runtime: [local] sandbox 't2' was not ready after 20s: probe Tcp { port: 9999 } never passed
rc=1

ID        STATUS  LOCATION  KIND       RUNTIME
local:t2  ready   local     container  runc

t2  Up 26 seconds

cua: not found: sandbox t2
exec rc=3
```

The container keeps running until `cua sb delete -f t2`. An agent that retries a failing create leaves one running
container per attempt (each with the 4 GiB / 2 CPU limits from the create).

Same flags, Ctrl-C during "Waiting for its services":
```
Cancelling...
cua: cancelled: removed t4
rc=130
```
`t4` is gone from `cua sb list` and `docker ps -a`.

Same without `--name`: `sb-96564f13` was left running after the timeout; Ctrl-C removed `sb-3e39bbbe`.

### Environment

- macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), Docker Desktop 4.97.0 (engine 29.9.2), runc (no runsc)
- cua 0.9.0, cua-sandbox 0.9.1 (pip), Python 3.13.3
- Code read at main `8fbdf83c1`

### Evidence

From main `8fbdf83c1`:
- The error comes from `cua-vmm`'s container start: `probe Tcp { port: 9999 } never passed` with no address is the
  detail built at `libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/container/mod.rs:2460`.
- That start runs before `Sandboxes::create` reaches its cleanup: `let sandbox = sandbox?;` at
  `libs/cua/crates/cua-sandbox-core/src/sandbox.rs:817` returns the error, and the "A failed create deletes what it
  made" block at `:844` only covers the core's own `wait_ready` / `wait_spacesd` afterwards.
- The Ctrl-C path deletes through `cancel_create` (`cua-cli/src/sandbox.rs`), which is why it differs.
- `libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/spaces.rs:2823` describes the same gap ("a readiness probe that never passed leaves
  a running VM no registry lists") and deletes by name after the failure, but only for generated names. The CLI docs
  say any failed create is deleted unless `--keep-on-failure`, so `cua sb create` (named or not) doesn't match them.

### Workaround and additional context

- `cua sb delete -f <name>` removes the leftover (worked for a running and a stopped one).
- A second trigger on older Docker Desktop (4.41.2, engine 28.1.1): plain `cua sb create linux --tier slim` failed 3/3
  with `probe port 3211 is not published by this sandbox`, leaving the same running orphan. A direct-socket check showed
  that Docker Desktop fills in the ephemeral host port 5–16 ms after `start` returns there, and CUA reads it once right
  after start (`endpoints_from`). On 4.97.0 the port is there at the first read, so that trigger is gone; noting it in
  case older Docker Desktop matters to you.
- Happy to send a PR: run the same cleanup when `create_local` returns a readiness failure (still honouring
  `keep_on_failure` and pre-existing sandboxes), with a test that a create whose probe never passes leaves no container.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): print get_guide text from the call command
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `cua-driver call get_guide ...` never shows the guide. `call` prints a tool's structured JSON and leaves its text blocks out. That suits most tools, because their text only repeats the structured data. `get_guide` is the exception: the guide is a text block, and the structured content is only its metadata (topic, platform, sources).
- What changed: `call` gains an opt-in `--text` flag that prints the result's text blocks instead of the JSON. A result with no text blocks falls back to the normal output. Without the flag the output is unchanged.

## Related work

Refs: none. I did not find an existing issue or pull request for this.

RFC: not opened. The flag is additive and opt-in, and the default output does not change, so I treated this as not a contract change. If you want an RFC for a new CLI flag, say so and I will open one.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: a new opt-in CLI flag, `--text`, on `call`. Default output, exit codes, and the daemon and MCP protocol are unchanged, so scripts that parse the JSON keep working.
- Risk and rollback: low. The change is output selection in the CLI only (`render_call_stdout`). Reverting the commit removes the flag.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: output selection moved into `render_call_stdout` so it can be tested without a daemon. Seven unit tests cover the new flag and the behavior it must not change (structured-only output, text-only output, image merging, empty results). Breaking the flag fails the two tests that assert on its output. `cargo test -p cua-driver --locked`: 468 passed, 0 failed. `rustfmt --check` is clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: on macOS 27.2 against a running daemon, `cua-driver call --text get_guide '{"topic":"browser"}'` prints the guide text, and the same call without `--text` prints the same JSON as before. The change is in the shared CLI crate and the tests do not depend on the platform. I have not run it on Windows or Linux.
- Known gaps or CI still required: I ran the tests with rustc 1.99.1. The repo pins 1.97.1, so CI is the check on the pinned version.

title: hyprland-plugin: primary-seat fallback for Chromium/Electron
body:
## Problem

Background input doesn't work in Chrome or Electron apps on Hyprland (Figma, Slack, Obsidian). Chromium only binds the *first* `wl_seat` it sees, so it never binds the agent seats and every click or key fails with `client_not_bound` (#4833).

## Why not lazy agent seats

I read the decision on #4257 (create agent seats per session, never fall back to the user's seat). That fixes apps that keep the *last* seat, like imv and Zed, but Chromium ignores every seat after the first one (`WaylandSeat::Instantiate` returns early once a seat is bound), so an agent seat created later still never reaches it. For Chrome/Electron there's no agent seat to wait for.

## Solution

An explicit escape hatch, off by default: `plugin:cua:primary_seat_fallback`. When the target has no agent seat, input goes to that app's own resources on the user's seat, without changing focus or moving the cursor, and never while the user is in that same app. Keys are mapped to the user's keymap.

I know this goes against "never fall back to the user's seat", so happy to close this if you'd rather keep that rule. Just wanted to show it's the only way I found to reach Chrome/Electron.

## Testing

Hyprland 0.56.2, Chromium 152/153, with another window focused:
- off: `client_not_bound`, nothing arrives
- on: clicks, drags, typing (us and no/mac) and Ctrl+A all land; focus stays put
- also works in the Figma and Obsidian apps
- select popups, context menus, drag-and-drop and window-move drags: the user's pointer and keyboard are never grabbed, and Hyprland refuses the move
- ctest passes

My coding agent found this and wrote most of it; I reviewed and tested it.

title: fix(cua-driver): type desktop text as physical keys behind keyboard event taps
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: with Karabiner-Elements' CGEventTap fallback on, desktop-scope `type_text` types every character as `a` (#5779). The driver posts each character as key code 0 with the text attached as a Unicode string. Karabiner's tap rebuilds the event from the key code and flags, the string is lost, and key code 0 is `a`.
- What changed: a macOS daemon started with `CUA_DRIVER_TEXT_KEY_EVENTS=physical` types desktop-scope text by pressing the US-keyboard key for each character, with Shift where needed. It uses the existing `type_text_physical_global`, the same path Screen Sharing text already takes. Text with a character that has no US key (`é`, emoji) is refused with `physical_key_unavailable` before any key is sent; it does not fall back to Unicode. A value other than `unicode` or `physical` refuses with `text_key_events_invalid`. Unset keeps the current behavior.

On #5779 the maintainer suggested a gated delivery mode. I gated it at daemon launch instead of adding a `type_text` argument. The tap affects every app on the Mac, and the driver can see that Karabiner is running but not whether the fallback is on, so an agent has no way to know when to pass a per-call flag. Whoever turned the fallback on does know. It also leaves the MCP schema alone.

The driver already reads host-level input settings this way. `CUA_DRIVER_KEY_GAP_MS` (`key_pacing.rs`), `CUA_DRIVER_BATCH_PACING` (`step_pacing.rs`) and `CUA_DRIVER_WINDOW_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_MS` / `_POLL_MS` (`window_observation.rs`) are defined in `cua-driver-core`, read only from the daemon environment, documented in `EMBEDDING.md`, and passed through by `EmbeddedCuaDriverHost`. The new variable follows the same pattern. If a per-call option fits better, I can switch.

Docs: `EMBEDDING.md`, `use-the-sdk.mdx`, and a troubleshooting entry for the `a` symptom. A daemon started on demand inherits the environment of whatever starts it (`open` passes the caller's environment; `launchctl setenv` doesn't reach it), so the entry says to export the variable where the MCP client starts, or set it in the LaunchAgent plist.

## Related work

Refs #5779

Two paths from the issue are not affected by this PR and still type `a` behind the tap:

- `cua do type`: cua-spacesd always adds `pid` and `window_id`, so it uses window-targeted `type_text`, not the desktop path.
- The Cua Spaces viewer, which types through `commit_text` in `interactive.rs`.

Covering them means carrying the setting through cua-spacesd and the viewer's input session, which crosses components, so that would need an RFC.

RFC: not required for this PR. It adds no tool argument, config key or result field.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only, and only for a daemon started with the variable set. Window-targeted typing is unchanged. Linux and Windows don't read the variable.
- Risk and rollback: low. The default path is unchanged. Revert the commits.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - macOS 26.7.2, Apple M4, on `653a6aff`: `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` passed (640 passed, 7 ignored), including `desktop_text_takes_the_host_selected_key_events`, `physical_desktop_text_refuses_a_character_without_a_us_key` (asserts `physical_key_unavailable` for `é`, `U+00E9`) and `invalid_text_key_events_setting_refuses_desktop_text` (asserts `text_key_events_invalid`). `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib text_key_events`: 3 passed. [`CI: Rust macOS unit`](https://github.com/stanley50z/cua/actions/runs/40615174185) also passed on `16ad1ea3`.
  - Windows: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver-sdk --lib` passed (1075 + 92), including `embedded::tests::text_key_events_env_propagates`, which failed before the allowlist change.
  - Local runs of the docs and pre-push CI on the Mac at `653a6aff`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, SPDX headers, generated docs current (`Cua Driver (macOS registry) reference is up to date`), docs generator tests (119), code-block lint, CLI-shape and config lanes, internal links, hygiene, structure, `pnpm build:budget`, the em-dash check and docs page tests (23) all pass. `cargo clippy -D warnings` reports one `single_match` in `ax/reveal_scroll.rs`, which is already on `main`; nothing in the changed files.
- Manual or platform evidence: same Mac, Karabiner-Elements 16.3.0, `CuaDriverLocal.app` built from `16ad1ea3` by `libs/cua-driver/scripts/install-local.sh`. Each run cleared a TextEdit document through accessibility, called `type_text '{"scope":"desktop","text":...}'` with TextEdit in front, and read the text area back through accessibility.

  | Karabiner fallback | `CUA_DRIVER_TEXT_KEY_EVENTS` | Typed | Read back |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | off | unset | `xyz` | `xyz` |
  | on | unset | `xyz` | `aaa` (the bug) |
  | on | `physical` | `xyz` | `xyz` |
  | on | `physical` | `Hello, World! 123 (a+b)?` | `Hello, World! 123 (a+b)?` |
  | on | `physical` | `café` | refused: `physical_key_unavailable`, `U+00E9`, `delivered_chars: 0`; field stays empty |

  The run also showed that the `key_events` field I had added to the success result never reaches clients: successful actions publish the closed `ActionResult` contract. `653a6aff` removes the field and the doc sentence about it. That, the doc fix, and `99bf1ffd` (the same `EMBEDDING.md` section in the bundled copy `libs/cua/skills/cua-driver/`) are the only changes after `16ad1ea3`. The typing path is the same code, so I didn't repeat the manual runs.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the desktop E2E matrix hasn't run. It doesn't set the variable, so it covers only the unchanged default path.

body:
## Problem and correction

Strict Windows clippy reports nine baseline diagnostics across Driver core,
cursor themes and the testkit. This focused cleanup:

- Passes the generated desktop name directly to the generic `wide` helper.

No existing Windows test is disabled, no lint is suppressed, and no public API
changes. Runtime defaults, paths and handle ownership remain the same. This PR
is based directly on upstream main and is independent of `select_text`.

## Validation

Candidate: `06012f69f90216dc1b074bffd2c6e5e75e09dc66`.

- macOS core unit suite: 1089 passed, one existing opt-in ignored.
- macOS testkit library: 113 passed, one existing opt-in ignored.

- Strict macOS clippy for all three changed crates, Rustfmt, SPDX and diff checks pass.
- [Original Windows proof](https://github.com/Veer376/cua/actions/runs/40570034340): compile/unit/protocol checks pass; additional strict clippy reports the first seven baseline diagnostics.
- [First cleanup proof](https://github.com/Veer376/cua/actions/runs/40634945570): those seven diagnostics clear; compilation then exposes the two cursor/testkit diagnostics also corrected here.
- [Broader Windows diagnostic](https://github.com/Veer376/cua/actions/runs/40635603366): final-candidate core units pass (1072 passed, one existing opt-in ignored). title: fix(cua-driver): report a text field's placeholder apart from its value
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `get_window_state` falls back to `AXPlaceholderValue` when a text field's `AXValue` is empty, so an empty field reads as filled with its hint text (#3786). #6893 added the raw `placeholder` to `elements[]`, but `value` and the tree row still carry the hint.
- What changed: `value` is now the raw `AXValue`, never the placeholder.
  - The tree row shows the hint in the bracketed metadata while the field is empty, next to `id=` and `help=`.
  - `label` still falls back to the placeholder after title, description and value, so an empty field keeps a readable name.
  - `elements[].placeholder` is #6893's and is unchanged.

Before and after, for an empty field with a hint (from the unit tests, not a live capture):

```
main:   - [3] AXTextField = "Type here…" [id=txt-input actions=[confirm]]
branch: - [3] AXTextField [id=txt-input placeholder="Type here…" actions=[confirm]]
```

A filled field renders as before: `- [3] AXTextField = "hello" [id=txt-input actions=[confirm]]`.

## Related work

Refs #3786

Refs, not Fixes: this covers the placeholder half of the issue. Whitespace trimming of non-empty values is unchanged (see Known gaps).

#3787 by @will-bogusz fixed this before it was closed as stale; this keeps only its placeholder part. #6893 added the raw `placeholder` field this builds on.

RFC: not needed. No output field is added, removed or renamed; `value` stops carrying the hint.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Windows and Linux never put the placeholder in `value`.
  - A disabled (non-indexed) empty field now renders as a bare `- AXTextField` row instead of `= "hint"`, because bracketed metadata only shows on indexed rows, as with `help=`. The row is kept and its `elements[]` entry still has the placeholder.
  - `verify_state` with `value_equals: ""` on an empty field now returns Unknown instead of Unsatisfied, because `value` is omitted when empty (existing test `elements_omit_empty_value`).
  - A filled field's tree row does not show its placeholder. `elements[]` still reports it, as on main.
- Risk and rollback: revert the commits.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 806 passed, 1 failed, 13 ignored, including the 3 new tests. The failure is `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`, which reads macOS's own button labels; this PR doesn't touch that file.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver`: 410 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. I didn't capture a live before/after on a real field. The issue's table (0.28.0, AppKit fixture) shows the before.
- Known gaps or CI still required: trimming whitespace from non-empty values (`" \tΩ café\n"`) is left for a follow-up.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): enforce machine slots during concurrent joins
body:
## Summary

Concurrent machine joins can exceed a static token's configured limit. The failure recorded in #6083 is `9 online, wanted 8`. A generation is allocated before taking the machine-registry lock, so its order can differ from insertion order: a lower generation arriving at a full registry still passes the old rank check.

Check occupied slots and insert under the same lock. Exclude the machine being replaced from the count, retaining reconnect replacement at capacity and the existing per-token scope. The existing reconnect-storm test and its assertions remain unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #6083. Scope and acceptance evidence: https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/6083#issuecomment-6469144344.

This corrects the existing machine-count invariant; it introduces no SDK, CLI, protocol, or permission contract. No RFC is required for this bounded correction.

## Compatibility and risk

The change affects registration after WebSocket upgrade. Existing occupants retain their slots; a rejected join follows the existing close-and-retry path. Same-machine reconnect replacement remains allowed at capacity. There is no state-file or schema migration; rollback is a code revert.

## Validation

- A deterministic regression using generations `2, 3, 1` fails against the original rank-based admission logic with only its insertion block extracted. It reports three stored machines for a limit of two. The replacement-at-capacity control passes before and after the fix.
- With the fix, all 11 `server::tests` tests pass on Linux with Rust 1.97.1.
- The full relay suites pass: **287 tests with all features** and **213 tests with default features**, with no failures or ignored tests. Both include the real reconnect-storm tests.
- The formerly flaky capacity/reconnect test passes **25 consecutive executions without retries**.
- Pre-push checks pass: SPDX headers, component Rust formatting, and strict Clippy. The original Linux pre-push run skipped Windows cross-Clippy because cargo-xwin was unavailable; native Windows tests and Clippy have now been run as recorded below.
- Native Windows validation on `d53b7577457e` with Rust 1.97.1: the full all-feature `cua-relay` crate suite passes **268 tests**, with zero failures. One Linux-native TLS/OpenSSL test is intentionally ignored on Windows. Strict all-target Clippy also passes with `-D warnings`. This includes the generation-order and replacement-at-capacity regressions.
- Required upstream CI and native macOS evidence remain pending. This draft changes no desktop/input behavior and runs no host-input tests.
- The native Windows **default-feature** build also passes **197 tests**, with zero failures and the same one Linux-only test intentionally ignored. Strict all-target Clippy passes with default features as well. These results cover the self-hosted build separately from the hosted-feature configuration.

Reproduce the focused check from `libs/cua-spacesd`:

```sh
cargo +1.97.1 test --locked -p cua-relay --all-features --lib server::tests::
```

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the current diff.

title: fix(cua-driver): give a macOS text input the keyboard focus when a background pixel click's AXPress leaves it unfocused
body:
On macOS, a background pixel `click` on a text input that its `AXPress` leaves unfocused now also gives it the keyboard focus, as a real click on a field does.

**Problem.** A background left click at a point first runs the AX hit-test backend, which performs `AXPress` on the element there. A Qt `QLineEdit` accepts `AXPress` and returns success without taking the focus. The click then reports `✅ PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX.`, but the keyboard focus stays in the field that had it.

In a chat-like Qt window with a search line edit and a chat input that holds the focus, `click` on the search field followed by `type_text` put the text into the chat input. The value read-back even reported `effect: confirmed`, because it reads the focused element. One Return away from sending the search text as a message.

**Fix.** After a successful `AXPress` on a text input (`AXTextField`, `AXTextArea`, `AXComboBox`, `AXSearchField`, the roles `type_text` already treats as text inputs), the click checks whether the element is the app's focused element. If it is not, the click sets `AXFocused` on it, the same write the pixel `focus` action uses.
- Elements that are not text inputs are untouched; for them the focus is not even read.
- Text inputs the press already focused are untouched too.
- AppKit text fields mostly decline `AXPress` and take the routed CGEvent path as before.

**Testing.**
- New unit test: `tools::click::tests::a_pressed_text_input_without_the_focus_takes_it`.
- On a macOS 26.5 VM with a Qt 6 Widgets fixture (search `QLineEdit`, chat `QPlainTextEdit` holding the focus, app in the background, also on a second display):
  - before this change, `click` on the search field and then `type_text "cmgs"` put the text in the chat input (1/1 on each display);
  - `click` with `action: "focus"` at the same point (the `AXFocused` write this change adds) and then `type_text` put the text in the search field.

Platforms: macOS only.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib tools::click` and `tools::type_text` pass on a macos-15-intel runner.

title: fix(cua-driver): a Linux launch settles on the window of a process its launcher forked, and a command line matches by its program
body:
On Linux, `launch_app` settles on a window of a process the launcher forked, and a command line matches a window class by its program instead of its last argument.

**Problem.**
- LibreOffice's launcher stays alive as `oosplash` while the `soffice.bin` it forked draws the window. The launcher never owns a window and never exits, so `launch_app` with `libreoffice --calc /tmp/x.ods` or `localc` waited the whole 20 s starting budget although Calc was up in about 0.6 s.
- The class match took its stem from the last path segment of the whole command line (`x.ods` for `libreoffice --calc /tmp/x.ods`), so a command line with a file argument matched no window, and a hand-off to an already running instance timed out.

**Fix.**
- A new window whose pid descends from the launcher's pid (parent chain read from `/proc/<pid>/stat`) settles the launch, as a window of the launcher itself does.
- The stem comes from the program, the first word of the command line, so `libreoffice --calc /tmp/x.ods` matches `libreoffice-calc` and `/usr/bin/gedit --new-window` matches `Gedit`.

**Testing.**
- New unit tests: `a_window_of_a_process_the_launcher_forked_is_the_launch`, `a_child_process_descends_from_this_one_and_not_the_reverse`; the class-match cases in `launch_resolution_tests.rs` gain command lines with paths and flags.
- On an Ubuntu 24.04 XFCE desktop with LibreOffice: `localc` and `libreoffice --calc <file>` settle in about 0.23 s instead of 20.07 s; a hand-off to a running Writer settles in 0.22 s instead of the 8 s refusal.

Platforms: Linux only.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `xvfb-run -a cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` (726 passed).

title: fix(cua-driver): the macOS background left-click route stamps the window-local point a real click carries as the event's window location
body:
On macOS, the background left-click route stamps the window-local point as each event's window location, as WindowServer does for a real click, instead of the screen point.

**Problem.** `chromium_click_route_plan` stamps the move, down and up events with the screen point through `CGEventSetWindowLocation`, on both the SkyLight and the public PID route. A real click carries the point local to the target window in that field. An app that reads the field puts the background click off by the window's origin: WeChat 4.1 on a two-display Mac clicked a fixed offset away from the target, and the offset equalled the window's origin.

**Fix.** The route plan gives the move, down and up events the window-local point (already passed in as `win_local_x`/`win_local_y`) for both the SkyLight and the public window location. The event location stays the screen point, and the off-screen primer keeps (-1, -1). The doc comments on the route and on `px_frame` say the same.

**Testing.**
- `input::mouse::tests::background_route_stamps_the_window_local_point_a_real_click_carries` (the former `capture_bound_background_route_preserves_nonzero_origin_hit`) now expects the window-local point in both window-location fields.
- On a Mac with WeChat 4.1 behind another window, background clicks on chat rows with this change landed on the target row 3 of 4 times; the fourth, the first click after the driver was swapped, had no effect and hit no other row.

Platforms: macOS only.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` (662 passed) on a macos-26 runner.



Rebased on main after #5492. #5492 stamps the window-local point only on macOS 27. This PR drops that version check: WeChat 4.1 on macOS 26 (two-display Mac) reads the field too and clicks off by the window's origin without it.

title: windows: print id= and enabled= on display-only rows in get_window_state
body:
On Windows, `get_window_state` reads the AutomationId of every node but only prints it on actionable rows.

`platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs`, `format_node_line`:

```rust
if let Some(idx) = node.element_index {
    // - [N] Type "Name" [value=... id=... actions=...]   <- has id=
} else {
    // - Type "Name" = "Value"                            <- no id=
}
```

`emit_cached_node` already fills in `node.automation_id` (and `enabled`) for display-only nodes. Those values just never get printed. That causes problems in two cases:

**1. Read-only labels.** A WinForms `Label` with `AutomationId=lblAgent` that shows `RP-20417` prints as `- Text "RP-20417"`, so you can't tell *which* label it is. On 0.37.0, a window with five `Text` rows that all have AutomationIds prints `id=` on none of them.

**2. Disabled controls.** When a modal opens, WinForms disables the owner window. `detect_cached_actions` returns nothing for disabled elements, so every control in that window becomes display-only and loses its `id=`. An `Edit` that printed as `[4] Edit "..." [value="..." id=dtReturn ...]` one snapshot earlier now prints as `- Edit "..." = "..."`. A client can't check the value it just typed until the dialog closes.

Your e2e already notes a related problem (`harness_wpf_test`: "a structured projection that omits display-only nodes cannot prove absence").

### Why the id matters here

Text isn't a reliable way to find an element. It's whatever data the form is showing at the moment, like a name, a date or a fee. Two fields can show the same thing, and the text changes whenever someone types. The AutomationId is the one thing that stays the same.

Example: in a library desktop app, the agent changes a book's return time and clicks Save. The app pops up "Late fee change — Continue?" with Cancel and Continue buttons. Before clicking Continue, the agent wants to check that the date it typed actually landed in the book-return-time field (AutomationId `dtReturn`). But the modal has disabled the main window, so that field now prints as a plain row with no id, and the agent can't tell which Edit is which. It has to click Continue without checking.

### Change

Display-only rows now also print `id=` and `enabled=`. Nothing else changes: these rows still have no index, no token and no actions. Rows that have neither field print exactly as before.

The staff-ID label at the top of the form (a read-only WinForms `Label`, AutomationId `lblAgent`):

```
before:  - Text "RP-20417"
after:   - Text "RP-20417" [id=lblAgent enabled=true]
```

The book-return-time field while the "Late fee change" modal is open (AutomationId `dtReturn`, disabled because its window is behind the modal):

```
before:  - Edit "Book return time" = "10/29/2026 10:15 AM"
after:   - Edit "Book return time" = "10/29/2026 10:15 AM" [id=dtReturn enabled=false]
```

Unit tests cover both rows above, plus a row with no id or enabled state and an actionable row, to show those two print the same as before.

Possible follow-up: include display-only rows in the structured `elements[]` with `element_token: null`, so `automation_id` and `enabled` are available there too.

### Repro

cua-driver 0.37.0, Windows Server 2022, any WinForms window with a labeled `Label`:

```
'{"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<hwnd>,"full_output":true,"include_screenshot":false}' | cua-driver get_window_state
```

`Text` rows have no `id=` and aren't in `elements[]`. Open a modal from the window and run it again: controls that had an index lose `[N]` and `id=`.

title: fix(spaces): Set up says Ready only after cua-driver is found and answers (CUA-1797, CUA-2769)
body:
**For users:** in Cua Spaces, Set up for background computer use now says Ready only when Cua Driver is installed and answering. Before, it said "done" even when the driver was missing, and agents then failed to start it.

Supersedes #5337 by @ddupont808, rebased onto current main with credit; his commit is kept as-is with him as author. Linear: [CUA-2769](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-2769) (part 1 of 6 under CUA-2706, "Cua Driver ships inside Cua Spaces").

## What #5337 does (unchanged)

- `cua-agent-setup` gains a `driver` module. `locate` finds cua-driver on the PATH, in `~/.local/bin`, or inside `CuaDriver.app`. `check` passes only when `cua-driver mcp` answers an MCP `initialize`. `ensure` installs cua-driver with its signed release installer when it's missing or broken.
- `setup_cua_driver` writes the MCP server only by absolute path, and only after `check` passes. Otherwise the agent's row fails with the reason and its config stays as it was. Re-running Set up repairs entries that point at a missing binary.
- The SDK's `AgentSetup.setup_cua_driver`, used by the Set up button, calls `ensure` first. The web card shows the reason in full instead of cutting it off.
- `cua agents setup --cua-driver` no longer writes a bare `cua-driver` entry.

See #5337 for Dillon's end-to-end verification on a spare Mac.

## What changed in the rebase

- `OnboardingView.swift` was deleted on main (#6079). The Swift part of #5337 is dropped, because both apps now show Set up through the shared web card, which this PR still updates.
- Tests added on main since then passed a driver path that doesn't exist: the uninstall tests that keep Cua Driver's entries, the Local channel tests, and "rerun changes nothing". Those tests now use a stand-in driver that answers `initialize` (`tests/common/mod.rs`). Those that need it are Unix-only, as Dillon's were.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-agent-setup`: all suites pass. `cargo clippy -p cua-agent-setup --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- Left to CI: `cua-cli` and `cua-sdk` (too heavy for the machine I'm on).

## What's next in the stack

This PR keeps the standalone CuaDriver.app as the fallback install. Later PRs bundle a pinned driver inside Cua Spaces (part 2) and run it as Cua Spaces' own child, so there's one app to allow in System Settings (parts 3–4).

body: **For users:** nothing changes yet, because all of this is behind a switch that's off. Once the backend ships and the switch is on, Cua Driver gets its own place in Cua Spaces: - a Cua Driver page under Machines; - a "Meet Cua Driver" step in the first run, with a live test; - "Agents can use this Mac" in the top bar on every page. Linear: [CUA-2775](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-2775), part of CUA-2706. Stacked on #6145. Scope, per Francesco: variations A and E. C, a status line for each machine in Machines, is on hold. You can still open another computer's driver page from the "Your computers" list on the A page. ## What's built (apps/cua-spaces-web) **A: the Cua Driver page** (`/driver`, a sidebar item under Machines): - The brand keycap and the line "Lets agents see and use the apps on this computer." - The state ("Working on this Mac.", with the last test) and the version. - **Update to x.y.z**, shown only when the backend reports an update (CUA-2776). - **Test now**, and **Pause agents**, which hides when the host can't pause. - A live preview of the agent pointer that follows the settings below. - **Agent pointer** settings: - show the pointer; - style (`cursor.motion.style`); - float (`cursor.float`); - marks (`cursor.marks`); - tilt (`cursor.rotate`); - name tag (`cursor.badges`). A row hides when the driver doesn't report its key, so drivers from before #6142 show fewer rows. - **Coding apps**: Claude Code, Codex and T3 Code. T3 Code brings its own driver, so it has no switch. If a person has their own `cua-driver` entry, the app leaves it alone and shows it read-only. - **Permissions**: the two switches in System Settings, both given to Cua Spaces. Allow opens them through the existing System Settings guide. - **Your computers**: every computer with a Cua Driver. Each one opens its own page (`/driver?machine=`). **E: the first run.** After Welcome there are three steps. "Not now" skips them. 1. "Meet Cua Driver" explains what it is. 2. "Turn on Cua Spaces" opens the real System Settings pane through `host.openSettings`, then waits for the switches. Nothing on screen imitates macOS. 3. "Watch the agent move" runs the live test, then offers Continue or Change the pointer. **E: the top bar.** "Agents can use this Mac" (or "Agents paused", or "Agents can't use this Mac yet") opens a small panel with: - which agent is using which app, with Pause; - the pointer switch; - Update, when one is ready; - a link to the Cua Driver settings. ## Behind the switch - A new flag, `spaces_embedded_driver`, is off by default. Testers can turn it on for one device in Settings → Advanced → Labs. It is the UI side of `CUA_SPACESD_EMBEDDED_DRIVER=1`. - New bridge operations live in `src/bridge/ops/driver.ts`: `driver.status`, `driver.list`, `driver.config`, `driver.setConfig`, `driver.test`, `driver.pause`, `driver.setApp` and `driver.update`. They map onto `EmbeddedDriver` in #6145: `status()`, `get_config()`, `set_config()`, `permissions()` and `live_test()`. - `driver.setConfig` takes `set_config` keys. The one exception is `agent_cursor.enabled`, which the host turns into `set_agent_cursor_enabled`. - The demo host answers these operations. The SwiftUI, Electron and Tauri hosts reject them as unsupported until the app API PR routes them, and the coverage table records why. **So on a real host, nothing shows yet, even with the flag on.** ## Screenshots (demo mode) The Cua Driver page (A), light and dark: Another computer's page, opened from "Your computers": The first run (E): Meet Cua Driver, then waiting while you turn on Cua Spaces in System Settings, then the live test: The top-bar line and its panel (E): ## Checks - `pnpm typecheck` is clean. - `src/components/__tests__/driver.test.tsx` is new and has 8 tests. They cover: - the sidebar item appears only with the flag on and a host that answers; - the page's state, Update, Test now, pointer rows and coding apps; - Update hides with no update reported, and a pointer row hides when its key is missing; - a pointer change goes through `set_config`; - the top-bar line and its panel; - nothing is drawn on a host without the driver. - The bridge contract and coverage tests pass, with the shapes document regenerated. The design-language lint passes. - In the full `vitest run`, 19 tests fail: the same 19 that fail on the base branch, in agent-identity, agents-chat, space-header, space-thread and detail. This PR adds no new failures. - I did not run the Swift `BridgeContractTests` or the Electron contract tests. No host methods were added, so neither should be affected. ## Not in this PR - The app API that answers `driver.*` on the native hosts. That is the next PR under CUA-2775. - The in-place update flow (CUA-2776). - C (Machines rows), D (the menu bar section) and B (the Home card), which the brief defers. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cua-daemon): name a digest-pinned Lume image's digest once
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: a Lume create from `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26@sha256:<D>` added the resolved digest to a reference that already had it. The base VM key became `…:26@<D>@<D>`, so it missed the base already cached for the tag at `<D>`. `lume pull` was then handed a digest reference, which it rejects. The client still answered "Try again; it picks up where it stopped", but retrying can never work.
- What changed:
  - The Lume placement drops the input's own digest before adding the resolved one. A `tag@digest` create now uses the same base as the tag at that digest, and Lume still pulls by tag.
  - A digest-only reference is refused at placement with an `InvalidArgument` saying Lume needs a tag.
  - Lume's `ArgumentParser.ValidationError` is reported as an invalid request, not as a download to resume.

## Related work

Fixes #6137

## Compatibility and risk

- Impact:
  - Digest-pinned Lume creates now work and reuse cached bases.
  - Digest-only Lume references fail earlier, with a clearer message. They already failed before this change.
- Risk and rollback: this only touches Lume placement and the Lume pull error. Rollback is reverting the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cua-daemon/tests/placement.rs` now covers `tag@digest` and digest-only Lume references. The `tag@digest` case fails on main with the doubled digest.
  - The Lume client test covers the validation-error mapping.
  - `FakeRegistry` now serves `repo:tag@digest` by its digest, as a registry does. Before, that lookup fell back to the reference as given and hid the bug.
  - Passing: `cargo test` for cua-daemon, cua-vmm (lume) and cua-image, plus `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast` and clippy with `-D warnings`. One exception is cua-image's `containerdisk_private`, which needs 5 GiB of free disk and fails the same way on main on this machine.
- Manual or platform evidence: daemon log lines on Apple silicon showing the same `base_name` for the tag and `tag@digest` creates, to follow.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the post-pull digest check from the issue's "Related" section is left for a follow-up.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [ ] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

title: [Bug]: `cua do` against host fails with "missing or invalid bearer token" unless CUA_ENV_TOKEN is set (macOS, app-helper)
body:
### Primary area

CLI (`cua do`, host target)

### Summary

On a Mac whose host service runs as the Cua Spaces app helper, `cua do screenshot` against the `host` target always fails with `unauthenticated: missing or invalid bearer token`. It works only when the host's env token is passed through the environment (`CUA_ENV_TOKEN=... cua do --embedded screenshot`). It looks like `cua do` connects to the local cua-spacesd (127.0.0.1:3211) without the token, similar to #5073 for the viewer.

### Environment

- macOS, Apple silicon
- Cua Spaces 0.15.0 (auto-updated from 0.13.0 today), bundled cua 0.9.0, cua-spacesd 0.8.0
- Also tried standalone CLI cua 0.5.0: same result
- Host service: app-helper (moved into the Cua Spaces app with `cua host migrate` a few days ago)

### What happened

1. The daemon log repeated `HTTP 403 Forbidden: this device is not enrolled for your cua.ai account`.
2. Ran `cua auth login`, and the device now shows `enrolled` in `cua devices ls`.
3. Restarted Cua Spaces. The 403s are gone and the mesh connects directly.
4. `cua do screenshot` still fails:

```
❌ unauthenticated: unauthenticated: missing or invalid bearer token (Unauthenticated)
💻 host	🔍 zoom: off
```

### What I tried

- `cua do switch host` returned "Switched to host (local PC)", then the same error.
- `cua do --embedded screenshot` and `--daemon ~/.cua/cua.sock` gave the same error.
- `cua host setup` returned "Already set up ... Nothing to change", then the same error.
- `cua doctor`: 21 passed, 0 failed (Screen Recording and Accessibility granted).
- `cua host status`: online, desktop shared.
- cua-spacesd serves `127.0.0.1:3211` with `token=file:~/.cua/host/env-token`. driver.log shows no rejection entry.
- Debug trace: the client connects to 127.0.0.1:3211, gets response headers, then fails with Unauthenticated.

### Workaround

This works (the screenshot is saved):

```sh
CUA_ENV_TOKEN="$(cat ~/.cua/host/env-token)" cua do --embedded screenshot --save ~/.cua/screenshots/test.png
```

### Expected behavior

`cua do` on the `host` target picks up the local host's token by itself, without CUA_ENV_TOKEN.

### Additional context

- `~/.cua/host/host.json` `spaces_daemon.cua_bin` still points to `~/.local/bin/cua` (0.5.0), not the app's bundled binary. Not sure if related.
- Using cua-driver directly works fine.
- Related: #5073 (viewer connects to a direct Space without the stored token).

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials and private data from this report.

title: fix(cua-driver): the macOS key-window records never defocus the window they make key
body:
On macOS, `type_text` in the background no longer makes the target window lose and regain key when that window is already the app's key window.

**Problem.** Before posting keys, background `type_text` makes the addressed window the app's key window (`enter_exact_window_key`). It treats the window as settled only when `AXFocusedWindow` is the target and a focused element exists in it. An app that reports no focused element never settles, so the driver posts the key-window records on every call:
1. a defocus record for the current key window;
2. a focus record for the target;
3. the make-key pair.

After a background click, the current key window is the target itself. The app therefore sees its window resign and regain key about 120 ms before the first keyDown. A Qt app that resets its focus to a default field on window activation, e.g. WeChat for Mac, which exposes no focused element, moves the focus away from the field the click had just focused. The typed text then lands in the default field (WeChat's chat input instead of its search box).

**Fix.** `post_window_key_records` skips the defocus record when the current key window is the target. The focus record and the make-key pair are still posted, so an app that has to be primed still is.

**Why not skip the records entirely.** A LibreOffice Writer window launched in the background and never activated is key but has no focused element, the same reading as above. It drops every key until it gets the records. With the records skipped whenever the target is already the focused window, background typing into it failed 0/2. With only the self-defocus dropped, it worked 3/3 on an experiment build and 2/2 on this exact change.

**Testing.**
- New unit test: `input::skylight::key_prime_tests::the_key_records_never_defocus_the_window_they_make_key`.
- macOS 26.5 VM. Fixture: a Qt 6 `QRasterWindow` with no accessibility tree, a search box and a chat input, which moves its focus to the chat input on `focusIn`. The app is in the background behind another app. Background `click` on the search box, then `type_text "cmgs"`:

  | Driver | Text lands in | Fixture log between the click and the first key |
  |---|---|---|
  | before | chat input, 4/4 | `focusOut`, application inactive, application active, `focusIn`, focus reset to the chat input |
  | after | search box, 3/3 on this exact change, 4/4 on an experiment build of the same rule | no focus events |

- LibreOffice Writer launched in the background and never activated, `type_text` into its document: works before (1/1) and after (2/2).

Platforms: macOS only.

Checks: `cargo fmt -- --check`; `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib input::skylight` passes on a macos-15-intel runner.

title: feat(cua-driver): macOS background type_text and press_key take an opt-in locked_input flag that sends the keys while the screen is locked
body:
On macOS, background `type_text` and `press_key` take an opt-in per-call flag, `locked_input`, that sends the keys while the screen is locked instead of refusing with `screen_locked`. Without the flag, or with `locked_input: false`, nothing changes.

**Problem.** A locked session makes every background route refuse with `screen_locked`, since accessibility hides every window's contents. Not everything is blocked, though. With the display kept on, keys posted to the pid still reach the app's key window as it was before the lock. A caller that has already placed the focus can therefore keep typing, for example an agent that works while its user locks the Mac and steps away. Every other route stays blind.

**Fix.**
- `cua-driver-core`: `decide_background_input_under_lock` lets the pid-keyboard actions (`InsertText`, `GenericKey`, `ExactWindowKeys`) execute while the session is locked, once WindowServer attributes the window to the pid. Everything else decides exactly as `decide_background_input`:
  - the AX semantic route and the routed pointer still refuse with `screen_locked`;
  - a stale or foreign window id is still refused;
  - an unlocked session is not affected.
- macOS `type_text` and `press_key` advertise `locked_input` (boolean, default false); only `true` opts in. Under a lock they:
  - skip the key-window records, which the lock leaves unconfirmable;
  - skip the focused-element check, which cannot be read;
  - answer `effect: "unverifiable"`, `locked_input: true`, and a note that the keys went to the app's key window as it was before the lock;
  - offer no foreground escalation, since foreground input would reach the lock screen.

Independent of #6157.

**Testing.**
- `background_input::tests::locked_input_lets_only_pid_keys_through_a_lock`:
  - the three keyboard actions execute under a lock;
  - the AX semantic route and the routed pointer refuse with `screen_locked`;
  - a foreign pid is refused;
  - an unlocked two-window ambiguity is still refused.
- Schema tests: `locked_input` is an advertised boolean on both tools.
- On a macOS 26.5.2 VM (x86_64), with a real lock (display sleep with a password required, woken to the lock screen and kept on), TextEdit focused on a document before the lock, and background calls addressed to that window:

| run | `type_text` | `press_key` | `click` | window capture |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unlocked | delivered | delivered | delivered | live |
| locked, `locked_input: true` | sent, unverifiable | sent, unverifiable | refused `screen_locked` | live, shows the typed text |
| locked, no flag | refused `screen_locked` | refused | refused | live, unchanged |
| locked, `locked_input: true` again | sent | sent | refused | live |

  After unlock the document held the text from both flagged runs, and none from the unflagged one.

Platforms: macOS only. The flag is not read on Linux or Windows.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib` (1093 passed) and `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` (640 passed) on a macos-15 runner; clippy reports nothing in the touched files.

title: cua-driver: `include_display_only` — the structured elements with the display-only rows too
body:
Follow-up to #6132, which was the Markdown half of the same problem. This is the structured half.

### Problem

`get_window_state`'s `elements[]` holds only the actionable rows. `Static text`, `labels`, `read-only values` and `disabled controls` are in `tree_markdown` alone, so a client that needs to read something, not click it, must parse the markdown.

Same library app as in #6132: the agent changes a book's return time and clicks Save; the app then asks "Late fee change — Continue?". Before clicking Continue, it wants to confirm two facts:

- the staff-ID label at the top of the form says `RP-20417` (a read-only WinForms `Label`, AutomationId `lblAgent`);
- the date it typed landed in the book-return-time field (AutomationId `dtReturn`), which is now disabled behind the modal and therefore display-only.

Neither row is in `elements[]`. In the Markdown they are `- Text "RP-20417"` and `- Edit "Book return time" = "10/29/2026 10:15 AM"` — but without the id, five `Text` rows look alike, and after #6132 the id is there but still only as text to be parsed.

### Change

New boolean input `include_display_only` (default `false`). When it is on, `elements` holds every row of the tree in `DFS` order, not only the actionable ones.

* Display-only rows have `display_only: true` and no `element_index` / `element_token`, so `click`, `set_value` and the other input tools can't target them. They carry `role`, `label`, `value` (if any), `enabled`, `depth` / `parent_index` and `automation_id` (if set).
* Actionable rows are the same as before, whether the switch is on or off.
* Every row now carries `automation_id` where the platform reports one: UIA `AutomationId` on Windows, `AXIdentifier` on macOS. AT-SPI on Linux has no equivalent. The walkers already read this value, but the row never emitted it. It is the only change you can see with the switch off.
* `total_element_count` counts the actionable rows, or every row when the switch is on.
* `tree_format`: if it is unset, the switch implies `"elements"`. With `"both"`, the switch applies to the array. With `"markdown"`, the switch is ignored, because the markdown already shows these rows and the counts stay actionable.

Three consecutive rows from a real read: a caption, the field it labels, and a staff-ID label.

```jsonc
{"role":"Text","depth":2,"display_only":true,"label":"Loan id","enabled":true},
{"element_index":0,"element_token":"s00000002:0","role":"Edit","depth":2,"label":"Loan id","automation_id":"txtLoanId","enabled":true,"actions":["set_value","text"],"frame":{…}},
{"role":"Text","depth":2,"display_only":true,"label":"RP-20417","automation_id":"lblAgent","enabled":true},
```

This is not the existing `display_only` input, which is the capture-only preview mode. If the names are too close, `include_display_only_rows` is the alternative.

Contract (`cua-driver-contract`): adds `GetWindowStateInput.include_display_only: Option<bool>`, `WindowElement.display_only: Option<bool>` and `WindowElement.automation_id: Option<String>`. `WindowElement.element_index` becomes `Option<u64>` and is serialised only when present. Existing payloads deserialise unchanged.

### Known limitations

**`query` and `since` drop the display-only rows.** Both options narrow the response by `[N]`:

- `query` keeps the `elements` whose `element_index` appears in the projected markdown (`element_query.rs`).
- `since` keeps the ones whose index is in the diff (`retain_elements` in `window_state_view.rs`).

A display-only row has no `[N]`, so under either option it is always filtered out, and the response degrades to what it would have been without the switch.

**To get the display-only rows, call `get_window_state` with `include_display_only:true` and nothing else that narrows the tree — no `query`, no `since`.**

Keeping index-less rows through those filters needs a different row correspondence (DFS position rather than `[N]`); that is out of scope for this PR. The tool description and WORKFLOW.md state the same limitation.

**No `frame` on display-only rows (Windows).** The UIA walker reads `BoundingRectangle` only for actionable nodes (`uia/mod.rs` emits `rect: None` for the rest), so this PR cannot report one without touching the walker. A follow-up if anyone needs to click *near* a label.

### Tested

**Unit.** macOS, toolchain 1.97.1: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver-contract -p platform-macos --lib` — 639 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored (pre-existing GUI-bound). `platform-windows --lib` tests cross-built (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`) and run natively on Windows Server 2022: pass. The Linux crate is `cfg(target_os)`-gated and was not built or run.

**Windows, live WinForms app.** This ran on Windows against a live WinForms app. The PR build runs as its own daemon on a second named pipe, next to the stock 0.37.0 daemon. Every read below targets the same `pid` and the same window. The app is the library example from the Problem section, so the samples use its names: the search screen, the loan page with its value labels, and the late-fee modal. Each row in the table is one read. `include_display_only` omitted and `false` are the same thing (the parser maps both to off); the table says which one the read actually sent.

| screen | window | build | `tree_format` | `include_display_only` | rows in `elements` | of which `display_only` | of which with `automation_id` | `total_element_count` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| search | main | stock 0.37.0 | elements | (not accepted) | 9 | 0 | 0 | 9 |
| search | main | PR | elements | omitted / false | 9 | 0 | 4 | 9 |
| search | main | PR | elements | true | 16 | 7 | 6 | 16 |
| search | main | PR | markdown | true | no array | — | — | 9 |
| loan + modal up | owner | PR | elements | omitted / false | 16 | 0 | 9 | 16 |
| loan + modal up | owner | PR | elements | true | 40 | 24 | 19 | 40 |
| loan + modal up | dialog | PR | elements | omitted / false | 4 | 0 | 2 | 4 |
| loan + modal up | dialog | PR | elements | true | 7 | 3 | 3 | 7 |

How to read the table:

- **Rows 1 vs 2.** With the switch off, this PR matches stock. The only addition is `automation_id` on the four controls that have one: `txtLoanId`, `txtMember`, `txtPhone`, `btnSearch`. Nothing else changes.
- **Rows 2 vs 3.** Turning the switch on adds the 7 display-only rows. The count goes up to match.
- **Row 4.** With `markdown`, the switch does nothing. The markdown is unchanged. The count stays at 9.
- **Rows 5–8.** These show the same thing with the modal open. One thing to note: the owner's 16 actionable rows include the dialog's own rows. That's because UIA nests an owned dialog inside its owner.

Search screen, the 7 rows the switch adds — the `Window` root, four caption `Text`s, the staff-ID label and the `MenuBar`; two of them shown with their neighbours:

```jsonc
{"role":"Text","depth":2,"display_only":true,"label":"Agent:","enabled":true},
{"role":"Text","depth":2,"display_only":true,"label":"RP-20417","automation_id":"lblAgent","enabled":true},
{"element_index":4,"element_token":"s00000002:4","role":"TitleBar","depth":1,"label":"Library Desk", …},
{"role":"MenuBar","depth":2,"display_only":true,"label":"System","automation_id":"MenuBar","parent_index":4,"enabled":true},
```

Loan page with the late-fee modal up — the rows that were unreadable before, now from the structured side: every value label of the loan, the disabled Save button, and the dialog's message:

```jsonc
{"role":"Text","depth":4,"display_only":true,"label":"LN-48213","automation_id":"lblLoanId","enabled":true},
{"role":"Text","depth":4,"display_only":true,"label":"J. Doe","automation_id":"lblMember","enabled":true},
{"role":"Text","depth":4,"display_only":true,"label":"Oct 21 2026 10:21 AM","automation_id":"lblReturn","enabled":true},
{"role":"Button","depth":5,"display_only":true,"label":"Save","automation_id":"btnSave","enabled":false},
{"role":"Text","depth":1,"display_only":true,"automation_id":"lblFeeMessage","enabled":true,
 "label":"Changing the return time changes the late fee.\nOld fee: $2.00\nNew fee: $6.50"}
```

**macOS, live app** (native debug build, Calculator), the same three reads:

| `tree_format` | `include_display_only` | rows in `elements` | of which `display_only` | of which with `automation_id` | `total_element_count` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| elements | omitted / false | 33 | 0 | 22 | 33 |
| elements | true | 35 | 2 | 22 | 35 |
| markdown | true | no array | — | — | 33 |

The two rows the switch adds are the calculator's display — `AXStaticText "Last Expression" = "(, 175 − 134, ), ÷ 134"` and `"Edit field" = "0.30597015…"` — the result of the computation, absent from `elements` without the switch.

Happy to split the contract change out if `element_index: Option<u64>` is unwelcome for the generated bindings.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep idle macOS overlays out of window cycling
body:
## Summary

With Stage Manager enabled, cycling windows can activate the cursor overlay even when no cursor is visible. The macOS overlay is a normal-level fullscreen window that is ordered on screen at startup and left there after its contents clear.

Exclude the overlay from window cycling and keep it ordered out until there are pixels to draw. Order it out again after the last cursor fades, is disabled, or its session ends. Reassert its target-relative position when it becomes visible again. The daemon and authenticated remote connections keep running; no client API or permission changes are introduced.

## Validation

On macOS, a release-based build showed the overlay off-screen at startup, on-screen during cursor movement, off-screen after the configured idle timeout, visible after another movement, and off-screen after disable/session end. The foreground application did not change during those checks. Window capture and accessibility retrieval also succeeded.

On the rebased PR commit, all 11 focused macOS overlay tests pass. `rustfmt --check` and `git diff --check` also pass.

Test command: `cargo test --release --locked --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-macos --lib cursor::overlay::tests` (Rust 1.97).

## Remaining verification

This is a draft pending a complete native window-cycle regression check and maintainer review. The locally signed app needed fresh macOS permissions for its background helper, so the stock app was restored rather than leaving remote access offline. The manual lifecycle evidence above is from the isolated release-based helper, not a claim that the rebased app has passed the full desktop matrix.

Bumps [twisted](https://github.com/twisted/twisted) from 26.4.0 to 26.10.0rc1.
Release notes

Sourced from twisted's releases.

Twisted 26.10.0rc1

twisted 26.10.0rc1 (2026-10-22)

This is the last release with support for Python 3.10.

This include fixes for:

  • CVE-2026-83813 (GHSA-jj36-9pvh-vj5r),
  • GHSA-vpp8-g58w-m8mp (no CVE assigned yet)
  • GHSA-cwm5-jh59-mwxr (no CVE assigned yet)
  • GHSA-3476-c5c2-fr73 (no CVE assigned yet)
  • GHSA-q7qq-6mhp-9rc4 (no CVE assigned yet)
  • GHSA-2qrf-pqgx-qh9v (no CVE assigned yet)
  • GHSA-53xc-49m8-p798 (no CVE assigned yet)

Features

  • It is now possible to set the SO_REUSEPORT and SO_REUSEADDR TCP socket flags from user code. (#9101)
  • Python 3.14 is now supported. (#12640)
  • twisted.internet.defer.Deferred.__iter__, used when awaiting a Deferred, is now about 2-3% faster. (#12727)

Bugfixes

  • twisted.internet.tcp.Port.startListening() now closes the socket when raising CannotListenError. (#6108)
  • Initiating a TCP connection with an address literals and a port outside of the 1-65535 range in twisted.internet.tcp.BaseClient and twisted.internet.iocpreactor.tcp.Client now triggers an errback instead of an unhandled error. title: macOS 27.2: APNs/BAA failure persists from macOS 27.0.1
body:
### macOS compatibility status

The APNs/BAA failure previously observed in a macOS 27.0.1 VM also occurs in a freshly installed macOS **27.2 (26B123)** VM. Updating to 27.2 has therefore not resolved this macOS problem in our test.

### Test setup

Tested on **2026-10-30**, with both host and guest running macOS **27.2 (26B123)**.

The guest was freshly installed and Setup Assistant was completed manually with a local account, without signing into an Apple Account. APNs was checked with:

```sh
/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ApplePushService.framework/apsctl status
/usr/bin/log show --last 10m --process apsd --info --debug --style compact
```

### Observed result

The production connection remained disconnected in two status samples several minutes apart:

```text
connection environment: production
   connection status: No
```

The `apsd` log contains the same SEP key-generation and BAA certificate failure chain seen in the earlier macOS 27.0.1 test:

```text
unable to generate key: error e00002e2(-536870174)
SecKeyCreateRandomKey_ios failed: ... Code=-25308 "Failed to generate keypair"
APSBAAClientIdentityProvider failed to obtain a BAA cert
underlying identity provider has identity to connect? NO
told not to connect!
```

Two consecutive attempts produced this error chain at **10:35:33 UTC**. The later status sample at **10:40:51 UTC** still showed no production connection.

Related reports of the same APNs/BAA error pattern: [Apple Developer Forums thread 840500](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/840500).

This confirms persistence of the APNs/BAA failure in this 27.2 test.

title: fix(cua-driver): reopen running apps with launch_app
body:
`launch_app` currently sends `aevt/oapp` for every background launch. When an app is already running but its main window was closed, minimized, or hidden with ⌘H, many Electron apps ignore that event and leave no window on screen. A Dock click or `open -g` reopens the window without changing the frontmost app.

## What changed

- Select `aevt/rapp` (`kAEReopenApplication`) when the target app is already running and `creates_new_application_instance` is false.
- Keep `activates = false` and the existing focus-steal suppression behavior.
- Keep `aevt/oapp` for cold launches and new application instances.
- Apply the shared behavior to both bundle-ID and name launch paths.
- Add unit coverage for the event-selection contract and an ignored macOS E2E case that launches the test-owned AppKit harness, hides that test-owned AppKit process, calls `launch_app` again, and verifies that it becomes visible while Finder remains frontmost.

## Validation

- `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib`
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-e2e --test installed_app_launch_macos_test --no-run`
- `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast`

The installed-app E2E is gated with `#[ignore]` because it requires a logged-in macOS GUI session and the relevant TCC permissions. It should be selected by the canonical macOS desktop runner when those prerequisites are available.

A downstream consumer currently pins Cua Driver v0.31.0 and will use this behavior after upgrading.

title: fix(cua-cli): load saved token for consented local host
body:
## Summary

`cua do switch host` registers a direct sandbox, but without an explicit token it never loads the local host service's `host/env-token`. Later actions consequently reach the right service without its bearer token and fail authentication.

Add a final credential fallback for the sandbox named `host`, only when its endpoint exactly matches the configured local host URL and the existing host-consent marker is present. Read the token when resolving the connection, trim surrounding whitespace, and ignore missing or empty files. Already-selected hosts benefit without being registered again.

## Related work

Fixes #6154.

No RFC: this repairs credential loading for the existing consented host target. It adds no CLI flags, protocol fields, or permission grants.

## Compatibility and risk

- Remembered direct credentials, registry credentials, and `CUA_ENV_TOKEN` retain their existing precedence. `--token` and `CUA_HOST_ENV_TOKEN` continue to work through host selection.
- The automatic fallback does not apply to an unrelated endpoint, another sandbox name, or a host whose consent marker has been removed. The local token is not copied into the direct-credential store or printed.
- This changes CLI credential resolution only; it does not change host setup, authentication enforcement, desktop input, or the SDK protocol. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

From `libs/cua`, using the repository-pinned Rust 1.97.1 on macOS arm64:

- Before the production change, `host_target_uses_its_saved_token_after_consent` failed on the screenshot action with `unauthenticated: unauthenticated: bad token (Unauthenticated)` from the mock service.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p cua-cli --lib --test sandbox_do -- --test-threads=2`: 298 unit tests and 16 integration tests passed; one existing host-runtime probe remained ignored.
- Regression coverage includes saved-token loading with a trailing newline, consent enforcement and removal, explicit-token precedence, a custom endpoint, and a different sandbox at the local endpoint. Tests run the real CLI against loopback mocks with temporary homes; they do not use the developer's desktop or credentials.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p cua-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `bash scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast`: SPDX headers and CLI formatting passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The signed Cua Spaces app from the report was not exercised. Linux/Windows execution and upstream CI remain pending. The macOS test builds emit the same SDK unwind-table linker warning seen before the production change; Clippy passes without suppression.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused change; the description matches the diff.
- [x] No RFC is required for this bug fix.
- [x] Tests are included and platform gaps are stated.
- [x] Conventional Commit title describes the production change.
- [x] No external implementation was copied.

This is a user-visible fix; `no-release` is not requested.

title: [Bug]: recording turn times start about 1.5 s after the video's first frame
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

With `record_video: true`, each turn's `t_ms_from_session_start` is counted from a clock that starts after the video backend's 1.5 s startup probe. A click logged at 3.0 s in `action.json` shows up at about 4.5 s in `recording.mp4`, so anything that maps turns onto the video is off by that much, including `recording render`.

### Reproduction

1. On Hyprland, where video goes through wf-recorder, call `start_recording` with `record_video: true` and the cursor's click marks on.
2. Click a few times, with a few seconds between clicks.
3. Call `stop_recording`.
4. For each turn, compare `t_ms_from_session_start` in its `action.json` with the time its click mark appears in `recording.mp4`.

It happened on every turn of the recording, by the same amount.

### Expected behavior

Each click mark appears in `recording.mp4` at its turn's `t_ms_from_session_start`, within a frame or two.

### Actual behavior

In a recording of five clicks and typing, every action appeared in the video a steady 1.45 s after its `t_ms_from_session_start`.

### Environment

```text
Cua component and version/commit: Cua Driver 0.38.0; source read at main 895ede5
Operating system and architecture: Arch Linux (Omarchy), kernel 7.2.8, x86_64
Application/browser/window system/image: Chromium 155 in a nested Hyprland 0.56.2 session, cua-hyprland-plugin 0.33.2, wf-recorder 0.6.0
```

### Evidence

Observed in a local test run on 2026-10-29. The offset was the same on all five turns.

Reading the recorder on `main` gives a likely cause. I have not run a fixed build yet.

- `cua-driver-core/src/recording.rs:650` takes the monotonic anchor before the video starts. `cursor.jsonl` is timed from it.
- `video::start_video` then returns only after the backend's startup probe. The wf-recorder backend polls for 1500 ms that the child has not exited (`platform-linux/src/video_wayland.rs:224`). The ffmpeg backend has the same probe (`cua-driver-core/src/video_ffmpeg.rs:108`), so it is probably affected too, but I have not tried it.
- `recording.rs:690` reads `started_at_ms = now_ms()` after that, stores it as `session_start_ms` (line 710), and line 1406 computes `t_ms_from_session_start` from it.

So turn times start about 1.5 s after the anchor that the video and `cursor.jsonl` share, which the comment above line 650 says should not happen. The remaining 50 ms is likely wf-recorder's own startup before its first frame.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: add 1.5 s to each turn's offset before looking it up in the video.

A narrow fix is to read `now_ms()` next to the monotonic anchor, before the video starts. Computing turn offsets from `session_monotonic_start` instead of the wall clock would also remove the separate clock. I'm happy to send a PR with a test in `recording_action_timestamp.rs`.

Related: #4953 is about the same `started_at_ms` value in `session.json`, and its fix landed in #5145. Writing the video's measured start offset into `session.json` would let renderers check alignment, but that changes the file format, so I would raise it on RFC #4956 rather than here.

- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Feature]: fast-forward idle time in `cua-driver recording render`
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

Most of an agent recording is idle screen while the model thinks between actions. Someone who watches a recording to check what an agent did has to sit through all of it. In one of our test recordings, five actions took 20.3 s, and about 9 s of it showed something happening.

`recording render` zooms on clicks but plays every second at real speed. Cutting the idle time out instead would make a 20 s hang look instant, and could drop an effect that appears after the action, such as a page load or a toast.

### Desired outcome

An opt-in render mode that plays each action and what follows it at real speed, plays the time between actions fast, and shows how long each fast stretch really took. The 20.3 s recording above would render to about 9 s, with every skipped stretch visible as a skip.

### Current workaround

We cut the raw recording ourselves with ffmpeg, from the turn times in `action.json`.

### Affected components and platforms

- `cua-driver recording render` (CLI), which calls `render()` in `cua-driver-core/src/recording_render.rs`.
- `cua-driver-core/src/recording_zoom.rs` and `recording_loader.rs`.
- Every platform, since render works on files. The result depends on turn times matching the video, which is not the case on Hyprland today (#6210).

### Alternatives and prior art

#1360 added variable-speed rendering to the Swift driver. Parts of it were ported to Rust: the loader builds action spans (`recording_loader.rs:301`), and `map_pts` (`recording_zoom.rs:340`) remaps timestamps so gaps play at `ACTION_FAST_SPEED` (8x), with a unit test. `render()` never calls `map_pts`, so the Rust render plays everything at 1x.

Hard cuts are the other option. We decided against them for the reason above.

### Implementation ideas

- Add a render flag that the global CLI parser keeps. The comment on `run_recording_render` explains which flag forms survive it.
- Build a trim and concat filter graph from the padded and merged spans, and either apply it after zoompan or remap the zoom times through `map_pts`.
- Keep a window around each action, for example 0.3 s before to 1.5 s after, and extend it while frames are still changing (ffmpeg `freezedetect`), so a slow load stays at real speed.

Which mode should Cua have?

- Constant speed: gaps play at 8x, as in the Swift render. This reuses `map_pts` as it is.
- Fixed skip: each idle stretch becomes about 0.6 s, labelled with its real length ("+18 s"). Long waits stay short, and the label keeps the wait visible.

We need the fixed skip and would build either or both. The flag is additive and off by default. Does it need an RFC?

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: [Bug]: Remote health check misreports current Windows host as older Cua
body:
### Primary area

SDK or bindings

### Summary

Checking an online Windows computer from a Mac reports that the Windows computer runs an older Cua, even after updating Cua Spaces to 0.19.1. The installed Windows host is cua-spacesd 0.8.0, which is the version pinned by that app release.

### Reproduction

1. Install/update the official Cua Spaces Windows app to 0.19.1 and keep its host service running and online.
2. From the same owner's Mac, select that Windows computer on the Machines page.
3. Alternatively, run `cua doctor --machine <windows-machine-id> --json` from the Mac's bundled CLI.

### Expected behavior

Return the Windows computer's health, or explain that remote health checking on Windows is unsupported. Recommend an update only when a version check establishes that an available update supplies the feature.

### Actual behavior

The Mac CLI exits 1 with the following error (computer name redacted):

```text
cua: internal: machine health is not available on this host: <Windows computer> runs an older Cua that can't be checked; update Cua on it
```

The Mac UI displays the same update advice. Updating the Windows app does not clear it.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro x86_64, build 26300.
- Windows Cua Spaces 0.19.1, file version 0.19.1.125; bundled CLI 0.9.0.
- Windows `cua-spacesd --version`: 0.8.0.
- Mac client: bundled CLI 0.9.0, existing owner session over the normal relay route.

### Evidence

- Reproduced with one exact-machine CLI request from the Mac after the Windows update. The Windows host was online and its scheduled task was Running.
- Local Windows `cua doctor --machine this --json` completed two checks successfully. This does not prove the remote RPC works.
- The [0.19.1 app pin](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.19.1/libs/cua-spacesd/VERSION) is `0.8.0`; the independent host version is not evidence that the app update failed.
- In [cua-spacesd 0.8.0](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spacesd-v0.8.0/libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-server/src/host_spaces.rs), `diagnose_host` calls `forward`, which calls `daemon_channel`. Its non-Unix implementation returns `Code::Unimplemented` with `providing Spaces from a Windows host is not supported yet`.
- The [client in app 0.19.1](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.19.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/host_spaces.rs) maps an Unimplemented status from this call to the older-Cua update message. This loses the distinction between an old RPC and an unsupported Windows transport.

These are release-source observations and native CLI results, not a packet trace or a rebuilt host. No kernel, authentication, or sharing-policy changes were made.

### Workaround and additional context

Local diagnostics remain usable. Refs #5379, which introduced computer health checking and explicitly recorded that real remote-computer checks had not been verified in that PR. This report concerns the Windows remote-health error, not the separate scheduled-task status problem in #5969.
