title: [Bug]: Windows host restart leaves orphan driver online while scheduled task stays Ready
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### Summary

The Windows Cua Spaces app showed Service stopped while its cua-spacesd process remained online. Restart service did not restore the scheduled task to Running; the existing driver was an orphan of the task's launcher.

### Reproduction

This was observed on an official installer installation. The original event that detached the driver from the task is unknown; I do not have a deterministic way to produce that initial state.

Given that state:

1. The app shows Service stopped. Windows Task Scheduler reports `Cua\SpacesdHost` as Ready, while the driver process remains alive and the host is online.
2. Click Restart service, or run `cua host start --json`.
3. Compare the task state and driver process identity before and after.

### Expected behavior

The normal start/restart path should reconcile its existing owned driver and return the scheduled task to a correctly supervised Running state, or report an actionable failure.

### Actual behavior

`cua host start --json` exited 0 with no host error, but the same driver PID survived and `service.running` remained false. Task Scheduler still reported Ready. The user also observed that the app's Restart service button did not resolve the warning.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro x86_64, build 26300.
- Initially Cua Spaces 0.19.0, file version 0.19.0.124; bundled CLI 0.9.0; host cua-spacesd 0.8.0.
- Recovered host remained Running after the app was updated to 0.19.1.
- Official Windows scheduled-task runner, interactive user, Limited/LeastPrivilege, no execution time limit.

### Evidence

| Observation | Before recovery | After recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host status | online=true, sharing=true, error=null | online=true, sharing=true |
| Service status | installed=true, running=false | running=true |
| Task state | Ready (3) | Running (4) |
| Driver identity | Same old PID after normal start | One new PID |

The task action used the generated `conhost --headless cmd /d /c ... cua-spacesd join ...` launcher. The old driver's parent cmd process was alive, but its original conhost parent was absent. No permission-denied error was observed.

The current public [service.rs](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/cua/crates/cua-host/src/service.rs) is relevant: the task start path performs `/End` then `/Run`, while the uninstall path explicitly documents that `/End` can leave cmd and the driver running (CUA-1749). This is a source-level lead, not proof that the installed binary exactly matches current main.

### Workaround and additional context

After checking that there were no connected clients or provided Spaces, I stopped the service normally, confirmed the exact same orphan driver survived, terminated only that verified orphan, and started the service through the official CLI. The task then became Running with one new driver. The user confirmed the warning disappeared, and I separately inspected the app's Online state.

This is an operational recovery, not a permanent fix. No ACL, task definition, credentials, sharing policy, or elevation settings were changed.

Related but distinct: #5969 reports a localized CSV parser reading a genuinely Running task as stopped. Here the task was actually Ready, and the problem included the orphan driver and ineffective restart.

title: [Bug]: Windows shown as This Mac/macOS in Spaces UI and diagnostics
body:
### Primary area

Other

### Summary

Cua Spaces identifies the same local Windows computer as both Windows / This PC and This Mac / macOS. Platform-specific wording also appears in Windows service errors and local diagnostics, making it difficult to tell whether an issue belongs to the Windows computer or a connected Mac.

### Reproduction

1. On Windows, open the official Cua Spaces 0.19.1 app and go to Machines.
2. Select the local computer, whose list row correctly shows This PC and Windows.
3. Read its desktop entry under Spaces on this machine.
4. Run the bundled `cua doctor --machine this --json` and compare its producer platform with the disk-check message.

### Expected behavior

The local Windows computer, its desktop, diagnostic messages, and recovery instructions should consistently use Windows / PC terminology or platform-neutral wording. A real connected Mac should keep its own macOS labels.

### Actual behavior

| Surface | Observed on Windows | Evidence status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Machines list | `<local computer> / This PC / Windows` | Correct; freshly checked in 0.19.1 |
| That computer's desktop row | `This Mac / Desktop / macOS / This Mac` | Incorrect; freshly checked visually and through accessibility text in 0.19.1 |
| Desktop link | `cua-spaces://app/spaces/this-mac` | Observed internal route; not by itself proof of a routing defect |
| Service-stopped issue | `The Cua service isn't running, so your other machines can't reach this Mac.` | User screenshot from 0.19.0; service since recovered, so this warning was not forced again on 0.19.1 |
| Local disk check | `469 GB free on this Mac`, facts.volume=`this Mac` | Fresh bundled CLI output; producer explicitly says `this on windows, Cua 0.9.0` |

The mixed labels are observable. Whether every occurrence has the same implementation cause has not been established.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro x86_64, build 26300.
- Cua Spaces 0.19.1, file version 0.19.1.125; bundled CLI/daemon 0.9.0; host cua-spacesd 0.8.0.
- The standalone Cua Driver was subsequently updated to 0.38.0. The Windows/macOS label contradiction was still observed after that update.
- Same account also has a real Mac, making the platform confusion especially misleading.

### Evidence

Fresh accessibility excerpts with private names removed:

```text
option <local computer> This PC Desktop shared Windows
  graphic Windows
region <local computer> details
  text Online
  heading Spaces on this machine
  link This Mac Desktop macOS This Mac
    Description: Open This Mac
    Value: cua-spaces://app/spaces/this-mac
```

Fresh local CLI excerpt:

```json
{
  "producer": "cua doctor --machine (this on windows, Cua 0.9.0)",
  "check": {
    "id": "machine.disk",
    "status": "pass",
    "message": "469 GB free on this Mac",
    "facts": { "free_gb": "469", "volume": "this Mac" }
  }
}
```

The JSON is an excerpt, not the complete output schema. Actual screenshots were inspected locally; raw captures are omitted because they contain account and machine information. No sharing settings were changed to reproduce the labels.

### Related Windows setup and recovery problems

This section collects the same installation's user-visible problems in one place. The independent operational bugs retain their own reports rather than duplicating their reproduction and source analysis here.

| Problem | Current outcome | Tracking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows shown as Mac/macOS in UI and diagnostics | Still present in 0.19.1 | This issue |
| Mac client says the current Windows host is too old and recommends updating | Reproduced after app update; the Windows host RPC path returns Unimplemented, which is rendered as an older-version message | #6212 |
| Restart service leaves the host online but the scheduled task Ready | Recovered locally by reconciling the verified orphan; no upstream permanent fix claimed | #6213 |
| New Space says QEMU is missing after QEMU installation | Resolved locally by restarting only the Cua daemon with the updated PATH; attached doctor now reports QEMU ready and the Windows wizard warning disappeared | Context only; no separate product root cause established |

No kernel or permission failure has been demonstrated as the cause of these platform labels. VM readiness is not a VM boot test.

title: feat(wayland-helper): add Move to position a window
body:
## What this adds

`Move(id, x, y) -> bool` on `org.cua.WinRects` (helper API 12 → 13).

A Wayland client cannot place its own toplevel — only the compositor can — so
this is the one geometry operation that has no client-side equivalent. The id is
the same Shell stable sequence `Activate` and `GetRects` already use, and `x`/`y`
are the frame top-left corner in the stage-pixel space `GetRects` reports, so a
caller can compute a target corner from an existing snapshot.

Contract, deliberately matching `Activate`: the call reports whether the request
was **accepted**, not where the window landed. The caller reads a fresh
`GetRects` afterwards. A maximized window is unmaximized first, because Mutter
ignores a geometry request while maximized. Fullscreen windows, windows that do
not allow moving, and ids that are no longer mapped are refused with `false`.

The window lookup that `Activate` did inline is now `_windowForId()`, shared by
both calls, so the two cannot drift apart.

## Version numbering

API 11 went to `PlayCursorPath` and `SetCursorLook` upstream, and 12 to the
cursor-tip fix, so this lands as **13**. Both places that carry the number move
together, as they have in every previous bump: `GetVersion()` in `extension.js`
and `version` in `metadata.json` (the installers read the latter to decide
whether the installed helper is older).

## Why no Resize

I implemented `Resize`/`MoveResize` first and dropped them after measuring: a
Wayland client owns its own size. `move_resize_frame` does send
`xdg_toplevel.configure(520, 360)`, the client acks it, and the frame rect stays
`400x300` — the window never changes. Such a method would return `true` while
nothing happened, which is worse than not having it. Happy to add it if someone
knows a path where it takes effect (Xwayland-only? ignore the ack and re-assert?),
but it is not something I could make work.

## How it was verified

The guard that refuses GNOME 50 was removed **only in a throwaway copy** of the
extension, and the shell version was added to `shell-version` of that copy, so
`enable()` could run at all. Nothing in this PR touches either.

Stand: `gnome-shell --headless --wayland --wayland-display=ext-test` under
`dbus-run-session` (own session bus, `XDG_DATA_HOME` pointing at the throwaway
copy, `GSETTINGS_BACKEND=memory`), a real GTK4 and GTK3 client on that display,
and `gdbus` calls from the same bus.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `GetVersion()` | `(uint32 13,)` |
| `Move(id, 120, 90)` on a GTK4 client | `(true,)`, `GetRects` → `x=120 y=90 w=400 h=300` |
| `Move(id, 60, 60)` on a GTK3 client | `(true,)`, `GetRects` → `x=60 y=60` |
| `Move(999999, 10, 10)` | `(false,)` — refusal, no D-Bus error |
| Extension errors after enable | `(@as [],)` |
| `node --input-type=module --check` | passes |
| D-Bus interface XML | parses; 15 methods, `Move` arg types `u,i,i → b` |
| `metadata.json` | valid JSON, `version` 13 |

The behaviour above was measured on the same code as it stands now; the rebase
onto current `main` changed the version number and nothing else. The table now
states 13 because that is what this branch returns — say so if you would rather
see the run repeated on the branch head.

Not verified, and I would rather say so than imply otherwise:

- **The maximized branch.** I could not put a window into a maximized state in the
  headless stand without adding a test-only method; doing that aborted the shell
  (`meta_window_get_work_area_for_logical_monitor: assertion failed
  (logical_monitor)` — there is no logical monitor in headless mode), so the
  `unmaximize()`-then-move path is unexercised. Worth a manual check on a real
  session.
- **The fullscreen and `allows_move() === false` refusals.** Same reason: no way to
  reach those states from the stand.
- **A live GNOME 50 session.** `enable()` still refuses 50 and newer (the
  containment guard), so the method cannot be reached there at all; everything
  above ran in a 50.1 shell with that guard patched out of the copy only.
- No Rust consumer in this PR: `cua-driver` would call the method through its
  existing D-Bus plumbing. I can wire and test that path if you want it in the
  same change.

Positioning a window was the original ask behind
[this problem](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/67318357/how-to-set-the-position-of-a-wayland-window-on-the-screen):
every answer either patches the compositor or installs a third-party extension.
The helper is already installed, already trusted, and already talks to the
compositor, so this belongs here rather than in another extension.

title: fix(cua-sdk): report unsupported remote health checks accurately
body:
## Summary

`Spaces::machine_health` treats every `DiagnoseHost` `Unimplemented` response as proof that the remote computer runs an older Cua. The current Windows host returns the same status for its unsupported daemon transport, so the CLI and Spaces UI recommend an update that does not resolve the problem.

Report that the computer does not support remote health checks and suggest running `cua doctor --machine this` on that computer. Keep the existing error kind, timeout, ownership checks, successful response, and other RPC error handling unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #6212.

No RFC: this corrects misleading diagnostic text within an existing error path; it adds no API, protocol, permission, or platform capability.

## Compatibility and risk

- Shared client-side handling applies to both an unsupported Windows transport and an older server missing the RPC. Neither status alone establishes that an update supplies the feature.
- The `host_capability_missing` tag remains unchanged. No host settings or transport behavior change.
- This does not implement remote Windows health checking. Reverting the message change restores the previous diagnostic.

## Validation

On macOS arm64 with the repository-pinned Rust 1.97.1:

- Added three public-API integration tests through the existing loopback fake relay and gRPC host. They cover the Windows `Unimplemented` message, an unknown RPC, successful health responses, permission denial, and connection failure.
- Before the fix, the new unsupported-health test failed on the old update advice; the two control tests passed.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-spaces --test host_spaces -- --test-threads=4`: **44 passed**, including a rerun on candidate `12bf9f2f9ad67d447bc35338e4df9e540044fa85`.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-spaces --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast --base upstream/main`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Both crate doc tests passed. The remaining integration targets were run separately after Cargo stopped at the broader failures below.

The full crate run was **not clean**, and no full-suite or CI pass is claimed:

- `providers::a_space_that_fails_to_start_leaves_no_instance` expected one deletion but observed two. It failed identically after restoring all production source to upstream `78cbbecab6e1803d25b9cf093070e7e41bbb4c4d`; it is left unchanged.
- All 414 unit tests passed on the first run. A repeat run failed `mesh::tests::a_space_on_a_mesh_the_relay_turned_off_reconnects`; its isolated rerun passed.
- The scale target exceeded latency limits with four test threads during other testing. Running it alone with `--test-threads=1` passed all eight tests.

The Windows refusal is reproduced through the actual client RPC boundary using the server's reported status. A live Windows-to-Mac installation and native Spaces UI were not exercised. Fork CI and release-metadata validation remain for the maintainer-approved run.

## Review follow-up

Updated the diagnostic guidance from “on that computer” to “on that machine”, as suggested in review, and updated the existing exact-message assertion. Commit: `6c07fd6c4aa0fd2f594c8ddb6913f505b029ea49`.

After this wording change:

- `cargo test --locked --offline -p cua-spaces --test host_spaces -- --test-threads=4`: **44 passed**. Run outside the restricted sandbox so the mock relay could bind its loopback socket.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p cua-spaces --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Workspace formatting, fast pre-push checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

The broader-suite and native-platform limitations recorded above still apply. No upstream CI result is claimed.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Tests and platform validation limits are recorded above.

title: [Feature]: cua-hyprland-plugin: support the v3 input route on Hyprland 0.57.0
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

Hyprland 0.57.0 was released on October 28, and distros tracking the latest release (Arch, Omarchy edge) already ship it. The plugin pins the v3 input route to Hyprland 0.56.2 exactly, so `cua-hyprland-plugin` refuses to build with `CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT=ON` against 0.57.0. Anyone on 0.57.0 has to hold the compositor back or build the plugin without its input route.

### Desired outcome

The input route builds and passes requalification on Hyprland 0.57.0 and ships in a released driver tag, so the 0.57.0 rows collected in https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/5751 stop failing.

### Current workaround

Build the plugin with the input route off (discovery only), or stay on Hyprland 0.56.2.

### Affected components and platforms

- `libs/cua-driver/hyprland-plugin`, v3 input route (`CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT`), on main and on released tags up to v0.38.0
- Hyprland 0.57.0, on distros tracking the latest release: Arch, Omarchy edge

### Alternatives and prior art

PR #6153 widens the input pin to accept 0.56.2 and 0.57.0 and fixes the `m_exclusiveLSes` rename. Its notes say the 0.57.0 build, CTest, headless smoke, and live test are still pending, so 0.57.0 support is unverified. The compatibility matrix on the `hyprland-plugin-compat` branch records 0.57.0 as FAIL for main, v0.38.0, and v0.33.2. Portal input works without the plugin.

### Implementation ideas

I built the PR #6153 branch against the Hyprland 0.57.0 headers (gcc 16.2.0). The configure step passes and the rename fix works. Compilation still fails in `input_experiment.cpp` on `CWindow` members the PR does not touch:

- `CWindow::getPID()` no longer exists (`:1159`)
- `CWindow::m_isX11` no longer exists (`:537`, `:1160`)
- `CWindow::m_isMapped` is private now (`:536`, `:1160`)

title: fix(cua-driver): stop the video startup probe skewing recording times
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: with `record_video: true`, turn times start after the video backend's 1.5 s startup probe. An action logged at 3.0 s can appear at about 4.5 s in `recording.mp4`, and `recording render` inherits the offset. The probe also shortens ffmpeg's reported `duration_ms`.
- What changed: read the session's wall-clock start next to its monotonic anchor before starting video, so turns share the zero already used by `cursor.jsonl`. Start ffmpeg's duration clock before spawning the encoder. Both startup probes stay.

## Related work

Refs #6210

RFC: not required. This restores the existing timing contract without changing fields, schemas, traits, or public APIs.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: wf-recorder and ffmpeg turn offsets include their startup probe; `started_at_monotonic_ms` moves earlier accordingly. Remove any manual 1.5 s compensation. ffmpeg duration metadata now includes the probe.
- Risk and rollback: backend setup latency remains between the shared anchor and the first video frame. ScreenCaptureKit has no probe and now includes capture setup time in its turn clock, which may make turns lead the video. This requires macOS evidence. Both production changes are individual clock moves and revert independently. Wall-clock steps remain an existing risk.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the new `turn_times_count_from_before_the_video_backend_starts` failed before its fix with `turn start 0 ms`; the existing timestamp test passed. After the session fix both timestamp tests passed. The new `stop_recording_duration_includes_the_ffmpeg_startup_probe` then failed before its fix with `duration_ms 0`; both existing shutdown error tests passed.
- Complete core owner: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --locked` reports 1,142 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored across all 18 unit/integration/doc-test groups, including both new regressions and manifest start-time preservation. The runtime lost its command session handle before the shell saved the exit code; the complete log ends at the successful doc-test footer, and no test process remains.
- Protocol owners: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_media_test --test protocol_schema_test --locked` exits 0; schema tests pass 4/4. The media binary runs 0 tests because its whole-file cfg selects only macOS/Windows, so media protocol coverage is unverified on Linux. An unchanged dependency, `nom v1.2.4`, emits a future-Rust incompatibility warning.
- Final affected tests: after the review correction, both focused test binaries pass 5/5 (exit 0). Only test cfg/module organization and subsequent whitespace/comment cleanup changed after the wider runs; production sources are unchanged. Independent read-only review accepted the correction with no remaining actionable findings.
- Local checks: `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --base a9902d272655b65180fa713a8b1f2f1c1935e70b` exits 0; SPDX headers, scoped cargo fmt, and all-targets clippy with `-D warnings` pass. Windows clippy is skipped because cargo-xwin is absent. `git diff --check` passes.
- Manual or platform evidence: optional nested Hyprland/video smoke deferred; no release build or host input performed. The two new regressions are Linux-only because recording starts a live cursor sampler on macOS/Windows; no production test hooks were added.
- Known gaps or CI still required: real frame-level video alignment and ffprobe duration comparison, native macOS, Windows, X11, and complete desktop matrix are unverified. Windows clippy skipped (cargo-xwin absent). Native execution of the new regressions is unverified. Ready for maintainer review. No release certification claim.

title: [Feature]: keep typed secrets out of `action.json`
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

With recording on, `action.json` stores tool arguments as sent, so a password typed through `type_text` lands in the recording in plain text. `recording_args_for` (`cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs:6367`) already redacts `clipboard_write` text and `browser_dialog`'s `prompt_text`, but not `type_text`, `browser_type` or `set_value`.

### Desired outcome

A caller can type a secret during a recording without its value reaching the recording's files. The turn still shows that text was typed and where.

### Current workaround

After `stop_recording` we replace known values in every text file of the recording folder. The plain text stays on disk until then.

### Affected components and platforms

`recording_args_for`, the text tools, and `replay_trajectory`, which re-invokes each turn's call and can't type a redacted value. Every platform.

### Alternatives and prior art

Always redact typed text, like `clipboard_write`. Simple, but it breaks replay and hides ordinary typing when debugging.

### Implementation ideas

- Per call: `sensitive: true` on the text tools.
- Per session: secret values given to `start_recording` and replaced across the turn's text files.

We need the per-session shape, because the caller knows the values and the agent doing the typing may not mark them. Both change a public tool schema. Does this need an RFC?

title: fix(cua-driver): detect Hyprland input internals instead of pinning versions
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Hyprland 0.57.0 is on Arch and Omarchy edge, and the plugin's input route refuses to configure (`Input is pinned to Hyprland 0.56.2`). Lifting the pin is not enough. Against real 0.57.0 headers, `input_experiment.cpp` also fails to compile: `CWindow::m_isMapped` is now private, `m_isX11` and `getPID()` moved to `IWindowBackend`, and `CInputManager::m_exclusiveLSes` became `m_exclusiveKeyboardLSes` (hyprwm/Hyprland#15899).
- What changed:
  - A new `cua_detect_hyprland_window_api` compile-checks the window and layer-surface internals that input reads. It selects the 0.57 window-backend API or the legacy one, and any other result fails configuration. This follows the existing status-command API probe.
  - Four small helpers in `input_experiment.cpp` route each internal through the detected API.
  - Input no longer pins an exact Hyprland version. `CUA_HYPRLAND_EXPECTED_VERSION` acceptance builds and the release profiles keep their exact pins.
  - The `tests/cmake-api` mock headers cover the backend, legacy, unsupported and repeated-backend tiers.

## Related work

Refs #6232
Refs #5751

This supersedes #6153. That PR handles only the `m_exclusiveLSes` rename, and its own requalification run on its branch failed (run 40838915989). The three window internals above still break the 0.57.0 build there.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: the input route builds on Hyprland 0.57.0 and on 0.56.2. Behaviour on 0.56.2 compiles to the previous expressions.
- One 0.57 behaviour change comes from Hyprland itself, and it fails safe. `surfaceLogicalBox()` now returns nothing for windows that do not accept input: an inactive group tab, an inactive window in monocle, or a window behind a fullscreen window. title: fix(sdk): keep Keyvault payloads consistent when a batch commit fails
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `Vault::upsert_items` writes payloads, then commits the sealed index, then advances the external generation anchor. One cleanup closure handled every failure, which caused two problems:
  - If the anchor write failed after the index had landed, the closure deleted the new payload files. The committed index still listed those items, and `read_payload` returned `NotFound`.
  - If the index write itself failed after an existing item's record had been overwritten, the old index was left pointing at the new record, so the item failed its digest check. Before this change that failure appeared after reopening; `update_meta` also adopted the draft in memory before the write.
- What changed:
  - `save_meta` is split into `write_meta`, which seals the next generation and adopts it in memory only after the write lands, and `record_generation`, which advances the anchor.
  - `upsert_items` stages every record it replaces as a hard link, so nothing is copied. A failure before the commit point removes created files and renames the staged records back, which needs no free space; a restore that still fails is reported, not ignored. A failure after the commit keeps every payload the index references and still returns the error.
  - A record that is already missing counts as nothing to restore, so an upsert can repair an indexed item whose file is gone (review follow-up).

## Related work

Small, self-contained fix; no existing issue or PR found.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: none on success. On these failure paths, the vault now stays readable, matching either the previous committed state or the new one.
- Risk and rollback: the change is local to `cua-keyvault` `store.rs`. Revert to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `upsert_keeps_committed_payloads_when_the_anchor_write_fails`: with the anchor directory removed, a mixed update-and-create batch keeps every indexed item readable, in memory and after reopening.
  - `upsert_restores_overwritten_records_when_the_index_write_fails` (unix): with the vault root read-only and `items/` writable, the existing item keeps its old payload and no new file remains.
  - `upsert_repairs_an_indexed_item_whose_record_is_missing`: an indexed item with a deleted file is repaired by the next upsert, and no staged backup remains after an ordinary update.
  - Each test fails when its fix is reverted, the link restore is made a no-op, or staged-link cleanup is skipped (mutation-checked).
  - On this branch: `cargo test -p cua-keyvault` passed 168 tests across all targets. `cargo clippy -p cua-keyvault --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: a hermetic synthetic probe confirmed the original fault-path observations before the fix.
- Known gaps or CI still required: none known.

title: fix(sandbox): preserve registry identity for QEMU image layers
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on the local QEMU path, `NativeQEMURuntime._image_ref` returned `vm:<ref>` for a registry image only when the image had no build work. A registry image with layers, env or files fell through to `create_session_disk`, which lost the pinned registry identity. `NativeRuntime` already applies VM layers after boot through cua-spacesd and refuses when the image has no spacesd (`_require_spacesd_for_layers`), so those images should keep `vm:<ref>`.
- What changed: a registry image without an explicit disk now always resolves to `vm:<ref>`, and its layers are applied after boot by the existing owner. When layers are applied after boot, `NativeRuntime.start` waits for readiness probes only after the layers have run, because a layer may install the service a probe waits for (review follow-up). Explicit disks and non-registry images are unchanged.

## Related work

Small, self-contained fix; no existing issue or PR found.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: local QEMU sandboxes created from a registry image with layers boot the pinned registry disk and receive their layers after boot, instead of a locally rebuilt session disk.
- Risk and rollback: this is a one-condition change in `runtime/qemu.py`. Revert to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new parametrized `test_qemu_registry_layers_use_the_post_boot_owner` and related cases in `tests/test_runtime_adapters.py`. On this branch, with the native SDK built (`cargo build --release -p cua-sdk`, then the library staged), all 28 adapter tests pass and the full cua-sandbox suite passes (369 passed, 124 skipped). Restoring the old `not has_build_work(image)` condition makes 9 fail. Passing the probes at creation again makes `test_post_boot_layers_run_before_dependent_readiness` fail.

title: `--durable` Spaces are created but never placed or leased on macOS arm64 (0.9.0)
body:
## Summary

`cua spaces create <image> --on auto --durable --name <name>` creates a local Space and then fails with `not found: the durable Space <name> runs as relay:space-<hash>, which does not show yet`. The durable record is written with `state: "running"` but `holder: null` and `lease_expires_in_secs: null`, and no driver ever takes the lease, so every durable agent start fails with `its durable Space is not placed yet`. Retrying does not help: by the second attempt the relay record is visible in `spaces ls --json` and the error is unchanged.

`--on relay:<computer>` is rejected for durable Spaces, so there is no alternate target that works:

```
cua: invalid argument: a durable Space lives on your machines and moves when one goes away:
create it with on="auto" (`--on auto`)
```

## Environment

- `cua` 0.9.0, run from `/Applications/Cua Spaces.app/Contents/MacOS/cua` (the binary whose daemon is running)
- macOS 26.6.2, Apple M4 Pro, arm64, 48 GB RAM
- Host configured with `cua host setup --share spaces`; `host status` reports `runner: app-helper running`, `sharing: on, online`, `desktop: not shared`, `provides Spaces: on (at most 4; macOS VMs at most 2)`
- Space image `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`, local container runtime (colima/lima backend)

## Reproduction

1. `cua host setup --share spaces` — the first run fails at the service step with `launchctl kickstart gui/<uid>/com.trycua.spaces.helper failed: Could not find service`. Relaunching the app (`open -a "Cua Spaces"`) registers the login item and the helper starts. The error message points at System Settings, which is not where the fix is; worth correcting.

2. `cua spaces ls` confirms the machine is online and providing Spaces.

3. `cua spaces create linux --on auto --durable --name fmcheck`

   A local Space is created and running, then:

   ```
   cua: not found: the durable Space fmcheck runs as relay:space-ebce253338e56802, which does not show yet
   ```

4. Wait 25 s, confirm `relay:space-ebce253338e56802` is present in `cua spaces ls --json`, retry the same command. Same error, verbatim.

5. `cua spaces ls --json`, durable records:

   ```json
   {"name":"fmcheck","generation":2,"state":"running","holder":null,"lease_expires_in_secs":null,
    "node":"<host>","space":"relay:space-84f4d03b893a...","restored":"from-scratch",
    "setup":"ok","error":"","spec":{"cpus":4,"memory_mb":8192}}
   ```

   Note `holder: null` and `lease_expires_in_secs: null` alongside `state: "running"`.

6. Reproduced on a second, unrelated durable name, so this is not a stale record belonging to one Space.

7. Any durable agent start against such a Space:

   ```
   cua agent add <name> --harness claude-code --durable --in <space> "..."
   cua agent run <name> claude-code "..." --durable
   → its durable Space is not placed yet
   ```

   `cua agent sessions` reports the session `pending epoch 0 drive 0/5` indefinitely.

## Expected

`--durable` places the Space on a machine in the pool, the durable record acquires a `holder` with a non-null lease, and `cua agent ... --durable` drives the session and resumes it after the agent process or its Space is lost.

## Actual

The Space is created locally; the durable registration points at a `relay:space-<hash>` that never becomes addressable, so it is never placed and never leased. Crash survival is unavailable.

## Impact

There is no way to get a crash-surviving agent on this host. The working fallback is a named persistent agent, whose home is saved to Cua Volume: that survives a Space or agent restart, but not a reboot and not a machine crash — so it does not deliver the durability `--durable` advertises.

## Secondary: two 0.9.0 binaries with different `host setup` flags

- `/Applications/Cua Spaces.app/Contents/MacOS/cua` documents `--share <desktop|spaces|both|none>` and has no `--profile`, `--desktop`, or `--provide-spaces`.
- The CLI installed at `~/.local/bin/cua` documents `--profile desktop|spare`, `--desktop`, `--no-desktop`, `--provide-spaces`, `--no-provide-spaces`, and has no `--share`.

Both print `cua 0.9.0`, so `cua host setup ...` behaves differently depending on which binary PATH resolves, and a command that is correct for one fails on the other. Distinguishing version strings, or reconciling the flags, would remove a real trap.

title: ci: stop PR-scoped cache saves, cap the gate timeout, and measure it
body:
Stops pull requests from writing PR-scoped Rust caches in the E2E matrices, and caps the CI gate at three hours instead of six.

CUA-3211

## What changes

- `.github/workflows/e2e-rust-linux.yml`, `.github/workflows/e2e-rust-windows.yml`: the nine `save-if` guards read `github.ref_type == 'branch'`, which is also true on `pull_request`, so they never gated a PR save. The single `Swatinem/rust-cache` call honours `save-if` itself and was writing PR-scoped entries. It now saves only on `main` or a `workflow_dispatch`. The eight `.github/actions/rust-cache` sites now read `github.event_name != 'pull_request' && ...`. That action already decides `save` itself and only drops a save on the literal `"false"`, so for those eight the change states the intent rather than changing behaviour. Every guard keeps `needs.source.outputs.sha == github.sha`, so a dispatch that certifies an older commit cannot seed main's scope.
- `.github/workflows/ci-gate.yml`: `timeout-minutes` 360 to 180. The gate's longest run on main is well under that, so a wedged gate now releases the required check after three hours.
- Tests: `test_ci_gate_workflow.py` now expects 180. New `test_cache_saves_never_write_pull_request_scope_but_keep_dispatches` on Linux and Windows. It checks only the `save-if:` lines, so `setup-node`'s `cache:` inputs are untouched.

## Not changed

- `ci-gate` `sleep 120`: run creation can still fan out near the end of that window, and `test_gate_catches_a_failing_run_that_appears_inside_the_window` covers it.
- `poll_interval()`: `test_gate_poll_schedule_backs_off_and_stays_within_the_api_budget` pins the schedule.
- `concurrency:` on `ci-release-metadata.yml`: a cancelled call fails the required `validate` check (`test_installer_compatibility_never_cancels_a_superseded_caller`).

## Proof

The scoped repository checks pass on the merged head (`.github/scripts/tests`, em-dash check).

CI on this head is the proof for the workflow change. Every guarded job in the release gate's Linux and Windows E2E legs and in the Rust Linux interactive run logs `save-if: false`. The in-repo rust-cache plan prints `save=false`. After the run, the `refs/pull/6260/merge` cache scope holds only the two `setup-node` npm entries and no Rust or sccache entry. All required checks pass, including `ci-gate`.

title: fix(cua-driver): make accepted HTTP sockets non-inheritable on Windows
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On a Windows checkout, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver --no-fail-fast` fails 15 tests. One cause is a production defect; the rest are tests that only fail on Windows.
- What changed:
  - **Accepted HTTP sockets are non-inheritable on Windows.** Sockets accepted through tokio are inheritable there. A child spawned with `bInheritHandles = TRUE` (any `std::process::Command`) while a connection is open keeps a copy of the socket. The server's close then sends no FIN, the client gets a reset (10054) once the child exits, and a long-lived child keeps a handle to an authenticated connection. `mcp_http::clear_inherit_flag` clears `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` right after `accept` in the MCP HTTP listener, the driver service HTTP listener, and the `mcp_http` test helpers. The Windows named-pipe daemon already creates non-inheritable handles and is unchanged.
  - **Unit-test telemetry captures no longer count as pending sends.** `http_keeps_legacy_initialize_negotiation` started an MCP session, which made a real PostHog request and held `PENDING_SENDS` at 1 for about 800 ms. `pending_send_flush_waits_for_bounded_delivery` asserts the counter starts at 0, so it failed whenever that request was slow, and its panic poisoned `ENV_LOCK` for nine more telemetry tests. Since #6417, `post_to_posthog_with_timeout` already refuses the network under `cfg(test)`, but `spawn_payload` still increments `PENDING_SENDS` and spawns a sender thread. Under `cfg(test)`, `spawn_payload` now drops the event first. Integration tests already disable telemetry through `CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`.
  - **Three checks that assumed `/` or LF now pass on Windows:** `snapshot_dispatch_invariants` normalizes CRLF before searching the included macOS sources (`core.autocrlf` checkouts); `extension_manager_cli_test` compares the preview destination as a `Path`; `active_perception_extension_resolves_owned_worker_arguments` uses `Path::ends_with` for the manifest and runtime arguments.

## Related work

None found (searched open issues and pull requests).

RFC: not required. No public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, permission, or cross-component contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only, and only when the MCP HTTP or driver service HTTP port is configured. Connections now close with FIN even if the driver spawned a child while they were open, and children no longer receive those sockets. No behavior change on macOS or Linux (`clear_inherit_flag` is a no-op there). The telemetry change is `cfg(test)` only.
- Risk and rollback: If `SetHandleInformation` fails, the connection is still served and a warning is logged. Rollback is a plain revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (Windows 11, x64, MSVC):
  - Before: `http_keeps_legacy_initialize_negotiation` failed in 6 of 6 parallel runs of `cargo test -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver` and passed with `--test-threads=1`. Paired with only the `autostart`, `skills`, or `extension_manager` tests it failed; paired with other modules it passed. A trace showed the client received the complete response and the server task returned `Ok(())` before the reset. `GetHandleInformation` reported the accepted socket as inheritable; clearing the flag made the paired runs pass 5 of 5.
  - Before: the ten telemetry failures were one `left: 1, right: 0` assertion plus nine `PoisonError`s. A timestamp trace showed the only in-process send came from the MCP HTTP test, finishing 229–700 ms before the flush test started. Delaying that send by 2 s reproduced the same ten failures in 2 of 2 runs.
  - After: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver --locked --no-fail-fast` passed: 63 targets, 1563 passed, 0 failed. `cargo test -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver` passed 328/328 in 10 consecutive runs.
  - `rustfmt --check` is clean for the changed files.
  - Rebased onto `main` at `c62abf39b` (2026-11-09). Conflicts: `snapshot_dispatch_invariants` keeps the rewritten upstream check and adds the CRLF normalization; `telemetry.rs` keeps the upstream network guard from #6417. After the rebase, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver --locked --no-fail-fast` passed: 67 targets, 1721 passed, 0 failed, 19 ignored (one run). On `main` without this PR, the same command fails 4 tests on this machine.
- Manual or platform evidence: Windows only. Not run on macOS or Linux; the Windows-specific code is behind `cfg(windows)`, and the test changes compare paths component-wise, which holds on every platform.
- Known gaps or CI still required: The second `extension_manager_cli_test` assertion is inside a `review-trust-root` test, which needs a review signing key at build time; it is changed the same way but was not compiled locally. Not reproduced end to end on a running daemon (spawning a browser while an MCP HTTP connection is open); the fix was validated through the test suite.

title: fix(cua-driver): support Hyprland 0.57 in the v3 input plugin (keeps 0.56.2)
body:
## Summary
Makes the Hyprland plugin's **production v3 input path** (`CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT=ON`, `src/input_experiment.cpp`; also used by the `CUA_HYPRLAND_TEST_INPUT` experiment) build on **both Hyprland 0.56.2 and 0.57.0**. Hyprland 0.57 moved or renamed several `CWindow` / `CInputManager` members, so the input path previously failed to compile against 0.57.

## API mapping (0.56.2 → 0.57)
| 0.56.2 | 0.57 | Helper |
|---|---|---|
| `CWindow::m_isMapped` | `CWindow::mapped()` | `cuaWindowMapped()` |
| `CWindow::m_isX11` | `CWindow::backend().isX11()` | `cuaWindowIsX11()` |
| `CWindow::getPID()` | `CWindow::backend().pid()` | `cuaWindowPid()` |
| `g_pInputManager->m_exclusiveLSes` | `g_pInputManager->m_exclusiveKeyboardLSes` | `cuaExclusiveLayers()` |

## How
- `cmake/DetectHyprlandAPI.cmake`: new `cua_detect_hyprland_window_backend_api()` configure-time probe (same style as the status-command probe, C++26, cache unset on reconfigure). It sets `CUA_HYPRLAND_WINDOW_BACKEND_API=0/1`.
- `src/input_experiment.cpp`: the four helpers select the right member per flag; call sites use the helpers.
- `CMakeLists.txt`: exact version list `set(_v 0.56.2 0.57.0)` / `if(NOT HYPRLAND_VERSION IN_LIST _v)` instead of a regex; error message reports the found version.
- `README.md`, `protocol/cua-input-v3.md`: document both supported versions.

## Reviewer note: exclusive layer list
`m_exclusiveKeyboardLSes` is populated under the same condition as 0.56.2's `m_exclusiveLSes` (layers with exclusive keyboard interactivity), so `.grab` fires for the same layers. 0.57 no longer uses that list to confine the pointer, and has no pointer-exclusive replacement, so the check is intentionally keyboard-only (commented in code). Session lock is handled separately by `available()`.

## Testing
- Hyprland 0.57.0 (Omarchy/Arch, system headers): configure picks the backend API, build OK, `ctest` 20/20; plugin loaded live with no config errors and cua-driver delivered foreground click + type into a Chromium window.
- Hyprland 0.56.2: configured against a header tree from the v0.56.2 tag (src headers + generated protocol headers), probe selects the legacy API (and the legacy status-command API), build OK, `ctest` 20/20. Not runtime-tested on a 0.56.2 session.
- `-DCUA_HYPRLAND_EXPECTED_VERSION` pinning still works per version; release profiles are unchanged (still 0.56.2).

title: [Bug]: Hyprland 0.57.0 — unused specialWorkspace omits id, j/monitors fails to parse, list_windows always returns []
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Hyprland 0.57.0 every `list_windows` call returns `{"windows": []}` because the driver cannot deserialize `hyprctl -j monitors`. Hyprland 0.57.0 serializes an unused `specialWorkspace` as `{"address":"","type":"","name":""}` with no `id`, and `struct Workspace { id: i64 }` requires it. One failed `j/monitors` parse empties the whole window inventory. Reproduces on `0.33.4`, `0.38.0` and the `2026-11-01` nightly.

### Reproduction

1. Hyprland 0.57.0, native Wayland session, driver started with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`.
2. Open two or three toplevels. Native Wayland and XWayland windows are affected the same way.
3. `cua-driver call list_windows --json`.

Observed on every call, not intermittent. `cua-driver call get_desktop_state` still returns a valid PNG from the same session, so capture is unaffected.

### Expected behavior

`list_windows` returns the visible toplevels with their bounds, as reported working on Hyprland 0.56.2 in #3247.

### Actual behavior

```json
{ "windows": [] }
```

Daemon log, once per call:

```
WARN platform_linux::wayland: Hyprland window enumeration unavailable: invalid Hyprland IPC JSON: missing field `id` at line 25 column 5
```

`hyprctl -j monitors` on 0.57.0 omits the key for an unused special workspace, and line 25 column 5 of that payload is the closing brace of this object:

```json
"specialWorkspace": {
    "address": "",
    "type": "",
    "name": ""
},
```

`activeWorkspace` and client workspaces still carry `id`, so only an unused special workspace breaks the parse.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver` `0.33.4-2` (omarchy repo), `cua-driver` `0.38.0` (`cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0` release tarball), `cua-driver` `0.38.1-nightly.20261101.41272696578`. All three reproduce.

Operating system and architecture: Omarchy 4.0.6 / Arch Linux x86_64, Hyprland `0.57.0-1`, hyprutils `0.14.3-1`, one output `2048x1115` at scale `1.25`.

Application/browser/window system: native Wayland toplevels plus one XWayland (`kitty`) window. Affected identically.

### Evidence

The log line and the `hyprctl` fragment above. Adding `#[serde(default)]` to `Workspace.id` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/hyprland.rs` and building `0.38.0` locally makes the same session return all three windows with correct bounds, `get_window_state` return a window capture at `1019x1115`, and the AT-SPI walk return 250 nodes.

`Workspace.id` is only read to build the visible-workspace set, via `active_workspace.id` and `special_workspace.id` in `list_windows`, so an absent id on an unused special workspace cannot select a wrong workspace. `Option<i64>` would work as well.

### Workaround and additional context

This matters beyond the empty list, because discovery-only is the recommended route on 0.57.0: #6232 asks for the v3 input route on 0.57.0 and suggests building the plugin without it, and #5751 collects 0.57.0 requalification rows. On 0.57.0 discovery is broken too, so that route currently yields no windows at all.

Local workaround: patch `Workspace.id` with `#[serde(default)]` and rebuild.

title: fix(cua-driver): list windows when Hyprland omits a workspace id
body:
## Why

On Hyprland 0.57.0, `list_windows` returns `[]` for every app. `0.57.0` serializes an unused `specialWorkspace` as `{"address":"","type":"","name":""}`, without the `id` field every earlier release sends, and `struct Workspace { id: i64 }` required it. One failed `j/monitors` parse empties the whole window inventory, so discovery fails before any window identity, AT-SPI, or input path can run.

Fixes #6267

Refs #6232, #5751. Discovery-only is the 0.57.0 workaround suggested in #6232, and #5751 tracks 0.57.0 requalification. Both assume a driver that can list windows on 0.57.0, which this restores.

RFC: none required. This adds no contract, permission, or cross-component change; it restores behavior the driver already documents for a compositor it already supports. If you read 0.57.0 support itself as a compatibility change, say so and I will stop and file an RFC instead.

## What changed

`Workspace.id` is now `#[serde(default)]`, so an absent id reads as `0`, which the visible-workspace filter already treats as "not a live workspace". A reply that does report an id still decides visibility exactly as before, so windows on a special workspace are not hidden. The visible-set computation moved out of `list_windows` into `active_workspaces` so the reply parse and the resulting visible set are asserted together, which is the strongest boundary reachable without adding an injector to shipped code.

One file: `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/hyprland.rs`.

## Scope

- In: the `j/monitors` parse on the Hyprland adapter, plus one unit test covering a reply with and without the field.
- Out: window identity, AT-SPI correlation, input, and every other compositor.
- `#3448` also touches this adapter, but only `wayland/mod.rs`, not this parse, so the two do not overlap.

## Tradeoffs

If Hyprland ever omitted `id` for the *active* workspace, that workspace would read as `0` and be dropped from the visible set, hiding its windows. Hyprland reports the active workspace id in every release observed, and the tolerance only applies to a field that is absent. Rollback is reverting one line plus the extraction.

No `no-release` label is applied: this is a `fix` with a real release entry, not a non-releasing change.

## Blast Radius

Linux/Wayland/Hyprland only. Replies that carry `id` are unchanged. Replies that omit it now parse instead of failing. No API, CLI, or MCP surface change, and no other platform adapter is touched.

## Verification

- Focused tests: `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib wayland::hyprland` passes on this branch, including the new `monitor_reply_accepts_a_special_workspace_without_an_id`.
- `cargo fmt -p platform-linux --check` clean. SPDX header check clean.
- Platform evidence, Hyprland `0.57.0-1` (Omarchy 4.0.6, Arch x86_64, one 2048x1115 output at scale 1.25), release build from this branch, same session, same daemon flags (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`):
  - this branch: `list_windows` returns 3 toplevels with correct bounds, no warnings in the daemon log;
  - upstream `main` rebuilt from the same checkout with this commit reverted: `{"windows": []}` and `WARN platform_linux::wayland: Hyprland window enumeration unavailable: invalid Hyprland IPC JSON: missing field \`id\` at line 25 column 5`.
- Known gap: `scripts/ci/prepush.sh` reports the clippy step failing with 9 pre-existing lints in files this change does not touch (`input/mod.rs`, `get_window_state.rs`, `launch_app.rs`, `press_key.rs`, `wayland/mod.rs`, and the older `SCALED_OUTPUTS` constant in `hyprland.rs`). The identical list appears on unmodified `main` under the pinned `1.97.1` toolchain with `-D warnings`, so this change adds no lint. The Windows clippy step was skipped here (`cargo-xwin` not installed); CI covers it.
- Known gap: the crate-wide `cargo test -p platform-linux` has three failing tests on this host (`input::admission_tests::a_drag_abandoned_after_its_press_still_releases_the_button` and `input::own_dialog_tests::focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened` need `xvfb`; `overlay::tests::unreported_arrival_releases_the_waiter_after_the_cap` asserts on a timing floor). All three fail identically on unmodified `main`, so the suite's baseline is unchanged by this patch.

title: `type_text` inserts the text twice in Zen Browser
body:
### Current behaviour
In Zen Browser (Firefox/Gecko), one `type_text` call in the default `background` delivery mode leaves the text in the field twice.

Repro:
1. Open `data:text/html,<textarea autofocus></textarea>` in Zen.
2. Click into the textarea.
3. Call `type_text` with `{"target": {"kind": "window", "pid": <zen pid>, "window_id": <id>}, "text": "BONSAI_TOKEN abc123"}`. No `element_token` and no `delivery_mode` (so `background`).
4. Read the textarea back (screenshot or `AXValue`).

Expected: `BONSAI_TOKEN abc123`
Actual: `BONSAI_TOKEN abc123BONSAI_TOKEN abc123`

The whole string repeats once, end to end, not character by character. The same happened in a React form on tangled.org, and in Zen's address bar on 0.37.0 (the URL appeared twice). With `delivery_mode: "foreground"` on the same textarea, nothing was inserted. Pasting through the clipboard (`set clipboard` + cmd+V) inserts the text once.

### Likely cause
The `type_text` description says background mode does an AX insert (`kAXSelectedText`), then falls back to CGEvent typing, and that `AXValue` in web content doesn't prove the DOM saw the text. In Gecko both paths seem to land: the AX insert goes through, the result is treated as unverifiable, and the keystroke fallback types the same text again.

### Environment
- cua-driver 0.38.0 (also seen on 0.37.0), standalone CuaDriver.app, called over MCP
- macOS 27.0.1, arm64
- Zen Browser 1.24b

### Done when
A single background `type_text` into a Gecko text field (Zen or Firefox) leaves the text exactly once, either because the fallback is skipped when the AX insert takes effect, or because Gecko web content is routed to only one path.

---
Issue found and reported by Opus 5.5.

title: [Feature]: Evaluate get_window_state query predicates in-traversal and collapse anonymous wrapper depth
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

Dense native and Electron/Chromium windows (such as Apple Maps, macOS Mail message outlines, IDEs, and multi-pane studio/telemetry apps with `1,500+` accessibility nodes) routinely exceed `get_window_state`'s `max_elements` walk cap (`default 300`, `max 2,000`) inside a single large table or outline before DFS reaches sibling panes or footer controls:

1. **Post-walk `query` starvation**: `cua-driver-core::element_query::filter_tree_markdown` applies `query` *after* the platform walker has already stopped at `max_elements`. As a result, `get_window_state(query="Apply")` returns zero matches whenever `"Apply"` sits at DFS node `301+` (or `2,001+`), even though the caller explicitly asked to search for `"Apply"`.
2. **Anonymous web/Electron wrapper inflation on `max_depth`**: `max_depth` counts raw accessibility nodes rather than semantic containers. In Chromium/Electron apps, nested anonymous `<div>` wrappers (`AXGroup` / generic UIA or AT-SPI groups with no title, label, value, identifier, or primary action) consume `max_depth: 2..3` before traversal reaches actual split panes or toolbars.

### Desired outcome

1. **In-traversal `query` filtering**: When `query` is passed to `get_window_state`, evaluate the match predicate during traversal so non-matching rows do not exhaust `max_elements` (bounded by `timeout_ms` and a raw-visit safety ceiling), preserving matched rows and their ancestor container headers.
2. **Logical-depth / wrapper-transparent shallow reads**: Allow shallow structural reads (`max_depth` / skeleton overviews) to skip incrementing semantic depth on anonymous, actionless wrapper groups (while still enforcing a raw recursion ceiling) and surface child-count hints at depth boundaries.

### Current workaround

Callers must raise `max_elements` to `2,000` on full-window reads (incurring `1,000+` cross-process IPC reads per step and still failing past `2,000` nodes) or rely on manual `max_depth` tuning per app.

### Affected components and platforms

- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core` (`element_query.rs`, `tool_schema.rs`)
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos` (`ax/tree.rs`)
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows` (UIA tree walker)
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux` (AT-SPI tree walker)

### Alternatives and prior art

- Prior art such as `vercel-labs/agent-desktop` separates `raw_depth` from `logical_depth` (skipping unnamed, valueless web wrappers) and evaluates `find` predicates inside the traversal loop before allocating output refs.
- In controlled macOS benchmarks on a 1,500-node 4-region AppKit fixture (sidebar + 336-row telemetry grid + inspector + commit footer), post-walk truncation starved standard window reads before reaching the footer, whereas combining shallow region discovery with targeted subtree reads reduced cumulative `observe + verify` time by `31.1x` (`15,998 ms -> 514 ms`) and achieved `100%` task completion.

### Implementation ideas

- Pass an optional case-folded query matcher into the platform walkers so `max_elements` bounds *emitted* matches while a separate raw-node ceiling + `timeout_ms` bounds total IPC work.
- Classify anonymous wrapper groups (`AXGroup` / generic group with empty label/title/value/identifier and no press/value action) so shallow overview walks do not stall inside nested DOM wrappers.

- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): suppress macOS foreground focus steal during isolated browser launch
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On macOS, `browser_prepare` with `mode: "isolated"` and `posture: "background"` spawns standalone Chromium directly via `std::process::Command` (`BrowserPlatform::spawn_isolated_browser` previously fell through to the default unguarded spawn). Even with `--no-startup-window` and background posture, Chromium calls `NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps:)` inside `applicationDidFinishLaunching`, briefly stealing foreground activation and key focus from the user's active window during cold start.
- What changed: `MacOsBrowserPlatform::spawn_isolated_browser` now wraps the child spawn in `FocusStealPreventer::begin_suppression` (`BrowserPrepare.isolated.pre` -> `BrowserPrepare.isolated.post`) paired with a bounded (`<= 2.8 s`) `watch_self_activation` SkyLight key-focus/z-order guard that stops immediately if the child process exits early, followed by `restore_front_app_if_browser_front`.

Refs #6270

or cross-component contract change): Not required (internal macOS platform fix preserving existing `browser_prepare` background-posture contract; no schema, CLI, SDK, or permission changes).

title: perf(cua-driver): poll AXWebArea stabilization instead of sleeping 500ms on Chromium AX wake

## Summary

- Problem this solves: On macOS, `ax::enablement::await_web_content` unconditionally slept for `CHROMIUM_SETTLE_SECONDS` (`500 ms`) after detecting a populated `AXWebArea` and re-asserting `AXEnhancedUserInterface` / `AXManualAccessibility`, even when Chromium's accessibility subtree had already finished materializing within `50–100 ms`.

title: feat(cua-driver): add macOS AX root_element_token subtree walk, include_menubar, and pre-seeded regions
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On dense native and Electron macOS windows (`1,000+` AX nodes across split panes, sidebars, toolbars, and detail tables), the depth-first `max_elements` walk can exhaust its budget inside the first large pane before sibling panes are even discovered, forcing agents into full-window `full_output: true` walks (`~15 s` of cross-process AX IPC) to reach or re-verify controls in later regions. In addition, `query` / `full_output` walks previously expanded `AXMenuBar` unconditionally even when callers only wanted in-window content.
- What changed:
  - **Pre-seeded `regions` and `surfaces` (macOS)**: Before the depth-first walk truncates at `max_elements`, `ax::tree` performs a shallow top-level scan of landmark containers (`AXSplitGroup`, `AXScrollArea`, `AXToolbar`, `AXTabGroup`, `AXOutline`, `AXTable`, `AXSheet`, `AXPopover`, etc.), publishing `structuredContent.regions[]` (each carrying an addressable `region_token` of the form `<snapshot_id>:r<N>`, bounds, role, label, and `child_count_hint`) plus window-level `structuredContent.surfaces` (`window`, `sheet`, `popover`, `menubar`) even when the element walk truncates early.
  - **`root_element_token` subtree walk (`get_window_state`)**: Accepts an element token (`<snapshot_id>:<row>`) or region token (`<snapshot_id>:r<N>`) from a live snapshot of the same `(pid, window_id)` and walks only that container's AX subtree while preserving window-level status `AXStaticText` siblings for post-action verification. Refuses fail-closed without evicting the existing live snapshot on `invalid_element_token`, `stale_element_token` (including `current_snapshots`), `conflicting_element_target`, or `detached_root_element`, and returns an explicit `root_element_token_unsupported` refusal on Linux and Windows.
  - **`include_menubar` (`get_window_state`)**: Optional boolean (default `true`, preserving existing behavior); setting `include_menubar: false` skips `AXMenuBar` traversal completely on macOS.
  - **`ViewKey` isolation & MCP reference docs**: Tracks `subtree_scope` and `include_menubar` in `ViewKey` so `since: "latest"` never cross-diffs a scoped subtree read against a full-window baseline, and regenerates the MCP tool reference and macOS/Linux/Windows registry snapshots.

## Related work

Refs #6270

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Additive optional MCP tool parameters (`root_element_token`, `include_menubar`) and additive `structuredContent` metadata (`regions`, `surfaces`) on `get_window_state`; the portable `GetWindowStateInput` UniFFI/Python/TypeScript/C-ABI contract (`SchemaMode::PortableSubset`) is unchanged. Happy to add a companion `docs/rfcs/` document if maintainers would like one for the new optional MCP parameters before merge.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - Default `get_window_state` behavior when `root_element_token` and `include_menubar` are omitted is preserved on all platforms; macOS responses gain additive `structuredContent.regions` and `structuredContent.surfaces` arrays when landmarks/surfaces are present.
  - Linux and Windows accept `include_menubar` without error and fail closed with `root_element_token_unsupported` if `root_element_token` is supplied.
  - `SnapshotPayload` adds default-implemented `region_len()` (`0`) and `retain_region()` (`None`) methods, keeping non-macOS `SnapshotStore` payloads source-compatible.
- Risk and rollback: Refusal paths in `SnapshotStore::resolve_root_token` and `GetWindowStateTool` run before snapshot publication so an invalid, stale, cross-window, or detached `root_element_token` never clobbers the caller's live snapshot. Revert this commit to roll back cleanly.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast` (`SPDX headers`, `generated docs are current`, `cargo fmt`)
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib` (`1110 passed; 0 failed`, including `element_token::tests::region_and_element_root_tokens_round_trip` and `snapshot_store::tests::resolve_root_token_handles_elements_regions_and_preserves_snapshot_on_refusal`)
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib ax::` (`63 passed; 0 failed`) and `tools::get_window_state` (schema and view option tests)
  - `CUA_TEST_REQUIRE_DRIVER_BIN=1 cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test schema_consistency_test --test compatibility_contract_test` (`pass`)
  - `node docs/node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs --test scripts/docs-generators/runner.test.ts scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.test.ts scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver-platform.test.ts scripts/docs-generators/prose-style.test.ts scripts/docs-generators/reference-quality.test.ts` (`45 pass; 0 fail`)
- Manual or platform evidence: Benchmarked on macOS against a 4-region, `1,500`-row native AppKit split-view harness where pane 4 sits past the default `max_elements` walk budget:
  - Full-window fallback (`full_output: true`, `max_elements: 2000`): `15,998.2 ms` (`observe + click + verify`)
  - Pre-seeded `region_token` (`s...:r3`) -> `get_window_state(root_element_token="s...:r3", include_menubar=false)`: **`514.5 ms`** (`31.1x` speedup, `0` foreground focus steals, `11/11` end-to-end suite pass).

title: fix(spaces): enforce the notch helper line limit before appending
body:
## Summary

The notch helper promises to drop lines longer than 32 MiB. The check currently covers only the unfinished buffer. If a newline arrives in the same chunk as the whole line, or as the bytes that take it over the limit, the oversized line reaches the decoder.

Check the remaining byte allowance before appending each segment, including the one before a newline. Drop the whole oversized line and continue with the next one. Lines exactly at the limit still pass, and one chunk may contain several valid lines.

## Related work

Small, self-contained fix; no linked issue. No RFC is needed: this enforces the existing `NotchProtocol.maxLine` contract without changing the wire format.

## Compatibility and risk

Only the macOS notch helper changes. The main risk is discarding a valid line at the boundary or losing the next message after a rejection; both have regression coverage. The two-file change can be reverted on its own.

## Validation

Checked commit: `dc7f3a43a1f1f3ba9229e52bc19c9bf6a4319b98`.

- `libs/spaces-notch-swift/scripts/test.sh`: all 21 tests passed. New regressions fail against the original implementation for complete oversized lines and lines whose final chunk crosses the limit. Exact-limit, fragmented-input and recovery controls pass.
- `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast --base origin/main`: applicable SPDX check passed.
- `swift build --package-path libs/spaces-notch-swift -c release --product CuaSpacesNotch` and the built helper's `--selftest`: passed.
- Sent an oversized JSON quit line to the optimized helper's stdin, then hello and quit. It dropped the oversized record, answered hello and exited 0 without stderr. A separate hello exactly at 32 MiB also passed.
- Local platform: macOS 26.5.1, arm64, Apple Swift 6.3.2; the package uses Swift 5 language mode.

The visible Electron app was not exercised. These checks cover the splitter's public interface and the real helper process.

As of November 3, 2026, this PR is ready for review. The CLA is signed and the contributor-attribution check passed. Codex's automated review completed on the checked commit with no findings; no human review has been submitted. title: fix(spaces): preserve newer typing across repeated notch search echoes
body:
## Summary

The notch helper can replace newer typing with an older search echo. Type "a", then "ab", and let the host send "a" twice while other notch state changes. The first echo is skipped. The second is treated as a host replacement, so the search goes back to "a".

Remember the last text received from the core. Another state carrying that text does not consume another acknowledgement. New host text still acknowledges typing or replaces it, and a closed panel's empty query clears pending typing even when the previous host text was already empty.

## Related work

Small, self-contained fix; no linked issue. No RFC is needed: the existing search events and state messages keep their wire format and meaning.

## Compatibility and risk

Only the macOS notch helper changes. Host clears must keep working, including Escape while open and closing after a pending backspace to empty. Focused tests cover those paths, repeated empty and nonempty echoes, and typing that returns to an earlier query. The two-file change can be reverted on its own.

## Validation

Checked commit: `d32f6c3000506ce676d96f99d268705b1a74b55d`.

- `libs/spaces-notch-swift/scripts/test.sh`: all 22 tests passed. New regressions reproduce the rollback against the original implementation. They drive the real Swift helper's public search/receive interface with its existing panel-free fixture, check the text the views read, and confirm unrelated state still applies.
- `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast --base origin/main`: applicable SPDX check passed.
- `swift build --package-path libs/spaces-notch-swift -c release --product CuaSpacesNotch` and the built helper's `--selftest`: passed.
- Local platform: macOS 26.5.1, arm64, Apple Swift 6.3.2; the package uses Swift 5 language mode.

Physical typing in the visible Electron app was not exercised. GitHub CI is held for workflow approval before any jobs have started (GitHub reports action_required). The contributor-attribution check passed; the CLA check requires the author's acceptance. The release-metadata and macOS test workflows have not run, and no reviews have been submitted. This PR remains a draft until the contribution gates and required checks clear.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC.
- [x] Tests and platform evidence are included; remaining gaps are explained.
- [x] The title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse unsafe background input for UTM
body:
## 개요
- UTM guest console에서 background text 입력이 A 키 반복으로 변형되는 경로를 안전하게 거절합니다.
- 공개 버그 #6296의 재현 경로를 대상으로 하며, 서명된 배포 앱이나 VM 설정은 바꾸지 않습니다.

## 문제 배경
Cua Driver의 PID-routed Unicode text 이벤트는 keycode 0과 Unicode payload를 함께 보냅니다. UTM은 payload 대신 physical key transition을 guest에 전달할 수 있어, 정상 문자열이 반복된 a로 오염됩니다. 이 경로를 성공으로 보고하면 자동화가 잘못된 명령을 실행할 위험이 있습니다.

## 무엇을 바꿨는가
- platform-macos keyboard: com.utmapp.UTM을 input forwarder로 exact-match 분류했습니다.
- type_text와 modifier hotkey: background route를 UTM_REQUIRES_FOREGROUND_HID로 fail-closed 처리하고 명시적 foreground HID/window_id만 안내합니다.
- 기존 Screen Sharing의 SCREEN_SHARING_REQUIRES_FOREGROUND_HID 계약은 유지하도록 회귀 테스트를 추가했습니다.

## 검증
- cargo test -p platform-macos --lib: 638 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored
- cargo +1.97.1 clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings: 통과
- cargo +1.97.1 build -p cua-driver: 통과
- scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast: 통과
- read-only Codex 구현 검토는 실행했지만 이 환경의 runner가 최종 출력을 보존하지 않아, 이 Draft PR에서 독립 리뷰를 다시 받아야 합니다.

Refs #6296. 이 변경은 손상되는 background 경로를 거절할 뿐 foreground 자동화를 넓히지 않습니다.

title: [Bug]: get_browser_state closes the CDP connection when DOM.getDocument is over 16 MiB
body:
### Primary area Cua Driver ### Summary `get_browser_state` (both `semantic_v2` and `dom_refs_v1`) closes the driver's CDP connection on any page whose `DOM.getDocument` reply is over 16 MiB. The read is refused, the browser target is lost, and each loss uses one of the grant's three reconnects. ### Reproduction 1. Serve a page with few elements and a large DOM, using Node on the machine running the browser: ```js import http from "node:http"; const attribute = "x".repeat(1024 * 1024); http.createServer((req, res) => { const mb = Number(new URL(req.url, "http://x").searchParams.get("mb")); res.setHeader("content-type", "text/html"); res.end("

size test

" + Array.from({ length: mb }, () => `
x
`).join("")); }).listen(8123, "127.0.0.1"); ``` 2. Start `cua-driver mcp --direct`, call `browser_prepare` with `strategy: {kind: "existing_profile"}` for a Chromium window, and bind it with `get_browser_state`. 3. `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:8123/?mb=15`, then call `get_browser_state` with `snapshot_format: "semantic_v2"` and with `"dom_refs_v1"`. Both succeed. 4. `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:8123/?mb=16` and repeat. Each format closes the socket. 5. Keep binding the window again and repeating step 4 at 20 MB. The fourth bind in a row refuses until `browser_prepare` runs again. This reproduces every time. ### Expected behavior A read succeeds or refuses without losing the connection and the binding. ### Actual behavior ``` refused (browser_route_unavailable): DOM.getDocument failed: CDP socket closed during DOM.getDocument ``` The target is lost with the socket, so calls with its `target_id` fail with `browser_binding_stale` until the window is bound again. After three losses: ``` refused (browser_reconnect_exhausted): the bounded existing-profile reconnect attempts did not establish a proven browser socket ``` Real pages reach this. A Google Flights results page measured 26.8 MB from `DOM.getDocument {depth: -1, pierce: true}`, across about 96,000 elements. ### Environment - Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver-rs v0.38.0 release binary, linux-x86_64. The limit is still in `main` at a58b3edd3. - Operating system and architecture: Linux x86_64, X11 - Application/browser/window system/image: Chromium in `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04` ### Evidence Results from the reproduction above, on the stock release binary: | DOM size | `semantic_v2` | `dom_refs_v1` | | --- | --- | --- | | 15 MB | ok, 436 ms | ok, 277 ms | | 16 MB | socket closed | socket closed | | 20 MB | socket closed | socket closed | ### Workaround and additional context The likely cause: `CdpConnection::connect` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/cdp_ws.rs` calls `tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(ws_url)`, so tungstenite's defaults apply: `max_frame_size` 16 MiB and `max_message_size` 64 MiB. Chromium sends each DevTools message as one frame, so a larger reply is a protocol error on the read side, and `read_loop` treats any read error as a closed socket. The bounded-depth fallback in `semantic_document` doesn't run for this, because `is_semantic_document_size_error` doesn't match "CDP socket closed". A patched build that connects with `connect_async_with_config` and no frame limit stopped the socket closing: ```rust let mut config = WebSocketConfig::default(); config.max_frame_size = None; config.max_message_size = None; tokio_tungstenite::connect_async_with_config(ws_url, Some(config), false) ``` That isn't enough alone. With that change a `semantic_v2` read on Google Flights took 31 to 34 seconds, in a build with `opt-level=2` and no LTO, and a `query` result reached 303 KB. Chromium's three replies took about 6 seconds of that when timed separately (`DOM.getDocument` 1.3 s, `DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot` 2.4 s, `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` 2.3 s), so most of the time looks like processing in the driver. Workaround: `run_steps` by role and name and `get_window_state` with a `query` use AT-SPI, so they work on these pages. Reading the page's text over a separate DevTools connection also works. `browser_prepare` restores the grant after `browser_reconnect_exhausted`. ### Submission checks - [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests. - [x] This issue describes a single problem. - [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: feat(spaces): Secure Spaces, child Spaces, conformance, space jobs and the macOS developer-tools image, behind experiments
body:
This puts the next set of Spaces features on main behind experiment switches, with the fixes that need no switch already merged earlier (QEMU monitor on a private socket, microVM restart, Containerization pulls).

## What changes when nobody turns anything on

Nothing a user can see. The new commands and flags are hidden from `--help` and refuse with how to enable them. Spaces keep the open network they have today. Persisted fields are additive and optional.

## Secure Spaces and experiments (off by default)

- `cua experiments list|enable|disable`; switches live in `<CUA_HOME>/experiments/`, or `CUA_EXPERIMENTS=secure-spaces,-child-spaces` per process.
- With `secure-spaces` on: network presets, host-side enforcement, per-tree networks, `cua network`. A Space made before the switch keeps running; restarting a stopped one is refused with the two ways forward (turn it off, or copy files out and recreate).

## Child Spaces (off by default)

Spaces can create child Spaces under a tree budget, and keep commands running as services. Switch: `child-spaces`.

## Runtime conformance

A registry of runtime behaviors, a generated docs page, and a live driver (`libs/cua/scripts/conformance/run.py`). No behavior change.

## Settings, Advanced, Labs

Rows for the two experiments appear only once an experiment is already on. Hidden otherwise, so no UI change for anyone by default.

## Space jobs

Run a job in a Space and read its result, through the Spaces tools and the SDK (`space_jobs`). Additive tools; the tool count and contract are regenerated.

## macOS developer-tools image

The macOS Space with Xcode as a tier (`ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26-xcode`), built locally as the fallback when it is not published. The Xcode build only runs on the manual dispatch path, not on pull requests.

## Also in this update

- The interim guest-side guard that drops inbound IPv4 options in Linux VM images (CVE-2026-98432), from its own branch.
- cua-vmm now embeds committed copies of the macOS recipe files (`libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/recipe/`), so the Rust build reads only `libs/cua`. A test fails when a copy falls behind; refresh with `scripts/images/sync-cua-vmm-recipe.sh`.
- The doctor no longer reports the child-Space tools as a mismatch between `/mcp` and ListTools (they are the MCP server's alone).
- User-facing strings in this change say "computers".
- The CLI Spaces page and the Spaces tools reference are split to stay under the docs page limits.

## Known limits

- With secure-spaces on, macOS microVMs, QEMU on macOS and Windows, macOS VMs, Apple's Containerization and your own cloud refuse or start without network rather than open.
- A QEMU VM started by this build keeps its monitor on a private socket; stop QEMU VMs with this build before going back to an older one.

## Checks run locally

prepush with bindings (all pass except the two items below), regenerated contract, bindings and docs, `buf breaking`, gitleaks, nextest for the touched crates and the spacesd workspace, web check (186 files, 1293 tests), Windows clippy for the touched crates.

- Windows clippy of the whole `libs/cua` workspace fails in the opus C build of `cua-media-codec` (an untouched crate) on this machine; the touched crates pass.
- nextest failures are the ones that also fail on main on a Mac: qemu `live_tpm_vm_refusals`, `providers`, the `scale` tests, a mesh timing test, and the TCP probe in `a_failing_health_check_restarts_a_service`.
- The old-build-then-new-build run over one isolated home and the replica chaos run passed on the earlier stack (secure spaces, child Spaces); they were not repeated on this final head.

## Needs a maintainer

None of the commits here edits a workflow file (the push token cannot).

## CI state at 92fbcbae5

Every check passes except `release` in "CD: Image omarchy" (and `ci-gate`, which fails only because of it). No macOS job timed out.

The Omarchy doctor fails on the display fixture ("grid not located", `input.click`, `input.drag`, `input.scroll`, `screenshot.fixture_pixel`); the build and the 14 e2e checks pass. The same image job is red on unrelated branches: `ci/omarchy-edge-watch` (run 41536122372, same doctor failure), `chore/remove-fleet-mentions` (run 41502099729, an Omarchy mirror signature file over pacman's size limit) and the Hyprland pin and requalify branches. This change only adds `nftables` and the IPv4 options guard unit to that image.
