title: fix(cua-driver): accept CDP frames within the message budget
body:
## Summary

A `DOM.getDocument` reply above 16 MiB closes the CDP socket even though the client already allows messages up to 64 MiB. Chromium sends these replies in a single frame, so tungstenite's default 16 MiB frame limit rejects them before the message limit is reached.

Configure the shared CDP client with a 64 MiB frame limit and retain the existing 64 MiB aggregate-message limit. Both snapshot formats retain the original connection and binding across repeated 20 MiB reads; a real Chrome transport probe also covers 27 MiB replies.

## Related work

Refs #6299.

No RFC: this aligns the frame allowance with the existing message budget; it adds no public API, protocol field or permission.

## Compatibility and risk

- The shared client is used by macOS, Windows and Linux browser adapters.
- Both single-frame and fragmented messages retain an explicit 64 MiB wire-size bound. JSON parsing and cloning can use more memory than the wire payload.
- Replies above 64 MiB still close the connection. Graceful handling beyond that limit and large-DOM processing performance remain unresolved, so this PR uses `Refs`, not `Fixes`.
- Rollback is a revert of the connection configuration.

## Validation

On macOS arm64 with the repository-pinned Rust 1.97.1:

- Before the production change, both new existing-profile snapshot regressions failed with `DOM.getDocument failed: CDP socket closed during DOM.getDocument`.
- After the fix, each format reads a 20 MiB-attribute DOM four times using the original target/tab IDs, checks nonempty refs and one WebSocket handshake, then completes a normal read.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p cua-driver-core --lib`: **1,113 passed, one existing ignored test**.
- Frame-header and fragmented-message regressions protect both size bounds. Removing each respective cap caused its guard test to fail; restoring the patch passed the focused suite.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`, workspace formatting, core doc tests, fast pre-push gates and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Supporting real-browser probe: the production `CdpConnection` read a loopback fixture in disposable headless Chrome **156.0.8078.76**, with page sizes `15, 16, 20, 27, 20, 20, 20` MiB. Every read and subsequent page-text query succeeded on the same connection.

## Remaining verification

This is a draft pending ordinary CI and the canonical desktop/browser matrix required before readiness. The headless probe verifies real Chrome CDP transport; it does not certify native window attachment, Chrome/Edge desktop behavior, or Windows/Linux execution.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused change; the description matches the diff.
- [x] No RFC is required for this bug fix.
- [x] Regression tests and platform limitations are recorded.
- [x] Conventional Commit title describes the production change.
- [x] No external implementation was incorporated.

This is a user-visible driver fix; `no-release` is not requested.

title: fix(images): omarchy drops the Hyprland 0.57-only bell_sound key while pinned to 0.56.2 (CUA-3107)
body:
Linear: CUA-3107 (parent CUA-3105). Stacked on #6326.

**What changes for users:** the Omarchy Space image boots to a clean desktop again (no Hyprland config-error bar), and its windows behave as before, so the image can be published.

**Cause.** The image build pins Hyprland to 0.56.2-4 because `cua-hyprland-plugin` requires that exact version (#6326). Omarchy edge's config package (`omarchy-dev`) has no older versions to pin, and it moved from r7437.g7f4b1dd (last green image, 30 Oct) to r7561.ga69b19f, which targets Hyprland 0.57 and sets `misc.bell_sound`. Hyprland 0.56.2 rejects the whole `hl.config` block in `default/hypr/looknfeel.lua` (`focus_on_activate`, dwindle, cursor and more) and shows a config-error bar. Both doctor lanes then fail `screenshot.fixture_pixel` and the three input checks that need the grid. The re-run of #6326 failed the same way in both lanes. cua-spacesd is not the cause.

**Fix (stopgap).** Drop only that key at build time, and only while the installed Hyprland is older than 0.57. The build fails if the key is still there. The real fix is to qualify the plugin for Hyprland 0.57 so the image can follow Omarchy edge again. That work is tracked on CUA-3107, and this stopgap turns itself off once it lands.

title: fix(cua-driver): qualify the Hyprland plugin for Hyprland 0.57.0 (CUA-3107)
body:
Cua's Hyprland plugin now builds against Hyprland 0.57.0, so the Omarchy image can follow Omarchy edge again instead of staying on 0.56.2.

Refs CUA-3107 (and CUA-3105, #6326, #6328).

## What changed
- Ported the input code to the 0.57 plugin headers. The plugin API version is now 0.2. Only three things the plugin uses changed:
  - Window state moved behind `CWindow::backend()`: `m_isX11` is now `backend().isX11()`, `getPID()` is now `backend().pid()`, and `m_isMapped` is private (use `mapped()`).
  - `CInputManager::m_exclusiveLSes` is now `m_exclusiveKeyboardLSes`. It still counts as a grab, so behavior is unchanged.
  - The hyprctl command API is the Socket1 one, which the plugin already supported.
- `src/hyprland_compat.hpp` holds these shims, selected by CMake (`CUA_HYPRLAND_WINDOW_BACKEND_API`). 0.56.2 still builds.
- Input builds are accepted for 0.56.2 and 0.57.0 (was 0.56.2 only). The Arch recipe defaults to 0.57.0 headers.
- Omarchy image: right after the package install, the build now fails early if the installed `hyprland` differs from the version `cua-hyprland-plugin` pins.

Checked by diffing the Hyprland v0.56.2 and v0.57.0 headers for every symbol the plugin uses. Nothing was compiled on the authoring host; CI is the qualification (below).

## Relation to #6326 and #6328
Both are still open and are not touched here. #6326 (archive pin) is still right while the packaged plugin pins 0.56.2. #6328 (drop `bell_sound` below 0.57) turns itself off once the image has Hyprland 0.57, so it can be closed after the follow-ups below.

## Needs after merge (follow-ups)
1. Cut a cua-hyprland-plugin release from this source.
2. Update Omarchy's AUR/package entry to that release, rebuilt against `hyprland=0.57.0-1`. The image installs Omarchy's packaged plugin, so it only moves to 0.57 after this.
3. Re-run the image build and doctor lanes, then close #6328 if it is still open.
4. The native release kit (`packaging/release`, the 0.56.2-1 profile) is a separate certified bundle and is not changed here.

## Requalification
Run through CI with workflow_dispatch on this branch: Hyprland plugin requalify, Omarchy image build (no publish) and the image doctor.

title: ci: Omarchy edge watch, plugin release on pin change, gated Omarchy update request (CUA-3108)
body:
Linear: CUA-3108. Approved by Francesco, 2 Nov 2026.

**What changes for users:** Omarchy edge moves are caught the day they happen, the plugin is requalified and released without hand work, and Omarchy is asked to update only after Francesco approves.

- `Omarchy: edge watch` (daily + dispatch): detects a new Hyprland or omarchy config package, compares with `omarchy-qualified.json`, then lints Omarchy's Lua config (real run: flags `misc.bell_sound` against Hyprland 0.56.2-4, clean on 0.57.0-3), reruns requalification, and the image build with doctor lanes (new `gate_only` input, never publishes). Green opens a pin PR with auto-merge; red opens or updates one issue (failing step, log excerpt, doctor screenshot artifact link). Failed runs reach Alertmanager via `workflow-failure-alerts.yml`.
- `Release: Omarchy plugin`: when `plugin_pin` moves on main, builds the kit with `bundle.py` and queues auto-merge on the Driver release PR; the tag then publishes plugin assets through the existing Driver release.
- `Omarchy: update request`: prepares the Omarchy issue text (job summary + artifact); posting is in the `omarchy-outreach` environment and needs reviewer approval and the secret `OMARCHY_ISSUE_TOKEN`.
- Post-update recheck: when Omarchy ships our released plugin, the lanes rerun and a green run drops the recorded stopgaps (cua#6328) and closes their open PRs.

Also: `workflow_call` added to the requalification workflow, `gate_only` to the image workflow, unit tests wired into the plugin CI. README section: "Omarchy edge watch".

title: feat(cua-driver): fast path with act-time target guards, behind a default-off flag (CUA-3102)
body:
Linear: CUA-3102

Adds the Cua Driver "fast path" behind a new `fast_path` setting, which is **off by default**. With it on, the agent can act on the elements it already read, without taking a fresh full snapshot first. Before each action the driver checks that the target is still the one the agent saw, and it refuses when the target changed.

**For users:** with the setting off, nothing changes. With `set_config {"fast_path": "guard"}` (or `on`), a click on something that moved, changed or disappeared since the last read is refused with `target_changed` and a pointer to fresh state, instead of landing on the wrong thing.

### What's in it
- `cua-driver-core::fast_path` holds the platform-free checks, all std-only and unit-tested:
  - AX fingerprint check: gone, relabelled, role changed, moved, resized, hit mismatch.
  - Pixel check for sparse or no-tree targets: a read-time crop compared with two act-time crops 50 ms apart, an animation settle budget, and a template match for pure shifts, with cursor masking and a wider tolerance for remote desktops.
  - Window guards, per-target classification, and the changed-region finder.
- Modes:
  - `off` (default): no checks.
  - `shadow`: checks run and report `would_refuse`, but never refuse.
  - `guard`: refuses on a mismatch.
  - `on`: guard, plus direct actions return a `since:latest` delta in the same result, and `since:` re-reads are tree-only unless the tree is sparse.
- The setting works on macOS, Linux and Windows through `set_config`/`get_config` (env `CUA_DRIVER_FAST_PATH`). The act-time guards are wired for macOS `click` only so far (token and pixel paths).

### Tests
- Unit tests for each guard reason and the tolerance edges.
- A randomized race over 1,000 iterations per delivery mode (move, swap, remove, row reuse, cover): zero wrong-target actions, zero static false refusals.
- A canvas target that moves or is redrawn, a no-tree window, 1,000 blinking-caret clicks, and a remote-desktop stream with noise and an in-content cursor.

### Flag-off safety
With `fast_path` off, every new entry point returns before doing any work. The only visible changes are the new `fast_path` key in the `set_config` schema and in `get_config`/`set_config` output.

### Not yet
- Guards for the other action tools (`double_click`, `drag`, `type_text`…) and for Windows and Linux.
- A per-call `verify_target` override (implemented in core, not exposed in schemas yet).
- A source-rect window capture for cheaper act-time crops (today each crop captures the whole window).
- Change crops in sparse-target results.

title: feat(cua-driver): keep typed secrets out of recordings
body:
Closes #6250. Linear: CUA-3110.

**What changes for users:** you can type a password during a recording without it landing in the recording's files. Pass it to `start_recording` in `redact_values`, and every turn shows `[redacted]` in its place.

## Changes

- `start_recording` takes an optional `redact_values` (1 to 64 non-empty strings). The values are held in memory only, never written, and cleared on stop or restart. Validation errors name the position, never the value.
- Each turn's `action.json` (arguments, result summary, action truth) and `before_state.json` / `after_state.json` / `app_state.json` are scrubbed. JSON state is scrubbed structurally, so an escaped character can't hide a value. Longer values are replaced first.
- A turn whose arguments lost a value is marked `"redacted": true`. `replay_trajectory` refuses it instead of typing the placeholder.
- Screenshots and video are not altered (the OS masks secure fields). The docs and tool description say so.
- The generated MCP reference gains the new row.

This takes the per-session shape from the issue: the caller knows the values even when the typing agent doesn't. It adds one optional field and changes no existing behaviour.

## Tests

- `redact_values_never_reach_turn_files` walks every file a turn writes and checks that no value appears, raw or JSON-escaped. It also checks the `redacted` mark and that stopping forgets the values.
- Separate tests cover longest-first replacement, schema validation that never echoes a value, and the replay refusal.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib -- recording redact`: all pass except `turn_capture_brackets_action_and_preserves_post_action_aliases`. That test fails the same way on unmodified `main` when run alongside the module (shared capture hooks) and passes alone.

title: [Bug]: `cua join` always fails with `internal: secret name "space-member.mem_…"` and uses up the join code
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

`cua join <code>` accepts the code and then fails with `cua: internal: secret name "space-member.mem_…"`. It never saves the member credential, so the computer does not join the Space. The code is used up, and a retry with the same code fails with "This code doesn't work".

### Reproduction

1. In Cua Spaces, open a Space and choose Add an agent to get a "Join my Cua Space" link.
2. On a signed-in computer, run `cua join <code>`.
3. Run `cua join <code>` again.
4. Run `cua thread read`.

This happened every time: 2 of 2 attempts, each with a new code.

### Expected behavior

`cua join` saves the member credential and the computer joins the Space. After that, `cua thread join`, `cua thread inbox` and `cua thread post` work.

### Actual behavior

Step 2:

```
$ cua join F64G-3ED7 --json
cua: internal: secret name "space-member.mem_652cf79a39be44a7"
exit=1
```

Step 3:

```
This code doesn't work: it was used, cancelled or has expired, or it is for a Space on another computer. Ask for a new link in Add an agent.
exit=4
```

Step 4:

```
cua: not found: this computer hasn't joined a Space; run cua join <code> first
```

An empty `~/.cua/threads/local-<space>/` directory was created anyway.

### Environment

- Cua component and version: cua CLI 0.10.0 (`cua-sdk-v0.10.0`), daemon 0.10.0, Cua Spaces app 0.19.3 (both the latest release)
- Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2, arm64
- Credential store: default (`CUA_CREDENTIAL_STORE` not set); keyvault unlocked; signed in (`cua auth status` OK)

### Evidence

The member ID in the error is `mem_652cf79a39be44a7`. The first attempt failed the same way with `mem_6f122a4c2f479a08`.

The cause seems to be a mismatch between the secret name the join command builds and the names the credential store accepts:

- `libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/member_cmd.rs`:
  ```rust
  fn secret_name(member_id: &str) -> String {
      format!("space-member.{member_id}")
  }
  ```
  `save_secret(&secret_name(&m.member_id), …)` is called on join (around line 409).
- `libs/cua/crates/cua-auth/src/lib.rs`, `Store::secret_path` (around line 803):
  ```rust
  if name.is_empty() || !name.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_lowercase() || b == b'-') {
      return Err(Error::InvalidArgument(format!("secret name {name:?}")));
  }
  ```

`write_secret_text`, `load_secret` and `clear_secret` call `secret_path(name)` before they branch on the store type. The check therefore applies to the Keychain store and to the file store. `space-member.mem_<hex>` contains `.`, `_` and digits, so the check rejects every member ID that the server issues. The same code is in the `cua-sdk-v0.10.0` tag and on `main`. I did not find a test in `member_cmd.rs` that uses a real member ID.

### Workaround and additional context

I don't know of a workaround. Possible fixes:

- Make `secret_name` produce a name that `secret_path` accepts, for example by encoding the member ID into `[a-z-]`.
- Make `secret_path` accept digits, `_` and `.`, and keep the rejection of path separators and `..`.

`cua join` should also save the credential before it uses up the code, or let the code be retried after a local failure. Then a failure like this one would not use up the invite.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Linux update --apply ends client-owned `cua-driver mcp` stdio servers (installer pkill -x backstop)
body:
### What happens

On Linux, `cua-driver update --apply` (and a plain run of `_install-rust.sh`) ends every process named `cua-driver` on the host, including the `cua-driver mcp` stdio servers that running MCP clients own. Those agent sessions lose the driver in the middle of their work. The updater process itself is also a `cua-driver` process, so `update --apply` exits with status 143 (SIGTERM) even when the install succeeds.

The cause is `stop_cua_driver_daemons` in `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-common.sh`: after `systemctl --user stop cua-driver-rs.service`, the Linux branch runs `pkill -x cua-driver` as a backstop. On Linux there is no daemon to restart for stdio MCP use, and a running stdio server keeps working on its old inode after the `packages/current` symlink flips.

### Reproduction (0.38.0, Debian 12, no display)

```sh
work=$(mktemp -d)
cp /bin/sleep "$work/cua-driver"
"$work/cua-driver" 600 &          # stands in for a client-owned `cua-driver mcp`
victim=$!
curl -fsSL -o "$work/install.sh" \
  https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download/cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0/_install-rust.sh
HOME="$work/home" bash "$work/install.sh" --no-modify-path
kill -0 "$victim" && echo survived || echo "killed by installer"
```

Output:

```text
==> stopping any running cua-driver daemons before swap
cua-driver-rs 0.38.0 installed.
killed by installer
```

The victim ran from a different HOME than the install target, so the backstop is not limited to the install being replaced.

With real MCP clients, the update log also shows the backstop fail on processes it cannot signal:

```text
Note: 15 cua-driver process(es) still running after best-effort kill (...)
      They are probably owned by another user, or are ignoring SIGTERM.
```

### Expected

An update does not end stdio MCP servers that clients own. Options:

1. On Linux, stop only the supervised `serve` daemon (the systemd unit), or only processes whose executable is under the install root being replaced.
2. Keep the symlink flip atomic and let running stdio servers finish on the old release, as the release directory is retained anyway.
3. Exclude the updater's own pid and its parent from the stop.

### Related

- The installer also appends an `export PATH=...` line to the shell rc file on each run when `~/.local/bin` is not on the installer's PATH (for example under a systemd user timer). After daily updates one rc file had 8 identical copies. `--no-modify-path` works around it; a check for an existing line would fix it.

title: Windows CUA field report: Chromium actions take effect but report unverifiable; foreground scroll restoration fails
body:
## Summary

A bounded Windows/Chromium reproduction shows **native UI effects can occur while CUA's action result remains `unverifiable`**. In a separate fresh trial, a foreground scroll was delivered but restoring the previously active window failed. We stopped rather than replaying any uncertain action.

This is a **field report and request for supported integration guidance**, not a claim that an upstream release has a new regression. The newer 0.38.0 executable below is a **locally modified, unsigned development candidate** and must not be mistaken for the official 0.38.0 release.

## Environment

- Host: Windows 11, OS build 26300, interactive session; installed CUA Driver **0.33.4**.
- Isolated Windows VM: Chrome **156.0.8078.74**, CUA Driver reporting **0.38.0** from a **local patched build** (SHA-256 `aea0eeb48cf106ae36b923ae246cc5d830cfea525d1189b4d062f7493b1f7d7f`).
- All actions: single-use local HTML fixture, fresh Chromium profiles, exact PID/HWND, standard permission mode; private candidate daemon/socket on the VM. No user accounts, credentials, external websites or production configuration.
- Browser launched with `--force-renderer-accessibility=complete --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` to avoid the UIA exposure problem documented in #1620. Exact input controls were independently visible in UIA before actions.

## Fixture

A standalone HTML document containing:

- Button `CLICK_COUNT=0`; onclick increments `window.clicks` and the visible `CLICK_READOUT`.
- Text input `aria-label="CUA_TEST_FIELD_A"`, starting value `INITIAL_A`.
- Independent overflow scroll region `aria-label="CUA_TEST_SCROLL_REGION"` with visible `SCROLL_Y` readout.

Each test began with counter 0, scroll 0 and input `INITIAL_A`. Each action was called **once**, followed by independent UIA and/or DOM inspection. No retry after an uncertain delivery.

## Observed results

| Action | Installed 0.33.4 on host | Local patched 0.38.0 candidate in VM |
|---|---|---|
| Click button | Driver returned `UNVERIFIABLE`, `actionDispatched=false`, `nativeDispatchState=UNKNOWN`; independent UIA button/readout showed **0→1** | Driver returned `UNVERIFIABLE`, `actionDispatched=true`, `nativeDispatchState=DRIVER_REPORTED`; independent DOM/UIA showed **0→1** |
| Scroll region, down 3 lines | Driver returned `UNVERIFIABLE`; independent UIA `SCROLL_Y` showed **0→530** | Driver returned **`FOREGROUND_RESTORE_FAILED`**, `actionDispatched=true`, `nativeDispatchState=DRIVER_REPORTED`, `verified=false`; independent DOM/UIA showed **0→726**; local integration reported unresolved risk scoped to **DESKTOP** |
| Replace input text | Driver reported `UNVERIFIABLE`, `actionDispatched=false`; independent UIA readback confirmed new value | **Not re-tested on the matched fixture after the restore failure.** An earlier, *different* VM fixture test with the same candidate had `actionDispatched=true`, `nativeApplicationState=STATE_CONFIRMED`, 2 exact UIA readbacks and matching DOM input but `verified=false` under stricter integration policy. |

For the VM's scroll trial, the background attempt was `NOT_DISPATCHED`, the single foreground attempt was `DRIVER_REPORTED`, the actual region scrolled, but the foreground restore failed. The local fail-closed adapter quarantined subsequent native input. The fresh VM test browser and private daemon were cleaned up.

The local adapter differentiates **driver-reported dispatch**, independent **sampled application state**, and **proof that earlier native input can no longer cause delayed effects**. The third property has not been established. We therefore do not claim continuous click→scroll→verified typing is safe or production-ready.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Which **documented public result fields / postcondition APIs** should a Windows consumer rely on to distinguish *not dispatched*, *dispatched but unobserved*, and *independently observed state change*? Is `effect: unverifiable` expected even when a separate application-state observer later proves the effect?
2. For `delivery_mode:foreground` scroll on Chromium, is **restoration of the prior foreground window** guaranteed by the driver, or explicitly best-effort? If it fails *after* actual scrolling, what recovery path avoids focus surprises or unsafe input replay?
3. Is there any supported operation-completion / input-drain mechanism that prevents later effects from a previous call? If **not**, we intend to use app-level idempotent postconditions and stop (no automatic fallback/replay) on uncertainty rather than treating `unverifiable` as success.
4. Is a browser-native route (`browser_click`/`browser_type` with trusted input, when available) the recommended alternative for Chromium tasks where a native UIA route returns unverifiable?

## Related upstream work

- #2206 foreground delivery/restore contract
- #3171 Windows missing window-change evidence
- #2883 `ActionEffect` and `unverifiable` semantics
- #1620 Chromium occlusion/accessibility (closed)

We have preserved structured, timestamped redacted observations and can provide a minimal isolated repro script if helpful. No private paths, user account content, or production data are needed.

title: fix(cua-driver): deliver deep CDP replies instead of timing out
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `get_browser_state` takes 20 s and returns an incomplete `semantic_v2` snapshot, or refuses in `dom_refs_v1`, on any page deeper than about 63 elements. A full-depth `DOM.getDocument` reply nests two JSON levels per DOM level, so ordinary pages exceed serde_json's default 128-level recursion limit. ChatGPT's home and conversation pages render 69 levels deep (reply nesting 143). `read_loop` silently dropped every frame it could not parse, so the caller waited out the 20 s `CALL_TIMEOUT` even though Chromium had answered in about 20 ms.
- What changed:
  - The CDP reader parses frames with serde_json's recursion limit replaced by an explicit 512-level bound. Chromium refuses to serialize replies past its 300-level CBOR stack limit, so every reply it sends is accepted, while parser recursion and stack use stay bounded.
  - A reply that still cannot be decoded now fails its own call immediately, matched by the leading `id` Chromium writes first, and the socket stays usable. No reply is dropped into a timeout any more.
  - Chromium's own refusal for pages deeper than about 150 elements (`Failed to convert response to JSON: CBOR: stack limit exceeded`) now takes the existing bounded-depth fallback instead of failing the snapshot.

## Related work

Refs #6299 and #6307. Those fix reply *size* above the 16 MiB WebSocket frame limit in the connection config. This fixes reply *nesting depth* in frame decoding. The two changes are independent and touch different lines.

RFC: not required. No public API, protocol field, MCP schema or permission changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: deep pages snapshot in milliseconds instead of 20 s. `semantic_v2` returns complete trees where it used to fall back. `dom_refs_v1` succeeds where it used to refuse. Applies to every platform adapter that uses the shared CDP client.
- Risk: frames are now scanned once for nesting before parsing, a linear pass over bytes. The 512-level bound keeps recursive parsing and `Value` drops within default thread stacks; the cap is exercised in a debug-build test.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::` passes, 239 tests on `main` and 251 on the host integration build. New tests:
  - deep replies at 300 levels and at the cap are delivered without waiting for `CALL_TIMEOUT`;
  - a reply above the cap fails its call immediately with a decode error, and the next call on the same socket succeeds;
  - Chromium's verbatim CBOR stack-limit refusal takes the bounded fallback.
- With the production change reverted, both new reader tests fail.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Real browser, Linux X11, Chrome 156.0.8078.79, existing-profile attachment, same tabs, same session flow. Release build before and after:

| Page | Format | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| chatgpt.com home (DOM depth 69) | semantic_v2 | 20,326 ms, incomplete | 587 ms |
| chatgpt.com home | dom_refs_v1 | 20,013 ms, refused (`DOM.getDocument timed out after 20s`) | 27 ms |
| example.com with a 64-deep `div` chain | semantic_v2 | 20,017 ms, incomplete | 16 ms, complete |
| example.com with a 64-deep `div` chain | dom_refs_v1 | 20,013 ms, refused | 13 ms |

  The ChatGPT `semantic_v2` result after the fix is incomplete only because the page has more nodes than the 300-node budget; it returns a continuation.
- Over 13 days of production use on this host, 78 successful snapshots each paid the 20 s timeout, nearly all on ChatGPT pages.
- Known gaps: macOS and Windows adapters were not run live; they share the changed reader. CI and the desktop/browser matrix are still required.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC.
- [x] Tests and platform evidence are included, and the gaps are explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] No external contribution is included.
- [x] This is a user-visible driver fix; `no-release` is not requested.

title: [Bug]: `open_space_viewer` / `show_space_pip` fail with "Cua Spaces app isn't running" while CuaSpacesMac is running; `spaces-control.json` is never written
body:
### Primary area

Other

### Summary

The Cua Spaces app process (`CuaSpacesMac`) is running, but it never writes `~/.cua/spaces-control.json`. The MCP tools that draw on the user's desktop (`open_space_viewer`, `show_space_pip`) therefore fail with `operator_display is not available on this host`. The error says the app isn't running, which is wrong: the process is up and the daemon works.

## Related problems seen in the same session

1. **`create_space` blocks with no progress.** The MCP call was aborted after 1800 s of silence ("sent no response or progress") while the image pull was still running (269/300 layers). The pull progress only appeared in `~/.cua/vmm/lume/serve.log`. Progress notifications, or an async create, would avoid this.
2. **Local Network permission error.** While the Space was running, the daemon logged `re-attach still failing ... Local Network access is not available ... No route to host` for `192.168.64.5:3211`, and every guest-agent tool returned `this Space's image runs no cua-spacesd`. `nc -z 192.168.64.5 3211` from a normal shell succeeded, so the route was fine and only the app was blocked. The error message misleads: `list_spaces` still advertised `desktop_stream`, and the tool errors blamed the image rather than the permission. Toggling Cua Spaces in Privacy & Security → Local Network and turning Tailscale off did not help. Only the `AllowedEthernetLocalNetworkAddresses` / `AllowedWiFiLocalNetworkAddresses` workaround from the log, plus a reboot, did.
3. **`cua-driver` MCP server fails to start** (see below).




### Reproduction

1. Install Cua Spaces and connect the `cua` MCP server.
2. Call `create_space(image="macos", on="local")`. The first run pulls the 22.5 GB base image and takes about 30 minutes.
3. Call `open_space_viewer(space="local:space-666b491caf")`.

### Expected behavior

Either the app writes `spaces-control.json` at launch, or the tool error names the real cause (for example "the app has no window open yet") and says how to fix it.

### Actual behavior

```
error: operator_display is not available on this host: the Cua Spaces app isn't running
(no control server at /Users/davidmcgregor/.cua/spaces-control.json: No such file or directory (os error 2))
```

- `pgrep` shows `/Applications/Cua Spaces.app/Contents/MacOS/CuaSpacesMac` and the `--service-helper` process.
- `ls ~/.cua | grep control` shows only `host/mesh-control.sock`, never `spaces-control.json`.
- Quitting and relaunching the app (`osascript -e 'quit app "Cua Spaces"'`, then `open -a "Cua Spaces"`) did not create the file.
- After a Mac reboot the file was missing again, and `start_space` was needed because the Space was Stopped.
- `daemon.log` and `log show` have no line about the control server.

### Environment

- macOS 27.2 (arm64), MacBook Pro
- Cua Spaces app 0.19.3, `cua` CLI 0.10.0 (cua-spacesd 0.10.0 on the host; 0.7.0 in the guest)
- Space: `local:space-666b491caf`, image `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26` (Lume 0.6.0, built-in), created with `create_space(image="macos", on="local")`
- Tailscale was installed and running during part of the test

### Evidence

## `cua-driver` not on `$PATH`

`~/.claude.json` has `{"type": "stdio", "command": "cua-driver", "args": ["mcp"]}`. Claude Code reports `Failed to connect: Executable not found in $PATH: "cua-driver"`.

The binary does exist at `/Applications/Cua Spaces.app/Contents/Helpers/cua-driver`, and only `~/.local/bin/cua` is on `$PATH`. The installer or docs could either symlink `cua-driver` next to `cua` or document the full path.

## Search of existing issues

No match for `spaces-control.json`, `open_space_viewer` or `operator_display`. Related but different: #4823 (viewer "Open when ready" button), #5795 (guest freezes when the volume host goes away).

### Workaround and additional context

_No response_

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: feat(cua-driver): ship portal ScreenCast capture in Linux release builds so released binaries can record KDE and other portal-only desktops
body: ## Description **What** Linux release binaries move from `portal-input` to `portal-input,portal-capture`, with no new load-time dependency (Verification). With the native Wayland backend enabled (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`), a released binary can record KDE/KWin and other portal-only Wayland desktops through the xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast route from #6361. The cost is on that opt-in path only; X11, Wayland without the opt-in, GNOME with helper frames, and wlr-screencopy record as before. It also reaches GNOME without the WinRects helper, where portal recording is unverified. No release-shaped binary has recorded through this route yet. | Surface | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Released binary with the Wayland opt-in, `start_recording(record_video=true)` on KDE/KWin, GNOME without the helper, or another portal-only desktop | Fails at once: "compiled without the `portal-capture` feature" | Loads `libpipewire-0.3.so.0`, asks for consent unless a saved grant applies, and waits up to about 93 s for the grant and a first frame. Refusal, a missing library, or a timeout lands in `last_error`. | | `cua-driver manifest` on a released Linux binary | `"portal_capture": false` | `"portal_capture": true` | | E2E builds that follow the published features (`run-rust-e2e.sh` on the GNOME/KDE lanes, `run-rust-standalone-browser-e2e.sh`, `e2e-rust-standalone-browsers.yml`) | `portal-input` | Both; a local Linux run of either script now needs the PipeWire/SPA headers and libclang. | **Why** On portal-only desktops an official binary cannot record video; only Nix, which ships this feature pair, and source builds can. #6361 made libpipewire a run-time load, which left one build blocker: `libspa-sys` needs SPA headers newer than Debian 11's stock 0.3.19. **How** The release container adds bullseye-backports from the same pinned `snapshot.debian.org` timestamp, and to the `archive.debian.org` fallback. A separate `-t bullseye-backports` step installs the 0.3.65 `libpipewire-0.3-dev` and `libspa-0.2-dev` packages, and `libclang-11-dev` joins the stock packages for bindgen. libspa is header-only. ## Architecture ## Repro Recipe On Plasma 6 Wayland with ffmpeg and `libpipewire-0.3-0`, with a release artifact built from this head: export CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1 cua-driver mcp {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}} {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"start_recording","arguments":{"output_dir":"/tmp/cua-6340-kde","record_video":true}}} # Choose a monitor in KDE's dialog; id 2 answers after that. {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"stop_recording","arguments":{}}} # In another shell: ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height /tmp/cua-6340-kde/recording.mp4 I ran these requests on X11 under Xvfb (Verification), not on Plasma. ## Related Issue Refs #2004, #1946. Follows #6361. RFC: none filed. title: fix(spaces-macos): serve the loopback control server so open_space_viewer works
body:
Refs #6339

## Problem

The Swift app (`apps/cua-spaces-macos`) never writes `~/.cua/spaces-control.json`. Only the Tauri app (`apps/cua-spaces/src-tauri/src/control.rs`) serves the control protocol that `cua_spaces::operator::ControlServerDisplay` calls. So `open_space_viewer` and `show_space_pip` fail with "the Cua Spaces app isn't running" while `CuaSpacesMac` is running.

## Change

- `SpacesControlServer` (new): listens on `127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>`, writes `{port, token}` to `<cua home>/spaces-control.json` (mode 0600, atomic rename), requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and removes the file on quit.
- `POST /viewer/open` resolves the Space (id, short id or name) and opens its page in the main window, as the notch does.
- `/pip/pin`, `/pip/unpin` and `/window/stream` answer `501` with a clear message. Known gap: the app doesn't present those natively through this path yet.
- The cua home follows `CUA_HOME`, then the bundle's `CuaHome` (Cua Spaces Local), then `~/.cua`. A bundle of another channel with no usable home writes nothing. `HelperService.homeDirectory` is the shared piece, split out of `specPath`.
- Not started in an offscreen run.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter "SpacesControlServerTests|HelperServiceTests"`: 15 tests pass. The new suite runs a real server on a real port and checks the file mode, the bearer check (401), unknown Space (404), missing field (400), the 501 routes, and file removal on stop.
- Not yet verified: an end-to-end run of the MCP `open_space_viewer` tool against a built app bundle. I'd like a maintainer or a second pair of eyes on that.
- The full `swift test` suite and the desktop E2E matrix were not run.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop the X11 agent cursor splitting in two while it moves
body:
Fixes CUA-3120. Part of CUA-3103 (new cursor on Windows and Linux).

**For users:** on Linux X11 desktops the agent cursor no longer splits into two pieces while it moves.

## Root cause

The X11 overlay is one full-screen window. Every frame it set a new bounding shape and then uploaded the cursor's pixels as separate requests.

- **With a compositing manager** (picom on the XFCE desktop where the bug was recorded), the manager learns the new shape and the new pixels from separate events, and fetches the shape asynchronously. A composited frame could pair one frame's shape with another frame's pixels, so the arrow showed as two offset pieces.
- **Without one**, pixels the cursor left kept our paint until the window under them answered its Expose, so the previous frame's arrow stayed on screen beside the new one.

## Fix

- **Compositing manager present:** the overlay stops reshaping. The bounding shape stays the whole window, and alpha does the hiding. Each frame clears the rects the last frame drew to transparent and copies the new tiles in. The window sets `_NET_WM_BYPASS_COMPOSITOR=2`, so no manager unredirects it. This path runs only on a 32-bit ARGB window.
- **No compositing manager:** the overlay paints the save-under of the frame on screen back over the pixels it vacates, and only then shrinks the shape. The window underneath then repaints pixels that already look right.
- **Both:** frames are uploaded into offscreen pixmaps first and presented in one short server grab, so no client can read half a frame. The grab holds only small requests, flushed together with the ungrab.

## Tests

Two live X11 regressions (`#[ignore]`, run in CI under `xvfb-run`) paint 600 to 6,000 frames of an alternating-colour square while a second connection reads the root. Every read must show exactly one whole square.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| No compositor, a window that never answers Expose | 927 of 928 reads torn | 0 |
| picom | 43 of 861 reads torn | 0 |

CI installs `picom` for the second run. I re-recorded the same XFCE script with the main build and with this build, under picom: main splits the arrow during moves, and this build shows one whole arrow in every frame.

title: fix(cua-driver): draw the GNOME helper cursor's tip on the click point
body:
Fixes CUA-3121. Part of CUA-3103.

**For users:** on GNOME the agent cursor's tip now sits exactly on the point it clicks.

## Root cause

The GNOME Shell helper (`winrects@cua`) places its cursor actor with its centre on the cursor point. The repaint then mapped the canvas centre (64, 64) to that centre instead of the arrow's tip (55, 30). At 42/128 scale that is 2.95 px left and 11.16 px up, which matches the "about 3 px left and 11 px above" seen in the recording. The pose stream already sends the tip; its test asserts that the last sample equals the target.

## Fix

- The repaint maps the tip (`TIP_X`, `TIP_Y`) to the actor centre.
- The click squish now scales about the tip, like the Rust renderer, so a press no longer moves the point.
- A click the helper plays by itself (`ClickPulse`) no longer draws click marks. Marks show only when cua-driver asks for them (`cursor.marks`). This was the sparkle seen at the tip with marks off.
- The helper is bumped to v12, so a fixed helper can be told apart. The pose API minimum stays 11.

## Tests

- `scripts/tests/test_wayland_helper_cursor_paint.mjs` (run by pytest) paints the helper into a recording Cairo context. It asserts that the tip lands on the point at rest, while travelling (point plus float), on arrival, mid-squish and on clicks. It also asserts that the arrow and halo keep one colour from rest to arrival, and that self-played clicks draw no marks. On main it fails with the tip at (297.05, 188.84) for (300, 200).
- I re-recorded the GNOME 46 Wayland script on a VM: with helper v12 the click point (green cross) lands on the tip.

title: [Feature]: Persist get_window_state max_elements and max_depth defaults
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (macOS; `get_window_state` and persistent configuration)

### User problem

A dense Electron window had a text composer after a large sidebar in the accessibility tree. On Cua Driver **0.21.0**, a read of the same exact window with a composer-label `query` found **zero** `AXTextArea` matches at `max_elements: 100`, `200`, and `300`, but found the composer when raised to `500` (and at `800`). The control was accessible; a small depth-first walk budget made it appear absent. No application-specific content or screenshots are included here.

We upgraded to **0.38.0** stable. The current `get_window_state` schema documents a default `max_elements` of **250** (`2,000` with `full_output: true`) and `max_depth` of **25**. We have **not** repeated the GUI reproduction on 0.38.0; the observed small-budget miss above is from 0.21.0. On the installed 0.38.0, both `cua-driver config get max_elements` and `cua-driver config get max_depth` return `Unknown config key`. The `set_config` schema likewise has no AX-walk default keys.

In repeated automation, relying on every caller to supply the same higher budget is error-prone. Some integrations expose these parameters on every call, while others omit them and inherit a built-in default. A persistent, bounded default would let a user choose a suitable budget for their usual applications without relying on prompt-level instructions or editing every tool call.

### Requested behavior

- Support persistent defaults for `get_window_state.max_elements` and `get_window_state.max_depth` (for example, via `cua-driver config set ...` and the existing driver config file), with documented validation and safe bounds.
- When an argument is omitted, use the saved default; an explicit per-call value must continue to take precedence. If session-scoped overrides are supported, document their precedence too.
- Expose the saved/effective values in `config show` / `config get` and the tool description, and keep truncation/completeness indicators and the independent `timeout_ms` budget intact.
- Do not silently override a smaller explicit cap chosen by a client. A persistent default is not a substitute for fixing query starvation during traversal.

### Current workaround and related work

We currently pass `max_elements: 2000`, `max_depth: 25`, and a precise `query` on each relevant read, backed by a persistent integration-level instruction. This is not a driver setting and cannot enforce a default for other clients. Related but distinct: #6270 tracks post-walk `query` starvation and wrapper depth; this request is specifically about configurable *defaults* for calls that omit these limits.

### Environment / privacy

macOS; upgraded from Cua Driver 0.21.0 to 0.38.0 stable. Reproduction details are limited to roles, limits, and match counts; no prompts, window titles, paths, credentials, or screenshots are attached.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the GNOME agent cursor in its session colour
body:
Fixes CUA-3126. Part of CUA-3103. Found next to CUA-3121.

**For users:** on GNOME the agent cursor keeps one colour. Before, it flashed other colours as it moved and just before clicks.

## Root cause

Every CLI call first sends a few cursor commands (an empty label, an idle cue and a system cue) under its own per-call session, then the named session's commands. Platforms with one cursor per session never draw that per-call cursor, because it is never placed. The GNOME Shell helper draws a single cursor, and `SharedCursorSurface` gave it to whichever session sent any command, so each call recoloured the arrow and halo. A D-Bus capture of the helper during one `demo` session showed five different `SetCursorColor` values; with this change it shows one.

## Fix

- `SharedCursorSurface::on_command` takes a `places` flag. Only a move, snap or click can take the shared cursor or claim an empty one. Labels and cues from another session leave it alone, which matches what a per-session renderer shows.
- When a session takes the cursor over, the helper gets its label and cue replayed, because what it sent before it owned the cursor never reached the helper.

## Tests

- `the_helper_cursor_keeps_its_colour_from_rest_through_travel_to_arrival` plays a rest, per-call burst, travel and arrival script. It asserts that the helper only ever gets the named session's arrow colour and one halo colour, with one takeover.
- `taking_the_helper_cursor_over_replays_the_owners_label` and `only_a_placing_command_takes_the_shared_surface` cover the takeover rules.

title: fix(cua-relay): mint a new service token on a 401 and refresh at half-life (CUA-2959)
body:
Fixes CUA-2959.

**What changes for users:** nothing visible. Team and plan checks on the hosted relay no longer hit a steady trickle of refused lookups, so the relay stops falling back to cached plans, and the error alert reflects real failures only.

## Root cause

The relay already calls the Spaces API with its own client-credentials token (`cua-relay-svc`). It never forwards user or machine tokens. The 401s were the API refusing that service token as **expired**:

- The token issuer's clock ran about 60 s behind the API's. The issuer stamps `exp` from its own clock, and the API checks it against its own clock with 30 s of leeway.
- The relay used each 300 s token for 270 s (`expires_in - 30`). With 60 s of skew, the token looked expired to the API for the last second or so of each 270 s window. Production logs show the refusals at exactly 270 s intervals.
- On a 401 the relay retried with the **same** cached token. Every lookup in that second failed, and every attempt counted in `cua_relay_org_api_errors_total`. Reconnect bursts made those seconds busier.

## Fix (standard OAuth client pattern)

- Replace the service token at **half its lifetime** (150 s for 300 s tokens). That tolerates minutes of skew between issuer and API.
- On a 401, **mint a new token once and resend**. Concurrent refusals mint a single token. Only a 401 to a freshly minted token is an error (`TOKEN_REFUSED`), and plan lookups don't retry it further, so a misconfigured secret can't fan out into 6x token mints.
- New counters: `cua_relay_org_service_token_fetches_total`, `_errors_total` and `_refused_total` (recovered refusals). `cua_relay_org_api_errors_total` now counts only real failures. `fail_closed` behaviour is unchanged.
- New `cua_relay_auth_rejections_total{route,reason}`: the relay's own 401s to its callers. Revoked, rotated or deleted machines and devices still reconnecting (`unknown_machine_token`, `ticket_revoked`) are counted there as expected outcomes, apart from Spaces API errors.

## Tests

- `a_refused_cached_token_is_replaced_and_not_an_api_error`: the API refuses token 1 and accepts token 2. The call succeeds with 0 API errors and 1 recovered refusal.
- `a_refused_fresh_token_is_one_api_error_and_final`: every token is refused. That gives exactly 2 mints, 2 API hits and 1 error, and the plan lookup adds no retries.
- `concurrent_refusals_mint_one_new_token`
- `service_tokens_are_replaced_at_half_their_lifetime`
- `revoked_machines_are_counted_apart_by_reason` and `every_reason_and_route_has_its_own_slot`

`cargo test -p cua-relay --features hosted` passes, and clippy is clean with and without `hosted`.

The clock drift itself is being fixed separately in our infrastructure. This change makes the relay correct under any realistic skew.

title: fix(cua-cli): encode member credential names for storage
body:
## Summary

`cua join` saves a returned member key as `space-member.<member_id>`, but the credential store accepts only lowercase ASCII letters and hyphens. The dot, underscore and digits make every server-issued member ID fail validation after the join code has been redeemed.

Encode each member-ID byte as two lowercase letters under the `space-member-` prefix. The existing shared helper supplies the name for saving, loading and removing credentials, and preserves distinctions between IDs rather than stripping punctuation or folding case. Update the module documentation to match.

## Related work

Refs #6334, reported by @DoWhileGeek.

No RFC is required: this repairs an internal credential-name mismatch without changing CLI arguments, protocol fields or the credential store's accepted names.

## Compatibility and risk

The member ID and key remain unchanged. Previously generated names could not pass the store's validation, so this change does not need to migrate successfully stored credentials from that format.

This fixes the deterministic local naming failure. Already consumed join codes still need replacing. General retryability or atomicity when redemption succeeds but a later vault/disk write fails is outside this patch.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the new regression failed with the reported `InvalidArgument("secret name \"space-member.mem_…\"")` error.
- After the fix, it passes against the file store and test-keychain backend. It covers independent save/load round trips for server-shaped, punctuation-distinct and case-distinct IDs, removal, repeated removal and preservation of another member's key.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p cua-cli -p cua-auth --lib -- --test-threads=4`: 307 CLI tests and 57 authentication tests passed; one existing host-runtime probe remained ignored.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p cua-cli --test auth -- --test-threads=4`: eight integration tests passed.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p cua-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Workspace formatting, fast pre-push checks, release-title syntax validation and `git diff --check`: passed.

Tests used the repository's pinned Rust 1.97.1 and isolated temporary homes. This does not claim a live signed-app join, real OS keychain exercise or Linux/Windows execution. The test builds emitted the existing SDK unwind-table linker warning, also seen before the production change.

Draft pending upstream CI, including the release-metadata gate. No upstream CI result is claimed.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused change; the description matches the diff.
- [x] No RFC is required for this internal bug fix.
- [x] Regression coverage and validation limits are recorded.
- [x] Conventional Commit title describes the production fix.
- [x] No external implementation was incorporated.

This is a user-visible CLI fix; `no-release` is not requested.

title: [Bug]: Linux cua-driver serve stops answering list_apps minutes after first boot (all threads in futex wait), stdio mcp unaffected
body:
## What happens

On a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 server, `cua-driver serve` stops answering a few minutes after first boot. `cua-driver call list_apps` against the daemon socket never returns (killed after 20 s). Restarting the daemon fixes it. Seen on 3 of 3 fresh boxes. `cua-driver mcp` (stdio) kept working the whole time the daemon was stuck.

## Environment

- cua-driver 0.38.0 (installed with `curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh`, telemetry disabled)
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Hetzner Cloud cx33 (x86_64, 4 vCPU, 8 GB), no GPU
- XFCE 4.18 on TigerVNC (`Xvnc :1`), `at-spi2-core` and `libxi6` installed, `DISPLAY=:1`
- Daemon runs as a systemd user service inside that session: `cua-driver serve --socket ~/.cache/cua-driver/cua-driver.sock`
- Google Chrome (stable) running in the same session with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`

## Steps

1. Boot the box, start Xvnc + XFCE, Chrome and `cua-driver serve` as user services.
2. Call `cua-driver call list_apps` once a minute.
3. A few minutes after boot (first SSH login was around the same time, not proven related), the call stops returning.

## What the daemon looks like while stuck

All threads are parked, none in D state. Main thread, `cua-overlay-x11` and most `tokio-rt-worker` threads sit in `futex_wait_queue`; two tokio workers sit in `ep_poll`:

```
13255 cua-driver       wchan=futex_wait_queue  futex_wait_queue / __futex_wait / futex_wait / do_futex
13265 tokio-rt-worker  wchan=ep_poll           ep_poll / do_epoll_wait
13267 cua-overlay-x11  wchan=futex_wait_queue  futex_wait_queue / __futex_wait / futex_wait / do_futex
13270 cua-driver       wchan=futex_wait_queue  ...
13271 cua-driver       wchan=futex_wait_queue  ...
13272 tokio-rt-worker  wchan=futex_wait_queue  ...
13273 tokio-rt-worker  wchan=ep_poll           ...
13274-13926 tokio-rt-worker wchan=futex_wait_queue ...
```

The only startup log line besides "listening" is:

```
WARN platform_linux::overlay: X11 overlay: root reads cannot see this window's own pixels; save-unders will be served without readback confirmation
```

That points at a lock held between the X11 overlay thread and the request path, but no userspace backtrace was captured.

## Workaround in use

A systemd timer runs `timeout -s KILL 20 cua-driver call list_apps` every minute and restarts the daemon if it fails. After a restart the daemon stays healthy.

## Expected

`list_apps` keeps answering, or the daemon logs/exits instead of hanging.

title: fix(cua-driver): avoid terminating client stdio MCP servers and duplicate PATH on Linux (#6335)
body:
Fixes #6335

### Problem
1. On Linux, `_install-common.sh` executed `pkill -x cua-driver` as a blanket backstop after stopping the systemd unit. This terminated:
   - Client-owned `cua-driver mcp` stdio processes mid-session.
   - The calling `cua-driver update --apply` process itself (exiting with status 143 / SIGTERM).
   - Unrelated processes from other users or test harnesses.
2. In `_install-rust.sh`, repeated or timer-based runs without `$BIN_DIR` in the caller's `$PATH` appended duplicate `export PATH=...` entries to shell rc files.

### Solution
1. **Scope Linux daemon shutdown (`_install-common.sh`)**:
   - Removed blanket `pkill -x cua-driver` on Linux.
   - Preserves running client stdio MCP sessions across the atomic symlink flip (`packages/current`) so active sessions continue executing smoothly on their existing held inode.
   - Protects the updater PID (`$$`) and parent PID (`$PPID`).
   - Targets only unmanaged `serve` background daemons owned by the current user.
   - Scoped `show_cua_driver_daemon_survivors` on Linux to unmanaged `serve` daemons to eliminate false survivor warnings for active client stdio sessions.
2. **De-duplicate shell RC modifications (`_install-rust.sh`)**:
   - Added an idempotency check (`! grep -Fq "$BIN_DIR" "$SHELL_RC"`) before appending `export PATH="..."`.
3. **Tests**:
   - Added `test_installer_swap_step_skips_blanket_pkill_on_linux` in `test_uninstall_stops_daemons_from_other_copies.py`.

### Validation
- Validated shell syntax with `bash -n` on `_install-common.sh` and `_install-rust.sh`.
- Ran helper drift tests: `test_uninstall_copy_of_each_shared_helper_has_not_drifted` (5/5 passed).
- Simulated PATH idempotency across 3 consecutive runs (single export entry retained).

title: feat(spaces): ask first, CI runners, TCP shares, secure networks and the phone app, behind experiments
body:
## What this adds

Five features that were developed separately and are merged here once, in this order. Each new surface is behind its own experiment (off by default, turned on with `cua experiments enable <name>` or Settings, Advanced, Labs), except the About page change.

| Experiment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ask-first` | An agent asks you on a card before anything leaves its Space, starting with a push to GitHub. Connections lists GitHub; thread cards show the request. |
| `ci-runners` | GitHub Actions jobs run in a fresh Space each, on your computers: `cua ci`, the CI Runners page, and the `cua-ci` crate. |
| `tcp-shares` | Share a raw TCP service in a Space (a game server) at a public address, with the relay edge and `cua share --tcp`. |
| `secure-spaces`, `child-spaces` | The secure default network for a Space (exit-through, hotspot, mesh paths, Volume isolation, clipboard gate), the agent home image (slim Linux plus the cua CLI), and the child-Space conformance case. The two experiments already exist; this adds the network and sharing UI behind them. |
| `mobile` | The Cua Spaces phone app: the daemon serves a phone's tools (start a task, tool rows, changes and diffs, approval scopes) and reports events for push alerts; relay phone endpoints and `cua-spacesd phone`. |
| (none) | About, Reset welcome: a second button on the About page that starts the welcome again (`session.resetOnboarding`). |

- Order: ask-first, ci-runners, onboarding-reset, secure-spaces and tcp-shares, mobile. The CVE guard already on main was skipped.
- All of them add one experiment to the same registration files (gate, app core, FFI, telemetry schema, web bridge, desktop, macOS). The result keeps every entry; `Experiment::ALL` has 10 entries and `Gate::ALL` has 6, with `mobile` last.

- Wording: computers (not machines or devices) in the new text; no middle dots in UI text.

## Checks

- `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast` pieces: SPDX headers, actionlint, cargo fmt, lockfiles (five lock files bumped to the current version), image refs, web typecheck and tests (1361 passed), Electron shell typecheck and tests (561 passed).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on every touched crate in both Rust workspaces, `cargo nextest` on them under a no-UI sandbox with an isolated home.

Swift tests (the macOS package compiles; linking needs the staged SDK library), image builds, relay deployment, and a run of the phone app against a real relay.

title: docs(cua-driver): explain declarative hl.plugin.load in Hyprland Lua configs
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: The plugin README warns against adding a `plugin =` line until the module has been checked, but Omarchy uses Hyprland's Lua configuration, where autoloading is a call to `hl.plugin.load()`. The README does not say how those calls behave. The obvious guard, skipping the call when `hl.get_loaded_plugins()` already lists `cua-hyprland-plugin`, hangs the compositor at every login.
- What changed: A paragraph in "Load, inspect, and unload" explains that `hl.plugin.load()` is a declaration and shows the unconditional call. It explains why a guard on the loaded state never settles, and notes that conditions which do not change between evaluations (such as the ABI check) and modules loaded with `hyprctl plugin load` are unaffected.

## Related work

None. I searched issues and pull requests (`hyprland startup`, `hang`, `autoload`, `uwsm`, `hl.plugin.load`, `cua-hyprland-plugin`) and found nothing covering this. This is a small, self-contained documentation fix.

RFC: not required (documentation only).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: documentation only; no code, protocol, or package change.
- Risk and rollback: none beyond the wording; revert the commit.
- Release metadata: the README is under `libs/cua-driver/`, which `CI: Release metadata` treats as release-tracked, so this `docs(...)` title needs the `no-release` label. I can't add labels from a fork; please apply it if you agree this is non-releasing.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `prettier@3.6.2 --check` with the repository's `.prettierrc.yaml` passes on the changed README.
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Setup: Omarchy 4.0.6, Hyprland 0.56.2-4 (`efb50993`), Lua configuration, NVIDIA RTX 3060, SDDM autologin through uwsm. The plugin was built from the `cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0` source with `CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT=ON` and installed under `~/.local/lib/cua/hyprland`.
  - With the guarded load, every session start stalled: `wayland-session-waitenv` timed out waiting for `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, and SDDM fell back to the greeter. Reproduced 3 of 3 times.
  - A core dump taken 12 s into a stalled start shows `CCompositor::initManagers` → `CConfigManager::handlePluginLoads` → `reload` → `postConfigReload` → `handlePluginLoads`, repeated 544 times, with the full Lua configuration re-evaluated at each level.
  - The v0.56.2 source matches this. `hlPluginLoad` only appends to `m_registeredPlugins`, and `reload()` clears that list. `CPluginSystem::updateConfigPlugins` unloads config-loaded plugins that are no longer listed and sets `changed`, and `handlePluginLoads` then calls `reload()` again.
  - With the call made on every evaluation (keeping only the ABI check), the session started in about 1 s. `hyprctl -j cua:status` reported `"configured": true` and `"transport": {"ready": true}`.
- Known gaps or CI still required: verified only with Hyprland 0.56.2's Lua configuration. The existing `plugin =` guidance for legacy configurations is unchanged.

- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

Part of CUA-3098 (bringing the staging work into this repository). Implements CUA-2851 here.

## What changed

**Off (the default):** setup is the one from #6323. It opens on first launch, and the "Finish setting up" button, the Claude Code detection and the check for Macs that can't run virtual machines are unchanged.

**On** (`spaces_new_onboarding`, this device only; it also turns on the new Home it ends on):
- Preparing starts at launch: a Linux Space for Claude Code, then the agent in it. Progress is saved after each step, so a quit resumes where it was. A dropped connection is retried by itself, and a failure that won't clear shows Try again.
- Setup has no "Try it" screen. The last screen's button, "Open Cua", ends on Home with the prompt box and the suggestions.

- Downloads of the Linux runtime tools, its disk and Apple's container package resume from the bytes already downloaded instead of starting over, and are checked end to end (`cua-vmm` `fetch.rs`).
- `cua-image` can unpack zstd layers.

title: fix(cua-driver): record KDE Wayland desktops through the portal ScreenCast
body:
## Why

https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4034 by factory-ain3sh adds Wayland video recording through the xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast for compositors without wlr-screencopy (KDE/KWin), behind the optional `portal-capture` feature. Its fork CI never ran, because every `pull_request` workflow is waiting on approval. This PR keeps its commits unchanged and adds fixes on top, plus a merge of main.

On a live Mutter + PipeWire session, two failure paths did not behave as #4034 describes. Separately, `portal-capture` builds linked libpipewire, so `cua-driver` and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` (which the Python SDK loads) failed to load at all on a host without PipeWire, not just when recording.

## What changed

- **libpipewire is loaded at runtime.** The capture calls its 16 `pw_*` functions through a table that libloading resolves when a portal recording starts. Each entry's type is checked at compile time against pipewire-sys. `run_frame_stream` uses raw libpipewire calls instead of the `pipewire` crate, which only links. pipewire-sys stays for types and constants, and libspa for pods (header-only). Without the library, the binary and the SDK load and every other tool works. A portal video recording reports `portal ScreenCast video needs the PipeWire client library, and libpipewire-0.3.so.0 could not be loaded (...). Install it (libpipewire-0.3-0 on Debian and Ubuntu, pipewire-libs on Fedora, libpipewire on Arch) and start the recording again.` in `last_error`, before any consent dialog opens. A failed load is not cached, so installing PipeWire works without a restart.
- `ScreencastSession::open` bounds session setup (CreateSession, SelectSources) and `OpenPipeWireRemote` with `PORTAL_CALL_TIMEOUT`. Before, a portal that never answered parked `PortalVideoBackend::start` indefinitely.
- `run_frame_stream` watches the PipeWire registry and ends the capture with the stream-loss error when the cast node is removed. Before, the pacer kept duplicating the last frame, so a revoked share recorded a frozen tail and `stop()` reported success.
- CI and packaging:
  - The installer-compat and branded-installer checks keep their runtime package lists without libpipewire. They now fail if the installed `cua-driver` lists it as NEEDED.
  - The Nix package adds PipeWire back to the RUNPATH, because the fixup keeps only linked libraries. Its build fails if `cua-driver` links libpipewire.
  - The release build comment says libpipewire is not part of the distro floor.

## Scope

Covers the portal video route that https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4034 adds, which builds only with `portal-capture`. Release builds don't enable that feature. The published nightly needs only libX11, libXi and libxkbcommon beyond libc, so the installer package lists were already right for it and stay as they are. Turning `portal-capture` on for releases is https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6340, open in https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2004. With this change it no longer adds a load-time dependency.

The recorder mutex held across the portal consent wait is fixed separately in https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6376, stacked on this branch.

## Tradeoffs

- **Trampoline symbols instead of a table:** exported `pw_*` trampolines would keep the old call sites but export `pw_*` from the SDK cdylib, where they would clash with a host process that loads the real libpipewire.
- **pipewire-rs:** it has no runtime-loading option (pipewire-sys links through system-deps), so keeping it means keeping the link.

## Blast radius

Linux builds with `portal-capture` (Nix and local builds) on Wayland compositors without wlr-screencopy. GNOME with the trusted Shell helper still takes its route, and wlroots still uses wf-recorder. Default and release builds compile none of this code. The FFI rewrite keeps the old event set and teardown order. The loop is now quit only after the callback's `RefCell` borrow ends. The old closures quit it while borrowed, so a re-entrant dispatch could panic across the C boundary.

## Verification

All runs below are at the head in the `verify:` line, on a Debian 13 arm64 host with libpipewire 1.4.2, using a release build with `portal-capture`.

- `readelf -d` on `cua-driver` and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` lists libX11, libXi, libxkbcommon, libgcc_s, libm and libc, with no libpipewire. `ldd` shows no pipewire line, and neither file imports a `pw_*` symbol. Before, both listed `libpipewire-0.3.so.0` and imported 20 `pw_*` symbols.
- Without libpipewire (bubblewrap binding `/dev/null` over the library file, inside a headless Mutter Wayland session):
  - `cua-driver --version` exits 0, and `serve` starts with libpipewire not mapped.
  - `list_windows` returns the session's windows.
  - The Python SDK imports, lists 64 tools and runs `list_windows`.
  - `start_recording` with `record_video: true`, from both the CLI and the SDK, returns the install message above in `last_error`.
- With libpipewire present:
  - `run_frame_stream` recorded a real Mutter ScreenCast PipeWire node into a 1280x800 mp4. In 5 s it wrote 48 frames, and ffprobe counts 48.
  - With the node removed at 3 s, the capture ended with "the compositor removed the source" and 26 frames.
  - The release daemon maps libpipewire only once `start_recording` begins, then reaches the portal consent wait.
- The scoped repository checks pass. `platform-linux` tests pass with `--features portal-input,portal-capture` (935) and without `portal-capture` (922). Clippy `-D warnings` reports the same locations as before this change, none in the changed files. A unit test reads the test binary's NEEDED entries with the capture code kept live. It turns red when `run_frame_stream` calls a `pw_*` function directly.

Not run: a full KDE consent-to-cast round trip. KWin's screencast plugin needs OpenGL compositing, and the test host has no DRM device. The host's xdg-desktop-portal-gnome crashes when Share is pressed. Nix was not built here, so the RUNPATH and NEEDED checks in `package.nix` run first in CI. Windows and macOS platform checks could not run here, and this change touches neither.

Review: a second review found nothing blocking. Fixed the re-entrant loop quit and the NEEDED test that could pass on dead code. Dismissed: the `errno` text on a NULL return (pipewire-rs gave no detail at all), and a test for the uncached failed load (the soname is fixed, so the test would need a seam that exists only for itself).

Size: over the production-line target because it carries https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4034 whole, and the libpipewire table replaces the `pipewire` crate's wrappers with direct calls.

title: fix(spaces): keep prereleases off the Stable Sparkle feed (CUA-3131)

For users: nothing changes. Macs on Stable keep getting stable updates only. If a future prerelease ever lands in the appcast without its channel, the release now fails before the feed goes live.

title: [Bug]: [Cua Spaces macOS] Selecting 'This Mac' in Home composer navigates to 'This Space isn't here'
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

In Cua Spaces for macOS (0.10.1 / build 0.19.4.128), selecting 'This Mac' in the Home prompt composer and sending a message immediately redirects to `/spaces/relay:<machineId>` and displays "This Space isn't here — It may have been deleted, or it runs on a machine this app can't see."

### Reproduction

1. Set up the local Mac as a host (`cua host setup --share both`, `mode: "relay"`, `share_desktop: true`).
2. Open Cua Spaces.app (0.10.1) and go to the Home tab.
3. Enter a prompt (e.g., `hi`), pick an agent (e.g., `OpenCode` or `Codex`), select `in This Mac` in the location picker, and click Send.

### Expected behavior

Selecting 'This Mac' in the Home prompt bar and sending a message should navigate to a valid, interactive Space view for This Mac and start the agent conversation.

### Actual behavior

The router navigates to `/spaces/relay:<machineId>`, which is not present in `spaces.list` because `app_without_this_relay_machine` strips the local machine's `relay:<machineId>` entry and `app_with_this_machine` replaces it with a synthetic entry with `id: "this-mac"`. As a result, `/spaces/$spaceId` (`spaces.find(t => t.id === spaceId)`) returns `undefined` and renders "This Space isn't here".

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: Cua Spaces.app 0.10.1 (build 0.19.4.128), cua CLI / cua-spacesd 0.10.1
Operating system and architecture: macOS (arm64)
Application/browser/window system/image: Cua Spaces native macOS app (WKWebView)

### Evidence

1. In `use-agent-attempts` / `ask-first`, selecting `This Mac` (`where = { kind: "this-mac" }`) maps to `{ kind: "host" }` and resolves the Space ID from `host.status`:
```js
function hostSpaceId(e) {
  if (!e?.configured || !e.sharing || e.shareDesktop === false) return null;
  if (e.mode === "relay" && e.machineId) return `relay:${e.machineId}`;
  if (e.mode === "direct" && e.directUrl)
    try { return `direct:${new URL(e.directUrl).host}`; } catch { return null; }
  return null;
}
```
2. `startAttempt` then calls `onSpace("relay:<machineId>")`, navigating to `/spaces/relay:<machineId>`.
3. Meanwhile, `libcua_sdk.dylib` (`app_without_this_relay_machine` + `app_with_this_machine`) removes `relay:<this_machine_id>` from `spaces.list` and inserts `id: "this-mac"` instead.
4. Additionally, `updateTask(id, { spaceId: o, onHost: true })` sets `spaceId` before `thread.members` / `agents.start` completes, so if `agents.start` throws, the `catch` block (`getTask(id)?.spaceId || onNoSpace?.()`) skips `onNoSpace()`.

### Workaround and additional context

Add the local `cua-spacesd` daemon (`127.0.0.1:3211`) as a direct Space (`cua spaces add 127.0.0.1:3211 --token $(cat ~/.cua/host/env-token) --name local-mac`) and select `local-mac` (`direct:127.0.0.1:3211`) instead of `This Mac` in the Home location picker.

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(ci): quarantine the linux-kvm concurrent flake, fix the TCC seed lock and the Windows portmap pick
body:
Two known CI flakes were blocking the Spaces port PRs. This handles both without hiding real failures.

**linux-kvm (concurrent)** (CUA-3132). With four creates at once on a hosted runner, one create sometimes gets `registry: Not authorized` from ghcr on a public manifest, and others miss the 10 s spacesd connect window. Only the concurrent shape gets one more run, and only when every failure line matches one of those two signatures. Any other failure, or a second failure, still fails the job. The retry is reported in the job summary and as a warning. The root cause stays open on CUA-3132.

**macOS hosted E2E TCC seed** (CUA-3133). tccd keeps TCC.db open, so the seeder's bare `sqlite3` calls could fail at once with `database is locked`. Every TCC.db access now waits up to 30 s for the lock, and the seed transaction is `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. This fixes the cause, so it needs no quarantine.

**cua-spacesd Windows test `volume_portmap::serves_over_tcp_and_udp`**. On some Windows runners, `Portmap::start(0)` failed all 32 picks with `PermissionDenied` (os error 10013). The runner excludes a block of UDP ports, and Windows hands out TCP ports in order, so every TCP-first pick landed in that block. Picks now alternate between TCP-first and UDP-first, and refused ports stay bound so the same number isn't handed out again. The fixed-port path (production, port 111) is unchanged.

All three are listed in `.github/workflows/FLAKY.md`.

Tests: the new `test_macos_lume_runner.py` cases hold a write lock and check that the seed invocation waits for it (22 passed). I ran the retry step locally against the real failure log with a stubbed `cargo` in four cases: a known flake that then passes (green), a known flake twice (red), the sequential shape (red, no retry), and an unknown failure (red, no retry).

Refs CUA-3098.

title: ci: shard the five slowest jobs (CUA-3134)
body: Checks that were the slowest on pull requests now run in parallel pieces, so contributors wait less. Check names that other tooling matches stay the same. - **Rust (Linux) in the cua SDK workflow:** the test run is split into three parallel shards with cargo-nextest (one retry, flaky-test reporting). Before: about 32-37 min. The check `rust (ubuntu-latest)` is now a small job that passes when all three shards pass, so the PR-result reuse list still matches. macOS and Windows legs are unchanged. - **Rust Windows unit and compile:** the test steps are split over three shards. The check `Rust Windows unit and compile` is now a small job that passes when all three shards pass. Before: about 22-27 min. - **Image doctor with the driver and daemon under test:** the three binaries (CLI, spacesd, driver) are built in parallel jobs and the doctor jobs download them, instead of building in sequence. Before: about 21 min. - **Nix Rust unit tests:** the derivation no longer does a separate 15 minute release build that the tests never used. Before: about 26-33 min. Not changed: `swift tests (macOS)` in e2b-bindings.yml. The Swift tests take about 20 seconds; the 47 minutes are the release SDK build (35 min) and the fixtures build (11 min), which cannot be split across shards. Also: a new `fetch-under-test` action, a `cache-key` input on `build-cua-under-test`, and one updated test for the new job structure in `test_ci_reuse_pr_result.py`. Runner labels are unchanged.
