title: fix(cua-driver): stop unit tests mutating the process environment
body:
The cua-driver unit test binary crashed with SIGSEGV on the Linux runner (seen twice on #6376), and a few of its tests, plus some in cua-driver-core, fail now and then. This PR fixes the causes.

## Root cause

Tests in the `cua-driver` binary called `std::env::set_var` / `remove_var` from parallel test threads. Each module guarded them with its own lock (telemetry, version_check plus release_source, extension_manager, responsibility/bundle with none at all), so the locks never excluded each other. Rust's env lock only covers readers that go through `std::env`. On glibc older than 2.41 (the ubuntu-24.04 runner ships 2.39), `setenv` replaces and frees the `environ` array, while libc readers walk it with no lock. Two of those readers run in this binary: the resolver inside `getaddrinfo`, and libX11's `XOpenDisplay`.

The resolver is reached because telemetry tests that strip `DO_NOT_TRACK`/`CUA_TELEMETRY` let another test's capture spawn a real PostHog POST. That puts `getaddrinfo` on a detached thread while the version_check and telemetry tests keep rewriting the environment. On glibc 2.41 `setenv` never frees a live array, which is why hundreds of runs on a 2.41 machine never crashed.

## Fix

- New `env_vars` module: `var_os` / `var` read the process env, except that a unit test can override names for its own thread with `Overrides`. `Overrides::apply` passes the same overrides to child processes the test spawns. The production reads that these tests exercise (telemetry, version_check, release_channel, release_source token, extension_manager home/catalog, macOS disclaim flag, Windows truthy env) use it. `cua_driver_core::embedded_mode`'s rule is split out as `is_embedded_sentinel` so telemetry can apply it to an overridden value.
- No test in the `cua-driver` binary calls `set_var` / `remove_var` now. The only remaining callers are CLI startup paths that run before any threads exist.
- Telemetry delivery returns an error under `cfg(test)`, so no unit test reaches the network whatever the runner's opt-out variables say.
- The telemetry tests keep one shared lock, because they also share process-wide statics (pending sends, session aggregates). A poisoned lock no longer cascades into a dozen unrelated failures.

Smaller flakes found by the same stress runs, and by CI on main over the last week:

- `updater::tests::ownership_*` (Nix CI run 41689174991 on main): the fake `pacman` script is written, then spawned. A fork from a parallel test can still hold its write descriptor, so `spawn` fails with ETXTBSY and is counted as "not owned". `pacman_owns_path` now retries on `ExecutableFileBusy`.
- `telemetry::tests::lifecycle_markers_are_written_only_after_each_2xx` (and the retry test): a child forked by another test briefly holds a copy of the lifecycle lock descriptor, so the non-blocking lock reports busy and the poster never runs. These tests now retry until the poster runs.
- `batch_tools::tests::{every_step_but_the_last_is_paced_as_a_batched_step, observation_inherits_the_window_and_stays_bounded}` (Nix CI runs 40716480281 and 41033310787 on main): text-input admission is a process-wide per-pid lock, and three tests typed into pid 42 at once, so one got `input_busy`. Each now uses its own pid.

## Proof

The SIGSEGV was reproduced on unpatched main by emulating glibc 2.39's `setenv` memory behaviour (move and free the array on insert) through an `LD_PRELOAD` shim. A second shim widens the unlocked `environ` walk at `getaddrinfo`. The same shims ran against both binaries, with `CUA_TELEMETRY=0 DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `DISPLAY` unset as in CI, `--test-threads=64`, filter `telemetry:: mcp_http:: serve:: sdk_adapter:: version_check:: release_source:: env_vars::`:

| binary | runs | pass | SIGSEGV | test failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 30 | 10 | 12 | 8 |
| this PR | 30 | 30 | 0 | 0 |

The full binary with no shims:

| binary | threads | runs | pass | failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4 | 40 | 38 | 2 |
| this PR | 4 | 40 | 40 | 0 |
| main | 64 | 20 | 19 | 1 |
| this PR | 64 | 20 | 20 | 0 |

Targeted runs at 64 threads, 100 iterations each: `updater::` 99/100 on main, 100/100 here. `cua-driver-core` `batch_tools::tests::` 93/100 on main (all `input_busy` for pid 42), 100/100 here.

Also checked on this branch: zero `setenv`/`unsetenv` calls in a full run of the `cua-driver` unit binary, and zero `getaddrinfo` calls in 5 full runs at 64 threads with the telemetry opt-out variables removed. On main, the first count was 160 calls in a single-threaded run, and `getaddrinfo` reached `eu.i.posthog.com` in every 64-thread run.

The scoped repository checks pass: fmt and test for `cua-driver` and `cua-driver-core`. Clippy with `-D warnings` reports only lints that already exist on main in files this PR does not touch (platform-linux, `fast_path/pixel_guard.rs`).

Could not run here: the macOS and Windows builds. The cfg-gated edits in `responsibility.rs` (macOS) and `bundle.rs` (Windows) rely on the CI macOS and Windows unit jobs.

Size: the `env_vars` module, about 50 production lines, accounts for most of the production additions. The rest of the diff is tests.

title: fix(cua-mesh): a mesh forward keeps its UDP port when Windows excludes a UDP range
body:
## Why

`mesh_sessions_count_against_the_allowance` timed out on Windows at "Carol's media session is live". CUA-2294 fixed a different wait in this test (the first probe through the forward) and never touched the media path, so this is a new cause and the test was not at fault. `Mesh::forward_on` gets its TCP and UDP sockets from `bind_pair`, and `bind_pair` picked every port TCP-first. Windows hands TCP ports out in order and excludes UDP ranges per protocol, so all 16 picks could land in a block that refuses UDP. The forward then came up TCP-only and dropped media datagrams without saying so. The machine never saw a UDP flow and never reported the session. A real Windows user forwarding QUIC media gets the same silent drop.

## What changed

- `bind_pair` alternates which protocol picks the port number. Refused picks stay bound until it returns, so the OS cannot hand the same number out again. This is the same fix `volume_portmap` got in #6365.
- When it still falls back to TCP-only, it logs a warning that includes the last bind error.

## Scope

One function in `cua-mesh`. The test is unchanged. The other open flaky issues are left out.

## Blast Radius

Every `Mesh::forward` / `forward_on` caller (the `cua` CLI forwards, gang forwards). When a port is free for both protocols on the first pick, behaviour is the same as before. The function holds at most 16 extra sockets, for microseconds, and only while picks are being refused.

## Verification

The failure was reproduced on macOS by holding 39 of every 40 ephemeral UDP ports, which simulates a Windows excluded UDP range.

- Before (origin/main): 5 of 20 runs passed. All 15 failures were `timed out waiting for Carol's media session is live`, the same panic as the CI run. A probe on the fallback branch confirmed every failing run had taken the TCP-only path. Without the UDP hold, main passed 40/40 runs, 4 in parallel, and 90/90 more under a CPU hog, so plain load does not explain it.
- After (this head): 20/20 with the UDP hold and 20/20 without it, plus 110/110 on earlier revisions of the fix.
- The scoped repository checks pass for `cua-mesh` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test). The Windows leg was not run locally; CI's windows-latest job is the platform check.

Fixes #6384
CUA-3175

title: Three narrow lifecycle contracts for downstream integrators: attach-only connection, handle release and settlement, create operation status
body:
We build a desktop app that manages lab VMs through Cua (the CLI and SDK 0.4.1 today; we have also read the 0.9.0 source). Reading the SDK and the daemon source, we found three places where a downstream integrator cannot get a guarantee it needs, because the behavior is either undocumented or not exposed. Each ask below is deliberately narrow, and each stands on its own.

## 1. An attach-only connection to an already initialized Space

**Problem.** An integrator that must only observe an existing Space, by its registered id (`local:<name>`), has no operation that is guaranteed never to initialize it. We need a connection that works only if the guest control service is already initialized, and otherwise refuses without changing anything.

**Current behavior (SDK 0.4.1, commit `ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95`).**
- [`Spaces.space`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/reference/spaces/index.mdx#L906-L922) takes a Space identifier and an optional abort signal; it exposes no attach-only or no-initialize policy. The daemon's [ConnectSpace implementation](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/spaces_svc.rs#L430-L438) calls the same underlying `Spaces::space`.
- Its local branch [can call `sandbox.spacesd()` when no token is known](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/spaces.rs#L1332-L1346). That method [checks capabilities, installs a held or fresh token with `Init`, persists it and reconnects](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-sandbox-core/src/sandbox.rs#L3024-L3072) when the guest is uninitialized.
- `Cua.connect` itself [builds a lazy client for an existing host daemon](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-sdk/src/native/cua.rs#L309-L326); the initialization risk comes later, when a Space is connected.
- The lower-level [`Cua.spacesd(url, token)`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-sdk/src/native/cua.rs#L407-L420) probes `GetCapabilities` directly, but it needs an explicit endpoint and credential and has no mapping from a registered Space id.
- [`SpaceInfo`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/reference/spaces/index.mdx#L1059-L1084) carries the last handshake's features and version and the recorded power state, not an "already initialized" predicate.
- SDK 0.9.0 (`cdf971573ef1343fcdeb29bdb814ed8d75c86993`) keeps the same [local bootstrap call](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cdf971573ef1343fcdeb29bdb814ed8d75c86993/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/spaces.rs#L1795-L1803) and [conditional `Init`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cdf971573ef1343fcdeb29bdb814ed8d75c86993/libs/cua/crates/cua-sandbox-core/src/sandbox.rs#L2710-L2740). This is a source comparison, not a runtime test.

**Requested contract.** A registry-bound attach operation (a separate method or an explicit option on the existing one) that:
- connects only to a Space whose guest control is already initialized and authenticated;
- never calls `Init`, never mints, installs or rotates credentials, and never starts, resumes, boots or bootstraps anything;
- otherwise returns a typed refusal that distinguishes at least: not initialized, not running, unknown id, and unavailable;
- exposes no secret or endpoint to the caller.

A documented, non-secret predicate would also serve, if the documentation guarantees that a later attach after a positive answer cannot initialize anything.

**Why it matters.** Registry readiness or a successful CLI call cannot prove that connecting will leave the guest untouched, because the connection itself can initialize it before any capabilities check. A caller that must not alter a machine it did not initialize has no supported way to show that today.

## 2. A documented release and settlement contract for retained handles

**Problem.** An integrator that keeps `Space`, `Spaces` and `Cua` handles open must be able to release them and know when the connection is settled, for example when ownership of a Space changes and no stale handle may act afterwards.

**Current behavior (SDK 0.4.1).**
- The generated TypeScript exposes `uniffiDestroy()` on [`Space`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/typescript/src/native/cua_sdk.ts#L32278-L32285), [`Spaces`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/typescript/src/native/cua_sdk.ts#L35051-L35058) and [`Cua`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/typescript/src/native/cua_sdk.ts#L35488-L35495). It frees the native pointer; nothing documents an awaited release order, removal of the cached connection, cancellation or draining of in-flight calls, or daemon-side settlement.
- We found no supported close or dispose contract for these handles in the package declarations or reference documentation. The core [`forget_connection`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/spaces.rs#L1184-L1192) is not exposed as a Node lifecycle API.

**Requested contract.** Documentation, and where needed an awaitable release on `Space`, `Spaces` and `Cua`, that states:
- what releasing guarantees: in-flight calls are cancelled, drained or rejected (say which); the cached connection is removed so the next use reconnects; the handle makes no further daemon calls;
- how a caller observes that the connection is settled: for example a promise that resolves only then, with a typed result, idempotent on repeat calls and with defined behavior when the daemon is unreachable;
- the order and dependency between releasing a `Space` and its parent `Spaces` and `Cua` handles;
- what happens when release is called while a call is in flight.

**Why it matters.** Freeing a native pointer, or deleting the caller's own map entry, proves nothing about the connection. Without a settlement signal an integrator cannot show that a replaced or restarted owner has no live connection left to the same Space.

## 3. A create operation id and a read-only, restart-durable status for it

**Problem.** After an interrupted create (an app crash, a forced quit, a lost client), an integrator needs to prove that the original create is terminally quiescent, including background work it delegated, before it clears its own records. Today no supported read can prove that.

**Current behavior.**
- The CLI create returns no operation identity: the id it prints is the Space's own id (`local:<name>`), which is the name the caller chose. The daemon's `CreateSpaceStream` accepts a caller-chosen [`create_id`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/reference/protocol/daemon-spaces.mdx#L435) ([stream description](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/reference/protocol/daemon-spaces.mdx#L110-L125)), but it is not reachable from the CLI, is not provider-issued, and only keys `CancelCreateSpace`. Progress messages carry no operation id, and the stream exists only while the client is connected.
- The only public read that consults in-flight create tracking is the cancel call, and its not-running answer [merges "already finished, failed or cancelled"](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/creating.rs#L76-L82) (and a create that never started) into one result. Whether a create is still running is decided by [process liveness, with an age fallback on Windows](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/creating.rs#L416-L428), which is an internal mechanism rather than a documented read.
- Work can outlive the client. The macOS image pull is [handed to Lume's own service](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/lume/client.rs#L462-L467), which runs it as a [detached task](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3350f504014c85416009a90fcb339fe556ce02fc/libs/lume/src/Server/Handlers.swift#L160-L162) registered [under the VM name](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3350f504014c85416009a90fcb339fe556ce02fc/libs/lume/src/Server/Handlers.swift#L143-L147). The client's cancellation is best effort, and [the source notes](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ed22ad958a5ab6d764c98261b24d65f80f3a6f95/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/lume/client.rs#L694-L698) that such a Lume "cannot cancel a pull; it finishes in the background as a reusable base".
- Lume tracks [`completed`, `failed` and `cancelled` outcomes](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3350f504014c85416009a90fcb339fe556ce02fc/libs/lume/src/LumeController.swift#L38-L44) in memory, but [a cancelled pull leaves no entry and no error behind](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3350f504014c85416009a90fcb339fe556ce02fc/libs/lume/src/LumeController.swift#L97-L100), a failure is surfaced [as an error on the VM lookup](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3350f504014c85416009a90fcb339fe556ce02fc/libs/lume/src/Server/Handlers.swift#L32-L36) only while it is retained, and the registry does not survive a restart of the Lume service. Later create steps have no equivalent status.

**Requested contract.**
- A provider-issued, immutable **create operation id**, returned before any machine exists: in the CLI's JSON output and as the first message of the daemon's create stream.
- A **read-only status lookup** by that id, available from the CLI and the SDK, returning a durable, versioned state: `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `unknown`. For a terminal state it states explicitly that no delegated or background work (a pull, clone or configure step) remains. An unknown or expired id answers `unknown`, never "not creating".
- The status survives a CLI exit, a daemon restart and a Lume service restart for a stated retention period, and reading it never cancels, starts, resumes or changes anything.

**Why it matters.** An inventory snapshot, elapsed time, a missing machine or a missing process cannot show that a delegated pull will not later publish the machine, so today an integrator must keep its record of an interrupted create indefinitely. A terminal, quiescent status for a specific operation id lets it clear that record safely, and only that record.

---

We would value any one of these independently. We are glad to supply reproduction details or test an implementation against these cases.

title: [Bug]: Double-click and triple-click do nothing when a person drives a macOS Space from a viewer
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

When a person drives a macOS Space through the viewer's input channel (`interactive_input` on the media session), every press reaches the app as a single click. Double-clicking a word does not select it, triple-clicking does not select a line, and double-clicking a Finder icon does not open it. Single clicks, drags and keys work. Agents using the `double_click` tool are unaffected.

### Reproduction

1. Start a macOS Space running cua-spacesd 0.7.0 and open it in the HTML5 viewer (or any client that speaks wire v2 `interactive_input`).
2. Open TextEdit in the Space and type a few words.
3. From the viewer, double-click a word.
4. Double-click an icon on the Desktop.

### Expected behavior

The word is selected and the icon opens, as with a physical mouse.

### Actual behavior

The caret moves to the click point. The icon is selected but not opened. The acknowledgements report `delivered: true` for every event.

### Environment

- Space: Mac mini, cua-spacesd 0.7.0, display session (`AllowActivation`, whole-desktop view)
- Client: cua-spacesd HTML5 viewer at `libs/cua/crates/cua-spacesd-html5/web/src/input.ts`, and a third-party viewer sending the same events
- Checked against `main` at `0e87302f`; the relevant code is unchanged

### Evidence

The wire protocol has no click count field, so the Space must infer it. The macOS session does not:

- `libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/lib.rs:1191` opens `platform_macos::input::InteractiveInputSession` for the display, always `PersistentForeground`.
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/input/interactive.rs:388` (`NativeInputState::pointer`) creates one `CGEvent` per down/up and `post_pointer` at `interactive.rs:526` posts it to the HID tap. `MOUSE_EVENT_CLICK_STATE` is never set.
- `CGEventCreateMouseEvent` pre-fills that field as 1 on a down and 0 on an up (the driver's own test at `mouse.rs:2121` asserts this), and macOS does not recompute click counts for posted events. AppKit's `NSEvent.clickCount` therefore reads 1 for every press.
- The `double_click` tool shows the field is required: `mouse.rs:236` to `mouse.rs:250` stamps 1, 2, 3 on each pair when posting to the same HID tap.
- In background mode `post_pointer` passes `i64::from(click)`, so the stamped click state is always 1 there too.

### Workaround and additional context

No workaround from the viewer.

Proposed fix: track the last press (button, screen point, receipt time) in `NativeInputState`. A press of the same button within `NSEvent.doubleClickInterval` (objc2-app-kit, `NSEvent` feature already enabled) and within `CLICK_SLOP_PX` (4 points, `cua-driver-core/src/interactive_input/gestures.rs:32`) increments the count; otherwise it resets to 1. Stamp the count on the down, drags while held, and the up, in both delivery modes. Bump `click_group_id` only when the count resets to 1 so a multi-click stays one gesture, matching the tool paths at `mouse.rs:426` and `mouse.rs:673`. The counter can live in `cua-driver-core::interactive_input` with hermetic unit tests; a macOS unit test in `interactive.rs` can read the field back from created events; an E2E sibling of `e2e_macos_desktop_stream_click_on_the_dock_opens_finder` in `libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces-ext/tests/e2e_macos_input.rs` can double-click a word and read the selection back with ⌘C. Linux X11 is unaffected: XTest events get timestamps and the toolkits count clicks themselves.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Double-clicks are lost when a person drives a Windows or Hyprland Space from a viewer
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

When a person drives a Windows or Hyprland Space through the viewer's input channel, two quick clicks arrive at the app as two separate single clicks. Double-clicking a word in Notepad does not select it and double-clicking a file in Explorer does not open it. Agents using the `double_click` tool are unaffected.

### Reproduction

1. Open a Windows Space (or a Hyprland Linux Space) in the HTML5 viewer with input enabled.
2. Double-click a word in Notepad, or a file icon in Explorer.

### Expected behavior

The word is selected; the file opens.

### Actual behavior

Two single clicks. Background delivery on Windows cannot produce a double-click this way at all; foreground delivery depends on two separate tool calls landing inside `GetDoubleClickTime`, which the per-call foreground swap and restore makes unlikely.

### Environment

- Checked against `main` at `0e87302f`
- Windows Spaces and Hyprland Spaces, any session policy that allows input

### Evidence

On Windows and Hyprland, cua-spacesd has no live cua-driver input session. It converts each `interactive_input` batch into tool calls:

- `libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/lib.rs:1079` (Hyprland) and the Windows branch below it open `tool_input::open` instead of a native session.
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/interactive_input/gestures.rs:146`: `GestureFolder` turns every down/up pair within `CLICK_SLOP_PX` into its own `Gesture::Click`. There is no count.
- `libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/tool_input.rs:312`: `Gesture::Click` becomes a `click` call with `x`, `y`, `button` and modifiers only. The tool accepts `count` (`cua-driver-core/src/tool_args.rs:86`) but it is never set.
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/input/mouse.rs:201`: the PostMessage path notes that Win32 controls do not infer a double-click from two posted downs; it only sends `WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK` when a single call carries `count >= 2`.

### Workaround and additional context

No workaround from the viewer.

Proposed fix: give `GestureFolder` a click counter (same button, within the platform double-click interval, within `CLICK_SLOP_PX` of the previous click) and emit `Gesture::Click { count }`. `tool_input.rs` passes `count` through to the `click` tool, which already handles 2 and 3 on both platforms. The folder is pure Rust in `cua-driver-core`, so the owner test is a hermetic unit test there; `tool_input.rs` already has table tests for the emitted calls that can assert `count: 2`. One caveat for the folder: it sees events in batches without timestamps, so the interval must be measured at receipt, and a double-click split across two batches must still count.

Related: https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/6423 shares the root cause (the wire carries no click count) but its fix lives in `platform-macos/src/input/interactive.rs` rather than the folder.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): count a viewer's double- and triple-clicks on macOS
body:
Fixes #6423

## Summary

A viewer's presses reach a macOS Space through `InteractiveInputSession`, which posted them with CoreGraphics' default click state. macOS does not count a posted event's presses the way it counts a physical mouse's, so every double-click arrived as two single clicks.

```diff
 NativeInputState::pointer (platform-macos/src/input/interactive.rs)
   resolve_point
   CGEvent::new_mouse_event            # click state: 1 on a down, 0 on an up
+  on a down: ClickCounter::press      # same button, within NSEvent.doubleClickInterval, within 4 pt → 2, 3…
+  on a down that starts over: next click_group_id   # was: a new group on every down
+  on a down, up or cancel: set MOUSE_EVENT_CLICK_STATE
   post_pointer                        # HID tap, or post_mouse_event with the same count (was always 1)
```

`ClickCounter` lives in `cua-driver-core::interactive_input` (no I/O, receipt time passed in) so a platform that folds presses into gestures (#6424) can count the same way.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on the Mac mini this was reported from (cua-spacesd 0.7.0), a double-click in TextEdit through the HTML5 viewer moves the caret and selects nothing. The new macOS unit test `repeated_presses_at_one_spot_carry_the_click_count` fails with the stamp removed (mutation check):
  ```text
  thread '...' panicked at crates/platform-macos/src/input/interactive.rs:769:13:
    left: Some(1)
   right: Some(0)
  ```
  **After:** the same Mac mini running a cua-spacesd built from this branch, driven over the media socket by the new opt-in E2E `e2e_macos_desktop_stream_double_click_selects_a_word` (`libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces-ext/tests/e2e_macos_input.rs`). It opens a document of one repeated word in TextEdit, single-clicks it and sends ⌘C (the clipboard keeps its sentinel), then double-clicks it and sends ⌘C (the clipboard reads the word):
  ```text
  test e2e_macos_desktop_stream_double_click_selects_a_word ... ok
  ```
  Also: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib input::interactive` 6 passed (macOS 26.7.2); `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib interactive_input` 16 passed; clippy has no findings in the changed files.

The E2E needs `CUA_SPACES_MACOS_E2E_URL` and `CUA_SPACES_MACOS_E2E_TOKEN` like its siblings and is skipped otherwise. It quits TextEdit and overwrites the Space's clipboard, which the file's doc comment now says.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

A revert restores the previous single-click behavior with no state to migrate.

**Blast Radius:** small

Only the macOS interactive session changes. The public `InteractiveInputSession::dispatch` is untouched, so `cua-spacesd-desktop` needs no change. Agents' `click` and `double_click` tools use a different path. Linux X11 counts clicks in the toolkits already. Windows and Hyprland viewers have the same symptom through the gesture folder; that is #6424.

title: fix(spaces): typecheck the Electron app without the web UI's node_modules (CUA-3232)
body:
CUA-3232

The Electron jobs in "CD: Cua Spaces build (shadow)" have failed on main since a6005a4a4 (run 41735350517, and again at d6855806e in run 41747889970). `pnpm build` in `apps/cua-spaces-desktop` runs `tsc --noEmit`, and it stops with:

```
../cua-spaces-web/src/bridge/core/index.ts(4,23): error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for 'vite/client'.
../cua-spaces-web/src/bridge/core/index.ts(105,29): error TS2339: Property 'glob' does not exist on type 'ImportMeta'.
```

Root cause: since a6005a4a4, `test/bridge-native.test.ts` imports the web UI's `bridge/__tests__/testCore.ts`, which imports `bridge/core/index.ts`. That file's `/// <reference types="vite/client" />` resolves from `apps/cua-spaces-web`, and the Electron jobs install only `apps/cua-spaces-desktop`'s dependencies.

What changed:
- Removed the triple-slash reference. The web `tsconfig.json` already lists `vite/client` in `types`.
- The desktop `tsconfig.json` lists `vite/client` in `types`, and `vite` 8.3.2 is a desktop devDependency. That version was already locked through vitest, so the lockfile only gains the importer entry.
- Updated `bridge/DEPENDENCIES.md`, which still recommended the triple-slash reference.

Proof:
- Before: with no `apps/cua-spaces-web/node_modules`, which matches CI, `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/cua-spaces-desktop` gave the same two errors.
- After: the desktop `tsc --noEmit` passes with no web `node_modules`, and so does `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Desktop `vitest run` passes (73 files). `tsdown` and `check-channels` build. The web `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passes.
- The scoped repository checks pass (em-dash check).

Note: the vite client types now cover the Electron main and preload typecheck as well, so `import.meta.env.*` would typecheck there. Nothing in `src` uses it today.

Not in this PR: the darwin-universal (SwiftUI) job in the same run fails separately with `libs/cua/netgw/build.sh: line 21: go: command not found` (exit 127). That is a missing Go toolchain on the runner, which https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6422 addresses.

title: fix(spaces-web): expect the bridge's own drop line when the core is not built
body:
CUA-3240

The drop-well test in `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/bridge/__tests__/detail.test.ts` fails when the app core wasm is not built. It expects `done: notes.txt … verified in` and gets `done: notes.txt`.

## Root cause

The component is fine. The test assumed the core was always built. The "verified in" wording comes from the core (`transfer::drop_sent_text`, called through `transfer.dropSentText`). If `src/bridge/core/wasm/` is missing, `testCore()` returns an unavailable core and `dropSentText` falls back to the file names, which is what the bridge is meant to show in that case. CI builds the wasm before `pnpm test`, so CI stayed green. A checkout without the wasm32 toolchain (`pnpm test` treats that build as optional) hits the fallback, so the test went red there. The assertion has been there since the shared UI landed in #4893, and no open PR touches this test or `space-files.ts`.

## Change

When the core is built, the line still has to be the core's wording. Without the core, the test now expects exactly the bridge's fallback (`done: notes.txt`). The rest of the test (working line, failure path, empty drop) doesn't need the core, so it keeps running either way. I didn't use `skipIf`, because that would drop those checks too.

## Proof

- On origin/main without the wasm: `vitest run src/bridge/__tests__/detail.test.ts` gives 1 failed, 16 passed, 5 skipped.
- On this branch without the wasm: 17 passed, 5 skipped. `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- With the core built (CI path): the assertion is the same as before.
- The scoped repository checks have no Rust, Python or Markdown in scope for this diff.

title: fix(cua-driver): tell picom's damage lag from a torn frame in the X11 overlay test
body:
Fixes CUA-3172.

## Why

`x11_overlay_frames_are_never_composited_half_presented` fails now and then in Rust Linux unit on main. Its failing reads are all one solid square in one colour, cropped to 157x159 or 154x158 (for example "red 24963, blue 0, other 0"). That crop comes from picom, and the overlay presents frames correctly. picom 10.2's `repair_win` subtracts a window's damage, then paints that region from the window's live contents. When the next frame lands in between, picom shows that frame clipped to the previous frame's damage until it handles the next DamageNotify. The overlay square moves (+3, +1) each frame, so 157x159 is one frame of overlap and 154x158 is two. The test wanted a full 160x160 square and counted this lag as a tear.

## What changed

- Under a compositor, the test accepts one solid rectangle of one colour, no larger than the square, whose top-left corner is the newest frame's origin and whose colour is that frame's colour. Stale pixels from an earlier frame inside the new shape share that origin but have the other colour, so they still fail. So do mixed colours and foreign pixels.
- The compositor-less run keeps the full-square check, and the square must now also sit where a frame puts it.
- The settle loop at the end stops waiting once the observer thread has exited. Before, an observer error made it spin forever.

## Scope

Test-only. One function in `crates/platform-linux/src/overlay.rs`. The overlay's present path and the CI workflow are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

The overlay can't remove the crop, because picom paints a damaged region from the window's live contents. Pacing the test's frames also made the loop pass locally, but it only makes the race rarer on a slow runner, and the test would stop stressing the present path.

## Blast Radius

Only this ignored live-X11 test, which runs in Rust Linux unit under xvfb+picom and xvfb alone. Production code is not touched.

## Verification

The stress loop runs the CI step 1:1: `xvfb-run` at 1920x1080x24, `picom --backend xrender` (the Ubuntu 24.04 picom 10.2 package that CI installs), then the ignored test.
- main: 9 of 20 runs failed, each with 1 to 5 single-colour cropped squares.
- this branch: 0 of 20 runs failed at the head (another 25 and 20 earlier, also 0).
- To check that the guard still bites, I put back the pre-#6343 present path (reshape, then PutImage straight to the window) in a local build. The new check failed 5 of 5 runs, each with 640 or more two-colour reads like "red 637, blue 24963".
- The no-compositor test `x11_overlay_frames_are_never_seen_half_presented` passed 3 of 3. The scoped repository checks (fmt and test for platform-linux) passed. Windows and macOS were not built because the change is in the Linux-only crate.

title: fix(cua-driver): count a viewer's double- and triple-clicks on Windows and Hyprland
body:
Fixes #6424

Stacked on #6427 (it uses the `ClickCounter` that PR adds); the diff shows that PR's commits until it merges. The change of this PR is 4647bec1.

## Summary

A viewer's presses reach a Windows or Hyprland Space through `tool_input.rs`, which folds each batch into `click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `press_key` and `type_text` tool calls. The fold turned every down/up pair into a `click` with no count, so two quick clicks were two single clicks: a double-click never selected a word or opened a file.

```diff
 GestureFolder::fold (cua-driver-core/src/interactive_input/gestures.rs)
+  takes the batch's receipt time       # batches carry no timestamps
   on a down: remember the press
+  on a down: ClickCounter::press       # same button, within 500 ms and 4 px of the previous press → 2, 3
+  on a down after a 3: start over      # the click tool takes 1..=3
-  on an up within 4 px: Click { x, y, button, modifiers }
+  on an up within 4 px: Click { x, y, button, count, modifiers }
+  on a drag or cancel: forget the sequence

 ToolInputLease::call (cua-spacesd-desktop/src/tool_input.rs)
+  Click with count > 1 → `click` with `count`   # WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK on Windows, a press train on Hyprland
```

A viewer's double-click thus becomes `click` then `click { count: 2 }`. The second call delivers the press pair a double-click needs; the app sees one extra single click before it, which is what the `double_click` tool already sends. The interval is a constant (the Windows default; Hyprland has no system setting) rather than `GetDoubleClickTime`, to keep the fold platform-neutral. Say if you'd rather it read the Windows setting.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the new owner tests fail on `main` because `Gesture::Click` has no `count` and `click` is called without one.
- **After:** hermetic unit tests, run on Windows 11:
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib interactive_input`: 18 passed, including `quick_presses_at_one_spot_count_up_across_batches_up_to_three` (counts 1, 2 in one batch, 3 in the next, then starts over) and `a_late_far_or_dragged_press_starts_a_new_click_sequence`.
  - `cargo test -p cua-spacesd-desktop --lib tool_input`: 10 passed, including `a_viewers_double_click_reaches_the_click_tool_with_a_count` (two batches → `click`, then `click` with `"count": 2`).
  - clippy has no findings in the changed files.
- Not done: a live double-click through a viewer on a Windows or Hyprland Space. The native half (`count: 2` → `WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK` / `CLICK … 2`) is the path the `double_click` tool already uses; this PR only reaches it. `cua-spaces-ext` has no Windows or Hyprland input E2E sibling of the macOS one to extend.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

A revert restores the previous single-click behavior with no state to migrate.

**Blast Radius:** small

`Gesture::Click` gains a field and `GestureFolder::fold` a parameter; `tool_input.rs` is their only caller. Single clicks produce the same tool call as before (`count` is only set above 1). macOS and X11 do not use the fold.

title: fix(cua-driver): treat a niri focus read-back the deadline cut off as unconfirmed
body:
## Why
`wayland::niri::gate::tests::focus_taken_without_any_move_refuses_the_next_event` failed on main (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/41333855733) with "niri IPC FocusedWindow failed" instead of the not-confirmed refusal. `confirm_focus` keeps reading FocusedWindow until its 500 ms deadline, and each read-back shares that deadline. If one is still in flight when the deadline passes, `Lines::reply` times out and `?` returns the transport error in place of "niri did not confirm focus". The fake niri was correct. A loaded runner just delays its thread past the deadline. Real niri hits the same thing when it is slow, so the fix is in production code, not in the test.

## What changed
- In `confirm_focus`, a read-back that the deadline cut off (`io::ErrorKind::TimedOut` in its chain) counts as not confirmed. Any other IPC error still propagates.
- The refusal says `focused: unknown` when no read-back answered, so a stalled niri is not reported as "no focused window".
- New test `a_read_back_the_deadline_cuts_off_still_refuses_as_unconfirmed`: a fake answers twice and then stalls, and a second fake never answers.

## Scope
Only `confirm_focus` in `platform-linux/src/wayland/niri/focus.rs`. The sibling Workspaces confirm loops in `restore_focus` and `restore_workspace` have the same pattern. They already fail with an error either way and only the wording differs, so they are left for a follow-up.

## Blast Radius
This affects `PointerGate::holds`, `activate_in` and the prior-window restore. Each of them already refused in this case. The change is that they now return the coded `foreground_unavailable` refusal and not an uncoded IPC error. Connect timeouts are not affected because `attested_connection` turns them into plain text errors with no `io::Error` behind them.

## Verification
- A stress loop ran the gate test 3000 times, 48 processes at once, on a 4-core arm64 VM. Before the fix it failed 6, 15 and 18 times across three rounds, every time with the CI message. A probe showed each failure about 500 ms into the second `holds()` with an "niri IPC reply timed out" cause. After the fix, 4 rounds of 3000 had 0 failures. The new test also ran 2000 times under the same load with no failures.
- The new test fails on the test-only commit (`left: "niri IPC FocusedWindow failed"`) and passes with the fix.
- The scoped repository checks (fmt and test for `platform-linux`) pass. `cargo clippy -D warnings` fails only on existing lints in files this PR doesn't touch (`input/mod.rs`, `get_window_state.rs`, `hyprland.rs`, `wayland/mod.rs`, `launch_app.rs`, `press_key.rs`).
- After merging main (which brings the X11 overlay test deflake from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6431), the scoped repository checks pass again: fmt and test for `platform-linux`, including every `wayland::niri` test. The earlier CI reds were outside this diff. `overlay::tests::x11_overlay_frames_are_never_composited_half_presented` is fixed on main by that PR, and `relay e2e (docker)` failed in `cua-spacesd-server/tests/mesh_gang.rs`, which also fails on main.

CUA-3213

title: fix(spaces-web): compile components at dev server start so parity's first detail visit is not cold
body:
CUA-3238

Fixes #6081. `parity.spec.ts > parity flows > create-cancel [chromium]` failed on its first attempt because the Space detail page had not been compiled yet.

## Root cause

All 57 recorded failures are the same. `checkSpaceDetail` navigates to `/spaces/pending%3A1` and waits 5 s for `[data-detail-title]`, and the title never shows up. The trace from run 41766305906 shows:

- The URL changed to `/spaces/pending%3A1` right after the navigate.
- Only then did the dev server start serving `$spaceId.tsx?tsr-split=component`, followed by each component that page imports (`agents-section.tsx`, `facts.tsx`, `stream-section.tsx`, the network and thread components). Some of those requests were still in flight when the wait ran out.
- The error snapshot shows the Spaces list still drawn.

The detail route is code-split, so its first visit makes Vite transform its components on demand. On a loaded runner that takes longer than the 5 s wait. create-cancel runs early in the suite, so it is the first flow to open a Space detail on a cold server. The retry passes because by then the transforms are cached.

## Change

`apps/cua-spaces-web/vite.config.ts` sets `server.warmup.clientFiles: ["./src/components/**/*.tsx"]`, so Vite transforms the components when the server starts. A first visit then comes from the cache. The setting only affects the dev server, which is what the parity job runs. `vite build` and vitest ignore it.

I also tried warming only `./src/routes/**/*.tsx`. It did not stop the slow first visit, so it is not included.

## Proof

Reproduced with a one-off probe spec (not committed). It loads `/spaces?bridge=demo&parity`, calls `__cuaParity.navigate("/spaces/local%3Adesign-review")` on a fresh dev server, and waits 5 s for `[data-detail-title]`, the same wait the parity test uses. CPU load came from background `yes` processes. One worker, a fresh server each run:

| load | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| none | drawn, 4 of 4 | drawn, 4 of 4 |
| 10 busy procs | drawn, 3 of 3 | drawn, 3 of 3 |
| 20 busy procs | drawn, 3 of 3 | drawn, 3 of 3 |
| 40 busy procs | **not drawn in 5 s, 4 of 4** | drawn, 3 of 3 |

Before the change, the 40-process runs failed the same way CI does. After it, every run drew the detail page.

The scoped repository checks pass. They select nothing for a TypeScript-only diff. `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passes. The other chromium e2e specs fail identically with and without the change in a checkout without the wasm core: 8 of them fail on "the wasm core loaded" or follow-on waits, same specs both times.

Not run here: the full `pnpm parity` suite, because building the wasm core needs cargo and wasm-bindgen-cli, which this task avoids. The Electron parity job and Linux CI runners were also not run. CI on this PR runs both parity jobs.

title: test(cua-spacesd): make cursor coalescing coverage deterministic
body:
## Summary

The CI failure in #6388 is at the assertion that the newest cursor position arrived. The test uses real-time sleeps, then drains the receiver without synchronizing with the background flusher. This makes its timing dependent on runner load.

Run the existing test on Tokio's paused clock, as the neighboring 30 Hz test already does. Send the final two positions without advancing time, so the newest-position assertion requires the background flusher to deliver the pending update. Keep all rate-limit, minimum-delivery and final-position assertions.

Fixes #6388

## Compatibility and risk

Test-only: one file, 6 additions and 2 deletions. No production behavior, public API, dependencies or protocol changes; no RFC required.

## Validation

Tested source matches commit `3232ca5d095b9191c4443d09456c030546cfbc01`.

- Linux arm64, Rust 1.98.1, using the repository's Linux test image recipe:
  - `cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p cua-spacesd-desktop -- --test-threads=4`: 137 passed; one existing doctest ignored.
  - Focused test: 500/500 passes across four concurrent workers.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-spacesd -p cua-spacesd-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Mutation checks: removing rate limiting fails the count assertion; disabling the background flusher fails the newest-position assertion. Both temporary mutations were restored.
- `bin/ci --base upstream/main --no-install --jobs 2`: formatting, SPDX, image-reference and Windows static-cfg checks passed. Native macOS Clippy/tests could not build because the installed SDK is 15.5 and upstream `apple-metal` uses newer Metal APIs. Windows was not compiled locally.
- The original test passed normally locally; the exact intermittent CI failure was not reproduced. No quarantine, longer delay or relaxed assertion was added.

Upstream fork workflows, including Release metadata, currently require maintainer approval. This remains draft pending that gate; the cua-spacesd test jobs also skip drafts and run on `ready_for_review`.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop cutting off non-ASCII text typed into GTK3 and Qt fields
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `type_text` by accessibility cut non-ASCII text short in GTK3 and Qt fields and reported `unverifiable`. Example: `ñ🙂ab` became `ñ` in GTK3 and `ñ🙂a` in Qt.
- What changed: `EditableText.InsertText` takes a length, and toolkits read it differently. The driver now reads the toolkit name and sends UTF-16 units to Qt and bytes to everything else.

| Toolkit and widget | How it reads `length` | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| GTK3 `GtkEntry`, `GtkTextView` | Bytes | Cut short | Exact |
| GTK4 `GtkTextView` | Bytes, through `gtk_text_buffer_insert` | Cut short | Exact |
| GTK4 `GtkEntry` | Ignored: `GtkEditable` passes -1 | Exact | Exact |
| Qt `QLineEdit`, `QPlainTextEdit` | UTF-16 units: `text.resize(length)` in `atspiadaptor.cpp` | Cut short for non-BMP text | Exact |

Too small a count in Qt cuts the text. Too large appends uninitialized memory. So bytes alone, as `text.len()` on Issue #4754 suggests, fixes GTK3 and corrupts Qt.

**When the toolkit lookup misses.** A slow walk can spend the whole 1.5 s input budget, and the write still goes out. Two changes keep that safe:

1. The lookup gets its own 250 ms floor, so a spent budget doesn't skip it.
2. A real miss sends the UTF-16 count, which is never above the byte count. It can't over-read in Qt. Elsewhere it can only cut the text short, as main does today.

## Related work

Fixes #4754

**Relation to PR #4911.** That PR sends bytes to every toolkit, which fixes GTK3 and regresses Qt. On real Qt at its head `8bce0fbe7`, the same 8 strings gave 1/8 exact: Qt appended uninitialized memory (`✓ABC` became `✓ABC\0008`), and the driver reported `confirmed`. Its fixture is byte-bounded, not a real toolkit, so it couldn't show this.

RFC: not needed.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: non-ASCII text typed by element now arrives whole. No API change. Linux only, since this is AT-SPI.
- Risk: `toolkit_measures_from_frame` now reads the name through the same helper. It's one bounded call instead of three, with the same budget clamp. LibreOffice, the only toolkit it matches, wasn't run for this PR.
- Rollback: revert the PR.

## Validation

All measured with the real driver on `5baf9b797`. Its last merge from main changed nothing under `libs/cua-driver`, so the driver binary was built from `f38603623`. Debug build with `portal-input`. Real KWin on Wayland in a container, with KWin's permission checks on. Ground truth is the app's own changed signal.

**`type_text` by element, 8 strings** including typing after existing text and emoji:

| KWin (distro) | GTK3 Entry | GTK4 Entry | Qt LineEdit | GTK3 TextView | GTK4 TextView | Qt PlainTextEdit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6.6.6 (Ubuntu 26.04) | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| 6.8.2 (Fedora 45) | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 |

**The budget-spent path.** A focused field in an app with 6000 labels, under XWayland, with a driver that sees only X11. The walk really spends the budget (`collect_visited time budget exhausted` in its log). 3 strings each:

| Build | Qt | GTK3 |
|---|---|---|
| Previous head of this PR | 0/3, `✓ABC` became `✓ABC\x008` | 3/3 |
| `is_none_or` alone | 3/3 | 0/3, `✓ABC` became `✓A` |
| This branch | 3/3 | 3/3 |

Mutation check, `toolkit_of` forced to always return None: `text` mode drops to GTK3 Entry 1/8, GTK3 TextView 1/8, GTK4 TextView 1/8. The old ASCII GTK3 row stayed green, so that row now types `ax-ñ🙂-typed`, and the same mutant fails it. Qt has no row in the repo's matrix: `text` mode on KWin is its real check.

**Checks**

- `bin/ci --quick` on `5baf9b797`: 5 passed, 4 skipped by `--quick`.
- `spdx-headers.py --check libs/cua-driver`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --check`: passed.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --features portal-input --lib`: 938 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-linux -p cua-driver-e2e --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `harness_gtk3_type_text_ax_foreground`, run inside the same container: passed. I ran only this row, not the whole GTK3 binary. The background rows need the Electron sentinel, which that container lacks.

**Known gaps**

- With `--features portal-input`, clippy reports 6 findings in `wayland/libei.rs` and `wayland/mod.rs`. This PR doesn't touch those files.
- Debian 13 (KWin 6.3.6) wasn't rerun on this commit. The driver is built on Ubuntu 26.04 and needs a newer glibc than Debian has.
- Chromium text fields exposed no EditableText interface on my machine, so this path wasn't reached there.
- A real Kubuntu desktop wasn't rerun on this commit.
- Compositors other than KWin weren't run. This code is AT-SPI and doesn't depend on the compositor.
- The end-to-end, image and native Windows lanes run in CI only.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.

title: fix(cua-driver): find a pid's window on Wayland and name NO_AT_BRIDGE when it hides one
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Electron sets `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1` for itself, so a GTK3 app started from an Electron terminal or agent host stays off the accessibility bus, and the driver's answer points at the wrong thing. While tracing that, a second bug turned up: on native Wayland, `get_window_state({pid})` failed for every app, because it chose the window from X11 alone.
- What changed: `get_window_state` now picks a pid's window the same way the input tools do. The variable is named only where it can really hide a window, and `Provide window_id` always stays.

Answers on real KWin 6.6.6, native Wayland, `get_window_state({pid})` with no `window_id`:

| App | `NO_AT_BRIDGE` | Joined the bus | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GTK3 | 1 | No | `No windows found for pid N. atspi_bridge_disabled: ...never joined...` | `No windows found for pid N. Provide window_id. atspi_bridge_disabled: ...` |
| GTK3 | 0 | Yes | `No windows found for pid N. Provide window_id.` | Tree returned |
| GTK4, Qt | 1 | Yes | `...atspi_bridge_disabled: ...never joined...`, which is false | Tree returned |
| GTK4, Qt | 0 | Yes | `No windows found for pid N. Provide window_id.` | Tree returned |

"Before" is the previous head of this PR, merged onto main.

The new note reads: `atspi_bridge_disabled: the target runs with NO_AT_BRIDGE=1, which keeps GTK3 and other ATK apps off the accessibility bus. Start it with launch_app, or with that variable unset, to get its tree.`

**Where the note appears**

| Answer | When |
|---|---|
| `get_window_state`, `No windows found` | Wayland, and `list_windows` also finds nothing for that pid |
| Input tools, `window_target_not_found` | Wayland, and the variable is set. This guard answers before the tool runs |
| `list_windows`, text only | Wayland, a pid filter, nothing listed |
| `get_window_state` with a `window_id`, `degraded_reason` | Any session, when the walk returned no tree |

On X11 the window is listed whatever the variable says, so `No windows found` never blames the bridge there.

**Why the five other tools keep their old string.** The input tools are wrapped in a guard that already chooses the window through the dispatch. With a real pid they never reach their own `No windows found` line, so the note went to the guard's refusal.

**Why `list_windows` has no `reason` field.** `ListWindowsOutput` is a typed cross-platform record with generated bindings, so a field means a contract change on every platform. The note goes in its text.

**Limit of the advice.** In these KWin runs, a GTK3 app with the bridge off isn't in the unfiltered list either, so the caller has no `window_id` to give. The note is what tells them to restart it there.

## Related work

Fixes #6499

RFC: not needed. No contract or schema change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: `get_window_state({pid})` now works on native Wayland. Error text changes on Linux, as above. `PidOnlyWindowTargetGuard` gains an optional note. Only Linux sets it, so macOS and Windows answer as before.
- Risk: on Wayland, `get_window_state({pid})` now picks the pid's topmost on-screen window, as the input tools do. X11 keeps its focused, dialog, active, largest order. PR #6450 edits the same lines and calls the same resolver, so the merge is small.
- Rollback: revert the PR.

Merge note: this and PR #6450 change the same `get_window_state` lines, so the second one to land needs a small conflict resolved: `pid_only_window`'s last closure calls `pid_fallback_window_resolver()`. Tested merged together.

## Validation

All measured with the real driver on `1d7412774`, debug build with `portal-input`, in a container with KWin's permission checks on. "Joined the bus" is read from the accessibility registry itself, not from the driver.

| Session | KWin (distro) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Native Wayland | 6.6.6 (Ubuntu 26.04) | The "Now" column above, and `bridge` mode: `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1` shows the note, `=0` reaches the field |
| Native Wayland | 6.8.2 (Fedora 45) | The same table |
| X11 through XWayland, driver sees only X11 | 6.6.6 (Ubuntu 26.04) | GTK3 with `=1` is listed and returns `degraded_reason`, no tree. GTK3 with `=0`, and GTK4 and Qt with either value, return the tree |

`type_text` in the `bridge` row is cut to `ñ` until PR #6443 lands. That's a separate bug.

**New e2e tests in `harness_gtk3_test.rs`**, run on native Wayland and on X11:

| Test | Previous head | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `harness_gtk3_ax_tree_by_pid` | Wayland failed, X11 passed | Both passed |
| `harness_gtk3_no_windows_names_the_bridge_only_on_wayland` | Both failed | Both passed |

Mutation checks, each one failed for the expected reason:

- Dropping the walk's fallback to the environment fails `an_empty_walk_reads_the_reason_from_the_real_process`.
- Dropping the guard's note fails the second e2e test on Wayland.
- Dropping the Wayland gate fails the same test on X11.
- Dropping the `list_windows` note fails the same test on Wayland.

**Checks**

- `bin/ci --quick` on `1d7412774`: 5 passed, 4 skipped by `--quick`.
- `spdx-headers.py --check libs/cua-driver`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --check`: passed.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --features portal-input --lib`: 938 passed.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 1193 passed, 16 failed. All 16 are `perception_*` tests whose fixture needs `python3`, which the build container lacks. This PR doesn't touch that code. CI runs them.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-linux -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver-e2e --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Known gaps**

- With `--features portal-input`, clippy reports 6 findings in `wayland/libei.rs` and `wayland/mod.rs`. This PR doesn't touch those files.
- Debian 13 (KWin 6.3.6) wasn't rerun on this commit. The driver is built on Ubuntu 26.04 and needs a newer glibc than Debian has.
- GNOME, Hyprland, niri and Sway weren't run. From reading the code: GNOME's helper, Hyprland and niri attest a window's pid, so a bridge-off GTK3 window is still found and the note stays off. Sway lists no pid, so it should answer like KWin here.
- I didn't run this error path on a real Kubuntu desktop.
- The end-to-end, image and native Windows lanes run in CI only.

title: fix(cua-driver): report a sent but unanswered AT-SPI option pick as may-have-landed
body:
## Why

On Linux, `set_value` on a combo box picks an option over AT-SPI (`Selection.SelectChild`, or the popup item's `doAction`). If that call was sent and then failed or never answered, `activate_option_ref` and `select_option_ref` returned a plain error. `set_value` reported that as a failed write, so a pick that may already have taken effect looked like nothing happened, and the caller was asked to pick again.

## What changed

- `atspi/native.rs`: both pick routes now go through `send_pick`. `true` is picked. `false` (refused) and replies saying the option is gone (`UnknownObject`, `UnknownMethod`, `UnknownInterface`, `ServiceUnknown`) stay plain errors. Any other error reply, or no answer, becomes the typed `OptionPickSent`. A pick is not reported as sent when the deadline has already passed and the call was never made.
- `tools/set_value.rs`: `OptionPickSent` is handled on both the focus-free route and the popup route. The result reads the combo box back: `confirmed` when it shows the option, otherwise `effect: unverifiable` with a note and no escalation.

## Scope

Covers the two combo-option pick routes and how `set_value` reports them. It leaves out the other AT-SPI input routes (`doAction` on clicks, `EditableText` writes), which #5574 covers with its own `InputMayHaveLanded` type. This branch and #5574 merge with no conflicts. Once both land, the two error types could be folded into one.

## Blast Radius

Linux `set_value` on combo boxes and lists only. Successful, refused and unknown-option picks behave as before. The only change is that a pick which was sent but got an error reply or no answer is now reported with its readback instead of as an error.

## Verification

- New `tests/atspi_option_pick.rs` drives `activate_option_ref` and `select_option_ref` against a fake accessible combo box on a private dbus-daemon, with options that act, decline, vanish, raise and stall. On origin/main it fails with `activate Stalls: a sent pick came back as a plain error: option action did not answer in time`. With the fix it passes.
- `a_sent_pick_is_never_reported_as_failed_or_a_noop` pins the `set_value` result: confirmed on a matching readback, otherwise `unverifiable` with no escalation.
- The scoped repository checks (fmt and tests for `platform-linux`) pass, and clippy reports no new warnings. A live GTK or Qt combo box was not driven, and neither were Windows or macOS (not affected and not buildable here).

Review notes: the background popup route still drops the focus-guard report when the pick errors, because `focus_guard::guarded` returns early on `Err`. That predates this change and is left for a follow-up.

CUA-3236

title: fix(ci): accept transient upstream 5xx in the docs external link check
body:
The docs external link check (lychee) failed on a link that works. On #3897, `https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions` returned 500 after lychee's default 3 retries. The same URL answers 301 to aistudio.google.com and then 200 on repeated requests now. A server error on the far end says nothing about whether our link is right, so the gate should not fail on it.

## Change

`--accept 100..=399` becomes `--accept 100..=399,500,502..=504` in `.github/workflows/ci-check-docs-links.yml`. 500, 502, 503 and 504 are the usual transient outage codes. 4xx (including 429), 501, 505 and above (including Cloudflare's 521/522 "origin down" codes) and connection failures still fail.

Alternatives not taken:
- A `.lycheeignore` entry for the URL would hide it for good and only cover one host.
- More retries would not get past a 500 that lasts longer than the retry window.

## Proof

- Using lychee 0.24.2 (the version the action installs, per the failed run's log) against a local server that returns a fixed status: 200, 500, 502, 503 and 504 exit 0. 501, 505, 521, 522, 404 and 429 exit 2. A refused connection exits 1.
- I ran the full CI lychee command over `docs/content/**/*.mdx` with this accept range: 0 errors.
- The scoped repository checks pass. Nothing touched is a crate or a pyproject, so they reduce to the em-dash check, which passes.

Known cost: a page that stays broken on the server side (a long-lived 500) now passes until someone notices it.

CUA-3253

risk: light

title: fix(cua-driver): type exact text on the active keyboard layout or refuse it
body:
## Summary

**Problem this solves.** Desktop `type_text` through libei could report success with the wrong text. It read only the first layout in the keymap, guessed modifiers from level numbers, and ignored Caps Lock. A long text could also fail while it kept typing, so a retry typed it twice.

**The contract now:** exact text, or a refusal with nothing typed.

**What changed:**

1. **Active layout and lock keys.** Keys follow the layout and lock keys in effect, from libei when the compositor reports them, otherwise from KWin itself (D-Bus `org.kde.keyboard` and the `org_kde_kwin_keystate` global).
2. **Every key is proven.** Each key and modifier chord is checked with `xkb::State` before anything is sent. Libei and niri share one lookup in `text_keys.rs`.
3. **Long text.** Text goes out one acknowledged step at a time from the worker loop, so the worker keeps serving EIS. The caller waits as long as the text keeps moving, and a stuck text says how far it got.
4. **One refusal.** `code: "foreground_unavailable"`, `effect: "none"`, detail ending in `nothing was typed`, on libei, niri, wtype and Hyprland. Control characters other than line feed, carriage return and tab are refused on all four. A CRLF is one Return.
5. **Earlier work on this branch stays:** AltGr, only keys Chromium receives (X11 apps then get them too), Return for line breaks, and no `ei_text` while an X11 app may have focus.

| Case | Before | Now | Measured on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `de,us`, `us` active, `y\nz` | `z\ny`, success | exact | KWin 6.3.6, 6.6.6, 6.8.2, Qt on Wayland and Xwayland |
| Caps Lock on, `Hello 123` | `hELLO 123`, success | exact | same |
| Caps Lock on and `us` active before the driver starts | not measured | exact | 6.6.6, 6.8.2, Qt on Wayland |
| `th`, `1` (only on a keypad level) | nothing typed, success | refused | 6.6.6 |
| `th`, `123 ฟ` | ` ฟ`, success | refused | 6.6.6 |
| 200 lines plus an emoji | 20.56 s, "did not become ready" while the text finished | 20.71 s, success, exact, once | 6.8.2 |
| 200 long lines, 13889 characters | 0.25 s, EAGAIN error, 2108 characters landed, the next call timed out | 0.65 s, exact, next call exact in 0.12 s | 6.8.2 |
| Driver has no `DISPLAY`, X11 app, `日本` | lost, success | refused | Before on 6.8.2, now on 6.6.6 and 6.8.2 |
| Xwayland stopped (SIGSTOP), 6 calls | not measured | exact or refused, one extra thread and one extra fd | 6.6.6 |

## Related work

Fixes #6500

RFC: not required. No API or protocol change, only which text is refused and how.

## Compatibility and risk

**Behavior changes:**

1. Text the active layout can't type is refused whole. On plain `us` that includes `€`, which exists there only on a key X11 apps can't receive.
2. **KWin 6.3 to 6.5 without a desktop entry refuses letters.** These versions offer `org_kde_kwin_keystate` only to programs whose entry lists it in `X-KDE-Wayland-Interfaces`, and they send no modifier events. With Caps Lock unknown, text whose keys depend on it is refused, while digits and most punctuation still go out. Measured on 6.3.6, read from KWin's source for 6.4 and 6.5. KWin 6.6 offers the global to any client (measured on 6.6.6).
   - PR #6785 writes this entry and must add it: `X-KDE-Wayland-Interfaces=org_kde_plasma_window_management,org_kde_kwin_keystate`, comma separated. A semicolon list was not honored on 6.3.6.
   - **Merge that with or before this PR**, or KDE on Debian 13 can't type letters until then.
3. The driver taps Shift once before its first text when nothing has reported the keyboard yet, because KWin 6.8 reports only changes. Apps see it as a no-op key.
4. A held or latched modifier refuses the text.
5. Characters reachable only behind Ctrl, Alt or Super are refused on libei. On niri they now go on a spare key.
6. `gdbus` is needed on KWin before 6.8 to read a multi-layout keymap. Without it, such a keymap is refused.

**New file under another license:** `protocol/keystate.xml` comes from KDE's plasma-wayland-protocols, LGPL-2.1-or-later, with its header kept.

**Rollback:** revert the PR.

Merge note: this and PR #6448 each add a `mod` line at the same place in `wayland/mod.rs`, so the second one to land keeps both lines. Tested merged together.

## Validation

**45 cases, typed one at a time,** at desktop scope with the real portal and libei. Commit a6f6042e7, `us altgr-intl`, permission checks on, driver granted through a desktop entry. The entry on 6.3.6 lists `org_kde_kwin_keystate`.

| System | KWin | Qt, Wayland | Qt, Xwayland | Chrome, Wayland | Chrome, Xwayland |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu 26.04 packages | 6.6.6 | 45/45 | 45/45 | 45/45 | 45/45 |
| Debian 13 | 6.3.6 | 45/45 | 45/45 | 45/45 | 45/45 |
| Fedora 45 | 6.8.2 | 45/45 | 45/45 | 45/45 | 45/45 |

- With plain `us` on the same commit: 6.6.6 is 40/45 in all four clients, and 6.8.2 is 40/45 in both Xwayland clients and 45/45 in both Wayland clients. The other 5 are clean refusals of `€ ¿ ñ é Ñ`. Plain `us` was not run on 6.3.6.
- `main`, measured earlier and not rerun: 37 or 38 of 45 on 6.3.6 and 6.6.6, and 42 to 45 on 6.8.2.

**Also on a6f6042e7, on all three KWins:**

1. `layouts` with `de,us`, 24 cases: no wrong text. 22 exact and 2 refused on 6.3.6 and 6.6.6, 23 exact and 1 refused on 6.8.2. The refusals are `ñ`, which the layout lacks.
2. `long`: as in the table on 6.8.2. On 6.3.6 and 6.6.6 the emoji case is refused, since they have no `ei_text`, and the rest is exact.
3. `altgr` with `us altgr-intl`: the 4 Latin strings are exact everywhere. `日本語` and `abc日def` are refused on 6.3.6 and 6.6.6, exact on 6.8.2.
4. `typeroute`: `plain ascii 123` is exact in a Qt field, a Qt widget that only takes keys, GTK3 and GTK4. `ñandú €5` is exact on 6.8.2 and refused on 6.3.6 and 6.6.6 on plain `us`, the same as before this rework. The harness labels those refusals `LOST` and `WRONG`; they have `effect: none`.

**Also on a6f6042e7:**

1. KWin 6.3.6 with the entry not listing the global: letters refused, nothing typed.
2. `keypad:oss_latin9`, `÷` (needs Alt): refused on 6.6.6. The earlier code also refused it on that KWin, so it never reached the wrong text there.
3. `de neo`: `κ` on level 5 and `…` are exact on 6.6.6. Levels 5 to 8 work where a plain modifier key reaches them.

On 6.8.2, typing right after a `ctrl+a` hotkey, and `a\tb`, are exact.

**The binary on Debian 13** was built on Ubuntu 26.04, then patched to use a bundled glibc 2.43, because Debian's glibc is older. The driver code is the same.

**Tests:**

1. `platform-linux` unit tests: 969 pass, 11 ignored, with `portal-input`, on 556c01103. The final commit a6f6042e7 changes only a code comment, and the shared build image was gone when I went to rerun them.
2. New tests send through `Cmd::TypeText` to a real worker and a local EIS with a keyboard and `ei_text`, with no host X server or D-Bus. The seam is `DesktopFacts`, read by the caller.
3. 25 mutants across layout, proof, ranking, refusal, routing, pacing and giving up were all killed. Six first survived or failed to compile, so tests were added for them. One of those tests found a real overflow panic in the worker, now fixed.
4. Most of these tests were written with the code, so they were mutation-checked rather than watched fail against the old API.
5. On 556c01103, `clippy -D warnings` with `portal-input` and `cargo check` without it are clean. On a6f6042e7, `bin/ci --quick` passes 5 of 5 run checks, rustfmt included, with the other 4 skipped in quick mode, and `spdx-headers.py --check` passes.

**Earlier evidence, not rerun on this commit:**

1. niri: on real niri 26.04 in a headless cage, Chrome saw `Digit9` for `(`, and `a(b)c$*+!` was exact in Qt, foot and Chrome. Today niri is covered by unit tests only.
2. A real Kubuntu 26.04.1 desktop, Plasma 6.6.6, `us altgr-intl`, with a build combining six KDE PRs: `ñandú ¿qué? €5` and line breaks were exact.

**Known gaps:**

1. GNOME/Mutter was not run. That it reports the keyboard at device creation is read from its source.
2. A compositor that reports nothing and offers no `org_kde_kwin_keystate` refuses letters.
3. wlroots through `wtype` and Hyprland were not run; their refusals are unit tested.
4. Hyprland text still uses fixed US keycodes, so a non-US layout there can still type wrong letters. This PR doesn't change that.
5. The X11 session routes are unchanged. From reading the code, they send CR and LF as two Returns and don't refuse control characters. Not measured.
6. Text with line breaks that needs `ei_text` takes about 100 ms per line, so 200 lines take 20 s. It no longer blocks the worker.
7. A text returns once EIS has acknowledged every key. A Qt field can still be working through a long text after that: 13889 characters took a few more seconds. That the keys have already left KWin for that app, so a focus change can't redirect them, is inferred, not measured.
8. `drag` still sleeps in the worker, for at most 10 s, unchanged.
9. A hung X server or `DISPLAY` unset with an X socket present counts as an X11 app having focus, so on KWin 6.8 such text goes as keys and may be refused.
10. Full `bin/ci` and `--signoff` were not run, because this is a shared host. GitHub CI is the remaining check.

The harness scenarios (`layouts`, `long`, `capsfirst`, `hungx`, `nodisplay`, `texts`, `refusal`, `modlog`) ran in disposable containers, and the portal dialog was clicked by the test.

title: fix(cua-driver): use KWin's logical desktop frame for capture and input
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on a scaled KWin session, a pixel read off a desktop screenshot lands in the wrong place when clicked. KWin's screenshots are physical pixels and libei pointer input is logical. `get_screen_size` also fails with `$DISPLAY variable not set` when there's no X11 display.
- What changed: the driver reads KWin's logical layout from `xdg-output` and uses it as the desktop frame, the same `DesktopFrame` model as Hyprland and niri. Capture is resized to that frame and desktop input converts through it, on any layout. Other compositors are unchanged, except that a desktop click at (0, 0) on any libei route now lands there instead of on the output's center.

Behavior on KWin:

1. `get_screen_size` and `get_desktop_state` report one frame and one scale, the largest output's. `get_screen_size` lists every monitor.
2. A layout that doesn't start at (0, 0) works. Frame pixel (0, 0) is its top-left point. `get_desktop_state` window geometry and `get_cursor_position` use that frame too.
3. A KWin that can't report its layout is an error, not a silent return to the physical frame.
4. These refuse, with a message that says why:
   - a point in a gap between monitors;
   - a point at negative layout coordinates, which libei can't address (KWin dropped the motion, and the click landed at the old pointer position, when I let one through);
   - on KWin below 6.6, a point on an output rotated 90 or 270 degrees. KWin 6.3.6 draws that output distorted in the capture, even alone at scale 1, where the driver doesn't resize. The screenshot still returns, and `distorted_outputs` names the output.

KWin is recognised by its `kde_output_*` globals, matched by prefix, because 6.8 renamed `kde_output_device_v2` to `kde_output_device_registry_v2`.

## Related work

Refs #3061 (GNOME is not fixed here)

RFC: not required.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: KWin only. `get_screen_size` on KWin gains `monitors` and its text now says **Desktop frame**. `get_desktop_state` gains `distorted_outputs` when it applies. Desktop clicks at (0, 0) are literal on every libei route, GNOME included (not run on GNOME). Window-scoped libei clicks keep their existing center behavior.
- Risk and rollback: a KWin without `zxdg_output_manager_v1` now gets an error where it used to get wrong coordinates. Revert the PR to roll back.

Merge note: this and PR #6447 each add a `mod` line at the same place in `wayland/mod.rs`, so the second one to land keeps both lines. Tested merged together.

## Validation

All measured on this PR's head, on real KWin with the real Screenshot and RemoteDesktop portals in a container, with KWin's permission checks on and no grant. The portal's dialogs were clicked by the test, inside that disposable session.

Ground truth is the press each window logged, or KWin's own pointer position.

| Measure, KWin 6.6.6 | Before (7080cc181) | Now | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Only output at (864,0): `get_screen_size` and `get_desktop_state` | Both error | 1920x1080, screenshot returned | Works |
| Same layout: click on a screenshot marker | No screenshot to read | On target, 2 of 2 | On target |
| Outputs at scale 1 and 2, in that order: `get_screen_size` / `get_desktop_state` scale | 1.0 / 2.0 | 2.0 / 2.0 | Same, largest |
| Click at screenshot (0, 0), scale 1.25: real pointer | (800, 450) | (0, 0) | (0, 0) |
| `LAYOUT=two`: `get_screen_size` output | "Main display", no monitors | "Desktop frame", 2 monitors | Every monitor |
| `frame OUTPUT_SCALE=1.25` | (320, 220), on target | (320, 220), on target | On target |
| `frame`, scale 1.0 | Not rerun | (319, 219), on target | On target |
| `monitors LAYOUT=two`, desktop rows | 13 of 13 | 13 of 13 | All |

The other 11 `monitors` rows need window bounds and window capture, which aren't in this PR and fail the same way before and after with no grant.

On the same non-origin layout, `move_cursor`, `scroll` and `drag` also landed on the screenshot point, and `get_cursor_position` returned the frame point.

- Focused tests and checks: new owner test `kwin_logical_frame_test`, `#[ignore]`d and on the manual allowlist. It compares the frame with GDK's view of the outputs, then clicks a marker and the first pixel of every output.

| Layout | KWin 6.3.6 (Debian 13) | KWin 6.6.6 (Ubuntu 26.04) | KWin 6.8.2 (Fedora 45) |
|---|---|---|---|
| One output at scale 1.25 | Pass | Pass | Pass |
| Two outputs at 1.25, one rotated | Pass, rotated output refuses | Pass | Pass |
| One output at (864,0) | Pass | Pass | Pass |
| Scales 1 and 2 | Pass | Pass | Pass |
| An output at (-1920,-200), clicks there refuse | Pass | Pass | Pass |
| One output at (864,0) at scale 1.25 | Not run | Pass | Not run |

title: fix(ci): give the shared Electron + Tauri E2E leg its own sccache family
body:
The shared Electron + Tauri E2E leg on Linux and Windows now saves its own sccache entry. Before, it restored an entry that held none of its release units and rebuilt them on every run.

CUA-3237

## Why

`.github/actions/rust-cache` ignores `key:`. It names the cache family after the first workspace, so every `libs/cua-driver/rust` job on main shares `libs-cua-driver-rust`, with one entry per UTC day. Debug-only unit jobs save that entry first each day, for example `CI: Rust Linux unit` and `cua-driver Valgrind`, where it is 909 MiB at 99% hits. The shared leg in the 06:00 nightly gate then gets an exact hit, skips its save, and finds almost none of its release units in the entry.

On main's nightly gate run 41589165345 (3 Nov), the Linux shared job logs `restored 913M in 948 files (exact hit)` and then `Cache hit occurred on the primary key ..., not saving cache`. Its sccache summary is 28% hits with 1037 Rust misses. It does three full release builds: `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`, the Tauri fixture, and install-local's `cargo build --release -p cua-driver -p cursor-theme-cli`. Windows is the same at 44%. Fingerprint inputs are not the cause: RUSTFLAGS, profile and target dir are the same between runs, and the misses are units the restored entry never held.

## What changed

- `e2e-rust-linux.yml`, `e2e-rust-windows.yml`: the `shared` job's cache step sets `shared-key: cua-driver-e2e-shared` in place of the ignored `key: e2e-shared`. The nightly gate on main saves that entry, and PRs restore it.
- Tests in `test_e2e_rust_{linux,windows}_workflow.py` pin the shared job to its own family. They fail on the old workflows.

## Scope

Covers the shared leg only. The native, capture and installer legs still share `libs-cua-driver-rust`. The verify-skill job's `Swatinem/rust-cache` step is not changed.

## Blast Radius

CI cache only. Until the first nightly after merge saves the new family, PR runs of the shared leg start cold. Before, they got a partial prefix hit.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks pass. Two `workflow_dispatch` runs of each workflow with `lane=shared` on this branch:

- Seeding runs (Linux 41786844798, Windows 41786848326): `family=cua-driver-e2e-shared`, `miss, starting cold`, then `Cache saved with key: sccache-v2-<OS>-X64-cua-driver-e2e-shared_20261104`.
- Warm Linux run 41792600894: `restored 1.7G in 1688 files (exact hit)`, then `100% - 1546 hits, 0 misses`. No Rust unit recompiled. Before this change, main's nightly got 28% here.
- Warm Windows run 41792603861: `restored 1.7G in 1425 files (exact hit)`, then `90% - 1278 hits, 147 misses`. Before this change, main's nightly got 44% here.

This PR's own release-gate run (41786914511) started at the same time as the seeding runs and found no entry, so it started cold. A PR restores main's entries, so PR runs warm up after the first nightly that runs after merge.
