title: feat(spaces): the new prompt box with a model and an optional repo
body:
## What changes

Home's box is now the first prompt of a chat app. The old row ("Describe the job in your own words ... @claude in New Space") is replaced by the job on top and one row under it:

- **Agent menu.** The groups are the coding apps the person has connected: Codex, Hermes, Claude Code and OpenCode first, the others only once one of their accounts works. Under each app are its accounts (sign-ins and keys, by the names the connector data already shows, such as a Claude Max sign-in or "work Max") as rows to pick; picking one picks the app and the account. An app with no account has a "Sign in" row. The chevron on an app's header opens that app's sign-ins in place: which is the default, make default, rename, remove and add. The model is a quiet "Model" line at the bottom of the menu, shown only for an account that offers a choice. The chip in the box shows only the app ("Claude Code"); the account is the ticked row inside the menu. An account reads as `ada@example.com (Max)` (identifier, plan when known), the name the person gave it, `ChatGPT` when no email is known, or `API Key (*abcd)`; the label is the app core's, shared by the web, SwiftUI and Electron hosts.
- **What is remembered.** The account is the app's own choice, kept by the host (`agentKeys.use`, beside the keys), so a run uses the one shown and it survives relaunch; the app and the model are kept on this computer. The app has no general preferences store in the bridge. A remembered account that is no longer saved is never used: the app's own choice, else its first account, stands in; with nothing remembered the first connected app in the menu's order is used.
- **Run side.** Claude Code and Codex can now be told which credential to use (they were fixed to one sign-in), under the app's setup id whichever of it and the harness id a caller has. Another Claude sign-in can be added beside the first (a pasted token with a name), and any saved key or sign-in can be renamed (`agent_keys.rename`, `agentKeys.rename`, through the web, SwiftUI and Electron hosts).
- **Core.** `connectors.agents` (`AgentsView`, `AgentGroup`, `AgentAccount`, `AgentRef`) in the app core with parity flows and goldens; the words are the core's and have no middle dot or "device".
- **Optional repo chip.** "Add a repo" takes a link (repo, issue, pull request, folder, or ssh) or `owner/name`, refuses what is not a repo, keeps the five used lately, and shows the repo as a chip with a way to remove it. The repo goes into the job's message as one plain line (`Repo: <url>`), so the agent starts by getting it.
- **Where it runs.** Without the Child Spaces experiment it stays as a quiet picker in the same row (a new computer, This Mac, or a running Space). With Ask first and Child Spaces both on, there is no where row at all (see the next section).
- **The model reaches the agent.** The picked model rides with the agent when it joins the Space (`thread.agentAdd` now carries `model`, `standby` and `brief` through the web, macOS and desktop bridges; adding the same member again updates it), and with `agents.start` on the run path and the first-run preparing path.

## The agent's Home Space (Ask first and Child Spaces on)

With both existing experiments on, the empty box shows only the model and the repo chip. The job goes to the agent's Home Space instead:

- A normal Space page on the existing slim Linux image, `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim`, made on the first request and reused by the next ones (one per agent; "Let the agent decide, in a new Home" asks for a fresh one), with the spawn capability on and no new image family. The Home is tagged "Home" in the Spaces list and found again by its `cua.home` label on a new computer.
- The agent makes the Spaces the job needs (Linux, Windows or macOS), inside the tree's budget, on the person's own computers when asked in plain words. Nothing to pick.
- A place is named with `@` in the text; the "..." button then appears with the agent's choice, a new computer, This Mac, your computers and your running Spaces. An `@mention` of a Space or computer (or "on my Mac") is the grant, so no card asks. Picking from the menu also keeps a quiet "in <place>" note.
- An agent's request for an ability (list all Spaces, use a computer) is a standard approval card in the Home's thread; allowing it is remembered per agent and written where the daemon reads it, so it takes effect in the running Home at once.
- Home keeps the agent's Home warm, and one quiet line under the box says "Agent ready", "Starting agent" or "Reconnect needed".

What it adds, by layer:

- Web: the child Spaces store (`spaces.tree`, `children.set`, `budget.*`, `services.*`), `lib/agent-home`, the Home tag, the ability approval card, the demo (`?demo=agent-home`).
- Daemon: `children/home.rs`, the three abilities as this host enforces them (list Spaces, spawn a child, use a computer) from the Home's `cua.home.*` labels and a grants file only the app writes; listing granted Spaces and refusing a computer the person has not allowed, in words the agent can act on.
- SwiftUI and Electron hosts: the tree, children, budget and services operations, the Home grants file, and the create's `children` and `labels`.

## Depends on the slim image change

The Home only works end to end once the slim image carries the `cua` CLI and a spawn-capable `cua-spacesd` (a separate image change; this one touches no image recipe). Until then the Home Space is created and takes the job, but an agent in it cannot run `cua spaces create`. The coding apps are installed on first run as in any Space.

## What was already here

The daemon side (`brief` and `briefed_run` on persistent agent records, `model` and `standby` on the agent-add input) and the preparing driver's `model` and `repo` fields were already on main, so this change is the web UI, the bridge argument mapping, the demo adapter and the macOS pass-through only. Sign-in and the guided first run are untouched.

## Tests

- New: `ask-box.test.tsx` (the default app and account, groups and Sign in rows, pick and remember across a reload, the sign-ins page with default, rename and remove, the model line, Enter and Shift+Enter, nothing signed in, repo add, refuse, keep, remove, repo line in the posted message, wording guard), `ask-first-model.test.ts` (remembered account gone, fallbacks), `ask-first-repo.test.ts`; Rust tests for `agents_view`, the choice of account for Claude Code and Codex, adding another Claude sign-in and rename, and the `connectors.agents` parity flows.
- Updated for the new box (tests that need Claude Code remember it as the last pick): `ask-first-in-space`, `ask-first-start-failed`, `home-agents`, `onboarding-lands-on-home`, `warming-home-hidden`.
- Removed `home-agent-picker.test.tsx`: it tested the installed-apps "Who does it" menu and "Install Claude Code", which the model-driven box replaces.
- New: `agent-home-box.test.tsx` (no where row until `@`, the job goes to the Home on the slim image with the spawn capability, the model on standby and the briefing), `lib/agent-home` tests, child store and Home label tests, Rust tests for the abilities (`children::tests`), desktop and Swift tests for the grants file and create extras.
- `bin/ci` (rustfmt, web typecheck, design lint, tests and bridge contract, SPDX, image refs), desktop typecheck and tests, and clippy on `cua-daemon` pass.

## Not in this change

- The Children sheet on the Space page (budget and kept commands UI) and the secure network panels: the store and operations are here, the sheet is not needed by the box.
- The headless image tier and any image recipe.
- The Swift code and its tests compile, but the Swift tests were not run here (they need the native SDK library).

Screenshots for review (simulated accounts: three Claude, one Codex, none for Hermes or OpenCode) are in the owner's shots folder; real-run screenshots are still to be taken before merge.

title: fix(cua-daemon): wait for the lock after release in the instance-lock test
body:
CUA-3334

`instance_lock_tests::a_second_daemon_for_the_same_home_is_refused` fails on `rust (macos-26)` on main. It panics at the last step, the re-acquire after `drop(first)`, with `InstanceHeld { pid: Some(<test pid>) }`. The refusal assertions themselves pass.

Cause: other tests in the same binary spawn child processes. A child forked while `first` holds the lock inherits a copy of the descriptor, and the `flock` stays held until that child's exec closes the copy (std opens files `O_CLOEXEC`). If the child is still between fork and exec when the test drops its handle, an immediate `try_lock` (`Duration::ZERO`) finds the lock still held. Real daemons don't hit this because they acquire with a wait. The lock code isn't wrong. The test just leaves no room for that window.

Fix: re-acquire with a 5 s wait, which is what a restarting daemon does. Test-only change.

Repro on macOS arm64: with four threads spawning `/usr/bin/true` in a loop inside the test, main fails the test 5/20 runs and this branch fails it 0/20. A standalone drop-then-`try_lock` loop with concurrent spawns hits the held lock often on immediate re-acquire, and never once it waits.

title: fix(cua-driver): detect Hyprland input internals instead of pinning 0.56.2
body:
## Why

The Hyprland plugin's input route refuses to configure on anything but Hyprland 0.56.2 (`Input is pinned to Hyprland 0.56.2`, `libs/cua-driver/hyprland-plugin/CMakeLists.txt:250`). That pin is why the Hyprland nightly goes red now that Arch ships 0.57.1. This salvages https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6253 by @chrisohearn, merged onto current main with the contributor's commits kept. It drops the pin and compile-checks the window and layer-surface internals that input reads, so it doesn't swap in a pin to 0.57.0.

CUA-3320. Refs https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/5751, https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6253.

## What changed

- `cua_detect_hyprland_window_api` (in `cmake/DetectHyprlandAPI.cmake`) picks the 0.57 window-backend API (`mapped()`, `backend().isX11()/pid()`, `m_exclusiveKeyboardLSes`) or the legacy one (`m_isMapped`, `m_isX11`, `getPID()`, `m_exclusiveLSes`). Any other result fails configuration.
- `input_experiment.cpp` reads those four internals through small helpers chosen by `CUA_HYPRLAND_WINDOW_BACKEND_API`.
- The `tests/cmake-api` mock headers cover the backend, legacy and unsupported tiers, plus a repeat of backend to show the tier is re-probed rather than read from cache. Those headers ship in the release source bundle, and the release test runs `cmake_api` from the bundle.

## Scope

Covers the configure gate and the input reads. Release packaging keeps its exact 0.56.2 pins (`packaging/release/*`), and `CUA_HYPRLAND_EXPECTED_VERSION` acceptance builds still refuse a different header version. Updating the Omarchy package is out of scope.

## Blast Radius

Only Hyprland plugin builds with `CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT` or `CUA_HYPRLAND_TEST_INPUT` are affected. On 0.56.2 the helpers compile to the old expressions. On 0.57, Hyprland's own `surfaceLogicalBox()` returns nothing for windows that don't accept input (an inactive group tab, or a window behind a fullscreen one), so input to those windows is refused instead of delivered. That fails safe.

## Verification

All runs used the nightly's production options (`CUA_HYPRLAND_INPUT=ON`, Release, g++, `-Werror`, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`) in an Arch Linux ARM aarch64 root with real Hyprland headers:
- Main with Hyprland 0.57.1 (`hyprland 0.57.1-1`): configure fails with `Input is pinned to Hyprland 0.56.2`, which reproduces the nightly failure.
- This branch with 0.57.1: configure selects "window-backend input API", `cua-hyprland-plugin.so` builds, CTest passes 20/20, and every undefined symbol in the module resolves against the `Hyprland` binary or its libraries. Reconfiguring a 0.56.2 build directory against 0.57.1 headers re-probes and picks the backend tier.
- This branch with 0.56.2 (`hyprland 0.56.2-4` headers): configure selects "legacy window input API", the build passes, CTest passes 20/20, and the module's `.text` is byte-identical to main's 0.56.2 build.

The CI unit job's steps also pass: the clang mock suite (20/20), requalify unit tests, release contract tests (133), and the `tests/` Python suite. If the backend and legacy tiers are swapped in the detector, `cua_hyprland_cmake_api_test` fails with `Expected window_backend (1), found 0`.

Size: production lines are within limits.

Review notes: one reviewer finding is dismissed. It flagged `Co-Authored-By` trailers on the three contributor commits, but those commits are the outside contributor's and are kept unchanged. Two minor findings are left for follow-ups: no CI job builds the legacy input tier, and the probe checks member names but not the exact `std::vector<PHLLSREF>` type.

title: fix(cua-volume): a store being created by a clone is no longer taken for removed
body:
CUA-3276

On Windows, `vfs::tests::a_concurrent_remote_write_becomes_a_visible_conflict_copy` failed once on main (07460674e, 3 Nov) with `NotFound("the store ...\shared was removed")` on the test's first write. It passed in every other Windows run of CI: cua SDK on main since 28 Oct (54 runs). So it is an intermittent race, not a Windows delete or rename problem.

Cause: `FsBackend::ensure_root` checked `root.is_dir()` before it read the shared `seen` flag. In that test two `FsBackend` clones share one store that doesn't exist yet: the feed heartbeat from `spawn()` and the session's first `put`. If caller A sees no directory, then caller B creates it and sets `seen`, A reads `seen == true` and reports the store as removed. The fix reads `seen` before the directory check. `seen` is only set once the directory exists, so a missing directory with `seen` already set still means the store was removed (`a_removed_store_is_not_brought_back_by_a_later_write` still passes).

The new test `fs::tests::concurrent_first_writes_all_create_the_store` races 16 clones on a fresh store. It failed 3 of 3 runs on the old order (on macOS) and passes with the fix.

The six `volume_e2e` failures in the issue are no longer on main. That binary now has one test, and it passed on Windows in every run checked.

title: ci: warn on missing Cua Driver SPDX headers in bin/ci so driver PRs pass the quick stage
body: ## Description **What** `bin/ci`'s Cua Driver SPDX check now warns instead of failing, the severity `ci-spdx-headers.yml` already gives it. Pull requests that touch a driver `.rs` or `.swift` file pass the `quick` stage again. The warning still prints the missing-header count and the `--apply` command. **Why** `ci-spdx-headers.yml` runs `scripts/spdx-headers.py --check libs/cua-driver` with `continue-on-error: true` until the existing tree is stamped: 658 of the driver's 698 Rust and Swift files on `main` (`effe7a5ab`) have no header. `bin/ci` ran the same command as a hard failure. Since #6465 made `bin/ci --quick` the first job of 46 workflows, that failure fails `quick` on every PR that touches one of those files, and the heavy jobs that wait on `quick` never run. Of the open PRs updated since #6465 merged, 11 touch driver Rust or Swift files. The two whose `quick` job has run, #5591 ([job](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/41885334957/job/126768138532)) and #3897 ([job](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/41895610410/job/126804177591)), fail on this check and nothing else. **How** The check is now `advisory=True`, like the Windows cfg grep check. Its workflow reference includes the step's `continue-on-error: true` line, so a PR that makes the workflow enforcing fails `bin/ci --verify-sync` until it also edits this check, where the comment says to drop `advisory`. ## Architecture **Which declaration owns the check's severity, and what keeps `bin/ci` in step with it?** ## Related Issue Follows #6465. ## Reviewer Guide **Review depth:** Skim. One `Check(...)` call in `static_checks()` changes. **Open for pushback:** warning here instead of stamping the 658 files in this PR. The workflow plans that sweep as its own PR, and adding license headers across the driver tree is a maintainer decision. ## Risk & Impact - A new driver file without a header now fails neither `bin/ci` nor `quick`. It gets the warning `ci-spdx-headers.yml` already gives, and enforcement waits for the sweep in both places. - `bin/ci --fix` repairs only failures, so it no longer runs `spdx-headers.py --apply libs/cua-driver`. On a driver PR, that command stamped all 658 unstamped files into the contributor's diff. ## Verification **Behavior verified @ `b5898c5b1`:** `bin/ci --quick` on a branch that changes driver Rust files (8 changed files): | `bin/ci` from | Result | Exit | | --- | --- | ---: | | `main` (`effe7a5ab`) | `FAIL SPDX headers (Cua Driver, MIT)`, 658 files missing | 1 | | this branch | `warn SPDX headers (Cua Driver, MIT)`, same count and fix command | 0 | **Regression coverage:** `bin/ci --verify-sync` matches all 36 workflow references. Deleting `continue-on-error: true` from `ci-spdx-headers.yml` makes both `--verify-sync` and the `Sync` test in `scripts/ci/tests/test_bin_ci.py` fail. **Standard validators @ `b5898c5b1`:** `bin/ci --quick` and `bin/ci` pass (bin/ci tests and workflow sync, image refs); `scripts/ci/tests` runs 46 tests, all passing. **Not tested:** this PR's own `quick` job does not run `spdx-driver`, because the PR changes no driver file. The table above covers that path. ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above. - [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained. - [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change. - [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included. - [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. title: fix(cua-driver): load libxkbcommon's 1.0 text functions at run time so the driver starts on Ubuntu 20.04
body: ## Description **What** Before, `cua-driver` and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` imported libxkbcommon's two 1.0 functions, `xkb_utf32_to_keysym` and `xkb_keymap_key_get_mods_for_level`, so neither loaded on libxkbcommon 0.10 (Ubuntu 20.04). Now they import only libxkbcommon's `V_0.5.0` and `V_0.6.0` symbols and look the two functions up at run time, so only the Wayland keyboard routes built on `text_keys` need libxkbcommon 1.0. On 0.10 those routes refuse with: ```text foreground_unavailable: typing needs libxkbcommon 1.0 or later (libxkbcommon0 on Debian and Ubuntu); nothing was typed ``` In a Debian 11 build matching the release job, the binary now prints `cua-driver 0.47.4` on stock `ubuntu:20.04`. The newest published release, `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.13`, exits 1 there with ``version `V_1.0.0' not found``. On libxkbcommon 0.10: | Surface | `main` | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | Driver start, SDK library load | fails: ``version `V_1.0.0' not found`` | starts | | Pointer input, screenshots, X11 typing | unreachable | work | | libei key presses (GNOME, KDE) | unreachable | work | | libei text (GNOME, KDE) | unreachable | refuses | | `wtype` and Hyprland text | unreachable | refuses | | niri text and key presses | unreachable | **refuses before the keyboard session queries niri's focus or layout or binds a keyboard** | | cua-compositor text, targeted AT-SPI and nested-compositor delivery | unreachable | work (they do not use `text_keys`) | On libxkbcommon 1.0 or later, every route types as it does on `main`, through the looked-up functions. **Why** #6209 made niri's keyboard call the two functions directly. #6827 then moved typing into `wayland/text_keys.rs`, which the libei keyboard (GNOME, KDE) and the niri keyboard share, so `main` still imports them from there. The dynamic loader resolves those imports before any code runs, so on Ubuntu 20.04 the driver fails to start and the SDK library fails to load for every Linux user, X11 and headless included. The 2026-11-04 nightly fails this way (#6457), and so does the newest release, `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.13`. **How** `text_keys.rs` declares one table, `Xkb1`, with the typed loader macro that `wayland/dynamic_library.rs` now shares with `libpipewire.rs`. `xkb1()` resolves it once per process from the `libxkbcommon.so.0` the process already loaded, and it is the one place that refuses. `text_sym`, `level_mods` and `find_key` take `&Xkb1`, so no typing path reaches the two functions without the table. ## Architecture **Where do the two 1.0 functions come from now, who calls them, and where does typing refuse?** ## Related Issue Fixes #6457. On the issue, f-trycua said the team is weighing building against an older libxkbcommon or documenting Ubuntu 22.04 as the minimum. An older libxkbcommon does not work (see **Open for pushback**), so this PR keeps 20.04 the other way; if you would rather move to 22.04, we will close it. #6340, also open, states the release floor as Ubuntu 22.04+ in `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml` and the docs. Whichever of the two merges second updates that floor text to match the other. ## Reviewer Guide **Review depth:** Standard. The behavior lives in `text_keys.rs`; the other files pass the table through, move an existing macro, or follow from a dependency change. **Read order:** 1. `platform-linux/src/wayland/text_keys.rs`: the `Xkb1` table, `xkb1()` and `load_xkb1`; `text_sym`, `level_mods` and `find_key` taking `&Xkb1`; `typable_text` asking `xkb1()` first. 2. `platform-linux/src/wayland/libei.rs` and `niri/keyboard.rs`: `text_route` and `run_session` get the table from `xkb1()` before any other work, then pass it down. niri's own table is gone. 3. `platform-linux/src/wayland/dynamic_library.rs` and `libpipewire.rs`: the macro moves out of `libpipewire.rs` and takes the table name and FFI module as arguments. `open` is now `unsafe`, so each caller states its library's load-time safety. 4. `platform-linux/Cargo.toml` and three `libs/cua-spacesd` lockfiles: `libloading` is no longer optional behind `portal-capture`, so those lockfiles gain its entry. 5. Tests in `text_keys.rs`: `the_crate_does_not_require_libxkbcommon_1_0` reads the test binary's version needs; `a_missing_library_names_the_requirement` pins the refusal. **Open for pushback:** looking the functions up instead of replacing them with 0.x calls. A replacement for `xkb_utf32_to_keysym` would need libxkbcommon's legacy-keysym table, because `find_key` matches keysyms exactly and layouts put `€` on `EuroSign`, not on its Unicode keysym. `xkb_keymap_key_get_mods_for_level` has no 0.x equivalent. Building against an older libxkbcommon does not work either: 0.10 exports neither function, so the typing code does not link against it. ## Risk & Impact - **Wayland typing on libxkbcommon older than 1.0:** the routes in the table above refuse where today the process fails to start. - **Cached failure:** `xkb1()` caches a failed lookup for the life of the process, so a driver started before libxkbcommon is upgraded keeps refusing until it restarts. - **Dependency:** `libloading` becomes a non-optional dependency of `platform-linux`. ## Verification **Behavior verified @ `3e1db6f0e`.** A maintainer has since merged `main` into the branch (head `dea20ab9d`). I gathered the evidence below at `3e1db6f0e` and have not re-run it on the merged head. - Release build in Debian 11, matching the CD job: `cargo build --locked -p cua-driver -p cursor-theme-cli -p cua-driver-sdk --release --features cua-driver/portal-input --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, exit 0. - `readelf -V`: `cua-driver` and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` each need `libxkbcommon.so.0 Cnt: 2` (`V_0.5.0`, `V_0.6.0`), with no `V_1.0.0`; the highest glibc requirement is `GLIBC_2.30`. The published v0.47.4 binaries need `Cnt: 3`, including `V_1.0.0`. - Stock `ubuntu:20.04` with `libxkbcommon0` 0.10.0-1: this build's `cua-driver --version` prints `cua-driver 0.47.4` and exits 0, `cua-driver doctor --json` exits 0 with `"ok": true` (no display or accessibility bus, as expected in a container), and `libcua_driver_sdk.so` loads through Python `ctypes` with `RTLD_LOCAL`. The published `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.4` (`linux-x86_64` asset, sha256 `472de19fe6e347b6db009b010d4447ff8ed6d9af8459844c157acfa6770779e8`, matching GitHub's digest) exits 1 in the same container with ``version `V_1.0.0' not found``. In a separate run on 2026-11-12, the newest published release, `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.13` (`linux-x86_64` asset, sha256 `508e0cc33853b3066b99ea5c338a047a9bf88cbdd3696b1c60cf32e4b2adacc0`, matching GitHub's digest), exits 1 on stock `ubuntu:20.04` with the same error, and its `libcua_driver_sdk.so` fails to load through `ctypes` the same way. - The `platform-linux` test binary on the same 0.10 image: the `text_keys` tests pass, and the typing tests refuse with the message under **What**. **Regression coverage:** `the_crate_does_not_require_libxkbcommon_1_0` fails on `main` (`09b38ab66`, exit 101, listing `V_1.0.0`) and passes here. `a_missing_library_names_the_requirement` pins the exact refusal. `platform-linux` lib tests: 1011 passed with default features and 1076 with the portal features, 0 failed. **Standard validators:** `bin/ci --only spdx,spdx-driver,lockfiles,image-refs,rust-fmt` passes across all three Rust roots (7 passed). `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with default features and with `--features portal-input,portal-capture`. CI has since run on the merged head `dea20ab9d`: `validate` and `contributor-attribution` passed, and `ci-gate` failed through one check, `Rust Linux unit and compile`, where `connect::tests::one_failure_does_not_fail_the_others_or_the_exit_code` failed with `Text file busy (os error 26)` (395 passed, 1 failed). `connect.rs` is not in this diff, the same check passed on `3e1db6f0e`, and the same test failed with the same error on #6340's last run. The evidence above is local. **Not tested:** a live niri, GNOME or KDE session (none was available), arm64, and workspace-wide clippy. The `cua-spacesd` e2e crates were not compiled; their lockfiles resolve with `cargo metadata --locked`. Pointer input, screenshots, X11 typing, libei key presses and the cua-compositor, AT-SPI and nested-compositor routes on 0.10 were not run live; their rows in the table follow from those paths never calling `xkb1()`. ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above. - [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained. - [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change. - [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included. - [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. This PR releases as `fix(cua-driver)`. - [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). The focused `bin/ci` checks above pass locally; `--signoff` sets the `local-ci` status on trycua/cua, which this fork account cannot write.

title: [Bug]: A GTK3 app started with NO_AT_BRIDGE=1 gets an error that doesn't name the cause
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Electron sets `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1` for itself, so anything started from an Electron terminal or agent host inherits it. A GTK3 app started that way never joins the accessibility bus, and the driver's answer points somewhere else.

### Reproduction


1. Start a GTK3 app with `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1`, by any route other than `launch_app`, which already sets it to 0.
2. Call `get_window_state` with its pid.

### Expected behavior

The answer names `NO_AT_BRIDGE` and how to fix it.

### Actual behavior


- On X11: `x11_property_fallback_partial: AT-SPI was unavailable...`
- On Wayland: `No windows found for pid N. Provide window_id.`

### Environment

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (the same packages as Kubuntu 26.04 LTS), Debian 13, Fedora 45. KWin 6.6.6, 6.3.6 and 6.8.2. Run in containers.

### Evidence

With `NO_AT_BRIDGE=0`, the same app returns its full tree and `type_text` reaches the field.

### Workaround and additional context

Start the app with `launch_app`, or from a shell with `env -u NO_AT_BRIDGE`.

Fix proposed in PR #6444. Prepared with an AI coding agent, and I ran the checks on my own machine.

title: [Bug]: Desktop type_text through libei silently loses characters on KWin
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Desktop `type_text` through libei drops characters that need AltGr, can lose `€` and line breaks, and reports no failure.

### Reproduction


1. Use KWin 6.6.6 with the `us altgr-intl` layout.
2. Focus a text field in a Qt or Chrome window.
3. Call desktop `type_text` with `ñ`, then `€`, then `a\nb`.

- `€` is lost in every client except native Qt.
- `a\nb` is lost in every client except Chrome on Xwayland.

Real KWin with the real RemoteDesktop portal and libei, in containers on a virtual output, main at `6fc3c04b6`.

title: [Feature]: Capture the KWin desktop through ScreenShot2 when the driver holds the grant
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

A KDE desktop screenshot goes through the Screenshot portal, which needs a consent dialog on first use and is slower, even when the driver could ask KWin directly.

### Desired outcome

With the `org.kde.KWin.ScreenShot2` grant, desktop capture uses it with no dialog. Without the grant, the existing cascade runs as it does today.

This changes who decides: ScreenShot2 runs before the portal, so with the grant, the portal's dialog and a saved **Deny** no longer apply to desktop screenshots.

### Current workaround

Approve the portal dialog.

### Affected components and platforms

Cua Driver, Linux, KDE Wayland.

### Alternatives and prior art

Window capture through ScreenShot2 in PR #6450, which provides the grant.

### Implementation ideas

Measured on KWin 6.6.6, one 1600x900 output, 30 samples, two runs each:

| Route | First call | Median |
|---|---|---|
| Portal | 620 ms, plus a dialog | 126 ms |
| ScreenShot2 | 64-70 ms, no dialog | 43 ms |

Proposed in PR #6451. Prepared with an AI coding agent, and I ran the checks on my own machine.

title: fix(cua-driver): click web content that does not advertise AXPress
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, an element-token `click` on web content in Dia (The Browser Company) never reached the page. The driver reported `✅ Performed AXPress` with `effect: suspected_noop`. Its recommended next rung, a background pixel click, pressed the same element again through the AX hit-test and reported success. The page received nothing either time.
  - Root cause: Chromium advertises and performs `AXPress` on web content only in screen-reader mode. Blink serialises an element's default action verb only with `AXMode::kExtendedProperties`, and `BrowserAccessibilityCocoa` adds `AXPress` only when that verb is present.
  - Chrome rejects `AXManualAccessibility` (`kAXErrorAttributeUnsupported`), so the driver falls back to `AXEnhancedUserInterface`. Chrome's `BrowserCrApplication` turns that into `kAXModeComplete` after a 2 s debounce, so Chrome's web elements gain `AXPress`.
  - Dia handles `AXManualAccessibility` itself and swallows `AXEnhancedUserInterface` (it reads back `0` after a set), so its web content never leaves the basic mode. Its buttons, checkboxes and links advertise only `AXShowMenu` and `AXScrollToVisible`, and `AXPress` returns success without effect.
- What changed:
  - **Element-token press.** When the target is web content (an `AXWebArea` ancestor, via the existing `target_in_web_area`) and does not advertise `AXPress`, the driver delivers a routed pixel click at the element's center instead of the hollow press. This is the same `click_at_xy_with_window_local` delivery and `WindowPointer` gate that the selection fallback already uses. The result reports `path: cgevent`, `effect: unverifiable`.
  - **Background pixel hit-test.** The hit-test no longer presses such an element. It falls through to the routed pixel path, as it already did for LibreOffice's VCL.
  - Both paths share one predicate, `press_is_hollow`. Elements that advertise `AXPress`, including Chrome's after its mode switch, and native elements without it keep today's AX path.

## Related work

Refs #5723 (Dia attach for the browser tools). This fix is independent of it: it applies to the AX click path for any Chromium embedder that never enters screen-reader mode.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. No contract change: the `click` tool's inputs and result shape are unchanged, and only which delivery path a hollow press takes changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - macOS only. A token click on web content that lacks `AXPress` now delivers a real click (`path: cgevent`, `effect: unverifiable`) instead of `path: ax`, `effect: suspected_noop`.
  - Background delivery uses the routed event behind the `WindowPointer` gate. It neither raises the window nor moves the hardware pointer. If the gate refuses (for example, a minimized window), the old AX path runs unchanged.
  - Windows and Linux are untouched: their adapters don't use `AXPress`.
- Risk and rollback:
  - The risk is a web element without `AXPress` whose AX press did act. In Chromium that press is a no-op without the default action verb, which is what this targets.
  - Native (non-web) elements are excluded, so AppKit controls that honor an unadvertised press keep it.
  - Rollback is reverting this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks, on `3a4ec34` plus this change:
  - New owner test `hollow_press_tests::only_an_unadvertised_press_on_a_hollow_surface_is_replaced`. It is mutation-checked: dropping the surface condition from `press_is_hollow` makes it fail.
  - `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 652 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored.
  - `cargo fmt -p platform-macos -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: no findings in the changed file. Local clippy 1.98 reports two findings in untouched files (`capture.rs`, `permissions/gate.rs`); the pinned 1.97.1 toolchain wasn't available locally.
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Setup: macOS 26.4 (Darwin 25.4.0), Dia 1.55.1 and Chrome 156.0.8078.80.
  - Fixture: a local page with a button, a checkbox and a link, logging `event.isTrusted` for each event.
  - Before, in Dia: a token click on the button returned `Performed AXPress … suspected_noop`, and the page was unchanged. A background pixel click returned `PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX`, and the page was unchanged. A raw `AXUIElementPerformAction(kAXPressAction)` returned `kAXErrorSuccess` with no effect.
  - After, in Dia: token clicks on the button and the checkbox each reached the page as trusted events (`click true`, `check true`), and the checkbox became checked. A background pixel click on the button also reached the page. The window wasn't raised and the pointer didn't move.
  - Chrome: the elements advertise `AXPress` after the fallback's mode switch. A token click still takes `Performed AXPress` and reaches the page, so its path is unchanged.
  - The manual run used the same change applied to a local 0.38.0 build of the #5723 branch. This PR is that change on `main`, with the predicate extracted for the test.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - There is no canonical `cua-driver-e2e` row. It would need a Chromium embedder on the runner that never enters screen-reader mode, and Dia isn't available there.
  - `bin/ci` on this head (affected mode, base `3a4ec34`) passed rustfmt, Windows cfg, SPDX headers (FSL) and image refs.
    - It **failed `spdx-driver`**, but that is pre-existing: `scripts/spdx-headers.py --check libs/cua-driver` reports 658 files missing the MIT header on `main` itself, and this PR adds none. CI runs the same check as "Check SPDX headers (warn-only)", which passed on #6332's merge commit with the same files. So `bin/ci`'s hard failure disagrees with CI, and it blocks `--signoff` for any cua-driver change. Is `bin/ci` meant to treat it as a warning too?
    - It **skipped** clippy, unit tests, the generated reference and the UniFFI bindings for low disk (under 40 GB free). The crate's clippy and unit tests were run separately (see above), and CI will run all four.
    - So there's no `local-ci` sign-off yet: `--signoff` refuses a run with a failure or a skipped check.

## Contributor and release checks

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse disabled macOS controls on every token writer
body:
CUA-3290

## Problem

https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5635 publishes disabled macOS controls with `enabled: false`, but only `click` re-read `AXEnabled` before acting. `set_value`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `click(button: "middle")` and `type_text` with an `element_token` still acted on a disabled control. The one refusal that did exist was untyped text, and it told the caller to retry in the foreground or call `bring_to_front`, even when the app was already frontmost and fronting could not help.

## Change

- `input::ax_actions::ensure_ax_action_enabled` now returns a typed `ElementDisabled` error.
- `tools::refuse_if_disabled` re-reads `AXEnabled` on the token target after the exact-target gate and before any cursor, focus or input work. `set_value`, `right_click`, `double_click`, middle-click and `type_text` call it. `click`'s existing check in `perform_ax_click` maps to the same result.
- The refusal is structured: `code: element_disabled`, `effect: refused`, `pid`, `window_id`, `action`. It adds `escalation: {recommended: "foreground"}` only for a background call into an app that is not frontmost, since some controls (menu and toolbar items) are disabled only while their app is in the background. `run_steps`' `foreground_fallback` reads that field. When the app is already frontmost, there is no escalation.
- A foreground call into an app that is not frontmost skips the early read, because activation can enable the control. Click keeps its post-activation check.

Size: the shared refusal helper and its two unit tests in `tools/mod.rs` account for most of the added lines. Splitting them across five tools would add more.

## Proof

- The AppKit E2E cell `harness_appkit_disabled_control_is_published_and_its_press_refused` now calls `click`, `set_value`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `click(button: "middle")` and `type_text` on the fixture's disabled checkbox. Each one comes back `element_disabled` with the foreground escalation, and the checkbox reads back unchanged. It passed in the macOS Lume full matrix at this head.
- Unit tests pin the typed error, the message no longer advising a futile foreground retry, and both refusal shapes (with and without escalation).
- The full macOS matrix reported 178 delivered, 5 refused, 0 failed cells at this head. The `bring-to-front` lane's `exact_secondary_window_is_verified_and_prior_app_can_recover_focus` failed with "no running application for pid N". It fails the same way on main at a79ecf8d (one of two full runs). At this head it passed 4 of 4 times run alone in the same guest, and also after the disabled-control, SwiftUI and TextEdit lanes. It is not caused by this change.

title: feat(relay): default Space settings and detach-not-delete for removed computers (CUA-3413)
body:
What changes for users: your default computer for Spaces can be saved on your account, so the app, CLI, phone and agents all open the same one. When a computer is removed from your account, the Spaces it hosted are kept (hidden) and come back if you add that computer again, instead of vanishing.

Server side only (the relay). Nothing changes for current clients until they call the new routes.

## What it adds

- `GET` / `PUT /v1/spaces/settings`: `{default_space, fallback, fallback_on, updated_at}` per account. PUT replaces the whole object. 400 for a bad id, a duplicate in `fallback`, or more than 16 entries; 403 for a computer the caller cannot see (own, shared, or through a team/org) and for a computer token. Stored in `<state>.spaces.json` (atomic write, private mode) and erased with the account.
- `GET /v1/spaces/default?here=<machine-id>`: the resolution every client uses. Order: default, then the fallback list (or, when empty, every online computer the account can use, oldest first), then `here`. Reason is `default`, `fallback`, `here` or `unset`.
- `DELETE /v1/machines/{id}` now detaches the Spaces that name it as `host`: they are not listed and connections (client, plus the Space's own tunnel and token) are refused with 403 "its computer was removed from the account". Registering the computer again with the same id restores them. `?spaces=delete` (owner, not a computer token) removes them and drops their connections. The hosted shared list and TCP share reconcile skip detached Spaces.

## Tests

New `tests/spaces_settings.rs`: settings round trip and defaults; validation (bad id, duplicate, over 16, not visible, nonexistent, machine token, with exact errors); persistence across a restart and file mode; resolution (unset, nothing online, automatic oldest-first, explicit order, `here` skipped and last, fallback off, default online, a Space of the default computer, default no longer visible); detach hides and refuses, re-register restores; `spaces=delete` removes, rejects bad values and machine tokens. `tests/account_erase.rs` now covers erasing the settings (count, file scan, restart). Unit tests for id parsing and the store.

`cargo test -p cua-relay --features hosted` and `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` pass, except `tests/load.rs` (2 tests), which fails the same way on current main on the build host.

Refs CUA-3413

title: feat(spaces-macos): Cua Driver built into Cua Spaces (CUA-2771, CUA-2775)
body:
**For users:** Cua Spaces for Mac now carries Cua Driver. A new **Cua Driver** page in the sidebar shows whether it's working, lets you turn agents on or off for this Mac, and connects Claude Code and Codex with one Set up button. The driver uses the Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions you gave Cua Spaces, so there is no second app to allow in System Settings.

Linear: [CUA-2771](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-2771), [CUA-2775](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-2775) (under CUA-2706). Supersedes #6143, #6145 and #6147, rebased onto main; their commits are kept.

## What changes

**cua-spacesd runs the driver** (from #6145, now on by default on macOS)
- In a desktop session, cua-spacesd starts the bundled `Contents/Helpers/cua-driver serve --embedded` as its own child on `<CuaHome>/run/cua-driver.sock`, with Cua Spaces' bundle id as the host. macOS holds Cua Spaces responsible for it, so the permissions are Cua Spaces'.
- It restarts the driver when it exits (1 s backoff, doubling to 60 s).
- `CUA_SPACESD_EMBEDDED_DRIVER=0` turns it off.
- While `<CuaHome>/run/cua-driver.off` exists, the driver is stopped. That file is the page's "Let agents use apps on this Mac" switch.

**The Mac app answers the page** (`WebUIBridge+Driver.swift`, `EmbeddedDriver.swift`)
- It reads the driver over its socket: `metadata` for the version, `check_permissions`, `get_config` and `set_config`.
- Permissions come from Cua Spaces' own check, in a fresh process. A running process keeps the Screen Recording answer it had at launch, so when Cua Spaces has both grants but the driver still says no, the app restarts the driver once.
- Set up and Repair write `cua-driver mcp --embedded --socket … --host-bundle-id …` into the MCP configs of Claude Code and Codex, install the cua-driver skill, and run a live test: both permissions, a screen read and one agent-pointer move. Cua Spaces Local writes `cua-driver-local`, so it never overwrites the released app's entry.
- The Volume page's existing driver card (`agents.setupDriver`) now uses the same embedded entry, instead of installing the separate CuaDriver.app.

**The page** (from #6147, cut down to design A)
- The sidebar entry "Cua Driver" sits under Machines. It shows only where the host carries a driver: the Mac app, not Electron or Tauri.
- The page shows the state, the version and the last test, with **Set up** or **Repair** and **Test now**.
- A switch, "Let agents use apps on this Mac".
- The agent pointer's settings.
- **Connected agents:** Claude Code, Codex, and T3 Code, which brings its own driver.
- **Permissions:** each one shows On or Missing. Allow opens Cua Spaces' own guide to System Settings (`PermissionGuide`).
- There is no first-run step, no top-bar line and no feature flag. Those parts of #6147 are dropped.

## Not in this PR
- The released app bundles cua-spacesd from its pinned release (`libs/cua-spacesd/VERSION`). Users get the embedded driver only after a cua-spacesd release that includes this change, and a bump of that pin.
- The driver runs only once this Mac is set up in Cua Spaces, because the host service needs a spec. Until then the page says so.

## Verification
- `apps/cua-spaces-web`: typecheck and the full vitest suite pass, including new driver page tests and the coverage and contract tests.
- New Swift tests: `EmbeddedDriverTests` covers paths per channel, config parsing for Claude Code (JSON) and Codex (TOML), and the socket client against a fake driver. `BridgeContractTests` lists the new methods.
- The end-to-end check in a macOS VM passed (see the comment below): only Cua Spaces in the permission lists, Set up connecting Claude Code and Codex, background typing in TextEdit through the MCP entry, revoke and restore, cua-spacesd and driver restarts, and the agents switch.
- The Electron shell answers the driver methods: `driver.status` is null there, so the page stays hidden on Windows and Linux.

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve named browsers when implicit sessions expire
body:
An unnamed MCP tool call can activate the transport's implicit session while a browser belongs to a named session on that transport. When the implicit session expires, cleanup currently kills that browser even if the named session is still active.

Track the browser's owning session separately from its transport access identity. Idle cleanup now follows the owning session; transport disconnect still ends all sessions owned by that transport and removes their browsers.

Validation:
- Added a regression that failed before the fix and passes afterward. It also verifies browser cleanup when the transport ends.
- Full `cua-driver-core` test suite passed in an arm64 Linux Docker environment: 1,177 unit tests plus integration tests.
- A narrow backport to the deployed 0.38.0 driver passed all 237 browser tests.
- Real Chromium in an arm64 Linux sandbox remained readable on the same named binding for eight checks, ending approximately 350 seconds after an unnamed `list_windows` call activated the implicit session. This exceeds the 300-second idle TTL and 30-second sweep interval. Explicitly ending the owning session removed the browser process.
- `bin/ci --quick`: formatting, Windows cfg scan, FSL headers, and image references passed. The SPDX check reports 658 existing missing headers across the driver; this patch does not alter those headers.

Draft pending native platform coverage required by this repository. Related lifecycle context: #5123.

title: feat(spaces): Spaces as a tree and a default Space, behind Labs, with the SDK bindings and CLI (CUA-3413)
body:
**One stacked PR: the SDK bindings, CLI and MCP part (piece B) and the apps (piece C) of CUA-3413.** The SDK commits from `feat/spaces-default-sdk`, which never had their own PR, are folded in here. The relay API it calls (#6504) has merged, and this branch is rebased on main.

For users: with the new Labs switch "Spaces as a tree" on, your computers and the Spaces made on them show as one list, and new tasks from Home run on your default Space instead of a new Linux computer. With the switch off, nothing changes.

## What changes

**Labs switch (`spaces_tree`)**
- Off by default. Settings, Advanced, Labs, next to "Try the new setup". Turning it on also turns on the new Home.

**Sidebar and Spaces page**
- Each computer gets a top row, This Mac first, and the Spaces made on it sit underneath. Each computer can be folded.
- Machines leaves the nav. Its page still opens.
- The Spaces page is a table with Name, Status, Who's on it and Agent tasks.
- When a computer is offline, its Spaces are greyed out with "Waits for <computer>", and their running tasks read "Paused".
- New empty and single-computer states.
- Rename by double-clicking a name, or from the row's menu.
- Removing a computer opens a dialog that names each Space on it and the tasks that will stop. The "Also delete" box starts unticked. Ticked, the page deletes each Space through the computer first, then removes the computer with `deleteSpaces`.

**Home's "in" picker**
- Your default comes first, marked "Default", then the tree, then "New Space on <computer>" (the only rows that make a computer), with "Make this my default" on each row.
- When the default is offline, a line under the box says why and lists the order the task tries.
- A task never makes a computer silently: with nothing else online, it runs on This Mac.

**Settings, General**
- New rows: "Default Space", "If it's offline" and "Order to try" (drag, or use the arrow keys).

## SDK, CLI and MCP (included here)
- `cua-host` relay client: `spaces_settings`, `set_spaces_settings`, `resolve_default_space`, and removing a computer with `spaces=delete` (detach by default).
- `cua-sdk` (UniFFI): `Devices.spacesSettings`, `setSpacesSettings`, `resolveDefaultSpace`; `Spaces.relayUnregisterComputer(id, deleteSpaces)`. Bindings regenerated, including the committed Electron bindings.
- `list_spaces` (MCP and `cua spaces ls --json`): each row gains `parent` (its computer's Space id, null for a computer) and `default`. The default is cached briefly and never holds up the list when you're signed out or the relay is down. The tool's description in `cua-spaces-contract` says so.
- Tests: `libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/tests/default_space.rs` (rows get `parent` and `default`; signed out or relay down leaves `default` false), and the `cua-host` relay client against its in-process mock relay (`testing.rs`): settings read/replace/resolve, `spaces=delete` on remove.
- CLI: `cua spaces default` shows or sets the account's default Space and the order to try. `cua spaces rm <computer>` takes one of your computers off the relay and keeps its Spaces detached (`--delete-spaces` deletes them, `--yes` skips the prompt). `cua machines` is a hidden alias that says it is now `cua spaces`, and it is left out of the CLI reference groups.
- Computer removal stays out of the Space delete cycle (`cua-spaces` relay).
- Generated: the UniFFI bindings (Python, Swift, Kotlin, TypeScript, the Electron copy) and the Rust, SDK and Spaces reference pages.

## Bridge methods (all hosts; Tauri unsupported)
- `spaces.settings {}` -> `{ defaultSpace: string|null, fallback: string[], fallbackOn: boolean, updatedAt: number } | null`
- `spaces.setSettings { defaultSpace, fallback, fallbackOn }` -> the same shape. A bad id is refused with `bad_args` before the relay is asked.
- `spaces.resolveDefault {}` -> `{ space: string|null, reason, defaultSpace, defaultOnline, order: {space,name,online,role}[] } | null`
- `machines.remove` takes `deleteSpaces?: boolean`. Without it, the relay detaches the Spaces.

SwiftUI (`WebUIBridge`, `DevicesRunning`, `AppModel.removeMachine`) calls the SDK's `Devices.spacesSettings`, `setSpacesSettings`, `resolveDefaultSpace` and `Spaces.relayUnregisterComputer`. Electron (`src/bridge/spaces-settings.ts`, `machines.ts`, `backend.ts`) calls the same methods. The demo host answers all of them in memory.

## Tests
- Web unit tests (`lib/spaces-tree.test.ts`) cover:
  - grouping, This Mac first, and orphan Spaces
  - an offline computer greying its Spaces, with paused tasks
  - counts, and the empty and single states
  - the default when none is set
  - fallback: the default online, the default offline going to the next online computer, nothing online going to This Mac, and fallback off
  - the relay's own answer winning
  - a pick that went away never becoming a new computer
- Web app tests (`__tests__/spaces-tree.test.tsx`, real routes and wasm core) cover:
  - the switch off leaves today's UI unchanged
  - the switch on: Machines leaves the nav, the tree shows in both places, and folding works
  - an offline parent's Spaces
  - rename with Enter and Esc
  - the remove dialog, with and without "Also delete"
  - Home's default, the fallback line, and the This Mac last resort
  - the picker's rows and "Make this my default"
  - the Labs switch and the Settings rows
- Bridge contract: coverage, shapes (`bridge-shapes.json`), webkit and demo args.
- Electron (`test/machines-view.test.ts`): `deleteSpaces` on remove; settings read, replace and resolve; bad args; signed out.
- Swift: `BridgeContractTests` (the 3 new methods added to the shape cases) and `MachinesViewTests` (remove with Spaces; default Space read, replace, resolve and bad args).

- Fixed on this branch: the tree tests' waits returned `null` instead of throwing, so they never waited. Home's picker also dropped the "Default" label when the relay named the default before the setting was read. The tree now uses the relay's answer until the setting is read.

## Fixed after clicking through a real build (macOS VM, staging relay)
- **Rename by double-click opened the Space.** The first click of a double-click navigated before the dblclick arrived. A click now waits out the double-click time (300 ms) before opening; a double-click cancels it and starts the rename; a keyboard press opens at once. The test now sends the real click, click, dblclick sequence.
- **A computer that went offline stayed green** ("Online, Default") for minutes while Home already said it was offline, and Remove stayed greyed out. The always-shown tree never re-read the computers, and the machines list counts a relay connection that hasn't been dropped yet. The tree now re-reads them every 30 s and takes the relay's own answer from the default resolution (the same data as Home's fallback line). Remove is enabled once the relay calls the computer offline; the relay still refuses a connected one.
- **With no default set, an offline computer was marked Default** while tasks ran on This Mac with no line saying why. Unset, the default is now where a task actually goes (the relay's rule): the first online computer that isn't this Mac, else This Mac.
- **A removed computer couldn't be added again.** After Remove on another device, `cua host setup` there (even with a pairing code) said "Already set up … Nothing to change". Host status now reports `revoked` when the relay refuses the computer's token, and setup registers it again (same computer id; its detached Spaces come back).
- **"Also delete" said more than it does** (stopgap, labelled in code). A computer can only be removed while offline, so its Spaces can't be deleted on it: ticked, they leave the account and their files stay on the computer. The dialog now says exactly that, and the button reads "Remove and delete". The real fix (the computer deletes them when it is next online) is a relay and host change, tracked on CUA-3413.
- The Name column got a few letters at 1024 px; Name and Status now share the width 3:2, and the rename field fills the row.

Tests added: the click sequence and single-click open (`__tests__/spaces-tree.test.tsx`), a relay-offline computer being offline and removable, the unset default skipping offline computers (`lib/spaces-tree.test.ts`), the honest "Also delete" copy, and `onboard::a_computer_removed_from_the_account_is_set_up_again` (cua-cli).

VM results with screenshots are in the CUA-3413 test report (linked on the Linear issue). Windows and Linux app click-throughs run on main's signed build after this merges.

Refs CUA-3413

title: fix(cua-mesh): the NAT rebinding test accepts either of the client's new ports (CUA-3277)
body:
CUA-3277

`cua-mesh --test mesh` failed twice on the Windows Rust job on main on 3 Nov, and each time a different test failed:

- `a_revoked_device_fails_fast_with_the_reason`: "no denial seen". The client waited out its full reconnect backoff (up to about 11 s) before it saw the 403, which is past the test's 10 s deadline. #6355 already fixed this by adding `reconnect_speedup` to that test, and it has not failed since.
- `a_nat_rebinding_falls_back_and_finds_a_new_direct_path`: `left: 61575, right: 61574`, "the machine follows the client's new port". This PR fixes that one.

Cause: after `rebind()`, the client's IPv4 and IPv6 sockets can land on different ports. The IPv6 socket falls back to any free port when it cannot bind the IPv4 one; the off-by-one ports in the log (61575 vs 61574) point to that on the Windows runner. The test compared the machine's path against the first sorted endpoint only, which is the IPv4 port, so a direct path to the client's new IPv6 port counted as a failure. The check also ran once, so it could catch the machine's old direct path while that path was still inside its trust window.

Fix: the test now polls for up to 15 s until the machine's direct path is on any of the client's post-rebind endpoint ports. It still checks the same behaviour (the machine leaves the old port for a new one). Only the test changed; no production code.

Evidence that the mesh step is otherwise healthy: across the Windows mesh step on main from 2 to 5 Nov, it failed 3 times in 53 runs. Those three were the two failures above and an earlier `loopback_forwards_carry_tcp_and_udp` failure on 2 Nov. None has failed since the 3 Nov 06:55 UTC run.

title: fix(spaces-mobile): the phone says why the Spaces list is empty or incomplete
body:
## Phone app: say why the Spaces list is empty or incomplete

Against a real account, Home listed only old offline Spaces and showed "Some computers did not answer. Pull down to try again." with no way to tell why.

### What was wrong
- `DeviceManager.session()` swallowed the relay's pending or not-enrolled refusal and returned null. Every per Space call then failed with a 403 `NOT_ENROLLED`, and Home folded that into the generic banner.
- The banner never said which computer failed, or whether it needed an update, timed out or could not be reached.
- A computer that was online but not providing Spaces (`cua.host.spaces` off) listed nothing and said nothing.

### What changed (apps/cua-spaces-mobile)
1. **Pending approval.** `DeviceManager` now remembers the refusal (`approval()`), fetches a one-time code if it has none, and asks the relay again on the next call (at most every 3 seconds), so pulling down on Home retries. The live backend makes no per Space calls while the phone is waiting, and returns `waiting`. Home shows "This phone is waiting for approval", the code, and the exact command `cua devices approve <CODE>` to run on a computer that is already signed in. A 403 `NOT_ENROLLED` from a Space call is treated the same way and is never counted against a computer.
2. **Which computer, and why.** `listSpaces` returns `problems`: one entry per computer that failed, with a kind. Home shows one plain line each: "needs an update" (`PHONE_OLD_COMPUTER`), "took too long to answer", or "could not be reached". The generic line remains only when nothing says which.
3. **Not providing Spaces.** An online, sharing computer with `cua.host.spaces` off gets the note "Not providing Spaces to your phone. In Cua Spaces turn on Provide Spaces, or run cua host setup --share spaces on it." in the Computers section.

New helper: `src/data/live/reach.ts` (classification and wording).

### Tests
`__tests__/reach.test.tsx` (new, 10 tests): pending approval (device manager remembers, throttles, retries, clears; network failure is not "pending"; backend returns `waiting` once and no computer problems; no per Space calls while waiting; Home card with code and command), old computer, timeout, unreachable, not providing, the wording of each line, and Home showing named lines instead of the generic banner. `fakeDaemon` gained a per computer `threadFails` option.

Whole mobile suite: 188 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean.


This is a UI change, so it stays a draft until it has been tried on a phone.

title: fix(cua-driver): start the composited X11 overlay test's reads once its desktop is on screen
body:
Fixes CUA-3246.

## Why

Under picom 12.5, `x11_overlay_frames_are_never_composited_half_presented` fails because of one read where the whole 480x480 area is black (`red 0, blue 0, other 230400`). The overlay doesn't cause it. That read is always the observer's first one, and it comes before the test's own white desktop window has been composited. picom 12.5 paints a root with no wallpaper black, and a newly mapped window only shows up once picom has painted it. So the first read can land in that gap and see the bare root.

Probes under Xvfb with `picom --backend xrender` 12.5:
- With nothing mapped, a root read is entirely black.
- An opaque root-visual window, mapped and filled white, reads black for a few frames after the map and then white (20 of 20 maps).
- A fully transparent ARGB window mapped over a desktop that has already settled never reads black (0 of 20 maps).
- The real composited present path (`paint_x11_tiles`, map and unmap, 40 cycles over a settled white desktop, 3 runs) never read black.

The overlay window does not flash black when it maps. The test was reading before its fixture was on screen.

## What changed

Test-only. Before the observer starts, the test waits (up to 3 s) for the white desktop to read back all white. The overlay is still unmapped at that point, since it first maps in the first `paint_x11_tiles` call. The observer still covers the overlay's first map and every frame after it, so a real black flash on map would still count as `other` pixels and fail.

## Verification

Runs that mirror the CI step 1:1 (`xvfb-run` at 1920x1080x24, `picom --backend xrender`, the ignored test), with picom 12.5:
- main: 10 of 10 runs failed, each with exactly one all-black read #0.
- this branch: 30 of 30 runs passed.
- `x11_overlay_frames_are_never_seen_half_presented` (no compositor) passed.
- The scoped repository checks: fmt passed, and the platform-linux test suite passed. clippy `-D warnings` fails with the same errors on main, all in files this change doesn't touch.
- The verify-cua-driver X11 lane was skipped. Its Electron fixture aborts in preflight on this host because `/dev/shm` isn't writable, and that lane doesn't exercise this test. Windows and macOS weren't built, since the change is in the Linux-only crate.

title: feat(spaces): the warming home stays out of the top bar and off the phone until a person writes into it
body:
## Hide the warming home from the top bar and the phone

### Problem

The home that warms in the background for Home's prompt box (`home-claude-code`) is meant to be invisible
until a person writes into it. The Spaces list, sidebar and palette already hide it (`prepare::hidden_spaces`),
but it still showed in the Mac top bar (menu bar count and notch) and the tray, and the relay publish pass
listed it on the owner's phone.

### What changes

One rule, kept in the daemon and the core so every app and every list agrees:

- The app creates the warming home hidden: label `cua.hidden=home` together with the existing relay opt-out
  (`cua.relay=off`, the same as `--no-relay`). The web create request (`homeCreateRequest`) sends them through the generic
  `labels` field of `spaces.create`, so no new create plumbing is needed in either app.
- `SpaceInfo` has a plain `hidden` flag. Core listing APIs are not filtered. `cua spaces ls` shows the home with
  a note (`(hidden: warming for Home: home-claude-code)`), `ls --json` and the MCP tools (`list_spaces`, ...) return
  it with `"hidden": true`, so a person or an agent can still find, use, stop or delete it.
- The relay publish pass never lists a hidden Space.
- When a person writes into the Space's thread (`thread_post`, from the app, the CLI, MCP or the phone), the
  daemon makes it visible (`Spaces::reveal`): the label goes, `set_on_relay(true)` runs, and the next publish pass
  lists it. `set_on_relay(true)` now also clears a `cua.relay=off` label, which would otherwise keep a Space off
  for good.
- Top bar views filter with the core: `spaces::openable_spaces` (the one list behind the menu bar count, the notch
  tab and its tiles) skips hidden Spaces; the Windows and Linux tray list and the SwiftUI `realSpaces` do too.
- A home the prepare record did not prepare is never created hidden, so it is never hidden.
- Prewarm pool members are not Spaces until claimed: the pool keeps them out of the Spaces registry, so the publish
  pass cannot see them, and a claimed member is an ordinary Space that follows the normal relay rule. `prewarm_list`
  and `sandbox_pool_list` still show the pools unfiltered.

A message queued in Home before the agent is ready counts as "asked" for the Spaces list at once (unchanged); the
top bar and the phone list the home when that message reaches its thread.

### Tests

- `cua-spaces` `relay_publish`: a hidden home stays off the fake relay, `list()` and the JSON carry
  `hidden`, `reveal` lists it on the next pass, a same-name home that was not made hidden is listed from the start.
- `cua-spaces-ext` `hidden_home_thread`: `list_spaces` returns the hidden home marked; reading its thread keeps it
  hidden; a person's post makes it visible; a home the app did not prepare is never hidden.
- `cua-cli` `label_flags_parse_filter_and_show`: `ls --json` flag and the table note.
- `cua-spaces-app-core`: a warming home is in no top bar view (menu bar status line, notch tab and tiles) until the
  first message, and the core's listing keeps the row.
- App tests: Electron `host-bridge` (menu, tray, notch) and `create-extras`, SwiftUI `SpaceMenuTests` and `CreateExtrasTests`, web `home-request` (asserts the labels).

### Screenshots

The top bar menu with the warming home hidden and after the first message, from the SwiftUI app on fixture data.

title: fix(cua-driver): clear a dialog record Chromium no longer shows
body:
A tab whose dialog record went stale was locked for good. `browser_click` refuses while the driver's dialog record for a tab exists, and on main the only way to clear that record is a `Page.javascriptDialogClosed` event or a successful `browser_dialog` accept or dismiss. If the close event never arrives, Chromium answers `browser_dialog` with `No dialog is showing`. On main that answer came back as a plain refusal and the record stayed, so the tab refused every click until the connection closed.

CUA-3307. Follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5621.

**Change** (`cua-driver-core` browser module)
- `browser_dialog`: when `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog` on the dialog's own session fails with `-32602 No dialog is showing`, clear that dialog's record and refuse with `dialog.present: false`. After that, inspect reports no dialog and clicks go through. The clear is generation-checked, so a newer dialog is never dropped.
- CDP reader: on a browser-level `Target.detachedFromTarget`, drop that session's target mapping and any dialog record bound to it. A detached session sends no more events, its close included, and cannot resolve the dialog, so its record could never clear. Once the mapping is dropped, the next attach subscribes a fresh session to dialog events (before this change, `has_dialog_session` stayed true for the dead session).

**Root cause.** The record is a mirror of Chromium's state that only one event could clear. When Chromium says outright that no dialog is showing, or that the session holding the record is gone, the driver now follows Chromium instead of its stale copy. There is no timeout.

**Chromium behaviour this relies on.** I checked these against Chrome 156 with a scripted CDP probe:
- `Page.crash` and SIGKILL of the renderer both send `javascriptDialogClosed`, and `handleJavaScriptDialog` then answers `-32602 No dialog is showing`. So a crash is not a confirmed way to lose the close, and the first fix covers any lost close, whatever caused it.
- After a top-level `Target.detachFromTarget`, the old session answers `-32001 Session with given id not found`.
- Known limit: if a tab session is detached while its dialog is still open, the record is dropped but the page stays blocked. A new session's `Page.enable` hangs, and the next click waits for the frame-revalidation timeout instead of failing fast. The driver never detaches a top-level tab session itself, so this only happens when something outside the driver detaches it.

Updated by merging main (#6562 and #6643 touched the same dialog code). Both sides of the `v2_tests.rs` mock are kept.

**Tests** (each fails on main, passes here):
- `v2_tests::a_dialog_chromium_no_longer_shows_stops_locking_the_tab`: a dom_event click opens a confirm, then the mock drops the dialog without a close event. Dismiss now refuses with `dialog.present: false`, inspect reports no dialog, and a coordinate click dispatches.
- `cdp_ws::tests::a_detached_dialog_session_drops_its_dialog_record`.

title: feat(images): the slim Linux image carries the cua CLI and a spawn-capable cua-spacesd; drop agent-home
body:
An agent in its Home Space (the Space the web app creates on `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim` with child Spaces on) must be able to run `cua spaces create ...` when asked in plain language. Today the published slim image has no `cua` CLI, so that fails. This puts the CLI in the slim image and removes the separate `agent-home` image family, which was added by mistake: the home Space runs on the slim image.

## What changes

- **Slim tier carries the `cua` CLI** at `/usr/local/bin/cua` (on the `cua` user's PATH). `full` and `docker` are `FROM slim`, so they have it too. `CUA_CLI_SOURCE` works like `CUA_SPACESD_SOURCE`: `local` (default; CI hands over the CLI it built from the same commit as the image), `release` (needs a pinned `CUA_CLI_VERSION`, never `latest`, and the archive is checked against `CUA_CLI_SHA256` or the release's `checksums.txt`), `none`.
- **Spawn-capable cua-spacesd**: the slim image already builds cua-spacesd from the same commit; `spawn` is now a required claim of the image (it was optional), so `cua-spacesd doctor --strict` fails an image whose daemon cannot serve the spawn channel.
- **`agent-home` removed**: recipe, catalog entries, README section, conformance default (`--home-image` is now `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim`) and the conformance doc. `build-cua-linux.sh` moved to `libs/images/linux/build-cua-cli-linux.sh` (`CUA_CLI_BIN=` stages an already built binary).
- **Gates** (`libs/images/linux/release.json`):
  - tier claim `cua --version`, checked by every doctor lane (runc, gVisor, QEMU) on all tiers;
  - new `smoke-cua-cli.sh` under runc and gVisor: the container is healthy, cua-spacesd's health script answers, `cua --version` works as the desktop user, and `cua spaces ls` with a spawn channel in its environment connects to that channel (a listener stands in for it and must receive the HTTP/2 connection), and does not connect without one;
  - a size gate on the slim tier: unpacked image at most 1.55 GB per arch.
- The catalog entries of the slim image say what it carries. The local e2e setup builds the CLI before the image.

## Size

The CLI adds about 85 MB compressed (78 MB on arm64), about 200 MB unpacked, because the released CLI archive is that big. Slim goes from about 0.49 GB to about 0.58 GB compressed, and from 1.23 GB to 1.43 GB unpacked on amd64 (1.27 GB arm64 before). We accept it because child Spaces from the Home Space need the CLI; a thin in-Space CLI can cut it later.

## Not in this PR

Nothing is published by hand. The image workflow publishes `24.04-slim[-disk]` when a `linux-image-v*` tag is pushed, or on the weekly run when the content changed.

Verified locally: `bin/ci --base` for the affected checks (image refs, image tests, docs checks, actionlint, workflow sync), the image manifest tests, and `cua images release --dry-run` for the new steps. The image build and the new smoke test run only in this PR's CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): add SPDX headers to cua-driver sources so the quick stage passes
body:
CUA-3388

The quick stage runs `python3 scripts/spdx-headers.py --check libs/cua-driver` as a blocking check (added in #6465), and 658 driver sources had no SPDX header. That made `quick`, `ci-gate`, `Check Documentation Sync` and `E2E gate / result` fail on every cua-driver PR (#5591, #6503, #6512). This PR adds the missing headers. It changes no code.

- **657 MIT files**: header added by `spdx-headers.py --apply libs/cua-driver`. Every LICENSE file and every Cargo `license` field under `libs/cua-driver` is MIT.
- **`scripts/node-runtime-trampoline-cache.rs`**: this is vendored MPL-2.0 code (`runtimes/napi/src/callback/cache.rs` from uniffi-bindgen-react-native #440), so it gets `SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0` instead. It cannot be replaced with a dependency. Upstream ships it only inside the npm package as a module of the `uniffi-runtime-napi` crate, which is not on crates.io. The file is identical to the one in 0.31.0-5. Release 0.31.0-6 reworked it, and the 0.31.0-4 release that also changes the RustBuffer boundary is why the build backports only this file. `build-node-runtime.mjs` and `node-runtime-NOTICE.md` now say the only change to the upstream file is the added SPDX line.
- **The check needs no change.** Driver mode already accepts any `SPDX-License-Identifier` value; only `--fsl` compares the id. No skip list.
- **`compat-fixtures/apps/rust/src/main.rs`**: one `assert!` reflowed by rustfmt. It already failed `cargo fmt --check` on main, and touching the file brings that check into the quick stage.

title: Fix: an @mention by the host's agent name wakes the Space's agent (and say so when nobody is there)
body:
Fixes a Home message (and any thread @mention by the host's name) that did nothing and said nothing.

Root cause: the Home flow built the summon input from the host's unique member key (`claude-8`, what `cua agent ls` shows) instead of the Space's handle (`claude`), so it posted `@claude-8 hi`. The thread matches handles, so it matched no member: nothing woke, nothing said so. The Space page composer was right (it used the handle); Home, the prepared/warm home path and the Agents DM composer used the key.

- Core: one resolution rule for @mention, add and wake (`Persistent::member_named`): the Space's handle first, the host key as an alias, only inside that member's own Space. Adding a member by its key no longer creates a duplicate.
- App core `summon.*`: `SummonMember.key`; Ask first and Home name the handle; new `mine` flag so a Home's agent with no sign-in on this computer is reported ("Claude Code isn't connected yet", Connect) instead of posting to nobody; an @ of nobody in the Space is reported plainly under the message ("Nobody called @ghost is in this Space"), only visible to you, no Connect or Send again.
- Web: Home/prepare, the Agents DM send and the member card use the handle.

Tests: core (`thread_compat`: alias resolves, add by key is not a third member, another Space's key is nobody's), app core summon unit tests, web `agent-home-box` (Home posts `@claude`, not `@claude-8`; fails without the fix) and `ask-first-in-space` (@ of nobody is said).

title: Fix: a Space's mesh node no longer probes the local network its network refuses
body:
A Space's own mesh node (cua-mesh inside the Space's cua-spacesd) pinged peers' local-network endpoints every discovery round. The default Space network (internet only) correctly refuses those, and every refusal counted: the Space page showed "Blocked: this Space can't reach your local network" and `cua network log` filled with attempts nobody made (786, then 901 and climbing about once a second on a real Space).

Fix at the root, not by hiding the notice: the mesh node has a local-network switch (`MeshConfig::lan`, `CUA_MESH_LAN=0`). Off, it never learns, pings, answers on or advertises a local address (`send_udp` is the single choke point), so the network has nothing to refuse and the notice and log stay truthful for what the agent and person tried. A Space attached at run time defaults to off (`CUA_MESH_LAN=1` opens it); direct-over-internet and relay paths are unchanged, and hosts keep the default.

Tests: engine unit tests (no LAN candidate, send, ping or advertised endpoint; turning it off later drops learned LAN paths and a LAN best path), an integration test that a `lan = false` node still carries streams with no LAN path, existing mesh suites unchanged. Enforcement (nftables/gateway) is untouched, so the runtime conformance suite does not apply.

Not verified: I could not run a container here, so the live source (this node) is inferred from the Space's own mesh code path and the roughly once-per-discovery-round rate, not captured in a running Space. Spaces on older images keep probing until their image is rebuilt with this spacesd.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep a full budget for each dom_event click readback
body:
CUA-3247

Fixes the one-off CI failure of `browser::v2_tests::dom_event_click_remains_unverifiable_when_only_focus_changes` on Rust Linux unit (run 40748521749). The failure came from a real timing bug in the driver, not from the test.

**Cause.** After a `dom_event` click, `observe_dom_click` polls the semantic readback for up to 400 ms. It gave each in-flight read only whatever time was left in that window. When a read started near the end of the window and the page answered a little late, the read timed out and the result became "semantic target readback was unavailable", not "target state remained unchanged". That is the wrong outcome for a live page whose state did not change, and on a busy CI runner it flips the test's text assertion.

**Repro.** Holding each readback reply for 8 ms in the mock made the test fail 17/30 times; at 15 ms it failed 8/30. Without a delay it passed 200/200 alone, 150/150 with the CPU loaded and 100/100 pinned to one contended core. With the fix it passed 30/30 at each of 8, 15 and 40 ms.

**Change.**
- `tools.rs`: the 400 ms window now only decides whether to start another read. Each read keeps the full readback budget, so the observation still ends in bounded time.
- `mock_cdp.rs`: `MockReply` gets an optional reply `delay` for tests.
- `v2_tests.rs`: new `dom_event_click_keeps_readback_when_reads_are_slow`, where every read takes 150 ms. It fails without the fix and passes with it.

No quarantine entry is needed.
