title: fix(cua-driver): treat niri workspace read-backs the cleanup deadline cut off as unconfirmed
body:
CUA-3250. Follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6436.

#6436 made `confirm_focus` treat a read-back cut off by the shared confirm deadline as "not confirmed yet". The two workspace confirm loops in `crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/niri/focus.rs` (the final poll in `restore_focus`, and `restore_workspace`) still propagated that timeout. A workspace restore niri was slow to apply failed with `niri IPC Workspaces failed: niri IPC reply timed out` instead of naming the workspace.

Change:
- A `read_back` helper returns `None` for a read-back the deadline cut off and passes every other error through. All three confirm loops use it, so the inline match from #6436 is gone.
- `restore_workspace` now fails with `niri did not confirm focus on workspace N`, and `restore_focus` with `niri did not restore workspace N on output X`, matching how `confirm_focus` reports.

Tests (test commits land first):
- `a_workspace_read_back_the_deadline_cuts_off_still_refuses_as_unconfirmed` and `a_workspace_restore_check_the_deadline_cuts_off_names_the_workspace` fail on main with `niri IPC Workspaces failed: niri IPC reply timed out` and pass with the fix.
- `a_read_back_niri_hangs_up_on_is_still_an_ipc_error` pins that a closed connection is still an IPC error. It fails if the timeout guard is widened to every error.

title: fix(cua-compat): name the user on file calls to an agent that switches users
body:
On a guest whose agent switches users itself, the file calls left over from #6459 now name their user. That agent is the Linux image's `cua` holding `CAP_SETUID`/`CAP_SETGID`, and a cua-spacesd file call with an empty `run_as` runs as `cua`, not as the requested user.

CUA-3292

## What was still wrong on main

Each of these was checked against main at d38ff7e2f and was still wrong:

- **Daytona toolbox.** `create_folder`, `move_file` (the 409 stat and the move) and `delete_file` sent no `run_as` on the native path, so they ran as `cua` instead of the sandbox user.
- **`guestfs::first_missing`.** Its stat ran as `cua`, so a directory `cua` cannot enter hid what was missing below it.
- **E2B `fsops::native::*`.** The fallbacks a guest without `sh`/GNU find gets ran as `cua`, while envd acts with root's rights. `make_dir` and `rename` also never gave the directories they created to the request's user, which the script path does.
- **First `read_file` in `e2b/files.rs`.** It ran as `cua`, and only a `PERMISSION_DENIED` retried as root.
- **`ensure_default_user` (and Daytona's `prepare_user`).** The script sent `useradd`'s stderr to `/dev/null`, so the `compat: creating user` warning was empty.

## Change

- `guest::file_run_as(driver, user)` gives the `run_as` for a file call. It names the user only for an agent that switches users itself (driver `root`). Other drivers send nothing, as before, and keep their `sudo` paths.
- Daytona folder, move and delete name the sandbox user, the same user the `sudo` path already ran them as. A folder made that way is no longer chowned again afterwards.
- `first_missing`, the E2B native fallbacks and the first E2B read name root. The native `make_dir` and `rename` give what they created to the user. `rename` makes the destination's new parents before the move, so the moved file keeps its owner.
- `guest::create_user_script` is shared by E2B and Daytona and keeps stderr.

One behaviour change: on a capability agent, a Daytona folder, move or delete for a sandbox user that does not exist on the guest now fails with 400 (`no such user`) instead of running as `cua`. Commands have failed the same way since #6459. The test mock's guest now has the `daytona` user the gateway creates on a real guest, so the hermetic SDK suites still run as the default sandbox user.

The test mock (`cua-spacesd-client/src/testing.rs`) only records each file call's `run_as`. It does not model process users, which CUA-3293 covers.

## Proof

- `file_calls_name_the_sandbox_user_to_an_agent_that_switches_users` (Daytona) checks `run_as` on folder, move and delete. It failed on main with `left: [""]`, `right: ["alice"]`.
- `root_file_calls_name_root_to_an_agent_that_switches_users` (E2B) checks Stat, ListDir, MakeDir, Move, Remove and the `/files` read through the native fallbacks. It failed on main at the `run_as == "root"` assertion.
- `native_file_calls_give_what_they_make_to_the_user` checks the chown of what MakeDir and Move created, and that the move's parent is made first. It failed on main with `left: []`.
- `a_failed_useradd_says_why` runs the script with a failing `useradd` and checks its message reaches stderr. It failed with the old `2>&1` (stderr `""`).

Size: the production diff is over the net target because six native fallbacks needed the driver threaded through, and the two chowns needed new code.

title: feat(cua-driver): release idle MCP runtimes safely
body:
## Summary

```text
lightweight MCP endpoint
  metadata / tools/list -> stays lightweight
  tools/call -> start or reuse the native runtime worker
  4h without real calls -> stop the worker
  next tools/call -> start a fresh worker
```

- Add a macOS default idle timeout of four hours for the native MCP runtime; metadata and keepalives do not reset it, and in-flight calls are protected.
- Keep the host-facing MCP endpoint alive so the next real tool call can restart the worker.
- In `CUA_DRIVER_AX_ONLY=1` mode, refuse foreground setup fallbacks before activation or global input; keep app selection independent of app names.
- `Refs #2002`; this reduces idle runtime cost but does not claim to meet that issue's separate couple-seconds process-exit expectation.

## Evidence

- Candidate `0204b5dd` is based on upstream `83a40652`.
- `git apply --cached --check` passed for both fork patches on `83a40652`; the resulting index matches the candidate tree exactly.
- `bin/ci --quick`: 4 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped. The failure is the image-reference catalog check. Running `python3 scripts/images/check-image-refs.py` on the exact `origin/main` base also fails with the same 49 stale allowlist entries.
- The installed fork binary's isolated policy probe passed 14/14 checks without GUI actions. It is not the candidate build.
- No candidate Rust build/unit suite, native GUI run, or literal four-hour wait was performed on this shared host. The PR is draft; it has no local-CI sign-off because the quick gate is red on the base.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way; revert the commits to roll back the supervisor and background guards.

**Blast Radius:** medium — changes MCP worker lifetime and macOS AX-only delivery behavior; public tools are unchanged.

title: fix(cua-spacesd-client): mock runs commands and files as the user they name
body:
The mock cua-spacesd now runs each process and file call as a specific user, and tests can assert which one. Before this, `ci-cua-compat` could not see root commands running as the agent's own user.

CUA-3293. Follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6459.

## Why the mock missed #6459

`cua-spacesd-client`'s mock ran every command the same way, whatever `ProcessConfig.user` said. `id`, `whoami` and `sudo` exited 127, and `$HOME` was always `/home/cua`. A root command that reached the agent without a user looked the same as one that named root. The only way to catch it was to assert on the request field, which is what the #6459 test does. Nothing checked what the command itself saw.

## Change (mock and tests only)

- The mock agent runs as `cua` (uid 1000), like the Linux images, unless `run_as_mode` is `root`. A process that names no user runs as `cua`. A named `user` runs as that user. `sudo [-u U] [--] [env K=V...] PROG` is unwrapped and runs PROG as U, or as root when there is no `-u`. `sudo` is refused when the agent reports `run_as` mode `none`, and for a user the guest does not have.
- `whoami`, `id -un`, `id -u` and `printf %s "$HOME"` answer for that user (`/root` for root). `MockState::process_user(pid)` records it, and `MockState::agent_user()` returns the agent's own user.
- A file written or made without `run_as` now belongs to the agent's user (`cua`) instead of the placeholder `mock`. `MOCK_DEFAULT_OWNER` had no users outside the mock and is removed. `cp` onto an existing file keeps that file's owner.
- New cua-compat gateway test `a_root_command_runs_as_root_on_a_non_root_agent`. It runs `whoami`, `id -u` and `printf %s "$HOME"` as E2B root and checks the output.
- New client test `the_mock_runs_a_command_as_the_user_it_names`. `sudo_is_the_fallback_for_older_and_sudo_agents_only` now also checks the user the `sudo` fallback ran as.

No cua-compat source changes. The remaining call sites are handled separately.

## Proof

- With the pre-#6459 `guest.rs`, `guestfs.rs` and `daytona/toolbox.rs` put back, the new gateway test fails with `left: ["cua", "1000", "/home/cua"]`, `right: ["root", "0", "/root"]`. On this branch it passes.
- Removing the `sudo` user check from the mock makes `the_mock_runs_a_command_as_the_user_it_names` fail.
- I ran the crates that use the mock with its `testing` feature: cua-spacesd-client, cua-compat, cua-sandbox-core, cua-contrib, cua-sdk, cua-spaces, cua-cli, cua-spaces-ext, cua-daemon, cua-spaces-cli and cua-agents. All pass except `cua-spaces` `relay_publish::spaces_added_by_address_and_opted_out_ones_stay_off`. That test fails the same way on main because it reads the host's experiments setting (child-spaces is off here).

Size: about 135 net lines in `testing.rs`. Modelling sudo, `id` and `$HOME` per user is the change itself.

title: [Bug]: Windows type_text assigns embedded web textarea values without delivering typed input
body:
### Primary area Cua Driver ### Summary On Windows, background `type_text` addressed to an editable element inside an embedded WebView2 can execute `UIA ValuePattern.SetValue` successfully without delivering any typed input to an event-driven control. With xterm 6.0.0, the textarea value changes but `terminal.onData` remains empty. ### Reproduction 1. Run an embedded WebView2 host, such as this repository's Windows WebView2 fixture, with the following page. The xterm package URLs are pinned to 6.0.0; local copies of the same assets also work. ```html 

   

   
   
   ```

2. Observe the exact host window with `get_window_state`. Obtain the fresh element token for the `Terminal input` edit control.
3. Call `type_text` with that token and `text: "hello"`, keeping the default background delivery.
4. Observe the textarea value, the input event, and the `received` output independently of the Driver's UIA value readback.

This reproduces consistently with a fresh page. Focusing the textarea first or making it visible does not change the result.

### Expected behavior

`type_text` delivers the requested typed text to the target's input handling, or refuses before mutating the target when the available background route cannot provide that behavior. An explicit `set_value` operation can remain available for callers that intend a value assignment.

### Actual behavior

The target textarea becomes `hello`, but xterm receives no input. The browser publishes this event:

```json
{"constructor":"Event","trusted":true,"hasData":false,"data":null,"hasInputType":false,"inputType":null,"value":"hello"}
```

xterm's input handler requires nonempty `event.data` and `event.inputType === "insertText"` in this initial state. Its `onData` callback is never called. Waiting for UIA publication does not deliver the missing text.

The Driver accurately reports an unverified accessibility write rather than a confirmed application effect:

```json
{"route":"accessibility","delivery":{"mode":"background"},"effect":"unverifiable"}
```

The remaining problem is that a typed-input request has already taken an assignment path that cannot satisfy this consumer. A fresh read of the changed textarea value cannot establish that typed input was delivered.

### Environment

- Component: Cua Driver, Windows x86_64.
- Reproduced release binaries: 0.26.1, 0.28.2 and 0.38.0.
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, build 26300.
- Embedded host: repository WebView2/WPF fixture; WebView2 156.0.4314.58.
- Target: xterm 6.0.0, default screenReaderMode=false.
- The 0.38.0 Windows release archive was verified against its published checksum.

### Evidence

Independent controls narrow the cause:

- Calling Windows UIAutomationClient's `ValuePattern.SetValue` directly produces the same field changes and incomplete input event, without any Driver routing or focus guards.
- An ordinary textarea receives the same generic input event. Its value can be read successfully, which is different from delivering an input payload to xterm.
- Supplying `data: "hello"` and `inputType: "insertText"` on an input event makes xterm emit `hello`. Omitting either field does not. An ordinary Event with those two properties also works, so the constructor name is not the deciding factor.
- Native foreground character input delivers ASCII text to xterm. It was tested only as an explicitly selected control after background delivery was refused.
- A standalone Edge window returns `background_unavailable` for default `type_text` before mutation. The embedded WebView2 host instead admits its UIA value-write path. Explicit `set_value` and raw UIA exhibit the event limitation in both hosts.

The Windows `TypeTextTool` branch currently appends to `CurrentValue` and calls `SetValue` when an element exposes ValuePattern. This report concerns the difference between that assignment and typed input, not a missing UIA provider write.

### Workaround and additional context

For ASCII text, explicitly selecting foreground character input with fresh target coordinates works in the tested host. Do not blindly replay a request after an unverifiable value write, since that write can still publish asynchronously.

Related but distinct: #2876 proposes admitting more Chromium ValuePattern `type_text` calls. This report demonstrates why a successful ValuePattern write does not establish typed-input compatibility for event-driven controls, including cases already admitted in embedded WebView2.

The proposed focused fix is to avoid substituting a web-content value assignment for typed input, preserve native UIA form-control behavior and explicit `set_value`, and provide an existing explicit refusal when no supported background typing route is available. It should retain the current foreground permission boundary and add application-event regression evidence.

title: feat(relay,spacesd): a removed computer deletes its Spaces when it next comes online (CUA-3479)
body:
Linear: [CUA-3479](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3479) (follow-up to CUA-3413, which shipped the stopgap copy in #6508 and #6504).

**For users:** ticking "Also delete" when removing an offline computer now really deletes its Spaces. They leave the account at once, and the computer deletes them, files included, the next time it comes online. Before, they left the account but kept running on the computer, unseen.

## Design: server-side intent, client-side execution

**Relay** (`libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-relay/src/pending_deletions.rs`)
- `DELETE /v1/machines/{id}?spaces=delete` first writes a pending-deletion record for the computer: the Space ids and names, who asked, and the computer's token hash. Then it forgets the Spaces. If the write fails, the removal is refused (500) and nothing is removed.
- Stored like `<state>.spaces.json`: `<state>.pending-deletions.json` (atomic replace, private mode, reported to the storage health).
- `GET /v1/machines/{id}/pending-deletions` and `POST /v1/machines/{id}/pending-deletions/{space}/ack` accept only that computer's machine token: the one it had when removed (by hash), or its new one if it was added again with the same id. Another computer's token or an account token gets 403; an unknown token gets 401.
- Acks are idempotent, and the last ack clears the record. Records expire 90 days after the latest request. Account erasure drops them.
- Deleted means deleted: adding the computer again keeps the record, and the relay refuses to register a pending Space id again (410) until it is acked.

**cua-spacesd** (`cua-spacesd-server/src/pending_deletions.rs`, wired in `cua-spacesd join` for hosts)
- Each relay dial (start and every reconnect, via a new `JoinConfig::dialing` signal) triggers a sweep, at most once a minute. The sweep reads the list with the machine token and deletes each Space through the host's cua daemon, as the machine's owner (`DeleteHostSpace`, else `DeleteCloudSpace`). Each Space is acked once it's deleted.
- A Space already gone is acked. A failed delete isn't acked and is retried later. Nothing off the list is touched: only plain relay ids are passed to the daemon.
- When the relay doesn't know the token (a computer removed without delete), the sweeper asks again only hourly, or at once when the token changes (`cua host setup` adding it again).

**App** (`spaces-tree-page.tsx`)
- The remove dialog says "The 2 Spaces leave your account now and won't come back. Linux box deletes them, with their files, the next time it comes online." It no longer tries to delete each Space through the offline computer first (that always failed). The rows disappear at once.

**CLI and docs:** the `cua spaces rm --delete-spaces` prompt and the add-a-computer guide say the same thing. The relay README documents the routes, the 90-day expiry and the storage file.

## Tests
- Relay unit tests: record, merge, ack, idempotence, expiry, persistence, and erase by account.
- Relay integration (`tests/pending_deletions.rs`):
  - record and fetch, and survival across a restart;
  - auth: another computer's token is refused (403), as are another account's computer and an account token (403), and no token or an unknown one (401);
  - acks, and the record clearing;
  - remove without delete records nothing;
  - adding the computer again keeps the record and refuses the ids (410) until they are acked;
  - a second removal adds to the record.
- Account erasure test: `pending_deletions` is counted and dropped.
- cua-spacesd (`cua-spacesd-server/tests/pending_deletions.rs`, real relay in process plus a fake cua daemon on a Unix socket):
  - a sweep deletes only listed Spaces, acks one already gone, and retries a failure;
  - end to end: an offline computer is removed with delete, comes back (its dial is refused, the sweep still runs), and its Spaces are deleted and acked while an unlisted one stays;
  - a computer added again with a new token still deletes them first.
- Web: the tree test checks the new copy and that only `machines.remove` (with `deleteSpaces`) is called.

## Rollout
The relay ships staging first, then goes to prod after a green staging smoke. An older cua-spacesd ignores the record, which waits up to 90 days. An older relay without the routes makes the sweeper retry quietly.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse web value writes as background typing
body:
## Summary

Background `type_text(element_token)` in embedded Chromium can assign an editor's textarea value without producing the inserted-text event payload the editor consumes. Carry the existing web-content classification into retained UIA targets and return `background_unavailable` before that assignment. Native UIA controls, explicit `set_value`, and the existing foreground path keep their behavior.

The focused WebView2 regression checks an application-owned input payload, explicit assignment support, the exact refusal, unchanged field state, and the background focus/input oracles. Windows Tauri AX typing expectations follow the same refusal boundary.

## Related work

Fixes #6531

Related: #2876 discusses admitting additional Chromium UIA value writes. This change addresses the event fidelity of a value write in embedded web content.

RFC: not required for this Windows bug fix to the existing typed-input and background-refusal behavior. No public tool, argument, or foreground authorization is added.

## Compatibility and risk

- Windows web-content background typing that previously performed a value assignment now refuses before mutation. Callers can deliberately use `set_value`, browser input, or an explicitly selected supported foreground typing route.
- Classification requires both a snapshot target below a Document and a Chromium descendant of the native host. Native UIA controls outside web content retain their value-write path.
- Background calls do not activate the target or replay text through another route. Removing the admission check reintroduces the original assignment behavior.
- The regression fixture uses only standard input-event payloads; it adds no editor-specific dependency or production test hook.

title: fix(spaces): Cua Driver runs after the new first run, whatever the Mac shares (CUA-3485)
body:
**For users:** after "Add this computer" in the new first run, agents can use the apps on this Mac. The Cua Driver page shows "Working on this Mac" instead of "Not answering".

Linear: [CUA-3485](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3485)

## Cause
The new first run sets this Mac up to keep its screen private (`--no-desktop --no-driver --no-mcp`). cua-spacesd only started the built-in Cua Driver (#6505) when the desktop was shared, so it never ran.

## Fix
- **cua-spacesd** starts the embedded Cua Driver whatever `--no-desktop` and `--no-driver` say. Those flags are about remote callers. Only the "Let agents use apps on this Mac" switch (on by default) and `CUA_SPACESD_EMBEDDED_DRIVER=0` keep it off. A Mac set up earlier with `--no-driver` gets the driver as soon as the new cua-spacesd runs.
- **Start request:** the app can write `<CuaHome>/run/cua-driver.start` so a driver that's waiting out its restart backoff starts at once.
- **Set up, Repair and turning the switch on** start a driver that isn't answering. They send a start request first, then restart the host service if that didn't work.
- The old first run path (desktop shared) is unchanged.

## Tests
- `cua-spacesd/tests/embedded_driver_bin.rs` (macOS): the real binary with `--no-desktop --no-driver --no-mcp` starts the driver, and the pause marker alone decides whether it runs. Removing the marker starts it, which covers hosts set up before with `--no-driver`.
- `embedded_driver.rs`: a start request cuts the backoff short and is consumed.
- `EmbeddedDriverTests.swift`: the app's start steps (paused, running, not set up, ask, restart).
- `cua-host` spare-profile test: the setup never disables the embedded driver.

title: fix(spaces-web): default line, first-run list, Continue on menu, demo desktops (CUA-3486)
body:
For users: Home no longer says your default is offline when it isn't, the new setup keeps Continue on screen however many computers you have, and "Continue on" only lists computers that could actually carry on the chat.

Linear: https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3486

Fixes items 2 to 5 found while capturing the 5 Nov Spaces UI storyboard (the Cua Driver item is a separate PR).

## What changes

**Home's line under the box (Spaces as a tree)**
- The line is built from parts (the default's name, why it can't take the task, where it runs instead), so it can never say "your default" twice.
- A saved default whose computer was removed is ignored, both in the tree and in the resolver the app uses when it can't ask the relay. This was behind "Your default, your default, is offline" while This Mac (the real default) was online.
- A computer that is online but doesn't share its desktop is no longer treated as offline or as "Next to try". The task goes to the next computer that can take it (or This Mac), and the line and "Where a task goes" say why ("is online but doesn't share its desktop"). The picker's note for such a computer says the same instead of "On now".

**New setup, screen 2 (Labs "Try the new setup")**
- Two or more offline computers fold into one "N offline" row that opens to show them. One offline computer still shows as itself.
- Continue sits in a footer that stays at the bottom of the window.

**"Continue on" in a continued chat**
- Lists only your other computers that are online and shared, each once. Web browsers, phones and other signed-in devices are left out, and a short line counts the offline computers.
- The menu opens above the box, flips when there's no room, and scrolls within the window instead of running off it.

**Demo host**
- With `?demo=desktops` the Mac mini shares its desktop too, so Home can start on it when it's the default. The demo's resolver also knows when a Space on a computer is the default.

## Tests
- `lib/spaces-tree.test.ts`: removed default ignored (local and relay answers), "your default" never repeated, online-without-desktop computer skipped and never called offline, relay pick without a desktop moves on, default without a desktop explained, resolver treats an unknown default as unset.
- `__tests__/first-run-new.test.tsx`: the "14 offline" fold opens and closes, the count follows the data, Continue is in a sticky footer.
- `__tests__/pick-up.test.tsx` and `lib/machines.test.ts`: "Continue on" de-duplicates by machine id, drops devices and offline computers, and its menu is height-limited and scrolls.
- `__tests__/spaces-tree.test.tsx` (runs with the wasm core in CI): the demo starts on the Mac mini default, and with the default offline the line and the order agree.

Run locally: typecheck, the web package's vitest suite (the wasm-core tests run in CI), `bin/ci --quick`.

title: [BUG]: cua doctor rejects unset runtime path defaults
body:
## Description

`cua doctor` reports three failures when the optional runtime paths are unset. Unsetting the paths does not resolve the failures because their built-in defaults are empty strings.

## Environment

- Cua CLI: 0.10.1
- macOS: 27.2, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Lume: 0.6.1

## Steps to reproduce

1. Leave `runtime.container_path`, `runtime.vm_path`, and `runtime.microvm_path` unset in the Cua config and environment.
2. Run `cua doctor`.

## Expected behavior

Doctor accepts the unset paths as no override, allowing Cua to discover the runtime executables.

## Actual behavior

Doctor exits with code 1 and reports:

```text
[fail] host.defaults.runtime_container_path: runtime.container_path: expected the full path of a program (unset it to use the one found), got "" (default)
[fail] host.defaults.runtime_vm_path: runtime.vm_path: expected the full path of a program (unset it to use the one found), got "" (default)
[fail] host.defaults.runtime_microvm_path: runtime.microvm_path: expected the full path of a program (unset it to use the one found), got "" (default)
```

`cua config unset` confirmed all three paths were already unset. The failures persisted on the next doctor run.

## Likely cause

The [settings registry](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.10.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-sandbox-core/src/settings.rs#L69-L97) defines the three defaults as empty strings. [Doctor validates every effective value](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.10.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/doctor/host.rs#L55-L86), but the [path validator requires an absolute path](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.10.1/libs/cua/crates/cua-sandbox-core/src/settings.rs#L692-L706), so it rejects those defaults.

A fix could treat a default-sourced empty path as no override while still validating supplied paths. A regression test should exercise all three unset defaults through doctor.

title: Windows 11 26H2: browser_prepare always fails with browser_endpoint_owner_mismatch
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Windows 11 26H2 (10.0.26300.9818), every isolated browser launch fails with `browser_endpoint_owner_mismatch`. Chrome's DevTools listener is there and answers, but Windows reports its TCP state as 0 instead of LISTEN, and the listener lookup in `browser_platform.rs` only accepts LISTEN.

### Reproduction

1. Windows 11 10.0.26300.9818.
2. Call `browser_prepare` with `{"allow_launch": true, "profile": {"mode": "isolated_new"}}`.
3. It fails every time.

The existing unit test shows it too:

```text
cargo test -p platform-windows --lib native_owner_table_observes_a_real_loopback_listener

native owner table did not report current-process listener 50525: []
```

### Expected behavior

The browser launches and `browser_prepare` returns `status: "ok"`.

### Actual behavior

```json
{"status": "refused", "refusal": {"code": "browser_endpoint_owner_mismatch", "message": "the isolated browser profile endpoint did not match live loopback socket ownership"}}
```

`GetExtendedTcpTable(TCP_TABLE_OWNER_PID_LISTENER)` does list the DevTools port with the spawned Chrome's pid, just with `dwState` 0.

It isn't specific to Chrome. On this build `dwState` looks unreliable in general:

- live listeners in the listener table come back as 0, 1, 2 or 6 (20, 7, 6 and 7 of 40 rows on my machine)
- some established connections show up as 2 in the full table
- `netstat` is affected too: it shows sshd on port 22 as `FIN_WAIT_1` and leaves out SMB, RDP and lsass, which all accept connections

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.38.0 (`85e2b13`), also `main` at `1e1b9489f`
- Windows 11 Pro 26H2, 10.0.26300.9818 (October 28 update), x64
- Chrome 157.0.8103.39

### Evidence

DevTools port of one launch (`dwState, address, port, pid`; 18160 is the spawned Chrome):

```text
TCP_TABLE_OWNER_PID_ALL:      (0, '127.0.0.1', 63585, 18160)
TCP_TABLE_OWNER_PID_LISTENER: (0, '127.0.0.1', 63585, 18160)
```

### Workaround and additional context

No workaround that I found. Existing-profile attach uses the same lookup, so it's probably affected too, but I only tested isolated launch.

Fix in #6539: treat a listener-table row as listening when it has no remote peer, and stop reading `dwState`.

title: fix(cua-driver): find Windows DevTools listeners without trusting TCP row state

## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows 11 26H2 (10.0.26300.9818), `browser_prepare` fails every isolated launch with `browser_endpoint_owner_mismatch`. Windows reports `dwState` inconsistently there, even in the listener-only table, and we only accepted rows with `MIB_TCP_STATE_LISTEN`.

title: fix(ci): run release-gate lanes when the PR-only quick job is skipped
body:
CUA-3471. Fixes #6525.

## Root cause

#6465 added a `quick` job that runs only on `pull_request` and made `decide` in `e2e-cua-driver-release-gate.yml`, and `source` in `e2e-rust-linux.yml`, depend on it. Both of those jobs have `!failure() && !cancelled()`, so they still run when `quick` is skipped. The jobs after them did not have it. GitHub skips any job whose `needs` chain has a skipped job unless its `if:` calls a status function. So on the 5 Nov schedule run, `decide` passed with `run=true mode=nightly` and then linux, windows, macos and browsers were all skipped. `result` and `nightly report` failed on the skipped lanes. The 4 Nov nightly ran before #6465 merged, and it passed.

The same problem hits `e2e-rust-linux.yml` whenever it is not a PR run: the stable-tag call from `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml`, manual dispatch, and the release-gate call. Its `verify-skill`, `shared`, `native`, `capture` and `installer` jobs would be skipped, so certification could not run either.

## Change

- `e2e-cua-driver-release-gate.yml`: add `!failure() && !cancelled()` to the `linux`, `windows`, `macos`, `macos-pr` and `browsers` conditions.
- `e2e-rust-linux.yml`: do the same for the lane jobs. `certify` used `success()`, which is also false when `quick` is skipped. It now checks that each lane it needs succeeded, so it still fails closed.
- New test `test_quick_skip_propagation.py`: any job behind the PR-only `quick` in these two workflows must call a status function in its `if:`. It fails against current main and passes with this change.

Other workflows have the same pattern (for example the `ci-cua-spaces-macos.yml`, `e2e-cua-sdk.yml` and `ci-cua-spacesd.yml` push runs skip their downstream jobs). They are left for a follow-up so this PR stays limited to the release gate.

## Proof

The scoped repository checks: the `.github/scripts` pytest suite passes, including the new test and the updated Linux workflow assertions. The new test fails on the unpatched workflows and names exactly the lanes that were skipped in the 5 Nov nightly. The nightly itself runs only on schedule or dispatch, so its first real proof is the next scheduled run or a manual dispatch after merge.

CUA-3489

`cursor-overlay` and `cursor-theme-cli` depend on `cua-driver-core` with `default-features = false`. Built that way, `cargo clippy -D warnings` fails in core on three items that only the `yaml` feature uses:

- the `std::path::Component` import in `session_manifest.rs` is now behind `#[cfg(feature = "yaml")]`
- the `TerminationGrant` variants, which only the YAML manifest parser constructs, get `allow(dead_code)` when `yaml` is off
- the `tool` binding in `PolicyEngine::is_potentially_listable` is discarded when neither `yaml` nor `rego` is on, the same way `evaluate` already discards it

The `--no-default-features` test build also gets a cfg-gated `allow(unused_mut)` on the budget list in `daemon.rs`, because only the `script` feature pushes to that list.

This doesn't change behavior. With default features the same code compiles.

Proof: the scoped repository checks were `cargo fmt --check`, plus `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on `cua-driver-core` with default features, with no default features, and with `yaml`, `rego`, `script` and all three enabled one at a time. They also covered `cursor-overlay` and `cursor-theme-cli`, and `cargo test` on core (default features), `cursor-overlay` and `cursor-theme-cli`. All passed.

title: fix(cua-compat): keep sweeping a Space a dead gateway's create makes late
body:
CUA-3463

The nightly "Chaos: cua-compat leak checks" run (real Spaces, QEMU) leaks in 6 to 7 of 40 seeds. The leaks are of two kinds.

**1. A sandbox record that no gateway owns** (seeds 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 19 on 5 Nov: `file:sandboxes e2b-<id>.json` plus `space e2b-<id>`). A create of the default image forks the gateway's base checkpoint, and the daemon runs that fork to completion even after its caller goes away. When the gateway is SIGKILLed mid-fork, the restarted gateway's sweeper finds the journaled name unclaimed and deletes it. That delete lands while the fork is still restoring, so it returns `Ok(true)`, and the sweeper then drops the name from `owned.jsonl`. A few seconds later the fork finishes and saves its state file. Nothing owns or deletes that file until the daemon's lifetime reaper picks it up long after the 150 s settle window. The daemon log shows this order: the fork starts, the gateway restarts, and the sandbox is ended only by "sandbox lifetime ended" about 25 minutes later. None of these names was still in the journal.

Fix: after a sweep deletes something, the sweeper keeps the name and restarts its settle clock. It resolves the name only once its deletes have found nothing for `CREATE_SETTLE`, which the not-found path already does. A Space recorded after its first sweep is then swept again.

**2. A VM directory with no state file** (seed 16: `file:vmm qemu/e2b-<id>`, holding only `disk.qcow2`). A cold QEMU create that was cancelled while `create_instance` was making the overlay dropped the future. Neither the `Ok` arm (save) nor the `Err` arm (remove_dir_all) ran, so the directory stayed. Nothing lists a VM without `state.json`, so nothing removes it. Fix: a drop guard removes the directory unless the state file was written.

Tests: a journal test covers a Space that is made again after its sweep (it gets swept again, and the name is kept until it settles). A cua-vmm test checks that a dropped guard removes the directory and a disarmed one keeps it.

Size-limit reason: none needed. Production lines are under add 200 / net 100.

title: ci(spaces): nightly channel on every platform, CI gate, no more betas (CUA-3503)
body:
Linear: [CUA-3503](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3503)

**For users:** Windows and Linux users can now get nightly builds too, the same way Mac users do, and Cua Spaces stops shipping one-off betas.

## What changes

**Nightly on every platform** (`nightly-cua-spaces.yml`, `cd-cua-spaces-build.yml`)
- The nightly now builds macOS, Windows (x64, arm64) and Linux (x64, arm64), signed like a release, and publishes all of it to the one rolling `cua-spaces-nightly` prerelease. Each night replaces its assets. It's never a new release, never a draft and never Latest.
- Feeds, all on `cua-spaces-nightly`:
  - macOS: `cua-spaces-nightly-appcast.xml`, Sparkle `nightly` channel (unchanged).
  - Windows: `nightly.yml`; Linux: `nightly-linux.yml`, `nightly-linux-arm64.yml`. electron-builder writes these for an `X.Y.Z-nightly.YYYYMMDD.N` version, pointed at the nightly release.
- **Version:** `X.Y.Z-nightly.YYYYMMDD.<run number>+sha7` (Windows and Linux carry it without `+sha7`). The run number makes every nightly unique and newer than the last, even two on one day, so Windows and Linux apps are offered each one. An HHMM time would need a leading zero, which semver forbids.
- Fixed-name downloads for docs and testers: `cua-spaces-nightly-darwin-universal.dmg`, `-windows-<arch>-setup.exe`, `-linux-<arch>.AppImage` and `.deb`.
- **Gate:** the nightly builds only when main's Spaces CI (`ci-cua-spaces*.yml` on main's head, or on the newest commit that ran it) is green, and only when the release inputs changed. Dispatch inputs `force` and `ignore_ci` override.
- A platform that fails keeps last night's build. The others still publish and the run ends red. The input tree is recorded only after a full success, so the next night retries.
- **After publishing, the job checks** that the release is a prerelease and not Latest, that every feed URL and fixed-name download resolves, that the nightly appcast holds only nightly items, and that the stable feeds on `cua-spaces-latest` hold no nightly.

**No more betas** (`cd-cua-spaces.yml`)
- A new first job, `refuse-beta`, refuses any `-beta` version (tag or manual run) unless the repository variable `ALLOW_SPACES_BETA` is `true`. Every other job needs it, so a refused beta builds nothing, requests no staging smoke and leaves no draft.
- `verify-release` now also requires a successful plan. Before this, it could run on an empty plan when an early job failed.
- Release Please and the canary/staging gate for stable are unchanged.

**Feed separation today (finding):** Windows and Linux already kept beta (`beta*.yml`, 0.21.0-beta.7) apart from stable (`latest*.yml`, 0.20.0) on `cua-spaces-latest`. Nightly feeds now live on a different release altogether.

**Docs:** new `docs/contributing/releasing-cua-spaces.md`, an AGENTS.md "Cua Spaces: no betas" section, and a pointer in the Mac app README.

## Tests
- `apps/cua-spaces-desktop/test/nightly-feeds.test.ts`: version ordering (same day, next day, next stable) with the semver electron-updater uses; the nightly config channel and URL; stable and beta keep `cua-spaces-latest`; feed merging and absolutizing; refusal of `latest*`/`beta*` files, non-nightly versions and URLs outside the nightly release.
- `.github/scripts/tests/test_spaces_nightly_gate.py`: green, red, pending, cancelled, other workflows, walk-back.
- `.github/scripts/tests/test_sparkle_feed.py`: the nightly appcast takes nightlies only.
- `.github/scripts/tests/test_spaces_nightly_wiring.py`: writes go only to the nightly tag, never Latest, every release job needs `refuse-beta`.
- Full `.github/scripts` suite (1540 passed), Electron vitest (589 passed), actionlint, `bin/ci --quick`.

The app-side Stable/Nightly picker (Mac and Electron) is #6548. The two PRs merge cleanly together.

title: feat(spaces): Stable / Nightly update channel; betas move to Nightly (CUA-3503)
body:
Linear: [CUA-3503](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3503). Supersedes #6015 (CUA-2354).

**For users:** Settings, Advanced, Updates now offers Stable (the default) or Nightly. "Nightly builds: get the newest changes from main every day. They may break." Anyone who had early releases (Beta) on moves to Nightly, and About shows a nightly's version and build day.

**What changed**
- **Core:** `UpdateChannel` is `Stable | Nightly`; Beta is gone, and `beta` reads as Nightly everywhere (serde alias, `from_id`, bridges). A prerelease's first launch starts on Nightly. New `feed_url` / `nightly_feed_url` (the nightly appcast next to `SUFeedURL`), the channel help line, the way back from a nightly on Stable (a note plus **Download Stable**), and About's `Version 0.21.0-nightly.20261105+55e1f5d, built 5 Nov 2026`. FFI mirror, Swift and TypeScript bindings, and the parity golden are regenerated.
- **macOS (Sparkle):** on Nightly, `feedURLString(for:)` returns `.../cua-spaces-nightly/cua-spaces-nightly-appcast.xml` and the allowed channels are `["nightly"]`; on Stable, `SUFeedURL` and no extra channels. A channel switch checks at once. A nightly's release notes link to the rolling nightly release.
- **Windows and Linux (electron-updater):** before each check, `setFeedURL` points at the chosen channel's rolling release: `cua-spaces-latest` with channel `latest`, or `cua-spaces-nightly` with channel `nightly` (`nightly.yml`, `nightly-linux*.yml`). It never relies on the URL baked into app-update.yml. `allowPrerelease` is on only for Nightly, and downgrades stay off. Electron on macOS serves no channel (the Mac app is the Swift app).
- **Web:** the Advanced tab's switch becomes a Stable | Nightly picker that uses the core's label, help, note and link. Contracts, shapes and `bridge-shapes.json` are updated, and the WebKit adapter reads an older host's `beta` as `nightly`.

**Settings storage (backward compatible):** an older release (0.20.0 and earlier) parses the whole settings file with serde and falls back to the defaults on a channel name it doesn't know. So `save` still writes Nightly as `"updateChannel": "beta"`, and this build reads both `beta` and `nightly` as Nightly. Someone who goes back to an old Stable build by hand keeps every setting, and that build sees them on Beta. A test checks this against a copy of the old two-variant enum. The Electron shell's own settings file is parsed leniently, so it stores `nightly` and reads a saved `beta` as Nightly.

**Tests**
- `cargo test -p cua-spaces-app-core`: all pass, including new migration, feed URL, build-day and picker tests, and the regenerated parity golden.
- App-core FFI mirror `--check` is current. Clippy reports no warnings in the changed crates.

title: [RFC]: Browser compatibility behavior and existing-profile trust boundaries
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Propose a browser compatibility mode for authorized automation sessions with explicit, per-session opt-in before any behavior that changes page-visible automation indicators or browser properties is used on an approved existing profile. Request a maintainer decision on whether such a mode belongs in Cua, what specific behavior it may use, and how its boundaries differ for Driver-launched isolated browsers and existing profiles. This is a request for discussion, not a request to merge an implementation.

### Motivation and current state

Some browser-based workflows encounter compatibility or sign-in obstacles when a site responds differently to an automated browser. These differences may prevent a user from completing an otherwise authorized workflow. The reasons for any particular site's behavior are not established by this proposal, and a compatibility mode cannot guarantee that a site will allow a session.

Cua Driver can launch a browser with an isolated profile or attach to an approved existing profile. The current existing-profile policy expressly refuses registration of document-start scripts. An [experiment on my fork](https://github.com/HaniLabs/cua/commit/86872e44351e2861e53e2bab34b4903d2d789480) explores different launch and page behavior. It applies the launch changes by default and provides an opt-out only for the attach-time script. It has not been accepted upstream and is not evidence of a supported or validated contract. Its existing-profile behavior would alter the current trust boundary and requires a separate decision.

Related [issue #3136](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/3136) addresses detecting browser challenges and rate limits and stopping retries. It explicitly excludes stealth fingerprint emulation. This RFC does not treat that issue as approval or as a request for this behavior.

### Goals

- Decide whether browser compatibility behavior that changes page-visible automation indicators or browser properties is appropriate for Cua at all.
- If appropriate, define a clear, explicitly selected contract that distinguishes Driver-launched isolated browsers from approved existing profiles.
- Make supported behavior, defaults, limitations, and errors observable to callers.
- Define evidence needed for every supported operating system and browser before any behavior is released.
- Preserve user control and make it clear that a delivered browser action does not imply a site accepted the session or that a task succeeded.

### Non-goals

- Solve CAPTCHAs, automate challenges, evade rate limits, or defeat a site's access controls.
- Guarantee access to a site or imply that an authorized user is entitled to automate a particular service.
- Conceal use of automation from a user or silently modify existing profiles.
- Infer that different browser or operating-system combinations support identical behavior without evidence.
- Collect, retain, or publish credentials, session data, browsing history, or page content for telemetry.

### Proposal

Propose a limited compatibility mode that is disabled by default. Define its public API and supported behavior before implementation. For an approved existing profile, require explicit user opt-in for the specific session and clearly communicate the mode and its effects to the caller. A normal profile-attachment approval alone would not enable the mode. Maintainers may reject the proposal or define narrower boundaries during review.

Treat the two browser ownership cases as separate decisions:

1. **Driver-launched isolated browser:** determine whether any browser launch configuration affecting page-visible automation signals is allowed, with explicit documentation of effects and limitations.
2. **Approved existing profile:** require explicit opt-in for the specific session in addition to normal profile-attachment authorization. Retain the current restrictions unless a separate review authorizes a specific change. Registering code that runs in future documents changes page behavior and must not be described as a read-only operation. Review whether it is appropriate at all, how consent is conveyed, which targets and documents it may affect, and how its lifecycle and removal would be enforced.

Callers should receive a clear indication when a requested mode is unavailable or only partially supported. Browser blockers and rate limits should be surfaced and handled responsibly rather than retried automatically; detection behavior remains separate work. Do not assume the fork experiment's flags, page scripts, defaults, or browser-property substitutions are the proposed or accepted design.

### Alternatives considered

- **Keep the existing behavior and do not add compatibility mode.** This preserves the existing trust boundary and avoids representing altered browser properties to websites. Users can perform affected steps manually or use an available approved integration.
- **Detect and report blockers, then stop or request user handoff.** This follows the direction of #3136 and makes the failure visible, but does not change how a site evaluates a browser session.
- **Use a service's supported API or other authorized interface.** This is preferable when available and permitted; it may not cover every browser task.
- **Permit limited opt-in behavior only for Driver-launched isolated browsers.** This avoids changing an existing personal profile, but still needs review of website interactions, caller expectations, cross-platform support, and the appropriate boundary.
- **Permit behavior for existing profiles as well.** This has a broader trust and compatibility impact and would need separate consent, policy, lifecycle, and security review; it should not be inferred from approval of isolated-browser behavior.

### Compatibility and migration

Keep existing behavior and profile restrictions as the baseline while this RFC is undecided. If a new mode is accepted, make activation explicit, document platform and browser support, and provide a rollback path that restores the prior behavior. Review whether any public API, launch option, or session capability requires a compatibility notice. Unsupported combinations must report the limitation rather than silently claiming the mode is active.

No migration or automatic change to existing profiles is proposed. Acceptance of an RFC would be required before implementation work intended for upstream, and the accepted RFC would be merged before or with any implementation PR.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

The Driver must honor its existing authorization model and target boundaries. Changes to an approved existing profile's permitted protocol surface and any code executed in documents need explicit review; an existing-profile attachment is not blanket consent for additional behavior. The design must address user disclosure, session scoping, cleanup, and what happens if setup or cleanup fails.

The mode must not solve challenges, automatically work around site blocks, or conceal a block from the caller. Telemetry must not contain credentials, cookies, profile contents, URLs with private data, page contents, or session identifiers. This RFC requests a design decision and does not report a vulnerability.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

If the proposal is accepted, agree on the contract and test plan before implementation. Evidence should include:

- Contract tests for explicit activation, default behavior, unsupported combinations, setup errors, cleanup, and rollback.
- Existing-profile policy tests proving the agreed permitted and refused operations and that no unrelated targets or profiles are affected.
- Browser tests using local controlled pages and fixtures, including navigation and session lifecycle; no real account or third-party service is required.
- Focused tests and native verification on each affected supported operating system and browser, with concrete limitations documented when equivalent behavior is unavailable.
- Regression coverage showing that challenge and rate-limit handling remains observable and does not initiate automatic bypass or retry loops.

No cross-platform or upstream validation is claimed for the fork experiment.

### Unresolved questions

1. Should Cua support any modification to page-visible automation indicators or browser properties, even on an explicit opt-in basis?
2. If yes, which isolated-browser behaviors and platforms are acceptable, and how should callers discover and consent to them?
3. Is explicit per-session opt-in sufficient to consider existing profiles, or should they remain outside this feature? What additional authorization, protocol restrictions, scope, and cleanup would be necessary?
4. How should partial support or setup failure be surfaced without creating a misleading guarantee?
5. Is blocker detection and user handoff sufficient for the user problem, or is another supported integration more appropriate?

### RFC document pull request

[Draft RFC document PR #6550](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6550) contains the proposal for review. It is not an accepted decision or an implementation PR.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for related issues and RFCs; #3136 addresses blocker reporting and explicitly excludes stealth fingerprint emulation.
- [x] This proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required, not only an implementation preference.

title: fix(cua-driver): send keys and clicks to a macOS window's open sheet
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: with a window's sheet open (Finder's Go to Folder, Save, "Replace?"), keys to the window were refused with `window_not_key` ("the app's focused window is 15304", the sheet's own CGWindowID), and a request naming the sheet's id was refused with `off_space_or_ax_unresolved`. `set_value` into the sheet already worked, so an agent could fill the field but never confirm it.
- What changed: a sheet now counts as the window it is attached to.
  - The focused-window reads behind the key gate, `bring_to_front` and pid-only keys resolve a focused sheet to its parent window, through the existing sheet-to-parent resolution.
  - A request naming a sheet's own id is judged as its parent for the background-input facts (AX membership, minimized, element ancestry, competing windows), while the event still goes to the sheet.
  - `get_window_state` on a sheet's id walks the parent window, sheet included. `bring_to_front` brings the parent and accepts the sheet in front of it.
  - Sheets are read from each AX window's `AXSheet` children, and only when the requested id is not a listed window.
  - A window that is neither the target nor one of its sheets is still refused. The document-edit check keeps the raw focused window.

## Related work

Refs: no upstream issue. Found while driving macOS apps from an agent (Finder's Go to Folder sheet; a Save As panel).

RFC: not required. No public SDK, CLI, MCP or protocol change; requests that were refused for a sheet are now accepted.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: keys, clicks, `get_window_state` and `bring_to_front` now work with a window's sheet open. Windows and Linux have no sheets of this kind and are unchanged.
- Not covered: the remote Save panel's own window belongs to the panel service, so naming it with the app's pid is still refused as another process's window. Address that panel through the document window, where its elements and now its keys land.
- Risk and rollback: one extra AX read of `AXSheet` children only when the requested id is not a listed window; two windows claiming one sheet resolve to nothing (still refused). Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: 5 new unit tests in `ax/exact_target.rs`, `ax/window_scope.rs` and `tools/bring_to_front.rs` (red against a stub, one mutation-checked). On this branch: `cargo test -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core --lib` passes (1174 + 656), `cargo fmt --check` is clean, clippy reports nothing in the touched files, `cargo check --workspace --tests` compiles.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 26, daemon built from this change, Accessibility granted): a Finder window, Go to Folder, the path filled with `set_value`, then Return. 0.37.0 answered `window_not_key … the app's focused window is Some(22752)`; this change delivered Return to the sheet and the window moved to the folder.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the remote Save panel above; Windows and Linux CI.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

On Windows and Linux, Cua Spaces now shows the right logo and name for your own computer ("This PC" / "This machine" instead of an Apple logo and "This Mac"), the title-bar buttons match the dark first run, and Remove no longer leaves a ghost of the removed computer.

Bugs fixed (found in a Windows 11 + Ubuntu real-machine test):
1. New first run showed an Apple mark for this computer; it now uses the host's real OS (computer row and the coding-agent header).
2. "This Mac" copy on Windows/Linux in the new Home, ask box, task view, imported chats, Settings (Labs and default rows), the Spaces tree and its empty state: all via `thisComputerLabel()` / `thisComputerText()`. macOS wording is unchanged.

title: fix(cua-driver): kill an app this session launched after its idle end
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `kill_app` refused a process this session had launched once the session had been idle-swept: `foreign_process_termination_denied`. The 5-minute idle sweep ends a session through the same end hooks as an explicit end, and both hooks that clean the ownership store (the registry's in `tool.rs` and the browser engine's `cleanup_prepared_session`) dropped the session's launch records. A client that starts the same session label again after the sweep could no longer kill what it launched.
- What changed:
  - Session cleanup now records why a session ended; `session_end_reason()` exposes it to end hooks while they run.
  - On an idle end, both hooks keep the session's launch records under its label. Every other end still drops them.
  - An explicit `end_session` for a session that already idled out (whose end hooks already ran) drops the kept records itself, when the caller owns that session.
  - Unchanged: every kill still checks the process fingerprint, and another session is still refused.

## Related work

Refs: no upstream issue. Found while an agent opened an app, worked more than five minutes without launching anything, then tried to close what it opened.

RFC: not required. No public SDK, CLI, MCP or protocol change; a kill that was refused after an idle sweep is now allowed for the session that launched the process.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: `kill_app` works for a session's own launches after that session was idle-swept and started again. Shared core code, so macOS, Windows and Linux alike.
- Risk and rollback: launch records of sessions that idle out and never come back stay in memory until an explicit end or a daemon restart (one small record per launch). A daemon restart still drops all records, as before. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: tests for both end hooks (`an_idle_end_keeps_the_launches_the_browser_hook_shares` and the registry hook), another session's kill, and the kill after an explicit end; red before the change, mutation-checked. On this branch: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos --lib` passes (1176 + 651), `cargo fmt --check` is clean, clippy reports nothing new, `cargo check --workspace --tests` compiles.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 26, daemon built from this change): `launch_app` in a session, 6 idle minutes, `start_session` with the same label, then `kill_app`. 0.37.0 answered `foreign_process_termination_denied`; this change answered `Sent SIGKILL to pid 75675`. A first version that changed only the registry hook failed this check, which is how the browser hook was found.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Windows and Linux CI.

title: [Bug]: Cua Driver: type_text writes the wrong text into iOS Simulator apps
body:
### Primary area
Cua Driver

### Summary
If you automate an iOS app in the Simulator and call `type_text` in the background, the app receives the wrong text. Every character arrives as the A key, so `abc` becomes `Aaa`. On the guest's Korean keyboard it becomes `ㅁㅁㅁ`.

The call does not fail. It reports `effect:"unverifiable"`, so an agent can carry on with a corrupted search query or form value unless it reads the field back.

### Reproduction
1. Boot an iOS Simulator device and open a screen with a text field, such as the Settings search field.
2. Tap the field so the on-screen keyboard appears.
3. Call `type_text` with the Simulator's `pid` and `window_id`, `text:"abc"`, and the field's `x,y`.
4. Read the field back.

### Expected behavior
The field contains `abc`, or the tool refuses with an exact code and types nothing.

### Actual behavior
| Guest keyboard | Requested | Field contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| English | `abc` | `Aaa` (the capital looks like iOS auto-capitalization) |
| Korean | `abc` | `ㅁㅁㅁ` |
| Korean | `한글` | `ㅁㅁ` |

Passing an `element_token` for a text field that accessibility exposes does not help: the AX write does not land and the key-event fallback appends `aaaaa`.

### Environment
- Cua Driver 0.38.0, macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 26.6 Build version 17F113
- iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator, iOS 26.5
- `delivery_mode` background

### Evidence
- `char_key_events` in `platform-macos/src/input/keyboard.rs` sends ordinary characters on key code 0 (the A key) with the text attached as a Unicode string. The Simulator appears to use the key code and ignore the string. The same file documents this behavior for Screen Sharing.
- `press_key` sends real key codes and works in the background: `a b c 1 space` gives `Abc1 `.
- Field contents were read from the guest's accessibility tree and from screenshots.

### Workaround and additional context
Both of these entered the requested text in the background, without bringing the Simulator forward:

- **`set_value`**, when accessibility exposes the field. `한글 set_value 시험` returned `effect:"confirmed"`, and the app enabled the button that depends on the field.
- **`xcrun simctl pbcopy <device>`, then pressing the guest's Paste menu item**, when it does not (the Settings search field is one such case). Korean, English, emoji and a 300-character mixed string all matched.

The pasteboard route replaces the guest pasteboard. The host pasteboard `changeCount` did not change during a short test with Automatically Sync Pasteboard on, but that does not rule out syncing later, so avoid it for secrets.

`delivery_mode:"foreground"` was not tested.

### Submission checks
- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): press a shortcut's key where the keyboard layout types it on macOS
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, every chord path (`press_key`, `hotkey`, their no-auth and global HID variants) pressed letters, digits and symbols at fixed US key positions. On a French (AZERTY) Mac, `hotkey cmd+a` pressed the key that types `q` and quit the app (Slack, three times in a row); `cmd+w` pressed `z` (undo), and `cmd+=` zoomed out.
- What changed: a single printable character in a chord is pressed by the key that types it with the chord's modifiers held, read from the current layout with `UCKeyTranslate` over the main typing keys:
  - Command held: the Command layer (QWERTY on Russian and on Dvorak - QWERTY Command, where macOS reads shortcuts);
  - Control held: the Control layer (the key that types `^C` for `ctrl+c`; Return and Tab are left out, as they type `^M` and `^I` too);
  - otherwise: the plain layer.
  - Of several keys, the US key is kept, then the one that types the character with no modifier.
  - A character the layer has no key for, named keys, and every key when the layout has no Unicode data keep the US position, as macOS does for a shortcut whose character is not on the layout.

## Related work

Refs: no upstream issue. Found while an agent drove apps on a French AZERTY Mac.

RFC: not required. No public SDK, CLI, MCP or protocol change; chords now arrive as the key the user's own keyboard would send.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: shortcuts land on the right key on non-US layouts (AZERTY, QWERTZ, Dvorak, Turkish, Russian, Greek, …). Unchanged on US layouts. Windows already sends layout virtual keys and X11 resolves keysyms on the current keymap, so both are untouched.
- Clients that already remap keys for the layout themselves must stop doing so, or keys would be placed twice.
- Known quirk: on 6 layouts (Czech - QWERTY, Polish - QWERTZ, Slovak - QWERTY, Italian, Albanian, Croatian - QWERTZ), macOS's Control layer swaps y and z (or w and z) compared with the keycaps. The rule follows the Control layer, so a terminal gets the exact control character asked for.
- Not changed: the viewer keystroke path still uses US positions.
- Risk and rollback: one `UCKeyTranslate` pass over 51 keys per chord. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: unit tests on layer rows dumped from real macOS 26 layouts (U.S., French, German, Russian, Dvorak - QWERTY Command, Hungarian, Lithuanian), covering AZERTY, QWERTZ, the Command and Control layers, digits, the US fallback and the tie-break. Red with US codes, green after. On this branch: `cargo test -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core --lib` passes (1174 + 658), the ignored host-layout test passes, `cargo fmt --check` is clean, clippy reports nothing in `keyboard.rs`, `cargo check --workspace --tests` compiles.
- Layout coverage: the real `chord_key_code` was run on all 249 layouts installed with macOS 26, for the 26 letters, 10 digits and 11 punctuation keys with Command and with Control. Independent code checked each result against that layout's layers: 0 wrong keys; when no key of the layer types the character, the US key.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 26, French - PC layout, daemon built from this change): 12 chords to a test app that logs key events. `cmd+a` → keycode 12 (`a`), `cmd+w` → 6, `cmd+q` → 0, `cmd+z` → 13, `ctrl+a` → `^A`, `ctrl+c` → `^C` on keycode 8, `ctrl+m` → `^M` on keycode 41 (not Return), `cmd+=` → 24, `cmd+-` → 22, `cmd+,` → 46, `ctrl+1` → `1`, `cmd+1` → the 1 key. 0.37.0 sent `cmd+a` as keycode 0 (`q`).
- Known gaps or CI still required: Windows and Linux CI.

title: fix(cua-host): keep staging and production host services apart; Windows host online right after setup
body:
Fixes CUA-3512 and CUA-3513 (Linear). Found in the Windows and Linux test of the new Spaces setup on 5 Nov (CUA-3413).

**What changes for users:** setting up staging on a computer that also runs the production host no longer takes over the production host. On Windows, a computer is online as soon as setup says it was added, not after the next sign-in. If it can't come online, setup now says why instead of "Added".

## CUA-3512: one set of service names per Cua home

The Windows task, the HKCU `Run` value, the systemd unit and the launchd label were fixed constants, or derived from `CUA_HOME` alone. A staging setup (`CUA_ENV=staging`, home `~/.cua/envs/staging`) used production's names. It ended production's task, overwrote its logon entry and replaced its systemd unit. The app and the CLI also disagreed on the Linux unit name.

- New `ServiceNames` (cua-host `service.rs`): every name comes from the resolved cua home and the channel, never from environment variables read later.

  | Home | systemd | Windows task | Run value | launchd |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `~/.cua` (production) | `cua-spacesd-host` | `Cua\SpacesdHost` | `CuaSpacesdHost` | `com.trycua.spacesd.host` |
  | `~/.cua/envs/staging` | `cua-spacesd-host-staging` | `Cua\SpacesdHost-staging` | `CuaSpacesdHost-staging` | `com.trycua.spacesd.host-staging` |
  | Local's homes | `-local`, `-local-prod` | same | same | `…host.local[-prod]` |
  | any other `CUA_HOME` | the same 8-hex hash as before | | | |

  Production keeps the names it always had.
- **Never touch another home's runner.** A runner is retired, ended, replaced or deleted only when its unit, task XML or `Run` command names this home's own host folder. Windows task names are machine-wide, so another Windows user's production task can hold `Cua\SpacesdHost`. In that case this user's host uses its own logon entry.
- **Migration:** setup (also when nothing else changes), `cua host migrate` and the macOS app's launch-time service migration move a service an older build left under the old names (the unsuffixed ones, or the old `CUA_HOME` hash such as `cua-spacesd-host-e9140ee2`) onto this home's own. If a staging setup had taken production's slot, production's service is put back from production's own config.
- A staging home never takes the channel's default ports (3211/3212), so production can always start again.
- The uninstallers (NSIS, `uninstall.ps1`, `uninstall.sh`, the deb's `prerm.sh`) also remove the staging names.

## CUA-3513: start the Windows host now, and confirm it is online

- When the logon entry is used, the host is started with `cmd.exe` (the logon entry's own `/d /c … >> driver.log` line) in a console without a window. The old start ran `conhost.exe --headless` under `DETACHED_PROCESS` with closed standard handles. Headless conhost uses those handles as its pseudo-console pipes and exits at once, so nothing ran until the next sign-in.
- Setup waits up to 20 s for the host process to appear (Windows scans a new exe on its first run), then checks it stays up. It then waits, up to 45 s, until the relay reports the machine online. Otherwise it fails with the reason and the driver's last log lines. `CUA_HOST_ONLINE_WAIT_SECS=0` skips the online wait for scripted setups against a relay the driver never joins (the docker host-flow test).
- On the scheduled-task runner, stop and remove now end this home's driver as well as the task's console host. Before, the driver kept its ports, so setting up again moved to other ports and the new driver never started, and remove failed with "Access is denied".
- The staging home joins into a Windows path with a forward slash (`envs/staging`). Process and ownership checks now compare paths with one separator, case-insensitively. Before, a staging host's driver was never found by path.

## Tests

- `instance_tests` (service.rs):
  - Every home gets distinct names on every OS, and production keeps its names.
  - Old names are retired only when they run this home.
  - A real `Systemd` runner with a recording `systemctl` sets staging up next to production and never touches production's unit.
  - The same runner moves staging off production's unit after a collision.
- `the_logon_entry_starts_now_without_headless_conhost`.
- Host flow tests:
  - `setup_waits_until_the_relay_sees_the_machine_online`
  - `setup_fails_when_the_machine_never_comes_online`
  - `an_old_service_name_moves_to_the_home_own_one`
- Verified on a Windows 11 VM and an Ubuntu 24.04 VM: results are on CUA-3512 and CUA-3513.

title: fix(windows): no firewall prompt for cua and cua-spacesd, and a real publisher name
body:
Fixes CUA-3515 (Linear). Found in the Windows test of the new Spaces setup on 5 Nov (CUA-3413).

**What changes for users:** on Windows, setting up Cua no longer stops on a Windows Security prompt asking to "allow public and private networks to access this app". If Windows ever shows one for Cua, it now names the app and shows "Cua AI, Inc." as the publisher, not "Unknown".

## 1. Why there was a prompt at all

It came from the mesh (`cua-mesh`, which runs in both `cua` and `cua-spacesd`). The engine binds its IPv4 UDP socket to an ephemeral port, then binds IPv6 to the **explicit port number IPv4 was given**. That's a fixed-port bind on every address, and Windows Firewall stops and asks about it.

I measured this on a Windows 11 VM, in a standard user's desktop session, using a fresh exe path per case:

| Bind | Prompt |
|---|---|
| UDP `0.0.0.0:0` (IPv4, ephemeral), then send | no |
| UDP `[::]:0` (IPv6, ephemeral) | no |
| UDP on one address (`10.4.0.4:0`) | no |
| UDP with no bind (implicit, on send) | no |
| TCP `127.0.0.1:0` | no |
| UDP `0.0.0.0:47123` (explicit port) | **yes** |
| UDP `0.0.0.0:0`, then `[::]:<that port>` (what the mesh did) | **yes** |
| TCP `0.0.0.0:0` | **yes** |

Every mesh node asks for an ephemeral port (`listen_port` is 0 everywhere), so IPv6 now asks for 0 too. The two sockets don't need to share a port: each socket's port is already advertised on its own (`local_ports`, STUN). Direct paths need no inbound firewall rule, because both peers send first and the stateful firewall lets the replies in. The daemon's own TCP listener is loopback only, and a joined host's TCP and QUIC listeners bind loopback.

Adding firewall rules at install wouldn't help. The installer is per-user (`nsis.perMachine: false`, installed under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`) and doesn't run elevated. A rule would need a UAC prompt, which is worse than the firewall prompt.

## 2. Why the publisher said "Unknown"

The files the firewall saw are the signed ones. The rules it wrote point at the installed `…\Programs\cua-spaces\resources\native\cua.exe` and `~\.cua\host\bin\cua-spacesd.exe`, both with a valid Cua AI, Inc. Authenticode signature. There's no temp copy and no unsigned shim. The Windows Security alert doesn't read the signature, though. It takes the name from the version resource's `FileDescription` and the publisher from `CompanyName`. Neither exe had a version resource, so the alert showed the file name and "Unknown". The Electron app exe has one.

- `cua.exe` (cua-cli `build.rs`, via `embed-resource`, as cua-spacesd and cua-driver already do) and `cua-spacesd.exe` (its existing resource script, now written to `OUT_DIR` with the DPI manifest) carry `CompanyName` "Cua AI, Inc.", `FileDescription` ("Cua", "Cua Spaces background service"), `ProductName` and the crate version.
- New Windows tests read the built exe's version info back.

## Verification

On a Windows 11 VM, in a standard user's desktop session, the patched `cua` and `cua-spacesd` ran two full host setups (a scheduled-task host and a logon-entry host) with no prompt, and no firewall rules were written for them. The released `cua-spacesd` 0.12.0 in the same session still prompted, with Publisher "Unknown". Details are on CUA-3515.

title: fix(platform-macos): raise own-process windows on the AppKit main queue
body:
CUA-3309

## What

Two macOS window-raise helpers still ran AX mutations against the driver's own process from whatever thread called them:

- `ax::bindings::raise_focused_window_of_pid` (used by the key-focus guard to put the user's window back on top)
- `ax::bindings::raise_exact_window_of_pid` (used by `bring_to_front` and the SkyLight foreground-HID path)

An AX action against another process runs in that process. When the target is the driver itself (embedded host), AppKit runs `AXRaise` in-process (`NSWindow makeKeyAndOrderFront:`) on the calling thread, and window ordering only works on the main thread. `invoke_menu` already handled this by queueing its self-process focus onto the AppKit main queue.

## Change

- New `ax::main_thread::run_ax_mutation(pid, timeout, work)`. It runs `work` inline for another process or when already on the main thread. Otherwise it dispatches `work` to the main queue, waits with a bound, and cancels the queued work on timeout so a stale raise can't fire later.
- Both raise helpers go through it now. A timeout reports "not raised" (`false`), and callers already handle that.
- `invoke_menu`'s focus path uses the same helper, so its own dispatch code is gone. Its behaviour and error text stay the same.

## Tests

Unit tests in `ax::main_thread`: only own-process calls off the main thread get queued; another pid runs inline on the calling thread; an own-process call from a worker thread does not run on that worker and times out with the queued work cancelled. The cargo test harness never drains the main queue, which is what that last test relies on. The existing `embedded_menu_restore` foreground fixture still covers the `invoke_menu` path end to end.
