title: fix(cua-driver): find a macOS app by any name it ships, wherever it is installed
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `launch_app`'s schema takes an app's display name, but macOS `locate_by_name` only found an exact `<name>.app` directly inside one of six folders (its localized-name scan was listed as skipped "until we hit a non-English-name app in the wild"). Real cases that answered `APP_NOT_INSTALLED`: "Échecs" (Chess on a French Mac; the name exists only in its `InfoPlist.loctable`), Adobe InDesign 2026 (installed one folder down, `/Applications/Adobe InDesign 2026/Adobe InDesign 2026.app`), apps whose display name differs from their file name, apps a vendor nests deeper, the system's own apps (Keychain Access, Archive Utility, in `/System/Library/CoreServices`) and apps outside the application folders.
- What changed:
  - When the existing fast paths miss (and only then), `locate_by_name` takes every app installed on the Mac instead of guessing folders: the apps Spotlight has indexed (`MDQuery` on `com.apple.application-bundle`, on a worker thread that gives up after 2 s), merged with the application folders walked on disk to 4 levels and `/System/Library/CoreServices`, so a disabled or busy index still finds the usual places. Helpers inside another bundle and apps in the Trash are left out.
  - It matches every name a bundle ships: its file name, `CFBundleDisplayName`, `CFBundleName`, and their localized values from `InfoPlist.loctable` and each `.lproj/InfoPlist.strings` (legacy folder names such as `German.lproj` included).
  - The ranking lives in a new core module, `app_names`. Names compare without case (Turkish dotted and dotless i included) and canonically decomposed, since macOS stores file names decomposed, but otherwise as shipped. Forgiving how a user spells a name (accents, spaces) is left to clients.
  - An exact name beats a name the query starts; at equal rank, a name in one of the user's preferred languages wins, then the app in the best place (the application folders, then the system's apps, then anywhere else), so an installed app beats a build copy of the same name. A tie in the same place is refused as `APP_NAME_AMBIGUOUS` with the candidates; a name found only inside another stays `APP_NOT_INSTALLED` with the closest names as suggestions. Never a guess.
  - `launch_app` launches the bundle the name resolved to instead of resolving the name a second time.
  - Windows and Linux name lookup are unchanged.

## Related work

Refs: no upstream issue. Completes step 3 of `locate_by_name` ("full localized-name scan").

RFC: not required. No protocol change. One new refusal code, `APP_NAME_AMBIGUOUS`, returned only for a name that resolved to nothing before.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: any name an app ships, in any language and case, now launches it, wherever the app is installed. Names that resolved before go through the same fast paths and resolve the same way.
- New dependency: `icu_normalizer` (canonical decomposition) in `cua-driver-core`, already in the graph through `url`'s IDNA support; the `Cargo.lock` files gain its entry.
- Not covered: `list_apps` is unchanged, so an app outside the application folders launches but isn't listed.
- Risk and rollback: only on a miss, the lookup asks Spotlight (bounded to 2 s) and reads the bundles' plists; a name no app ships is refused in about 0.4 s on a Mac with ~320 apps. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: tests on fake bundles (subfolder, two folders down, outside the folders, a build copy of an installed name, a nested helper and the Trash excluded, localized and display names, legacy `.lproj`), ranking tests in `app_names` (case, decomposition, Turkish i, exact over prefix, language and place tie-breaks, ambiguity), and an exact-code test for the refusal. On this branch: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos --lib` passes (1184 + 661), `cargo fmt --check` is clean, clippy reports nothing in the touched files, `cargo check --workspace --tests` compiles.
- Installed-app check: the real scan and ranking were run over the 83 apps installed on a macOS 26 Mac. Each of the 2,783 names they ship in any language, queried as shipped, in lower and upper case, and decomposed, finds its own app: 7,934 queries, none missed or wrong.
- Synthetic apps (macOS 26, daemon built from this change): 14 minimal bundles registered with Launch Services and indexed by Spotlight, covering a vendor subfolder, two folders down, an app outside the application folders, a display name, names only in `.lproj` or `InfoPlist.loctable` (one non-Latin), a Turkish name in capitals, twins, a build copy of an installed name and a helper nested in another app. Every app is found by its shipped names; twins are refused; the build copy never wins; the helper is never launched. 0.37.0 answered 4 of those 14 queries right.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Windows and Linux CI (no change there).

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): record released sources pinned to another Hyprland as unsupported
body:
CUA-3472, tracking #5751.

## Why the nightly is red

Run 41982437664 failed `arch hyprland 0.57.1-1` for plugin `cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0` and `cua-driver-rs-v0.33.2`. Both jobs did write `result.json`. The build stopped at configure:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:250 (message):
  Input is pinned to Hyprland 0.56.2
```

#6495 removed that pin on main, and main passes on 0.57.1. Every released Driver tag (v0.30.0 through v0.38.0) predates #6495, so it still refuses any Hyprland other than 0.56.2. The requalifier builds the latest tag and the tag Omarchy packages. It recorded each refusal as `fail`, retried it every night, and refiled the tracking issue, but only a new release can change the result. When the release-please PR ships v0.39.0 it will fix the latest-tag row. The v0.33.2 row, which Omarchy packages, would never go green.

## Change

- `qualify.py`: if a released source (one with a `driver_version`) fails configure with its own `Input is pinned to Hyprland X` and X is not the header version, the build is `unsupported` and gives the reason. main still fails on any configure error. A release that refuses its own pinned version still fails too.
- `channels.py`: `unsupported` is final for that (Hyprland build, tree), like `pass`, so it is not rebuilt nightly. It is not final when main has the same tree, so main's configure result is always rebuilt and reported. `--force` still rebuilds it.
- `manifest.py`: the matrix shows `unsupported`. It is not a tracking-issue failure.
- `COMPAT-BRANCH.md`: the status table documents `unsupported`.

The Omarchy edge finding stays. Its packaged `cua-hyprland-plugin 0.33.2-4` pins Hyprland 0.56.2-4, but the channel now ships 0.57.1-1. That is real and needs an Omarchy rebuild, so the issue stays open for that reason alone.

## Proof

- The scoped repository checks: the requalify unit and dry-run suite (`test_requalify.py`), including three new tests. One covers the unsupported classification and its limits. One checks that an unsupported row is not an issue and is not replanned. One checks that an unsupported tree main also builds is still replanned.
- Replayed this run's downloaded artifacts through the new code. Both tag rows become `unsupported`. The merged manifest leaves one problem, the Omarchy edge pin. Planning against the new manifest schedules no rebuilds.
- Not run here: the containerised Arch build and headless session. This PR's `pull_request` trigger of the requalify workflow covers them in dry-run.

title: fix(cua-driver): return from a trusted browser click when its handler opens a dialog
body:
CUA-3308. Follow-up of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5621, which fixed this for `input_route="dom_event"`.

## Problem

A trusted `browser_click` (the default route, `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, at coordinates or at a ref's box) whose page handler opens `alert()`, `confirm()` or `prompt()` waited out two 20 s CDP call timeouts. It then refused with `browser_input_trust_unavailable`, even though the click had landed.

On headless Chrome 156, once `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` fires, Chrome does not answer the mouse event that opened the dialog, or a later `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled`, until the dialog is handled. It then answers both and applies them in order. A mousedown handler blocks the `mousePressed` reply the same way, but Chrome still accepts and answers `mouseReleased`.

## Change

- The dom_event route's race against the tab's dialog state moves into `call_until_dialog`. Each trusted mouse event now goes through it too.
- When a dialog opened during the click, the focus-emulation cleanup is sent without waiting for its reply. The blocked renderer applies it once the dialog closes.
- The click still sends `mouseReleased` after a mousedown dialog, so the page is not left with the button held.
- The trusted result carries the same `dialog` block (`present`, `kind`, `dialog_id`) and `escalation` hint as the dom_event route. The tool description and the generated docs say this holds on either route.

## Proof

`trusted_coordinate_click_returns_when_its_handler_opens_a_dialog` drives the mock CDP endpoint, which now blocks input and emulation commands the way Chrome does once a dialog is open. The test covers a dialog opened on `mouseReleased` and one opened on `mousePressed`. It checks that the call returns promptly with the dialog block, that both mouse events went out, that focus emulation was switched off last, and that `browser_dialog` can then accept the dialog. Before the fix it failed after 40 s. Without the release fix it failed on the missing `mouseReleased`.

The scoped repository checks are listed in the verification comment.

title: fix(spacesd): volume attach no longer deadlocks a 1 vCPU Space
body:
## Problem

A new local Space on a 1 vCPU / 1 GB container (the size the Spaces app gives a new agent home) comes up Running, but its cua-spacesd stops answering a few seconds later. TCP connects succeed, nothing replies: healthz hangs, the first agent dispatch times out ("http2 error (operation timed out)"), and the Space still reads Running because the ready probe only checks that the port listens.

## Cause

With one vCPU the cua-spacesd tokio runtime has one worker. Volume attach (`attach_volume`, `mount`) did blocking filesystem calls on that worker: `default_mount_path` stats `/volume`, and `mount` runs `create_dir_all` on it. When `/volume` is already a live FUSE mount (an agent's volume attach, a re-attach), the FUSE helper answers the stat by dialling the volume listener that this same runtime serves. The worker waits for a task only that worker could run, so the server keeps accepting connections and never answers.

Reproduced on a fresh `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim` Space with 1 CPU: `cua agent add NAME --harness openai-codex --in local:SPACE "hi"` made healthz go from 200 in 0.6 ms to a hang within 3 s, the tokio worker's CPU time stopped advancing, and `ls /volume` hung. The same steps with 2 CPUs stayed healthy.

## Fix

- `default_mount_path`, the mount-point `create_dir_all` and the post-unmount `remove_dir` now run on the blocking pool.
- The persistent-agents supervisor logged the same "Space is Stopped" error for every agent on every pass (about 9 lines a second, ~1600 per 3 minutes with 9 stopped Spaces). Each distinct error is now logged once per five minutes.

## Second cause (found with a sandbox stack dump, `runsc debug --stacks`)

In a hung 1 vCPU Space the only blocked guest syscall is `close()` of a file under `/volume`, waiting for the FUSE helper, whose answer needs the volume listener served by the same runtime. The close ran on the only async worker: `AtomicWriter` dropped its `tokio::fs::File` there (`finish`, `abort`) and `ReadFile` dropped its file at the end of the read task. `cua agent add --harness openai-codex` writes the codex config under the mounted home (`/volume/agents/<name>`), so it hit this every time; claude-code writes nothing there. Fixes: `OffWorker` closes on the blocking pool, MakeDir / bulk-read open / xattr calls run on blocking threads, and cua-spacesd runs at least two async workers.

## Proof (isolated home, mock model endpoint, `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim`, codex `agent add`)

Runtime VM capped at 2 vCPU / 5 GiB. cua-spacesd from this branch (two-worker default), host built from this branch.

| | shipped 0.12.0 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 CPU / 1 GB, `agent add` | hangs: healthz times out 3 s after, `ls /volume` hangs | returns in 14 s; healthz 200 in under 3 ms and `ls /volume` ok on all 14 samples over 42 s |
| first request | never | `POST /v1/responses` reaches the mock |
| codex SQLite | n/a | `~/.cua/agents/codex-state/<name>/*.sqlite` ; nothing under `/volume/agents` |
| 2 CPU / 2 GB | healthy, codex exits `failed to initialize sqlite state runtime under /volume/agents/<name>.codex-sqlite` | returns in 9 s, healthz and `ls /volume` ok, requests reach the mock, SQLite under `codex-state` |

With one worker kept (targeted fixes only, no two-worker default) the 1 CPU Space also stayed healthy, so the closes were the cause and the second worker is the safety net.

The hang was found with `runsc debug --stacks` on the hung Space: the only blocked guest syscall was `close()` of a file under `/volume`.

## Tests

- `blocking_mount_work_leaves_the_only_worker_free` (cua-spacesd-server): a single-worker runtime where the "filesystem call" is answered by a task of the same runtime; it deadlocks (10 s timeout) if the call runs on the worker.
- `the_default_mount_path_is_the_blocking_one`.
- `a_dropped_value_is_closed_off_the_only_worker`, `close_waits_for_the_drop_off_the_only_worker` (single-worker runtime, drop that needs the runtime).
- `codex_sqlite_state_is_off_the_volume` (extended for `/volume/agents/<name>`).
- `a_repeated_supervisor_error_is_logged_once_per_window` (cua-spaces-ext).

`bin/ci --base d00a5bc003 --fix`: fmt, clippy (both crates), SPDX and image-ref checks pass; the unit-test stage was stopped by the local disk guard (target dir over 15 GB), so the full unit tests and the Windows cross-check run in CI. The three new tests were run locally and pass. No local-ci status posted.

The fix ships in cua-spacesd, so existing images need the usual image rebuild to pick it up.

title: perf(pool): a home claims the warm Space that serves it
body:
## What

With the `warm-pools` experiment on, a home Space (1 CPU, 1 GB, headless, labelled) never claimed the prepared warm Space (2 CPU, 4 GB desktop) because the pool matched creates by exact shape. Every home was cold-created and paid the in-Space agent install.

A create now claims a warm member of the experiment's source when that member serves it: same image, backend, runtime, network and probes; at least the requested CPUs and memory; a desktop wherever a desktop is asked for (a headless create runs fine on a desktop member, not the reverse). The smallest serving member goes first, the member's own shape refills, and a create can wait for a starting member of such a shape as before. Plain `pool.warm` and policy pools are unchanged (exact shape only). The pool stays at one member, so memory and disk stay bounded; nothing changes with the experiment off.

## Tests

- `a_home_claims_the_bigger_warm_space_and_only_that`: home-shaped create claims the 2 CPU/4 GB member in under 1 s (fake runtime), a bigger request does not, the member is refilled.
- `a_headless_member_does_not_serve_a_desktop_create_nor_a_plain_pool_a_home`.
- All 48 `pool::` tests pass.

## Measured on a real build

Own `CUA_HOME` and daemon, the built-in Linux runtime, `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim` at 1 CPU / 1 GB, `warm-pools` on, claude-code pointed at a local mock model server (`cua-mock-llm`), time until the mock receives its first request (arm64 Mac, debug build):

| path | create | create done to first model request | total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cold (experiment off) | 3.1 s | 30.2 s | 33.3 s |
| warm claim (this PR) | 1.1 s (claim 62 ms) | 0.62 s | 1.7 s |

Before the change a warm member was ready and the 1 CPU / 1 GB create still missed it. The first miss was the size; the second was the readiness check: a real create waits on a TCP probe for cua-spacesd, the member is checked over HTTP, and that stricter check now covers it (`probes_covered`). The 0.62 s is the agent start on the claimed Space with its tools already installed; the 30 s cold path is the in-Space install.

Caveat: the claimed home runs on the 2 CPU / 4 GB member as it is.

Baking node and the agent tools into slim is not proposed: node 24 alone is about 30 MB compressed and roughly 200 MB unpacked, against about 80 MB of headroom under the 1.55 GB gate on arm64.

title: ci-gate: wait for a late local-ci sign-off, fail fast on a failed one
body:
Makes a green `local-ci` sign-off the only way an agent PR merges, without stalling PRs. Behaviour is unchanged until the repository variable `REQUIRE_LOCAL_CI` is set to `true` (not set here).

Why: the sign-off comes from a serial Mac CI runner and takes 20-40 minutes (longer when queued). The gate used to poll for 5 minutes, before waiting for the other workflows, so a sign-off arriving later than that blocked the PR.

What changes in `ci-gate.yml`:
- The early step now looks once, without waiting. A `failure` or `error` fails the gate immediately. It also decides whether the PR is an agent PR (same rules as before: `cua-agents[bot]`, label `agent`, or an `agent/` branch of this repo) and hands the head SHA to the last step. Community PRs are exempt.
- A new last step, after "Wait for every other workflow", waits for the sign-off (bounded at 75 minutes, one check a minute). It succeeds on `success`, fails at once on `failure`/`error`, and fails with the usual message on timeout. Report-only mode still looks once and warns.
- Re-triggering on the `status` event was considered and rejected: `status` workflows run on the default branch, not on the PR, so they would not update the required `ci-gate` check on the PR. Waiting inside the single `ci-gate` run keeps one check that auto-merge sees, and the run's 180-minute timeout covers 75 minutes of waiting after the other workflows. If a sign-off still arrives later than that, re-running `ci-gate` picks it up.
- Merge queue: the same steps run for `merge_group`; the PR head SHA already has its status by then, so it passes on the first look.

Checks run: `bin/ci --quick --fix` (actionlint, workflow sync, others) green. User impact: none yet; once the switch is on, agent PRs merge as soon as their Mac CI sign-off is green, however late it lands.

title: Fix flaky ETXTBSY in cua-agent-setup tests

title: fix(spaces): open picked-up agent chats from the end of their file (CUA-3548)
body:
Picking up a Claude Code, Codex or Hermes chat from "Pick up where you left off" no longer freezes Cua Spaces Local, even for chats of hundreds of megabytes.

Linear: CUA-3548

**Root cause.** Opening a picked chat called `agent_thread_read`, which read the agent's whole file line by line and kept every message in memory before cutting to the newest 200. Francesco's real history has 9,000+ chats and files up to 400 MB. The page then asked for 200 messages at once.

**Fix.**
- `cua-agent-threads`: history reads from the end of the file (`lines::rev_each`) within a 16 MiB / 2 s budget and stops as soon as it has enough messages. Hermes uses `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT`. Listing was already metadata plus head and tail only.
- `earlier_omitted` is now "at least N" when older messages were left unread.
- Home: the chat opens on its newest 30 messages; "Show earlier messages" loads 100 more.

**Timings** (release build, warm cache, synthetic fixture: 300 chats, 6 of about 150 MB, example `measure`):
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| history, 150 MB chat | 94 ms, whole file read | 12 ms, 16 MiB at most |
| history, real 418 MB chat (Francesco's history) | 913 ms | 372 ms (a second 396 MB chat: 711 ms to 61 ms) |
| list 4 / 50 chats | 4 ms / 20 ms | 4 ms / 20 ms |

**Tests.** Unit tests for `rev_each` (order across chunk edges, early stop, byte budget, over-long lines), a history test that pins the bytes read on a 70+ MB chat, a listing test with 300 chats and 300 MB files, and a web test for the first view and "Show earlier messages".

title: fix(cua-spaces): publish running Spaces on the relay after a late cua-spacesd
body:
## Problem
Running local Spaces vanished from the phone after a container runtime restart and never came back. The daemon logged `does not support relay_attach ... image runs no cua-spacesd` 20 times in 5 s, then nothing more.

## Root cause
- A local Space whose runtime had not published the cua-spacesd port yet was connected as "no spacesd" with no retry marker, so it was cached and treated as unsupported for good. A Space whose spacesd answered slowly got the same message.
- The re-attach after a boot made a single attempt and gave up.
- The publish pass marked a pass "finished" while a Space was waiting for its retry, so it rested until the 5-minute verify.
- Rows were registered without `host`, so the phone treated them as "runs on its own" and could not read their thread.

## Fix
- A local Space the registry knows runs cua-spacesd is "still waking" (`SpacesdNotAvailable`), never unsupported. Its connection is dialed again. Images with no spacesd keep the existing message.
- Re-attach after a boot retries in the background: one task per Space, doubling pauses, bounded to about 3 minutes.
- The publish pass retries a waking Space after 10 s (60 s for other failures) and does not settle while a retry is pending.
- Rows the computer registers for its own Spaces name this computer as `host`. The pass also re-registers an online row that lacks it. The host serves the thread of a Space it registered itself.

## Tests
Fake runtime and fake relay in `cua-spaces/tests/relay_publish.rs`: late spacesd ends up listed with paced retries, a waking Space is not "unsupported", rows carry the host id and an old hostless row is repaired. Not covered: the in-guest boot path itself (the fake runtime cannot power off), and a real VM.

`bin/ci --quick` passes; heavy checks go to CI.

title: ci: retry apt and fall back to archive.debian.org when snapshot.debian.org fails
body:
Impact: release and bootstrap builds in Debian 11 containers no longer fail when snapshot.debian.org has a 503/504 or 404 outage.

## What failed
5 Nov 2026: nightly cua-driver linux-x86_64 (run 41967274244, 504 on `pkg-config`) and "Debian 11 bootstrap (arm64)" on #6578 (run 42089055198, 504 then "503 No healthy backends"). #6567 only retried tool downloads, not apt.

## Where apt hits a pinned mirror
- `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml` (build-linux, also what the bootstrap CI job runs): snapshot pin 20260901T000000Z.
- `cd-cua-sdk.yml` (linux containers): same pin.
- `libs/cua-spacesd/packaging/release/debian-build-deps.sh` (cd-cua-spacesd, build-linux-docker.sh): live mirror with an archive.debian.org fallback already.
No Dockerfiles or image builds use a pinned Debian mirror (they use their base image's default sources).

## Changes
- Shared retry policy in `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-cua-retries`: `Acquire::Retries "5"`, 30s http/https timeouts. Both pre-checkout bootstraps and the spacesd script write it. The bootstraps run before checkout, so they cannot source a repo file; the block is identical in both workflows.
- APT retries have no backoff, so the shell also retries `update` and `install` 3 times, waiting 20s then 40s. The old driver step had `Acquire::Retries=5` and still failed on a sustained outage.
- Fallback: if the snapshot still fails, clear the lists and use archive.debian.org bullseye, bullseye-updates and bullseye-security. The mirror used is logged ("apt mirror used: ...") and the fallback emits a `::warning::` annotation. The sdk's NodeSource `nodejs` install also gets the retry wrapper.
- `debian-build-deps.sh` now logs which mirror was used and writes the shared snippet.
- `test_driver_linux_bootstrap.py` checks the retry snippet, snapshot-first ordering, the fallback and the package set.

## Pinning
Snapshot stays primary, with the same date pin and `signed-by` keyring. The fallback does not weaken the versions: bullseye is end-of-life, so archive.debian.org holds the same final package set the pin froze, and APT still verifies signatures and hashes. The only relaxation is `check-valid-until=no` on the archive sources (their Release files are past Valid-Until by design); the test limits it to exactly those three lines. deb.debian.org is not used for Debian 11 because its bullseye-security pool 404s.

## Tested
Ran the driver bootstrap in `debian:11` (arm64). snapshot.debian.org was returning 404s on .debs at the time, which exercised the full path: two backoff retries, the warning, fallback to archive.debian.org, install success. `bin/ci --quick --fix` is green.

title: fix(spaces-web): stop the first run and Settings jumping between steps and tabs (CUA-3554)
body:
Fixes [CUA-3554](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3554/spaces-first-run-and-settings-jump-when-you-switch-steps-or-tabs). Related: #6580 (footer, step dots; merged, this PR is rebased on it) and #6579 (permissions step).

**For users:** when you move through the new setup's steps, the headline, the button, the logo and the step dots no longer move. When you switch Settings tabs in the Mac app, the tabs and the content no longer move sideways.

## Causes (measured, not guessed)

I measured each anchor's bounding box in the browser demo (Playwright, WebKit and Chromium) at 1000x640, 1180x820 and 1440x900.

- **First run.** Each step was centred vertically, so a taller step pushed the headline up and the button down. The header also lost 4 px on steps without Skip for now. On steps without dots, the space where the dots go was 4 to 6 px shorter, so the area above it changed height too.
- **Settings.** `Page` relies on `scrollbar-gutter: stable`. But the app styles its scrollbars (`::-webkit-scrollbar`, 10 px), and WebKit (the Mac app's web view) reserves no gutter for a styled scrollbar. So a tab that scrolls was 10 px narrower than one that doesn't, and the centred column moved 5 px. Chromium does reserve the gutter, which is why the existing `settings-tab-layout` spec never caught it.

## Fix (layout components only)

- **First-run shell** (`NewFirstRun`): every step now starts at the same height under the header, and the screen fills the content area.
  - A shared `Actions` row holds each screen's buttons. It uses `mt-auto` plus `sticky bottom-0`, so it sits at the bottom of the area on every step. Long content scrolls above it.
  - The header has a fixed height. The dots' row keeps a fixed height when a step has no dots.
  - #6580's `useFadeUnder` now runs once for the whole page instead of only on the Where step. On any step that overflows, the content fades out above the buttons. The row still has no background, so the stars and keys show through.
- **Agent step**: Continue now shows (disabled) while the app is still looking for agents, so it no longer pops in. On the install state, the note sits above the buttons, so Install lines up with Continue on the other steps.
- **Scrollers**: a new `scroll-y-stable` utility (`overflow-y: scroll`, with the gutter kept as well) replaces `overflow-y-auto [scrollbar-gutter:stable]` in `Page`, the Home page and the All agents page. The track is transparent, so a page that doesn't scroll shows nothing there. This fixes the whole class of problem, not just Settings.

## Movement, before → after (WebKit, px, relative to the first step)

Before is origin/main with #6580. Negative means up, positive means down.

| 1180x820 | logo | headline top | primary button top |
|---|---|---|---|
| Welcome | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Sign-in | 0 → 0 | −14 → 0 | +20 → 0 |
| Where | 0 → 0 | −158 → 0 | +217 → 0 |
| Agent | 0 → 0 | −81 → 0 | +113 → 0 |
| Ready | −4 → 0 | −123 → 0 | +166 → 0 |
| Next | −4 → 0 | −62 → 0 | +81 → 0 |

Largest swing per window size:

| Window | headline (before → after) | primary (before → after) | logo | dots row |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000x640 | 107 → 0 | 143 → 0 | 4 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| 1180x820 | 159 → 0 | 219 → 0 | 4 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| 1440x900 | 182 → 0 | 242 → 0 | 4 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

Settings: heading, tab bar and content left edge (px, relative to Account):

| Window | General | Connections | Advanced | About |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000x640 (every tab scrolls) | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| 1180x820 | −5 → 0 | −5 → 0 | −5 → 0 | −5 → 0 |
| 1440x900 | −5 → 0 | −5 → 0 | −5 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

## Regression test

`e2e/layout-anchors.spec.ts` runs in `pnpm parity` at all three sizes:

- It walks every first-run step: Welcome, Sign-in (with the `signin-wait` demo flag), Where, Agent, Ready and Next.
- It switches through every Settings tab.
- It asserts that the logo, headline top, dots row, primary button, Settings heading, tab bar and content stay within 1 px.
- It turns off `scrollbar-gutter` on the Settings pass, so Chromium sees the page the way WebKit does. With the old `Page`, it fails at 1180x820 and 1440x900.

When #6579 lands, its permissions step should use `Actions` for its button row. Once the step is in the walk, this test will catch it if it doesn't.

## Checks

- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: green.
- `vitest`: 223 files and 1574 tests pass.
- `pnpm parity` (browser): 60 passed, 17 skipped.

title: feat(spaces): Local dev builds keep agent keys in a private file without the Keychain; install-local.sh signs with its own Keychain
body:
## What

Makes the Local channel (Cua Spaces Local) usable for end-to-end development without the Keychain or CI signing.

**A. Agent keys and sign-ins without the Keychain, Local only.** `CuaChannel::allows_insecure_dev_store()` is true only for `Local`. When the vault is unavailable (an ad hoc signed build), `AgentKeys::new_for` keeps keys in a 0600 file `~/.cua-local/agent-keys` instead of refusing, and `agent_keys.list` reports an `insecure` warning. Settings > Connections shows it in the existing notice ("Keychain not available in this development build: keys are stored unencrypted in ~/.cua-local/agent-keys. Do not use real production secrets.") while the buttons stay on, so importing the existing Claude Code / Codex logins works as in the released app. `cua agent keys` and `cua connections` print it as a warning. Stable keeps refusing with the same words (tests cover both channels and the Keychain stand-in).

New optional `warning` field on `AgentKeysInput` (generated FFI, Swift, web and desktop bridges updated by hand to match the generator output; parity flow and golden-free case added to `parity/agent-keys.json`).

**B. `install-local.sh` signs with a Keychain it owns.** The stable local certificate now lives in `~/Library/Keychains/cua-spaces-local-signing.keychain-db` (empty password, created and unlocked by the script, key opened to codesign without a prompt). Nothing is written to the login Keychain or the search list. An existing certificate in the login Keychain or Cua Driver's Keychain is still reused so grants survive. macOS still needs one trust prompt for a new certificate (`--setup-signing`); until then the app is signed ad hoc and the script says why in one line with the command to run (including a locked login Keychain in an SSH session). `CUA_LOCAL_SIGNING_OWN_KEYCHAIN=0` turns it off.

## Not in this PR
No change to onboarding, Labs, Machines UI or the chat sign-in flow. No file touched by #6576, #6577, #6579, #6580, #6557, #6558, #6578. Small generated-file hunks (`cua_spaces_ffi.ts`, `bridge-shapes.json`) may need a regenerate after #6547 / #6579 merge.

## Checks
`bin/ci --quick --fix` green; `scripts/tests/install-local-test.sh` all 293+ checks pass (new: own Keychain, login Keychain untouched). Rust, Swift and wasm suites run in CI. UI: draft until the owner has seen screenshots of the warning.

title: Spaces: one list of your computers, and the new first run and Home by default (CUA-3551)
body:
> **Do not merge yet.** The Linux run passed (6 Nov, on this branch's web UI and app code). This lands once the macOS and Windows runs pass too; auto-merge is queued only then.

Linear: CUA-3551

## What changes for people

Machines and Spaces are now one list, called **Computers**. It shows every computer you added, with the Spaces made on each one underneath. The separate Machines page is gone, and Cua Driver is now a setting on This Mac's page instead of its own sidebar item.

Everyone now gets the new first run and opens on the new Home, on macOS, Windows and Linux. The "Try the new Home" and "Try the new setup" switches leave Labs.

## What's in it

1. **One view.** The list of your computers and their Spaces (the tree from #6508 and #6546) is the only view of `/spaces`, with no Labs switch. The old grid and the Machines page are deleted, along with their route, the `nav.machines` command (⌘2) and the code that only they used. Agents is now ⌘2 and Keyvault ⌘3, in the web UI and the Mac menu.
   - Clicking a computer opens its own page at `/spaces/computer/<id>`. That page holds the switches, issues, Spaces (with their disk size on This Mac), New Space here, Details, trust, recent access, Rename and Remove. Clouds have their own page at `/spaces/cloud/<id>`.
   - Everything else the Machines page had now sits around the list: computers waiting to be added (with the count on the sidebar item), the clouds and Connect a cloud, "Also signed in" for sign-ins that aren't computers, Remove old computers on the offline row, the low-disk warning, the page tip and the upsell line.
   - The list also gained a few things the grid used to show: New Space in the header, the step and progress of a Space being made (on this computer or another), Pin to notch, and the Home tag. "Reaching N computers…" now shows while computers are still answering.
   - **Old links still work.** `/machines`, `/machines?add=1` and `/machines?join=<code>&relay=…` (including `cua://add` links from older apps) open the list with Add a computer open. `/machines?machine=<id>` opens that computer's page. `/settings/devices` opens This Mac's page. `/driver` and `/driver?machine=<id>` open Cua Driver under the right computer. The Electron and Mac shells now route deep links, notifications and Add a computer to the new addresses directly.
2. **Cua Driver under This Mac.** It's a "Cua Driver" row on This Mac's page that opens `/spaces/computer/this-mac/driver`, with a back link to This Mac. As before, it shows only where this Cua Spaces carries the driver. The command palette still finds it by name.
3. **One word.** The copy now says "computer" everywhere and keeps "Space" for the separate computers Cua makes. This covers the nav, page titles, empty states, onboarding, the palette, the Add a computer sheet, Settings, and the core strings these pages show (the computer page, trust and approvals, the host switches, the checklist, the tips and the "This computer" label on Linux). Parity goldens are regenerated. Cloud sizes ("Largest machine") are left alone, since they describe cloud machines.
4. **`spaces_tree` is gone.** The flag only ever existed in the web app: there was no Rust, FFI, Swift, Electron or telemetry mirror to remove. I deleted it from `flags.ts`, the bridge exports and the Labs list, and a stored override is cleared on start (`RETIRED_FLAGS`). Home's tree-based "in" picker, which only ran behind this flag, is removed too. Home keeps the This Mac picker from #6580, so it doesn't change for anyone. The default Space stays in Settings and in the list, because MCP and CLI tasks still use it. The FFI and Swift bindings were regenerated with the repo generators and came out unchanged.

5. **The new first run and the new Home are the defaults** (0.21.1). `spaces_ask_first_home` and `spaces_new_onboarding` are deleted with their off paths, as `upsell_cards` was in #6547.
   - Old settings still load: a stored override of either flag, or of `spaces_tree`, is cleared on start. `flags.ts` now only holds that clean-up.
   - The old first run page and its bridge hook (`useFirstRun`) are deleted, with their unit tests and the two e2e specs for its screens. The app core's `firstRun.*` view code stays for now: Settings still uses its CLI view, and removing the rest is a follow-up.
   - Home is first in the nav and `/` opens it. "Ask before a task uses This computer" moves from Labs to a Home group in Settings, Advanced.
   - The new first run sends the onboarding funnel events the old one sent (start, each screen viewed, skipped, finished), on the existing schema. Without this, the funnel would have gone dark.
   - The first Linux Space is prepared after a first run only when that run happened on this install. Someone who set up with an older app and updates doesn't get a Space they didn't ask for.
   - The Mac-only steps (permissions, Cua Driver) stay Mac-only in the new first run, as before. Electron gets the same defaults, because they live in the shared web UI.
6. **Layout shift.** Turning the new Home on by default made the parity layout-shift check measure it for the first time. Home now draws once its lists have loaded (at most 0.8 s), so the welcome no longer turns into the lists and the agents no longer push the Spaces down (0.13 to 0.0004). In Settings, General, the default Space group moves to the end of the tab, so its late arrival moves nothing (0.107 to 0.03).

7. **Setup gaps, option B** (decided 6 Nov).
   - The first setup screen says what usage data Cua collects, links "What is collected", and has a switch to turn it off. The hosts already hold every usage event until the run leaves this screen, so the choice comes before anything is sent. When the environment decides (Do Not Track, CI), the switch is greyed and says who set it.
   - "Now bring the rest in" gets **Use Cua from Terminal** as its last row, only where this app carries the `cua` command and it isn't installed yet. It opens in place with Install, then the line to try.
8. **After the rebase onto main.**
   - No hidden Linux Space: main's #6662 (CUA-3622) is kept, so a Space is made only when someone asks for one. The tests that relied on the old warm-up stay deleted.
   - The computer page carries main's Machines fixes: it trusts the relay's online answer and re-reads every 30 s (#6637), and "Use a code from another computer" opens Enter a code (#6710). The refusal message now says "go to Computers and click Add a computer".
   - From the Linux run: Skip for now lands on Home (it went to the Computers list), and New Space's hint for adding another computer says "install Cua Spaces on it and sign in" instead of naming a switch that is gone.

## Tests

- Vitest: 1496 passed, 1 skipped (after the rebase and the setup-gap changes).
  - `first-run-new.test.tsx`: the usage line, its switch, the locked case and the link; `settings.set` on the real route while the run stays on screen 1; the Terminal row only where the command is missing; Install on the real route.
  - `computers-merge.test.tsx`: This Mac's page offers a code from another computer and opens Enter a code. `computers-page.test.tsx`: the list and the computer page follow the relay's offline answer.
  - `retired-flags.test.ts` checks that leftover overrides of every retired flag are cleared. `prepare-launch.test.tsx` checks that an updated install makes no Space.
  - New `computers-merge.test.tsx` covers the redirects (`/machines`, `?join`, `?machine`, `/settings/devices`, `/driver`), Cua Driver on This Mac's page (and missing on other computers and on hosts without the driver), and the back link.
  - `spaces-tree.test.tsx` checks that the list is the only view, that the nav has no Machines or Cua Driver, that a stored `spaces_tree` override is cleared and that Labs has no switch.
  - The old Machines tests are ported to `computers-page.test.tsx` and `machines-account.test.tsx`. The grid-only tests are deleted. Tests that need a Space tile now run on Home.
- `cargo test -p cua-spaces-app-core` is green, and the parity goldens are regenerated (`UPDATE_PARITY=1`). After the rebase, the FFI mirror and the Electron and Swift bindings are regenerated.
- `pnpm perf --shift` is green: every route is under the 0.05 layout-shift budget.
- The Playwright parity flows now read the list and the computer pages instead of the Machines page.
- The Electron, Tauri and Swift tests are updated for the new routes and copy.

title: ci(spaces): retry SwiftPM binary downloads and wait for the cua-spacesd pin (CI cut 3, part 1)
body:
Part 1 of CI audit cut 3 (Linear CUA-3562): fix why the macOS main pipelines fail, before collapsing them.

Root causes, from the red main runs of 5 Nov 2026:
- 2 of 3 failures of `CD: Cua Spaces build (shadow)`: `swift build` downloads the Sparkle and Sentry binary targets from github.com releases and got `badResponseStatusCode(504)`, after a 60 to 90 minute Rust build. SwiftPM does not retry binary downloads. New action `swiftpm-resolve` resolves with 6 attempts and a growing pause before the build; used by the shadow build and the release build (`cd-cua-spaces.yml`).
- 1 of 3: a push that bumps `libs/cua-spacesd/VERSION` starts the pin check at the same moment `cd-cua-spacesd.yml` starts publishing that release, so the check failed on a release that appeared minutes later. `check_spacesd_published.sh` takes `SPACESD_WAIT_MINUTES`; the main build waits up to 30 minutes (default 0, so other callers are unchanged).
- The SwiftUI Rust slice producer is mostly green; most of its "failures" are runs replaced while pending (`cancelled`) by the one-at-a-time concurrency group. Part 2 removes that duplicate run.

Users: fewer red main builds and wasted reruns on the Spaces release path.

title: ci(rust): build Linux tests once, run in 3 shards (CUA-3560, audit cut 5)
body:
Cut 5 of the 5 Nov CI audit.

For users: Rust PR checks finish sooner, so Rust changes merge sooner.

- **Build once, run in shards.** New `rust linux build` job runs `cargo nextest archive` once (and compiles the test binaries the cargo test steps of shards 1 and 2 use, so the shared sccache entry has every unit). The three `rust linux shard N/3` jobs download the archive and run `cargo nextest run --archive-file ... --partition hash:N/3`. The same package list is archived and the same partitions run, so coverage is the same. Before, each shard compiled and linked all 176 test binaries (11 to 19 min) for 2 to 5 min of tests. Shards only restore the cache; the build job saves it.
- **Model checks to nightly.** `pool_protocol_is_safe` (254 s), `mutation_no_epoch_check_breaks_single_writer` (112 s) and `finding_stale_holder_cancels_current_attempt` (62 s) are filtered out on PR runs only. They still run on every push to main, in this workflow's nightly schedule, on a PR with `ci:full`, and on the macOS and Windows legs. A failed nightly run opens or updates one issue (`.github/actions/nightly-issue`, identical file in the other cut PRs).
- **Linker and debug info.** x86_64 Linux already links with rust-lld (rustc's default since 1.90; the toolchain is pinned at 1.97.1), so no mold or apt lld. CI test builds already set `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`, lighter than `line-tables-only` (which `libs/cua/Cargo.toml` keeps for local builds), and keeps the archive small. macOS and Windows keep their linkers: not safe to swap without a run on each OS.
- Tests updated: the workspace-coverage test now reads the archive command's `-p` list; new tests pin the build-once wiring and the filter.

Needs a first CI run to confirm: archive size, the download time, and that the tests that look for built binaries or paths work from the archive (nextest remaps the workspace to the same path). The filter was checked against nextest locally.

Expected saving: 8 to 12 min on about 35% of PRs; about 3k Linux min/week.

title: ci(spaces): one macOS producer per libs/cua tree (CI cut 3, part 2)
body:
Part 2 of CI audit cut 3 (Linear CUA-3562). Build-once pipeline from `docs/design/desktop-release-build-once-promote.md`: one producer per `libs/cua` tree hash, an alert when the cache misses on main, release restores it, the tag run promotes. Signing and notarization still happen where they do today.

What changes:
- `ci-cua-spaces-rust-slice.yml` (SwiftUI Rust slice producer) and `cd-cua-spaces-natives-main.yml` (natives warm-up) lose their push triggers and become `workflow_call` stages. They no longer run beside the main build and compile the same crates at the same time.

title: ci: scope relay e2e (docker) to the relay, shard it, retry timing flakes (CUA-3558 #6)
body:
Cut #6 of the CI audit (Linear CUA-3558).

**What changes for contributors:** PRs that do not touch the relay or its dependencies no longer wait for `relay e2e (docker)`. When it does run, it finishes sooner and fails less.

**Scope (uses the package graph to start the job).** `ci_component_scope.py relay-e2e` loads `ci_graph.py` and starts the lane only if a changed file is in the dependency closure of `cua-relay`, `cua-spacesd`, `cua-spacesd-server`, `-socks`, `-teleport` and `tests/teleport-e2e` (macOS and Windows platform crates excluded, the lane is Linux). Pushes, release PRs, shared inputs (lockfiles, workflows, scope scripts) and unknown spacesd files fail closed and run it. So `cua-driver`, `cua-driver-e2e`, `cua-oidc` and similar changes skip it, while `cua-driver-core` or `cua-mesh` changes still run it, because the closure says they affect the build.

**Shards.** One parallel job per shard: `core`, `hosted`, `teleport`, `tunnel`. The old job ran them in sequence (core lane 28 to 34 min, relay lane 3 to 5 min). Reuse by tree still works per shard.

**Why it failed 32% of the time.** In the 40 most recent failing runs of this workflow, all 18 failures of this job were in the `linux-core-tests.sh` step, and every one was a timing test: `reconnect_storm` (4), `churn_bounded`, `share_links`, `pending_deletions`, `conformance::a_failing_health_check_restarts_a_service`, and `mesh_gang` (6, same assertion for four PRs in a row, then gone). This was the only Linux test lane that ran plain `cargo test` with no retry; the ubuntu `test` job and every other lane use nextest with the CI profile (one retry, flaky reporting). The shards now run under nextest with that profile, copy the JUnit files out, and report through `flaky.py`, so a test that passes only on the retry shows in the weekly flaky issue instead of failing the PR.

**Not done:** the compile still happens once per shard (no shared build cache between jobs). Cut #5 (build once with `cargo nextest archive`) would remove that.

Expected saving: wall time on the PRs that run it drops from about 34 min to about 22 to 25 min (the longest shard), and the lane is skipped on driver-only and other out-of-closure PRs. Linux minutes per run go up (four compiles); fewer runs bring the total down.

Tests: `.github/scripts/tests/test_ci_component_scope.py` (new relay cases), actionlint, `bin/ci --quick`.

title: ci(cua-driver): quick desktop E2E lane on PRs, full suite after merge and at release

title: fix(cua-cli): bound process start and Space lookup so a silent relay stream fails instead of hanging
body:
CUA-3541

`cua do shell` could hang forever when a relay stream went silent. Nothing put a deadline on the process start (the client waited for `ProcessStart` with no bound) or on finding and dialing the Space. Now both are bounded, and a silent link fails with a timeout error.

**Change**

- `cua-spacesd-client`: `start` waits at most `PROCESS_START_DEADLINE` (30s) for the first message on `StartProcess`, then returns `Error::Timeout`. The deadline is the new `ConnectOptions::start_timeout`, so tests and callers can change it. It covers the start only: once the process has started, the existing keepalive liveness check and the command's own timeout apply as before. This covers `run` and `spawn`, so `cua do shell`, `cua sb exec` and the interactive PTY path are all bounded.
- `cua-cli`: `env_of` limits the relay Space lookup (resolve plus the bounded `RELAY_START_WAIT` retry) and the `space_for` lookup to `SPACE_LOOKUP_DEADLINE` (60s). After that it returns `timed out: <space> did not answer within 60s; check that it is online: cua spaces ls`. The 60s budget is longer than `RELAY_START_WAIT` (30s), so a Space that is still starting still says so first.
- Mock spacesd: a new `silent_start` flag accepts `StartProcess` and never answers.
- Docs: the generated `cua-spacesd-client` Rust reference now lists `start_timeout` and `PROCESS_START_DEADLINE`.

**Tests**

- `a_silent_start_times_out` (native gRPC and gRPC-Web): `run` and `spawn` against a silent start both return `Error::Timeout`, and the next start that does get a reply finishes normally. With the deadline taken out, the test hangs until the per-test watchdog fails it.
- `a_space_lookup_that_never_answers_times_out_with_its_name`: a lookup that never resolves gives a `Timeout` naming the Space, and an error that arrives in time is passed through unchanged.

**Proof**

The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `cua-spacesd-client` (with `testing`) and `cua-cli`, run with the stack size CI uses. The cua-rust reference check is clean. All passed. The verify-cua-spaces journey only runs on Linux and was not run.

title: ci: per-file test times, weekly CI speed report, faster ci-gate finish (CUA-3558 #12)
body:
Cut #12 of the CI audit (Linear CUA-3558): add the measurements we lack.

**What changes for the team:** a weekly "CI speed this week" issue with the numbers the audit had to estimate, per-file test times in job summaries, and a faster `ci-gate` finish.

**Per-file test times** (`.github/scripts/flaky/timings.py`)
- Every suite wrapped by `flaky.py run` (nextest JUnit, vitest, Swift logs) now also writes a "Slowest test files" table to the job summary and uploads `timings-<suite>` (10 days) through the existing `flaky-upload` action.
- pytest: `--durations=25 --junitxml` plus the same table in `ci-test-python` (both jobs) and `ci-py-bench`.
- Swift: `swift test` in `ci-cua-sdk` (spaces-sdk-swift) and `ci-cua-microvm`, per XCTest suite. The exit code is still swift's.
- vitest: the existing flaky reporter also writes per-file durations.

**Weekly report** (`ci_weekly_report.py`, `ci-weekly-report.yml`, Mondays, same one-issue pattern as "Flaky tests this week"): push-to-green, green-to-merged, the `ci-gate` tail split into sign-off wait and other, release-PR wait, CD time per workflow, slowest test files. Dry run on the last 7 days of trycua/cua (273 merged PRs):
- push to green: median 37.8 min, p90 105.6 min
- release PRs: 16 in the week, opened to merged median 561 min
- CD: `CD: Cua Spaces natives on main` median 102 min, `CD: Cua Spaces build (shadow)` 104 min with 14 of 54 runs failed, `CD: cua SDK` 136 min

**Why `ci-gate` ended 26 min after the last check at p90.** It is not mainly a polling interval. Measured from the workflow runs of each PR's last commit, the gate finishes a median 1.9 min and p90 2.3 min after the last other workflow (n=266). The audit's 26 min came from reading check runs through the GraphQL rollup, which truncates at 80 contexts and so missed the real last check. The median 1.9 min is poll lag: the gate needed two identical listings, each up to 60 s apart. The long tail is the `local-ci` sign-off wait (2 PRs this week: 41 and 76 min), bounded at 75 min, and it will grow now that every PR needs the sign-off.
- Fix: once every run is complete, the confirming listing happens after 10 s, not a full poll interval. Expect the median 1.9 min to drop to about 0.5 min.
- The sign-off wait polls every 15 s instead of 60 s (same 75 min bound).
- What is not fixed here: the sign-off queue on the Mac runner. The report now shows it separately each week.

**Heads up.** `GET /repos/trycua/cua/actions/artifacts` answers 500 on this repository, even with `per_page=5`. `flaky.py digest` uses that call, so the weekly flaky issue may be failing silently. The new report avoids it by walking each workflow's runs.

Tests: `test_ci_weekly_report.py` (10 cases), `test_flaky.py`, gate tests, actionlint.

title: feat(cua-driver-bench): Windows port of the BenchLab tasks
body:
Linear: CUA-3563

**What changes for users:** Cua Driver Bench can now run all ten Bench v2 tasks on Windows, so results for a computer-use tool on Windows sit next to its macOS and Linux results with the same seeds, checkers and "user undisturbed" rules.

## What's in it

The seven BenchLab tasks (MB-09 to MB-11, IR-01 to IR-04) ran on macOS and Linux only. This adds a Windows port that mirrors the Linux port:

- `windows/benchlab.py`: the seven modes in wxPython, so every control is a native Win32 control (Button, Edit, ComboBox, CheckBox, list view, tooltip) that UI Automation exposes. It uses `probes/_common/benchlab_common.py` unchanged, so seeds, the state file, the event log and the checkers are identical across OSes.
- `windows/sentinel.py`: the "User activity" window and its log, in the Linux sentinel's format, read by `swift/summarize_sentinel.py` unchanged. It measures all eight A22 criteria: foreground and key focus, windows raised over the user window, lost or redirected typing, real pointer movement, clipboard changes, virtual desktop switches, dialogs on the user's app, and activation changes.
- `windows/guard.py`: the GUI-only guard on Windows. A shell, console or script host (PowerShell, cmd, Windows Terminal, wscript/cscript, mshta, WSL) started in the desktop session outside the runner's own processes, or one in front, fails and stops the trial. Tool inputs are also scanned for PowerShell, cmd and script-host commands, on top of the existing patterns.
- `launch/windows_session.py`: runs one trial end to end. It renders the brief, starts BenchLab and the sentinel, arms the sentinel, runs the agent with the guard watching, then runs the checker and writes `row.json`. `windows/oracle.py` solves each task through the GUI with real input; it is used for validation only.
- `probes/*/launch.windows.json`, and the manifest now lists Windows for all ten tasks. The README's generated table and the Windows notes are updated.
- Tests: `tests/test_windows_tools.py` runs on any OS and covers guard rules, brief, descriptors, parity of modes and events with the Linux port, and that a Windows-shaped sentinel log measures all eight criteria. `tests/test_windows_desktop.py` runs on a Windows desktop. A new CI job, `windows-desktop`, runs both on `windows-latest`.

Where Windows behaves differently is written up in the README ("Windows (the BenchLab tasks)"). In short:

- MB-09 uses a native list-view drag.
- MB-10 and MB-11 stay foreground-only, because hover and tooltips follow the real pointer on Windows too.
- BenchLab's dialogs open without activation when BenchLab is behind, so the app never raises itself over the user's window.

## Validation

On a Windows 11 VM, through the real launcher:

- The scripted oracle passes the checker of all seven tasks, with no GUI-only violation.
- A no-op agent fails the checker, and the sentinel reports all eight criteria held.
- A deliberate disturbance (focus steal, raise, pointer move, clipboard) is flagged on key focus, window raised, typing, pointer, clipboard and activation.
- One full Claude Code trial per setup (IR-02, background) ran end to end.

Locally: `pytest tests probes/tests swift/tests` (354 passed) and `tools/taskset.py check` both pass, and ruff 0.14.10 is clean.

No results are published here.

title: fix(spaces): one clean reply when an agent answers in a thread
body:
## Why

"@claude hi" posted a messy first reply: the agent's narration before its tool call ("I'll check the thread and respond. Let me get the tool schemas first.") glued to its answer with no space, a "woke up and joined" line, and a "New" divider.

## What

- Runner events of a turn are split at tool calls. The reply a thread gets (and the live row preview, and the finished notification) is only the text after the last tool call; a turn that ends right after a tool call posts its last non-empty text. Segments are never glued: `cua agent run` / `logs` still get the whole transcript, with segments separated by a blank line.
- Prompt: the home brief and the thread framing are a short rule set (final text is the one reply, nothing before a tool, greetings and answerable questions get one or two sentences and no tools, never list abilities unless asked). The ability list stays, behind "when asked or when a job needs it". The framing no longer names the thread tools, so a plain reply does not send the model looking for their schemas.
- Thread rows: "woke up and joined" is not drawn between a person's message and the agent's reply (kept for a task another agent gave); the "New" divider is not drawn for an agent's answer to the reader's own message.

## Evidence

- New `agent_one_reply` test (in-process spacesd mock, temp cua home, runner events as files). On main it posts `I'll check the thread and respond. Let me get the tool schemas first.Hi! I'm ready to help. ...`; now `Hi! I'm ready to help. What would you like me to do?`.
- Unit tests for `final_reply` / `summarize`, thread fold tests, agent-home prompt test.
- Screenshots (before/after) are in the PR thread: real web UI, thread data from the test run.

## Not covered

Whether Claude Code defers the thread tools behind ToolSearch is decided by the harness (tool count), not this repo; the framing change removes the prompt that sent the model to look for them.

title: feat(spaces): Network picker with an "Also allow" list (localhost and local network are siblings)
body:
Draft for review (UI change).

## What
In a Space's Network setting, "Allow this computer's localhost" and "Allow my local network" were radio buttons, so one looked like a superset of the other (the web ranked local network above localhost). They are siblings: each is Internet only plus one extra.

Now: the base is Internet only, No network or Custom, and under Internet only an "Also allow" list has two independent checkboxes:

- Services on this computer (with its warning and the ports field)
- Other devices on my network (with its warning)

Both can be ticked. The Details row reads "Internet only", "Internet and this computer's services", "Internet and your local network" or "Internet, this computer's services and your local network" (full text on hover when the column truncates it). A child Space can only tick an extra its parent has.

Screenshots (real web UI, demo mode, before and after): `~/projects/.cua-work/netpicker-shots/` on the author's Mac (before-*.png, after-*.png). They are not attached here.

## Model
The policy could not express both extras any other way: Custom allows cannot open the host's loopback (only the localhost preset does), so this adds one preset, `localhost+lan` (`NetworkPreset::LocalhostLan`). `localhost` and `lan` keep their meaning.

- Preset is a string on the wire (proto, SDK, MCP, settings files, saved Spaces), so no proto fields change and old files and clients keep working; `buf breaking` has nothing to flag (comments only).
- `localhost+lan` takes the ports of `localhost` (`cua network set --network localhost+lan:5432,3000`, `localhost+lan:all`; `lan+localhost` is accepted).
- Children: the meet keeps each extra only when both sides have it (localhost+lan under lan is lan; under localhost, localhost; ports intersect, and if none are shared the local network stays). Agents (MCP) still cannot open either extra.
- The web, Electron and SwiftUI word parsers take the new word. Generated bindings and docs are regenerated.

## Tests
- Rust (cua-vmm, cua-spaces): rules for both extras together, validation, words and JSON round trip including old settings files, summary and widenings, intersections both ways, VM port forwarding, agent refusal, the existing property tests now cover the new preset. `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean.
- Web vitest: picker with nothing, one box, both, No network/Custom hiding the list, child ceiling; summaries; ceiling and word functions. Full web suite passes; typecheck and design lint clean.
- Desktop and SwiftUI parser tests added; not run here (no Electron/Swift build).

Not run locally: the heavy generator checks (docs reference for cua-rust and cua-cli, Electron `--check-bindings`, Swift app binding), the hand-edited CLI and SDK reference pages, and Swift tests; CI will say.

Based on the "Internet only" label fix in #6605 (this branch contains it; it drops out when that merges).

title: [Bug]: cua-driver skill fails Agent Skills frontmatter validation
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

The cua-driver skill fails Agent Skills reference validation because its frontmatter contains an unexpected top-level `version` field.

### Reproduction

1. Get `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/SKILL.md` from the Cua repository and save it as `cua-driver/SKILL.md`.
2. Run `uvx --from 'git+https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills.git#subdirectory=skills-ref' skills-ref validate cua-driver`.

### Expected behavior

The skill passes frontmatter validation against the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).

### Actual behavior

```text
Validation failed for cua-driver:
  - Unexpected fields in frontmatter: version. Only ['allowed-tools', 'compatibility', 'description', 'license', 'metadata', 'name'] are allowed.
```

### Environment

Cua Driver 0.38.0 on macOS 27.0 (arm64). Also reproduced with the skill from Cua `main` at commit `81f3e1bb`, version 0.39.0, and `skills-ref` at commit `83021e2be457a9b6679148719c1f6074f0ad975e`.

### Evidence

The field is in [`rust/Skills/cua-driver/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/81f3e1bb/libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/SKILL.md#L4). The installed skill also caused my skill frontmatter check to fail.

### Workaround and additional context

Moving the version into `metadata` made my local frontmatter check pass. The release version checker currently looks for a top-level `version` line.

title: fix(spaces): a new message and an agent's tool calls no longer wait on a slow Space
body:
## What

A message posted to a new home reached its agent 40 to 80 s late, and Claude Code's first token came 31 s after the turn started.

Causes (measured in the Local app):
- The app posts the message in another process than the daemon's supervisor, so the in-process wake never fired. The supervisor pass itself took 30 to 60 s (sequential calls into old Spaces that do not answer), and a new member's setup, standby start, dispatch and the agent's bridge (MCP tool list, answered only at pass time, hence the 31 s) all waited on it.

## Change

- A dispatcher task looks twice a second (and on a wake): settles a new member's setup, starts its standby run, hands queued tasks to members, and reads each live session on its own task (every quarter second while the agent talks to its bridge).
- A Space that does not answer holds up only its own agent.
- Logs for standby starts and for a task waiting behind a serving member.

## Numbers (real Local app, `Hi` in a new home, warm Space claimed)

Before: delivered 39 to 79 s, session_ready +1 s, first_token +31 s. After: delivered 0.3 s, session_ready 1.95 s, first_token 4.1 s, turn_ended 4.2 s.

## Test

Existing `a_posted_task_wakes_the_supervisor_without_waiting_for_the_poll` (60 s poll) still passes by design; the cross-process path was verified in the app.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): wait for each VideoToolbox frame on macOS so encoder surfaces do not pile up
body:
On macOS, a stream whose VideoToolbox session encodes slower than ScreenCaptureKit captures queues frames inside VideoToolbox. This happens on a large display, or when several sessions share the media engine. Each queued frame holds its own encoder surface. The daemon's footprint grows with that backlog, and the viewer falls behind by the same amount.

The cause is in `macos_h264.rs`. The one-slot mailbox only drops frames that have not been submitted yet. `VTCompressionSessionEncodeFrame` returns before the frame is encoded, so the worker kept handing VideoToolbox more frames than it could finish.

The fix calls `VTCompressionSessionCompleteFrames` after each frame, which the `cua-media-codec` VideoToolbox backend already does. The mailbox now drops the frames the encoder can't keep up with, as it was meant to, and each session holds one set of encoder surfaces.

Measured on a Mac mini with a virtual 5K display and full-screen motion, streaming over QUIC:

- Sessions now hold one set of encoder surfaces each, where before they built up a large backlog of them. The daemon's footprint drops several-fold once two or more sessions run at once.
- Frame rate per session is unchanged.
- Capture-to-receive latency per session drops to a fraction of what it was.
- A single session on a 1080p display was already fine and does not change.

Test: `videotoolbox_emits_each_frame_before_the_next_is_submitted` encodes three frames and requires each one's output before the next is submitted. It fails without the fix.

CUA-3327

title: fix(cua-driver-core): gate YAML capability-manifest tests on the yaml feature
body:
CUA-3504

## Problem

`cargo test -p cua-driver-core --no-default-features` failed 16 tests in `authorization`, `batch_tools`, `consent`, `session_authorization` and `tool::runtime_isolation_tests`. Each one builds a capability manifest from YAML through `session_manifest::load_manifest`. Without the `yaml` feature that function returns "capability manifest support requires the yaml feature", so the tests panicked while setting up.

## Change

These tests exercise manifest behaviour that a build without `yaml` cannot reach. They are now gated with `#[cfg(feature = "yaml")]`, the same gate `session_manifest`'s own tests already use. The gate also covers the YAML helpers they use (`bounded_context`, `manifest_context`, `manifest_with_allowed_tool`, `authorization_context_with_manifest`) and the `std::io::Write` imports that only those helpers need, so there are no new unused-code warnings. The change is test-only and production code is untouched.

## Proof

The scoped repository checks for `cua-driver-core`, run with default features and with `--no-default-features`:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test`

Library tests: 1116 passed under `--no-default-features` (16 failed before this change) and 1179 passed with default features. Every integration test target passes in both configurations.

title: fix(auth): the Local channel never touches the login Keychain
body:
Stacked on #6587 (base `localkeys`); retarget to main once it merges.

Cua Spaces Local is signed ad hoc, so macOS sees every rebuild as a new app and asks for Keychain access on each launch. Local now never reads or writes the login Keychain:

- `CuaChannel::uses_login_keychain` (false for Local) is the one gate.
- `Store::from_env` (cua-auth): Local is always the 0600 file store, even with `CUA_CREDENTIAL_STORE=keychain`.
- `vault_fallback_applies`: Local never reads the vault's copy of a named secret (the device key under `ai.cua.session.local`), the read that prompted on a Local launch with an item left by an earlier build.
- Daemon Keyvault (cua-spaces-ext): Local builds it without the OS protector, so opening an existing vault no longer reads or writes the `Cua Keyvault Generation` Keychain item named by the vault id.

Stable and Nightly behavior is unchanged. Tests: Local never calls an injected vault read, Stable still does, and the store choice and fallback rules for Stable are asserted.

title: feat(cua-driver-bench): run the BenchLab tasks on Hyprland (Wayland), e.g. Omarchy
body:
Refs CUA-3573.

**What this means for users:** Cua Driver Bench v2 can now measure computer-use drivers on a Wayland Linux desktop (Hyprland, such as Omarchy), including whether they leave the person using the computer undisturbed.

## What changes

A Hyprland port of the BenchLab trial, next to the Linux/X11 and Windows ports:

- `hyprland/sentinel.py`: the "User activity" witness as a native Wayland GTK3 window. The eight A22 criteria come from Hyprland's IPC socket (active window, stacking order of `clients`, top and overlay layer surfaces, `cursorpos`, active and special workspaces, full-screen windows, a second window of the sentinel's process), `wl-paste --watch` (data-control) for the clipboard, and GTK events for key focus and leaked keys, clicks and scrolls. Compositor reads run off the GTK thread.
- `hyprland/guard.py`: the GUI-only guard. Terminal emulators started outside the runner's tree, or a terminal or Omarchy TUI window active for three samples, fail the trial; tool inputs are scanned for `hyprctl`, compositor `exec`, uwsm and Omarchy launchers, and terminal names.
- `launch/hyprland_session.py` + `hyprland/bench.lua`: one trial (brief, BenchLab, sentinel, guard, checker, `row.json`), with floating frames placed through IPC, 1920x1080 so the shared frames fit, and window rules so BenchLab's windows never take focus on open and its dialogs open over BenchLab instead of over the user window (the macOS sheet / Windows dialog behaviour).
- `hyprland/oracle.py`: solves each task through the GUI with real input (a uinput pointer and keyboard), to validate the port.
- `probes/*/launch.hyprland.json`, README section "Linux on Hyprland", `tests/test_hyprland_tools.py`.

BenchLab itself (`linux/benchlab.py`), the seeds, the checkers and `summarize_sentinel.py` are unchanged.

## Validation

On the Omarchy edge image (Hyprland 0.56.2, GTK 3.24.52): the oracle passes all seven checkers; doing nothing fails all seven and leaves the user undisturbed; a deliberate focus change, raise, pointer move, clipboard change, keystroke and workspace switch are each caught. `pytest tests probes/tests swift/tests` passes (364 passed) and `tools/taskset.py check` is ok.
