title: feat(cua): Windows 11 on Apple silicon built locally, ISO downloaded automatically (QEMU+HVF); Windows 10, Server 2019 and 2025 from an ISO
body:
## What this does

A Windows 11 Space works on an Apple silicon Mac with no manual step. In New Space (or `cua sb create windows:11`), choose Windows 11: cua downloads the ARM64 ISO from Microsoft, installs Windows unattended under QEMU with HVF (native speed; Windows 11 on ARM runs x64 apps), installs cua-spacesd, seals the disk as a base image, and boots the Space. Every later Space is a copy-on-write clone that answers in about 40 seconds. The same machinery builds `windows:2025`, `windows:2019` and `windows:10` (x64) from Microsoft's evaluation ISOs or your own (`--iso`); a Windows PC builds through WSL2 with KVM. `windows` / `windows:2022` stays the published Server 2022 containerDisk. Design and verification status: `docs/windows-images.md`.

This branch also carries the 9 dogfooding commits of `fix/winlike-windows-builder-whpx` (Python builder).

## Verified (Mac Studio, Apple silicon, macOS 26.6, QEMU 10.2 with HVF)

From the CLI and in the real Cua Spaces Local app, built from this branch:

* **Nothing to a Windows 11 desktop, unattended.** ISO download from Microsoft (8.5 GB, checked against Microsoft's published SHA-256, 7 min), install, cua-spacesd, seal, first boot. With the ISO cached: 8 to 9 minutes from Create to Running.
* **The second create is a clone**: cua-spacesd answers 36 s (CLI) and 36 s / 40 s (app; the second ran while the first was up) after Create.
* **Cua Spaces works in the guest**: screenshot, `exec` (cmd.exe), `cua do click/type/key` through cua-spacesd (Notepad opened from the Start menu and typed into); in the app the Space is listed like any other, with its desktop streaming, window list and "Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 on This Mac".
* **Progress in plain words**, read in the app: "Downloading Windows (first time only)... 1.5 of 7.9 GB, 14 MB/s, about 8 min", "Installing Windows (first time only)..." with a bar that moves (32% a minute in), "Booting Windows...", Running.
* **Cancel** (`cua spaces cancel`, the call the app's Cancel makes) stops the install VM and its TPM within seconds and releases the build lock.
* **`--runtime auto`** picks QEMU with HVF for ARM64 Windows on Apple silicon (unit test `auto::tests` and the real runs). x64 Windows there is refused in plain words, in the dialog, `cua sb create` and `cua spaces create`.
* Tests: `cua-image` 162, `cua-spaces-app-core` 891, `cua-spaces` windows guard, `cua-daemon` 204 (one timing test flaked once and passed on re-run), `cua-cli` 378, `cua-vmm` qemu/auto/cloudinit/fetch/preflight (1 failure, `qemu::tests::live_tpm_vm_refusals`, which also fails on the base commit on macOS: an egress policy the runtime refuses). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on the 8 crates, on macOS.

Screenshots (real, from the app on the test Mac) are in the Linear issue linked below; they are not attached here because the GitHub API cannot upload images.

## NOT verified

* An interrupted ISO download resuming for real (unit tested with a fake server; a real retry hit Microsoft's rate limit, see below).
* **Windows 10, Server 2019, Server 2025 (x64) builds and the Evaluation Center scraping**: no x64 host; answer file, ISO resolution and runtime selection are unit tested only.
* **The Windows PC path (WSL2/KVM, WHPX)**: unit tested only. The WSL install driver now waits for the guest to power itself off and presses Enter for the first 14 s only; no Windows PC has run it. Running a UEFI Windows guest from the Rust QEMU runtime on a Windows PC still uses WHPX, which hangs in OVMF on current QEMU (known gap, unchanged).
* **No native ARM64 cua-spacesd exists** (releases carry only x86_64 Windows). The guest tries the native asset first and falls back to the x64 build, which Windows 11 on ARM runs under its own emulation; that is what was verified. A release job for `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` is a follow-up.
* The ARM64 display is `ramfb` at 800x600 (virtio-win has an ARM64 `viogpudo`; not done).
* **No ISO-path field in the New Space dialog** (an `isoPath` needs the create request, the SDK options and the bindings changed). Windows 11 on a Mac needs none; `cua sb create windows:11 --iso <path>` registers one.
* Microsoft limits how many download links one network gets in a short time ("Sentinel marked this request as rejected"). It happened after about eight link requests in a day of testing; the create then fails with that cause in words and `--iso` as the way out.

## Questions for the owner

1. **Licence (not decided here).** Microsoft publishes no ARM64 Windows 11 evaluation ISO. For ARM64, cua uses the same account-free service the "Download Windows 11" pages use (the page's edition id, then a link on `software.download.prss.microsoft.com`, checked against the SHA-256 the page publishes; cua never bundles, mirrors or republishes an ISO). That is Microsoft's **consumer media, installed as Windows 11 Pro unactivated** (the answer file uses the public generic Pro key, which activates nothing): it runs with a watermark and limited personalisation until a licence is added. Is that acceptable as the default, or should ARM64 ask for `--iso` or a licence step first? The CLI prints it before the first build.
2. **Software emulation (decided, with the reason; say if you disagree).** x64 Windows on an Apple silicon Mac (and ARM64 Windows on an x64 computer) could only run in software emulation (TCG). That is refused by default, in plain words, before anything is downloaded: it takes hours to install and is too slow for an agent's screenshot and click loop. The message names the way out (on a Mac use `windows:11`) and `CUA_ALLOW_SOFTWARE_EMULATION=1` accepts the slowness (12 hours allowed for the install). One message serves `--runtime auto` (`auto::select`), the QEMU runtime and the build.

## What changed since the Windows-PC-only draft

* **ISO**: Microsoft's download service for ARM64, checksum-checked, resumable, with bytes, rate and time left.
* **Build**: cua-spacesd installed the way the published Windows image does it (scheduled task in the desktop session, bootstrap mode, token directory), the newest cua-spacesd release with a Windows build, then **sealing** (no token or per-machine state) and power-off; the host waits for the power-off. The install VM is stopped at once when the create is cancelled. Enter is pressed only while the screen shows "Press any key to boot from CD": a blind timer reached Setup's Cancel button twice in real runs.
* **Runtime**: ARM64 Windows boots on the generic edk2 firmware when no Secure Boot pair exists (Homebrew's QEMU ships none; Setup's checks are bypassed); swtpm is installed with Homebrew on demand.
* **Create path**: a local Windows build resolves to an image that declares cua-spacesd (`create` returned immediately before), `--kind` defaults to a VM, the catalog's guest OS is used (without it the Space booted as Linux: no TPM, wrong display and disk), and the install VM's own boot reports no longer push the app's progress bar past the install.
* **New Space**: Windows is offered on Apple silicon and picks Windows 11; Server and Windows 10 there are refused with the reason (wizard and Spaces create guard). Row labels: "Downloading Windows (first time only)", "Installing Windows (first time only)".
* **Fixes found on the way**: Windows guests refused the host's telemetry setting; `cua sb exec` ran `/bin/sh` in Windows guests (now `cmd.exe`); `qemu_builder.py` used `_plat` before importing it; the catalog's four local builds are in the `distro` group (the `canonical` group is generated from canonical.rs); docs generator accepts `local_build`; FFI, Swift and Electron bindings regenerated.

## Update 2026-11-12: merged with main, Mac gate removed end to end, verified on a second Mac

* **Merged main** (451 commits) and fixed what the merge broke: feature gates in `cua-vmm` and `cua-sdk`, the `CreateAction` parent field, Swift tests and the bridge for the new fix action (`choose-windows-iso`, link fields; this was the red SwiftUI lane), formatting.
* **No more "coming soon" on a Mac.** The Windows tile reads "Windows" and is selectable on a Mac that has a build for it (Windows 11 on Apple silicon). It is greyed out with its reason only when the processor is unknown; a Mac without QEMU gets "Needs QEMU: ..." with Continue waiting; x64 images keep the "Choose Windows 11" reason. The refusal in `spaces.rs` is renamed (`WINDOWS_EMULATION_ONLY`); goldens regenerated with `UPDATE_PARITY=1`; the Electron wizard test and the Swift tests follow.
* **Bug found by running it:** main now always puts non-Linux QEMU guests behind the secure network gateway, and its DHCP offer carried an empty DNS search list (option 119), which Windows refuses (error 0xD, stays on 169.254). No Windows guest had a network, so the first-logon script could not fetch cua-spacesd. The gateway no longer sends the option without search domains (unit test included).
* **End to end on a spare Apple silicon Mac** (macOS 26.6, QEMU 11.1, HVF, Cua Spaces Local built from this branch): New Space, Windows (tile enabled, Windows 11), Create: the ISO downloaded from Microsoft with its SHA-256 checked, Windows 11 installed unattended, the Space reached Running, `cua sb exec` answered through cua-spacesd (`Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26300.9457]`), the guest had 10.0.2.15 and internet. Not verified: Windows 10, Server (x64 only), a Windows PC, resuming an interrupted download.
* **Security review findings, fixed:** `cua-spacesd.exe` is run only if it matches the SHA-256 the release publishes beside it (a missing or different one fails the install); virtio-win is pinned to release 0.1.302-1 by its versioned URL and SHA-256 (a mismatch deletes the file and fails the create; the Python builder too); the consumer ISO link must be https on a Microsoft domain. `docs/windows-images.md` lists every download and its check, says the x64 evaluation ISOs (no published hash) rely on TLS, and notes the passwordless administrator (as in the published image).
* **Also fixed:** `cua-sdk` did not compile without its `spaces` feature (also on main: `bin/ci`'s per-crate clippy of `cua-compat-cmd` fails there); the dead-code lints that exposed are allowed for that reduced feature set; a telemetry test lacked the new `parent` field.
* **Re-verified after those changes** on the spare Mac (a fresh Windows 11 Space: the guest log shows the cua-spacesd SHA-256 matching the published one, the Space reached Running, `cua sb exec` answered, the guest had internet).
* **Checks run locally:** bin/ci in batches (its single run stops at the 15 GB target cap): prettier, rustfmt, SPDX, lockfiles, generated docs and bindings (cua-cli, cua-sdk, cua-rust, UniFFI, Electron, Swift), spaces contract, web and desktop tests, apps/cua-spaces vitest; the CI native clippy command; `--lib` tests of cua-image, cua-vmm, cua-spaces-app-core, cua-spaces, cua-cli, cua-sdk plus the parity goldens; Go tests of the gateway; the Swift tests (3 failures there depend on the test Mac's own state: a running Cua daemon, real experiment switches, a timing margin).

title: fix(spaces): say why a warm-pool refill waits, and end the agents of a deleted Space
body:
Fixes CUA-3579. Follow-up to #6619 (independent of it; touches different code).

**Warm pool.** The pool decided silently (debug level) not to refill. Reproduced in the real Local app: with seven Spaces running in the 4 CPU / 6 GiB runtime VM the daemon removed the idle member ("memory is short") and deferred the refill, because free memory fell under the 1 GiB floor:

```
warm pool: memory is short; removing a member member=cua-pool-ff03...
warm pool: refill deferred shape=a2d1... reason=not enough free memory: 5044 MiB of 5910 MiB in use by running Spaces, a member needs about 200 MiB and 1024 MiB stay free (pool holds 0 of its 5910 MiB share)
```

So the next new home had no warm Space. Now:
- a deferred refill says why, with the numbers, once per reason and again every 2 minutes (capacity wanted elsewhere, busy CPUs, memory, repeated start failures);
- a shape that failed three starts in a row is tried again after 5 minutes instead of never;
- the refill is retried every pool tick (2 s), so it starts as soon as a Space is deleted: in the app, deleting a home started the new member 2 s later.
The memory floor is kept on purpose: the pool does not take memory from running homes.

**Deleted Spaces and persistent agents.** `Spaces::delete` now tells extensions (`space_deleted`); the persistent-agent extension removes the agents that lived in the Space as `agent rm` does (run stopped, open tasks failed, routines and standby sessions dropped; the home stays in the Cua Volume). Agents of a cloud Space released on pause and durable members are kept. The supervisor also marks agents whose local Space is not registered (deleted behind its back) `gone` after 20 s: paused, unsupervised, no more log lines; `agent rm` still forgets them, `agent ls` shows `gone`.

**Tests.** `pool::` unit tests (memory deferral and recovery, never above the pool size, failure cool-down) and `tests/deleted_space_agents.rs` (delete removes agents and schedules, other Spaces untouched, gone reconciliation with grace, rm still works).

**In the app** (merged build with #6619): three homes back to back all claimed a warm Space (56-353 ms), delivered 261-465 ms, first token 4.3-5.1 s; the pool refilled 1.9-2.8 s after each claim. Deleting homes removed their agents at once.

title: test(agentic): prompt tests v1: plain-English goals, hard checks, record and replay
body:
Prompt tests v1 ([CUA-3570](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3570)). A prompt test is a plain-English goal ("add a second computer, then remove it"). An agent carries it out by driving the real Cua Spaces app through Cua Driver. Hard checks decide pass or fail; the model never does.

**What changes for users:** regressions like the ghost row after Remove, a PC that stays offline after setup, staging taking over a production host, a Windows Firewall prompt during setup, or a computer that never shows as offline get caught every night, before a release.

Design note: `docs/rfcs/prompt-tests.md`.

## What's here

- **Specs:** `tests/agentic/<area>/<name>.yaml`, with `name`, `os`, `setup` (build, canary account, hosts), `prompt`, `budget` and `expect`. `bin/agentic-e2e validate` checks them; an unknown key is an error.
- **Runner:** `bin/agentic-e2e run`. It installs the build, starts Cua Driver, sets up the hosts (each one is its own Cua home), signs the canary account in with the device code flow (staging realm only), runs the agent, runs the checks and writes `report.md` with screenshots, the video and every tool call. Then it tears everything down and takes every computer and device the run added off the account.
- **Agent:** Claude Code in headless mode. The model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) and the harness version are pinned in `tests/agentic/config.yaml`. Its only tools are Cua Driver's, through a pass-through MCP server that logs every call, enforces the step budget and starts Cua Driver's `start_recording` on the agent's own session.
- **Checks:** `relay` and `cli` take jq predicates. `ui` asserts on the accessibility tree (`contains`, `absent`, `row`), held for `hold_s` or reached within `within_s`, optionally timed from an event such as `power_off:2`. `no_dialogs` watches every window title from install to the last check. `file`.
- **Record and replay:** a passing `--record` run saves the turn files that `start_recording` writes, plus a `portable.json` that maps pids, windows and element tokens onto the live app. `--mode auto` replays them and runs live if the replay breaks.
- **Workflow:** `e2e-agentic.yml`. Nightly live runs on `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` (macOS gets a lane once a test lists it). `workflow_call` is ready for the release gate. On PRs it validates the specs and runs the unit tests. A nightly failure opens or updates one issue.
- **Tests:** five, written from the 5 Nov Windows and Linux bugs (CUA-3512, CUA-3513, CUA-3515, CUA-3525 and the offline flip).

## Live results (5 Nov, Linux test VM, nightly build 0.21.0-nightly.20261105.16)

| Test | Result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| offline-flips-fast | **Pass** (live $0.46, then replay $0) | The details showed Offline 1 s after the power-off; the relay agreed. The trajectory is committed, and its replay passed on a fresh machine with no model. |
| add-remove-no-ghost | **Fail** (2 runs, $0.71 / $0.74) | The agent added the computer with a pairing code and turned it off. The Machines page kept it "Online" with a Running Space for 5+ minutes, while the same page's Issues box said it was offline and the relay had it offline. Remove stayed disabled, so the ghost-row step never ran. |
| remove-readd-rejoins | **Fail** (2 runs, $0.42 / $0.46) | Same as above: the app kept the computer "Online" after power-off, so "Remove from account" stayed disabled ("It's online"). |
| staging-prod-isolation | **Blocked** | The staging canary account reached the relay's 64-device cap mid-session. Every fresh sign-in enrolls a device, and the runner didn't revoke them yet (fixed here: teardown revokes each host's device). No new computer can join until stale devices are revoked. Also, on a reused VM, default homes map to isolated ones, so this test only reproduces CUA-3512 fully on a fresh CI runner. |
| no-firewall-prompt (Windows) | **Blocked** | The repo secrets below are missing, so it can't run on `windows-latest`. Our Windows test VM was in use by the benchmark runs all session. |

Also seen: on Linux, a **"Choose password for new keyring"** dialog appeared while using the app (now on the watched-dialogs list), and the Machines list rows expose no online or offline text in the accessibility tree (status is a coloured dot only).

## Secrets to add

`CUA_E2E_CANARY_USERNAME` and `CUA_E2E_CANARY_PASSWORD` (the staging canary account). `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` already exists. Without them, the nightly job fails with the names of the missing secrets.

## Not in v1

macOS tests (hosted macOS needs Cua Driver TCC seeding), PR replay (v2), the release gate wiring (after the secrets and a green week), and pid, window and token mapping inside `replay_trajectory` itself.

title: fix(cua-driver-core): derive desktop coordination from the action contract
body:
CUA-3473

## Plan

`is_physical_desktop_action` in `cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs` decides which tools take the process-wide desktop lane (`requires_desktop_coordination`). It was a hand-kept list beside the contract's `ACTION_RESULT_TOOLS`, and it had already drifted: `type_text_chars` and `invoke_menu` return the shared action result but were missing, so they ran outside the lane alongside other native input.

- Add `cua_driver_contract::is_desktop_action_result_tool`: action-result tools other than `browser_*` (the browser engine serializes those per CDP tab).
- `is_physical_desktop_action` becomes that predicate plus `bring_to_front`, which activates a window but has its own result shape.
- Behaviour change: `type_text_chars` and `invoke_menu` now wait for the desktop lane. The existing independent-lane exemption for exact background windows still applies. Neither tool re-enters the registry, so no nested acquire can happen.

## Proof

- New unit test `every_native_action_result_tool_takes_the_desktop_lane` covers every contract action-result tool (browser tools excluded), `bring_to_front`, and some read-only and browser tools that must stay out.
- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests for `cua-driver-contract`, `cua-driver-core` and `platform-macos`.
- Not run: Linux and Windows platform crates, the Linux X11/Wayland desktop E2E lane, and the macOS Lume E2E lane.

title: feat(cua-driver-bench): shared-desktop tasks PA-01 (parallel agents) and UM-01 (mouse user)
body:
**What this means for users:** Cua Driver Bench can now measure two things people run into when agents share a computer: whether several agents can work at once in their own copies of an app without stepping on each other, and whether a person can keep using their mouse while an agent works in the background.

Stacked on #6630 (Hyprland port); GitHub retargets it to `main` when that merges.

## Design note

[`automated-eval/macos_bench/SHARED-DESKTOP.md`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/feat/driver-bench-parallel-and-mouse-user/libs/cua-driver-bench/automated-eval/macos_bench/SHARED-DESKTOP.md): why the tasks matter, exact starting states, sub-tasks, seeds, checkers, scoring, budgets, how they relate to the eight undisturbed criteria, platform notes (macOS, Windows, Linux X11, Hyprland) and threats to validity. Both tasks are deterministic and checker-graded, like every v2 task. They sit in a new `shared_desktop` category and are selected by id or `--task-set shared-desktop`; they are not added to the ten registered v2 tasks (a dated amendment registers them before the first scored trial).

## The tasks

| Task | Starting state | Agent(s) | Checker pass | Full pass adds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **PA-01** parallel agents | N copies of BenchLab (`desk` mode) in a fixed 5 x 2 grid; labels, codes and shelves from the seed (N = 10; also 4, and 1 for the speed-up baseline) | N agents started at the same moment, one per copy, each told its copy by title and grid position | every copy: right code, right shelf, one Submit, no letter of another copy's code (code letters are unique per copy, so cross-talk is attributable), Submit within the shared 360 s budget | background: the eight undisturbed criteria |
| **UM-01** the user's mouse keeps working | one copy partly under the "User activity" window, whose user moves and clicks the real pointer on a seeded path over eight dots | one agent, background only | the copy's checks | the pointer never displaced from the user's script (3 px), every user click landed on its dot, no agent input in the user window, plus the other undisturbed criteria |

PA-01 also reports copies passed, cross-talk, makespan, throughput (copies per minute) and the speed-up over N = 1 for the same run index. A driver without multi-session support may serialise the agents; its copies count if they are correct within the budget.

On macOS and Windows the mouse user tags its own events (`kCGEventSourceUserData`, `dwExtraInfo`) and a listen-only tap or low-level hook counts any other pointer event; on X11 and Hyprland the sentinel compares the observed pointer with its own script 40 times a second.

## What changes

- BenchLab `desk` mode on macOS (`swift/BenchLabShared.swift`), Linux GTK (X11 and Wayland) and Windows (wxPython).
- `--mouse-user SCRIPT` in every sentinel (macOS, X11, Hyprland, Windows); `summarize_sentinel` reports `mouse_user` and puts the displacement in `pointer_max_deviation_px`; `bench_v2` scores the pointer and input criteria against the mouse user.
- N concurrent agents: `run_bench.py` (macOS, Linux X11), `launch/windows_session.py` and `launch/hyprland_session.py` (`--instances`, `{instance}` and `{title}` in the agent command). Any agent's GUI-only violation ends all of them.
- Checkers `probes/PA-01/evaluate.py` and `probes/UM-01/evaluate.py`; shared derivations in `benchlab_common.py`; runner helpers in `shared_desktop.py`.
- `tools/analyze_v2.py`: PA-01 per N (all copies passed, cross-talk, makespan, throughput, speed-up) and UM-01 (checker pass, full pass, displacement, lost clicks); `--session-rows` reads Windows and Hyprland `row.json`.
- Manifest entries, README table, `TASKS.md`, a pointer in `METHOD.md`, launch descriptors for Windows and Hyprland, TCC grants for the macOS sentinel (Accessibility, Input Monitoring).
- `tools/validate_shared.py`: a model-free real-desktop validation on macOS (accessibility-only oracles, deliberate cross-talk, pointer displacement, covered canvas).

## Testing

title: fix(cua-driver): bound browser_dialog Page.enable retry by the dialog subscription deadline
body:
CUA-3439

`browser_dialog` retries the tab's `Page.enable` dialog subscription when the attach-time subscribe did not take. That retry used the full CDP call timeout (`CALL_TIMEOUT`, 20 s), while the attach-time subscribe in `engine.rs` uses the short `DIALOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TIMEOUT` (2 s). A renderer already blocked by an unseen dialog never answers `Page.enable`, so `browser_dialog` hung for the long deadline before refusing.

Change:
- `engine.rs`: expose `DIALOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TIMEOUT` to the crate.
- `tools.rs`: the `browser_dialog` re-subscribe calls `call_with_timeout(..., DIALOG_SUBSCRIPTION_TIMEOUT)`. The refusal and unregister behaviour on failure are unchanged.

Proof:
- New test `browser_dialog_resubscribe_uses_the_short_dialog_deadline`: the mock tab never answers `Page.enable`. `browser_dialog inspect` must return within two short deadlines (one for the attach subscribe, one for the retry) plus slack, record the retry, and refuse with `browser_action_unavailable`. Against the old `tools.rs` the test fails because it waits out the call timeout.
- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`, all targets) and the full test suite for `cua-driver-core`.

title: lume serve: forced stop racing guest power-off leaves the VM's run lock held; later stops fail with "Cannot verify the owner"
body:
**Lume version:** 0.20.0 from Homebrew (`lume --version` prints 0.6.1). macOS Tahoe host, Apple Silicon (M1), macOS guest.

### Summary

VMs are run inside `lume serve`. When a forced stop (`POST /lume/vms/:name/stop` with `force: true`) races the guest's own power-off, the Virtualization.framework stop fails with *"The virtual machine stopped unexpectedly"*. `lume serve` then keeps the VM's config-file run lock and owner record. It falls back to resolving the lock holder, finds that the holder is itself, and refuses:

```
Cannot verify the owner of VM ‘<name>’. Stop the VM from the terminal that started it.
```

After that the VM is stuck:
- `lume ls` reports it `running`, with its IP, but the guest is gone;
- every later stop answers 400 with the same message;
- suspend answers "not running";
- the VM can't be started again or deleted.

The only way out is to restart `lume serve`, which also ends every other VM it hosts.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `lume serve --port 7777`, then start a macOS VM through the API.
2. Inside the guest, run `sudo shutdown -h now`. A resumed guest that takes a while to power off makes this easier to hit.
3. While the guest is powering off, send `POST /lume/vms/<name>/stop` with `{"force": true}`.

### Server log, first forced stop

```
INFO: Stopping VM via virtualization service name=<vm>
ERROR: Failed to stop VM via virtualization service error=Internal Virtualization error. The virtual machine stopped unexpectedly.
INFO: Resolving process holding the config-file run lock path=~/.lume/<vm>/config.json
ERROR: Failed to stop VM error=Cannot verify the owner of VM ‘<vm>’. Stop the VM from the terminal that started it.
INFO: Sending response statusCode=400
```

### Server log, every stop after that

```
INFO: Attempting to stop VM force=true name=<vm>
INFO: Resolving process holding the config-file run lock path=~/.lume/<vm>/config.json
ERROR: Failed to stop VM error=Cannot verify the owner of VM ‘<vm>’. ...
```

### Expected

If the framework reports the VM stopped, unexpectedly or not, `lume serve` should end that VM's run: release the run lock, remove the owner record, and treat the VM as stopped. If a run is held by `lume serve` itself, a stop sent to that same server should act on its own in-process VM rather than taking the "unverifiable owner" path.

### Workaround

Restart `lume serve`, but only when no other VM is running in it, because the restart ends them all.

title: perf(spaces): a new home is warm as soon as the person's agents are prepared
body:
A new home is cold for minutes after an update because the warm member waits for every app and a filesystem save, and the saved filesystem is thrown away too easily. This makes a home warm as soon as the person's own agents are prepared.

Root cause of the cold first message (owner log): the shape hash changed with the new build, so there was no saved filesystem: prepare of all 8 harnesses took 125 s, then the save 102 s, and the member was claimable only 241 s after launch. Separately the cache budget (8.2 GiB) is smaller than base image plus the full filesystem (7.5 GiB), so budget eviction removed it again minutes after it was saved.

- The member waits only for the first apps (Claude Code, then the agents and recent runs from persistent/agents.json and phases.jsonl, at most 3). It never waits for a save.
- The filesystem with every app is built beside the pool by a member nobody can claim (first layer saved at once, then the rest), because saving a member that can be claimed would capture a claim's data.
- The saved filesystem is keyed by backend, image, platform and the apps (at their pinned versions), in an index next to the pool records. A network preset, size or build change no longer discards it, and a superset is reused. An app outside the saved set installs in the Space as before.
- The newest two prepared filesystems stay under a small cache budget (cua-disk).
- Logs: `member ready ... claimable_after_start_s`, `prepared filesystem reused (tag, covers, wanted)`, `no prepared filesystem to reuse (reason)`, `the prepared filesystem has every app`.

Measured in the real Local app (4 CPU, 6 GiB VM), claude-code home:
- No saved filesystem at all: member claimable 21 s after it starts (boot 2 s, prepare 19 s), against 241 s. First layer saved at +69 s, all 8 apps at +270 s, in the background.
- Member from the first layer: ready in 2.6 s. After a relaunch, a refill from the full filesystem: ready in 2.4 s (`covers=8 wanted=8`), no preparing; the GC kept it at 60 s.
- A home 60 s after relaunch: delivered 430 ms, first_token 4.5 s.

Tests: pool unit tests (first-layer claimability and background build, reuse under another network preset and size, pin mismatch re-prepares, superset reuse), ordering of the first apps, GC keeps the newest prepared images. Based on #6632 (same file); base it on main once that merges.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse clicks fast while a detached session's dialog blocks the tab
body:
CUA-3438. Follow-up to #6514 (CUA-3307), now merged; this PR targets `main`.

#6514 drops a tab's dialog record when the session that saw the dialog open gets a `Target.detachedFromTarget`. If something outside the driver detaches that session while the dialog is still showing, the page stays blocked but the driver has no record. `browser_click` then stops refusing as dialog-present, and its frame revalidation waits out the 20 s call timeout.

**Chromium behaviour** (checked against the installed Chrome with a scripted CDP probe):
- Once the session that saw `javascriptDialogOpening` detaches, every newer session gets `-32602 No dialog is showing` from `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog`. Its `Page.enable` and `Runtime.evaluate` never reply.
- A navigation started from another session closes the dialog and sends `Page.javascriptDialogClosed` to the session that is waiting on `Page.enable`, and then `Page.enable` replies.

**Change** (`cua-driver-core` browser module)
- CDP reader: on `Target.detachedFromTarget`, keep the dialog record and mark it `detached` instead of dropping it. The session mapping is still dropped, so the next attach subscribes a fresh session, and a close event on that session clears the record.
- `browser_click`: the existing dialog-present refusal now covers a detached dialog. It fails fast and says the driver cannot resolve the dialog. The dialog block carries `resolvable: false`.
- `browser_dialog`: inspect reports `resolvable`. Accept or dismiss on a detached dialog refuses with the same detail and does not send `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog`. That call would only return `No dialog is showing`, and #6514 would then clear a record for a page that is still blocked.
- Tab attach: a detached record no longer skips the dialog subscription. If the new session's bounded `Page.enable` replies, the renderer is no longer blocked, so the stale record is cleared (generation-checked). This covers a dialog that closed while no session was listening.

**Tests**
- `cdp_ws::tests::a_detached_dialog_session_marks_its_dialog_unresolvable` (replaces `a_detached_dialog_session_drops_its_dialog_record`): the record survives the detach as `detached`, and a new subscriber's close event clears it.
- `v2_tests::a_dialog_whose_session_detached_refuses_clicks_without_waiting`: after the detach, a coordinate click refuses with `resolvable: false` well inside the call timeout and dispatches no input. Inspect reports `resolvable: false`, and dismiss refuses without calling Chromium. Fails without the reader change.
- `v2_tests::a_detached_dialog_that_closed_unseen_stops_blocking_clicks`: when the new session's `Page.enable` answers, the click dispatches. Fails without the attach-time clear.

title: fix(cua-spaces): retire interrupted-create journals whose sandbox is gone
body:
CUA-3505

After a daemon restart, `recover_interrupted_creates` reports every local create whose recovery failed as "local attempt retained" and keeps its journal in `home/creating/`, so that the sandbox can be inspected. Once that sandbox is gone (removed by hand, or never started because the process died while resolving the image), nothing ever removed the journal. Every restart reported the same records again, and chaos runs left dozens.

Recovery now retires such a journal with `RecoveryOutcome::NothingLeft` (its stale `.cancel` marker goes with it). This happens only when all of the following hold:

- nothing is registered under its id,
- no sandbox state file records the name,
- the local runtime answers `NotFound` (new `Sandboxes::local_name_gone`).

If any of these fails, including an engine that is down, an unconfigured local runtime, or a borrowed sandbox that still exists, the journal stays as it did before. Nothing is deleted except the journal. The change keeps the "retain evidence, no speculative cleanup" rule from a597517d8: a journal is removed only after the runtime confirms there is nothing left to inspect.

The issue is filed under cua-compat, but the journals and the recovery live in cua-spaces (`creating.rs`, `Spaces::recover_interrupted_creates`). cua-compat has no code that writes `home/creating`.

Tests:
- `tests/providers.rs` `an_interrupted_local_create_is_registered_or_preserved`: the "early" journal (no sandbox was ever started) is now retired as `NothingLeft`. "cut", where the runtime holds an unrecorded instance, is still retained.
- `tests/cancel.rs` `a_cancel_after_a_restart_undoes_the_journal`: after a retained, cancel-marked sandbox is removed, the next recovery retires its journal and marker. The borrowed one, whose sandbox still exists, stays retained, and no sandbox gets deleted.

risk: standard

follow-ups:
- `mesh::tests::a_space_on_a_mesh_the_relay_turned_off_reconnects` in cua-spaces is flaky ("the cut is explained" panic, 1 of 3 runs alone). It is unrelated to this change.
- A journal whose sandbox still exists is still reported on every restart. Getting rid of those needs an explicit cleanup verb, or a policy on how long retained attempts are kept.

title: fix(cua-driver): lock the daemon socket so a racing launch cannot orphan a daemon
body:
## Why
Two `cua-driver serve` launches on one socket could both pass the liveness probe. The second unlinked the first's socket and bound its own, so the first kept running unreachable, and on exit it deleted the live daemon's pid file. Fixes CUA-3432.

## What changed
- The standalone Unix daemon takes an exclusive non-blocking lock on `<socket>.lock` before it clears a stale socket, and holds it for the life of `run_serve`. The kernel releases it on exit or crash.
- A launch that loses the race exits with the existing "already running … Run `cua-driver stop` first." message.
- Unit test: a second claim fails while the first is held, the bound socket survives, and the claim succeeds once the first is dropped.

## Scope
Covers standalone daemons on macOS and Linux. Embedded mode keeps its host-owned no-unlink rule and takes no lock. Windows named pipes are unchanged. The `.lock` file stays behind after exit on purpose, since an unheld lock file is harmless.

## Blast Radius
Every standalone `serve` start goes through the new lock. A lone launch works as before, and a stale socket left by a crashed daemon is still cleared, because a dead process holds no lock.

## Verification
- Repro script launching two `serve` processes on one socket at once: before the fix, both stayed alive and the pid file named only one of them. After it, 3 of 3 runs left one live daemon, and the other exited with "already running". `status` reported the survivor's pid and `stop` removed the socket and pid file.
- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo test -p cua-driver` pass.
- macOS Lume focused cell `macos-wkwebview-left-click-ax-background-typed-sdk` passed at the head.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the Windows daemon pid file owned by the running daemon
body:
## Why
A standalone Windows daemon creates its named pipe without reserving the name, so a second `cua-driver serve` that passes the liveness probe at the same moment serves beside the first. Both write the shared pid file, and whichever exits first deletes it while the other is still running. This is the Windows half of the ownership rule from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6652. Fixes CUA-3599.

## What changed
- A daemon removes its pid file on exit only while the file still holds its own pid. This applies on Unix and Windows.
- A standalone Windows daemon holds an exclusive lock for its pipe name from before the pid write until after cleanup. A launch that loses the race exits with the existing "already running … Run `cua-driver stop` first." message. The lock file is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cua-driver-pipe-locks\<sha256 of the uppercased pipe name>.lock`, so case variants of one name share a lock and long names still fit.
- Unit tests: a second claim fails while the first is held, a waiting claim succeeds once the holder releases, and exit keeps a pid file that names another process.

## Scope
Covers standalone Windows daemons and pid-file removal on every platform. Embedded Windows daemons already reserve their host-chosen pipe name with `first_pipe_instance(true)`, so they take no lock. The Unix socket lock stays in #6652, and the two diffs merge cleanly. One gap remains: when daemons on different sockets share a pid file, the read-then-remove step can still race with a write from the other daemon. Main deleted that file unconditionally, so the window is narrower than before and is left for a follow-up.

## Tradeoffs
I kept the standalone pipe on `first_pipe_instance(false)` instead of reserving the name the way embedded mode does. `stop` returns once the listening instance is gone, and connected instances can keep the name alive a little longer, so a reserving relaunch right after `stop` would fail. The lock waits up to 2 s for a stopping daemon instead.

## Blast Radius
Every standalone Windows `serve` start now takes the lock. A lone launch behaves as before. A crashed daemon holds no lock, because the OS releases it with the handle. On Unix the only change is the pid-file ownership check on exit.

## Verification
- Repro on macOS with two daemons on different sockets sharing one pid file, then stopping the first. On main the pid file was gone and `status` for the live daemon reported `pid: unknown (no pid file)`. title: fix(cua-driver-bench): Windows guard treats a driver's own helper shell like macOS (disclosed rule)
body:
Follow-up to #6633 (Windows multi-app tasks). Refs CUA-3563.

**What changes for users:** the Windows GUI-only guard now treats setups the same way the macOS guard does. A shell that a driver's own binary starts for itself no longer ends the trial. The rule is stated in METHOD.md, so it is a disclosed scoring rule, not a silent change.

**The rule, the same for every setup.** `launch/windows_session.py --tool-exe <exe>` (repeatable). A shell or script host whose parent process is one of these binaries is logged in the row as `gui_only.tool_helpers`, and it is not a violation. The four Windows setups pass their own binaries:
- `cua-driver.exe`
- `agent-desktop-win32-x64.exe`
- `windows-harness.exe`
- `codex-computer-use.exe`

Interpreters that run code the agent supplied (`python.exe` for a harness's `exec`, `node.exe` for a JavaScript REPL) are never on the list, so a shell the agent starts that way still counts.

**Why.** The macOS guard flags only named side-door apps ("a process named Script Editor, Automator, iTerm2 or Shortcuts exists") and tool inputs that contain code that runs outside the GUI. A driver's own helper processes were never violations there. On Windows, Cua Driver starts PowerShell in `get_browser_state` / `browser_prepare` to read browser processes; this was reproduced, and the parent process is `cua-driver.exe`. The stricter Windows guard stopped 7 of its 10 CDB-G04 trials for that, even though no tool input asked for a shell. Those trials were rerun with the same seeds.

**Effect on earlier results, checked for all four setups.** Every Windows row with a process violation was audited: run1 browser-use MB-11 r0/r2/r3 and every browser-use multi-app violation. In each case the shell followed a tool input in which the agent itself asked for PowerShell or a subprocess (`subprocess.run(["powershell", ...])`, `win.script(...)`), so its parent is an interpreter and the verdict is unchanged. Codex computer use and agent-desktop had no process violations.

Also in this PR:
- **METHOD.md:** the Windows release scope now covers all ten tasks, with app versions and the Windows driver list including Codex computer use.
- **README:**
  - The approval names Codex computer use uses on Windows. LibreOffice is `soffice.bin`; without it on the allowlist, every Calc approval is declined.
  - The `--tool-exe` note in the Windows guard description.

Tests: `pytest tests probes/tests swift/tests` (402 passed, plus a new unit test for the helper rule), `tools/taskset.py check` ok.

title: ci(cua-driver-bench): stop Linux headless contracts job timing out on slow apt mirror
body:
The `Linux headless desktop contracts (no model)` job was cancelled at its 10 min `timeout-minutes` on several recent PRs, which turned `ci-gate` red until a manual rerun. The cancelled attempts were all stuck in `Install desktop dependencies`: the Azure Ubuntu mirror was throttled and `apt-get` fetched small packages at one every 5-60 s. The tests take about 2.5 min, and every rerun passed.

Changes in `.github/workflows/ci-cua-driver-bench.yml`:
- Job timeout 10 -> 25 min.
- The apt install gets its own 15 min step cap, `Acquire::Retries` and HTTP timeouts, and up to 3 attempts of 5 min each, so a stalled download is aborted and retried.
- The pytest step gets an 8 min cap, so a real hang fails fast and names its step.

For users: CI on bench PRs no longer goes red from mirror slowness, so no manual rerun is needed.

title: fix(cua-driver): find a macOS app by any name it ships, without guessing
body:
## Why

`launch_app` by name only found an exact `<name>.app` directly inside six folders, although its schema takes the display name. @AlexFalher's https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6560 matches every name a bundle ships (file name, `CFBundleDisplayName`, `CFBundleName` and their localizations), one folder down included. This PR keeps that commit as authored and fixes four defects review found at 7bbb033f.

Salvaged from #6560. Linear: CUA-3539.

## What changed

- **Copies of one bundle id:** `apps/names.rs` no longer merges them into the first path with every copy's names. Each copy stays a candidate (`NamedApp.id`), and a top tie among copies of one id goes to the first copy. A name only a second install ships now launches that install.
- **No pre-ranking guess:** `locate_by_name` dropped the `<name>.app` fast path and the Finder special case. It takes an absolute `.app` path, then a bundle id LaunchServices knows, then ranks all names (`locate_in`). A file name another app also displays is refused as `APP_NAME_AMBIGUOUS`.
- **Base and Finder:** `Base` localizations count as unlocalized names. `/System/Library/CoreServices/Finder.app` is scanned as a single-bundle root (the rest of CoreServices is agents and helpers). The scan visits each bundle path once, because `/Applications/Utilities` is both a root and one folder down.
- **No second resolution:** `launch_located` / `launch_with_urls_located` take the resolved `AppLocator`. The tool no longer turns it into a string and looks it up again, so a bundle-id locator cannot turn into a filename match.

## Scope

macOS name lookup for `launch_app` only. Windows and Linux lookup are unchanged. `list_apps` still does not list apps one folder down.

## Blast Radius

Name-based `launch_app` on macOS. Bundle ids, absolute paths and exact file names resolve as before, unless another app displays the same name, which is now refused. Each name lookup scans the roots and reads bundle plists, where before the scan ran only on a miss.

## Verification

- New unit tests for each finding. The `names.rs` tests fail on 7bbb033f and pass here. The scoped repository checks (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cua-driver-core` and `platform-macos` lib tests) pass.
- `launch_app` over MCP on macOS 26 with a release build: `Chess`, `Échecs` (composed and decomposed), `com.apple.Chess`, `Calculator.app`, `Finder` and an absolute bundle path launch the expected bundle id. `Ma` returns `APP_NAME_AMBIGUOUS` with suggestions, and `ess` returns `APP_NOT_INSTALLED` with suggestions.

Size: the name scan and ranking are one new feature from #6560 that can't land in parts, so production lines exceed the add<=200 target.

title: fix(cua-driver): press a shortcut's key where the keyboard layout types it on macOS
body:
## Why

On a non-US Mac, every macOS chord path pressed letters, digits and symbols at fixed US key positions, so on AZERTY `hotkey cmd+a` pressed the key that types `q` and quit the app. This salvages https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6556 by @AlexFalher, which resolves a chord's key from the current layout with `UCKeyTranslate`. It also fixes one regression that change would have caused. Apple Screen Sharing forwards key positions to a guest whose layout the host cannot read, so reading the host layout there would press the AZERTY A key (US Q) for `cmd+a` on a US guest.

Refs CUA-3604. Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6556. The contributor's commit and authorship are kept as is.

## What changed

- The contributor's commit (`2c13ba9a8`): `chord_key_code` and `current_layout` in `platform-macos/src/input/keyboard.rs` press a single printable character on the key that types it with the chord's modifiers held: the Command layer, the Control layer or the plain layer. Named keys, and characters the layer has no key for, keep the US position.
- Ours: every chord path now resolves its key through `target_key_code(pid)`, which keeps US positions when the target is Screen Sharing. That matches the existing Screen Sharing text path (`physical_key_for_char`). `press_key_bare_global` takes the target pid, and desktop-scope `press_key_global` uses the frontmost pid. `layout_key_code` is deleted so no path can skip the rule.

## Scope

macOS chord key selection only: `press_key`, `hotkey`, their no-auth, global and bare-global variants. Typed text, the viewer keystroke path, Windows and Linux are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

US-layout hosts behave as before. On non-US hosts, chords to ordinary apps land on the layout's key. Chords to Screen Sharing keep the pre-change US positions, which assumes a US guest, the same assumption its text path already makes. Clients that remap keys for the layout themselves would now place them twice.

Size: over the net production budget because the layout reader (`UCKeyTranslate` FFI over three modifier layers) is one indivisible unit from the contributor's change.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks on `platform-macos`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --lib` pass, plus the ignored host-layout test. The new `screen_sharing_chords_keep_us_positions` test pins the US position for Screen Sharing.
- macOS Lume full matrix at the head: results are in the `verified` comment.
- Not run: a live Screen Sharing cross-layout repro, since this host was at its two-VM limit. Windows and Linux CI were not run locally.

title: bench: park the real pointer before every trial (Amendment 24)
body:
Part of the Cua Driver Bench v2 protocol work (`libs/cua-driver-bench`).

## What changed for users
A pointer left resting over BenchLab by an earlier task could make macOS activate BenchLab when it showed a background sheet, which changed the interruption (IR) results under every tool. The harness now puts the real pointer at a fixed point before each trial, so every setup starts from the same state.

## Change
- Before every trial, move the real pointer to (1000, 12), outside every registered window frame (user window, BenchLab, witness) and every task-pack window. Read the position back and record it in the trial row as `pointer_parked`. A park that does not land within 3 px fails the trial setup (a harness error, never scored).
- macOS: through the recorder daemon. Linux X11: `xdotool`. Hyprland and Windows session launchers: dispatcher / `SetCursorPos`, with the same read-back check. A platform with no supported way raises instead of pretending.
- `--park-pointer` is now on by default (`--no-park-pointer` turns it off).
- `METHOD.md`: dated Amendment 24 with the disclosure sentence.

## Tests
- Park point is outside every registered frame and every window in the task pack launch descriptors.
- Park record accepts a landed read-back and rejects a missed or missing one.
- `run_bench.park_pointer` returns the record on success and raises on a miss or on an unsupported platform.
- Existing suite: 351 passed, 52 skipped.

Not exercised on live Hyprland or Windows desktops here; there a failed park is visible as a harness error rather than a silent skip.

title: fix(installers): accept a rebuilt Cua Spaces release only with a signed claim for its tag
body:
Narrows the trust widened in #6649. Before this, the installers accepted any build signed by `cd-cua-spaces.yml@refs/heads/main`. Now a rebuilt Cua Spaces release verifies only with a signed claim that names the tag being installed.

**What changes for users:** nothing for normal releases (tag identity, unchanged). A rebuilt release still installs, but only if its run signed a tag claim.

## Why a claim

A Sigstore certificate for a `workflow_dispatch` from main carries the workflow ref (`refs/heads/main`), the main commit SHA and the trigger. The tag being rebuilt is only a dispatch input, so no certificate field or cosign flag can encode it. `--certificate-github-workflow-ref/-trigger/-sha` alone would still pass any main-branch dispatch.

So the rebuild run also signs `rebuild-claim.txt`: a `tag cua-spaces-vX.Y.Z` line and the sha256 of every signed asset, with its own bundle, uploaded next to the assets (kept out of the manifest). The claim comes from a run that passed the `rebuild_tag` guard (tag must resolve to `rebuild_sha`, release unpublished).

## Installer check (install.sh, install.ps1)

For the app, accept either:
1. the tag identity (`...@refs/tags/cua-spaces-v<version>`), as before; or
2. the main identity, verified with `--certificate-github-workflow-repository`, `--certificate-github-workflow-ref refs/heads/main` and `--certificate-github-workflow-trigger workflow_dispatch`, plus a claim that verifies under the same pins, names `cua-spaces-v<version>` and lists this file's sha256 under its name.

A missing claim, a claim for another tag, or a claim without the artifact's hash fails with "cosign signature check failed". The CLI identity is unchanged.

## Tests

- `scripts/install/tests/run.sh`: 144 pass (new: no claim aborts, claim accepted with the pinned flags, other-tag claim aborts, wrong-sha claim aborts).
- Pester: added tests (identity helpers, claim verification). Pester/pwsh is not installed here, so they were NOT run locally; CI is the first run.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: green.
- Not tested against real signatures: no 0.21.0 rebuild run or signatures exist yet.

## Ordering for the 0.21.0 rebuild

The claim is produced by the workflow in this PR. The 0.21.0 dispatch must run from a main that includes this PR. A rebuild dispatched from the current main signs no claim, and installers with cosign installed would reject it. I did not touch the in-flight release. After the run, verify with real bundles: `cosign verify-blob` on the claim and an asset using the flags above.

title: fix(cua-driver): find localized Chrome setup controls without English names
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `browser_prepare` with `strategy.kind = existing_profile` refuses on a non-English Chrome before it does anything. Run on main with Chrome's UI language set to zh-Hans, the hosted macOS browser lane fails like this:

  ```
  refused (browser_wrong_target_refused): the approved Google Chrome window has no exact New Tab button
  ```

  Setup finds three native controls by their English accessible names: `New Tab`, `Close` and `Address and search bar`. Chrome 156 in zh-Hans names them `新标签页`, `关闭` and `地址和搜索栏`. The `chrome://inspect` page stays English, and #4590 covers the localized consent sheet, so these three controls are what still stops setup.
- What changed: the English match stays and is tried first. When it finds nothing, the control is identified by structure, with no translation table. Every count other than exactly one still refuses.
  - **New tab:** the one native pressable `AXButton` outside every tab that spans the topmost row of native tabs (their top and height). Horizontal position is not used: Chrome overlaps the control with the last tab. The topmost row matters because Translate's bubble, which a non-English Chrome opens on English pages, has its own native tabs below the toolbar.
  - **The new tab's close control (cleanup):** the one native pressable button inside the tab that the existing before/after diff proved new.
  - **Address field:** the window's one native *pressable* text field, the field `unique_omnibox` presses. Chrome also exposes an unnamed native text field that cannot be pressed. The five setup-URL checks now share this identity instead of repeating the English-label predicate, so a find bar holding the setup URL never counts as the address field, in any language.

## Related work

Refs #3139

#4393 by @AidenNovak proposed the same structural approach. Its author closed it without review, noting that it still needed an E2E run on a non-English Chrome. This PR carries that design forward with that E2E evidence, plus the two cases the E2E run exposed: the Translate bubble and the unpressable native field. The commit credits @AidenNovak as co-author. #5304 / #5343 changed the same file (the initial native walk) and do not overlap with these lines.

RFC: not needed. There is no public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol or permission change.

## Compatibility and risk

- Impact: macOS only. Existing-profile setup now works on a localized Chrome instead of refusing. An English Chrome matches the English names first, exactly as before. The one change for English is that the address-field checks are stricter: an extra native field holding the setup URL no longer counts. Windows and Linux are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: the fallbacks run only when no English name matches, and each one refuses unless exactly one candidate fits. A layout the rules do not expect, such as vertical tabs, refuses with the existing codes. To roll back, revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `bin/ci` at this commit runs 9 affected checks (rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `platform-macos` unit tests, SPDX, image refs, generated reference, UniFFI bindings), and all 9 pass. `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib -- browser::` passes 95 tests.
  - Four new tests fail on main (6e7e939d5) and pass here: `new_tab_button_selects_the_localized_control_spanning_the_tab_strip` (a zh-Hans tab strip with frames measured on Chrome 156 / macOS 26.6), `new_tab_cleanup_selects_the_one_localized_button_inside_the_new_tab`, `localized_omnibox_is_the_one_native_text_field` and `a_find_bar_holding_the_setup_url_is_not_the_address_field`.
  - The other new tests pin the guards. I removed each guard in turn, and each removal fails a test:
    - pressable-only counting → `a_hidden_unpressable_native_field_leaves_the_localized_address_field`
    - uniqueness of the address field → `a_find_bar_holding_the_setup_url_is_not_the_address_field`
    - topmost tab row → `structural_new_tab_button_ignores_a_tabbed_bubble_below_the_strip`
    - outside-a-tab → `structural_new_tab_button_requires_every_condition`
- Platform evidence: hosted macOS lane (`scripts/ci/macos/run-hosted-rust-e2e.sh`, `macos-26`, Chrome 156) on a fork, with Chrome's UI language set per row via `defaults write com.google.Chrome AppleLanguages`:

  | Source | Cases | Chrome UI zh-Hans | Chrome UI en |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | main 6e7e939d5 | existing-profile cases | setup refused: `no exact New Tab button` | pass |
  | this PR c4e5aeca3 | full standalone lane, Chrome + Edge | every case passes except `native_omnibox_select_all` (test-side English lookup, see Known gaps) | 40/40 pass (38 delivered, 2 expected refusals) |

  Runs: main <https://github.com/YiTaiiiiii/cua/actions/runs/42216932418>, this PR <https://github.com/YiTaiiiiii/cua/actions/runs/42216937134> (evidence, including per-case recordings, is attached to each run).

  On an earlier revision, the lane found two cases that the unit tests had missed. Setup's cleanup refused while Translate's bubble was open, and the unpressable native field kept the address field from being unique. Both are fixed above and covered by tests.
- Review: an independent review with Codex (GPT-6 Astra, `gpt-6.1-sol`) found that the first revision let a find bar stand in for the address field. That is fixed and tested here.
- Known gaps:
  - Only Google Chrome was run localized (zh-Hans). Edge uses the same rules and ran in English.
  - Other locales, including RTL, were not run. No rule uses horizontal position.
  - Vertical tabs and tab groups were not tested. The fallback refuses rather than guesses.
  - `standalone_browser_native_omnibox_select_all` fails on a zh-Hans Chrome on main as well, because the test itself looks for `Address and search bar` (`native_omnibox` in the E2E file). This PR leaves the test unchanged.
  - If a new tab were pinned between the press and the read, its close control would be hidden. If that tab also showed a mute toggle, cleanup would press the mute toggle instead. A tab that was not closed leaves no other effect.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

title: fix(ci): don't fail the release-gate report when a post-merge push runs no lanes
body:
## What
The "E2E: Cua Driver release gate" run on main goes red on every push that touches no gated path, even though no lane ran.

## Cause
Since #6600, a push to main runs `decide`, which sets `run=false` when the pushed files touch no gated paths. Every lane is then `skipped`. The `nightly-report` job still ran (`mode == post-merge`) and counted each skipped lane as a failed lane, so it opened or updated the "release gate failing on main" issue (#6648) and exited 1. Runs 42220089490, 42222872653 and 42225476391 all show `decide: run=false ... push without gated paths`, all lanes skipped, and only `nightly report` failing. `E2E gate / result` already handles `run != true` and passed.

## Fix
`nightly-report` now runs only when `decide.outputs.run == 'true'`. A skipped push neither reports nor closes the tracking issue; real full runs behave as before.

## User effect
A red gate on main blocks cua-driver releases. Pushes with no gated change no longer turn it red falsely. Real lane failures still do.

Note: runs from earlier today with `run=true` (e.g. the 06:20Z schedule run) may be genuine lane failures; this PR does not touch those.

title: [Bug]: cua-perception extension reports unhealthy on nightly builds (prerelease version fails ">=0.28.2" requirement)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On a nightly Driver build (`0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244`), the installed `cua-perception` extension is reported unhealthy because its `requires Driver >=0.28.2` requirement is not satisfied by the prerelease version string, so the extension cannot be used on nightly.

### Reproduction

1. Install the nightly channel: `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)" -- --channel nightly --no-modify-path`
2. Download the signed catalog and archive for `cua-perception` 0.2.1 (darwin-arm64) from the GitHub release.
3. Register it: `cua-driver extension install cua-perception --catalog <catalog.json>`
4. Run `cua-driver extension status cua-perception --json`

### Expected behavior

A nightly build such as `0.38.1-nightly.*` is newer than 0.28.2 and should satisfy `requires Driver >=0.28.2`. The extension should report healthy and `parse_visual_regions` should be usable.

### Actual behavior

`cua-driver extension status cua-perception --json` reports:
```
"installed": true, "healthy": false,
"detail": "unhealthy: extension 0.2.1 requires Driver >=0.28.2; running Driver is 0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244"
```
I did not read the source. My guess is that the version comparison treats the prerelease tag as lower than the release, but I do not know the cause.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2, arm64
Application/browser/window system/image: cua-perception 0.2.1, darwin-arm64

### Evidence

Output of `cua-driver extension status cua-perception --json` shown above.

### Workaround and additional context

None verified. Staying on the stable 0.38.0 release may avoid the prerelease comparison, but I have not tested that with `parse_visual_regions`.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

Release bump PRs were closed within a second, five times in a row (#6679 to #6685). The PRs were already created with the GitHub App token. title: cua-driver: SwiftUI form controls labelled through AXTitleUIElement read as unlabelled (label, run_steps name lookup)
body:
## Problem

A SwiftUI `Toggle` inside a grouped `Form` exposes its label only through `AXTitleUIElement`; the checkbox's own
`AXTitle` and `AXDescription` are empty. `get_window_state` does not follow `AXTitleUIElement`, so the control reads as
unlabelled:

- `tree_format:"elements"`: the `AXCheckBox` row has **no `label` key**; the label text is a separate, un-indexed
  `AXStaticText` row that appears only in the markdown, directly before the checkbox.
- `run_steps` cannot target it by name: `{role:"checkbox", name:"Launch at login"}` fails with `not_found`
  ("no checkbox "Launch at login" in window …"), while `{text:"Launch at login"}` and `{role:"checkbox", value:"0"}`
  both resolve.
- `query:"Launch at login"` returns the static text, not the checkbox.

VoiceOver and other AX clients read this label through the standard `AXTitleUIElement` attribute, so a read-back that
does not follow it reports a missing label where there is none, and name-based targeting fails for every SwiftUI form
control built this way.

## Reproduction

- Cua Driver 0.38.0 (Homebrew cask `cuadriver`), daemon in `standard` mode, macOS 27.2 (arm64), Swift 6.4.2.
- A minimal SwiftUI app:

```swift
Form {
    Toggle("Launch at login", isOn: $launchAtLogin)
    Toggle("Show in menu bar", isOn: $showInMenuBar)
}
.formStyle(.grouped)
```

- `get_window_state {pid, window_id}` (lean markdown):

```text
    - AXStaticText = "Launch at login"
    - [12] AXCheckBox [actions=[press]]
    - AXStaticText = "Show in menu bar"
    - [13] AXCheckBox [actions=[press]]
```

- `tree_format:"elements"`:

```json
{"actions":["AXPress"],"depth":2,"element_index":12,"enabled":true,"frame":{"h":15,"w":26,"x":1729,"y":394},"parent_index":7,"role":"AXCheckBox","selected":false,"value":"0"}
```

- The public AX API on the same window (`AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue`, AX-trusted process):

```text
AXCheckBox title="" description="" titleUIElement="Launch at login"
AXCheckBox title="" description="" titleUIElement="Show in menu bar"
```

Still the case after 0.38.0, as far as I can tell: the 0.39.0 and 0.40.1 release notes do not mention it, and
`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs` on `main` (`5fce016f4e26`) builds a row from `AXTitle`,
`AXValue` / `AXPlaceholderValue`, `AXDescription`, `AXIdentifier` and `AXHelp` — `AXTitleUIElement` is not read.

## Expected

When a control has no `AXTitle` / `AXDescription` but has an `AXTitleUIElement`, use that element's value (or title)
as the control's `label`: in `elements[]`, in the markdown row (`[12] AXCheckBox "Launch at login"`), and in the name
lookup of `run_steps` and `query`. If a fallback is not wanted by default, an opt-in field (for example
`title_ui_element`) would let callers verify the label without a second AX client.

## Scope

Observation and targeting only; AX actions on the checkbox (`click` by token) work. Safari web form controls read in the
same session carry their label on the element itself (`AXCheckBox "Show inactive"`) and are not affected.

title: fix(cua-driver): re-read AXEnabled after foreground activation on macOS
body:
## Why

A foreground `double_click`, middle `click` or `type_text` with an element token into a background app skips the early `AXEnabled` read so activation can enable the control first (#6503). Nothing read it again afterwards. A control that stayed disabled was double-clicked or typed into, and no `element_disabled` refusal came back. Fixes CUA-3635.

## What changed

- Each of those foreground paths now re-reads `AXEnabled` after activation and right before input. A disabled control gets the structured `element_disabled` refusal. The new `element_disabled_error` in `tools/mod.rs` maps the error.
- Foreground AX `double_click` and unmodified foreground middle click never activated the app, so a read there would still come before activation. Both now front the exact window, act and restore, the same as `click`'s foreground AX path (`with_foreground_assist`).
- New macOS E2E cell `harness_appkit_disabled_control_is_refused_in_foreground_from_the_background`. The AppKit harness with a disabled checkbox sits behind the foreground sentinel. Foreground `double_click`, middle `click` and `type_text` must each return `element_disabled`, and the checkbox must stay unchanged.

## Scope

macOS only. It covers the three tools that skip the early read. `right_click` and `set_value` always read early. `click`'s main AX path already reads inside `perform_ax_click` after activation. No fixture control is enabled only while its app is active, so the activation-enables-it case is covered by the code path, not by an E2E cell.

## Tradeoffs

The cold verifier flagged that `with_foreground_assist` still runs its body when fronting is unavailable or focus never settles. A control that needs activation could then be refused. Not changed: that result is a refusal with no input sent, so it fails closed, and `click`'s existing foreground AX path behaves the same way.

## Blast Radius

Foreground element-token `double_click` and middle click now briefly front the target window and restore the previous app, as foreground `click` already does. Background delivery is unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test --lib` for `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-e2e` (675 unit tests pass).
- macOS Lume full matrix at 5fb094c07482f2c9444dfbeb6eacbc35b767bb0e: 179 delivered, 5 refused, 0 failed. The new cell `macos-appkit-disabled-control-foreground-ax-foreground` and the existing `macos-appkit-disabled-control-press-ax-background` both pass.

title: fix(spaces-macos): Cua Driver runs on every Mac, not only one set up for sharing (CUA-3638)
body:
Fixes CUA-3638 (release blocker for 0.21.1).

**For users:** Cua Driver now runs on every Mac with Cua Spaces. It no longer depends on the Mac being shared, signed in, or signed in to the account it was first set up with. When it can't start, the Cua Driver page says why.

## Root cause

In 0.21.0, Cua Driver for this Mac's coding agents ran only as a child of the host service, cua-spacesd (`libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd/src/main.rs:973`, `embedded_driver::spawn`). That service runs only while this Mac is set up for sharing under the signed-in account (`~/.cua/helper/service.json`). When there is no host service, there is no driver and no `~/.cua/run/`. That happens when:

- the person signs out, or signs in with another account (`pause_signed_out` uninstalls the service, `libs/cua/crates/cua-host/src/host.rs:2472`);
- the relay won't register this Mac yet ("add computers from a computer you already added, or with a pairing code" for a second Mac on an account);
- host setup fails for any other reason.

Set up then skipped starting the driver without a word (`WebUIBridge+Driver.swift`, `.needsSetUp`), so Test now said only "Cua Driver isn't running".

We reproduced this on a macOS test VM with the prod canary account and 0.21.0. The Mac was set up under another account, so sharing was paused. "Share With This Account" failed with the relay 403 above, and the page showed "Something went wrong".

## Fix

- **Cua Driver gets its own login item**: `com.trycua.spaces.driver`, which runs `CuaSpacesMac --driver-helper run` (`DriverLauncher`, `DriverSupervisor`).
  - The app registers and starts it at launch, and again on Set up, Repair and switching agents back on.
  - It keeps `cua-driver serve --embedded` running as its child, with the same arguments as the SDK's embedded host. Cua Spaces stays the responsible app, so the driver uses Cua Spaces' Accessibility and Screen Recording.
  - It restarts the driver with a backoff from 1 s up to 60 s, and clears a dead driver's socket the way the SDK does.
  - It follows the pause switch and start requests, restarts onto an update, and stops when the app is removed.
  - Sharing, sign-in and the signed-in account play no part.
- **No second driver from the host service.** It starts cua-spacesd with `CUA_SPACESD_EMBEDDED_DRIVER=0`. This needs no cua-spacesd release.
- **The real error is shown.** The login item writes `<CuaHome>/run/cua-driver.status.json` with its state and last error: the exit code plus the driver's last log line, from `<CuaHome>/logs/cua-driver.log`. The page and Test now show that reason, or that macOS is holding the item back in Login Items, instead of "set up this Mac".
- **Plain words for the relay refusal.** It now reads "Add this Mac from another computer" instead of "Something went wrong".
- `build-app.sh`, `build-release.sh`, `check-local-bundle.sh` and the VM check script know about the new login item. Local builds get `com.trycua.spaces.local.driver`.

## Tests

`DriverSupervisorTests` covers:

- a driver that won't start reports its exit code and last log line, and is retried;
- a missing binary is reported;
- a stand-in driver starts, is restarted after a kill, and stops;
- after a SIGKILL leaves its socket behind, the driver still comes back;
- stale-socket handling, the pause, the backoff, and the arguments and environment.

`EmbeddedDriverTests` covers the start steps and channel labels. `HostSetupFailureTests` covers the relay refusal. All of these pass locally (`scripts/test.sh --filter ...`).

## Verified on a macOS VM

Setup: the 0.21.0 bundle with this build's executable, ad hoc signed. The Mac was set up under another account with sharing paused, and Cua Spaces was then signed out.

- The driver login item starts at app launch and `~/.cua/run/` appears. The driver's parent is `CuaSpacesMac --driver-helper run`.
- The agent route answers. A SIGKILLed driver is back within seconds.
- The page shows "Working on this Mac. Last test passed just now."
- With the socket path broken, the page shows "Cua Driver didn't start: … is in the way (not a socket)". It recovers once the path is fixed.

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): keep background popups and drags off the user's seat
body:
## What changes for users

On Hyprland (Omarchy), when an agent works in a background app and that app opens a menu or a combo-box list, the user's keyboard no longer jumps to that popup. Before, the window the user was typing in silently lost keyboard focus until the popup closed, and whatever they typed meanwhile was lost. A drag-and-drop a background app starts is now cancelled instead of following the user's mouse and dropping on their next click.

## Root cause

Hyprland 0.56 and 0.57 ignore the seat and serial in `xdg_popup.grab` and `wl_data_device.start_drag`: every grabbing popup takes the user's seat (keyboard focus moves to the popup until it closes), and every drag runs on the user's pointer (ending it re-sends the user's keyboard focus). An accessibility action that presses a combo box in a background GTK app, or a click from one of the plugin's agent seats, is enough to trigger it. Hyprland's active window does not change, so window-level checks miss it; the user's window gets a `wl_keyboard.leave`.

The agent cursor overlay (`cua-agent-cursor` layer) was a coincidence, not the cause: it maps on the agent's first pointer action, which was the combo-box press. Mapping the overlay alone, repeatedly, never moved keyboard focus.

## Fix

The input build of the plugin hooks both requests (`CXDGShellProtocol::addOrStartGrab`, `CWLDataDeviceProtocol::initiateDrag`) and grants them only to the client that holds the user's keyboard or pointer focus, which every popup and drag the user starts does (clicked app, focused app, clicked panel). Anything else:

- popup: maps and works normally, without the grab;
- drag: the source gets `wl_data_source.cancelled` at once.

`cua:status` reports `user_seat_guard`, `popup_grabs_withheld` and `drags_withheld`. The decision is a small header (`src/user_seat_policy.hpp`) with its own unit test; the new files are added to the release bundle allowlist.

## Testing

- `ctest` (mock Hyprland, plugin hooks off): all 19 tests pass, including the new `user_seat_policy_test` and the lifetime test checking the guard is installed, reported and removed.
- Built against Hyprland 0.56.2 headers and loaded in an Omarchy edge VM:
  - Repro: a user typing continuously into one window while cua-driver presses a GTK combo box in a background window. Before: the user's window lost keyboard focus until the menu closed and keys were dropped (every run). After: no focus change, no keys lost; the combo box still opens and its item can be chosen.
  - Real-agent runs on the same task with continuous typing: no keys lost (see the PR comment for the run count).
  - A background drag in a GTK drag-and-drop list: before, it took the user's pointer and re-sent their keyboard focus; after, it is cancelled and the user is untouched.
- `packaging/release` unit tests: same 5 failures as on `main` (workflow-text assertions), none new.

Background drag-and-drop through the agent seats (reordering a GTK list from the background) still needs plugin support and is tracked separately.

Refs CUA-3582. Follow-up: CUA-3652.
