title: fix(cua-driver): admit any native Wayland app to Hyprland background input
body:
## What changes for users

On Hyprland (Omarchy), cua-driver's background pointer and key input now works in ordinary apps, not only in two exact package versions. An agent can click, scroll, drag and type into a GTK 3, GTK 4 or Qt 6 app in the background, including its dialogs, while the user keeps working in another window. Before, every app other than LibreOffice Calc `26.2.5-3` and Inkscape `1.4.4-6` was refused with `background_unavailable (client_not_qualified)`.

## Why it was an allowlist

`hyprland_compatibility.rs` was the initial qualification scope from the isolated-input RFC (#3550): only Calc and Inkscape had been proven end to end, so everything else refused until "qualified". It was not a record of failures. The agent seats (`Cua-Agent`, `Cua-Agent-2`) are ordinary `wl_seat` globals; any client that binds them receives their input the same way, and the plugin already refuses a client that has no pointer or keyboard on the lane seat (`client_not_bound`) before sending anything.

Checking real clients on Omarchy edge (Hyprland 0.56.2):

| Client | Binds the agent seats | Background pointer (click, drag) | Background keys |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GTK 3 | yes | delivered | delivered |
| GTK 4 | yes | delivered | delivered |
| Qt 6 (Qt Quick) | yes | delivered | dropped by Qt: keys go only to Qt's active window |
| Chromium (Ozone) | only the first `wl_seat` | `client_not_bound` | `client_not_bound` |
| XWayland | n/a | refused | refused |

## Change

- Admission is now a capability check on the live target: the compositor must report the exact `(pid, window)` as a native Wayland client (`client_xwayland` / `client_unattested` otherwise) and the process must be alive. The plugin keeps its dispatch-time checks, including `client_not_bound`.
- A short quirk list covers toolkits that bind the seat but drop its input. It has one entry, with the failure it reproduces: Qt 6 (`libQt6Gui` mapped) refuses background keys with `client_drops_background_keys`; its pointer input still goes through.
- Refusals whose reason starts with `client_` carry a hint naming the alternatives (element tokens, the browser tools, or `delivery_mode:"foreground"`).
- The GTK3 e2e harness now expects delivery, not refusal, for background pointer and key rows when the agent seats are present, and records the new `linux_hyprland_isolated_input` route.
- Docs (platform support, Linux skill, plugin README and protocol notes, test-harness guide) describe the new admission.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` for the admission module and the refusal hint (7 tests, Linux).
- `cargo check -p cua-driver-e2e --test harness_gtk3_test`.
- On an Omarchy edge VM with the plugin enabled, a source build of this branch:
  - probe apps per toolkit (table above): GTK 3/4 got the click, typed text and a full press/motion/release drag; Qt 6 got click and drag, keys refused; Chromium refused with `client_not_bound`. The user's focused window stayed active in every case.
  - the BenchLab tasks on Omarchy with a real agent: background pixel clicks on the app's separate permission and save dialogs now land.

A drag that the app turns into drag-and-drop (reordering a GTK list) still cannot complete in the background: Hyprland runs every drag-and-drop on the user's seat. The companion plugin PR #6705 cancels such drags instead of letting them take the user's pointer; doing drag-and-drop on the agent seats is tracked separately.

Refs CUA-3583. Related: #6705, CUA-3652.

title: fix(spaces): start never pulls a moved image, pending first message for a new home, pet-name default names
body:
## What the owner saw

Home said "agent ready", then a new Space sat in Starting while a 556 MB image downloaded, and only then did the agent install and run. His "@claude hi" did not show in the thread until the Space was up. New Spaces were named `home-hi-iy4` and `space-a572d9e2af`.

## Root cause

Creates resolve the image tag to a digest on every start, and the warm pool's shape key and prepared filesystem are keyed by that digest. When the registry moved the tag, the next create resolved the new digest, missed the warm member of the old one and pulled the image itself. The kept-warm Space only caught up some time later. "Agent ready" came from the old home's member and knew nothing about this.

## Changes

- Core (cua-daemon): a request whose shape is kept warm no longer moves to a newer digest when the registry changes. Creates keep the current image, the new one is pulled and a warm member of it is prepared in the background beside the old member (source `warm-pools-next`), and creates switch only once that member is ready. A start never has to pull. First-ever use, with no warm member yet, still has to pull; that case is unchanged.
- Web: a message typed for a new home shows in its thread at once with the existing pending treatment ("only you can see this", sends when ready), and the pending copy goes away when the real message is posted.
- Default names: one generator in `cua-spaces-contract` (`names.rs`, 100+ adjectives and animals), used by the SDK, CLI, MCP `create_space`, the new-Space wizard and Home. A taken name retries another pair; a short suffix is the last resort. Names given explicitly and existing Spaces are unchanged. The web has a generated copy of the lists with a drift test.

## Tests

- Rust: `hold_refresh` decision test (daemon), names format, list sanity, collision and suffix tests, wizard and parity goldens, home name test.
- Web: `pet-name.test.ts`, `queued.test.ts` (pending shows, survives the create, drops once posted).

## Real run

Built and ran Cua Spaces Local from this branch with its own home directory. The new-Space wizard shows the generated name (`noble-llama`). I could not take the pending-message screenshot in that isolated build: signing in to an agent needs the Keychain, which an ad hoc build cannot use and which I did not touch. The digest hold is covered by the unit test, not by a real registry move.

Note: #6631 also touches `wizard.rs` (different region).

title: fix(spaces): explain a refused new computer and offer a code from another computer
body:
Fixes CUA-3653. Sibling 0.21.1 fix to #6704.

**For users:** on a new Mac signed in to an account that already has other computers, "Share With This Account" now says **"Confirm it's you"**: *"To add this Mac to your account, enter a code from a computer you already added. On that computer, open Cua Spaces, go to Machines and click Add machine."* A **Use a code from another computer** button opens Enter a code. Before this, the app showed only "Couldn't set up this Mac for access".

The relay still refuses a new computer that has no proof it belongs to the owner (S5, #6355). This PR only gets that refusal's reason to the person.

## What changed

- **Relay:** the S5 refusal (`POST /v1/machines`, 403) now sends a stable `code: new_computer_needs_proof` alongside its existing reason, using a new `coded_error` helper. The rule itself is unchanged.
- **cua-host:** a 403 keeps the relay's code in the error text (`relay: <reason> [code: <code>]`), and `cua_host::refusal_code` reads it back. The code has to travel inside the message because the SDK error is flat across the FFI. A relay without this PR is recognised by the wording of its refusal, so 0.21.1 works against the current prod relay.
- **Pairing code on a paused Mac:** `cua host setup --pair` used to resume the old account's registration on a Mac paused for another account. It now moves the Mac to the account that made the code (`Host::rejoin_with_code`, the same path a sign-in switch uses).
- **Bridges:** the macOS (`WebUIBridge.reply`) and desktop (`reply`) bridges pass `kind` and `refusalCode` to the page with every host failure, so later refusals can get their own screens too.
- **Web UI:** `FailureView` shows the needs-proof state as the existing grouped card, with a neutral shield icon and a plain title (no coloured stripe). Its button opens Enter a code, wired on Machines, the setup form, Settings > Advanced and the new first run. When a code joins, the failure clears.

## Not included

There is no in-app "Sign in again with two-step verification" action. The app has no step-up sign-in today (no `acr_values` or `prompt` in the client sign-in), and building one is out of scope, so only the code action ships.

## Tests

- Relay: `a_new_computer_from_a_token_alone_is_refused_with_a_code`
- cua-host: `a_refusal_keeps_the_relays_code` (including an old relay), `a_pairing_code_moves_a_paused_computer_to_the_codes_account`
- Swift: `HostSetupFailureTests` (needs-proof mapping, no jargon, code parsing) and `WebUIHostTests` (kind and code in the bridge reply). These compile locally, but I did not run them because the FFI static libraries weren't built here; CI runs them.
- Desktop: host-failure mapping and bridge reply.
- Web: needs-proof UI state, failure clears after joining, Retry fallback, first-run row.

Ran locally: `bin/ci --quick --fix`, clippy on cua-host and cua-relay, the web and desktop test suites, and the new Rust tests.

title: [Bug]: Wayland type_text and press_key fail with foreground_unavailable on generic wlroots (labwc) while click and hotkey succeed
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On generic wlroots Wayland compositors (`labwc`) that expose `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` and `zwp_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1` without a compositor-specific IPC adapter, `type_text(pid, window_id, text)` and `press_key(pid, window_id, key)` unconditionally fail with `foreground_unavailable`, even though `hotkey`, `click`, and `scroll` succeed on the exact same `(pid, window_id)` target.

### Reproduction

1. Run `cua-driver` inside a generic wlroots Wayland session (`labwc`, e.g., `linuxserver/chromium` container with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/config/.XDG` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`).
2. Call `list_windows` to obtain the target window's `pid` (e.g., `707`) and `window_id` (e.g., `4278190080`).
3. Call `hotkey` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, "keys": ["ctrl", "l"]}`) or `click` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, "x": 300, "y": 82}`) -> both succeed.
4. Call `type_text` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, "text": "https://example.com"}`) or `press_key` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, "key": "Return"}`).

### Expected behavior

`type_text` and `press_key` should activate/verify the target window via `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1::activate(&seat)` (just like `hotkey` and `RestoreMode::LeaveFocused` pointer gestures do) and inject the keystrokes via `zwp_virtual_keyboard_v1`.

### Actual behavior

Both `type_text` and `press_key` refuse with:
```json
{
  "code": "foreground_unavailable",
  "message": "foreground_unavailable: no trusted Wayland compositor adapter can confirm exact target window 4278190080 for pid 707; no global keyboard input was sent"
}
```

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver 0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244` (commit `b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`)
Operating system and architecture: Linux (`aarch64`, Ubuntu/Debian container)
Application/browser/window system/image: `linuxserver/chromium` (Selkies WebRTC + `labwc 0.9.7`, exposing `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` v3, `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` v1, `zwp_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1` v1, `zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1` v2)

### Evidence

Root cause verified in source (`b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`):
- `type_text` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/type_text.rs:621-634, 705-720`) and `press_key` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/press_key.rs:418-436`) invoke `interaction::with_target_foreground(pid, window_id, RestoreMode::RestorePrevious, ...)`.
- In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/interaction/mod.rs:75-138`:
  - `RestoreMode::LeaveFocused` (lines 75-84, used by `click`/`scroll`) calls `crate::wayland::activate_window_for_input_target(window_id, Some(pid))`, which activates the target via `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1::activate(&seat)` and verifies `toplevel.activated == true` (`wayland/mod.rs:1982-2043`).
  - `RestoreMode::RestorePrevious` (lines 85-138, used by `type_text`/`press_key`) only checks `niri::is_session()`, `sway_ipc::window_for_id()`, `kwin_helper::trusted_window_for_id()`, and `shell_helper::trusted_window_for_id()`, then falls through to line 136 and fails with `foreground_unavailable`.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: Pass an explicit AT-SPI `element_token` to `type_text`, or use `hotkey` for single keys.
Suggested fix: In `interaction::with_target_foreground` (`interaction/mod.rs:85-138`), when no compositor-specific IPC adapter matches but `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` is available, snapshot the previously `activated` `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1` before calling `wayland::activate_window_for_input_target(window_id, Some(pid))` and re-activate it on `RestoreFocusGuard::drop` (or fall back to `activate_window_for_input_target(window_id, Some(pid))`).

### Submission checks

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Linux browser_platform is_only_exact_native_window returns None on generic Wayland, preventing cardinality upgrade and refusing browser_* mutations
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On generic Wayland compositors (`labwc`) without a compositor-specific IPC adapter, `LinuxBrowserPlatform::is_only_exact_native_window` falls through and returns `Ok(None)`. This prevents `cardinality_exact_candidate` from upgrading a single-window Chromium session from `Heuristic` to `Exact` binding, causing all `browser_*` mutations (`browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_navigate`, etc.) to refuse with `browser_wrong_target_refused`.

### Reproduction

1. Launch a single Chromium window with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` inside a generic Wayland session (`labwc`, e.g., `linuxserver/chromium` container where only 1 browser window exists in the entire session).
2. Call `get_browser_state` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080}`) -> returns `"binding_quality": "heuristic"`, `"mutation_allowed": false`.
3. Call any browser mutation tool such as `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, or `browser_type` (`{"pid": 707, "window_id": 4278190080, ...}`).

### Expected behavior

When there is only 1 browser window owned by `pid` (and only 1 CDP window representative with an exact title match), `cardinality_exact_candidate` (`cua-driver-core/src/browser/binding.rs:66-92`) should upgrade the binding to `BindingQuality::Exact` (`CorrelationMethod::Cardinality`, `mutation_allowed: true`) so `browser_*` mutations succeed in single-window generic Wayland sessions.

### Actual behavior

`get_browser_state` reports `"binding_quality": "heuristic"` (`"mutation_allowed": false`), and every `browser_*` mutation refuses with:
```json
{
  "code": "browser_wrong_target_refused",
  "message": "browser_wrong_target_refused: window 4278190080 is bound to CDP target ... only heuristically; refusing mutation because exact window-to-tab identity is not proven"
}
```

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver 0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244` (commit `b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`)
Operating system and architecture: Linux (`aarch64`, Ubuntu/Debian container)
Application/browser/window system/image: Chromium in `linuxserver/chromium` (`labwc 0.9.7`, exposing `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` v3 and `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` v1, with AT-SPI enabled)

### Evidence

Root cause verified in source (`b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`):
- `BrowserEngine::resolve_binding` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/engine.rs:1376-1388`) calls `self.platform.is_only_exact_native_window(pid, window_id)` and passes the result to `cardinality_exact_candidate` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/binding.rs:66-92`), which requires `is_only_exact_native_window == Some(true)` (line 71).
- However, in `LinuxBrowserPlatform::is_only_exact_native_window` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/browser_platform.rs:753-827`), after checking X11, Hyprland, Sway, GNOME Shell helper, and `wayland::is_inject_mode()`, generic Wayland sessions fall through to line 817 and return `Ok(None)`.

### Workaround and additional context

Suggested fix:
In `LinuxBrowserPlatform::is_only_exact_native_window` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/browser_platform.rs:795-817`), when `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` / `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` is active and `wayland::list_windows_dispatch(Some(pid_u32))` confirms that `pid` owns only 1 native window matching `window_id` (especially when total foreign-toplevel count for the app/session is 1), return `Ok(Some(true)` so `cardinality_exact_candidate` can upgrade single-window browser sessions to `Exact`.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: ci(cua-driver): fix Hyprland release-contract tests failing with RELEASE_REF unbound
body:
Five tests in `libs/cua-driver/hyprland-plugin/packaging/release` failed on main (and on every PR, e.g. #6705, #6706) with `RELEASE_REF: unbound variable`.

**Cause:** #6606 (rebuild_tag dispatch) made the plugin-source job read `RELEASE_REF` (workflow-level env) and changed its `if:`/`ref:` expressions. The tests extract that step and run it in bash without `RELEASE_REF`, and still asserted the old expressions. The workflow is correct; the tests were stale.

**Fix:** tests set `RELEASE_REF` as the workflow does, and the text contracts assert the current `if:`/`ref:` expressions. No tests skipped or removed; full suite 133/133 pass locally.

Plain words: no user-facing change; unblocks CI on all PRs.

title: [Feature]: Support labwc.sock IPC in LinuxServer.io / Selkies Wayland containers for attested window geometry, PID, and capture
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

`linuxserver/*` GUI containers (such as `linuxserver/chromium`, powered by Selkies WebRTC + `labwc`) are among the most popular Docker desktop environments for running `cua-driver` and browser/GUI agents.

Today, because upstream `labwc 0.9.7` only exposes `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` (v3) and `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` (v1) (neither of which carries `(x, y, width, height)` or `pid`) and does not yet implement `ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1`:
1. `list_windows` returns `bounds: {x: 0, y: 0, width: 0, height: 0}` on `labwc`.
2. `get_window_state(include_screenshot=true)` fails with `surface_identity_unproven: Wayland capture cannot prove pixels belong to window ...: no compositor-attested window geometry is available` (`wayland/mod.rs:1202-1233`).
3. `zoom`, `mouse_button_down`, `mouse_button_up`, and `drag` fail downstream with `screenshot_context_missing: no_screenshot`.

### Desired outcome

Add a compositor IPC adapter for `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock` (shipped in Selkies / LinuxServer `labwc` images) in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/`, attested via `compositor_peer::peer_pid` (`SO_PEERCRED`) just like `sway_ipc.rs` and `niri/ipc.rs`.

With this adapter active:
- `list_windows` reports compositor-attested `(x, y, width, height)`, `pid`, `focused`, and `!minimized` visibility on `labwc`.
- `get_window_state(include_screenshot=true)` can prove single-window / unoccluded crop geometry via `zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1` + `labwc.sock` geometry without failing with `surface_identity_unproven`.
- `with_target_foreground` and `LinuxBrowserPlatform` gain compositor-attested PID, focus readback, and window bounds.

### Current workaround

Currently users in `linuxserver/*` / Selkies containers must either force apps onto Xwayland (`--ozone-platform=x11`, which can conflict with Selkies fullscreen/maximized window management rules) or avoid per-window screenshots (`include_screenshot=false` / full-desktop `get_desktop_state`).

### Affected components and platforms

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/` (`mod.rs`, `compositor_peer.rs`, new `labwc_ipc.rs`), `interaction/mod.rs`, `browser_platform.rs`.

### Alternatives and prior art

Related to #5327 (Wayland compositor support tracking). Upstream `labwc` does not yet implement `ext-image-copy-capture-v1` toplevel capture (`ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1`), whereas Selkies / LinuxServer containers already ship `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock` out of the box.

### Implementation ideas

Verified in `linuxserver/chromium` (`labwc 0.9.7-dirty`, Selkies build):
The `labwc` compositor process (the exact same PID that owns `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, verifiable via `SO_PEERCRED` in `compositor_peer::peer_pid`) listens on the Unix domain stream socket `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock` (`src/ipc.c`).

Supported commands over `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock`:
- `GET_WINDOWS\n` -> returns JSON array:
  ```json
  [
    {
      "pid": 707,
      "x": 0,
      "y": 0,
      "width": 1457,
      "height": 827,
      "title": "New Tab - Chromium",
      "app_id": "chromium",
      "minimized": false,
      "fullscreen": false,
      "maximized": true,
      "tiled": false,
      "focused": true
    }
  ]
  ```
- `GET_WINDOW_BY_PID <pid>\n` -> returns single JSON object or `null`.
- `GET_FOCUSED_WINDOW\n` -> returns single JSON object or `null`.

Because `labwc` in Selkies does not expose window creation order in `GET_WINDOWS`, `labwc.sock` records can be correlated with `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1` / `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` handles via `(app_id, title, focused, minimized, maximized, fullscreen)` (and exact cardinality when a process owns a single window).

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): accept AltGr layouts for foreground typing
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Hyprland foreground typing refuses `us(altgr-intl)` and layouts built on it, even though they type the same as US on every key the driver presses.
- What changed: the whole-keymap check now skips Right Alt and the ISO `KEY_102ND` key, the only two keys where `us(altgr-intl)` differs from US. The driver never presses either one, and `foreground_chord_failure` still refuses a chord that does. `us(intl)` is still refused, since its dead keys change normal typing.

## Related work

Refs #3968, which made the same check accept Omarchy's default options.

RFC: not needed. No contract, permission, or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: foreground typing works on AltGr international layouts on Hyprland, where it used to refuse. Nothing changes for layouts that already passed.
- Risk and rollback: low. The up-front check now ignores 2 keys the driver never sends, and the per-chord check still covers them. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `keymap_equivalence_test` accepts `us(altgr-intl)` and still refuses `us(intl)`. `keyboard_layout_test` checks that `foreground_chord_failure` refuses both skipped keys under `us(altgr-intl)`. All 20 plugin tests pass against Hyprland 0.57.1 with `CUA_HYPRLAND_REQUIRE_XKBCOMMON=1`, and `bin/ci` passes locally.
- Manual or platform evidence: on Hyprland 0.57.1 with a custom layout built on `us(altgr-intl)`, foreground `type_text` of ``Hello World 1234567890 -=[]\;',./`~!@#$%^&*()_+{}|:"<>?`` plus Enter into a zenity entry returned exactly that text, and the plugin's dispatch count rose to match.
- Known gaps or CI still required: tested on one machine with one layout. This comes from a fork, so the sign-off is the `CI: Quick` run.

title: bin/ci: run on Windows (Git for Windows' bash, never WSL's)
body:
## What

`bin/ci` now runs on Windows (PowerShell, cmd or Git Bash): `python bin\ci --quick`, then `python bin\ci --signoff` after pushing. The sign-off format is unchanged (the status description ends with `(win32)`).

## Why it did not work

- The checks are bash. A bare `bash` on Windows is usually `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`, which is **WSL**: the first Windows run executed checks inside the user's Linux distribution. `bin/ci` now finds Git for Windows' bash next to `git` (`CUA_CI_BASH` overrides) and never uses `bash` from `PATH`.
- Windows read files in the ANSI code page (the repo is UTF-8): `bin/ci` re-runs itself in UTF-8 mode.
- The checks call `python3`, which Windows does not have (or has as a Store stub): a `python3` shim for the check's `PATH`.
- Paths: `package_of` and `spdx-headers.py` compared `\` paths with `/` exemption lists.
- Process cleanup used `killpg`/`SIGKILL` (now `taskkill`), `du` was assumed, a log being rewritten by a nested run could not be deleted, and the docs router quoted a Windows path for cmd.exe.
- The tests of `bin/ci` itself ran hook scripts directly and used a bare `bash`.

## Verified on Windows 11 (PowerShell 5.1 and Git Bash, Python 3.13)

`python bin\ci --quick`: SPDX headers, image refs, docs image refs (needs `crane`), bin/ci tests and workflow sync all pass. Not run here: Mac/Linux (the POSIX paths are unchanged apart from `bash -c` replacing `shell=True, executable=/bin/bash`), `--full` and the cargo checks.

title: Cua Spaces Local on Windows: install-local.ps1 and uninstall-local.ps1
body:
## What

`apps/cua-spaces-desktop/scripts/install-local.ps1` builds this checkout on Windows and installs it as **Cua Spaces Local** next to a released Cua Spaces, so a branch (a new UI, the `windows:*` images) can be dogfooded without touching the app in use. It is the Windows counterpart of `apps/cua-spaces-macos/scripts/install-local.sh`; `uninstall-local.ps1` removes it. Unsigned, no installer, no update feed.

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File apps\cua-spaces-desktop\scripts\install-local.ps1
```

Flags: `-Release` (release Electron fuses), `-NoLaunch`, `-Prefix DIR`, `-SkipRustBuild`, `-SkipWebBuild`, `-NoIntegration` (no Start Menu/PATH/scheme), `-NormalPriority` (builds run at BelowNormal by default). Prerequisites (Rust+MSVC Build Tools, CMake, Node 22+, pnpm, wasm32 target, wasm-bindgen-cli) are checked up front in one message.

## How it isolates Local

- The Electron shell gets a channel (`src/channel.ts`): Local when `CUA_CHANNEL=local` or the executable is `Cua Spaces Local.exe`. Local pins `CUA_CHANNEL=local` and `CUA_HOME=%USERPROFILE%\.cua-local` before the native layer loads, and has its own AppUserModelID (`ai.cua.spaces.desktop.local`), user data folder, Run entry, registry key, window title and `cua-local://` scheme. Stable's names are unchanged (tests).
- `packaging/electron-builder.local.cjs`: dir build, own app id and product name, no `app-update.yml`.
- Installs only: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Cua Spaces Local\` (with `bin\cua-local.exe`, a copy of the bundled `cua.exe`; the CLI is Local by its name), a user-PATH entry for that `bin`, a Start Menu shortcut carrying the AUMID, and `HKCU\Software\Classes\cua-local`.
- Staged build, verified (`cua-local --version`, native layer, web UI, no update feed), then swapped; the old copy is put back if the swap fails. It refuses a `-Prefix` that is, holds or is inside anything the released app owns, and any folder at the Local path without its `.cua-spaces-local.json` marker; only processes running from the Local folder are stopped. The user PATH is read and written as stored (no `%VAR%` expansion).
- The pinned pnpm (11.x) is installed into `.local-tools` when the PC's pnpm is another major (pnpm 10 cannot read the lockfile).

## Verified on Windows 11 (PowerShell 5.1)

Ran the script for real (twice: fresh install, then an in-place reinstall from this branch's worktree): web UI and native layer built, staged copy verified, app launched with the title "Cua Spaces Local" at normal priority, `cua-local --version` prints `cua 0.10.1`, the app's daemon runs from the Local folder, state in `%USERPROFILE%\.cua-local` and `%APPDATA%\Cua Spaces Local`, `cua-local://` and PATH entries registered, the released `%USERPROFILE%\.cua` and its `cua` PATH entry untouched. `scripts/tests/install-local.tests.ps1` (path/refusal/PATH/version checks, names match `src/channel.ts`, the builder config and `CuaChannel::Local`) and `test/channel.test.ts` pass; the desktop suite has the same 12 Windows-only failures as `main` (packaging file modes, nsh CRLF, updater, browser tests) and nothing new. `bin/ci --quick` checks (SPDX, image refs, docs image refs, bin/ci tests, desktop typecheck) pass on Windows with the port from #6719; `local-ci` is signed off.

Not verified: PowerShell 7 (not installed here; the script avoids 5.1-only and 7-only syntax), arm64, `-Release` fuses, `-Prefix` on another drive, an uninstall run on the real install (only its pure parts are tested), sign-in (staging) and creating a Space from the Local app.

## Notes

- Stacked on #6719 (bin/ci on Windows); the first two commits are that PR's and drop out when it merges.
- Dogfooding the `windows:*` images (local ISO build via WSL2/KVM) needs the branch of #6631 checked out: this PR is based on `main`. That branch also needs a small fix (not part of this PR): `AppSandboxImage` in `cua-spaces-ffi` lacks the new `local_build` field, so the Spaces app library does not compile there (E0063); the TypeScript binding needs regenerating and `libs/spaces-app-swift` needs regenerating on a Mac.
- The unattended-access host service (`cua host setup`) still downloads the pinned `cua-spacesd`, which does not know the Local ports.

title: [Bug]: Wayland type_text shells out to wtype on wlroots, corrupting >=14 distinct chars (evdev 14/28) and non-BMP Unicode/Emoji
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On wlroots Wayland compositors (`labwc`, `sway`, `hyprland`), `wayland::type_into` (`wayland/mod.rs:2769-2785`) only uses the built-in XKB keymap planner on `niri` and still shells out to external `wtype` on all other compositors. This causes two reproducible bugs in Chromium/Electron and Wayland apps: (1) non-BMP Unicode characters (Emoji > U+FFFF) are truncated to 16-bit keysyms or dropped, and (2) strings with >=14 distinct characters map to evdev keycode 14 (Backspace) and 28 (Enter), deleting characters or prematurely submitting forms.

### Reproduction

1. Run `cua-driver` inside a wlroots Wayland session (`labwc` or `sway`) with Chromium focused.
2. Call `type_text` with non-BMP Emoji: `{"scope": "desktop", "delivery_mode": "foreground", "text": "Hello 🚀😀🎉"}`.
3. Call `type_text` with a string containing >=14 distinct characters into a Chromium input field: `{"scope": "desktop", "delivery_mode": "foreground", "text": "abcdefghijklmnop0123456789!@"}`.

### Expected behavior

1. Non-BMP Unicode characters (Emoji such as `🚀😀🎉`) should be delivered intact without 16-bit keysym truncation.
2. Strings with >=14 distinct characters should be typed without triggering `Backspace` (evdev 14) or `Enter` (evdev 28) in Chromium/Electron.

### Actual behavior

1. Non-BMP Emoji characters (`> U+FFFF`) are either dropped by `wtype` or truncated to 16-bit keysyms by Chromium.
2. Because `wtype` assigns the n-th distinct character of a call to `evdev code n`, the 14th distinct character triggers `Backspace` (deleting the previous character) and the 28th triggers `Enter`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver v0.40.2 (commit dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c)
Operating system and architecture: Linux (aarch64 / x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04 container)
Application/browser/window system/image: Chromium on wlroots Wayland (labwc 0.9.7 / sway, zwp_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1)

### Evidence

Verified in `v0.40.2` source (`dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c`):
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/mod.rs:2774-2782`:
  ```rust
  if niri::is_session() {
      return niri::keyboard::type_text(window.or_else(niri_expected_window), text);
  }
  let result = wtype_output(&["-k", "Shift_L", "--", text]);
  ```
- Meanwhile, `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/niri/keyboard.rs:6-28` explicitly documents both `wtype` defects:
  - Lines 6-10: *"A tool like `wtype` instead numbers the n-th distinct character of a call as evdev code n, and Chromium and Electron take the DOM `code` from the evdev code: a punctuation mark on code 1 (Escape) is dropped, one on code 14 (Backspace) deletes the character before it, and one on code 28 (Enter) can submit a form."*
  - Lines 24-27: *"Text outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as most emoji, goes out as its Unicode keysym like any other character, as `wtype` sends it. Chromium cuts a keysym's character to 16 bits, so it types a wrong character there whatever the input route."*

### Workaround and additional context

Suggested fix:
1. Generalize the `CHROMIUM_CODES` + `BORROWABLE` (`F13..=F24`) XKB keymap planner in `wayland/niri/keyboard.rs` so all `zwp_virtual_keyboard_v1` compositors (`labwc`, `sway`, `hyprland`, `niri`) use the native Rust virtual-keyboard keymap planner instead of shelling out to `wtype`.
2. When `text` contains non-BMP characters (`c as u32 > 0xFFFF`, such as Emoji) on Wayland, deliver the non-BMP segment via AT-SPI `EditableText` or a transient clipboard paste (`wl-copy` + `Ctrl+V` with prior clipboard restoration) so Chromium/Electron receives the full UTF-8 code points intact.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Feature]: Support parallel_mouse_drag on wlroots Wayland via zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1 without requiring CUA_INJECT_SOCKET
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On standard wlroots Wayland compositors (`labwc`, `sway`, `hyprland`) that expose `zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1`, calling `parallel_mouse_drag` unconditionally refuses with:
`parallel_mouse_drag requires the cua-compositor inject socket on Wayland (set CUA_INJECT_SOCKET to the cua-compositor control socket), or run the target under X11.`
This prevents agents running in standard Wayland sessions from executing multi-pointer drag gestures (`parallel_mouse_drag`).

### Desired outcome

When `wayland::is_wayland()` is true and `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` is not set, `parallel_mouse_drag` should drive concurrent `ZwlrVirtualPointerV1` virtual pointers via `zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1` (reusing the multi-cursor architecture in `wayland/persistent_vptr.rs` and `wayland::window_local_to_output`), rather than immediately bailing out.

### Current workaround

Currently users on standard wlroots Wayland must either fall back to sequential single-pointer `drag` calls or run a custom `cua-compositor` with `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET`.

### Affected components and platforms

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/parallel_mouse_drag.rs` (`invoke`, lines 136-148), `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/persistent_vptr.rs`, `wayland/mod.rs`.

### Alternatives and prior art

X11 MPX (`send_parallel_virtual_pointer_drags`) only works on X11, and `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` is only available in custom `cua-compositor` builds.

### Implementation ideas

In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/persistent_vptr.rs`, the owner thread already manages a `HashMap<String, ActivePointer>` where each `cursor_id` binds its own independent `ZwlrVirtualPointerV1` instance on the Wayland connection.
In `parallel_mouse_drag.rs:142-148`, instead of returning an error on native Wayland, translate each drag item's waypoints via `wayland::window_local_to_output`, bind a per-item `ZwlrVirtualPointerV1`, press all buttons, step through the interpolated motion frames in lockstep across all virtual pointers, and release all buttons.

title: fix(spaces): New Space Continue did nothing for a Windows image on a Windows PC
body:
## Problem
In Cua Spaces Local on Windows, New Space > Windows > image `ghcr.io/trycua/windows:11` (any Windows image), pressing Continue did nothing: no error, no progress.

## Root cause
`wizard.reduce` (the `Next` action) decided whether Continue is allowed with `view(&s, env)`, which is the view *as a Mac* (`view_on(.., SpaceOs::Macos)`). On a Mac a Windows image is "coming soon" (`windows_soon`), so `can_continue` was false and `Next` was a silent no-op, while the view the person sees (`wizard.view` with `hostOs: "windows"`) showed Continue enabled. Reduce and view disagreed about the host system. Also affects `microvm_support`-dependent checks. Present on main; independent of the windows image aliases in #6631 (which only add the `windows:11` presets).

## Fix
- `wizard::reduce_on(state, action, env, os)`; `reduce` stays as the Mac default (Swift/FFI callers unchanged), like `view`/`view_on`.
- `wizard.reduce` dispatch accepts `hostOs`; `wizardReduce` in the web bridge and the desktop `NewSpaceWizard` pass `hostOs()` on every reduce call.

## Tests
- Rust: `continue_advances_a_windows_image_on_a_windows_pc` (Windows host advances, Mac host stays on step 0). `cargo test -p cua-spaces-app-core --lib wizard`: 58 passed.
- Vitest: `NewSpaceWizard.test.tsx` "go on to the next step on a Windows PC when Continue is enabled" (not run locally: needs the wasm core build; run in CI).

## Verified in the real app
Before: installed Cua Spaces Local, New Space > Windows > `ghcr.io/trycua/windows:11`, Continue clicked (UIA invoke): stays on "Choose a system". After rebuilding with `scripts/install-local.ps1` (from #install-local branch + this commit) and repeating: Continue goes to Resources (4 cores / 8 GB, "Virtual machine").

## Notes / dependencies
- Runtime requirements are already surfaced by the wizard (e.g. Linux shows "This PC cannot run container Spaces: ... missing: a running container engine"; Windows VM needs QEMU ready). The managed runtimes and disk-space checks are being done in the separate runtime PR; not duplicated here.
- Seen, not fixed here: on the Resources step the fact reads "Available 49 GB on this Mac" on a Windows PC.
- `bin/ci --quick` here: rustfmt, web typecheck, design lint, image refs ok; the SPDX check fails only on files this PR does not touch (cua-spacesd-html5 assets, cua-driver-bench taskpack).

title: [Feature]: Support set_window_frame on labwc / wlroots Wayland via compositor IPC and wlr-foreign-toplevel state requests
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On `labwc` and generic wlroots Wayland sessions (such as `linuxserver/*` / Selkies desktop containers), calling `set_window_frame` always fails with:
`set_window_frame: this Wayland compositor exposes no protocol that permits a client to set another top-level window's geometry`
(`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/set_window_frame.rs:31-35`).

### Desired outcome

Allow `set_window_frame` to succeed on `labwc` / wlroots Wayland sessions by:
1. Supporting compositor IPC geometry commands when `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/labwc.sock` (see #6714) is available, or Xwayland `configure_window` when the target surface is an Xwayland window.
2. Supporting `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1::set_maximized` / `unset_maximized` / `set_fullscreen` when requested bounds match the output dimensions.

### Current workaround

Currently callers must skip `set_window_frame` on `labwc` or rely on pre-configured `rc.xml` window rules.

### Affected components and platforms

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/set_window_frame.rs`, `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/wayland/mod.rs`.

### Alternatives and prior art

Related to #6714 (`labwc.sock` IPC support) and #5327 (Wayland compositor support tracking).

### Implementation ideas

In `tools/set_window_frame.rs` and `wayland/mod.rs`:
1. Route `labwc` sessions through `labwc_ipc` (when supported) or check if the requested `(x, y, width, height)` matches the primary output geometry from `get_screen_size`.
2. When the requested frame matches the output size (or when `labwc.sock` confirms the window is already maximized at those exact bounds), apply `zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1::set_maximized` and verify the resulting geometry via `labwc.sock`.

title: [Feature]: Implement cua-driver autostart subcommand on Linux (systemd --user unit and XDG/container service detection)
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### User problem

Running `cua-driver autostart status` (or `enable` / `disable` / `kick`) on Linux currently fails with exit code 1:
`cua-driver autostart is currently Windows-only`
(`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/autostart.rs:16-19`). This is the only CLI subcommand out of all 28 `cua-driver` CLI commands that fails on Linux.

### Desired outcome

Implement `cua-driver autostart {status|enable|disable|kick}` on Linux:
1. On systemd desktop sessions (`systemctl --user`), manage `~/.config/systemd/user/cua-driver-serve.service`.
2. On non-systemd / container desktop environments (such as s6-overlay / XDG autostart containers where `cua-driver serve` is managed by init or `~/.config/autostart/cua-driver.desktop`), allow `cua-driver autostart status` to detect the active daemon / XDG autostart entry and return `registered (running)` (exit 0) instead of failing with a Windows-only error.

### Current workaround

Users currently have to manually create systemd user units, XDG `.desktop` files, or container s6 init scripts, and `cua-driver autostart status` still exits with code 1.

### Affected components and platforms

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/autostart.rs` (`#[cfg(target_os = "linux")] mod platform`).

### Alternatives and prior art

`scripts/install-local.sh --autostart` handles initial install-time setup, but the `cua-driver autostart` CLI subcommand itself remains stubbed out on Linux.

### Implementation ideas

Add a `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")] mod platform` implementation in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/autostart.rs`:
- `enable()`: write `~/.config/systemd/user/cua-driver-serve.service` (if `systemctl --user` is available) or `~/.config/autostart/cua-driver-serve.desktop` as fallback.
- `status()`: check `systemctl --user is-enabled/is-active cua-driver-serve.service`, `~/.config/autostart/cua-driver-serve.desktop`, or `/etc/xdg/autostart` / running daemon status, returning `Status::RegisteredRunning`, `Status::RegisteredIdle`, or `Status::NotRegistered`.

title: [Bug]: _install-rust.sh leaves CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION at 0.38.0 and omits cua-cursor-theme symlink on macOS
body:
### Primary area

Build, packaging, or release

### Summary

The published installer `https://cua.ai/driver/_install-rust.sh` (and `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:671` on `main` / `v0.40.2`) still hardcodes `CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION="0.38.0"`, causing `--channel stable` installs to install stale v0.38.0 instead of the latest stable release (v0.40.2). In addition, on macOS it only symlinks `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` (`_install-rust.sh:1435`) and omits `~/.local/bin/cua-cursor-theme`.

### Reproduction

1. Run the official stable installer on macOS:
   `curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh | bash`
2. Check the installed version:
   `cua-driver --version`
3. Run `cua-driver cursor-theme list --json` when `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS` is not in `PATH` (only `~/.local/bin` is in `PATH`).

### Expected behavior

1. The stable installer should install the latest published stable release (`cua-driver 0.40.2`).
2. `cua-driver cursor-theme list --json` should locate `cua-cursor-theme` via symlink in `~/.local/bin` or by resolving `realpath` of the `cua-driver` executable.

### Actual behavior

1. The installer logs `using baked release: cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0` and installs `0.38.0` instead of `0.40.2`.
2. `cua-driver cursor-theme` fails with `No such file or directory (os error 2)` unless `~/.local/bin/cua-cursor-theme` is manually symlinked to `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-cursor-theme`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver v0.40.2 (commit dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2 (arm64, Apple Silicon)
Application/browser/window system/image: Official installer script `_install-rust.sh`

### Evidence

Verified in `v0.40.2` source (`dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c`):
- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:670-672`:
  ```bash
  # ~~~ BAKED_VERSION: auto-updated after release publication — do not edit ~~~
  CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION="0.38.0" # published-installer-version
  # ~~~ END_BAKED_VERSION ~~~
  ```
- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_install-rust.sh:1435` only symlinks `cua-driver`:
  ```bash
  ln -sf "$APP_BINARY" "$BIN_LINK"
  ```

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround:
1. Strip `CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION` before piping to bash so the installer falls back to GitHub Releases API resolution:
   `curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/_install-rust.sh | sed 's/^CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION=.*/CUA_DRIVER_RS_BAKED_VERSION=""/' | bash -s -- --channel stable`
2. Manually symlink `ln -sf /Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-cursor-theme ~/.local/bin/cua-cursor-theme`.

title: [Bug]: browser_download hardcodes a 30-second timeout with no configurable timeout_ms parameter
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`browser_download` hardcodes `const DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30)` (`browser/download.rs:32`) with no configurable `timeout_ms` parameter in its input schema. Any approved download that takes longer than 30 seconds fails with `browser_action_unavailable: the approved browser download did not complete within 30 seconds` (and attempts `remove_proven_partial`), even while the browser is actively downloading.

### Reproduction

1. Start `cua-driver serve --permission-mode unrestricted --dangerously-bypass-approvals`.
2. Attach to or prepare a Chromium window via `browser_prepare` and `get_browser_state`.
3. Trigger a large file download (>30s over the current network) via `browser_download` with a valid `ref` and `destination_root`.

### Expected behavior

`browser_download` should accept an optional `timeout_ms` parameter (or track active download byte progress before timing out) so large legitimate downloads can complete without failing at a fixed 30s wall-clock cutoff.

### Actual behavior

After 30 seconds, `browser_download` returns:
`browser_action_unavailable: the approved browser download did not complete within 30 seconds`
even though `.crdownload` is actively growing in `destination_root`.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver v0.40.2 (commit dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2 (arm64, Apple Silicon)
Application/browser/window system/image: Google Chrome / Chromium CDP via `browser_download`

### Evidence

Verified in `v0.40.2` source (`dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c`):
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/download.rs:32`:
  ```rust
  const DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
  ```
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/download.rs:498-503`:
  ```rust
  remove_proven_partial(&destination_root, observed_guid.as_deref());
  BrowserRefusal::new(
      BrowserRefusalCode::BrowserActionUnavailable,
      "the approved browser download did not complete within 30 seconds",
  )
  .to_tool_result()
  ```

### Workaround and additional context

Suggested fix: Add an optional `timeout_ms` parameter to `browser_download` (e.g., default 30000ms, max 600000ms) or extend the deadline while `Browser.downloadProgress` events report `receivedBytes` increasing.

title: [Bug]: get_window_state / get_desktop_state omit capture_id and parse_visual_regions only returns a count in MCP text content
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

Over MCP, `get_window_state` and `get_desktop_state` omit `capture_id` from their `content[0].text` summary header, and `parse_visual_regions` (`perception_tools.rs:162`) returns only `"Parsed N visual regions"` in `content[0].text` while placing `capture_id` and `regions` exclusively in `structuredContent`. MCP hosts/agents that only forward `content[].text` to the model (such as Antigravity) cannot read `capture_id` or the parsed visual regions.

### Reproduction

1. With `cua-perception` installed, call `get_window_state` or `get_desktop_state` over `cua-driver mcp` stdio.
2. Inspect `result.content[0].text`: observe `window_id=112507 pid=24388 size=460x816 elements=34 snapshot_id=s00000001` (no `capture_id=...`).
3. Call `parse_visual_regions` with the `capture_id` from `structuredContent`.
4. Inspect `result.content[0].text`: observe it contains only `"Parsed 5 visual regions"` with no region bounds, kinds, labels, or text.

### Expected behavior

1. `get_window_state` and `get_desktop_state` text headers should include `capture_id=<id>` alongside `snapshot_id=<id>` when a capture is registered.
2. `parse_visual_regions` text content should include a compact Markdown/text listing of the parsed regions (id, kind, bounds, confidence, text/label) in addition to `structuredContent`, similar to #4719.

### Actual behavior

1. `get_window_state` and `get_desktop_state` omit `capture_id` from `content[].text`.
2. `parse_visual_regions` returns only `"Parsed N visual regions"` in `content[0].text`, making the tool unusable in MCP clients that do not expose `structuredContent` to the LLM.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver v0.40.2 (commit dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c) + cua-perception 0.2.1
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2 (arm64, Apple Silicon)
Application/browser/window system/image: MCP stdio (`cua-driver mcp`) with Antigravity vs Codex

### Evidence

Verified in `v0.40.2` source (`dd0f673f2ea6352e767d89800d4636d73cf82a3c`):
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/perception_tools.rs:161-163`:
  ```rust
  let structured = serde_json::to_value(&output).expect("visual output serializes");
  ToolResult::text(format!("Parsed {} visual regions", output.regions.len()))
      .with_structured(structured)
  ```
- Raw MCP wire response:
  `content: [{"text": "Parsed 5 visual regions", "type": "text"}]`

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround for text-only MCP hosts: Use `run_script` (`const st = await app.getState(); return st.capture_id;`) to read `capture_id`, or shell out to `cua-driver call parse_visual_regions`.
Related issue: #4719 (`list_windows` MCP text content is only a count; window rows exist only in `structuredContent`).

title: fix(spaces): every agent message is appended to the thread, child Spaces work from inside a Space, and child agents show in the chat
body:
## What

Three fixes for what an agent does in a Space thread.

### 1. Every message an agent posts is appended
The thread held one reply per task, glued from the turn's text and posted when the turn ended. In a real thread this dropped messages: an agent said "Creating the macOS space...", its turn ended, a background job failed, the agent woke on its own and explained, and that explanation arrived after the task was closed and was never posted. A streaming "live" line was also replaced by the final reply.

Now each stretch of agent text between tool calls is its own thread entry, appended in order as it is written (`Persistent::post_said`, `cua_agents::subagents::said`). Nothing is replaced, glued or dropped:
- text that arrives after the turn ended is posted after 1.5 s without growth;
- posts are idempotent (a restart or a re-read never repeats one);
- the agent can `thread_reply` under a task it already closed (appended, the task keeps its state), and a reply it already posted word for word is not added twice (a restarted bridge runs old calls again);
- a turn that said nothing still ends with `Finished.`, and a failed turn always says why;
- the "working" row stays status UI; it shows the message being written until it lands as an entry.

The ugly first message is handled in what the agent is told: the thread framing, the `thread_reply` tool text and the home brief now say that everything written between tool calls is posted in order, to say in one short sentence what it will do before a long job, not to repeat itself or narrate starting up (the app shows that), and how to make a child computer. A task is quoted once when an agent says several things under it (web and phone).

### 2. Child Spaces from inside a Space
Reproduced with a real agent in a Linux home Space. Causes:
- the Space's MCP tools `create_space`, `delete_space`, `space_bash` and the other child-Space tools had no reviewed risk classification, so the MCP server refused every call ("no reviewed risk classification"). They are classified now, with a test that every tool the Space adds is.
- `cua sb create` inside a Space failed with a bare "unsupported". It now says to use `cua spaces create IMAGE --name NAME`, `cua sb exec NAME`, `cua spaces delete --force NAME`.
- A child macOS or VM computer needs `cua-netgw` next to `cua`; the Local build never bundled it and the refusal quoted a build script. `install-local.sh` now builds and bundles it when Go is installed. A full disk or a missing gateway reaches the agent in words for the person (what is missing, that retrying will not help), not `cua cache prune`.
- Verified in a Local build: an agent's `cua spaces create linux`, `cua sb exec`, then `cua spaces delete --force` from inside a home Space work.

### 3. Child agents in the chat, desktop and phone
Core: events carry `parent_tool_id`; `cua_agents::subagents::fold` derives each subagent (task, running/done/failed, steps, result). The thread records one note when a subagent starts and one when it ends, and one for each child Space made while the agent works; the live row carries the running ones. Web and phone fold a subagent's notes into one quiet row (title, state, steps, result behind a disclosure) and show a child Space as a row with an Open link. The CLI log indents a subagent's steps.

## Evidence
- Real Claude in a Local build with a separate home: a narrated multi-step turn gave seven separate, ordered messages; a subagent turn gave the start note, a finished note with its result and the agent's use of it.
- Tests: `agent_all_messages.rs` (8: order, no duplicates, a message after the turn ended, late `thread_reply`, the same reply run twice, a silent turn, subagent notes and the live row), `subagents.rs` (7), `children/api.rs` (3), a spacesd test that every child-Space tool is classified, web and phone fold tests.
- `durable_member_wiring` has two failures that are the same on `origin/main`.

Not verified: the phone layout was checked by tests only; a child macOS computer was not run (disk).

title: fix(spaces-mobile): send the registered one-slash OAuth redirect
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Sign-in on the Cua Spaces phone app fails. The cua.ai sign-in sheet shows "Invalid parameter: redirect_uri" and the user cannot sign in. The app sends `redirect_uri=ai.cua.spaces://oauth/callback` (two slashes), because `expo-auth-session`'s `makeRedirectUri({ scheme, path })` always puts `//` after a custom scheme. The `cua-spaces-mobile` client accepts exactly `ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback` (one slash), as `apps/cua-spaces-mobile/docs/SETUP.md` and `src/auth/config.ts` already say.
- What changed: The app builds the redirect from the configured scheme and path with one slash (`ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback`) and sends that same value in the authorization request and in the code exchange. The scheme in `app.json` (`ai.cua.spaces`) is unchanged, so the callback still opens the app.

## Related work

No issue. Before opening this, I searched open and closed issues and pull requests (`redirect_uri`, `oauth/callback`, `makeRedirectUri`, `spaces-mobile` sign-in). I also checked `src/auth/session.ts` in the 82 open pull requests created since 1 Nov 2026. None of them changes the redirect, and `main` at 39ae68a still sends two slashes.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Not required. This is an app-internal bug fix.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Phone sign-in against `auth.cua.ai` works again. There are no API, CLI, MCP, protocol or permission changes. A staging or custom issuer (`EXPO_PUBLIC_CUA_OIDC_ISSUER`) must register the same one-slash redirect, which `docs/SETUP.md` already requires.
- Risk and rollback: Low. The change is one line in `src/auth/session.ts` plus one test. To roll back, revert this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - New `__tests__/session-signin.test.ts` drives `session.signIn()` through a mocked `expo-auth-session`. It checks that the `AuthRequest` and `exchangeCodeAsync` both get `ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback`.
    - Before the fix (current `main`), it fails:
      ```
      -   "redirectUri": "ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback",
      +   "redirectUri": "ai.cua.spaces://oauth/callback",
      ```
    - After the fix, it passes.
  - `pnpm typecheck` passes.
  - `pnpm test` (all of `apps/cua-spaces-mobile`): 32 suites passed, 1 skipped; 179 tests passed, 1 skipped.
  - `bin/ci` and `bin/ci --quick` pass (SPDX headers, image refs).
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Provider check (6 Nov 2026, reproducible without an account). This sends the authorization request the app sends (client `cua-spaces-mobile`, PKCE S256) and changes only the redirect:
    ```sh
    for r in 'ai.cua.spaces://oauth/callback' 'ai.cua.spaces:/oauth/callback'; do
      enc=$(python3 -c 'import sys,urllib.parse;print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[1],safe=""))' "$r")
      curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$r -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" \
        "https://auth.cua.ai/realms/cyclops-cs/protocol/openid-connect/auth?client_id=cua-spaces-mobile&redirect_uri=$enc&response_type=code&scope=openid&state=probe&code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeKt8URWbuGjSaR2YsKk&code_challenge_method=S256"
    done
    ```
    - Before (two slashes): HTTP 400, page "Sign-in didn't finish" with "Invalid parameter: redirect_uri".
    - After (one slash): HTTP 200, the "Sign in to Cua Spaces" login form.
  - iPhone (6 Nov 2026): I installed a build of `apps/cua-spaces-mobile` from `main` on a physical iPhone.
    - Before: "Sign in" opened the sign-in sheet, and it showed "Invalid parameter: redirect_uri".
    - After, with this change: sign-in finished, the app returned from the sheet, and the phone enrolled and listed its computers.
    - That device build also carried unrelated local patches (a custom relay setting). Those patches are not part of this pull request.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - No GitHub workflow runs the `apps/cua-spaces-mobile` Jest suite (`spaces-mobile` in `.github/ci-areas.json` maps only to docs links and license checks), so the tests above are local runs.
  - Android was not tested on a device. It uses the same `ai.cua.spaces` scheme from `app.json`.
  - `pnpm proto:check` reports drift in `host_pb.ts` and `tunnel_pb.ts`. The same drift is on unmodified `main`, and this change does not touch protos.

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: fix(spaces): say This PC (not This Mac) for the current computer on Windows
body:
## What
The Cua Spaces UI called the current computer "This Mac" / "on this Mac" / "your Mac" on Windows (Agents page "On This Mac", resource warnings, Settings, nudges, CLI columns...). It now says "This PC" on Windows, "This machine" on Linux (the existing convention in `host-os.ts`, `SpaceOs::this_machine`), and keeps "This Mac" on macOS.

## How (driven by the host OS the shell reports, no UA sniffing)
- **Core answers, one place:** `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/bridge/host-words.ts` words every string of an app-core answer for `hostOs()` (Electron's `process.platform`) where `wasmCore.call` hands it to the page. Only the phrases that mean this computer ("This Mac", "this Mac", "your Mac") are replaced. Text about macOS itself (Lume, Keychain, Finder, Xcode, Intel, Touch ID, Apple), "Mac mini" and other Macs are left alone. Display only: nothing is written back, so a Mac user's stored names are untouched and a Windows user's stored "This Mac" displays as "This PC".
- **Web strings that were hardcoded:** Agents page and empty state, empty home, Driver page, Settings quick set-up error, resources (low-disk warning, "uses about X on ..."), add-computer sheet name, first-run default place, the this-computer desktop chat error, the "can't make a Space" toast: now use `thisComputerLabel()/thisComputerText()` (host-labels).
- **Desktop shell:** the Space-ready notification says "this PC" on Windows (was "this machine").
- **CLI/Rust:** `cua_spaces::resources::words::Host` (Mac/Pc/Other); the low-disk warning, `cua host status` "This PC" block and the `DISK ON THIS PC` column follow the system the binary runs on (`warning_on`, `header_on`, `this_mac_lines_on` take the host; the old functions use `Host::current()`). The clap help no longer names "THIS MAC".

## Choices
Linux says "This machine" (what `SpaceOs::this_machine` and `THIS_MACHINE` already use), not "This computer".
Left on purpose: macOS-only copy (Keychain, Lume, teleport, Local Network, notch, SwiftUI app), demo adapters and fixtures, JSON/API keys and ids (`thisMac`, `this-mac`). `cua-vmm` `auto.rs` wording ("this Mac's own container engine") is owned by the managed-runtime PR; `storage.rs` volume naming is in #6724.

## Tests

title: [Bug]: Cua Volume on a bucket without versioning (Cloudflare R2) reads old cached bytes after another machine rewrites a file
body:
### Primary area

Other (Cua Volume, libs/cua/crates/cua-volume)

### Summary

When Cua Volume uses an S3-compatible bucket that has no object versioning (Cloudflare R2), a machine that has read a file once keeps serving those old bytes from its block cache after another machine rewrites the file. On macOS the mount shows the new size, but the content is the old bytes followed by zero bytes, so the file looks empty or damaged. `cua volume cat` on the same machine shows the correct content.

### Reproduction

1. Point two machines at one R2 bucket: `cua volume config set --backend s3 --endpoint https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com --region auto --bucket <bucket>`, keys through `cua volume config set-keys`. R2 does not offer bucket versioning.
2. On machine A (Linux): `python3 -c "import sys;sys.stdout.write('version-1 '*20)" | cua volume put public/t/a.txt -` (200 bytes).
3. On machine B (macOS), read it through the mount once: `xxd ~/"Cua Volume"/public/t/a.txt`. This fills B's block cache.
4. On machine A: write a longer version to the same path: `'version-2 '*60` (600 bytes).
5. On machine B, after the change feed delivers the change (10 s, and again 45 s later), read through the mount again, and with `cua volume cat public/t/a.txt`.

It happens every time.

### Expected behavior

The mount on machine B shows the new content (600 bytes of `version-2 `), the same as `cua volume cat`.

### Actual behavior

The mount on machine B stayed wrong at both 10 s and 45 s after each write. `cua volume cat` on machine B was correct every time.

```
v1  200 bytes  first read on B, correct: md5 8f7fabf6d6daba897e17413f8d9cf0b3

v2  600 bytes  correct md5 5f5f50e76a422d98b1dbad3ae49242d6 (cat on B matches)
    mount on B: size 600, md5 1d9885a1ca9523e930b3a870e50d809e
    00000000: 7665 7273 696f 6e2d 3120 7665 7273 696f  version-1 versio
    00000250: 0000 0000 0000 0000                      ........

v3   30 bytes  correct md5 7a0b303c1aec057b4b15b00be803f833 (cat on B matches)
    mount on B: size 30, md5 cb3d2ef45cf6844a04c812b7e3941503
    00000000: 7665 7273 696f 6e2d 3120 7665 7273 696f  version-1 versio
    00000010: 6e2d 3120 7665 7273 696f 6e2d 3120       n-1 version-1
```

The v2 md5 is exactly the 200 bytes of v1 plus 400 zero bytes. The v3 md5 is exactly the first 30 bytes of v1.

Other cases I measured:

- **Same-size rewrite (200 to 200 bytes):** the mount on B kept the old content (md5 `1e8999e2d8e621aeaa43446054613807`, `cat` gives `59bebf3bce5b31aa18fccaf1817b36f5`). The size does not change and there are no zero bytes, so nothing shows the file is wrong.
- **Write through machine A's FUSE mount instead of `cua volume put`:** same result on B (size 600, md5 `fc91e232f3b989b0e697d8ea7249fe9b`, which is the old 200 bytes plus 400 zero bytes).
- **Controls, both correct on B:** a file B had not read before the rewrite, and a file whose first version was 0 bytes.
- **macOS page cache:** a read on B with `F_NOCACHE` returned the same old bytes, so this does not look like the NFS client's cache.
- **The machine that wrote the file (Linux FUSE mount, machine A), so this does not need a second machine:** 35 s after `put` of a 600-byte rewrite, `stat` gave 600 and a read returned the old 200 bytes. Reads right after each `put` failed with `Input/output error`, and the first version read correctly at 35 s.

Version ids:

- `cua volume put` prints an id for each write: `7e5e4dca1a08e5c8a28bc8bf2310fac2` (v1), `7e5e4dc9d8c6e300b5a22caec87667a6` (v2), `7e5e4dc9044ccefc1690321de773542d` (v3).
- `cua volume history` fails: `NotImplemented: ListObjectVersions not implemented`.
- `cua volume cat --version <id>` with an id from `put` fails: `NotImplemented: versionId not implemented`.

### Environment

- Cua Spaces 0.22.0 (`cua` 0.10.1, `cua-spacesd` 0.12.1) on macOS arm64 (Volume mounted over the localhost NFS server) and on Linux cua-spaces 0.21.0 (`cua` 0.10.1, `cua-spacesd` 0.12.2), aarch64, Ubuntu 24.04 (Volume mounted over FUSE).
- cua-volume is unchanged from cua-spaces-v0.21.0 through cua-spaces-v0.21.1 and main (39ae68a).
- Store: Cloudflare R2 (`--region auto`), no bucket versioning.

### Evidence

Unit test that reproduces it without a bucket: a test backend over `FsBackend` that returns empty version ids (as `S3Backend::head` appears to on R2, `out.version_id().unwrap_or_default()`) and reports `remote() = true`, two devices on it with their own block caches and change feeds. Device A writes `{"v":1}`, device B reads it through its `Vfs`, A writes a longer version, B waits for the new size, then reads. On main it fails:

```
assertion `left == right` failed: the Mac read stale cached bytes
  left: "{\"v\":1}"
 right: "{\"v\":2,\"name\":\"Ada\",\"model\":\"opus\"}"
```

Why, as far as I can tell from the code:

- `cache::block_id` keys a block by backend identity, key, version and block index.
- On R2 a `put` returns a version id, but `Vfs::read` takes its version from `head`, and the reads behave as if that id is `""` (I did not capture the `head` response directly). So every content of a key gets the same block ids.
- `Vfs::read` pins the new object (`head`: new size), then `Streamer::read` hits the old block in `BlockCache::read`. It returns the old bytes. The read of the rest returns nothing with `eof = false`, and the macOS NFS client fills the rest of the file size with zeros. A shorter rewrite returns the old bytes cut to the new size.
- `Vfs::ensure_dirty` copies the current content through the same path, so an in-place edit on B can also write the stale bytes back to the bucket.
- The `Input/output error` right after a `put` looks like the same missing versioning by a different path: the writer pins the id from `put` (`PIN_TTL` is 30 s), and R2 refuses a read with that id. The empty-id fix below would not cover it.

### Workaround and additional context

- Workaround: a bucket with versioning on (AWS S3, MinIO). I found none for R2.
- The app's Settings > Storage refuses a bucket with versioning off (`versioning_off`), but `cua volume config set --backend s3` accepts it without a warning, and `versioning_help` describes R2 as working without history.
- Possible fix (I can open a PR): when a version id is empty or `"null"`, `Streamer::read` reads the range from the store instead of the block cache. A fuller fix could key such blocks by etag and fetch them with `If-Match`.
- I searched open and closed issues and pull requests (Volume, R2, NFS, empty, truncate, stale, cache, sync) and found no report of this. Related but different: #6321 / #6322, #6238, #5795.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep idle-end launch ownership only until a terminal end
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: after the 5-minute idle sweep, `kill_app` refused a process the same session label had launched, with `foreign_process_termination_denied`. #6553 fixed that by keeping a session's launch records across an idle end. Review of #6553 found three ways the kept records could outlive or erase their lifecycle. This PR ships #6553 with those three fixed.
- What changed:
  - An idle end leaves a session dormant, not finished. Every later terminal end runs the end hooks again with its own reason and drops the records: `end_session`, transport teardown and revocation. Before this, teardown and revocation listed only live sessions and skipped idled ones. A terminal end also overrides an idle end that is still waiting on an in-flight dispatch.
  - Each isolated browser keeps its launch fingerprint. Browser ownership is re-proved against the live process, not the pid alone. Reaping the browser removes only its own record, so a later `launch_app` that reused the pid keeps its record.
  - Revival is refused while an end's cleanup is still pending. This covers `start_session` and the next-call recreation of an unnamed session. So an end's cleanup can no longer erase the launches of the episode that revived it. An idle cleanup pass that a terminal end overtakes also runs the terminal hooks. Capture-scope clearing now happens inside that tracked cleanup.

## Related work

Salvaged from #6553 (AlexFalher). Their commit is cherry-picked with `-x` and keeps its author. The follow-up commits are separate.

Refs CUA-3651

RFC: not required. No SDK, CLI, MCP or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a session idled out and restarted with the same label can kill what it launched. Ending it, closing its transport or revoking it afterwards drops that ownership. Shared core, so macOS, Windows and Linux behave the same.
- Risk and rollback: this touches the session-end state machine (end hooks, revival admission). A revival that races an unfinished end now gets the existing `session cleanup is incomplete` refusal and must retry. Before this, it could succeed early. Rollback is a revert.
- Size: production lines exceed the target because the end-hook rerun and the revival barrier both have to change in `session.rs`.

## Validation

- Focused tests: seven regression tests cover terminal ends after an idle end, browser pid reuse, end/revival races and a deferred idle end. Each one fails on the code before its fix and passes after.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `cua-driver-core`, `platform-macos`, `cua-driver-sdk` and `cua-driver`, plus `cargo check --workspace --tests`.
- macOS: the Lume guest full matrix passed at the PR head (183 cells).
- Known gaps: Linux and Windows platform tests and desktop E2E did not run here. They are left to CI.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep polling macOS grants after the permissions gate times out
body:
## Why

CUA-3664. If Accessibility or Screen Recording was not granted within the macOS permissions gate's 10-minute deadline, the daemon stayed gated until it was restarted. `wait_for_grants` returned an error at the deadline, `main.rs` cleared the pending flag only when the gate passed, and stderr told the user to restart the daemon. Now a timed-out gate keeps polling in the background, so a later grant opens tool calls in the running daemon.

## What changed

- `serve::settle_permission_gate` now owns the pending flag after the gate. A pass clears it right away. A timeout starts a `cua-permissions-poll` thread that clears it once the wait succeeds. `main.rs` makes one call to it.
- `GateOpts::after_timeout()` returns the options for that wait: no deadline, a fresh helper-process probe every 5s, and a status line every 5 minutes.
- The timeout message no longer tells the user to restart. It says tool calls stay gated while the daemon keeps checking.

## Scope

Covers only the macOS serve gate after its deadline. The daemon still never runs a TCC preflight in its own process. Each poll uses the short-lived helper probe, as before. Moving the gate check into `SdkAdapter::invoke_raw` (the MCP bypass) is a separate ticket.

## Blast Radius

Affects only macOS `serve` launches that hit the gate deadline. Those launches used to stay gated until restarted. Now they keep one more thread that starts a probe child process every 5s until both grants arrive. The opt-out, embedded and already-granted paths return `Ok`, so they never start the thread.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks for `platform-macos` and `cua-driver` passed on macOS: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` on all targets, and the full test suites.
- New tests: `wait_after_timeout_picks_up_a_late_grant` drives the wait with an injected probe, and `a_late_grant_reopens_tool_calls_without_a_restart` covers the pass, never-granted and late-grant paths through the pending-response check. Two mutations turn the second test red: dropping the clear in the poll thread, and restoring the old terminal timeout.
- Not run: the macOS Lume lane, because another run held the Lume lock, and a real post-timeout TCC grant in a guest. Linux and Windows are not affected.
