title: fix(cua-driver): one macOS focus arbiter decides every activation undo
body:
## Why

On macOS, five watchers undo a background app's activation: the activation observer, the key-focus guard's revert and order watch, launch_app's demotion loop and watchdog, the browser attach watcher, and the background-pixel restore. Each one decided on its own whether an activation was the driver's or the user's. Some checked the intentional-activation epoch, some checked recent hardware input, and some checked neither. `apps::activate_pid` and `make_exact_window_key` never counted as driver activations (F17), so a watcher could undo a front the driver had just asked for. Now one arbiter makes that decision for all of them.

CUA-3671

## What changed

- New `focus_arbiter` module. It owns the driver-activation epoch (`note_intentional`), the hardware-input check moved from `key_focus_guard`, and `UndoWatch`, which is one action's right to undo. `UndoWatch::decide()` returns `Undo` only when no driver activation and no hardware mouse-down or modifier change has happened since the watch was armed. Once a watch returns `Leave` it keeps returning `Leave`, and every lease and loop of that action shares the result. So a user's switch is not undone later, after the input is more than a second old. The arbiter also holds the detached window-watch lease. `window_change_detector`'s `TAIL`/`end_tail` and its separate epoch are deleted.
- Every undo path asks the action's watch: `focus_steal` entries (`snapshot_matches`), `key_focus_guard` revert, launch_app's pre, post and watchdog leases plus its demotion loop (one watch per launch), the browser attach watcher, and the click/drag pixel restore. Window-order restores check only the epoch, since they already require the user's app to be frontmost.
- `apps::activate_pid` and `skylight::make_exact_window_key` now call `note_intentional`, as bring_to_front, launch_app and foreground delivery already did. Putting the user's own app back goes through the new `apps::reactivate_app` and `skylight::return_key_to`, which do not count as driver activations. Before this split, an undo would have cancelled the very watcher doing it.

## Scope

macOS `platform-macos` only. This covers the S, M and L steps of the CUA-3671 migration in one change. It leaves the overlapping open PRs https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4652 (sibling window raise in foreground HID delivery) and https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6271 (isolated browser cold-launch guard) alone. If #6271 lands, its leases should arm through `begin_suppression_for` with one `UndoWatch`, the way launch_app's do.

## Tradeoffs

- invoke_menu's foreground path restores the user's prior window through `focus_exact_window`, which now counts as a driver activation. That is deliberate. The restore ends a foreground turn the driver owns, and watchers armed while the target was in front should stand down.
- A small gap remains between an `Undo` decision and the restore call it allows. Closing it would mean holding a lock across Cocoa and SkyLight activation calls that `note_intentional` callers would then wait on. Main has the same gap with its epoch compare.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS background action that arms focus-steal suppression, the key-focus guard, launch_app and browser attach. Undo now happens in fewer cases, never in more: there is no new undo path, and every existing one gained a check. The detached lease keeps its id-checked release and its release when the thread spawn fails.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --lib` for `platform-macos` (685 passed, 8 ignored). New unit tests cover the decision table, a Leave staying final across an action's watchers, and observer entries armed before a driver activation.
- The macOS Lume full matrix ran at the head: 179 delivered, 5 expected refusals, 0 failed, recordings for every cell. The standalone-browser lane did not run.

Size limit: production code is over budget because every undo path and every activation caller moves to the arbiter in the same change, and the old TAIL and epoch code is deleted with it.

title: fix(cua-driver): admit per-pid state-capture workers in one critical section
body:
CUA-3675

## Why
`run_state_hook` checked a per-pid abandoned-walk count and only inserted into it later, at timeout, in a separate lock acquisition. Two turns for the same pid could both pass the check and both start a walk of that application. This change makes admission one critical section.

## What changed
- One mutex-guarded `HashMap<i64, Worker>`, where `Worker` is `Running` or `Abandoned { since }`, replaces the abandoned counter. `Entry` does the check and the insert under a single lock.
- The worker thread delivers its result, or removes its `Abandoned` entry, under that same lock. The timeout path calls `try_recv` under the lock before it marks `Abandoned`, so a late result is not lost and no entry leaks. A failed spawn and a panicking hook also free the pid.
- New test `state_hook_admits_one_running_walk_per_pid`: it fails on main and passes here.

## Scope
Only the state-capture worker table in `cua-driver-core/src/recording.rs`. The mutex is its own and shares no invariant with the recorder's other state. Platform snapshot hooks are unchanged.

## Blast Radius
Recording turns on every platform go through `run_state_hook`. A second concurrent walk for a pid whose walk is still running now returns `state_capture_busy`. Before, it started a second walk. Different pids are still independent. Logging and the hook itself run outside the lock.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`, all passing.
- The new test fails at the test-only commit (`left: None, right: Some("state_capture_busy")`) and passes at the fix.
- Not run: Linux and Windows platform crates, and the desktop E2E lanes. The change is in platform-independent core code.

title: fix(cua-driver): commit or roll back browser setup explicitly
body:
## Why
`PendingExistingProfileSetup` relied on `Drop` for rollback on one path. When the protected consent host declined, `approve(...)?` returned early, and the rollback was only spawned from `Drop`, after the refusal had already gone back to the caller. Every other path called `abort` through a `setup_pending` flag plus an `Option` guard.

## What changed
- The guard gets consuming `commit(self)` and `rollback(self, error)` finishers. A `settled` flag replaces the `Option<request>` and the `setup_pending` flag, and the "already finalized" error path goes away.
- Every refusal after setup, the declined-consent path included, goes through `rollback_pending_setup` before it returns.
- `Drop` is only a backstop for a cancelled request. It logs a `warn` when it schedules rollback and an `error` when no runtime is available.

## Scope
Only `browser/prepare.rs` and one test in `browser/v2_tests.rs`. Platform adapters are untouched. A failed commit is still rolled back inside each adapter's `close_for_success`.

## Blast Radius
Existing-profile `browser_prepare` on every platform. The success path and all previous rollback sites behave the same. The only behavior change is that a declined protected consent finishes its rollback before the refusal returns.

## Verification
- New test `declined_consent_rolls_back_pending_setup_before_refusing` fails on the base `prepare.rs` and passes with the fix.
- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and the lib tests for `cua-driver-core`, plus clippy for `platform-macos`, all pass.

CUA-3676

title: fix(cua-driver): report a timed-out capture worker to the next caller
body:
## Why

When a ScreenCaptureKit worker timed out and stayed blocked in Apple's callback, the next caller was refused with the same "already in flight" error it gets during a normal overlapping capture. Nothing told it that the holder was a stalled worker whose caller had already given up (CUA-3677).

## What changed

- `NativeCaptureGate` is now a state machine (`Idle`, `InFlight { ticket }`, `Stalled { ticket, since }`) instead of an `AtomicBool`. A timeout marks the permit `Stalled`, and the worker-owned permit returns the gate to `Idle` when the worker really exits.
- A caller refused by a stalled worker gets "a timed-out ScreenCaptureKit worker is still blocked after N ms", which reaches the shell-fallback error context and the display-capture warning.
- Each permit carries a ticket, so a late timeout cannot mark a newer caller's permit stalled.

## Scope

Covers the window and display capture gates in `platform-macos/src/capture.rs`. Fallback behavior is unchanged: callers still go to `screencapture` on refusal, and the gate still admits one worker at a time.

## Blast Radius

macOS capture only. The change touches the gate type and the refusal text. Locking moved from a single atomic to a short uncontended mutex around state transitions.

## Verification

- `timed_out_native_worker_blocks_replacement_until_original_returns` now asserts the stalled-worker refusal, then that the gate returns to `Idle` after the worker returns. `late_timeout_cannot_mark_a_newer_permit_stalled` covers ticket isolation. Removing `mark_stalled` or the ticket check turns each test red.
- The scoped repository checks (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `capture::` unit tests for `platform-macos`) pass, as does `bin/ci --quick`.
- The macOS Lume focused cell `macos-electron-scroll-ax-background` passes at this head.

title: fix(spaces): start Claude agents on Sonnet 5.5 and list the Claude 5 family
body:
## Problem
In Cua Spaces the Anthropic provider's default model was `claude-haiku-4-5` ("Fast"), so every Home agent and Claude Code run started on it. A run on it did not raise an approval card with the thread tool, asked "Can I proceed?" in plain text, then tried to fake the tool call in bash and looped. The catalog was also behind the current Claude 5 family.

## What changed
- Default Anthropic model is now `claude-sonnet-5-5` (Claude Sonnet 5.5). Agent homes do multi-step tool work, so the default is the one reliable at tool use, not the fastest.
- Model list is the Claude 5 family: Haiku 5.5 (tagged "Fast"), Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1.
- `claude-haiku-4-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` stay accepted as `legacy` rows (new optional `legacy = true` in the provider TOML). They are not shown in the menu unless currently picked, and are never a default. A person who chose Haiku 4.5 keeps it; only people who never chose get the new default.
- The "new prompt starts with the first fast model" rule is gone in both places it lived (`models_view` and the per-account `default_model` in `cua-spaces-app-core`); both now use the provider's default. Fast is still one tap away in the ask box model page.
- Generated files (Rust table, `providers.json`, web `providers.ts`, SwiftUI registry) and the parity golden are regenerated with `cua-connections-gen` and `UPDATE_PARITY=1`.

## Speed question (is Haiku the default on purpose?)
No Home-specific model override exists, and nothing in the warm pool, instant-reply dispatcher or phases path references a model: the default came only from "first fast model" in the picker. The harness start phases (spawn, install, runner start) happen before any model call, so they do not depend on the model; only the final first-token wait does. I did not measure the model-dependent share here, so I make no latency claim; Haiku 5.5 stays one tap away for people who want speed.

## Tests
- Registry: the default model is in the list and is not legacy (all top providers); older Anthropic ids are present and legacy.
- Core: a new Claude prompt defaults to Sonnet 5.5, the menu shows the four 5.x models, Haiku 4.5 is still offered but never the default.
- Web: a saved legacy model id is preserved by `resolveAgent` and `pickAccount`; ask box shows Sonnet 5.5 selected, Haiku 5.5 "Fast", no 4.x row.

Not changed: `cua do` snapshot model and `.github/model-matrix.txt` (separate purposes, not the Spaces default).

title: fix(cua-driver): accept RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE when UIA walks initialise COM
body:
## Why
CUA-3680. `walk_tree` and `walk_native_tree` dropped the `CoInitializeEx` result. A thread already in an STA gets `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE`, which is fine for UIA. Any real failure was hidden, and the walk then reported it as a `CoCreateInstance` failure.

## What changed
- New `ensure_com()` in `uia/mod.rs` treats `S_OK`, `S_FALSE` and `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE` as usable and returns `COM init failed: …` for any other HRESULT. It never calls `CoUninitialize`, same as before, because retained element pointers outlive the walk.
- `walk_tree_unsafe` and `walk_native_tree` call it.
- Tests: a mapping test for the HRESULT cases, and a Windows runtime test that puts a fresh thread in an STA, checks the MTA init returns `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE`, then creates `CUIAutomation`.

## Scope
Only the two walk entry points in `uia/mod.rs`. The other ignored `CoInitializeEx` results (`uia/scroll.rs`, `tools/page.rs`) are left for a follow-up.

## Blast Radius
Windows UIA tree walks. Success cases behave as before. Only a real COM init failure changes, and it now gets its own error message.

## Tradeoffs
The tests call `ensure_com` directly, not through a walk. Testing at the walk level would need an HRESULT-injection seam used only by tests, and each call site is a single line.

## Verification
The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` for `platform-windows` against `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (C deps stubbed). Clippy reports the same warning locations as on base. The Windows tests run in the CI Windows lane, not locally.

title: fix(cua-driver): resolve cursor-theme helper through symlinks
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `cua-driver cursor-theme` can fail after a normal installation because `current_exe()` retains the `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` symlink. The helper lookup then searches beside the symlink instead of inside the app bundle.

Resolve the executable path before locating its sibling `cua-cursor-theme`, retaining the existing fallback if resolution fails. Add a hermetic CLI regression covering direct launch, absolute and relative symlinks, paths containing spaces, argument forwarding, helper exit status, and the missing-helper diagnostic.

## Related work

Refs #6728. This addresses the remaining helper-lookup problem; the release-managed baked-version issue was fixed separately upstream. No installer or release-version changes are included.

## Compatibility and risk

The CLI interface and helper arguments are unchanged. The helper is located beside the resolved driver executable. Tests use a temporary installation and the testkit's isolated home, with telemetry disabled; they do not access the desktop or modify an installed application.

Windows execution has not been validated locally. The filesystem change uses the standard cross-platform API; the symlink regression is Unix-only.

## Validation

Rust 1.97.1:

- The new CLI test failed on macOS before the fix with the reported missing-helper error, and passed after the fix.
- `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test cursor_theme_cli_test`: passed on macOS and Linux arm64.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on Linux arm64.
- Formatting and contribution diff checks passed.
- Full native `bin/ci --base upstream/main --keep-target --no-install` was run. It is not green: macOS Clippy reports the existing `needless_return` in `selftest.rs:560` (already tracked by #6813), and the full test run fails `updater::tests::ownership_requires_successful_query_with_literal_path`. Both failures were also observed before the production fix. The cursor-theme regression passes with the fix.

This remains draft pending those baseline check failures and maintainer CI. No green `local-ci` sign-off is claimed.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This is an existing CLI bug fix and does not require an RFC.
- [x] Tests and native macOS/Linux evidence are included; the Windows gap is recorded.
- [x] The title describes the production change with the `cua-driver` release scope.
- [x] No external contribution is included.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`).

title: RFC: a Cua-owned QEMU + WHPX runtime on Windows (spike findings)
body:
Feasibility spike requested because the WSL service on the dev PC wedged twice. Measured on Windows 11 with QEMU 11.1.0 and `-accel whpx` (q35, cua's pinned 6.1.155 kernel, Ubuntu 24.04 base rootfs): acceleration is on (guest sees Hyper-V; a compute loop is 21x faster than TCG), 0.82 s to init, agent channel ready in 1.6 s, virtio-blk/net/serial and hostfwd work, idle overhead about 150 MB and about 1% of a core. `-M microvm` hangs under WHPX in this QEMU; no 9p/virtiofs on Windows. Design, UAC flow (`WHvGetCapability` detection without elevation, elevated dism for HypervisorPlatform), risks and a staged plan are in the RFC. Nothing is implemented; needs approval before any backend work.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux XTest typing keeps the text's case while Caps Lock is on
body:
## Problem

On Linux X11, `type_text` through XTest (desktop scope, foreground delivery, the `set_value` key fallback) types the text with its case inverted while Caps Lock is on: "Hello" comes out as "hELLO". XTest key events go through the core keyboard's live state, and `send_type_text_xtest` chose Shift per character as if no lock were set.

## Fix

When the core keyboard has Lock set, the typing route taps the Lock-modifier key off before the text and on again after it, on the same XTest queue, so the order is kept. This is what xdotool does for active modifiers.

Inverting Shift for letter keys is not enough: a character the keymap lacks is typed on a spare keycode bound to it at every level, and the Caps Lock transformation in Xlib and xkbcommon upper-cases that keysym whatever Shift does (measured with XLookupString on Xvfb: a spare keycode bound to `eacute` gives `Eacute` with and without Shift under Lock).

## Test

`caps_lock_tests::xtest_typing_keeps_case_under_caps_lock` (Xvfb): Caps Lock on, type "Hello é" into a focused window, decode the KeyPress events. Without the fix it decodes "hELLO" and every key carries Lock; with it the text is "Hello", no key carries Lock, and Lock is on again afterwards.

Also checked on an XFCE/X11 desktop: Caps Lock on, desktop `type_text` "Hello World é" into Mousepad saves "Hello World é" (before: "hELLO wORLD É").

title: perf(spaces): connect Space desktop streams in under a second
body:
## What

Opening or switching a Space's Desktop in Cua Spaces took 10 s or more on "Connecting…" (about 30 s on the owner's Macs). It now connects in about 0.1 s, and a Space already open again is on screen in a few milliseconds.

## Root cause

The viewer joins presence before it opens the stream, so the Space attributes its input to its own cursor. `Space::join_presence` then waited for the QUIC datagram channel for the whole join timeout (10 s). A local Space's UDP port has no route from the daemon (a container behind a port forward), so the channel never opened and every open paid the timeout. The per-hop timing below shows it: `presence=10025 ms`, then `opened` 54 ms later.

Not the cause: the daemon hop, the OpenMedia ticket and the media socket (13 to 20 ms each on loopback), the encoder or the first keyframe (3 ms after the socket).

## Changes

- `cua-spaces`: `Space::join_presence` returns as soon as the Join stream answers and opens the datagram channel behind it. Cursors ride the stream until the channel is up, then move to it. `join_presence_with(.., true)` still waits (the live presence tests need that).
- `LiveStreamSession` (Swift): the open waits at most 500 ms for presence and goes on without it, so a slow daemon or Space can never hold the picture back for a whole timeout again.
- Cua Spaces (macOS) intent: the page tells the host (`{ type: "prewarm", spaceId }`) when the pointer rests on a link to a Space for 120 ms or presses one, unless the person turned off connecting by itself. The host opens that Space's viewer stream then, counts it as a warm stream (`maxWarm`) and lets it go after 15 s if no slot takes it. A prewarm that failed is not a verdict on the slot: it opens again.
- Cua Spaces (macOS) poster: while a slot connects, the Space's last picture draws in its place, dimmed (the page's "Connecting…" shows through) and taking no input. Kept per Space, at most 8, 30 minutes.
- Timing: every open writes a `stream.open` span, times only, never frame content. Host: unified log, subsystem `ai.cua.spaces`, category `stream.timing` (`slot`, `resolved`, `begun`, `presence`, `opened`, `decoded`, `painted`, and `first_frame_ms` per slot). Daemon and client, at debug level in the daemon log with `CUA_LOG=info,cua::stream::timing=debug`: `connect_space`, `ticket`, `attached`, `connection_established`, `session_opened`, `first_frame`, `first_keyframe`. The page marks `stream.open:<space>` in `performance`.
- Regression guard: `e2e_docker_stream_timing` (opt-in, runs against a real container) now fails when a cold open takes over 2 s or the warm p95 over 1 s (`CUA_STREAM_COLD_BUDGET_MS`, `CUA_STREAM_WARM_BUDGET_MS` loosen it for a slow runner). New unit tests below.

Composes with the other stream work in flight: no change to direct attach or to the Space page layout, and the page-side change to `stream-surface.ts` is one added message type.

## Measurements

Mac Studio (cua.local), isolated `CUA_HOME`, a copy of the app, two Linux (`linux:24.04-slim`, container) Spaces, driven through the real GUI with cua-driver. Time from the slot attaching (the click) to the first painted frame, from the host's own `stream.slot` log line. Before is this branch's instrumentation without the fix.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open the Desktop, cold (first open after launch) | 10 091 ms, 10 081 ms (n=2) | min 70, p50 86, p95 131, max 131 ms (n=13) |
| Open again within the 45 s grace (warm) | 1 ms (n=2) | p50 1, p95 5, max 7 ms (n=20) |
| Switch to another Space (cold) | 10 081 ms | 82 ms (and 70 to 131 across the n=13) |
| Switch back to the first Space (warm) | 1 ms | 0 to 7 ms (n=20, alternating two Spaces) |
| Hover the tile, then click | not available | 2 ms (stream opened 77 ms after the hover) |
| Low-rate tile streams (Spaces grid) | 34 to 175 ms | unchanged |

Per hop after the fix (ms from the click, cold): resolved 1, begun 2, presence 12 to 37, opened 63 to 122, decoded +6 to +16, painted at once. Before: presence 10 025, opened 10 079.

Not measured, and why: a macOS Space desktop (no macOS VM of my own on the test machine: a 23 GB image, and the only one running is another agent's), a window stream (this host draws Desktop slots only; cross-Space window streams are the other agent's work), reopening after the app lost focus or a page fold (the same warm-session path; covered by the existing and new unit tests, not driven by hand), and the owner's Mac (the 30 s there is the same wait, repeated). The fix is in the shared presence layer, so it applies to every runtime.

Before and after frames: before, "Connecting… Still connecting. This is taking longer than usual." 5 s after the click; after, the live desktop 1 s after the click.

## Tests

- `cua-spaces` `presence_datagram_background`: the join returns in under 300 ms while the channel takes 600 ms to open, then the uplink attaches and its events arrive. Mutation-checked: with the wait restored it fails ("the join waited 603 ms for the datagram channel"). `presence_v5` still passes.
- Swift `StreamLifecycleTests.aSlowPresenceJoinNeverHoldsTheStreamBack`: a presence join that takes 60 s does not hold the open. 
- Swift `WebUIVideoSurfacesTests`: the prewarm message; a prewarmed stream is live at once when its slot comes (no second open); unclaimed streams are let go; the warm limit and a hidden window; a failed prewarm opens again for its slot; the poster shows while connecting, takes no input and is bounded and expiring. 41 tests pass.
- Web `stream-intent.test.ts` (8 tests): which links count, the hover delay, a press, the repeat window, the autoconnect setting, no native video.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix --jobs 1` is clean. Web tests for `src/lib`, `src/components/video` and `src/components/space-detail` pass (363), and the web typecheck is clean.

title: feat(spaces): show a child Space's window in the parent's Stream section and stream it directly from the child
body:
## What

An agent that makes a child Space and opens an app there can now show that window in its own Space's Stream section, and the person watching streams it straight from the child.

- `stream_space_window(space=<child>, into=<your Space>)` registers the window with the daemon. `into` defaults to the Space that made the child; `into=desktop` keeps the old "open on the operator's desktop" behaviour.
- The parent's window list (`list_space_windows`, SDK `Space.windows()`, the Stream section) is its own windows plus the shown ones, as rows with an additive `origin` (Space id, name, OS, window). Own windows carry no `origin`, so old clients are unaffected. The row shows the app or title, the origin's OS mark and the origin's name.
- Opening a shown window (`stream_endpoint`, SDK `Space.open_stream` / `stream_session`) decides the route once: the viewer owns the origin or holds a grant, so the ticket is the origin's own, scoped to that Space and window (`direct`); otherwise the runtime that holds the origin mints it and the client attaches through the bridge (`proxied`).
- An in-Space agent reaches this through its scoped channel: `stream_space_window` is now one of the tools it may call on its children, and the daemon pins `into` to the calling Space.
- Entries end when the window closes, when the origin stops, is suspended or deleted, and when the parent is deleted.
- New proto (additive, `buf lint` and `buf breaking` clean): `SpaceService.ListStreamWindows` and `OpenStreamEntry`.

## Design note

Registry. A shown window is an entry `{parent, origin, window, app, title, os}` kept by the `Spaces` runtime the daemon hosts, because the app reads windows through the SDK over gRPC and an entry has to outlive any one client. The parent's window list merges its entries in as rows whose handle is `xs:<entry>`, so every shell that already lists, labels, opens and picture-in-pictures windows keeps one code path, and the first non-desktop stream of a home Space still auto-opens like any other row. Listing prunes entries whose window or origin is gone, and stop, suspend, remove and delete drop them at once.

Direct attach. The route is decided at open time by `decide(access)`, where access is what the viewer's own account holds on the origin (owner, grant, none). A direct open never goes through the parent: the SDK connects the viewer's own handle to the origin and mints the ticket there, so there is no relay hop and no second encode, and the attach uses the origin's credentials. Presence stays as if the stream came through the parent: `MergedRoster` and `FanoutSender` (cua-spaces `presence`) join the origin's and the parent's channels, publish the cursor to both and fold the two rosters into one avatar and one cursor per viewer (by principal id); input goes to the origin window through its normal stream session. A viewer with no access is proxied.

## Also in this PR (second round)

- The branch merges `main`, #6793, #6799, #6797, #6818 (`perf/spaces-stream-fast`) and #6775 as normal merge commits; the only conflict was two test modules in `children/api.rs`, both kept. Bindings were regenerated, not hand-edited. One lint error from the stream-fast branch (`needless_update` in `presence_datagram_background.rs`) is fixed.
- Presence: `DualPresence` (cua-spaces) joins the origin's and the parent's channel for a direct attach, publishes the cursor to both and reads them as one: one avatar and one cursor per viewer, the viewer's second identity never shows, heartbeats list everyone. The SDK exposes it as `Space.join_presence_for(window_id, ...)`, and the SwiftUI `LiveStreamSession` now joins with its source, so a direct attach gets the merged presence. Input still goes to the origin window through the normal stream session; the agent cursor overlay is drawn in the guest and is untouched.
- Proxied route: for a viewer with no handle on the origin the SDK asks the daemon's media bridge (`OpenMediaBridge`) for the origin's window and attaches to the daemon with the parent's credentials. The daemon no longer mints a ticket for a plain `OpenStreamEntry`.
- `close_stream` now goes to the Space that minted the session (the origin) and leaves both presence channels with `SpacePresence.leave`.
- The docs generator gets a `spaces/presence` page so the Space reference stays under its size cap.

## Not done yet (stated plainly)

- The live scenario has not been run: Linux home Space, macOS child, Safari, `stream_space_window`, the Stream row, auto-open, direct versus proxied in daemon logs and byte counters, two viewers on a real stream, first-frame time warm and cold, tool-call counts and wall time. It needs a Local build that contains this branch (merged now) and the macOS child fix.
- The real-Claude run on the owner's Mac (narration versus raw events) has not been run.
- The proxied route and the Swift presence wiring are covered by unit and mock tests and by CI compilation, not by a run against a real daemon.
- Grant behaviour is covered by the decision function; no relay account was available for a real grant.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cua-spaces --lib stream_registry` and `--lib merged_tests`
- `cargo test -p cua-spaces --test stream_registry` (two spacesd mocks: tool results, direct ticket scoped to the origin, cleanup on window close, origin removal, parent removal, default `into`)
- `cargo test -p cua-daemon --lib stream_scope_tests`
- `cargo test -p cua-spaces-app-core --lib stream`
- `bin/ci --quick --fix --jobs 1`

Base: `main`. The live macOS-child scenario also needs #6793.

title: fix(cua-driver): give KWin windows exact bounds, stacking, capture and bring_to_front
body:
Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6450 by @astrovm, which carries @ShellWen's commits from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4378. Their commits are kept unchanged under their own names. Fixes #4377. Linear: CUA-3715.

## Why

#6450 gives KWin Wayland windows exact bounds, stacking, capture and `bring_to_front`. Before this rework, the Nix package granted that at install time, and on KWin 6.8 and newer it was on for everyone, because KWin dropped its own checks there. Now the person running the driver decides at runtime. The adapter is off by default on every KWin release, and with it off the driver takes main's code paths.

## What changed

- **Operator switch, read on every call.** `cua-driver kwin-capture on|off|status` saves `~/.cua-driver/kwin-window-capture`. No tool writes that file, so a model can't turn the adapter on, and a change needs no restart of the driver or KWin. On KWin 6.7 and older, `on` writes the per-user desktop entry KWin checks and rebuilds KSycoca, and `off` removes it. For a release install the entry names `packages/current/cua-driver`, which KWin resolves when it checks, so an update keeps the grant. `on` then lists windows every 100 ms, for up to about 5 s, until KWin grants a fresh connection, so it applies from the next call. If KWin hasn't granted it by then, `on` prints the status line and exits 0. The Nix `postInstall` entry is gone. A screenshot Deny saved in the desktop portal keeps the adapter off unless the operator runs `on --override-portal-deny`. A permission store that doesn't answer counts as a Deny.
- **One predicate, nothing new for the model.** Listing, capture and activation all ask whether the adapter is on. A failed exact capture now returns the soft `surface_identity_unproven` with the tree, as on other compositors, where before it was a hard `get_window_state` error. Raw input at a KWin handle gets the generic Wayland `foreground_unavailable` text. LINUX.md, which the model reads, names capabilities and refusal codes only. Setup moved to `docs/kwin-window-capture.md`.
- **Element-click fallback scoped to KWin.** The earlier hunk rerouted the AT-SPI element-click pointer fallback on every native Wayland session. That code is back to main. Only a KWin handle is refused: `background_unavailable` in background, `foreground_unavailable` in foreground.

The activation fix from the previous head (`request_active`, confirmed only by state after a `wl_display.sync`) is unchanged.

## Scope

This covers the KWin adapter's gate, its CLI, its docs, and the generated CLI reference. Other compositors are unchanged from main. It leaves out a per-session grant in the capability manifest, and the installer, which only needs to mention `kwin-capture on`. It doesn't touch #6451, #6444, #6447 or #6448.

## Tradeoffs

- A setup-time-only grant and a Nix package arg were dropped. A store path fixed at build time can't be switched at runtime, and on KWin 6.8+ it switches nothing.
- Ask-on-first-use was dropped. It would have the driver raise a consent prompt from inside a tool call, which the driver doesn't do for any other permission.
- The portal answer is reused for up to a second, so one tool call's several checks make one D-Bus lookup. `off` is read from the setting file first, so it never waits on that answer.
- `on` waits on the real grant instead of a fixed sleep, and `list_windows` has no retry of its own. The wait runs only in the CLI command, only for `on`, and only when the session may be KWin.
- The installer grants nothing. It only mentions `kwin-capture on` (https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6836). Keystate stays behind this switch: the `on` entry lists `org_kde_kwin_keystate`.

## Blast Radius

KDE Plasma Wayland users only, and only after an operator turns the adapter on. Everyone else, and KWin with it off, takes main's routes. The new CLI command is inert on macOS and Windows.

## Verification

- **Live, nested KWin 6.3.6 Wayland session** (virtual output, private D-Bus, AT-SPI and XDG dirs), against a running daemon with two same-title GTK windows. The scenario passed 17 of 17 checks on each of three runs at this head. The new check holds that `on` has applied by the time it returns: the first `list_windows` after it already lists KWin ids. The previous head, run the same way, needed three calls. Off by default, the windows list under non-KWin ids. After `kwin-capture on`, with no restart, both get KWin ids and stacking. A failed exact capture is the soft refusal with the tree. Key input and the element-click fallback (both modes) refuse with the generic codes and don't raise the window. `bring_to_front` raises the covered window. A saved portal Deny turns it off on the next calls, and an old KWin id is refused like any unknown id. `status` reports the Deny, and `--override-portal-deny` turns it back on. `off` removes the entry and restores main's refusals.
- **Live, update keeps the grant.** In the same session, a release-layout install ran `kwin-capture on`. Then `packages/current` was swapped to a new release directory and the old one was deleted. With no second `on`, a fresh daemon still got KWin ids, and `status` still reported the entry as current. That passed 4 of 4 checks on each of two runs. The previous head failed 3 of them, because it named the versioned release path.
- **The scoped repository checks:** `cargo fmt --all --check`. For Linux aarch64, `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux -p cua-driver --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `platform-linux`'s lib tests passed 972 on Debian 13. On macOS, `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver` passed, including the 0.12.6 compatibility contract, which failed at the previous head because `kwin-capture` sat inside the pinned help line. `cargo clippy -p cua-driver -p platform-macos --all-targets -D warnings` is clean after the main merge. The cua-driver reference generator `--check` and its node tests (25) pass.
- **Not run:** the manual `kwin_native_capture_test` needs `org.kde.KWin.ScreenShot2`, which KWin loads only with OpenGL compositing, and the VM has no GPU, so exact-capture pixels and the scale and resize checks did not run. Also not run: KWin 6.8+, the verify-cua-driver X11/Wayland lanes, the Linux `cua-driver` test binary, and Windows.

Size: over the production-line target because this carries all of #6450's KWin adapter. The rework adds the setting, gate and CLI (about 330 lines, a third of them CLI catalog entries) and removes the Nix entry and the all-compositor click hunk.

title: fix(cua-driver): use KWin's logical desktop frame for capture and input
body:
Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6448 by @astrovm. Their 7 commits are kept unchanged under their own authorship, plus a merge of main and one fix commit. Refs #3061. Linear: CUA-3716.

## Why

#6448 makes KWin desktop capture and libei input share KWin's logical layout, read from `xdg-output`, so a pixel read off a scaled or offset KWin screenshot is clicked where it was read. Review found one fail-open path. If the Wayland connection or the first registry roundtrip failed, `kwin_layout::query` returned `Ok(None)`, the same answer as "this compositor is not KWin". Input and capture sizing then fell back to the unconverted physical frame, so on a scaled or offset KWin layout a click could land away from its screenshot point.

## What changed

- The contributor's change, unchanged: the KWin layout read (`wayland/kwin_layout.rs`), the desktop frame in `get_screen_size`, `get_desktop_state` and `get_cursor_position`, desktop input converted through it, and the ignored `kwin_logical_frame_test` owner test. Their PR description has the full behavior and the KWin 6.3, 6.6 and 6.8 runs.
- `kwin_layout::query` now returns an error when the compositor cannot be reached or does not answer the registry roundtrip. `Ok(None)` now means only that the compositor answered and announced no `kde_output_*` global.
- A new scripted-compositor unit test hangs up before the first sync and expects that error.

## Scope

Covers KWin layout discovery on opted-in Wayland sessions. It does not touch GNOME, Hyprland or niri routing, or the KWin window geometry and capture work in #6450 and #6451.

## Blast Radius

On an opted-in Wayland session that is not Hyprland or niri, a `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` whose socket is unreachable now makes desktop input, `get_screen_size` and `get_desktop_state` return an error where they used to fall back to the physical frame. That session had no working Wayland capture or input either, so an explicit error replaces a silent miss. Sway, GNOME and other compositors that answer the registry are unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks for `platform-linux`, run on a Linux aarch64 host: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --features portal-input` passed 953 and `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux` passed 936.
- The new test fails with the old `Ok(None)` restored and passes with the fix. All 17 `kwin_layout` tests pass.
- Not run: the KWin owner E2E test (no KWin desktop available), the verify-cua-driver Linux X11 and Wayland lanes, and Windows and macOS platform checks (this diff touches neither). With `--features portal-input`, clippy reports 6 findings in `libei.rs` and `mod.rs`, all on lines from main.

Size: production lines are over the add<=200 limit because this PR carries the whole contributor feature. The fix commit is 6 production lines.

title: fix(cua-driver): find a pid's window on Wayland and name NO_AT_BRIDGE when it hides one
body:
## Why

Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6444 by @astrovm (CLA signed), Linear CUA-3719. Their four commits are kept as they wrote them. Two follow-up commits fix gaps in pid-only window reads. The contributor's description of the NO_AT_BRIDGE note, its measured KWin results and its e2e tests is on https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6444.

The PR moved `get_window_state({pid})` onto the input tools' pid fallback, which brought two gaps with it. On Hyprland every window is listed without a stacking position, so that fallback picked a multi-window app's window in list order. On every Wayland session the fallback skips off-screen windows, so a pid whose one window was on another workspace showed up in `list_windows` but answered `No windows found` to a read.

## What changed

- From @astrovm: `get_window_state({pid})` uses the shared pid fallback, so it works on native Wayland. It also names `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1` where that variable can hide a window.
- Hyprland: the fallback now picks the pid's visible window with the most recent `focusHistoryID`, and never picks a window missing from focus history. Other Wayland sessions pick the only on-screen window or the highest stacking position. If neither applies, they pick nothing instead of the first window in the list.
- A pid-only read the fallback can't place now uses the pid's listed windows. It reads the only one, even off-screen. With several it refuses with `ambiguous_window_target` and lists the candidates. With none, `No windows found` stays.

## Scope

Linux driver only: `get_window_state`, the Linux pid fallback and Hyprland window listing. X11 and niri selection are unchanged. The overlap with https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6450 and https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6820 in `pid_only_window` is left for after this lands. The e2e file overlap with https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6443 is untouched.

## Blast Radius

Keyboard tools (`type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey`) share the fallback, but the guard asks it only when a pid has several eligible windows. On Hyprland they now follow focus history instead of list order. On a Wayland session that has no stacking data and several on-screen windows, they now refuse with the candidate list instead of guessing.

## Verification

- Unit tests cover Hyprland focus history, a missing `focusHistoryID`, Wayland stacking selection and the off-screen single-window read.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, macOS `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` and clippy, Linux-target clippy for `platform-linux`, `cua-driver-core` and `cua-driver-e2e` with all targets (type-check only), and the SPDX header check all passed.
- Not run: Linux unit tests and the Linux X11 and Wayland desktop lanes, because they couldn't run on the build host. CI runs the Linux unit tests.

Size: over the net production budget, because this carries the contributor's NO_AT_BRIDGE work and both read fixes in one PR.

title: [Bug]: Windows: several "background" paths hand foreground or real input to the target app (right_click, invoke_menu, click expand)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, with the default `delivery_mode` (background), a few actions still move foreground or send real (global) input to the target application. `right_click` routed through `global_input` with delivery `unknown`, and `invoke_menu` plus `click` action `expand` on classic Win32 menus made the target app take foreground repeatedly. The `delivery_mode` description says background "never swaps foreground", so a caller that only allows background has no way to know these calls are unsafe until they have happened.

## Reproduction

Classic Win32 Notepad (`notepad.exe` on Windows 10), another window in front. The JSON-RPC calls below are minimal and written from the tool schemas. The observations in this report come from longer agent-driven runs, not from this exact script.

1. `launch_app {"path":"C:/Windows/System32/notepad.exe"}` -> note `pid`; `list_windows {"pid":<pid>}` -> note `window_id`.
2. `get_window_state {"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<window_id>}` -> note a point in the edit area.
3. `right_click {"pid":<pid>,"x":<x>,"y":<y>}` with no `delivery_mode` (default background).
4. `invoke_menu {"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<window_id>,"path":["Edit","Select All"]}`.
5. In `get_window_state`, find the Edit menu item and call `click` with `"action":"expand"` on its `element_token`.
6. Watch foreground (for example `SetWinEventHook(EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND)`) and the screen while running steps 3 to 5.

## Expected behavior

With `delivery_mode` omitted (background), none of these calls change the foreground window or send real input. If a target cannot be driven in the background, the call returns `background_unavailable`, as the `delivery_mode` description promises.

## Actual behavior

1. `right_click` (background): result `delivery: "unknown"`, route `global_input`, and a context menu appeared on the user's screen. The tool description says right-click is posted as WM_RBUTTONDOWN/UP with PostMessage, so a `global_input` route is unexpected.
2. `invoke_menu` and `click` with action `expand` on the Notepad Edit menu: Notepad took foreground. In one run, the `invoke_menu` loop produced 6 foreground changes about 0.5 s apart (t = 162.5 s to 166 s), plus one at the earlier `expand` click (click at t = 101.3 s, foreground seen at 107.6 s) and one more at 284.5 s. The `invoke_menu` description says it uses accessibility APIs and never falls back to pixels, and nothing in the result says foreground was involved.
3. `type_text` with no `x`/`y` or `element_token` on a covered window fails, and the error text points the caller to `delivery_mode=foreground`. For an automated caller that reads as the next thing to try, which is the escalation the `delivery_mode` description tells callers not to make.
4. `run_script`: the `app.click` and `app.typeText` helpers do not pass `delivery_mode`. A policy that requires `delivery_mode: background` therefore refuses them, even though background is the default. (The policy side is in the companion request.)

## Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.38.0 (a newer version, 0.41.2, was reported as available; not retested)
Operating system and architecture: Windows 10 Pro 19045, x64
Application/browser/window system/image: classic Notepad and Paint (notepad.exe / mspaint.exe, not the packaged apps)

## Evidence

- Foreground changes were recorded with a `SetWinEventHook(EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND)` listener, and in earlier runs with 50 ms polling. Polling alone misses short flips, so sub-50 ms activations are not excluded in the polling-only runs.
- The `global_input` route and `delivery: "unknown"` for `right_click` are quoted from the tool result. I do not have a redacted log to attach; I can re-run with verbose logging and attach one on request.
- A control: the same actions run with cua-driver itself started on a separate Windows desktop (see the companion feature request) produced no foreground change and no injected input on the user's desktop.

## Workaround and additional context

- A deny rule for `invoke_menu`, `right_click`, and `click` with `action: expand` in the caller's policy avoids all three, at the cost of losing those actions.
- Related but different: #3908 (Windows hotkey on XAML targets), #6538 and #5959 (Windows browser_prepare). #4615 and #5355 show similar symptoms on macOS.
- I did not find an existing issue about these specific Windows paths (searched: right_click, invoke_menu, global_input, background focus, delivery_mode).

## Submission checks
- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem (the background-mode guarantee not holding on Windows). Policy, browser, and isolated-desktop requests are in a separate companion issue.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details.

title: [Feature]: Windows: policy cannot enforce defaults or constrain launch_app; browser_* cannot bind headless browsers; request an official isolated-desktop mode
body:
## Problem

Callers that need a hard "never touch the user's desktop" guarantee on Windows cannot get it from the current policy and browser tooling. Three gaps, plus one measured approach that works.

1. Policy argument constraints only pass when the argument is present. A rule such as `delivery_mode: [background]` cannot enforce the default, so a call that omits the argument (including the `run_script` helpers `app.click` and `app.typeText`, which never send `delivery_mode`) is refused instead of being treated as background. There is also no way to constrain `launch_app` arguments (`aumid`, `additional_arguments`, `path`), so a policy can only allow or deny `launch_app` as a whole.
2. `browser_prepare` and `get_browser_state` need a `window_id` from cua's own window list. A headless Chromium/Edge (`--headless=new`) has CDP up and no windows, so every `window_id` is refused with `browser_binding_stale` ("not owned by pid"). Headless is the one browser mode that cannot touch the user's desktop, and it is the one these tools cannot drive.
3. `type_text` without `x`/`y` on a covered window errors and suggests `delivery_mode=foreground` (see the companion bug).

## What works well (measured)

Running cua-driver itself on a separate desktop created with `CreateDesktopW`, with child processes started using `STARTUPINFO.lpDesktop` set to that desktop (never `SwitchDesktop`):

- Notepad, Paint and Edge run and paint there; cua `list_windows` sees only that desktop's windows (2 windows in the test).
- On the user's desktop, 3 runs recorded 0 foreground changes and 0 injected keyboard or mouse events (low-level hooks plus `SetWinEventHook`). One leftover: a 16x16 off-screen UIA helper window becomes visible for 15 to 35 ms on `get_window_state` of Notepad; it also appears on the default desktop, so it is not caused by the isolation.
- `get_window_state` works: Notepad 1.2 s, Paint 0.5 s, with real pixels (PrintWindow) and the UIA tree. `type_text`, `press_key`, background `click` (275 pixels changed on the Paint canvas) and `right_click` (the menu appears only on the hidden desktop) work.
- `browser_prepare` + `get_browser_state` bind exactly when cua-driver runs on the same desktop as Edge; `browser_navigate` and a trusted background `browser_click` worked, with a SetWinEventHook monitor over 32.5 s showing 0 foreground changes and 0 visible agent-browser windows. The same Edge is refused (`not owned by pid`) by a cua-driver on the user's desktop.
- Fails safely: `SendInput` returns 0 (error 5) from the other desktop, so `hotkey` (ctrl+a), `press_key` with modifiers, `invoke_menu` ("target window could not be activated"), `bring_to_front` and `delivery_mode=foreground` do nothing instead of leaking input.
- Not available there: `BitBlt` of the desktop DC (black; `get_desktop_state` fails with "BitBlt failed: handle is invalid") and Windows.Graphics.Capture. cua falls back to PrintWindow, which works for GDI apps. Black captures for GPU/DirectComposition apps were not tested.

I ran this with a small wrapper that creates the desktop and starts `cua-driver mcp` on it. It is not an official mode, so lifecycle (orphaned hidden apps, modal dialogs the user cannot see, the clipboard being shared per window station) is left to the caller.

## Proposed behavior

- An official opt-in isolated-desktop mode on Windows: the driver creates a named desktop, runs the runtime and launched apps there, never switches to it, and fails closed instead of falling back to the user's desktop. Related: RFC #3400 (closed) proposed a child-session workspace and listed `CreateDesktop` as an alternative; the measurements above are an input to that comparison. Plain `.exe` launches are the tested case; packaged/Store apps and `aumid` launches were not tested.
- Policy: let constraints apply to defaults (for example, an absent argument is treated as its default), or add an "allowed values if present, otherwise default" form, and allow constraining `launch_app` arguments.
- `run_script` helpers should pass the effective `delivery_mode` so policies can evaluate them.
- Let `browser_prepare` bind a CDP browser by pid or endpoint when it has no cua-visible window, at least for a driver-owned or loopback-owned headless browser.
- Make the `type_text` error point to `get_window_state` + `element_token` first and not suggest `delivery_mode=foreground`.

## Alternatives considered

Denying `launch_app`, `invoke_menu`, `hotkey` and `bring_to_front` in policy avoids the leaks but removes the tools. A focus-restoring guard (restore the previous foreground after any change) worked in tests but needed 170 to 450 ms per restore, which is a visible flash.

## Environment

cua-driver 0.38.0, Windows 10 Pro 19045 x64, classic Notepad/Paint, Edge. Newer version 0.41.2 not retested.

title: ci(release): adopt the untagged Release Please draft instead of publishing a second release
body:
Release Please (draft: true) lists a new release as untagged-<hash> until its tag exists. publish-draft looked up drafts by tag only, found none, and the CD workflow created a second release for the tag. The original draft stayed behind: 28 piled up by 7 Nov (12 deleted by hand; all duplicates of published releases, no assets).

Fix: when no release has the tag, publish-draft adopts the single draft titled '<component>: v<version>' and sets its tag on publish. Test added.

Touches release workflow scripts, so it needs a human look before merge.

title: fix(cua-driver): type exact text on the active keyboard layout or refuse it
body:
## Why

Desktop `type_text` through libei could report success with the wrong text: it read only the first keymap layout, guessed modifiers and ignored Caps Lock. This lands astrovm's #6447, which types exact text on the active KWin layout or refuses it with nothing typed, plus fixes for three gaps found in review where unknown state was treated as safe.

Salvaged from #6447

CUA-3717, CUA-3788

## What changed

- astrovm's commits from #6447, unchanged, with authorship kept. Their PR body has the full design and the measured KWin 6.3.6, 6.6.6 and 6.8.2 runs.
- Unknown modifier state is refused, not assumed clear. Without an EIS report, `org_kde_kwin_keystate` is bound at version 5 and read for held and latched modifiers as well as the lock keys. When that global isn't offered, or is older than version 5, key typing is refused. A held modifier that EIS reports also refuses text that would go out partly through `ei_text`, since a held Shift turns Return into Shift+Return.
- A missing or mistyped `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` or `_NET_CLIENT_LIST` now means the X11 focus is unknown, so text takes the key route. Before, it read as "no X11 app", so `ei_text` could reach an X11 app that drops what the layout lacks.
- A compositor with `ei_text` and no keyboard now refuses text when an X11 app may have focus, and refuses line breaks, instead of sending the whole string through `ei_text`.
- The unknown-keyboard-state refusal now names its fix: on KDE Plasma 6.3 to 6.5, `cua-driver kwin-capture on` lets the driver read the keys.
- Merged with main's `delay_ms` pacing (#6892). A paced call budgets for both pacings. Paced Wayland text is checked whole, with its line endings made line feeds, before the first character goes out. An untypable character therefore types nothing, and `\r\n` is a single Return. A failure after some text went out reports how far typing got instead of saying nothing was typed.

## Scope

Linux libei typing (`wayland/libei.rs`, `wayland/kwin_keystate.rs`, `x11/mod.rs`) and its Skills doc. niri, wtype and Hyprland keep the contributor's behavior. Nothing else in the KWin series is included.

## Tradeoffs

The contributor's version typed digits and punctuation when the lock keys were unknown. That is now refused too: with modifier state unknown, a held Shift changes digits as well as letters. On KWin 6.3 to 6.5 without the `X-KDE-Wayland-Interfaces` entry from #6785, and on KWin before 6.3, libei key typing is refused until that entry lands, or until EIS reports the keyboard itself (KWin 6.8, Mutter).

## Blast Radius

Merge after #6820, which adds the `cua-driver kwin-capture on` command the refusal names. Linux desktop `type_text` on libei (KDE and GNOME). Every new path refuses with `foreground_unavailable` and nothing typed. None of them sends different text. #6785 should land with or before this, as the contributor notes. This PR and #6448 each add a `mod` line at the same place in `wayland/mod.rs`.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, lint) passes. `cargo clippy -D warnings --all-targets` for `platform-linux`, with and without `portal-input`, is clean when type-checked against the Linux target.
- New tests cover KWin's keystate answers (held, latched and locked Shift; held Caps Lock), unknown X11 focus properties, a text-only EIS device with X11 focus or a line break, and held or unknown modifiers on the key and `ei_text` routes. Each asserts the exact refusal and that nothing was sent. They were type-checked here but not run: Linux unit tests and Linux desktop E2E could not run on the verification host, so CI's Linux lanes are their first run.
- The contributor's KWin desktop matrix was not rerun on this head.
- After the merge with main, rustfmt and Linux-target clippy (with and without `portal-input`) pass. Two new unit tests cover the paced refusals and were type-checked but not run.

Size: the contributor's change is about 2,300 added lines, most of it the layout-aware key planner and its tests; the review fixes on top add about 120 production lines.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop cutting off non-ASCII text typed into GTK3 and Qt fields
body:
Salvaged from #6443 (CUA-3720). @astrovm's three commits keep their authorship. A merge of main and one fix commit for the review findings sit on top.

## Why

`type_text` and `set_value` by accessibility cut non-ASCII text short in GTK3 and Qt fields, because `EditableText.InsertText` got a character count. GTK reads `length` in bytes and Qt reads UTF-16 units. #6443 reads the toolkit name and sends the unit that toolkit reads. Review found two gaps in how it handled a slow or failed toolkit lookup, and the last commit closes both.

## What changed

- From #6443: `InsertText` gets UTF-16 units for Qt and bytes for every other toolkit. The GTK3 accessibility row now types `ax-ñ🙂-typed`.
- A failed lookup no longer guesses. ASCII has the same length in every unit, so it skips the lookup entirely. Other text for an unknown toolkit gets no `InsertText`, because UTF-16 units would cut GTK short and bytes would over-read in Qt. `type_text` then moves to its next delivery route.
- The lookup gets no budget past the operation's deadline anymore. It runs only while 250 ms of the budget remain for the write. Before, a slow lookup could push the write past the deadline, and the timeout would retry it as synthetic input after the text had already landed.

## Scope

Linux AT-SPI EditableText writes in `platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs`, plus the GTK3 e2e row. A write whose own reply comes back after the backstop can still be retried. Main has the same window, and it is left for a follow-up.

## Tradeoffs

- A toolkit name that isn't Qt still gets bytes. ATK defines `length` in bytes, and Qt is the one known exception, so treating every other name as unknown would take the EditableText route away from toolkits that follow the spec.
- When the toolkit is unknown and the text is not ASCII, `SetTextContents` is not tried either. It replaces the whole field, and `type_text` inserts at the caret.

## Blast Radius

Linux only. ASCII writes now skip the toolkit lookup and send the same length as before. For non-ASCII text, an app whose toolkit name can't be read inside the budget no longer gets an EditableText insert and falls through to the next input route instead of getting truncated text.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks for `platform-linux` and `cua-driver-e2e` ran on a Linux aarch64 host: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux -p cua-driver-e2e --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` passed 925, and 941 with `--features portal-input`.
- New tests cover a failed lookup, a lookup slower than the budget, and a budget that only has the reserve left, all on tokio's paused clock. Putting back the UTF-16 guess fails 2 of them, and dropping the reserve fails 2.
- `harness_gtk3_type_text_ax_foreground` passes on Xvfb with openbox, typing `ax-ñ🙂-typed` into the real GTK3 fixture. With GTK sent UTF-16 units it fails with the text cut short.
- Not run: the background GTK3 row (it needs the Electron sentinel, which wasn't staged), Qt fixtures, the Wayland and KDE lanes, and Windows and macOS platform checks (the diff touches neither).

Size: production adds are under the limit (71 added, 17 removed); no size reason needed.

title: [Bug]: macOS: direct capture consent not honored by daemon after `permissions grant` reports success (direct_capture_consent_required)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On a fresh install, `cua-driver permissions grant` reports "✅ … Accessibility, Screen Recording, and direct capture access. You're set." after the macOS prompt is answered, but `get_desktop_state` still fails with `direct_capture_consent_required` on every daemon started afterwards. Capture only works when the daemon is started with `CUA_DRIVER_ALLOW_CAPTURE_CONSENT_ALERT=1`, and that does not persist across daemon restarts.

### Reproduction

1. Fresh install: `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)" -- --no-modify-path --require-signature` (checksum and Sigstore signature verified).
2. `cua-driver permissions grant`, then answer the macOS prompts. Output ends with "✅ CuaDriver has Accessibility, Screen Recording, and direct capture access. You're set."
3. `cua-driver call get_desktop_state`
4. Run `cua-driver permissions grant` again (with a fresh daemon started via `open -a /Applications/CuaDriver.app --args serve`), then repeat step 3.
5. Stop the daemon, then start it with `open -a /Applications/CuaDriver.app --env CUA_DRIVER_ALLOW_CAPTURE_CONSENT_ALERT=1 --args serve` and repeat step 3.
6. `cua-driver stop`, then start it again without the env var and repeat step 3.

### Expected behavior

After `permissions grant` reports direct capture as granted, `get_desktop_state` captures the screen on any later daemon start, without the env override.

### Actual behavior

- Steps 3 and 4: `Desktop screenshot failed: direct_capture_consent_required: screen capture skipped. macOS has not yet asked whether CuaDriver.app may capture the screen directly …`
- Step 5: capture succeeds (`capture_id` returned, display `primary`, scale factor 2.0).
- Step 6: `direct_capture_consent_required` again.
- `cua-driver permissions status --json` after all of the above:
  ```json
  {
    "accessibility": true,
    "screen_recording": true,
    "screen_recording_capturable": null,
    "direct_capture_status": "not_checked",
    "direct_capture_error": null,
    "direct_capture_verification": {
      "bundle_id": "com.trycua.driver",
      "source": "permissions_grant",
      "verified_at": "2026-11-07T11:42:21Z"
    },
    "source": { "attribution": "driver-daemon", "bundle_id": "com.trycua.driver", "responsible_ppid": 1 }
  }
  ```
- `cua-driver doctor` reports all checks OK. `get_screen_size` works.

I do not know the cause. The `direct_capture_verification` record from `permissions_grant` exists, but the daemon's capture path still behaves as if consent has not been requested.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver 0.41.2 (release `cua-driver-rs-v0.41.2`, git 86b5ea2d4030), installed at `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`

Operating system and architecture: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64

Application/browser/window system/image: none (desktop capture only); daemon started through LaunchServices (`open -a`), terminal not involved in TCC attribution

Possibly related: #2881 (grant claims success but direct capture is unobservable), #2443 (readiness reported before Tahoe consent), #4802 (daemon permissions depend on who starts it).

title: fix(cua-driver): read backup publisher trust when its commit was interrupted
body:
CUA-3727

## Why
Committing publisher trust renames the active file to a backup, then renames the new file into place. A crash between those two renames leaves only the backup. Every trust read then failed with "publisher trust update is interrupted", which broke verified install and update, remove, status, path and perception startup. Only `--allow-unsigned-local` reached the recovery path. The backup is the committed trust that `recover_publisher_trust_locked` restores, so reads now use it.

## What changed
- `load_publisher_trust_at` reads the active file, or the backup if only the backup exists, and validates it the same way. It uses the same no-follow private-file checks.
- `ExtensionStore::load_publisher_trust` drops its duplicate check and calls `load_publisher_trust_at`.
- New test `interrupted_trust_commit_reads_the_backup_everywhere`. The test-only `signed_fixture` now ships a runtime contract so the startup path can load a signed install.

## Scope
Only reads change. Recovery, commit and anti-rollback logic are unchanged. When the active file exists it still wins over any backup. A leftover `.publisher-trust.new.json` is still ignored.

## Blast Radius
This touches every caller of publisher trust in cua-driver extension management. The only state that reads differently is "backup present, active missing", which used to fail.

## Verification
- The new test fails on main at `load_publisher_trust` with "publisher trust update is interrupted". It passes with the fix, and covers `load_publisher_trust`, `info(..).healthy`, `active_path`, `perception_worker_config_in`, `remove` and a verified `install_source`.
- CLI repro on a debug build with an isolated `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME` holding only a valid backup: `cua-driver extension install cua-perception --catalog <catalog>` fails on main with "publisher trust update is interrupted". On this branch the trust read succeeds and the install stops later at catalog verification (`catalog target does not match the current target`).
- The scoped repository checks for cua-driver: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, and the full cua-driver binary test suite.

title: feat(cua-driver): write the KWin desktop entry for the install that owns the CLI
body:
## Why

On KDE Plasma Wayland, KWin grants window management and exact window capture only to an executable named by a desktop entry. #6785 had the release installer write that entry with no prompt. https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6820 makes the grant an operator switch instead (`cua-driver kwin-capture on`), off by default. So the installer now grants nothing. It tells KWin users the command, and the uninstaller cleans up the entry that command writes. CUA-3726. Salvaged from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6785. The contributor's commits stay in history unchanged.

## What changed

- `install.sh` writes no desktop entry. When `kwin_wayland` is on the `PATH` it logs one line: "KWin window capture is off; `cua-driver kwin-capture on` turns it on". The installer-side entry writer and its `X-Cua-Cli` ownership logic are deleted, so `_install-common.sh` matches main.
- `uninstall.sh` removes `$XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/ai.cua.driver.desktop` (default `~/.local/share/applications`) when its `Exec` names this install, through `packages/current` or a release directory. An entry naming another executable stays.
- The scripts README says the same.

## Scope

The install hint and the uninstall cleanup. The grant itself, its stable `packages/current` path and its keystate interface are in #6820. Merge #6820 first: until it lands, the command the hint names doesn't exist.

## Blast Radius

Linux release installs on machines with `kwin_wayland` see one extra log line. The uninstaller touches only an entry that names this install. macOS, Windows and machines without KWin take no new path.

## Verification

- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/` passes (360 passed, 24 skipped). The uninstall tests cover an entry naming `current` or a release directory (removed), another executable or a mere mention of the line (kept), and `XDG_DATA_HOME`. They fail when the uninstall match is broken.
- `test_cua_driver_installer_integrity.py` runs the whole installer. Its KWin test is Linux-only, so it also ran from a copy with the platform skip lifted: 16 passed, 11 skipped (PowerShell). With KWin present, stdout has the hint exactly once and there is no applications directory. Without KWin, there is no hint. The test fails if the line is printed twice.
- Not run: real KWin or Plasma, and native Linux CI. The scoped repository checks ran on macOS.

title: fix(cua-driver): leave time for non-ASCII text after a walk in a big app
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: since PR #6829, background `type_text` without an element refuses non-ASCII text in an app with a big accessibility tree. The tree walk spends the whole 1.5 s budget, so the toolkit lookup has no time left, no safe `InsertText` length is known, and nothing gets typed (`background_unavailable`).
- What changed: a walk that finds the element to write into now stops 500 ms before the operation's deadline. That leaves time for the toolkit lookup and for the write, so the write also answers inside the deadline. A failed or slow lookup still sends nothing, as PR #6829 made it.

**Symptom:** with 6000 labels in the window, `type_text({pid, window_id, text: "ñ🙂ab"})` refuses in Qt and GTK3.
**Target:** every non-ASCII text exact and typed once, with no change on normal apps.
**Measure:** the field's own text after each call, on real KWin 6.6.6, Qt and GTK3 over XWayland, the driver seeing only XWayland, so the route is `type_into_editable`.

| Real KWin 6.6.6, big app, background | main c8c79893d | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Non-ASCII texts, exact | 0/10, all refused | 10/10 |
| ASCII, exact | 4/4 | 4/4 |
| Time for a non-ASCII text | About 4520 ms, refused | About 2520 ms, typed |
| Time for ASCII | About 3020 ms | About 2520 ms |

KWin 6.3.6 and 6.8.2 with this PR: 6/6 non-ASCII on each, also about 2520 ms.

## Related work

Refs #6829

Before PR #6829, the same test got 1/6 on main with wrong text reported as delivered, and 10/10 on PR #6443, which gave the lookup a 250 ms floor past the deadline. This keeps PR #6829's rule against spending time past the deadline.

RFC: not needed, no contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux AT-SPI only. Background non-ASCII typing works again in big apps, and pid-only typing there takes about 500 ms less per walk.
- Risk and rollback: each walk ahead of a write has 500 ms less, so on the 1.5 s routes a field late in a big tree could fall outside a partial walk where it was reached before. That wasn't measured. The target of the walk still has to be found the same way, and a miss falls through to the next route. Revert to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new `a_walk_that_outlasts_the_budget_leaves_the_lookup_and_the_write_their_time`. It fails on `assertion failed: !deadline_passed()` when the helper doesn't move the deadline, and passes with it.
- Manual or platform evidence, on the same KWin 6.6.6 session type:
  - Normal apps, `type_text` by element on native Wayland: 48/48 across 6 widgets.
  - Big app by `element_token`: 6/6 before and after. Big app `set_value` by `element_token`: 6/6 before and after. Those use a cached element, with no walk.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - `insert_text`, `type_into_editable_at` and `set_value` by index use the same helper, but no test run reaches their walks.
  - The call sites are covered by the KWin runs above, not by a test in this repo. The new unit test covers the helper.
  - Upstream CI needs a maintainer's approval.
  - Clippy with `portal-input` reports 6 findings in `libei.rs` and `wayland/mod.rs`, also listed on PR #6821. This PR changes neither file.

## Done when

- [x] Non-ASCII in the big app goes from 0/10 to 10/10, typed once, on e51c8258a.
- [x] Normal apps stay at 48/48 on e51c8258a.
- [x] A failed or too-slow lookup still sends nothing: the existing `editable_insert_length_tests` still pass.
- [x] Full `platform-linux` unit tests: 952 passed, and 969 with `portal-input`. `cargo fmt --all --check` and clippy without `portal-input` are clean.
- [x] The same big-app test on KWin 6.3.6 (6/6) and 6.8.2 (6/6). The 6.3.6 run used the Ubuntu build with its own libraries bundled, because Debian 13's glibc is older.
- [ ] Upstream CI.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. Not applicable: this releases.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). `bin/ci --quick --base upstream/main` passes. A fork's sign-off is `CI: Quick`.

title: ci: finish moving apt installs to the cached retry action

What changes for users: fewer CI jobs that hang on a slow Ubuntu mirror.

- Host-runner steps that mixed apt with other commands now install in their own step with `./.github/actions/apt-install`.

title: fix(cua-driver): retry perception resolve after extension lock contention
body:
## Why

`LivePerceptionClient::current` caches whatever the resolver returns, keyed by the install fingerprint it sampled before resolving. Resolving takes the per-extension lock. If another command holds that lock (an install, or `extension status --self-test` running health hooks), resolve gives up after its 1 s retry and returns unavailable. The holder can then exit without touching anything the fingerprint covers, and the running Driver keeps reporting perception as not installed until it restarts. CUA-3729, unit C of CUA-3681.

## What changed

- `PerceptionClientResolver::resolve` returns `Result<PerceptionClient, ResolutionDeferred>`. `current()` returns unavailable for a deferred result without caching it, so the next request resolves again.
- `InstalledPerceptionResolver` defers when the error chain holds a lock-contended `io::Error`. Missing, corrupt or unverifiable installs still resolve to a cached unavailable client. The Windows ACL lease timeout now keeps its `io::Error` source, so that path is classified the same way.
- New test `live_perception_client_retries_after_lock_contention` holds `store.lock(PERCEPTION_ID)` across one `current()`, drops it, and asserts the next `current()` is available.

## Scope

Covers the live perception resolver in `cua-driver` and its trait in `cua-driver-core`. It leaves out the other CUA-3681 units: staging cleanup and partial-remove recovery.

## Blast Radius

The trait is `pub`, and the only implementor outside tests is the binary's `InstalledPerceptionResolver`. `cua-driver-sdk` passes the trait object through without calling `resolve`. While the lock is busy, every request re-runs verification instead of hitting the cache. That lasts only as long as the holder keeps the lock.

## Verification

- The new test fails on the test-only commit at the post-unlock assertion and passes with the fix.
- The scoped repository checks for `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver` and `cua-driver-sdk` pass: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings` on all targets, the `cua-driver-core` perception tests, and the `cua-driver` extension_manager tests.
- Not run: the Linux X11 desktop lane and Windows builds, which need other hosts.

Size: production add and net are within the limits (about +45/-15).

risk: standard

title: fix(cua-driver): sweep orphaned extension staging and clean it on every refusal
body:
## Why

If an extension install crashes between creating `.staging/<id>-<pid>-<n>` and the placement rename, the staging dir stays in the extension store forever. It can hold up to 8 GiB of expanded payload, and nothing removes it. Four ordinary refusals also skipped cleanup after staging existed: the active-version parse, `validate_source_metadata` (for example a catalog that expired between preview and mutation), the existing-version permission check, and the error when opening the existing version dir. This is CUA-3728, unit B of the CUA-3681 crash-recovery research. Unit A shipped in https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6835.

## What changed

- `install_source` calls the new `sweep_orphaned_staging` right after it opens `.staging`. It removes entries named exactly `<entry.id>-<digits>-<digits>` (the `unique_name` format) whose pid is not this process's, using `remove_cap_subdirectory`. The per-extension lock is held, so no live installer of that id can own them. A failed sweep logs a warning and does not fail the install.
- Every step between creating staging and choosing the existing-version or placement branch now runs in one `prepared` closure. Its error path removes this run's staging dir. The existing-version and fresh-placement branches are unchanged.

## Scope

This covers the `.staging` leak only. It leaves out sticky-unavailable caching in the perception client (CUA-3681 unit C), non-atomic `remove`, and pruning of old version dirs.

## Blast Radius

The change touches only the extension install and update path in `cua-driver`. The sweep only deletes this extension id's own staging names from other pids. It never follows symlinks, and it refuses trees with foreign ownership or permissions, the same checks every existing staging cleanup uses. The registry currently has a single id (`cua-perception`), so one id's sweep can't match another id's staging names.

## Verification

- New tests `install_sweeps_staging_left_by_a_dead_installer` and `every_refusal_after_staging_cleans_it` fail on the tests-only first commit, with the orphan still present and "expired catalog leaked staging". Both pass at head.
- The real CLI (`extension install perception --archive <fixture> --allow-unsigned-local`) was run against a store with a planted `.staging/cua-perception-99999-0`. The main build left the orphan in place, and this branch removed it.
- The scoped repository checks passed for `cua-driver` on macOS: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-driver`. The Linux and Windows builds, including the Windows ACL path, could not run here.
