title: ci: run each package's pinned pnpm through corepack in bin/ci
body:
Agents running `bin/ci --quick --fix` with a machine pnpm 11 rewrote pnpm 9 lockfiles, which failed the `quick` job (broke #6839). Same class of fix as #6769 for Rust.

- A pnpm shim (`scripts/ci/lib/pnpm/pnpm`) goes first on PATH in `bin/ci` and `scripts/ci/check-lockfiles.sh`. It reads the nearest `packageManager` pin and runs exactly that version via corepack (`npx corepack` if corepack is not installed).
- No pin, a non-pnpm pin, or a version that cannot be activated fails fast with a clear message. `bin/ci` also fails up front if any pnpm-lock.yaml package lacks a pin.
- Added pins to the six lockfile packages that lacked one, matching what CI already used (web 11.20.0, the rest 9.0.4). Removed the duplicated versions from the WEB_PACKAGES table.
- Policy test: every package with a pnpm-lock.yaml declares `packageManager`.

For users: nothing changes; this only stops contributor tooling from producing lockfile noise.

title: fix(cua-driver): leave time for non-ASCII text after a walk in a big app
body:
## Why

Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6840 by @astrovm, with their commit kept as authored. In an app with a big accessibility tree, the walk in front of an EditableText write used up the whole budget, so background non-ASCII `type_text` was refused. Their commit stops those walks 500 ms before the deadline. That makes partial walks more common. On a partial walk, `pick_editable` still chose the first editable in web content even when the focused field sat later in the tree. Text could then land silently in the wrong field. The second commit closes that gap.

## What changed

- `walk_before_write` (from #6840) runs the walks in `type_into_editable`, `type_into_editable_at`, `insert_text` and `set_value` under a deadline 500 ms earlier.
- After a partial walk, `pick_editable` only takes a focused editable. If it hasn't reached one, the write is refused and `type_text` moves on to its next route. After a complete walk the order stays as before: the focused field, then a web-content field, then the first editable.
- The selection rule is now `pick_editable_index` over `EditableFlags`, with unit tests for both kinds of walk.

## Scope

Linux AT-SPI only (`platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs`). No contract, CLI or MCP changes. Main's Windows clippy failure is unrelated and is fixed in https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6847.

## Blast Radius

Background typing on Linux by pid alone, with no element. After a partial walk, a web page whose field doesn't report focus now goes to the next route instead of AT-SPI. That route might type the text through keyboard events, or refuse it. Writes by index or by element token don't use `pick_editable`.

## Verification

- On Linux, the scoped repository checks pass: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, and `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` (956 passed, and 973 with `portal-input`). With the old rule put back, 2 of the 4 new `pick_editable_tests` fail.
- On Xvfb with openbox, `harness_gtk3_type_text_ax_foreground` passes and types `ax-ñ🙂-typed` into the real GTK3 fixture. `harness_gtk3_ax_tree` passes too.
- Not run: the GTK3 background rows, because the Electron sentinel couldn't be staged without Node. Also not run: the Qt fixtures, the large-tree KWin repro, the Wayland and KDE lanes, and the Windows and macOS platform checks, none of which this change touches.

CUA-3741

title: cua-driver (macOS): action results omit opened-window identity
body:
On macOS, `WindowChangeDetector` already records `WindowEvent { window_id, pid, title }` for both the action's immediate `new_windows` and the previous action's detached-tail `earlier_new_windows`. The click and press_key results expose those observations only through the human-readable window suffix; their `structuredContent` omits the window identity.

This affects both the AX and pixel click result paths and the confirmed/unverifiable press_key path. A caller that needs to bind or inspect the new window has to poll `list_windows` after the action, and can miss the detached-tail observation until another action happens.

Linux already reports structured `new_windows` entries. macOS should publish the same `{ window_id, pid, title }` shape for the combined immediate and detached-tail observations, without changing the existing observation deadline or result suffix. An AX result carrying such an observation should be `unverifiable`, not `suspected_noop`; the window does not prove which action caused it.

Observed on upstream main d3effec5831ce0e604f5ef9bb488f65d563b8dc0. GOAT's downstream tracking issue is https://github.com/goat-si/goat/issues/2326; its driver change uses the newer downstream `OpenedSurface` contract, while the upstream patch retains the existing Linux-compatible `new_windows` shape.

title: cua-driver (macOS): report opened-window identity in action results
body:
On macOS, `WindowChangeDetector` already knows the identity of windows seen during the immediate observation and the previous action's detached tail, but click and press_key results expose it only in the text suffix. Publish the combined observations as `new_windows: [{ window_id, pid, title }]`, matching the existing Linux result shape, on AX click, pixel click, and confirmed/unverifiable press_key results.

The existing observation deadline and text suffix are unchanged. Empty or unobserved results omit `new_windows`. An AX click carrying a window observation now reports `unverifiable` instead of `suspected_noop`, since the observation does not confirm which action caused it.

Adds a focused mapping test covering immediate and detached-tail identity plus empty, unpolled, and deferred observations.

Fixes #6853.

Validation: not run locally. The patch was prepared against upstream main d3effec5831ce0e604f5ef9bb488f65d563b8dc0 through the GitHub API because the authoring session was restricted to its existing downstream worktree. Requesting upstream CI for compile and test verification.

title: macOS: expose search field identity attributes
body:
macOS structured window elements currently expose a display `label` and `value`, but not the raw title, description, placeholder, or subrole identities. A search field named only by `AXPlaceholderValue` has that placeholder folded into `value`, so a client cannot distinguish it from a message composer whose typed text happens to contain a search hint.

This change preserves raw `AXPlaceholderValue` and `AXSubrole` on `AXNode` and emits trimmed `title`, `description`, `placeholder`, and `subrole` keys in `element_entry`. The existing label and placeholder-value fallback behavior is unchanged, and none of the four identities is derived from `AXValue`.

Regression coverage includes placeholder-only and subrole-only searches, composer identity, search-like values, unnamed fields, send-button role/title/frame, and a result passed through `conforming_tool_result("get_window_state", ...)` to prove the additive keys survive the advertised output schema.

title: [Bug]: Volume replica logs the same .cua-devices warning hundreds to thousands of times a minute
body:
### What happens

On two of our three Macs, the Cua daemon writes the same Cua Volume replica warning many times a second, all day, for the device presence file under `.cua-devices/`. The warnings are about the same few keys over and over, so they look like a retry loop rather than real sync work.

Masked samples from `~/.cua/logs/daemon.log` (device IDs replaced with `<device-id>`):

```text
WARN cua_volume::replica::owner: replica: could not apply a saved change here yet key=.cua-devices/<device-id>.json not found: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

```text
WARN cua_volume::replica::owner: replica: the owner could not take a change yet key=.cua-devices/<device-id>.json not found: not found: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

### How often

Counted over 10 minutes on 2026-11-07, around 16:30 UTC:

| Mac | Replica warnings in 10 minutes | About per minute | Message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mac mini (always on) | 1,809 | 180 | "could not apply a saved change here yet" |
| MacBook | 37,560 | 3,750 | "the owner could not take a change yet" |
| Second Mac mini | 0 | 0 | none |

Every replica warning in each sample has the same shape and points at a `.cua-devices/<device-id>.json` key. We measured the same rates (about 180 and 2,900 a minute) on 2026-11-06, so this is steady rather than a burst.

The log rotates at 4 × 10 MB, so disk use stays bounded. But on the MacBook, 40 MB of log holds only about half an hour, so any other daemon message is pushed out of the log within minutes. That makes real problems hard to see.

### What we tried

- **The relay.** We turned off sharing on all three Macs (`cua host status` shows "sharing: off" on each). The warnings went on at the same rate.

### A possible link

This may be related to #6238 and its fix #6290 ("keep no history for a device's presence record in the local Volume store", merged 2026-11-01). If the replica still expects a saved version of a presence record that is no longer kept, it would retry against a file that is not there. This is a guess from the key and the timing; we have not read the replica code.

### Expected

A presence record that cannot be applied is either skipped or retried with backoff, and logged once rather than many times a second.

### Environment

- `cua` CLI 0.10.1 on all three Macs
- Cua Spaces app 0.19.4 (both Mac minis) and 0.20.0 (MacBook); Cua Driver 0.38.0
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple silicon
- Three Macs signed in to one Cua account

Related issues: #6238, #6290

title: fix(spaces): keep the host service running through an update and bring it back by itself
body:
## What

After the Cua Spaces 0.22.0 auto-update a Mac could stay offline ("The Cua service isn't running") until it was removed and added again. This fixes the helper (the host service login item) so it comes back by itself, and keeps the evidence if it does not. It is part A of CUA-3746; the Machines page fixes follow in another PR.

## Why it happened

- Three restarters fought over one update: `AppHelper::install` unregistered the helper whenever it was merely stopped, `start()` ran `kickstart -k`, and the app ran `kickstart -k` again at launch. launchd ended the fresh launcher (SIGTERM after 22 ms), and the last one left exited 0, which launchd leaves stopped.
- A bundle swap that took longer than the watch's two looks (about 10 s) made the launcher exit 0 as if the host had been removed.
- The app tried to start a stopped helper three times and then never again.
- The service log lived in `~/.cua/host`, which `host remove` deletes, so the workaround wiped the evidence.

## Changes

- `cua-host`: unregister only when launchd could not start the program (a registration left by another copy); a stopped job gets a plain `kickstart`, `-k` only for a running one.
- Launcher: files gone while the host is set up exits 75 (launchd retries); a stop in the first 5 s of a start exits 75; a stop later, or the spec gone, still exits 0. The driver login item gets the same fix.
- App: restarts a stopped helper with backoff (now, 15 s, 30 s, 1 min, 2 min, then every 5 min, reset once it runs). At launch it waits 30 s for a helper to restart itself before it restarts it.
- Service log moves to `~/.cua/logs/host.log` (outside the host folder, rotated at 5 MB).
- Open question from the issue, answered: a transient network error at wake could not reach `pause_signed_out` through the sign-in service errors (they are `Http`/`Timeout`/`Transport`, which the token read retries and then rethrows, and the reconcile ignores). One path could: when Cua had not started yet (`live == nil`) the token read returned nil, read as signed out. It now throws, and a test covers it.

## Tests

- Rust (`cua-host --lib`): registration and kickstart decision, log location, rotation, and `host remove` keeps the log.
- Swift (`HelperServiceTests`, `HelperMoveTests`, `HostSignInSharingTests`): watch verdicts, launcher exit codes, backoff, repair through the model, log rotation, not-started is not signed out. Run on cua.local.
- `apps/cua-spaces-macos/scripts/tests/helper-selfheal-test.sh`: a fake app with the built launcher under real launchd (own label and scratch home): a swap restarts onto the new daemon, files gone 14 s then back runs again, SIGTERM at the start comes back, a later stop stays stopped, a removed host stays stopped. On cua.local it passes; against the launcher from main it fails at "it runs again once the files are back" (stays stopped), which is the reported bug.

title: fix(cua-volume): a saved presence heartbeat replaces the last one, and a saved change whose bytes are gone is forgotten
body:
Fixes #6859.

## What was wrong
A device writes its presence record (`.cua-devices/<id>.json`) every 30 seconds, and since #6290 the store keeps only the newest version of it. While the Volume's owner was away or the owner was this Mac itself catching up, every heartbeat was saved to the outbox as its own change, and the next heartbeat deleted the bytes of the one before. The outbox then kept retrying changes whose bytes no longer existed, so each pass logged "could not apply a saved change here yet" or "the owner could not take a change yet" for the same few keys.

## What changed
- A saved heartbeat now replaces the earlier saved one for the same record (the new one follows whatever the oldest followed).
- The outbox forgets a saved change whose bytes are gone from the machine, so a Mac already stuck in this state recovers on its next pass, with one warning per dropped change instead of a stream.

## Checks
- Two new simulation tests in `crates/cua-volume/tests/replica_sim.rs`; both fail on `main` (the outbox never drains) and pass here.
- `cargo test -p cua-volume --lib --test replica_sim --test replica_supervision` passes.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix --jobs 1` passes.

title: fix(cua-sandbox): drag over the QMP transport takes the path Mouse.drag sends
body:
Fixes #5966.

`Mouse.drag` sends `path=[[x, y], ...]`, but the QMP transport's drag handler only took `start_x`, `start_y`, `end_x`, `end_y`, so every drag on a QMP-driven VM raised a `TypeError` and nothing was dragged.

The handler now takes the path (press at the first point, move through each point, release at the last) and still accepts the older keyword form. A path with fewer than two points, or a call with neither form, is refused with a plain error before anything is sent.

## Checks
- New `tests/test_qmp_drag.py` (4 tests, mocked QMP socket); the issue's reproduction fails on `main` with the reported `TypeError` and passes here.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix --jobs 1` passes.

title: fix(cua-sdk): the per-platform release archives keep cua executable
body:
Fixes #5709.

## What was wrong
`actions/download-artifact` drops file modes. `@trycua/cua-<platform>` already sets the executable bit when it builds the npm package (`build-npm-packages.mjs`), and the `cua-cli-*` archives set it before archiving, but the `cua-<version>-<platform>.tar.gz` archives did not: I checked the published 0.13.0 `cua-0.13.0-linux-arm64-gnu.tar.gz` and it still holds `cua` as `-rw-r--r--`, so an extracted `cua` fails with "Permission denied". (The 0.13.0 npm packages are already 0755.)

## What changed
The publish job sets the executable bit on `cua`, `cua-vz`, `cua-microvm-init` and the static `cua-spacesd` before it archives each native directory. Libraries stay 0644.

## Checks
- New `.github/scripts/tests/test_cua_sdk_archive_modes.py` runs the real archive loop from the workflow on 0644 inputs and reads the modes back from the tarball; it fails without the change and passes with it.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix --jobs 1` passes (actionlint included).
- The next SDK release's `cua-<version>-<platform>.tar.gz` is where this shows up.

title: [Bug]: Windows UIA COM leak in get_window_state — non-actionable/content nodes are never released
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

get_window_state on Windows leaks one native COM reference per UIA node that has text content but no element_index. Those references are never released, and a single retained root keeps the window's entire UIA bulk cache alive, so the host process's private memory grows about 100–400 KB per observation, even with max_elements set to 1. The leak is in the Rust platform-windows UIA snapshot hand-off, not in the Node runtime.

### Reproduction

1. Load cua_driver_sdk (win32-x64-msvc) in a Node or Electron host. Reproduced with 0.28.0 (cua_driver_sdk.dll 25,250,128 bytes, sha256 db217a8dbbcfd1ec49de6d73e1623a3959c0b5806412d8d5ad0058868c72da69).
2. list_windows, then pick a window with a UIA tree; explorer's Program Manager has 50 elements.
3. Call get_window_state 300 times with include_screenshot:false, include_accessibility_tree:true (default max_elements; also run once with max_elements:1).
4. Every 25 calls, run global.gc() and record `(Get-Process -Id <host-pid>).PrivateMemorySize64`.

### Expected behavior

Memory should be flat after warm-up; shutdown() should return all native memory.

### Actual behavior

0.28.0, 300 calls: +38.4 MiB (about 128–135 KB/call), linear; max_elements:1, 100 calls: +11.4 MiB, so it is not proportional to the returned tree; DSH Electron window, 100 calls: +40.3 MiB (about 415 KB/call). V8 heap +0.6 MiB, external 4.103 MiB unchanged, handles 317->318; shutdown()+uniffiDestroy() does not return the memory.

0.40.1 with a local COM-ownership patch: +2.8 MiB/300 calls, +2.8 MiB/1200, +10.1 MiB/2400 (about 5.7 KB/call). The residual is the separate Node-runtime leak tracked in #5671 / #4339, not this UIA leak.

### Environment

Cua component: cua-driver-sdk 0.28.0 win32-x64-msvc; cua_driver_sdk.dll sha256 db217a8dbbcfd1ec49de6d73e1623a3959c0b5806412d8d5ad0058868c72da69. Source of 0.41.3 checked at tag bd0e299c67dec6397b3d41a259452b2ea13a1cd5.
OS: Windows 11 Home (Chinese), 10.0.26200.9711, x64, 150% DPI, 2560x1600.
Host: Node 24.14.1 (Electron/DSH) and the SDK's own Node runtime; the leak reproduces in both.

### Evidence

Source inspection at tag 0.41.3 (bd0e299c67dec6397b3d41a259452b2ea13a1cd5) still contains the same pattern.

libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs, emit_cached_node: for every node where is_actionable || has_content it clones the IUIAutomationElement, stores element.as_raw() as usize in UiaNode.element_ptr, and calls std::mem::forget on the clone.

libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/uia/snapshot.rs, UiaSnapshot::from_nodes: it filters nodes to element_index.is_some(), copies element_ptr into RetainedElement, and releases only those pointers in RetainedElement::drop. Nodes without element_index are dropped as plain usize; UiaNode has no Drop. libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/get_window_state.rs calls from_nodes(&tree.nodes, kind) and then drops the tree. release_walk_nodes is only used on error/menu paths.

0.28.0 has the same ownership model in uia/cache.rs (ElementCache::update_with_kind); I backported the fix there and measured the numbers above.

### Workaround and additional context

I can test a candidate patch and provide the minimal harness if useful; I already have a 0.28.0 backport and A/B numbers, and can open a PR against 0.41.x. This is not a duplicate of #5671/#4339: those are the Node ThreadsafeFunction/libuv leak; this one is Windows UIA/COM ownership.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(spaces): a slow-starting desktop no longer keeps a sleeping Space awake
body:
## What

A Space that sleeps on its own could stay awake forever when its desktop started slowly. The quiet check counted any process started more than 30 s after the Space booted as the agent's, and with several Spaces booting at once the desktop panel helpers start later than that. In an 8-Space run one Space never slept and held the runtime VM up for the whole run (`not asleep yet: 4 process(es) ... up 541 s`).

The check now treats a process as the Space's own when it is part of its start-up, or is one of the desktop's helpers (matched by name) that was not started through `cua-spacesd`. Anything started through `cua-spacesd` (every agent run, exec and job) and any other process still counts as the agent's, so a forgotten shell still keeps the Space awake.

## Checked

The new check counted 0 on the stuck Space in the 8-Space run (it counted 4 before). Follow-up of #6754, tracked in CUA-3661.

title: fix(spaces): the permission guide always docks under System Settings, and the rows show each switch live (CUA-3551)
body:
**What changes for users:** when you press Allow for "See the screen" or "Use the mouse and keyboard", the guide panel now always sits under System Settings and says what to do there: drag Cua Spaces into the list if it isn't there, turn its switch on if it is, then that it's on. Back in Cua Spaces, also after Quit & Reopen, each permission row says "Waiting for the switch" and turns to a check and "On" within a second of the grant.

Fixes two bugs Francesco hit while dogfooding the new onboarding ([CUA-3551](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-3551)).

## Bug 1: a listed-but-off app got only a banner at the top

**Cause:** `PermissionGuide` guessed whether the app had a row in the list from a UserDefaults note, set whenever it had once seen a grant (`isListed` / `markListed`). When the note said "listed", it skipped PermissionFlow's docked panel and drew a separate hint at the top of the screen. The note is wrong for a rebuilt Cua Spaces Local: it's signed ad hoc, so its old row stays in the list but this copy has no grant. The top hint was also easy to miss.

**Fix:**
- **Where each pane stands now comes from macOS.** The public preflight answers "on". TCC's own preflight (`TCCAccessPreflight`, looked up at run time, so a macOS without it degrades to "unknown") tells "a row switched off" (1) from "no row" (2). On a fresh macOS 26.4 VM: a fresh app read 2, listed and off read 1, switched on read 0, and a rebuilt copy whose old row still looks on read 1. In that last case it is off for this copy.
- **One docked panel for every state.** PermissionFlow 2.11.4 (MIT) is now vendored in `apps/cua-spaces-macos/Vendor/PermissionFlow` with one addition, `setGuidance`, so the panel's words and drag tile follow the state. The top banner is gone. The drag tile stays while the switch is off, for a row an older build left behind. `Vendor/PermissionFlow/README.md` lists the change for the next upgrade.
- **The guide reads the pane every second** and updates the panel in place, the same way Cua Driver's guide does (#6766).

| State | Panel line | Second line | Tile |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not in the list | Drag **Cua Spaces Local** into the list above to allow **Accessibility**. | Then make sure its switch is on. | yes |
| In the list, off | Turn on the switch next to **Cua Spaces Local** in the list above. | Already on, or not in the list? Drag this in. | yes |
| On | **Accessibility** is on for **Cua Spaces Local**. | (Screen Recording: If macOS asks, choose Quit & Reopen…) | no |

## Bug 2: no sign the grant applied after Quit & Reopen

**Cause:** the rows only knew whether a permission was granted, polled every 2.5 s, and showed nothing while waiting. After a relaunch nothing remembered that Allow had been pressed.

**Fix:**
- `driver.permissions` rows carry `state` (`on`, `off`, `absent`, `unknown`). The bridge contract and demo host are updated.
- `useAppPermissions` remembers Allow for 15 minutes across a relaunch (localStorage). It polls every second while waiting and re-reads on focus.
- `AppPermissionList` (the first run's step, the Cua Driver page, This Mac) shows a live status on each row: a check and "On", a spinner and "Waiting for the switch", "Off", or "Not in the list yet".
- The Mac app notes the pane it's guiding. After a relaunch with System Settings still open, it guides whatever is still missing (`resumeAfterRelaunch`).

Home's "Now bring the rest in" card exists only on #6787's branch, so its part of this fix is a separate PR against that branch.

## Tests
- Swift `PermissionGuideTests` (26 with `BridgeContractTests`, all green locally): state mapping, panel words for each state, report parsing (including an older build's `1`/`0`), resume after relaunch, and bridge rows carrying `state`.
- Web `app-permissions-live.test.tsx`: state and status mapping; rows turning On live after Allow, after a reload with Allow pending, and on window focus; and forgetting an Allow older than 15 minutes. `first-run-new` and `driver` tests are updated for "On" and "Off".
- `bin/ci --quick --fix` is green.
- Real macOS: on a fresh macOS 26.4 VM I checked the TCC states above, and the docked panel in all three states with a harness app that links the vendored package. The full Cua Spaces Local build wasn't run in the VM.

title: test(cua-driver): wait for the child's exec in the NO_AT_BRIDGE test
body:
## Summary

**Problem:** `an_empty_walk_reads_the_reason_from_the_real_process` fails about 1 run in 30 (14 of 400 on a busy machine). `spawn` can return while the kernel is still finishing the child's exec, and until then `/proc/<pid>/environ` can read empty, so the test sees no `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1`.

**Fix:** the test helper waits up to 5 s until the child's environ holds the value. Only test code changes.

**Evidence:** 14 of 400 runs failed before and 0 of 400 after. A temporary probe caught the variable missing right after `spawn` returned, often with an empty environ.

## Related work

RFC: not needed, no contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none. Test code only.
- Risk and rollback: a child that never finishes exec now fails this test after 5 s with `sleep never finished exec`. Revert to drop it.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the 400-run loop of `atspi::bridge_disabled_reason_tests`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings`, all in a container on the fix before its last rebase. `bin/ci --quick --base upstream/main` passes on this head.
- Manual or platform evidence: not applicable, this is a test helper.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the full unit suite on this exact commit. The rebase picked up no change to this file.

title: feat(spaces): Child Spaces and Warm start are always on, their Labs switches are gone (CUA-3751)
body:
## What

Child Spaces and Warm start are always on. Their Labs switches are gone (Settings, Advanced, Labs; `cua experiments`), the same way Ask first and Secure Spaces went in #6775.

Part of CUA-3551, tracked in CUA-3751. Stacked on #6775 (which is stacked on #6593): this PR targets that branch so the diff shows only this change, and it merges after both. It replaces #6858, whose web-side warm start depended on a flag #6593 deletes.

## What changes for people

- The Labs rows for Child Spaces and Warm start disappear. Cua Volume, CI runners, Public TCP shares and the Phone app stay.
- `cua experiments enable child-spaces` (or `warm-pools`) says the feature is always on and has no switch. A switch someone turned off once is ignored and removed the next time the app saves its settings.
- Child Spaces: the commands and calls (`cua spaces children`, `budget`, `orphans`, `ls --tree`, `create --parent`, `cua spaces service add`, the SDK and the agent tools) work without an opt-in. The per-Space "may make child Spaces" setting stays; an agent run turns it on for its own Space.
- Home's line under the box no longer says "Starting agent" for a session a finished run closed, and a job whose Space was never made ends as "Didn't start" (Try again) instead of waiting for hours.
- A Space the host marks hidden (the warm home) is hidden even when this page has no record of preparing it.
- Home's prompt box now starts from the agent's Home Space for everyone. That mode was reached only with the Child Spaces switch on, so graduating the switch is what turns it on.
- Computers (the Spaces tree): a child Space now sits under the Space that made it, one step further in for each generation, and can be folded. A parent's task count includes its children's; Delete and Remove name the children that go with it. Before, child Spaces sat flat beside their parent.
- Warm start: once the first run is over (done or skipped) and a coding app is installed, the app keeps one hidden Linux home warm, so the first message is handed to a Space that is already there. The home is not in the tree, its counts, the sidebar, the palette or the Agents list until a person writes into it; its own page and Home's preparing line still show it. Nothing starts while the first run shows. This is the pre-#6662 behaviour, restored without a flag.
- The first Linux Space Home offers is the slim tier (`linux:24.04-slim`, about 470 MB), the image the daemon keeps ready.
- The daemon keeps one warm Space ready on every computer (2 hours without a create, and whenever the computer needs the memory). `CUA_WARM_START=0` turns it off for one daemon as an operator override, not a setting.

## What's in it

- `cua-vmm` `experiments.rs`: `Gate` loses `ChildSpaces` and `WarmPools`; `RETIRED` lists the two names.
- Daemon, `cua-spaces`, SDK, CLI, phone control: the experiment checks are gone; warm pool is always applied unless `CUA_WARM_START=0`.
- App core, FFI, generated bindings, the app shells, telemetry schema, parity golden and docs follow.
- Web: `buildSpacesTree` takes the child-to-parent map and nests rows (`spaces-tree.ts`, `spaces-tree-page.tsx`, `use-spaces-tree.ts`); `PrepareRoot` drives the warm home again (start at launch, resume once per load, rebuild a removed home, follow the connection).

## Tests

- New: `spaces-tree.test.ts` (child nesting: parents and grandchildren, counts, tasks, offline wait, missing parent, loop), `warm-start-home.test.tsx` (hidden from the tree, summary and sidebar, stays hidden after a restart, shows after the first message, silent when it cannot be made, nothing before the first run is over), `prepare-launch.test.tsx` (one create, labelled hidden; rebuilt once when gone), `warm_start_is_always_on_unless_the_operator_turns_it_off`, CLI always-on commands. The pool's idle drain keeps its existing test (`an idle warm Space keeps no member`).
- Updated: Labs rows, retired switch files, parity golden, the first Space offer.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix --jobs 1` and `bin/ci --signoff`; cargo tests per crate with `--lib` (cua-vmm, cua-spaces, cua-spaces-app-core, cua-spaces-ffi, cua-telemetry, cua-cli, cua-daemon), the web vitest suite with the wasm core built.

title: feat(spaces): existing homes and the warm Space sleep by default
body:
Stacked on #6868 (the probe fix); until it merges this diff shows both.

## What

The owner's homes (`epic-penguin`, `mild-fox`, `daring-moose`) never slept: they carry `cua.home` and `cua.home.agent` but no `cua.sleep`, and the idle policy treated that as `never`.

- A Space with no `cua.sleep` label is now `auto` when it is an agent home (`cua.home=1`) or the hidden home warming for Home (`cua.hidden`). So homes made before the setting pick it up with no recreation and no migration step. Any other Space is still `never`. An explicit label or a stored setting wins.
- `Spaces::set_sleep`, `Spaces::keep_awake` (at most 2 h) and `Spaces::keep_awake_of` store a per-Space override in `sleep.json` next to the registry; the sleep check honours both, and a kept-awake Space says so in the log. CLI, SDK, MCP and the Space page come in the next pieces.
- The warm Space for Home is given back after 30 minutes unused instead of 2 hours (`HOME_WARM_IDLE`, used only for this home warming; every other warm pool keeps `WARM_POOLS_IDLE`, 2 hours). It is a pool member, so the pool drains it; the app-side warming home removed in #6662 is not re-added.

## Checked on a Mac Studio (mock provider, isolated home, 8 homes labelled only `cua.home=1`, no `cua.sleep`)

All 8 agents completed (the last at 214 s). All 8 Spaces were stopped at 398 s, the runtime VM stopped at 514 s, and the Mac was back at its idle level at 521 s. The straggler fixed in #6868 did not occur. A message to a stopped home got its reply in 8.7 s with the runtime VM up and 26.9 s from fully cold.

`cargo test -p cua-spaces --lib sleep` passes (new test for the helper default).

Tracked in CUA-3661.

title: fix(spaces): pair a machine with its device by the id it publishes, and show the stopped service's log
body:
## What

CUA-3746 parts B and the rest of fix 3. UI-visible (the service issue now shows log lines): this PR waits for screenshots before merge.

- **Stable device-to-machine link.** The relay keeps no link between a machine and the device the account enrolled on the same computer, so the Machines page paired them by guessing from names. Two devices named "Francesco's MacBook Pro" (a device is named after its hostname) were paired wrongly or not at all, and a machine missing between remove and re-add left its device as a second row. Now the host publishes its device id in relay meta (`cua.host.device`, written at setup and again at re-registration), `RelayMachine` carries it as `device_id`, and the core pairs a machine with that device alone: `MachineIn.device_id` and `MachinesPageInput.device_ids` in `machines.rs`, and `deviceId` in `derive.ts`. A machine without the id (an older host) is still paired by the old name guesses.
- **Shells.** SwiftUI app (`machineDeviceIds` into the page input and the web bridge), Electron app (the same into `AppMachinesPageInput` and its bridge), and the web adapter. The Tauri app has no machine pairing input of its own (it never passed hostnames either), so it uses the web fallback in `derive.ts`.
- **Service log in the issue.** When the service is set up but not running, `host status` carries the last lines of its log (`service_log`), and the "The Cua service isn't running" issue shows them under the sentence, so the reason is on the page.
- Bindings regenerated (SDK, Electron, SwiftUI) and the drift gates pass.

## Tests

- Rust `machines`: two devices with one name pair by id; remove and re-add keeps one row per computer, also when renamed in between; a machine whose device is not listed never guesses another by name; page rows read the id by machine id. `cua-host`: meta carries only a `dev_` id, the log lines. `cua-sdk`: `RelayMachine.device_id`. App core: the service issue carries the log lines. Whole `cua-spaces-app-core --lib` passes (897).
- Web: the same two-devices and remove-and-add case through the webkit adapter and `derive.ts`; the full web suite passes (1639). Desktop suite passes (834).
- Swift: `DevicesTests`, `MachinesViewTests`, `MachinesPaletteTests`, `BridgeContractTests`, `ParityTests`, `HostSetupAuthTests` pass (97 tests). Run on cua.local.

Stacks on nothing: it reads `HostPaths::log()`, which #6862 moves to `~/.cua/logs/host.log`; until that merges the lines come from the old location.

title: fix(cua-driver): type exact text on the active keyboard layout and name kwin-capture on in its refusal
body:
## Why

#6447 by @astrovm types exact text on the active keyboard layout or refuses it with nothing typed. When the compositor doesn't report Caps Lock or Num Lock, it refuses letters but doesn't say how to fix that. On KDE Plasma 6.3 to 6.5, KWin offers the lock-key global only to a program whose desktop entry lists it, and `cua-driver kwin-capture on` writes that entry. This PR supersedes #6447, keeps astrovm's commits, and adds the fix to the refusal text.

Salvaged from #6447

## What changed

- astrovm's commits from #6447, unchanged, authorship kept. Their PR body has the full design and the measured KWin 6.3.6, 6.6.6 and 6.8.2 runs.
- `plan_on_any` in `wayland/libei.rs`: the unknown-lock-keys refusal now ends "on KDE Plasma 6.3 to 6.5, `cua-driver kwin-capture on` lets the driver read them". Its test asserts the full new text.
- A merge of main. The only conflict was one `mod` line in `wayland/mod.rs` (main's `kwin_layout`, this branch's `kwin_keystate`), and both are kept.

## Scope

Linux libei typing and its refusal text. Nothing else in the KWin series is included.

## Blast Radius

Linux desktop `type_text` on libei (KDE and GNOME), as in #6447. Merge after #6820, which adds the `cua-driver kwin-capture on` command the refusal names. #6827 is an earlier salvage of #6447 that has the same commits plus review fixes. The two overlap in `libei.rs`, so only one of them should land.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, lint) passes. `cargo clippy -D warnings --all-targets` for `platform-linux`, with and without `portal-input`, is clean on aarch64 Linux.
- `platform-linux` lib tests with `portal-input` ran on a Linux VM: 1008 passed, 0 failed, including `with_the_lock_keys_unknown_only_text_they_dont_change_goes_out` with the new text.
- Not run: the verify-cua-driver X11 and Wayland lanes, and the contributor's KWin desktop matrix on this head.

Size: the contributor's change is about 2,300 added lines, most of it the layout-aware key planner and its tests; this PR adds one sentence on top.

title: perf(cua-driver): read each AX node in one batched round trip
body:
Rebased onto current main from #5921, original work by gakonst. Supersedes #5921.

What changes for users: the accessibility tree walk behind get_window_state drops from 117-145 ms to 56-61 ms (Calculator) and 128-144 ms to 69-85 ms (TextEdit) under load, and from 47-51 ms to 16-19 ms on an idle machine (measured in the original PR).

Checks on current main: `cargo test --lib` for the touched crate passes on a macOS machine, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.

---

## Summary

The macOS tree walker reads every node attribute by attribute: AXRole, AXTitle, AXValue, AXPlaceholderValue, AXDescription, AXIdentifier, AXHelp, AXEnabled, AXPosition, AXSize, AXValueDescription, AXMinValue, AXMaxValue, AXSelected and AXChildren are each one Mach round trip that the target app answers on its main thread.

This reads them with one `AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues` call per node (new `ax/batch.rs`) and converts the reply with the same rules as the single-read helpers (`copy_string_attr`, `copy_stringish_attr`, `copy_bool_attr`, `copy_number_attr`, `element_screen_rect`, `copy_children`), so `tree_markdown` and `elements` are unchanged. Action names and `AXValue` settability stay separate reads.

- If an app refuses the batch, the node falls back to the single reads.
- If the app does not answer in time (`kAXErrorCannotComplete`), the node is treated as unreadable instead of waiting out the 2 s messaging timeout once per attribute.

Refs #1757. That draft batches the same attributes on a much older walker. This version is rebased onto the current walker (menu collapsing, control state, web-content marker, value-settable rows). If maintainers would rather land it through #1757, I'm happy to close this one.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1, about 1,400 WindowServer windows open. Daemon run as `CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED=1 cua-driver serve --socket …`, driven by a stdio MCP client through `cua-driver mcp --socket …`. Walk phase from timing marks around `walk_tree_budgeted` in `get_window_state`, median of 15:

| window | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Calculator (36 indexed rows) | 117–145 ms | 56–61 ms |
| TextEdit document | 128–144 ms | 69–85 ms |

Those runs were under machine load (load average about 10). On an idle machine the walk went from 47–51 ms to 16–19 ms, combined with the window-lookup change in the companion PR.

## Validation

- Live A/B on the same windows: `tree_markdown`, `elements` (minus tokens) and the structured key set are byte-identical to main for Calculator and a TextEdit document.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 639 passed. One unrelated port-discovery test (`owned_discovery_prefers_profile_endpoint_over_inherited_listener`) failed once and passed on three reruns.
- `cargo fmt` passes. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets` adds no new warnings.

title: perf(cua-driver): identify apps without spawning ps or listing every process
body:
Rebased onto current main from #5923, original work by gakonst. Supersedes #5923.

What changes for users: each background click, type_text, scroll, hotkey and set_value saves about 34 ms (the Electron check goes from 35 ms to 1.1 ms), and get_window_state saves 7.7-10.5 ms per read (measured in the original PR).

Checks on current main: `cargo test --lib` for the touched crate passes on a macOS machine, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.

---

## Summary

- `apps::get_app_name_for_pid` spawned `ps -p <pid> -o comm=` on every call, and `get_window_state` called it twice per read through `chromium_browser_window`.
- `ElectronJs::is_electron` runs before every background click, `type_text`, scroll, hotkey and `set_value`. It listed every running app (about 35 ms with roughly 950 processes) to find the pid's name, then spawned `ps` for the executable path.

This PR:

- The `comm` column is the process's argv[0]. `process_command` reads it with `sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2)`, which the kernel answers for the user's own processes (every app the driver targets). It falls back to the setuid `ps` only when the kernel withholds the arguments.
- `get_window_state` asks once per read.
- `is_electron` checks the executable first. It lists the running apps only when the pid's own bundle name could lead to an Electron bundle. Both checks still run whenever either could be true, so the answer is unchanged.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1:

- `is_electron` over all 948 running pids: old and new agree on every pid (4 Electron). Total time drops from 33.8 s to 1.06 s, about 35 ms to 1.1 ms per call.
- `get_window_state` tree-only: the two `ps` spawns cost 7.7–10.5 ms per read, now 0.2 ms.
- AX click on Calculator: the key-window prime step falls by the `is_electron` cost.

## Validation

- New unit tests: `procargs2_argv0_skips_the_executable_path_and_padding` (parser) and `app_name_matches_ps_for_this_process` (`ps` and the new path agree for the test process).
- A one-off equivalence test (not committed) compared old and new `is_electron` on every running pid.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` passes. `cargo fmt` passes. `cargo clippy` adds no new warnings.

title: perf(cua-driver): poll AXWebArea instead of sleeping 500 ms on Chromium AX wake
body:
Rebased onto current main from #6272, original work by saariuslystoned. Supersedes #6272.

What changes for users: the first get_window_state on a Chromium or Electron app saves up to 450 ms when the web content settles quickly; pages that keep growing still wait the full 500 ms (from the original PR).

Checks on current main: `cargo test --lib` for the touched crate passes on a macOS machine, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.

---

## Summary

- Problem this solves: On macOS, `ax::enablement::await_web_content` unconditionally slept for `CHROMIUM_SETTLE_SECONDS` (`500 ms`) after detecting a populated `AXWebArea` and re-asserting `AXEnhancedUserInterface` / `AXManualAccessibility`, even when Chromium's accessibility subtree had already finished materializing within `50–100 ms`.
- What changed: `probe_web_content` now samples a bounded `AXWebArea` descendant count (`WEB_AREA_SETTLE_SAMPLE_CAP = 128`, depth `4`), and `await_web_content` polls in `50 ms` slices (`CHROMIUM_SETTLE_POLL_SECONDS`) up to the existing `500 ms` ceiling (`CHROMIUM_SETTLE_MAX_SECONDS`), returning early once two consecutive slices observe the same non-zero descendant count.

## Related work

Refs #6270

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Not required (internal macOS AX wake latency optimization; zero API, CLI, MCP, SDK, or permission changes).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only; zero public schema or behavior changes. First-read `get_window_state` on Chromium/Electron apps saves up to `450 ms` when the `AXWebArea` subtree stabilizes quickly while retaining the exact `500 ms` upper bound for actively growing pages.
- Risk and rollback: Bounded descendant sampling (`<= 128` nodes, depth `<= 4`) keeps probe overhead sub-millisecond, and continuously mutating pages still settle up to the full `500 ms` ceiling. Revert `platform-macos/src/ax/enablement.rs` to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `scripts/ci/prepush.sh --fast` (SPDX headers + `cargo fmt`)
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib ax::enablement` (`11 passed; 0 failed`, covering immediate stabilization, multi-slice growth stabilization, continuous-growth 500 ms ceiling enforcement, and timeout behavior)
- Manual or platform evidence: Exercised against live macOS Electron and Chrome targets in end-to-end `get_window_state` background automation runs.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Upstream CI lanes.

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

title: perf(cua-driver): capture the macOS desktop with captureImage(in:) when there is no overlay to leave out
body:
Rebased onto current main from #6028, original work by loomhand. Supersedes #6028.

What changes for users: get_desktop_state without the agent cursor overlay goes from p50 325 ms to 170 ms at 1024 px (A/B/B/A on a macOS 26.5 VM, from the original PR).

Checks on current main: `cargo test --lib` for the touched crate passes on a macOS machine, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.

---

On macOS, `get_desktop_state` captures the main display in about half the time when the agent cursor overlay is not on screen.

**Problem.** With no overlay window to leave out, `screenshot_display_bytes_excluding_overlay` runs `/usr/sbin/screencapture -x`: a process, a temporary file and a PNG decode, about 300 ms per call on a 1280x800 display.

**Fix.** That path now captures with `SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(in:)` over the main display bounds, which skips the shareable-content query and the content filter: about 115 ms for the same pixels, against 180–240 ms for the content-filter capture the overlay path uses. `screencapture` stays the fallback when ScreenCaptureKit fails. The `screencapturekit` feature moves from `macos_15_0` to `macos_15_2`; the crate's bridge checks `#available(macOS 15.2, *)` at run time and returns an error before 15.2, so older systems keep the `screencapture` path.

**Testing.** macOS 26.5 VM without GPU, `get_desktop_state` at 1024 px, builds alternated A/B/B/A: p50 325 → 170 ms. At 2x (2560x1600) the image size is unchanged and the 1024 px image is identical; at full size the only difference is the menu bar's screen-recording indicator. No unit test: the capture needs a display and Screen Recording, which plain `cargo test` does not use.

Platforms: macOS only.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` (636 passed) on a macos-15 runner. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` reports nothing in the touched files; it stops on `ax/reveal_scroll.rs:185` (`single_match`), which is on `main` too.

title: perf(cua-driver): look up one window by id instead of enumerating all
body:
## What changes for users

Every action on a window (`get_window_state`, clicks, typing) now finds its target window with one WindowServer lookup instead of listing every window on the Mac. Calls are faster, and the saving grows with the number of open windows.

## How

- New `windows::describe_window(id)` reads one window with `CGWindowListCreateDescriptionFromArray`. A window below the normal level is checked against the existing desktop-element enumeration, so a lookup lists exactly what that enumeration lists (wallpaper, desktop icons and similar stay excluded).
- The description parsing is now shared with `enumerate_windows` (`parse_description`), so both paths read windows the same way.
- `resolve_window_owner`, `window_bounds_by_id`, the capture identity check, the `get_window_state` title and app lookups, and the focus-failure hint use it.
- `window_on_current_space_by_id` and `window_space_view_by_id` ask SkyLight for the Spaces of that one window, not of every window.
- The keyboard-sibling count in `gather_background_facts` describes only the windows the accessibility tree maps, lazily.
- `list_running_apps` skips the per-window Space queries, since it only reads owner pids.

Ported onto current main, keeping main's `enumerate_windows` (pid filter, spaces flag) and the `focused_window_id_of_pid` focus-hint semantics.

## Measurements

Per-lookup, median of 50, on a macOS test machine with 246 listed windows (new ignored test `single_window_lookup_timing`):

| lookup | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| window_info_by_id vs describe_window | 2.68 ms | 0.16 ms |
| window_on_current_space_by_id | 32.6 ms | 0.39 ms |

End-to-end `get_window_state` p50 from the original PR, measured on a Mac with about 1,400 windows:

| call | main | this change |
|---|---|---|
| tree only (Calculator) | 129-134 ms | 67 ms |
| tree + screenshot (Calculator) | 183-188 ms | 79-83 ms |
| tree only (TextEdit) | 139-141 ms | 75-76 ms |
| tree + screenshot (TextEdit) | 242-244 ms | 130-133 ms |

## Validation

- `cargo test --lib -p platform-macos`: 695 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored. One browser-discovery test was flaky once in a full run and passed on rerun.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-macos -- -D warnings`: clean.

Supersedes #5922; original work by gakonst. Refs #4534 and #4940.

title: perf(cua-driver): memoize the installed-app scan behind a root-mtime key
body:
Rebased onto current main from #3492, original work by hyprcat. Supersedes #3492.

What changes for users: repeated list_apps calls skip the app scan: p50 drops from about 620 ms to 0.04 ms for a warm call, and 8 concurrent cold callers share one scan (974 ms to 586 ms p50). The first call and the call after an install cost the same as before (exact-head A/B on an M5 with 83 bundles, from the original PR).

Checks on current main: `cargo test --lib` for the touched crate passes on a macOS machine, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.

---

## Problem

`list_all_apps` re-walks five app directories and re-reads every bundle's `Info.plist` on **every call** — hundreds of file reads for an answer that changes only when something is installed or removed. Measured against the 0.16 binary under adversarial load (6 CPU spinners, fresh connection per request): `list_apps` p50 **1.2–2.6 s**, dominated by this scan.

## Change

`scan_installed_apps` is memoized behind a two-part key:

- **Root mtimes** — adding or removing a `.app` bundle touches its parent directory, so an install/uninstall invalidates the cache instantly.
- **30s TTL** — per-bundle `last_used` timestamps (filesystem mtime heuristic) can change without any root directory noticing; the TTL bounds that drift.

An unreadable root keys as `None`, and two `None`s compare equal — a permanently missing root (e.g. no `~/Applications`) still caches instead of rescanning forever. Running apps are untouched: `list_running_apps` still runs live on every call, and running entries are still backfilled from the (now cached) installed scan.

The freshness contract (`installed_cache_is_fresh`) is a pure function with a unit test covering: matching key within TTL → serve; changed mtime, appearing/disappearing root, or expired TTL → rescan.

## Numbers

With the equivalent mtime-keyed cache in the Swift driver this Rust tree mirrors, the same adversarial bench answered `list_apps` in **~15–23 ms** (vs 1.2–2.6 s), with correctness checked against `NSWorkspace` ground truth (21/21 running apps, all bundle ids present).

`cargo test -p platform-macos` — 353 passed. `cargo fmt` applied.

title: perf(cua-driver): batch macOS type_text key events and stop polling a field that never changes
body:
`type_text` took 4.8 s at p50 in the public Cua Driver Bench data (0.38.0, macOS, 31 calls). Typing into an app where the AX write is not available now takes a fraction of that.

**Where the time went.** AX `AXSelectedText` was already the first rung. The slow cases fall through to key events: one down/up pair per character with a 30 ms pause after each (about 38 ms per character, so about 4 s for 100 characters), then a read-back poll that waited the full 2 s when the field never changed (web content echoing a stale value, or an app ignoring the keys). Windows and Linux have their own per-character `delay_ms` default of 30; this PR does not touch them.

**Changes (macOS)**
- Default `delay_ms` is now 0, which sends text in batched key events of up to 16 UTF-16 units (no character is split; Return and Tab stay real key presses). A positive `delay_ms` keeps one paced key per character, for debounced search boxes.
- If a native field takes only part of a batch, the undelivered tail is retyped one paced key at a time. Web content is never retyped, because its read-back cannot prove how much landed and a retype could duplicate text.
- A readable field that has not changed after 500 ms stops the poll instead of waiting out the 2 s timeout. Polling is every 5 ms instead of 10 ms.
- Unchanged: AX-first order, terminals (key events, no read-back), secure fields, the verification and refusal rules, and the foreground and desktop-scope paths.

**Numbers** (posting a 103-character string to TextEdit on a loaded build host, p50 of 9 runs, `bench_type_text_posting`): paced 30 ms default 7967 ms, batched 313 ms. The host was at load average 60, so the absolute values are inflated; the ratio is the point. Idle-host expectation for the before case is about 4 s.

**Relation to other PRs.** #3490 makes the 30 ms default an env knob (`CUA_DRIVER_RS_TYPE_TEXT_DELAY_MS`) at the same two call sites. This PR changes the default itself, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase: keep the knob and make its default 0.

**Tests.** Chunk planner (limits, astral characters, controls, round trip), the give-up window, and the default. `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib -- type_text` passes (27 tests).

Risk: an app that reads only the first character of a multi-character key event gets the tail retyped paced, so it is correct but slower for that app. The generated tool reference text for `delay_ms` changed and may need regenerating in CI.

title: perf(cua-driver): capture PiP frames off the request path
body:
Rebased onto current main from #5769, original work by Shahfarzane. Supersedes #5769.

What changes for users: with the experimental PiP preview on, each action result no longer waits for a window capture, which held results back 2.2 s for a 1332x1049 window and 0.5 s for a 640x558 window (from the original PR's daemon phase timings). With PiP off nothing changes.

Checks on current main: `cargo test --lib` for the touched crate passes on a macOS machine, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.

---

## Summary

- Problem this solves: with the experimental PiP preview on, every action tool captured and PNG-encoded the action's window before it returned its result. In a debug build that held each result back 2.2 s for a 1332x1049 window and 0.5 s for a 640x558 window (Astro Gold 6.7.6, from the daemon's phase timings). For a menu command that was most of a 2.3 to 3.0 s call.
- What changed: the frame is captured on its own thread after the result is returned. One capture runs at a time. An action that finishes while a capture is still running gets no frame of its own; the next action after that capture ends gets one. With PiP off (no PiP backend registered), nothing changes.

## Related work

No issue filed. I found no open PR that changes when the PiP frame is captured.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. No tool, schema, or result change. Only the timing of the PiP preview frame changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - Only with the experimental PiP preview on. Tool results return without waiting for the capture.
  - The preview frame now shows the window a moment after the result returns, not just before. Under fast consecutive actions, some actions get no preview frame.
  - The code is in `cua-driver-core`, so it applies on every platform with a PiP backend.
- Risk and rollback: at most one capture thread is alive at a time; a busy flag is cleared when the thread ends and when the thread fails to spawn. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (macOS 27.2 arm64, from `libs/cua-driver/rust`):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo build -p cua-driver --locked`: ok.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core`: 1125 passed, 2 ignored.
  - `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test`: 2 passed, 1 ignored.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 27.2 arm64, debug build, Astro Gold 6.7.6, PiP on, another app frontmost):
  - The capture this PR moves off the request path cost 2.2 s per action on the 1332x1049 main window and 0.5 s on a 640x558 window.
  - On a prototype branch that also carried #5770 (background menus) and #5771 (pop-ups and dialog fields), `invoke_menu` calls went from 2.3 to 3.0 s down to 0.44 to 0.45 s, and a background `click` on a dialog button from 1.55 s to 1.25 s. Those totals mix this change with the others, so I only claim the capture cost above for this PR.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - No unit test drives the background capture. It needs a registered PiP backend and a live window.
  - Not timed on a release build: on this macOS beta, release-profile proc-macro dylibs fail to load, so only debug builds run here.
  - Not run on Windows or Linux.
  - `cargo clippy` was not run: clippy is not installed for the pinned 1.97.1 toolchain on this machine.

title: perf(cua-driver): run health checks concurrently
body:
Rebased onto current main from #3500, original work by hyprcat. Supersedes #3500.

What changes for users: a full health_report on Windows and Linux takes about as long as its slowest probe instead of the sum of all probes. On macOS the provider checks run synchronously, so this PR changes nothing there (stated in the original PR). One unrelated timing test, batch_tools pauses_between_steps_but_not_after_the_last, also fails on plain main when the build machine is under heavy load.

Checks on current main: `cargo test --lib` for the touched crate passes on a macOS machine, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.

---

## Problem

`HealthReportTool::invoke` awaits each provider check in sequence, so a full report pays the **sum** of every probe's latency — and the slow probes (capture, AX, subprocess-backed checks) dominate. The checks are independent probes; nothing about the report depends on execution order.

## Change

The loop becomes `futures_util::future::join_all` (already a dependency of `cua-driver-core`) over the same per-name closure:

- All check futures are polled **within the same task** — no extra threads, and no new `Send`/`Sync` requirements on `HealthCheckProvider` implementations.
- `join_all` returns results in input order, so the report keeps its canonical check order (pinned by the existing fixture test, still green).
- Skip-filter behavior unchanged: filtered names still yield their skip entries in place.

A provider whose checks must not overlap can still serialize internally, but none of the in-tree providers do — each check is a self-contained probe.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos` — green, including `invoke_full_run_produces_macos_check_set` (canonical order) and the core fixture suite.
- In the Swift driver this Rust tree mirrors, the same change (task group with order-preserving slots) took a warm quiet `health_report` from ~43ms to ~0.4ms; the report's floor becomes the slowest single probe instead of the sum of all probes.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse an ambiguous AT-SPI editable pick on Linux
body:
On Linux, an app with several text fields and no reported focus no longer gets text written into the first field in tree order. The driver now refuses that pick and falls through to real key events, which go where focus actually is.

Before, in Geany the first editable is the toolbar search entry, several nodes above the document. When another process held X input focus, text meant for the document went into that entry and the write was still reported as confirmed. The last rung of `pick_editable_index` now fires only when the app has exactly one editable.

This is the part of #3049 that main still lacked. The rest is already on main, so I left it out:

- Foreground `type_text` for every toolkit: the foreground branch in `tools/type_text.rs` runs before any AT-SPI probe.
- Cursor tap: the Windows-style tap is now `emit_cursor_hook`, called from `reveal_pointer_action_for`, and it works without an overlay renderer.
- Keysym spellings such as `Page_Down`: the table accepts them.
- Capture timeout: window capture is bounded. The full-display `import` fallback is still unbounded; I left it for a separate change.
- Windows `window_center`: already done.

Tests: `pick_editable_tests` gains a case for several editables with no focus (`None`), and the existing single-editable and page-content cases still pass. I ran the pure picker tests on a macOS host; the Linux lanes in CI cover the crate build.

Linear: CUA-3763. Replaces #3049, with Dillon DuPont credited as co-author.

title: feat(cua-driver): tool profiles to cut the advertised tool list (draft)
body:
Draft. Changes the public tool surface only when opted in; default stays `full`. Needs design review before it leaves draft.

**What users get:** agents that load every schema pay for 62 tools. With `CUA_DRIVER_TOOL_PROFILE=core` or `standard` the server advertises fewer, so clients that load all tools spend fewer tokens and choose among fewer tools.

**What it does**
- `CUA_DRIVER_TOOL_PROFILE=full|core|standard|core,<group>,...` (groups: core, browser, recording, cursor, session, admin, input_extra). Unset or invalid means `full`.
- Narrows only the `tools/list` result (direct server and stdio proxy), adds a `tool_profile` field listing what is hidden, and adds one line to the server instructions.
- Hidden tools stay registered and callable by name through the same authorization. Nothing is proxied. A tool that no group names is always listed.
- `rust/scripts/measure-tool-tokens.py` counts tokens per tool.

**Measured** (tiktoken o200k_base as a proxy tokenizer; model-visible = name + description + schema, on main 0.42.3)

| Profile | Tools | Tokens |
|---|---|---|
| full | 62 | 30,959 |
| standard (core + browser) | 39 | 22,668 (-27%) |
| core | 27 | 17,259 (-44%) |

Groups are drawn from tool-call frequencies in 90 recorded bench trials: `standard` covers 99.8% of the calls recorded there, `core` 95.5%. A rough cut of the repeated description text suggests about 9.4k for `core`; not part of this PR.

**Not done yet**

- `--tools` CLI flag and config key (env var only).
- Instruction text still names `browser_*` tools when they are hidden (the profile line says what is off).
- CI check that every registered tool is in a group.

title: perf(cua-driver): wait for web focus instead of a fixed 800 ms (CUA-3763)
body:
Clicking a text field in a web page no longer waits a fixed 800 ms. It returns as soon as the page reports the field focused. Linear: CUA-3763. Supersedes #3490, which only lowered the fixed number; its mouse pacing knobs are kept here with the same defaults.

**What changed for users:** the click on a web text field in Safari or another WebKit view returns when focus has landed instead of after 800 ms. A page that never reports focus still waits the old 800 ms, so nothing gets slower.

**How it works**
- After an AX press on a text field inside an `AXWebArea`, the driver reads the field's `AXFocused` every 4 ms. It returns when two reads 8 ms apart agree, or at the cap.
- `CUA_DRIVER_WEBKIT_SETTLE_MS` is the hard cap (default 800, `0` skips the wait, max 5000). The fixed sleep on this path is gone.
- Mouse pacing: the `mouseMoved` primer settle, the click down/up gap and the multi-click gap now read `CUA_DRIVER_MOUSE_PRIMER_MS` (12), `CUA_DRIVER_CLICK_GAP_MS` (28) and `CUA_DRIVER_MULTI_CLICK_GAP_MS` (80). Defaults are unchanged, because a tight down/up gap can drop an NSButton click and there is no signal to wait on there. Values are clamped to 2 to 200 ms.
- All four are admitted into embedded and worker launches, and documented in EMBEDDING.md.
- The 40 to 100 ms foreground warp and settle sleeps are untouched.

**Numbers** (simulated page, real clock, median of 20 runs, test Mac under load; run `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib bench_webkit_settle -- --ignored --nocapture`)

| Focus lands after | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 10 ms | 800 ms | 40 ms |
| 30 ms | 800 ms | 75 ms |
| 100 ms | 800 ms | 130 ms |
| 300 ms | 800 ms | 344 ms |
| never | 800 ms | 823 ms (the cap) |

Roughly 8 ms of the "after" time is the stability read. #3490 measured 933 to 97 ms in Safari with the number lowered by hand. I could not repeat a live Safari run: the new build has no Accessibility grant on the test Mac.

**Tests:** `input_pacing` unit tests (env parsing and clamping, early exit, flapping signal, cap, zero cap) on a fake clock; allowlist test for the four names. `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver-sdk` pass. `platform-macos` lib: 694 passed, 1 failed (`browser::platform::tests::existing_discovery_requires_one_endpoint_but_reproof_keeps_exact_approval`, browser discovery, untouched by this change). `bin/ci --quick --fix` passes.

**Risk:** a page that reports `AXFocused` late or only on a parent costs up to the old 800 ms, never more. Set `CUA_DRIVER_WEBKIT_SETTLE_MS` lower to trade safety for speed.

title: feat(cua-driver): capture the KWin desktop through ScreenShot2 behind kwin-capture
body:
Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6451 by @astrovm. Their commits are kept unchanged under their own authorship. On top are one merge and three commits of ours. Linear: CUA-3711.

**Stacked on https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6820.** #6451 carries #6450's window-capture work, and #6820 is our salvage of #6450. This branch is #6820's head (`996968175c`) with #6451 merged in, so until #6820 merges, this diff also shows all of #6820. Merge #6820 first. After that, this PR's own change is the four files under `wayland/` and `docs/kwin-window-capture.md` listed below.

## Why

#6451 makes a KWin desktop screenshot call ScreenShot2 `CaptureWorkspace` before the Screenshot portal, so there is no consent dialog and no portal request to wait on. Review found two problems. First, ScreenShot2 never asks the portal, and the tier ran for every KWin session, so a screenshot Deny saved in the portal no longer stopped a desktop capture. Second, the new route had no automated coverage. Review also asked whether a multi-output workspace image shares a frame with window records and input.

## What changed

- The tier runs only when `kwin_access::allowed()` says yes. That is the `cua-driver kwin-capture` switch #6820 adds for window capture. It is off by default, `on` keeps a saved portal Deny in force, and only `on --override-portal-deny` bypasses that Deny. When the tier is off or KWin refuses, the cascade continues to wlroots, ext-image-copy and the portal as before.
- Frame: with `native-resolution` false, KWin captures `Workspace::geometry()`. That is the union of the outputs' logical rectangles at one pixel per logical pixel, the same bounding box `kwin_layout::frame_of` reads from xdg-output (main's #6821). `get_desktop_state` already rebases KWin window records and desktop input onto that frame. A new test pins the rebase on a layout with an output at negative coordinates, a 1x output, a 2x output and a 1.25x output.
- Tests for the route. The gate gets a unit test. `CaptureWorkspace` runs against a fake ScreenShot2 on a private `dbus-daemon`, which checks the requested options, the pixel decoding and the refusal of a non-raw reply. `capture_workspace` is split so the exchange can be tested without the trusted-compositor owner check. The docs say the tier follows the switch, and a broken `#permissions` link now points at the section that exists.

## Scope

Covers the KWin desktop-capture tier in `screenshot_display_dispatch`, plus its docs. It does not change window capture, the switch itself (#6820), or the GNOME, Hyprland, niri or wlroots tiers.

## Blast Radius

Only KWin sessions that turned `kwin-capture` on reach the new tier. Every other session gets exactly main's desktop cascade. With the switch on, desktop screenshots skip the portal dialog, and a saved portal Deny still keeps them on the portal path.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. Clippy with `-D warnings` is clean for `platform-linux` and `cua-driver` on aarch64 Linux (cross-built), and for `cua-driver` and `platform-macos` on macOS. The `platform-linux` lib tests ran on a Debian aarch64 host: 976 passed, 0 failed. Each new test failed under a matching mutation (gate dropped, `native-resolution` flipped, raw check dropped).
- Live, on nested KWin 6.3.6 with a single virtual output, the driver ran in five states: off, on, on with a saved portal Deny, `--override-portal-deny`, and off again. At this head KWin was asked only in the on and override states (3 of 3 runs pass). The binary from before this change asked KWin in all five states, Deny included (3 of 7 checks fail).
- Not run: this host's KWin has no OpenGL, so it exports no ScreenShot2 object and no live workspace image was captured. The multi-output, scaled and negative-origin frame is covered by the unit test and by reading KWin's source, not by a live capture. Also not run: `kwin_logical_frame_test` and `kwin_native_capture_test` (they need native KWin with GL), the verify-cua-driver X11 and Wayland lanes, and Windows. The macOS lane doesn't apply because no macOS code changed.

Size: the PR carries #6820 and the contributor's feature in full. Our own commits add about 45 production lines (the gate and the `workspace_image` split).

title: perf(cua-driver): batch type_text key events on Windows and Linux
body:
Brings the macOS `type_text` speedup from #6884 to Windows and Linux X11. `type_text` on those platforms now sends text in batches by default instead of pacing every character.

Refs CUA-3763.

**What changed**
- `delay_ms` now defaults to 0. A positive value keeps one paced key per character.
- Shared contract in `cua-driver-core::type_pacing`: the default, the 0-200 clamp, a chunk planner (batches of up to 16 UTF-16 units, a surrogate pair is never split, Return and Tab stay real key presses) and the 30 ms tail pace.
- Windows, background (`WM_CHAR`): posts a batch, waits for the target to pump, then lets it drain (2 ms per unit). Tab is now a real key press like Return. The existing read-back retypes a dropped tail, now paced at 30 ms.
- Windows, foreground (`SendInput`, `KEYEVENTF_UNICODE`): one `SendInput` per batch with a single drain sentinel, still confirmed as read before the next batch. A positive `delay_ms` now also applies here. UIA ValuePattern (with `element_token`) is unchanged: it is atomic, so `delay_ms` does not apply.
- Linux X11 (XTest and XSendEvent): no per-key pause, and a server round trip every 16 keys. The virtual-keyboard (uinput) route drops its per-step pause and still confirms the last key. `type_text` accepts `delay_ms`.
- Linux Wayland routes (wtype, libei, KWin, Hyprland, niri) already send a whole string or are acknowledgement-paced, so they are unchanged, except that a positive `delay_ms` now sends one character per call.
- Secure fields and IME paths are unchanged: no new routes, only the pacing of existing ones.

**Numbers** (GitHub-hosted runners, 78 characters, p50 of 9 runs; the same bench file runs before and after)

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Windows `WM_CHAR` into an EDIT control (before = `delay_ms` 30, the old default) | 2683 ms | 163 ms |
| Linux X11 XTest (Xvfb) | 789 ms | 0.9 ms |
| Linux X11 XSendEvent (Xvfb) | 790 ms | 1.1 ms |

Linux numbers measure delivery into the X server; they do not include how fast a real toolkit reads the keys. The Windows run confirmed all 78 characters landed in order.

**Tests**
- Core planner: limits, surrogate pairs, keys as their own chunks, full coverage (7 tests, pass).
- Windows: unit tests for Tab, batches and key events pass on a Windows runner; the cross-compiled `cargo xwin` check and clippy are clean. New ignored desktop tests: `bench_post_type_text` (the numbers above) and a Tab-between-batches test.
- Linux: `TypePacing` unit tests pass. New X11 tests: batches deliver every key in order, `delay_ms` paces each key, XSendEvent batches. `text_delivers_distinct_unmapped_keysyms_on_both_paths` now runs paced, because it reads each borrowed keycode's keysym while the key is still borrowed.
- Benchmarks: `platform-linux/tests/type_text_bench_x11.rs`, and `bench_post_type_text` in `platform-windows/src/input/keyboard.rs`.

**Still running, not in this PR:** one more Linux X11 run of the full `key_input_x11` file on this exact head. Its output lands in the log of the latest run on branch `tmp/type-text-bench-3763` (`gh run list --repo trycua/cua --branch tmp/type-text-bench-3763`, job `linux (after)`, step `Detail`). That branch gets deleted once it is read.

**Risks**
- A Windows target slower than 2 ms per character can still hold queued characters after the call returns. The read-back retype only repairs a proven prefix and does not duplicate text, but a target that stalls mid-drain could be mis-read. The uinput and XSendEvent routes have no read-back, so a client that drops fast keys is not repaired.
- Tab on Windows is now a real key press: in a dialog it moves focus instead of inserting a tab.
- The generated tool reference for `delay_ms` changed and may need regenerating in CI.
- Not run: the Linux uinput and Wayland routes (no test host), and the Windows foreground `SendInput` path (needs an interactive desktop).

title: feat(cua-driver): expose macOS search field identity attributes
body:
Salvage of https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6857 by @lidge-jun, whose commit is kept unchanged with its authorship. Linear: CUA-3754.

## Why

macOS `get_window_state` elements expose only a merged `label` and `value`. A search field named only by `AXPlaceholderValue` therefore looks the same as a composer whose typed text happens to read like a search hint. #6857 adds raw `title`, `description`, `placeholder` and `subrole` keys. Review found that its `AXSubrole` read, plus an `AXPlaceholderValue` read even when `AXValue` is set, ran for every visited node. That includes display-only rows the public `elements` array never shows. Each is a synchronous AX request that spends the walk's time budget. Since #6878, main reads each node in one batched `AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues` call. `AXSubrole` now joins that batch, and the gate still applies on the per-attribute fallback path used by apps that refuse the batch.

## What changed

- `AXNode` gains `placeholder` and `subrole`, and `element_entry` emits trimmed `title`, `description`, `placeholder` and `subrole` (the #6857 commit).
- `NodeAttr::Subrole` joins the batched node read in `ax/batch.rs`. `read_identity_attrs` in `ax/tree.rs` gates which identity values each node keeps and, on the fallback path, which ones it requests. Indexed nodes read both. Display-only nodes read `AXPlaceholderValue` only as the empty-`AXValue` fallback that main already uses, and never read `AXSubrole`.
- Unit tests check which attributes each kind of node reads, alongside the #6857 schema-conformance and identity tests.

## Scope

Only the macOS walker and `get_window_state` element entries. The label and value fallbacks behave as on main, and no AX request is added for a node that main skipped. Production lines are about +60/-10, within the size limit.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS `get_window_state` and `verify_state` element gains up to four optional keys, which pass the advertised output schema (`search_field_identities_survive_protocol_conformance`). Display-only rows in `verify_state`'s observation array carry `placeholder` only when it is also their value, and never carry `subrole`.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `platform-macos` all pass.
- The macOS Lume full matrix from the verify-cua-driver skill ran at fb68c90e. All cells passed, and the worker was stopped by hand after the wrapper's own stop step failed.
- Instrumented walks of a synthetic AppKit window that is mostly static labels with a few search fields. Before main's batching, #6857 alone read `AXSubrole` and `AXPlaceholderValue` on every node, and with the gate both were read only on the indexed fields. After merging main, the batch answers every node and the walk makes no single-attribute identity reads.

title: microVMs on Windows: QEMU on the Windows Hypervisor Platform, with checkpoints, forks and warm pools
body:
## What

microVM Spaces on Windows: QEMU on the Windows Hypervisor Platform (hardware acceleration only, never TCG), managed like the macOS runtime.

- WHPX detected without elevation (`WHvGetCapability`); one UAC prompt runs `dism /enable-feature HypervisorPlatform` when missing; QEMU installed with winget; pinned kernel; static guest init shipped with the app (TCP link with a per-VM key, since Windows QEMU has no vsock).
- Doctor and New Space say what is missing; the MicroVM option is enabled on Windows hosts; disk-space guard.
- Lifecycle: create, exec, stop (ACPI power-off), start, delete, pause/resume (QMP over an AF_UNIX socket).
- Checkpoint, fork and warm pool, disk-only: WHPX blocks QEMU migration, so no memory snapshots. Scratch disk is a qcow2 over a shared read-only template; a pool member is booted and paused and claimed by hard links.
- Network: QEMU user networking enforces no rules, so a Windows microVM is `NoNetworkOnly` (no network unless the user picks No protection).

## Benchmarks (same harness as cua.ai/compare, `libs/cua/bench/microvm-fork-windows`)

| Row | Mac p50 | Windows p50 |
|---|---|---|
| checkpoint | 650 ms | 308 ms |
| restore | 610 ms | 3970 ms |
| fork of running | 1160 ms | 4052 ms |
| fan-out (4) | 1460 ms | 5202 ms |
| create from warm pool | - | 360 ms |
| memory per fork | 1620 MiB | 684 MiB |

Restore, fork and fan-out stay slower because WHPX cannot save VM memory; details and iteration log in `RESULTS.md`.

## Verification
