title: fix(cua-driver): call Text Input Sources only with the thread affinity macOS requires (CUA-3763)
body:
Linear: CUA-3763. Replaces #6930.

## What changed for users
On macOS 26.5 and later, a `press_key` or `hotkey` call could crash Cua Driver's background service. Key presses now read the keyboard layout the way macOS requires, so the service stays up, and shortcuts still follow the user's keyboard layout (AZERTY, Russian and so on).

## Root cause
Since #6659 (layout-aware shortcut keys, in 0.41.3 through 0.43.2), `press_key` and `hotkey` read the layout with `TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource` / `TISGetInputSourceProperty` / `UCKeyTranslate` on a tokio blocking thread. HIToolbox's own rule (from its abort message): a UI application must call TIS/TSM on the main thread; a non-UI process must not call it from two threads at once. The daemon is a UI process: its main thread runs AppKit for the cursor overlay.

- **macOS 26.5.2:** every daemon crash report from the overnight Bench (8 of 8 with a TIS frame) is `EXC_BREAKPOINT`/SIGTRAP in `_dispatch_assert_queue_fail` < `islGetInputSourceListWithAdditions` < `isValidateInputSourceRef` < `TSMGetInputSourceProperty` < `keyboard::target_layout` < `press_key` / `press_key_bare_global` on a tokio blocking thread. HIToolbox asserts the main queue whenever it has to rebuild its input-source list off the main thread: first use on a worker, after an input-source change, or overlapping AppKit's own TSM work.
- **macOS 26.4 and 26.6.2:** the same call aborts (SIGABRT, "Text Input Sources or Text Services Manager API is being called in two threads concurrently") when an off-main call overlaps TSM work on another thread.
- **The trigger:** a daemon started as a plain child process (by an MCP client, a shell or the Bench harness) traps on its very first `press_key`/`hotkey`. A daemon opened through LaunchServices does not, which is why a quick CLI test against the installed app survived.

`press_key`, `hotkey` and every chord path go through `target_layout`; `type_text` sends Unicode payloads and makes no TIS call. There are no other TIS/HIToolbox/`UCKeyTranslate` callers in the repo.

## Fix
- New `platform_macos::input::input_source` is the one way to call TIS:
  - In a UI process, the work runs on the main dispatch queue and the caller waits. A process is a UI process once the cursor overlay, PiP or permission panel declares it (`main_thread_runs_event_loop()`, called before `NSApplication` starts and under the same lock workers use, so AppKit's TSM setup can't overlap an in-flight call), or once `NSApp` exists (an embedding app).
  - In a non-UI process (CLI, tests, a daemon without overlay), the work runs inline under one process-wide lock.
  - A main queue that isn't serviced costs one caller a 1 s wait. Later callers get the US key positions at once until the queued read runs.
- The layout is cached and re-read only after `kTISNotifySelectedKeyboardInputSourceChanged` / `kTISNotifyEnabledKeyboardInputSourcesChanged`, which are observed on the main run loop. So the hot path makes no TIS call at all, and a layout switch takes effect on the next chord.
- `examples/tis_stress.rs`: in-process stress (AppKit main loop, N worker threads, optional input-source switches). `--raw` reproduces the old unmarshalled call.
- `scripts/stress-press-key-tis.sh`: daemon stress over the CLI (concurrent `press_key` + `hotkey`, optional layout switches), and it reports whether the daemon survived.

## Verification
Builds: before = main at 85d75c1689 (same keyboard code as 0.43.2), after = this branch. Both are release builds, run as bundled apps in macOS VMs.

**Daemon, macOS 26.5.2** (`scripts/stress-press-key-tis.sh`, daemon launched as a plain child process the way MCP clients and the Bench start it, 8 concurrent CLI clients alternating `press_key cmd+a` and `hotkey ctrl+e`, background delivery):

| build | run | calls | ok | daemon |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | plain | 500 | 0 | SIGTRAP (`Trace/BPT trap: 5`) on the first call |
| before | + layout switches every 250 ms | 500 | 0 | SIGTRAP on the first call |
| after | plain | 500 | 500 | alive |
| after | + layout switches every 250 ms (3,193 switches, ABC <-> French) | 500 | 500 | alive |

The trigger is the launch, not the load. The same before-build daemon traps on its first `press_key` whenever it is a direct child of a shell, with a full or empty environment and with the real or an empty HOME (4/4). The same build opened through LaunchServices survived 500/500 calls with 3,087 layout switches: macOS registers it as an app, so HIToolbox doesn't rebuild its list off the main thread. That's why a single `cmd+a` from the CLI against an app-launched daemon didn't crash.

**In-process, `examples/tis_stress` (AppKit main loop, 8 threads x 500 lookups):**
- macOS 26.5.2: old direct call (`--raw`) aborted in 2 of 4 runs; fixed path 0 of 5 (with and without layout switches, and in a non-UI process).
- macOS 26.6.2: `--raw` aborted 3 of 3 (SIGABRT, "TIS/TSM API ... called in two threads concurrently"); fixed path 0 of 3; non-UI 0 of 1.

**macOS 26.4:** the daemon survived 500/500 calls with layout switches on both builds. 26.4 only aborts on overlapping calls, and a small C probe did reproduce that abort.

## Tests
- `input_source` unit tests: in a non-UI process, 8 workers x 50 calls run inline and never overlap; nothing is cached without change notifications. Existing keyboard tests pass (90 passed).
- The UI-process path needs a GUI session, so it's covered by the stress example and script above, not by `cargo test`.

title: fix(cua-driver): clear portal-input clippy lints in platform-linux
body:
## Why
CI's Linux clippy step runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` with default features only. The `portal-input` code in platform-linux is never linted there, and it fails `-D warnings` on main with six Rust 1.97 lints. CUA-3251 filed the default-feature lints, and #6658 and #6695 already cleared those.

## What changed
- `wayland/libei.rs`: moved the handshake-version and Xkb keymap checks into their match patterns (`collapsible_match`) and replaced `max(1).min(500)` with `clamp(1, 500)` (`manual_clamp`).
- `wayland/mod.rs`: removed the `return` before the trailing expression in the `portal-input` cfg blocks of `libei_recovery` and `chord_into` (`needless_return`).

## Scope
Lint fixes only, with no behaviour change. Unmatched events still fall through to `_ => {}`, and every return value is unchanged. The PR does not add `portal-input` to CI clippy, and it does not touch `portal-capture`/`portal-libei` lints, which could not be built here.

## Blast Radius
The code is only built with `portal-input` (GNOME/KDE libei input). The edits are mechanical rewrites with the same semantics.

## Verification
- Cross-target `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- -D warnings` passes with default features and with `--features portal-input`. Before this change, the `portal-input` run failed with these six lints.
- `cargo fmt -p platform-linux --check` passes.
- Linux tests, the X11/Wayland verify lanes, and `portal-capture`/`portal-libei` clippy did not run (no Linux host or libspa headers).

CUA-3251

title: GPU in containers on a Windows PC (NVIDIA through WSL 2) and the gap audit for the GPU pool
body:
## What

Containers on a Windows PC get the NVIDIA GPU through WSL 2: the built-in runtime's distribution has `/dev/dxg` and the driver libraries in `/usr/lib/wsl`, and had no `nvidia` runtime, so `--gpu nvidia` answered "Containers here run in a Linux VM with no GPU access".

- `cua spaces gpus` offers `nvidia (NVIDIA GPUs (WSL 2))` for runc containers when the PC has an NVIDIA driver and the engine is a WSL 2 kernel with no `nvidia` runtime; gVisor still gets none.
- A GPU container is created with `/dev/dxg`, `/usr/lib/wsl` read-only and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`/`PATH` for it, in place of the nvidia device request.
- `managed_wsl::provision` refuses when the distribution is already registered. Before, a failed `wsl --import` ("install location already in use") deleted the disk of the runtime in use.
- `docs/rfcs/6900-gpu-supercomputer-gap-audit.md`: the ranked gap list for "many computers as one AI supercomputer" (this fixes G4).

## Verified on this PC

`cua sb create ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04-slim --gpu nvidia --kind container` then `nvidia-smi` in the Space prints `NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, 97887 MiB`. Unit tests for the option and the container body; clippy `-D warnings`.

title: fix(cluster): GPU jobs are admitted by free video memory and run on Windows hosts
body:
Fix, not a feature: the supercomputer skill that is on main already tells agents to write `@app.function(gpu="nvidia", gpu_memory="16GB", ...)` and says the pool "places the job where it fits and queues it while the GPU is full". Neither is true on main. Evidence below was produced without any NVIDIA run (a fake inventory and the unit tests; the PC's GPU was not used).

## What fails on main

**1. The documented decorator does not work.** Running the skill's own example against main's `cua` shim:

```
App().function(gpu="nvidia", gpu_memory="16GB")  ->  TypeError: App.function() got an unexpected keyword argument 'gpu'
App().function(on="local")                      ->  ValueError: on must be 'auto', 'aws' or 'host:NAME', got 'local'
```

The skill documents `gpu=`, `gpu_memory=`, models (`"L4"`, `"H100"`), `"any"` and `on="local"`; the shim only knows `accelerator=` with `gpu|apple|nvidia`.

**2. A GPU with no video memory free still takes every GPU job (over-commit).** On main the scheduler matches an accelerator by vendor word only (`accelerator_fits`), the host reports no free video memory, and a job cannot ask for any. A test on main (`Candidate::misfit`) with a host whose only GPU reports `nvidia:L4:24 GB:0 GB free`: four jobs asking for `nvidia` are all admitted (`misfit` is `None` each time), and `normalize_accelerator("nvidia:16GB")` is an error, so a request for memory cannot even be written. Two or more jobs that each need most of the card therefore land on one GPU and fail with out-of-memory.

**3. Windows computers cannot be placed on sensibly.** On Windows `total_memory_mb()` and `available_memory_mb()` return `None` (main only implements Linux and macOS), so `this_machine_status` reports the 4096 MiB fallback for a 96 GB machine and a GPU job that needs more memory than that is refused there. A test on main run on a Windows 11 host fails: `total memory unknown: the host reports the 4096 MiB fallback`.

## What this PR does

- Accepts `gpu=`, `gpu_memory=` (and `on="local"`) in the decorator and resolves them to the pool's accelerator word (`nvidia:L4:24GB`), exactly the forms the skill documents.
- Reports free video memory per NVIDIA GPU in the host inventory (`nvidia-smi`, at most every 5 s), subtracts what accepted jobs have asked for and not yet allocated, and admits by free memory at both ends: the scheduler (counting what it already sent since the last report, also in batch planning) and the host (refuses when the card is full, whatever the scheduler thought).
- Reports memory on Windows (`GlobalMemoryStatusEx`).

Before / after (same tests): the host above refuses the second 16 GB job on a 24 GB card and the first when it has 0 GB free; a GPU with room is chosen over a busy one; a Windows host reports its real memory.

## Dropped to keep this a fix

- `cua run --accelerator nvidia:16GB` (model and memory on the CLI flag): not documented by the skill, so it is not in this PR; the decorator path carries the request.

Kept although it looks like surface: model matching (`"L4"`, `"H100"`) and `"any"`, because the skill on main documents them; without them the skill would still be wrong.

## Tests

`cua-cluster` unit tests for parsing, admission, reservation and batch pending memory; the Python shim tests for `gpu=`/`gpu_memory=`. No test needs an NVIDIA GPU.

title: feat(spaces): a Space uses the pool, its runs are its children and are cleaned up with it
body:
## What

A Space's agent can use the pool (`cua run`, `cua jobs`, `cua computers`) and what it submits is its own tree's, never an orphan.

- **Pool from inside a Space.** The scoped channel answered `deny()` to `pool_request`. It now allows `status`, `pool`, `submit`, `runs`, `run`, `jobs`, `job`, `job_output`, `run_result`, `cancel_run`, `cancel_job`: a Space sees and cancels only its tree's runs (another tree's run is "not found", as another tree's Space is).
- **Runs are children.** Each submit is recorded under the Space and its tree root (`<home>/spawn/runs.json`, `children/runs.rs`). The daemon's reaper cancels the runs of a Space that is deleted or stopped, within seconds, and forgets them; the pool's own host-death, lost-lease and fencing handling stays as is.
- **`cua` in a Space finds its channel.** `ensure_daemon` ignored the spawn channel and started a daemon of its own in the Space ("this cua daemon does not have them").
- **A Space's own window.** `stream_space_window`, `show_space_pip`, `hide_space_pip` and `open_space_viewer` are allowed for the caller itself and its children, so the agent can put a window on the person's screen.
- **Teaching.** `libs/cua/skills/cua-pool/SKILL.md` and one line in the Home brief.

## Verified (isolated CUA_HOME, real Space)

Inside a child-capable container Space: `cua computers` shows this PC's `nvidia:RTX PRO 6000 ... 96 GB`; `cua run --on local --accelerator nvidia -- ...` is accepted and recorded under the Space; `cua sb rm` of the Space cancels the run (daemon log: "canceled a run whose Space is gone") and empties the ledger. Unit tests for the ledger; clippy `-D warnings`; the web brief test.

title: fix(cua-driver): cover foreground activation enabling a macOS AppKit control
body:
CUA-3648, follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6702.

#6702 skips the early `AXEnabled` read when a foreground call targets a background macOS app, and reads it again after activation. Until now only the refusal side had an E2E cell. The AppKit harness had no control that activation enables, so the success side was covered by code alone.

## Change

- AppKit harness, `disabled_control` scenario: adds a button (`btn-active-only`) and a text field (`txt-active-only`) that are enabled only while the app is active. They report `active_only=click|double_click|text:<value>`. An `activations=` label counts the app's activations. The controls are created lazily, so ordinary harness launches stay unchanged.
- The refusal-only cell becomes `harness_appkit_foreground_from_the_background_rereads_enablement_after_activation` (`macos-appkit-activation-enablement-ax-foreground`). Each row puts the harness behind another app, checks that the target reads `enabled: false`, then sends a foreground call:
  - `click`, `double_click` and `type_text` on the active-only controls succeed, and the fixture records each one.
  - `double_click`, middle `click` and `type_text` on the always-disabled checkbox are refused as `element_disabled`, and the activation count rises. A refusal made before activation would fail.
- `scenarios.json` documents the new controls. The macOS runner list carries the renamed cell.

A first version created the controls eagerly on every launch. That made `macos-appkit-invoke-menu-ax-foreground` invoke its background-disabled menu item instead of refusing it. The cell had passed at the base and in about 40 earlier runs. Running these tests with the base fixture made it pass again. With lazy creation the full matrix passes. The exact AppKit mechanism is not proven.

## Proof

The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-e2e --tests -- -D warnings`, a `swiftc` compile of the AppKit fixture, and a JSON parse of `scenarios.json`. I ran the full macOS Lume guest matrix at the head through the verify-cua-driver skill: 179 delivered, 5 refused, 0 failed. The new cell's transcript shows three successful foreground calls and three `element_disabled` refusals, and the activation count rises at every call.

Not run: Linux and Windows lanes (this changes only the macOS fixture and macOS cells), standalone browsers, and the SIP-on permission flow.

title: fix(cua-driver): skip a background invoke_menu press after its call is cancelled
body:
CUA-3310
CUA-3805

## Why

On macOS, `invoke_menu` with the app in the background presses the menu item on a `spawn_blocking` worker. That worker keeps running after the caller's future is dropped (a cancelled call, a dropped MCP request, an outer timeout). With nothing checking cancellation, it could still press the item, after up to 600 ms of enablement polling, for a call that had already ended. The Linux input path guards the same case with `Action::admit` and `abandon_on_drop`. The macOS background menu route had no such check.

## What changed

- `run_admitted` runs the background worker with a `PressAdmission` flag. A guard held across the await sets the flag when the waiting future is dropped.
- `invoke_path_in_background` skips the SkyLight enablement priming once the call is cancelled, and runs the final `perform_action` only through `admission.admit`, which refuses after cancellation.
- Tests: `a_dropped_background_call_never_presses_its_item` aborts a task awaiting `run_admitted` while its worker is parked, then releases the worker and asserts it did not press. `a_live_background_call_presses_once` covers the live call and the refusal text.

## Scope

Only the background route in `platform-macos/src/tools/invoke_menu.rs`. The background `hotkey` key-equivalent route calls the same `run_in_background`, so it gets the check too. The foreground `invoke_menu` path and other tools are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

A press already sent cannot be recalled. The check runs right before `perform_action`, so a cancel that arrives between that check and the end of the call can still land. Holding a lock across the press would close that window, but then dropping a cancelled call would block a Tokio worker for up to the 2 s AX messaging timeout. Linux's `admit` can hold its lock because its `send` never blocks, and an AX press can.

## Blast Radius

Live calls behave as before: the flag is only set when the waiting future is dropped, and then nothing reads the result. If a cancelled call reaches the press, it now returns a refusal that nobody receives.

## Verification

- The new drop test fails when the guard is removed from `run_admitted`, and also when `admit` ignores the flag. It passes with the fix.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` all pass.
- verify-cua-driver macOS Lume full matrix at this head: 183 of 184 cells passed, including both `invoke_menu` AppKit cells. The one failed cell, and a `bring_to_front` lane failure, are unrelated to this diff; details are in the verification comment.

Size: about 50 production lines added, within the size limit.

title: A Windows computer can be a pool host (daemon reached on loopback)
body:
## What

`cua host setup --share spaces` worked on a Windows PC, but the PC was never a pool host: its cua-spacesd forwards `HostSpacesService`, `HostJobsService` and `HostSnapshotsService` to the host's cua daemon over a **Unix socket**, and on Windows answered "providing Spaces from a Windows host is not supported yet". - The channel type becomes `InterceptedService<Channel, DaemonAuth>` for the three clients.

title: fix(cua-driver): make an unconfirmed pixel click readable (CUA-3763, numbers pending)
body:
Linear: CUA-3763 (hill-climb round 2). Numbers pending.

**Loss.** Bench task CDB-G03 (reconcile payments in GnuCash, Calc and a mail app) went 0/3 before round 1 and 0/3 after, every trial at the 45-turn cap.

**Cause (from the 3 round-1 transcripts and the GnuCash transaction logs).** The GnuCash register draws its own cells, so a pixel click returns `effect: unverifiable` and there is nothing to read back. Two driver behaviours made that expensive:
- The unverifiable-click hint pointed at `get_window_state`, which shows no cell state for that surface. Agents could not tell whether the click worked.
- `zoom` shrinks any region wider than 500 px. The agents zoomed an 800 px wide register strip, so the one-letter reconcile flag became unreadable.
- Result: repeated clicks. The log shows the reconcile flag going n to c to n (a repeat click toggles it back), the checking splits never reached `y`, and the turn budget ran out.

**Fix.**
- An unverifiable coordinate click now returns `next_call` = `zoom` on the clicked spot, with text that says not to click again.
- `zoom` enlarges a narrow crop up to 4x and says when it had to shrink a wide region, and how to fix it.
- Tests: recovery hint (new and updated), crop scaling and coordinate mapping.

Numbers pending: G03 x 3 foreground on a macOS 26.5.2 VM with this build, results to follow. Auto-merge only after a pass-rate gain.

title: fix(cua-driver): explain why background hover and drag-and-drop cannot work, and how to read a tooltip (CUA-3763)
body:
Draft. Linear: CUA-3763 (overnight Cua Driver hill-climb, round 3).

**The loss.** In the background condition, bench tasks MB-09 (reorder a native list by drag and drop), MB-10 (hover-only toolbar) and MB-11 (native tooltip) pass 1 of 6, against 6 of 6 in the foreground.

**What each needs, and what a VM check found** (macOS 26.5.2, BenchLab, Sonnet 5.5, same seeds as the overnight headfix runs):
- MB-09, `NSTableView` row drag. The drag starts a drag-and-drop session. With the drag kept going to the end of its path the drop fired, on the row where the drag started: the session follows the real pointer, not posted events. No background route.
- MB-10, `NSTrackingArea` toolbar. Posting stamped `mouseMoved` events to the pid, window made AppKit-key without a raise, 1.2 s dwell: the toolbar did not appear. No background route.
- MB-11, rect-based `NSView` tooltip. Same experiment: no tooltip. With the real pointer a tooltip does appear for an app that is not active, as a small window of the app; its screenshot is the text and its accessibility tree is empty.

**Numbers (experiment build, 2 runs of each task in the background).** The pass count looks like 3/6 (MB-10 1/2, MB-11 2/2, MB-09 0/2), but every pass moved the real pointer (agent fell back to a desktop hover: pointer deviation 375 to 850 px, human-input flag set). Counted as the benchmark counts background, that is 0/6, and MB-09 and one MB-10 trial ended BLOCKED or failed. No change in the background pass rate; the honest answer for these three is a clear refusal, not a route.

**Change (this PR, after reverting the experiment)**
- The background-hover note now says what was tested, names the accessibility route first, and tells the agent to stop and report when only the user's pointer works.
- The note after a desktop hover no longer claims tooltips need the active app, and names the route to read the tooltip window (`list_windows`, then `get_window_state` on its window id).
- MACOS.md records both findings. No behaviour change to any tool.

Plain words: when an agent cannot hover or drag over a background Mac app without touching the user's mouse, Cua Driver now says exactly why and what to do instead, and no longer misdescribes how tooltips work.

title: ci: preview:windows and preview:linux labels build installable Cua Spaces from a PR
body:
Adds `preview:windows` and `preview:linux`, next to `preview:mac` from #6915. A maintainer adds the label to a branch PR; CI builds an installable Cua Spaces for that system from the PR head and posts one sticky comment with the download links. For people trying a PR, this means they can install a Windows or Linux build without building it themselves.

**Stacked on #6915.** The base is `ci/preview-mac-label`, so the diff shows only this change. Retarget to `main` once #6915 merges.

**Factoring.** Two new self-contained workflows beside the mac one, not one shared `preview-build.yml`. A reusable file would mean editing the mac workflow inside an unmerged PR, and the three builds share only the comment step (about 60 lines). Trigger, concurrency group and the same-repo guard live per workflow anyway, since `concurrency` and `if` cannot be inherited from a called workflow.

Same as #6915: `labeled`, plus `synchronize` while the label is on; one concurrency group per PR with cancel-in-progress; never runs for fork PRs; `contents: read` for the builds and `pull-requests: write` only in the two comment jobs, which check out nothing; no signing secrets or environment; corepack pnpm; 14-day artifacts; `ci-gate` ignores them (its ignore pattern is now `ci-cua-spaces-preview-`, test updated).

Beyond #6915: the result job also has `actions: read`, to list this run's artifacts and link each architecture directly. The comment says "partly built" if one architecture fails.

What each builds, from `cd-cua-spaces-build.yml` without the signing:
- The web UI and the native layer build in parallel. The binding check (`pnpm native -- --skip-build --check-bindings`) needs the compiled library, so it runs on the x64 native layer right before packaging. The native layer uses `.github/actions/spaces-native`, the release's cache key, so a tree main already built is restored.
- **Windows** (x64 on `windows-latest`, arm64 native on `windows-11-arm`): the "Cua Spaces Local" config that `install-local.ps1` uses, as a zipped portable folder. It runs beside a released Cua Spaces (own app id, executable, URL scheme, no update feed). It shows "Local · Staging" (the Local channel default deployment; no preview points at production). Unsigned, so SmartScreen shows More info, then Run anyway. There is no installer: the repo has no side-by-side NSIS variant.
- **Linux** (x64 and arm64): the release config's AppImage and deb. There is no side-by-side Linux variant, so the deb replaces an installed Cua Spaces and uses production unless started with `CUA_ENV=staging`; the comment says so.

Times, from the release build's job timings: about 10 minutes with the native layer cached, up to about 60 minutes (Linux) or 100 (Windows) when a change under `libs/cua` forces a cold compile.

Also: labels `preview:windows` and `preview:linux` created; documented next to `preview:mac` in `docs/contributing/CI.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`. `bin/ci --quick --fix` passes and actionlint is clean.

title: fix(cua-driver-bench): resume a killed run with the same command
body:
## Why

A stopped bench run could not be resumed safely (CUA-3793). The resume of the interrupted CUA-3543 foreground run failed for two reasons. Its session command reruns `make_linux_pins.py`, which refused to overwrite its own identical `pins.json`. Then the evidence check called the attempt directory cut off by the VM loss an orphan. Other gaps showed up while testing. A resumed retry restarted at `a1` and recorded the same attempt twice with a fresh retry budget. A row cut off mid-write was glued to the next row. Two runners could share one run directory. A resume with different flags mixed two setups under one run id.

The fix makes start and resume the same command. `results.jsonl` stays the run's only state, and there is no supervisor, state file or new flag.

## What changed

- **Resume.** `execute_trial` continues after a trial's recorded attempts and keeps their retry budgets. Rows are fsynced, and a torn last row is dropped at the next start. `run.lock` (flock) makes `run`, `finalize` and `preflight` single-owner. Video compression publishes `video.json` before it deletes the raw file, a resume requeues unfinished videos, and `DONE` waits for them.
- **Refusal.** A start exits 6 before it writes into the run directory when it would change what a recorded trial measures. Each row records that: its schedule slot and setup (`trial_identity`), the measured options in the recorded argv, the Cua Driver binary and skills hashes, and `bench_src_sha256`. Growing the schedule (adding phase 2) is still a resume.
- **Linux session.** `make_linux_pins.py` is a no-op for identical pins and still refuses different ones. `check_run_evidence.py` accepts what a stopped run leaves for its resume (one in-flight attempt, a torn last row, pending compression) and stays strict once the run is `DONE`. With both changes, the whole `linux_session.sh` command in the README can be rerun as is. A directory with none of `run.lock`, `results.jsonl` or `manifest.json` is not a run and fails the check, so an empty directory still exits 1.

## Scope

Covers `libs/cua-driver-bench/automated-eval/macos_bench`: the runner, the pins writer, the evidence checker, tests, `RUNNER.md` and `README.md`. Agent processes orphaned after a runner SIGKILL on macOS are not covered. On Linux the session's PID namespace already ends them. No auto-restart was added. After a crash, a person or the calling job reruns the command once.

## Tradeoffs

- No supervisor or respawn loop. On 6 Nov the bench VM was killed from the host, and a respawning supervisor inside the VM could not have helped. A supervisor would add a second state machine next to `results.jsonl`.
- Resume refusal reads the identity the rows already record, rather than a separate checkpoint file, so there is one source of truth.
- Size: production code adds about 295 lines against an aim of 200. The cases the cold verification found (schedule, options, driver build, video) each needed their own check.

## Blast radius

Bench operators only. A run recorded by main resumes on this branch. A copy of the paused CUA-3543 foreground run gives no conflicts with its original command, and its rows' driver and skills hashes match the files on disk. New exit codes: 5 (run locked) and 6 (setup changed), plus the stop flag `STOPPED_COMPRESS`.

## Verification

- `tests/test_resume.py` runs the real `run_bench.py run` in a child process with the GUI, daemon and model stubbed (`tests/fake_runner.py`). It SIGKILLs the run mid-attempt, halfway through a row, during a retry, and from outside at five fixed delays. It also sends SIGTERM, starts a second runner on a live run, runs preflight on a live run, resumes with each of several setup changes, and resumes a smoke run. Each resume ends with every scheduled trial final exactly once and every earlier row kept. On main the same tests fail: duplicate attempt rows, `a1` rerun instead of `a2`, the orphan report, the pins refusal, no lock, and no refusal on a changed setup.
- The scoped repository checks pass: the harness, checker and sentinel pytest suites, `tools/taskset.py check`, the fairness unittests, ruff check and format, and the SPDX check.
- Linux and Windows desktop contract tests could not run on this macOS host. CI runs them.

title: fix(cua-driver): recommend foreground for unverifiable background keys to Chromium and Electron apps
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a background `hotkey` or `press_key` sent to a Chrome-family browser or an Electron app (Slack, for example) is often dropped by the renderer. The result is a bare `effect: "unverifiable"`, the same as for a key that landed, so the caller gets no hint to retry in the foreground. In the Slack case on #4997, a background cmd+k did nothing and the next `type_text` went to the field that still had focus.
- What changed: when a background `hotkey` or `press_key` to a Chromium or Electron app ends `unverifiable`, the structured result now carries `escalation: { recommended: "foreground", reason, requires: ["window_id"] }`, the shape the Screen Sharing refusals already use, and the text result gets one sentence saying the same. `press_key` also sets the escalation on its action record, so its public `ActionResult` carries `escalation.target: "foreground"`. Foreground calls, confirmed results and other apps are unchanged.

The target check is a new `type_text::is_chromium_embedder(pid)`: the existing `is_chromium_identity` bundle check, or `ElectronJs::is_electron`. It replaces an identical private helper in `set_value.rs`, and it runs only after a background key was posted and the result is unverifiable.

## Related work

Refs #4997
Refs #5355 (WKWebView targets are not covered here)

RFC: not needed. The change adds an existing optional field to more results and leaves the contract as it is. #4009 deferred a producer-observed `escalation.reason`, so the projected reason stays `delivery_failed`, as for every `foreground` escalation today.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Background key results for Chromium and Electron apps gain an `escalation` and one sentence of text. A caller that ignores `escalation` sees no change. Linux already refuses background keys to Chromium embedders; Windows is unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: the hint also appears on a key that did land, because nothing can tell the two apart. The text says the key "may not have arrived" and asks the caller to check the window before retrying. Reverting the commit rolls it back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: tests in `hotkey.rs` and `press_key.rs` assert the whole structured payload for each branch (background to a Chromium app, background to another app, foreground to a Chromium app, confirmed), and that `press_key`'s public `ActionResult` gets `escalation.target: foreground` only in the first. With the helper stubbed to return no escalation, the two Chromium tests failed and the other 14 passed. With the fix, `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` passes (722 passed, 11 ignored, after rebasing on current main). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. I did not send real keys to a desktop app for this change. The target check reuses the helpers `set_value` and the menu-equivalent route already rely on.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the `hotkey` description still says Chromium and Electron accept background combos "as trusted live input", which #4997 points out. Changing it regenerates the MCP reference docs, so I left it for a follow-up unless you want it here. I ran the crate's fmt, clippy and tests rather than `bin/ci`, and without write access I cannot run `bin/ci --signoff`.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`)

title: fix(cua-driver): keep Linux action abandonment in one ActionPhase
body:
## Why

`Action` kept one fact in two mutexes. `admit` read `abandoned: Mutex<bool>` while `is_abandoned` and `fence` read the flag inside `fenced: Mutex<(bool, Vec<OwnedFd>)>`. `abandon` set the second flag before the first, so for a moment `is_abandoned()` was true and `admit` still let a send through. The new test hits that window on every run at the base commit.

## What changed

- One `phase: Mutex<ActionPhase>` with `Active(Vec<OwnedFd>)` and `Abandoned` replaces both flags. `admit`, `is_abandoned` and `fence` all read it.
- A data-free `sending: Mutex<()>` is held across each admitted send. `abandon` shuts the fenced sockets and sets `Abandoned` under `phase`, releases `phase`, then waits on `sending`. A wedged send to a fenced socket still cannot block it, and `is_abandoned()` reads true only after the sockets are shut.
- Two tests: once the action reads abandoned it admits nothing, and abandoned reads true only after fenced sockets are shut.

## Scope

Only `platform-linux/src/input/action.rs`. This is the ActionPhase item from the merge plan (L4 / F13). Other F13 work in CUA-3433 is left out. Callers keep the same API.

## Tradeoffs

The ticket sketched a third `Fenced(Vec<OwnedFd>)` variant. It is folded into `Active`, since an empty fence list behaves the same as no fence. The second mutex stays because `abandon` has to shut sockets before it waits for a send in flight, and that wait cannot happen while holding the lock that `is_abandoned` and `fence` read.

## Blast Radius

Every Linux input route that calls `action::admit` or `action::fence` (X11 XTest, targeted input, Wayland, niri, Hyprland, libei, persistent vptr), plus `Delivered::drop` through `is_abandoned`. Lock order is always `sending` then `phase`, and `abandon` never holds both, so `fence` or `is_abandoned` called inside an admitted send cannot deadlock.

## Verification

- `once_an_action_reads_abandoned_it_admits_nothing` fails on every run at the test-only commit on top of main and passes at head.
- The scoped repository checks for `platform-linux` pass: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, and the lib tests.
- The verify-cua-driver X11 lane delivered both Electron click cells, with evidence complete after cleanup.

Size: within the production line limit, so no size reason is needed.

CUA-3678

title: fix(vmm): the runtime doctor's report makes no Local Network connect, so macOS doesn't ask at launch
body:
## Why
The macOS app reads the runtime doctor at launch. Its preflight report built the `macos_vm` entry by running the Local Network check, a TCP connect to the router. That connect makes macOS show "Allow Cua Spaces to find devices on local networks?" seconds after launch, before anything explains it and on the way to a Linux Space that never needs it. Apple's guidance (TN3179) is to ask when the person does the thing that needs it.

## What changed
- `cua_vmm::preflight::report()` no longer runs the Local Network check. The create of a macOS Space still runs it, with its 30 s patience (`gather_waiting`, called by the daemon's `preflight_refusal`).
- A test counts Local Network checks: `report()` makes none, and a create makes one.

## Scope
Only the runtime doctor's report. The Machines page check (`machine.local_network`) and the create preflight are unchanged.

## Blast Radius
`preflight.macos_vm` in the doctor report no longer carries a Local Network issue. No reader depends on that: the create still refuses with it, and the app reads preflight issues generically.

## Verification
- `cua runtime doctor --embedded` from 0.22.0 made 1 port-9 connect on en0 in each of 2 runs (kernel log). This branch's build made 0 in 2 runs.
- A fresh first run of a build with this change made 0 port-9 connects and 0 Local Network lookups for the app.
- cua-vmm fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-vmm --lib preflight` (7 pass). Pointing `report()` back at a probe fails the new test.

title: fix(spaces-macos): the Local Network step waits on macOS's prompt when it is already open
body:
## Why
`LocalNetworkGate.waitForAnswer` counted macOS's prompt windows when Continue was pressed and waited only if the count went up. When macOS had already asked (at launch), no new prompt appeared, so 3 s later the app showed "Can't connect to macOS Spaces" while the prompt was still on screen.

## What changed
- Any macOS prompt on screen keeps the gate waiting, until the existing answer timeout.
- A test covers a prompt already open when the gate starts. The test fakes no longer treat the first read as a baseline.

## Scope
The macOS app's Local Network gate.

## Tradeoffs
The gate counts any `UserNotificationCenter` window, not only the Local Network prompt. If another system alert is already open and access stays blocked, the gate waits until that alert closes or 60 s pass (`promptAnswered`), instead of failing at 3 s. Telling the alerts apart needs window titles, which macOS hides without Screen Recording access. A bounded wait in a rare case was preferred over the false "Can't connect" this fixes.

## Verification
- Swift suite passes. The new test fails on the old baseline check.

title: fix(platform-macos): run bring_to_front activation off the async worker
body:
CUA-3311

## Why

On macOS, `bring_to_front` did all of its blocking work inside the async `invoke`. That covers the Cocoa activation request, the exact-window AX raise, and the verification poll, which sleeps for up to 900 ms. When the target is the driver's own process, the raise waits up to 2 s for the AppKit main queue (`ax::main_thread::run_ax_mutation`). The tokio worker running the call could do nothing else in the meantime.

## What changed

- `BringToFrontTool::invoke` still parses `pid` and `window_id`, then runs the rest in `activate_blocking` on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. Result JSON, error codes and check order are unchanged.
- The blocking closure holds the call's `DesktopLease`. If the dispatch is cancelled while activation is running, the desktop input lane stays held until the worker stops, and is not handed to the next action. This matches `platform-linux`'s `Action`.
- New test `own_process_activation_does_not_block_the_async_worker`. It re-runs the test binary as a child with `NSApp` set to activation policy Prohibited, so the process check polls for the full timeout. The child invokes the tool on its own pid on a single-thread runtime and counts 10 ms ticks of a sibling task. It then cancels a second call inside a `DesktopCall` scope and checks that the next `DesktopCall::acquire` waits for the worker. It skips without a window server session.

## Scope

Only `platform-macos/src/tools/bring_to_front.rs`. Other own-process callers of the same raise (the foreground HID path in `input/skylight.rs`, `type_text`'s browser rung) already run on `spawn_blocking` workers. The exact-window own-pid raise is not covered by a cargo test, because the test harness never drains the main queue. It runs behind the same `spawn_blocking` boundary as the pid-only path the test covers.

## Blast Radius

Embedded hosts and the daemon, for every `bring_to_front` call on macOS. A call now takes one extra hop to the blocking pool. A cancelled call keeps the input lane until its activation finishes; before this change, cancelling dropped the work along with the future.

## Verification

- The new test fails on the test-only commit with `async worker stalled: 0 ticks in 1.93s`. With the fix it passes. If the worker drops the lease, it fails with `lane handed on while the worker still ran`.
- The scoped repository checks for `platform-macos`: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, and the lib tests.
- verify-cua-driver macOS Lume full matrix at the head: 179 delivered, 5 expected refusals, 0 failed, all 4 `bring_to_front_macos_test` cases passed.

title: fix(cua-driver): classify the Linux desktop once and read foreground restore from one table
body:
## Why

platform-linux worked out which desktop it was running on at every call site, from `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, the native-Wayland opt-in and each compositor's socket variable. Each foreground call site also hard-coded its own restore mode. CUA-3674 asks for one classification and one restore-policy table that every site reads, with no change in behaviour.

## What changed

- `platform_linux::desktop::Desktop` (`X11`, `XWayland(Compositor)`, `Wayland(Compositor)`; `Compositor` is `Injected`, `Hyprland`, `Niri` or `Other`) is classified on first use. It is classified again only when this process rewrites its display variables: the nested session, and the unit-test display override. `is_wayland`, `hyprland::is_session`, the niri adapter gate, `list_windows_dispatch`, the lock probe and the `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` checks in the overlay, health report and browser flows now read it. `wayland_input_enabled` was a copy of `is_wayland` and is removed.
- `interaction::foreground_policy(Desktop) -> ForegroundPolicy` has one row per desktop and one column per action kind: typing, key, click, gesture, menu and setup. Each `with_x11_foreground` / `with_target_foreground` call site reads `session_policy().<column>` instead of naming a `RestoreMode`, and `pointer_gesture_restore` becomes the gesture column.
- The rows are today's modes. On X11 and XWayland, typing and the browser setup flows restore the prior focus (the CUA-3663 fix) and everything else leaves the target active. On Wayland, everything but menus and gestures restores, and niri restores gestures as well.

## Scope

Covers platform-linux route selection and foreground restore modes, plus the e2e tests that called the removed `wayland_input_enabled`. It does not change any restore mode, and it does not touch compositor-specific checks that need I/O. Sway's `SWAYSOCK`, KWin's and GNOME's `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` probes, and niri's socket attestation all stay where they are. niri is still confirmed through its IPC attestation, which `Desktop::attested` asks for and which also wins over a Hyprland signature that niri inherited.

## Blast Radius

Every Linux input, capture and listing route reads the classification, so a wrong classification would misroute all of them. The classifier has unit tests for each environment combination, and each `session_policy()` site was checked against the literal mode it replaced on every desktop that can reach it. The one leftover literal is the libei re-entry in `click_focused`, which runs inside an outer transaction that has already chosen its mode.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` for platform-linux, cua-driver-e2e and cua-driver, and platform-linux tests for all targets under Xvfb. The CI-gated ignored X11 click and key suites also pass.
- `x11_foreground_restore_linux_test` (CUA-3663) passes on Xvfb with openbox. With the X11 `typing` row flipped to `LeaveFocused`, it fails with "left the active window on the target", so it pins this row.
- The verify-cua-driver X11 lane reports 2 delivered, 0 failed, with complete evidence. Wayland, KWin, GNOME, niri and Hyprland sessions were not run. macOS and Windows builds could not run here.

Size: about 350 production lines added and 200 net, because moving every classification and restore call site has to land in one change.

CUA-3674

title: fix(cua-driver): an exact frame match names its Linux window among cascaded windows of one size
body:
## Problem

On Linux, `get_window_state` for one of two same-size windows of one process returned the elements of both windows. Chrome cascades a new window by 10 px: two Chrome windows of one pid at (10,37) and (20,47), both 1050x753, sit 20 px apart in `frame_geometry_distance`, under `FRAME_MATCH_MARGIN_PX` (24). `correlate_frame_to_window` refused, and the read walked every window of the application.

Measured on an X11 (Xfwm) desktop with two such Chrome windows:

- a read of the second window listed 80 elements, with the frame, field and button of the first window among them, so an element index from that list clicked a button in the other window;
- with `max_elements` 300 the walk spent the budget on the first window and returned none of the requested window's own fields.

## Fix

A frame that matches the window's geometry exactly (distance 0), while no other frame does, resolves without the margin. Two frames at distance 0, or a best frame that is close but not exact, refuse as before.

## Test

`frame_correlation_tests::an_exact_match_resolves_among_cascaded_windows_of_one_size`: each of the two cascaded frames resolves to its own window, and a window between them still refuses.

On the same desktop with the fix:

- a read of either window lists only that window's elements (36 and 37 instead of 80);
- the other window's button is no longer listed;
- with `max_elements` 300 the requested window's field and button come back.

The read costs the same: median 275 ms with the fix, 274 ms without, 60 interleaved calls each.

## Checks

- [x] `bin/ci --quick`: 5 passed. Skipped in quick mode: clippy, unit tests, docs reference, UniFFI bindings.
- [x] On an ubuntu-24.04 runner: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` (990 passed, under Xvfb).

title: fix(cua-driver): the macOS permission guide names the app the driver runs in
body:
## Problem

System Settings lists the app bundle the driver runs in. When the driver ships inside another app (`Host.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver`, or under `Contents/Resources`), Accessibility and Screen Recording list that app's name. The guide window, its drag tile and the terminal banner still told the person to turn on "Cua Driver", a row that is not in the list. - The guide takes the shown name of the bundle that holds the running executable, as System Settings does: NSBundle's localized `CFBundleDisplayName`, else `CFBundleName`.

- When that bundle is not in `/Applications`, the banner names the folder that holds it.

title: Flaky Linux test: an_empty_walk_reads_the_reason_from_the_real_process sees no NO_AT_BRIDGE (left: None)
body:
## Problem

`atspi::bridge_disabled_reason_tests::an_empty_walk_reads_the_reason_from_the_real_process` (from #6822) fails intermittently in the Linux platform unit tests:

```
thread 'atspi::bridge_disabled_reason_tests::an_empty_walk_reads_the_reason_from_the_real_process' panicked at crates/platform-linux/src/atspi/mod.rs:1180:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: None
 right: Some("atspi_bridge_disabled: the target runs with NO_AT_BRIDGE=1, ...")
```

It failed in 3 of 13 runs of `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` on GitHub's ubuntu-24.04 runners (image 20261101.360.1) on 2026-11-08, each time on a commit that passed on re-run:

- https://github.com/loomhand/cua/actions/runs/42468035707/attempts/1
- https://github.com/loomhand/cua/actions/runs/42468338976/attempts/1
- https://github.com/loomhand/cua/actions/runs/42481893891/attempts/1

None of those commits touches `atspi/mod.rs`.

## Likely cause

The test spawns `sleep` with `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1` and reads `/proc/<pid>/environ` right away. `Command::spawn` returns once the child is in `execve`. The kernel releases the parent from `exec_mmap`, before `load_elf_binary` sets the new image's `env_start`/`env_end`. So a read in that window can come back empty, `bridge_disabled_reason` finds no `NO_AT_BRIDGE=1`, and the test sees `None`.

## What I could not show

I could not reproduce it on demand. On ubuntu-24.04 runners, upstream main (ef1e84d6c) passed every time:

- the full platform-linux lib suite, 20 runs;
- the `bridge_disabled_reason_tests` module, 50 runs;
- the test alone with every CPU busy, 200 runs.

The same counts with the candidate fix below were also clean. So the window above is a likely cause, not a confirmed one.

## Candidate fix (test only)

The `Sleeper` helper waits, up to 2 s, until `/proc/<pid>/environ` is non-empty before the test reads it. No change to the code under test. Branch: https://github.com/loomhand/cua/commit/f6014fe36 (on ef1e84d6c). I can open it as a pull request if that approach is welcome.

title: Flaky Linux test: focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened fails at the second SUBSTRUCTURE_REDIRECT selection (mod.rs:4632)
body:
## Problem

`input::own_dialog_tests::focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened` fails intermittently in the Linux platform unit tests on upstream main.

In 20 runs of `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` on main ef1e84d6c (GitHub ubuntu-24.04 runner, image 20261101.360.1, under Xvfb), it failed 2 times. Both failures were at the same line, and the rest of the suite passed:

```
input::own_dialog_tests::focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened --- FAILED
thread 'input::own_dialog_tests::focus_restore_leaves_focus_on_a_dialog_the_app_opened' (23087) panicked at crates/platform-linux/src/input/mod.rs:4632:10:
test result: FAILED. 988 passed; 1 failed; 11 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 10.94s
```

Run: https://github.com/loomhand/cua/actions/runs/42488635525. The workflow runs the suite 20 times and printed `full suite failed 2 of 20`. It kept only the FAILED and panicked lines, so the panic payload is not in the log.

## Likely cause

`mod.rs:4632` is the `.check().unwrap()` after the test's fake window manager selects `SUBSTRUCTURE_REDIRECT` on the root for the "closed saved window" case:

```rust
let (wm, _) = RustConnection::connect(Some(&name)).unwrap();
wm.change_window_attributes(
    root,
    &ChangeWindowAttributesAux::new().event_mask(EventMask::SUBSTRUCTURE_REDIRECT),
)
.unwrap()
.check()
.unwrap();
```

Only one client may select `SubstructureRedirect` on a window; a second one gets `BadAccess`. The previous fake window manager is a connection that the loop above moved into its event thread. It is dropped when that thread ends, and nothing waits for the X server to process that disconnect before the next connection selects the same mask. A late disconnect would fail this check.

## Possible fix

Test only, either of:

- keep one window-manager connection for the whole test and reuse it;
- after joining the thread, retry the selection briefly while it fails with `BadAccess`.

title: fix(cua-driver): a Linux app that did not answer GetChildren stays app_unresponsive without a walk until it answers a GetState probe
body:
## Problem

On Linux, `get_window_state` on an app that stopped answering AT-SPI (stopped, or stuck in a modal grab) spent its whole time budget on every call: 1 s by default (`timeout_ms`). The application lookup goes through the D-Bus daemon, which still answers. The app's own `GetChildren` then waits out the budget, the walk returns `app_unresponsive` with an empty tree, and nothing records the miss, so the next call pays the full budget again.

Measured on an X11 desktop with a GTK3 window whose process was stopped with SIGSTOP (10 episodes, 4 calls each while stopped):

- first call while stopped: 1018 ms;
- every later call while stopped: median 1017 ms.

## Fix

The `!app_answered` branch remembers the pid with its bus and root path. While remembered, a walk of that pid returns the same `app_unresponsive` result at once. One `GetState` probe to the root runs on the AT-SPI runtime at a time, bounded by the existing operation timeout. Any reply forgets the pid, so the next walk reads the app again. No new setting.

## Test

`unresponsive_tests::one_probe_runs_at_a_time_and_only_an_answer_clears_the_mark`: one probe is claimed at a time, a probe without a reply keeps the mark, and a reply clears it.

On the same desktop with the fix:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| warm call | 32–46 ms | 32–46 ms |
| first call while stopped | 1018 ms | 1018 ms |
| later calls while stopped, short stops (n=30) | median 1017 ms | median 15 ms |
| later calls while stopped, 30 s stops | median 1019 ms | median 17 ms |
| first full tree after SIGCONT | first call, 29–37 ms | first call, 30–34 ms |

Measured on a 0.38-based build. On main the walk budget (1000 ms default) and the lookup are the same, and nothing remembers an unresponsive pid, so the same cost applies.

## Checks

- [x] `bin/ci --quick`: 5 passed. Skipped in quick mode: clippy, unit tests, docs reference, UniFFI bindings.
- [x] On an ubuntu-24.04 runner: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` (992 passed, under Xvfb).
- [ ] `bin/ci --signoff`: not set. The full `bin/ci` cannot run its Linux tests on a Mac, and this account cannot write commit statuses on trycua/cua (HTTP 404).

The Swift job had a 30-minute limit. title: feat(cua-driver): type_text takes literal, which types the text without stripping trailing agent-protocol tags
body:
## Problem

`type_text` drops a trailing run of unbalanced agent-protocol closing tags before typing (`text_sanitize::strip_trailing_agent_protocol_tags`). A client that types a multi-line text sends one call per line. A closing tag on its own line, such as the `</text>` that ends an SVG text element or a prompt template, has no opener in that call: it is dropped, nothing is typed, and the call reports success. The client cannot tell that part of its text is missing.

## Fix

`type_text` takes `literal` (boolean, default false) on macOS, Linux and Windows. With `literal: true` the text is typed exactly as given. A client that runs the protocol-tag check once on the whole text sends its lines with `literal: true`. The default is unchanged.

## Test

`text_sanitize::tests::a_literal_call_keeps_a_trailing_closing_tag`: a line that is only a closing tag is kept with `literal: true`, and stripped to "" without it or with `literal: false`.


## Checks

- [x] `bin/ci --quick`: 7 passed. Skipped in quick mode: clippy, unit tests, docs reference, UniFFI bindings.
- [x] On ubuntu-24.04, windows-2025 and macos-15 runners: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `text_sanitize` tests, and the host's platform lib tests (Linux 991 passed under Xvfb, Windows 320, macOS 718).
- [x] Reference regenerated the way `ci-check-docs.yml` does it: each host dumped its own MCP snapshot (`runner.ts --library cua-driver`), and the pages were rendered from all three.
- [ ] `bin/ci --signoff`: not set. This account cannot write commit statuses on trycua/cua (HTTP 404).

title: fix(cua-driver): Windows type_text writes through the focused document at its caret or selection
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `type_text` with no element writes through the focused UI Automation document (SetValue with read-back and caret placement) only when the document is empty. Every later line goes in as SendInput Unicode packets. Windows 11 Notepad collapses queued packets into a run of one character after a `/` or `€`, and the batched key route from #6892 does not change that.

Measured on upstream main da8e73b9c (0.44.0): Windows 11 Notepad, foreground, unthrottled, 20 trials per text, arms interleaved ACCA.

| text | main: exact | main: what arrived | main: p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a/text>` after a line break | 3/20 | 16 trials gave `a/>>>>>` | — |
| a 2000-character line with `/` and `€` | 0/20 | runs of one character: 0–1463 of 2018 bytes, 2 files empty | 640 ms |

## Fix

The focused-document route takes a document of at most 1 MiB with one selection:

1. It reads the text before the selection and the selected text, and requires that they and the rest rebuild the value exactly.
2. It writes the text in place of the selection.
3. It puts the caret after the text (UTF-16 units first, then scalar values) and checks the text before the caret.

A write whose caret cannot be verified is reported as unverifiable and is not retried. Anything else still goes the key route as before.

Known limits, the same as the existing empty-document write:

- Notepad does not mark the document modified after a UI Automation write; Ctrl+S still saves it.
- Ctrl+Z does not undo it.
- Notepad's Autocorrect does not act on it.

## Test

Unit tests in `uia::focused_document`: `a_selection_maps_onto_the_value_only_when_prefix_selection_and_rest_rebuild_it`, `a_selection_that_moved_before_the_write_sends_the_text_by_keys`, `the_size_probe_admits_the_cap_and_refuses_one_unit_more`.

Same setup with this change:

| text | exact | result | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a/text>` after a line break | 20/20 | "Wrote and verified" | 20 ms |
| a 2000-character line with `/` and `€` | 20/20 | | 23 ms |

## Checks

- [x] `bin/ci --quick`: 5 passed. Skipped in quick mode: clippy, unit tests, docs reference, UniFFI bindings.
- [x] On a windows-2025 runner: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p platform-windows --lib` (324 passed).
- [x] The measured binaries are release builds of main da8e73b9c and of this branch (`cargo build --locked --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`).
- [ ] `bin/ci --signoff`: not set. This account cannot write commit statuses on trycua/cua (HTTP 404).

title: fix(cua-driver): Windows type_text waits out a slow focused-document probe and sends no keys after it
body:
Builds on #6995 (focused-document write at the caret). The new change is only the last commit, 4be5723a0: https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6996/commits/4be5723a012cacbad6e3dc8d19a299b54a423704 (the first commit is #6995's).

## Problem

Before it writes, the focused-document route probes the document through UI Automation within 200 ms. A probe that missed that deadline was treated as "not applicable", so `type_text` fell back to SendInput Unicode keys. The probe misses the deadline when the target is busy or starved, which is exactly when Windows 11 Notepad defers key messages and replays them later: a replayed VK_PACKET takes the thread's last packet character, so the text comes out as runs of one character with about half of it lost.

A probe that finds the previous probe still running (the single-flight gate is `Busy`) took the same fallback.

## Fix

- The probe gets 2 s, the time the key route already gives a target to read one unit.
- A probe that still has not answered, or a call that finds the previous probe still running, returns an error that says nothing was written and no keys were sent. Only an unavailable UI Automation still falls back to keys.
- The single-flight permit is dropped before the worker sends its result, so a caller that receives the result can start the next probe at once instead of finding the gate still held.

## Test

Unit tests in `uia::focused_document`: `a_probe_past_its_deadline_or_still_running_before_the_write_sends_no_keys`, `an_unavailable_worker_before_the_write_allows_native_fallback`, and the `type_text` result test for the new outcome.

Measured on upstream main da8e73b9c (0.44.0): Windows 11 25H2, Notepad 11.2607. Each trial types `line1`, presses Return, types a 2000-character line with `/` and `€`, then saves with Ctrl+S, all `scope: desktop`; the saved file is compared byte for byte. The VM's CPU was cut to 10 % in random 50–400 ms bursts (1371 bursts, 0 failed writes). 200 trials per arm, arms interleaved in blocks (CDDC).

| | #6995 only | #6995 + this change |
|---|---|---|
| garbled text | 8/200 | 0/200 (one-sided Fisher p = 0.0036) |
| fallbacks to keys (line1 + 2000-char) | 13 + 8 | 0 |
| "write still in flight" unknown results | 2 + 2 | 0 |
| 2000-char round trip p50 / p90 / p99 / max | 21 / 29 / 1916 / 2549 ms | 22 / 27 / 383 / 423 ms |
| line1 round trip p50 / p90 / p99 / max | 26 / 172 / 385 / 434 ms | 28 / 207 / 424 / 462 ms |

With this change, 25 calls took longer than 200 ms; all were verified UI Automation writes, the slowest 462 ms. Unthrottled, a 2000-character call is unchanged: p50 22 ms vs 21 ms (100 trials per arm, measured earlier on a 0.43.1-based build).

### Earlier measurement, on a 0.43.1-based build (before #6892)

A Notepad target held unresponsive for 3 s. `type_text` of 20 characters is called once, then retried; 3 trials each, one call and multi-line.

| build | first call | retry |
|---|---|---|
| caret write only (#6995) | `text_delivery_stalled`: unit 1 inserted and may still appear (keys sent) | same, keys sent again |
| this change without the `Busy` mapping | "did not answer UI Automation in time; nothing was written and no keys were sent" | `text_delivery_stalled` (the probe still running took the key route) |
| this change | "did not answer UI Automation in time; nothing was written and no keys were sent" | the same error at once (0 ms), no keys |

Nothing landed in any of these trials.

## Checks

title: fix(cua-sandbox): avoid closing context tunnels twice
body:
## Summary

- A tunnel opened with `async with` was closed on context exit but its `TunnelInfo` retained an active closer. Calling `close()` on that object afterwards closed the underlying tunnel a second time.
- Close through the same `TunnelInfo` path used for explicit close, so successful context cleanup also marks each handle closed. A failed close remains retryable. Correct the `close()` docstring to reflect that a handle may also be closed inside a context.

## Related work

No related issue found in the repository search. This fixes the already-documented no-op behavior for a closed handle; it does not introduce a new public API or protocol contract.

## Compatibility and risk

A caller no longer receives a second underlying close after exiting the context and then calling `close()` again. If a close fails, the handle remains retryable. No migration is required.

## Validation

- `PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/test_tunnel.py -q` in `libs/python/cua-sandbox`: 10 passed with Python 3.12. The new regression failed before the fix with two underlying close calls. Tests cover manual close inside the context, multiple tunnels and close failure/retry.
- Ruff, Black, isort on the two changed files, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `bin/ci --quick --no-install --base upstream/main --only spdx,image-refs`: 2 checks passed.
- Full `bin/ci` and signoff were not run: docs generator routing requires installed docs dependencies and the machine has limited disk space. No real sandbox/network tunnel was exercised; tests use the transport mock.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] No external contribution is included.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`)

Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, test creation and this description. This draft is awaiting human review.

title: [Bug]: cua-driver test fails on Linux with macOS permission fixes
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux, `cua-driver test` always fails at the first step. It says Cua Driver can't use the mouse and keyboard or see the screen, and tells you to turn on Accessibility and Screen Recording, which are macOS settings.

### Reproduction

1. Install cua-driver 0.44.0 on Linux (KDE Plasma 6.6.6, Wayland).
2. Run `cua-driver test --json`.

### Expected behavior

The test checks what Linux actually needs, reads the screen and passes when the driver works.

### Actual behavior

```
"ok": false
accessibility: fail, "Cua Driver can't use your mouse and keyboard yet"
screen_recording: fail, "Cua Driver can't see your screen yet"
fix: "Turn on Accessibility for Cua Driver: run `cua-driver permissions grant`"
```

On Linux, `cua-driver permissions` says it's macOS only.

### Environment

Ubuntu 26.04.1, KWin 6.6.6, cua-driver 0.44.0. Same result on 0.42.1.

### Evidence

On the same daemon, `get_desktop_state` returns a screenshot and `get_window_state` returns a valid window capture.

`selftest.rs` reads `accessibility` and `screen_recording` from `check_permissions`. On Linux, `check_permissions` returns `atspi`, `wayland`, `x11` and `xsend_event` instead, so both flags read as false and the test stops before the screen read (main at `4bf944e73`).

### Workaround and additional context

Ignore the result on Linux. Prepared with an AI coding agent, and I ran the checks on my own machine.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Install log and health report misstate KWin capture when kwin-capture is on
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

With `cua-driver kwin-capture on`, the installer still logs that KWin window capture is off, and `health_report` still says capture goes through the portal. Neither one checks the switch.

### Reproduction

1. On KDE Plasma Wayland, run `cua-driver kwin-capture on`.
2. Rerun the installer.
3. Call `health_report`.

The installer says capture is on when the switch is on. The health report names the KWin ScreenShot2 route when it's enabled.

title: fix(spaces): a run submitted from a Space is a child of that Space and cannot escape its rules
body:
## What

A run submitted from inside a Space is now a **child of that Space**, wherever it is placed, and cannot escape the Space's rules.

- The scoped `submit` (the daemon, not the client) stamps `CUA_PARENT_SPACE`, `CUA_ROOT_SPACE`, `CUA_TREE_DEPTH` and `CUA_PARENT_NETWORK` into the run's environment (also into explicit `jobs[].spec`), over anything the Space put there.
- The host that creates the job's Space (`SpacesExecutor`) records it as a child: a real tree record (`SpaceCreate.parent`: listed under the parent, deleted/stopped with it, network no more open than the parent's) when the parent lives on that computer; on another computer the `cua.parent`/`cua.root`/`cua.depth` labels and the parent's network settings, cut down by `intersect`.
- Refused with an actionable message, before anything is recorded: a native `kind=machine` job from a Space that has network rules (it would run outside them), host `services`, a cloud provider in `on` (the owner's money, outside the tree's budget), and a run deeper than the tree allows.

Before this, a job Space was created with the default `internet` network and no parent, whatever its submitter's policy: a Space with `none` could run a job with the internet (escape, high severity), and the Space tree never listed the job.

## Tests
- unit: `confine_submit` (stamps over a forged claim, both submit shapes, each refusal), in `children/runs.rs`
- red team on the real scoped channel, from a Space whose network is `none`: `a_restricted_space_cannot_start_a_run_that_escapes_its_rules`
- `cargo test -p cua-daemon --lib children::` 49 passed

## Risk and rollback
- Stacked on #6945 (the scoped pool). Revert this PR alone; nothing else depends on it.
- A Space with plain `internet` networking is unchanged except that its job Spaces now have a parent (and are deleted with it). Users with `none`/custom networks who ran native machine jobs or cloud runs from a Space now get a refusal that says what to do; ask the owner or use a container job.
- Older hosts ignore the new environment variables: the job Space is then unparented, as before.
- Existing Spaces, ledgers and records are untouched (no format change).

## What

`cua_daemon::client::ensure_daemon()` in a Space (`CUA_SPACE` set) with no spawn channel now returns a clear error instead of finding or starting a daemon: a Space does not start or reach a cua daemon of its own, because Spaces it made that way would run under no parent's tree, network or budget. The spawn channel (children on) is unchanged and remains the only way in. The enforcement of what a child may do stays in the daemon's scoped channel, not here.

## Risk and rollback
- Stacked on #6945. Revert alone.

title: test(cua-relay): fix flaky handover_process test (port taken between pick and bind)
body:
The process tests picked a free port by binding to port 0 and closing it, then started the relay on it. Another test process could take the port in between, so the relay exited with AddrInUse and the test panicked with "nothing answered on port" (example: run 42498713123).

Fix: the relay start is retried on fresh ports (max 5 tries) when the relay exits while starting, and a stranger answering on the port no longer counts as ready. Same pattern fixed in shutdown.rs and mesh_default.rs. Other tests in the crate let the relay bind port 0 itself.

Local: 30 runs of the three test files with --test-threads=8, 0 failures; bin/ci --fix and --quick pass.

No user-facing change (test only).

title: fix(cua-agents): an agent's log event bigger than the read window no longer stalls the reader, and the journal keeps lines small
body:
## What happened (root cause, with evidence)

In a recorded run the Home agent finished (`agent status`: `end_turn`, full final report) but the thread kept showing "claude is using Read File, Working for 34m", and the final message never appeared.

- `events.jsonl` in the Space held all 287 events. The app read only up to seq 185.
- The log has image events: a tool that reads a PNG returns it as base64, hundreds of KB, twice in one event (lines of 187 KB, 373 KB, 547 KB, 592 KB).
- The reader (`Agents::events`) reads fixed 512 KiB windows and parses whole lines. Replaying it on the real file (kept as evidence) shows it can never pass seq 259: that line (547,563 B) is larger than the window, so the page has no complete line, the cursor does not move, and every later poll repeats the same read. Nothing after it, including the turn end, reaches the thread.

Not a hung tool, not the harness: the agent process was idle and waiting for a follow-up.

## Fix
1. `events::read_page`: when a window holds no complete line and the file goes on, the window grows (x4, up to 256 MiB) and the read repeats. A window that ends inside a line is no longer reported as "caught up".
2. The runner journals every event through `shrink`: strings over 32 KiB are cut with a note of how much was left out, and base64/binary data becomes a one-line note. The model and the person already had the data; the log keeps what a resumed turn and the thread read.

Tests: reader (a line 20x the window, and a window ending inside a line), `runner/test/journal-size.test.mjs` (image data, long output, small values untouched).

## Compared with the durable-agent references (what I actually read)

| Mechanism | pi-durable (`packages/durable`) | vercel-labs/durable-harness | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Big tool output / images in the log | The transcript stores only `output` and `details`; `bash` keeps the retained tail and puts the full output in a file; `read` bounds images (2000x2000, 4.5 MB base64) | README does not cover it | Match: the journal keeps text cut at 32 KiB with a note, and no image data |
| Reading the log | Watches hold the newest 50 entries and page older ones on demand, by entry, not by bytes | not covered | We read by byte windows, so the window must be able to grow to hold one entry (new), and the journal bounds entries so it rarely has to |
| Resume after a crash | Atomic commits, `Harness.open()` recovers, `restartLimit` ends crash loops | Run event log; resume the turn from it | Unchanged: the runner's existing durable mode (epoch fence, journal, heartbeat) |
| Hung turn / stall watchdog | `settings.stream.timeoutMs` for a model request; no stalled-tool watchdog | not covered | Deliberately none added: no reference interrupts a quiet tool automatically, and a tool that runs for hours is normal. This incident was not a hang |

## Risk and rollback
- The log of a new run has long strings cut and images replaced by a note (the data is the tool's own, in the Space). Old logs are read the same way as before, now without the livelock.
- Revert this PR alone; no format change (the lines are still the same JSON).

title: fix(spaces-macos): ask for Local Network when this Mac starts accepting Spaces from your other computers
body:
Follow-up to #6970 (merged), per the 8 Nov decision to take option A.

## Why
#6970 removed the Local Network ask when this Mac starts providing Spaces. After it, a macOS Space that another device creates on this Mac reaches the daemon's create preflight (`cua-daemon/src/local.rs`, `preflight_refusal`), and its connect can raise macOS's own prompt, with no explanation, on a Mac nobody may be watching. If nobody answers in 30 s, the requester's create fails. Apple's guidance is to ask in context, and to ask early when the operation will later run with nobody there to answer (TN3179).

## What changed
- When this Mac starts accepting Spaces from other computers, the app shows its explanation, then makes macOS ask (the existing `LocalNetworkGate`, with `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`). That covers the "Let other computers create Spaces here" switch, the setup form and a join code (`HostModel.followProviding`, `AppModel.askLocalNetworkForHosting`).
- Nothing asks during sign-in. The setup that sign-in runs, and any setup while the first run shows, wait. Finishing the first run asks instead (`onboarding.complete`).
- A local macOS create still asks first (`followCreate`). `LocalNetworkGate.check` now runs one check at a time, so a create and the hosting ask never show two explanations, whichever starts first.
- Tests: the sign-in's setup asks only when the first run ends, the switch asks once, a later sign-in asks nothing, and a create overlapping the hosting ask explains once, in both orders. Removing any guard fails its test.

No new state: one optional task handle on the model, and the gate's last check.

## Scope
The macOS app's Local Network triggers only. No daemon, core or web change.

## Tradeoffs
- The switch and a join code ask even before the first run is marked done ("Skip for now" leaves it undone). The person is in Settings or on the add-computer sheet at that moment, so the ask is in context.
- A Mac that already provided Spaces before this build gets no hosting ask until the switch goes off and on again, or until its first local macOS create.
- If the status read right after a join code fails, the transition is missed and that Mac is not asked until the next switch or local create.

## Blast Radius
Macs that provide Spaces to your other devices: they now see the explanation once, when providing turns on or when the first run ends.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks: the macOS app's Swift suite passes in full. Mutation checks: removing each guard fails its test.
- Live on a Mac mini, driven with cua-driver, on a Local build with a fresh Local Network state (a new bundle id and new executable UUIDs, because macOS keys the answer by both):
  - Launch: no prompt and no Local Network connect.
  - Switch off: nothing. Switch on: the explanation, Continue, then macOS's prompt once; Allow. Off and on again: nothing.
  - Signed out, first run, sign-in: this Mac was set up to provide Spaces, with no explanation and no prompt during the sign-in or the minute after. Finishing the first run: the explanation, then macOS's prompt once; Allow.
  - A macOS Space created on this Mac from the CLI as `--on host:<this Mac>` passed the daemon's preflight with no prompt. On this Mac the daemon's own probe raised no prompt either, even for an id that had never been asked, so this run cannot show the bare prompt going away. It does show the hosting ask happening first.
- Not run: the Linux and Windows lanes (no change there), and a create from a second physical device.
