title: fix(cua-driver): route macOS element-token middle clicks to the target window
body:
CUA-3797, follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6947.

An element-token middle click never reached an AppKit control. The element path in `click` posted through `middle_click_at_xy`, which stamps no window-local point and no window id. AppKit hit-tests that stamp, so the `otherMouseDown` never arrived, in background and in foreground delivery. The pixel middle click and the double_click AX fallback already use the window-routed primitive and do reach the control. AppKit buttons do take middle clicks. The driver was not routing this one.

## Change

- `platform-macos` `click`, `button: "middle"` with `element_token`: translate the element center by the window's bounds and post through `middle_click_at_xy_with_window_local`, like the pixel path. If the bounds can't be resolved it errors and sends nothing. The foreground-with-modifiers branch is unchanged, since it posts at the HID tap.
- AppKit fixture: the active-only button reports `active_only=middle_click` on `otherMouseDown` while it is enabled.
- `macos-appkit-activation-enablement-ax-foreground` gains a success row. A foreground element-token middle click on the active-only button from behind another app must land. The refusal row on the always-disabled checkbox stays.

## Proof

Repro on the host with a minimal AppKit window holding one NSButton that logs `otherMouseDown`: at the base, element-token middle clicks in foreground and in background delivery logged nothing. Pixel middle clicks at the same point logged `middle_down`/`middle_up`. With the fix, element-token middle clicks logged `middle_down`/`middle_up` in foreground, in background, and in foreground with the app starting behind Finder.

The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-e2e --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`, and a `swiftc` compile of the AppKit fixture. Full macOS Lume guest matrix at the head through the verify-cua-driver skill: 179 delivered, 5 refused, 0 failed. In the new row the fixture records `active_only=middle_click` after the call. Two earlier full runs at this head each failed only `macos-appkit-invoke-menu-ax-foreground`: a background-disabled menu item got invoked. That cell is not touched here. It failed the same way at three earlier heads of #6947, and the base run on main passed it, so it reads as intermittent.

Not run: Linux and Windows lanes (macOS-only change), standalone browsers, SIP-on permission flow.

title: Linux X11: a driver stopped or killed while typing leaves its borrowed spare keycodes bound, and later text runs out of spares
body:
## Problem

A character with no key on the layout is typed through a spare keycode: `reserve_spare_keycode` binds the keysym on every level (`vec![keysym; per]`, `platform-linux/src/input/mod.rs:4942`). Only `RemappedKeycode::drop` (`:4894`) restores the original NoSymbol mapping. If the daemon goes away while a text is being typed, the keycodes stay bound until the X server restarts.

`is_spare_keycode` (`:4910`) only takes keycodes that are NoSymbol on every level, so a leaked keycode is never reused. Each interrupted text can take up to one batch of spares from the pool. Once the pool is empty, the routes that need spares can no longer type characters that are missing from the layout.

## Reproduction

X11 desktop (Ubuntu 24.04, Xfce), 19 free keycodes. The daemon runs as `cua-driver serve`.

1. `xmodmap -pke | grep -cE 'U[0-9A-F]{4}'` gives 0, and 19 keycodes are empty.
2. Focus an xterm and call `type_text {"scope": "desktop", "text": <120 CJK characters, 60 distinct>}`.
3. About 300 ms in, stop the daemon in one of three ways: `cua-driver stop`, `kill -TERM <pid>`, or `kill -KILL <pid>`.
4. Run `xmodmap -pke` again. All three ways give the same result: 18 keycodes still hold the driver's bindings (`keycode 93 = U8D77 U8D77 U8D77 U8D77`, `keycode 97 = U7ECF …`, …), and 1 of 19 is empty. With `cua-driver stop`, the daemon exited within 1 s and the call was cut off. Resetting the keycodes with `xmodmap` brings back 19 empty keycodes.

This was measured on a 0.45.1-based build. On main 6285c481d the code above is the same.

## Why each path leaks

- SIGKILL: nothing can run.
- SIGTERM: the daemon installs no signal handler (no `SIGTERM`, `signal::unix` or `ctrl_c` in cua-driver, cua-driver-core or platform-linux), so the default action ends the process without unwinding.
- `cua-driver stop`: the accept loop ends, `connection_tasks.shutdown()` runs (`serve.rs:1486`), and then `rt.shutdown_timeout(30 s)` (`serve.rs:2417`). The typing runs on a `spawn_blocking` thread. I have not traced why it still exits without restoring the keycodes. The observed result is the same as with a kill.

## Possible fixes

1. **Reclaim at startup, with a marker.** Before it binds a spare keycode, the driver records the keycode in a property on the root window, for example `_CUA_DRIVER_SPARE_KEYCODES`. It removes the entry after the restore. At startup, before it reserves any spare, the driver resets to NoSymbol every listed keycode that still holds its pattern (the same Unicode keysym on every level), then clears the property. A root-window property outlives the process, so this covers a stop, a kill and a crash. The cost is one property change per bind and one per restore.
2. **Restore on shutdown.** Keep the borrowed keycodes in a process-wide registry, and restore them on SIGTERM/SIGINT and on the `stop` path before the process exits. This misses SIGKILL and a crash, so on its own it is weaker than 1.

1 alone covers every case. 2 also makes a normal stop clean without waiting for the next start. I can send a PR for 1, or for both.

title: fix(cua-driver): the Linux virtual keyboard waits for the X server to read each run of about 8 key events before it sends more
body:
## Problem

Since #6892, background `type_text` on X11 through the virtual master keyboard (`path=mpx_uinput`) writes the whole text to the uinput device at once and confirms only its last key. When the X server is short of CPU, most of the text is lost. The call still answers ok, because the last key arrives.

`type_text` with `pid` + `window_id` of a 48-character line (15 CJK), n=20 per cell (A/B/D interleaved ABBA; a host suspend cut the last block short, so some busy cells are n=10–15), on one X11 desktop (Ubuntu 24.04, Xfce). "4 CPUs busy" means four busy loops on a 4-vCPU guest.

| target | load | 0.43.1-based build (paced) | 0.45.1-based build (batched) | with this change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| xterm | 4 CPUs busy | 10/10 exact, 1646 ms | 0/15, 715 chars lost | 20/20, 660 ms |
| mousepad | 4 CPUs busy | 10/10, 1645 ms | 1/14, 609 lost | 20/20, 660 ms |
| xterm | idle | 20/20, 1536 ms | 19/20, 38 lost, 551 ms | 20/20, 577 ms |
| mousepad | idle | 20/20, 1532 ms | 18/20, 64 lost | 20/20, 572 ms |

Times are p50 per call. The last column was measured before the wait moved to `poll(2)`. With the final commit, the busy cells were run again: xterm 10/10 at 644 ms and mousepad 10/10 at 625 ms, with 0 SYN_DROPPED. All losses are deletions. What lands is the start of the text (`''`, `k`, `k451 `). In the same run, the Xorg log recorded libinput's "SYN_DROPPED event - some input events have been lost" 33 times for the batched build and 0 times for the other two. Across all runs on that box it recorded 87 against 0.

## Cause

The uinput keyboard is keys-only (`with_keys`, no ABS or REL axes), so evdev gives each reader a 64-event buffer:
- `input_estimate_events_per_packet` gives 1 + 7 = 8.
- `evdev_compute_buffer_size` returns `roundup_pow_of_two(max(8 * EVDEV_BUF_PACKETS, EVDEV_MIN_BUFFER_SIZE))` = 64.

Each key transition is two events (the key and its `SYN_REPORT`), so the buffer holds 32 transitions, about 16 typed characters. When the reader falls behind, `__pass_event` "drops all unconsumed events, leaving EV_SYN/SYN_DROPPED plus the newest event in the queue". A starved X server therefore loses everything queued except the start it had already read and the last key, which is the one the call waits for. Before #6892, the 10 ms pause after every step kept the queue short.

## Change

- `confirm_points` marks the step that ends each run of at least 8 transitions with no key held.
- At each mark, `deliver` counts the slave keyboard's raw key events until the server has read every transition sent so far. At most one run (8 to 11 transitions, at most 22 events) is ever queued.
- A run ends only with every key released, so no key is held through a wait, and the server never autorepeats one.
- If the server reads nothing for `DELIVERY_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT` (1.5 s), the call fails and says how many characters the server read, instead of losing the rest silently.
- `next_raw_key` now holds the event loop of `wait_for_raw_key`. It waits in `poll(2)` on the X connection instead of sleeping 2 ms per empty check.
- Key chords have fewer than 8 steps, so they never wait.

## Cost

- An idle server reads each run at once: xterm 551 → 577 ms (+26 ms) per call at idle for the 48-character line above, in the same run. mousepad's batched p50 (332 ms) is skewed by trials that lost text.
- Under load, the call takes as long as the server needs to read the keys: 660 ms against 1645 ms for the paced build.

## Test

`mpx_keyboard::tests::a_long_text_is_confirmed_in_windows_that_fit_the_evdev_buffer`: for an 80-character text with shifted characters, each run between confirms is at most 11 transitions and balanced (every press released), and the last step is never a confirm point. The uinput, Xorg and XInput2 path itself was measured on hardware (the table above).

## Checks

- [x] On ubuntu-24.04: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, platform-linux lib tests (1006 passed). The first attempt hit the flaky test in #6987, which #7067 fixes.
- [x] Hardware: the table above.
- [ ] `bin/ci --signoff`: not set. This account cannot write commit statuses on trycua/cua (HTTP 404).

title: macOS: background type_text at the default delay_ms 0 sends nothing into a long-running background Chrome page field and still answers ok
body:
## Problem

Since #6884, macOS `type_text` at the default `delay_ms` 0 sends its CGEvent fallback through `keyboard::type_text_batched`. That sends one key-down/key-up pair per run of up to 16 UTF-16 units, as a Unicode payload on key code 0, to the pid (`post_keyboard_event`).

A Chrome window that has been in the background for a while drops these multi-unit events: nothing reaches the page's text field. The call still answers ok:

- text: `📨 Sent (unverified) 620 char(s) via CGEvent (0ms delay). — driver could not confirm the text landed; …`
- `structuredContent`: `{"effect": "unverifiable", "route": "synthetic_events", "escalation": {"reason": "delivery_failed", "target": "foreground"}}`

## Measured

macOS 26.5.2, Google Chrome, a page with a `<textarea>`, Chrome's window in the background. `type_text` of a 620-character ASCII text to the Chrome pid; arms interleaved.

| build | delay_ms | Chrome long in the background | time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.45.1-based (batched) | 0 | 0/9 and 0/7 exact, 0 of 620 characters land | ~1.4 s |
| 0.45.1-based | 1 | 9/9 and 5/5 exact | 6.9–7.0 s (11.2 ms/char) |
| 0.45.1-based | 0, into a freshly launched Chrome | 3/3 exact | |
| 0.43.1-based (one character per event, no pause) | 0 | 5/5 exact | 11.5 s |
| both builds | 20 calls of 1 character at delay_ms 0 | 5/5 exact | |

The difference is not speed: one character per event with no pause (0.43.1-based) lands, and batched events do not. The drop needs Chrome's long-running background state; a freshly launched Chrome takes the same batched events.

Other targets at delay_ms 0 are fine: Safari 10/10 at 0.87 s, and Terminal 10/10. TextEdit uses the AX insert, so `delay_ms` does not reach it.

## Possible fixes

1. For Chromium web content, send one character per event at `delay_ms` 0, and keep batching for native fields and Safari. A global delay would cost Safari and Terminal about 8×.
2. Report a `delivery_failed` escalation as not delivered (`isError`, or a status a caller can branch on), instead of ok with `effect: "unverifiable"`.

Our client works around this by passing `delay_ms: 1` for Chromium-family background targets. I can send a PR for 1, 2 or both.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep a Linux text's borrowed keycodes until the client has had time to look its keys up
body:
## Problem

A character with no key on the layout (CJK, for example) is typed through a spare keycode. The keycode is bound for the text and restored after it. Before the restore, `TextClient::release` pings the client with `_NET_WM_PING`. A client that does not list the ping (xterm, Tk) gives `ClientSync::Unsupported`, and the keycodes go back as soon as the last key is sent.

Xlib and Qt look a key up in the keymap they hold when they handle the event, and both reload that keymap from the server when it changes. So a key that is still unhandled at the restore comes out as `NoSymbol`. Since #6892 removed the per-key pause, that is most of a CJK text.

A ping answer does not prove the keys were handled either. In Qt 5.15's xcb plugin:
- `QXcbEventQueue::takeFirst` (`qxcbeventqueue.cpp:118-145`) moves key and button events aside into `m_inputEvents` whenever Qt runs an event loop with `QEventLoop::ExcludeUserInputEvents`, and hands out the next non-input event first.
- The `_NET_WM_PING` reply is sent when that ClientMessage is handled (`qxcbwindow.cpp:1780`).
- An XKB map notify reloads the keymap from the server (`qxcbconnection.cpp:752` → `QXcbKeyboard::updateKeymap`, `qxcbkeyboard.cpp:368`, `xkb_x11_keymap_new_from_device`).

So Qt can answer the ping, then reload the restored keymap, and only after that handle the keys it set aside.

## Measured

`type_text` on one X11 desktop (Ubuntu 24.04, Xfce, 19 free keycodes), arms interleaved ABBA. "4 CPUs busy" means four busy loops on a 4-vCPU guest. Times are p50 per call. The batched-build column comes from an earlier run, the others from runs that interleaved the paced build with this change, on the same desktop with the same texts.

| target | text | load | 0.43.1-based (paced) | 0.45.1-based (batched) | with this change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| xterm (no ping), desktop | 48 chars, 15 CJK | idle | 20/20, 529 ms | 1/20 exact, 275 chars lost | 20/20, 480 ms |
| xterm, desktop | same | 4 CPUs busy | 20/20, 627 ms | 5/20, 129 lost | 20/20, 561 ms |
| Tk (no ping), desktop | 40 distinct CJK (3 spare batches) | 4 CPUs busy | 20/20, 903 ms | 9/20, 39 lost | 20/20, 1945 ms |
| featherpad (Qt 5, answers the ping), desktop | 40 distinct CJK | idle | 4/4 | 0/4, 3–9 of 40 kept (ping confirm only) | 4/4 |
| featherpad, foreground | 120 CJK | idle | 4/4 | 0/4, 8–28 of 120 kept | 4/4 |
| mousepad (GTK, answers the ping), desktop | 48 chars, 15 CJK | idle | 4/4, 554 ms | 4/4, 137 ms | 4/4, 519 ms |
| xterm, desktop | 48 ASCII chars | idle | 20/20, 487 ms | 20/20, 5 ms | 4/4, 8 ms |

An intermediate build paced and waited out only clients without the ping, and trusted the ping for the rest. For xterm and Tk it ran exactly this code, so their rows use its n=20 runs; the final commit gave xterm 4/4 at 488 ms and Tk (busy) 10/10 at 1942 ms. The featherpad desktop row's middle column is that intermediate build. Under load, a 150 ms wait without the pacing below gave 18/20, 19/20 and 20/20 in three Tk runs, each miss one character in the middle of the first batch. With this change the X server reported no SYN_DROPPED, and no keycode stayed bound after any run.

## Change

- A key on a borrowed keycode gets the paced 10 ms hold and 10 ms gap (`pacing_for`, applied in the XSendEvent and XTest send closures). This keeps the client's backlog of unhandled keys short.
- `release` waits until 150 ms after the last such key before it drops the borrowed keycodes and restores the map (`mark_sent` stamps that key's time once its events are flushed). enigo uses the same idle window (enigo-rs/enigo#569). `release` runs once per spare-keycode batch, before any rebinding, so the wait also covers keycodes rebound between batches.
- The ping is unchanged: a client that does not answer still stops the text before keycodes are rebound.
- The virtual keyboard route (`path=mpx_uinput`, `mpx_keyboard::deliver`) follows the same rule. Its steps on a remapped keycode get the 10 ms key pacing, and the remaps stay until 150 ms after the last such step. A text with no remaps keeps the 30 ms settle. Hardware numbers for this route will follow in a comment.

## Cost

- Keys on keycodes the layout already has: none. ASCII 5 → 8 ms is noise at n=4.
- Characters typed through a spare keycode: +20 ms each, plus up to 150 ms per spare-keycode batch (a batch holds as many characters as there are free keycodes). mousepad's 15-CJK line goes 137 → 519 ms and xterm's 200 → 480 ms, both still under the paced build.
- On the virtual keyboard route the same characters cost +20 ms each (10 ms after the press and 10 ms after the release), plus the 150 ms tail once per text.
- All typing stays inside the existing call budget (12 s + 40 ms per character), on the `spawn_blocking` thread that types.

## Test

`input::spare_keycode_restore_tests` runs on a private Xvfb. It types 7 CJK characters through `type_text_in_spare_batches` with XTest, and its send step applies `pacing_for` and `mark_sent` the way the real closures do.
- `a_client_without_ping_looks_its_spare_keycodes_up_before_they_are_restored`: a window with no `WM_PROTOCOLS` looks its keys up 50 ms after the last one arrives.
- `a_client_that_answers_the_ping_before_its_lookups_still_reads_them`: a window that lists `_NET_WM_PING` answers every ping at once, and looks its keys up 50 ms after it answers the first ping that follows them, as Qt does with keys it set aside.
- Both: 0/20 failures with this change. With the idle wait removed, each fails 20/20 with all 7 characters NoSymbol.

## Checks

- [x] On ubuntu-24.04: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, platform-linux lib tests (1007 passed), the new tests 20 times.
- [x] Hardware: the table above.
- [ ] `bin/ci --signoff`: not set. This account cannot write commit statuses on trycua/cua (HTTP 404).

title: fix(cua-driver): wait for the child's exec in the NO_AT_BRIDGE test
body:
## Why

`an_empty_walk_reads_the_reason_from_the_real_process` flakes because `spawn` can return before the child's exec finishes, so `/proc/<pid>/environ` reads empty for a moment. This salvages https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6871 by @astrovm, keeping its commit, which waits up to 5 s for the environ to hold `NO_AT_BRIDGE=<value>`. A second commit fixes two review findings on that wait (CUA-3942, review CUA-3822).

## What changed

- `Sleeper::with_bridge` builds the `Sleeper` guard before it polls. If the wait times out, the panic now drops the guard, which kills and reaps the `sleep` child. Before, the child leaked.
- The poll loop sleeps 5 ms between reads. It used to spin on `yield_now` for up to 5 s.

## Scope

Test code only, in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/atspi/mod.rs`. https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7067 changes the same helper in the same spot with a different wait. It is not folded in here, and whichever lands second will conflict.

## Verification

On a Debian arm64 guest:

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` all pass (1005 passed, 11 ignored). The `bridge_disabled_reason_tests` module also passed 300 runs in a row with 0 failures.
- Forced-timeout probe: I patched the helper to expect a value the child never has, with a 1 s deadline. On the contributor's commit, the failed test left a `sleep` process behind. On this head, it left none.

title: fix(cua-driver): start the AppKit background menu refusal once the item is disabled
body:
CUA-3796, follow-up to https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6947.

## Summary

- Problem: `macos-appkit-invoke-menu-ax-foreground` sometimes invoked Window > Arrange > Left in the background when it should have refused. The test launches a second harness to take activation and sends the background `invoke_menu` straight away. AppKit marks the item disabled only after the target has handled losing activation. Until then the item reads `AXEnabled` true, so the driver pressed an item that AppKit still reported as enabled.
- Change: after launching the distractor, the test polls the target's snapshot until the item shows `enabled=false` (10 s limit). Only then does it send the background call.

## Cause

Of 40 retained full guest runs of this cell, 3 invoked the item. All 3 have the shortest gap between the test's previous call and the background call (855 to 858 ms). In all 3, the AX snapshot the recorder took just before that call shows the item still enabled. In 36 of the 37 runs that refused, the same snapshot shows it disabled.

The #6947 fixture change did not cause this. One of the 3 failures ran at a commit whose fixture already created the active-only controls lazily, and the same commit passed in two other runs. The earlier eager and lazy runs differed by timing, not by a different code path.

The driver is not at fault. Its background route presses a menu item that AppKit reports enabled, which is intended: some apps keep menu items enabled while in the background. The fixture's item is enabled only while the app is active and its window is key, so the test has to wait until AppKit has applied the background state.

## Proof

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-e2e --tests -- -D warnings`.
- Full macOS Lume guest matrix at ac91acd (this change before the main merge): 178 delivered, 5 refused, 1 error. In this cell, the first two snapshots after the distractor launch still show the item enabled. The third shows it disabled, and the call then refuses with `background_unavailable`. The bring_to_front and foreground invoke that follow both succeed. The one error is `macos-tk-perception-published-capture-click-px-foreground`, whose release-asset download returned HTTP 504.
- Not run: Linux and Windows lanes (macOS-only test), standalone browsers, the SIP-on permission flow.

title: fix(cua-driver): release session labels when their owner transport closes
body:
## Why

Every `cua-driver mcp` process is its own transport on the shared macOS daemon. When one exits, its named sessions end with a tombstone that only that transport may lift, and it never comes back. The next process that picks the same short label (`screen-report`, `calc`) gets `session has ended` on every call, and the suggested `start_session` fails with `session is not available to this transport`. MCP clients that start one server per run, such as `droid exec`, hit this on most runs after the first. This is #3329 and the rule f-trycua settled on in the #5048 review.

## What changed

- When a transport closes, a label it held and did not end with `end_session` is released. Another transport's next ordinary call starts a fresh episode on it, after the old episode's cleanup finishes.
- A label ended with `end_session` stays refused for ordinary calls. Once its owner has closed, any transport may `start_session` it.
- A closed transport's late calls, including `start_session` on its own labels, stay refused. The closed-transport set is pruned when the last tombstone naming an owner goes.

Salvaged from #5048 by @JohnnyVizz, with authorship kept on the main commit. It is ported onto current main, which has since gained idle revival (`IdleRevival`, dormant sessions). The later commits close gaps the cold reviews found once labels can move between transports. A closed owner could `start_session` its own old label. A transport close, a deferred end, and an owner-checked `end_session` ended sessions by label, so they could end an episode another transport had just claimed. Those ends now carry the owner they checked and leave any other owner's episode alone.

## Scope

Core session lifecycle (`cua-driver-core/src/session.rs`), the daemon's early refusal (`serve.rs`, `sdk_adapter.rs`), and one paragraph in `how-cua-driver-works.mdx`. The `start_session` description still says ordinary actions never revive ended names. That text is agent-facing contract (manifest, contract test), so it is left for a follow-up, as asked on #5048.

## Blast radius

All platforms, because the change is in core. While a label's owner transport is live, nothing changes. Revocation still fails closed through the runtime suspend latch. Size-limit reason: the port carries #5048's reviewed design whole, two new side sets and their pruning, so splitting it would leave a half rule.

## Verification

- `a_closed_transports_session_labels_are_reusable` (daemon socket, three transports) fails on main at the reuse step and passes here.
- A raw MCP script drove five consecutive `cua-driver mcp` processes on one label. Installed 0.44.0 refused the second process and the later `start_session`. This branch let the second process reuse the label, refused the ordinary call after an explicit `end_session`, and accepted `start_session`.
- Factory Droid on terra (`gpt-5.6-terra`), MCP only, with the daemon left running across runs: no `session has ended` refusals across consecutive runs that reused labels (`screen-report`, `calc-terra`, `textedit-terra-mcp2`).

risk: deep

Refs #3329

title: feat(cua-driver): connect Factory Droid over MCP at medium autonomy (CUA-628)
body:
## Why

Droid's documented MCP setup only worked at `droid exec --auto high`. Droid 1.6.0 rates a stdio MCP tool `low` when it declares `readOnlyHint` and `high` otherwise. So `launch_app`, `click`, `type_text` and even `start_session` stopped a run at default or `--auto medium` autonomy. The same actions run as shell `cua-driver call …` commands are rated `medium` by Droid itself. Droid honours a user-level `mcpAutonomyOverrides` map in `~/.factory/settings.json`, which is how a server's tools get a level other than its built-in rule.

## What changed

- `cua-driver connect` finds Factory Droid (`droid` on `PATH` or `~/.factory`), merges the `cua-driver` stdio server into `~/.factory/mcp.json`, and rates each tool without `readOnlyHint` `medium` under `mcpAutonomyOverrides["cua-driver"].tools`. It leaves `kill_app` at Droid's default and keeps any rating already there.
- `connect-your-agent.mdx` gets a Factory Droid row that documents MCP plus `connect --client droid` and `--auto medium` as the setup.
- The CLI reference text and `cli-specs/cua-driver.json` name Droid.

## Scope

Droid only. It does not change any tool's annotations, so other clients see the same `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` values. Droid has no `connect` CLI, so both files are merged as JSON, the same way Cursor's `mcp.json` is. A file that does not parse as JSON is never overwritten. An empty file is treated as missing, the same as Cursor's merge on main.

## Tradeoffs

Marking action tools `readOnlyHint` would have been wrong for every client. A blanket `defaultLevel: "medium"` for the server would also pull `kill_app` below `high`. Per-tool ratings written from the live tool inventory cover new tools on the next `connect` run.

## Verification

- `connect::tests` covers the Droid merge, keeping user ratings, a second run reporting already connected, invalid settings left untouched, and dry run writing nothing. The scoped repository checks and the cua-driver docs drift check pass.
- Factory Droid on terra (`gpt-5.6-terra`) with the config `connect --client droid` wrote, MCP only, at `--auto medium`: the screenshot, Calculator and TextEdit save tasks all ran their action tools with no autonomy refusal. On main the same tasks stopped at the first action tool. Failed runs looped on no-op shell calls, which is model behaviour, not a driver error.

Size-limit reason: the Droid merge needs a second config file (the autonomy ratings) next to the `mcp.json` merge Cursor already has.

title: fix(cua-driver): bound macOS off-Space window capture
body:
## Summary

A macOS window on another Space can take about 33 seconds to return a screenshot. A process sample showed the capture blocked in `SLSHWCaptureWindowListToIOSurfaceProxying` inside WindowServer's SkyLight call. The off-Space route invokes that call before ScreenCaptureKit.

Try the existing desktop-independent ScreenCaptureKit capture first on every Space, then `screencapture`, then SkyLight. Give each compatibility backend a three-second caller deadline. A stalled worker keeps its own permit until it returns, so retries cannot pile up behind the same backend and a stuck fallback does not prevent a later ScreenCaptureKit success.

## Related work

Refs #4996, which added the private backing-store fallback for off-Space windows that public APIs could not capture.

## Compatibility and risk

The change is internal to macOS window capture. It preserves the tool schemas, screenshot formats, consent check, and existing capture backends. It adds no application activation, window ordering, or Space-switching calls. When a fallback cannot finish within its deadline, the caller can proceed or receive an error with backend context. The deadline bounds the caller's wait because the synchronous system call itself may still be running.

## Validation

- All 20 macOS capture unit tests passed. They cover public success bypassing SkyLight on either Space, fallback on failure or empty output, and refusal of replacement workers until a timed-out worker exits.
- A separate public-API probe on macOS 26.5.1 captured an off-screen Notes window while a different application remained full-screen. Three stable captures took 80–85 ms in `SCScreenshotManager.captureImage` and 187–200 ms including enumeration and PNG encoding. The foreground app stayed the same in all 170 samples. These timings are from the standalone probe.
- Local `bin/ci` passed seven checks, including Clippy and 720 macOS unit tests plus two integration tests. The UniFFI binding check was skipped because the TypeScript npm dependencies could not be installed.
- The patched driver still needs canonical desktop validation across Space types and target apps before marking the PR ready.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] This change is internal and requires no RFC.
- [x] Tests and platform evidence are included, with the desktop validation gap recorded.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.

title: cua-driver: background click coords offset by window origin; AX fallback silently no-ops
body:
## Environment

- cua-driver 0.38.0 (daemon), macOS, main display 1728×1117 @2x, background delivery mode
- Target app: Microsoft Excel for Mac (also observed on Chrome)
- `get_window_state` screenshot is 1366×819 px for a window of 1365×818 pt — 1:1, so HiDPI scaling is not the cause

## Problem 1 — click coordinates are offset by the window origin

The screenshot returned by `get_window_state` maps 1:1 onto the window's points. But `click(x, y)` appears to add `window.bounds.origin` to values that are already window-local, so every click lands `(bounds.x, bounds.y)` further to the bottom-right than intended.

Measured with window bounds `x=200 y=157 w=1365 h=818`:

| passed | landed on |
|---|---|
| `(70, 280)` | `D13` |
| `(250, 280)` | `G13` |

D13's center is around (270, 437) and G13's around (450, 437) in screenshot pixels, so `passed ≈ target − bounds.origin` within roughly 10 px on both axes. Reproduced after moving the window to `x=149 y=209`: `(250, 300)` → `F17`, `(200, 150)` → `E8`.

Note the driver's own validation message treats the input as window-local ("window-local point (-74.9, 247.8) pt lies outside window 6123's 1365×818 pt frame"), yet delivery adds the origin again — so validation and delivery disagree about the coordinate space.

**Workaround that hits exactly:** pass `target_screenshot_px − window.bounds.origin`, recomputed whenever the window moves.

## Problem 2 — a top band of the window silently ignores clicks while still reporting success

Same window (`x=149 y=209`), x fixed at 200:

| passed | route reported | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `(200, 113)` | `PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX` | selection unchanged |
| `(200, 119)` | same | unchanged |
| `(200, 130)` | same | unchanged |
| `(200, 138)` | `Posted click ... synthetic_events` | `E7` |
| `(200, 150)` | `Posted click ... synthetic_events` | `E8` |
| `(500, 119)` | `PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX` | unchanged |

The band is horizontal and independent of x, covering roughly the top 135 pt of the window (the toolbar / formula-bar strip). The call still returns `ok: true` with `next_step: "verify_state"`, so an agent has no signal that nothing happened — the app state simply never changes.

Inference: the AX hit-test resolves the point in a different coordinate space than the synthetic-event path, so small window-local `y` values get matched against chrome/background elements instead of the content area.

## Why it matters

Agent loops cannot distinguish "clicked the wrong thing" from "click did nothing", so they keep retrying with slightly different pixels and burn turns without converging.

Suggested direction: use one window-local space for both validation and delivery (add the origin exactly once), and make the AX fallback fail loudly instead of returning success when it produces no state change.

title: [Bug]: macOS VM desktop stream fails when VideoToolbox rejects ConstrainedBaseline
body:
### Primary area

Other — cua-spacesd macOS desktop streaming

### Summary

The Cua Spaces desktop viewer receives no picture from a local macOS VM even though screenshot capture works. In the affected VM, VideoToolbox rejects the mandatory H.264 ConstrainedBaseline profile with status `-12902`, preventing the native H.264 encoder from initializing.

### Reproduction

1. Start a local Apple Silicon macOS VM using `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26` (guest macOS 26.5.2).
2. Ensure the in-guest Cua Spacesd app has Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions.
3. Open the VM's Desktop stream in Cua Spaces.
4. On the affected VM encoder, wait for the viewer timeout. Screenshot capture still succeeds, but the H.264 media session delivers no frames.

This was reproducible in the tested VM; whether all macOS VM encoder configurations are affected is unknown.

### Expected behavior

The desktop stream displays and updates when capture permissions are granted and an H.264 profile supported by the encoder is available.

### Actual behavior

The viewer reports:

```text
Could not connect to the desktop
No picture arrived from the desktop within 20 seconds.
```

`NativeEncoder::new(1024, 768, 30, Some(4_000), sink)` fails during profile configuration. The session exposes a generic `capture_failed` event rather than the underlying VideoToolbox status.

### Environment

- Component: cua-spacesd 0.7.0, deployed source commit `fca21937bc4e1420a23d544d11dbdf987f0266e6`.
- Guest: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64, local Lume VM.
- Image: `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26`.
- Relevant implementation: `libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/macos_h264.rs`.
- Source inspection of main at `6285c481d2d867eb954a6e6c5531ba8a88182832` shows the same mandatory ConstrainedBaseline profile selection. The original failure was reproduced on the deployed commit above.

### Evidence

Minimal error from an encoder-initialization regression test before the fix:

```text
desktop encoder initialization failed: Some("VTSessionSetProperty returned -12902")
```

During approximately 6.5-second media probes, raw BGRA capture delivered 34 frames while H.264 delivered 0 before the fix. Retrying `kVTProfileLevel_H264_Baseline_AutoLevel` after the ConstrainedBaseline rejection allowed H.264 initialization and streaming.

After installing a build with that fallback and granting permissions to its new signature, an H.264 probe after a VM restart received 11 frames (335647 bytes), including a keyframe at 1024×768. The native Cua Spaces management viewer displayed the guest desktop, reflected a newly launched application, and reconnected after hiding/showing the Desktop stream.

### Workaround and additional context

VNC remains usable. The tested code workaround preserves ConstrainedBaseline when supported and retries Baseline only when profile selection returns `-12900` (property not supported) or `-12902` (parameter error). It preserves other errors and reports both statuses if the fallback also fails.

This report is scoped to encoder initialization, rather than high-resolution capture or a backlog after encoding starts.

Proposed fix: https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7088

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): fall back to Baseline in macOS VMs
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: some macOS VM VideoToolbox encoders reject the required ConstrainedBaseline H.264 profile with `-12902`. The encoder never initializes, leaving the desktop viewer without a picture even though screenshot capture works.
- What changed: preserve ConstrainedBaseline when accepted; retry Baseline only for `kVTPropertyNotSupportedErr` (`-12900`) or `kVTParameterErr` (`-12902`). Preserve unrelated errors and include both statuses if the fallback fails. Add profile-selection coverage and a real encoder-initialization regression test.

## Related work

Fixes #7087

RFC: not required; this is a private macOS encoder implementation fix with no SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, permission, or architectural contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: restores H.264 desktop streaming on the affected macOS VM. Existing encoders that accept ConstrainedBaseline retain the same profile. No configuration or permission policy changes.
- Risk and rollback: fallback is restricted to two profile-setting error statuses. Baseline output was verified in the native viewer on the affected VM, but other hardware/macOS combinations need CI and maintainer coverage. Reverting this change restores the previous mandatory profile and its failure on that VM.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: on the deployed 0.7.0 source base, the new initialization regression failed with `VTSessionSetProperty returned -12902` before the change. With the fix, all 105 desktop-library tests passed, including real encoding, keyframe recovery, resize, and the new fallback tests. `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-spacesd-desktop --lib --no-deps` completed with existing dependency/platform warnings.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS 26.5.2 arm64 VM; after replacing the in-guest daemon and regranting permissions for the locally signed build, an H.264 probe received 11 frames/335647 bytes in approximately 6.5 seconds after VM restart. The native viewer displayed the desktop, updated when an application launched, and reconnected after hiding/showing the stream.
- Upstream-base validation: The patch has been reapplied to main at `6285c481d2d867eb954a6e6c5531ba8a88182832`, preserving its existing frame-completion/backlog fix. On the resulting PR source (`6bd734c3ee3f88615ee494ff0b961ac105c6117c`), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --locked -p cua-spacesd-desktop --lib` (109 passed, 0 failed), and `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-spacesd-desktop --lib --no-deps` all completed successfully in the VM. title: fix(release): count Cua Spaces additional-paths commits in Release Please
body:
## Why

Release Please logged "Considering: 0 commits" for cua-spaces, so no 0.24.1 release PR opened and the Windows signing fix (#7038) has not shipped. The pinned engine (release-please 17.3.0, and every later 17.x) has no `additional-paths` option. It drops the key while parsing the config, so only `apps/cua-spaces-macos` commits ever counted. That is why #7056 had no effect and was reverted in #7062. This PR adds the option to the pinned engine in a preload and opens release PRs through it.

## What changed

- `.github/scripts/release_please_additional_paths.cjs` wraps the engine's commit split: a commit that touches a package's `additional-paths` also counts for that package, in history order. It reads the target branch's config (the same copy the engine reads), refuses any engine other than 17.3.0, and refuses `additional-paths` combined with `exclude-paths`. `.github/scripts/release_please.sh` checks the npm integrity and runs the CLI with it.
- `release-please.yml`: the action now only tags (`skip-github-pull-request: true`). Automatic and targeted release PRs both go through `release_please.sh`. `apps/cua-spaces-desktop` joins the cua-spaces `additional-paths`.
- The release notes, auto-merge staleness and branch rebase checks count the additional paths too, so the notes and freshness checks match the changelog.

## Scope

Covers which commits count toward cua-spaces. Out of scope: dispatching or merging any release, and upstreaming the option (googleapis/release-please#2534 proposes the same behaviour). Delete the preload once the pinned engine supports the key.

## Tradeoffs

- A root `.` package or per-commit bot PRs into `apps/cua-spaces-macos` would avoid the preload. The first renames the manifest key every release tool reads. The second adds a PR per commit, like the bundle-cua bot PRs that already go stale.
- The preload patches one engine method. The version check makes a future engine bump fail loudly instead of silently dropping the option again.

## Blast Radius

Every Release Please component goes through the new release-PR step. A dry run of the whole repo with and without the preload gives byte-identical release PRs for cua-driver-rs, sandbox, cua-sdk, cua-spacesd and bench. Only cua-spaces changes. Tagging still runs in the pinned action, behind the existing tag guard.

## Verification

- Live `release-pr --dry-run` of all components against trycua/cua. Unpatched engine on main: cua-spaces "Considering: 0 commits", 5 PRs. Patched engine reading this branch's config: cua-spaces "Considering: 25 commits", a 0.25.0 PR whose changelog lists #7038, #7055, #6945 and 7 more, and the other 5 PRs are unchanged. The targeted dispatch path (`--path=apps/cua-spaces-macos --release-as=0.24.1`) goes from 0 PRs to one 0.24.1 PR.
- `release_please_spaces_preview.cjs` with an Electron, web and core commit fails on the test commit and passes at the head. The other four engine previews pass.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci` affected mode (actionlint, `.github/scripts` tests, headers, workflow sync) passed.

title: Windows: get_window_state/get_desktop_state return stale frames for fullscreen flip-model Direct3D windows
body:
### Environment

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (build 19045.6466)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060, driver 32.0.16.1714
- Display: single 2560x1440 monitor, 125% Windows scaling
- cua-driver: `@trycua/cua-driver` on Windows; source verified against `main` @ 6285c48 (the same capture code is present there)
- Target: a Unity game using a fullscreen, flip-model Direct3D 11 swap chain (`ABYA_PB.exe`, window rect 0,0,2560,1440)

### Summary

On Windows, `get_window_state`, `get_desktop_state` and `zoom` return stale frames for a fullscreen Direct3D game window. The screenshot shows an older camera position / UI than what is actually on screen (for example, the current dialogue line and the current plugin HUD are missing). Capturing the same screen at the same moment with DXGI Desktop Duplication (for example `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "ddagrab=output_idx=0:framerate=1" -vf "hwdownload,format=bgra" -frames:v 1`) shows the current frame, so the display output itself is up to date.

The stale frame is intermittent: while a scene is static both paths often agree, and while the game is changing (camera movement, scene transitions, plugin UI toggling) the capture surfaces keep returning an older frame for a while.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch a fullscreen, flip-model Direct3D game on Windows (Unity/Unreal; fullscreen exclusive or borderless fullscreen both present this way).
2. Call `get_window_state` for the game window (or `get_desktop_state`, or `zoom`) repeatedly while the scene changes.
3. Compare the returned screenshot with the actual screen / a DXGI Desktop Duplication capture of the same display: the CUA screenshot is stale.

### Root cause

`platform-windows/src/capture.rs` captures ordinary (non-XAML) windows with `PrintWindow(hwnd, ..., PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` and falls back to a `BitBlt` from the window DC. A fullscreen, flip-model Direct3D swap chain is scanned out directly by the display controller instead of being composed into the window's DWM redirection surface; DWM only holds the last composed copy. `PrintWindow` / window-DC `BitBlt` then return that stale copy while the display keeps updating. `Windows.Graphics.Capture` was only used for XAML/DirectComposition targets and for mostly-black frames, and there was no DXGI Desktop Duplication path. `screenshot_display_bytes` had the same problem: it is GDI-only (`GetDC(NULL)` + `BitBlt`), so `get_desktop_state` can also return a stale desktop image.

While implementing the fix we also found that the first frame a fresh `IDXGIOutputDuplication` hands out is an unpopulated placeholder: `LastPresentTime == 0`, `AccumulatedFrames == 0`, and the desktop image is all-zero. It has to be skipped (released) and a real presented frame awaited, otherwise the very first capture is a blank image.

### Evidence

A standalone probe calls, in one process and milliseconds apart, (a) the driver's current window-capture entry point and (b) a replica of the current `PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` + `GetDIBits` path. A DXGI Desktop Duplication capture of the same display (ffmpeg `ddagrab`) is used as ground truth.

![game before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yingyu4451/cua/9ac4d2d143cf494e2b983d38608eef565eb7a19a/evidence/game-before-after.png)

Game-only evidence below: both frames are captures of the same Unity game window taken milliseconds apart. In this run the legacy PrintWindow path returned a stale frame - the in-game bottom dialogue and the plugin HUD overlay were missing - while Desktop Duplication returned the live frame including the bottom dialogue line and the HUD. 91.2% of sampled pixels differ (mean absolute RGB diff 64.17). In another run the same probe had PrintWindow return an old game scene while the display had already moved on.

- [before - stale game frame (old path)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yingyu4451/cua/9ac4d2d143cf494e2b983d38608eef565eb7a19a/evidence/game-before-stale.png)
- [after - live game frame (duplication path)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yingyu4451/cua/9ac4d2d143cf494e2b983d38608eef565eb7a19a/evidence/game-after-live.png)
- [reference - ffmpeg ddagrab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yingyu4451/cua/e7ba4f04d6e3bdb14af0a4a016169c291963c6cc/evidence/reference-ffmpeg-ddagra.png)

### Fix

Fixed in the pull request linked from this issue: a new `platform-windows/src/dxgi_duplication.rs` captures the real display image for the monitor covered by a window, and the window/display capture paths use it first, with the existing PrintWindow / WGC / BitBlt ladder kept as the fallback. The initial unpopulated frame is skipped. With the fix the captured frame matches the Desktop Duplication ground truth for the same window.

### Additional observation (not addressed here)

On the reporter's machine the installed npm build also returned `capture binding is invalid` when `screenshot_out_file` was used. That is a separate capture-publication path (`_session_id` binding); `main` binds a transport session for CLI calls, so this may be version-specific and is not part of the PR above.

title: fix(cua-driver): capture fullscreen flip-model Direct3D windows via DXGI Desktop Duplication
body:
## Summary

Fixes #7091.

On Windows, window and desktop capture relied on PrintWindow and GDI BitBlt. For a fullscreen, flip-model Direct3D swap chain (the presentation mode Unity/Unreal games use) the display is scanned out directly by the display controller and DWM only keeps the last composed copy, so those paths can return a stale frame while the screen keeps updating. This PR adds a DXGI Desktop Duplication fast path.

- **New `platform-windows/src/dxgi_duplication.rs`**: captures the display output covered by a window (D3D11 device created on the same adapter, staging texture readback, identity-rotation outputs only, acquisition retried on `DXGI_ERROR_WAIT_TIMEOUT` within a 1 s budget).
- **Window capture** (`screenshot_window_bytes_with_occlusion_unsafe`): if the window is unoccluded and fully covers one monitor, capture the displayed frame through duplication and crop it to the window's screen rectangle. Returns the same `FrameGeometry` as the existing paths, so click-target mapping and `zoom` keep working.
- **Display capture** (`screenshot_display_bytes`): prefer duplication for the primary output (only used when its dimensions match the screen metrics), then fall back to the existing GDI body.
- Everything else — other windows, occluded windows, a window that does not fully cover a monitor, rotated output, protected/exclusive content, expired/duplicated outputs, remote sessions — still goes through the existing PrintWindow / WGC / BitBlt ladder unchanged, including the CUA-542 XAML routing.
- The first frame a fresh `IDXGIOutputDuplication` hands out is an unpopulated placeholder (`LastPresentTime == 0`, all-zero desktop image). It is released and skipped; a real presented frame is awaited within the budget. A desktop that does not present falls back to the existing ladder instead of returning a blank frame.

## Why this fixes the report

The reporter's Unity game (2560x1440 fullscreen flip-model D3D 11) returned an older camera position/UI from `get_window_state`, while a DXGI Desktop Duplication capture of the same display showed the current frame. PrintWindow was reading a frozen DWM copy. With this change the same probe now matches the duplication ground truth.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt -p platform-windows` — clean
- `cargo check -p platform-windows` — passes
- `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib dxgi_duplication` — 5 passed (rect-coverage math only, hermetic; no real windows/input/clipboard)
- Runtime verification: Windows 10 22H2, NVIDIA RTX 5060, 2560x1440 Unity game.
  - Duplicated capture of the game window matches an ffmpeg `ddagrab` reference of the same display (mean absolute RGB diff 0.46/255 on a 4-px grid in a static scene).
  - The legacy PrintWindow path returned a stale frame in the same scenario (91.2% of sampled pixels differed), including the unpopulated-HUD sample below.
  - The initial unpopulated duplication frame was also caught and skipped in isolation (fresh duplication: first frame all-zero with `LastPresentTime == 0`; next frame carried the real image).

Game-only evidence (both frames are the same Unity game window, milliseconds apart): the old path returns a stale frame without the in-game bottom dialogue or HUD; the duplication path returns the live frame with both.

![game before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yingyu4451/cua/9ac4d2d143cf494e2b983d38608eef565eb7a19a/evidence/game-before-after.png)

- [before - stale game frame (old path)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yingyu4451/cua/9ac4d2d143cf494e2b983d38608eef565eb7a19a/evidence/game-before-stale.png)
- [after - live game frame (duplication path)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yingyu4451/cua/9ac4d2d143cf494e2b983d38608eef565eb7a19a/evidence/game-after-live.png)

## Notes / limits

- Only identity-rotation outputs are captured through duplication; rotated displays keep the old ladder.
- An occluded window is not captured from the desktop image (so unrelated windows are not included); it keeps the old ladder.
- The fast path is best-effort: every error is logged at debug level and falls through to the existing capture code, so behavior only changes for windows where PrintWindow is known to be unreliable.
- Full repo CI (`bin/ci`) was not run from this checkout (sparse checkout); the three commands above are the local checks.

title: ci(spaces): regenerate stale generated bindings on the PR branch
body:
Closes CUA-3953 (under CUA-3856).

**Problem.** Any FFI change on main made every open Spaces PR fail "SwiftUI and Electron bindings are up to date", and someone regenerated them by hand on each PR (twice in 12 hours, 5 PRs each time).

**Choice: (b), auto-fix on the PR branch.**
- (a) Not committing generated bindings: the Swift package and the Electron shell build without cargo (about 280k generated lines are consumed by Xcode and pnpm builds and several jobs with no Rust toolchain). Making each consumer build the Rust library and run uniffi would add a 20 to 60 minute cold build to every one of them and make release builds depend on a toolchain they do not have today.
- (c) A merge queue only reports the staleness at the end; it does not remove the manual step.
- (b) fixes the whole class: the bindings stay committed and reproducible, and CI keeps them current.

**What changes.** In `ci-cua-spaces-macos.yml`, on a pull request from this repository only, the `core` (FFI mirrors) and `bindings` (Swift and Electron) jobs regenerate instead of checking, then a new composite action `.github/actions/push-generated` commits the generated files to the PR branch as the release GitHub App (so CI restarts on the new head; a GITHUB_TOKEN push would not). The job passes, and the next run on the new head is a no-op. Main, the merge queue and fork PRs keep the strict `--check`, as does `bin/ci` locally (`bin/ci --verify-sync` still passes). Only generated paths are committed, overwritten from the merged result. Release builds are unchanged.

**Proof.** Locally: actionlint and `bin/ci --quick` pass. End-to-end proof (change one FFI type on a scratch branch, watch the bot commit) needs the macOS runners and the release app secrets, so it runs on CI.

For users: faster merges, no hand regeneration.

title: fix(auth): redact tokens in Debug output (#7071)
body:
Fixes #7071. cc @ddupont808 (owner of the issue; fixed here to close the exposure quickly, please review).

## What changed

`Credentials` in `cua_auth` used a derived `Debug`, so `{:?}` printed the access, refresh and ID tokens in full. Any log line, error or panic message that formatted a `Credentials` value would have included them.

- `Credentials` now has a manual `Debug` that prints `<redacted>` for `access_token`, `refresh_token` and `id_token`. Expiry, token type and scope still print, so logs stay useful. Serialization (what the credential store reads and writes) is unchanged.
- The same fix is applied to 57 other structs in `libs/cua` that hold bearer tokens, passwords, S3 secret keys, API keys or machine tokens and derived `Debug` (for example the Spaces daemon/relay registrations, VM/VNC/SSH endpoints, the compat layer's stored keys and sandbox records, the drive storage updates, and the CLI/SDK create options). Field names, types and serde behaviour are unchanged; only the `Debug` output differs.
- New test `credentials_debug_redacts_every_token` asserts that neither `{:?}` nor `{:#?}` contains any token value.

Not changed: fields that are identifiers rather than secrets (cache keys, pairing and join codes, public keys), and `Serialize` impls, which are needed to persist and send these values.

## Were tokens logged?

I found no place in this repo that formats `Credentials` with `{:?}` or `?creds` in a log macro, and no local log contains a formatted `Credentials` value. I could not inspect production logs or Sentry from here, so I can't rule it out for builds that format one of these structs through a path I could not grep (for example an `assert_eq!` or `unwrap_err()` message in a panic). `cua-crash` scrubs home paths, emails and URL credentials before sending events but not token strings. Follow-up: search Sentry and log storage for JWT-shaped strings and rotate if any are found.

## Checks

- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: green.
- clippy `-D warnings` (workspace, all targets) and `cargo test -p cua-auth` run on g17-4; results are in the CI checks below.

title: fix(crash): scrub tokens before sending to Sentry
body:
Follow-up to #7097 (issue #7071).

The crash reporters already clear messages, vars and breadcrumbs and scrub home paths and emails in `before_send`. They did not redact token-shaped strings left in tags, extra fields, frame names and similar. This adds that to the shared text scrub in each reporter.

Redacted as `[redacted]`:
- JWT-shaped strings
- `Bearer <credential>`
- AWS access key ids (AKIA, ASIA and the other IAM id prefixes)
- long base64/hex values after `token`, `key`, `secret` (any prefix, `=` or `:`) and `password`

Covers `cua-crash` (Rust), the Electron main process, the web app, and the Swift app (`CrashReporting.swift`, which also sets `beforeBreadcrumb` to drop breadcrumbs). Tests added in all four. Rust clippy and tests ran on g17-4; both TS suites pass; Swift tests are left to CI.

What changed for users: crash reports can no longer carry a session token or cloud key by accident.

title: fix(cua-driver): honour a caller-supplied timeout for browser_download
body:
## Problem

`browser_download` waited a hardcoded 30 seconds for an approved download:

```rust
const DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
```

Any legitimate download slower than that returned `browser_action_unavailable` — and removed the partial file — while the `.crdownload` was still growing. There was no input that could move the deadline.

Fixes #6729.

## Change

One file, `cua-driver-core/src/browser/download.rs`:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` (30s, fixed) | `DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s) + `MAX_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` (600s) |
| no `timeout_ms` input | optional `timeout_ms` (integer, 1–600000) |
| refusal always said "30 seconds" | refusal reports the deadline actually in effect |

The deadline is resolved once, next to the other argument validation, before any lock is taken:

```rust
let timeout = match resolve_download_timeout(&args) {
    Ok(timeout) => timeout,
    Err(error) => return error,
};
```

## Two decisions worth reviewing

**Out-of-range and wrong-typed values are refused, not clamped or defaulted.** A caller that asked for an hour should learn the cap rather than silently get ten minutes and fail again on a deadline it never set. For the same reason the resolver reads the raw JSON instead of `opt_u64`, which reports a wrong-typed field as *absent* — a `timeout_ms: "60000"` string silently falling back to 30s would recreate exactly the bug this parameter removes. The comment in the code says so, so the choice is not mistaken for an oversight later.

**The cap is 600s, not unlimited.** `browser_download_gate()` is a process-wide mutex, so an unbounded deadline lets one slow download hold off every other exact-tab download for as long as the caller likes.

## Not in this PR

The issue also suggests extending the deadline while `Browser.downloadProgress` reports `receivedBytes` increasing. That is a separate behaviour change on the same call — a progress heuristic that needs its own failure modes thought through (stalled downloads, restarted transfers) — so it reads better as its own review than bolted onto a parameter addition.

## Validation

```
$ cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib --no-default-features download::
running 11 tests
test browser::download::tests::timeout_defaults_when_the_caller_does_not_ask_for_one ... ok
test browser::download::tests::timeout_honours_a_caller_override ... ok
test browser::download::tests::timeout_accepts_the_cap_and_refuses_beyond_it ... ok
test browser::download::tests::timeout_refuses_a_value_of_the_wrong_type ... ok
test browser::download::tests::timeout_is_described_in_the_units_it_was_set_in ... ok
... plus the 6 pre-existing download tests
test result: ok. 11 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo fmt -p cua-driver-core -- --check   # clean
$ cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --lib --no-default-features   # clean
```

**Known gap, stated rather than hidden:** those runs used `--no-default-features`, which drops `rego`. This machine has no Visual Studio Spectre-mitigated libraries, and `regorus` declares `msvc_spectre_libs` with the `error` feature, so its build script panics before anything compiles. That is an environment limitation on my side, not a property of this change — `download.rs` is not feature-gated, and CI will be the first full-feature build.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse macOS type_text keys when the target can't hold keyboard focus
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `type_text` aimed at a control that does not take keyboard focus types the text twice into whatever does hold focus. Reproduced in Chrome: `type_text` with `element_index` on the "Bookmark this tab" button wrote the URL twice into the address bar next to it (`…/type.html?x=1127.0.0.1:8765/type.html?x=1`) and answered `delivered 0 of 28`, in 3 of 3 runs on the 0.45.2 nightly. 0.37.0 typed it once but gave the same `delivered 0` answer, which invites the caller to send it again.
- Cause: when the AX write does not land, the fallback posts keystrokes to the process, so they reach the app's focused element, not the target. The read-back then reads the target, sees it unchanged, and counts 0 delivered. Since #6884 a batched send with a short read-back retypes the "missing" tail, here the whole text, one paced key at a time.
- What changed: before posting any key, `cgevent_type_verified` focuses the explicit target and confirms it holds keyboard focus, using `press_key`'s `with_confirmed_key_focus` (focus re-applied for up to 200 ms, `element_has_keyboard_focus` by either read-back). If focus can't be confirmed, nothing is typed and the call is refused with the same result as `press_key`: `target_focus_unconfirmed`, effect `"refused"`, `dispatched: false`. Without an explicit target nothing changes. The helper and its refusal mapping are now `pub(super)` in `press_key.rs` and shared; the tool description and generated reference mention the refusal.
- Review round 1 changed the approach. The first version checked focus after the keys were posted and answered "unverifiable". The text still landed once in the wrong field, and the generic "re-call with foreground" advice then typed it there a second time through the foreground rung.

## Related work

Refs: no upstream issue. Follows #6884.

RFC: not required. No protocol change; it reuses `press_key`'s existing `target_focus_unconfirmed` refusal.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: typing at a control that cannot hold keyboard focus is now refused with nothing typed, instead of typing into the focused field and answering "delivered 0". Targets that hold focus (native fields, the address bar, page fields) behave as before.
- Risk: an app that takes the keys but reports neither app focus (`AXFocusedUIElement`) nor the element's `AXFocused` is now refused. Reviewer checked live that background TextEdit reports its text area as focused. Inactive Chrome, VS Code, Slack, Notion and Terminal return no `AXFocusedUIElement`, so for them the element's own `AXFocused` decides, the same dependency `press_key` already has. Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Local `bin/ci` on 930e237c91: 11/11 passed (rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings` and unit tests for platform-macos, generated reference, UniFFI bindings, headers, docs checks). `bin/ci --signoff` can't post from this account (no write access to trycua/cua); for this fork PR ci-gate needs a green "CI: Quick", which waits for a maintainer to approve the workflow runs.
- Unit tests: the shared contract (refuse without dispatch, retry focus, dispatch once when confirmed) is owned by `press_key`'s existing `with_confirmed_key_focus` tests. No unit test fails if the call in `type_text` is removed; that needs the live run below.
- Live (macOS 26, Chrome, daemon built from the **first** version of this change, local test page). Not re-run on 930e237c91 yet; the expected new result for the button row is "refused, nothing typed":

  | `type_text` target | nightly 0.45.2 | first version (130842e7a6) |

  | address bar | typed once, confirmed | typed once, confirmed |
  | page `<textarea>` | typed once, unverifiable (web) | typed once, unverifiable (web) |

- Known gaps or CI still required: the live rows above (plus a background-mode button row) on 930e237c91; Windows and Linux CI (no change there).

title: [Feature]: open a tab in a bound browser window without activating it
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

An agent drives the user's own Chrome or Edge through the browser tools (`browser_prepare` with `existing_profile`, then `get_browser_state`, `browser_click`, `browser_navigate`). No tool opens a new tab: `browser_navigate` requires a `tab_id` and replaces the page the user may be reading.

The host's only option is relaunching the browser executable with the URL. Chromium's launcher calls `AllowSetForegroundWindow` on the running instance before handing the URL over (`chrome/browser/win/chrome_process_finder.cc`), so the browser jumps in front of the user's app. Every other browser action stays in the background; this one does not.

Talking to the DevTools port directly (`PUT /json/new`) avoids the foreground change, but bypasses the driver's consent model, and the port is not on the command line when the driver enabled remote debugging itself during `existing_profile` setup.

### Desired outcome

A tool (e.g. `browser_new_tab {target_id, url}`), or `browser_navigate` without `tab_id`, that creates a tab in the bound window over the driver's existing CDP connection (`Target.createTarget` with `background: true`, in the bound window) and returns the new `tab_id`. The contract's cursor classification already lists a `browser_new_tab` name.

### Current workaround

Relaunch the browser executable with its own flags and the URL, then poll `get_browser_state` for the new tab. The browser takes the foreground.

### Affected components and platforms

cua-driver 0.44.0 browser tools; seen on Windows 11 with Edge, applies to every platform.

### Alternatives and prior art

`launch_app` with `urls` (#5987) also opens in the front window and activates it.

title: [Feature]: tie a standalone serve daemon's life to its host (stdin EOF or --owner-pid)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

A host app starts `cua-driver serve` (directly or through a CLI wrapper) for its agent runs. When the host crashes or is killed, the daemon keeps running: it keeps its socket or named pipe, its pid file, and any browser DevTools connection it held. The idle sweep ends sessions after five minutes, but the process stays.

The driver already has the mechanism: `CUA_DRIVER_PARENT_LIVENESS_STDIN=1` makes `serve` shut down on stdin EOF (`wait_for_parent_stdin_eof` in `serve.rs`). `parent_liveness_stdin_enabled()` honours it only in embedded mode (`CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED`), so a standalone daemon cannot use it.

### Desired outcome

One of:
- `serve --exit-on-stdin-eof` (or the existing env var honoured outside embedded mode): shut down as `shutdown` does, sessions ended, when stdin closes.
- `serve --owner-pid PID`: the same when that process exits.

### Current workaround

The host stops the daemon on clean exit. After a crash, the next start finds the stale daemon and reuses it. A wrapper process that holds a pipe from the host and stops the daemon on EOF works, but every host reimplements it.

### Affected components and platforms

`cua-driver serve` 0.44.0, all platforms; most visible on Windows, where no process group ties the daemon to the host.

### Alternatives and prior art

#3278 (embedded host parity) keeps parent-liveness for embedded hosts.

title: [Feature]: key chords to a bound browser tab through DevTools on Windows
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On Windows, `hotkey` and `press_key` to a Chromium window (`Chrome_WidgetWin_1`) that is not in front are refused `background_unavailable`: Chromium reads modifier state live, so a posted chord does nothing. In 0.44.0 a single key (`F5`) is refused too. The only way to send `ctrl+a`, `ctrl+z`, `ctrl+f` or `F5` to a page is `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, which raises the browser over the user's app.

When the window is already bound through the browser tools, the driver holds a DevTools connection that could deliver these keys without touching the foreground. `browser_type` with `mode: "keystrokes"` sends characters but no modifiers.

### Desired outcome

For a bound tab, keys and chords reach the page through `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` with modifiers: a `browser_hotkey {target_id, tab_id, keys}` tool, or chords accepted by `browser_type` in `keystrokes` mode. Browser-level shortcuts DevTools cannot trigger (`ctrl+t`, `ctrl+w`) could be refused with a `next_call` naming their `Target` equivalents.

### Current workaround

`hotkey` with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`: visible to the user and racy with their input.

### Affected components and platforms

cua-driver 0.44.0, Windows (`platform-windows/src/tools/hotkey.rs`); the browser tool would help every platform.

### Alternatives and prior art

The contract's cursor classification already lists `browser_hotkey` and `browser_press_key` names.

title: fix(spaces-desktop): resolve the web app's i18n dependencies in the Electron build
body:
Fixes the Cua Spaces Electron release builds (linux and windows, x64 and arm64), which failed in typecheck with `Cannot find module 'i18next'`, `'i18next-icu'` and `'react-i18next'`.

**Cause:** #7022 added i18n to `apps/cua-spaces-web`. The Electron shell imports web sources (`../cua-spaces-web/src/lib/messages.ts` now pulls in `src/i18n`), and the release build installs only the shell, so those packages could not resolve. PR CI installs both apps, so it passed.

**Fix**
- The shell declares i18next, i18next-icu, intl-messageformat, react-i18next and react (the same versions as the web lockfile), with the lockfile updated.
- `tsconfig.json` maps bare imports to the shell's own `node_modules` (`paths: { "*": ["./node_modules/*"] }`), so web sources resolve there, in typecheck and in the tsdown bundle.
- New CI job `desktop-standalone` installs only the shell and runs `pnpm build`, as the release build does. The next web dependency that the shell reaches now fails in its PR, with the missing package named.

**Checked on g17-4** with the web app not installed: `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` (tsdown plus channel check) pass; `electron-builder --linux dir --x64` runs through packaging up to the native-layer check, which needs the prebuilt natives from CI.

For users: the Cua Spaces desktop app for Windows and Linux ships again.

title: feat(spaces): one storage API, configurable locations, caps and clean uninstall (CUA-3813)
body:
Part of CUA-3813 (keep user state clean). Phase 1: nothing moves on disk by default; every storage location goes through one API and the large ones become configurable. The move to OS-standard folders and the migration are phase 2 (separate PR after review).

## What changes
- `cua_home::storage`: one answer to "where does Cua keep X" by kind (config, data, cache, logs, runtimes, images, trajectories, keys). Order: per-kind env var (`CUA_RUNTIMES_DIR`, `CUA_IMAGES_DIR`, `CUA_CACHE_DIR`, `CUA_LOGS_DIR`, `CUA_TRAJECTORIES_DIR`), then `$CUA_HOME/storage.toml`, then today's default.
- Validation (full path, writable, free space, no overlap), a copy-verify-switch move that is resumable and never deletes, refuses while the daemon runs, and a remove of the old copy that only works on a folder marked by a move and not in use.
- Daemon log, image cache, built-in Linux and Lume runtimes, trajectories and the icon, thumbnail and install caches ask the API.
- `cua storage` (show, check, set --move, reset, remove).
- `cua cache` lists runtimes per version (VM disks are never evicted) and counts downloaded Linux images as evictable cache.
- Caps: trajectories 30 days and 2 GiB (oldest first, never a session in use), Sparkle downloads cleared after an update and capped at 200 MiB; daemon.log already rotates.
- Settings, Advanced: a Storage group (sizes, Change..., Remove... with confirms, Uninstall... with a Keychain checkbox, off by default). Mac app only; Electron and Tauri answer "unsupported" and hide it.
- `uninstall.sh`: `--keep-keychain`, `--wait-for-pid`, Sparkle staging and the stray test preference files. The Local bundle does not ship it (it would remove the released app) and a bundle check enforces that.
- Swift tests use unique UserDefaults suites removed at exit.

## What is and is not relocatable (honest list, CUA-3969 tracks the rest)
Moves with a folder change: the built-in Linux runtime (its computers' disks, Colima and Lima, downloaded Linux images), the built-in Lume binary, the image cache, icons, thumbnails and install downloads, the daemon log and the cua-driver install log, trajectories.
Stays where it is, and `cua storage` and Settings say so: macOS computer disks (`~/.lume`), QEMU, microVM and other VM disks (`<home>/vmm`), build outputs, job caches, the Volume block cache, helper logs (`host/driver.log`, Lume `serve.log`, cua-driver log, `~/Library/Logs/cua-spacesd*`), `cua do` screenshots, `~/.cua-driver`.
Environment variables (`CUA_*_DIR`) are seen only by processes started from that shell, not by the app, its LaunchAgent or the host service; `storage.toml` is the supported way. `cua storage` shows where each kind comes from (default, settings or environment).

## Audit fixes
- `cua storage remove` (and Settings, Remove old copy) follows the same rule: only Cua's own entries go. A move copies only Cua's own entries and warns about unrecognised files in the current or new folder; a target that contains the current folder is refused.
- A folder in use can never be removed (live folders, their parents and children, symlinks resolved, folders a running process uses); the audit's reset-then-remove repro is a test.
- A move is refused while any process runs from the folder, uses the real (logical) size off APFS, refuses FAT32 for big files, rejects runtimes paths over the 103-byte socket limit, and `check` removes the folders it created.
- `uninstall.sh` and `uninstall.ps1` read `storage.toml` and the five variables, list relocated folders, remove cache and logs (unless keep-data) and runtimes, images and trajectories only with delete-spaces, and remove only the entries Cua itself writes for that kind (runtimes: linux, lume; images: blobs, disks, rootfs, refs; cache: icons, installables, thumbnails; logs: *.log; trajectories: session folders). In a folder Cua did not create (no created-by marker: pointed at by hand, an environment variable, or `set` without `--move`) nothing is deleted at all, whatever the entries are called; Cua only lists what it would have removed. A person's own files in other folders are named and left alone, and the folder goes only when nothing else is in it. Relocated folders that a program still uses are skipped with the reason (Cua's own Lima/QEMU/lume programs are asked to stop first). The in-app Uninstall button was not tested: Local hides it and it needs a Stable-channel build. `storage.toml` is removed (the kept lines say how to point Cua back after a reinstall). Plain uninstall no longer removes `<home>/runtimes` (it holds Linux computers' disks). The `.ps1` change is not run here (no PowerShell on this Mac); CI's Windows lane covers it.
- The usage summary counts every relocated folder; free space is the least on any volume Cua writes to; the low-disk checks and preflight watch the runtimes and images volumes.

## Safety test (cua.local, clone of a real 128 GB ~/.cua)
- Old nightly `cua` 0.12.1 and this build's `cua` 0.18.0 list the same computers; `cua storage`/`cache du` ran with zero file changes (name, size, hash diff of 36,161 files).
- Move: refused while a daemon is alive; on a home without one, 11.9 GiB moved, repeat is a no-op, old copy kept, old build on the same home still works, old copy removed only after confirm. Bugs found there are fixed in this PR.
- Not tested: Keychain items (never touched by this change), the Sparkle trim at runtime, the in-app Uninstall end to end (only the script, via its fake-command python tests).

## Checks
- `cargo test -p cua-home --lib`, `-p cua-disk --lib --test gc`, `scripts/install/tests/test_uninstall.py`, web vitest for the bridge/coverage/i18n, `bin/ci --quick`.
