title: fix(cua-spacesd-doctor): wait for the form's entry focus before typing (replaces the #7290 retry)
body:
Plain words: the Windows image check that types into the form stopped failing the whole cua-spacesd image release at random, because it now waits until the form is really ready for typing instead of retrying after a failure.

## Root cause

The `input.type` doctor check typed as soon as `ActivateWindow` and a click on the Name entry had returned. On the Windows image the form is a PowerShell/WinForms process whose UI thread applies the focus change (and runs slow script-block handlers) after those calls return, so the first keystrokes reach a control that does not hold keyboard focus yet. The driver's report is clean in every case (`Typed 6 character(s)`) because `SendInput` and the drain sentinel both succeed; the loss happens inside the form.

Evidence from `windows / image` doctor logs of `cd-images-spacesd-release`:

| run | result of `input.type` |
| --- | --- |
| 42866618402 (v0.15.0) | fail: entry never changed, the form saw 1 key press (the drain sentinel) |
| 42325506448 | fail: entry read `ctor`, the first two characters (`do`) were lost; no retry would have helped |
| 42313668217, 42337644226, 42394653248, 42415532963, 42614588397, 42684840041, 42842043415, 42895898819 | pass |

The second failure shows the retry-once stopgap from #7290 was incomplete: it only retried when no `entry_changed` arrived, so a partly lost string still failed.

## Fix

- The form fixtures (Windows `form.ps1`, Linux `form.py`) log `widget_focus` records when the Name entry gains or loses keyboard focus and say `focus_events: true` in their `ready` record. The Windows form also makes the entry its active control when shown.
- The doctor waits for that ready signal: the latest `widget_focus` for Name is `focused: true`, then a Backspace probe (harmless on the empty entry) must come back as a key press with the entry focused. That proves focus is in place and the form's thread is draining input. Only then does it type.
- The retry from #7290 is removed. A form without `focus_events` (an older image) falls back to the window-focus check the doctor already did.
- A failure to become ready says which focus records the form logged.

## Tests

Unit tests for the focus-record parsing and the probe matcher (`entry_ready_tests`). `cargo test -p cua-spacesd-doctor --lib` (49 pass) and `clippy -D warnings` are clean on a Mac. The end-to-end proof is the next `windows / image` job; it needs the image workflow to run on this branch.

title: ci: raise the open-files limit before every script that runs cargo test
body:
Plain words: cua-spaces tests no longer fail with "Too many open files" on a Mac that still has the default shell limit of 256.

## Root cause

macOS shells start with a soft open-files limit of 256. The cua-spaces test binaries (`host_spaces`, `scale`, `relay_publish`, the cua-compat chaos suite) open more than that, so on such a Mac they fail for no code reason. `bin/ci` already raised the limit for its own children, but the many scripts that run `cargo test` directly (E2E runners, image gates, the macOS and Linux driver E2E scripts) did not.

## Fix

- Every tracked shell script that runs `cargo test` or `cargo nextest` (27 of them) carries one canonical line after its `set -e...` that raises the soft limit to 10240, never lowers a higher limit, falls back to the hard limit, and cannot abort a `set -e` script. Checked on a Mac whose shell limit is 256: it reads 10240 afterwards.
- The cua-sdk E2E runner (`tests/e2e/cua-sdk/run.py`) raises the limit itself before it starts `cargo test`.
- `bin/ci` already did (`raise_open_file_limit`); a test now pins it.

## Guard

`scripts/ci/tests/test_nofile_limit.py` (runs in `bin/ci` and in CI Test Scripts, which now also triggers on any `*.sh` change):
- fails when a tracked shell script runs `cargo test` / `cargo nextest` without the line, or runs it before the line;
- checks the line itself: 256 becomes 10240, a higher limit is kept, and it survives `set -eu`;
- checks that `bin/ci` and the cua-sdk runner raise 256.

A new script that runs cargo test without the line now fails `bin/ci` and CI with the exact line to paste.

title: [Bug]: Ending a session on Linux X11 crashes every running Qt 6 app (master pointer removal, QTBUG-146876)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, when a cua-driver session that used background input ends, the driver removes its XInput2 master pointer, and every running Qt 6.5+ application segfaults. This is a Qt bug ([QTBUG-146876](https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-146876), open, still in Qt 6.12 per [QTBUG-151420](https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-151420)), but any `XIRemoveMaster` triggers it, so the driver's session teardown kills the user's Qt apps.

### Reproduction

1. X11 desktop with `/dev/uinput` writable by the user, so background input takes the MPX route. Start two PySide6 6.10.1 windows and one PySide6-Essentials 6.8.3 window (any plain `QWidget` with a `QLineEdit` does it), plus a GTK window to act on.
2. One `cua-driver mcp` connection, session `e0`: `get_window_state` on the GTK window, `click` at a blank point of it (`path=mpx_pointer`), `type_text` a few characters (`path=mpx_uinput`). The session adds its `CUA v1.… pointer` master pair.
3. `end_session {"session": "e0"}` → `✅ Session 'e0' ended.`
4. All three Qt processes are gone within a second.

10 of 10 trials on each build. The same happens when the client just exits without `end_session` (stdin closed), when a killed driver's pair is cleaned up by the next `cua-driver serve` at startup, and when a session is left connected but idle.

### Expected behavior

Ending a session leaves the user's other applications running.

### Actual behavior

Qt windows killed per case (each trial: two Qt 6.10.1 windows and one Qt 6.8.3 window):

| Case | 0.46.1 release binary | 0.47.4 (built from 09b38ab66, the release commit) | masters removed |
|---|---|---|---|
| act, then `end_session` | 30 / 30 (10 trials) | 30 / 30 | 1 per trial |
| act, then the client exits (stdin closed) | 30 / 30 | 30 / 30 | 1 per trial |
| `cua-driver mcp` SIGKILLed after acting, then `cua-driver serve` starts and acts | 9 / 9 (3 trials) | 9 / 9 | 2 per trial (startup reaper) |
| act once, stay connected and idle | 3 / 3 (1 trial), dead by the 330 s poll | 3 / 3, same | 1 |
| control: one session acts every trial, never ended | 0 / 30 | 0 / 30 | 0 |
| control: `cua-driver mcp` SIGKILLed, a new `mcp` acts (no reaper) | 0 / 9 | 0 / 9 | 0 |
| control, no Cua: `xinput create-master x` then `xinput remove-master "x pointer"` | 9 / 9 (3 trials) | (same guest, not repeated) | 1 per trial |

Every death lines up with a `master_removed` XI2 hierarchy event. The kernel log shows `general protection fault ... in libQt6XcbQpa.so.6` at offsets `+0x279e4` or `+0x2755c` (or a jump to 0 in the interpreter right after), the same offsets as the plain `xinput remove-master` control.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.46.1 (`cua-driver-rs-0.46.1-linux-x86_64-binary.tar.gz`) and cua-driver 0.47.4 built with their release recipe (`cargo build --locked -p cua-driver --release --features cua-driver/portal-input`) from 09b38ab66 (the `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.4` release commit, current main). Ubuntu 24.04.5 KVM guest, Xorg 21.1.12 (modesetting), mutter 46.2 X11 session, `/dev/uinput` writable, PySide6 6.10.1 and PySide6-Essentials 6.8.3 (bundled Qt), GTK 3.24.41. Telemetry disabled.

### Evidence

Per-trial rows (Qt pids, kernel trap lines, every XI2 hierarchy event in the trial, Cua's replies) are from a scripted MCP client, no model involved. Happy to attach the scripts if useful; the core is just steps 1-3 above.

### Workaround and additional context

Qt 6.5's `QXcbConnection::xi2SetupDevices()` deletes the `QInputDevice`s for devices X no longer lists, but slave devices have their master as QObject parent, so deleting the master deletes the slaves and the loop deletes them again (introduced by qtbase 2a9d93efc6, picked to 6.5.0). Only master removal triggers it: adding a master, reattaching or floating a slave killed 0 of 30 Qt 6.10 and 6.12 windows in our runs, removing one killed 20 of 30. Qt 6.4 and Qt 5.15 are not affected.

In cua-driver the removals are `remove_master_pair` / `remove_master_pointer` in `platform-linux/src/input/mod.rs`, reached from `end_session` (`forget_master_pointer`), idle teardown (in our runs the pair went about five minutes after the last action with the connection still open; I didn't trace which timer, `MPX_IDLE_TTL` is 30 minutes), the popup waiter, the startup `reap_orphaned_master_pointers`, and the no-hotplug failure path in `ensure_master_pointer_for_session`.

#2304 looks like this same crash (`libQt6XcbQpa.so.6.11.1` in the kernel line; its title says the pointer was ephemeral then, so a removal followed every action). #2888 fixed it for KDE Plasma X11 by turning the route off there, but Qt 6.5+ apps on any other X11 desktop still die whenever a pair is removed: it's the client's own device handling, not the window manager (it also happens on a bare Xvfb with no WM).

We hit the same thing in our own tool and fixed it by never removing a master while the X server lives: a session takes a free pair (marked by a property on the master device naming its holder, claimed under `XGrabServer`), adds one only when none is free, and at the end unplugs its uinput slaves, parks the cursor and marks the pair free; pairs whose holder process is dead are taken over instead of removed; and the uinput slave has to show up as an X device before any master is added, so a server without hotplug never gets one. The cost is that pairs stay in `xinput list` until the server exits, as many as the most sessions that used background input at once. In the same kind of run that went from 20/20 Qt windows killed to 0/20. Happy to put up a PR in that shape if you want it.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: type_text after a refused click on a covered Chromium window reports "Typed 6 characters" but the field stays empty
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, after `click` on a covered Chromium window is refused as `target_occluded`, `type_text` into that window still answers "Typed 6 character(s)… not verified", and the field stays empty, 10 of 10. The keys do reach the page, but no field there has focus because the click that would have focused it never happened, so the text goes nowhere. The reply's hint ("The text was delivered but not read back. Read the field before typing again, or it may be duplicated") points the caller the wrong way.

### Reproduction

1. X11 desktop with `/dev/uinput` writable (MPX route). A Chromium `--app` page with one `<input>` that does not have focus (the page's `document.activeElement` is `BODY`), fully covered by another app's focused window.
2. `get_window_state` on the Chromium window, then `click` at the input's screen point: refused with `target_occluded`, as expected.
3. `type_text {"pid": …, "window_id": …, "text": "M0wzqk"}` in the same session.
4. Read the input's value from the page itself.

### Expected behavior

The caller learns the text did not go into a field: something like a refusal or a not-applied result saying the window has no focused editable element (Chromium exposes its focused element over AT-SPI), or at least a result that does not say "delivered". When the click before it was refused, nothing in that window was focused by the caller.

### Actual behavior

Click, every trial:

```
"code": "target_occluded", "effect": "refused", "covering_title": "FX-USER", "path": "mpx_pointer"
```

type_text, every trial:

```json
{
  "delivery": {"mode": "background"},
  "effect": "unverifiable",
  "hint": "The text was delivered but not read back. Read the field before typing again, or it may be duplicated.",
  "route": "global_input",
  "summary": "Typed 6 character(s) as real key events through a virtual master keyboard (path=mpx_uinput, focus untouched) (delivery_mode=background); not verified — confirm with a screenshot."
}
```

The page logged a `focus` and all six key events, `isTrusted: true`, with `document.activeElement` still `BODY`; the input read back empty in 10 of 10 on each build. Nothing reached the covering window either (0 of 10), so the user was not disturbed.

Contrast, same cell: when the input already had focus before the window was covered, the same calls put the text in 10 of 10 (0.46.1). The GTK and Qt targets landed 3 of 3 each on both builds for the same reason (their entry already had keyboard focus). So `type_text` is right only when the field happened to be focused already, and the reply is identical either way.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.46.1 (release binary) and 0.47.4 built from 09b38ab66 (the `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.4` release commit). Ubuntu 24.04.5 KVM guest, Xorg 21.1.12, mutter 46.2 X11 session, Chrome for Testing 154 as `--app`, covering window GTK 3.24.41. One `cua-driver mcp` stdio connection, scripted client, telemetry off.

### Evidence

Verbatim replies above. Field value and key events come from the page's own log and HTTP state endpoint, not through the driver. Covering window text was checked the same way.

### Workaround and additional context

Callers can read the field back with `get_window_state` and retype, which the hint discourages. Related in spirit: #4997 (macOS Chromium, unverifiable result with no target-aware hint).

title: [Bug]: Linux type_text puts letters into a Qt QIntValidator field and reports confirmed
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux, `type_text` into a Qt `QLineEdit` that has a `QIntValidator` puts letters in the field and reports `effect: "confirmed"`. A user typing the same keys gets nothing. The driver's AT-SPI EditableText write turns into `QLineEdit::setText` on Qt's side, which skips the validator and input mask (and, per Qt's docs, doesn't emit `textEdited`), so the app ends up holding a value its own UI would never allow.

### Reproduction

1. PySide6 window with a few `QLineEdit`s; one has `setValidator(QIntValidator(0, 999999))` and `setAccessibleName("int-field")`. Keyboard focus on another field.
2. `get_window_state` on the window, then `type_text {"pid": …, "window_id": …, "element_token": "<token of int-field>", "text": "AB"}`.
3. Read the field's `text()` from the app itself.
4. Control: focus the window, Tab to int-field, `xdotool type AB`.

### Expected behavior

The field rejects the letters the way it does for the keyboard, and the reply says the text didn't go in.

### Actual behavior

```json
{
  "delivery": {"mode": "background"},
  "effect": "confirmed",
  "evidence": [{"kind": "value_readback"}, {"detail": "element [2] reads back the typed text", "kind": "value_readback"}],
  "route": "accessibility",
  "summary": "Typed 2 character(s) into element [2] (via targeted AT-SPI); it reads back 'AB'."
}
```

The field holds `AB`: 3 of 3 on 0.46.1, 6 of 6 on 0.47.4. The xdotool control leaves the field empty every time. `12` goes in both ways.

On Qt's side, `QAccessibleLineEdit::insertText` (qtbase `src/widgets/accessible/simplewidgets.cpp`) builds the new string and calls `lineEdit()->setText(...)`, and `setText` is documented as not validating. Spin boxes and date edits forward the same call to their line edit. In cua-driver the route is `write_into_editable_acc` / `write_through_editable_proxies` in `platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs` (InsertText, falling back to SetTextContents), tried before any key events.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.46.1 (release binary) and 0.47.4 built from 09b38ab66 (the `cua-driver-rs-v0.47.4` release commit). Ubuntu 24.04.5 KVM guest, Xorg 21.1.12, mutter 46.2 X11 session, PySide6 6.10.1, at-spi2-core 2.52. Scripted MCP client, telemetry off.

### Evidence

Reply above, verbatim. Field state read from the app over its own HTTP endpoint, not through the driver.

### Workaround and additional context

None from the caller's side: the reply says confirmed and the read-back agrees. The same probably applies to `QLineEdit::setInputMask` fields and to any app that only reacts to `textEdited` (search-as-you-type, form dirty flags), but I only measured the validator.

title: docs: repoint five relative links at paths that exist
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: five relative links under `libs/` resolve to paths that do not exist in the repository.
- What changed: the hrefs only, no prose.

The three `libs/qemu-docker/*/README.md` pages say "Use the images in
[`libs/images`](../images/README.md)". From `libs/qemu-docker/<os>/` that
resolves to `libs/qemu-docker/images/README.md` — there is no `images` directory
under `qemu-docker`. The page they mean is `libs/images/README.md`, one level
higher, so the link needs `../../`.

`libs/cua-driver/docs/driver-permission-modes-and-consent-plan.md` linked
`docs/content/docs/concepts/how-permission-policies-work.mdx` and
`docs/content/docs/reference/cua-driver/permission-policies.mdx`. Both paths
were removed when the pages moved. `docs/content/docs/redirects.json` maps each
of those two slugs to `cua-driver/guides/permissions`, so both links now point at
`docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/permissions.mdx`. They do end up on the
same page; I kept both links so the sentence still reads as "concept" and
"reference" — say the word if you would rather collapse them into one.

## Related work

No issue — docs-only link fix.

## Compatibility and risk

- No user-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact.
- Risk: none beyond the diff. Rollback: revert the commit.

## Validation

- Resolver run over every touched link (output below): the four post-patch
  targets exist, the five pre-patch targets do not.
- `docs/scripts/check-links.ts` only scans `docs/content/docs/**/*.mdx`, which is

  covered by it.
- Known gap: `bin/ci` does not run on this Windows host — it probes `pnpm` and

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse input to macOS security and consent prompts
body:
Salvaged from #7255

## Why

An agent clicked Allow on "HoloWork would like to access data from other apps", and the macOS driver also typed into an administrator password sheet. Nothing stopped input from reaching the system prompts that grant access on the user's behalf. This lands @AlexFalher's change from #7255 (his commit is first, author kept) and reworks it so every route is covered, the refusal is one authorization adapter, and unrestricted mode can still answer a prompt on a disposable machine.

## What changed

- A new `os_security_prompt` enforcement adapter (R4, unrestricted only) in `authorization.rs` owns the refusal. Standard and bounded mode refuse with `status: refused`, `refusal.code: security_prompt_protected`. The dispatch boundary records the adapter's decision for the call's mode in a reserved argument, which callers cannot set.
- The macOS check sits inside each global HID primitive in `input/mouse.rs` and `input/keyboard.rs`. It runs right before the first cursor warp or event, after any foreground activation. Pointer input is refused when a prompt window is under the point, on any layer. Keys are refused when a prompt owns the front. Pid-addressed routes are refused at the target pid. This covers the two foreground element fallbacks that #7255 missed (modified middle-click, AX selection with modifiers) and foreground keys aimed at another app while a prompt is in front.
- UserNotificationCenter windows count only when they ask for consent. That means a secure field, or a button whose label is one of the system's own consent labels, read from the TCC and NetworkExtension string tables in every language. Crash alerts ("… quit unexpectedly") no longer refuse clicks near them. An alert that cannot be read in full counts as consent.

## Scope

macOS only. The prompt owners are SecurityAgent, UserNotificationCenter (consent alerts only), universalAccessAuthWarn, coreautha, CoreServicesUIAgent and CoreLocationAgent. Reading prompts (window state, screenshots) stays allowed. Windows Credential UI and Linux polkit agents are not checked yet, as #7255 noted. Docs: the permissions guide and the Lume seed steps now say an unattended seed must answer the admin-password dialog from an unrestricted daemon.

## Tradeoffs

- One check inside each HID primitive replaces the dozen tool call sites in #7255, so a new tool route cannot skip it. Window-scoped foreground scroll and drag post to the target pid, not the HID queue, so they are no longer point-checked. The target-pid guard still covers them.
- Matching consent labels from the OS string tables is a heuristic. Every way it can fail (unreadable alert, unlabeled button, missing table) refuses.

## Blast radius

Every macOS input tool, the browser setup assists, and every permission mode. Standard and bounded mode now refuse input that would land on one of these prompts. That is the intended change. A test harness that clicks a Gatekeeper or password dialog has to run unrestricted. Unrestricted behaves as before.

## Verification

- Tests drive every HID primitive and every pid-addressed tool against a prompt fixture, refused and allowed. With any one guard removed, a test fails. Core tests cover the adapter per mode and show a forged decision argument is stripped.
- Read-only probe of the live prompts on a macOS 26 desktop. A SecurityAgent sheet (layer 1000), a universalAccessAuthWarn alert (layer 0) and a "find devices on local networks" consent alert were refused. Crash alerts on the same desktop were not.
- The scoped repository checks and the macOS Lume full matrix passed. The live prompt cases in a Lume guest did not run (details in the verification comment).

title: ci: enable KVM via udev rule and require it for bench verify
body:
## What changed for users
Image releases no longer fail slowly: the osworld bench image verify now boots its VM with hardware acceleration (KVM) on GitHub-hosted amd64 runners, and a missing KVM fails in seconds with the reason, not after 30 minutes.

## Why
`bench / verify (amd64)` in `cd-images-spacesd-release.yml` timed out (1849 s, "cua-spacesd did not answer") even with `time_to_start=1500`. A desktop image under QEMU TCG (software emulation) boots in 900-1300+ s on a hosted runner. The runtime also fell back to TCG silently (a warning only), including when KVM stalled at start.

## Change
- `scripts/images/enable-kvm.sh [--require]`: the documented static udev rule (`99-kvm4all.rules`, reload, trigger), so installing QEMU can't reset `/dev/kvm` to 0660. `--require` errors if KVM is missing.
- `install-release-tools.sh` and all workflows that boot QEMU on hosted Linux (images linux/windows, bench, nightly qemu/build/ready/vmm/fork, vm-density, perf channel, space-egress, e2b-core) use it instead of `chmod 666 /dev/kvm`.
- `cd-bench-images.yml` verify: amd64 runs `enable-kvm.sh --require` and sets `CUA_REQUIRE_KVM=1`.
- `cua-vmm` QEMU runtime: with `CUA_REQUIRE_KVM=1` a same-arch Linux guest never falls back to TCG (neither at accelerator selection nor on the KVM-stall retry); it errors naming `/dev/kvm`. Unit test added.
- `smoke.py`: same preflight for the containerdisk variant.
- `.github/scripts/tests/test_workflow_kvm_policy.py`: no raw `chmod /dev/kvm`; bench verify requires KVM on amd64.

arm64 hosted runners have no KVM and keep the TCG doctor path (`CUA_REQUIRE_KVM` is only set for amd64).

`bin/ci --quick` passes.

title: fix(cua-driver): check the cells a verify-linux.sh run declared
body:
## Why

CUA-4014. `verify-linux.sh` runs `check-evidence.sh` after every run, and the checker hard-coded the two default background left-click labels. Any `CUA_E2E_CELL_FILTER` run then failed with `expected one current recording for linux-electron-left-click-ax-background`, even when its selected cells passed. That covers the foreground-only commands the feature map documents, such as `linux-electron-left-click-px-foreground`. The checker now validates the cells the run declared in `cases.jsonl`.

## What changed

- `check-evidence.sh` reads `cases.jsonl` and checks each declared cell. It needs exactly one current recording, one summary row with the expected outcome (`Delivered` or `Refused`) and `Pass`, and the transcript and fixture journal. Sentinel and desktop-observation evidence with a heartbeat is required only for background cells. The `last_action` marker and the MCP-tool screenshot pair are required only for delivered click cells. If `cases.jsonl` is missing, empty or malformed, the check fails.
- The offline checker regression writes `cases.jsonl` and adds foreground-only, background-refusal and broken-declaration scenarios.
- SKILL.md and execution.md describe what the checker now requires.

## Scope

Covers the Linux verify helper's evidence checker and its offline test. The Rust runner, the report format and the macOS lane are unchanged. The default run still checks both background AX left-click cells to the same standard as before.

## Blast Radius

The checker is used only by the verify skill and by the `verify-skill` CI job. For the default filter it applies the same checks as before. The difference is that the cell list now comes from the run's own declarations instead of a constant.

## Verification

- On main, X11 runs filtered to `linux-electron-left-click-px-foreground`, `linux-electron-right-click-ax-foreground`, `linux-electron-type-text-ax-foreground` and `linux-electron-type-text-ax-background` all failed the evidence check, although every cell passed in `summary.md`. The new checker accepts all four retained evidence directories.
- At this head, the X11 helper exits 0 for `CUA_E2E_CELL_FILTER=linux-electron-left-click-ax-foreground` and for the default filter.
- The scoped repository checks (`test_e2e_rust_linux_workflow.py`) pass. With the base checker in place, the new `foreground` and `refused-background` scenarios fail.

title: fix(cua-driver): on Linux, set_value refuses an option on a combo box that lists none
body:
Fixes CUA-4013.

## Problem

On Linux, `set_value` on a combo box with no accessibility write route opens the combo's popup and picks the option from it. When the popup listed no options, the fallback failed with the untyped error "the combo box popup listed no options". That error surfaced as `tool_invocation_failed`, so an agent could not tell it apart from a driver crash. The no-options path also had no test.

Repro on main: a GTK3 `ComboBoxText` with no items, and `set_value` with `delivery_mode:"foreground"` returns `tool_invocation_failed` ("the combo box popup listed no options").

## Fix

- The AT-SPI option scan (`list_options`) now reports whether every read it made answered.
- `activate_option_ref` returns the new `OptionPick::NoOptions` when the scan answered and found nothing, and `Unavailable` when a read failed or timed out.
- The popup fallback (`pick_listed_option`) waits for options as before. When the wait ends:
  - `NoOptions` becomes the same `option_not_found` refusal (`effect: none`) as an unknown option. The message says the element lists no options.
  - `Unavailable` stays a plain error. A populated popup can be unreadable too, so an unreadable one is never reported as having no such option.
- The popup is still closed in both cases.

## Tests

- Unit tests (`set_value_tests`) cover: an empty popup is refused as `option_not_found` with `effect: none`; an unreadable popup is never `no_such_option`; a popup that lists its options late still gets the pick.
- The fake-bus test `tests/atspi_option_pick.rs` adds an empty combo box (`NoOptions`) and one whose child cannot be read (`Unavailable`). With the scan's completeness ignored, the test fails.
- Live smoke: the GTK3 fixture gains an empty "Empty" combo box. A Linux-only check runs foreground `set_value` on it and requires three things: `option_not_found`, an unchanged label, and a following click by token that still lands, which proves no popup was left behind. With main's binary the check fails with `tool_invocation_failed`. At this head it passes, along with every other row.

title: fix(spaces): forward create_space CPU and memory limits
body:
## Summary

`create_space` drops CPU and memory requests: its MCP schema has neither field, and the handler leaves both at their defaults. On a small host, an agent can receive `host_capacity` advice to create a smaller Space but cannot request one.

Expose optional `cpus` and `memory_mb` using the existing resource types, and forward them to `SpaceCreate` for single and multi-Space requests. Omitting either setting preserves the current default. Regenerate the tool manifest and Spaces reference.

For example, `create_space(on="host:my-host", image="linux", kind="vm", cpus=1, memory_mb=1536)` can now pass the requested size to the existing creation path.

## Related work

Fixes #7309.

## Compatibility and risk

This restores the resource controls already available to the CLI and underlying creation code. It adds optional MCP inputs without changing defaults, allocation logic, or the wire protocol. The fields follow `resize_space`'s types. No backend refactor or new dependency.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the schema regression fails because `cpus` is missing; the integration regression requests 1 CPU but observes 2 at the runtime.
- Full `cua-spaces` and `cua-spaces-contract` test suites: **755 tests passed** across 37 test binaries/doctest groups, including the new regressions.
- Tests cover CPU-only, memory-only, both, omitted defaults, malformed resource types, and both members of a two-Space request.
- Clippy with `--all-targets -- -D warnings` passed for the affected crates and dependency checks. The two app crates that initially lacked CMake were rechecked successfully together after installing it.
- Generated manifest, control fixture and Spaces reference checks pass.
- Full affected `bin/ci`: **10 passed, 2 failed**. Its initial dependent-Clippy failure was a missing local CMake executable; after installing CMake, both affected app crates passed the retry. The remaining failure is `docs-image-refs`: 12 existing image references lack doctor ledger entries, including `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`. Image references, the baseline and checker are unchanged by this PR. No green `local-ci` sign-off is claimed. All CLI, Rust and Spaces generated-reference checks passed.

Integration tests reuse the existing fake runtime and loopback mock server. Live VM/cloud provisioning and hosted PR CI have not been run locally.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused diff; description matches the final change.
- [x] Small bug fix using existing creation semantics; no new architecture or permission boundary.
- [x] Regression tests and generated documentation included.
- [x] Conventional `fix(spaces)` title describes the production change.
- [x] No external contribution was adapted.
- [x] No `no-release` label requested for this behavior fix.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off.

title: fix(cua-driver): never carry a consent grant across a session end
body:
## Why

A consent prompt that was still open, or still queued behind another prompt, when its session ended could store its grant after the end. `revoke_session` runs from the session-end hook and takes only the grants lock. It found nothing to revoke, the user accepted, and `authorize` inserted the grant. The grant key holds no episode, so the same transport's next `start_session` on that label reused the approval without a prompt for up to 30 minutes idle (8 hours absolute). An operator's `cua-driver revoke --session` was bypassed the same way.

A call could also carry an approval across the end without storing anything. It took a stored grant just before its session ended, and lifecycle admission then recreated the session for it. The call ran in the new episode on the old episode's approval.

A grant never carries over to a later episode of the same label.

## What changed

- `ProtectedResourceGrants` counts revocations. `authorize` snapshots the count when it starts. After the provider accepts, it stores the grant only if no `revoke_session` naming its session, and no `revoke_all`, ran since that snapshot. Otherwise it revokes the approval and returns `authorization_canceled`. Right after the snapshot it reads the session's tombstone. A session already ended there never reuses a stored grant, and its fresh approval covers that one call and is not stored.
- Dispatch keeps every grant its `authorize_*` helpers return, and holds an `AuthorizationWindow` from before its first adapter until lifecycle admission. After admission, a call holding any approval is refused with the new retryable code `authorization_session_ended` in two cases: one of its grants was revoked, or a `revoke_session` naming its session (or a `revoke_all`) ran after that grant's own authorization started. Each grant carries the revocation count its authorization started at, and the window keeps revocations recorded until admission. An approval granted in a session recreated before its authorization started is not refused. An end revokes its episode's approvals before admission may recreate the session, so either case means the approval belongs to an ended episode. The window also covers a one-call approval, which is never stored and so never marked revoked. A recovery hint tells the client to retry once, and the retry prompts again.

## Scope

`cua-driver-core`: `consent.rs`, the protected-authorization helpers and dispatch in `tool.rs`, and one rule in `recovery_hint.rs`. Grant keys, TTLs, the end hook, and the adapters' own scope checks are unchanged. Other findings from the same statechart audit (desktop-lane leases for input workers, serve drain, macOS foreground restore, closed-transport labels) are separate PRs.

## Tradeoffs

Putting the episode in `ResourceGrantKey` would also work, but the lifecycle layer has no episode id to read. The revocation count and the liveness check after admission need nothing from it. Checking whether admission recreated the session would miss an `end_session` plus another caller's `start_session` that lands before admission. The liveness check catches that too.

## Blast Radius

Every protected-resource adapter that prompts in standard mode. A call whose session ended mid-prompt gets `authorization_canceled` instead of a stored grant. A call whose approval was revoked before its admission gets `authorization_session_ended`, and retrying it prompts. That includes a `revoke_all` or `revoke_resource` that lands in that window, which used to let the call run once. A call that holds no approval is never refused by the new check. Calls on live sessions behave as before.

## Verification

- The four consent tests fail at their test commits and pass with their fixes. Three tool tests drive the real end hook, idle eviction and recreation at admission: for a stored grant, for a one-call approval, and for an approval granted after recreation, which must not be refused. Each fails when the part of the check it covers is disabled or measured from the window's start.
- No shipped seam pauses dispatch between authorization and admission, so those tests call the refusal helper with the window themselves. Wiring the helper into dispatch is covered by review, not by a test.
- The TLA+ model (`consent_grant.tla`, in #7353) fails CG1 on main and passes with the counter and tombstone read. It was not rerun for the later changes. The scoped repository checks are in the `verified` comment.

title: fix(cua-driver): a closed transport's late call cannot claim a label
body:
## Why

A call sent by a transport just before its control connection closed could land after the close and bind a new label to the dead transport. `end_sessions_for_owner` recorded the owner as closed only when a label still named it after the ends. `begin_session_dispatch_inner` never read `CLOSED_TRANSPORTS` for a label with no tombstone. The late call then held the label: every other transport got "session is not available to this transport" until the idle sweep. After the sweep, the tombstone named an owner that was never marked closed, so `start_session` from anyone else stayed refused until the daemon restarted.

## What changed

- `end_sessions_for_owner` records the owner as closed before it ends anything, under the tombstone lock. Admission (`begin_session_dispatch_inner`, refusing with `DispatchRefusal::Ended`) and `activate_or_revive_session_for_owner` refuse a closed owner on any label (`closed_label_owner`). The transport's own unnamed id keeps its current behaviour.
- `CLOSED_TRANSPORTS` keeps the close time. At each close, owners past `CLOSED_OWNER_GRACE` (the default idle TTL) that no labelled episode and no pending call names are forgotten in one pass. The native dispatch boundary counts each call per owner transport until it finishes (`begin_owner_dispatch`), so a call waiting on consent or the desktop input lane keeps its closed owner refused however long it waits. Owners a label still names stay until that label is claimed, and runtime teardown drops them as before. This replaces the per-tombstone bookkeeping (`names_labels_of`).
- New test: a transport closes holding no label, its late call and late `start_session` are refused, and another transport can still use the label. The existing forgotten-owner test is rewritten for the new rule, a grace test is added, and a dispatch test parks a call in consent and checks its owner stays pending until it finishes.
- Two test races fixed. The grace test pruned the shared closed set past the grace and forgot owners that parallel tests had just closed. The observer test's permanent cursor reader observed every session, so a later `a_revival_during_a_slow_end_keeps_its_capture_policy` never reached its own reader and hung.

## Scope

`cua-driver-core/src/session.rs`, plus the pending-call guard at the dispatch boundary in `tool.rs`. It does not change label release, `end_session` semantics, or the idle sweep. Since #7811 typed the admission refusals, a closed owner's late call on a label is refused as `session_ended`, not `session_owned_by_other_transport`, whose recovery hint does not apply to a dead connection. Other findings from the same audit are separate PRs.

## Tradeoffs

Keeping every closed id until runtime teardown would be simpler, but an HTTP connection mints a transport id before authentication, so the set would grow without bound. The grace window bounds it to recent closes plus owners that labels still name. The grace window now covers only a call the transport read but has not yet dispatched; a dispatched call is covered by the pending count, however long it waits.

## Blast Radius

Every transport close (MCP stdio proxy control connections, the envelope stream, MCP HTTP connections, one-shot CLI calls). The audit checked trusted-session resume, legacy `session_end`, the shared `cli-explicit` transport and the per-connection UUID cleanups, and none of them reuses a closed id to bind a label.

## Verification

- The new test fails at the test commit and passes with the fix. Removing the pending-call check, or the guard in `tool.rs`, fails the grace and dispatch tests. After merging main, the `session::` tests pass in 400 of 400 parallel runs; before the two race fixes they failed or hung intermittently. `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver-sdk` and `cua-driver` tests, clippy and fmt are green on macOS.
- The TLA+ model (`label_release.tla`, in #7353) fails LR1 on main and passes with the fix.
- The scoped repository checks are in the `verified` comment.

title: fix(cua-driver): submit a macOS single-line field with its own Return on background type_text
body:
## Problem

On macOS, a background `type_text` of `"netflix.com\n"` into Safari's address bar searched for "netflix.com netflix.com" instead of opening the site. The background route inserts the text through accessibility. The read-back can't confirm a value containing a newline, because the field drops it. So the code fell through and typed the whole string again as keys.

## Fix

When the target is a single-line field (`AXTextField`, `AXSearchField`, `AXComboBox`) and the text is one line plus one trailing Return:

- Insert the line alone with `AXSelectedText` and confirm it through the read-back.
- Send Return as its own key, but only if two checks pass:
  - the read-back equals the value from before the write with its selection replaced by the line, and differs from that earlier value (a no-op write, a field that already held the line, or a partial write does not count), and
  - the written field holds keyboard focus.
- If either check fails, report the line as delivered with `verified: false` and say why Return was not sent. Return is pid-routed, so sending it then could submit a different field.
- If the write changed the field into anything other than the full insert, report it as unverified partial delivery. Do not type the line and Return again as keys.
- Semantic-only keyboard policy keeps the old path, since Return is a synthesized key.

## Test plan

- Unit tests: `single_line_fields_split_off_one_trailing_return` and `submit_needs_a_visible_change_from_the_insert`.
- On a macOS Lume guest, through cua-driver:
  - Fresh Safari, background `type_text "netflix.com\n"` into the address bar's element token. Main doubled the text in most runs. With this change every run opened netflix.com.
  - Background `"abc\n"` into a page `<input>`: unchanged behaviour.

title: fix(cua-vmm): boot cold when a guest cannot take a restored identity; one readiness budget per start
body:
Fixes the `bench / verify (amd64, ubuntu-24.04)` failure in `cd-images-spacesd-release.yml` (`verify/amd64/containerdisk`: `cua-spacesd did not answer within 0ns`). Linear: CUA-4051.

**For users:** cua-spacesd releases can promote the OSWorld bench image again, and a local OSWorld VM (or any image whose agent is not root) starts in seconds instead of hanging for the whole start timeout before booting.

## Root cause

KVM was in use all along (the run that passed on 10 Nov printed `KVM present`), so the slow-TCG theory behind #7342 was not the cause, and a bigger `time_to_start` (#7304) only moved the failure.

The QEMU runtime's warm start was. On a fresh runner every OSWorld smoke:

1. booted a template VM and recorded a golden memory snapshot (about 90 s);
2. restored it and asked the guest to take a new identity: the renewal runs as root through cua-spacesd (`sudo -n sh -c ...`). The OSWorld disk's cua-spacesd runs as `user`, so the renewal failed on every attempt, and `renew` retried until the whole readiness budget (900 s, later 1500 s) was gone;
3. then booted cold with a fresh budget of its own (up in about 15 s), and returned. The SDK's own clock had run out by then, so its cua-spacesd wait got 0 ns: one 200 ms try, which a guest 15 s into its boot loses.

Evidence, from a diagnostic run of the same image and CLI on a hosted runner with the guest console and process list captured:

| | ready | result |
|---|---|---|
| `CUA_QEMU_WARM=0` | 307 s (pull + KVM cold boot; cua-spacesd serving 10 s after kernel start) | pass |
| warm starts on (default) | template 226-317 s, restored VM 317-1819 s (exactly the 1500 s budget), cold boot at 1819 s | `did not answer within 0ns` at 1826 s |

Every failing release run fits the same sum: budget + pull + cold boot (1372 s with 900 s; 1849 s and 1858 s with 1500 s). The one pass (run 42866618402) won the single 200 ms try: its guest had booted 14 s before ready.

## Changes

- **No golden snapshot from a guest that cannot renew its identity.** `GuestIdentity::check_renewable` (cua-spacesd: `[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || sudo -n true` as the agent) runs on the template before the snapshot is written. A guest that cannot is marked cold on disk (`_golden/<key>.cold`, with the reason), so later starts on that host boot cold at once without recording again. A guest that does not answer the question records nothing this time and is asked again next time, so a transient error never marks an image cold.
- **A refused renewal fails fast.** When the guest ran the renewal script and it failed, `renew` gives up after 3 refusals instead of retrying until the deadline. Transport errors still retry until the deadline.
- **One readiness budget per QEMU start.** Counted from when the image is present (as the SDK counts it), shared by the golden recording, the restore and its renewal, a cold boot after a failed restore, and the probes. Before, each phase got the whole `ready_timeout` again.
- **Failures print the guest console.** `scripts/bench-images/smoke.py` copies the serial console and QEMU log of the VM (and of any golden recording) into the evidence while the sandbox starts, and prints their tails on failure. A failed create deletes the VM directory, so these were lost before.

## Tests

- `cua-vmm`: `a_cold_marked_configuration_records_no_golden`, `phases_of_a_start_share_one_readiness_budget`
- `cua-daemon-core`: `a_refused_renewal_is_given_up_without_waiting_out_the_budget`, `the_renewable_command_needs_root_or_passwordless_sudo`
- `scripts/bench-images/test_bench.py`: `ConsoleCapture` (the console outlives the deleted VM and its golden recording)
- Local: `cargo test -p cua-vmm -p cua-daemon-core --lib`, clippy `-D warnings` on 1.97.1 for both crates, `bin/ci --quick` green.
- End to end: `cd-images-spacesd-release.yml` dispatched on this branch (`build=true`); the result is posted below.

Refs #7342, #7304.

title: test(spaces): fix flaky prewarm grace test (offline provider race)
body:
Fixes the recurring `anUnclaimedPrewarmedStreamIsLetGoAfterItsGrace` failure (seen on #7337: "Expectation failed: (s.stats().count -> 0) == 1", also on the in-job rerun).

Cause: the test prewarmed a stream on `OfflineStreamSourceProvider`, which refuses to open a session. A warm stream whose session fails is let go at once (`statusChanged` -> `dropWarm`), so the stream could vanish before the first expectation. It was never the 800 ms grace; the failing rerun took 0.36 s.

Fix: use a provider that really streams (`SyntheticStreamProvider`, as the neighbouring prewarm test does) and check the registered stream synchronously after `handle`, before any suspension. The grace-expiry assertion is unchanged.

User impact: none (test only).

title: fix(cua-driver/linux): pool XI2 master pairs instead of removing them (Qt 6 crash, #7325)
body:
Fixes #7325. Linear: CUA-4052.

**For users:** on Linux X11, ending a Cua Driver session (or letting it time out, or restarting the driver after a crash) no longer kills the Qt 6 apps you have open.

## Cause

When a session that used background input ended, the driver removed its XInput2 master pointer pair with `XIRemoveMaster`. Qt 6.5+ double-deletes slave devices whenever any master disappears ([QTBUG-146876](https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-146876), still open in 6.12), so every running Qt 6 client on the display segfaulted. All five removal paths triggered it: `end_session`, the idle timeout, the popup waiter, the startup orphan reaper and the no-hotplug failure path.

## Fix

Master pairs now live for the X server's lifetime and are reused, the shape @will-bogusz suggested in the issue:

- A session takes a free pair and adds one only when none is free. The holder is a `_CUA_MPX_HOLDER` device property on the master pointer, written under `XGrabServer` so two driver processes never take the same pair.
- Releasing a pair unplugs the session's uinput slaves, parks its cursor in the bottom-right corner and marks it free. Nothing is removed.
- Pairs whose holder is provably gone (same boot, PID namespace and uid, process dead or PID reused) are taken over. Startup recovery now frees them instead of removing them.
- The uinput slave must show up as an X device before any pair is taken or added, so a server without hotplug never gains one.

The cost: idle `CUA v1.… pointer` pairs stay in `xinput list` until the X server exits. There are as many as the most sessions that used background input at the same time.

## Tests

- New unit tests: holder marks, which pairs can be taken, and a guard that fails if any code in `platform-linux` issues a master removal.
- New ignored real-Xorg test, `tests/mpx_pool_xorg.rs`. Three sessions in a row free and reuse one pair, no `MASTER_REMOVED` hierarchy event fires, and with `CUA_TEST_QT6_PYTHON` set a live PySide6 window survives. GitHub CI only has Xvfb (no uinput hotplug), so this one runs by hand:
  `DISPLAY=:0 CUA_TEST_QT6_PYTHON=<python with PySide6> cargo test -p platform-linux --test mpx_pool_xorg -- --ignored`
- Manual check on Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME on Xorg (mutter 46), PySide6 6.10.1, the issue's steps (click, then `type_text` into a GTK window, then `end_session`, then the client exits):
  - 0.47.8 release: 9 of 9 Qt windows killed, with `general protection fault in libQt6XcbQpa.so.6` in the kernel log.
  - This branch: 0 of 21 killed. Masters stayed at 2 before, during and after each session, and the pair was reused every time.
  - This branch, two live sessions, then one `cua-driver mcp` SIGKILLed, then `cua-driver serve` starts (startup recovery), then a new session: 0 of 3 killed. The dead driver's pair was freed and reused, and no master was removed.

## Follow-up

#2888 turned the background-input route off on KDE Plasma X11 for what looks like this same crash. That gate is unchanged here. Lifting it should get its own check on a KDE X11 machine.

title: [Bug]: existing-profile bind refuses as ambiguous when a same-bounds window has a background tab with the selected tab's title
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`get_browser_state(pid, window_id)` refuses with `browser_binding_ambiguous` (`candidate_count: 2`) for a window whose visible tab title is unique to that window, whenever another Chrome window has the same bounds and merely *contains* a background tab with that title.

In `correlate` (`cua-driver-core/src/browser/binding.rs`), the title tie-break runs over the per-window representatives built by `window_representatives`. That function prefers, for **every** CDP window, any tab whose title matches the *requested* native window's title. So when two windows share bounds, a background tab in the other window that happens to have the same title (a duplicated settings page, a second `New Tab`, the same site open twice) promotes that window into the tie-break. Both representatives then match and the bind is refused, even though only one window is actually displaying that title.

This is easy to hit on a normal daily-driver profile: windows are often the same maximized size on one display, and `New Tab` exists in almost every window. In practice the agent can only bind when the user happens to be looking at a tab whose title is unique across all same-size windows.

### Reproduction

1. Chrome on macOS, attach the existing profile with `browser_prepare` (`strategy: existing_profile`).
2. Open two normal windows with identical bounds (e.g. both 1920×1050 at the same origin on one display).
3. In window A, select tab "Page X". In window B, open a tab also titled "Page X", then select a different tab in B (so B's native title is something else).
4. `get_browser_state({pid, window_id: A})`.

Same result with step 3 replaced by: press ⌘T in window A (selected tab becomes `New Tab`) while window B also has a background `New Tab`.

### Expected behavior

Bind window A exactly. Window B's native title is different, so B cannot be the window currently showing "Page X". Only the selected tab of each window should be able to make that window match the requested title.

### Actual behavior

```
{"refusal":{"code":"browser_binding_ambiguous","detail":{"candidate_count":2},
 "message":"multiple CDP targets match the native window and the title tie-break cannot pick a unique one"}}
```

When window A is switched to a tab whose title exists in no other window, the same call binds with `binding_quality: exact`. So this looks like the tie-break and not a geometry or ownership problem.

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.38.0 (`serve --dangerously-bypass-approvals`), MCP transport
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon
- Google Chrome 157.0.8103.39, existing default profile, `DevToolsActivePort` endpoint
- Source read for the analysis: `main` at 8854478

### Evidence

- The refusal shows up only when the two windows' bounds are identical. `list_windows` reports both at `x=1098, y=-1050, 1920×1050`. A third window of a different width is not counted.
- Calling the bind right after ⌘T in window A (selected tab `New Tab`) still gives `candidate_count: 2`.
- I observed the symptoms above on a real profile. The cause described in the summary comes from reading `correlate` / `window_representatives`. I did not build a minimal fixture, so the two-window steps in Reproduction are derived from the code, not recorded.

### Workaround and additional context

Workarounds we use: give the agent its own Chrome window with a distinct size, or bind only while the selected tab's title is unique.

Possible fixes, in case useful:

1. When several CDP windows match by bounds, also take the titles of the *other* native windows of the same pid with the same bounds. A CDP window whose tabs contain another native window's title is better explained by that window. Matching native windows to CDP windows one-to-one by their own titles would settle this case without guessing.
2. Use page visibility as an extra signal: only each window's selected tab reports `document.visibilityState === "visible"` (occlusion can make it `hidden` too, so it would narrow candidates, not prove the match on its own).

Related: #3681 covers the same-bounds ambiguity fixture. This report is about the refusal also happening when the visible titles differ.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: scroll on a Qt list reports "Scrolled down 3 ticks" but nothing moves
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, `scroll` on a Qt list answers "Scrolled down 3 ticks" and the list does not move, on Qt 5 and Qt 6, even with the Qt window focused. A real wheel event at the same point scrolls it.

### Reproduction

1. X11 session (Xvfb + openbox here), a PyQt5 or PyQt6 window with a 20-row `QListWidget`, window focused.
2. `get_window_state` on it, then `scroll {"pid": …, "window_id": …, "x": <list center>, "y": <list center>, "direction": "down", "amount": 3}`.
3. Read the list's scroll position from the app.
4. Control: `xdotool mousemove --window <id> x y click --repeat 3 5` at the same point.

Script: [cua_x11_repro.py](https://gist.github.com/will-bogusz/e8696f3238aaa108cf3e7c0b730440dc), `python3 cua_x11_repro.py scroll --qt 5` (or `--qt 6`). It starts its own window and reads the position from the app itself.

### Expected behavior

The list scrolls, or the call says it couldn't.

### Actual behavior

```
{"trial": 0, "active": "cua-repro-qt", "scroll": {"ok": true, "text": "Scrolled down 3 ticks (delivery_mode=background)."}, "list_top_before": 0, "list_top_after_cua": 0, "list_top_after_xdotool_wheel": 9}
```

3 of 3 on Qt 5 and 3 of 3 on Qt 6 with the script. In a larger matrix on the same build: 80 of 80 across focused, unfocused, covered and user-typing windows, Qt 5 and Qt 6, while the xdotool wheel control moved it every time. GTK 3 on the same guest refuses background scroll with an exact refusal, which is fine; Qt gets a success it didn't earn.

[INFERENCE] Qt's xcb plugin takes wheel input from XI2 and probably drops a synthetic core button 4/5 event, so whatever route the background scroll uses here never reaches it.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.47.9 (`cua-driver-rs-0.47.9` linux arm64 release binary; same result on 0.46.1). Ubuntu 22.04.5 aarch64, Xvfb + openbox (no compositor), AT-SPI 2.44, PyQt5 5.15 (Qt 5.15.3), PyQt6 6.3.1 (Qt 6.2.4). Scripted MCP client, telemetry off.

### Evidence

Output above from the script. The list position is read from the app's own scroll bar, not through the driver.

### Workaround and additional context

`delivery_mode: "foreground"`, or scroll through AT-SPI where the list exposes it.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: hotkey to an unfocused Qt window reports "Pressed ctrl+m" but the shortcut never fires
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, `hotkey ctrl+m` to a Qt window that isn't focused answers "Pressed ctrl+m on pid …" and the window's Ctrl+M action doesn't fire, on Qt 5 and Qt 6. The same call works when the Qt window is focused.

### Reproduction

1. X11 session, a PyQt5 or PyQt6 window with a File menu `QAction` "Mark" bound to Ctrl+M, and another window focused.
2. `hotkey {"pid": …, "window_id": <the Qt window>, "keys": ["ctrl", "m"]}`.
3. Read the action's trigger count from the app.
4. Control: focus the Qt window, same call.

Script: [cua_x11_repro.py](https://gist.github.com/will-bogusz/e8696f3238aaa108cf3e7c0b730440dc), `python3 cua_x11_repro.py hotkey --qt 5` (or `--qt 6`).

### Expected behavior

The shortcut fires, or the call refuses the way it does for GTK 3 in the same spot. Saying "Pressed" while nothing happened is the problem.

### Actual behavior

```
{"trial": 0, "qt_focused": false, "active": "cua-repro-user", "hotkey": {"ok": true, "text": "Pressed ctrl+m on pid 3176 (delivery_mode=background)."}, "mark_before": 0, "mark_after": 0}
{"trial": 0, "qt_focused": true, "active": "cua-repro-qt", "hotkey": {"ok": true, "text": "Pressed ctrl+m on pid 3176 (delivery_mode=background)."}, "mark_before": 0, "mark_after": 1}
```

cua-driver 0.47.9 (`cua-driver-rs-0.47.9` linux arm64 release binary; same on 0.46.1). Ubuntu 22.04.5 aarch64, Xvfb + openbox, AT-SPI 2.44, PyQt5 5.15 (Qt 5.15.3), PyQt6 6.3.1 (Qt 6.2.4). Scripted MCP client, telemetry off.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: invoke_menu on a background GTK 3 window drops the user's keystrokes in their own window
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, `invoke_menu` on a background GTK 3 window drops a couple of the user's keystrokes in whatever window they're typing in. The menu command runs, the reply says "focus untouched", and the user's text comes out with characters missing.

### Reproduction

1. X11 session, a GTK 3 window with File > Mark (a plain `Gtk.MenuItem`), and a second GTK window focused where the user is typing (here `xdotool type --delay 80` a 43-character sentence).
2. While the user is typing: `invoke_menu {"pid": …, "window_id": <the menu window>, "path": ["File", "Mark"]}`.
3. Compare what the user's window received with what was typed. Control: same trial without the call.

Script: [cua_x11_repro.py](https://gist.github.com/will-bogusz/e8696f3238aaa108cf3e7c0b730440dc), `python3 cua_x11_repro.py menu-keys`.

### Expected behavior

The user's typing is untouched, as "focus untouched" says.

### Actual behavior

```
{"trial": 0, "invoke_menu": {"ok": true, "text": "Resolved the live native menu path and dispatched its final accessibility action (delivery_mode=background, focus untouched); verify the command's semantic effect from fresh state."}, "user_typed": "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", "user_got": "the quick brown fox jumpover the lazy dog", "lost": 2}
{"trial": 0, "invoke_menu": null, "user_typed": "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", "user_got": "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", "lost": 0}
```

The user lost 2 characters in 8 of 8 trials with the call (5 + 3 across two runs), 0 in 8 of 8 controls. A larger matrix on the same build saw the same in 10 of 10 (5 characters in one trial). [INFERENCE] Opening the menu shell to resolve the live path takes a keyboard grab for a moment, and keys typed during it go to the grab.

### Environment

cua-driver 0.47.9 (`cua-driver-rs-0.47.9` linux arm64 release binary; same on 0.46.1). Ubuntu 22.04.5 aarch64, Xvfb + openbox, AT-SPI 2.44, GTK 3.24. Scripted MCP client, telemetry off.

### Evidence

Output above from the script. Text read from the user window's own buffer.

### Workaround and additional context

None from the caller's side; the call can't know the user is typing. Separately, in 2 of 3 trials of the latest run the menu item's `activate` fired twice, 7-16 ms apart, for one `invoke_menu` call. I haven't pinned that down (another fixture with an accelerator on the item counted one per call), so I'm only noting it here.

title: fix(cua-driver): stamp the window-local point on macOS 27 background drags
body:
## Why

On macOS 27, WindowServer hands a pid-routed event's `CGEventSetWindowLocation` stamp to the target as its window-local point. #5492 switched background clicks to the window-local stamp on macOS 27, but `drag_at_xy_background` still stamped every event with the screen point. A background drag inside a window then pressed, moved and released at points offset by the window's origin, so it moved nothing and still reported a posted drag. Refs CUA-4056.

## What changed

- `drag_at_xy_background` takes the window's screen origin and stamps each move, press, drag and release with `point - origin` on macOS 27+ (the same `window_location_is_window_local` gate as the click route), and with the screen point before. The off-screen primer keeps `(-1, -1)`, and a release cut short by a drag-and-drop session is stamped at the point where it stopped.
- The drag tool and `drag_at_xy_observed` pass the origin from the frame they already resolved.

## Scope

macOS background pixel drags only. Foreground HID drags, Electron main-process drags, clicks and scrolls are unchanged. Linux and Windows are untouched.

## Blast radius

Every macOS background `drag`. Before macOS 27 the stamp is the screen point exactly as before, so current releases see no change.

## Verification

- A new unit test pins the macOS 27 stamps of a whole drag plan against a window at a non-zero origin, and checks that the pre-27 stamps stay the screen points. It fails if the stamp goes back to the screen point.
- Not run: no macOS 27 host or image exists, so the macOS 27 path itself has not been exercised live. The macOS 26 Lume run checks that releases before 27 behave as before.

title: fix(cua-driver): release actions at the native arrival under floor cursor timings
body:
## Why

The default cursor timing, `steady` (#5044), makes every agent-cursor move take at least 600 ms, so a person can follow short hops. A direct action waits for the cursor's arrival signal before it sends input, so that floor became a latency floor on every short action with the cursor on. Refs CUA-4054.

## What changed

- The overlay now releases the waiting action when the same move under `native` timing would have arrived. A floor timing (`relaxed`, `steady`, `calm`) still plays the stretched glide to the target, and the cursor finishes during the action.
- A move the floor does not stretch, and every other timing, release at their own arrival as before. The Linux shell helper's pose track carries the same release time.
- `EMBEDDING.md` says what the floor costs.

## Scope

`cursor-overlay`'s arrival signal, shared by macOS, Windows, X11 and Wayland. The motion planner, golden trajectories, timings and the `steady` default are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

- Making `native` the default would also remove the wait, but it undoes the look chosen in #5044.
- Capping a direct call's glide wait at the batch's 120 ms would cut long moves short too. Releasing at the native arrival keeps long moves exactly as they are.

## Blast radius

Direct actions with the agent cursor on and a floor timing. The click can now land while the cursor is still easing in on the last stretch of a short hop. The input point is unchanged.

## Verification

title: feat(cua-driver): add require_verified to refuse unconfirmed actions per call
body:
## Why

When the driver cannot confirm an action, such as a background pixel click or keys into a web view, the result is still a success with `effect: "unverifiable"`. An agent that checks only `isError` carries on as if the action had worked. Refusing every unconfirmed action by default would break the many routes that work but can't be read back. So this adds an opt-in per call. Refs CUA-4053.

## What changed

- Every action-result tool accepts an optional `require_verified` boolean. With `true`, an `unverifiable`, `suspected_noop` or `partial` result comes back as an error with `code: "action_unverified"` and `execution_state: "delivered"`. The error keeps the effect, route, delivery, summary, `hint` and `next_call`, and the action is still recorded. Omitted or `false` changes nothing. A non-boolean value is refused as `invalid_arguments` before the tool runs.
- The dispatch boundary applies it, so it means the same on every platform and inside `run_steps` and `run_script`, where a strict step stops the batch. A strict menu-bar `click` that `run_steps` reroutes to `invoke_menu` carries the flag along, so the reroute stays strict.
- macOS summaries for actions the driver can't confirm (background pixel click, drag, middle-click, pixel and key scroll, desktop click) start with "📨" instead of "✅". The skill's `WORKFLOW.md` documents the flag, and the generated tool reference and MCP snapshots include it.

## Scope

`cua-driver-core` dispatch, its recovery-hint table, the macOS summary prefixes, and docs. No platform adapter changes how it delivers input or classifies an effect.

## Tradeoffs

- A daemon-wide setting was the other option. A per-call flag lets one agent ask for strict results without changing them for every other client of the daemon.

## Compatibility

Additive and optional. It adds one argument to every action tool's input schema on every platform. Clients that don't send it see no change apart from the macOS summary emoji. It follows the same pattern as `post_action_wait` (#6033): a dispatcher-owned per-call argument with no separate RFC.

## Blast radius

Only callers that pass `require_verified: true`. Every other result is byte-identical apart from the summary emoji on macOS.

## Verification

- A dispatch test covers an unconfirmed click with and without the flag, a confirmed click with it, the dispatcher consuming it, and the `invalid_arguments` refusal. Module tests cover argument parsing and the error shape.
- After merging main, a batch test covers the menu-bar reroute: a strict click run as `invoke_menu` stops the batch with `action_unverified`. It fails without the fix.
- The scoped repository checks passed for `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver-contract`, `cua-driver` and `platform-macos`, plus the generated reference check. The Linux and Windows MCP snapshots were updated by hand to match, and their native dump runs in CI.

title: feat(cua-driver): compact default MCP tool list (profiles + lead-paragraph docs)
body:
## What users get

`cua-driver mcp` now lists a compact tool set by default. An agent harness that loads every listed tool schema on every request spends far fewer tokens, and nothing is removed:

- `tools/list` shows the 34 everyday tools (profile `agent`). The other tools stay registered and callable by name, through the same authorization.
- Listed tools carry their lead paragraph and short parameter notes. The lead paragraphs of the agent tools were rewritten so each one stands alone: what the tool does, the preferred way to call it, the one key caveat. Detail stays after the blank line in the full description.
- `get_guide({tool: "<name>"})` returns any tool's full description and full parameter docs. `cua-driver describe <tool>` is unchanged.
- The server instructions name only listed tools, and add one line on how to get the rest.

Supersedes #6888 (same profile mechanism, now with the `agent` default, compact docs and the instructions change).

## Measured (macOS arm64, `cua-driver mcp --direct` over stdio)

| | tools | description bytes | input-schema bytes | name + description + schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before (main) | 62 | 52,067 | 87,344 | 140,248 |
| after (default) | 34 | 10,443 | 31,030 | 41,853 |

Whole `tools/list` JSON on the wire: about 206 KB before, 89 KB after.

## Settings

- `CUA_DRIVER_TOOL_PROFILE` (config key `tool_profile`): `agent` (default), `full`, or `agent,<group>` with groups `browser`, `recording`, `cursor`, `session`, `admin`, `desktop`. A tool no group names is always listed. A typo falls back to `full` with a warning.
- `CUA_DRIVER_TOOL_DOCS` (config key `tool_docs`): `compact` (default) or `full`.
- The environment variable wins over the config key. The compact rendering keeps `outputSchema` and `annotations` unchanged, and leaves out `session`, `target` and `debug_image_out` from listed input schemas unless a tool requires them (they are still accepted when sent).
- Server-side validation of `tools/call` still uses the full tool list, so hidden tools and omitted parameters keep working. HTTP and stdio MCP both list through the same path.

## Tests

- Unit: profile parsing and resolution, filtering and the reported `tool_profile` field, compact rendering (required properties kept, advanced properties dropped, sentence-boundary cuts, a property named `title` kept), instructions under each profile, and a dispatch test that a hidden tool answers a call.
- Integration (`tool_surface_test`): every registered tool is in a group, the default list is exactly the 34 agent tools on macOS, the model-visible size is at most 60 KB (logs the number: about 41 KB), hidden tools are callable, `get_guide({tool})` returns the full docs.
- Existing contract tests keep reading the full surface (the testkit pins `CUA_DRIVER_TOOL_PROFILE=full` and `CUA_DRIVER_TOOL_DOCS=full`). The timing test `batch_tools::pauses_between_steps_but_not_after_the_last` is flaky under parallel load and passes alone.
- Lead paragraphs were rewritten for the macOS tools and the shared browser and batch tools; the Windows and Linux descriptions are unchanged (compact rendering still cuts them to their lead paragraph).

title: fix(cua-driver): keep isolated macOS browsers off the login keychain and stop launch loops
body:
Fixes CUA-4065.

## What changes for users

On macOS, browsers that Cua Driver launches for an agent (`browser_prepare` with an isolated profile) no longer ask for the login keychain, so they never show "… wants to use your confidential information stored in '… Safe Storage' in your keychain". If a launch fails or a security prompt is on screen anyway, Cua Driver stops with a clear error instead of launching more browsers.

## Cause

`isolated_browser_command` in `cua-driver-core/src/browser/prepare.rs` passed `--password-store=basic` on Linux but had no macOS counterpart. Every driver-launched Chromium therefore read the "<Browser> Safe Storage" item from the login keychain. When the launched binary is not on that item's access list (another Chromium build or tool created it), or the keychain is locked, macOS shows a SecurityAgent prompt for each new browser process, and nothing stopped repeated launches from stacking them.

## Changes

1. **Mock keychain for driver-owned profiles (macOS).** Isolated launches add `--use-mock-keychain` (as Playwright does). The launch command is now built only through `driver_owned_browser_command`, which refuses any directory that is not a marked driver-owned profile directly under the driver's profile root. The user's own profile is only ever attached to its running browser (`strategy=existing_profile`); it is never launched or relaunched, so the mock keychain can never make its cookies unreadable. The standalone-browser E2E test launcher gets the same switch for its throwaway profiles.
2. **Launch circuit breaker.** After 3 consecutive failed isolated launches (spawn error, early exit, no DevTools, endpoint mismatch, or a security prompt), `browser_prepare` refuses further launches for an exponential back-off (30 s, doubling to 10 min) with `detail.reason = "isolated_launch_backoff"`, `retry_after_seconds`, and the last failure. One attempt is let through after the back-off; a success resets it.
3. **Keychain prompt guard.** New `BrowserPlatform::security_prompt_open` (macOS: an on-screen SecurityAgent or LocalAuthentication window, i.e. keychain and password prompts; privacy consent and Gatekeeper prompts do not count; it only looks). Before launching, an open prompt refuses the launch (`security_prompt_open`). While waiting for DevTools and once after attestation, a prompt that appears stops the launch, kills that browser, removes its profile, and opens the breaker at once (`security_prompt_appeared`). Cua Driver never clicks, types into, or dismisses the prompt.
4. Docs: the isolated-browser section of the browsers guide explains the keychain behaviour and the new refusal reasons.

## Tests

- `isolated_launch_uses_a_deterministic_clean_profile`: macOS args include `--use-mock-keychain` (Linux still `--password-store=basic`).
- `only_driver_owned_profiles_get_a_launch_command`: unmarked dirs, marked dirs outside the root, and missing dirs are refused; the owned profile gets the switch on macOS.
- `existing_profile_requests_never_launch_a_browser`: every existing-profile request shape leaves the spawn count at 0.
- `an_open_security_prompt_blocks_isolated_launches`, `a_prompt_raised_by_a_launch_stops_it_and_further_launches`: no spawn while a prompt is open; a prompt during launch stops it and an immediate retry is held back.
- Breaker unit tests (threshold, back-off doubling and cap, half-open, reset, prompt opens at once) and a macOS fixture test for `security_prompt_on_screen`.

Local: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::` and `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib security_prompt` on macOS arm64; clippy `-D warnings`; `bin/ci --quick`.

VM check: macOS VM, Google Chrome 154, `browser_prepare` with `isolated_new` 20 times per run; prompts counted from on-screen SecurityAgent windows and `securityd` "displaying keychain prompt" log lines, never answered.

| Run | "Chrome Safe Storage" item | Keychain prompt requests | Launch results |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (release 0.47.10) | created by Chrome itself | 0 / 20 | 20 ok |
| Before (release 0.47.10) | created by another binary (Chrome not on its access list) | 20 / 20 (one per launch, queued behind each other) | 20 ok, launching continued |
| After (this branch) | created by another binary | 0 / 20; every Chrome has `--use-mock-keychain` | 20 ok |
| After, with 20 old prompts still on screen | created by another binary | 0 new | 2 refused with `security_prompt_open`, no browser started |

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux background invoke_menu never opens a menu, so the user's typing is kept (#7371)
body:
Closes #7371. Linear: CUA-4062.

**For users:** a background `invoke_menu` on Linux no longer eats letters from what you're typing in your own window, and the menu command runs exactly once.

## Cause

`invoke_menu` resolved a path one level at a time: it fired **File**, which pops the GTK menu up, then fired **Mark** inside it. An open GTK, Qt or VCL menu grabs the core keyboard, so while it was open every key the user typed went to the menu. A swallowed space also activated the selected item, which is why **Mark** sometimes ran twice for one call (the second activation noted in the report).

## Fix

- GTK 3 and Qt publish closed menus through AT-SPI, so the final item is already in the first walk. `invoke_menu` now fires that item's own action directly. GTK runs its `activate` and leaves the menus unposted, so no menu opens and nothing grabs the keyboard.
- Background delivery never opens a menu. If an app only publishes the item once its menu is open, or declines a closed item's action, the call refuses with `background_unavailable` and runs nothing. Foreground keeps the level-by-level walk as the fallback after the direct try.

## Before and after

The reporter's `menu-keys` script, GTK 3.24, on Xvfb + openbox and on GNOME Xorg:

| | Characters lost per call | Mark activations per call |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 1-2 in 6 of 6 calls | 2 in 2 of 3 calls on Xvfb |
| After | 0 in 12 of 12 calls | exactly 1 in every call |

Controls without the call lost nothing in both runs, and after background calls the user's own File menu still opens and runs Mark from the keyboard.

## Tests

- `tests/background_menu_xorg.rs` (ignored, needs a real X11 session): a background `invoke_menu` while `xdotool` types into another window. It passes on GNOME Xorg and on Xvfb + openbox with the fix.
- Unit tests for the leaf plan (a command item runs directly; a submenu would open a menu) and for the refusal mapping.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`: 1032 passed.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux X11 background scroll on Qt moves the list or refuses (#7369)
body:
Closes #7369. Linear: CUA-4062.

**For users:** a background `scroll` on a Qt app on Linux now moves the list by every detent, or says it can't, instead of reporting success while nothing moves.

## Cause

There are two causes, one for each kind of X server.

- **No agent pointer device** (Xvfb, Xtigervnc, or no writable `/dev/uinput`): background scroll fell back to synthetic Button4/5 `XSendEvent`s. Qt reads the wheel only from XI2 scroll valuators and drops those events, so the call said "Scrolled" and nothing moved. GTK was already refused here.
- **Agent pointer available** (real Xorg): Qt re-reads a scroll device's valuators with a synchronous `XIQueryDevice` on a slave switch and on pointer enter. The first detent after the warp was a slave switch. When Qt's re-read ran after later detents had already landed, Qt took the post-scroll value as its baseline and the detents cancelled out. 3 detents down moved the list 0 or 2 detents. Qt's own input log shows the re-read reading the final value.

## Fix

- The background refusal now covers every toolkit that drops synthetic pointer input (GTK, Qt, LibreOffice VCL) when there is no agent pointer. That applies to `scroll`, `right_click`, `double_click` and `drag`. The agent wheel never falls back to `XSendEvent` for those toolkits.
- Before the first detent, the agent pointer makes the slave switch with a one-pixel step and back, confirmed through `XIQueryPointer`. It then waits on a `_NET_WM_PING` round trip, so the app has finished its re-read before any detent lands.
- The X11 result says what was sent and reports `effect: "unverifiable"` instead of "Scrolled".

## Before and after

The reporter's `scroll` script and the new test, with 3 detents down (9 rows expected):

| Setup | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Xvfb + openbox, Qt 6 | "Scrolled", 0 rows (2 of 2) | `background_unavailable`, 0 rows |
| GNOME Xorg, no uinput, Qt 6 | "Scrolled", 0 rows (3 of 3) | `background_unavailable`, 0 rows |
| GNOME Xorg, uinput, Qt 6 | 6, 0, 6 rows | 9 rows, 5 of 5 |
| GNOME Xorg, uinput, Qt 5.15 | 6, 6 rows | 9 rows, 5 of 5 |
| GNOME Xorg, uinput, Qt window inactive | not measured | 9 rows, 3 of 3 |

## Tests

- `tests/background_scroll_xorg.rs` (ignored, needs a real X11 session): scrolls a Qt list with the Qt window active and inactive. The list must move exactly 9 rows, or the call must refuse with no movement. It passes on GNOME Xorg with uinput and on Xvfb + openbox.
- Unit test for the toolkit refusal rule.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`: 1032 passed.
