title: fix(cua-driver): show when direct capture was last verified in permissions status
body:
## Why

`permissions grant` already records a successful direct-capture check (#2904), and the read-only status call already returns that record as `direct_capture_verification`. The status text dropped it to "worked last time it was checked", with no date and no source. With no record it said "not checked yet" and gave no next step. `grant` printed the same success whether macOS had just asked for consent or had answered from an earlier one, which is the issue's secondary question.

## What changed

- `permissions status` prints `Test screenshot: ✅ worked on <YYYY-MM-DD> (checked by `<cli> permissions grant`)` from the recorded verification. It still runs no probe.
- When the macOS check reports `not_checked` and nothing is recorded, status ends with `Next: run `<cli> permissions grant`.` even if both switches are on.
- After a successful `grant`, it says whether a verification was already recorded before this run's probe ("A test screenshot had already worked on <day>, so macOS may not have asked again.") or not ("This is the first working test screenshot recorded for this Cua Driver."). It then says that status now shows it.

## Scope

CLI text in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs` only. The persisted record, its validation and the probe are unchanged. Whether the probe itself raises Tahoe's consent is #2443 and is not addressed here. The "already recorded" line is the best signal the driver has. macOS does not report whether it showed a dialog.

## Blast Radius

Human-readable `permissions status` and `permissions grant` output on macOS. `--json` output is unchanged. Linux and Windows status never send `direct_capture_status`, so their text and next step are unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-driver --bin cua-driver permission_`, and the `platform-macos` `check_permissions` and `permission_observation` tests all pass. The new status test fails with the old text put back.
- `permissions status` from this branch's binary against a running installed driver prints `Test screenshot: ✅ worked on 2026-11-06 (checked by `cua-driver permissions grant`)`. The released binary prints `worked last time it was checked` for the same record.
- `permissions grant` was not run interactively because it raises system dialogs.

title: feat(cua-driver): attach to an existing Chrome profile in the background on the user's Space (macOS)
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `browser_prepare` with `strategy.kind:"existing_profile"` refuses with `background_unavailable` whenever Chrome's window is on the user's Space and another app is in front, which is the usual desktop. The only way through is `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, which puts Chrome over the user's window for about a second and, if the user is typing, fails anyway (table 1).
- What changed: the self-activation guard from #5052 now also runs when Chrome's window is shown on the user's Space. The setup loop waits for the labelled accessibility checkbox before it considers the pixel route, which cannot toggle it in the background. A Chrome window that is minimized or hidden on the user's Space, or whose Space is unknown, still refuses: Chrome brings such a window back on screen (table 3). Under the guard, setup takes no route that needs the foreground: if the setup page does not open in the background, the attach is rolled back and refused with `background_unavailable` (`cause.limitation: "setup_requires_foreground"`), and Edge's checkbox and its rollback are toggled from the keyboard. The address field is confirmed only once it reads back the exact setup URL.
- This revisits the decision in #5052 to refuse on the user's Space because the consent window "opens over the user's window for about 0.9 s". Under the guard I do not measure that for a shown window: Chrome's window was above the user's in 1 of 49 attaches, for 137 ms. I do measure it for a minimized window (0.5 s, every time), which is why that case keeps the refusal.

## Related work

Fixes #8460

Refs #5052

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): #8488, proposed and open. It states the guarantees, refusals and acceptance thresholds this PR implements. The MCP tool keeps its schema, but `browser_prepare` now attaches where it refused, its description changes, and the refusal detail `background_attach_requires` is gone.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. What the user sees during a background attach: their window stays in front and keeps the keyboard; Chrome's own window, where it is not covered, opens the setup tab, returns to the page and shows Chrome's debugging infobar ([frame](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/f10c9b50033badd103e171f546ef4e30fbbb7b04/ab/evidence/same-space-background-attach.jpg)). `end_session` turns remote debugging off the same way.
- Risk and rollback: the residual disturbance is in table 1. Chrome is the frontmost process for 0 to 63 ms per call (111 ms once) before the guard hands the front back, and a user typing 25 keys per second loses at most one keystroke in about one call in seven. Rollback is reverting the last commit; the refusal comes back.

## Validation

All on `macos-26` hosted runners (arm64), fresh profile, Chrome 157.0.8103.x (one job on 156.0.8078.82). TextEdit is in front with a typist posting a key every 40 ms; Chrome's window is behind it on the same Space. Front app and topmost window owner are polled every 3 ms. Tables 1 to 3: main is `e3b909029d`, the branch is `ec1252c0ad`. Table 4 is the current head.

**1. Attach while the user types**

| | main, background | main, `foreground` | branch, background |
|---|---|---|---|
| calls | 10 | 10 | 49 (24 first attaches after a Chrome launch, 25 in 5-rep sessions) |
| attached | 0, refused | 0, refused | 49 |
| Chrome window above the user's | never | 10/10, 728 to 1159 ms | 1/49, 137 ms |
| Chrome frontmost process | never | 10/10, 1143 to 1527 ms | 12/49, 5 to 44 ms (111 ms once) |
| keystrokes that missed the user's document | 0/188 | 136/643 | 8/4079 |
| call duration | 0.02 to 0.08 s | 3.4 to 5.9 s | 3.3 to 12.0 s, median 6.2 s |

Main's foreground attach is refused in all 10. The refusal logged for the first rep of each job is "the exact address field no longer contained the fixed setup URL": the user's keys land in Chrome.

`end_session` on the branch (25 calls, same typing): Chrome window above the user's 2/25 (19 and 27 ms), Chrome frontmost 5/25 (11 to 63 ms), keystrokes missed 3/3036, 6.4 to 14.6 s per call, median 8.6 s. Acting on the page over CDP between the two (23 calls): no change of front app or window order.

Frames, about 6 per second, from the first attaches and one 5-rep job: on the branch 0 of 1529 show anything over the user's window, 3 show its title bar inactive. On main's foreground attach 16 of 120 show Chrome in front ([frame](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/d2202ccf18a3156075cc4a69fbe98124cdb83a1c/ab/evidence/main-foreground-attach.jpg)).

Runs: [first attaches and lane](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43215177875), [5-rep sessions](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43228221601), [main](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43200020958).

The existing-profile rows no longer expect the same-Space refusal: they attach in the background on Chrome and Edge under the Focus, ZOrder, NoLeakedInput and Cursor oracles.

title: feat(cua-driver): deprecate replay_trajectory, install_ffmpeg, get_accessibility_tree
body:
Linear: CUA-4112

## What changes for users

Three tools still work but now say they are going away, and the old `page` tool can no longer run page actions. Nothing in our skills, bench, Spaces, SDK examples, cua-sandbox or the cloud repo calls any of the three tools or the `page` actions (checked with `gh search code --owner trycua`). The only outside hits: `trycua/e2e-test-agent` and the copy in `trycua/cloud` call `install_ffmpeg` only when the driver lists it, so they keep working after removal; the cloud repo's `get_accessibility_tree` hits are its own android and OSWorld servers, not the driver.

## Release notes

### Deprecated

Removed in the first Cua Driver release after **26 Nov 2026**. Until then each tool works as before, every response ends with a deprecation notice that names the date and the replacement, and `tools/list` carries a `deprecated` entry plus a DEPRECATED description prefix (so `describe` and the reference docs show it).

- `replay_trajectory`: call the recorded steps yourself with `run_steps`. Recording (`start_recording`, `stop_recording`, `get_recording_state`) stays.
- `install_ffmpeg`: install ffmpeg with your package manager (`brew install ffmpeg`, `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`, apt/dnf/pacman). The "ffmpeg was not found" recording error now says this.
- `get_accessibility_tree`: use `list_windows` and `list_apps`, and `get_window_state` for one window's tree.

### Removed

- The legacy `page` tool's page actions (`execute_javascript`, `click_element`, `insert_text`, `type_keystrokes`, `enable_javascript_apple_events`) and the `CUA_DRIVER_ENABLE_LEGACY_PAGE_MUTATIONS` switch. They were already off unless an operator opted in. `page` keeps `get_text` and `query_dom`, the way to read Safari and Firefox pages. Act on a page with the typed `browser_*` tools. The Windows bookmark JavaScript bridge, the Linux/Windows CDP evaluate paths and the macOS Apple Events preferences patcher are deleted with them.

## Design

The deprecations live in one table, `cua_driver_core::deprecation`. Removing a tool later means deleting its row and the tool.

## Verification

- `cargo test` on macOS (run on a separate host) for cua-driver-core, -contract, -sdk, -testkit, cua-driver and platform-macos: all pass, including the new tests `deprecated_tools_still_work_and_say_when_they_go`, `deprecated_tools_are_marked_in_tools_list` (end to end through the proxy), the rewritten `removed_legacy_page_actions_are_refused_even_with_the_old_opt_in` and the rewritten `page` unit tests. Changed tests also include the `server`, `session`, `telemetry` and `cli` tests that used `page` actions as examples.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` passes for the macOS crates; `bin/ci --quick` is green; `docs:check` for cua-driver is clean on macOS (Linux and Windows snapshots edited to match).
- Not run locally: the Linux and Windows builds. The Windows lane is the check for the deletions in `platform-windows` and `platform-linux`.
- Removed on purpose: the Windows-only live e2e tests that exercised the removed `page` actions (`harness_webview_page_tool`, `harness_electron_page_tool`, `harness_electron_click_element`) and `harness_webview_left_click_px_background`, which used `page.click_element` to find the button position. That pixel-click coverage needs a new way to get the position; follow-up.

title: fix(cua-driver): GTK3 disabled-control E2E case never starts its video, so the Linux GTK lane is red on main
body:
`E2E: Cua Driver release gate / gate / Linux E2E / Linux / GTK3 + GTK4 native harnesses` has been red on main since 841974073 (#7469), run 43236600698.

Every GTK3 test passes (`test result: ok. 43 passed`). The lane then fails in `cua-e2e-report` result validation:

```
[VIDEO FAIL] .../linux-gtk3-disabled-control-refused-ax-not-applicable-pid…-007/recording-error.txt
E2E behavioral video boundary was never reached; fixture setup or posture failed before capture
invalid E2E report:
video evidence is missing or empty: .../linux-gtk3-disabled-control-refused-ax-not-applicable-…/recording.mp4
behavioral video phase is not finalized for linux-gtk3-disabled-control-refused-ax-not-applicable: "pending"
Linux E2E result validation failed
```

Cause: `harness_gtk3_disabled_control_is_published_and_its_writers_refused` (libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/harness_gtk3_test.rs) sets `*evidence = recording_evidence(driver.recording_dir())` and launches the fixture with `launch_with_env`, but never calls `driver.start_behavior_recording()`. `run_case` and the stale-target case both call it after launch. So the case declares video evidence that it never records, and the report validator rejects it. This is deterministic, not flaky.

Fix: call `driver.start_behavior_recording();` right after `launch_with_env(...)` in that test, or declare the case without video evidence if a read-and-refuse case should not record.

Why the PR did not show it: on #7469 the release gate ran `lanes=quick` (shared Electron harness only), so `GTK3 + GTK4 native harnesses` was skipped. The merge-queue run skipped `E2E gate / decide`. The full GTK lane runs only on the push to main.

title: fix(cua-driver): retry release downloads for two minutes past a CDN outage
body:
## Why

On 8 Nov GitHub's release CDN answered cua-driver release downloads with HTTP 504. The installer retried three times with 1 s and 2 s waits, so a job failed with `download failed after 3 attempt(s) (HTTP 504, curl exit 0)` about three seconds after the first 504. A neighbouring job failed the same way on the `.sigstore.json` fetch. A CDN outage lasts minutes, so the retries need to cover minutes too.

## What changed

- `_install-rust.sh`: the tarball download and the `SHA256SUMS`/checksums/Sigstore bundle fetch share one `fetch_release_url` helper. It makes seven attempts, waiting 5, 10, 15, 30, 30 and 30 s between them, about two minutes in all.
- `install.ps1`: `Get-ReleaseZip` and `Get-ReleaseFile` use the same schedule from `$Script:ReleaseRetryDelays`.
- Tests: the Unix retry test now expects seven attempts and checks the waits. New tests cover a 504 outage that clears after a minute, and the checksum/bundle fetch getting the same retries. The PowerShell test expects seven attempts.

## Scope

Touches the installer scripts only. Which failures get retried is unchanged: a 404 still returns at once and is the only thing that can trigger the fallback to an older release. A 401 or another 4xx still fails at once. This PR does not add a second download source. The release assets live only on GitHub Releases, and serving the tarball from anywhere else would mean publishing it somewhere new in the release workflow.

## Tradeoffs

When GitHub is down for good, an install now fails after about two minutes, not three seconds. A user running the installer by hand sees one line per retry, giving the HTTP status and the wait.

## Blast Radius

Everyone who installs cua-driver with `install.sh` or `install.ps1`: users, the release gate, the nightly and installer-compat workflows, and the docs smoke. When downloads succeed nothing changes.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass: the `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests` and `.github/scripts/tests` suites and `bin/ci --quick`.
- The real download function ran under macOS's bash 3.2 with `set -euo pipefail` against a local HTTP server that returned four 504s and then 200. Main's script failed after three attempts. This branch downloaded the tarball on the fifth. Both returned the 404 code for a missing asset.
- The PowerShell tests and the Linux-only installer integrity tests were skipped because there was no PowerShell or Linux host to run them on.

Refs CUA-4105

title: fix(ci): check a release PR's changelog on the merge queue commit, add changelog addenda
body:
## What changed for users
Cua Driver 0.47.20 (cursor on every display, no action marks) was stuck before it could build. This lets it ship, and stops a release PR from reaching a tag with a stale changelog.

## Cause
#7483 merged at 16:04, three minutes before release PR #7486 merged at 16:07, after Release Please built it. The tag carries #7483; the immutable 0.47.20 changelog section does not. `release attribution preflight` failed with `changelog section is missing pull requests: [7483]`. Same class as 0.41.5. The existing guard (`release_pr_automerge.py staleness`) only switches auto-merge off, and cannot remove a PR already in the merge queue.

## Fix
- `ci-gate` (required) now runs `release_queue_preflight.py` on the merge queue commit of a release PR, which is main plus the release PR. A stale changelog fails the gate and ejects the release PR; Release Please rebuilds it. Does not depend on `CI_QUEUE_RUNS`. Scripts come from the base commit.
- `ci-release-metadata` calls the same script, replacing three copies of the product arguments.
- `release_attribution.py collect --changelog-addenda`: a reviewed file on main (not the tag) naming PRs a tag carries but its changelog lacks, each with a reason. Used for the existing 0.47.20 tag, which cannot be moved; `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml` passes it in both collect steps.
- Tests: addenda accepted or refused, script arguments match the release workflow, gate wiring. Reproduced against the real release commit: fails with `[7483]` without the addendum, passes with it.

After merge: rerun `cd-rust-cua-driver.yml` with `rebuild_tag=cua-driver-rs-v0.47.20`, `rebuild_sha=271ea2c365e68d5fe64a50f771949c6469faca3c` from main.

title: fix(cua-driver): disambiguate same-bounds browser windows
body:
## Summary

Two Chrome windows can share bounds while only one displays the requested title. A matching background tab in the other window currently makes `get_browser_state(pid, window_id)` refuse with two candidates.

For an otherwise ambiguous bind, use a complete native-window snapshot to check one-to-one native/CDP window assignments. Bind only when every valid assignment gives the requested window the same CDP owner. Missing, inconsistent or genuinely ambiguous evidence retains the existing refusal.

## Related work

Fixes #7362. This follows the native-window matching approach suggested in the report by @Haizhepi.

The issue is assigned to @injaneity, and @Andrew9603 has expressed interest in implementing it. I developed and verified this independently; sharing the tested patch here for coordination and maintainer review.

No RFC: this restores the existing exact-or-refuse binding contract without changing public tool schemas or permission requirements.

## Compatibility and risk

- Matching is shared code; the macOS adapter supplies the native snapshot. Other adapters retain their existing behavior through the default unsupported result.
- Only ambiguous binds take the new path. Existing exact bindings are unchanged.
- Requires complete, PID-owned, consistent geometry and a forced one-to-one assignment; caps native-window matching at 32 windows.
- Binding performs no tab activation, foreground input or page-script evaluation. A stale/incomplete snapshot refuses conservatively.

## Validation

Tested source is committed as `88aa0d10984b9f86b94bf48d5202a97d6d6b2ecb`; no executable changes were made between testing and committing.

- Complete core suite: **1,311 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored**, including integration tests and doctests.
- Focused macOS browser suite: **29 passed**.
- Full macOS suite: **745 passed, 1 failed, 13 ignored**. The failing consent-label test expects ASCII `Don't Allow` while this host returns a curly apostrophe. The identical failure was reproduced with all five contribution files restored to the upstream base.
- Strict Clippy for both changed crates, all targets: passed.
- `bin/ci --base upstream/main --quick --no-install`: **5 passed, 3 skipped**. Heavy tests, Clippy and release binding generation are skipped by quick mode; the tests and Clippy listed above were run separately. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Regression sensitivity: disabling the engine wiring reproduced the expected two-candidate refusal in the tool-level test.
- Real Chrome, same disposable profile and exact patched/baseline binaries: baseline refuses the background-title collision; patched binds the requested window exactly. Reversed native foreground order gives the same outcome. Both builds refuse genuinely duplicate selected titles. Removing the duplicate background tab makes both builds succeed.
- Each live bind preserved fixture titles, geometry and independently observed WindowServer order. Cua screen capture also worked. The disposable Chrome process/profile and private test daemons were cleaned up.

Canonical cross-platform desktop certification and hosted CI remain outstanding. This PR stays draft pending that evidence and maintainer scope review. The live Chrome check is a focused regression, not a complete desktop-matrix result.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused diff and current description.
- [x] No RFC required.
- [x] Tests and platform evidence included; remaining gaps stated.
- [x] Conventional production-fix title.
- [x] No external code incorporated; report's design suggestion credited above.
- [x] User-visible driver fix uses a release-tracked `fix(cua-driver)` title.
- [x] `bin/ci --quick` passed, with skips disclosed above.

title: Windows set_value on text fields reports success with no signal of whether the app processed the change
body:
### Summary

On Windows, `set_value` on a plain text field (WinForms TextBox, standard edit control) writes through UIA ValuePattern.SetValue and returns plain-text success (`✅ Set AXValue on [idx] (UIA ValuePattern).`) with no structured result. The write lands — the text is correct — but the target app never processes it as an input event, and the result gives the caller no way to tell "written" from "delivered". Apps that act on user input (validation, dirty flags, auto-save) behave as if nothing happened.

The combo path already handles this correctly: native Win32 combos get the app's own notifications (CBN_SELENDOK / CBN_SELCHANGE), and the non-native combo route returns structured `{ verified: false, effect: "unverifiable" }` with a warning that a UIA value write "may change the shown text without the app treating it as a selection". The tool description even admits the failure mode for web inputs — but the text-field success result carries no signal at all.

### Reproduction (measured, cua-driver-rs v0.41.3, Windows)

Target app: WinForms multiline TextBox that logs its TextChanged events. Verification used independent channels only (the app's own event log + WM_GETTEXT + a sampler watching the foreground window), not the driver's return values:

| approach | text written correctly | app saw the change | foreground stolen |
|---|---|---|---|
| background `set_value` (no focus change) | 5/5 | **0/5** | 0 |
| focus via `press_key(end)`, then a space+backspace keystroke nudge | 5/5 | 5/5 | 5/5 (UIA SetFocus pulls the background window to the foreground) |
| full keyboard path | text cleared (SetFocus selects all; typing replaces it) | 3 events | 2/2 |

So "the text is correct" (background write) and "the app reacts like a user typed" (foreground path) are mutually exclusive, and the background path's result doesn't say so.

### Suggested fix

- Mirror the combo route's structured result on the ValuePattern route: something like `{ verified: false, change_notified: false }` plus a next-step hint ("if the app must react to this value, focus the field and use type_text / delivery_mode foreground").
- Optionally: a notification-safe write variant (e.g. WM_SETTEXT with the parent notifications, or an opt-in post-write keyboard nudge) for callers that need the app to process the change without stealing foreground.

Happy to test any build; we consume the prebuilt release binaries.

title: fix(cua-driver): setting a popup in the background no longer raises its window on macOS
body:
Linear: [CUA-4113](https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-4113/cua-driver-setting-a-popup-value-in-the-background-briefly-raises-its)

**For users:** when an agent works in an app behind your window, choosing a value in that app's popup menu (or opening a context menu) no longer makes its window flash above yours. Where macOS gives no way to do it without that flash, the agent is told so and nothing changes, instead of a "done in the background" that you saw.

## The bug

Opening a menu in an app that is not frontmost (a popup button's menu, a context menu) makes WindowServer order the menu's window group to the front, and that group includes the app's window. The key-focus guard put the user's window back about 20 ms later, but the raise was on screen for a frame or two on every background `set_value` on an AppKit popup, every background `click` on one, and every background context-menu `right_click`. The tool still reported a clean background success.

There is no raise-free route for AppKit popups: a closed `NSPopUpButton` publishes no items, its `AXValue` is not settable, `AXSelectedChildren` is not settable, typing a letter into it does nothing, and the arrow keys open the menu. Pressing the popup with plain accessibility calls and no driver at all leaves the window raised for good; the driver only shortened it.

## The fix

In the background, the driver never opens a menu in a window that another app's window covers:

- `set_value`, `click` and `right_click` on such a popup are refused with `background_unavailable`, reason `popup_menu_would_raise_window`. Nothing is sent; the refusal gives the popup's current value and the route (with the user's agreement, `bring_to_front`, then `set_value`).
- `right_click`, or `click` with `button:"right"` / `action:"show_menu"`, on an element that has a context menu is refused the same way, reason `context_menu_would_raise_window`, pointing at `invoke_menu` or the shortcut.
- A Chromium `<select>` keeps its type-ahead route (the menu never opens); its fallback to opening the menu is refused the same way.
- Nothing changes when the app is frontmost, when its window is already above every other app's window, or when the menu is already open.
- If an app still raises its window or activates itself during `set_value`, the driver puts the user's window back and the result now says so in `user_disturbance` (it used to say nothing).

The macOS skill text, the tool descriptions and the recovery hints describe the new behaviour.

## Test

The macOS e2e observer now samples the window order every few milliseconds while a background action runs, so the z-order oracle fails on a raise that is put back before the action ends (before, it compared only the start and the end, which is why the old popup rows passed). title: fix(cua-driver): classify trusted browser_click effects with target readback
body:
Fixes #2883

## What was wrong

A ref-targeted `browser_click` on the default `trusted` route returned no typed action record. Canonical dispatch then built one from the legacy payload, which carries no effect, so every trusted click published `effect: "unverifiable"`. A click that toggled its target and a click that missed it looked the same.

The `dom_event` route already reads bounded target state before and after the click (#2956, landed as 1bf24b83ed). The trusted route resolves the same `backendNodeId` but never read it.

## Change

- Before the press, a trusted ref click resolves its node and reads the same bounded semantic state the `dom_event` route uses: ARIA state, `disabled`, `checked`, `value`, bounded `innerText` and the document URL. After the release it polls that state to the same 400 ms deadline.
- A change publishes `confirmed` with `value_readback` evidence. Unchanged state stays `unverifiable` with readback evidence. A missing readback, or a node that no longer resolves, stays `unverifiable` with no evidence. The record carries `trusted_input` as the route and the delivery mode that was actually used.
- Coordinate clicks have no node, and a click that opens a page dialog blocks the renderer, so both stay `unverifiable` as before.
- The record helper now takes the transport and delivery mode, so both routes share one classifier.
- `docs/action-result-contract.md` now says which `browser_click` routes are read back and what each outcome means.

Unchanged state is still reported as `unverifiable`, not `suspected_noop`. Main chose that in 045a05bff4 and documents it in the contract: effects elsewhere on the page can be invisible to a target-only readback. This PR keeps that choice for both routes.

## Scope

This PR covers only the browser side of #2883. Widening `effect_from_value_readback` across the desktop tools on macOS, Windows and Linux is a separate change. The changelog entry comes from release-please through this PR's title.

## Tests

New `browser::v2_tests` cases use the mock CDP fixture:
- `trusted_ref_click_confirms_a_target_state_change`
- `trusted_ref_click_that_changes_nothing_is_unverifiable_with_readback`
- `trusted_ref_click_without_readback_is_unverifiable_without_evidence`
- `trusted_ref_click_whose_node_does_not_resolve_is_unverifiable_without_evidence`
- `trusted_coordinate_click_has_no_target_to_read_back`

The first three fail on the commit that adds only the tests and pass with the fix. The scoped repository checks were `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets` and `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`. The macOS Lume standalone-browser lane could not boot its worker VM, so real-browser behaviour is unverified here. Linux and Windows lanes were not run.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux CUA_DRIVER_RS_REMOVE_MPX_MASTERS=1 removes the master pairs the driver takes instead of pooling them
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: since #7358 the Linux driver pools XInput2 master pairs for the X server's lifetime instead of removing them, because removing a master device crashes every running Qt 6.5+ client (#7325, QTBUG-146876). Each pooled pair carries a master keyboard. Chrome builds without Chromium daacc0455020 on X11 (every current stable channel) accepts key events only from the last-listed master keyboard, and Xorg appends an enabled device to the end of the device list, so after the first background input the pooled master keyboard is last and Chrome drops all core keyboard input, including the user's own typing. Chromium fixed this in [daacc0455020](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/daacc045502047fd60cbaefb416bb095fea1d3bb) (main@{#1742023}, 2026-11-11), but no stable release carries the fix yet.
- What changed: an opt-in, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_REMOVE_MPX_MASTERS=1` in the environment of `cua-driver serve` (only the value `1` counts, read once per process), brings back removal for the pairs this driver takes, for deployments that drive Chrome on X11 and accept the Qt 6.5+ removal crash:
  - a session adds a fresh pair instead of claiming a pooled one;
  - `end_session`, the idle teardown and the popup waiter unplug the uinput slaves, then `XIRemoveMaster` the pair (its devices go back to the virtual core devices); a failed removal logs a warning;
  - a slave that fails to attach gets its fresh pair removed;
  - startup removes a Cua pair whose holder is provably gone, or a free pair whose creator, named in the pair, is gone.

  With the variable unset, every path keeps today's pooling, with no extra reads at startup. The no-removal guard test still forbids `XIRemoveMaster` everywhere except inside `remove_master_pointer`, and requires its one call site to be `MasterMode::retire`. `LINUX.md` documents the trade-off and that the flag does not shorten the Chrome loss: it lasts as long as the session holds the pair, up to the 30-minute idle timeout.

## Related work

Refs #7325, #7358

Upstream Chromium fix: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/daacc045502047fd60cbaefb416bb095fea1d3bb

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. This adds one opt-in environment variable on Linux X11 and changes no default.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux X11 only. Default behaviour is unchanged. With the flag set, every running Qt 6.5+ client on the display can crash when a pair is removed (#7325); this is the documented trade-off and the reason it is opt-in.
- Risk and rollback: unset the variable and restart the daemon to get the pooling back. Pairs that a flagged daemon already removed are gone; pairs it leaves behind are pooled by a later unflagged daemon as usual.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (Linux arm64 container, Rust 1.97.1, under Xvfb):
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux`: 1063 passed, 0 failed, 47 ignored (lib 1049 passed; ignored = the tests already marked `#[ignore]` on main)
  - new `mpx_pool_tests`: `only_a_remove_mpx_masters_value_of_1_turns_removal_on`, `only_pool_mode_takes_from_the_pool_and_only_remove_mode_removes_on_release`, `the_startup_reaper_pools_gone_holders_and_with_removal_also_removes_free_pairs_of_gone_creators`, and the extended `no_code_path_removes_an_xi2_master_device`.
- Manual or platform evidence (Ubuntu 24.04 Xorg VM, XFCE session, Chrome stable on X11; after background input, 9 keys typed through XTEST into the Virtual core keyboard while Chrome is focused):
  - 0.47.14 with pooling: Chrome received 0 of 9 keys in every sequence.
  - Same build with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_REMOVE_MPX_MASTERS=1`: 9 of 9 keys arrived; 0 extra master pairs remained after 69 background calls.
  - Control run without the flag: 9 of 9 keys lost, with the pooled pair listed in `xinput list`.
  - Root cause: Chromium `ui/events/devices/x11/touch_factory_x11.cc` lines 144-145 and 174-178 at 32f99a1f keep only the last master keyboard for key events; Xorg 21.1.12 `dix/devices.c` lines 405-410 append an enabled device to the end of the device list.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Qt 6.5+ crash with the flag set is expected and not covered here; CI on this PR.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`)

title: fix(cua-driver): declare each platform's accepted browser defaults
body:
Linux browser actions now render the agent cursor. #3778 implemented `visualize_browser_action` on Linux. This PR covers the rest of the issue: no platform can drop back to a silent `BrowserPlatform` default again without the change being declared and reviewed.

## Change

- `ACCEPTED_DEFAULTS` in the `browser/platform.rs` tests lists, for each platform adapter (Linux, macOS, Windows), every defaulted `BrowserPlatform` method it leaves in place, with a reason.
- `every_platform_declares_the_browser_platform_defaults_it_accepts` reads the trait and each adapter's `impl BrowserPlatform for` block. So the test goes red in three cases: a new defaulted trait method, a dropped override, or a newly added override that is still listed as a default.

The `discover_spawned_endpoint` question from the issue: keeping the default on macOS and Linux is deliberate. The override exists for a short-lived launcher process that hands the browser to a descendant. Only Windows does that (`clean_spawn_exit_can_be_launcher_handoff` in `prepare.rs` is Windows-only). On macOS and Linux the spawned browser owns its listener, so the default's exact-pid check is the right one. The table records this.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse trusted browser ref clicks whose point misses the ref
body:
Fixes #2882

## Problem

`browser_click` and `browser_pointer` send a trusted CDP mouse event at a ref's box center and never check what the page draws at that point. When a sticky footer, modal or overlay covers part of the element, or the center sits past the viewport edge, the event lands on the other element, and the tool still reports a click. That is Finding 2 in the issue: the event reached a `DIV` instead of the row, and the result looked the same as a success.

## Change

A trusted ref is now resolved through one helper (`browser/input.rs`) shared by both tools:

1. It scrolls the ref into view and takes its content-box center, as before.
2. It checks the point is inside the frame's visible viewport (`Page.getLayoutMetrics`, pinch-zoom offset included).
3. It hit-tests the point with `DOM.getNodeForLocation` and accepts it only when the hit is the ref or one of its descendants, shadow hosts included. Chromium hit-tests that method in document coordinates. At a scrolled offset, viewport coordinates return "No node found", so the helper adds the layout viewport's scroll offset.

4. After focus emulation starts and settles, right before dispatch, it hit-tests the same point again. A page focus handler can draw an overlay in that window. On that refusal it leaves focus emulation, and if that fails the refusal says so with `detail.focus_emulation_restored: false`.

On a miss, no `Input.*` call is sent, and a miss at resolution also skips focus emulation. The tool returns `browser_input_trust_unavailable` with `detail.hit_test` set to `covered` or `outside_viewport`, `alternative_route: "dom_event"` and `trusted_delivery_attempted: false`, so the existing recovery hint points at the DOM route.

For a ref-to-ref drag, the origin is checked again in place after the destination scrolls into view, because that scroll can move the origin.

Not changed: coordinate clicks are sent where the caller aims, `dom_event` dispatches on the element as before, and the per-platform background declarations stay as they are. `DOM.getNodeForLocation` joins the read-only existing-profile CDP allowlist. Two copies of `quad_center` and the scroll and box lookup are folded into the new helper.

Other parts of the issue are left alone here. Windows and Linux foreground re-validation and the consent-surface hypothesis are measurement tasks for those desktops. Effect classification is #2883.

## Tests

- New unit cases in `v2_tests.rs` use a fixture that hit-tests like Chromium (document coordinates, an error for an empty point). They cover a covered ref (click and pointer), a point outside the viewport, a scrolled page, a hit on a descendant, a drag whose destination scroll moves the origin, an overlay drawn when focus emulation starts (click and pointer, plus a failed focus restore), and controls showing coordinate clicks and `dom_event` are not hit-tested. Each behaviour case fails on the code before this change.
- New standalone-browser E2E case `standalone_browser_trusted_click_covered_ref`. A transparent overlay covers the counter button. The trusted ref click must refuse with the counter unchanged, and `dom_event` on the same ref must then increment it. It is added to the macOS/Linux and Windows browser lane lists.
- The skill doc (`BROWSER.md`) already said the driver hit-tests before dispatch. It now describes the actual check and its refusal detail, and the public browser guide's refusal table mentions the hit-test case.

## Test plan

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and compiling the e2e browser test crate.
- macOS Lume full lane: the AppKit matrix and the Chrome standalone-browser matrix, including the new covered-ref row.
- Real Chrome CDP checks before writing the code: document-coordinate hit testing, a hidden-tab trusted click landing on exactly what the hit test names, OOPIF child sessions, and open shadow roots.
- Not run here: Linux X11/Wayland and Windows desktop lanes.

title: cua-driver: measure trusted browser input foreground on Windows and Linux, the consent-prompt confound, and dom_event-only limits
body:
## Context

#2882 is closed by #7512, which fixes its Finding 2: a trusted ref click now hit-tests its point and refuses with `browser_input_trust_unavailable` (`detail.hit_test: covered | outside_viewport`) instead of landing on another element. The measurement tasks in #2882 were outside that PR. This issue carries them forward.

Current state on main:

- macOS no longer declares `standalone_trusted_input_background_limitation`. It was re-measured on Chrome 155 in #5109 and fixed in #5110.
- Linux still declares it (`platform-linux/src/browser_platform.rs`: "Chromium's trusted CDP Input route activates its standalone browser window on Linux"). That claim was never measured against a verified background baseline.
- Windows declares no limitation, so trusted input is allowed. That has not been re-checked since #2261.
- macOS separately declares `existing_profile_attach_background_limitation`: Chrome brings itself to the front about 50 ms after any new DevTools client connects, to show "Allow remote debugging?".

## 1. Re-check the trusted foreground route on Windows and Linux

For each platform, with a standalone Chrome/Chromium that is verifiably not foreground before each dispatch:

- [ ] Windows: trusted `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` (with and without focus emulation) into the active tab of a window behind another app, and into a hidden tab. Sample the foreground window before dispatch and repeatedly after it. Prove delivery with a page-side capture listener that records `event.isTrusted` and coordinates.
- [ ] Linux X11: the same measurement.
- [ ] Linux Wayland: the same measurement on each compositor the driver supports for browser input.
- [ ] Record the Chrome version and the method for each result. Remove the Linux declaration if it does not reproduce, as macOS did in #5110.

#2285 tracks finding a trusted full-background route on macOS and Linux if one is needed. This issue only asks whether the current declarations still match measured behaviour.

## 2. Consent-surface confound

The original split (trusted activates on macOS and Linux, not on Windows) may have come from Chrome's connect-time "Allow remote debugging?" prompt rather than from input dispatch. On macOS, Chrome was seen coming to the front right after a fresh CDP connection, seconds before any input was sent.

- [ ] On Windows and Linux, measure foreground changes on a fresh DevTools connection with no input sent, separately from the input measurement in section 1.
- [ ] Repeat with a shared, already-approved connection (#5115), so a fresh connection is not part of the input measurement.
- [ ] State for each platform whether the original measurement could have counted the prompt as input-route activation.

## 3. Limits that only show up with `dom_event`

`dom_event` replays synthetic pointer and mouse events and then `click` at the element's center (#5109). It is the background alternative wherever trusted input is refused. Make a list of what it cannot do, each item with a minimal repro page and the result on current Chrome:

- [ ] Controls that check `event.isTrusted` (already known; covered by the `trust_gated_dom_click` row).
- [ ] Flows that need a user-activation token: `window.open`, fullscreen, clipboard read/write, media/autoplay with sound, `showPicker()`.
- [ ] File inputs and file pickers.
- [ ] HTML5 drag and drop (`dragstart`/`drop` with a `DataTransfer`).
- [ ] Paste-gated and clipboard-gated inputs.
- [ ] Elements that open a JS dialog (#3982).
- [ ] Clicks reported `ok` with no effect (#2953).

The outcome decides whether `dom_event`-only is a legitimate simplification or the trusted route must stay.

## Done when

- [ ] Platform declarations on main match the measured behaviour on all three platforms.
- [ ] `Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md` (route text and platform matrix) and `Skills/cua-driver/MACOS.md` match those results.
- [ ] The `dom_event` limits list is in `BROWSER.md`.

Related: #2882, #7512, #2285, #2892, #5109. Effect classification was #2883.

title: Cua Driver: optional VNC backend on macOS to get through first-run permission (TCC) setup
body:
## Problem

The first time Cua Driver runs on a Mac, it needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permission (TCC). Until those are granted, Cua Driver can't click or see anything, so it can't help the user grant them. People get stuck on this step, especially on remote or headless Macs where nobody is in front of the screen.

We already work around this in our own test VMs by driving the macOS permission prompts over VNC (vncdotool). That works because VNC input comes from the Screen Sharing service, which doesn't depend on Cua Driver's own TCC grants.

## Proposal

Add an optional VNC (RFB) backend to Cua Driver for macOS, used as a fallback when the native backend lacks TCC permission. First use case: walking through the TCC grant flow (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility / Screen Recording, and the first-run prompts).

- Connect to the Mac's Screen Sharing / Remote Management VNC server (local or remote), take screenshots and send pointer and key events over RFB.
- Expose it as an explicit opt-in (e.g. a `backend: "vnc"` option or a dedicated `grant_permissions` flow), never a silent default.
- Hand back to the native backend as soon as the permissions are granted.

## Things to decide

- **Security and consent:** VNC needs Screen Sharing enabled and credentials. Where do they come from, how are they stored (Keychain), and how does the user explicitly approve this? The driver must never type a user's password or answer passkey/2FA/Keychain prompts on its own.
- **Scope:** TCC setup only, or a general-purpose fallback backend?
- **Local vs remote:** local loopback VNC vs connecting to another Mac.
- **Detection:** how the driver knows it's missing TCC and should offer the fallback.
- **Cross-platform:** whether the same RFB backend is useful on Linux/Windows hosts too.

## Acceptance

On a fresh macOS install with Screen Sharing enabled, a user (or agent, with the user's approval) can go from "Cua Driver has no permissions" to "Accessibility and Screen Recording granted" without touching the Mac physically, and the driver then switches to its native backend.

title: fix(ci): keep the Windows rust leg's compile cache
body:
`rust (windows-latest)` in `CI: cua SDK` compiles from nothing on every run. Its sccache family (`libs-cua-test`) has no Windows entry: the action saves only when the whole job passes, and on main this job has not passed since 26 Oct, so main never saved one and every run restores nothing (the latest PR run logged `Cache not found` and spent 30 of its 60 minutes compiling). A run that times out or fails a test throws the compile away and the next one starts cold again.

The `rust` job now uses `save-always: "true"` with a closing `rust-cache-save` step under `always()`, the same pattern the swift smoke job already uses. Main saves the warm compile whatever the tests do, and pull requests and the merge queue restore it. Caching only changes when saves happen, so pull requests behave the same apart from the restore.

A repository test now checks that every `save-always` rust-cache step has a closing save step that runs under `always()` and reads that step's outputs.

- `pytest .github/scripts/tests/test_rust_cache_action.py`: passes, and the Windows-leg check fails without the workflow change.
- the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`, actionlint).
- After merge: the first main run of `CI: cua SDK` saves `sccache-v2-Windows-X64-libs-cua-test_<day>` even if a test fails (shown by `gh cache list`).

title: [Lume] sip off fails on macOS 27: Utilities click lands on the Recovery menu, and Recovery's language follows the host region
body:
`lume sip off` fails on a macOS 27.2.1 guest: it opens the Recovery app menu instead of Utilities, so Terminal never launches and the `csrutil prompt` OCR wait times out. Disabling SIP by hand over the same VNC session works.

**Setup:** Lume 0.6.1 (the code is unchanged on `main`), host macOS 27.3, guest created from `UniversalMac_27.2.1_26B131_Restore.ipsw` with `--unattended tahoe`. The preset itself worked on 27: the credential preflight and SSH both pass.

```
lume sip off faim-sip --yes --admin-password-stdin --screenshot-dir shots
Error: VNC driver timeout: Framebuffer for 'csrutil prompt' did not contain expected text; last OCR text: recovery & file edit utilities window restore. recovery version 1.0 (531) ...
```

## 1. The Utilities click lands on the wrong menu

`Sip.swift` clicks a fixed point, then arrows down three items:

```swift
try driver.click(x: 243, y: 14)
```

On 27 the Recovery framebuffer is 1920×1440 (the VM's display setting is 1024×768), and the menu bar reads `Recovery  File  Edit  Utilities  Window`. (243, 14) hits **Recovery**, so the three `down` presses select "About Recovery". `03-terminal-highlighted.png` shows the Recovery menu open with "About Recovery" highlighted. On this guest, Utilities sits at about (480, 30) and its Terminal item at about (487, 192).

Locating "Utilities" by OCR, or opening Terminal with its shortcut (the Utilities menu lists Terminal as ⇧⌘T), would avoid depending on the resolution.

## 2. Recovery's language follows the guest's `prev-lang:kbd`, which the preset leaves unset

On a host whose region isn't English-speaking, the first run's Recovery came up in German ("Wiederherstellung, Ablage, Bearbeiten, Dienstprogramme"). The language step only presses Enter, so it accepts that default, and the English-only menu and OCR steps can't match. `nvram prev-lang:kbd` was unset in the guest. After `sudo nvram prev-lang:kbd=en-US:0` in the guest, Recovery started in English.

Setting `prev-lang:kbd` in the unattended presets, or before `lume sip` boots Recovery, would make the flow independent of the host's region.

## Manual workaround

```
lume run <vm> --no-display --recovery-mode true --vnc-port 5999 --vnc-password <pw>
vncdo -s 127.0.0.1::5999 -p <pw> key right pause 1 key right pause 1 key enter   # Options
# Enter on the language screen, wait for the main menu
vncdo ... move 480 30 click 1        # Utilities
vncdo ... move 487 192 click 1       # Terminal
vncdo ... pause 5 type "csrutil disable" key enter pause 4 key y key enter pause 3 type lume key enter
```

`csrutil status` in the normally booted guest then reports `disabled`. I can attach the step screenshots if they'd help.

title: fix(cua-driver): place the session cursor for desktop-scope keyboard actions
body:
Fixes #3011

## Why

#4287 made `press_key`, `hotkey` and untargeted `type_text` place a named session's agent cursor before window-targeted input, and made a semantic cue re-reveal an idle-faded cursor. The desktop-scope form (`scope: "desktop"`, no `pid` or `window_id`) still returned on macOS and Windows before any placement, so a session whose first action was a desktop-scope key or text call kept `get_agent_cursor_state` at `position: null`. Linux already placed the cursor there.

## What changed

- macOS: the desktop-scope branches of `press_key`, `hotkey` and `type_text` call the new `position_desktop_keyboard_cursor`, which resolves the frontmost app's focused window and hands it to the existing `position_keyboard_cursor`.
- macOS and Windows: `position_keyboard_cursor` falls back to the hardware pointer position when there is no window centre. That makes the order explicit element, remembered position, window centre, pointer, as on Linux. Windows desktop-scope branches pass the foreground window they already resolve. `pointer_location` moved from the macOS drag tool into `cursor_tools` so both callers share it.
- New desktop E2E row `desktop_keyboard_first_session_places_its_cursor` in `agent_cursor_showcase_test` (macOS and Windows). It brings the native harness to the front, sends a desktop-scope `press_key` from a fresh session, and requires the cursor on that window's centre. `docs/cursor-themes.md` documents the desktop-scope placement.

## Scope

Covers only the desktop-scope keyboard and text calls on macOS and Windows. Anonymous calls (no `session` or `_session_id`) keep their existing behavior. The physical pointer, focus and frontmost app don't change, because the move happens only in the overlay. The cross-platform first-action pixel oracle stays with #2879, and following focus changes during typing stays with #1945.

## Blast Radius

Named sessions that send desktop-scope keyboard or text input. Placement happens before input and is observational: geometry or overlay failures never change the input result.

## Verification

- On a macOS host at the base commit, a fresh session's desktop-scope `press_key` left `position: null`. At this branch, desktop-scope `press_key`, `hotkey` and `type_text` each set a position. `get_cursor_position` was the same before and after, and the frontmost app did not change. An anonymous call still left the cursor unplaced.
- The scoped repository checks pass: rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the cross-compiled Windows check, and the unit tests for `cua-driver-e2e`, `platform-macos` and `platform-windows`.
- Desktop E2E at the head passes on macOS hosted (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43349365016), Windows (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43349361911) and Linux X11 (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43349368464). Both keyboard-first rows pass on macOS and Windows. With the new row named so that it ran first, the Windows lane's window-targeted keyboard-first row refused with `input_delivery_stalled` (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43326094731). At main, and with the current name, both rows pass (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43330261783), so the row's name keeps it second.

title: raw-linux bench arm: set an AT-SPI timeout so one unresponsive app doesn't stall every script by 15 s
body:
Found by the raw-linux full bench run (branch `exp/raw-linux-full`, head `3172a5891d`).

**What happens.** When one app on the AT-SPI bus stops answering, a fresh process's first desktop walk waits the full D-Bus default timeout (15 s) before moving on. The raw-linux arm starts a fresh runner (`tools/raw_linux/runner.py`) per call, so from the point an app hung, almost every raw script took about 15 s. That stall is most of the arm's wall-time gap against the driver arms, whose long-lived daemon pays the cost once.

**Probe.** `Atspi.set_timeout(800, 800)` in a fresh process cuts the wait to about 0.8 s (probe `hung1` in the run's evidence).

**Fix.** Either call `Atspi.set_timeout` in the runner, or keep one runner per trial instead of one per call. Then rerun the 7 BenchLab tasks to measure the wall time again (the improvement is only estimated so far).

Which app hung wasn't confirmed; probably a leftover from earlier trials.

title: raw-linux bench: add a multi-app task that isn't at the floor for main

title: cua-driver: explain ax_window_unresolved when Chrome has its accessibility tree off
body:
## Summary

When Chrome has not enabled its accessibility tree, `get_window_state` on any Chrome window returns `ax_window_unresolved` ("none of the 0 AXWindow elements under that pid"). Window-scoped actions are then refused, including pixel clicks, `set_window_frame` and `invoke_menu`, even with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`. Desktop-scope input (`get_desktop_state` plus desktop clicks and typing) still works.

The behaviour is correct, since there's no window to target. But the error doesn't tell the agent why or what to do, so agents lose time retrying window-scoped calls.

## Observed

- cua-driver 0.36.0 on macOS. `health_report` ok, Accessibility and Screen Recording granted, daemon running.
- Chrome (signed-in profile, a normal user launch) exposes 0 AXWindow elements for every window.
- `get_window_state({pid, window_id})` returns `ax_window_unresolved`, and the hint says to "act with foreground".
- A `window_id`-scoped foreground click is still refused because no window screenshot is available.
- Desktop-scope clicks on `get_desktop_state` screenshots work.

## Proposed improvements

1. **Clearer error and hint.** When the target app has 0 AXWindow elements and it's a Chromium browser, say so explicitly. For example: "Chrome is not exposing its accessibility tree (0 AX windows). Use desktop scope (`get_desktop_state` with `target:{kind:"desktop"}`) or enable Chrome accessibility." Do the same for other apps with no AX windows.
2. **Document the Chrome accessibility setting.** Chrome only builds its tree when assistive tech is detected. Document enabling it, e.g. launch with `--force-renderer-accessibility` or turn it on at `chrome://accessibility`. Consider a `check_permissions` or `health_report` line that flags it for running Chromium browsers.
3. **Optional:** let a `window_id` target fall back to a window-bounds crop of the desktop screenshot when the window can't be resolved through AX but CoreGraphics can still see it, so foreground clicks can still be scoped to that window.

## Why it matters

Agents driving signed-in Chrome sessions hit this often, and the current message reads like a permissions or driver failure.

title: fix(ci): run driver release-gate lanes in the merge queue
body:
Merge queue entries now run the Cua Driver release gate's push-only lanes that fit the queue's 60-minute timeout, on the merged result. Before this, every `merge_group` run skipped (`CI_QUEUE_RUNS` is off), so a break those lanes catch only showed up on main after merge. All 4 red release-gate runs since 28 Oct were the Linux GTK3 + GTK4 lane, which pull requests never run.

What runs in the queue
- A workflow runs there only if the base commit's `.github/ci-areas.json` lists it under `queue` and the change reaches it. The list is one workflow: `E2E: Cua Driver release gate`. CI: Quick's scope job passes `--merge-queue` to `ci_gate_scope.py`, and every other `merge_group` run skips as before. A base commit whose selector predates the flag also skips, so nothing changes until this is on main.
- The release gate's `decide` compares the queue's base and head through the gated-path script. A gated change gets `lanes=queue`: every Linux lane, and the Windows native, capture and installer lanes. A change outside the gated paths runs nothing. A file list the API cannot give in full (an error on any page, or 300 files) runs the lanes. The same read now guards the post-merge push decision, which used to accept a partial list.
- Left to the run after merge: Windows shared Electron + Tauri (up to 54 min; the pull request's quick lane ran its Electron cells), hosted macOS (51 to 73 min plus runner queueing) and the standalone browser lanes (40 to 53 min). Measured lane end times over 11 full runs: Linux lanes up to 44 min, Windows native 32, capture 25, installer 21.
- `CI: cua SDK` stays out. Its Windows rust leg needs more than an hour: the long test step compiles for 26 to 31 minutes even with a warm cache, then runs for about 17.
- `e2e-rust-windows.yml` accepts a comma list of lanes. Certification still needs `all`.

How the gate judges it
- `ci-gate` judges a workflow's queue run in addition to its pull request run, never instead of it. Before, with `CI_QUEUE_RUNS` on, a green queue run replaced a red pull request run. A new test shows the old wait script passing that case and this one failing it.

Test plan
- `pytest .github/scripts/tests`: the whole directory passes (2026 tests, 0 failures, as at the base plus the new ones). New tests cover the masking case, the selector's `--merge-queue` decision, the queue lanes, the partial file list and the Windows comma list.
- The release gate's `result` expression, run in jq for pull request quick, push full, and merge queue with lanes green, skipped or failed.
- the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`, actionlint, the no-larger-runners guard).
- Not run here: a live merge queue entry. The first queued pull request that touches a gated path after this merges is the live proof.

title: feat(cua-driver): refusals say what will work instead
body:
## What changed for users

When Cua Driver refuses an action, it now says what to try instead, in the result text as well as in `hint` and `next_call`.

## Changes

- A refusal's text ends with a `Next: <hint>` line. Clients that show only the text now deliver the hint (before, it sat only in `structuredContent`).
- Electron background scroll, typing and key refusals name the routes that work (`get_window_state` + `element_token`, `set_value`, `invoke_menu`, `set_window_frame`) and name foreground delivery only with its condition.
- New hints for `element_disabled` (macOS, Linux, Windows), `invalid_element_token`, window mismatch codes, `input_delivery_unavailable`, `modified_pointer_unavailable`, `ax_timeout`.
- No new contract fields: `hint` and `next_call` already cover the machine-readable side on every platform. `docs/action-result-contract.md` notes the text line.

## Tests

Unit tests in `recovery_hint/tests.rs` assert each new code and Electron variant carries a hint and stays within 240 characters, that refusal text ends with the hint, and that confirmed results are untouched. The AppKit e2e disabled-control test also checks the refusal has a next step. Built and run on CI only (not on this host).

title: fix(cua-driver): do not strip proc-macro dylibs in release builds
body:
Fixes CUA-4124 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-4124).

**Users:** `install-local.sh --release` builds Cua Driver again on current Xcode / Command Line Tools without setting `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=none`.

**Cause:** `strip = "symbols"` (#7316) also applies to proc-macro dylibs. The post-link `strip` on Xcode/CLT 27 leaves a mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool, so `dlopen` refuses the dylib and every derive crate fails (`mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool`, `can't find crate for zeroize_derive`). Reproduced on macos-test-2 (CLT 27, ld-27037.1) with a 2-line crate: serde + derive + `strip = "symbols"`.

**Fix:** `[profile.release.build-override] strip = "none"` in the cua-driver and cua workspaces. Proc-macros and build scripts never ship; shipped artifacts keep `strip = "symbols"`.

**Evidence (macos-test-2):** before, `cargo build --release -p cua-driver` on origin/main fails in 16 s with `can't find crate for zeroize_derive`. After: see the comment below.

title: perf(cua-driver): thin Python wheel that fetches the signed executable on first run
body:
Refs CUA-4110

**For users:** `pip install cua-driver` downloads 60% less (155 MB -> 61 MB across the five wheels of a release), and on macOS the `cua-driver` command now runs the same signed Cua Driver app as a normal install, so permission grants are shared instead of being a separate "cua-driver" entry.

## What changed
The wheel shipped the driver twice: the `cua-driver` executable (52 MB on macOS) and the SDK library (42 MB). `import cua_driver` needs the library in-process; the executable is a client that, on macOS, launches `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` anyway.

- Thin wheel: SDK library + `_release.json` (the signed release archive of this exact version, its size and SHA-256 from the release's checksums). Same approach as cua-cli in #7474.
- First `cua-driver` run (or `python -m cua_driver.fetch fetch`) downloads that archive, checks size + SHA-256, then installs:
  - macOS: notarized `CuaDriver.app` to `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, only after `codesign --verify --deep --strict -R` against Cua's team requirement (`com.trycua.driver`, team YCK386LBJ7). Staged next to the target and moved with one rename. An existing app is used and never overwritten (older ones get a hint to run `cua-driver update --apply`). If `/Applications` is not writable the error points at install.sh.
  - Linux/Windows: the `-binary` archive unpacked into a per-version cache; regular files only, no absolute or `..` paths, links refused.
- Offline overrides: `CUA_DRIVER_BINARY`, `CUA_DRIVER_DOWNLOAD_BASE` (mirror or `file://`), `CUA_DRIVER_CACHE_DIR`. `build_wheel.py --bundle-cli` keeps the old layout for local builds.
- CD smoke test: every platform runs `cua-driver --version` through the real download path, then a second run with an unreachable mirror; a size gate fails any wheel over 25 MB.

## Sizes (0.47.22 wheels, measured; thin wheels repacked without the executable)
| wheel | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| macOS universal2 | 41.1 MB | 17.5 MB |
| Linux arm64 | 26.8 | 11.9 |
| Linux x86_64 | 28.8 | 12.9 |
| Windows x64 | 30.2 | 9.8 |
| Windows arm64 | 28.0 | 9.1 |
| total | 154.7 | 61.2 (-60%) |

## macOS permissions finding (macOS 26 test VM, SIP off)
- Old wheel: the bare binary outside the app is its own responsible process (the driver itself warns "running unbundled"). System Settings showed a separate `cua-driver` entry, off, and TCC recorded it as a path-keyed row for the site-packages location (`client_type 1`, auth 0). Every venv or upgrade is a new path, so a new identity.
- Thin path: with grants already made for `com.trycua.driver`, the wheel's fetch code installed the notarized 0.47.22 app to `/Applications`; `spctl` says "Notarized Developer ID", `permissions status` reported Accessibility and Screen Recording granted with no prompt, attributed to `com.trycua.driver`. Replacing it with 0.47.24 kept both grants and the TCC rows unchanged (same bundle id and designated requirement).
- The codesign requirement check passes the real app, fails for a wrong team id, and fails for a tampered bundle.
- The SDK library cannot be dropped: it is what Python loads. It cannot be shared with the executable either, as the app bundle holds no library. Making the executable link the shared library instead of embedding the driver would save about 40 MB more per macOS download; that is a Rust build change, not in this PR.

## Not done
- No real wheel was built on this machine (rule: builds only on CI or the Mac test host); sizes come from repacking the released wheels. The CD run will show the real ones.
- Published thin wheels pin release archives by SHA-256, so release assets must not be re-uploaded after promotion (documented in docs/pypi-publishing.md).

Tests: `tests/test_fetch.py` (download, tamper, size, traversal, symlink, mirror, offline, macOS signature gate and app handling), `test_build_wheel.py`, `bin/ci --quick` green.

title: fix(cua-agent-setup): use one separator in Windows paths
body:
With the earlier steps of `CI: cua SDK`'s `rust (windows-latest)` fixed, 12 cua-agent-setup tests fail on Windows. Two causes, plus one fixture.

- **CRLF skills.** `libs/cua/skills/**` is checked out with CRLF on Windows (`* text=auto`), so the skills cua-agent-setup embeds and installs differ from every other platform's, and the front-matter checks (`\nname: cua-driver\n`, the version line) fail. `.gitattributes` now pins them to LF, like the other byte-compared trees. The cua-driver skill is bundled from `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver` since #7774, so that folder is pinned too. The index already holds them as LF, so no file changes.
- **Mixed separators.** Several paths were built as `home.join(".local/bin")` or `join("CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS")`, which leaves `/` inside a Windows path (`...\home\.local/bin\cua-driver.exe`). The crate's `registry::join` and `connection::tilde` already build paths one segment at a time. The other joins (bin dirs, AppData, the app bundle, the Cursor and OpenClaw sign-in files) now do the same, and `claude_login`'s `~/...` description uses `connection::tilde`, so a Windows user reads `~/.claude/.credentials.json` instead of `~/.claude\.credentials.json`. The tests build their expected paths the same way through a small `rel()` helper.
- **Fixture.** `detection_uses_path_markers_and_app_bundles` wrote `codex.exe` only under `cfg(unix)`, so on Windows there was no codex to detect.

Test plan
- `cargo test -p cua-agent-setup` on macOS: every suite passes.
- `cargo xwin test --no-run -p cua-agent-setup --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`: compiles.
- `rust (windows-latest)` (ci:full) on this PR runs them on Windows. A probe branch with this PR, #7508 and the 90-minute change ran the whole Windows job.
- the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`).

title: cua-driver Linux X11: click that opens a modal reports not_restored focus error even though it worked
body:
On Linux X11, a foreground `click` on a button that opens a modal dialog returns an error even though the click worked:

> the input was sent, but the prior focus could not be restored: not_restored

The click lands and the modal opens. The modal takes focus, as it should, and then the focus guard tries to give focus back to the window that the modal now blocks. That restore fails, so the whole call comes back as an error.

Where: `platform-linux` `interaction/mod.rs` and `click.rs` in `libs/cua-driver/rust`. This behaviour already exists on main; #7477 did not add it.

Seen during the live X11 verification of #7477 (GTK3 harness, Xvfb + openbox + picom). The #7477 test now opens its dialog through the AT-SPI action to work around this.

Expected: when focus moves to a modal transient of the target window (`WM_TRANSIENT_FOR` names the target), treat that as an expected result of the click, not as a failed restore.

title: ci(cua-sdk): build the xcframework slices on parallel runners
body:
Fixes CUA-4125 (https://linear.app/trycua/issue/CUA-4125).

**Users:** the Swift `CuaSDKFFI.xcframework.zip` reaches a cua SDK release in about 50 minutes instead of 1h40 to 2h30 (no more 150 minute cancellations).

title: cua-driver (macOS): a second daemon started from the same executable gets no ScreenCaptureKit screenshot and dies with SIGTRAP
body:
### Primary area

cua-driver (macOS)

### Summary

While one `cua-driver serve` process that has taken a display screenshot is alive, a second `serve` process started from the same executable gets no answer from ScreenCaptureKit for `get_desktop_state`. On current main the second daemon then dies with SIGTRAP and every later call to it fails.

### Reproduction

1. Start a daemon on its own socket and take a display screenshot: `cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/a.sock --no-overlay &` then `cua-driver call --socket /tmp/a.sock get_desktop_state`.
2. Leave it running. Start a second daemon from the same binary on another socket and do the same: `cua-driver serve --socket /tmp/b.sock --no-overlay &` then `cua-driver call --socket /tmp/b.sock get_desktop_state`.

Script that does this for any sequence of builds: [`multi_daemons.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/a07bfcd2f0da56460f159b6d2f7c188cad016b66/ab/multi_daemons.py).

It does not need the driver. A 45-line Swift program that takes one screenshot and stays alive shows the same thing when started twice from one path: [`two_clients.swift`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/a07bfcd2f0da56460f159b6d2f7c188cad016b66/ab/two_clients.swift).

```
swiftc -O -o two_clients two_clients.swift
./two_clients rect 20 &     # ok 1920x1080 after 112 ms
sleep 3; ./two_clients rect 0   # Trace/BPT trap: 5
```

### Expected behavior

The second daemon captures the display like the first one.

### Actual behavior

Second daemon, main `57edfe91a8` (0.47.22):

```
WARN platform_macos::capture: ScreenCaptureKit display capture failed: ScreenCaptureKit capture timed out after 5000 ms
```

then the process exits with SIGTRAP (`EXC_BREAKPOINT`), top frames:

```
@objc completion handler block implementation for @escaping @callee_unowned @convention(block) @Sendable (@unowned CGImageRef?, @unowned NSError?) -> () with result type CGImageRef
libdispatch.dylib _dispatch_call_block_and_release
```

That is the completion handler of `SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(in:)` being called with neither an image nor an error.

What decides it is the executable path, not the capture API:

| first process (alive) | second process | second process result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `captureImage(in:)` | same path, `captureImage(in:)` | SIGTRAP: Swift program 3 of 3, daemon 4 of 4 (arm64), 6 of 6 (Intel runners) |
| `captureImage(contentFilter:)` | same path, `captureImage(contentFilter:)` | never completes: Swift program 3 of 3, daemon 5 of 5 (arm64), 10 of 10 (Intel runners). The daemon times out after 5 s and serves every call through the `screencapture` fallback |
| either | a copy of the same binary at another path | works: Swift program 7 of 7, daemon 1 of 1 |
| either | a different build | works: 8 of 8 (4 arm64, 4 Intel runners) |

Once the first process exits, a new one works again. One exception to the table: a same-path Swift client started right after two other-path clients got its image.

I do not know why macOS does this. Only `get_desktop_state` was tested in the second daemon; three `get_window_state` calls there returned normally.

### Environment

- cua-driver main `57edfe91a8` (0.47.22), ad-hoc signed release builds. Also seen with the signed 0.45.2 release binary while an older daemon of the same install was running.
- macOS 26.7 arm64 (MacBook, M3); macOS 26.6.1 and 15.7.9 x86_64 (GitHub `macos-26-intel`, `macos-15-intel`).

### Evidence

- Intel runs where daemons were left alive by accident, then on purpose: [43304817245](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43304817245), [43315924502](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43315924502).
- Local matrix (arm64, 5 `get_desktop_state` calls per daemon, `A` = main, `C` = #7549):

```
== A A
#1 A first=310 ms rest_p50=141 ms failed=0/5 exit=alive
#2 A first=5408 ms failed=5/5 sck_timeouts=1 exit=-5
== C C C C
#1 C first=264 ms rest_p50=119 ms failed=0/5 sck_timeouts=0 exit=alive
#2 C first=5305 ms rest_p50=272 ms failed=0/5 sck_timeouts=1 sck_blocked=4 exit=alive
#3 C first=5399 ms rest_p50=355 ms failed=0/5 sck_timeouts=1 sck_blocked=4 exit=alive
#4 C first=5541 ms rest_p50=442 ms failed=0/5 sck_timeouts=1 sck_blocked=4 exit=alive
== C A C
#1 C first=436 ms failed=0/5 exit=alive
#2 A first=213 ms failed=0/5 exit=alive
#3 C first=5304 ms failed=0/5 sck_timeouts=1 sck_blocked=4 exit=alive
```

### Workaround and additional context

- Workaround: stop the older daemon before starting another one from the same install.
- The crash needs `captureImage(in:)`, which `get_desktop_state` uses since #6881 (0.42.4). #7549 (fix for #4663) moves that capture back to the display filter for a memory reason, which also turns the crash into the 5 s timeout plus fallback shown above. The missing answer from ScreenCaptureKit stays.
- A comment on #4663 mentions "a driver where the native capture never completes"; this may be the same situation.
