title: fix(cua-driver): preserve physical pixels in embedded Windows SDK
body:
Salvaged from #3450

Fixes #3449

Thanks to @wszkxlllll, whose commit carries the fix. This PR brings it up to date with main.

## Why

The standalone driver gets Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness from its manifest. The embedded SDK runs inside whatever process loads it. In a DPI-unaware host on a scaled display, Windows virtualizes the SDK's coordinates: on a 2560x1600 display at 150%, screen size and screenshots came back as 1707x1067, which is the top-left part of the desktop. This change sets PMv2 on the threads the SDK owns and leaves the host's threads alone.

## What changed

- `platform_windows::dpi` (new). The ABI executor's Tokio threads and the SDK's dedicated UIA, package-scan, overlay and recorder threads start in PMv2. If Windows rejects the context on any of those threads, including blocking workers created later, the executor stays failed. From then on GUI work returns `RuntimeUnavailable` and never a virtualized result. Shutdown and cleanup still run.
- `cua-driver-sdk` ABI. Regular and trusted-adapter calls go through one guarded dispatcher. `cua_driver_is_available_v1` and trusted-session creation both report the failed state.
- If the executor fails at startup (PMv2 rejected, or a worker fails to start in time), it shuts down in the background. A host that creates the SDK inside its own Tokio runtime then gets the startup error instead of a panic on drop.
- Outside Windows, in-process hosts such as the daemon do not build the ABI executor. Trusted-adapter calls run on the caller's runtime, as they did before this change. Otherwise the executor's blocking-pool threads outlived daemon shutdown, and the Linux Memcheck E2E reported them as possibly lost.
- Platform-windows blocking dispatches go through `crate::dpi::spawn_blocking` and `crate::dpi::spawn`. Capture entry points check the thread first. The recorder's application-state worker runs a registered initializer before its hook.

## Scope

Windows embedded SDK only. The standalone executable, coordinate conversion and the tool and ABI schemas are unchanged. Merging main also routes main's new Electron-identity lookup and abandoned-consent dismissal through the DPI guard. Earlier merges moved the PR's edits onto main's per-tool files under `platform-windows/src/tools/`, its new recorder worker map, and `recording_hooks::install()`. The merge also fixes two clippy lints the PR introduced and adds the missing SPDX header to `dpi.rs`.

## Blast Radius

Every Windows tool dispatch now passes through the DPI guard. On a thread that the embedded executor does not own, the guard is a no-op, so the standalone daemon behaves as before. In the embedded SDK, a rejected PMv2 context now fails calls that used to succeed with wrong coordinates.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: Linux `cua-driver-sdk` lib tests and `cua-driver-core` recording tests passed, including the new test that the recorder initializer fails closed. Windows-target `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, cross-compiled from Linux, passed. Linux clippy on the touched crates, rustfmt and the E2E inventory test also passed. The Linux server E2E under Memcheck passed on the new head. Before the fix it failed every run.
- Latest head: the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) passed. `cargo xwin clippy -p cua-driver-sdk --tests --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -D warnings` passed. The DPI-rejection test now runs inside a host Tokio runtime and needs Windows CI to execute it.
- Not run here: the Windows runtime tests (late-thread failure, unaware-host ABI capture in the `capture` lane) need a Windows desktop and are left to Windows CI. Earlier heads of #3450 passed the Windows MSVC workflow. Since then, one native-lane case (`windows-webview2-left-click-px-background`) failed twice, and that failure has not been tied to this change. Server 2025 at 100% and 150% scaling remains untested.

fix(cua-driver): uninstall-local stops app-bundle daemons and removes release markers
body:
`uninstall-local.sh` no longer reports success while a daemon from the local install is still running or its `.release_installed` markers remain.

Before this change, the script only stopped daemons started through the CLI link or `packages/current/cua-driver-local`. On macOS, a daemon started straight from `/Applications/CuaDriverLocal.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver-local` kept running after its bundle was deleted. Also, `.release_installed` (the per-version marker directory the telemetry code writes) was not in the cleanup list, so the local home was never removed. The script then printed `cua-driver-local uninstalled` anyway.

## Changes

- The script now also stops daemons running from the app-bundle executable. It waits for them to exit, sends `-KILL` to any that remain, and exits 1 with an error before deleting anything if a local daemon is still alive. It checks again just before printing success.
- The LaunchAgent and systemd unit files are removed only after every daemon is confirmed stopped. If an uninstall fails, the install is left intact and the uninstall can be rerun.
- Daemon paths are matched literally (regex metacharacters escaped). Matching is limited to the invoking user, because other accounts may run the shared `/Applications` bundle.
- If `pgrep` fails (any exit status other than 1), the script treats it as a surviving daemon, not as "none running".
- `.release_installed` is removed in both `uninstall-local.sh` and `uninstall-local.ps1`.

## Test plan

- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_uninstall_local.py` gains these tests:
  - the app-bundle path is stopped (scoped to the user)
  - a surviving daemon or a `pgrep` error stops the uninstall, deletes no files, keeps the LaunchAgent and prints no success line
  - a real process whose argv[0] is a local daemon path, under a home path containing `.`, a space and parentheses, is stopped and the uninstall succeeds
  - the existing removal test now also removes `.release_installed`
- All of these new or extended tests fail against the current main script.
- The scoped repository checks were run on macOS: the local uninstall, elevation and cross-copy daemon-stop suites pass. A real-process check confirmed that macOS `pkill`/`pgrep` accept `-U` together with `-f`.
- Not run: Linux and Windows native lanes. The Windows change adds one name to the list of removed children.

Fixes #3513

title: fix(cua-driver): respect canceled dragstart in synthetic browser drags
body:
## Summary

A page can cancel `dragstart` to veto a drag. The synthetic `browser_pointer` route still dispatched `drop` to the destination, which could change page state after the veto. Release the pointer at the source when dispatch is canceled and return the existing `browser_action_unavailable` refusal. The regression checks both the tool result and what the destination actually received.

## Related work

Refs #7514 for the broader investigation of the DOM event route.

## Compatibility and risk

The change is limited to canceled drags sent with `input_route=dom_event`. The tool schema and trusted-input route are unchanged. Pages that relied on receiving a drop after canceling it will observe the source's veto.

## Validation

- On Windows x64, the JavaScript embedded in the original and patched Rust sources was run in headless Chrome 157.0.8103.52 and Edge 157.0.4341.46. Each browser recorded one drop for a canceled drag before the fix and zero after it. An allowed drag recorded one drop in both versions.
- Added an end-to-end regression to `standalone_browser_pointer_actions` in `cua-driver-e2e`. The test also requires `pointerup` on the source. With the same fixture in headless Chrome and Edge, releasing on the destination, emitting an unexpected drop, or omitting the release each produced a different outcome from the passing case. The [full driver E2E for the updated test](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43452009436) ran on `adaf266`. The Windows and Linux matrices passed, including the updated regression in [Windows Chrome and Edge](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43452009436/job/131976441870) and [Linux Chrome](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43452009436/job/131976441847). In attempts 1–4 the full gate could not allocate a hosted macOS arm64 runner. The [fourth environment probe](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43452009436/job/132040665708) stopped before any macOS tests ran. The fifth attempt was still queued on November 15.
- Independent fork runs checked out `adaf2665d92fb40c0a9a59568b9237edb015fca2` on hosted macOS 26 arm64. The [upstream browser E2E suite](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43599493039/job/132460987700) passed all 20 scenarios. `standalone_browser_pointer_actions` ran against installed Chrome and Edge and passed, including the canceled-drag assertions. The [Rust build, Clippy and unit tests](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43601419631/job/132466773314) also passed. The remaining hosted macOS 26 suites passed on the same commit in a [separate fork run](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43709116338): [shared desktop](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43709116338/job/132796638853), [native apps](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43709116338/job/132796638764), and [screen capture](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43709116338/job/132796638761). The three jobs reported no case retries.
- The [full driver E2E run on the fork](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43427172376) was manually dispatched on the previous revision `bcab95eb26f641ea2a90c5ac54239e0ffb732bb7`. The gate selected `lanes=full` and passed on Windows, Linux and hosted macOS. Rust source builds passed on Windows and Linux. The pointer regression passed in the [Windows Chrome and Edge job](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43427172376/job/131891887137), the [Linux Chrome job](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43427172376/job/131891887061), and the [macOS browser job](https://github.com/sansuizhu8-source/cua/actions/runs/43427172376/job/131892324880). Upstream Actions runs still require maintainer approval.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The title and scope describe the production fix.
- [x] The existing API and refusal code cover this behavior.
- [x] Browser evidence and the fork CI results are recorded above.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off.

title: Hyprland plugin: always-present agent seats break pointer polling in GTK 3 apps (wxWidgets hover previews)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (Hyprland plugin)

### Summary

Another case for the seat-lifetime plan in #4257 (item 2, "an agent seat exists only while a lane is in use"): with the plugin loaded, the always-present agent seats break **pointer polling in GTK 3 apps**, even ones that never bind an agent seat for input.

GTK 3's Wayland backend answers the legacy `gdk_device_manager_get_client_pointer()` with the pointer of the seat that most recently gained pointer capability, which is `Cua-Agent-2`. `gdk_display_get_default_seat()` still returns `Hyprland`. Apps that poll the pointer through the legacy call get the idle agent pointer at `(0,0)`, while mouse events keep arriving from the Hyprland seat with correct coordinates. wxWidgets uses that call for `wxGetMousePosition()` and `wxGetMouseState()` on GTK 3. In PrusaSlicer 2.9.6, the paint-brush sphere is placed by raycasting `wxGetMousePosition()`, so it disappears, while clicking still paints.

### Reproduction

1. Omarchy 4.5.0, Hyprland 0.56.2, `cua-hyprland-plugin` 0.33.2-3 loaded (`hyprctl -j cua:status` shows two lanes, `seat_lifetime: compositor`).
2. Native Wayland wxWidgets/GTK 3 test app that logs the `wxEVT_MOTION` position and `ScreenToClient(wxGetMousePosition())`.
3. Move the normal mouse over it. To exclude agent input, I used a `/dev/uinput` virtual mouse on the normal input path.

### Observed

| Setup | Event position | Polled position |
|---|---|---|
| All three seats visible | (394,351) | (0,0) |
| `Cua-Agent` and `Cua-Agent-2` globals hidden from the test process only | (418,375) | (418,375) |
| XWayland | (450,387) | (450,387) |

No agent session was active; the plugin only had to advertise the seats.

### Expected

Apps outside an agent session see only the user's seat, as planned in #4257, item 2. Until then, documenting this class of side effect (GTK 3 legacy client pointer, so wxWidgets apps' hover and preview features) next to the imv and Zed cases would help users diagnose it.

### Client-side fixes filed

- wxWidgets: wxWidgets/wxWidgets#27347 (use the default seat's pointer on GTK 3.20+). Separately, wxWidgets master crashed on startup with three seats; fixed in wxWidgets/wxWidgets#27346.
- GTK 3: the legacy client pointer should follow the default seat (report drafted for GNOME GitLab).
- A local workaround that needs no plugin change: a GTK 3 module that replaces the Wayland device manager's `get_client_pointer` vfunc with `gdk_seat_get_pointer(gdk_display_get_default_seat())`, loaded via `GTK_MODULES`. It fixed the test app and PrusaSlicer here.

### Environment

Omarchy 4.5.0 (Arch), kernel 7.2.15, Hyprland 0.56.2-4, cua-hyprland-plugin 0.33.2-3 (source rev c82d32e), GTK 3.24.52, wxWidgets 3.2.12, NVIDIA GTX 1080 Ti (580.178.04).

title: raw-linux bench desktop: find the unlogged process that stalls the AT-SPI bus
body:
Found by the raw-linux pure bench run (branch `exp/raw-linux-pure`, head `57f8ccca1a`). Follows #7529, which covers the timeout fix, not the cause.

**What happens.** In the splice session (run `rlp-r1`, the 22 reruns of CDB-G03, CDB-G02 and MB-09), one app on the bench desktop's AT-SPI bus stopped answering. Its pid was 773, a process the harness did not log, and it stalled in 245 raw calls. The 2 s `Atspi.set_timeout` from #7529 kept those calls short, but the app stayed unresponsive.

**Already ruled out.** A cua-driver daemon running alongside a foreground drag did not slow the bus (probe `db1`). In rawfull-r1 the stall began at MB-09-r4's first call, before that trial's own drag.

**To do.** Find out which process stalls the bus on the bench desktop: log the process name and command line for every pid that hits the AT-SPI timeout, then fix or exclude it at desktop setup. With the timeout in place, any trial that still pays one 2 s read per stuck app will skew the arm's wall time.

title: fix(cua-driver): report the PID of the daemon serving the selected socket
body:
## Why

`cua-driver status` could print another daemon's PID. Every `serve` wrote the default pid file, even on a custom `--socket`, and `status` read that shared file whatever socket it was asked about. Now only the default-socket daemon writes the default pid file, and `status` asks the daemon on the selected socket for its PID.

## What changed

- `serve` without `--pid-file` writes the default pid file only when it serves the default endpoint (`serve::PidFile::DefaultEndpoint`). It decides after binding: on Unix it compares the bound socket's device and inode with the default socket (following a symlink there), on Windows it compares pipe names case-insensitively. Any spelling of the default endpoint (case, `./`, a symlink) still writes the default pid file. An explicit `--pid-file` is still honored on any socket.
- `status` without `--pid-file` prints the PID from the presence probe of the daemon on the selected socket. `status --pid-file <path>` still reads that file.
- The "already running" message from `serve` already takes the PID from the daemon on that socket on main, so this PR leaves it alone.

## Scope

Covers the PID that `serve` and `status` report. It leaves out the `diagnose` identity gap mentioned in the issue. Uninstall reads the default pid file only for the release daemon on the default socket, and that daemon still writes it.

## Blast Radius

The CLI's `serve` and `status` on macOS, Linux and Windows. A daemon started on a custom socket without `--pid-file` no longer creates a pid file. Nothing in the repo reads one for a custom-socket daemon: the embedded SDK launch and the testkit find daemons through their sockets.

## Verification

- New test `status_reports_the_daemon_serving_each_socket` in `status_pid_file_cli_test.rs` runs two daemons in one isolated home, one on the default socket and one on a custom socket. `status` with each socket must print that daemon's PID, and the default pid file must still name the default daemon. Without the fix it fails because plain `status` prints the custom daemon's PID. With the fix it passes, along with the existing `--pid-file` test, which now expects the daemon's PID where it used to expect `unknown (no pid file)`.
- Ran the issue's repro on macOS with a debug build: `status` and `status --socket <custom>` each print the PID that owns their socket, the default pid file keeps the default daemon's PID, and a second `serve` on the busy custom socket names the custom daemon's PID.
- In that test the default daemon binds another socket that the default socket path links to. It fails if the daemon compares path spelling, or the link's own inode, instead of the bound endpoint.
- Manual macOS check with a debug build: `serve --socket .../CUA-DRIVER.sock` (the default socket in another case) writes the default pid file; a custom socket does not.
- After merging main: the scoped repository checks (fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, `status_pid_file_cli_test`) pass on macOS. The two-daemon test's helpers are now Unix-only, matching the test, which fixes the Windows clippy dead-code failure. Linux and Windows run in CI.

Fixes #3514

title: verify-cua-driver macOS Lume runner: report the host macOS guest limit instead of "worker stopped during boot"
body:
## What happened

On the relay Mac mini (Lume 0.5.3, macOS 26.6.2), 16 of 24 macOS Lume full-lane runs on 2026-11-13 ended `infrastructure_failed` with `worker stopped during boot`. The lume log for each worker shows two different causes behind that one message:

- **Host macOS guest limit (5 runs: 20261113T045324Z-975ee99a, 071830Z-9d542df8, 114430Z-2995cbff, 123247Z-884d85d2, 123633Z-a02172d7).** `lume run --detach` logged `Failed in VM.run ... The number of virtual machines exceeds the limit. The maximum supported number of active virtual machines has been reached.` Other sessions on the host already had two macOS guests running. The runner's `run.lock` serializes only lume-e2e runs, so a guest started outside it still takes one of the two slots. The runner saw `stopped` and reported a boot failure, which reads like a broken seed or guest.
- **False first `stopped` read (11 runs, including the four for #7614).** The runner gave up within about 6 s of the lume log's `VM started successfully`. In 7 of them the log shows `Wrote VNC config to VM via SSH` 16 to 20 s after the start, so the guest was booting normally. That part is #7513.

## Expected

When the host is at its macOS guest limit, the runner reports that as the reason (for example `blocked: host limit of 2 running macOS guests reached`, matching the wording #3958 gave `lume serve`). It reports it before cloning, or waits for a slot, rather than calling it a boot failure. The verify skill's "Blocked before a VM starts" note in `.cursor/skills/verify-cua-driver/macos-lume.md` lists this case next to the disk floor and `run.lock`.

## Done when

- A run started while two macOS guests are active ends with a reason that names the host guest limit, not `worker stopped during boot`.
- `macos-lume.md` documents the limit as a blocked lane.

Related: #7513 (the false `stopped` read), #3880 and #3958 (the same limit through the HTTP API).

title: fix(cua-driver): let Windows ffmpeg finish shutdown and stop shimmed encoders
body:
Fixes #3713

## Cause

The failing preflight's retained recording from https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/34499846099 shows what happened. The MP4 is finalized (`ftyp`, `moov`, `mdat`, faststart applied), but it holds 2 frames over 1.83 s. A healthy preflight holds 80 to 120. The cursor sampler kept running for 6.9 s after the last preflight action. So gdigrab stalled on one frame grab, and ffmpeg reads `q` only between frames. Its clean shutdown ran past the 3 s deadline, and `stop` declared failure.

At the deadline `stop` killed the process it had spawned. With Chocolatey that process is the shim, so the real encoder kept running and finalized the file afterwards. That's why a "failed" recording still had a valid `moov`. The shim also meant a timed-out stop could leave an encoder running against the output path.

The diagnostics on #3739 point the same way. Every slow passing shutdown (1205 and 1686 ms) came from a runner's first preflight after the hosted console was minimized. One of them also had a frame gap of a third of a second and only 14 frames. That is the same grab stall, short of the deadline.

## Change

- Give a clean ffmpeg shutdown 10 s instead of 3 s. That stays well under the testkit's 25 s tool-call timeout. A real exit failure still reports at once, and a hung encoder still reports `ffmpeg shutdown timed out`.
- On Windows, spawn ffmpeg suspended in a kill-on-close job object, then resume it, so anything a shim starts is in the job. A timeout terminates the whole job, and dropping the backend kills any leftover.

## Tests

- `stop_recording_waits_for_a_slow_clean_encoder_shutdown`: a fixture encoder takes 4.5 s to finish after `q`, then writes its output. Through the public `start_recording`/`stop_recording`/`get_recording_state` tools, stop succeeds and reports the video. With the old 3 s deadline it fails with `ffmpeg shutdown timed out after 3000 ms`.
- `shutdown_timeout_stops_the_encoder_behind_a_shim` (Windows only, runs in the existing `recording_shutdown_errors` step of the Windows CI): the fixture acts as a shim that starts a child encoder, and the child ignores `q`. After the timeout, the child process must be gone.

## Verification

Ran the scoped repository checks: rustfmt, clippy with `-D warnings` for macOS and cross-checked for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `recording_shutdown_errors` (3 passed on macOS), and the core library's recording tests. The Windows-only shim test and native Windows and Linux X11 desktop E2E could not run on the macOS host. Windows CI runs the shim test.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: two unit tests fail on main (`f4c72198c0`) outside the platforms CI builds them on, so every local or fork run there starts red.
  1. Windows, `extension_manager::tests::active_perception_extension_resolves_owned_worker_arguments`: `assertion failed: config.args[1].ends_with("models/model-manifest.json")`. The worker paths are built with `Path::join`, so on Windows they end in `models\model-manifest.json` and `runtime\onnxruntime.dll`; the test compares strings with `/`.
  2. macOS 15.7.9, `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`: `Don't Allow in [...]`. The labels are read from the system's own tables. On macOS 26.7 the straight-apostrophe spelling is the value of one TCC key, `REQUEST_ACCESS_DONT_ALLOW`; every other deny label, and the NetworkExtension one, is the typographic `Don’t Allow`. The labels read on macOS 15.7.9 hold only the typographic one. The test asked for both.

title: fix(cua-driver): make set_value on a native text field reach the app
body:
## Why

On macOS, `set_value` on a native single-line text field wrote `AXValue` and read it back, but an `AXValue` write never goes through AppKit's field editor, so a control bound to a model kept its old value while the read-back showed the new one (#3807). The result also had no way to say whether the app took the value (#3851). This lands @will-bogusz's work from #3858 on current main, with his commits kept as authored.

## What changed

- A native non-secure, non-search `AXTextField` is now written by focusing it, selecting the old value (in UTF-16 units), typing the new value and pressing Tab. Secure fields keep the `AXValue`-only write. Search, combo, date and time fields keep `AXValue`, followed by `AXConfirm` or Return/Tab.
- New optional `ActionResult.committed` (`committed`, `not_committed`, `unproven`), contract 0.9.0, implementing items 2 and 4 of RFC #4009. It is `committed` only when a typed edit ended with the value in place. `type_text` on such a field reports `unproven`. Manifest and Python/TypeScript UniFFI bindings are regenerated.
- One fix on top: the retype route now refuses when the field's `AXValue` cannot be read, and trusts the `AXValue` clear fallback only when the field reads back empty. Before, an unreadable value counted as an empty field, so the typed text could be appended to the old one.

## Scope

macOS `set_value` and `type_text`, the contract type and its generated bindings, and two AppKit e2e cases added to the macOS e2e selection. `AXTextArea` and web content are not retyped; they report `not_committed`. The RFC document is #4367.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS `set_value` on a plain text field now sends keystrokes instead of an `AXValue` write, so it goes through the background keystroke gate. When that gate refuses, the write falls back to the control's own `AXConfirm` if it has one, and otherwise refuses. `ActionResult` denies unknown fields, so a typed 0.8.0 SDK rejects a 0.9.0 daemon's `committed` field: SDK and daemon must upgrade together.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks on Linux passed: fmt, clippy and tests for `cua-driver-contract` and `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver-e2e` test build, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, and the cua-driver Linux X11 and Wayland verify lanes on the contributor's head merged with main.
- Not run: platform-macos unit tests and the macOS AppKit e2e cases (`harness_appkit_set_value_commits_the_edit`, `harness_appkit_set_value_replaces_a_non_bmp_value_whole`), which need a macOS host; the UniFFI binding drift check and the Python/TypeScript SDK tests, whose package environments were not installed. CI's macOS lanes cover them.

Salvaged from #3858
Fixes #3807
Fixes #3851

title: feat(cua-driver): add OpenJev decision model adapter
body:
## Why

jev-use has a `DecisionModel` seam with mock, TypeSafe and loopback S1 backends, but none that reaches a remote OpenJev-compatible System One server. @kvnloo built that backend in #3961, re-cut to the scope the maintainer review asked for. This PR carries those commits unchanged and adds two fixes found in review.

## What changed

- `python/openjev_model.py` and `typescript/openjev_model.ts` (by @kvnloo): an OpenJev `DecisionModel` that sends the validated `cua.jev_choice_request_v1|v2` as System One `state` to `OPENJEV_BASE_URL` and returns scores for the supplied candidate IDs only. `choose_decision.py --model openjev` and `verify_decision_cli.py --model openjev` select it. An API key is sent only over HTTPS. URL credentials, query and fragment are rejected. Redirects are refused, bodies over 256 KiB fail, and failures make exactly one request.
- `decision_models.choose()` no longer replaces an empty `selected_id` with the argmax. A provider that answered `choice: ""` used to get an actionable `selected` result. It now gets `error` / `model_error`.
- The TypeScript transport now reads the response body inside its error classification, so a timeout or reset during the body read is an `OpenJevError` (`timeout` / `http_error`) and no longer a raw error.

## Scope

Covers the OpenJev adapter in Python and TypeScript, its tests, the CLI choice and the `decision-models.md` section. Leaves out browser-runner provider selection, backend receipts in JSONL events, and TypeSafe base URL/model/timeout configuration. No change to Driver or visual routing.

## Blast Radius

Everything is under `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use`. The `choose()` change affects every decision model. Only a model that returns an empty-string `selected_id` sees different behavior, and no backend in the tree builds one: mock and S1 pass `None`, and TypeSafe passes a validated ID.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks for jev-use (the `ci-jev-use.yml` commands) pass on this head: the full Python unittest suite, `npm test` and `npm run typecheck`. The Linux mock E2E job needs a Linux desktop and was not run here.
- `choose_decision.py --model openjev` was run against a loopback server. A valid answer returns `selected`. A 302 and an oversized body each return an error, and the redirect target gets no request. An API key with an `http://` URL exits before any request.
- Each new regression test fails when its fix is reverted and passes with it.


Salvaged from #3961
Fixes #3915

title: fix(cua-driver): let callers perform an app's own macOS element actions
body:
## Why

macOS hands an app's own element actions (Reminders' "Pin List") to the driver as raw multi-line envelopes like `Name:Pin List\nTarget:0x0\nSelector:(null)`. They ended up in `actions` as text that `click` refused, so callers could never perform them. Groups that carry their app's label or help were also collapsed out of the tree.

## What changed

- `ax/actions.rs` splits advertised action names. `AX*` names stay in `actions`, and app actions are published once each as `custom_actions: [{name, raw}]` in `get_window_state` and as `custom_actions=["Pin List"]` in the tree text. `click` (and `perform_ax_action`) takes either spelling. A standard name such as `press` always wins over a custom action with the same name, and that custom action stays reachable by its raw envelope. Unknown names are still refused before dispatch.
- `AXGroup` and `AXScrollArea` now collapse only when title, description, value and help are all empty, which is checked before the action query. A kept group gets an element index when it has an action of its own (a press or a custom action), or when it was kept for its help or value. A named section that advertises only the generic menu and scroll actions stays an unindexed display row, as on main, so the text row that repeats its name keeps its index.
- Contract: an optional `custom_actions` field (`ElementCustomAction`) on `WindowElement`, with the manifest and the Python and TypeScript bindings regenerated.

## Scope

macOS only. Windows and Linux never emit `custom_actions`. `ActionResult` and the action-outcome contract don't change. The parts of #3949 that covered disabled-control indexing and `subrole` already landed in #5635 and #6893.

## Tradeoffs

An unnamed group whose only content is a numeric or Boolean `AXValue` still collapses. Only a non-empty string value keeps a group. On main every unnamed group collapsed, so this is not a regression. Counting `0`/`1` state as content would turn plain layout wrappers into rows and shift element indices.

## Blast Radius

macOS snapshots now keep groups that have a label, help or value, so element indices can shift on apps that have such groups. Envelopes leave `actions`, but nothing could invoke them from there before. Default clicks keep their standard action even on an element that also advertises a same-named custom action.

## Verification

- At this head, the scoped repository checks for `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-contract` passed (fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, unit tests), as did the contract generator drift check and `bin/ci --quick`. The unit tests cover envelope parsing, dedupe, one tree row per element, refusal before dispatch, and a standard name beating a custom one.
- Two AppKit E2E cases are added and wired into `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh`: `harness_appkit_custom_actions_are_published_and_dispatch_by_name_or_envelope` and `harness_appkit_a_content_bearing_group_stays_addressable`.
- After merging main, the scoped repository checks for `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-contract` (fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, unit tests), the contract generator drift check and the generated docs check passed. The macOS Lume full matrix passed at 4c969d91a07509f31f578d4a6167d86b367bd5a7 with 0 failures: both new cells (`group_custom_action`, `group_with_help`) and the Tauri and WKWebView scroll cells that cover named web sections passed, and the only refusals were the expected Electron background-text and page-tool ones. Linux and Windows lanes were not run.

- Latest round: main merged again (only the generated Python binding conflicted; `is_password` from main and `custom_actions` kept in the Rust field order, and CI's UniFFI drift check passed on it). `click` now reads an element's live action list in `spawn_blocking`, and only for a non-standard action name, so an unresponsive target no longer stalls the async worker during validation. rustfmt and `bin/ci --quick` passed locally; Rust build, clippy, unit tests and E2E are left to CI on this head.

Salvaged from #3950. Thanks @will-bogusz; the original commits keep their authorship.

Refs #3949

title: fix(cua-driver): one ScreenCaptureKit user per unbundled macOS executable
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: two processes started from the same `cua-driver` executable cannot both use ScreenCaptureKit, and while both are alive they keep `replayd` busy (#7548).
  - `replayd` names a client by its bundle identifier, and one without a bundle by its executable path (log: `+[RPConnectionManager uniqueClientIdentifierWithPID:] using identifier from executablePath`). When a second process from that path connects, `replayd` cancels the first one's connection (`invalidated because the current process cancelled the connection by calling xpc_connection_cancel()`). ReplayKit in the first reconnects at once, which cancels the second one's, and so on: 5,811 `accepted client connection` lines in 6 s.
  - Effect on main, two daemons from one binary, each after one `get_window_state`, then idle:

    | | `replayd` CPU | each daemon, CPU | each daemon, footprint while idle | capture in the first daemon |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | M3, macOS 26.7 | 71 to 74% | 11 to 14% | 18 to 45 MB in 32 s | 3348 ms (3 s timeout, then `screencapture`) |
    | hosted arm64 VM, macOS 26.7.2 | 58 to 72% | 12 to 15% | 20 to 32 MB in 32 s | 3143 ms |
    | hosted arm64 VM, macOS 15.8.2 | 70 to 74% | 15 to 16% | 15 to 31 MB in 32 s | 3172 ms |

    It lasts as long as both live and stops when one exits. With `get_desktop_state` the second daemon dies instead (SIGTRAP inside `captureImage(in:)`, all three machines).
  - A bare binary is what the Python wheel and `cargo install` give. An app's `Contents/MacOS` executable is named by bundle identifier and does not collide; a binary under `Contents/Resources` or `Contents/Helpers` of an app does, and so does one with an embedded `__info_plist`.
- What changed: a process outside an app bundle takes an exclusive lock named after its executable path before its first ScreenCaptureKit call and holds it for life (the kernel drops it when the process ends). A process that finds the lock taken never calls ScreenCaptureKit: window and desktop captures go straight to the existing `screencapture` fallback, the grant probe uses `screencapture`, and starting a recording returns an error that names the holder. Once the holder exits, the next capture takes the lock and uses ScreenCaptureKit again.

Same runs with this PR:

| | `replayd` CPU | each daemon, CPU | footprint while idle | captures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M3, window | 0.0% | 0.0% | flat | 375 ms and 401 ms, both daemons |
| M3, desktop | 0.0% | 0.0% | flat | 247 ms (holder) and 289 ms (`screencapture`), second daemon alive |
| VM 26.7.2, window | 0.0% | 0.0% | flat | 84 ms and 107 ms |
| VM 26.7.2, desktop | 0.0% | 0.0% | flat | 70 ms and 123 ms, second daemon alive |
| VM 15.8.2, window | 0.0% | 0.0% | flat | 80 ms and 141 ms |
| VM 15.8.2, desktop | 0.0% | 0.0% | flat | 80 ms and 138 ms, second daemon alive |

After the rebase onto #7549 (head `3f56a9da0b` against its base `1f037e4397`), M3, macOS 26.7, same harness, 48 s of idle:

| | `replayd` CPU | each daemon, CPU | each daemon, footprint while idle | captures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base, window | 83.6 to 84.0% | 15.2 to 15.4% | 85 to 121 MB, up and down | 3335 and 3338 ms in the daemon that lost the connection |
| base, desktop | 83.5 to 85.0% | 15.2 to 15.4% | 78 to 144 MB, up and down | 5371 and 5324 ms, second daemon alive |
| this PR, window | 0.0% | 0.0% | 95 to 17 MB and 95 to 48 MB, not growing | 197 and 281 ms |
| this PR, desktop | 0.0% | 0.0% | 130 MB and 97 MB, constant | 229 ms (holder) and 264 ms (`screencapture`); 280, 229, 219 ms once the holder is stopped |

## Related work

Fixes #7548

Refs #7549 (merged while this PR was open; rebased on it). It moved the desktop capture to the content-filter route, so on current main two daemons loop on desktop captures as they do on window captures, and the second one stays alive (table above).

RFC: not needed, no public contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only, and only for a second process of the same executable while the first is alive. No tool, schema or permission change.
  - In that second process the desktop capture cannot leave the cursor overlay out; `agent_overlay_capture` reports it, as it already does whenever the fallback is used. Recording (`SCStream`) is refused there with an explicit error.
  - A single daemon, and daemons at different paths, behave as before: they take the lock and nothing else changes.
  - The lock file lives in the per-user cache directory macOS assigns (`confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)`), so it does not depend on the environment the process was started with.
- Risk and rollback:
  - A process of an older build running from the same path holds no lock, so a new one next to it still collides, as today.
  - If the lock file cannot be opened the process goes ahead without it, as today.
  - One new module, `platform-macos/src/capture_owner.rs`, called from the four places that reach ScreenCaptureKit. Reverting the PR restores the previous behavior.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` on macOS 26 x86_64: 752 passed, 0 failed. `a_claimed_executable_refuses_a_second_claim_until_the_first_is_released` covers the lock.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Harness [`storm.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/59929a4709c37f1c380bac3005eb9d27c3ad70be/ab/storm.py): start daemon 1, capture, start daemon 2 from the same binary, capture, sample CPU (`top`) and footprint for 30 s, capture again in both, stop one. Main `f4c72198c0` (M) against this PR (L), arm64 release builds. Hosted runner output, macOS 26.7.2 and 15.8.2: [run 43447583137](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43447583137). From the macOS 26 job:

    ```
    == M:window M:window                                   (main)
    #2 M first window capture ok=True 3154 ms
       idle CPU with 2 daemon(s): replayd=57.9% #1=12.3%/20MB #2=12.4%/19MB
       idle CPU after 32 s more:  replayd=71.9% #1=14.5%/32MB #2=14.6%/31MB
    == L:window L:window                                   (this PR)
    #2 L first window capture ok=True 130 ms
       idle CPU after 32 s more:  replayd=0.0%  #1=0.0%/17MB  #2=0.0%/15MB
    == M:desktop M:desktop
    #2 M later desktop capture ok=False exit=-5
    == L:desktop L:desktop
    #2 L later desktop capture ok=True 123 ms exit=alive
    ```
  - Handover: with the first daemon stopped, the next three desktop captures of the second one take 62, 45 and 44 ms on the macOS 26 VM and 80, 45 and 46 ms on the macOS 15 one (139 and 224 ms through `screencapture` before) and log no further fallback.
  - What `replayd` keys on, with a 40-line ScreenCaptureKit client and no driver ([`two_clients.swift`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/59929a4709c37f1c380bac3005eb9d27c3ad70be/ab/two_clients.swift), [`pair.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/59929a4709c37f1c380bac3005eb9d27c3ad70be/ab/pair.py)), M3, macOS 26.7, each case at least twice:

    | two clients alive together | `replayd` CPU | second client |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | same path, bare binary | 64 to 82% | no answer in 12 s |
    | same path, bare binary with an embedded `__info_plist` | 79%, 79% | no answer |
    | same path, under `X.app/Contents/Resources` or `Contents/Helpers` | 72%, 74%, 72%, 53% | no answer |
    | two paths, bare binaries | 0.0% | image |
    | two paths, two apps with the same bundle identifier | 0.0% | image |
    | same path, `X.app/Contents/MacOS` | 0.0% | image |
  - The in-process SDK has the same limit (release 0.45.2): a second Python process from the same interpreter that loads the library and calls `get_desktop_state` while the first is alive exits with SIGTRAP.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The hosted-runner numbers are from `ae35fc6bfa`, one commit before the head, which adds the same check to the permission-request path (`register_with_screen_capture_kit`). The M3 run was repeated at the head `82a379dde8`: `replayd` 0.0%, both daemons 0.0% and flat, captures 289 and 288 ms (window), 244 and 285 ms (desktop, second daemon alive), and 272, 183, 176 ms once the first daemon is stopped. Main in the same session: `replayd` 69%, each daemon 12.6%.
  - Hosted arm64 runners had no capacity for a rerun at the head (three attempts cancelled unassigned).
  - "main" in the tables is `f4c72198c0`, before #7549. The rebase on `1f037e4397` had one conflict, in the two desktop capture call sites, which now take the claim before the content-filter capture. The two-daemon runs on the rebased head are from the M3 only; the hosted-runner numbers predate the rebase.
  - macOS 14 was not run.
  - The second in-process SDK host was not rerun with this PR; it goes through the same functions.
  - `bin/ci` was not run locally.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.

title: perf(cua-driver): encode the macOS desktop screenshot once and keep its display filter
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: #7549 (merged) fixed the memory growth of `get_desktop_state` but costs about 50 ms a call on a Retina display, because the leak-free route needs ScreenCaptureKit's shareable-content query. Two costs in that call can go:
  1. **The frame is PNG-encoded twice.** The capture is encoded at full size, then decoded again, resized and encoded a second time. `sample` on the daemon (3420x2214): 121 ms on CPU per call with the default size cap, 96 ms without a resize.
  2. **The display filter is rebuilt for every call.** The shareable-content query takes about as long as the capture itself (Swift, same machine: query p50 78 ms, capture with a kept filter p50 70 ms).
- What changed:
  - The desktop capture hands its pixels to `CapturedImage::encode`, as `get_window_state` already does: resize first, encode once.
  - The display filter and its configuration are kept between captures. They are rebuilt when the main display, its bounds, its pixel size or the window left out change, and once more when a capture with the kept filter fails.

`get_desktop_state` p50 over the CLI, daemons run in rotation, 40 calls each, M3, macOS 26.7, 3420x2214:

| build | default size cap | overlay enabled | no resize (`max_image_dimension: 0`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before #7549 (`f4c72198c0`) | 199 ms | 195 ms | |
| main with #7549 | 251 ms | 250 ms | 168 ms |
| + one encode | 206 ms | 204 ms | 165 ms |
| + kept filter (this PR) | 163 ms | 161 ms | 128 ms |

Footprint after those runs: 1567 to 1611 MB before #7549, 102 to 114 MB with this PR.

## Related work

Follows #7549, which is merged; this PR is rebased on it (`1f037e4397`).

Refs #6881 (removed the shareable-content query through `captureImage(in:)`, which is the call that keeps the frames alive)

RFC: not needed, no public contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. No tool, schema or permission change. The screenshot bytes are the same as on #7549 (see Validation).
- Risk and rollback:
  - **A kept filter and a changing screen.** A display filter names what to leave out, not what to show, and `SCStream` keeps one for the life of a recording. Checked through the daemon: a window that opens after the filter was built is in the next screenshot, is gone after it closes, and a window opened elsewhere later shows too (output under Validation).
  - **A stale filter.** A display change is seen before the capture (identity above). Anything else that makes the kept filter fail costs one failed capture, then a rebuild in the same call.
  - The kept filter holds one `SCContentFilter` and one `SCStreamConfiguration` for the life of the process: no frame, no surface (150 captures, twice: 0 live `CGImage` and `IOSurface`, footprint in the same range as #7549).
  - Two commits, one per change; either can be reverted alone.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` on macOS 26 x86_64: 752 passed, 0 failed. `a_capture_plan_is_kept_until_it_is_stale_or_its_capture_fails` covers the keep, replace and retry rule; `image_utils` already asserts that `encode` gives the bytes of the two-step path.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Harness [`perf_ab.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/2c0d9244963c8646920a530b67e4b980739a0c3e/ab/perf_ab.py): one daemon per build, calls interleaved build by build so every build sees the same machine state. M3, three builds in rotation, p50 (p10 to p90):

    ```
    #7549:         229 ms (224 to 238)   230 ms (224 to 241)   226 ms (222 to 235)
    + one encode:  190 ms (186 to 203)   191 ms (185 to 201)   190 ms (184 to 194)
    + kept filter: 152 ms (148 to 162)   151 ms (146 to 159)   150 ms (147 to 155)
    ```
  - Hosted arm64 VMs (M1 virtual, display below the size cap, so only the kept filter shows): [run 43447583137](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43447583137), p50 of 40, 40, 40 (overlay) and 20 (no resize) calls:

    | | macOS 26.7.2 | macOS 15.8.2 |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | #7549 | 55, 55, 55, 53 ms | 50, 72, 65, 57 ms |
    | + one encode | 57, 56, 55, 53 ms | 51, 69, 65, 57 ms |
    | + kept filter | 46, 45, 44, 44 ms | 43, 64, 57, 45 ms |
  - Same bytes: on the VMs the PNG of each build equals the one #7549 returns for the same round in 139 of 140 rounds on macOS 26.7.2 and 140 of 140 on macOS 15.8.2, for both builds. On the M3, where other windows repaint between calls, 35 to 39 of 40 rounds are equal for both builds, against 38 of 40 for a second copy of #7549 itself.
  - Same image as main: when the screen holds still between two calls, the PNG of main and of this PR's head are byte-identical at native size, and so are main and #7549 at native size and with the default cap, and #7549 and the head with the default cap ([`png_enc.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/1aa05dc2e45931241fac858de4475484fd985c8b/ab/png_enc.py), 4 of 4 comparisons). Over 12 rounds of main, this PR, main at native size, no pixel that held still between main's two captures differs every time ([`systematic_diff.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/1aa05dc2e45931241fac858de4475484fd985c8b/ab/systematic_diff.py)). Neither build draws the mouse pointer.
  - Kept filter end to end, [`kept_filter_e2e.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/2c0d9244963c8646920a530b67e4b980739a0c3e/ab/kept_filter_e2e.py): four captures, then a magenta window opens, closes, and another opens elsewhere; one pixel inside it is read from each screenshot. M3, this PR (Z); #7549 prints the same.

    ```
    Z before any window: magenta at (300,300)=False
    Z window opened after 4 captures: magenta at (300,300)=True
    Z window closed: magenta at (300,300)=False
    Z another window opened elsewhere: magenta at (800,500)=True at (300,300)=False
    Z closed again: magenta at (800,500)=False
    Z display capture warnings in the daemon log: 0
    ```
  - Filter semantics without the driver, [`stale_filter.swift`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/2c0d9244963c8646920a530b67e4b980739a0c3e/ab/stale_filter.swift): a filter built before a window exists shows it once it opens and after it moves; a filter that leaves a window out keeps leaving it out after the window moves 400 pt.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - A display reconfiguration (resolution change, external display plugged in) while the daemon runs was not exercised by hand; the identity check and the retry cover it by construction.
  - The tables are from `d805284276`. The head `f58433c84d` moves the keep, replace and retry rule into one function so the test above can drive it. Both in one rotation on the M3 (default cap / overlay / no resize, machine busier than for the tables): head 172 / 170 / 141 ms, `d805284276` 176 / 175 / 147 ms, #7549 260 / 276 / 183 ms, main 214 / 223 ms. The window test above passes at the head too.
  - Hosted arm64 runners had no capacity for a rerun at the head (three attempts cancelled unassigned).
  - Measured before the rebase, on the #7549 head `7759de89e0`. Main `1f037e4397` differs from it only outside the capture code (`video_ffmpeg.rs` and its tests), and the two commits of this PR apply with the same diff. Where the text says main, it means `f4c72198c0`, before #7549.
  - The no-resize column comes from a rotation of three builds without main, the other two columns from a rotation of four.
  - No Intel timing.
  - `bin/ci` was not run locally.

title: [Bug]: Windows: Cua Spaces app and cua daemon open visible terminal windows for status checks (schtasks, qemu --version, powershell, wsl, nvidia-smi)
body:
### Primary area

Other (the Cua Spaces desktop app, and the `cua` CLI daemon it starts)

### Summary

On Windows, the Cua Spaces app and the `cua daemon` it runs start short-lived console programs (`schtasks`, `qemu-system-x86_64 --version`, `powershell`, `wsl`, `nvidia-smi`) as visible console processes. With Windows Terminal as the default terminal, each one opens a terminal window that appears and closes, repeatedly, while the app is open. It is most noticeable when changing anything in Settings (for example toggling an agent in the Agent menu) or opening Settings or a computer's page.

### Reproduction

1. On Windows 11, with Windows Terminal set as the default terminal application, start Cua Spaces (the app starts `cua.exe daemon start --foreground --loopback 127.0.0.1:0`).
2. Open Settings and toggle any switch (for example an entry under Agent menu), or open Computers > this PC.
3. Terminal windows open and close several times. They keep appearing while those pages are open.

To see which processes are behind them, poll `Win32_Process` for new PIDs and their parents for about 20 seconds (PowerShell, every 150 ms). I ran this with the app open and nobody touching it.

### Expected behavior

No visible windows: diagnostic and status helpers started by the app or the daemon do not create a console window (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, or `windowsHide: true` for Node `child_process`).

### Actual behavior

In one 20-second window, with no user input:

| Parent | Children started |
|---|---|
| `Cua Spaces.exe` (Electron main process) | `schtasks.exe`, `qemu-system-x86_64.exe --version` (x2), `powershell.exe` (x2), each with its own `conhost.exe 0x4` |
| `cua.exe daemon start --foreground --loopback 127.0.0.1:0` | `wsl.exe`, `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "... Get-CimInstance Win32_OptionalFeature -Filter \"Name='HypervisorPlatform'\" ..."`, `nvidia-smi.exe` |
| `svchost.exe` (DCOM) | `OpenConsole.exe -Embedding` (x2), the Windows Terminal default-terminal handoff, which is what puts the windows on screen |

As a control, a console program started hidden (`Start-Process cmd.exe -ArgumentList '/c timeout /t 4' -WindowStyle Hidden`) on the same machine started no `OpenConsole`/Windows Terminal process and showed no window. So the windows come from these processes being started without a hidden or no-window flag, not from the default-terminal setting by itself.

I do not know which code path in the app issues each call. The parent PIDs above are what I observed.

### Environment

- Cua Spaces app 0.36.10 (Windows, user install under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\cua-spaces`)
- `cua` CLI 0.27.4 (bundled at `resources\native\cua.exe`), `cua-spacesd` 0.15.2 as the host service
- Windows 11 Home, build 26300, x64
- Windows Terminal 1.25.2733.0 set as the default terminal application

### Evidence

Process listing from the 20-second poll (machine-specific IDs omitted):

```
schtasks.exe              <- Cua Spaces.exe
conhost.exe               <- schtasks.exe
qemu-system-x86_64.exe    <- Cua Spaces.exe   :: "C:\Program Files\qemu\qemu-system-x86_64.exe" --version
conhost.exe 0x4           <- qemu-system-x86_64.exe
OpenConsole.exe -Embedding <- svchost.exe
wsl.exe                   <- cua.exe (daemon)
conhost.exe               <- wsl.exe
powershell.exe            <- cua.exe (daemon) :: -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; Get-CimInstance Win32_OptionalFeature -Filter \"Name='HypervisorPlatform'\" | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Insta..."
powershell.exe            <- Cua Spaces.exe
conhost.exe               <- powershell.exe
nvidia-smi.exe            <- cua.exe (daemon)
```

### Workaround and additional context

- Switching the Windows default terminal to "Windows Console Host" should turn the Windows Terminal windows into plain console flashes (untested here). It does not remove them, and it changes the default for every app.
- Staying off the Settings and Computers pages reduces how often it happens.
- Related, but a different component: #3410 (Cua Driver diagnostic helpers without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) and #5040 (embedded cua-driver daemon console window, closed). This report is about the Cua Spaces app's own child processes and the `cua daemon`'s.
- Possibly related, not confirmed: on the same pages, toggles sometimes flicker between states after a change, as if the page re-renders while these status checks run.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): Linux consent scans skip web content and honor a late confirmed Allow
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux, `browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile` is refused with `browser_wrong_target_refused: Chromium remote-debugging consent did not settle within its bounded attempt (consent attempt deadline expired)` whenever the active tab is a heavy page, even though the driver presses Allow and Chromium accepts the connection (the "Chrome is being controlled by automated test software" bar appears). The consent loop in `platform-linux/src/browser_consent_ui.rs` has a 4 s deadline, walks the whole AT-SPI tree of the window (web content included) on every step, and checks the deadline before looking whether the prompt closed. With Google Maps active one walk took ~2.1 s (577 nodes), so the walk confirming the closed prompt always ended past the deadline. When the deadline expired before the press, the prompt also stayed open after the driver dropped its socket, and later attempts queued behind it.
- What changed:
  - consent walks (`handle`, `trusted_allow_click`, `dismiss`) use a walk that does not descend into web document subtrees. The prompt matcher already ignores anything inside web content (`trusted_prompt_nodes`), so nothing it can match is lost;
  - a performed Allow whose prompt has closed is accepted even when the walk that observed it ended after the deadline, and once Allow was pressed one confirmation walk may start after the deadline. This mirrors the macOS behavior from #5216 on Linux.

## Related work

Refs #5216, #4630

title: fix(cua-driver): list no tools when a policy layer fails to load
body:
Salvaged from #4020

## Why

`is_tool_listable` returned `true` when a policy layer failed to load, so `tools/list` could advertise every tool while `authorize_tool_call` refused all of them. `revoke_authorization` also reported `revoked: 1` when `end_session` came back with `isError`, for example after a cleanup hook failed. This lands @Al-aminI's fixes for both from #4020 (his two commits are first, author kept) on current main.

## What changed

- `is_tool_listable` lists nothing when either the managed or the user policy layer failed to load. The decision is in `tool_listable_in`, with unit tests for both layers.
- `SdkAdapter::end_session` returns an error when the tool result has `isError: true`, so a failed end is no longer reported as a revoke. A new test registers a failing cleanup hook and checks the error.
- README: an unset `CUA_DRIVER_POLICY_FILE` means no enforcement, and a set but missing or unloadable path stops startup, which is what the code already did. The deny example names real tools. A direct-MCP test covers the missing-path refusal on Linux and Windows.

## Scope

Left out of #4020 because main already has them or they add a new surface nobody asked for: `CUA_DRIVER_REQUIRE_POLICY`, the `policy_mode` metadata field, the C-linkage symbol test (main imports those symbols through `ffi` and checks the header), the `default_capabilities_for` warning (telemetry calls it with arbitrary names, so it would warn on every unknown tool), and the schema-test skip gate (the testkit already panics on a missing binary under `CUA_TEST_REQUIRE_DRIVER_BIN=1`). The session tombstone cap was already reverted in #4020 and is tracked in #4993.

## Blast radius

Only a process whose policy failed to load sees the listing change, and startup validation normally stops that process first. Revoke callers now get an error instead of `revoked: 1` when the session did not end cleanly.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks passed on macOS: workspace clippy with `-D warnings`, `cua-driver-core` lib tests, the `sdk_adapter` tests and `daemon_required_test`. Each new unit test fails with its fix reverted.
- On macOS, `cua-driver mcp` with `CUA_DRIVER_POLICY_FILE` pointing at a missing file exits 1 with nothing on stdout and stderr `configured permission policy path does not exist`.
- The macOS Lume matrix did not run (the worker VM failed to boot). The Linux and Windows lanes, including the new direct-MCP test, run in CI.

title: cua-driver-sdk: dropping the private-worker shutdown future while it is queued skips the deadline kill
body:
### Summary

`PrivateWorkerClient::shutdown` in `cua-driver-sdk` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-sdk/src/worker.rs`) does not kill the private worker by its shutdown deadline when the caller drops the shutdown future while the shutdown task is still waiting in Tokio's blocking pool.

- On main, `shutdown()` runs `shutdown_sync` through `spawn_blocking`, and the deadline is computed inside `shutdown_sync`. Time spent queued behind a saturated blocking pool is never bounded, whether or not the caller keeps waiting.
- #7646 (salvaged from #3996) adds an off-pool deadline thread, but that thread belongs to the caller's future (`ShutdownDeadline` is dropped with it). If the caller drops the future while the task is queued, the watchdog is cancelled and nothing kills the child until a pool thread picks up the task. #3996's description already scopes this case out.

### Reproduction

At the #7646 head (7fd302e7), with the existing `worker/shutdown_tests.rs` fixtures (`shutdown_timeout` 100 ms, a current-thread runtime with `max_blocking_threads(1)`):

1. Occupy the only blocking thread with a 1.5 s `spawn_blocking` sleep.
2. Spawn an `unread` fixture child and call `client.shutdown()` under `tokio::time::timeout(20 ms, …)`, so the future is dropped while the shutdown task is queued.
3. Poll the child until 400 ms after the call.

Result: the child is still running at 405 ms, four times the 100 ms budget. It exits only once the blocker frees the pool thread.

### Proposed fix

Make deadline cleanup independent of the caller's future. Once shutdown has started, the off-pool deadline thread should own the expiry path: on timeout it gates transmission, aborts the queued task and calls `schedule_cleanup()`. Dropping the future then only stops the caller from waiting and does not cancel the kill.

### Tests

Add a shutdown test that drops (cancels) the shutdown future while the blocking pool is saturated, and asserts the owned child is killed and reaped by the deadline (the same bound `assert_reaped_by` uses), without the queued request being transmitted late.

title: fix(cua-driver): report the macOS keyboard route as window-addressed keys are gated
body:
Fixes #4241

## What was wrong

On macOS, Chrome with one browser window could refuse background `type_text`, `press_key` and `hotkey` with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`. The other "windows" were Chrome's helper surfaces: off-screen or 1x1 strips and the omnibox suggestion popup.

On main, the tools themselves no longer refuse in this case:

- #4821 made the keyboard-ambiguity count skip off-screen and near-zero-size siblings. It also counts nothing when accessibility proves the target is the app's key window.
- #5306 gates window-addressed `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `type_text_chars` as exact-window keys. The driver makes the addressed window key before posting, so a visible sibling such as an open omnibox popup is not ambiguous for these tools.

One surface still said otherwise. The read-only `background_input` section of `get_window_state` judged its `pid_keyboard` route as the generic key class. With the omnibox popup open and the browser window not key, it reported `pid_keyboard: refused, same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` and sent agents to `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, even though the tools would deliver.

## Change

`background_input_capability_report` now takes the keyboard action class from the platform. On macOS, `get_window_state` passes the same `window_keyboard_action(GenericKey)` that the keyboard tools gate on. That is exact-window keys where the key-window transport exists, and the generic class otherwise. The report and the tools now give the same answer. All other guards (minimized or hidden, off-Space, element ancestry, screen locked) still apply to the route.

## Tests

- New `capability_report_judges_pid_keyboard_as_the_tools_gate_it` covers a target with one competing same-pid destination (the open omnibox popup). The route is `available` under exact-window keys, still `refused` with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` under the generic class, and `minimized_or_hidden_window` once the target is minimized. With the hard-coded generic class restored, the test fails.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` all pass.
- Not run: `platform-macos` could not be built or tested on the Linux host, and no macOS guest was available, so the native Chrome check did not run. Windows checks were not run either. The Linux X11 desktop lane stopped at a build timeout before any cell ran, and Linux does not call this report.

title: cua-driver diagnose (macOS): local builds report the release bundle's install paths and TCC identity
body:
## What's wrong

`cua-driver diagnose` on a local build (`cua-driver-local`, `CuaDriverLocal.app`, bundle id `com.trycua.driver.local`) reports the release install instead of its own. In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs` at current `main`:

- `diagnose_install_layout_section` hardcodes `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, `~/.local/bin/cua-driver` and `/usr/local/bin/cua-driver`.
- `diagnose_tcc_db_section` queries TCC rows only for `client='com.trycua.driver'` and titles the section with that id.

`crate::bundle` already has the local identity (`is_local_installation()`, `app_bundle_path()`, `bundle_id()`, `cli_name()`), and `diagnose_config_paths_section` already uses it. The install-layout and TCC sections don't. On a host with a local build, the report shows the release bundle's codesign and TCC rows (or none at all), which is the wrong data for a permissions audit of the build that is actually running.

This is the "Related diagnostic gap" noted in #3514. #7626 fixes the PID part of #3514 and leaves `diagnose` unchanged.

## Expected

On a local build, `diagnose` reports `CuaDriverLocal.app`, the `cua-driver-local` CLI paths and the TCC rows for `com.trycua.driver.local`. A release build's output stays unchanged.

## Done when

- The install-layout and TCC-database sections take their paths and bundle id from `crate::bundle`.
- A unit test covers both identities.

title: fix(cua-driver): pin before AX double-click pulse
body:
## Why

On macOS, the AX `double_click` pointer fallback sent its `ClickPulse` without pinning the cursor to the target window first. Since #4068, `PinAbove` is where the overlay checks whether the target window is on the current Space, so this path skipped that check. A fresh session cursor could paint at an off-Space target's coordinates over the user's current Space, and a cursor pinned to an earlier window kept that window's state. Every other macOS pointer tool already pins before it pulses.

## What changed

- `ax_double_click` sends `PinAbove(wid)` and then `ClickPulse`, through a small `pulse_on_window` helper.
- A unit test applies those commands to a fresh cursor and to one pinned to another window, and checks that both end pinned to the target window. With the pin removed, the test fails.

## Scope

This covers the macOS AX double-click path used when the element has no `AXOpen`, and the foreground fallback after `AXOpen` fails. The pixel double-click already delegates to `click`, which pins. Linux and Windows are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

The change affects only the overlay cursor for AX double-clicks on macOS. Input delivery is unchanged. For a target on the current Space, the only difference is one extra `PinAbove`, the same command `click` sends.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks passed: fmt, clippy and the `platform-macos` double_click and cursor overlay tests, plus `cursor-overlay`'s off-workspace paint test. With `PinAbove` removed from the helper, the new test fails.
- The macOS Lume full lane of the verify-cua-driver skill passed at this head.
- Not run: a real second-Space or fullscreen setup, which the harness cannot script. Linux and Windows checks did not run either, since this change touches only macOS.

Reported in #3886 by @lorenzozanee.

Fixes #3801

This release was published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.

Changelog

Sourced from dnspython's changelog.

2.9.2

  • A maliciously crafted zone file could use a WKS record to consume excessive memory and CPU, possibly causing the process to exit due to memory exhaustion. Thanks to Jace (GitHub @​manus-use) for discovering and reporting this issue.

2.9.1

  • LOC text parsing now converts the altitude, size, horizontal precision, and vertical precision fields to centimeters exactly, and requires them to be decimal numbers of meters with at most two fractional digits, as RFC 1876 section 3 specifies. They were converted with float(), so 9.29m became 928 cm rather than 929 cm and the text and wire forms of the record disagreed, forms such as 1e3m, 1_000m, +10m, nanm, and infm were accepted, extra fractional digits were silently dropped, and an altitude outside the representable range was accepted and then failed in to_wire() with a non-DNS exception. dns.exception.SyntaxError is now raised for all of these.

  • The resolver now assigns a new random query id to every query.

  • For transports that require a 0 query id, set it in a way that does not break TSIG.

  • dns.message.QueryMessage.resolve_chaining() now caps the minimum TTL of a negative response with no SOA record at 300 seconds (dns.message.NEGATIVE_TTL_WITHOUT_SOA). Previously the TTL was left at its initial value of 2^32 - 1, so a single NXDOMAIN or NODATA response with no SOA, e.g. a spoofed one, stayed in the resolver cache for the life of the process.

  • DNSSEC validation now rejects an RRSIG whose type covered or class does not match the RRset, as RFC 4035 section 5.3.1 requires. This was not checked, so a revoked DNSKEY, which may only validate the DNSKEY RRset, still validated any RRset signed with its private key if the RRSIG claimed to cover DNSKEY.

  • dns.tokenizer.Tokenizer now ends a line at a carriage return, or at a carriage return followed by a line feed, unless the carriage return is in a quoted string. The carriage return of CRLF line ends used to stay in the last token of each line and in the text of a comment, so e.g. dns.zone.from_text() rejected a zone with CRLF line ends.

  • DNSSEC validation no longer uses a DNSKEY with the REVOKE flag set to validate anything other than the DNSKEY RRset. RFC 5011 section 2.1 says a revoked key must not be used for any other purpose, but it was a candidate key like any other, so as long as the revoked key was still published, data signed with its private key, e.g. by whoever compromised it, validated.

title: cua-driver (macOS): overlay commands are silently dropped when the cursor channel is full, so a PinAbove can be lost before its ClickPulse
body:
Found by reading the code on main at `d6a5c4f9ef`. Not observed in a run.

## What the code does

The macOS cursor overlay takes commands on one bounded channel of 4096 messages ([overlay.rs#L341](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L341)). Every sender uses `try_send` and throws away the result:

- `send_command` ([overlay.rs#L407-L416](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L407-L416)). Its doc comment says it "drops if the channel is full (old commands are less important than new ones)". The code doesn't match the comment: once the queue is full, the **new** command is the one that gets thrown away, and the old ones stay queued.
- `remove_cursor` ([#L449](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L449)) and `revive_cursor` ([#L460](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L460)) do the same.

Nothing is logged when a command is dropped.

The render loop is the only reader ([overlay.rs#L943-L1020](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L943-L1020)). It reads between frames, and it can wait on the main thread inside the loop: `on_appkit` calls `dispatch_sync_f` on the main queue when the display layout changes ([#L976-L985](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L976-L985), [#L835](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L835)). If the main thread is busy, the loop stops reading. Tools keep sending in the meantime. Drags send one `track_pointer_command` per step ([drag.rs#L190](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/drag.rs#L190), [#L437](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/drag.rs#L437)), and several sessions can send at once. When 4096 messages pile up, later commands are dropped until the loop catches up.

## Why PinAbove then ClickPulse is exposed

Several tools send `PinAbove(wid)` and then a `ClickPulse` or `MoveTo` as two separate `try_send` calls:

- double_click AX path: `pulse_on_window` ([double_click.rs#L233-L238](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/double_click.rs#L233-L238)), sent at [#L284-L286](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/double_click.rs#L284-L286)
- right_click ([right_click.rs#L224-L237](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/right_click.rs#L224-L237))
- click ([click.rs#L1227](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1227) then [#L1320](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1320); [#L1432](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1432) then [#L1450](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/click.rs#L1450))
- browser ([browser/platform.rs#L944-L962](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs#L944-L962))
- PinAbove followed by an `animate_cursor_to` MoveTo in drag, scroll, set_value, move_cursor and cursor_tools

If the channel is full when `PinAbove` is sent and one slot opens before the next command, the pin is dropped and the pulse or move is accepted. The pulse then runs with the previous `pinned_wid` and `pinned_target_off_workspace` ([overlay.rs#L733-L742](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L733-L742)). The z-order then stays tied to the previous window, and the cursor can paint over the current Space for a target that's on another Space. That's the case #3801 / #7659 fixed by sending the pin first. A dropped `MoveTo` from `animate_cursor_to` ([#L570](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d6a5c4f9efab5607c7c5632066be9054c84769d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L570)) also leaves its arrival waiter with nothing to wait for, and a dropped `Remove` leaves an ended session's cursor in the render map.

## How likely

Low. The queue only fills while the render loop is stalled, which needs a busy main thread and a lot of commands in flight. I haven't seen it happen. Other commands can be dropped the same way. The pin case gets its own section because a dropped pin leaves the overlay in the wrong place without any error.

## Possible directions (not decided)

- Send the pin and the command that follows it as one message, or one batch, so either both are applied or neither is.
- Never drop lifecycle messages (`Remove`, `Revive`, `PinAbove`). For example, block briefly or use a separate unbounded control lane.
- At minimum, log a `TrySendError::Full` and fix the doc comment on `send_command`.

title: [Bug]: get_guide returns its text only in the content block; the structured result has no guide text
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`get_guide` returns the guide's text only in the text content block. Its structured result holds `platform`, `sources`, `topic` and `topics`, with no text. Clients that show `structuredContent` when a tool returns one (Claude Code does), and `cua-driver call`, show the list of sources and never the guide, so the "Guides: `get_guide({topic})`" pointer in the server instructions leads nowhere.

### Reproduction

1. `cua-driver call get_guide '{"topic":"menus"}'`
2. Or call `get_guide` with `{"topic": "menus"}` from Claude Code through `cua-driver mcp`.

### Expected behavior

The guide's text reaches the caller: for example a `text` field in the structured result, or a structured result that is the same information as the text block.

### Actual behavior

Both print only:

```json
{
  "platform": "macOS",
  "sources": [
    { "file": "MACOS.md", "heading": "Navigating native menu bars (AXMenuBar)" },
    { "file": "MACOS.md", "heading": "Menus opened in the background keep the user's keyboard" }
  ],
  "topic": "menus",
  "topics": ["overview", "drag", "browser", "permissions", "batching", "menus"]
}
```

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.44.0, macOS 26.5.2, arm64; Claude Code 2.1 as the MCP client.
- Unchanged in the source at `cua-driver-rs-v0.49.4`: `cua-driver-core/src/guide.rs` builds `ToolResult::text(guide.text).with_structured(json!({ … "sources": sources … }))`.

### Evidence

The output above, from both routes.

### Workaround and additional context

The same files can be read as MCP resources (`skill://cua-driver/MACOS.md` and the others), but whole: `MACOS.md` is 59 KB, where the `menus` topic is two sections of it.

title: [Bug]: macOS get_window_state: a newline in an AX action name splits the tree row
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `get_window_state`'s Markdown tree writes accessibility action names as they are. An action whose name contains newlines splits its row over several lines, and the rows after it read as that element's children.

### Reproduction

1. Open a presentation in Microsoft PowerPoint for Mac (16.115).
2. `get_window_state` on the presentation window (`include_screenshot: false` is enough).

### Expected behavior

One line per element: control characters in an action name (and in `help` and `id`, which are written the same way) are escaped or replaced.

### Actual behavior

The Copilot button has a custom action whose name holds two newlines. The tree begins:

```
- [0] AXWindow "Presentation1" [actions=[raise]]
    - [1] AXButton (Copilot Chat) [help="Copilot Chat (⌃⌘I)" actions=[press,name:expand
target:0x0
selector:(null)]]
      - AXList (Thumbnail Pane)
        - [2] AXList [enabled=false]
          - AXCell (Slide 1 of 1 Slides)
        - AXLayoutArea (Slide Editor Pane, Slide 1 of 1 Slides)
        - AXLayoutArea (Notes Pane)
  - AXTabGroup (ribbon)
```

The thumbnail pane, the slide and the notes pane are siblings of that button in the window, not its children. A `query` read returns the stray fragment as a row of its own: `selector:(null)]]`.

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.44.0, macOS 26.5.2, arm64, through `cua-driver mcp` and `cua-driver call`.
- Unchanged in the source at `cua-driver-rs-v0.49.4`: `platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs` maps each action through `strip_prefix("AX")` and `to_lowercase()` and joins them into `actions=[…]`.

### Evidence

The tree above.

### Workaround and additional context

None needed to keep working, but a reader of the tree (a model) takes the wrong parent for everything under that row.
