**Blast Radius:** preparation.

Review the changed lifecycle semantics and run the project's remaining gates before making this draft ready. No merge, deployment, or release is requested.

title: Windows: background press_key with a modifier on a classic Win32 target types the bare key and reports success
body:
Environment: Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (19045), physical machine, interactive console session. Classic `C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe` (class `Notepad`, `Edit` child). cua-driver-rs **0.33.4** (x86_64-windows), run as `cua-driver.exe mcp --direct --embedded` from a non-elevated (Medium IL) process. Source references are to **v0.49.9** (`7239c061`), where each code path is unchanged.

**Version:** 0.33.4; same logic in v0.49.9.

**Repro**

1. `launch_app {"name":"notepad"}` (Win10 classic Notepad), click into the text.
2. `press_key {"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<hwnd>,"key":"z","modifiers":["ctrl"]}` (default `delivery_mode` = background).

**Expected:** Undo, or a `background_unavailable` refusal like the one VCL/Tk/Chromium targets get.
**Actual:** a literal `z` is inserted into the document, and the tool reports:

```
📨 Sent z to pid 10476 via PostMessage (not verified). If it didn't land, retry with delivery_mode:"foreground".
```

**Cause (by source):** `would_be_silently_dropped` (`platform-windows/src/input/delivery.rs:104`) refuses `KeyCombo` only for Chromium, WebView2 hosts, WPF, Tk and VCL. A classic Win32 window falls through to `post_key` (`input/keyboard.rs:422`), which posts `WM_KEYDOWN VK_CONTROL` and then the key. The Edit control reads the modifier through `GetKeyState`, which PostMessage does not update, so it sees a plain `z`. The tool description says as much ("classic Notepad ... DON'T fire the accelerator"), but press_key neither refuses nor escalates. With `"delivery_mode":"foreground"` (SendInput) the same call works.

title: Windows: type_text verification compares \n with the Edit control's \r\n and falsely reports a dropped delivery
body:
Environment: Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (19045), physical machine, interactive console session. Classic `C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe` (class `Notepad`, `Edit` child). cua-driver-rs **0.33.4** (x86_64-windows), run as `cua-driver.exe mcp --direct --embedded` from a non-elevated (Medium IL) process. Source references are to **v0.49.9** (`7239c061`), where each code path is unchanged.

**Version:** 0.33.4; same check in v0.49.9.

**Repro**

1. `launch_app {"name":"notepad"}` (Win10 classic Notepad), `get_window_state`.
2. `type_text {"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<hwnd>,"element_token":"<edit token>","text":"hello\n你好\ntest"}`

**Actual:** the text lands. A fresh `get_window_state` shows the Edit value containing `hello\r\n你好\r\ntest`. Yet the tool returns:

```
📨 Sent 13 char(s) to pid 10476 via PostMessage, but the focused field's value did not contain the requested text after dispatch — delivery was incomplete or dropped (e.g. a VCL/LibreOffice grid not in cell-edit mode). Retry with delivery_mode:"foreground".
```

with `"verify":"unchanged"`. An agent that follows the advice types the text a second time.

**Cause (by source):** `post_message_readback_observed` (`platform-windows/src/tools/type_text.rs:879`) checks `after.contains(requested_text)` on raw strings. Edit controls store Enter as CRLF. `plan_tail_retry` in the same file already normalizes with `normalize_newlines`, but this verdict does not.

Related: #4477 (closed; foreground multiline typing), different code path.

title: Windows: set_value is listed in actions for a classic Notepad Edit that has no ValuePattern
body:
Environment: Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (19045), physical machine, interactive console session. Classic `C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe` (class `Notepad`, `Edit` child). cua-driver-rs **0.33.4** (x86_64-windows), run as `cua-driver.exe mcp --direct --embedded` from a non-elevated (Medium IL) process. Source references are to **v0.49.9** (`7239c061`), where each code path is unchanged.

**Version:** 0.33.4; same code in v0.49.9.

**Repro**

1. `launch_app {"name":"notepad"}` (Win10 classic Notepad).
2. `get_window_state` lists `[0] Edit "文本编辑器" [id=15 actions=[set_value,scroll]]`.
3. `set_value {"pid":<pid>,"window_id":<hwnd>,"element_token":"<that token>","value":"abc"}`, with background or foreground delivery and with or without newlines in `value`.

**Actual**

```
set_value: element [0] does not implement ValuePattern or RangeValuePattern. For controls with TogglePattern (CheckBox) or SelectionItemPattern (RadioButton / ComboBoxItem), use the `click` tool instead.
```

(`structuredContent`: `{"code":"tool_invocation_failed"}`)

**Expected:** `set_value` should not be advertised for an element where it cannot work, or set_value should work for it.

**Cause (by source):** the tree adds `set_value` whenever `GetCachedPattern(UIA_ValuePatternId)` returns `Ok` (`platform-windows/src/uia/mod.rs:1027`). The tool then needs `GetCurrentPattern(UIA_ValuePatternId)` to cast to `IUIAutomationValuePattern` (`tools/set_value.rs`, error at line 197), and for this multiline Edit it does not. The tree also shows no `value` for this Edit, which fits.

Related but different: #7496 (set_value reports success without a signal).

title: macOS get_window_state: publish custom actions on an unlabeled AXGroup/AXScrollArea
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (macOS)

### Problem

`platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs` collapses an `AXGroup` or `AXScrollArea` that has no label: it recurses into the children, but the container itself never becomes an element. If the app hangs a custom action on that container (one listed by `AXUIElementCopyActionNames`, beyond the standard press/show-menu actions), `get_window_state` does not publish the container, so a caller cannot perform that action by name or by envelope.

#7637 narrows the collapse so a content-bearing group stays addressable, and it publishes custom actions on elements that are emitted. It documents the remaining case (an unlabeled container whose only interesting property is an action) as a known gap. #7637 did not cause it: before #7637, every `AXGroup` and `AXScrollArea` collapsed.

### Desired outcome

- Read the container's action names before deciding to collapse it. A container that exposes an action other than the standard ones is emitted as an element, and its custom actions are published like any other element's.
- Pure layout wrappers with no actions keep collapsing, so tree depth and size don't grow.
- Add an AppKit harness fixture: an unlabeled `NSView` group that exposes a custom accessibility action, and a test that the action is listed and dispatches by name and by envelope, next to `harness_appkit_custom_actions_are_published_and_dispatch_by_name_or_envelope`.

### Related

- #7637 (adds custom-action publishing and the content-bearing group case)
- #6270 (collapsing anonymous wrapper depth; it relies on the same "no primary action" test to decide what is a wrapper)

title: cua-driver: add Brave to isolated browser launch, and assert which browser the isolated test launched
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (browser, isolated launch)

### Problem

`browser_prepare` with an isolated launch (no `pid`) starts the first trusted installed browser through `select_isolated_browser_executable`. Brave is not among the candidates on main. #4390's commit 87f77ba adds Brave after Chrome and Edge. It was left out of the salvage #7708 for two reasons:

- Candidates are tried in the order Chrome, Edge, Brave, so Brave starts only where neither Chrome nor Edge is installed. GitHub's Windows and Ubuntu runners ship both, and the fork CI's isolated test passed without starting Brave: its Windows recording shows Chrome opening. The test does not check which browser started.
- Adding a binary the driver launches with DevTools enabled widens the trust boundary. The trust anchors need review on their own (macOS team ID `KL8N8XSYF4` / `com.brave.Browser`, Windows Authenticode signer of `brave.exe`, Linux root-owned `/opt/brave.com/brave/brave`; Snap and Flatpak not covered).

### Desired outcome

A separate PR that:

- adds Brave's trusted install locations to the isolated-launch candidates on each platform, with the trust anchors above and their source;
- makes the isolated-launch E2E assert which browser product and executable it launched, so a lane that asks for `brave` fails if Chrome or Edge starts instead (this check is also worth having for the existing Chrome and Edge lanes);
- has docs saying when Brave is picked for an isolated launch (only when no earlier candidate is installed, unless a product can be requested).

### Related

- #4390 (commit 87f77ba), #7708, #7053

title: CI: run the standalone browser E2E with CUA_E2E_BROWSER_PRODUCTS=brave on Linux X11
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (CI)

### Problem

`.github/workflows/e2e-rust-standalone-browsers.yml` runs `CUA_E2E_BROWSER_PRODUCTS=chrome,edge` on Windows and `chrome` on Linux X11. No workflow runs a Brave product. The existing-profile setup for Brave (#7708, #7059) touches shared code in `cua-driver-core` and Linux and macOS adapters, and one Linux defect was found only by a live run: Brave opens `brave://inspect/#remote-debugging` but reports the document URI as `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging`, so the Linux setup check refused the page. CI would not catch a regression there.

### Desired outcome

- Once the harness accepts `brave` in `CUA_E2E_BROWSER_PRODUCTS` (it does in #7708), add a matrix entry that installs Brave from Brave's apt repository on `ubuntu-latest` and runs the standalone browser E2E with `CUA_E2E_BROWSER_PRODUCTS=brave` under Linux X11, covering `standalone_browser_existing_profile_standard_refusal`, `standalone_browser_existing_profile` and `standalone_browser_existing_profile_setup`.
- Windows and macOS Brave lanes are worth adding later, so the browsers guide can mark those platforms validated.

### Related

title: fix(cua-driver): resolve Brave's default profile root on Linux and macOS
body:
## Why
If Brave runs on its default profile, with no `--user-data-dir`, the driver has no profile root for it on Linux or macOS. It then never reads Brave's `DevToolsActivePort`, so existing-profile setup can't find Brave's endpoint. Windows already maps Brave. This is a follow-up to #7059, which adds the Brave setup descriptor.

Refs #7059

## What changed
- macOS: Brave maps to `~/Library/Application Support/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser`. This is the `CrProductDirName` in Brave's Info.plist (Brave's `build/config.gni` sets `brave_product_dir_name`), which Chromium appends to Application Support.
- Linux: Brave maps to `BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser` under the config home. This follows brave-core's `chromium_src/chrome/common/chrome_paths_linux.cc`.
- Linux: the config home now comes from the browser process's own environment (`/proc/<pid>/environ`). It uses `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when set, otherwise `HOME/.config`, which is the rule Chromium's `GetXDGDirectory` uses. A relative result goes through the same `/proc/<pid>/cwd` resolution as a relative `--user-data-dir`. Chrome, Edge and Chromium get the same fix.

## Scope
Covers the stable channel only. Beta, Dev and Nightly add a suffix such as `-Beta`, and they still need `--user-data-dir`, the same as other browsers' side channels today. The setup descriptor and docs are in #7059 and are not repeated here.

## Blast Radius
This only touches the fallback used when the browser has no `--user-data-dir`. Explicit absolute, relative and duplicated `--user-data-dir` handling is unchanged. A found port file must still match a loopback listener that the browser process owns, so a wrong root can only miss an endpoint. It cannot attach to the wrong one.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` and `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets` pass. The new Brave test fails (`left: None`) with the mapping removed.
- Brave's official macOS DMG reports `CrProductDirName` = `BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser` and bundle id `com.brave.Browser`.
- On the macOS host, the Linux crate was not built. `default_user_data_dir` and its test pass as a standalone extraction there. Linux crate checks run in CI.

title: feat(cua-driver): read spreadsheet cells back after keyboard actions
body:
## What changed for users

Agents filling a spreadsheet with the keyboard now see what each keystroke did to the sheet in the action's own result: which cells changed and to what, where the cursor is, and when another sheet came up. Reading a sheet is also much shorter: cells are listed one line per sheet row (empty runs collapsed) instead of one tree row per visible cell.

## Why

Spreadsheet apps (LibreOffice Calc here) expose the visible cells as an `AXTable` whose children are named by address (`AXTextField "E2" = "..."`), plus a name box whose value is the active cell. Two costs follow:

- `type_text`, `press_key` and `hotkey` into a sheet return `unverifiable` ("verify via screenshot"), so after each entry the caller re-reads the window or takes a screenshot, and often types again to be sure. The typed values are in the accessibility tree; nothing reads them back.
- A read of a sheet window lists every visible cell, most of them empty: one screen of a sheet is several hundred tree rows.

## How

- `cua_driver_core::sheet_grid` (platform-neutral): finds a grid in walked nodes (a table/grid whose descendants are cells named with A1-style addresses, at least 4), the active cell (a combo box whose value is an address, else the one selected cell), diffs two reads (changed values for cells visible in both, active cell moved, table renamed = another sheet, visible range scrolled) and renders the change. Structural detection only; no app names.
- `get_window_state`: when the tree has a grid, its cell rows are rewritten as one `row "N"` line per sheet row: filled cells as `[index] A1="value"`, runs of empty cells as `[first..last] B1..D1 empty`, and consecutive all-empty rows as one `rows "9..40"` line. Every cell keeps its index, so tokens still act on any cell. `full_output:true` keeps the raw rows. The grid is remembered per window.
- Action results (the tools already wrapped for visible-effect evidence: click, type_text, press_key, hotkey, scroll, invoke_menu, ...): for a window whose last read or action showed a grid, the grid is read again after a 250 ms settle (once more after 400 ms if nothing changed yet, for long typed input) and the result gets one line, e.g.
  `Sheet table "Sheet Data" read back after the action: 2 cell(s) changed: B2 "" -> "12.5", A3 "" -> "Bo". Active cell B3 (was B2), empty.`
  A change adds `window_change` evidence, confirms an otherwise unverified action and drops the "read it again" hint; no change leaves the verdict as it was (an uncommitted entry is still in the cell editor). The baseline is the last complete read, else a read before the action. Bounded: each grid read walks at most 4000 nodes / 1.5 s, and other windows pay nothing.

## Tests

- `sheet_grid`: 13 unit tests (address parsing/printing, grid detection vs ordinary tables, name box vs selected cell, diff of typed values / moves / another sheet / scrolling, rendering, compact markdown incl. empty runs, merged empty rows and multi-line values).
- `action_evidence`: 2 new tests (a changed sheet confirms and drops the re-read hint; an unchanged sheet keeps the verdict).
- clippy `-D warnings` (cua-driver-core, platform-macos, all targets); `bin/ci --quick`.

Stacked on #7701. Refs CUA-4064.

title: test(cua-driver): drive an NSSavePanel sheet through its macOS window
body:
## Why

#4551 by @Ed-Key made foreground keys aimed at a macOS window reach a sheet attached to it, and made a read of the sheet's own id name its parent window. #6758 has since landed the same behavior on main. Its `AxWindowId::is` makes a focused sheet confirm keys addressed to its parent, in both `await_window_focused` and `with_foreground_hid_activation`, and a read of a sheet's own id now walks the sheet. #4551 now conflicts with main, and its runtime change is redundant there. Its NSSavePanel fixture and e2e rows still add coverage that main lacks: a real Save panel, not a plain test sheet. This PR keeps those tests, with Ed-Key as the commit author.

Salvaged from #4551

Fixes #3351
Fixes #4392

## What changed

- The AppKit fixture has a new opt-in `save_sheet` scenario (`CUA_APPKIT_SAVE_SHEET=1`). It adds a button that opens an `NSSavePanel` as a sheet on the main window, and a label that records how the panel ended.
- `harness_appkit_save_sheet_controls_act_through_their_window` sets the sheet's name field and presses Save by element token through the parent window in the background. It then reads the sheet by its own id and checks that the read holds the name field and not the parent's controls.
- `harness_appkit_foreground_key_reaches_an_attached_sheet` sends foreground Return aimed at the parent window while the sheet holds focus, which saves the file. It then sends Escape aimed at the sheet's own id, which cancels. Both rows are registered in `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh`.

## Scope

Tests and fixture only. The driver code is unchanged. The sheet-id read now asserts main's #6758 contract (the sheet's own tree) instead of #4551's `escalation.parent_window_id`. On main a sheet's id resolves, so that field is never emitted. Windows and Linux have no sheets of this kind.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (fmt, clippy for `cua-driver-e2e` tests, the AppKit fixture build) pass.
- The macOS Lume full lane passed at this head. Both new rows passed, and so did main's existing `sheet_and_parent_ids_both_reach_the_sheet_and_the_sheet_snapshot_is_isolated`.
- Linux and Windows checks did not run (macOS host).

title: fix(cua-driver): count focus in a window's inline rename field as focus on that window
body:
Salvaged from #4616
Fixes #4615
Refs #7727

## Why

With Finder in front and its inline rename field open, a foreground key on the Finder window is refused with "exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery". That route is the one #4483's `file_name_needs_rename` refusal points to. While the field holds focus, Finder reports no `AXFocusedWindow`, so foreground HID delivery re-keys the window and then cannot see it focused. The field is an `AXTextField` in its own small WindowServer window, and that window's WindowServer parent is the Finder window. The field's AX parent is the application and it has no `AXWindow`, so WindowServer's parent record is the only link back to the Finder window.

## What changed

- `window_parent_id` in `input/skylight.rs` reads a window's WindowServer parent through `SLSWindowQueryWindows` and `SLSWindowIteratorGetParentID`.
- `inline_editor_open` in `ax/bindings.rs` checks whether the app's focused element is an `AXTextField` whose own window is a child of the requested window. The decision is the pure `is_inline_editor`, which has unit tests.
- `with_foreground_hid_activation` uses that check only when the app reports no focused window, and then treats the requested window as focused. A reported focused window is handled as before.

## Scope

This covers foreground HID delivery while the target app reports no focused window. It does not cover Finder dropping the rename field when another app is in front (the second half of #4615, now tracked in #7727). The original author plans that as a follow-up built on this change.

The original commit by @Ed-Key is cherry-picked with `-x` and keeps its author. It is adapted to current main in two places. `focused_window_id_of_pid` now returns an `AxWindowId`, so the fallback wraps the target with `AxWindowId::window`. Main removed `get_active_space`, so the old merge conflict resolves to adding only `window_parent_id`.

## Blast Radius

This touches macOS foreground keyboard delivery only. The fallback applies only when every condition holds: the app reports no focused window, it reports a focused `AXTextField`, and that field's own window is a WindowServer child of exactly the requested window. In every other case, including a failed lookup, behavior is unchanged. Both AX reads use 0.2 s messaging timeouts.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks run here were `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check` and the em dash check. All passed. A static review of the adapted types and the CF/AX ownership in the new FFI found no issues.
- On macOS (arm64), at this head, `platform-macos` builds, its unit tests pass (including the two new `is_inline_editor` tests), and `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. CI's "Rust macOS unit" and "fmt, clippy, test (macos-26)" jobs also pass at this head.
- The macOS Lume lane, and with it a live Finder rename run, did not run. The Lume host was short of disk and busy with other runs, and the registered matrix has no Finder rename cell. Linux and Windows checks don't apply to this macOS-only diff and did not run here.
- On the original branch, the author's runs with Finder in front completed the rename by both the keyboard route and the File > Rename route. On main, both routes end with the final Return refused. The author's other foreground cases did not change. The reproduction steps are in #4616.

title: [Bug]: macOS Finder rename through foreground keys or File > Rename never commits when another app is in front
body:
Split out of #4615 so its other-app-in-front half stays tracked once #7725 closes it. #7725 fixes only the Finder-in-front half: the final foreground `press_key return` refused with "exact target window did not become focused for foreground HID delivery".

With another app in front (TextEdit, or the agent's own terminal), a Finder rename through foreground keys or File > Rename still never commits, and every call reports success. A foreground `press_key return` opens Finder's rename field, then cua-driver hands the front back to the previous app, and Finder cancels the field within about 0.2 s. With `invoke_menu ["File", "Rename"]` the front goes back before the field opens at all. Both foreground restores (the one in `with_foreground_hid_activation` and the one in `invoke_menu`) give the front back while the field is open or about to open.

Reproduction, quoted from #4615:

> 1. In a logged-in macOS session with cua-driver 0.33.1 (main `2400bbefd`), create a folder with `draft.txt` and `other.txt` and open it in Finder. Open two more Finder windows (Documents, Downloads), so Finder has three windows. Background keys to Finder are then refused `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`, so agents use `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.
> 2. Put TextEdit in front.
> 3. `list_windows` gives Finder's `<pid>` and the folder window's `<window_id>`. `get_window_state` on it, then `click` the `draft.txt` name cell's `element_token` (selects the row).
> 4. Keyboard route, each call on the folder window:
>    ```json
>    {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "key": "return", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
>    {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "keys": ["cmd", "a"], "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
>    {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "text": "final.txt", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
>    {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "key": "return", "delivery_mode": "foreground"}
>    ```
>    (`press_key`, `hotkey`, `type_text`, `press_key`.)
> 5. Menu route instead of the first Return: `invoke_menu` with `{"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <window_id>, "path": ["File", "Rename"]}`, then the same `hotkey`, `type_text` and `press_key` calls.
> 6. List the folder on disk after each call.
>
> Reproduced 5 of 5 times for each route, with Finder relaunched clean and a fresh fixture before each run.

Actual behavior with TextEdit in front, quoted from #4615:

> TextEdit in front, keyboard route, every run:
>
> ```text
> press_key return   -> "✅ Pressed return on pid <pid> (delivery_mode:foreground)."
> hotkey cmd+a       -> "Pressed cmd+a on pid <pid> (delivery_mode:foreground)."
> type_text          -> "📨 Sent (unverified) 9 char(s) via foreground keystrokes (30ms delay). — driver could not confirm; verify via screenshot."
> press_key return   -> "✅ Pressed return on pid <pid> (delivery_mode:foreground)."
> ```
>
> The disk listing stayed `["draft.txt", "other.txt"]` after every call. A 20 ms poll of the front app and of Finder's focused element (read outside cua-driver) shows each foreground Return: Finder becomes active, its rename field (an `AXTextField` in its own small window) takes focus, TextEdit is made active again about 100 to 200 ms later, and the field is gone. cmd+a and the typed text then reach Finder's list, not a field, and the final Return just opens a new field that is cancelled the same way.
>
> Menu route, every run: `invoke_menu` returns "Resolved the live native menu path and dispatched its final accessibility action; verify the command's semantic effect from fresh state." The front app returns to TextEdit about 100 ms after the menu closes, before Finder shows the rename field (about 0.4 s after the press), so no field ever opens; the remaining calls report success as above, and the disk is unchanged.

Expected: the file is renamed, or a call that cannot get there says so.

Environment in #4615: cua-driver 0.33.1, main `2400bbefd`, macOS 26.4 on Apple Silicon, Finder list view. The workaround there still applies: bring Finder to the front first, or send the keys with `scope: "desktop"` while Finder is frontmost.

Related: #4615, #4616, #7725, #4483.

title: fix(cua-driver): unload all known LaunchAgents before the app swap
body:
## What changed

`stop_cua_driver_daemons` (Darwin) claimed to unload "Both known LaunchAgent plists" but only unloaded `com.trycua.cua-driver-rs.plist`, and checked that one path twice in a nested `if`. On a host where the `com.trycua.cua-driver` agent is loaded (the label `uninstall.sh` treats as the non-legacy name), `KeepAlive` respawned `serve` inside the swap window. The respawned daemon either execs the old binary off the renamed backup bundle or starts while the install is half-swapped, and its permission gate is wrong from then on: `diagnose` probes return `unknown`/`false`, the setup wizard waits for a switch that is already on, and MCP calls return `permissions_pending`.

Both plist paths are now unloaded and both labels are removed, so a job cannot respawn mid-swap whether or not its plist file still exists. The survivor note also admits launchd respawns as a cause and points at `launchctl list | grep trycua`, instead of only blaming ignored signals and suggesting a logout.

## How this was found

Updating in place (0.47.18 to 0.49.10 via `update --apply`, and separately `brew reinstall --cask cuadriver`) left a wedged `serve` every time: the graceful stop fired, launchd respawned the daemon mid-swap, and `lsof` showed the survivor running the old binary out of `CuaDriver.app.install-backup.*`. Killing it let launchd respawn a healthy daemon, so the grants themselves were never the problem. Full evidence and repro details in #7461.

Refs #7461. A daemon-side hardening idea (re-initialise the gate when `current_exe()` no longer resolves under the live bundle, near `fresh_status_with_request`) is left as a possible follow-up; this change covers the installer side.

## Validation

- New test `test_installer_stop_unloads_every_known_launchagent` asserts `launchctl unload` fires for both plist paths and `launchctl remove` for both labels. It fails on the pre-change code, where only the `-rs` plist was touched.
- `pytest libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_uninstall_stops_daemons_from_other_copies.py` - 19 passed.
- `pytest` on `test_installer_bash32_syntax`, `test_install_macos_tcc`, `test_uninstall_autostart`, `test_install_isolated_autostart`, `test_install_autostart_summary` - all pass.
- `bash -n` clean.
- `bin/ci --quick` could not run in this sparse checkout: its pnpm lockfile scan checks index paths that are not materialised on disk. Left to CI.

title: feat(cua-driver): background drag-and-drop on macOS
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a background `drag` that starts an AppKit drag-and-drop session (reordering a table row, moving an item onto a drop target) was refused with `background_unavailable`, reason `drag_and_drop_session`. Tasks that need a native drag could not finish while another app stays in front.
- What changed: the drag now completes in the background. AppKit ends a session started by window-routed events soon after it starts, dropping at the last dragged point. So once the drag image window shows, the driver skips the rest of the path, posts drags at the drop point until the drag image closes (up to 1.5 s), then releases there. The result says the session ended at the drop point and carries `drag_session: true`. A session still open after the hold returns the same `drag_and_drop_session` refusal as before, and the optional brief foreground step still applies to it.

The real pointer does not move, the window is not raised, and the frontmost app keeps key focus. No hardware events are posted.

## Related work

Fixes #5477

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a background drag that used to be refused now drops. Drags that start no session are unchanged. Recovery hint text and docs for the refusal were updated to describe the new failure case.
- Risk and rollback: the drop lands where AppKit's session ends. On a busy app the drop can land one row off. The result stays `unverifiable`, so the agent reads the window back as before. Revert restores the refusal.

## Validation

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core --all-targets`, `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib input::mouse` (new tests for the hold, the release point and a session that never ends), `cargo test -p cua-driver-core recovery_hint`, and the `cua-driver` build.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS 26 VM, an NSTableView reorder fixture behind a frontmost sentinel app. Background `drag` reorders the rows through the daemon, with no front change, key loss, pointer move or raise on the sentinel. On `main` the same call is refused.
- Known gaps: Linux and Windows code is untouched and was not built here.

risk: standard

title: feat(cua-driver): add screenshot compression, screenshot-only mode, and screenshot_clip crop to get_browser_state
body:
<!--
Open PR linked to #7454 with full code diffs, unit/integration verification, and live 2x Retina visual captures alongside the scoping discussion in trycua/cua#7454.
-->

## Summary

- Problem this solves: While `get_window_state` already scopes desktop captures to `(pid, window_id)` (with `screenshot_format`, `screenshot_quality`, `max_dimension`, `max_image_dimension`, `include_accessibility_tree: false`, and `zoom`) and `get_browser_state` snapshot mode already captures only the browser tab viewport via CDP `Page.captureScreenshot`, `get_browser_state` still returned full native high-DPI PNGs, re-emitted the full DOM ref tree (`MAX_REFS_PER_SNAPSHOT = 300`) when only inspecting pixels, and lacked sub-viewport region cropping.
- What changed:
  1. **Viewport screenshot compression & long-edge sizing (`414fbc7`)**: Added opt-in `screenshot_format` (`"png"` default or `"jpeg"`), `screenshot_quality` (`1..=95`, default `85`, `"jpeg"` only), and `max_image_dimension` (`>= 0`, `0` or omitted keeps native pixels) to `get_browser_state` snapshot mode. Reused `CapturedImage::encode` in `capture_tab_screenshot` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/engine.rs`) and `with_tab_screenshot` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs`), returning matching `image/jpeg` or `image/png` MCP blocks, updating `screenshot_mime_type`, recalculating `pixel_to_css_scale_x/y`, and tightening bind mode (`pid` + `window_id`) to reject explicit `include_screenshot: true` or screenshot params with `invalid_arguments`.
  2. **Screenshot-only capture `include_snapshot: false` (`73b79ba`)**: Added `include_snapshot` (default `true`) to `get_browser_state` snapshot mode (requiring `include_screenshot: true` and rejecting `snapshot_format`, `scope_ref`, `query`, and `continuation`). Skips `snapshot_tab` / `snapshot_tab_semantic`, omits `snapshot_id`, `url`, `refs`, and `outline`, returns `mode: "screenshot"` while preserving previously minted tab `refs`, and adds `ToolOperation::BrowserScreenshot` (`"browser_screenshot"`, `is_computer_action: false`) in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/server.rs`.
  3. **Viewport-relative region crop `screenshot_clip` (`3616499`)**: Added `screenshot_clip: { x, y, width, height }` in `viewport_css_px` (`x >= 0`, `y >= 0`, `width > 0`, `height > 0`, strict 4-key finite object without `exclusiveMinimum` for Vertex AI schema compatibility). Offsets CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` `clip` by the visual viewport scroll origin (`page_x`, `page_y`), clamps overflows past the right/bottom edge (`clip_clamped: true`), refuses `< 1.0` CSS px intersection with `invalid_arguments`, sets `screenshot.scope: "clip"` + `screenshot.clip` + `screenshot.clip_clamped`, recalculates `pixel_to_css_scale_x/y = clip.width/height / pixel_width/height`, combines freely with `include_snapshot: false` / `jpeg` / `max_image_dimension`, and updates `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md`, `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/mcp-tools/pointer-cursor-and-browser.mdx`, and `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/cli-specs/cua-driver-mcp-{linux,macos,windows}.json`.

### Scope & Design Trade-offs (Open PR Paired with Decision Note in #7454)

Submitted alongside a product/design decision comment in #7454 so maintainers can inspect the full diff and live captures while deciding whether to pursue this direction and which parts to keep, cut, rename, or split:

- **Potentially over-scoped pending maintainer preference**:
  - Bundles all 3 capabilities (`9` files, `+1172/-41`) in a single branch before the design note in #7454 was aligned.
  - Enforces strict `invalid_arguments` when bind mode (`pid` + `window_id`) receives `include_screenshot: true` or screenshot args (instead of silently ignoring).
  - Adds a new telemetry operation variant `ToolOperation::BrowserScreenshot` (`"browser_screenshot"`).
- **Not implemented / intentional gaps**:
  - Desktop/native `get_window_state` is untouched (already window-scoped with `screenshot_format`, `max_dimension`, `max_image_dimension`, `include_accessibility_tree: false`, and `zoom`).
  - `screenshot_clip` accepts viewport CSS coordinates only (no selector/`ref` crop, no `full_page`), and `get_browser_state` does not add a `max_dimension` legacy alias alongside `max_image_dimension`.
  - Dense 2x Retina monospace diff regions still weigh `73,266 B` at `799x274` JPEG `q=80` (`-87.4%` vs `579,737 B` full viewport), above the `20-30 KB` target mentioned in #7454, whereas simple/modal crops land at `6.5-27.2 KB`.
  - `libs/cua/skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md` is not modified because the repo skill sync helper already fails on unrelated drift on base `fc0dff2`.

## Related work

Refs #7454

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission, or cross-component contract change): Pending maintainer scoping decision in #7454 (this PR supplies concrete diffs and measurements for that decision).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Additive optional schema fields on `get_browser_state` snapshot mode; default behavior (`screenshot_format: "png"`, `include_snapshot: true`, unclipped viewport, native resolution) is unchanged. Note two deliberate strictness choices open to feedback: (1) bind mode (`pid` + `window_id`) explicitly passing `include_screenshot: true` or any screenshot parameter now returns `invalid_arguments`, and (2) `ToolOperation::BrowserScreenshot` introduces a new telemetry event name. Schema avoids `exclusiveMinimum` for Vertex AI compatibility.
- Risk and rollback: Changes are isolated to `browser/engine.rs`, `browser/tools.rs`, `server.rs`, tests, and generated CLI/docs contracts (`9` files). Any subset (compression only, `include_snapshot: false`, or `screenshot_clip`) can be dropped cleanly per commit (`414fbc7`, `73b79ba`, `3616499`) or reverted cleanly without migration.

## Validation

- Manual or platform evidence (live 2x Retina Chrome E2E via `cua-driver serve --embedded` and `cua-driver call --screenshot-out-file` on `3616499`, Exit `0`):
  - **Ref preservation (`simple.html`)**: Minted button `p17:0` -> ran `get_browser_state(include_snapshot: false, include_screenshot: true, screenshot_format: "jpeg", screenshot_quality: 80, max_image_dimension: 1280)` (`mode: "screenshot"`) -> clicked `p17:0` via `browser_click(input_route: "dom_event")` (`effect: "confirmed"`) -> `semantic_v2` readback confirmed `Clicked!`.
  - **Scroll-offset crop + pixel-to-CSS click (`scroll.html`)**: After scrolling past a `1024px` spacer, clipped `{20, 0, 500, 220}` (`1000x440` PNG, `26,867 B` pre-click / `28,342 B` post-click), computed orange button centroid `(254.66, 245.99)` from raw PNG pixels, mapped `(147.33, 122.99)` via `css = clip + img * pixel_to_css_scale`, and dispatched background `trusted` click -> `Clip Clicked!` / `CLIP_COORDS_OK`.
  - **Clamping & strict errors**: Overflow `{900, 556, 600, 400}` clamped cleanly to `{900, 556, 300, 180}` (`clip_clamped: true`, `600x360` JPEG `6,532 B`); all `10` live `invalid_arguments` test cases (missing screenshot, quality on PNG, snapshot query with `include_snapshot: false`, bind mode with screenshot/clip, out-of-viewport `{1235, 0}` on `1185x736`, negative `x`, zero `width`, extra unknown field) exited `1` with `invalid_arguments`.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 摘要

- **解决的问题**：`get_window_state` 目前已支持按 `(pid, window_id)` 隔离窗口截图（并具备 `screenshot_format`、`screenshot_quality`、`max_dimension`、`max_image_dimension`、`include_accessibility_tree: false` 与 `zoom` 能力），`get_browser_state` 快照模式也已通过 CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` 仅截取浏览器标签页视口（不包含桌面周围元素）。但 `get_browser_state` 仍直接返回原生高分屏大图 PNG，仅看图时仍会附带整套 DOM 引用列表（`MAX_REFS_PER_SNAPSHOT = 300`），且缺少按视口局部区域裁剪的能力。
- **核心改动**：
  1. **视口截图压缩与长边限幅（`414fbc7`）**：为 `get_browser_state` 快照模式新增按需参数 `screenshot_format`（默认 `"png"` 或 `"jpeg"`）、`screenshot_quality`（`1..=95`，默认 `85`，仅 `"jpeg"` 生效）与 `max_image_dimension`（`>= 0`，`0` 或省略保留原生像素）。在 `capture_tab_screenshot`（`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/engine.rs`）与 `with_tab_screenshot`（`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs`）中复用 `CapturedImage::encode`，返回匹配的 `image/jpeg` 或 `image/png` 内容块、更新 `screenshot_mime_type`、重算 `pixel_to_css_scale_x/y`，并收紧绑定模式（`pid` + `window_id`）校验，拒绝显式 `include_screenshot: true` 或任何截图参数（返回 `invalid_arguments`）。
  2. **轻量只截图模式 `include_snapshot: false`（`73b79ba`）**：为 `get_browser_state` 快照模式新增 `include_snapshot`（默认 `true`），设为 `false` 时要求同时传 `include_screenshot: true` 并拒绝 `snapshot_format`、`scope_ref`、`query` 与 `continuation`。跳过 `snapshot_tab` / `snapshot_tab_semantic`，省略 `snapshot_id`、`url`、`refs` 与 `outline`，返回 `mode: "screenshot"` 且保留标签页既有 `refs`，并在 `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/server.rs` 新增 `ToolOperation::BrowserScreenshot`（`"browser_screenshot"`，`is_computer_action: false`）。
  3. **视口 CSS 局部裁剪 `screenshot_clip`（`3616499`）**：为 `get_browser_state` 快照模式新增 `screenshot_clip: { x, y, width, height }`，单位为相对当前视口左上角的 CSS 像素（`x >= 0`、`y >= 0`、`width > 0`、`height > 0`，严格 4 键有限数字且不带 `exclusiveMinimum` 以兼容 Vertex AI Schema）。自动叠加视觉视口滚动偏移（`page_x`、`page_y`）定位 CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` 的裁剪区域，超出右/底边界自动裁齐并返回 `clip_clamped: true`，可见交集 `< 1.0` CSS 像素时返回 `invalid_arguments`，返回 `screenshot.scope: "clip"`、`screenshot.clip` 与 `screenshot.clip_clamped` 并按 `pixel_to_css_scale_x/y = clip.width/height / pixel_width/height` 重算比例，支持与 `include_snapshot: false`、`jpeg` 和 `max_image_dimension` 自由组合，并同步更新 `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md`、`docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/mcp-tools/pointer-cursor-and-browser.mdx` 与 `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/cli-specs/cua-driver-mcp-{linux,macos,windows}.json`。

### 改动边界与方案取舍（配合 `#7454` 决策讨论的正式待审 PR）

title: fix(cua-driver): press a real Enter for a trailing newline in browser_type
body:
Salvaged from #4499

Fixes #4482

## Why

`browser_type` with text ending in `"\n"` reported every character as delivered, but the page never got a working Enter. #7857 has since re-landed @sahiljagtap08's fix from #4499 on main: a single-line input gets a real Enter (`code: "Enter"`, key code 13) and a textarea keeps the newline. This PR merges main and keeps the review fixes that #7857 does not have. The branch still carries #4499's original commits with their authorship.

## What changed

- In `insert_text` mode the trailing Enter now runs inside CDP focus emulation, as `keystrokes` mode already did, because an inactive tab drops key events without it.
- If the single-line probe fails, the call refuses before typing anything. Before, it fell back to `insertText`, which drops the newline on an input and reports success.
- Once an Enter key event is sent, a failure is reported as `browser_input_incomplete` with `enter_uncertain: true` and tells the caller to read the page before retrying, since a CDP timeout or dropped socket can follow a key event Chrome already dispatched. A failure only in focus-emulation cleanup after a pressed Enter says that Enter was pressed.

## Scope

Covers `browser_type` in `cua-driver-core`'s shared CDP path. Against current main the diff is `browser/tools.rs` and its mock-CDP tests. Other browser tools, native `type_text`, and the generated references are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

All platforms share this CDP path. Only calls whose text ends in a newline change: an `insert_text` call into a single-line field now toggles focus emulation, a failed probe refuses instead of typing, and a failed Enter reports `enter_uncertain`.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cua-driver-core` browser tests pass at the merged head (306), including new mock-CDP tests for the focus-emulation ordering, a failed probe, a partial Enter and a failed cleanup. `bin/ci --quick` passes.
- Linux and Windows platform checks could not run, because the macOS host cannot build them.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC.
- [x] Tests are included; the Linux and Windows platform gap is explained above.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved (#4499's commits are on the branch).
- [x] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --quick --signoff` on the head commit).

title: feat(cua-driver): add browser_motion_policy for driver-owned tabs
body:
## Why

#4557 proposes an opt-in way to give driver-owned browser tabs `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, so pages that honour the preference stop decorative animation between observe and act. This adds that first slice as the `browser_motion_policy` MCP tool. It uses only the standard media-feature emulation: no CSS injection, no timer or video freezing, and existing profiles are not touched. It builds on @kvnloo's prototype in kvnloo/cua#110, whose commit keeps its author here.

Fixes #4557

## What changed

- New `browser_motion_policy` tool (`target_id`, `tab_id`, `mode: reduce | default`). `reduce` sends `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia` with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` on one exactly bound tab, and `default` clears it. It is wired into authorization (R2, bound-input adapter), capabilities (`browser.motion.policy`), telemetry, the MCP compat tool list and the generated MCP reference.
- Tabs that are not driver-owned (approved existing profiles, embedded applications) are refused with `browser_wrong_target_refused` and reason `motion_policy_driver_owned_only`, and no CDP command is sent.
- Chromium keeps an emulation override only while the CDP session that set it stays attached, and every call attaches a fresh tab session. The prototype therefore sent `default` on a new session and left the page reduced. The connection now records which session holds each target's override, and both modes go to it. A failed reply keeps the holder, since the override may have applied. A detach, or Chromium's session-not-found answer, drops it.

## Scope

Covers driver-owned isolated Chromium tabs, for the life of the session that prepared them. The override follows the tab across navigation and ends when the session's browser is reaped at session end. Out of scope: existing personal profiles, embedded apps, CSS suppression, freezing timers/video/canvas, and any change to default behaviour. The benchmark arm the RFC describes (screenshot churn and step latency, baseline vs reduced) is not part of this change.

## Tradeoffs

The override is kept per target on the CDP connection, not on the tab record. Chromium ties the override to the CDP session, and the connection already tracks session detaches for dialogs, so detach and socket close clear it without new lifecycle code.

## Blast Radius

A new tool only. Existing browser tools are unchanged. The shared code touched is an extra map on `CdpConnection`, written only by this tool and cleared on detach or close, and a test-only helper in `prepare.rs`.

## Verification

- Unit tests against the mock CDP endpoint cover the refusal path, `default` clearing on the session that ran `reduce`, a lost `reduce` reply, and a holder that Chromium reports gone. The refusal and same-session tests each fail with their fix reverted.
- The ignored real-browser row `standalone_browser_reduced_motion_policy` passes on Linux X11 (Xvfb) with real Chromium. Page `matchMedia` flips to reduce, the semantic action surface is unchanged, a click still lands, `default` restores the baseline, and `end_session` removes the isolated profile. Before the session fix, the same row failed at the reset with the page still reporting `motion=reduce`.
- The scoped repository checks for cua-driver passed: rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the browser unit tests, the `.github/scripts` tests and the generated reference. The Windows cross-check passed at an earlier head of this branch. One `.github/scripts` test, `test_a_release_install_grants_nothing_on_kwin_and_says_how_to[False]`, also fails on main without this change. macOS and Windows native runs were not possible on this host.

title: fix(ci): retry GitHub release API rate-limited 403 responses
body:
## Summary

- Problem: the release API client retries 429 and transient 5xx responses but immediately fails a GitHub rate-limit response using HTTP 403.
- Change: retry a 403 only when rate-limit headers identify it. Respect `Retry-After`, or wait until `X-RateLimit-Reset` when the primary quota is exhausted. Permission-denied 403 responses still fail immediately.

## Related work

A focused internal release-tooling repair. [GitHub's rate-limit guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api#handle-rate-limit-errors-appropriately) describes both wait headers. No public SDK, CLI, MCP, permission, or cross-component contract change; no RFC required.

## Compatibility and risk

- Existing retry limits, transient-error handling and successful response decoding remain intact.
- Only explicitly rate-limited 403s are retried; ordinary authorization errors are not delayed.
- A rate-limit retry can wait longer because it now follows the server-provided reset time. Revert the focused retry changes to roll back.

## Validation

- Two header-driven 403 cases fail on unchanged main. The permission-denied control passes there and after the repair.
- Release script tests: **13 passed**, all transport and clocks replaced in-process; no GitHub API calls or sleeps occur in these tests.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` pass.
- `bin/ci --base fb2b0df98ef42d8f9c4bbb4a2b447a3e9e3ed3f4`: **3 passed**, including the full `.github/scripts` suite (3m37s), after a fresh disk check met the 40 GB requirement. No threshold was overridden.
- `bin/ci --signoff`: set **local-ci=success** on current head `216a21662ce5d752bdc79762e6247853f9fd2227`.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused diff and current description.
- [x] No RFC required for internal tooling.
- [x] Test evidence recorded.
- [x] Conventional Commit title.
- [x] Authorship preserved; AI assistance: Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, tests, and this description.
- [x] N/A: no release-tracked product/version files changed.
- [x] `bin/ci` green and signed off on the current head.

title: fix(ci): compare release asset digests before reuse
body:
## Summary

- Problem: rerunning release finalization silently reuses an uploaded asset when its filename and size match, even if GitHub's SHA-256 digest proves its contents differ. Published-release verification also accepts that stale same-size asset.
- Change: compare available asset digests with a streamed hash of the local file in both paths. Drafts replace mismatches; published releases fail verification without mutation. Matching assets remain reusable.

## Related work

A focused internal release-tooling bug, found while exercising same-size rebuilds. The [GitHub release-assets API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/assets#list-release-assets) includes the `digest` field used here. No public SDK, CLI, MCP, permission, or cross-component contract changes, so no RFC is needed.

## Compatibility and risk

- Release artifacts are still selected by filename, uploaded state, and size. Legacy assets without digest metadata retain the existing size-only behavior; this is not a claim of content verification for such assets.
- Hashing streams local files in 1 MiB chunks. No additional network downloads are needed. Published releases are never rewritten by verification.
- Rollback: revert the focused helper and call-site changes.

## Validation

- Same-size stale draft and published assets fail the new tests on unchanged main. The matching-digest control passes.

title: embedded macOS demo exits before the host completes its probes
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### What happened

The embedded-host demo runner exits its wait loop when the host logs `grant the missing item(s)`, then immediately requires `DEMO COMPLETE: PASS`. The host emits that message before it starts the embedded daemon and continues its live permission, screenshot, window, and cursor probes, so the runner can report failure and exit while the app is still performing the demo.

### Expected

Wait for an explicit terminal result or bounded timeout, even when the initial permission message appears. Preserve actionable timeout/error reporting and do not alter TCC permissions.

### Evidence

At main `31185b10a5166880c450f2139c102b1726837f5a`, see `libs/cua-driver/rust/examples/embedded-host-macos/demo.sh` lines 72–82 and `ExampleAgentHarness.swift` lines 32–45. This is a source inspection; a new native run has not been performed.

### Submission checks

- searched open issues and pull requests
- contains no secrets or private evidence

title: permissions status ignores a selected custom daemon socket
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### What happened

The `permissions status` command uses `default_socket_path()` unconditionally. A caller selecting a custom daemon socket can therefore receive status for a different daemon. This is distinct from the PID-file identity issue #3514 and is especially confusing for embedded hosts.

### Expected

Status should query the socket the user selected, or explicitly reject unsupported socket selection rather than silently querying another daemon. The appropriate command-line contract and backward compatibility need review.

### Evidence

At main `31185b10a5166880c450f2139c102b1726837f5a`, inspect `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/cli.rs::run_permissions_status`. Historical reproduction reported `permissions status --json` querying the default socket. This report has not been freshly reproduced against current main.

### Submission checks

- searched issues and pull requests for permissions status and custom sockets
- contains no private evidence

title: macOS isolated browser discovery discards codesign failure details
body:
### Primary area

### What happened

The macOS isolated-browser discovery path verifies candidate signatures but discards `codesign` failure diagnostics. When no candidate passes, the user receives a generic vendor-signed-browser refusal even if an installed browser was found and a specific signature check failed.

title: SDK shutdown leaves registry runtime cleanup callbacks until final drop
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### What happened

A historical runtime-lifecycle audit found `DriverRuntime::shutdown` drains dispatch and recording but retains its registry, while registry runtime cleanup callbacks execute on drop. A host retaining an SDK driver after shutdown may therefore retain platform resources until the last owner is destroyed. The desired lifecycle contract and affected callbacks need verification before changing behavior.

### Expected

Shutdown either releases runtime-owned resources at the documented lifecycle boundary or explicitly documents which resources require final owner drop.

### Evidence

Historical report `9cbc12d3f64a`. On main `31185b10a5166880c450f2139c102b1726837f5a`, inspect `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-sdk/src/runtime.rs` shutdown and `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs` registry cleanup/drop. This is source-level evidence, not a reproduced resource leak or a proposed permission-boundary change.

### Submission checks

- searched issues and pull requests for SDK registry cleanup
- no private evidence included

title: feat(cua-driver): set_value on LibreOffice Calc cells through the Name Box
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `set_value` on a LibreOffice Calc cell wrote AXValue, which Calc accepts and ignores, then failed with `write_not_applied` and a message saying the cell cannot be edited in the background. Keys posted to Calc's window do edit cells while another app stays in front, so the tool refused a task it could do, and the message steered agents to stop or bring the window forward.
- What changed: on a Calc cell, `set_value` now goes to the cell the way a keyboard user does, with keys posted to the window. It presses Cmd+Shift+F5 and waits for the Name Box to take focus, then types the address key by key and presses Return. Once the Name Box shows the address it types the value, presses Return, and reads the cell back. Each step waits for the AX read-back before the next one. An empty value clears the cell with Forward Delete. `set_value` on the Name Box itself takes a cell address and goes there. A value with Tab or Return is refused, since one call fills one cell. The result carries `path:"keys"`, the `cell` address and `cell_value`. It is `confirmed` when the cell reads the value and `unverifiable` when Calc changed the entry (AutoCorrect, a number or date format, a formula) or the cell could not be read back.

The window is held as the app's key window by the existing key-scope route, so nothing is raised or activated and the pointer does not move. Only targets with the LibreOffice VCL toolkit loaded take this route. Other apps keep the AXValue write. The `write_not_applied` text for LibreOffice now names the keyboard route.

## Related work

Fixes #7186

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: `set_value` on a Calc cell now succeeds in the background instead of returning `write_not_applied`. The tool description and the macOS guide describe the route.
- Risk and rollback: the route moves Calc's cell selection to the target cell, as a keyboard user would. Revert restores the old error.

## Validation

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib calc_cell` and `set_value` (address parsing, cell detection, outcome wording, read-back of an empty cell, the action record), `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_schema_test`, and the `cua-driver` build.
- Manual or platform evidence: macOS 26 VM, LibreOffice Calc behind a frontmost sentinel app. `set_value` on cells sets text and time values and clears a cell. An AutoCorrect-capitalised entry reports `unverifiable` with the cell's text, and `set_value` on the Name Box moves to the address. Tab values and non-addresses are refused. The sentinel recorded no front change, key loss, raise or leaked input.
- Known gaps: Linux and Windows code is untouched and was not built here.

title: fix(cua-driver): report macOS 27 browser profile denials
body:
Salvaged from #4629

Fixes #4275

On macOS 27 an app without Full Disk Access or a per-app grant gets `EPERM` reading the Chrome and Edge profile folders, LaunchAgents included. Attaching through the daemon to an existing profile then refused with `could not read the browser's DevToolsActivePort file: Operation not permitted (os error 1)` and gave no reason. macOS browser adapter and the browsers guide. The `enable_javascript_apple_events` half of #4629 is dropped because main removed that page action in #7483. Windows and Linux adapters are untouched.

title: fix(cua-driver): say when a refused Catalyst menu item leaves its menu open
body:
Salvaged from #4620
Fixes #4619
Refs #7752

## Why

In a Mac Catalyst app, a background `click` on a pop-up menu item is refused `element_outside_target_window` and the menu is left open. The refusal only advises a fresh `get_window_state` snapshot, and following that advice gets the same refusal. The menu also swallows the next background click on the window, which reports success. This change keeps the refusal and makes it say the menu is still open and that the foreground route picks the item. Work by @Ed-Key in #4620, rebased onto current main, plus a test of the refusal path.

## What changed

- `ax/exact_target.rs`: `in_parentless_menu` returns true for an `AXMenuItem` whose `AXMenu` has no readable `AXParent`, which is the shape of a Catalyst pop-up's menu. A unit test covers the Catalyst shape and AppKit/application-menu negatives.
- `tools/mod.rs`: the decision now goes through `decide_with_open_menu`. When the element is unproven, it is such an item, and the app has a layer-101 menu window on screen, an `element_outside_target_window` refusal gets a sentence saying so, and `escalation.recommended` becomes `"foreground"`.
- New tests run `decide_with_open_menu`. They check the structured refusal, and check that it admits and refuses exactly what `decide_background_input` does for every action and element state.

## Scope

Covers refusal text and advice only. Admission is unchanged: the new tests check every action refused before is still refused. Out of scope: proving these items belong to the window so background actions can run (the rest of #4619, tracked in #7752), and submenus of such menus.

## Blast Radius

Only `element_outside_target_window` refusals on macOS. The extra AX reads and the WindowServer query run only when the element is already unproven, so admitted actions do no extra work.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks, run at the head: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets` with no warnings, `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` (767 passed), `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`, and `cargo build --release -p cua-driver`.
- Mutation check: each of these makes a new test fail. Dropping the open-menu guard, dropping the refusal-code guard, or dropping the `foreground` advice. Removing the production call makes clippy warn that `decide_with_open_menu` is never used.
- Did not run: a live Catalyst run here (no Catalyst pop-up fixture), so the positive case rests on the source PR's recorded runs on macOS 26.4. Linux and Windows checks could not run on this host.

title: test(agents): cover the missing Volume home that made a persistent agent fail with spawn ENOENT
body:
## What was wrong

#4624 reported `could not start the agent: spawn /home/cua/.cua/tools/pi/0.87.1/node_modules/pi-acp/dist/index.js ENOENT` from `cua agent tell`, and guessed the harness was started on the host.

It was not. A persistent agent's run has always started inside the Space: `Agents::spawn_run` (`libs/cua/crates/cua-agents/src/runs.rs`) launches `launch.sh` through the Space's cua-spacesd, and it already did at the time of the report. The runner inside the Space spawns the harness with Node's `child_process.spawn`, which reports a missing working folder as `spawn <program> ENOENT`. A persistent agent works in its home on the Cua Volume, and that folder is not there until the Volume shows it. So the message named the program even though the program was installed, which matches the report that the files existed and ran by hand.

#6174 fixed the cause: the runner makes the working folder before every start, and names the real cause when a start still fails. Running the runner as it was at the time of the report, with an installed harness script and a missing Volume home, reproduces the issue's message exactly. The current runner starts the harness. A maintainer also checked current main end to end in a local Space (comment on #4624) and saw no ENOENT.

## Change

This PR is test only. The existing test "a missing working folder is made again before the agent starts" ran `node -e 0` from an unrelated folder, so it did not exercise this report's setup. It now uses an installed harness script at `tools/pi-acp/dist/index.js` and a missing `volume/agents/<name>/work` home, and it asserts two things: the harness ran in that folder, and the run carries no ENOENT error.

## Test plan

- `node --test libs/cua/crates/cua-agents/runner/test/` passes.
- The test fails against the runner from before #6174, with `spawn .../pi-acp/dist/index.js ENOENT` (the issue's message). It also fails when only the runner's `mkdirSync(cfg.cwd)` line is removed.
- `cargo test -p cua-agents --test runner_node` and the scoped repository checks pass.
- Not run: the Linux Space end to end and the Windows lanes, which cannot run on the host used.

Fixes #4624

title: fix(cua-driver): send AXEnhancedUserInterface only to Chromium and Electron apps
body:
Salvaged from #4640

## Why

On macOS, one read-only `get_window_state` of a native app (TextEdit, Calculator, Stocks) turns on that app's `AXEnhancedUserInterface`, the legacy screen-reader flag, for the rest of the app's life. The Chromium opt-in falls back to that flag whenever `AXManualAccessibility` is unsupported, and native AppKit and Catalyst apps reject the modern attribute but accept the legacy one. This is @Ed-Key's fix from #4640, rebased onto current main.

## What changed

- `enable_chromium_accessibility` writes `AXEnhancedUserInterface` only when the app is Chromium-family by name or bundle id (`browser::platform::is_chromium`) or its bundle carries `Electron Framework.framework` (`apps::bundles_electron`). Other apps get a new `AccessibilityOptIn::NotNeeded` outcome.
- `NotNeeded` is cached per process lifetime as `Wait::NotNeeded`. Later walks skip it, and `flush_pending_web_updates` does not treat the app as a Chromium web process. This last part is new relative to #4640: main added the web-update flush after #4640 was written, and that flush keys off the same cache.

## Scope

macOS `platform-macos` accessibility enablement only. Chromium and Electron keep the current behaviour, including Chrome, which answers `AXManualAccessibility` as unsupported and relies on the legacy fallback. No public API, MCP schema or contract change.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS snapshot and background action runs this opt-in. Native apps stop being switched into screen-reader mode. The risk is an app that needs the legacy flag to build its tree but is neither on the Chromium name list nor bundles Electron Framework (for example a CEF app that also rejects `AXManualAccessibility`). Such an app would no longer get the flag.

## Verification

- #4640 reports a before/after run on a macOS 26.4 VM: TextEdit, Calculator and Stocks went from `AXEnhancedUserInterface` 0 to 1 after one `get_window_state` on main, and stayed at 0 on the branch. Chrome and the Electron fixture were unchanged.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and the em-dash check passed. The diff and its callers were reviewed. Unit tests cover the opt-in choice, Electron bundle detection, and the `NotNeeded` cache and flush behaviour.
- Not run for this rebase: the macOS build, unit tests and the live TextEdit probe. The review host is Linux and cannot build `platform-macos`, so the macOS CI lanes are the first build of the rebased code.

title: cua-driver: admit background actions on Mac Catalyst pop-up menu items (rest of #4619)
body:
Follow-up to #4619, part (b).

In a Mac Catalyst app, a `UIButton` pop-up (`showsMenuAsPrimaryAction`) opens its menu in its own WindowServer window. Its `AXMenuItem`s are listed in `get_window_state` of the app's window, but a background `click` on one is refused `element_outside_target_window`. The reason: `element_window_id` in `ax/exact_target.rs` cannot tie the item to the window. The item's `AXMenu` has no readable `AXParent`, neither has `AXWindow`, and `_AXUIElementGetWindow` fails on both. The window's root `AXGroup` does list the `AXMenu` among its children.

#7746 (salvaged from #4620) covers part (a) only: the refusal now says the menu is still open and recommends `delivery_mode: "foreground"`. Admission is unchanged.

Still open: prove that such an item belongs to the target window, for example with a bounded search of the window's own AX subtree for the parentless `AXMenu`, so that semantic AX actions on the item are admitted in the background.

The author of #4620 plans to send this as a follow-up PR.

title: cua-driver: decide how open #5389 relates to merged #5492 (macOS background click window-location stamp)
body:
### Summary

Open PR #5389 and merged PR #5492 both change the `CGEventSetWindowLocation` stamp that `chromium_click_route_plan` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/input/mouse.rs` puts on background left-clicks. Someone needs to decide how #5389 relates to what is on main now.

### What each change does

- #5492 (merged 4 Nov, `b743c33a4d`) stamps the window-local point on macOS 27 and later, on both the SkyLight route and the public pid fallback. Releases before 27 keep the screen point. #7372 then did the same for background drags.
- #5389 (open, head `cf519a16d4`, conflicts with main) stamps the window-local point on the public pid route on every macOS release, and leaves the SkyLight stamp on the screen point. It also adds a transport split: targets matching `is_chromium_identity` keep SkyLight, and every other target moves to the public pid route.

### Overlap

1. Same lines. Both rewrite the `public_window_location` fields of the route plan and the stamp in `click_at_xy_chromium`, so #5389 can't merge as it is. It has to be rebuilt on top of #5492.
2. Different version rule. #5492 gates on macOS 27. #5389's measurements were taken on macOS 26, and it reports that on 26 a plain AppKit `NSButton` received background clicks only with the public route plus the window-local stamp, and dropped them on SkyLight with the screen point. If that holds, it is evidence about the open question on #4631: whether releases before 27 also miss custom-drawn views when the window is away from the screen origin.
3. The transport split is not part of #5492. The open review on #5389 already asks for it to be dropped: `is_chromium_identity` matches only a handful of browser names, so Arc, Electron apps, Safari and iPhone Mirroring would move off SkyLight.

### To decide

- Whether anything in #5389 is still needed once #5492 is on main. The candidate is the window-local stamp on releases before 27, which depends on the macOS 26 answer for #4631.
- If it is needed, whether to salvage only that part, without the transport split.

Related: #4631, #4632, #5492, #7372, #5389.

title: fix(cua-driver): release a background Command chord's base key without Command
body:
## Why

A Mac Catalyst app in the background repeats a `UIKeyCommand` from a single background Command chord, because it drops a PID-routed key-up that carries the Command flag and UIKit treats the key as still held. This salvages @Ed-Key's fix from #4642, rebased onto current main, with their authorship preserved.

## What changed

- The background PID-routed `keyboard::press_key` (background `hotkey` and `press_key`) sends its key-up without Command. The key-down keeps every modifier, so menus and key commands still match it. Shift, Option, Control and fn stay on both halves.
- The pair of events comes from a small `pid_key_press` function with a unit test.
- Rebase only: main's `press_key` now resolves keys through `target_key_code` (#6659), and the salvage keeps that call for both the plain key and the `+` mapping.

## Scope

macOS background keyboard path only. The foreground menu-shortcut helpers (`hotkey_no_auth`, `press_key_no_auth`) and the global HID paths are unchanged. Linux and Windows are untouched.

## Blast Radius

Every caller of `keyboard::press_key` on macOS. A background consumer that reads Command from the key-up rather than the key-down would see it missing. In #4642 the author checked AppKit text handling (background cmd+shift+right in TextEdit), and it behaved the same before and after.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks that run on Linux passed: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p platform-macos` (this does not compile the macOS-only keyboard module), plus `cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` for `cua-driver-core`.
- The diff review found the rebase changes only the key-up flags against main.
- Not run here: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` and the Catalyst probe repro, which need macOS. #4642 describes the probe and its before/after results.

Salvaged from #4642

title: fix(cua-driver): run invoke_menu on a macOS window on another Space without raising it
body:
## Summary

- Problem: on macOS, `invoke_menu` on a window on another Space failed with `menu_path_unavailable`, "target accessibility window is unavailable", even though `get_window_state` resolves that window through the off-Space probe. When the window's app was frontmost, `invoke_menu` took the foreground route. That route looks the window up in `AXWindows`, which leaves out windows on other Spaces, and raising the window would switch the user's Space anyway.
- What changed:
  - A window that WindowServer places on another Space now takes the background route even when its app is frontmost. That route resolves the menu path without opening a menu or raising the window.
  - The background route reads the window's document through `copy_ax_windows_including`, the lookup `get_window_state` uses, so a background Save on an off-Space document window is still checked on disk.
  - Sometimes a sibling window on the current Space holds the app's menu context. The existing guard still refuses then with `window_not_key`, because dispatching would act on the sibling. The refusal now says the window is on another Space and points at `bring_to_front`. It no longer recommends `foreground`, which takes the same route for that window.
- `set_window_frame`, the other half of the issue, was fixed by #4636.

## Related work

Fixes #4635

RFC: not required. No schema, CLI or MCP change.

## Compatibility and risk

- macOS only. Windows on the current Space take the same routes as before. When Space membership can't be read, the old route is kept.
- Risk and rollback: low. Revert to roll back.

risk: standard

## Validation

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib`, `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`.
- New tests: `a_window_on_another_space_takes_the_background_route` (route table for app-in-front and Space membership) and `an_unbound_off_space_window_is_refused_with_the_space_named`.
- Not run: the issue's live repro (a TextEdit window on another Space) and the macOS Lume E2E. The test guest couldn't start on the test host, and the harness can't put a window on another Space yet. Linux and Windows checks don't apply to this macOS-only file.

title: fix(cua-driver): count a macOS AXOpen that replaced its own element
body:
Salvaged from #4641

Fixes #3835

## Why

Finder's AXOpen on a folder icon navigates the window, which destroys the icon it ran on, and the call then returns -25205. `click` with `action: "open"` and `double_click` by element token report that as a failure, so the agent retries or falls back to pixels. In the foreground, `double_click` also fires a pixel double-click where the icon used to be. @Ed-Key found and fixed this in #4641. This PR carries their commit (authorship kept, cherry-picked with `-x`) onto current main, where `perform_ax_click` now returns `AxClickOutcome` instead of a tuple.

## What changed

- For an advertised AXOpen, the driver reads the element's window title before the action. If the action returns -25205, it polls for up to 800 ms. When the element no longer exists and the window title has changed, it reports the open as performed, names the AX error and both titles, and tells the caller to take a fresh snapshot.
- Both `click` (`action: "open"`) and `double_click`'s AXOpen route use the check. In `double_click` it runs before the background refusal and the foreground pixel fallback.
- The only change from #4641 is porting `click`'s early return to `AxClickOutcome` (not verified, no page probe). It projects as `effect: "unverifiable"`.

## Scope

macOS `platform-macos` only. Every other case keeps today's error: other error codes (a stale handle's -25202 included), an AXOpen the element does not advertise, an element that still exists, an unchanged title, or no title readable before the action. AXPress actions that navigate and destroy their own button are out of scope.

## Tradeoffs

A false success needs the element to vanish and its window title to change for some other reason inside the same 800 ms. The result is reported as unverifiable, never confirmed, so a caller still checks with a snapshot.

## Blast Radius

Only macOS AXOpen through `click` and `double_click`. An advertised AXOpen that returns -25205 and leaves its element in place now waits up to 800 ms longer before it errors. Each advertised AXOpen also does one short window-title read before the action.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, the em-dash check and the SPDX header check pass. The `platform-macos` crate does not build on Linux, so its compile and the unit test `an_erroring_open_counts_only_when_its_element_is_gone_and_the_window_changed` rely on this PR's macOS CI. On #4641's head that test passed in `Rust macOS unit`.
- #4641 has the before and after Finder reproduction (icon view, background and foreground `double_click`, `click` with `action: "open"`, and controls). It was not rerun for this salvage.

title: cua-driver (macOS): a foreground Command hotkey repeats a Mac Catalyst key command
body:
## What happens

On macOS, one `hotkey` with Command sent with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` to a Mac Catalyst app fires the app's `UIKeyCommand` over and over. The key command keeps firing until some other key event reaches the app.

This is the same symptom #4642 (salvaged as #7755) fixes on the background PID-routed path. That fix leaves the foreground menu-shortcut helpers alone: `hotkey_no_auth` and `press_key_no_auth` in `platform-macos/src/input/keyboard.rs`. They still post the key-up with the same modifier flags as the key-down.

## Evidence

From the measurements in #4642, taken with a Catalyst probe app that registers a cmd+shift+[ `UIKeyCommand`:

| Path | Firings in 3 s from one call | Key-up flags |
|---|---|---|
| Foreground cmd+shift+[, main | 125-126, 3 of 3 | cmd+shift |
| Foreground cmd+shift+[, #4642 branch | 124-125, 3 of 3 | cmd+shift |
| Background cmd+shift+[, #4642 branch | 1, 3 of 3 | shift |

The author lists the foreground rung as a known gap in #4642 and offered to follow up separately.

## Why it was left out

The foreground rung exists so AppKit `NSMenu` key equivalents dispatch: it posts without the auth envelope, so the events go through `IOHIDPostEvent`. Removing Command from its key-up needs its own check that AppKit menu key equivalents still fire.

## Done when

- One foreground Command chord to a Catalyst app fires its key command once.
- AppKit menu key equivalents sent through `hotkey_no_auth` still dispatch, for example in TextEdit.
- A unit test covers the foreground key-down/key-up pair, like `pid_key_press` does for the background path in #7755.

title: fix(cua-driver): capture the main window when an action closes its target window
body:
## Root cause

The release gate for cua-driver-rs-v0.49.12 failed twice on `macos-appkit-save-sheet-press-key-ax-foreground`, turn 4: `after.png` and `screenshot.png` missing (`capture_failed`). The case was added in #7724. Its last step sends Escape aimed at the save sheet's own window id. The sheet closes, so the post-action capture of that exact window id has nothing to photograph, and the macOS recording hook returned no image. The case itself passed; only the `cua-e2e-report` evidence validator rejected the run.

## Fix

In the macOS screenshot hook, when the targeted window id can no longer be captured and a pid is known, capture the app's main window instead. The after-image now shows the real post-dismissal state (the parent window with the sheet gone).

## Why this is not a weakened gate

The validator is unchanged and still requires turn-N before/after screenshots for every case. No case declaration was edited and no exemption was added. The evidence is real and stronger (what the user would see after the action), instead of absent.

## Release note

A re-run of the 0.49.12 tag cannot pick this up (old workflow and tagged code). The fix ships in 0.49.13 via release-please. 0.49.12 stays a draft.

Verification: `bin/ci --quick` green locally; the macOS hosted E2E lane runs in CI.
