title: fix(cua-driver): keep a macOS menu command's window key within its app
body:
Salvaged from #4651

## Why

On macOS, `invoke_menu` File > Save on a TextEdit document that is not the key window reports success but saves the other document. The tool makes the requested window key, presses the item, then re-keys the window that was key before the call, even when that window belongs to the same app. AppKit runs some menu actions after the press returns, against whichever window is key at that moment, so the restore retargets them. This salvages @Ed-Key's fix from https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4651 onto current main, with their authorship preserved. Credit for the diagnosis, the fix and the TextEdit evidence goes to them.

## What changed

- Once the command was dispatched, the requested window stays key within its own app. When another application was in front before the call, it is still brought back. When the path is refused, the sibling window is still put back.
- The decision is a small `restores_prior_window` function with a unit test.
- Rebase only: main moved code around the restore block, so the cherry-pick conflicted. The commit's hunks are byte-identical to #4651's.

## Scope

The macOS foreground `invoke_menu` path only. The background menu path, Linux and Windows are untouched. No schema, contract or result text change.

## Blast Radius

Callers of macOS `invoke_menu` on an app that is already in front. After a dispatched command, the requested window now stays key instead of the sibling that was key before the call. A caller that relied on the sibling coming back now finds the requested window key. For deferred commands, that restore is what broke them.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks that run on Linux passed: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, the no-em-dash check and `bin/ci --quick`.
- #4651's head, which carries the same change, passed `CI: Rust macOS unit`, which runs the new unit test.
- Not run here: the macOS TextEdit repro and the Lume E2E matrix, because no macOS guest was available. #4651 gives the repro and before/after results on a macOS 26.4 VM: note.txt is saved on disk in 3 of 3 runs, and the single-window, refused-path and Save As controls are unchanged.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep named macOS accessibility groups in the tree
body:
Salvaged from #4650

## Why

On macOS, `get_window_state` collapses every AXGroup and AXScrollArea before it reads the name. A named section disappears along with the anonymous layout wrappers around it. Two Save buttons in groups described "Profile" and "Billing" come out as two identical rows, and Stocks, Clock and Weather lose section names such as "Stock list" and "World clocks". This carries @Ed-Key's fix from #4650 onto current main, with one follow-up fix.

## What changed

- An AXGroup or AXScrollArea with a non-empty AXTitle or AXDescription keeps a row (`AXGroup (Billing)`) and indents its children. Unnamed ones collapse as before. A kept group reads no actions, so it gets no `element_index`, and later indexes do not shift (@Ed-Key's commit, unchanged).
- Merged main: the group's name now comes from main's single batched node attribute read, so a kept group costs no extra AX round trip.
- `max_depth` is now counted on a walk depth that kept named groups do not increase, kept separate from the rendered indent. Without this, a control at the depth limit under a named group dropped out of the elements and shifted every later index.

## Scope

Only the macOS AX tree walker (`platform-macos/src/ax/tree.rs`). Addressability for other roles, the browser page reader and other platforms are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

`tree_markdown` from macOS `get_window_state` gains one unindexed line for each named section, and `AXNode.depth` goes one level deeper under it. A client that parses the tree by indentation sees the extra level. The structured element list, the indexes and the elements admitted under `max_depth` are unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` all pass. The new unit tests cover the collapse decision and the depth budget under a kept group.
- Dismissed review finding: there is no traversal-level test of a named group at the `max_depth` boundary. `walk_element` reads only live AX elements and the crate has no fake-AX seam, so that test needs a real window.
- Not run: the macOS Lume end-to-end lane (blocked by host disk before a VM started). Linux and Windows are untouched and were not run. The before/after trees and the clip on #4650 show the rendered change on a fixture and on stock apps.

title: fix(cua-driver): report native Windows diagnostics
body:
Salvaged from #4653

Refs #3895

## Why

On Windows, `cua-driver diagnose` prints the macOS report: codesign, TCC probes, `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`, LaunchAgents and the TCC database. It also reports "daemon unavailable" even when `cua-driver status` shows the daemon running. This is the "Additional defect" in #3895. @AyinLee987's #4653 swaps that report for the native Windows doctor probes. Since it was written, `doctor::run` has gained a `fix: bool` argument on main, so the PR no longer compiles for Windows. This PR carries their commit unchanged, plus a one-line fix.

## What changed

- On Windows, `diagnose` prints the running-process section, a `## daemon endpoint` section and `## Windows diagnostics` from `doctor::run(false)`. The endpoint section gives the named pipe path and whether a pipe instance is available. An unavailable pipe is reported as "absent, busy, or inaccessible", not as a stopped daemon.
- The macOS-only section builders are compiled out on Windows. The macOS and Linux report is unchanged.
- A unit test checks that the Windows report keeps the probe status lines, shows both pipe states, and contains no macOS-only text.

## Scope

This covers the `diagnose` output on Windows. The UIA health-probe timeout that is the main subject of #3895 is not fixed here, so this PR does not close that issue.

## Blast Radius

Only `cua-driver diagnose`, and only on Windows. It runs the same read-only probes that `cua-driver doctor` already runs, with `fix` off.

## Verification

- Windows cross-target `cargo xwin check` and `cargo xwin clippy -D warnings` pass on this branch. The original #4653 head merged with main fails the same check with E0061 at the `doctor::run()` call.
- On Linux, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver --all-targets -D warnings` and the new test `windows_diagnose_preserves_native_probes_and_pipe_uncertainty` pass. `cua-driver diagnose` still prints the same six sections.
- We have not run `diagnose` on a real Windows desktop. The author reports a native Windows run in #4653. macOS runtime checks did not run either.

Thanks to @AyinLee987 for the original change.

title: feat(cua-driver): put each tool description's first sentence on its own line
body:
## Why

Clients that load tools on demand show one line per tool when they search, and that line is the description's first line. For most Cua Driver tools the first line is a whole paragraph, so every search result repeats long text the agent does not need to pick a tool. Putting the first sentence on its own line makes that summary one sentence.

## What changed

- `ToolDef::to_list_entry` puts each tool description's first sentence on its own line (`lead_on_own_line`). It replaces the one space after that sentence with a newline and changes nothing else; periods inside code spans, brackets and after "e.g." do not end the sentence.
- Regenerated the MCP reference pages and the macOS, Linux and Windows registry snapshots.

## Scope

Tool descriptions in `tools/list` (direct server, proxy and daemon all use this path). Parameter schemas, tool names, results and behaviour are unchanged. `cua-driver list-tools` prints the same summaries as before.

## Blast Radius

Agents that read whole descriptions see the same words with one line break. Tests that compare a live description with its contract now compare against the same transform.

## Verification

- With newlines read as spaces, every `tools/list` description from a release build equals main's, with at most one added line break per tool. `list-tools` output is identical.
- The scoped repository checks pass: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`, the `cua-driver` schema, handshake and guide integration tests, clippy, the contract `--check`, the Cua Driver docs `--check` and `bin/ci --quick`. The new unit test fails when the split is disabled.
- Not run here: Linux and Windows native builds (CI covers them). No desktop lane was needed because no input or capture path changed.

title: feat(cua-driver): shorter shared parameter descriptions
body:
## Why

The `session`, `post_action_wait`, `element_token` and generic `delivery_mode` parameters repeat on most action tools, so an agent pays for their descriptions on every tool it loads, every turn. Several were a paragraph long, and `session` had a dozen slightly different wordings.

## What changed

- One-sentence descriptions for those shared parameters, in their shared fragments. `session` keeps the guidance the schema gate requires: prefer a short public label for multi-call work and repeat it on every call that accepts it.
- Platform tools that typed their own `session` schema now use `tool_schema::session_schema()`. The `target` object keeps its description; its `kind`, `pid`, `window_id` and `display_id` fields rely on their names and enum.
- Regenerated the contract manifest, the TypeScript UniFFI binding comments, the MCP reference and the registry snapshots.

## Scope

Parameter descriptions only. Every input schema keeps the same properties, types, enums, patterns and required lists, and validation is unchanged. Tool descriptions are untouched.

## Blast Radius

Agents and SDK users read shorter parameter docs. Omitting `session` still uses the implicit lifecycle session; the skill and SDK examples keep saying so.

## Verification

- A live `tools/list` from a release build matches main's with every `description` removed, for every tool, and the top-level tool descriptions are identical.
- The scoped repository checks pass: `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract -p cua-driver-core`, the `cua-driver` schema and protocol integration tests, clippy, contract-gen `--check`, UniFFI bindings `--check`, the Cua Driver docs `--check` and `bin/ci --quick`. Dropping the "repeat it on every call" guidance fails the contract and core tests.
- Not run here: Linux and Windows native builds (CI covers them). No desktop lane was needed because no input or capture path changed.

title: fix(cua-driver): pass max_image_dimension in the Python SDK guide example
body:
## Why

The Python example in the Cua Driver "Use the SDK" guide builds `GetWindowStateInput(...)` without `max_image_dimension`. The generated Python constructors are keyword-only, and a field with no UniFFI default is required even when its type is `Optional`, so the example raises `TypeError` before it reaches the driver. The Python package README had the same bug: `StartSessionInput(...)` without `cursor_motion`. Nothing caught either one because driver examples are `skip="no-runner"`.

## What changed

- The guide passes `max_image_dimension=None` and the README passes `cursor_motion=None`. The other arguments are unchanged, so the default capture limits stay as written.
- New `tests/e2e/cua-sdk/docs/test_driver_constructors.py` (stdlib only). It reads every Python fence that imports from `cua_driver` in `docs/content/docs` and `libs/cua-driver`, and checks each constructor call of an imported name against `__init__` in the generated `_native_contract.py`. It reports missing required fields, unknown keywords, extra positionals and arguments given twice, and it does not load the native library.
- `ci-check-docs-links.yml` also runs when `_native_contract.py` changes, so a PR that adds a required field fails until the examples are updated.

## Scope

Python docs and README examples that construct `cua_driver` records. TypeScript examples are unaffected because their `.new({...})` factories take optional fields. Runtime driver behavior is not touched.

## Blast Radius

Docs, one README and a static test in the existing docs code-block job. The workflow change only adds a trigger path. A future binding change that adds a required field now has to update the examples in the same PR, which is the intent.

## Verification

- The new test fails on the docs as they were, naming `use-the-sdk.mdx` `GetWindowStateInput` missing `max_image_dimension` and `libs/cua-driver/python/README.md` `StartSessionInput` missing `cursor_motion`. It passes with the fixes, and the rest of the docs code-block suite stays green.
- Against the published `cua-driver` wheel from PyPI, the guide's and README's calls as printed on `main` raise `TypeError: ... missing 1 required keyword-only argument`, and as printed here they construct.
- The scoped repository checks pass. actionlint and the docs image doctor did not run because the tools were not installed.

Fixes #4683

title: fix(cua-agent-setup): bundle the cua-driver skill from its release source
body:
## Why

`cua agents setup` installs the `cua-driver` skill from `libs/cua/skills/cua-driver`, a hand-synced copy of `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver`. Nothing in CI ran `scripts/sync-skills.sh --check`, so the copy fell behind: it still says `version: 0.31.0`, and its macOS drag row gives a call shape the driver now refuses. This PR removes the copy. The build now bundles the skill folder that each cua-driver release versions, so the two can't drift apart.

Fixes #4685

## What changed

- `cua-agent-setup/build.rs` has a second `FILES` row that copies `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver` into the bundle as `skills/cua-driver`. `publish-crates.sh` vendors that row like the first, so the crates.io package carries it too. `libs/cua/skills/cua-driver` is deleted, and `sync-skills.sh` and the crate README now only cover `gui-automation`.
- A new unit test, `skills_with_a_canonical_source_install_it_byte_for_byte`, writes each bundled skill that has a canonical source (`cua-driver`, `gui-automation`) and compares the result's tree hash with that source. It runs in the existing `cua-agent-setup` test step of CI: cua SDK, so drift now fails CI.
- `cd-cua-spaces-build.yml` push paths include the driver skill folder. The Spaces Rust slice reads it at build time now, and `test_spaces_rust_slice_inputs.py` requires every build input to trigger that workflow.

## Scope

Covers the bundled `cua-driver` skill and its drift check. It doesn't change the skill text, `cua-driver skills install`, or the other bundled skills.

## Blast Radius

`cua agents setup`, the Spaces apps and cua-driver all link `cua-agent-setup`. After this change they install the current driver skill, not the stale one. Users who installed the old copy see it as outdated and get it refreshed on their next setup, the same as after any skill update. The Nix driver source set already includes all of `libs/cua-driver/rust`.

## Verification

- With the test added and the copy still present, `cargo test -p cua-agent-setup --lib skills::` fails: `the bundled cua-driver skill differs from .../libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver`. At the head, the full `cua-agent-setup` suite, clippy with `-D warnings`, fmt, `sync-skills.sh --check` (exit 0, `gui-automation` still checked) and the `.github/scripts` slice-input, e2e-scope and nix-path tests pass.
- I built `cua` and ran `cua agents setup --agents claude --skills-only --yes` under a temporary HOME. The installed `~/.claude/skills/cua-driver` is identical to `libs/cua-driver/rust/Skills/cua-driver` (`diff -r` is empty), and its MACOS.md drag row has `delivery_mode:"foreground"`. The installed `gui-automation` matches `skills/gui-automation`.
- `cargo check -p cua-driver` passes on Linux. I only read the vendored fallback in `build.rs` (each row falls back to `vendor/<name>`) and didn't build a packaged crate. The scoped repository checks ran on Linux only, so the macOS and Windows builds weren't run.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse an ended session on the daemon socket with session_ended
body:
## Why

When a call used a named session that `end_session` had already ended, the daemon socket refused it with a plain daemon error and no code. `cua-driver call --socket` printed bare text on stderr. `cua-driver mcp --socket` (the default `cua-driver mcp` route on macOS) wrapped that error as `{"code": "tool_invocation_failed", "exit_code": 1}`. The in-process runtime returns `session_ended` for the same call, which is what the docs promise. This change makes the socket's early guard return that same refusal.

## What changed

- `cua_driver_core::tool::session_ended_refusal` now builds the `session_ended` tool result, with the recovery text for a named or unnamed session. The in-process dispatch and the daemon socket both use it, so the two paths cannot drift apart.
- When `invoke_daemon_tool` sees an ended session, it returns that tool result in an ok daemon envelope with `isError: true`, the same way other tool-level refusals such as `stale_element_token` travel. `call --socket` prints the refusal JSON and still exits 1. The MCP proxy forwards `structuredContent.refusal.code` unchanged.
- The daemon socket tests now check the exact `session_ended` code and message instead of the substring `has ended`.

## Scope

Covers the daemon socket path, used by `call --socket`, `mcp --socket` and the SDK daemon backend. Leaves out #4724, where a live label owned by another transport is refused as `session_ended`. That needs its own refusal code.

## Blast Radius

Daemon clients that relied on a non-ok daemon response for this refusal now get an ok envelope with `isError: true`. The repository has no consumers of the old text or of the exit code for this case. The CLI exit status stays 1. The refusal message wording now matches the in-process runtime.

## Verification

- With only the test commit applied, the three daemon socket tests fail with the old `ok: false` plain error. With the fix applied, the scoped repository checks pass: the `cua-driver` binary tests, the `cua-driver-core` library tests and clippy with warnings denied on both crates.
- I ran the issue's reproduction on Linux against a private daemon with both the base and the fixed binary. On the base binary, `call --socket` prints plain text and `mcp --socket` returns `tool_invocation_failed`. On the fixed binary, both return `refusal.code` `session_ended`. `start_session` still revives the label, and a call on a live label is unaffected.
- The Linux X11 E2E smoke passes. macOS and Windows checks could not run on the Linux host. The changed code is shared and has no platform branches.

Fixes #4680

title: fix(cua-driver): keep a text row that repeats an unindexed group's name in the macOS tree
body:
## Failure

The Cua Driver 0.50.0 tag release gate failed twice (attempts 1 and 2 of run 43638250838), job "release gate / macOS hosted E2E / hosted shared lane". `shared_web_action_matrix_is_state_verified` panics with `shared-web: missing AX element "scroll-tall"` for the Tauri and WKWebView harness windows. Cases without evidence: `macos-tauri-scroll-ax-foreground`, `macos-tauri-scroll-px-foreground`, `macos-wkwebview-scroll-ax-foreground`, `macos-wkwebview-scroll-px-foreground`. The 0.49.12 tag run passed this lane. The main-branch gate on the release SHA reported success only because its macOS E2E jobs were skipped (`gate / macOS hosted E2E` and `(dispatched)` both skipped), so only the tag gate runs these cases.

## Root cause

#7762 ("keep named macOS accessibility groups in the tree"). The web harness scroll region is a named AXGroup `scroll-tall` containing a text child that also reads `scroll-tall`. Before #7762 the group collapsed, so the child `AXStaticText = "scroll-tall"` stayed in the tree with an element_index and the test found it by its visible label. Now the group is kept as a display row with no element_index, and the existing `prune_echo_text_rows` pass treats the child as an echo of the group's name and drops it from the rendered tree. Result: no row containing `scroll-tall` has an index (the failing tree shows `- AXGroup "scroll-tall"` and the child index jumping from 33 to 35).

#7751 (AXEnhancedUserInterface only for Chromium and Electron) is not the cause: the failing tree has the full WebKit DOM tree (counter, inputs, editor, drag targets), so web AX is enabled.

## Fix

`prune_echo_text_rows` now drops an echo text row only when its parent row is itself indexed (addressable). A display-only kept group has no index, so its echoing text row stays as the target. Unit test `echo_text_under_an_unindexed_group_is_kept_as_the_target` covers the shape; the existing echo-pruning tests still hold.

## How CI validates it

The unit tests in platform-macos run in the normal CI. The behaviour itself is only exercised by the release gate's macOS hosted shared lane, which runs the `macos-tauri-scroll-{ax,px}-foreground` and `macos-wkwebview-scroll-{ax,px}-foreground` cases; I did not run it here. It needs a tag gate run (or a dispatched macOS hosted E2E on this branch) after merge to confirm.

## Release note

After this merges, release-please will cut a new patch release (0.50.1). The 0.50.0 release stays a draft.

title: fix(cua-driver): exit 64 when a command gets an option it does not take
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `cua-driver` skipped any option it did not recognise and ran the command as if the option were absent. A typo gave a wrong result instead of an error. `status --sokcet <path>` checked the default socket. `stop --expected-pidd 1` stopped the daemon without the PID check. `serve --permision-mode bounded` started in standard mode.
- What changed: `parse_command` now checks every option against the options the selected command takes, and exits 64 (usage error, as the CLI reference documents) before it contacts, starts or stops a daemon. The accepted set comes from the command's `dump-docs` entry, the same table `--help` and the generated reference render. It is merged along the subcommand path and includes a default subcommand's options (`channel --json`). Only `UNLISTED_OPTIONS` is kept by hand: the embedded host's `--parent-liveness-stdio`, the removed `--experimental-pip*` flags that are still accepted, and the cursor flags direct `mcp` reads.

```
$ cua-driver stop --socket /tmp/d.sock --expected-pidd 1
cua-driver stop: unknown option '--expected-pidd'. Run `cua-driver stop --help` for the options it takes.
$ echo $?
64
```

Edge cases:
- A value option followed by another option is a usage error (`--socket --expected-pidd 1` no longer lets `--socket` swallow the typo). A value that starts with `-` is written `--option=-value`. Numbers and a lone `-` stay values.
- `-psn_<n>_<n>`, the process serial number macOS LaunchServices adds, is ignored.
- `extension`, `perception` and `cursor-theme` keep parsing their own options. An option placed before their name is rejected, because nothing reads it.

## Related work

Fixes #4698

RFC: not needed. This enforces the existing documented contract (exit 64 for an unknown argument) and adds no option.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a script that passes an option the command does not take now exits 64 instead of silently running. `status --json` is one example. Launcher argv built in this repo passes the check: the SDK embedded host, the Spaces supervisor, the daemon relaunch arguments and the testkit. A unit test pins each of those shapes.
- Risk and rollback: the check is one function called from `parse_command`. Reverting the PR restores the old behaviour.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `tests/unknown_option_cli_test.rs` starts a real daemon and covers the issue's cases. It fails at the base commit (`status --bogus-flag` exits 0) and passes here. `stop --expected-pidd` exits 64 and leaves the daemon running, and documented options still exit 0. New `cli::tests` unit cases cover the accepted launcher argv and the rejected shapes.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test -p cua-driver`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver --all-targets -D warnings` and `bin/ci --quick` pass on Linux. The issue's repro script now gives exit 64 for every misspelled-option step, while the controls are unchanged.
- Known gaps: macOS and Windows builds could not run on the Linux host; CI covers them. The parser has no platform-specific code.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`): `bin/ci --quick` is green. The heavy lanes ran as the cargo commands above and run again in CI.

title: [Bug]: cua-driver perception and cursor-theme exit 1 or 0 on an unknown option instead of 64
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Follow-up to #4698 and PR #7782. #7782 makes `parse_command` reject an option the selected command does not take, with exit 64. It leaves `extension`, `perception` and `cursor-theme` to parse their own options, and only rejects an option placed before their name. Two of those parsers still break the documented contract for an unknown option:

- `perception` rejects an unknown option, but with exit 1. The CLI reference says an unknown argument is a usage error with exit 64.
- `cursor-theme list` ignores an unknown option and exits 0 (`cursor-theme list --bogus`, `cursor-theme list --json --bogus`). That is the silent-accept behaviour #4698 describes. `cursor-theme --bogus`, an unknown subcommand, exits 1, not 64.

`extension` already exits 64 for an unknown option on `main` and on the #7782 head, and its usage errors are pinned by `cli_rejects_ambiguous_extension_arguments` in `tests/extension_manager_cli_test.rs`.

### Reproduction

Run from `libs/cua-driver/rust` after `cargo build -p cua-driver -p cursor-theme-cli` (the `cursor-theme` command needs the `cua-cursor-theme` sidecar next to `cua-driver`). No daemon is needed.

```bash
export HOME="$(mktemp -d)" CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=0 DO_NOT_TRACK=1
B=target/debug/cua-driver
for a in "extension status --bogus" \
         "perception --bogus" \
         "perception parse --bogus" \
         "perception parse --image a.png --capture c.json --json --bogus" \
         "cursor-theme --bogus" \
         "cursor-theme list --bogus" \
         "cursor-theme list --json --bogus"; do
  echo "== $a"; $B $a </dev/null 2>&1 | head -2; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
done
```

### Expected behavior

Each unknown option or subcommand is a usage error: exit 64 and a message naming it, as for every other command since #7782. Nothing is listed, parsed or run.

### Actual behavior

The same results on `main` (`80c5fdfc8d`) and on the #7782 head (`fa86a8d026`):

| Command | Exit | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `extension status --bogus` | 64 | `unknown extension option "--bogus"` (control) |
| `perception --bogus` | 1 | stdout `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"invalid_arguments","message":"usage: cua-driver perception parse --image <png> --capture <capture.json> --json",...}}` |
| `perception parse --bogus` | 1 | stdout `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"invalid_arguments","message":"unknown perception parse argument \"--bogus\"",...}}` |
| `perception parse --image a.png --capture c.json --json --bogus` | 1 | same `unknown perception parse argument` envelope |
| `cursor-theme --bogus` | 1 | ``cua-driver cursor-theme: unknown cursor-theme command `--bogus` `` plus usage |
| `cursor-theme list --bogus` | 0 | `cua.default`; the option is ignored |
| `cursor-theme list --json --bogus` | 0 | `["cua.default"]`; the option is ignored |

On `main` an option placed before the command name is also ignored (`--bogus extension list` and `--bogus cursor-theme list` exit 0). #7782 changes that case to exit 64.

### Environment

- `cua-driver` built from source with `cargo build -p cua-driver -p cursor-theme-cli` (debug profile), at `main` `80c5fdfc8d` and at the PR #7782 head `fa86a8d026`.
- macOS, arm64.

### Evidence

- Expected source: the `64` row in the "Exit codes" table of `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/cli/index.mdx`: "Usage error: an unknown or missing subcommand or argument, or conflicting flags".
- Failure sources:
  - `perception_cli::run` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/perception_cli.rs` sends every `CliError` to `std::process::exit(1)`, including the `invalid_arguments` errors from `parse_args`.
  - `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cursor-theme-cli/src/main.rs` exits 1 on any error. Its `list` arm checks only whether `--json` is present and never rejects other arguments.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: none needed for `extension`. For `perception`, callers can read `error.code == "invalid_arguments"` from the JSON envelope instead of the exit code. For `cursor-theme`, check options against `cua-driver cursor-theme <command> --help` before running.

Restoration check: rerun the script. Every `perception` and `cursor-theme` line exits 64. The `extension status --bogus` control still exits 64. Documented invocations such as `cursor-theme list --json` and a valid `perception parse --image <png> --capture <capture.json> --json` keep their current exit codes.

Related: #4698 (the top-level parser accepts unknown options), #7782 (the fix that leaves these three commands to their own parsers).

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse macOS clicks when the observed control has changed
body:
## Why

On macOS, `click` accepted an element token after the app renamed the control behind it. An agent that read a "Submit" button could press it after it had become "Changed Submit", and the snapshot store only proved the AX object was still alive. The fix records what the read showed for each token and refuses the click when the control no longer matches.

## What changed

- `AxSnapshot` stores an observed identity per token: role, trimmed title, trimmed description and identifier, normalised the way the tree prints them. `RetainedElement` carries it.
- `click` re-reads that identity before dispatch, and again inside each dispatch closure after cursor movement and activation: AX press, and all three `button: "middle"` pixel-fallback branches. A mismatch returns `stale_element_token` and sends no input. Value and frame changes do not invalidate a token.
- New AppKit E2E `snapshot_publication::harness_appkit_relabelled_cached_click_fails_closed`. It relabels the fixture button without a new read, expects the refusal with zero clicks, then reads again and clicks the renamed button once.

## Scope

macOS element-token clicks only. `right_click`, `double_click`, `set_value` and other platforms are unchanged. The two commits from #4677 keep their author. The third commit adapts them to current main: it places the check before the fast-path guard, covers the foreground-assisted middle-click branch that main added since, and treats a token with no recorded identity, or a null element, as stale.

## Blast Radius

A token now goes stale when its control's label or identifier changes, for example a Play button that turns into Pause. The agent gets the same `stale_element_token` refusal and recovery hint that a replaced snapshot already produces, and one fresh `get_window_state` recovers. Value-only changes such as form fields and sliders keep working.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks passed: rustfmt, clippy, unit tests for `platform-macos`, `cua-driver-e2e` and `cua-driver-sdk`, the Windows cross-check, generated reference and bindings. The `ax::snapshot` unit tests passed 6 of 6.
- Full macOS Lume matrix at this head: the new regression passes. The stale-token, pending-snapshot and every other AppKit and SwiftUI cell also pass.
- The same matrix at main plus only the new test and fixture fails the regression with `cached changed action ran: Performed AXPress on [1] AXButton "Changed action"`. That reproduces the bug.
- The shared-web scroll cells for Tauri and WKWebView (`missing AX element "scroll-tall"`) fail in both runs, so this diff did not cause them. No cell fails here that passes at main. Linux and Windows desktop lanes were not run.

Salvaged from #4677

Fixes #4696

title: fix(verify-cua-driver): prune old macOS Lume run evidence before the disk floor blocks runs
body:
## What happened

The macOS Lume verify lane's wrapper keeps every run under `~/.local/share/cua-lume-e2e/runs` and never removes anything. On the relay Mac mini on 2026-11-15 that store held 362 run dirs, 176 GB in total:

- `source.tar`: 66 GB across 185 runs. Each is a `git archive` of the run's SHA, so it can be rebuilt.
- `evidence.tar`: 54 GB.
- `evidence/`: 55 GB. 287 runs keep both the tar and its extracted dir, so most evidence is stored twice.
- 175 run dirs date from before 2026-11-07, some going back to 2026-09-07.

The doctor refuses a run when free disk is below `minimum_free_gib` (80). While #7789 was being verified, two verifier rounds were refused for low disk. They only went ahead after `source.tar` was deleted by hand from 174 finished runs older than 7 days. Free disk is now about 100 GiB, so a few more full-matrix runs will reach the floor again.

## Expected

Old runs are pruned on a policy instead of by hand when the floor blocks a run. For example:

- Keep `result.json` for every run.
- Drop `source.tar` once the run is collected, since it can be rebuilt from the SHA.
- Keep one copy of the evidence, not both `evidence.tar` and the extracted `evidence/`.
- Remove evidence for finished runs older than N days, except runs that a still-open PR or issue cites.
- Never touch the dir of a running or uncollected run (one that still holds `run.lock`, or has no `result.json`).

The "Blocked before a VM starts" note in `.cursor/skills/verify-cua-driver/macos-lume.md` should document the policy, or the command that applies it.

## Done when

- A collected run no longer keeps a `source.tar` or a second copy of its evidence.
- Finished runs past the retention age are pruned automatically, or by one documented command, and a running run is never pruned.
- `macos-lume.md` says what is kept and for how long.

Context: #7789 (two disk-floor refusals during its verification). Related: #3429 (nominating obsolete VMs and evidence at workflow completion), #7627 (another way the same runner gets blocked).

title: fix(cua-driver): accept --socket on permissions again (hosted macOS gate regression from #7782)
body:
## Failure

The Cua Driver 0.51.1 tag release gate failed in all four hosted macOS lanes (shared, capture, native, browser) during setup. After the TCC seed and `tccd_restarted: 1`, the script printed `hosted-macos-e2e: installed daemon did not report the seeded app-specific permissions` and exited 2. The 0.51.0 gate, about an hour earlier, passed the same lanes on the same runner image.

## Root cause

#7782 (in 0.51.1) made every command reject options its CLI docs entry does not list. `permissions` does not list `--socket`, but `scripts/ci/macos/run-hosted-rust-e2e.sh` polls the daemon with `cua-driver --socket S permissions status --json`. Each poll exited 64 with `unknown option '--socket'` (the failed run's `permissions.err` artifact shows exactly that), so the 60-try loop never saw a permissions report. The seeding itself was fine: the seed log matches the passing run. The status command ignores `--socket`, so this was a behaviour regression for users who pass it, not only a CI problem.

## Fix

Accept `--socket` (with a value) on `permissions` again, through the existing `UNLISTED_OPTIONS` table, and ignore it as before. The launcher-argv test now pins both argument orders the gate and users use.

No Rust build was run locally; `bin/ci --quick` passed, and the full release gate is dispatched on this branch to prove the macOS lanes.

## Release note

0.51.1 stays a draft. This fix ships in the next patch.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse macOS clicks on controls behind an attached sheet
body:
## Why

On macOS, `click` with an element token taken before an attached sheet opened still pressed the parent window's button behind the sheet. Element ownership maps a sheet's controls to the window it is attached to (#4392), so the stale parent token passed every existing check. `click` now refuses that token with `stale_element_token` and leaves the sheet's own controls usable.

Salvaged from #4678

Fixes #4697

## What changed

- `element_blocked_by_sheet` (`platform-macos/src/ax/exact_target.rs`) walks `AXParent` from the element. It reports a block when a window or sheet on the way has an `AXSheet` child that the element is not inside. A parentless menu or the application element ends the walk clear. An unreadable role, parent or child list counts as blocked, and a menu ends the walk clear only when it answers `AXParent` as absent. Window ownership stays with the existing exact-target gate.
- `click` runs this check before dispatch, and again inside the foreground and background dispatch closures for the AX path and the middle-click path. A sheet that opens during activation is still caught. The AX path checks once more right before `AXUIElementPerformAction`, after a background press makes the window key and after the menu wait, so a sheet the app opens on becoming key is caught too.
- The AppKit `SnapshotPublication` fixture can open a sheet. A new E2E test, `harness_appkit_cached_click_cannot_press_behind_sheet`, is registered in `scripts/ci/macos/appkit-cells.tsv` as cell `macos-appkit-cached-click-sheet-ax-foreground`. It covers refusal in both delivery modes, zero parent clicks, the sheet's Close button, the parent button after dismissal, and a foreground app-menu item.

## Scope

Covers macOS element clicks (left, right and middle). Pixel clicks, other tools and other platforms are unchanged. Finding every surface that blocks input, the broader work in #2589, stays open.

## Tradeoffs

The two commits from #4678 are cherry-picked with their author kept. The third commit drops #4678's comparison of the requested window id against the root window. That comparison refused a sheet control addressed by the sheet's own window id, and it refused background menu items. The gate added in #4392 already decides which window an element belongs to.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS element click now does one bounded `AXParent` walk with a child read at each window or sheet. A window without a sheet behaves as before. When the AX tree can't be read, the click is refused, not dispatched.

## Verification

- Scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with `-D warnings` for `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-e2e`, and `cargo test -p platform-macos` all pass. Unit tests cover the walk over a fake AX tree: a parent control behind a sheet, the sheet's own control, nested sheets, app and context menus, and unreadable or cyclic ancestry.
- macOS Lume full lane, after merging main (which brought the observed-identity guard from #7789 into the same files): passed, with no failing cells. The new sheet test passes. So do `harness_appkit_relabelled_cached_click_fails_closed`, `harness_appkit_save_sheet_controls_act_through_their_window`, `harness_appkit_foreground_key_reaches_an_attached_sheet`, `harness_appkit_pending_snapshot_cannot_retarget_token`, `harness_appkit_stale_element_token_fails_closed` and `harness_appkit_invoke_menu_live_path`.
- After merging main again (which brought in `retained_elements` and the AppKit cell manifest): CI at the head passes macOS clippy, `platform-macos` unit tests, hosted native and shared E2E, and `ci-gate`. The hosted `macos-appkit-cached-click-sheet-ax-foreground` cell passes, app-menu step included. A unit case covers a menu whose `AXParent` read fails, and it fails when the absence check is removed. The full Lume lane was not rerun at this head.
- The last check before the AX press has no E2E of its own: a fixture that opens a sheet when its window becomes key, while another app is frontmost, is not reliable on the hosted runner. Its build and the existing sheet cell rest on CI at the head.
- Not run: the new test against the unpatched driver (#4678 reports that it fails there), Linux and Windows platform crates, and the standalone-browser lane.

title: fix(cua-driver-core): advise only the retry that lifts each PARTIAL TREE cut
body:
## Why

`truncation_note` heads every partial `get_window_state` tree on macOS, Windows and Linux. It now pairs each truncation reason with the one retry that can lift that cut. Before this change, every reason except `node_budget` fell through to "retry with a larger timeout_ms". That advice cannot expand a Linux `huge_container`, and the issue reports agents looping on the timeout advice after a `max_elements` cut. The 0.34.0 build in the issue predates the `node_budget` branch, and nothing pinned that branch.

## What changed

- `truncation_note` maps each reason to a `(why, remedy)` pair. `node_budget` gets a larger `max_elements` or a narrower `query` / `max_depth`. `timeout` gets a larger `timeout_ms` or a narrower query. `app_unresponsive` and `app_lookup_timeout` get "retry in a moment or with a larger timeout_ms". `huge_container` gets a `max_elements` above the container's child count, or a pixel action inside it.
- A table test checks the exact remedy for each reason and that no remedy names a knob that cannot lift its cut. A second test builds the issue's case (20 nodes visited, 15 pending) through `WalkBudget` and checks the whole note.

## Scope

Covers the note text only. No schema or structured field changes. Leaves out the tool descriptions and the short `Tree truncated at max_elements=…` line in `window_state_view.rs`, which already named `max_elements`.

## Blast Radius

Every platform's partial-tree text, plus the Linux `degraded_reason` for an empty truncated tree. Only the advice wording changes, so clients that parse `truncation_reason` see no difference.

## Verification

- The test commit fails on the old `truncation_note` and passes after the fix. The rest of the `cua-driver-core` lib tests, the Linux truncation test and clippy pass.
- The Linux X11 verify lane passes. In a Linux X11 repro of the issue (a GTK fixture over MCP, `max_elements: 20`), the note ends "retry with a larger max_elements or narrow with query / max_depth."
- The macOS and Windows platform crates could not build on the Linux host. They call the same shared function.

Fixes #4720

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse page query_dom selectors the macOS AX fallback cannot apply
body:
## Why

On macOS, when `page` `query_dom` has no JavaScript or CDP route to a window (an Electron app without a debugging port, or a WKWebView/Tauri app), it reads the accessibility tree instead. That fallback treated every selector it could not map, such as `select#model` or `nav`, as `*`. The tool then returned every AX element of the window as a successful answer and gave no sign that the selector was ignored. It now refuses those selectors with an error that names the selector and says what to use instead.

## What changed

- `AxRoleFilter::from_css` replaces `css_selector_to_ax_roles`. It returns `Any` for `*` or an empty selector, the AX roles for a bare tag, and `None` for anything else. `AXPageReader::query` now takes the filter.
- `ax_query_fallback` refuses a `None` filter before it walks the tree: `css_selector '<sel>' was not applied: …`, and it points to `get_window_state` with `query` or to `browser_prepare`. If JavaScript failed first, `(JavaScript read failed first: …)` is still appended.
- The `page` tool description and `Skills/cua-driver/BROWSER.md` now document the refusal, and the generated Cua Driver reference (the macOS, Linux and Windows registry snapshots and `pointer-cursor-and-browser.mdx`) is regenerated to match.

## Scope

This covers only the macOS legacy `page` `query_dom` AX fallback. The Linux and Windows page backends already refuse unmapped selectors and are unchanged. So are `get_text` and the JavaScript/CDP routes, which still run the real selector.

## Tradeoffs

The issue allowed either a refusal or an approximate match by role. A role-only match on `select#model` would return every popup button, which is still the wrong answer to the query, so this PR refuses. Bare tags that map to a role still return filtered results.

## Blast Radius

A macOS client that sent a compound selector to a window with no DOM route used to get a full AX dump. It now gets `isError`. Bare tag selectors and `*` behave as before.

## Verification

- At main, `AXPageReader::query("select#model", …)` returned 3 of 3 rows in a fixture tree. At this head, `AxRoleFilter::from_css` returns `None` for `select#model`, `nav`, `div.menu`, `input[type=text]` and `a, button`, and `h1` returns only the heading (new unit tests in `ax_page_reader.rs`).
- New test `an_unmappable_selector_fails_the_ax_fallback_with_the_reason` in `tools/page.rs`.
- The scoped repository checks ran: the `ax_page_reader` tests standalone, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core page::`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core`, and `cargo fmt --check`. Neither the `platform-macos` crate build nor a live Electron repro could run on the Linux host, so the `tools/page.rs` test runs first in macOS CI.
- The Cua Driver reference generator ran natively on macOS and its `--check` passes. The description is shared from `cua-driver-core`, so the Linux and Windows snapshots carry the same line. Their native checks run in CI.

Fixes #4721

title: fix(cua-driver): drop the success glyph from unconfirmed action text
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: an action result reports `effect: "unverifiable"` in `structuredContent`, but its text still opens with `✅`. One example is `✅ Performed AXPress on [2] AXButton ""` from a macOS click, and another is `✅ Sent down scroll … via pixel wheel` from a pixel-wheel scroll. Clients that show the model only the text read that as a confirmed success.
- What changed: `publish_action_result` is the dispatch seam that projects every action-result tool into the public `ActionResult`. It now swaps a leading `✅` for words that match `effect`:
  - `unverifiable` → `Sent, effect not verified: …`
  - `suspected_noop` → `Sent, but probably had no effect: …`
  - `partial` → `Partly done: …`
  - `refused` → `Refused: …`
  
  A `confirmed` result keeps `✅`. `summary` mirrors the rewritten text. The seam covers every platform and the calls nested in `run_steps` and `run_script`. The text recorded for recording and replay is captured before this point, so it keeps the producer's original wording.
- Two e2e harness asserts (WPF drag, LibreOffice expand) checked `starts_with("✅")` as a stand-in for success. They now check `!is_error()`.
- `action-result-contract.md` documents the rule.

Fixes #4723

## Related work

#7421 (draft) proposes a larger rewrite with a verdict headline on every action result. This PR is the narrow fix for the glyph the issue reports and does not depend on #7421.
If #7421 lands first, it removes the glyph from the producers and this rewrite becomes a no-op, so nothing here needs to carry over.

RFC: none. No schema changes. Only the leading glyph of non-confirmed action text and `summary` changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible: an unconfirmed action's text no longer starts with `✅`. A client that parsed the glyph as success should read `effect`.
- Rollback: text only. A revert restores the old wording.

## Validation

- New unit tests in `cua-driver-core` cover `unverifiable`, `suspected_noop`, `partial` and `confirmed` through `publish_action_result`. The non-confirmed cases fail when the rewrite call is removed.
- The scoped repository checks run on Linux: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -D warnings`, the full `cua-driver-core`, `platform-linux` lib and `cua-driver` test suites, `cargo check -p cua-driver-e2e --tests`, and the Linux X11 driver verification lane. All passed.
- Skipped: the Linux Wayland lane could not start because the host has no AT-SPI bus launcher. macOS and Windows platform crates were not built, so they rely on CI. The macOS repros from the issue (Calculator click, pixel-wheel scroll) were not run on a Mac.

title: fix(cua-driver-core): keep each session's own snapshot of a shared window
body:
## Why

When two sessions shared one daemon, a `get_window_state` from session B on a window retired the element tokens session A had just read for that window. A's next click was refused with `stale_element_token`, even though the window had not changed. The snapshot store kept one current snapshot per `(pid, window)` and replaced it on any read, whatever the session. The `reads` map next to it was already keyed by `(session, pid, window)`.

## What changed

- Each snapshot now belongs to the session whose read published it. Publish, screenshot-only refresh, unscoped removal (`SnapshotStore::remove` now takes the session), zoom lookup and the per-pid LRU cap touch only the caller's own snapshots. A session's own re-read still retires its earlier tokens.
- A full `s<id>:<row>` token still resolves from any session, because snapshot ids are unique. A bare row number resolves against the caller's own read. Stale refusals list the caller's own current snapshots.
- The `get_window_state` descriptions on macOS and Windows and the skill pack (`SKILL.md`, `WINDOWS.md`) now say snapshots are per session.

## Scope

This covers the shared snapshot store in `cua-driver-core` and its `remove` call sites on macOS, Linux and Windows (the Windows one is the use-after-free repro test). Unchanged: screenshot frames were already per session, so pixel actions still never use another session's screenshot. Focus, keyboard input and application state remain shared between sessions. The generated Driver reference is regenerated in this PR. The macOS registry and pages come from a native dump. The Windows registry (`cua-driver-mcp-windows.json`) can't be dumped off Windows, so it is the native snapshot that CI's `Reference / cua-driver / windows` job published for the previous head. The only change in it is the reworded `get_window_state` description.

## Tradeoffs

The comment thread on #4722 proposed a smaller alternative: keep one snapshot per window and reword the refusal. That would still break any setup where two agents share a window, which is the case the reporters hit. So this PR changes the store's keying instead.

## Blast Radius

This affects every client that runs more than one session against one daemon. Those clients now keep their tokens where they used to get `stale_element_token`. A process can hold up to 8 snapshots per session instead of 8 in total, and each session's eviction is bounded by its own reads. Single-session use behaves as before.

## Verification

- The two-connection repro script from the issue thread, run against a source-built `cua-driver serve` on Linux X11. Base: `A's click refused after B's read: 10/10 stale_element_token`. Head: `0/10 stale_element_token; control (no read by B): 10/10 ok; button clicked 20 times in total`.
- The new store test `another_sessions_read_of_the_same_window_keeps_this_sessions_tokens` covers: B's read of the same window, B's screenshot refresh, B filling its LRU cap, and B's unscoped removal. None of these retire A's token. A's own re-read still does.
- The scoped repository checks passed: the `cua-driver-core`, `platform-linux` and `cua-driver-sdk` tests, clippy with `-D warnings`, rustfmt, and the Linux X11 and Wayland driver lanes (Electron AX click and its typed-SDK sibling). The macOS and Windows platform crates cannot be built on the Linux verification host, so their call-site and description changes were checked only by review on that host. On a macOS host, the `cua-driver-core` snapshot store tests and rustfmt passed, and the cua-driver reference check reported the generated reference up to date. The Windows test fix was checked by review and by CI's Windows jobs.

## RFC

This changes the MCP snapshot contract (`SKILL.md` rule 6 said separate sessions share snapshot caches), so it carries [RFC 4722: Session-scoped element snapshots](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/bf2ddbd192817a05197cdb26444b1bb86ffa89bf/docs/rfcs/4722-session-scoped-snapshots.md) (`docs/rfcs/4722-session-scoped-snapshots.md`). It covers the old and new behaviour across sessions, who is affected, compatibility and migration, and the alternatives considered.

Fixes #4722

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse a live label held by another transport with session_owned_by_other_transport
body:
## Why

When a named session was live on one connection, a call on that label from another connection was refused with code `session_ended`. The usual case is a label started over `cua-driver mcp` and then used from `cua-driver call`. The session had not ended, so the `session_ended` recovery (`start_session` with the same label) was refused as well. Agents then retried under new labels. This change gives that case its own refusal code.

## What changed

- `cua_driver_core::session::begin_session_dispatch` now returns a typed `DispatchRefusal` instead of a string. The owned-by-another-transport case carries the holder's `SessionTransport`.
- At the dispatch seam that case becomes refusal code `session_owned_by_other_transport`. The message names the label and the holder's transport (`mcp_stdio`, `cli`, ...), and the refusal also carries `owner_transport`. A new recovery hint tells the agent to make the call from the holding connection or to use a new label. The ended, cleanup-incomplete and ending refusals still return `session_ended` with the same messages.
- The sessions paragraph in "How Cua Driver works" documents the new code.

## Scope

This covers ordinary tool calls on a label that another live transport holds. It does not let a CLI call join a session held by an MCP connection. That would change the session model, and the issue thread names it as a separate, larger option. A `start_session` on such a label still returns `session_unavailable` as before.

## Blast Radius

Only clients that branched on `session_ended` for this case see a change. That code was wrong for it, because the recovery it pointed to always failed. The repository has no consumers of the old message for this case. The other refusal paths are unchanged, and the platform-linux Hyprland caller keeps its existing message text.

## Verification

- With only the test commit applied, the new daemon socket test fails with `{"code": "session_ended", "message": "session is not available to this transport"}`. With the fix it passes. The scoped repository checks pass: the `cua-driver-core` library and integration tests, the `cua-driver` binary tests, clippy with warnings denied on `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver` and `platform-linux`, and a test build of `cua-spacesd-server`, which also calls `begin_session_dispatch`.
- I ran the issue's reproduction on Linux against a private daemon. `cua-driver mcp --socket` started `ra-transport`, and while it was open `cua-driver call --socket … list_apps '{"session":"ra-transport"}'` ran. The base binary returned `session_ended`. The fixed binary returned `session_owned_by_other_transport` with `owner_transport: "mcp_stdio"`. After the MCP process closed, the same CLI call succeeded.
- The Linux X11 E2E smoke did not run (no staged release build or fixture on the host). The macOS and Windows checks could not run on the Linux host. The changed code is shared core code with no platform branches.

Fixes #4724

title: cua-driver: start_session on a label held by another transport returns generic session_unavailable
body:
When a named session is live on one transport (for example a `cua-driver mcp` connection) and another transport calls `start_session` with the same label, the refusal is the generic `session_unavailable` code with the message "session is not available to this transport".

#7811 gives ordinary tool calls on such a label their own refusal: `session_owned_by_other_transport`, with the holder's transport in `owner_transport` and a recovery hint (make the call from the holding connection, or use a new label). Its scope note leaves `start_session` unchanged, so the two refusals for the same situation still differ.

**Expected:** `start_session` on a label that another live transport holds returns `session_owned_by_other_transport` with the same `owner_transport` field and recovery hint as other tool calls.

**Repro**
1. Start a session `demo` over `cua-driver mcp` and keep the connection open.
2. From `cua-driver call`, run `start_session` with label `demo`.
3. The refusal is `session_unavailable` / "session is not available to this transport" rather than `session_owned_by_other_transport`.

Context: #7811, #4724.

title: fix(cua-driver): bind Electron apps by their runtime and name the isolated launch
body:
## Why

`get_browser_state` refused every Electron app whose executable name did not contain "electron" (Slack, Obsidian, VS Code) with `browser_route_unavailable: pid N is not a recognized browser process`. The bound route for Electron already existed (`embedded_single_page`, exact binding), but it only covered the test harness, which ships as `CuaTestHarness.Electron`. When an app had no DevTools endpoint, the refusal pointed at `existing_profile` setup, which cannot attach an Electron app.

## What changed

- `classify_browser` recognizes Electron by its runtime, not its name. On Linux and Windows that is a `resources/app.asar`, `resources/app/package.json` or `resources/default_app.asar` next to the executable (new `is_electron_app_layout`). On macOS it is the bundled Electron Framework (`ElectronJs::is_electron`). These apps classify as Chromium + `Electron` + `EmbeddedApplication`, so the existing exact-binding and revalidation rules apply unchanged.
- An Electron app without an endpoint now refuses `browser_requires_setup` with `detail.reason: embedded_application_endpoint_closed`. Its `detail.next_call` is `browser_prepare` with `allow_launch: true, profile: {mode: isolated_new}`, which launches a separate driver-owned copy on a fresh profile that then binds exact. The message says that attaching the user's own instance needs a restart with `--remote-debugging-port=0`. The recovery hint keeps the producer's `next_call` for `browser_requires_setup` instead of rebuilding the `existing_profile` call.
- `BROWSER.md` documents both Electron routes. It also says the typed tools do not return arbitrary DOM attributes.

## Scope

Covers binding an Electron app's own page via `get_browser_state` / `browser_prepare` on macOS, Linux and Windows. It does not add DOM attribute reads to the typed tools, and it does not touch the `page query_dom` AX fallback the issue calls a separate bug. The user's running instance is never relaunched or modified. Attaching to it still needs the app to have been started with a debugging port.

## Tradeoffs

The other option was to relaunch the user's own instance with a driver-owned endpoint, as the issue suggests. That restarts the user's app and loses its unsaved state, so this PR offers the isolated copy instead and leaves the restart to the user.

## Blast Radius

The change is limited to browser classification and one refusal. A process now counts as Electron only when the runtime's own files are present, and Chrome, Edge, Chromium and Brave have none of them, so their classification is unchanged. Electron apps that already bound (name contains "electron") take the same path as before.

## Verification

- Linux X11, real Electron 39 app renamed to `notes` with `resources/app/`: at base, `get_browser_state` refused `not a recognized browser process`. With this change, launched with `--remote-debugging-port=0`, it binds `exact` (`embedded_application`). Launched without the port, it refuses with the new `next_call`. Making that call over one MCP session launches a driver-owned copy, which binds `exact`, and the user's instance keeps running.
- The new unit tests (Electron layout detection, the refusal's `next_call`, and the hint keeping it) fail at base and pass here. The scoped repository checks pass: fmt, clippy, the core browser and recovery-hint tests, the Linux `browser_platform` tests, the skills tests, and the X11 verification lane (both Electron click cells delivered).
- The macOS and Windows platform crates could not be built on the Linux host. Their classification changes are covered by CI only.

Fixes #4726

title: fix(cua-driver): state zero-match get_window_state queries and match a|b alternatives
body:
## Why

A `get_window_state` `query` that matched no row came back as the header over an empty tree. Nothing in the text said zero rows matched, so agents repeated the query. Agents also write alternations like `"Build|Reload|plugin"`, and those were matched as one literal substring, so they never matched anything.

## What changed

- `|` in `query` now separates alternatives: a row is kept if it contains any of them (case-insensitive, trimmed, blank alternatives dropped). The three per-platform copies of `filter_tree` (macOS, Linux, Windows) are replaced by one in `cua_driver_core::element_query`. Apart from alternation, filtering works as before (matching rows plus their ancestor chain, with the original indices).
- A non-blank query that matches no row ends the tree text block with `0 of N elements match query "…".` plus a short hint. This happens in the shared view shaping, so it covers all three platforms, `full_output:true` included.
- The query schema descriptions, `Skills/cua-driver/WORKFLOW.md`, the cli-specs snapshots and the generated MCP reference page describe both behaviors.

## Scope

Covers the zero-match statement and `a|b` alternation from the issue. Menu-bar scoping of common words is #2242 and is not changed here. No other regex syntax is interpreted.

## Tradeoffs

Alternation was chosen over refusing `|`, because agents write it constantly and refusing would only add another round-trip. The cost is that a literal `|` in a label can no longer be searched as part of a longer query. A query made only of bars and spaces is still matched literally.

## Blast Radius

Changes `get_window_state` text output when a query matches nothing, and query matching when the query contains `|`. Structured content is unchanged: `filtered_element_count` and `returned_element_count` behave as before. The Linux and Windows walkers only switch to the shared function.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cua-driver-core` and `platform-macos` unit tests, clippy with `-D warnings`, rustfmt, and the cua-driver docs drift check. New unit tests cover alternation, the zero-match line (including after a walk note and with `full_output`), and that no line is added when rows match, when there is no query, or for capture-only reads.
- The macOS Lume full lane passed with 190 cells before main was merged in. That includes the AppKit `query_projection` cell, which now asserts that `btn-increment|btn-reset` returns both rows and that a no-match alternation prints the `elements match query` line.
- After merging main, the lane at the new head has one failure, `harness_appkit_counter_px_background` ("double_click must refuse another client's screenshot transform"). The same assertion fails on main alone, so it comes from main and not from this diff. #7831 is the open fix. The `query_projection` cell passed at the new head.
- Linux and Windows crates were not built or run on this host. CI covers them.

Fixes #4725

title: [Feature]: read-only DOM attribute/selector query on a bound browser tab
body:
### Problem

The typed browser tools can't read an arbitrary DOM attribute from a bound tab. `get_browser_state` (semantic snapshot) returns roles, names, text and refs, but not arbitrary element attributes such as `data-*` values, `class`, or which stylesheet `<link>` elements are loaded. The `browser_*` tools act on the page; none of them reads it.

The only other read path is the legacy `page` tool (`get_text`, `query_dom`). BROWSER.md says new workflows should not start with it, because it is less precise and does not keep exact window binding. Its JavaScript route was removed with the page mutations.

So an agent that needs DOM state to check its own work, like the "data attribute" and "which plugin CSS is loaded" examples in #4726, has no supported way to read it on an exactly bound tab.

### Context

#4726 asked for a DOM route to Electron apps. PR #7818 binds Electron apps through the typed browser tools, but the typed tools still return no arbitrary attributes, so this part of #4726 stays open after it lands.

### Desired outcome

A read-only query on an exactly bound tab: a CSS selector and a list of attribute names in, a bounded list of matching elements with those attribute values (and ideally refs that line up with the semantic snapshot) out. It should have the same binding, session and untrusted-content rules as `get_browser_state`, and no script execution. The tool shape, limits and authorization need their own design before implementation.

### Related

- #4726 (parent request)
- #7818 (Electron binding)
- #4721 (`page query_dom` on Electron ignores `css_selector`)

title: feat(cua-driver): add deepseek-harness to mcp-config and skills install
body:
## Why

DeepSeek Harness (DSH) users wire cua-driver up by hand, because `mcp-config` has no DSH client and the skill pack never lands where DSH looks for skills. This adds `--client deepseek-harness` and a DSH entry to the skill-install targets.

## What changed

- `cua-driver mcp-config --client deepseek-harness` prints a Cordis patch entry: one `insert` of a stdio `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row that runs `<driver> mcp`. A comment above it says to append it to `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` (every profile) or `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`.
- `mcp-config --client deepseek-harness` and `cua-driver skills install` link the skill pack into `~/.agents/skills` when `~/.dsh` exists. Telemetry gets a `deepseek_harness` client kind.
- The connect guide, the `mcp-config` reference text, the CLI spec and the post-install hints name the new client.

## Scope

Covers the two asks in the issue. It does not edit DSH's config files itself; like the other config-file clients, it prints the entry for the user to paste in.

## Tradeoffs

- **Skill location.** The issue suggests `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/skills`. DSH's built-in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` provider has no per-profile root. It scans `<project>/.dsh/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills`, `~/.dsh/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`. Linking into `~/.agents/skills` reuses the link Codex, Pi and Cursor already share. If the pack were also in `~/.dsh/skills`, DSH would log a duplicate-name warning.
- **No skill-filesystem entry.** DSH's base bundle already mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`. Inserting a second one under the default provider name fails registration, so the printed patch carries only the MCP client row.

## Blast Radius

The change only adds a new `--client` value and a new skill-install target that is gated on `~/.dsh`. Other clients' output and placement are unchanged, and their existing tests still pass.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass: the `mcp_config_skills_cli_test` integration tests, including a new test that parses the printed YAML and checks the row and the driver path, plus a placement row for DSH; the cua-driver skills and telemetry unit tests; clippy; fmt; the release-wiring tests; and the Linux X11 driver lane.
- Real DSH, `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.2.2-rc.3 from npm, with a throwaway home. The printed entry was saved as `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`. `dsh headless --dump-config` shows the `cua-driver` row. A `dsh headless` run recorded the `mcp__cua-driver__*` tools and a `cua-driver` skill-catalog entry in its session. The model turn itself stopped at the missing DeepSeek API key.
- Not run: macOS and Windows (no host for them here), so the DSH desktop app on macOS has not been tried.

Fixes #4727

title: fix(cua-driver-rs): probe cross-client screenshot refusal from a client that never read the window
body:
## What broke

The 0.51.6 release gate (CD run 43702337602) failed on three lanes with one shared cause:

- Linux: `harness_gtk3_left_click_px_background` and `_foreground`, `harness_gtk3_test.rs:1053`, "double_click must refuse another client's screenshot transform"
- Windows: `harness_wpf_left_click_px_background`, `harness_wpf_test.rs:801`
- macOS: `harness_appkit_counter_px_background`, `harness_appkit_test.rs:2603`, left `Null`, right `"screenshot_context_missing"`

0.51.5 passed. The only driver change in between is #7809 (snapshots are kept per session).

## Root cause

These tests read a window with the driver (small image), then let a second client on the same daemon read it at native size, and expected the driver's own pixel actions (`double_click`, `right_click`, `scroll`, `drag`, `from_zoom` clicks) to be refused, because the old store let the second read take over the window's single snapshot.

#7809 deliberately changed that: each session keeps its own snapshot, so a second client's read no longer retires the first client's frame or zoom. The driver's own `double_click` now correctly succeeds with its own transform, so the test assertion (error code `screenshot_context_missing`) saw no error. This is a test that encoded the old behaviour, not a product regression. The refusal still holds for what it was protecting: a client may not use a transform it did not read.

## Fix

In the three harnesses, run the refusal probes from a third client (`spawn_peer_unrecorded`) that has not read the window. It holds no frame and no zoom, so it gets the same `screenshot_context_missing` / `zoom_context_missing` codes, and the cross-client rule is still covered on every platform. The driver's own flow (re-read, then click) is unchanged. Test-only change; no product code touched.

Why complete: all three lanes use the same pattern and all three are updated (grep for `spawn_peer_unrecorded` finds no other users). The per-session semantics themselves are covered by the `snapshot_store` unit tests from #7809.

## Checks

- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: passed
- `cargo check -p cua-driver-e2e --tests`: compiles (macOS)
- Linux and Windows e2e lanes run in CI on this PR; the release gate is also dispatched on the branch.

title: fix(cua-driver): revive an idle-reaped named session on its owner's next call
body:
## Why

When the idle sweep (five minutes by default) reclaimed a named session, every later call with that label was refused with `session_ended` until the agent called `start_session`. Agents pause for longer than that all the time, for example while waiting on a user login or a permission grant. Many then picked a new label instead of recovering. #4283 already brought back the unnamed implicit session on its next call. This change does the same for named sessions, so only `end_session` makes a label refuse.

## What changed

- `cua-driver-core/src/session.rs`: an idle end now leaves every session dormant, named or unnamed. The owner transport's next session-requiring call starts a new episode on the same label. The `IdleRevival` enum, which kept named sessions on the `start_session`-only path, is gone, and `IDLE_ENDED_SESSIONS` is now a plain set.
- The tests that pinned the old named refusal now pin the new contract. Only an explicit `end_session` still refuses.
- Docs: the MCP tools reference (header and generated page) and the bundled `RUNTIME.md` skill now describe the revival and say that old snapshots and element tokens stay retired.

## Scope

This covers the first option in the issue. It does not add a configurable per-session idle TTL, and `get_session` still does not count as activity.

Unchanged:
- Cleanup from the idle end (snapshots, element tokens, grants, cursors) still runs, and a call waits on it (`CleanupIncomplete`) before the label comes back.
- Another transport cannot claim an idle-ended label.
- A late call from a closed transport stays refused.
- An idle end followed by `end_session` is terminal.

## Blast Radius

This changes behaviour on every platform, because the logic lives in the shared core crate. A named session that was reaped for idleness now comes back for its owner instead of refusing. Callers that already recover by calling `start_session` and retrying keep working. A client that treated the idle refusal as an "abandoned" signal will no longer see that refusal. Launch ownership already outlived idle ends (#6738), so a revived label still owns what it launched.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` passed: 1286 tests. The two new contract tests fail by assertion at the test-only commit, with the session logic as it is on main.
- `protocol_proxy_recovery_test` passed against a real daemon with a 1 s TTL, through a `cua-driver mcp --socket` proxy. The reaped `named-idle` label works on its next `get_config`, and after `end_session` its next call is refused with a message naming `start_session`.
- The issue's repro, run over MCP stdio against a daemon with a 1 s TTL: `start_session idle-a`, `list_windows`, 70 s idle, then `list_windows idle-a` returns `Found 0 windows`. After `end_session` it returns `session_ended`. The released 0.51.0 binary refuses the post-idle call with `session 'idle-a' has ended`.
- The scoped repository checks passed: `session_lifecycle`, the cua-driver adapter/serve unit tests, `cua-driver-sdk`, clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `pnpm docs:check:cua-driver`, and the Linux X11 verify lane. Not run on this host: macOS, Windows and Wayland.

Fixes #4728

title: ci: close fork pull requests that change CI workflow files
body:
## What changed for contributors

If someone outside the team opens a pull request from a fork that changes `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/`, it is closed automatically within about 10 minutes. The author gets one comment asking them to open an issue for the CI change instead.

## How it works

- `close-fork-workflow-prs.yml` runs every 10 minutes from the default branch. It can also be run by hand, with a dry-run option.
- `close_fork_workflow_prs.py` lists open pull requests through the API and closes one when all of these hold:
  - its head is in a fork, or the fork was deleted;
  - its author is not an owner, member or collaborator;
  - it has no `allow-workflow-change` label;
  - it was opened on or after 15 Nov 2026;
  - it adds, edits, deletes or renames a file under one of those two folders.
- Pull requests opened before 15 Nov 2026 are left for a person to review.

## Why a schedule and not a pull request trigger

- Fork runs from new contributors wait for approval. A `pull_request` trigger would not run until someone approved the very run we want to stop.
- `pull_request_target` is banned in this repo (see `test_no_pull_request_target.py`).
- The job checks out only the script, from the default branch. It reads pull requests as API data and never checks out or runs their code. Its only write permission is `pull-requests: write`, with no secrets and no `id-token`.

## Testing

- Unit tests are in `test_close_fork_workflow_prs.py`. They cover forks, deleted forks, trusted authors, the override label, renames, the cutoff, dry runs, the duplicate-comment guard, and the workflow's permissions and checkout.
- `bin/ci --quick` and actionlint pass.
- A dry run against the live repo would close 0 pull requests. Without the cutoff it would close 16 older ones.

title: feat(jev-use): stop bounded native no-progress loops
body:
Salvaged from #4734

Fixes #4374

## Why
A native `jev-use` run could spend its whole step budget on repeated `reobserve`, stale or refused recovery, or the same action with no effect. This carries @kvnloo's guard from #4734, which stops such a run early as `abstained` with `reason=no_progress`. It adds one fix: normal one-retry-per-step recovery on save-note no longer stops early.

## What changed
- Native Python and TypeScript runners check a `NoProgressGuard` before each step and abstain with `reason`, `pattern` and `streak` after three steps without app-owned progress (#4734, unchanged).
- On tasks with no intermediate progress score, only the first attempt at a candidate not tried since the last observed progress opens a fresh evidence window. Before this, a stale or refused first attempt at Save note inherited the set-note streak, so `stale set-note → set-note → stale save-note` abstained before the save retry. Alternating between candidates already tried stays bounded.
- Parity tests in both languages for both cases.

## Scope
Only `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use`. No Driver, MCP, provider or planner contract changes.

## Blast Radius
The guard only affects the native `jev-use` example runners. A guard that stops too early turns a run that would have verified into `abstained`. `max_steps` still bounds every run.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks for `jev-use` on Linux: Python unit suite, the mock choice and decision CLI lanes, and TypeScript typecheck passed. In the TypeScript tests, everything except `openjev_model.test.ts` passed. That file is unchanged and timed out on this host. The full `npm test` lane passed on #4734's head merged with main.
- The new tests fail against #4734's guard and pass with the fix, in both languages.
- Not run: the Linux desktop and macOS/Windows native harness lanes.
