title: cua-driver-bench: CDB-G04 never runs on Linux, browser window "did not appear" (Bench v2 Linux browser launch)
body:
## What happens

On the Bench v2 Linux lane (X11 session started by `launch/linux_session.sh`, foreground condition), CDB-G04 never reaches the agent. Every trial stops in setup with:

```
status: infra_error
infra_failure: harness_exception
RuntimeError: window of app browser did not appear
```

`cdb_adapter.py` `start_apps()` raises it when `run_bench.place_window()` finds no window whose title contains "Morrowglass Archive" within its 90 s wait. The runner retries, then excludes the trial (`excluded_reason: infra_failure:harness_exception`) with no tool calls. So the Linux lane has never scored CDB-G04, and the task is missing from every Linux comparison. On macOS the same harness runs and scores CDB-G04.

## Evidence

- Seen on every cua-driver release benched so far on Linux (0.49.4, 0.49.11, 0.51.0) and on every trial, at harness commits 31185b10a5 and 9c50780301. The driver build makes no difference.
- Host: Debian 13 (trixie) arm64, Chromium 156 (`/usr/bin/chromium`, exposed to the launch descriptor as `google-chrome`), with `gnome-keyring` installed.
- The other CDB-G04 apps start. The archive site logs `Morrowglass Archive listening on http://127.0.0.1:4184/` and passes its `ready.http` check.
- The browser process starts and opens a window. The failure screenshot shows:
  - the Chromium window at `127.0.0.1:4184` with the tab still on **"Loading..."**, so the window title never contains "Morrowglass Archive";
  - a **"Choose password for new keyring"** dialog ("An application wants to create a new keyring called 'Default Keyring'") on top of the desktop;
  - the Electron app windows not yet painted.
- `app-browser.log` ends with Chromium errors: a missing `org.freedesktop.UPower` service, `ContextResult::kTransientFailure: Failed to send GpuControl.CreateCommandBuffer`, and `Failed to send GetTerminationStatus message to zygote`.

## Likely cause (not confirmed)

`taskpack/tasks/shared/cdb-s04/platform/launch.linux.json` starts the browser with a fresh `--user-data-dir` and no password-store flag. On a desktop where `gnome-keyring` is installed, Chromium on Linux asks to create a keyring for a new profile, and the prompt blocks the session. The page, and with it the title the harness waits for, does not finish loading in time. The GPU-process errors may add to the slow first load. The macOS and Windows descriptors use the same flags, but neither platform has this keyring prompt.

## Fix wanted (Bench v2 Linux browser launch)

- Launch the Linux browser so that it cannot prompt: for example `--password-store=basic`, plus `--disable-gpu` or `--use-gl=swiftshader` if the GPU errors turn out to matter, or run the session without a keyring daemon. Confirm the window title reaches "Morrowglass Archive" on the Linux bench host.
- Accept `chromium` as well as `google-chrome` for the Linux browser binary, or make it configurable, and record the browser and version that ran in the trial pins.
- Make the window wait report what it did see (the titles of the browser's windows and whether the process is still alive) rather than only "did not appear".
- Add a Linux preflight check that opens the CDB-G04 browser window and checks its title, so a host that cannot run the task fails before a lane starts instead of producing excluded rows.

title: fix(cua-driver): land the action and read overlap example and run its tests in CI
body:
Salvaged from #4747

Fixes #4744

#4744 asks for an opt-in caller example that runs read-only work while a cua-driver action is still in flight, without letting an early matching value count as completion. #4747 built that example and its tests, then closed unmerged. This PR lands it with the contributor's commit preserved (`cherry-pick -x`) and makes CI run its tests.

What lands:

- `libs/cua-driver/examples/action-read-overlap/`, unchanged from #4747. `action_with_read_warming` dispatches one already-bound action, takes at most two advisory reads while it runs, waits for the action to finish, then always takes a fresh final read. Advisory reads are never returned. A read failure or a cancellation joins the in-flight action and never re-dispatches it. Driver tools, defaults and action timing do not change.
- CI coverage. `CI: Test Scripts` now triggers on the example directory and runs its unit tests. `bin/ci` gets a matching `read-overlap-tests` check, held in sync with the workflow by `--verify-sync`.

Test plan:

- The four example tests pass. They cover an early match followed by a deferred rejection (the final read must see the rejection), a read failure joining the action without retry, a cancellation after an early match that still joins the action, and bounded advisory reads.
- Mutations fail the tests. Returning the advisory read instead of a fresh final read fails two tests. Removing the join in the error path fails the read-failure and cancellation tests.
- The scoped repository checks pass: `bin/ci` in affected mode, `bin/ci --verify-sync`, the `scripts/ci` unit tests, actionlint on the workflow, and the SPDX check.
- Not run: live AppKit trials through cua-driver (the example is caller-side Python and takes no driver change), and Linux and Windows desktop lanes.

title: fix(cua-driver): pin batched macOS label reads against absent, empty and typed slots
body:
## Why

#4746 asks that large macOS accessibility snapshots read each control's AXTitle, AXDescription, AXIdentifier and AXHelp in one call instead of four. Main already does this: #6878 moved the tree walker onto one `AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues` call per node (`ax/batch.rs`), and that call covers these four labels. It falls back to single reads when an application rejects the batch. What was missing is a test for the semantics the issue lists, so this PR adds one.

## What changed

- New unit test `batched_labels_keep_absent_empty_and_typed_values_apart` in `platform-macos/src/ax/batch.rs`. It builds a batched reply the way an application sends one for a Calculator-style digit button: AXTitle unsupported (an AXError placeholder), AXDescription `"2"`, AXIdentifier an empty string, AXHelp set, a numeric AXValue and a boolean AXEnabled. It then checks what `NodeAttributes` decodes from that reply.

## Scope

Test only, no runtime change. It covers the label, typed-value and unsupported-slot behaviour the issue names. The single-read fallback and traversal limits are unchanged from #6878 and keep their existing coverage. Top-level window discovery (`top_level_candidate`) still reads AXRole, AXSubrole and AXIdentifier one at a time. It runs once per top-level window, not once per node, so it is left alone.

## Blast Radius

None at runtime. The test drops the batched reply through `NodeAttributes`, the same way the walker does, and asserts that the caller's reference survives. A double release would show up as a failure here instead of a crash somewhere else.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` passes (792 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` for the crate are clean.
- Mutation: when the batched string reader drops empty strings, the test fails (`left: None, right: Some("")`). When the batched boolean reader ignores CFBoolean, it fails too (`left: None, right: Some(true)`).
- Not run: the live macOS Lume lane (the diff changes no runtime code), and the Linux and Windows checks (macOS-only change).

Fixes #4746

title: feat(jev-use): add opt-in literal text-plan recipe
body:
## Why

A caller that already holds exact text-field labels and literal values still has to ask a chooser to pick each sole permitted setter, which costs provider calls and adds no intent. This adds an opt-in jev-use recipe that runs those setters directly and keeps the existing native binding, risk and verification rules.

## What changed

- `python/literal_text_plan.py`: `execute_literal_text_plan` runs one to three caller-supplied `LiteralTextStep(label, value)` setters with no model call. For each step it observes the window, binds the label to exactly one eligible non-risky `text_input`, observes again, and types through the fresh token only when the stable ID, label, value and selection still match. The caller's context guard runs on every observation. Independent step and final oracles decide completion. `validate_literal_text_plan` accepts a model-transcribed plan only when it matches the caller's owner and steps exactly and in order.
- `run_native.observe` now takes a `WindowScope | None` instead of a whole `NativeTask`, so the recipe reuses its `full_output` request and the runner's single reobserve budget.
- The README has a new "Literal text plans" section under the native tasks.

## Scope

This is Python example code beside jev-use. It changes no Driver, SDK, CLI, MCP protocol, default, permission or TypeScript runner. It refuses to infer actions from an open-ended goal. Ambiguous, missing, risky or changed fields, a failed context guard and a failed oracle raise `LiteralPlanHandoff`. Driver errors, refusals and the plan deadline propagate. Input is never retried.

## Tradeoffs

Muness's original PR also checked in a qualification packet (raw traces, analysis scripts and timing tables). This PR leaves it out and ships the recipe, tests and docs. The behavior is covered by deterministic tests here, and the measurements stay on #4751.

## Verification

- The jev-use Python suite passes, including 17 focused literal-plan tests. They cover a two-step plan with no chooser, the checked-in AppKit window state, fresh-token binding, a changed field, a duplicate label, a risky label, the wrong owner, a context check that runs before the reobserve, a failed oracle, a Driver refusal, a timeout after input, and model-plan tampering. The suite also includes `verify_choice_cli.py`, `verify_decision_cli.py --model mock`, `npm test` and `npm run typecheck`.
- I mutated each guard (risk, context, context order, binding check, fresh token, step oracle, reobserve), and each mutation turned at least one test red.
- The scoped repository checks pass. These checks did not cover live macOS/AppKit or live Jev runs, or Windows.

title: CI: jev-use flakes on push to main: OpenJev stalled-body test gets 'transport was refused' instead of timeout
body:
`CI: jev-use` fails intermittently on push to main. The TypeScript unit test `loopback body that stalls past the timeout is a bounded timeout` (`libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use/typescript/openjev_model.test.ts`) gets `OpenJevError: OpenJev redirect or transport was refused` instead of an error with code `timeout`.

Push runs on main:

| head | run | result |
|---|---|---|
| 362e57ae5 | https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43607507319 | failure |
| 193c2df46 | https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43670320437 | failure |
| d83e33324 | https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43718866935 | failure (`not ok 160`) |
| 793adbfe8 | https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43724446596 | success (`ok 160`) |

Nothing under `openjev_model*` changed between d83e33324 and 793adbfe8, so the test is flaky, not broken by one commit. Every `merge_group` and `pull_request` run of the workflow on 15 Nov passed, so most runs never see it.

Likely cause (unconfirmed): the server sends headers and a partial body, then stalls. When `AbortSignal.timeout` fires during `reader.read()` in `readBoundedBody`, undici can reject the read with a `TypeError` ("terminated") rather than a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError`. `transportError` maps every `TypeError` to `http_error` "redirect or transport was refused". If that is it, the fix is to check `signal.aborted` (or the signal's `reason`) in `transportError` before falling back on the error name, and the test then holds on every run.

Repro idea: run the test in a loop (`node --test --test-name-pattern 'stalls past the timeout'`) on the CI Node version until it fails, and log `error.name` and `error.cause` at the catch in `defaultTransport`.

title: fix(cua-driver): expose snapshot identity in full window-state text
body:
## Why

A text-only MCP client sees the `get_window_state` text and never `structuredContent`, so it can address an element only if the text header carries `snapshot_id`. Lean non-empty reads already carry it. `full_output:true` reads and empty trees, including a query that matched nothing, did not. This moves the header insertion to the top of `window_state_view::apply`, before any view is chosen.

## What changed

- `window_state_view::apply` appends ` snapshot_id=<id>` once to the first `window_id=` text line whenever `structuredContent.snapshot_id` exists, then runs the zero-match line and the view selection unchanged. The later lean-path insertion is removed so the id appears exactly once.
- Tests cover token resolution from the text header in every view, stale and wrong-window refusals, empty trees with and without a published snapshot, and `full_output` leaving the structured payload byte for byte. The zero-match test now expects the id in its header.
- `cross_platform_behavior_test` builds AX `element_token`s from the text header. `tool-output-format.md` documents the field.

## Scope

Text header only. Structured payloads, the `since` diff output, token resolution and refusals are unchanged. A read that published no snapshot gets no id. This is #4347 by @saariuslystoned with its net diff re-applied to current main and a merge conflict resolved against #7819's zero-match line. The id goes in first, then the zero-match line.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass on macOS: rustfmt, clippy with `-D warnings` on `cua-driver-core` and `cua-driver-e2e`, the `cua-driver-core` lib tests, and the hermetic `cross_platform_behavior_test` tests. One first-run failure, `batch_tools::tests::pauses_between_steps_but_not_after_the_last`, is a timing assert in a file this diff does not touch. It passed three isolated reruns and a full-suite rerun.
- With the `apply()` change reverted and the new tests kept, four `window_state_view` tests fail. With the change in place they pass.
- The full macOS Lume driver lane passed at this head. Its shared web action matrix drives every AX cell with an `element_token` built from the text header. Every retained `get_window_state` response with a text tree header, default and `full_output:true` reads and a zero-match `full_output` query among them, carries the structured `snapshot_id` exactly once.
- Linux X11/Wayland and Windows desktop lanes did not run here.

Salvaged from #4347

Fixes #4346

title: cua-driver-core test batch_tools::tests::pauses_between_steps_but_not_after_the_last flakes on a wall-clock timing assert under load
body:
`batch_tools::tests::pauses_between_steps_but_not_after_the_last` in `cua-driver-core` failed once during review of #4347 / #7844 (review run `cua-4347-review-b01f432-r2`, salvage head `2633ed291f`, macOS arm64). It failed on the upper-bound timing assert while the full `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib` suite was running (1296 passed, 1 failed). The diff under review did not touch this file:

```
thread 'batch_tools::tests::pauses_between_steps_but_not_after_the_last' panicked at crates/cua-driver-core/src/batch_tools/tests.rs:414:5:
512ms
```

It passed three isolated reruns and one full-suite rerun.

#6453 already moved this test to `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` so that a slow runner could not push elapsed time past the bound, and the failing head includes that change. The elapsed time is therefore paused-clock time: some timer other than the single 120 ms `delay_ms` sleep was auto-advanced. One possible cause: when the paused runtime goes idle while a step waits on something outside tokio's timers (a blocking thread, a lock held under load), tokio jumps the clock to the next pending timer, which can be some unrelated timeout in the invoke path. This has not been confirmed.

Proposal: test the behaviour instead of the exact time.
- Assert that one pause happens between the two steps and none after the last. For example, record the paused-clock instant at each probe call and check that the gap between them is at least `delay_ms` and that the call returns without another `delay_ms` sleep. Or count sleeps through a hook, with no upper bound on total elapsed time.
- Or, if that is not worth it now, add a quarantine entry for this test until it is rewritten.

title: fix(macos): recognize Perplexity Comet as a Chromium browser
body:
## Problem

On macOS every `browser_*` call for a Perplexity Comet window refuses before any CDP connection is attempted:

```json
{"refusal":{"code":"browser_route_unavailable","message":"pid <n> is not a recognized browser process"}}
```

Comet is a Chromium 157 fork with bundle id `ai.perplexity.comet`. `is_chromium` tokenizes the app name and bundle id against a fixed product list (`chrome`, `chromium`, `electron`, `brave`, `edge`, `vivaldi`, `opera`, `arc`, `thorium`, `iridium`, `yandex`); `comet` is not in it, so `BrowserClassification.is_browser` and `supports_cdp` are both false and `engine.rs` refuses in `bind_native_window` (`engine.rs:1375`) before touching the browser.

Comet is otherwise ready for the existing-profile route: with its per-instance remote-debugging switch on it publishes `DevToolsActivePort` under `~/Library/Application Support/Comet/`, the same file the route already reads for Chrome.

## Change

- `platform-macos`: add the `comet` token to `is_chromium`; map `ai.perplexity.comet` / name `Comet` to a new `BrowserProduct::Comet`; include it in the standalone-consumer role; add its profile root `Library/Application Support/Comet`.
- `cua-driver-core`: add the `BrowserProduct::Comet` variant and a setup descriptor using `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` with the Chromium inspect-page titles.
- Tests: classification, profile root and setup URL.

Linux and Windows product detection is unchanged; Comet ships on macOS only.

## Verification

- `cargo check -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core` — clean.
- `cargo fmt -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos comet --lib` — 1 passed (`comet_is_a_standalone_chromium_browser_with_its_own_profile_root`).
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core setup_is_limited --lib` — 1 passed (descriptor assertion includes Comet).
- Full `cargo test -p platform-macos -p cua-driver-core --lib` — 791 passed, 1 failed, 13 ignored. The failure is `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`, which reads the OS consent-label tables and requires both `Don’t Allow` and `Don't Allow`; the local table only carries the curly-apostrophe variant. That file and test are untouched by this commit, so it appears unrelated to this change.
- Live Comet window before the change: `get_browser_state` refused with the message above, while the accessibility route (`get_window_state`) returned a populated tree for the same process, confirming that only the classifier gate blocked the browser route.

title: verify-cua-driver evidence checker requires files native capture cells never write
body:
`.cursor/skills/verify-cua-driver/scripts/check-evidence.sh` requires `fixture-state.json` in every declared cell's recording, and requires a before/after screenshot pair in every cell. Only the shared web host runner (`cross_platform_behavior_test.rs`, harnesses electron, tauri, wkwebview, webview2) writes `fixture-state.json`, and only its background cells write `sentinel-events.jsonl` and `desktop-observation.txt`. Native harness cells such as GTK3 read fixture state from the accessibility tree, and read-only capture cells (`delivery: not_applicable`) dispatch no action, so they record no screenshot pair.

As a result, the checker fails every run of the nested-Sway capture lane (`CUA_E2E_INTERNAL_LANE=capture`, `CUA_E2E_HARNESS_FILTER=gtk3`) even when every cell passes:

```
Invalid evidence: missing linux-gtk3-tree-and-screenshot-not-applicable-not-applicable/fixture-state.json
```

That cell declares the `ax_state` and `pixels` oracles, and neither uses that file.

Expected: the checker requires the files a cell's declaration implies (its harness, delivery and oracles), and still fails when one of those is missing.

title: fix(cua-driver): batch the macOS identity and window-scope string reads
body:
## Why

The macOS tree walker already reads each node in one `AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues` round trip (#6878). Two snapshot paths still read string attributes one cross-process request at a time:

- the identity recheck that runs before an `element_token` click (`ObservedIdentity::read`) makes four requests for AXRole, AXTitle, AXDescription and AXIdentifier
- each top-level window-scope candidate (`top_level_candidate`) makes three requests for AXRole, AXSubrole and AXIdentifier

## What changed

- `ax/batch.rs` gains `copy_string_attrs`, which reads N string attributes in one batched request. Each slot is decoded the same way `copy_string_attr` decodes a single read: an empty string stays `Some("")`, and an AXError value, kCFNull or a non-string comes back as `None`. If the application refuses the batch, it falls back to one read per name. If it does not answer in time, every slot is `None`.
- `NodeAttributes::read` (the walker) and `copy_string_attrs` now share one `copy_multiple` request with a three-state reply, so the refused and timed-out cases are handled in one place.
- `ObservedIdentity::read` and `top_level_candidate` use the new helper. The identity recheck drops from four requests to one, and each window-scope candidate from three to one.

## Scope

Covers the snapshot identity recheck and the window-scope candidate reads. Labels, typed values, frames, actions, hierarchy, stale-token refusal and the fallback paths behave as before. There is no public API change and no change to the default observation policy. Single reads in individual tools (`set_value`, `click`, `invoke_menu` and others) are out of scope.

## Blast Radius

macOS only. Every stale-token click and every window-scoped read goes through the changed paths. The decoding matches single reads slot for slot, and an application that rejects the batch call gets the old per-attribute reads.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test --lib` for `platform-macos` all pass. The new test `string_slots_read_like_single_string_reads` fails when an empty string is decoded as missing.
- The full macOS Lume lane passed at this head, including the stale-token, relabelled-cached-click and save-sheet cases.
- Not run: Linux and Windows platform crates and the Linux desktop end-to-end lanes, which this change does not touch.

Refs #4748, #4762. Those drafts batched the same walker reads on an older tree; #6878 landed that part.

Fixes #4761

title: fix(cua-driver): require only the evidence files a verify cell declares
body:
Fixes #7853

## Problem

`check-evidence.sh` required `fixture-state.json` in every declared cell's recording, and a before/after screenshot pair in every cell. Only the shared web host runner (`cross_platform_behavior_test.rs`: electron, tauri, wkwebview, webview2) writes `fixture-state.json`, and only its background cells write `sentinel-events.jsonl` and `desktop-observation.txt`. Native cells such as GTK3 read fixture state from the accessibility tree, and read-only capture cells dispatch no action. So every nested-Sway capture lane run failed the check even when all its cells passed:

```
Invalid evidence: missing linux-gtk3-tree-and-screenshot-not-applicable-not-applicable/fixture-state.json
```

## Change

The checker now reads each cell's `harness` and `oracles` from `cases.jsonl` and requires:

- `tool-calls.jsonl` for every cell, as before.
- `fixture-state.json`, and the `last_action` click marker, only for web host cells that declare the `fixture_state` oracle.
- The sentinel journal and desktop observation only for web host background cells, as before for those cells.
- A screenshot pair for every cell that dispatches an action. Read-only `not_applicable` cells skip it.

A declaration without an `oracles` array is now rejected as malformed. The checker test gains passing and failing native read-only and native foreground scenarios.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `python3 -m unittest test_e2e_rust_linux_workflow` passes. With the previous checker, the new native read-only and native foreground scenarios fail.
- Real nested-Sway capture lane evidence (GTK3, 7 delivered, 1 refused, 0 failed, run at the head of #7851): the previous checker fails on `fixture-state.json`, the new one passes.
- The same evidence with one declared file removed still fails: a read-only cell's `tool-calls.jsonl`, a foreground cell's `tool-calls.jsonl`, a foreground cell's `after.png`, or a whole declared cell's recording.
- Electron background X11 lane evidence still passes. With an electron cell's `fixture-state.json` or `sentinel-events.jsonl` removed, it fails.
- Not run: shellcheck (not available), macOS and Windows lanes (the checker is only called from the Linux helper).

title: cua-driver (macOS): batch the single attribute reads in the action tools
body:
Follow-up to #7854.

#7854 adds `copy_string_attrs` in `ax/batch.rs`, which reads N string attributes in one `AXUIElementCopyMultipleAttributeValues` request, and uses it for the snapshot identity recheck and the window-scope candidate reads.

The action tools still read attributes one cross-process request at a time with `copy_string_attr` / `copy_bool_attr`:

- `set_value.rs`
- `click.rs`
- `invoke_menu.rs`
- `type_text.rs`
- `reveal_scroll.rs`

Where a tool reads several attributes of the same element in a row, those reads could go through `copy_string_attrs` (plus a bool equivalent if needed), keeping the same per-slot decoding and the per-attribute fallback for applications that refuse the batch call.

Out of scope for #7854, so it is tracked here. Done when each of these tools reads same-element attributes in one batched request where it reads more than one, with behaviour unchanged.

title: fix(cua-driver): pin that the desktop lane frees before the detached window watch
body:
This closes the gap #4771 measured. A macOS action no longer holds the process-wide desktop lane through the post-action window watch. Main already behaves this way, but no test enforced it, and this PR adds one.

What main already does:

- #4915 returns a quiet action after a 300 ms report window. The rest of the watch runs detached and keeps the focus-steal lease (`Snapshot::continue_detached`).
- #6033 added `post_action_wait: "none"`. With it the result returns as soon as input is delivered, and the whole watch runs detached.
- The registry drops the action's `DesktopCall` right after the tool returns, before evidence capture and result shaping. The detached thread takes only the focus-steal lease and never a `DesktopLease` clone. The next desktop action is admitted at once. Its snapshot ends the earlier detached watch.

What this PR adds:

- A test, `the_desktop_lane_is_free_while_the_detached_watch_runs`. An action takes the desktop lane, runs a quiet watch with a 10 s deadline, and then drops its call. The test asserts three things: the next `DesktopCall::acquire()` succeeds within 5 s, the detached watch is still running at that point, and the whole sequence ends well before the deadline. If the detached watch kept the lane, the test would fail with "the next desktop action waited for the detached watch". That regression was checked by temporarily moving `DesktopLease::current()` into the detached thread, and the test turned red.
- A paragraph in the embedding guide (`Skills/cua-driver/EMBEDDING.md`). It says that admission ends when the result returns and does not last through the detached watch.

Out of scope: the RFC's receipt lifecycle (dispatch, commit and supervision states, application acknowledgements) has no maintainer decision, and its RFC and draft implementation PRs (#4772, #4776) were closed by their author. This PR adds no new tool surface.

Test plan: the scoped repository checks. They are the macOS `platform-macos` window-change-detector unit tests, the `cua-driver-core` skills-bundle tests, rustfmt, clippy on `platform-macos` tests and the whitespace check. Linux and Windows checks did not run, because those platform crates are unchanged and this test is macOS only.

Refs #4771

title: fix(cua-driver): skip the glide wait for a cursor turned off at runtime
body:
## Why

`set_agent_cursor_enabled {"enabled": false}` hides the cursor but does not stop the wait. On macOS and Windows, `animate_cursor_to_target` checked only the launch-time `cfg.enabled`. A placed cursor that was turned off at runtime still got a `MoveTo`, and every action waited for its arrival (up to the 8 s arrival limit on macOS) before it pressed anything. This is the disabled-cursor delay in #4276.

## What changed

- `RenderStateCore::animates()` in `cursor-overlay` answers "glide and wait?": enabled at launch, not turned off at runtime, and placed.
- The macOS, Windows and Linux `animate_cursor_to_target` all use it. Linux already checked runtime visibility, so its behavior does not change.
- Tests: a shared one shows that a cursor turned off after it was shown no longer animates. A macOS one shows that `animate_cursor_to` registers no arrival waiter for that cursor. Each test fails when its half of the fix is reverted.

## Scope

This covers the runtime-disable wait only. It leaves out the rest of #4308:
- The second-display re-seeding half is already on main. #4305 and the coordinate-independent `placed` flag mean a cursor on a negative-coordinate display is no longer re-seeded. The #4308 thread measured that on the reporter's setup.
- The macOS overlay painting changes are superseded by #5650 and #7458, which paint each display separately.
- Synchronous `SetEnabled` inside `send_command`, motion quiescing, and the Windows dirty-rect change are left out. The tool path needs none of them for this fix, and they change the render threads' state ownership.

## Blast Radius

The change only affects actions on a session whose cursor was turned off at runtime. Those actions now skip the glide and the wait, as they already did for a cursor disabled at launch. An enabled cursor animates exactly as before. Target checks and focus waits elsewhere in the click path are untouched.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks passed: formatting, clippy with warnings denied, `cursor-overlay` tests, and three full runs of the `platform-macos` lib tests.
- The macOS Lume full matrix passed at this head: 190 cells, runner exit 0.
- Not run here: the Windows and Linux platform crates, and the Linux desktop lanes. CI covers those.

title: [Feature]: live timed check for cursor-off click latency on a real second display
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

#7860 and #4308 fix the second-display click delay reported in #4276. On that bug, a click on a second display waited for the agent cursor's glide even after the cursor had been turned off at runtime. Unit and mutation tests cover the code path. They show that a cursor turned off at runtime no longer animates and registers no arrival waiter. No test times a click on a real multi-display layout, so a regression in the timing could ship without any test failing.

### Desired outcome

A repeatable live check that times the click itself on a second display:

1. Use a real second display, or a CGVirtualDisplay inside a Lume guest.
2. Click an element on that display once with the agent cursor on, so the cursor is placed.
3. Turn the cursor off at runtime with `set_agent_cursor_enabled {"enabled": false}`.
4. Time the next element click on the same display.

The check passes when that click no longer waits for the glide. It fails when the click still takes about as long as the glide or the arrival limit.

### Current workaround

Someone has to time clicks by hand on their own multi-display setup.

### Affected components and platforms

cua-driver on macOS: `platform-macos` cursor overlay and `cursor-overlay`. Windows has the same code path and could get the same check where a second display is available.

### Alternatives and prior art

- #4276: the original report.
- #4308 and #7860: the fixes. Their tests cover the logic but not the timing.
- #5336: drawing the cursor on the target display. It is related but does not cover this timing.

### Implementation ideas

Add a cell to the macOS Lume verification lane that creates a CGVirtualDisplay in the guest, opens a fixture window on it, and runs the four steps above. It should record per-click durations and compare the post-disable click against the configured glide duration.

Refs #4276
Refs #7860

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): let users admit apps past Hyprland background input quirks
body:
## Why

Users on Omarchy could not admit an app they had checked themselves for background Hyprland input. Since #6706 the driver admits any native Wayland app. The one app-level refusal left is the toolkit quirk list: Qt 6 apps refuse background keys with `client_drops_background_keys`. Contrawrite, the Qt Quick editor in this issue, hits it. This adds the opt-in the issue asks for, a user-owned list that lifts that refusal for named executables.

## What changed

- `hyprland_compatibility::admit` reads `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cua-driver/hyprland-apps.txt` (absolute paths, one per line, `#` comments). It reads the list only when a quirk would refuse the target, and matches each canonicalised entry against `/proc/<pid>/exe`. On a match it returns `Admission::User`.
- A dispatch admitted this way carries `admission: "user"` in its structured result, and its text and action-record detail say the user qualified the app, not Cua.
- The Linux skill and the platform-support page document the file and its limits.

## Scope

Driver admission only. The list does not lift `client_xwayland`, `client_unattested` or `target_unavailable`, and the plugin's own dispatch checks (`client_not_bound` for Chromium and Electron) still apply. With no file, behaviour is unchanged. The plugin is untouched.

## Tradeoffs

The issue's local patch matched a list against the old `PACKAGES` allowlist, which #6706 removed. A config key in the driver's settings was the alternative. A plain file under the driver's config dir follows the shape the issue proposed and needs no schema change.

## Blast Radius

This only affects background Hyprland input with the production plugin, and only targets that a quirk refuses. When nothing is listed, the result payload on success is unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` for the Hyprland and admission tests, plus clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. The new tests cover a listed executable, a symlinked entry, unlisted, relative, commented and missing entries, and the live-target refusals that stay in force. Making the list read as empty turns two of them red.
- A live Hyprland run (a real Qt app taking background keys) did not run here. No Hyprland session was available, and macOS and Windows checks do not apply.

Fixes #4779

title: fix(cua-daemon): re-land the digest-pinned Lume image handling from #6150
body:
Re-lands @Alex-Wengg's #6150 on current main, with their authorship kept as co-author. A fork PR cannot get the local CI sign-off that merging needs, so the reviewed diff is applied here.

Lume pulls macOS images by tag, and the digest only keys the cached base VM. This change makes that handling honest end to end:

- A Lume reference names its digest once (`repo:tag@sha256:...`), even when the input already carried one.
- A digest-only reference is refused with a plain message, because Lume has no tag to pull.
- After a pull, the digest Lume recorded is compared with the one the base is named for. When the tag has moved off a pinned digest, the pulled base is removed instead of being kept under the old digest's name, and the error says what to do. A tag that moved during an unpinned create is a retryable failure.
- A pull Lume refuses outright is an invalid argument, so `on=auto` does not try every other computer with it.

Tests: 649 in `cua-vmm`, 60 in `cua-sandbox-core`, 173 in `cua-image`, 187 in `cua-daemon-core`, 526 in `cua-spaces` and 63 in `cua-daemon` lib tests pass, as do the `lume_pull_digest` and `placement` integration tests. Clippy (including each `cua-vmm` backend alone), rustfmt and the generated references are clean under `bin/ci`.

Closes #6150.

title: cua-driver: live Omarchy check for user-admitted Hyprland apps (Qt 6 background type_text, admission: "user")
body:
## What is owed

#7867 (for #4779) lets a user admit an executable past the Hyprland background-input quirk refusals by listing it in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cua-driver/hyprland-apps.txt`. A user-admitted dispatch reports `admission: "user"`. The PR's unit tests cover the list parsing and the admission decision. A live check on a real Hyprland session did not run, because no Hyprland session was available where the PR was built.

## Check to run on Omarchy (Hyprland, production plugin)

1. Start a Qt 6 app that the quirk list refuses today with `client_drops_background_keys` (for example a Qt Quick editor such as Contrawrite, from #4779).
2. Without the list file, background `type_text` to its window should be refused with `client_drops_background_keys`, as it is on main.
3. Add the app's absolute executable path to `~/.config/cua-driver/hyprland-apps.txt`. Then `list_windows` should list the app, and background `type_text` into a focused-in-app text field (with another window holding user focus) should reach the field. Read the field back from fresh state.
4. The `type_text` structured result should carry `admission: "user"`, and its text should say the user qualified the app, not Cua.
5. Focus should not move: the user's window keeps focus throughout.

Keep the driver output and a screenshot or AX readback of the field as evidence. If step 3 or 4 fails, report it on #7867, or on a new issue if #7867 has merged.

Refs #4779, #7867

title: fix(cua-driver): return a native set_value once its field settles
body:
A native text `set_value` whose read-back already confirmed the value no longer waits out the 300 ms window-change report window. It returns once the field has kept that value for 150 ms with no new window or foreground change seen.

Fixes #4792

## What changed

- `window_change_detector.rs`: `Snapshot::detect_async_until(settled)` ends the report-window poll early when `settled()` holds. A window or foreground change seen first is still reported. The rest of the deadline still runs detached with the focus-steal lease, exactly as after a quiet report window, so protection lasts as long as before and a late window is still reported on the next result.
- `set_value.rs`: for a native AXValue write whose read-back verified, a watcher thread re-reads the field every 25 ms and sets a flag once it has held the read-back value for 150 ms since the write. A different value or an unreadable field, even once, rules settling out, and the result waits the usual report window. The detector's poll only reads the flag, so an app that stops answering accessibility calls cannot stall the window watch or delay its lease.
- Web content (AX echo is not trusted), unverified writes, popups, Calc cells and errors keep the existing wait. Result text and structured fields are unchanged.

This takes the narrow part of the issue, early return on a settled field with the protection window untouched, on the current detector. It does not bring back the owned-supervision receipts from the closed #4776 and #4793.

## Test plan

- Unit tests: `a_settled_action_returns_early_and_keeps_the_detached_watch` (returns before the report window, detached lease still held), `a_window_seen_before_settling_is_still_reported`, and `FieldSettle` cases for a quiet field, a later change, and an unreadable or unknown field.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`, `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test snapshot_dispatch_invariants`, and `bin/ci --quick` pass on macOS arm64.
- Not run: a live macOS Lume before/after `set_value` on an AppKit text field, and the Linux and Windows lanes (this change touches only the macOS adapter).

title: fix(cua-driver): attribute macOS permissions to the responsible process, not the parent pid
body:
## Why

On macOS, `check_permissions` called a CuaDriver.app daemon `driver-daemon` ("its own responsible process") whenever its parent pid was 1. A daemon started inside another app's process tree, such as a host shell running `CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve &` and then exiting, is reparented to launchd, so its parent pid becomes 1. macOS still charges its TCC requests to the app that started it. The daemon was mislabelled, and `permissions status` reported grants that its tool calls did not use. The fix asks the kernel which process is responsible instead of guessing from the parent pid.

## What changed

- `check_permissions` gets the responsible process from `responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid`. It reports `driver-daemon` only when the daemon is its own responsible process and runs from a CuaDriver bundle. `source` now carries `parent_pid`, `responsible_pid`, `responsible_executable` and `responsible_bundle_id`. `parent_pid` replaces `responsible_ppid`, which held the parent pid under a misleading name. The `caller` note names the responsible app.
- `permissions status` reports the running daemon's answer whatever its attribution, because those are the grants its tool calls get. It names the app those grants belong to and gives one next step: turn them on for that app, or `cua-driver stop` and then `cua-driver permissions grant`. An embedded daemon (`host` attribution) is told to turn them on for the host app instead of running `permissions grant`.
- The docs (EMBEDDING.md, troubleshooting, the `permissions` CLI reference) describe the new fields and the started-by-another-app case.

## Scope

This covers attribution and reporting on macOS. `cua-driver call` still does not start a daemon when the socket is missing, which was the issue's first suggestion. That was decided against (#7883): auto-start would change which app identity owns the daemon's macOS permissions. Instead, the daemon-not-running message from `call`, `config` and `recording` now points at a start that keeps Cua Driver's own identity. For the default socket it says `cua-driver permissions grant`. For a custom one it gives `open -n -g /Applications/CuaDriver.app --args serve --socket <path>`, with the path made absolute (LaunchServices starts the app in `/`) and shell-quoted; when the absolute path exceeds the 103 bytes macOS allows for a socket, it asks for a shorter one. The old hint, a bare `cua-driver serve`, made the daemon use the grants of the shell that ran it. Embedded hosts, Linux and Windows keep the `serve` hint.

## Blast Radius

Any consumer of `check_permissions` or `permissions status --json` on macOS is affected. Daemons launched through LaunchServices (`open -n -g CuaDriver.app --args serve`, `permissions grant`) still report `driver-daemon`, so the CI and Lume gates that check `.source.attribution == "driver-daemon"` keep passing. `source.responsible_ppid` has been removed; no consumer of it exists in this repository. The responsibility symbol comes from the same private libSystem API family the driver already links for `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim`.

## Verification

- The issue's second launch path, reproduced on macOS. A Terminal-run script starts the bundled daemon in the background and exits. Before the fix, `check_permissions` returned `attribution: "driver-daemon"`, `responsible_ppid: 1`. After it, the result is `attribution: "caller"`, `parent_pid: 1`, `responsible_bundle_id: "com.apple.Terminal"`. `permissions status` prints "These are the permissions of com.apple.Terminal, not the Cua Driver app." and one Next line.
- A LaunchServices launch of a re-signed copy of the app with the new binary still reports `attribution: "driver-daemon"`, with the responsible pid equal to the daemon's pid.
- The scoped repository checks passed: rustfmt, clippy, unit tests for `cua-driver` and `platform-macos`, generated reference, UniFFI bindings, the Windows cross-check and SPDX headers. New unit tests cover `tcc_identity` (including responsible pid ≠ own pid with parent pid 1), the caller note, the kernel lookup, and the status text for `caller` and `host`.

Fixes #4802

title: verify-cua-driver: rerun the macOS Lume full lane for #7880 at fcae3c9942 once guest SSH writes are healthy
body:
Follow-up from #7880 (fixes #4802).

The verify-cua-driver macOS Lume full lane has not run to completion at the PR head `fcae3c9942d8ed3b76b96d2b7b845b76e5dcda41`. Both attempts ended as infrastructure failures before any cell was judged:

1. `source transfer failed`: the `tar` stream over SSH into the guest exited non-zero, and no guest evidence was collected.
2. The host-side SSH write that hands the signing-keychain password to the guest runner (`cat > <run dir>/unlock`) hit its 60 second timeout.

Findings on the second failure: the collected `runner.log` shows the guest runner had already read the password from the FIFO and moved on to signing, history setup and the cargo build. So the password arrived, and the host's SSH session did not exit within 60 s. The same signature (the guest consumed it, the host's SSH timed out) appears in two earlier unlock failures on this host on other heads, and alongside a 300 s source-transfer timeout and a 30 s status-poll timeout. Every one is an SSH session to a guest stalling under host load. None is a credential or keychain problem. During the second attempt a 6-CPU, 12 GB benchmark VM was running beside the 4-CPU worker on the 10-core host. The wrapper waits for memory pressure before cloning, but not for CPU load. That correlation is an inference, not a proven cause. Other full-lane runs on the same seed passed between these failures.

To do:
- Rerun the full lane at `fcae3c9942` (or at #7880's head at the time, if it has moved) once the host's guest SSH writes are healthy, and record the result on #7880.
- If the result is green, nothing else is needed for #4802's verification. If a cell fails, run it at the base before blaming the diff.

Refs #7880, #4802.

title: fix(cua-driver): report foregrounded_window when Chrome comes forward during existing-profile attach
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `browser_prepare` with `strategy.kind:"existing_profile"` returned `side_effects.foregrounded_window: false` while Chrome came to the front. Chrome activates itself to show its "Allow remote debugging?" prompt. That happens outside any setup step that reports it, so nothing set the flag.
- What changed: every existing-profile attach now watches the browser for the whole call, including one that starts with Chrome in front, and sets `foregrounded_window` when the browser came forward, even if it lost the front again before the call returned. On macOS the watch records the `NSWorkspaceDidActivateApplicationNotification` for Chrome's pid. The background guard (Chrome window on another Space) also counts each self-activation it reverts, and it is joined before its answer is read. Core also checks whether the browser is frontmost at the end. A refusal carries the same flag in its detail.

## Related work

Fixes #4810

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: `foregrounded_window` can now be `true` for existing-profile attaches where it used to be `false`. No field is added or removed. Linux and Windows keep the trait defaults (no watch), and their behaviour is unchanged.
- `BrowserPlatform::guard_background_attach` now returns `Box<dyn BrowserForegroundWatch>` instead of `Box<dyn Any + Send>`. There is a new defaulted `watch_browser_foreground`, and both are declared in `ACCEPTED_DEFAULTS`.
- Known limit, documented in BROWSER.md: an unguarded attach counts what macOS reported before the call returned. If the user switches away in the last moments of the call while the notice is still queued, the activation can be missed. A guarded attach counts every revert it made.
- Risk and rollback: the change only affects reporting and the guard's shutdown, which now joins its watch thread. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed locally; the `cua-driver-core` browser tests, `platform-macos` browser and focus_steal tests, and clippy `-D warnings` run in CI. New and extended owner tests cover a foreground attach, a guarded off-Space attach, a browser that loses the front again before return, a guarded attach whose activation notice arrives late, the browser already in front (stays `false`), the browser in front at the start that comes forward again after the user switched away, and the activation record at the platform boundary. Mutation checks: removing the flag update, the foreground watch, the guard as a source, or the notification hook each turns at least one of these tests red.
- Manual or platform evidence: no live Chrome consent run. It needs a granted CuaDriver build and Chrome's real consent prompt.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Linux and Windows platform crates and Linux desktop E2E were not run here, so CI covers them.

title: feat(cua-driver): Hyprland Chromium and Electron accept background input via per-client agent seat
body:
## What changes for users

Chromium and Electron apps on Hyprland now accept background clicks and typing when the agent launches them with `launch_app` and `agent_seat: true`. Before, the Hyprland plugin refused them with `client_not_bound`, because Chromium's Wayland backend binds only the first `wl_seat` it sees (the user's) and never the `Cua-Agent` seats.

Limit to know about: an app started this way has only the agent seat, so your own mouse and keyboard do not reach it while it runs. Quit it to get it back.

## Approach

Per-client seat binding, as discussed in the design note on #7869.

- `launch_app agent_seat: true` (optional `agent_seat_lane: 1|2`) starts the app in a transient systemd user scope named `cua-agent-seat-<lane>-<token>.scope`. The tag is the cgroup, not an environment variable: Chromium and Electron overwrite their environment at startup, so `/proc/<pid>/environ` is empty when they connect (found on the real desktop below). Where there is no systemd, the launch sets `CUA_AGENT_SEAT=<lane>` instead, which only works for apps that keep their environment.
- The plugin hooks Hyprland's `wl_seat` bind (`CWLSeatProtocol::bindManager`). For a client carrying that tag it binds the lane's agent seat on the same object id instead of the user's seat, so the agent seat is the client's first and only seat. Every other client's bind is Hyprland's own, unchanged. No display-wide global filter is installed.
- Driver reads the same tag from the target process and connects to that lane's socket only, so a tagged app is driven through its own lane. A busy lane is `lane_busy`, with no fallback.
- Already-running apps cannot be moved, because the tag is read at bind. They keep refusing with `client_not_bound`, now with a detail and hint: `client_not_agent_seat_bound` (relaunch with `agent_seat`) or `client_bound_to_other_lane`. `launch_app` reports `agent_seat.tagged` and warns when the app joined an already-running instance.
- `hyprctl -j cua:status` reports `agent_seat_binding` and `agent_seat_binds`.

No regression of the #4257 decisions: untagged clients (imv, Zed and the rest) see what they saw before, nothing falls back to the user's seat, and there is no plugin-owned global filter or process-name matching.

## Tests

- Plugin unit tests: tag parser (`agent_seat_tag_test`), entry-point lifetime test with the new hook and status fields, and the key-repeat fixture still builds against `input_experiment.cpp`.
- Driver unit tests: tag parsing, lane-pinned claim (no fallback to the other lane), `launch_app` argument validation and child environment, hint text.
- Requalification session (`requalify/headless.py`, runs on each Hyprland build in the nightly workflow and on this PR): `first_seat_client.c` binds only its first `wl_seat`, as Chromium does. Tagged, it must get `Cua-Agent` and receive a background click and key; untagged, it must keep the user's seat and still be refused with `client_not_agent_seat_bound`. The result is recorded under `smoke.agent_seat`. It does not gate the nightly status yet; I suggest gating it after a few green nights.
- Real desktop (below).

## Real desktop check (Omarchy edge VM)

Hyprland 0.57.2 on the Omarchy edge image, plugin built in the guest from this branch (22/22 CTest pass against the real headers; `cua:status` reports `agent_seat_binding: true`), Driver built from this branch on Linux (platform-linux unit tests pass except two existing input tests this change does not touch, clippy clean). A terminal held focus and received a real user's keystrokes (a uinput keyboard, one key every 200 ms) while the user's pointer rested over it. Each app's own page logged what it received.

| App | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Chromium 157, started with `agent_seat` | Background click into a text field, typing "hello agent" and a button click all landed (page logged trusted events). Focus stayed on the terminal, the user's pointer did not move. |
| Electron 44, started with `agent_seat` | Same: click, typing and button click landed in the background. |
| Chromium, started without `agent_seat` | Pointer and key input refused with `client_not_agent_seat_bound` and the relaunch hint. Semantic AT-SPI clicks still work, as before. |
| Before this change (stock plugin, same VM) | Both Chromium cases refused with `client_not_bound`, reproducing the issue. |
| GTK 3 app (untagged) | Background click and typing both landed; the bind hook did not touch it (`agent_seat_binds` unchanged). |
| Qt 6 app (untagged) | Background click landed; keys refuse with `client_drops_background_keys`, as documented. |
| imv (single-seat style app, untagged) | Starts and runs; binds the three stock seats (`Hyprland`, `Cua-Agent`, `Cua-Agent-2`) exactly as before; the hook never touched it. |

The user's keystrokes all reached the terminal and no agent key leaked into it. Two things the check found and fixed here: the environment tag never reached Chromium and Electron, and the driver cannot read the launch scope back because Chromium moves itself into its own scope after startup, so Driver remembers the lane it launched on.

## Known limits

- Tag is read at bind, so apps already running need a relaunch. Chromium and Electron hand a second launch on the same profile to the running instance, so quit it or use a separate profile.
- The hook needs the `bindManager` symbol; each Hyprland build is requalified for it. Without it, tagged apps behave as untagged ones and status says so.
- XWayland is unchanged (still refuses).
- Only the plugin and Driver changed here; released Driver builds in the nightly do not know `agent_seat` yet.

Fixes #7869

title: fix(cua-driver): wait for a woken Chromium AT-SPI tree before the first Linux walk
body:
## Why

On Linux, Chromium and Electron publish their AT-SPI tree only after a client reads an object's attributes. They don't need `--force-renderer-accessibility` for this. #5074 already makes the driver send that `GetAttributes` call once per process. Chromium then builds the tree asynchronously, and for a few tens of milliseconds the web document exists with no children. A first snapshot taken during that window comes back with only the window chrome. With no flag, the base driver's first `get_window_state` on the Electron fixture missed the page in 5 of 54 fresh launches.

## What changed

- `collect_visited_bounded_opts` wakes each process once. For Chromium it then waits until the web document under the requested window (or under the app, when no window is resolved) has children. Each check is one `Collection.GetMatches` call, the wait stops after 500 ms, and it never takes more than half the walk's budget. Concurrent walks share the wake and the wait, and a walk that joins another walk's wait spends at most half its own budget on it. The wake runs on its own task, so a walk that runs out of budget leaves it in flight for the next walk and skips the wait. A wait cut short or left unanswered is retried on the next walk instead of being cached.
- New ignored e2e test `chromium_tree_wake_linux_test`, routed in the Linux shared suite. It launches the Electron fixture 20 times without the flag and requires the first snapshot to contain the page marker.
- The browser guide and the existing-profile setup message no longer say the flag is required on Linux. The accessibility bus still has to be on before the app starts.

## Scope

Linux AT-SPI walks of Chromium-toolkit apps only. Other toolkits skip the wait. The accessibility bus must be on before the app starts; an app launched with the bus off never registers, and this PR does not change that (the issue documents it). `launch_app` still adds the flag for apps it starts itself.

## Tradeoffs

A page that never gets content, such as `about:blank`, pays the 500 ms wait once per window: its first snapshot took 923 ms here, against 388 ms on main. Polling a role match is cheaper than walking the tree again and doesn't depend on event delivery.

## Blast Radius

Applies to the first walk of every Chromium/Electron window on Linux (`get_window_state` and the actions that walk first). macOS and Windows are unaffected. The GTK3 first snapshot was unchanged in timing (533 ms on main, 508 ms with this change).

## Verification

Ran the scoped repository checks, Linux X11 under Xvfb, Chromium 156, Electron 39:
- First `get_window_state` on the Electron fixture with no flag, fresh process each time: main missed the page in 5 of 54 launches, this branch missed it in 0 of 57.
- The new e2e test passes 20/20 at the head. With the wake removed it fails on launch 1.
- The verify-cua-driver X11 lane passed both Electron AX background click cells. fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and the `platform-linux` unit tests (1071 passed) are green. So is the e2e inventory test.

Not run: Wayland compositors (Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, KDE), macOS and Windows.

Fixes #4768

title: cua-driver/Linux: stop adding --force-renderer-accessibility in launch_app for Chromium apps
body:
Follow-up to #7886.

#7886 makes the Linux AT-SPI walk wake Chromium and Electron processes and wait for the web document to get children, so the page tree shows up on the first snapshot without `--force-renderer-accessibility`. `launch_app` on Linux still appends the flag to every Chromium-family app it starts (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/launch_app.rs`, the `chromium_family_program(prog)` branch).

With #7886 merged, the flag is probably no longer needed there. Dropping it would make apps the driver launches behave the same as apps the user launched, which is the path #7886 tested.

This should be its own PR, because #7886 only checked X11 under Xvfb. Before dropping the flag:

- Check the first `get_window_state` on a `launch_app`-started Chromium and Electron app with no flag, on X11 and on the Wayland compositors (Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, KDE).
- Keep `ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED=1` / `NO_AT_BRIDGE=0`. The accessibility bus still has to be on before the app starts.
- Keep a caller's own `--force-renderer-accessibility` in `additional_arguments` working.

title: cua-driver e2e: run Linux Chromium/Electron fixtures without --force-renderer-accessibility
body:
Follow-up to #7886.

The cua-driver e2e fixtures still start Chromium and Electron with `--force-renderer-accessibility` on Linux:

- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/cross_platform_behavior_test.rs` (Linux Electron host spec)
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-testkit/src/sentinel.rs`

This should be a separate PR from #7886 and from the `launch_app` change. Run the affected e2e suites on Linux X11 and Wayland without the flag. Leave the macOS and Windows host specs alone unless they are checked on those platforms.

title: fix(cua-driver): bind window screenshots on the nested cua-compositor
body:
## Why

On the nested cua-compositor, `get_window_state` read the fixture's accessibility tree but every window screenshot failed with `surface_identity_unproven: no compositor-attested window geometry is available`. The only crop sources were Sway IPC and the GNOME helper, and neither exists on that compositor, so all three compositor E2E lanes stopped at preflight. This fix has the compositor attest the window rectangle, and the driver crops the output only when that attestation holds for the whole capture.

## What changed

- `cua_compositor_patch.py` adds a read-only `w <pid>` control query. For the target's process family it returns the scene rectangle in output pixels, the output size and a scene epoch. It refuses with a reason when the target is ambiguous, occluded by a visible toplevel, or on more than one output, a scaled output or a transformed output. Map, unmap, restacking, placement and xdg geometry commits bump the epoch. The query never focuses or raises.
- New `wayland/cua_compositor_capture.rs`. When `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` is set, window capture checks that the window was listed for that process. It then queries the compositor before and after a screencopy, on a Wayland connection whose peer process is the same as the control socket's. It crops only when both replies match, the image is the attested output and the rectangle lies wholly inside it. ID-only callers such as `zoom` must resolve to one listed process.
- `wayland/mod.rs` routes inject-mode window capture there. It also splits the screencopy helper so the capture can reuse the already-attested connection. A refusal keeps the `surface_identity_unproven` code and names the compositor's reason.

## Scope

This covers foreground or unoccluded window capture on cua-compositor. Background capture of an occluded target is still refused (#4827). Cursor rendering (#4828), desktop pointer delivery (#4829) and the GTK3 and Electron effect failures (#4832, #4833, #4834) are separate.

## Tradeoffs

#4826 took the same approach and also matched the window title. This version leaves the title out, because the title is not what proves the pixels belong to the window: the process match, the scene epoch and the same-process sockets do. It also treats a toplevel stacked above the target as occluding only when that toplevel still draws a buffer. wlroots keeps an unmapped toplevel's scene root enabled, so the simpler check would refuse a window that is actually visible.

## Blast Radius

Only sessions with `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` set take the new path. Sway, GNOME, KWin, Hyprland, niri and X11 capture are unchanged. On cua-compositor, a window capture that cannot be proven still fails closed, just as it does today.

## Verification

- Headless cua-compositor built from this patch against wlroots 0.19, driven with the GTK3 fixture. Before the fix, `get_window_state` refused the screenshot with "no compositor-attested window geometry". After it returns a 560x757 PNG of only the fixture window. With a second fixture on top, capture is refused with `target-occluded`. With a window that maps on top and then hides, capture succeeds.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` passes, including eight new tests for the parser, the before/after bracket, bounds, ID-only resolution and same-process binding. `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets` is clean.
- The [cua-compositor E2E lane at this head](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43787393207) passes `e2e_environment_preflight_test` in the shared, native and capture lanes. [At main](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/43782695113) all three stopped there. The later cells that fail belong to the issues listed under Scope.

macOS and Windows checks do not apply to this Linux-only change.

Fixes #4825

title: fix(docs): sandbox install guide pins a version absent from PyPI
body:
## Primary area

Documentation.

## Summary

The deployed Python desktop guide instructs users to install an exact `cua-sandbox[driver]` version that is absent from PyPI. Following that pin fails dependency resolution before the desktop example can run; the agent-frameworks guide also advertises the unavailable version.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Python in the agent-frameworks guide's supported range (`>=3.11,<3.14`) and the uv version stated under Runtime or environment.
2. Read the [live desktop guide](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-sdk/guides/desktop.md), under “Typed Cua Driver,” and take its exact package requirement.
3. In an empty scratch directory, create a throwaway environment and dry-run that requirement against public PyPI:

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
uv pip install --dry-run --python .venv/bin/python --default-index https://pypi.org/simple 'cua-sandbox[driver]==0.11.7'
```

4. As an index and resolver control, dry-run the newest package version actually published on PyPI:

```bash
uv pip install --dry-run --python .venv/bin/python --default-index https://pypi.org/simple 'cua-sandbox[driver]==0.10.2'
```

These dry runs were executed in one fresh environment. They resolve packages without installing Cua or running any host setup.

## Expected behavior

The exact requirement in the deployed installation guide resolves from PyPI on a supported Python version. Public documentation should identify an installable release for the example, whether that is achieved through package publication or documentation changes.

## Actual behavior

The documented pin exits 1:

```text
error: No solution found when resolving dependencies
  cause: Because there is no version of cua-sandbox[driver]==0.11.7 and you require cua-sandbox[driver]==0.11.7, we can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.
```

The published-version control exits 0, resolves 43 packages, and reports “Would install 43 packages.” The PyPI JSON response has no entry for the documented version. This establishes an unavailable release rather than a failure caused by the optional Driver dependency or an unsupported Python interpreter. No desktop or agent recipe was executed.

## Runtime or environment

- Documentation source: default branch `main`, commit `3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0`; live desktop, agent-frameworks, and how-sandboxes-work Markdown pages independently checked.
- Current documented and source-package version: `cua-sandbox` 0.11.7.
- Latest published PyPI package: `cua-sandbox` 0.10.2.
- Resolver: uv 0.13.8, Python 3.12.15, Linux x86_64, public PyPI explicitly selected, fresh virtual environment, no project or user uv configuration.

## Evidence

- Expected source: the desktop guide's [install instruction](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/desktop.mdx#L112-L116), which matches the live desktop page; the [agent-frameworks source](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/agent-frameworks.mdx#L8-L13) also pins that package version.
- Failure source: the executed dry-run commands and their output above, corroborated by the [PyPI JSON API](https://pypi.org/pypi/cua-sandbox/json): `info.version` identifies the published-version control and `releases` lacks the documented version.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The [Sandbox release procedure](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#L121-L142) says preparing a release does not publish the package; publishing the resulting GitHub release triggers PyPI publication. A matching Git tag exists, but registry publication has not occurred. The latest observed successful `cd-py-sandbox.yml` run publishes the control version; no subsequent Sandbox publication run appears in the workflow history inspected. This report leaves the release-versus-documentation remedy to maintainers.

## Restoration check

Run the exact requirement shown in the deployed desktop installation guide against public PyPI in a fresh environment using a supported Python version. It must resolve successfully, including its Driver extra; merely changing the documentation to another unavailable version does not restore this contract. Verify that the agent-frameworks guide names an available package version too, and retain the published-version control to distinguish index/network failures.

## Workaround and additional context

Using the published-version control resolves the installation step today. Its compatibility with all current desktop and framework examples was not tested, so this is an installation workaround only.

## References

- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7234 — synchronizes documentation pins as part of Sandbox release preparation, which precedes package publication.
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7871 — advances the current Sandbox package and documentation pins; the PyPI resolution failure remains after this release PR merged.

## Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The documented installation deterministically fails in the tested supported environment before users can run the example; the scope is the pinned Python installation path.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: Selecting the published-version control resolves all dependencies in the same environment. This bypasses the install failure; compatibility of current examples with that older package remains untested.

title: [Bug]: Spaces first-run guides describe per-agent Connect buttons instead of default-selected agents
body:
## Summary

The Spaces install and agent-connection guides describe an older first-run flow in which each agent has a Connect button and stays untouched until that button is pressed. Current first run instead selects every detected coding agent by default, and Continue starts setup for every selected agent. A reader relying on the guides can therefore start changes to agents they did not intend to connect.

## Steps to reproduce

These are source-inspection steps, executed against both baselines below; the installed Spaces UI was not launched and no agent configurations were changed.

1. Read the live install guide's First run table and the agent-connection guide's Connect from the app section.
2. In each baseline, follow `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/routes/onboarding/index.tsx` to `NewFirstRun` and inspect `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/components/first-run-new/first-run-new.tsx` and `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/lib/first-run-new.ts`.
3. Trace a fresh run reaching the agent step with Claude Code and Codex installed, a working native adapter, and no saved `agentsOff` entries. The component obtains installed agents from `agents.setup`; `agentView` marks both picked and `chosenAgents` returns both without a row being clicked.
4. Trace the displayed Continue button to `continueAgent`, `connectPlan`, `runPart`, and `agents.connect`. Compare those operations with the guides' claimed need for a per-agent Connect action. This is static analysis; clicking Continue in a running native app was not performed.

## Expected behavior

The first-run guides should accurately describe the shipped controls, the initially selected agents, and the action that starts changes, so readers can leave unwanted agents' settings untouched. This report concerns the documentation mismatch, not a request to change the intentional default-selection design.

## Actual behavior

The live install guide says: "Press Connect on each one you want; nothing is connected until you do." The live agent-connection guide likewise says: "Nothing is connected until you press it." Both describe individual Connect buttons.

In both inspected source baselines, the screen instead renders selectable rows and a single Continue button. `agentsOff` initially defaults to `[]`; `picked: !off.includes(a.id)` selects all found agents. Continue calls `chosenAgents(found, agentsOff)` and executes the resulting checklist, with separate MCP and skills operations for each selected agent. The native bridge passes these through to agent setup; `connect_full` calls `configure_mcp` and `install_skills` for the requested parts. These are configuration-changing operations, not merely advancing the screen.

For a signed-in run, the checklist also starts with this computer's host setup. On macOS it requests the bundled Driver connection; supported agent sign-ins are requested separately and can require further action. This does not imply that every operation always succeeds or that sign-in completes without approval.

The Driver guide already describes the newer flow: agents are ticked and Continue connects them. Thus the guides disagree with each other as well as with the implementation. No runtime reproduction or actual unexpected writes were observed in this investigation.

## Runtime or environment

- Current default branch inspected: `main` at 3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0.
- Latest published Spaces release inspected: `cua-spaces-v0.36.24`, resolving to 19890ffc4eca25acf811e40572a3627013d91444. Its published app artifacts exist, and the canonical Linux update feed resolves version 0.36.24. The relevant first-run code and two Spaces guide files are identical between this release tag and the inspected default branch.
- Verification method: fresh source clone plus direct HTTPS retrieval of the deployed Markdown pages; no Spaces app installation, launch, host setup, or agent integration commands.
- The first-run UI is shared by the macOS, Linux and Windows hosts. Host-specific Driver work is macOS-only; host setup is conditional on sign-in.

## Evidence

- Expected source: The live [Spaces install guide](https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/guides/install.md), First run table, and [Connect your agent guide](https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/guides/connect-your-agent.md), Connect from the app section, promise a per-agent Connect action before connection.
- Failure source: The release-tagged first-run logic and component establish the contrary reachable flow; the native bridge and setup core establish the requested configuration changes, as located below.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Runtime reproduction was not run. The concrete valid trigger is a fresh native first run with installed detected agents, an available adapter, no saved deselections, and Continue pressed; the reachable default state, rendered control and handlers were inspected. The source call path is the primary failure evidence, and the deployed documentation text was fetched directly.

Source locators at the release tag:

- [Initial state, default selection, chosen agents, plan and operation arguments](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/apps/cua-spaces-web/src/lib/first-run-new.ts#L302-L441): `agentView`, `chosenAgents`, `connectPlan`, `connectArgs`.
- [Agent screen and Continue control](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/apps/cua-spaces-web/src/components/first-run-new/first-run-new.tsx#L468-L539): rows toggle selection; Continue invokes `onContinue`.
- [Detection, empty deselection default and execution path](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/apps/cua-spaces-web/src/components/first-run-new/first-run-new.tsx#L1040-L1161): installed-agent filtering, `agentsOff`, `runThisComputer`, `runPart`, `continueAgent`.
- [Native Electron bridge](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/apps/cua-spaces-desktop/src/bridge/agents.ts#L124-L128) and [configuration-changing setup implementation](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/libs/cua/crates/cua-agent-setup/src/connection.rs#L1081-L1127).
- [Driver guide](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-driver/guides/cua-spaces.md), installation step 4, already documents ticked agents and Continue.

## Restoration check

Read the two Spaces guides alongside a fresh first-run agent screen and its implementation. The documented controls, initial selections, operation trigger and way to leave agents untouched should agree. If Continue still starts setup for all selected agents, the guides must not promise that a separate per-agent Connect button is required. Keep later Settings connection instructions distinguishable from first run.

## Workaround and additional context

Source inspection shows that unticking unwanted agents excludes them from `chosenAgents`; Choose later, or unticking every agent, skips agent connection. These paths were not exercised in a running native app. The intended select-all behavior is recorded in the merged setup change below; correcting the stale guides can resolve this issue without changing that design.

Primary area: Documentation.

Submission checks: searched duplicate issues and active pull requests; this report covers one documentation mismatch; credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots and vulnerability details have been removed.

## References
