title: fix(cua-cli): release archives omit the gateway required for networked VZ microVMs
body:
## Summary

The standalone CLI release does not include `cua-netgw`, so a networked VZ microVM cannot be created on an Apple Silicon Mac without a separately built gateway. The archive includes `cua-vz` and the static guest init, but the create exits with the missing-gateway error before starting a VM.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On an Apple Silicon Mac with no separately installed `cua-netgw`, extract the standalone Darwin ARM64 CLI archive from the SDK release listed below. Verify it against the release's `checksums.txt` and inspect its members with `tar -tzf`.
2. From the extracted directory, use an empty scratch home and the default secure network mode. Run the following commands; these were executed with the released binary. The image is the small public Alpine container image, booted as a microVM rather than a desktop VM.

```sh
probe_home=$(mktemp -d)
export HOME="$probe_home" CUA_HOME="$probe_home/.cua"
export CUA_TELEMETRY=0 CUA_DRIVER_RS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=0
unset CUA_NETGW CUA_VZ CUA_MICROVM_INIT CUA_DAEMON CUA_SECURE_DEFAULT
./cua sb create alpine:3.22 --kind microvm --runtime vz --embedded \
  --name gateway-probe --network default --no-spacesd \
  --cpu 1 --memory 512MB -- /bin/sleep 300
```

3. Observe exit status 1 and the error below. `./cua sb ls --embedded --json` returns `[]` after this failed create. Remove the scratch home and extracted release files afterward.

## Expected behavior

The standalone release supplies the gateway it requires to create a networked VZ microVM, as the documentation and installer describe. A clean CLI installation should not require building an additional binary from the source repository to use this engine with its default network.

## Actual behavior

The standalone Darwin ARM64 archive contains exactly:

```text
cua
cua-vz
cua-microvm-init
cua-spacesd-linux-aarch64
```

The create fails with exit status 1:

```text
cua: local runtime: [local] cua-netgw is not available: the network gateway ships next to `cua`; set CUA_NETGW to its path or put it in ~/.cua/bin (libs/cua/netgw/build.sh builds it)
```

`cua runtime doctor --json` separately reports the bundled VZ monitor, a static guest init and a supported host, but `vz.gateway` is `null`; its VZ backend's only missing item is ``cua-netgw, the network gateway (ships next to `cua`)``.

Archive inspection found no `cua-netgw` or `cua-netgw.exe` in any of these distributions. Every inspected archive or wheel passed SHA-256 verification against the release checksum file or PyPI file metadata:

| Distribution | Platforms inspected | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone CLI archives, `cua-cli-*` | Darwin ARM64/x64, Linux ARM64/x64, Windows ARM64/x64 | Missing in all six |
| SDK native archives, `cua-*` | Darwin ARM64/x64, Linux ARM64/x64 GNU, Windows ARM64/x64 MSVC | Missing in all six |
| PyPI `cua` wheels | macOS ARM64/x86_64, Linux aarch64/x86_64, Windows ARM64/amd64 | Missing in all six |
| PyPI `cua-cli` wheels | macOS ARM64/x86_64, Linux aarch64/x86_64, Windows ARM64/amd64 | Missing in all six |

Only the standalone Darwin ARM64 create was executed. The other results are package-content observations, not runtime failure claims for those platforms. A read-only listing of an installed macOS ARM64 uv-tool environment also found no gateway in either package.

## Runtime or environment

- SDK/CLI GitHub release: `cua-sdk-v0.27.7`; the downloaded binary reports `cua 0.27.7`.
- PyPI and installed uv-tool packages: `cua==0.25.2`, `cua-cli==0.25.2`; these were the current PyPI versions when inspected.
- Runtime host: macOS 27.2.1, Apple Silicon/aarch64; no Cua Spaces app or separate gateway installation; scratch `HOME` and `CUA_HOME`, telemetry disabled, embedded runtime, default secure network mode.
- Source inspected: default branch `main` at `3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0`.
- Primary area: Build, packaging, or release.

## Evidence

- Expected source: [Egress guide, VM tree networking](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/egress.mdx#L98-L104) says the gateway ships next to `cua`; the [CLI installer](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/scripts/install/install.sh#L1205-L1215) likewise expects the gateway as a CLI companion.
- Failure source: Direct SHA-256-verified [release archive](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-sdk-v0.27.7) listings and the released-binary create output quoted above. The [SDK release build/package workflow](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/.github/workflows/cd-cua-sdk.yml#L231-L285) builds the CLI, monitor and init, but contains no gateway build; its standalone companion list at lines 733–750 also omits the gateway.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

One create was attempted and failed, and the subsequent sandbox listing was empty. Current-source inspection separately corroborates the dependency and packaging omission.

The [gateway lookup](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/netgw.rs#L62-L100) checks `CUA_NETGW`, the running executable's directory, the `CUA_VZ` directory, the Cua home `bin` directory and `PATH`; it does not download the gateway. The [VZ start path](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/microvm/mod.rs#L1887-L1902) requires that lookup for a networked guest in secure mode. This report concerns a refused create and missing release dependency, not an egress-policy bypass.

## Restoration check

On a clean Apple Silicon Mac installation of the standalone CLI, repeat the same networked Alpine VZ create without a separately built gateway. The release must provide or obtain its required gateway, the create must get past the missing-gateway failure, and the guest must start with its default network policy enforced. Merely suppressing the error or disabling the secure network default does not restore the contract. Remove the created VM and its scratch files after verification.

## Workaround and additional context

The error suggests building `libs/cua/netgw/build.sh` and setting `CUA_NETGW`; that source-build workaround was not tested. Disabling the secure network default was not attempted. This report makes no claim about the Spaces app bundle, which has a separate gateway build path.

## References

- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6071 — closed implementation history explicitly intended the gateway to ship in the CLI tarballs; the current released archive still lacks it. The closure says work moved elsewhere, rather than declining this packaging requirement.
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6422 — merged fix installs Go for the Spaces app release build; it changes the app's build script and does not cover the standalone CLI/SDK release workflow.

- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6733 — merged local-app build fix acknowledges that a missing gateway refuses child VM creation and adds it to `install-local.sh`; it does not cover the published standalone archives.

## Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: A clean standalone CLI installation reproducibly cannot create a networked VZ microVM because a required release companion is absent. The observed failure is bounded to this selected engine and installation condition; runtime reach beyond the tested macOS path is not established.
- Workaround status: unverified
- Workaround basis: The error documents a separate source build and `CUA_NETGW` override, but that workaround was not executed; availability of a prebuilt standalone gateway was not established.

title: fix(docs): child Space cleanup example uses a refused command
body:
## Summary

The Child Spaces guide tells an agent inside a Space to remove its newly created child with `cua spaces rm worker`. That command cannot delete the child on the scoped spawn channel: the CLI calls registration removal, and the scoped service denies that operation. Following the example leaves the child allocated instead of completing the documented cleanup.

## Steps to reproduce

These are source-inspection steps, executed against the baselines below. No live Space was created and runtime reproduction was not run.

1. Read “Inside the Space” in the live [Child Spaces guide](https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/guides/child-spaces.md). It shows this sequence inside a parent Space with children enabled:

```sh
cua spaces create linux --name worker
cua spaces ls
cua sb exec worker -- make test
cua spaces rm worker
```

2. For a successfully created child named `worker`, trace `Command::Spaces(Rm)` through `open` and `host::run_spaces_sdk`.
3. `open` selects the parent's scoped spawn channel. `Rm` resolves the child and either refuses it in `rm_refusal` or reaches `Spaces::remove`, which calls the channel's `SpaceService.RemoveSpace`.
4. Inspect `children::api::Scoped::remove_space`: it unconditionally calls `deny()`, returning permission denied. It does not delete the child. Compare with the supported scoped `delete_space` handler.

## Expected behavior

The inside-Space cleanup example uses an operation allowed by the child-management channel that actually deletes the child and releases its allocated resources. The guide itself advertises deletion and lists `delete_space` among the tools available inside a Space.

## Actual behavior

Static proof establishes that the documented `rm` operation cannot perform cleanup in the documented context. The host CLI's local-sandbox refusal is not the only relevant path: even when that guard does not fire in the guest, the final scoped `RemoveSpace` RPC is always denied. Its error text is built as “a Space can only create, list and manage its own children; ask the owner to do this outside the Space”. This is source-derived text, not captured runtime output.

The scoped API separately implements `DeleteSpace` by resolving the child and calling `delete_tree`. Thus the documented situation has a supported deletion path, but the example selects registration removal instead.

## Runtime or environment

- Default branch inspected: `main` at 5ee5974492839bb3b5a3db8919e3cf517e23ffe3.
- Latest published CLI/SDK source inspected: `cua-sdk-v0.27.7`; latest published Spaces app and guide baseline: `cua-spaces-v0.36.24`.
- The cited CLI routing, SDK removal, scoped API handlers and guide example are unchanged between these release tags and the inspected default branch.
- Valid trigger: a parent Space with children enabled and an established spawn channel, a successfully created and resolvable child named `worker`, and the guide's final command run inside the parent. No app launch, sign-in or runtime child creation was performed.

## Evidence

- Expected source: The guide's introduction promises that an agent inside a Space can create, use and delete children; its [inside-Space example](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/docs/content/docs/spaces/guides/child-spaces.mdx#L40-L55) selects `rm` as the cleanup step.
- Failure source: The release's scoped removal handler unconditionally denies the operation, as detailed in the call path below.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Runtime reproduction was not run. The concrete valid trigger and every relevant routing premise are stated above. Source call path:

- [CLI spawn-channel selection](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/lib.rs#L1265-L1272) connects to the scoped parent service; [command dispatch](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/lib.rs#L1890-L1966) sends `Rm` to `run_spaces_sdk`.
- [CLI removal branch](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/host.rs#L1248-L1268) resolves the child, applies `rm_refusal`, then calls `spaces.remove` if not refused.
- [SDK removal](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-sdk/src/native/spaces.rs#L4230-L4249) sends `RemoveSpace` in daemon mode.
- [Scoped service routing](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/children/mod.rs#L248-L263) installs the scoped `SpaceService`; [removal handler](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/children/api.rs#L925-L927) always denies it. The [deny helper](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/children/api.rs#L53-L61) constructs the refusal.
- [Scoped deletion](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/children/api.rs#L1086-L1093) is implemented, unlike registration removal.

## Restoration check

Inside a parent Space with children enabled, create a disposable child, follow the corrected cleanup instruction, and confirm that the child leaves the parent's list and its sandbox resources are released. Keep the parent's scope restrictions intact: the correction should not require allowing registration removal or access to unrelated Spaces.

## Workaround and additional context

Primary area: Documentation.

Submission checks: searched open and closed issues and pull requests; this report describes one problem; credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots and vulnerability details have been removed.

The existing deletion command is `cua spaces delete worker` with interactive confirmation; automated non-terminal use requires `--force`. The [CLI deletion branch](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/host.rs#L1934-L1969) calls `delete_tree` after confirmation. This workaround is supported by source inspection, not a live guest run.

## References

- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6072 — closed in favor of work elsewhere; its original description claimed inside-Space `rm` support, but the current scoped removal handler refuses the operation.
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6733 — fixed separate child-tool risk classification and inside-Space sandbox-create errors, and reports successful `cua spaces delete --force`; the guide's remaining `rm` example is the distinct documentation defect here.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: Following the documented lifecycle example cannot clean up the child and leaves its sandbox allocated; the reachable refusal is established statically, without measuring live resource use.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The existing CLI deletion branch and scoped DeleteSpace handler provide the intended cleanup; noninteractive callers use --force. This availability was verified from source only.

title: fix(docs): legacy Hotspot URL redirects to a missing anchor
body:
## Summary

The legacy Spaces Hotspot reference redirects to an anchor absent from its destination page. Readers following the old URL land on the general Spaces reference instead of the Hotspot documentation.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Request the legacy public URL:

```sh
curl -sI https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/reference/hotspot
```

2. Read the returned `Location` and fetch its target page. Inspect that page's rendered HTML for an element whose `id` is `hotspot`.
3. Fetch the current [Sharing, hotspot and cloud tools reference](https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/reference/sharing-and-clouds) and inspect its Hotspot heading.

## Expected behavior

The old reference URL takes readers to the current Hotspot section through a redirect whose fragment exists on the target page.

## Actual behavior

The executed HEAD request returns:

```text
HTTP/2 301
location: /docs/spaces/reference/spaces#hotspot
```

The fetched target HTML contains no `id="hotspot"`. The Sharing, hotspot and cloud tools HTML does contain `id="hotspot"`, followed by `hotspot_start`, `hotspot_stop` and `hotspot_status`. The Markdown versions agree: the general Spaces reference has no Hotspot heading, while the sharing reference does.

- The deployed documentation was fetched directly over HTTPS, including the redirect response and rendered target HTML. No Spaces app, host or hotspot command was run; application version and desktop platform do not affect this public documentation failure.

## Evidence

- Expected source: The legacy URL identifies the Hotspot reference; the current sharing reference contains the Hotspot section and its tools.
- Failure source: The observed HTTP response redirects to a nonexistent target fragment. The [redirect entry](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/docs/content/docs/redirects.json#L628) matches the deployed result; the [current section](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/docs/content/docs/spaces/reference/sharing-and-clouds.mdx#L12-L20) lives on another page.

- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

## Restoration check

Repeat the HEAD request, fetch its resolved target and verify that the target fragment names an existing Hotspot section. Following the legacy URL should reach the Hotspot reference directly rather than the top of the Spaces page.

## Workaround and additional context

Primary area: Documentation.

Submission checks: searched open and closed issues and pull requests; this report describes one problem; credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots and vulnerability details have been removed.

## Triage assessment

title: fix(docs): agent connection guide understates the Spaces MCP tool count
body:
## Summary

The Connect your agent guide says the cua MCP server gives an agent “33 Spaces tools”. The released CLI advertises 118 agent-accessible Spaces tools, with all permissions enabled by default. The documented number is stale rather than a documented default subset.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Read “What your agent can do” in the live [Connect your agent guide](https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/guides/connect-your-agent.md), which says “33 Spaces tools plus sandbox and computer tools”.
2. Run the released CLI's read-only documentation export:

```sh
cua dump-docs --type mcp > mcp.json
python3 -c 'import json; d=json.load(open("mcp.json")); print(sum(t["group"] == "spaces" for t in d["tools"]))'
```

3. Compare with `cua mcp --help`, which states that the default permissions are all, and with the permission parser and tool-list source cited below. No MCP server, daemon, app or sign-in needs to be started.

## Expected behavior

The agent connection guide describes the current MCP tool surface accurately. If a count refers to a restricted subset, it identifies that subset and its enabling configuration.

## Actual behavior

The export command exits 0 and the count prints `118`. It contains 179 total tools across groups. The CLI help says `--permissions` defaults to all. Source expands empty/default permissions to all non-person-only contract tools; the server enumerates those allowed tools rather than selecting 33.

The [Spaces reference index](https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/reference/index.md) names 122 tools in the contract. That total includes four person-only tools (`cloud_approve`, `agent_threads`, `agent_thread_read`, `agent_sign_in`) that agents do not receive. Thus neither the full contract total nor the agent-accessible count supports the guide's number. This report does not ask to expose person-only tools to agents.

## Runtime or environment

- Default branch inspected: `main` at 5ee5974492839bb3b5a3db8919e3cf517e23ffe3.
- Latest published CLI/SDK inspected and executed: `cua-sdk-v0.27.7`; checksum-verified official Linux x64 CLI archive reporting `cua 0.27.7`, using isolated `HOME` and `CUA_HOME` with telemetry disabled.
- Latest published Spaces app and guide baseline: `cua-spaces-v0.36.24`. The relevant guide, MCP default permission logic and contract tool filtering are unchanged between the release tags and the inspected default branch.
- The export and help commands were run; no live MCP handshake or Spaces app was run.

## Evidence

- Expected source: The guide explicitly describes what an agent receives from the cua MCP server, and the CLI help documents all permissions as the default.
- Failure source: The guide's [tool-count sentence](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-spaces-v0.36.24/docs/content/docs/spaces/guides/connect-your-agent.mdx#L184-L188) says 33; the executed release export contains 118 group=`spaces` tools.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The [agent setup defaults](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-agent-setup/src/lib.rs#L398-L406) launch `cua mcp` without a restricted permission list. The source corroborates the export: [permission expansion](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/mcp.rs#L32-L42) excludes only person-only tools when building Spaces permissions; [default groups](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/mcp.rs#L86-L116) expand to all; [server exposure and enumeration](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/mcp/mod.rs#L276-L293) list the filtered contract. The [four person-only names](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/cua-sdk-v0.27.7/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces-contract/src/lib.rs#L2294-L2302) explain the difference from the full contract count.

## Restoration check

Compare the guide with the current released CLI export, default permission policy and contract's person-only exclusions. Its description should match the current agent-accessible surface or avoid a fixed count. Restricted permission configurations must remain distinguishable from the default, and person-only tools must remain excluded.

## Workaround and additional context

Primary area: Documentation.

Submission checks: searched open and closed issues and pull requests; this report describes one problem; credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots and vulnerability details have been removed.

Readers can use the export and reference index to inspect the current tools, taking account of the person-only exclusions.

## References

- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7141 — closed as superseded by the following test change; it identifies the contract's growth to 122 but does not address this guide's older number.
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7142 — derives binding-test tool sets from the manifest; the agent connection guide's fixed count remains a separate documentation issue.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P3
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The guide understates the available tool surface; no failure in tool execution or consequential behavior change was observed.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The released read-only documentation export enumerates the agent-accessible tools and the reference lists the contract.

title: fix(docs): Cloud migration guide says the current local --pool flag was removed
body:
## Primary area

Documentation.

## Summary

The Cua Cloud migration guide lists `--pool` without qualification among features removed from the `cua` CLI. The current standalone CLI and sandbox reference expose `cua sb create --pool NAME` for local ready pools, so the blanket removal statement obscures a supported local capability.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Read the live [Cua Cloud migration guide](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-sdk/guides/cua-cloud-ended.md), under “In your code,” especially the list of removed SDK/CLI features.
2. With the standalone release listed under Runtime or environment, run these read-only commands:

```bash
cua sb create --help
cua sb pool --help
```

3. Compare the removal statement with the [sandbox reference](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-cli/reference/cli/sandboxes.md), which describes `cua sb create --pool NAME` and the local pool commands.

## Expected behavior

The migration guide distinguishes the removed hosted Fleet pool interface from the currently supported local `cua sb create --pool NAME` flag and `cua sb pool` commands. Readers should be able to tell which pool functionality remains available.

## Actual behavior

The live guide says that `Cua.fleet()`, `cua fleet`, `cua pools`, `--pool`, `FLEETS_TOKEN` and other cloud features “are removed from the SDKs and the `cua` CLI.” It does not qualify the removed flag or distinguish its local namesake. Both help commands exit 0; create help lists:

```text
--pool <POOL>
    Create from this pool (`cua sb pool create`): the sandbox gets the pool's image and size and takes one of its ready ones in about 0.1 s
```

Pool help describes local pools and lists create, ls and rm subcommands. No pool was created; this is a documentation-scope disagreement with the exposed current CLI interface, not a claim about pool runtime performance.

## Runtime or environment

- Documentation source: default branch `main`, commit `3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0`; both live Markdown pages were fetched independently and carry the described statements.
- CLI: `cua-sdk-v0.27.7`, checksum-verified `cua-cli-0.27.7-linux-x64.tar.gz`, executable reports `cua 0.27.7`, Linux x86_64, isolated scratch home, telemetry disabled and external networking unavailable.

## Evidence

- Failure source: the [unqualified removal statement](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/cua-cloud-ended.mdx#L32-L34), also present in the live migration guide.
- Evidence provenance: observed

## Workaround and additional context

title: fix(cli): network none help still says containers reject it under the secure default
body:
## Primary area

Documentation.

## Summary

`cua sb create --help` says containers reject `--network none`. The current container admission path explicitly accepts that restriction under the default Secure network mode and maps it to the `none` network settings, so the unconditional help statement describes only the legacy case.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `cua sb create --help` with the checksum-verified standalone binary listed under Runtime or environment. It exits 0 and prints the quoted restriction below.
2. Inspect the same release's source path from the CLI network option through `NetworkMode::None`, `StartSpec`, and the container admission guard described under Evidence. Leave `CUA_SECURE_DEFAULT` unset, which selects Secure mode.
3. Compare the help with the documented `none` preset and the source's Secure-mode exception for containers.

The help command was executed. No container creation, container-engine command, egress probe or source build was executed; the runtime applicability below is established by source inspection rather than a container boot.

## Expected behavior

The flag's help and generated CLI reference describe the current conditional support: containers accept the no-egress restriction under Secure mode, while the legacy mode rejects that container setting. Documentation should not unconditionally rule out containers when the admission guard explicitly permits them in the default mode.

## Actual behavior

The released help and live [sandbox reference](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-cli/reference/cli/sandboxes.md) say:

```text
Guest network: `default` (outbound network, like a Docker container) or `none` (no egress; published ports still work). `none` needs a local QEMU VM; containers and Lume reject it
```

In source, `reject_restricted_network` returns `Ok(())` for the Container backend in Secure mode even when `spec.restrict_network` is true. The source also contains a test asserting that acceptance. The [network guide](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-sdk/guides/egress.md) documents the `none` preset and container enforcement. This report concerns the stale container rejection claim; it does not infer support for other runtimes from the container exception.

## Runtime or environment

- Default branch inspected: `main`, commit `3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0`.
- Release: `cua-sdk-v0.27.7`, `cua-cli-0.27.7-linux-x64.tar.gz`; archive SHA-256 verified against the release checksum manifest, binary reports `cua 0.27.7`, Linux x86_64.
- The cited CLI, sandbox-core and VMM files are unchanged between the release tag and the inspected default branch. Help ran with an isolated scratch home, telemetry disabled and no external networking. The source analysis assumes the default Secure mode, with `CUA_SECURE_DEFAULT` unset.

## Evidence

- Expected source: the [container admission guard](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/types.rs#L509-L533) explicitly accepts Container in Secure mode, which is selected by [the default mode parser](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/network.rs#L954-L970); the [container start path](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/container/mod.rs#L1242-L1246) calls that guard.
- Failure source: the observed release help and its [source text](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/sandbox.rs#L163-L167), also rendered in the live sandbox reference.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The concrete supported input is `cua sb create linux --on local --runtime runc --network none --name network-check` on an otherwise ready container host in Secure mode, without durable/reuse or unrelated options. This creation command was not run. The [CLI copies the flag into create options](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-cli/src/sandbox.rs#L1985-L1988); [daemon option conversion parses it](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon-core/src/runtime.rs#L2015-L2017); [sandbox-core produces a restricted StartSpec with effective network settings](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-sandbox-core/src/sandbox.rs#L1221-L1228); and [legacy-none mapping selects the none preset](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/network.rs#L456-L480). The [existing source test](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/types.rs#L982-L1002) also distinguishes Lume rejection from default-mode container acceptance. It was read, not executed. Successful creation still requires an otherwise ready host; this report makes no claim that those prerequisites were exercised.

## Restoration check

Compare the released help and generated reference with the actual container admission modes. They must distinguish default Secure-mode container support from legacy-mode rejection. A container integration check can separately verify that a created `none` sandbox cannot egress while Cua's published-port control path remains usable; that boot/enforcement check was not run here.

## Workaround and additional context

The network guide describes the supported `none` preset, and the source makes the mode-dependent distinction explicit. No runtime workaround was tested.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.

- Impact basis: User-facing help incorrectly rules out a supported default-mode container setting; no container creation or network enforcement failure was observed.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The network guide documents the none preset and the source identifies its mode-dependent container support; this addresses the documentation discrepancy, not an observed runtime failure.

title: fix(docs): scope the English-only browser setup warning by platform
body:
## Summary

The existing-profile browser guide says setup recognizes English UI labels only across its supported platform list. That warning is accurate for the remaining macOS setup matchers, but overstates the restriction on Windows and Linux: Windows setup uses structural UIA matching, and Linux accepts localized native browser controls while its internal setup page retains English labels.

## Primary area

Documentation

## Steps to reproduce

1. Read the existing-profile setup paragraph in the [live browser guide](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-driver/guides/browsers.md), immediately after its supported-platform list.
2. Compare it with the Windows and Linux setup matchers and their localized-control test fixtures at the baseline below. Compare macOS separately so the remaining limitation is preserved.
3. Observe that the warning has no platform qualification despite the different matching contracts. These document and source inspection steps were performed; native localized browser preparation was not rerun.

## Expected behavior

The guide should describe each platform's current setup limitation. Windows setup does not require English accessible names. Linux native controls and consent can be localized, while the internal setup heading and checkbox are still matched by their English strings. The remaining macOS setup dependence on English native labels should remain explicit.

## Actual behavior

The guide states: “Setup recognizes English UI labels only.” Windows finds native controls and the renderer-owned toggle by structure, actions, exact URL, and uniqueness rather than English names. Its regression fixture replaces all setup labels with non-English names and still matches the toggle. Linux identifies the omnibox structurally and proves the setup page from its AT-SPI document URI; its German-UI fixture has a localized omnibox and an English internal page. macOS still requires `Address and search bar` and other English setup labels. The unqualified warning hides these distinctions.

## Runtime or environment

- Default branch inspected in a fresh clone: `main` at `3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0`.
- Latest published non-nightly Driver component: `cua-driver-rs-v0.52.3`, target `e7d713b28f7a8f7102cf7b15f567efb46f300beb`. The relevant documentation and source files are identical between the release tag and inspected default branch.
- This is a documentation/source comparison. No desktop automation or installation was performed.

## Evidence

- Expected source: [Windows setup contract and structural selectors](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/browser_setup_ui.rs#L25-L98), including `checkbox_requires_exact_internal_url_and_unique_web_toggle` at lines 836–861 and `native_address_control_is_language_independent_without_trusting_web_content` at line 946; [Linux native-field and document-URI matching](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/browser_setup_ui.rs#L37-L128), including the German-UI fixture and `document_uri_proves_the_setup_page_behind_a_localized_omnibox` at lines 870–906.
- Failure source: [Guide's unqualified English-only warning](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/browsers.mdx#L205-L207), also observed on the live page.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The reproduced failure is the documentation mismatch, not a claim that a localized browser failed at runtime. [The macOS setup matcher](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/3f1661d00f382145720dea568ccde58b993fc0f0/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/browser/setup_ui.rs#L137-L164) still checks English names, so removing every language caveat would also be inaccurate. The platform implementations and test fixtures were inspected, not executed.

## Restoration check

Read the same paragraph and compare it with all three platform implementations. The Windows and Linux setup capabilities must no longer be described as universally English-only, and the remaining macOS and Linux internal-page constraints must remain accurately scoped. No browser behavior or permission change is requested.

## Workaround and additional context

Consult the platform source and merged localization work to distinguish supported localized native controls from remaining label requirements. This report concerns the documentation warning, not a request to redo localization or change supported browser topology.

## References

- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3135 — landed the Windows language-independent setup contract; that behavior is present in the inspected release and source.
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7587 — landed localized Linux native-control and consent matching while intentionally retaining English internal-page labels.
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/3139 — covers the still-open macOS implementation limitation; fixing that implementation is distinct from accurately documenting the other platforms now.

body:
## Summary

The Driver quickstart restricts its Linux prerequisite to x86_64 even though the canonical installer explicitly accepts Linux ARM64 and the current component release ships native ARM64 Driver and Python SDK artifacts. 2. Inspect the canonical [Unix installer](https://cua.ai/driver/_install-rust.sh): its architecture selection accepts `Linux-aarch64|Linux-arm64` and selects `linux-arm64` with Rust target `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11: after the background (MPX) input route runs, Google Chrome ignores all keyboard input until the CUA master pair is removed
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, once the driver's background input route has run (`path=mpx_uinput` or `mpx_pointer`) for **any** app, Google Chrome ignores all keyboard input: driver keys with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, and `xdotool` keys too. A `CUA v1.…` XInput2 master pointer/keyboard pair stays in the server's device hierarchy after the action and after the MCP connection closes. Removing that pair with `xinput remove-master` restores Chrome's keyboard at once. Relaunching Chrome does not; restarting the X session does.

### Reproduction

1. Start an X11 session (XFCE, no compositor) with `/dev/uinput` writable, so the MPX route is available.
2. Launch Google Chrome (`--no-first-run`) and focus its address bar. `xdotool key ctrl+l; xdotool type example.org; xdotool key Return` navigates, and `xinput list` shows only the core devices.
3. Through the driver, do one background keyboard action on another app, for example `type_text {"pid": <gnome-calculator>, "window_id": …, "text": "7"}`. It reports `path=mpx_uinput`.
4. `xinput list` now shows `CUA v1.<id> pointer` / `CUA v1.<id> keyboard` masters, with their XTEST slaves, even after the MCP connection is closed.
5. Repeat step 2's keys, either with `xdotool` or with the driver's `hotkey` / `type_text` and `delivery_mode: "foreground"`. Chrome does nothing: no navigation, and Ctrl+T doesn't open a tab.
6. `xinput remove-master <CUA pointer id>`, then repeat step 2: it works again.

A single background pixel `click` on Chrome (`path=mpx_pointer`) has the same effect. Accessibility-action clicks (`x11_atspi`) do not.

### Expected behavior

Using the background route for one app doesn't change how other apps receive keyboard input. The master pair is torn down after the delivery, as `input/mpx_keyboard.rs` describes ("the pair is torn down again so a non-MPX-aware WM never sees a lingering foreign master"), and at the latest when the session ends.

### Actual behavior

The pair stays. While it exists, Chrome (157, X11) ignores the core keyboard. Firefox and GTK apps are unaffected.

After the pair is removed externally, the same driver session's next `mpx_uinput` `type_text` fails with "virtual master keyboard could not take focus on window …" until the client reconnects.

### Environment

- cua-driver-rs 0.52.1, linux-arm64
- Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS arm64 VM; Xorg 21.1.12 (xserver-xorg-core 2:21.1.12-1ubuntu1.9); XFCE 4.18, xfwm4 4.18.0, compositing off
- Google Chrome 157.0.8103.78 (official arm64 .deb); for comparison, Firefox 160 and GNOME Calculator
- at-spi2-core 2.52.0, GTK 3.24.41

### Evidence

`xinput list --short` after step 3:

```
⎡ Virtual core pointer                    	id=2	[master pointer  (3)]
...
⎡ CUA v1.<id> pointer	id=10	[master pointer  (11)]
⎜   ↳ CUA v1.<id> XTEST pointer	id=12	[slave  pointer  (10)]
⎣ CUA v1.<id> keyboard	id=11	[master keyboard (10)]
    ↳ CUA v1.<id> XTEST keyboard	id=13	[slave  keyboard (11)]
```

Reproduced in three separate sessions: fresh session OK, then broken after one background action, then fixed by `remove-master`.

### Workaround and additional context

Remove `CUA v1.*` masters (`xinput remove-master`) before Chrome needs the keyboard, and send input aimed at Chrome in the foreground. Background input into Chrome itself also doesn't land: `type_text` via `mpx_uinput` reports "Typed N characters" but the field stays empty.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Linux: invoke_menu that opens a modal GTK 3 dialog (Mousepad Save As) leaves the app unresponsive to AT-SPI
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux, `invoke_menu` on a menu item that opens a modal GTK 3 file dialog leaves the app unresponsive to AT-SPI. The case seen is Mousepad's File → Save As…. The dialog appears, but every later accessibility read of the app reports `atspi_app_unresponsive`, and the app has to be killed. Opening the same dialog with its keyboard shortcut works.

### Reproduction

1. Launch Mousepad 0.6.1 and type some text.
2. `invoke_menu {"pid": …, "window_id": …, "path": ["File", "Save As..."]}`. It returns with `effect: "unverifiable"`, and the Save As window appears in `list_windows`.
3. `get_window_state` on the dialog (or the main window), even with `timeout_ms: 6000`.

### Expected behavior

The dialog's tree is readable (for example, the name field for `set_value`), as it is when the dialog was opened another way.

### Actual behavior

`degraded: true`, `degraded_reason: "atspi_app_unresponsive: the application is registered with AT-SPI but did not answer GetChildren…"`, one element. The app's threads sit in `futex_wait_queue`. It never recovers; `kill_app` was needed.

A background `hotkey ["ctrl","s"]` or `["ctrl","shift","s"]` opens a dialog whose tree reads normally (3/3 trials each; `invoke_menu` gave 3/3 unresponsive). LibreOffice Writer's File → Save As... via `invoke_menu` is fine. This looks like GTK running the modal dialog's nested main loop inside the AT-SPI action handler, so the action's reply, and every call after it, waits on the dialog.

### Environment

- cua-driver-rs 0.52.1, linux-arm64
- Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS arm64; Xorg 21.1.12; XFCE 4.18
- Mousepad 0.6.1, GTK 3.24.41, at-spi2-core 2.52.0

### Evidence

See the reproduction; consistent across fresh launches.

### Workaround and additional context

Open dialogs with the app's keyboard shortcut instead of `invoke_menu` in plain GTK 3 apps. If the driver can't avoid the block, `invoke_menu` could report it (for example a timeout or "action did not return") rather than leaving the app wedged.

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the GTK3 scroll viewport inside the default window
body:
## Why

On the nested cua-compositor, `linux-gtk3-scroll-px-foreground` aims at the GTK3 fixture's `scroll-tall-viewport`, which sits below the window's default 720 px of content. The compositor shows the window at its default height (560x757 with the header bar), and the target's top edge is at y=761. The scroll can't land on it. On main, the test's PX point lands on the outer scroller. With #7926's window geometry it falls outside the capture and the test refuses it. Sway sizes the window to 940x780 and X11 shows it at 560x720 with the target at y≈701, which is why the cell passes there and is flaky or fails on cua-compositor. This matches the issue's note that the command was aimed below the visible pane.

## What changed

- The GTK3 fixture puts the `scroll-tall` section before the context-menu section, so the scroll viewport sits inside the default window. Every section after it can still be reached through AT-SPI or the outer scroller.

## Scope

This is a fixture-layout change only. It does not touch the driver, the compositor or the test's effect oracle. On main alone the cell still fails, because AT-SPI reports the GTK3 frame with its client-side shadow (612x809), so the test's scale and offset are wrong. Open PR #7926 fixes that geometry. With both changes the cell passes. The background PX cells and the two desktop-lane AX cells that fail on cua-compositor are tracked separately (#4827, #4829).

## Blast Radius

The fixture is used only by the GTK3 E2E harness, the desktop-scope Linux tests and the jev-use GTK3 task window (a separate `TaskWindow` class that this change does not touch). Nothing looks up controls by section order. They find them by accessible name.

## Verification

- With #7926 applied, on a headless cua-compositor in the native lane: `harness_gtk3_scroll_px_foreground` fails at the old fixture with `outside the capture: rect=(12,761,536,34) capture=(560,757)` and passed 3 of 3 runs with this change.
- With #7926 applied, I ran the full GTK3 harness (43 cells) once with the old fixture and once with the new one. Only `linux-gtk3-scroll-px-foreground` changed outcome, from fail to pass. The 8 cells that fail on both sides are the 6 background PX cells and 2 desktop-lane cells.
- `git diff --check` and Python compile pass. X11, macOS and Windows lanes were not run. CI on main shows the X11 window at 560x720 with the target inside it.

Fixes #4832

title: cua-driver (macOS): GTK apps drop background clicks unless they first get an AppKit activation event
body:
## Problem

GTK apps on macOS, such as GnuCash, throw away posted mouse-downs while they believe they're inactive. In `gdk/quartz/gdkevents-quartz.c` (gtk-3-24), a mouse-down that arrives while `![NSApp isActive]` makes GDK call `[NSApp activateIgnoringOtherApps:YES]` and `return FALSE`, so the click is dropped. Posting the click to the pid doesn't help, and window-under-pointer fields don't either. Keys are routed through `[nsevent window]`, so they need a key window, and a background app doesn't have one.

When cua-driver posts background clicks and keys to GnuCash, the window doesn't change. The SkyLight focus records can make a window key, but they don't flip `NSApp isActive`. In the background, GnuCash can't be driven past its menu bar, which is all it exposes to AX.

## What worked (native APIs only, macOS 26 guest, GnuCash 5)

1. Post a native AppKit activation event to the target pid only: `NSEvent otherEventWithType:NSEventTypeAppKitDefined (13) … windowNumber:<target window> subtype:NSEventSubtypeApplicationActivated (1)`, then `CGEventPostToPid(pid, ev.CGEvent)`. The app's `AXFrontmost` turns true, and WindowServer's front app stays the user's.
2. Build each mouse event with `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:…windowNumber:<target window>…` and take its `.CGEvent`. Set the screen location, `CGEventSetWindowLocation`, and fields 91/92 (window under pointer) to the window id, then post it per pid. Plain `CGEventCreateMouseEvent` clicks were still dropped after the activation event. The NSEvent-built ones landed.
3. Undo it when done with the same event and subtype 2 (`ApplicationDeactivated`). `AXFrontmost` goes back to false.

With that, the following all landed while another app stayed frontmost: selecting a GnuCash account row, the Open toolbar button, typing into a register's Description cell, Return to commit the transaction (it shows up in GnuCash's own transaction log), and File > Save by AX (the saved book contains the new transaction). A bench sentinel window watching the user's focus recorded no front change, no key loss and no raised window.

Without the activation event, the same sequence raised GnuCash and took the user's focus, because GDK's `activateIgnoringOtherApps:` ran.

The same pre-event also opens LibreOffice Calc's key route on macOS. After the activation event and one NSEvent-built click to make the window key, arrow keys, typed text and Return posted per pid moved the cell cursor and wrote a cell, and an AX File > Save wrote it to the .ods. Without the event, Calc ignored the keys.

## Details seen

- The first click after the activation event makes the window key and doesn't reach the widget. Later clicks do.
- GTK sometimes shows the effect of an input event only once the next event arrives (for example, the register opened on the key that followed the Open click). A deterministic wrapper could post a harmless trailing event, or check the result after the next action.
- App dialogs (for example "Could not determine the account currency") appear as new untitled windows of the same pid. They take NSEvent-built clicks the same way.

## Proposal

cua-driver likely needs the same pre-event on macOS: before posting background clicks or keys to an app, post the AppKit activation event to that pid, and post the deactivation event when the action or session ends. Mouse events would be built as NSEvents with the window number. Where it goes (always on, per app, or opt-in) is a maintainer call.

title: fix(cua-driver): post background element keys to the control's own HWND on Windows
body:
## Why

On Windows, a background `press_key` with an `element_token` called UIA `SetFocus` on the element before posting the key. For a WinForms TextBox that activates the top-level window even while `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` is set. The background contract says the target is never activated, so restoring foreground afterwards does not make it safe. Background element keys now go straight to the control's own HWND, and an element with no HWND refuses before anything happens.

## What changed

- `press_key` (platform-windows): background element keys outside embedded WebView hosts read the element's `CurrentNativeWindowHandle`, check that it belongs to the pid and is the admitted window or its child, and post `WM_KEYDOWN`/`WM_KEYUP` (or the `WM_CHAR` Unicode fallback) to that exact HWND. There is no focus step. A windowless element, or a handle outside the admitted window, returns `background_unavailable` before the cursor moves or any input is sent. `wait_for_focused_descendant` lost its only caller and is deleted.
- A WinForms fixture (`--winforms-keyboard` mode of the WPF harness) with a target TextBox, a focused decoy TextBox and a windowless LinkLabel. It journals key receipts, focus transitions and `Activated` events.
- Three desktop E2E rows in `harness_wpf_test.rs`. A background F6 and a background Unicode key reach the exact control with no activation and no focus change. A windowless element refuses with no fixture change. A foreground F6 still reaches the exact control.

## Scope

Covers Windows background `press_key` with an `element_token`. Foreground delivery, the px form, untargeted background keys and the WebView2 focus-click route are unchanged. `type_text` and `hotkey` already avoid UIA focus on their background paths and are not touched. #4876's other changes (WebView2 harness geometry, testkit recording timeout, WPF accelerator rows, the UniFFI script) are not part of this fix and are left out.

## Tradeoffs

A background key to an element that has no HWND of its own, such as a windowless WPF or WinUI control, now refuses instead of reporting unverified success. WPF background keystrokes were already refused by `would_be_silently_dropped`, and no existing E2E cell sends such a key, so no current expectation changes. Callers get the usual escalation to `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.

## Blast Radius

Windows Cua Driver only. A native control that previously relied on the focus step to receive a posted key now gets the key directly at its own HWND, which is the window that would have held focus.

## Verification

- Windows crates cross-compiled with `cargo xwin check` and `cargo xwin clippy -D warnings` (platform-windows, cua-driver-e2e with tests). Both are clean.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) and the E2E inventory gate pass.
- Not run here: the three `harness_winforms_*` rows and the .NET fixture build need a Windows desktop. #4876 ran the same rows natively, with no activation and no focus change, against the same fixture and driver logic.

Salvaged from #4876
Fixes #4843

title: feat(cua-driver): background input for GTK 3 apps on macOS through the AppKit activation event
body:
## What

On macOS, background input now reaches GTK 3 apps (GnuCash, GIMP 2.10, Inkscape 1.x) without raising them or taking the user's focus. A WebKit form field that ignores an accessibility value write while it is unfocused now takes the write after the field is focused.

Fixes #7936

## Why

GDK's Quartz backend drops a mouse-down while `[NSApp isActive]` is false and calls `activateIgnoringOtherApps:` instead (`gdk/quartz/gdkevents-quartz.c`, gtk-3-24). A background click on GnuCash therefore raised it and took the user's focus, and its keys never reached a window. AppKit sets `NSApp.active` when it receives an `NSEventTypeAppKitDefined` event with subtype `ApplicationActivated`. Posting that event to the target pid makes the app active in its own eyes while WindowServer's front process stays the user's. Subtype `ApplicationDeactivated` undoes it. While the app is active, GDK takes mouse events built with `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:…windowNumber:` and converted with `.CGEvent`. Plain `CGEventCreateMouseEvent` events are still dropped.

## How

- `input/appkit_activation.rs` (new): `ActivationLease` posts the activation event to one pid, waits for `AXFrontmost` to confirm it, and refuses when it doesn't, so no input is sent that would make GDK raise the app. The lease is shared across a burst of actions. The deactivation event goes out once the target has been idle for 1.5 s, or straight away when another app is activated. `click()` posts a move and then counted down/up pairs as NSEvent-built events, with the screen location, `CGEventSetWindowLocation` and the window-under-pointer fields stamped, each posted per pid.
- `pointer_toolkit`: new `GdkQuartz`, detected from a mapped `libgdk-3*.dylib`.
- `pixel_route`: a background left click with no modifiers on `GdkQuartz` takes the new `BackgroundAppKitActivated` route (`path: "appkit_activated"`). Right and middle clicks and drags on it keep the `background_unavailable` refusal, because GDK activates itself on those presses.
- `key_scope` (press_key, hotkey, type_text, type_text_chars, Calc set_value): for a `GdkQuartz` target it takes the activation lease before making the window key, and the scope holds the lease until key is handed back.
- `set_value`: on WebKit web content (not Chromium or Electron), a write that reads back unapplied is retried once after `AXFocused` is set on the field. Focus moves inside the app only.
- `action_record`: the new route's `path: "appkit_activated"` is recorded as a pid-routed CGEvent.
- `type_text` is unchanged. GTK exposes no widgets to accessibility, so its focused element reads as the window, and `type_text` still refuses with `no_focused_text_input`, because a focused list and a focused entry look the same. `press_key` reaches the confirmed key window.

## Test plan

- Unit: route table (`gtk_left_clicks_take_the_activation_route_and_other_presses_refuse`), toolkit classification (`classifies_gtk3_gdk_and_not_its_siblings`), lease transitions and click plan (`appkit_activation::tests`).
- macOS guest, real app: GnuCash on its own book, driven through one MCP session of the built driver while a sentinel window holds the user's focus. Background pixel click on the Liabilities row and on the toolbar Open button, Return (the register opens), Tab, Tab, `press_key` per character, Return (commits; dismiss the currency dialog with Return), `invoke_menu` File > Save.
  - Result on this branch: the saved book contains the typed text. The sentinel recorded no front change, no key loss and no raised window, and the front app stayed the sentinel throughout.
  - Result on main with the same sequence: the book is unchanged and nothing was raised. The clicks were dropped.
- macOS guest, the verify-cua-driver macOS Lume lane, full matrix, at this head: passed.
- A paired agent run on macOS (this branch against main at the same base, every task in both conditions) showed no regression, with background gains on the WebKit form task. The GnuCash task still fails on both builds; see the follow-up below.

## Follow-up

GTK often repaints only when the next event arrives, so a background click that worked can look like it changed nothing in the screenshot that follows. Agents then give up on it. A post-click flush or a re-read after the next input is the next step.
- Linux and Windows are untouched by this diff.

title: fix(cua-driver): post background element keys to the exact control HWND
body:
Salvaged from #4876

Fixes #4843

## Why

On Windows, `press_key` with an `element_token` and `delivery_mode: "background"` called UIA `SetFocus` on the element first. Some providers activate their frame on `SetFocus`, even with `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` set, so the target window became the foreground window for a moment before the key arrived (#4843). This change posts the key straight to the element's own native HWND and never calls `SetFocus` on the background path. When no safe exact target exists, it refuses before sending any input.

## What changed

- `press_key` (Windows): for a background key on a native control, it reads the element's `NativeWindowHandle` and checks that the HWND belongs to the requested pid and is the admitted window or one of its children. It then posts `WM_KEYDOWN`/`WM_KEYUP` (or the Unicode text fallback) to that exact HWND, with no retarget to the frame's focused descendant. Windowless elements, and targets outside the admitted window, return a structured `background_unavailable` with "no keyboard input was sent". Foreground delivery is unchanged. The existing embedded-WebView focus-click route now applies only to elements whose nearest HWND (their own, or for a windowless element its nearest windowed UIA ancestor) sits inside a Chromium window. A native control in a window that also hosts a WebView keeps exact-HWND delivery, and a windowless native control there is refused instead of focus-clicked. Unit tests cover that route decision.
- Harness: the WPF fixture has a `--winforms-keyboard` mode with native EDIT controls, a decoy, a windowless link, and activation/focus journals. `harness_wpf_test.rs` adds three WinForms rows: a background key reaches the exact control with no activation, a windowless target is refused, and a foreground key reaches the exact control. The testkit can set `state_timeout_ms` for behavioral recording, which the WPF accelerator rows use.
- The tool description, the generated Windows MCP spec and the reference docs describe the new targeting.

## Scope

This PR keeps the contributor's commits as authored and merges current main on top. The contributor's WebView2 harness changes (DOM/viewport geometry and the custom publish-path selector) are superseded by main's rewrite of `harness_web_test.rs` in #7537, so the merge takes main's version of that file. A follow-up commit drops the `Win32_UI_HiDpi` feature, which only that superseded code used. The contributor's change to `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs` is also superseded: main now runs the UBRN Cargo entrypoint directly, so the merge takes main's version. The change is Windows only. Linux and macOS key delivery are untouched.

## Blast Radius

Windows background `press_key` calls that pass an `element_token` for a native control. A call that used to succeed after an activating `SetFocus` now either posts to the exact control or returns `background_unavailable` and suggests `delivery_mode: "foreground"`. One behavior change for callers: a background key no longer moves keyboard focus to the control, so later keys sent without an `element_token` go wherever focus already was. The tool description says this.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass at this head: `bin/ci --quick`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, the e2e inventory test, and in CI the Windows clippy, unit, compile and shard jobs, which build platform-windows and run the new route-decision unit tests.
- The latest commit, which narrows the WebView route, is checked by CI's Windows clippy, unit and shard jobs; it has not run on a desktop yet.
- The PR's shared Windows E2E lane passes. The native WPF/WinForms rows run only in the release gate's queue lanes, so they have not run at this head. The contributor's description on #4876 has native receipts from an earlier head.
- `gate / macOS hosted E2E` failed on an earlier head in `shared_web_action_matrix_is_state_verified` (Electron `px-background` type_text). The same failure appeared on branches without this diff, and the lane passed after main was merged in.

title: feat(cua-driver): add metadata-only RuntimeWitnessV0 contract
body:
Salvaged from #4883

## Why
The generated contract and live `tools/list` say what a build advertises, and `health_report` says whether the runtime is broadly usable. Neither records whether a read-only tool call actually completed on one build and platform with a valid result. This adds a typed, metadata-only record of that evidence, with no runner yet.

## What changed
- `cua-driver-contract` gains an experimental `RuntimeWitnessV0` with `validate()` and `runtime_witness_schema()`. It binds a witness to the contract, tools-list and capability versions, and keeps one sorted row per probed tool with outcome, output-schema result, elapsed time and a bounded diagnostic code.
- Validation refuses acting probes by the probe's `read_only` flag and by the tool's published `read_only` annotation, so a probe naming `click` cannot pass by claiming to be read-only. It also refuses tools outside the portable contract, which have no published annotation to check. It refuses a probe that claims a capability its tool does not publish.
- A design note in `libs/cua-driver/docs/runtime-conformance-witness-v0.md`, linked from the contract README.

## Scope
Covers the type, its validation, its schema and docs. Leaves out the runner, any `tools/list` or MCP change, and the generated manifest and bindings, which stay unchanged. v0 probes only portable-contract tools.

## Blast Radius
Nothing calls the new type yet, so runtime behavior does not change. `pub use witness::*` adds names to the contract crate root; the dependent Linux crates build without collisions.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, and the contract crate's tests including the new witness tests, all green on Linux.
- The contract generator and the UniFFI binding check produced no drift, and the core, Linux platform and driver crates build.
- macOS and Windows platform crates were not built; the change adds no platform code.

title: feat(cua-driver-testkit): reject action-truth claims that contradict E2E oracles
body:
Salvaged from #4884

Refs #3171

## Why

The Driver records an internal `action_truth` for each action, and the E2E harness classifies the outcome independently through fixture oracles. Today the two are validated separately, so a recording where the Driver claims `refused` while the fixture saw delivery passes the catalog validator. This adds a conservative check that rejects the contradiction once both facts exist.

## What changed

- `validate_action_truthfulness` runs on every retained turn that carries `action_truth`. It rejects a missing or unknown effect and `confirmed` with no evidence. On a single-turn recording it also rejects claims that contradict the case's `observed_behavior`: delivered vs `refused`/`suspected_noop`, refused vs anything but `refused`, no-effect vs `confirmed`/`partial`. `DELIVERED` with `unverifiable` stays valid.
- Two existing refusal tests recorded a `refused` action under a case observed as delivered. They now declare and observe the refusal through a `refused_turn_fixture` helper.
- rustfmt on the new code, which failed `cargo fmt --check` in the quick-contracts job.

## Scope

Only the testkit validator in `cua-driver-testkit`. There are no schema changes to `ActionResult`, `CaseSpec` or E2E results. Recordings without `action_truth` stay accepted. Multi-turn recordings keep the internal checks but are not compared to the case-level oracle, because nothing yet says which turn owns it. This does not add Windows `window_change` readback.

## Blast Radius

E2E release-gate lanes that validate turn evidence. A lane whose recorded Driver claim contradicts its own fixture oracle now fails. That is the intended signal. The producer (`ActionExecutionRecord::debug_json`) emits only the five effect names the validator accepts, and it downgrades `confirmed` without evidence before recording.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks pass: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit` (all pass, including the new action-truth and catalog-binding tests) and `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-testkit --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- At the original #4884 head, `cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit --lib` fails the two refusal tests above. Both pass at this head.
- When the refused-oracle arm is disabled, `action_truthfulness_rejects_refusal_mismatch` fails.
- Not run: the Linux desktop E2E lane, and the macOS and Windows lanes.

title: docs(qemu-docker): point the libs/images link at the directory that exists
body:
The three platform READMEs under `libs/qemu-docker/` link their deprecation notice to a directory that does not exist.

## The defect

```markdown
Use the images in [`libs/images`](../images/README.md) ...
```

From `libs/qemu-docker/<platform>/README.md`, `../images/README.md` resolves to **`libs/qemu-docker/images/README.md`**. That directory does not exist — the real one is `libs/images/`, one level higher. The link text already says `libs/images`, so the href is what disagrees with the sentence it sits in.

Rendered targets, checked with `curl -L -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'`:

| URL | status |
|---|---|
| `github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/qemu-docker/images/README.md` | **404** |
| `github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/libs/images/README.md` | **200** |

```
$ find libs -type d -name images
libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-perception/tests/quality-corpus/images
libs/images
```

There is no `images` directory under `libs/qemu-docker/`, so the link cannot resolve for any of the three platforms.

## Change

Three files, one character each: `../images/README.md` → `../../images/README.md`.

- `libs/qemu-docker/android/README.md`
- `libs/qemu-docker/linux/README.md`
- `libs/qemu-docker/windows/README.md`

## Why the link check did not catch it

`.github/workflows/ci-check-docs-links.yml` runs `next-validate-link` over the docs app and the code-block lanes. These three links live in `libs/**` and are rendered by GitHub, not by the docs site, so no step resolves them. I am not proposing a workflow change here — only flagging it in case you want that coverage later.

## Verification

- The replacement target exists in the tree (`libs/images/README.md`) and returns 200 on the rendered blob URL.
- `grep -rl '\.\./images/README.md' libs/` returns seven files. Four of them (`libs/kasm`, `libs/xfce`, `libs/xfce-cua`, `libs/qemu-docker/README.md`) sit one level higher, where `../images/` resolves to `libs/images/` and works. These three are the only ones that sit one level too deep — which is also why the pattern looked fine when it was copy-pasted.
- Docs-only: no code, no config, no generated output touched.

title: fix(spaces): keep a deleted prepared agent home removed
body:
## Summary

Deleting or cancelling the prepared agent home could recreate `home-claude-code` while the app stayed open. The preparation driver treated a missing home as a request to make another one, including after the daemon had removed its persistent agent.

This stops preparation before the host removes the Space, keeps the stop across an app relaunch, and ignores late create and setup callbacks from work that was cancelled. A new explicit request can still prepare a home, and queued messages stay in the saved record.

Re-landed from #7710 by @k0nkupa, because pull requests from forks cannot carry the local CI sign-off the merge queue needs. The diff is theirs unchanged, and they are credited as co-author. Closes #7710 and #7707.

## Validation

- `cargo test --locked -p cua-spaces-app-core --lib`: 928 passed, including the regenerated prepare parity fixture.
- `bin/ci` signed off on this head, which includes the web app tests.

title: Flaky test: x11_overlay_frames_are_never_composited_half_presented
body:
`overlay::tests::x11_overlay_frames_are_never_composited_half_presented` (platform-linux, `crates/platform-linux/src/overlay.rs`) failed once in CI on a PR that does not touch the overlay code.

- PR: #5574, commit `8d2a3afba5770822e019c21f7fb4448932e43781`
- Run: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/41747393355/job/126331653247 (CI: Rust Linux unit, "Rust Linux unit and compile", attempt 2)
- The other X11 overlay tests in the same job passed, `x11_overlay_frames_are_never_seen_half_presented` among them.

Failure:

```
thread 'overlay::tests::x11_overlay_frames_are_never_composited_half_presented' panicked at crates/platform-linux/src/overlay.rs:4456:9:
1 of 1063 reads saw a half-presented frame, first: ["red 24963, blue 0, other 0"]
```

PR #5574 changes no file under the overlay code, so this looks like a timing flake in the composited (xvfb + picom) path: one read in 1063 counted as half-presented.

If it fails again, please investigate it as a flake. Either the test samples the composited output before the compositor has settled, or the overlay can really present a partial frame under a compositor.
