title: cua-driver-bench: Linux CDB-G03 on 0.52.6 reports GnuCash unresponsive, a failure mode not seen on 0.52.1
body:
Found by the cua-driver 0.52.6 release bench (Bench v2, Linux X11 lane, foreground), compared against 0.52.1.

**What changed.** CDB-G03 (the multi-app GnuCash task) fails on both releases, but the way it fails changed. On 0.52.1 every failed trial ran out of turns. On 0.52.6 most trials stopped early with the agent reporting BLOCKED because GnuCash had stopped responding, and the rest ran out of turns. We have not seen the "GnuCash unresponsive" mode on any earlier release.

**Not yet known.** Whether this comes from a driver change in 0.52.2–0.52.6 or from the app or desktop on that run. One bench is not enough to tell.

**Ask.**
1. On the next release bench, check whether CDB-G03 on Linux still reports GnuCash unresponsive.
2. If it does, read those trial transcripts against #7032 (read-backs replacing fixed settles). Look for a read-back that polls GnuCash's accessibility tree hard enough, or early enough after an action, to stall it where the old fixed settle did not.

Related: #7621 (an unlogged process stalling the AT-SPI bus on the bench desktop), #7531 (CDB-G03 is at the floor for every arm).

title: cua-driver: browser_prepare existing_profile on macOS Chrome re-prompts every attempt and ignores the person's Allow
body:
## Summary

On macOS with Google Chrome (tested on Chrome 157, macOS 26), `browser_prepare` with `strategy: {kind: "existing_profile"}` against a signed-in Chrome profile can fail in a way a person cannot recover from: every attempt raises a new "Allow remote debugging?" prompt, clicking **Allow** does not attach, and the refusal says the driver "could not prove this page belongs to that window", which is not what happened.

Reported against cua-driver 0.36.0 and 0.52.9 (Rust).

## What the user sees

1. `browser_prepare` returns `browser_wrong_target_refused` with the message "browser consent did not settle within its bounded attempt" and the hint "could not prove this page belongs to that window".
2. Each retry raises another "Allow remote debugging?" prompt. Prompts stack (one centred on the target window, another on a different Chrome window).
3. A person who clicks **Allow** closes the prompt, but the call still refuses and `get_browser_state` still reports `browser_consent_required`.
4. The prompt window could not be read or clicked with the driver's own window tools in that setup.
5. Separately: `cua-driver serve --grant existing-profile` run from a shell answers every call with `permissions_pending` even though `cua-driver permissions status` reports both permissions on. The same command started by launchd works. A daemon started by `cua-driver mcp` without `--grant` cannot be given the grant later; the refusal does not say how to get it.

## Reproduction (throwaway profile, no personal data needed)

1. Start a separate Chrome instance: `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --user-data-dir=<empty temp dir> --no-first-run`.
2. Open `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and tick "Allow remote debugging for this browser instance". Chrome writes `DevToolsActivePort` in the profile directory.
3. Open a raw WebSocket to `ws://127.0.0.1:<port><path>` from that file and hold it. Chrome shows "Allow remote debugging?" as a separate 448x240 window titled exactly that, whose accessibility root is an `AXSheet` with **Turn off in settings**, **Cancel** and **Allow** buttons. With several browser windows open it attaches to the window used last, not necessarily the target window.
4. Observations:
   - The WebSocket handshake gets no answer until the prompt is answered. A late **Allow** (11 s in our test) completes the same handshake with `101`.
   - If the client closes first, the prompt stays on screen. Clicking **Allow** on it then does nothing, and the next connection raises a new prompt.
5. With the driver: when the driver cannot press **Allow** itself within about 4 s (for example the prompt cannot be read, the scan across many large windows is slow, or the match is ambiguous), `browser_prepare` drops its pending connection. That leaves an orphaned prompt and refuses with `browser_wrong_target_refused`.

## Root causes

- **(a) A new prompt on every attempt.** Chrome asks for consent per browser-level WebSocket. After about 4.5 s the driver drops its pending connection, so the approval a person gives later belongs to a connection that no longer exists. The next attempt dials again and raises a new prompt. The abandoned prompt is never closed, so prompts stack.
- **(b) Approval never settles.** The consent wait is bounded at 4 s, which is enough for the driver's own AX press but far too short for a person. The generic CDP connect timeout (10 s) would also kill a held handshake. The driver ignores the one signal that matters, whether the pending handshake completed.
- **(c) Misleading error.** The consent timeout is reported as `browser_wrong_target_refused`. That code's recovery hint ("could not prove this page belongs to that window... bind again") describes a page-to-window binding failure that never ran.
- **(d) The prompt is not read directly.** The macOS consent scanner skips windows titled "Allow remote debugging?" and only looks for an `AXSheet` inside normal browser windows. It walks every titled browser window (up to 5,000 elements each) before it can find the sheet, which can use up the 4 s budget. When the same sheet is reachable both through its own window and through its parent, the two references are not treated as one element.
- **(e) TCC attribution from a shell.** `serve` disclaims responsibility only when the executable is outside `CuaDriver.app`. The installed `cua-driver` command is a link into the bundle, so a shell-started daemon keeps the shell's host as its responsible process, and TCC checks that host's grants. Launch grants are deliberately launcher-only, and the refusal does not tell the person how to restart with one.

## Expected

- One prompt per attach attempt. A person's **Allow** attaches that same pending connection. Cancel or dismiss returns `browser_consent_revoked`. Nobody answering returns `browser_consent_required` with a hint to answer the prompt, and the prompt is closed.
- The driver reads the prompt window first.
- `cua-driver serve` behaves the same whether it is started from a shell or by launchd.

title: test(spaces-web): agents-populate-timing and add-computer-sheet tests fail under load on wall-clock limits
body:
Two `apps/cua-spaces-web` tests check real elapsed time against fixed limits, so they fail when the machine is busy even though nothing in the code changed.

## What failed

Both failures came from one `bin/ci` web test run on a Linux machine that was also running other test suites. The PR under test did not touch either file.

- `src/__tests__/agents-populate-timing.test.tsx` > "the next visit draws from the last one at once, before the slow Spaces answer": `AssertionError: expected 411 to be less than 400`. The test reads `Date.now()` around a real `setTimeout` sleep and polls the DOM every 10 ms. Then it asserts the warm-visit rows appear in under 400 ms. The cold-visit test has the same kind of limits (1500 ms and 2500 ms).
- `src/components/__tests__/add-computer-sheet.test.tsx` > "Add a machine: states > renews the code, the link, the command and the prompt by itself when it expires": `expected null to be truthy`. The first code is set to expire `Date.now() / 1000 + 1`. The test then gives `waitFor` 4000 ms of real time to see the renewed code. Other tests in this file also wait on real time (`setTimeout(r, 600)`, `waitFor` timeouts of 3000 to 4000 ms).

Each file passed 3 of 3 times when run alone, and the full suite (264 files) passed when nothing else was running.

## Suggested fix

Use fake timers (`vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: false })` and `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync`, or `vi.setSystemTime` for the expiry) to control the clock in these tests. The limits would then measure the page's own scheduling, not how busy the machine is. For example, in the timing test the slow Spaces' delays are advanced in steps, and the test checks which rows are drawn before the slow ones answer. That is the behavior the 400 ms limit stands in for.

Same kind of problem as #5839 and #7847 (wall-clock asserts that flake under load), in different code.

title: fix(cua-driver): attach existing Chrome profiles after one consent prompt
body:
Fixes #7997. Linear: CUA-4305.

## What changes for users

On macOS with Chrome, `browser_prepare` with `strategy: {kind: "existing_profile"}` now needs one prompt per attempt, and clicking **Allow** on it attaches. Before, each attempt raised another prompt and the attempt refused even after Allow. A declined or unanswered prompt now gets a clear refusal, and the driver closes the prompt it raised. `cua-driver serve` started from a terminal now uses Cua Driver's own macOS permissions.

## Root causes and fixes

- **The pending connection was dropped after 4 s.** Chrome holds the WebSocket handshake until its prompt is answered and ties the approval to that one connection. The driver dropped the connection, so a later Allow attached nothing and left an orphaned prompt. Now, when the driver did not press Allow itself, an attach the user can see keeps that same connection open for up to 120 s (`PERSON_CONSENT_BOUND`), and the browser's answer decides the result:
  - handshake completes: attached
  - Chrome returns 403 on **Cancel**: `browser_consent_revoked` (`reason: browser_consent_declined`)
  - no answer: `browser_consent_required` (`reason: browser_consent_unanswered`)

  Attaches under the background guard, where the prompt opens on another Space, keep the old 4 s bound. They now get the same honest code.
- **The generic 10 s CDP connect timeout** cut the consent-gated dial short. `claim_existing` now has its own handshake bound, and `browser_prepare` cancels the dial first.
- **Orphaned prompts.** A new `BrowserPlatform::dismiss_abandoned_existing_profile_consent` hook, implemented on macOS, Linux and Windows, presses the exact Cancel on the prompt of any connection the driver abandons. That covers both `browser_prepare` and the engine's reconnect path.
- **Wrong code and hint.** Consent timeouts were reported as `browser_wrong_target_refused`, whose hint says "could not prove this page belongs to that window". They now use consent codes, and `browser_consent_required` with `browser_consent_unanswered` has its own hint: ask the user to click Allow, then retry once.
- **macOS scanner.** Chrome 157 shows the prompt as its own window whose AX root is an `AXSheet`, attached to the last-active browser window. The scanner skipped that window and walked every large browser window first. It now reads prompt windows first, and collapses the same sheet seen through its parent window into one element (`CFEqual`).
- **TCC attribution.** `serve` skipped the responsibility disclaim whenever the executable was inside `CuaDriver.app`, which is also true for the installed `cua-driver` command run from a shell, so TCC checked the shell host's grants. The decision now uses the actual responsible pid (`responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid`, with a `getppid() == 1` fallback).
- The standard-mode refusal and BROWSER.md now say how to restart with `--grant existing-profile`.

## Testing

- New unit tests:
  - a person answers 30 s after the driver gave up, both after a scanner error and after a scanner timeout (paused clock)
  - an unanswered prompt, and the background (zero-wait) path
  - a closed handshake reads as a decline
  - prompt-window-first ordering, and dedupe of the same sheet seen twice
  - responsible-process detection
  - hint selection for `browser_consent_unanswered`
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` (1309 passed) and `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib browser::` (88 passed), plus the responsibility tests in `cua-driver`.
- Manual check on macOS 26 with Chrome 157, using a throwaway `--user-data-dir` instance and a debug daemon on its own socket. The debug daemon has no Accessibility grant, so it cannot press Allow itself.
  - Allow pressed about 15 s in: `attached_existing_profile`, `displayed_consent_prompt: true`.
  - Cancel: `browser_consent_revoked` / `browser_consent_declined`, with Chrome answering `403 Forbidden`.
- `bin/ci --quick` is green. The Linux and Windows hook implementations are covered by CI only.

body:
## What changed for users
The download and the repo's Latest badge can no longer briefly go back to an older Cua Spaces version when two releases finish out of order.

## Cause
Each `cua-spaces-v*` tag runs its own CD run (never cancelled, about 2 to 2.5 h). The 0.37.0 run was slower (its SwiftUI Rust build took about 100 min) and its publish job ran at 23:59Z, after 0.37.1 (23:37Z). The publish step always passed `--latest`, and the 15-minute guard returned early whenever Latest was on any Spaces release, so nothing corrected it until a manual reset.

## Fix
- `cd-cua-spaces.yml`: the publish step passes `--latest=false` when a newer stable Spaces release is already published (logs a warning).
- `pin_latest_release.py`: the guard also resets Latest when it sits on a Spaces release that is not the newest published stable one.
- New unit test for the guard.

Not covered here: the verify step "cua.ai serves the new release" fails for a stale release (correctly, the site serves the newer one); a stale run should skip it.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the OpenJev stalled-body timeout alive through GC
body:
## Scope

Fixes #7843

`CI: jev-use` sometimes fails `loopback body that stalls past the timeout is a bounded timeout`. When it does, the test runs for about 300 s and gets `OpenJevError: OpenJev redirect or transport was refused` instead of code `timeout`. It failed the same way on main push runs and on #3897 twice in a row.

Cause: after `fetch` resolves, nothing in `defaultTransport` holds the `AbortSignal.timeout()` signal or undici's abort hook on the response body. If GC runs while the body stalls, the timeout is dropped. `reader.read()` then waits until the server's keep-alive closes the socket and rejects with `TypeError: terminated`, which `transportError` maps to `http_error`. A standalone fetch with `gc()` forced every 10 ms reproduces it on every run on Node 22.

Fix in `openjev_model.ts`:

- Hold the timer and its `AbortController` for the whole request, and clear the timer when the request ends.
- Cancel the body reader when the signal aborts, and check `throwIfAborted()` after each read.
- Map any error after an abort to `timeout`.

The stalled-body test now forces GC every 10 ms while it waits, so it fails on every run without the fix instead of only when GC happens to land.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks: `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use` (258 passed). With main's `openjev_model.ts` and the new test, the stalled-body test hangs past a 30 s bound. With this change it passes 5 of 5 runs. Not run: desktop E2E and Lume lanes, which this example-only change does not touch, and native Windows/macOS.

title: test(spaces-web): add-agent.test.tsx fails misleadingly when the wasm app core isn't built
body:
When `add-agent.test.tsx` runs locally without first building the Rust-to-WebAssembly app core, the test "says before Start that the agent needs a provider when none is connected" fails with `expected null not to be null` at `add-agent.test.tsx:46` (waiting for `[data-start-needs-key]`), while the other tests in the same file still pass. That makes a local run look like a real regression on main.

Cause: with the core files missing, `testCore()` falls back to `unavailableCore`, a stand-in that does nothing. The "needs a provider" note comes from `setupCard(core, …)` in `add-agent-sheet.tsx:254`, so it never renders.

This is not a bug on main: CI builds the core first, and the file passes 12/12 there (e.g. run 43988200496 at `fcdf49c`). Locally, after `node scripts/build-core-wasm.mjs`, the file passed 12/12 in three runs on `bff492d`.

Suggested fix: skip core-dependent tests when the core isn't built (the helper already exposes `wasmBuilt`), or fail fast at the start of the file with a message saying to build the core.

Found while unsticking #6975.

title: [Bug]: get_window_state accepts max_dimension: 0 (schema minimum is 1) and returns a 1x1 PNG
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`get_window_state` accepts `max_dimension: 0` even though the tool's own published input schema declares `"minimum": 1`, and returns a **1x1 PNG** (`screenshot_width = 1`, `screenshot_height = 1`) as an apparently successful capture instead of rejecting the value or falling back to the configured default.

### Reproduction

1. Launch any app and note `pid` / `window_id` (here: Windows Calculator).
2. Call:
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <wid>, "include_accessibility_tree": false,
    "include_screenshot": true, "max_dimension": 0}
   ```
3. Inspect `structuredContent`: `screenshot_width` and `screenshot_height` are both `1`, and `content` carries a valid but 1x1 PNG.
4. Repeat with `max_dimension` omitted or `1024` -> correct capture (e.g. 666x1014 for the same window).

Reproduced twice on the same host with different windows. The published schema obtained from `listToolsJson` for `get_window_state` says:

```json
"max_dimension": {"description": "Optional cap on the returned screenshot's long edge ...", "minimum": 1, "type": "integer"}
```

### Expected behavior

Either reject `0` with an input-validation error naming `max_dimension` and its minimum, or treat `0` as "no cap" and return the native-size capture. A 1x1 success result is the worst of the three: the caller has no way to distinguish it from a real capture.

### Actual behavior

```json
"structuredContent": { "screenshot_width": 1, "screenshot_height": 1, ... }
```
and an image is returned. No error, no warning.

### Environment

- cua-driver **0.28.0** (x86_64-windows), embedded in-process through
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-computer-use-cua-driver-native 0.2.2-rc.3` inside
  DeepSeek Harness Desktop 0.2.2-rc.3 (the provider pins the exact npm version).
- Windows 10 build 10.0.17763.6775, x86_64, display 2560x1600 @ 2x scale factor.
- `health_report` is `overall: ok` (UIA reachable, D3D11 capture reachable); `check_permissions`
  elevated=true, High IL.
- I realize 0.28.0 is old relative to 0.52.4; I am reporting against the version pinned by the
  consumer. If this is already fixed on latest, please just say so and close.

### Extra context

This surfaced through an agent-driven session where the argument was constructed programmatically; the schema-invalid value was passed through the MCP/tool layer unvalidated, so the driver is the last line of defense. Happy to test a patched build.

title: [Bug]: classic Win32 title-bar buttons advertise actions=[invoke] but click silently no-ops with route=synthetic_events
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On classic Win32 dialogs, `get_window_state` exposes title-bar buttons (minimize / maximize / close) with `actions=[invoke]`, but `click` cannot activate them: both documented addressing modes return `route: "synthetic_events"`, `effect: "unverifiable"`, and the window state does not change (no error, no escalation hint). The same `click` works on UWP title bars and on client-area controls.

### Reproduction

1. Launch classic Notepad: `launch_app {"name": "Notepad"}` (Win10 `C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe`, class `Notepad`), note `pid` / `window_id`.
2. `get_window_state` for that window. The tree includes title-bar controls advertised as invokable:
   ```
   [3] Button "最小化" [actions=[invoke]]
   [4] Button "最大化" [actions=[invoke]]
   [5] Button "关闭"  [actions=[invoke]]
   ```
3. Click using the **preferred** token addressing (same thing happens with `element_index` + `snapshot_id`):
   ```json
   {"pid": <pid>, "window_id": <wid>, "element_token": "s0000001e:4"}
   ```
   Response:
   ```json
   {"delivery":{"mode":"background"},"effect":"unverifiable","route":"synthetic_events"}
   ```
4. `get_window_state` again: `window_bounds` unchanged (`{x:121,y:120,width:1000,height:641}`); the window is not maximized.
5. Repeat with `element_index: 4` + matching `snapshot_id`: identical response, still no change.
6. Control on the same host: UWP Calculator title bar, same two calls -> `route: "accessibility"`, and `window_bounds` changes 644x1015 -> 2560x1520 (works).

This is reproducible on every classic Win32 title bar I tried (Notepad), in both fresh and long-lived sessions.

### Expected behavior

Either actually invoke the control through the accessibility pattern the catalog advertises, or fail explicitly (structured error) / return an escalation hint. The docs for `click` say `element_index` + `window_id` "performs the UIA Invoke pattern on the cached element"; a silent unverifiable no-op for a control that advertises `invoke` means a caller cannot tell "acted" from "did nothing".

### Actual behavior

`route: "synthetic_events"`, `effect: "unverifiable"`, no state change. Because the button lives in the non-client area, the posted client-area mouse messages are discarded by the window.

### Environment

- cua-driver **0.28.0** (x86_64-windows), embedded in-process via
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-computer-use-cua-driver-native 0.2.2-rc.3` in
  DeepSeek Harness Desktop 0.2.2-rc.3.
- Windows 10 build 10.0.17763.6775, x86_64, 2560x1600 @ 2x; window scope, background delivery.
- Session is a headless/disconnected console (GetForegroundWindow -> 0x0), so foreground delivery
  is unavailable on this host by design; background is the only route, which is why the silent
  no-op matters.
- Related but distinct: #6823 (background paths unexpectedly taking foreground). Here nothing
  takes foreground; the action simply never lands.

### Extra context

Workaround used: drive window placement with `set_window_frame` / `bring_to_front` instead of
clicking caption buttons. Happy to retest on a newer driver build if 0.28.0 is too old.

title: feat(cua-driver): dock the macOS permission guide under System Settings
body:
## Problem

The permission guide is a 480 x 420 floating window at the top right of the main screen. Once System Settings opens, the person works across two windows: the step and the drag tile are in one, the list and its switch in the other, often at the far side of the screen. On smaller screens the guide also covers the list (#6984 measured this on a 1280 x 800 VM).

## Change

While System Settings has a window, the guide shrinks to the step, what to do there and the drag tile, and docks under the settings pane, moving with the window. The placement is the one the Cua Spaces guide already uses (`PanelPlacement`, #6870).

- `permissions/settings_window.rs`: finds System Settings by bundle id (`com.apple.systempreferences`, not its translated name) and reads its frontmost layer-0 window from the window server (`windows::pid_on_screen_windows_any_layer`). This needs no permission, so it works before Accessibility or Screen Recording is on.
- `permissions/dock.rs`: the placement as plain geometry, with tests. The guide goes under the content area right of the 230 pt sidebar, inside the visible frame of the screen that holds most of the window. When there is no room below, it overlaps the window's bottom instead of leaving the screen.
- `permissions/panel.rs`: a docked view (title, what to do, drag hint, tile) next to the existing step and finished views, and a 30 Hz follow timer in the modal run-loop mode. When System Settings has had no window for 12 ticks (about 0.4 s), or the guide finishes, the full window comes back where it was. The docked window can't be dragged by hand, so it never fights the follow timer.

The gate, the status checks, the request order and the copy are unchanged.

This also covers #6984's case. While System Settings is open, the guide sits under it instead of over its list. While it is closed, the full window stays at the top right.

## Test

- `permissions::dock::tests`: window-server to AppKit conversion, docking with and without room below, screen edges, and which display wins. Plus `panel::tests::docked_layout_fits_its_view`.
- Manual runs used `permission_guide_preview` wrapped in an ad hoc signed `.app` on a macOS 26.7 VM and a macOS 15.8 VM, both 1920 x 1080:
  - With the Accessibility pane open, the guide docked under the pane. On macOS 26 it overlapped the window's bottom by about 30 pt to stay above the Dock.
  - After dragging System Settings to the top left, the guide followed it.
  - After quitting System Settings, the full window came back at the top right. After reopening System Settings, the guide docked again.
  - Dragging the tile from the docked guide into the Accessibility list worked: System Settings accepted the drop and asked for the admin password to add the app.
  - The Screen Recording step docked the same way.

## Checks

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib`: 815 passed, 13 ignored
- [ ] `bin/ci`: not run

title: feat(cua-driver): show the macOS permission guide in Simplified Chinese
body:
## Problem

The permission guide is English only. On a Mac set to Simplified Chinese, System Settings says 辅助功能 and 录屏与系统录音, while the guide asks the person, in English, to find "Accessibility" and "Screen Recording". Cua Spaces' guide already ships Simplified Chinese through PermissionFlow; the driver's guide does not.

## Change

- `permissions/guide.rs`:
  - `Language` picks the guide's language from the person's preferred languages, in order. The first one that is English or Simplified Chinese (`zh-Hans…`, `zh-CN`, `zh-SG`) wins, and English is the fallback. Traditional Chinese has no words yet, so the next preferred language decides.
  - `Words::of(language)` holds the fixed words, and `GuideStep::copy_in(language)` holds the step copy. The English constants and `GuideStep::copy()` are unchanged and remain the English source.
- `permissions/panel.rs`: reads `NSLocale.preferredLanguages` once per guide and shows every label, button, tooltip and window title through `words()` / `copy_in(language())`. The array is read through its enumerator because AppKit may return a Swift-bridged array whose `count` is typed `Int`, which `msg_send!`'s type check rejects.

The Chinese copy uses System Settings' own names (系统设置, 退出并重新打开) and keeps the app's name, Cua Driver, as macOS lists it. The terminal banner stays in English.

## Test

- `guide::tests::the_first_preferred_language_with_words_wins`: `zh-Hans-CN`, `zh-CN`, `zh_CN`, `en-GB` first, `zh-Hant` falling through to the next language, unsupported languages, and an empty list.
- `guide::tests::simplified_chinese_has_every_word_english_has`: every English word and step line has a Chinese counterpart (empty where English is empty), and English through `copy_in` equals `copy()`.
- On a macOS 26.7 VM, `permission_guide_preview screen-recording -AppleLanguages "(zh-Hans-CN)"` in an ad hoc signed `.app` showed the whole window in Chinese with no clipped labels. Without the argument it showed English.

## Checks

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib`: 810 passed, 13 ignored
- [ ] `bin/ci`: not run

This PR and #8012 both touch `panel.rs`. Whichever lands second, I'll rebase it and route the docked view's labels through `words()`.

title: jev-use: s1_service.ts body read may lose its AbortSignal.timeout under GC (same shape as #7843)
body:
Follow-up from #8004 (fix for #7843).

`libs/cua-driver/examples/jev-use/typescript/s1_service.ts` passes `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` to `fetch` (line 101), then reads the body with `await response.text()` (line 108). #8004 found that in `openjev_model.ts` nothing holds that signal once `fetch` resolves, so if GC runs while the body stalls, the timeout is dropped and the read waits until keep-alive closes the socket.

`s1_service.ts` has the same shape and may have the same bug. Its tests never stall a body, so nothing exercises it. #8004 did not change it.

To do:
- Add a stalled-body test for `s1_service.ts` that forces GC while it waits, as #8004 did for OpenJev.
- If it hangs, apply the same fix: hold the timer and `AbortController` for the whole request and map errors after abort to `timeout`.

title: fix(agents): suppress replayed history when resuming ACP sessions
body: ## Summary An ACP agent can replay earlier replies and tool updates while handling `session/resume`. Cua currently treats those updates as new output: an old reply is emitted again, and the trailing old text can be concatenated with the new answer. Apply the existing startup replay guard to both `session/load` and `session/resume`, before text buffering and tool-ledger handling. A regression fixture sends old text, a completed tool call, and a trailing old text chunk through the real ACP transport; only the new answer may reach the event log. ## Related work Refs #6234. That change recovers a lost durable session; this fixes duplicate output when an existing session resumes successfully. Current open issues and PRs were searched for Hermes, session/resume, bridge restart, and saved-home recovery. No competing replay-suppression change was found. No RFC is required: this is an internal runner bug fix with no public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, permission, or file-format change. This is an unselected contribution pending maintainer review. ## Compatibility and risk The guard already applies to `session/load`. Both startup paths now discard historical updates, and the existing `finally` clears the guard on success or failure so new prompt updates continue normally. Agent-neutral behavior; no provider or endpoint configuration changes. Revert this commit to roll back. ## Validation Published head: `d32f603af1a7003325cb0642b333280f12131ec1`, based on `2ef2bf996e`. The browser-created commits have the same runner contents as reviewed local candidate `29d1433e`. - Before the production fix, the five-test resume suite had one failure: `session/resume` emitted `an old answer` and `the last old answercarrying on`; the load case passed. - Full runner suite on published head with pinned ACP SDK 1.5.0: **80 passed, zero failed, zero skipped**. - `bin/ci --quick`: two checks passed, no skips; no heavy builds on the shared host. - Independent code review: no findings; focused resume suite independently passed 5/5. - `git diff --check`: passed. - Prior local validation reproduced the issue in a real Hermes session and confirmed resumed messages and memory without history replay. This exact upstream candidate has deterministic runner validation; GitHub CI remains required. No fresh desktop matrix is claimed. Reproduce the runner checks with the pinned SDK (all paths below are disposable): ```sh npm install --prefix /tmp/cua-acp-sdk-1.5.0 --no-audit --no-fund @agentclientprotocol/sdk@1.5.0 ACP_SDK_DIR=/tmp/cua-acp-sdk-1.5.0 \ CUA_ACP_SDK_DIR=/tmp/cua-acp-sdk-1.5.0/node_modules/@agentclientprotocol/sdk \ node --test libs/cua/crates/cua-agents/runner/test/*.test.mjs python3 bin/ci --quick ``` ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] No RFC is required. - [x] Regression tests and remaining validation gaps are documented. - [x] Conventional Commit title describes the production change. - [x] The same contributor authored both browser commits with a GitHub-linked noreply identity; commit descriptions credit the original local source. - [x] User-facing bug fix; `no-release` is not requested. - [ ] GitHub CI and the repository local-ci/fork sign-off requirement have passed on the published head. ## UI reproduction These are **isolated/simulated reconstructions**. Actual before/after replies from the real ACP runner and scripted ACP transport are displayed by Cua Spaces’ existing 0.27.7 message renderer through its demo adapter. Only synthetic seed data changes; no live Space is connected. The regression test above is the behavior oracle. Before: after resuming, `an old answer` appears again and `the last old answer` is joined directly to `carrying on`. After: earlier history stays in place and only `carrying on` is appended.

title: fix(cua): skip answered bridge calls after supervisor restart
body:
## Summary

When a host supervisor restarts while an agent's file-backed MCP bridge stays open, its in-memory input offsets disappear. Reading the old input again can repeat completed calls, including thread posts and notifications.

Recover completed request IDs from the existing response journal before dispatching old input. Count typed IDs so sequential ID reuse remains valid, and keep unanswered members of batches. Read receipts in bounded chunks and refuse malformed or incomplete receipts before consuming requests.

## Related work

Refs #8016. That PR prevents ACP history from being emitted as fresh chat output; this independently prevents already answered MCP bridge calls from being dispatched again. Targeted open/closed issue and PR searches for bridge restart/recovery found no competing implementation.

No RFC is required: this repairs internal recovery using existing files and JSON-RPC messages; no public schema, permission or architecture changes. This is an unselected contribution pending maintainer review.

## Compatibility and risk

Agent-neutral and shared host-side code. Existing journals need no migration. New/unanswered requests continue normally; ambiguous receipts fail closed with an explicit error. This does **not** promise exactly-once execution if a process dies after a side effect but before its response is saved. Revert these two commits to roll back.

## Validation

title: fix(cua): unblock agent home save and restore in macOS Spaces
body:
## Summary

Persistent agents need their saved home to carry memory and working files between runs. When Cua copies that home into or out of a macOS Space, the manifest command fails on an existing directory because it uses GNU-only `find -printf`. It also assumes `sha256sum` is installed. Both restore and save depend on this command.

That failure can stop an agent before it launches, or leave a completed turn's updated files unsaved. Some restore paths fall back to an offline run without the saved home. In the copied-home completion path, a save error also returns before the supervisor updates `saved_turn` and its event cursor, so a model can finish its answer while Cua fails to finish recording the turn.

Use batched `find -exec`, detect GNU or BSD `stat`, and fall back to macOS's native `shasum -a 256`. This lets the existing save and restore flow run with the tools macOS provides.

The change applies to all agents that use the copy path, including Hermes.

## Related work

Refs #6174 and #7979, which concern home acquisition and recreation rather than native manifest commands. Targeted searches of open and closed issues and PRs found no competing implementation of this fix.

No RFC is proposed: this repairs an internal shell command without changing a public interface, permission boundary or persisted format. This would be an unselected contribution pending maintainer review.

## Compatibility and risk

The manifest format, cache pruning and credential exclusions stay the same. Tests cover paths containing spaces and quotes, empty or missing homes, hashes and file sizes. Existing limitations for filenames containing newlines remain outside this change.

The GNU `stat` probe runs first, so a file named `%z` cannot misidentify a GNU installation as BSD. Revert the two-file change to roll back; no migration is required.

## Validation

Published head `df1aeaa71d1b4fe456540e1b274c4a94f17c09ce` has the same two changed files as tested candidate `1b70512319cbac25e7f6705c2c64eb91c08d5f24`, based on upstream `2ef2bf996ea840b695ab43f10ba87f98301d7b44`:

- Isolated macOS 26.5.2 arm64 build Space, Rust 1.97.1, current upstream 0.28.0 source: `cargo test --locked -p cua-spaces-ext --lib`: 176 passed, zero failed, one pre-existing ignored test.
- Restoring the old GNU-only manifest command makes both new tests fail: 174 passed, two failed, one ignored.
- The native-tools test also uses a temporary PATH containing only the real macOS `find`, `stat` and `shasum`, ensuring the fallback is exercised even when GNU hashing tools are installed.
- `cargo +1.97.1 fmt -p cua-spaces-ext -- --check` passed in the build Space.
- Shared-host `bin/ci --quick`: two passed, Rust checks skipped because Cargo is not installed on the host. Component formatting was checked in the isolated Space as described above.
- A separate code-review agent found the GNU/BSD probe issue; the candidate includes the correction. Its follow-up review reported no findings. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh Linux validation, repository CI and release metadata checks are still required. No full desktop matrix is claimed; this does not alter input-driver behavior.

title: fix(agents): stop overwriting saved Hermes configuration
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Starting persistent Hermes with a Cua connection replaces its saved config.yaml. That deletes settings such as mcp_servers, terminal options and model tuning. An agent can still answer in chat while losing the configured browser or computer tools it needs to finish a task.
- What changed: Merge connection settings into the persistent Hermes config. Keep unrelated settings and an existing model.context_length override; refresh provider/model routing and fallbacks. Explicit caller settings update matching fields without deleting unrelated nested keys. Invalid YAML or malformed model/auth sections stop launch before the config is replaced.

- Follow-up validation fixes: synchronize seven downstream Cargo lockfiles for the YAML dependencies, and give the teleport integration fixture's fake receiver its existing temporary destination home. The latter corrects a pre-existing macOS test setup defect exposed by the broader checks; it changes no production teleport behavior.

The merge edits YAML syntax rather than reserializing decoded values. Hermes uses PyYAML, where quoted "off" and plain off have different types. Tests cover those scalar differences, aliases and merge keys, plus unchanged quotes and collection formatting.

## Related work

Refs #7417, which supplies Hermes configuration from saved Cua connections. Saving configurations seems to be a desired feature. This preserves settings when that configuration is written; connection selection and endpoint precedence stay in place.

#7285 concerns duplicate mcp_servers keys in a setup snippet and remains separate. No existing issue is claimed as fixed by this PR.

RFC: not required under docs/rfcs/README.md's small-bug-fix exception. The production change is confined to the persistent Hermes writer in cua-agents. Follow-ups synchronize dependent lockfiles and correct a hermetic teleport test fixture. There is no new public API, config format or permission policy.

## Compatibility and risk

- Applies to persistent Hermes launches, including explicit endpoints. One-shot Hermes keeps the supplied file verbatim. Existing routing ownership and adopt_external_logins: false policy remain in effect.
- Untouched settings retain their YAML spelling and comments. Inherited model/auth mappings are made explicit before editing so their source defaults stay intact. Edited inherited mappings can be reformatted; byte-for-byte preservation of every equivalent YAML form is not promised.
- An existing context override survives provider/model changes; users remain responsible for choosing a value the model supports. Absent overrides receive the generated default.
- Adds yaml-edit 0.3.6 for syntax-preserving edits and uses serde_yaml_ng for validation. Invalid saved configuration now produces a launch error rather than being silently discarded. Reverting restores the previous overwrite behavior and cannot recover settings that were already lost.

## Validation

### Original Hermes validation

- Isolated macOS validation, Rust 1.97.1: cargo fmt check and clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed. Locked cua-agents tests: 119 library tests passed, 1 ignored; all 3 launch integration tests passed. The 18 merge regressions are included in that library total.

The six original Hermes files matched the locally validated candidate. Subsequent commits are covered below. Validation logs remain private and are not included in this PR or its branch.

- Lockfile synchronization: `89094a68e3d945dfb75619c43bf8878d40ba8307` updates seven dependent Cargo lockfiles without changing existing package versions, sources, or checksums. All 18 repository lockfiles validate. The Hermes library, launch regressions, Node-runner integration, and focused Clippy passed locally.

title: cua-driver Linux: set_value has no route for LibreOffice Calc cells (macOS uses the Name Box)
body:
## Problem

On Linux, `set_value` has no route for LibreOffice Calc cells. macOS has one (#7744). There, `set_value` on a cell goes through the Name Box with keys, types the value, commits with Return, and reads the cell back.

On Linux, Calc's cells expose no AT-SPI `EditableText` or writable `Value`, so `set_value` on a cell falls through to the keyboard fallback, or is refused without foreground. Agents then fill a sheet by hand. They pixel-click the Name Box, press Ctrl+A, type the address, press Return, type the value, press Tab, and repeat for every cell, each step in the foreground. A sheet of 20 cells uses most of a 45-turn budget. In a multi-app task that left the workbook unfinished when the turns ran out. A script driving the same Name Box route through XTest finished the sheet in one call.

## Expected

`set_value` on a Calc cell (an AT-SPI `table cell` under a `table` in a `soffice` process) or on the Name Box uses the same route as macOS:

1. Focus the Name Box (Ctrl+Shift+F5 or the Name Box's own action).
2. Type the address and press Return.
3. Type the value and press Return.
4. Read the cell back through the AT-SPI `Table` interface.

The result is `path: "keys"`, with the `cell` address and the read-back value. A value containing Tab or Return is refused, as on macOS. The route needs a foreground or focus-free keyboard path. Where neither exists, it refuses with the existing `set_value_unavailable` code.

## Where

`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/set_value.rs`. The macOS reference is `platform-macos/src/tools/calc_cell.rs`.

title: [Bug]: set_agent_cursor_enabled reports enabled:true but the cursor never enables when the host renders no overlay frames
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`set_agent_cursor_enabled` returns `{"enabled": true}` but the cursor never becomes enabled: an immediate `get_agent_cursor_state` reports `enabled: false`, `position: null`, and `visual_state.frame: 0`. Window-scope `move_cursor` calls are silent no-ops, and no overlay ever appears in captures. This happens when the embedding host (DeepSeek Harness) mounts the native SDK tools but does not render cursor frames itself.

### Reproduction

Environment: cua-driver **0.28.0** (x86_64-windows), loaded in-process by
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-computer-use-cua-driver-native 0.2.2-rc.3` inside DeepSeek Harness
Desktop 0.2.2-rc.3. Windows 10 build 10.0.17763, 2560x1600 display.

1. `start_session {session:"s", cursor_theme:{theme_id:"cua.default", reduced_motion:"off"}}`
   -> active; `capture_scope:"auto"`, `desktop_capture_authorized:false`, `effective_scope:"window"`.
2. `set_agent_cursor_enabled {session:"s", enabled:true}`
   -> `{"enabled": true, "session": "s"}`
3. `get_agent_cursor_state {session:"s"}` immediately after
   -> `{"enabled": false, "position": null, "visual_state": {"frame": 0, "phase": "loop", "requested_action": "idle", "resolved_action": "idle"}, ...}`
4. `move_cursor {session:"s", target:{kind:"window", pid:<pid>, window_id:<wid>}, x:300, y:200}`
   -> `{"delivery":{"mode":"not_applicable"},"effect":"unverifiable","route":"synthetic_events"}`
   State is unchanged (still `enabled:false`, `position:null`, frame 0) and a fresh
   `get_window_state` screenshot contains no overlay.

Control that does work on the same host/session: `move_cursor` with
`target:{kind:"desktop", display_id:"primary"}` -> `route:"global_input"`; the real OS pointer
moves and `get_cursor_position` reflects it (verified over 60 moves).

### Expected behavior

One of:

- The cursor actually becomes enabled and frames advance (so a host can render them), and the
  success response matches `get_agent_cursor_state`; or
- An explicit unsupported/unavailable error (e.g. `facility_unavailable`) when no cursor renderer is
  attached, instead of a success that cannot be observed; or
- Documentation plus a capability flag (e.g. `cursor_overlay_supported: false`) so embedding hosts
  and agents do not assume a visible pointer.

### Actual behavior

Silent no-op with a misleading success response; `enabled` flips back to `false` and
`visual_state.frame` never advances, so callers cannot distinguish "overlay hidden" from
"overlay unsupported by this host".

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.28.0, x86_64-windows (embedded via the DSH native provider above)
- Windows 10 build 17763, 2560x1600 primary display
- Health report at the time: `overall: ok` (UIA reachable, D3D11 capture reachable)

### Extra context

0.28.0 is old relative to 0.52.4; reporting against the version pinned by the consumer. If this is
already addressed on latest, close freely. Related open items: #1902 (bake the virtual cursor into
captured pixels), #4070 (bounded cursor render cadence), #3062/#2992/#5336 (overlay lifecycle and
visibility bugs). This report is specifically about the enable/state contract being unobservable for
hosts that do not render cursor frames.

When one connection owns a live named session, `start_session` from another connection returns `session_unavailable`, while ordinary calls return `session_owned_by_other_transport`. Return the same structured refusal, holder transport, and recovery hint from both paths.

title: cua-driver (macOS): GTK apps repaint late after a background click, so the effect is missing from the next screenshot
body:
Follow-up to #7950 (background input for GTK 3 apps on macOS) and #7936.

GTK often repaints only when the next event arrives. After a background click that did land, the screenshot taken right after can still show the old state, so an agent concludes the click did nothing and gives up. This showed up in the paired macOS agent run for #7950 (the GnuCash task fails on both main and the branch).

Next step: after a background click on a GTK app, post a harmless trailing event to flush the repaint, or re-read the window after the next input, so agents see the effect of the click.

title: fix(cua-driver): close the macOS permission guide on Not Now
body:
## Problem

When the permission guide is dismissed with "Not Now", or its window is closed, the window does not go away. It stays on screen frozen, and the cursor over it spins. This lasts until the gate ends, which can be the full 10 minute deadline.

`run_if_needed_with_observer` handles `ShownDismissed` by falling through to `wait_for_grants`. That runs on the main thread, and `wait_for_grants_with` waits between checks with `std::thread::sleep`. AppKit only acts while the main run loop turns, so the guide's `orderOut:` at the end of `run_window` never takes effect, and the window stops handling events.

Sampling the frozen `serve` process shows the main thread in `nanosleep`, between `posix_spawn` calls for the status helper.

## Change

`wait_for_grants_with` waits through a new `wait_poll_interval`, which turns the run loop with `panel::pump_run_loop_briefly` until the poll interval has passed. This is the same approach as `ax::enablement::pump_for`. Off the main thread, `pump_run_loop_briefly` still sleeps, so the `after_timeout` wait on its own thread and the unit tests behave as before.

## Test

I tested on macOS 13.7.8, 14.8.9, 15.8.1 and 26.7.3 VMs (Intel, 1920 x 1080). On each one I reset the Accessibility and Screen Recording grants, then ran `open -n -g CuaDriver.app --args serve` and clicked Not Now in the guide:

- **Released 0.52.9 app, on all four, and a build of `main` on 26.7.3:** the guide stayed on screen and the cursor over it spun.
- **This branch**, built and put in an ad hoc signed copy of the bundle: the guide closed at once, and `serve` kept waiting for the grants.

Recordings and a side-by-side image for every version are in the comments below.

title: docs(hoy): make the quickstart's desktop and image-name steps work as written
body:
## What a new user hits today

Following the Hoy overview and quickstart on a fresh Apple silicon Mac:

1. `hoy image create` builds the newest macOS the Mac supports (on a macOS 26 Mac: `macos-26.6.2`), but the quickstart then runs `hoy create demo --image macos-26.5.2`, which fails with "no tested image named macos-26.5.2".
2. The overview says `hoy vnc demo` opens the desktop after `hoy create demo --image ...`. A VM created without `--window`/`--vnc` has no VNC console, so `hoy vnc demo` and `hoy start demo --window` exit 5 ("demo has no VNC console ... cannot be switched on afterwards").

## Changes

- Overview and quickstart: create the example VM with `--window`, and say it can only be chosen at create time.
- Quickstart: say which image name to use (the one `hoy image create` printed), and add an "Open its desktop" section (`hoy vnc`, `hoy start --window`, the clipboard password, Ctrl-C).
- Install: the Full Disk Access entry can show as "Hoy" or by its file name depending on the macOS version; options go after `bash -s --` (the command uses `bash`).

Docs only. No product change.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the macOS agent cursor above a window that already had focus after a foreground click
body:
## Why

#7569 added the `window-agent-cursor-first-actions-video` row, which reads the recorded MP4 and requires the agent pointer to rest at each first action's point. On macOS the row still failed at #7569's merged head. The pointer showed for 2 sampled frames after the foreground coordinate click and then disappeared until the next `move_cursor`.

The cause is in `with_foreground_hid_activation`. When the target window already holds focus, it skips activation and returns straight after the action, so it never calls `request_repin`. The app still orders its window to the front while it handles the click. That covers the normal-level overlay, and a resting cursor's parked render loop leaves it covered.

## What changed

- The already-focused path in `with_foreground_hid_activation` now waits the same 40 ms settle as the activating path, then asks the overlay to re-pin above its target. The action's result is returned unchanged.

## Scope

macOS only, one function in `platform-macos/src/input/skylight.rs`. The exact-window focus guard is unchanged.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, the `platform-macos` lib tests) pass. The full macOS native lane passes at this head, and the first-actions video row is included. The same row failed at #7569's merged head without this change. The Linux and Windows desktop lanes are not affected and were not run.

Refs #2879

title: [Bug] WinINet cache query fails with 12004 under SAFER NormalUser + Medium integrity on Windows
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Windows, applications launched through an elevated **Cua Driver 0.38.0** using `launch_app` can receive `FALSE / 12004 (ERROR_INTERNET_INTERNAL_ERROR)` from `GetUrlCacheEntryInfoA/W`, even for a never-fetched reserved `.invalid` URL. The same x86 diagnostic returns the expected cache-miss error `2 (ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND)` under the user's ordinary UAC-filtered token.

An independent launcher **without Cua** reproduced the distinction. A SAFER NormalUser token derived from an elevated token returned error 2 while retaining High integrity, but returned 12004 when changed to Medium integrity. The direct cause inside WinINet is still unknown. The result does **not** mean that SAFER alone or Medium integrity alone is defective.

No browser, enterprise application, authentication, network requests, or cookies are necessary to reproduce the cache query failure.

### Reproduction

1. Use an x86 WinINet cache-query diagnostic under the signed-in administrator's ordinary UAC-filtered Medium token (the control used an Interactive/Limited task).
2. Run the same diagnostic through elevated Cua Driver 0.38.0 `launch_app`, comparing the ordinary shell route and the direct executable route (`start_minimized=true`).
3. Independently of Cua, compare a SAFER NormalUser token derived from the elevated token with High integrity retained versus lowered to Medium integrity, keeping the same user/session and diagnostic.
4. Compare `GetUrlCacheEntryInfoA/W` return values and immediately captured last-error values. These are cache queries only, not HTTP requests.

The observations below are from the earlier diagnostic runs, not a fresh execution of the compact excerpt or a corrected standalone launcher.

All five variants used the same Windows user SID, interactive session, x86 diagnostic, profile and cache configuration. The 16-query matrix varied A/W, two URLs, NULL/non-NULL result buffer, and before/after `InternetOpenW`.

| Launch context | Cache API result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary UAC-filtered Medium token, via Interactive/Limited task | **16/16 error 2** |
| Cua `launch_app` ordinary shell route | **16/16 error 12004** |
| Cua `launch_app` direct executable route (`start_minimized=true`) | **16/16 error 12004** |
| Independently created SAFER NormalUser token, High IL retained | **16/16 error 2** |
| Independently created SAFER NormalUser token, lowered to Medium IL | **16/16 error 12004** |

In the original matrix, one URL was `https://example.invalid/...`; all eight checks for this URL alone followed the same pattern. No HTTP GET was sent. The second URL in the original matrix was later replaced with another `.invalid` URL in a sanitized public draft. That sanitized version was compiled and its ordinary UAC branch was executed (16/16 error 2); its SAFER branches were **not rerun** after the URL replacement. This report does not claim those unrerun source branches have been execution-validated.

### Expected behavior

A cache query for a never-fetched `.invalid` URL should return `FALSE / 2 (ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND)`, as under the ordinary UAC-filtered token, rather than an internal WinINet failure. Error 2 is a valid cache miss, not proof of application-level recovery. See Microsoft's [GetUrlCacheEntryInfoA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wininet/nf-wininet-geturlcacheentryinfoa) and [GetUrlCacheEntryInfoW](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wininet/nf-wininet-geturlcacheentryinfow) documentation.

### Actual behavior

Both Cua launch routes and the independent SAFER NormalUser + Medium context returned `FALSE / 12004 (ERROR_INTERNET_INTERNAL_ERROR)` across the 16-query matrix, including all eight checks for the original `.invalid` URL. The ordinary UAC Medium control and independent SAFER High control returned error 2. Microsoft documents [12004](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/wininet/wininet-errors) as an internal error; the failing WinINet internal operation is unknown.

### Environment

- Windows x64, reported build `26300.9711`, Windows 26H2. Other Windows builds not tested.
- Signed-in local administrator using split UAC tokens, elevated Driver in the interactive session.
- Official Cua Driver **[0.38.0](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.38.0)**, matching the official release binary; release commit `85e2b1318bd77ccf3cfa88ccdf875a4bb7eaed19` (identified via release, not embedded `source_sha`).
- Diagnostic executable compiled x86 using the Windows .NET Framework C# compiler.

### Evidence

#### Minimal API probe

A compact illustration of the failing API (the broader tested matrix used two URLs, buffer variations and `InternetOpenW`). Compile as **x86** and execute under the compared token contexts. This compact excerpt has not been separately executed as a standalone program.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;

class CacheProbe {
    [DllImport("wininet.dll", EntryPoint = "GetUrlCacheEntryInfoA",
        CharSet = CharSet.Ansi, ExactSpelling = true, SetLastError = true)]
    static extern bool CacheA(string url, IntPtr entry, ref uint size);

    [DllImport("wininet.dll", EntryPoint = "GetUrlCacheEntryInfoW",
        CharSet = CharSet.Unicode, ExactSpelling = true, SetLastError = true)]
    static extern bool CacheW(string url, IntPtr entry, ref uint size);

    static void Main() {
        const string url = "https://example.invalid/cua-wininet-repro";
        uint sizeA = 0;
        bool resultA = CacheA(url, IntPtr.Zero, ref sizeA);
        int errorA = Marshal.GetLastWin32Error();
        uint sizeW = 0;
        bool resultW = CacheW(url, IntPtr.Zero, ref sizeW);
        int errorW = Marshal.GetLastWin32Error();
        Console.WriteLine("A: " + resultA + " / " + errorA + " / " + sizeA);
        Console.WriteLine("W: " + resultW + " / " + errorW + " / " + sizeW);
    }
}
```

#### Relevant token observations

- Ordinary UAC Medium: `TokenElevationType=Limited`, `TokenElevation=0`, Administrators deny-only, ordinary user privileges.
- Cua and independently created SAFER Medium: `TokenElevationType=Full`, `TokenElevation=1`, Medium IL, Administrators deny-only, only `SeChangeNotifyPrivilege` retained.
- SAFER High and Medium kept the elevated-side `AuthenticationId`. The ordinary UAC token used the filtered-side `AuthenticationId`.
- In the independent High-to-Medium comparison, the inspected differences were the integrity level and associated integrity SID. No additional privilege removal was needed in either variant. Job Object restriction details were not proven identical.

The SAFER+Medium context is observably different from an ordinary UAC Medium token; the specific Windows security check or WinINet internal operation producing 12004 has **not** been located.

### Workaround and additional context

#### Connection to Cua

- [PR #4234](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4234) added the SAFER-derived standard-user token for browsers launched from an elevated Driver; [`browser_standard_user.rs` at the release commit](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85e2b1318bd77ccf3cfa88ccdf875a4bb7eaed19/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/browser_standard_user.rs#L163-L233) lowers that token to Medium IL.
- [PR #4282](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4282) reuses the token for `launch_app` direct and shell-helper launches ([release source](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/85e2b1318bd77ccf3cfa88ccdf875a4bb7eaed19/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/standard_user_launch.rs#L57-L77)).

The security goals of these PRs should be preserved. A workaround that launches the application elevated or globally disables the Driver's restrictions is not being requested.

#### A linked UAC-token alternative was not validated

A local exploratory experiment queried `TokenLinkedToken`. The returned token had the inspected SID/group/IL/elevation attributes of the ordinary UAC filtered token, but `TokenType=TokenImpersonation` with `SecurityIdentification`. Attempting `DuplicateTokenEx` to a primary token failed with `1346 / ERROR_BAD_IMPERSONATION_LEVEL`. No child was created or WinINet query executed under the linked handle. Therefore, simply substituting this handle is **not** a demonstrated fix.

A possible upstream solution may involve a legitimately obtainable primary UAC-filtered token, or an ordinary-user launch broker, with explicit checks for user, session, privileges, integrity, lifecycle and handle inheritance. This is a design direction, not a working patch.

#### Request

Please investigate WinINet compatibility with the elevated-Driver SAFER NormalUser + Medium launch context and consider regression coverage for x86 WinINet cache misses, A/W variants, both Cua launch routes, ordinary UAC versus derived token, browser process-tree launch, same-user/session enforcement, and no elevated fallback.

If requested, an expanded source-only reproduction bundle and anonymized token comparison can be provided after reviewing/correcting the integrity-label marshalling and rerunning the sanitized standalone SAFER branches. Those branches have not yet been rerun, and the draft launcher still requires marshalling review/correction and runtime validation; it is not included here as a validated reproducer. No company-specific URLs, credentials or full machine token logs are needed to reproduce the cache failure.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): correlate Sway windows with their AT-SPI top-level
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Sway, `browser_prepare` with `strategy: {kind: "existing_profile"}` refuses every time for a native-Wayland Chrome, with `browser_wrong_target_refused` or `browser_binding_ambiguous` ("could not prove which of pid N's accessibility top-levels renders window W"). `resolve_window_frame` has compositor routes for Hyprland and niri; on Sway it falls through to the X11 lookup, which never finds a Wayland container id, so an application with more than one AT-SPI top-level is never window-scoped. Chrome always has two: its `BrowserRootView` and an untitled `RootView` popup.
- What changed: on a Wayland session that is neither Hyprland nor niri, `resolve_window_frame` asks Sway's IPC for the process's containers. When Sway lists the requested id for that pid, the AT-SPI top-levels are correlated the way niri windows already are (`correlate_niri_frame`: by title, or by size for a Chromium root, keeping the single-root shortcut only while the compositor shows the process exactly one window). An id Sway doesn't list for the pid, such as an X11 window id, keeps the existing routes, so X11, Hyprland and niri behave as before.

## Related work

No existing issue that I could find.

RFC: not required; no public contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- Platform impact: Sway sessions only. Where Sway lists the requested container for the pid, window scope now requires a title (or Chromium root size) match. Before, a process with a single AT-SPI top-level was scoped however many Sway windows it had; that shortcut now holds only while Sway shows the process exactly one window, which is stricter.
- Not changed: `snapshot_binds_window_for` still doesn't treat Sway container ids as exact the way it does Hyprland and niri ids. That seemed better as a separate change.
- Risk and rollback: one function and a small helper in `platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs`; reverting the commit restores the old behaviour.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new unit test `sway_binds_only_the_requested_containers_root`, built from measured Sway and Chrome data; the existing Hyprland/niri correlation and `sway_ipc` tests pass; `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` passes (1113, under Xvfb); `cargo fmt --check` is clean; `cargo build --release -p cua-driver --features portal-input` succeeds.
- Manual platform evidence: headless Sway 1.12, Google Chrome 157 on native Wayland (`--ozone-platform=wayland --force-renderer-accessibility`), one browser window, driver run as `serve --permission-mode standard --grant existing-profile`:

  | Call | Before (0.52.13) | After (this branch) |
  |---|---|---|
  | `browser_prepare`, existing profile | `browser_wrong_target_refused`: could not prove which of the pid's accessibility top-levels renders window 5 | `ok`, `attached_existing_profile` |
  | `get_browser_state` | not reached | `binding_quality: exact`, `mutation_allowed: true` |
  | `browser_navigate` to https://example.com, semantic snapshot | not reached | "Example Domain" with its `Learn more` ref |
  | `browser_click` on `Learn more` (`delivery_mode: foreground`) | not reached | arrives at https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains |

- Known gaps:
  - I haven't run `bin/ci`.
  - Clippy on Rust 1.95 reports lints only in files this PR doesn't touch; I didn't run the pinned 1.97.1 toolchain.
  - No Sway end-to-end lane was run.
  - The size fallback can't match on Sway as written: Sway's container size includes its border, and Chrome's root view reports a different size again. So with several Chrome windows that share a title, binding still refuses, as before.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (Not applicable: this is meant to release.)
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). Not run; see Known gaps.

title: fix(agents): invalidate Git/uv caches when requirements change
body:
## Summary

A cached Git/uv installation can be reused after its repository, commit, Python version, or dependency extras change. Both the installer and the agent launch shortcut currently accept any completion marker under the same version directory. For example, adding a dependency extra to Hermes' manifest updates a fresh Space but leaves an existing installation on the old requirements.

With this fix, existing Spaces pick up changed requirements on their next managed start, without users clearing caches or recreating the Space. This prevents stale dependencies from being silently reused when an agent needs updated packages to start or load its tools. Unchanged installations continue to use the cache.

This gives Git/uv installations a completion marker derived from their source and dependency requirements. Matching caches are reused. Legacy or mismatched caches are rebuilt under the existing installation lock, and the marker is written after installation succeeds. The launch shortcut checks the same marker and verifies the agent's binary links, so links left pointing at an older baked copy are repaired before launch.

## Related work

Refs #6229 and #7978. Those changes cover installing without Git and selecting macOS uv archives. This addresses cache reuse after installation requirements change.

RFC: not required under the small internal bug-fix exemption. The change corrects cache validity checks within cua-agents and preserves public APIs, the manifest schema, and permission behavior.

## Compatibility and risk

Existing Git/uv caches receive a one-time rebuild on their next managed installation or launch. That can require downloads and delay the first start. Stale image caches are left in place; the repaired installation goes into the writable cache. Archive and npm cache behavior stays unchanged.

Switching between older and newer clients can trigger another rebuild. Binary links left by an older client are repaired using the matching cached installation. Saved agent homes, chats, credentials, and model configuration are outside the installation cache and remain unchanged.

## Validation

- Six regression tests execute the generated POSIX shell against isolated caches. They cover legacy writable and image caches, changes to each Git/uv requirement at the same version, matching cache reuse, failed repair and retry, launch readiness, stale binary links after rollback, and archive/npm cache compatibility. Git/uv and download commands are stubbed; cache checks, installation control flow, filesystem changes, and binary links run normally.
- Observed the cache regressions fail against the baseline, then pass with the fix. The stale-link case found during review also failed before its fix.
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64 and Ubuntu 24.04.5 arm64, Rust 1.97.1 and the manifest-pinned Node 24.21.0: `cargo test --locked -p cua-agents` passed, with 107 library tests passing and one existing opt-in test ignored. The Node runner integration passed on both platforms. Formatting and `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-agents --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- Host `bin/ci --quick --no-install --base 2ef2bf996ea840b695ab43f10ba87f98301d7b44`: two checks passed, one skipped because Cargo is unavailable on the shared host. Rust checks ran in the isolated environments. The docs generator router was unavailable locally; full CI and its sign-off remain pending.

title: No tool to read or invoke a menu-bar status item (MenuBarExtra) of an app with no windows
body:
invoke_menu requires a window_id, so an app that lives only in the menu bar (for example a SwiftUI MenuBarExtra app) cannot be driven: list_windows returns no windows and invoke_menu answers invalid_arguments (missing window_id).

The app's own accessibility element exposes AXExtrasMenuBar -> AXMenuBarItem -> AXMenu -> AXMenuItem, and AXPick on an entry works in the background (no pointer, no activation). Verified on macOS 27.3 with a menu-bar-only SwiftUI app: AXPick on an entry opened its window while the front app stayed unchanged.

Fix in our fork: new tool invoke_menu_extra {pid, item?, path?}; no path lists status items and entries; path invokes the entry; a menu the app has not built refuses menu_not_materialized and opens nothing. https://github.com/nqh-packages/cua/commit/c981db3b0 . Happy to open a PR.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep Finder in front while a foreground key leaves its rename field open
body:
Fixes #4615
Fixes #7727

## Why

With another app in front, a Finder rename through foreground keys never commits, and every call reports success. A foreground `press_key return` on the Finder window opens the rename field, then foreground HID delivery hands the front back to the previous app. Finder cancels the rename field when it stops being the active app, so the field closes about 0.2 s later. The typed name and the final Return then go to Finder's list. #7725 fixed the Finder-in-front half of #4615. This PR fixes the other-app-in-front half, which #7727 tracks.

## What changed

- `with_foreground_hid_activation` waits up to 250 ms after a successful action for an inline editor of the target window (the check #7725 added: a focused `AXTextField` in a WindowServer child window of that window). When the target is Finder and the field is open, it leaves Finder in front. Otherwise it hands the front back as before.
- The wait is a hard bound. Each accessibility probe gets only the time left of the 250 ms, and no probe starts once it is spent, so a busy Finder cannot hold the restore longer.
- Once Finder stays in front, the later `hotkey`, `type_text` and final `press_key return` calls reach the field through the path #7725 fixed.
- `press_key` reports it when it leaves Finder in front: the app's inline edit field is open, and the app ends the edit if it loses the front. The result says to finish the edit and then `bring_to_front` the previous app.

## Scope

This covers foreground HID keys (`press_key`, `hotkey`, foreground clicks with modifiers and the other callers of that helper) on Finder. Only `press_key` adds the note to its result. Other apps keep today's restore. Their behaviour was not measured.

`invoke_menu ["File", "Rename"]` with another app in front takes the background route on current main (#7756, #7761) and no longer activates Finder or hands the front back. This PR does not change it. Whether that route opens a field that the keys can then reach goes to the verification run below.

## Tradeoffs

- The previous app does not get the front back after the edit ends. Handing it back automatically would need state across calls. The result says how to do it instead.
- A foreground HID action on Finder that opens no field waits the full 250 ms before the front goes back. Other apps pay nothing.

## Blast Radius

macOS foreground HID delivery to Finder only. Finder stays in front only when the action succeeded and a focused text field sits in a child window of exactly the requested window. Every other case, including a failed lookup, restores as before. Rollback: revert the commit.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passed. Clippy, unit tests and the generated-reference check were skipped on this shared host and run in CI.
- New unit tests cover the keep-front decision: a field that appears after the key keeps the front, no field hands it back at the end of the wait, each probe's budget is only the time left, and an app other than Finder is never polled.
- Live Finder runs of the #4615 reproduction (keyboard route and menu route, TextEdit in front) still need to run on a macOS VM.

title: CI: Rust Linux unit rootless Xwayland capture step exits 1 after its test passes (compositor IPC: Unable to receive IPC response)
body:
`CI: Rust Linux unit` failed twice on pushes to main on 17 Nov, at 2501dda8 (run 44015497608) and aed25e92 (run 44076220576). Both commits are release PRs, so the code under test did not cause it.

The failing step is **Run X11 desktop capture regression (Xvfb and rootless Xwayland)** in `.github/workflows/ci-rust-linux.yml`. In both runs, `capture::tests::live_desktop_capture_shows_stacked_windows_at_their_screen_position` passes (`test result: ok. 1 passed`). Then, about 3 s later, the step logs:

```
[ERROR] [common/ipc-client.c:86] Unable to receive IPC response
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The test passed, so the exit code comes from the rootless Xwayland wrapper (`scripts/ci/linux/with-rootless-xwayland.sh`) or the compositor's IPC client around it, not from the test. The next push run was green both times.

Expected: a passed test leaves the step green. If the compositor IPC call is a readiness or teardown probe, it should retry or be bounded, not fail the step.

No existing issue covers it. Searched for `ipc-client.c`, `Unable to receive IPC response` and the test name.

title: fix(docs): install cua-sandbox without pinning an unpublished version
body:
Fixes #7899

## Problem

The Sandbox install pages named the source-tree version, which PyPI does not have:

- `guides/desktop.mdx`: `pip install 'cua-sandbox[driver]==0.11.9'` fails to resolve. PyPI's newest `cua-sandbox` is 0.10.2, and the 0.11.8 and 0.11.9 GitHub releases are still drafts.
- `guides/agent-frameworks.mdx` said the script "pins `cua-sandbox==0.11.9`". The script actually declares `cua-sandbox==0.9.0` in its inline metadata, so the sentence was wrong regardless of PyPI.
- `concepts/how-sandboxes-work.mdx` said `Sandbox.snapshot()` is not available "in `cua-sandbox` 0.11.9".

The cause is structural. The release PR stamps the new version into these pages, and that PR merges, and the docs deploy, before the GitHub release is published to PyPI. A new hard-coded version would go stale the same way, so this PR drops the versions from the pages.

## Change

- The desktop guide installs `cua-sandbox[driver]` without a pin. The agent-frameworks guide says the script declares its own `cua-sandbox` dependency, which `uv run` installs. The concepts page drops the version: no source version has `Sandbox.snapshot()`.
- `docs/scripts/tests/test_docs_version_facts.py` required the manifest version on these three pages. It now asserts that they do not pin `cua-sandbox` to an exact version.
- The docstring of `sync_sandbox_release_docs.py` explains the new rule. The script is unchanged, and it still updates any other page that names the previous version.

## Test plan

- The docs version-facts test and the sync-script tests pass. I put the `==0.11.9` pin back in the desktop guide and the test failed with `cua-sdk/guides/desktop.mdx pins 'cua-sandbox[driver]==0.11.9'`.
- Issue repro: in a fresh Python 3.12 uv environment, `uv pip install --dry-run --default-index https://pypi.org/simple 'cua-sandbox[driver]'` resolves to `cua-sandbox==0.10.2` ("Would install 42 packages"). 0.10.2 has the `driver` extra and `Sandbox.driver`.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass. The docs image-ref doctor check was skipped because the tool it needs was missing.

## Note

In the issue thread, a maintainer said the fix should be to publish the release and that the page would stay as it is. This PR changes the page anyway, because the docs are ahead of PyPI after every Sandbox release PR, not only for 0.11.7. Publishing the draft releases is still worth doing.

- [x] `bin/ci` (quick)
