title: fix(cua-driver): admit background AX actions on Catalyst pop-up menu items
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: a Mac Catalyst pop-up (`UIButton` with `showsMenuAsPrimaryAction`) opens its menu in a WindowServer window of its own. The menu's `AXMenu` has no `AXParent`, and neither it nor its items has `AXWindow`, so `element_window_id` cannot tie an item to the window and a background `click` on the item is refused `element_outside_target_window`. Since #7746 the refusal says the menu is still open, but the item can only be picked in the foreground.
- What changed: when an `AXMenuItem`'s menu answers both `AXParent` and `AXWindow` as absent (no value or unsupported; a failed read of either stays unproven), the gate now searches the requested window's own AX subtree for that menu, breadth first and bounded at 4096 elements read (children are fetched with `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValues`, capped at the room left, and never once the budget is full). The window's root group lists the menu among its children, so a match proves the item for **semantic AX actions only** (new `ElementAncestry::ProvenSemanticOnly`). A background `click` on the item by its token then runs `AXPress`. Routed pointer and key input stay refused, because the item does not draw in the requested window. Their refusal now says so and recommends acting by element.

## Related work

Fixes #4619
Fixes #7752

The approach is the one @Ed-Key proposed in #4619 and #4620. Part (a), the refusal note, shipped in #7746. Related: #3792 / #3793 (menu bar rows), #4507 (sheets), #4484.

RFC: not required. No new tool, parameter or refusal code. One semantic-only admission case is added inside the existing exact-target gate.

## Compatibility and risk

- Impact: macOS only. The only behaviour change: a semantic AX action on an item of a parentless `AXMenu` is admitted when the requested window's AX subtree lists that menu. All other refusals are unchanged. A menu the window does not list, or one the search budget does not reach, stays `Unproven` and keeps the #7746 note.
- Not covered: submenus of such a menu (the submenu's parent is an item, not nothing) and a menu listed only under a sheet addressed by the sheet's own id. Both stay refused, as on main.
- Risk and rollback: the search runs only when an addressed element is an item of a parentless menu and has no window ancestor, so ordinary clicks pay nothing. Rollback: revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `semantic_only_element_admits_only_semantic_ax` (core: `AxSemantic` executes; `WindowPointer`, `InsertText`, `GenericKey` and `ExactWindowKeys` refuse `element_outside_target_window` with advice `accessibility`; off-Space still refuses first), `a_listed_detached_menu_item_is_proven_for_semantic_actions_only` and `a_menu_is_found_only_under_the_window_within_the_budget` (macOS: the measured Catalyst tree shape, a menu the window does not list, an exhausted budget, a cycle, no children read past the budget) and `a_menu_is_detached_only_when_it_answers_no_parent_and_no_window` (a failed `AXParent` or `AXWindow` read is not an absence). Both new guards were mutation-checked: removing either makes its test fail. `admission_and_other_refusals_are_unchanged` now covers the new variant.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed; `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib exact_target` (19 passed) and `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -D warnings` passed locally. The full test suite and cross-target builds run in CI.
- Known gaps: no Catalyst fixture in the e2e harness, so there is no automated end-to-end run against a real Catalyst pop-up.

title: feat(cua-driver): support Helium profile attachment on Linux and macOS
body:
Salvaged from #3253

Fixes #3252

## Why

Cua Driver treated Helium as an unknown browser, so authorized existing-profile attachment failed before it could look for an endpoint. This lands @saatvik333's work from #3253 on current main. Their commits are kept as authored; our merge, docs and review-fix commits sit on top.

## What changed

- Linux and macOS now recognize Helium as a Chromium-family standalone browser and resolve its default profile (`net.imput.helium` under the XDG config home on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/net.imput.helium` on macOS).
- Existing-profile attachment to Helium goes only through its own process-owned `DevToolsActivePort`; the generic `/json/version` listener fallback stays off for that route. Ordinary preparation and actions keep the PID-owned listener contract Chrome and Edge use. On Linux, a `--user-data-dir` recovered from Helium's packed (space-joined) command line counts only when the process tree holds the listening socket that the directory's `SingletonSocket` links to, and that directory is the only one, among the directories on the paths of every file the process tree holds open, that links to the socket. A symlink is only text, and the real profile always lies on the path of the browser's open databases, so a forged directory linking to the real socket either holds no browser file or becomes a second claimant, and is refused.
- Merged main: the Linux default-profile lookup now goes through main's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`-aware resolver, and the macOS Helium gate moved into main's shared `discover_endpoint`. The two reference pages #3253 edited were removed on main, so the Helium notes moved to the Browsers guide and the platform-support table.

- Review fixes: the Linux `/proc/net/unix` parser reads bytes and keeps each path verbatim, so a non-UTF-8 path no longer hides every listener and a profile under a `TMPDIR` with consecutive spaces still matches its socket; macOS recognizes Helium only by Imput's `net.imput.helium` bundle id, since an unrelated WebKit app shares the name; the isolated-launch E2E row omits `pid` instead of sending `null` for Chrome and Edge.

## Scope

Covers Linux and macOS attachment to a Helium profile that already exposes an endpoint. Leaves out automated setup of Helium's internal remote-debugging page (still a refusal), and does not recognize Helium on Windows.

## Blast Radius

Only processes whose executable basename is exactly `helium` (Linux) or whose bundle id is `net.imput.helium` or one of its helpers (macOS) take the new paths. Other browsers keep their current parsing and discovery. The new CI steps install a pinned Helium build, check its SHA-256, and run it only in the standalone-browser and hosted macOS lanes.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (quick stage) pass on this head, after merging main.
- The standalone-browser E2E workflow, which holds the Linux Helium lane, is dispatched on this head.
- Not changed on review: applying the `DevToolsActivePort` requirement to ordinary Helium preparation. That path grants the same PID-owned listener trust it grants Chrome and Edge, so it opens nothing new for Helium.
- `platform-linux` browser-platform unit tests cover the packed command line, a forged `--user-data-dir`, a foreign-owned socket, and a forged directory aliasing the real socket (sibling, sibling holding an incidental file, ancestor, descendant), plus datagram and dead sockets. They run in CI; this host ran out of space to build them.
- A real Chromium on Linux holds dozens of files open under its profile's `Default/`, which is the evidence the ownership check reads.
- macOS and the desktop E2E lanes run in CI. They did not run on this Linux host.

title: fix(cua-driver): bound CDP sends and existing-profile endpoint proofs
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: after an existing-profile attach, browser calls could wait forever instead of refusing. Three awaits on that path had no deadline:
  - A CDP send held the socket's writer lock without a deadline. If the browser stopped reading, the send stalled, and every later call on the shared existing-profile socket queued behind it. The call timeout only started after the send finished.
  - Each exact bind re-proves the approved endpoint. On macOS that reads `DevToolsActivePort` and runs `lsof`, and neither had a timeout.
  - The existing-profile reconnect checked its 32 s deadline only between steps. The wait on another caller's reconnect, and the classification, fingerprint, consent and re-proof steps, could each hang past it.
- What changed:
  - The call deadline now also covers taking the writer lock and sending. If the send is cut short, the socket is shut down before the writer lock is released, because a partly written frame leaves it unusable: both halves are dropped, so the browser sees the connection end even while the pool still holds it. A call that then takes the lock sees the socket closed and sends nothing. The next call reconnects through the normal path.
  - Endpoint re-proofs time out after 10 s with `browser_route_unavailable`.
  - The whole reconnect, including the wait on another caller's reconnect and the grant and pool lookups after it, ends within its 32 s bound. When it runs out of time, the driver removes the grant and returns `browser_reconnect_exhausted` with `last_error: "timed_out"` at the deadline; releasing the grant and closing any prompt finish afterwards on their own. If the pool had already opened a socket for this reconnect, the driver tries for up to 5 s to close the prompt that dial may have raised. Before that, including while waiting for another caller's dial, a prompt in the window belongs to someone else and is left alone; the same rule applies when the consent step fails. Because the platform finds a prompt by its window rather than by its dial, closing it also waits until no other dial to the same browser endpoint is running, and is skipped if one still is when the 5 s run out. The close runs as its own task that keeps that endpoint's dials waiting until the platform's native work has returned, even after the caller stops waiting. Each endpoint has its own prompt lock, which a dial takes before the pool-wide dial gate, so a stalled close never holds up dials to other browsers. Consent handling for a reconnect attempt starts only after that attempt's own dial has begun, so a reconnect queued behind another caller's dial does not answer that caller's prompt. The grant moves to its new generation before the pool hands the socket over, so if the reconnect fails or is cut short first, the pool releases the old generation; it no longer keeps the socket or the endpoint's port. A follower that waits out the bound gets `last_error: "reconnect_in_progress"` and does not end the grant.
  - Releasing an ended grant (socket, consent, and turning remote debugging back off if the driver turned it on) now runs as its own task, so a caller cancelled partway cannot leave the socket or consent held. The remote-debugging cleanup is browser UI work on macOS. It used to run inline on an async worker and now runs on a blocking thread. Other callers that end a grant wait at most 10 s for the socket release and this cleanup together (a timed-out reconnect does not wait), since the release needs the pool lock a slow dial can hold. A failure is queued for the session-end retry even when it arrives later. If the session already ended while the cleanup was running, the cleanup retries at once instead. A cleanup counts as running from the moment its grant leaves the registry, under the same lock the session-end hook holds, and under both the public and the transport session id. The session-end hook also merges its own failures into the retry queue instead of replacing entries queued meanwhile.
  - macOS: `lsof` is killed when the proof that started it gives up.

## Related work

Fixes #3241

This bounds every browser-side await on the attach, bind and reconnect path that the issue's acceptance list asks for. I could not reproduce the original wedge, so I have not proven which await caused it. It was reported once, on a nightly that predates both #3211 and #7999. The follow-up symptom, where `browser_prepare` succeeds and the next bind asks for the grant again, did not reproduce in the current tree: prepare and bind use the same grant key for CLI, MCP and SDK callers, and `approved_existing_profile_attach_claims_then_binds_one_generation` covers it.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: an existing-profile call that used to hang now returns a structured refusal (`browser_route_unavailable` or `browser_reconnect_exhausted`). No schema, tool or protocol changes.
- Risk and rollback: a send that takes longer than the call's whole timeout now closes the socket. A healthy local browser never comes close to that. For an existing-profile socket, the redial that follows may show Chrome's consent prompt again. Rollback is a plain revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new tests; the first three hang on main and pass with the fix:
  - `cdp_ws::tests::a_stalled_send_cannot_hold_other_calls_past_their_timeout`
  - `v2_tests::existing_profile_bind_refuses_when_the_endpoint_reproof_stalls`
  - `v2_tests::existing_profile_reconnect_refuses_within_its_bound_when_a_process_check_stalls`
  - `v2_tests::a_cleanup_that_fails_after_its_session_ended_retries_at_once` (covers a session end by either id; fails without the session-end coordination)
- The stalled-send test also checks that the browser sees the socket end while the connection is still held. The reconnect test runs three cases: a stall before any dial (no prompt is closed), a stall after a failed dial (the prompt close is bounded), and a stall after a dial while another caller's dial to the same browser is still running (no prompt is closed). Each case asserts the refusal arrives within the 32 s bound. The stalled-close case also checks that the endpoint stays locked while dials to another browser are not held up.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib -- browser::` (all pass), `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -D warnings`, `bin/ci --quick` green.
- Mutation checks: the reconnect test fails if the timed-out reconnect waits for the grant release before refusing, if the prompt-close bound or the cleanup bound is removed, if a late cleanup failure is not queued, or if a reconnect that never dialed closes a prompt. The stalled-send test fails if an interrupted send only marks the socket closed without dropping it. The pool's reconnect tests fail if a reconnect counts as dialed before it takes the dial gate or when it joins a reopened socket. `a_reconnect_waiting_for_another_dial_leaves_its_prompt_alone` fails if consent handling does not wait for this attempt's dial, and `a_reconnect_dropped_before_its_handoff_retires_the_old_generation` fails without the old-generation release. The reconnect test's third case, where another caller's dial is still running at the timeout, fails if the prompt is closed without waiting for the dial gate.

title: fix(cua-driver): recommend foreground for unverifiable background keys to Chromium and Electron apps
body:
## Why

On macOS, Chrome-family browsers and Electron apps often drop a background `press_key` or `hotkey`, and the result was a bare `effect: "unverifiable"`, the same as for a key that landed. The caller got no sign to retry in the foreground. This lands @lucharo's fix from #6967 and corrects the `hotkey` description that still called the background path trusted by Chromium.

Salvaged from #6967
Fixes #4997

## What changed

- When a background `press_key` or `hotkey` to a Chromium or Electron app ends `unverifiable`, the public `ActionResult` carries `escalation.target: "foreground"` and the text result adds one sentence. Internally the tool payload uses the legacy `escalation: { recommended: "foreground", reason, requires: ["window_id"] }` shape the Screen Sharing refusals use, which the dispatch seam projects to `escalation.target`; `press_key` also sets the escalation on its action record directly. (#6967, authored by @lucharo)
- A new `type_text::is_chromium_embedder(pid)` (bundle check or Electron) replaces the identical private helper in `set_value.rs`. (#6967)
- The `press_key` and `hotkey` descriptions, and the generated MCP reference, now name this escalation by its public field, `escalation.target`. `hotkey` no longer says Chromium and Electron accept background combos as trusted live input.

## Scope

macOS `press_key` and `hotkey` only. Foreground calls, confirmed results and other apps are unchanged. Linux already refuses background keys to Chromium embedders; Windows is unchanged. WKWebView targets (#5355) are not covered.

## Tradeoffs

The hint also appears on a key that did land, because no oracle tells the two apart. The text says the key "may not have arrived" and asks the caller to check the window before retrying. A producer-observed `escalation.reason` stays deferred to #4009, so the projected public reason stays `delivery_failed` as for every `foreground` escalation.

## Blast Radius

Callers of macOS background keys to Chromium and Electron apps see one optional field and one sentence more. A caller that ignores `escalation` sees no change.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (quick stage) pass. The Rust checks and the generated-reference drift check need a macOS build and run in CI.
- #6967's tests in `press_key.rs` and `hotkey.rs` assert the full structured payload for each branch (background to a Chromium app, background to another app, foreground to a Chromium app, confirmed).

Downstream migrations, such as Hermes, belong in their own repositories.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse background type_text keys when the target lacks focus
body:
## Why

A background `type_text` addressed by `element_token` falls through to CGEvent keys when the AX insert does not land. That rung wrote `AXFocused` on the element and posted process-scoped keys without checking that focus moved. When a web field kept focus on its sibling, the text went into the sibling: in Safari's iCloud Mail compose, the Subject text landed in To. The earlier fix for #5354 stopped this from reporting a false zero with retry advice, but the keys still went to the wrong field.

## What changed

- Background rung 2 now confirms the addressed element holds keyboard focus (`element_has_keyboard_focus`, retried for up to 200ms) before posting any key, using the same gate `press_key` already uses. If focus never arrives, the call returns `target_focus_unconfirmed` with `dispatched: false` and posts nothing.
- The refusal is `effect: "refused"`, `retryable: true`, `delivered_chars: 0` when the AX insert before it is known to have missed, and points at the pixel form (x,y). When that AX insert could not be observed (web content), it is `effect: "indeterminate"`, not retryable, with no delivered count, and says to read the window first.
- `with_confirmed_key_focus` and `KeyFocusUnconfirmed` move from `press_key.rs` to `input/ax_actions.rs` so both tools share them.

## Scope

Covers the macOS background CGEvent rung reached with an `element_token`. It leaves out the foreground rung (#3912), the terminal-emulator rung, and the pixel-focus form, which already focuses by clicking. It does not add the "delivered elsewhere" detection the issue suggested (watching the previously focused element); refusing before any key is sent makes that unnecessary for this rung.

## Blast Radius

macOS `type_text` only. An element-token call whose AX insert fails and whose element does not report keyboard focus now gets a refusal instead of keys sent to whatever was focused. Chromium and WebKit web fields that do take focus report it through `AXFocused`, which the gate accepts, as it does for `press_key`.

## Verification

- Repro on the real surface with the installed driver: a WKWebView page with To and Subject fields, where Subject hands focus back to To unless a pointer press focuses it. `type_text` by Subject's token put `hello subject` into To, left Subject empty, and returned "Sent (unverified)".
- New unit test `unfocused_target_refuses_before_any_key_and_keeps_retry_safe` pins both refusal shapes. The existing `press_key` tests cover the shared gate never dispatching without focus.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass. Rust build, tests and clippy run in CI.

Fixes #5182

title: test(spaces-macos): pin a window click on the web UI viewer reaching the Space
body:
## Why

#4676 reports that clicks in the Cua Spaces viewer never reached a local Linux Space, while keys did (app 0.7.0, spacesd 0.5.0, ARM64). On current main, clicks do reach it, on the same image and architecture. So this PR has no product change. It adds a test for the one link in that path that had none, so a regression fails CI.

## What changed

- New test `aClickOnTheViewerThroughTheWindowGoesToTheSpace`: a mouse down and up routed the way `NSWindow` routes them (a hit test from the frame view, through the `WKWebView`) reach the viewer surface. The viewer then emits `move`, `down` and `up` at the clicked normalized point.
- The old `viewer.hitTest(...) === viewer.input` line only checked the surface view on its own, and the new test covers it, so it is gone. That test is renamed `aTileAndAHiddenViewerTakeNoPointerInput` to match what it still checks.

## Scope

Covers the web UI's inline viewer (`VideoSurfaceView` over the page's `WKWebView`). `ViewerInputTests` already covers the native Space window path, from click to `interactive_input` on the session. The guest side (spacesd to X11) is covered by the image gates. No product code changes.

## Verification

- Ran the app's real viewer stack against a local `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04` Space (aarch64, spacesd 0.16.1, Xvfb on `:1`). That stack is `WebUIVideoSurfaces` with a `WKWebView` in a window, `LiveStreamSession` on the SDK, and a mouse down and up sent through `NSWindow.sendEvent`. A full-screen `xev` in the guest logged `ButtonPress` and `ButtonRelease`, button 1, at root (320,200), which is (0.25, 0.25) of 1280×800.
- `cua sb stream-probe ... --action click:0.5,0.5` on the same Space returned `delivered: true`, and `xev` logged the press and release.
- Mutation check: when `VideoSurfaceView.hitTest` returns nil for clicks (the reported symptom), the click lands on the `WKWebView`, no pointer events are sent, and the new test fails. The `WebUIVideoSurfacesTests` suite passes (44 tests), and the scoped repository checks pass.

Refs #4676. This PR does not fix it, since current main already forwards clicks. Whether to close #4676 depends on the reporter re-testing, as asked on the issue.

title: test(cua-driver): pin the macOS cursor to the target's display on the layouts from #5336

The later reports in the thread are from 0.38.0, before that fix. This PR pins the fix to the display layouts reported in the issue so it stays fixed, and closes the issue.

For each one it checks that only the display holding the target paints the cursor, at that display's backing scale, with the target inside the painted tile.

title: [Bug]: Windows: clicking an item in a dropdown or menu from a viewer closes it without selecting the item
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

From a viewer on a Windows Space, clicking an item in an open popup closes the popup without choosing the item. Opening the popup and hovering its items work.

The driver's desktop click forces the popup to the foreground before clicking, and that alone makes the app close it. The same move, down and up sent without that activation selects the item.

Seen with a Chrome `<select>` list, a Chrome datalist dropdown, Chrome's page context menu, a Win32 context menu and a WinForms ComboBox list.

### Reproduction

1. Open a Windows Space in a viewer that speaks wire v2 `interactive_input` (display session, input enabled).
2. In Chrome, open a page with `<select><option>Fall</option><option selected>Spring</option></select>`.
3. Click the select. The list opens.
4. Click "Fall".

### Expected behavior

The list closes and the select shows "Fall", as with a physical mouse.

### Actual behavior

The list closes and the select still shows "Spring". The page sees its window lose and regain focus (`blur`, then `focus`) and no `change` event. Depending on timing, the acknowledgement either reports success or a `DeliveryFailed` rejection.

### Environment

- Space: Windows 11 Pro 24H2 (26100), 3840x2160 at 200% scaling, cua-spacesd 0.10.1, display session
- Browser: Chrome 156.0.8078.75
- Reproduced through cua-driver 0.38.1-nightly.20261104 with `click` and `scope: "desktop"`, the call cua-spacesd makes for a viewer click
- Line references are at `dde4a4b6`; the click path is byte-identical to cua-spacesd 0.10.1 (`3458aae1d`)

### Evidence

**Cause**

1. cua-spacesd folds a viewer's down and up into one `click` call with `scope: "desktop"` (`libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/tool_input.rs:313-328`). Hover becomes `move_cursor` (`tool_input.rs:406-418`), so hovering works.
2. The desktop click resolves its target with `WindowFromPoint` and `GetAncestor(GA_ROOT)` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/click.rs:300-318`). With a popup open, that is the popup window, not the app's main window.
3. `ClickMode::Desktop` always activates the target (`platform-windows/src/input/mouse.rs:569`) through `force_foreground_assisted` (`mouse.rs:671`, `input/inject.rs:123-162`). **Activating the popup deactivates the window that owns it, and the app dismisses the popup in response.**

Activation alone reproduces it, with no mouse input:
- `AttachThreadInput` plus `SetForegroundWindow` on an open Chrome select list succeeds, even though the list has `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`.
- The browser window gets `blur`.
- Chrome hides the list about 138 ms later and destroys it about 12 ms after that.

**What the caller sees depends on timing.** The after-click check runs 120 ms after the input (`mouse.rs:756`, `mouse.rs:799-812`), inside that window:
- When the popup is already destroyed and its owner is in front, `post_action_foreground_allowed` accepts it (`platform-windows/src/win32/windows.rs:202-209`). The tool returns `✅ Sent click ... (desktop scope)` although nothing was selected.
- When the popup is hidden but not yet destroyed, the check fails after the input was sent.
- When activation fails, the driver sends `VK_NONAME` and retries (`inject.rs:150-160`). The page receives `keydown` with key `Unidentified`, and the call returns `foreground_unavailable: Windows did not activate exact target HWND 0x… (actual foreground HWND 0x…); no mouse input was sent`.

The error has no structured `code`, so cua-spacesd maps it to `DeliveryFailed` (`libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/lib.rs:341-353`). `viewer.rs:599-601` logs only the code, not the message.

**Popups tested**

| Popup | Window | Desktop `click` | Plain `SendInput` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chrome `<select>` list | `Chrome_WidgetWin_1`, `WS_POPUP`, `NOACTIVATE\|TOOLWINDOW`, owned by the browser window | not selected, 3 of 3, tool reported success | selected |
| Chrome datalist dropdown | same, plus `TOPMOST` | not selected, tool reported success | selected |
| Chrome page context menu | same as datalist | Reload not run, `foreground_unavailable` before input | not tested |
| Win32 context menu | `#32768`, `WS_POPUP`, `TOOLWINDOW\|TOPMOST`, no owner | not run, `foreground_unavailable` before input | item ran |
| WinForms ComboBox list | `ComboLBox`, child of the desktop, no owner | not selected, `foreground_unavailable` before input | selected |

"Plain `SendInput`" is the same absolute move, down and up the driver sends (`mouse.rs:604-716`), without the activation step.

### Workaround and additional context

Workaround: after opening the popup, choose an item with the arrow keys and Enter.

**Proposed fix.** In `send_click_synthesized_mods_impl` (`mouse.rs:560`), skip activation for `ClickMode::Desktop` when the target:
- is not the foreground window, and
- runs on the foreground window's thread (`GetWindowThreadProcessId`).

A window on that thread already shares the active window's input state, so a plain `SendInput` reaches it the way a physical click does.

This covers every popup above. Chrome's popups are owned by the browser window and run on its UI thread. `#32768` and `ComboLBox` have no owner but run on the form's thread.

Checking `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` instead would miss `#32768`, `ComboLBox` and a WinForms `ContextMenuStrip`, which don't set it.

Two follow-on changes in the same function:
- Gate the background-only steps on `mode == ClickMode::NonActivating` instead of `!activate`, so the new case doesn't pick them up. These are `NoActivateGuard`, the TOPMOST raise and restore (`mouse.rs:692-704`), and the cursor restore (`mouse.rs:756-782`).
- Skip the after-click check for this case.

The desktop drag path has the same activation step (`mouse.rs:1018-1022`), for example when dragging a dropdown's scrollbar.

**Tests.**
- Unit-test the same-thread decision as a pure function, next to the foreground policy tests at `windows.rs:725-790`.
- Add an E2E sibling of `desktop_scope_windowless_click_lands_on_control` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-e2e/tests/desktop_scope_windows_test.rs:241`). It opens the WPF fixture's `CboColor` (`libs/cua-driver/tests/fixtures/apps/windows/wpf/MainWindow.xaml:216`) and clicks an item, both with desktop clicks. I haven't confirmed that WPF popups reproduce this on current `main`, so the test needs a mutation check.

**Related.**
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5412 fixes a separate false failure seen in the same testing. A WinForms `ContextMenuStrip` item click lands, but the driver reports `foreground_unavailable` because the strip hides instead of being destroyed.
- https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/7696 is the macOS counterpart for background clicks on Chrome popup rows, with a different mechanism.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): report safe browser signature diagnostics
body:
## Summary

When macOS isolated-browser discovery finds an installed browser but its signature verification fails, it currently discards the reason and returns only a generic unavailable refusal.

Preserve bounded, safe verification details for failed candidates: the fixed browser identifier, verification stage, diagnostic category and exit code. Keep looking for a trusted candidate and return diagnostics only when discovery fails. Raw command output, paths and certificate details never enter the response.

## Related work

Fixes #7742.

This is a focused diagnostic correction using the existing optional refusal detail field. No SDK signatures, refusal codes, permission boundaries or trust requirements change; no RFC proposed.

## Compatibility and risk

- Keep the Apple anchor, vendor team and identifier requirements, sealed-symlink verification, trusted installation locations, candidate ordering and success short-circuit unchanged.
- Preserve the existing refusal code and message. No installed candidate retains its existing detail-free refusal.
- Unknown or localized codesign failures receive a generic safe category, not raw stderr. Signature checks are never bypassed.
- macOS adapter only; no generated bindings or dependency changes in this patch. Reverting the commit restores the previous generic diagnostics.

## Validation

On macOS arm64, before syncing the subsequent main-branch release/packaging/docs changes:
- 34 browser-platform unit tests passed, including four new tests covering failure categories/stages, private/oversized command output, candidate fallback/short-circuit, and aggregate failure details.
- Strict `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- `bin/ci --quick --no-install`: 5 passed, 3 heavy checks skipped.
- Full platform-macos test run: 819 unit tests passed, 1 failed, 13 ignored; 2 integration tests passed. Desktop-only and documentation tests remained skipped/ignored as designed.
- The failing, unchanged `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow` expects the ASCII-apostrophe `Don't Allow`, which is absent from this host's system labels (the curly-apostrophe form is present). Restoring the exact main baseline reproduced the same failure; restoring the candidate then passed all 34 focused tests again.
- A temporary native harness compiled the exact modified verification helper: stock Chrome and Edge passed, and an intentionally mismatched identifier on unchanged Chrome returned `vendor_requirement_not_satisfied`, stage `signature_verification`, exit code 3. No browser was altered or re-signed. This is a controlled negative check, not a natural damaged-installation end-to-end reproduction.

Final head `00cc287cde822c0ff8a9a248c91145c7f353e55d`, based on main `dde4a4b64a`:
- All 34 focused browser-platform tests passed again.
- `bin/ci --no-install`: 6 checks passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped. Strict Clippy, formatting, headers, image refs and Windows cfg checks passed. The same system-consent-label test failed (819 passed, 1 failed, 13 ignored); both integration tests passed.
- The release UniFFI drift check was skipped because `libs/cua-driver/typescript/node_modules` is absent. Docs generators were not routed because docs dependencies are absent. No dependencies were installed for these checks.
- No claim of a fully green aggregate suite or completed desktop/cross-platform E2E is made. The local-CI signoff is intentionally unchecked.

title: Hoy 0.17.2 counts VMPal MCP helpers as running VMs and blocks VMPal launch
body:
## Environment

- Apple silicon, macOS 27.3 beta (26C5047e)
- `hoy 0.17.2`, release `0.17.2-80749511` (commit `80749511`)
- Hoy Endpoint Security extension active, version 0.17.2
- VMPal 0.122

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have VMPal's MCP servers running in an MCP client. The process modes are `VMPalMachine --mcp-library` and `VMPalMachine --mcp <VM UUID>`. In my case, the guest was suspended and no `VMPalMachine --machine` process was running.
2. With the Hoy extension active, run `hoy doctor`.
3. Open VMPal, or run the `VMPalMachine` executable bundled with VMPal with `--help`.

## Expected

VMPal opens and `--help` prints usage. Idle MCP server processes consume zero macOS VM slots.

## Actual

The Hoy extension blocked both the VMPal GUI and its helper. `VMPalMachine --help` exited with status 137. The denial log listed existing MCP server PIDs among the occupied slots. I checked those processes' arguments and confirmed they were in MCP server modes.

On the same retry, `hoy doctor` reported:

```text
ok   vm-slots         0 of 2 macOS VM slots in use (Virtualization.framework 0, QEMU 0, hoy VMM 0)
ok   limit-service    the Hoy system extension is approved and active (0.17.2)
```

The extension logged (PIDs and paths omitted):

```text
com.trycua.hoy.es [limit] refused a macOS guest: … (…/VMPalMachine) exec'd a hypervisor image [unknown] with 12 of 2 places taken
```

A Hoy image download was in progress when I first observed the issue. Whether that is required to reproduce it is unknown.

title: fix(cua-driver): reject invalid legacy screenshot dimensions
body:
## Summary

Fixes #8010. Current main accepts `max_dimension: 0` at the shared dispatch boundary despite its schema minimum. Reject zero, negative, non-integer and out-of-range legacy screenshot limits with structured `invalid_arguments` before any platform lookup or capture. The separate `max_image_dimension: 0` native-resolution override remains valid.

## Validation

The new boundary regression fails on upstream main and passes with this fix. Valid limits, omission, null and native-resolution overrides are covered. Complete core tests, strict all-target core Clippy, formatting and diff checks passed. Quick CI: 5 passed, 3 skipped; tests and Clippy ran separately. Native screenshot capture, Linux/Windows execution and hosted CI are outstanding. No full local-CI signoff is claimed.

No RFC: enforces the existing input contract. This is a user-visible fix; no `no-release` label is requested.

title: test(cua-driver): cover native Hyprland overlay focus isolation
body:
Salvaged from #3465

## Why
The native Wayland cursor overlay already ships (#3152, #3572), but nothing checks on a live Hyprland desktop that it stays out of the way: one `cua-agent-cursor` layer-shell surface per output, no focusable client, and no workspace or active-window change while the cursor moves. #3465 by @LikelyLucid adds that regression test; this PR lands it.

## What changed
- @LikelyLucid's commit adds `hyprland_overlay_focus_test`, kept as authored.
- On top: the test moves into `cua-driver-e2e` next to the other native Hyprland rows and drives the daemon through the testkit's `McpDriver`. That gives it an isolated state root, a private socket and a reaped daemon, replacing a fixed `/tmp` socket that a failed assertion left behind.
- The test subscribes to Hyprland's event socket before the daemon starts and fails on any focus, workspace, monitor-focus or window-open event until the daemon exits, so a change that reverts on its own still fails.
- The test is listed in the manual native-Hyprland gate (`manual-e2e-allowlist.txt` and the test harnesses guide), which the ignored-test inventory requires. Without that entry the inventory check fails on current main.

## Scope
Test and docs only. No product code changes. The test is `#[ignore]` and runs only in a disposable native Hyprland desktop, like `hyprland_native_observation_test`.

## Blast Radius
None for users. Plain `cargo test` is unaffected because the test is ignored. The inventory check now covers it.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks (formatting, SPDX headers) pass.
- The ignored-test inventory check fails with the contributor's commit alone on current main and passes with this PR's allowlist entry.
- No automated Hyprland lane exists, so the live run is a manual native-Hyprland gate.

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve physical pixels in embedded Windows SDK
body:
Salvaged from #3450

Fixes #3449

## Why

On Windows at more than 100% display scaling, the embedded SDK runs inside a DPI-unaware host such as Node and reports and captures only the virtualized upper-left part of the desktop (`1707x1067 @ 1.0` on a `2560x1600 @ 150%` screen). The standalone daemon, which has a PMv2 manifest, captures the whole desktop. @wszkxlllll's change makes every thread the embedded runtime owns enter Per-Monitor V2 awareness. It leaves the host process and the caller's thread as they are, and it fails closed when Windows refuses the context.

## What changed

- @wszkxlllll's commits, kept as authored: a new `platform_windows::dpi` module (shared failure state for each executor, gated `spawn_blocking` and `spawn`, an `owned_thread` wrapper), an ABI executor whose Tokio threads all start through it, `RuntimeUnavailable` on DPI failure, guards on capture entry points, and regressions for late thread creation.
- A merge of current main. Main split `tools/impl_.rs` into per-tool modules, so a follow-up commit routes every Windows tool module through `crate::dpi::spawn_blocking` and `crate::dpi::spawn`, the same way the original PR routed `impl_.rs`.
- Main redesigned the recorder's state worker in `cua-driver-core`. The core-level thread initializer this PR added there is dropped. `recording_hooks::app_state_json_for` already joins the executor's owner through `with_recording_state_thread` on the recorder thread, so the cross-platform crate stays unchanged.
- An overlay started on the host thread during registry creation now joins the registered ABI executor's DPI owner instead of taking its own. A PMv2 rejection there makes the executor unavailable instead of only logging. Without an embedded executor (the standalone daemon), it still gets an independent owner.

## Scope

Covers Windows embedded-SDK capture and input coordinates, and the Windows threads Cua owns (the Tokio ABI executor, UIA and package-scan workers, the overlay thread, the recorder state worker). Coordinate conversion, the public tool and ABI schemas, and the standalone executable's manifest are unchanged. macOS and Linux only get the `AbiExecutor` wrapper around the same Tokio runtime.

## Blast Radius

Windows only, in practice: every Windows tool's blocking work now runs a per-thread DPI check before and after its body. With no owner (the standalone daemon), the check is a no-op. An embedded executor that loses PMv2 refuses new GUI work with `RuntimeUnavailable`, and shutdown, session revocation and recording finalization keep working.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX, lockfiles) pass, as does the e2e inventory test, which now includes the new ignored SDK capture test.
- `cargo xwin clippy -p cua-driver-sdk -p platform-windows --tests --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Not run here: the Windows unit tests, the interactive capture lane (`embedded_abi_uses_physical_pixels_from_an_unaware_host_thread`) and the Windows desktop matrix. On #3450, the native lane's `windows-webview2-left-click-px-background` row failed twice at the same SHA after a UIA cooldown, and nobody showed whether the DPI change caused it. That row has to be rerun at this head.

title: fix(cua-driver): skip drops refused by synthetic drag targets
body:
A synthetic browser drag currently dispatches `drop` even when an ordinary destination ignores `dragover` or explicitly sets `dropEffect = "none"`. A page can therefore handle a drop it refused, and the driver reports delivery.

This change makes the `browser_pointer` DOM-event route honor the destination's acceptance and the source's allowed effects. On refusal it sends `dragleave`, ends the gesture with `dropEffect = "none"`, releases the pointer, and returns `browser_action_unavailable`. It preserves accepted drops, including the plain-text editable-target case. The regression fixture checks both refusal paths, their event order, and the existing accepted-drop case.

### Verification

- Compared the JavaScript embedded in the upstream driver and this patch in headless Chrome 157 and Edge 157 on Windows. Each browser passed 40 candidate cases across element-reference and coordinate destinations. In both browsers the upstream handler emitted one drop for each of the two refusal cases on each route. The patched handler emitted zero.
- Ran the accepted case and both rejected cases from the Rust test's HTML fixture in both browsers. Checked both changed Rust files with rustfmt.

Related to #7617, which covers a drag canceled at its source.

title: fix(cua-driver): build move_cursor action records in its producers
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `move_cursor` was one of the action families whose public result came from `ActionExecutionRecord::from_legacy` reading hand-written JSON (`scope`, `path`, `hover_delivered`, `screen_point`, ...). The dispatch seam then replaced that JSON with the projected `ActionResult`, so the JSON existed only to be interpreted. This is a Slice B family migration from RFC #3473.
- What changed:
  - New `ActionExecutionRecord::cursor_move(transport, args)` in `cua-driver-core`: a cursor move is `unverifiable` with `not_applicable` delivery, whichever transport moved it. Requested delivery is computed the same way `from_legacy` did.
  - The macOS, Windows and Linux `move_cursor` producers attach that record on every success branch. Real-pointer moves use the transport that ran: `MacosCgEventHid`, `WindowsSetCursorPos`, `LinuxWaylandVirtualPointer`, `LinuxLibei` (when the Wayland desktop move falls back to libei) or `LinuxXTest`. Agent-cursor and window-target moves use `AgentCursorOverlay`. A Linux Hyprland hover that did or may have reached the app uses `LinuxHyprlandIsolatedInput`, which projects the same `synthetic_events` route.
  - The off-target `MoveCursorTool` stubs in `platform-linux` and `platform-windows` attach the same overlay record.
  - Deleted: the per-branch JSON payloads, the `move_cursor` arm and the `SetCursorPos` path in `transport_from_legacy`, the overlay check in `actual_delivery_from_legacy`, and the Linux `HoverOutcome::Refused(reason)` / `refusal_reason`, whose reason only ever reached the discarded JSON.

## Related work

Refs #3473

RFC: #3473 (Slice B, typed action producers). This PR migrates one family. It does not finish Slice B or the RFC.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: none intended. The first commit pins the public projection that `from_legacy` produced on main for every `move_cursor` payload shape: real-pointer moves → `global_input`, agent-cursor and window moves → `synthetic_events`, all `unverifiable` with `not_applicable` delivery. The second commit checks that the direct records produce the same projection. Result text is unchanged. Two things change only internally: the recorded transport for a Hyprland agent-seat hover, and the `next_call` and `reason` fields in the discarded producer JSON. The dispatch seam already replaced those fields before any caller saw them, and the generic recovery hint still adds `next_call`.
- Risk and rollback: if a `move_cursor` branch returned success without a record, `from_legacy` now returns `None` for every scope, desktop included (only `move_cursor` refusals still normalize there, agent-cursor and window refusals on the overlay route; `move_cursor_refusal_normalizes_on_the_overlay_route` pins that), and dispatch reports `action_outcome_mismatch` instead of guessing a route. `move_cursor_is_not_interpreted_from_legacy_payloads` pins that. Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` (1330 passed); `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib move_cursor` (5 passed); `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs: pass); `cargo check -p platform-windows --tests` on Linux, which builds the Windows stubs. The pin test passed on main before the migration commit.
- Manual or platform evidence: none.
- After merging main and fixing three review findings (desktop-scope recordless success, libei fallback transport, overlay route for refusals), the scoped repository checks ran again: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passed on this macOS host; CI runs the Rust, clippy, Windows and desktop lanes at the new head.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the macOS and Windows crates were not compiled on this Linux host, and clippy, the Windows cross-check and the desktop E2E lanes did not run here. CI covers the build lanes.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`): only `bin/ci --quick` ran on this shared host.

title: fix(cua-driver): run a background pixel-targeted menu key equivalent on macOS
body:
## Why

On macOS, a background `hotkey` whose combo is a menu item's key equivalent runs that menu item through accessibility, because key events never reach an inactive app's menus. That route was skipped when the call passed `x`,`y`. The pixel form sent key events instead, so a background Cmd+V to a WKWebView page reported "Pressed cmd+v" and nothing was pasted. WebKit pastes only from the `paste:` action.

Fixes #5355

## What changed

- `hotkey` takes the menu route for the `x`,`y` form too. It first gates the window and focuses the field with the pixel focus click, then runs the menu item (Edit > Paste for Cmd+V). An `element_token` in web content gets the same pixel focus, since WebKit can acknowledge `AXFocused` without moving the page's focus. The web-content focus-point lookup moves into one helper that both the menu route and the key route use.
- The WKWebView fixture now has the standard Edit menu that WebKit apps ship. A new macOS E2E test, `webkit_background_paste_runs_the_edit_menu_item`, sends a background Cmd+V to the Tauri and WKWebView fixtures, by element and by pixel, and reads the pasted text back from the page. The macOS runner runs it.
- `MACOS.md` says how the pixel and web-content forms reach the menu route.

## Scope

macOS background `hotkey` with a combo that is a menu key equivalent in a native (non-browser, non-Electron) app that is not in front. Foreground delivery, browsers, Electron, and combos without Command are unchanged. Linux and Windows are not touched.

## Blast Radius

A background pixel-targeted Command combo to a native app (for example `x`,`y` plus Cmd+A in TextEdit) now runs the matching menu item instead of sending keys that the app's menus never saw. If the menu route reports `background_unavailable`, the call still falls back to keys as before. #8067 also edits `hotkey.rs`, but in the result text of the key route, not this block.

## Verification

- macOS Lume VM, new test before the fix (test and fixture commit only): both pixel rows and the Tauri element row fail. At 140accf: all four rows paste and pass their focus, z-order and no-leaked-input oracles, and the full macOS matrix passes (195 cells), including the shared WKWebView and Tauri rows.
- The hosted macOS lane (harness filter `electron`) failed at 140accf because the new test panicked when the filter excluded both WebKit fixtures. It now skips with a message; that command passes locally.
- The scoped repository checks, Rust macOS unit tests, and clippy on macOS, Linux and Windows pass in CI.

title: feat(spaces): stream direct Spaces over the advertised QUIC media endpoint
body:
## Why

A Space added by address (`cua spaces add <host>:<port>`, provider `direct`) always streamed over the `/media` WebSocket, even when cua-spacesd advertised `quic_media` and a QUIC media port. Nothing on that path asked for QUIC: `Space::open_stream` hard-coded `prefer_quic: false`, and the Spaces stream client only dialed the WebSocket. The client now tries the guest's QUIC listener first and falls back to the WebSocket when the listener doesn't answer.

Fixes #5346

## What changed

- `cua-media-transport`: the viewer's QUIC media client (pinned handshake, ticket, reliable stream, datagram reassembly) moves to `quic::MediaQuic`, and `cua-viewer` uses it. That leaves one copy of the code.
- `cua-spaces`: `open_stream` sets `prefer_quic` for a Space reached straight by its own address, whether in-process or through the `cua daemon` passthrough, as long as its guest offers `quic_media`. The listener goes on the new `StreamTicket::quic` field (`QuicTarget`), using the host the Space was added by. The field is not serialized, so the `stream_endpoint` JSON stays the same.
- `cua-spaces-ext`: `MediaStream` reads from either transport, a WebSocket or QUIC, through one `MediaClient` pump. It attaches over QUIC first and keeps that connection once the server answers. It falls back to the ticket's WebSocket in three cases: no answer within `QUIC_ATTACH` (3 s, covering lookup, handshake, stream, ticket and first message), a different certificate, or a close before the first message. When datagram video is lost, the client requests a keyframe. Media that arrives before `session_opened` (a datagram can overtake the reliable stream) is held and delivered once the session is open; media beyond the hold's cap is dropped and followed by a keyframe request.
- `cua-media-transport`: the datagram reassembler reports a skipped packet ID as a lost frame, so a frame whose fragments were all lost also triggers a keyframe request. This applies to the viewer's QUIC path too.

## Scope

Covers the SDK `Space::stream_session` path, which is the path Cua Spaces for macOS uses (native video surfaces). The following keep the WebSocket:

- Spaces reached through another machine (`*.via.cua`)
- relay, mesh, local and cloud Spaces
- proxied child-Space window streams

The Electron/web media bridge (`OpenMediaBridge`) is unchanged, because its consumer is a browser WebSocket. The docs now say that direct Spaces use UDP 3212 when it answers.

## Tradeoffs

- QUIC is tried first instead of racing it against the WebSocket. A race would attach the ticket twice.
- The ticket is validated without being consumed, and attach is per connection. A QUIC attempt that fails before the greeting therefore leaves the same ticket valid for the WebSocket.
- When UDP is blocked, each stream open waits `QUIC_ATTACH` before falling back. The fallback is not cached per Space.

## Blast Radius

This touches every stream that Cua Spaces and SDK users open on `direct:` Spaces whose guest offers `quic_media`. A failed QUIC attempt still ends on the WebSocket path, as before; the cost is up to 3 s of extra open time. A connection that goes wrong after QUIC attaches is not retried over the WebSocket; it closes like a WebSocket close does today.

## Verification

- New `cua-spaces-ext` tests against loopback fakes:
  - a ticket with a QUIC listener delivers a keyframe over QUIC while nothing listens on the WebSocket, with that keyframe sent before the greeting and numbered apart from the later ones, so the test sees it delivered after the session opens;
  - a silent UDP port falls back to the WebSocket after `QUIC_ATTACH`;
  - a different certificate falls back to the WebSocket;
  - a listener that completes the handshake but grants no stream gives up within the deadline.
- Mutation checks: with the QUIC dial disabled, the first two tests fail; with the deadline covering only the handshake (the first version of this PR), the no-stream test hangs.
- A reassembler unit test covers a skipped packet ID counting as a lost frame.
- `quic_media_host` unit tests cover direct, daemon-passthrough, IPv6 and hostname Spaces (QUIC) and routed, relay, mesh, local and cloud Spaces (WebSocket).
- The viewer's existing `quic_window_session_uses_the_pinned_endpoint_and_datagrams` passes on the shared client.
- The unit suites of `cua-media-transport`, `cua-spaces`, `cua-spaces-ext` and `cua-viewer` pass, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on those crates.
- The quick stage of the scoped repository checks passes. No live direct Space over a tailnet was streamed for this change.

- [x] `bin/ci --quick`

title: feat(cua-driver): sample the Hyprland cursor during recording
body:
Salvaged from #3553

Refs #2194

## Why

On Linux the recording cursor sampler always returned nothing, so `cursor.jsonl` stayed empty and the zoom renderer fell back to click points only. Hyprland answers a JSON `cursorpos` query on its instance socket. This salvage keeps @austindixson's three commits as authored, merges current main, and adds two commits of ours on top.

## What changed

- On Linux, the sampler sends a JSON `j/cursorpos` request to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket.sock`. The socket is non-blocking with a 100 ms total deadline, and reads stop when the sampler's stop flag is set, so a stalled compositor cannot hold up recording shutdown.
- It skips the query when session metadata says X11 or a desktop other than Hyprland, so a signature inherited from a parent Hyprland session is ignored. A non-empty `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` takes precedence over `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP`. Non-object replies, oversized replies and non-finite coordinates are rejected, and the sampler never writes a non-finite row.
- Between samples the thread parks, and `stop` and `drop` unpark it. It wakes once per sample interval on every platform, not every 5 ms, and stops without waiting out the interval. A reply whose EOF arrives after the deadline or a stop is discarded.
- One of our commits removes `stop_returns_while_a_sample_is_blocked`, which only stubbed the sample closure. `stop_and_drop_abort_a_blocked_socket_sample` covers the same shutdown contract over a real socket.

## Scope

Covers recording telemetry on Hyprland only. Other Wayland compositors and X11 still write no samples. The Linux observer, the native-case `Cursor` oracle, and background pointer input stay out of scope (#2194, #3550–#3552).

## Blast Radius

The change is in `cursor_sampler.rs` and runs only while a recording is in progress. On Windows and macOS the sample function's signature changes, and the wait between samples now parks the thread instead of sleeping. On Linux without a Hyprland session, path discovery returns `None` before any socket is opened. Hyprland reports cursor positions in logical global-layout coordinates, the same point space as macOS, which `display_scale_factor` multiplies into video pixels.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passed on this branch. The Rust unit and E2E lanes run in this PR's CI.
- The contributor reports that `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` passes on a native Omarchy/Hyprland 0.56.2 host and in a Linux ARM64 container, and that a read-only live `j/cursorpos` query returned a finite `{x, y}` reply. These runs are the contributor's own and were not repeated here.

title: fix(cua-driver): make set_value on a native text field reach the app
body:
## Why

On macOS, `set_value` on a native single-line text field wrote `AXValue` and read it back. An `AXValue` write never goes through AppKit's field editor, so a control bound to a model kept its old value while the read-back showed the new one (#3807). The result also had no way to say whether the app took the value (#3851). This lands @will-bogusz's work from #3858 on current main, with his commits kept as authored at the #3858 head. It replaces #7632, which carried the same change but has a commit under an author identity that has not signed the CLA.

## What changed

- A native non-secure, non-search `AXTextField` is now written by focusing it, selecting the old value (in UTF-16 units), typing the new value and pressing Tab. Secure fields keep the `AXValue`-only write. Search, combo, date and time fields keep `AXValue`, then `AXConfirm` or Return/Tab.
- New optional `ActionResult.committed` (`committed`, `not_committed`, `unproven`), contract 0.9.0, implementing items 2 and 4 of RFC #4009. It is `committed` only when a typed edit ended with the value in place. `type_text` on such a field reports `unproven`. The manifest and the Python/TypeScript UniFFI bindings are regenerated.
- Our commits on top: the retype route refuses when the field's `AXValue` cannot be read, and trusts the `AXValue` clear fallback only when the field reads back empty (before, an unreadable value counted as empty, so typed text could be appended to the old text). A gate refusal with no `AXConfirm` now returns the refusal before anything is written, the Return/Tab route confirms the field holds focus before sending the key, and `committed` needs a readable focus that has moved to another element (otherwise `unproven`). The macOS reference docs are regenerated. The merge with main keeps main's WebKit focused retry, LibreOffice Calc cell route and field-settle wait, and registers the two new AppKit cases in `appkit-cells.tsv`. A later merge with main keeps main's content-bearing group case beside them; the contract stays 0.9.0, as main's later additive fields did.

## Scope

Covers macOS `set_value` and `type_text`, the contract type and its generated bindings, and two AppKit e2e cases (`harness_appkit_set_value_commits_the_edit`, `harness_appkit_set_value_replaces_a_non_bmp_value_whole`). `AXTextArea` and web content are not retyped; they report `not_committed`. The RFC document is #4367.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS `set_value` on a plain text field now sends keystrokes instead of an `AXValue` write, so it goes through the background keystroke gate. When the gate refuses, the write falls back to the control's own `AXConfirm` if it has one, and otherwise refuses. `ActionResult` denies unknown fields, so a typed 0.8.0 SDK rejects a 0.9.0 daemon's `committed` field: SDK and daemon must upgrade together.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks ran on Linux: `bin/ci --quick` (formatting, headers, TypeScript typecheck), `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cua-driver-contract` tests, and the AppKit cell manifest tests.
- On macOS after the latest change: `bin/ci --quick`, the `platform-macos` `set_value` unit tests and clippy with `-D warnings`.
- Not run anywhere yet: the two AppKit `set_value` e2e cases. They drive host input, and hosted macOS CI runs the shared Electron lane, not the AppKit cells, so they need the local Lume lane.

Salvaged from #3858
Fixes #3807
Fixes #3851

title: fix(cua-spacesd): stop capture leases outside the locks their callbacks take
body:
## Why

On macOS, cua-spacesd can stop answering :3211 after a viewer is torn down. `MediaSession::shutdown` called `lease.stop()` while still holding the session's `capture` mutex. `MacosCaptureLease::stop` then waited on a callback gate. Meanwhile a ScreenCaptureKit frame callback held that gate and asked for a keyframe through the same `capture` mutex, so each side waited on the other forever. The process stays up, so launchd never restarts it.

A second path deadlocked too. When a captured window closes, the monitor thread emits `Closed` while holding the gate. That tears the session down on the same thread, so `stop()` tried to take a gate the thread already held, and then to join its own thread.

## What changed

- `MediaSession::shutdown` takes the capture and audio leases out of their mutexes and only then stops them.
- The macOS capture callbacks no longer hold a lock while they deliver to the sink. Once the lease is retired they drop their events, as the issue suggests. The sinks already ignore events from an old generation.
- The new `Retirement` struct owns the stop sequence: it retires the callbacks, joins the monitor unless `stop` is running on the monitor thread, and makes sure the stream is stopped only once. A lease stopped after `Closed` now still stops its stream; before, the early return skipped `stop_capture`.
- Because a callback can now arrive after `stop`, the gRPC connection's `HubCaptureSink` keeps its generation in a mutex for the length of each delivery. Before closing a session, `ActiveSession::stop_capture` advances the generation and only then stops the capture. A late frame is dropped and cannot bring a forgotten target back into the hub. The hub sink also retires itself when it delivers `Closed`, so a frame still in flight when the window closes cannot recreate the target before the connection handles the close.

## Scope

Covers the macOS capture lease and the media session teardown. It does not touch the Linux lease from #5409, which joins its monitor the same way. It does not add the health endpoint the issue also suggests.

## Blast Radius

Affects every media session teardown (window and display, all platforms), and frame delivery on macOS. A single frame already in flight can now reach the sink after `stop` returns. The media session sink and the hub sink both drop it by generation; the hub sink now advances its generation on close as well as on a preference change. The H.264 encoder's mailbox ignores input once closed. Windows capture never waited for its callbacks, so the macOS lease now behaves the same way.

## Verification

- `closing_does_not_hold_the_capture_lease_while_it_stops` (cua-spacesd-session) failed before the fix, because the callback was still blocked on the lease lock when stop returned. It passes after, along with the rest of the crate's tests.
- `a_frame_after_close_does_not_revive_the_target` (cua-spacesd-session) failed before the hub sink change and passes after.
- `a_frame_after_a_native_close_does_not_revive_the_target` (cua-spacesd-session) covers a frame that arrives after the monitor's `Closed` and before the connection drains it. It is added as its own commit ahead of the fix, and CI runs it.
- `the_monitor_can_stop_its_own_lease` (cua-spacesd-desktop, macOS) passes. Putting the self-join back makes it fail with "failed to join thread: Resource deadlock avoided".
- The scoped repository checks pass: `bin/ci --quick` and clippy `-D warnings` for both crates on macOS. Not run here: a live repro against ScreenCaptureKit, and the Windows cross-check.

Fixes #5376

title: fix(cua-driver): do not retype a macOS web AX write as keys when AXValue lags
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS Firefox, one background `type_text` call with an `element_token` inserted its text twice (`plain-17plain-17`).
- What changed: when an `AXSelectedText` write is accepted inside an `AXWebArea` but the immediate `AXValue` read-back has not moved, `type_text` now returns an unverified `ax` result and sends no key events. Before, it treated that read-back as a failed write and typed the same text again as keys.

Firefox applies the write and updates `AXValue` a moment later. The issue's own page counters fit this: 9 input events and 8 keydowns for an 8-character string, which is one AX insert plus 8 typed keys.

## Related work

Fixes #5383

Refs #5384 (coordinate-targeted typing in the same Firefox setup; a separate cause, not touched here)

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: for this case the result is now `path:"ax"`, `effect:"unverifiable"`, with no `delivered_chars`, and the detail says the text was not typed again and to read the field before retrying. A single-line submit (`text` ending in `\n`) sends no Return in this case.
- Unchanged: native fields, a refused AX write (Chromium/Electron fields that do not support `AXSelectedText` still fall back to keys), an unreadable `AXValue` (Catalyst), complete and partial AX writes, terminals, and the foreground rung.
- Risk: a web field that accepts the write and then drops it would no longer get the key fallback in the same call. The caller gets an unverified result and the usual escalation instead of a possible double insert. Rollback is a revert of the second commit.
- Platform: macOS only. The change is in the macOS AX write rung; Windows, X11 and Wayland have no equivalent path.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the first commit moves the existing decision into `after_unlanded_ax_write` and adds `an_accepted_web_write_is_never_typed_again_as_keys`, which fails there (`left: TypeKeys(Unverifiable)`, `right: MayHaveLanded`). With the fix, it and the other 31 `tools::type_text` tests pass. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and `bin/ci --quick` passed.
- Manual or platform evidence: I could not reproduce live. On the test host, the installed driver daemon timed out on every action call against Firefox 160, so no text was sent and the page counters stayed at zero. The mechanism above comes from the code path and the issue's counters, not from a run here.

title: [Bug]: run_steps rejects typed window targets when a window is inherited
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

A `run_steps` step with an explicit typed window target is refused when the batch supplies window defaults. The same hotkey works directly. Steps before it in the batch have already run when it is refused.

### Reproduction

1. Start a standalone Driver daemon in an isolated Linux desktop. Open and modify a throwaway Mousepad document.
2. Obtain its current decimal `pid` and `window_id` with `list_windows`.
3. Save this as `reproduce.py` and run `python3 reproduce.py "$DRIVER" "$SOCKET" "$PID" "$WINDOW_ID"`, using that executable, daemon socket and window's IDs:

```python
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

driver, socket, pid, window_id = sys.argv[1:]
window = {"pid": int(pid), "window_id": int(window_id)}

def invoke(tool, args):
    return subprocess.run(
        [driver, "call", "--socket", socket, tool],
        input=json.dumps({"session": "batch-target-example", **args}),
        text=True, capture_output=True,
        env={**os.environ, "CUA_TELEMETRY": "0"},
    )

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="batch-target-") as scratch:
    before = invoke("get_window_state", {
        **window, "screenshot_out_file": str(Path(scratch) / "before.png"),
    })
    if before.returncode:
        print(before.stdout)
        print(before.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(before.returncode)
    result = invoke("run_steps", {
        **window,
        "delivery_mode": "foreground",
        "steps": [{"tool": "hotkey", "args": {
            "target": {"kind": "window", **window},
            "keys": ["ctrl", "s"],
        }}],
        "observe": {},
    })
    print(result.stdout)
    print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(result.returncode)
```

### Expected behavior

Ctrl+S saves the explicitly targeted document. Batch defaults do not invalidate a valid per-step target.

### Actual behavior

Exit 1, `failed_step: 0`:

```text
invalid_action_target
target cannot be combined with legacy scope, pid, or window_id fields
```

With a token-targeted `type_text` before this hotkey, the text enters the editor but the hotkey is refused and the saved file retains its previous contents.

### Environment

Standalone CLI/daemon 0.53.0 and 0.37.0; Ubuntu 22.04.5 x86_64, X11/XFCE/Xvfb, Mousepad 0.5.8; default standard permission profile.

### Evidence

The two-step case failed on both releases. Independent file reads showed the pending edit was saved after sending the same typed-target hotkey directly. The one-step example above also reproduces on its own, on both releases.

### Workaround and additional context

Send the hotkey directly, or give the step flat `pid` and `window_id` instead of `target`: with the same batch defaults, that form saved the targeted document on both releases. On 0.53.0, removing root defaults from the two-step batch is insufficient: its earlier token step supplies inherited window context. That batch saves on 0.37.0. A separate one-step batch with no defaults and no earlier token step saves successfully.

At 0.53.0 (`aed25e921ff303315d95ea23ea2f853b0fb26998`), [`take_selector`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/aed25e921ff303315d95ea23ea2f853b0fb26998/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/batch_tools/locate.rs#L252-L272) ignores nested `target`; [`run_step`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/aed25e921ff303315d95ea23ea2f853b0fb26998/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/batch_tools.rs#L946-L955) then adds flat IDs beside it, which the target normalizer rejects. The causal files are unchanged on main at `dde4a4b64a49629ef41fb0faf19c45a178e0b08a` (source comparison).

Related: trycua/cua#7553 added token-window inheritance and flat-step support. Its token-window inheritance is why the two-step batch without root defaults fails on 0.53.0 but not on 0.37.0. It does not change how a typed target is read.

title: fix(cua-driver): focus the field under a macOS background pixel type_text in Firefox
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS Firefox, a background `type_text` with `x, y` and no `element_token` sent no input to the field. The page saw no `input` or `keydown` events and the call returned `type_text_incomplete` with `delivered_chars: 0`.
- What changed: the pixel focus step now counts focus as held at the point only when the field there has it. Before, a focused element whose rect merely enclosed the point counted, so the step skipped its focus click whenever Firefox's page document had focus. The keys then reached the document, not the input.

Focus now holds at the point when one of these is true:
- the focused element is the element hit-tested at the point, or sits inside it (Chromium's omnibox hit-tests to an enclosing group);
- the focused element is itself a text input whose rect contains the point (its hit-test can return one of its own text runs);
- the hit-tested element reports `AXFocused` (background web content where `AXFocusedUIElement` does not name the DOM control).

The same check decides whether a background focus click landed, so the foreground rung falls back to its real click in the Firefox case too.

## Related work

Fixes #5384

Refs #5383. That is the element-token duplicate insert on the same Firefox page, a separate cause handled in #8089.

## Compatibility and risk

- Impact: macOS only. The check sits in `focus_by_pixel`, which pixel `type_text`, `press_key` and `hotkey` share, so all three now focus a field inside a focused document instead of skipping the focus step. Windows, X11 and Wayland have no equivalent path.
- Risk: a surface where a focused container was the right target and the hit-tested element neither is nor contains the focused element now gets one AX focus write on the element at the point before typing. The early return that keeps a selection (#4148) still applies when the field itself has focus, including the Chromium omnibox case. Rollback is a revert of the second commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the first commit moves the decision into `focus_holds_pixel` with its old rule and adds tests. `a_focused_container_around_the_point_does_not_hold_it` and `the_field_at_the_point_holds_it` fail there and pass with the fix. The platform-macos `tools::` unit tests, clippy with `-D warnings`, and the scoped repository checks (quick mode) pass.
- Manual or platform evidence: not reproduced live. On the test host the shared driver daemon's screenshot capture hung for every app, Firefox 160 exposed no AX window to it, and a locally built daemon had no Accessibility grant. The cause above is inferred from the code and the issue's counters: zero `keydown` events on the input means it never had focus when the keys went out.
- Known gaps or CI still required: a live Firefox run of the issue's fixture on a build of this branch, and the macOS desktop matrix for the pixel `type_text`, `press_key` and `hotkey` cells (Electron, Tauri, AppKit).

title: fix(cua-driver): report the window covering a verified bring_to_front target
body:
## Why

In #5385, `bring_to_front` returned `activated: true` for a Chrome Open dialog. A moment later the desktop pointer guard and browser setup refused, because they read the front process from a different source. The screenshot showed another app's window over the dialog.

The source split is already gone on main. #6182 made `apps::frontmost_pid()` read the SkyLight front process, the same one `bring_to_front` checks, so activation, the pointer guard and browser setup now agree on which process is in front. One gap was left: a verified result said nothing about a window covering the target. A client could reasonably take it as ready for pointer input, and a desktop pointer event at a covered point may land on the covering window instead.

## What changed

- An exact-window `bring_to_front` now reports `exact_window_effect.unobstructed` and `observed.occluding_window` (`pid`, `window_id`): the frontmost ordinary (layer-0) window that sits above the target and overlaps it, from the same window list the pointer guard reads. When the result is a success, the text names that window as a possible obstruction: bounds alone cannot tell whether it takes pointer events.
- The tool description and the generated MCP reference say what the new fields mean.

## Scope

This adds reporting only. `activated` still does not require global z-order. #3784 dropped that requirement on purpose, and this report gives no reason to bring it back. The pointer guard and browser authorization stay as they are. Nothing that touches the desktop got new tests here; the coverage is unit tests over the observation model.

## Blast Radius

Two fields are added to the macOS `bring_to_front` structured result, and a sentence is appended to its success text. Existing fields and outcome classification are unchanged.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib bring_to_front`: 20 passed. The new test sets up the #5385 case: Chrome is the front process, the dialog is key and front within Chrome, and another app's window covers it. It asserts `activated: true`, `unobstructed: false` and the named occluder. A second test covers a window below the target, one on another display, the frontmost of several, and a target that is off screen.
- Mutation check: with the occluder dropped from `unobstructed`, `a_verified_target_under_another_applications_window_reports_the_occluder` fails (`left: Bool(true)`, `right: false`).
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`), `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -D warnings`, and a regenerated `cua-driver` reference, all green. A full `bin/ci` and the desktop E2E lanes were not run on this host; CI covers them.

Fixes #5385

body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `cua-driver --help` described the update-check cache as a "20h on-disk cache", but the cache lifetime has been one hour since #4757 (`CACHE_REFRESH_SECONDS = 60 * 60`). The generated CLI reference already said "1-hour", so the two descriptions of the same cache disagreed, and a user reading the top-level help would wait up to 20 hours for a cache that expires after one.
- What changed: the top-level help now states the one-hour lifetime that `CACHE_REFRESH_SECONDS` actually implements.

This is a help-text-only correction. The cache behaviour itself is unchanged.
