title: fix(cua-driver): report macOS AX enumeration counts in ax_window_unresolved
body:
## Why

Issue #4039: for days, `get_window_state` returned `ax_window_unresolved` with "none of the 0 AXWindow element(s)" for TextEdit windows that `list_windows` saw. The reason names how many AXWindow elements matched, but not whether `AXChildren` and `AXWindows` were empty, or whether the windows were there and `_AXUIElementGetWindow` mapped none of them. This adds those counts to the degraded response so the next occurrence can be told apart.

## What changed

- `get_window_state` adds `ax_enumeration` (`children_count`, `windows_count`, `union_count`, `ax_window_count`, `mapped_window_count`) to its structured output when the requested window's AX scope is unresolved.
- `copy_top_level` and `scope_top_level` record the counts on the walk they already do, so no extra AX reads.

## Scope

Diagnostics only. Window matching is unchanged and an unresolved scope still returns an empty tree. A clean snapshot does not carry the new field. It makes the #4039 state diagnosable, which is that issue's expected behavior; it does not change how the driver recovers from it.

## Tradeoffs

The original PR emitted `ax_enumeration` on every snapshot. On current main that would add the field to every response, and an unscoped walk would report zero AXWindows. It is now set only for an unresolved scope, where it explains the empty tree.

## Blast Radius

macOS `get_window_state` responses that are already degraded with an unresolved window scope gain one additive field. No other platform or tool changes.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: formatting and headers pass on this host. The macOS build, clippy and unit tests (including the new `enumeration_counts_windows_and_mapped_windows_only`) run in macOS CI.
- No live reproduction: the #4039 state is not reproducible on demand.

Salvaged from #4061
Fixes #4039

Thanks @lorenzozanee: your commit is kept as authored; this merges main into it and adapts it to the refactored window-scope code.

title: fix(cua-driver): report native AX results behind ax_window_unresolved
body:
## Why

When `get_window_state` on macOS returns `ax_window_unresolved`, the scope decision keeps only a count of readable `AXWindow` candidates. AXChildren errors, wrong-type values, filtered array entries, failed role reads, failed window-id conversions and the focused window are dropped, so a caller cannot tell those cases apart. #5386 asks for a supported, read-only way to see them.

## What changed

- `verbose:true` on a read that degrades to `ax_window_unresolved` adds `ax_diagnostics`. It comes from a separate read-only probe (`ax/scope_diagnostics.rs`) that reports:
  - `ax_children` / `ax_windows`: the native AXError (code and name), the value type, the raw array count and the AX-element count.
  - Per top-level item (capped at 32): which lists named it, pid or pid error, whether it is the application element, role or role error, subrole, and window id or conversion error.
  - `counts`: the union, items inspected, items with role `AXWindow`, and items mapped exactly to the requested id.
  - `focused_window`: the AXFocusedWindow read plus its role and window id. `matches_requested` is `null` when focus is unknown and `false` when it is a different window.
  - `partial`, `limits` (32 items, 250 ms AX messaging timeout, 1.5 s deadline), and `build` (version, git sha, executable sha256). The deadline is checked before every native read, and `partial` is true whenever it stopped one.
- The macOS `get_window_state` description and generated reference document the field.

## Scope

Diagnostics only. The probe sends no input, does not activate the app, does not enable AX and captures no content, and every ownership, exact-window, sibling-input and focus guard is unchanged. Default (non-verbose) responses are unchanged. Left out: `bring_to_front` request outcomes reported apart from strict verification (item 5 of the issue). The typed `WindowStateOutput` contract does not carry the field yet: like `escalation` and `background_input`, it is untyped structured JSON.

## Tradeoffs

The probe reads the attributes a second time instead of threading every read through the walk. The walk's hot path stays as it is, but the report can differ from the snapshot if the app changes in between. The module doc says so.

## Blast Radius

macOS `get_window_state` with `verbose:true` on an unresolved window only. It adds at most one bounded read in that case.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib scope_diagnostics`: 4 new tests pass. They cover separate union, role and exact-mapped counts; unknown focus kept apart from a different window; native error codes and names surviving serialization; a spent budget refusing every later read.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. `bin/ci --quick` and the generated-reference check pass.
- Not run here: a live probe against an app whose window stays unresolved, and the full `bin/ci`.

Fixes #5386

title: test(cua-driver): add a Wayland presentation-timestamp fixture
body:
Salvaged from #4236

Fixes #4012
Refs #3963
Refs #3971

## Why

Linux/Wayland latency evidence could not say when a Driver action's surface update was actually presented, so dispatch delay, paint delay, compositor scheduling and Driver post-action waiting all read as one slow action. @RyanL2's #4236 adds a repository-owned raw Wayland fixture that requests `wp_presentation.feedback` for each fixture-owned content commit, plus an E2E cell in the native Sway lane that joins those stamps with the Driver's own request and return stamps. This PR carries their seven commits, rebased onto current main, with fix-up commits on top.

## What changed

- RyanL2's commits, unchanged: the fixture under `tests/fixtures/apps/linux/wayland-presentation`, `wayland_presentation_latency_test.rs` in `cua-driver-e2e`, the probe classifier scripts, the runner wiring in `run-rust-e2e.sh`, and docs.
- Fix-ups: MIT SPDX headers on the new Rust files; a corrected dependency note (the fixture uses wayland-client's pure-Rust backend, so it needs no `libwayland-dev`); three clippy lints; em dashes removed from the fixture README; the cell reads the window once before its pixel clicks.
- The fixture is a raw Wayland client with no AT-SPI tree, so every recorded turn's state was `capture_failed` and the lane failed result validation. The cell now starts recording with the public `include_accessibility_tree: false` option (`McpDriver::start_behavior_recording_without_accessibility_tree`), which also keeps the per-turn walk out of the Driver return stamp it measures. The testkit declares this as `"accessibility_tree": "disabled"` in `trajectory.json`, and the validator accepts `not_applicable/state_capture_disabled` state only under that declaration.

## Scope

Test fixture, testkit, E2E runner and docs only. No scheduler, Driver action, recorder or public contract changes. The native cell runs only on native Wayland (no `DISPLAY`) and is `#[ignore]`d in ordinary `cargo test`. A compositor without comparable presentation feedback records a typed limitation, not a latency number. One Sway lane is not a cross-compositor claim.

## Blast Radius

Native Wayland lanes of `run-rust-e2e.sh` build one more fixture and run one more cell. The validator change is opt-in per recording: a turn with disabled state still fails unless its trajectory declares the tree disabled, and no other cell declares it.

## Verification

- New testkit unit test `validator_accepts_disabled_state_only_when_the_trajectory_declares_it` covers both the undeclared rejection and the declared acceptance.
- Native Sway cell (`E2E: Rust Linux Wayland`, environment `sway`, lane `native`, dispatch-only): see the run linked below on this head.

title: fix(cua-driver): honor x,y for background pixel clicks on macOS web content
body:
## Why

On macOS, a background left click at `x,y` pressed the element under the point with `AXPress` whenever the hit-test found one, and reported `PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX`. In Chromium, Electron and WebKit web content that press drops the coordinates. A canvas, a pointer handler or a caret placement never sees the click: the VS Code caret stays put, and a full-window `<canvas>` in Safari or Chrome gets no event. The fix keys on the accessibility role under the point, not on the app: anything in web content takes the routed pixel click, which delivers at the requested point.

## What changed

- The background hit-test in `click` no longer presses an element that is an `AXWebArea` or sits inside one. It falls through to the routed pixel path, as an element that does not advertise `AXPress` already does. Both rules live in main's predicate `hit_test_acts_on`, which now also takes the web-content check, with unit tests.
- The page probe the hit-test ran before a web press (from #7694) is removed, because the hit-test no longer presses web content. Element-token presses keep it.
- New macOS standalone-browser row `standalone_browser_background_canvas_pixel_click`: a canvas with no accessibility element of its own is clicked twice in the background, at two points away from its centre, and the page must see each pointerdown at the requested point, converted to viewport coordinates, on both axes.

## Scope

macOS `click` with `x,y`, left button, single click, no modifiers, background delivery. Native elements keep the AX hit-test press. Pixel `focus` (as used by `type_text` with `x,y`) is unchanged. Element-token clicks are unchanged. Windows and Linux are untouched.

## Tradeoffs

- A coordinate click on a web button or link now arrives as a routed mouse event instead of an `AXPress`. That route already handles Chromium double-clicks and modified clicks, and it runs the focus-without-raise prologue and the focus-restore lease, so the window is not raised.
- The pixel result reports `effect: unverifiable`, as before. A background press the page ignored used to come back as `suspected_noop` with a foreground escalation through the hit-test probe. Routed pixel clicks have no page read-back, so that hint is gone for coordinate clicks. Element-token clicks still give it.

## Blast Radius

Every background coordinate left click on web content in a macOS browser or web view: Chrome, Safari, Edge, Electron apps and WebKit views. It now delivers a real pointer event at the point instead of an accessibility press on whatever element the point resolved to. The risk is a page that took the `AXPress` but ignores a routed pointer event while in the background. `delivery_mode:"foreground"` stays the escalation for that case.

## Verification

- `standalone_browser_background_canvas_pixel_click` fails on the old behaviour by construction: an AX press on a canvas gives no pointerdown, or one at its centre. The PR's `e2e-gate` quick lane skips the browser lanes, so the full hosted macOS matrix (shared, native, capture and browser lanes) was dispatched on `0fdfa7462143a059eadef1615b9f8fc9f4fbf484` and passed, with this row green in Chrome and Edge. The Linux and Windows standalone-browser lanes also passed at that head.
- Unit tests beside `hit_test_acts_on`: web content takes the pixel path without reading its actions, a focus is still taken, a native element with `AXPress` is pressed, and one without it falls through.
- Main merged in; the one conflict was main replacing the LibreOffice/GTK toolkit rule with "press only an advertised `AXPress`" (`hit_test_acts_on`), so the web rule moved into that function. The scoped repository checks (quick stage: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) pass at the head. Clippy, the crate's unit tests and the macOS desktop rows are left to CI and the verifier.
- Not run: a live before/after in Safari and VS Code, and the local Lume lane (too little disk on this host). Safari and Electron have no row; the predicate keys on `AXWebArea`, which both expose.

title: feat(cua-driver): attach to a logged-in Brave profile
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `browser_prepare` refused to attach to a running Brave ("approved existing-profile setup is not implemented for Brave"), though Brave has the same per-instance remote-debugging switch as Chrome. Isolated launch never started Brave either.
- What changed:
  - Brave gets an existing-profile setup descriptor for `brave://inspect/#remote-debugging`. On macOS the driver attaches to a Brave whose remote debugging is already on, but refuses setup with `browser_requires_setup` before touching Brave's UI: on Brave 1.87 and macOS 27 a refused setup left remote debugging on. The refusal tells the user to turn it on at `brave://inspect` themselves. #4390's trusted-click checkbox fallback for Brave is dropped with it, since only setup used it.
  - macOS setup UI steps wait up to 8 s instead of 2 s for a new tab, omnibox suggestion or checkbox rollback. Each wait returns as soon as the change shows, so only slow browsers wait longer.
  - Isolated launch accepts Brave's vendor-signed install on macOS and Windows and its root-owned package binary on Linux, after Chrome and Edge. The docs now say Brave starts only when no earlier browser in the launch order passes the trust checks, that Linux checks root ownership rather than a signature, and that Brave's macOS 27 profile folder needs the same Full Disk Access as Chrome's.
  - Linux: Brave opens `brave://inspect/#remote-debugging` but reports the document as `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` over AT-SPI, so the document-URI check from #7587 refused the page it had just reached. The descriptor now carries a `document_url` next to `setup_url`; Chrome, Chromium and Edge keep the same value in both.
  - The standalone-browser E2E accepts `CUA_E2E_BROWSER_PRODUCTS=brave` and finds Brave's installs, so a maintainer can run the existing-profile cases against Brave from this branch.

Salvaged from #4390 by @DragonQLF. Their commits are kept as authored, rebased onto current main. Brave's default profile root on Linux and macOS already landed in #7717, so that part of #4390 resolves to main's code. The `document_url` fix and the E2E product selection come from #7708, which this PR replaces.

## Related work

Refs #3252

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): Not required. Brave joins the existing, already-gated existing-profile and isolated-launch flows; no API, permission or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: existing-profile attachment works for Brave on Windows and Linux X11 under the same grant as Chrome, and on macOS when Brave's remote debugging is already on. Isolated launch can start Brave from the installs above, which adds Brave to the binaries the driver starts with DevTools on. On macOS every browser's setup UI steps can wait longer.
- Risk and rollback: other products are unchanged apart from the longer macOS waits. The isolated-launch commit can be reverted on its own.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: SPDX headers, docs code blocks, image refs) pass at this head; the Rust build, tests and clippy run in GitHub CI. The macOS Brave setup-refusal E2E case now requests `delivery_mode: "foreground"`: it runs with the sentinel in front on the same Space, so a background request stopped at `background_unavailable` before the Brave guard. Unit tests cover the Brave descriptor, the macOS, Windows and Linux isolated-launch candidates, the trusted-checkbox predicate and the setup step bound.
- Manual or platform evidence, from #4390: a live macOS run (Brave 149, about 42 tabs) attached through `DevToolsActivePort`; a fork run on Windows and Linux X11 with Brave 154 passed attach, setup, standard-mode refusal and isolated launch. A reviewer on macOS 27 with Brave 1.87 attached with remote debugging already on.

Without the `document_url` fix the setup case refused with "did not reach its fixed setup page".
- Known gaps or CI still required: no lane in this repo runs Brave. Fork CI's isolated-launch run likely started Chrome, since the runners have Chrome and Edge installed. On Brave 1.87 the macOS setup path enabled remote debugging but could not read the checkbox back, refused, and could not restore it (`restored_remote_debugging: false`). This PR therefore refuses Brave setup on macOS. Lifting that needs a macOS run where setup refuses and the rollback is shown to turn remote debugging off. Brave 1.91 on macOS 26.3 did attach through setup in #4390.

title: feat(cua-driver): keep policy-forced extensions in isolated browser launches
body:
## Why

`browser_prepare` isolated launches always pass `--disable-extensions`, `--disable-background-networking` and `--disable-component-update`. Because of that, Chrome never installs extensions an administrator forces through managed policy, and relaunching an `isolated_named` profile removes one it already has. With this change, the driver checks the admin-only policy store of the browser it is about to launch. When that policy forces extensions, it leaves those three switches out.

## What changed

- Core: new `BrowserPlatform::managed_extension_policy(executable)` and a shared `managed_policy::policy_forces_extensions` parser. A non-empty `ExtensionInstallForcelist` counts, as does an `ExtensionSettings` entry other than `*` whose `installation_mode` is `force_installed` or `normal_installed`. `isolated_browser_command` drops the three switches only when the platform reports such a policy. The check runs on every launch, both pid-free and pid-selected.
- Adapters (all three implement the hook, so `ACCEPTED_DEFAULTS` is unchanged):
  - Linux reads `*.json` files in the launched product's `/etc/.../policies/managed` directory. A file counts only if it and every directory above it are root-owned, not group- or world-writable, and not symlinks.
  - macOS counts only `CFPreferencesAppValueIsForced` values in the browser's policy domain. Edge's `com.microsoft.edgemac` bundles map to `com.microsoft.Edge`.
  - Windows reads `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\<vendor>\<product>`.
- The browsers guide gains a section describing the behavior and listing the policy sources per platform.

## Scope

The change covers mandatory machine policy, including per-user managed preferences on macOS, which only a configuration profile or root can write. It does not read Windows `HKCU` policy, recommended policy, or cloud-delivered browser policy. `--load-extension` stays unsupported. `browser_prepare`'s result does not report that policy kept extensions on; the driver logs it at info level.

## Tradeoffs

- **Auto-detection or a setting.** I chose auto-detection. `set_config` is model input, so it can't serve as the "trusted driver setting" the issue mentions, and the policy store is already admin-only.
- **Which switches to drop.** All three go, because the reporter confirmed that combination installs the extension. Leaving `--disable-component-update` in place might also work, but nobody has tested it.

## Blast Radius

Only isolated launches on machines whose admin forces extensions on that browser are affected. Those launches now allow background networking and component updates, and the browser's own extension rules decide what else can be installed. The guide shows admins how to allow only the forced extensions with `ExtensionInstallBlocklist: ["*"]`. All other launches keep the same flags.

## Verification

Run so far: the scoped repository checks in quick mode (rustfmt, SPDX headers, docs checks), all passing. Unit tests, clippy, the Windows cross-compile and the end-to-end lanes are left to CI and to verification on a VM.

New tests:
- `isolated_launch_keeps_extensions_only_under_managed_extension_policy` launches the same named profile twice through `browser_prepare`, once without policy and once with it.
- Parser fixtures.
- Linux: policy directory per product, plus trusted, untrusted and malformed policy files.
- macOS: property list to JSON conversion and the Edge policy domain.
- Windows: policy key per product and the registry-value document.

Fixes #5501

title: [Bug]: Windows cua-driver-rs installs unsigned hidden elevated logon task (\cua-driver-serve) that appears to trigger Riot Vanguard permanent + HWID ban
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Installing `cua-driver-rs` (v0.6.8) on Windows registers a hidden, Administrator-elevated logon scheduled task (`\cua-driver-serve`) that keeps an unsigned `cua-driver.exe` binary running in the background at every boot. Because the unsigned elevated binary imports `SendInput`, `SetCursorPos`, `keybd_event`, `BitBlt`, and `OpenProcess`, it appears to trigger kernel-level anti-cheat false positives (specifically Riot Vanguard permanent account ban + HWID restriction in VALORANT).

### Reproduction

1. Install `cua-driver-rs` `0.6.8-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` on Windows 11 using the official Windows installer (`install.ps1`), which creates the `\cua-driver-serve` scheduled task (`RunLevel=HighestAvailable`, `-WindowStyle Hidden`, `LogonTrigger`).
2. Reboot/log into Windows so `cua-driver.exe serve` auto-starts silently in the background as an elevated process.
3. Launch and play VALORANT (with Riot Vanguard `vgk.sys` active — build `2026-11-12T20:23:07Z`) without closing or using `cua-driver.exe`.
4. Observe mid-match termination (`matchterminated`) and automatic permanent suspension for "Prohibited Third Party Apps/Mods" + hardware restriction (`VanguardFail`).

### Expected behavior

- `cua-driver-rs` Windows binaries should be digitally code-signed with valid publisher metadata.
- The installer should not silently register a hidden, Administrator-elevated persistent logon daemon (`\cua-driver-serve`) without an explicit warning and opt-in (especially warning Windows users about kernel anti-cheat conflicts like Riot Vanguard, EAC, and BattlEye).
- Users should be able to clearly see when `cua-driver.exe` is running and cleanly stop/disable it when not actively developing.

### Actual behavior

On November 17, 2026 at ~22:30 IST (17:00 UTC), while playing VALORANT on my college/development laptop with `cua-driver.exe` sitting idle in the background (installed June 28, 2026 and forgotten), I received an automatic permanent suspension for "Prohibited Third Party Apps/Mods" and an active hardware (HWID) restriction (`VanguardFail` / `vgc` terminated with `Incorrect function`, Event ID 7023).

I cannot confirm the exact internal detection trigger with 100% certainty because Riot Vanguard's `vgk` logs are encrypted. However, a full system audit (Riot Repair Tool `Process.txt`, `DxDiag.txt`, Windows Event Viewer, and loaded kernel drivers) confirmed zero unsigned/cheat kernel drivers and identified `cua-driver.exe` as the only unsigned, hidden, Admin-elevated process importing input-injection and screen-capture APIs.

### Environment

- Component/Package: `cua-driver-rs` `0.6.8-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (`cua-driver.exe`, `cua-driver-uia.exe`)
- OS: Windows 11 Home Single Language, x64 (ASUS ROG Strix G16, NVIDIA RTX 4060)
- Anti-Cheat / App: VALORANT / Riot Vanguard (`vgk.sys` Version 10.0, build `2026-11-12T20:23:07Z`)
- Install date of `cua-driver`: 2026-06-28
- Ban date: 2026-11-17 ~17:00 UTC (22:30 IST)

### Evidence

Redacted system audit details (sensitive IDs/paths redacted):

1. Scheduled task exported XML (`\cua-driver-serve`):
```xml
<Description>cua-driver-rs: serve daemon, auto-start at interactive logon, RunLevel=Highest for UWP/AppContainer support</Description>
<RunLevel>HighestAvailable</RunLevel>
<Command>powershell.exe</Command>
<Arguments>-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -NonInteractive -Command "Start-Process -FilePath '<USERPROFILE>\.cua-driver\packages\releases\0.6.8-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\cua-driver.exe' -ArgumentList 'serve' -WindowStyle Hidden -WorkingDirectory '<USERPROFILE>'"</Arguments>
```

2. Authenticode signature check (`Get-AuthenticodeSignature`):
- `cua-driver.exe`: `Status: NotSigned`, `SignatureType: None`, empty VersionInfo/CompanyName
- `cua-driver-uia.exe`: `Status: NotSigned`, `SignatureType: None`

3. Win32 API strings present in `cua-driver.exe`:
- `SendInput`, `keybd_event`, `SetCursorPos`, `BitBlt`, `OpenProcess`, `AttachThreadInput`, `UIAutomation`, `LoadLibrary`

4. Riot Repair Tool / Event Viewer timeline (2026-11-17):
- `cua-driver.exe` was actively running and captured in Riot Repair Tool's `Process.txt`.
- All running third-party kernel drivers were legitimately signed (`AsIO3.sys` ASUSTeK, `semav6msr64.sys` Intel, `FrameViewKM_x64.sys` NVIDIA, `vgk.sys` Riot Games).
- `19:27:57 IST`: `vgm.exe` `APPCRASH` (Event ID 1000 / `DxDiag.txt`).
- `22:30:56 IST` (`17:00:56 UTC`): VALORANT `ShooterGame` log recorded `/riot-messaging-service/v1/messages/ares-core-game/core-game/v1/matchterminated` -> `Platform Faulted: 5 (SessionRefreshFail)`.
- `22:32:36 IST`: Vanguard `vgk` log size jumped from normal ~6 KB to 93 KB (`vgk_2026-11-17_22-32-36.log`).
- Subsequent launches failed immediately with `Marking Platform Faulted for Reason: VanguardFail` and `vgc` Event ID 7023 (`Incorrect function`).

(Full unredacted Riot Repair Tool `.zip` logs are attached privately on Riot Support Ticket `#140795532` and not uploaded publicly here for privacy.)

### Workaround and additional context

**Workaround:** Windows users who play games protected by Riot Vanguard (or other kernel anti-cheats) should disable/remove the `\cua-driver-serve` scheduled task and stop `cua-driver.exe` before launching games, or run Cua only inside an isolated VM/dev machine.

**Additional context & request for help:**
- For full transparency, my laptop also had legitimately signed apps running in `Process.txt` (`Wispr Flow Helper.exe` v1.6.1483 and `SafeExamBrowser.Service.exe`), plus standard dev tools (VS Code, Docker/WSL) — none of which are unsigned elevated hidden input/screen automation daemons like `cua-driver.exe`.
- I am a college student who never cheated or used Cua with any game. I lost my 1.5-year main VALORANT account (`OnlyForShawtyy#ahmm`, Ascendant 3 peak, ₹20,000+ spent) and received a hardware ban on my only laptop.
- I submitted a full technical appeal with all 4 Riot Repair Tool `.zip` files under **Riot Support Ticket `#140795532`** (after `#140774537`, `#140777080`, `#140777830`), and it was auto-closed in 4 minutes with a boilerplate "decision is final" message without a human reviewing the logs.
- If the `trycua` maintainers can:
  1. Add a prominent Windows anti-cheat warning and avoid hidden `RunLevel=Highest` autostart by default (and code-sign release binaries), and
  2. Confirm publicly (or reach out to Riot Games / Vanguard if you have any developer contact) that `cua-driver-rs` is a legitimate open-source AI development tool so genuine false-positive tickets like `#140795532` can get a manual anti-cheat review — it would mean the world to me.
- If any other Windows `trycua/cua` users were recently flagged by Vanguard after the Nov 12 `vgk.sys` update, please comment here.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): wait for the menu a macOS menu-button press opens
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a background `click` (AX press) on a SwiftUI `Menu` (`AXMenuButton`) returns before SwiftUI publishes the menu, so a `get_window_state` taken right after the click has no menu items. The click reports `effect: "unverifiable"`.
- What changed:
  - A press or show-menu on an `AXMenuButton` or `AXPopUpButton` that has no menu beside it now waits up to 1 s for an `AXMenu` with items to appear among the control's children or siblings. SwiftUI publishes it in both places; AppKit publishes it under the popup button. The wait ends at the first read that finds the menu. Each AX read of the wait is capped at 100 ms and at what is left of the budget, no read starts after the deadline, and the scan stops at the first populated menu, so an app that stops answering after the press cannot hold the click past 1 s.
  - When the menu appears, the click reports `verified: true` and `effect: "confirmed"` with `accessibility_readback` evidence, and the text says the menu is open. When it doesn't appear, the click still succeeds and the text says no open menu appeared within 1 s. `post_action_wait: "none"` skips the wait.
  - The SwiftUI fixture gains a `Menu` (`menu-create`, items New Item and New Note). A new opt-in E2E cell, `macos-swiftui-menu-open-ax-background`, presses it in the background and expects the items in the very next snapshot, with no sleep between the two calls.

## Related work

Fixes #6082

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: this is macOS only. Menu-button and popup-button presses can now take up to 1 s longer, and they return as soon as the menu shows. The `click` description says so. No MCP schema change.
  - Menu bar items are excluded because they keep their `AXMenu` in the tree while closed, so there would be nothing to wait for. Context menus (`AXShowMenu` on other roles) are excluded because they hang off no element.
  - A control that already has a menu beside it skips the wait, so an AppKit control that always exposes its menu is not slowed down.
  - Windows and Linux are unchanged. Their menu-opening paths go through different adapters, and this PR does not claim the same contract for them.
- Risk and rollback: the change is local to `perform_ax_click`. Revert the fix commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks pass. `platform-macos` click unit tests cover which roles wait, the early exit, and that the poll hands each read its deadline and never sleeps past it (CI runs them). `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. The `cua-driver-e2e` SwiftUI test binary compiles. The macOS Lume runner tests (152) and the E2E inventory tests (12) pass. `bin/ci --quick` is green.
- Manual or platform evidence: a full hosted macOS E2E dispatch at the head, 8f33758: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/44584093568. An earlier full dispatch at 02f4114 (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/44283147238) passed every lane: native, capture, browser and shared. In the native lane, `harness_swiftui_menu_button_background` (cell `macos-swiftui-menu-open-ax-background`) passed. It presses the SwiftUI `Menu` in the background, expects `effect: "confirmed"`, and finds "New Item" in the very next snapshot with no sleep in between. The other SwiftUI cells also passed.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the cell was not run against the base driver to show it failing before the fix. The machine this was written on could not run a background press, and the Lume lane had no disk room. Windows and Linux are untouched.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: fix(cua-driver): avoid activation during background element keys
body:
Salvaged from #4876

Fixes #4843

## Why

On Windows, a background `press_key` with an `element_token` called UIA `SetFocus` on the control first. Some providers activate their frame from `SetFocus`, so a WinForms window was briefly activated even under `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`. That breaks the background no-activation contract. Now the key is posted straight to the control's own HWND, and if no safe exact target exists the call refuses before any input is sent.

## What changed

- `press_key` (Windows, background, `element_token`, native control): no UIA focus step. It reads the element's `NativeWindowHandle`, checks that the handle belongs to the admitted pid and window, and posts to that exact HWND (`post_key_to_hwnd`). If there is no native handle (windowless controls, including WPF) or it is outside the admitted window, the call returns `background_unavailable` before any keyboard input.
- Embedded WebView elements keep their existing background focus-click route. The route is chosen per element: a control whose own HWND has no Chromium window between it and the frame takes the exact-HWND path even in a window that also hosts a WebView. Modified keys in such a window are still refused before any input by the frame's embedded-WebView chord rule, as on main: posted modifiers do not update `GetKeyState`, so a handler could read the chord as a plain key. Windowless elements in such a window keep the focus-click route, as on main. Foreground delivery is unchanged.
- A WinForms keyboard mode in the WPF fixture, with four ignored E2E rows: a background key preserves activation and focus, in a window that also hosts a real WebView2 child (`--with-webview`) an unmodified key reaches the exact control and a Ctrl chord refuses without side effects, a windowless link refuses without side effects, and a foreground key reaches the exact control. The WPF accelerator rows read the fixture's state file. The tool description and the generated Windows reference are updated.

## Scope

Windows only. macOS, X11 and Wayland press_key paths are untouched. Main replaced the WebView2 pixel-click test that #4876 also reworked, so this PR keeps main's version, along with the `Win32_UI_HiDpi` feature that only that test used. #4876's UBRN launcher change in `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs` has nothing to do with this fix and is left out.

## Blast Radius

Windows background element-addressed `press_key`. A WPF or other windowless control now returns `background_unavailable` where it used to get a focus step and a posted key. That is the refusal #4843 asks for when exact-control background delivery is unsafe. Callers can retry with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (quick mode) pass: rustfmt, SPDX headers, docs code blocks, image refs.
- The Windows native WPF + WinUI3 + WebView2 lane ran on c36875d (run 44662466877): all four WinForms keyboard rows passed, including the WebView-host row. The first attempt failed in `input_delivery_stalled` on the WinForms foreground row and `text_delivery_stalled` on the unchanged WPF foreground `type_text` row; the rerun passed. Main's own run of this lane on 311df23e fails with the same foreground `text_delivery_stalled` rows, so the foreground stall is not from this diff, but the new foreground row adds one more row exposed to it.
- The WinForms foreground row now checks F6's own receipt (`target_modifiers_by_key`) instead of `last_key`: in the merge queue, F6 reached the exact control and a later key event on the target overwrote `last_key`.

title: fix(cua-driver): record background-unavailable refusals as refused and reject action truth that contradicts E2E oracles
body:
Salvaged from #4884

Refs #2512
Refs #2885
Refs #3171
Refs #3355

## Why

The driver records an `action_truth` for each action, and the E2E harness classifies what happened through its own oracles. The catalog validator checked them separately, so a driver claim could contradict the oracle without failing anything. This adds a floor in the turn-evidence validator that rejects those contradictions. The floor is @hippoley's work from #4884, rebased onto main with their commits kept as authored. In the merge queue it caught a real driver bug, and this PR fixes that too.

## What changed

- With retained `action_truth`, the validator fails on: oracle `NO_EFFECT` with `confirmed`/`partial`; oracle `REFUSED` with any effect other than `refused`; oracle `DELIVERED` with `refused`/`suspected_noop`; `confirmed` with no evidence; a missing or unknown effect. `DELIVERED` with `unverifiable` stays valid. The effect is parsed into the contract's `ActionEffect` and matched exhaustively.
- The case-level oracle is compared only for an action case with exactly one turn. A read-only case (`AxRead`, `WindowState`, capture scope) passes as delivered when its reads hold, even while the one action it probes is refused (a stale element token, a windowless pid), so its oracle does not describe that turn.
- `cua_driver_core::delivery::background_unavailable_result` now sets `effect: "refused"`, the key the desktop-click guard already passed, unless the caller names the effect of input it already sent (a busy UIA invoke stays `unverifiable`, a macOS drag-and-drop stays `no_drop`). Without it the dispatch seam recorded every background-unavailable refusal (Windows WPF `press_key`/`drag`, Linux Wayland) as an `unverifiable` action with no refusal code, even though the tool returned an error.
- On Windows, a background pen or touch stroke whose `InjectSyntheticPointerInput` call fails after the stroke began may already have reached the target, so `background_injection_error` reports it as `unverifiable`. A failure before any input is sent (stale window, UIPI, occlusion, WPF drag) stays `refused`.

## Scope

The testkit validator, the structured payload of the shared background-unavailable refusal, and the effect a Windows background injection failure reports. Recordings without `action_truth` are still accepted. It does not add Windows `window_change` readback and does not fix #3171 or #3355.

## Blast Radius

Every desktop E2E lane that validates catalog evidence runs the new check, so a lane whose driver claim disagrees with its oracle now fails. Callers of a background-unavailable refusal get one more structured field. `is_error`, `code`, `suggestion` and `escalation` are unchanged, and the recovery-hint and selftest paths already treated `is_error` as a refusal. The recorded action truth for these refusals is now `refused` with the refusal code, which is what the contract's `ErrorRequiresRefused` invariant requires.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks in quick mode (rustfmt, SPDX headers) pass.
- The first merge-queue run failed the Linux GTK3 and Windows WPF native E2E lanes on five contradictions: two read-only fail-closed cases bound to their refused probe, and three Windows background refusals recorded as `unverifiable`. The two fixes target exactly those cases. A dispatched run of the E2E release gate on this branch reruns those lanes.
- New unit tests: an interrupted Windows stroke reports `unverifiable` and a pre-send failure reports `refused`; a background-unavailable payload normalizes to a `refused` action with its code; an `AxRead` case with a refused probe turn raises no contradiction.

title: fix(cua-driver): print get_guide text from the call command
body:
Salvaged from #6088

## Why

`cua-driver call get_guide ...` never shows the guide. `call` prints a tool's structured JSON and drops its text blocks, and `get_guide` puts the guide in a text block with only metadata (topic, platform, sources) as structured content. @Alx8g's commit adds an opt-in `--text` flag to `call` that prints the text blocks instead.

## What changed

- `call --text` prints the result's text blocks; a result with no text falls back to the default output. Default output is unchanged. (Alx8g's commit, kept as authored.)
- The merge of main folds main's page-read path (`call_text`, from #5590) into the same `render_call_stdout` function as `with_text`, so `page` `get_text`/`query_dom` still print text after the JSON.
- The generated CLI reference lists `--text` and its example.

## Scope

Covers the `call` command's stdout selection and its reference docs. Leaves the daemon, MCP protocol, and exit codes alone. #6088 names no issue.

## Blast Radius

Every `cua-driver call` goes through the new output function. Without `--text` it prints the same thing as before, including the image merge into `screenshot_png_b64` and the page-read text; unit tests pin each of those cases.

## Verification

Unit tests in `cli.rs` cover default JSON output, `--text` output, several text blocks, the no-text fallback, empty results, the image merge, and the page-read text. The scoped repository checks (rustfmt, SPDX) pass; clippy, unit tests and the generated-reference check run in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): map Hyprland browser bounds onto the window's output
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Hyprland, browser bind correlation never matched by geometry on an output with a scale other than 1 or a layout origin other than (0, 0). The adapter handed core the compositor's global logical rect. Chromium's `Browser.getWindowBounds` reports the window relative to its output and multiplied by the output scale. A browser with more than one window therefore bound only as a read-only heuristic. A single-window browser reached `exact` only through the cardinality upgrade.
- What changed: `native_window()` on Hyprland now maps the client's rect onto its own output, `(at - output origin) * scale` and `size * scale`, using the client's `monitor` id and that monitor's `id` from `j/monitors`. If the window's output is missing or out of the layout (for example a mirror), the rect stays in layout coordinates and is marked `geometry_exact: false`, so the bind stays read-only and can't claim a geometry match.

## Related work

Fixes #4944

RFC: not required. This is an internal adapter fix that brings Hyprland in line with the existing `Rect` contract in `cua-driver-core`.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: on Hyprland, multi-window Chromium browsers on scaled or offset outputs can now bind `exact` through bounds correlation. Unscaled outputs at (0, 0) produce the same rect as before.
- Risk: the mapping comes from the single sample in #4944 (Chrome 154, Wayland-native, scale 1.2). There, every edge matches within 1 px. A Chromium build that reports scaled DIPs instead of output device pixels would still fail to correlate. That leaves it in the same read-only heuristic it gets today. Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the new `hyprland` unit tests rebuild the #4944 sample (an output at (0, 360) with scale 1.2 next to an unscaled output at (-1920, 0)) and check that every edge lands within 1 px of the reported CDP bounds. They also check that a window with no output, an unknown output or a mirrored output gets no output-space rect. The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers) pass.
- Manual or platform evidence: not run on a live Hyprland desktop.
- Known gaps or CI still required: unit tests, clippy and the Windows cross-check run in CI.

title: feat(cua-driver): opt-in driver-owned headless browser route
body:
Salvaged from #4934

## Why

Agents need typed browser work on hosts with no compositor, display or native window. @chrisohearn's #4934 adds an opt-in headless route to `browser_prepare`. It was stacked on #4931 and now conflicts with main. This PR carries only its headless commit, ported onto current main without #4931.

## What changed

- `browser_prepare {headless: true, allow_launch: true, profile: {mode: "isolated_new"}}` launches a driver-owned Chromium with `--headless=new`. It returns an opaque, session-scoped `attachment.headless_target`. `get_browser_state {headless_target}` binds it with `binding_route: "driver_owned_headless"`, and no native window is involved. Bind and every mutation re-check the launch record (process start identity, endpoint, session) and refuse on drift. Session end kills the driver-launched process group and deletes the profile. This is the contributor's commit, kept as authored.
- Port fixes on top. The conflicts are resolved against main's newer launch path (`driver_owned_browser_command`, launch breaker, `BrowserRefusal::new`), and the `#4931` focus-guard hook is dropped from the test platform. Three test expectations change for main's behaviour: a replaced process now fails main's driver-owned lifecycle check first, with `browser_consent_required`, and a DOM click is reported through `action_record` in both the mock and the real-browser test.
- Merged current main. Main's managed-extension policy (#5501) now also takes a parameter on `isolated_browser_command`; the launch keeps both, so a headless launch still drops the extension switches only when policy forces extensions.
- Bounded mode: with a capability manifest, a `headless_target` bind now attests the session's live headless launch (pid and re-proven process fingerprint) as a `driver_owned_headless_browser` resource, which the manifest admits for private observation. Before this, authorization fell through to display discovery and refused on a host with no display. Ownership also resolves the anchor by session now, because dispatch strips the transport id from public arguments. The bind and every mutation still require the exact transport.
- The launch breaker now records success only after the headless start identity is proven. A headless launch refused at that check counts as a failed launch, so repeated refusals open the breaker instead of resetting it.
- On Windows, which has no process group to signal, session cleanup and launch refusals of a headless launch reap its process tree with `taskkill /T`, as the launcher-handoff case already does.
- Linux CI's unit job runs the real headless Chrome test against the hosted Chrome with no display. Before this, no runner selected it.
- The generated MCP tool reference and the three platform registry snapshots now include `headless` and `headless_target`.

## Scope

Covers the headless route only. #4931 (guarded existing-profile setup on Hyprland) is not included. `existing_profile` and pid/window binding are unchanged. `isolated_named`, `existing_profile`, `pid` and `window_id` are refused when `headless` is set.

## Tradeoffs

A manifest admits `driver_owned_headless_browser` without listing it, as it does `session_trajectory_recording`. The resource is a browser this session launched. The bind reports a tab outside the manifest's origins only by its `tab_id`, with no title or URL, and each later tab observation or input is still checked against the manifest's origins. A manifest field that opts in to headless binds would be stricter. That is a policy choice for the API review.

## Blast Radius

The route is opt-in: without `headless: true`, prepare and bind behave as before. The added `window_id: Option` on target records affects every binding, and the mutation checks skip native-window correlation only when a record has a headless anchor. The shared `kill_process_group` signals only while the leader has not been reaped. Real-browser coverage exists only for Linux. The Windows tree cleanup has not run against a real browser. The Windows unit workflow skips draft PRs, so it was dispatched on the branch to compile and test it. The macOS and Windows routes compile but have not been run against a real headless browser.

Known gap, from the source PR: if the leader is reaped, a surviving Chromium descendant is not signalled and could race profile deletion.

## Verification

- Scoped repository checks: `cua-driver-core` `browser::` unit tests pass (306) with `DISPLAY` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset. This includes the headless prepare → bind → navigate/type/click flow, the refusals, anchor forgery, drift, record removal and cleanup.
- clippy `-D warnings` on `cua-driver-core` and `platform-linux` (with tests) is clean, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.
- The opt-in real-browser test (`CUA_TEST_REAL_HEADLESS_CHROME=1 ... real_headless_chrome -- --ignored`) passes on Linux against the installed Chromium with no display variables set: prepare, bind by anchor, navigate, type, DOM click, readback of the clicked state, profile removed, process reaped. Its click assertion now reads the action record, as main's click tool reports there.

The runs above are from the head before the main merge and the bounded-mode fix. The current head relies on CI and the verifier, because this shared host had no disk for a local build. The new registry-dispatch test covers prepare, then bind by anchor under a bounded manifest, redacts a tab outside the manifest, and refuses a forged anchor with `browser_binding_stale`. CI's Linux job also ran the real headless Chrome test with no display, and it passed. The merge head and the two fixes on top are left to CI and the verifier. This shared host ran only `bin/ci --quick` and `rustfmt --check` on them. The new `headless_launch_with_unproven_identity_counts_as_a_failed_launch` test covers the breaker fix.

## Checks

- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green: only `--quick` ran on this shared host; heavy lanes are left to CI.

Draft: #4934 adds a new `browser_prepare` option, and the team asked to agree on its API shape before merging.

title: fix(cua-driver): explain session-scoped snapshots in the stale token error
body:
Salvaged from #6089

## Why
Each one-shot `cua-driver call` without a `session` label gets its own session, and the daemon ends that session after the response. If an agent reads a window with one call and clicks an `element_token` with the next, the read's snapshot is already gone. The refusal said only that the pid "has no current snapshot", which gave no hint about the cause. #6089 by @Alx8g added the explanation. This PR moves it onto current main, where snapshots are now kept per session.

## What changed
- @Alx8g's commit, kept as authored and rebased onto main's session-scoped `stale_token_refusal`. When the caller has no current snapshot for the process, the refusal explains why and says to pass the same `session` label to `get_window_state` and to the action.
- Follow-up commit: the hint now says "session" instead of "connection", because a named CLI session spans processes. The text lives in one place, `SESSION_SCOPED_SNAPSHOTS`, and the token-only refusal (`stale_token_without_pid`) uses it too. A click that carries only an `element_token` hits that refusal.
- Tests: one unit test for the pid path, and new assertions on the existing token-only and listing tests. The listing test in #6089 duplicated `stale_token_names_the_current_snapshots`, so its assertion moved into that test.

## Scope
Changes refusal message text only. The `stale_element_token` code, the structured fields, and the refusal that lists current snapshots stay the same.

## Blast Radius
Anything that reads the refusal message for the no-snapshot case gets a longer message. The message still starts with the same text up to the pid, and now says "in this session" after "no current snapshot". Nothing in the repository or docs matches on that text.

## Verification
The scoped repository checks (quick stage) passed: rustfmt and the SPDX header checks. The `cua-driver-core` unit tests run in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): reopen running apps with launch_app
body:
Salvaged from #6198

## Why

`launch_app` sends `aevt/oapp` on every background launch. When the app is already running with its window closed, minimized or hidden (⌘H), many apps, Electron ones especially, ignore `oapp` and nothing appears. A Dock click or `open -g` sends `aevt/rapp` instead, which reopens the window without changing the frontmost app.

## What changed

- `nsworkspace::open_application` sends `aevt/rapp` when the target bundle already has a running process and `creates_new_instance` is false, and keeps `aevt/oapp` for cold launches and new instances. `activates = false` is unchanged. Bundle-ID and name launches both go through this path.
- Unit tests own the event choice; a new ignored macOS E2E row, `appkit_launch_reopens_hidden_running_app_without_focus_steal`, hides the test-owned AppKit harness, calls `launch_app` again, and checks the app becomes visible while Finder stays frontmost.
- On top of @maxvint's commits: main merged in, a test that compared one helper's output with itself (and the helper) removed, and the test guides list the new row.

## Scope

macOS `launch_app` and `launch_app` by name only. `open_urls_with_application` still sends `oapp`. Windows and Linux launch paths are untouched; they have no AppleEvent equivalent.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS `launch_app` call on an already-running app now sends `rapp` instead of `oapp`. An app whose `rapp` handler activates itself could take focus; the E2E row checks Finder stays frontmost for the AppKit harness.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): pass.
- The new E2E row runs in the canonical macOS desktop lane (`scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh` runs the whole `installed_app_launch_macos_test` binary with `--ignored`).

Thanks @maxvint for the fix and the E2E case.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse background type_text into the iOS Simulator
body:
## Why

Xcode's Simulator forwards physical key codes to the iOS guest and ignores the Unicode string that background `type_text` attaches to key code 0 (the A key). Every character arrived as A: `abc` became `Aaa`, or `ㅁㅁㅁ` on a Korean guest keyboard, and the call still reported `effect:"unverifiable"`. Screen Sharing has the same problem and Cua Driver already handles it, so the Simulator now takes the same route.

Fixes #6555

## What changed

- `KeyForwarder` in `input/keyboard.rs` classifies Screen Sharing (`com.apple.ScreenSharing`) and the Simulator (`com.apple.iphonesimulator`) by exact bundle id. `is_screen_sharing_pid` (used by `hotkey`) is now built on it.
- Background `type_text` to the Simulator, or a call without `window_id`, refuses with `IOS_SIMULATOR_REQUIRES_FOREGROUND_HID` before it sends any event. The refusal suggests `delivery_mode:"foreground"` with `window_id`, or `set_value` / `press_key` in the background.
- Foreground `type_text` with a `window_id` sends physical HID key transitions to the Simulator, as it already does for Screen Sharing. When the call names an `element_token`, the HID path focuses that field after activation and refuses with `target_focus_unconfirmed` before any key if it can't confirm the focus, so keys never land in whichever field already had it. This reuses `press_key`'s `with_confirmed_key_focus`, now moved to `input/ax_actions.rs`.

## Scope

macOS `type_text` only. `hotkey` keeps its Screen Sharing-only modifier gate, because the issue reports that `press_key` already works against the Simulator. Desktop-scope `type_text` (no pid, frontmost app) is unchanged. A pasteboard route (`simctl pbcopy` plus Paste) is out of scope because it replaces the guest pasteboard.

## Tradeoffs

Background typing could send per-character key codes through PID routing, the way `press_key` does. Those codes are interpreted by the guest's keyboard layout, which the host can't read, so `abc` would still come out as Hangul on a Korean guest. A refusal with an exact code is one of the two outcomes the issue lists as expected.

The foreground physical path covers printable ASCII only. Characters outside it, such as `한글`, are refused before any key is sent, the same as for Screen Sharing.

## Blast Radius

The new behaviour applies only to apps whose bundle id is exactly `com.apple.iphonesimulator`. Screen Sharing keeps its refusal code, message and foreground path, with one change: a foreground call that names an `element_token` now needs that element confirmed focused, and is refused with `target_focus_unconfirmed` otherwise. Calls without an `element_token` are unchanged. The physical-text error message drops its "Screen Sharing" prefix because it now covers both apps.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (quick stage: rustfmt and SPDX headers) passed locally. The `platform-macos` unit tests and clippy run in CI (`Rust macOS unit`), not on this host.
- `key_forwarder_detection_is_exact_and_case_sensitive` pins the bundle-id mapping. `key_forwarder_text_fails_closed_without_foreground_window` pins both refusal codes and the foreground pass-through. `press_key`'s existing `targeted_key_*` tests still own the confirmed-focus guard.
- No live Simulator run: Xcode isn't installed on this host, so neither the background refusal nor foreground typing into a Simulator field has been exercised.

- [x] `bin/ci --quick` (the heavy stages run in CI)

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve Windows right-click modifiers
body:
Salvaged from #4947

## Why

Windows `right_click` accepts `modifier`, but both foreground paths (element token and screenshot pixels) passed an empty modifier list to SendInput, so a Shift-right-click arrived as a plain right-click. This forwards the modifiers to the existing pointer injector, which already presses and releases them around the click. A background right-click with modifiers now returns `background_unavailable` before any input, the same refusal Windows `click` gives.

## What changed

- `right_click` on Windows passes `modifier` to `send_click_synthesized_active_mods` on both foreground paths, and refuses modified background right-clicks with `background_unavailable`. The tool description, the Windows CLI spec and the docs page say so.
- The WPF fixture records `Keyboard.Modifiers` and a right-click count on right-button down, and its double-click handler ignores non-left buttons so a second right-click cannot overwrite that label.
- `harness_wpf_right_click` covers both addressing modes: the exact background refusal with no effect on the fixture, Shift at right-button down, then `None` on the next plain right-click. It keeps main's check that a foreground right-click leaves the real cursor where it was.

## Scope

Windows `right_click` only. `double_click` still ignores `modifier` on Windows; that is a separate change. macOS and Linux are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Callers that sent `modifier` to a background Windows `right_click` used to get a plain right-click and now get a refusal that recommends foreground. That matches Windows `click`. Foreground right-clicks without modifiers are unchanged.

## Verification

The contributor ran `harness_wpf_right_click` on a Windows desktop session at #4947's head, and it passed in both addressing modes. This PR merges current main into that branch and moves the change into the per-tool `right_click.rs` module that main split out of `impl_.rs`. The scoped repository checks (formatting, headers, docs code blocks) pass on this head; the Windows build and the WPF owner test run in CI and the Windows lanes.

Credit to @hqhq1025, whose commits are kept as authored.

title: fix(cua-driver): label macOS controls through AXTitleUIElement
body:
## Why

A SwiftUI `Toggle` in a grouped `Form` names its checkbox only through `AXTitleUIElement`. The checkbox's own `AXTitle` and `AXDescription` are empty. The macOS walker never read that attribute, so the control showed up unlabelled: no `label` in `elements[]`, a bare `[N] AXCheckBox` row, `query` matching only the separate static text, and `run_steps` refusing `{role:"checkbox", name:"Launch at login"}` with `not_found`. VoiceOver reads the label through the same attribute.

## What changed

- An addressable control with neither `AXTitle` nor `AXDescription` takes the text of its `AXTitleUIElement` (its `AXValue`, else its `AXTitle`) as its title. The row then reads `[N] AXCheckBox "Launch at login"`, and `elements[].label`, `query` and `run_steps` name lookup all match it.
- The token identity recheck (`ObservedIdentity::read`) and the fast-path guard's act-time observation follow the attribute the same way. Without that, a click by token on a now-labelled control would fail the identity check.
- The SwiftUI harness gets a grouped `Form` toggle (`form_labels` scenario) and a `harness_swiftui_form_toggle_label` E2E case that checks the row, the label, `query` and the `run_steps` name lookup. The macOS native runner (`run-rust-e2e.sh`) selects it as cell `macos-swiftui-form-toggle-label-ax-not-applicable`, and the Lume runner can retry it.

## Scope

Covers macOS AX reads only. Controls that already have an `AXTitle` or `AXDescription` are unchanged, and display-only rows never follow the attribute. Windows UIA `LabeledBy` and AT-SPI `labelled-by` are not touched here. The label's own `AXStaticText` row stays in the tree.

## Tradeoffs

The issue suggested an opt-in `title_ui_element` field as an alternative. Filling the title instead is what makes name lookup and `query` work without callers changing anything, and `AXTitleUIElement` is the attribute macOS defines for a control's title.

## Blast Radius

macOS Cua Driver users reading or targeting SwiftUI form controls (and any AppKit control labelled the same way). Unnamed controls cost up to two extra AX round trips each; named controls cost none. A control whose `AXTitleUIElement` text was previously absent now shows a title, which can change its `elements[].label` from its value or identifier to that text.

## Verification

- Reproduced on the rebuilt SwiftUI harness with the installed driver (0.44.0): the form toggle read as `[7] AXCheckBox [actions=[press]]` with no `label`, and `run_steps` returned `no checkbox "Launch at login" in window …`.
- New unit tests `an_unnamed_control_takes_its_title_element_text` and `a_named_control_never_reads_its_title_element` pass; `harness_swiftui_test` compiles.
- The scoped repository checks ran in quick mode (SPDX headers, bin/ci tests, image refs): green. The E2E inventory and Lume runner tests pass. Clippy, the full unit suite and the desktop E2E case are left to CI and the verifier.

Fixes #6697

title: [Bug]: [Hoy] Apple Screen Sharing disconnects during VNC authentication on macOS 27.3 beta
body:
## Primary area

Other (Hoy)

## Summary

On an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 27.3 beta, `hoy vnc` opens Apple's built-in Screen Sharing. The client reaches Hoy's loopback port, then disconnects during the VNC handshake. TigerVNC can authenticate and display the same guest through a Hoy loopback bridge.

## Reproduction

1. With a tested `macos-27.2.1` image available, run `hoy create hoy-macos --image macos-27.2.1 --window`.
2. Run `hoy start hoy-macos --wait ready`.
3. Run `hoy vnc hoy-macos`. Paste the password copied by Hoy if Screen Sharing prompts for it. [Hoy Quickstart](https://cua.ai/docs/hoy/quickstart#open-its-desktop)

## Expected behavior

Apple Screen Sharing connects and displays the guest desktop.

## Actual behavior

Screen Sharing displays `Unable to communicate with “127.0.0.1:<port>”`, followed by instructions to check whether the remote computer is available and whether the firewall is blocking screen sharing. The failure reproduced after an orderly stop and restart of the VM.

## Environment

- Apple M3 Max host running macOS 27.3 beta, build `26C5047e`.
- Apple Screen Sharing `7.1` (`788.2`).
- Hoy stable `0.17.2-80749511`, commit `80749511`, VMM `hoy-vmm` with Hoy devices `r71`.
- macOS `27.2.1` guest (`26B131`), built from an Apple restore image. Hoy's image smoke test passed the Dock, Finder, sudo and guest-agent checks.
- TigerVNC Java viewer `1.16.2` for comparison.

## Evidence

The `hoy vnc` bridge records the Apple client connecting and leaving before sign-in.

```text
hoy: vnc: client connected
hoy: vnc: client disconnected before signing in; waiting for the viewer
```

The matching excerpt from `hoy logs hoy-macos --kind vmm` after the VM restart records the negotiated version and EOF. The timestamps are relative to VMM start.

```text
28.513591834s  INFO vnc:          client RFB version version="RFB 003.003"
30.892483209s  INFO vmapple_gfx:  vmapple vnc: viewer session ended id=0x1 error=socket error: unexpected end of file
```

- In a separate attempt, Apple's log transitioned from `kSSSessionStateConnecting` to `kSSSessionStateNotConnected` in about 4 seconds. The loopback port was still listening at the time of inspection. Hoy subsequently reported that it closed an unauthenticated bridge after 120 seconds.
- A minimal RFB client using the same VM password negotiated RFB `3.3` through a disposable Hoy loopback bridge. It received security type `2` (`VNC Authentication`), passed authentication and received a `1920×1440` `ServerInit`. Direct tests against the VM's Unix socket also passed with RFB `3.3` and `3.8`. [RFB 3.3 security handshake](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6143.html#appendix-A.1)

`hoy doctor` reported that the host was ready.

```text
ok   chip             Apple M3 Max
ok   macos            macOS 27.3
ok   hypervisor       kern.hv_support is 1
ok   limit-service    the Hoy system extension is approved and active (0.17.2)
ok   full-disk-access Full Disk Access is on for the extension
ok   vmm              hoy-vmm (hoy devices r71)
ok   daemon           hoyd answers
ok   guest:hoy-macos  hoy-macos: hoyd reaches it over the internal channel
doctor: this host is ready
```

## Workaround and additional context

TigerVNC Java `1.16.2` negotiated RFB `3.8` over a fresh `hoy vnc hoy-macos --no-open` loopback bridge. Hoy logged `viewer signed in`, and TigerVNC displayed the desktop.

Could the Hoy team try the documented `hoy vnc` flow with Apple Screen Sharing `7.1 (788.2)` on host build `26C5047e`? The logs narrow the failure to Apple's connection after RFB version negotiation. The exact message or client condition that triggered the disconnect is still unknown. Testing covered one host build.

## Submission checks

- [x] Searched existing issues and active pull requests for duplicates.
- [x] Reported one problem.
- [x] Removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots and vulnerability details.

title: [Bug]: macOS background run_steps briefly raises the target window when a sheet appears mid-batch (0.52.13)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (macOS)

### Summary

During `run_steps` calls with `delivery_mode:"background"`, the target app's window was briefly ordered above the user's frontmost window. Each occurrence lasted about 50-150 ms (one to three 20 Hz samples). Most occurred when the batch's own step opened an alert sheet. Keyboard focus and app activation stayed with the user's window in every sample, so this is a z-order raise, not a focus steal. Bench v2 still scores it as `windows_raised`, so the trial is not clean.

### Reproduction

Observed in the Bench v2 BenchLab interruption tasks (IR-01, IR-02, IR-03; `--condition background`). A minimal reproduction I have not run myself:

1. Put a "user" window frontmost (any app).
2. Have a background app that shows an alert sheet when a button is pressed.
3. `run_steps` with `delivery_mode:"background"`, one `click` on that button, and an `observe` end step. Sample `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)` at 100+ Hz and record any window of the target pid above the user window.
4. Compare: the same click as a single `click` call without `observe`, then a separate `get_window_state` after the sheet is up. This splits the action path from the observation path.

### Expected behavior

With `delivery_mode:"background"`, the target window stays at its existing z-order and never appears above the user's frontmost window, including when the action causes the target to present a sheet, menu or overlay.

### Actual behavior

In 7 of 21 trials (10 intervals), a BenchLab window was sampled above the user's frontmost window for about 50-150 ms during an in-flight background `run_steps`. Key focus and activation stayed with the user's window in every sample.

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.52.13 (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app`), MCP transport, private daemon home per the bench harness
- macOS 27.2.1, Apple Silicon, Retina display (scale 2)
- Harness: `libs/cua-driver-bench` at dde4a4b, Bench v2, `--condition background`, arm `cc-cua-driver-main-skill`
- Local harness patches, unrelated to this path: the pointer park uses `delivery_mode:"foreground"` plus pixel scale, and iTerm2 is removed from `SIDE_DOOR_PROCESSES`
- Agent skill: a local variant of the cua-driver skill. It never sends `bring_to_front`, foreground delivery or desktop-scope input; the transcripts confirm zero such calls in these trials.
- Not retested on 0.53.0, which was released after these runs.

### Evidence

Results across the 21 trials (7 tasks x 3 runs):

10 raise intervals across 7 trials, all in the interruption tasks (IR-01, IR-02, IR-03). Every interval fell inside an in-flight `run_steps` call, typically 0.1-0.9 s before the call returned, during or near the end observation.

| Batches (IR tasks) | Raised | Not raised |
|---|---|---|
| A new `AXSheet (alert)` appeared in the end-observation diff | 7 | 2 |
| No sheet in the result | 3 | 37 |
| `get_window_state` (standalone, never saw a sheet) | 0 | 13 |
| `list_windows` | 0 | 12 |

The 3 no-sheet raises: 2 followed a BenchLab banner overlay (IR-02 `banner_shown`), and 1 batch opened a pop-up menu (`AXMenu` added in its diff).

Per-event detail (sentinel `above` list, the BenchLab event just before the raise, and timing within the agent call):

| Trial | Above user window | Preceding lab event | Raise at / call duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| IR-01 r1 | BenchLab | permission_prompt_shown (+1046 ms) | 3229 / 3361 ms |
| IR-01 r1 | BenchLab | field_edit (pop-up menu opened) | 1787 / 2295 ms |
| IR-01 r3 | BenchLab | permission_prompt_shown (+623 ms) | 2398 / 2928 ms |
| IR-02 r2 | BenchLab | banner_shown (+1479 ms) | 1943 / 2793 ms |
| IR-02 r3 | BenchLab | banner_shown (+1733 ms) | 2070 / 2997 ms |
| IR-03 r1 | Cua Driver, BenchLab | save_prompt_shown (+591 ms) | 2637 / 2947 ms |
| IR-03 r2 | BenchLab | save_prompt_shown (+559 ms) | 1964 / 2076 ms |
| IR-03 r2 | BenchLab | save_prompt_shown (+567 ms) | 3001 / 3877 ms |
| IR-03 r3 | BenchLab | save_prompt_shown (+694 ms) | 3020 / 3238 ms |
| IR-03 r3 | BenchLab | save_prompt_shown (+332 ms) | 1103 / 1561 ms |

Call-start times come from the agent stream's tool_use timestamps, which may lead daemon receipt slightly. Sentinel resolution is about 50 ms.

Example batch (IR-01 r1):

```json
{"steps":[
  {"tool":"set_value","args":{"pid":22853,"window_id":14991,"element_token":"s00000022:1","value":"..."}},
  {"tool":"set_value","args":{"pid":22853,"window_id":14991,"element_token":"s00000022:2","value":"..."}},
  {"tool":"click","args":{"pid":22853,"window_id":14991,"element_token":"s00000022:3","delivery_mode":"background"}}],
 "observe":{},"delivery_mode":"background"}
```

The end-observation diff includes `+ [7] AXSheet (alert) [id=_NS:87 actions=[raise]]`.

### Workaround and additional context

Hypothesis (unverified): Something on the end-observation or post-action path orders the target window (or its sheet's parent) to the front when the window has a newly attached sheet, menu or overlay. The driver then restores the order, or the sheet settles. Candidates: an AX action or attribute write on the sheet or its parent, or the screenshot/capture path for a window whose child-window list just changed. The one sample that lists a "Cua Driver" window above the user's window suggests the driver's own overlay window takes part in at least one case.

Per-trial sentinel.jsonl, lab-events.jsonl and agent stream logs are available on request.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the screenshot frame after an ax_window_unresolved read on macOS
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a `get_window_state` read that ends in `degraded_reason: ax_window_unresolved` recommends `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, but it also dropped the window's snapshot. Every window-scope pixel action after it (`click` x,y, `zoom`) was then refused with `screenshot_context_missing` / `window_never_read`, even right after the read and even in the foreground.
- What changed: when an unresolved read carries a verified screenshot of the requested window, it now publishes an empty snapshot with that screenshot's pixel frame instead of removing the snapshot. Foreground pixel actions can map x,y off the screenshot. Background input is still refused, because the exact-target background gate checks the AX window itself and does not look at the snapshot. Without a verified screenshot (a tree-only read, or a frame that failed verification), the read still drops the snapshot as before. Only `ax_window_unresolved` keeps the frame: an `ax_app_launching` or locked-screen read stays observation-only and drops the snapshot. The escalation text now says to act by pixel off this screenshot with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, and that foreground delivery is still refused if the window does not become the app's focused AXWindow. When the read carried no screenshot, it says to re-snapshot with one first.

The snapshot bookkeeping moved into one helper, `update_snapshot`, so the decision can be tested against a real snapshot store.

## Related work

Fixes #6755

RFC: not needed. No contract change; this makes the existing escalation hint accurate.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: macOS only. After an unresolved read, the response now has a `snapshot_id` (with no element rows) and a `capture_id`, and foreground pixel actions on that window work. Old element tokens for the window are still invalidated, now listed as replaced rather than removed.
- Risk and rollback: low. A screenshot-only read (`include_accessibility_tree:false`) already publishes this same empty, frame-carrying snapshot for any window, unresolved ones included, so no new kind of state is introduced. Revert the PR to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib get_window_state` (42 passed). The new `unresolved_read_keeps_its_screenshot_frame_for_pixel_actions` failed on the first commit, which has the old behavior, and passes after the fix. `unresolved_read_without_a_screenshot_drops_the_window_snapshot` pins the tree-only case. `only_an_unresolved_window_read_keeps_its_screenshot_frame` pins the launching and locked-screen cases. `bin/ci --signoff` passed all 9 scoped repository checks (clippy, unit tests, Windows cross-check, generated reference, UniFFI bindings, formatting, headers).
- Manual or platform evidence: none yet. I could not reproduce an unresolved AXWindow on purpose.
- Known gaps or CI still required: native Windows and Linux lanes and the macOS E2E lanes run in CI only.
