title: fix(cua-driver): honor the permissions grant verification in the macOS capture consent gate
body:
## Why

After `cua-driver permissions grant` reported direct capture as granted, the daemon still refused every implicit capture with `direct_capture_consent_required`. The capture gate trusted only replayd's `ScreenCaptureApprovals.plist`, and on the reporter's macOS 26.6.2 machine that file had no entry for `CuaDriver.app`. The grant's own record (`direct_capture_verification`, source `permissions_grant`) was there, but the gate never read it.

## What changed

- The grant record gains `consent_alert_raised`. The grant sets it when its probe frame captured on macOS 15 or later while macOS held the process responsible for itself (`responsibility_get_pid_responsible_for_pid`), which means the probe raised the alert for this bundle and not for a launcher. Records without the field, and records from macOS 14, still show in `permissions status` but count as no consent.
- `capture_consent::consent_state` treats such a record for the running bundle as recorded consent, checked before the approvals file. The gate reads it through `driver_daemon_direct_capture_evidence_store`, only when the process is attributed as the driver daemon and macOS also holds the reading process responsible for itself. An embedded (`serve --embedded`), caller-launched or reparented driver gets no record, because macOS attributes its captures, and the alert, to another app.
- The out-of-range timestamp check that `permissions status` applies now also guards the gate.
- Unit tests: a record that raised the alert counts as consent with no approvals entry; a record without the flag (macOS 14, foreign-responsible writer, legacy file) does not; neither does a record for the other bundle (`CuaDriverLocal.app`), the driver's record under host, caller or unknown attribution, or a reader that is not responsible for itself.

## Scope

macOS capture gate and the grant record it reads. Reading the approvals file, the `CUA_DRIVER_ALLOW_CAPTURE_CONSENT_ALERT` override and the grant flow otherwise work as before. I have not explained why replayd's file has no entry on 26.6.2. On the dev host, opening that file blocks (the call keeps returning `EINTR`), so I could not inspect it.

## Tradeoffs

The gate asks macOS for the responsible process instead of trusting a parent pid of 1: a bundled driver reparented to launchd after its launcher exits still answers to that launcher's host. `permissions status` keeps its existing attribution rule. Users who granted before this change have a record without the flag and need to run `permissions grant` once more before the record opens the gate; until then the approvals-file check applies, as before.

## Blast Radius

Only affects macOS 15+ daemons running from `CuaDriver.app` or `CuaDriverLocal.app` where a flagged grant record exists. When the record is missing, invalid or unflagged, behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks in quick mode (formatting incl. rustfmt for `platform-macos`, SPDX headers, image refs) pass.
- CI "Rust macOS unit" and "fmt, clippy, test (macos-26)" run the `platform-macos` unit tests, including `a_verified_grant_counts_as_consent_without_an_approvals_entry` and `only_records_that_raised_the_alert_count_as_consent`. Rust was not built locally (shared host).
- Not run: a desktop E2E on a fresh macOS 26.6 install, and an executed mutation of the tests.

- [x] `bin/ci --quick` run before push (shared host; heavy checks run in CI)

Fixes #6831

title: fix(cua-driver): emit Windows agent cursor hook updates
body:
Salvaged from #4951
Refs #4947

## Why

On Windows the agent cursor is drawn, but a registered cursor hook never gets an event, and `cursor_hook_supported()` stays false. This carries @hqhq1025's #4951 onto current main: the Windows overlay now reports the applied hotspot after each command and animation tick, and declares hook support once its overlay window is up.

## What changed

- `platform-windows` overlay: queues a `CursorHookEvent` from the applied render state (glide samples, click pulses, drag holds and releases) and publishes after releasing the render lock. Anonymous, human-origin, ended and retired sessions are skipped. Each render entry owns a lifetime flag that session end and removal clear, so queued samples from a retired session are dropped. (#4951)
- `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs`: runs the pinned UBRN Cargo entrypoint directly instead of the npm `ubrn.cmd` launcher, which Windows Node cannot spawn without a shell and which joins arguments without quoting. (#4951)
- On top of #4951: merged main (adapted to `seed_start_if_unplaced` and `RenderStateCore::placed`), gave the generator test a `TEMP` directory so it passes on the Linux script-test lane, and updated the core cursor hook test's doc comment, which still said Windows has no emitter.

## Scope

Windows adapter emission only. Public SDK records, options and generated bindings are unchanged. #4947 (Windows right-click modifiers) is a separate PR and not included.

## Tradeoffs

Windows reports rendered positions, so a glide produces one event per changed frame. macOS and Linux report the commanded target once per move. Both are cursor positions in screen coordinates. Windows also needs the overlay thread running to emit, and reports support only after that thread starts, so an embedder that checks support before the overlay is up sees `false`.

## Blast Radius

Windows cua-driver processes with a registered cursor hook. Without a hook, `cursor_hook_enabled()` short-circuits every new path. The generator change affects anyone regenerating bindings: on Unix it runs the same `cargo run --manifest-path` command that the npm launcher runs.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `platform-windows` library tests (93 passed, including the new cursor hook owner test) and the core `cursor_hook_platform_support` test, on Linux. These exercise the adapter's portable code, not Win32 behavior.
- `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/` (381 passed). Restoring main's generator makes the new generator test fail with "never launch an npm .cmd through spawnSync".
- Native Windows behavior was not run here and is left to the Windows CI lanes.

title: fix(cua-driver): identify Windows pipe clients from the pipe token
body:
## Why

On Windows, a daemon started from a normal (unelevated) window rejected the same user's SSH session with `os error 233`. The daemon checked the client by opening its process and reading the process token. An elevated SSH shell's process DACL grants only Administrators, SYSTEM and the SSH logon SID, so `OpenProcess` failed with access denied and the connection was dropped before any request was read. The fix identifies the client from the pipe connection itself.

## What changed

- `named_pipe_client_sid` now reads the user SID from the token the pipe captured for its client (`ImpersonateNamedPipeClient`, `OpenThreadToken`, `RevertToSelf`). The process token is kept as the fallback. If `RevertToSelf` fails, the daemon aborts, so a runtime thread never keeps running as the client.
- The accept loop now checks the client after reading the first request line and before parsing it. A client that opens the pipe with dynamic context tracking (the `CreateFileW` default) hands the pipe its token only when it writes. A rejected connection is closed without parsing anything.
- The duplicated token-to-SID code is now one helper, `token_user_sid`. New Windows test `named_pipe_authentication_tests::connected_client_is_identified_from_the_pipe_token`: for both static and dynamic context tracking, a client writes one line, the server reads it, and the SID read from the pipe must match the current user.

## Scope

Covers the Windows daemon's named-pipe accept check in `serve.rs`. The SID comparison and the pipe ACL are unchanged, so another user is still refused. Leaves out the `cua-driver-uia` helper pipe, whose only client is the daemon that spawns it under the same token.

## Tradeoffs

Without the process-token fallback, a client that opens the pipe at anonymous impersonation level would be refused. Such a client was accepted before this change, and the fallback keeps it accepted. Both sources give the client's real user SID.

## Blast Radius

Every Windows daemon connection goes through this check. Same-user clients that work today still match: the captured token is the client's own token, and the old path remains the fallback. The new case that now connects is the same user's elevated client from another logon session.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers) passed. Clippy, the unit tests and the Windows cross-compile were skipped on this machine and run in the Windows CI lane, which runs `named_pipe_authentication_tests::`.
- The cross-logon-session case (unelevated daemon on the desktop, elevated SSH client) is not automated. The reporter offered to test it on their setup.

Fixes #4957

title: fix(cua-driver): the macOS permission guide names the app the driver runs in
body:
Salvaged from #6985

## Why

System Settings lists the app bundle the driver runs in. When the driver ships inside another app (`Host.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver`, or under `Contents/Resources`), Accessibility and Screen Recording show that app's name, but the permission guide and the terminal lines still said to turn on "Cua Driver", which is not in the list.

## What changed

- The guide reads the shown name of the bundle that holds the running executable, as System Settings does: NSBundle's localized `CFBundleDisplayName`, else `CFBundleName`. The window title, step texts, drag hint and tile, done title, terminal banner, and the "Still waiting" and "All set" lines use it.
- The banner's "click + and choose …" step names the app as the file picker lists it, by its Finder name (`NSFileManager displayNameAtPath:`), and names the folder that holds it when that is not `/Applications`. The picker lists the file name, not the bundle name: CuaDriver.app is "CuaDriver" there, not "Cua Driver".
- The host bundle is the nearest enclosing `.app` that has a `Contents/Info.plist`, so a plain folder named `*.app` inside the host's Resources does not hide it.
- The guide's rows take the height their wrapped words need, and the window grows to hold the taller step, so a long host name is not clipped. With "Cua Driver" the layout is unchanged.
- #8219 moved the guide to the top left of the screen. Its `guide_origin` now takes the grown window height, so a taller guide still opens 48 points below the top of the screen.

## Scope

CMGS's commit from #6985, unchanged, rebased onto main and since merged with current main, with our fixes on top as separate commits. #6985's base predates the quarantine renewal on main, so its `quarantine list and flaky tooling` check failed on two expired entries; on current main that check passes. Outside an app bundle the copy stays "Cua Driver". CuaDriver.app's `CFBundleName` and `CFBundleDisplayName` are both "Cua Driver", so its copy is unchanged except the picker step, which now says "choose CuaDriver". The `cua-driver permissions` and `cua-driver test` output (`cli.rs`, `selftest.rs`) still says "Cua Driver" and is left for a follow-up.

## Blast Radius

macOS only: the permission guide window and the permission gate's terminal output. The name lookup falls back to "Cua Driver" whenever the bundle or its keys can't be read.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (quick mode) and `cargo fmt --all --check` pass on the branch merged with current main.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib permissions::` on macOS: 49 passed. The new `vendor.app` case in `the_host_is_the_app_that_encloses_the_executable` failed before the Info.plist check and passes after it. `layout_fits_the_window` pins the old row positions and window height, and `rows_grow_to_fit_a_long_host_name` covers the growth.
- New tests: `permissions::guide::tests::every_name_in_the_copy_follows_the_host_app`, `permissions::panel::tests::the_host_is_the_app_that_encloses_the_executable`, `permissions::panel::tests::the_shown_name_is_the_localized_one_settings_lists`, `permissions::gate::tests::terminal_lines_name_the_host_app`, `permissions::gate::tests::the_banner_points_to_the_host_app_as_the_file_picker_shows_it`. They run in this PR's macOS CI.
- From #6985: on a fresh macOS 26 VM with the driver bundled in another app, the guide, both steps, the tile, the banner and the status lines named the host app, matching the System Settings rows.

title: feat(cua-driver): report is_password for Windows Edit elements
body:
Salvaged from #4958

## Why

UIA exposes a Windows password box as an ordinary `Edit` with `IsPassword` set, and `get_window_state` never read it, so a caller could not tell a password field from a plain text field. macOS and Linux already show this through the role. @WingedGuardian's change reads `UIA_IsPasswordPropertyId` and surfaces it. This PR carries their commit onto current main (the `get_window_state` tool moved into its own module since) and fixes three gaps found in review.

## What changed

- From #4958: `WindowElement.is_password`, a `password` marker on the Markdown row, and a password field's value dropped before it reaches `value`, the label or the Markdown row.
- An unsupported `IsPassword` stays absent. It is read with `GetCachedPropertyValueEx(ignoreDefaultValue)`, because the plain getter turns an unsupported property into its default `false`.
- `is_password: false` is reported only on `Edit` controls. It was keyed on the `set_value` and `text` actions, which sliders, progress bars and read-only document views also carry. Non-indexed password rows in the Markdown now get the marker too.

## Scope

Windows UIA walk only. The MSAA fallback leaves the field absent. Other tools that read a UIA value live are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Adds one optional field to the Windows `get_window_state` output and a marker to its Markdown rows. Existing consumers ignore the new field. The only behavior removed is echoing the value of a field that reports `IsPassword`.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks (formatting, headers, TypeScript typecheck) pass. The Windows build, `platform-windows` unit tests, the contract and binding drift checks, and the docs reference check run in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the macOS cursor overlay out of Mission Control
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, the agent cursor overlay is a display-sized, normal-level window that joins every Space with `Stationary` behavior. It was created ordered in and stayed on screen even with no cursor drawn, including after a session ended. The reporter saw Mission Control's Desktop thumbnails show only wallpaper while it existed, and the previews came back once the daemon stopped and the window was gone.
- What changed:
  - The overlay surfaces start ordered out. The render loop orders them in only while a cursor paints a tile, and orders them out when the last tile clears. Ending a session or hiding the cursor now removes the window.
  - The surfaces use `Transient | IgnoresCycle` instead of `Stationary`, so Mission Control leaves the overlay out while a cursor is showing.
  - The render loop keeps tracking the last pin target while the surfaces are ordered out. A frame without a cursor command falls back to it, so a stale target would repin a newly shown cursor above the previous session's window.
  - A new macOS E2E, `overlay_window_macos_test.rs`, starts an overlay daemon and checks CoreGraphics' on-screen list: no daemon window before a cursor, one after `move_cursor`, none after `end_session`. It runs in the canonical macOS native lane.

## Related work

Fixes #7212

## Scope

macOS overlay only. Mission Control is a macOS feature. The Windows and Linux overlays are unchanged.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: while no agent cursor is drawn, the overlay is not in CoreGraphics' window list. `list_windows` already left it out. Capture exclusion already skipped it when nothing painted.
- Risk: z-ordering when the cursor appears. Order-in goes through the existing paths: above the pinned target window, or `orderFrontRegardless` when there is no target. A display reconfiguration reapplies the order. Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `bin/ci --quick` (formatting, headers, workflow sync) and `rustfmt --check` on `overlay.rs` pass. The scoped repository checks need a build, so compilation and unit tests are left to CI.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. Display capture timed out on the available macOS host, so I could not reproduce Mission Control live. The root cause is inferred from the issue's evidence: the only recovery that worked was removing the overlay window.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the new E2E has to run on the canonical logged-in macOS lane. Checking the thumbnails themselves in Mission Control needs a person on a multi-Space Mac.

title: fix(cua-driver): match running Windows Store apps to their bundle_id grant
body:
Salvaged from #4962

Fixes #3330

## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, a running Store (packaged) app showed up in `list_apps` with `bundle_id: null`, so a capability-manifest grant such as `bundle_id: Microsoft.WindowsNotepad_8wekyb3d8bbwe` could never match it. The only grant that worked was the versioned `WindowsApps` executable path, which changes with every Store update. This was the part of #3330 still open after the desktop fix.
- What changed: `list_apps` reads the package identity Windows reports for each running process (`GetApplicationUserModelId`, `GetPackageFamilyName`) and uses it to pick the installed `uwp` entry before the existing executable-name match. The running Store app then reports the same `bundle_id` that its installed entry already shows, and the bounded-mode grant check reads `bundle_id` from `list_apps`, so the grant matches. Unpackaged apps are unchanged.

Bryan Cruz (@Bryancruzcb) wrote the fix in #4962. This PR keeps their commit as authored and adds one commit on top. That commit moves the change onto current main, where `list_apps` now lives in its own module. It also updates the `list_apps` description, its generated reference and the grant-check comments to describe packaged-app matching. Three more commits fix the AppxManifest scan the installed `uwp` entries come from. It matched the `<Applications>` wrapper first, found no `Id`, and fell back to `!App`. It also read only the literal spelling `Id="` and could pick an `<Application>` inside a comment. It now skips comments, CDATA, processing instructions and declarations, takes the first real `<Application>` tag, and reads its attributes in XML syntax. A Store app whose application Id is anything else got a `launch_path` its AUMID never equals, so it would still have reported no `bundle_id`.

## Related work

RFC: not required. There is no new grant type or contract. A `bundle_id` grant now matches the identity `list_apps` already reports for the installed app, and that identity comes from the OS rather than from the executable name.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. A running packaged app's `list_apps` entry is merged with its installed `uwp` entry (`kind: "uwp"`, `bundle_id`, `launch_path`) instead of appearing as an anonymous `desktop` entry. Matching rules:
  - An exact AUMID match wins.
  - A packaged process with no AUMID matches only when its package family has exactly one installed entry.
  - A different app in the same package never takes another app's entry.
  - An unpackaged process never matches a `uwp` entry.
- Risk and rollback: the change is limited to Windows `list_apps` matching. An unpackaged process cannot claim a package identity, so the grant check's existing rule (Windows path grants are compared only against the OS-reported executable path) is unchanged. To roll back, revert this PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: eight new unit tests cover the matching rules, four cover the manifest `Application` Id scan (the wrapper and markup tests fail on the old scan), plus one test that the unpackaged test process has no package identity. They run in the Windows lane. The scoped repository checks (formatting, lockfiles, SPDX headers, docs code blocks) pass. The heavy checks (Windows cross-check, clippy, unit tests, generated-reference check) run in CI.
- Manual or platform evidence: from #4962, on Windows 11 Pro x64 in bounded mode with a one-app manifest and Store Notepad running:

  | Grant | Before (0.34.1) | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `bundle_id: Microsoft.WindowsNotepad_8wekyb3d8bbwe` | `list_windows` refused (`bounded_resource_outside_manifest`) | `list_windows` and `get_window_state` allowed |
  | `executable: <WindowsApps path>` | allowed | allowed |
  | Chrome (not in the manifest), both runs | refused | refused |

- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - A packaged process whose package is not in the installed `Main` package list (some system components, for example) still gets no identity.
  - Multi-app packages are covered by unit tests only.
  - A grant written as a full AUMID (`…!App`) still does not match a running app, because `list_apps` reports the package family name as `bundle_id`. Before this PR it did not match either.

title: fix(cua-driver): never retype a batched macOS send into a terminal
body:
Salvaged from #7276
Fixes #7245

This lands @CMGS's three commits from #7276 unchanged, rebased onto main. Their authorship is kept on each commit.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: a background `type_text` into a macOS terminal at a no-echo prompt (`read -s`, `sudo`, `ssh`) types the text twice. The batched send's read-back sees an unchanged screen, counts 0 delivered, and the retype branch in `cgevent_type_verified` sends the whole text again. The reply then says "delivered 0 of N … retry" with `retry_from_character: 0`, which invites a third copy. vim's `dd` shrinks the screen and also counts as 0. A native control that keeps only the first character of each batched event ("aq" for "abcdefghijklmnopq") was retyped from character 2 and ended as "aqcdefghijklmnopq".
- What changed: terminals now skip the batched retype, as web content already did. A native field's tail is retyped only when the read-back equals the old value followed by the first `done` characters of the text (`retype_from`, `appends_prefix`). With `done` 0 that means an unchanged value, so the retype of a field that took nothing (#6884) stays. A terminal key insert that the screen does not show in full reports no delivered count (`reported`) on both the background and foreground key routes. The reply is unverified instead of `type_text_incomplete`.

## Related work

Related, not part of this PR: #7277 (foreground-retry advice for an unconfirmed terminal insert) and #7278 (terminal confirmation against existing scrollback).

## Compatibility and risk

- A terminal insert at a no-echo prompt goes in once and replies unverified.
- A native field that took a strict prefix of the text is finished as before, and a field that took nothing is still retyped.
- A native partial whose read-back is not the old value followed by the typed prefix (an insert at a mid-field cursor, or a field that rewrote the text) now replies unverified instead of being retyped from the counted position.
- Scope: macOS `type_text` key rung only (`platform-macos`). No other platform has this retype path. Reverting the PR restores the old retype.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `a_native_field_retypes_only_a_proven_partial_tail`, `a_first_character_per_event_read_back_is_not_retyped`, `a_partial_is_retyped_only_after_its_typed_prefix`, `a_terminal_screen_is_never_retyped`, `an_unconfirmed_terminal_insert_reports_no_delivered_count`.
- The commits cherry-picked onto main without conflicts. The scoped repository checks (quick stage) passed. Rust checks run in CI.
- Contributor evidence from #7276: on a macOS 26 VM, a background `read -s` given "abc" received 3 characters instead of 6, and vim `dd` deleted one line.

title: fix(cua-driver): match packaged-app frames to their app in capability manifests
body:
## Why

A packaged Windows app's top-level frame is owned by `ApplicationFrameHost.exe`, which shares one pid across unrelated apps. The bounded-mode manifest check attested identity from that host pid, so it got `bundle_id=null` / `launch_path=null` and no app grant could match. Every window-scoped call on a packaged app was refused with `bounded_resource_outside_manifest`, even when the manifest listed the app.

## What changed

- `ToolRegistry::set_window_identity_resolver` lets a platform map a `(pid, window_id)` owned by a shared host to the pid of the app it hosts. Manifest enrichment then attests the fingerprint and `list_apps` identity of that app. The resource's `pid` and `window_id` are unchanged.
- Windows installs a resolver that accepts only the system's own `ApplicationFrameHost.exe` (the full path in the system directory) as a host, then uses the existing `resolve_uwp_app_pid` to find the app process that owns the frame's `CoreWindow`.

## Scope

Covers window-scoped calls (`get_window_state`, `click` and other input with a `window_id`), which are the handles `launch_app` returns for a packaged app. A pid-only call on the host pid (`kill_app`, `list_windows(pid)` on the host) stays refused: that pid hosts many apps, so no single app grant can cover it.

Not included: making a running packaged app report its AUMID or package family as `bundle_id` in `list_apps`. #4962 does that. With both changes, a `bundle_id` grant matches a packaged app's frame. With this one alone, an `executable` grant for the app's `WindowsApps` path matches it. macOS and Linux install no resolver, so their windows keep their owning pid's identity.

## Blast Radius

Only bounded mode or a loaded capability manifest reads the resolved identity. The host check means another process can't claim an app's identity by giving its own window the frame class and reparenting that app's window under it.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --features yaml --lib bounded_window_grant_matches_the_app_its_shared_host_frames` passes. The test covers three cases: no resolver is refused (the old behavior), a resolved frame is allowed, and a frame the resolver can't attribute is refused.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass. Windows cross-compile, clippy and the full unit suites run in CI.
- Not run: a live Windows bounded-mode run against Calculator. This host can't run Windows.

Fixes #4991

title: fix(cua-driver): confirm macOS terminal typed text only by a copy the scrollback did not already hold
body:
Salvaged from #7278
Fixes #7242

This lands @CMGS's two scrollback-count commits from #7278 unchanged, with their authorship kept on each commit. #7278 was stacked on #7276, which shipped as #8128; main is merged in, so the diff is only the scrollback count plus one follow-up commit of ours.

## Why

A terminal's `AXValue` is its whole scrollback, so `typed_progress`'s `contains()` confirmed a command typed again ("git push" already on screen from an earlier run) whose keys landed only in part ("git pu"). The reply said verified, and a caller that sends Return after a verified line ran the partial command.

## What changed

- On the terminal key rung, `Complete` needs `after != before` and more copies of the text in `after` than in `before`. The copies in `before` are counted once per poll loop (`await_typed_delivery`), and an unreadable `before` never confirms.
- A terminal reads that `before` again after focus settles, just before the keys go out, so an activation that restores a different pane cannot confirm with an old copy from that pane.
- The `AXSelectedText` write and non-terminal keys keep `contains()`: a selection replaced by the same text leaves the count unchanged there and would read as not landed.

## Scope

macOS `type_text` key rung only (`platform-macos`). kitty's `AXValue` route (`ax_value_insert_landed`) has the same blind spot (#7242) and is not touched here.

## Blast Radius

A partial terminal insert whose text is already in the scrollback now replies unverified instead of verified. If the scrollback drops an old copy as the new one lands (`clear`, a trimmed buffer), the count does not grow and the reply is unverified, never a false confirm. Non-terminal targets behave as before.

## Verification

- Focused test `a_terminal_confirms_only_a_copy_its_scrollback_did_not_already_hold`: partial delivery with the text in the scrollback, fresh delivery, full new copy, shrinking value, unchanged value, unreadable `before`, and the non-terminal cases. `a_terminal_screen_is_never_retyped` now runs with the terminal flag set.
- Merged with main (conflicts only where main's copy of #8128 lacked the terminal flag). The scoped repository checks (quick stage) passed; Rust checks run in CI.
- Contributor evidence from #7278: with the terminal guard dropped, or with `contains()` kept for terminals, the focused test fails.

## Review notes

- Kept: a batched send into a native field that showed no change is still retyped in full. Main does this since #6884, and c9813ffbb5 keeps it on purpose. Terminals and web content are never retyped.

title: fix(cua-driver): fall back to WARP for unusable Windows captures
body:
Salvaged from #5001

Refs #1600

## Why

Windows.Graphics.Capture can succeed and still hand back an entirely black frame. On Windows 11 ARM64 under UTM with VioGpu3D, every single-window screenshot came back black, while desktop capture and UIA worked. @SDSLeon's #5001 retries an unusable hardware WGC frame once on a software WARP device, which recovers the window's own pixels even when another window covers it. This PR keeps their three commits as authored, merges current main, and adds one fix on top.

## What changed

- From #5001 (SDSLeon): a WARP retry after hardware WGC errors or returns an invalid or all-RGB-black frame. WGC frames are normalized to the same DWM-inset geometry that PrintWindow capture and `bitmap_to_screen` use, so click mapping now works on WGC frames. The screen-region fallback crops to DWM bounds and refuses windows that are partly off-screen. `screenshot_window_bytes` refuses a fallback image that shows a covering window, and GDI bitmaps are deselected before `GetDIBits`.
- Ours: the off-screen check in the screen-region fallback now requires the capture rectangle to lie on real monitors (`monitors_cover`, an exact union test, so overlapping mirroring pseudo-monitors neither double-count nor hide a gap). Before, it only checked the virtual screen's bounding box. With staggered monitors, a window over a gap in that box passed, and BitBlt returned black pixels as a valid capture.

## Scope

Windows capture only (`platform-windows` capture, WGC, `bitmap_to_screen`) and the WPF background-capture E2E case. macOS and Linux are unchanged. #1600 (UWP capture) is related, but this PR does not resolve it.

## Blast Radius

Every Windows window screenshot goes through this path. On hardware where WGC already works, the first attempt succeeds and nothing changes. There are two deliberate behavior changes. First, `get_window_state` and `zoom` now return an error instead of an image when the only image available shows a covering window. Second, when PrintWindow comes back mostly black and every fallback fails, callers get an error instead of the black bitmap. A target that really is entirely black can't be told apart from a broken capture.

## Verification

- At #5001's head merged with main: the scoped repository checks passed. That covers `bin/ci --quick`, rustfmt, and cross-compiled `check` and `clippy --all-targets` for `platform-windows` and `cua-driver`, plus a `--tests` check of `cua-driver-e2e` for the Windows MSVC target.
- On this branch: `bin/ci --quick` passed. New unit tests cover a staggered two-monitor layout and overlapping monitors. The overlap test fails against a sum-of-areas version.
- Native Windows unit tests and the Windows capture E2E did not run locally (Linux host). They run in this PR's Windows CI lanes. #5001 has the contributor's native ARM64 and canonical-matrix evidence for their commits.

title: fix(cua-driver): stamp macOS pointer gestures with their start time, not a click-group ID
body:
## Why

CGEvent integer field 58 is the event timestamp. The macOS pixel click, drag, scroll primer and interactive pointer paths wrote a "click-group ID" there: the sub-second part of the wall clock, or a small counter in the interactive stream. Chromium and Electron then saw a click from the first second after boot, older than the page, and Blink's soft-navigation check crashed the renderer whenever the click started a same-document navigation.

## What changed

- Every window-addressed pointer gesture still shares one field 58 value across its events, but that value is now the gesture's start time: `gesture_timestamp()`, `CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW` nanoseconds, the clock `NSEvent.timestamp` reads in seconds. The interactive pointer stream takes a fresh one on each press in place of its counter.
- A new test, `window_addressed_pointer_gestures_carry_their_start_time`, drives a background double click, a foreground window click, a right click and a background drag, and requires each gesture's events to share one timestamp taken between the uptime read before and after.

## Scope

macOS pointer events only. Window routing (f51/f91/f92), the pid filter (f40), click state, button and subtype stamps, and which events carry field 58 are unchanged. Keyboard and AX paths never wrote field 58.

## Tradeoffs

Two earlier heads of this PR dropped the shared stamp. Leaving field 58 unset (f567f91) or stamping each event at post (d520cbd) made the macOS hosted lane's Electron background double clicks deliver nothing, not even a mousedown. The per-event stamp also lost the background focus click before typing. Main's shared value delivered both. So this keeps the shared value and fixes only its clock.

## Blast Radius

Every window-addressed pixel click, double click, right and middle click, drag, scroll primer and interactive pointer event on macOS. The events, fields and routes are main's; only the field 58 value changes, from a sub-second wall-clock value to the current uptime.

## Verification

- On macOS 26 (this host, no events posted): `CGEventSetTimestamp(e, clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW))` gives `NSEvent.timestamp` equal to `systemUptime`.
- macOS hosted E2E at f567f91 and d520cbd failed `shared_web_action_matrix_is_state_verified` (Electron background `double_click`, plus background type-after-click at d520cbd, with `clicks=0`), on both attempts each. Main passes those rows.
- The scoped repository checks (quick stage: rustfmt, SPDX headers) passed at this head. Unit tests, clippy and the E2E lanes for this head run in CI and in verification.

Fixes #7292

title: fix(cua-driver): read Chrome's page content on macOS on the first read and while polling
body:
Salvaged from #7410

Fixes #4126

## Why

On macOS, `get_window_state` on Chrome or Edge returns only the browser chrome. The first read of a fresh browser never includes the page, and a client that reads more often than every 2 s never gets it. Chrome rejects both accessibility opt-in writes, yet the rejected `AXEnhancedUserInterface` write still starts Chromium's 2 s debounce before it turns web accessibility on. The driver cached nothing and wrote both attributes again on every walk, which restarted that countdown each time.

## What changed

- abonneth's three commits from #7410, unchanged. Authorship is kept.
  - A refusal of both attributes is cached per process lifetime (`AccessibilityOptIn::Refused`, `Wait::Refused`) and is not written again for 3 s.
  - If the rejected `AXEnhancedUserInterface` reads back as set (`AccessibilityOptIn::Deferred`, which is what Chrome does), the first read waits for the web tree without writing again during the wait.
  - The two macOS browser rows held back for #4126 run in the Darwin browser lane again, and their allowlist entries are removed.
- One commit on top that names the #4126 rows in the lane script's comment.

## Scope

macOS `platform-macos` accessibility enablement and the macOS standalone browser lane list. No API, schema or MCP change; `AccessibilityOptIn` is crate-internal. Apps that accept either attribute take the same path as before. Apps that are neither Chromium nor Electron stay `NotNeeded`, as on main.

## Blast Radius

Only Chromium and Electron processes on macOS. The first read of a Chrome or Edge process now waits for the page tree once per browser process. Later reads are unchanged. A Chromium-family app that refuses both writes and does not read the attribute back as set is now asked at most once per 3 s instead of on every walk.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `cargo fmt --check`, the E2E inventory test and `bin/ci --quick` pass. #7410's CI at its head passed macOS clippy and unit tests.
- The hosted macOS E2E lane, including the standalone browser rows, passed at the pre-merge head and is rerun at the head that includes current main.
- Review note, dismissed: a Chromium-family app that rejects both writes and does not read `AXEnhancedUserInterface` back as set (`Refused`) still returns its first read without waiting for a web tree. This is deliberate. On main that case returned at once too, and it wrote both attributes again on every walk. Chrome reads the attribute back as set and takes the `Deferred` path, which waits. A `Refused` app has given no sign that it will build a tree, so it pays no wait. It is asked again after 3 s, which is what `a_refused_opt_in_is_not_repeated_until_chrome_had_time_to_act_on_it` pins.

The contributor's hosted-runner measurements are in #7410.

title: test(cua-driver): pin Windows posted clicks against an SDL-style mouse leave
body:
Fixes #5071

## Why

#5071 showed that a background click posted to an SDL 2 window failed while the real cursor sat outside it: the window's own `TrackMouseEvent(TME_LEAVE)` call made Windows post `WM_MOUSELEAVE` between the press and the release, SDL moved its pointer to the window edge, and the release missed the button. #5584 (released in cua-driver-rs 0.38.0) fixed this by suspending the target's GUI thread while the move, press and release are posted, so the leave is always queued after the release. Its regression test, though, fakes the leave by posting `WM_MOUSELEAVE` from the window procedure and checks only message order. This PR pins the click against the real Windows mechanism and the outcome the issue measured: a completed click.

## What changed

- The test receiver in `platform-windows/src/input/mouse.rs` now behaves like SDL 2's Win32 window procedure. On an untracked move it calls `TrackMouseEvent(TME_LEAVE)`. It takes the pointer position from `WM_MOUSEMOVE`, and on `WM_MOUSELEAVE` from the real cursor clamped to the window. A press counts only over the button, moving off the button cancels it, and a release over the button completes a click.
- The window is hidden and placed off every monitor, so the real cursor is never over it and Windows posts the leave as soon as the move is handled. That is the issue's failing "cursor outside" condition, without real input.
- The race, double-click and same-thread tests now also assert the completed-click count (200, 2 and 1).

## Scope

Test-only, so it carries `no-release`. The issue's "cursor inside the window" condition is left out because it needs the real cursor moved, and plain `cargo test` stays hermetic. Two things are not covered here and are listed as follow-ups: posted drags (`post_drag`, `post_drag_screen`) still post across sleeps without suspending the target, so an SDL target can see the same leave in the middle of a drag; and the Plants vs. Zombies report in the issue thread, which the reporter traced to a separate focus symptom with no SDL involved.

## Blast Radius

Only `#[cfg(test)]` code in `platform-windows` changes. No production code changes.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass, and `cargo clippy --tests -D warnings` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` on `platform-windows` is clean.
- The Windows unit lane runs the tests on this PR.
- Mutation check: with the thread suspension turned off on a throwaway branch, the Windows unit lane failed both tests the way the issue reports. The real leave arrived between press and release (`[MOVE, DOWN, LEAVE, UP]` for click 0), and the double click completed 1 of 2 clicks. With the suspension in place (this PR), the same tests run on the PR's Windows unit lane.

title: fix(cua-driver): exit the macOS daemon when an update replaces its app
body:
## Why

After an in-place update (`cua-driver update --apply`, `brew reinstall --cask cuadriver`), a `serve` daemon can keep running the old image: launchd's `KeepAlive` respawns it inside the swap window, so it runs from the renamed backup bundle or from a bundle that has since been deleted. macOS then judges its TCC grants against an install that no longer exists. The probes report Accessibility and Screen Recording off while System Settings shows them on, and the setup wizard waits at step 1 indefinitely. In both reproductions on #7461, killing that daemon was enough to recover. This change makes the daemon notice the swap itself and exit.

## What changed

- `platform_macos::running_image::was_replaced()` compares the vnode the process image is mapped from (`proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDREGIONPATHINFO)`) with the file now at the launch path. It reports a replacement when the image was deleted or moved aside, or when the launch path is missing.
- The standalone macOS `serve` loop checks it every 2 seconds and shuts down cleanly (removing its socket and pid file) once it is true. launchd's `KeepAlive`, or the next client's `open -n -g CuaDriver.app --args serve`, then starts the new install.

## Scope

- Covers every install path that swaps the bundle under a running daemon: the install script, `update --apply`, and the Homebrew cask. The daemon side does not depend on which installer ran.
- #7728 (installer: unload both LaunchAgents before the swap) is complementary. It stops the respawn on the install-script path. This PR recovers any daemon that still ends up on a stale image, including after a cask reinstall, which never runs our installer.
- Linux and Windows are unchanged. TCC attribution is macOS-only, and Windows locks a running executable against replacement.
- Embedded daemons are unchanged, because the host owns their lifetime.

## Tradeoffs

- `proc_pidpath` was considered and rejected: on this macOS it still returned the original path after the file was deleted, so it misses the brew case. Mapped-vnode identity catches both a rename and a delete.
- A daemon run from a build directory will also exit when the binary is rebuilt. That is the same "binary replaced" condition, and clients relaunch the daemon on demand.

## Blast Radius

Only macOS standalone daemons whose executable changes on disk are affected, and for them exiting is the intended behavior. If the region lookup or the `stat` fails for any reason other than a missing file, the check reports "not replaced", so the daemon keeps running as it does today.

## Verification

- New unit tests cover the judgment for an unchanged file, a file swapped in over the path, a deleted image, and a missing path.
- `the_running_process_sees_its_executable_swapped` copies the test binary, runs the copy, renames a new file over its path the way the installer swaps the bundle, and asserts that the running copy reports `before=false after=true`. Before writing the module, I checked the same rename and delete cases against the kernel API with a standalone probe.
- The scoped repository checks (quick stage: rustfmt, SPDX headers) pass. Build, clippy, and the macOS unit tests are left to CI and the verifier.

Fixes #7461
Refs #7728

title: feat(cua-driver): download installer release assets from a mirror
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: users in mainland China report Cua Driver on Windows as too slow to be usable (#5084). The one China-specific cost in our own code path is the installer: `install.ps1` and `_install-rust.sh` download every release asset from `github.com/trycua/cua/releases/download`, which is slow or unreachable from there, and `cua-driver update --apply` goes through the same path. There was no way to point the installers at a mirror.
- What changed:
  - `CUA_DRIVER_RS_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL` replaces the GitHub Releases download base in both Cua Driver installers. The archive, `SHA256SUMS`/`checksums.txt` and the Sigstore bundles are all fetched as `<url>/<tag>/<asset>`, and a trailing slash is ignored. Unset, nothing changes.
  - The checksum, Sigstore and (on Windows) Authenticode checks run unchanged against what the mirror serves.
  - The operate guide documents the variable for both platforms, and notes that `update --apply` inherits it.

## Related work

Fixes #5084

RFC: not required. This adds an optional installer environment variable and leaves the existing defaults unchanged.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: only for users who set the new variable. The default install and update path is byte-for-byte the same URL as before.
- Risk and rollback: a mirror is trusted to serve the right files, but cannot get past the integrity checks the installer already runs (SHA256SUMS, cosign-verified Sigstore bundles when cosign is present or `-RequireSignature`/`--require-signature` is set, and the Authenticode check on Windows). Release resolution still uses the baked version, and falls back to the GitHub API only when the baked asset is missing. Revert is a single commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_install_version_fallback.py`: new Unix tests for the default GitHub URL and for the mirror on both the archive and `SHA256SUMS` fetch; new Windows tests for the default and mirror base; the existing Windows retry/classification test now downloads through the mirror override and asserts the exact requested path. Mutation-checked: reverting the Unix archive URL to the hard-coded GitHub base fails the mirror test.
  - The installer contract tests in `.github/scripts/tests` that pinned the old URL text now pin the new download base, and the PowerShell integrity harness loads `$ReleaseDownloadBase`.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): refuse a rootless Xwayland desktop instead of streaming black
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on a GNOME 50 Wayland host, cua-spacesd's X11 backend captures the session's Xwayland `:0`. That server is rootless, so its root window holds no desktop pixels. The XShm grab cua-spacesd uses still succeeds there and returns black frames. The Space showed a black desktop, and nothing reported an error.
- What changed: before a display stream or display screenshot starts, cua-spacesd reads one pixel of the root with a core `GetImage`. A rootless Xwayland refuses that read with BadMatch. Xvfb, Xorg and a rootful Xwayland allow it. When the read is refused, the capture fails with `Unsupported` and a message telling the user to stream an X11 window or point cua-spacesd at an X11 session. An ignored live test checks the refusal, and the Linux leg of `CI: cua-spacesd` runs it against a rootless Xwayland in a headless sway.

## Related work

Fixes #5236

The issue offered two acceptable outcomes: show the GNOME desktop, or report that capture is unsupported. This PR does the second. Native GNOME capture through the ScreenCast portal or Mutter's ScreenCast D-Bus API would be a separate feature.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: on a rootless Xwayland (GNOME, KDE or sway without a Hyprland signature), opening the desktop now fails with an explanation and no longer streams black. Streaming X11 windows works as before. Hyprland still uses its own screencopy backend and never runs this check.
- Risk and rollback: an X server that refuses a root read on a healthy desktop would lose desktop streaming. Xvfb, Xorg and rootful Xwayland were checked and allow the read. Reverting the fix commit rolls the change back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`, plus `cargo check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` for `cua-spacesd-desktop --tests`) pass. The new live test `linux_stream::tests::rootless_xwayland_desktop_is_refused_not_streamed_black` runs in CI. The first commit adds the test alone, so it fails at that commit and passes at the fix commit.
- Manual evidence: on a rootless Xwayland in a headless sway, `xwd -root` fails with BadMatch on `X_GetImage`, and an `ffmpeg -f x11grab` (XShm) grab of the same root succeeds and returns black, as the issue reports for GNOME. A standalone build of the probe returned "unreadable" on that rootless Xwayland. It returned "readable" on Xvfb and on a rootful `Xwayland :77 -geometry 640x480`.
- Known gaps: no GNOME 50 host was available, so the refusal on Mutter's Xwayland is inferred from the shared Xwayland root behavior and the reporter's ffmpeg evidence. The live test was not run locally; CI runs it.

title: fix(cua-driver): confirm dom_event browser clicks from the page changes their handlers cause
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: a `browser_click` with `input_route: "dom_event"` checked only the clicked element's own state (aria attributes, `checked`, `value`, text). A button that reveals fields somewhere else, like the "Enter address manually" button in #5253, keeps its own state, so the click came back `unverifiable` even when it worked, and the agent had to take a new snapshot to find out.
- What changed: the synthetic click is still one `Runtime.callFunctionOn`, now awaited, and it yields a task (a `MessageChannel` message, which background-tab timer throttling does not delay) between its hover, press and release phases. Every phase dispatches at the point and on the descendant hit-tested first, so a handler that re-renders between phases cannot move the click onto another node. The microtask checkpoint before each yield runs every microtask the previous phase's handlers queued, so hover and focus handlers, however deep their promise chains, settle outside the counts. The press phase sends `pointerdown` and `mousedown` and counts the page mutations their handlers made, then focus moves; the release phase sends `pointerup`, `mouseup` and `click` and counts theirs. Each count watches the node's document (and its shadow root) with a `MutationObserver` and counts mutations on nodes still in the page, outside the target's subtree, until the microtasks its handlers queued have run. No other task can run in that window, so every mutation it counts comes from the click's own handlers. Attribute changes on the target's ancestors (focus-intent classes on `<html>` and similar) are left out, following shadow roots out to their hosts; the ancestors and root are read as each counted phase starts. When the total is above zero, the click is `confirmed`, with evidence that its handlers changed the page outside the target. A sequence that threw counts nothing. Otherwise the existing target-state readback runs as before. A dialog a handler opens pauses the call, and the rest of the sequence runs once it is dismissed, as on main.
- Each count waits a bounded 256 microtask turns, not for a later task, so unrelated timers and network callbacks never land in the count. A handler whose change comes later than that leaves the click `unverifiable`, as before this PR, never falsely `confirmed`.
- Tests: a fake-CDP unit test for the new confirmation, and the desktop browser E2E cases updated. `dom_event` clicks on the fixture's `Increment` button, whose handler writes the counter label next to it, now expect `confirmed`. In the frame case, the shadow-DOM and out-of-process-iframe buttons expect `confirmed`, and the same-process iframe button stays `unverifiable`, because its handler writes only to the parent document. The trust-gated fixture now records an ignored untrusted click in a later task, as an app that ignores the click leaves the page alone, and adds a hover handler that changes the page after a 50-step promise chain. That click must stay `unverifiable`. The same fixture adds a shadow-DOM button whose focus styles its host and `<body>` and shows a hint beside it, with no click handler. Its `dom_event` click must also stay `unverifiable`.

The other two asks in #5253 are already on main:
- Standalone Chrome on macOS takes background trusted clicks since #5110: `standalone_trusted_input_background_limitation` returns `None` there. Linux Chromium still refuses, and the refusal names its limitation.
- `delivery_mode` is in the `browser_click` schema, so the `delivery_mode="foreground"` the refusal suggests is a real parameter.

## Related work

Fixes #5253

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: more `dom_event` clicks report `effect: confirmed` instead of `unverifiable`. The JSON schema is unchanged; the `input_route` description now says when the effect is confirmed, and the generated reference docs and CLI specs carry the new wording. The change is in the shared crate, so it applies the same way on macOS, Windows and Linux.
- Risk and rollback: a handler that changes the page outside the target without doing what the agent wanted (a ripple appended to `<body>`, analytics markup) now reads as `confirmed`. This applies only to the opt-in synthetic route, and the mutations still have to come from that click's own handlers. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new `dom_event_click_confirms_when_its_handlers_change_the_page` in `v2_tests.rs` (the test is the first commit, the fix the second). It also checks that the click is sent with `awaitPromise` and `returnByValue`. `dom_event_click_counts_no_page_change_when_its_sequence_throws` covers a sequence that threw. The existing `dom_event_click_remains_unverifiable_when_only_focus_changes` covers a click that reports zero page mutations. Formatting, SPDX and docs checks from the scoped repository checks pass.
- Manual or platform evidence: drove both CDP calls against headless Chromium on Linux with `Runtime.callFunctionOn`. A click handler that unhides a sibling counts 1 mutation. A button with no handler counts 0. A `mouseenter` handler that appends to `<body>` counts 0, directly or after a 50-step promise chain. A click handler whose change comes after a 50-step promise chain counts 1. With a page timer rewriting an unrelated element every tick, a button with no handler still counts 0. The trust-gated fixture counts 0 and still records `activation=ignored-untrusted` afterwards. A same-process iframe button writing to its parent counts 0. With the single-call sequence and task yields, in headless Chromium on Linux: a click handler that unhides a sibling counts 1; no handler counts 0; a `mouseenter` handler that appends to `<body>` after a 50-step promise chain counts 0; a focus handler writing a sibling after a 400-step chain counts 0; a `mousedown` handler writing a sibling counts 1; with `pointerdown` prevented, `mousedown` is not sent and a click handler's write counts 1; a page timer rewriting an unrelated element leaves a button with no handler at 0; a click handler whose change comes after a 50-step chain counts 1; focus classes on `<html>`, `<body>` and a wrapper count 0; a shadow-DOM button whose click writes a sibling counts 1; the trust-gated fixture counts 0 and still records `ignored-untrusted`; a click handler that changes an icon inside the button and then removes it counts 0; an `alert()` in `mouseenter` pauses the call, and after it is dismissed the click still runs. A hover handler that wraps the button leaves a click that styles the wrapper at 0, and one that moves the button into a shadow root lets a click writing beside it there count 1.
- Known gaps or CI still required: unit tests, clippy and the generated-reference check did not run locally because the host is short on disk, so CI runs them. The cua-driver desktop E2E lanes, whose expectations this PR updates, did not run here.

title: feat(cua-driver): approve macOS permission prompts over Screen Sharing with `permissions vnc`
body:
## Why

Until Cua Driver has Accessibility and Screen Recording, it can't click or see, so it can't help grant them. On a Mac nobody is sitting at, setup stalls there. Input that arrives over Screen Sharing doesn't depend on Cua Driver's own grants. This PR builds that route into the driver, so the owner, or an agent they authorize, can approve the prompts remotely. The only other way was a documented vncdotool script.

## What changed

- `cua-driver permissions vnc shot <png> | click <x> <y> --label <text> | type-env <NAME>`: a small RFB client inside the driver. It authenticates with None, a VNC password, or Apple Remote Desktop (type 30, which macOS Screen Sharing offers for a macOS account). It reads credentials only from `CUA_VNC_USER` and `CUA_VNC_PASSWORD`, saves screenshots readable only by their owner (mode 0600 on Unix, an owner, SYSTEM and Administrators ACL on Windows), and appends every click and typed variable to an approval log (`$CUA_VNC_LOG`) before sending it. If the log can't be written, nothing is sent. It refuses degenerate ARD key-exchange parameters (an even prime, or a generator or server key of 0, 1 or p-1).
- When `permissions grant` times out with a switch still off, it now points to `permissions vnc`.
- The operator-authorized section of the skill's MACOS.md now uses the command in place of the vncdotool helper script. The CLI reference pages are regenerated.

## Scope

This covers the TCC grant flow only, as the issue's first use case asks. It answers the issue's open questions as follows:

- **Opt-in and consent:** the command only runs when someone invokes it. Nothing switches to VNC automatically, and it is not an MCP tool, because agent tool calls may not raise or answer OS permission prompts. The MACOS.md guardrails still apply: approve only prompts that name CuaDriver, and only with the owner's authorization for this task.
- **Credentials:** they come from environment variables only, never argv, and are zeroized after use. Nothing is stored. Keychain storage is left out.
- **Passwords:** the command never types anything on its own. `type-env` types only a variable the caller names explicitly, and the guide limits that to a disposable VM password the owner provided.
- **Local or remote:** both. The client is cross-platform, so a Linux or Windows machine can approve a remote Mac.
- **Detection and handback:** `permissions grant` points to the command when switches stay off. Once `permissions status` reports both grants, the driver uses its native input and capture; VNC plays no further part.

Left out: a general VNC backend for other tools, Keychain-stored credentials, and the newer Screen Sharing security types 33, 35 and 36 (SRP and RSA). macOS still offers type 30 alongside them.

## Tradeoffs

- **Own RFB client vs. vnc-rs (used by cua-vmm):** vnc-rs rejects the whole offer list when it contains a type it doesn't know, so it can't connect to macOS Screen Sharing, which offers `[30, 33, 36, 35]`.
- **Raw encoding plus DesktopSize:** the client requests DesktopSize because Apple's Virtualization-framework VNC server (Lume VMs) stopped the VM when a client requested Raw alone. This happened during testing, and the log said so.

## Blast Radius

This adds a new subcommand and four small RustCrypto/num dependencies (`des` is new to the lockfile; `aes`, `md-5` and `num-bigint` were already in it). Existing commands only gain the new hint line in `permissions grant`. The command can click and type on a remote screen, so its safety rests on the credential handling above and on the MACOS.md guardrails. RFB encrypts only the ARD credential block, not the session, so screenshots and typed text cross the network in the clear; the usage text and MACOS.md say to use an SSH tunnel or a trusted network for a remote Mac, and never to use `type-env` over an untrusted one. Telemetry records the operation only as `vnc`, never the arguments.

## Verification

- Unit tests (fake RFB server on loopback), run in CI: the DES and ARD responses match vectors computed independently with Python's `cryptography` using vncdotool's algorithm; the server-side ARD decrypt recovers the credentials; there are exact-error tests for a missing user, a refused password and degenerate DH parameters, and an approval-log test for an unwritable path and owner-only appends; and the screenshot, resize, click and typing tests check the bytes on the wire. The CLI parse, option-check and telemetry-operation tests are extended.
- Live, against a Lume macOS 26.5 VM: `shot` over the VM display (type 2) saved a correct 1024x768 PNG, and the VM stayed up. Against Apple Screen Sharing inside the VM (type 30, account auth), authentication succeeded. Against this host's macOS 26.6 Screen Sharing over loopback, the type-30 key exchange ran end to end and returned the server's refusal reason for wrong credentials, and a missing `CUA_VNC_USER` gave the expected hint.
- Not yet run: in the VM, Apple Screen Sharing returned a black frame and typed text did not arrive. That looks like a limit of Screen Sharing in a Virtualization-framework guest, but this is unproven. So the full grant flow over type 30 on real Mac hardware is still unverified. The full driver build, clippy, tests and the generated-reference check run in CI, not locally (this is a shared host). The Windows ACL path is exercised only by the Windows CI lanes. The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) passed.

Fixes #7522

title: fix(cua-driver): aim element scroll at the part inside the window
body:
Salvaged from #5365

Fixes #5281

## Why

On macOS, `scroll` with an element token posts the wheel at the centre of the element's whole AX frame. When the element is taller or wider than its window, as a long text view or web area usually is, that centre lies outside the window, so background delivery is refused with the outside-window error. @S3yon's change aims the wheel at the centre of the element's part inside the window instead.

## What changed

- @S3yon's commit, kept as authored: the element path takes the centre of the element frame intersected with the window bounds, using the existing `intersect` helper in `ax/reveal_scroll.rs` (now `pub(crate)`).
- On top of it: the fallback comes from the same AX rect instead of a second `AXPosition`/`AXSize` read through `element_screen_center`. `element_wheel_point` now returns the whole-element centre when the window is unknown or they don't overlap, so those two cases are unit-tested as well.

## Scope

Only the macOS element-token wheel path in `tools/scroll.rs`. Pixel-targeted scroll, the AX scroll-bar path and the keyboard fallback are unchanged. Windows scrolls element tokens through UIA ScrollPattern, and most Linux targets go through AT-SPI, so neither posts a wheel there. The exception is WebKitGTK on native Wayland: it posts a compositor wheel at the element's AT-SPI centre (`resolve_element_local_coords`), so a web view taller than its window can hit the same problem. This PR leaves that Linux path alone; it is a separate follow-up.

## Blast Radius

An element that fits inside its window gets the same point as before. When the element and the window don't overlap, the point is the old centre, so the existing outside-window refusal still applies. The Electron reveal path takes the same point as its hit-test location, and it now lands inside the window for large elements too.

## Verification

- Unit tests for `element_wheel_point`: element inside the window, taller than the window, partly above it, outside it, and no window bounds.
- The scoped repository checks (formatting, SPDX headers) pass. The macOS unit and clippy lanes run in CI.

- [x] `bin/ci --quick` passed and signed off on the head, after merging main

title: fix(cua-spacesd): send desktop Super chords through the desktop scope
body:
## Why

From the Spaces viewer, Super chords never reached Hyprland on an Omarchy guest: Super+W showed up in the focused window as a plain `w`. On a display stream, cua-spacesd sent every key as a window-addressed foreground `press_key`. On Hyprland, that call goes through the input plugin's foreground key path, which writes `wl_keyboard` events straight to the client. Hyprland's key bindings never see them. `cua do hotkey super+return` worked because it uses the desktop scope, where the virtual keyboard goes through the compositor.

## What changed

- `ToolInputLease::keyboard_base` now takes the key's modifiers. On a display target, a chord that includes Super (`Modifier::Command`) goes to `scope: desktop`. All other keys and text still go to the focused window in the foreground.
- New regression test `desktop_super_chords_reach_the_compositor_through_the_desktop_scope`. It sends Super+W and Super+Shift+W and expects the desktop scope. It sends Ctrl+W and expects the focused window. The test landed one commit before the fix.

## Scope

This covers Spaces display streams that route input through cua-driver tools. On Linux that is Hyprland. Window streams are unchanged. Windows display leases already send every key to the desktop scope, so nothing changes there. macOS does not use this adapter. Out of scope: the host-side keyboard shortcut inhibitor the issue mentions for niri hosts, which is a viewer change, and the macOS viewer's Super handling (#5345).

## Tradeoffs

Only Super chords move. Moving every display key to the desktop scope would also fix Ctrl+Alt bindings, but it would take ordinary typing off the plugin's verified focused-window route. A Super chord is aimed at the compositor in practice, so that route is the one it needs.

## Blast Radius

This affects Hyprland Spaces viewers that press a Super chord. Those chords now reach the focused application through the compositor, the same as `cua do hotkey`, so an unbound Super chord still reaches the app with Super held, as it would from a physical keyboard. Nothing else changes.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks in quick mode passed: SPDX headers, rustfmt and image refs. The unit tests, clippy and the Windows cross-clippy lane were skipped locally because the shared host is low on disk, so they run in CI.
- The `cua-spacesd-desktop` unit tests will show the new test failing at the test commit and passing at the fix.
- No live Omarchy guest check ran. The desktop-scope Super route is the one the issue reports working with `cua do hotkey super+return`.

Fixes #5344

title: fix(cua-driver): capture ext-listed Wayland windows by their toplevel
body:
## Why

On a wlroots compositor with no adapter of its own, such as Umbriel, `get_window_state` refused every window screenshot with `surface_identity_unproven: ... no compositor-attested window geometry is available`, even though the compositor offers `ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1`. The window ids came from wlr-foreign-toplevel handles, which can't name a capture source. Window capture had only one option: crop the output using Sway or GNOME geometry.

## What changed

- `list_windows` now uses `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` when the compositor advertises both the ext toplevel capture source manager and the copy manager. Each `window_id` then stands for the toplevel's stable ext `identifier`.
- For such a window, capture finds that identifier on a new connection and has the compositor copy the toplevel itself through `ext-image-copy-capture`. No output crop is involved, so covering windows and other workspaces never show up in it.
- In that listing, a window takes its pid and geometry from AT-SPI only when the title or app id is unique among the ext windows and among all AT-SPI windows, including ones already paired, because a guessed pid would pair this window's pixels with another app's accessibility tree. Otherwise pid and geometry stay unknown.
- Ext window ids now carry bit 48 (`1 << 48 | 0xF000_0000 + n`). AT-SPI window ids are `pid << 16 | ordinal`, below 2^48, so the old `0xF000_0000` ids were also the ids of real AT-SPI windows (pid 61440 and up), and capture could copy an unrelated toplevel for one. The low 32 bits keep a value no X server issues, for paths that truncate to u32.
- A refused copy is still the typed `surface_identity_unproven` error, and it now gives the cause (for example, a missing global or a closed toplevel). An ext session that stops before its frame is ready now fails at once instead of waiting out the timeout.

## Scope

This covers window listing and window-scoped capture on compositors that advertise the ext toplevel capture globals. The Sway session (attested by `SWAYSOCK`) keeps its IPC container ids and geometry crop, and cua-compositor (inject mode) keeps its own targets. Hyprland, niri, KWin and the GNOME helper are handled before this path and don't change.

Out of scope: ext-listed windows still take pid and geometry only from AT-SPI, as the existing ext fallback already did. A window AT-SPI doesn't know keeps `pid=?` and zero geometry, so window-local pixel input on it has nothing to translate against. Desktop-scope input is unaffected.

## Blast Radius

Linux Wayland sessions on compositors that advertise both `ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1` and `ext_image_copy_capture_manager_v1`, excluding Sway and cua-compositor: Umbriel, labwc on wlroots 0.19+ and similar. On those, window ids move from the wlr protocol-id space to the ext id namespace (`1 << 48 | 0xF000_0000` and up). The identity used for wlr activation is recorded for each listed window, so `bring_to_front` still finds the window by title and app id. Other compositors get the same listing as before, except that windows from the plain ext fallback listing move to the same new id range.

## Tradeoffs

Activating an ext-listed window (`bring_to_front`) still resolves the wlr handle by first title match, then first app-id match. This PR doesn't change that: on Umbriel, the wlr listing it replaces recorded the same title/app_id identity and resolved it through the same `matching_handle`. Two windows with the same title can still activate the wrong one, as before. Fixing that belongs in `matching_handle` for every wlr compositor, not here.

## Verification

- New unit tests in `platform-linux`: an ext-listed window returns the toplevel copy and never calls the crop or output capture; a refused copy fails closed with the exact typed error; ext window ids map back to their identifier; the capturable merge leaves a repeated title or app id unpaired, even when an earlier window already paired one of the repeats. Every issued ext id sits above the highest possible AT-SPI id. Disabling any of these guards fails a test. All `wayland::` lib tests pass. Disabling the new dispatch branch makes both dispatch tests fail.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -D warnings` and the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) are green. `bin/ci --signoff` was refused because quick mode skips the heavy checks, so those run in CI.
- Not run: a live capture on a compositor with the ext toplevel capture source. The available host has sway on wlroots 0.18, which doesn't implement that protocol.

Fixes #5327

title: fix(spaces): send the Mac clipboard on paste in the native viewer
body:
## Why

In the Cua Spaces macOS app, ⌘V in a Linux Space reached the guest as Control+V, but the Space's clipboard stayed empty, so nothing was pasted. The app's native viewer only sent key chords. Nothing in it moved the Mac's clipboard (the HTML5 viewer does). Separately, `cua spaces set <space> --clipboard …` failed for every Space with "only 'cua spaces ls' runs over the registry directly".

## What changed

- On ⌘V or ⌘⇧V in a focused native viewer, `LiveStreamSession.paste` first puts the Mac's clipboard text on the Space, empty text when the Mac's clipboard holds none, so a paste never inserts what the Space copied before (`ComputerService.SetClipboard` through the Space's own cua-spacesd connection, so relay, direct and mesh Spaces all use it), then sends the chord. It does this only when the Space's clipboard setting is `viewing` (the default). The setting is read from the Space's record on each paste (`Space.clipboardSetting()`), because a stream handle's info is a connection-time snapshot and a warm session can outlive a change made in Settings or with `cua spaces set`. Keys typed in the meantime queue behind the chord, and so does another paste, which keeps its own text. If a transfer fails or takes more than 2 s, the keys go anyway. A late transfer cannot be recalled (the bindings do not pass cancellation through), so when one lands after a newer one, the newest text is sent again as a transfer of its own. The Space ends up with the last paste's text however late any transfer lands. Stopping the stream or switching its source drops anything still held.
- `SpacesCmd::runs_through_sdk` decides which `cua spaces` commands go through the SDK handle. It has no wildcard arm, so any new command has to choose a route. `set` and `rename` had no route after the Secure Spaces gate was removed, and both now go through the SDK again.

## Scope

Covers text paste from the Mac to the Space in the macOS app's native viewer (the main window and the web-hosted viewer surfaces), plus CLI routing for `cua spaces set` and `cua spaces rename`. Not covered:
- copy from the Space back to the Mac;
- file clipboards;
- the `ask` setting, which needs a prompt this viewer does not have yet, so it sends nothing, as `off` does;
- the Windows/Linux Electron viewer.

## Tradeoffs

The clipboard goes right before the paste, not through a background sync loop. That matches the `viewing` contract ("paste sends this computer's clipboard once"), and the Space never sees clipboard contents the user did not paste.

## Blast Radius

Only paste chords in an interactive native viewer change. `SpaceStreamSourceProviding.sendClipboard` has a default that sends nothing, so other providers and test fakes behave as before. The CLI change only affects `set` and `rename`, which errored before.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-cli --lib only_ls_and_default_skip_the_sdk`: failed on `["set", "local:studio", "--clipboard", "viewing"]` before the fix, passes after.
- `libs/spaces-app-swift/scripts/test.sh`: 73/73 passed before the empty-clipboard fix, which adds `anEmptyClipboardStillGoesBeforeTheChord`; this host cannot link the suite (no Rust toolchain for `cua_sdk`), so CI's Swift lane runs it at the current head. In mutation checks, `pasteSendsTheClipboardBeforeTheChord` fails when `paste` skips the transfer, and `pastesQueueWithTheirOwnTextAndAStopDropsThem` fails when a queued paste loses its text, a stop keeps held input, or a late transfer or a late repair is not followed by the newest text.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): rustfmt, SPDX headers and image refs pass. Clippy, the full cua-cli unit tests, and the binding and reference drift checks are left to CI.

- `CuaBackedTests` (spaces-sdk-swift, against the fixtures in CI): after the stream handle is cached, setting `off` through `Spaces.setClipboard` shows as `off` in `clipboardSetting()` while the handle's info still has the old value.

Not run: a live paste into a Linux VM Space behind a self-hosted relay.

Fixes #7589

title: feat(cua-driver): add agent_display, a session-owned virtual display on macOS
body:
## Why

Background input keeps the user's frontmost app and pointer, but app windows still open on the user's screen. `agent_display` gives an agent its own virtual display on macOS. The agent moves windows onto it with `set_window_frame`, and the display goes away when the agent's session ends.

## What changed

- New macOS tool `agent_display` with actions `create` (width, height, name), `list` and `remove`. `create` makes a `CGVirtualDisplay` in the daemon and returns `display_id`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`.
- The calling session owns the display. A session-end hook removes it on `end_session` or the idle timeout, and the daemon releases it when it exits. Ownership is recorded in the same blocking task that creates the display, so a cancelled caller still leaves it owned. If the session ends during a create, even if the same id is revived before the create finishes, the display is removed and `create` returns an error.
- `CGVirtualDisplay*` are private CoreGraphics classes. Before messaging them, the tool checks that every class and selector it uses exists. On a macOS build that renamed or dropped one, it returns an error instead of raising an Objective-C exception. Each display gets a serial that is never reused while the daemon runs.
- The MCP client compatibility roster (`expected-tools.json` and its release wiring test) expects `agent_display` on macOS.
- The MCP reference lists `agent_display` under the screen tools as macOS only, and the macOS skill explains how to use it and that Linux and Windows do not register it.

## Scope

This covers macOS only. Linux and Windows do not register the tool. Recording a chosen display (the fork's `display_recording`, mentioned on the issue) is left for a follow-up.

## Tradeoffs

- The guard checks for the classes and selectors rather than a macOS version number. A version check would let a release that changes the private API crash the daemon, and would block a release that still works.
- Screenshots of a virtual display are 1:1 pixels, not Retina. When a display is removed, macOS moves its windows back to the main screen.

## Blast Radius

Only callers of `agent_display` are affected. Other tools change only through two table entries: the cursor semantics classification (`App`) and the `display.virtual` capability. The private classes are touched only when `create` runs.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `platform-macos` unit tests for the size limits, the class and selector guard, a host test that every private class and selector the guard lists exists on this macOS, and session ownership, including a caller cancelled mid-create and a session that ends, or ends and is revived, mid-create. Also the `.github/scripts` tests, the `cua-driver-core` and `cua-driver-contract` unit tests, the contract `--check`, the cua-driver docs generator `--check`, and `bin/ci --quick`.
- Mutation checks: misspelling one guarded selector fails the host test; ignoring a session end during a create fails both end tests.
- Not run here: the full `bin/ci` (the host is short on disk) and the docs policy test that needs a release binary, and a live run that creates a real display on this shared desktop. CI runs the first two.

Fixes #7597

Adapted from @nqh-packages' fork commit nqh-packages/cua@a5ddd1167, which is kept with its original author.
