title: fix(cua-driver): serve the main queue when the overlay is off
body:
## Why

On macOS, `launch_app` for Finder with a folder URL hands the folder to Finder on the main dispatch queue and waits up to 5 s. A daemon started with `serve --no-overlay` never served that queue: its main thread only joined the serve thread. Every such call failed with `Timed out waiting for Finder folder handoff on the AppKit main queue`.

## What changed

- New `platform_macos::cursor::overlay::serve_main_queue()` runs `CFRunLoopRun` on the main thread. That serves the main queue on the real main thread without creating an `NSApplication`, so there is still no Dock icon and no Window Server registration.
- `serve` calls it when the overlay is off. The serve thread already exits the process when it ends, so the join is no longer needed there. It now also exits the process (status 1) when it panics, since the main thread no longer returns after a failed join. The overlay-less branches of `run_on_main_thread` (no `init`, overlay disabled, headless per #1724) also call it instead of parking.
- Tests: an ignored e2e case in `installed_app_launch_macos_test.rs` opens a temp folder in Finder through a dedicated `--no-overlay` instance of the installed app, which keeps its Screen Recording grant for the lane's required video (the canonical macOS lane runs that whole binary with `--ignored`). That daemon helper moved from `perception_capture_loop_test.rs` into the testkit as `InstalledMacosDaemon`, and both tests use it. A hermetic `harness = false` test, `main_queue_without_overlay`, checks that work sent to the main queue runs on the main thread while it sits in `serve_main_queue`. The macOS Rust CI job now runs it as its own step, since that job runs only `platform-macos --lib`.

## Scope

macOS daemon startup only. The overlay-on path (`run_appkit`) is unchanged. Windows and Linux are untouched.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS `serve --no-overlay` daemon, including embedded hosts that default to no overlay, and the headless path from #1724. The main thread now idles in a CF run loop instead of `park`/`join`; it does no work until something is dispatched to it. With no graphic session, main-queue work now runs and returns its own error instead of timing out.

## Verification

- Reproduced on the release binary 0.44.0: `serve --no-overlay`, then `launch_app {"bundle_id":"com.apple.finder","urls":["<folder>"]}` returned `LAUNCH_FAILED` after 5.16 s.
- The scoped repository checks in quick mode passed (rustfmt, lockfiles, SPDX headers), and the e2e inventory check passed. Build, clippy, unit tests and the macOS e2e lane were not run locally; they run in CI.

Fixes #7613

title: fix(cua-driver): invoke a menu for a window behind the user's window without raising it on macOS
body:
Salvaged from #5380

Refs #3780
Refs #4955

## Why

On macOS, `invoke_menu` on a window of the frontmost app that is not its key window raises and focuses that window, then opens the menu on screen. The user is working in that app, so their window loses key and their typing can land in the menu or in the raised window. Since #7761, the user's window also stays behind after the call. @skap3214's fix in #5380 makes the target key through the in-app key-window record (no raise, no activation), presses the item through the background route, and hands key back. This PR carries their commits onto current main. The design, the route rules and the tests are theirs.

## What changed

- @skap3214's commits are kept as authored. A merge of main resolves the conflicts with the menu work that landed since: the off-Space background route (#7756), the kept key window after a dispatched foreground command (#7761), the cancellable press worker (#6953, #7039), the automation-consent refusal and the sheet-aware focused-window id.
- `menu_route` now also takes the window's Space: an off-Space window takes the background route first, and the PR's routes apply to windows on the current Space. The key-window check uses `AxWindowId::is`, so a sheet on the target counts as the target being key.
- One `PressHold` (the pid's mutation lease, plus the key scope on the behind-window route) goes into main's press worker in place of the PR's `with_held_lease` reentrancy. Key goes back before the lease is released, and only after both the call (including the Save readback) and the worker have finished. Every blocking worker that changes key (the key-scope setup, the press, and the old foreground raise, press and restore) owns the lease until it returns, so a cancelled call can't release it while key is still moving.
- When `enter_exact_window_key` posts the key-window records or sets `AXFocusedWindow` and then can't confirm the target, it now hands key back before it refuses. Before, the refusal left the user's key window moved. Every caller of the no-raise key scope gets the same restore.

## Scope

The macOS `invoke_menu` routes for a frontmost app, plus the `invoke_menu` disabled-item recovery hint and `MACOS.md`. `hotkey`'s menu route keeps the same behavior through `run_in_background`. The background-app and off-Space routes are unchanged. Linux and Windows are not touched.

## Tradeoffs

A menu command that AppKit runs after the press returns would run after key went back to the user's window. Save is covered, because key stays on the target through the 2 s on-disk readback. Other deferred commands are not. `hotkey`'s background menu route on main already hands key back the same way, so this is not new; it is listed as a follow-up.

## Blast Radius

macOS callers that run `invoke_menu` on a non-key window of the app in front. That call now presses without raising, or is refused with `window_not_key` (escalation `bring_to_front`) when the target cannot be confirmed key. `invoke_menu` now holds the pid's mutation lease for the whole call, so same-pid background actions wait for it.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks that run on Linux: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passed on the merged head and on the fix. Clippy, the `platform-macos` unit tests and the cross-target builds run in CI.
- Not run: a live macOS run of `invoke_menu` on a second window of a frontmost TextEdit, checking that the user's window keeps key and order and that the command lands in the target.

title: fix(cua-driver): encode the macOS desktop screenshot once and keep its display filter
body:
Salvaged from #7640

Refs #6881

## Why

Since #7549, `get_desktop_state` on macOS builds a ScreenCaptureKit display filter on every call, and that needs the shareable-content query. It also encodes the frame as PNG, decodes it, resizes it and encodes it again. @abonneth's two commits remove both costs. Their commits are kept as authored. One small commit of ours sits on top.

## What changed

- The desktop capture passes raw RGBA pixels to `CapturedImage::encode`, so a capped screenshot is resized and then encoded once, the way `get_window_state` already works.
- The display filter and its stream configuration are kept between captures (`capture_with_kept_plan`). They are rebuilt when the main display id, its bounds, its pixel size or the excluded overlay window changes, and once more when a capture with the kept filter fails.
- Ours: removes the old `cgimage_to_png` doc line that the first commit left above `cgimage_to_rgba`, and moves the new test below the tests module's imports.

## Scope

macOS `get_desktop_state` only. Window capture, the `screencapture` fallback, Windows and Linux are unchanged. No tool, schema or permission change.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS desktop screenshot goes through this path. A display filter lists the windows to leave out, not the ones to show, so windows that open, move or close after the filter was built still appear correctly. Changes to the display are caught by the identity check before each capture. Any other stale filter costs one failed capture and a rebuild within the same call. The kept state is one `SCContentFilter` and one `SCStreamConfiguration`, and no frames or surfaces.

## Verification

- `a_capture_plan_is_kept_until_it_is_stale_or_its_capture_fails` covers the rules for keeping, replacing and retrying the filter. The existing `image_utils` tests check that `encode` produces the same bytes as the old two-step path.
- The scoped repository checks pass (`bin/ci --quick`).
- #7640 has the contributor's end-to-end evidence: identical PNG bytes compared with #7549, and windows opened after the filter was built showing up in later screenshots.

title: fix(cua-driver): press a background web menu button on macOS instead of refusing it as a <select>
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a background `click` on a web menu button (`<button aria-haspopup="menu">`, such as a Radix `DropdownMenu.Trigger`) in Chrome or an Electron app was refused with `select_menu_would_raise_window`, as if it were a `<select>`. Its menu is drawn in the page, so pressing it raises no window, and `set_value` (the suggested route) does not apply to a menu of commands.
- What changed: Chromium gives both elements the role `AXPopUpButton`. The `<select>` guard now also requires what only a `<select>` has: its options as `AXMenuItem` (or `AXMenu`) children, or a selected option as its `AXValue`. A menu button has no children and an empty value, so it is pressed in the background like any other button. If the value, the children, or any child's role cannot be read, the control counts as a `<select>` and the press is refused. Both the element-token path and the pixel path use the same check. The `click` tool description, the generated MCP reference and the macOS skill note say so.

## Related work

Fixes #7664

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. A background click on a web menu button now opens its in-page menu instead of returning `select_menu_would_raise_window`. A `<select>` is still refused the same way.
- Risk and rollback: a `<select>` with no options and no value would no longer be refused. Revert the PR to restore the old guard.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: a new unit test, `a_chromium_select_is_told_apart_from_a_web_menu_button`, covers the classifier with the attribute shapes the issue reports for each element, plus the unreadable-value, unreadable-children and unreadable-role cases. The scoped repository checks that ran here: rustfmt and SPDX headers. Clippy, unit tests, the generated-reference check and the Windows cross-check were skipped for low disk and are left to CI.
- Manual or platform evidence: on live Chrome (macOS), the issue's repro page reads `AXPopUpButton "Real select" = "One"` and `AXPopUpButton "Menu button"` with no value, the attribute the classifier keys on. The options-as-children half rests on the issue's Electron reading. A background click through this build's guard was not driven: that needs a local build, which this shared host leaves to CI.
- CI: left to the head's run (macOS unit tests, clippy, reference drift checks); main was merged in again before this round.

title: fix(cua-driver): isolate semantic AX lookups by renderer target
body:
Salvaged from #5387

Fixes #5381

## Why

`get_browser_state` can loop forever in `SemanticDocument::page` when an out-of-process iframe reuses AX node IDs from the page. Subtree, ancestor and outline lookups used one AX-ID map across every merged frame, so a parent ID in one target could resolve to a node in another, including a cycle. The outline depth walk had no cycle guard.

## What changed

- Subtree and ancestor lookups key on (OOPIF target id, AX node id). Same-process iframes share the page's namespace, so a container still reaches iframe content in the same renderer.
- `render_outline` stops its parent walk when it revisits a node.
- A `scope_ref` carries its ref's OOPIF target id with its backend DOM id (`SemanticScope`), on the first page and in continuations, so the scope root resolves in its own renderer when backend ids collide across targets.
- Tests: colliding IDs across targets, a dangling ignored parent, a cross-target cycle, self and two-node cycles in one frame, a scoped container over same-process iframe content, and an OOPIF scope root whose backend id collides with the page's.

## Scope

Shared browser core only (`browser/semantic.rs`, plus the scope plumbing in `browser/engine.rs` and `browser/store.rs`). Raw AX IDs, backend DOM IDs, action refs and response fields are unchanged. Async worker cancellation and ignored-node flattening are untouched.

The branch also renews the `handover_process::the_next_relay_waits_then_serves_what_queued` flaky quarantine entry (CUA-3855) for 7 days, as #7887 did. It expired on 2026-11-22, so the flaky quarantine check fails on every PR into main. The flake still needs its own fix.

This carries @Iflaqbhat's two commits from #5387 unchanged, rebased onto main and since updated by merging main. #5387's branch could not be updated by maintainers and its CI never started at its old base, so it moves here to run CI. Thanks @Iflaqbhat for the fix and @jacklau04 for the reproduction in #5381.

## Blast Radius

Every `get_browser_state` semantic snapshot goes through these lookups. If a target key were wrong, subtree membership or outline indentation would be wrong. That cannot hang or crash. The engine sets `oopif_target_id` on every frame it reads from a child target and leaves it unset for the tab's own frames, which is the split the key needs.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (quick stage: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) pass on this branch.
- On #5387, the author ran the new same-process iframe test, which fails before the second commit and passes after it, and the full `cua-driver-core` unit suite, which passes. A native Chrome OOPIF reproduction has not run.

title: fix(cua-driver): escape control characters in macOS tree row metadata
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `get_window_state` wrote accessibility action names, `help` and `id` into the Markdown tree as they were. PowerPoint's Copilot button has a custom action whose name holds two newlines, so its row split over three lines and the rows after it read as that button's children. A `query` read also returned the stray `selector:(null)]]` fragment as a row of its own.
- What changed: `format_node_line` escapes control characters (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\u{1}`) in action names, `help` and `id`, so each element stays on one row. A unit test pins the row for a button shaped like the Copilot one.

## Related work

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS `get_window_state` Markdown only. Rows whose metadata holds a control character now show it as an escape; every other row is byte-identical. The structured `elements` keep the raw strings, so callers that act on an action name are unchanged. Titles, values and descriptions are written as before. Windows and Linux rows are untouched, since neither writes app-supplied action names into the row.

title: fix(cua-driver): rank macOS list_windows z_index by live stacking
body:
Salvaged from #5395

Fixes #3471

## Why

On macOS, `list_windows` numbered `z_index` by position in the all-windows CGWindowList array. That order does not follow a raise and puts off-screen windows ahead of on-screen ones, so "take the maximum `z_index`" could pick an off-screen or occluded window. @S3yon's change ranks windows by one on-screen-only pass instead, matched by `window_id`, and reports `null` for off-screen windows.

## What changed

- @S3yon's commits, kept as authored: `WindowInfo.z_index` is `Option<usize>`. All-windows enumerations take their order from the live on-screen list. Off-screen windows get `null`. `normalize_z_indices` renumbers only the non-null values to contiguous 0..n-1.
- Main merged in.
- Our commit: the macOS-only `cua-spacesd-desktop` test fixture builds `WindowInfo` with `z_index: Some(0)`. On #5395's head it failed to compile in macOS CI (`expected Option<usize>, found integer`).

## Scope

macOS only. The `list_windows` contract already allows `"z_index": ["integer","null"]`, so the schema, Windows and Linux are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Callers that pick a window by maximum `z_index` either filter to on-screen windows or read an on-screen list, and `None` sorts below any `Some`, so they keep picking the front on-screen window. One behavior change: in `browser_js.rs`, Chromium windows with identical bounds are now ordered with on-screen windows first. All-windows enumerations make one extra `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` call.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (quick stage: formatting, SPDX headers, image refs) pass on this head.
- PR CI at 4ebcfacc01 is green, including `ci-gate`. That covers the macOS Rust build and unit tests for `platform-macos` and `cua-spacesd-desktop`, where the three contract tests (`z_index_follows_on_screen_order_when_all_windows_order_disagrees`, `app_with_no_on_screen_windows_has_no_z_index`, `off_screen_window_record_has_null_z_index`) ran and passed, and the hosted macOS, Windows and Linux E2E lanes.
- Not run: local cargo checks and the Lume macOS E2E lane on the dev host. cargo isn't installed there, and the host didn't have enough free disk.

title: fix(cua-driver): send a background pixel click past an element without AXPress
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a background pixel click resolves the AX element under the point and presses it. When that element does not advertise `AXPress` (an Excel toolbar group, a Finder list cell), the app takes the press as a no-op, and the click still returned `ok` with "PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX". Agents could not tell a click that did nothing from one that landed. This was problem 2 of #7086. Only LibreOffice VCL and GTK 3 targets already fell through.
- What changed: the hit-test now acts only on an element that advertises `AXPress`, or for the internal focus action. On every toolkit, any other element falls through to the routed pixel click. That click reaches what is drawn at the point, or refuses with `background_unavailable` on a toolkit that cannot take it. The element-token path already treats a press the element does not advertise as hollow, so both paths now follow the same rule.

Problem 1 of #7086, the window-origin offset, was already fixed before this PR. The report was made on cua-driver 0.38.0. On macOS 27, WindowServer reads the `CGEventSetWindowLocation` stamp as the window-local point, and the driver stamped the screen point, so the origin was added twice. #5492 stamps the window-local point on macOS 27 and later, and it first shipped in `cua-driver-rs-v0.39.0`. The reporter's band of no-op clicks near the top of the window came from the same offset: correctly translated points landed on the ribbon and formula-bar groups, while the event path added the origin a second time.

## Related work

Fixes #7086

Refs #4864, #5492

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. A background left click by pixel whose hit-test lands on an element without `AXPress` now goes out as the routed pixel click, the same route used when the hit-test finds nothing. Its result reports that route instead of a false AX press. Elements that advertise `AXPress` (buttons, toolbar items, web controls Chromium marks clickable) are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: an app that does something on an `AXPress` it does not advertise loses that path and gets the pixel click instead. Rollback is reverting the second commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `hit_test_acts_only_on_an_advertised_press_or_a_focus` in `platform-macos` `tools::click` tests. The first commit pins the old rule and adds the test, which fails there on every toolkit except VCL and GTK 3. The second commit changes the rule. Of the scoped repository checks, the quick stage (rustfmt, SPDX headers) passed.
- Manual or platform evidence: none yet. The live repro could not run on the authoring host (see the gaps below).
- Known gaps or CI still required: cargo test and clippy for `platform-macos` are left to CI. Still needed: a live background pixel click on an element without `AXPress` on a macOS host, plus the AppKit PX harness row and the standalone browser rows.

title: fix(cua-driver): wait 40 ms after a foreground Windows desktop click and accept a hidden owned dialog
body:
Salvaged from #5410
Refs #5412

## Why

A foreground desktop-scope click on Windows waited 120 ms after the input, though desktop scope restores neither the cursor nor the z-order afterwards. #5410 by @CMGS cuts that wait to 40 ms, the same as a background click. As #5410 notes, the shorter wait alone breaks clicks on Save or OK in a common dialog: the dialog hides at once and is destroyed only later, so the post-click check still saw a live target with its owner in the foreground and reported `foreground_unavailable`. #5410 relied on #5412 for that.

## What changed

- CMGS's commit, unchanged: the post-click wait is 40 ms.
- A foreground window-scope click keeps 120 ms. Since #5772 it restores the cursor after the wait, so the reason #5410 gives for the shorter wait holds only for desktop scope.
- The post-click foreground check counts a target that is the same window and now hidden as dismissed, like a destroyed one. Success still requires the foreground to return to the owner snapshotted before input. Foreground typing keeps the old check, so a dialog that hides mid-text still stops with `foreground_lost`.

## Scope

Windows foreground clicks in `platform-windows` only. Background clicks and drags are unchanged. #5412 also accepts a click that closes an unowned window while some other window takes the foreground. This PR leaves that case alone, because #2812 refuses it on purpose; #5412 stays open for that decision.

## Tradeoffs

#5412 skips the foreground check whenever the target is gone or hidden. This PR keeps the check and extends its existing dismissal rule instead, so a foreground that lands on an unrelated window after the click still fails closed.

## Blast Radius

Every agent that clicks through the Windows desktop scope sees a shorter wait after each click. The relaxed check applies only when the target window still exists, belongs to the same process and is hidden, and the foreground is its own snapshotted owner.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (formatting, headers) pass. A new unit test pins the hidden-or-destroyed dismissal rule.
- Windows builds, unit tests and the desktop E2E lanes run in CI. This host cannot run Windows.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): probe hardware encoders off the GetCapabilities path
body:
## Why

With desktop sharing on, every `GetCapabilities` ran the hardware encoder probe (`cua_media_codec::probe()`) inline on a tokio worker. The probe initializes CUDA for NVENC and libva for VA-API. On the reporter's Hyprland host with an RTX 3090 that call blocked in `drm_modeset_lock`, and the blocked worker took the relay reader and graceful shutdown with it. The CUDA thread in the issue's thread dump points at the probe. That is inferred from the code and the dump; I have no NVIDIA host to reproduce it on.

## What changed

- The daemon starts the encoder probe on its own thread when it builds the desktop services. Each backend is probed in a child of the daemon's own executable (`cua_media_codec`'s existing `Isolation::Subprocess`), which is killed after 10 seconds. `main` calls `maybe_run_probe_child` first, so the child probes, prints its result and exits.
- `h264_hw` (Linux X11 and the tool backend for Hyprland, macOS and Windows) reads the result without waiting. Until the probe lands it is unsupported with "the hardware encoder probe has not finished". A process that started no probe gets an in-process one on a background thread. A probe that panics or cannot start counts as finding no encoders, so nothing waits on it forever.
- Stream encoders wait for the same background probe instead of running their own, so a backend whose probe hung is reported unavailable and never opened in the daemon. In `cua-media-codec`, a probe child that outlives SIGKILL (stuck in an uninterruptible driver call) is reaped on its own thread, so the probe still returns after the timeout.

## Scope

Covers the encoder probe in the capabilities path on every platform. It does not move other synchronous work in `features()` and `displays()` (X11 connect, `hyprctl`) off the async workers, and it does not change Wayland capture to the portal.

## Blast Radius

Every cua-spacesd with desktop services. `h264_hw` reads unsupported for the first moments after startup until the probe finishes. Clients that read it once right at startup may see the software path until they re-query. With `--no-desktop`, nothing changes.

## Verification

- The new `encoder_probe` unit tests pass: a probe blocked on a channel leaves `h264_hw` answering at once as pending, it reports the encoder once the probe returns, and a panicking probe lands as no encoders. The existing `cua-media-codec` probe tests pass, including the hanging-child kill.
- `codec_probe_child_bin` runs the real binary with `CUA_CODEC_PROBE_CHILD=openh264` and expects one JSON result and an exit. It passes at the head. Without the fix the binary ignores the variable and starts serving; I did not rerun it at the test-only commit.
- The scoped repository checks in quick mode and clippy on `cua-spacesd-desktop` passed. The full unit tests and the Windows cross-compile run in CI. No test covers a child stuck in uninterruptible sleep, which userspace cannot stage.

Fixes #5409

title: fix(cua-driver): return at once from macOS bring_to_front when the exact window is already front
body:
Salvaged from #5411

## Why

On macOS, `bring_to_front` with a `window_id` ran the full activation and its stability poll even when the exact window was already in front with focus, which leaves nothing to activate. It now returns early in that case. @CMGS wrote the change in #5411. This PR carries their two commits onto current main, where the tool's activation runs in `activate_blocking`, and adds follow-up fixes.

## What changed

- `already_front` returns early only when the exact postcondition holds, the window is first in the global layer-0 order, and the front process pid is the target whenever one is reported. Every other state takes the full activation path as before. (CMGS)
- Every read behind that check is WindowServer or AX state. So `confirm_already_front` then sends the exact make-key sequence and a Cocoa activation that brings forward only the key window. It observes again after those requests. The result reports `path: "already_front"` only when the window is still already front; otherwise the call takes the full activation path. This covers AppKit holding another app active, AX focus without a native key window, and a sibling ordered above the target during the reads. The early path skips the persistent SkyLight front request, the all-windows activation, the AX raise and the stability poll.
- The ignored macOS e2e test `exact_secondary_window_is_verified_and_prior_app_can_recover_focus` now repeats the exact call and asserts the `already_front` path.

## Scope

Only the macOS exact-window path of `bring_to_front`. The pid-only path, other tools, and the Windows and Linux drivers are unchanged. The tool description and the generated reference are unchanged, because neither lists `path` values.

## Tradeoffs

The early path confirms with one observation after its requests instead of the full path's stability poll. A change that lands after that observation is not caught here. The full path catches it the same way, through the next call's observation.

## Blast Radius

Agents that call `bring_to_front` on a window that is already in front. If the check is wrong, the window stays where it was, which is already in front. Agents that read `path` see one new value.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks in quick mode: rustfmt and SPDX headers pass. A full local run (clippy, unit tests) was not possible on this shared host. Those run in CI.
- Unit tests cover the `already_front` predicate (front and focused, another window on top, another window focused, an inactive process, a front pid that differs from the window owner) and `confirm_already_front` (a window that loses the front during the requests takes the full path, a window that stays front returns early, and a window that is not front sends no early requests).
- Still required: the ignored macOS e2e test on a macOS desktop runner.

title: fix(cua-driver): accept a Windows click that closes or hides an unowned target window
body:
Salvaged from #5412

## Why

On Windows, a desktop-scope click that closes or hides its own window, such as a Close button, is reported as `foreground_unavailable` even though it worked. The post-click check wants the foreground back on the target or its owner. A window with no owner has neither once it is gone, and Windows may activate any other window. A false failure invites a retry, and that retry clicks whatever now sits under the point. #5412 by @CMGS fixes this by skipping the check whenever the target is destroyed or hidden.

## What changed

- CMGS's three commits, unchanged: the check is skipped for a destroyed or hidden target, and the text summary ends with "The window closed or hid." in that case.
- Our commit keeps the check and adds one rule to it. A click that destroys or hides a target with no owner passes. An owned dialog still has to hand the foreground back to the owner snapshotted before input, as #8160 requires.
- The summary note uses the same shared destroyed-or-hidden probe.

## Scope

Post-click verification for Windows foreground clicks in `platform-windows`. Keyboard and typing checks, which also run before input, are unchanged, so a destroyed target still refuses input there.

It builds on #8160 (the salvage of #5410), now merged into main.

## Tradeoffs

#5412 skips the check for any dismissed target. That would also accept an owned dialog whose dismissal sends the foreground to an unrelated window, which #2812 refuses on purpose. Moving the rule into the shared predicate keeps that refusal.

## Blast Radius

Agents clicking through the Windows desktop or window scope. The relaxed case covers only a target that had no owner and is destroyed, or is still the same process's window and hidden, after the click. Incomplete input still fails earlier, before this check.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (formatting, SPDX headers) pass. A new unit test pins the unowned-dismissal rule next to the existing owner-return tests.
- Windows builds, unit tests and the desktop E2E lanes run in CI. This host cannot run Windows.

title: fix(cua-driver): rebase Chromium screen extents only from a frame the size of the target window
body:
Salvaged from #5414

Refs #4967

## Why

On X11, `screen_extent_rebase` moves Chromium's renderer-local "Screen" extents by the X11 window origin. An override-redirect submenu has no accessible top level of its own, so an unscoped walk picked the application's first frame (a panel or the desktop at (0,0)) as the target's frame. Every popup element then moved by the popup's origin, and element clicks on XFCE submenu items missed. The rebase now applies only when the accessible frame is the same size as the target X11 window.

## What changed

- `x11_window_geometry` returns the target window's root origin and size. `x11_window_origin` now wraps it.
- `screen_extent_rebase` returns `None` when the frame's size differs from the window's.
- New tests cover a popup measured against another window's frame, and a Chromium frame reported in DIPs under device scale 2. Neither is rebased.

## Scope

Linux X11 AT-SPI element bounds only. The DIP-to-pixel conversion for Chromium under a device scale is out of scope. Element bounds are already wrong there whether or not the rebase runs, and that needs its own change.

## Blast Radius

The change touches Chromium and Electron windows on X11. A same-sized client frame keeps its rebase, and every existing rebase test still passes. The new rule can only turn the rebase off. If a frame's size ever differs slightly from its X11 client window, that window goes back to its un-rebased coordinates. #4890 also edits `screen_extent_rebase`, so whichever PR lands second needs a small rebase.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (formatting, headers, lockfiles) passed.
- CMGS's commits are kept as authored. CMGS reports running this change on XFCE desktops, where it fixed submenu element clicks.

title: fix(cua-driver): verify existing-profile CDP readiness
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `browser_prepare` with `existing_profile` reported success once the WebSocket handshake finished, even when the browser never answered a CDP command on that socket.

On a probe error or cancellation, only the preparing generation's socket hold is released, so a peer's shared socket stays open and a later claim redials when the failed probe was the last holder. title: fix(cua-driver): refuse GNOME window screenshots from helpers below API 9
body:
## Why

On GNOME Wayland, a WinRects helper below API 9 still got a window screenshot by cropping the Shell stage to the window's frame. That crop shows whatever covers the window, yet the driver labelled it as the target and issued a `capture_id` for it. As RFC #5443 proposes, a window image now comes only from the helper's per-window `CaptureWindow`.

## What changed

- The helper boundary now reports three outcomes: no verified helper, a verified helper that is too old (`HelperTooOld { api }`, which includes a failed `GetVersion`), or a capture result.
- On GNOME, `HelperTooOld` and a helper refusal both return `surface_identity_unproven`. For an older helper, the reason names the API it reports (or says it reported none), the required API 9, and the fix: re-run the installer, then log out and back in. The GNOME stage-crop branch in `wayland_window_crop` is gone. Only "no verified helper" takes another route.
- For window capture only, `GetVersion` gets half the time left, so the owner recheck still runs when a helper never answers. Other trusted helper callers (focus, activation, cursor) keep the full deadline. A verified helper that times out then gets the upgrade guidance instead of looking like no helper.
- The helper README and the skill's Linux notes describe the refusal.

## Scope

Covers GNOME window capture through `screenshot_dispatch`, which backs `get_window_state`, screenshot-only reads and `zoom`. The helper D-Bus API, the installer, X11, Sway/wlroots, Hyprland, niri, KDE, macOS and Windows are unchanged. No new error code or response field: the refusal reuses the existing `screenshot_frame_valid: false` and `screenshot_error` shape.

## Tradeoffs

The RFC's alternatives were keeping the crop for older helpers (the #4882 choice), refusing only when `GetRects` shows an overlap, or withholding only the `capture_id`. Each one still lets another app's pixels reach the caller. `GetRects` also lists no Shell surfaces (notifications, menus, Shell dialogs), so it cannot prove a crop clean.

## Blast Radius

GNOME Wayland users whose loaded helper is below API 9 lose window screenshots until they update the helper and log in again. The accessibility tree, `get_desktop_state`, desktop-target input and recordings keep working. Users on API 9 or newer see no change. Rollback is reverting this commit.

## Verification

- New unit tests: `window_capture_needs_a_verified_helper_at_api_9` covers the version gate (API 9 accepted; API 8 and a failed `GetVersion` give `HelperTooOld`; a missing or re-owned helper gives `NoHelper`). `gnome_window_capture_refuses_helpers_below_api_9` covers the refusal text and the no-fallback rule. Both were mutation-checked. Letting `HelperTooOld` fall through to another route fails the second test. Treating a failed `GetVersion` as no helper fails the first. `version_call_leaves_time_for_the_owner_recheck` covers the time split.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` (SPDX headers, rustfmt, image refs) passed, and the five focused `platform-linux` tests passed. Formatting, the full `platform-linux` suite, clippy, and `cargo check -p cua-driver --features portal-input` passed at the first head. The last commit (window-capture-only version budget, doc wording) was checked here with rustfmt and `bin/ci --quick`; compiling and tests are left to CI because of the shared host's disk guard.
- Not run here: a GNOME desktop session with an API 8 helper loaded. That run is the RFC's remaining acceptance evidence.

Fixes #5443

title: fix(cua-driver): bound a stalled S1 service body read
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `chooseS1Service` in the jev-use TypeScript example passed `AbortSignal.timeout` to `fetch`, then read the body with `response.text()`. When the body stalls past the timeout, the abort escapes as a raw `TimeoutError` instead of `S1ServiceError`, so `run_native.ts` rethrows it instead of logging an `unknown` outcome. Nothing holds the signal once `fetch` resolves either, the shape #8004 fixed in `openjev_model.ts`.
- What changed: the request holds its own timer and `AbortController` for the whole request, reads the body through a reader that cancels on abort (as in #8004), and maps any failure after the abort to `S1ServiceError("S1 service timed out")`. The 256 KiB response cap is now enforced while reading.

## Related work

Fixes #8014
Follows #8004.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: example code only. A timeout before the response headers now reads "S1 service timed out" instead of "S1 service is unreachable: TimeoutError".
- Risk and rollback: small; revert the commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: added `chooseS1Service bounds a body that stalls past the timeout` (stalled loopback body, forced GC). It fails on main and passes with the fix. `npm test` (259 pass) and `npm run typecheck` on Node 22.23.4 and 26.12.1, macOS.
- Manual or platform evidence: 40 stalled reads with forced GC per Node version. Before: 40/40 raw `TimeoutError`. After: 40/40 `S1ServiceError: S1 service timed out`. I could not reproduce the GC hang itself on this machine. The fix removes the dependence on GC anyway.

title: fix(cua-driver): honor a run_steps step's typed window target
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: a `run_steps` step with its own `target: {kind: "window", pid, window_id}` was refused with `invalid_action_target` whenever the batch, or an earlier token step, supplied a window. The run added flat `pid`/`window_id` beside `target`, because `take_selector` reads only flat ids. Earlier steps had already run, so the batch half-applied.
- What changed: a step whose args carry an object `target` names its own window or display. It no longer inherits the batch's window (plan-time probe and run-time lookup). A window target also becomes the window later steps and the end `observe` inherit, the way a token step does.

## Related work

title: feat(cua-driver): add scope_ancestor_role to semantic browser snapshots
body:
Fixes #5452

## Why

In a list or table, every row can repeat the same action name (`Options`). A caller that holds a ref to one row's label has no way to reach that row's action: `scope_ref` only searches below the ref, and a page-wide query returns every row's control. RFC #5452 proposes an opt-in `scope_ancestor_role` on `get_browser_state` (`semantic_v2`). It walks from the ref to its nearest strict ancestor with that role, in the ref's own frame, then runs `query` inside that subtree.

This lands loonghao's fork commit [`9de510aa`](https://github.com/loonghao/cua/commit/9de510aa6c407c5b36a5f62b288702127192f40c) as authored, cherry-picked with `-x` onto current main, with a second commit that adapts it to the RFC.

## What changed

- `get_browser_state` takes `scope_ancestor_role` (an ASCII role of 1–128 bytes, compared lowercase). It requires `target_id`, `tab_id`, `session`, `semantic_v2`, `scope_ref` and `query`. A success returns `snapshot.scope: "ancestor_subtree"` and `snapshot.scope_anchor` (`requested_ref`, `role`, `name`, `frame`, `distance`). Continuation pages keep the same anchor and re-prove its frame first. A continuation token now serves one page: if a concurrent snapshot or another use of the token gets there first, the call refuses with `browser_ref_stale` instead of returning refs that were never stored.
- If the scope can't be proven, the call refuses with the new `browser_scope_unavailable` code and a `detail.reason`: `source_missing`, `source_not_semantic`, `ancestor_missing`, `unproven_frame`, `broken_parent`, `cycle`, `ambiguous` or `cross_frame`. A source with no raw accessibility node (a DOM-supplemented action) refuses with `broken_parent`, since its first edge would be a DOM parent. If the source changed, or a concurrent snapshot superseded the source's snapshot while the call ran, it refuses with `browser_ref_stale` and `source_changed`. If the anchor's frame reloaded before a continuation, it refuses with `browser_ref_stale` and `scope_frame_changed`. None of these widens to a page-wide query.
- What the second commit changes from the prototype:
  - Direct `scope_ref` goes through main's backend-id traversal again, so legacy results, including same-process iframe content, stay the same.
  - `SemanticContinuation` keeps its public fields; the anchor lives in a crate-private map.
  - The top-level `allOf` is gone from the input schema (the protocol lint rejects it for Bedrock), and `invoke` enforces the combinations instead.
  - `scope_anchor` appears only on ancestor scopes.
  - Adds a recovery hint, the browsers guide section and the generated-reference row.

## Scope

Covers the RFC's proposal for the shared browser core, across every surface that calls the tool (CLI, MCP, SDK, raw protocol). It leaves out the RFC's non-goals: no new actions, no selectors, no lookups across frame boundaries, and no native-window ancestor lookup. The ancestor path refuses a cross-document edge in the path or in the subtree (the RFC's proposed answer to its open question 3). It does not build on #5387, which is still open; the ancestor path keys every lookup by frame itself, and #5387 can land independently.

## Tradeoffs

- The schema states only the role's syntax. The rule that `scope_ancestor_role` needs `scope_ref` and `query` is enforced at runtime, like `browser_prepare`'s conditional fields, because a top-level `allOf` breaks Bedrock clients.
- `BrowserRefusalCode`, `ToolRefusalCode` and the testkit `RefusalCode` each gain a variant. They are not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so exhaustive matches downstream need a new arm. Earlier feat PRs added refusal codes the same way (#3015).

## Blast Radius

The new code paths run only when `scope_ancestor_role` is present. Requests without it keep their inputs, response shape (no `scope_anchor` key) and direct-scope traversal; a unit test pins direct scope following `childIds` into a same-process iframe. The RFC has no maintainer decision summary posted yet, so this needs a maintainer's read before merging.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::`: 315 passed, including the fork's mock-CDP tests (row precision, refusal reasons, continuation across a page boundary at 300 nodes, OOPIF loader change) and new unit tests: a source whose own role matches is skipped, a cross-frame child edge refuses, direct scope still reaches same-process iframe content. A mock-CDP test runs two continuations on one token at once: exactly one succeeds and the other gets `browser_ref_stale`. With the consume check disabled, that test fails.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass. The generated-reference drift check needs a release build and is left to CI. The real-browser desktop E2E matrix did not run.
- The branch is updated by merging main; the merge had no conflicts, and CI covers the compile and tests at the new head.
- Three mock-CDP tests cover refusal reasons on ancestor continuations: a main-frame navigation returns `browser_ref_stale` with `scope_frame_changed`, and losing OOPIF attach support or the tab's frame tree returns `browser_scope_unavailable` with `unproven_frame`.
- Later commits refuse a DOM-supplemented source as `broken_parent` (unit test) and refuse an ancestor request whose source ref a concurrent snapshot superseded during the call (mock-CDP test racing a refresh against the ancestor request). This host could not build or test them; CI compiles them and runs the tests. The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass on the new head.

title: [Bug]: macOS get_desktop_state reports agent_overlay_capture "not_present" after the agent cursor's idle hide, while its PNG shows the cursor
body:
### Primary area
Cua Driver

### Summary
On macOS, once a session's agent cursor reaches its idle hide (`idle_hide_ms`, default 15000, counted from the session's last call that moves or cues the cursor), `get_desktop_state` in that session returns `agent_overlay_capture: {"status": "not_present"}`, but the returned PNG shows the cursor. VNC frames of the real screen show the cursor faded before that call and back on screen right after it. The `not_present` contract from #4194 / #4199 says "No Driver overlay pixels were on screen".

### Reproduction
macOS guest, Calculator open, every call in one session `S`:
1. `cua-driver get_window_state '{"pid":PID,"window_id":WID,"session":"S"}'`
2. `cua-driver click '{"element_token":"<snapshot_id>:5","session":"S"}'` (the 7 button)
3. Immediately: `cua-driver get_desktop_state '{"session":"S","screenshot_out_file":"/tmp/a.png","max_image_dimension":0}'`
4. Make no call in `S` for 20 s, then the same call to `/tmp/b.png`.

In the runs counted below, each `get_desktop_state` was preceded by `cua-driver get_agent_cursor_state '{"session":"S"}'`. The steps as written, with step 4 about 30 s after step 3, gave a wrong step 4 in 2 of 3 runs on 0.53.2.

Control: the same steps with `cua-driver set_agent_cursor_motion '{"session":"S","idle_hide_ms":0}'` first.

Frequency (no retries): on 0.53.2, 7 of 8 captures taken after a gap longer than `idle_hide_ms` were wrong, and 0 of 2 with `idle_hide_ms: 0`. On 0.53.1, 7 of 7 and 0 of 2; on 0.38.0, 2 of 2 and 0 of 2. All 11 captures taken right after the click were correct. On 0.53.1, 9 of 9 captures from 0 to 25 s after the click were correct when no gap between calls exceeded about 7 s.

### Expected behavior
Either the idle-hidden cursor is gone from the screen and the PNG is clean, or the capture excludes the overlay and reports `excluded`. A capture reported `not_present` holds no overlay pixels.

### Actual behavior
Step 3: `{"method":"screencapturekit_excluding_windows","status":"excluded"}`, PNG clean (correct).
Step 4: `{"status":"not_present"}`, and the PNG shows the agent cursor over the 7 button. In runs that also called `get_session` just before step 4, it returned `"cursor_visible": false` (`idle_seconds` 19 to 22). On 0.53.1, a VNC frame of the real screen taken right after the capture also shows the cursor. With `idle_hide_ms: 0`, step 4 reads `excluded` and the PNG is clean.

### Environment
Cua Driver 0.53.2 (`248e95bd3395`), 0.53.1 (`004e38a75000`) and 0.38.0 (`85e2b1318bd7`), each installed with `install.sh` and `CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION`, all reproduce. CLI calls forwarded to the running daemon.
macOS 26.4 (25E246) arm64 VM, one 1920x1440 display at scale 2, default cursor theme. Target app: Calculator.

### Evidence
The step 3 and step 4 captures from one 0.53.2 run (`step3-excluded.png` and `step4-not-present.png`, unmodified) are available on request.

### Workaround and additional context
Workaround: set `idle_hide_ms: 0` for sessions whose desktop captures must be clean, or keep every gap between calls that move or cue the cursor (such as `click` or `get_desktop_state`) under `idle_hide_ms`. A `get_agent_cursor_state` or `get_session` call right before the capture does not help once the hide has fired; neither sends a cursor cue ([cursor.rs#L504-L508](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/248e95bd3395d03de7e694002b450c0dd37580d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-contract/src/cursor.rs#L504-L508)).

Where it decides, at `cua-driver-rs-v0.53.2`: `OverlayExcluder::exclude` returns `NotPresent` when `overlay_may_show_pixels()` is false ([capture.rs#L1083-L1094](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/248e95bd3395d03de7e694002b450c0dd37580d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/capture.rs#L1083-L1094)). That flag comes from the last composed frame's `cursor_may_paint` plus a 250 ms grace ([overlay.rs#L140-L167](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/248e95bd3395d03de7e694002b450c0dd37580d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs#L140-L167)), and the display is then captured with no window excluded and `ResidualCheck::Clean`, with no pixel check ([capture.rs#L1111-L1122](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/248e95bd3395d03de7e694002b450c0dd37580d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/capture.rs#L1111-L1122)). Suspected, not traced: `get_desktop_state` first sends a cursor cue ([tool.rs#L2507](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/248e95bd3395d03de7e694002b450c0dd37580d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs#L2507)) that re-reveals an idle-faded cursor ([render_state.rs#L1076-L1079](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/248e95bd3395d03de7e694002b450c0dd37580d5/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cursor-overlay/src/render_state.rs#L1076-L1079), the behavior #3011 asked for). If the overlay thread has not composed that frame yet, the excluder reads the stale flag, and the screenshot taken after it holds the cursor. That would also explain the occasional correct capture.

`main` at `9346cabc2e06` has no change to these files since 0.53.2. #6171 (open) orders the overlay out after the idle fade, which may change this path; not tested.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): honor disabled UIA ancestors
body:
Salvaged from #5631.

Ethan's commit (ethanblake4) and the two follow-ups from #5653 are kept as authored, rebased onto main. Two commits on top adapt them to #7469, which landed after #5631 was written.

## Why

On Windows, an enabled-looking control inside a disabled container can't actually be used, but Cua reported it as enabled. #5631 passes the disabled state down through the cached and native UIA walks. Since #5631 was written, #7469 started indexing disabled Windows controls, publishing `enabled: false`, and refusing their token writers. This salvage keeps that contract and extends it to controls under a disabled ancestor.

## What changed

- From #5631: the walk reports a control under a disabled ancestor as `enabled: false`, and an owned `Window` starts its own enabled scope. Walk nodes own their COM references, and snapshots adopt them, so the manual `release_nodes` calls are gone. This also covers #8370's content-only leak: a row that is not adopted drops its reference with the walk, so main's `from_nodes` hand-off is replaced by `adopt_nodes` and its regression test now runs against it. A menu path target with no retained UIA element is refused.
- New: the token writers' live re-check (`refuse_if_disabled`) uses the same rule. It climbs control-view parents up to the nearest `Window`, reading an ancestor whose state can't be read as enabled and climbing past it, as the cached walk does. It also climbs from a target whose own state can't be read. So `click`, `set_value` and `type_text` on such a control get `element_disabled` even when the provider reports the child as enabled.
- New: the WPF `disabled_ancestors` case now expects main's contract. The checkbox is indexed with `enabled: false`, its writers are refused as `element_disabled` and leave it untoggled, and it reads as enabled once the ancestor is enabled.

## Scope

Windows UIA only. The MSAA walk does not pass down ancestor state. macOS and Linux are unchanged. The #5631 design that removed disabled descendants' indices and actions is dropped in favour of #7469's indexed rows.

## Blast Radius

Windows `get_window_state` now reports `enabled: false` for controls under a disabled container. Token writers on those controls get `element_disabled` instead of input the app would ignore. Each live re-check now makes one UIA parent read per ancestor level up to the window. The walk's COM reference handling changed: only indexed nodes keep a reference.

## Verification

- Updated by merging main. The conflicts with #8370 resolve to the node-guard model above.
- The live climb matches the cached walk on every Window-rooted chain of up to four Button, Pane and Window nodes with each enabled, disabled or unreadable state (a standalone copy of both functions).
- The scoped repository checks (quick stage): rustfmt, lockfiles, SPDX headers, and the e2e inventory test pass. The Windows build, unit tests and the WPF e2e case were not run on this host and are left to Windows CI and the desktop lanes.

title: fix(cua-driver): accept trusted certs and authorize new local keys
body:
## Summary

Developers could not install the local driver with a trusted signing certificate or a newly generated key in strict signing mode.

Accept either certificate pin spelling and authorize the newly imported key when its keychain password is supplied. Without a password, print the scoped authorization command. Release signing checks are exactly main's: a root-pinned certificate is accepted only on the local history path.

Review first: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/_local-signing.sh::ensure_local_signing_identity` and `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/history_runtime.rs::validate_history_app_signature`.

## Related work

Fixes #3799. #3800 was closed as stale; happy to reopen it instead if useful. #3666 improves signing prompt handling; #5981 replaces bundle ID literals in the history test.

RFC: not required for this bug fix.

## Compatibility and risk

No public interface changes. Authorization is limited to the named local private key. Existing identities are not modified. Rollback restores leaf-only admission and manual key authorization.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Commands and mutation proof</summary>

From the repo root, on macOS:

```bash
uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with pytest==8.4.2 python -m pytest libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/ -v
bash -n libs/cua-driver/scripts/_local-signing.sh libs/cua-driver/tests/runners/macos-lume/run-all.sh
```

title: fix(cua-driver): warn when pruning referenced release dirs
body:
Salvaged from #5681

Refs #3957

## Why

The release installer keeps the newest five per-target dirs under `~/.cua-driver/packages/releases` and deletes the rest. A hand-written systemd user unit or desktop entry that pins one of those versioned paths breaks silently when its dir is pruned, then fails on every start with `Failed at step EXEC` (#3957). This warns before the delete, naming each referencing file and the stable `packages/current/cua-driver` path.

## What changed

- `prune_old_releases` calls `warn_referenced_release_dirs` before `rm -rf`. It scans systemd user `*.service`, `*.socket` and `*.timer` units, XDG application entries and XDG autostart entries for the `packages/releases/<dir>` suffix, so absolute, `%h/...` and `$HOME/...` spellings all match. (Contributor commit, kept as authored.)
- On top: desktop entries are looked up under `XDG_DATA_HOME` when it is set, matching the uninstaller and `kwin-capture`, with a test for it.
- The warning runs in a subshell with its status ignored. Without that, a closed stderr pipe made its `printf` raise SIGPIPE and stop the installer before `rm -rf`.

## Scope

Installer diagnostics only. Retention, exit status and the deleted set are unchanged. Linux only, since only the Linux branch calls the pruner. Not covered: references through wrapper scripts, systemd drop-ins, or symlinks. #3957's other asks (official Linux autostart, retention docs) are out of scope, so the issue stays open.

## Blast Radius

Extra `warning:` lines on stderr during an install that prunes a referenced dir. The scan is read-only. `ai.cua.driver.desktop` from `kwin-capture on` names `packages/current`, so it does not trigger the warning.

## Verification

- `test_install_prune_references.py`: 10 passed. The `XDG_DATA_HOME` case and the closed-stderr case each failed before their fix commit.
- `test_installer_bash32_syntax.py` passed. The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) passed.

body:
Release Please opens a Cua Spaces or cua SDK release PR while its pinned cua-spacesd release is still a draft. The check "cua-spacesd pin is published" runs once, fails, and stays red after the release publishes until someone reruns it (#8155, #8174).

New workflow `ci-spacesd-pin-recheck.yml` reruns the failed job on every open PR whose newest pin check failed, when a `cua-spacesd-v*` release publishes. It triggers on `release: published` and on the `CD: cua-spacesd` run completing, because that CD publishes with the workflow token, which never fires `release` events. Permissions are `actions: write` and `contents: read`; unit tests are included. The check still fails on a draft, now saying the release is in progress and re-runs automatically.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep Qt line edit validators on background type_text
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On Linux, background typing into a Qt line edit refuses once #8485 stops the write that skipped its validator.
- What changed: on X11 it now focuses the field without activating its window and sends keys, so the validator applies, and reads the field back; it refuses when the field is hidden or a popup or modal is open. Wayland still refuses.

## Related work

Refs #7327. Builds on #8485 (first two commits here); review the third.

RFC: not required.

## Compatibility and risk

Review first: `type_text.rs::qt_line_edit_background`, then `qt_key_blocker`.

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux X11 only.
- Risk and rollback: one commit; reverting it restores the refusal.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: production +426/-19, tests +210/-28 (unit test; PyQt test, which fails with `src` reverted to #8485).
- Manual or platform evidence: supporting: guards refused before any key 20/20 per blocker; normal rows 40/40 per text; Xorg and Xvfb, at the pre-split head. PyQt test passes at this head (real Xorg, Xvfb; Qt5, Qt6).
- Known gaps or CI still required: guards miss a grab without a popup, and a popup or focus change after the check. No runner selects the `#[ignore]`d PyQt test. KDE X11, E2E not run.

<details>
<summary>Routes measured, guards, commands</summary>

Each candidate route into an unfocused PyQt window while a simulated user types `qwqwqw` into a focused GTK window. 40 tries per cell = 10 each of Qt6 and Qt5, `QLineEdit` + `QIntValidator` and `QSpinBox`. "Allowed" means the field holds only what the validator accepts (`12`, empty, `12`).

| X server | route | `12` allowed | `AB` allowed | `1a2` allowed | user kept activation, focus and every key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| real Xorg | AT-SPI `generate_keyboard_event` | 0/40 | 40/40 (empty) | 0/40 | 0/120 (typed into the user's window) |
| real Xorg | GrabFocus + virtual master keyboard | 40/40 | 40/40 | 40/40 | 120/120 |
| real Xorg | GrabFocus + `XSendEvent` | 40/40 | 40/40 | 40/40 | 120/120 |
| real Xorg | foreground | 40/40 | 40/40 | 40/40 | 0/120 (by design) |
| Xvfb | GrabFocus + `XSendEvent` | 40/40 | 40/40 | 40/40 | 120/120 |

Measured with a probe build of these routes (each route selected by hand) on a real Xorg guest (Ubuntu 24.04, mutter, `/dev/uinput`) and on Xvfb + openbox; the shipped head is checked by the PyQt test below. The write this replaces and the refusal are measured in #8485.

GNOME Wayland (Fedora 44 guest, one try each on Qt5 and Qt6): `XSendEvent` to an XWayland Qt window after `GrabFocus` left the field empty. The driver's Wayland keyboard routes reach only the focused surface, so the call refuses there.

PyQt test (`type_text_qt_line_edit_xorg`), background:

| typed into | field holds | effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line edit + `QIntValidator`: `12` / `AB` / `1a2` | `12` / empty / `12` | `confirmed` / `suspected_noop` / `unverifiable` (summary: "now reads '12', which is not its earlier value with the typed text inserted") |
| spin box: `12` / `AB` / `1a2` | contains `12` / `0` / contains `12` | same |
| plain line edit: `Hi, Zoë {x}!` / `中文 ok` | the text | `confirmed` |
| plain-text edit: `AB` | `AB` | `confirmed` (accessibility write, unchanged) |

`confirmed` needs a changed value equal to the old one with the text inserted at one position (or, for a spin box only, the same whole number); text with Tab or Return is never confirmed from one field.

At `f36709a63` (one run each, rebased on #8485's `set_value` commit, which adds a background `set_value` row to this test): passes on real Xorg with the agent keyboard (`route: global_input`) and on Xvfb with `XSendEvent` (`synthetic_events`), Qt6 and Qt5.

Guards, checked just before the focus request: background `"12"` into the line edit with the user's GTK window active. 20 runs each server (10 Qt6, 10 Qt5) at the pre-split head `0d79c1a42`, whose key-route code this commit carries unchanged; a pass means refused with `background_unavailable` naming the cause, no Qt widget (fields, combo, dialog field, menu action) changed, the user's window unchanged.

| blocker | real Xorg | Xvfb |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field hidden | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| `QMenu` open | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| `QComboBox` list open | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| modal `QDialog` | 20/20 | 20/20 |

In the same runs every normal row (line edit and spin box, `12` / `AB` / `1a2`) gave its expected effect 40/40 per text on each server.

What the guards see: the field's AT-SPI states as the toolkit exports them (`showing`, `visible`, `focusable`, enabled, not `read-only`), the app's mapped override-redirect windows (Qt menus and combo box lists are not in its AT-SPI tree) and `_NET_WM_STATE_MODAL` on its other windows.

The gap between the check and the keys is wider on a first call, while the virtual keyboard plugs in; a focus change inside it was not observed, and the readback never reports `confirmed` for one.

From `libs/cua-driver/rust`:

```sh
# real Xorg session with a writable /dev/uinput, and Xvfb:
CUA_TEST_QT=6 cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --test type_text_qt_line_edit_xorg -- --ignored --nocapture
dbus-run-session -- xvfb-run -a bash -c '(openbox &); sleep 1;
  CUA_TEST_QT=5 cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --test type_text_qt_line_edit_xorg -- --ignored --nocapture'

cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets
cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

</details>

- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

body:
## Summary

Following the TypeScript example README installs Driver 0.19.2, but the examples use newer APIs including `ActionTarget`, `ClickPosition`, and `InputDeliveryMode`. A clean install produces nine type errors, and `npm run native` exits during import because `ActionTarget` is missing.

Pin the examples and platform packages to published Driver 0.54.0. Check the locked published SDK before CI replaces it with the candidate tarball, preserving the existing candidate check. Document `npm ci`, Node 22, and macOS host permission attribution.

## Related work

Refs #3100, which explicitly leaves this example/API mismatch outside its dependency-security scope. The two changes touch the same manifests and may need reconciliation. #4000 checks documentation snippets, not this executable example's published dependency path.

## Compatibility and risk

No Driver API, permission policy, or native implementation changes; no RFC is needed. Only the example's Driver dependency and its six optional platform packages change. Future example API changes must compile against both the pinned published SDK and the candidate SDK.

## Validation

- Node 22.22.2 on macOS arm64: clean `npm ci` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_fixture_server -v` passes.
- `npm run native` passes after granting the Node host Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions: desktop capture, input, Enter, independent `/state` verification, post-action capture, and normal exit. The browser and endpoint both observed the generated token.
- `git diff --check` and actionlint 1.7.12 pass.
- `bin/ci --no-install`: actionlint, lockfiles, workflow runner policy, image references, and local-CI tests/workflow sync pass. The image doctor ledger check is still running; local sign-off is pending.

Linux/Windows desktop behavior and authenticated Claude/Codex agent runs were not exercised locally. The unchanged candidate-package build remains covered by upstream CI.

title: ci(cua-driver): check examples against the locked published SDK before the candidate
body:
### Problem

The contract-clients workflow installs the agent SDK example dependencies with `npm ci`, then replaces the published Driver SDK with the candidate tarball before running `npm run typecheck`. This verifies candidate compatibility but can hide a broken README installation path.

At main `052dc3a0c19646f89d5e6ca30e110e2dd541eec2`, the examples pin Driver 0.19.2 while using newer APIs. A clean installation produces nine type errors, and `npm run native` exits during import because `ActionTarget` is missing. Installing published 0.54.0 resolves the type errors; the native example also passed on macOS with the required host permissions.

### Requested maintainer change

In `.github/workflows/ci-cua-driver-contract-clients.yml`, run `npm run typecheck` immediately after the example's `npm ci`, before installing the candidate tarball. Keep the existing typecheck after the candidate installation, with separate step names for published and candidate SDKs.

Acceptance: reverting the example pin to 0.19.2 should fail the published-package check even if the candidate package supports all the APIs.

### Related work

#8193 was automatically closed because fork PRs cannot change workflows. The dependency and README fix is #8195, without workflow changes. #3100 documents the same API mismatch but intentionally leaves it outside its dependency-security scope.

### HTTP regression tests

#8196 adds `npm test` for credential-free loopback HTTP timeout regressions in the same example directory. Please also run that command alongside the example checks; it does not load the native Driver or require desktop permissions.

title: fix(cua-driver): bound TypeScript fixture HTTP requests
body:
## Summary

The native TypeScript example declares a 10-second timeout, but `/reset` has no request timeout and `/state` only checks its deadline between requests. A fixture that accepts a connection without sending headers or finishing its response body can keep the example waiting past that limit.

Move fixture HTTP calls into a small module with an AbortController deadline. The submission deadline covers all polls, response bodies, and polling delays; reset has its own deadline. Requests are cancelled on timeout and non-success HTTP status codes remain visible. Desktop actions are never retried.

## Related work

#8195 separately fixes the existing published SDK/API mismatch. This PR leaves the dependency pin unchanged and can be reviewed independently. #8194 requests maintainer-owned CI integration; this PR changes no workflow or action files.

No public Driver API, native implementation, or permission policy changes; no RFC is needed.

## Validation

On Node 22.22.2, macOS arm64:

- `npm test`: eight tests pass using real loopback HTTP servers. They cover stalled headers and bodies for both operations, cancellation closing the connection, successful reset/submission, a shared polling deadline, and HTTP errors.
- Mutation check: removing the state request's abort signal makes the stalled-body test fail.
- Baseline executable with published SDK 0.54.0 remained pending beyond 11 seconds against a server that never responds. The fixed executable exits with `fixture reset timed out` (about 11.5 seconds including process startup).
- Strict standalone TypeScript checking of the helper and tests passes. Full example typechecking passes with SDK 0.54.0 installed temporarily without changing the manifest or lockfile. The untouched main pin, 0.19.2, still produces the nine existing API errors addressed by #8195.
- `git diff --check` passes. `bin/ci --no-install` passes all four selected checks: headers, lockfiles, image references, and the image-doctor ledger.

These HTTP tests require no desktop permissions, credentials, or model calls. Native input behavior is unchanged; the desktop walkthrough previously validated for #8195 was not repeated for this HTTP-only change. The new test command is `npm test` in `libs/cua-driver/examples/agent-sdks`.

title: [Bug]: Linux/X11 Cinnamon: first background pixel click (MPX master add) crashes Cinnamon with SIGSEGV; keyboard dead afterwards (0.54.0)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux Mint 22.2 / Cinnamon (X11), the first background pixel click of a session crashes Cinnamon (SIGSEGV). The click goes through the MPX route (`path=mpx_pointer`), which creates a `CUA v1.…` uinput pointer and an XInput2 master pointer/keyboard pair. Cinnamon crashes while handling the XI2 hierarchy event for the new master, about 2 s after the kernel registers the uinput device.

It happened twice on the same day, on two separate boots, each time on the first MPX click. Cinnamon has no other core dumps on record.

After Cinnamon restarts (`cinnamon --replace` / its fallback), keyboard input no longer reaches Brave, Orca, or the on-screen keyboard. Only the terminal accepts typing, and a reboot is needed. That looks like the leaked-master-keyboard symptom from #3337. The `CUA v1.…` master pair was still registered afterwards (ids 28–32).

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| cua-driver | 0.54.0 (`cua-driver mcp`, stdio, via OpenCode) |
| OS | Linux Mint 22.2 (Zara), kernel 7.0.0-43-generic |
| Desktop | Cinnamon 6.4.14+xia, muffin 6.4.1+xia (Mint `zara/backport`), Xorg |
| GTK | libgtk-3-0t64 3.24.41-4ubuntu1.3 |
| Monitors | 4 × 1920×1080 (2×2) |
| Target | Telegram Desktop (Flatpak), no AT-SPI tree (`degraded: x11_property_fallback_partial`) |
| Other input | `keyd` virtual keyboard/pointer present |

### Reproduction

1. `list_windows`, then `get_window_state` on a window without an AT-SPI tree (here Flatpak Telegram). Both are read-only and caused no problem.
2. `run_steps` with one step: `{"tool":"click","args":{"x":34,"y":34}}`, `pid`/`window_id` of that window, default `delivery_mode:"background"`.
3. Result: `Clicked … (delivery_mode=background, path=mpx_pointer, focus untouched)`.
4. Within about 2 s, Cinnamon segfaults and falls back to a fallback panel.

### Evidence (journalctl + coredumpctl)

Boot 1:
```
07:26:05 kernel: input: CUA v1.k17YH_Bsek7JziQCtY14ig.AABcPwAAAAAABFQ7.AAAAAAAAAAE uinput pointer as /devices/virtual/input/input42
07:26:07 systemd-coredump: Process 3276 (cinnamon) dumped core.   SIGSEGV
#0 _clutter_input_device_add_slave (libmuffin-clutter-0.so.0 + 0x75c11)
#1 add_device                      (libmuffin.so.0 + 0x78bb6)
#2 translate_hierarchy_event       (libmuffin.so.0 + 0x7d59c)
#3 meta_x11_handle_event.isra.0    (libmuffin.so.0 + 0x13393f)
#4 handle_host_xevent              (libmuffin.so.0 + 0x7aa74)
#7 g_main_loop_run → meta_run → main
```

Boot 2:
```
17:15:16 kernel: input: CUA v1.gJsMCsIzlU9E5hxr3aUwFw.AABihQAAAAAACWSZ.AAAAAAAAAAE uinput pointer as /devices/virtual/input/input50
17:15:16 keyd: DEVICE: ignoring 1234:5678:65620431 (CUA v1.… uinput pointer)
17:15:18 systemd-coredump: Process 3231 (cinnamon) dumped core.   SIGSEGV
#0 libgdk-3.so.0 + 0x35c16   (nearest export: gdk_device_list_slave_devices)
#1 libgdk-3.so.0 + 0xad186
#2 libgdk-3.so.0 + 0x89d8b   (nearest export: gdk_x11_device_manager_lookup)
#3 libgdk-3.so.0 + 0x90c28
#4 libgdk-3.so.0 + 0x93c54
#5 gdk_display_get_event
#9 g_main_loop_run → meta_run → main
```

After the crash:
```
⎡ CUA v1.gJsMCsIzlU9E5hxr3aUwFw… pointer   id=29 [master pointer  (30)]
⎜   ↳ … uinput pointer                     id=28 [slave  pointer  (29)]
⎜   ↳ … XTEST pointer                      id=31 [slave  pointer  (29)]
⎣ CUA v1.gJsMCsIzlU9E5hxr3aUwFw… keyboard  id=30 [master keyboard (29)]
    ↳ … XTEST keyboard                     id=32 [slave  keyboard (30)]
```

Symbol names for boot 2 are the nearest exported symbols (no debug symbols installed), so treat them as approximate. The boot-1 frames are symbolised by systemd-coredump.

### Expected behavior

A background click doesn't crash the user's desktop shell. Failing that, the driver detects a compositor/desktop that can't handle a new XI2 master and refuses or falls back (XTEST, or `background_unavailable`) instead of adding one.

### Actual behavior

Cinnamon segfaults on the hierarchy event for the new master (once in muffin's `translate_hierarchy_event` → `_clutter_input_device_add_slave`, once in GDK's XI2 device handling). Afterwards keyboard input is broken until reboot.

### Notes

- The root bug is probably in muffin/GDK's handling of a second XI2 master, similar to #7325 (Qt crashing on master *removal*), but here it's master *addition*. Any Cinnamon user with a writable `/dev/uinput` would hit it on their first MPX click.
- Possibly related: #3871 (Cinnamon/X11 full freeze with `cua-driver mcp`), #3337 (leaked master keyboard breaks typing). With #7358, master pairs are now kept instead of removed. That avoids #7325, but here it may leave the extra master keyboard that breaks typing after the shell restarts.
- Suggestion: an opt-out (env var/config) that disables the MPX route and uses XTEST or refuses, plus a doctor/health check warning on Cinnamon/muffin.

title: fix(cua-driver): block uinput pointer hotplug on Cinnamon X11
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Cinnamon X11 (Linux Mint 22.2, Cinnamon 6.4.14 / muffin 6.4.1, GTK 3.24.41), the first background pixel click of a session goes through the MPX route (`path=mpx_pointer`). It hotplugs a `CUA v1.…` uinput pointer and XI2 master pair, and Cinnamon segfaults on the resulting hierarchy event. After the shell restarts, keyboard input to Chromium/Electron apps stays broken until reboot. Full evidence (two cores, journal timelines, stacks) is in #8197.
- What changed: the existing KDE Plasma X11 hotplug gate now covers Cinnamon too. On Cinnamon X11 (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=X-Cinnamon`, `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP`/`DESKTOP_SESSION=cinnamon`), `real_pointer_input_available()` returns false, so no uinput device or master pair is created. Clicks, drags and scrolls use the existing XSendEvent background route. Input with no background route returns `background_unavailable` and the documented foreground (XTEST) escalation. The master-pair creation choke point refuses with a message that names the desktop (`disabled on Cinnamon X11; retry with delivery_mode='foreground'`).

The gate is the same one added for KDE in 56f13c3 (#2888): the KDE path and its refusal text are unchanged, only generalised to an enum. The `X-` prefix is stripped before matching, so `X-Cinnamon` matches and names like `cinnamon-ish` don't.

## Related work

Refs #8197

Possibly related: #3871 (Cinnamon/X11 freeze with `cua-driver mcp`), #3337 (leaked master keyboard breaks typing). This PR only prevents the MPX hotplug on Cinnamon. It doesn't change pair pooling or cleanup from #7358.

RFC: not required. Same behaviour as the existing KDE X11 gate, no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Cinnamon X11 only. Background pixel clicks no longer take the `mpx_pointer` route. Some apps ignore XSendEvent clicks, and background `type_text` to surfaces without AT-SPI now refuses with `background_unavailable` instead of crashing the shell. Element (AT-SPI) actions, foreground input, Wayland and every other desktop are unchanged. The agent cursor overlay is a separate override-redirect window and is unaffected.
- Risk and rollback: low. Desktop detection reads env vars only. Rollback is reverting this commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - Extended the existing owner test (renamed `unsafe_x11_desktops_disable_uinput_pointer_hotplug`) with Linux Mint's exact session environment, a bare `DESKTOP_SESSION=cinnamon`, Cinnamon on Wayland (not gated), a near-miss name (not gated), and the choke-point refusal text for both desktops. Mutation-checked: removing the Cinnamon match fails the test (`left: None, right: Some(Cinnamon)`).
  - `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib`: 1112 passed, 16 ignored.
  - `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `bin/ci --quick`: 5 passed, 4 skipped (quick mode).
- Manual or platform evidence: Linux Mint 22.2, Cinnamon 6.4.14+xia, muffin 6.4.1+xia, Xorg, writable `/dev/uinput`, 4 monitors. Release build of this branch run as `cua-driver serve` on the live session. Before and after every step: no new `kernel: input: CUA` line, no CUA devices in `xinput list`, Cinnamon pid unchanged, no new core.
  - `xlogo` (no AT-SPI): background click, right_click and drag used `path=x11_xsendevent`; scroll and press_key were delivered; background type_text refused with `background_unavailable`.
  - Flatpak Telegram (no AT-SPI, the window from #8197): a background click opened a chat; background type_text refused; foreground type_text plus a foreground Return sent a message.
  - Before the fix, the same Telegram click crashed Cinnamon within 2 s on two separate boots.
- Known gaps or CI still required: full `bin/ci` (unit tests, generated reference, bindings) and the desktop E2E lanes are left to CI. No Cinnamon lane exists. I didn't test a Cinnamon version other than 6.4.14, or the Cinnamon Wayland session (deliberately not gated).

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (N/A: releasing fix)
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). Only `bin/ci --quick` was run locally. Clippy and platform-linux unit tests were run separately (above).

Prepared with an AI coding agent. I've read the diff, and the checks above were run on my machine.

title: fix(cuabot): bump Playwright to 1.65.1 (Chromium 159)
body:
## What
Bumps cuabot's Playwright dependency from ^1.58.1 (locked 1.61.0) to ^1.65.1 and refreshes `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

## Why

- Lockfile-only change plus the version range; no source changes.
- Not covered here: the distro Chromium in the cuabot image comes from a PPA and is unpinned, so it updates on the next image build.
