title: ci(release): raise cua-sandbox's cua-driver bound automatically
body:
## What

Every Cua Driver 0.x minor used to block its release PR on `test_cua_sandbox_driver_range.py` until someone raised cua-sandbox's `driver` bound by hand (last time: #8162 for 0.54, earlier 0.48 and 0.50). This removes that manual step.

## How

- New job `driver-bound` in `release-please.yml`. When the open Driver release PR carries a version outside the bound, it runs `sync_cua_sandbox_driver_bound.py` (from main) and opens `fix(cua-sandbox): accept cua-driver 0.NN` with the Release App token, then queues auto-merge (squash). It is a `fix(cua-sandbox)` PR, so cua-sandbox ships the new range with the Driver, as in #8162.
- The script raises the bound to the next 0.x minor in the pyproject, README, docs and the five uv.lock files. It never lowers the bound, refuses non-0.x versions, validates the version with an anchored regex and asserts the result covers it.
- The existing contract-clients CI gates the PR, since it touches `libs/python/cua-sandbox/**`.
- `release_branch_needs_rebase.py` now refreshes the Driver release branch when cua-sandbox's pyproject changes, so its range check re-runs after the bound merges.
- Once merged, the version is in range and the job does nothing.

## Security

Separate job on a fresh main checkout with `persist-credentials: false`. Release-branch files are read as data, with VERSION and manifest required to agree. App token only (a `GITHUB_TOKEN` PR would not start checks). Push uses a lease, the diff must equal the files the script reports, and auto-merge uses `--match-head-commit`.

## Tests

`test_sync_cua_sandbox_driver_bound.py` covers the rewrite, idempotence, refusals, a file-list completeness check against the real repo, and the workflow wiring. `bin/ci --quick --fix` is green.

Linear: CUA-4388. Plain words: Driver releases no longer wait on a manual cua-sandbox edit.

title: fix(cua-driver): reopen running apps with launch_app
body:
Salvaged from #6198 by @maxvint. Their three commits are kept as authored and rebased onto main. One commit of ours sits on top.

## Why

`launch_app` sends `aevt/oapp` on every background launch. When the app is already running and its window is closed, minimized or hidden, many apps (Electron ones especially) ignore `oapp`, so no window comes back. A Dock click or `open -g` sends `aevt/rapp` (`kAEReopenApplication`) and gets the window back without changing the frontmost app.

## What changed

- `nsworkspace::open_application` sends `aevt/rapp` when the target bundle already has a running pid and `creates_new_instance` is false. It still sends `aevt/oapp` for a cold launch, a new instance, and the URL handoff path. `activates = false` and the focus-steal suppression are unchanged.
- The bundle-id and name launch paths share one `background_launch_config`.
- Unit tests cover the event choice. An ignored macOS E2E starts the AppKit test harness, hides it, calls `launch_app` again, and asserts that the harness becomes visible while Finder stays frontmost. `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh` already runs every ignored test in `installed_app_launch_macos_test`, so the canonical macOS runner picks it up.
- Ours: dropped `bundle_and_name_launches_share_background_launch_config`. It called the same function twice and compared the two results, so it could not fail.

## Scope

macOS `launch_app` without URLs, arguments, environment or a new instance. Windows and Linux launch paths are unchanged, since this is the macOS AppleEvent that LaunchServices attaches.

## Tradeoffs

`rapp` is the event a Dock click sends, so a running app with no windows now does what a Dock click does. A document app with no windows may open a new untitled document or an open panel, where `oapp` used to do nothing.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS `launch_app` call on a running app. A running app that already has a visible window gets `rapp` and keeps that window. Cold launches still get `oapp`, same as before.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt and SPDX headers) pass. The unit tests and the macOS installed-app E2E are covered by the verifier run on this head and by CI.

title: fix(cua-driver-sdk): stop graceful-shutdown test racing the 100 ms budget
body:
## What

`shutdown_deadline_allows_graceful_exit` (and its timerless twin) failed once in CI on an unrelated PR (run 44498714364).

## Root cause

The test builds its fixture client with the 100 ms `BUDGET` that the other tests use to prove the deadline is tight. This test checks the opposite: a prompt graceful exit reports success. The fixture is a re-executed test binary that must wake, read and parse the request, reply and exit, all inside the same 100 ms wall-clock budget. On a loaded CI host that can overrun, and the production deadline then correctly returns an interrupted error. The shutdown code is behaving as designed; the test coupled a success-path assertion to a tight real-time budget.

## Fix

Give the graceful-exit test a 30 s budget. It still returns as soon as the child exits, so it stays fast. The tight-deadline behaviour stays covered by the other shutdown tests, which keep `BUDGET`.

## Verification

- 200 runs each of the test, old and new code, under heavy CPU contention (64 spinning processes): 0 failures both ways. I could not reproduce the flake locally, so this is not a before/after proof. The cause is from reading the test and the deadline code.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix` passes.

For users: no behaviour change; this removes an intermittent CI failure.

title: fix(ci): fail the release digest job when the alert intake refuses the post
body:
The "CD: Unreleased Changes Digest" workflow posts to the alert intake with `curl -s`. When the repository secret `ALERTMANAGER_INTAKE_TOKEN` is stale, the intake answers 401, the job still prints "Slack digest sent." and the alert is dropped. This is why `AlertIntakeBadCredential` fired and nobody saw a red run.

This change makes curl fail the job on an HTTP error (`--fail-with-body`, 30 s timeout), so a wrong password shows as a failed run. It does not change the secret; the secret needs the current value of the `alertmanager/intake-token` password (set by hand, see the monitoring runbook in the cloud repo).

Plain words: a rejected release digest now shows as a red run instead of silently disappearing.

`bin/ci --quick --fix`: 4 passed.

title: A message to a named agent is delivered twice: once directly, once as a `[thread #N from …]` turn
body:
### What happens

Since Cua Spaces 0.36.25, every `cua agent send NAME TEXT` (or the `tell` alias)
that follows up on an agent's existing run is delivered to the agent twice:

1. a turn with the text as sent
2. a few seconds later, a second turn with the same text wrapped as
   `[thread #N from <account owner>] <text>` plus the
   "(Everything you write between tool calls is posted to this thread ...)" footer

The agent answers the same message twice. The first turn of a fresh run is not doubled.

### Expected

One turn per `agent send`.

### Versions

- Cua Spaces 0.38.13 (bundled cua 0.28.3). Also on 0.36.25 (bundled cua 0.27.7).
- Not on 0.13.0, the version in use before 0.36.25.
- Linux x86_64 (Arch), local container Spaces, harness `pi`.
- Named agents created before the 0.36 update, each in its own Space.

### How to reproduce

1. Have a named agent with an idle run in a local Space.
2. From the host: `cua agent send NAME "hello"` once.
3. `cua agent logs SPACE RUN_ID --json` and look at the `turn_started` events.

### Evidence

`turn_started` / `turn_ended` events from one run after a single send
(times local, prompt text removed):

    09:03:34 turn_started 8  <text as sent>
    09:03:38 turn_ended   8
    09:03:38 turn_started 9  [thread #736 from <account owner>] <same text> (Everything you write ...
    09:03:40 turn_ended   9

The sender logged one send. In one session of 40 host-sent turns, 39 got a
wrapped copy; the one without was the first turn of the run.

### Impact

Every message costs a second model turn. An agent that does not notice the
repeat could act twice on one instruction.

### Question

Is the thread copy intended to replace the direct turn? If so, is there a way
for `agent send` to deliver only one of the two?

title: fix(spaces): deliver agent messages once
body:
Fixes #8216

## What changed for users
`cua agent send` (and `tell`) now delivers each message to an agent once. Before, a follow-up to an idle run also arrived a second time as a wrapped thread turn.

## Root cause
`send_as_entry` delivers the message straight to the idle run, then writes the thread entry that records it as a queued task and claims it in a second step. Writing the entry wakes the dispatcher. The dispatcher reads the run as idle until its runner picks the message up, sees the task queued, and its `claim()` on a task already claimed by the same session succeeds (a same-session claim is a renewal). So it delivered the same text again as a wrapped turn. A fresh run was not doubled because it reads as running at once.

## Fix
- `ThreadStore::append_claimed` writes the task entry already claimed and working, in one write under the thread lock. It is never visible as queued.
- `ThreadStore::claim_queued` is used by the dispatcher's `deliver`: it refuses a task that is no longer queued, so a same-session claim cannot be taken as a renewal.

## Tests
- `claims::tests::a_task_written_claimed_is_never_queued_and_cannot_be_claimed_again` (unit)
- `agent_sessions::a_message_sent_to_an_idle_run_is_delivered_once` (integration, dispatcher ticking while `agent_send` runs)

`bin/ci --quick --fix` passes; full `cargo test -p cua-spaces-ext` passes.

title: fix(cua-driver): reopen running apps with launch_app
body:
Salvaged from #6198

## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `launch_app` sends `aevt/oapp` on every background launch. When the app is already running but its window was closed, minimized or hidden, many apps (Electron in particular) ignore `oapp`, so the call returns a pid with no window on screen.
- What changed: when the target is already running and `creates_new_application_instance` is false, `launch_app` now attaches `aevt/rapp` (`kAEReopenApplication`), which is the event a Dock click sends. Cold launches, new instances and URL handoffs keep `oapp`. `activates = false` and the focus-steal suppression are unchanged. The bundle-ID and name paths share one config builder.

maxvint's three commits are kept as authored. On top: the cherry-pick resolves a conflict with main's `launch_located` rename, one commit drops a unit test that built the same config twice and compared it to itself, and one makes the E2E's harness guard own the spawned app before its readiness wait, so a launch timeout no longer leaks it.

## Related work

Refs #6198

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. `launch_app` on an already-running app now reopens its window (unhides or creates one, as the app's reopen handler decides) instead of returning with no window. Windows and Linux launch paths are untouched; this fixes the macOS adapter's own event choice and does not change the shared contract.
- Risk and rollback: an app with a custom reopen handler may do something other than show its main window. Revert the PR to go back to `oapp` for every launch.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` covers the event selection (running → `rapp`, cold → `oapp`, new instance → `oapp`). The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass.

title: feat(cua-driver): support Helium profile attachment on Linux and macOS
body:
Salvaged from #3253 by @saatvik333. Their commits are kept as authored; the merge of main and the fixes on top are ours.

Fixes #3252

## Why

Cua Driver classified Helium as an unknown browser, so existing-profile attachment refused before it looked for an endpoint. This PR recognizes Helium as a Chromium-family standalone browser on Linux and macOS and resolves its default profile directory.

## What changed

- Linux and macOS identify Helium (exact `helium` executable basename; bundle id `net.imput.helium` and its helpers, never the app name alone), treat it as a standalone consumer, and resolve its default profile (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/net.imput.helium`, falling back to `~/.config/net.imput.helium`, and `~/Library/Application Support/net.imput.helium`).
- Helium attaches only through its own PID-owned `DevToolsActivePort`. Existing-profile discovery never falls back to `/json/version` for it, and it has no setup descriptor, so a profile with no endpoint refuses.
- On Linux, Helium helpers write their command line as one space-joined record. Role detection reads `--type=` from it. A packed record that names `--user-data-dir` refuses, because that text cannot be told apart from the same text inside a file name or URL. #3253 accepted it when the process held the profile's `SingletonSocket`, but anyone can plant that symlink and point it at the browser's real socket. A packed record that names no profile uses the default one. Every other process keeps NUL-delimited parsing.
- The standalone browser E2E suite accepts `CUA_E2E_BROWSER_PRODUCTS=helium`. The Linux X11 standalone lane and the hosted macOS browser lane install pinned Helium 0.18.1.1 builds checked against their SHA-256 digests.

Merging main: main moved Linux default profiles onto the browser's own `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, added Brave, and folded macOS discovery into `discover_endpoint`. Helium now uses each of those. The macOS no-legacy rule for Helium lives in `discover_endpoint` for the existing-profile path. Main deleted the docs pages the PR edited, so the Helium notes moved to `cua-driver/guides/browsers.mdx` and `cua-driver/concepts/platform-support.mdx`.

## Scope

Linux and macOS only. Helium is not recognized on Windows. Automated setup through Helium's internal page is not part of this change.

## Tradeoffs

A Helium main process whose command line arrives packed and names a custom `--user-data-dir` cannot attach. Chromium rewrites the command line of its helpers, not of the main browser, so this should reach only helper records, which refuse by role anyway. The Linux Helium E2E lane checks this with a real Helium.

## Blast Radius

The change affects Cua Driver browser classification and existing-profile discovery. Chrome, Edge, Chromium and Brave keep their current paths: the packed-argv recovery and the no-legacy rule apply only when `/proc/<pid>/exe` or the macOS bundle resolves to Helium. `BrowserProduct` gains a public `helium` variant.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): 7 passed. Skipped: clippy, unit tests, generated references and the Windows cross-check (quick mode), plus actionlint and crane (not installed on this host).
- Clippy, the other crates' unit tests and the Windows cross-check run in CI.
- `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib browser_platform`: 24 passed. Disabling the new packed-profile refusal fails both refusal tests.
- The Linux standalone browser lane with Helium and the full hosted macOS matrix were dispatched on the final head.
- [x] `bin/ci --quick` passes (shared host)

title: fix(cua-driver): cover Hyprland cursor overlay focus isolation with a live test
body:
Salvaged from #3465

## Why
The native Wayland cursor overlay landed in #3152 and #3572, but nothing checks that it stays out of Hyprland's focus. This adds @LikelyLucid's live regression for that, with the fixes it needed to pass the repository's test inventory rules.

## What changed
- `hyprland_overlay_focus_test` (LikelyLucid's commit, kept as authored): an `#[ignore]`d live test. It starts a source-built daemon, enables and moves the agent cursor, then asserts one `cua-agent-cursor` layer-shell surface per monitor, no Hyprland client owned by the daemon, and no change to the active workspace or window.
- Our commits on top: the SPDX header and a `manual-e2e-allowlist.txt` entry (without one, `test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py` fails). A `Drop` guard stops the daemon and restores focus even when a call panics. Before, a failed call leaked the daemon and its fixed `/tmp` socket, and the next run refused to start. The daemon gets an `IsolatedStateRoot`, with its socket inside, and every socket read and write has a deadline.
- Stronger assertions: the test subscribes to Hyprland's event socket before launch and fails on any `openwindow`, `activewindowv2` or `workspacev2` event, so a focus steal that gets restored before the final snapshot is still caught. A closed or failing event socket fails the test. It also requires exactly one overlay layer on every enabled output, not a matching total.

## Scope
Test-only. Needs Hyprland 0.48 or later (the test checks), since older releases leave `pid` out of `hyprctl -j layers`. Native Hyprland has no automated lane, so the test is a manual gate next to the other Hyprland rows in the allowlist. No product code changes.

## Verification
- `.github/scripts/tests/test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py`: fails on LikelyLucid's commit alone (unlisted ignored test), passes with ours.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): SPDX, rustfmt and image-ref checks pass. Clippy, unit tests and the Windows cross-check are left to CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): preserve physical pixels in the embedded Windows SDK
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows at more than 100% scaling, the in-process SDK inherits the host's DPI awareness. In a DPI-unaware host such as Node, `get_screen_size` and `get_desktop_state` report and capture the virtualized desktop (`1707x1067 @ 1.0` instead of `2560x1600 @ 1.5`). The standalone `cua-driver.exe` and `cua-spacesd` are unaffected because their manifests declare Per-Monitor V2.
- What changed:
  - Every thread of the SDK's own ABI executor switches itself to Per-Monitor V2 when it starts, including blocking-pool threads added later. The overlay and UIA enumeration threads and the recorder's application-state hook do the same. The host process and its threads keep their own context.
  - If Windows rejects the context, `cua_driver_create_v1` and in-process creation fail with `RuntimeUnavailable`, so callers never get virtualized pixels.
  - On Windows, trusted-adapter calls now run on the ABI executor instead of the caller's runtime, with cancel-on-drop kept. Other platforms keep the caller's runtime, so the executor's blocking threads do not outlive `cua-driver serve` (the Linux server Memcheck run catches that).
  - The recording cursor sampler reads `GetPhysicalCursorPos`.

Salvaged from #3450. @wszkxlllll's commits are kept as authored. On top of them, this merges main and slims the fix down. The PR's sticky-failure layer is removed: per-poll future guards, a thread-local owner registry, a recorder initializer hook in `cua-driver-core`, capture entry checks, and about 100 `spawn_blocking` call sites rewritten to a guarded wrapper. All of it guarded against a thread created after a successful startup failing to enter Per-Monitor V2. `SetThreadDpiAwarenessContext` rejects that context only when the OS lacks it, and that cannot change while the process runs. The constructor that injected those failures existed only for tests, which the repository's test rules do not allow in shipped code.

## Related work

Fixes #3449

RFC: not required; no public SDK, ABI or tool schema change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Windows embedded SDK callers in a DPI-unaware or system-aware host now get physical-pixel screen size, screenshots and coordinates, matching the daemon. On a Windows build without Per-Monitor V2 (before Windows 10 1703), embedded creation now fails with `RuntimeUnavailable` instead of returning virtualized results. macOS and Linux are unchanged: everything new is Windows-only.
- Risk and rollback: Windows only, embedded mode only. In the manifested executables every thread is already Per-Monitor V2, so setting it again changes nothing. Roll back by reverting this PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `abi::tests::abi_executor_threads_use_per_monitor_v2_including_late_workers`: an async worker, a blocking worker the pool creates after startup, and a child thread started through `dpi::owned_thread` all run in Per-Monitor V2.
  - `dpi::tests::owned_thread_uses_per_monitor_v2_without_changing_the_spawning_thread`.
  - `tests::dropping_trusted_adapter_call_cancels_shared_abi_operation`: covers the new trusted-adapter routing.
  - The ignored desktop test `tests::embedded_abi_uses_physical_pixels_from_an_unaware_host_thread` (from #3450) runs in the Windows capture lane. From a DPI-unaware host thread it checks screen size, desktop PNG dimensions and scale for regular and trusted calls, and that the host thread's context is unchanged.
- Manual or platform evidence: the canonical Windows run (`e2e-rust-windows.yml`, all lanes) passed at c34dce32f51b3347647bfd0b8054d7a88d9660b0: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/44598628546. The capture lane ran `embedded_abi_uses_physical_pixels_from_an_unaware_host_thread`, which passed. The native lane's first attempt failed in fixture setup of `minimized_window_is_listed_and_bring_to_front_restores_it`: the test's own `ShowWindow(SW_MINIMIZE)` never made the window iconic, before any driver call. A rerun of that lane at the same SHA passed. Linux and macOS behavior is unchanged. The scoped repository checks ran locally with `bin/ci --quick` (SPDX, lockfiles, rustfmt, bin/ci tests, image refs) and `.github/scripts/tests/test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py`.
- Known gaps or CI still required: nothing here was compiled for Windows locally; the host had too little disk for the cross-compiled check. In PR CI, Windows clippy, the three Windows Rust shards and the Linux server Memcheck run passed. Testing at 100% and 150% scaling on Server 2025, which #3450 left open, is still outstanding.

title: fix(cua-driver): sample the Hyprland cursor for recordings with a bounded socket query
body:
## Why

On Linux, recordings write an empty `cursor.jsonl`, so the zoom renderer can only follow click points. Hyprland can report the pointer position through its instance socket, so on Hyprland the sampler now asks for it. The query has a time limit, and stopping a recording cancels a query that is still running.

## What changed

- On Linux, `sample_cursor` sends a non-blocking `j/cursorpos` request to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket.sock`. Connect, write and read all share a 100ms deadline, and the read stops early when the sampler's stop flag is set. Inter-sample sleeps also check the stop flag.
- Session selection: a non-Wayland `XDG_SESSION_TYPE`, or a desktop that is not Hyprland, turns the query off even when a `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` was inherited from a parent session. A nonempty `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` takes precedence over `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP`.
- Replies that are not JSON objects, or that hold non-finite `x`/`y`, are dropped. The sampler also skips non-finite samples on every platform, so `cursor.jsonl` stays valid JSON.

## Scope

Covers only the cursor telemetry written during recordings. It does not add a LinuxObserver, the `Cursor` oracle for native cases, background pointer injection, or cursor support for Sway, GNOME or KWin. Those compositors still write no samples. The module docs also correct an old claim that X11 uses `XQueryPointer`: no X11 poll exists.

## Blast Radius

The change is limited to `cua-driver-core`'s `cursor_sampler.rs` on Linux. Windows and macOS sampling only gain the `stop` parameter and the finite-value filter. When Hyprland is not running, or the socket is missing or busy, the sample is skipped, so the output matches the old empty file.

## Verification

- The author ran `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib --locked` on Linux ARM64 and on a native Omarchy / Hyprland 0.56.2 session. Both passed, including the 10 new `linux_cursor_tests`, which cover the socket deadline, a full socket backlog, stop and drop during a stalled query, desktop precedence, and malformed replies. On that session, a read-only `j/cursorpos` query returned finite coordinates.
- `bin/ci --quick` passed on this branch (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs). The scoped repository checks (clippy, unit tests, the Windows cross-check) run in CI.

Salvaged from #3553. Thanks @austindixson: their three commits are kept as authored, main is merged on top, and one commit of ours follows. title: fix(cua-driver): scroll Chromium windows in the background on Windows
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, a background `scroll` in a Chromium window (Chrome, Edge, Electron apps such as VS Code or Slack) returns `background_unavailable` before any route is tried, and the refusal recommends `delivery_mode:"foreground"`. The foreground route sends a `SendInput` wheel at a screen point, so it lands on whatever window is under that point when each notch arrives. When the user switches apps while an agent scrolls, the remaining notches scroll the user's app.
- What changed: a background scroll in a Chromium window now goes through UIA `ScrollPattern`, the same accessibility channel the indexed WebView2/Tauri path already uses. The container is the indexed element or its nearest scrollable ancestor, or, without an `element_token`, the window's web `Document` (else the first element that scrolls along the requested axis). `by` maps to small or large increments. An indexed scroll in any window also walks up to the nearest scrollable ancestor instead of requiring `ScrollPattern` on the element itself. A Chromium window with no scrollable UIA element still returns `background_unavailable`, and a background Chromium scroll never falls through to the `WM_VSCROLL` message path.

## Related work

Refs #5281 (element-token scroll targeting; this PR does not change the macOS path)

RFC: not required; no public contract changes. The tool schema is unchanged; only the Windows `scroll` description now documents the UIA route.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Windows only. Background scrolls in Chromium windows succeed instead of being refused; `uia::scroll::scroll_element` is replaced by `uia::scroll::scroll_window`, which is crate-internal.
- Risk and rollback: UIA scrolling is programmatic: the page receives `scroll` events without `wheel` events. Revert this commit to restore the previous refusal.

## Validation

- Focused checks: `cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `platform-windows` with `--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (C dependencies stubbed for type-checking on macOS), `cargo fmt --check`, and `bin/ci` (Windows cfg, SPDX headers, rustfmt, image refs passed; clippy, unit tests, generated reference and bindings were skipped by its low-disk guard and are left to CI).
- Manual or platform evidence: none yet. I have not run this on a Windows machine.
- Known gaps: no Rust harness test observes the fixture scroll offset on Windows. Whether a backgrounded or occluded Chrome window honors `ScrollPattern.Scroll` needs a Windows run.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained. (Gap explained above.)

title: fix(spaces-macos): send the right ⌘ held alone as Super to Linux and Windows guests
body:
## Why

A Mac viewer maps ⌘ to Control for a Linux or Windows guest, so no key produced Super, and Super shortcuts such as Hyprland's could not be typed. The right ⌘ held without the left one now goes as Super. The left ⌘ still goes as Control.

## What changed

- spacesd-html5: `MediaSession` and the standalone viewer's `InputController` share a new `CommandKeys` tracker. After every key event, it presses and releases the guest's Super or Control to match the ⌘ keys held. If the left ⌘ joins a held right ⌘, Super is released before Control goes down. When the left ⌘ is released, Super comes back. Focus loss releases the guest's keys once, and a ⌘ still held is pressed again with the next key. On such a guest, right ⌘V and ⌘C are Super chords and skip the host clipboard paste and copy paths. In the standalone viewer, a Super chord goes down and up together (Chromium may drop the letter's key-up under ⌘). While a paste chord waits for the clipboard, ⌘ changes and a second ⌘V wait behind it, so Super never comes back before Control+V. Once anything waits there, later input waits too, so it keeps its order. The wait is capped at 2 s, the native viewer's paste wait. Until something waits, other keys go at once, as before.
- spaces-macos: `InputEncoder` reads the device-side ⌘ bits and marks a right-only ⌘ as `InputModifier.super`. `commandAsControl` leaves it alone and the wire sends it as `command`, so the guest gets Super. `LiveStreamSession.paste` sends a Super chord as plain input on a guest that takes ⌘ as Control. A macOS guest still pastes.
- cua-driver (Windows): the key and modifier name `super`, which cua-spacesd sends for Command and which the Linux and macOS drivers already accept, now maps to the Windows key. Before this, Windows dropped it, so Super shortcuts reached a Windows guest without the Windows key.
- Docs: the viewer keyboard sections in `apps/cua-spaces-desktop/docs/video.md` and `apps/cua-spaces-macos/docs/native-video.md`.

## Scope

Covers the web viewer, the Electron shell's `MediaSession`, and the native Mac viewer on Linux and Windows guests. On macOS guests ⌘ still goes as Command. Remapping keys inside the guest is out of scope.

## Tradeoffs

A browser reports only that some ⌘ is held, not which one. After a focus change, the viewer assumes the ⌘ held before it is still down until the next ⌘ press or a key without ⌘. So if the user swaps ⌘ keys while the viewer is unfocused, the first chord uses the old side. A ⌘ pressed before the viewer had focus goes as Control, as before.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks:
- `vitest run` in `cua-spacesd-html5/web`: 101 tests pass. `CommandKeys` has its own tests: Super and Control swapping as ⌘ keys join and leave, focus loss, and macOS guests. Each viewer has one wiring test, Super+V has a test showing it skips the paste path, and other tests cover ⌘ changes during a held paste and a clipboard that never arrives. Mutating the tracker breaks these tests. `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` pass, and the rebuilt `assets/viewer.js` is committed.
- `bin/ci --quick`: passes.
- `swift build` of `libs/spaces-app-swift`: passes. The Swift test targets (`ViewerInputTests`, including the new `aSuperChordIsNotAPaste`) need Xcode's Swift Testing module, so they run in CI's macOS lanes, not on the authoring host.
- The Windows driver's new unit test (`super_names_the_windows_key`) compiles only for Windows and runs in CI's Windows lane.
- Not run: a live Super shortcut on a Linux or Windows guest.

Fixes #5345

title: feat(spaces): change or turn off the macOS global shortcut
body:
## Why

Settings' Change sent the recorded keys as the global-shortcut row, but the SwiftUI host dropped that row and always registered Command-Shift-Space, ignoring the settings file's `hotkey`.

## What changed

- macOS host: registers the recorded keys before it lets go of the old ones, saves them as `hotkey`, starts from a hand-edited `hotkey`, and can turn the shortcut off to free the keys. Keys another app holds leave the old shortcut and fail with why, including when Settings re-chooses the current keys while another app still holds them.
- General's shortcut row gets Turn off, which sends the global-shortcut option `off`; the row then reads Off.
- The Electron host and the demo adapter take the same option; the Electron host remembers it as no keys.

## Scope

Covers the global-shortcut row on the macOS SwiftUI host, the web Settings page, the Electron host and the demo adapter. Leaves out everything else in Settings.

## Blast Radius

Only the one global shortcut. A failed registration keeps the old keys, so a refused change never leaves the app without a shortcut it had.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed. The web tests (settings-shortcut, shortcut-keys, host-labels), the Electron `global-shortcut` tests and the bridge and router contracts passed locally. The macOS Swift tests (`WebUIHostTests`, including the new `reChoosingTakenKeysSaysTheyAreTaken`) run in the macOS SwiftUI CI lane; they cannot link on the dev host without the Rust SDK build. Windows and Linux Electron and a live conflict with another app's hotkey were not run.

Fixes #7412

title: feat(spaces): send Super from the right ⌘ to Linux and Windows Spaces
body:
## Why

A Mac viewer sent both ⌘ keys to a Linux or Windows Space as Control. Nothing reached the guest as Super, so desktops driven by Super (Hyprland on Omarchy) could not be used from the keyboard. The left ⌘ still goes as Control. The right ⌘ held alone now goes as Super.

## What changed

- Native viewer: `InputEncoder.modifiers(from:)` reads the device ⌘ bits and reports the right ⌘ held alone as `InputModifier.superKey`. `commandAsControl` leaves `superKey` alone, and it goes on the wire as `command`.
- HTML5 viewer and the app's web session: `CommandSides` tracks which ⌘ is held, and `metaAsControl` is skipped while only the right ⌘ is down. `viewer.js` is rebuilt.
- On a Linux or Windows Space the right ⌘+V goes as Super+V in every viewer, not through the host paste path. A macOS Space still pastes from it. The web viewers forget which ⌘ is held when they lose focus, so a ⌘ released elsewhere does not change the next chord.
- The viewer docs say the right ⌘ held alone goes as Super.

## Scope

This covers a Mac viewing a Linux or Windows Space. A macOS guest, and viewers that are not on a Mac, behave as before. Pointer modifiers are unchanged. #8234 overlaps this work and is left open.

## Blast Radius

Mac users of the native viewer, the desktop app and the HTML5 viewer who press the right ⌘ alone with a Linux or Windows Space. Chords that also use the left ⌘ still go as Control.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass at the head.
- New unit tests: `ViewerInputTests` (Swift), `input.test.ts` and `mediaSession.test.ts` (vitest) cover the right ⌘ alone as Super, the left ⌘ as Control, focus loss and the right ⌘+V.

- [x] `bin/ci` (quick) run before push

Fixes #5345

title: fix(cua-driver): bind Hyprland Chrome windows by scaled size
body:
Chromium on Wayland reports every window at 0,0 and sizes it in its own scaled units, so bounds never matched the compositor rect. With more than one Chrome window the bind fell back to a read-only title match. Hyprland now reports the size of every client the browser pid owns. Core pairs every native window one-to-one with every CDP window under a single common scale and binds exactly only when that pairing is unique.

When titles cannot pair them, BrowserRootView frames now pair with the pid's Hyprland clients by the same unique common-scale pairing; this also covers grouped Chrome tabs whose accessible frame title carries tab-group and profile text the compositor title lacks. A scaled-size bind is kept when other Chrome windows share a size if every valid common-scale pairing gives the target the same partner. The overlay arrival-cap test is gated on the desktop the overlay checks.

Fixes #4931

title: fix(cua-spaces): clarify sign-in sharing in local and remote Spaces
body:
## Summary

A connected Claude Code account on the host can still leave a local Space/VM without a sign-in: sharing is off by default, but the switch was grouped under “On another computer” and the failure only said to connect Claude again.

Give sharing its own **Sign-ins in Spaces** section and label it **Use saved sign-ins in Spaces**. Explain that it covers local Spaces/VMs and remote Spaces. Claude Code and Codex authentication errors in a Space explain that the Space needs a working sign-in. When sharing is off, the error offers a link to the setting alongside the existing Space sign-in and API-key actions. The link scrolls to the section after Connections finishes loading.

## User and business impact

A user can complete Claude Code sign-in, see **Connected**, and still be blocked from starting an agent in a local VM. 

_Placing the required sharing switch under **On another computer** suggests it only applies to a separate physical machine, so users running a VM on the same Mac have little reason to look there_. The generic error then tells them to connect Claude again even though their host credentials are valid.

This blocks the first successful agent run and can lead to repeated login attempts, unnecessary credential troubleshooting, and support requests. Naming local Spaces/VMs explicitly and linking the failure to the relevant setting gives users a direct recovery path while keeping sign-in sharing an explicit choice.

## Related work

Small, self-contained correction reported with screenshots. No matching open sign-in-sharing PR found. No public API, credential-delivery, permission, or default-setting changes; no RFC required.

title: fix(cua-vmm): wait for a starting container engine; name and retry its failed pings
body:
## Why
In the field, `engine_error` is the biggest group of macOS Local Space create failures: 148 failures across 49 people with `failed_step=unknown`, plus 59 across 33 at `create_container` (PostHog, real users 25 Oct to 19 Nov, CI and synthetic excluded). `engine_error` is the catch-all for any container-engine API error, so the telemetry could not say more.

One cause that fits the code: a container engine whose socket accepts connections but does not answer the API yet (Colima's VM or Docker Desktop still starting). `Engine::connect` pinged once, failed the create at once with `did not answer ping`, reported `failed_step=unknown`, and the app did not retry because that failure had no subclass.

## Change
- `Engine::connect` pings up to five times, two seconds apart, when the socket accepts but does not answer, instead of failing on the first ping. A socket that is not accepting still fails at once.
- `did not answer ping` is the `runtime_start` subclass, so the app runs the create once more by itself and the failure reports `failed_step=start_runtime`.
- An `engine_error` in the `preparing` phase reports `failed_step=start_runtime` (getting the engine ready) instead of `unknown`. In `creating` it stays `create_container`.

## Not covered
I could not reproduce on cua.local: that machine was not reachable in this session, so nothing here was driven against a real engine. The fix is from reading the code, and each change has a unit test. Other engine API errors (a create conflict, for one) stay `engine_error` and are not retried. The error text is never sent in telemetry, so the remaining `engine_error` cases need a finer subclass word to be told apart; that is a telemetry-schema change left for a decision.

## Test
- `cargo test -p cua-create-failure --lib`: 36 pass, including the new ping classification and retry test
- `cargo test -p cua-telemetry --test privacy`: 47 pass, with the new step assertions
- `cargo test -p cua-vmm --lib --features container a_slow_engine`: passes
- `bin/ci --signoff`: 7 checks passed. The Windows cross-build warned: `audiopus_sys` could not be cross-built on this Mac, so the crates that need it were not checked for Windows; every other crate passed.

title: fix(vmm): a Windows PC without Docker is not told to install Docker Desktop
body:
## What
On a clean Windows PC, creating a local Linux Space stopped at "Install Docker Desktop to run Linux computers" (`runtime_missing`) before the built-in Linux runtime was ever tried.

## Why
`cua_vmm::preflight::engine_required()` said a missing container engine blocks a Linux create everywhere except macOS. The built-in runtime (a WSL 2 distribution with Docker inside) shipped for Windows on 6 Nov (#6740), but this check was never widened.

Reproduced on a fresh Windows Server 2025 PC with cua 0.28.5: `cua runtime doctor` lists the built-in runtime, then `cua spaces create linux` refuses with the Docker Desktop message. In PostHog it is the largest create failure on Windows: 127 failures across 52 people since 10 Nov, on app versions that have the built-in runtime.

## Change
`engine_required()` now skips the engine requirement wherever the built-in runtime stands in (macOS and Windows), unless the setting says `system`. The rule is a small pure function with a test.

## Not in this PR
A Windows PC without WSL 2 still needs WSL turned on; the follow-up PR makes that one step in the app (a single Windows prompt) instead of a manual one. This PR only stops the wrong "install Docker Desktop" refusal.

## Test
- `cargo test -p cua-vmm --lib --features container preflight`: 8 pass, including the new truth-table test.
- `bin/ci --signoff`: 7 checks pass on macOS. Windows-only code is covered by CI's Windows lane (a Mac cannot cross-build one audio crate).

title: fix(spaces): Windows sets up WSL 2 in one step; Docker Desktop is never offered
body:
## What
Local Linux Spaces on Windows run in a runtime Cua Spaces manages itself (a WSL 2 distribution with Docker inside, #6740), like the built-in runtime on a Mac. New Space still offered to download and install Docker Desktop (about 600 MB, a license screen, a restart) when WSL 2 was not set up, and the troubleshooting and quickstart docs said the same.

## Change
- **One step.** The New Space fix is now "Set up Linux support": one Windows (UAC) prompt runs `wsl --install --no-distribution --web-download`. No distribution, no Docker.
- **Restart.** When Windows needs one, New Space says so and registers Cua Spaces to open again by itself after it (a RunOnce entry), where the built-in runtime takes over.
- **Virtualization off** still says how to turn it on, or to use another computer.
- **Docker Desktop is never offered.** A person who wants their own engine picks it in Settings, Runtimes. The "not installed" and "not running" Docker Desktop copy is gone from the reason text and the docs (quickstart, troubleshooting).
- Runtime fix actions are `setup-wsl`, `restart-app`, `open-windows-features`; the web contract and generated bridge shapes follow.

Pairs with #8242 (the pre-create check no longer refuses a Windows PC without Docker).

## Test
- `windows-runtime.test.ts` rewritten for the new flow (26 desktop tests pass with `local-runtime.test.ts`): one UAC prompt, restart plus RunOnce, declined prompt, no result written, no mention of Docker anywhere in the advice.
- `bin/ci --signoff`: typecheck (desktop, web), desktop tests and router contract, web tests and bridge contract, design lint, docs checks, lockfiles pass.

## Verified on a clean Windows 11 PC
Windows 11 Enterprise evaluation (build 26200) under KVM on AWS, WSL not installed, Cua Spaces 0.38.16 with this branch's app code on top.
- New Space shows the reason and **Set up Linux support**, with no Docker Desktop anywhere.
- One UAC prompt, then "Setting up…".
- Setup turned out not to be enough to continue: the WSL package answers `wsl --version` as soon as it is installed, so the app's own engine looked ready while Windows still had to restart for the Virtual Machine Platform, and **Continue** was enabled. Fixed in this PR (2d9b7365d): while the setup's own restart is outstanding the wizard says "Restart this PC to finish setting up Linux support" and keeps Continue off. A pending update elsewhere does not block it.
- After the restart Cua Spaces opened again by itself (RunOnce), the warning was gone, and New Space went through.
- Creating the Linux computer then needs #8242 (merged); with it, a nightly app on the same PC created Ubuntu 24.04 and streamed its desktop.

After a restart the app opens again by itself but does not finish the create the person had started; they click Create again.

title: [Bug]: cua-sandbox action's cua-version install looks for linux-x64-gnu, but releases publish linux-x64
body:
`.github/actions/cua-sandbox/cua-sandbox.sh` (line ~95 on `main` @ `6c5193d`) maps Linux/x86_64 to `linux-x64-gnu` (and arm64 to `linux-arm64-gnu`). The `cua-sdk` releases publish `cua-cli-<v>-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `...-linux-arm64.tar.gz` (checked 0.28.3, 0.28.4 and 0.28.5), so `cua-version: <release>` fails on `ubuntu-latest`.

*Workaround:* download and verify the release tarball in an earlier step, then pass it as `cua-bin`.

*Suggested fix:* drop the `-gnu` suffix, or publish assets under both names. Happy to open a PR.

Example workflow: https://github.com/waellerbe/hello-cowork/blob/main/.github/workflows/cua-sandbox-starter.yml

title: [Bug]: linux sandbox image doesn't include the cua-driver binary
body:
With the `cua-sandbox` action (`image: linux`, `on: local`), `cua-driver` isn't on PATH in the guest. `libs/images/linux/Dockerfile` (`main` @ `6c5193d`) mentions cua-driver only in comments. The image ships `cua-spacesd` and Chromium, but not the driver its browser tools depend on.

*Workaround:* overlay the `cua-driver-rs` v0.54.0 Linux binary (`overlay: cua-driver=<path>:/usr/local/bin/cua-driver`) and start `cua-driver serve` in the guest.

Is the driver meant to be baked into the image, or is overlaying it the intended path? If it's the latter, a note in the action README would help.

Example workflow: https://github.com/waellerbe/hello-cowork/blob/main/.github/workflows/cua-sandbox-starter.yml

title: Background keyboard input unavailable in the linux sandbox (no /dev/uinput)
body:
In the `linux` sandbox (X11, `on: local` on `ubuntu-latest`), cua-driver v0.54.0 `type_text` returns `background_unavailable`. The hint says X11 background keyboard delivery needs a uinput-backed virtual keyboard, and the guest has no `/dev/uinput`.

*Workaround:* retry with `delivery_mode: foreground`, which works.

Is there a supported way to give the sandbox `/dev/uinput`, for example a create flag or a device passthrough option for the action? Related: #3550.

Example workflow: https://github.com/waellerbe/hello-cowork/blob/main/.github/workflows/cua-sandbox-starter.yml

title: [Bug]: cua-sandbox action uploads with a Node 20 actions/upload-artifact
body:
`action.yml` (line ~239 on `main` @ `6c5193d`) pins `actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8...` (v4), which targets Node 20. Every run that uses it shows GitHub's deprecation warning: "Node.js 20 is deprecated ... being forced to run on Node.js 24."

*Workaround:* `upload-artifacts: "false"`, then upload `steps.<id>.outputs.artifacts-dir` with `actions/upload-artifact@cf430e0...` (v7.0.2, Node 24).

*Suggested fix:* bump the pin to v7.x. Happy to open a PR.

title: fix(release): repair a release branch that rewrote another component's manifest version
body:
Release PR #8209 (cua-driver-rs 0.55.0) failed `contract`, `validate`, `test` and `ci-gate` with one cause: its manifest had `libs/cua-spacesd` at 0.16.4 while main and the registry say 0.16.5.

Release Please wrote that stale line in its release commit. The line applied cleanly on main, so the rebase decision said "keep" and the replay had nothing to reconcile.

What changes:
- `release_branch_needs_rebase.py`: rebase when the branch itself rewrote another component's manifest entry.
- `replay_release_branch.sh`: after every replay, restore main's versions for components the branch does not own, in a follow-up commit.
- Tests for both.

For users: no change; this keeps release PRs mergeable without hand edits.

After this merges, the release-please run on main replays #8209 and fixes its manifest. No hand edit of #8209.

title: [Bug]: Windows Cua Spaces app never writes `spaces-control.json`, so `open_space_viewer` / `show_space_pip` fail with "Cua Spaces app isn't running"
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### Summary

On Windows, the Cua Spaces app is running but `%USERPROFILE%\.cua\spaces-control.json` is never created. Every MCP tool that needs the operator display (`open_space_viewer`, `show_space_pip`, `hide_space_pip`) fails with "the Cua Spaces app isn't running". This looks like the Windows side of #6339, which was fixed for the macOS app in #6342; the Windows app 0.38.16 still shows it.

### Reproduction

1. Start Cua Spaces on Windows 11 and wait until its window is open.
2. Connect an agent to `cua mcp` (here: Hermes Agent).
3. `create_space` with `{"on": "local"}`. The Space is created and `space_bash` works in it.
4. Call `open_space_viewer` or `show_space_pip` with that Space's id.

### Expected behavior

The app writes `spaces-control.json` at launch and the viewer or PiP opens. If PiP is not supported on Windows, the tool says that instead of reporting the app as not running.

### Actual behavior

```
error: operator_display is not available on this host: the Cua Spaces app isn't running (no control server at C:\Users\<user>\.cua\spaces-control.json: The system cannot find the file specified. (os error 2))
```

- Four `Cua Spaces.exe` processes and the app's bundled `cua.exe` daemon are running; `cua daemon status` answers.
- `%USERPROFILE%\.cua` holds `spaces.json`, `space-meta.json`, `daemon.json` and others, but no `spaces-control.json`, before and after an app restart.
- The same error comes from the standalone `cua` 0.27.0 and from the app's bundled `cua` 0.28.4, so it is not a CLI version mismatch.
- Updating the app from 0.38.15 to 0.38.16 (the signed installer relaunched the app) did not create the file; checked 45 s after launch.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, x64
- Cua Spaces app 0.38.16 (also seen on 0.38.15)
- `cua` CLI 0.27.0 (standalone install) and 0.28.4 (bundled in the app)
- Docker Engine 29.9.3; local Linux Space created with `create_space {"on": "local"}`, runtime `runc`
- Agent: Hermes Agent with `cua mcp` over stdio

### Evidence

- `open_space_viewer`, `show_space_pip` and `hide_space_pip` all return the error above for a ready local Space.
- The client side knows the protocol: the strings `/viewer/open` and `/pip/pin` are present in the app's `resources\native\cua_spaces_ffi.dll` and `resources\native\cua.exe`. They are not in `resources\app.asar`.

### Workaround and additional context

Opening the Space by hand in the Cua Spaces window works, and `cua sb view <space> --view-only` gives a browser viewer link. Agents cannot show the Space on the user's desktop themselves.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(spaces): serve the loopback control server on Windows and Linux so open_space_viewer works
body:
Fixes #8254.

## Problem
On Windows (and Linux) the Cua Spaces app is the Electron app, which never had the loopback control server the macOS app (#6342) and the Tauri app serve. It never wrote `<cua home>/spaces-control.json`, so `cua mcp`'s `open_space_viewer`, `show_space_pip` and `hide_space_pip` all reported "the Cua Spaces app isn't running" while the app was open.

## Fix
`apps/cua-spaces-desktop/src/control-server.ts` serves the same protocol as `SpacesControlServer.swift`:
- binds `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port, requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (constant-time compare);
- writes `{port, token}` to `<cua home>/spaces-control.json` (`CUA_HOME`, so Cua Spaces Local keeps its own), owner-only, by renaming a private file into place;
- removes the file on quit, and only if it is still this app's (a newer app's stays);
- `POST /viewer/open {space_id}` opens the Space's viewer window, by id or by name (a name shared by two Spaces is a 404, not a guess);
- `/pip/pin`, `/pip/unpin`, `/window/stream` answer 501, which the client reports as a status instead of "isn't running". Wiring PiP for agents is separate work.
- a server that can't start or write is logged and the app runs without it, as on macOS.

`main.ts` starts it once the model is up.

## Verified
- Before: the SDK's `HostPresentation.openViewer` against no server fails with `host_unavailable ... does not appear to be running`.
- After, with the real SDK client against this server over real HTTP: `openViewer` succeeds and opens the viewer for the right Space; an unknown Space is 404; `pin` is 501; after stop the file is gone and the client says "isn't running" again.
- `test/control-server.test.ts` (7 tests): control file contents and mode, removal on stop, a newer app's file left alone, id and name resolution, 401/400/404, 501 for PiP, bearer compare, startup failure.
- `bin/ci`: typecheck, desktop tests and router contract, prettier, SPDX headers, image refs.

Not run on a real Windows 11 PC: the code is plain Node `http` and `fs`, and no Windows-specific API is used.

title: [Bug]: macOS Space checkpoint forks time out and restarted Spaces boot unreachable behind cua-netgw
body:
### Primary area

Local Spaces: macOS (Lume) checkpoints and forks

### Summary

A new local macOS Space works. After `cua sb checkpoint` it no longer comes back: a fork of the checkpoint times out waiting for cua-spacesd, and starting the source Space again boots the VM behind `cua-netgw`, where cua-spacesd never answers. The checkpoint itself succeeds in about 2 s. This blocks a macOS Cua CI pool that starts each runner from a checkpoint (`cua ci connect --own-app --image checkpoint:<name> --os macos`).

Possibly related: #5364 (resume times out with "no route to host"). The difference here: Local Network access works on this host, because a macOS Space created before the network gateway existed (no `cua-netgw` process) stops and starts normally and answers `space_bash` 23 s after boot.

### Reproduction

1. `create_space(image="ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26", on="local", name="ckpt-probe")`: ready, cua-spacesd 0.7.0, macOS 26.5.2. A `cua-netgw -config ~/.cua/vmm/lume/ckpt-probe/netgw.json` process starts.
2. `cua sb checkpoint ckpt-probe probe-ckpt`: `Checkpoint 'probe-ckpt' of 'ckpt-probe' saved (2.16s)`. Daemon log: `checkpointed a running VM with its memory ... save_ms=869`. Afterwards `lume ls` shows `ckpt-probe` as stopped (the help says the source keeps running).
3. `cua sb fork probe-ckpt ckpt-fork`: after 3 min 23 s, `timed out: sandbox ckpt-fork: cua-spacesd did not answer within 180s (protocol error: no connection within 2.5s)`. The only daemon log line is `WARN cua_vmm::lume: could not set the guest's hostname vm=ckpt-fork`. The fork sandbox is removed afterwards (`cua sb logs ckpt-fork`: not found).
4. `start_space(local:ckpt-probe)` returns `state: running`, but `space_bash` fails with `this Space's image runs no cua-spacesd`. A `com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachine` process runs (about 6 GB RSS), `lume ls` reports the VM as stopped with no IP, `lume run ckpt-probe` says it is already running (config lock held), and a second `cua-netgw` process for `ckpt-probe` starts next to the first. Daemon log: `no Cua Volume in this Space: its cua-spacesd predates the volume`.
5. After `delete_space(local:ckpt-probe)` and `cua sb checkpoints rm probe-ckpt`, one `cua-netgw` process for the deleted Space kept running and had to be killed by hand.

### Expected behavior

A fork of a macOS checkpoint, and a restarted macOS Space, boot with a reachable cua-spacesd, as a freshly created one does. Deleting a Space ends its `cua-netgw`.

### Actual behavior

The fork times out and is removed. A restart leaves a running VM that Cua and Lume can't reach and that Lume reports as stopped. A gateway process leaks after delete.

### Environment

- cua 0.28.2, Cua Spaces app (login item), lume 0.7.0 (`lume serve` on 7777)
- Host: Mac Studio (Apple silicon), macOS 27.2.1
- Image `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26` (`sha256:7cb23670cad48a6723cf667bc63c444b83dc0c73756c23b614897127d5ba22ba`), guest cua-spacesd 0.7.0
- `cua experiments list` no longer shows Secure Spaces. With Secure Spaces on in an earlier version, macOS creates showed the same symptom: the VM on the gateway network with no IP Lume can find.
- `cua doctor`: Screen Recording and Accessibility granted. It warns about Local Network, but routing works for the older macOS Space above.

### Evidence

Log lines are quoted in the reproduction steps above. Timings: checkpoint 2.16 s with about 1.5 GB of host disk; fork timeout 180 s (3 min 23 s wall clock).

### Workaround and additional context

The workaround is a long-lived macOS runner Space that is never checkpointed. Its disk only grows, because the guest frees blocks and the host image never shrinks; ours is at 101 GB of 150 GB after about two weeks of CI. Fork-per-job is what would fix that, which is why this matters for macOS Cua CI pools.

title: ci(release): fail a PR whose squash message Release Please cannot parse
body:
Release PR #8209 (cua-driver-rs 0.55.0) failed attribution: PR #7637 was missing from its changelog.

Cause: Release Please parses the whole squash message and drops a commit it cannot parse. #7637's commit body had `Selector:(null)` inside a code span, and the parser stopped with "unexpected token '(' at 24:70". The release-please log said "commit could not be parsed", and nothing else flagged it.

This adds a PR check that builds the squash message GitHub will create (title plus each commit as a bullet) and parses it with `@conventional-commits/parser` 0.4.1, the version Release Please 17.3.0 pins (integrity-checked). A message that would be dropped now fails before merge.

For #7637 itself, I added a `BEGIN_COMMIT_OVERRIDE` block to its merged PR body, which is Release Please's supported repair. #8209 is not hand-edited; release-please regenerates it on the next push to main.

For users: no change; changes are no longer silently left out of release notes.

title: [Bug]: macOS Space creates behind cua-netgw time out: `lume ssh` can't find or reach a gateway VM
body:
### Primary area Spaces: macOS (Lume) Spaces behind `cua-netgw`, created on a host machine (`--on host:`) ### Summary Creating a macOS Space on a machine set up with `cua host setup --profile spare --no-desktop --provide-spaces` always fails after 3 minutes: ``` env: internal server error: sandbox 'agents' was not ready after 180s: could not set the sandbox environment over `lume ssh`: Error: VM 'agents' has no IP address. Wait for it to boot completely. ``` The VM itself boots and networks fine behind `cua-netgw`. The failing step is cua's guest-environment write, which runs `lume ssh `. A separate `lume ssh` process cannot find, or reach, a VM on a `gateway:` network. Possibly related: #8258 (its environment notes mention the same "gateway network with no IP Lume can find" symptom for creates). ### Reproduction 1. Host Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 26.5): cua 0.28.6 CLI plus the Cua Spaces app 0.38.16 (for `cua-netgw`), and Lume 0.7.2 from `cua runtime setup lume` (`lume serve` on 7777). `cua host setup --profile spare --no-desktop --provide-spaces --max-spaces 2 --name ` succeeds; Local Network access granted for cua-spacesd. 2. From a second enrolled Mac on the same account, run `cua --json spaces create macos:26-slim --on host: --name agents`. 3. The image pulls and the clone boots: `cua-netgw -config ~/.cua/vmm/lume/agents/netgw.json` starts, and Lume logs `VM started successfully`. After 180 s the create fails with the error above, and the VM is deleted. Reproduced three times, plus once with `runtime.vm = builtin`, which fails earlier with `lume is not available: needed to set a macOS guest's environment (lume ssh)`. ### Expected behavior cua writes the guest environment over a path that works behind the gateway, and the Space becomes ready. ### Actual behavior `sync_macos_env` retries `lume ssh` until `MACOS_ENV_BUDGET` (180 s) runs out, because every attempt fails with `noIPAddress`. ### Environment - cua 0.28.6 (`cua-sdk-v0.28.6`), cua-spacesd 0.16.5 (host service), Cua Spaces app 0.38.16 - Lume 0.7.2 (latest stable; the built-in pin is 0.7.0) - Host: MacBook Air (Apple silicon), macOS 26.5. Client: MacBook Pro, same account, connected through the relay. - Image `ghcr.io/trycua/macos:26-slim` (`sha256:5d348440b03074cba9fe3f2a82cf627181e4a21c18694e9803784077844e10ba`) ### Evidence While the create is waiting: - `netgw.json` for the VM has `static_leases: {"10.0.3.15": ""}` and forwards `127.0.0.1:

-> 10.0.3.15:22` and `127.0.0.1: -> 10.0.3.15:3211`. `nc -z 127.0.0.1

` succeeds. - `network-events.jsonl` shows guest traffic: `{"event":"blocked","reason":"platform:gateway","proto":"udp","dst":"10.0.3.255:137"}`. - `lume get agents --format json` reports `status: running`, `ipAddress: null`, `sshAvailable: null`. Root cause, reading `main` at 8f484f3: 1. `libs/lume/src/LumeController.swift`, `getVMDetailsLightweight` (around L346-L419): in a process that is not running the VM, `SharedVM.shared.liveVM(name:)` is nil, so `VM.ipAddress(forMAC:networkMode:)` gets `networkMode: nil` and falls back to vmnet's DHCP leases. A `gateway:` VM is never in those leases, so `ipAddress` is nil and `lume ssh` throws `SSHError.noIPAddress` (`libs/lume/src/Commands/SSH.swift`, L66-L68). The gateway is chosen per run and not stored with the VM (`libs/lume/src/VM/NetworkMode.swift`, L83), so no other process can recover it. 2. Even with the lease, `lume ssh` connects to `:22`. Behind the gateway that address is not reachable from the host (see the comment in `libs/lume/src/VM/VM.swift` around L148-L152). Only the gateway's loopback forward is. 3. `libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/lume/mod.rs`: `guest_exec` (around L3270-L3284) always returns `LumeSshExec` for macOS guests, and `sync_macos_env` -> `apply_macos_env` (around L1832-L1857 and L2135-L2163) uses it. But cua already knows the right endpoint: `gateway_network` (around L1294-L1379) forwards guest port 22 to a host loopback port and saves it in `gateway.json`, and `with_gateway` (around L1250) rewrites the SSH endpoint to `127.0.0.1:`. Guest exec just never uses it. `sync_macos_env` only runs when the create passes a workload environment, which host-provided Spaces do. That may be why a plain local `create_space` without `env` works. ### Workaround and additional context There is no workaround that keeps the gateway network. Disabling the gateway, back to Apple NAT, is the only path that works, and it gives up the isolation. Possible fixes, for the maintainers to choose: - **cua:** when `gateway.json` has a port-22 forward, run guest commands over `127.0.0.1:` instead of `lume ssh`. `SshExec` is key-only (`BatchMode=yes`), and macOS guests use Lume's `lume`/`lume` password login, so this needs password support or a key provisioned into the guest. - **Lume:** add `--host` and `--port` to `lume ssh`, so that cua's `LumeSshExec` can pass the gateway forward and keep Lume's password handling, gated on the Lume version that ships it. ### Submission checks - [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests. - [x] This issue describes a single problem. - [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): retry uncertain input only when evidence rules out a duplicate
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On Windows and macOS, refused, timed-out or unverified input can land after the next read, so a retry can duplicate it.
- What changed: Rule out duplicates before retrying. Disable `foreground_fallback` if a step can send input then refuse.

## Related work

Refs #5431, where this wording came from. Builds on #5574.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop reporting an off-Space macOS cursor as visible
body:
## Why

On macOS, a cursor pinned to a window on another Space paints nothing (#4068), but `cursor_is_externally_visible` still counted it as visible. The session cursor outcome, which reads `is_visible_for_session`, then reported a cursor the user could not see. #3886 added the same check for its own hide flag. Main already hides the cursor itself through `pinned_target_off_workspace`, so that check is the part of #3886 that still applies.

## What changed

- `cursor_is_externally_visible` returns false while `pinned_target_off_workspace` is set.
- `only_enabled_on_screen_cursor_is_externally_visible` checks that a visible cursor stops counting once it is pinned off-Space.

## Scope

macOS only. Linux and Windows never set `pinned_target_off_workspace`, and their `is_visible_for_session` is unchanged. Painting, pinning and input delivery are unchanged. The rest of #3886 (a background-only hide flag and per-tool routing) duplicates what main already does through `PinAbove`, so it is left out.

## Blast Radius

This touches the macOS overlay's visibility report: the session cursor outcome and the unpinned-overlay raise check. The raise check only runs when no window is pinned, and a cursor with no pinned window never has this flag set, so the raise behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passed. They skipped clippy and the `platform-macos` unit tests, which need macOS.
- The `platform-macos` build and tests run in macOS CI.

Salvaged from #3886
Fixes #3801

Credit to @lorenzozanee for the original change in #3886.

title: fix(cua-vmm): run macOS guest commands over the gateway's SSH forward
body:
## Summary

- **Problem this solves:** a macOS Space whose VM runs behind its network gateway (`cua-netgw`, the secure default) could not take a workload environment. Every macOS create that passes `env`, which host-provided Spaces (`--on host:<machine>`) always do, timed out after 180 s with `could not set the sandbox environment over lume ssh: VM '<name>' has no IP address`. A Lume CLI process other than the one running the VM only finds guests in vmnet's DHCP leases. The gateway hands out its own lease, and the guest's address is not reachable from the host anyway. Root cause and evidence are in #8262.
- **What changed:**
  - Guest commands for a macOS VM behind a running gateway (the environment write, `guest_exec`, and the background host-name step after a resume or pool claim) now log in to the gateway's existing loopback forward of guest port 22 as the image's `lume` account.
  - `SshExec` gains an additive password login for this. OpenSSH asks a private `SSH_ASKPASS` helper, written to a fresh `0700` temporary directory per command and removed afterwards, so the password never appears in argv or the environment. Password and keyboard-interactive auth are switched on explicitly, so a hardened `~/.ssh/config` cannot turn them off, and connection sharing is disabled because loopback forward ports are recycled.
  - A gateway that is no longer running is never dialled: `guest_exec` runs `mend_gateway` first, as `endpoints` does.
  - Hardening on the gateway path: the environment script reaches the guest over ssh's stdin (`/bin/sh -s`), so its values are on no host command line; a password login reads no ssh config (`-F /dev/null`); and the gateway channel checks that the gateway still runs and re-reads its forward port before every command, failing at once with `NotRunning` instead of dialling a stale port.
  - The askpass helper deletes itself the moment `ssh` runs it, so the password is not left on disk while the login runs, nor if the daemon is killed after `ssh` read it. The host-name script, which hands `sudo` the password, also goes over stdin on the gateway path, so no secret is on a host command line. A replaced gateway's `gateway.json` is removed before the new gateway starts, so a command never pairs the new gateway with the previous one's port 22 forward, which another VM's gateway may have taken.
  - VMs on Apple's NAT keep using `lume ssh`, and key-based `SshExec` logins are unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #8262

Possibly related: #8258, where forks and restarts behind `cua-netgw` are unreachable. This PR does not claim to fix it.

RFC: not needed. The change is internal to `cua-vmm`, with no public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol or permission contract change. `SshExec` only gains an optional `password` field and builder.

## Compatibility and risk

- **User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:** macOS Spaces behind the gateway become creatable with an environment; nothing else changes. `SshExec::from_endpoint` now keeps an endpoint's `password`, which is ignored whenever a key is set. Both existing callers (QEMU, `cua-image`) always set one.
- **Risk and rollback:** the change is limited to how cua-vmm runs commands in macOS gateway guests. The password is the images' documented default (`lume`). Revert the PR to restore `lume ssh` everywhere.

## Validation

- **Focused tests and checks:**
  - New unit tests: password-login ssh options, including over a hardened config; the askpass helper's output, `0700` modes and removal; the extra environment reaching both the collected and the streaming spawn paths; and gateway SSH selection (NAT, no SSH forward, a gateway that is not running, a forwarded login).
  - New tests also cover the helper deleting itself on its one read (it fails with the deletion removed) and the host-name script staying off `ssh`'s argv.
  - `bin/ci` in affected mode on the head's tree (0c1baed, identical to the rebased commit it ran on): all 8 checks passed. They cover rustfmt, SPDX, image refs, the Windows cfg grep, clippy `-D warnings` for the 10 direct crates and each cua-vmm backend feature alone, `cargo test -p cua-vmm`, and the Spaces contract manifest and control fixtures.
  - A plain parallel `cargo test -p cua-vmm --lib` also fails `qemu::tpm_tests::a_launch_cancelled_while_waiting_for_qmp_keeps_the_vm_until_cleanup` on unmodified `main` in 2 of 2 runs here. It passes alone and under `bin/ci`'s `--test-threads=4`.
- **Manual or platform evidence:**
  - Host: MacBook Air (Apple silicon, macOS 26.5) running `cua host setup --profile spare --no-desktop --provide-spaces`, Lume 0.7.2, Cua Spaces 0.38.16 for `cua-netgw`. Client: a second enrolled Mac.
  - With the released cua 0.28.6, `cua spaces create macos:26-slim --on host:<host>` failed four times out of four after 180 s, as described in #8262.
  - With this branch's `cua` as the host's daemon, the same create succeeded in 42 s, then in 52 s and 50 s on later runs. `space_bash` in the new Space returned `26.5.2` / `lume` / exit 0 from both Macs.
  - A plain password login to the gateway's forward also succeeded while `lume ssh` was failing.
  - With the final ssh options and the self-deleting helper, a login over a running Space's gateway forward on the same host returned `26.5.2` / `lume`, exit 0, and left the helper's directory empty. The same channel ran a stdin script to completion.
- **Known gaps or CI still required:**
  - The full CI, end-to-end and image lanes have not run locally.
  - This is a fork PR, so the sign-off is `CI: Quick` in GitHub Actions, which needs a maintainer to approve the workflow runs.
  - The host-name `sudo` itself was not exercised live over the stdin path; the script, its delivery and the channel were.
  - Live evidence covers host-provided Spaces. A local `create_space` with `env` takes the same code path but was not exercised separately.

title: test(cua-driver): qualify one Android candidate on an emulator, then a physical phone
body:
Salvaged from #4249 by @saariuslystoned. Their two commits are kept as authored; one fix commit sits on top.

Refs #3673

## Why

#4249 adds `qualify.py`, which runs one built Android candidate on an emulator and then on a physical phone and writes a receipt. It also fixes two `smoke.py`/`lifecycle-smoke.py` assumptions that broke on real devices. Review found three ways a `full` receipt could overstate what ran, so this PR carries the original work plus fixes for those.

## What changed

- The original #4249 commits: `qualify.py`, `test_qualify.py`, the `smoke.py` notification-permission grant and focus precondition, the `lifecycle-smoke.py` notification-row expansion, and README docs.
- Cleanup now reports `unverified`, without raising past the original failure, when a residue probe fails. Before, a failed probe read as zero residue, so a disconnected device could still produce `full`. A lease wait is counted only when residue was actually seen, so a slow first probe no longer fails the phase. An unsupported device whose environment probe fails still gets a receipt.
- `--driver` is resolved once, so the file that is hashed is the binary that runs. Installed identity refuses split APKs instead of hashing only the base.

## Scope

Android harness scripts only, under `libs/cua-driver/android`. No runtime, SDK, contract or CLI change. The base is `feat/cua-driver-android-local`, the prototype from #3674, which was closed unmerged. `libs/cua-driver/android` does not exist on `main`, so this cannot land there on its own. It is a draft until a maintainer decides whether the Android prototype comes back.

## Blast Radius

Only people who run the Android harness by hand against local devices. `smoke.py` now grants `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` to the synthetic demo APK, as `lifecycle-smoke.py` already did.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` in `libs/cua-driver/android`: all pass, including two new tests for the cleanup result and split-APK refusal. A mutation check showed that both fail when their fix is reverted.
- The `qualify.py` refusals were checked without devices, and each exits 2 with no evidence directory: no phone role given, `--runs 0`, the same serial in both roles, an evidence directory inside the repository, and an absent serial.
- Not run here: deploy, smoke and lifecycle on an emulator or phone, because this host has no Android SDK or adb. The author's device receipts for the original head are linked in #4249.

title: fix(cua-driver): avoid activation during background element keys
body:
Salvaged from #4876

Fixes #4843

## Why

On Windows, background `press_key` with an `element_token` called UIA `SetFocus` on the control before posting the key. Some providers (WinForms among them) activate their top-level frame from `SetFocus`, even under `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`, so the target window came to the front briefly. That breaks the background no-foreground-swap contract. This is @qsgy-edge's fix from #4876, merged with current main.

## What changed

- Background element keys to a native control post `WM_KEYDOWN`/`WM_KEYUP` straight to the element's own HWND, with no focus preparation. The HWND must belong to the admitted pid and be the admitted window or a child of it, and it passes the UIPI check. An unmappable character falls back to `WM_CHAR` on that same HWND.
- An element with no native HWND (a windowless control) gets a structured `background_unavailable` refusal before any input is sent. Embedded WebView elements keep their existing posted focus-click route.
- The WPF fixture binary gains a `--winforms-keyboard` mode, which the new `harness_wpf_test.rs` rows use to check background F6 and Unicode delivery to the exact control with no activation or focus change, the windowless refusal, and foreground delivery. The WPF accelerator rows read the fixture's state file and use a 5000 ms recording state budget.

## Scope

Covers `press_key` on Windows only. `hotkey` and `type_text` with an `element_token` are not changed here. On top of #4876 this branch merges main and adds one commit. That commit points the testkit's state-timeout setter at main's `BehaviorVideo` state and removes the `Win32_UI_HiDpi` e2e feature. The merge drops #4876's WebView2 harness and UniFFI generator changes, because #7537 and main replaced those files.

## Blast Radius

Windows clients that send background `press_key` with an `element_token` to a windowless UIA control (WPF, WinUI, UWP content) now get `background_unavailable` instead of a key that briefly activated the window. The refusal says to retry with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`. Native HWND controls and WebView hosts still get background delivery.

## Verification

title: fix(cua-host): set the Windows host up over SSH, and say when nothing will start it after a restart
body:
## Problem
Setting up a Windows computer that nobody sits at (a headless VM) hit two problems.

1. `cua host setup` over SSH failed: `schtasks /Create ... ERROR: No mapping between account names and security IDs was done`. The logon task named its user from `USERDOMAIN`, which is `WORKGROUP` in an SSH session on a computer outside a domain, and the real account is `COMPUTER\user`.
2. Once set up, the host runs from a Task Scheduler logon task, so after a restart nothing starts it until someone signs in. Nothing said so.

## Fix
- The task's user is now what `whoami` prints (`desktop-xxxx\cua`), with `USERDOMAIN\USERNAME` as the fallback.
- `cua host setup` on Windows prints one warning when the host runs from the logon task and the computer does not sign in by itself (`AutoAdminLogon` is not 1), pointing at Sysinternals Autologon and a dedicated non-administrator account. With `--json` it goes to stderr.

## Verified on a clean Windows 11 PC
Windows 11 Enterprise evaluation, `cua.exe` cross-built from this branch.
- Before: from an SSH session (`USERDOMAIN=WORKGROUP`), `cua host setup --direct 127.0.0.1:PORT --runner windows-task` exits 1 with the error above. From the desktop session it succeeds.
- After: the same command from the SSH session exits 0, the task is installed as "Interactive only" and running, and the warning is printed.
- With no auto-logon and nobody signed in, after a restart the task stays "Ready", no `cua-spacesd` runs, and nothing listens until someone signs in at the console. That is what the warning describes. With Sysinternals Autologon set, the computer signs in at boot and the host starts in session 1; Autologon leaves no `DefaultPassword` value in the registry.

Unit tests: `the_logon_account_is_the_one_whoami_names_not_the_workgroup`, `a_windows_logon_task_warns_unless_the_computer_signs_in_by_itself`. `bin/ci` passed (rustfmt, clippy on 13 crates, unit tests for cua-cli and cua-host).

## Not in this PR
Starting a provider-only host (`--share spaces`) at boot without any sign-in. I confirmed on the same VM that it works (a boot-trigger task, run as a user with the batch-logon right, created a Linux computer in Session 0 with nobody signed in), but it needs a dedicated account and an elevated setup step, so it is separate work.
