title: fix(cua-driver): support guarded existing-profile browser setup on Hyprland
body:
Salvaged from #4931

## Why

On Hyprland, existing-profile `browser_prepare` cannot run its setup: main's Linux foreground transaction has no Hyprland branch, so the setup keystrokes are refused before anything is sent. @chrisohearn's #4931 routes setup and teardown through the Hyprland input adapter, proves which tab the setup created, and hands the person's focus back afterwards, including after Chromium's own consent prompt. This PR lands that work on current main, with their twelve setup-transaction commits kept as authored and the conflicts resolved onto main's `interaction/` layer and #7587's setup code.

## What changed

- **Guarded setup input.** On Hyprland, setup keystrokes, the setup URL and the closing Ctrl+W go through the plugin's exact-window foreground route. Each one first re-checks process and window identity, session lifecycle and cancellation. A dispatch guard re-reads the owned tab's selected state right before each packet, and the URL is typed through the plugin, so the clipboard is never used. Other backends keep main's `with_target_foreground` route and clipboard paste. A refused or partially delivered input is reported as possibly delivered.
- **Tab ownership.** Setup claims a tab only when the same new tab is uniquely selected in two consecutive walks. It closes that tab only while the tab still shows the fixed setup page, and proves the close by the tab disappearing.
- **Focus hand-back.** Setup and the consent prompt capture the person's window, workspace and pointer before the first contact with the endpoint. They restore them only if the person gave no input in the meantime, judged by the plugin's new content-free `external_input_count` or, with an older plugin, an `ext-idle-notify-v1` watch. Dispatches try the Hyprland 0.56 Lua form first and fall back once to the classic form. The Linux consent deadline now scales with observed AT-SPI walk time, inside a 13 s Linux bound. Other platforms keep 4 s.

## Scope

Covers commits 1–8 and 10–13 of #4931. Not here:
- Commit 9 (input availability), which landed in #7983.
- Commits 14–17 (scaled-size Chrome window binding and the X11 overlay test gate), which are in #8237.

Port changes on top of the contributor's commits:
- Consent and setup actions keep main's walked-identity window proof and #5574's rule that an action which may have landed is read back, not refused. The contributor's pre-dispatch guard now runs inside `perform_action_walked_guarded`.
- The niri refusal still comes before any input or clipboard use.
- Main dropped Hyprland's stale-geometry retry in #6209, so the dispatch guard runs once before the single packet, and its test is rewritten for that path.
- Main's newer `FixturePlatform` fixture gets the consent-guard fields.
- The release bundle allowlist ships `external_input.hpp` and its test.
- `input_quiet.rs` gets its SPDX header.
- Main's automatic consent bound follows the per-platform consent timeout, so its unanswered-prompt message and tests track Linux's longer bound. macOS and Windows declare the new trait default, and the unattended test reads its DOM click from main's action record.
- On routes where the setup module sends keys itself, the lifecycle check and owned-tab guard run inside the foreground callback, right before each shortcut and paste, followed by a read-back that the exact window still holds the keyboard focus and a final cancellation and lifecycle check.
- Before the closing Ctrl+W, the setup page is proven again after the wait for quiet input. Cleanup keeps that page's document object: the one reporting the setup URL, or the only document when the browser reports no URIs. The dispatch guard re-reads it right before the shortcut. Navigating away retires the object or changes its URI, and either refuses, as does a failed read.
- A checkbox toggle counts as attempted only once it was sent or may have landed, so rollback never flips a checkbox setup never touched.
- A consent walk that cannot be proven window-scoped no longer ends the attempt as an unavailable route. Observation continues, so the pending connection stays open for a person.

## Blast Radius

- Linux existing-profile setup on every backend now requires a complete, window-scoped tab tree before it opens a setup tab, and an admitted session lifecycle before setup or cleanup input.
- On Hyprland, setup also needs the plugin's foreground route. Without it, setup refuses before sending anything.
- `BrowserPlatform` gains `existing_profile_consent_focus_guard`, which defaults to `None`, so macOS and Windows change only in the shared consent timeout constant, which stays 4 s there.
- Public MCP schemas are unchanged.
- The Hyprland Edge trusted-click fallback refuses instead of clicking.
- Restoration is skipped on multi-output desktops. A tab whose ownership was never proven may stay open rather than be closed.

## Verification

- At head `8b5745bb` (current main merged in): `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::` (308 pass), the full `platform-linux` library suite, the plugin's Python release tests, the plugin-disabled CTest including `cua_hyprland_external_input_test`, clippy `-D warnings` on both crates, and `bin/ci --quick` all pass.
- Several independent review passes found check-then-act gaps in the setup and consent paths and four main-drift test failures, all fixed in the commits above. A disposable Chromium AT-SPI probe confirmed that a fragment navigation changes the document URI and leaving the page retires the document object, which the close guard relies on.
- Not run: a live Hyprland desktop on this head, the native plugin build (this host's Hyprland headers fail it at the base too), X11 and Sway desktop E2E, and macOS and Windows builds. #4931 records the contributor's live Omarchy runs against the pre-port code.

## Checks

- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green: only `--quick` ran on this shared host; heavy lanes are left to CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): attribute hosted Windows Store apps in list_apps by exact AUMID
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: #8127 (salvaged from #4962) makes Windows `list_apps` give a running Store app its installed `bundle_id`, so a capability-manifest `bundle_id` grant matches it. Three gaps remain:
  1. A packaged process with no AUMID falls back to its package family's single `uwp` entry. The installed catalog keeps one entry per package, so that check can't tell a single-app package from a multi-app one, and a helper process can take the first app's name and launch path.
  2. A hosted UWP app such as Calculator owns no top-level window; its frame belongs to `ApplicationFrameHost.exe`. `list_apps` therefore has no row for the app's pid. Bounded mode resolves the frame to that pid before reading `bundle_id` from `list_apps`, so a valid grant still fails.
  3. With a hosted app's frame in front, only the `ApplicationFrameHost.exe` row is marked `active`.
- What changed:
  1. Only an exact AUMID match (ASCII case-insensitive, against `shell:appsFolder\{AUMID}`) merges a running process into a `uwp` entry. `process_package_identity` / `PackageIdentity` become `process_app_user_model_id`, so `GetPackageFamilyName` is no longer called.
  2. `list_apps` also lists the app pid behind each frame, found with the existing trusted `hosted_app_pid` resolver (only the system's `ApplicationFrameHost.exe` counts).
  3. The foreground pid goes through the same resolver, so the hosted app's row is the `active` one.

## Related work

Refs #8127, #4962, #3330

RFC: not required. No new grant type or contract.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows `list_apps` only. A packaged process without an AUMID now shows as an unmatched `desktop` row, as it did before #8127. A hosted Store app gains its own row (`kind: "uwp"`, `bundle_id`, `launch_path`). The host's `ApplicationFrameHost.exe` row stays, but `active` moves from it to the app's row when the app's frame is in front. The tool description still holds, so the generated reference is unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: contained in `platform-windows` `list_apps`. Revert to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, lockfiles, image refs) pass. The unit tests now cover the AUMID-only matching rules, an unpackaged test process having no AUMID, and the ordering and dedupe of hosted-app pids. They run in the Windows CI lanes.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. This host is Linux. The bounded-mode check on Windows (Store Notepad and Calculator allowed by a `bundle_id` grant, an ungranted app refused) has not been run.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Windows build and tests run in CI only. The catalog lists one app per package, so a running app that isn't its package's first app is not matched.

## Contributor and release checks

title: fix(cua-driver): bound Windows semantic click provider calls
body:
## Why

A Windows element-token click on a WinForms button whose handler calls `ShowDialog` stays pending until the modal closes: the UIA `Invoke` call blocks inside the provider, and the element path awaited it with no deadline. This runs the element path's Invoke, Toggle, SelectionItem and ExpandCollapse sequence under the same deadline and single-flight gate the point-based UIA path already uses.

Salvaged from #5046 by @OnslaughtSnail, whose four commits are kept as authored. Main split `tools/impl_.rs` into per-tool modules after that PR, so the element-click dispatch now lands in `tools/click.rs`.

Fixes #5012

## What changed

- New `uia::element_click::try_click_element` runs the pattern sequence on a UIA worker with the 4 s `SUBTREE_OP_TIMEOUT`. The worker keeps the gate permit, the retained element and its COM apartment until the provider returns. Each later COM call checks the deadline flag first, so a call that returns after the deadline does not start another pattern.
- A timeout or worker exit returns `background_unavailable` with effect `unverifiable`; a busy gate returns effect `refused`. Neither falls through to coordinate input, and the hint says not to replay the click. A completed miss keeps the existing coordinate fallback.
- Adds a WinForms modal fixture and `semantic_click_deadline_windows_test`, run by the native lane of `scripts/ci/windows/run-rust-e2e.ps1`.

## Scope

Windows element-token single left or middle clicks only. Pixel clicks, Chromium's coordinate-first route, right-clicks, multi-clicks and other platforms are unchanged. This does not cancel a COM call that has already started.

## Blast Radius

While a timed-out provider call is still blocked, it holds the shared UIA gate, so other UIA calls report busy until it returns. Win32 window enumeration and foreground dismissal of the modal still work, and the e2e test drives both.

## Verification

- `semantic_deadline_stops_the_route_and_preserves_unknown_effect` (unit, `platform-windows`) and `cancelled_operation_cannot_enter_another_provider_call` (unit, `element_click`) cover the result contract and the cancellation check.
- `semantic_click_deadline_windows_test` (native Windows e2e): the modal click returns a timeout before the modal closes, a retry returns busy, the fixture journal records one open and no mouse-down, and after dismissal ordinary semantic clicks and the coordinate fallback work again.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, bin/ci sync) and the e2e inventory tests pass. The Windows build, clippy, unit tests and the native e2e lane were not run on this host and run in CI.

## Checklist

title: fix(cua-driver): fall back on what a run_steps step last sent
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: when a `run_steps` step's token went stale, the step found the element again and retried it. If that retry was refused in the background, `foreground_fallback` re-sent the step's original arguments, with the stale token (and `click` instead of `invoke_menu` for a menu-bar item). The retry failed stale, yet the step still noted "background delivery was refused, so it ran in the foreground". Separately, `DeliveryMode::parse` collapsed an omitted `delivery_mode` and an explicit `"background"` into one `Background` variant, although only the omitted one may escalate. That rule lived in a second string check, `background_requested_explicitly`.
- What changed:
  - `run_step` keeps what the step last sent in a `StepAttempt` (`Original`, `MenuRoute`, `Refound`). The foreground fallback re-sends `attempt.current_args()` with the attempt's tool, and is offered only when that tool takes `delivery_mode`. If the foreground retry fails, the message says "background delivery was refused, and the foreground retry failed: …" and no longer claims the step ran in the foreground. The re-find note now says the element was "found … again" instead of "acted on", since it also leads a failed step's message.
  - `DeliveryMode` is `BackgroundPreferred` (omitted, the default), `BackgroundStrict` (explicit `"background"`) or `Foreground`. `allows_escalation()` is true only for `BackgroundPreferred`. It gates both the macOS brief foreground drag (it replaces `background_requested_explicitly`, which is deleted) and the `run_steps` fallback, and each step's mode is parsed once. Platform adapters that only care about background versus foreground use `is_background()`; their behavior does not change.

## Related work

Refs the cua-driver everystate report: B1 and simplifications #3 and #9.
Compatible with #8172, which changes the step's window lookup and not the retry ladder. #7374 and #7218 edit the same ladder lines and will need a rebase on top of this.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: no schema or wire change. A step with `foreground_fallback` whose stale target was found again now lands on the re-found element in the foreground. A menu-bar route falls back through `invoke_menu`. A failed fallback reports the failure truthfully. The omitted-versus-explicit rule is unchanged: explicit `"background"` still opts out of the brief foreground step and the fallback.
- Risk and rollback: the platform edits are a mechanical move from `== DeliveryMode::Background` to `.is_background()` (Windows) and from test constructors to `BackgroundPreferred` (macOS, Linux). Revert the PR to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `batch_tools::reliability_tests::a_found_again_target_refused_in_the_background_falls_back_on_its_fresh_token`: a fake window whose tokens go stale on re-render and that refuses background clicks. The test asserts the click sequence (stale original, re-found token in the background, then the same re-found token in the foreground) and the note. A second pass makes the foreground fail and asserts the "foreground retry failed" message, without "ran in the foreground". This test is committed first and should fail on main.
  - `an_explicit_background_step_is_never_sent_in_the_foreground`: explicit `"background"` on the step, or as run_steps' default, gets no fallback and no hint.
  - `delivery::tests::delivery_mode_parse_fronts_only_on_explicit_foreground` and `only_an_omitted_delivery_mode_allows_escalation`: strict versus preferred parsing.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, SPDX headers), and the Mac CI runner set `local-ci` on this head. At head `c49803e63a`, CI's Rust lanes passed: `Rust macOS unit`, `Rust Linux unit and compile`, the three `Rust Windows` shards and `Rust Windows clippy`, `fmt, clippy, test` on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows, and `platform-linux compiles on macOS`. The macOS unit log shows all four new tests passing.
- Known gaps: the failure of the B1 test at its own commit (`76d964ad0f`, before the fix) was not run, because this shared host keeps cargo builds off it. There is no fake `invoke_menu` that refuses background, so the `MenuRoute` fallback is covered only by its shared code path.

title: fix(cua-driver): aim element scroll at the part inside the window
body:
Salvaged from #5365 by @S3yon. Their commit is kept as authored, rebased onto current main.

Fixes #5281

## Why

On macOS, `scroll` with an element token posts the wheel at the centre of the element's whole AX frame. When the element is taller or wider than its window (a long text view or web area), that centre falls outside the window and background delivery is refused.

## What changed

- The element path aims at the centre of the element frame intersected with the window bounds. With no overlap, or an unknown rect or window, it falls back to the old centre, so the outside-window refusal still applies.
- `reveal_scroll::intersect` is now `pub(crate)` so `tools/scroll.rs` can reuse it.

## Scope

macOS element-token scroll only. The pixel and keystroke paths, and the other platforms, are unchanged. An element that fits inside its window gets the same point as before.

## Blast Radius

One call site in `platform-macos/src/tools/scroll.rs`. No schema, API or contract change.

## Verification

- Four unit tests for `element_wheel_point`: element inside the window, taller than it, partly above it, and outside it.
- The scoped repository checks (quick stage) pass. The macOS build, unit tests and clippy run in CI; the PR host is Linux.

body:
Salvaged from #5380

Refs #3780
Refs #4955

## Why

On macOS, `invoke_menu` on a window of the frontmost app that is not its key window raises and focuses that window (`focus_exact_window`), opens the menu on screen and presses the item. The user is working in another window of that app, so their window loses key and the target covers it for the call. @skap3214's #5380 sends that case through the background press route instead: the target is made key through the in-app key-window record without a raise, the item is pressed without opening its menu, and key goes back to the user's window. Credit for the design, the route rules and the tests goes to them; their three commits are kept as authored.

## What changed

- `MenuRoute` now has four cases: `Background` (app behind, or target on another Space as #7756 added), `BehindUsersWindow` (new key-scope route), `KeyWindowInFront` (the old raise-and-open path), and `KeyWindowUnknown` (refused with `window_not_key` and `bring_to_front` when the key window cannot be read and the target is not the app's front window).
- Results and refusals on the new route say the window was behind the user's window, not that the app was in the background. `invoke_menu` holds the pid's mutation lease across the route decision, the key change, the press and the hand-back.
- Rebase onto main: main's off-Space rule (#7756) is folded into `menu_route`, the automation-consent refusal and the off-Space `window_not_key` text are kept, and main's `focused_window_id_of_pid` now returns an `AxWindowId`. #5380 shared the lease through a task-local (`lease_unless_held`). Main's #7039 needs the press worker itself to own an `Arc` of the lease, so `run_in_background` now takes that `Arc` from its caller. `invoke` and `hotkey`'s menu route each pass one in, and `lease_unless_held` is gone. Four commits on top. The first updates `MACOS.md` for the other-Space case. The second, third and fourth put the behind-window key scope and both leases (pid mutation, desktop lane) into one `PressHold` that the press worker shares. Key always goes back before either lease is released, even when the call is cancelled while key is being set or during the press. That hand-back runs on the blocking pool and waits until the app reports the user's window as key again (`WindowKeyScope::confirm_hand_back`). If the app never confirms it, the next `invoke_menu` on that pid is refused with `window_not_key` while key still reads as the temporary window or cannot be read, for at most two seconds (`settle_hand_back`).

## Scope

macOS `invoke_menu` only, plus the matching recovery hint and the driver's `MACOS.md`. Background apps, other-Space windows and the frontmost app's key window keep their current routes. Linux and Windows are untouched. No schema or refusal-code change.

## Tradeoffs

- #7761 found that AppKit runs some menu actions after the press returns, against whichever window is key at that point (TextEdit File > Save on a sibling window saved the wrong document). That is why the raise path now leaves the target key. The new route hands key back right after the press. A Save on this route waits for the file on disk before key goes back, so Save is covered. Any other command that AppKit defers would act on the user's window. #5380 lists this as an untested risk, and nobody has checked yet whether a press on a closed menu item defers the way a press inside an open menu does.
- On main, a sibling window's menu item works by raising the window. On this route it is refused with `window_not_key` when the key-window record does not also move `AXMainWindow`, because the background route requires both to be the target. Nobody has checked that on a desktop.

## Blast Radius

Agents that call `invoke_menu` on a non-key window of the app the user is in. The menu command now runs without raising that window, or is refused with `window_not_key` and `bring_to_front` advice, where it used to raise the window and succeed. Same-pid background actions now wait while an `invoke_menu` call holds the lease on the raise path too.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks that run on Linux passed: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) and `git diff --check`.
- Not run here: `platform-macos` unit tests and clippy, which need macOS and run in `CI: Rust macOS unit`. Also not run: the Lume desktop run that matters most, `invoke_menu` on a second window of a frontmost TextEdit, which would check that the user's window keeps key and order, that `AXMainWindow` follows the key-window record, and that the command lands in the target window.

title: [RFC]: Trusted SDK API for user-installed cursor themes
body:
### Primary area
SDK or bindings

### Summary
Add a trusted host-side Cua Driver SDK API to install a user-selected, compiled .cua-theme artifact into the current user’s theme store, so desktop applications can offer cursor-theme upload and selection without shelling out to the CLI. This must remain separate from agent-facing tools.

### Motivation and current state
Cua Driver exposes selection of an already-installed theme through the SDK. Theme compilation and installation are currently CLI-only, and the SDK deliberately does not let agent calls install theme data. Desktop applications embedding the SDK therefore cannot provide an in-app user-initiated upload flow without relying on an separately installed CLI.

### Goals
- Let a trusted embedding application install a user-selected compiled .cua-theme artifact through the public SDK.
- Reuse the existing bounded artifact validation and atomic install path.
- Keep theme installation out of agent-facing tools and MCP schemas.
- Preserve the existing CLI and installed-theme selection behavior across macOS, Windows, and Linux.

### Non-goals
- Accept arbitrary image files or uncompiled Lottie source in this SDK operation.
- Let an agent install, remove, or overwrite cursor themes.
- Change the .cua-theme file format or make themes executable.

### Proposal
Add a trusted embedding-host method that accepts bounded compiled artifact bytes, validates the artifact and theme identifier with the existing cursor-overlay theme-authoring path, and installs it atomically to the current user’s theme store. Do not add it to the generic agent tool inventory or remote receiver. The embedding application invokes it only after explicit user action; agent sessions may only select an installed theme id. The API should report the installed id and a structured validation or install error. Platform storage resolution must reuse the existing cross-platform theme-store implementation.

### Alternatives considered
- Require the Cua CLI to be installed and spawn cua-driver cursor-theme install: adds an external runtime dependency and process handling to every embedding app.
- Allow the agent-facing set_agent_cursor_theme tool to install arbitrary bytes: violates the current trust boundary and is not acceptable.
- Implement a separate theme store in each host application: duplicates validation, storage, and compatibility logic.

### Compatibility and migration
This is an additive SDK API and does not change the MCP/tool protocol or existing CLI behavior. The caller must use the same SDK version that includes the operation. Existing installed themes and default theme remain unchanged; uninstall continues through the existing trusted CLI workflow.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry
Accept only bounded compiled theme artifacts and reuse canonical validation before writing. Write atomically into the current user’s theme store. Never execute uploaded content. Do not accept a file path from an agent or allow agent-facing methods to install or remove themes. Do not collect or emit artwork bytes, filenames, theme contents, or user-specific paths in telemetry. The embedding app owns the user confirmation and upload UI.

### Validation and acceptance evidence
- Hermetic tests for invalid, oversized, valid, and duplicate theme artifacts; atomic install behavior; and structured errors.
- SDK binding generation and drift checks for each published binding.
- Platform coverage for store resolution and install behavior on macOS, Windows, and Linux; document any OS limitation.
- Confirm the operation is absent from generic tool inventories and remote/agent-facing APIs.
- Run the required focused Rust, binding, and repository CI checks.

### Unresolved questions
- Should the SDK return only the installed theme id, or also safe theme metadata for an in-app theme picker?
- Should removal remain CLI-only, or should a separately gated trusted-host remove API be included?

### RFC document pull request
Not yet opened; awaiting maintainer guidance on the contract.

### Submission checks
- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep consent grants inside the session episode that approved them
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: a protected-resource grant could outlive the session episode it was approved in. Resource consent ran before lifecycle admission, so a call waiting on a person was not in flight. `end_session` (or the idle sweep) ended the session at once, the person approved, `authorize` stored the grant, and the call was refused. After `start_session` on the same label, the next protected call reused that grant without asking. Episodes had no identity, so the grant store could not tell the two apart.
- What changed:
  - `session.rs`: `LifecycleRecord` and the `ENDED_SESSIONS`, `IDLE_ENDED_SESSIONS`, `EXPLICITLY_ENDED_SESSIONS`, `CLOSED_TRANSPORTS`, `SUSPENDED_RUNTIME_SCOPES` and `SESSION_CLEANUP_PROGRESS` collections are now one `Lifecycle` under one lock. Each id maps to an `Episode { id: EpisodeId, phase }` with `EpisodePhase::{Live, Ending { reason, explicit }, Ended { by: Explicit | Idle | TransportClosed, owner, cleanup: Pending | Done }}`. `EpisodeId` grows on every new episode, including a revival and a recreation by the next call. Admission (`begin_session_dispatch`) and revival (`activate_or_revive_session_for_owner`, `revive_session_for_owner`, `recreates_on_next_call`) call the same `Lifecycle::claim`.
  - `consent.rs`: `ResourceGrantKey` carries the `EpisodeId`. `authorize` stores an approval only if the episode it started in is still live; otherwise it revokes the approval and returns `authorization_canceled`. A session already ending or ended gets an approval for that one call, which is not stored.
  - `tool.rs`: `begin_session_dispatch` runs before the resource adapters, so consent waits inside `in_flight` and `end_session` or the idle sweep defers. An end that lands while the person decides still wins: the call is refused before it acts, as before.

## Related work

Supersedes #7349 and #7350. Both invariants are covered here:
- #7349 (a grant must not outlive its episode): the episode check in `authorize`, with its three orderings ported as tests (accepted after the end, queued behind another session's prompt while the end lands, and ended before authorization started).
- #7350 (a closed transport's late call cannot claim a label): `end_sessions_for_owner` records the owner as closed before it ends anything, `claim` refuses a closed owner on any label, and closed owners that no label names are forgotten after `CLOSED_OWNER_GRACE` (the idle TTL). Its three tests are ported.

Checked for compatibility with #8033 (it can map the shared `DispatchRefusal::OwnedByOtherTransport` from `claim` to its start refusal), #5971 (main already releases a closed owner's labels; that behavior is unchanged) and #3048 (no overlap with the lifecycle state). Bounding ended-entry growth (CUA-4993) stays possible: an `Ended` entry whose cleanup is `Done` can be evicted, and new episodes still get larger ids.

No RFC: no public SDK, CLI, MCP or protocol contract changes. Public `session` functions keep their signatures; `EpisodeId`, `EpisodeStatus`, `episode_status` and `DispatchRefusal::TransportClosed` are added.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a protected call whose session ends while its prompt is open now returns `authorization_canceled` and stores no grant. The label's next episode is prompted again. `end_session` during an open prompt reports `session_cleanup_pending` and completes when the call returns, as it already did for any other in-flight call. A closed transport's late call on a label is refused with "session is not available to this transport".
- Tradeoffs: admission now runs before consent. A call on an idle-reclaimed session starts its new episode (and fires the revive hooks) before the prompt, so a declined prompt leaves that new episode live until the idle sweep. Previously a declined call started nothing. A closed transport's own unnamed id can still be started again by that transport, as in #7350.
- Risk: deep. Every session admission, end, revival and protected grant goes through the new map. Rollback is a revert of this PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `a_grant_approved_after_end_session_does_not_reach_the_next_episode` (tool.rs, blocking `ProtectedConsentProvider`, `end_session` while approval is pending, `start_session`, second call must prompt again; it is the first commit, so it fails on main); the three ported #7349 orderings and `a_grant_is_reused_within_its_episode_only` (consent.rs); the three ported #7350 tests and `every_new_episode_of_an_id_gets_a_larger_episode_id` covering Live, Ending, Ended, revival and idle recreation (session.rs).
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passes. Builds and tests ran in CI only, not locally: this is a shared host.
- Known gaps: no desktop E2E. The change is in `cua-driver-core` and runs the same on every platform; native Windows and Linux run in CI.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`): only `bin/ci --quick` ran here (shared host); the full checks run in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep stop truthful while a daemon is starting
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `cua-driver stop` decided whether a daemon was present from one signal, a successful `list`. A launch that had started but was not answering yet got "Cua Driver daemon is not running" (exit 1) and kept running, so `stop` followed by `update` or by a different `serve` could leave a daemon behind. `serve`, `status` and `wait_for_release` each read presence from a different signal: the `<socket>.lock`, the socket file, the pid file or the `list` answer. A macOS daemon that answers `list` but refuses every tool with `permissions_pending` also read as fully up.
- What changed:
  - `cua_driver_core::daemon::probe_presence(socket)` returns `DaemonPresence { Absent, Stale { socket_file }, Starting { lock_held }, Serving { pid, gate: Open | PermissionsPending } }`. It reads the `metadata` answer, then tries the daemon lock and releases it at once, then checks for a socket file. `metadata` gains an additive `permissions_pending` field. Older daemons omit it and read as `Open`.
  - `serve` claims its socket lock as the first step of the serve command, before it builds the desktop runtime, and the disclaimed macOS relaunch inherits that claim. `stop` waits up to 10 s for a `Starting` daemon to answer, then shuts it down. When `stop` finds no daemon at all, it keeps looking for 500 ms, so a `serve` process that has started but not yet reached its claim is still caught.
  - `serve`'s already-running check, `status` and `wait_for_release` all use the probe. There is one already-running message, with the PID the daemon itself reports. `status` prints `tool calls: open` or `tool calls: waiting for permissions …` and reports a starting daemon or a stale socket file. A stale socket file no longer counts as "not released".
  - On Windows, `wait_for_release` counts the daemon as released only once no instance of its pipe is left, free or busy. That holds with or without the daemon lock, so a late `metadata` reply never counts, even when the probe itself holds the only instance. `serve` refuses to start while any instance of the pipe exists, as main did, so it never starts beside a lockless embedded daemon that is slow to answer. Every daemon now takes its first pipe instance with the first-instance flag, so a lockless embedded daemon that takes the name after a standalone launch's check, while the launch builds its runtime, still makes that launch fail with "already held by another process". A Windows daemon writes its PID file only after its first pipe instance exists, as a Unix daemon does after bind.
  - An endpoint that is still held while nothing answers counts as a daemon that is not answering yet, even with no lock (an embedded daemon takes none). On Windows that means any instance of the pipe; on Unix, a socket that still accepts connections. `stop` waits for it as it waits for a starting daemon, `status` says the endpoint exists but is not answering, `serve` refuses to launch beside it, `wait_for_release` waits for it, and the stale-socket cleanup never unlinks a socket that still listens.
  - On Unix a symlink at the socket path that leads to a socket that still listens counts as held too. The lock probe opens `<socket>.lock` without blocking and counts only a regular file, so a FIFO at the lock path cannot hang it.

## Related work

Refs the cua-driver everystate report, items B3, #4 and #13 (daemon presence).

Overlaps, checked against their diffs:
- #7626 changes `status` and the already-running hint to report the PID the serving daemon gives in `metadata`. This PR takes `Serving { pid }` from that same answer and leaves `status`'s PID lines alone, so the two compose. Expect a small textual conflict in `run_serve_cmd` / `run_status_cmd`.
- #7150 adds an `owner_pid` argument to `run_serve_cmd`. This PR adds `socket_lock` to it. Expect a trivial signature merge.

RFC: not needed. The CLI gains clearer `status` / `stop` messages. The wire change is one additive field on `metadata`.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact:
  - `stop` run against a launch that is still starting now waits, then stops the daemon (exit 0). If the daemon never answers it prints "still starting after 10s" (exit 1). With nothing running, `stop` takes 500 ms longer to say "not running". No lock can cover the moment between process start and the claim, so the settle window covers it instead. A launch that starts after `stop` has given up is outside `stop`'s view.
  - `status` adds a `tool calls:` line. When nothing is serving, `status` and `stop` still say "Cua Driver daemon is not running" and exit 1. They add a line when a dead daemon's socket is left over (`Stale`, only ever an actual socket), or when a file that is not a socket occupies the path. A starting daemon makes `status` print "Cua Driver daemon is starting" and exit 1.
  - The Unix standalone lock claim now waits up to 2 s, as Windows already did, so the probe briefly taking the lock cannot refuse a real launch.
  - The early claim takes only the lock. A dead daemon's socket is removed after startup authorization passes, just before bind, and only if it is a socket. A rejected launch, such as `--permission-mode invalid`, leaves whatever is at `--socket` alone. Before this PR, any file there was unlinked.
  - On Unix the presence probe connects without blocking. A full accept queue is retried until the probe's 2 s reply deadline and never holds the probe, which a blocking `connect` does on Linux. The socket check counts a full queue as a listener that is still there. `send_request` keeps its blocking connect.
  - The probe only reads the lock and never creates it. On Windows its `metadata` request runs on a thread with a 2 s bound, because the pipe client has no read timeout. If a pipe accepts but never replies, that thread stays blocked until the CLI process exits. Each probe waits out its bound before the next one, so `stop` leaves at most about six such threads behind. Cancellable overlapped pipe I/O would remove them, but it is a larger change to the shared pipe client.
- Lock handoff on macOS: the launching process keeps its lock descriptor open across the disclaimed `posix_spawn`. The child validates the raw descriptor first: it must be the same lock file (device and inode). The child then marks it close-on-exec, refusing it if that fails, so tool and helper processes never inherit it. Only after that does it take ownership, and only if the lock is held by that open file or by nobody. The parent restores close-on-exec after the spawn.
- Embedded daemons take no lock, as before. The probe reports an embedded daemon that has bound its socket but not answered yet as `Stale`. Everything that acts on `Stale` first checks whether the socket still accepts connections, and treats it as held if it does.
- Risk and rollback: the risk is in the lifecycle of `serve`, `stop` and `status`. Revert this PR to restore the old behavior. Nothing persistent changes.

## Validation

- Focused tests (new, in `serve.rs` `presence_tests`):
  - `stop_waits_for_a_starting_daemon_and_stops_it`: the lock is held, nothing is serving yet, and `stop` must wait, stop the daemon once it serves, and leave `Absent`. It fails when `stop` treats `Starting` as not running (mutation-checked).
  - `stop_sees_a_launch_that_claims_the_socket_just_after_it_starts`: `stop` starts before anything holds the lock, and the launch claims 150 ms later. It fails without the settle window (mutation-checked).
  - `only_a_stale_socket_is_cleared_and_only_after_the_claim`: claiming does not unlink, and a non-socket file is never removed.
  - `a_dead_daemons_socket_reads_as_stale_and_released`: covers Absent, then Stale, then Starting when the lock is held. It also checks that a stale file counts as released and that the probe leaves the lock free.
  - `a_listening_socket_that_never_answers_is_held_not_stale` (Unix): a bound socket that never answers, with no lock, is not released, refuses a launch, makes `stop` report still starting, and is not unlinked by the stale-socket cleanup. Once the listener closes, it counts as released and a launch may proceed.
  - `a_listener_with_a_full_accept_queue_is_held_and_never_blocks_a_probe` (Linux): a backlog-0 listener with a full accept queue. Probing it returns within its deadline instead of blocking in `connect`, reads as held rather than released, refuses a launch, and is not unlinked. Once the listener closes, it counts as released.
  - `a_symlink_to_a_socket_that_never_answers_is_held` (Unix): a symlink to a listener that never answers reads `Absent`, is not released and refuses a launch, until the listener closes.
  - `a_fifo_at_the_lock_path_never_blocks_a_probe` (Unix): a FIFO at the lock path reads as `Absent` within the deadline.
  - `presence_reports_a_permissions_pending_gate`: a real `run_serve` with the gate pending reads as `Serving { gate: PermissionsPending }`, and as `Open` once the gate opens. It fails when `metadata` drops the flag (mutation-checked).
  - `a_relaunch_adopts_only_the_lock_its_launcher_holds` (macOS): an inherited descriptor is adopted, while a foreign open of the lock file or an unrelated file is refused.
  - `metadata_from_a_daemon_without_a_gate_reads_as_open` (core).
  - `a_daemon_whose_pipe_never_answers_has_not_released` (Windows, `pipe_release_tests`, run by Windows shard 1): one pipe instance that never replies, held busy by the first probe. It reads `Absent` without the lock and `Starting` with it. Neither counts as released, `stop` reports it as still starting, and a launch is refused, until the pipe closes.
  - `a_launch_never_serves_beside_a_pipe_taken_after_its_check` (Windows, `pipe_release_tests`): a pipe taken after the launch claimed its lock makes `serve` fail at once instead of opening a second instance, and leaves the holder's PID file untouched.
- CI: the macOS unit lane and Windows shard 1 now run the whole `cua-driver` binary test suite, which includes `presence_tests` and `pipe_release_tests`. Running the Windows suite whole exposed one existing test, `extension_manager::tests::active_perception_extension_resolves_owned_worker_arguments`, that matched worker paths as strings with forward slashes; it now compares them as paths.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` for `cua-driver`, `cua-driver-core` and `cua-driver-sdk` are green on macOS. Windows clippy (`cargo xwin clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, cross-compiled) is green, and `bin/ci --quick` is green.
- Manual, macOS, the original repro (`serve &` then an immediate `stop` on a private socket, with an isolated HOME):
  - the installed 0.44.0 binary and this branch before the lock moved: "not running", exit 1, daemon still alive;
  - this branch: `stop` exit 0 and the daemon is gone, 10/10 runs with the disclaim shortcut and 10/10 on the real disclaimed relaunch path.
  - `serve --permission-mode invalid` exits 64 and leaves a regular file at `--socket` intact.
  - `status` gives the expected output for absent, serving (`tool calls: open`), stale after `kill -9`, and relaunching over a stale socket. A second `serve` gets the single already-running message with the daemon's PID.
- Known gap, macOS socket probe: a Unix socket counts as no longer listening only after `connect` is refused on every one of five tries over about half a second, or the path is gone. Any other error counts as still listening. macOS also refuses a live listener whose accept queue is full, so a listener whose queue stays full for that whole window still reads as gone. In that case `main` unlinked the path unconditionally before binding.
- Known gaps: Linux was not built on this machine, so CI's Linux lane covers it. The `PermissionsPending` line in `status` was not exercised live, because that needs an ungranted interactive TCC gate. The unit test covers the probe that feeds it.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.

title: fix(cua-driver): isolate semantic AX lookups by renderer target
body:
Salvaged from #5387 by @Iflaqbhat. Their two commits are kept as authored. The only commit on top is a merge of main, because that fork doesn't allow maintainer edits.

Fixes #5381

## Why

`get_browser_state` could hang in `SemanticDocument::page` when an out-of-process iframe reused AX node ids from the page. The subtree, ancestor and outline lookups used one AX-id map across all merged frames, so a parent id could resolve to a node in another renderer and form a cycle. The outline depth walk had no cycle guard.

## What changed

- `scoped_indices`, `with_ancestors` and `render_outline` key nodes by `(oopif_target_id, ax_id)` (`AxNodeKey`). Same-process iframes share the page's AX namespace and stay linked. Separate OOPIF targets are isolated from each other.
- `render_outline` stops its parent walk when it revisits a node.
- Five unit tests cover colliding ids across targets, dangling parents, cross-target and same-frame cycles, and same-process iframe content under a scoped container.

## Scope

Only `cua-driver-core/src/browser/semantic.rs` changes. Raw AX ids, backend node ids, action refs and response fields are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Semantic snapshots in `get_browser_state`. Every frame collected from one OOPIF session gets that session's target id (`engine.rs` semantic collection), and same-process frames get `None`, so the key follows Chrome's AX id namespaces.

## Verification

The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) pass on the merged head. The contributor reports the core suite and clippy passing on 17b9a45. A live browser repro hasn't run.

title: fix(cua-driver): stamp the window-local point on the public background click fallback
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS before 27, a background window click that falls back to the public `CGEventPostToPid` route (when SkyLight's `SLEventPostToPid` does not resolve) stamps the screen point through `CGEventSetWindowLocation`. A public pid post needs the window-local point, so the click hit-tests outside the target window and is dropped. Every other public pid post in `mouse.rs` already stamps the window-local point. The route plan built `public_window_location` but never read it.
- What changed: `chromium_click_route_plan` always puts the window-local point in `public_window_location`. `click_at_xy_chromium` resolves the route once per gesture and stamps the location that matches it. SkyLight keeps the version-gated stamp from #5492: the window-local point on macOS 27+, the screen point before.

## Related work

Salvaged from #5389

kianwoon's first commit is cherry-picked as authored, with conflicts resolved against #5492, which already shipped the macOS 27 window-local stamp for SkyLight. One commit of ours on top corrects an inline comment. Their other three commits are left out:

- The target-class transport selection (Chromium on SkyLight, every other target on the public route) is not included. Its evidence that SkyLight drops on a plain AppKit `NSButton` came from the probe before it ran `prepare_background_pixel_click`, the prelude the production click tool runs first. The fourth commit shows the same missing prelude made a Chromium target drop. Moving every non-Chromium background click off SkyLight would change the default route for all of them on that evidence.
- The probe example (`background_window_local_click.rs`) and its `--prologue` flag were the measurement tool, not product code.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only, and only on the public fallback inside background clicks, which runs when the SkyLight symbol is missing. The SkyLight route and foreground clicks are unchanged. Other platform adapters are untouched.
- Risk and rollback: low. Revert the PR to restore the screen-point stamp on the fallback.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `public_route_stamps_window_local_point_from_win_local_inputs` pins the public stamp to the window-local inputs and SkyLight's to the screen point before macOS 27. `capture_bound_background_route_preserves_nonzero_origin_hit` is updated for the public field. The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) pass. The `platform-macos` unit tests and clippy need macOS and run in CI.
- Manual or platform evidence: none from us. #5389 reports that a background public pid post delivers to a plain AppKit button on macOS 26 only when it carries the window-local point.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the fallback does not run on a host where SkyLight resolves, so no live run covers it.

title: perf(cua-driver): batch macOS action attribute reads
body:
## Summary

macOS action tools read several attributes of the same accessibility element through separate cross-process calls. Batch the adjacent reads used for click/type labels, popup options, Finder name-field checks, menu shortcuts, and post-write value classification.

String-only groups use `copy_string_attrs` from #7854. Mixed string/boolean/number/URL groups use a small typed reader backed by the same batch request and refusal/timeout handling. Missing or incorrectly typed slots retain the single-read decoding rules; refused batches fall back to individual reads. Reads separated by input, flushing or settling remain separate.

Refs #7856. Builds on #7854.

`ax/reveal_scroll.rs` was also inspected: its current implementation has only one string attribute read per ancestor and no boolean reads, so there is no string/boolean group to combine there. Geometry and tree traversal are outside this change.

## Compatibility and risk

macOS only; no tool schema, permission or public API changes. The main risk is differences in application support for batched AX reads. Existing per-attribute fallback is retained. No RFC is needed for this internal optimization.

## Validation

Candidate commit: `86fad6c6a699c140be6f275305f7550c0770700c`. Its Git tree (`9a205eea34ddf69d55ad14ee6c7106a6756de42b`) matches the locally tested tree exactly.

- Batch reader unit tests: 5 passed, including mixed types, missing values and unanswered batches.
- Focused action tests: click 15, type_text 31, set_value 21, invoke_menu 17 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --lib --tests --locked -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `bin/ci --base upstream/main --quick --no-install`: 5 passed, 3 skipped. Quick mode skips unit tests, Clippy and release binding generation; focused tests and Clippy were run separately.

The full macOS library suite did not complete in the restricted local environment: native input tests stalled with macOS service connection errors. A broader tools-only run also failed an own-process activation test and stalled. These runs are not claimed as passing. Live AX behavior, performance measurements and the canonical desktop matrix remain unverified; this PR stays draft pending platform evidence and maintainer scope review.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11 GNOME Text Editor (GTK4): first keystrokes after foreground activation are lost while type_text reports success
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (Linux, X11 keyboard input)

### Summary

Typing into GNOME Text Editor (GTK4) on X11 gives a different wrong result on each run. After the window is brought to the front, the first keystrokes are lost, and the driver still reports success.

### Reproduction

1. GNOME X11 session. Open a file containing `initial` in GNOME Text Editor.
2. Leave another window focused.
3. With Cua Driver, replace the document text with an ASCII sentence that starts with `Native Linux`, save, then read the file from disk.
4. Repeat several times.

Our harness ran this sequence through the driver's MCP tools. The exact call list was not preserved.

### Expected behavior

Every run leaves exactly the new sentence in the file. If the driver cannot confirm the window is ready for keys, it refuses instead of reporting success.

### Actual behavior

Three failing runs gave three different results:

- the old text `initial` stayed after the new text;
- the file did not change at all;
- the first 13 characters (`Native Linux `) were missing.

Every run reported success. With forced foreground delivery only, ASCII passed and non-ASCII still failed.

### Environment

- Observed on: cua-driver-rs 0.46.1 (Linux x86_64 build).
- Code references below are pinned to `cua-driver-rs-v0.55.0` (8f484f305), where the paths involved look unchanged for this case. We have not re-run the scenario on 0.55.0 yet.
- OS: GNOME on X11, in a fresh VM.
- Exact GNOME, application and browser versions were not recorded in our run.

### Evidence

No logs were kept from the run. We read the relevant code at 0.55.0:

- The foreground transaction confirms that the X server reports `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` and input focus, then sends XTest keys at once ([interaction/mod.rs#L231-L236](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/interaction/mod.rs#L231-L236), [input/foreground.rs#L780-L790](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/input/foreground.rs#L780-L790)). Nothing waits for the GTK4 client itself to have processed the focus change.
- `type_text` uses `ForegroundOptions::pointer()` (800 ms settle, `keyboard: false`) for its XTest typing ([tools/type_text.rs#L1069-L1074](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/type_text.rs#L1069-L1074), [#L1177-L1184](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/type_text.rs#L1177-L1184)). `ForegroundOptions::keyboard()` exists for exactly this case: "GTK/VCL toplevels accept [focus] a beat after being raised" ([input/foreground.rs#L58-L76](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/input/foreground.rs#L58-L76)).

We do not know the cause. These two points are the suspected area.

### Workaround and additional context

No reliable workaround. e730ff4cb (#7145) fixed early-key loss in the uinput buffer, which is a different route from this XTest path. Since 7bdd2b44a (#7164), `press_key` and `click` restore focus after each call, so a multi-step edit re-activates the window several times.

### Submission checks

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11 VS Code: non-ASCII type_text reorders or garbles characters (Größe becomes Görße)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (Linux, X11 keyboard input)

### Summary

Typing non-ASCII text into VS Code on X11 produces reordered or garbled characters, and the driver reports success. ASCII text is typed correctly.

### Reproduction

1. GNOME X11 session with a US keyboard layout. Open an empty file in VS Code.
2. Call `type_text` with `Größe`. Both `ö` and `ß` are missing from the layout, so the driver borrows spare keycodes.
3. Read the editor content. Repeat several times.

### Expected behavior

The editor contains `Größe` on every run, or the call fails.

### Actual behavior

- Some runs reordered characters: `Größe` became `Görße`.
- Other runs produced garbage such as `N n n`.
- ASCII text passed in the same setup. Each failing call reported success.

### Environment

- Observed on: cua-driver-rs 0.46.1 (Linux x86_64 build).
- Code references below are pinned to `cua-driver-rs-v0.55.0` (8f484f305), where the paths involved look unchanged for this case. We have not re-run the scenario on 0.55.0 yet.
- OS: GNOME on X11, in a fresh VM.
- Exact GNOME, application and browser versions were not recorded in our run.

### Evidence

No logs were kept from the run. Relevant code at 0.55.0:

- `type_text_in_spare_batches` remaps every unmapped character of a batch first, then sends all the keys ([input/mod.rs#L3989-L4046](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/input/mod.rs#L3989-L4046)). Each remap is an `XChangeKeyboardMapping` and a `MappingNotify` to the client.
- Chromium/Electron reloads its keymap asynchronously after `MappingNotify`. Keys on remapped keycodes can be translated before or after that reload, while keys on stable keycodes are translated at once. This is our guess at why the order changes. We have not proved it.

### Workaround and additional context

No workaround in the driver. e730ff4cb (#7145, #7146) added hold and gap timing for borrowed keycodes and a 150 ms delayed restore (`SPARE_KEYCODE_IDLE`). That may explain why the `N n n` case is less likely now. We see nothing addressing the reordering.

title: [Bug]: Linux X11 Firefox: default type_text reports "Typed N character(s) (via AT-SPI)" but the field stays empty
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (Linux, AT-SPI text input)

### Summary

In Firefox on Linux X11, `type_text` in the default (background) delivery mode reports `Typed 12 character(s) (via AT-SPI)`, but the focused form field stays empty. Only forced foreground delivery fills the field.

### Reproduction

1. GNOME X11 session. Open a page with a plain HTML text input in Firefox and focus the input.
2. Call `type_text` with a 12-character string, without `delivery_mode` and without an element index.
3. Look at the field, or read its value.

### Expected behavior

The field contains the text. If the AT-SPI write did not land, the driver reports failure or uses another route. It must not report success.

### Actual behavior

The tool result is `Typed 12 character(s) (via AT-SPI)`, and the field is empty.

### Environment

- Observed on: cua-driver-rs 0.46.1 (Linux x86_64 build).
- Code references below are pinned to `cua-driver-rs-v0.55.0` (8f484f305), where the paths involved look unchanged for this case. We have not re-run the scenario on 0.55.0 yet.
- OS: GNOME on X11, in a fresh VM.
- Exact GNOME, application and browser versions were not recorded in our run.

### Evidence

Relevant code at 0.55.0:

- The default branch calls `atspi::type_into_editable(pid, text)`. On `Ok(())` it returns success at once ([tools/type_text.rs#L1093-L1105](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/type_text.rs#L1093-L1105)).
- `type_into_editable` writes into the focused editable from the event log, or the best editable found by a tree walk ([atspi/native.rs#L3166-L3190](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/atspi/native.rs#L3166-L3190)). It returns `Ok` when the EditableText call is acknowledged.
- The success result has no value read-back. Only Chromium embedders get the `unverified` wording ([tools/type_text.rs#L280-L293](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/type_text.rs#L280-L293)). Firefox (Gecko) gets the plain "Typed N character(s)" text.
- A read-back helper already exists for element-addressed inserts, `type_text_ax_result_verified` ([tools/type_text.rs#L185-L250](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/type_text.rs#L185-L250)). The default branch does not use it.
- abc5c46ca (#5574) covers writes that were sent and then errored or timed out. It does not cover a write that is acknowledged but never shows up.

### Workaround and additional context

Forcing `delivery_mode: "foreground"` fills the field. Possible fixes: read the value back on this path and fall back or refuse on mismatch, or treat Gecko like the Chromium embedders.

title: [Bug]: Linux GNOME X11: input is accepted while org.gnome.ScreenSaver reports the screen locked
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (Linux, lock-state policy)

### Summary

On GNOME X11, while the screen is locked (`org.gnome.ScreenSaver.GetActive` returns `true`), the driver still accepts and sends input in both the default (background) and the foreground delivery modes. We expected a `screen_locked` refusal.

### Reproduction

1. GNOME X11 session. Lock the screen.
2. Confirm: `gdbus call --session -d org.gnome.ScreenSaver -o /org/gnome/ScreenSaver -m org.gnome.ScreenSaver.GetActive` returns `(true,)`.
3. Call `type_text` on an application window: once in default mode, once with `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.

### Expected behavior

Both calls fail with `screen_locked` and send nothing.

### Actual behavior

Both calls were accepted and reported success.

### Environment

- Observed on: cua-driver-rs 0.46.1 (Linux x86_64 build).
- Code references below are pinned to `cua-driver-rs-v0.55.0` (8f484f305), where the paths involved look unchanged for this case. We have not re-run the scenario on 0.55.0 yet.
- OS: GNOME on X11, in a fresh VM.
- Exact GNOME, application and browser versions were not recorded in our run.

### Evidence

Relevant code at 0.55.0:

- **Background routes never check the lock.** `admit_lock` is called only from the foreground transaction ([interaction/mod.rs#L117-L136](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/interaction/mod.rs#L117-L136), [#L231-L233](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/interaction/mod.rs#L231-L233)), desktop input ([tools/impl_.rs#L4434-L4440](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/impl_.rs#L4434-L4440)) and capture ([capture_action_frame.rs#L23-L27](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/capture_action_frame.rs#L23-L27)). The default `type_text` routes have no lock check: AT-SPI `type_into_editable`/`insert_text`, Tk send and the MPX virtual keyboard ([tools/type_text.rs#L1093-L1192](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/tools/type_text.rs#L1093-L1192)). The core `screen_locked` refusal in `background_input.rs` is not used by platform-linux.
- **Foreground accepts when the lock state is unknown.** The X11 transaction always passes `focused = Known(true)` ([interaction/mod.rs#L232](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/interaction/mod.rs#L232)). `policy::lock` admits `Unknown` lock plus `Known(true)` focus ([interaction/policy.rs#L27-L44](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/interaction/policy.rs#L27-L44)). So on X11, an unknown lock state never refuses.
- **`facts::locked()` can return `Unknown` on a locked GNOME session** ([interaction/facts.rs#L33-L103](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/8f484f30586eef722bede7a5ce315de1148cca96/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/interaction/facts.rs#L33-L103)). We did not capture which branch ran. Candidates:
  - `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` in the driver's environment does not contain `GNOME`, so it queries `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` instead.
  - `GetSessionByPID` for the driver process resolves to another logind session, or to none.
  - The probe exceeds the 250 ms cap.

### Workaround and additional context

No workaround. Possible fixes:

- check the lock on every background input route;
- refuse X11 window input when the lock state is `Unknown` on a desktop known to report it;
- fall back to logind's `LockedHint` when the screensaver probe fails.

Related: #5964 (stale X11 window captures while locked).

title: fix(cua-driver): keep browser attachment state on the grant
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: whether an existing-profile browser attachment holds a socket, has parked it for the next session, or owes a remote-debugging cleanup was spread across three owners: the grant registry, the CDP pool's empty-holder "parked" sockets with their own idle reaper, and the engine's `pending_existing_profile_cleanups` queue. When a reconnect found the approved endpoint gone (`browser_requires_setup`) or owned by another process (`browser_endpoint_owner_mismatch`), the grant stayed live with its reconnect budget but held no socket. The agent got a refusal with no `next_call`, and nothing recorded that state.
- What changed: each grant now carries one `Attachment`:
  - `Attached`: the grant holds the shared socket.
  - `Parked { since }`: the session ended normally. The grant authorizes nothing but keeps the already-consented socket open until the 30 minute parking bound passes.
  - `NeedsSetup { refusal }`: the endpoint could not be proven. The approval and reconnect budget are kept and no socket is held. Every call reports the refusal with `detail.attachment: "needs_setup"` and a `browser_prepare` `next_call` until `browser_prepare` attaches the browser again.
  - `Expired`: the grant ended and turning remote debugging back off failed. The record stays only for its session end to retry the cleanup.

## Plan

1. `grant.rs`: add `Attachment` to `ExistingProfileGrant`. The registry keeps live grants (`Attached` / `NeedsSetup`) by key and ended grants (`Parked` / `Expired`) in a list that authorizes nothing. Transitions: `end_session` (Attached → Parked, or released when cleanup is owed), `mint` over an attached grant (it parks the replaced generation, so the new one joins the socket without a prompt), `needs_setup` (generation-checked), `owe_cleanup`, `take_idle_parked` / `take_parked_on` / `take_parked`.
2. `engine.rs`:
   - Reconnect (`connect_existing_profile`), bind (`get_browser_state`) and mutation revalidation move a grant to `NeedsSetup` on those two refusals and release its socket.
   - `attached_existing_profile_grant` reports the stored refusal, or revokes the grant when the browser process changed.
   - Expiry, revocation and cleanup releases close the socket and also end the grants parked on it, which matches releasing the last holder before.
   - The parked reaper and `close_parked_browser_sockets` (used by revoke-all) now run over the grant registry.
   - A reconnect attempt starts only while the grant is still attached at the generation it read. A socket claimed for a grant that moved on during the dial is released. A session end that finds its socket already closed or past its absolute bound ends every grant parked on it. When a holder joins a shared socket, the pool asks the grant registry under its entry lock whether any holder still keeps the socket in use. A socket held only by grants parked past their idle bound is dialed fresh, as the pool's own idle check on reuse did before.
   - `pending_existing_profile_cleanups` is deleted.
3. `cdp_ws.rs`: the pool keeps socket handles, holders, and the absolute bound measured from the consent that opened the socket. The parking bound is read from the grant registry through `SharedSocketHolders`. `SharedSocketRelease`, the idle TTL, `last_used_at`, the pool reaper and `close_parked` are deleted.

## Related work

Refs the cua-driver everystate audit, implicit state #10.

Overlaps, checked against their current heads:
- #8066 also replaces `pending_existing_profile_cleanups` (with `SetupCleanups`) and splits the reconnect loop. It conflicts here. When it rebases, its running-cleanup bookkeeping can sit on the `Expired` grant record instead of a side map.
- #7678's 403-declined branch in the reconnect `select!` is untouched by this diff and rebases cleanly.
- #8275, #8237, #8176, #7731 and #8109 touch other parts of `engine.rs`.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible: after a reconnect or bind finds the approved endpoint gone or foreign-owned, calls keep returning the same refusal code, now with `detail.attachment` and a `browser_prepare` `next_call`. Before, each call re-ran the endpoint proof and could silently reattach if the endpoint came back. Now only `browser_prepare` leaves `NeedsSetup`, which is the explicit transition the audit asked for. A changed process still revokes the grant, and expiry still applies.
- Parking, the absolute socket bound and remote-debugging cleanup keep their timing. A parked grant still never authorizes a call, and its consent is revoked at session end as before.
- Failed cleanups are now retried at the end of either the grant's public or its transport session. The old queue was keyed by the public session only.
- Rollback: revert this PR. No persisted state changes.

## Validation

The scoped repository checks:
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::`: 318 passed, 1 ignored (the existing manual real-Chrome test).
- New grant unit tests: Attached → Parked, a grant owing cleanup is released rather than parked, re-mint parks the replaced generation, Attached → NeedsSetup (generation-checked), NeedsSetup → Expired, prepare out of NeedsSetup, a failed cleanup waits on its grant for session end, and closing a socket ends only the grants parked on it.
- New engine tests through the public tools: `get_browser_state` reports NeedsSetup with `next_call` for both a gone endpoint and a foreign owner, keeps reporting it after the endpoint returns, and attaches again after `browser_prepare`. A reconnect whose endpoint proof fails lands in NeedsSetup with its reconnect budget intact. A platform proof that itself refuses the owner during reconnect also lands in NeedsSetup. A revocation also closes a socket an ended session parked. A session end on a socket that is already gone ends every parked hold on it. The pool reports a socket past its absolute bound as not live. Revoke-all ends parked grants.
- Mutation-checked: disabling the NeedsSetup gate, the bind-path transition, the reconnect transition, the parked sweep on close, the revoke-all release, the typed-refusal mapping in reconnect, and the dead-socket sweep at session end each fails its owner test. The join-time parking check is covered by a pool test with a stand-in registry and a registry test of its answer; the engine wiring has no idle-bound test, since the engine's parking bound is the fixed 30 minutes. The reconnect/bind race guard is covered at the registry level (a reconnect attempt refuses a grant that moved on); the interleaving itself has no deterministic engine test.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver --tests -D warnings` and `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs): green.
- Not run on this host: a full `bin/ci`, the Windows cross-check and the desktop E2E lanes. The change is in platform-neutral core code; CI runs those lanes.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep since diff bases on the snapshot store
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `get_window_state` kept the rows a `since` diff compares against in a private cache in `window_state_view.rs` (8 per window, 32 in all, 15-minute TTL). The snapshot store that decides which element tokens are live is separate (8 per pid per session, no TTL). So a token could be stale while its diff base still diffed, or a live token's base could expire, and `since:"latest"` then quietly returned a full read with `since_status: unknown_snapshot`.
- What changed:
  - The rows each read renders are kept on its snapshot in `SnapshotStore`, which is now the only place `since` resolves against. A base retires with its tokens: when a later read replaces the snapshot, when it is evicted, when it is removed, or when its session ends. There is no separate count or TTL.
  - The read that replaces a snapshot can still diff against it. That read is what retires it, so the old tokens and the old base go stale at the same moment. The claim is dropped once that read is shaped, and also on a screenshot-only refresh.
  - When `since` names a retired snapshot, the fallback now says `since_status: "retired_snapshot"` instead of `unknown_snapshot`. `since:"latest"` takes the newest same-view read that is still a valid base. If the only match is a retired read, it reports `retired_snapshot` with that id instead of `no_baseline`.
  - `run_steps` finding a stale token's element again (`snapshot_row`, `snapshot_menu_path`) reads rows through a new `ToolRegistry::set_snapshot_rows` hook. Each platform installs its store next to the existing token-window resolver. Retired snapshots keep their rows (the newest 32) for this purpose only, and those rows are never a diff base.

## Related work

Refs the cua-driver everystate report, implicit state #5 ("diff-baseline cache separate from the token snapshot store").

RFC: none. The MCP-visible change is one new `since_status` value plus updated description text.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible: `since` against a snapshot whose tokens are stale now falls back to a full read with `retired_snapshot`. Before, it could still diff for up to 15 minutes. The common flow (read, act, re-read with `since:"latest"` or the previous id) still diffs. One flow does not: a read, then the same session reads with a different `query`, then a `since:"latest"` read of the first view. That now returns a full read with `retired_snapshot`, because the query read retired the first snapshot. `since` against another session's live read of the window still diffs, as before.
- `ViewContext` gains a `snapshots` field, so the three platform `get_window_state` call sites changed. #7555 also adds a `ViewContext` field, and the two will conflict mechanically only.
- Risk and rollback: the change is confined to `since` resolution and the stale-token row lookup. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - New `retiring_a_snapshot_retires_its_diff_base`: a snapshot that is evicted (LRU), ended with its session, or removed is not a base (`retired_snapshot`).
  - New `a_live_snapshot_keeps_its_diff_base_however_much_else_is_read`: a live snapshot still diffs after 40 other-session reads of the same window and 40 reads of other windows. The old cache's per-window and total caps would have dropped it.
  - New store tests: only the replacing read diffs against what it replaced, and a refresh ends that claim; a screenshot-only read keeps a snapshot's rows; retired rows still find a stale token's row and are capped.
  - Existing `since`, `latest`, re-find and menu-route tests now run against a real store.
  - Mutation check: when retired rows are allowed to act as a base, the new retirement test and two `since` tests fail.
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --tests` passed (1350 lib tests plus integration tests). `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib` passed (871). `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core -p platform-macos --tests -D warnings` was clean.
  - `bin/ci --quick` and `bin/ci --only driver-contract` passed.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. This host is macOS.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Linux and Windows crates could not be type-checked here because the host has no C cross toolchain for `rquickjs-sys`/`zstd-sys`. Their edits are one-line (`snapshots: &*state.snapshots` and `set_snapshot_rows`) and sit in the same scope as existing `state.snapshots` uses. The generated reference (`docs-ref:cua-driver`) and UniFFI TypeScript doc comment were updated by hand to match the new text, and CI's generator checks will confirm them.

title: fix(relay): stop machines retrying a refused token every few seconds
body:
## What changed for users and customers

A computer that the relay no longer recognises (removed from the account, token rotated, account deleted) used to knock on the relay every 15-30 seconds forever, and a few thousand of them did. Now it retries once, then waits one to sixty minutes between tries, logs a clear "sign in again" message once, and tries immediately when its token file changes (`cua host setup`).

## Root cause

`cua_relay::client::run` treated an HTTP 401 on the join like any transient failure: the backoff capped at 30 s and never grew past it, so a computer with a dead machine token retried about 2 to 4 times a minute indefinitely. On the relay, the join limiter ran before the token check, so each stale-token request also spent a join slot and could turn a legitimate machine's join into a 503.

Prod relay counters over about 5 h: 10.4k `unknown_machine_token` on join and 6.1k on the machines API (pending-deletion polls from builds before the 1 h back-off landed), about 3.8k/h in the live log sample. These 401s are cheap (rejected before the WebSocket upgrade, no state kept), so on their own they do not explain memory growth.

## Fix

- Client: new `SessionEnd::Unauthorized` for a 401 join. The first 401 is one ordinary retry (it re-reads the token file, which is the only "refresh" a machine token has). From the second, the wait starts at `min_reauth_backoff` (60 s), doubles to `max_reauth_backoff` (1 h), with 50-100% jitter, and ends early when the token file's contents change. One `error` log line says to sign in again.
- Server: the machine join checks the credential before the join limiter, so refused tokens get a 401 without taking a slot.
- No rate limiting by IP or token: the data shows the volume is small and already cheap, so it is not warranted.

## Tests

- `tests/unauthorized_backoff.rs`: a relay that answers 401 sees 2 to 3 joins in 3 s (was dozens); a new token in the file ends the wait.
- `tests/reconnect_storm.rs`: stale tokens get 401 and leave the slot for a real machine.
- Unit test for the backoff schedule.

Already-released clients keep their old behaviour until they update.
