title: fix(cua-driver): give authorization one AuthorizationPhase clock
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: authorization had two idle and expiry clocks that ran independently of each other and of the session lifecycle. One was on `EffectiveAuthorizationContext` (`expires_at`, `idle_ttl`, a sticky `idle_expired` flag, `revoked`). The other was on `SessionManifest` (its own `last_authorized_dispatch` and sticky `idle_expired`). They fired in either order. A call could refresh the context lease and then be refused by the manifest lease. Lifecycle revival read neither clock.
- What changed:
  - `EffectiveAuthorizationContext` owns one `AuthorizationPhase { Active { last_dispatch }, IdleExpired, Expired, Revoked }` behind one lock. It combines the context's TTLs with the manifest's declared `expires_after` and `idle_timeout`, using the shorter idle TTL. `phase()` reads it. `commit_authorized_dispatch()` refreshes it, or returns the terminal phase, without refreshing anything on a refusal.
  - `SessionManifest` keeps only its declared limits. `is_idle_expired`, `check_lifetime`, `commit_authorized_dispatch` and the `authorize_dispatch` alias are removed (no callers outside core). Compatibility contexts built from the configured manifest share one process-wide clock, as the manifest's clock was shared before, and status `capability_manifest.idle_expired` reads it.
  - Dispatch checks the phase before any lifecycle work. `start_session` on an idle-expired, expired or revoked context refuses and leaves the ended episode ended. It no longer appears to start a session that every later call would be denied in. Refusal codes are unchanged (`permission_denied` for expiry, `authorization_revoked` for revocation), and the refusal gains `authorization_phase`.

## Related work

Refs the cua-driver everystate report, implicit state #8 (one authorization clock).

RFC: not required. No public SDK, CLI, MCP or protocol shape changes. The refusal codes stay the same and only add a field.

## Compatibility and risk

- Scope: only the authorization clocks. It does not include the episode identity / lifecycle map rewrite (#1/B2) or any other everystate item, and `session.rs` is untouched. It stays compatible with #3369, which calls `context.commit_authorized_dispatch().map_err(|_| …)`.
- User-visible impact:
  - A trusted delegated session whose manifest declares a shorter `idle_timeout` than the session's `idle_ttl` now gets the shorter value as its lifecycle idle TTL too, so the lifecycle and authorization expire together.
  - Status `idle_expired` now turns true as soon as the idle timeout has passed. Before, it only flipped on the next call.
  - The idle comparison is now `>=` everywhere. Before, the context used `>=` and the manifest used `>`.
- Tradeoff: the configured manifest's process-wide clock is matched by manifest sha256, so two compatibility contexts loaded from identical manifest contents share it. Any other manifest gets its own clock per context, as it did per manifest instance before.
- Risk and rollback: core-only change, one commit, revert is clean.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - New unit tests in `session_authorization.rs` cover Active → IdleExpired (sticky, and a refused commit refreshes nothing), Active → Expired (absolute expiry takes precedence over idle), and any phase → Revoked. They also show the manifest's idle timeout driving the context clock in standard, bounded and unrestricted mode, and a delegated session's lifecycle idle TTL following the shorter manifest idle.
  - New `tool.rs` test `start_session_cannot_revive_an_episode_its_authorization_phase_denies`: for each terminal phase, `start_session` on an ended episode refuses with the phase and the episode stays ended. Mutation check: with the dispatch phase check disabled, this test fails.
  - `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver-sdk` passes on macOS, `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --tests` is clean, and `bin/ci --quick` passes.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. This is platform-independent core logic.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the full scoped repository checks (clippy across crates, Windows cross-check, bindings) run in CI.

title: feat(cua-relay): drain connections on SIGTERM before closing tunnels
body:
## What
On SIGTERM/SIGINT the relay now drains before it closes tunnels:
1. New machine tunnels and mesh connections get 503 + `Retry-After` (checked at the door and again at insertion, so none slips in unseen). Clients already treat this as "come back shortly".
2. Open tunnels stay up while client streams already running finish, up to `CUA_RELAY_DRAIN_SECS`.
3. Then every tunnel closes cleanly (yamux GoAway plus a WebSocket close; mesh close code 4000, which clients already treat as "reconnect now") right before the process exits, so the next relay takes the state lock at once.

The hard stop is drain plus `CUA_RELAY_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS`. Default `CUA_RELAY_DRAIN_SECS=0` keeps today's behaviour, so nothing changes until a manifest sets it. A drain report is logged (tunnels, streams at start, streams cut, wait time).

## Why (plain words)
Today every rollout cuts every running session the moment the old relay is told to stop. Now running sessions get a bounded chance to finish, and tunnels close at the last moment instead of the first. Step 2 of the relay zero-downtime plan (the boot-id header is #8308). The restart gap for tunnels is not removed (single relay, single state writer); client-side resume and multi-replica are the follow-ups.

## Tests
New `tests/drain.rs`: a running request finishes while a new tunnel is refused; the drain is bounded when a stream is stuck; drain 0 closes at once. Existing handover, shutdown, reconnect-storm and probe tests pass; clippy clean.

title: fix(relay): cut per-connection memory and give freed memory back
body:
Part of CUA-3138 (prod relay memory).

## What users get
The relay holds less memory per connected computer and phone and gives freed memory back to the system, so it stops creeping toward its memory limit and the out-of-memory restarts that drop every live session.

## What we found
- Prod relay (4e5a10e78, 8Gi limit) reached about 2.9 GB in its first hours with about 30 open streams, then went flat: +0.3 MB in 7 minutes at 5 h of uptime. The curve is concave, not linear.
- No leak on the suspected paths. Session replace, mesh reconnect, plan-limit refusal and rejected client routes all free their state (also covered by `tests/churn_bounded.rs`).
- Memory scales with connections: about 1.6k mesh nodes and 1.6k machine tunnels. Each mesh WebSocket allocated the default 128 KiB read buffer up front, for frames that hold one packet.
- glibc malloc keeps every peak. In a churn run on Linux (11k-node registry, ~1.3k mesh connections, flapping keys, machine replaces, rejected HTTP), glibc RSS stayed at its 264 MB peak after the churn stopped.
- Every mesh reconnect, disconnect and endpoint report rewrote the whole mesh registry (about 4.5 MB of JSON at prod size), about 3 times a second in prod (`cua_relay_state_writes_total{store="mesh"}` +1,411 in 7 min), for a change to `last_seen` only.

## Changes
- Mesh WebSocket read buffer: 16 KiB, down from 128 KiB.
- `cua-relay` binary runs on jemalloc with its background purge thread. New gauges: `cua_relay_heap_allocated_bytes`, `cua_relay_heap_resident_bytes` and `cua_relay_heap_retained_bytes`. A real leak grows `allocated`; allocator retention grows only the gap to `cua_relay_process_resident_bytes`.
- Mesh registry: a change to `last_seen` only is written at most every 5 minutes and at shutdown. New nodes and pairings are still written before they are confirmed.
- The "replacing previous session" log line now includes both versions and the old session's age, to find two installs that share one computer id.

## Measured (same churn run, Linux, 240 s churn then 60 s quiet)
| build | live heap under churn | RSS under churn | RSS after churn |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (glibc) | n/a | 264 MB | 264 MB (kept) |
| jemalloc only | 194 MB | 328 MB | 183 MB (heap 11 MB) |
| this PR | 50 MB | 184 MB | 170 MB (heap 12 MB) |

## Tests
- New `tests/mesh_registry_writes.rs`: six reconnects of a known mesh node rewrote the registry 12 times on main (fails). With this PR it is 0 (passes), and a clean shutdown still writes `last_seen`.
- `cargo test -p cua-relay --features hosted`, `cargo clippy -p cua-relay --features hosted --all-targets -D warnings` and `bin/ci --quick` pass.

## Rollout
Reaches staging through the normal pin. Prod needs a promote, which reconnects every session once. After deploy, check that `cua_relay_heap_allocated_bytes` is flat and that RSS follows it.

title: [RFC]: Signed updater for standalone Cua Driver on macOS
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Provide a Cua-signed update path for standalone CuaDriver.app without giving the calling shell or agent general App Management access.

### Motivation and current state

On Apple Silicon macOS 27.2.1, standalone 0.53.0 runs normally, but App Management denies bundle writes from background maintenance. The 0.55.0 CLI still delegates to a shell installer that stops the driver before replacing it. No destructive test was run.

### Goals

Verified background updates at the existing app path; preserve working grants and driver availability; refuse before stopping if unauthorized.

### Non-goals

No changes to Accessibility, Screen Recording, system policy, or Cua Spaces enrollment.

### Proposal

Use a same-team signed, app-scoped updater or Apple-supported signed package. Verify the candidate and admission before stopping; keep a verified rollback.

### Alternatives considered

Homebrew targets the same protected bundle. Cua Spaces updates a different bundled driver. Broad App Management is not suitable for a shared agent.

### Compatibility and migration

Keep the existing standalone bundle identity and path. Document the supported migration and rollback.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Limit update authority to the vendor updater; accept only verified Cua releases; no broad permissions or extra user data collection.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

Test signed upgrades in a background user session, denial before stop, grant preservation, and rollback; confirm the new running version.

### Unresolved questions

Which signed update mechanism can Cua support for the standalone app?

### RFC document pull request

_No response_

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: fix(images): use Playwright's pinned Chromium in the Linux image (CVE-2026-130959)
body:
## What changed for users
Linux Spaces images (slim, full, docker tiers, and bench-web which inherits them) will ship Chromium 159 instead of Chromium 156.

## Why
The image installed Chromium from the xtradeb PPA, which only carries 156.0.8078.73 on both arches. That is below 158.0.8127.36, the fix for CVE-2026-130959. Same approach as #8202 (cuabot).

## Change
- New `playwright-chromium` build stage in `libs/images/linux/Dockerfile`: Node (existing pinned tarball + sha256) runs `playwright install chromium` at `PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION=1.65.1` (same as cuabot); only the browser directory is copied into slim. amd64 and arm64 get the same build.
- Installed as the real root-owned file `/usr/lib/chromium/chromium` (cua-driver's `browser_prepare` and `image.json` use that path and reject symlinks). `/usr/bin/chromium` and `chromium-browser` are a launcher (`files/chromium-launcher`) that sources `/etc/chromium.d/*` and execs it, so the per-runtime sandbox flags (`cua-sandbox`, `cua-chromium`) keep working.
- Managed policy is written to `/etc/chromium/policies/managed` and `/etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed` (Playwright's build is Chrome for Testing, Chrome-branded). `chromium.desktop` and a default `mimeapps.list` keep the menu, XFCE helper and default browser.
- Playwright's runtime libraries are added to slim's apt list.
- Build fails if the browser is older than `MIN_CHROMIUM_MAJOR=158`, if `ldd` reports a missing library, or if the payload is a symlink. Version is recorded in `/etc/cua-image/chromium-version`.
- `chromium-pin` CI check reworked (not removed): minimum must be >= 158, the pinned Playwright's `browsers.json` must ship >= the minimum, no xtradeb reference may return, libs/cuabot must pin the same Playwright. Still runs on PRs and daily.
- bench-web drops its own PPA install and inherits the base Chromium; the vendored xtradeb key is removed.

## Not verified
Not built locally (disk); CI builds the image. `bin/ci --quick --fix` passes. Window match `Chromium` in `image.json` launch_app is untested against Chrome for Testing's window class and title.

## Licence note
Playwright's Chromium is Google's Chrome for Testing build. The bench-web Dockerfile previously said this public image must not ship it; the comment and bench.json licence line are updated to match.

title: fix(ci): bin/ci quick sign-off works; docs image refs check runs crane anonymously
body:
Two root fixes so `bin/ci --quick --fix --signoff` produces the required `local-ci` status.

**1. A quick run could never be signed off.** Since 5 Nov the sign-off is the quick check, and `ci-gate` tells people to run `bin/ci --quick`, then `bin/ci --signoff`. But `--quick` marks every build-tier check (for example `sdk-bindings`) as skipped, and `signoff()` refused any run with a skipped check. The two rules contradicted each other, so agents ran the full suite. Skips now carry a kind. A `profile` skip is the mode leaving the build tier to GitHub CI on purpose; it is recorded as `deferred` and the status description says how many build checks were left to CI. An `unavailable` skip (missing tool, low disk, tripped guard) still blocks a sign-off in every mode. `--full` defers nothing, so its sign-off is as strict as before. Failures still block.

**2. The docs image refs check hung on a headless Mac.** `crane` read the Docker config and called the Docker Desktop credential helper (osxkeychain/desktop), which waits for a GUI. The 60 s `subprocess.run` timeout did not help, because killing crane left the helper holding the pipes. The refs are public, so the check now runs crane anonymously: crane has no `--anonymous` flag, so the script points `DOCKER_CONFIG` at an empty directory it creates, and crane never reaches a credential helper. No user env setting is needed. Each call runs in its own process group with a bounded timeout (`CUA_CRANE_TIMEOUT`, default 60 s); on timeout the group is killed and the check fails with a clear "timed out" error.

Tests: new cases in `.github/scripts/tests/test_bin_ci_logs.py` (quick sign-off with deferred checks, missing-tool skips still block in all modes, full is unchanged) and `scripts/images/tests/test_docs_image_refs.py` (a fake crane that hangs on a real Docker config resolves anonymously; a hung crane times out with an error). `bin/ci --quick --fix --signoff` on this branch now posts the sign-off.

Plain words: contributors and agents can sign off with the quick run again, and the docs image check no longer freezes on headless Macs.

title: fix(cua-driver): suppress macOS focus steal during isolated browser launch
body:
Salvaged from #6271

Refs #6270

## Why

On macOS, a cold isolated browser launch (`browser_prepare` with an isolated profile) spawns standalone Chromium straight from `std::process::Command`. Chromium calls `NSApp.activate` while it finishes launching, even with `--no-startup-window`, so it briefly takes the front and key focus from the user's window. @saariuslystoned's change guards that launch window.

## What changed

- `MacOsBrowserPlatform::spawn_isolated_browser` now holds a `FocusStealPreventer` suppression across the spawn, then runs `watch_self_activation` against the child for up to 2.8 s and hands the front back with `restore_front_app_if_browser_front`. The returned `GuardedIsolatedBrowserChild` stops that watch as soon as the child exits, is killed or is dropped. This is the contributor's commit, kept as authored and cherry-picked onto current main; the conflict resolution keeps main's `managed_extension_policy` and `security_prompt_open` next to the new method.
- On top of that, the leases, the watcher and the final restore share one `UndoWatch` (`watch_self_activation` now takes the watch it starts under). The final restore asks that watch first, so a driver activation or a user switch to the new browser during the launch window is no longer undone.
- The unit tests no longer call the live focus path (frontmost app, AppKit observers). They check that `GuardedIsolatedBrowserChild` stops the guard on `wait`, `try_wait`, `kill` and drop. The missing-executable refusal mapping matches the core default and is no longer tested through the macOS override.

## Scope

macOS isolated launch only. Existing-profile attach, the Windows and Linux platforms, and the core `BrowserPlatform` contract are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS isolated browser launch goes through the guard. It is bounded to the launch window and follows the focus arbiter's rules, so intentional activations are left alone. The existing attach guard (`SelfActivationGuard`) behaves the same as before: it passes a freshly armed watch.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): SPDX headers and rustfmt for `platform-macos` pass. Clippy, the crate's unit tests and macOS E2E need a macOS host and run in CI.
- The contributor reported a live macOS cold isolated Chrome launch with another app frontmost going from 78 focus or key steals to 0 under `FocusMonitor`. That run predates the shared-watch fix.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse removed --session-policy and Claude Code compat flags
body:
## Why

`--session-policy` and `--approve-session-policy` were deprecated aliases for `--capability-manifest` and `--approve-capability-manifest`. `--claude-code-computer-use-compat` had no effect on the tool surface. Each one still added a branch to CLI parsing and a line to help, the manifest and the reference docs. This PR removes all three. An old config that still passes one now fails with an error that says what to use instead. Before this change the aliases were accepted and the compat flag was silently ignored.

## What changed

- `cua-driver` exits 64 when it sees any of the three flags, in either the `--flag` or the `--flag=value` form, on any command. The check runs first in `parse_command`, ahead of `--help`, `--version` and every other argument check. The error names the replacement:
  - `--session-policy was removed; use cua-driver serve --capability-manifest <path> instead.`
  - `--approve-session-policy was removed; use cua-driver serve --approve-capability-manifest instead.`
  - `--claude-code-computer-use-compat was removed; it had no effect on the tool surface. Remove it and register the server as plain cua-driver mcp (see "Claude Code registration" in the Cua Driver README, or run cua-driver mcp-config --client claude).`
- The CLI no longer carries `claude_code_compat` from `mcp` to the daemon it auto-launches. `aliased_flag_value` is deleted. The SDK's `claude_code_compatibility` option is unchanged, and the CLI host passes `false`, which is what every launch already did in effect.
- Removed the three flags from `--help`, `cua-driver manifest`, the CLI docs JSON, `compat-fixtures/cli.json` (with a note in its README), `cli-specs/cua-driver.json`, the generated reference page, the README and `RUNTIME.md`.
- Dropped `--session-policy` from `CUA_DRIVER_VALUE_FLAGS` in `scripts/_install-common.sh`. That list must equal the CLI's `VALUE_FLAGS`, and `test_serve_detection_skips_the_same_value_flags_as_the_cli` enforces it.
- Added `CUA_DRIVER_REMOVED_VALUE_FLAGS` (`--session-policy`) to the same script. Linux upgrade and uninstall still skip its value, so they still recognise and stop a daemon an older release started as `cua-driver --session-policy <path> serve`.

## Scope

This PR covers only these three CLI flags. It leaves out the `type_text_chars` alias, the `set_config capture_scope` retirement and its module, the SDK `EmbeddedDriverHostOptions.session_policy_path` / `approve_session_policy` fields (a UniFFI binding surface), and the macOS resume marker's `NOT_REPLAYED_FLAGS` filter, which still drops `--approve-session-policy` from markers written by an older binary.

## Blast Radius

The change affects anyone whose launch config still passes one of these flags. That includes older Claude Code registrations that used `args: ["mcp", "--claude-code-computer-use-compat"]`. Those configs now fail at startup with exit 64 and the message above, where before they started normally. `cua-driver mcp-config` and `connect` stopped emitting the compat flag some time ago. The embedded host, the Spaces supervisor and the `mcp` daemon auto-launch already pass only `--capability-manifest` / `--approve-capability-manifest`.

## Verification

- `cargo check -p cua-driver --tests` on macOS: clean, no warnings.
- `test_uninstall_stops_daemons_from_other_copies.py`: 21 passed locally. Its serve-detection case now includes a legacy `--session-policy policy.yaml serve` command line, and that case fails when the removed-flags list is emptied.
- `bin/ci --quick` on this branch: 6 passed. Clippy, unit tests, the generated-reference check and the Windows cross-check were skipped because quick mode skips them. They run in CI.
- New owner test `removed_flags_fail_and_name_their_replacement` in `permission_policy_startup_test.rs` runs the binary with each removed flag on `serve`, `mcp` and bare invocation, including the `=` form, and checks for exit 64 and the exact message. `approved_capability_manifest_reaches_bounded_lifetime_validation` replaces the old alias test, so the canonical `--capability-manifest` path is still covered. The owner test also covers a removed flag combined with `--help`, `--version` or `--expected-pid`. A cold review found that those combinations had bypassed the check, and the second commit fixes that; extracted-parser repros now exit 64 for all three.

title: fix(cua-driver): deliver deep CDP replies instead of timing out
body:
Salvaged from #6338 by @chrisohearn. Their commit is kept as authored, rebased onto current main.

Refs #6299 (reply size over the 16 MiB frame limit; this PR fixes reply nesting depth, not size).

## Why

A full-depth `DOM.getDocument` reply nests two JSON levels per DOM level, so pages deeper than about 63 elements exceed serde_json's default 128-level recursion limit. The CDP reader dropped every frame it could not parse, so `get_browser_state` waited out the 20 s call timeout and then returned an incomplete `semantic_v2` snapshot or refused in `dom_refs_v1`.

## What changed

- `decode_frame` in `cdp_ws.rs` parses frames with serde_json's recursion limit replaced by an explicit 512-level bound, above the 300-level CBOR stack limit Chromium applies before it serializes a reply.
- A reply that still cannot be decoded fails its own call at once (`CallOutcome::Undecodable`), matched by the leading `id`, and the socket stays usable.
- Chromium's `CBOR: stack limit exceeded` refusal and the new decode error take the existing bounded-depth DOM fallback in `engine.rs`.

## Scope

The shared CDP reader in `cua-driver-core`, used by every platform adapter. The rebase onto main only merged `MockReply` with the `delay` and `response_ready` fields added on main since #6338 was opened. Reply size limits (#6307) are untouched.

## Blast Radius

Every CDP call reads frames through `decode_frame`. It adds one linear byte scan per frame before the parse. Frames under 128 levels parse exactly as before.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): formatting, headers and lockfiles pass.
- New mock-CDP tests cover replies at 300 and 511 levels, a reply over the bound that fails its call while the next call on the socket succeeds, and the CBOR refusal taking the fallback.
- The contributor ran the fix against live Chrome on Linux X11 (see #6338). macOS and Windows were not run live here.

title: docs(cua-driver): explain declarative hl.plugin.load in Hyprland Lua configs
body:
Salvaged from #6359 by @yu2001-s. Their commit is kept as authored.

## Why

The plugin README covers the legacy `plugin =` line but not Hyprland's Lua configuration, where autoloading is `hl.plugin.load()`. Hyprland treats that call as a declaration, so the obvious guard (skip the call when `hl.get_loaded_plugins()` already lists `cua-hyprland-plugin`) makes startup load and unload the module in a reload loop and the compositor never finishes starting.

## What changed

- A paragraph in "Load, inspect, and unload" shows the unconditional `hl.plugin.load()` call, explains why a guard on loaded state never settles, and notes that stable conditions (such as the ABI check) and modules loaded with `hyprctl plugin load` are unaffected.

## Scope

Documentation only, in `libs/cua-driver/hyprland-plugin/README.md`. No code, protocol, or package change, so this carries `no-release`. The `plugin =` guidance for legacy configurations is unchanged.

Compared with #6359, the commit message drops a tool co-author trailer, since squash merges here carry commit messages into main.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass on this branch.
- #6359 reports the hang on Omarchy 4.0.6 with Hyprland 0.56.2 (3 of 3 logins with the guarded load; a core dump shows `handlePluginLoads` → `reload` → `postConfigReload` recursing), and a roughly 1 s start with the unconditional call. Only Hyprland 0.56.2's Lua configuration was tested.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop only serve daemons on Linux update and append PATH once
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux, `cua-driver update --apply` and `_install-rust.sh` ran `pkill -x cua-driver` after stopping the systemd unit. That ended every `cua-driver` process on the host, including the `cua-driver mcp` stdio servers that MCP clients own and the updater itself (exit 143). Separately, each run without `BIN_DIR` on `PATH`, such as a systemd timer update, appended another `export PATH=...` line to the shell rc file.
- What changed:
  - On Linux the backstop now stops only the current user's `cua-driver serve` daemons. It decides by reading the first positional argument from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, skipping the same value-taking flags as the CLI's `VALUE_FLAGS`. A stdio server keeps running on its old inode across the `packages/current` flip. The survivor note now lists only `serve` daemons that are still running. macOS and other Unixes are unchanged.
  - The installer appends the PATH line only when the rc file does not already contain that exact line.

Salvaged from #6354 by @Mohit20057. Their two commits are kept as authored. On top of them: the helper moved above the `stop_cua_driver_daemons` doc comment it had split from its function, the doc comment describes the new Linux behavior, `$$`/`$PPID` guards were dropped because the `serve` filter already excludes the updater, the PATH check matches the exact line instead of any mention of `BIN_DIR`, and the subcommand parser skips every CLI value flag, with a test that keeps its list equal to `VALUE_FLAGS` in `cli.rs`.

## Related work

Fixes #6335

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux installs and updates no longer end client-owned `cua-driver mcp` sessions or other users' processes. A stdio server keeps running the old release until its client restarts it. The release directory is kept, so it keeps working.
- Risk and rollback: a daemon is recognized only if its cmdline parses to `serve` the way the CLI parses it. The driver itself always starts the daemon with `serve` as the first argument. To roll back, revert this PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_uninstall_stops_daemons_from_other_copies.py`, `test_install_shell_rc_path.py` (new) and `test_installer_bash32_syntax.py` pass: 32 tests. The parser test covers `--host-bundle-id serve mcp` (not a daemon) and `--cursor-theme cua.default serve` (a daemon). The new PATH test fails against main's `_install-rust.sh` (3 copies of the line after 3 runs). The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass.
- Manual or platform evidence (Linux arm64): I sourced `_install-common.sh`, then ran `stop_cua_driver_daemons` and `show_cua_driver_daemon_survivors` against two live processes named `cua-driver`: one started as `serve`, and one started as `mcp --socket /tmp/x-serve.sock`. On main both were stopped. On this branch the `serve` daemon was stopped and the `mcp` server survived.
- Known gaps or CI still required: macOS and Windows code paths are unchanged. No VM end-to-end run.

title: fix(cua-driver): admit input lanes after consent, with explicit lane and gate state
body:
## Why

Three pieces of cua-driver input state could only be read from their mechanics. The desktop lane decided "a worker outlived its call" from `Arc::strong_count(held) > 1` inside `Drop` impls. Per-pid text admission and the desktop lane were two admissions that both refused with `input_busy`, so an agent couldn't tell which one refused it, and the pid admission was taken before consent, so a call still being authorized refused every other `type_text` to the same process. `SingleFlight` kept four states across two atomics and a mutex.

## What changed

- `LaneState { Free, Held { gen }, Orphaned { gen, since } }` sits behind the lane's mutex, and only `acquire`, `DesktopCall::drop` and the last `HeldLane::drop` change it. The call's drop releases its own lease first, then orphans the hold only if it is still `Held` by the same generation, so no refcount arithmetic is needed.
- One `InputAdmission` over `Lane::Desktop | Lane::Pid(pid)`. The pid lane is now taken after every consent adapter (just before `commit_authorized_dispatch`), and the desktop lane where it was before. The `input_busy` refusal gains `refusal.lane`: `{"kind": "desktop"}` or `{"kind": "pid", "pid": N}`. LINUX.md documents the field.
- `SingleFlight` holds one `Gate { Open, Busy { timed_out }, Cooling { until } }` under one mutex. The Windows callers' `timed_out.store(true)` + `arm_cooldown()` pair becomes `SingleFlightDeadline::expire()`, which does both under the lock: a worker still running goes to `Busy { timed_out: true }` and cools down when it returns, and one that already returned starts the cooldown at once. The per-permit flag stays as the worker's cancellation signal.

## Scope

Covers everystate report items #6, #7 and #12 only. It does not touch session identity (#11), the session episode (#1), or consent/lifecycle ordering (#2). The lane rules hold as before: one desktop action at a time (ActsAlone), and `input_busy` from the desktop lane only behind a worker that outlived its call (BusyMeansStale).

## Tradeoffs

- The pid lane is now released with the desktop lane, after the cursor overlay's `end_tool`, instead of just after `drop(lifecycle_dispatch)`. Both points still come before recording evidence capture. One release point is what makes it a single admission.
- In `type_text` today, the consent phase only waits on async work (manifest enrichment, process attestation); `desktop_input` is Routine and never prompts a person. The ordering test parks a call in manifest enrichment for that reason. The fix also covers a future prompting adapter.
- `expire()` racing a different worker: if a timed-out worker returns and a new caller takes the gate before the old caller's `expire()`, the new worker is marked `timed_out` and its return starts the cooldown. Its own cancellation flag is untouched. Before this change, the cooldown was armed unconditionally at that moment, so the only difference is when the cooldown starts. With the UIA gates' zero cooldown, nothing changes.

## Blast Radius

The dispatch boundary in `cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs`, plus the three Windows `SingleFlight` users (`launch_uwp.rs`, `uia/windows_enum.rs`, `win32/installed_apps.rs`). The refusal change is additive: `code` and `message` are unchanged. Linux's `DesktopCall`/`DesktopLease` users compile against the same public API. Draft #4231 (parallel background lanes) is built on the old `desktop_action_coordinator` mutex and already conflicts with main. If it is revived, a shared mode would go in `LaneState`.

## Verification

- New unit tests: `LaneState` transitions without strong_count (`a_call_whose_input_has_stopped_frees_the_lane_without_orphaning_it`, `a_worker_that_outlives_its_call_orphans_the_hold_until_it_stops`), distinct `lane` details on the desktop and pid refusals, `a_call_still_being_authorized_holds_no_input_lane` (a second `type_text` to the same pid succeeds while the first is parked in authorization; on main it is refused `input_busy`), and `Gate` transitions Open → Busy → Busy { timed_out } → Cooling → Open, the late-return race, and zero cooldown.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` green (rustfmt, SPDX, image refs). This is a shared host, so cargo test, clippy and the Windows cross-check run in CI.

title: macOS: any installed custom cursor theme keeps the overlay at ~1 CPU core while the cursor is visible (built-in `cua.default` ~4%)
body:
**Version:** cua-driver-rs 0.55.0 (`cua-driver-rs-0.55.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz`, release binary), macOS 27.0, Apple silicon Mac mini, `serve --embedded`.

**What happens:** While the agent cursor is visible (the ~15 s before idle-hide), the daemon uses 105–117% CPU whenever the session's cursor theme is a custom installed theme. With the built-in `cua.default` the same scenario uses 4–5%. Once the cursor hides, both drop to 0%.

It does not depend on the artwork:
- a custom theme whose `idle` is a single still frame (no resting motion): ~108%
- the repository's own `cua.default.lottie`, rebuilt with `cua-driver cursor-theme build` after changing only `id` in `cua/theme.json`: ~110%

**Repro:**
1. Build that copy of `cua.default.lottie` and put it in `CUA_DRIVER_CURSOR_THEME_DIR`.
2. `start_session {"session":"s"}`, then `set_agent_cursor_theme {"session":"s","theme_id":"<copy id>"}`, then `click` any window.
3. Watch the daemon with `top -pid <pid>` during the next ~15 s; then repeat with `theme_id: "cua.default"`.

**Profile** (`sample`, custom theme): the main thread spends nearly all its time in `CA::Transaction::commit` → `CA::Layer::prepare_contents` → `CA::Render::copy_image` → `create_image_by_rendering` (vImage colour conversion, `vLookupTable_Planar16WithClipping`, premultiply / unpremultiply). That looks like a new `CGImage` is committed as layer contents on every frame and needs a colour-space conversion. The built-in theme path doesn't seem to hit it.

**Expected:** custom themes cost about the same as `cua.default`, at least when their idle animation is a single frame.

title: fix(cua-driver): count a viewer's double- and triple-clicks on macOS
body:
Salvaged from #6427

Fixes #6423
Refs #6424

## Why

A viewer's presses reach a macOS Space through `InteractiveInputSession`, which posted every press with CoreGraphics' default click state (1 on a down, 0 on an up). macOS does not count posted presses the way it counts a physical mouse's, so a viewer's double-click arrived as two single clicks: no word selected, no Finder icon opened. The session now counts presses itself and stamps `kCGMouseEventClickState` 1, 2, 3… on each press and release.

## What changed

- `cua-driver-core::interactive_input::ClickCounter`: counts presses of one button within an interval and within `CLICK_SLOP_PX` of the previous press. No I/O; the caller passes the receipt time, so the Windows and Hyprland gesture folder (#6424) can count the same way.
- `platform-macos` interactive session: counts each down with the user's `NSEvent.doubleClickInterval`, stamps the count on the down, the up and a cancel, in both the HID and the targeted delivery mode, and keeps one click group id across a multi-click. A cancel resets the count.
- An opt-in E2E, `e2e_macos_desktop_stream_double_click_selects_a_word`, double-clicks a word in TextEdit over the media socket and reads the clipboard after ⌘C.

stanley50z's commits are kept as authored; this branch adds only a merge of main.

## Scope

macOS interactive (viewer) input only. The agents' `click` and `double_click` tools use a different path and are unchanged. Windows and Hyprland are #6424.

## Blast Radius

Only the macOS interactive session's pointer events change. The public `InteractiveInputSession::dispatch` is unchanged, so `cua-spacesd-desktop` needs no change.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): SPDX headers and rustfmt pass; clippy and unit tests are left to CI.
- From #6427: `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib input::interactive` and `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib interactive_input` pass on macOS 26; the new macOS unit test fails with the stamp removed; the opt-in TextEdit E2E passes against a Space running cua-spacesd built from the branch.

title: fix(cua-driver): carry call identity as a typed DispatchIdentity
body:
## Why

A call's session identity travelled as reserved JSON keys (`_session_id`, `_transport_session_id`, `_public_session_label`) plus a returned `runtime_prefix` string. The registry stripped those keys from caller input, stamped them back in, and then read them back out of the JSON for every later decision. Protected-resource grant keys were rebuilt from strings with a public-session-then-transport fallback, which is how a review of the revoke path went wrong. This is item 11 in the cua-driver implicit-state catalog.

## What changed

- New `dispatch_identity` module: `DispatchIdentity { runtime: RuntimeScope, lifecycle: Option<SessionId>, transport: Option<SessionId>, public_label }`. It is resolved once per call from trusted adapter evidence, the authorization context and the public `session` label. Reserved keys in the arguments are never read.
- `invoke_authorized_unannotated` reads the typed value for the ended-session check, lifecycle admission, every consent adapter, process ownership, recording and history. The platform tool's arguments are stamped from it in one place (`DispatchIdentity::stamp`, called from `platform_args`), which replaces or removes any reserved identity key already present. `namespace_runtime_args` is gone.
- `ResourceGrantKey` is `{ runtime_scope, lifecycle, transport, adapter_id, resource_digest }`, taken straight from the identity. `revoke_session` matches the lifecycle id. `authorize` and `revoke_resource` take `&DispatchIdentity`.

## Scope

Covers identity plumbing in `tool.rs` and `consent.rs`. Caller sanitization stays where it was, at the outer boundary (`sanitize_reserved_args` and `TrustedInvocationEvidence::extract_from_adapter_args`). Public session labels and their runtime namespacing are unchanged on the wire, and policy and manifests still evaluate the public request.

Out of scope: platform tools still read `_session_id` and friends from their arguments. Moving the identity into the `Tool::invoke` signature touches every macOS, Windows and Linux tool, so it gets its own PR. The consent request shown to a person keeps its existing `public_session` / `transport_session` labels. Lane admission, `SingleFlight` and episode ids (#8287) are not touched. #8287 changes `resource_grant_key` too, so whichever PR lands second has to thread `EpisodeId` into this key; it slots in next to `lifecycle`.

## Blast Radius

Every tool call goes through this code. The values that reach platform tools are the same as before in every case the tests pin, with one exception. A sessionless call through a file-transfer adapter (`browser_set_input_files`, downloads) used to lose its implicit `_session_id`, because that path rebuilt its arguments from the public ones without re-adding it. It now gets the same `…:implicit-direct` session as every other sessionless call, so the browser tool keys it the same way `browser_prepare` does. The test that pinned the old behavior is updated.

Grant map keys are internal. Two keys are different now: the compatibility context's public field is no longer double-prefixed, and the transport field holds the namespaced transport. Revocation already worked through the lifecycle id in every context, and still does.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core`: all suites pass (lib: 1355 passed, 2 ignored).
- New tests: `dispatch_identity::tests` (reserved keys never choose the identity, trusted evidence wins over the label, a foreign `__cua_runtime_*` prefix in a label cannot reach another runtime, implicit sessions, an empty trusted transport id kept as the owner, the shared `default` label); `consent::tests::grant_keys_resolve_from_the_dispatch_identity` and `reserved_argument_keys_cannot_select_another_sessions_grant`; `tool::runtime_isolation_tests::reserved_identity_keys_in_arguments_never_win_over_the_typed_identity`.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --tests -D warnings`, `cargo check -p cua-driver-sdk -p cua-driver --tests` and `bin/ci --quick` are clean. This shared host ran no Windows or Linux builds, so those lanes are left to CI.

## Contributor and release checks

title: fix(spacesd): keep jemalloc out of the cua-spacesd build
body:
## What changed for users

cua-spacesd 0.17.1 could not be released: its static aarch64 Linux build failed, so the release stayed a draft and the version the Cua Spaces app and the cua CLI pin to was never published. This fixes the build so the next cua-spacesd release (0.17.2) publishes.

## Root cause

#8314 added jemalloc to `cua-relay` as the relay binary's allocator. `cua-spacesd` embeds `cua-relay` as a library, so `tikv-jemalloc-sys` was compiled into every cua-spacesd build, although only the relay binary sets jemalloc as its global allocator. `tikv-jemalloc-sys` does not build for `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` ("`background_threads_runtime_support` not supported", then C errors in `atomic.h`), which is the static `cua-spacesd-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` release asset. CI never builds that target, so it only showed up in `CD: cua-spacesd` for 0.17.1. The other targets built.

## Fix

- `cua-relay`: jemalloc is behind a `jemalloc` feature, on by default, so `cargo build -p cua-relay` (the relay image) is unchanged. The `churn_bounded` test needs it and says so.
- `cua-spacesd` and `cua-spacesd-server` depend on `cua-relay` with `default-features = false`, so cua-spacesd no longer links an allocator it does not use.
- `CI: cua-spacesd` gets a check that cua-spacesd's dependency graph has no `tikv-jemalloc*` crate, since CI does not build the musl targets.
- Two `Cargo.lock` files drop the jemalloc crates (cua-spacesd's and the teleport-e2e one).

## After merge

Release Please opens cua-spacesd 0.17.2; merging it runs `CD: cua-spacesd` on a commit with this fix. `libs/cua-spacesd/VERSION` moves to 0.17.2, which clears the pin alert once 0.17.2 is published. Re-running the 0.17.1 run would build the same broken tag, so it is not re-run. The 0.17.1 draft is not touched here.

## Checks

`bin/ci --quick --fix --signoff` green. `cargo check -p cua-relay --all-targets` with and without default features; `cargo tree -p cua-spacesd --target all` shows no jemalloc.

title: fix(cua-driver): tell apps how many wheel clicks a Hyprland scroll was
body:
Salvaged from #6489

## Why

On Hyprland, `scroll` reported success but Zed did not move. The plugin marked the scroll as a mouse wheel but never sent how many clicks it was, and Zed ignores wheel scrolls without that count. @somtooo's commit sends `axis_value120` (wl_pointer v8+) or `axis_discrete` (v5 to 7) before each `axis` event, in both background and foreground input.

## What changed

- somtooo's commit, kept as authored: both SCROLL paths send the click count. The driver sends 10 units per click, so 3 clicks is 360 in `axis_value120`.
- On top: the duplicated math moves into `send_wheel_steps` (`src/wheel_steps.hpp`), which both paths call, with a unit test. A scroll too small to round to a step sends neither event instead of a zero, which `axis_value120` forbids. The driver never sends one, but the plugin protocol accepts any value in [-1000, 1000]. The new files join the release source allowlist.

## Scope

Only the Hyprland plugin's SCROLL input. The driver, the plugin protocol and the `axis` event are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Apps that already scrolled now also get the click count. That is what a real wheel sends, so behavior should match a physical mouse. Only Zed has been checked by hand.

## Verification

- `cua_hyprland_wheel_steps_test` passes. It fails when the 120-per-click scale or either zero guard is broken. The release bundle tests pass.
- `send_wheel_steps` compiles against Hyprland 0.55.2's `CWlPointer` and `CWLPointerResource`. The plugin build with input enabled needs newer headers and has not been run on this change.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass.
- From #6489: on Omarchy (Hyprland 0.56.2), Zed received `axis_value120(0, 600)` then `axis(..., 50)` for 5 clicks and scrolled. That was foreground input only, on 0.33.2 plus this fix.

title: fix(cua-driver): click web content that does not advertise AXPress
body:
Salvaged from #6502 by @terra-alex. Their commit is kept as authored; the merge of main and one fix sit on top.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, an element-token `click` on web content in a Chromium embedder that never enters screen-reader mode (Dia) never reached the page. Chromium advertises and performs `AXPress` on web content only in that mode, so the press returned success and did nothing. The background pixel rung then pressed the same element through its AX hit-test, with the same result.
- What changed:
  - Element-token press: when the target has an `AXWebArea` ancestor and does not advertise `AXPress`, the driver posts a routed pixel click at the element's center, behind the same `WindowPointer` gate the selection fallback uses. The result reports `path: cgevent`. (#6502)
  - Background pixel hit-test: such an element is no longer pressed through AX; it falls through to the routed pixel path, as LibreOffice (VCL) and GTK 3 already do. Both paths share one predicate, `press_is_hollow`. (#6502)
  - On top of #6502: the merge with main keeps main's GTK 3 toolkit in that predicate and returns main's `AxClickOutcome`. The background web pixel click now reads the browser window before delivery, as a background web `AXPress` does since #7694, so a page that ignores it reports `suspected_noop` with the foreground escalation instead of `unverifiable`.
  - On top of #6502: the element-token replacement hit-tests the element's center first and keeps the AX press when something else (a sticky header, an overlay) is under it. In the background it posts the same focus record the background pixel path posts before its click, so an inactive Chromium window takes the click without being raised.

## Related work

Refs #5723 (Dia attach for the browser tools). This fix does not depend on it.

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not required. The `click` inputs and result shape are unchanged; only the delivery path of a hollow web press changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. A token click on web content without `AXPress` now delivers a real click instead of returning `path: ax`, `effect: suspected_noop`. Background delivery does not raise the window or move the pointer; when the `WindowPointer` gate refuses (a minimized window, for example), the old AX path runs. Windows and Linux adapters are untouched.
- Risk and rollback: an element that keeps advertising `AXPress`, including Chrome's after its accessibility mode switch, keeps the AX path, as do native elements without `AXPress`. Rollback is reverting this PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: owner test `hollow_press_tests::only_an_unadvertised_press_on_a_hollow_surface_is_replaced` (from #6502). The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) pass on this head. Clippy, unit tests and the macOS build run in CI; this Linux host does not build the macOS crate.
- Manual or platform evidence: #6502 reports a manual run on macOS 26.4 with Dia 1.55.1 and Chrome 156: token and background clicks on a button and a checkbox reached the page as trusted events in Dia, and Chrome kept the `AXPress` path. That run was not repeated on this merged head.
- Known gaps or CI still required: no canonical `cua-driver-e2e` row, since the runners have no Chromium embedder that stays out of screen-reader mode.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse web value writes as background typing
body:
Salvaged from #6533

Fixes #6531

## Why

On Windows, background `type_text` with an `element_token` inside embedded Chromium web content (WebView2, Tauri) wrote the field through UIA ValuePattern. That changes the DOM value without firing the `insertText` input event that event-driven editors such as xterm consume, so the call reported success while the editor saw nothing. This PR carries sealpp's fix from #6533: the retained UIA element keeps the snapshot's web-content classification, and background typing into web content under a Chromium-hosting window now returns `background_unavailable` before any write.

## What changed

- `RetainedElement` gains `in_web_content`, and `type_text` refuses background typing into web content of a window with a Chromium descendant (sealpp's commits, kept as authored).
- A WebView2 harness test checks that `set_value` still works, that background `type_text` refuses with `background_unavailable`, and that the field value and inserted-text payload are unchanged. The Windows Tauri AX typing expectations in the shared matrix now expect the same refusal. The troubleshooting guide explains the refusal.
- Our commits on top: merged main (resolved against `delivery.is_background()`), moved the new test under the WebView2 section, made it assert no mutation against a journal snapshot taken after the refusal (a `set_value` barrier on a second field), and updated the WebView2 comment in `would_be_silently_dropped`.

## Scope

Windows only. Native UIA controls, explicit `set_value`, and foreground typing keep their behavior. Standalone Chrome/Edge windows were already refused. No new tool, argument or foreground authorization.

## Blast Radius

Callers who used background `type_text` on WebView2/Tauri web fields and relied on a value readback now get a refusal. Those writes never reached event-driven editors, so the old success was not reliable. Callers can use `set_value`, browser input, or foreground delivery.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): rustfmt, SPDX headers, docs code-block dispositions, image catalog. 5 passed, 5 skipped in quick mode.
- The E2E inventory test (`test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py`) passes.

title: fix(cua-driver): find Windows DevTools listeners without trusting TCP row state
body:
Salvaged from #6539

Fixes #6538

## Why

On Windows 11 10.0.26300.9818, `GetExtendedTcpTable(TCP_TABLE_OWNER_PID_LISTENER)` returns unreliable `dwState` values (live listeners show 0, 1, 2 or 6). The DevTools listener lookup only accepted `MIB_TCP_STATE_LISTEN`, so every isolated `browser_prepare` refused with `browser_endpoint_owner_mismatch`. thomasklemenc's fix stops reading `dwState`.

## What changed

- thomasklemenc's commit, cherry-picked unchanged onto current main: `TcpOwnerRow` drops `state`, and a row counted as listening when its remote endpoint was unspecified.
- Our commit on top drops that remote-endpoint check as well. Windows documents a listening row's remote fields as having no meaning, so requiring zeros could miss a real listener. The listener-only table now decides which rows are listeners; a row counts when it is loopback and owned by an allowed pid.
- `native_listener_discovery_ignores_unreliable_row_states` covers IPv4 and IPv6 rows with the states that build returns and with nonzero remote fields.

## Scope

Windows only. No changes to tool inputs, outputs or refusal codes. Existing-profile attach uses the same lookup but was not tested on the affected build.

## Tradeoffs

Keeping the remote-endpoint check would also filter out connected sockets if Windows ever put them in the listener table. Nothing shows that it does, and an extra row could only add a port owned by the same trusted browser process tree. The pid check is the trust boundary.

## Blast Radius

Windows Cua Driver browser endpoint discovery, for isolated launch and existing-profile attach. Rows still come from the listener-only table and must be loopback and owned by an allowed pid, so the change can't widen which processes are trusted.

## Verification

- The contributor reports that on 10.0.26300.9818 the existing `native_owner_table_observes_a_real_loopback_listener` fails on main and passes with their change, and that a release build ran `browser_prepare` (`isolated_new`) plus navigate, type, click, file input, dialog and download against Chrome 157.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passes. The Windows unit and clippy lanes run in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): find localized Chrome setup controls without English names
body:
Salvaged from #6664 by @YiTaiiiiii, whose commit lands here unchanged except for one dropped trailer. It still credits @AidenNovak for the design from #4393.

Refs #3139

## Why

On macOS, `browser_prepare` with an `existing_profile` strategy refuses on a non-English Chrome before it does anything (`the approved Google Chrome window has no exact New Tab button`). Setup finds the new-tab button, the new tab's close button and the address field by their English accessible names, and Chrome in zh-Hans names them `新标签页`, `关闭` and `地址和搜索栏`.

## What changed

- The English match still runs first. When it finds nothing, the control is picked by structure, and any count other than one refuses:
  - New tab: the one native pressable `AXButton`, outside every tab, whose top and height match the topmost row of native tabs. This ignores the Translate bubble's tabs below the toolbar.
  - Cleanup close: the one native pressable button inside the tab the before/after diff proved new.
  - Address field: the window's one native pressable text field.
- All five setup-URL checks now go through one helper, `setup_url_omniboxes`, so a find bar holding the setup URL never counts as the address field, in any language.
- A second commit, on top of the contributor's, tightens the fallbacks. Each runs only when no native control carries the English name, so an English control that fails another check (for example, one that can't be pressed) refuses instead of letting another control stand in for it. A button counts as inside a tab when any ancestor is a tab, not just its direct parent. Cleanup picks the new tab and its close button from native nodes only, because the `before` walk can be native-only while the `after` walk includes the page.

## Scope

Only `platform-macos/src/browser/setup_ui.rs`. The localized consent sheet is #4590's. This PR leaves #3139's omnibox suggestion-text item and the E2E test's own English lookup (`standalone_browser_native_omnibox_select_all`) unchanged, so #3139 stays open.

## Blast Radius

macOS existing-profile setup for Chromium browsers. An English Chrome matches the English names first, as before. For English, the only change is that the address-field check is stricter: the field must be native. Unexpected layouts such as vertical tabs or tab groups refuse with the existing `browser_wrong_target_refused` code; they do not guess. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

## Verification

- The contributor's hosted macOS lane on Chrome 156: on main, zh-Hans setup refuses. At #6664's head, the full standalone lane passes in English and passes in zh-Hans apart from the known test-side `native_omnibox_select_all` lookup. Runs: https://github.com/YiTaiiiiii/cua/actions/runs/42216932418 (main), https://github.com/YiTaiiiiii/cua/actions/runs/42216937134 (PR).
- The commit cherry-picks cleanly onto current main, which has changed this file since #6664's base (#7999, #7637). The quick scoped repository checks pass (rustfmt, SPDX, image refs). The macOS unit tests and clippy run in CI, including four new tests for the second commit. Each of them exercises a case that the first commit alone handled wrongly.

title: fix(cua-driver): skip unchanged macOS cursor composites
body:
## Summary

On macOS, a cursor waiting at constant opacity for its idle-hide timer still ticks to advance its clock and to keep the overlay's z-order heartbeat. Previously those bookkeeping ticks also repainted and submitted an unchanged image to AppKit. This is especially expensive for custom themes, for which the existing compositor deliberately uses a full-display surface.

Separate that visual paint decision from the timer. Repaint on commands, display refits, hover changes, and visual animation. Keep the prior visual-tick flag for one iteration so animation and fade completion still submit the final frame, including a clear. The timer, bounded frame deltas, repin cadence, and custom-theme paint bounds are unchanged.

Refs #8345. This addresses the settled static countdown, not the cost of genuinely animated custom themes.

## Validation

Same source base (`497c9460`), Rust debug profile, and macOS arm64 fixture for both binaries. A temporary nonactivating window and Driver-only overlay movement kept real input and captures out of the benchmark. With a 15 s hide timeout, the daemon's mean CPU was sampled over five seconds following a four-second settle. One core is 100%.

| Theme / settled state | Baseline | Patched |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Single-frame custom idle, reduced motion | 151.5% | 0.6% |
| Separate custom theme with 48-frame animated idle | 161.6% | 162.1% |

Patched static trials reported the session cursor visible before the timeout and hidden after it; late CPU was 0.0%. These are process CPU samples, not WindowServer CPU or screenshot evidence.

- Native macOS overlay unit suite: 19 passed, including countdown/fade, resting animation, pixel parity, seam, and repin tests.

title: fix(cua-driver): let nightly builds satisfy extension Driver requirements
body:
## Why

A nightly Driver such as `0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244` reports `cua-perception` as unhealthy because its manifest requires `>=0.28.2`. The `semver` crate never lets a prerelease satisfy a comparator that has no prerelease of its own, so every nightly fails every plain requirement.

## What changed

A nightly `0.38.1-nightly.*` now satisfies `>=0.38.1`, even though strict semver orders it before `0.38.1`. Nightlies are cut from main ahead of that release, so they already carry everything the release will have. Exact pins such as `=0.38.1-nightly.…` still match as before.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse a Windows element action on a hung app within 2 s instead of waiting for it
body:
## Problem

Before it acts, a Windows element action makes UI Automation reads on the target: `IsEnabled` for every `element_token` action, `IsOffscreen` on the SendInput and inject paths, the scroll into view of an off-screen element, and for a background click the Invoke, Toggle, SelectionItem and ExpandCollapse pattern reads. None of them had a deadline. When the target app's UI thread does not pump, each read waits for UI Automation's own timeout or until the app wakes, and then the action goes on: the input lands late, after the caller has already given up on the call.

Measured on a Windows 11 test VM with a WinForms app whose UI thread sleeps 60 s, driving the driver through a client that reads the window, starts the hang, then acts on a cached `element_token`:

| action on the hung app | without this change |
|---|---|
| background `click` on a button | 60.7-61.1 s, the click lands when the app wakes (3/3) |
| foreground `click` (SendInput path) | 59.1-59.6 s, the click lands when the app wakes (2/2) |
| background `press_key` on an Edit | 59.0 s, the key lands 11-16 ms after the app wakes (2/2) |
| background `scroll` on a List | 59.0-59.1 s, three scroll messages arrive after the app wakes (2/2) |

## Fix

**Bounded reads.** Each of these reads now runs on a worker that owns its own element reference: the state and pattern reads within 2 s, the scroll into view within 4 s. Each read takes a single-flight gate keyed by the target's process id, kept in a map only while a worker holds it, so a hung app holds up only its own reads and element actions on other apps go on. UWP apps share the gate of ApplicationFrameHost, which owns their frame windows, so while one UWP app is hung, other UWP apps' element reads are refused too.

**Refusal before any input.** A read that is late, or that finds its process gate held by an earlier read that has not returned, refuses the action before any input:

- a late or busy `IsEnabled` read refuses `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `set_value`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `scroll` on an element; only the first five also refuse an element that reports `IsEnabled=false`, as before;
- a late or busy `IsOffscreen` read, pattern read with no earlier failed pattern call, scroll into view, or modifier click's pre-scroll refuses the same way.

The refusal carries the code `app_unresponsive`, `effect: refused`, and a new recovery hint: wait until the app responds, then read the window again. A read that fails outright, rather than late, still fails open as before. `app_unresponsive` is added to the e2e testkit's refusal codes.

**Unknown effect after a failed pattern call.** A failed Invoke, Toggle, Select or Expand call may still take effect (a WPF button's Invoke can fire and return an error). When a later read is late, a later route refuses, or a later send fails, the reply is `background_unavailable` with reason `earlier_call_failed`, `effect: unverifiable`, the failed calls, and the follow-up's code as `cause_code`. It carries no foreground suggestion or escalation, and the `earlier_call_failed` recovery hint says to read the window again and check the target before acting, since a foreground retry could repeat a Save, a Send or a Submit. A background element click now hands every such refusal to the caller with its code, effect and hint; its blocking closure used to turn them into a text-only error.

**Limits.** The Invoke, Toggle, Select and Expand calls themselves stay unbounded: a handler that opens a modal blocks inside them, and a held gate would then refuse the click on the modal's own buttons. An app that hangs inside the dispatch call, or between a timely read and the action, still waits as before (measured: a button whose Invoke handler sleeps 60 s costs about 61 s with and without this change). A scroll that runs past its 4 s budget may go on scrolling the target after the refusal. A late worker stays blocked until its provider call returns, at most one per hung process.

**Cost.** On a healthy app, one worker spawn plus one map lock and lookup per bounded read. A background Invoke click does one pattern read; a fall-through to Toggle, SelectionItem or ExpandCollapse does up to four sequential reads.

## Test

Unit tests:

- `uia::windows_enum`: `a_stuck_process_gate_admits_other_processes_and_is_dropped_once_free`.
- `tools::impl_`: `the_element_tools_refuse_an_unanswered_read_and_only_five_refuse_a_disabled_one`, `only_an_unanswered_scroll_into_view_refuses_with_app_unresponsive`.
- `tools::click`: `a_refusal_before_any_pattern_call_reaches_the_caller_unchanged`, `a_refusal_after_a_failed_pattern_call_has_an_unknown_effect`, `a_failed_send_after_a_failed_pattern_call_has_an_unknown_effect`, `a_late_pattern_read_after_a_failed_pattern_call_has_an_unknown_effect`.
- `cua-driver-core` `recovery_hint`: `an_unresponsive_app_waits_then_reads_the_same_window_again`, `an_earlier_failed_call_reads_the_window_and_never_retries_in_the_foreground`.
- `cua-driver-testkit`: `an_unresponsive_app_is_a_refusal_code`.
- Two tests need a live UI Automation root and are `#[ignore]`d like the crate's other desktop-bound tests; they hold a process gate and check that the action refuses before any input: `tools::impl_::is_enabled_refusal_tests::a_busy_is_enabled_read_refuses_before_any_input` and `tools::scroll::element_refusal_tests::an_element_scroll_refuses_while_its_app_holds_the_read_gate`.

Device evidence, same Windows 11 test VM and hung WinForms app as above. "With this change" is a downstream build based on cua-driver-rs 0.54.0 that carries it, measured before the reply-code commits, so its refusals carried `element_not_visible`; those commits change codes and text only. The `click` rows "without" are a build without any of it; the `press_key` and `scroll` rows "without" are a build that bounded the reads but did not refuse key and scroll yet, which is upstream behaviour for those tools.

| action on the hung app | without this change | with this change |
|---|---|---|
| background `click` on a button (3 trials) | 60.7-61.1 s, lands when the app wakes 3/3 | refused in 2001-2016 ms in the driver (3.1-3.2 s per client call), nothing landed |
| a second `click` while the first read is still stuck (3) | - | refused in 0-1 ms, nothing landed |
| background `press_key` on an Edit (2) | 59.0 s, key lands after the wake | refused in 2001-2002 ms, no key |
| background `scroll` on a List (2) | 59.0-59.1 s, scrolls after the wake | refused in 2001-2003 ms, no scroll |
| foreground `click`, SendInput path (2) | 59.1-59.6 s, lands after the wake | refused in 3.1 s per client call, nothing landed |

title: fix(cua-driver): attach to the Windows foreground thread only when it answers WM_NULL within 250 ms
body:
## Problem

`force_foreground_attached` attaches this thread's input to the foreground window's thread (`AttachThreadInput`) before `SetForegroundWindow`. When the foreground window's thread is hung, the attach and the activation wait until it pumps again, so any action that brings another, healthy window to the front stalls for as long as the hung app sleeps.

Measured on a Windows 11 test VM with a WinForms window in front whose UI thread sleeps 60 s, acting on a healthy app's window behind it (3 trials each):

| action on the healthy window | without this change |
|---|---|
| `bring_to_front` | no reply within the client's 30 s timeout |
| `bring_to_front`, then `press_key` "a" | no reply from `bring_to_front` within 30 s, nothing typed |

## Fix

Before attaching, the driver sends the foreground window a `WM_NULL` with `SendMessageTimeoutW(SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG | SMTO_BLOCK, 250 ms)` and attaches only when it answers. Otherwise it calls `SetForegroundWindow` unattached; a target that does not come to the front stays the existing `foreground_unavailable` refusal with nothing sent.

Cost: one `WM_NULL` round trip to the foreground thread per attach attempt. When that thread is busy or hung it is at most 250 ms per attempt, and only in the first 5 s of a hang, after which `SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG` answers at once: at most 4 attempts in an assisted foreground call, 5 in `invoke_menu` with its restore, and 8 in `browser_setup_ui`'s two calls. A front app that is busy for 0.25-5 s now gets a fast `foreground_unavailable` instead of a wait.

## Test

Same Windows 11 test VM, a downstream build based on cua-driver-rs 0.53.2 without and with this change, arms alternated, one fresh hang per call:

| action on the healthy window, hung window in front (3 per arm) | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| `bring_to_front` | over 30 s, no reply | 264-266 ms, the healthy window in front |
| `bring_to_front`, then `press_key` "a" | over 30 s, nothing typed | 277-293 ms, the key arrived 3/3 |

| same actions, healthy window in front (5 per action per arm, medians) | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| `bring_to_front` | 12.3 ms | 12.4 ms |
| `bring_to_front`, then `press_key` | 26.5 ms | 28.8 ms |

The probe's cost on a healthy front is within noise.

## Checks

title: fix(cua-driver): start the element_token snapshot counter at a random value per driver process
body:
## Problem

An `element_token` names a snapshot id, minted from a process-wide counter, and a row in that snapshot (`s00001234:42`). The counter started at 1 in every driver process. A client that kept a token across a driver restart (a daemon restart, an update, a crash) could hand it to a new process that had minted the same snapshot id for the same pid and window. That process accepted the token and resolved it to whatever element now sits at that row of its own snapshot, so the action went to an element the client never saw, instead of answering `stale_element_token`.

## Fix

The counter is seeded once per process from std's `RandomState`. Two driver processes' id ranges then overlap only with a chance of about the number of ids they minted over 2^32, and a token from an earlier process is refused as stale. The token format and the per-process sequence are unchanged; the counter still wraps as before.

Cost: one `RandomState` hash on the first snapshot of a process.

## Test

- `element_token`: `each_seed_differs_from_the_one_before`.
- `snapshot_store`: the existing pid-for-token test adds 1000 to a random snapshot id with `wrapping_add`, so it no longer overflows when the seed is near `u32::MAX`.

## Checks

- [x] On a windows-2025 runner (run 44755293583): `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib` (1321 passed), `cargo test --locked -p platform-windows --lib` (344 passed, 5 ignored).

title: feat(cua-driver): add optional and items constraints to YAML policies
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: a YAML policy constraint failed whenever its argument was absent. A `delivery_mode: [background]` rule therefore refused every call that relied on the default, including the run_script helpers `app.click` and `app.typeText`, which never send `delivery_mode`. Array arguments such as `launch_app`'s `additional_arguments` could only be compared as a whole, and nothing could require an argument to be absent, such as `launch_path`, which `launch_app` on Windows prefers over `path`.
- What changed:
  - A constraint can set `optional: true`. An absent argument then passes and the tool uses its own default. A present argument must still pass every check.
  - A new `items` constraint applies its checks to every element of an array argument. A non-array value is denied.
  - `optional: true` with `allowed: []` forbids an argument. The permissions guide adds a separate Windows policy example with a `launch_app` rule that pins `path`, forbids `launch_path` and `urls`, and constrains each additional argument. It is separate because, in one file, the macOS `bundle_id` rule would admit a Windows launch whose `launch_path` overrides `bundle_id`. Its click rule also limits `scope` to `window`, because a `scope: desktop` click with no `delivery_mode` uses foreground input on Windows.

## Related work

Fixes #6824

This PR covers the policy part of the issue. Binding headless CDP browsers in `browser_prepare`, an official isolated-desktop mode, and the `type_text` escalation message (the issue's companion bug) are not in this change.

RFC: none. The YAML syntax change is additive: policies that load today behave the same.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: two new YAML constraint keys. Constraints without them behave as before: an absent argument is denied and an array never matches `pattern` or `max_length`. Rego policies are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: an `optional` constraint trusts the tool's default. The guide says to check the default first and gives the desktop-click case, where an omitted `delivery_mode` still means foreground input. Rollback is a revert. Policies that use the new keys would then fail to load, and the daemon refuses to start without a valid policy, so the failure is closed.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: three new `policy.rs` unit tests cover an absent, a background and a foreground `delivery_mode`; `launch_app` with an allowed path, matching and non-matching `additional_arguments` items, a non-array value, a present `launch_path` and a missing `path`; and load-time rejection of `optional` alone and of `optional` inside `items`. All three fail against main's policy code and pass with this change. I ran them in a scratch crate that compiles the `YamlPolicy` section of `policy.rs`, because this host does not have enough free disk for a full `cua-driver-core` build. Both of the guide's YAML examples load in the same harness. The main example allows a window click and denies a desktop click and a foreground click. The Windows example allows the Notepad launch and denies launches that add `launch_path` or `urls`, or that use `bundle_id` with `launch_path`.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passes 5 checks: SPDX headers, docs code-block dispositions, rustfmt and catalog image refs. Clippy, `cua-driver-core` unit tests, UniFFI bindings and the Windows cross-check are deferred to GitHub CI. The docs-image-refs check was skipped because `crane` is not installed here.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the full `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` run happens in CI. No live Windows run, since the change is platform-neutral policy evaluation.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep Windows invoke_menu, menu expand and right_click in the background
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, three actions broke the background contract when `delivery_mode` was omitted. `invoke_menu` always activated the target and opened its menus. `click` with `action:"expand"` on a classic Win32 menu item opened the menu in the window's modal menu loop, which makes the window foreground. `right_click` returned no action record, so its result said `route: global_input` and `delivery: unknown` even when the click was posted with PostMessage.
- What changed:
  - `invoke_menu` on Windows now honors `delivery_mode`, as Linux does. Background resolves the path through the window's classic menu bar (`GetMenu` HMENU tree), sends the `WM_INITMENU` the bar gets when the menu activates and the `WM_INITMENUPOPUP` each submenu gets before opening (refusing if the window does not answer, since its menu state may be stale), and posts the final item's `WM_COMMAND`, or `WM_MENUCOMMAND` by position for an `MNS_NOTIFYBYPOS` menu. No menu opens and the window is not activated. When the item can only be reached by opening a menu (WPF, XAML, owner-drawn or lazily filled menus), the call returns `background_unavailable`. `delivery_mode:"foreground"` keeps the UI Automation route.
  - A background `click` with `action:"expand"` on a UIA `MenuItem` whose framework is `Win32` returns `background_unavailable` and points to `invoke_menu`. WPF, WinForms and XAML expands are unchanged.
  - `right_click` attaches an action record with the route it took: PostMessage (synthetic events, background), coordinate injection (background), or SendInput (foreground).

## Related work

Fixes #6823

RFC: not needed. The `invoke_menu` `delivery_mode` field and its background refusal already exist in the contract; this makes Windows honor them, and the field's doc now says so.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a Windows `invoke_menu` call without `delivery_mode` on a window that has no classic menu bar (WPF, WinUI, most modern apps) now returns `background_unavailable` instead of activating the window. Callers retry with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, the same escalation every other background refusal asks for. The WPF E2E case now asserts that refusal, then runs its foreground path.
- Risk: the HMENU route trusts the menu's enabled state after `WM_INITMENU` and `WM_INITMENUPOPUP`. An app that enables items some other way could receive a `WM_COMMAND` for an item it would have grayed; the app's own command handler still runs. Rollback is a revert of this PR.
- Not changed: the Windows MSAA (VCL/LibreOffice) click path still uses non-activating SendInput for `expand` in background, and the issue's `type_text` and `run_script` points are left for follow-ups.

## Validation

- Focused tests: the new `menu_command` unit tests (label normalization against UIA names, path resolution, must-open versus path errors, WM_COMMAND versus WM_MENUCOMMAND dispatch) pass, run standalone with `rustc --test` on Linux.
- New Windows E2E `win32_menu_windows_test` (selected in the native suite of `scripts/ci/windows/run-rust-e2e.ps1`): the test process owns a classic menu window whose item is enabled only in `WM_INITMENU`; background `invoke_menu` must deliver its `WM_COMMAND`, report `synthetic_events`/`background`, and never activate the window. A second case sets `MNS_NOTIFYBYPOS` on the bar inside `WM_INITMENU` and expects `WM_MENUCOMMAND` instead. `test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py` passes.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` green (rustfmt, SPDX headers, TypeScript typecheck, image refs); `cua-contract-gen all --check` passes on the regenerated manifest.
- Known gaps, CI required: this was written on a Linux host without a Windows desktop, so the Windows compile, clippy, unit and desktop E2E lanes (the new classic-menu test, WPF `harness_wpf_invoke_menu_live_path`) run only in CI. The UniFFI TypeScript doc comment was updated by hand to match the generator's output; the bindings drift check in CI confirms it.

Clients that list one line per tool (tool search results, `list-tools`) show the first line of each description. Most first lines are a whole paragraph, so a search result carries far more text than it needs. Putting the first sentence on its own line makes that line a one-sentence summary. #7764 did this and was reverted by #7790 because it was benched together with #7765, so its effect could not be separated. This PR re-lands it alone so it can be benched alone.

- `ToolDef::to_list_entry` puts the first sentence of each description on its own line (`lead_on_own_line`). Only that one space becomes a newline; no words change. The guide hint and deprecation prefix keep their places.
