title: fix(cua-driver): Linux XTest typing keeps the text's case while Caps Lock is on
body:
Salvaged from #6817

## Why

On Linux X11, XTest typing (desktop `type_text`, foreground delivery, and the `set_value` key fallback) typed the text with its case inverted while Caps Lock was on: "Hello" came out as "hELLO". CMGS's commit clears Lock for the duration of the text and restores it afterwards. Our commit on top sets the XKB lock state directly. The original version tapped the Lock key to turn Lock off and on, but a tap does nothing while that key is held down, so Lock stayed off after typing.

## What changed

- CMGS's commit: `CapsLockOff` guards `type_text_xtest`, clearing Lock before the text and restoring it on drop, including on error paths. A private-Xvfb test decodes the typed KeyPress events.
- Our commits: the guard reads the XKB locked modifiers and clears and restores Lock with XKB `LatchLockState` (x11rb `xkb` feature). A second test holds Caps Lock down during typing and checks that Lock is locked again afterwards. When a call is abandoned (timed out or cancelled) its X11 connection is shut, so the guard then restores Lock on a fresh connection, through the same path that releases held keys. The tests connect to their private Xvfb with no auth, and `test_env::x11_display` points `XAUTHORITY` at an empty file, so they never read the host's cookies.

## Scope

Only the X11 XTest typing route. Synthetic `XSendEvent` typing sets its key state explicitly and is not affected. Wayland, macOS and Windows are unchanged. A Caps Lock key physically held while text is typed still applies Lock, just as a held Shift would. The guard only restores the lock state correctly.

## Blast Radius

When Lock is not locked, XTest typing makes one extra XKB state query. The fresh-connection helper that releases an abandoned call's held keys now also carries the Caps Lock restore; its behavior for key releases is unchanged. When XKB is missing, the guard does nothing, which is the behavior before this change.

## Verification

- `caps_lock_tests` on a private Xvfb: with the guard disabled, the text decodes as `hELLO`. With CMGS's key-tap guard and Caps Lock held, Lock ends unlocked. Without the fresh-connection restore, abandoning the call mid-typing leaves Lock off. With this head, all three tests pass, and the full platform-linux lib suite passes.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick --signoff` passed, and `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -D warnings` was clean. The tests also pass with `XAUTHORITY` pointing at a FIFO, which used to block them.
- CMGS also checked the original commit on an XFCE/X11 desktop (Mousepad). That desktop run was not repeated here.

title: fix(cua-driver): release content-only UIA references after get_window_state
body:
Fixes #6867

## Why
On Windows, the UIA walker AddRefs every row it emits: actionable rows and content-only rows (named text, values). `UiaSnapshot::from_nodes` kept only the indexed rows and dropped the rest as plain integers. Every `get_window_state` therefore leaked one COM reference per content-only row, and the driver's private bytes grew with each call. @moonxmboo-eng found the cause and measured it in the issue thread.

## What changed
- `UiaSnapshot::from_nodes` now takes `&mut [UiaNode]` and takes every reference out of it: indexed rows move into the snapshot, the rest are released through the matching UIA or MSAA vtable, and each `element_ptr` is zeroed so a node no longer owns anything.
- The CoreWindow fallback in `walk_tree_unsafe` now releases whichever node set it discards: the primary walk when the fallback wins, the fallback walk otherwise.
- New test `snapshot_handoff_releases_content_only_walker_references` uses the existing fake refcounted COM object to check that the content row ends at refcount 0, the indexed row stays at 1 until the snapshot drops, and nothing is touched after release.

## Scope
Windows `platform-windows` only, in the `get_window_state` and recording-hook snapshot paths and the CoreWindow fallback. The browser consent and setup flows already release all nodes and are unchanged. This is the smaller of the two shapes from the issue thread (the release happens in the hand-off). Making `UiaNode.element_ptr` an owning type would also touch the browser flows and the many tests that use fake pointer values, so it is left out.

## Blast Radius
Every Windows tree read goes through this hand-off. Element indices and tokens are unchanged, because the snapshot keeps the same indexed rows in the same order. Nothing reads `element_ptr` from the nodes after the hand-off, so zeroing it changes no behavior.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): rustfmt and headers passed. Clippy, the unit tests and the Windows cross-check were skipped on this shared Linux host and run in CI's Windows lane.
- The new unit test is Windows-only and runs in CI.

title: [Bug]: lume crashes in Virtualization's VNC server (_VZVNCServer → addAccessorObserver assertion) and the VM stops
body:
### Primary area

Lume

### Summary

`lume run` crashed twice with `EXC_BREAKPOINT` (an assertion inside Virtualization.framework's private VNC server), and the running macOS VM stopped with it. Both crashes came within seconds of a VNC client connecting or disconnecting.

### Reproduction

1. `lume run <vm> --display none` (VNC enabled, the default) for a macOS 27.2.1 guest, from a LaunchAgent and once with `--detach`.
2. Connect a scripted VNC client to the local URL from `lume get --format json`, take a screenshot or click, and disconnect. I used `vncdo -s 127.0.0.1::<port> -p <password> move X Y pause 1 capture shot.png`, a new connection each time, closed abruptly when the command ends.
3. Repeat. It is intermittent: in about a dozen connections over 30 minutes, lume crashed twice (both times in a VM session that had several connections already).

### Expected behavior

The VNC session ends and the VM keeps running.

### Actual behavior

lume exits with `Trace/BPT trap: 5`, `asi: libsystem_c.dylib: assertion failed`, and the VM stops (no "stopping VM" log line; `lume ls` shows it stopped). Faulting thread, queue `com.apple.virtualization.vzvirtualmachine-accessor-manager`:

```
Virtualization  Base::assertion_trap()
Virtualization  -[_VZVirtualMachineAccessor addAccessorObserver:]
Virtualization  …Callback<…-[_VZVNCServer _setupVirtualMachineAccessor]::$_18>…::__invoke
libdispatch     _dispatch_client_callout
libdispatch     _dispatch_lane_serial_drain
libdispatch     _dispatch_lane_invoke
libdispatch     _dispatch_root_queue_drain_deferred_wlh
libdispatch     _dispatch_workloop_worker_thread
```

The two crash reports are identical. Timeline of the first: VNC capture at 10:46:10, lume logged `(Virtualization) VNC: Connection had error` at 10:47:10, and crashed at 10:47:13. The second came right as a new `vncdo` connection opened (its capture never completed).

I don't know whether the trigger is a new connection, the earlier connection's teardown, or both. The stack shows the VNC server re-running `_setupVirtualMachineAccessor` and the accessor asserting on the observer it adds.

### Environment

- lume 0.7.2 (Developer ID build from the `lume-v0.7.2` release)
- Host: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Mac16,5, arm64
- Guest: macOS 27.2.1 (26B131) from `UniversalMac_27.2.1_26B131_Restore.ipsw`, 8 vCPU, 16 GB, NAT
- VNC client: vncdotool 1.4.2

### Evidence

Crash reports `lume-2026-11-20-104713.ips` and `lume-2026-11-20-105431.ips` (the faulting stack is above; I can attach the full reports if useful).

### Workaround and additional context

`lume run <vm> --display none --vnc disabled`, driving the guest over SSH instead. No crash since.

Since the assertion is inside Apple's private `_VZVNCServer`, it may be a framework bug that only shows up under rapid connect/disconnect. Still, lume might avoid it, for example by keeping one VNC server for the VM's lifetime, or by not creating a new accessor per connection. Related: #3878 (an explicit bind address for VNC, since the listener is also reachable on the LAN).

title: fix(cua-driver): map DIP element frames onto X11 window screenshots
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux X11, an Electron window at device scale 2 got negative root `screenshot_frame` values (`{-520,-220,920,680}` for a 1840x1360 capture). Chromium reports AT-SPI extents in DIPs, but `get_window_state` subtracted the X11 window origin, which is in device pixels, and applied no DIP-to-pixel scale.
- What changed: new `with_x11_screenshot_frames` reads the X11 window geometry and checks the shallowest top-level (`frame`/`window`/`dialog`) element frames, the window-level ones, for one that, times a factor of 1 or more, equals the X11 window rectangle. The factor must fit x, y, w and h within one DIP of rounding. An application-wide tree can hold several (at a device scale the walk cannot scope DIP extents to the X11 window), and a match at factor 1 wins. Among DIP matches, the frame closest to the window's edges wins. With a match above 1, frames map from that frame's own origin times the factor, and the matched root's `screenshot_frame` is the delivered capture, since its DIP size is rounded. The same goes for any element with the root's exact bounds. With no such match the old math runs unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #6935

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Linux X11 only, `screenshot_frame` on device-scaled Chromium/Electron windows. The root now starts at (0,0) and spans the native capture. `frame` (screen space) is unchanged. Wayland, popups and DPR 1 windows take the same path as before.
- Risk and rollback: the scale applies only when a window-level frame matches the X11 window's size and origin within one DIP. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `x11_screenshot_frame_tests` in `platform-linux/src/tools/get_window_state.rs` covers the issue's DPR 2 numbers, a DPR 1 control, a half-size dialog elsewhere, a half-size dialog at the window origin (in a window-scoped tree and in an application-wide one; neither dialog may be read as a scale), an application-wide tree with two DPR 2 windows, a larger nested dialog that must not win the match, an odd X11 origin, a rounded DIP height, a rounded DIP width far from the origin, a neighbouring DIP frame that must not beat an exact match, and two maximized windows with identical bounds. Neither rounding case may leave an offset or a short root. These ran in an extracted crate. With the scale forced to 1 (the old behavior), the DPR 2 test fails with the issue's exact `{-520,-220,920,680}`. With the fix it passes.
- Scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passes (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs). Clippy and crate unit tests were skipped locally because the host is low on disk, so they are left to CI.
- Known gaps: not run against a live DPR 2 Electron window on X11. `frame` stays in Chromium's DIP space rather than X11 root pixels, which is a separate question about desktop-scope targeting.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep X11 native dialogs from returning the main window's tree
body:
## Why

On X11, `resolve_window_frame` bound the sole AT-SPI root to any window the caller named. An Electron native modal has its own X11 window but no AT-SPI root. So `get_window_state` on the dialog returned the main window's tree, bound its element tokens to the dialog and reported `elements_complete: true`.

## What changed

- The X11 sole-root shortcut, and the X11 rule that lets an uncorrelated (application-wide) walk stand for a window, now hold only for an override-redirect popup or for a process with no other window (`x11_app_tree_is_window`). Siblings come from the new `x11::window_inventory`. Without an EWMH client list, `list_windows` drops untitled windows and windows that publish no `_NET_WM_PID`. The inventory keeps every managed window, minimized ones included, attributes owners through `OwnerResolver` (which knows XRes), and returns nothing when it cannot walk the whole window tree. In that case nothing binds. Otherwise the root must match the window by geometry. If it does not, the snapshot is marked `accessibility_window_identity_unproven` and gets no element tokens.
- `correlate_frame_to_window` binds a frame only when every other window in that inventory that the frame plausibly fits has a decisively better frame of its own. So a frameless dialog near its main window blocks the main window's frame from binding to either window, whatever the decoration offsets, while cascaded windows that each publish a frame still bind one to one. `elements_complete` also requires the snapshot to be bound to the requested window.
- Unit tests cover the window rule (a dialog beside its main window, a dialog the inventory missed, a lone window, a popup), the inventory's client rule (every managed window counts, minimized or not, with no title or pid read), and the geometry match (a frameless dialog at two decoration offsets, cascaded windows, a distant dialog).

## Scope

Linux X11 `get_window_state` window binding. Wayland, Hyprland, niri and GNOME rules, element actions, and the X11 property fallback (which is read from the window itself) are unchanged. Override-redirect popups, detected by their X11 attribute, keep the application-wide tree they had before.

## Tradeoffs

The issue allows either the dialog's own tree or an explicit unavailable result. When AT-SPI publishes no root for the dialog, there is no dialog tree to return, so this returns the unavailable result.

## Blast Radius

- X11 apps with more than one managed window and a single AT-SPI root: a window whose geometry matches the root still binds, unless a frameless sibling sits close enough to match it too. Any other window now reports a degraded, application-scoped tree with `elements_complete: false` and no element tokens, where before it was given another window's controls.
- `list_windows` output is unchanged; only the binding checks read the untitled-inclusive inventory. Without a window manager, a mapped override-redirect window of the process (a tooltip) counts as a sibling, so the shortcut then defers to geometry.
- GNOME: a snapshot the Shell cannot prove belongs to the window now also reports `elements_complete: false`. It already got no tokens and was already marked degraded.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass: rustfmt and the SPDX headers. Clippy, the platform-linux unit tests and the Windows cross-check were skipped on this shared host and run in CI.
- The changed pure functions and their tests were compiled standalone with `rustc --test`: 11 tests pass. Removing the sibling-frame check, the listed-window requirement or the inventory's client rule each fails its test.
- The Electron native-dialog reproduction from the issue has not been run against this change.

- [x] `bin/ci` (quick mode on a shared host)

Fixes #6936

title: fix(cua-driver): recommend foreground for unverifiable background keys to Chromium and Electron apps
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a background `hotkey` or `press_key` to a Chrome-family browser or an Electron app is often dropped by the renderer, but the result reads as a bare `effect: "unverifiable"`, so the caller gets no hint to retry in the foreground.
- What changed: when a background `hotkey` or `press_key` to a Chromium or Electron app ends `unverifiable`, the structured result carries `escalation: { recommended: "foreground", reason, requires: ["window_id"] }`, the text result gets one sentence saying the same, and `press_key`'s `ActionResult` gets `escalation.target: "foreground"`. The `hotkey` description no longer says Chromium and Electron accept background combos as trusted live input. Foreground calls, confirmed results and other apps are unchanged.

Salvaged from #6967 by @lucharo: their commit is kept as authored, with the `hotkey` description fix (the gap #6967 left open) on top.

## Related work

Refs #4997
Refs #5355 (WKWebView targets are not covered)

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Background key results for Chromium and Electron apps gain an `escalation` and one sentence of text; callers that ignore `escalation` see no change. The MCP reference page and macOS snapshot for `hotkey` are updated to the new description.
- Risk and rollback: the hint also appears on a key that did land, since nothing tells the two apart; the text says the key "may not have arrived" and asks the caller to check the window first. Revert to roll back.

title: [Bug]: On Windows, cua-driver skills install creates an NTFS junction that Antigravity ignores
body:
### Summary
On Windows, `cua-driver mcp-config --client antigravity` (and `cua-driver skills install`) installs the Antigravity skill by creating an **NTFS Junction** (`ReparsePoint`) at `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\config\skills\cua-driver` pointing to `%USERPROFILE%\.cua-driver\skills\cua-driver`.

Antigravity does not discover or load this skill when it is an NTFS junction.

### Environment
- **OS:** Windows 11 (`10.0.26300.9974`, `x86_64`)
- **cua-driver:** `0.55.0` (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, git `8f484f30586e`)
- **Client:** Google Antigravity (Language Server `2.33.0`)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Install `cua-driver` on Windows via `irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex`.
2. Run `cua-driver mcp-config --client antigravity` (or `cua-driver skills install`).
   - Output reports: `cua-driver: installed the skill pack for Antigravity IDE at C:\Users\<user>\.gemini\config\skills\cua-driver`
   - `Get-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.gemini\config\skills\cua-driver" -Force` shows `Attributes: Directory, ReparsePoint` and `LinkType: Junction`.
3. Restart Antigravity and check **Skills & Customizations** and the agent's loaded skills list.

### Expected Behavior
Antigravity discovers and loads the `cua-driver` skill.

### Actual Behavior
Antigravity completely ignores `cua-driver` — it does not appear in the UI or in the agent's available skills list.

### Root Cause & Verification
Antigravity's Go-based language server skips NTFS junctions when scanning `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\config\skills\` (on Windows, Go's `os.ReadDir` returns `DirEntry.IsDir() == false` for junctions/reparse points).

**Verified workaround:** Removing the junction and copying `%USERPROFILE%\.cua-driver\skills\cua-driver` as a regular directory to `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\config\skills\cua-driver` makes Antigravity immediately discover and load the `cua-driver` skill with no changes to `SKILL.md`.

### Suggested Fix
For Antigravity on Windows (or via a `--copy` option / per-agent copy strategy), materialize `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\config\skills\cua-driver` as a regular directory copy (and refresh it on `cua-driver skills update`) instead of an NTFS junction.

title: fix(cua-driver): an exact frame match names its Linux window among cascaded windows of one size
body:
Salvaged from #6983

## Why

On Linux, `get_window_state` for one of two same-size windows of one process returned the elements of both. Chrome cascades a new window by 10 px, so two such frames sit 20 px apart in `frame_geometry_distance`, under `FRAME_MATCH_MARGIN_PX` (24). `correlate_frame_to_window` refused and the read walked every window of the application, so an element index could land in the other window. @CMGS found and fixed this in #6983; this PR lands their commit on current main.

## What changed

- A frame that matches the window's geometry exactly (distance 0), while no other frame does, resolves without the margin. Two exact frames, or a close but inexact best frame, still refuse. (CMGS's commit, kept as authored.)
- The exact match counts only when every other frame within the margin has the window's own size, so it differs by position alone. A sibling that lands on the target's X11 bounds while the target's own frame includes a border still refuses, as on main.
- `resolve_window_frame` re-reads the window's X11 geometry after reading the AT-SPI extents, and refuses the correlation if the window moved in between, so a same-size sibling on its old bounds cannot win. The `FRAME_MATCH_*` docs name the exception.

## Scope

Linux AT-SPI frame correlation only. macOS, Windows and the Wayland/Hyprland frame paths do not call `correlate_frame_to_window`.

## Blast Radius

Linux reads of multi-window apps where one frame matches the X11 geometry exactly now scope to that window instead of the whole application. A frame offset by decorations still needs the margin, as before.

## Tradeoffs

The geometry recheck costs one more X11 query per correlated read. It has no unit test: it sits in the live AT-SPI and X11 path, and the repo keeps test-only hooks out of shipped code.

## Verification

- `frame_correlation_tests::an_exact_match_resolves_among_cascaded_windows_of_one_size`: each cascaded frame resolves to its own window, and a window midway between them refuses.
- `frame_correlation_tests::an_exact_match_beside_a_bordered_frame_still_refuses` failed on CMGS's commit (`Some(1)`) and passes with the size guard.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, headers); `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib frame_correlation_tests` (9 passed) and `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
- #6983 reports the read on an X11 (Xfwm) desktop with two cascaded Chrome windows listing only the requested window's elements after the fix.

title: fix(cua-driver): return app_unresponsive at once for a Linux app while its GetState probe is pending
body:
Salvaged from #6991

## Why

On Linux, `get_window_state` on an app that has stopped answering AT-SPI (stopped, or stuck in a modal grab) spent the caller's whole walk budget on every call before it returned `app_unresponsive`, because nothing recorded the miss. CMGS's commit marks the pid and returns `app_unresponsive` right away while a `GetState` probe to the app's root is pending. The fix on top clears the mark when the probe ends, whatever its result, so a probe that timed out can no longer leave the pid marked after the app resumes.

## What changed

- CMGS's commit (cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship kept): when an app misses `GetChildren`, its pid is marked and later walks of that pid return `app_unresponsive` at once, while one `GetState` probe, bounded by `OP_TIMEOUT`, runs on the AT-SPI runtime.
- Our fix: the mark lasts only while its probe is pending. A reply, an error or the timeout each clears it, and the next walk reads the app. Before this, a stop longer than `OP_TIMEOUT` left the pid marked, and the first walk after the app resumed returned a stale `app_unresponsive`. The per-pid probing flag and map are gone; a `HashSet` of pids holds the mark.
- Unit test `a_pid_stays_unresponsive_only_while_its_probe_is_pending` covers this. It is hermetic: the probe is a oneshot future, with no D-Bus.

## Scope

Linux AT-SPI walks (`collect_visited_bounded_opts`: snapshots and menu path walks) only. macOS and Windows are unchanged. There is no new setting and no change to the `app_unresponsive` contract.

## Blast Radius

While an app stays unresponsive, a walk of its pid now pays the full budget at most once per probe (about once per `OP_TIMEOUT`) instead of on every call. While a probe is pending, a caller that passes a longer `timeout_ms` gets `app_unresponsive` at once and does not wait out its budget.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks, quick stage (`bin/ci --quick`): rustfmt and headers pass. Clippy and unit tests run in CI.
- Platform evidence for the original change is in #6991.

title: fix(cua-driver): use managed directory copy for Antigravity skills on Windows (#8378)
body:
## Summary
Resolves #8378.

On Windows, `cua-driver skills install` and `cua-driver mcp-config --client antigravity` install skill packs by creating an NTFS junction (`mklink /J`) under `%USERPROFILE%\.gemini\config\skills\cua-driver`. Antigravity's Go language server skips NTFS junctions when enumerating skills directories because Go's `DirEntry.IsDir()` returns `false` on Windows for junctions/reparse points.

## Changes
- Introduce `InstallStrategy` in `skills.rs` (`Copy` on Windows for Antigravity targets, `Symlink` elsewhere).
- Materialize Antigravity skill folders on Windows as regular directory copies with a `.cua-driver-managed` marker.
- Automatically detect and migrate existing NTFS junctions to directory copies on install/update.
- Synchronize modified skill files during `skills update`.
- Support uninstallation of managed copies in both `skills.rs` and `uninstall.ps1`.
- Added unit tests verifying Windows copy strategy and marker creation.

title: fix(cua-driver): Windows type_text writes through the focused document at its caret or selection
body:
Salvaged from #6995

## Why

On Windows, no-element `type_text` writes through the focused UI Automation document only while that document is empty. Every later line goes in as SendInput Unicode packets, and Windows 11 Notepad collapses queued packets into a run of one character after a `/` or `€`. This lets the focused-document route write at the caret or over the selection of a non-empty document, so those lines arrive intact.

## What changed

- @CMGS's commit, kept as authored: the route now takes a writable document of at most 1M characters with one selection. It requires the text before the selection, the selection and the rest to rebuild the value exactly, writes the text in place of the selection, places the caret after it, and checks the text before the caret. A selection that moved before the write sends the text by keys as before.
- Our commits: a document with embedded objects or formatting that varies across it keeps the key route, since SetValue rewrites the whole document as plain text. The caret also tries the character count of the written text as the control stores it, where a CRLF counts as two. An append (selection at the end) keeps main's document-end caret.
- The generated Windows reference carries the new tool description.

## Scope

Windows `type_text` with no element, foreground, focused writable UIA Document only. The key route, `element_token` writes and Chromium/Electron boundaries are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Windows apps whose focused Document exposes a writable ValuePattern and a single-selection TextPattern, such as Windows 11 Notepad. As with the existing empty-document write, Notepad does not mark the document modified, Ctrl+Z does not undo the write, and Autocorrect does not act on it. Every write is read back; a write whose caret cannot be verified is reported as unverifiable and not retried.

## Verification

- `bin/ci --quick` (the scoped repository checks that run without a build): rustfmt and SPDX headers pass; clippy, unit tests and the Windows cross-compile run in CI.
- Unit tests in `uia::focused_document` cover the selection mapping, a selection that moved before the write, the size cap and the caret unit counts, including a stored CRLF. The rich-content check calls UIA directly and has no unit test; it needs a live Windows run.
- #6995 reports the Notepad behavior before and after on a Windows 11 host.

title: fix(cua-driver): Windows type_text waits out a slow focused-document probe and sends no keys after it
body:
Salvaged from #6996

Builds on #8386 (our salvage of #6995). The new commits are the last three; the first three are #8386's head.

## Why

On Windows, `type_text` with no element first probes the focused UI Automation document within 200 ms. When the probe missed that deadline, the call fell back to SendInput Unicode keys. A probe misses the deadline when the target is busy or starved, which is also when Windows 11 Notepad defers and replays key messages and garbles the text into runs of one character. This waits longer for the probe and, when the target still does not answer, returns an error that says nothing was written and no keys were sent.

## What changed

- @CMGS's commit, kept as authored: the probe gets 2 s. A probe that has not answered by then, or a call that finds the previous probe still running, returns `The target did not answer UI Automation in time; nothing was written and no keys were sent.` Only an unavailable UIA worker still falls back to keys. The single-flight permit is dropped before the worker sends its result, so the next call can start a probe at once.
- Our commit: the probe gate is process-wide, and a timed-out probe holds it until its provider call returns. Reporting every `Busy` as unanswered meant one stuck app made `type_text` fail in every other foreground window until then. `Busy` is now an error only when the running probe is for the same window; for another window the call takes the key route as before. The gate records each probe's window as it admits it, so a `Busy` always names the probe holding the gate, even one starved before it ran.

## Scope

Windows `type_text` with no element, `scope: desktop` or foreground delivery, to a window that is already foreground. Background delivery, `element_token` writes and the key route itself are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Any Windows foreground target whose UIA provider takes longer than 2 s to answer now gets an error instead of keys. Before, keys went in after 200 ms and could arrive garbled. A probe stuck on one window no longer affects other windows.

## Verification

- `bin/ci --quick` (the scoped repository checks that run without a build): rustfmt and SPDX headers pass; clippy, unit tests and the Windows cross-compile run in CI.
- Unit tests in `uia::focused_document` cover a timed-out or same-window busy probe (error, no keys), a probe still running for another window (keys), an unavailable worker (keys), and errors after a write started (unknown effect, no retry). A `uia::windows_enum` test holds a probe for one window and checks that a retry for it and a call for another window each get the right `Busy`.
- #6996 reports the throttled Windows 11 Notepad trials before and after CMGS's commit.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop cua-driver test from failing Linux and Windows on macOS grants
body:
Salvaged from #7009

Fixes #6998

## Why

On Linux and Windows, `cua-driver test` always failed at its first step. It read the macOS `accessibility` and `screen_recording` flags from `check_permissions`, which neither platform reports, then told the user to turn on Accessibility and Screen Recording. This lands @astrovm's fix from #7009, rebased on main, with their commit unchanged.

## What changed

- `selftest::Backend` gains `asks_for_permission_grants()`, true only on macOS. The grant steps run only where it is true. Elsewhere the screen read and pointer steps are the check.
- On Linux and Windows, failure fixes point to `cua-driver doctor` instead of the macOS-only `cua-driver permissions grant`.
- The `cua-driver test` help, CLI spec JSON and reference docs say that only macOS has permissions to check. A follow-up commit qualifies the top-level `test` help line and the `manifest` description the same way.

## Scope

Covers `cua-driver test` steps and fix text. macOS output, steps and exit codes are unchanged. On Linux and Windows, the JSON report no longer has `accessibility` or `screen_recording` steps.

## Blast Radius

Linux and Windows users of `cua-driver test` and the install script that runs it. A machine that can't read the screen still fails, at `screen_read`.

## Verification

- New `selftest` unit tests feed in what Linux `check_permissions` returns: no grant steps, no macOS setting names, and fixes that point to `doctor`.
- The contributor ran `cua-driver test` on KDE Plasma 6 Wayland: before the fix it printed the two macOS failures, after it the test passed and exited 0.
- The scoped repository checks run in CI on this branch.

- [x] `bin/ci --quick` passes.

title: fix(cua-driver): set up an existing Brave profile on Linux X11
body:
Salvaged from #7059

Fixes #7053

## Why

`browser_prepare` with `strategy: existing_profile` refused every Brave window. Brave serves Chromium's inspect page at `brave://inspect/#remote-debugging` with Chrome's labels, so @astrovm's commit gives it a setup descriptor. That descriptor is shared by every adapter, and Brave was read and attached only on Linux X11. A second commit keeps the other platforms refusing.

## What changed

- @astrovm's commit (kept as authored): a `BRAVE` setup descriptor, plus the browsers guide now lists Brave.
- `existing_profile_setup_descriptor` takes a `SetupPlatform` (`MacOS`, `Windows`, `LinuxX11`, `LinuxWayland`). Brave resolves only on `LinuxX11`. The Linux adapter maps XWayland and native Wayland to `LinuxWayland`.
- The guide says setup refuses Brave on other platforms.

## Scope

Covers existing-profile setup and cleanup for Brave. Chrome, Edge and Chromium resolve on every platform, as before. Out of scope: Brave on macOS, Windows and Wayland, which keep refusing with "not implemented for Brave" until someone verifies them, and Wayland existing-profile setup in general (#7054).

## Blast Radius

cua-driver's browser setup in the core crate and all three adapters. The only behavior change is on Linux X11, where Brave now attaches instead of refusing. Everywhere else, behavior is unchanged.

## Verification

- `setup_descriptor` unit tests: Chrome, Edge and Chromium resolve on all four platforms, and Brave resolves only on `LinuxX11`. The scoped repository checks run in CI.
- From #7059, the contributor ran Brave 1.99 on Linux X11 (Openbox on Xvfb): `attached_existing_profile` in 4 of 4 runs, then `get_browser_state` bound `exact`. Before the change it refused.
- Not run here: native Brave setup on any desktop, and macOS and Windows builds. CI covers the builds.

title: [Bug]: local windows:11 (ARM64) Space boots with Linux QEMU devices after a successful build, never becomes ready
body:
### Primary area

Containers or images

### Summary

On an Apple silicon Mac, `cua sb create ghcr.io/trycua/windows:11` builds the Windows 11 ARM64 base successfully, but every Space created from that base is started with the **Linux** QEMU device set (system disk on `virtio-blk-pci`, `virtio-gpu-pci`, cloud-init `cidata`, no `ramfb`, no TPM) instead of the Windows ARM set used by the build (`nvme`, `ramfb`, swtpm). Windows never boots and the create fails with `probe Tcp { port: 3211 } never passed`.

### Reproduction

1. Apple silicon Mac (16 GB), QEMU from Homebrew, Cua Spaces app installed.
2. `cua sb create ghcr.io/trycua/windows:11 --name w11 --memory 4GB` (the first run builds `~/.cua/images/windows/11-arm64/base.qcow2` from Microsoft's ISO; this part succeeds).
3. `cua sb create ghcr.io/trycua/windows:11 --name w11 --memory 4GB --ready-timeout 1500 --keep-on-failure`
4. Inspect `~/.cua/vmm/qemu/w11/cmdline` and `serial.log`.

Reproduced 3 times on cua 0.28.2 and again after updating to Cua Spaces 0.39.8 / cua 0.29.3. Every time.

### Expected behavior

The Space boots from the built base with the same Windows ARM device model as the build (NVMe system disk, `ramfb`, swtpm TPM), and cua-spacesd answers on port 3211.

### Actual behavior

The create waits the whole readiness budget and fails:

```
cua: local runtime: [local] sandbox 'w11' was not ready after 0s: probe Tcp { port: 3211 } never passed
```

The Space's overlay disk stays at ~197 KB (Windows never writes to it) and the serial log stops in the UEFI firmware. The "after 0s" text is misleading: with `--ready-timeout 1500` it waited ~25 minutes.

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: Cua Spaces 0.39.8 (cua CLI 0.29.3); first seen on Cua Spaces 0.38.10 (cua 0.28.2)
Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2.1, arm64 (Apple silicon), 16 GB RAM
Application/browser/window system/image: `ghcr.io/trycua/windows:11` (local build, `windows-iso`), QEMU 11.1.3 (Homebrew), HVF

### Evidence

Built base metadata (`~/.cua/images/windows/11-arm64/base.json`):

```json
}
```

### Workaround and additional context

No workaround found (longer `--ready-timeout` and the update to 0.29.3 do not change it).

Suspected area (not verified by building cua): in `libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/qemu/args.rs` the NVMe/`ramfb`/TPM path is taken only when `cfg.os == GuestOs::Windows && cfg.arch == Arch::Aarch64`, and `libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon-core/src/local.rs` starts the Space with `.os(os_of(&spec.os))`, where `os_of` maps anything other than `macos`/`windows` to `GuestOs::Linux`. The cmdline above matches the Linux branch, so it looks like the create request for the locally built `windows:11` base does not carry `os = "windows"` on the CLI path.

Possibly related open PRs: #4373 (report Windows QEMU startup failures), #4372, #4763.

Separate small note (happy to file it separately if preferred): the first build needs 8 GiB free regardless of `--memory` (`'cua-build-windows-11-arm64', expected to need 8.0 GiB, does not fit`), easy to hit on a 16 GB Mac.

I can test a fix on this machine: the built base and ISO are kept.

title: fix(cua-driver): never advise a foreground retry for an unconfirmed macOS terminal insert
body:
Salvaged from #7277
Fixes #7243

## Why

When a background `type_text` into a macOS terminal can't be confirmed, the reply says to verify by screenshot and retry with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, and `escalation.recommended` is `"foreground"`. A terminal reading with echo off (`read -s`, `sudo`, `ssh`) never shows the text, so a caller that follows that advice types it a second time.

## What changed

- `unconfirmed_advice(path, is_terminal_target)` now picks the unverified note and decides whether a foreground escalation goes with it. For a terminal, the reply says the text may not echo and must not be typed again, and it carries no `escalation`, whichever route delivered it.
- A terminal whose read-back the web-content probe marks untrusted (Hyper is Electron, or the window's focused element can't be reacquired) stays unverified. It now gets the terminal note instead of the browser note and a `page` or `px` escalation telling the caller to retype (`advises_web_rung`).
- Other targets get the same notes and escalation as before.

## Scope

This covers the macOS `type_text` reply text and its `escalation` field for unverified inserts. Delivery behavior does not change. #7277 depended on #7276, which was closed. Main already carries the equivalent `reported()` filter, which turns an unechoed terminal insert into an unverified result instead of `type_text_incomplete`, so this change works on main by itself.

## Blast Radius

It affects only callers that type into a terminal and get an unverified result: they no longer get advice to retype. It is macOS only. The other platforms have no matching advice path.

## Verification

- Focused unit tests: `an_unconfirmed_terminal_insert_is_never_sent_to_the_foreground` and `a_terminal_with_web_read_back_never_gets_web_retype_advice`.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass.

Thanks @CMGS for the fix. Their commit is kept as authored, and our fixes are separate commits on top.

title: Session idle eviction hook leaves every later Chrome spawn in the host process windowless until runtime shutdown
body:
## Summary

On macOS, after the idle-TTL eviction hook runs for a driver session (remove_session + cleanup_prepared_session + the owned-browser process-group SIGKILL), any Chrome process spawned afterwards by the same host process is created **without a native window** — including Chrome spawned directly by the embedding host, not through the driver. The Chrome process stays alive, its DevTools endpoint works, and its main thread runs the normal AppKit event loop, but CGWindowList reports zero Chrome windows. The state persists until the driver runtime is shut down: `shutdown()` clears it, and a fresh runtime in the same process spawns windowed Chrome again.

## Reproduction (TTL=5 forced; macOS 27.2 arm64; Google Chrome 158)

1. `start_session` → `browser_prepare` (isolated) → window appears, bind, navigate — all normal.
2. Idle past the eviction sweep (TTL + ≤30 s): the owned Chrome is killed, session evicted.
3. `start_session` (revive) → `browser_prepare` again: the new Chrome process is alive, its CDP endpoint is alive, **but no window is created** — full `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` enumeration shows no Chrome entry at all, so it is not a pid-attribution issue.
4. From the same host process, spawn Chrome directly (`posix_spawn`, fresh profile): also windowless.
5. `driver.shutdown()` → a Chrome spawned by the host immediately gets a window again.

## Evidence

- Hard-kill (`kill -9`) a healthy bound browser (eviction hook never runs) → later rebuilds spawn windowed Chrome normally. The trigger is the eviction hook path, not browser death itself.
- In the bad state, host-side direct Chrome spawn is also windowless → the contamination is host-process-wide, not specific to the driver's spawn route.
- After `driver.shutdown()`, spawns recover immediately → instance-scoped and cleared by shutdown.
- `sample` of the windowless Chrome: main thread idle in the normal AppKit event loop, CDP alive → not a hang.
- Full CGWindowList enumeration in the bad state: zero Chrome entries → Chrome never created a window.

## Static scoping

Our local patch chain (three patched builds of 0.28.0) touches none of the eviction/cleanup/process-group paths — the hook path is unmodified upstream code. The exact upstream line that poisons the process state was not located; the failure manifests as Chrome-side window creation not happening, cause unknown.

## Suggested directions

- Instrument the session-end hook path (remove_session → cleanup_prepared_session → process-group kill → profile cleanup) for process-global side effects visible to later `posix_spawn` children (environment, mach ports, launchd/bootstrap session claims).
- Diff process state before/after eviction for anything a freshly spawned Chrome would inherit.

## Local mitigation (context, not a fix)

The embedding plugin detects the driver tombstone and reopens the runtime before the next `browser_prepare`, and raises the default via `CUA_DRIVER_RS_SESSION_IDLE_TTL_SECS`. This closes the user-visible path, but the underlying contamination remains.

**Environment:** macOS 27.2 arm64, embedded cua-driver 0.28.0 (local patched builds of upstream `1b50c02e`), Google Chrome 158.0.8127.37.

title: fix(cua-driver): one ScreenCaptureKit user per unbundled macOS executable
body:
## Why

`replayd` identifies a ScreenCaptureKit client by its bundle identifier, or by its executable path when it has no bundle. When two processes start from the same unbundled `cua-driver` binary (the Python wheel and `cargo install` both ship one), each new connection cancels the other. `replayd` then spins, both daemons grow while idle, every ScreenCaptureKit capture times out, and the second daemon can die with SIGTRAP in `captureImage(in:)`. With this change, only one process per executable path uses ScreenCaptureKit.

## What changed

- New `platform-macos/src/capture_owner.rs`. Before its first ScreenCaptureKit call, a process outside an app bundle takes an exclusive file lock named after its executable path and holds it for life. The lock lives in the per-user cache directory from `confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)`.
- Window and desktop captures, the permission registration, the Screen Recording probe and `SCStream` recording all take that claim first. A process that finds it held uses the existing `screencapture` fallback, probes with `screencapture`, and refuses to start a recording with an error that names the holder. Once the holder exits, the next capture takes the claim.
- On top of abonneth's commit, our commit drops the measurement figures from the module doc.

## Scope

macOS only. Covers a second process from the same executable while the first one is alive. A single daemon, daemons at different paths, and app `Contents/MacOS` executables behave as before. No tool, schema or permission change. An older build that runs from the same path holds no lock, so it still collides.

## Blast Radius

Any process that cannot get the claim behaves as described above. Its desktop capture cannot leave out the cursor overlay, and `agent_overlay_capture` reports that, as it already does whenever the fallback is used. If the lock file cannot be opened, the process continues without the claim, which is the current behavior.

## Verification

- `a_claimed_executable_refuses_a_second_claim_until_the_first_is_released` covers the lock: a second claim is refused and names the holder's pid until the first claim is dropped.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass. The Rust checks run in CI.
- In #7639 the contributor ran two daemons from one binary on macOS 26.7 and 15.8. On main, `replayd` stayed busy until one daemon exited. With this change it went idle and both daemons returned captures.

Salvaged from #7639

Fixes #7548
Refs #7549

title: fix(macos): recognize Perplexity Comet as a Chromium browser
body:
Salvaged from #7848

## Why

On macOS every `browser_*` call against a Perplexity Comet window refused with `browser_route_unavailable` ("pid … is not a recognized browser process"). Comet is a Chromium fork (bundle id `ai.perplexity.comet`), but `is_chromium` checks names against a fixed token list that did not include `comet`.

## What changed

- `platform-macos`: `comet` joins the Chromium token list, a new `BrowserProduct::Comet` gets the standalone-consumer role, and its profile root is `Library/Application Support/Comet`.
- `cua-driver-core`: `BrowserProduct::Comet` plus an existing-profile setup descriptor at `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` with the Chromium inspect-page anchors.
- Docs: Comet on macOS joins the "Detected, not release-accepted" row in platform support.

## Scope

macOS detection only. Comet also ships for Windows, and Windows and Linux classification stay as they are. The setup descriptor reuses the Chromium page anchors. They match exactly, so if Comet's labels turn out different, setup refuses rather than acting on the wrong control.

## Blast Radius

Only processes whose name or bundle id has a `comet` token. Before this change they were refused outright. Other products classify the same as before.

## Verification

- Unit tests cover the classification, the profile root and the setup descriptor.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass.
- The contributor saw the refusal on a live Comet 157 window, and saw the accessibility route return a tree for the same process.

Thanks @KaraboGerald for the original fix.

title: feat(cua-driver): bind KDE foreground input to the target window
body:
## Why

On KDE Wayland, KWin sends each libei event to whichever window has focus when it processes that event. If focus moves between activating the target and sending input, keys or clicks reach another application, so the driver refused all foreground input on KWin. This adds an input gate to the Cua KWin helper. The gate lets the driver's own libei events reach only the target window or its transients, and holds back everything else.

Salvaged from #7070 by @astrovm. Their commits are kept as authored. On top of them, this PR merges `main` (resolving a conflict in `libs/cua-driver/docs/action-support.md`) and adds four fix commits:

- The gate is disarmed only after a libei barrier confirms that EIS has acknowledged all the input the driver sent. Before this, input whose caller had stopped waiting could reach KWin after the disarm and go out ungated. The barrier waits behind every earlier queued command. If EIS never acknowledges it, the gate stays armed and KWin input is refused until the driver restarts.
- A held-back key press is marked filtered in KWin (`addFilteredKey`, in KWin 6.3 through 6.8). Otherwise KWin still counted it as held and named it in the keyboard enter of the next focused window.
- `kwin-capture off` calls the new `CloseInputGate()` and then unloads the helper over the same D-Bus connection. The helper refuses new gates while that connection is open, so it is never unloaded while a gate is armed. Only one caller can hold the gate closed at a time.
- The helper's watchers on a gate's owner and closer are installed before it confirms the caller is still connected. Before this, a caller that left before its watcher existed went unnoticed, which left the gate armed, or new gates refused, until the helper was reloaded. A disconnect from a disarmed gate's owner also no longer drops a newer gate's watcher.
- One-off helper D-Bus calls such as `GetFocus` are bounded by the call timeout.

Fixes #7054

## Open findings (not merge-ready)

The last review at `47f2e8fc30` found these in the helper. Each needs a KWin build and a run of `kwin-target-helper/tests/run.sh`, which no CI lane does:

1. A key pressed while the target had focus has its release passed to whichever window has focus when the release arrives. After focus moves to B, KWin names the held key in B's keyboard enter, and B gets the release.
2. If B holds a Wayland popup grab when A is activated, the gate passes a key because the seat reports A, but KWin's later popup filter sends it to B's popup.
3. With Xwayland key sharing on, a later KWin filter can forward a key that passed for A to X11 clients.
4. `DisarmInput` checks the arm id but not the D-Bus sender, so another connection can clear a gate while its action is still sending.
5. If the helper fails to register its D-Bus name at load, KWin keeps an inert copy loaded that `kwin-capture on` cannot replace and `off` does not unload.

## What changed

- KWin helper protocol 2 adds `ArmInput`, `GetInputGate`, `DisarmInput` and `GetFocus`. The gate is a KWin input filter that covers only the devices of the `cua-driver <pid>` libei client that armed it. It is released on `DisarmInput` or when the arming D-Bus connection closes.
- The driver arms the gate around each KWin `click`, `scroll`, `drag`, `type_text`, `press_key` and `hotkey` call. Inside the gate it activates the target, confirms keyboard focus, sends the input, and then gives focus back to the window that had it. If the gate held back any event, the call fails with `input_interrupted`. While the gate is armed, the non-libei routes and `ei_text` stand down. Without protocol 2, KWin input is still refused, and the refusal now names `cua-driver kwin-capture on`.
- `cua-driver kwin-capture on/off/status` now also loads or unloads the helper and sets or clears its `kwinrc` autostart entry. A new `kwin-target-helper/install.sh` builds and installs the helper. An opt-in container kit (`kwin-target-helper/tests`) covers Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 45. `type_text` and `press_key` replies on Wayland now name the route that actually sent the keys.

## Scope

Covers foreground keyboard and pointer input to KWin windows on Plasma 6 Wayland. Background input on KWin is still refused. Also includes one CI tooling commit from the contributor: `bin/ci` now reads the image-doctor ledger from `trycua/cua` instead of `origin`, so a fork checkout no longer fails every docs image ref. The KDE desktop E2E matrix is not wired up. The helper kit is opt-in and needs `/dev/dri`.

## Tradeoffs

- Text that the active layout has no key for is refused while the gate is armed. KWin 6.8 hands `ei_text` strings to the input method without passing any input filter, so the gate could not bind them to the target.
- KWin moves the pointer and updates modifier state before input filters run. An event the gate holds back can still move the cursor or leave a modifier set in KWin's state. It never reaches another window. The helper README documents this.

## Blast Radius

The helper is a KWin effect plugin, so a bug in it runs inside KWin. The filter returns early when no gate is armed and only reads focus. Users without the protocol 2 helper see the same refusal as before. `kwin-capture on` writes one `kwinrc` key, and only when KWin lists the helper as installed; `off` removes it.

## Verification

- `bin/ci --quick` at the fix commit, after `cargo fmt`: 6 passed, 5 skipped. The skipped steps were clippy, unit tests, UniFFI bindings and the Windows cross-check (all skipped by `--quick`), plus docs image refs (crane is not installed). The docs generators were not routed because pnpm was missing on the host. The scoped repository checks run in CI.
- No CI lane compiles `kwin_target_helper.cpp`, and the helper's fix commits have not been built or run against KWin. They need a run of `kwin-target-helper/tests/run.sh` before release.
- From #7070: the contributor's container kit passed the gate suite 10/10 and the driver suite 6/6 on KWin 6.3.6, 6.6.6 and 6.8.2. The driver suite also passed 6/6 on a real Plasma 6.6.6 session. There was no real Plasma 6.8 session.

title: Add `max_image_dimension` to `zoom`
body:
`get_window_state` and `get_desktop_state` already accept `max_image_dimension` to cap the long edge of a screenshot. In Cua Driver 0.33.4 (`ba0033a`), `zoom` takes a fresh native-resolution window capture and caps its crop at 500 px wide. Its schema has no long-edge limit. [Window capture](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ba0033a661101669c60ce05f1fe5753bf8bad748/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/get_window_state.rs#L128-L139) · [Desktop capture](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ba0033a661101669c60ce05f1fe5753bf8bad748/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/get_desktop_state.rs#L37-L52) · [Zoom schema](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ba0033a661101669c60ce05f1fe5753bf8bad748/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/zoom.rs#L18-L41) · [Crop and resize](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ba0033a661101669c60ce05f1fe5753bf8bad748/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cursor-overlay/src/capture_utils.rs#L62-L84)

On a 2× Retina Mac, I used a 400 × 1025 point window with an 800 × 2050 native capture. `get_window_state` with `max_image_dimension: 1568` returned a 612 × 1568 PNG. On the same connection, `zoom` on that window with `x1=100, y1=0, x2=300, y2=1568` returned a **366 × 2050 JPEG**.

An MCP host with a 2048 px limit can resize that image before it reaches the model. In a loopback test, Codex 0.162.0 sent the JPEG onward at **366 × 2048**. The driver stores its `from_zoom` mapping using its own crop and resize, so coordinates taken from the host-resized image can land at a different point. [How `zoom` stores the mapping](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ba0033a661101669c60ce05f1fe5753bf8bad748/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/zoom.rs#L98-L127) · [Coordinate formula](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/ba0033a661101669c60ce05f1fe5753bf8bad748/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/snapshot_store.rs#L54-L69)

Please add an optional `max_image_dimension` to `zoom`. Apply it to the JPEG’s long edge alongside the existing width cap, preserve the aspect ratio, and calculate the `from_zoom` mapping from the final JPEG dimensions.

Measured with Cua Driver 0.33.4 on macOS (2× display). The offset in this example is small (2050 → 2048 px); taller native frames, such as a portrait 4K display, would exceed the limit by much more.

title: fix(cua-driver): restore Linux X11 spare keycodes a stopped driver left bound
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux X11, a driver that is killed, stopped, or has its call abandoned while typing leaves its borrowed spare keycodes bound. `is_spare_keycode` only takes keycodes that are NoSymbol on every level, so those keycodes are never borrowed again, and once the pool is empty, text with characters missing from the layout fails until someone resets the keymap by hand.
- What changed:
  - Before it binds a spare keycode, each driver adds the keycode and the keysym it binds to a root-window property named for its pid, `_CUA_DRIVER_SPARE_KEYCODES_<pid>`, and removes them after the restore. The property outlives the process.
  - Every keyboard-map load (`keyboard_mapping`, which all the X11 key routes now use) restores the keycodes listed by drivers whose pid no longer runs, then deletes their properties. This happens under a server grab, and only for keycodes that still hold the keysym the dead driver's marker lists (with any other level NoSymbol, since XKB reads 4 of the 7 bound levels back) and that no running driver lists. A keycode rebound since is left alone. When every listed pid is alive, nothing is grabbed.
  - When `RemappedKeycode`'s restore fails because an abandoned call's connection was shut, the restore is retried on a fresh connection. This uses the same helper `release_abandoned` uses for held keys.

This is option 1 from the issue, plus the fresh-connection restore for the abandoned-call path from the thread. Option 2 (a signal handler that restores on SIGTERM) is left out: with option 1, the next driver to load the keymap cleans up after any exit.

## Related work

Fixes #7075

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Linux X11 only. Typing that needed spare keycodes no longer fails after a driver restart. Keycodes that a build without this fix leaked carry no marker, so they are not reclaimed.
- Risk: the reclaim trusts the pid in the property name. A driver in a separate pid namespace that shares the same X server would look dead to this one, but its keycodes are still safe while it is between the bind and the restore, because the reclaim skips keycodes any live driver lists only when it can see that driver as alive. Rollback is a revert. The property is ignored by older builds.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (in `spare_keycode_restore_tests`, which the `Run X11 spare keycode restore regressions` step of `ci-rust-linux.yml` runs with `--ignored`):
  - `the_next_driver_restores_the_spare_keycodes_of_one_that_was_killed` starts a child test process that binds a spare keycode on its own Xvfb, SIGKILLs it, checks that the keycode is still bound and listed in the child's marker, then loads the keymap and asserts the keycode is NoSymbol and the marker is gone.
  - `a_killed_drivers_spare_keycode_that_was_rebound_since_is_left_alone` rebinds the killed child's keycode to F13 before the keymap load and asserts it keeps F13.
  - `an_abandoned_call_still_restores_its_spare_keycode` binds a spare under an `Action`, checks that loading the keymap leaves a live driver's keycode alone, abandons the action, drops the guard, and asserts the keycode is NoSymbol and unmarked.
  - The tests land in a commit before the fix, so CI can check that they fail on the base.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs). Clippy, unit tests and the build were skipped locally because this host was out of disk; CI runs them.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Linux X11 CI lane, for the Xvfb regressions above. macOS, Windows and Wayland are unaffected: the change is in the X11 spare-keycode path only.

title: fix(cua-driver): answer a typed app_not_found refusal when launch_app finds no application on Linux
body:
## Summary

### Problem this solves

On Linux, five `launch_app` failures leave as plain text, with no code. Three of them share one message prefix:

```text
launch_app { name | launch_path }
 ├─ remote-debugging flag refused         → "Chromium remote-debugging flags moved …"   text only
 ├─ matched .desktop launcher fails       → "Failed to launch: …"   text only
 ├─ nothing by that name exists           → "Failed to launch: …"   text only   ◀ this PR
 ├─ xdg-open could not open               → "Failed to launch: …"   text only
 └─ task panic                            → "Task error: …"         text only
```

A caller cannot tell "nothing by that name exists" from "something was found and failed" without parsing the message. In the first case no process started, so it is a refusal.

### What changed

That one case now answers a typed refusal. The text is unchanged; `structuredContent` is new:

```text
launch_app { "name": "cua-no-such-application" }

isError:           true
text:              Failed to launch: 'cua-no-such-application' is not an executable on PATH and
                   matches no installed .desktop application. Call list_apps and round-trip its launch_path.
structuredContent: { "code": "app_not_found", "effect": "refused",
                     "name": "cua-no-such-application", "pid": null, "running": null }
```

- **Shape.** `launch_handoff_timeout_result` in the same file already answers `effect: "refused"` plus a `code`, so this follows it. The `{"status": "refused", "refusal": {...}}` shape of other Linux tools does not appear in `launch_app.rs`.
- **Inputs.** `name` and `launch_path` share one launch path, so both get the refusal. `name` in the structured content is the requested command.
- **Other failures.** The four other rows of the tree above are unchanged.

### When the refusal is given

Pseudocode of the new path, after the existing checks (no `.desktop` match, not a URL, not an existing path):

```text
Pseudocode
unlaunchable_command_error(spawn_error, cmd, $PATH, installed):
    program = first whitespace token of cmd
    if  spawn_error.kind == NotFound              # direct spawn of cmd only
    and not names_installed_app(installed, cmd)
    and not program_may_exist(program, $PATH):
        return AppNotFound(cmd)                    # → launch_failure_result → typed refusal
    else:
        return plain error, same text              # → "Failed to launch: …" as today
```

| Predicate | Answers "may exist" (plain text kept) | Answers "absent" |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `program_may_exist`, `program` has a `/` | the path exists, or `try_exists` fails with another error | `try_exists` is `Ok(false)`, `NotFound` or `NotADirectory` |
| `program_may_exist`, bare name | a `$PATH` directory holds it, a probe fails with another error, or `$PATH` is unset | no `$PATH` directory holds it (an entry that is a file holds nothing) |
| `names_installed_app` | an entry's display name contains `cmd`, its desktop-file id or Exec basename equals `cmd` (these three ignore ASCII case), or its `launch_path` starts with the same program | no entry matches |

`names_installed_app` uses the criteria of `match_installed_app` without its uniqueness rule, so an ambiguous name keeps the plain text.

Results by case. Each row is a case of the new integration test:

| Request | Direct spawn error | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| absent `name` | `NotFound` | **`app_not_found`** |
| absent `launch_path` | `NotFound` | **`app_not_found`** |
| absent program with arguments: `cua-definitely-absent --flag` | `NotFound` | **`app_not_found`** |
| program on `$PATH` whose script interpreter is missing (as `name`, and as a multi-token `launch_path`) | `NotFound` | plain: the probe finds the program |
| program on `$PATH` without execute permission | `PermissionDenied` | plain |
| absent program, NUL byte in `additional_arguments` | `InvalidInput` | plain |
| URL, no `xdg-open` on `$PATH` | `NotFound` from `xdg-open`, not from the direct spawn | plain |
| name that two installed entries match | — | plain: may name an installed app |
| installed entry whose launcher program is missing: by name, by its `list_apps` `launch_path`, and by that launcher with other arguments | `NotFound` | plain: may name an installed app |

### Size of the change

```text
libs/cua-driver/rust/
├── Cargo.lock                                     +1    cua-driver-testkit
└── crates/platform-linux/
    ├── Cargo.toml                                 +1    cua-driver-testkit (dev-dependency)
    ├── src/tools/launch_app.rs                    +167 −7
    │     invoke                       binds spawn_error; replaces the bail!; maps the Ok(Err(e)) arm
    │     AppNotFound                  error type; Display is the old text
    │     program_may_exist            the path / $PATH probe
    │     names_installed_app          the installed-application check
    │     unlaunchable_command_error   the classification above
    │     launch_failure_result        AppNotFound → typed refusal, else plain text
    │     app_not_found_result         the refusal
    │     unit test                    a_program_may_exist_by_path_or_in_a_search_path_directory
    └── tests/launch_app_missing_application.rs    +363  new test binary, 2 tests
```

## Known limits

`app_not_found` means "the driver's own resolution found nothing", not a proof of absence. What remains:

- The installed-application check compares launcher paths as strings, so `/opt/acme/./editor` is not recognized as `/opt/acme/editor`.
- The first token stands for the program, so a runner command such as `flatpak run org.acme.Editor` is judged by `flatpak`.
- Desktop-entry discovery reads only the direct children of `applications/`, and skips a `.desktop` file or directory it cannot read without saying so (existing behavior in `installed_apps.rs`, unchanged here); a match there can be missed.
- Names are tokenized on whitespace, so a name such as `My Editor` is judged by `My`.
- With no `PATH` set, a bare program is never classified (the default search path then differs between C libraries).
- The probe runs after the spawn, so a file that appears or disappears in between can misclassify one launch.

## Related work

- Refs #2856 (closed): an unknown name made the Windows launch hang. This is the Linux counterpart: an unknown name now answers a not-found error with a code. It does not cover a launch that hangs.
- Open PR #6119 also changes the Linux launch path, but only `process_exited` and below, and their tests. This PR touches `invoke`, the new functions next to it, and the end of the test module: no shared lines.

### RFC: not opened

`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for an RFC when a change affects a public MCP contract. This PR adds a code to the structured content of an existing error result: no new tool, parameter or input schema, and no change to a successful result. Precedents:

| PR | Change | RFC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #3882 | added `launch_handoff_timeout` | "RFC: not opened yet"; merged with none linked ([a reviewer asked](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3882#issuecomment-5804440309)) |
| #4856 | added the `browser_field_needs_keystrokes` refusal | no RFC line |
| #8377 | added an existing optional field to more results | "RFC: not needed" |

Questions for the maintainers:

1. Should `app_not_found` mean "the driver's resolution found nothing" (this PR, with the limits above), or a stronger guarantee of absence that would need a different resolution?
2. Do you want an RFC for this new caller-visible code? I will write one if so.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux only. `launch_app` for an unknown name now also carries `structuredContent` with a `code`; `isError` and the text are as before.
- Risk and rollback: low; a single revert restores the plain-text error.

## Validation

### Focused tests and checks

```text
tests/launch_app_missing_application.rs  on the unpatched launch_app.rs  → FAIL  (no structuredContent)
                                         after the change                → PASS
```

The integration test drives `launch_app` through the tool registry. It asserts the whole structured object for the three `app_not_found` rows of the table above. For the other rows, it asserts the exact previous text and no structured content.

What the fixture isolates from the host:

| Host input | In the test |
| --- | --- |
| desktop entries | `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_DIRS` → a private `data/` |
| programs | `PATH` → a private `bin/` |
| home and state directories | the testkit's `IsolatedStateRoot` |
| working directory | a private `work/`; `PATH`, the XDG directories and each launcher command are relative to it, so the test also passes with a space and a colon in `TMPDIR` |
| display | `DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset |
| authorization | permission mode, capability manifest and policy file variables unset |

The fixture restores the environment and the working directory on drop. Before each case, the test spawns the program directly and asserts the spawn error kind that the case relies on. If the filesystem cannot produce it (for example a `noexec` mount), the test fails with a message that names the filesystem. The missing-interpreter case is its own test, so such a mount fails only that test.

The unit test of `program_may_exist` covers, with temporary directories: a present and an absent program, by name and by path; a `$PATH` entry that is a file; a directory without search permission (asserted only where the platform makes `try_exists` fail there); and no search path.

Commands:

| Environment | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rust:1.97.1` + the packages of `linux-rust-prep` | `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --lib` | 1120 passed, 16 ignored |
| same | `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --tests` | passed |
| same | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | passed |
| same | `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings` | passed |
| full checkout + Node + pnpm | `bin/ci` (affected mode, not `--quick`) | 10/10 selected checks passed on the previous revision¹ |
| — | `bin/ci --signoff` | not run |

¹ SPDX headers, rustfmt, image refs, cargo lockfiles, Windows cfg grep, clippy with the reverse dependencies it selects, `platform-linux` unit tests, the generated docs reference, the UniFFI bindings check. The last revision changes only the fixture of the integration test; on it, only the four `cargo` commands above ran.

### Manual or platform evidence

None beyond the tests.

### Known gaps or CI still required

No `local-ci` sign-off. The GitHub CI jobs (the X11/Wayland desktop lanes, the Windows and macOS builds) have not run.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [ ] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above. (Left to the maintainers; see the RFC note above.)
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.

title: fix(cua-driver): capture fullscreen flip-model Direct3D windows via DXGI Desktop Duplication
body:
Salvaged from #7092
Fixes #7091

## Why

On Windows, `get_window_state` and `get_desktop_state` capture through PrintWindow and GDI BitBlt. For a fullscreen, flip-model Direct3D window (how Unity and Unreal games present), DWM keeps only the last frame it composed, so both return a stale frame while the screen keeps changing. @yingyu4451's change adds a DXGI Desktop Duplication path for windows that fully cover a monitor. This PR keeps their commit as they wrote it, merges main, and adds two fixes on top.

## What changed

- yingyu4451's commit: a `dxgi_duplication` module, plus a first capture step for unoccluded windows that cover a monitor and for the primary display. Every failure falls back to the existing PrintWindow / WGC / BitBlt ladder.
- Window path fix: the duplicated monitor image is now cropped to the same DWM-inset frame PrintWindow returns. Before this, the image's origin was the monitor's corner while `bitmap_to_screen` maps from the inset frame, so a pixel click on a fullscreen window's screenshot landed one pixel off. The agent cursor overlay is now kept out of the duplicated frame, as desktop captures already do. Monitor coverage is checked before the overlay is hidden, so windows that don't cover a monitor skip that step.
- Visibility and frame release: the duplication path no longer relies on the five-point occlusion probe, which misses a small window between its samples (a notification over a game, say). It now walks the z-order above the target before and after the capture, and falls back when any visible window from another process overlaps the captured frame. Before and after the capture, the target itself must be visible, not minimized, uncloaked, opaque (not layered, no custom region, has a redirection bitmap, and no corners Windows 11 may round) and at the same bounds, with its frame on the one monitor it covers. The capture falls back when the agent cursor overlay could not be excluded or when the frame has protected content masked out. Every acquired duplication frame is now released, including on early error returns.
- Display path fix: the primary display uses duplication only when the foreground window covers it. A new duplication session waits for the next present, and an idle desktop may not send one, so every desktop screenshot would otherwise wait out the one-second acquire budget before falling back.

## Scope

Windows `platform-windows` capture only. Rotated outputs, layered, regioned, DirectComposition-surface or round-cornered windows, windows that any other window overlaps, windows that don't cover a whole monitor, protected content and remote sessions keep the existing ladder. The duplication session is still created fresh for each capture; it is not kept between calls.

A pointer drawn in software into the desktop image stays in the duplicated frame; the hardware pointer does not.

## Tradeoffs

Keeping one duplication session open per output would remove the wait for a first present and the per-call device setup. It would also keep DWM copying frames for as long as the daemon runs. This PR keeps the per-call session and limits where it runs.

## Blast Radius

Only Windows screenshots of windows that cover a monitor and that no other window overlaps, and desktop screenshots while such a window is in the foreground. A fullscreen window that isn't presenting (for example a paused borderless app) still waits up to the one-second budget, then falls back to the old path.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): rustfmt and SPDX headers pass. Clippy, the platform-windows unit tests (including the new `crop_bgra` and `overlaps` tests) and the Windows cross-compile were skipped on this Linux host and run in CI.
- Runtime evidence for the fullscreen game case is in #7092 (Windows 10 22H2, Unity at 2560x1440). The crop and the display gate have not been exercised on a real Windows desktop.

title: fix(cua-driver): do not retype a batched macOS send into a native field that showed no change
body:
## Problem

#8128 finishes a batched macOS `type_text` send that a native field took only in part. `retype_from` resumes at the delivered count, and `appends_prefix` first checks that the field shows its old value followed by that many characters of the text.

`retype_from` also returns `Some(0)` when the field showed no change at all within `UNCHANGED_GIVE_UP` (500 ms). With `done == 0`, `appends_prefix` only checks that the field still shows its old value. That is what a field shows when the keys have not landed yet or are not echoed. The whole text is then posted a second time:

- a native field whose AXValue lags the keys by more than 500 ms gets the text twice, once from the batch and once from the retype;
- a view that does not echo what it reads, and is not on the terminal list (for example a `read -s` password prompt in a terminal app the driver does not recognize as a terminal), gets the secret twice.

A count of zero is no evidence that the field took a prefix and stopped. The case the retype is for, an app that reads only the first character of a multi-character event, shows a count of 1 or more.

## Fix

`retype_from` requires `done > 0`. A field that showed no change reports `(false, Some(0))`, as it did before #8128, and the caller decides whether to send again. #7276, which #8128 salvaged, carried this guard.

## Test

`a_native_field_retypes_only_a_proven_partial_tail`: `retype_from((false, Some(0)), 5, false, || false)` is now `None`.

## Checks

- [x] On a macos-15 runner (run 44853642558):
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`;
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`;
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib tools::type_text::` (37 passed);
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib`: 874 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`, which this change does not touch.
- [ ] `bin/ci --quick` and `bin/ci --signoff`: not run; this account cannot write commit statuses on trycua/cua.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse macOS type_text keys when the target can't hold keyboard focus
body:
Salvaged from #7110 by @AlexFalher. Their two commits are cherry-picked onto current main with their authorship kept.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, when `type_text` is aimed at an `element_token` that cannot take keyboard focus (in #7110's repro, Chrome's "Bookmark this tab" button) and has to fall back to key events, the keys go to whichever element does hold focus. The target's read-back stays unchanged, so the call reports `delivered 0`. Since #6884 a batched send then retypes the "missing" text, so the URL was typed twice into the address bar.
- What changed: before posting any key, `cgevent_type_verified` focuses the explicit target and confirms it holds keyboard focus with `with_confirmed_key_focus`, the same helper `press_key` uses. The focus write is re-applied for up to 200 ms, and either focus read-back counts. If focus can't be confirmed, no key is sent and the call is refused with `target_focus_unconfirmed`, effect `"refused"`, `dispatched: false`, through the mapping `type_text` already has on main. A follow-up commit checks focus again after the foreground first-key settle, so a first responder that AppKit installs during that sleep is caught before any key is sent. Another checks it again before the batched retype sends the remaining text; if focus is gone by then, the partial delivery is reported. A call with no explicit target is unchanged. The tool description and the generated reference mention the refusal.

## Related work

Salvaged from #7110. #7110 names no issue. It follows #6884.

RFC: not required. There is no protocol change: this reuses the existing `target_focus_unconfirmed` refusal.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact (macOS only): typing at a control that can't hold keyboard focus is now refused with nothing typed. Before, the text went into the focused field and the call answered `delivered 0`. Targets that hold focus behave as before. Windows and Linux are untouched.
- Risk: a background app that accepts the keys but reports neither `AXFocusedUIElement` nor the element's own `AXFocused = true` is now refused. `press_key` already has this dependency. Background terminal and native-field targets addressed by `element_token` are the cases to watch. Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed rustfmt, the SPDX headers, docs code blocks and image refs. Clippy, unit tests, UniFFI bindings and the Windows cross-check are skipped in quick mode and run in CI. The docs generator drift check could not run on this host.
- No hermetic unit test owns the new call site, because `cgevent_type_verified` posts real keys. The focus-confirmation contract itself is owned by the `with_confirmed_key_focus` tests in `press_key`.
- Live macOS evidence is from #7110's author, on its first version only: see the table in #7110. The refusal rows still need a macOS run at this head.
