title: feat(cua-driver): add browser_new_tab to open a background tab in a bound window
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: no browser tool opens a tab. `browser_navigate` needs a `tab_id` and replaces the page the user may be reading, so hosts relaunch the browser executable with a URL, and Chromium's launcher brings the browser to the front.
- What changed: a new MCP tool, `browser_new_tab {target_id, tab_id, url, session}`. It runs `Target.createTarget {url: "about:blank", background: true}` over the binding's existing DevTools connection, checks with `Browser.getWindowForTarget` that the tab is in the bound window, navigates it with `Page.navigate`, and returns the new `tab_id` on the same `target_id`. It never activates the tab or the window. `Target.createTarget` is added to the existing-profile CDP method allowlist.

This follows the `browser_new_tab` half of @abonneth's RFC #7257 (their probe: `Target.createTarget` opened the tab 5/5 with no foreground change, against 4/5 foreground changes for the relaunch workaround).

## Related work

Fixes #7111
Refs #7257

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): #7257, still in review. This PR answers two of its open questions; see below.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: additive. One new tool on macOS, Linux and Windows; capability token `browser.tab.new`; risk class R2 under the `browser_bound_input` adapter with the `browser_navigate` resource shape (`action_class: "navigation"`, `requested_origin` from `url`); a bounded capability manifest checks `url` the same way it checks `browser_navigate`. No existing tool changes behavior.
- Choices on the RFC's open questions:
  - When the browser puts the tab in a window other than the bound one, the call refuses with `browser_wrong_target_refused` (`detail.reason: "new_tab_window_mismatch"`), records no tab and does not navigate. The stray `about:blank` tab stays open: closing it would also need `Target.closeTarget` in the allowlist, which the RFC does not propose.
  - A binding with no CDP window id (a single-page embedded app) is refused, because there is no window to check the new tab against.
- Risk and rollback: the tool goes through the same exact-binding revalidation as `browser_navigate`. Revert the PR to remove it.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (mock CDP, in `cua-driver-core`):
  - `new_tab_opens_in_the_bound_window_without_activating_it`: `Target.createTarget` is a browser-level call with exactly `{url: about:blank, background: true}`. `Page.navigate` runs on the new tab's session. There is no `Page.bringToFront` or `Target.activateTarget` call. The returned `tab_id` then works with `browser_navigate`.
  - `new_tab_in_another_window_refuses_before_navigation`: checks the refusal code and reason, no navigation, no recorded tab.
  - The existing-profile CDP surface test now also opens a tab, so the allowlist entry is covered.
  - Added `browser_new_tab` to the bad-URL, unknown-target, registration, annotation, schema and capability-manifest tests.
- Manual or platform evidence: new real-browser row `standalone_browser_new_tab` in `cua-driver-e2e`. It runs under the background sentinel (focus, z-order, no leaked input, and cursor where supported) and is added to the Unix and Windows standalone-browser runners.
- CI at this head: the Rust `fmt, clippy, test` jobs pass on Linux, macOS and Windows, as do `Rust Linux unit and compile` and the Linux and Windows E2E gates. The new and changed tests are named in the passing logs.
- `ci-gate` is red on `E2E: Rust macOS hosted`, which failed twice, rerun included. It is the Electron background-typing row (`fixture journal did not reach "mirror=cua-px-background"`). The same two assertions fail on `fix/kwin-input-gate`, `t3/fix-x11-spare-keycode-leak` and `fix/cua-driver-brave-existing-profile`, so the failure comes from the base or the runner, not from this diff.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Rust build, clippy and tests were not run locally (shared host, low disk); they run in CI. The reference pages and `cli-specs` snapshots were written by hand to match the generator's output, because regenerating them needs a built driver. The release docs workflow regenerates both.

title: feat(vmm): choose which NVIDIA GPUs a container gets
body:
## What changes

The `nvidia` GPU option of a container Space can name the cards it wants: `nvidia:<id>[,<id>...]`, where each id is an index or a UUID as `nvidia-smi -L` lists them. Plain `nvidia` keeps its current meaning (every NVIDIA GPU).

- `gpu::nvidia_devices` parses the option into the named ids.
- `types.rs` `reject_gpu` accepts `nvidia:<ids>` for containers.
- `container/mod.rs` `gpu_requests` sends the named ids as the Docker `DeviceRequest.device_ids` instead of `count: -1`.

## Why

`CreateHostSpaceRequest.gpu` carries one option id, and the container runtime always built one device request with `count: -1` (`--gpus all`). Setting `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` in the container environment did not narrow it: on a host with three V100s the container still listed all three. A host with several GPUs could therefore not give one card to each Space.

## Tests

`cargo test -p cua-vmm --lib -- nvidia named_nvidia gpu`: 11 passed, 0 failed, including the new `gpu::tests::nvidia_option_names_the_gpus_it_wants` and `container::tests::named_nvidia_gpus_become_device_ids`.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse a zoom made against a screenshot frame a refresh replaced
body:
## Why

`ScreenshotContext { snapshot_id, window_id, scale }` came through a screenshot-only refresh unchanged whenever the scale stayed the same. A `zoom` that took its context before the refresh and finished after it passed the `set_zoom` equality check and bound its crop to the new image (ABA). Every new screenshot now gets a frame id, so the context names the image itself.

## What changed

- `ScreenshotContext` gains `frame_id: u64`. Each publish that carries a scale and each `refresh_screenshot_for_session` mints a new one.
- The snapshot's loose `screenshot_scale`, `screenshot_window_size` and `zoom` fields become one `ScreenshotFrame { frame_id, scale, window_size, zoom }`. A tree-only read that keeps the previous image keeps its frame id.
- `set_zoom` still compares the whole context, so the stale zoom gets exactly `zoom_context_missing` and the zoom tools on all three platforms need no change.

## Scope

This covers only `cua-driver-core/src/snapshot_store.rs`. It adds no observation store, overflow store or mutation generation. Screenshot-owner theft was fixed in #7809 and is not touched. #8301 is still open. Its diff edits lines next to the refresh and publish code changed here, so whichever lands second needs a textual merge. Its tree-only-read behavior is unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Only the zoom tool reads the frame id, and only through `screenshot_context_for_zoom` → `set_zoom`. Pixel scale lookups read the same scale as before.

## Verification

- New hermetic test `a_zoom_against_a_refreshed_frame_is_refused_even_at_the_same_scale`. It is the first commit, so it can run at the base, where it should fail, and at the head, where it should pass.
- `tree_only_read_keeps_the_screenshot_frame_while_the_window_keeps_its_size` now also checks that the frame id is kept.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, headers). `cargo test` and clippy did not run on the shared host. They run in CI and in verification.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep fast-path guard state per runtime and session
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: the fast-path `GuardStore` was a process-global singleton (`fast_path::store::global()`). It held window images and fingerprints across every runtime and session, and no `session_end` ever cleared it.
- What changed:
  - `ToolRegistry` now owns one `GuardStore` per runtime, the same way it owns its `CaptureService`. On macOS it reaches `ToolState` through `registry.guard_store()`, next to the snapshot store. `global()` is deleted.
  - Window images, window fingerprints and snapshot fingerprints are keyed by `(session, pid, window_id)`. Every read and act-time lookup passes the call's `_session_id`, which is the same key the snapshot store uses.
  - The registry's existing scoped `session_end` hook calls `GuardStore::retire_session`. That hook is registered on all three OSes.
  - `get_window_state` builds the guard image in its capture worker but stores it only after the join, so a cancelled read cannot write the image back after `session_end` has run.

## Scope

Covers ownership, session keying and cleanup of the guard state. The act-time guard is still macOS-only, and its default (`off`) is unchanged. Windows and Linux still record nothing, so their only change is the shared cleanup. Nothing is migrated: since #7809 a session cannot act on a snapshot that another session read.

## Tradeoffs

The brief put construction next to each platform's `SnapshotStore` and cleanup in each platform's own hook. I put both in the core registry instead, the same way `CaptureService` is handled. That gives one owner and one cleanup site that all three OSes share. It also lets the `on`-mode delta lookup in core dispatch (`wire::delta_target`) read the runtime's store without a global. Windows and Linux never write to the store, so a field in their `ToolState` would go unused.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: none while `fast_path` is `off`, the default. With `shadow`/`guard`/`on`, a session's guard checks and re-read screenshot skipping now use only that session's own reads. Before this change they could use another session's or another runtime's read.
- Risk and rollback: low to medium. Revert the single commit.

## Verification

- `bin/ci --quick`: SPDX headers, rustfmt and image refs pass. Clippy, unit tests, bindings and the Windows cross-check were skipped on this shared host and run in CI.
- New hermetic tests:
  - `fast_path::store::tests::each_session_sees_only_its_own_reads`
  - `fast_path::store::tests::retiring_a_session_drops_only_its_reads`
  - `tool::runtime_isolation_tests::guard_state_belongs_to_its_runtime_and_ends_with_its_session`. It checks that two registries don't share images and that the real `session_end` hook clears only the ended session.
- An earlier verification round found the cancelled-read race above, and the third commit fixes it.
- Still required: the scoped repository checks in CI, a mutation check of the hook line, and a macOS click E2E with `fast_path:"guard"` on the final candidate SHA.

title: feat(cua-driver): add browser_press_key for keys and chords to a bound tab
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, `press_key` and `hotkey` to a Chromium window that is not in front return `background_unavailable`, because Chromium reads modifier state from the live keyboard. The only way to send `ctrl+a`, `ctrl+z` or `f5` to a page was `delivery_mode: "foreground"`, which raises the browser over the user's app.
- What changed: a new `browser_press_key {target_id, tab_id, session, key, modifiers?, ref?}` tool. It sends one key or chord over the bound tab's DevTools session with `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` and never changes the OS foreground.

## Related work

Fixes #7113

RFC: implements step 1 (`browser_press_key`) of the RFC in #7257 by @abonneth. That RFC is still `status: review`, so a maintainer should accept it before this merges. `browser_new_tab` (#7111) is left to its own PR.

## What changed

- `browser_press_key` (new `cua-driver-core/src/browser/press_key.rs`): each modifier goes down, then the key goes down and up, then the modifiers go up. Every event carries the CDP modifier bitmask. A printable key with no ctrl, alt or meta carries its text, so `a` or `shift+1` still types. An optional `ref` focuses its element first, on its own frame's session (tab or OOPIF). The agent-cursor visual is not shown for a key press, because its geometry lookup could stall behind a dialog that a focus handler opens. Focus emulation is held during the press so a background or inactive tab handles it. On macOS, Cmd+A/C/X/V/Z and Shift+Cmd+Z name their editor command, because a CDP key event skips the Cocoa mapping that would otherwise run it.
- Failure reporting: the tool refuses up front while a page dialog is open. Entering focus emulation and focusing the ref both watch for a dialog that a focus handler opens, and refuse with the dialog block before any key is sent. Each key event goes through the same dialog-aware wait `browser_click` uses. Key-downs stop at the first failure or dialog. The tool then releases every modifier that may have gone down, including one whose down wasn't acknowledged, and also releases the key once its down was sent. A dialog opened by the key's handler gives ok with the dialog block and `effect: "unverifiable"`. A dialog opened by a modifier's handler, or a failed modifier-down, refuses with `browser_input_incomplete` and `pressed: false`, and the key is never sent. An unacknowledged key-down refuses with `delivery: "unknown"`, and its recovery hint says to read the page rather than press again. `released` and `focus_emulation_restored` are true only when acknowledged. A failed focus-emulation enable attempts a bounded restore. Every press invalidates the tab's refs, since anything that reached the page may have reloaded or edited it.
- Wiring: the tool shares `press_key`'s key vocabulary and argument normalization (`"ctrl+a"` in `key`, `Page_Down`). It joins `browser_bound_input` authorization at R2, gets a `key_input` protected-resource action class and a `browser.input.key` capability, and counts as a computer action and a browser call in telemetry. It is annotated `destructive`. It also gets a recovery hint for an unpressed key, and it is added to the three MCP registry snapshots, the reference pages, the MCP compat roster (62 tools) and `BROWSER.md`.

## Scope

Covers keys and chords to an exactly-bound tab on every platform that has the browser tools. Out of scope: native `press_key`/`hotkey` on unbound windows (unchanged), `browser_new_tab` (#7111), and pointing the Windows `hotkey` `background_unavailable` refusal at the new tool.

## Tradeoffs

- One tool with a `modifiers` array, as the RFC proposes, rather than chords in `browser_type` keystrokes mode. `browser_type` requires an editable ref and counts characters. A chord needs neither.
- Browser shortcuts (`ctrl+t`, `ctrl+w`, `f5`) are not refused. The RFC probe showed CDP key events reach them on Edge, and `destructive: true` plus the protected-resource scope is how the caller is warned. The RFC's open questions (refusing print/save chords, `key_input` versus `page_input`) are left to its review. This PR takes the RFC's current answers.

- Dialogs that a handler defers until after its reply (for example with `setTimeout`) race the driver's check before the next key-down. Chromium gives the driver no ordering signal here. If the driver sees the dialog first, the key is not sent and the press is refused. Otherwise the key is sent, it is reported pressed with the dialog and an unverifiable effect, and Chromium applies it once the dialog closes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: one additive MCP tool and one capability token. No existing tool's behavior changes. The existing-profile CDP allowlist already permits every method it uses (`Input.dispatchKeyEvent`, `DOM.focus`, `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled`).
- Risk and rollback: the tool reaches whatever shortcut the page's focus allows, which is why it is marked destructive. Rollback is reverting this PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: mock-CDP tests in `v2_tests.rs` cover the chord's event order, bitmask and session, with no `Page.bringToFront` or `Target.activateTarget` and refs going stale afterward. They also cover ref focus routed to the OOPIF session, modifier release when the key-down fails, an unacknowledged key-down, a lost release with the remaining releases still sent, a key or modifier handler that opens a dialog, a failed focus-emulation enable, and refusal of unknown keys and modifiers before any input. Unit tests in `press_key.rs` cover the key table and the macOS command mapping. The heuristic-binding, unknown-target, authorization, registration, schema and recovery-hint tests now include the tool.
- Run on this machine: `bin/ci --quick` (SPDX, rustfmt, docs code blocks, image refs) is green, and `test_cua_driver_release_wiring.py` passes. The reference pages were rendered from the committed snapshots with the repository renderer, and only the new tool's rows changed. Cargo build, clippy and tests were not run here (shared host, disk-guarded). They run in the scoped repository checks in CI.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the macOS and Windows registry snapshots were edited by hand to match the Linux entry, so the native docs lanes are what confirm them. No live-browser E2E has run yet. The RFC's acceptance plan (Edge on Windows with a host window in front: `ctrl+a` selects, `f5` reloads, foreground unchanged) is not yet covered, and neither is macOS Cmd+A.

title: feat(cua-driver): serve --owner-pid shuts the daemon down once its owner exits
body:
Salvaged from #7150 by @abonneth.

Fixes #7112

## Why
When a host starts `cua-driver serve` and then crashes or is killed, the daemon keeps running and holds on to its socket or named pipe, its pid file and its browser connections. The stdin-EOF lifetime pipe only covers embedded daemons. `serve --owner-pid PID` ties a standalone daemon to its host process.

## What changed
- abonneth's commit (kept as authored): `serve --owner-pid PID` opens the owner once at startup as an OS handle: a process handle on Windows, kqueue `NOTE_EXIT` on macOS, and a pidfd on Linux, falling back to `kill(pid, 0)` polling on kernels without `pidfd_open`. When the owner exits, the daemon leaves its serve loop through the same path the lifetime pipe uses. If the PID is not running, startup fails. `--owner-pid` on any command other than `serve` exits 64.
- Ours on top: main merged in, and the flag added to the committed CLI spec (`scripts/docs-generators/cli-specs/cua-driver.json`) and the generated `serve` reference page, so the reference drift check matches `cli_docs_literal`. `--owner-pid` is also added to the uninstall script's copy of `VALUE_FLAGS` (`_install-common.sh`), so uninstall can still find a daemon that was started with the flag.
- Ours: an owner that exited but has not been reaped now counts as gone. Before, `pidfd_open`, a still-open Windows process handle and `kill(pid, 0)` all accepted it, so `serve` started and then shut down at once instead of refusing the PID. On kernels without pidfd, the fallback kept the daemon up until the owner was reaped. Now each platform checks at startup whether the owner has already exited, and the fallback reads the owner's `/proc/<pid>/stat` as bytes. A zombie leader counts as exited only when no other thread is left, since a leader that called `pthread_exit` is a zombie while its other threads keep running. On every platform, a PID with no running process is refused as `ErrorKind::NotFound`.
- Ours: the contract now has one owner test, `tests/serve_owner_pid_test.rs`. It drives `cua-driver serve` and checks three things: the daemon shuts down and removes its pid file once its owner exits; it refuses a gone owner with exit 1; and it refuses an exited but unreaped owner. The macOS and Windows workflows now run it by name, because neither runs the `cua-driver` binary's unit tests. The `owner.rs` unit tests it duplicates are removed, and only the Linux polling-fallback tests remain inline.

## Scope
Covers `cua-driver serve` on Windows, macOS and Linux. It leaves out an `--exit-on-stdin-eof` flag for standalone daemons (the issue's other option), and it does not change the cua SDK or CLI wrappers to pass the flag.

## Blast Radius
New optional flag. The watcher thread starts only when the flag is passed. Without it, `owner::exited()` never resolves and serve behaves as it does today. On Linux kernels without pidfd, PID reuse is possible during the 250 ms poll window.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, docs code blocks, image refs, docs image doctor reports, bin/ci sync, actionlint) pass. Clippy, unit tests and the Windows cross-check run in CI.
- `serve_owner_pid_test` runs in the Linux, macOS and Windows unit lanes. Locally it was only type-checked and linted for all three targets, since the disk could not hold a full build. The inline Linux fallback tests (an unreaped zombie, and stat parsing with a live thread group and a non-UTF-8 command name) pass in a standalone build of `owner.rs`, and each fails when its check is removed.
- `test_uninstall_stops_daemons_from_other_copies.py` passes locally. It failed in CI before the `VALUE_FLAGS` fix.
- In #7150, abonneth ran a detached `serve` and killed its host, 5 runs per platform. With the flag, the daemon exited and removed its pid file on Windows, Linux and macOS. Without it, the daemon stayed up.

## Checklist
- [x] `bin/ci --quick` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --quick --signoff`)

title: fix(cua-driver): drain Windows daemon connections and release proxy sessions on shutdown
body:
Stacked on #8289 and #8339: both branches are merged into this one. Once they land, main gets merged in here.

## Why

On shutdown, the Windows named-pipe serve path detached its connection tasks. Accepted connections kept running against an SDK runtime that was being torn down, and their proxy sessions stayed registered. It also wrote the PID file before the first pipe instance existed, so a daemon that failed to bind could leave a PID behind. The Unix path already drains, releases, and writes the PID after bind. This change brings Windows in line with it.

## What changed

- Windows accepted connections now go into a `JoinSet`. Finished tasks are reaped on each accept. On shutdown the set is aborted and joined, then `release_active_proxy_sessions` runs, in the same order the Unix path uses.
- The Windows PID file is written right after the first pipe instance is created, next to the "listening" banner.
- New Windows-only tests in `pipe_shutdown_tests`. One holds a proxy control connection open, sends `shutdown` on a second connection, and checks three things: the open connection closes, its proxy session is released, and the PID file is removed. The other checks that a pipe that fails to create writes no PID file. `connection_reaping_tests` now runs on Windows too.
- Windows shard 3 of `ci-rust-windows.yml` runs every `serve::` test module. Until now the shards compiled these tests and ran none of them. The step fails if the drain test does not run. `browser_download_approval_requires_a_live_proxy_session` now takes `test_runtime_lock`, because the shutdown tests clear the shared proxy-session set.

## Scope

The Windows serve path in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/serve.rs`, plus one Windows CI step that runs its tests. The Unix code is unchanged; its two helpers just widen their `cfg` to include Windows. No shared listener is extracted, and the two dispatch bodies stay separate.

## Blast Radius

Windows `cua-driver serve` and `stop`. A shutdown now aborts in-flight requests on other connections, as Unix already does. Any client still attached at shutdown gets EOF or a broken pipe; before, it stayed attached to a dying process.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`, including rustfmt) pass on macOS.
- This macOS host has no Windows build or test lane, so the new Windows tests run in the Windows shard 3 step this PR adds, and serve/stop is covered by CI's Windows lanes.

title: fix(cua-driver): bound Windows daemon replies by REPLY_DEADLINE
body:
Stacked on #8289 (merged into this branch). #8339 has already landed on main.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows the daemon client (`cua_driver_core::daemon::send_request`, used by the CLI, MCP proxy and SDK) and the SDK's trusted service session opened the pipe through `std::fs` and then called `read_line`/`write_all` with no limit. A daemon that accepted the connection and never answered hung the caller forever. Unix clients give up after `REPLY_DEADLINE`, polling in 10 s slices.
- What changed:
  - New `cua_driver_core::pipe_stream::PipeStream` (Windows only): opens the pipe with `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, runs each `ReadFile`/`WriteFile` against an event, waits with `WaitForSingleObject` for at most the read or write timeout, and on expiry calls `CancelIoEx` and then `GetOverlappedResult(wait = TRUE)` so nothing stays in flight. An expired operation fails with `TimedOut`, the same way a socket read past `SO_RCVTIMEO` does. It keeps the existing 3 s open retry.
  - The Unix `exchange` loop in `daemon.rs` and the service session's `write_request`/`read_response_line` now also build on Windows over `PipeStream`, so Windows waits until the same `REPLY_DEADLINE` (150 s) in the same 10 s slices and returns the same timeout errors. The Windows-only copies are gone.
  - `probe_presence` on Windows goes through the bounded `exchange` as well, so it no longer leaves a thread blocked on a stalled daemon. `exchange` now spends one deadline on connect, write and read, which keeps the probe within its 2 s.
  - The service-session reader checks its deadline after every buffer instead of inside `read_until`, so a peer that trickles bytes without a newline still times out.

## Related work

Refs #8289

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a Windows client of a stalled daemon now fails after `REPLY_DEADLINE` with `timed out after 150s waiting for daemon response ...` (or `... waiting for trusted service response`) instead of hanging. The wire protocol and the Unix values (150 s, 10 s read slices, 5 s write slices) are unchanged. Unix shares the deadline loops, so two stall cases get tighter there as well: a daemon that stalls the request write now counts against the same 150 s as the reply, and a service peer that trickles bytes without a newline now stops at the deadline.
- Risk and rollback: medium. The new code is raw Win32 overlapped I/O. Cancellation always waits for the operation to settle before the buffer and `OVERLAPPED` go out of scope. Revert this one commit to roll back.

## Tradeoffs

- A worker thread with `CancelSynchronousIo` would also work, but it needs one extra thread per call. A tokio client through `block_on` was ruled out because callers may already be running inside a runtime.
- `PipeStream` declares its own `kernel32` externs, as `is_daemon_listening` already does, rather than adding features to the `windows` crate. It does not touch the planned shared IPC module.
- `PipeStream` also takes an absolute deadline that caps every read and write, which the daemon exchange and the service session set on their pipe handles. On Windows no operation runs past the deadline. The Unix socket paths keep their existing slices, so a Unix service-session read can still overrun by up to one 10 s slice, as it does today.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks (Windows, run by CI):
  - `pipe_stream::tests`: a stalled read fails with `TimedOut` and a later read on the same handle still gets the reply, which shows the cancelled read left nothing pending. A deadline cuts a longer read timeout short, and once it has passed a read fails at once. A closed server reads as EOF.
  - `daemon::tests::a_stalled_pipe_daemon_times_out_at_the_reply_deadline`: a local pipe server sends 6 bytes and stalls. The test asserts the exact `exchange` error.
  - `service_session::windows_tests::a_stalled_service_reply_times_out_at_the_reply_deadline`: the exact trusted-service timeout error.
  - `service_session` trickle tests (Unix and Windows): a peer that sends one byte every 10 ms and no newline gets the exact timeout error.
- Ran locally: `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passed. This is a shared macOS host, so the Windows cross-check, clippy and unit tests were skipped here and run in CI.
- Known gaps or CI still required: Windows CI lanes, plus the Windows E2E serve, call and service-session rows.

title: fix(cua-driver): include capture_id and region details in MCP text
body:
Salvaged from #7195

Fixes #6731

## Why

MCP hosts that forward only `content[].text` never saw `capture_id` from `get_window_state` or `get_desktop_state`, and `parse_visual_regions` returned only "Parsed N visual regions". The ids and regions were already in `structuredContent`. This carries @MaxWang007's change from #7195 with their commit kept as authored, updates it with main, and adds fixes on top.

## What changed

- `window_state_view::apply` puts `capture_id=<id>` on the `window_id=` header line next to `snapshot_id` when a non-empty capture id was registered. The new `append_capture_id` does the same for the `get_desktop_state` summary on macOS, Linux and Windows. On Windows, capture publication now runs before the summary is built so the id is known.
- `parse_visual_regions` text keeps the count first, then `capture_id`, then one row per region with quoted id, kind, bounds, confidence, and quoted text or label.
- Our commits on top: a capture-only `get_window_state` read that returns only an inline image (no `window_id=` text) now gets a `capture_id=<id>` text part, so `apply` takes `&mut Vec<Content>`; region ids are quoted, since they are unconstrained strings and a newline would break the row format; an unused `bool` return on `rewrite_tree_block` is dropped.

## Scope

Text content only. Tool arguments, schemas and `structuredContent` are unchanged. Live desktop runs were not done.

## Blast Radius

Every text-only MCP client of these three tools sees extra fields on the first summary line and extra region rows. Clients that read `structuredContent` see no change. Anything that matches the exact old `Parsed N visual regions` string will now see ` capture_id=...` after it on that line.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib -- window_state_view perception_tools`: 50 passed, including the new header, image-only capture and region-text tests. Removing the image-only fallback makes its test fail.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): rustfmt and SPDX headers passed; clippy, unit tests and the Windows cross-check go to CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): list macOS modal panels in list_windows without a pid
body:
Salvaged from #7200

## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS an app's own alerts, open and save panels and app-modal dialogs sit on CGWindow layer 8 (`kCGModalPanelWindowLevel`). `list_windows` without a `pid` listed layer 0 only, so a client that lists windows to find its target never saw the dialog holding the app's key focus. Keys to the document were then refused with `window_not_key` naming a window the client could not find. `list_windows` with a `pid`, `get_window_state` and the input tools already reach these windows.
- What changed: `list_windows` without a `pid` now also returns visible, panel-sized layer-8 windows (alpha above 0, both edges at least 40 pt; untitled is allowed, since alerts often are). That size and alpha check keeps out invisible system helpers on layer 8, such as UserNotificationCenter's 4x4 pt alpha-0 window, which would otherwise rank as frontmost. Floating panels, the Dock, the menu bar, status items and menus stay out. With a `pid`, nothing changes. The rest of the driver (focus, stacking, change detection) still enumerates layer 0 only. The tool description and its generated reference pages are updated.

This keeps @AlexFalher's two commits from #7200 as authored, rebased onto current main. The salvage changes only the commit messages and the PR text, so they meet this repository's rules for commit and PR metadata. The code is unchanged.

## Related work

Refs #7200. #7200 names no issue. #6758 made a sheet answer to its own window id; this covers dialogs that are separate windows rather than sheets.

RFC: not required. The schema is unchanged; an unfiltered `list_windows` returns more records, each already carrying `layer`.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact (macOS only): an unfiltered `list_windows` also returns open modal panels. A client that takes the highest `z_index` as the front window now gets the dialog that holds focus, which is where keys go. A client that assumed every unfiltered record is layer 0 will now see layer-8 ones, and the `layer` field marks them.
- Windows and Linux: unchanged. Their `list_windows` has no layer filter, and owned dialogs and transient windows are already listed.
- Risk and rollback: revert the two commits.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: a unit test pins the filter. Layers 0 and 8 are admitted; -1, 3, 20, 24, 25 and 101 are not. An untitled layer-8 panel is admitted. The 4x4 alpha-0 helper is not, and neither is a layer-8 window failing only the alpha check or only one edge check. Layer 0 is never filtered by size or alpha.
- The scoped repository checks ran on this head with `bin/ci --quick` (rustfmt, SPDX headers, docs code blocks, image refs): green. Clippy, the platform-macos unit tests, the UniFFI bindings check and the Windows cross-compile were skipped on this shared Linux host and run in CI. The generated-reference drift check was not routed locally (the pnpm activation failed) and runs in CI.
- Manual or platform evidence: #7200 reports live macOS 26 runs with an AppleScript app-modal alert and an in-process open panel. Before the change both were missing from an unfiltered `list_windows`; after it they were listed front-most, read, and answered in the background. Those runs predate the visibility filter. This host cannot run macOS, so they were not repeated here.

title: fix(cua-driver): don't report a macOS press as failed when it closed its own window
body:
Salvaged from #7201

## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, a button that closes its own window (an open panel's "Choose", a dialog's OK) can make `AXUIElementPerformAction(AXPress)` return an error such as `kAXErrorCannotComplete` (-25204), because the window is gone before the app answers. The press ran, but `click` returned `AX action failed`, which invites a retry on a dialog that no longer exists.
- What changed: when the press errors, after the existing AXOpen, toggle and row-selection fallbacks, `perform_ax_click` checks with `describe_window` whether the press's window still exists, polling up to the selection read-back timeout. If the window existed just before the press and is gone after it, the click is reported as performed but unverifiable and names the closed window. A hidden window (ordered out, minimized, alpha 0) still has a WindowServer record and counts as open, so the error is returned as before.

## Related work

Refs: no upstream issue. This is AlexFalher's work from #7201, moved onto main without the #7200 commits it was stacked on. The two commits don't depend on #7200 and cherry-pick cleanly. Their authorship is kept; only the tool co-author trailer was dropped from the commit messages.

RFC: not required. No protocol change; such a click returns the existing `unverifiable` effect instead of an error.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: macOS only. A press that closed its own window no longer reads as failed.
- Risk and rollback: a press that errors on a window that stays open waits up to 500 ms before the same error. A window that closes for another reason in that time is reported as unverifiable, which still tells the caller to look. Windows and Linux are unchanged; #7201 explains why each behaves differently (UIA Invoke is asynchronous; AT-SPI `doAction` errors still read as failed, which would be a separate change). Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: unit tests cover the window poll (a window that closes after a few reads counts, one that stays does not), the hidden-window rule, and the open-before-press rule. The scoped repository checks ran in quick mode here (rustfmt and SPDX headers passed). Clippy and the platform-macos unit tests need macOS and run in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): probe daemon presence with the same request on every OS
body:
Stacked on #8289 (merged into this branch). #8339 has already landed on main.

## Why

`is_daemon_listening` meant different things per OS. Unix sent the read-only `list` request. Windows called `WaitNamedPipeW`, which only shows that a pipe instance exists, so an endpoint that never answers read as a running daemon. Every OS now connects and sends `list`.

## What changed

- `cua_driver_core::daemon::probe_endpoint(path, reply_within) -> EndpointProbe { Answers, Unanswered, Closed }`: one connect attempt and one read-only `list`, with the connection closed before it returns. `Closed` means the path has no listener (Unix: not found or refused; Windows: no pipe instance). A busy or inaccessible pipe reads as `Unanswered`, never `Closed`. `is_daemon_listening` is `probe_endpoint(.., 2 s) == Answers`, using the presence probe's existing 2 s deadline. On Windows the pipe is opened for overlapped I/O. A transfer still pending at the deadline is cancelled and the handle closed, and no transfer starts after the deadline, so a late or endless reply leaves no thread or pipe instance behind and cannot outrun the bound.
- `probe_presence`'s `metadata` request goes through the same single-connect path on both OSes, so the Windows `WaitNamedPipeW` precheck in `daemon.rs` is gone.
- On Windows, `wait_for_release` still counts a daemon as released only when its pipe is closed, which keeps #8289's model: a pipe that listens without answering is not released, lock or no lock. Each poll is now one `probe_endpoint` bounded by what is left of the 2 s release budget, not a `metadata` probe followed by a second check. `diagnose` on Windows now reports `daemon: answers` or `daemon: does not answer (…)` rather than `pipe instance: …`.

## Scope

Covers presence probing in `cua-driver-core/src/daemon.rs` and its two Windows callers in `serve.rs` and `cli.rs`. It leaves out the shared listener and the dispatch bodies (seam-p4), and the `WaitNamedPipeW` calls in test harnesses (`cua-driver-testkit`, `named_pipe_instance_recovery_test.rs`), which test pipe-instance availability on purpose.

## Tradeoffs

- On Windows a probe now briefly takes a pipe instance and waits for a reply. That is slower than `WaitNamedPipeW`, and the trade is accepted for a truthful answer.
- On Unix, `is_daemon_listening` used to wait on `list` for the full tool reply deadline. It now waits up to the 2 s presence deadline from #8289, the same bound on both OSes. A daemon that cannot answer `list` within 2 s reads as not listening.

## Blast Radius

Every `is_daemon_listening` caller (CLI start/stop/status/update, proxy, SDK, autostart). On Unix the request is the same and only the reply bound changes. On Windows, callers that saw a pipe with no daemon behind it as "listening" now see it as not listening.

## Verification

- New hermetic tests in `daemon::probe_endpoint_tests`, for Unix sockets and Windows named pipes: no listener and a dead daemon's socket read as `Closed`; a listener that never answers reads as `Unanswered`; only an `ok` answer to `list` reads as `Answers`; an unanswered probe closes its connection, so the server sees EOF; a reply that never ends its line stops at the bound. They pass on macOS. Two mutations were each caught: counting any reply as `Answers`, and leaking the probe's connection.
- The scoped repository checks: `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` is clean for `cua-driver-core` on macOS, and for `cua-driver-core` and `cua-driver` cross-compiled to `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. `bin/ci --quick` is green.
- Still to run in CI or on Windows: the probe tests and `serve::pipe_release_tests` on native Windows, plus the Windows shared E2E lane (`serve`, `status`, `stop`), dispatched on this head.

title: fix(cua-driver): restore macOS web type_text keys and unhide reopened apps
body:
## Why
The cross-platform Cua Driver CD workflow has been red since run 325 (0.55.1) and still was on run 331 (0.56.1). The macOS hosted E2E lanes fail with the same three tests every time. Those lanes only run post-merge, so the regressions landed unseen. Run 330, the one reported red, fails on all three.

## Cause (two product regressions, not infrastructure or flakes)
- `type_text` (#8089): an unchanged AXValue read-back inside any AXWebArea sent no keys. That is documented only for Gecko (#5383). Chromium, Electron, Tauri and WKWebView leave AXValue unchanged because they did not take the write, so the text never arrived. Failing tests: `shared_web_action_matrix_is_state_verified` (electron, tauri and wkwebview ax and px background) and `standalone_browser_generic_type_text_completion` (0 of 842 chars).
- `launch_app` (#8220): an `aevt/rapp` event only asks a running app to show a window, and a hidden app that was not started by LaunchServices ignores it. Failing test: `appkit_launch_reopens_hidden_running_app_without_focus_steal`. That test was added by #8220 and has never passed on the hosted runner.

## Fix
- The no-retype rule now applies to Gecko browsers only. Every other engine falls back to keys again.
- After a reopen, the app is unhidden with `NSRunningApplication.unhide`, which does not activate, so the previous frontmost app stays on top.

## What changes for users
Typing into Chrome, Electron and WebKit pages in the background works again, and `launch_app` on a hidden running app makes it visible again.

## Verification
- Unit tests added or kept for the Gecko gate. `cargo check` for platform-macos passes. `bin/ci --quick --fix` is green.
- I could not run the hosted macOS lanes locally. They run on the next release-gate run after merge, which will show whether these two fixes are enough.

title: fix(cua-driver): detect the Linux desktop in one place
body:
Stacked on #8289 (its branch is merged in here). #8339, the other prerequisite, is already on main.

## Why
`desktop.rs` is meant to be the one place the Linux desktop gets classified, but `input/mod.rs` (the KDE-on-X11 uinput hotplug check), `wayland/mod.rs` (the native-Wayland opt-in) and `video_wayland.rs` (wf-recorder's `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` check) still read those variables themselves. The later route-table PRs need a single classification source, so this moves those reads.

## What changed
- `desktop::kde_x11()` replaces `kde_x11_uinput_hotplug_is_unsafe{,_from_env}` in `input/mod.rs`. It reads the same variables and uses the same rules, and still reads them on every call.
- `desktop::wayland_opted_in()` replaces `wayland::wayland_enabled()`, and `opted_in` is now private to `desktop.rs`.
- wf-recorder refuses to start when `desktop()` is `Desktop::X11` (the cached form of "no `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`").

## Scope
This only moves detection. It adds no `LinuxRoutes`, and capture, windows, pointer, keyboard and overlay routing are untouched (P13b–f). These reads stay where they are: IPC endpoint reads (`NIRI_SOCKET`, `SWAYSOCK`, `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`, `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` paths), diagnostics that print raw `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, and the desktop-name matchers for GNOME/KDE in `shell_helper`, `kwin_capture`, `interaction/facts` and `a11y`, since each of those parses the name differently. The musl exclusion of `platform-linux` and the `!Send` Wayland workers are unchanged.

## Blast Radius
This touches the Linux driver only. The KDE/X11 table covers every case from the old positional test, plus `DESKTOP_SESSION`, a `KDE_FULL_SESSION` spelling, blank `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and no-display cases, so the moved rule is pinned to its old results. `desktop()` already re-classifies after the nested session rewrites its display variables, so wf-recorder's check sees the same value it used to read.

title: ci(cua-driver): gate every driver change on the hosted E2E lanes before merge
body:
## Incident
- #8089 broke `type_text` into Chromium, Electron, Tauri and WKWebView, and #8220 broke `launch_app` reopen (it no longer unhides the app). Both shipped in 0.55.1 through 0.56.x with no E2E lane run on their PRs. The fix for the regressions themselves is #8434.

## Root cause
A PR gate already exists (`E2E: Cua Driver release gate`, check `E2E gate / result`), but it only ran for file names on a behavior allowlist (cursor, overlay, focus, background, browser, input). `platform-macos/src/tools/type_text.rs` and `platform-macos/src/apps/` matched none of them. Even when it ran on macOS, the quick lane skipped the native lane, the only one with `installed_app_launch_macos_test`.

## Change
- `cua_driver_e2e_gate_paths.py`: gate the whole driver tree (crates, test apps, build inputs, contract, fixtures, the gate itself). Docs, markdown and changelogs stay out. Tests added for both incident files.
- `e2e-rust-macos.yml`: quick runs `shared` on the Electron (Chromium engine) and WKWebView harnesses, plus the whole `native` lane. Electron refuses background AX type_text by design, so WKWebView is what exercises that path.
- Post-merge, nightly and tag release runs are unchanged. The `result` job already passes when paths are untouched and fails when a lane fails.
- Forks: the hosted macOS lane needs a same-repo branch and `actions: write`, so fork PRs skip it with no secret exposed.

## Gate to require
`E2E gate / result` (always reports, green when no driver paths changed). Not added to the ruleset here; a repo admin has to add it.

## Cost per driver PR
About 45 to 55 min wall clock (was about 30). macOS runner time rises from about 30 to about 90 min (`shared` about 40 to 45 + `native` about 45), an estimate from the full-lane timings. The same PR also runs the Linux and Windows quick lanes already in the gate. Non-driver PRs: none. The merge queue still skips macOS (60-minute queue timeout).

title: feat(cua-driver): support tiled niri windows and multi-output capture
body:
Salvaged from #7224 by @goncalompontes. Their commits are kept as authored; our fixes sit on top as separate commits.

Refs #6722

## Why

niri merged niri#4711 after 26.04, so `tile_pos_in_workspace_view` now gives tiled windows a position while they intersect the view. The niri adapter refused every tiled window before reading the field. #7224 uses the position, and also adds multi-output capture and desktop scope, toplevel image-source capture, a screenshot fallback for tiled windows on 26.04, clipboard paste for non-BMP text, browser identity routes, and `frame_suppressed` reporting.

## What changed

- From #7224: tiled placement from `tile_pos_in_workspace_view`, with the `Tiled` refusal kept for releases that never report it. Window capture copies the window's own output. `get_desktop_state` and desktop-scope input span every output's bounding box and refuse points in the gaps, and report `display: "composite"`. Toplevel image-source capture (niri#4599) is used when niri advertises it. Non-BMP text is pasted through the clipboard and the old text put back. `browser_prepare` and exact browser binding now run on niri. `get_window_state` reports `frame_suppressed` and `frame_suppressed_reason`.
- Merge with main: main already loads libxkbcommon 1.0 at run time (#6498), so #7224's `xkb_runtime.rs` is dropped for main's version. Main's localized browser-setup tests are kept, and the niri refusal test is gone because the refusal is gone.
- Our fixes: toplevel capture now uses the attested niri socket and bounded round trips. It and the screenshot fallback check the window's owner pid. The fallback sends `ScreenshotWindow` over the attested IPC into a private directory instead of running `niri msg` from PATH. It needs niri 25.11, where `path` exists, and no longer moves focus or deletes files from the user's screenshot directory. It puts the clipboard text back after niri replaces it. The fallback and the non-BMP paste share one guard: a clipboard offering anything besides plain text (HTML next to text, an image, files), or whose formats can't be read, refuses before anything is written, and a failed restore is reported. Capture shared memory is now freed when a bounded round trip times out. A multi-output KWin term in `get_desktop_state` that no longer compiled against main is dropped.

## Scope

Linux niri adapter, shared Wayland capture, and the niri docs rows. Other compositors are unchanged, except that the Hyprland frame composer is now shared. Window-coordinate pointer input still needs one output.

## Blast Radius

niri sessions only. On niri 26.04 a tiled window now gets a capture where it used to refuse. That capture replaces the clipboard for a moment and, in niri builds with dbus, shows a screenshot notification. Text outside the BMP now goes through the clipboard on niri for every app, not only Chromium.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): rustfmt, SPDX headers, docs code blocks and image refs pass. Clippy, unit tests and builds run in CI. This host had too little disk to build.
- Live niri runs come from the contributor's reports on #7224 (26.04 and niri main `7f81a7f`, nested, plus vkms for multi-output). They predate our fixes, and our fixes have not run on a live niri.

title: fix(cua-driver): skip the Linux focus guard's settle watch when a delivery sends nothing
body:
Fixes #7279

## Why

Since #7208, `focus_guard::guarded` restores focus on every exit path and always runs the 220 ms settle watch. A delivery refused before it sent any key, such as a virtual-keyboard text that needs more spare keycodes than the keymap has free, had nothing to wait for but still paid the full watch.

## What changed

- `focus_guard::RefusedBeforeInput` marks an error raised before any input went out. The new `focus_guard::guarded_one_delivery` reads it from the error chain and restores with one check instead of the settle watch. The restore still runs, so any focus change is still undone. `type_text`'s background text route uses it.
- `guarded` keeps the settle watch for every error, since some bodies (for example `set_value`'s click, Ctrl+A, then text) send input before the call that refuses.
- The spare-keycode preflight refusal (`typed 0 of N characters: the text needs M spare keycodes`) now carries that marker. Its message is unchanged.

## Scope

Linux only, and only that preflight refusal. Other errors, and a refusal inside a body that already sent input (such as `set_value`), keep the settle watch. Successful deliveries are unchanged. macOS and Windows have no equivalent guard watch.

## Verification

- New unit tests `a_single_delivery_refused_before_input_restores_without_the_settle_watch` and `a_refusal_after_other_input_in_the_body_keeps_the_settle_watch`, plus the existing failure and success tests, which now also assert the restore still runs the settle watch after any other error and after success.
- `text_plan_fails_without_steps_and_restores_remaps_when_spares_run_out` also asserts the preflight error is a `RefusedBeforeInput`.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, headers). Clippy and unit tests were not run on this host because it is out of disk; they run in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): build every Windows crate against windows 0.61
body:
Stacked on #8289: its branch is merged in here, so this diff includes its commits until #8289 lands. #8339, the other prerequisite, is already on main.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: the driver workspace built three versions of the `windows` crate. `cua-driver`, the testkit and the e2e crate used 0.61. `cua-driver-core`, `cua-driver-sdk` (dev-dependencies) and `platform-windows` used 0.58, and `clipboard-rs` brought in 0.59. New Windows IPC code in the shared-IPC chain needs a single `windows` version underneath it.
- What changed: core, the SDK and platform-windows now build against windows 0.61. The API changes are ported mechanically:
  - `BOOL` now comes from `windows::core`.
  - `VARIANT` now comes from `Win32::System::Variant`. This adds the `Win32_System_Ole` and `Win32_System_Variant` features, which gate the UIA and MSAA methods that take or return a `VARIANT`. Its fields are read directly, and `VARIANT`'s own `Drop` still frees the value.
  - `PROPERTYKEY` now comes from `Win32::Foundation`.
  - Nullable handle, string and flag parameters are now `Option<_>`. Null handles pass `None`. `HBITMAP` and `HMODULE` convert into `HGDIOBJ` and `HINSTANCE`.
- `perception_client/containment` stays in core. Its Windows code compiles against 0.61 without changes.
- `LocalIpcClient` and `LocalIpcListener` are not part of this PR.

## Related work

Shared-IPC chain P0 → P3 → P4. This PR is P0. P3 and P4 build on top of it.

RFC: none needed. This is a dependency bump with no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none intended. Only Windows code changed, and the changes are mechanical. No public type in `platform-windows` takes or returns a `windows` type that the cua-spacesd crates pass in. Those crates call it with plain Rust values, so they keep their own windows 0.58 dependency.
- Lockfile: windows 0.58 is no longer in the driver lockfile. windows 0.59 is still there because `clipboard-rs` 0.3.5, its latest release, depends on it. That dependency is outside this PR's scope. Out-of-scope crates still on 0.58 keep it in other lockfiles: cua-media-codec, cua-teleport, cua-spacesd, cua-spacesd-desktop and cua-spacesd-test-apps. The cua-spacesd, spaces-e2e and teleport-e2e lockfiles now resolve platform-windows and cua-driver-core to 0.61.

title: fix(cua-driver): wait for Save to report enabled in the AppKit save-sheet E2E
body:
## What changed for users
Nothing user-facing. The driver's behaviour was correct; the AppKit E2E case that drives the Save sheet was racy and only passed on the gate's retry.

## Cause
Run 44883632815 (macOS hosted, first attempt) failed with `refusing AXPress: the target reports AXEnabled=false` on the sheet's Save button, then passed on retry ("[FLAKY] ... failed once then passed"). The main nightly and release-gate runs after #8434 pass this case; the nightly failures there are other cases (`appkit_launch_reopens_hidden_running_app...`, browser `type_text`) that #8434 addressed.

This is a harness setup bug, with real macOS behaviour behind it. NSSavePanel re-validates the file name after the name field's value changes and reports Save `AXEnabled=false` until that settles. The test read the Save token right after `set_value` and pressed it at once, so it sometimes hit the window where Save was still disabled. The driver already acts through the sheet's own window and reads `AXEnabled` from the right element (the pressed button), so it is not a driver bug.

## Fix
The test waits, on a fresh snapshot with a 5 s deadline, for Save to be published `enabled`, then presses that token. The press is still `delivery_mode: "background"` and the assertions are unchanged. No skip, quarantine or retry. The driver keeps refusing to press a control that reports disabled, which is the safe documented behaviour (`element_disabled`, covered by `harness_appkit_disabled_control_is_published_and_its_press_refused`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cua-driver): Windows existing-profile setup never takes the foreground
body:
Salvaged from #7379

Work by @abonneth. Their commit is kept as authored; one follow-up commit sits on top.

## Why

On Windows, an existing-profile attach that has to turn on remote debugging brought the browser to the front for several seconds, and `end_session` did it again when it turned debugging back off. Chromium activates its window for UIA `Invoke`, `SetValue`, `Toggle` and `SetFocus`. It does not activate it for the MSAA default action, the MSAA value, or keys posted to its HWND, so setup now uses only those.

## What changed

- `browser_setup_ui.rs` (#7379): the new-tab button, the remote-debugging checkbox and the tab close use `LegacyIAccessible` `DoDefaultAction`. The address field uses the MSAA value. Enter is posted to the exact browser HWND, with the UIPI check. The setup tab is closed through the selected tab's own close button, found structurally, in place of Ctrl+W. The foreground assist, the focus step and `input_may_be_unread` are gone.
- Follow-up: the Windows `SetupUiHandle` drops `focused_setup_address_field`, `foregrounded_window` and `injected_global_input`. Nothing set them any more, and the outcome now reports `false` for them directly.

## Scope

Windows existing-profile setup only. The macOS and Linux setup paths and the cross-platform `side_effects` shape are unchanged. On Windows, `side_effects` no longer reports `foregrounded_window`, `injected_global_input` or `focused_setup_address_field` as true.

## Blast Radius

Chrome and Edge existing-profile attach on Windows. If the posted Enter does not reach the address field, the setup page never shows up, and the existing ready timeout rolls the setup back. Every existing proof is still checked: exact tab count, address-field value, setup URL and checkbox state.

## Verification

- New unit test `setup_tab_close_is_the_selected_tabs_own_close_action` on the Edge 153 fixture. In #7379, `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib browser_` passed on `windows-11-arm`, and all of #7379's CI passed at 2815562.
- The contributor ran an A/B on `windows-11-arm` with Edge 156 and a probe window in the foreground. Edge took the foreground on attach and on `end_session` in 5/5 runs on main and 0/5 with this change. Attach bound and the toggle reverted in 5/5 runs on both.

title: feat(cua-driver): share one local IPC client
body:
Stacked on #8289, #8444 (windows 0.61) and #8428 (Windows `REPLY_DEADLINE`). Their branches are merged in, so this diff includes their commits until they land. #8339 is already on main. Once they land, main gets merged in here.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: the daemon request path (`cua_driver_core::daemon`) and the SDK trusted service session each had their own sync socket and pipe client: their own connect retry, poll loop, deadline handling and error text. The MCP proxy and the MCP envelope relay each opened the socket or pipe in their own `cfg(unix)` and `cfg(windows)` blocks. The Windows pipe client was written as hand-declared `kernel32` externs.
- What changed:
  - New `cua_driver_core::ipc`. `LocalIpcClient::connect(path, ConnectPolicy)` and `exchange_line(request, deadline)` send one newline-terminated request and read one reply line. Reads wait in 10 s slices and writes in 5 s slices, each cut to whatever is left before the deadline. On Unix the socket is nonblocking and each read or write waits in `poll(2)`. On Windows each overlapped operation is cancelled when its wait ends. Neither OS runs past the deadline. Bytes after the reply line are kept for the next exchange. `ExchangeError` is `Write`, `Read`, `TimedOut { received }` or `Closed`, and each caller turns it into its own message. `ConnectPolicy { retry, budget }` never pauses past what is left of its budget. It has `ONCE`, `STARTUP` (50 ms for up to 3 s) and `REQUEST`. `REQUEST` retries like `STARTUP` on Windows, where a pipe whose instances are all busy refuses clients for a moment, and connects once on Unix, where the listener queues connections.
  - `daemon::exchange` (the parameterized deadline from #8289, which #8428 extended to Windows) and the service session's request, resume and close now go through `LocalIpcClient`. `REPLY_DEADLINE` (150 s) is still the deadline on both. The presence probe keeps #8289's semantics: same requests, the same 2 s bound, the same `WaitNamedPipeW` precheck.
  - The proxy control connection (`ConnectPolicy::STARTUP`) and the MCP envelope relay (`ConnectPolicy::REQUEST`) connect through the async `LocalIpcStream::connect`, so each has one code path for both OSes.
  - `ipc/windows.rs` holds the overlapped pipe client from #8428 and `WaitNamedPipeW`, now written against windows 0.61 (`Win32_Storage_FileSystem`, `Win32_System_IO`, `Win32_System_Pipes`). `pipe_stream.rs` and `socket_io.rs` are deleted.

## Related work

Refs #8289, #8444, #8428. Shared-IPC chain: P0 (#8444) → P2 (#8428) → this PR (P3) → P4, the shared listener.

RFC: not needed. The wire protocol, deadlines and public SDK API are unchanged.

## Scope

Client side only. `serve.rs` keeps its `DaemonRequest` dispatch, accept loops, peer checks and drain. Those move into `ipc` in P4. UIAccess, perception and compositor IPC are left out because their framing and trust models are different.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:
  - The trusted service session's transport error text changes slightly, for example `timed out after 150s waiting for the reply to trusted service request`. Nothing matches on these strings. The daemon client's messages are unchanged, except that a Windows connect failure now reads `connect to <pipe>: …` instead of `connect to named pipe <pipe>: …`.
  - On Windows the MCP envelope relay now retries a busy pipe for up to 3 s. Before, it failed on the first busy instance.
  - A reply that is not valid UTF-8 is now a read error on the daemon path too. Before, it was decoded lossily. The daemon only ever writes `serde_json` output.
  - The SDK's fallback for targets that are neither Unix nor Windows is removed. The binary already supported only those two, and the core's own fallback is still there.
- Risk and rollback: medium. Every daemon client goes through the new module. Revert this commit to roll back.

## Tradeoffs

- An async tokio client called through `block_on` from sync callers was ruled out, because those callers can already be inside a runtime.
- The poll slice is a private parameter (`exchange_polling`), so tests can use short slices without a public switch.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - New hermetic `ipc::tests`. With a fake transport (OS independent): a write waits out a peer that drains slowly and in small pieces, a peer that never drains stops at the deadline with the exact error, and a read that never ends its line stops at the deadline. Over a real Unix socket: one line out and one in, keeping what follows the reply; a poll slice expiring mid-character keeps waiting and keeps split UTF-8; a stalling server hits the deadline with `TimedOut { received: 6 }`; a trickling reply with no newline hits the deadline; a server that never reads stops a 16 MB write at its 200 ms deadline; a close before any reply reads as `Closed` and a close after some bytes returns them; sync and async connects retry only within their budget, and a 5 s retry pause is cut to a 100 ms budget. Windows named-pipe versions of the stalled-read cancellation, closed-server EOF, stalling-server deadline, write-deadline, poll-slice and connect-retry tests are in `ipc/windows.rs`.
  - Mutation checks: letting a write wait a full 5 s slice regardless of the deadline, or letting a retry pause ignore the budget, each fails its test.
  - Exact-message owner tests: `daemon::tests::a_stalled_socket_daemon_times_out_at_the_reply_deadline` (new, Unix) and `a_stalled_pipe_daemon_times_out_at_the_reply_deadline` (Windows), and `service_session::tests::a_stalled_service_reply_times_out_at_the_reply_deadline`. The service-session poll and trickle tests moved into `ipc`, which now owns that contract.
  - Ran on macOS: `cargo test` for `ipc::` and `daemon::` in cua-driver-core (21 passed), `service_session` in cua-driver-sdk (2 passed), and `proxy::` and `mcp_envelope::` in cua-driver (31 passed). `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` is clean for cua-driver-core, cua-driver-sdk and cua-driver on macOS and cross-compiled to `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass.
- Manual or platform evidence: none on this host. It is a shared macOS machine with no Windows or Linux test lane.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Windows and Linux `cargo test` lanes in CI (the Windows `ipc` tests run only there), and the E2E proxy and MCP rows on macOS, Windows and Linux on the final candidate SHA.

title: fix(cua-driver): pin input lane order and keep browser tools off the desktop lane
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: the input lane order that #8344 left in `ToolRegistry` (pid lane, then desktop lane, browser tools on neither) holds today, but nothing documents it and no test pins it. A regression could put a browser tool on the desktop lane, which would let a call hold the desktop while it waits for a browser mutation gate.
- What changed:
  - A doc comment on `InputAdmission` states the order: `Lane::Pid` first, never waiting for its holder (a busy pid is refused at once); `Lane::Desktop` last, the only lane that waits, possibly while the call holds a pid lane, which cannot deadlock because nothing waits for a pid lane. Browser tools take neither lane, and the browser operations that mutate a tab serialize on the engine's `MutationGates`.
  - `no_registered_browser_tool_takes_the_desktop_lane`: for every tool `register_browser_tools` registers, across several argument shapes, `has_independent_input_lane` is false and `requires_desktop_coordination` is false. It also checks every `browser_*` action-result tool in the contract is registered, so the loop cannot pass empty. It is now the one owner of the browser exemption; `every_native_action_result_tool_takes_the_desktop_lane` checks native actions only.
  - `the_guard_keeps_its_tool_on_the_lane_the_tool_attests`: `PidOnlyWindowTargetGuard` forwards its inner tool's `has_independent_input_lane`, and the trait default is false.

Admission behavior is unchanged. The only non-test code changes are the doc comment, `requires_desktop_coordination` becoming `pub(crate)`, and a `#[cfg(test)]` registry accessor.

## Related work

Refs #8344 (originally stacked on it; it has since merged, so this branches from main).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none.
- Risk and rollback: low; documentation and tests.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passed. Unit tests and clippy were not run on this shared host; they run in CI and in verification.
- Mutation check (test plan): making `is_desktop_action_result_tool` keep one browser tool, for example `browser_type`, must fail `no_registered_browser_tool_takes_the_desktop_lane`.
- Known gaps or CI still required: hermetic only, no desktop E2E row needed.

title: [Bug]: Linux/X11: uinput/XI2 device churn crashes every Qt 6.11 app with SIGSEGV (use-after-free), 6 waves captured (refs #8197)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux/X11, the driver's uinput/XI2 device create-and-destroy churn crashes every Qt 6.11.3 app on the desktop with SIGSEGV, in the same second as an input-device removal. This looks like the same root vector as #8197 (Cinnamon dies on the master-add hierarchy event); here the victims are Qt client applications, dying with what the kernel disassembly shows as a use-after-free on the device-destroy side of the churn.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Driver | embedded cua-driver of OpenMausBot AppImage 0.1.154 (`cua-driver serve --embedded --no-overlay`, OpenMausBot README pins Cua Driver 0.41.3) |
| OS | NixOS 26.05.20261120.ab5c18f, kernel 6.18.64 (unsupported target, reported for the data point) |
| Desktop | Xorg X11, two 3840x2160 monitors |
| Victims | flameshot 13.3.0, krusader 2.9.0, kate 26.04.3, telegram-desktop 7.4.3, all linking system Qt 6.11.3 (nixpkgs) |

### Evidence (2026-11-21, six crash waves on one desktop)

Each wave started within 23 to 161 seconds of the kernel registering `CUA v1.5... uinput pointer/keyboard` devices:

| device created | crash wave |
|---|---|
| 10:00:01 input22 (ptr) | 10:00:39 |
| 12:30:26 input23/24 (ptr+kb) | 12:30:49 |
| 14:33:06 input29/30 (ptr+kb) | 14:34:07 |
| 14:58:30 input31 (ptr) | 14:59:30 |
| 15:51:36 input32 (ptr) | 15:54:17 |
| 16:06:22 input33/34 (ptr+kb) | 16:06:50 |

- No injected input events at all were captured between device creation and the crashes. `xinput test` loggers attached to the driver's X11 slave devices recorded zero motion, button or key events. The victims die on device lifecycle events, not on injected input.
- The fatal moment is a device removal: `acpid: input device has been disconnected` is logged in the same second as the crashes (wave 6, 16:06:50).
- Kernel disassembly of the flameshot fault (offset 0x54fac in libQt6XcbQpa.so.6.11.3): `mov (%r12),%rdi; test %rdi,%rdi; mov (%rdi),%rax; call *0x20(%rax)` faulting at a wild address, a virtual call through a vtable loaded from a freed object. Use-after-free.
- All four applications fault at the identical instruction across six separate occasions. telegram-desktop additionally dies with `segfault at 0x20 ip 0x20` (call through a null vtable) a second later.

### What the driver does (observed)

Per session: creates two uinput devices (pointer, keyboard, product string `CUA v1.5...`); the X server attaches six slaves (XTEST and uinput pairs). The pointer slaves attach and detach again within about one second; keyboard slaves stay for the session; everything is torn down at session end, with additional mid-session churn.

### Request

Keep one persistent uinput/XI2 device pair alive for the driver's lifetime (create once, reuse, destroy at exit), or gate the churn behind an option. Desktops and toolkit versions that do not tolerate hierarchy churn (Cinnamon per #8197, Qt 6.11.3 clients here) currently cannot coexist with host-control mode on X11.

### Repro notes

Any create/destroy burst of uinput devices while Qt 6.11.3 X11 apps are idle reproduces on this host. Raw `xinput test` capture log, journalctl excerpts and coredump metadata available on request.

title: feat(cua-driver): resolve app paths in one place
body:
Stacked on #8289: its branch is merged into this one. #8339 has already landed on main.

## Why
The driver worked out its per-user locations (socket, pid file, lock, product home, config, history store, skills stage, telemetry directory) in about a dozen places. Each one read `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `LOCALAPPDATA` or `XDG_*` and applied its own fallback. `cua_driver_core::paths::AppPaths::for_namespace(ns)` now resolves all of them, and the migration changes no resolved path.

## What changed
- New `AppPaths` with `user_home`, `home`, `cache_dir`, `state_dir`, `config_file`, `socket`, `pid_file`, `pipe_lock`, `telemetry_dir`, `skills_dir` and `history_root`. Each field keeps the exact rule and fallback of the code it replaces, quirks included: the daemon strings keep their `/` formatting on Windows, and `skills_dir` reads `USERPROFILE` on Windows where the others read `HOME` first. `bundle::app_paths()` resolves it for this installation's namespace through the test-overridable `env_vars` reader.
- Callers moved over: core (`daemon`, `config_file`, `script_tool`), the SDK's default socket, and the binary's `serve`, `telemetry`, `release_channel`, `version_check`, `skills`, `history_runtime` and `doctor`. Deleted `daemon::socket_path_for_namespace`, `daemon::daemon_lock_path` (now `AppPaths::pipe_lock_for`) and `bundle::user_home_subdirectory`.
- Parity tests in `cua-driver/tests/app_paths_parity_test.rs` pin the resolved paths per OS from the testkit's `IsolatedStateRoot`, with and without `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME`, with `CUA_DRIVER_TELEMETRY_HOME`, and with no home at all. The old history-root test is removed because the parity test now covers that contract. On Windows the test sets `USERPROFILE` to a different directory from `HOME`, and it covers an empty `CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME` and a set or empty `XDG_STATE_HOME`. The Linux lane runs it with every target. The macOS and Windows lanes now select the test binary by name.

## Scope
Covers the driver's own state paths. App discovery, browser profiles and agent-host skill directories are not part of it. Neither is `main()`, which is seam-p6's job. A few `HOME` reads remain because they don't resolve one of the fields: `~` expansion in tools and the `recording` CLI, the installed-package helper path in `history_runtime`, `extension_root`, `connect`'s agent config dirs, the macOS `diagnose` text, and `cursor-overlay`.

## Blast Radius
This touches every entry point that finds the daemon (CLI, MCP proxy, SDK, autostart, updater). A changed path would split clients from the daemon, and the parity tests exist to catch exactly that. Outside tests, `bundle::app_paths()` reads the same process environment the old code read.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass. This shared host builds nothing, so compiling, clippy and the unit tests, parity tests included, run in CI on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- At `2c842e5388` every driver Rust lane passed, and the parity tests ran and passed on macOS, Linux and Windows while they still lived in `bundle.rs`. This head moves them, unchanged, into their own test binary.
- The first commit carried a temporary test comparing `AppPaths` with the old resolvers. That commit failed clippy on dead code before its tests could run, so the only proof of equivalence is the parity literals, which were read off the old code.

title: feat(cua-driver): spawn owned child processes through ManagedChild
body:
Stacked on #8289 (its branch is merged in; #8339 has already landed on main). Once #8289 lands, main is merged in here.

## Why

Five places spawn a child the driver owns, and each one sets up the OS-level tie to its owner by hand: the detached daemon in `cli.rs` (a `process_group(0)` branch on Unix and a raw `CreateProcessW` on Windows), the Job Object for ffmpeg in core, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` in the SDK, and plain `spawn` plus repeated kill/wait code in the private worker and the Linux recorders. This PR moves that setup into one narrow type, `cua_driver_core::process::ManagedChild`.

## What changed

- New `core::process::ManagedChild::builder()` with four options:
  - `.detached()`: on Unix, `process_group(0)`. On Windows, `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` with handle inheritance turned off; this is the `CreateProcessW` path moved out of `cli.rs`.
  - `.no_window()`: `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`.
  - `.kill_with_owner()`: on Windows, a `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` job, with the child started suspended, assigned to the job, then resumed (moved out of `video_ffmpeg.rs`). On Unix, the child gets its own process group, killed on drop, on `kill()`, and when `try_wait`/`wait` see the child exit. They check for that exit with `waitid(WNOWAIT)` and kill the group while the exited leader still holds the group ID, then reap it. A reaped leader's ID is never signalled again.
  - `.reap_on_drop()`: dropping a child that is still running kills it and waits for it.

  `ManagedChild` doesn't deref to `Child`. Callers use its `id`, `take_stdin`/`take_stdout`/`take_stderr`, `kill`, `try_wait`, `wait` and `wait_with_output`, so nothing can reap the leader around the group handling. `.detached().spawn(program, args)` takes a program and arguments rather than a `Command`, with null stdio and the owner's environment, so it can't express settings a Windows detached child would drop.
- Callers moved to it:
  - The detached daemon uses `detached`.
  - ffmpeg in core uses `kill_with_owner` and `reap_on_drop`.
  - The private worker uses `reap_on_drop`. It still does no process-group signalling.
  - The SDK embedded daemon uses `no_window` through `configure()` on its tokio command, still only when the host has no console. The SDK's own lifecycle struct is renamed `DaemonProcess` so the name doesn't collide with the new type.
  - The Linux recorders (GNOME ffmpeg, wf-recorder, portal ffmpeg) use `kill_with_owner` and `reap_on_drop`.
- Tests:
  - Unix: hermetic tests spawn `sh` with a backgrounded `sleep`. They check that dropping or killing a `kill_with_owner` child ends the grandchild, that `wait` on an exited leader kills the group and drops the tie before reaping, and that `reap_on_drop` alone reaps the child but leaves the rest of the group running.
  - Windows: a test spawns `cmd` running `ping` inside the job and waits on every process the job lists after the drop. Another test covers command-line quoting. `ci-rust-windows.yml` already runs `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`, so both run there.

## Scope

Covers the callers listed above. Sandbox containment (`perception_client/containment`) still builds its own spawn: it is a security boundary, and `ManagedChild` is only process ownership. `main()` is not unified (that is seam-p6). Other `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` sites (autostart, platform-windows tools) and the testkit reaper are not touched.

## Tradeoffs

- On Windows, a detached child inherits no handles, so the detached API takes only a program and arguments. The daemon launch needs nothing more.
- A Unix `kill_with_owner` child is killed when its `ManagedChild` is dropped or killed. If the owner dies without unwinding, the group keeps running. Doing better needs `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` on Linux, which has no macOS equivalent.

## Blast Radius

- Unix ffmpeg and the Linux recorders now run in their own process group, so a Ctrl+C typed in a terminal no longer reaches them directly. They are stopped through `q`, SIGINT to the pid, or closing stdin, as before.
- A recorder backend dropped without `stop` used to leave its encoder running. It is now killed and reaped.
- Windows behavior for the daemon launch and ffmpeg should be the same as before: the code moved but its flags did not change.

## Verification

- [x] `bin/ci --quick` (the scoped repository checks): 6 passed, 6 skipped by `--quick`.
