title: fix(cua-driver): run every OS through one main with platform hooks
body:
Stacked on #8289 (its branch is merged in) and #8339 (already on main). Review the commits after the #8289 merge; the rest is #8289.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: macOS had one `main` and Windows/Linux had another. The two copies of the command dispatch drifted. On Windows and Linux, early `?` returns skipped the telemetry flush and printed anyhow's `Error: …` form.
- What changed:
  - One `main() -> ExitCode` and one `dispatch()` for every OS. The new `platform_main.rs` (binary crate only) adds `PlatformMainHooks`, which holds the OS differences:
    - `early_exit`: on macOS the permission probe, permission-guide resume and LaunchServices host request; on Windows the standard-user shell-launch helper.
    - `serve_preflight`: on macOS the Apple Events automation refusal, the gate options and gate-started telemetry. It returns a `ServeGate` that holds tool calls before bind and settles on the main thread.
    - `run_long_lived`: `work` runs on its own thread. On macOS, AppKit (gate, then overlay) owns the main thread. Elsewhere the main thread joins `work`, as `serve` did before. Running it on the main thread instead leaks std's lazily created main-thread handle, and the Memcheck server E2E fails. `serve` and the private worker are the only callers. Finite commands (`list-tools`, `describe`, `call`, …) never reach it, so they never start AppKit on any OS.
  - `telemetry::flush_pending` now runs at one point, after `dispatch` returns, for every command.
  - Startup authorization/config exit codes stay per OS (`STARTUP_AUTHORIZATION_EXIT`: 64 on macOS, 1 on Windows and Linux). `permission_policy_startup_test.rs` now pins the exact code for every rejected `serve` configuration, plus 1 for direct MCP on every OS. The macOS and Windows Rust CI lanes now run that test; before, macOS skipped it and Windows only compiled it.

## Related work

Refs the Cua Driver platform-seam RFC, item P6. Stacked on #8289. #8339 is merged.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact:
  - Exit codes are unchanged.
  - On Windows and Linux, a rejected `serve` startup now prints `cua-driver: authorization startup error: …`, `cua-driver: Computer History admission error: …` or `cua-driver: cannot create desktop runtime: …`, the same lines macOS prints, in place of `Error: …`.
  - A private-worker failure prints `cua-driver private worker: …` on every OS.
  - The direct-MCP authorization error now prints `cua-driver-rs: …` and flushes telemetry, as macOS already did.
- No separate overlay hook: the Windows STA pump and the Linux overlay worker already start their own threads when the platform tool registry is built, and SDK hosts rely on that. Only macOS needs the main thread, and `run_long_lived` covers it.
- Ordering changes:
  - The macOS host request now runs before logging init. It is a LaunchServices child with no logging output.
  - On Windows and Linux, the private worker now runs on a spawned thread joined by main, the same as `serve`.
  - On macOS the private worker's main thread joins the worker when its runtime fails to start, where it used to return 0 early. A panicking long-lived worker now exits 101, not 0, on every OS.
- Not in this PR: AppPaths (#8453), ManagedChild (#8456), IPC and Linux routes.
- Risk: high (process entry point on three OSes). Rollback: revert this PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, SPDX headers, workflow sync). This host is shared, so clippy, unit tests and the Windows cross-check were skipped locally and run in CI.
- Manual or platform evidence: pending. Needed: the macOS E2E rows for the AppKit overlay, permission-guide resume and private worker; Windows shell-launch helper coverage (`launch_app_standard_user_test`); a Linux smoke. These run once on the final candidate SHA.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the full CI matrix.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [ ] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). Only `bin/ci --quick` ran, as this is a shared host.

title: [Bug]: Linux foreground hotkey gives the focus back to the main window over the dialog it opened
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Linux X11, a foreground `hotkey` sent to the app already in front opens that app's dialog, then the driver gives the keyboard focus back to the main window behind it. The dialog stays open without the focus, and the reply says `effect: confirmed`.

### Reproduction

1. XFCE on Xvfb, Mousepad open and active.
2. Call `hotkey` with `keys: ["ctrl", "shift", "s"]`, `target: {kind: "window", pid, window_id}` of Mousepad's main window, `delivery_mode: "foreground"`.
3. 3 s later, read `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` and the X input focus.

Script: [`dialog_focus.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/5d022c1d207a57d68ed416ef1f15b7c11145a798/ab/dialog_focus.py). 5 of 5 runs.

### Expected behavior

The Save As dialog has the focus, as when the same chord is typed.

### Actual behavior

Mousepad's main window is active and holds the input focus; the dialog sits above it, unfocused. The reply:

```
"effect": "confirmed", "route": "global_input"
"detail": "focus_after=same_pid; appeared: window 33554471 \"Save As\", ..."
```

### Environment

- cua-driver 0.56.4, release binary `linux-x86_64`. Code below read at main `04d952f8c`.
- Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 (GitHub-hosted runner), Xvfb, xfwm4 4.18.0, Mousepad 0.6.1.

### Evidence

| Mousepad in front, `ctrl+shift+s` | Dialog opened | Dialog transient for main | Focus after 3 s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| driver `hotkey`, foreground | 5/5 | 5/5 | main window 5/5 |
| `xdotool key`, same chord | 5/5 | 5/5 | dialog 5/5 |

[Run 44908490047](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44908490047)

### Workaround and additional context

Where it comes from, as far as I can read it:

- [`restore_after_foreground`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/04d952f8c8336b1d2083b22c513a3fa9f662927e/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/input/focus_guard.rs#L629-L644) calls `restore_guarded` with `same_app = false`. Its doc says this is on purpose: "a foreground action gives the focus back even to a prior window of the target's process".
- [`own_new_window`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/04d952f8c8336b1d2083b22c513a3fa9f662927e/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/input/focus_guard.rs#L820-L842) does find the dialog here (the target owned the focus before the action, the window is new and its own), but only to end the settle watch. [`guard_restore`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/04d952f8c8336b1d2083b22c513a3fa9f662927e/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-linux/src/input/focus_guard.rs#L749-L781) gets `target_pid.filter(|_| same_app)`, which is `None`, so it returns `Restore`.

A possible direction: in the foreground restore, keep the focus on a window that `own_new_window` returns, as `SameAppDialog` does. Windows that existed before the action keep the documented rule.

Likely since #7164 (not bisected). Workaround: the caller brings the new window to the front after the call with `bring_to_front`.

- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: [Bug]: A declined browser remote-debugging prompt is reported as browser_reconnect_exhausted, and a reconnect accepts a new one
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

When the person presses Cancel on the browser's remote-debugging prompt, the driver does not report a decline. `browser_prepare` returns `browser_reconnect_exhausted` with a hint to bind again, and a reconnect redials until the driver accepts a later prompt.

### Reproduction

`browser_prepare`:

1. Edge's default profile, remote debugging turned on.
2. `browser_prepare` with `strategy.kind: "existing_profile"`.
3. Press Cancel on the prompt 0, 200 or 400 ms after it appears.

Reconnect:

1. Attach, then drop the driver's CDP connection.
2. Call `get_browser_state` and press Cancel on the first prompt.

Harness: [`consent_dismiss.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/44239b6ba4f8275caca4410e8fe5b74ac4f0d4f0/ab/consent_dismiss.py), which finds the prompt through UI Automation and presses Cancel at a set delay.

### Expected behavior

`browser_consent_revoked`, and no new prompt from the driver.

### Actual behavior

| Windows 11 arm64, Edge 157, 3 runs per row | main `fcc16ebb62` |
| --- | --- |
| `browser_prepare`, Cancel at 0, 200, 400 ms | `browser_reconnect_exhausted`, hint: bind again (9 of 9) |
| following that hint | a new prompt, which the driver accepts (3 of 3) |
| reconnect, Cancel on the first prompt | a second prompt 1.4 s later, the driver accepts it, bound (3 of 3) |
| reconnect, Cancel on every prompt | 3 prompts in about 3 s, then `browser_reconnect_exhausted` (3 of 3) |

The dial fails with `HTTP error: 403 Forbidden`, 9 of 9. Chromium answers the pending WebSocket upgrade with 403 when the prompt is denied ([`HandleDebuggingApproval`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/fab3a7a197e67f8603b254ce4498da687421e3b5/content/browser/devtools/devtools_http_handler.cc#L846-L864)). The driver looks for the prompt only after 500 ms, so an earlier Cancel reaches it as a failed dial, which it treats as transient.

### Environment

- cua-driver main `fcc16ebb62`, release build. Main `04d952f8c` has no 403 case in the dial path either.
- Windows 11 arm64 (GitHub-hosted `windows-11-arm`), Edge 157.0.4341.46.

### Evidence

- [Run 44073648478](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44073648478): all rows above.
- [Run 43532239465](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43532239465): the 403, from a build that adds the dial error to the refusal detail.

### Workaround and additional context

- No workaround for the caller: nothing in the reply tells a decline from a dropped connection.
- Raised in the review of #7378 ("a user who dismisses the prompt").
- #7999 added `browser_consent_revoked` for a prompt the driver leaves to the person. It does not cover this case: re-measured on it, same results.
- Proposed fix: #7678.

title: [Feature]: macOS background attach to an existing Chrome window on the user's Space
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On macOS, `browser_prepare` with `strategy.kind: "existing_profile"` refuses with `background_unavailable` (`background_attach_requires: "browser_window_on_another_space"`) whenever Chrome's window is on the user's Space and another app is in front. That is the usual desktop: the user works in one app, Chrome sits behind it.

The only way through is `delivery_mode: "foreground"`. It puts Chrome above the user's window for about a second, and if the user is typing, the attach fails anyway.

| macOS 26 arm64, Chrome 157, TextEdit in front, a key every 40 ms | main, background | main, foreground |
| --- | --- | --- |
| attached | 0/10, refused | 0/10, refused |
| Chrome window above the user's | never | 10/10, 728 to 1159 ms |
| keystrokes that missed the user's document | 0/188 | 136/643 |

The foreground refusals read "the exact address field no longer contained the fixed setup URL": the user's keys land in Chrome. [Run 43200020958](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/43200020958).

### Desired outcome

A background attach to a Chrome window shown on the user's Space, with the user's window kept in front and keeping the keyboard.

### Current workaround

None that leaves the user alone: move Chrome to another Space, or accept the foreground attach above.

### Affected components and platforms

cua-driver, macOS only: `browser_prepare` and `end_session` for `existing_profile`.

### Alternatives and prior art

#5052 refused this case because the consent window "opens over the user's window for about 0.9 s". With the self-activation guard from #5052 also applied to a window shown on the user's Space, I do not measure that: Chrome's window was above the user's in 1 of 49 attaches, for 137 ms. Attaching to a minimized window does put it above the user's for about 0.5 s every time, and a hidden one comes back on screen, so both should keep the refusal.

### Implementation ideas

#7482: run the guard for a shown window on the user's Space, and keep refusing a minimized, hidden or unknown-Space window. The MCP schema does not change, but the refusal detail `background_attach_requires` goes away. Maintainers to say whether that needs an RFC.

title: [Bug]: Two cua-driver unit tests fail on Windows and macOS 15
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Two cua-driver unit tests fail on main outside the platforms CI runs them on: one on Windows, one on macOS 15.

### Reproduction

1. Windows 11: `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver --bins`.
2. macOS 15.7.9: `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib security_prompt`.

### Expected behavior

Both pass.

### Actual behavior

1. `extension_manager::tests::active_perception_extension_resolves_owned_worker_arguments`: `assertion failed: config.args[1].ends_with("models/model-manifest.json")`. The paths are built with `Path::join`, so on Windows they end in `models\model-manifest.json`; the test compares strings with `/`.
2. `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`: `Don't Allow in [...]`. The labels come from the system's own tables. macOS 15.7.9 ships only the typographic `Don’t Allow`; on macOS 26.7 the straight-apostrophe spelling is the value of one key, `REQUEST_ACCESS_DONT_ALLOW`. The test asks for both.

### Environment

- cua-driver main `f4c72198c0`; both assertions are unchanged on `04d952f8c`.
- Windows 11 arm64 and macOS 15.7.9 x86_64, GitHub-hosted runners.

title: [RFC]: cua-bench per-variant timeout (cb run --variant-timeout) and Tinker rollout run timeout
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

`cb run` should bound how long one variant's setup, agent, and evaluation may run via a new `--variant-timeout SECONDS` flag, and the Tinker rollout should bound the whole `cb run` subprocess it spawns via `--run-timeout`. A variant past the bound is cancelled the same way Ctrl-C cancels it, recorded `failed`, and not retried. The rollout stop sequence sends SIGTERM, waits a grace period, then sends SIGKILL to the process group, keeping every variant that already finished. Reference implementation: PR #5679, fixing issue #5193.

### Motivation and current state

On `main`, `BatchRunner` bounds nothing inside a variant. If one sandbox call never returns, `asyncio.gather` never returns, `summary.json` is never written, the finished siblings' results are stranded, and the hung variant's sandbox stays up (issue #5193). The Tinker rollout then waits on `cb run` with no timeout and, if `cb` is killed, polls the session store for up to `timeout` (3600 s) for sessions that can no longer finish. The observed failure is silent: training stops with no error.

### Goals

- A hung variant fails after a bounded time and releases its sandbox; the batch finishes and `summary.json` is written.
- Finished variants of a stopped or crashed `cb run` reach the trainer; a dead `cb` is never polled.
- The default bound sits above every adapter phase envelope so healthy runs are not cut off.
- `0` opts out and restores the previous unbounded behavior, including the unbounded sandbox release path.

### Non-goals

- Bounding sandbox start: owned by `--retries` and the existing 900 s `TIME_TO_START_S`. A slow first start is an infrastructure failure and stays retryable.
- A batch-wide timeout on the `cb` CLI itself. The whole-run bound lives in the trainer, which owns the subprocess.
- Any schema change: `RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 2 and a timed-out variant uses the existing `failed` status.
- Retrying timed-out variants.

### Proposal

| flag | where | default | `0` or disable semantics | on expiry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--variant-timeout SECONDS` | `cb run task`, `cb run dataset`; `BatchRunner(variant_timeout_s=)` | `max(10800, CUA_BENCH_HARNESS_TIMEOUT + 5400)` | `0` = no episode deadline and no sandbox release bound (`open_sandbox(..., release_timeout_s=0)`) | variant cancelled as by Ctrl-C, recorded `failed`, not retried; run exits 1 |
| `--variant-timeout SECONDS` | Tinker `rl_loop` | unset: nothing forwarded, `cb`'s default applies | `0` forwarded, disables the bound in `cb` | same as `cb` |
| `--run-timeout SECONDS` | Tinker `rl_loop`; `run_rollouts(run_timeout=)` | unset: wait indefinitely | `0` = wait indefinitely | SIGTERM to `cb`, 360 s grace, SIGKILL the process group; finished variants kept |

#### Adapter phase envelopes and default bound derivation

All eight concrete `BenchAdapter` subclasses in `libs/cua-bench/tasks/` inherit the base timeouts from `libs/cua-bench/cua_bench/adapters/base.py` without overriding `timeouts` or `health_timeout`:

- `BenchAdapter.health_timeout = 300.0` s (`_wait_healthy`, runs before `setup` when `server` is set and not `tcp`, wrapped in its own `_bounded("setup", ...)` call).
- `BenchAdapter.timeouts = {"setup": 1800.0, "evaluate": 1800.0, "oracle": 3600.0}`.
- Episode wrapper overhead in `cua_bench/runner/episode.py` and `cua_bench/runner/desktop.py`: `wait_for_desktop` (`CUA_BENCH_DESKTOP_READY_S`, default `60.0` s; skipped for dataset tasks), post-setup `2.0` s pause, and up to two `_screenshot` calls (`SCREENSHOT_TIMEOUT_S = 20.0` s each: `20 s` in agent mode, `40 s` in oracle mode).
- `HarnessAgent` (`cua_bench/agents/harness_agent.py`): `CUA_BENCH_HARNESS_TIMEOUT` default `1800` s. Step-based agents (`cua-agent`: `max_steps=100`; `gemini`, `opencua`, `qwen3vl`, `qwen35`: `max_steps=50`) are step-bounded and define no wall-clock timeout.

| Adapter (`libs/cua-bench/tasks/`) | `wait_for_desktop` | `health_timeout` | `setup` | `oracle` | `evaluate` | pause + shots | Worst-case oracle total | Worst-case non-agent total (+ agent) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `OSWorldAdapter` (`osworld`) | 60 s | 300 s (`:5000`) | 1800 s | 3600 s | 1800 s | 42 s (oracle), 22 s (agent) | 7602 s | 3982 s + agent |
| `WAAAdapter` (`winarena_adapter`) | 60 s | none | 1800 s | none | 1800 s | 22 s | n/a | 3682 s + agent |
| `MiniWoBAdapter` (`miniwob`, `BenchWebAdapter`) | 60 s | 300 s (`:7000`) | 1800 s | 3600 s | 1800 s | 42 s (oracle), 22 s (agent) | 7602 s | 3982 s + agent |
| `WebVoyagerAdapter` (`webvoyager`, `LiveWebAdapter`) | 60 s | 300 s (`:7000`) | 1800 s | none | 1800 s | 22 s | n/a | 3982 s + agent |
| `OnlineMind2WebAdapter` (`online_mind2web`, `LiveWebAdapter`) | 60 s | 300 s (`:7000`) | 1800 s | none | 1800 s | 22 s | n/a | 3982 s + agent |
| `WebGymAdapter` (`webgym`, `LiveWebAdapter`) | 60 s | 300 s (`:7000`) | 1800 s | none | 1800 s | 22 s | n/a | 3982 s + agent |
| `OSWorldGAdapter` (`osworld_g`, `GroundingAdapter`) | 0 s (`dataset`) | none | 1800 s | 3600 s | 1800 s | 42 s (oracle), 22 s (agent) | 7242 s | 3622 s + agent |
| `ScreenSpotProAdapter` (`screenspot_pro`, `GroundingAdapter`) | 0 s (`dataset`) | none | 1800 s | 3600 s | 1800 s | 42 s (oracle), 22 s (agent) | 7242 s | 3622 s + agent |

Notes on inner timeouts already enclosed by those phase bounds: `BenchWebAdapter` `ctl()` calls use `90 s`; `MiniWoBAdapter` sets the in-page timer `CUA_BENCH_MINIWOB_SECONDS` (default `600 s`); `LiveWebAdapter` judges use `OpenAIChat(timeout=180 s)` inside `evaluate` (`1800 s`). Sandbox start (`TIME_TO_START_S = 900 s`) and sandbox release (`TIME_TO_RELEASE_S = 300 s`) sit outside the variant deadline.

Checking `max(10800, CUA_BENCH_HARNESS_TIMEOUT + 5400)` against the table:

- Oracle mode worst case is `7602 s` (`OSWorldAdapter` and `MiniWoBAdapter`). The `10800 s` floor leaves `3198 s` (~53 min) of headroom.
- `HarnessAgent` at default `CUA_BENCH_HARNESS_TIMEOUT = 1800 s` has a worst-case envelope of `3982 + 1800 = 5782 s` (`5018 s` below `10800 s`).
- `HarnessAgent` with any larger `CUA_BENCH_HARNESS_TIMEOUT = B` has a worst-case envelope of `3982 + B`. `B + 5400` sits `1418 s` (~23.6 min) above `3982 + B`.

#### Semantics

- The bound is a monotonic deadline armed only after sandbox start, so it covers `wait_for_desktop`, task setup, agent or oracle, and evaluation, and nothing else.
- Validation: the value must be finite and `>= 0`. `nan`, `inf`, and negative values are rejected at the CLI, in `BatchRunner`, and in `open_sandbox(release_timeout_s=)`.
- `0` opt-out semantics: when `variant_timeout_s == 0`, `BatchRunner` skips `asyncio.timeout` around `run_episode` and calls `open_sandbox(..., release_timeout_s=0)`. `open_sandbox` with `release_timeout_s=0` takes the original `async with sandbox_cls.ephemeral(image, **kwargs) as sb:` path with no release timeout, so both the episode and sandbox cleanup match `main` exactly.
- On expiry, the variant's `result.json` records `failed` with `"variant timed out after N s"` and the run exits 1, as for any failed variant. A variant's own `TimeoutError` that the deadline did not cause stays retryable.
- When `variant_timeout_s > 0`, sandbox release is separately bounded at `300 s` (`TIME_TO_RELEASE_S`). Past that bound, `open_sandbox` logs a warning that the sandbox may leak and lets the batch proceed.
- Rollout: `cb` is spawned in its own session. SIGTERM goes to `cb` alone so its cancel handler can release sandboxes. After a `360 s` grace period, deliberately longer than the `300 s` release bound, the whole process group receives SIGKILL so a grandchild holding `cb`'s pipes cannot hold EOF open.
- Partial results: finished variants are counted by `*/result.json` with status other than `cancelled`. A stopped or non-zero `cb` with finished variants returns the run directory; with none it raises. The existing `3600 s` session-store poll is skipped whenever `cb` timed out or exited non-zero.
- Signal paths: SIGTERM and SIGHUP become `SystemExit` while `cb` is awaited, and any exception on the wait, Ctrl-C included, runs the same stop sequence before propagating. `cb` cannot be orphaned.

### Alternatives considered

- A global batch timeout on `cb run`: bounds the wrong axis. It cannot free a hung variant while siblings still run, and a fair bound scales with variant count.
- Per-phase timeouts only: setup, oracle, and evaluate already carry envelopes, but a hang in agent code outside them is uncovered. One deadline covers any stall inside the variant.
- Including sandbox start in the budget: a slow image pull would eat the variant's compute budget, and start failures are already retried as infrastructure failures under `--retries`.
- Default `0` (opt-in): safest for compatibility, but the failure is silent; users meet it only after losing a run. A finite default was chosen, with `0` as the documented opt-out.
- An external watchdog killing `cb run`: finished variants are left on disk while the session-store poll still waits out its `3600 s`. The bound has to live where the subprocess is owned.

### Compatibility and migration

`cb run` gains one flag, `BatchRunner` gains `variant_timeout_s`, and `open_sandbox` gains `release_timeout_s`. The only change without flags is that variants now run under a `>= 10800 s` deadline (and a `300 s` sandbox release bound) where none existed. A user whose variant legitimately exceeds the bound passes `--variant-timeout 0` (which also disables the release bound) or a larger value. `rl_loop` defaults are unchanged: with no flag, the previous indefinite wait is kept. Rollback is a revert; no persistent state or schema changes.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

None. The change adds no permissions, network access, or telemetry. The process-group kill uses POSIX `killpg` with a `proc.kill` fallback elsewhere and is confined to the process tree the trainer spawned.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

- New tests pin: a hung variant fails while its sibling completes; sandbox start sits outside the budget; a variant's own `TimeoutError` stays retryable; a wedged release is bounded at `300 s`; `--variant-timeout 0` leaves both the episode and sandbox cleanup unbounded (including on cancellation); non-finite input is rejected; a pipe-holding grandchild dies with the process group; interrupt cleanup leaves `cb` SIGKILLed; a crashed `cb` with no finished variants raises.
- Suites on PR #5679: `libs/cua-bench` 386 passed / 7 skipped, `libs/cua-bench-rl` 63 passed / 1 skipped, ruff clean.
- Manual repro from issue #5193: before, the batch stalled past a 15 s watchdog with no `summary.json`; after, the hung variant recorded `failed` at the deadline, the sibling `completed`, and both sandboxes were released.
- Known gap: the sandbox lifecycle is exercised via fakes rather than a live Docker run, and `rl_loop` needs the `tinker` extra so its parser additions are covered only indirectly in CI.

### Unresolved questions

- Finite default vs opt-in: is `max(10800, CUA_BENCH_HARNESS_TIMEOUT + 5400)` acceptable as a behavior change, or should the flag ship `0` by default?
- Naming: `--variant-timeout` vs `--episode-timeout` or `--per-variant-timeout`, and `run_timeout` vs `rollout_timeout` on the trainer side.
- Should a timed-out variant be retryable under `--retries`, or behind a separate switch? It is currently hard-coded not retryable.
- Should `rl_loop --run-timeout` get a finite default, for example derived from `num_rollouts` times the variant timeout, rather than unset?

### RFC document pull request

title: sandbox_write builds a shell command from an unquoted path, so spaces break the write and shell metacharacters run
body:
## Affected revision

- Repository: `trycua/cua`
- Location: `libs/python/cua-sandbox-apps/cua_sandbox_apps/pipeline/sandbox_tools.py:174`


## Summary

`sandbox_write` writes a file by running `cat > {path} << 'SANDBOX_EOF'` and `chmod +x {path}` through the sandbox shell, with `path` interpolated verbatim. A path containing a space writes to the wrong file while still reporting success, and a path containing `;` executes an extra command inside the sandbox.

## Expected behavior

The content should be written to exactly the path the caller supplied. Characters such as spaces, `;`, `$`, or quotes in the path must be treated as ordinary filename characters and must never be interpreted by the shell.

## Actual behavior

With the sandbox shell bound to a local shell that runs the command it is given:

```sh
$ python3 driver.py
write result: OK: wrote 5 bytes to /tmp/report.txt; touch /tmp/INJECTED
injected file exists: True
space-path result: OK: wrote 5 bytes to /tmp/my report.txt
intended file /tmp/my report.txt exists: False
stray file /tmp/my exists: True | /tmp/report.txt exists: True
```

Two failures are visible:

* The path `/tmp/report.txt; touch /tmp/INJECTED` returns "OK" and the injected `touch` does run — the caller-supplied path became shell syntax.
* The ordinary path `/tmp/my report.txt` also returns "OK", but the intended file does not exist: the shell split the redirect at the space, creating `/tmp/my` and passing `report.txt` as an argument to `cat`. The caller is told the write succeeded when it silently wrote to the wrong name.

## Root cause

In `sandbox_write` (inside `make_sandbox_tools`):

```python
await sb.shell.run(f"cat > {path} << 'SANDBOX_EOF'\n{content}\nSANDBOX_EOF")
if executable:
    await sb.shell.run(f"chmod +x {path}")
```

`path` is concatenated into the command string without quoting or escaping. The heredoc quoting protects `content`, but the redirect target and the `chmod` argument are raw shell text.

## Suggested fix

Quote the path before it reaches the shell, and quote it once for every command that uses it:

```python
import shlex
q = shlex.quote(path)
await sb.shell.run(f"cat > {q} << 'SANDBOX_EOF'\n{content}\nSANDBOX_EOF")
if executable:
    await sb.shell.run(f"chmod +x {q}")
```

Preferably avoid the shell entirely and use the sandbox file API (`sb.fs.write(path, content)`) so the path is never parsed as shell syntax; validate that the path is absolute and normalizes inside the sandbox before writing.

title: sandbox_read passes the requested path to `head` through the shell, allowing command execution instead of a file read
body:
## Affected revision

- Repository: `trycua/cua`
- Location: `libs/python/cua-sandbox-apps/cua_sandbox_apps/pipeline/sandbox_tools.py:210`


## Summary

`sandbox_read` builds `head -n {max_lines} {path}` and runs it through the sandbox shell with the path concatenated in. A path containing a command separator runs that command inside the sandbox, and its output is returned to the caller as if it were the file's contents.

## Expected behavior

The tool should return the first `max_lines` lines of the file at `path` and nothing else. Shell metacharacters in `path` must be treated as part of the filename, not as shell syntax.

## Actual behavior

With the sandbox shell bound to a local shell that executes the command it is given:

```sh
$ python3 driver_read.py
read result: 941d1d1a3568
INJECTED-BY-PATH
```

The requested "file" was `/etc/hostname; echo INJECTED-BY-PATH`. `head` printed the hostname, and the appended `echo` ran as a separate command, so its output was returned to the caller as part of the file contents.

## Root cause

In `sandbox_read` (inside `make_sandbox_tools`):

```python
result = await sb.shell.run(f"head -n {max_lines} {path}")
```

`path` is interpolated into the shell command with no quoting or escaping, so `;`, `&&`, backticks, or `$()` in the path are executed by the sandbox shell.

## Suggested fix

Quote the path (and the numeric argument) before building the command:

```python
import shlex
result = await sb.shell.run(f"head -n {int(max_lines)} {shlex.quote(path)}")
```

Better, read the file through the sandbox file API (`sb.fs.read(path)`) and truncate in Python, so the path is never parsed by a shell. Also validate that the path is absolute and does not escape the sandbox root.

title: cua-driver: connect test second_run_is_idempotent_for_cursor_and_claude_already_exists is flaky (likely ETXTBSY on a just-written fake CLI)
body:
`connect::tests::second_run_is_idempotent_for_cursor_and_claude_already_exists` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/connect.rs` fails now and then on main, and passes on the next run:

- 21 Nov 05:47 UTC, CI: Nix Linux Rust source, run 44871634833 at 0f8165b4
- 20 Nov, CI: Rust Linux unit, at 8f484f30 (green on the next push)

```
panicked at crates/cua-driver/src/connect.rs:1198:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: Failed
 right: AlreadyConnected
```

The test writes a fake `claude` script with `fake_cli` and runs it at once. Neither diff touched `connect.rs`; its last change is #7190 (10 Nov).

**Likely cause (not reproduced):** `ETXTBSY`. `fake_cli` writes the script with `std::fs::write` and `chmod`s it, while other tests in the same process spawn children. A `fork` in another thread can inherit the still-open write descriptor, so `exec` of the new script fails with "Text file busy". `connect_agents` then reports `Failed` instead of reading the "already exists" stderr.

**Fix options:** retry the spawn on `ETXTBSY` in the test helper's runner, or have `fake_cli` write to a temp name and `rename` it into place (the descriptor is closed before the final path exists), or run the scripts through `sh <path>` so nothing execs a file just written. The rename is the smallest.

To reproduce: run `cargo test -p cua-driver connect::tests -- --test-threads=16` in a loop on Linux and count failures.

title: fix(cua-driver): make accepted HTTP sockets non-inheritable on Windows
body:
Salvaged from #6261 by @DaveTseng2019. Their three commits are kept as authored; two commits of ours sit on top.

## Summary

- Problem this solves: On Windows, sockets accepted by the MCP HTTP and driver service HTTP listeners are inheritable. A child spawned while a connection is open (every `std::process::Command` passes `bInheritHandles = TRUE`) keeps a copy of the socket, so the server's close sends no FIN, the client gets a reset (10054) once the child exits, and a long-lived child holds an authenticated connection. Several unit tests also failed on Windows checkouts.
- What changed:
  - `mcp_http::clear_inherit_flag` clears `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` right after `accept` in both HTTP listeners and the `mcp_http` test helpers. It is a no-op off Windows. A failure logs a warning and the connection is still served. Windows has no accept flag for this, and the listener is already created non-inheritable, so a child spawned on another thread between `accept` and the call can still inherit that one socket. The change narrows that race to a few instructions; it does not remove it.
  - New Windows test `mcp_http::tests::accepted_sockets_are_made_non_inheritable` reads the flag with `GetHandleInformation`: set after a tokio `accept`, clear after `clear_inherit_flag`. The Windows shard 3 lane now runs the whole `cua-driver` bin unit suite, so this test and the Windows-only test fixes below run in CI.
  - Under `cfg(test)`, `telemetry::spawn_payload` returns before it touches `PENDING_SENDS`, so a capture from another unit test can no longer make `pending_send_flush_waits_for_bounded_delivery` fail and poison `ENV_LOCK` for the other telemetry tests. The cleanup commit uses the file's existing `if cfg!(test)` idiom in place of a `#[cfg(test)]` block plus `#[allow(unreachable_code)]`.
  - `snapshot_dispatch_invariants`, `extension_manager_cli_test` and `active_perception_extension_resolves_owned_worker_arguments` compare paths component-wise and normalize CRLF, so they pass on Windows.

## Related work

#6261 links no issue.

RFC: not required. No public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, permission or cross-component contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only, and only when an HTTP port is configured. The named-pipe daemon already creates non-inheritable handles and is unchanged. The telemetry change is test-only.
- Risk and rollback: Low. Plain revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (SPDX headers, rustfmt, actionlint, image refs) and is signed off. Its build tier was left to CI.
- Manual or platform evidence: The contributor reported on Windows 11 x64 MSVC that `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver --locked --no-fail-fast` went from 4 failures on main to 0, and that `GetHandleInformation` showed the accepted socket as inheritable before the change. Not reproduced here: this host has no Windows.
- Known gaps or CI still required: The Windows test and the full `cua-driver` unit suite on Windows run in CI (`Rust Windows shard 3/3`). The race described above has no test.

title: feat(cua-driver): route Linux capture through LinuxRoutes
body:
Stacked on #8289 and #8436 (P13a, Linux desktop detection). Both branches are merged in here. #8339, the other prerequisite, is already on main.

## Why
Linux capture picked its backend through two hand-written cascades in `wayland/mod.rs`, plus an `is_wayland()` switch in `capture.rs`. This is the first `LinuxRoutes` table: each capability becomes an ordered list of named routes, chosen from the classified `Desktop`, and later P13 PRs add windows, focus, pointer, keyboard and overlay to the same table.

## What changed
- New `routes.rs` holds `LinuxRoutes`, the `LinuxCapture` trait, `Outcome` (`Done` / `Refused` / `NotApplicable`), and the pure selection functions `display_routes` and `window_routes`. The routes are built on first use and rebuilt by `desktop::reclassify()`.
- The old cascade steps are now `DisplayRoute` and `WindowRoute` variants. Their bodies (`impl … { fn run }` in `wayland/mod.rs`) are the old code moved over unchanged. A runtime check that used to skip a step now returns `NotApplicable`: niri attestation, a window KWin listed, GNOME helper availability, the KWin switch, an unreachable portal, and screencopy or ext-image-copy being unavailable. An early `return` is now `Done` or `Refused`.
- `wayland::screenshot_dispatch{,_with_pid}`, `screenshot_window_dispatch` and `screenshot_display_dispatch` are removed. Their callers use `routes().capture_window(xid, pid)` or `capture::screenshot_display_bytes()`, which now runs the display routes.

## Scope
This PR covers capture only. Windows/focus, pointer, keyboard, and overlay/readout stay where they are (P13c–f). X11 and XWayland each get one explicit route per kind: `X11Root` for the display, and `X11` for a window (the existing MIT-SHM → XGetImage → `import` chain, kept as one route so its combined error text stays the same). musl is unaffected, and no `!Send` worker moved.

## Tradeoffs
- The routes are chosen from the unattested `Desktop`. niri attestation stays a per-call check inside the `Niri` route, as before: probing at build time would move the socket probe and change when an `Unknown` probe is seen. That's why every non-injected Wayland compositor lists `Niri` first for display capture. For window capture, `Hyprland` still comes before `Niri`, matching the old order.
- A route that can never pass the call on is the last in its list: Hyprland window capture is `[KWin, Hyprland]` and injected is `[KWin, CuaCompositor]`. The old code reached nothing after those steps either.
- `Wayland(Injected)` stands in for the old `is_wayland() && is_inject_mode()`. Both read the same non-empty `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET`. The one difference is that the classification is cached until `reclassify()`, the same caching `is_wayland()` already had.

## Blast Radius
This touches every Linux capture caller: `get_window_state`, `get_desktop_state`, `zoom`, recording hooks, the action-frame check and the overlay capture. No behavior change is intended. The hermetic tests pin the route list for every `(Desktop, Compositor)` pair, plus the runner's done/refuse/pass-on rules. The existing tests for the crop fail-closed rule, GNOME helper terminality, KWin gating and the portal fall-through still run, now against the route bodies. The portal D-Bus integration test (`tests/portal_screenshot_cascade.rs`) drives the public entry point unchanged.

title: feat(cua-driver): route Linux desktop pointer input through LinuxRoutes
body:
Stacked on #8289, #8339, #8436 (P13a, Linux desktop detection) and #8470 (P13b, capture routes). All four branches are merged in. P13c's branch has no PR yet, so this PR doesn't include it.

## Why
Desktop-scope pointer input (`scope: "desktop"` on click, scroll, drag and move_cursor) picked its backend in two places. Each tool checked `is_wayland()` and then chose between a `wayland::*_desktop` function and an XTest call. Each of those functions then checked `is_inject_mode()` and used `with_libei_fallback`. This PR adds the pointer entry to `LinuxRoutes`: one ordered list, chosen from the classified `Desktop`, with X11 as an explicit entry.

## What changed
- `routes.rs` gains the `LinuxPointer` trait (`click_desktop`, `scroll_desktop`, `drag_desktop`, `move_cursor_desktop`), `DesktopPointerRoute` (`Injected`, `VirtualPointer`, `Libei`, `X11`) and the pure selection function `desktop_pointer_routes`. Native Wayland gets `[Injected, VirtualPointer, Libei]` (no `Libei` without `portal-input`). X11 and every XWayland desktop get `[X11]`.
- The route bodies (`impl DesktopPointerRoute` in `wayland/mod.rs`) are the old `wayland::{click,scroll,drag,move_cursor}_desktop` bodies and the tools' XTest branches, moved over. Those four functions are removed. `Injected` passes on unless `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` is set, and for drag and move it always passes on, as before. A missing virtual pointer passes on to `Libei` through `virtual_pointer_outcome`, which `libei_recovery` now uses as well, so the niri refusal and the no-feature error stay as they were.
- The callers in `tools/{click,scroll,drag,move_cursor}.rs` and the Edge setup checkbox click in `browser_setup_ui.rs` now go through `LinuxPointer`.

## Scope
This PR covers desktop-scope pointer input only. Window-targeted pointer input (click, double/right click, scroll, drag against a `window_id`) still picks its route in each tool. Those tools order the injector, Wayland and X11 differently: `click` checks Wayland before the injector, and `right_click` checks the injector first. Moving them is a separate change. This PR doesn't touch keyboard, overlay/readout (P13e–f), capture, windows or focus. No `!Send` worker moved, and musl is unaffected.

## Tradeoffs
- The tools still read `is_wayland()` for their result `path` label (`wayland_desktop` / `xtest`), for the refusal of modified clicks and drags on native Wayland, and, in `move_cursor`, to build the input space only on Wayland, as before. Making the routes return the label would change the result shape.
- `browser_setup_ui` used the Wayland desktop click on every non-X11 session, XWayland included. It keeps that behavior by building `LinuxRoutes` for `Wayland(compositor)` when the session is `XWayland(compositor)`.
- `Injected` stays first in the list and reads `is_inject_mode()` per call, as the old functions did, rather than relying on the cached `Compositor::Injected` classification.

## Blast Radius
This touches desktop-scope click, scroll, drag and move_cursor on every Linux desktop, plus the Microsoft Edge remote-debugging setup click. No behavior change is intended. The hermetic tests pin the pointer list for X11, every `XWayland(c)` and every `Wayland(c)`, with and without `portal-input`. The existing `niri_never_recovers_input_through_libei` test now runs through `virtual_pointer_outcome`.

- [x] `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib routes` on macOS, default features and `--features portal-input`: all 7 route-selection and runner tests pass. The Linux-only route bodies don't compile on this host (no X11 headers); CI builds them.

title: feat(cua-driver): route Linux keyboard through LinuxRoutes
body:
Stacked on #8470 (P13b, capture routes), which brings in #8289 and #8436 (P13a). #8339 is already on main. P13c and P13d have no open PR yet, so this branch does not include them.

## Why
The Wayland keyboard path picks its backend through three hand-written cascades in `wayland/mod.rs`, one each for typing, single keys and chords. This PR adds keyboard to the `LinuxRoutes` table from P13b as one ordered list of named routes, chosen from the classified `Desktop`.

## What changed
- `routes.rs` gains `KeyboardRoute` (`Injected`, `Niri`, `VirtualKeyboard`, `Wtype`), the `LinuxKeyboard` trait (`type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey`), the pure `keyboard_routes(desktop)`, and a `keyboard` list on `LinuxRoutes`. The list is rebuilt by `reclassify()` along with the capture lists.
- `type_into`, `press_into` and `chord_into` keep their early work (empty-text check, `typable_text`, window activation), then call `routes().type_text/press_key/hotkey`. The `is_inject_mode()` branches in `press_key_focused` and `hotkey_focused` become the `Injected` route.
- The route bodies (`impl KeyboardRoute` in `wayland/mod.rs`) are the old code, moved. A step that used to be skipped now returns `NotApplicable`: inject mode off or a window given, niri not attested, a failed virtual-keyboard chord, or a route that doesn't serve the operation. An early `return` becomes `Done` or `Refused`.

## Scope
This PR covers keyboard only. Capture (P13b) is unchanged. Windows/focus (P13c), pointer (P13d) and overlay/readout (P13f) are left alone. The niri keyboard session and the libei worker stay as they are, and no `!Send` worker moved. musl is unaffected.

It leaves out the tool-level choice between this Wayland cascade and X11 XTest (`press_key`/`hotkey` desktop scope, `browser_setup_ui`). Those callers gate on different predicates: the tools use `is_wayland()`, and `browser_setup_ui` uses `desktop() != X11`. They disagree on XWayland, so making them one route would change behavior.

## Tradeoffs
- `Injected` is listed on `X11`, `XWayland(Injected)` and `Wayland(Injected)`. `CUA_INJECT_SOCKET` classifies as `Injected` only next to a `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, while the old check read the variable on any desktop. The route body still reads it, so X11 with the variable set behaves as before.
- `Niri` is listed only on non-injected native Wayland, the only desktops where `niri::is_session()` can be true. Attestation stays a per-call check inside the route.
- A chord with no final key was refused before the niri check. The first non-injected route now runs `partition_modifiers` before anything else and refuses with the same error.
- `type_text_then_key_focused` has no callers and was left alone.

## Blast Radius
This touches every Wayland keyboard caller: `type_text`, `type_text_chars`, `press_key`, `hotkey`, and the browser setup flow on Wayland and XWayland. No behavior change is intended. The hermetic test pins the keyboard list for all nine `(Desktop, Compositor)` pairs, and a mutation check confirmed it fails when a list changes. P13b's runner test covers the done/refuse/pass-on rules.

title: fix(ci): assemble electron-windows in one upload so the Windows feed is never dropped
body:
The Spaces CD for cua-spaces-v0.41.2 failed in Electron publish with `no latest.yml`, leaving the v0.41.2 release a draft (0.41.1 stays Latest). Same failure hit v0.39.11.

Root cause: the `electron-windows` join job merged its artifact with `upload-artifact/merge` over `electron-windows-*`. That pattern also matches `electron-windows-feed`, uploaded seconds earlier in the same job. The artifact listing can lag, so the merge intermittently saw 2 artifacts instead of 3 (log: "The 2 artifact(s) have been successfully merged", versus 3 in every passing run). The joined `latest.yml` was then missing from `electron-windows`, and Electron publish failed its feed check.

Fix: the join job downloads the finished per-arch artifacts, writes the joined feed into the same directory and uploads `electron-windows` once. Nothing depends on listing an artifact that was just uploaded. Same installers, blockmaps, signing note and feed contents as before.

User impact: none yet. The v0.41.2 changes ship in the next release-please Spaces version (0.41.3), which this fix lets publish.

Checked: `bin/ci --quick --signoff` green (actionlint, workflow sync).

title: feat(cua-driver): route Linux overlay and cursor readout through LinuxRoutes
body:
Stacked on #8289 and #8339 (prereqs), and on the open P13 route PRs: #8436 (P13a, desktop detection), #8470 (P13b, capture), #8473 (P13d, pointer) and #8474 (P13e, keyboard). Their branches are merged in, not rebased. P13c (windows/focus) has no open PR yet, so it is not included. Merging #8289 into current main needed conflict resolution in `daemon.rs`, `serve.rs` and `ci-rust-windows.yml`: main already carries an earlier squash of #8289's presence work (#8444), so each conflict took #8289's newer side, and those three files now match #8289's branch exactly. #8473 and #8474 conflicted in `routes.rs` and the `wayland/mod.rs` import; I kept both sides.

## Why
The overlay dispatch and `get_cursor_position` still choose their backend with inline `is_wayland()` / `hyprland::is_session()` / `desktop() != X11` checks. This PR adds them to the `LinuxRoutes` table as two ordered route lists, chosen from the classified `Desktop`, so they follow the same pattern as the earlier capabilities.

## What changed
- `routes.rs` adds `LinuxOverlay` (`dispatch`) with `OverlayRoute { X11Owner, Wayland(WaylandOverlayBackend) }`, and `LinuxCursorReadout` (`cursor_position`) with `CursorReadoutRoute { Hyprland, LastSynthetic, X11 }` returning `CursorReadout { Compositor, X11, Unsupported { last_synthetic } }`. `overlay_routes` and `cursor_readout_routes` are pure functions, and `reclassify()` rebuilds both lists with the rest of `LinuxRoutes`.
- Overlay: `X11` → `[X11Owner]`; `XWayland(_)` → `[]` (no overlay, as before); `Wayland(_)` → the three Wayland backends in `select_wayland_overlay_backend`'s order. Each backend route applies only when it matches the backend probed once per process. `try_send_command_for` and the Wayland half of `remove_cursor`/`revive_cursor` go through `routes().dispatch()`. The bodies in `overlay.rs` are the old code, moved.
- Cursor readout: `X11 | XWayland(_)` → `[X11]`, `Wayland(Hyprland)` → `[Hyprland]`, any other native Wayland → `[LastSynthetic]`. Native Wayland readout stays explicitly unsupported: `CursorReadout::Unsupported` carries the last position this process synthesized, and the tool still labels it `source: "synthetic"`. The bodies (`impl CursorReadoutRoute` in `wayland/mod.rs`) are the old tool code, moved. Text, structured output and error messages are unchanged.

## Scope
This PR covers overlay dispatch and cursor readout only. Capture, pointer and keyboard routes are unchanged. The `!Send` workers in `wayland/overlay.rs` and `persistent_vptr.rs` stay as they are: routes hold only the existing `Send` channel (`CMD_TX`, `wayland::overlay::forward`). The cursor readout FFI stays in this crate (moving it to core is P17). Left out: the overlay's other `is_wayland()` reads (arrival budget, capture limitation), which aren't backend choices, and the unconditional X11-owner send in `remove_cursor`/`revive_cursor`. That send still goes out on every desktop, so an owner thread started before a reclassify still drops the cursor. musl is unaffected.

## Tradeoffs
- The Wayland overlay keeps its one-time probe (`wayland_overlay_backend()`'s `OnceLock`). The route list encodes the order, and each route checks the cached choice, so the D-Bus and layer-shell probes are not repeated per command.
- `Hyprland` readout is listed only on `Wayland(Hyprland)`. `hyprland::is_session()` is defined as `desktop().compositor() == Some(Hyprland)`, so this is the same predicate the tool used. It is terminal and never falls back to the synthetic position, as before.
- The tool now does one `spawn_blocking` for the whole readout where it used to do one per branch.

## Blast Radius
This touches every Linux agent-cursor command (the X11 owner, the GNOME Shell helper, the layer-shell overlay) and `get_cursor_position` on every Linux desktop. No behavior change is intended. Hermetic tests pin the overlay and readout lists for X11, XWayland and native Wayland with every compositor.

## Verification
- [x] `bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, headers and workflow sync pass. Cargo build, test and clippy were skipped on this shared host; the scoped repository checks run them.
- [x] `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib` and `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --tests` on macOS: 77 tests pass, including the 10 route tests, and clippy is clean. The Linux-only route bodies don't compile on this host (no Linux cross toolchain here), so CI builds them.
- [ ] Linux desktop lanes (Sway, Sway-XWayland, cua-compositor, niri, hosted X11, Hyprland; GNOME/KDE supporting) on the final candidate SHA.

title: fix(sandbox-apps): quote paths and use the file API in sandbox_read/sandbox_write
body:
Fixes #8465, fixes #8467. Thanks to soarkit for the report.

`sandbox_write` and `sandbox_read` built shell strings with the path unquoted (`cat > {path} << 'SANDBOX_EOF'`, `chmod +x {path}`, `head -n N {path}`). Paths with spaces or shell metacharacters broke or ran extra commands, content containing the heredoc terminator was cut short, `sandbox_write` always reported OK, and the `escaped` variable was dead code. A security review found no vulnerability (these tools sit behind the same in-process `sandbox_run` shell), but the code was wrong.

What changed for users: files with unusual names or content are now written and read exactly as given, and a failed write now says why.

- Both tools use `sb.files.write_text` / `sb.files.read_text`, with no shell. `sandbox_read` truncates to `max_lines` in Python.
- Only when an image lacks the file API do they fall back to shell: `shlex.quote`d paths, content carried as base64, `chmod -- +x`, and an encoded PowerShell branch for Windows.
- Failures, including `chmod`, return the real error.
- Removed the dead `escaped` variable.
- New tests (`libs/python/cua-sandbox-apps/tests/test_sandbox_tools.py`) cover paths and content with spaces, `;`, `$()`, backticks, quotes, a leading dash and the old `SANDBOX_EOF` terminator, on both the file-API and shell-fallback paths.

Test: `uv run --extra dev python -m pytest tests` in `libs/python/cua-sandbox-apps` (113 passed). `bin/ci --quick --signoff` is green.

title: fix(cua-driver): re-pin the macOS agent cursor overlay when the active app changes
body:
## What failed

The cua-driver-rs 0.56.5 release gate failed in the hosted macOS native lane, in `session_first_actions_show_pointer_and_badge_in_the_video`: "the coordinate click never showed its cursor for 5 frames". Both attempts failed. The same failure hit 0.55.5 once, and 0.56.0 to 0.56.4 passed, so it is intermittent. The driver code is identical between 0.56.4 and 0.56.5.

## Root cause

A foreground pixel click raises the target window over the normal-level cursor overlay, then hands the front back to the previous app. Both are asynchronous WindowServer changes. The single re-order issued right after them (`request_repin`) can land before they finish, so the overlay stays behind the target and nothing re-orders it, because the render loop is parked. The failing video shows the cursor vanish at the click and never return; a passing run shows it missing for one frame.

## Fix

The overlay is re-pinned on the event that changes the order: an `NSWorkspaceDidActivateApplicationNotification` observer requests a repin whenever another app is activated, after that activation has completed. There is no timer.

A higher fixed window level (status bar or floating) is not viable. The overlay is deliberately at the normal level and ordered directly above its target window, so it never paints over an unrelated foreground app during background actions, and it must appear in CGWindowList layer 0 for `list_windows`.

## Second cause (found from the first CI run on this PR)

The activation observer alone did not fix the hosted run. The test window is already the focused front window, so `with_foreground_hid_activation` returned early: no activation, so no activation event and no repin. The real HID click then makes WindowServer raise the clicked window over the overlay. That branch now re-orders the overlay after the event is delivered (the same 40 ms settle the other branch already waits).

## Verification

- New unit test: another app's activation requests a repin, this process's own does not. It does not compile without the fix.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix --signoff` is green (`local-ci = success`). The hosted macOS native lane runs the failing test on this PR.

For users: on macOS, the agent cursor no longer sometimes disappears after a foreground click.

title: [Feature]: macOS browser actions start lsof six times each
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On macOS, every browser action on an existing-profile Chrome starts `lsof` six times before Chrome receives anything. `lsof` costs little on an idle machine but grows with system load, so on a busy developer Mac it becomes most of the action's time.

Where the six come from, for one `browser_click` or `browser_type` in standard mode:

- The binding is proved three times: at dispatch by `authorize_attested_resource`, again by `validate_attested_resource`, then by the tool under its mutation lock (`revalidate_for_mutation`).
- Each proof re-proves the endpoint through `reprove_existing_profile_endpoint`, which runs `lsof -a -n -p PID -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -Fn -P` once, then again inside `active_port_endpoint` (`platform-macos/src/browser/platform.rs`).

Unrestricted mode skips the two dispatch proofs, so it spawns two.

| hosted `macos-26`, Chrome, standard mode `--grant existing-profile --no-overlay`, median of 20 calls, two runners | main `04d952f8c8` | listeners read through libproc |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `browser_click` (`input_route: dom_event`) | 565, 553 ms | 470, 454 ms |
| `browser_type` (`replace: true`) | 272, 253 ms | 178, 185 ms |
| `get_browser_state` (`semantic_v2`) | 55, 49 ms | 21, 15 ms |
| `browser_dialog` inspect | 104, 88 ms | 39, 37 ms |
| `browser_navigate` (5 calls) | 165, 136 ms | 91, 38 ms |

All 20 clicks and the last typed value were read back from the page in every run, with no refusal. [Run 44918186217](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44918186217), harness [`web_perf.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/ae5e51c563dc8effb9b89e01ed710058d2525f40/ab/web_perf.py).

On a developer Mac under load (load average about 110, macOS 26.7, arm64), one `lsof` against a process with a single loopback listener took a median of 2307 ms (1825 to 4227 ms, 7 runs). A C program making the same libproc calls took 30 to 41 ms, including its own process start. At that cost six spawns put an action in the 10 s range. That figure is an estimate from the per-spawn cost; I did not drive Chrome on that machine.

### Desired outcome

A browser action's binding proof costs the same on a busy Mac as on an idle one, and keeps exactly today's checks.

### Current workaround

None. `--permission-mode unrestricted` drops four of the six spawns along with the dispatch checks.

### Affected components and platforms

`platform-macos` browser endpoint discovery and re-proof (`loopback_ports_for_pid`) and the Electron/CDP helper `listening_ports`. macOS only: Linux reads `/proc` in-process.

### Alternatives and prior art

- The `lsof` listener proof came with #2257, the existing-profile re-proof with #2261, and the second spawn in `active_port_endpoint` with #2301.
- #3663: browser operations fail with `could not inspect browser listeners: Too many open files`. That message comes from the failed `lsof` spawn.
- #8066 bounds the same `lsof` with a timeout and kills it on cancel. That stops a hang, but not the cost.
- Keeping `lsof` but proving the binding once per action would remove four spawns, but it changes the permission dispatch. Reading listeners in-process keeps every check and removes all six spawns.

### Implementation ideas

#8481 reads the listeners through libproc in libSystem (`proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDLISTFDS)`, then `proc_pidfdinfo(PROC_PIDFDSOCKETINFO)` per socket), with the same filter: TCP, LISTEN, exactly `127.0.0.1` or `::1`. No subprocess, entitlement or new dependency. It also opens no descriptor, so the `Too many open files` error from #3663 cannot come from this check anymore.

- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.

title: perf(cua-driver): read macOS browser listeners through libproc instead of lsof
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS each browser action on an existing-profile Chrome starts `lsof` six times in standard mode (two in unrestricted) to re-prove the DevTools listener. `lsof` slows down with system load: on a busy developer Mac one spawn took a median of 2.3 s. See #8480 for where the six come from.
- What changed: the listening sockets of the browser process are read in-process through libproc in libSystem (`proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDLISTFDS)`, then `proc_pidfdinfo(PROC_PIDFDSOCKETINFO)` per socket descriptor). The filter is the same as before: TCP, LISTEN, local address exactly `127.0.0.1` or `::1`. Every check still runs, with the same refusal code and message. The Electron/CDP helper `listening_ports` uses the same read.

| hosted `macos-26`, Chrome, standard mode `--grant existing-profile --no-overlay`, median of 20 calls, two runners | main `04d952f8c8` | this PR `5881d4f047` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `browser_click` (`input_route: dom_event`) | 565, 553 ms | 470, 454 ms |
| `browser_type` (`replace: true`) | 272, 253 ms | 178, 185 ms |
| `get_browser_state` (`semantic_v2`) | 55, 49 ms | 21, 15 ms |
| `browser_dialog` inspect | 104, 88 ms | 39, 37 ms |
| `browser_navigate` (5 calls) | 165, 136 ms | 91, 38 ms |

| one listener lookup, developer Mac at load average about 110, 7 runs | median | range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lsof -a -n -P -p PID -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN` | 2307 ms | 1825 to 4227 ms |
| the same libproc calls, in a C program, including its process start | 30 to 41 ms | 21 to 68 ms |

## Related work

Fixes #8480

Refs #3663, #8066

RFC: not needed. No schema, tool, refusal or permission change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Browser actions get faster. A listener lookup can no longer fail with `Too many open files`, because it opens no descriptor (the `ps` fingerprint spawn still can, see #3663).
- Risk and rollback:
  - The C structs are declared in Rust with compile-time checks of their size and field offsets against `<sys/proc_info.h>` (`socket_fdinfo` 792 bytes, `soi_proto` at 240, `insi_laddr` at 48, `tcpsi_state` at 80).
  - Same answers as `lsof` on every listener macOS can bind: `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, including a dual-stack `::1`, are accepted; `0.0.0.0` and `::` are rejected. macOS refuses to bind `127.0.0.2` or `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, so those cannot occur.
  - A process that has exited, or belongs to another user, has no listeners (as with `lsof`), so the proof fails closed.
  - Conflicts with #8066 only on its `kill_on_drop` line for the `lsof` spawn, which this PR removes.
  - Rollback is a plain revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `browser::listeners::tests`: this process's v4, v6 and wildcard listeners are found by address and its connected socket is not; a missing pid has none.
  - On this PR's head, hosted runners: `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass on `macos-26` ([run 44924834096](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44924834096)); the tests pass on `macos-26-intel`. On `macos-15` the only failure is `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`, which fails on main too and is fixed by #7631 ([run 44923099079](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44923099079)).
- Manual or platform evidence: harness [`web_perf.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/ae5e51c563dc8effb9b89e01ed710058d2525f40/ab/web_perf.py) on hosted `macos-26`, each build bootstrapped by `scripts/ci/macos/run-hosted-rust-e2e.sh`. It attaches to a Chrome existing profile with `browser_prepare`, then repeats what `cua web` sends per command: `browser_dialog` inspect, `get_browser_state`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, then 5 `browser_navigate`. The page's click counter read 20 and the field held the last typed value in every run, with no refusal. [Run 44918186217](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44918186217) for the table; a second run on two more runners gave `browser_click` 507, 535 ms on main and 487, 486 ms here, `browser_type` 198, 235 ms and 188, 190 ms ([run 44922759221](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44922759221)).
- Known gaps or CI still required: no end-to-end browser run on a loaded Mac; the per-lookup cost there is measured on its own. `bin/ci` was not run.

title: [Feature]: browser_click waits 400 ms when the clicked element itself does not change
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

A `browser_click` with `input_route: "dom_event"` waits 400 ms after the click whenever the clicked element's own state does not change, then reports `effect: "unverifiable"`. Many buttons are like that: their handler changes another part of the page (a counter, a list, a dialog), or it sends a request. Agents pay the full 400 ms on each such click, and get back the same `unverifiable` they would get without waiting.

`observe_dom_click` (`cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs`) reads the target's `aria-pressed`, `aria-selected`, `aria-checked`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-current`, `aria-disabled`, `disabled`, `checked`, `value`, `innerText` and the document URL every 25 ms, up to `DOM_CLICK_READBACK_DEADLINE` (400 ms). A change returns `confirmed` at once. No change returns `unverifiable` at the deadline.

| hosted `macos-26`, Chrome, main `04d952f8c8`, `--no-overlay`, median of 20 clicks, two runners | standard mode | unrestricted mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| button whose handler updates a counter elsewhere on the page | 507, 535 ms | 446, 474 ms |
| button whose handler flips its own `aria-pressed` | 101, 141 ms | 48, 65 ms |

Both buttons took effect on every click: the counter read 20 at the end. [Run 44922759221](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44922759221). A third runner recorded each click's result: the counter button returned `unverifiable` 20 of 20 times, with the hint to read the page again with `get_browser_state`, and the toggle returned `confirmed` 20 of 20 times ([run 44925866256](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44925866256), harness [`web_perf.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/adfb77bfc6f04bf0f12935f671acd16f05b96b22/ab/web_perf.py)).

### Desired outcome

A click that changes the page returns once the change is seen, and a target whose own state changes is still reported `confirmed`.

### Current workaround

None: the trusted route, given a ref, waits on the same readback.

### Affected components and platforms

`cua-driver-core` browser click (`dom_event` route, and the trusted route's ref readback). All platforms.

### Alternatives and prior art

- #2956, merged as #5586, added the readback to tell a click that visibly changed its target from one whose effect cannot be seen. The 400 ms window gives an asynchronous handler time to change the target.
- A shorter fixed window would also cut the wait, but a handler that awaits a request would be confirmed less often.

### Implementation ideas

Two shapes, for maintainers to choose:

1. Stop waiting at the first change anywhere in the document (a `MutationObserver` on the document, plus the URL that is already read), and still report `unverifiable` unless the target itself changed. The result schema stays the same. The cost: a target that changes after an unrelated change elsewhere is no longer confirmed, and on a page that mutates all the time (a clock, an animation) almost no click is.
2. Let the caller set the window (for example `readback_ms`, default 400). Callers that read the page state after every action anyway could pass 0. This adds a parameter to a public tool, so it probably needs an RFC.

I can measure either against the harness above before a PR.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop Linux type_text and set_value writing past a Qt line edit validator
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On Linux, background typing or setting a value into a Qt line edit put in text its validator rejects and reported it confirmed.
- What changed: Qt applies an accessibility write to a single-line field as `setText`, skipping its validator; neither typing nor `set_value` sends it any more.

## Related work

Fixes #7327. Split from #8188, the key route, which builds on this. RFC: not required.

## Compatibility and risk

Review first: `native.rs::editable_write_toolkit` and its callers.

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux only. In the background, `type_text` by token into a Qt line edit or spin box refuses until #8188 lands, and `set_value` there types keys, which needs a writable `/dev/uinput` or else refuses with `set_value_unavailable`, which #8188 does not change; foreground works for both.
- Risk and rollback: two commits.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: production +92/-32, tests +199/-4; each commit's tests fail without it.
- Manual or platform evidence: supporting: `main` wrote `AB` 40/40; now refused 120/120, and `set_value` `AB` leaves it empty 18/18. PyQt test passes at this head (real Xorg, Xvfb; Qt5, Qt6).
- Known gaps or CI still required: no runner selects the PyQt test; KDE X11, E2E not run.

<details>
<summary>Before and after, commands</summary>

Release note (Release Please reads this override from the body):

BEGIN_COMMIT_OVERRIDE
fix(cua-driver): stop Linux type_text and set_value writing past a Qt line edit validator; in the background, type_text by token into Qt line edits and spin boxes refuses until #8188 lands, and set_value there needs a writable /dev/uinput or else refuses with set_value_unavailable, which #8188 does not change (foreground works for both)
END_COMMIT_OVERRIDE

Background `type_text` into an unfocused PyQt window while a simulated user types into a focused GTK window. 40 tries per cell = 10 each of Qt6 and Qt5, `QLineEdit` + `QIntValidator` and `QSpinBox`.

| X server | build | `12` | `AB` | `1a2` | user kept activation, focus and every key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| real Xorg | `main` (AT-SPI `EditableText` write) | field holds `12`, 40/40 | holds `AB`, 40/40 | holds `1a2`, 40/40 | 120/120 |
| Xvfb | this change (`cc63c45c5`, the same refusal before the re-resolve guard in `atspi/mod.rs`) | refused, field unchanged, 40/40 | refused, 40/40 | refused, 40/40 | 120/120 |

The `main` row is from a probe build with that route selected by hand on a real Xorg guest (Ubuntu 24.04, mutter); the refusal row ran on Xvfb + openbox.

PyQt test (`type_text_qt_line_edit_xorg`) at this head, one run each on a real Xorg guest and on Xvfb + openbox, Qt6 and Qt5:

| call | result |
| --- | --- |
| background `AB` / `12` into the line edit and the spin box | `background_unavailable` naming `setText`; field unchanged; focused field unchanged |
| background `AB` into a `QPlainTextEdit` | `confirmed`, field reads `AB` (accessibility write, unchanged) |
| foreground `AB` / `12` into the line edit | field reads empty / `12` (real keys) |

The fixture test `typing_sends_no_write_to_a_qt_single_line_field` drives `insert_text` and `type_into_editable_at` against a scripted AT-SPI app for toolkit Qt, GTK and none, single- and multi-line: only Qt single-line receives no write and fails with `QtLineEditSetsText`.

Mutation check: with the three-line guard in `write_into_editable_acc` removed (the error type kept, so the tests build), the fixture test panics on `unwrap_err` and the PyQt test fails on its first row: background `AB` into the line edit answers `confirmed` and the field holds `AB`.

`set_value` had its own `EditableText` write (`set_value_on`: `SetTextContents`, then `InsertText`), outside `write_into_editable_acc`. The second commit sends both through `editable_write_toolkit`, so a Qt single-line field gets no accessibility write from either; `set_value` then takes its existing keyboard route (click, select all, type, Tab), on the session's virtual pointer and keyboard in the background. The length helper only the old `set_value` path used is removed; its deadline tests now run against the composition both writes use.

Background `set_value` into the probe form (Qt line edit + `QIntValidator`, `QSpinBox`, plain line edit) with a GTK window active; field = what the widget holds after the call. Qt5 and Qt6, equal counts each.

| X server | build | line edit `AB` | line edit `12` | spin box `1a2` | spin box `12` | user's window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Xvfb | first commit only | `AB`, `confirmed`, 10/10 | `12`, `confirmed` | shows `1a2`, value 0, `suspected_noop` | `12`, `confirmed` | text unchanged 50/50 |
| real Xorg | first commit only | `AB`, `confirmed`, 4/4 | `12`, `confirmed` | shows `1a2`, `suspected_noop` | `12`, `confirmed` | still active, text unchanged, 20/20 |
| real Xorg | both commits | empty, `suspected_noop`, 4/4 | `12`, `confirmed` | `12`, `suspected_noop` | `12`, `confirmed` | still active, text unchanged, 20/20 |
| Xvfb | both commits | `set_value_unavailable` (no `/dev/uinput`), field unchanged, 10/10 | same | same | same | text unchanged 50/50 |

Foreground `set_value` at both commits, Xvfb, 6 per cell (Qt5 and Qt6): line edit `AB` empty, `suspected_noop`; `12` `confirmed`; spin box `1a2` holds `12`, `suspected_noop`. Qt5 and Qt6 agree in every row. Mutation check: with `src` at the first commit, `no_write_reaches_a_qt_single_line_field` panics on `unwrap_err` and the PyQt test fails at `set_value put "AB" past the validator`.

Why the check sits in the shared write: the token route, the focused-field route and the walk fallback all end in `write_into_editable_acc`, so no typing route sends `setText` to a single-line field of an app whose toolkit name reads as Qt. Calls without an element token keep their existing key routes after the refused write. If the toolkit name cannot be read, ASCII text still takes the write, as on `main`.

From `libs/cua-driver/rust`:

```sh
dbus-run-session -- xvfb-run -a bash -c '(openbox &); sleep 1;
  CUA_TEST_QT=6 cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --test type_text_qt_line_edit_xorg -- --ignored --nocapture'

env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u XAUTHORITY -u AT_SPI_BUS_ADDRESS \
  -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS -u NO_AT_BRIDGE \
  dbus-run-session -- env CUA_PRIVATE_ATSPI_TEST=1 \
  cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --test set_value_fallback -- \
  --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1

cargo test --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets
cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

title: [Bug]: On Chrome, the driver's Allow press on the remote-debugging prompt can be ignored, and browser_prepare waits 150 s per prompt
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On Windows, the driver accepts the browser's remote-debugging prompt with one UI Automation Invoke on Allow, then reports it accepted without checking that the prompt closed. Chrome ignores a press on the prompt that comes within 500 ms of a previous press. When a person pressed the prompt shortly before the driver did, Chrome ignores the driver's press, the prompt stays open, and `browser_prepare` waits out the 150 s handshake timeout, once per prompt.

### Reproduction

1. Chrome's default profile, remote debugging turned on.
2. `browser_prepare` with `strategy.kind: "existing_profile"`.
3. Press Cancel on the prompt 200 or 400 ms after it appears. Chrome ignores this press too, because it comes within 500 ms of the prompt appearing.

Harness: [`consent_dismiss.py`](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/blob/61132f096de8026b2dd51218c5a1bb812944a4ef/ab/consent_dismiss.py), which finds the prompt through UI Automation and presses a button at a set delay.

### Expected behavior

Within a few seconds, the driver's Allow takes effect, or the driver reports that the prompt is still open.

### Actual behavior

| Windows 11 arm64, Chrome 157.0.8103.79, 3 runs per row | main `fcc16ebb62` | #7678 `2500d80c49` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cancel at 0 ms | attached about 0.5 s after the press (3 of 3) | attached about 0.5 s after the press (3 of 3) |
| Cancel at 200 ms | attached after 152 s (1 of 3), `browser_reconnect_exhausted` after 301 s (2 of 3) | attached after 152 s (2 of 3), `browser_reconnect_exhausted` after 301 s (1 of 3) |
| Cancel at 400 ms | attached after 152 s (1 of 3), `browser_reconnect_exhausted` after 301 s (2 of 3) | `browser_reconnect_exhausted` after 301 s (3 of 3) |

152 s is one `CONSENT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` (150 s) and 301 s is two. A driver that had not pressed would have stopped at the 120 s `PERSON_CONSENT_BOUND` instead. At 0 ms, the driver's press comes more than 500 ms after the person's and takes effect.

Chrome's rule, measured without the driver: a script opens a DevTools WebSocket upgrade and presses the prompt by UI Automation Invoke, 2 runs per cell.

| first press | second press | upgrade answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | Cancel 450 to 700 ms after the prompt appears | `403 Forbidden` (10 of 10) |
| Cancel at 0, 200 or 400 ms (ignored) | Allow 300 ms later | none within 20 s (6 of 6) |
| Cancel at 0, 200 or 400 ms (ignored) | Allow 500, 700 or 1000 ms later | `101` (18 of 18) |

Even 700 ms after the prompt appears (400 + 300), a press 300 ms after an ignored one is ignored. That matches [`DefaultInputProtectionPolicy::IsPossiblyUnintendedInteraction`](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main/ui/views/input_protection/default_input_protection_policy.cc). It rejects an event within one double-click interval of the previous event, or of the dialog appearing. Edge 157 applies the rule to mouse clicks but not to UI Automation Invoke: Invoke took effect at every delay from 0 ms, 20 of 20. So the driver's own press is affected on Chrome only.

The path on main `0adc9a8d19`:

- [`browser_consent_ui.rs#L473-L476`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/0adc9a8d19fd94681c1ad4f7aa1b57b96c79c37f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/browser_consent_ui.rs#L473-L476) invokes Allow and returns `Accepted`.
- [`prepare.rs#L272`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/0adc9a8d19fd94681c1ad4f7aa1b57b96c79c37f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/prepare.rs#L272) then waits for the claim, bounded by [`CONSENT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/0adc9a8d19fd94681c1ad4f7aa1b57b96c79c37f/libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/cdp_ws.rs#L38).

### Environment

- cua-driver main `fcc16ebb62` and #7678 `2500d80c49`, release builds. The code path is unchanged on main `0adc9a8d19`.
- Windows 11 arm64 (GitHub-hosted `windows-11-arm`), Chrome 157.0.8103.79, Edge 157.0.4341.46.

### Evidence

- [Run 44935476017](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44935476017): the driver rows above.
- [Run 44944602115](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44944602115): Chrome's rule without the driver.
- [Run 44943644338](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/44943644338): Chrome and Edge, Invoke and mouse click, without the driver.

### Workaround and additional context

- No workaround for the caller: the wait happens inside one call.
- One possible fix: after the Invoke, read the tree until the prompt is gone. If it is still there after one double-click interval (`GetDoubleClickTime`), refuse at once or press again. Whether the driver may press Allow again after a person's press, even an ignored one, is a consent question for a maintainer.
- Found while answering the Chrome question in #8459.
