title: perf(cua-driver): test page occlusion only against the boxes that can occlude
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `get_browser_state` with `snapshot_format: "semantic_v2"` takes seconds to tens of seconds on dense pages (social feeds, long threads), on one core. On the pages measured below (two captured x.com pages, and a synthetic feed's first reads), nearly all of it is `apply_page_occlusion`. For every eligible in-viewport node it scans up to every layout node and calls `DomIndex::shares_dom_branch` first. That call is up to two ancestor walks, each allocating a `HashSet`, and it runs before the cheap paint-order, position, pointer-events, hidden and bounds tests. The cost grows with in-viewport nodes × layout nodes × DOM depth.
- What changed: the layout nodes that can occlude anything (a paint order, fixed or absolute, taking pointer events, not hidden, with an area) are collected once per occlusion pass (once for each frame a read composes). Each target is then tested only against them, with the DOM walk last, for an overlay that actually covers it. When no overlay qualifies, the function returns at once. Every node's visibility is the same as before.

## Related work

Refs #3661: its commit f13a4f9ca (0xjohnnydev) moved `shares_dom_branch` after the other tests, which is the first half of this change. That commit lives in a draft about the DevTools port, which has a `conflict` label and no review. This PR is the occlusion change alone, on today's `main`, and also takes the target-independent tests out of the per-target loop: 34 to 351 times faster than the reorder alone across six synthetic cases (34× in the one where an overlay covers the targets). The test extends #3661's fixture, so its author is a co-author of the commit.

Refs #6299: 31–34 s `semantic_v2` reads on Google Flights, measured after a local workaround of the CDP frame limit, put down to "processing in the driver", with no profile. I have not verified that those reads are this cost.

RFC: not needed. No contract changes: every node's visibility is the same (see the caveat below).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none beyond speed. Every node's `visibility` (`page_occluded` or not) is identical. One caveat: outline lines that share a `document_order` already come out in no fixed order (the outline sort is stable over a `HashSet`'s order, and creating fewer `HashSet`s changes the thread's hash seed sequence). Their relative order may differ from before, as it already could between runs.
- Risk and rollback: one function, plus a test. A revert restores the old behaviour.

## Validation

- **Focused tests and checks:** `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::semantic` gives 13 passed, among them the existing `fixed_painted_overlay_marks_covered_action_as_page_occluded` and `dialog_container_does_not_occlude_its_own_actions`. `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- **New test:** `page_occlusion_tests_each_control_against_the_boxes_that_can_cover_it` checks the rules on 4,096 static boxes painted above 64 controls. It covers:
  - a fixed header that covers some of them;
  - an unrelated absolute box that covers one;
  - a fixed box with `pointer-events: none`, which covers none;
  - an absolute box that is a control's own ancestor, which does not cover it.

  It checks behaviour, not time, so it passes on the old code too. There it takes about 10 s in a debug build; on this change it takes 0.02 s. The speed itself is not asserted by a test, since a timing assertion would be flaky on shared CI runners; the numbers below are the evidence.
- **Equivalence:**
  - In the tests, `page_occlusion_marks_every_node_as_before_overlays_were_collected_once` keeps the old function unchanged and runs both over 2,000 generated pages (fixed seed). The pages have:
    - DOM forests, with nodes missing from the DOM or the layout;
    - every `position`, and `pointer-events` set to `none` or `auto`;
    - `display`, `visibility` and `opacity` that hide or do not;
    - boxes without bounds, area or paint order, on a coarse grid so that they often cover, touch or match;
    - nodes in and out of the viewport, some without a backend node.

    Every node's visibility must be the same in both, and the pages must occlude over 300 nodes. The test fails on each of four deliberate breaks of the new pass: dropping the DOM-branch test, `>=` for the paint order, letting `pointer-events: none` occlude, and letting hidden boxes occlude.
  - On two captured x.com pages, `compose_accessibility_tree` with the old and the new function gave the same `(ax_id, visibility)` for every node it kept.
  - A 200,000-case random comparison of the old predicate, the new one, and a reference with no short-circuiting covered missing ids, parent cycles, `None` paint orders, `i64` limits, NaN, ±inf and odd styles. All three agreed in every case.
- **Timing, the function alone** (release build without LTO, one core, two captured x.com pages):

  | Page | DOM nodes | Old | New |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 1,265 | 3,089 ms | 1.09 ms |
  | 2 | 1,425 | 4,449 ms | 1.09 ms |

- **Timing, the whole read** (`get_browser_state`, `semantic_v2`, end to end through MCP), on 0.56.9:
  - **Binaries:** the release binary (`cua-driver-rs-0.56.9-linux-x86_64-binary.tar.gz`) against the same source with this change, built on `rust:1.100.0-trixie` (Debian 13) with the toolchain the workspace pins and a command comparable to the release's (`cargo build --locked --release -p cua-driver -p cursor-theme-cli -p cua-driver-sdk --features cua-driver/portal-input`, without its explicit `--target`). The release binary is built on Debian 11, so this is a binary-to-binary comparison, not a same-environment one.
  - **Setup:** each process limited to 0.5 CPU, on a Linux host (x86_64, Debian 13), against the same Chrome page, in alternating turns.
  - **Page:** a synthetic feed of posts, each with an avatar, links, text and four buttons, under a fixed header and a fixed nav, and nested about 30 elements deep as a framework would. At every size, both binaries said the same of the first piece and of the whole page, its first piece and every continuation. They were compared once each driver's own identifiers (tab and target ids, the read number in refs and in the summary, continuation tokens) were taken out.
  - **Results:** a first read was 14–16× faster at every size, and the whole page 6–10× (each continuation costs both about the same):

    | Posts | Semantic snapshot nodes | Release, first piece (median) | This change | Whole page (release → this change) |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | 50 | 1,162 | 4.32 s | 0.27 s | 4.43 s → 0.42 s |
    | 100 | 2,312 | 8.85 s | 0.57 s | 9.14 s → 0.97 s |
    | 200 | 4,612 | 17.90 s | 1.24 s | 19.36 s → 2.42 s |
    | 400 | 9,212 | 36.39 s | 2.38 s | 40.57 s → 6.82 s |

  - **Live pages, at the same CPU:** `x.com/notifications` took 18–23 s with the release and 0.40–0.47 s with this change. A single x.com post took 6.2–7.3 s and 0.17–0.19 s. The answers were the same size.
- **Known gaps or CI still required:** I have not run `bin/ci` locally. This was built and tested from a sparse checkout of `libs/cua-driver/rust`, `libs/cua` and `libs/images`, and `--signoff` is not available from a fork. The sign-off path for a fork is a green `CI: Quick` run on this PR's head, which needs a maintainer's approval for a first-time contributor.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (Not applicable: this is meant to release as a `perf` patch.)
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). (See "Known gaps".)

title: feat(cua-driver): discover and invoke macOS menu extras by exact label
body:
Fixes #3301

Salvaged from #3304

## Why
Agents reach macOS menu extras (Wi-Fi, sound, Control Center, a third-party status item) through a screenshot and fixed coordinates, because `invoke_menu` only walks an application's `AXMenuBar` for an exact window. This adds the two tools #3301 proposes: they address an application's `AXExtrasMenuBar` by exact labels, with no window target and no pixel fallback. The implementation is @mwildehahn's from #3304, kept as their commits and ported onto current main.

## What changed
- `get_menu_extra_state` (read-only, capability `accessibility.menu_extra.observe`) returns a bounded tree of one running application's extras menu bar. `invoke_menu_extra` (capability `accessibility.menu_extra.invoke`) presses an exact 1–16 label path. Each hop re-resolves from the live root, untitled `AXMenu` containers are transparent, and a same-process popup such as Control Center's is searched once the menu-bar hop opened it. Targets are an exact `pid` or a `bundle_id` that must match exactly one running process. Missing, duplicate, disabled, foreign-owner, permission and limit failures each refuse with their own code.
- On top of #3304: targets resolve from the process table, not AppKit's running-application cache, which a long-lived daemon never refreshes (main already reads `list_running_apps` this way). A path that fails after pressing a hop now closes the menu it opened and says so in the refusal, as `invoke_menu` does. An intermediate press that times out while its menu opens is not treated as a failure, because the next hop resolves from live state.
- The AppKit harness gets an opt-in `NSStatusItem` (`CUA_APPKIT_STATUS_ITEM=1`), and the new background cell `macos-appkit-invoke-menu-extra-ax-background` runs `harness_appkit_invoke_menu_extra_exact_path_background`.

## Scope
macOS only. The contract publishes both tools with `platforms: ["macos"]`, so Windows and Linux do not advertise them; that is how the manifest marks the limitation. A notification-area or status-notifier adapter is left for a later RFC, as #3301 says. `invoke_menu` is unchanged except that its `choose_action` is shared.

## Tradeoffs
- #3301 suggests that Windows and Linux register the tools and return `unsupported_platform`. This keeps the repository's existing per-platform contract instead: a tool missing from a platform's manifest is already the published "unavailable".
- The invoke result stays `unverifiable`, and becomes `partial` when the frontmost app or focused window changed during the call. The caller confirms the effect from fresh state.

## Blast Radius
Additive: two new tools, two new SDK methods, a new opt-in fixture path. Existing tool schemas are unchanged. Both tools are R2 operation-sensitive, and recordings keep only the path length, never its labels.

## Verification
The scoped repository checks that ran on this host (a shared host, so no driver build): `bin/ci --quick` passed, and `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract` passed (69 tests). The Swift fixture typechecks with `swiftc -parse-as-library -typecheck`. The platform build, UniFFI bindings, generated reference docs and the macOS E2E cell run in CI and in the verifier's VM lane.

title: ci(spaces): stop the Rust dependency cache missing for PRs (unblocks #8486)
body:
Refs #8486

## What users see
The release bot's "bundle Cua Driver" PR (#8486) could never go green: its "Cua Spaces app library (built once)" check ran for an hour or more and was cancelled by the next bot force-push, every time.

## Root cause
- The step "Restore main's compiled library, or build on top of main's dependency cache" found no cache. Main's compiled slice is keyed by the whole `libs/cua` tree, so a PR merged onto a moving main usually misses it (by design). The fallback is main's Rust dependency cache (Swatinem/rust-cache), and that one never matched either.
- rust-cache hashes every `CARGO*` variable into its key. `ci-cua-spaces-macos.yml` sets `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`, `CARGO_NET_RETRY`, `CARGO_HTTP_TIMEOUT` and `CARGO_HTTP_MULTIPLEXING`; the producer on main does not. The two computed different env hashes (`62005a91` vs `5e16ab0e`; the lockfile hash `d04ef6bf` was identical), so the PR built the whole dependency tree cold (run 44976120494, 57 min and still compiling).

## Fix
Blank those four variables for the rust-cache step in `.github/actions/spaces-rust-slice/action.yml`, so every caller (PR CI, producer, release) computes the same dependency-cache key. They only change how a build runs, not what it produces, and the build step still sets `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` itself. Variables that do change output (`RUSTFLAGS`) still key the cache. The producer's key is unchanged, so main's existing cache stays valid.

No retries, no longer timeouts.

## Check
The `ffi` job on this PR should log "Restored from cache key ... v0-rust-swiftui-rust-aarch64-apple-darwin-Darwin-arm64-5e16ab0e-d04ef6bf" and compile only the changed crates. After it merges, #8486's next run should do the same.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the macOS agent cursor under a window covering its background target
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, after a background click, the agent cursor sometimes shows on top of the window in front instead of staying with its target behind it (#3332).
- What changed: the overlay's fallback raise (`orderFrontRegardless` in `dispatch_pin_above`) used to run whenever NSWorkspace said the target's app was active. A background pixel click first runs a focus-without-raise prologue (`prepare_background_pixel_click`), and that makes NSWorkspace report the target app active while its window stays behind the user's. The click then re-pins the overlay, and the fallback raised it above every window. Now `target_is_frontmost_visible_window` also refuses the raise when another app's on-screen window above the target overlaps it. The overlay's own windows are left out of that stack. `overlap_area` moved from `bring_to_front.rs` to `windows.rs` so both callers share it.

The overlay is still ordered directly above its target with `orderWindow:relativeTo:`. Only the fallback raise changes.

## Related work

Fixes #3332

RFC: not needed. This changes how the overlay is stacked, not a contract.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible: macOS only. The agent cursor stays under a window that covers its background target. Windows and Linux have their own overlay ordering and are not touched.
- Tradeoff: the existing test assumed WindowServer can briefly list another app's window ahead of a target that is really frontmost, and so it trusted the active app over the stack (#2493). If that happens, the overlay now skips the fallback raise for that frame and stays behind the target until the next repin. The activation observer from #8478 and the periodic repin re-check it. A cursor hidden for a moment is a better failure than one painted over the user's window.
- Rollback: revert this PR.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `frontmost_target_can_raise_overlay_without_covering_another_app` now covers both cases: another app's window ahead that overlaps the target blocks the raise, and one ahead that doesn't overlap does not. The test commit comes before the fix. The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) pass. The crate was not compiled or tested locally: the build host is under the disk threshold for heavy checks, so CI's macOS lanes run them.
- Manual or platform evidence: the cause comes from reading the code (`click.rs` sends `PinAbove` right after `prepare_background_pixel_click`, and `restore_user_focus_after_background_pixel` documents the NSWorkspace report). It was not reproduced live: the host's installed driver timed out and screen capture was unavailable.
- Known gaps or CI still required: macOS native lanes in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): slow macOS permission probes while a grant stays off
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: #3523 reported a new `cua-driver` process about every second, each making its own `TCCAccessRequest()` call, while tool calls kept returning `permissions_pending`. Those processes are the macOS permission gate's status probes. macOS caches a "no" in the process that asked, so each check runs in a fresh copy of the executable. While a grant stays off, the gate started one probe per second for 10 minutes, then one every 5 s for as long as the daemon ran.
- What changed: a shared `PollSchedule` (`permissions/guide.rs`) decides when the next check is due. The terminal wait (`gate::wait_for_grants_with`) and the guide window's 1 s timer (`panel::tick`) both use it.
  - Interactive (`PollCadence::INTERACTIVE`): every second for 30 s after something happens, every 5 s otherwise. "Something happens" means the wait starts, the status changes (a switch turned on), or the person clicks Open System Settings.
  - After the interactive deadline (`GateOpts::after_timeout`): every 30 s instead of every 5 s, still with no deadline, so a late grant still opens tool calls without a restart (#6739).
  - `GateOpts::poll_interval` is replaced by `GateOpts::poll: PollCadence`. Nothing outside `gate.rs` read it.

## Related work

Fixes #3523

Scope: this covers the probe churn. Two other parts of the report are already handled on main or can't be reproduced:
- Grants that read as off while System Settings shows them on: the report's daemon was attributed to the app that launched it. `responsibility::reexec_disclaimed_if_needed` now relaunches `serve` as its own responsible process, so its probes read Cua Driver's own grants.
- The MCP `initialize` hang ("daemon did not acknowledge the MCP control session") was not reproduced. On main, `session_begin` is answered before the permission gate's check, and the accept loop does no slow work.

Left out: listening for the `com.apple.accessibility.api` distributed notification to check right after an Accessibility change. Whether macOS still posts it for a System Settings toggle can't be confirmed without a person flipping the switch. The backoff stands on its own.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: macOS only. Once 30 s pass with nothing happening, a switch turned on in System Settings can take up to 5 s to show in the guide or terminal (was 1 s). A grant made after the 10-minute gate deadline can take up to 30 s to open tool calls (was 5 s). Linux and Windows are not affected.
- Risk and rollback: the probes, requests, the guide's step logic and the daemon-side gating are unchanged; only when a probe runs changes. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `checks_are_quick_only_for_a_while_after_something_happens` (guide.rs) steps a `PollSchedule` through 120 synthetic seconds with activity at 60 s and asserts the exact gaps between checks, for both the interactive and the steady after-timeout cadence. The existing `wait_after_timeout_picks_up_a_late_grant` and `opt_out_short_circuits_run_if_needed` now use `PollCadence::steady`. `cargo check -p platform-macos --tests` passed locally, and `bin/ci --quick` passed (fmt, SPDX headers, image refs).
- Manual or platform evidence: `log stream --predicate 'process == "cua-driver"'` on macOS showed that `cua-driver status` and `list-tools` make no TCC calls and that each `--cua-internal-permission-probe` child makes them. So every TCC line in the report came from a gate probe.
- Known gaps or CI still required: unit tests and clippy run in the scoped repository checks and CI, not on this shared host. Counting probe PIDs against a real ungranted daemon needs a disposable macOS permission state, since a gated daemon raises TCC prompts and opens System Settings.

title: cua-driver-rs background mode fails on classic Win32 Notepad and WinForms controls on a non-input desktop
body:
## Environment

- cua-driver-rs 0.47.7 and 0.57.0. Results were the same on both versions for every finding below. Release: https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.57.0
- Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045
- The app runs on a separate Win32 desktop made with CreateDesktopW and started with STARTUPINFO.lpDesktop. This is not the input desktop, and no Explorer runs on it. The measured foreground HWND on that desktop is 0x0.
- Notepad is classic Win32 notepad.exe at C:/Windows/System32/notepad.exe.
- A scripted test harness drives the apps through the MCP server over stdio. Each step ran 3 times.

Related: #6823

## a. hotkey refuses Ctrl+S, Ctrl+A and Ctrl+H on classic Notepad

Call: `hotkey(keys=['ctrl','s'], delivery_mode='background')`

Error:
```
RuntimeError: hotkey failed: hotkey on a modern XAML / UWP target (pid ..., hwnd ...) could not find a UIA AcceleratorKey or (Ctrl+X)-style name hint matching ctrl+s (scanned 27 element(s)).
```
(pid and hwnd values elided here.) The same error appears for `ctrl+a` and `ctrl+h`.

Repro: start notepad.exe on the desktop, make it the target window, and make the call above. The error reports the target as a modern XAML/UWP window. Classic Win32 notepad.exe is not one.

Result: 0 of 3 reps passed for Save (Ctrl+S), Select All (Ctrl+A), and Replace (Ctrl+H), on both versions.

Another tool: it sends WM_KEYDOWN and WM_KEYUP with modifier state straight to the target window, with no activation.

## b. press_key drops the modifier in background mode

Calls:
- `press_key(key='a', modifiers=['ctrl'], delivery_mode='background')`, then `press_key('delete')`, then `type_text(...)`

Error after the text check:
```
AssertionError: Editor value 'aFresh text after Ctrl+A DeleteLD_CONTENT_TO_DELETE' != 'Fresh text after Ctrl+A Delete'
```
The value starts with a literal 'a'. Text that should have been deleted remains.

- `press_key(key='s', modifiers=['ctrl'], delivery_mode='background')`
  Error: `TimeoutError: No new dialog window appeared for pid=... title_sub='Save'`
- `press_key(key='e', modifiers=['alt'], delivery_mode='background')`, then `press_key(key='r', delivery_mode='background')`
  Error: `TimeoutError: No new dialog window appeared for pid=... title_sub='Replace'`

Repro: start notepad.exe on the desktop and make each call above. The Alt+E, R sequence opens no dialog.

Another tool: it sends the key with modifier state in the key message (WM_KEYDOWN with modifier state).

## c. click on a WinForms button that opens a modal MessageBox wedges the driver

Call: `click(element='Remove', action='invoke', delivery_mode='background')`

The button's handler calls MessageBox.Show, which opens a modal dialog.

Error:
```
TimeoutError: click timed out after 15.0s
```

With no client-side timeout, the same call failed with `click: RPC timeout after 60s` (0.47.7, 3 of 3 reps), and the server answered no other call in the meantime.

The call blocks inside the synchronous UIA InvokePattern.Invoke until the dialog closes. The driver stays wedged. The harness restarted the driver once per rep: 3 restarts in 3 reps, on each version.

Workaround that opened the dialog: `double_click(element='Remove', delivery_mode='background')`. It posts WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK asynchronously. It returned in under 1 s on both versions.

Another tool: it dispatches BN_CLICKED and BM_CLICK to the button instead of a synchronous InvokePattern.Invoke call. It does not block and needs no restart.

## d. click on a WinForms ListBox item does not select it

Call: `click(element='Item 080', delivery_mode='background')` on a ListBox item.

Error:
```
AssertionError: 'Item 080' selected=False
```

The click does not select the item. The reporter expected SelectionItemPattern.Select() to be called on the ListItem.

Workaround that selected the item: `double_click(element='Item 080')`. It posts WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK, and the item reads back as selected.

Another tool: it writes LB_SETCURSEL to the ListBox and sends LBN_SELCHANGE, then reads back the selection.

## e. invoke_menu and menu expand fail when the window cannot be activated

Call: `invoke_menu(path=['Edit','Replace...'])`

Error:
```
RuntimeError: invoke_menu failed: invoke_menu: target window could not be activated
```
On 0.57.0 the same call adds a second line that starts with `Next: That menu path or option does not exist in the app right now.` The report cuts that line off.

Call: `click(element=MenuItem 'Edit', action='expand')`

Error:
```
RuntimeError: click failed: ExpandCollapse.Expand failed: 0x80040200
```

Call: `click(element=MenuItem 'Edit', action='invoke')`, then `click(element=MenuItem 'Replace...')`

Error:
```
RuntimeError: MenuItem 'Replace...' not visible after invoke on 'Edit'
```

A PostMessage left-click on the menu bar item does not open the dropdown.

Result: on classic Notepad, every menu rung failed in 3 of 3 reps, on both versions.

Another tool: it resolves the menu command ID and posts WM_COMMAND straight to the window. It does not open or activate the menu.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep foreground type_text out of sibling windows
body:
## Why

On macOS, a window-addressed `type_text` with `delivery_mode: "foreground"` sent its keys even when the target never became the app's focused window. The keys are pid-routed, so AppKit gives them to its key window. When that is a sibling window of the same process, the text lands there and the driver reports `unverifiable`. Now the driver refuses before any key is sent while AX shows another window of the app holding the focus.

## What changed

- `skylight::sibling_window_focused` reads `AXFocusedWindow`. A different window of the app counts as a sibling; an attached sheet counts as the target. The new `keyboard::type_text_while` asks before every key press (each batched chunk, or each paced character) and returns how many characters it sent.
- The generic window-addressed foreground branch of `type_text` sends through it. If a sibling still holds the focus after the activation, it first takes the focus the way the HID foreground path does (`skylight::focus_exact_window`: make the window key, raise it, ask once more). Making the window key alone left a sibling TextEdit document focused on the hosted runner, which is the reported bug. If the check fails before the first key, the call is refused with an error naming the focused window, and nothing is typed. If it fails partway, sending stops and the call fails with an error saying typing stopped and to check what arrived before retrying. No delivered count or retry offset is claimed. That covers an activation wait that timed out, fronting SPIs that were unavailable, and focus that moves during the send.
- Desktop E2E row `macos-textedit-type-text-window-foreground-sibling` (`installed_app_textedit_macos_test.rs`, wired into `scripts/ci/macos/run-rust-e2e.sh`): a window-only foreground `type_text` at one TextEdit document, sent while a sibling document holds focus, types into the target and leaves the sibling's AX value unchanged.

## Scope

This covers the generic AppKit foreground keyboard path. It does not change these:
- the browser branch, because Chrome's omnibox suggestion popup is a separate window of the same process;
- the key-forwarder (Screen Sharing / Simulator) branch, because `with_foreground_hid_activation` already refuses when the exact window does not take focus;
- the background rungs.

An app that reports no focused window keeps today's best-effort delivery.

## Tradeoffs

The driver could instead refuse whenever focus on the target is never observed. That would break the Catalyst surfaces the existing best-effort contract covers. This change refuses only when focus is proven to be somewhere else.

## Blast Radius

Callers of macOS foreground `type_text` that address a window whose app keeps another window focused now get an error instead of text typed into the wrong window. Same-window targets and apps that report no focused window are unaffected.

## Verification

- Hosted macOS E2E, before the focus step was added: the sibling row reproduced the issue's root cause. Making the target key left the sibling document focused, and the guard refused with `exact target window did not become focused for foreground keyboard delivery, so nothing was typed: window_id … "sibling….txt" of the same app holds focus`. The sibling's text was unchanged.
- Hosted macOS E2E with the focus step: the sibling row passes, typing into the target with the sibling unchanged. The other TextEdit rows, including hotkey-sibling, pass.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) and `test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py` pass, and unit test `keys_are_refused_only_while_a_sibling_window_holds_focus` covers the predicate. I dropped a TextEdit Open-panel refusal row: on the hosted runner its setup could not reliably put the sandboxed panel in focus.

Fixes #3574

title: fix(cua-sandbox): resolve Linux CLI release archive names
body:
## Summary

`cua-version` installation in the sandbox action requests Linux CLI archives with `-gnu`, while the published CLI archives use plain `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64` names. This prevents pinned-release installs on Linux runners.

Download the checksum manifest first and select the plain CLI name when listed, with the `-gnu` name as a fallback when that is the published entry. Download and verify that exact archive before extracting it. A failed download or checksum mismatch does not trigger a fallback to other contents. Darwin naming is unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #8247. The issue reporter identified the naming mismatch; @f-trycua suggested preserving older `-gnu` names.

No RFC: restores the existing pinned-release installation path.

## Compatibility and risk

No new inputs, dependencies, or runtime changes. Name selection uses the existing checksum manifest and preserves its hash verification. Linux `x86_64`, `aarch64`, and `arm64` aliases are covered. No release is published by this PR.

## Validation

- Checked the published assets and downloaded `checksums.txt` for `cua-sdk-v0.31.0`: both `cua-cli-0.31.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `cua-cli-0.31.0-linux-arm64.tar.gz` exist and are listed without `-gnu`.
- Before the fix, the public setup-phase regression fails on the current Linux archive names; legacy GNU and Darwin controls pass.
- After the fix, all **9 tests** pass using local archive/checksum fixtures and intercepted downloads. Coverage includes both Linux architectures, the `arm64` alias, legacy naming, plain-name precedence, Darwin, missing manifests/entries/archives, and rejection before extraction on checksum mismatch.
- The 3 existing KVM-policy tests pass. Bash syntax and `git diff --check` pass.
- `bin/ci --base upstream/main --quick --no-install`: **3 passed, 2 skipped**. Actionlint is not installed; the full `.github/scripts` suite is outside quick mode. The new regression suite ran separately using Python unittest.

The setup tests run the real action script with mocked `uname` and downloads on macOS. They do not boot a sandbox, execute a released Linux CLI, or replace hosted CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): name the selected tab from the tab strip when titles cannot
body:
## Summary

- **Problem this solves:** `get_browser_state` with `pid` and `window_id` proves the window's selected tab only by title, through `selected_tab_target_id`: the one tab whose CDP title the native window title contains. When several tabs of the window share that title, every tab comes back with `active` unset. The same happens for a moment after a navigation, while the native window title still shows the previous page's title (unless that stale title happens to belong to exactly one other tab, which the title test then names, as today).
  - Tabs can share a title when Chrome restores tabs from a profile and never loads them: they show their URL as their title. A page that is still loading does the same.
  - A client that follows the active tab then loses its page. On x.com, an agent session saw one such answer right after a navigation, and a full minute of answers with no active tab while two restored tabs titled `x.com/notifications` sat beside the shown one.
- **What changed:** when the title test proves nothing and the window is proven without its title (an exact bind that no title tie-break chose), the bind reads Chromium's tab strip.
  1. `Target.getTargets`, filtered to `tab` targets, gives each tab's `embedderData.tabActive`.
  2. The bind keeps the bound window's one selected tab, checked with `Browser.getWindowForTarget`.
  3. It attaches to that tab target and auto-attaches its primary page (flat, `waitForDebuggerOnStart: false`) to learn the page target id. A prerender (a page with a `subtype`) is skipped.
  4. It detaches both sessions and accepts the page only if it is a candidate in that window.

  Each reply is awaited for at most 1 s after its command is sent. Both sessions are always detached from a task of their own, which the bind waits for and which runs to its end even if the bind is cancelled meanwhile (or is spawned on drop if the bind is cancelled before), each detach tried twice; if neither attempt takes effect, the session can remain attached (see Risk). Nothing is evaluated in a page, and no tab is selected.

**A question for maintainers before review:** a bind that falls back now attaches to the selected tab and its page, while `get_browser_state` describes itself as read-only (effects under Risk). Is that acceptable for bind mode, or would you rather this be opt-in, or go through an RFC? I opened this as a draft for that decision.

## Related work

Refs #2307 and #2323. #2323 made selection report "unknown" rather than guess among same-title siblings. Its premise, stated on `selected_tab_target_id`, is that "Chromium exposes the native window title but no browser-level selected-tab bit".

Chromium now exposes that bit on tab targets, and this uses it only where the title test gives "unknown". The title proof still comes first, and nothing is inferred from `document.visibilityState` or page script.

Refs #7362 and #7495, the same-bounds window ambiguity. That is a different step, choosing the window. #7495 touches the same `binding` import line in `engine.rs`. #5723 changes `title_matches`, which this leaves alone.

RFC: pending the maintainers' decision above. `active` keeps its meaning (`true`/`false` only when proven, unset otherwise), but a falling-back bind now attaches to the selected tab, which the tool's read-only annotation, and the driver skipping an action-turn recording for read-only tools, do not account for.

## Compatibility and risk

- **User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact:** binds that used to leave `active` unset now name the selected tab. A bind that falls back also attaches to the selected tab and its page, which a window-only bind did not do before. `get_browser_state` describes itself as read-only, so this is a behaviour change for maintainers to weigh; the effects are under Risk.
  - The title proof still runs first, and a bind whose title proves the tab attaches to nothing. Nor does a bind whose window the title chose: a heuristic bind (title alone), or an exact one where the title broke a tie between windows of the same bounds. Either may be the wrong window, since a native title stale after a navigation can name another window's tabs, so its selection stays unknown, as today.
  - A Chromium without `tab` targets or `tabActive` keeps today's answer.
  - No new CDP methods are needed: all are in `EXISTING_PROFILE_METHODS`.
- **Risk and rollback:**
  - A bind that falls back attaches to the selected tab and its page, as a read of that tab already does. Chromium can therefore reload a selected tab whose renderer is gone. During a pending first renderer-initiated navigation, it can show `about:blank` until commit.
  - Selection is a sample: a tab switch or a tab moved to another window between the tab-strip read and the bind's answer can name the tab that was selected a moment earlier.
  - If Chromium answers the tab attach only after its 1 s deadline, or the bind is cancelled while that attach is pending, the driver never learns that session's id, and it stays attached (auto-attach not yet on) until the pooled socket closes; a detach that fails twice leaves its session the same way. Writer contention on the shared socket can lengthen a bind beyond the per-reply deadlines.
  - Revert restores the title-only behaviour.

## Validation

- **Focused tests and checks:** `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver-core --lib browser::` gives 316 passed. Eight new tests are in `v2_tests.rs`. The fixture now models a tab strip and applies `Target.getTargets` filters as Chromium does (first matching entry decides, `exclude` drops, tab targets excluded by default):
  - `same_title_tabs_name_the_one_the_tab_strip_selects` fails on `main` and passes here. It also checks that nothing is evaluated on the tab-strip sessions, no tab is activated or brought to front, and both sessions are detached, the page's on its tab's session.
  - `same_title_tabs_without_a_tab_strip_name_no_tab`
  - `same_title_tabs_on_a_tab_strip_without_tab_active_name_no_tab`: a Chromium whose tab targets carry no `embedderData.tabActive` names no tab and attaches nothing, even when the strip lists a single tab target. This is today's behaviour, kept.
  - `a_failing_detach_is_tried_twice_and_the_bind_still_answers`: when every detach fails while the sessions live on, each is tried exactly twice and then left. Both stay attached (the fixture tracks attached sessions, and the passing case asserts none is left), and the bind still answers, naming the selected tab.

  - `a_window_bound_by_title_alone_never_asks_the_tab_strip` and `a_window_chosen_by_title_among_same_bounds_windows_never_asks_the_tab_strip`: neither queries nor attaches the tab strip, and both name no tab.

  The last four fail on deliberate breaks: counting a missing `tabActive` as selected, dropping the retry, or dropping either gate.
  - `a_selected_tab_whose_page_is_not_in_the_window_names_no_tab`
  - `a_selected_tab_of_another_window_names_no_tab`
- **Standalone browser test:** `standalone_browser_behavior_test.rs`'s same-title case, added in #2323, required both tabs' `active` to be unset. It now asks the browser itself (`Target.getTargets` on tab targets, and `Browser.getWindowForTarget`) whether exactly one tab of the fixture's window is marked `tabActive: true` (a tab that closes before its window is looked up is skipped). If so, the tab brought to the front must be named active and its sibling not; if not, both must stay unset: never a guess. I could not run that suite here; `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-e2e --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

  `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- **Manual or platform evidence:** Chrome 158 on Linux (Wayland), existing-profile bind.
  - **Same-title tabs:** four tabs, three titled the same. `main` answers `active` unset for every tab. This change marks exactly the tab whose document is visible, at 53–63 ms per bind against about 52 ms, over nine binds, with no page target added or left.
  - **Unique titles:** unchanged.
  - **Downstream:** in a downstream end-to-end test (easi.run), a page opens a second tab of itself. It fails on `main` (both tabs `active: null`) and passes with this change.
- **Known gaps or CI still required:** I have not run `bin/ci` locally (sparse checkout, fork), nor the standalone browser suite. This needs a green `CI: Quick` on this PR's head, and the standalone browser run.

title: ci(spaces): reuse main's compiled workspace crates in the app library build
body:
## What changed for users

Pull requests that touch the Cua Spaces macOS app (including the release-bot PRs that bundle a new Cua Driver, #8486) stop waiting about an hour for a Rust build that recompiles code nobody changed.

## Root cause

1. `rust-cache` restores third-party dependencies but always deletes the 52 workspace `cua-*` crates, so every run that misses the compiled-slice cache recompiles all of them at opt-level 3 on a 3-vCPU runner. Run 44983094456 shows a full match on the dependency cache and still 65m40s in `cargo build` (cua-spaces-ext, app-core, cluster and the ffi link are most of it).
2. The compiled-slice cache for main's tree is only saved when main's producer finishes, which takes the same ~55 to 60 minutes, so a PR that starts in that window (or that is force-pushed again, as the bot PRs are) misses. The key itself is right (it hashes only the build's inputs): main saved `d638edb6...` at 04:26Z, 25 minutes after the PR run had looked for it.

Faster compiles is the fix for both, since the lag is the compile time.

## Fix

Use the repo's standard pattern, `.github/actions/rust-cache` (sccache, content addressed), for the workspace crates in the slice action:

- New input `compile-cache` on `spaces-rust-slice`: `none` (default, the release build is unchanged), `read` (PRs), `seed` (the producer).
- Producer on main: still compiles everything from scratch (`SCCACHE_RECACHE`, so the library the release restores is a clean build) and writes each crate's object; main saves the directory once a day.
- PR `ffi` job: restores main's directory and compiles only the crates it changed and their dependents. A PR with no Rust change compiles nothing but the two final links.
- sccache keys include every `CARGO_*` variable, and this workflow sets `CARGO_NET_RETRY` etc. at workflow level (the producer does not), so keys would differ and every crate would miss. I checked this locally with sccache 0.19: same target dir, `CARGO_NET_RETRY` set gives a miss, unset gives a hit. The build step now passes the same settings as `--config` (not hashed) and unsets the variables for that command. `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` does not affect keys (checked).
- The sccache step runs after `rust-cache`, because `rust-cache` hashes `RUSTC_WRAPPER` into the dependency key; this keeps main's existing dependency cache valid.

Not done on purpose: no retries, no timeout change, no skipped build, no opt-level change for the shipped library.

## Expected duration

- PR with no change to the Rust crates, slice cache missed: about 66 min to roughly 10 to 15 min (dependency cache restore, sccache restore, two links).
- PR changing a top-of-chain crate (ext, app-core, cluster, ffi): still compiles those crates (about 45 min on the runner); a PR changing a low crate (cua-home) rebuilds nearly everything. Exact slice-cache hit: unchanged (seconds).
- The first main run after this merges seeds sccache, so PRs only benefit after that run's save; sccache saves once per UTC day per family.

I could not run the hosted macOS job locally. Local checks: the cargo timings for the build (release 24 min cold on 20 cores; cli chain is about 27% of workspace CPU) and the sccache key behaviour above. Verification is this PR's own CI run: the "sccache enabled" and "sccache stats" lines of the `ffi` job.

## Related

- Bundle-driver PR: #8486
- Dependency-cache key fix: #8509. This branch is stacked on #8509's commit (it needs the same step). Fold #8509 in or merge it first; either order is fine.

title: fix(cua-driver): raise the agent cursor after an untargeted move that follows a click
body:
## Why

A click pins the agent cursor overlay just above its target window, and nothing ever cleared that pin. A later `move_cursor` with no target window kept the overlay at the old target's level, so the cursor stayed hidden under any window that covered the target. On macOS the raise for unpinned cursors (#2616) never ran, because the cursor still had a pin.

## What changed

- `cursor-overlay`: new `OverlayCommand::Unpin`. The shared `apply_command_base` clears `pinned_wid` and the off-Space hide that the old pin set.
- The untargeted `move_cursor` path sends `Unpin` before it animates, on macOS, Windows and Linux. Targeted moves and clicks still pin as before.

## Scope

Covers a move with no target window after any action that pinned the cursor. A click itself still pins just above its target, so a background action stays below unrelated foreground apps. This PR does not change that behavior; the maintainer comment on the issue explains why. A move with no target already means "top of the normal band" under the shared `ZOrderEnforcer` contract: macOS raises the overlay with `orderFrontRegardless`, and Windows and X11 use `reassert(None)`. This change makes the untargeted move reach that state after a click too.

## Blast Radius

The change affects `move_cursor` without `window_id` on all three platforms. Before this change, such a move by a fresh session already went through the unpinned path. Now a session that clicked earlier takes the same path. No other caller sends `Unpin`.

## Verification

- `bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers and image refs passed. Cargo builds and tests were skipped on this shared host and are left to CI.
- New owner test `unpin_drops_the_window_an_earlier_action_pinned` (cursor-overlay) runs in CI.
- Not run here: live overlay z-order checks on macOS, Windows or Linux.

title: fix(cua-driver): answer sent messages while attached to the target input queue on Windows
body:
## What changes for users

Foreground `type_text` on Windows no longer freezes the target app. Before, when the driver had to bring the app forward first, the app could stop reading keys for 2 s and the driver reported `text_delivery_stalled`. The text then showed up late. The driver now answers the app's messages while it waits. If another window holds the foreground, the error names that window.

## Evidence (merge-group run 45020095461, `rust-windows-native` artifact)

- `harness_wpf_type_text_foreground_single_line_application_state` failed on both attempts with `text_delivery_stalled`, 0 of 32 units read. The harness was the foreground window, and the page file was normal (`temp=False`).
- The after-state the recorder took right after the failure shows `mirror=FOREGROUND-SINGL`. That is exactly units 1..16, in the right TextBox. So focus was correct and the input was not lost; it was read late.
- In the recording, the harness starts inactive (grey title bar). The driver activates it and focus moves to `txt-input`. Then the caret **stops blinking for about 2 s**, so the WPF UI thread is not pumping. The 16 characters appear right when the driver gives up and detaches.
- Passing cases in the same run: in `harness_wpf_type_text` the harness was already active. In `..._multiline_application_state` it was activated the same way, and typing started at once.

## Root cause

`with_confirmed_foreground` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/input/keyboard.rs`) attaches the driver's thread to the target thread's input queue (`InputQueueAttachment::attach`). Then it waits for a sentinel key to be read (`send_and_await_read`, `wait_for_drain`). Attached threads share one input queue, with its activation and focus state. The wait spun on `yield_now()` / `sleep()` and never serviced messages sent to the driver thread. If the target sent the attached thread a message, for example while finishing the activation the driver had just forced, it blocked until the driver detached.

## Fix

- Every attached wait goes through `InputQueueAttachment::idle`. It dispatches only sent messages (`PeekMessageW` with `PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE`, `PM_NOREMOVE`). Posted and input messages stay with the target.
- A stall now reports how many sent-message batches the driver answered while attached, and whether the target answers `WM_NULL` within 200 ms.
- New unit test `attached_wait_answers_a_message_the_target_sends`. It attaches to a helper thread, which sends a message to the waiting thread, and requires an answer within 1 s. The old spin wait fails it: the helper times out.
- Kept from before: the foreign-foreground error, and page file plus foreground diagnostics.
- `e2e-diagnostics.ps1` reads the `TempPageFile` registry value only when it exists. Strict mode threw `The property 'TempPageFile' cannot be found`. `Win32_PageFileUsage.TempPageFile` stays the source of truth.

The paging-file modal in runs 44930184906 and 44981193269 was a separate trigger. It is not the cause of this stall.

## Not verified

- I did not identify which message the target sends. It is inferred from the frozen caret and from the text arriving at the moment of detach. If the stall happens again, the new stall detail settles it: a non-zero answered count, or a target that does not answer `WM_NULL`.
- Not compiled locally (no `cargo xwin`). Windows CI compiles it and runs the new unit test.
- Native lane dispatches on this head: 45024981496, 45024984182, 45024987028.

title: Icon metadata paths are interpolated into shell commands during result submission
body:
## Affected revision

- Repository: `trycua/cua`
- Location: `libs/python/cua-sandbox-apps/cua_sandbox_apps/pipeline/creator_agent.py:604`

## Summary

During `submit_result`, each path in `metadata.icon_paths` is interpolated
directly into two shell commands:

```python
f"file {icon_path} 2>/dev/null | grep -oP '\\d+ x \\d+' | head -1"
f"base64 {icon_path} 2>/dev/null"
```

The path is not quoted or passed as a separate argument. A path containing
`;`, `|`, `$()`, or backticks executes additional commands in the target
sandbox.

## Expected behavior

The icon path must be treated as a single argument. Shell commands should use
argument arrays or a properly quoted path, and the sandbox API should not parse
caller-controlled metadata as shell syntax.

## Actual behavior

The real `_make_submit_tool` source was loaded from the target commit, with the
external sandbox shell replaced by a local execution stub and the screenshot
verifier stubbed to pass. Calling `submit_result` with:

```text
icon_paths = ["/tmp/cua-icon; touch /tmp/cua-creator-full-pwned"]
```

reached the icon extraction code and executed both commands:

```text
TARGET_RUN: file /tmp/cua-icon; touch /tmp/cua-creator-full-pwned 2>/dev/null | grep -oP '\d+ x \d+' | head -1
TARGET_RUN: base64 /tmp/cua-icon; touch /tmp/cua-creator-full-pwned 2>/dev/null
RETURN: {'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': 'OK: result accepted for test on linux. ...'}]}
PWNED: True
```

`submit_result` returned OK after the injected command ran.

## Root cause

`submit_result` builds shell command strings with f-strings and passes them to
`sb.shell.run`. No quoting, escaping, or argument separation is applied to
`icon_path`, even though `icon_paths` comes from submitted metadata.

## Suggested fix

Pass the path as a separate argument:

```python
await sb.shell.run("file", ["--", icon_path])
await sb.shell.run("base64", ["--", icon_path])
```

or quote it with a shell-escaping helper. Validate that icon paths are absolute
paths inside the sandbox and reject control characters and shell metacharacters.

title: fix(cua-driver): scope background scroll keys to the target window
body:
## Summary

Background scroll’s keyboard fallback can refuse with `same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity` when the addressed window has a competing same-process destination, such as a Chrome popup. It uses the generic key gate without acquiring the exact-window transport used by the other keyboard tools.

Both fallback gates now use the existing window-keyboard action classifier. Before focusing the element or posting keys, the fallback acquires the existing exact-window key scope and moves it into the blocking posting worker. This keeps the scope alive through the final key, including if the awaiting call is cancelled.

When that transport is unavailable, the generic ambiguity refusal remains in place.

Fixes #7681. Thanks to @injaneity for reporting the issue and identifying the transport requirement.

## Compatibility and risk

Restores the existing macOS window-addressed keyboard behavior. No new API, protocol, dependencies, or permissions; no RFC required.

Only `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/scroll.rs` changes. The principal risk is native key-window and focus restoration. Rollback is reverting this commit.

## Validation

- Added a regression with one competing same-pid destination. Confirmed it fails with the original generic action (`same_pid_keyboard_ambiguity`) and passes with the fix on this Mac.
- The regression also checks that generic keys remain refused and requires the same refusal when the exact-window transport is unavailable.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p platform-macos tools::scroll::tests`: **2 passed**.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p platform-macos`: **897 passed, 13 ignored, 1 failed**. The failure is `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`; it also fails on unchanged base code because this host supplies curly-apostrophe “Don’t Allow” while the test expects ASCII “Don't Allow”.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`: **passed**.
- `bin/ci --base upstream/main --quick --no-install`: **5 passed, 3 skipped**.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

Ready for review as-is. The regression verifies the gate decision; it is not a live Chrome-popup reproduction. Maintainer approval to run CI and native macOS verification of target delivery and focus/z-order restoration remain outstanding. Required desktop certification must run on the final candidate SHA before merge.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused change and description match the diff.
- [x] Restores an existing contract; no RFC required.
- [x] Regression evidence and remaining verification gaps are stated.
- [x] Conventional production-fix title for cua-driver.
- [x] No external implementation copied; issue reporter credited.
- [ ] Native Chrome-popup verification and final desktop certification.
- [ ] Hosted CI and full local-CI signoff.

title: fix(cua-sandbox-apps): stop shell interpolation of icon paths in creator submit_result
body:
Fixes #8523

## What changed

`submit_result` in the creator agent built two sandbox shell commands from each `metadata.icon_paths` entry without quoting (`file {icon_path} ... | grep ...` and `base64 {icon_path}`). A path containing `;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks or spaces was parsed by the shell.

- Icon bytes are now read through the sandbox file API (`sb.files.read_bytes`), so the path is never part of a command.
- The image width is read from the PNG header in Python (falling back to the `NxN` hint in the path, as before). This replaces `file | grep`.
- On images without a file API, the fallback is `base64 < <shlex-quoted path>`. The path is stdin, so it cannot be parsed as an option (this works with both GNU and macOS `base64`).
- The saved extension is limited to `.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8}` (default `.png`), and non-string or empty entries are skipped.

I audited the other sandbox shell calls in `cua-sandbox-apps`. The remaining `sb.shell.run` calls in `creator_agent.py` use fixed strings. `sandbox_tools.py` already quotes every interpolated value (#8477). The `sandbox_bash` tool passes the agent's own command by design. The host `subprocess` calls use argv lists. The icon extraction was the only site that interpolated an agent-controlled value into a shell string, so 2 command sites are fixed.

## Impact

The commands ran inside the target sandbox VM, not on the host. `metadata.icon_paths` is set by the creator agent (an LLM with web access, working from the app and install pages it researches) when it calls `submit_result`. It is not set by a human caller. Whether any security advisory applies is for Francesco to decide.

## Tests

`tests/test_icon_extraction.py`: paths containing `; touch`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks, `&&`, spaces, single and double quotes and a leading dash reach the sandbox as one literal argument. With the file API there is no shell command at all. In the fallback the command is exactly `base64 < <quoted>` and `shlex.split` yields the path as a single token. No `PWNED` file appears. Normal paths still extract, with the correct width from the header or path.

User-visible: a malformed icon path no longer runs extra commands in the sandbox.

title: fix(cua-driver): cache UIA pattern availability instead of pattern objects
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, `get_window_state` cost more per element than a raw UIA `FindAll` over the same window. #7963 already moved `list_windows` off UI Automation. This PR covers the part that remained: the bulk `BuildUpdatedCache` request behind the tree walk asked for eight control patterns (Invoke, Toggle, SelectionItem, ExpandCollapse, Value, RangeValue, Text, Scroll). For every element that supports one of those patterns, the provider then had to build a pattern object and marshal it to the driver, across the whole subtree.
- What changed: the walk only needs to know which patterns an element supports, and the toggle and selection state it reports were already cached as properties. The cache request now carries the eight `Is*PatternAvailable` boolean properties in place of the patterns. Actions and `selected` are read from those booleans. Each row gets the same actions in the same order as before.

## Related work

Fixes #2100

RFC: not needed. No contract changes.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. `actions`, `selected` and the element indexes keep their current shape and order. Actions themselves still resolve live patterns with `GetCurrentPattern`, so no code path depended on the cached pattern objects.
- Risk and rollback: a provider might report a pattern as available but not hand it out, or the reverse. That would change which rows are indexed. UIA computes availability from the same provider query, so this is not expected. Rollback is a revert of this one commit.

## Validation

title: cua-agent: spend cap crashes with TypeError when litellm has no price for the model
body:
A spend cap on an agent run crashes on the first model response when the model has no pricing in litellm (for example a self-hosted model behind `api_base`).

**What happens.** litellm sets `_hidden_params["response_cost"]` to `None` for a model it has no price for. The loops read it with `.get("response_cost", 0.0)`, so the default does not apply: the key is present and holds `None`. `BudgetManagerCallback.on_usage` then runs `self.total_cost += usage["response_cost"]` (`libs/python/agent/cua_agent/callbacks/budget_manager.py`), which raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'float' and 'NoneType'`. The CLI usage mode does the same with `total_cost += result.get("usage", {}).get("response_cost", 0)` (`cua_agent/cli.py`).

**Scope.** The same `.get("response_cost", 0.0)` read is in 14 places under `cua_agent/loops/` and `cua_agent/callbacks/telemetry.py`. Where nothing adds it, a `None` cost passes through and is silently treated as zero.

**Root fix, not a patch at the crash site.**
- Normalise the cost once, where usage is built, with one shared helper that returns a float or an explicit "unknown" and is used by every loop.
- A budget cap cannot be enforced for a model with no price. `BudgetManagerCallback` should say so up front (or when the first unpriced response arrives), not count the cost as zero and let the run go on past its cap.
- Tests: a `None` cost through the budget callback and the CLI usage path.

Found from an outside report against `cua-agent` 0.9.1; I confirmed the code is unchanged on `main`.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the private worker from opening a console window
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, `createPrivateWorker` from a host without a console (Electron, any GUI app) opens a visible console window for the worker. It sits over the automated app and closing it kills the worker.
- What changed: `PrivateWorkerClient::spawn` now calls the same `prevent_console_window` the embedded host uses (sets `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` only when the host has no console). The helper takes a `std::process::Command`; the embedded host passes `command.as_std_mut()`.

## Related work

Fixes #8192. Same approach as #5040 for the embedded daemon.

## Compatibility and risk

- Console hosts are unchanged: the flag is only set when `GetConsoleCP() == 0`, so a worker started from a terminal still shares the host's console.
- Windows-only, behind `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]`. No API change.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

## Validation

- New test `private_worker_opens_no_console_window_for_a_host_without_one` (`crates/cua-driver/tests/private_worker_test.rs`): relaunches the test binary with `DETACHED_PROCESS` (no console, like a GUI host, same technique as `daemon_console_window_follows_the_host_console`). That probe creates a private worker, `AttachConsole`s to the worker pid and asserts `GetConsoleWindow()` is null.
- Before the fix, Windows 11: probe fails with "a console window was opened for the private worker".
- After: passes. Windows 11: `cargo test -p cua-driver --test private_worker_test` 4 passed; `cargo test -p cua-driver-sdk` 113 passed (incl. `daemon_console_window_follows_the_host_console`); `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver -p cua-driver-sdk --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- `bin/ci` (affected mode, WSL Ubuntu 24.04, Rust 1.97.1): SPDX (FSL, driver), rustfmt, Windows cfg grep, image refs, clippy -D warnings, unit tests (665 passed) all ok. The two heavy generator checks ran on Windows (my WSL has 2 GB RAM): `generate-uniffi-bindings.mjs --check` "UniFFI bindings are up to date", docs runner `--library cua-driver --check` "All documentation is up to date".
- Known gap: the host is a `DETACHED_PROCESS` console-subsystem process, not a real GUI-subsystem binary. Both have no console (`GetConsoleCP() == 0`), which is the condition the fix keys on. Happy to add a GUI-subsystem helper bin if you want the literal case.

title: fix(cua-driver): retry connect's agent CLI spawn on ETXTBSY
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `connect::tests` fail now and then on Linux CI (#8468). A test writes a fake agent CLI with `fake_cli` and `connect_agents` runs it at once. If another test thread forks in between, the child holds the inherited write descriptor until it execs, so the spawn fails with `Text file busy (os error 26)` and the agent is reported `Failed`.
- What changed: `run_cli` in `connect.rs` retries the spawn on `ErrorKind::ExecutableFileBusy`, up to 20 times 10 ms apart. This is the pattern `updater.rs` (`pacman_owns_path`) already uses in the same crate.

## Related work

Fixes #8468. Same root cause as #6575, which fixed it in `cua-agent-setup`'s tests.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: none. Only a spawn that fails with ETXTBSY behaves differently, and it now waits at most about 200 ms before reporting the same error.
- Why a retry and not the write-then-rename suggested in the issue: `rename` keeps the inode, and ETXTBSY is decided per inode, so a child forked during the write still holds a write descriptor to the renamed file until it execs. Renaming narrows the window, it doesn't close it. Retrying the spawn handles every case.
- Risk and rollback: one function, revert the commit.

## Validation

- Repro on unmodified main (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, 2 CPUs): the `cua-driver` unit test binary run with `connect::tests --test-threads=16` in a loop, 3 failures in 300 runs. They hit three different tests (`detects_claude_and_codex_on_path_and_cursor_by_folder` twice, `one_failure_does_not_fail_the_others_or_the_exit_code` once); the last one printed `could not run /tmp/.tmp…/bin/claude: Text file busy (os error 26)`.
- After the fix, same loop: 0 failures in 600 runs.
- `bin/ci` (affected mode, WSL Ubuntu 24.04): SPDX headers, rustfmt, Windows cfg grep, image refs, clippy -D warnings and unit tests for `cua-driver`, 7 passed.
- Known gaps: the loop ran on Linux only. Windows and macOS don't raise ETXTBSY, so the retry never triggers there.

title: feat(lume): optional guest time service over virtio-vsock
body:
## Summary

Adds an optional, opt-in guest time service to `lume run`: guests that lack a real-time clock can read the host's wall-clock time over virtio-vsock at boot.

- New `lume run --time-vsock <port>` option and `timeVsockPort` field on `POST /lume/vms/:name/run`. Off by default.
- When set, the VM gets a virtio socket device (`VZVirtioSocketDeviceConfiguration`) and the host listens on that vsock port. Each guest connection to the host (CID 2) on the port receives one line and is closed:

  ```
  time-v1 <seconds> <nanoseconds>\n
  ```

  `seconds` is UTC seconds since the Unix epoch and `nanoseconds` the fraction within that second, read when the connection arrives. The guest sends nothing, so it can't change the host clock.
- Robustness: the reply is one non-blocking `send` with `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, so a guest that resets the connection or never reads can't block or crash lume. (`SO_NOSIGPIPE` alone isn't enough: setting it fails once the peer has already closed.) Ports 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF are rejected.
- Works alongside `forwards` (they share the socket device). A resume now follows the saved state's devices: a state saved with a socket device keeps it even when the resuming run passes neither option (before, such a restore could fail its configuration check), and a state saved without one resumes without the service.
- CLI and HTTP API reference regenerated (`docs:generate:lume`).

## Testing

- `swift test`: 281 tests pass, including the new `GuestTimeServiceTests` (reply format, the served time, a peer that already closed, a peer that never reads, port range, socket-device selection, CLI and HTTP validation).
- Manual, on a macOS 26 guest started with `lume run <vm> --display none --time-vsock 5000`: a guest-side AF_VSOCK client connecting to CID 2 port 5000 receives `time-v1 <s> <ns>` matching host time; 300 back-to-back connections (half closed without reading) are all served or dropped cleanly and lume keeps running; other ports are refused.

title: [Bug]: Direct host registered with --host is missing from the macOS app's New Space host picker
body:
### Primary area

Other

### Summary

The CLI recognizes a Linux direct host registered with `--host`. A fresh macOS app snapshot confirms that its direct entry appears as an ordinary Space under Computers. The host is also reported absent from New Space's Run on picker; that picker state and the failing `spaces.createOptions.env` payload have not yet been independently captured.

### Reproduction

The names below are generic examples. HOST_IP is the Linux host's reachable private address; CUA_ENV_TOKEN is the local token generated by host setup. No real address or token is included.

1. On the Linux host, enable direct hosting:
```sh
cua host setup --direct "$HOST_IP:3211" --share spaces --name example-linux-host
```

2. On the macOS client, register it as a host:
```sh
cua spaces add "$HOST_IP:3211" --host --name example-linux-host --token "$CUA_ENV_TOKEN"
```

3. Run `cua spaces ls --json`. Confirm the host is listed in `machines` with `via: "direct"`, `online: true`, container resources, and the registered direct Space advertises `host_spaces`.
4. Open the macOS app's Computers page. The observed app classifies the entry as a Space and shows zero computers despite the direct host registration.
5. Open New Space and inspect Run on. The registered host is missing. Use a Linux image when reproducing the picker behavior to avoid an incompatible-OS selection.

The Computers classification was checked from a fresh app snapshot. The missing picker entry was reported in the app; the failing `spaces.createOptions.env` payload has not yet been captured.

### Expected behavior

The registered direct host should appear as a Computer and be selectable as a New Space target corresponding to `host:example-linux-host`. A host that advertises `host_spaces` should be usable through its local token without requiring a Cua account sign-in.

### Actual behavior

The CLI lists an online direct host with available container resources. The macOS app displays its direct entry as an ordinary Space, reports zero computers, and omits the host from the New Space picker. A failed host discovery should also be surfaced to the user instead of making a capable host silently disappear.

### Environment

- Client: Cua Spaces for macOS 0.41.3; bundled cua CLI 0.31.0.
- Host: Linux, cua-spacesd 0.17.2, direct listener with local token authentication.
- Host configuration: `sharing: true`, `provideSpaces: true`; zero provided Spaces, limit four.
- Host runtime reported to the client: container / runc.

### Evidence

Anonymized, shortened excerpts from `cua spaces ls --json`:
```json
{
  "machines": [
    {
      "id": "example-linux-host",
      "name": "example-linux-host",
      "via": "direct",
      "online": true,
      "node": {
        "kinds": ["container"],
        "runtimes": ["runc"]
      }
    }
  ],
  "spaces": [
    {
      "id": "direct:<HOST_IP>:3211",
      "name": "example-linux-host",
      "provider": "direct",
      "parent": null,
      "features": ["host_spaces"]
    }
  ]
}
```
Identifiers were replaced with examples and feature/resource lists were shortened. The registered direct Space has no `host` field.

Code observations at commit `37a981c7119f05a2ada3f3b41c1dd3a9f6779e2a`:
- [machines.rs:488](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/37a981c7119f05a2ada3f3b41c1dd3a9f6779e2a/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces-app-core/src/machines.rs#L488): `own_desktop()` recognizes only Relay-provider records.
- [machines.rs:569](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/37a981c7119f05a2ada3f3b41c1dd3a9f6779e2a/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces-app-core/src/machines.rs#L569): `page_rows()` skips a record that is neither an own relay desktop nor a hosted child with `space.host`. This matches the direct entry being counted as a Space rather than a computer.
- [AppModel.swift:1086](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/37a981c7119f05a2ada3f3b41c1dd3a9f6779e2a/apps/cua-spaces-macos/Sources/CuaSpacesMacKit/Models/AppModel.swift#L1086): `newSpaceEnv()` obtains hosts from `backend.hosts()`.
- [SpacesBackend.swift:715](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/37a981c7119f05a2ada3f3b41c1dd3a9f6779e2a/apps/cua-spaces-macos/Sources/CuaSpacesMacKit/Models/SpacesBackend.swift#L715): host discovery errors or a 10-second timeout are converted to an empty list.
- [wizard.rs:3626](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/37a981c7119f05a2ada3f3b41c1dd3a9f6779e2a/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces-app-core/src/wizard.rs#L3626): the shared wizard iterates all `env.hosts` and supports `host:<id>`; it does not exclude direct hosts.

The Computers classification issue is supported by the observed record shape and code. The exact runtime reason for the missing picker entry remains unconfirmed; the Computers classification and candidate-host discovery are separate paths.

Source inspection used the revision above; the installed app and CLI binaries have not been verified as builds of that revision.

### Workaround and additional context

A possible way to bypass the app's picker is explicit CLI placement:
```sh
cua spaces create linux --on host:example-linux-host --name example-linux-space --no-relay
```
This command was not executed as part of this report, so successful creation is not claimed.

Related: [#6204](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/6204) concerns repeated direct-host registration under new names. This report uses one canonical, lowercase host name and an existing single direct-host registry entry.

title: fix(cua-driver): attach to the Windows input queue only after the target processed its activation
body:
Fixes #8543 (not marked "Fixes" until the native lane is green on repeat runs).

## What users see

Foreground `type_text` and `press_key` on Windows could stall for 2 s and report `text_delivery_stalled` on a target that was in front and responsive. The text then appeared only after the driver gave up. With this change the driver waits until the target window has actually become active before it shares the target's input queue, so the keys are read as they arrive.

## Root cause

`with_confirmed_foreground` (`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/input/keyboard.rs`) attached the driver thread to the target's input queue (`InputQueueAttachment::attach`) as soon as `GetForegroundWindow()` named the target. That pointer changes the moment `SetForegroundWindow` succeeds. The target thread becomes active only when it reads the activation event Windows queued for it, and until then its queue has no active or focus window. Attaching in that interval shares a queue whose pending activation, and every key routed by it, waits on the driver thread. The driver thread never reads input (since #8522 it only answers sent messages), so the target reads nothing until the attachment is dropped.

## Evidence

From the recording of the failing case in nightly run 45042522800 (`windows-wpf-type-text-ax-foreground-single-line-state`), sampled at 10 fps:

- For the first ~2.3 s, the WPF title bar is drawn inactive and the caret keeps blinking in the *deferred* field. The target thread is alive and pumping timers, but it has not processed its activation and has no input to read.
- At ~2.3 s, which is the 2 s stall plus setup, the window turns active and focus moves to `txt-input` in the same frame: the moment the driver detached.
- The passing neighbour case (`windows-wpf-type-text-ax-foreground`, same run) starts with the window already active, and the text lands immediately.

This also matches the error text: the target answered `WM_NULL` (alive) and was the foreground (pointer set), yet read 0 units. It also matches the earlier run 45020095461, where the 16 characters appeared exactly when the driver detached.

## Fix

- After the foreground is confirmed, wait (bounded, 500 ms) until the target thread's own queue reports the target as its active window. This uses `GetGUIThreadInfo(...).hwndActive` and is read without attaching. Only then run the focus step.
- After the focus step, repeat the check for the window that is actually in front (it may be an owned window), and attach only once it passes.
- If activation is not processed in time, fail with `foreground_unavailable` and send no input.
- The stall detail now also reports the target queue's active and focus HWNDs.
- New Windows unit test: a window its thread has never activated is not treated as ready for attachment.

Why not detach before injecting: the attachment is the only exact signal that the target *read* the input. The `GetKeyState` toggle of the drain sentinel on the shared queue is what keeps the restore of the previous window from handing the unread tail to it (#4477). The evidence shows the attachment's timing is the fault, not its presence during injection, so this keeps the read confirmation and removes the pending-activation window.

## Verification

- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: green (rustfmt, headers).
- Windows build and tests run in GitHub CI. A local cross-compile was not possible on macOS (missing MSVC SDK headers).
- Three Windows native-lane dispatches on this branch: 45059999669, 45060002533, 45060005629.
