title: fix(cua-driver): pin X11 pixel clicks to the header-bar screenshot frame
body:
Fixes #3237

## Why

On cua-driver 0.20.0, a pixel click on an X11 GTK4 window with a header bar landed one title bar (about 47px) below where the `get_window_state` screenshot showed the target. The reporter retested on 0.56.6 and the offset is gone: the X11 capture and `window_local_to_screen` both use the client window's origin, so the two frames agree. Nothing tested that, so this PR adds a regression test for it.

## What changed

- The GTK4 fixture now draws a stock `Gtk.HeaderBar`, so its client window and screenshot include the title bar, like the gnome-calculator window in the report. It also has a 160x20 magenta button that counts clicks in a `GTK4_PIXEL_CLICKS=N` label.
- `harness_gtk4_test` finds the magenta target on the screenshot from its pixels only, the way a vision model grounds a click, and clicks the center of the target. It runs this in background delivery (AT-SPI hit test, with the background oracles) and foreground delivery (XTest). The target is shorter than a header bar and has only margin under it, so a click that is off by the title-bar height misses it.

## Scope

Test and fixture only. The X11 native lane already runs `harness_gtk4_test` with `--ignored`, so both new tests run there without workflow changes. Wayland is out of scope: that lane does not run the X11-only GTK4 fixture.

## Blast Radius

The existing `gtk4_tree_resolves_after_foreign_gtk3_application` test uses the same fixture. Its markers are unchanged. The fixture window is now taller because of the header bar and the new widgets.

## Verification

- I ran the fixture under Xvfb. The client window is 420x264. Its capture includes the header bar, and the target sits at (130, 219) with a size of 160x20.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) pass. The E2E run is left to the verifier and the X11 native CI lane.

title: feat(cua-driver): leave caller windows out of get_desktop_state on macOS
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: an embedder's own floating panel (for example its Stop button) shows up in every `get_desktop_state` image, so the model can see it and try to click it. The driver had no way to leave a window out of the desktop capture.
- What changed: `get_desktop_state` takes an optional `exclude_window_ids` (window ids from `list_windows`).
  - **macOS:** the ids are added to the ScreenCaptureKit display filter that already leaves out the driver's own cursor overlay. The call fails closed: an id ScreenCaptureKit doesn't list returns `excluded_window_not_found`, and a ScreenCaptureKit failure returns `window_exclusion_unavailable` with no image. It never falls back to `screencapture`, because that would include the window. A successful response echoes `excluded_window_ids`.
  - **Windows and Linux:** a non-empty list is refused with `window_exclusion_unsupported` and a reason, since their display capture can't leave out another process's window. Omitting the field or passing an empty list behaves exactly as before.
  - The field is in the shared Rust contract, the contract manifest and the generated Python/TypeScript bindings. It is an optional field that defaults to unset.

## Related work

Fixes #3242

RFC: none. This adds an optional MCP/SDK parameter, and the RFC process covers public MCP contract changes. See the open question below.

The two documentation points in the issue (`get_screen_size` "points" wording, and `scale_factor` reporting 1.0 for a 2x capture) are not addressed here.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a new optional input on `get_desktop_state` on every platform. Existing calls are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: on macOS, the new path runs only when the list is non-empty. The overlay-only path and its `screencapture` fallback are untouched apart from a signature change. Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests:
  - Unit tests for the shared refusal helper (`cua-driver-core` `tool_schema`) and for macOS window-id range parsing.
  - New e2e tests, run by the existing desktop-scope runners with `--ignored`:
    - `desktop_scope_macos_test::desktop_state_leaves_excluded_window_out`: captures with the AppKit harness in front, captures again excluding it, asserts most interior pixels changed and the response echoes the id, then asserts an unknown id is refused with `excluded_window_not_found`.
    - `desktop_scope_linux_test::desktop_state_refuses_window_exclusion` and `desktop_scope_windows_test::desktop_state_refuses_window_exclusion`.
- Run locally on Linux arm64 (the scoped repository checks):

  - clippy `-D warnings` on contract, core, sdk, platform-linux and cua-driver-e2e.
  - `cargo xwin check` for platform-windows and cua-driver-e2e tests.
  - Contract manifest and UniFFI binding drift checks.

title: feat(cua-driver): add mouse_move_relative for pointer-locked apps
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: an app that locks or captures the pointer (a first-person game's camera, a web page under Pointer Lock) reads motion deltas and ignores where the cursor is. `move_cursor` and click coordinates are absolute, so the Cua Driver could not turn such a camera.
- What changed: a new MCP tool, `mouse_move_relative {dx, dy, duration_ms?}`, sends native relative motion on every platform. It never falls back to an absolute warp.
  - macOS: a HID mouse-moved event with the delta fields set, or the dragged event of a held button. The cursor is never warped.
  - Windows: `SendInput` with `MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE` and no `MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE`.
  - X11: XTest relative motion.
  - Wayland: the wlroots virtual pointer's relative `motion` (sway, Hyprland, niri), falling back to the libei relative pointer (GNOME, KDE).

The schema, argument checks, step splitting and result shapes live in one shared module, `cua_driver_core::relative_pointer`; each platform adapter only sends one native event per step.
- `duration_ms` (0 to 10000) spreads the move over steps about 8 ms apart, each followed by an equal share of the duration. The steps always sum exactly to `dx`/`dy`.
- A backend with no relative route refuses with `unsupported_operation` and sends nothing. This covers a Wayland compositor with no wlroots virtual pointer and a libei session whose seats, once settled, offer no relative pointer. libei motion is written out inside the call's admission, so a call that has timed out sends nothing more (only an EIS socket the compositor has stopped reading could still hold a frame back, as for every libei command).
- If a later step fails, the result is `effect: partial` with the number of events delivered. If nothing was sent (including a display or device that cannot be opened), it is `delivery_failed`.
- On macOS, the existing desktop pointer guard checks each event's own location (live cursor plus delta) right before it is posted, against one snapshot of the windows and the frontmost app. Over a window of an app that is not in front it refuses (before the first event) or stops (later, reported as partial), unless `delivery_mode:"foreground"`.

## Related work

Fixes #3298

RFC: none. This is an additive tool that follows the existing desktop-pointer contract (`move_cursor` with `scope:"desktop"`). If maintainers want an RFC for a new MCP tool, it stays open for that.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: one new MCP tool on all three platforms, with capability tokens `input.pointer.move` and `input.pointer.move.relative`. It joins the action-result, desktop-input authorization, risk-class and origin-scoped-manifest lists the same way `move_cursor` does. It needs a desktop capture scope (a window-scoped session refuses it with `desktop_scope_disabled`). It moves the user's real pointer.
- Scope left out:
  - Key holds: there is no `key_down`/`key_up` tool yet.
  - Routing relative motion through a Linux `mouse_button_down` hold's persistent virtual pointer.
  - `run_steps` batching and the remote receiver subset.
  - A Minecraft demonstration.
- Risk and rollback: the change adds a new tool and touches no existing tool's behaviour, apart from wording in the macOS guard's refusal for the new tool. Reverting the PR removes it.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - The shared module has unit tests for the exact-sum step split (negative, asymmetric, zero and boundary deltas), the pacing, symmetric rounding, argument refusals with `invalid_arguments`, and the partial/`delivery_failed`/`unsupported_operation` results.
  - Further unit tests cover capture scope (`desktop_scope_disabled` for a window session), the libei relative command through the fake EIS server (including no motion once the call is over), the macOS guard's refusal text, and the macOS event type for each held button.
  - Ran on Linux: `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` (1401 passed), `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract`, `cargo test -p platform-linux --features portal-input --lib` (1184 passed), `cargo clippy -D warnings` on core, contract and platform-linux, `cua-contract-gen all --check`, `cargo check -p cua-driver-e2e -p cua-driver --tests`, and `bin/ci --quick` (green).
- Manual or platform evidence: a new opt-in test, `relative_motion_moves_the_pointer_by_the_delta`, in `desktop_scope_linux_test` (already selected by the Linux desktop lanes). On X11 it asserts the pointer moves by exactly the delta, both in one event and spread over several, read back through `get_cursor_position`. It passed under Xvfb with `-noreset`. Mutation check: making the XTest request absolute makes it fail, landing at (3, 0) instead of (403, 298). On Wayland the test reports a limitation and returns, because Wayland gives clients no pointer position to read back.
- Known gaps or CI still required:
  - The macOS and Windows code was not compiled on this Linux machine: a C dependency cannot be cross-built here. CI's native lanes check both.
  - The macOS and Windows MCP snapshots (`cli-specs/cua-driver-mcp-{macos,windows}.json`) were written from the shared definition, not dumped natively. Their docs check verifies them.
  - No native captured-pointer run yet on macOS, Windows or a Wayland compositor. On Windows, the visible cursor moves by the delta after the user's pointer speed and acceleration settings; raw-input readers get the delta as sent.

title: fix(cua-sandbox): stage installer downloads privately and verify them
body:
Fixes #8573.

**What changes for users:** the Windows QEMU and wimlib auto-install in cua-sandbox now checks each download against a pinned SHA-256 and keeps it in a private folder under `~/.cua` while it installs. Nothing else changes.

### Changes
- `runtime/qemu_installer.py`: `_download_zip` no longer uses `tempfile.mktemp()`. The archive goes into a new `TemporaryDirectory` (mode 0700, random name) next to the install directory inside the user's cua home, is opened with exclusive create (`"xb"`), and is extracted only after its SHA-256 matches a pinned value (`QEMU_PORTABLE_SHA256`, `WIMLIB_SHA256`). A mismatch raises and installs nothing. The staging directory is always removed.
- `builder/pwa2apk.py`: the host-side builder no longer looks for an existing checkout at `/tmp/pwa2apk`; it only uses `cua_home()/pwa2apk` (cloning there if missing), so it never runs code from a shared directory.
- `tests/test_install_temp_safety.py`: regression tests. They fail on main and pass here.

### Testing
- `pytest libs/python/cua-sandbox/tests/test_install_temp_safety.py` (4 passed; 4 failed against the old code)
- `bin/ci --quick` green
- Pinned hashes taken from the current release assets; archive layouts checked against `QEMU_INNER_DIR` and `wimlib-imagex.exe`.

title: fix(cua-driver): mark DWM-cloaked and zero-area Windows windows as off-screen
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: On Windows 10/11, `EnumWindows` and `window_info_by_handle` return DWM-cloaked top-level windows (such as closed `StartMenuExperienceHost.exe`, `SearchHost.exe`, `TextInputHost.exe`, suspended UWP frames, and windows on other virtual desktops) as well as zero-area shell hosts (such as `ShellExperienceHost.exe` notification windows with height `0`). Because `enum_windows_cb` and `window_info_by_handle` only checked `IsWindowVisible` and set `is_on_screen: !minimized`, those invisible windows were reported as on-screen at the top of the z-order even when `list_windows(on_screen_only: true)` was requested. While #7963 added a `DWMWA_CLOAKED` guard to `immersive_window_info` for handles skipped by `EnumWindows`, cloaked windows already yielded by `EnumWindows` bypassed that check.
- What changed: Added `is_dwm_cloaked` (`DwmGetWindowAttribute(..., DWMWA_CLOAKED, ...) == Ok && cloaked != 0`) and `window_is_on_screen(minimized, cloaked, width, height)` in `platform-windows`, and used them in both `enum_windows_cb` and `window_info_by_handle`. Cloaked and zero-area windows remain addressable in unfiltered `list_windows()` output with `is_on_screen: false`, and are excluded when `on_screen_only: true`. If DWM is unavailable (`DwmGetWindowAttribute` returns `Err`), `is_dwm_cloaked` returns `false` so ordinary windows are not falsely marked off-screen.

## Related work

Refs #7963

RFC: Not required (bug fix preserving the existing `list_windows` contract and `is_on_screen` / `on_screen_only` semantics).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. `list_windows(on_screen_only: true)` drops DWM-cloaked and zero-area windows instead of reporting them above active application windows, and unfiltered `list_windows()` marks them `is_on_screen: false` (`[off-screen]`). Uncloaked open flyouts (e.g. an open Start menu or Search panel) continue to report `is_on_screen: true`.
- Risk and rollback: Low risk — scoped strictly to `is_on_screen` computation in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/win32/windows.rs`. Revertible in a single commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - Added unit test `cloaked_minimized_or_zero_area_windows_are_not_on_screen` in `win32::windows::exact_window_tests`.
  - Passed `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/win32/windows.rs`.
- Manual or platform evidence: Observed on Windows 11 where `list_windows(on_screen_only: true)` reported closed `StartMenuExperienceHost.exe ("开始")` `[0,0 1920x1032]`, `TextInputHost.exe ("Windows 输入体验")` `[0,0 1920x1080]`, and `ShellExperienceHost.exe ("新通知")` `[1524,1032 396x0]` with `is_on_screen: true` at the top of the z-order while `WindowFromPoint` resolved directly to the focused application window underneath.

title: feat(cua-driver): end the macOS hover reveal wait at the window's first repaint
body:
Fixes #3493

## Why
Some macOS actions sleep a fixed time so the UI can repaint before the driver reads it back. This adds the damage signal the issue asks for: a ScreenCaptureKit stream delivers a frame only when the display changed, so a wait can end at the first changed frame and keep the old constant as its cap.

## What changed
- `cua_driver_core::damage_settle`: a `DamageSignal` takes each frame's FNV-1a digest and dirty rectangles. A caller arms it for the region it acts on, then `settle(armed, cap)` ends at the first frame that differs from the one before it and was redrawn in that region. Otherwise it sleeps the rest of the cap: no watcher, a watcher that fails, or a stream that has not started yet.
- `platform_macos::damage_watch`: one `SCStream` per display, 256 px wide, cursor hidden, queue depth 3, with the driver's own windows left out (the agent cursor overlay). It is armed on the display that holds the target window's centre. It starts in the background on first use, so starting never delays an action, and stops after 30 s with no arm. It starts only with Screen Recording and a recorded direct-capture approval (`capture_consent::direct_capture_consented`). Any case the consent check cannot decide counts as no, so the stream cannot raise that alert. A display gets no new stream while its old one is still listed or stopping. If ScreenCaptureKit does not confirm a stream's stop, that display keeps the fixed wait for the rest of the process.
- The background hover's 150 ms wait after `AXShowAlternateUI` (`input/hover.rs`) now ends at the target window's first repaint. The fixed wait stays in two cases, because another repaint would end the wait early: the same hover just hid another element's controls, or another window in front overlaps the target (`windows::uncovered_bounds`).

## Scope
Only the hover reveal uses the signal. The other macOS waits stay as they are, because a changed frame does not prove what they wait for:
- The WebKit text-field focus wait already ends on AX focus.
- `launch_app` holds focus-steal suppression windows.
- The 150 ms after a foreground AX click and the drag tail let the target consume input before the previous app is restored.
- The `document_edit` and `invoke_menu` waits cover focus and key delivery.

Windows, X11 and Wayland have no watcher and keep their fixed sleeps.

## Tradeoffs
- A changed frame is not application readiness, and the module docs say so. The watch is limited to the rectangle of a target window that nothing covers, so a caret blinking in the user's own window does not end the wait.
- The stream could be per action instead of persistent, but then every action would pay the stream's start-up cost.
- While a stream runs, macOS shows its screen-capture indicator. It goes away 30 s after the last hover.

## Blast Radius
Only macOS background hover (`move_cursor` over a background app's alternate-UI element) is affected. Without Screen Recording or a recorded consent, and for an overlapped target, the behaviour is the same as before.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib damage_settle` covers 10 cases on Linux. A change in the region wakes the wait early. A change elsewhere, or an identical redraw, waits out the cap. Missing dirty rects count as the whole frame. A change before the wait is kept. The first frame is not a change. A failed watcher sleeps the full cap. The idle stop follows the rules above. Mutation check: making the region test always true fails `a_change_elsewhere_rides_out_the_cap`.
- `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --lib --tests -D warnings` and `bin/ci --quick` both pass.
- `windows::uncovered_in` has a unit test for windows in front, windows behind, transparent windows and the driver's own windows. It runs only in the macOS lane.
- Not run here: the build host is Linux, so `platform-macos` was not compiled or run, and its compile and tests are left to the macOS CI lanes. A live hover against Finder's sidebar on macOS with Screen Recording granted has not been run.

title: feat(cua-driver): warm the app scan at daemon start and serve recent list_windows replies
body:
## Why

Fixes #3495. Every daemon starts with the installed-app scan uncached, so the first `list_apps` pays for it. Agent loops that call `list_windows` back to back recompute the same enumeration each time. This warms the scan right after the socket binds, and lets a host opt in to serving recent `list_windows` replies.

## What changed

- `cua_driver_core::read_cache`: a stale-while-revalidate cache for `list_windows` replies, enabled by `CUA_DRIVER_LIST_WINDOWS_CACHE_MS` (1 to 1000, clamped). A reply is fresh for that long and served stale for up to 20 times that, while one background call per argument set recomputes it. Each entry has a unique id, and a refresh may end the refresh of, and replace, only the entry with that id. A result computed before an action is never stored after it, and a read from before an action leaves a newer entry in place. Dispatch holds an `Actuation` guard around any tool that is not read-only. The guard bumps a generation when it starts and when it drops, including when the caller is cancelled, and replies from an older generation are never served. Errors are never cached. The macOS, Windows and Linux registries wrap only the public `list_windows`; `verify_state` and the post-action window watch still read live. `EmbeddedCuaDriverHost` admits the variable.
- `platform_macos::apps::warm_session_caches`: after bind, a background thread runs `list_all_apps` once, the same code `list_apps` runs. It reads the process table and bundle plists only, so it needs no TCC grant and cannot raise a prompt, and it does not wait on the permission gate.
- Docs: `Skills/cua-driver/EMBEDDING.md` and the SDK guide describe the variable and its staleness cost.

## Scope

Covers the two outcomes in the issue. Leaves out:
- an event-source cache: none exists, since `CGEventSource` is created per call;
- capture-plan warming: plans are per window, last 2 s, and depend on Screen Recording;
- accessibility-tree replies: `get_window_state` mints element tokens and snapshot ids, and replaying a reply would hand out indices for a snapshot that no longer exists;
- Windows and Linux warm-up: neither keeps an installed-app or enumeration cache between calls, so there is nothing to warm.

## Tradeoffs

- Opt-in rather than on by default. With a 2 s stale cap, an agent calling once a second would always see the previous call's list. Unset, `list_windows` behaves exactly as before.
- Any action retires every cached reply, not only the ones for the acted-on app. That keeps the rule simple: a read after an action is live.
- The cache key is the full argument object, including the session fields dispatch adds, so sessions and runtimes never share a reply.
- The macOS installed-app cache keeps its existing 30 s TTL, so the warm-up helps a `list_apps` that comes within that window of daemon start.

## Blast Radius

- Without the variable, the only runtime change is an atomic counter increment around non-read-only dispatch, plus the macOS warm-up thread. That thread reads the same files `list_apps` already reads.
- With the variable set, a change that lands after an action's call ends can be missing from a reply for up to 20 times the value. That includes a window a person or another app opens or closes, a window an app opens after `launch_app` returns, and work a cancelled call's platform worker (for example Linux `launch_app`'s `spawn_blocking`) still finishes.

## Review dismissals

- Round 4 asked for an invalidation guard inside every detached platform worker, so that a cancelled `launch_app` that still launches would retire replies. I did not do this. A late effect from a cancelled call is the same class as a window an app opens after a normal `launch_app` returns. The opt-in already accepts that class for at most 20 times the TTL, and only the default-off cache is affected. Threading a guard through every platform's workers would touch each adapter for a bound the cap already gives. The docs now state this case.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib -- read_cache an_action_between_cached` on Linux: 14 passed. The whole `cua-driver-core` lib suite: 1404 passed, 2 ignored. Mutation checks: disabling the dispatch hook fails `an_action_between_cached_window_reads_makes_the_next_read_live` (`left: 1, right: 2`). Letting any refresh release the flag fails `a_late_refresh_never_releases_a_newer_entrys_refresh`. Dropping the generation check in `store` fails `a_refresh_from_before_an_action_never_replaces_a_reply_from_after_it`. Letting a refresh store over another entry fails `a_refresh_never_replaces_an_entry_other_than_its_own`. Letting an older read remove a newer entry fails `a_read_from_before_an_action_keeps_a_reply_from_after_it`. Removing the bump on drop fails `a_cancelled_action_retires_window_reads_cached_while_it_ran` (when run alone, since other dispatch tests bump the shared generation) and `an_actuation_retires_replies_when_it_starts_and_when_it_is_dropped`.
- Three review rounds found six cache interleavings, and all six are fixed with a test that failed before its fix:
  - a late refresh could release a newer entry's refresh flag;
  - a refresh from before an action could overwrite a reply computed after it;
  - a refresh that started after its entry was replaced could overwrite the replacement;
  - a read from before an action could delete a newer entry;
  - a cancelled action skipped its closing bump;
  - two entries that started on the same clock tick shared a refresh token.
- `cargo check -p platform-linux -p cua-driver-sdk` on Linux: clean. The macOS and Windows code could not be compiled on this host, so their wiring relies on CI.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`): 5 passed, 5 skipped (clippy, unit tests, bindings and the Windows cross-check are skipped in quick mode; the docs generators were not routed because pnpm is not installed here).

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC: it adds one opt-in daemon environment variable and changes no tool schema.
- [x] Tests and documentation are included; the macOS and Windows gaps are listed above.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] No external contribution is included.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off: only `bin/ci --quick` ran, because this is a shared host.

title: fix(agent): preserve unknown model costs and stop unenforceable budgets
body:
## Summary

An unpriced model returns `response_cost=None`. The budget callback and CLI add it to a number and crash; substituting zero would make the spending cap unenforceable.

- Normalize provider costs through one shared helper: finite, nonnegative numbers become floats; missing or invalid pricing stays unknown.
- Report unknown pricing on the first unpriced response. Budgeted runs stop before the next model call; `raise_error=True` raises the existing budget exception immediately.
- Keep CLI, logging, trajectory and telemetry totals unknown after any unpriced response, rather than presenting a partial total as complete.
- Handle serialization that drops `None` fields, and explicitly mark tool-result usage as zero cost while preserving its existing `Usage` object type.

## Related work

Fixes #8538, opened by @f-trycua and assigned to @ddupont808. This patch is offered for the existing owner's review.

The package is deprecated and its hosted test/build/publishing lanes are disabled. This PR addresses the reported defect in the retained source; it does not reactivate the package or promise a release.

No RFC: this repairs unknown-cost handling in the existing usage and budget interfaces.

## Compatibility and risk

**Direct Gemini SDK limitation:** this loop reports token counts but no response price. Any run using that loop with `max_trajectory_budget` stops after the first response (or raises immediately with `raise_error=True`). Non-budgeted runs continue with an unknown total. Local/self-hosted models without configured pricing have the same limitation. Estimating prices from token counts is outside this fix.

Known-price and genuinely zero-cost responses retain normal accumulation and budget thresholds. Unknown pricing is not treated as free. Reset behavior follows `reset_after_each_run`.

The wider file count comes from replacing the duplicated cost reads across provider loops and updating existing consumers to accept unknown costs. No dependency, workflow or credential-handling changes.

The ordinary budget path stops at its existing continuation boundary, before another model request; it does not undo a request or tool action already completed. The first request may incur a cost before the provider reveals that pricing is unavailable.

## Validation

Candidate: `ef64c685bfc463e43a9f69c9f0555e3f8c506e77`. Python 3.12, isolated environment, local dependencies, telemetry and dotenv loading disabled. Provider calls are mocked.

- Before the fix: all three initial budget/CLI regressions failed, including both reported `TypeError` paths.
- Full agent suite: **113 passed, 2 skipped**. Includes real agent-run integration, dict/model provider responses, known/zero/unknown costs, budget reset/error modes, final-response diagnostics, serialized usage, CLI and reporting callbacks.
- A mutation treating unknown pricing as zero fails the budget/CLI regressions.
- `bin/ci --base upstream/main --quick --no-install`: **3 passed, 1 skipped**, including isort, Black and Ruff. The README triggered an image check that was skipped because `crane` is not installed.
- Direct Gemini SDK regressions cover token metadata present and absent; both report unknown pricing and prevent continuation. The README and constructor docs explicitly describe this behavior.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

No live model requests or paid API calls were made. Hosted CI is not claimed.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] Focused on #8538; description matches the final diff.
- [x] No RFC required.
- [x] Regressions and local verification included; disabled hosted lanes disclosed.
- [x] Conventional fix title.
- [x] No external implementation incorporated.
- [x] Local quick checks passed; no hosted sign-off claimed.

This is a behavioral fix; `no-release` is not requested.

title: fix(cua-driver): guard Linux X11 set_value foreground clicks against wrong-window input
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: When Linux X11 `set_value` uses `click_type_fg` on a scrolled, moved, occluded, or reassigned element, it clicks the stale centre, types into another window or control, and reports success (`effect: suspected_noop`) instead of refusing before input.
- What changed: On foreground X11 routes (`click_type_fg`, `click_select_fg`) only, check AT-SPI `Showing`, window-local bounds, `click`'s `point_ownership` (pre/post-activate, non-web; `Mismatch`/`Redirect` refuses), and X11 `point_owned_by_window` before any XTest click. Failures refuse (`element_bounds_unavailable`, `effect: "none"`) with zero input; MPX is unchanged. No focus check or empty read-back error is added (a stale point passing the guard behaves as on `main`).

## Related work

Refs #7945 (follow-ups left: focus check, empty read-back error). RFC: not required (reuses `element_bounds_unavailable`).

## Compatibility and risk

- Impact: `platform-linux` foreground X11 `set_value` + X11 E2E only; MPX/macOS/Windows unaffected. Non-`Showing` minimised/hidden elements refuse (like `click`).

title: [Bug]: set_window_frame refuses to move a Stage Manager strip window at its own size
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

With Stage Manager on, `set_window_frame` refuses to move a fixed-size window that sits in the recent-app strip, even when the requested size is the window's current size. The fixed-size path from #4133 writes `AXSize` only when the size changes, but it decides that by comparing the request with the WindowServer frame. For a strip window, WindowServer reports the thumbnail (about 44 x 104), while AX keeps the logical frame (230 x 408 for Calculator).

### Reproduction

1. Turn on Stage Manager and keep another app active, so Calculator lands in the recent-app strip.
2. `launch_app({"bundle_id":"com.apple.calculator"})`. `list_windows` reports the window at about 44 x 104 near the screen edge, while `get_window_state` with `tree_format:"elements"` reports the AXWindow frame as 230 x 408.
3. `agent_display({"action":"create"})`, then `set_window_frame({pid, window_id, "x": <inside the display>, "y": <inside the display>, "width": 230, "height": 408})`.

### Expected behavior

The window moves onto the agent display. Only `AXPosition` is written, because the requested size equals the window's size.

### Actual behavior

`set_window_frame: window_id <id> does not expose a settable AXSize`

### Environment

Cua Driver 0.59.5 (signed release app), macOS 27.3 (26C5047e), Apple silicon, Stage Manager on with "Displays have separate Spaces".

### Evidence

Calculator in the strip: `list_windows` and `window_bounds` report 44 x 104 at the right edge of the main display, the `get_window_state` screenshot is 44 x 104, and the AX tree is complete (34 elements). With Calculator on the active stage, where WindowServer and AX agree on 230 x 408, the same move succeeds.

### Workaround and additional context

Moving a strip window onto an agent display is the way to get a full-size capture and working pixel input (#3631 covers the thumbnail capture itself). A resizable window can be moved by requesting a different size, but a fixed-size window has no workaround short of activating it.

Proposed fix: decide whether the size changes from the AX frame, which is the frame the `AXSize` write targets, and fall back to WindowServer when AX has no usable frame. Confirmation still reads WindowServer. I'll open a draft PR with this change and a focused unit test.

title: [Feature]: agent_display option for a display that outlives the calling session
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

`agent_display` lets an agent work on an app without touching the user's screen. With Stage Manager on, it is also the way around the recent-app strip: a window moved onto an agent display gets a full-size capture and working pixel input (tested with Chess at 889 x 699 and a pixel drag e2–e4, with the user's front app unchanged). But the display belongs to the calling session and is removed when that session ends or idles out (five minutes). macOS then moves the parked windows back to the user's screen, usually into the strip. An agent that parks a background app across turns or sessions has to keep one session busy.

### Desired outcome

An agent can create an agent display that stays until it is explicitly removed or the daemon exits, independent of any session. `list` says which displays are like that, so a later session can find and reuse them.

### Current workaround

Keep an MCP connection or named session busy with periodic calls so the owning session never idles out.

### Affected components and platforms

Cua Driver, macOS only (`agent_display` is macOS only).

### Alternatives and prior art

A per-session idle timeout on `start_session` would be more general, but it still ties parked windows to one session label. A client-side keepalive loop works but is fragile.

### Implementation ideas

An optional `lifetime: "session" | "daemon"` on `create`, defaulting to `session`, so existing behavior is unchanged. A `daemon` display skips session ownership. `list` reports each display's `lifetime`. This adds one optional field to the `agent_display` MCP input and one field to its output. I read that as a small additive change, but if maintainers want it to go through the RFC form instead, I'll move it there; the draft PR I'll open waits on that call.

title: [Feature]: launch_app option to open an app's windows on an agent display
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

To work on an app without touching the user's screen, an agent launches it and then moves its window onto an agent display with `set_window_frame`. Between those two calls, the new window appears on the user's screen. With Stage Manager on, it can briefly join the user's active stage. A person watching the screen sees an app flash up and may close it, which happened during testing.

### Desired outcome

An agent can launch an app so that its windows open on a given agent display and never appear on the user's screen.

### Current workaround

Launch, then move each window with `set_window_frame` as soon as `list_windows` shows it. macOS remembers the last position, so a relaunch sometimes opens on the agent display, but not reliably.

### Affected components and platforms

Cua Driver, macOS (`agent_display` and `launch_app`).

### Alternatives and prior art

None found in the tracker.

### Implementation ideas

An optional `display_id` on `launch_app`, limited to displays this daemon created. The driver moves each new window of the launched process onto that display as soon as it appears, before returning. This is an additive MCP field, so it may warrant an RFC; happy to follow maintainers' call.

title: [Feature]: macOS autostart that keeps serve flags across restarts and updates
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On macOS, CuaDriver.app starts `cua-driver serve` with no flags. A user who wants `--grant existing-profile`, `--no-automation-prompts`, or launch environment tuning (`CUA_DRIVER_KEY_GAP_MS`, `CUA_DRIVER_FAST_PATH`) has to write and maintain their own LaunchAgent. If anything restarts the daemon through the app instead, for example an update, it silently comes back without those settings. `cua-driver autostart` is Windows-only, although `install-local.sh --autostart` already writes a macOS LaunchAgent for dev builds.

### Desired outcome

A supported way on macOS to start the daemon at login with chosen serve flags and launch environment, which survives `cua-driver update --apply` and other restarts.

### Current workaround

A hand-written LaunchAgent (KeepAlive, Aqua session) that runs `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver serve <flags>` with `EnvironmentVariables`. After an update, `cua-driver stop` hands the socket back to it.

### Affected components and platforms

Cua Driver CLI and installer, macOS.

### Alternatives and prior art

`cua-driver autostart` on Windows; `install-local.sh --autostart` on macOS for dev builds.

### Implementation ideas

`cua-driver autostart enable [serve flags…]` on macOS writes that LaunchAgent, and `update --apply` restarts the daemon through it when it exists. Grants stay a trusted-launch decision: only the user running the command sets them. Because this touches the permission boundary (launch grants), it may need the RFC form; happy to move it there.

title: fix(cua-driver): move Stage Manager strip windows with set_window_frame
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: with Stage Manager on, `set_window_frame` refuses to move a fixed-size window that sits in the recent-app strip (for example Calculator), even when the requested size is the window's own size. It fails with `does not expose a settable AXSize`. WindowServer reports a strip window at its thumbnail size (44 x 104 for Calculator), so the size-change check from #4133 saw a resize that wasn't requested.
- What changed: the macOS adapter decides whether the size changes from the AX frame, which is the frame the `AXSize` write targets. It falls back to the WindowServer frame only when AX has no usable frame. Confirmation still reads WindowServer, as before.

## Related work

Fixes #8602

Refs #4133 (fixed-size moves), #3631 (strip thumbnail captures; moving a window onto an agent display is the workaround this unblocks)

RFC (required for a public SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, compatibility, permission,
or cross-component contract change): not needed. This is a macOS adapter bug fix with no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Moves that previously succeeded behave the same, because AX and WindowServer agree outside the Stage Manager strip. No schema change.
- Risk and rollback: low. If AX ever reports a size that differs from WindowServer for a reason other than the strip, the request now writes `AXSize` based on AX, which is the attribute being written. Revert is one commit.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new unit tests `a_stage_manager_strip_thumbnail_does_not_turn_a_move_into_a_resize` (using the frames observed live: AX 230 x 408, WindowServer 44 x 104) and `size_reference_falls_back_to_window_server_without_a_usable_ax_frame`. Mutation check: preferring the WindowServer frame makes the first test fail. `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib tools::set_window_frame` (10 passed), `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `rustfmt --check` all pass on the rebased branch.
- Manual or platform evidence (macOS 27.3, Apple silicon, Stage Manager on): with the 0.59.5 release, a strip-resident Calculator reproduced the refusal. With a local `install-local.sh` build of this branch, `set_window_frame` moved Calculator (230 x 408, fixed size) onto an `agent_display` display and the action record was `confirmed` from WindowServer readback. The full-size capture and window-pixel clicks there worked (7 + 3 = 10).
- Known gaps or CI still required: I couldn't re-create the strip state on demand for the live run of this branch, because Stage Manager kept the relaunched window on the active stage, so the strip case is covered by the unit test with the observed frames. `bin/ci` was not run: my checkout is sparse, and `bin/ci --quick` stops on lockfiles outside it. The repository CI needs to run.

title: fix(relay): move state persistence off the request path (CUA-4413)
body:
Linear: CUA-4413

## What users saw

On 23 Nov the relay's disk stopped answering for about 80 seconds. For that time the whole relay stalled: its calls to the Spaces API, to sign-in (OIDC discovery) and to PostHog timed out together, and hundreds of requests queued, then arrived all at once when the disk came back. Nobody lost access (the relay served its cached answers), but a longer stall would have started refusing people.

## Root cause

The relay's state stores (machine directory, devices, audit log, device sessions, teams, pairing codes, grants, Space settings, pending deletions, usage, pool) wrote and fsynced their files inside request handlers, while holding the same mutexes every reader of that store takes. When an fsync hung, the handler's tokio worker hung, and every other worker that touched the store blocked on its lock. With all workers blocked, the runtime itself stopped: timers, the I/O driver and outbound connections included.

## Fix

- **New `persist::StateFile`**: one writer thread per state file. A store changes its state in memory under its lock, hands the writer a snapshot, and releases the lock. Write, fsync and rename happen on the writer thread, never under a store lock and never on an async worker. Files stay atomic (fresh 0600 temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync).
- **Latest state wins.** A snapshot queued behind a stalled write replaces the older one, so a burst of changes during a stall costs one write. Journals (audit log, session journal) queue appended lines, written in one batch with one `fdatasync`. The queue is bounded (8 MiB of lines): past it, or after a failed append, the store rewrites the journal whole from memory, so the file never has a gap in the audit hash chain.
- **Durability is awaited, not blocked on.** Each change returns a `Durable` future. Requests that must not answer before their change is on disk (registering a machine, enrolling a device, team changes, pairing codes, account erase and so on) now `.await` it, so they yield their worker. If the write fails, the change is undone in memory (unless a newer change replaced it), and the caller gets the same storage error as before. Best-effort state (grants, usage, audit lines, access-path team audit, plan cache, TCP share leases) is queued and not awaited. A failed write is counted, and the next write retries it.
- **Pool:** each account's pool lock is now an async mutex. Its file writes run on the blocking pool while the lock is held, and requests waiting for it no longer block workers. Opening an account's pool from disk and erasing it also moved off the workers.
- **DNS:** reqwest now uses the `hickory-dns` async resolver, so name lookups no longer go through blocking `getaddrinfo` on tokio's blocking pool.
- **Visibility:** new `cua_relay_state_writer_behind_seconds` (how long the oldest unwritten change has waited, per store), `cua_relay_state_write_duration_seconds` (histogram), `cua_relay_state_writes_coalesced_total` and `cua_relay_state_journal_overflows_total`. `/readyz` reports `behind_secs` per store, and a write slower than 5 s logs `state write slow`.
- **Shutdown:** after draining, the relay waits up to 20 s for every writer to flush (`Storage::flush_writers`), and a dropped `StateFile` flushes what is queued.

trycua/cua#8314 (fewer mesh registry writes) is separate and already merged; this PR does not touch it.

## How tested

- New regression test `stall_tests::requests_and_outbound_calls_proceed_while_the_state_disk_is_stalled`. It runs on a 2-worker runtime, holds the directory's writer the way a hung fsync would, and starts 6 machine registrations (more than there are workers). While they wait, `GET /v1/machines`, `/healthz`, outbound HTTP calls and timers all answer within 5 s, and the behind gauge shows the lag. Once the stall lifts, every registration succeeds and is on disk. Mutation-checked: putting the old blocking write back under the lock makes this test fail.
- `stall_tests::device_sessions_open_and_are_checked_while_their_journal_is_stalled`: sessions open and validate while the session journal and audit writers are stalled, then land on disk.
- `persist` unit tests: coalescing, journal ordering after a snapshot, bounded queue with rewrite, failed append leaves no gap, awaiting without blocking.
- Existing tests updated where they read a file right after a change (they now flush the writer first). Audit-log failure semantics changed: a failed write keeps the event and rewrites the log. `cargo test -p cua-relay --features hosted` (unit and integration) and `cargo test -p cua-relay` pass, and `bin/ci --quick` is green.

## Rollout

Prod relay promotion is a separate, gated step (a "prod: promote Relay" PR in the cloud repo, staging first). This PR does not touch prod.

title: fix(relay): a stalled state volume no longer holds /readyz or /metrics (CUA-4413)
body:
Follow-up to #8608 (Linear CUA-4413). **Stacked on #8608**, which is not merged yet: this branch starts from its head (`fix/relay-persistence-off-request-path`), so the base is that branch. Retarget to `main` once #8608 merges.

## Finding
Prod runs one relay pod, so a readiness probe that fails on a disk pause would cause a full outage. That is not the case today: the pod's startup, readiness and liveness probes all use `/healthz`, which never touches the disk, and the README says not to point readiness at `/readyz`. So a disk pause does not remove the relay from the Service, and I did not change any probe or manifest.

## What was wrong
`/readyz` and `/metrics` both waited on the same lock as the disk write probe, and the probe held that lock while it wrote and fsynced. During a disk pause both endpoints hung, so the alert signals went dark at the moment they were needed, and each scrape tied up a blocking thread.

## Change
- The write probe no longer holds a lock while it touches the disk, and only one runs at a time.
- `/readyz` waits at most 0.5 s for a fresh probe. A pause shorter than 5 s keeps the last result (still ready). A probe stuck for 5 s or more answers 503 "state volume not answering".
- New gauge `cua_relay_state_probe_running_seconds` and a `probe_running_secs` field in the `/readyz` body, so a stalled volume can be alerted on (suggested: above 5 for 1 minute).
- Liveness is deliberately unchanged. Restarting the relay would not unstall the disk and would drop every connected machine.

## Tests
New test `a_stalled_volume_does_not_block_readyz_and_a_long_wedge_is_reported`: with the probe stalled, `/readyz` answers 200 in under 2 s, `/healthz` in under 0.5 s; after 5 s `/readyz` answers 503 in under 2 s, `/metrics` answers in under 2 s and shows the running time. Full `cua-relay` tests pass; `bin/ci --quick` passes.

For users: nothing changes. Operators now keep seeing disk health during a disk pause.

title: feat(cua-driver): add ui_tree_revision and refuse actions with a stale one
body:
## Why

#3586 asks for a per-window UI-tree revision that callers can attach to an action, so the driver refuses the action when the tree has moved on. `since` already answers `no_change`/`diff`, but no token stays stable across unchanged reads, and actions have no structured `stale_revision` refusal. This PR adds both, in the shared core, so every platform gets the same contract.

## What changed

- `get_window_state` returns `ui_tree_revision` in structuredContent and in the text header (`... snapshot_id=s… ui_tree_revision=N`). The value stays the same while reads of the same view (query, max_elements, max_depth) return the same rows, and grows when the rows change. A `since` read that answers `no_change` keeps it, and one that answers `diff` moves it. A screenshot-only read leaves it alone.
- `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `hotkey` and `set_value` accept an optional `ui_tree_revision`. Dispatch resolves the window from `pid` + `window_id`, or from the read an `element_token` came from, and refuses before any input with `refusal.code: "stale_revision"` and `reason`:
  - `changed`: a later read saw different rows (`expected` and `current` are returned);
  - `no_revision`: this driver has not read the window's tree;
  - `unknown_window`: the call names no window it can resolve.
- The check runs once the action holds its input lanes, so a read that finishes while the action waits for them is seen.
- A new revision is the larger of the previous one plus one and the wall clock in microseconds. Revisions only grow, and those from an earlier driver process stay below a later one's unless the system clock was set back in between.

## Scope

Covers the revision token and the action-side refusal (ask 1 in the issue, and the part the maintainer narrowed the issue to).

Not covered: answering `since` without a UIA walk. This needs change tracking between reads, using UIA structure/property events plus WinEvent hooks. Not every provider raises those events (owner-drawn controls, parts of WinForms and Chromium), so skipping the walk on events alone can return a false `no_change`. A false `no_change` is the stale-world failure this issue is meant to remove. This PR changes nothing in the walk, and `since` still walks. Shipping the event-gated skip as its own PR keeps that risk separate.

The check covers changes a read has observed. The ledger does not watch the window between reads.

## Tradeoffs

- **Per-view row hashes.** Reading a view for the first time records its rows without bumping the revision, so alternating views does not trigger false `stale_revision` refusals. The cost: a change that only a brand-new view could see does not bump the revision until that view is read again.
- **Screenshot-only reads.** A read with `include_accessibility_tree:false` records nothing. Every tree read is recorded, including one that returns no rows, so a window whose rows all disappear moves its revision.
- **Contract struct not updated.** `ui_tree_revision` is not yet in the generated `WindowStateOutput` contract struct, matching `diff_counts` and `invalidated_snapshot_ids`. Adding it regenerates the UniFFI bindings and can follow separately.

## Blast Radius

The only output change is one additive structured field and one additive header token, on all three platforms. Actions without `ui_tree_revision` behave exactly as before. The new argument is advertised the same way as `post_action_wait`, through `advertised_runtime_input_schema`, and is removed from the arguments before the platform adapter runs.

## Verification

- `bin/ci --quick`: SPDX headers, rustfmt and image-ref checks pass. Clippy, unit tests, UniFFI bindings and the Windows cross-check were skipped locally because this host is below the disk floor for builds. CI runs them.
- MCP reference: the per-platform registry snapshots come from this PR's CI `Reference / cua-driver / <platform>` artifacts. The pages were re-rendered from them with the generator's own `renderReference`, and the same render over main's snapshots reproduces main's pages exactly.
- New unit tests (run in CI):
  - `ui_tree_revision::tests`: same rows keep the revision, changed rows move it, views and windows are independent, exact `stale_revision` reasons, and `invalid_arguments` for malformed values.
  - `window_state_view`: `no_change` keeps the revision and `diff` moves it; a tree read that empties moves it, and a screenshot-only read does not.
  - `tool.rs`: a stale revision is refused at dispatch with `stale_revision`/`changed` and the probe tool is not invoked.

Fixes #3586

title: fix(cua-driver): drain autoreleased objects when creating initial macOS overlay surfaces
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `run_appkit` creates the initial cursor overlay `NSWindow` via `rebuild_surfaces(&layout, Vec::new())` on the main thread before entering `[NSApp run]` and without an `autoreleasepool`. AppKit autoreleases internal references to that startup `NSWindow` into the pre-runloop pool, which never drains while `[NSApp run]` is running. After the first display sleep/wake or display reconfiguration calls `dispose_surface` (`orderOut:`, `close`, `release`), the initial overlay window stays alive off-screen in `WindowServer` / `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` for the rest of the daemon's lifetime. Surfaces created later inside `on_appkit` (via `dispatch_sync_f` on the main queue, where GCD drains a per-dispatch autorelease pool) deallocate cleanly on subsequent wakes.
- What changed: wrapped `rebuild_surfaces` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/cursor/overlay.rs` in `objc2::rc::autoreleasepool`, matching `capture.rs` and `input/appkit_activation.rs`, so autoreleased references from both initial pre-`[NSApp run]` creation and subsequent rebuilds/disposals drain immediately.

## Related work

No existing issue or PR found covering this startup `NSWindow` leak (PR #5170 and PR #7549 added `autoreleasepool` for ScreenCaptureKit capture workers; PR #8126 changes overlay order-in and collection behavior without adding an `autoreleasepool` around initial surface creation).

RFC: not required (internal macOS resource-lifecycle bug fix; no public contract change).

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Prevents the initial overlay `NSWindow` from remaining leaked off-screen in `WindowServer` after the first display wake or display layout rebuild. No API, CLI, MCP, or permission changes.
- Risk and rollback: low risk — `create_surface` holds a `+1` retained `NSWindow` (`setReleasedWhenClosed: false`) and `tile_layer` is retained by its superlayer, so draining autoreleased temporaries does not free live surfaces. Rollback is a straight revert of the single wrapper in `rebuild_surfaces`.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo fmt --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-macos -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo test --locked --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-macos --lib cursor::overlay`: 20 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo test --locked --manifest-path libs/cua-driver/rust/Cargo.toml -p platform-macos --lib`: 906 passed, 1 failed (`security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`, unrelated OS consent-label failure on this macOS version), 13 ignored.
  - `bin/ci --quick`: 5 passed, 4 skipped (build-tier checks run via the commands above).
- Manual or platform evidence:
  - Standalone Objective-C reproduction (`-fno-objc-arc`) on macOS 27.2.1 (Build 26B131, arm64) showed `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` retaining `1` off-screen window after `orderOut:` + `close` + `release` without `@autoreleasepool` around pre-`[NSApp run]` creation, and `0` with `@autoreleasepool`.

title: fix(relay): refresh the service token in the background; no lock across network calls
body:
Fixes CUA-4415. Follows CUA-4413 (#8608) and CUA-2276.

## What users saw
Several times a week (23 Nov at 15:28, 17:22 and 19:09 UTC; earlier on 10, 13, 16, 17 and 20 Nov; 25 Oct) the relay's calls to the Spaces API stopped for a minute or more, then all went through at once. Cached answers covered members during these stalls, but a longer stall, or a first-time lookup, would have been refused.

## Root cause
Every relay call to the Spaces API first takes the relay's service token. The token cache's lock was held across the HTTP call that mints a new token at the auth server. When that one mint hung (slow connect, DNS or auth server), every Spaces API call queued behind it, and each waiter then retried the mint in turn. The result was zero calls for a minute, then a burst.

The share check had the same shape: one call in flight per owner, but after a failure each waiter asked again, one after another.

## Fix
- **Service token refreshed in the background.** One task mints the next token at 70-80% of the existing skew-safe replace-by point (half the lifetime, CUA-2959), with jitter. Each mint is bounded (6 s) and retried with exponential backoff (1 s doubling, capped at 30 s). The lock only guards reading or swapping the token and is never held across network I/O.
- **Callers never wait while a token is valid.** They read the current token. If a refresh is failing or hanging, they keep using it until close to its real expiry (lifetime minus a tenth, at most 30 s).
- **Only callers with no valid token wait,** at most 6 s, for the single mint in flight. While the refresher is backing off after a failure, callers get the error at once instead of queueing. A 401 still marks the token as refused and triggers one shared re-mint, as before.
- **Share checks share one call's answer or error.** Followers wait (bounded) for the call in flight and no longer retry it one after another.
- **Connect timeouts** added to the remaining outbound HTTP clients (usage meter, share login, TCP shares, pending-device client). All clients already resolve names with the async resolver from #8608.

Audit of other locks held across network calls:
- OIDC signing keys: already renewed in the background (CUA-2323). Only a token with an unknown key id waits, bounded, for one fetch. No change.
- Plan lookups: no lock across I/O (std cache plus a semaphore). No change.
- Usage meter: posts from its own task with no lock held. Connect timeout added.
- Account erase: a deliberate one-at-a-time mutex on an internal admin route. No change.

## Tests
New tests in `org_access::token_refresh_tests`:
- A stub auth server hangs on refresh while a valid token is cached. 32 Spaces API calls all succeed in under 1 s (the mint budget is 5 s), and only one refresh is sent.
- The token has expired and the refresh hangs. 16 concurrent callers fail together inside one bounded wait, with a single mint and no unauthenticated calls. During the backoff that follows, the next caller fails at once. When the auth server recovers, calls work again.
- 16 concurrent first callers share one mint.
- 8 concurrent share checks for one owner against a failing API make 1 call, not 8 in a row.
- Unit tests for the refresh schedule and the backoff.

Existing relay tests pass with and without `--features hosted`, as do clippy `-D warnings` (both feature sets), the CI rustfmt step and `bin/ci --quick`.

## Rollout
Merging does not change prod. Promoting the prod relay is a separate, gated step, together with #8608.

title: [RFC]: structured codes for browser_navigate failures
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

The two failure branches of the `Page.navigate` call in `browser_navigate` should carry a machine-readable code, as many other Cua Driver error results already do with `structuredContent.code`. One code would say that Chromium returned `errorText` for the navigation; the other would say that the driver did not confirm the navigation. A client could then branch on each case without parsing the English message.

### Motivation and current state

After its argument, session and URL checks, `browser_navigate` calls `Page.navigate` through `conn.call` and has two failure branches in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/browser/tools.rs` (lines 1327 and 1341 on `main` at 27d4788cf8a3):

```rust
if let Some(err_text) = result.get("errorText").and_then(Value::as_str) {
    return ToolResult::error(format!("navigation failed: {err_text}"));
}
// …
Err(e) => ToolResult::error(format!("Page.navigate failed: {e}")),
```

Both return `isError: true` with one text block and no `structuredContent`. Before the result leaves the dispatcher, `recovery_hint::annotate` adds `code: invalid_arguments` and a hint only when that text contains a missing-parameter message; otherwise the result keeps no code. Through `cua-driver call`, a client gets exit status 1 and the text on stdout: it knows that the call failed, but it has no stable reason to branch on.

The two branches give different evidence. The first means that Chromium returned a string `errorText` for this navigation. The second means that `conn.call` returned an error (`browser/cdp_ws.rs`): a socket that closed before the send, a send failure, the 20-second reply timeout after the send, or a CDP error reply. In some of these cases the command never reached Chromium; after a reply timeout, Chromium can still carry it out. The tool invalidates its tab snapshots only on the success path.

We integrate Cua Driver 0.55.0 in a computer-use tool that runs `cua-driver call` in a container and turns each failed answer into an error that a model reads. On a host whose network did not reach the requested site, `browser_navigate` failed in both ways:

| Try | Exit | Duration | stdout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 20.1 s | `Page.navigate failed: CDP Page.navigate timed out after 20s` |
| 2 | 1 | 10.1 s | `navigation failed: net::ERR_TIMED_OUT` |

Without a code, the integration can show the text, but it cannot branch on it without parsing the English prefixes of one driver version. Many other error results of the driver already avoid this by adding `.with_structured(json!({ "code": ... }))` to `ToolResult::error(...)`, for example `invalid_arguments` and `option_not_found` in `platform-linux/src/tools/set_value.rs`.

### Goals

- Each failure branch of the `Page.navigate` call carries `structuredContent` with a stable `code` that names the branch.
- When Chromium returns `errorText`, the result carries that string as its own field.
- MCP clients see the same `isError` and the same text block as today.
- `cua-driver call` users keep the human-readable message, inside the JSON object.

### Non-goals

- The errors before the `Page.navigate` call: missing or mistyped arguments, an empty or `default` session, and an unsupported URL scheme. They stay as they are; extending the codes to them can be a follow-up.
- The lock and revalidation refusals of the same tool, which already carry a code.
- Detecting blocked or challenged pages (CAPTCHA, HTTP 429) and retry or backoff policy: #3136 covers those.
- Changing how long `browser_navigate` waits, or adding a wait for page load.
- Codes for the other browser tools.
- A value in `BrowserRefusalCode`: these failures are not refusals (see Alternatives).

### Proposal

In `BrowserNavigateTool`, keep each `ToolResult::error(...)` with its current text and add structured content:

| Branch | `code` | Meaning | Other fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Page.navigate` returned a string `errorText` | `browser_navigation_failed` | Chromium reported this navigation as failed | `error_text`: the string Chromium supplied, unchanged (for example `net::ERR_TIMED_OUT`; not a closed set); `message`: the text block |
| `conn.call` returned an error | `browser_navigation_unconfirmed` | The driver did not confirm the navigation. The code alone does not say whether the command reached Chromium; because some of these failures happen after the send, a client should read the tab's state and refresh its references before a retry | `cdp_error`: the driver's diagnostic text for the failed call, not a stable value; `message`: the text block |

Exactly one of `error_text` and `cdp_error` is present. The codes and field names are the stable contract; the contents of `error_text`, `cdp_error` and `message` are diagnostic. The result does not repeat `url`, `target_id` or `tab_id`: the caller passed them, and a URL can hold private query data.

The change stays in `cua-driver-core`. Wherever a platform build reaches these two branches, it produces the same shape; the platform adapters do not change.

### Alternatives considered

- **Clients parse the text.** No driver change, but each client depends on the English prefixes `navigation failed: ` and `Page.navigate failed: ` of one version, and a wording change silently breaks them.
- **One code with a required discriminator field.** It can express the same two facts, and gives one branch to clients that only care that the call failed; clients that need the distinction must read the field instead of the code. Neither design makes a blind retry safe.
- **A `BrowserRefusalCode` value.** It would reuse the browser vocabulary, but `BrowserRefusal::to_tool_result` leaves `isError` unset ("the call executed correctly and its outcome is the refusal"), so `cua-driver call` would exit 0 and clients that check `isError` would treat a failed navigation as a success. It also extends the closed vocabulary, its exhaustive mirror in `server.rs`, and, when the code needs escalation advice, the map in `action_record.rs`.
- **Fold into #3136.** #3136 classifies blocked states from page content; these failures come from the navigation command call.

### Compatibility and migration

For MCP clients the change adds `structuredContent`; `isError` and the text block do not change. `structured_error_class` in `server.rs` maps an unknown code to `InternalError`, the class these failures have today.

One case changes beyond the new field. Today, when the text of a failed call contains a missing-parameter message (possible in a CDP error reply), `recovery_hint::annotate` gives the result `code: invalid_arguments` and a hint. With structured content present, annotate takes its structured path, and no hint rule matches the new codes, so such a result carries `browser_navigation_unconfirmed` and no hint. The maintainers can add a hint rule for the new codes if they want one.

For `cua-driver call`, stdout changes. When a result has structured content, the CLI prints the JSON object and `call_text` then prints no text for this tool (`cua-driver/src/cli.rs`). The stdout of a failed navigation therefore changes from the text to a JSON object, whose `message` field holds the same text; the exit status stays 1. A script that matches the old stdout must parse the JSON instead, and keep a fallback for older drivers and for the errors that stay without a code.

A revert of the two sites rolls the change back. If the maintainers rate the stdout change as breaking, the title becomes `feat(cua-driver)!` and the RFC stays open for the seven-day review that `docs/rfcs/README.md` recommends for breaking public contracts.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

No new permission. The new fields hold Chromium's error string and the driver's diagnostic text, which the text block already contains; the result adds no URL, identifier or page content. The output grows by up to twice the diagnostic text (`message` and the branch field), which can move a result into another output-size bucket of the existing telemetry; no telemetry field is added.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

- With the existing mock CDP endpoint (`browser/mock_cdp.rs`), a test for each branch through the normal dispatch path, so that `recovery_hint::annotate` runs, asserts the exact `code`, the one field present, `message`, `isError: true` and the unchanged text block. One case uses a CDP error reply whose message contains a missing-parameter text.
- A test of `cua-driver call` for each branch asserts the stdout JSON and exit status 1.
- The change and its tests are in `cua-driver-core`, which every platform build compiles; no platform adapter changes, so the usual CI lanes of each platform are the platform evidence.
- `bin/ci` green.

### Unresolved questions

- The code names, and whether one code per branch or one code with a discriminator field is preferred.
- Whether JSON-only stdout with `message` is acceptable for error results of `cua-driver call`. Printing the text after the JSON would keep the human-readable line, but stdout would still differ from today's text-only output.
- Whether the new codes should get a recovery hint rule.
- Whether the errors before the `Page.navigate` call should get codes in the same change.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: feat(cua-driver): report user input on Windows with get_user_input_events
body:
## Why

#3587 asks for a read-only signal that someone else used the machine while an agent acted, so the agent can mark its cached observation as suspect and read again. Polling `get_cursor_position` only gives the end state: it cannot say who moved the pointer, and it misses a click that starts and ends between two polls. This PR adds `get_user_input_events` on Windows. It is backed by low-level mouse and keyboard hooks, and each event names its source and the window it went to.

## What changed

- **New tool `get_user_input_events` (Windows).** A call without `since` starts watching and returns a `cursor`. Passing that cursor back returns every input since then, plus a new cursor. Each event has:
  - `kind`: `mouse_move`, `mouse_down`, `mouse_up`, `wheel`, `key_down` or `key_up`;
  - `button` and screen `x`/`y` for mouse input;
  - `source`: `hardware`, `driver` or `injected`;
  - `pid` and `window_id` of the target: for mouse input the top-level window holding mouse capture (as during a drag), or else the one under the pointer, except that a wheel goes where Windows routes it (the foreground window under focus routing, or under hybrid routing unless a Store app window is under the pointer); for keys the foreground window;
  - `seq`, `first_time_ms`/`time_ms` and `count`.

  Keys never carry their identity. Consecutive moves from one source to one window fold into one event until a read returns it, so no reader gets a count or start time from before its cursor. Refusals: `unknown_cursor` for a cursor from another driver process, `monitor_unavailable` when the hooks cannot be installed. `history_lost: true` means events after the cursor were lost: they fell out of the 1024-event log, or arrived while a read held the log and its 1024-input queue was full. The description also says that no events does not prove nobody acted.
- **Attribution.** Input without the hook's injected flag reports as `hardware`. The driver's `SendInput` mouse input now sets `dwExtraInfo` to a driver tag, so it reports as `driver`. Anything else injected reports as `injected`, including the driver's own keystrokes (see Tradeoffs). `SetCursorPos` raises no low-level hook event (the Windows E2E run saw none after a desktop `move_cursor`), so the driver's cursor placements are not reported at all.
- **Shared core and thin adapter.** The log, cursor, move folding and the tool live in `cua-driver-core/src/user_input.rs`. The Windows adapter in `platform-windows/src/user_input_monitor.rs` decodes the hook messages and installs the hooks.

## Scope

Covers the hook-event option from the issue, on Windows: events with pid attribution and a source, which the issue author said is strictly more informative than the displacement flag. The displacement probe is not a separate API. A `mouse_move` event with `source: hardware` is that signal.

Not covered:
- **macOS and Linux.** The tool is registered on Windows only, like `debug_window_info`, and the reference marks it Windows. A macOS event tap or an X11 XInput2 monitor can sit behind the same core trait in a follow-up.
- **Pen and touch background input.** Synthetic pointer injection carries no tag, so the driver's pen and touch background clicks and drags report as `injected`. The tool description says so.
- **`PostMessage` delivery.** The driver's background `PostMessage` input never passes through the system input queue, so the hooks do not see it.

## Tradeoffs

- **Watching starts on the first call.** Hooks cost a callback on every system input, so the driver installs them only once a client asks. Input from before that call is not reported.
- **Target, not sender.** The hooks give no sender process, so `pid` names the window the input went to. Sender attribution is coarse: `driver` versus `injected`.
- **Driver keystrokes are untagged.** With the tag on keyboard input, the WPF harness's foreground `type_text` tests stalled on their first text unit and failed the native lane in 3 of 4 runs (45268528093, 45270762232, 45293191421; 45271625444 passed). With keys untagged, 3 of 3 runs passed the lane (45276611665, 45282270810, 45287872978, one stall passing on retry), as main does. The driver's keys therefore keep `dwExtraInfo` 0 and report as `injected`. That never creates a false `hardware` event.
- **Silent hook removal.** Windows removes a low-level hook without notice when its callback exceeds `LowLevelHooksTimeout`. The callback only decodes the input, looks up the target window and records it. Recording never waits on a reader: the input goes through an `mpsc` channel, whose send takes no lock, and is taken into the log when no read holds it. A record takes at most 64 queued inputs into the log, and every read drains the channel first.  The driver still cannot detect a removal if one happens.

## Blast Radius

- **Driver input.** The only change to input the driver already sent is the `dwExtraInfo` value on its `SendInput` mouse input (previously 0). No call path in the driver reads `dwExtraInfo`. The tag is not the touch-promotion signature that apps check for.
- **Other platforms.** macOS and Linux are unchanged.
- **Authorization.** The tool is classified R2 as a private observation, like `list_windows`, and claims the new capability token `input.user_activity.read`.

## Verification

Run on this Linux host:

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 1419 passed at the first head. At this head, 1425 passed, including 15 `user_input::tests` (inputs that overflow the queue count as lost, queued inputs stay ahead of the loss, the lost mark never moves back, and moves do not fold across lost input): ordering, folding only until a read, a record made while a read holds the log, a bounded drain per record, history loss, unknown cursors, the tool's output shape and its refusals. Removing the fold-until-read condition makes the folding test fail.
- `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib user_input_monitor`: 3 passed (mouse and key message decoding, source classification).
- `cargo xwin clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings` on `platform-windows` and `cua-driver-core` (`--tests`) and on `cua-driver-e2e --test user_input_events_windows_test`: clean. Linux clippy on `cua-driver-core` and `platform-windows`: clean.
- `.github/scripts/tests/test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py` and `test_cua_driver_release_wiring.py`: 66 passed.
- `bin/ci --quick`: passes. It could not route the docs generators because pnpm would not activate here. The MCP reference pages were rendered with the generator's own `renderReference` over the committed snapshots. The Windows snapshot entry was written by hand from the tool definition. No per-PR job dumps the Windows registry. The release-tag refresh (`cd-cua-driver-docs.yml`) re-dumps it natively.

Needs a Windows desktop: the new `user_input_events_windows_test`, added to the `native` suite of `scripts/ci/windows/run-rust-e2e.ps1`. The PR gate's quick lane runs only `shared`, and the merge queue runs `native`. It checks that a desktop `scroll` reports a `driver` wheel and no `injected` one, that a desktop `move_cursor` leaves no move reported as `injected` or `hardware`, and that a `SendInput` move from the test process is seen as `injected` moves only. Native-lane dispatch on this head: https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/45306428558. The previous heads `2de1463897` and `6516ad5da3` passed the native lane (runs 45302278837 and 45298125001). Runs on earlier heads are listed under Tradeoffs; on every head since `9e4b4da072` this test passed.

Fixes #3587

title: fix(cua-driver): wait for Edge's quiet permission indicator in the browser E2E
body:
Refs CUA-3855.

For users: nothing changes. This unblocks every PR, because the required check "quarantine list and flaky tooling" fails on all of them since the quarantine entry for `handover_process::the_next_relay_waits_then_serves_what_queued` expired on 22 Nov.

**Root cause.** The flake was a race in the test's own setup: it picks a free port by binding port 0 and closing it, then starts the relay on that port. A parallel test process could take the port in between, and the relay died with "address in use". That was fixed in #7003 (the test now retries the start on fresh ports when the relay exits while starting). The quarantine entry added next to it was never removed, and was renewed once without a new failure.

**Why it is safe to remove.** I read the relay's startup and standby code too: it binds the main port and then the health port before waiting for the state lock, so "health answers" really means both ports are held, and no further race turned up. Stability evidence, with 0 failures:
- 40 serial runs of the test
- 96 runs, 12 in parallel, with 8 CPU hogs running
- 60 runs, 6 in parallel, alongside the `shutdown` and `mesh_default` relay process tests and 6 CPU hogs
- about 30 sampled spacesd CI runs since 8 Nov: the test passes on the first try, with no retry or failure

The change deletes the entry, so a regression fails the spacesd lanes again instead of being forgiven. `flaky.py validate` passes and `bin/ci --quick` is green.
