title: build(deps): bump setuptools from 81.0.0 to 84.1.0
body:
Bumps [setuptools](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools) from 81.0.0 to 84.1.0.
Changelog

Sourced from setuptools's changelog.

v84.1.0

Features

  • setuptools.archive_util now raises the new UnsafeMember exception when an archive member would be extracted outside of the extraction directory, where previously such a member was silently skipped. Aborting makes a malicious or malformed archive visible to the caller instead of yielding a quietly incomplete extraction, and matches the behavior of the standard library's tarfile extraction filters.

Bugfixes

  • Wheel.install_as_egg no longer creates namespace package directories outside of the destination egg directory. Entries in a wheel's namespace_packages.txt were split on . and passed straight to os.path.join, so an entry that was absolute, drive-qualified, or UNC discarded the destination and placed an __init__.py at a path chosen by the wheel. Namespace entries are now validated as dotted module names on every platform -- see GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w.

    This code path is reached only by the deprecated setup_requires mechanism when setup() is invoked outside a PEP 517 frontend; the setuptools build backend never reaches it.

  • setuptools.archive_util no longer extracts archive members outside of the requested extraction directory. Both the tar and zip formats specify / as the only path separator, but the guard against .. components split member names on / alone, so a name such as ..\escaped.txt was treated as a single component and then resolved as a traversal by the filesystem on Windows. Member names containing a backslash, a drive letter, or a UNC prefix are now rejected on every platform, as are members whose resolved destination falls outside the extraction directory -- see GHSA-grgh-hr87-3jpw.

v84.0.0

Features

title: feat(lume): optional runs without audio or clipboard devices
body:
## Summary

Optional hardening: run macOS VMs without clipboard/audio devices.

Today every `lume run` attaches a virtio sound device wired to the host's audio input and output, and a SPICE agent console port that shares the host clipboard. Some deployments want a guest with neither. This adds two opt-outs:

- `lume run --no-audio-device`: the VM gets no sound device, so the guest has no audio device and no path to the host's microphone or speakers.
- `lume run --no-clipboard-device`: the VM gets no SPICE agent clipboard port, and lume's SSH clipboard sync (automatic with the native display) stays off. It is rejected together with `--clipboard`.
- The HTTP run API takes the same options as `noAudioDevice` and `noClipboardDevice`.

Defaults are unchanged: both devices stay attached unless a run asks otherwise.

A VM with a saved state (`suspend`) whose devices differ from the requested set cannot restore into the new configuration, so it boots fresh with the requested devices; the requested set always wins.

## Changes

- `HostDeviceOptions` builds the sound and clipboard devices; the macOS and Linux configurations both use it instead of attaching them unconditionally.
- Options threaded through `Run`, `RunVMRequest`, the HTTP handler, `LumeController.runVM` and `VM.run`.
- Reference docs (`cli.mdx`, `http-api.mdx`) and `cli-specs/lume.json` regenerated with `docs:generate:lume`.

## Tests

- New `HostDeviceOptionsTests`: default configuration has both devices; each flag removes exactly its device; other console devices are kept; flag and API parsing; `--clipboard` conflict; native clipboard sync stays off.
- `swift test` in `libs/lume`: 281 tests pass.

title: fix(images): fetch omarchy Arch packages through curl and cache them per week
body:
Omarchy image builds no longer fail when archive.archlinux.org stalls on a package download.

**What changed for users:** the daily Omarchy image release stops failing on a slow Arch package server, so `omarchy:edge` stays fresh. The packages installed are the same dated snapshot as before.

**Cause:** run 45256854452 failed on `bash-5.3.20-1` ("Operation too slow. Less than 1 bytes/sec transferred the last 10 seconds"). pacman's built-in downloader hard-codes that 10 s limit, and archive.archlinux.org is the only host that keeps old package versions (I found no public mirror of it that serves the dated snapshots). Retrying the same download is not a fix.

**Fix:**
- pacman downloads through curl during the build (`files/pacman-build-xfer.conf`): resumable, with a real 60 s stall timeout. The setting is removed before the layer ends, so the guest's `pacman.conf` is unchanged.
- `/var/cache/pacman/pkg` is a BuildKit cache mount in both `Dockerfile` and `vm.Dockerfile`. `cd-image-omarchy.yml` restores a weekly GitHub Actions cache into it (`scripts/images/omarchy-pkgcache.sh`) and saves it again after the build, even if a gate fails, when the package set changed. Each package version then comes from the archive once, not once per run.
- Reproducibility is unchanged: the snapshot day is still resolved the same way, and pacman checks every cached file against the snapshot database and its signature. A cache miss is a normal download.

Other Arch builds (cua-e2b template, CI containers) use `archlinux:base` without the archive, so they have nothing to change.

Checked: actionlint, shellcheck, `docker buildx build --check` on `vm.Dockerfile`, `bin/ci --quick`. The full image build runs in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): report why a Windows key press stalled, and what the doctor's form read
body:
## What changes for users

When Cua Driver can't confirm that a Windows app read a key press, the error now says whether the app was still responding and where its focus was. Before, it only said the key "may still appear". The Windows image check also records what its test form actually received.

## Why

The Windows image release run 45256854452 failed `input.type` in `windows / verify` with `input_delivery_stalled` on a single Backspace. The image ships Cua Driver 0.60.0 (linked into cua-spacesd 0.17.5, matching its pin), so the image isn't running an old driver. "doctor" had already been typed and read. Only the Backspace that followed was never confirmed, and the form answered accessibility calls right afterwards. The same disk passed `input.type` before the push in the same run, and earlier Windows verify runs passed it too. So far this has failed once.

The key-press stall error gave none of the evidence that the text stall error already gives, so the logs can't tell a target that was busy in its own handler from a target that never got the input. This PR doesn't guess a fix. It makes the next occurrence show which of those two it is:

- `input_delivery_stalled` on the foreground key path now includes the foreground window and the attachment's stall detail: whether the target thread answers WM_NULL within 200 ms, its queue's active and focus HWNDs, and how many sent-message batches the driver answered while attached.
- In `cua-spacesd doctor`, a failed press in `input.type` now lists the key presses, entry changes and focus records the form logged after the press.

No retries, no longer timeouts, no behaviour change.

## Testing

- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: green.
- `cargo check -p cua-spacesd-doctor`: green.
- The Windows crate is checked by the Windows CI lanes on this PR.

Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

title: [Feature]: Allow configuring macOS agent_display position/arrangement (avoid default left-edge cursor trapping)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### User problem

On macOS, calling `agent_display({action: "create"})` creates a `CGVirtualDisplay` without configuring its origin in the display layout, so macOS WindowServer defaults to placing the virtual display on the left edge of the user's primary screen.

As a result, when a user moves their mouse to the left edge of their primary monitor, the hardware pointer easily slips into the invisible virtual display and gets "eaten"/trapped off-screen.

In addition, because `NEXT_SERIAL` in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/virtual_display.rs` increments on every `create()` call (`0x6001`, `0x6002`, ...) while `VENDOR_ID` (`0x0505`) and `PRODUCT_ID` (`0x5678`) are fixed, macOS treats each newly created virtual display as a brand-new monitor and cannot remember the user's manual arrangement from System Settings > Displays across sessions.

### Desired outcome

1. Allow callers (and/or driver config) to specify where `agent_display({action: "create"})` places the virtual display relative to the main display — e.g. a `placement` option (`right`, `left`, `top`, `bottom`, `bottom_right_corner`, `top_right_corner`) and/or explicit `origin_x` / `origin_y` coordinates.
2. Support a cursor-safe corner placement (such as bottom-right diagonal touching by 1px, `(main_width, main_height - 1)`), so all four primary-screen edges remain natural cursor stops while keeping coordinates positive and avoiding menu bar interference.
3. Return the post-arrangement `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` from `agent_display({action: "create"})` so subsequent `set_window_frame` calls use accurate coordinates immediately without a race condition.

### Current workaround

Currently users must either:
- Manually drag the virtual display in System Settings > Displays every time a new virtual display is created (not persisted across creates within the same daemon lifetime due to incrementing `NEXT_SERIAL`), or
- Run a separate local CoreGraphics script calling `CGBeginDisplayConfiguration` / `CGConfigureDisplayOrigin` / `CGCompleteDisplayConfiguration` after `agent_display({action: "create"})` and then re-query `agent_display({action: "list"})` for updated coordinates.

### Affected components and platforms

- `cua-driver` (`v0.60.0`), macOS (`platform-macos`)
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/tools/agent_display.rs`
- `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/virtual_display.rs`

### Alternatives and prior art

- Related issues: #7597 (initial macOS `agent_display` tool), #8603 (display outliving calling session), #8604 (`launch_app` option to open windows on an agent display). None of these cover display arrangement/origin control or serial persistence.
- External tools like `displayplacer` or custom `CGDisplayRegisterReconfigurationCallback` daemons work asynchronously after creation, which creates a coordinate race with the `x, y` already returned by `agent_display({action: "create"})`.

### Implementation ideas

In `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/virtual_display.rs`:
1. After `applySettings:` succeeds and `displayID` is obtained, configure the display origin via public CoreGraphics APIs (`CGBeginDisplayConfiguration`, `CGConfigureDisplayOrigin`, `CGCompleteDisplayConfiguration` with `kCGConfigureForSession`) before returning `bounds_of(display_id)`.
2. Consider reusing a deterministic serial slot (e.g. lowest unused serial starting at `0x6001` once prior virtu

- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse Windows pixel clicks outside the target window
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, a pixel `click` aimed at a window on a secondary monitor could land on another window (the reporter saw `Progman`) and then fail with `foreground_unavailable`. `x`/`y` are window-local screenshot pixels, and the driver adds the window's screen origin to them. The reporter passed screen pixels `[3228, 770]` for a window whose frame starts near x=1920. On the primary monitor the origin is about `(0, 0)`, so the two frames agree and the mistake never shows. On the secondary monitor the point became about `(5148, 770)`, outside the window and outside the 3840 px virtual desktop, and `SendInput` clamped it to whatever sat at the edge.
- What changed: `click`, `double_click` and `right_click` now refuse a window-local point outside the target window's screenshot frame before sending any input. The refusal uses `point_outside_window`, the code Linux already returns and the shared recovery hint already handles. It gives the window's bounds and origin, and says to send screen pixels through `click` with `scope:"desktop"` (with `count:2` or `button:"right"` for the other two tools). The check runs on the unrounded point and maps it to the pixel that contains it, so a fraction just past an edge is refused instead of being pulled back onto the edge. A `capture_id` point now maps to its containing pixel instead of being rounded, so a valid point in the last half pixel still lands inside the window.

The issue's two proposed fixes were already in place before 0.23.2. `MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK` normalization has been in `send_click_synthesized` since #1705, and the Per-Monitor-V2 manifests have been in both executables. Neither one caused this bug.

The issue's second point, `accessibility.element_tokens` missing from `click`'s capabilities, is already fixed on main: the shared capability map in `cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs` declares it for every tool that takes a token, and `every_token_accepting_tool_claims_element_tokens_capability` plus `protocol_element_token_test.rs` check it. This PR does not change it.

## Related work

Fixes #3613

RFC: not required. `point_outside_window` is already part of the shared refusal contract (Linux, `cua-driver-contract`, `recovery_hint`). Windows now returns it where it used to send misrouted input.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. A pixel click, double-click or right-click whose window-local point falls outside the target window is now refused with no input sent. Before, the point was sent anyway and hit whatever was on screen there. Points inside the window, element-token clicks, `scope:"desktop"` clicks, and clicks with a `capture_id` (already bounds-checked at admission) work as before. If the window frame can't be read, the point is mapped as before.
- Risk and rollback: the risk is a caller that relied on clicking just outside its target window through a window-scoped click. Such a caller should use `scope:"desktop"`. Rollback is a revert.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `window_point.rs` unit tests cover the reporter's layout (inside points map by the frame origin, the reporter's screen point is refused with `point_outside_window`, and each edge just outside the frame is refused, including fractions and NaN). `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib window_point` passed locally. The module is cross-platform, so these tests run on any host. The quick stage of the scoped repository checks (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) passed locally.
- Manual or platform evidence: none. The multi-monitor Windows case was not reproduced on hardware here.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the Windows build, clippy and unit tests for `platform-windows`, and the Windows desktop lanes, run in CI.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [x] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied.
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`): only `bin/ci --quick` ran locally. The heavy checks run in CI.

title: fix(cua-driver): fail Linux doctor when the RemoteDesktop portal backend offers no input devices
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on GNOME Wayland, `cua-driver doctor` passed `wayland_backend` while every click and key press failed with `No such interface 'org.freedesktop.impl.portal.RemoteDesktop'`. Doctor only checked that the portal frontend exports RemoteDesktop. In the reported setup the frontend routed RemoteDesktop to `xdg-desktop-portal-kde`, which doesn't export the backend interface in a Mutter session. This is finding 1.A of the field report.
- What changed:
  - When it starts, xdg-desktop-portal copies `AvailableDeviceTypes` from the backend it routes RemoteDesktop to. If that backend doesn't export `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.RemoteDesktop`, the frontend's public `AvailableDeviceTypes` is 0. The frontend listens for the wrong notify signal, so the value isn't refreshed when a backend exports the interface later, and 0 alone can be stale.
  - Doctor now reads the property from the running frontend. When it lacks a keyboard or a pointer, doctor creates a RemoteDesktop session through the same route and closes it right away. That shows no consent dialog, which only appears with `Start`. `wayland_backend` fails only when the backend refuses that session. The message names the likely cause, and the hint says to set `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.RemoteDesktop=<backend>` in the `portals.conf` in use, keeping its other entries, and restart the portal.
  - A property read that fails or times out keeps the old verdict, and `LIBEI_SOCKET` (which bypasses the portal) skips the check.
  - The troubleshooting guide covers this failure and finding 1.B. GNOME grants capture and input separately (**Allow Remote Interaction**), and **Remember This Selection** saves the grant to `~/.config/cua-driver/libei-persistent.token`.

## Related work

Fixes #3638

RFC: not required. This adds a doctor failure case and changes no contract.

## Scope

Covers findings 1.A and 1.B. Leaves out 1.C (overlay vs the Mutter screenshot portal), 1.D (AT-SPI without Orca; the driver already avoids toggling those flags), 1.E (X11 `TranslateCoordinates` on Wayland-native windows) and the macOS notes. None of those were reproduced against the current release, and the maintainer comment on the issue asks for each to be filed separately.

The report says xdg-desktop-portal ignores a `0600` `portals.conf`. That wasn't verified, and this PR doesn't check file modes. The portal runs as the same user, who can read a `0600` file they own.

## Tradeoffs

- An earlier revision of this PR predicted the route from `portals.conf` and the installed `.portal` files. Review found it couldn't match every frontend version (selection rules differ between 1.18, 1.20 and 1.22), build layout, or config edit made after the portal started. Reading the running frontend's own property needs none of that, so the prediction was removed.
- The failure names the likely cause (another desktop's backend) instead of the backend that is actually routed. The frontend doesn't expose which backend it picked.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: Linux `doctor` on portal/libei builds can now fail `wayland_backend` where it used to pass, only when the running frontend's RemoteDesktop offers no keyboard or no pointer and the backend it routes to refuses a session. In that state input can't be delivered anyway. No CLI, MCP or schema change.
- Risk and rollback: one extra D-Bus property read on the RemoteDesktop proxy doctor already creates. Only when a keyboard or pointer is missing, doctor also creates and closes one RemoteDesktop session. Each step has its own 2 s timeout. Anything that fails or times out keeps the old verdict. Revert to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks:
  - `cargo test -p platform-linux --features portal-input --lib health_report` passes 14 tests, three of them new. A mutation that ignores missing devices fails two of them.
  - `cargo clippy -p platform-linux --tests -- -D warnings` is clean with and without `portal-input`.
  - The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`) are green.
- Manual or platform evidence: I ran the real `xdg-desktop-portal` 1.20.3 on this host under `dbus-run-session` with `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME`, the host's stock `gnome.portal`/`kde.portal` files, and fake `gnome` and `kde` backends. The fake `gnome` exports `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.RemoteDesktop` with `AvailableDeviceTypes=3`; the fake `kde` doesn't export it. With `default=gnome`, the frontend's `RemoteDesktop.AvailableDeviceTypes` read through ashpd 0.13.11 (the driver's version) was 3. With `default=kde` the frontend logged `Using kde.portal for org.freedesktop.impl.portal.RemoteDesktop (config)`, the property was 0, and `CreateSession` came back `Response(Other)`. When the gnome backend missed the frontend's startup property load (the stale case), the property was 0 but `CreateSession` succeeded and closed. A frontend without RemoteDesktop gives ashpd's `PortalNotFound`, which doctor already treats as unreachable.
- Known gaps or CI still required: not run on a real GNOME or KDE Wayland session, and the end-to-end `doctor` binary wasn't built here (shared host). CI runs the full build and tests.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above.
- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.
- [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change.
- [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included.
- [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. (Not applicable: this releases with Cua Driver.)
- [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`). Only `bin/ci --quick` ran here (shared host). The heavy checks run in CI.

title: build(deps): bump setuptools from 84.0.0 to 84.1.0 in /docs/scripts/docs-mcp-server
body:
Bumps [setuptools](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools) from 84.0.0 to 84.1.0.
Changelog

Sourced from setuptools's changelog.

v84.1.0

Features

  • setuptools.archive_util now raises the new UnsafeMember exception when an archive member would be extracted outside of the extraction directory, where previously such a member was silently skipped. Aborting makes a malicious or malformed archive visible to the caller instead of yielding a quietly incomplete extraction, and matches the behavior of the standard library's tarfile extraction filters.

Bugfixes

  • Wheel.install_as_egg no longer creates namespace package directories outside of the destination egg directory. Entries in a wheel's namespace_packages.txt were split on . and passed straight to os.path.join, so an entry that was absolute, drive-qualified, or UNC discarded the destination and placed an __init__.py at a path chosen by the wheel. Namespace entries are now validated as dotted module names on every platform -- see GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w.

    This code path is reached only by the deprecated setup_requires mechanism when setup() is invoked outside a PEP 517 frontend; the setuptools build backend never reaches it.

  • setuptools.archive_util no longer extracts archive members outside of the requested extraction directory. Both the tar and zip formats specify / as the only path separator, but the guard against .. components split member names on / alone, so a name such as ..\escaped.txt was treated as a single component and then resolved as a traversal by the filesystem on Windows. Member names containing a backslash, a drive letter, or a UNC prefix are now rejected on every platform, as are members whose resolved destination falls outside the extraction directory -- see GHSA-grgh-hr87-3jpw.

title: fix(cua-driver): keep the Windows agent cursor overlay in its z-slot while idle
body:
## What changed for users

The agent cursor overlay on Windows now reliably sits directly above the window the agent is driving as soon as an action starts, instead of occasionally staying in the wrong layer for a moment.

## Root cause

The overlay re-asserted its z-order only on ticks that painted pixels, at most once per 80 ms, with no trailing pass. If the pin target changed on a tick that painted nothing, or the last painted frame fell inside the 80 ms window, the overlay kept a stale slot until some later render. The release-gate test `agent_cursor_overlay_obeys_untargeted_and_targeted_z_order` then timed out after 2 s waiting for the overlay to sit above its target (merge-group run 45312318357; the "Windows agent cursor" case was also flaky in #8566).

## Fix (product)

In `platform-windows/src/overlay.rs`:
- compute the pin target on every tick, not only rendered ticks
- re-assert immediately when the pin target changes
- otherwise re-assert (throttled to 80 ms) whenever the overlay is observably not directly above its target, including on the idle heartbeat

The test is unchanged: it already waits on the real z-order via `GW_HWNDPREV` with a bounded deadline. No retries, longer sleeps or loosened assertions.

## Validation

`bin/ci --quick --fix` passes and the non-Windows build of the crate checks. The Windows code path cannot be compiled or run on the author's Mac; the Windows E2E lane in CI is the real check.

Refs #8566

title: fix(cua-driver): create every Windows UIA client through uia::new_automation
body:
Draft, not proposed for merge. I could not find a fix for #3656 that the evidence supports. This PR records the investigation; the decision on next steps is a maintainer's.

## Why

#3656 reports an elevated `cua-driver serve` (0.23.2) crashing with 0xC0000005 in `uiautomationcore.dll` 7.2.19041.4355 at offset `0x30eb1`, while walking an elevated Task Manager.

## What was found

- **The faulting function.** With Microsoft's public symbols for that exact DLL build, offset `0x30eb1` falls in `NavigationHelperProxyOneCore::GetParentViewId`. The faulting instruction reads a method from the vtable of the ComponentUI broker that `EnsureComponentUIBroker` caches at `this+0x278`. The pointer slot itself reads fine; the vtable it points to does not.
- **The cached broker is process-wide and never released.** `NavigationHelperProxyOneCore` is a singleton that a global holds for the life of the process and releases only from `DllMain`. `+0x278` is written in the constructor, filled by `EnsureComponentUIBroker`, and released only in the destructor. `EnsureComponentUIBroker` creates a manager object out of process (`CoCreateInstance`, `CLSCTX_LOCAL_SERVER`), calls its vtable slot 3 to get the broker, then releases the manager. If the broker returned through slot 3 is not referenced independently of the manager, it dangles on first use. That would fail deterministically, which fits the four identical crashes in the report. This is inferred from the disassembly, not observed.
- **The hypothesis I first built a fix around does not hold.** My first idea was that the daemon's paired `CoInitializeEx`/`CoUninitialize` calls let COM shut down between calls and unload the proxy code. Probes on a `windows-latest` runner, each run alone in its own process, show that once a process makes any real UIA call, the implicit MTA stays alive. That held at every check for at least 12 minutes, whether the caller was an STA that called `CoUninitialize`, an MTA that called `CoUninitialize`, or an MTA thread that exited without uninitializing. The broker is only created during a real UIA call, so COM never shuts down under it. Pinning the MTA with `CoIncrementMTAUsage` is therefore not a fix, and that commit is not pushed.
- **No reproduction on current Windows.** A runner built from `main` started an elevated `cua-driver serve`, opened an elevated Task Manager, then ran `health_report`, `list_windows`, pid-filtered `list_windows` and `get_window_state` three or four times. The daemon stayed up on Server 2025 (uiautomationcore 7.2.26100.1, 237 elements) and on Server 2022 (7.2.20348.1, 11 elements). No Windows 10 19041 runner was available.

## What this branch contains

- `uia::new_automation()`: every `CoCreateInstance(&CUIAutomation, ...)` site now goes through one constructor. This changes no behavior. It is the single place a future fix would go.
- No test. An MTA-lifetime test was added and then removed: it passed or failed depending on which other tests shared its process, and it guarded nothing related to #3656.

## Scope

Investigation only. It contains no change that addresses #3656.

## Verification

- Symbolization: `uiautomationcore.dll` and `UIAutomationCore.pdb` for 7.2.19041.4355 (x64) from the Microsoft symbol server, disassembled with `llvm-objdump`.
- COM apartment probes and the elevated Task Manager repro ran on throwaway branches through `workflow_dispatch` of `CI: Rust Windows unit` (`windows-latest` and `windows-2022`).
- Nothing here ran on Windows 10 19041.

title: docs(rfc): propose bounded desktop held input
body:
## Why

#3757 asks for a recorded RFC decision before any public SDK or MCP held-input operation ships. Its proposal document, #3759 by @steipete, was closed as stale before review, so no decision exists yet. This PR puts that proposal back up for review on current main, so maintainers can record a decision under the [RFC process](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/main/docs/rfcs/README.md#lifecycle).

## What changed

- Salvaged from #3759: @steipete's two commits are cherry-picked as authored, adding `docs/rfcs/3757-bounded-held-input.md` with `status: review`.
- Two follow-up commits put the file in `docs/rfcs/` (RFCs moved there after #3759), fixes the relative link to `cua-driver-contract/src/inputs.rs`, records that #3489 has since merged, and points `rfc_pr` at this PR.

## Scope

This PR only adds the proposal document. It adds no `hold_inputs` code, schema, or capability. Implementation waits for the maintainer decision in #3757, as the RFC's own decision record says. That's why this PR uses `Refs #3757` rather than closing the discussion issue, and why it's a draft: under the lifecycle, the RFC merges once it's `accepted`, before or with the first implementation PR.

## Blast Radius

Docs only. No code, generated contract, or release-tracked package changes.

- On main, `PressKeyInput` and `HotkeyInput` still carry no duration, and no held-input operation exists, so the RFC's "Current state" section still holds.

Refs #3757

title: [Bug]: docs_capability_manifests fails on Windows: permissions.mdx example executable is not absolute
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

`documented_capability_manifests_load_in_bounded_mode` (added in #8579) fails on Windows. The manifest example in `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/guides/permissions.mdx` uses `executable: /usr/bin/example-editor`, and the driver rejects it on Windows because that path is not absolute there.

### Reproduction

1. On Windows, check out `main` at `287362472`.
2. In `libs/cua-driver/rust`, run `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --test docs_capability_manifests --locked`.
3. The test `documented_capability_manifests_load_in_bounded_mode` fails. It failed in both of my runs: one full `cargo test -p cua-driver-core -p cua-driver --locked --no-fail-fast` run, and one run of this test alone.

### Expected behavior

The test passes on Windows, as it does on Linux and macOS, or it does not run on platforms where the documented example path is not valid.

### Actual behavior

```
documented capability manifests the driver rejects:
<repo>\docs/content/docs/cua-driver\guides\permissions.mdx:89: application executable identities must be canonical absolute paths
test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored
```

The fence at `permissions.mdx:89` contains:

```yaml
resources:
  apps:
    - executable: /usr/bin/example-editor   # macOS: bundle_id: com.example.Editor
```

`session_manifest.rs` rejects an executable when `Path::is_absolute()` is false. On Windows, `Path::new("/usr/bin/example-editor").is_absolute()` is false, because a Windows absolute path needs a drive or UNC prefix.

All other tests in that full run passed (1927 passed, 1 failed, 19 ignored).

### Environment

Cua component and version/commit: cua-driver-rs 0.61.2, `main` at `287362472`
Operating system and architecture: Windows 11 Pro (build 26200), x86_64
Toolchain: rustc 1.100.0, cargo 1.100.0

### Evidence

The error text above is from the test log. No other artifact.

### Workaround and additional context

Regression range: the test was added in #8579 (`d838b25d8`). The example in `permissions.mdx` is older.

`ci-rust-windows.yml` builds this test with `--all-targets --no-run`, but it runs only `cua-driver-core --lib` and `--test recording_shutdown_errors`. So Windows CI does not run this test, and that can explain why CI did not catch it.

The page itself says "an absolute `executable` on Windows and Linux", so the example is a Linux path. I do not know which fix you prefer. Some options: run the test only on Unix, give the test a Windows path for this example, or add a Windows example to the docs.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-driver): fall back to a pixel right-click when AXShowMenu opens no menu
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `right_click` with an element and `click` with `button: "right"` reported a context menu as shown whenever `AXShowMenu` returned success. Many AppKit views advertise the action and do nothing, so the agent was told a menu was open when none was, and the pixel right-click fallback never ran.
- What changed:
  - After a successful `AXShowMenu`, the driver waits up to 500 ms for a new menu-level window (layer 101) from the target pid. When none appears it right-clicks the element center, the fallback it already used for elements that do not advertise the action, and the reply names the reason.
  - `right_click` and `click` (`button: "right"` or `action: "show_menu"` on any role other than a popup or menu button) share `show_menu_outcome` and `right_click_element_center`. A popup or menu button keeps its existing accessibility-tree menu wait.
  - If the window list can't be read, the reply says the menu is unconfirmed and does not claim it opened.

## Related work

Fixes #3808

RFC: not required. The MCP tool contract is unchanged; only reply text and the fallback behavior change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: a no-op `AXShowMenu` now gets a real right-click at the element center, and the reply changes from `Shown menu ...` to `Right-clicked ... (pixel right-click; AXShowMenu returned success but no menu opened)`. A menu that opens adds `its menu is on screen` to the reply. An `AXShowMenu` that opens nothing now takes up to 500 ms longer.
- Risk: an app that opens its menu more than 500 ms after `AXShowMenu` returns would get a second right-click. Rollback is reverting this PR.
- Scope: macOS only. Windows, X11 and Wayland do not dispatch `AXShowMenu` and are unchanged. The macOS MCP reference snapshot is regenerated by the docs release workflow on a macOS runner.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new hermetic unit tests `right_click::tests::a_show_menu_that_opens_no_menu_is_not_reported_as_shown` and `a_failed_show_menu_does_not_wait_for_a_menu`; `windows::tests::menu_polling_keeps_an_unreadable_window_list_unknown` now also covers waiting for a menu to open. The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs) pass.
- Manual or platform evidence: none from the authoring host, which is Linux and cannot build `platform-macos`. The macOS build, clippy and unit tests run in CI.
- Known gaps: no live repro against an AppKit view whose `AXShowMenu` is a no-op.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop macOS type_text reporting a stale field's read-back as incomplete
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, keystroke `type_text` into an addressed element verified delivery only by reading `AXValue` off the pointer it resolved before typing. AppKit edits an `NSTextField` through a field editor, and some apps re-create the edited row, so that pointer can keep the pre-edit string while the text lands. Complete delivery came back as `type_text_incomplete`, with advice to retype a suffix that was already in the field.
- What changed: `cgevent_type_verified` also reads the window's focused field (through `focused_element_in_window`, so a sibling window's focus is never used). The baseline is taken just before the keys go out, and only when the focused element is the addressed element or inside it. It records the value and the caret or selection. On each later read, `focus_evidence` reports one of three things:
  - **Confirms**: focus is still inside the addressed element and holds exactly the baseline with the payload typed at that caret or over that selection. The result is complete.
  - **Left**: focus is no longer inside the addressed element, because the app replaced it or moved focus. A partial or unchanged read off the stale pointer becomes unverified (`delivered_chars` absent, no retype), not a shortfall to retry.
  - **Silent**: anything else. The addressed result stands.
  
  `await_typed_delivery` now takes a progress closure instead of a single value reader.

## Related work

Fixes #3809

RFC: not needed; no contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible impact: for a field edited through a field editor, delivery that landed is reported as delivered. For a row the app re-created, the result is unverified (confirm with a screenshot) instead of a false `type_text_incomplete` that invites a duplicate suffix. No accessibility attribute reliably identifies a re-created row (an `AXIdentifier` can be shared by every row of a list), so that case is never reported as confirmed. With no addressed element, or no window, nothing changes.
- Risk and rollback: the focused field can only confirm on an exact match inside the addressed element. Otherwise it downgrades a shortfall to unverified, which never retypes. A field that already held the text, an edit away from the caret, or an unknown caret confirm nothing. Revert the commits to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new unit tests `a_stale_addressed_read_is_corrected_by_the_focused_field` (a stale addressed read plus a field editor holding `555-1234` reports complete; a replaced row reports unverified with no retype; the full table of how the evidence adjusts each result) and `the_focused_field_confirms_only_the_payload_typed_at_its_caret` (caret insert and typed-over selection confirm; a field outside the addressed element, a baseline outside it, a field that already held the text, `555-1234`→`555-12345`, `aaa`→`aaaa` with the caret at the end, an unknown caret, and an edit away from the caret do not). Existing `await_typed_delivery` tests moved to the new signature with the same intent.
- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs). This Linux host cannot build the macOS crate; the macOS Rust CI lanes compile, lint and run the unit tests.
- Known gaps or CI still required: a live Contacts repro on macOS was not run here.

title: fix(images): settle the Omarchy e2e guest before typing and keep forensics on failure
body:
## What
The scheduled Omarchy image gate (https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/45333401375, job 138271798497) failed in e2e/amd64:

- `SDK type + key into foot`: `foreground_unavailable (stale_target)` from `cua do type`.
- `desktop stream: type + key into foot`: the file held `cua-e2e-typed-... cua-e2e-stream-...`.

The second failure is a consequence of the first. The SDK type had already put part of its text into the terminal when the plugin refused a later key with `stale_target`. That half-typed line was never ended, so the next check's text was appended to it.

The build itself is fine. An earlier run of the same image (run 45291413953) passed this check, so this is a timing failure, not a deterministic one.

## Cause
`stale_target` comes from the Hyprland plugin when a key's target window fails its live lookup or geometry check. The harness started input the moment `hyprctl` answered. On the software-emulated guest the session autostart and each new shell's rc files were still running (Hyprland sat near 270% CPU in the same run), so input went into a desktop that was still rearranging itself. Typing took about 9 s in the failing run.

No guest log was kept, so the exact plugin-side trigger can't be read from the artifacts. This PR removes the harness race and makes the next occurrence attributable.

## Changes (tests/e2e/omarchy/omarchy_e2e.py)
- Wait for the guest to be idle (CPU) after the session is up and after each terminal launch, before sending input.
- End any half-typed line before each later typing check, so one failure cannot cascade into the next check.
- On any failed check, save `hyprctl` clients/layers/activewindow, the Hyprland log tail, process list and user journal into the evidence directory.

`cd-images-spacesd-release.yml` has been red behind this gate; it should recover once Omarchy is green.

If it still reproduces with the forensics, the fix belongs in the Hyprland plugin and will be a separate PR.

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): stop Hyprland refocus passes from cancelling foreground typing
body:
## What changes for users

On Hyprland (the Omarchy image), typing into a window with foreground delivery no longer stops part-way when the desktop is busy, for example while bars and notifications start up after login. If the user really moves the mouse or touches the keyboard mid-type, typing still stops, and the error now says `foreground_interrupted` instead of calling a live window `stale_target`.

## Root cause

The scheduled Omarchy image build failed the e2e gate on both attempts of https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/45333401375 with `cua do type ... -> foreground_unavailable (stale_target)` after part of the text was typed into a live foot window.

Foreground text is sent one key at a time: `FOREGROUND_TARGET` binds a token, then `KEY` uses it. The plugin cancels a foreground lane on any user input, and it listened to Hyprland's `input.mouse.move` bus event for pointer motion. Hyprland emits that event from `mouseMoveUnified`, which it also runs with no device event at all: `simulateMouseMovement()` and `refocus()` after a layer surface, popup or subsurface maps or commits, a workspace or monitor change, and so on. Those passes report the cursor where it already was.

Each such pass cancelled the lane and cleared the client's token. The next `KEY` then found an empty token and was refused as `stale_target`, although the window was fine. On an idle desktop the gap between `FOREGROUND_TARGET` and `KEY` is short and nothing maps in it. During session autostart (Hyprland near 270% CPU), layer surfaces map often and each key takes longer, so a refocus pass lands inside a gap and typing stops mid-string.

## Fix

- `src/external_pointer_motion.hpp`: a `mouse.move` emission counts as the user's motion only when the floored cursor position changed. Hyprland only reaches that emission from a device when the floored position changed, so real motion is still caught. The plugin rebases after its own `warpTo`, so a later refocus pass at the warped position does not cancel its own action.
- `input_experiment.cpp`: the `mouse.move` listener uses that filter. Buttons, wheel, keys, touch and tablet still cancel unconditionally.
- When the desktop (not the client) retires a bound foreground target (`foreground_interrupted`, `primary_target_busy`), the next action on it is refused with that code instead of `stale_target`. Explicit Stop/Cancel and unbound clients are unchanged.
- No timeout or retry was changed.

## Tests

- New `tests/external_pointer_motion_test.cpp` (CTest): reproduces the old rule refusing a live target with `stale_target` when refocus passes land between `FOREGROUND_TARGET` and `KEY`, and checks the whole 46-character command now types; real motion and motion after the plugin's own warp still interrupt, with `foreground_interrupted`.
- `tests/desktop_fault_policy_fixture.cpp` runs the production `cancel_authority`/`invalidate` bodies and now checks that the cancellation reason reaches the bound client, survives a repeated cancel, and that Stop keeps `stale_target`.
- `tests/foreground_modifiers_test.py` fixture gains the `warp_pointer` helper that `start_foreground` now calls.

## How this is proven end to end

The Omarchy image installs `cua-hyprland-plugin` from Omarchy's package repository (currently 0.47.8-8), not from this branch, so dispatching the image workflow here would still run the old plugin. This PR is covered by "CI: Hyprland plugin unit and mock". The image e2e proves it after the next Cua Driver release is packaged by the Hyprland plugin kit and the Omarchy package is bumped; `SDK type + key into foot` should then pass under autostart load.

Related: #8659 (test harness waits for idle and captures Hyprland logs on failure; it makes the gate easier to debug but is not the fix).

title: fix(cua-driver): a macOS type_text send that a native field showed no change for is not offered a retry from character 0
body:
## Problem

`TypeTextTool::invoke` answers a key-event send whose read-back shows fewer characters than were sent with `type_text_incomplete`: "delivered N of M character(s); retry only the remaining suffix", with `effect: "partial"`, `retryable: true` and `retry_from_character: N`.

`await_typed_delivery` reports `(false, Some(0))` when the field's AXValue still equals its value from before the send once `UNCHANGED_GIVE_UP` (500 ms) has passed. For web content it drops the 0, and `reported` drops it for a terminal, but a native field keeps it. The reply is then "delivered 0 of M character(s); retry only the remaining suffix" with `retry_from_character: 0`, which tells the caller to type the whole text again.

The keys were posted. A field that shows no change is also what a field shows when the keys have not landed yet or are not echoed:

- a native field whose AXValue lags the keys by more than 500 ms;
- a view that does not echo what it reads and is not on the terminal list (for example a `read -s` password prompt in a terminal app the driver does not recognize as a terminal).

A caller that follows the hint types the text twice, and a secret twice. On the current main a batched send in this state has already been retyped once by `retype_from` (#8409 removes that retype); the reply then asks for a third copy. A paced send (`delay_ms` > 0) is not retyped, but gets the same reply.

## Fix

The incomplete reply moves into `incomplete_result`. When the delivered count is 0, the reply says the keys were sent, the field showed no change, the effect is unknown, and the field must be read before typing again. Its structured content keeps `code: "type_text_incomplete"`, and has `effect: "indeterminate"`, `retryable: false`, no `delivered_chars` or `retry_from_character`, and `escalation.recommended: "verify_state"`. This is the same shape `synthesis_refusal_result` gives an unobserved atomic AX write. A partial delivery (1 to M-1 characters) keeps its reply and its retry from the delivered count.

This is the reply-side follow-up to #8409. Both handle a send whose read-back showed no change: #8409 stops the driver from retyping it, and this change stops the reply from asking the caller to retype it. It merges cleanly onto main with or without #8409.

## Test

`a_send_the_field_showed_no_change_for_is_not_retried_from_zero`: for 0 of 5 characters delivered, `retryable` is false, `retry_from_character` is absent, `effect` is `indeterminate`, `escalation.recommended` is `verify_state`, and the text says "read the field before typing again" and not "retry only the remaining suffix". For 2 of 5, `retryable` is true, `retry_from_character` is 2 and `effect` is `partial`.

title: fix(cua-driver): a background hotkey whose menu item macOS keeps disabled is refused in a native app, not posted as keys
body:
## Problem

`HotkeyTool::invoke` runs a background combo that is a menu item's key equivalent in a native app that is not in front through `invoke_menu::run_in_background`, because background key events never reach a native app's menu key equivalents. When that route answers `background_unavailable` (macOS keeps the item disabled while the app is in the background), `menu_allows_key_fallback` lets the call go on and post the combo as key events. The keys reach no menu, so the reply is "Pressed" with `effect: "unverifiable"` and nothing changes. A background `cmd+a` or `cmd+b` to TextEdit, whose Select All and Bold are disabled while TextEdit is inactive, is one case. The tool description already says that such an item "is refused with `background_unavailable`".

The fallback came from #5306 for LibreOffice, whose VCL handles its shortcuts from key events (Format > Bold is disabled in the background, but the keys work). Every other native app goes through the same branch.

With an `element_token` or `x`,`y` target, the menu route first moves the keyboard focus to that element: `focus_hotkey_element` writes AXFocused, or, for `x`,`y` and elements in web content, `focus_by_pixel` runs a background `click` with `action: "focus"` at the point (no mouse event). An error from the menu route that follows (`background_unavailable`, `automation_consent_required`, a window refusal) returns without saying that the focus moved, so the reply reads as if the call changed nothing.

## Fix

- `menu_route_result` decides the result of the menu route. A `background_unavailable` answer goes out as keys only when `pointer_toolkit::detect` reports LibreOffice's VCL. In any other native app it is returned as the refusal, with `effect: "refused"`, no key sent, and `escalation: { recommended: "foreground", requires: ["window_id"] }`. Every other answer of the route is returned as before. The toolkit is read only after the route answered `background_unavailable`.
- Every error result of the menu route that follows a focus write ends with "Before the menu command, the call wrote the keyboard focus to element [N]." (or "to the element at (x, y)"), in the text and in `structuredContent.refusal.message`. A successful menu command is unchanged.
- `focus_by_pixel` now returns `Ok(true)` when a focus action ran and `Ok(false)` when the focused element already covered the point. The hotkey menu route drops the focus note on `Ok(false)`; the other callers ignore the value.
- MACOS.md: the LibreOffice section says that only LibreOffice gets a disabled menu shortcut as background keys, and that a disabled Save still saves through the app's scripting interface.

## Test

- `a_disabled_menu_item_is_refused_unless_the_app_takes_its_shortcut_as_keys`: a `background_unavailable` answer in a non-VCL app is returned as an error with `code: "background_unavailable"`, `effect: "refused"` and `escalation.recommended: "foreground"`; in a VCL app it returns `None` (the combo goes out as keys); a `window_not_key` refusal and a success are returned in a VCL app too.
- `a_disabled_menu_refusal_names_the_element_the_call_focused`: with a focused element, the refusal text ends with the focus note and equals `refusal.message`; without one the text is unchanged; an `automation_consent_required` error also gets the note; a success text is unchanged.

## Merging with the scripted Save change

This branch and #8666 (a scripted Save that reached the app returns `save_indeterminate`) are independent: the only file both touch is `Skills/cua-driver/MACOS.md`, and they edit different sections of it. Each merges cleanly onto main alone, and the two merge cleanly in either order (checked with `git merge-tree --write-tree`). With both, a background `cmd+s` whose scripted save did not confirm returns `save_indeterminate`, and one that never reached the app is refused in a native app instead of posted as keys.

title: fix(cua-driver): a background Save whose scripted save reached the app but did not confirm is indeterminate, not refused
body:
## Problem

When File > Save of a file-backed document is disabled because the app is in the background, `invoke_menu::run_in_background` saves it through `apple_events::save_document`. That runs `SAVE_DOCUMENT_SCRIPT` in `osascript` (send `«event coresave»` to the document, then read its `«property imod»` modified flag) with a 30 s timeout. Every error except `automation_consent_required` is answered with `background_unavailable`: "... saving through <app>'s scripting interface did not complete (<code>: <reason>). Nothing was saved", followed by the advice to `bring_to_front` the window or send the shortcut with `delivery_mode:"foreground"`.

Three of those errors can come after the save event reached the app, or may have reached it:

- `save_unconfirmed`: the app answered the save, but still reports unsaved changes, or answered something other than `true` or `false`;
- `automation_timeout`: `osascript` was killed after 30 s, for example while a sheet in the app holds the save;
- `automation_failed` from a modified-flag read that raised after the save ran (the document closed in between), because the save and the read run in one script.

"Nothing was saved" is wrong in these cases, and a caller that follows the advice and saves again in the foreground acts on a document whose save may already have run or still be pending. A background `hotkey` `cmd+s` takes the same route; because the answer is `background_unavailable`, `menu_allows_key_fallback` then also posts `cmd+s` as key events, which a native app's menu never receives, and the call reports "Pressed".

One timeout does mean nothing was sent. Without `--no-automation-prompts`, a first scripted Save to an app that macOS has not asked Automation consent for yet blocks in the document lookup on the consent prompt until `osascript` is killed at 30 s. That case must stay a refusal, so that the caller can use the foreground save, which needs no consent.

## Fix

- `save_document` keeps the permission it read before the script and passes the script's result to the new `save_result`, which maps it to a refusal code. On a timeout after a preflight of `NeedsConsent`, it reads the permission again: still `NeedsConsent` answers `automation_consent_pending` (no permission yet, a consent prompt may be waiting, no save reached the app), and `Denied` answers `automation_consent_declined` ("the user declined Automation for <app>, so no save reached it"). Every other timeout stays `automation_timeout`, with the reason "<app> did not answer within 30 s" and no mention of a waiting prompt. The second permission read happens only on that timeout path.
- `SAVE_DOCUMENT_SCRIPT` reads the modified flag in its own `try`; a read that raises returns `saved-unread`, which maps to `save_unconfirmed`. A save event that raises still fails the script as before.
- `save_failure` builds the reply in `run_in_background`. `save_unconfirmed` and `automation_timeout` return `code: "save_indeterminate"` with `status` and `effect` `"indeterminate"`, `retryable: false` and `escalation.recommended: "verify_state"`. The text says the save request was sent (or, after a timeout, may have reached the app), that its outcome is unknown, and to read the document's state (the window's edited mark or the file on disk) before saving again; it has no `background_unavailable` advice. `automation_consent_required` is unchanged. Every other code (`automation_denied`, `automation_failed`, `automation_consent_pending`, `automation_consent_declined`) keeps the `background_unavailable` refusal and "Nothing was saved".
- A background `hotkey` falls back to keys only on `background_unavailable`, so `save_indeterminate` also ends a background `cmd+s` without posting keys.
- MACOS.md: the Save paragraph describes `save_indeterminate` and the timeout that sent nothing.

## Test

- `apple_events::tests::a_save_whose_modified_flag_cannot_be_read_is_unconfirmed`: the script has the `on error` branch that returns `saved-unread`; `save_result` maps `saved-unread` to `save_unconfirmed`, `false` to `Ok(())`, and passes an `automation_failed` error through unchanged.
- `tools::invoke_menu::tests::a_save_that_reached_the_app_is_indeterminate_and_not_refused_as_unavailable`: for `save_unconfirmed` and `automation_timeout`, the result is an error whose code is not `background_unavailable`, with `effect: "indeterminate"`, `retryable: false`, `escalation.recommended: "verify_state"`, "outcome is unknown" and no background advice in the text, and "was sent" or "may have reached the app" in both the text and the escalation reason. `automation_failed` and `automation_denied` stay `background_unavailable` with `effect: "refused"`; `automation_consent_required` keeps its code.
- `tools::invoke_menu::tests::a_save_that_timed_out_at_the_consent_prompt_is_refused_as_unavailable`: for a timeout, a preflight of `NeedsConsent` rechecked as `NeedsConsent` or `Denied` is `background_unavailable`; `Granted` then `Unknown`, `Granted` then `Denied`, `NeedsConsent` then `Granted`, `Unknown` then `Denied` and `Unknown` then `NeedsConsent` are `save_indeterminate`, and their text has no "prompt may be waiting". The declined case names the user declining Automation for the app, and the pending case says a consent prompt may be waiting.

## Merging with the disabled-menu hotkey change

This branch and #8665 (a background hotkey whose menu item macOS keeps disabled is refused in a native app) are independent: the only file both touch is `Skills/cua-driver/MACOS.md`, and they edit different sections of it. Each merges cleanly onto main alone, and the two merge cleanly in either order (checked with `git merge-tree --write-tree`). With both, a background `cmd+s` whose scripted save did not confirm returns `save_indeterminate`, and one that never reached the app is refused in a native app instead of posted as keys.

## Checks

- [x] On a macos-15-intel runner (run 45353515227), on this branch:
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`;
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`;
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib tools::invoke_menu::` (19 passed);
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib apple_events::` (8 passed);
  - `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib`: 916 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`, which this change does not touch.

title: fix(cua-driver): report a scoped Linux snapshot complete when its window was walked
body:
## Why

Main already walks the requested window first, so a capped snapshot of a second window now lists that window's controls. The walk still continues into the application's other windows afterwards. When the node budget (250 by default) or the deadline runs out there, `get_window_state` reports `truncated: true` and `elements_complete: false` for a window it walked in full. Negative existence stays unknowable for any window of an application with more than 250 controls in total.

## What changed

- `collect_visited_bounded_opts` drops a truncation when no node of the scoped window is still pending, and ignores unexpanded huge containers that belong to other windows. The rule lives in `truncation_in_scope`.
- The GTK3 fixture opens a second top-level with three buttons when `CUA_GTK3_SECOND_WINDOW=1`.
- New e2e `harness_gtk3_capped_second_window_snapshot_is_complete`: with `max_elements: 10`, the main window comes back truncated and the second window lists `second-00`..`second-02`, with `truncated: false` and `elements_complete: true`.

## Scope

Linux AT-SPI snapshots scoped to one window. Unscoped walks (`xid == 0`, or a window the walk cannot correlate) keep their current truncation. Index numbering does not change, because the scoped window is still visited first and the actuators walk in the same order.

## Tradeoffs

The walk could stop as soon as it finishes the scoped window. That would save time, but the actuators that share this walk would then fail to find elements in other windows, and their refusal messages would change. This PR only corrects what the snapshot reports.

## Blast Radius

Linux `get_window_state` and recording snapshots that pass a window. A snapshot cut inside the requested window is still reported truncated (covered by the unit test and the main-window assertion in the e2e).

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, SPDX headers, image refs). The host has no disk headroom for cargo builds, so clippy, unit tests and the GTK3 e2e lane are left to CI and the verifier.
- `gtk3-native-harness` in `scripts/ci/linux/run-rust-e2e.sh` runs the whole `harness_gtk3_test` binary, which includes the new test.

Fixes #3812

title: fix(cua-driver): report a real elements_complete from macOS get_window_state
body:
## Why

On macOS, `get_window_state` always reported `elements_complete: false`. That meant a `verify_state` predicate with no match always came back Unknown, even for a small window the walk read in full. The walker already noted budget and depth stops. It could not tell a failed `AXChildren` read from an element with no children, so this PR records that case and uses the result.

## What changed

- `NodeAttributes::children` returns `None` when the application failed to answer the `AXChildren` read (an AXError other than no-value or unsupported, or an unanswered node). The walker records that in a new `TreeWalkResult::children_unread`, and it sets the same flag when it leaves a closed menu collapsed.
- `TreeWalkResult::complete()` is true when the window scope resolved and nothing was given up: no budget or timeout stop, no depth cut, no unread child list. `get_window_state` publishes it as `elements_complete`. The `truncated` field is still written by `WalkOutcome::apply`.
- `docs/tool-output-format.md` gets a macOS paragraph next to the Windows one.

## Scope

macOS only. Like Windows, `elements_complete` describes the walk before any `query` projection. A plain model-facing read collapses the menu bar's closed menus, so it reports `false` for any window with a menu bar. The `verify_state` observation read, `query` reads and `full_output` reads walk the menus. Not covered here: the browser setup and consent proofs, which still check only `truncated`. Linux and Windows are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

The only consumer of `elements_complete: true` is `cua-driver-core::expectation`. It also requires untruncated `observations` and no web-content rows before it calls a missing match Unsatisfied. The `web_effect` digest keeps reading a failed child list as empty, as it did before.

## Verification

- `only_a_resolved_walk_that_gave_nothing_up_is_complete` (new, `platform-macos` `ax::tree`) covers the complete/incomplete matrix.
- The scoped repository checks (`bin/ci --quick`: rustfmt, headers) pass. This Linux host could not build or test `platform-macos`. The macOS unit tests and a live Calculator read (`elements_complete` true through the observation path, false with `max_elements: 1`) are left to CI and the verifier.

Fixes #3815

title: [Feature]: Configurable default timeout_ms for get_window_state tree walks
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver (`get_window_state` and persistent configuration)

### User problem

`get_window_state` stops its accessibility-tree walk after `timeout_ms`. A call that leaves it out gets 1,000 ms, or 2,000 ms on a window's first read. On Linux (X11, AT-SPI), a walk of a small Chromium page often takes longer than that, so default reads come back partial (`truncation_reason: "timeout"`).

Measured on 0.61.2 (and 0.44.0) on an X11 display, using a local test page with 649 accessibility nodes in Google Chrome started with `--force-renderer-accessibility`:

- With `timeout_ms: 20000` and `max_elements: 1000`, every read completed. Medians were about 2.6 s, with single reads from 2.3 to 3.9 s. When the machine was busy, reads took up to 8.8 s.
- With no `timeout_ms`, reads after the first were cut at 1,000 ms after 163 to 236 nodes.

In repeated automation, many callers (agents in particular) omit `timeout_ms` and inherit the built-in default. The partial tree is flagged, but callers often treat it as the whole window, and the element they need is missing. Today the only way to change the default for every caller is a wrapper that rewrites each MCP request or CLI call to add `timeout_ms`. That is what we do now, and it cannot reach reads made inside `run_script`.

### Requested behavior

- A persistent default for `get_window_state.timeout_ms`, settable through `cua-driver config set ...` / `set_config` and the driver config file (or an environment variable read at runtime start), with documented bounds (the per-call range is 100 to 120000).
- When a call omits `timeout_ms`, use the saved default. An explicit per-call value still wins. Please document how the saved default interacts with the cold-start budget of a window's first read.
- Apply the same default to the end-of-batch `observe` read in `run_steps` and to `getState` reads inside `run_script`.
- Report the effective value in `get_config` / `config show` and in the tool description, and keep `truncated`, `truncation_reason` and `elements_complete` as they are.

### Related

- #6345 asks for the same kind of persistent default for `max_elements` and `max_depth`. One config surface for all three would fit together.
- #4356 covers the first snapshot of a cold Chromium or Electron app. This request is about every read after that.

title: feat(cua-driver): expose link url in get_window_state elements
body:
Fixes #3824

Salvaged from #3825 by @rrmars, rebased onto current main with their commit kept as authored.

## Why

On macOS, `get_window_state` elements give a link's text and let you press it, but they don't say where it goes. Chromium and WebKit expose the target as `AXURL` on `AXLink`.

## What changed

- `WindowElement.url` (optional, skipped when absent) in `cua-driver-contract`. The manifest, UniFFI bindings and macOS tool reference are updated to match.
- The macOS walker asks for `AXURL` in its existing batched attribute request. It keeps the value only for actionable `AXLink` nodes, inside the actionable-only control-state read, so the walk makes no extra round trip.
- `build_elements_array` emits `url` when present. `tree_markdown` is unchanged.

## Scope

macOS only. Windows UIA already reports a link URL through `value`, and AT-SPI could expose it through Hyperlink; both are left for later, as the issue proposes.

## Blast Radius

The field is optional and additive, so existing consumers keep working. The batched read now asks every node for one more attribute in the same request. Nodes that don't support it answer with an unsupported-attribute slot, which reads as `None`.

## Verification

- [x] `bin/ci --quick`: formatting, headers and the TypeScript typecheck pass.
- [ ] Heavy checks (contract and bindings drift, clippy, macOS unit tests) were skipped on this host because it is short on disk; CI runs them in the scoped repository checks.
- New tests: `url_slots_read_like_single_url_reads` (a batched CFURL slot resolves to its absolute string and a string slot reads as `None`, like `copy_url_attr`), `link_url_is_read_only_for_links`, `elements_surface_link_url`, and `url` added to the omitted-when-absent test.

title: fix(cua-driver): settle the macOS AX read-back before reporting a partial type_text
body:
Fixes #3841
Fixes #3917

Salvaged from #3842 and #3921 by @will-bogusz. Both of their commits are kept as authored, and one small commit of ours sits on top.

## Why

On macOS, the `AXSelectedText` rung of `type_text` read `AXValue` once, right after the write, and reported a prefix there as `type_text_incomplete`. AppKit fields that rebuild their editor around the insertion (Contacts) publish the full value a moment later, so callers were told to retype a suffix that was already in the field. When the transient value was later discarded (#3917), the `Partial` verdict also ended the ladder before the keystroke rung could run.

## What changed

- The AX rung settles a partial first read through the same drain as the keystroke rung (`await_typed_progress`, split out of `await_typed_delivery`).
- The drain now classifies from the last readable value, not the strongest one seen. A partial that the settled read contradicts becomes `Unchanged`, which falls through to keystrokes. The strongest partial is used only when the last read is unreadable.
- Only a partial first read is drained. An unchanged or unreadable read decides immediately, as it does on main, so writes a web view ignores still go to keystrokes without waiting through the unchanged give-up window. The submit checks (`submit_read_back_matches`, `write_left_field_untouched`) use the settled value.
- A first-read partial is never typed again over text that landed. If every later read is unreadable, the first partial stands. If the field settles at its old length with a different value, as a replaced selection does, the write is reported unverified with no keys sent (the path Gecko writes already take). Keystrokes follow only when the field holds its pre-write value again.

## Scope

macOS `type_text` only: both the AX rung and the keystroke drain. The Gecko late-apply decision, the retype-tail logic and other platforms are unchanged; the shared unverified message now says "target" instead of "page". Adds an opt-in AppKit fixture knob, `CUA_APPKIT_AX_VALUE_LAG_MS`, a harness cell `macos-appkit-type-text-lagging-readback-ax-background`, and unit tests for the drain.

## Blast Radius

Every macOS `type_text` call that reaches the AX rung. Calls whose first read is complete, unchanged or unreadable behave as before. A partial first read now waits for the field to settle, bounded by `DELIVERY_DRAIN_TIMEOUT`, instead of returning a false partial at once. The keystroke drain reports the settled count instead of the peak count, so `delivered_chars` can be lower than before when a field drops text after showing it.

## Verification

title: feat(cua-driver): hide a cursor's session label with set_agent_cursor_badge
body:
## Why

An embedding app that already shows the active task in its own UI has no way to drop the session name painted under the native agent cursor. Renaming the session changes lookup semantics, and custom themes can't help because the badge is host-rendered. This adds a per-session, default-on switch for the label text alone, as #3874 proposes.

## What changed

- `start_session` takes `cursor_badge: {show_session_label}`, applied before the cursor first shows. A new `set_agent_cursor_badge` tool changes it later, and `get_agent_cursor_state` reports it as `badge.show_session_label`.
- The shared `RenderStateCore` keeps the flag. While it is off, it paints no label (initial reveal, hover, or next to other cursors) and stops the label-only hover poll and frame ticks. Delivery and target chips still paint on their own pill, and there is no empty pill. Turning it back on replays the initial reveal.
- macOS, Windows and X11/Wayland layer-shell route it through that shared state. The GNOME Shell helper, which paints its own badge, tracks it per session and sends a session's own label when that session takes the single helper cursor over.

## Scope

Covers the RFC's proposal: the initial setting, the per-session setter, and the readout. The session id, label sanitizing, transport ownership, key-combo chip, delivery/target chips, consent and stop controls are unchanged. Repeated `start_session` without `cursor_badge`, theme changes, metadata refreshes and idle wakeups keep the setting; `end_session` drops it with the cursor. `badge` is optional in the state output, so SDKs still parse older daemons.

## Tradeoffs

- The RFC left placement open. I used a dedicated `set_agent_cursor_badge` tool rather than a field on `set_agent_cursor_motion`, since motion is a different concern and the badge may grow more fields.
- The readout comes from the render map, the same source as `motion` and `theme`. A read sent right after a set can briefly show the old value until the overlay applies the command.

## Blast Radius

Additive contract change: one new tool, one optional `start_session` field, one optional output field. Callers that don't send the field see no change. The UniFFI bindings, contract manifest, MCP reference and registry snapshots are regenerated. Generated SDK clients gain a `set_agent_cursor_badge` method. The new `agent_cursor.set_badge` capability joins the canonical vocabulary, and the MCP compatibility manifest now expects 62 base tools and one more output schema per platform.

## Verification

Test plan for the verifier and CI:
- `cargo test -p cursor-overlay` (`hidden_session_label_keeps_the_cursor_and_its_chips`, `session_label_visibility_is_per_session_and_ends_with_it`), `cargo test -p cua-driver-core` (`start_session_label_visibility_is_emitted_only_when_set`), `cargo test -p cua-driver-contract` (`session_label_visibility_round_trips_and_is_optional_on_older_daemons`), `cargo test -p platform-linux` (`shell_helper_label_follows_the_session_that_takes_the_cursor`, mutation-checked).
- The scoped repository checks: contract and UniFFI binding drift, docs drift, clippy, and the Windows cross-check.
- Ran on Linux after merging main: `cargo clippy -D warnings` on platform-linux, cua-driver-sdk, cua-driver-core, cursor-overlay and cua-driver-contract; their unit tests; the contract and UniFFI binding drift checks; the docs code-block tests; the `.github/scripts` tests; `bin/ci --quick`. macOS and Windows builds run only in CI.
- Native overlay evidence (macOS, Windows, X11, Wayland) is not part of this run. The RFC asks for it before calling the feature complete.

Fixes #3874

title: fix(cua-driver): release every held XTest key when a Linux input route fails
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux X11, an XTest chord that fails after its modifiers are pressed can leave Ctrl, Shift, Alt or Super held for the whole desktop. Example: an interactive session sends Ctrl plus an unknown key. The call errors, the queued Ctrl press goes out on the next flush, and nothing releases it. Every later Ctrl shortcut on that display misbehaves. Separately, the foreground targeted API skips modifiers it cannot name: `["altgr", "x"]` types a bare `x` and reports success.
- What changed: `Delivered` now holds its connection, and dropping it releases whatever is still held, on that connection. The fresh-connection path for abandoned calls is unchanged. The targeted and interactive XTest paths (modifiers, `tap`, drag button) record their presses in `Delivered`. They resolve every keycode before the first press and refuse an unknown modifier as `Unsupported`.

| Live Xvfb repro, `ubuntu-24.04` | main `ace7dac9c` | this PR `c999499f6` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ctrl + unknown key in an interactive session, then QueryKeymap | `keycodes left held: [37]` (Control_L) | none held |
| `xinput query-state` after the test process exits | `key[37]=down` | none |
| Foreground hotkey `["altgr", "x"]` | `Ok(...)`, bare `x` typed | `Unsupported`, nothing sent |
| Existing `xtest_key_taps_have_a_delivered_hold_interval` run after it | fails, `received 3 of 4 keyboard events` | passes |

## Related work

RFC: not needed. A local bug fix inside the Linux X11 input routes, with no API or protocol change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux X11 only. Foreground targeted and interactive chords with a modifier the adapter cannot map (for example `altgr`, `fn`, `hyper`) now return `Unsupported` and send nothing, where they used to send the key without that modifier. The background path already refused unknown modifiers. No change to public signatures.
- Risk and rollback: the new release only runs when a route exits with a key or button still held, so successful calls send the same events as before. Revert the single commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: two X11 tests in `platform-linux/tests/key_input_x11.rs`: `a_failed_xtest_chord_leaves_no_key_held` and `an_xtest_hotkey_with_an_unknown_modifier_sends_nothing`. On this PR (hosted `ubuntu-24.04`): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-linux --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p platform-linux` (1157 passed), the `key_input_x11` X11 suite (22 passed) and the `click_input_x11` X11 suite (4 passed), all under Xvfb: [fix job](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45441888319/job/138614976479).
- Manual or platform evidence: the same harness builds main with this PR's test file, runs the two tests on a `-noreset` Xvfb, then reads the XTest keyboard state from a separate process. Main: [job](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45441888319/job/138614975920) shows `key[37]=down` after the process exits. This PR: [job](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45441888319/job/138614976479) shows no key down.
- Known gaps or CI still required: the timing-only paths are not reproduced live. These are an admission refused at the deadline between two presses, and a failed motion mid-drag. They take the same `Delivered` drop path the repro exercises. `bin/ci` was not run.
