title: fix(cua-driver): inject into a terminal pty only when its window is unambiguous
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Linux X11, `type_text` and `press_key` Enter aimed at one window of a multi-window terminal (one emulator process, several windows or tabs) could be written into another window's shell, and still report success. The window to pty mapping indexed a pid-sorted list of every descendant's stdin tty, with no dedupe, so a `vim` inside `bash` shifted every later window. Separately, Enter and typed newlines were injected as LF (Ctrl-J), which fzf and other raw-mode apps read as "down", not Return.
- What changed: the pty route is used only when the emulator has exactly one toplevel window (the target) and holds exactly one pty master, found from its own fds. Otherwise the tools fall through to the normal key routes. Newlines (from `press_key` Enter and in `type_text` text) are injected as CR, the byte a terminal sends for Return.

| xfce4-terminal (one process, 2 windows) + xterm, ubuntu-24.04 Xvfb | main `ace7dac9c` | this PR `5eb70a542` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| foreground `type_text` + Enter to window B | lands in A: `A got ['to-B'], B got []` | lands in B: `A got [], B got ['to-B']` |
| background `type_text "bg-B\n"` to window B | lands in A: `A got ['to-B', 'bg-B']` | refused `background_unavailable`, A untouched |
| single-window xterm, background `type_text` + Enter | delivered via pty | delivered via pty |
| `press_key Return` in fzf (single-window xterm) | not accepted (`''`) | accepted (`'one'`) |
| `type_text "\n"` in fzf (single-window xterm) | not accepted (`''`) | accepted (`'one'`) |

## Related work

RFC: not needed. Bug fix inside one private helper, no API change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Linux only. A terminal emulator that owns several windows or tabs (gnome-terminal-server, xfce4-terminal, konsole, kitty single-instance) no longer gets focus-free pty typing. It uses the same XTest / XI2 key routes as other apps, or gets the usual `background_unavailable` refusal. Single-window terminals keep the pty route.
- Risk and rollback: low. Narrows when an existing fast path is used. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: `tty::tests::injects_only_when_the_process_holds_a_single_pty` (writes through a sole pty, refuses with two). title: fix(cua-driver): escape and cap element text in tree rows
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: `get_window_state` printed element text (titles, values, labels, help, ids) raw into its markdown rows. A field value or web page text containing a newline followed by `- [99] push button "Forged"` showed up as a real row, matched `query`, broke the `since` diff, and could be picked up by stale-token refind. A `"` in the text broke the quoting, and a whole document as a value bloated every snapshot.
- What changed: one shared helper, `cua_driver_core::tree_text::escape`, escapes backslash, `"`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t` and other control characters, and cuts a field after 4096 characters (as much as the Linux backend already reads from a text node) with a `…[+N chars]` marker. The macOS, Windows and Linux tree renderers (and their `query_dom` fallbacks) use it. Code that reads labels and values back from rows (display rows, menu paths, stale-token refind, the macOS page reader) now uses the matching `unquote` / `unescape`, and `query` also matches text in its escaped form.

| Repro, runner | main `ace7dac9c` | this PR `bbcc2fd58` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GTK3 entry and label with `\n- [99] push button "Forged entry"`, `get_window_state`, ubuntu-24.04 Xvfb | `- [99] push button "Forged entry""` is a row, `query=Forged` returns only the forged rows | one row per element: `value="ok \"quoted\"\n- [99] push button \"Forged entry\""`, `query=Forged` returns the real entry `[0]` |

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: `tree_markdown` text now uses JSON-style escapes, so a Windows path reads `C:\\Users` and a quote inside a label reads `\"`. title: fix(cua-driver): keep serving after accept errors and shut down cleanly on signals
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: One failed `accept` on the Unix socket (for example `EMFILE` when the daemon runs out of file descriptors) ends `cua-driver serve`, and one failed `accept` on the envelope HTTP port silently closes that listener while the daemon keeps running. SIGTERM or SIGINT kills the daemon with no cleanup: the socket and pid files stay behind, `status` reports a stale socket, and a video recording is never finalized. On macOS, `serve` started from a shell relaunches itself as a disclaimed child, so a signal sent to the pid the caller holds stops only the launcher and leaves the real daemon running.
- What changed:
  - The Unix socket, envelope HTTP and MCP HTTP accept loops share one helper: log the error, wait 100 ms, keep serving.
  - `cua-driver serve` turns SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP (Unix) and Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Break (Windows) into the same shutdown path as a `shutdown` request.
  - The macOS launcher relays SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP to the disclaimed child and still exits with the child's status.
  - A signal the launcher inherited as ignored (`nohup`, background jobs) stays ignored.

| Repro (hosted runner) | main `ace7dac9c` | this PR `12be1f8c7` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ubuntu-24.04, `ulimit -n 64`, 128 idle socket connections | daemon exits: `Too many open files` | stays up, answers `status` after |
| ubuntu-24.04, `ulimit -n 64`, 128 connections to the envelope HTTP port | listener gone, later requests refused | answers again (HTTP 405 to a probe) |
| ubuntu-24.04, SIGTERM while recording video | exit 143, socket and pid file left, `ffmpeg` still running, mp4 not playable | exit 0, both removed, mp4 playable, `session.json` finalized |
| macos-15-intel, SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP to the relaunching `serve` | launcher dies, daemon keeps running, socket and pid file left | launcher exits 0 after the daemon shuts down, both removed |
| windows-latest, Ctrl+Break | exit `0xc000013a`, pid file left | exit 0, pid file removed |

## Related work

Companion: #8686 makes the pip `cua-driver` command exec the binary, so on macOS its signals reach the daemon through the launcher relay added here.

RFC: not needed. Bug fix inside the daemon's lifecycle; no protocol, CLI or MCP change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: `kill <pid>`, Ctrl+C and closing the terminal now stop the daemon the way `cua-driver stop` does (exit 0, files removed, recording finalized), so shutdown can take as long as `stop` (up to 10 s to finalize a video). On macOS this holds for both the launcher pid and the daemon pid. The MCP HTTP listener already paused 100 ms after an accept error (40 warnings and 0.02 s CPU over 4 s of exhaustion, before and after); only its log line changes. The Windows named-pipe loop already retried failed instances and only gains the signal arm.
- Risk and rollback: Low. A persistent accept error now logs a warning every 100 ms instead of closing the listener. Revert the commits to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new `serve_lifecycle_cli_test` covers descriptor exhaustion of the socket and the envelope HTTP port, SIGTERM cleanup, and (macOS) SIGTERM to the relaunching launcher. All its tests fail on main and pass here on ubuntu-24.04 and macos-15-intel. On the PR head, `cargo fmt --all --check` (Linux and macOS), `cargo clippy --locked -p cua-driver --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked -p cua-driver` pass on ubuntu-24.04, macos-15-intel and windows-latest ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45452819286)).
- Manual or platform evidence: the same hosted harness on main ([Linux and macOS](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45452677262), [Windows](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45441372982)) and on this PR ([Linux, macOS and Windows](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45452819286)).
- Known gaps or CI still required: Windows console close (`CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT`) and `TerminateProcess` still skip cleanup. A signal that lands between the macOS relaunch and the relay install still stops only the launcher. `scripts/ci/linux/run-mpx-recovery-e2e.py` is not affected by the graceful SIGTERM: it attributes master pairs by name, and pairs are never removed since #7358, so its signal cases see the same pairs either way. It was not run (it needs real Xorg and `/dev/uinput`). `bin/ci` was not run.

title: fix(cua-driver): let signals sent to the Python CLI reach the daemon
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: The pip-installed `cua-driver` command runs the bundled binary as a child process. A supervisor or script that holds its pid and sends SIGTERM stops only the Python wrapper, and the real `cua-driver serve` keeps running as an orphan.
- What changed: On POSIX the CLI entry point replaces the Python process with the binary (`os.execve`, same environment), so its pid is the daemon's pid. Windows keeps the subprocess path. `run_cua_driver()` is unchanged for library callers.

| ubuntu-24.04, `cua-driver serve` via the wrapper, `kill -TERM <pid>` | main `ace7dac9c` | this PR `55d64ee89` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pid the shell holds vs daemon pid | 17192 vs 17197 | 16420 vs 16420 |
| daemon after SIGTERM | still running, answers `status` | stopped |

## Related work

RFC: not needed. Process launch detail of the CLI wrapper; no API change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: On macOS and Linux, `cua-driver` from the Python package now becomes the binary instead of waiting on it, so signals, exit codes and `ps` all see the binary directly. Windows and the public `run_cua_driver()` behave as before. On macOS the exec'd binary relaunches itself as a disclaimed child, and signals reach that child through the launcher relay added in #8685.
- Risk and rollback: Low. If `execve` fails the wrapper prints the same error as before and exits 1. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new `test_cli_entry_signals_reach_the_binary` checks that the binary runs under the CLI's pid and that SIGTERM to that pid stops it. `tests/test_wrapper.py` and `tests/test_compatibility_contract.py` pass with the real binary bundled and `ruff check` is clean on the touched files ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45441845662)).
- Manual or platform evidence: package installed with `pip install` into a venv with a source-built binary, `cua-driver serve` started through its console script, SIGTERM sent to the pid the shell holds: on main ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45441372982)) and on this PR ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45441845662)).
- Known gaps or CI still required: Windows is unchanged: terminating the wrapper there still leaves the child running. On macOS, this PR together with #8685 was run end to end: the pid the shell holds exits 0 on SIGTERM and no daemon is left ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45452819286)); with this PR alone the daemon is still orphaned there ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45452677262)). `bin/ci` was not run.

title: [Bug]: cua spaces add keys relay /m/<machine-id> URLs by host:port and overwrites sibling machines
body:
### Primary area

CLI

### Summary

`Spaces::add_with_service` ignores `EndpointKind::Relay { machine_id }` when given a `https://<relay>/m/<machine-id>` URL and stores the Space as `direct:<relay-host>:<port>`. Registering a second machine behind the same relay overwrites the first machine's registry record, and `cua sb` strips the `/m/<machine-id>` path.

### Reproduction

The hostnames and machine IDs below are synthetic examples.

1. Expose two `cua-spacesd` instances through one `cua-relay` at `https://relay.example.com/m/machine-alpha-01` and `https://relay.example.com/m/machine-bravo-02` (as documented in `docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/spacesd.mdx`).
2. Register the first machine:
   ```sh
   cua spaces add https://relay.example.com/m/machine-alpha-01 --name alpha
   ```
3. Register the second machine on the same relay:
   ```sh
   cua spaces add https://relay.example.com/m/machine-bravo-02 --name bravo
   ```
4. Run `cua spaces ls --json` and inspect `spaces.json`.
5. Run `cua sb get bravo` or `cua sb exec bravo -- uname -a`.

### Expected behavior

- Each `/m/<machine-id>` endpoint registered through `cua spaces add` has a distinct Space identity (consistent with `EndpointKind::Relay { machine_id }` and `Spaces: relay:<machine-id>` in `spacesd.mdx`), so `alpha` and `bravo` coexist in `spaces.json` with separate names, endpoints, and volume directories.
- Presence treats the Space as a relay stream rather than opening a direct UDP datagram channel.
- `cua sb` resolves the Space with its `/m/<machine-id>` path intact.

### Actual behavior

- Both registrations resolve to `id: "direct:relay.example.com:443"` with `provider: "direct"`. Step 3 overwrites `alpha` in `spaces.json` and `spaces-credentials.json`, reusing the existing `uid` volume directory.
- Because `provider` is `Provider::Direct`, `presence.rs` enables `want_datagrams` and attempts UDP cursor transport that `cua-relay` does not carry.
- `SandboxRef::parse` reduces any `https://<relay>/m/<machine-id>` URL to `SandboxRef::Direct { authority: "<relay>:443" }` without the `/m/<machine-id>` path, so `cua sb` commands fail against the root authority instead of reaching `/m/<machine-id>`.

### Environment

- Cua component and commit: `cua-spaces`, `cua-sandbox-core`, and `cua-cli` `0.31.0` (verified on `main` at `d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06`)
- Operating system and architecture: Linux `x86_64` and macOS `arm64` (platform-independent logic)

### Evidence

Code inspection at commit `d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06`:

- [spacesd.mdx:103-106](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/docs/content/docs/cua-sdk/guides/spacesd.mdx#L103-L106) documents `cua-spacesd join` clients reaching `https://<relay>/m/<machine-id>/` (`Spaces: relay:<machine-id>`).
- [endpoint.rs:170-175](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/libs/cua/crates/cua-spacesd-client/src/endpoint.rs#L170-L175): `Endpoint::parse` already classifies `/m/<machine-id>` URLs as `EndpointKind::Relay { machine_id }`.
- [spaces.rs:1373-1377](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/spaces.rs#L1373-L1377): `Spaces::add_with_service` discards `endpoint.kind()` and unconditionally builds `SpaceId::Direct { authority: authority(endpoint.host(), endpoint.port()) }`.
- [presence.rs:898-903](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/presence.rs#L898-L903): `want_datagrams` is disabled only for `Provider::Cloud` and `Provider::Relay`, not `Provider::Direct`.
- [refs.rs:224-231](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/libs/cua/crates/cua-sandbox-core/src/refs.rs#L224-L231): `SandboxRef::parse` discards URL path segments when constructing `SandboxRef::Direct`.

### Workaround and additional context

Calling `SpacesdClient::connect("https://relay.example.com/m/<machine-id>")` directly from the Rust, Python, or TypeScript SDK works for individual connections because `Endpoint::parse` preserves the base URL and `/m/<machine-id>` path, bypassing the `spaces.json` `direct:<host>:<port>` key.

title: [Bug]: cua daemon ListSpaces and GetSpace drop sharing metadata for registry-backed Spaces
body:
### Primary area

SDK or bindings

### Summary

`SpaceService::list_spaces` and `SpaceService::record` in `cua-daemon` discard `SpaceInfo.sharing` (and `durable`) for any Space already stored in `spaces.json`, such as a local Space shared through the relay or an entry added via `cua spaces add relay:<id>`. The Tauri `SpaceRow` in `apps/cua-spaces` also omits `sharing` when serializing rows to `cua-spaces-app-core`.

### Reproduction

1. Create a local Space (`local:demo`) while `cua daemon` is running and sign in to a relay account.
2. Share the Space with another user (`cua spaces share demo collaborator@example.com`).
3. Compare the `sharing` field returned by an embedded `cua_spaces::Spaces::list_all()` call against the `pb::Space` entries returned by `cua daemon` over `SpaceService/ListSpaces` and `SpaceService/GetSpace` (which back `cua-spaces-desktop`, `cua-spaces-macos`, and `cua --daemon`).
4. Alternatively, register a relay Space in `spaces.json` with `cua spaces add relay:<machine-id>` and inspect `Spaces::list()` and `SpaceService/ListSpaces`.

### Expected behavior

- `SpaceService/ListSpaces` and `SpaceService/GetSpace` preserve `sharing` (`share_count` and collaborator shares) and `durable` for `spaces.json`-backed Spaces, matching embedded `Spaces::list_all()`.
- `Spaces::list()` merges live relay directory metadata (`sharing`, `cloud`, `host`, `power`) when a `relay:<machine-id>` entry is also present in `spaces.json`.
- `apps/cua-spaces` forwards `sharing` on `SpaceRow` so `cua-spaces-app-core` computes identical `SpaceAccess` facts across shells.

### Actual behavior

- In `SpaceService::list_spaces`, `spaces` is loaded first from `self.spaces().registry().list()`, where `s.sharing` is `None`. When `others` from `list_known` or `list_all` (where `apply_attached_sharing` populated `info.sharing`) is merged, matching IDs copy only `s.display_name = info.display_name` and drop `info.sharing` and `info.durable`.
- `SpaceService::record` (used by `GetSpace` and single-Space RPCs) returns early on `spaces.registry().get(id)` after `fill_records`, leaving `sharing` as `None`.
- In `Spaces::list()`, `if !out.iter().any(|i| i.id == info.id)` skips the `relay_info(m)` merge whenever `relay:<id>` exists in `spaces.json`, leaving `sharing` as `None`.
- In `apps/cua-spaces/src-tauri/src/core.rs`, `SpaceRow` has no `sharing` field, so `cua-spaces-app-core` receives `row.sharing == None`.

### Environment

- Cua component and commit: `cua-daemon`, `cua-spaces` `0.31.0`, and `apps/cua-spaces` `0.41.9` (verified on `main` at `d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06`)
- Operating system and architecture: macOS, Linux, and Windows (daemon gRPC and Tauri bridge logic)

### Evidence

Code inspection at commit `d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06`:

- [spaces.rs:952-959](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/libs/cua/crates/cua-spaces/src/spaces.rs#L952-L959): `Spaces::list()` populates `info.sharing` for attached local Spaces via `apply_attached_sharing(&mut out)` and `info.durable` via `mark_durable(&mut out)`, while skipping `relay_info(m)` if `out` already holds `info.id`.
- [spaces_svc.rs:141](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/spaces_svc.rs#L141) vs [spaces_svc.rs:450-457](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/spaces_svc.rs#L450-L457): `info_record` maps `sharing: info.sharing.as_ref().map(Into::into)` only in the `else if info.provider == Provider::Relay` branch; when `spaces.iter_mut().find(|s| s.id == info.id)` matches an existing registry entry, only `s.display_name = info.display_name` is copied.
- [spaces_svc.rs:88-97](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/libs/cua/crates/cua-daemon/src/spaces_svc.rs#L88-L97): `record()` returns the registry record without reading `sharing` from `Spaces::find` or `Spaces::list`.
- [core.rs:319-395](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/d534dfea8d6946cd9f82caf73a8c33a6e7713a06/apps/cua-spaces/src-tauri/src/core.rs#L319-L395): `SpaceRow` omits `sharing`.

### Workaround and additional context

Querying `cua spaces shares <space>` (`list_space_shares`) directly reads the relay's share list on demand, bypassing `ListSpaces` and `GetSpace`.

title: [Bug]: macOS background type_text without x,y is refused with no_focused_text_input on custom-rendered editors with no AX text tree (e.g., WordCraft)
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

On macOS, `type_text` without `x, y` (or `element_token`) is refused with `no_focused_text_input` on custom-rendered canvas editors that expose no AX text subtree (e.g., WordCraft), even after the document canvas has already been focused via an earlier pixel click or `type_text({x, y})`. Forcing `x, y` on every subsequent `type_text` sends an extra click into the document before each write, which clears pending inline formatting toggles (Bold/Italic) clicked in the ribbon and can reposition the caret.

### Reproduction

1. Open a custom-rendered Metal/AppKit editor with no document AX subtree (e.g., **WordCraft**, whose `get_window_state` exposes only 7 AX nodes: `AXWindow`, 3 window traffic-light buttons, `AXMenuBar`, and 2 `AXMenuBarItem`s).
2. Focus the blank document canvas and type an initial heading in the background using pixel coordinates:
   ```bash
   cua-driver call type_text '{"pid":<PID>,"window_id":<WID>,"x":500,"y":300,"text":"Title","session":"demo"}'
   cua-driver call press_key '{"pid":<PID>,"window_id":<WID>,"key":"return","session":"demo"}'
   ```
   Both succeed in the background (`press_key` works without `x, y`).
3. Toggle an inline formatting button on the ribbon (e.g., click Bold or Italic via `click({x, y})`), then attempt to type at the current caret without re-clicking the page:
   ```bash
   cua-driver call type_text '{"pid":<PID>,"window_id":<WID>,"text":"Hello","session":"demo"}'
   ```
4. Observe that `type_text` is refused with `code: "no_focused_text_input"`.
5. Work around the refusal by passing `x, y` in the empty white page area below the text (`type_text({x: 700, y: 790, text: "Hello"})`). Observe that the extra pixel click resets the pending inline Bold/Italic toggle on the caret before typing begins (while paragraph-level styles still survive).

Observed 100% of the time (deterministic).

### Expected behavior

After a window without an AX text subtree has already been pixel-focused in the same session (or when typing into an already-focused custom canvas editor), `type_text` should be able to dispatch background keystrokes at the current caret without forcing a fresh mouse click on every call — consistent with `press_key` and `hotkey`, which already work without `x, y` on the same window.

### Actual behavior

Every `type_text` call without `x, y` or `element_token` is refused immediately with `no_focused_text_input`:

```json
{
  "code": "no_focused_text_input",
  "effect": "refused",
  "escalation": {
    "reason": "the focused element in this window is not a text input, so typed keys would act on the window instead (in Finder they move the selection by type-to-select). Nothing was sent. Pass the field's element_token, or x,y to focus it by pixel first. To rename a file in Finder, use set_value on its name cell.",
    "recommended": "px"
  },
  "pid": 14434,
  "reason": "the focused element in this window is not a text input, so typed keys would act on the window instead (in Finder they move the selection by type-to-select). Nothing was sent. Pass the field's element_token, or x,y to focus it by pixel first. To rename a file in Finder, use set_value on its name cell.",
  "window_id": 42234
}
```

### Environment

- Cua component and version/commit: `cua-driver 0.61.3` (`aarch64-macos`, git `7ab6c28edcae`)
- Operating system and architecture: macOS 27.2 (`arm64`)
- Application/browser/window system/image: WordCraft (native AppKit + Metal custom-rendered document editor, 7 AX nodes total in `get_window_state`)

### Evidence

- `get_window_state` on WordCraft reports `element_count: 7` (only `AXWindow`, 3 `AXButton` window controls, `AXMenuBar`, `Apple`, `WordCraft`) and `background_input.routes`: `accessibility: available`, `window_pointer: available`, `pid_keyboard: available`.
- Exact refusal JSON from `cua-driver call type_text` without `x, y` is included in Actual behavior above.
- `press_key` (`return`, `delete`) and `hotkey` (`cmd+a`, `cmd+left`, `option+shift+right`, `cmd+shift+left`) all succeed on the exact same `(pid, window_id)` without passing `x, y`.

### Workaround and additional context

- **Workaround:** Pass `x, y` in empty page whitespace below the last line on every `type_text`, and apply inline Bold/Italic *after* typing by selecting ranges via keyboard (`cmd+left`, `option+shift+right`) and clicking the ribbon button. This works for simple edits but is fragile on wrapped lines and adds unnecessary clicks.
- The `no_focused_text_input` guard makes great sense for Finder/Dock or apps with rich AX trees where a non-text control holds AX focus, but custom-rendered editors with no AX document tree have no AX text element to report as focused.

title: [Feature]: Auto-reconnect or auto-relaunch the macOS daemon from cua-driver mcp when the daemon stops or restarts
body:
### Primary area

MCP or agent integration

### User problem

On macOS, `cua-driver mcp` runs as a stdio proxy to the signed `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` daemon (`cua-driver serve`). At startup, if no daemon is running, `cua-driver mcp` already auto-launches `CuaDriver.app` cleanly.

However, if the backend daemon is stopped or restarted *during* an active IDE/agent MCP session (for example after `cua-driver update --apply` or `cua-driver stop`), the running `cua-driver mcp` process immediately exits with status `1` (`cua-driver-rs: daemon control session closed; reconnect the MCP client`). Many MCP host clients (such as IDE agents) do not automatically respawn a crashed stdio MCP server mid-conversation, leaving all `cua-driver` MCP tools broken (`failed to load: exit status 1`) until the user reloads MCP or starts a new conversation.

### Desired outcome

When the daemon socket closes while `cua-driver mcp` is running on macOS:

- `cua-driver mcp` stays alive on stdio instead of exiting with code `1`.
- On the next MCP request (or after a short backoff), it reconnects to the restarted daemon — or auto-launches `/Applications/CuaDriver.app` again, matching its cold-start behavior — and surfaces any invalidated session/snapshot state cleanly via normal MCP tool errors rather than terminating the stdio transport.

### Current workaround

Fall back to one-shot `cua-driver call ...` CLI commands from a shell, or manually restart/reload the MCP client in the IDE after any daemon restart or driver upgrade.

### Affected components and platforms

- Component: `cua-driver 0.61.3` (`aarch64-macos`, git `7ab6c28edcae`), `cua-driver mcp` stdio proxy
- Platform: macOS 27.2 (`arm64`)

### Alternatives and prior art

Minimal reproduction confirming current behavior on an isolated socket:

1. Start `cua-driver mcp --socket /tmp/test-cua-mcp-repro.sock`, send `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, and `tools/call` (`health_report`) → returns `ok` (`cua-driver 0.61.3`).
2. Run `cua-driver stop --socket /tmp/test-cua-mcp-repro.sock` while keeping the MCP stdio session open.
3. `cua-driver mcp` exits immediately with code `1` and stderr:
   ```text
   cua-driver: mcp launched without CuaDriver.app's TCC grants; auto-launching the installed CuaDriver.app daemon and proxying MCP requests through it.
   cua-driver-rs: daemon control session closed; reconnect the MCP client
   ```

Keeping the stdio JSON-RPC loop alive across daemon restarts (with explicit session-reset semantics, since snapshots are daemon-scoped) matches standard resilient proxy behavior for long-lived MCP clients.

### Implementation ideas

- Treat EOF on the daemon control socket as a reconnectable transport state rather than a fatal process exit.
- On the next incoming JSON-RPC call, attempt to reconnect to the configured socket (or auto-launch `CuaDriver.app` on macOS when using the default signed service) and return a structured error only if reconnect/relaunch fails.
- Preserve safety boundaries: do not silently carry over old `snapshot_id`s or `element_token`s across daemon generations (they are already retired when a new daemon starts).

- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(cua-driver): refuse ValuePattern type_text when the current value is unreadable
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on Windows, background `type_text` with an `element_token` appends through UIA `ValuePattern`. When `CurrentValue()` fails, it treated the value as empty, so `SetValue` replaced the whole field with the typed text, and the read-back then reported `confirmed`.
- What changed: when the current value cannot be read, `type_text` does not write and returns the existing `background_unavailable` refusal, which recommends `delivery_mode:"foreground"`. Readable fields keep the append route. A WPF fixture field (prefilled, `get_Value` fails, `SetValue` works) and an e2e case cover it.

| Background `type_text "typed"` into a field prefilled with `prefill-`, `windows-2025` | main `ace7dac9c` | this PR `663fd792f` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Driver result | `✅ Wrote 5 char(s) ... verify: confirmed` | `background_unavailable` refusal, foreground escalation |
| Field content after the call (read from the app) | `typed` (prefill lost) | `prefill-` |

## Related work

RFC: not needed. Bug fix inside one existing route, no new API.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: Windows only. Background `type_text` into an element whose UIA value cannot be read now returns `background_unavailable` (effect `refused`) instead of overwriting it. Foreground delivery and readable fields are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: low. One branch in the ValuePattern rung. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: new e2e case `harness_wpf_type_text_refuses_to_replace_an_unreadable_value` (fixture `UnreadableValueTextBox`). On `windows-2025`: `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-windows -p cua-driver-e2e --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo test --locked -p platform-windows --lib` 347 passed, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean ([checks](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45444919555/job/138625913999), [fmt](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45444919555/job/138625914158)).
- Manual or platform evidence: same e2e case on main plus the test commit fails ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45444919555/job/138625913818): field `typed`, driver said `confirmed`), passes on this PR ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45444919555/job/138625913435)). Full `harness_wpf_test` suite: main 30/30, this PR 31/31 ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45450743192); the first attempt on this PR hit one foreground `text_delivery_stalled` in the multiline SendInput case, which does not use this code path, and passed on rerun).
- Known gaps or CI still required: real WinForms and WPF password fields return an empty `Value` (no error) and accept `SetValue`, so this fix does not cover them; a prefilled password field is still replaced. The full Windows e2e matrix was not run. `bin/ci` was not run.

title: fix(cua-driver): pump the driver thread's own queue while attached to a Windows target
body:
## What users see

Foreground `type_text` and `press_key` on Windows could fail with `text_delivery_stalled` after 2 s on a target that was in front, active and responsive. The keys were read only after the driver gave up. This blocked the Cua Driver 0.61.4 release gate ([run 45363565804](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/45363565804), native WPF lane: `harness_wpf_type_text_foreground_single_line_application_state` and `harness_wpf_type_text_multiline_application_state`). With this change the driver keeps its side of the shared input queue moving, so the target reads the keys as they arrive.

## Root cause

For foreground input the driver thread attaches to the target thread's input queue (`InputQueueAttachment` in `platform-windows/src/input/keyboard.rs`) and watches the shared key state for a sentinel key. `AttachThreadInput` makes the two threads share one input queue, which Windows processes in order, and it expects every attached thread to keep retrieving its own messages. The driver thread only answered sent messages (`PeekMessage` with `PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE | PM_NOREMOVE`, added in #8522). Anything else Windows queued for it stayed ahead of the target's keys. The target kept answering `WM_NULL` but read no input until the driver detached.

Evidence, from a stall captured on this branch with extra diagnostics ([run 45444174110](https://github.com/trycua/cua/actions/runs/45444174110)):

- The target was foreground, its queue's active and focus window was the target, and its caption was drawn active. So the activation had been processed. The earlier theory behind #8550 (attaching before the target processed its activation) does not explain this stall.
- The target answered `WM_NULL` within 200 ms, so its thread was alive.
- The driver thread (MTA) found a pending wake about 400 times in 2 s, a steady 5 ms cadence in every stall we have (this run, the release gate, and #8618's runs 45268528093, 45270762232 and 45293191421). A thread-local `WH_CALLWNDPROC` hook saw no window message sent to it. Whatever was waiting for the driver thread was not something `PM_QS_SENDMESSAGE` delivers, so it was never cleared.
- Every recorded stall resolves at the moment the driver detaches (#8522, #8550, and the recordings here).

Why it depends on timing: the stall needs something queued for the driver thread at the moment it is attached. That depends on how the foreground handoff just before it went. `force_foreground_attached` attaches the same thread to the previous foreground thread to inherit foreground rights. So the stall shows up on some runs and not others.

What is not settled: we did not identify the exact item queued for the driver thread. Windows does not expose the shared queue's contents. The fix does not depend on knowing it: whatever Windows queues for the driver thread, the driver thread now retrieves it.

## Fix

- While attached, every wait step pumps the driver thread's own queue completely (`PeekMessage(PM_REMOVE)` with no filter, bounded to 64 messages a step). `PeekMessage` only returns this thread's own messages, so the target's keys stay with the target. The same pump runs once just before attaching, to clear anything left from the foreground handoff.
- The driver thread owns no window, so it should never be handed input. If it is, that input is counted and not dispatched, and the sentinel toggle no longer counts as "read" (the driver reading the sentinel would flip it too). The call fails as a stall instead of reporting a false success.
- The stall detail now reports the driver thread's apartment, the sent messages it answered (by message and window class), how many messages it retrieved and whether any were input, the target's caption state, and the driver thread's queue status before attaching, right after, and at the stall. If it ever recurs, the next log names the cause.

#8618 does not address this. It adds `get_user_input_events`, and the stall showed up on that branch whether or not keyboard input was tagged. Its lane results are the same intermittent stall.

## Tests

- New deterministic unit tests (`attached_wait_pumps_own_queue`, run by `cargo test -p platform-windows --lib` on every Windows unit run):
  - a message posted to the attached driver thread is retrieved by the wait. The old sent-only wait leaves it queued and fails this test;
  - input handed to the driver thread is counted and never reported as read.
- New desktop tests (`busy_target_activation_tests`, run in `ci-rust-windows.yml` when the runner has an interactive session) cover foreground typing into a target whose UI thread was busy when it was activated, a target that activated itself in the background, an idle one, and a busy previous foreground window.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix`: green.

## Verification

Native WPF lane (`e2e-rust-windows.yml`, lane `native`) dispatches on this branch are listed in the comments below with their results.

title: fix(cua-driver): write set_value as a number only to macOS controls that hold one
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: on macOS, `set_value` with a value that parses as a number (`"007"`, `"0612345678"`, `"1.50"`) on a Chromium or Electron text input empties the field. Chromium takes the CFNumber AXValue write as success, so the string write never runs.
- What changed: `set_value` writes a CFNumber only when the element's current AXValue is a CFNumber or CFBoolean (sliders, steppers, checkboxes). Every other element gets the exact string. The slider stepping fallback is unchanged.

| Hosted e2e, `macos-26` | main `ace7dac9c` (+ test only) | this PR `c8cc24854` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Electron `<input>`, `set_value "007"`, renderer value | `""` (field emptied) | `"007"` |
| WKWebView and Tauri `<input>`, `"007"` | `"007"` | `"007"` |
| AppKit NSTextField `"007"` / NSSlider `"42"` | `"007"` / `42` | `"007"` / `42` |

Raw AX write, same sequence as main, `macos-15-intel`:

| Element | CFNumber write | Field after `"007"` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome `<input>` | success | `""` |
| NSTextField, SwiftUI TextField | -25201, string fallback | `"007"` |
| NSSlider | success | `42` |

## Related work

RFC: not needed. Small internal fix to one tool's write path; no API change.

## Compatibility and risk

- User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS only. Text fields in Chromium and Electron now receive numeric-looking text exactly. No schema or API change.
- Risk and rollback: an element that holds a number but exposes no readable AXValue now gets a string write first. Revert the fix commit to roll back.

## Validation

- Focused tests and checks: e2e `web_set_value_keeps_numeric_text_exact` (Electron, WKWebView, Tauri) and `harness_appkit_set_value_keeps_numeric_text_exact` (NSTextField and NSSlider). On `macos-26-intel`: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` on `platform-macos` and `cua-driver-e2e`, `platform-macos` lib tests (921 passed), hermetic `cua-driver-e2e` tests, AppKit cell manifest check: [run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45509607810).
- Manual or platform evidence: web e2e on main fails on Electron ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45495052698)) and passes on this PR ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45509643909)). AppKit e2e passes on main ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45439719544)) and with this fix ([run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45494992741), same code, comment differs). Raw AX probe: [run](https://github.com/abonneth/cua-fork/actions/runs/45486627434).
- Known gaps or CI still required: the new e2e rows run only in the hosted macOS and Lume lanes. NSStepper ignores the AXValue write on both main and this PR (left out of scope). `bin/ci` was not run.

- [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained.

title: [RFC]: Read-only same-transport daemon authorization evidence over public MCP
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Add an opt-in, read-only, no-argument public stdio MCP tool (or namespaced method) that returns a sanitized authorization snapshot from the **serving daemon**, over the same client transport used for actions. This RFC asks for a maintainer decision on the contract, including field sufficiency and continuity semantics; it does not propose an implementation PR or permission changes. “Attestation” here means local runtime evidence, not cryptographic assurance against a compromised host.

### Motivation and current state

Clients that require explicit effective-policy evidence cannot infer it from static tool descriptions or proxy defaults. At release-source commit `3f69010ccd901a04ecf7b009b2b95400c3cb4ab8`, `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/proxy.rs:860–910` dispatches `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`; the existing daemon authorization status is not a public MCP operation. A separate CLI query cannot establish that its evidence belongs to the daemon serving the client's action connection.

`ToolRegistry::authorization_status_json` exists in `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs:1640–1643`. Its existence is **not evidence that its current fields are sufficient**. The RFC must settle which fields can be reused, which must be sanitized, and whether runtime/executable identity and policy generations can be represented adequately.

Related but distinct work: #2381 (permission modes), #2437 (per-session modes), and #2262 (desktop target identity). This proposal concerns read-only serving-runtime policy evidence, not selecting modes or identifying a desktop target.

### Goals

- Expose effective mode; manifest validity and digest; managed-policy and user-policy validity and digests; residual enforcement ceilings; serving runtime identity/generation; and policy-snapshot generation.
- Bind the snapshot to the actual serving executable/runtime, not merely the proxy process, through the same stdio MCP connection used for actions.
- Make reconnect, daemon replacement/restart, and policy changes invalidate prior evidence.
- Return explicit `unsupported` or `unavailable` when evidence cannot be established; never assume `standard` mode.
- Specify what the snapshot does **not** prove about a later action.

### Non-goals

Changing mode, approvals, policy, grants, profiles, environment or identity; desktop capture/input; implementation or driver upgrades; general daemon RPC passthrough; alternate/private transports; local forks or ad-hoc binaries; cryptographic remote attestation. Acceptance of this RFC is a design decision, not permission to perform native actions.

### Proposal

Expose one additive no-argument operation, provisionally `authorization_status` (final tool/method name for maintainers). It reads a consistent authorization snapshot from the daemon actually serving that MCP connection. Reject nonempty/malformed parameters. Do not synthesize success from proxy defaults, static `tools/list`, a separate CLI, or a different daemon. Reuse the existing producer/serialization only where its semantics satisfy the agreed contract.

The versioned, sanitized response should distinguish supported evidence from explicit unsupported/unavailable outcomes and carry:

| Evidence | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Effective mode | Daemon's effective mode, not requested configuration or proxy mode |
| Manifest, managed policy, user policy | Separate validity states and digests for each effective source; absence distinguished from invalid/unreadable, never silently treated as valid |
| Residual enforcement ceilings | Structured restrictions still enforced beyond the reported mode; no policy rule contents or application identifiers |
| Runtime/executable identity and generation | Opaque serving-runtime generation plus content-free executable identity sufficient to detect a different serving executable; a proxy PID/version alone is insufficient |
| Policy-snapshot generation | Changes whenever the effective authorization snapshot changes, including validity or ceilings; no ABA reuse within a runtime |

Maintainers should decide the exact schema, digest canonicalization, absence representation, and executable-identity mechanism. If a required field, schema version, enum value or identity cannot be understood or verified, the consumer must classify the evidence as unsupported/unavailable, not infer permissions. Unknown fields must not silently count as understood evidence: schema evolution needs explicit negotiation or an explicit unsupported outcome. Missing fields, daemon failures and identity mismatches likewise cannot produce a usable success. Unsupported legacy servers may return MCP method/tool-not-found, which clients classify explicitly as unsupported.

**Continuity and invalidation:** associate a response with the client's current transport epoch and the daemon's runtime/policy generations. Discard it on reconnect even if identifiers appear unchanged; invalidate on daemon replacement, restart, executable mismatch or policy change. Do not cache success across generations. The daemon must obtain fields from one consistent effective snapshot, not mixed reads across reloads. A proxy silently reconnecting to a replacement daemon must not preserve apparent continuity.

**Policy/action race:** a successful query is point-in-time evidence only. It does not prove that a later action used that runtime or policy generation, even on the same stdio connection; a second status query after an action is not proof either. The accepted contract must explain whether an existing mechanism pins execution to that snapshot, whether generation comparison can be performed atomically at action admission, or whether this operation explicitly offers observation only. An atomic compare-and-refuse/action receipt design is a possible topic for maintainers, **not an implementation commitment in this read-only RFC**. If generation-bound action assurance requires broader authorization redesign, please record that disposition rather than treating this status-only addition as sufficient. Clients requiring that assurance must remain unsupported until the stronger contract is separately settled.

Use the same public serialization and failure meanings on macOS, Windows and Linux. This query must neither invoke desktop operations nor grant OS permissions. Platform-specific inability to establish an identity or ceiling must be explicit, not substituted with another platform's defaults.

### Alternatives considered

- Separate CLI status: useful diagnostics, but does not bind evidence to the action-serving MCP connection.
- Infer status from `tools/list` or proxy configuration: cannot establish effective daemon policy.
- Expose the existing JSON producer unchanged: minimal code, but field sufficiency, privacy, executable identity and generations remain unproven.
- General daemon passthrough: needlessly enlarges the public surface and permission boundary.
- Broader generation-bound action protocol: potentially necessary for race-free assurance; request an explicit redesign disposition if the read-only scope cannot provide useful, accurately bounded evidence.
- No new public operation: valid maintainer outcome; consumers continue to report this preflight as unsupported rather than bypassing it.

### Compatibility and migration

Additive, opt-in client capability with explicit schema/version handling; existing action behavior and permission enforcement remain unchanged. Old servers remain unsupported for this preflight, not presumed safe. No automatic driver upgrade is implied. If accepted, any future implementation, platform validation and supported component release are separate stages; disabling client use rolls back adoption without changing policy. No implementation has been performed or tested for this RFC.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Return metadata only. Exclude policy contents, filesystem paths, app/window/session content or identifiers, credentials, user/host-identifying data and raw diagnostics. Digests and executable metadata also require privacy review (correlation and dictionary-guessing risks); define canonical inputs and exposure limits before implementation. Opaque runtime generations should not become persistent host identifiers. No new telemetry is requested; errors/logs must preserve the same filtering boundary. Reading the snapshot must not mutate policy, acquire grants, launch applications, or trigger capture. This is a boundary-design proposal, not a report of an exploitable defect.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

Planned upstream tests, **not tests claimed as executed**:

- Public stdio MCP integration against isolated daemon fixtures.
- Proxy/daemon policy disagreement: report daemon-enforced state, never proxy defaults.
- Absent and invalid manifest/managed/user policies with distinct validity outcomes.
- Unavailable daemon; missing/unknown fields; schema/enum incompatibility; identity mismatch; explicit fail-closed outcomes.
- Malformed/nonempty parameters rejected without side effects.
- Restart, reconnect, daemon/executable replacement and policy-change invalidation; no cached success across generations, including silent proxy reconnects.
- Concurrent policy reload: consistent snapshots and documented policy/action race behavior; do not assert that a status-only query proves action admission.
- Consistency with actual enforced residual ceilings.
- No grants or policy/state mutation and no desktop actions.
- Content/privacy filtering, including error paths and logs.
- Supported-platform serialization parity and legacy-client/server compatibility.

An accepted design must define observable acceptance evidence before a separate implementation begins. RFC acceptance itself is not runtime validation.

### Unresolved questions

1. Would maintainers accept this bounded read-only addition, decline it, or require a broader redesign?
2. MCP tool versus namespaced method, and final schema/version negotiation?
3. Which existing `authorization_status_json` fields suffice, which need filtering, and which required evidence is absent?
4. What executable/runtime and policy-generation semantics can the serving daemon guarantee across reloads and proxy reconnects?
5. Is useful evidence observation-only, or can an existing mechanism establish atomic action-generation continuity? If neither satisfies the intended guarantee, please say so explicitly.
6. Are the proposed policy digests and identity metadata acceptable under the privacy boundary?

Please record a maintainer decision summary in this issue, including material feedback, accepted changes, rejected alternatives, remaining risks and final disposition, as requested by `docs/rfcs/README.md`. A decline or a request for broader redesign is a useful final answer; no workaround or implementation will follow from this submission alone.

Changelog

Sourced from setuptools's changelog.

v84.1.0

Features

  • setuptools.archive_util now raises the new UnsafeMember exception when an archive member would be extracted outside of the extraction directory, where previously such a member was silently skipped. Aborting makes a malicious or malformed archive visible to the caller instead of yielding a quietly incomplete extraction, and matches the behavior of the standard library's tarfile extraction filters.

Bugfixes

  • Wheel.install_as_egg no longer creates namespace package directories outside of the destination egg directory. Entries in a wheel's namespace_packages.txt were split on . and passed straight to os.path.join, so an entry that was absolute, drive-qualified, or UNC discarded the destination and placed an __init__.py at a path chosen by the wheel. Namespace entries are now validated as dotted module names on every platform -- see GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w.

    This code path is reached only by the deprecated setup_requires mechanism when setup() is invoked outside a PEP 517 frontend; the setuptools build backend never reaches it.

  • setuptools.archive_util no longer extracts archive members outside of the requested extraction directory. Both the tar and zip formats specify / as the only path separator, but the guard against .. components split member names on / alone, so a name such as ..\escaped.txt was treated as a single component and then resolved as a traversal by the filesystem on Windows. Member names containing a backslash, a drive letter, or a UNC prefix are now rejected on every platform, as are members whose resolved destination falls outside the extraction directory -- see GHSA-grgh-hr87-3jpw.

title: [Bug]: macOS H.264 stream makes Chrome's hardware decoder lag 4 frames
body:
### Primary area

Other (cua-spacesd)

### Summary

The SPS from cua-spacesd's macOS encoder has no VUI, so the stream never says it doesn't reorder frames. Without this info, Chrome's hardware decoder on Windows falls back to the spec's worst-case reorder buffer (MaxDpbFrames, 4 frames at 1080p) and lags about 300 ms at 15 fps.

### Reproduction

1. Stream a 1080p Mac Space as H.264.
2. On Windows, decode it in Chrome with WebCodecs using `prefer-hardware` and `optimizeForLatency`, as the web app and HTML5 viewer do.
3. Time each frame from `decode()` to output.

### Expected behavior

About 1 ms per frame, the same as with `prefer-software`.

### Actual behavior

310 ms p50, with 4–5 frames pending. The Cua Spaces desktop app's video bench shows a 136 ms median decode time, versus 1.3 ms with `CUA_SPACES_VIDEO_DECODE=software`.

### Environment

cua-spacesd 0.7.0 on macOS 26.7.2 (the encoder code on `main` is unchanged). Windows 11, Chrome and Edge 158, Cua Spaces 0.41.11.

### Evidence

SPS `2742c028ab403c0113f2a0` (1080p, level 4.0): `ffmpeg -bsf:v trace_headers` shows `vui_parameters_present_flag = 0`. The same stream with a VUI that sets `max_num_reorder_frames = 0` decodes in 0.5 ms and produces identical frames.

### Workaround and additional context

The encoder never reorders (RealTime, `AllowFrameReordering = false`), but without VUI `bitstream_restriction`, H.264 E.2.1 tells the decoder to assume up to MaxDpbFrames (4 here) may be reordered. Software decoders guess otherwise and don't wait. Workaround: `CUA_SPACES_VIDEO_DECODE=software`.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests.
- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: fix(cua-spacesd): declare no frame reordering in the macOS H.264 SPS
body:
## Summary

- Problem this solves: VideoToolbox writes an SPS without a VUI, so Chrome's hardware decoder on Windows holds 4 frames (~300 ms) before output.
- What changed: both VideoToolbox encoders (`macos_h264.rs` in spacesd and the cua-media-codec backend) now add a VUI with `max_num_reorder_frames = 0` to the SPS on each keyframe. An SPS that already has a VUI is left alone. OpenH264 already writes one; the hardware backends don't encode yet.

## Related work

Fixes #8710

## Compatibility and risk

- Impact: hardware decoders that follow the spec output each frame at once. Decoded pictures are unchanged.
- Risk and rollback: a bad rewrite would break every keyframe; the tests below cover the real SPS. Revert to roll back.

## Validation

- Unit tests on the real VideoToolbox SPS (rewritten, already-has-VUI, truncated, non-SPS). The encoder conformance test now asserts every SPS has a VUI. `bin/ci` (clippy and unit tests for cua-media-codec and cua-spacesd-desktop) passes on Windows.
- A 150-frame 1080p Mac recording run through the fix: ffmpeg reads `max_num_reorder_frames = 0` and decodes identical frames. Chrome 158 WebCodecs, prefer-hardware: 310 ms → 0.5 ms per frame.
- Gap: the macOS code compiles only on macOS CI.

title: [Bug]: OrbStack-backed Linux Space fails because the engine helper requires /usr/bin/sleep
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

A local Linux Space fails to start on OrbStack. Cua's Docker helper mounts the engine's `/usr` and launches `/usr/bin/sleep`. OrbStack provides `sleep` under `/bin`.

### Reproduction

1. Start OrbStack and select its Docker endpoint explicitly. Use a fresh Space name and the released Cua CLI.
```sh
endpoint=$(docker context inspect orbstack --format '{{.Endpoints.docker.Host}}')
env -u DOCKER_CONTEXT CUA_RUNTIME_CONTAINER=system DOCKER_HOST="$endpoint" \
  cua spaces create linux --embedded --on local --kind container \
  --runtime runc --name orb-helper-repro --cpus 2 --memory-mb 4096 --no-relay
```

2. Inspect `cua-runsc-helper` on the OrbStack engine. The helper is left in `created`, and the Ubuntu Space does not start.

### Expected behavior

Cua starts the Ubuntu Space on the selected OrbStack engine, enforces the default network policy, and makes the desktop available to the viewer.

### Actual behavior

The helper container remains in `created`. Docker records:

```text
OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: exec: "/usr/bin/sleep": stat /usr/bin/sleep: no such file or directory
```

### Environment

- Cua Spaces 0.41.11
- - Cua CLI 0.31.0
- - - OrbStack 2.2.5
- - - - macOS 27.3 (26C5035r), arm64
- - - - - Local Linux container using OrbStack as the system Docker engine and `runc`

### Evidence

The following probe uses an already cached Ubuntu image and only disposable, offline, read-only containers.

```sh
image='ghcr.io/trycua/linux@sha256:b5f4912eb32839b2bd86bb37dc8c601e06b6dac0e11888ce7882dae0cec18eed'
docker --context orbstack run --rm --pull=never --network none --read-only \
  --entrypoint /usr/bin/sleep "$image" 0
docker --context orbstack run --rm --pull=never --network none --read-only \
  -v /usr:/engine-usr:ro -v /bin:/engine-bin:ro \
  --entrypoint /bin/sh "$image" -ec '
    awk '\''$5=="/engine-usr" || $5=="/engine-bin" {print $4, "->", $5}'\'' /proc/self/mountinfo
    test ! -e /engine-usr/bin/sleep
    echo "/engine-usr/bin/sleep: absent"
    readlink /engine-bin/sleep
  '
```

The first command exits 0. The second prints:

```text
/opt/docker-rootfs/bin -> /engine-bin
/opt/docker-rootfs/usr -> /engine-usr
/engine-usr/bin/sleep: absent
/bin/busybox
```

`docker inspect` reports `cua-vmm/helper:1`, `/usr/bin/sleep infinity`, and binds `/usr:/usr:ro` and `/:/host`. [The Cua SDK 0.31.0 source](https://github.com/trycua/cua/blob/78fe31378569aab57ddb5131a08fc90fc3c6fbb9/libs/cua/crates/cua-vmm/src/container/snapshot.rs#L442-L451) configures the same entrypoint and mounts.

### Workaround and additional context

#6791 fixed the same startup assumption on Windows by changing the managed WSL runtime's base image. The external OrbStack engine still uses its own split-`/usr` layout.

I tested a local patch that starts the helper from a digest-pinned BusyBox image providing `sleep` and `chroot`, while still running Cua's existing commands inside the engine root. The patched build launched Ubuntu on OrbStack and rendered the desktop in the browser viewer. Public HTTPS worked and the default network policy blocked a host listener that a plain OrbStack container could reach.

- [x] This issue describes a single problem.
- [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: cua-driver existing_profile: English-only "New Tab" match, and refusals with Stage Manager
body:
**Version:** cua-driver 0.62.1 (CuaDriver.app), macOS 27.2.1, Google Chrome with Chinese (Simplified) UI, Stage Manager on.

## 1. Bounded setup looks for an English "New Tab" button

With `serve --grant existing-profile`, `browser_prepare {strategy: existing_profile, delivery_mode: "foreground"}` on a normal Chrome window refused with `browser_wrong_target_refused: the approved Google Chrome window has no exact New Tab button`. Chrome's UI is Chinese, so the button is labelled 「新标签页」. After the user enabled remote debugging by hand at `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging`, the same call attached (Chrome showed its own consent prompt, the user allowed it) and everything worked.

**Ask:** match the New Tab button by role/identifier rather than its English title, or localize the label.

## 2. Mutations refused when two windows share geometry or a window is a Stage Manager thumbnail

- Two Chrome windows with identical bounds (a new window opens at the same frame as the previous one): `browser_click`, `browser_type` and `browser_set_input_files` refused with `CDP window no longer has an exact geometry or singleton-cardinality correlation with the native window`.
- When Stage Manager moves the window into the strip, the bounds become the thumbnail's (about 190×157 at x≈-262) and the binding goes stale; `set_window_frame` on such a window returned `WindowServer returned a frame that did not match the request`.
- With a single Chrome window on center stage, everything worked, including trusted clicks (`isTrusted=true`) and file input.

**Ask:** when the geometry can't be correlated, say which of the two causes it is and what to do ("two windows share this frame" / "window is in the Stage Manager strip, bring it to the stage"); consider correlating by CDP `windowId` plus title when frames are equal.

title: perf(cua-sdk): link the cua SDK release binaries with fat LTO to slow PyPI project growth
body:
Fixes the growth of the PyPI `cua` project (10 GB cap, 8.33 GB used). Linear: CUA-4491.

**Findings**
- `cua-cli` and `cua` are already on the weekly stable-only promotion: #7471 (the `cua-sdk` component of `pypi-promote.yml` uploads `cua-cli` then `cua`) and #7474 (`cua-cli` became a thin wheel under 1 MB). Nothing else uploads them to PyPI, so no workflow change is needed. Every merge still produces a GitHub release.
- The 2 GB/week came from before 12 Nov: 7 and 11 releases in the two weeks before, six wheels of about 455 MB each for `cua-cli`. Since then PyPI has one release a week for each project (0.27.5 on 16 Nov, 0.31.0 on 23 Nov). The health check's 28-day average still contains the old weeks and decays to about 0 by early December.
- What is left is `cua`: six wheels of 51-58 MB a week, mostly `libcua_sdk` (96 MB uncompressed on macOS arm64, built with strip but no LTO) and the static Linux `cua-spacesd` (about 13 MB compressed in every wheel).

**Change**
- `libs/cua/Cargo.toml`: `lto = "fat"` and `codegen-units = 1` in `[profile.release]`, as #7316 did for Cua Driver. Same code, same exported symbols; release builds link slower (the SDK job has a 240 minute timeout).
- `docs/pypi-publishing.md`: note to keep the profile.

Measured locally (macOS arm64): `libcua_sdk.dylib` 96.6 MB to 61.5 MB, gzip 38.8 MB to about 29 MB. Expected: `cua` about 0.33 to 0.27 GB a week, `cua-cli` about 0.

**Not done (recommendation)**: the Linux `cua-spacesd` ships in every platform wheel (about 80 MB a release). Fetching it on demand, as the thin `cua-cli` wheel does, would cut `cua` growth by about another 25%, but it changes offline behaviour. No PyPI releases were deleted or yanked.

v4.2.6: Turn of Events

This release adds an experimental CodeModeClient, which wraps a Client or ClientGroup and runs CodeMode on the client side, so an agent gets the search, schema and execute meta-tools over servers that don't run CodeMode themselves, and one execute block can chain tools across servers. Server spans now carry network.transport and, over HTTP, network.protocol.name and network.protocol.version. Fixes cover client callbacks and results, OpenAPI schemas and path parameters, resource links returned by a mounted server's tools (now namespaced like the rest of the mount), and response limiting, which now keeps truncated results within max_size as serialized.

Authlib is no longer installed with fastmcp. The client and server no longer use it, so code that imports authlib directly must declare it as its own dependency.

Experimental events are now their own package, fastmcp-events, with a new API. In 4.2.5 the Events extension lived in fastmcp.experimental.events and each event type was a check function. That module is gone: install the events extra (pip install "fastmcp[events]") and import from fastmcp_events. Each event type is now a Pydantic model: register it with @events.event("name"), then feed it with await events.emit(...) or with a reader registered by @events.reader(Model), so port each check function to a model and a reader. An optional for_subscription method on the model takes the subscription arguments and decides what each subscription receives. Emitted events can be kept in Redis through Docket with DocketEventLog (add fastmcp-events[docket]), so they survive restarts and reach every replica.

title: Windows: element-addressed type_text re-focuses an already focused control and collapses transient UI
body:
On Windows, `type_text` (and the other element-addressed keyboard tools) with
`delivery_mode: "foreground"` and an `element_token` always calls UIA `SetFocus`
on the cached element in `focus_cached_element_for_foreground`
(`libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-windows/src/tools/impl_.rs`), even when
that element already has keyboard focus.

In Chromium/CEF-based desktop apps this extra `SetFocus` is not a no-op. In one
production chat client the message-search `Edit` was already focused; the
repeated `SetFocus` collapsed the search box and the typed text never appeared.

Controlled A/B on the same build, process, window and element token (both runs
read `CurrentHasKeyboardFocus == true` before input):

| run | SetFocus before typing | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control | yes (current behaviour) | search box collapsed, no text |
| skip | no | exact text in the field, matching results shown |

Everything else (foreground activation, AttachThreadInput, the 350 ms focus
wait, SendInput, sentinels) was identical.

Driver: cua-driver-rs 0.57.0 (`37a981c7`); the function is unchanged on current
`main` (blob `ce740939`). Windows 11 26200, x64.

We carry a one-file downstream patch for this and are happy to open a PR with a regression test if the approach (skip `SetFocus` only when the same element already reports focus; keep the existing path for `false`/unknown) sounds right.

title: fix(cua-driver): focus a macOS text role on click instead of pressing it
body:
## Why

On macOS, `click` on a text field with no selectable ancestor (Automator's Save As name field, an action-parameter field) dispatched `AXPress`, which no text role advertises. The app answered `-25206` and nothing took focus. A click on a text field means "put the caret here", so the driver now focuses it and proves that it did.

Fixes #3850

Salvaged from #3856 by @will-bogusz, adapted to current `main`: `perform_ax_click` now returns `AxClickOutcome`, and the harness suite has moved to `cua-driver-e2e`.

## What changed

- `perform_ax_click`: when the selection fallbacks find nothing, an unmodified click on an `AXTextField`, `AXTextArea`, `AXSecureTextField`, `AXSearchField`, `AXComboBox`, `AXDateField` or `AXTimeField` with no `AXPress` goes to the new `focus_text_entry`. That function writes `AXFocused` and confirms it with `element_has_keyboard_focus`, the same read-back `type_text` and `press_key` do before they type. If the write does not stick, it sends a pointer click to the control's centre and checks again. Focus confirmed either way reports `effect: "confirmed"`. A pointer click that still leaves focus elsewhere says so and reports `unverifiable`. With no pointer route, the call errors and says nothing else was sent.
- The click's pixel fallback target now falls back to the text control's own centre, through the same background `WindowPointer` gate the selection fallback uses.
- New AppKit E2E cell `macos-appkit-click-text-focus-ax-background` (`harness_appkit_click_on_a_text_role_focuses_it`). It clicks `txt-note` and types, then clicks `txt-input` and types, and asserts that the input's mirror shows only the second string. On `main` the first click errors with `-25206`.

## Scope

This covers macOS element clicks on text-entry roles that do not advertise `AXPress`. Left out: modified clicks (`cmd`/`shift`, which keep the selection path), right-click, text fields that do advertise `AXPress` (such as WebKit inputs, whose press and DOM-focus settle are unchanged), and the separate `-25206`-as-error handling for other roles (#3835).

## Blast Radius

Only macOS `click` changes, and only for text roles that `AXPress` could not act on. Collection rows and Finder labels keep the selection fallback, which still runs first. Windows, X11 and Wayland are untouched: their adapters do not have this unadvertised-action path.

## Verification

- The scoped repository checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed (rustfmt, SPDX headers, Windows cfg, bin/ci tests, image refs). Clippy, unit tests and bindings were skipped in quick mode.
- `test_cua_driver_e2e_inventory.py` and `test_macos_lume_runner.py`: 163 passed, 1 skipped. These cover the new `appkit-cells.tsv` row.
- Not run here: this is a Linux host, so `platform-macos` was not compiled and its unit tests and the AppKit E2E cell did not run. The macOS CI lanes and the canonical Lume runner (`--retry-cell macos-appkit-click-text-focus-ax-background --retry-harness appkit --retry-only`) have to cover them.
