fix(cua-sandbox): bump upload-artifact pin to v7.0.2 (Node 24)
body:
## Summary

- **Problem this solves:** `.github/actions/cua-sandbox/action.yml` pins `actions/upload-artifact` at the v4 commit (`ea165f8…`), which declares `using: node20`. Every workflow using `cua-sandbox` therefore emits GitHub's "Node.js 20 is deprecated … forced to run on Node.js 24" warning. Reported in #8251 and confirmed there by @f-trycua.
- **What changed:** bumped the pin to the **v7.0.2** commit (`cf430e0…`), which declares `using: node24`. Kept the existing convention of a full commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment, as requested.

```diff
-      uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
+      uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
```

## Related work

Fixes #8251

**RFC:** not required — this is a single dependency pin inside a composite action. No SDK, CLI, MCP, protocol, permission, or cross-component contract change.

## Compatibility and risk

- **User-visible / API / CLI / MCP impact:** none. The action's own input surface (`artifact-name`, `upload-artifacts`, …) is untouched; only the version of the action it calls internally changes.
- **Input compatibility:** verified against both `action.yml` files. Inputs used here — `name`, `path`, `if-no-files-found`, `retention-days` — are all still present in v7. The v4 → v7 diff **removes no inputs** and only adds an optional `archive` input.
- **Runtime:** `node20` → `node24`, which is the point of the change.
- **Risk / rollback:** low; revert is a one-line change back to the previous SHA.

## Validation

- **Pin correctness:** `git ls-remote actions/upload-artifact refs/tags/v7.0.2` returns `cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9` — the SHA used here.
- **Runtime confirmation:** `using: node24` in v7.0.2's `action.yml`; `using: node20` in the previous v4 commit.
- **Input diff:** `removed in v7: none` / `added in v7: ['archive']`.
- **YAML:** file parses; single-line change, no structural edits.
- **Known gap:** I could not run `lint-docs-yaml.py` end-to-end locally because it reads `docs/content/…` pages I did not check out. It lints YAML fences in docs, and this PR changes no docs.

## Contributor and release checks

- [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff.
- [x] This change does not require an RFC.
- [x] Validation evidence is included; the only gap is explained above.

title: [RFC]: `lume ip` to print a VM's address, with an optional wait for the lease
body:
### Primary area

Lume

### Summary

Add `lume ip <name> [--wait <seconds>] [--storage <location>]`. It prints a running VM's IPv4 address and nothing else, exits 1 when there is no address, and with `--wait` polls until the guest gets a lease.

### Motivation and current state

Scripts that reach a guest with scp, rsync, Ansible, or a browser need its address. Today that means `lume get <vm> -f json | jq -r .ipAddress`, which returns `null` until the guest has a DHCP lease, so each boot-then-connect script writes its own sleep loop.

Lume already resolves the address in `VM.ipAddress(forMAC:networkMode:)` (vmnet leases, the ARP fallback, and gateway mode), and `lume ssh` uses it through `LumeController.getDetails`. No command exposes that lookup on its own. `CommandRegistry.swift` has no `ip` command on main.

### Goals

- One command that prints only the address, so `$(lume ip my-vm)` works in shell scripts.
- An optional bounded wait for the lease during boot.
- The same answer as `lume get` and `lume ssh` in nat, bridged, and gateway modes.

### Non-goals

- No new resolver or change to how addresses are found.
- No fix for #8262 (gateway VM address lookup in `lume ssh`). `lume ip` reports whatever the shared lookup returns.
- No HTTP API change.

### Proposal

- `lume ip <name>`: one lookup. Prints the address plus a newline on stdout and exits 0. Exits 1 with a message on stderr if the VM is not running or has no address.
- `--wait N` (default 0): poll `getDetails` once per second for up to N seconds while the VM runs. A VM that is not running at the first poll fails at once, since waiting cannot start it. Timeout exits 1 with `no IP address for VM '<name>' after N seconds`.
- `--storage` matches the other VM commands.

Implementation: a new `Commands/IP.swift` that follows the lookup in `SSH.swift`, registered in `CommandRegistry`, plus an `ipDoc` entry in `CommandDocExtractor` so `CommandDocExtractorTests` and the generated CLI reference stay in sync. The polling loop takes an injected lookup and sleep so it can be unit tested without a VM. About 150 lines with tests.

### Alternatives considered

- `lume get <vm> --field ip`: a generic field selector is a bigger contract change and still has no wait.
- `--wait-ip` on `lume run --detach`: ties lookup to one way of starting a VM. `lume ip --wait` also works for VMs started by `lume serve` or another process.

### Compatibility and migration

Additive. No existing command, flag, output, or endpoint changes. A new minor `feat(lume)` release entry.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Reads the same VM details `lume get` already prints. No new permissions. Records one telemetry event, `lume_ip`, the same way `lume ssh` records its own.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

- Unit tests (swift-testing) for argument parsing, `--wait` validation, immediate hit, wait-then-hit, timeout, and stopped VM failing fast.
- Manual run on a macOS host: `lume ip` on a running VM, `lume ip --wait 120` during boot, and a stopped VM, checked against `lume get -f json`.
- `CommandDocExtractorTests` and the CLI reference drift check pass.

### Unresolved questions

- Should `lume ip` also print an IPv6 address when the guest has one, or stay IPv4-only like `lume get`?
- Reuse `SSHError` cases, or add a small `IPError` so messages don't mention SSH? I'd lean toward the latter.

title: [RFC]: `lume prune --older-than` and `--space-budget` for partial cache cleanup
body:
### Primary area

Lume

### Summary

Let `lume prune` remove only some cached images: `--older-than <days>`, `--space-budget <GB>` (least recently used first), and `--dry-run`. `lume prune` with no options stays as it is.

### Motivation and current state

A cached macOS image is tens of gigabytes. On main, `Prune.swift` takes no options and `LumeController.pruneImages()` deletes the whole `<cache>/ghcr` directory, so on a laptop or CI host the choice is keeping every image ever pulled or downloading the one in daily use again. Lume already refuses writable starts when free disk space is low, so a growing cache can stop VMs from starting.

Each cache entry under `<cache>/ghcr/<org>/<manifestId>/` already has a `metadata.json` with a timestamp, and `ImageContainerRegistry.getImages()` already walks those entries. Selecting by age or size needs no new state.

### Goals

- Remove cached images not used in N days.
- Trim the cache to a size budget, evicting least recently used entries first.
- Preview what would be removed before removing it.

### Non-goals

- No automatic cache cap on pull. That changes pull behavior and needs its own discussion about defaults.
- No change to `POST /lume/prune`. It keeps deleting the whole cache.
- No pruning of VMs, only cached images.

### Proposal

```
lume prune [--older-than <days>] [--space-budget <GB>] [--dry-run]
```

- No options: unchanged.
- `--older-than N`: remove entries last used more than N days ago.
- `--space-budget G`: after any age filter, if the cache is still over G GB, remove least recently used entries until it fits.
- `--dry-run`: print what would be removed and the space freed, remove nothing. Requires one of the other two options.
- Output: one line per entry (image, short manifest id, size) and a total.
- "Last used" is the newer of the `metadata.json` timestamp and the entry directory's modification time. When a pull reuses a cached entry, its timestamp is refreshed so the order reflects use, not first download.

Implementation: a small pure selector (`ImageCachePruner.swift`) with a scanner over the cache tree, optional parameters on `pruneImages()`, the options on `Prune.swift`, the timestamp refresh on cache reuse, and the options added to `pruneDoc` in `CommandDocExtractor`. About 250 lines with tests.

### Alternatives considered

- A cache size cap in `lume config` enforced on every pull: automatic, but it changes pull behavior. An explicit command is the smaller first step, and a later cap could call the same selector.
- Prune by image name pattern: useful, but age and size are what address disk pressure.

### Compatibility and migration

Additive. The no-option CLI behavior and the HTTP endpoint are unchanged. The only behavior change is that reusing a cached image refreshes its `metadata.json` timestamp.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Deletes only entries inside Lume's own image cache directory. No new permissions or telemetry.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

- Unit tests over a temp cache tree: age filter, budget eviction order, both options together, dry-run removes nothing, missing metadata falls back to directory mtime, and the no-option path still removes everything.
- Manual run on a host with two or more cached images: `--dry-run` output, then a real prune, with `lume images` before and after.
- `CommandDocExtractorTests` and the CLI reference drift check pass.

### Unresolved questions

- Should "last used" also count a VM created from the image, or only pulls?
- Should a later change let `POST /lume/prune` accept the same two parameters?

title: Linux/Hyprland: list_windows returns an empty list when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is unset, with only a daemon-log warning
body:
## Summary

With `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1` on a Hyprland session, if the daemon is started from a shell where `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is not exported (common for agents, systemd user units and ssh), `list_windows` succeeds with `{"windows": []}` even though Hyprland has several clients. The only signal is a WARN line in the daemon log.

## Reproduction

1. Hyprland session, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000`, `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset, `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`.
2. `cua-driver serve --socket S` then `cua-driver call --socket S list_windows '{"session":"s"}'`.

## Observed

```
{"windows": []}
```
Daemon log: `WARN platform_linux::wayland: Hyprland window enumeration unavailable: invalid WAYLAND_DISPLAY socket name`. With `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1` exported the same call lists every client.

## Expected

Hyprland IPC (the instance socket) does not need `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; if the Wayland socket is required for another step, the tool should return a typed refusal naming the missing variable instead of an empty success. An empty list is indistinguishable from an empty desktop for an agent.

Verified: the empty result and the log line. Suspected cause: the enumeration path connects to the Wayland socket before or alongside the Hyprland IPC query and maps the error to an empty list.

Found while integrating Hyprland support in a fork (cua-driver 0.62.1 built from main, Hyprland 0.57.2, plugin input v3 candidate). Duplicates checked: searched open and closed issues and PRs for hidden or special workspace launch, exact-address activation, WAYLAND_DISPLAY and list_windows empty; none cover this (#3247 is a different cause; #6267 and #6268 are closed and about workspace parsing).

title: Linux/Hyprland: launch and adopt windows on a hidden per-session special workspace
body:
## Gap

An agent driving a GUI app on Hyprland currently has to put the app on a visible workspace, which interrupts the user. Hyprland special workspaces are not shown unless toggled, so a per-session special workspace (`special:cua-<session>`) would give the agent a place for its windows that never appears on a screen or takes focus, while the window stays listable, capturable and drivable.

## What works today (fork prototype)

- `launch_app` with a `hidden` flag launches the app inside the special workspace (silent, no focus change) and confirms the window by exact address; `adopt` moves an existing native window there and `release` moves it back only if it is still where it was put. Adopt refuses XWayland, grouped, pinned and focused windows.
- Windows on the special workspace are reported as drivable although `is_on_screen` is false (they are never on a screen), so list_windows, get_window_state, click, type_text, press_key, hotkey and invoke_menu all work on them. Live on a GTK 3 app with a menu bar: element click, pixel click, background typing, Ctrl+A, and invoke_menu File > Mark all worked with the user's focus unchanged.
- Caveat found live: `bring_to_front` on such a window shows the special workspace on the user's monitor (Hyprland focuses a window on a hidden special workspace by revealing it). That is the documented foreground escalation, but an agent should not call it on an owned hidden window.

## Open question

Is a first-class hidden-workspace concept wanted in the driver, or should it stay compositor-specific in the plugin? The fork keeps it in the driver (Hyprland dispatch via the IPC socket) so it needs no plugin change.

Found while integrating Hyprland support in a fork (cua-driver 0.62.1 built from main, Hyprland 0.57.2, plugin input v3 candidate). Duplicates checked: searched open and closed issues and PRs for hidden or special workspace launch, exact-address activation, WAYLAND_DISPLAY and list_windows empty; none cover this (#3247 is a different cause; #6267 and #6268 are closed and about workspace parsing).

title: Linux/Hyprland: get_cursor_position refuses on multi-monitor desktops with any rotated output
body:
## Summary

`get_cursor_position` on Hyprland fails with `Could not read the Hyprland pointer position: Hyprland multi-monitor desktops require unrotated outputs` when one of two monitors has `transform: 1` (90 degree rotation). The other tools (list_windows, click, type_text, the agent cursor overlay) work on the same desktop, so the refusal blocks only cursor readout.

## Reproduction

Two outputs, one rotated (`hyprctl -j monitors` shows `transform: 1`), then `cua-driver call get_cursor_position '{"session":"s"}'`.

## Expected

Either map the pointer through the output transform (the rect math for scaled outputs already exists), or return a typed unsupported result that says which output blocks it. Related: #4305 added multi-monitor support and introduced the unrotated-output guard.

Verified: the error text. Suspected cause: the guard in the Hyprland desktop-frame computation.

Found while integrating Hyprland support in a fork (cua-driver 0.62.1 built from main, Hyprland 0.57.2, plugin input v3 candidate). Duplicates checked: searched open and closed issues and PRs for hidden or special workspace launch, exact-address activation, WAYLAND_DISPLAY and list_windows empty; none cover this (#3247 is a different cause; #6267 and #6268 are closed and about workspace parsing).

title: [RFC]: Select a secondary display for Cua Driver on GNOME Wayland
body:
### Primary area

Cua Driver

### Summary

Let a client explicitly select a secondary display in GNOME Wayland, capture it, and use the capture coordinates for pointer actions. This applies to both landscape and portrait displays. Desktop calls that omit a display selector retain their current behavior.

### Motivation and current state

On a multi-monitor setup, an agent needs to see and interact with a window on a secondary display while the user's current primary display stays in place. Today the portable desktop action target accepts only `display_id: "primary"`. The desktop capture request has no per-display selector. Moving the window or changing the primary display changes the user's workspace to accommodate the agent.

The GNOME logical frame and the Wayland portal pointer dispatch already provide parts of the required geometry and input path. See [#7687](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7687) and [#5853](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5853). Display identity is discussed in [#3797](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/3797). The GNOME layout work in [#5956](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5956) provides related monitor geometry. This proposal covers the client's explicit selection and its binding to an authorized stream and input region.

### Goals

- Discover the available displays and select a secondary display while keeping the current primary display.
- Return an image of the selected display and bind its capture reference to the display identity, the layout revision and the capture-to-input transform.
- Translate a click from that image into the same logical point on the display. Refuse input if the display is unavailable, the capture is stale, or the point is outside the captured display.

### Non-goals

Changing the primary display, adding support for other compositors in the first implementation, and distributing this feature in OpenClaw.

### Proposal

Add an optional display selector to the typed desktop capture request and expose selectable display identifiers through the existing display geometry response. Reuse `capture_id` and the scoped desktop action target for physical pointer input. Keep monitor-local image coordinates in the capture snapshot and convert them to compositor logical coordinates at dispatch. The Linux adapter supplies the monitor bounds, scale and transform. The shared contract defines how the selector, capture and action target must agree.

The first implementation targets GNOME Wayland through a shared RemoteDesktop and ScreenCast portal session. The user selects the desired monitor and can grant keyboard and pointer access in the portal picker. The driver matches the authorized monitor stream's compositor position and size against the selected output and uses the PipeWire frame dimensions for image coordinates. For pointer actions, pair the stream with its libei absolute region using `mapping_id` and verify that the region and transformed point agree with the capture. Treat the mapping as session-scoped. Return a structured refusal if the authorized stream cannot be identified, the input grant is absent, or the capture or absolute region has become invalid. Check the portal's returned keyboard and pointer device bits before connecting to EIS. A view-only grant permits capture and provides zero input device bits.

Keyboard input follows compositor focus. It can be used after an authorized click focuses a window on the selected display. The default desktop request and its coordinate contract stay compatible.

See the [ScreenCast portal interface](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/doc-org.freedesktop.portal.ScreenCast.html#org.freedesktop.portal.ScreenCast.Start) for the approved stream properties.

### Alternatives considered

- Capture the entire desktop. This exposes unrelated displays and leaves the caller to identify each monitor region.
- Target an individual window. This can cover application-specific work. It leaves desktop surfaces and interactions across windows unaddressed.
- Rely on ordinal monitor indices. Enumeration order can change after display reconfiguration and makes saved references ambiguous.

### Compatibility and migration

The selector is optional. Capable providers advertise the new behavior, and clients that request an unsupported selector receive a structured refusal. The OpenClaw adapter can integrate the SDK and declare the feature after the driver implementation ships.

### Security, privacy, permissions, and telemetry

Use the existing capture and input authorization paths. An action using a capture reference must satisfy those permissions and match its display and session. Permission for one output carries no authority to capture another. A refusal emits no input. Telemetry omits pixels, window contents and hardware identifiers.

### Validation and acceptance evidence

- The baseline VM used GNOME Shell 50.1. On upstream commit `922af4cdf1c5`, all 79 contract tests and 1,208 Linux platform tests with the portal features enabled passed.
- The compiled MCP server detected both virtual displays in two configurations: two 1600×900 landscape displays, and the same secondary display rotated 90 degrees to 900×1600. In both cases it rejected the explicit `display_id` argument to `get_desktop_state` and refused a click explicitly targeted at the secondary display. The same display stayed primary before and after each run.
- In the same VM, a test of Mutter's private capture and input interfaces returned a 900×1600 image of the secondary output, then delivered a click at (450, 350) and one keypress to the GTK fixture visible in the image. The active stream showed the fixture change after the click. Both the portrait mode and the 90-degree rotation passed. A compositor layout readback confirmed the same primary output before and after each test.
- The public portal proof on GNOME Shell 50.1 used ScreenCast version 5 and RemoteDesktop version 2. The authorized stream reported origin (1600, 0) and size 900×1600 in portrait mode and with a 90-degree rotation. Its `mapping_id` matched an absolute libei region with those same bounds. The portrait fixture recorded the click and key, and the PipeWire stream showed the fixture respond. The landscape fixture recorded zero clicks. Cancellation returned neither a stream nor input permission. Selecting the primary output returned a distinct stream, which the proof rejected before opening PipeWire or sending input. View-only sharing returned the portrait stream and zero input device bits. The proposed Cua Driver contract still needs implementation and validation.
- The implementation needs unit and contract tests for the optional selector, omitted-selector compatibility, rotation and scaling, session binding and stale references.
- In the VM, use distinct fixtures on both displays and click a marker using the selected capture. Verify that the intended fixture receives the click and the other fixture receives zero clicks. Verify a key reaches the focused fixture. Run the same checks with two landscape displays and with the secondary display rotated 90 degrees. Also verify refusal after a layout change invalidates the capture and for an out-of-bounds click. Verify the primary display before and after.
- Repeat the passing candidate on a physical GNOME Wayland desktop with the secondary display in both orientations.

### Unresolved questions

- Decide whether the selector names a display attachment or a longer-lived physical display. Decide how identities and captures expire after a replug.
- Confirm the public selector and refusal keys across the SDK and MCP.
- Define the supported compositor and portal versions for the first release. Verify matching and pixel-to-logical coordinates with mixed-scale displays.

### RFC document pull request

_No response_

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues and RFCs.
- [x] This public proposal contains no credentials, private user or partner data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.
- [x] I described the problem, alternatives, migration, and evidence required—not only an implementation preference.

title: [Feature]: Web administration UI for self-hosted Relay
body:
### Primary area

Cross-component

### User problem

Self-hosted Relay operators currently have no supported browser-based inventory and administration experience for Relay machines and Spaces.

In Account Relay Mode, the OIDC provider's administration console manages identities, not Relay resources. The Relay container exposes APIs and an HTML5 machine viewer, but not a machine/Spaces management UI. `apps/cua-spaces-web` contains the Cua Spaces screens, but a standalone browser currently falls back to the in-memory demo adapter unless a native host such as Electron, SwiftUI/WKWebView, or Tauri supplies the real data bridge.

As a result, an operator who wants to inspect Relay resources from a browser must install/use the CLI or desktop app, or build and maintain a custom web integration.

### Desired outcome

Consider an officially supported Web administration UI for self-hosted `cua-relay`.

A useful first version could be deliberately small and read-only:

- Sign in through the Relay's existing Account Relay Mode OIDC configuration.
- List only the machines and Spaces the signed-in account is authorized to view.
- Show ownership/sharing role, connection state, last-seen information, host metadata, and registered Spaces where available.
- Link to the existing authorized HTML5 viewer for a machine.

Later iterations could expose owner/admin actions already supported by the underlying APIs, such as removing stale registrations or managing sharing, without bypassing existing authorization checks.

The initial success condition is: a self-hosted operator can open a browser, authenticate, and inspect their Relay resources without installing a native client or building a custom adapter.

### Current workaround

- Use `cua spaces ls` and other CLI commands for Relay and sandbox inventory.
- Use the cloud provider's console or `cua cloud status` / `cua cloud sweep` for provider-owned resources.
- Use the OIDC provider's administration UI for users, clients, and sessions.
- Install the Cua Spaces desktop app where a graphical UI is required.
- Build a custom integration against the Relay APIs.

### Affected components and platforms

- `libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-relay`
- Potentially `apps/cua-spaces-web` and its browser `DataAdapter`/host boundary
- Account Relay Mode, OIDC authentication, device enrollment, and existing authorization rules
- Browsers on macOS, Windows, and Linux
- Optional containerized deployment for self-hosted environments

Cloud-provider lifecycle and credentials should remain outside the Relay Web UI's initial scope. Native-only functionality such as OS Keyvault integration also need not be part of an initial browser version.

### Alternatives and prior art

- The Keycloak/OIDC administration console manages identities, not Relay machines or Spaces.
- The Relay's embedded HTML5 viewer provides access to one machine's desktop, not an account-level inventory or administration page.
- The Cua Spaces desktop app supplies the native host bridge required by the shared Web UI, but requires a desktop installation.
- Serving `apps/cua-spaces-web` directly from a static web server currently produces the demo experience rather than a Relay-backed administration UI.

I did not find an existing issue, RFC, or active pull request requesting a self-hosted Relay Web administration UI.

### Implementation ideas

Two possible directions, leaving the architecture choice to maintainers:

1. Add a production browser adapter for the shared Cua Spaces Web UI, backed by versioned Relay/daemon APIs and the existing OIDC session.
2. Start with a smaller, read-only Relay administration frontend focused on the machine directory, then expand only where existing APIs and authorization semantics permit.

An optional separate container or opt-in static bundle would let self-hosted operators deploy the UI without changing the default Relay attack surface. The browser should never receive the Relay admin token or cloud-provider credentials; all resource access should remain scoped to the authenticated account and existing authorization checks.

### Submission checks

- [x] I searched for existing issues, RFCs, and active pull requests.
- [x] I reviewed the RFC criteria and used the RFC form instead when this requires a public contract or architectural decision.
- [x] This public request contains no credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, or vulnerability details.

title: fix(hyprland-plugin): reviewed Omarchy edge profile for Hyprland 0.57.2-7

title: fix(ci): pick the npm dist-tag from registry state for Cua Driver SDK publishes
body:
Fixes CUA-4504.

## What happened

The `publish-npm` job of `CD: Cua Driver SDK packages` failed for 0.63.0 with `Cannot implicitly apply the "latest" tag because previously published version 0.63.1 is higher than the new version 0.63.0`.

0.63.1 is not a bogus publish. Release PRs #8733 (0.63.0) and #8740 (0.63.1) both merged on 26 Nov. The 0.63.1 GitHub release was published at 14:57Z, before the 0.63.0 one at 15:00Z, so the SDK publish for 0.63.1 ran first (npm `latest` became 0.63.1) and the 0.63.0 run then hit npm's guard. No GitHub release, tag or CI run was bogus; both versions are real.

## Root cause

The publish step passed no `--tag`, so npm applies `latest` implicitly, and that is only valid when the version is the highest published. Out-of-order releases are normal here (separate release PRs, manual publish dispatches), so the tag has to come from registry state.

## Fix

`.github/scripts/npm_dist_tag.py` picks the tag per package: higher than the current `latest` gives `latest`, a prerelease gives `next`, a lower version gives `backport-X.Y`. A late 0.63.0 therefore never moves `latest` backwards. Both publish steps use it. Unit tests: `.github/scripts/tests/test_npm_dist_tag.py`.

User impact: none for `latest` (it correctly stays 0.63.1). After merge, re-run the failed workflow to publish the missing 0.63.0 packages (already-published packages are skipped).

## npm cleanup

Nothing on npm needs deprecating: 0.63.1 is legitimate. No unpublish or deprecate commands are needed.

## npm token note

npm warned that 2FA-bypass tokens are being restricted for direct publishing (https://gh.io/npm-gat-bypass2fa-deprecation). This workflow publishes with `secrets.NPM_TOKEN` (`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`), not trusted publishing, even though it already has `id-token: write` and `--provenance`. Migration: on npmjs.com add a Trusted Publisher (repo `trycua/cua`, workflow `cd-py-cua-driver.yml`) to `@trycua/cua-driver` and each `@trycua/cua-driver-*` platform package, then drop `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from the two publish steps (needs npm 11.5.1+; Node 24 is already used). `ts-reusable-publish.yml` should be checked the same way. No npm settings were changed.

Tests: `bin/ci --quick` passed.

title: fix(cua-driver): give browser_prepare E2E calls room for the driver's setup bounds
body:
Refs #8748. Linear: CUA-4531.

The release gate's Windows standalone-browser lane failed on `standalone_browser_existing_profile_setup` with `TIMEOUT (>25s) on browser_prepare`. No driver code changed since the passing 0.63.0 gate, and later gate runs are green, so this is not a driver regression.

Root cause: the test harness caps every tool call at a flat 25 s. `browser_prepare` chains bounded driver phases (3 s tab stabilisation, 3 s new tab, 12 s setup-page ready, then rollback), which can add up to more than 25 s on a loaded runner while a behavioural recording runs. The harness then killed the call and the case had no evidence.

Fix: `browser_prepare` gets a 75 s ceiling in the testkit (same tool-aware mechanism as the macOS recorded-call timeout), with a unit test pinning it above the sum of the driver's bounds. No retries, skips or ignores added.

User impact: none (test harness only); unblocks the next Cua Driver release.

Checks: `bin/ci --quick` passed; `cargo test -p cua-driver-testkit --lib timeout` passes.

title: [Bug]: cua-driver: agent cursor overlay is drawn half a screen down-right of move_cursor position (0.38.0, macOS)
body: ### Primary area Cua Driver ### Summary With the agent cursor enabled on macOS, `move_cursor` on a window target succeeds and `get_agent_cursor_state` reports the expected coordinates, but the visible cursor overlay is drawn about (+756, +491) pt down-right of that position on a 1512 × 982 pt display. Actual `click` inputs using the same coordinates land accurately; only the drawn overlay cursor is offset. ### Reproduction Reproduces 100% of the time (every call, across different points in the window and after restarting `cua-driver`). Over one stdio MCP connection (protocol `2025-03-26`) to `/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver mcp`, with `P` = TextEdit's pid and `W` = its document window id: 1. Call `get_window_state` with `{session: "probe-1", pid: P, window_id: W, include_screenshot: true, include_accessibility_tree: false, max_image_dimension: 1280}`. 2. Call `set_agent_cursor_enabled` with `{session: "probe-1", enabled: true}`. 3. Call `move_cursor` with `{session: "probe-1", target: {kind: "window", pid: P, window_id: W}, x: 586.0, y: 488.0}` (pixel coordinates in the screenshot returned in step 1). 4. Wait 1.5 s and capture the full screen (`screencapture -x`). 5. Call `get_agent_cursor_state` with `{session: "probe-1"}`. ### Expected behavior The agent cursor overlay is drawn at the point inside the target window named by `(x, y)` — the same screen position that `get_agent_cursor_state` reports and that `click` with those coordinates hits. ### Actual behavior - Every MCP call returns ok with no error, and `get_agent_cursor_state` reports the requested screen position. - In the full-screen capture, the overlay cursor is drawn approximately (+756, +491) pt from that reported position (outside the target window). - The same (+756, +491) pt offset occurs for different target points in the window and persists after restarting `cua-driver`. - `click` with the same coordinates acts on the intended element, so input coordinate mapping is unaffected. - Root cause is not confirmed from outside the binary. ### Environment - Component / version: `cua-driver` 0.38.0 (`/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/MacOS/cua-driver mcp`, stdio) - OS / architecture: macOS 27.2 (build 26B123, beta), Apple silicon (arm64) - Display: Single built-in Retina display, 1512 × 982 pt (scale 2), no external display - Target application: macOS TextEdit (single document window) ### Evidence ### Workaround and additional context - **Workaround:** None (no client-side coordinate offset applied). - **Suspected area:** On the 1512 × 982 pt display, the observed (+756, +491) pt shift equals exactly `(+W/2, +H/2)` (half the display width and height), which may indicate a centre-origin vs. top-left-origin mismatch when positioning the macOS overlay window/layer on this OS build. - **Not checked:** External display, non-Retina display, non-beta macOS build, or other `cua-driver` versions. ### Submission checks - [x] I searched for duplicate issues and active pull requests. - [x] This issue describes a single problem. - [x] I removed credentials, private data, sensitive screenshots, and vulnerability details from this public report.

title: lume cp host → guest fails: destination path is quoted twice before scp
body:
**Version:** lume 0.9.0 (installed with `install.sh`, `LUME_VERSION=0.9.0`), macOS 27.2.1 host, macOS 27.2.1 guest created with `lume create … --unattended tahoe`.

**Repro**
```sh
lume run vm --no-display --detach
echo hello > /tmp/hello.txt
lume cp /tmp/hello.txt vm:/Users/lume/hello.txt
```

**Expected:** `/Users/lume/hello.txt` exists in the guest.

**Actual:**
```
Error: Command failed with exit code 1: /usr/bin/scp: dest open "'/Users/lume/hello.txt'": No such file or directory
/usr/bin/scp: failed to upload file /tmp/hello.txt to '/Users/lume/hello.txt'
```

The remote side is asked to open a file whose name includes the single quotes (`'/Users/lume/hello.txt'`). It looks like the destination is shell-escaped (the escaping added for `lume ssh` in #3879/#3911) and then passed to `scp` as a single argv element. Modern `scp` uses SFTP by default and does not run the path through a remote shell, so the quotes end up in the filename. The same happens for any destination path, including one without spaces.

**Workaround:** a `--shared-dir` mount, or `lume ssh vm -- 'cat > path'` with stdin.

**Suggested fix:** don't shell-quote the path in the SFTP/`scp` code path. Quote it only when the command goes through a remote shell, or pass `-O` to force the legacy protocol when quoting is kept.

title: fix(ci): make the cua SDK workflow finish and pass on main
body:
## What and why

`CI: cua SDK` had no green run on main in its last 15 (11 cancelled, 4 failed). Three unrelated causes:

1. **Windows failed on Unix-only tests.** The `space_jobs` tests run the job's POSIX `sh` scripts through `/bin/sh` (the module already refuses a Windows guest), and `paths::tests::no_mesh_says_the_tree_stays_here` expects the Unix mesh socket lookup. Windows has neither. Both are now Unix-only, and Windows gets its own test for what `machine_paths` really says there. No `#[ignore]`.
2. **The macOS smoke jobs (swift, node, python) were "cancelled" by their own 60 minute timeout, not by a newer push.** Main runs never cancel in progress (`cancel-in-progress` is PR-only). A cold macOS compile takes more than 60 minutes. The job was killed before it saved the warm compile, so the next run started cold again, forever. They now get 120 minutes (as the rust leg already has), a 100 minute step timeout so the save still runs, and `save-always` with the swift job's cache family (same release SDK and fixtures).
3. **`idle_cpu` budget was below what a hosted macOS runner measures.** It already measures the daemon's own CPU time, not machine load. The same build uses about 1.4% of a core on a quiet laptop and 1.6% to 2.1% on the hosted runner (failures on 26 and 27 Nov), against a 1.5% budget (the failure text also rounded it to "2%"; it now prints one decimal). A profile of the idle daemon shows no single hot spot: the cost is spread over the poll work, so this is a budget set too tight, not a regression. The bug the test guards against used about 25% of a core, so 3% still catches it by a wide margin. The offline-dial assertion is unchanged.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p cua-spaces --lib -- space_jobs paths` and `cargo test -p cua-spaces-cli --test idle_cpu` pass on macOS.
- `bin/ci --quick --fix` passes.
- The workflow change needs a main run to prove the macOS jobs finish; not waited on.

title: [Bug]: macOS: Cua Spaces polling driver.permissions every 2.5 s keeps PreventUserIdleDisplaySleep held indefinitely
body:
## Summary

On macOS, leaving Cua Spaces open on a view that mounts `useAppPermissions` (such as the Cua Driver page) prevents display sleep indefinitely, even when no agent or session is active.

`pmset -g assertions` shows `cua-driver` holding `PreventUserIdleDisplaySleep` (`"Cua Driver: an agent is working on this Mac"`) continuously for days (observed held for 59.5 hours straight, starting 8 seconds after `cua-driver` launched, with `cua-driver sessions` reporting `No live sessions.`).

## Environment

- Cua Spaces `0.41.9` (`cua-driver` `0.61.2`, embedded via `com.trycua.spaces.driver`)
- Verified all four code paths are still unchanged on `main` (`837f6a0383ad`)
- macOS (Apple Silicon)

## Root Cause

Two behaviors combine to keep the 10-minute display-awake timer permanently reset:

1. **Cua Spaces polls `check_permissions` on `cua-driver` every 2.5 seconds even after both permissions are granted:**
   - `apps/cua-spaces-web/src/bridge/app-permissions.ts` (`APP_PERMISSIONS_POLL_MS = 2_500`, line 28 & line 112) polls `driver.permissions` every 2.5 s while mounted.
   - `apps/cua-spaces-macos/Sources/CuaSpacesMacKit/WebHost/WebUIBridge+Driver.swift` (`appPermissions()`, lines 113–120) calls `restartDriverIfStale(driver, force: false)` whenever Screen Recording and Accessibility are granted.
   - `restartDriverIfStale()` (lines 219–230) only sets `state.lastRestart` when it actually restarts a stale driver, so when permissions are already healthy it calls `driver.call("check_permissions", ["prompt": false])` over the socket on every 2.5 s tick (also triggering `TCCAccessPreflight` repeatedly in the background).

2. **`cua-driver` treats every tool dispatch — including read-only probes — as active agent work:**
   - `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver-core/src/tool.rs` (line 2738) calls `crate::tool_activity::note_tool_activity()` unconditionally before `tool.invoke(args)`.
   - `libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/platform-macos/src/display_awake.rs` (`DEFAULT_IDLE_WINDOW = 600s`, lines 41 & 103–141) acquires/refreshes `PreventUserIdleDisplaySleep` on every `note_tool_activity()` call.

Because `check_permissions` arrives every 2.5 s (< 600 s), the `cua-display-awake` thread never sees an idle window and never releases the assertion.

## Observed Impact

- Display sleep is blocked indefinitely (`PreventUserIdleDisplaySleep` held continuously with `cua-driver sessions` empty).
- Continuous background CPU / TCC traffic (~68 min CPU on `cua-driver` and ~60 min CPU on `CuaSpacesMac` over ~59.5 hours of idle uptime).

## Suggested Fix

Both halves are worth fixing independently:

1. **In `cua-driver`:** Don't call `note_tool_activity()` for passive/read-only status and configuration tools (`check_permissions`, `health_report`, `get_config`, `list_sessions`, `check_for_update`), or only arm the display-awake guard for observation/input tools that require an unlocked display.
2. **In `CuaSpacesMac` (`WebUIBridge+Driver.swift`):** Once `restartDriverIfStale()` confirms that a given `meta.pid` already sees both permissions granted, cache that `pid` so it does not call `driver.call("check_permissions", ...)` again on every 2.5 s poll unless the driver PID changes (or `force: true`).

## Workaround

Setting `CUA_DRIVER_KEEP_DISPLAY_AWAKE=0` in `launchd` and restarting `com.trycua.spaces.driver` releases the assertion immediately (`PreventUserIdleDisplaySleep` drops to `0`), though the 2.5 s `check_permissions` polling still continues in the background.

title: fix(cua-volume): a write waits for a holder whose link is briefly down
body:
Fixes the Windows-only failure of `two_machines_agree_on_an_owner_and_hold_two_copies` that keeps "CI: cua SDK" red on main (Linear CUA-4556).

**What was wrong.** When the owner waits for the second copy of a write, it counted the other machine as "could still hold it" only if its control link was open at that exact instant. A link that drops and is redialed (two machines dialing each other, or a slow heartbeat on a loaded runner) made the write return `Local(1)` immediately, although the other machine was healthy and about to acknowledge. This is a real product race, not a test-harness problem: a write could report "one copy" while the second machine was fine.

**Fix.** `copies_at` no longer treats a momentarily missing link as "away". Whether a holder is away is decided by the failure detector, a goodbye, or the missed-ack count, which already exist.

**Evidence.** On macOS under CPU load the test failed 23 of 24 parallel runs before the change and 0 of 72 after; 50 of 50 sequential runs pass. The tests for a vanished laptop, a closed laptop, a goodbye, a refusing machine and a flaky laptop pass 8 of 8 each.

title: fix(cua-driver): stop the stray second press after macOS 27 background clicks and drags
body: ## Summary - Problem this solves: on macOS 27, a background `click` or `drag` on a view in a resizable window is followed by a second `mouseDown` one point outside the window's top-left corner, about 500 ms after the route's off-screen primer (#8725). On a drag it arrives in the middle of the gesture. macOS 27 reads the `CGEventSetWindowLocation` stamp as window-local, so the primer's (-1, -1) is no longer off-screen: it sits on the window's resize edge. - What changed: on macOS 27+ the primer is stamped at window-local (-10000, -10000), which no window edge reaches. Its event location stays (-1, -1), and earlier macOS versions keep the (-1, -1) stamp. The click and drag routes share the value. ## Related work Fixes #8725 Refs #5492 and #7372, which moved the target stamps to window-local and left the primer at (-1, -1). #6126 and #8132 edit the same plan and do not move the primer, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. ## Compatibility and risk - User-visible, API/CLI/MCP, migration, permission, or platform impact: macOS 27 only. Background left clicks and drags stop sending the extra press. macOS 26 and earlier build the same plan as before. No API change. - Risk and rollback: low; one constant and the primer stamps in `input/mouse.rs`. Chrome needs the primer before it accepts the target click, and it still accepted every click below. Revert to roll back. ## Validation Candidate: `1c73124a9c` on main `837f6a0383`. - Focused tests and checks: `macos_27_route_stamps_the_window_local_point` and `macos_27_background_drag_stamps_window_local_points` expect the new stamp; both fail with the constant set back to (-1, -1), which is what main stamps. `cargo test --locked -p platform-macos --lib` on macOS 27.0: 920 passed, 1 failed, 13 ignored. The failure is `security_prompt::tests::the_system_consent_labels_include_allow_and_dont_allow`, which fails the same way on main. `cargo clippy --locked -p platform-macos --all-targets -- -D warnings`, rustfmt and `bin/ci --quick` (5 passed, 4 left to CI) are clean. - Manual or platform evidence: A/B on macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon, 2x. Debug builds of main and this branch through `cua-driver mcp --direct --no-overlay`, with another app in front. The receiver is the `StrayRepro.swift` from #8725 with drags logged too, in a 360 by 98 window on a second display at (-1500, 1719). | | A (main) | B (this PR) | |---|---|---| | Resizable window, 10 background clicks: second presses | 10 | 0 | | Fixed-size window, 10 background clicks: second presses | 0 | 0 | | Resizable window, 5 background drags: second presses | 5 | 0 | | Chrome 158 on another Space, 10 background clicks on a page element: trusted clicks with user activation | 10/10 | 10/10 | In A the second press came 502 to 553 ms after the primer, and each drag reached the view as a press, a second press and release at (-1, -1), then the release. In B each drag is one press, 20 drags and one release. - Known gaps or CI still required: macOS 26 was not run (`capture_bound_background_route_preserves_nonzero_origin_hit` pins the unchanged plan there); Electron, GPUI and full-screen windows were not run; the canonical AppKit harness was not run. ## Contributor and release checks - [x] The PR is focused and the description matches the final diff. - [x] This change does not require an RFC, or the accepted RFC is linked above. - [x] Tests, documentation, and platform evidence are included or the gap is explained. - [x] The PR title is a Conventional Commit describing the production change. - [x] External contributor authorship is preserved, or no external contribution is included. - [ ] If release-tracked files changed but this is intentionally non-releasing, the `no-release` label is applied. - [ ] `bin/ci` is green and signed off (`bin/ci --signoff`)

title: fix(cua-agent-setup,cua-volume): finish the Windows CI lane
body:
Fixes the remaining Windows failures in "CI: cua SDK" `rust (windows-latest)` (CUA-4556), from the `--no-fail-fast` run.

What changed for users: on Windows, the paths cua writes into agent configs no longer mix `\` and `/`; and a laptop whose link to the studio keeps flapping no longer risks taking the volume over.

- cua-agent-setup: `~/.local/bin`, `AppData/*` and `CuaDriver.app` folders are now built component by component (product fix). Tests compare native paths, and `detection_uses_path_markers_and_app_bundles` now creates the `codex.exe` it expects on Windows (it was only written on Unix).
- cua-volume: the idle takeover counted time since the verdict turned "down", which a flapping peer never leaves on a slow runner. It now also requires unbroken silence (`Detector::gone_for`, with a unit test).

Tested locally on macOS: cua-agent-setup full suite, cua-volume lib + the flaky-laptop sim, `bin/ci --quick`.
